uz: Ularning harakatini eshitish juda yoqimli! - deb o'ylaydi Ailis. ~~~ Qanday qilib hamisha yaxshi gapira olasiz?

en: 'I've been in many gardens before, but none of the flowers could talk.' 'Put your hand down, and feel the ground,' said the Tiger-lily.
uz: Men ilgari ko'plab bog'larda bo'lganman, lekin gullarning hech biri gapira olmagan. - Qo'lingni pastga tushirib, yerga tushib ko'ring, - dedi bo'r-li.

en: 'Then you'll know why.
uz: Keyin nima sababini bilasiz.

en: 'It's very hard,' she said, 'but I don't see what that has to do with it.' 'In most gardens,' the Tiger-lily said, 'they make the beds too soft —so that the flowers are always asleep.' This sounded a very good reason, and Alice was quite pleased to know it.
uz: Bu juda qiyin, - dedi u, - lekin bu bilan nima bog'liqligini tushunmayapman. - Ko'pgina bog'larda, - dedi o'g'ir-lily, - to'shaglarni juda yumshatishadi, shunda gullar doimo uxlaydi. Bu juda yaxshi sababga o'xshardi va Alice buni bilib juda xursand bo'ldi.

en: 'I never thought of that before!' she said.
uz: U shunday dedi: Men bundan oldin hech qachon bunday o'ylamaganman!

en: 'It's MY opinion that you never think AT ALL,' the Rose said in a rather severe tone.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, hech qachon o'ylamaydi, - dedi Roza kamroq qattiq so'zlar bilan.

en: 'I never saw anybody that looked stupider,' a Violet said, so suddenly, that Alice quite jumped; for it hadn't spoken before.
uz: Men hech qachon o'zgacha ko'rinadigan hech kimni ko'rmadim, - dedi Violet, shunday to'satdan, Alice juda ko'p o'tib ketdi; chunki u ilgari hech qachon gapirmagan edi.

en: 'Hold YOUR tongue!' cried the Tiger-lily.
uz: TINGLINGni tutib tur! - deb baqirgan bo'lib qoldi.

en: 'As if YOU ever saw anybody!
uz: Agar siz hech kimni ko'rgan bo'lsangiz!

en: You keep your head under the leaves, and snore away there, till you know no more what's going on in the world, than if you were a bud!' 'Are there any more people in the garden besides me?' Alice said, not choosing to notice the Rose's last remark.
uz: Boshingizni barglar ostiga qo'yib, dunyoda nimalar sodir bo'layotganini bilmaguningizcha orqaga qovurasiz! Sen bog'da mendan tashqari boshqa odamlar bormi? - deb so'radi Alice, Rozaning so'nggi gapini sezmay.

en: 'There's one other flower in the garden that can move about like you,' said the Rose.
uz: - Bog'da siz kabi harakatlanadigan yana bir gul bor, - dedi Roza.

en: 'I wonder how you do it—' ('You're always wondering,' said the Tiger-lily), 'but she's more bushy than you are.' 'Is she like me?' Alice asked eagerly, for the thought crossed her mind, 'There's another little girl in the garden, somewhere!' 'Well, she has the same awkward shape as you,' the Rose said, 'but she's redder—and her petals are shorter, I think.' 'Her petals are done up close, almost like a dahlia,' the Tiger-lily interrupted: 'not tumbled about anyhow, like yours.' 'But that's not YOUR fault,' the Rose added kindly: 'you're beginning to fade, you know—and then one can't help one's petals getting a little untidy.' Alice didn't like this idea at all: so, to change the subject, she asked 'Does she ever come out here?'
uz: Siz buni qanday qilasiz deb o'ylayman (Siz har doim o'ylab yurasiz, - dedi boyarli baliq),  lekin u sizdan ko'ra ko'proq o'tkir. U menga o'xshadimi? - deb so'radi Alisa, chunki uning ongida bu fikr o'tib ketdi: Bir joyda bog'da boshqa bir qizcha bor! - deb o'yladi. U siz kabi noqulay shaklga ega, - dedi roza, lekin u qizilroq va uning ko'kraklari qisqa, deb o'ylayman. Uning ko'kraklari yaqinroq, deyarli dahliya kabi tayyorlangan, - dedi boyarli baliq: Sizning kabi hech qanday holatda tushmagan, - deb to'xtatdi. Ammo bu sizning aybingiz emas, - dedi roza mehribonlik bilan qo'shimcha qildi: Siz o'zingizga o'xshaydi, bilasiz va keyin birovning ko'kraklarini biroz o'zgartirib yuborishga yordam bera olmaysiz.

en: 'I daresay you'll see her soon,' said the Rose.
uz: O'ylaymanki, siz uni yaqinda ko'rasiz, dedi Roza.

en: 'She's one of the thorny kind.' 'Where does she wear the thorns?' Alice asked with some curiosity.
uz: U tikanlilardan biri. U tikanlarni qayerda kiyadi? - deb so'radi Alisa qiziquvchanlik bilan.

en: 'Why all round her head, of course,' the Rose replied.
uz: Nima uchun, albatta, boshini o'rab olgan, deb javob berdi Roza.

en: 'I was wondering YOU hadn't got some too.
uz: O'zimga: Sening ham birozga ega bo'lmaganingmi?

en: I thought it was the regular rule.' 'She's coming!' cried the Larkspur.
uz: Men buni odatdagi qoida deb o'ylardim.U kelyapti! - deb baqirdi Larkspur.

en: 'I hear her footstep, thump, thump, thump, along the gravel-walk!' Alice looked round eagerly, and found that it was the Red Queen.
uz: Men uning qadamlarini eshityapman, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron, toshbo'ron.

en: 'She's grown a good deal!' was her first remark.
uz: U juda ulg'aygan! - deb o'ylagan uning birinchi so'zlari edi.

en: She had indeed: when Alice first found her in the ashes, she had been only three inches high—and here she was, half a head taller than Alice herself!
uz: Haqiqatan ham shunday edi: Alice uni birinchi marta kulda topganida, u atigi uch dyuym baland edi va mana, u Alicedan yarim bosh baland edi!

en: 'It's the fresh air that does it,' said the Rose: 'wonderfully fine air it is, out here.' 'I think I'll go and meet her,' said Alice, for, though the flowers were interesting enough, she felt that it would be far grander to have a talk with a real Queen.
uz: Bu toza havo uchun, dedi Roza: bu erda ajoyib yaxshi havo bor. Men o'ylaymanki, men u bilan uchrashishga ketaman, dedi Alice, chunki gullar etarlicha qiziqarli bo'lsa-da, u haqiqiy Qiroli bilan suhbatlashish ancha buyukroq bo'lishini his qildi.

en: 'You can't possibly do that,' said the Rose: '_I_ should advise you to walk the other way.' This sounded nonsense to Alice, so she said nothing, but set off at once towards the Red Queen.
uz: Siz buni qila olmaysiz, dedi Roza: Men sizga boshqa yo'ldan yurishni maslahat beraman.Bu Alice uchun g'alati tuyuldi, shuning uchun u hech narsa aytmadi, lekin darhol Qizil Qirolicha tomon yo'lga chiqdi.

en: To her surprise, she lost sight of her in a moment, and found herself walking in at the front-door again.
uz: O'zi hayron bo'lganida, u o'zini ko'rishni yo'qotdi va yana old eshikdan kirib keldi.

en: A little provoked, she drew back, and after looking everywhere for the queen (whom she spied out at last, a long way off), she thought she would try the plan, this time, of walking in the opposite direction.
uz: U biroz xafa bo'lib, orqaga qaytdi va hamma joyda qirolicha qidirib topgandan so'ng (uncha uzoqdan, oxir-oqibat, uning orqasidan g'ofil bo'lgan) bu safar o'ziga qarama-qarshi yo'nalishda yurish rejasini sinab ko'rishni o'yladi.

en: It succeeded beautifully.
uz: Bu ajoyib muvaffaqiyatga erishdi.

en: She had not been walking a minute before she found herself face to face with the Red Queen, and full in sight of the hill she had been so long aiming at.
uz: U bir daqiqa ham yurmay, qizil Qiroli bilan yuzma-yuz ko'rishni va uzoq vaqtdan beri intilayotgan tog'ning ko'rinishini ko'rishni boshladi.

en: 'Where do you come from?' said the Red Queen.
uz: Qizil kraliça: Sen qayerdan kelding? - deb so'radi.

en: 'And where are you going?
uz: 'Va qayerga ketyapsan?

en: Look up, speak nicely, and don't twiddle your fingers all the time.' Alice attended to all these directions, and explained, as well as she could, that she had lost her way.
uz: Yuqoriga qarab, yaxshi gapirib, barmoqlaringizni to'xtatib turmang, - deb aytdi Alisa, bu yo'nalishlarga amal qilib, o'z yo'lidan adashganini imkon qadar yaxshi tushuntirdi.

en: 'I don't know what you mean by YOUR way,' said the Queen: 'all the ways about here belong to ME—but why did you come out here
uz: Siz O'Z yo'lingiz bilan nima demoqchi ekaningizni bilmayman, - dedi QIROLOLO: bu yerda bo'lgan barcha yo'llar MENGA tegishli, lekin nega bu yerga keldingiz?

en: at all?' she added in a kinder tone.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda? - deb qo'shimcha qildi u kichkinagina o'z o'rnida.

en: 'Curtsey while you're thinking what to say, it saves time.' Alice wondered a little at this, but she was too much in awe of the Queen to disbelieve it.
uz: Curtsey, nima deyishni o'ylayotgan bo'lsangiz, bu vaqtni tejaydi, - deb o'yladi Alice bu haqda ozgina o'ylab ko'rdi, lekin u kralichaga ishonmay qo'ydi.

en: 'I'll try it when I go home,' she thought to herself, 'the next time I'm a little late for dinner.' 'It's time for you to answer now,' the Queen said, looking at her watch: 'open your mouth a LITTLE wider when you speak, and always say your Majesty.' 'I only wanted to see what the garden was like, your Majesty—' 'That's right,' said the Queen, patting her on the head, which Alice didn't like at all, 'though, when you say garden,—I'VE seen gardens, compared with which this would be a wilderness.' Alice didn't dare to argue the point, but went on: '—and I thought I'd try and find my way to the top of that hill—' 'When you say hill,' the Queen interrupted, '_I_ could show you hills, in comparison with which you'd call that a valley.' 'No, I shouldn't,' said Alice, surprised into contradicting her at last: 'a hill CAN'T be a valley, you know.
uz: O'z uyimga borganimda sinab ko'raman, - deb o'yladi u o'ziga. Keyin kechki ovqatga biroz kech qolganimda, - deb javob berish vaqti keldi. Bu endi, deb aytdi Qirolicha, soatlariga qarab: Siz gapirganingizda og'zingizni biroz kengroq oching va har doim Mening Oliyligim deb ayting. Men faqat bog'ning qanday bo'lishini ko'rmoqchiman, Oliyligingiz deb o'yladi. Bu to'g'ri, deb aytdi Qirolicha, boshini tatib, Alicega yoqmadi. Agar siz bog', deb aytganda, Men bog'larni ko'rdim, bu yovvoyilik bo'ladi, deb aytasiz.

en: That would be nonsense—' The Red Queen shook her head, 'You may call it nonsense if you like,' she said, 'but I'VE heard nonsense, compared with which that would be as sensible as a dictionary!' Alice curtseyed again, as she was afraid from the Queen's tone that she was a LITTLE offended: and they walked on in silence till they got to the top of the little hill.
uz: Qizil Kraliça boshini silkitdi: Agar xohlasangiz, bu gapni da'vo deb atashingiz mumkin, - dedi u, - lekin men bu so'zlarni eshitganman, shunga qaraganda bu so'zlamagina oqilona bo'ladi! - deb aytdi Aliza yana qo'rqib, kraliçaning ozgina xafa bo'lgan tonidan qo'rqqanida.

en: For some minutes Alice stood without speaking, looking out in all directions over the country—and a most curious country it was.
uz: Bir necha daqiqa davomida Alisa so'zsiz turib, mamlakatning barcha tomonlarini ko'rib turdi va bu juda qiziqarli mamlakat edi.

en: There were a number of tiny little brooks running straight across it from side to side, and the ground between was divided up into squares by a number of little green hedges, that reached from brook to brook.
uz: Uning yonidan-yonida bir qator kichkina oqlar oqib o'tadi va ularning orasidagi yer bir qator kichik yashil o'rmonlar tomonidan kvadratlarga bo'linadi, ular oqdan oqgacha ketadi.

en: 'I declare it's marked out just like a large chessboard!' Alice said at last.
uz: Men uni katta shaxmat plakatini o'rab olganimni bildiraman! - dedi Ailis nihoyat.

en: 'There ought to be some men moving about somewhere —and so there are!' She added in a tone of delight, and her heart began to beat quick with excitement as she went on.
uz: Bir joyda erkaklar harakatlanishi kerak, shunday bo'lishi kerak! - dedi u quvonch bilan qo'shimcha qilib, yuragi shodlik bilan tezda urishga tushdi.

en: 'It's a great huge game of chess that's being played—all over the world—if this IS the world at all, you know.
uz: Bu butun dunyo bo'ylab o'ynaydigan juda katta shaxmat o'yinidir.

en: How I WISH I was one of them!
uz: Men ulardan biri bo'lishni juda istayman!

en: wouldn't mind being a Pawn, if only I might join—though of course I should LIKE to be a Queen, best.' She glanced rather shyly at the real Queen as she said this, but her companion only smiled pleasantly, and said, 'That's easily managed.
uz: Pawn bo'lishga xalaqit bermasdim, agar men ham qo'shilishsam, lekin albatta men QIROLON bo'lishni yaxshi ko'raman, eng yaxshisi.U buni aytayotganda real Qirolonga juda uyalgancha qarab qo'ydi, ammo uning hamkori faqat yoqimli tabassum qilib: Bu osonlikcha hal qilinadi.

en: You can be the White Queen's Pawn, if you like, as Lily's too young to play; and you're in the Second Square to begin with: when you get to the Eighth Square you'll be a Queen —' Just at this moment, somehow or other, they began to run.
uz: Agar xohlasangiz, siz Oq Qirolning Pawn bo'lishingiz mumkin, chunki Lili o'ynash uchun juda yosh; va siz ikkinchi maydonda boshlang: sakkizinchi maydonga yetganingizda siz Qirol bo'lasiz.

en: Alice never could quite make out, in thinking it over afterwards, how it was that they began: all she remembers is, that they were running hand in hand, and the Queen went so fast that it was all she could do to keep up with her: and still the Queen kept crying 'Faster!
uz: Alice buni keyinchalik o'ylab ko'rgach, ular qanday boshlashganini hech qachon aniqlay olmagan: faqatgina ular qo'l-qo'l bilan yugurishganini eslaydi, Qirolicha esa shunchalik tez o'tib ketdiki, uni qo'llab-quvvatlashga qodir bo'lgan hamma narsasi bor edi.

en: Faster!' but Alice felt she COULD NOT go faster, though she had not breath left to say so.
uz: Tezroq! - deb aytdi, lekin Alice shuni his qildiki, u tezroq borolmaydi, ammo o'sha paytgacha nafas olmagan edi.

en: The most curious part of the thing was, that the trees and the other things round them never changed their places at all: however fast they went, they never seemed to pass anything.
uz: Bularning eng qiziqarli qismi shundaki, daraxtlar va atrofidagi narsalar hech qachon o'z joylarini o'zgartirmagan: ular qanchalik tez yursalar ham, hech qachon hech narsa o'tmayotgandek ko'rinardi.

en: 'I wonder if all the things move along with us?' thought poor puzzled Alice.
uz: Mening o'ylaymanki, barchasi biz bilan birga harakatlanadimi? - deb o'yladi kambag'al Alice.

en: And the Queen seemed to guess her thoughts, for she cried, 'Faster!
uz: Qirolicha o'z fikrlarini tasavvur qilgan bo'lib tuyuladi, chunki u: Shoshilinch!

en: Don't try to talk!' Not that Alice had any idea of doing THAT.
uz: So'zlashga urinma! - deb o'ylamagan Alice bu haqda hech qanday tasavvurga ega emas edi.

en: She felt as if she would never be able to talk again, she was getting so much out of breath: and still the Queen cried 'Faster!
uz: O'zini boshqa hech qachon gapira olmaydigan bo'lib his qildi, nafasidan tushib qoldi: ammo Qirolicha: Ozgina!

en: Faster!' and dragged her along.
uz: Tezroq! - deb, qizni olib ketdi.

en: 'Are we nearly there?' Alice managed to pant out at last.
uz: O'sha yerga yaqin keldikmi? - deb so'raganida, Alisa nihoyat o'zini tashlab ketishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: 'Nearly there!' the Queen repeated.
uz: Qirolicha yana aytdi: O'shanda yo'q!

en: 'Why, we passed it ten minutes ago!
uz: Biz buni o'n daqiqa oldin o'tkazdik!

en: Faster!' And they ran on for a time in silence, with the wind whistling in Alice's ears, and almost blowing her hair off her head, she fancied.
uz: Tezroq! - deb o'ylashdi va ular bir muncha vaqt sukutdan yugurib ketishdi, shamol Ailisning quloqlarida pishirib, sochlarini taxminan sochlari bilan o'chirib yubordi, deb o'yladi.

en: Now!' cried the Queen.
uz: Endi! - deb qichqirdi Qirolicha.

en: Faster!' And they went so fast that at last they seemed to skim through the air, hardly touching the ground with their feet, till suddenly, just as Alice was getting quite exhausted, they stopped, and she found herself sitting on the ground, breathless and giddy.
uz: Ular shunchalik tez borishdiki, nihoyat ular havo orqali o'zlarini ko'targan, oyoqlari yerga tegmay, to to'satdan, xuddi Aliz charchagan paytda to'xtashdi va u o'zini yerga o'tirib qolgan, nafassiz va ko'ngilsiz ko'rindi.

en: The Queen propped her up against a tree, and said kindly, 'You may rest a little now.' Alice looked round her in great surprise.
uz: Qirolicha uni daraxtga tikib, mehribonlik ila: Siz endi biroz dam olishingiz mumkin, - dedi.

en: 'Why, I do believe we've been under this tree the whole time!
uz: Menga ishonamanki, biz butun vaqt davomida bu daraxt ostida bo'lganmiz!

en: Everything's just as it was!'
uz: Hamma narsa avvalgidek bo'ldi!

en: 'Of course it is,' said the Queen, 'what would you have it?' 'Well, in OUR country,' said Alice, still panting a little, 'you'd generally get to somewhere else—if you ran very fast for a long time, as we've been doing.' 'A slow sort of country!' said the Queen.
uz: - Albatta, - dedi Qirolicha, - nima iste'mol qilasiz? - O'Z mamlakatimizda, - dedi Alisa, hali ham biroz nafas olib, - agar biz kabi uzoq vaqt tezda yugurgan bo'lsangiz, odatda boshqa joyga borasiz.

en: 'Now, HERE, you see, it takes all the running YOU can do, to keep in the same place.
uz: HOL, siz ko'ryapsiz, bir xil joyda qolish uchun siz qila oladigan barcha yugurish kerak.

en: If you want to get somewhere else, you must run at least twice as fast as that!' 'I'd rather not try, please!' said Alice.
uz: Agar boshqa joyga bormoqchi bo'lsangiz, undan kamida ikki baravar tezroq yugurishingiz kerak! - Men harakat qilmaslikni afzal ko'raman, iltimos! - dedi Alice.

en: 'I'm quite content to stay here —only I AM so hot and thirsty!' 'I know what YOU'D like!' the Queen said good-naturedly, taking a little box out of her pocket.
uz: Men bu yerda qolishdan mamnunman, faqat men juda issiq va chanqoqman! - deb aytdi Qirolicha yaxshilik bilan, pokidan kichik bir quti chiqarib.

en: 'Have a biscuit?' Alice thought it would not be civil to say 'No,' though it wasn't at all what she wanted.
uz: Sening keksaning bormi? - deb o'ylagan Alice Yo'q deb aytish xushmuomala bo'lmasligini his qildi, ammo bu uning xohishi emas edi.

en: So she took it, and ate it as well as she could: and it was VERY dry; and she thought she had never been so nearly choked in all her life.
uz: Shunda u uni olib, imkon qadar yaxshi ovqatlandi va u juda quruq edi va o'zi hech qachon o'z hayotida bunday bo'shashgan bo'lmaganini his qildi.

en: 'While you're refreshing yourself,' said the Queen, 'I'll just take the measurements.' And she took a ribbon out of her pocket, marked in inches, and began measuring the ground, and sticking little pegs in here and there.
uz: Siz o'zingizni ta'minlayotganda, - dedi Qirolicha, men o'lchovlarni o'tayman, - deb so'radi va o'z qopqosidan o'lchamiga o'rnatilgan lentani olib, yerga o'lchamiga kirdi va u erda-u erda kichik pichoqlar qo'yib qo'ydi.

en: 'At the end of two yards,' she said, putting in a peg to mark the distance, 'I shall give you your directions—have another biscuit?' 'No, thank you,' said Alice: 'one's QUITE enough!' 'Thirst quenched, I hope?' said the Queen.
uz: Keli metrdan so'ng, dedi u, masofani belgilash uchun bir to'plam qo'yib, Senga yo'l-yo'riq beraman yana bir keksa bormi? - Yo'q, rahmat, dedi Alisa: Birinchi to'g'ri! - deb aytdi.

en: Alice did not know what to say to this, but luckily the Queen did not wait for an answer, but went on.
uz: Alice bunga qanday javob berish kerakligini bilmadi, lekin xotini baxtga ko'ra javobni kutmadi, balki davom etdi.

en: 'At the end of THREE yards I shall repeat them—for fear of your forgetting them.
uz: ÜZ metrdan so'ng ularni takrorlayman, chunki siz ularni unutishingizdan qo'rqaman.

en: At then end of FOUR, I shall say good-bye.
uz: To'rtning oxirida men salom aytaman.

en: And at then end of FIVE, I shall go!' She had got all the pegs put in by this time, and Alice looked on with great interest as she returned to the tree, and then began slowly walking down the row.
uz: Beshning oxiriga kelib, men ketaman! - deb o'ylaganida, u o'sha paytga qadar barcha to'g'rilarni o'rnatgan edi va Alice daraxtga qaytib borayotganini katta qiziqish bilan ko'rdi va keyin sekin-sekin qatorni bosib o'tishni boshladi.

en: At the two-yard peg she faced round, and said, 'A pawn goes two squares in its first move, you know.
uz: Ikki metrlik bo'limda o'z yuziga qarab, shunday dedi: Paxon o'zining birinchi harakatida ikki kvadratga o'tadi.

en: So you'll go VERY quickly through the Third Square—by railway, I should think—and you'll find yourself in the Fourth Square in no time.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz uchinchi kvadratdan tezda temir yo'ldan o'tasiz, deb o'ylayman va o'zingizni to'rtinchi kvadratga tezda topasiz.

en: Well, THAT square belongs to Tweedledum and Tweedledee—the Fifth is mostly water—the Sixth belongs to Humpty Dumpty—But you make no remark?'
uz: O'ShIShINCHI maydoni asosan suvga to'g'ri keladi, oltinchisi esa Humpty Dumptyga to'g'ri keladi, lekin siz hech qanday fikr bildirmayapsizmi?

en: 'I—I didn't know I had to make one—just then,' Alice faltered out.
uz: O'sha paytda bir tanani yaratishim kerakligini bilmasdim, - deb o'ylaydi Ailis.

en: 'You SHOULD have said,' 'It's extremely kind of you to tell me all this—however, we'll suppose it said—the Seventh Square is all forest—however, one of the Knights will show you the way—and in the Eighth Square we shall be Queens together, and it's all feasting and fun!' Alice got up and curtseyed, and sat down again.
uz: Siz aytishingiz kerak edi, man uchun bularning barchasini aytish juda mehribonlikdir, ammo, biz yettinchi maydon butunlay o'rmon deb aytilganini tasavvur qilamiz, ammo, shoirlardan biri sizga yo'l ko'rsatadi va sakkizinchi maydonda biz birgalikda quynas bo'lamiz, va bu hamma narsa ziyofat va zavq bilan sodir bo'ladi! - deb aytdi.

en: At the next peg the Queen turned again, and this time she said, 'Speak in French when you can't think of the English for a thing — turn out your toes as you walk—and remember who you are!' She did not wait for Alice to curtsey this time, but walked on quickly to the next peg, where she turned for a moment to say 'good-bye,' and then hurried on to the last.
uz: Keyingi bo'limda kraliça yana o'girilib, bu safar shunday dedi: Ingliz tilini o'ylab ko'rmaganda fransuzcha gapiring, yurganingizda barmoqlaringizni ko'tarib, kim ekaningizni eslang! U bu safar Alisaning o'zini qo'zg'atishini kutmadi, balki tezda keyingi bo'limga o'tdi, u yerda bir zumga qarab, xudojo'y deb aytdi va so'ng oxirgi bo'limga bordi.

en: How it happened, Alice never knew, but exactly as she came to the last peg, she was gone.
uz: Qanday qilib sodir bo'lganini Alice hech qachon bilmagan, lekin o'zining so'nggi o'yinida u yo'qolgan.

en: Whether she vanished into the air, or whether she ran quickly into the wood ('and she CAN run very fast!' thought Alice), there was no way of guessing, but she was gone, and Alice began to remember that she was a Pawn, and that it would soon be time for her to move.
uz: U havoga ko'tarildi yoki o'rmonga tezda yugurdi (U juda tez yugurishi mumkin! - deb o'yladi Alisa), buni tasavvur qilishning iloji yo'q edi, lekin u yo'qolgan edi va Alisa o'zining Pawn ekanligini va tez orada uning harakatlanishga vaqti kelganini eslay boshladi.

en: 'It's something very like learning geography,' thought Alice, as she stood on tiptoe in hopes of being able to see a little further.
uz: Bu geografiyani o'rganishga o'xshaydi, - deb o'yladi Ailis, biroz uzoqroq ko'rish umidi bilan oyoq boshiga turardi.

en: 'Principal rivers— there ARE none.
uz: Buyuk daryolar yo'q.

en: Principal mountains—I'm on the only one, but I don't think it's got any name.
uz: Asosiy tog'larMen faqat bitta tog'da yashayman, lekin uning hech qanday nomi bo'lmagan deb o'ylayman.

en: Principal towns—why, what ARE those creatures, making honey down there?
uz: Nima uchun, u yerda o'simliklarni o'rab olib, o'simliklarni o'rab olishadi?

en: They can't be bees— nobody ever saw bees a mile off, you know—' and for some time she stood silent, watching one of them that was bustling about among the flowers, poking its proboscis into them, 'just as if it was a regular bee,' thought Alice.
uz: Ular asalari bo'lishi mumkin emas, hech kim asalarini bir mil uzoqlikda ko'rmagan, bilasiz, deb aytdi va u bir muncha vaqt davomida sukut saqlab, ular orasidan biri gullar o'rtasida harakatlanayotganini ko'rib turardi, ularga o'z qo'llarini tikib, o'zi oddiy asali kabi, deb o'yladi Alice.

en: However, this was anything but a regular bee: in fact it was an elephant—as Alice soon found out, though the idea quite took her breath away at first.
uz: Biroq, bu odatdagi arndan tashqari hamma narsa edi: aslida u fil edi, deb o'yladi Alicen, ammo bu fikr boshida uni hayajonga soladi.

en: 'And what enormous flowers they must be!' was her next idea.
uz: Keyingi g'oya: Ular qanday ulkan gullar bo'lishi kerak!

en: 'Something like cottages with the roofs taken off, and stalks put to them—and what quantities of honey they must make!
uz: Ularda toshlar qo'yilgan, toshlar qo'yilgan va qancha bal ishlab chiqarishi kerak!

en: I think I'll go down and—no, I won't JUST yet,' she went on, checking herself just as she was beginning to run down the hill, and trying to find some excuse for turning shy so suddenly.
uz: O'ylaymanki, pastga tushaman va yo'q, hozircha yo'q, - deb davom etdi u, toshni pastga tushishni boshlaganida o'zini tekshirib ko'rib, birdan uyatchan bo'lib qolish uchun biron bir uzr izlashga harakat qildi.

en: 'It'll never do to go down among them without a good long branch to brush them away— and what fun it'll be when they ask me how I like my walk.
uz: Ular orasida yaxshi uzoq shoxsiz pastga tushish hech qachon yaxshi bo'lmaydi va ular mendan yurishni qanday yoqtirganimni so'rashganda qanchalik zavqlanadi.

en: I shall say — Oh, I like it well enough—' (here came the favourite little toss of the head), 'only it was so dusty and hot, and the elephants did tease so!' 'I think I'll go down the other way,' she said after a pause: 'and perhaps I may visit the elephants later on.
uz: Men aytaman: Oh, menga juda yoqadi (bu erda eng sevimli bosh tashlash) , faqat u juda changli va issiq edi, fillar esa shunday urishardi! Men boshqa yo'ldan tushaman deb o'ylayman, dedi u to'xtatishdan so'ng: va ehtimol keyinchalik fillarni ko'rib chiqaman.

en: Besides, I do so want to get into the Third Square!'
uz: Bundan tashqari, Men uchinchi maydonga kirishni juda xohlayman!

en: So with this excuse she ran down the hill and jumped over the first of the six little brooks.
uz: Shunday qilib, u bu bahona yordamida tepalikdan pastga yugurib, olti ko'chadan birinchi bo'lib sakrab o'tdi.

en: * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * 'Tickets, please!' said the Guard, putting his head in at the window.
uz: * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * Biletlar, iltimos! - dedi qo'riqchi, boshini oynada qo'yib.

en: In a moment everybody was holding out a ticket: they were about the same size as the people, and quite seemed to fill the carriage.
uz: Bir zumda hamma chipta ko'tarib turardi: ular odamlarning o'lchamiga teng edilar va vagonni to'ldirishdi.

en: Show your ticket, child!' the Guard went on, looking angrily at Alice.
uz: Chiptaingizni ko'rsating, bola! - dedi qo'riqchi Alicega g'azab bilan qarab.

en: And a great many voices all said together ('like the chorus of a song,' thought Alice), 'Don't keep him waiting, child!
uz: Va ko'plab ovozlar birgalikda (qor qo'shig'i kabi, deb o'yladi Alisa), Uni kutishga majbur qilma, bola!

en: Why, his time is worth a thousand pounds a minute!' 'I'm afraid I haven't got one,' Alice said in a frightened tone: 'there wasn't a ticket-office where I came from.' And again the chorus of voices went on.
uz: Uning vaqti bir daqiqada ming funt pulga arziydi! - deb qo'rqqan Alice: Men kelgan joyda biletxona yo'q edi, - deb aytdi.

en: 'There wasn't room for one where she came from.
uz: U kelgan joyda uning uchun joy yo'q edi.

en: The land there is worth a thousand pounds an inch!' 'Don't make excuses,' said the Guard: 'you should have bought one from the engine-driver.' And once more the chorus of voices went on with 'The man that drives the engine.
uz: U yerning qiymati bir santimetrga ming funt bo'ladi! - dedi qo'riqchi: Agar siz birorta bahona topa olmasangiz, siz mashinani haydovchiga sotib olishingiz kerak edi, - dedi.

en: Why, the smoke alone is worth a thousand pounds a puff!' Alice thought to herself, 'Then there's no use in speaking.' The voices didn't join in this time, as she hadn't spoken, but to her great surprise, they all THOUGHT in chorus (I hope you understand what THINKING IN CHORUS means—for I must confess that _I_ don't), 'Better say nothing at all.
uz: O'zicha, tutun har bir puf uchun ming funt pulga teng! - deb o'yladi Alisa o'ziga: Shuning uchun gapirishning foydasi yo'q, - deb o'yladi.O'sha payt ovozlar qo'shilmadi, chunki u gapirmagan edi, lekin uning katta ajablanishiga ko'ra, ular hammasi chorusda o'ylashdi (Ushbu chorusda o'ylash nimani anglatishini tushunishingizni umid qilaman, chunki men buni tan olsam kerak), O'zim hech narsa aytmasligim yaxshiroq.

en: Language is worth a thousand pounds a word!' 'I shall dream about a thousand pounds tonight, I know I shall!' thought Alice.
uz: Til har bir so'z ming funtga arziydi! - deb o'yladi Alisa.

en: All this time the Guard was looking at her, first through a telescope, then through a microscope, and then through an opera- glass.
uz: Bu vaqt davomida qo'riqchi uni birinchi navbatda teleskop orqali, so'ngra mikroskop orqali, so'ngra opera shisha orqali ko'rib turardi.

en: At last he said, 'You're travelling the wrong way,' and shut up the window and went away.
uz: Nihoyat u: Siz noto'g'ri yo'ldan ketyapsiz, - dedi va darsni yopib, ketib ketdi.

en: 'So young a child,' said the gentleman sitting opposite to her (he was dressed in white paper), 'ought to know which way she's going, even if she doesn't know her own name!' A Goat, that was sitting next to the gentleman in white, shut his eyes and said in a loud voice, 'She ought to know her way to the
uz: O'sha qadar yosh bola, dedi uning qarshisida o'tirgan erkak (u oq qog'oz kiygan edi), o'zining o'z ismini bilmasa ham, qaysi yo'ldan borayotganini bilishi kerak! - deb aytdi oq kiyimli erkakning yonida o'tirgan echki ko'zlarini yopib, baland ovoz bilan: O'zi o'z yo'lini bilishi kerak.

en: ticket-office, even if she doesn't know her alphabet!' There was a Beetle sitting next to the Goat (it was a very queer carriage-full of passengers altogether), and, as the rule seemed to be that they should all speak in turn, HE went on with 'She'll have to go back from here as luggage!' Alice couldn't see who was sitting beyond the Beetle, but a hoarse voice spoke next.
uz: O'z alifbosini bilmasa-da, ofis-ofisda! - deb gapirganida, Kechkining yonida bir qaroq o'tirgan edi (bu juda g'ayritabiiy yo'lovchilarga to'la vagon edi) va, qoidaga ko'ra, ularning hammasi bir-birlari bilan navbatma-ket gapirishlari kerak edi, U davom etib: U bu yerdan bagaj sifatida qaytishi kerak! - deb aytdi.

en: 'Change engines—' it said, and was obliged to leave off.
uz: Motorlarni o'zgartir deb aytdi va u to'xtatishga majbur bo'ldi.

en: 'It sounds like a horse,' Alice thought to herself.
uz: Bu otga o'xshaydi, - deb o'yladi Alisa o'ziga.

en: And an extremely small voice, close to her ear, said, 'You might make a joke on that— something about horse and hoarse, you know.' Then a very gentle voice in the distance said, 'She must be labelled Lass, with care, you know—' And after that other voices went on (What a number of people there are in the carriage!' thought Alice), saying, 'She must go by post, as she's got a head on her—' 'She must be sent as a message by the telegraph—' 'She must draw the train herself the rest of the way—' and so on.
uz: Va quloqlariga yaqin bo'lgan juda kichik bir ovoz: Bu bilan tash va tash to'g'risida o'ylashingiz mumkin, - dedi. Keyin uzoqdagi juda mehribon ovoz: O'ziga Lass, ehtiyotkorlik bilan deb belgi qo'yilishi kerak, - dedi. Keyin boshqa ovozlar davom etdi (Alis o'yladi: Arabada qancha odamlar bor?), U pochta orqali borishi kerak, chunki uning boshi uning ustida U telegraf orqali xabar sifatida yuborilishi kerak U o'zi yo'lning qolgan qismini o'zi chizishi kerak va hokazo.

en: But the gentleman dressed in white paper leaned forwards and whispered in her ear, 'Never mind what they all say, my dear, but take a return-ticket every time the train stops.' 'Indeed I shan't!' Alice said rather impatiently.
uz: Ammo oq qog'oz kiygan yigit oldinga qarab, uning quloqlariga shovqin qilib dedi: Barchasi nima deyishidan qat'iy nazar, azizim, lekin har safar poezd to'xtab qolganda qaytish chiptasini oling. - Ha, yo'q! - dedi Alisa juda sabrsizlik bilan.

en: 'I don't belong to this railway journey at all—I was in a wood just now —and I wish I could get back there.' 'You might make a joke on THAT,' said the little voice close to her ear: 'something about you WOULD if you could, you know.' 'Don't tease so,' said Alice, looking about in vain to see where the voice came from; 'if you're so anxious to have a joke made, why don't you make one yourself?' The little voice sighed deeply: it was VERY unhappy, evidently, and Alice would have said something pitying to comfort it, 'If it would only sigh like other people!' she thought.
uz: Men bu temir yo'lga umuman tegishli emasmanMen o'rmonda edim va o'sha yerga qaytib borishni xohlardim. Sening O'

en: But this was such a wonderfully small sigh, that she wouldn't have heard it at all, if it hadn't come QUITE close to her ear.
uz: Ammo bu shunchalik chiroyli kichik nafas ediki, agar u quloqlariga juda yaqin kelmaganida, u hech qachon uni eshitmagan bo'lardi.

en: The consequence of this was that it tickled her ear very much, and quite took off her thoughts from the unhappiness of the poor little creature.
uz: Buning natijasi shundaki, bu uning quloqlarini juda qizg'inlashtirdi va kamtarin kichkina yaratilishning baxtsizligidan fikrlarini kesib qo'ydi.

en: 'I know you are a friend, the little voice went on; 'a dear friend, and an old friend.
uz: Sening do'st ekanligingni bilaman, - dedi o'sha kichik ovoz, qizig'i do'st va eski do'st.

en: And you won't hurt me, though I AM an insect.' 'What kind of insect?' Alice inquired a little anxiously.
uz: Men hasharot bo'lsam ham, menga zarar etkazmaysiz. - Qanday hasharot? - deb so'radi Alice biroz tashvishlanib.

en: What she really wanted to know was, whether it could sting or not, but she thought this wouldn't be quite a civil question to ask.
uz: U bilmoqchi bo'lgan narsa, bu og'ir bo'lishi mumkinmi yoki yo'qmi edi, lekin u bu savolni berish uchun o'zi uchun murabbiy savol emas deb o'ylagan.

en: 'What, then you don't—' the little voice began, when it was drowned by a shrill scream from the engine, and everybody jumped up in alarm, Alice among the rest.
uz: Nima, nima, nima qilmayapsan? - deb boshlandi kichik ovoz, u mashinadan kelgan qichqiriq bilan cho'kkanida va hamma qo'rqinchga to'lib, o'zlariga qo'shilib ketdi, qolganlar orasida Alice ham bor edi.

en: The Horse, who had put his head out of the window, quietly drew it in and said, 'It's only a brook we have to jump over.' Everybody seemed satisfied with this, though Alice felt a little nervous at the idea of trains jumping at all.
uz: Boshini oynadan chiqarib olgan Atni xotirjamlik bilan olib kirdi va: Bu faqat bir daryo bo'lib o'tishi kerak, - dedi. - Hammasi bunga mamnun bo'lib ko'rinardi, lekin Alice poezdlar o'tishi haqida biroz xavotirlangan edi.

en: 'However, it'll take us into the Fourth Square, that's some comfort!' she said to herself.
uz: U o'zicha: Hamma, bu bizni to'rtinchi maydonga olib boradi, bu bizga tasalli beradi! - deb aytdi.

en: In another moment she felt the carriage rise straight up into the air, and in her fright she caught at the thing nearest to her hand, which happened to be the Goat's beard.
uz: Boshqa bir daqiqada u aravachani havoga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ko'targanini his qildi va qo'rqib qo'liga eng yaqin bo'lgan narsani, ya'ni echki soqolini qo'lga oldi.

en: * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * But the beard seemed to melt away as she touched it, and she found herself sitting quietly under a tree—while the Gnat (for that was the insect she had been talking to) was balancing itself on a twig just over her head, and fanning her with its wings.
uz: * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * Ammo u cho'qqanda soqol erib ketayotganga o'xshaydi va u o'zini bir daraxt ostida xotirjam o'tirgan holda topadi, o'sha paytda G'arq (bu u gapirgan hasharot edi) o'zini boshining ustida bo'lgan bo'g'a ustida muvozanat qilib, uni qanotlari bilan o'rab-o'rab o'tiradi.

en: It certainly was a VERY large Gnat: 'about the size of a chicken,' Alice thought.
uz: Bu, albatta, juda katta G'IRAT: Tuvushning o'lchamida, deb o'yladi Alisa.

en: Still, she couldn't feel nervous with it, after they had been talking together so long.
uz: Biroq, ular uzoq vaqtdan beri suhbatlashganidan so'ng, u bu haqda o'zini tashvishlanmasdi.

en: '—then you don't like all insects?' the Gnat went on, as quietly as if nothing had happened.
uz: Senga barcha hasharotlar yoqmaydi-ku? - deb so'ragan G'oyib, hech narsa bo'lmaganidek, sekinlik bilan davom etdi.

en: 'I like them when they can talk,' Alice said.
uz: Menga ular gapira olganda yoqadi, - dedi Ailis.

en: 'None of them ever talk, where _I_ come from.' 'What sort of insects do you rejoice in, where YOU come from?' the Gnat inquired.
uz: Ularning hech biri hech qachon gapirmaydi, men qayerdan kelganman. Siz qanday hasharotlar bilan quvonasiz, siz qayerdan kelgansiz? deb so'radi G'arq.

en: 'I don't REJOICE in insects at all,' Alice explained, 'because I'm rather afraid of them—at least the large kinds.
uz: Men hasharotlarga hech qachon quvonmayman, - deb tushuntirdi Alisa, chunki men ulardan qo'rqaman - hech bo'lmaganda katta turlardan.

en: But I can tell you the names of some of them.' 'Of course they answer to their names?' the Gnat remarked carelessly.
uz: Ammo ba'zilarining ismlarini aytib bersam bo'ladi. Agar ular o'z ismlariga javob berishsa, albatta? - dedi G'arib beparvolik bilan.

en: 'I never knew them do it.' 'What's the use of their having names the Gnat said, 'if they won't answer to them?' 'No use to THEM,' said Alice; 'but it's useful to the people who name them, I suppose.
uz: Men buni hech qachon bilmagan edim. Agar ular ularga javob bermasalar, ularning ismlari nima uchun kerak? - dedi G'ayrat. - Agar ular ularga javob bermasalar, ularga nima foyda? - dedi Alisa. - Agar ular bu ismlarni qo'ygan odamlarga foyda keltiradi, deb o'ylayman.

en: If not, why do things have names at all?' 'I can't say,' the Gnat replied.
uz: Agar yo'q bo'lsa, nima uchun narsalarning ismlari bor? - deb so'radi. - Men aytolmayman, - deb javob berdi Gnat.

en: 'Further on, in the wood down there, they've got no names—however, go on with your list of insects: you're wasting time.' 'Well, there's the Horse-fly,' Alice began, counting off the names on her fingers.
uz: O'shanda, o'rmonlarda ularning ismlari yo'q, lekin hasharotlar ro'yxatini o'qing: vaqtingizni o'tkazmayapsiz, - deb boshladi Alisa.

en: 'All right,' said the Gnat: 'half way up that bush, you'll see a Rocking-horse-fly, if you look.
uz: To'g'ri, dedi qo'zg'oqchi: o'sha butaga yarim yo'l borganda, agar ko'rsangiz, qo'rqinchli ot-uchuqni ko'rasiz.

en: It's made entirely of wood, and gets about by swinging itself from branch to branch.' 'What does it live on?' Alice asked, with great curiosity.
uz: U butunlay yog'ochdan yasalgan va o'zini shoxdan shoxga o'zgartirgan holda harakatlanadi. U nimaga tirik? - deb so'radi Alice katta qiziqish bilan.

en: 'Sap and sawdust,' said the Gnat.
uz: Sabon va sergak, - dedi Gnat.

en: 'Go on with the list.' Alice looked up at the Rocking-horse-fly with great interest, and made up her mind that it must have been just repainted, it looked so bright and sticky; and then she went on.
uz: Lista bilan davom eting. Alisa ko'z o'ngida ko'tarib turgan Rocking-horse-flyni katta qiziqish bilan ko'rib, u shunchaki qayta bo'yilgan bo'lishi kerakligini, juda yorqin va yopishqoq ko'rinishi kerakligini o'yladi va keyin davom etdi.

en: 'And there's the Dragon-fly.' 'Look on the branch above your head,' said the Gnat, 'and there you'll find a snap-dragon-fly.
uz: O'zingizning boshingizdan yuqori bo'lgan sho'rga qarang, - dedi qo'zg'oqchi, - va u erda siz chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli o't topasiz.

en: Its body is made of plum-pudding, its wings of holly-leaves, and its head is a raisin burning in brandy.' 'And what does it live on?' 'Frumenty and mince pie,' the Gnat replied; 'and it makes its nest in a Christmas box.' 'And then there's the Butterfly,' Alice went on, after she had taken a good look at the insect with its head on fire, and had thought to herself, 'I wonder if that's the reason insects are so fond of flying into candles—because they want to turn into Snap-dragon-flies!' 'Crawling at your feet,' said the Gnat (Alice drew her feet back in some alarm), 'you may observe a Bread-and-Butterfly.
uz: Uning tanasi plum puddingdan, qanotlari holli-barglardan, boshi esa brendi bilan yonayotgan uzumdan yasalgan.' Va u nimaga tayanadi? - deb javob berdi Gnat; va u o'z yuzini Rojdestvo qutisida o'ynaydi. - So'ngra Butterfly bor, deb davom etdi Alice, boshini olovda tutgan hasharotga diqqat bilan qaraganidan so'ng, o'z-o'ziga shunday deb o'yladi: Men bu hasharotlar shamollarga uchib o'tishni shunchalik yaxshi ko'rishining sababi bo'ladimi deb o'ylayman, chunki ular Snap-dragon-moshilarga aylanishadi! - dedi Gnat.

en: Its wings are thin slices of Bread-and-butter, its body is a crust, and its head is a lump of sugar.' 'And what does IT live on?' 'Weak tea with cream in it.' A new difficulty came into Alice's head.
uz: Uning qanotlari non va yog'ochdan yasalgan ince bo'laklar, tanasi qurt, boshini esa qandoq shakar. - U nimaga tayanadi? - Karmli, kremli choy. - Alice boshida yangi qiyinchilik paydo bo'ldi.

en: 'Supposing it couldn't find any?' she suggested.
uz: Agar u hech qanday topolmasa? - deb aytdi u.

en: 'Then it would die, of course.' 'But that must happen very often,' Alice remarked thoughtfully.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa, albatta, o'ladi, - deb o'ylaydi Ailis. Ammo bu juda tez-tez sodir bo'lishi kerak.

en: 'It always happens,' said the Gnat.
uz: Bu har doim sodir bo'ladi, dedi Gnat.

en: After this, Alice was silent for a minute or two, pondering.
uz: Bundan so'ng, Alisa bir yoki ikki daqiqacha sukut saqlashdi va o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: The Gnat amused itself meanwhile by humming round and round her head: at last it settled again and remarked, 'I suppose you don't want to lose your name?' 'No, indeed,' Alice said, a little anxiously.
uz: Shu paytning o'zida G'arqov o'zini mashg'ul qilib, boshini to'ldirib yurdi: nihoyat, u yana o'tirib, Sening ismingni yo'qotmoqchi emassanmi? deb so'radi. Yo'q, albatta, - dedi Alisa biroz tashvishlanib.

en: 'And yet I don't know,' the Gnat went on in a careless tone: 'only think how convenient it would be if you could manage to go home without it!
uz: Agar bilmasam ham, - dedi Gnat beparvo ton bilan davom etib: Agar sen bu yo'lsiz uyga borishga muvaffaq bo'lsang, qanchalik qulay bo'lishini o'ylab ko'ring!

en: For instance, if the governess wanted to call you to your lessons, she would call out come here—, and there she would have to leave off, because there wouldn't be any name for her to call, and of course you wouldn't have to go, you know.' 'That would never do, I'm sure,' said Alice: 'the governess would never think of excusing me lessons for that.
uz: Misol uchun, agar o'qituvchi sizni darsingizga chaqirmoqchi bo'lsa, u: Bu yerga kel deb qo'shib qo'yardi va u erda to'xtatishi kerak bo'lardi, chunki uning chaqirishi uchun hech qanday ism bo'lmasdi va albatta siz ketishingiz shart emas edi.

en: If she couldn't remember my name, she'd call me Miss! as the servants do.' 'Well.
uz: Agar u ismimni eslay olmasa, xizmatkorlar kabi meni Miss! deb chaqirdi.

en: if she said Miss, and didn't say anything more,' the Gnat remarked, 'of course you'd miss your lessons.
uz: Agar u Miss, deb aytsa va boshqa hech narsa aytmasa, albatta, sinflaringizni o'tkazib yuborasiz.

en: I wish YOU had made it.' 'Why do you wish _I_ had made it?' Alice asked.
uz: Nima uchun siz men uni yaratgan bo'lardim deb o'ylaysiz? - deb so'radi Alice.

en: 'It's a very bad one.' But the Gnat only sighed deeply, while two large tears came rolling down its cheeks.
uz: Bu juda yomon narsa, - deb aytdi u. Ammo Gnat faqat chuqur nafas oldi, ikkita katta ko'z yoshlari uning yig'inlariga tushib ketdi.

en: 'You shouldn't make jokes,' Alice said, 'if it makes you so unhappy.' Then came another of those melancholy little sighs, and this time the poor Gnat really seemed to have sighed itself away, for, when Alice looked up, there was nothing whatever to be seen on the twig, and, as she was getting quite chilly with sitting still so long, she got up and walked on.
uz: O'zingni baxtsiz qilsang, o'yin-kulgi qilmasang kerak, - dedi Alisa. - So'ngra yana bir o'sha melanxolis kichik nafas keldi va bu safar kambag'al Gnat o'zini tashlab ketibdi, chunki Alisa ko'z ko'targanida, bo'g'ida hech narsa ko'rinmadi va uzoq vaqt o'tirganidan so'ng juda sovuq bo'lib qolganidan so'ng u turib ketdi va davom etdi.

en: She very soon came to an open field, with a wood on the other side of it: it looked much darker than the last wood, and Alice felt a LITTLE timid about going into it.
uz: Tez orada u ochiq maydonga keldi, uning boshqa tomoniga yogʻoch bor edi: u oʻtgan yogʻochdan ancha qorongʻi koʻrinardi va Aliza unga kirishdan bir oz qoʻrqqan edi.

en: However, on second thoughts, she made up her mind to go on: 'for I certainly won't go BACK,' she thought to herself, and this was the only way to the Eighth Square.
uz: Biroq, o'ylab ko'rgach, u davom etishni qaror qildi: Men albatta qaytib bormayman, deb o'yladi u o'zi, va bu sakkizinchi maydonga borishning yagona yo'li edi.

en: 'This must be the wood, she said thoughtfully to herself, 'where things have no names.
uz: Bu o'simlik bo'lishi kerak, - deb o'ziga o'yladi u, - bu yerda narsalarning ismlari yo'q.

en: I wonder what'll become of MY name when I
uz: O'zimni o'ylab ko'ramanki, men o'zimni o'ldirganimda, ismim qanday bo'ladi?

en: I shouldn't like to lose it at all—because they'd have to give me another, and it would be almost certain to be an ugly one.
uz: Hech qachon uni yo'qotishni istamayman, chunki ular menga yana birini berishlari kerak bo'ladi va u deyarli chindan ham yomon bo'lishi mumkin.

en: But then the fun would be trying to find the creature that had got my old name!
uz: Ammo o'shanda mening eski ismimni olgan mavjudotni topishga harakat qilish qiziqarli bo'lardi!

en: That's just like the advertisements, you know, when people lose dogs—ANSWERS TO THE NAME OF 'DASH:' HAD ON A BRASS COLLAR—just fancy calling everything you met Alice, till one of them answered!
uz: Bu reklamalarga o'xshaydi, bilasizmi, odamlar itlarni yo'qotgandaDASHNING NAMISIGA JAVBORLAR: Bars kollasida o'tirganmanSiz uchratgan har bir kishini Alice deb atab, ulardan biri javob bermaguncha o'zingizni o'ylab ko'ring!

en: Only they wouldn't answer at all, if they were wise.' She was rambling on in this way when she reached the wood: it looked very cool and shady.
uz: Faqat dono bo'lsalar, ular hech qachon javob bermas edilar. U daraxtga yetib borganda, bu yo'ldan yuribdi: u juda sovuq va soyalarsiz ko'rinardi.

en: 'Well, at any rate it's a great comfort,' she said as she stepped under the trees, 'after being so hot, to get into the—into WHAT?' she went on, rather surprised at not being able to think of the word.
uz: U daraxtlar ostiga qadam bosganida: Agar shunday issiq bo'lgan bo'lsangiz ham, nimaga kirishingiz katta tasalli beradi? - dedi.

en: 'I mean to get under the—under the—under THIS, you know!' putting her hand on the trunk of the tree.
uz: Mening fikrim shuki, bu daraxtning ostiga qo'lini qo'yib, uning ostiga tushishim kerak.

en: 'What DOES it call itself, I wonder?
uz: O'Zidan nima deb so'ragan, deb o'ylayman.

en: I do believe it's got no name—why, to be sure it hasn't!' She stood silent for a minute, thinking: then she suddenly began again.
uz: U bir daqiqa sukut saqlashdi va o'ylagan: keyin u to'satdan yana boshlandi.

en: 'Then it really HAS happened, after all!
uz: Keyin bu haqiqatan ham sodir bo'ldi!

en: I WILL remember, if I can!
uz: Agar iloji bo'lsa, eslayman!

en: I'm determined to do it!' But being determined didn't help much, and all she could say, after a great deal of puzzling, was, 'L, I KNOW it begins with L!' Just then a Fawn came wandering by: it looked at Alice with its large gentle eyes, but didn't seem at all frightened.
uz: Men uni bajarishga qat'iy qaror qildim! - deb aytdi, ammo qat'iy qaror ko'p yordam bermadi va u juda ko'p g'alati so'zlardan so'ng: L, men bilaman, bu L bilan boshlanadi! - deb aytdi. O'shanda bir Fawn o'tib keldi: u Alicega o'zining katta, mehribon ko'zlari bilan qaradi, ammo umuman qo'rqmagan.

en: Here then!' Alice said, as she held out her hand and tried to stroke it; but it only started back a little, and then stood looking at her again.
uz: Mana shunday! - dedi Alisa qo'lini uzatib, uni tiyishga harakat qildi; lekin u faqat biroz qaytadan boshlandi va keyin yana unga qarab turdi.

en: 'What do you call yourself?' the Fawn said at last.
uz: O'zingizni nima deb ataysiz? - deb so'radi Faun oxir-oqibat.

en: Such a soft sweet voice it had!
uz: O'sha o'rindagi o'sha yumshoq va shirin ovoz!

en: 'I wish I knew!' thought poor Alice.
uz: Agar bilgan bo'lardim! - deb o'yladi kambag'al Alice.

en: She answered, rather sadly, 'Nothing, just now.' 'Think again,' it said: 'that won't do.' Alice thought, but nothing came of it.
uz: U juda xafa bo'lib: Bir oz o'ylab ko'ring, - deb javob berdi.

en: 'Please, would you tell me what YOU call yourself?' she said timidly.
uz: Xullas, o'zingni nima deb atayotganingni aytasanmi? - dedi u qo'rqmasdan.

en: 'I think that might help a little.' 'I'll tell you, if you'll move a little further on,' the Fawn said.
uz: Men o'ylaymanki, bu biroz yordam berishi mumkin. - Men sizga aytaman, agar siz biroz ko'proq harakat qilsangiz, dedi Fawn.

en: 'I can't remember here.' So they walked on together through the wood, Alice with her arms clasped lovingly round the soft neck of the Fawn, till they came out
uz: Men bu yerda eslay olmayman, - deb aytdi u. Shunday qilib, ular o'rmonda o'zlari bilan yurishdi, Aliza qo'llarini mehribonlik bilan Faunning yumshatli bo'yni atrofida bog'lab, ular tashqariga chiqmaguncha, o'zlariga yaqinlashdilar.

en: into another open field, and here the Fawn gave a sudden bound into the air, and shook itself free from Alice's arms.
uz: Boshqa ochiq maydonchaga kirib, bu yerda Fawn to'satdan havoga qo'shilib, o'zini Alisaning qo'llaridan ozod qildi.

en: 'I'm a Fawn!' it cried out in a voice of delight, 'and, dear me!
uz: Men Fawnman! - deb hayqirdi u quvonch bilan, va, mening azizim!

en: you're a human child!' A sudden look of alarm came into its beautiful brown eyes, and in another moment it had darted away at full speed.
uz: Sen inson bolasan! - deb qo'rqinchli ko'zlariga to'satdan qo'rqinch tushdi va yana bir daqiqada u to'la tezlikda o'tib ketdi.

en: Alice stood looking after it, almost ready to cry with vexation at having lost her dear little fellow-traveller so suddenly.
uz: Alice uni kuzatib turardi va o'zining sevimli sayohatdoshini shu paytdan boshlab yo'qotganidan xafa bo'lib yig'lashga tayyor edi.

en: 'However, I know my name now.' she said, 'that's SOME comfort.
uz: Hamma, hozir ismimni bilaman, - dedi u, bu bir oz tasalli beradi.

en: Alice—Alice—I won't forget it again.
uz: AliceAliceMen buni yana unutmayman.

en: And now, which of these finger-posts ought I to follow, I wonder?' It was not a very difficult question to answer, as there was only one road through the wood, and the two finger-posts both pointed along it.
uz: Endi men bu barmoqlarning qaysi biriga amal qilishim kerak, deb o'ylaymanmi? - deb so'ragan savolga javob berish qiyin emas edi, chunki o'rmon orqali faqat bitta yo'l bor edi va ikkita barmoqning barmoqlari bu yo'l bo'ylab ko'rsatilgan edi.

en: 'I'll settle it,' Alice said to herself, 'when the road divides and they point different ways.' But this did not seem likely to happen.
uz: Men buni hal qilaman, - deb o'yladi Alisa o'ziga, yo'l bo'lib ketganda va ular turli yo'llarni ko'rsatganda.

en: She went on and on, a long way, but wherever the road divided there were sure to be two finger- posts pointing the same way, one marked 'TO TWEEDLEDUM'S HOUSE' and the other 'TO THE HOUSE OF TWEEDLEDEE.' 'I do believe,' said Alice at last, 'that they live in the same house!
uz: U uzoq yo'lni davom ettirgan, ammo yo'l qayerda bo'lsa ham, u erda bir xil yo'lni ko'rsatadigan ikkita barmoq ustunlari bor edi, biri TWEEDLEDUM HOUSE va ikkinchisi TWEEDLEDEE HOUSE deb yozilgan edi.

en: I wonder I never thought of that before—But I can't stay there long.
uz: O'ylaymanki, men bundan oldin hech qachon bu haqda o'ylamaganman, lekin uzoq vaqt o'sha yerda qololmayman.

en: I'll just call and say how d'you do? and ask them the way out of the wood.
uz: Men shunchaki qo'ng'iroq qilib: Sizlar qanday? deb so'rayman va o'rmondan chiqish yo'lini so'rayman.

en: If I could only get to the Eighth Square before it gets dark!' So she wandered on, talking to herself as she went, till, on turning a sharp corner, she came upon two fat little men, so suddenly that she could not help starting back, but in another moment she recovered herself, feeling sure that they must be.
uz: Kechqurun sakkizinchi maydonga borishim mumkin bo'lsa-da! - deb so'raganida, u o'zi bilan gaplashib yuribdi va o'zini o'zi o'zi bilan o'tkazdi, hatto o'tkir burchakni o'zgartirganida, ikki semiz yigitni uchratib qoldi, to'satdan yana boshlashdan bosh tortmadi, ammo boshqa bir daqiqada o'zini tikladi va ular bo'lishi kerakligiga ishonch hosil qildi.

en: Cඐඉ඘ගඍක 4 Tඟඍඍඌඔඍඌඝඕ ඉඖඌ Tඟඍඍඌඔඍඌඍඍ They were standing under a tree, each with an arm round the other's neck, and Alice knew which was which in a moment, because one of them had 'DUM' embroidered on his collar, and the other 'DEE.' 'I suppose they've each got TWEEDLE round at the back of the collar,' she said to herself.
uz: Ular daraxt ostida, har biri o'z qo'li bilan bir-biriga bo'lgan bo'lak ostida turishgan edi va Alice bir lahzada qaysi biri qaysi biri ekanligini biladi, chunki ulardan biri bo'lakida DUM va boshqa DEE tikilgan edi.

en: They stood so still that she quite forgot they were alive, and she was just looking round to see if the word TWEEDLE was written at the back of each collar, when she was startled by a voice coming from the one marked 'DUM.' 'If you think we're wax-works,' he said, 'you ought to pay, you know.
uz: Ular shunchalik to'xtab turdilarki, u ularning tirikligini unutib qo'ydi va har bir qo'lqonchada TWEEDLE so'zi yozilgan-yo'qligini ko'rish uchun atrofini ko'rib turardi, ammo DUM belgisi bilan yozilgan ovozdan qo'rqqan edi.

en: Wax-works weren't made to be looked at for nothing, nohow!' 'Contrariwise,' added the one marked 'DEE,' 'if you think we're alive, you ought to speak.' 'I'm sure I'm very sorry,' was all Alice could say; for the words of the old song kept ringing through her head like the ticking of a clock, and she could hardly help saying them out loud:— 'Tweedledum and Tweedledee Agreed to have a battle; For Tweedledum said Tweedledee Had spoiled his nice new rattle.
uz: Makka, - dedi DEE, - agar biz tirikmiz deb o'ylasangiz, gapirishingiz kerak. - Men juda afsusman, - deb aytish mumkin bo'lgan yagona narsa Alice edi; chunki eski qo'shiqning so'zlari uning boshiga soat tikish kabi o'qishni davom ettirgan va u ularni baland ovoz bilan aytishdan bosh tortmagan: Tweedledum va Tweedledee jang qilishga rozi bo'ldilar; chunki Tweedledum Tweedledee yangi raftini buzganini aytdi.

en: Just then flew down a monstrous crow, As black as a tar-barrel; Which frightened both the heroes so, They quite forgot their quarrel.'
uz: O'shanda bir qahramon qo'rqoq, qora qora qora kabi, o'tib ketdi; bu ikki qahramonni ham shunday qo'rqitdiki, ular o'zlarining bahsini unutib qo'yishdi.

en: 'I know what you're thinking about,' said Tweedledum: 'but it isn't so, nohow.' 'Contrariwise,' continued Tweedledee, 'if it was so, it might be; and if it were so, it would be; but as it isn't, it ain't.
uz: Men siz nima haqida o'ylayotganingizni bilaman, dedi Tweedledum: lekin bu shunday emas, chunki. Makkalasida, deb davom etdi Tweedledee, agar shunday bo'lgan bo'lsa, bo'lishi mumkin; va agar shunday bo'lgan bo'lsa, bo'lishi mumkin; lekin bo'lmaganidek, bo'lmaydi.

en: That's logic.' 'I was thinking,' Alice said very politely, 'which is the best way out of this wood: it's getting so dark.
uz: Men o'ylayapman, - dedi Alisa xushmuomalalik bilan, - bu yog'ochdan chiqishning eng yaxshi yo'li nima: qorong'i bo'lib bormoqda.

en: Would you tell me, please?' But the little men only looked at each other and grinned.
uz: Iltimos, menga aytasizmi? - deb so'rashdi, lekin kichkina yigitlar faqat bir-birlariga ko'z tikib, tabassum qilishdi.

en: They looked so exactly like a couple of great schoolboys, that Alice couldn't help pointing her finger at Tweedledum, and saying 'First Boy!' 'Nohow!' Tweedledum cried out briskly, and shut his mouth up again with a snap.
uz: Ular juda yaxshi o'quvchilarga o'xshaydigan edilar, shu bois Alice o'z barmog'ini Tweedledumga ko'rsatib, First Boy! deb aytadi.

en: 'Next Boy!' said Alice, passing on to Tweedledee, though she felt quite certain he would only shout out 'Contrariwise!' and so he did.
uz: Next Boy! - dedi Ailis, Tweedledee-ga o'tadi, ammo u faqat Kontrariwise! deb qichqirishiga amin bo'ldi va u shunday qildi.

en: 'You've been wrong!' cried Tweedledum.
uz: Siz noto'g'ri yo'l tutgansiz! - dedi Tweedledum.

en: 'The first thing in a visit is to say How d'ye do? and shake hands!' And here the two brothers gave each other a hug, and then they held out the two hands that were free, to shake hands with her.
uz: Zohirlik chog'ida birinchi bo'lib: Sizlar qanday ekansiz? - deb so'rash va qo'l urish kerak! - deb aytish kerak edi va bu yerda ikki birodar bir-birlarini quchoqlab olishardi, so'ngra ular ayolga qo'l urish uchun erkin bo'lgan qo'llarini uzatishdi.

en: Alice did not like shaking hands with either of them first, for fear of hurting the other one's feelings; so, as the best way out of the difficulty, she took hold of both hands at once: the next moment they were dancing round in a ring.
uz: Alice boshida ikkalasi bilan qo'l urishni yoqtirmasdi, chunki u o'z hissasiga zarar yetkazishdan qo'rqardi; shuning uchun qiyinchilikdan xalos bo'lishning eng yaxshi usuli sifatida u bir vaqtning o'zida ikkala qo'lidan ham qo'lga oldi: keyingi daqiqada ular ringda raqs yurishardi.

en: This seemed quite natural (she remembered afterwards), and she was not even surprised to hear music playing: it seemed to come from the tree under which they were dancing, and it was done (as well as she could make it out) by the branches rubbing one across the other, like fiddles and fiddle- sticks.
uz: Bu juda tabiiy tuyulgan (o'shanda esladi) va musiqa o'ynashini eshitish unga hatto ajablantirmagan: u ular raqs qilayotgan daraxtning ostidan kelib chiqqan bo'lib ko'rinardi va bu bo'laklar bir-biriga o'tkirib, viyola va viyola tayoqlari kabi o'tkirib o'tirganidan (va u buni o'zi ham qila olgan) amalga oshdi.

en: 'But it certainly WAS funny,' (Alice said afterwards, when she was telling her sister the history of all this,) 'to find myself singing HERE WE GO ROUND THE MULBERRY BUSH. I don't know when I began it, but somehow I felt as if I'd been singing it a long long time!' The other two dancers were fat, and very soon out of breath.
uz: Ammo o'zimni HERE WE GO RUND THE MULBERRY BUSH qo'shig'ini kuylayotgan holda ko'rishim juda qiziqarli edi, - dedi (Alice keyinchalik opasiga bularning barchasini aytib berganda) Men buni qachon boshlaganimni bilmayman, lekin bir yo'l bilan o'zimni uzoq vaqtdan beri kuylayotganimdek his qildim! Boshqa ikki raqschi ham yumshoq va tez orada nafassiz edilar.

en: 'Four times round is enough for one dance,' Tweedledum panted out, and they left off dancing as suddenly as they had begun: the music stopped at the same moment.
uz: To'rt marta to'ldirish bir raqs uchun etarli, - dedi Tweedledum va ular raqsni boshlaganidek to'satdan to'xtatishdi: musiqa bir xil daqiqada to'xtadi.

en: Then they let go of Alice's hands, and stood looking at her for a minute: there was a rather awkward pause, as Alice didn't know how
uz: So'ngra ular Alisning qo'llarini qo'yib, bir daqiqa unga qarab turishdi: Alice qanday qilib harakat qilishni bilmagani sababli, biroz noqulay to'xtatish bo'ldi.

en: to begin a conversation with people she had just been dancing with.
uz: u yaqinda raqs qilgan odamlar bilan suhbat boshlash uchun.

en: 'It would never do to say How d'ye do? NOW,' she said to herself: 'we seem to have got beyond that, somehow!' 'I hope you're not much tired?' she said at last.
uz: O'ziga shunday dedi: Hndi, biz bundan ham ortig'iga yetib keldik, deb o'ylayman! - Umid qilamanki, siz juda charchagan emassiz? - dedi u oxir-oqibat.

en: And thank you VERY much for asking,' said Tweedledum.
uz: Va so'rashingiz uchun katta rahmat, - dedi Tweedledum.

en: 'So much obliged!' added Tweedledee.
uz: Ushbu qadar minnatdorman! deb qo'shib qo'ydi Tweedledee.

en: 'You like poetry?' 'Ye-es, pretty well—SOME poetry,' Alice said doubtfully.
uz: Senga she'r yoqadimi? - Ha, juda yaxshiBIR she'r yoqadi, - dedi Alisa shubhali so'zlar bilan.

en: 'Would you tell me which road leads out of the wood?' 'What shall I repeat to her?' said Tweedledee, looking round at Tweedledum with great solemn eyes, and not noticing Alice's question.
uz: Menga o'rmondan qaysi yo'l chiqishini aytasizmi? - deb so'radi Tweedledee, o'z ko'zlari bilan Tweedledumga qarab, Alisning savolini ko'rmay.

en: 'THE WALRUS AND THE CARPENTER is the longest,' Tweedledum replied, giving his brother an affectionate hug.
uz: The WALRUS AND THE CARPENTER eng uzoqdir, - deb javob berdi Tweedledum, ukasiga mehr-muhabbat bilan quchoq berdi.

en: Tweedledee began instantly: 'The sun was shining—' Here Alice ventured to interrupt him.
uz: Tweedledee darhol boshlandi:  Quyosh parlayotgandir Bu yerda Alisa uni to'xtatishga jur'at qildi.

en: 'If it's VERY long,' she said, as politely as she could, 'would you please tell me first which road—' Tweedledee smiled gently, and began again: 'The sun was shining on the sea, Shining with all his might: He did his very best to make The billows smooth and bright— And this was odd, because it was The middle of the night.
uz: Agar bu juda uzoq bo'lsa, dedi u, imkon qadar xushmuomala, ilgari menga qaysi yo'lni aytinglar, - deb so'radi Tweedledee yengillab tabassum qilib, yana boshlandi: Kosh dengizda parvarish qilardi, butun kuch-qudrat bilan parvarish qilardi: U to'lqinlarni sekin va yorqin qilish uchun qo'lidan kelganini qildi.

en: The moon was shining sulkily, Because she thought the sun Had got no business to be there After the day was done— It's very rude of him, she said, To come and spoil the fun! The sea was wet as wet could be, The sands were dry as dry.
uz: Oʻsha kun oʻtgandan keyin quyosh oʻsha yerda boʻlishiga hech qanday sabab yoʻq deb oʻylagani uchun oy qizgʻin shinamlik bilan parvarish qilardi, chunki u quyoshning oʻsha yerda boʻlishiga hech qanday ish qoʻymasligini his qilardi Uning oʻrnidan juda qoʻpol boʻldi, - dedi u. Oʻyinni buzish uchun kelishi kerak edi! deb aytdi.

en: You could not see a cloud, because No cloud was in the sky: No birds were flying over head— There were no birds to fly.
uz: Bulut ko'rinmas edi, chunki osmonda bulut yo'q edi: qushlar bosh ustida uchmasdi.

en: The Walrus and the Carpenter
uz: O'lchami va cho'g'irchi

en: Were walking close at hand; They wept like anything to see Such quantities of sand: If this were only cleared away, They said, it WOULD be grand! If seven maids with seven mops Swept it for half a year, Do you suppose, the Walrus said, That they could get it clear? I doubt it, said the Carpenter, And shed a bitter tear.
uz: Agar yetti qiz o'g'li yetti mop bilan uni yarim yil davomida to'ldirib yurganida, o'ylaysizmi? - deb so'ragan bo'lsa, Ular uni to'ldirib olishadi, deb o'ylaydi. Men bunga shubha qilaman, deb aytdi o'g'ir cho'g'i, va achchiq ko'z yoshini to'kdi.

en: O Oysters, come and walk with us! The Walrus did beseech.
uz: Tehyorlar, kelinglar, biz bilan yurib ketinglar! - deb yolvordi.

en: A pleasant walk, a pleasant talk, Along the briny beach: We cannot do with more than four, To give a hand to each. The eldest Oyster looked at him.
uz: Yaxshi yurish, yoqimli suhbat, tuzli plyaj bo'ylab: Biz to'rtdan ko'proq odam bilan shug'ullanolmaymiz, har bir kishiga qo'l beramiz.

en: But never a word he said: The eldest Oyster winked his eye, And shook his heavy head— Meaning to say he did not choose To leave the oyster-bed.
uz: Ammo u hech qachon bir so'z aytmadi: eng keksa Oyster ko'zini cho'kib, og'ir boshini shovqirdi Bu o'zi oyster yotoqidan ketishni tanlamaganini aytmoqchi emasligini anglatadi.

en: But four young oysters hurried up, All eager for the treat: Their coats were brushed, their faces washed, Their shoes were clean and neat— And this was odd, because, you know, They hadn't any feet.
uz: Ammo to'rtta yosh ostirga shoshilib keldilar, ularning barchasi mehribonlikka intilib: ularning kiyimlari yuvilgan, yuzlari yuvilgan, poyabzallari toza va bezak edi. Bu g'alati edi, chunki ularning oyoqlari yo'q edi.

en: Four other Oysters followed them, And yet another four; And thick and fast they came at last, And more, and more, and more— All hopping through the frothy waves, And scrambling to the shore.
uz: Ulardan keyin yana to'rtta ostirani, yana to'rtta ostirani kuzatib borishdi va nihoyat, qalin va tez kelib, ko'proq, ko'proq va ko'proq bo'ldilar. Ularning barchasi changli to'lqinlardan o'tib, qirg'oqqa qaytib borishdi.

en: The Walrus and the Carpenter Walked on a mile or so,
uz: Walrus va cho'g'irchi bir kilometr yoki undan ortiq yo'l bosib o'tdilar.

en: And then they rested on a rock Conveniently low: And all the little Oysters stood And waited in a row.
uz: So'ngra ular bir tosh ustida o'tirdilar.

en: The time has come, the Walrus said, To talk of many things: Of shoes—and ships—and sealing-wax— Of cabbages—and kings— And why the sea is boiling hot— And whether pigs have wings. But wait a bit, the Oysters cried, Before we have our chat; For some of us are out of breath, And all of us are fat! No hurry! said the Carpenter.
uz: Vaqt keldi, - deb aytdi O'rmon, ko'plab narsalar haqida gapirish: poyabzallar va kemalar, cho'g'lar va podshohlar haqida, dengiz qaynab issiq bo'lganining sababi, cho'chqalarning qanotlari bor-yo'qligi haqida.

en: They thanked him much for that.
uz: Ular bu uchun unga katta minnatdorchilik bildirishdi.

en: A loaf of bread, the Walrus said, Is what we chiefly need: Pepper and vinegar besides Are very good indeed— Now if you're ready Oysters dear, We can begin to feed. But not on us! the Oysters cried, Turning a little blue, After such kindness, that would be A dismal thing to do! The night is fine, the Walrus said Do you admire the view?
uz: Buning uchun bizga non kerak, - deb javob berdi marvarid. Bizga kerak bo'lgan asosiy narsa shuki, shisha va sirtoqdan tashqari juda yaxshi bo'ladi Endi tayyor bo'lsangiz, aziz marvaridlar, biz ovqatlanishni boshlashimiz mumkin.  Ammo bizga emas! deb baqirgan marvaridlar, biroz ko'k bo'lib, Ushbu kabi mehribonlikdan so'ng, bu juda dahshatli ish bo'ladi! deb javob berishdi. Kechasi yaxshi, deb aytdi marvarid: Ko'rinishga hayratlanasizmi?

en: It was so kind of you to come!
uz: Siz kelishingizdan juda mehribon bo'ldingiz!
