uz: Tush va roza U qizil gullarni olib kelsam, men bilan raqsga tushishini aytdi, - deb baqirdi yosh o'quvchi; - lekin butun bog'imda hech qanday qizil gul yo'q. - O'z yuvidan o'simlik daraxtidagi o'simlikdagi qorong'i o'simlik uni eshitdi, u varaqlardan ko'tarib, hayron qoldi.

en: “No red rose in all my garden!” he cried, and his beautiful eyes ﬁlled with tears.
uz: "Butun bog'imda qizil roza yo'q edi!" - deb yig'ladi u. Uning go'zal ko'zlari ko'z yoshlari bilan to'lib-toshdi.

en: “Ah, on what little things does happiness depend!
uz: Ah, baxtning qancha kichik narsalarga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin!

en: I have read all that the wise men have written, and all the secrets of philosophy are mine, yet for want of a red rose is my life made wretched.” “Here at last is a true lover,” said the Nightingale.
uz: Donolar yozgan har bir narsani o'qib chiqdim va falsafaning barcha sirlari meningdir, ammo qizil roza yetishmagani uchun hayotim ayanchli bo'ldi.  "Akhri haqiqiy sevganim bor", - deb aytdi Yovuz.

en: “Night after night have I sung of him, though I knew him not: night after night have I told his story to the stars, and now I see him.
uz: Kechasi-kechasi men uni tanimasam ham, u haqida kuylardim: kechasi-kechasi uning hikoyasini yulduzlarga aytib berardim va endi uni ko'raman.

en: His hair is dark as the hyacinth-blos- som, and his lips are red as the rose of his desire; but passion has made his face like pale ivory, and sorrow has set her seal upon his brow.” “The Prince gives a ball to-morrow night,” murmured the young Student, “and my love will be of the company.
uz: Uning sochlari yashaq qizil, og'izlari ham istaklarining rozi kabi qizil, lekin ishtiyoq uning yuzini o'ta bo'lak-bo'lak kabi qildi, qayg'u esa uning burchasiga muhr qo'ydi.Dastlab kechasi Prins balo o'tkazadi, - deb g'azablandi yosh Talaba, va mening sevgim kompaniyamda bo'ladi.

en: If I bring her a red rose she will dance with me till dawn.
uz: Agar unga qizil roza olib kelsam, u men bilan tonggacha raqs qiladi.

en: If I bring her a red rose, I shall hold her in my arms, and she will lean her head upon my shoulder, and her hand will be clasped in mine.
uz: Agar qizil roza olib kelsam, uni qo'limdan ushlab, boshini omonimga tiklaydi, qo'li esa mening qo'limga yopishib qoladi.

en: But there is no red rose in my garden, so I shall sit lonely, and she will pass me by.
uz: Ammo bog'imda qizil gul yo'q, shuning uchun men yolg'iz o'tiraman va u yonimdan o'tadi.

en: She will have no heed of me, and my heart will break.” “Here indeed is the true lover,” said the Nightingale.
uz: U menga e'tibor bermaydi va yuragim sindirib ketadi. "Haqiqatan ham, bu erda haqiqiy muhabbatkor bor", - deb aytdi Yovuz.

en: “What I sing of, he suffers—what is joy to me, to him is pain.
uz: Men qo'shiq kuylaganimda, u azob chekadi, men uchun bu quvonch, unga esa bu og'riq.

en: Surely Love is a wonderful thing.
uz: Darhaqiqat, sevgi ajoyib narsa.

en: It is more precious than emeralds, and dearer than ﬁne opals.
uz: U smaragdlardan ham qimmatbaho, yaxshi opallardan ham qimmatbaho.

en: Pearls and pomegranates cannot buy it, nor is it set forth in the marketplace.
uz: U mutilar va narvidan sotib olinmaydi, bozorda ham taqdim etilmaydi.

en: It may not be purchased of the merchants, nor can it be weighed out in the balance for gold.” “The musicians will sit in their gallery,” said the young Student, “and play upon their stringed instruments, and my love will dance to the sound of the harp and the violin.
uz: Uni savdogarlardan sotib olish mumkin emas, shuningdek, oltin bilan tenglamada o'lchash mumkin emas.Muziklar o'z galereyalarida o'tiradilar, dedi yosh Talaba,va o'z qo'shiqli asboblarida o'ynashadi, mening sevgim esa arfa va piyola tovushlariga raqs qiladi.

en: She will dance so lightly that her feet will not touch
uz: U shunchalik yengil raqs qiladiki, oyoqlari unga tegmaydi.

en: the ﬂoor, and the courtiers in their gay dresses will throng round her.
uz: Yerni, gey kiyim kiygan hovliqlar uning atrofida to'planib turadi.

en: But with me she will not dance, for I have no red rose to give her”; and he ﬂung himself down on the grass, and buried his face in his hands, and wept.
uz: Lekin u men bilan raqsga bormaydi, chunki unga beradigan qizil rozalarim yo'q, - dedi u o'zini o'tga tashlab, yuzini qo'llarida ko'mib yig'ladi.

en: “Why is he weeping?” asked a little Green Lizard, as he ran past him with his tail in the air.
uz: U nima uchun yig'layapti? - deb so'radi kichkina yashil tovuq, quyruqini havoga ko'targan holda uning yonidan o'tib yugurdi.

en: “Why, indeed?” said a Butterﬂy, who was ﬂuttering about after a sunbeam.
uz: Nima uchun, haqiqatan ham? - dedi quyosh nuridan orqaga qarab o'tirgan ko'pik.

en: “Why, indeed?” whispered a Daisy to his neighbour, in a soft, low voice.
uz: Nima uchun, haqiqatan ham? o'z qo'shnisiga Daisy so'zlab berdi, yumshak, past ovoz bilan.

en: “He is weeping for a red rose,” said the Nightingale.
uz: "U qizil roza uchun yig'layapti", - dedi Yolg'oq.

en: “For a red rose?” they cried; “how very ridiculous!” and the little Lizard, who was something of a cynic, laughed outright.
uz: Qizil roza uchun? - deb baqirdilar, - naqadar kulgili! - va kichkinagina qaroqchoq, biroz sinik bo'lgan, o'z ko'zidan-o'zi kuldi.

en: But the Nightingale understood the secret of the Student’s sorrow, and she sat silent in the oak-tree, and thought about the mystery of Love.
uz: Ammo kechqurun o'quvchi qayg'u sirini tushundi va u o'q daraxtida xotirjamlik bilan o'tirib, Sevgining sirini o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: Suddenly she spread her brown wings for ﬂight, and soared into the air.
uz: Toʻsatdan u oʻzining qalin qanotlarini koʻtarib, havoga koʻtardi.

en: She passed through the grove like a shadow, and like a shadow she sailed across the garden.
uz: U o'simliklardan soya kabi o'tib o'tdi va soya kabi bog'dan o'tdi.

en: In the centre of the grass-plot was standing a beautiful Rose-tree, and when she saw it she ﬂew over to it, and lit upon a spray.
uz: O't-o'tning o'rtasida go'zal bir gulzor daraxt turgan edi va uni ko'rganida u u yerga o'tirib, unga yonib, surtqazish ustiga yonib qo'ydi.

en: “Give me a red rose,” she cried, “and I will sing you my sweetest song.” But the Tree shook its head.
uz: Menga qizil roza bering, - deb baqirdi u, - va men sizga eng shirin qo'shiqlarimni kuylayman. - Lekin daraxt boshini silkitdi.

en: “My roses are white,” it answered; “as white as the foam of the sea, and whiter than the snow upon the mountain.
uz: - Mening gullarim oq, - deb javob berdi u, - dengiz cho'g'i kabi oq va tog'dagi qordan oqroq.

en: But go to my brother who grows round the old sun-dial, and perhaps he will give you what you want.” So the Nightingale ﬂew over to the Rose-tree that was growing round the old sun-dial.
uz: Ammo eski quyosh soatining atrofida o'sadigan akamning oldiga boring va ehtimol u sizga xohlaganingizni beradi. Shunday qilib, kechqurun eski quyosh soatining atrofida o'sib borayotgan roz daraxtga uchdi.

en: “My roses are yellow,” it answered; “as yellow as the hair of the mer- maiden who sits upon an amber throne, and yellower than the daffodil that blooms in the meadow before the mower comes with his scythe.
uz: "Mening gul gul gullarim", - deb javob berdi u, "bir yaltiroq taxtda o'tirgan qizning sochlari kabi sariq, cho'g'irni kesib oluvchi o'z qiliqini olib kelmasidan oldin cho'lda gullab o'tadigan narviddan sariqroq".

en: But go to my brother who grows beneath the Student’s window, and perhaps he will give you what you want.” So the Nightingale ﬂew over to the Rose-tree that was growing beneath the Student’s window.
uz: Ammo o'quvchi daraxti ostida o'sadigan akamning oldiga boring, ehtimol u sizga xohlaganingizni beradi. Shunday qilib, kechqurun o'quvchi daraxti ostida o'sib borayotgan gulzorga uchdi.

en: “My roses are red,” it answered, “as red as the feet of the dove, and red- der than the great fans of coral that wave and wave in the ocean-cavern.
uz: Mening gullarim qizil, deb javob berdi u, guvonga o'xshab qizil va okean g'orida to'sib-to'sib o'tiradigan korallning katta muxlislaridan qizilroq.

en: But the winter has chilled my veins, and the frost has nipped my buds, and the storm has broken my branches, and I shall have no roses at all this year.” “One red rose is all I want,” cried the Nightingale, “only one red rose!
uz: Ammo qish jonlarimni sovuq qilib qo'ydi, sovuq urug'larimni yutib qo'ydi, bo'ron shoxlarimni buzdi va bu yil rosalar bo'lmaydi.Men faqat bitta qizil roza istayman,Nightingale xitob qildi,Bor bir qizil roza!

en: Is there no way by which I can get it?” “There is away,” answered the Tree; “but it is so terrible that I dare not tell it to you.” “Tell it to me,” said the Nightingale, “I am not afraid.” “If you want a red rose,” said the Tree, “you must build it out of music by moonlight, and stain it with your own heart’s-blood.
uz: Uni olish uchun hech qanday yo'l yo'qmi?  U yo'q, - deb javob berdi Daraxt;  lekin bu shunchalik dahshatliki, men sizga aytishga jur'at qilmayman.  Menga ayt, deb aytdi Yovuz, Men qo'rqmayman.  Agar siz qizil gulni istasangiz, dedi Daraxt, siz uni oy nuri bilan musiqadan qurishingiz kerak, va uni o'zingizning yurak qoningiz bilan moylashingiz kerak.

en: You must sing to me with your breast against a thorn.
uz: Menga o'g'ir cho'g'ga qarshi ko'ngling bilan kuylashing kerak.

en: All night long you must sing to me, and the thorn must pierce your heart, and your life-blood must ﬂow into my veins, and become mine.” “Death is a great price to pay for a red rose,” cried the Nightingale, “and Life is very dear to all.
uz: Kecha bo'yi menga qo'shiq kuylashingiz kerak, tikan yuragingizni o'tkazib yuborishi kerak, hayot qoningiz mening damarlarimga oqib, mening o'zimga aylanishi kerak.O'lim - qizil gul uchun to'lash uchun katta narx, - deb hayqirdi Yovuz,Va hayot hamma uchun juda qadrli.

en: It is pleasant to sit in the green wood, and to watch the Sun in his chariot of gold, and the Moon in her chariot of pearl.
uz: Yashil daraxtda o'tirib, uning oltin aravalarida quyosh va marvarid aravalarida oyni kuzatish yoqimli.

en: Sweet is the scent of the hawthorn, and sweet are the bluebells that hide in the val- ley, and the heather that blows on the hill.
uz: O'g'irning hidlari shirin, vodiyda yashiringan ko'k qo'ylar va tog'da puflaydigan cho'g'lar ham shirin.

en: Yet Love is better than Life, and what is the heart of a bird compared to the heart of a man?” So she spread her brown wings for ﬂight, and soared into the air.
uz: Ammo sevgi hayotdan yaxshiroqdir va qushning yuragi inson yuragi bilan solishtirganda nima? Shunday qilib, u qo'rqinchli qanotlarini ko'tardi va havoga uchdi.

en: She swept over the garden like a shadow, and like a shadow she sailed through the grove.
uz: U bog'ni soya kabi o'rab oldi va soya kabi o't o't o't o't o't o't o't o't o't o't o't o'tadi.

en: The young Student was still lying on the grass, where she had left him, and the tears were not yet dry in his beautiful eyes.
uz: Yosh O'quvchi hali ham uni tashlagan joyida o'tda yotgan edi va uning go'zal ko'zlarida ko'z yoshlari hali qurmagan edi.

en: “Be happy,” cried the Nightingale, “be happy; you shall have your red rose.
uz: Baxtli bo'ling, Nightingale xitob qildi, Baxtli bo'ling, qizil rozalaringiz bo'ladi.

en: I will build it out of music by moonlight, and stain it with my own heart’s-blood.
uz: Men uni oy yorug'ligida musiqadan yarataman va uni o'z yuragim bilan to'ldiraman.

en: All that I ask of you in return is that you will be a true lover, for Love is wiser than Philosophy, though she is wise, and mightier than Power, though he is mighty.
uz: Sizdan faqatgina haqiqiy muhabbatkor bo'lishingizni so'rayman, chunki muhabbat falsafadan dono, u dono bo'lsa-da, dono va qudratdan kuchliroq.

en: Flame-coloured are his wings, and coloured like ﬂame is his body.
uz: Uning qanotlari olov rangida, tanasi esa olov rangida.

en: His lips are sweet as honey, and his breath is like frankincense.” The Student looked up from the grass, and listened, but he could not un- derstand what the Nightingale was saying to him, for he only knew the things that are written down in books.
uz: Uning og'izlari asal kabi shirin, nafaslari xushbo'y tutatqi kabi. Talaba o'tdan ko'tarib, tingladi, lekin u Yashak unga nima deyayotganini tushunolmadi, chunki u faqat kitoblarda yozilgan narsalarni bilardi.

en: But the Oak-tree understood, and felt sad, for he was very fond of the lit- tle Nightingale who had built her nest in his branches.
uz: Ammo Oak daraxtini tushunib, xafa bo'ldi, chunki u o'z shoxlarida o'z yuzini qurgan yoritilgan Nightingale-ga juda yoqardi.

en: “Sing me one last song,” he whispered; “I shall feel very lonely when you are gone.” So the Nightingale sang to the Oak-tree, and her voice was like water bubbling from a silver jar.
uz: Menga so'nggi bir qo'shiqni kuyla, u shov-shuv qildi;  Sen ketganingda men o'zimni juda yolg'iz his qilaman. Shunday qilib, Yashvonga Oak daraxtiga qo'shiq kuyladi va uning ovozi kumush idishdan qaynayotgan suv kabi edi.

en: When she had ﬁnished her song the Student got up, and pulled a note- book and a lead-pencil out of his pocket.
uz: U qo'shiqni tugatganida, Talaba o'rnidan turib, hisob daftarini va olovli qalamni kiyimidan chiqardi.

en: “She has form,” he said to himself, as he walked away through the grove —“that cannot be denied to her; but has she got feeling?
uz: U o'z-o'zidan so'radi: "O'sha ayolning shakli bor, u o'sha daraxtdan yurib ketayotganda, bu ayolga hech narsa inkor etilmaydi, lekin u his-tuyg'ularga ega bo'ladimi?

en: In fact, she is like most artists; she is all style, without any sincerity.
uz: Aslida, u ko'pgina san'atkorlar singari; u butunlay o'ziga xos, samimiyatsiz.

en: She would not sacriﬁce herself for others.
uz: U o'zini boshqalar uchun qurbon qilmasdi.

en: She thinks merely of music, and everybody knows that the arts are selﬁsh.
uz: U faqat musiqa haqida o'ylaydi va san'atlarning xudbin ekanligini hamma biladi.

en: Still, it must be admitted that she has some beautiful notes in her voice.
uz: Shunga qaramay, u o'z ovozidagi chiroyli notlarni o'z ichiga olganini tan olish kerak.

en: What a pity it is that they do not mean anything, or do any practical good.”  And he went into his room, and lay down on his little pallet-bed, and began to think of his love; and, after a time, he fell asleep.
uz: Bularning hech qanday ma'nosi yo'qligi juda achinarli. U o'z xonasiga kirib, o'zining kichkina pallet yotoqida o'tirdi va o'z sevgisi haqida o'ylay boshladi va vaqt o'tib uxladi.

en: And when the Moon shone in the heavens the Nightingale ﬂew to the Rose-tree, and set her breast against the thorn.
uz: Osmonda oy shoshganida, qushqo'l rosa daraxtga uchib, ko'ksi tikaning orqasida o'rnagan.

en: All night long she sang with her breast against the thorn, and the cold crystal Moon leaned down and lis- tened.
uz: U butun kecha o'z ko'kraklarini tikan ustiga qo'yib kuylagan va sovuq kristallli oy yerga tiklanib, o'zini ko'targan.

en: All night long she sang, and the thorn went deeper and deeper into her breast, and her life-blood ebbed away from her.
uz: U butun kecha kuylagan va tikan ko'kraklariga chuqurroq va chuqurroq kirib, hayot qonlari undan oqib ketdi.

en: She sang ﬁrst of the birth of love in the heart of a boy and a girl.
uz: U birinchi bo'lib o'g'il va qizning qalbida sevgi tug'ilishi haqida kuyladi.

en: And on the top-most spray of the Rose-tree there blossomed a marvellous rose, petal following petal, as song followed song.
uz: Va roza daraxtining yuqori qismida go'zal roza gullab o'tdi, qo'shiq qo'shiqdan keyin.

en: Pale was it, at ﬁrst, as the mist that hangs over the river—pale as the feet of the morning, and silver as the wings of the dawn.
uz: Boshida, daryo ustida so'lib turgan bulut kabi bo'lak edi, ertalabning oyoqlari kabi bo'lak va tongning qanotlari kabi kumush.

en: As the shadow of a rose in a mirror of silver, as the shadow of a rose in a water-pool, so was the rose that blossomed on the top- most spray of the Tree.
uz: Kumush ko'rinmasida rozaning soyasi, suv hovuzidagi rozaning soyasi kabi, daraxtning yuqori qismida gullab-yashgan roza ham shunday edi.

en: But the Tree cried to the Nightingale to press closer against the thorn.
uz: Ammo daraxt qorong'ichaga yaqinroq bo'lib, tikanni bosishga chaqirdi.

en: “Press closer, little Nightingale,” cried the Tree, “or the Day will come be- fore the rose is ﬁnished.” So the Nightingale pressed closer against the thorn, and louder and loud- er grew her song, for she sang of the birth of passion in the soul of a man and a maid.
uz: Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, kichkinag'im, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, Shuning balandroq va balandroq bo'lsin, chunki u bir erkak va bir ayolning ruhida tuyg'u tug'ilishi haqida qo'shib qo'ydi.

en: And a delicate ﬂush of pink came into the leaves of the rose, like the ﬂush in the face of the bridegroom when he kisses the lips of the bride.
uz: Roza barglariga rosa rangli qizil rang tushdi, u kelinning og'izlarini o'pganda kelinning yuzidagi qizil rangga o'xshaydi.

en: the thorn had not yet reached her heart, so the rose’s heart remained white, for only a Nightingale’s heart’s-blood can crimson the heart of a rose.
uz: Tikan hali uning qalbiga yetib kelmagan edi, shuning uchun gulning yuragi oq bo'lib qoldi, chunki faqat kechqurunning qoni bir gulning yuragini qizitishi mumkin.

en: And the Tree cried to the Nightingale to press closer against the thorn.
uz: O'simlik qushga yaqinroq bo'lib, tikanni bosishga chaqirdi.

en: “Press closer, little Nightingale,” cried the Tree, “or the Day will come be- fore the rose is ﬁnished.” So the Nightingale pressed closer against the thorn, and the thorn touched her heart, and a ﬁerce pang of pain shot through her.
uz: Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin, kichkinag'im,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,Shuning yaqinroq bo'lsin,

en: Bitter, bitter was the pain, and wilder and wilder grew her song, for she sang of the Love that is perfected by Death, of the Love that dies not in the tomb.
uz: Og'riq og'ir, og'ir edi va uning qo'shiqlari har doim o'sib borardi, chunki u o'lim bilan mukammallashtirilgan Sevgi, qabrda o'lmas Sevgi haqida qo'shiq kuylagan edi.

en: And the marvellous rose became crimson, like the rose of the eastern sky.
uz: Va ajoyib gul sharqiy osmondagi gulga o'xshaydigan qizil rangga aylandi.

en: Crimson was the girdle of petals, and crimson as a ruby was the heart.
uz: Qizil ko'krak - ko'kraklar quritmasi edi, qizil ko'krak - rubiy ko'krak yuragi edi.

en: But the Nightingale’s voice grew fainter, and her little wings began to beat, and a ﬁlm came over her eyes.
uz: Ammo kechqurunning ovozi susayib borardi va uning kichik qanotlari urishni boshladi va uning ko'zlari ustidan bir film ko'rindi.

en: Fainter and fainter grew her song, and she felt something choking her in her throat.
uz: Uning qo'shiqini ko'paytirgan Fainter va Fainter o'sdi va u bo'yniga biror narsa tushib qolganini his qildi.

en: Then she gave one last burst of music.
uz: So'ngra u yana bir marta musiqa bilan band bo'ldi.

en: The white Moon heard it, and she forgot the dawn, and lingered on in the sky.
uz: Oq oy buni eshitib, tongni unutib, osmonda qoldi.

en: The red rose heard it, and it trembled all over with ecstasy, and opened its petals to the cold morning air.
uz: Qizil gul buni eshitib, ekstazdan titrab, ko'kraklarini sovuq ertalabgi havoga ochdi.

en: Echo bore it to her purple cavern in the hills, and woke the sleeping shepherds from their dreams.
uz: Echo uni tog'larda o'zining bo'yoq ko'chasiga olib bordi va uxlayotgan cho'ponlarni tushlaridan uyg'otdi.

en: It ﬂoated through the reeds of the river, and they carried its message to the sea.
uz: U daryo qirg'og'i orasidan suzib o'tadi va ular o'z xabarini dengizga yetkazdilar.

en: “Look, look!” cried the Tree, “the rose is ﬁnished now”; but the Nightin- gale made no answer, for she was lying dead in the long grass, with the thorn in her heart.
uz: "Qarang, qarang!" - deb baqirgan Daraxt, "Roz endi tugagan", - deb aytdi, ammo Nightin-gaif hech qanday javob bermadi, chunki u yuragida tikanli, uzun o'tda o'lik yotgan edi.

en: And at noon the Student opened his window and looked out.
uz: Tush paytida Shogird o'z darvozasini ochib, tashqariga ko'rdi.

en: “Why, what a wonderful piece of luck!” he cried; “here is a red rose!
uz: Qani, naqadar ajoyib omad! - deb baqirdi u. - Mana, qizil roza!

en: I have never seen any rose like it in all my life.
uz: Hayotimda hech qachon bunday gul ko'rmaganman.

en: It is so beautiful that I am sure it has a long Latin name”; and he leaned down and plucked it.
uz: U shunchalik chiroyli bo'lganki, uning uzoq lotincha nomi borligiga aminman; u o'zini yerga tikib, uni o'rab oldi.

en: Then he put on his hat, and ran up to the Professor’s house with the rose in his hand.
uz: So'ngra u to'pini kiyib, qo'lida gulni olib, professorning uyiga yugurdi.

en: The daughter of the Professor was sitting in the doorway winding blue silk on a reel, and her little dog was lying at her feet.
uz: Professorning qizi eshikda ko'k rangli ipakni rulga o'rab o'tirgan edi va uning oyoqlari oldida uning itlari yotgan edi.

en: “You said that you would dance with me if I brought you a red rose,” cried the Student.
uz: Agar men sizga qizil roza olib kelsam, men bilan raqsga borishni aytding, - deb yig'ladi o'quvchi.

en: “Here is the reddest rose in all the world.
uz: Mana butun dunyodagi eng qizil roza.

en: You will wear it to-night next your heart, and as we dance together it will tell you how I love you.” But the girl frowned.
uz: Siz uni bugun kechqurun yuragingiz yonida kiyib turasiz va birga raqs yurganimizda bu sizga men sizni qanchalik yaxshi ko'ramanligini aytadi. Ammo qiz yuz o'girdi.

en: “I am afraid it will not go with my dress,” she answered; “and, besides, the Chamberlain’s nephew has sent me some real jewels, and everybody knows that jewels cost far more than ﬂowers.” “Well, upon my word, you are very ungrateful,” said the Student angrily; and he threw the rose into the street, where it fell into the gutter, and a cart- wheel went over it.
uz: Mening kiyimimga mos kelmaydi, deb qo'rqaman, - dedi u. - Bundan tashqari, Chamberlainning ne'ti menga haqiqiy zargarliklarni yubordi va har kim zargarliklarning gullardan ancha qimmatroq ekanligini biladi.Men aytganimcha, siz juda minnatdorchilik bildirmayapsiz, - dedi talaba g'azabda. - U rosani ko'lga tashladi, u cho'lga tushdi va arava velosiped uning ustidan o'tdi.

en: “Ungrateful!” said the girl.
uz: "Qizlar, shukr qilmanglar!" - dedi qiz.

en: “I tell you what, you are very rude; and, after all, who are you?
uz: Sizga nima deyman, siz juda qo'polsiz; va, oxir-oqibat, siz kimsiz?

en: Why, I don’t believe you have even got silver buckles to your shoes as the Chamberlain’s nephew has”; and she got up from her chair and went into the house.
uz: Ehtimol, siz ham Chamberlainning ne'ti kabi oyoq kiyimingizga kumush qiliqlarni qo'yib qo'ygan bo'lsangiz-da; u o'rindiqidan turib, uyga kirdi.

en: “What I a silly thing Love is,” said the Student as he walked away.
uz: Men sevgining ahmoqona narsasi ekanman, dedi o'quvchi, u ketayotganda.

en: “It is not half as useful as Logic, for it does not prove anything, and it is always telling one of things that are not going to happen, and making one believe things that are not true.
uz: U mantiqqa o'xshamaydi, chunki u hech narsani isbotlamaydi va har doim sodir bo'lmaydigan narsalarni aytib, haqiqat bo'lmagan narsalarni ishonishga undaydi.

en: In fact, it is quite unpractical, and, as in this age to be practical is everything, I shall go back to Philosophy and study Metaphysics.” So he returned to his room and pulled out a great dusty book, and began to read.
uz: Darhaqiqat, bu juda amaliy emas va, bu davrda amaliy bo'lish hamma narsa bo'lgani uchun, men falsafaga qaytib, metafizikaning fanini o'rganaman. Shunday qilib, u o'z xonasiga qaytib kelib, katta bug'doy kitobni olib chiqdi va o'qishni boshladi.

en: THE SELFISH GIANT Every afternoon, as they were coming from school, the children used to go and play in the Giant’s garden.
uz: O'ZINGIZNI O'ZGA QILISh HAQIM Har kuni kechqurun, maktabdan qaytib kelayotgan bolalar Giant bog'ida o'ynash uchun o'tishardi.

en: It was a large lovely garden, with soft green grass.
uz: Bu katta va chiroyli bog' edi, u yumshoq yashil o'tlar bilan o'ralgan edi.

en: Here and there over the grass stood beautiful ﬂowers like stars, and there were twelve peach- trees that in the spring-time broke out into delicate blossoms of pink and pearl, and in the autumn bore rich fruit.
uz: Bu yerda va u yerda o'tlar kabi go'zal gullar paydo bo'ldi va bahorda rosa va marvarid gullarga aylangan o'n ikki shark daraxtlari paytida boy meva berdi.

en: The birds sat on the trees and sang so sweetly that the children used to stop their games in order to listen to them.
uz: Qushlar daraxtlar ustida o'tirib, shunchalik shirin kuylashganki, bolalar ularni tinglash uchun o'yinlarini to'xtatishgan.

en: “How happy we are here!” they cried to each other.
uz: Bizlar bu yerda qanchalik baxtli ekanmiz! Ular bir-birlariga baqirdilar.

en: One day the Giant came back.
uz: Bir kuni Raqqos qaytib keldi.

en: He had been to visit his friend the Cornish ogre, and had stayed with him for seven years.
uz: U do'sti Korn ostasini ko'rish uchun borgan edi va u bilan yetti yil birga bo'lgan edi.

en: After the seven years were over he had said all that he had to say, for his conversation was limited, and he determined to return to his own castle.
uz: Yetti yil o'tgach, u aytadigan hamma narsani aytdi, chunki uning suhbatlari cheklangan edi va u o'z qal'asiga qaytishga qaror qildi.

en: When he arrived he saw the chil- dren playing in the garden.
uz: U yerga yetib kelganida, bog'da o'yin o'ynayotgan chill-drenni ko'rdi.

en: “What are you doing here?” he cried in a very gruff voice, and the chil- dren ran away.
uz: - Bu yerda nima qilyapsan? - deb qattiq baqirdi u, bola esa qochib ketdi.

en: “My own garden is my own garden,” said the Giant; “any one can under- stand that, and I will allow nobody to play in it but myself.”  So he built a high wall all round it, and put up a notice-board.
uz: O'z bog'im mening bog'im,  dedi ulkan odam; Har kim buni tushunishi mumkin, va men o'zimdan boshqa hech kimga u erda o'ynashga ruxsat bermayman. Shunday qilib, u atrofida baland devor qurdi va notishbord o'rnatdi.

en: TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED He was a very selﬁsh Giant.
uz: U juda xudbin ulkan shaxs edi.

en: The poor children had now nowhere to play.
uz: Endi kambag'al bolalar o'ynash uchun hech qanday joyga ega bo'lmadilar.

en: They tried to play on the road, but the road was very dusty and full of hard stones, and they did not like it.
uz: Ular yo'lda o'ynashga harakat qilishdi, lekin yo'l juda changli va qattiq toshlarga to'lib-toshgan va ularga yoqmadi.

en: They used to wander round the high wall when their lessons were over, and talk about the beautiful garden inside.
uz: Darslari tugaganida ular baland devor atrofida yurib, ichkaridagi go'zal bog' haqida gapirishardi.

en: “How happy we were there,” they said to each other.
uz: Ular bir-birlariga: "Biz u yerda qanchalik baxtli edik", - deyishdi.

en: Then the Spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds.
uz: Keyin Bahor keldi va butun mamlakatda kichkina gullar va kichik qushlar bor edi.

en: Only in the garden of the Selﬁsh Giant it was still winter.
uz: Faqat o'zboshimchalik bilan yirikning bog'ida hali qish edi.

en: The birds did not care to sing in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossom.
uz: Qushlar u yerda kuylashni istamadilar, chunki bolalar yo'q edi va daraxtlar gullashni unutib qo'ydi.

en: Once a beautiful ﬂower put its head out from the grass, but when it saw the notice-board it was so sorry for the children that it slipped back into the ground again, and went off to sleep.
uz: Bir marta go'zal gul o'z boshini o'tdan chiqardi, lekin o'sha ko'rsatkichni ko'rganida bolalarga shunchalik achindiki, yana yerga yiqildi va uxlashga ketdi.

en: The only people who were pleased were the Snow and the Frost.
uz: Faqatgina qar va muzdan xursand bo'lganlar bor edi.

en: “Spring has forgotten this garden,” they cried, “so we will live here all the year round.”  The Snow covered up the grass with her great white cloak, and the Frost painted all the trees silver.
uz: Bahor bu bog'ni unutdi,  ular baqirdilar,  shuning uchun biz yil davomida bu yerda yashaymiz. Qar katta oq ko'ylak bilan o'tlarni qopladi, sovuq esa daraxtlarning barchasini kumush rangga bo'yintirdi.

en: Then they invited the North Wind to stay with them, and he came.
uz: So'ngra ular Shimoliy shamolni o'zlari bilan qolishga taklif qilishdi va u keldi.

en: He was wrapped in furs, and he roared all day about the garden, and blew the chimney-pots down.
uz: U to'qimaga o'rab, butun kun bog' atrofida qichqirishardi va cho'mirli idishlarni puflashardi.

en: “This is a delightful spot,” he said, “we must ask the Hail on a visit.”  So the Hail came.
uz: Bu ajoyib joy, dedi u, Biz "Hayl"ni tashrif buyurganimizda so'rashimiz kerak. Shunday qilib, "Hayl" keldi.

en: Every day for three hours he rattled on the roof of the castle till he broke most of the slates, and then he ran round and round the garden as fast as he could go.
uz: Har kuni uch soat davomida qalʼaning tomida oʻtirib, koʻpgina pillalarni sindirib tashlaganidan soʻng, u bogʻning atrofida tezroq yugurib borardi.

en: He was dressed in grey, and his breath was like ice.
uz: U griq kiyim kiygan edi va uning nafaslari muz kabi edi.

en: “I cannot understand why the Spring is so late in coming,” said the Self- ish Giant, as he sat at the window and looked out at his cold white garden; “I hope there will be a change in the weather.” But the Spring never came, nor the Summer.
uz: Men bahorning nima uchun kechikib kelishini tushunolmayman, - dedi o'z-o'zini ko'rsatadigan ulkan o'g'il, o'zining sovuq oq bog'ini ko'rib, darvozasiga o'tiribdi; Men ob-havo o'zgarishini umid qilaman. Ammo bahor hech qachon kelmadi, yozgi ham kelmadi.

en: The Autumn gave golden fruit to every garden, but to the Giant’s garden she gave none.
uz: O'smir har bir bog'ga oltin meva berdi, ammo ulkan bog'ga hech qanday meva bermadi.

en: “He is too selﬁsh,” she said.
uz: "U juda xudbin", dedi u.

en: So it was always Winter there, and the North Wind, and the Hail, and the Frost, and the Snow danced about through the trees.
uz: Shunday qilib, u erda har doim qish bo'lgan va Shimoliy shamol, yomg'ir, sovuq va qor daraxtlar orasida raqsga tushardi.

en: One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music.
uz: Bir kuni ertalab ul o'z yotoqida uyg'onib, chiroyli musiqa eshitdi.

en: It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by.
uz: Bu uning quloqlariga shunchalik yoqimli tuyulganki, u o'tib ketayotgan Kingning musiqachilari bo'lishi kerak deb o'yladi.

en: It was really only a little linnet singing out- side his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his gar- den that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, o'z darvozasidan tashqariga kichkina bir linnet qo'shiq kuylagan edi, ammo u bog'ida qush qo'shiq kuylayotganini eshitganidan beri shunchalik vaqt o'tdiki, unga dunyodagi eng chiroyli musiqa tuyuldi.

en: Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement.
uz: Keyin esa yomg'ir uning boshi ustida raqs o'tkazishni to'xtatdi, Shimoliy shamol esa qichqirishni to'xtatdi va ochilgan qabrdan unga mazali xushbo'y tutatqi keldi.

en: “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.
uz: Men bahor nihoyat keldi deb o'ylayman,  dedi ulkan; va u o'z yotoqidan tushib, tashqariga ko'rdi.

en: He saw a most wonderful sight.
uz: U juda ajoyib ko'rinishni ko'rdi.

en: Through a little hole in the wall the chil- dren had crept in, and they were sitting in the branches of the trees.
uz: Childrenlar devordagi kichkina cho'g'idan kirib, daraxt shoxlarida o'tirgan edilar.

en: In every tree that he could see there was a little child.
uz: U ko'rgan har bir daraxtda kichkina bir bola bor edi.

en: And the trees were so glad to have the children back again that they had covered themselves with blossoms, and were waving their arms gently above the children’s heads.
uz: Daraxtlar bolalarni qaytarib olishdan shunchalik xursand bo'lishdiki, ular o'zlarini gullar bilan qoplab, qo'llarini bolalarning boshlari ustida yumshatishdi.

en: The birds were ﬂying about and twittering with delight, and the ﬂowers
uz: Qushlar o'z joylarida uchib, quvonch bilan tvitirlashar edilar, gullar esa quvonch bilan tvitirlashar edi.

en: were looking up through the green grass and laughing.
uz: yashil o'tlar o'rtasida ko'tarilib, kulishardi.

en: It was a lovely scene, only in one corner it was still winter.
uz: Bu chiroyli ko'rinish edi, faqat bir burchada hali qish edi.

en: It was the farthest corner of the garden, and in it was standing a little boy.
uz: U bogʻning eng uzoq burchagida edi va u yerda kichkina bir o'g'il turgan edi.

en: He was so small that he could not reach up to the branches of the tree, and he was wandering all round it, crying bitterly.
uz: U shunchalik kichkina ediki, daraxtning shoxlarigacha yetib borolmadi va u atrofida aylanib, achchiq-achchiq yig'lab yurardi.

en: The poor tree was still quite covered with frost and snow, and the North Wind was blowing and roaring above it.
uz: Yomon daraxt hali ham sovuq va qor bilan qoplangan edi va shimoliy shamol uning ustida shov-shuv qilib yurgan edi.

en: little boy,” said the Tree, and it bent its branches down as low as it could; but the boy was too tiny.
uz: "O'g'il", - dedi daraxt, shoxlarini imkon qadar pastga burib qo'ydi, lekin o'g'il juda kichkina edi.

en: And the Giant’s heart melted as he looked out.
uz: Ulug'ning yuragi uni ko'rib turganida erib ketdi.

en: “How selﬁsh I have been!” he said; “now I know why the Spring would not come here.
uz: Men qanchalik xudbin bo'lganman! - dedi u. - Endi men Bahor nega bu yerga kelmaganini bilaman.

en: I will put that poor little boy on the top of the tree, and then I will knock down the wall, and my garden shall be the children’s playground for ever and ever.”  He was really very sorry for what he had done.
uz: Oʻsha kambagʻal oʻgʻilchani daraxtning ustiga qoʻyib, devorni qulab tashlayman va bogʻim bolalar oʻyin maydoni boʻlib qoladi. U qilgan ishidan juda afsuslanardi.

en: So he crept downstairs and opened the front door quite softly, and went out into the garden.
uz: U pastga tushib, eshikni juda sekin ochib, bog'ga kirdi.

en: But when the children saw him they were so frightened that they all ran away, and the garden became winter again.
uz: Bolalar uni ko'rib, shunchalik qo'rqib ketishdiki, hammalari qochib ketishdi va bog' yana qishga aylandi.

en: Only the little boy did not run, for his eyes were so full of tears that he did not see the Gi- ant coming.
uz: Faqat kichkina o'g'il yugurmadi, chunki uning ko'zlari shunchalik ko'z yoshlari bilan to'lib-toshganki, ulkan jangovarning kelishini ko'rmadi.

en: And the Giant stole up behind him and took him gently in his hand, and put him up into the tree.
uz: Ulug' u kishining orqasidan o'rnashib, uni qo'lidan ushlab, daraxtga ko'tardi.

en: And the tree broke at once into blossom, and the birds came and sang on it, and the little boy stretched out his two arms and ﬂung them round the Giant’s neck, and kissed him.
uz: Daraxt darhol gullab-yashnab, qushlar kelib, unga qo'shiq kuylashdi, kichkina bola esa ikki qo'lini uzatdi va ularni ulkanning bo'yniga tashlab, o'pdi.

en: And the other children, when they saw that the Giant was not wicked any longer, came running back, and with them came the Spring.
uz: Qolgan bolalar esa ulkanning endi yovuz emasligini ko'rib, qaytib kelishdi va ular bilan birga Bahor keldi.

en: “It is your garden now, little children,” said the Giant, and he took a great axe and knocked down the wall.
uz: "Bu endi sizning bog'ingiz, bolalar", - dedi ulkan o'g'il va katta o'g'irni olib, devorni qulab yubordi.

en: And when the people were going to market at twelve o’clock they found the Giant playing with the children in the most beautiful garden they had ever seen.
uz: Va odamlar soat o'n ikkida bozorga ketayotganlarida, ulkanni ular ko'rgan eng chiroyli bog'da bolalar bilan o'ynashganini ko'rishdi.

en: All day long they played, and in the evening they came to the Giant to bid him good-bye.
uz: Ular kun bo'yi o'ynashdi va kechqurun ulkan odamga borib, undan xayrlashishdi.

en: “But where is your little companion?” he said: “the boy I put into the tree.”  The Giant loved him the best because he had kissed him.
uz: Ammo sizning kichkina hamkoringiz qayerda? - dedi u. - Men daraxtga qo'ygan o'g'lim. - Ulug' uni o'pgani uchun eng yaxshi ko'rgan.

en: “We don’t know,” answered the children; “he has gone away.” “You must tell him to be sure and come here to-morrow,” said the Giant.
uz: "Bila olmaymiz", - deb javob berishdi bolalar; "u ketib ketdi". - Siz unga shubhalanishini va ertaga bu yerga kelishini aytishingiz kerak, - dedi ulkan.

en: But the children said that they did not know where he lived, and had never seen him before; and the Giant felt very sad.
uz: Ammo bolalar uning qayerda yashayotganini bilmasligini va uni ilgari hech qachon ko'rmaganligini aytishdi va ulkan o'zidan juda xafa bo'ldi.

en: Every afternoon, when school was over, the children came and played with the Giant.
uz: Har kuni kechki payt maktabdan keyin bolalar kelib, ulkan bilan o'ynashardi.

en: But the little boy whom the Giant loved was never seen
uz: Ammo ulkanning sevgan kichkina o'g'li hech qachon ko'rilmagan.

en: The Giant was very kind to all the children, yet he longed for his ﬁrst little friend, and often spoke of him.
uz: U barcha bolalarga nisbatan juda mehribon bo'lgan, ammo u o'zining birinchi do'stini orzu qilardi va u haqida tez-tez gapirardi.

en: “How I would like to see him!” he used to say.
uz: "Men uni ko'rishni juda istayman!" - deyishardi u.

en: Years went over, and the Giant grew very old and feeble.
uz: Yillar o'tib ketdi va ul ul ul ul ul juda keksa va zaif bo'ldi.

en: He could not play about any more, so he sat in a huge armchair, and watched the children at their games, and admired his garden.
uz: U endi o'ynashdan to'xtamaydi, shuning uchun ulkan kursiga o'tirib, bolalarning o'yinlarini kuzatib, bog'ini hayratda qoldirdi.

en: “I have many beautiful ﬂowers,” he said; “but the children are the most beautiful ﬂowers of all.” One winter morning he looked out of his window as he was dressing.
uz: "Mening ko'plab chiroyli gullarim bor", - dedi u, "lekin bolalar eng chiroyli gullardir. Bir qish ertalab o'zini kiyganida o'z derazasidan ko'z ochdi.

en: He did not hate the Winter now, for he knew that it was merely the Spring asleep, and that the ﬂowers were resting.
uz: Endi u Qishdan nafratlanmadi, chunki u faqat uyqusida bo'lgan Bahor ekanligini va gullarning dam olishini bilardi.

en: Suddenly he rubbed his eyes in wonder, and looked and looked.
uz: Toʻsatdan u hayronlik bilan koʻzlarini burib, koʻz oʻngidan koʻrmadi.

en: It cer- tainly was a marvellous sight.
uz: Bu, albatta, ajoyib ko'rinish edi.

en: In the farthest corner of the garden was a tree quite covered with lovely white blossoms.
uz: Bogʻning eng uzoq burchagida go'zal oq gullar bilan qoplangan daraxt bor edi.

en: Its branches were all gold- en, and silver fruit hung down from them, and underneath it stood the little boy he had loved.
uz: Uning shoxlari butunlay oltin va kumush mevalar bilan bog'langan edi va uning ostiga sevgan kichkina o'g'il turgan edi.

en: Downstairs ran the Giant in great joy, and out into the garden.
uz: Ulug' katta quvonch bilan pastga yugurib, bog'ga chiqdi.

en: He has- tened across the grass, and came near to the child.
uz: U o't o'g'irdan o'tib, bolaga yaqinlashdi.

en: And when he came quite close his face grew red with anger, and he said, “Who hath dared to wound thee?”  For on the palms of the child’s hands were the prints of two nails, and the prints of two nails were on the little feet.
uz: U yaqinlashganda, uning yuzi g'azabdan qizg'onib, dedi: "Seni kim jarohatlashga jur'at qildi?" Chunki bolaning qo'llarida ikkita pichoqning izlari bor edi, ikkita pichoqning izlari esa kichkina oyoqlarda edi.

en: “Who hath dared to wound thee?” cried the Giant; “tell me, that I may take my big sword and slay him.” “Nay!” answered the child; “but these are the wounds of Love.” “Who art thou?” said the Giant, and a strange awe fell on him, and he knelt before the little child.
uz: "Seni kim jarohatlashga jur'at qildi?" deb baqirdi ulkan, "ey, ayt, men katta qilichimni olib, uni o'ldiraman". "Yo'q", - dedi bola. "lekin bular Sevgining yaralari". "Sen kimsan?" - deb so'radi ulkan, uning ustiga g'alati qo'rquv tushib, u kichik bola oldida tiz cho'kdi.

en: And the child smiled on the Giant, and said to him, “You let me play once in your garden, to-day you shall come with me to my garden, which is Paradise.” And when the children ran in that afternoon, they found the Giant lying dead under the tree, all covered with white blossoms.
uz: Bola ulunga tabassum qilib, unga shunday dedi: "Sen menga bog'ingda bir marta o'ynashga ruxsat ber, bugun sen men bilan mening bog'imga, ya'ni jannatga borasan. Bolalar o'sha kechqurun yugurib ketganda, ul o'likni daraxt ostida o'tirib ko'rishdi, ularning barchasi oq gullar bilan qoplangan edi.

en: THE DEVOTED FRIEND One morning the old Water-rat put his head out of his hole.
uz: Bir kuni ertalab keksa suvli podshoh boshini cho'g'idan chiqardi.

en: He had bright beady eyes and stiff grey whiskers and his tail was like a long bit of black india-rubber.
uz: Uning ko'zlari yorqin, burun bo'laklari qattiq, quyruqlari esa qora g'ildirakga o'xshardi.

en: The little ducks were swimming about in the pond, looking just like a lot of yellow canaries, and their mother, who was pure white with real red legs, was trying to teach them how to stand on their heads in the water.
uz: Kichik tovuqlar hovuzda suzishardi, ular sariq kanarlarga o'xshar edilar va ularning onasi oq va qizil oyoqlari bilan ularni suvda boshlari ustida turishga o'rgatmoqchi edi.

en: “You will never be in the best society unless you can stand on your heads,” she kept saying to them; and every now and then she showed them how it was done.
uz: "Agar boshingizda turolmasangiz, hech qachon eng yaxshi jamiyatda bo'la olmaysiz", - deb aytdi u ularga, vaqti-vaqti bilan ularga buni qanday qilish kerakligini ko'rsatadi.

en: But the little ducks paid no attention to her.
uz: Ammo bu chaqaloqlar unga e'tibor bermadilar.

en: They were so young that they did not know what an advantage it is to be in society at all.
uz: Ular shunchalik yosh edilarki, jamiyatda bo'lishning qanday afzalligini bilmas edilar.

en: “What disobedient children!” cried the old Water-rat; “they really deserve to be drowned.” “Nothing of the kind,” answered the Duck, “every one must make a be- ginning, and parents cannot be too patient.” “Ah!
uz: "Qanday itoatsiz bolalar!" deb qichqirdi keksa suvli podshoh; "ular chindan ham cho'kishga loyiqdirlar". "Bu kabi narsa yo'q", - deb javob berdi Tovuq, "har kim o'zini o'zgartirishi kerak, ota-onalar esa juda sabrli bo'lishi mumkin emas".Ah!

en: I know nothing about the feelings of parents,” said the Water-rat; “I am not a family man.
uz: Men ota-onalarning his-tuyg'ulari haqida hech narsa bilmayman, - dedi Suvli tovuq; - Men oila a'zosi emasman.

en: In fact, I have never been married, and I never intend to be.
uz: Aslida, men hech qachon turmushga chiqmaganman va bunday bo'lishni hech qachon xohlamayman.

en: Love is all very well in its way, but friendship is much higher.
uz: Sevgi o'z yo'lida juda yaxshi, ammo do'stlik ancha yuqori.

en: In- deed, I know of nothing in the world that is either nobler or rarer than a de- voted friendship.” “And what, pray, is your idea of the duties of a devoted friend?” asked a Green Linnet, who was sitting in a willow-tree hard by, and had overheard the conversation.
uz: Darhaqiqat, dunyodagi do'stlikni bekor qilishdan ko'ra eng buyuk yoki kam uchraydigan hech narsa yo'qligini bilaman. Va, ibodat qiling, sodiq do'stning vazifalari haqida sizning tasavvuringiz qanday? deb so'radi o'rtada o'tirgan yashil Linnet, suhbatni tinglagan.

en: “Yes, that is just what I want to know,” said the Duck; and she swam away to the end of the pond, and stood upon her head, in order to give her children a good example.
uz: "Ha, men aynan shu narsani bilmoqchiman", - deb aytdi Tovuq.U o'z bolalariga yaxshi o'rnak ko'rsatish uchun hovuzning oxirigacha suzib ketdi va boshini ko'tarib turdi.

en: “What a silly question!” cried the Water-rat.
uz: Qanday ahmoqona savol! Suvli podshohning ovozi chiqdi.

en: “I should expect my devot- ed friend to be devoted to me, of course.” “And what would you do in return?” said the little bird, swinging upon a silver spray, and ﬂapping his tiny wings.
uz: Men, albatta, sodiq do'stim menga sodiq bo'lishini kutishim kerak. Va siz nima qilasiz? - dedi kichik qush, kumush spray ustida o'ynagan va kichkina qanotlarini o'qib.

en: “I don’t understand you,” answered the Water-rat.
uz: Men sizlarni tushunmayman, deb javob berdi Suv-sot.

en: “Let me tell you a story on the subject,” said the Linnet.
uz: Men sizga bu borada bir hikoyani aytib beraman, dedi Linnet.

en: “Is the story about me?” asked the Water-rat.
uz: Bu hikoya men haqimdami? deb so'radi Suvli jigar.

en: “If so, I will listen to it, for I am extremely fond of ﬁction.” “It is applicable to you,” answered the Linnet; and he ﬂew down, and alighting upon the bank, he told the story of The Devoted Friend.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, men uni tinglayman, chunki men fiksiyalarni juda yaxshi ko'raman.  Bu sizga ham tegishli, deb javob berdi Linnet; va u oshib tushdi va bankga tushdi va u "Devokat do'st" haqidagi hikoyani aytib berdi.

en: “Once upon a time,” said the Linnet, “there was an honest little fellow named Hans.” “Was he very distinguished?” asked the Water-rat.
uz: "Bir vaqtlar, - deydi Linnet, - Hans ismli bir halol yigit bor edi. - U juda mashhur bo'lganmi? - deb so'radi suvli podshoh.

en: “No,” answered the Linnet, “I don’t think he was distinguished at all, ex- cept for his kind heart, and his funny round good-humoured face.
uz: - Yo'q, - deb javob berdi Linnet, - U umuman ajralib turardi, deb o'ylamayman, faqat mehribon yuragi va qiziqarli yuzli, xushmuomala yuzi uchun.

en: He lived in a tiny cottage all by himself, and every day he worked in his garden.
uz: U o'zi yolg'iz kichkina uyda yashardi va har kuni bog'ida ishlaydi.

en: In all the country-side there was no garden so lovely as his.
uz: Butun qishloqda uning bog'i kabi go'zal bog' yo'q edi.

en: Sweet-william grew there, and Gilly-ﬂowers, and Shepherds’-purses, and Fair-maids of France.
uz: U yerda Sweet-William, Gilly-kullar, Cho'ponlar va Frantsiyaning go'zal qizlari o'sgan.

en: There were damask Roses, and yellow Roses, lilac Crocuses, and gold, purple Violets and white.
uz: Damashk rosalari va sariq rosalar, lilac crocuses va oltin, bo'yoq violet va oq bo'lgan.

en: Columbine and Ladysmock, Marjoram and Wild Basil, the Cowslip and the Flower-de-luce, the Daffodil and the Clove-Pink bloomed or blossomed in their proper order as the months went by, one ﬂower taking another ﬂower’s place, so that there were always beautiful things to look at, and pleasant odours to smell.
uz: Columbine va Ladysmock, Marjoram va Wild Basil, Cow'slip va Flower-de-luce, Daffodil va Clove-Pink oylar o'tib o'tishi bilan o'z navbatida gullashdi yoki gullashdi, bir gul boshqa gulning o'rnini egallaydi, shuning uchun har doim ko'rish uchun go'zal narsalar va xushbo'y hidlar bor edi.

en: “Little Hans had a great many friends, but the most devoted friend of all was big Hugh the Miller.
uz: Kichik Xansning juda ko'p do'stlari bor edi, lekin ularning eng sodiq do'sti katta Hugu Miller edi.

en: Indeed, so devoted was the rich Miller to little Hans, that be would never go by his garden without leaning over the wall and plucking a large nosegay, or a handful of sweet herbs, or ﬁlling his pockets with plums and cherries if it was the fruit season.
uz: Darhaqiqat, boy Miller kichkina Xansga shunchalik sodiq bo'lganki, u hech qachon o'z bog'idan o'tib, devor ustida tiklanib, katta burchakni yoki bir nechta shirin o'simliklarni o'rab olmagan yoki meva mavsumida sumka va cherrylar bilan kiyimlarini to'ldirmagan.

en: “‘Real friends should have everything in common,’ the Miller used to say, and little Hans nodded and smiled, and felt very proud of having a friend with such noble ideas.
uz: Haqiqiy do'stlar hamma narsaga umumiy bo'lishlari kerak,  Miller aytishicha, kichkina Xans bosh ko'tardi va tabassum qildi va o'zini bunday buyuk g'oyalarga ega bo'lgan do'stga ega bo'lganidan juda faxrlanardi.

en: “Sometimes, indeed, the neighbours thought it strange that the rich Miller never gave little Hans anything in return, though he had a hundred sacks of ﬂour stored away in his mill, and six milch cows, and a large ﬂock of wool- ly sheep; but Hans never troubled his head about these things, and nothing gave him greater pleasure than to listen to all the wonderful things the Miller used to say about the unselﬁshness of true friendship.
uz: Ba'zan qo'shnilar boy Millerning kichkina Xansga hech narsa qaytarib bermasligini g'alati deb o'ylashardi, garchi u o'zining moliniga yuz to'pqa un, olti sutli sigir va katta to'pka junli qo'ylarni saqlagan bo'lsa-da; lekin Xans bu narsalar haqida hech qachon o'zini bezovta qilmagan va Millerning haqiqiy do'stlikning begʻarazligi haqida aytgan barcha ajoyib narsalarni tinglashdan ko'ra unga hech narsa katta zavq keltirmagan.

en: “So little Hans worked away in his garden.
uz: Shunday kichik Xans bog'ida ishlagan.

en: During the spring, the sum- mer, and the autumn he was very happy, but when the winter came, and he had no fruit or ﬂowers to bring to the market, he suffered a good deal from
uz: Bahorda, yozda va kuzda u juda baxtli edi, lekin qish kelganda va bozorga keltirish uchun meva yoki gullari bo'lmaganida, u juda ko'p azob chekardi.

en: cold and hunger, and often had to go to bed without any supper but a few dried pears or some hard nuts.
uz: Soyuq va och, ko'pincha kechki ovqatdan tashqari bir necha quritilgan pir yoki qattiq yong'oqlardan tashqari hech qanday ovqatsiz uxlash kerak edi.

en: In the winter, also, he was extremely lonely, as the Miller never came to see him then.
uz: Qish paytida ham u juda yolg'iz edi, chunki Millerlar uni hech qachon ko'rishga kelmagan.

en: “‘There is no good in my going to see little Hans as long as the snow lasts,’ the Miller used to say to his wife, ‘for when people are in trouble they should be left alone, and not be bothered by visitors.
uz: Qizil Xansni qar davom etganicha ko'rishimga hech qanday foyda yo'q,  Miller o'z xotiniga: Agar odamlar muammolarga duchor bo'lsalar, ular yolg'iz qolishlari kerak va tashrif buyuruvchilar ularni bezovta qilmasligi kerak, deb aytadi.

en: That at least is my idea about friendship, and I am sure I am right.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda, do'stlik haqida mening fikrim shunaqa bo'ladi va men haqli ekanligimdan shubhalanmayman.

en: So I shall wait till the spring comes, and then I shall pay him a visit, and he will be able to give me a large basket of primroses and that will make him so happy.’ “‘You are certainly very thoughtful about others,’ answered the Wife, as she sat in her comfortable armchair by the big pinewood ﬁre; ‘very thought- ful indeed.
uz: Shunday qilib, men bahor kelishini kutaman, so'ngra unga tashrif buyuraman va u menga katta sovg'alarni berishga qodir bo'ladi va bu uni juda baxtli qiladi. "Siz boshqalarga juda e'tiborli ekansiz", - deb javob berdi Xotin, u o'zining qulay kursiga o'tirib, katta bo'ron o'tining yonida o'tirgan edi.

en: It is quite a treat to hear you talk about friendship.
uz: Sizni do'stlik haqida gapirayotganingizni eshitish juda yoqimli.

en: I am sure the clergyman himself could not say such beautiful things as you do, though he does live in a three-storied house, and wear a gold ring on his little ﬁnger.’ “‘But could we not ask little Hans up here?’ said the Miller’s youngest son.
uz: Ishonchim komilki, ruhoniy o'zi siz kabi go'zal so'zlarni aytishi mumkin emas, garchi u uch qavatli uyda yashasa-da, kichik barmog'ida oltin bog'liq bo'lsa-da. Ammo kichik Xansni bu yerda so'rashimiz mumkin emasmi? dedi Millerning kichik o'g'li.

en: ‘If poor Hans is in trouble I will give him half my porridge, and show him my white rabbits.’ “‘What a silly boy you are’!
uz: Agar kambag'al Xans muammolarga duch kelsak, men unga yarim porushimni beraman va unga oq tovuqlarimni ko'rsataman. Qanday ahmoq o'g'ilsan sen!

en: cried the Miller; ‘I really don’t know what is the use of sending you to school.
uz: Miller yig'lab yubordi: "Sizni maktabga yuborishning nima foydasi borligini bilmayman.

en: You seem not to learn anything.
uz: Siz hech narsa o'rganmayapsiz.

en: Why, if little Hans came up here, and saw our warm ﬁre, and our good supper, and our great cask of red wine, he might get envious, and envy is a most terrible thing, and would spoil anybody’s nature.
uz: Agar kichkina Xans bu yerga kelib, bizning iliq olovimizni, yaxshi kechki ovqatimizni va ajoyib qadoq qizil sharobimizni ko'rsa, u hasadga tushishi mumkin, hasad esa juda dahshatli narsa va har kimning tabiatini buzib qo'yadi.

en: I certainly will not allow Hans’ nature to be spoiled.
uz: Albatta, men tabiatning buzilishiga yo'l qo'ymayman.

en: I am his best friend, and I will always watch over him, and see that he is not led into any temptations.
uz: Men uning eng yaxshi do'stiman va men har doim uni kuzatib turaman va hech qanday vasvasalarga duch kelmasligiga g'amxo'rlik qilaman.

en: Besides, if Hans came here, he might ask me to let him have some ﬂour on credit, and that I could not do.
uz: Bundan tashqari, agar Xans bu yerga kelsa, undan unga kreditda un berishimni so'rab qolishi mumkin edi va men buni qila olmasdim.

en: Flour is one thing, and friendship is another, and they should not be confused.
uz: Un - bir narsa, do'stlik esa boshqacha narsa va bu juftlikni chalg'itmaslik kerak.

en: Why, the words are spelt differently, and mean quite different things.
uz: Bu so'zlar har xil yozilmoqda va o'zgacha ma'noga ega.

en: Everybody can see that.’ “‘How well you talk’!
uz: Buni hamma ko'rishi mumkin.Qanday yaxshi gapirasiz!

en: said the Miller’s Wife, pouring herself out a large glass of warm ale; ‘really I feel quite drowsy.
uz: Millerning xotini o'ziga katta stakan issiq pivo quyib, dedi: "Haqiqatan ham men o'zimni juda uxlab ketaman.

en: It is just like being in church.’ “‘Lots of people act well,’ answered the Miller; ‘but very few people talk well, which shows that talking is much the more difﬁcult thing of the two, and much the ﬁner thing also’; and he looked sternly across the table at his little son, who felt so ashamed of himself that he hung his head down, and grew quite scarlet, and began to cry into his tea.
uz: Bu xuddi cherkovda bo'lish kabi.Ko'p odamlar yaxshi yo'l tutishadi, Miller javob berdi; lekin juda oz odamlar yaxshi gapirishadi, bu esa gapirish ikkovidan ham qiyinroq, yana ko'proq yaxshi ish ekanligini ko'rsatadi; u o'z o'g'liga o'zidan shunchalik o'zlarini sharmanda his qilgan o'g'liga o'zini qattiq ko'rib, o'zini pastga surib qo'ydi, boshini pastga ko'tardi va juda qizil bo'lib, choy ichishiga yig'lay boshladi.

en: However, he was so young that you must excuse him.”
uz: Biroq, u shunchalik yosh ediki, uni kechirishingiz kerak.

en: “Is that the end of the story?” asked the Water-rat.
uz: Bu hikoyaning oxiri bo'ladimi? - deb so'radi Suvli jigar.

en: “Certainly not,” answered the Linnet, “that is the beginning.” “Then you are quite behind the age,” said the Water-rat.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, siz yoshdan ancha ortda qoldingiz, dedi suvli podshoh.

en: “Every good story-teller nowadays starts with the end, and then goes on to the beginning, and concludes with the middle.
uz: Bugun kunlarda har bir yaxshi hikoyachi oxiri bilan boshlanadi, so'ngra boshiga o'tadi va o'rta bilan yakunlanadi.

en: That is the new method.
uz: Bu yangi usul.

en: I heard all about it the other day from a critic who was walking round the pond with a young man.
uz: O'tgan kun bir yigit bilan hovuz atrofida yurgan tanqidchi menga bu haqda xabar berdi.

en: He spoke of the matter at great length, and I am sure he must have been right, for he had blue spectacles and a bald head, and whenever the young man made any remark, he always answered ‘Pooh!’  But pray go on with your story.
uz: U bu mavzu haqida juda ko'p gapirgan va shubhasiz, u to'g'ri gapirgan, chunki uning ko'k ko'z ko'zlari va sochli boshi bor edi va yigit biron-bir fikr bildirganda, u har doim "Puh!" deb javob berardi.

en: I like the Miller immensely.
uz: Millerni juda yaxshi ko'raman.

en: I have all kinds of beautiful sentiments myself, so there is a great sympathy between us.” “Well,” said the Linnet, hopping now on one leg and now on the other, “as soon as the winter was over, and the primroses began to open their pale yellow stars, the Miller said to his wife that he would go down and see little Hans.
uz: O'zim ham turli xil go'zal his-tuyg'ularga egaman, shuning uchun biz o'rtasida katta hamdardlik bor.Linnet, endi bir oyoq va endi boshqa oyoq bilan sakrashgan holda,Qış o'tib ketgandan so'ng, o'simliklar o'z qalin sariq yulduzlarini ochishni boshlaganida, Miller o'z xotiniga pastga tushib, kichkina Hansni ko'rishini aytdi.

en: “‘Why, what a good heart you have’!
uz: Qani, naqadar yaxshi yuragingiz bor!

en: cried his Wife; ‘you are always thinking of others.
uz: Xotini yig'lab yubordi: "Siz har doim boshqalarni o'ylayapsiz.

en: And mind you take the big basket with you for the ﬂowers.’ “So the Miller tied the sails of the windmill together with a strong iron chain, and went down the hill with the basket on his arm.
uz: Gullar uchun katta kosani o'zingiz bilan olib ketishni unutmang. Shuning uchun Miller shamol chigitining yelkalarini kuchli temir zanjir bilan bog'lab, qo'lida kosani olib, tog'dan tushdi.

en: “‘Good morning, little Hans,’ said the Miller.
uz: "Xavf qiling, kichkina Hans", - dedi Miller.

en: “‘Good morning,’ said Hans, leaning on his spade, and smiling from ear to ear.
uz: "Xayrli kunlar", - dedi Xans, o'z ko'krakida tiklanib, quloqdan quloqgacha tabassum qildi.

en: “‘And how have you been all the winter?’ said the Miller.
uz: "Va siz butun qish qanday bo'lgansiz?" - deb so'radi Miller.

en: “‘Well, really,’ cried Hans, ‘it is very good of you to ask, very good in- deed.
uz: Ha, haqiqatan ham, - deb yig'ladi Xans, - so'rashingiz juda yaxshi, juda yaxshi amal qilishingiz kerak.

en: I am afraid I had rather a hard time of it, but now the spring has come, and I am quite happy, and all my ﬂowers are doing well.’ “‘We often talked of you during the winter, Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘and wondered how you were getting on.’ “‘That was kind of you,’ said Hans; ‘I was half afraid you had forgotten me.’ “‘Hans, I am surprised at you,’ said the Miller; ‘friendship never forgets.
uz: Qo'rqamanki, men uchun bu juda qiyin bo'ldi, lekin hozir bahor keldi va men juda xursandman va barcha gullarim yaxshi o'tdi.Biz qish paytida siz haqingizda tez-tez gapirardik, - dedi Hans Miller, - va sizning qanday holatda bo'lishingizni o'yladim.Bu sizdan juda mehribon edi, - dedi Hans;Men meni unutib qo'yganingizdan yarim qo'rqardim.Hans, men sizdan hayratlanaman, - dedi Miller;do'stlik hech qachon unutmaydi.

en: That is the wonderful thing about it, but I am afraid you don’t understand the poetry of life.
uz: Bu uning ajoyib tomonidir, lekin qo'rqamanki, siz hayotning she'rini tushunmayapsiz.

en: How lovely your primroses are looking, by-the-bye”!
uz: Sizlarning o'g'illari juda chiroyli ko'rinadi, xolos!

en: “‘They are certainly very lovely,’ said Hans, ‘and it is a most lucky thing for me that I have so many.
uz: Ular, albatta, juda chiroyli, - dedi Xans, - va men uchun shunchalar borligi juda baxtli.

en: I am going to bring them into the market and
uz: Men ularni bozorga olib boraman va

en: sell them to the Burgomaster’s daughter, and buy back my wheelbarrow with the money.’ “‘Buy back your wheelbarrow?
uz: Ularni Burgomasterning qiziga soting va pul bilan mening vagonimni sotib oling.Vagoningizni qaytarib oling?

en: You don’t mean to say you have sold it?
uz: Siz uni sotganingizni aytmoqchi emasmisiz?

en: What a very stupid thing to do’!
uz: Bu juda ahmoqona ish!

en: “‘Well, the fact is,’ said Hans, ‘that I was obliged to.
uz: Haqiqat shundaki, Xans shunday dedi: "Men bunga majbur bo'ldim.

en: You see the winter was a very bad time for me, and I really had no money at all to buy bread with.
uz: Qish men uchun juda yomon vaqt edi va men uchun non sotib olish uchun pul yo'q edi.

en: So I ﬁrst sold the silver buttons off my Sunday coat, and then I sold my silver chain, and then I sold my big pipe, and at last I sold my wheelbar- row.
uz: Shunday qilib, avvalambor yakshanba kiyimimdan kumush tugmalarni sotdim, so'ngra kumush zanjirimni sotdim, so'ngra katta quvurimni sotdim va nihoyat, to'g'rilik barmoqlarini sotdim.

en: But I am going to buy them all back again now.’ “‘Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘I will give you my wheelbarrow.
uz: Lekin men ularni hammasini yana sotib olyapman.Hans, dedi Miller,Men sizga o'z aravachani beraman.

en: It is not in very good repair; indeed, one side is gone, and there is something wrong with the wheel-spokes; but in spite of that I will give it to you.
uz: U yaxshi ta'mirlanmagan; haqiqatan ham, bir tomoni yo'qolgan, va haydashlar bilan biron bir muammo bor; lekin bunga qaramay, men uni sizga beraman.

en: I know it is very generous of me, and a great many people would think me extremely foolish for parting with it, but I am not like the rest of the world.
uz: Bu men uchun juda saxiy ekanligini bilaman va ko'p odamlar men bilan ajrashish uchun juda ahmoq deb o'ylashadi, ammo men boshqa odamlarga o'xshamayapman.

en: I think that generosity is the essence of friendship, and, besides, I have got a new wheelbarrow for myself.
uz: Menimcha, saxiylik do'stlikning mohiyatidir va bundan tashqari, o'zim uchun yangi arava sotib oldim.

en: Yes, you may set your mind at ease, I will give you my wheelbarrow.’ “‘Well, really, that is generous of you,’ said little Hans, and his funny round face glowed all over with pleasure.
uz: Ha, o'zingizni tinchlantiring, men sizga aravachani beraman. Ha, haqiqatan ham, bu sizning saxiyligingizdir, - dedi kichkina Xans, uning qiziqarli yuzli yuzi esa hamma joyda zavq-shafqat bilan nurlanardi.

en: ‘I can easily put it in repair, as I have a plank of wood in the house.’ “‘A plank of wood’!
uz: Men uni osonlikcha ta'mirlashim mumkin, chunki uyimda yog'och taxtim bor. O'g'och taxtim bor!

en: said the Miller; ‘why, that is just what I want for the roof of my barn.
uz: Miller shunday dedi: "Nima uchun, o'g'limning cho'qqisi uchun aynan shu narsani xohlayman.

en: There is a very large hole in it, and the corn will all get damp if I don’t stop it up.
uz: Uning ichida juda katta cho'l bor va agar uni to'xtatmasam, bug'doy hammasi nam bo'ladi.

en: How lucky you mentioned it!
uz: O'zingizning omadingiz borki, bu haqda gapirgansiz!

en: It is quite remark- able how one good action always breeds another.
uz: Bir yaxshi harakat har doim boshqa harakatni keltirib chiqarishi juda diqqatga sazovor.

en: I have given you my wheelbarrow, and now you are going to give me your plank.
uz: Men sizga o'z aravachani berdim va endi siz menga o'zingizning plakatingizni berasiz.

en: Of course, the wheelbarrow is worth far more than the plank, but true, friendship never no- tices things like that.
uz: To'g'ri, aravacha pilladan ko'ra ko'proq qiymatga ega, ammo haqiqat shundaki, do'stlik hech qachon bunday narsalarni yo'q qiladi.

en: Pray get it at once, and I will set to work at my barn this very day.’ “‘Certainly,’ cried little Hans, and he ran into the shed and dragged the plank out.
uz: Iltijo qiling, uni darhol oling, va men shu kuni o'tqazimda ishlashga kirishaman. Chindan ham, kichkina Xans baqirib yubordi va u cho'nqaga yugurib, lavhani olib chiqdi.

en: “‘It is not a very big plank,’ said the Miller, looking at it, ‘and I am afraid that after I have mended my barn-roof there won’t be any left for you to mend the wheelbarrow with; but, of course, that is not my fault.
uz: "Bu juda katta pilla emas", - dedi Miller uni ko'rib, "va men qo'rqamanki, o'g'limning cho'qqisini tuzatganimdan so'ng, sizlarning aravachani tuzatishingiz uchun hech narsa qolmaydi; lekin, albatta, bu mening aybim emas.

en: And now, as I have given you my wheelbarrow, I am sure you would like to give me some ﬂowers in return.
uz: Endi esa, men sizga aravachani berganim uchun, siz menga o'rinda gullar berishingizni xohlaysiz.

en: Here is the basket, and mind you ﬁll it quite full.’ “‘Quite full?’ said little Hans, rather sorrowfully, for it was really a very big basket, and he knew that if he ﬁlled it he would have no ﬂowers left for
uz: Mana, to'plamni to'ldirib qo'ying. dedi kichik Xans, o'ta xafa bo'lib, chunki bu juda katta to'plam edi va u uni to'ldirib qo'ysa, unga gul qolmasligini bilardi.

en: the market and he was very anxious to get his silver buttons back.
uz: bozorga borib, o'zining kumush tugmalarini qaytarib olishni juda istaydi.

en: “‘Well, really,’ answered the Miller, ‘as I have given you my wheelbar- row, I don’t think that it is much to ask you for a few ﬂowers.
uz: Ha, haqiqatan ham,  Miller javob berdi, Men sizga o'ng qo'limni berganim sababli, sizdan bir necha gul so'rash juda ko'p emas deb o'ylayman.

en: I may be wrong, but I should have thought that friendship, true friendship, was quite free from selﬁshness of any kind.’ “‘My dear friend, my best friend,’ cried little Hans, ‘you are welcome to all the ﬂowers in my garden.
uz: Ehtimol, men xato qilyapman, lekin do'stlik, haqiqiy do'stlik, har qanday xudbinlikdan ozod deb o'ylashim kerak edi. Shog'r do'stim, eng yaxshi do'stim, kichkina Hans yig'ladi, sen bog'imda barcha gullarga xush kelibsiz.

en: I would much sooner have your good opinion than my silver buttons, any day’; and he ran and plucked all his pretty prim- roses, and ﬁlled the Miller’s basket.
uz: Men sizlarning yaxshi fikrlaringizni o'zimning kumush tugmalarimdan ko'ra ko'ra tezroq olishim kerak edi; u esa yugurib borib, o'zining barcha go'zal ro'zalarini yig'di va Millerning koshini to'ldirdi.

en: “‘Good-bye, little Hans,’ said the Miller, as he went up the hill with the plank on his shoulder, and the big basket in his hand.
uz: Xans bilan vedalash, kichik Hans,  dedi Miller, balandlikka chiqib, omborida taxti, qo'lida katta kosani olib keldi.

en: “‘Good-bye,’ said little Hans, and he began to dig away quite merrily, he was so pleased about the wheelbarrow.
uz: "Xayr-so'ng", - dedi kichkina Xans va u juda xursand bo'lib o'rab olishni boshladi, u velosipeddan juda mamnun edi.

en: “The next day he was nailing up some honeysuckle against the porch, when he heard the Miller’s voice calling to him from the road.
uz: Ertasi kuni u chekkadan biroz o't qo'yib o'tirgan edi, lekin yo'ldan Millerning ovozini eshitdi.

en: So he jumped off the ladder, and ran down the garden, and looked over the wall.
uz: U daraxt daraxtidan tushib, bog'dan pastga yugurib, devorga qaradi.

en: “There was the Miller with a large sack of ﬂour on his back.
uz: U yerda Millerning orqasida katta to'pka un bor edi.

en: “‘Dear little Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘would you mind carrying this sack of ﬂour for me to market?’ “‘Oh, I am so sorry,’ said Hans, ‘but I am really very busy to-day.
uz: Shog'ri Hans, Millier dedi, Bu xamir sumkasini men uchun bozorga olib borishga xalaqit berasizmi?Oh, men juda afsusman, dedi Hans, lekin men bugun juda bandman.

en: I have got all my creepers to nail up, and all my ﬂowers to water, and all my grass to roll.’ “‘Well, really,’ said the Miller, ‘I think that, considering that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow, it is rather unfriendly of you to refuse.’ “‘Oh, don’t say that,’ cried little Hans, ‘I wouldn’t be unfriendly for the whole world’; and he ran in for his cap, and trudged off with the big sack on his shoulders.
uz: Men barcha o'zimning qo'zg'olishimni to'sib qo'yishim kerak, barcha gullarim suvga to'lib, barcha o'tlarim o'rnatilishi kerak. Ha, ha, ha, ha, - dedi Miller, - Men o'ylaymanki, men sizga aravachani beraman, deb o'ylayman, sizdan rad etish juda yomon bo'ladi. Oh, shunday aytmang, kichik Xans qayg'urdi, Men butun dunyo uchun yomon bo'lmasdim; va u to'pini olib kirdi va katta sumkani yelkasiga olib ketdi.

en: “It was a very hot day, and the road was terribly dusty, and before Hans had reached the sixth milestone he was so tired that he had to sit down and rest.
uz: Chindan ham issiq kun edi va yo'l juda changli edi va Xans oltinchi qadamga yetib kelishidan oldin juda charchagan bo'lib, o'tirib, dam olishga majbur bo'lgan.

en: However, he went on bravely, and as last he reached the market.
uz: Biroq u jasorat bilan davom etdi va so'nggi marta bozorga yetdi.

en: After he had waited there some time, he sold the sack of ﬂour for a very good price, and then he returned home at once, for he was afraid that if he stopped too late he might meet some robbers on the way.
uz: U yerda bir muncha vaqt kutgandan so'ng, o'sha zaxirani juda yaxshi narxga sotdi va darhol uyga qaytib keldi, chunki agar kech qolsa, yo'lda talonchilarga duch kelishi mumkinligidan qo'rqardi.

en: “‘It has certainly been a hard day,’ said little Hans to himself as he was going to bed, ‘but I am glad I did not refuse the Miller, for he is my best friend, and, besides, he is going to give me his wheelbarrow.’
uz: "Bu, albatta, og'ir kun edi", - dedi kichkina Xans o'ziga uyquga ketayotib, "lekin Millerni rad etmaganimdan xursandman, chunki u mening eng yaxshi do'stimdir va, bundan tashqari, u menga o'z aravachasini berishga tayyor".

en: “Early the next morning the Miller came down to get the money for his sack of ﬂour, but little Hans was so tired that he was still in bed.
uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab Miller o'zining xamir to'plamini sotib olish uchun tushdi, lekin kichkina Xans juda charchagan bo'lib, hali ham yotoqda edi.

en: “‘Upon my word,’ said the Miller, ‘you are very lazy.
uz: Miller aytgan so'zimga ko'ra, siz juda dangasa.

en: Really, consider- ing that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow, I think you might work harder.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, men sizga aravachani beraman, deb o'ylaganimda, siz yanada ko'proq ishlashingiz mumkin.

en: Idleness is a great sin, and I certainly don’t like any of my friends to be idle or sluggish.
uz: Bechoralik katta gunohdir va men do'stlarimning bechora yoki bechora bo'lishini yoqtirmayman.

en: You must not mind my speaking quite plainly to you.
uz: Sizga aniq gapirganimdan xafa bo'lmasligingiz kerak.

en: Of course I should not dream of doing so if I were not your friend.
uz: Albatta, agar men sizning do'stingiz bo'lmasam, bunday qilishni orzu qilmasdim.

en: But what is the good of friendship if one cannot say exactly what one means?
uz: Ammo do'stlikning nima foydasi bor, agar kimdir aniq ma'nosini aytolmasa?

en: Anybody can say charming things and try to please and to ﬂatter, but a true friend always says unpleasant things, and does not mind giving pain.
uz: Har kim yoqimli so'zlarni aytishi va yoqtirishga va maqtanishga harakat qilishi mumkin, ammo haqiqiy do'st har doim yoqimsiz so'zlarni aytadi va og'riq berishga xalaqit bermaydi.

en: In- deed, if he is a really true friend he prefers it, for he knows that then he is doing good.’ “‘I am very sorry,’ said little Hans, rubbing his eyes and pulling off his night-cap, ‘but I was so tired that I thought I would lie in bed for a little time, and listen to the birds singing.
uz: Darhaqiqat, agar u haqiqiy do'st bo'lsa, u buni afzal ko'radi, chunki u o'z ishini yaxshi bajarayotganini biladi.Men juda afsusdaman, kichik Xans ko'zlarini burib, kechki kiyimini olib tashlab dedi, lekin men juda charchadim va ozgina o'tirib, qushlarning kuylashiga quloq solaman deb o'yladim.

en: Do you know that I always work better after hearing the birds sing?’ “‘Well, I am glad of that,’ said the Miller, clapping little Hans on the back, ‘for I want you to come up to the mill as soon as you are dressed, and mend my barn-roof for me.’ “Poor little Hans was very anxious to go and work in his garden, for his ﬂowers had not been watered for two days, but he did not like to refuse the Miller, as he was such a good friend to him.
uz: Qushlarning kuylagandan keyin men har doim yaxshiroq ishlayotganimni bilasanmi?Besh, men bunga quvonaman, - dedi Miller, kichkina Hansni orqa tomoniga taqib, chunki, kiyim kiyganingizdan so'ng molxonaga kelib, do'konimni tuzatishingizni xohlayman.Boshqa Hans o'zining bog'ida ishlashni juda xohlardi, chunki uning gullari ikki kun davomida sug'orilmagan edi, lekin u Millerni rad etishni xohlamagan, chunki u uchun u juda yaxshi do'st edi.

en: “‘Do you think it would be unfriendly of me if I said I was busy?’ he in- quired in a shy and timid voice.
uz: Sizga o'xshamaydimi, agar men mashg'ul bo'lganimni aytsam? - deb so'radi u uyalgan va uyalgan ovoz bilan.

en: “‘Well, really,’ answered the Miller, ‘I do not think it is much to ask of you, considering that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow; but of course if you refuse I will go and do it myself.’ “‘Oh!
uz: Ha, haqiqatan ham,  Miller javob berdi, Men sizdan juda ko'p narsani so'rashim kerak deb o'ylamayman, chunki men sizga aravachani beraman; lekin, albatta, agar siz rad qilsangiz, men o'zim boraman va uni o'zim qilaman.Oh!

en: on no account,’ cried little Hans and he jumped out of bed, and dressed himself, and went up to the barn.
uz: Hech qanday sababga ko'ra, kichkina Xans yig'ladi va u to'shagidan tushib, kiyimlarini kiyib, cho'nqaga bordi.

en: “He worked there all day long, till sunset, and at sunset the Miller came to see how he was getting on.
uz: U kun bo'yi quyosh botguncha u yerda ishlagan va quyosh botganida Miller uning holatini ko'rish uchun kelgan.

en: “‘Have you mended the hole in the roof yet, little Hans?’ cried the Miller in a cheery voice.
uz: Siz hali ham xonadondagi teshikni tuzatganmisiz, kichik Hans? Miller xursand ovoz bilan baqirib yubordi.

en: “‘It is quite mended,’ answered little Hans, coming down the ladder.
uz: "U juda yaxshi", - deb javob berdi kichik Xans, poyezddan tushayotganda.

en: said the Miller, ‘there is no work so delightful as the work one does for others.’
uz: Miller shunday dedi: "O'zgalar uchun qilingan ishdan ko'ra ko'proq zavq keltiradigan ish yo'q.

en: “‘It is certainly a great privilege to hear you talk,’ answered little Hans, sitting down, and wiping his forehead, ‘a very great privilege.
uz: "Sizni gapirganingizni eshitish, albatta, katta sharafdir", - deb javob berdi kichkina Xans, o'tirib, peshanasini o'chirib, - bu juda katta sharaf.

en: But I am afraid I shall never have such beautiful ideas as you have.’ “‘Oh!
uz: Ammo men qo'rqamanki, men hech qachon siz kabi ajoyib g'oyalarga ega bo'lmayman.

en: they will come to you,’ said the Miller, ‘but you must take more pains.
uz: Ular sizga keladi, - dedi Miller, - lekin siz yanada ko'proq harakat qilishingiz kerak.

en: At present you have only the practice of friendship; some day you will have the theory also.’ “‘Do you really think I shall?’ asked little Hans.
uz: Hozirda sizda faqat do'stlik amaliyotlari mavjud; bir kun sizda ham nazariya bo'ladi. Siz haqiqatan ham men shunday qilaman deb o'ylaysizmi? - deb so'radi kichkina Xans.

en: “‘I have no doubt of it,’ answered the Miller, ‘but now that you have mended the roof, you had better go home and rest, for I want you to drive my sheep to the mountain to-morrow.’ “Poor little Hans was afraid to say anything to this, and early the next morning the Miller brought his sheep round to the cottage, and Hans started off with them to the mountain.
uz: Men bunga shubha yo'q,  Miller javob berdi,  lekin endi siz tomonni tuzatganingizdan so'ng, uyingizga borib dam oling, chunki ertaga qo'ylarim bilan tog'ga olib borishni xohlayman.  Zavqsiz kichkina Xans bunga biron narsa aytishdan qo'rqqan va ertasi kuni ertalab Miller qo'ylarini uyga olib keldi va Xans ular bilan tog'ga chiqdi.

en: It took him the whole day to get there and back; and when he returned he was so tired that he went off to sleep in his chair, and did not wake up till it was broad daylight.
uz: U yerga va qaytib borish uchun butun kun kerak edi; qaytib kelganida esa u shunchalik charchagan ediki, o'z kursi ustida uxlab ketadi va kun yorug' bo'lgunga qadar uyg'onmaydi.

en: “‘What a delightful time I shall have in my garden,’ he said, and he went to work at once.
uz: O'z bog'imda qanday ajoyib vaqt o'tkazaman, - dedi u va darhol ishga kirdi.

en: “But somehow he was never able to look after his ﬂowers at all, for his friend the Miller was always coming round and sending him off on long er- rands, or getting him to help at the mill.
uz: Ammo u hech qachon o'z gullariga g'amxo'rlik qila olmagan, chunki uning do'sti Miller doimo kelib, uni uzoq sayohatlarga yuboradi yoki molxonada yordam berishga majburlaydi.

en: Little Hans was very much dis- tressed at times, as he was afraid his ﬂowers would think he had forgotten them, but he consoled himself by the reﬂection that the Miller was his best friend.
uz: Kichik Xans ba'zan juda xavotirlangan edi, chunki gullari uni unutgan deb o'ylashidan qo'rqardi, ammo Miller uning eng yaxshi do'sti ekanligini ko'rib tasalli topdi.

en: ‘Besides,’ he used to say, ‘he is going to give me his wheelbarrow, and that is an act of pure generosity.’ “So little Hans worked away for the Miller, and the Miller said all kinds of beautiful things about friendship, which Hans took down in a note-book, and used to read over at night, for he was a very good scholar.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u menga o'z aravachasini berishini aytardi va bu sof saxiylik amalidir.Xususan, kichkina Xans Miller uchun ishlaydi va Miller do'stlik haqida turli xil go'zal narsalarni aytadi.Xans bu haqda yozuvchisiga yozib qo'ygan va kechasi o'qigan, chunki u juda yaxshi o'qituvchi edi.

en: “Now it happened that one evening little Hans was sitting by his ﬁreside when a loud rap came at the door.
uz: Bir kuni kechqurun kichkina Xans o'zining olov yonida o'tirganida, eshik oldida baland ovoz bilan qichqiriq eshitildi.

en: It was a very wild night, and the wind was blowing and roaring round the house so terribly that at ﬁrst he thought it was merely the storm.
uz: Bu juda yovvoyi kechasi edi va shamol o'tib, uyni shunchalik dahshatli bo'lib o'rab oldiki, dastlab u bu shunchaki shamol deb o'yladi.

en: But a second rap came, and then a third, louder than any of the others.
