en: The feet of the dead Witch had disappeared entirely, and nothing was left but the silver shoes.
uz: O'lgan sehrgarning oyoqlari butunlay yo'qolgan edi va kumush poyabzallardan boshqa hech narsa qolmagan edi.

en: "She was so old," explained the Witch of the North, "that she dried up quickly in the sun.
uz: "U shunchalik keksa edi", - deb tushuntirdi Shimoliy sehrgar, "ki, u quyoshda tez qurib ketdi.

en: That is the end of her.
uz: Bu uning oxiri.

en: shoes are yours, and you shall have them to wear." She reached down and picked up the shoes, and after shaking the dust out of them handed them to Dorothy.
uz: Bu oyoqlar seningki va ularni kiyib olishing kerak". - deb qoʻlini uzdi va oyoqlarini koʻtarib oldi va toʻstini silkitib, ularni Dorotiga berdi.

en: "The Witch of the East was proud of those silver shoes," said one of the Munchkins, "and there is some charm connected with them; but what it is we never knew." Dorothy carried the shoes into the house and placed them on the table.
uz: Munchkinlardan biri shunday dedi: "Tashriq sehrosi o'sha kumush poyabzallar bilan faxrlanardi va ular bilan bog'liq bir xil mashhurlik bor edi; lekin nima ekanligini biz hech qachon bilmagan edik".

en: Then she came out again to the Munchkins and said: "I am anxious to get back to my aunt and uncle, for I am sure they will worry about me.
uz: Keyin u yana Munchkinlar qaramogʻiga chiqib: "Men onam va onam bilan birga boʻlishni juda istayman, chunki ular men uchun tashvishlanishlariga aminman.

en: Can you help me find my way?" The Munchkins and the Witch first looked at one another, and then at Dorothy, and then shook their heads.
uz: Menga yo'l topishimga yordam bera olasizmi?" - deb so'ragan Munchkinlar va sehrgarlar avval bir-birlariga, so'ngra Dorotsiyaga qarab, boshlarini shovqin qilishdi.

en: "At the East, not far from here," said one, "there is a great desert, and none could live to cross it." "It is the same at the South," said another, "for I have been there and seen it.
uz: "Shariqda, bu yerdan uzoq emas, - dedi bir kishi, - katta cho'l bor va uni kesib o'tish uchun hech kim yashamaydi. - Janubiyda ham xuddi shunday, - dedi yana bir kishi, - chunki men u yerda bo'lib, uni ko'rdim.

en: The South is the country of the Quadlings." "I am told," said the third man, "that it is the same at the West.
uz: Janubiy - bu Quadlinglar yurti". - Uchinchi kishi dedi: "Menga aytishganda, G'arbda ham xuddi shunday.

en: And that country, where the Winkies live, is ruled by the Wicked Witch of the West, who would make you her slave if you passed her way." "The North is my home," said the old lady, "and at its edge is the same great desert that surrounds this Land of Oz.
uz: Va Winkilar yashaydigan bu mamlakatga G'arbning yovuz sehrgarasi hukmronlik qiladi, agar siz uning yo'lidan o'tgan bo'lsangiz, u sizni uning quli qiladi. " "Shimoliy - mening uyim", dedi keksa ayol, "va uning chegarasida Oz yurti atrofidagi xuddi shu katta sahro bor.

en: I'm afraid, my dear, you will have to live with us." Dorothy began to sob at this, for she felt lonely among all these strange people.
uz: Qo'rqaman, azizim, sen biz bilan birga yashashing kerak". - deb qo'rqitdi Dorotiya, chunki u o'zini bu g'alati odamlar orasida yolg'iz his qilardi.

en: Her tears seemed to grieve the kind-hearted Munchkins, for they immediately took out their handkerchiefs and began to weep also.
uz: Uning ko'z yoshlari mehribon Munchkinlarni xafa qilganiga o'xshardi, chunki ular darhol to'qimalarini olib, yig'lashga boshlashdi.

en: As for the little old woman, she took off her cap and balanced the point on the end of her nose, while she counted "One, two, three" in a solemn voice.
uz: Kichik keksa ayol esa toʻpini olib, burunning soʻngida joylashgan nuqtani muvozanatga qoʻydi va "Bir, ikki, uch" soʻzini soʻnggi ovoz bilan sanab oʻtdi.

en: At once the cap changed to a slate, on which was written in big, white chalk marks: "LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS"
uz: Shu zahoti qo'rqinchli, oq chalk belgilari bilan yozilgan, "LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS" deb yozilgan slaytga aylandi.

en: The little old woman took the slate from her nose, and having read the words on it, asked, "Is your name Dorothy, my dear?" "Yes," answered the child, looking up and drying her tears.
uz: Kichik keksa ayol o'z burunidan pillani olib, ulardagi so'zlarni o'qib, "Sening isming Dorotimi, azizim?" deb so'radi. "Ha", - deb javob berdi bola, ko'zlarini ko'tarib, ko'z yoshlarini quritdi.

en: "Then you must go to the City of Emeralds.
uz: "O'shanda siz Emeraldlar shahriga borishingiz kerak.

en: Perhaps Oz will help you." "Where is this city?" asked Dorothy.
uz: Ehtimol Oz sizga yordam beradi". - "Bu shahar qayerda?" deb so'radi Doroti.

en: "It is exactly in the center of the country, and is ruled by Oz, the Great Wizard I told you of." "Is he a good man?" inquired the girl anxiously.
uz: "Bu mamlakatning markazida joylashgan va sizga aytib o'tgan buyuk sehrgar Oz tomonidan boshqariladi". - U yaxshi odammi? - deb so'radi qiz tashvish bilan.

en: "He is a good Wizard.
uz: "U yaxshi sehrgar.

en: Whether he is a man or not I cannot tell, for I have never seen him." "How can I get there?" asked Dorothy.
uz: U erkakmi yoki yo'qmi, demayman, chunki men uni hech qachon ko'rmaganman". - "U yerga qanday etib borishim mumkin?" deb so'radi Doroti.

en: It is a long journey, through a country that is sometimes pleasant and sometimes dark and terrible.
uz: Bu uzoq sayohat, ba'zan yoqimli, ba'zan qorong'i va dahshatli mamlakat orqali.

en: However, I will use all the magic arts I know of to keep you from harm." "Won't you go with me?" pleaded the girl, who had begun to look upon the little old woman as her only friend.
uz: Biroq, senga zarar yetkazmaslik uchun bilgan barcha sehr-jodu san'atlaridan foydalanaman", deb yolvorgan qiz, kichkina keksa ayolga o'zining yagona do'sti sifatida qaray boshlagan edi. "Men bilan kelmaysanmi?"

en: "No, I cannot do that," she replied, "but I will give you my kiss, and no one will dare injure a person who has been kissed by the Witch of the North." She came close to Dorothy and kissed her gently on the forehead.
uz: - Yo'q, men buni qila olmayman, - deb javob berdi u, - lekin men senga o'zimning o'zimni o'g'ib beraman va hech kim Shimoliy sehrgar tomonidan o'g'ib olingan odamga zarar yetkazishga jur'at qilmaydi.

en: Where her lips touched the girl they left a round, shining mark, as Dorothy found out soon after.
uz: Uning og'izlari qizga teggan joyda, Dorothy tez orada bilib olganidek, yuziga to'liq, yorqin iz qoldirdi.

en: "The road to the City of Emeralds is paved with yellow brick," said the Witch, "so you cannot miss it.
uz: "Smeraldlar shahriga boradigan yo'l sariq g'isht bilan pavilyajlangan, shuning uchun uni o'tkazib yuborish mumkin emas.

en: When you get to Oz do not be afraid of him, but tell your story and ask him to help you.
uz: Oz shahriga yetganingizda undan qo'rqmang, o'zingizning hikoyangizni aytib bering va Undan yordam so'rang.

en: Good-bye, my dear." The three Munchkins bowed low to her and wished her a pleasant journey, after which they walked away through the trees.
uz: Xo'sh, azizim". Uchta Munchkin ayolga sajda qilib, unga yaxshi sayohat tiladilar va keyin daraxtlar o'rtasida yurishdi.

en: The Witch gave Dorothy a friendly little nod, whirled around on her left heel
uz: Qoʻzicha Dorothyga doʻstona bosh koʻtardi va chap boʻgʻinida aylanib chiqdi.

en: three times, and straightway disappeared, much to the surprise of little Toto, who barked after her loudly enough when she had gone, because he had been afraid even to growl while she stood by.
uz: uch marta va darhol yo'qoldi, bu esa kichkina Totoga ajablanarli bo'ldi, chunki u ketib ketgach, u ayolning orqasidan qo'rqqan, chunki u qo'rqqanida u qo'rqqan.

en: But Dorothy, knowing her to be a witch, had expected her to disappear in just that way, and was not surprised in the least.
uz: Ammo Doroti uning sehrgar ekanligini bilgan holda, uning shu tarzda yo'qolishini kutgan va hecham ajablanib qolmagan.

en: Chapter III How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow When Dorothy was left alone she began to feel hungry.
uz: III bob: Dorothy qo'rquvchini qanday qutqardi?Dorothy yolg'iz qolganda, u o'zini och his qila boshladi.

en: So she went to the cupboard and cut herself some bread, which she spread with butter.
uz: Shu sababli u omborga borib, o'ziga non kesib, uni yog' bilan tarqatdi.

en: She gave some to Toto, and taking a pail from the shelf she carried it down to the little brook and filled it with clear, sparkling water.
uz: U Totoga biroz berdi va raftdan bir qadoq olib, uni kichik daryoga olib bordi va uni toza, parcha-parcha suv bilan to'ldirdi.

en: Toto ran over to the trees and began to bark at the birds sitting there.
uz: Toto daraxtlarga yugurib borib, o'sha yerda o'tirgan qushlarga qichqirishni boshladi.

en: Dorothy went to get him, and saw such delicious fruit hanging from the branches that she gathered some of it, finding it just what she wanted to help out her breakfast.
uz: Doroti uni olib ketishga bordi va shoxlardan osilgan go'zal mevalarni ko'rib, ulardan ba'zilarini to'pladi va kechki ovqatga yordam bermoqchi bo'lganini topdi.

en: Then she went back to the house, and having helped herself and Toto to a good drink of the cool, clear water, she set about making ready for the journey to the City of Emeralds.
uz: Keyin u uyga qaytib ketdi va o'zi va Totoga sovuq, toza suv ichishga yordam berganidan so'ng, Emeraldlar shahriga borishga tayyorgarlik ko'rdi.

en: Dorothy had only one other dress, but that happened to be clean and was hanging on a peg beside her bed.
uz: Dorotining yana bir kiyimlari bor edi, lekin u toza edi va o'z yotoqining yonida yonayotgan bir pishirganida o'tirgan edi.

en: It was gingham, with checks of white and blue; and although the blue was somewhat faded with many washings, it was still a pretty frock.
uz: Bu gingham edi, oq va ko'k ranglar bor edi; ko'k rang ko'pgina yuvishlar bilan biroz o'zgarib ketgan bo'lsa-da, u hali ham chiroyli kiyim edi.

en: The girl washed herself carefully, dressed herself in the clean gingham, and tied her pink sunbonnet on her head.
uz: Qiz o'zini ehtiyotkorlik bilan yuvdi, toza gingham kiyimini kiydirdi va boshiga rosa quyoshni bog'ladi.

en: She took a little basket and filled it with bread from the cupboard, laying a white cloth over the top.
uz: U kichik bir koska olib, uni ombordan non bilan to'ldirdi va ustiga oq mato qo'ydi.

en: Then she looked down at her feet and noticed how old and worn her shoes were.
uz: So'ngra o'z oyoqlariga qarab, uning qancha yosh va kiygan poyabzallari borligini ko'rdi.

en: "They surely will never do for a long journey, Toto," she said.
uz: "Ular hech qachon uzoq sayohat qilmaydilar, Toto", dedi u.

en: And Toto looked up into her face with his little black eyes and wagged his tail to show he knew what she meant.
uz: To'to uning yuziga o'zining kichik qora ko'zlari bilan qarab, uning nimani nazarda tutayotganini bilishini ko'rsatish uchun quyruqini silkitdi.

en: At that moment Dorothy saw lying on the table the silver shoes that had belonged to the Witch of the East.
uz: O'sha paytda Doroti sharq sehrog'iga tegishli bo'lgan kumush poyabzallarni stol ustida yotganini ko'rdi.

en: "I wonder if they will fit me," she said to Toto.
uz: "Menga mos keladimi, deb o'ylayman", - dedi u Totoga.

en: "They would be just the thing to take a long walk in, for they could not wear out." She took off her old leather shoes and tried on the silver ones, which fitted her as well as if they had been made for her.
uz: U eski charm kiyimlarini olib, kumush kiyimlarini sinab ko'rdi, ular o'zi uchun tayyorlangan bo'lgani kabi, unga ham mos kelardi.

en: Finally she picked up her basket.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, u o'z koshchasini ko'tarib oldi.

en: "Come along, Toto," she said.
uz: U: "Kelib kel, To'to", - dedi.

en: "We will go to the Emerald City and ask the Great Oz how to get back to Kansas again." She closed the door, locked it, and put the key carefully in the pocket of her dress.
uz: "Biz Emerald Cityga boramiz va Buyuk Ozdan Kansasga qaytib borish yo'lini so'raymiz". U eshikni yopdi, qulflab qo'ydi va kalitni kiygan kiyimining qopqoqida ehtiyotkorlik bilan qo'ydi.

en: And so, with Toto trotting along soberly behind her, she started on her journey.
uz: Shunday qilib, Toto o'z orqasidan ketayotganda, u sayohatni boshladi.

en: There were several roads near by, but it did not take her long to find the one paved with yellow bricks.
uz: Bu yerda bir necha yo'l bor edi, lekin u sariq toshlar bilan paxtalashtirilgan yo'lni topishi uchun ko'p vaqt talab qilmadi.

en: Within a short time she was walking briskly toward the Emerald City, her silver shoes tinkling merrily on the hard, yellow road-bed.
uz: Ko'p o'tmay u Emerald Cityga yaqinlashib borayotgan edi, uning kumush poyabzallari qattiq, sariq yo'l yotoqida quvonch bilan qichqirib turardi.

en: The sun shone bright and the birds sang sweetly, and Dorothy did not feel nearly so bad as you might think a little girl would who had been suddenly whisked away from her own country and set down in the midst of a strange land.
uz: Quyosh yorqin, qushlar shirin kuylab, Dorothy o'zini o'zicha his qilmay, o'z yurtidan to'satdan olib ketilgan va o'zga yurtning o'rtasida o'tirgan kichkina qizcha o'zini o'ta yomon his qilgan.

en: She was surprised, as she walked along, to see how pretty the country was about her.
uz: U yurgan joyda mamlakatning qanchalik chiroyli ekanini ko'rib hayron qoldi.

en: There were neat fences at the sides of the road, painted a dainty blue color, and beyond them were fields of grain and vegetables in abundance.
uz: Yo'l yonlarida yaxshi o'rnatilgan, chiroyli ko'k rangda bo'yilgan to'siqlar bor edi va ularning tashqarisida ko'p miqdorda don va sabzavot ekinzorlari bor edi.

en: Evidently the Munchkins were good farmers and able to raise large crops.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, Munchkinlar yaxshi dehqonlar va katta hosilni yetishtirishga qodir edilar.

en: Once in a while she would pass a house, and the people came out to look at her and bow low as she went by; for everyone knew she had been the means of destroying the Wicked Witch and setting them free from bondage.
uz: Vaqti-vaqti u uydan o'tib ketardi va odamlar unga qarash uchun chiqardilar va u o'tib ketayotganda yuzini egib sajda qilishardi; chunki hamma uning yovuz sehrgarni yo'q qilish va ularni qullikdan ozod qilish uchun vosita ekanligini bilardi.

en: The houses of the Munchkins were odd-looking dwellings,
uz: Munchkinlar uylari o'zgacha ko'rinadigan uylar edi.

en: for each was round, with a big dome for a roof.
uz: Har biri yuzli edi, tom uchun katta qo'llanma bor edi.

en: All were painted blue, for in this country of the East blue was the favorite color.
uz: Hammasi ko'k rangga bo'yilgan edi, chunki Sharqning bu mamlakatida ko'k rang eng sevimli rang edi.

en: Toward evening, when Dorothy was tired with her long walk and began to wonder where she should pass the night, she came to a house rather larger than the rest.
uz: Kechaga yaqin, Doroti uzoq yurishdan charchaganida va kechani qayerda o'tkazishni o'ylay boshlaganida, u boshqalardan ancha kattaroq uyga keldi.

en: On the green lawn before it many men and women were dancing.
uz: Uning oldidagi yashil gazonda ko'plab erkaklar va ayollar raqsga tushdilar.

en: Five little fiddlers played as loudly as possible, and the people were laughing and singing, while a big table near by was loaded with delicious fruits and nuts, pies and cakes, and many other good things to eat.
uz: Beshta kichkina violonchilar iloji boricha baland ovoz bilan o'ynashdi va odamlar kulish va kuylashardi, yaqin atrofdagi katta stol esa mazali mevalar va yong'oqlar, tortlar va keklar va boshqa ko'plab yaxshi ovqatlar bilan to'ldirilgan edi.

en: The people greeted Dorothy kindly, and invited her to supper and to pass the night with them; for this was the home of one of the richest Munchkins in the land, and his friends were gathered with him to celebrate their freedom from the bondage of the Wicked Witch.
uz: Odamlar Dorothyga mehribonlik bilan salom berishdi va uni kechki ovqatga taklif qilishdi va ular bilan kechki payt o'tkazishga taklif qilishdi; chunki bu mamlakatning eng boy munchkinlaridan biri uyida edi va uning do'stlari u bilan birga yovuz sehrgarning qulligidan ozod bo'lishlarini nishonlash uchun yig'ilishdi.

en: Dorothy ate a hearty supper and was waited upon by the rich Munchkin himself, whose name was Boq.
uz: Doroti juda yaxshi ovqat yeydi va boy Munchkinning o'zi uni kutib oldi, uning ismi Boq edi.

en: Then she sat upon a settee and watched the people dance.
uz: So'ngra u bir setda o'tirib, odamlar raqsga tushayotganini kuzatdi.

en: When Boq saw her silver shoes he said, "You must be a great sorceress." "Why?" asked the girl.
uz: Boq uning kumush poyabzallarini ko'rganida: "Sen ajoyib sehrgarsan", - dedi.

en: "Because you wear silver shoes and have killed the Wicked Witch.
uz: Chunki siz kumush poyabzallar kiygansiz va Yovuz sehrgarni o'ldirgansiz.

en: Besides, you have white in your frock, and only witches and sorceresses wear white." "My dress is blue and white checked," said Dorothy, smoothing out the wrinkles in it.
uz: Bundan tashqari, kiyimingizda oq kiyim bor va faqat sehrgarlar va sehrgarlar oq kiyim kiyishadi". - Mening kiyimim ko'k va oq bo'lib ko'rinadi, - dedi Dorotsiya, uning burchaklarini sozlab.

en: "It is kind of you to wear that," said Boq.
uz: "Sening bunday kiyinishing juda mehribon", dedi Boq.

en: "Blue is the color of the Munchkins, and white is the witch color.
uz: "Munchkinlarning ranglari ko'k, oq esa sehrgarlarning rangidir.

en: So we know you are a friendly witch." Dorothy did not know what to say to this, for all the people seemed to think her a witch, and she knew very well she was only an ordinary little girl who had come by the chance of a cyclone into a strange land.
uz: Shunday qilib, biz sizning do'stlik bilan shug'ullanayotgan sehrgar ekanligingizni bilamiz".Dorothy bunga nima deb javob berishni bilmadi, chunki hamma uni sehrgar deb o'ylagandek tuyuladi va u oddiy bir qizchadan iboratligini juda yaxshi bilardi.

en: When she had tired watching the dancing, Boq led her into the house, where he gave her a room with a pretty bed in it.
uz: U raqslarni ko'rib charchaganida, Boq uni uyga olib kirdi va u erda unga chiroyli yotoq bo'lgan xonani berdi.

en: The sheets were made of blue cloth, and Dorothy slept soundly in them till morning, with Toto curled up on the blue rug beside her.
uz: Yopaklar ko'k kiyimdan yasalgan edi va Doroti ertalabgacha o'shalarda qattiq uxlab, To'to uning yonida ko'k kiyimda o'tirib qolgan edi.

en: She ate a hearty breakfast, and watched a wee Munchkin baby, who played with Toto and pulled his tail and crowed and laughed in a way that greatly amused Dorothy.
uz: U yaxshi ovqat yeydi va To'to bilan o'ynashgan va quyruqlarini tortib, qichqiriq va kulishni ko'rgan kichkina Munchkin chaqaloqini ko'rib, Dorothyga juda yoqdi.

en: Toto was a fine curiosity to all the people, for they had never seen a dog before.
uz: Toto barcha odamlar uchun ajoyib qiziquvchanlik edi, chunki ular ilgari hech qachon itni ko'rmagan edilar.

en: "How far is it to the Emerald City?" the girl asked.
uz: Qiz: "Smerald shahriga qancha yo'l bor?" - deb so'radi.

en: "I do not know," answered Boq gravely, "for I have never been there.
uz: - Bilmayman, - dedi Boq jiddiy javob berib, - chunki men hech qachon u yerga bormaganman.

en: It is better for people to keep away from Oz, unless they have business with him.
uz: Odamlar uchun Ozdan uzoqlashish yaxshiroqdir, agar ular u bilan ish qilmasalar.

en: But it is a long way to the Emerald City, and it will take you many days.
uz: Ammo bu Emerald Shaharga uzoq yo'l va ko'p kunlar kerak bo'ladi.

en: The country here is rich and pleasant, but you must pass through rough and dangerous places before you reach the end of your journey." This worried Dorothy a little, but she knew that only the Great Oz could help her get to Kansas again, so she bravely resolved not to turn back.
uz: Bu mamlakat boy va yoqimli, lekin sayohatning oxiriga yetib kelishdan oldin siz og'ir va xavfli joylardan o'tishingiz kerak". Bu Dorothyni biroz xavotirga solgan, ammo u faqat Buyuk Ozning Kanzasga qaytishga yordam berishi mumkinligini bilardi, shuning uchun u jasorat ila orqaga qaytib kelmaslikka qaror qildi.

en: She bade her friends good-bye, and again started along the road of yellow brick.
uz: U do'stlari bilan xayrlashib, yana sariq g'isht yo'lidan boshladi.

en: When she had gone several miles she thought she would stop to rest, and so climbed to the top of the fence beside the road and sat down.
uz: Bir necha kilometr yurganidan so'ng, dam olish uchun to'xtab turishni o'ylagan va yo'l yonidagi to'siqning yuqoriga chiqib, o'tirdi.

en: There was a great cornfield beyond the fence, and not far away she saw a Scarecrow, placed high on a pole to keep the birds from the ripe corn.
uz: Sichqonchaning tashqarisida katta donzor bor edi va undan uzoq emas, u qushlarni o'simliklardan saqlab qolish uchun ustunning yuqoriga qo'yilgan qo'rqinchli qushni ko'rdi.

en: Dorothy leaned her chin upon her hand and gazed thoughtfully at the Scarecrow.
uz: Dorotiya o'zining cho'ntagini qo'liga tikib, qo'rqinchli qo'zg'olni diqqat bilan ko'rib turdi.

en: Its head was a small sack stuffed with straw, with eyes, nose, and mouth painted on it to represent a face.
uz: Uning boshi pastki bilan to'ldirilgan kichik sumka edi, uning ustiga yuzni tasvirlash uchun ko'zlar, burun va og'iz bo'yilgan edi.

en: An old, pointed blue hat, that had belonged to some Munchkin, was perched on his head, and the rest of the figure was a blue suit of clothes, worn and faded, which had also been stuffed with straw.
uz: Uning boshiga bir Munchkinga tegishli bo'lgan eski, oq ko'k to'pka o'rnatilgan edi, qolgan qismi esa kiyimning ko'k kiyimlari edi, bu kiyimlar ishlangan va o'zgarib ketgan edi, ular ham cho'g'a bilan to'ldirilgan edi.

en: On the feet were some old boots with blue tops, such as every man wore in this country, and the figure was raised above the stalks of corn by means of the pole stuck up its back.
uz: Oyoqlarida har bir erkak kiygan ko'k toptakli eski botlar bor edi va bu suratni orqaga bog'langan ustun yordamida bug'doy bo'g'inlari ustida ko'tarib qo'yishardi.

en: While Dorothy was looking earnestly into the queer, painted face of the Scarecrow, she was surprised to see one of the eyes slowly wink at her.
uz: Dorothy qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli suratga diqqat bilan qaraganida, uning ko'zlaridan birining unga sekin-sakin ko'z tikishini ko'rib hayron qoldi.

en: She thought she must have been mistaken at first, for none of the scarecrows in Kansas ever wink; but presently the figure nodded its head to her in a friendly way.

uz: Shuning uchun u yong'inlardan uzoqroq turardi va Dorotani faqat uyquga yotganda quruq barglar bilan qoplash uchun yaqinlashdi.

en: These kept her very snug and warm, and she slept soundly until morning.
uz: Bular uni juda yaqin va iliq saqlab turardi va u ertalabgacha yaxshi uxladi.

en: When it was daylight, the girl bathed her face in a little rippling brook, and soon after they all started toward the Emerald City.
uz: Kun yorug' bo'lganida, qiz ozgina to'lqinli daryoda yuzini yuvdi va tez orada ular barchasi Emerald Shahar tomon boshlashdi.

en: This was to be an eventful day for the travelers.
uz: Bu sayohatchilar uchun muhim kun bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: They had hardly been walking an hour when they saw before them a great ditch that crossed the road and divided the forest as far as they could see on either side.
uz: Ular bir soat yurganlaridan so'ng, yo'lni kesib, o'rmonni ikki tomondan ko'rishlari mumkin bo'lgancha uzoqroq bo'lib o'tgan katta quduqni ko'rishdi.

en: It was a very wide ditch, and when they crept up to the edge and looked into it they could see it was also very deep, and there were many big, jagged rocks at the bottom.
uz: Bu juda keng bo'lak edi va ular chekkasiga chiqib, uni ko'rib chiqganda, uning chuqurligi ham ko'rinib turardi va uning pastki qismida ko'plab yirik toshlar bor edi.

en: The sides were so steep that none of them could climb down, and for a moment it seemed that their journey must end.
uz: Bu tomonlar shunchalik baland ediki, ularning hech biri tusholmadi va bir zum davomida ularning sayohatlari tugashi kerak bo'lganidek tuyuldi.

en: "What shall we do?" asked Dorothy despairingly.
uz: "Biz nima qilamiz?" - deb so'radi Dorotsiya umidsizlikka tushib.

en: "I haven't the faintest idea," said the Tin Woodman, and the Lion shook his shaggy mane and looked thoughtful.
uz: "Mening hech qanday fikrim yo'q", - dedi Tin Woodman va Arslon o'z shag'i qo'rqinchli ko'rinishini shiddatli ko'rindi.

en: But the Scarecrow said, "We cannot fly, that is certain.
uz: Ammo qo'rqinchli: "Biz uchib bo'lmaydi, shubhasiz.

en: Neither can we climb down into this great ditch.
uz: Biz ham bu ulkan quduqqa tusholmaymiz.

en: Therefore, if we cannot jump over it, we must stop where we are." "I think I could jump over it," said the Cowardly Lion, after measuring the distance carefully in his mind.
uz: Shuning uchun, agar o'sha yerdan o'tishning iloji bo'lmasa, hozir turgan joyimizda to'xtashimiz kerak". - Men o'sha yerdan o'tishim mumkin deb o'ylayman, - dedi qo'rqinchli Arslon, o'z ongida masofani sinchiklab o'lchab.

en: "Then we are all right," answered the Scarecrow, "for you can carry us all over on your back, one at a time." "Well, I'll try it," said the Lion.
uz: "O'shanda biz yaxshimiz", - deb javob berdi qo'rqinchli, "chunki siz bizni bir-birimiz bilan orqaga ko'tarishingiz mumkin". - Men buni sinab ko'raman, - dedi Arslon.

en: "Who will go first?" "I will," declared the Scarecrow, "for, if you found that you could not jump over the gulf, Dorothy would be killed, or the Tin Woodman badly dented on the rocks below.
uz: - Kim birinchi bo'ladi? - deb aytdi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli, - Men boraman, chunki agar siz ko'chadan sopoqlay olmasligingizni bilsangiz, Doroti o'ldirilgan bo'ladi yoki Tin Woodman pastdagi toshlarga yomon tushib ketgan bo'ladi.

en: But if I am on your back it will not matter so much, for the fall would not hurt me at all."
uz: Ammo agar men sizning orqangizda bo'lsam, bu muhim emas, chunki yiqilish menga hech qanday zarar bermaydi".

en: "I am terribly afraid of falling, myself," said the Cowardly Lion, "but I suppose there is nothing to do but try it.
uz: "Men ham tushishdan qo'rqaman, - dedi qo'rqoq sher, - lekin men buni sinab ko'rishdan boshqa hech qanday yo'l yo'q deb o'ylayman.

en: So get on my back and we will make the attempt." The Scarecrow sat upon the Lion's back, and the big beast walked to the edge of the gulf and crouched down.
uz: Shunday qilib, mening orqamda turing va biz harakat qilamiz". Qo'rqinchli Arslonning orqasida o'tirdi, ulkan hayvon esa ko'lning chegarasiga yetib kelib, yonboshladi.

en: "Why don't you run and jump?" asked the Scarecrow.
uz: "Nima uchun siz yugurib sakrashmaysiz?" - deb so'radi qo'rqinchli.

en: "Because that isn't the way we Lions do these things," he replied.
uz: U: "Biz, sherlar, bu ishlarni shunday qilmayapmiz", - deb javob berdi.

en: Then giving a great spring, he shot through the air and landed safely on the other side.
uz: So'ngra ajoyib ko'chma chizig'ini berib, u havo orqali o'ynagan va boshqa tomonga omon tushgan.

en: They were all greatly pleased to see how easily he did it, and after the Scarecrow had got down from his back the Lion sprang across the ditch again.
uz: U buni qanchalik oson bajarganini ko'rib, hamma juda xursand bo'ldi va qo'rqinchli o'z orqasidan tushgandan so'ng, Arslon yana qo'lga tushibdi.

en: Dorothy thought she would go next; so she took Toto in her arms and climbed on the Lion's back, holding tightly to his mane with one hand.
uz: Doroti keyingi o'rinni egallaydi deb o'yladi, shuning uchun Totoni qo'liga olib, Arslonning orqasidan chiqib, bir qo'li bilan uning qo'lini qattiq ushlab turdi.

en: The next moment it seemed as if she were flying through the air; and then, before she had time to think about it, she was safe on the other side.
uz: Keyingi daqiqada u havo orqali uchib borayotgandek tuyuldi va keyin, bu haqda o'ylashga vaqt yetmaguncha, u boshqa tomonda xavfsiz edi.

en: The Lion went back a third time and got the Tin Woodman, and then they all sat down for a few moments to give the beast a chance to rest, for his great leaps had made his breath short, and he panted like a big dog that has been running too long.
uz: Arslon uchinchi marta qaytib, Tin Woodmanni oldi va keyin hammasi bir necha daqiqaga o'tirib, hayvonga dam olish imkoniyatini berdilar, chunki uning katta sakrashlari uning nafasini qisqa qildi va u juda uzoq yugurgan katta it kabi nafas oldi.

en: They found the forest very thick on this side, and it looked dark and gloomy.
uz: Ular o'rmonning bu tomondan juda qalpoqligini va qorong'i va qorong'i ko'rinishini topdilar.

en: After the Lion had rested they started along the road of yellow brick, silently wondering, each in his own mind, if ever they would come to the end of the woods and reach the bright sunshine again.
uz: Arslon dam olganidan so'ng, ular o'zlarining o'ylarida, har biri o'z o'ylarida, hech qachon o'rmonning oxiriga kelib, yana yorqin quyoshga erishishlarini so'zsiz so'zlab, sariq tikan yo'li bo'ylab ketishdi.

en: To add to their discomfort, they soon heard strange noises in the depths of the forest, and the Lion whispered to them that it was in this part of the country that the Kalidahs lived.
uz: O'zlarining noqulayligini kuchaytirish uchun, ular o'rmonning chuqurliklarida g'alati tovushlarni eshitishdi va Arslon ularga kalidalar mamlakatning bu qismida yashayotganini shovqin qilib aytdi.

en: "What are the Kalidahs?" asked the girl.
uz: Qiz: "Kalidahlar nima?" - deb so'radi.

en: "They are monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers," replied the Lion, "and with claws so long and sharp that they could tear me in two as easily as I could kill Toto.
uz: "Ular g'ayritabiiy hayvonlardir, ular g'ayritabiiy bo'lib, idishlar kabi tanli va boshli bo'lib, toshlar kabi uzun va o'tkir bo'lib, meni Totoga o'ldirganimdek, ikkiga bo'g'ib yuborishlari mumkin.

en: I'm terribly afraid of the Kalidahs."
uz: Men kalidalardan juda qo'rqaman".

en: "I'm not surprised that you are," returned Dorothy.
uz: Doroti javob berdi: "Sen bunga hayron emasman.

en: "They must be dreadful beasts." The Lion was about to reply when suddenly they came to another gulf across the road.
uz: "Ular dahshatli hayvonlar bo'lishi kerak". - deb javob bermoqchi bo'lgan Arslon, to'satdan yo'l bo'ylab boshqa ko'chqaga yetib keldi.

en: But this one was so broad and deep that the Lion knew at once he could not leap across it.
uz: Ammo bu shunchalik keng va chuqur ediki, Arslon darhol o'sha yerga o'tishi mumkin emasligini tushungan.

en: So they sat down to consider what they should do, and after serious thought the Scarecrow said: "Here is a great tree, standing close to the ditch.
uz: Ular nima qilish kerakligini o'ylab o'tirishdi va qo'rqinchli hayvon jiddiy o'ylagandan so'ng shunday dedi: "Bola ko'ring, bu katta daraxt bo'lakning yonida turibdi.

en: If the Tin Woodman can chop it down, so that it will fall to the other side, we can walk across it easily." "That is a first-rate idea," said the Lion.
uz: Agar Tin Woodman uni kesib tashlasa, u boshqa tomonga tushib ketishi uchun, biz uni osonlikcha bosib o'tishimiz mumkin". - Bu birinchi darajali g'oya, - dedi Arslon.

en: "One would almost suspect you had brains in your head, instead of straw." The Woodman set to work at once, and so sharp was his axe that the tree was soon chopped nearly through.
uz: "Shuning o'rnagingda tuxumning o'rniga onging bor deb gumon qilish mumkin", - dedi Woodman darhol ishga tushdi va o'zining pichoqlari shunchalik o'tkir ediki, darhol daraxtni deyarli kesib tashladi.

en: Then the Lion put his strong front legs against the tree and pushed with all his might, and slowly the big tree tipped and fell with a crash across the ditch, with its top branches on the other side.
uz: Keyin Arslon o'zining kuchli old oyoqlarini daraxtga qo'ydi va butun kuchini ishga solib, katta daraxt asta-sekin burib tushdi va o'zlarining yuqori shoxlari boshqa tomonda bo'lib, cho'g'idan o'tib ketdi.

en: They had just started to cross this queer bridge when a sharp growl made them all look up, and to their horror they saw running toward them two great beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers.
uz: Ular o'sha g'ayritabiiy ko'prikdan o'tishni boshlashgan edi, lekin keskin qichqiriq ularning barchasini ko'tarib ko'rishga undagan va qo'rqinchlariga ko'ra, ularga qarab ikkita ulkan hayvonlar yugurib borayotganini ko'rishdi.

en: "They are the Kalidahs!" said the Cowardly Lion, beginning to tremble.
uz: "Ular Kalidahlar!" - dedi qo'rqinchli Arslon, qo'rqib boshladi.

en: "Quick!" cried the Scarecrow.
uz: "Shoshil!" - deb baqirdi qo'rqinchli.

en: "Let us cross over." So Dorothy went first, holding Toto in her arms, the Tin Woodman followed, and the Scarecrow came next.
uz: "O'tib ketaylik". Shunday qilib, Doroti birinchi bo'lib Totoni qo'llarida ushlab, Tin Woodman ketib, qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli qo'ng'iroq qildi.

en: The Lion, although he was certainly afraid, turned to face the Kalidahs, and then he gave so loud and terrible a roar that Dorothy screamed and the Scarecrow fell over backward, while even the fierce beasts stopped short and looked at him in surprise.
uz: Arslon, albatta qo'rqqan bo'lsa-da, Kalidalarga qaradi va keyin u shunchalik baland va dahshatli qichqiriq qildiki, Doroti qichqiriq qildi va qo'rqinchli hayvon orqa tomonga tushib qoldi, hatto yovvoyi hayvonlar ham to'xtadi va unga hayronlik bilan qaradi.

en: But, seeing they were bigger than the Lion, and remembering that there were two of them and only one of him, the Kalidahs again rushed forward, and the Lion crossed over the tree and turned to see what they would do next.
uz: Ammo ular Arslondan katta ekanini ko'rib, ulardan ikkitasini va faqat bittasini eslab, Kalidalar yana oldinga shoshishdi va Arslon daraxtni kesib o'tib, nima qilishini ko'rish uchun o'girilib ketdi.

en: Without stopping an instant the fierce beasts also began to cross the tree.
uz: Bir lahza to'xtamasdan yovvoyi hayvonlar ham daraxtni kesib o'tishni boshladilar.

en: And the Lion said to Dorothy: "We are lost, for they will surely tear us to pieces with their sharp claws.
uz: Arslon Dorotiga shunday dedi: "Biz yo'qolganmiz, chunki ular bizni o'z o'tkir to'qimalari bilan parchalab yuborishadi.

en: But stand close behind me, and I will fight them as long as I am alive." "Wait a minute!" called the Scarecrow.
uz: Lekin mening orqamda turinglar, men ular bilan tirik bo'lganimcha jang qilaman". "Bir daqiqa turinglar!" deb qo'rqitish qo'rquvi deb ataladi.

en: He had been thinking what was best to be done, and now he asked the Woodman to chop away the end of the tree that rested on their side of the ditch.
uz: U nima qilish kerakligi haqida o'ylab ko'rgan edi va endi o'rmon egasiga o'z tomoniga o'tirgan daraxtning bo'yinini kesib tashlashni so'radi.

en: The Tin Woodman began to use his axe at once, and, just as the two Kalidahs were nearly across, the tree fell with a crash into the gulf, carrying the ugly, snarling brutes with it, and both were dashed to pieces on the sharp rocks at the bottom.
uz: Tin Woodman darhol o'z pichoqidan foydalanishni boshladi va ikki Kalida o'rtasida yaqinlashib qolganida, daraxt ko'chga tushib, o'zida qo'rqinchli, qichqiriqli hayvonlarni olib tushdi va ikkalasi ham quviq toshlar ustida parchalanib ketdi.

en: "Well," said the Cowardly Lion, drawing a long breath of relief, "I see we are going to live a little while longer, and I am glad of it, for it must be a very uncomfortable thing not to be alive.
uz: "Ham, - dedi qo'rqoq sher, taskinli nafas olib, - ko'rib turibmanki, biz biroz ko'proq umr ko'ramiz va bundan xursandman, chunki tirik bo'lmaslik juda noqulay bo'lishi kerak.

en: Those creatures frightened me so badly that my heart is beating yet." "Ah," said the Tin Woodman sadly, "I wish I had a heart to beat." This adventure made the travelers more anxious than ever to get out of the forest, and they walked so fast that Dorothy became tired, and had to ride on the Lion's back.
uz: O'sha hayvonlar meni shunchalik qo'rqitdiki, yuragim hali ham urib ketyapti". "A, - dedi Tin Woodman, - agar urish uchun yuragim bo'lsa edi", - dedi. "Bu sarguzasht sayohatchilarni o'rmondan chiqib ketish uchun har qachongidan ham ko'proq tashvishlantirgan va ular shunchalik tez yurishganki, Doroti charchagan va Arslonning orqasida otlanishgan.

en: To their great joy the trees became thinner the farther they advanced, and in the afternoon they suddenly came upon a broad river, flowing swiftly just before them.
uz: Ularning katta quvonchlariga ko'ra, daraxtlar o'zlarining yo'nalishlarini yanada kengaytirib, kechqurun birdan ularning oldidan tez oqib o'tgan keng daryoga tushib qolishdi.

en: On the other side of the water they could see the road of yellow brick running through a beautiful country, with green meadows dotted with bright flowers and all the road bordered with trees hanging full of delicious fruits.
uz: Suvning boshqa tomonasida ular go'zal mamlakatdan o'tgan sari sariq tikanlardan yasalgan yo'lni ko'rishardi, yashil bo'laklar yorqin gullar bilan to'plandi va butun yo'l daraxtlar bilan bog'liq edi, ular go'zal mevalar bilan to'lgan edi.

en: They were greatly pleased to see this delightful country before them.
uz: Ular bu ajoyib yurtni ko'rishdan juda xursand bo'lishgan.

en: "How shall we cross the river?" asked Dorothy.
uz: "Biz daryoni qanday kesib o'tamiz?" - deb so'radi Dorotsiya.

en: "That is easily done," replied the Scarecrow.
uz: "Bu osonlikcha amalga oshadi", - deb javob berdi qo'rqinchli.

en: "The Tin Woodman must build us a raft, so we can float to the other side."
uz: "Tin Woodman biz uchun qayiq qurishi kerak, shunda biz boshqa tomonga suzishimiz mumkin".

en: So the Woodman took his axe and began to chop down small trees to make a raft, and while he was busy at this the Scarecrow found on the riverbank a tree full of fine fruit.
uz: O'simlik o'g'li esa o'z baltini olib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'simliklarni kesib tashlashga kirishibdi va o'sha ish bilan band bo'lganida, qo'rqinchchi daryo qirg'og'ida go'zal mevalarga to'lgan daraxtni topdi.

en: This pleased Dorothy, who had eaten nothing but nuts all day, and she made a hearty meal of the ripe fruit.
uz: Bu kun bo'yi yong'oqlardan boshqa hech narsa yemagan Dorotsiyaga yoqdi va u o'simlik mevalardan mehribon taom tayyorladi.

en: But it takes time to make a raft, even when one is as industrious and untiring as the Tin Woodman, and when night came the work was not done.
uz: Ammo kema qurish uchun vaqt kerak bo'ladi, hatto u Tin Woodman kabi mehnatsevar va charchamayotgan bo'lsa ham, kechasi esa ish bitmagan bo'lsa ham.

en: So they found a cozy place under the trees where they slept well until the morning; and Dorothy dreamed of the Emerald City, and of the good Wizard Oz, who would soon send her back to her own home again.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular daraxtlar ostida qulay joy topdilar va ertalabgacha yaxshi uxladilar; Doroti esa Esmerald shahrini va tez orada uni o'z uyiga qaytarib yuboradigan yaxshi sehrgar Ozni orzu qildi.

en: Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field Our little party of travelers awakened the next morning refreshed and full of hope, and Dorothy breakfasted like a princess off peaches and plums from the trees beside the river.
uz: VIII bob: O'limga sabab bo'lgan qachondir maydonimiz Bizning sayohatchilarning kichik guruhimiz ertasi kuni ertalab o'zini ta'minlab, umid bilan to'lgan holda uyg'ongan va Doroti daryo bo'yidagi daraxtlardan chiroqlar va plungalar kabi printsesa kabi nonushta qilib ovqatlanayotgan edi.

en: Behind them was the dark forest they had passed safely through, although they had suffered many discouragements; but before them was a lovely, sunny country that seemed to beckon them on to the Emerald City.
uz: Ularning orqasida ular xavfsiz o'tgan qorong'i o'rmon bor edi, ammo ko'pgina tushkunlikka tushishgan edi; lekin ularning orqasida go'zal, quyoshli mamlakat bor edi va bu ularni Emerald Cityga jalb qilgan bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: To be sure, the broad river now cut them off from this beautiful land.
uz: Shubhasizki, keng daryo endi ularni bu go'zal yurtdan kesib tashladi.

en: But the raft was nearly done, and after the Tin Woodman had cut a few more logs and fastened them together with wooden pins, they were ready to start.
uz: Ammo to'plangan ish deyarli tugadi va Tin Woodman yana bir necha daraxtni kesib, ularni yog'och cho'g'lar bilan birlashtirib qo'yganidan so'ng, ular ishga tushishga tayyor bo'lishdi.

en: Dorothy sat down in the middle of the raft and held Toto in her arms.
uz: Doroti to'fonning o'rtasida o'tirib, Totoni qo'llarida ushlab turdi.

en: When the Cowardly Lion stepped upon the raft it tipped badly, for he was big and heavy; but the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman stood upon the other end to steady it, and they had long poles in their hands to push the raft through the water.
uz: Qo'rqinchli Arslon qayiqqa qadam bosganida, u og'ir va katta bo'lgani uchun yomon tiklandi; lekin qo'rqinchli va qalin o'simlik uni turg'atish uchun boshqa tomonda turardi va qo'llarida qayiqni suvdan o'tkazishga yordam beradigan uzun ustunlar bor edi.

en: They got along quite well at first, but when they reached the middle of the river the swift current swept the raft downstream, farther and farther away from the road of yellow brick.
uz: Boshida ular juda yaxshi munosabatda bo'lishdi, lekin daryo o'rtalariga yetganlarida, tezkor oqim daryo bo'ylab, sariq g'isht yo'lidan uzoqroq va uzoqroq bo'lib ketadi.

en: And the water grew so deep that the long poles would not touch the bottom.
uz: Suv shunchalik chuqur bo'lganki, uzun poyalar quyiga tegolmadi.

en: "This is bad," said the Tin Woodman, "for if we cannot get to the land we shall be carried into the country of the Wicked Witch of the
uz: "Bu yomon narsa", - dedi Tin Woodman, "agar biz yerga yetib bormasak, biz Yovuz sehrgarning yurtiga olib ketiladigan bo'lamiz.

en: West, and she will enchant us and make us her slaves." "And then I should get no brains," said the Scarecrow.
uz: G'arbiy, u bizni sehrlab, qul qilib oladi". - "O'shanda men aqldan ozaman", dedi qo'rqinchli.

en: "And I should get no courage," said the Cowardly Lion.
uz: "Va men jasoratga ega bo'lmasam kerak", dedi qo'rqoq sher.

en: "And I should get no heart," said the Tin Woodman.
uz: "Va men yuragim bo'lmasligi kerak", dedi Tin Woodman.

en: "And I should never get back to Kansas," said Dorothy.
uz: "Va men hech qachon Kanzasga qaytib kelmasligim kerak", dedi Doroti.

en: "We must certainly get to the Emerald City if we can," the Scarecrow continued, and he pushed so hard on his long pole that it stuck fast in the mud at the bottom of the river.
uz: "Agar iloji bo'lsa, biz Emerald Cityga borishimiz kerak", - deb davom etdi qo'rqitgich va u o'zining uzun ustunini shunchalik qattiq bosib o'tdiki, u daryo tubidagi loyga qattiq yopishib qoldi.

en: Then, before he could pull it out again—or let go—the raft was swept away, and the poor Scarecrow left clinging to the pole in the middle of the river.
uz: Keyin, uni yana chiqarib tashlamadan yoki qo'yib yuborishdan oldin, qayiq olib ketildi va kambag'al qo'rqinchli daryo o'rtasida bo'lgan ustunga yopishib qoldi.

en: "Good-bye!" he called after them, and they were very sorry to leave him.
uz: "Xudojo'y!" deb ularni chaqirganida, ular uni tashlab ketishlaridan juda afsuslanishdi.

en: Indeed, the Tin Woodman began to cry, but fortunately remembered that he might rust, and so dried his tears on Dorothy's apron.
uz: Darhaqiqat, Tin Woodman yig'lay boshladi, ammo omad uchun u o'zining rang-barang bo'lishi mumkinligini esladi va o'z ko'z yoshlarini Dorotining choriq ustiga quritdi.

en: Of course this was a bad thing for the Scarecrow.
uz: Albatta, bu qo'rqinchli hayvon uchun yomon narsa edi.

en: "I am now worse off than when I first met Dorothy," he thought.
uz: U o'zicha: "Dorothy bilan uchrashganimda bo'lganiga qaraganda, hozir yomon ahvolda edim.

en: "Then, I was stuck on a pole in a cornfield, where I could make- believe scare the crows, at any rate.
uz: "O'shanda men momaqaldosh ekinzordagi ustunga yopishib qoldim, u yerda qo'rqinchlarni qo'rqitish uchun o'zimni qo'rqtirardim.

en: But surely there is no use for a Scarecrow stuck on a pole in the middle of a river.
uz: Ammo, albatta, daryo o'rtasida bo'lgan ustunga qo'yib qo'yilgan qo'rquvchining foydasi yo'q.

en: I am afraid I shall never have any brains, after all!" Down the stream the raft floated, and the poor Scarecrow was left far behind.
uz: Qo'rqamanki, hech qachon aql-idrokim bo'lmaydi!" - deb qo'rqaman.

en: Then the Lion said: "Something must be done to save us.
uz: Keyin Arslon: "Bizni qutqarish uchun biror narsa qilish kerak.

en: I think I can swim to the shore and pull the raft after me, if you will only hold fast to the tip of my tail." So he sprang into the water, and the Tin Woodman caught fast hold of his tail.

en: Then the Lion began to swim with all his might toward the shore.
uz: Shundan so'ng Arslon qirg'oqqa qarab butun kuchini ishga solib, suzishni boshladi.

en: It was hard work, although he was so big; but by and by they were drawn out of the current, and then Dorothy took the Tin Woodman's long pole and helped push the raft to the land.
uz: U juda katta bo'lsa-da, bu juda qiyin ish edi; lekin vaqt o'tib ular oqimdan chiqarib tashlandilar va keyin Doroti Tin Woodmanning uzun ustunini olib, qayiqni quruqlikka itishga yordam berdi.

en: They were all tired out when they reached the shore at last and stepped off upon the pretty green grass, and they also knew that the stream had carried them a long way past the road of yellow brick that led to the Emerald City.
uz: Ular nihoyat qirg'oqqa yetib, chiroyli yashil o'tlar ustida qadam qo'yishganida hamma charchagan edi va daryo ularni Sarimush shaharga olib boradigan sariq toshdan yasalgan yo'ldan uzoq yo'l o'tib olib ketganini bilishardi.

en: "What shall we do now?" asked the Tin Woodman, as the Lion lay down on the grass to let the sun dry him.
uz: "Bundan keyin nima qilamiz?" - deb so'ragan Tin Woodman, sher quyosh uni quritish uchun o'tlar ustida yotgan edi.

en: "We must get back to the road, in some way," said Dorothy.
uz: "Biz yo'lga qaytib borishimiz kerak", dedi Doroti.

en: "The best plan will be to walk along the riverbank until we come to the road again," remarked the Lion.
uz: "O'sha yo'lga qaytmagunimizcha, eng yaxshi reja - daryo bo'yida yurishdir", - dedi Arslon.

en: So, when they were rested, Dorothy picked up her basket and they started along the grassy bank, to the road from which the river had carried them.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular dam olgach, Doroti savatini olib, daryo ularni olib borgan yo'lga, o'tli qirg'oq bo'yi bo'ylab ketishdi.

en: It was a lovely country, with plenty of flowers and fruit trees and sunshine to cheer them, and had they not felt so sorry for the poor Scarecrow, they could have been very happy.

en: They walked along as fast as they could, Dorothy only stopping once to pick a beautiful flower; and after a time the Tin Woodman cried out: "Look!" Then they all looked at the river and saw the Scarecrow perched upon his pole in the middle of the water, looking very lonely and sad.
uz: Ular iloji boricha tezroq yurishdi, Doroti go'zal gulni olish uchun faqat bir marta to'xtadi va bir muncha vaqt o'tgach, Tin Woodman: "Qarang!" - deb baqirdi. Keyin hammalari daryoga qarab, qo'rqinchli qo'zg'oloning suvning o'rtasida o'zining ustunida o'tirganini ko'rishdi.

en: "Who are you and where are you going?" asked the Stork.
uz: "Siz kimsiz va qayerga ketyapsiz?" - deb so'radi Stork.

en: "I am Dorothy," answered the girl, "and these are my friends, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion; and we are going to the Emerald City." "This isn't the road," said the Stork, as she twisted her long neck and looked sharply at the queer party.
uz: Qiz javob berdi: "Men Dorothyman va bu mening do'stlarim, Tin Woodman va Qo'rqoq Arslondir va biz Emerald Cityga boramiz". "Bu yo'l emas", dedi Stork, u o'zining uzun bo'yni burib, g'ayritabiiy partiyaga keskin qaradi.

en: "I know it," returned Dorothy, "but we have lost the Scarecrow, and are wondering how we shall get him again." "Where is he?" asked the Stork.
uz: - Bilaman, - deb javob berdi Doroti, - lekin qo'rqinchli qo'zg'olonni yo'qotganmiz va uni qaytarib olishni xohlayotganmiz. - U qayerda? - deb so'radi qo'rqinchli.

en: "Over there in the river," answered the little girl.
uz: "O'sha yerda, daryoda", deb javob berdi qizcha.

en: "If he wasn't so big and heavy I would get him for you," remarked the Stork.
uz: "Agar u shunchalik katta va og'ir bo'lmaganida, men uni siz uchun olib ketardim", - dedi Stork.

en: "He isn't heavy a bit," said Dorothy eagerly, "for he is stuffed with straw; and if you will bring him back to us, we shall thank you ever and ever so much." "Well, I'll try," said the Stork, "but if I find he is too heavy to carry I shall have to drop him in the river again." So the big bird flew into the air and over the water till she came to where the Scarecrow was perched upon his pole.
uz: "U biroz og'ir emas", - dedi Doroti qizg'inlik bilan, "chunki u cho'g'a bilan to'ldirilgan; agar siz uni bizga qaytarib kelsangiz, biz sizga har doim ham minnatdorchilik bildiramiz". - "Agar men uni ko'tarib olish uchun juda og'ir deb topsam, uni yana daryoga tashlashim kerak bo'ladi", - dedi Stork.

en: Then the Stork with her great claws grabbed the Scarecrow by the arm and carried him up into the air and back to the bank, where Dorothy and the Lion and the Tin Woodman and Toto were sitting.
uz: Keyin Stork o'zining ulkan barmoqlari bilan qo'lidan qo'lga olib, qo'rqinchli qo'zg'orni havoga ko'tarib, qaytib Dorothy va Arslon, Tin Woodman va Toto o'tirgan qirg'oqqa yetib bordi.

en: When the Scarecrow found himself among his friends again, he was so happy that he hugged them all, even the Lion and Toto; and as they walked along he sang "Tol-de-ri-de-oh!" at every step, he felt so gay.
uz: Qo'rqinchli yana o'z do'stlari orasida bo'lganida, u shunchalik xursand bo'ldiki, hammalarini, hatto Arslon va Totoni ham quchoqlab olgan va ular yo'lda ketayotganda u har qadamda "Tol-de-ri-de-oh!" deb kuylagan.

en: "I was afraid I should have to stay in the river forever," he said, "but the kind Stork saved me, and if I ever get any brains I shall find the Stork again and do her some kindness in return." "That's all right," said the Stork, who was flying along beside them.
uz: U shunday dedi: "Men o'zimni abadiy daryoda qoldirishim kerak deb qo'rqardim, lekin menga o'xshash Stork qutqardi va agar biror marta aql-idrokga ega bo'lsam, men Stork-ni yana topib, o'z navbatida unga mehribonlik ko'rsataman".

en: "I always like to help anyone in trouble.
uz: "Men har doim muammolarga duch kelgan har bir kishiga yordam berishni yaxshi ko'raman.

en: But I must go now, for my babies are waiting in the nest for me.
uz: Lekin men borishim kerak, chunki bolalarim meni o'rmonda kutmoqdalar.

en: I hope you will find the Emerald City and that Oz will help you." "Thank you," replied Dorothy, and then the kind Stork flew into the air and was soon out of sight.
uz: Umid qilamanki, siz Emerald Cityni topasiz va Oz sizga yordam beradi". - "Rahmat", - deb javob berdi Doroti, so'ngra esa o'sha turdagi Stork havoga uchib ketdi va tez orada ko'rinmas edi.

en: They walked along listening to the singing of the brightly colored birds and looking at the lovely flowers which now became so thick
uz: Ular yorqin rangli qushlarning kuylashiga quloq solib, chiroyli gullarni ko'rib yurishgan.

en: that the ground was carpeted with them.
uz: Ular bilan yerni ko'ylaklar bilan qoplashgan.

en: There were big yellow and white and blue and purple blossoms, besides great clusters of scarlet poppies, which were so brilliant in color they almost dazzled Dorothy's eyes.
uz: U yerda katta sariq, oq, ko'k va bo'yoq gullar bor edi, shu bilan birga, Dorothyning ko'zlarini deyarli cho'ktiradigan rangli qizil qovoqlarning katta to'plamlari ham bor edi.

en: "Aren't they beautiful?" the girl asked, as she breathed in the spicy scent of the bright flowers.
uz: "Bular chiroyli emasmi?" - deb so'radi qizcha, yorqin gullarning sharbatli hidini nafas olib.

en: "I suppose so," answered the Scarecrow.
uz: - O'ylaymanki, shunday, - deb javob berdi qo'rqinchli.

en: "When I have brains, I shall probably like them better." "If I only had a heart, I should love them," added the Tin Woodman.
uz: "Menda miya bo'lganda, ehtimol, ularni ko'proq yoqtiraman". "Agar faqat yuragim bo'lganida, ularni yaxshi ko'raman", - deb qo'shimcha qildi Tin Woodman.

en: "I always did like flowers," said the Lion.
uz: "Men doimo gullarni yaxshi ko'rardim", - dedi Arslon.

en: "They seem so helpless and frail.
uz: "Ular juda yordamsiz va zaif ko'rinadi.

en: But there are none in the forest so bright as these." They now came upon more and more of the big scarlet poppies, and fewer and fewer of the other flowers; and soon they found themselves in the midst of a great meadow of poppies.
uz: Ammo o'rmonda bu kabi chiroqlar yo'q". Endi ular ko'proq katta qizil qovoqlarni va boshqa gullarni ko'proq ko'rishardi va tez orada o'zlarini katta qovoqlarning o'rtasida topdilar.

en: Now it is well known that when there are many of these flowers together their odor is so powerful that anyone who breathes it falls asleep, and if the sleeper is not carried away from the scent of the flowers, he sleeps on and on forever.
uz: Endi yaxshi ma'lumki, bu gullarning ko'pchiligi bir-biri bilan birga bo'lganda, ularning hidlari shunchalik kuchli bo'ladiki, uni nafas olgan har bir kishi uxlab ketadi va agar uxlovchi gullarning hididan uzoqlashtirilmasa, u abadiy uxlaydi.

en: But Dorothy did not know this, nor could she get away from the bright red flowers that were everywhere about; so presently her eyes grew heavy and she felt she must sit down to rest and to sleep.
uz: Ammo Doroti buni bilmas edi va hamma joyda bo'lgan chiroq qizil gullardan qochib ketolmas edi; shuning uchun uning ko'zlari og'irlashib, uxlash uchun o'tirishi kerakligini his qildi.

en: But the Tin Woodman would not let her do this.
uz: Ammo Tin Woodman unga bunday qilishga yo'l qo'ymaydi.

en: "We must hurry and get back to the road of yellow brick before dark," he said; and the Scarecrow agreed with him.
uz: U: "Qo'r bo'lishdan oldin biz darrov sariq tikan yo'liga qaytishimiz kerak", - dedi va qo'rqinchli hayvon unga rozi bo'ldi.

en: So they kept walking until Dorothy could stand no longer.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular Dorothy endi turolmaguncha yurishda davom etishdi.

en: Her eyes closed in spite of herself and she forgot where she was and fell among the poppies, fast asleep.
uz: O'ziga qaramasdan ko'zlarini yopib, qayerdaligini unutib qo'ydi va o'simliklar orasida uxlab qoldi.

en: "What shall we do?" asked the Tin Woodman.
uz: "Biz nima qilishimiz kerak?" - deb so'radi Tin Woodman.

en: "If we leave her here she will die," said the Lion.
uz: "Agar biz uni bu yerda qoldirsak, u o'ladi", - dedi Arslon.

en: "The smell of the flowers is killing us all.
uz: Gullarning hidlari hammamizni o'ldirmoqda.

en: I myself can scarcely keep my eyes open, and the dog is asleep already."
uz: Men o'zim ham ko'zimni ocholmayapman va it allaqachon uxlab qoldi".

en: It was true; Toto had fallen down beside his little mistress.
uz: To'to o'z sevimli xotini yonida yiqilib ketgan edi.

en: But the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, not being made of flesh, were not troubled by the scent of the flowers.
uz: Ammo qo'rqinchli hayvon va qalin yog'ochni, ular go'shtdan emas, balki gullarning hididan xavotirlanmagan.

en: "Run fast," said the Scarecrow to the Lion, "and get out of this deadly flower bed as soon as you can.
uz: "Shoshil", - dedi qo'rqinchli aslanga, "va imkon qadar tezroq bu o'limga olib boradigan gulxonadan chiqib keting.

en: We will bring the little girl with us, but if you should fall asleep you are too big to be carried." So the Lion aroused himself and bounded forward as fast as he could go.
uz: Kichkina qizchani o'zimiz bilan olib boramiz, lekin uxlab ketsangiz, siz ko'tarib olinmaydigan darajada katta bo'lasiz".Shunga ko'ra Arslon o'zini uyg'otdi va imkon qadar tezroq oldinga o'tdi.

en: In a moment he was out of sight.
uz: Bir zumda u ko'rinmas edi.

en: "Let us make a chair with our hands and carry her," said the Scarecrow.
uz: "O'z qo'llarimiz bilan o'rindiqni tayyorlab, uni ko'tarib boraylik", - dedi qo'rqinchli.

en: So they picked up Toto and put the dog in Dorothy's lap, and then they made a chair with their hands for the seat and their arms for the arms and carried the sleeping girl between them through the flowers.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular Totoni olib, itni Dorotining qoshiga qo'yishdi, so'ngra o'rindiq uchun qo'llari bilan o'rindiqni, qo'llari bilan qo'llari bilan qo'llari bilan o'rindiqni qurib, o'zlarining o'rtasida gullar orqali uxlayotgan qizni ko'tarib olishdi.

en: On and on they walked, and it seemed that the great carpet of deadly flowers that surrounded them would never end.
uz: Ular bor-yo'g'i yurishgan va atrofidagi o'limli gullardan iborat ulkan ko'ylak hech qachon tugamaydi deb o'ylardilar.

en: They followed the bend of the river, and at last came upon their friend the Lion, lying fast asleep among the poppies.
uz: Ular daryo bo'yinini kuzatib borishdi va nihoyat, o'z do'stlari Arslonni ko'rishdi.

en: The flowers had been too strong for the huge beast and he had given up at last, and fallen only a short distance from the end of the poppy bed, where the sweet grass spread in beautiful green fields before them.
uz: Gullar ulkan hayvon uchun juda kuchli edi va u nihoyat taslim bo'lib, o'zidan oldin go'zal o'tlar ko'plab yashil maydonlarda tarqalgan maydonning so'ngidan biroz uzoqlikda tushib qoldi.

en: "We can do nothing for him," said the Tin Woodman, sadly; "for he is much too heavy to lift.
uz: "Biz u uchun hech narsa qila olmaymiz", - dedi Tin Woodman, afsuski, "chunki u ko'tarish uchun juda og'ir.

en: We must leave him here to sleep on forever, and perhaps he will dream that he has found courage at last." "I'm sorry," said the Scarecrow.
uz: Biz uni bu yerda abadiy uxlab qolishga qoldirishimiz kerak va ehtimol u oxir-oqibat jasorat topganini orzu qiladi". - Afsus, - dedi qo'rqinchli.

en: "The Lion was a very good comrade for one so cowardly.
uz: "Arslon bunday qo'rqoq odam uchun juda yaxshi hamroh edi.

en: But let us go on." They carried the sleeping girl to a pretty spot beside the river, far enough from the poppy field to prevent her breathing any more of the poison of the flowers, and here they laid her gently on the soft grass and waited for the fresh breeze to waken her.
uz: Lekin keling, davom etaylik". Ular uxlayotgan qizni daryo bo'yiga olib ketishdi, bu yerda uni gullarning zaharidan yana nafas olishni to'xtatish uchun ko'p mayda bo'lgan maydonlardan uzoqroq edi va ular uni yumush o'tlar ustida muloyimlik bilan qo'yib, yangi shamolning uyg'onishini kutishdi.

en: Chapter IX The Queen of the Field Mice "We cannot be far from the road of yellow brick, now," remarked the Scarecrow, as he stood beside the girl, "for we have come nearly as far as the river carried us away." The Tin Woodman was about to reply when he heard a low growl, and turning his head (which worked beautifully on hinges) he saw a strange beast come bounding over the grass toward them.
uz: IX bob - Dalali tovuqlarning qiroli "Biz sariq g'isht yo'lidan uzoq bo'lmaymiz, endi", - dedi qo'rqinchli qizning yonida turib, "chunki biz deyarli daryo bizni olib ketganigacha yetib keldik". Tin o'g'li past qichqirishni eshitib, javob bermoqchi edi va boshini burib (bu tovuqlar ustida chiroyli ishlaydi) o'ziga qarab o'sha o'g'illar ustida bir g'ayritabiiy hayvon kelib turishini ko'rdi.

en: It was, indeed, a great yellow Wildcat, and the Woodman thought it must be chasing something, for its ears were lying close to its head and its mouth was wide open, showing two rows of ugly teeth, while its red eyes glowed like balls of fire.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bu katta sariq yovvoyi qush edi va Woodman uning quloqlari uning boshiga yaqin, og'zi esa keng ochilgan bo'lib, ikki qator dahshatli tishlarni ko'rsatgan bo'lsa-da, qizil ko'zlari esa olov to'plamlari kabi yoritib turgan deb o'yladi.

en: As it came nearer the Tin Woodman saw that running before the beast was a little gray field mouse, and although he had no heart he knew it was wrong for the Wildcat to try to kill such a pretty, harmless creature.
uz: U yaqinlashib kelayotganda, Tin Woodman hayvonning oldidan yugurayotgan kichkinagina griz maydon egasi ekanligini ko'rdi va yuragi yo'q bo'lsa-da, yovvoyi mushukning bunday chiroyli, zararsiz mavjudotni o'ldirishga urinishi noto'g'ri ekanligini bilardi.

en: So the Woodman raised his axe, and as the Wildcat ran by he gave it a quick blow that cut the beast's head clean off from its body, and it rolled over at his feet in two pieces.
uz: O'simlik o'g'li esa o'z baltini ko'tarib, yovvoyi mushuk o'tib ketayotganda, unga tezda urib, hayvonning boshi uning tanasidan kesildi va u oyoqlari oldida ikki bo'lakga aylanib ketdi.

en: The field mouse, now that it was freed from its enemy, stopped short; and coming slowly up to the Woodman it said, in a squeaky little voice: "Oh, thank you!
uz: Tush, endi dushman qo'lidan ozod bo'lganidan so'ng, to'xtab qoldi va oz-oz bo'lib o'rmon odamga yaqinlashib, qichqiriqsiz ovoz bilan shunday dedi: "Oh, rahmat!

en: Thank you ever so much for saving my life."
uz: Hayotimni qutqardingiz uchun sizga katta rahmat".

en: "Don't speak of it, I beg of you," replied the Woodman.
uz: "Bu haqda gapirmang, iltijo qilaman", - deb javob berdi Woodman.

en: "I have no heart, you know, so I am careful to help all those who may need a friend, even if it happens to be only a mouse." "Only a mouse!" cried the little animal, indignantly.
uz: "Mening yuragim yo'q, bilasiz, shuning uchun do'stga muhtoj bo'lganlarga yordam berishga harakat qilaman, hatto u faqatgina tovuq bo'lsa ham". - "Yegan tovuq!" - deb hayqirdi kichkina hayvon.

en: "Why, I am a Queen—the Queen of all the Field Mice!" "Oh, indeed," said the Woodman, making a bow.
uz: "Men barcha maydon tuproqlarining qiroli ekanman!" - dedi o'rmonchi, o'z ko'zidan o'tkazib.

en: "Therefore you have done a great deed, as well as a brave one, in saving my life," added the Queen.
uz: "Shuning uchun siz mening hayotimni qutqarishda katta va jasoratli ish qildingiz", - deb qo'shib qo'ydi kraliça.

en: At that moment several mice were seen running up as fast as their little legs could carry them, and when they saw their Queen they exclaimed: "Oh, your Majesty, we thought you would be killed!
uz: O'sha paytda bir nechta tovuqlar o'zlarining kichik oyoqlari ko'tarishi mumkin bo'lgan tezlikda yugurib borayotganini ko'rishdi va ular o'z kralichasini ko'rganlarida: "O, Oliy hukmdor, biz sizni o'ldirishingizni o'ylagan edik!

en: How did you manage to escape the great Wildcat?" They all bowed so low to the little Queen that they almost stood upon their heads.
uz: Qanday qilib siz ulkan yovvoyi mushukdan qochishga muvaffaq bo'ldingiz?" - deyishdi. Ularning hammasi kichkina Qirolichaga shunchalik quvonishganki, deyarli boshlari ustida turishibdi.

en: "This funny tin man," she answered, "killed the Wildcat and saved my life.
uz: U shunday javob berdi: "Bu g'alati qadoq odam yovvoyi mushukni o'ldirib, hayotimni qutqardi.

en: So hereafter you must all serve him, and obey his slightest wish." "We will!" cried all the mice, in a shrill chorus.
uz: Shunday qilib, bundan buyon hammangiz unga xizmat qilib, uning eng kichik istaklariga quloq solishingiz kerak". - "Biz qilamiz!" - deb baqirdi barcha tuproqlar, shrill chorusda.

en: And then they scampered in all directions, for Toto had awakened from his sleep, and seeing all these mice around him he gave one bark of delight and jumped right into the middle of the group.
uz: So'ngra ular har tomonga ko'tarildilar, chunki Toto uxlaganidan uyg'onib, atrofidagi shuncha tovuqlarni ko'rib, u bir marta quvonchga to'lib, guruhning o'rtasida o'tib ketdi.

en: Toto had always loved to chase mice when he lived in Kansas, and he saw no harm in it.
uz: To'to Kanzasda yashar ekan, juda yaxshi ko'rgan edi va bu uning zararini ko'rmadi.

en: But the Tin Woodman caught the dog in his arms and held him tight, while he called to the mice, "Come back!
uz: Ammo Tin Woodman itni qo'liga olib, qattiq ushlab turdi va u tovuqlarga: "Qayta kelinglar!

en: Toto shall not hurt you." At this the Queen of the Mice stuck her head out from underneath a clump of grass and asked, in a timid voice, "Are you sure he will not bite us?" "I will not let him," said the Woodman; "so do not be afraid."
uz: Toto sizga zarar etkazmaydi". Shu payt Tovuqlar Qiroliasi o'z boshini o't daraxtining pastligidan chiqarib, qo'rqinchli ovoz bilan so'radi: "U bizni urmasligiga ishonchingiz komilmi?" - "Unga yo'l qo'ymayman", - dedi o'rmon. - Shunday qilib, qo'rqma".

en: One by one the mice came creeping back, and Toto did not bark again, although he tried to get out of the Woodman's arms, and would have bitten him had he not known very well he was made of tin.
uz: Tovuqlar birma-bir orqaga qaytishdi va Toto yana qichqirmadi, garchi u Woodmanning qo'lidan chiqib ketishga harakat qilgan bo'lsa-da, agar o'zi tangadan yasalganligini yaxshi bilmaganida uni o'g'irlagan bo'lar edi.

en: Finally one of the biggest mice spoke.
uz: Nihoyat, eng yirik toshlardan biri gapirdi.

en: "Is there anything we can do," it asked, "to repay you for saving the life of our Queen?" "Nothing that I know of," answered the Woodman; but the Scarecrow, who had been trying to think, but could not because his head was stuffed with straw, said, quickly, "Oh, yes; you can save our friend, the Cowardly Lion, who is asleep in the poppy bed."
