uz: "Sizni biz bilan qoldirishni xohlaymiz, lekin agar siz Kanzasga qaytishni xohlasangiz, umid qilamanki, siz yo'l topasiz". Keyin u tashqi devorning darvozasini ochdi va ular yo'lga chiqishdi.

en: The sun shone brightly as our friends turned their faces toward the Land of the South.
uz: Do'stlarimiz yuzlarini Janubiy yurtga qaratib, quyoshni ko'tarishardi.

en: They were all in the best of spirits, and laughed and chatted together.
uz: Ularning barchasi yaxshi ruhda edilar va birga kulishdi va suhbatlashdilar.

en: Dorothy was once more filled with the hope of getting home, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were glad to be of use to her.
uz: Dorotsiya yana uyga qaytish umidi bilan to'lib-toshdi va Qo'rqinchli va Tin Woodman unga foydali bo'lishdan xursand bo'lishdi.

en: As for the Lion, he sniffed the fresh air with delight and whisked his tail from side to side in pure joy at being in the country again, while Toto ran around them and chased the moths and butterflies, barking merrily all the time.
uz: Arslonga kelsak, u yangi havoga hayajon bilan kirdi va yana qishloqda bo'lganidan chindan ham xursand bo'lib, quyruqini yon-yurtga o'tkazib yubordi, To'to esa ularning atrofida yugurib, ko'piklar va ko'piklarni quvg'in qilib, doimo quvonch bilan qichqirdi.

en: "City life does not agree with me at all," remarked the Lion, as they walked along at a brisk pace.
uz: Shahardagi hayot men bilan hech qanday o'xshash emas, - deb aytdi Arslon, ular tez yurishganida.

en: "I have lost much flesh since I lived there, and now I am anxious for a chance to show the other beasts how courageous I have grown." They now turned and took a last look at the Emerald City.
uz: "O'sha yerda yashaganimdan beri ko'p go'sht yo'qotdim va endi boshqa hayvonlarga qanchalik jasoratli bo'lganimni ko'rsatish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lishni istayman". Ular endi orqaga burildilar va Emerald Cityga so'nggi marta nazar tashladilar.

en: All they could see was a mass of towers and steeples behind the green walls, and high up above everything the spires and dome of the Palace of Oz.
uz: Ular yashil devorlar ortida ko'rishlari mumkin bo'lgan yagona to'rlar va burjlar, va hamma narsadan yuqori bo'lgan O'z saroyining burjlari va qo'llari.

en: "Oz was not such a bad Wizard, after all," said the Tin Woodman, as he felt his heart rattling around in his breast.
uz: "Oz yomon sehrgar emas edi, xolos", - dedi Tin Woodman, chunki u ko'krakidagi yuragining shovqinini his qilardi.

en: "He knew how to give me brains, and very good brains, too," said the Scarecrow.
uz: "U menga miyamni va juda yaxshi miyamni qanday berish kerakligini bilardi", - dedi qo'rqitgich.

en: "If Oz had taken a dose of the same courage he gave me," added the Lion, "he would have been a brave man." Dorothy said nothing.
uz: "Agar Oz menga bergan jasoratni qabul qilganida edi, u jasoratli odam bo'lar edi", - deb qo'shib qo'ydi Arslon.

en: Oz had not kept the promise he made her, but he had done his best, so she forgave him.
uz: Oz unga bergan va'dasini bajarmagan edi, lekin u qo'lidan kelganini qilgan edi, shuning uchun u uni kechirgan.

en: As he said, he was a good man, even if he was a bad Wizard.
uz: O'zi aytganidek, u yaxshi odam edi, hatto yomon sehrgar bo'lsa ham.

en: The first day's journey was through the green fields and bright flowers that stretched about the Emerald City on every side.
uz: Birinchi kunlik sayohat, har tomondan Emerald Shahar atrofida tarqalgan yashil dalalar va yorqin gullar orqali amalga oshirildi.

en: They slept that night on the grass, with nothing but the stars over them; and they rested very well indeed.
uz: O'sha kecha ular o'tda, yulduzlardan boshqa hech narsa yo'qligida uxladilar va chindan ham yaxshi uxladilar.

en: In the morning they traveled on until they came to a thick wood.
uz: Ertalab ular o'tkir daraxtga yetib kelishlaricha sayohatni davom ettirishdi.

en: There was no way of going around it, for it seemed to extend to the right and left as far as they could see; and, besides, they did not
uz: Uning atrofini o'tkazishning iloji yo'q edi, chunki u ular ko'rishlari mumkin bo'lgancha o'ng va chap tomonga uzilgan edi; bundan tashqari, ular buni ko'rmadilar.

en: dare change the direction of their journey for fear of getting lost.
uz: Yo'qolishdan qo'rqqanlari uchun sayohat yo'nalishini o'zgartirishga jur'at qilishadi.

en: So they looked for the place where it would be easiest to get into the forest.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular o'rmonga kirish eng oson joyni qidirdilar.

en: The Scarecrow, who was in the lead, finally discovered a big tree with such wide-spreading branches that there was room for the party to pass underneath.
uz: Avvalo, boshchiligidagi qo'rqinchli odam katta daraxtni kashf etdi va uning shoxlari shunchalik keng tarqalganki, uning pastidan partiya o'tishi uchun joy bo'ldi.

en: So he walked forward to the tree, but just as he came under the first branches they bent down and twined around him, and the next minute he was raised from the ground and flung headlong among his fellow travelers.
uz: U daraxtga yaqinlashdi, lekin birinchi shoxlar ostida bo'lganida, ular o'zlarini egib, atrofida bog'lanishdi va keyingi daqiqada u yerdan ko'tarilib, yo'lovchilarning o'rtasida o'z boshini tashladi.

en: This did not hurt the Scarecrow, but it surprised him, and he looked rather dizzy when Dorothy picked him up.
uz: Bu qo'rqinchli odamga yomon ta'sir qilmadi, lekin uni hayratda qoldirdi va Doroti uni ko'tarib olganda, u biroz cho'kkan ko'rinardi.

en: "Here is another space between the trees," called the Lion.
uz: Arslon deb nomlangan daraxtlar o'rtasida yana bir bo'sh joy bor.

en: "Let me try it first," said the Scarecrow, "for it doesn't hurt me to get thrown about." He walked up to another tree, as he spoke, but its branches immediately seized him and tossed him back again.
uz: - Avval sinab ko'rsam bo'ladi, - dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli, - bu menga tashlab ketishning zarari yo'q. - U gapirganida boshqa daraxtga yetib bordi, ammo uning shoxlari darhol uni ushlab, yana qaytarib yubordi.

en: "This is strange," exclaimed Dorothy.
uz: "Bu g'alati narsa", - dedi Doroti.

en: "What shall we do?" "The trees seem to have made up their minds to fight us, and stop our journey," remarked the Lion.
uz: "Biz nima qilishimiz kerak?" - deb aytdi Arslon. - Daraxtlar bizga qarshi jang qilib, safarimizni to'xtatishga qaror qilishgan.

en: "I believe I will try it myself," said the Woodman, and shouldering his axe, he marched up to the first tree that had handled the Scarecrow so roughly.
uz: "Men o'zim sinab ko'raman deb o'ylayman", - dedi Woodman va o'z baltini ko'tarib, qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli hayvon bilan shunday qattiq muomala qilgan birinchi daraxtga yetib keldi.

en: When a big branch bent down to seize him the Woodman chopped at it so fiercely that he cut it in two.
uz: Ulkan shox uni ushlab qolish uchun egri bo'lganida, Woodman uni shunchalik qattiq kesib qo'ydiki, uni ikkiga bo'g'ib yubordi.

en: At once the tree began shaking all its branches as if in pain, and the Tin Woodman passed safely under it.
uz: Darhol daraxtning barcha shoxlari og'riqli bo'lib, silkitib turadi va o'sha daraxtning pastidan Tin Woodman xavfsiz o'tadi.

en: "Come on!" he shouted to the others.
uz: "Qo'shinglar!" - deb baqiribdi u boshqalarga.

en: "Be quick!" They all ran forward and passed under the tree without injury, except Toto, who was caught by a small branch and shaken until he howled.
uz: "Shoshilin!" - deb, hammalari oldinga yugurib, daraxt ostida jarohatlanmasdan o'tib ketishdi, faqat Toto kichik bo'g'iga tushib, qichqirganga qadar silkitdi.

en: But the Woodman promptly chopped off the branch and set the little dog free.
uz: Ammo Vudman darhol shoxni kesib, itni ozod qildi.

en: The other trees of the forest did nothing to keep them back, so they made up their minds that only the first row of trees could bend down their branches, and that probably these were the policemen of
uz: O'rmondagi boshqa daraxtlar ularni orqaga qaytarish uchun hech narsa qilmadilar, shuning uchun ular faqat birinchi qator daraxtlargina shoxlarini egib qo'yishi mumkinligini va ehtimol bular o'sha shaharning politsiya xodimlari ekanligi haqida qaror qilishdi.

en: the forest, and given this wonderful power in order to keep strangers out of it.
uz: o'rmon, va bu ajoyib kuchga ega bo'lib, begonalarni u yerdan olib qo'yish uchun.

en: The four travelers walked with ease through the trees until they came to the farther edge of the wood.
uz: To'rtta sayohatchi o'simliklarning uzoq bo'yiga yetguncha o'simliklar orqali osonlikcha yurishdi.

en: Then, to their surprise, they found before them a high wall which seemed to be made of white china.
uz: Keyin, ularning hayron qolishlariga ko'ra, ularning oldida oq pornaydan yasalgan baland devor ko'rinardi.

en: It was smooth, like the surface of a dish, and higher than their heads.
uz: U pishirmaning yuziga o'xshaydigan, boshlaridan ham baland edi.

en: "What shall we do now?" asked Dorothy.
uz: "Bundan keyin nima qilamiz?" - deb so'radi Dorotsiya.

en: "I will make a ladder," said the Tin Woodman, "for we certainly must climb over the wall."
uz: "Men bir narvon tayyorlayman", dedi Tin Woodman, "chunki biz albatta devordan oshib borishimiz kerak".

en: Chapter XX The Dainty China Country While the Woodman was making a ladder from wood which he found in the forest Dorothy lay down and slept, for she was tired by the long walk.
uz: XX bob - Go'zal Xitoy yurti O'simlik daraxtdan daraxtdan burchak yasaganida, Dorothy uzoq yurishdan charchaganligi uchun o'tirib uxladi.

en: The Lion also curled himself up to sleep and Toto lay beside him.
uz: Arslon ham uxlab ketishga o'zini yig'di va Toto uning yonida yotgan edi.

en: The Scarecrow watched the Woodman while he worked, and said to him: "I cannot think why this wall is here, nor what it is made of." "Rest your brains and do not worry about the wall," replied the Woodman.
uz: Qo'rqinchli odam Woodman ishlashiga qarab unga shunday dedi: "Men bu devorning nima uchun bu yerda ekanligi va undan nima yasalganligi haqida o'ylay olmayman". - "O'zingizni dam oling va devor haqida tashvishlanmang", - deb javob berdi Woodman.

en: "When we have climbed over it, we shall know what is on the other side." After a time the ladder was finished.
uz: "O'shanda biz uning ustiga chiqib ketgach, boshqa tomonda nima borligini bilib olamiz". Bir muncha vaqt o'tgach, daraxtning usti tugadi.

en: It looked clumsy, but the Tin Woodman was sure it was strong and would answer their purpose.
uz: Bu o'ziga yarasha ko'rinmas edi, lekin Tin Woodman kuchli va maqsadlariga javob berishiga amin edi.

en: The Scarecrow waked Dorothy and the Lion and Toto, and told them that the ladder was ready.
uz: Qo'rqinchli Dorothy, Arslon va Totoni uyg'otib, eskalar tayyor ekanini aytdi.

en: The Scarecrow climbed up the ladder first, but he was so awkward that Dorothy had to follow close behind and keep him from falling off.
uz: Qo'rqinchli birinchi bo'lib sinchkaga chiqdi, lekin u shunchalik noqulay bo'lganki, Doroti uning orqasidan yaqinroq ergashib, uni pastga tushishdan saqlab qolishga majbur bo'ldi.

en: When he got his head over the top of the wall the Scarecrow said, "Oh, my!" "Go on," exclaimed Dorothy.
uz: Boshini devor ustiga ko'targanida qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli: "Oh, o'zim!" - dedi.

en: So the Scarecrow climbed farther up and sat down on the top of the wall, and Dorothy put her head over and cried, "Oh, my!" just as
uz: Shunday qilib, qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli yana yuqoriga chiqib, devor ustida o'tirdi va Doroti boshini ko'tarib: "Oh, o'zim!" - deb baqirdi.

en: the Scarecrow had done.
uz: qo'rqinchli hayvon o'zi bilan shug'ullandi.

en: Then Toto came up, and immediately began to bark, but Dorothy made him be still.
uz: Keyin Toto kelib, darhol qichqirishni boshladi, lekin Doroti uni to'xtatishga majbur qildi.

en: The Lion climbed the ladder next, and the Tin Woodman came last; but both of them cried, "Oh, my!" as soon as they looked over the wall.
uz: Arslon keyingi bosqichga chiqdi, Tin Woodman esa oxirgi bo'ldi; lekin ikkalasi ham devorga qarab, "O, ey!" deb baqirishdi.

en: When they were all sitting in a row on the top of the wall, they looked down and saw a strange sight.
uz: Ular devor ustida qatorda o'tirganlarida, pastga qarab, g'alati ko'rinishni ko'rishdi.

en: Before them was a great stretch of country having a floor as smooth and shining and white as the bottom of a big platter.
uz: Ularning oldiga katta yurt bo'lib, katta idishning quti kabi tekis, chiroq va oq bo'lgan katta qavat bor edi.

en: Scattered around were many houses made entirely of china and painted in the brightest colors.
uz: Bu yerda butunlayin xitoydan yasalgan va eng yorqin ranglarda bo'yilgan ko'plab uylar tarqalib turardi.

en: These houses were quite small, the biggest of them reaching only as high as Dorothy's waist.
uz: Ushbu uylar juda kichik edi, eng kattalari faqat Dorotining belini o'ylab topgan.

en: There were also pretty little barns, with china fences around them; and many cows and sheep and horses and pigs and chickens, all made of china, were standing about in groups.
uz: Bundan tashqari, atrofida china to'siqlari bilan o'ralgan chiroyli kichik donlar ham bor edi va ko'plab sigirlar, qo'ylar, otlar, cho'chqalar va tovuqlar guruh-guruh qilib turar edi.

en: But the strangest of all were the people who lived in this queer country.
uz: Ammo eng g'alati odamlar bu g'alati mamlakatda yashovchi odamlar edi.

en: There were milkmaids and shepherdesses, with brightly colored bodices and golden spots all over their gowns; and princesses with most gorgeous frocks of silver and gold and purple; and shepherds dressed in knee breeches with pink and yellow and blue stripes down them, and golden buckles on their shoes; and princes with jeweled crowns upon their heads, wearing ermine robes and satin doublets; and funny clowns in ruffled gowns, with round red spots upon their cheeks and tall, pointed caps.
uz: Bu yerda sut xizmatkorlari va cho'pon qizlari bor edilar, ular ko'ylaklarida chiroyli rangli bodislar va oltin maydonlar bor edilar; kumush, oltin va violet ko'ylaklar bilan o'ralgan princeslar bor edilar; sho'rlarida ro'za, sariq va ko'k chiziqlar bo'lgan to'ylaklar kiygan cho'ponlar, oyoqlarida oltin bog'lar bor edilar; boshlarida ermin liboslari va satin to'plamlari kiygan marvarislar bor edilar; va qo'pol maydonlar bilan o'ralgan maydonlar, buraklarida yuzli qizil maydonlar va baland, o'qilgan to'plamlari bor edilar.

en: And, strangest of all, these people were all made of china, even to their clothes, and were so small that the tallest of them was no higher than Dorothy's knee.
uz: Eng g'alati shundaki, bu odamlar hammasi china, hatto kiyim-kechaklardan yasalgan va shunchalik kichik edilarki, ularning eng balandlari Dorotiyning oyoqidan yuqori bo'lmagan.

en: No one did so much as look at the travelers at first, except one little purple china dog with an extra-large head, which came to the wall and barked at them in a tiny voice, afterwards running away again.
uz: Hech kim birinchi marta sayohatchilarga qaramasdi, faqat bitta kichkina bo'lib, o'ziga xos ulkan boshli bo'lib, devorga yaqinlashib, kichik ovozda ularga la'natdi va keyin yana qochib ketdi.

en: "How shall we get down?" asked Dorothy.
uz: "Biz qanday tushamiz?" - deb so'radi Dorotsiya.

en: They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet.
uz: Ular usti shunchalik og'ir bo'lganki, uni ko'tarib ko'tarolmadilar, shuning uchun qo'rqitgich devordan tushib tushdi va qolganlar qattiq qavat ularning oyoqlariga zarar bermasligi uchun uning ustiga qochib o'tishdi.

en: Of course they took pains not to light on his head and get the pins in their feet.
uz: Albatta, ular uning boshiga nur yoqmaslikka va oyoqlariga o't qo'ymaslikka harakat qilishdi.

en: When all were safely down they picked up the Scarecrow, whose body was quite flattened out, and patted his straw into shape again.
uz: Hamma xotirjam bo'lganidan so'ng, qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli odamni, uning tanasi to'liq tekis bo'lgan holda, ko'tarib, cho'qqisini yana shaklga kiritdi.

en: "We must cross this strange place in order to get to the other side," said Dorothy, "for it would be unwise for us to go any other way except due South." They began walking through the country of the china people, and the first thing they came to was a china milkmaid milking a china cow.
uz: "Biz bu g'alati joyni kesib o'tishimiz kerak", - dedi Doroti, "chunki Janubiy yo'ldan tashqari boshqa yo'ldan ketish oqilona bo'lmaydi". Ular xitoy xalqining mamlakatidan yurishni boshlashdi va ular birinchi bo'lib bir xitoy sut saqlovchisi xitoy sigirini soyalayotganini ko'rishdi.

en: As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.
uz: Ular yaqinlashayotganda, sigir birdan urib, stolni, bidonni va hatto sutxonaning o'zini urib tashladi va barchasi katta shovqin bilan china yerga yiqildi.

en: Dorothy was shocked to see that the cow had broken her leg off, and that the pail was lying in several small pieces, while the poor milkmaid had a nick in her left elbow.
uz: Dorotiyning oyoqlarini parchalaganini va bidonining bir nechta kichik bo'laklarga bo'linishini, kambag'al sut saqlovchisining esa chap qo'lqoshiga cho'qqiz qo'yganini ko'rib, hayratda qoldi.

en: "There!" cried the milkmaid angrily.
uz: - Mana! - deb qichqirdi sutxonasini g'azab bilan.

en: "See what you have done!
uz: "Qarang, nima qilgan bo'lsang!

en: My cow has broken her leg, and I must take her to the mender's shop and have it glued on again.
uz: Mening sigirim oyoqni sindirdi va men uni do'konga olib borib, yana bir bor uni yopishtirishim kerak.

en: What do you mean by coming here and frightening my cow?" "I'm very sorry," returned Dorothy.
uz: Bu yerga kelib, sigirimni qo'rqitib, nima demoqchi bo'lding?" - deb javob berdi Dorotsiya.

en: "Please forgive us." But the pretty milkmaid was much too vexed to make any answer.
uz: "Xullas, bizni kechiringlar". Ammo go'zal sutxonasini hech qanday javob berish uchun juda xafa bo'lgan.

en: She picked up the leg sulkily and led her cow away, the poor animal limping on three legs.
uz: U oyoqni g'alati ko'tarib, o'z sigirini yo'ldan ozdirdi, ahvolga tushgan hayvon uch oyoq bilan o'tirgan edi.

en: As she left them the milkmaid cast many reproachful glances over her shoulder at the clumsy strangers, holding her nicked elbow close to her side.
uz: Ularni tashlab ketayotganda, sutxonasini ko'p marta ko'tarib, o'z ko'nglini qo'yib qo'ydi.

en: Dorothy was quite grieved at this mishap.
uz: Doroti bu voqeadan juda xafa bo'lgan.

en: "We must be very careful here," said the kind-hearted Woodman, "or we may hurt these pretty little people so they will never get over it."
uz: "Biz bu yerda juda ehtiyotkor bo'lishimiz kerak", - dedi mehribon Woodman, "yoki biz bu go'zal kichik odamlarga zarar yetkazamiz, shuning uchun ular hech qachon buni yenga olmaydilar".

en: A little farther on Dorothy met a most beautifully dressed young Princess, who stopped short as she saw the strangers and started to run away.
uz: Biroz uzoqroq yurib, Doroti juda chiroyli kiyim kiygan yosh princess bilan uchrashdi, u begonalarni ko'rib, to'xtadi va qochib ketishni boshladi.

en: Dorothy wanted to see more of the Princess, so she ran after her.
uz: Dorotiya Qizani ko'proq ko'rmoqchi bo'lib, uning orqasidan yugurdi.

en: But the china girl cried out: "Don't chase me!
uz: Ammo xitoylik qiz: "Mening ortimdan quvma!

en: Don't chase me!" She had such a frightened little voice that Dorothy stopped and said, "Why not?" "Because," answered the Princess, also stopping, a safe distance away, "if I run I may fall down and break myself." "But could you not be mended?" asked the girl.
uz: Meni quvma!" - deb qo'rqqan qisqa ovozi bor edi va Doroti to'xtab: "Nima uchun yo'q?" - deb so'radi. - Chunki, - deb javob berdi printsesa, o'zi ham to'xtab, xavfsiz masofada turibdi. - Agar yugursam, yiqilib tushishim mumkin. - Lekin sen tuzatilmaysanmi? - deb so'radi qiz.

en: "Oh, yes; but one is never so pretty after being mended, you know," replied the Princess.
uz: "Ha, lekin hech qachon tuzatilganidan keyin hech qachon shu qadar chiroyli bo'lmaydi", - deb javob berdi Qiz.

en: "I suppose not," said Dorothy.
uz: "Yo'q, deb o'ylayman", dedi Doroti.

en: Joker, one of our clowns," continued the china lady, "who is always trying to stand upon his head.
uz: "Joker, bizning kulollarimizdan biri", - deb davom ettirgan xonim, "har doim boshida turishga harakat qiladi.

en: He has broken himself so often that he is mended in a hundred places, and doesn't look at all pretty.
uz: U o'zini juda ko'p marta buzgan bo'lsa-da, yuz marta tuzatilgan va hech qachon chiroyli ko'rinmaydi.

en: Here he comes now, so you can see for yourself." Indeed, a jolly little clown came walking toward them, and Dorothy could see that in spite of his pretty clothes of red and yellow and green he was completely covered with cracks, running every which way and showing plainly that he had been mended in many places.
uz: Mana, u hozir keladi, o'zingiz ko'ring". Haqiqatan ham, ularga yaqinlashib kelayotgan bir quvonchli kichkinagina paloshni ko'rish mumkin edi va Doroti qizil, sariq va yashil go'zal kiyimlariga qaramay, u butunlay yorilib, har tomonga yugurib, ko'p joylarda sog'ayganini ko'rsatadi.

en: The Clown put his hands in his pockets, and after puffing out his cheeks and nodding his head at them saucily, he said: {verse "My lady fair, Why do you stare At poor old Mr.
uz: Qoʻllarini kiyimlariga qoʻydi va yigʻinlarini puflaganidan soʻng, boshini oʻziga tikib: {Versus "My fair lady, nima uchun siz kambagʻal keksa Mr.

en: You're quite as stiff And prim as if You'd eaten up a poker!" {verse "Be quiet, sir!" said the Princess.
uz: Siz juda qattiq va jadalsiz, xuddi pokerni yutib yuborganingizdek!" {oyat "Xotirjam bo'ling, xo'jayinim!" deb aytdi princess.

en: "Can't you see these are strangers, and should be treated with respect?" "Well, that's respect, I expect," declared the Clown, and immediately stood upon his head.
uz: "Bular begona odamlar va ularga hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'lish kerakligini ko'rmayapsizmi?" - deb e'tirof etdi klaun va darhol boshini ko'tarib turdi.

en: Joker," said the Princess to Dorothy.
uz: Joker", - dedi princess Dorothyga.

en: "He is considerably cracked in his head, and that makes him foolish." "Oh, I don't mind him a bit," said Dorothy.
uz: "O'zining boshi sezilarli darajada parchalangan va bu uni ahmoqona qiladi. - Oh, men unga biroz ham xalaqit bermayman, - dedi Doroti.

en: "But you are so beautiful," she continued, "that I am sure I could love you dearly.
uz: - Lekin sen shunchalik chiroylisan, - dedi u davom etib, - men seni chin dildan sevishimga aminman.

en: Won't you let me carry you back to Kansas, and stand you on Aunt Em's mantel?
uz: Sizni Kanzasga olib qaytib ketib, Em onasi kiyimida turishimga ruxsat bermayapsizmi?

en: I could carry you in my basket." "That would make me very unhappy," answered the china Princess.
uz: Men seni kostimda ko'tarib olsam bo'ladi". - Bu meni juda baxtsiz qiladi, - deb javob berdi Xitoy princesasi.

en: "You see, here in our country we live contentedly, and can talk and move around as we please.
uz: "Qaranglar, biz mamlakatimizda mamnuniyat ila yashayapmiz va xohlaganimizcha gapirish va harakatlanishimiz mumkin.

en: But whenever any of us are taken away our joints at once stiffen, and we can only stand straight and look pretty.
uz: Ammo bizlardan har bir kishini olib tashlaganimizda, qo'shillarimiz birdan qattiqroq bo'ladi va biz faqat to'g'ri turib, chiroyli ko'rinishga ega bo'lamiz.

en: Of course that is all that is expected of us when we are on mantels and cabinets and drawing-room tables, but our lives are much pleasanter here in our own country." "I would not make you unhappy for all the world!" exclaimed Dorothy.
uz: To'g'ridan-to'g'ri, kiyimlar va kabinetlar ustida bo'lganimizda, bizdan faqat shu narsani kutish mumkin, ammo bizning hayotimiz bu mamlakatimizda ancha yoqimliroq". - "Men sizni butun dunyo uchun baxtsiz qilmayman!" - deb hayqirib yubordi Dorotsiya.

en: "So I'll just say good-bye." "Good-bye," replied the Princess.
uz: "Shunday qilib, men shunchaki salom aytam". - deb javob berdi Qiz.

en: They walked carefully through the china country.
uz: Ular Xitoy mamlakatidan ehtiyotkorlik bilan o'tdilar.

en: The little animals and all the people scampered out of their way, fearing the strangers would break them, and after an hour or so the travelers reached the other side of the country and came to another china wall.
uz: Kichik hayvonlar va barcha odamlar, begonalar ularni buzishidan qo'rqib, yo'ldan qochib ketishdi va bir soatdan keyin sayohatchilar mamlakatning boshqa tomonida joylashgan va boshqa porsiya devoriga yetib kelishdi.

en: It was not so high as the first, however, and by standing upon the Lion's back they all managed to scramble to the top.
uz: Biroq, u birinchi o'rinda bo'lgani kabi yuqori bo'lmagan va Lionning orqasida turib, ular barchasi yuqoriga ko'tarilishdi.

en: Then the Lion gathered his legs under him and jumped on the wall; but just as he
uz: Keyin Arslon oyoqlarini uning ostiga to'pladi va devor ustida sakrashdi; lekin xuddi o'sha paytda u

en: jumped, he upset a china church with his tail and smashed it all to pieces.
uz: U cho'kib, quyruq bilan bir cherkovni buzdi va butunlay parchaladi.

en: "That was too bad," said Dorothy, "but really I think we were lucky in not doing these little people more harm than breaking a cow's leg and a church.
uz: "Bu juda yomon bo'ldi", dedi Doroti, "lekin men o'ylaymanki, biz bu kichik odamlarga sigir va cherkovni buzishdan ko'ra ko'proq zarar yetkazmaganimizda omadli edik.

en: They are all so brittle!" "They are, indeed," said the Scarecrow, "and I am thankful I am made of straw and cannot be easily damaged.
uz: Ular hammasi juda murakkab!" - dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli, - "Haqiqatan ham ular bor va men shukr qilamanki, men to'siqdan yasalganman va osonlikcha shikastlanishi mumkin emas.

en: There are worse things in the world than being a Scarecrow."
uz: Dunyoda qo'rquvchisi bo'lishdan ham yomonroq narsalar bor".

en: Chapter XXI The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts After climbing down from the china wall the travelers found themselves in a disagreeable country, full of bogs and marshes and covered with tall, rank grass.
uz: XXI bob Arslon hayvonlarning shohi bo'ladi Sarvari xonadonga aylangan sayohatchilar china devoridan pastga chiqishganidan so'ng, o'zlarini bog'lar va bo'laklar bilan to'lgan, baland, rangli o'tlar bilan qoplangan noqulay mamlakatda topdilar.

en: It was difficult to walk without falling into muddy holes, for the grass was so thick that it hid them from sight.
uz: G'iybatli toshlarga tushib qolmasdan yurish qiyin edi, chunki o't shunchalik qal'iy ediki, ularni ko'rishdan yashirib qo'ydi.

en: However, by carefully picking their way, they got safely along until they reached solid ground.
uz: Biroq, ular o'z yo'llarini ehtiyotkorlik bilan tanlab olib, mustahkam yerga yetguncha xavfsiz yo'l olishdi.

en: But here the country seemed wilder than ever, and after a long and tiresome walk through the underbrush they entered another forest, where the trees were bigger and older than any they had ever seen.
uz: Ammo bu yerda qishloq har qachongidan ham yovvoyi ko'rinardi va uzoq va charchatiladigan yurish-turishlardan so'ng ular boshqa o'rmonga kirishdi, u yerda daraxtlar ular ko'rgan daraxtlardan kattaroq va keksa edi.

en: "This forest is perfectly delightful," declared the Lion, looking around him with joy.
uz: "Bu o'rmon chindan ham chiroyli", - deb e'lon qildi Arslon, atrofini quvonch bilan ko'rib.

en: "Never have I seen a more beautiful place." "It seems gloomy," said the Scarecrow.
uz: "Men bundan ham go'zal joyni ko'rmaganman". - dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli.

en: "Not a bit of it," answered the Lion.
uz: - Hech narsa emas, - deb javob berdi Arslon.

en: "I should like to live here all my life.
uz: "Men butun hayotim davomida bu yerda yashashni istayman.

en: See how soft the dried leaves are under your feet and how rich and green the moss is that clings to these old trees.
uz: Oyoqlaringiz ostida quritilgan barglarning qanchalik yumshligini va bu eski daraxtlarga bog'liq bo'lgan yoshning qanchalik boy va yashilligini ko'ring.

en: Surely no wild beast could wish a pleasanter home." "Perhaps there are wild beasts in the forest now," said Dorothy.
uz: Hech bir yovvoyi hayvon bundan ko'proq yoqimli uyni istamaydi". - Ehtimol, hozir o'rmonda yovvoyi hayvonlar bor", dedi Doroti.

en: "I suppose there are," returned the Lion, "but I do not see any of them about."
uz: "O'ylaymanki, mavjud", - deb javob berdi Arslon, "lekin ularning hech birini ko'rmayapman".

en: They walked through the forest until it became too dark to go any farther.
uz: Ular o'rmon atrofida yurishdi, o'tmishga qaralganidan so'ng, uzoqroq ketish uchun juda qorong'u bo'ldi.

en: Dorothy and Toto and the Lion lay down to sleep, while the Woodman and the Scarecrow kept watch over them as usual.
uz: Doroti, Toto va Arslon uxlab ketishdi, Vudman va qo'rqinchli esa odatdagidek ularni kuzatib turishdi.

en: When morning came, they started again.
uz: Ertalab esa ular yana boshlashdi.

en: Before they had gone far they heard a low rumble, as of the growling of many wild animals.
uz: Uzoq ketishdan oldin ular ko'plab yovvoyi hayvonlarning qichqiriqlariga o'xshatilgan past bir qichqiriq eshitishdi.

en: Toto whimpered a little, but none of the others was frightened, and they kept along the well-trodden path until they came to an opening in the wood, in which were gathered hundreds of beasts of every variety.
uz: Toto biroz g'azablandi, ammo qolganlar hech kim qo'rqmadi va ular to'g'ri yo'ldan yurib, daraxtdagi bir buloqqa yetib kelishdi, unda har xil hayvonlarning yuzlab hayvonlari to'plangan edi.

en: There were tigers and elephants and bears and wolves and foxes and all the others in the natural history, and for a moment Dorothy was afraid.
uz: Dorilar, fillar, g'urvalar, boʻriqlar va tilkashlar va tabiiy tarixdagi boshqa barcha mavjudotlar bor edi va bir zum davomida Doroti qo'rqqan edi.

en: But the Lion explained that the animals were holding a meeting, and he judged by their snarling and growling that they were in great trouble.
uz: Ammo Arslon hayvonlar yig'ilish o'tkazayotganini tushuntirdi va ularning qichqiriq va qichqiriqlariga ko'ra, ular katta muammoga duchor bo'lishganini aytdi.

en: As he spoke several of the beasts caught sight of him, and at once the great assemblage hushed as if by magic.
uz: U gapirganida, bir nechta hayvonlar uni ko'rishdi va shu zahoti katta jamoat sehr bilan o'chirib ketdi.

en: The biggest of the tigers came up to the Lion and bowed, saying: "Welcome, O King of Beasts!
uz: O'g'illarning eng kattalari sherga yaqinlashib, sajda qilib: "Qaroblar Podshohi, xush kelibsiz!

en: You have come in good time to fight our enemy and bring peace to all the animals of the forest once more." "What is your trouble?" asked the Lion quietly.
uz: Dushmanimizga qarshi jang qilish va o'rmon hayvonlariga tinchlik keltirish uchun siz o'z vaqtida keldingiz", - deb so'radi sher.

en: "We are all threatened," answered the tiger, "by a fierce enemy which has lately come into this forest.
uz: "Biz hammamiz bu o'rmonga yaqinda kirib kelgan shafqatsiz dushman tomonidan tahdid ostidamiz", - deb javob berdi sher.

en: It is a most tremendous monster, like a great spider, with a body as big as an elephant and legs as long as a tree trunk.
uz: Bu ulkan o'simlik kabi ulkan qudratli qudratli qudratli qudratli hayvon, uning tanasi fil kabi katta, oyoqlari esa daraxt daraxtining tomi kabi uzun.

en: It has eight of these long legs, and as the monster crawls through the forest he seizes an animal with a leg and drags it to his mouth, where he eats it as a spider does a fly.
uz: Uning sakkiz oyog'i shuncha uzun va o'rmon ichida o'rab-o'rab yurgan bo'lsa, u bir oyog'i bilan hayvonni ushlab, og'ziga tortib oladi va o'zini o'ldiradi.

en: Not one of us is safe while this fierce creature is alive, and we had called a meeting to decide how to take care of ourselves when you came among us." The Lion thought for a moment.
uz: Bu yovuz mavjudot tirik bo'lganda, bizlardan hech birimiz xavfsiz emasmiz va siz o'zimizga qanday g'amxo'rlik qilish kerakligini hal qilish uchun yig'ilish o'tkazdik", - deb o'yladi sher.

en: "Are there any other lions in this forest?" he asked.
uz: U: "Bu o'rmonda boshqa sherlar bormi?" - deb so'radi.

en: "No; there were some, but the monster has eaten them all.
uz: "Yo'q, ba'zilari bor edi, lekin vahshiy ularning barchasini yutib yubordi.

en: And, besides, there were none of them nearly so large and brave as you." "If I put an end to your enemy, will you bow down to me and obey me as King of the Forest?" inquired the Lion.
uz: Bundan tashqari, ularning hech biri siz kabi katta va jasoratli bo'lmagan". - Agar men dushmaningizni yo'q qilsam, siz menga sajda qilib, o'rmon shohi sifatida itoat etasizmi? - deb so'radi Arslon.

en: "We will do that gladly," returned the tiger; and all the other beasts roared with a mighty roar: "We will!" "Where is this great spider of yours now?" asked the Lion.
uz: "Biz buni xursandchilik bilan qilamiz", - deb javob berdi sher, qolgan barcha hayvonlar esa kuchli qichqiriq bilan: "Biz qilamiz!" - deb qichqirdilar. - Endi sizning buyuk o'spiningiz qayerda?" - deb so'radi Arslon.

en: "Yonder, among the oak trees," said the tiger, pointing with his forefoot.
uz: "Ushbu yerda, o'q daraxtlari orasida", - dedi sher, old oyoq bilan ko'rsatdi.

en: "Take good care of these friends of mine," said the Lion, "and I will go at once to fight the monster." He bade his comrades good-bye and marched proudly away to do battle with the enemy.
uz: "Mening bu do'stlarimga g'amxo'rlik qiling", - dedi Arslon, "men darhol g'animga qarshi jang qilishga ketaman". U qo'shnilariga salom berdi va dushman bilan jang qilish uchun mag'rurlik bilan yo'lga chiqdi.

en: The great spider was lying asleep when the Lion found him, and it looked so ugly that its foe turned up his nose in disgust.
uz: Buyuk oʻspin sher uni topganida uxlab yotgan edi va u shunchalik yomon koʻrinardiki, dushmani nafratdan oʻzini koʻtardi.

en: Its legs were quite as long as the tiger had said, and its body covered with coarse black hair.
uz: Uning oyoqlari sher aytganidek uzun edi va tanasi qora sochlar bilan qoplangan edi.

en: It had a great mouth, with a row of sharp teeth a foot long; but its head was joined to the pudgy body by a neck as slender as a wasp's waist.
uz: Uning og'zi katta va bir oy uzun bo'lgan o'tkir tishlar qatoridan iborat edi; lekin uning boshi bo'lakning belini o'xshaydigan bo'lak bilan bo'lakga qo'shilgan edi.

en: This gave the Lion a hint of the best way to attack the creature, and as he knew it was easier to fight it asleep than awake, he gave a great spring and landed directly upon the monster's back.
uz: Bu sherga hayvonga hujum qilishning eng yaxshi usuli haqida ma'lumot berdi va u uyqudan ko'ra uyg'onishdan ko'ra unga qarshi kurashish osonroq ekanligini bilgani uchun, u katta ko'tarish qo'yib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri hayvonning orqasidan tushib ketdi.

en: Then, with one blow of his heavy paw, all armed with sharp claws, he knocked the spider's head from its body.
uz: So'ngra o'tkir to'qnashlari bilan qurollangan og'ir cho'qqisidan bir marta urib, o'rgidaning boshini uning tanasidan urdi.

en: Jumping down, he watched it until the long legs stopped wiggling, when he knew it was quite dead.
uz: U yerga sakrab tushib, uning uzun oyoqlari to'xtalguncha uni kuzatib turdi, ammo u o'lganini bilib qoldi.

en: The Lion went back to the opening where the beasts of the forest were waiting for him and said proudly: "You need fear your enemy no longer." Then the beasts bowed down to the Lion as their King, and he promised to come back and rule over them as soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas.
uz: Arslon o'rmon hayvonlari uni kutib turgan ochilishga qaytib kelib, faxr bilan shunday dedi: "Dushmaningizdan qo'rqmanglar!" Keyin hayvonlar Arslonga o'z Podshohi sifatida sajda qildilar va Doroti Kanzasga omon-omon yo'lda bo'lganida, u qaytadi va ularga hukmronlik qiladi deb va'da berdi.

en: Chapter XXII The Country of the Quadlings The four travelers passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.
uz: Ba'zi to'rtta sayohatchi o'rmonning qolgan qismidan xavfsiz o'tdilar va qorong'ilikdan chiqib ketganda, ularning ko'z o'ngida baland tog' borligini ko'rishdi, u yuqoridan pastgacha katta tosh bo'laklari bilan qoplangan edi.

en: "That will be a hard climb," said the Scarecrow, "but we must get over the hill, nevertheless." So he led the way and the others followed.
uz: "Bu qiyin chiqish bo'ladi, - dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli, - lekin biz tog'dan o'tishimiz kerak", dedi.

en: They had nearly reached the first rock when they heard a rough voice cry out, "Keep back!" "Who are you?" asked the Scarecrow.
uz: Ular birinchi toshga yaqinlashishganida, qattiq ovozni eshitib: "O'zingizni orqaga qaytaring!" - deb so'radilar.

en: Then a head showed itself over the rock and the same voice said, "This hill belongs to us, and we don't allow anyone to cross it." "But we must cross it," said the Scarecrow.
uz: So'ngra tosh ustida bosh ko'rindi va xuddi shu ovoz: "Bu tog' bizga tegishli va biz hech kimga o'tishga ruxsat bermaymiz". - Lekin biz o'tishimiz kerak, dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli.

en: "We're going to the country of the Quadlings." "But you shall not!" replied the voice, and there stepped from behind the rock the strangest man the travelers had ever seen.
uz: "Biz Quadlinglar yurtiga boramiz". - Lekin yo'q! - deb javob berdi ovoz va sayohatchilar ko'rgan eng g'ayrioddiy odam tosh orqasidan qadam bosdi.

en: He was quite short and stout and had a big head, which was flat at the top and supported by a thick neck full of wrinkles.
uz: U juda qisqa va kuchli edi va katta boshga ega edi, u yuqorida tekis edi va o'z bo'yniga burchaklar bilan to'lgan qalin bo'lak bilan qo'llab-quvvatlanardi.

en: But he had no arms at all, and, seeing this, the Scarecrow did not fear that so helpless a creature could prevent them from climbing the hill.
uz: Ammo uning qo'li yo'q edi va qo'rqinchli hayvon buni ko'rib, qo'rqinchli hayvonning ularni tog'ga chiqishdan to'xtatishidan qo'rqmadi.

en: said, "I'm sorry not to do as you wish, but we must pass over your hill whether you like it or not," and he walked boldly forward.
uz: "Siz xohlaganingizni qilmaganim uchun uzr so'rayman, lekin sizga yoqadimi, yoqmasin, biz sizning tog'ingizdan o'tishimiz kerak", - dedi u va jasorat bilan oldinga qadam bosdi.

en: As quick as lightning the man's head shot forward and his neck stretched out until the top of the head, where it was flat, struck the Scarecrow in the middle and sent him tumbling, over and over, down the hill.
uz: Yomg'ir yog'g'aygancha, odamning boshi oldinga urildi va uning bo'yni boshning yuqori qismiga qadar uzildi, u yerda u tekis edi, qorong'ularni o'rtaga urdi va uni to'g'rilab, to'g'rilab, tog'dan pastga tushirdi.

en: Almost as quickly as it came the head went back to the body, and the man laughed harshly as he said, "It isn't as easy as you think!" A chorus of boisterous laughter came from the other rocks, and Dorothy saw hundreds of the armless Hammer-Heads upon the hillside, one behind every rock.
uz: To'g'ri kelgancha bosh o'ziga qaytib keldi va u kishi: "Bu siz o'ylaganidek oson emas!" - deb qo'shib qo'ydi. Boshqa toshlardan shov-shuvli kulgilar qo'shilib keldi va Doroti har bir tosh orqasida, tog'ning yonida yuzlab qo'lsiz Qichqiriq boshlarini ko'rdi.

en: The Lion became quite angry at the laughter caused by the Scarecrow's mishap, and giving a loud roar that echoed like thunder, he dashed up the hill.
uz: Arslon qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchning halokatidan kelib chiqqan kulgiga juda g'azablandi va g'alati ovoz bilan g'alati chaqmoq kabi ovoz chiqarib, tepalikka ko'tarildi.

en: Again a head shot swiftly out, and the great Lion went rolling down the hill as if he had been struck by a cannon ball.
uz: Yana bir marta bosh shovqin chiqib ketdi va buyuk Arslon toshni toshbo'ron bilan urgan bo'lib, toshbo'ron topidan tushdi.

en: Dorothy ran down and helped the Scarecrow to his feet, and the Lion came up to her, feeling rather bruised and sore, and said, "It is useless to fight people with shooting heads; no one can withstand them." "What can we do, then?" she asked.
uz: Doroti yugurib tushdi va qo'rqinchli hayvonning oyoqlariga yordam berdi. Sher unga yaqinlashdi va o'zini o'ta jarohatlangan va og'rigan his etib: "O'z boshlarini o'chirib odamlarga qarshi kurashish foydasiz; hech kim ularga qarshi tura olmaydi", - dedi.

en: "Call the Winged Monkeys," suggested the Tin Woodman.
uz: Tin Woodman: "Qo'ngli maymunlarni chaqiring", deb aytdi.

en: "You have still the right to command them once more." "Very well," she answered, and putting on the Golden Cap she uttered the magic words.
uz: "Siz hali ham ularga yana bir bor amr berishga haqingiz bor". "Toʻgʻri", deb javob berdi u, oltin toʻpka kiyib, sehrli soʻzlarni aytdi.

en: The Monkeys were as prompt as ever, and in a few moments the entire band stood before her.
uz: The Monkeys har doimgidek tezkor bo'lgan va bir necha daqiqadan so'ng butun guruh uning oldida turdi.

en: "What are your commands?" inquired the King of the Monkeys, bowing low.
uz: "Sizning buyruqlaringiz nima?" - deb so'radi Maymunlar Podshohi, bosh ko'tardi.

en: "Carry us over the hill to the country of the Quadlings," answered the girl.
uz: Qiz: "Bizni tog'dan Quadlinglar yurtiga olib boring", - deb javob berdi.

en: "It shall be done," said the King, and at once the Winged Monkeys caught the four travelers and Toto up in their arms and flew away with them.
uz: "Bu bo'ladi", - dedi shoh va darhol qanotli maymunlar to'rtta sayohatchini va To'to'ni qo'llarida olib, ular bilan uchib ketdilar.

en: As they passed over the hill the Hammer-Heads yelled with vexation, and shot their heads high in the air, but they could not reach the Winged Monkeys, which carried Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the beautiful country of the Quadlings.
uz: Togʻdan oʻtayotganlarida, Hammer-Heads gʻazab bilan qichqirib, boshlarini yuqoriga koʻtarishdi, lekin u qaniq maymunlarga yetib bormadi, chunki ular Dorothy va uning sheriklarini togʻdan xavfsiz olib chiqib, Quadlinglarning goʻzal mamlakatida joylashtirdilar.

en: "This is the last time you can summon us," said the leader to Dorothy; "so good-bye and good luck to you." "Good-bye, and thank you very much," returned the girl; and the Monkeys rose into the air and were out of sight in a twinkling.
uz: - Bu bizni oxirgi marta chaqirishingiz mumkin, - dedi boshliq Dorotiga, - juda salom va sizga omad. - Xayr, va sizga katta rahmat, - deb javob berdi qiz. - Maymunlar havoga ko'tarildi va bir muncha ko'rinmay qoldi.

en: The country of the Quadlings seemed rich and happy.
uz: Quadlinglar yurti boy va baxtli ko'rinardi.

en: There was field upon field of ripening grain, with well-paved roads running between, and pretty rippling brooks with strong bridges across them.
uz: O'simliklarning o'sib-ulg'ayishi, o'rtasida yo'l-yo'llar o'tishi va o'rtasida kuchli ko'priklar bo'lgan chiroyli o'simliklar bor edi.

en: The fences and houses and bridges were all painted bright red, just as they had been painted yellow in the country of the Winkies and blue in the country of the Munchkins.
uz: Qo'rqinch, uylar va ko'priklar chiroyli qizil rangda bo'yilgan edi, xuddi Winkies mamlakatida sariq, Munchkins mamlakatida ko'k rangda bo'yilgan bo'lgani kabi.

en: The Quadlings themselves, who were short and fat and looked chubby and good-natured, were dressed all in red, which showed bright against the green grass and the yellowing grain.
uz: Quadlinglar o'zlari, qisqa va semiz bo'lib, chiroyli va mehribon ko'rinishgan edilar, ular butunlay qizil kiyim kiygan edilar, bu esa yashil o't va sariq bo'lgan donlarga qaraganda yorqin ko'rinardi.

en: The Monkeys had set them down near a farmhouse, and the four travelers walked up to it and knocked at the door.
uz: Maymunlar ularni bir ferma uyining yonida joylashtirgan edilar va to'rtta sayohatchi u yerga yaqinlashib, eshikni taqillatishdi.

en: It was opened by the farmer's wife, and when Dorothy asked for something to eat the woman gave them all a good dinner, with three kinds of cake and four kinds of cookies, and a bowl of milk for Toto.
uz: Uni fermerning xotini ochdi va Doroti ovqat so'raganida, ayol hammalariga yaxshi kechki ovqat berdi, unda uch turdagi tort va to'rt turdagi keklar va Toto uchun bir qadah sut bor edi.

en: "How far is it to the Castle of Glinda?" asked the child.
uz: "Glinda qalʼasiga qancha yoʻl bor?" - deb soʻradi bola.

en: "It is not a great way," answered the farmer's wife.
uz: Farmerning xotini: "Bu yaxshi yo'l emas", - deb javob berdi.

en: "Take the road to the South and you will soon reach it." Thanking the good woman, they started afresh and walked by the fields and across the pretty bridges until they saw before them a very beautiful Castle.
uz: "Jonga boradigan yo'lni ko'ring va tez orada unga yetib borasiz". Yaxshi ayolga minnatdorchilik bildirgan holda ular yangidan boshlashdi va juda chiroyli qal'ani ko'rmagunlaricha dalalar va chiroyli ko'priklar o'rtasida yurishdi.

en: Before the gates were three young girls, dressed in handsome red uniforms trimmed with gold braid; and as Dorothy approached, one of them said to her:
uz: Darvozalar oldida uchta qiz, qizil kiyim kiygan, oltin to'plam bilan bezatilgan chiroyli uniformlar bor edi va Doroti yaqinlashganda, ulardan biri unga shunday dedi:

en: "Why have you come to the South Country?" "To see the Good Witch who rules here," she answered.
uz: "Nima uchun Janubiy mamlakatga keldingiz?" - deb so'radi u. - Bu yerda hukmronlik qiladigan Yaxshi sehrgarani ko'rish uchun.

en: "Will you take me to her?" "Let me have your name, and I will ask Glinda if she will receive you." They told who they were, and the girl soldier went into the Castle.
uz: "Meni uning oldiga olib borasizmi?" - deb so'radi. - Ismingni ayt, Glinda seni qabul qiladimi, deb so'rayman. - Ular kim ekanliklarini aytishdi va qiz askar Qaroqqa kirdi.

en: After a few moments she came back to say that Dorothy and the others were to be admitted at once.
uz: Bir necha daqiqadan so'ng u qaytib kelib, Doroti va boshqalarni darhol qabul qilishlarini aytdi.

en: Chapter XXIII Glinda The Good Witch Grants Dorothy's Wish Before they went to see Glinda, however, they were taken to a room of the Castle, where Dorothy washed her face and combed her hair, and the Lion shook the dust out of his mane, and the Scarecrow patted himself into his best shape, and the Woodman polished his tin and oiled his joints.
uz: XXIII bob Glinda Yaxshi sehrgar Dorotining tilagini bajaradi Glinda bilan uchrashishga borishdan oldin, ular Qaroqning bir xonasidan olib ketildi, u yerda Dorotining yuzi yuvilib, sochlarini pishirdi, Arslon o'z qo'lidan tuproqni ko'tardi, Qo'rqinchli o'zini eng yaxshi shaklga qo'ydi, Vudman esa qadoqlanishini o'zgartirdi va o'z qo'shmalarini moyladi.

en: When they were all quite presentable they followed the soldier girl into a big room where the Witch Glinda sat upon a throne of rubies.
uz: Ularning barchasi o'ziga xos bo'lganida, ular askar qizni katta xonaga kuzatib borishdi, u yerda sehrgar Glinda ko'p ko'rinadigan rubinlar taxtiga o'tirgan edi.

en: She was both beautiful and young to their eyes.
uz: Ularning ko'z o'ngida u ham go'zal, ham yosh edi.

en: Her hair was a rich red in color and fell in flowing ringlets over her shoulders.
uz: Uning sochlari qizil rangda bo'lib, shoxlari ustida oqib o'tgan bo'lak-bo'laklar bo'lib tushdi.

en: Her dress was pure white but her eyes were blue, and they looked kindly upon the little girl.
uz: Uning kiyimlari sof oq edi, lekin ko'zlari ko'k edi va ular qizchaga mehribonlik ila qarab turishgan.

en: "What can I do for you, my child?" she asked.
uz: "Sening uchun nima qilishim mumkin, qizim?" deb so'radi u.

en: Dorothy told the Witch all her story: how the cyclone had brought her to the Land of Oz, how she had found her companions, and of the wonderful adventures they had met with.
uz: Doroti o'zining butun hikoyasini sehrgarga aytib berdi: qanday qilib to'fon uni O'z yurtiga olib keldi, qanday qilib u o'z hamkorlarini topdi va ular bilan qanday ajoyib mashg'ulotlar yuz berdi.

en: "My greatest wish now," she added, "is to get back to Kansas, for Aunt Em will surely think something dreadful has happened to me, and that will make her put on mourning; and unless the crops are
uz: U qo'shimcha qildi: "Hndi mening eng katta tilakim - Kanzasga qaytish, chunki Em xonim menga dahshatli narsa sodir bo'lganini o'ylaydi va bu uni qayg'uga to'ldiradi.

en: better this year than they were last, I am sure Uncle Henry cannot afford it." Glinda leaned forward and kissed the sweet, upturned face of the loving little girl.
uz: Bu yil o'tgan yilga qaraganda yaxshiroq bo'ldi, men o'ylaymanki, Genri o'g'lim bunga qodir emas". - deb aytdi Glinda.

en: "Bless your dear heart," she said, "I am sure I can tell you of a way to get back to Kansas." Then she added, "But, if I do, you must give me the Golden Cap." "Willingly!" exclaimed Dorothy; "indeed, it is of no use to me now, and when you have it you can command the Winged Monkeys three times." "And I think I shall need their service just those three times," answered Glinda, smiling.
uz: - Sening aziz qalbingni duo qil, - dedi u, - albatta, men senga Kanzasga qaytish yo'lini aytib bera olaman. - Keyin qo'shib qo'ydi: - Agar shunday qilsam, menga Oltin to'pka berishing kerak. - Ishonch ila! - dedi Dorotsiya; - haqiqatan ham, bu menga endi foydasi yo'q, va qachonki bor bo'lsa, qanotli maymonga uch marta amr qila olasan. - Va men o'ylaymanki, faqat o'sha uch marta ularning xizmatlariga muhtoj bo'laman, - dedi Glinda tabassum bilan javob berdi.

en: Dorothy then gave her the Golden Cap, and the Witch said to the Scarecrow, "What will you do when Dorothy has left us?" "I will return to the Emerald City," he replied, "for Oz has made me its ruler and the people like me.
uz: Keyin Doroti unga oltin toʻpka berdi va sehrgar qoʻrqinchli odamga: "Doroti bizni tark etganida nima qilasan?" - dedi. - Men Emerald shahriga qaytaman, - dedi u, - chunki Oz meni uning hokimi va men kabi xalq qilib qoʻydi.

en: The only thing that worries me is how to cross the hill of the Hammer-Heads." "By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City," said Glinda, "for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler." "Am I really wonderful?" asked the Scarecrow.
uz: "Qizil qo'rqinchli maymonga Oltin to'pka yordamida sizlarni Emerald shahar darvozalariga olib borishni buyuraman", - dedi Glinda, "chunki odamlarni bunday ajoyib hukmdordan mahrum qilish uyat bo'lardi". "Men haqiqatan ham ajoyibmanmi?" - deb so'radi qo'rqinchli.

en: "You are unusual," replied Glinda.
uz: Glinda javob berdi: "Siz odatiy emassiz.

en: Turning to the Tin Woodman, she asked, "What will become of you when Dorothy leaves this country?" He leaned on his axe and thought a moment.
uz: U Tin Woodmanga qarab: "Dorothy bu mamlakatni tark etganida, sizdan nima bo'ladi?" - deb so'radi.

en: Then he said, "The Winkies were very kind to me, and wanted me to rule over them after the Wicked Witch died.
uz: Keyin u shunday dedi: "Winkilar menga juda mehribon bo'lishdi va yovuz sehrgar o'lganidan so'ng ularni boshqarishimni xohlashgan.

en: I am fond of the Winkies, and if I could get back again to the Country of the West, I should like nothing better than to rule over them forever."
uz: Men Winkilarni yaxshi ko'raman va agar men G'arbiy mamlakatga qaytishim mumkin bo'lsa, ular ustidan abadiy hukmronlik qilishdan ko'ra ko'proq narsani xohlamayman".

en: "My second command to the Winged Monkeys," said Glinda "will be that they carry you safely to the land of the Winkies.
uz: Glinda shunday dedi: "Qo'ngli maymunlarga bergan ikkinchi amrim shundaki, ular sizni Winkieslar yurtiga xavfsiz olib ketishadi.

en: Your brain may not be so large to look at as those of the Scarecrow, but you are really brighter than he is—when you are well polished—and I am sure you will rule the Winkies wisely and well." Then the Witch looked at the big, shaggy Lion and asked, "When Dorothy has returned to her own home, what will become of you?" "Over the hill of the Hammer-Heads," he answered, "lies a grand old forest, and all the beasts that live there have made me their King.
uz: Ehtimol, sizning miyangiz qo'rquvchining miyasi kabi katta bo'lmasligi mumkin, lekin siz uning o'g'lidan chiroyliroq bo'lishingiz mumkin, chunki siz yaxshi poliz bo'lganingizda va men Winkies-larni dono va yaxshi boshqarishingizdan shubhalanaman". Keyin sehrgar katta, qovurilgan Arslonga qarab, "Dorothy o'z uyiga qaytib kelganida, sizdan nima bo'ladi?" deb so'radi.

en: If I could only get back to this forest, I would pass my life very happily there." "My third command to the Winged Monkeys," said Glinda, "shall be to carry you to your forest.
uz: Agar men o'sha o'rmonga qaytib borishim mumkin bo'lganida, o'sha yerda hayotimni juda baxtli o'tkazardim". - dedi Glinda. - Winged Monkeysga bergan uchinchi amrim sizni o'rmoningizga olib ketish bo'ladi.

en: Then, having used up the powers of the Golden Cap, I shall give it to the King of the Monkeys, that he and his band may thereafter be free for evermore." The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion now thanked the Good Witch earnestly for her kindness; and Dorothy exclaimed: "You are certainly as good as you are beautiful!
uz: Keyin, oltin toʻpka qudratidan foydalanganimdan soʻng, uni Maymunlar Podshohiga beraman, shunda u va uning toʻpkalari bundan keyin abadiy ozod boʻlishlari mumkin". - deb aytdi qoʻrqinchli va Tin Woodman va Arslon endi yaxshi sehrgarga uning mehribonligi uchun minnatdorchilik bildirdi; Doroti esa: "Siz chindan ham goʻzalligingizdek yaxshisiz!

en: But you have not yet told me how to get back to Kansas." "Your Silver Shoes will carry you over the desert," replied Glinda.
uz: Ammo siz menga Kanzasga qaytib borish yo'lini hali aytmadingiz". - Glinda javob berdi: "Qumush poyabzallaringiz sizni sahroda ko'tarib ketadi.

en: "If you had known their power you could have gone back to your Aunt Em the very first day you came to this country." "But then I should not have had my wonderful brains!" cried the Scarecrow.
uz: "Agar siz ularning kuchini bilgan bo'lsangiz edi, ushbu mamlakatga kelgan birinchi kuningizda Em onangizning oldiga qaytib borgan bo'lar edingiz", - dedi qo'rqinchli qo'rqinchli.

en: "I might have passed my whole life in the farmer's cornfield." "And I should not have had my lovely heart," said the Tin Woodman.
uz: "Men butun hayotimni fermerning donzorida o'tkazgan bo'lardim", - dedi Tin Woodman.

en: "I might have stood and rusted in the forest till the end of the world." "And I should have lived a coward forever," declared the Lion, "and no beast in all the forest would have had a good word to say to me."
uz: "Men dunyoning oxirigacha o'rmonda to'xtatib, rang-barang bo'lar edim", - deb aytdi Arslon, "va men abadiy qo'rqoq bo'lib yashar edim va butun o'rmondagi hech bir hayvon menga yaxshi so'z aytmagan bo'lar edi".

en: "This is all true," said Dorothy, "and I am glad I was of use to these good friends.
uz: "Bularning barchasi haqiqatdir", dedi Doroti, "va men bu yaxshi do'stlar uchun foydali bo'lganimdan xursandman.

en: But now that each of them has had what he most desired, and each is happy in having a kingdom to rule besides, I think I should like to go back to Kansas." "The Silver Shoes," said the Good Witch, "have wonderful powers.
uz: Ammo endi ularning har biri eng ko'p xohlagan narsasiga ega bo'ldi va har biri hukmronlik qiladigan shohlikka ega bo'lishdan xursand bo'ldi, men o'ylaymanki, men Kanzasga qaytib borishni xohlayman. " "Qumush poyabzallar", dedi Yaxshi sehrgar, "qahramon kuchlarga ega.

en: And one of the most curious things about them is that they can carry you to any place in the world in three steps, and each step will be made in the wink of an eye.
uz: Ularning eng qiziqarli xususiyatlaridan biri shundaki, ular sizni uch bosqichda dunyodagi har qanday joyga olib ketishi mumkin va har bir qadam bir qarashda amalga oshiriladi.

en: All you have to do is to knock the heels together three times and command the shoes to carry you wherever you wish to go." "If that is so," said the child joyfully, "I will ask them to carry me back to Kansas at once." She threw her arms around the Lion's neck and kissed him, patting his big head tenderly.
uz: Faqat uch marta to'qnashuvlarni birlashtirib, poyabzallarga siz xohlagan joyga olib borishni buyurishingiz kerak". - Agar shunday bo'lsa, - dedi bola xursandchilik bilan, - men ulardan meni darhol Kanzasga olib borishni so'rayman. - O'z qo'llarini Arslonning bo'yniga tashladi va uni o'pdi, katta boshini yumshatdi.

en: Then she kissed the Tin Woodman, who was weeping in a way most dangerous to his joints.
uz: So'ngra u o'z qo'shiqlari uchun xavfli bo'lgan holda yig'layotgan Tin Woodmanni o'pdi.

en: But she hugged the soft, stuffed body of the Scarecrow in her arms instead of kissing his painted face, and found she was crying herself at this sorrowful parting from her loving comrades.
uz: Ammo u qo'rqinchli yuzini o'pishning o'rniga qo'llariga qo'shilib, qo'rqinchli qo'zg'oloning yumshatgan va to'ldirilgan tanasini quchoqladi va o'zini sevgan sheriklaridan bu qayg'uli bo'lishdan ko'ra yig'layotganini ko'rdi.

en: Glinda the Good stepped down from her ruby throne to give the little girl a good-bye kiss, and Dorothy thanked her for all the kindness she had shown to her friends and herself.
uz: Go'zal Glinda qizchaga xayrli muhabbat so'rab, o'zining rubin taxtidan tushdi va Doroti unga do'stlari va o'ziga ko'rsatgan barcha mehribonligi uchun minnatdorchilik bildirdi.

en: Dorothy now took Toto up solemnly in her arms, and having said one last good-bye she clapped the heels of her shoes together three times, saying: "Take me home to Aunt Em!" Instantly she was whirling through the air, so swiftly that all she could see or feel was the wind whistling past her ears.
uz: Doroti endi To'toni quchoqlariga ko'tarib oldi va oxirgi marta salom berib, uch marta poyabzallarining to'qnasini qo'yib: "Meni uyga Em qoni bilan olib boring!" - deb aytdi. O'sha zahoti u havoda o'z-o'zidan aylanib borardi, shunchalik tez ediki, u faqat shamolning qulog'idan o'tib ketishini ko'rdi yoki his qildi.

en: The Silver Shoes took but three steps, and then she stopped so suddenly that she rolled over upon the grass several times before she knew where she was.
uz: Qimgʻir poyabzallar faqat uch qadam qoʻydi va keyin u shunchalik toʻxtab qoldiki, u qaerdaligini bilmasdan oldin bir necha marta oʻt ustiga burildi.

en: At length, however, she sat up and looked about her.
uz: Biroq, oxir-oqibat u o'rnidan turib, atrofini ko'rdi.

en: "Good gracious!" she cried.
uz: "Go'zal mehribon!" - deb baqirdi u.

en: For she was sitting on the broad Kansas prairie, and just before her was the new farmhouse Uncle Henry built after the cyclone had carried away the old one.
uz: Chunki u keng Kanzas preriyasida o'tirgan edi, uning oldida esa Shaka Henrining yangi fermasi bor edi, u shamol eski fermani olib ketgandan so'ng qurilgan edi.

en: Uncle Henry was milking the cows in the barnyard, and Toto had jumped out of her arms and was running toward the barn, barking furiously.
uz: Onam Xenri hovuzda sigirlarni sug'orayotgan edi va Toto qo'llaridan tushib, g'azabga to'lib-toshgan holda hovuz tomon yugurib borar edi.

en: Dorothy stood up and found she was in her stocking-feet.
uz: Doroti o'rnidan turdi va o'zini chiroyli kiyimda ko'rdi.

en: For the Silver Shoes had fallen off in her flight through the air, and were lost forever in the desert.
uz: Chunki kumush poyabzallar u havo bo'ylab uchib ketayotganda tushdi va cho'lda abadiy yo'qoldi.

en: Chapter XXIV Home Again Aunt Em had just come out of the house to water the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.
uz: Ba'zi sahifalar haqida o'ylab ko'ring. XXIV Bobilga qaytish, tezda Em aka-uka ko'kraklarni sug'orish uchun uydan chiqqanida, ko'zlarini ko'tarib, Doroteni uning yoniga yugurib borayotganini ko'rdi.

en: "My darling child!" she cried, folding the little girl in her arms and covering her face with kisses.
uz: U: "Sevg'im!" - deb baqirib, qizchani qo'llarida o'rab, yuzini o'pish bilan qopladi.

en: "Where in the world did you come from?" "From the Land of Oz," said Dorothy gravely.
uz: "Sen qayerdan kelding?" - dedi Dorotsiya jiddiy ravishda.

en: "And here is Toto, too.

en: WHAT I CONSIDER TO HAVE BEEN THE BEGINNING OF MY YOUTH
uz: Men yoshligimning boshlanishi bo'lgan deb hisoblayman.

en: I have said that my friendship with Dimitri opened up for me a new view of my life and of its aim and relations.
uz: Dimitri bilan do'stligim menga hayotim, uning maqsadi va munosabatlari haqida yangi tasavvurni ochdi.

en: The essence of that view lay in the conviction that the destiny of man is to strive for moral improvement, and that such improvement is at once easy, possible, and lasting.
uz: Ushbu nuqtai nazarning mohiyati insoniyatning taqdiri axloqiy yaxshilanishga intilish va bunday yaxshilanish bir vaqtning o'zida oson, mumkin va uzoq davom etishi haqidagi e'tiqodda joylashgan.

en: Hitherto, however, I had found pleasure only in the new ideas which I discovered to arise from that conviction, and in the forming of brilliant plans for a moral, active future, while all the time my life had been continuing along its old petty, muddled, pleasure- seeking course, and the same virtuous thoughts which I and my adored friend Dimitri (“my own marvellous Mitia,” as I used to call him to myself in a whisper) had been wont to exchange with one another still pleased my intellect, but left my sensibility untouched.
uz: Biroq, hozirgacha men faqat o'sha ishonchdan kelib chiqqan yangi g'oyalardan va axloqiy, faol kelajak uchun ajoyib rejalar tuzishdan zavq oldim, butun umr mening hayotim o'zining eski mayda, chalg'itgan, zavq-shafqat yo'lida davom etgan bo'lsa-da, men va sevimli do'stim Dimitri (o'zimning ajoyib Mitia,o'zim uni shoshib o'zimga chaqirardim) bir-birimiz bilan almashgan bir xil fazilatli fikrlar men va o'zimning aql-idrokimni xursand qilgan, ammo hissiyligimni ta'sirlanmagan holda qoldirgan edim.

en: Nevertheless there came a moment when those thoughts swept into my head with a sudden freshness and force of moral revelation which left me aghast at the amount of time which I had been wasting, and made me feel as though I must at once—that very second—apply those thoughts to life, with the firm intention of never again changing them.
uz: Shunga qaramay, o'sha fikrlar boshimga to'satdan yangilik va axloqiy vahiylarning kuch-qudrati bilan kirib keldi, bu esa men o'tkazgan vaqtni hayron qoldirdi va o'zimni o'sha paytdan boshlab o'sha fikrlarni hayotga qo'llashim kerakligini his qildi va ularni boshqa hech qachon o'zgartirishga qaror qilmadim.

en: It is from that moment that I date the beginning of my youth.
uz: O'sha paytdan boshlab yoshligimning boshlanishi bilan tanishaman.

en: I was then nearly sixteen.
uz: O'shanda men deyarli o'n olti yoshda edim.

en: Tutors still attended to give me lessons, St.
uz: Menga dars berish uchun hali ham o'qituvchilar bor edi, St.

en: Jerome still acted as general supervisor of my education, and, willy-nilly, I was being prepared for the University.
uz: Jerom hali ham mening ta'lim-tarbiyamning bosh kuzatuvchisi bo'lib ishlagan va men universitetga tayyorlanayotgan edim.

en: In addition to my studies, my occupations included certain vague dreamings and ponderings, a number of gymnastic exercises to make myself the finest athlete in the world, a good deal of aimless, thoughtless wandering through the rooms of the house (but more especially along the maidservants’ corridor), and much looking at myself in the mirror.
uz: O'qishimdan tashqari, mening mashg'ulotlarimda ba'zi noaniq orzular va mulohazalar, o'zimni dunyodagi eng yaxshi sportchi bo'lish uchun bir qator gimnastik mashqlar, uy xonadonlarida maqsadsiz, o'ylamaslik bilan yurish (agar ayniqsa, xizmatkorlar koridori bo'ylab) va ko'p o'zimni ko'rinishda ko'rish o'z ichiga olgan.

en: From the latter, however, I always turned away with a vague feeling of depression, almost of repulsion.
uz: Biroq, men har doim depressiya, deyarli jirkanchlik hissi bilan yuz o'girardim.

en: Not only did I feel sure that my exterior was ugly, but I could derive no comfort from any of the usual consolations under such circumstances.
uz: Men nafaqat tashqi ko'rinishim yomon ekaniga ishonch hosil qildim, balki bunday sharoitlarda odatdagi tasallilardan hech qanday tasalli topolmadim.

en: I could not say, for instance, that I had at least an expressive, clever, or refined face, for there was nothing whatever expressive about it.
uz: Masalan, men hech bo'lmaganda ifodalangan, aqlli yoki sof suratga ega ekanimni aytolmasdim, chunki bu yerda hech qanday ifodalangan narsa yo'q edi.

en: Its features were of the most humdrum, dull, and unbecoming type, with small grey eyes which seemed to me, whenever I regarded them in the mirror, to be stupid rather than clever.
uz: Uning xususiyatlari eng chiroyli, chiroyli va o'rinsiz bo'lgan, kichik griz ko'zlar bilan ko'rinardi, ular menga ko'rinishda aqlsiz emas, aksincha ahmoqdek ko'rinardi.

en: Of manly bearing I possessed even less, since, although I was not exactly small of stature, and had,
uz: Erkaklik ruhidan men bundan ham kamroq ega bo'ldim, chunki, garchi men katta bo'lmagan bo'lsam-da,

en: moreover, plenty of strength for my years, every feature in my face was of the meek, sleepy-looking, indefinite type.
uz: Bundan tashqari, yoshlarim uchun ko'p kuch, yuzimdagi har bir xususiyat kamtarlik, uyqusizlik va cheksiz turdagi edi.

en: Even refinement was lacking in it, since, on the contrary, it precisely resembled that of a simple-looking moujik, while I also had the same big hands and feet as he.
uz: Hatto soflik ham yo'q edi, chunki, aksincha, u oddiy ko'rinishda bo'lgan moujikga o'xshaydi, men ham u kabi katta qo'l va oyoqlarim bor edi.

en: At the time, all this seemed to me very shameful.
uz: O'shanda bularning barchasi menga juda sharmanda tuyulgan.

en: SPRINGTIME Easter of the year when I entered the University fell late in April, so that the examinations were fixed for St.
uz: Men universitetga kirgan yildagi bahor o'tishi aprel oyining oxirida bo'lib o'tdi, shuning uchun imtihonlar St.

en: Thomas’s Week, [Easter week.] and I had to spend Good Friday in fasting and finally getting myself ready for the ordeal.
uz: Tomas haftasi, [bo'sh bayram haftasi] va men Buyuk juma kunini ro'za tutish va oxir-oqibat sinovga tayyorgarlik ko'rish bilan o'tkazishim kerak edi.

en: Following upon wet snow (the kind of stuff which Karl Ivanitch used to describe as “a child following, its father”), the weather had for three days been bright and mild and still.
uz: Issiq qordan so'ng (Karl Ivanitch uni "o'g'il, otasi" deb tasvirlagan) uch kun davomida yomg'ir yorqin, yengil va tinch bo'lgan.

en: Not a clot of snow was now to be seen in the streets, and the dirty slush had given place to wet, shining pavements and coursing rivulets.
uz: Ko'chalarda hatto bir oz ham qor ko'rinmasdi va bu yovvoyi suvlar issiq, yorqin piyodalar va oqib o'tadigan daryolarga joy berdi.

en: The last icicles on the roofs were fast melting in the sunshine, buds were swelling on the trees in the little garden, the path leading across the courtyard to the stables was soft instead of being a frozen ridge of mud, and mossy grass was showing green between the stones around the entrance- steps.
uz: Tovlardagi oxirgi muzlar quyosh nurida tez erib ketayotgan edi, kichkina bog'dagi daraxtlarda tug'ilgan tuxumlar yuzaga kelgan edi, hovli bo'ylab cho'plarga olib boradigan yo'l muzlangan maydan bo'lishning o'rniga yumshak edi va kirish daraxtlari atrofidagi toshlar o'rtasida o'simlik o't yashil ko'rinardi.

en: It was just that particular time in spring when the season exercises the strongest influence upon the human soul—when clear sunlight illuminates everything, yet sheds no warmth, when rivulets run trickling under one’s feet, when the air is charged with an odorous freshness, and when the bright blue sky is streaked with long, transparent clouds.
uz: Ba'zida bahorning o'sha ayni payti bo'lib, mavsum inson ruhiga eng kuchli ta'sir ko'rsatadi, - aniq quyosh nurlari hamma narsani yoritadi, lekin hech qanday issiqlik bermaydi, - ko'chalar bir qadam ostida oqib ketadi, - havo xushbo'y yangilik bilan to'ldirilgan va yorqin ko'k osmon uzun, shaffof bulutlar bilan to'lib-toshgan.

en: For some reason or another the influence of this early stage in the birth of spring always seems to me more perceptible and more impressive in a great town than in the country.
uz: Qaysi sababga ko'ra, bahor tug'ilishida ushbu erta bosqichning ta'siri menga har doim katta shaharda qishloqdan ko'ra ko'proq sezilarli va taassurot qoldiradi.

en: I was standing near the window—through the double frames of which the morning sun was throwing its mote-flecked beams upon the floor of what seemed to me my intolerably wearisome schoolroom—and working out a long algebraical equation on the blackboard.
uz: Men darcha yaqinida turgan edim, ertalab quyosh o'zining mo't-mo't bo'lgan soyalarini menga ko'rinmas darajada charchatadigan maktab xonadoni yer yuziga tashlab ketayotgan ikki martalik ramkalar orqali, qora lavha ustida uzoq algebraviy tenglamani ishlab chiqar edim.

en: In one hand I was holding a ragged, long-suffering “Algebra” and in the other a small piece of chalk which had already besmeared my hands, my face, and the elbows of my jacket.
uz: Bir qo'limda toshbo'ronli, uzoq vaqt sabrli algebra, ikkinchisida esa qo'llarim, yuzim va jaketimning qo'lqoplarini o'rab olgan mayda mayda mayda mayda mayda maydani ushlab turardim.

en: Nicola, clad in an apron, and with his sleeves rolled up, was picking out the putty from the window-frames with a pair of nippers, and unfastening the screws.
uz: Nikola, o'ziga o'rinli kiyim kiygan va qo'llarini o'girgan holda, bir juft to'plam bilan derazalar ramkalaridan to'plamni olib chiqib, burchaklarni ajratib qo'ydi.

en: The window looked out upon the little garden.
uz: Oyna o'sha kichkina bog'ga ko'z tikdi.

en: At length his occupation and the noise which he was making over it arrested my attention.
uz: Oxir oqibat uning ishlashi va uning tashqaridagi shovqin mening e'tiborimni jalb qildi.

en: At the moment I was in a very cross, dissatisfied frame of mind, for nothing seemed to be going right with me.
uz: O'sha paytda men juda xavotirda edim, mamnun emasman, chunki men bilan hech narsa yaxshi o'tmayotganga o'xshaydi.

en: I had made a mistake at the very beginning of my algebra, and so should have to work it out again; twice I had let the chalk drop.
uz: Algebra o'quvimning boshida xato qilib qo'ydim va uni yana hal qilishim kerak edi; ikki marta chalkani tushirib qo'ydim.

en: I was conscious that my hands and face were whitened all over; the sponge had rolled away into a corner; and the noise of Nicola’s operations was fast getting on my nerves.
uz: Men qo'llarim va yuzimning hamma tomoni oqlashganini bilardim; ko'krak burchakni burchakga aylantirib qo'yganini bilardim; Nikolasning operatsiyalarining shov-shuvlari tezda g'azabga tushardi.

en: I had a feeling as though I wanted to fly into a temper and grumble at some one, so I threw down chalk and “Algebra” alike, and began to pace the room.
uz: O'zimni g'azabga tushirib, kimgadir g'azablanmoqchi bo'lganimdek his qildim, shuning uchun men chalk va Algebrani tashlab, xonani tezda o'tkazishni boshladim.

en: Then suddenly I remembered that to-day we were to go to confession, and that therefore I must refrain from doing anything wrong.
uz: Oʻshanda birdan eslab qoldimki, bugun biz tanbehga boramiz va shuning uchun men hech qanday yomon ish qilmasligim kerak.

en: Next, with equal suddenness I relapsed into an extraordinarily goodhumoured frame of mind, and walked across to Nicola.
uz: Keyingi safar men ham xuddi shunday kutilmagan holatda g'azablanib, Nikolaga yetib keldim.

en: “Let me help you, Nicola,” I said, trying to speak as pleasantly as I possibly could.
uz: Men sizga yordam beraman, Nikola, deb aytdim va iloji boricha yoqimli so'zlashga harakat qildim.

en: The idea that I was performing a meritorious action in thus suppressing my ill-temper and offering to help him increased my good-humour all the more.
uz: O'zimning yomon ruhiy tuyg'ularimni yo'q qilib, unga yordam berishni taklif qilishda munosib harakat qilyapman degan g'oyam o'z humorimni yanada kuchaytirdi.

en: By this time the putty had been chipped out, and the screws removed, yet, though Nicola pulled with might and main at the cross- piece, the window-frame refused to budge.
uz: Bu vaqtga kelib, qo'lni kesib tashlab, shovqinlar olib tashlangan edi, ammo Nikola o'rta qismni kuchli va asosiy harakat bilan tortib olgan bo'lsa-da, deraza ramkasi o'tishni rad etdi.

en: “If it comes out as soon as he and I begin to pull at it together,” I thought, “it will be rather a shame, as then I shall have nothing more of the kind to do to-day.” Suddenly the frame yielded a little at one side, and came out.
uz: Agar u va men birgalikda harakat qilishni boshlaganimizdan so'ng u paydo bo'lsa, men o'yladimki, Bu juda yomon bo'ladi, chunki o'shanda men bugun hech qanday ishim bo'lmaydi. To'satdan ramka bir tomonga biroz tushdi va chiqdi.

en: “Where shall I put it?” I said.
uz: Qayerga qo'yishim kerak? - dedim men.

en: “Let ME see to it, if you please,” replied Nicola, evidently surprised as well as, seemingly, not over-pleased at my zeal.
uz: "Mening g'ayratim menga juda yoqmaydi", - deb javob berdi Nikola, ko'rinib turibdiki, bu menga hayratda va g'ayratimdan juda ham mamnun emas.

en: “We must not leave it here, but carry it away to the lumber-room, where I keep all the frames stored and numbered.” “Oh, but I can manage it,” I said as I lifted it up.
uz: Biz uni bu erda qoldirmasligimiz kerak, lekin uni o'simlik xonaga olib ketishimiz kerak, u erda men barcha ramkalarni saqlash va raqamlashni davom ettiraman.Oh, lekin men buni boshqarishim mumkin, deb aytdim, uni ko'targanimda.

en: I verily believe that if the lumber-room had been a couple of versts away, and the frame twice as heavy as it was, I should have been the more pleased.
uz: Agar o'simlik xonasi bir necha verst uzoqlikda bo'lganida va ramka ikki baravar og'ir bo'lganida, men bundan ham ko'proq mamnun bo'lar edim, deb o'ylayman.

en: I felt as though I wanted to tire myself out in performing this service for Nicola.
uz: Men o'zimni Nicola uchun bu xizmatni bajarishda charchatmoqchi bo'lganimdek his qildim.

en: When I returned to the room the bricks and screws had been replaced on the windowsill, and Nicola was sweeping the debris, as well as a few torpid flies, out of the open window.
uz: Xonaga qaytib kelganimda, deraza ustunidagi tikanlar va burchaklar almashtirilgan edi, nikola esa chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan edi.

en: The fresh, fragrant air was rushing into and filling all the room, while with it came also the dull murmur of the city and the twittering of sparrows in the garden.
uz: Yangi, xushbo'y havo butun xonani to'ldirib, unga shaharning g'alati shov-shuvlari va bog'dagi burgutlarning qichqiriqlari ham qo'shildi.

en: Everything was in brilliant light, the room looked cheerful, and a gentle spring breeze was stirring Nicola’s hair and the leaves of my “Algebra.” Approaching the window, I sat down upon the sill, turned my eyes downwards towards the garden, and fell into a brown study.
uz: Hamma narsa yorug' edi, xonadon hayajonli ko'rinardi va salqin bahor shamollari Nicola ning sochlarini va mening Algebra barglarimni hayratda qoldirdi. Oynaga yaqinlashib, ustunida o'tirib, bog'ga qarab ko'zimni pastga burdim va ko'k rangli o'rinbosarga tushib qoldim.

en: Something new to me, something extraordinarily potent and unfamiliar, had suddenly invaded my soul.
uz: O'zim uchun yangi, g'ayritabiiy kuchli va tanish bo'lmagan narsa birdan ruhimga kirib keldi.

en: The wet ground on which, here and there, a few yellowish stalks and blades of bright-green grass were to be seen; the little rivulets glittering in the sunshine, and sweeping clods of earth and tiny chips of wood along with them; the reddish twigs of the lilac, with their swelling buds, which nodded just beneath the window; the fussy twitterings of birds as they fluttered in the bush below; the blackened fence shining wet from the snow which had lately melted off it; and, most of all, the raw, odorous air and radiant sunlight—all spoke to me, clearly and unmistakably, of something new and beautiful, of something which, though I cannot repeat it here as it was then expressed to me, I will try to reproduce so far as I understood it.
uz: Bu yerda va u yerda bir nechta sariq rangli bo'laklar va yorqin yashil o'tlar bo'lgan boshoqlar ko'rinardi; quyosh nurida shishayotgan kichik daryolar va ular bilan birga yerning to'plamlari va kichik yog'och bo'laklarini ko'rib chiqish; chiroyli bo'laklar, o'zlarining yuzaga kelgan qo'llari bilan chiroyli to'plamlari, darcha ostida quvib yurgan qushlarning g'ayratli twitteringlari; so'nggi paytlarda erib ketgan qordan chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli to'siq; eng muhimi esa, xom, xushbo'y havo va yorqin quyosh nurlari menga yangi va chiroyli narsa haqida aniq gapirdi va men buni o'zim bilganimcha takrorlashga harakat qilaman, ammo men buni o'zim bilganimcha takrorlay olmayman.

en: Everything spoke to me of beauty, happiness, and virtue—as three things which were both easy and possible for me—and said that no one of them could exist without the other two, since beauty, happiness, and virtue were one.
