uz: Hamma narsa men uchun go'zallik, baxt va fazilat haqida uchta narsa sifatida gapirib, men uchun oson va mumkin bo'lgan va ularning hech biri boshqa ikkitasisiz mavjud bo'lmasligini aytdi, chunki go'zallik, baxt va fazilat bir narsa edi.

en: “How did I never come to understand that before?” I cried to myself.
uz: Qanday qilib men buni ilgari hech qachon tushunmaganman? O'zim uchun yig'ladim.

en: “How did I ever manage to be so wicked?
uz: Qanday qilib men bunday yovuzlikka erishdim?

en: Oh, but how good, how happy, I could be—nay, I WILL be—in the future!
uz: Oh, lekin men qanday yaxshi, qanday baxtli bo'lishim mumkin, kelajakda bo'laman!

en: At once, at once—yes, this
uz: Birdan, birdanyes, bu

en: very minute—I will become another being, and begin to live differently!” For all that, I continued sitting on the window-sill, continued merely dreaming, and doing nothing.
uz: O'zimni boshqa shaxsga aylantiraman va boshqacha hayot kechira boshlayman! Shunga qaramay, men o'zimni deraza ustunida o'tirib, shunchaki orzu qilib, hech narsa qilmay yurganman.

en: Have you ever, on a summer’s day, gone to bed in dull, rainy weather, and, waking just at sunset, opened your eyes and seen through the square space of the window—the space where the linen blind is blowing up and down, and beating its rod upon the window-sill—the rain-soaked, shadowy, purple vista of an avenue of lime-trees, with a damp garden path lit up by the clear, slanting beams of the sun, and then suddenly heard the joyous sounds of bird life in the garden, and seen insects flying to and fro at the open window, and glittering in the sunlight, and smelt the fragrance of the rain-washed air, and thought to yourself, “Am I not ashamed to be lying in bed on such an evening as this?” and, leaping joyously to your feet, gone out into the garden and revelled in all that welter of life?
uz: Yozgi kunlarda, chiroyli, yomg'ir yog'gan yomg'ir ostida uxlab ketib, quyosh botganida uyg'onib, ko'zlaringizni ochib, derazalar maydoni orqali ko'rdingizmi? - deb so'ragan bo'lsangiz, u yerdagi to'plamni ko'rib turibsizmi? - deb so'ragan bo'lsangiz kerak. - Yo'q, suvga cho'mgan, soya, bo'ylakli, mayda daraxtlar yo'li, quyoshning chiroyli nurlari bilan yorug' bo'lgan namli bog' yo'li bilan birga siz hech qachon yo'lga ketmaganmisiz? - deb o'yladingizmi? - deb so'raganingizda, to'satdan bog'dagi qushlar hayotining quvonchli tovushlarini eshitib, ochiq darchaga uchib borayotgan va quyosh nurida shinamlab borayotgan hasharotlar va yomg'irlangan havoga xushbo'y tuyg'ini eslab, o'zingizdan: "Men bunday bir kechada uxlab yotganimdan orzu emasmanmi?" deb o'yladingizmi?

en: If you have, then you can imagine for yourself the overpowering sensation which was then possessing me.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, unda o'zingiz uchun o'zimni o'zimda o'tkazgan qudratli hissiyotni tasavvur qila olasiz.

en: DREAMS “To-day I will make my confession and purge myself of every sin,” I thought to myself.
uz: Orzular Bugun men tanbeh beraman va o'zimni har qanday gunohdan tozalayman, deb o'yladim.

en: “Nor will I ever commit another one.” At this point I recalled all the peccadilloes which most troubled my conscience.
uz: Hamma qachon boshqa gunohni qilmayman. Shu payt vijdonimni xafa qilgan barcha gunohlarni esladim.

en: “I will go to church regularly every Sunday, as well as read the Gospel at the close of every hour throughout the day.
uz: Men har yakshanba kuni muntazam ravishda cherkovga boraman va kun bo'yi har bir soatning oxirida Injilni o'qib turaman.

en: What is more, I will set aside, out of the cheque which I shall receive each month after I have gone to the University, two-and-a-half roubles” (a tenth of my monthly allowance) “for people who are poor but not exactly beggars, yet without letting any one know anything about it.
uz: Bundan tashqari, universitetga o'tganimdan so'ng har oy qabul qiladigan chekdan, kambag'al bo'lgan, ammo begona bo'lmagan, ammo hech kimga bu haqda hech narsa bilmaslikka yordam beradigan odamlar uchun ikki yarim rubl (oylik ish haqining o'n bir qismi) ajrataman.

en: will begin to look out for people like that—orphans or old women—at once, yet never tell a soul what I am doing for them.
uz: Bunday odamlarga g'amxo'rlik qilishni boshlaydi, yetimlar yoki keksa ayollar bir marta, lekin hech qachon ular uchun nima qilayotganimni hech kimga aytmayman.

en: “Also, I will have a room here of my very own (St.
uz: Shuningdek, bu yerda o'zimning xonam bo'ladi (St.

en: Jerome’s, probably), and look after it myself, and keep it perfectly clean.
uz: Jeromes, ehtimol), va uni o'zim boqib, mukammal toza saqlash.

en: I will never let any one do anything for me, for every one is just a human being like myself.
uz: Men hech qachon hech kimning men uchun biror narsa qilishiga yo'l qo'ymayman, chunki har kim men kabi oddiy insondir.

en: Likewise I will walk every day, not drive, to the University.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, universitetga borish uchun har kuni piyoda emas, balki mashinada ketaman.

en: Even if some one gives me a drozhki [Russian phaeton.] I will sell it, and devote the money to the poor.
uz: Hatto kimdir menga bir drozhki [rus phaeton] bersa ham, uni sotaman va pulni kambag'allarga beraman.

en: Everything I will do exactly and always” (what that “always” meant I could not possibly have said, but at least I had a vivid consciousness of its connoting some kind of prudent, moral, and irreproachable life).
uz: Hamma narsani to'g'ri va doimo qilaman (men hech qachon aytolmasdim, lekin hech bo'lmaganda o'zimni o'ylaymanki, bu o'ta aqlli, axloqiy va aybsiz hayotni anglatadi).

en: “I will get up all my lectures thoroughly, and go over all the subjects beforehand, so that at the end of my first course I may come out top and write a thesis.
uz: Men barcha ma'ruzalarimni puxta o'tkazib, barcha mavzularni oldindan ko'rib chiqaman, shunda birinchi kursim yakunlanganda men yuqoriga chiqib, tezani yozishim mumkin.

en: During my second course also I will get up everything beforehand, so that I may soon be transferred to the third course, and at eighteen come out top in the examinations, and receive two gold medals, and go on to be Master of Arts, and Doctor, and the first scholar in Europe.
uz: Ikkinchi kursim davomida ham men hamma narsani oldindan uyg'otaman, shunda tez orada uchinchi kursga o'tkazilishim mumkin, o'n sakkiz yoshimda esa imtihonlarda birinchi o'rinni egallashim mumkin, ikkita oltin medal olishim mumkin va o'shanda San'at ustasi va doktor bo'lib, Evropadagi birinchi olim bo'lishim mumkin.

en: Yes, in all Europe I mean to be the first scholar.—Well, what next?” I asked myself at this point.
uz: Ha, butun Yevropada men birinchi olim bo'lishni xohlayman.Agar shunday bo'lsa, keyin nima bo'ladi? Men o'zimdan shunday so'radim.

en: Suddenly it struck me that dreams of this sort were a form of pride—a sin which I should have to confess to the priest that very evening, so I returned to the original thread of my meditations.
uz: Toʻsatdan, bunday tushlar magʻrurlikning bir shakli ekanligini angladim, oʻsha kuni kechqurun ruhoniyga tan berishim kerak boʻlgan gunoh, shuning uchun men oʻylashimning asl ustiga qaytdim.

en: “When getting up my lectures I will go to the Vorobievi Gori, [Sparrow Hills—a public park near Moscow.] and choose some spot under a tree, and read my lectures over there.
uz: Mening nutqlarimni qoldirganimda, Vorobievi Goriga boraman, [Moskva yaqinidagi Sparrow Hills] jamoat parkiga boraman va daraxt ostidagi biron bir joyni tanlayman va o'sha yerda nutqlarimni o'qib beraman.

en: Sometimes I will take with me something to eat —cheese or a pie from Pedotti’s, or something of the kind.
uz: Ba'zan men o'zim bilan cheys yoki Pedotti tarti yoki shunga o'xshash narsalarni yeyish uchun biror narsa olib boraman.

en: After that I will sleep a little, and then read some good book or other, or else draw pictures or play on some instrument (certainly I must learn to play the flute).
uz: Shundan so'ng biroz uxlab, keyin yaxshi kitob yoki boshqa narsalarni o'qib, rasm chizaman yoki biron bir asbobda o'ynayman (shuni aytish kerakki, men klaviaturada o'ynashni o'rganishim kerak).

en: Perhaps SHE too will be walking on the Vorobievi Gori, and will approach me one day and say, ‘Who are you?’ and I shall look at her, oh, so sadly, and say that I am the son of a priest, and that I am happy only when I am there alone, quite alone.
uz: Ehtimol, U ham Vorobievi Gori ustida yurib, bir kuni menga yaqinlashib: "Sen kimsan?" - deb so'raydi va men unga, ah, juda qayg'uli qarab, ruhoniy o'g'li ekanimni va faqat yolg'iz, yolg'iz bo'lganimda baxtli ekanimni aytaman.

en: Then she will give me her hand, and say something to me, and sit down beside me.
uz: Keyin u qo'lini uzatadi, menga biror narsa aytadi va yonimda o'tiradi.

en: So every day we shall go to the same spot, and be friends together, and I shall kiss her.
uz: Shunday qilib, biz har kuni bir xil joyga boramiz, do'st bo'lamiz va men uni o'paman.

en: That would not be right!
uz: Bu to'g'ri emas!

en: On the contrary, from this day forward I never mean to look at a woman again.
uz: Aksincha, bundan buyon boshqa hech qachon ayolga qarashni istamayman.

en: Never, never again do I mean to walk with a girl, nor
uz: Hech qachon, hech qachon boshqa qiz bilan yurishni xohlamayman.

en: even to go near one if I can help it.
uz: Hatto birortasiga yaqinlashishga ham, agar yordam bera olsam.

en: Yet, of course, in three years’ time, when I have come of age, I shall marry.
uz: Ammo, albatta, uch yildan keyin, katta bo'lganimda, turmush quraman.

en: Also, I mean to take as much exercise as ever I can, and to do gymnastics every day, so that, when I have turned twenty-five, I shall be stronger even than Rappo.
uz: Bundan tashqari, imkon qadar ko'proq mashq qilishni va har kuni jimnastikani o'tkazishni rejalashtiryapman, shunda yigirma besh yoshga to'lganimda, men Rappodan ham kuchliroq bo'laman.

en: On my first day’s training I mean to hold out half a pood [The Pood = ൥ൡ Russian pounds.] at arm’s length for five minutes, and the next day twenty-one pounds, and the third day twenty-two pounds, and so on, until at last I can hold out four poods in each hand, and be stronger even than a porter.
uz: Birinchi kunimdagi mashg'ulotlarimda men yarim puddni besh daqiqa davomida qo'llar uzunligida ushlab turishni, ertasi kuni yigirma bir funtni, uchinchi kuni yigirma ikki funtni ushlab turishni va shunga qadar har bir qo'limda to'rt pudd ushlab turishni va hatto porterdan ham kuchliroq bo'lishni nazarda tutaman.

en: Then, if ever any one should try to insult me or should begin to speak disrespectfully of HER, I shall take him so, by the front of his coat, and lift him up an arshin [The arshin = ൣ feet ൤ inches.] or two with one hand, and just hold him there, so that he may feel my strength and cease from his conduct.
uz: Keyin, agar kimdir meni haqoratlashga harakat qilsa yoki U haqda hurmatsizlik bilan gapira boshlasa, men uni kiyimining old tomonidan olib, bir qo'lim bilan arshin yoki ikki marta ko'tarib, uni o'sha yerda ushlab turaman, toki u mening kuchimni his etib, xulq-atvoridan voz kechsin.

en: Yet that too would not be right.
uz: Ammo bu ham to'g'ri emas.

en: No, no, it would not matter; I should not hurt him, merely show him that I—” Let no one blame me because the dreams of my youth were as foolish as those of my childhood and boyhood.
uz: Yo'q, yo'q, bu ahamiyatga ega emas; men unga zarar etkazmasam kerak, faqat unga menga hech kim ayb bermasligini ko'rsating, chunki yoshlik orzularim bolalik va bolalik orzularimdek ahmoqlik edi.

en: I am sure that, even if it be my fate to live to extreme old age and to continue my story with the years, I, an old man of seventy, shall be found dreaming dreams just as impossible and childish as those I am dreaming now.
uz: Ishonchim komilki, hatto cheksiz keksalikkacha yashash va hikoyamni yillar davomida davom ettirish taqdirim bo'lsa-da, yetmish yoshli keksa odam bo'lgan men ham hozirgi orzularimdek imkonsiz va bolalik orzularni ko'rib turibman.

en: I shall be dreaming of some lovely Maria who loves me, the toothless old man, as she might love a Mazeppa; of some imbecile son who, through some extraordinary chance, has suddenly become a minister of state; of my suddenly receiving a windfall of a million of roubles.
uz: Men meni sevgan go'zal Mariya, tishsiz keksa odamni, u mazeppa kabi sevgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb orzu qilaman; biron bir ahmoq o'g'lim, noyob tasodif tufayli to'satdan davlat vaziriga aylangan; mening to'satdan million rubl miqdorida to'lov topgan bo'lishim haqida orzu qilaman.

en: I am sure that there exists no human being, no human age, to whom or to which that gracious, consolatory power of dreaming is totally a stranger.
uz: Ishonchim komilki, hech qanday inson mavjud emas, hech qanday inson davri mavjud emas, unga yoki uning uchun orzu qilishning rahmli, tasalli beruvchi kuchi mutlaqo begona.

en: Yet, save for the one general feature of magic and impossibility, the dreams of each human being, of each age of man, have their own distinguishing characteristics.
uz: Biroq, sehr va imkonsizlikning bitta umumiy xususiyatidan tashqari, har bir insonning, har bir inson davrining orzularining o'z o'ziga xos xususiyatlari bor.

en: At the period upon which I look as having marked the close of my boyhood and the beginning of my youth, four leading sentiments formed the basis of my dreams.
uz: O'smirligimning oxiri va yoshligimning boshlanishi bo'lgan davrda to'rtta asosiy his-tuyg'ular orzularimga asos bo'ldi.

en: The first of those sentiments was love for HER—for an imaginary woman whom I always pictured the same in my dreams, and whom I somehow expected to meet some day and somewhere.
uz: Bu his-tuyg'ularning birinchi biri, men har doim tushimda xuddi shunday tasavvur qilgan, bir kun yoki bir joyda uchrashishni kutgan tasavvurga ega bo'lgan ayolga bo'lgan sevgim edi.

en: This she of mine had a little of Sonetchka in her, a little of Masha as Masha could look when she stood washing linen over the clothes- tub, and a little of a certain woman with pearls round her fair white
uz: Bu mening o'zimda bir oz Sonetchka bor edi, Masha kiyim-kechakni yuvishda turganida ko'rinishi mumkin bo'lgan Masha biroz, va o'zining chiroyli oq ko'rinishida marvaridlar bo'lgan bir ayolning biroz.

en: neck whom I had once seen long, long ago at a theatre, in a box below our own.
uz: Men bir vaqtlar teatrda, o'zimizning pastidagi quti ichida ko'rgan bo'limni ko'rdim.

en: My second sentiment was a craving for love.
uz: Ikkinchi his-tuyg'ularim sevgiga bo'lgan istak edi.

en: I wanted every one to know me and to love me.
uz: Men hamma meni tanib-bilishini va sevishini xohlardim.

en: I wanted to be able to utter my name—Nicola Irtenieff—and at once to see every one thunderstruck at it, and come crowding round me and thanking me for something or another, I hardly knew what.
uz: Men o'z ismimni aytishni istardim va birdan har bir odamning g'alaba qozonganini ko'rishni istardim va atrofimda to'planib, biror narsa uchun minnatdorchilik bildirishni xohlardim, lekin nima ekanligini bilmasdim.

en: My third sentiment was the expectation of some extraordinary, glorious happiness that was impending—some happiness so strong and assured as to verge upon ecstasy.
uz: Uchinchi his-tuyg'ularim, o'zgacha, ulug'vor baxtning kutishidir. Bu baxt juda kuchli va shubhasiz bo'lib, ekstazning o'rniga yetib boradi.

en: Indeed, so firmly persuaded was I that very, very soon some unexpected chance would suddenly make me the richest and most famous man in the world that I lived in constant, tremulous expectation of this magic good fortune befalling me.
uz: Darhaqiqat, men juda qattiq ishongan edimki, juda tezda kutilmagan holat meni dunyodagi eng boy va eng mashhur odamga aylantiradi, shuning uchun men o'zimga yuz beradigan bu sehrli omadning doimiy, dahshatli kutishida yashardim.

en: I was always thinking to myself that “IT is beginning,” and that I should go on thereafter to attain everything that a man could wish for.
uz: Men har doim o'zimga o'zimda shunday o'yladimki, bu boshlanmoqda va men o'sha paytdan keyin odam xohlagan hamma narsaga erishish uchun davom etishim kerak.

en: Consequently, I was for ever hurrying from place to place, in the belief that “IT” must be “beginning” just where I happened not to be.
uz: Natijada, men o'zim bo'lmagan joyda IT boshlanishi kerak deb o'yladim.

en: Lastly, my fourth and principal sentiment of all was abhorrence of myself, mingled with regret—yet a regret so blended with the certain expectation of happiness to which I have referred that it had in it nothing of sorrow.
uz: Va nihoyat, mening to'rtinchi va eng asosiy his-tuyg'ularim o'zimdan nafratlanish edi, bu afsus bilan aralashardi, ammo afsusning o'zi baxtga umid bog'lab qo'yilgan edi, shuning uchun u hech qanday qayg'u keltirmagan edi.

en: It seemed to me that it would be so easy and natural for me to tear myself away from my past and to remake it—to forget all that had been, and to begin my life, with all its relations, anew—that the past never troubled me, never clung to me at all.
uz: O'tmishimdan ajralib o'tish, o'tmishimni qayta tiklash, o'tmishdagi hamma narsani unutish va hayotimni, uning barcha aloqalari bilan yangidan boshlash men uchun shunchalik oson va tabiiy bo'lib tuyulganki, o'tmishim meni hech qachon bezovta qilmagan, menga hech qachon bog'liq bo'lmagan.

en: I even found a certain pleasure in detesting the past, and in seeing it in a darker light than the true one.
uz: Hatto o'tmishdan nafratlanib, uni haqiqatdan ham qorong'u yorug'likda ko'rishdan zavq oldim.

en: This note of regret and of a curious longing for perfection were the chief mental impressions which I gathered from that new stage of my growth—impressions which imparted new principles to my view of myself, of men, and of God’s world.
uz: O'zimga, odamlarga va Xudo dunyosiga bo'lgan nuqtai nazarimga yangi tamoyillarni o'rgatgan o'sishning o'sha yangi bosqichidan olgan asosiy ongimdagi taassurotlar bu afsus va mukammallikka bo'lgan qiziqarli orzu edi.

en: O good and consoling voice, which in later days, in sorrowful days when my soul yielded silently to the sway of life’s falseness and depravity, so often raised a sudden, bold protest against all iniquity, as well as mercilessly exposed the past, commanded, nay, compelled, me to love only the pure vista of the present, and promised me all that was fair and happy in the future!
uz: Ey yaxshi va tasalli beruvchi ovoz, o'tmishda, ruhim hayotning yolg'on va buzuqligi ta'siriga beparvo bo'lgan og'ir kunlarda, ko'pincha barcha yomonliklarga qarshi to'satdan jasoratli va g'ayratli qarshilik ko'tardi, o'tmishni shafqatsiz oshkor etdi, menga faqat hozirning sof ko'rinishini sevishga buyurdi va kelajakda adolatli va baxtli bo'lgan hamma narsani va'da qildi!

en: O good and consoling voice!
uz: Ey yaxshi va tasalli beruvchi ovoz!

en: Surely the day will never come when you are silent?
uz: Siz sukut saqlashingiz mumkin bo'lgan kun hech qachon kelmaydi, shundaymi?

en: OUR FAMILY CIRCLE PAPA was seldom at home that spring.
uz: Oʻsha bahorda otamiz kamdan-kam uyda boʻlgan.

en: Yet, whenever he was so, he seemed extraordinarily cheerful as he either strummed his favourite pieces on the piano or looked roguishly at us and made jokes about us all, not excluding even Mimi.
uz: Biroq, qachonki u shunday bo'lsa, o'zining sevimli musiqalarini piyanoga qo'shib qo'yganida yoki bizlarga qo'pol qarab, hatto Mimiga ham qo'shilib, hammamiz haqida hazillar qilganida, u juda quvonchli ko'rinardi.

en: For instance, he would say that the Tsarevitch himself had seen Mimi at the rink, and fallen so much in love with her that he had presented a petition to the Synod for divorce; or else that I had been granted an appointment as secretary to the Austrian ambassador—a piece of news which he imparted to us with a perfectly grave face.
uz: Misol uchun, u, Tsarevitchning o'zi Mimini rinkda ko'rib, unga shunchalik muhabbat ko'rsatganini va sinodga ajrashish uchun ariza berganini aytadi yoki menga Avstriya elchisining kotibi etib tayinlanganini aytadi.

en: Next, he would frighten Katenka with some spiders (of which she was very much afraid), engage in an animated conversation with our friends Dubkoff and Nechludoff, and tell us and our guests, over and over again, his plans for the year.
uz: Keyin u Katenkani ba'zi o'simliklar bilan qo'rqitadi (ulardan u juda qo'rqardi), do'stlarimiz Dubkoff va Nechludoff bilan jonli suhbatda ishtirok etadi va bizga va mehmonlarimizga yil uchun rejalarini takror-takror aytib beradi.

en: Although these plans changed almost from day to day, and were for ever contradicting one another, they seemed so attractive that we were always glad to listen to them, and Lubotshka, in particular, would glue her eyes to his face, so as not to lose a single word.
uz: Garchi ushbu rejalar deyarli kundan-kunga o'zgarib, bir-biriga zid bo'lsa-da, ular shunchalik jozibali ko'rinardiki, ularni tinglashdan doimo xursand edik va Lubotshka, ayniqsa, bir so'zni ham yo'qotmaslik uchun ko'zlarini uning yuziga yopib qo'yadi.

en: One day his plan would be that he should leave my brother and myself at the University, and go and live with Lubotshka in Italy for two years.
uz: Bir kuni uning rejasi mening ukam va menni universitetda qoldirib, ikki yil davomida Italiyada Lubotshka bilan birga yashash edi.

en: Next, the plan would be that he should buy an estate on the south coast of the Crimea, and take us for an annual visit there; next, that we should migrate en masse to St.
uz: Keyinchalik, reja shundaki, u Qrimning janubiy sohilidagi mulkni sotib olib, bizni u yerga har yili tashrif buyuradi; keyinchalik, biz St. Petersburgga ko'pchilik bilan ko'chib o'tamiz.

en: Petersburg; and so forth.
uz: Sankt-Peterburg va hokazo.

en: Yet, in addition to this unusual cheerfulness of his, another change had come over him of late—a change which greatly surprised me.
uz: Biroq, uning o'zgacha quvonchidan tashqari, u o'zining oxirgi o'zgarishlaridan tashqari yana bir o'zgarish sodir bo'ldi, bu esa meni hayratda qoldirdi.

en: This was that he had had some fashionable clothes made—an olive- coloured frockcoat, smart trousers with straps at the sides, and a long wadded greatcoat which fitted him to perfection.
uz: Buning sababi shundaki, u zeytun rangli paltaroshlik, qo'llarida qo'riqchilar bo'lgan aqlli kiyimlar va uni mukammal darajada to'ldiradigan uzun va chiroyli paltaroshlik bilan mashhur kiyimga ega edi.

en: Often, too, there was a delightful smell of scent about him when he came home from a party—more especially when he had been to see a lady of whom Mimi never spoke but with a sigh and a face that seemed to say: “Poor orphans!
uz: Ko'pincha u bir ziyofatdan uyga kelganida, ayniqsa, Mimi hech qachon gapirmagan bir xonimni ko'rganida, uni ko'rish uchun ko'pincha yoqimli xushbo'y tutatqi paydo bo'lardi.

en: It is a good thing that SHE is gone now!” and so on, and so on.
uz: Yaxshiyamki, hozir U yo'qolgan! va shunga o'xshab, va shunga o'xshab.

en: From Nicola (for Papa never
uz: Nicoladan (Papa uchun hech qachon)

en: spoke to us of his gambling) I had learnt that he (Papa) had been very fortunate in play that winter, and so had won an extraordinary amount of money, all of which he had placed in the bank after vowing that he would play no more that spring.
uz: O'sha qishda u (Papa) o'yinda juda omadli bo'lganini va katta miqdorda pul yutib olganini bilib oldim, bularning barchasini u bahorda yana o'ynamaslikka va'da berganidan so'ng bankga qo'ygan edi.

en: Evidently, it was his fear of being unable to resist again doing so that was rendering him anxious to leave for the country as soon as possible.
uz: Ko'rinib turganidek, bu ishni yana qila olmasligidan qo'rqish uni mamlakatni tezroq tark etishni istaydigan.

en: Indeed, he ended by deciding not to wait until I had entered the University, but to take the girls to Petrovskoe immediately after Easter, and to leave Woloda and myself to follow them at a later season.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, u universitetga kirgunicha kutmaslikka qaror qildi, balki qizlarni Fisih bayramidan so'ng Petrovskoyega olib ketishga va keyinchalik ularni kuzatib borish uchun Woloda va o'zimni tark etishga qaror qildi.

en: All that winter, until the opening of spring, Woloda had been inseparable from Dubkoff, while at the same time the pair of them had cooled greatly towards Dimitri.
uz: O'sha qish davomida, bahor ochilishidan oldin, Voloda Dubkoffdan ajralmas edi, ayni paytda ularning juftligi Dimitri tomon juda sovuq bo'lgan edi.

en: Their chief amusements (so I gathered from conversations overheard) were continual drinking of champagne, sledge-driving past the windows of a lady with whom both of them appeared to be in love, and dancing with her—not at children’s parties, either, but at real balls!
uz: Ularning asosiy zavqlari (men eshitgan suhbatlardan bilib olganimcha) doimiy ravishda shampan ichish, ikkalasi ham muhabbatga ega bo'lib ko'rinadigan bir ayolning derazalaridan pastga o'tish va bolalar partiyasida emas, balki haqiqiy to'ylarda u bilan raqs o'tkazish edi!

en: It was this last fact which, despite our love for one another, placed a vast gulf between Woloda and myself.
uz: Bu oxirgi fakt, bir-birimizga bo'lgan sevgimizga qaramay, Woloda va men o'rtasida katta bo'shliq yaratdi.

en: We felt that the distance between a boy still taking lessons under a tutor and a man who danced at real, grown-up balls was too great to allow of their exchanging mutual ideas.
uz: Biz o'yladikki, o'g'il o'qituvchisi tomonidan dars o'tayotgan o'g'il bilan haqiqiy kattalar balolarida raqs o'tkazadigan erkak o'rtasidagi masofada o'zaro fikr almashishga imkon berolmaydi.

en: Katenka, too, seemed grown-up now, and read innumerable novels; so that the idea that she would some day be getting married no longer seemed to me a joke.
uz: Katenka ham hozir katta bo'lib ko'rinardi va son-sanoqsiz romani o'qigan edi; shuning uchun u bir kun turmushga chiqishi haqidagi fikr menga hazil emas edi.

en: Yet, though she and Woloda were thus grown- up, they never made friends with one another, but, on the contrary, seemed to cherish a mutual contempt.
uz: Biroq, u va Voloda o'sha paytda katta bo'lishsa-da, hech qachon bir-birlari bilan do'stlashmagan, aksincha, o'zaro hurmatsizlikni o'z ichiga olgan edilar.

en: In general, when Katenka was at home alone, nothing but novels amused her, and they but slightly; but as soon as ever a visitor of the opposite sex called, she at once grew lively and amiable, and used her eyes for saying things which I could not then understand.
uz: Umuman olganda, Katenka uyda yolg'iz bo'lganida, uni faqatgina romandlar zavqlantirardi va ular birozgina zavqlantirardi; lekin har safar qarama-qarshi jinsiy tashrif buyuruvchi tashrif buyurganida, u darhol jonli va mehribon bo'lib, ko'zlarini o'zi tushunmagan narsalarni aytish uchun ishlatardi.

en: It was only later, when she one day informed me in conversation that the only thing a girl was allowed to indulge in was coquetry—coquetry of the eyes, I mean— that I understood those strange contortions of her features which to every one else had seemed a matter for no surprise at all.
uz: Keyinchalik, bir kuni u suhbatda menga qizning faqat ko'z koketiriyasiga berilib ketishi mumkinligini aytganda, men uning belgilarining o'zgacha contorsiyalarini tushunib yetdim, bu hamma uchun hech qanday ajablanarli bo'lmagan.

en: Lubotshka also had begun to wear what was almost a long dress—a dress which almost concealed her goose-shaped feet; yet she still remained as ready a weeper as ever.
uz: Lubotshka, shuningdek, deyarli uzun kiyim kiyishni boshlagan edi, bu kiyim deyarli qo'zg'ochga o'xshash oyoqlarini yashirgan edi; ammo u hali ham har doimgidek yig'lashga tayyor edi.

en: She dreamed now of marrying, not a hussar, but a singer or an instrumentalist, and accordingly
uz: Endi u husar emas, balki qo'shiqchi yoki asbob-uskunachilar bilan turmush qurishni orzu qilardi.

en: applied herself to her music with greater diligence than ever.
uz: O'z musiqasini har qachongidan ko'proq g'ayrat bilan qo'llab-quvvatladi.

en: Jerome, who knew that he was going to remain with us only until my examinations were over, and so had obtained for himself a new post in the family of some count or another, now looked with contempt upon the members of our household.
uz: Jerom faqatgina imtihonlarimni o'tkazmaguncha biz bilan qolishini bilgan va shu sababli o'zi uchun qandaydir homiy yoki boshqa oilada yangi lavozimga ega bo'lgan, endi uyimiz a'zolariga hurmatsizlik bilan qaragan edi.

en: He stayed indoors very little, took to smoking cigarettes (then all the rage), and was for ever whistling lively tunes on the edge of a card.
uz: U juda oz uyda qoldi, tamaki chekishni boshladi (o'shanda bu juda ko'p bo'lgan) va kartaning chegaralarida jonli qo'shiqlarni abadiy pishirib turardi.

en: Mimi daily grew more and more despondent, as though, now that we were beginning to grow up, she looked for nothing good from any one or anything.
uz: Mimi kundan-kunga ko'proq tushkunlikka tushib borardi, xuddi biz katta bo'la boshlaganimiz sababli, u hech kimdan yoki biron narsadan hech qanday yaxshilik izlamasdek edi.

en: When, on the day of which I am speaking, I went in to luncheon I found only Mimi, Katenka, Lubotshka, and St.
uz: O'sha kuni men tushlikka borganimda, faqat Mimi, Katenka, Lubotshka va St.

en: Jerome in the dining- room.
uz: Jerom oshxonada.

en: Papa was away, and Woloda in his own room, doing some preparation work for his examinations in company with a party of his comrades: wherefore he had requested that lunch should be sent to him there.
uz: Otam yo'q edi, Voloda esa o'z xonasida edi, u o'z imtihonlariga tayyorgarlik ko'rish ishlarini hamrohlar guruhi bilan o'tkazgan edi: shuning uchun u kechki ovqatni u yerga yuborishni so'ragan edi.

en: Of late, Mimi had usually taken the head of the table, and as none of us had any respect for her, luncheon had lost most of its refinement and charm.
uz: So'nggi paytlarda Mimi odatda stolning boshini egallab olgan edi va bizlardan hech kim unga hurmat ko'rsatmaganligi sababli, kechki ovqatning ko'pchiligi o'zining go'zalligi va jozibaliligini yo'qotgan edi.

en: That is to say, the meal was no longer what it had been in Mamma’s or our grandmother’s time, namely, a kind of rite which brought all the family together at a given hour and divided the day into two halves.
uz: Ya'ni, ovqat o'z vaqtida bo'lganidek bo'lmadi, chunki bu bir xil odat bo'lib, butun oilani ma'lum bir soatda bir joyga yig'ib, kunni ikkiga bo'linadi.

en: We allowed ourselves to come in as late as the second course, to drink wine in tumblers (St.
uz: Biz o'zimizga ikkinchi kursgacha kechiktirib, sharobni tumblerlarda ichishga ruxsat berdik (St.

en: Jerome himself set us the example), to roll about on our chairs, to depart without saying grace, and so on.
uz: Jeromning o'zi bizga o'rnak ko'rsatdi), o'z o'rindiqlarimizda aylanib yurish, rahmat aytmasdan ketish va hokazo.

en: In fact, luncheon had ceased to be a family ceremony.
uz: Darhaqiqat, kechki ovqat oilaviy marosim bo'lib qolmadi.

en: In the old days at Petrovskoe, every one had been used to wash and dress for the meal, and then to repair to the drawing- room as the appointed hour (two o’clock) drew near, and pass the time of waiting in lively conversation.
uz: Qadimda Petrovskoyda har bir kishi ovqatlanish uchun yuvish va kiyinish uchun ishlatilgan edi, so'ngra tayinlangan soat (ikki soat) yaqinlashganda, o'tirish xonasida tuzatish va jonli suhbatda kutish vaqtini o'tkazish uchun ishlatilgan edi.

en: Just as the clock in the servants’ hall was beginning to whirr before striking the hour, Foka would enter with noiseless footsteps, and, throwing his napkin over his arm and assuming a dignified, rather severe expression, would say in loud, measured tones: “Luncheon is ready!” Thereupon, with pleased, cheerful faces, we would form a procession—the elders going first and the juniors following, and, with much rustling of starched petticoats and subdued creaking of boots and shoes— would proceed to the dining-room, where, still talking in undertones, the company would seat themselves in their accustomed places.
uz: Xizmatkorlar zalidagi soat soat soatga to'kishdan oldin qichqirishni boshlagan paytda, Foka ovozsiz qadamlar bilan kirardi va o'z qo'li ustiga servetini tashlab, munosib, juda qattiq so'zlarni qabul qilib, baland ovozda: "Qutlug' kecha tayyor!" deb aytardi.Shundan so'ng, xursand, quvonchli yuzlar bilan biz bir marosimni tashkil qilardik.Ikki oqsoqollar birinchi bo'lib, kichiklar esa ketib, o'zlarining odatdagi o'rinlariga o'tirardilar.

en: Or, again, at Moscow, we would all of us be standing before the table
uz: Yoki yana Moskvada hammamiz dasturxon oldida turardik.

en: ready-laid in the hall, talking quietly among ourselves as we waited for our grandmother, whom the butler, Gabriel, had gone to acquaint with the fact that luncheon was ready.
uz: Jamoatda to'xtash uchun tayyor bo'lgan Gabriel uy egasi borib, tushlik tayyor ekanligi bilan tanishtirgan buvimizni kutganimizda, o'zaro xotirjamlik bilan gaplashib o'tirdik.

en: Suddenly the door would open, there would come the faint swish of a dress and the sound of footsteps, and our grandmother—dressed in a mob-cap trimmed with a quaint old lilac bow, and wearing either a smile or a severe expression on her face according as the state of her health inclined her—would issue from her room.
uz: Toʻsatdan eshik ochiladi, kiyimning soʻzlashi va qadamlarning ovozi paydo boʻladi, buvimiz esa ajoyib eski lilak qoʻrqinch bilan bezatilgan, tabassum yoki salomatligiga qarab yuzidagi qattiq ifodani kiygan va xonadonidan chiqib ketishga moyil boʻlgan moʻljallangan qoʻpollik toʻpasiga kiyingan.

en: Gabriel would hasten to precede her to her arm-chair, the other chairs would make a scraping sound, and, with a feeling as though a cold shiver (the precursor of appetite) were running down one’s back, one would seize upon one’s damp, starched napkin, nibble a morsel or two of bread, and, rubbing one’s hands softly under the table, gaze with eager, radiant impatience at the steaming plates of soup which the butler was beginning to dispense in order of ranks and ages or according to the favour of our grandmother.
uz: Uning orqasidan o'tirishga shoshilsa, boshqa o'rindiqlar qovurib ketadigan ovoz chiqaradi va so'ng ustozning orqasidan sovuq titroq (o'tishning avvali) ketayotgandek hissa paydo bo'ladi, u bir-birining issiq, o'simlik sovg'asini qo'lga oladi, bir-ikki tovuq nonni o'g'ib oladi va, qo'llarini jadal o'rnatib, jadval ostida ko'tarib, qaynoq, shiddatli surunqa plakatlariga ko'z tikadi, bu butler ranglar va yoshlar tartibida yoki buvimizning roziligiga ko'ra yetkazishni boshlaydi.

en: On the present occasion, however, I was conscious of neither excitement nor pleasure when I went in to luncheon.
uz: Biroq, hozirgi paytda men tushlikka borganimda, na hayajon va na quvonchga ega emas edim.

en: Even the mingled chatter of Mimi, the girls, and St.
uz: Hatto Mimi, qizlar va St.

en: Jerome about the horrible boots of our Russian tutor, the pleated dresses worn by the young Princesses Kornakoff, and so forth (chatter which at any other time would have filled me with a sincerity of contempt which I should have been at no pains to conceal—at all events so far as Lubotshka and Katenka were concerned), failed to shake the benevolent frame of mind into which I had fallen.
uz: Jerom rus o'qituvchimizning dahshatli poyabzallari, yosh princess Kornakoff kiygan pillali kiyimlari va hokazolar haqida (har qanday boshqa vaqtda meni hurmatsizlikning samimiyligi bilan to'ldirgan gap-so'zlar, men Lubotshka va Katenka uchun barcha voqealarni yashirish uchun hech qanday harakat qilmagan bo'lar edim), men tushgan mehribon ruhni silkitishga muvaffaq bo'lmadi.

en: I was unusually good-humoured that day, and listened to everything with a smile and a studied air of kindness.
uz: O'sha kuni o'zgacha yaxshi ruhda edim va hamma narsani tabassum va mehribonlik bilan tingladim.

en: Even when I asked for the kvas I did so politely, while I lost not a moment in agreeing with St.
uz: Hatto kvasni so'raganimda ham men buni xushmuomalalik bilan qildim, ammo St.

en: Jerome when he told me that it was undoubtedly more correct to say “Je peux” than “Je puis.” Yet, I must confess to a certain disappointment at finding that no one paid any particular attention to my politeness and good-humour.
uz: Jerom menga aytganda, men "Men qila olaman" degan so'zlarni aytishdan ko'ra "Men qila olaman" degan so'zlarni aytish shubhasiz ko'proq to'g'ri bo'lganini aytdi. Biroq, hech kim mening xushmuomalaligimga va xushmuomalaligimga alohida e'tibor bermaganini bilib, o'zimni kamsitganimni aytishim kerak.

en: After luncheon, Lubotshka showed me a paper on which she had written down a list of her sins: upon which I observed that, although the idea was excellent so far as it went, it would be still better for her to write down her sins on her SOUL—“a very different matter.” “Why is it ‘a very different matter’?” asked Lubotshka.
uz: Ovqatdan so'ng Lubotshka o'zining gunohlari ro'yxatini yozgan qog'ozni menga ko'rsatdi: uning ustida men fikr juda yaxshi bo'lgan bo'lsa-da, uning uchun o'z gunohlarini o'zining JONIYLASIDA yozish yaxshiroq bo'lishini payqadim. Nima uchun bu juda boshqacha masala? deb so'radi Lubotshka.

en: “Never mind: that is all right; you do not understand me,” and I went upstairs to my room, telling St.
uz: Bosh qilma: bu yaxshi; siz meni tushunmayapsiz, va men o'z xonamga ko'tarilganimda, St.

en: Jerome that I was going to work, but in reality purposing to occupy the hour and a half before confession time in writing down a list of my daily tasks and duties which should last me all my life, together with a statement of my life’s aim, and the rules by which I meant unswervingly to be guided.
uz: Yeromon menga ishga borishimni aytdi, lekin aslida tanbehdan bir yarim soat oldin kundalik vaziyatlarimni va butun hayotim davomida davom ettirishim kerak bo'lgan vazifalarimni ro'yxatga olishni va hayotimning maqsadi va qoidalari to'g'risida ma'lumotni hamda qat'iy yo'naltirilishni xohlagan qoidalarni yozishni xohladim.

en: MY RULES I TOOK some sheets of paper, and tried, first of all, to make a list of my tasks and duties for the coming year.
uz: Qoidalar Men qog'ozlarni olib, birinchi navbatda kelgusi yil uchun vazifalar va vazifalar ro'yxatini tuzishga harakat qildim.

en: The paper needed ruling, but, as I could not find the ruler, I had to use a Latin dictionary instead.
uz: Qog'ozga hukm kerak edi, lekin hukmni topolmagani uchun, uning o'rniga latin lug'atidan foydalanishim kerak edi.

en: The result was that, when I had drawn the pen along the edge of the dictionary and removed the latter, I found that, in place of a line, I had only made an oblong smudge on the paper, since the dictionary was not long enough to reach across it, and the pen had slipped round the soft, yielding corner of the book.
uz: Natija shundaki, tilkachani lug'atning chegara bo'ylab chizganimda va tilkachani olib tashlaganimda, bir satrning o'rniga qog'ozda faqat uzluksiz bir burchak ko'rsatganimni ko'rdim, chunki tilka unga yetib borishga yetarlicha uzun emas edi va tilka kitobning yumshak, samarasiz burchasiga o'girib ketgan edi.

en: Thereupon I took another piece of paper, and, by carefully manipulating the dictionary, contrived to rule what at least RESEMBLED lines.
uz: Shundan so'ng men yana bir qog'ozni olib, soʻzlamani ehtiyotkorlik bilan ishlatib, hech boʻlmaganda nimalarga oʻxshash boʻlganini hal qilish uchun harakat qildim.

en: Dividing my duties into three sections—my duties to myself, my duties to my neighbour, and my duties to God—I started to indite a list of the first of those sections, but they seemed to me so numerous, and therefore requiring to be divided into so many species and subdivisions, that I thought I had better first of all write down the heading of “Rules of My Life” before proceeding to their detailed inscription.
uz: O'z vazifamni uchta bo'limga bo'lishim uchun - o'zimga bo'lgan vazifamni, o'zgalarga bo'lgan vazifamni va Xudoga bo'lgan vazifamni o'z ichiga olgan bo'limlarning birinchisining ro'yxatini tuzishni boshladim, lekin ular menga shunchalik ko'p bo'lib, shuning uchun ko'p turlarga va bo'linmalarga bo'linishni talab qilgan bo'lib ko'rindi, shuning uchun ular haqida batafsil yozishdan oldin, avvalo, Rules of My Lifening boshliqini yozib olish yaxshiroq bo'lishini o'ylardim.

en: Accordingly, I proceeded to write “Rules of My Life” on the outside of the six sheets of paper which I had made into a sort of folio, but the words came out in such a crooked and uneven scrawl that for long I sat debating the question, “Shall I write them again?”—for long, sat in agonised contemplation of the ragged handwriting and disfigured title-page.
uz: Shuning uchun men o'sha olti varaqaning tashqarisiga "O'z hayotimning qoidalari" ni yozishga kirdim, lekin so'zlar shunday bo'g'ish va tengsiz bo'lib chiqdiki, men uzoq vaqt davomida savolni muhokama qilib o'tirdim: "Ularni yana yozishim kerakmi?"

en: Why was it that all the beauty and clarity which my soul then contained came out so misshapenly on paper (as in life itself) just when I was wishing to apply those qualities to what I was thinking at the moment?
uz: Nima uchun o'shanda o'z ruhimdagi barcha go'zallik va aniqlik qog'ozda (hayotda bo'lgani kabi) noto'g'ri tarzda paydo bo'ldi, ayni paytda men o'sha fazilatlarni o'zim o'ylayotgan narsaga qo'llashni xohlardim?

en: “The priest is here, so please come downstairs and hear his directions,” said Nicola as he entered.
uz: Pastor bu yerda, shuning uchun pastga tushib, uning yo'l-yo'riqlarini tinglang, - dedi Nikolay kirganida.

en: Hurriedly concealing my folio under the table-cloth, I looked at myself in the mirror, combed my hair upwards (I imagined this to give me a pensive air), and descended to the divannaia, [Room with divans, or ante-room] where the table stood covered with a cloth and had an ikon and candles placed upon it.
uz: Tez-tez foliyumni stol to'pasiga yashirib, o'zimni ko'zguga ko'rdim, sochimni yuqoriga pishirib (man buni o'ylayman) va divannaiaga tushdim, u erda stol to'pka bilan qoplangan edi va ustiga nishoncha va shamollar qo'yilgan edi.

en: Papa entered just as I did, but by another door: whereupon the priest—a grey-headed old monk with a severe, elderly face—blessed him, and Papa kissed his small, squat, wizened hand.
uz: Otam men kabi, lekin boshqa eshikdan kirdi: shu paytdan boshlab ruhoniy, qattiq, keksa yuzli oqsoqol uni duo qildi, otam esa uning kichkinagina, ko'kraklangan, chiroyli qo'lini o'pdi.

en: “Go and call Woldemar,” said Papa.
uz: Go and call Woldemar, dedi Papa.

en: Wait a minute, though.
uz: Lekin bir daqiqa turing.

en: Perhaps he is preparing for the Communion at the University?” “No, he is with the Prince,” said Katenka, and glanced at Lubotshka.
uz: Ehtimol, u universitetda Xushxabarni qabul qilishga tayyorgarlik ko'radi?Yo'q, u Prince bilan birga, dedi Katenka va Lubotshkaga nazar tashladi.

en: Suddenly the latter blushed for some reason or another, and then frowned.
uz: Toʻsatdan bu kishi shu yoki shu sababdan qizgʻaladi va soʻngra burun koʻrdi.

en: Finally, pretending that she was not well, she left the room, and I followed her.
uz: Nihoyat, u bemor bo'lib qolganini ko'rsatib, xonadan chiqib ketdi va men unga ergashdim.

en: In the drawing-room she halted, and began to pencil something fresh on her paper of peccadilloes.
uz: O'tirish xonasida u to'xtadi va gunohkorlar qog'ozida yangi bir narsani qalamga olishni boshladi.

en: “Well, what new sin have you gone and committed?” I asked.
uz: Xo'sh, qanday yangi gunoh qilib qo'ydingiz? - deb so'radim.

en: “Nothing,” she replied with another blush.
uz: - Hech narsa emas, - deb javob berdi u yana bir qizil ko'rinish bilan.

en: All at once we heard Dimitri’s voice raised in the hall as he took his leave of Woloda.
uz: Dimitriy Wolodan ketayotganida, biz birdan zalda baland ovoz bilan gapirganini eshitdik.

en: “It seems to me you are always experiencing some new temptation,” said Katenka, who had entered the room behind us, and now stood looking at Lubotshka.
uz: "Menga o'xshaydiki, siz har doim yangi vasvasaga duchor bo'lasiz", - dedi Katenka, u ortimizdan xonada kirib, endi Lubotshkaga qarab turardi.

en: What was the matter with my sister I could not conceive, but she was now so agitated that the tears were starting from her eyes.
uz: Qizim bilan nima bo'lganini tasavvur ham qilolmadim, lekin u endi shunchalik g'ayratli ediki, ko'zlaridan yoshlar tushib qoldi.

en: Finally her confusion grew uncontrollable, and vented itself in rage against both herself and Katenka, who appeared to be teasing her.
uz: Oxir-oqibat uning g'alati o'sib bordi va u o'ziga ham, Katenkaga ham g'azablanib, o'zini qo'zg'atgan ko'rinardi.

en: “Any one can see that you are a FOREIGNER!” she cried (nothing offended Katenka so much as to be called by that term, which is why Lubotshka used it).
uz: Siz chet ellik ekanligingizni har kim ko'rishi mumkin! - deb yig'ladi u (katenka bu so'z bilan atalishi uchun hech narsa uni ranjitmagan, shuning uchun Lubotshka uni ishlatgan).

en: “Just because I have the secret of which you know,” she went on, with anger ringing through her tone, “you
uz: Siz bilgan sirim borligi uchun u g'azabga to'lib-toshgan ton bilan davom etdi: you

en: purposely go and upset me!
uz: Niyat bilan borib, meni xafa qiling!

en: Please do understand that it is no joking matter.” “Do you know what she has gone and written on her paper, Nicolinka?” cried Katenka, much infuriated by the term “foreigner.” “She has written down that—” “Oh, I never could have believed that you could be so cruel!” exclaimed Lubotshka, now bursting into open sobbing as she moved away from us.
uz: Iltimos, bu hazil emasligini tushuning.Nikolinka, u nimalar yozganini bilasizmi? dedi Katenka, bu so'zdan juda g'azablandi.Xorijiy.U buni yozib qo'ydiOh, men sizning bunday shafqatsiz bo'lishingizga hech qachon ishonolmasdim! deb hayqirdi Lubotshka, endi bizdan uzoqlashganda ochiq yig'lab yubordi.

en: “You chose that moment on purpose!
uz: Siz o'sha vaqtni qasddan tanlagansiz!

en: You spend your whole time in trying to make me sin!
uz: Siz butun vaqtingizni meni gunoh qilishga undashga sarflaysiz!

en: I’ll never go to YOU again for sympathy and advice!” VI.
uz: Men yana hech qachon Senga hamdardlik va maslahat so'rab murojaat qilmayman! VI.

en: CONFESSION With these and other disjointed impressions in my mind, I returned to the divannaia.
uz: Tanbehda bu va boshqa bo'sh taassurotlar paydo bo'lganidan so'ng, men divannaiyaga qaytdim.

en: As soon as every one had reassembled, the priest rose and prepared to read the prayer before confession.
uz: Hamma yig'ilganidan so'ng, ruhoniy o'rnidan turib, tanbehdan oldin ibodatni o'qishga tayyorlandi.

en: The instant that the silence was broken by the stern, expressive voice of the monk as he recited the prayer—and more especially when he addressed to us the words: “Reveal thou all thy sins without shame, concealment, or extenuation, and let thy soul be cleansed before God: for if thou concealest aught, then great will be thy sin”—the same sensation of reverent awe came over me as I had felt during the morning.
uz: O'sha payt xudojo'y mo'minning qattiq va ifodalangan ovozi xotirjamlikni buzdi va ayniqsa, u bizga quyidagi so'zlarni aytganida: "O'z gunohlaringni utanmasdan, yashirinmasdan yoki kamaytirmasdan oshkor et, Xudo oldida joning pok bo'lsin, chunki agar biron narsani yashirsang, gunohing katta bo'ladi.

en: I even took a certain pleasure in recognising this condition of mine, and strove to preserve it, not only by restraining all other thoughts from entering my brain, but also by consciously exerting myself to feel no other sensation than this same one of reverence.
uz: Hatto mening bu holatimni tan olishdan zavqlanib, uni saqlab qolishga harakat qildim, nafaqat boshqa fikrlarni miyamga kirishiga to'sqinlik qilib, balki o'zimni faqat shu hurmat hissi bilan his qilish uchun o'zimni ko'p harakat qildim.

en: Papa was the first to go to confession.
uz: Ota birinchi bo'lib tanbehga borgan.

en: He remained a long, long time in the room which had belonged to our grandmother, and during that time the rest of us kept silence in the divannaia, or only
uz: U ko'p, ko'p vaqt bobomizning xonasi bo'lgan xonada qoldi va o'sha vaqt davomida qolganlarimiz divannaia da sukut saqladik.

en: whispered to one another on the subject of who should precede whom.
uz: Ular kim kimdan oldingi bo'lishi kerakligi haqida bir-biriga shoshib o'tirdilar.

en: At length, the voice of the priest again reading the prayer sounded from the doorway, and then Papa’s footsteps.
uz: Oxir oqibat, ibodatni yana o'qiyotgan ruhoniyning ovozi eshikdan eshitildi, so'ngra Papa qadamlar qo'ydi.

en: The door creaked as he came out, coughing and holding one shoulder higher than the other, in his usual way, and for the moment he did not look at any of us.
uz: U tashqariga chiqganda eshik qichqirib ketdi, bir shohni boshqa shoxdan yuqori ushlab, qo'llarini qo'yib, odatdagidek qo'yib turardi va bir zumgacha hech kimga nazar solmadi.

en: “YOU go now, Luba,” he said presently, as he gave her cheek a mischievous pinch.
uz: "SING endi ketasan, Luba", - deb aytdi u ayolning shavalasiga yomonlik bilan urib.

en: “Mind you tell him everything.
uz: Mind siz unga hamma narsani ayting.

en: You are my greatest sinner, you know.” Lubotshka went red and pale by turns, took her memorandum paper out of her apron, replaced it, and finally moved away towards the doorway with her head sunk between her shoulders as though she expected to receive a blow upon it from above.
uz: Sen mening eng katta gunohkorimsan, bilasiz. Lubotshka o'z navbatida qizil va oq bo'ldi, o'zining xat qog'ozini o'z shkafidan olib tashladi, o'rniga almashtirdi va nihoyat, boshini yelkalar o'rtasida cho'ktirib, eshikga qarab o'tdi, xuddi yuqoridan urishni kutgandek.

en: She was not long gone, and when she returned her shoulders were shaking with sobs.
uz: U uzoq vaqt o'tib ketmagan edi va qaytib kelganida uning yelkalari yig'lab-ichib qolibdi.

en: At length—next after the excellent Katenka (who came out of the doorway with a smile on her face)—my turn arrived.
uz: Keyinchalik, mukammal Katenka (o'zi yuzida tabassum bilan eshikdan chiqqan) mening navbatim keldi.

en: I entered the dimly-lighted room with the same vague feeling of awe, the same conscious eagerness to arouse that feeling more and more in my soul, that had possessed me up to the present moment.
uz: Men kam yorug'langan xonaga xuddi shu noaniq hayratlanish hissi bilan kirdim, o'zimni hozirgacha saqlab qolgan ruhimdagi o'sha tuyg'ularni yanada kuchaytirishga harakat qildim.

en: The priest, standing in front of a reading-desk, slowly turned his face to me.
uz: Ruhoniy o'qish stoli oldida turib, asta-sekin yuzimni menga qaratdi.

en: I was not more than five minutes in the room, but came out from it happy and (so I persuaded myself) entirely cleansed—a new, a morally reborn individual.
uz: Xonada besh daqiqadan ko'proq bo'lmagan edim, lekin undan xursand chiqib, (shunday qilib o'zimni ishontirdim) yangi, axloqiy jihatdan qayta tug'ilgan shaxsni butunlay tozaladim.

en: Despite the fact that the old surroundings of my life now struck me as unfamiliar (even though the rooms, the furniture, and my own figure—would to heavens that I could have changed my outer man for the better in the same way that I believed myself to have changed my inner I—were the same as before), I remained in that comfortable attitude of mine until the very moment of bedtime.
uz: Garchi hayotimning eski muhitlari hozir menga noma'lum tuyulsa-da (og'ir xonalar, mebellar va o'zimning shaxsiyatim o'zgargan bo'lsa-da, tashqi odamimni o'zgartirganim kabi, ichki odamimni ham o'zgartirganim kabi yaxshilikka o'zgartirgan bo'lsam-da), men o'zimni o'zgartirganim kabi o'zgartirganman, lekin uxlash paytimgacha o'zimning qulay nuqtai nazarimda qoldim.

en: Yet, no sooner had I begun to grow drowsy with the conning over of my sins than in a flash I recollected a particularly shameful sin which I had suppressed at confession time.
uz: Biroq, gunohlarimning aldanib ketishi bilan uyquga toʻlib ketgandim, bir lahzada men tanqid paytida yoʻqotgan oʻta sharmanda gunohimni esladim.

en: Instantly the words of the prayer before confession came back to my memory and began sounding in my ears.
uz: O'sha zahoti, tanbehdan oldin qilingan ibodat so'zlari xotiraga qaytib keldi va quloqlarimda tovush boshladi.

en: My peace was gone for ever.
uz: Mening tinchligim abadiy yo'q edi.

en: “For if thou concealest aught, then great will be thy sin.” Each time that the phrase recurred to me I saw myself a sinner for whom no punishment was adequate.
uz: Agar biror narsani yashirsang, gunohing katta bo'ladi. Bu so'z menga qaytadan kelganida, o'zimni hech qanday jazoga loyiq bo'lmagan gunohkor sifatida ko'rdim.

en: Long did I toss from side to side as I
uz: Uzoq vaqt davomida men o'zimni qo'lga olganimda, bir tomondan boshqa tomonga tashladimmi?

en: considered my position, while expecting every moment to be visited with the divine wrath—to be struck with sudden death, perhaps!—an insupportable thought!
uz: O'zimning mavqeyimni inobatga olgan holda, har bir daqiqani Xudoning g'azabiga duchor bo'lish, ehtimol, to'satdan o'limga duchor bo'lishni kutyapman!

en: Then suddenly the reassuring thought occurred to me: “Why should I not drive out to the monastery when the morning comes, and see the priest again, and make a second confession?” Thereafter I grew calmer.
uz: Oʻshanda birdan tasalli beruvchi fikr keldi: Nega ertalab monastirga borib, ruhoniy bilan yana uchrashsam va ikkinchi marta tanbeh bersam boʻlmasin? Shundan soʻng men tinchroq boʻldim.

en: THE EXPEDITION TO THE MONASTERY Several times that night I woke in terror at the thought that I might be oversleeping myself, and by six o’clock was out of bed, although the dawn was hardly peeping in at the window.
uz: O'sha kecha bir necha marta qo'rquvdan uyg'onib, o'zim ham o'zimni uyqudan tashqariga chiqardim deb o'yladim va soat oltigacha uxlamagan edim, garchi tong chindan ham oynada ko'rinmayotgan bo'lsa ham.

en: I put on my clothes and boots (all of which were lying tumbled and unbrushed beside the bed, since Nicola, of course had not been in yet to tidy them up), and, without a prayer said or my face washed, emerged, for the first time in my life, into the street ALONE.
uz: Kiyim-kechak va poyabzallarimni kiydirib (barchasi yotoq yonida to'planib, pishirilmagan edi, chunki Nikola, albatta, ularni tozalash uchun hali kelmagan edi) va ibodat qilmasdan yoki yuzimni yuvmasdan, hayotimda birinchi marta UChUN ko'chaga chiqdim.

en: Over the way, behind the green roof of a large building, the dim, cold dawn was beginning to blush red.
uz: Yo'lda, katta binoning yashil tomining orqasida, soyuq, sochiq tong qizil rangga aylanishni boshlagan.

en: The keen frost of the spring morning which had stiffened the pools and mud and made them crackle under my feet now nipped my face and hands also.
uz: Bahorning ertalabki sovuqligi hovuzlar va loylarni qattiqlashtirib, oyoqlarim ostida qirib tashlagan edi, endi yuzimni ham, qo'llarimni ham o'chirib yubordi.

en: Not a cab was to be seen, though I had counted upon one to make the journey out and home the quicker.
uz: O'zimni tezroq safarga olib, uyga qaytish uchun taksiga ega bo'lishim mumkin emas edi.

en: Only a file of waggons was rumbling along the Arbat Prospect, and a couple of bricklayers talking noisily together as they strode along the pavement.
uz: Arbat prospekti bo'ylab faqatgina vagonlar to'plami to'plandi va bir nechta toshbo'ylar piyoda yurib, bir-birlari bilan shovqinli suhbatlashdilar.

en: However, after walking a verst or so I began to meet men and women taking baskets to market or going with empty barrels to fetch the day’s water supply; until at length, at the cross streets near the Arbat Gate, where a pieman had set up his stall and a baker was just opening his
uz: Biroq, bir oz yurganimdan so'ng men bozorga koska olib kelayotgan yoki kunlik suv ta'minoti uchun bo'sh barrellar bilan ketayotgan erkaklar va ayollar bilan uchrashishni boshladim; oxir-oqibat, Arbat darvozasi yaqinidagi ko'chalar kesishganida, bu yerda bir pieman o'z stallini o'rnatgan va bir keker o'z stallini ochgan edi.

en: shop, I espied an old cabman shaking himself after indulging in a nap on the box of his be-scratched old blue-painted, hobble-de-hoy wreck of a drozhki.
uz: Men bir keksa taksi haydovchisining o'zini titrayotganini ko'rdim, chunki u o'zining ko'k, ko'k bo'yilgan, hozirgi zamondagi drozhki vayron bo'lgan eski do'konining quti ustiga cho'kkan edi.

en: He seemed barely awake as he asked twenty copecks as the fare to the monastery and back, but came to himself a moment afterwards, just as I was about to get in, and, touching up his horse with the spare end of the reins, started to drive off and leave me.
uz: U monastirga va qaytib borish uchun yigirma kopekni so'rab, o'zini o'zi o'ylab topdi, lekin men kirmoqchi bo'lganimdan bir zum o'tgach, otasiga qo'l tegizdi va o'z qo'llarini qo'yib, meni tashlab ketishni boshladi.

en: “My horse wants feeding,” he growled, “I can’t take you, barin.[Sir]” With some difficulty and a promise of FORTY copecks I persuaded him to stop.
uz: Atim oziqlanishni xohlaydi,  u qichqiradi,  Men sizni olib ketolmayman, ketaman.  Biroz qiyinchilik va FORTY copecks va'dasi bilan men uni to'xtatishga ishontirdim.

en: He eyed me narrowly as he pulled up, but nevertheless said: “Very well.
uz: O'tirganida u menga chiroyli qarab turdi, lekin hali ham shunday dedi: Chiroyli.

en: Get in, barin.” I must confess that I had some qualms lest he should drive me to a quiet corner somewhere, and then rob me, but I caught hold of the collar of his ragged driving-coat, close to where his wrinkled neck showed sadly lean above his hunched-up back, and climbed on to the blue-painted, curved, rickety scat.
uz: Kiring, keting. Men tan olsam kerakki, u meni qaysidir joyda xotirjam bo'lgan burchakga olib ketib, so'ngra meni talon-toroj qilishidan qo'rqardim, lekin men uning charchagan haydovchilik kiyimining bo'yinini tutdim, uning burqlangan bo'yni o'ziga o'xshaydigan orqaga yaqinlashib, ko'k bo'yilgan, egri, bo'g'aygan ko'rinishga tushib, ko'k bo'yilgan cho'g'iga chiqdim.

en: As we set off along Vozdvizhenka Street, I noticed that the back of the drozhki was covered with a strip of the same greenish material as that of which his coat was made.
uz: Vozdvizhenka ko'chasi bo'ylab yo'lga chiqqanimizda, drozhkining orqasida uning kiyimidan yasalgan xuddi shunday yashil materialdan yasalgan bo'lak borligini payqadim.

en: For some reason or another this reassured me, and I no longer felt nervous of being taken to a quiet spot and robbed.
uz: Bu meni qandaydir sabablarga ko'ra tasalli berardi va meni tinch joyga olib ketib, talon-toroj qilishdan qo'rqmas edi.

en: The sun had risen to a good height, and was gilding the cupolas of the churches, when we arrived at the monastery.
uz: Biz monastirga yetib kelganimizda, quyosh yaxshi balandlikka chiqdi va cherkovlarning kupolalarini oltinlashdi.

en: In the shade the frost had not yet given, but in the open roadway muddy rivulets of water were coursing along, and it was through fast-thawing mire that the horse went clip-clopping his way.
uz: Soyadda sovuq hali paydo bo'lmagan, lekin ochiq yo'l yo'llarda qora suv daryolari oqib o'tgan edi va ot tezda o'tadigan qora balchiqdan o'tadi.

en: Alighting, and entering the monastery grounds, I inquired of the first monk whom I met where I could find the priest whom I was seeking.
uz: Chiqib, monastir maydoniga kirganimda, uchratgan birinchi rafiqamdan qidirayotgan ruhoniyni qayerdan topishimni so'radim.

en: “His cell is over there,” replied the monk as he stopped a moment and pointed towards a little building up to which a flight of steps led.
uz: "O'zining hujayralari shu yerda", - deb javob berdi rafiq, bir zum to'xtatib, qadamlar to'g'risida o'ylaydigan kichik binoga ishora qildi.

en: “I respectfully thank you,” I said, and then fell to wondering what all the monks (who at that moment began to come filing out of the church) must be thinking of me as they glanced in my direction.
uz: Men hurmat bilan sizga rahmat aytdim, so'ngra barcha rafiqani (ular o'sha paytda cherkovdan to'qnashishni boshlashdi) so'rab, menga qarab nima haqida o'ylayotganini o'ylab ko'rdim.

en: I was neither a grown-up nor a child, while my face was unwashed, my hair unbrushed, my clothes tumbled, and my boots unblacked and muddy.
uz: Men katta ham, bola ham bo'lmaganman, yuzim yuvilmagan, sochlarim silmagan, kiyim-kechakim tushib ketgan va poyabzallarim qora va loysiz edi.

en: To what class of persons were the brethren assigning me—for they stared at me hard enough?
uz: Birodaru opa-singillar meni qaysi guruhga tayinlashdi, chunki ular menga juda ko'z tikishgan?

en: Nevertheless I proceeded in the direction which the young priest had pointed out to me.
uz: Shunga qaramay, yosh ruhoniy menga ko'rsatgan yo'nalishda davom ettirdim.

en: An old man with bushy grey eyebrows and a black cassock met me on the narrow path to the cells, and asked me what I wanted.
uz: O'simlikdagi qaroq ko'z burchaklari va qora so'qmoqli bir keksa kishi hujayralarga yetib boradigan tor yo'lda mendan uchrashdi va nima istayotganimni so'radi.

en: For a brief moment I felt inclined to say “Nothing,” and then run back to the drozhki and drive away home; but, for all its beetling brows, the face of the old man inspired confidence, and I merely said that I wished to see the priest (whom I named).
uz: Qisqa bir daqiqa davomida men hech narsa demayman, so'ngra droshkiga qaytib ketaman va uyga ketaman; lekin uning ko'krakli ko'z burchaklariga qaramay, keksa odamning yuzi ishonchni uyg'otdi va men faqat ruhoniyni ko'rishni xohlaganimni aytdim (men unga ism qo'ydim).

en: “Very well, young sir; I will take you to him,” said the old man as he turned round.
uz: "To'g'ri, yigit, men sizni uning oldiga olib boraman", - dedi keksa kishi o'girilib.

en: Clearly he had guessed my errand at a stroke.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, u o'zimning vazifamni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tasavvur qilgan.

en: “The father is at matins at this moment, but he will soon be back,” and, opening a door, the old man led me through a neat hall and corridor, all lined with clean matting, to a cell.
uz: Ota hozir ertalabda, lekin tez orada qaytib keladi, va eshikni ochib, keksa kishi meni toza chodir va chodir orqali bir qamoqqa olib keldi, ularning barchasi toza matdan qoplangan edi.

en: “Please to wait here,” he added, and then, with a kind, reassuring glance, departed.
uz: Xullas, bu yerda kutib turinglar", - deb qo'shimcha qildi u, so'ngra mehribon, tasalli beruvchi ko'z bilan ketib ketdi.

en: The little room in which I found myself was of the smallest possible dimensions, but extremely neat and clean.
uz: O'zimni topgan kichkina xonani eng kichik o'lchamlar bilan ta'minlash mumkin edi, ammo u juda yaxshi va toza edi.

en: Its furniture only consisted of a small table (covered with a cloth, and placed between two equally small casement-windows, in which stood two pots of geraniums), a stand of ikons, with a lamp suspended in front of them, a bench, and two chairs.
uz: Uning mebellari faqat kichik bir stoldan iborat edi (to'qima bilan qoplangan va ikki teng kichik darcha o'rtasida joylashtirilgan, unda ikkita geranium quroli bor edi), ramzlardan iborat stand, ularning oldida chiroq, bank va ikkita o'rindiq o'rnatilgan edi.

en: In one corner hung a wall clock, with little flowers painted on its dial, and brass weights to its chains, while upon two nails driven into a screen (which, fastened to the ceiling with whitewashed pegs, probably concealed the bed) hung a couple of cassocks.
uz: Bir burchada devor soati o'rnatilgan edi, uning raqamida kichik gullar bo'yilgan edi va zanjirlarida mis og'irligi bor edi, ikkita to'g'irning ustiga esa ekranga o'rnatilgan (o'tga oqlangan to'g'rilar bilan yopilgan, ehtimol yotoqni yashirgan) bir nechta so'qmoqlar o'rnatilgan edi.

en: The windows looked out upon a whitewashed wall, about two arshins distant, and in the space between them there grew a small lilac-bush.
uz: Do'konlar o'zaro ikki o'rtadan uzoq bo'lgan oqlangan devorga qarab ko'rinardi va ularning orasidagi joyda kichkina bir lilac-boshi o'sdi.

en: Not a sound penetrated from without, and in the stillness the measured, friendly stroke of the clock’s pendulum seemed to beat quite loudly.
uz: Tashqi tomondan hech qanday tovush kirib kelmadi va tinchlikda soatning pendulumi o'lchanadigan, do'stona urishi juda baland ovoz bilan urib ketayotganga o'xshardi.

en: The instant that I found myself alone in this calm retreat all other thoughts and recollections left my head as completely as though they had never been there, and I subsided into an inexpressibly pleasing kind of torpor.
uz: O'zimni shu xotirjam joyda yolg'iz topgan paytning o'zida, boshqa barcha fikrlar va xotiralar boshimdan hech qachon o'sha yerda bo'lmagan kabi butunlay chiqib ketdi va men so'zsiz yoqimli bir turdagi torporga tushdim.

en: The rusty alpaca cassocks with their frayed linings, the worn black leather bindings of the books with their metal clasps, the dull-green plants with their carefully watered leaves and soil, and, above all, the abrupt, regular beat of the pendulum, all spoke to me intimately of some new life hitherto unknown to me—a life of unity and prayer, of calm, restful happiness.
uz: O'zlarining bo'g'im-bo'g'im bo'lib qolgan alpakka soyalari, o'zlarining metall qulflari bilan kitoblarning eskirgan qora charmli bog'lari, o'zlarining ehtiyotkorlik bilan sug'orilgan barglari va tuproqlari bilan chiroyli yashil o'simliklar va, eng asosiysi, pendulning keskin, muntazam urishi, bularning barchasi men uchun ilgari noma'lum bo'lgan yangi hayotdan, yakdillik va ibodat, xotirjamlik va xotirjamlik hayotidan menga yaqindan gapirdi.

en: “The months, the years, may pass,” I thought to myself, “but he remains alone—always at peace, always knowing that his conscience is pure before God, that his prayer will be heard by Him.” For fully half an hour I sat on that chair, trying not to move, not even to breathe loudly, for fear I should mar the harmony of the sounds which were telling me so much, and ever the pendulum continued to beat the same—now a little louder to the right, now a little softer to the left.
uz: Oylar, yillar o'tib ketishi mumkin,  O'zim o'zimga o'yladim,  lekin u yolg'iz qoladi Har doim tinchlikda, har doim vijdoni Xudo oldida sof ekanligini, ibodatlari U tomonidan eshitilishi mumkinligini biladi. Yarim soat davomida men o'sha kursida o'tirdim, harakat qilmaslikka harakat qildim, hatto baland ovoz bilan nafas olmaslikka ham harakat qildim, chunki bu menga juda ko'p narsani aytadigan tovushlarning harmoniyasini buzishdan qo'rqardim, va har doim pendulum o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o

en: THE SECOND CONFESSION Suddenly the sound of the priest’s footsteps roused me from this reverie.
uz: Ikkinchi tanbeh: Birdan ruhoniy qadamlarining ovozi meni bu o'yindan uyg'otib qo'ydi.

en: “Good morning to you,” he said as he smoothed his grey hair with his hand.
uz: "Sizga salom", - dedi u qo'li bilan o'zining oq sochlarini sozlab.

en: “What can I do for you?” I besought him to give me his blessing, and then kissed his small, wizened hand with great fervour.
uz: Men siz uchun nima qilishim mumkin? Men undan duo qilib, menga duo qilishini so'radim va keyin uning kichkina, chiroyli qo'lini katta g'ayrat bilan o'pdim.

en: After I had explained to him my errand he said nothing, but moved away towards the ikons, and began to read the exhortation: whereupon I overcame my shame, and told him all that was in my heart.
uz: Men unga topshirigʻimni tushuntirganimdan soʻng u hech narsa aytmadi, balki ikonalarga qarab ketdi va nasihatni oʻqishni boshladi: shundan soʻng men oʻzimning sharmandaligimni yengdim va qalbimdagi hamma narsani Unga aytdim.

en: Finally he laid his hands upon my head, and pronounced in his even, resonant voice the words: “My son, may the blessing of Our Heavenly Father be upon thee, and may He always preserve thee in faithfulness, loving-kindness, and meekness.
uz: Nihoyat, u qo'llarini boshimga qo'ydi va kechqurun o'z ovozida shunday so'zlarni aytdi: "O'g'lim, samoviy Otamizning barakasi sening ustingda bo'lsin va U seni doimo sodiqlik, mehribonlik va muloyimlik bilan saqlab qolsin.

en: Amen.” I was entirely happy.
uz: Amin. Men mutlaqo baxtli edim.

en: Tears of joy coursed down my face as I kissed the hem of his cassock and then raised my head again.
uz: Men uning so'nggi so'zini o'qib, boshimni yana ko'targanimda, yuzimda quvonchning yoshlari oqib ketdi.

en: The face of the priest expressed perfect tranquillity.
uz: Ruhoniyning yuzi mukammal xotirjamlikni ifodalaydi.

en: So keenly did I feel the joy of reconciliation that, fearing in any way to dispel it, I took hasty leave of him, and, without looking to one side of me or the other (in order that my attention might not be distracted), left the grounds and re-entered the rickety, battered drozhki.
uz: Men o'zimni bir tomondan yoki boshqa tomonga ko'rmasdan (ehtiyotimni chalg'itmaslik uchun) u yerdan chiqib, qayg'urgan, urilgan drozhkiga qaytdim.

en: Yet the joltings of the vehicle and the variety of objects which flitted past my eyes soon dissipated that feeling, and I became filled with nothing but the idea that the priest must have thought me the finest-spirited young man he had ever met, or ever would meet, in the whole of his life.
uz: Ammo mashinaning shovqinlari va ko'zlarimdan o'tib o'tgan turli xil narsalar tez orada o'sha his-tuyg'ularni yo'q qildi va ruhoniy meni hayotida uchratgan yoki uchratadigan eng yaxshi ruhli yigit deb o'ylashi kerakligi haqidagi fikrdan boshqa hech narsa bilan to'ldim.

en: Indeed, I reflected, there could not be many such as myself—of that I felt sure, and the conviction produced in me the kind of complacency which craves for self-communication to another.
uz: Darhaqiqat, o'zim kabi ko'p odamlar bo'lmasligi haqida o'yladim, o'zimni shubhasiz his qilganman va bu ishonch menga o'zimni boshqalarga aytishni istagan o'zimni o'zim bilishga qodir bo'lishga yordam beradigan o'zimni o'zim o'zim bilishimga o'xshaydigan o'zimni o'zim o'zim bilishimga o'xshatdi.

en: I had a great desire
uz: Men katta istakga ega edim

en: to unbosom myself to some one, and as there was no one else to speak to, I addressed myself to the cabman.
uz: O'zimni kimgadir ochib berishga harakat qildim va boshqa hech kim bilan gaplashish uchun yo'q bo'lganim uchun, taksi haydovchisiga murojaat qildim.

en: “Was I very long gone?” I asked him.
uz: Men uzoq vaqtdan beri yo'q edimmi? Men undan so'radim.

en: “No, not very long,” he replied.
uz: "Yo'q, uzoq vaqt emas", deb javob berdi u.

en: He seemed to have grown more cheerful under the influence of the sunshine.
uz: U quyosh nurining ta'siri ostida ko'proq quvonchga to'lgan ko'rinardi.

en: “Yet now it is a good while past my horse’s feeding-time.
uz: Ammo endi otning ovqatlanish vaqti o'tib yaxshi vaqt o'tdi.

en: You see, I am a night cabman.” “Well, I only seemed to myself to be about a minute,” I went on.
uz: Mana, men kechasi taksi haydovchisi bo'lganman.  Xo'sh, men o'zimga faqat bir daqiqacha o'zimni ko'rsatib o'tdim, davom etdim.

en: “Do you know what I went there for?” I added, changing my seat to the well of the drozhki, so as to be nearer the driver.
uz: Men nima uchun u yerga borganimni bilasizmi? Men o'zimni haydovchisiga yaqinroq bo'lish uchun o'rinni drozhki quduqidan o'zgartirgan holda qo'shdim.

en: “What business is it of mine?
uz: Bu mening qanday ishim?

en: I drive a fare where he tells me to go,” he replied.
uz: Men o'zimga buyurgan joyga sayohat qilaman, - deb javob berdi u.

en: “Yes, but, all the same, what do you think I went there for?” I persisted.
uz: Ha, lekin nima uchun u yerga borganimni o'ylaysiz? Men qat'iy qaror qildim.

en: “I expect some one you know is going to be buried there, so you went to see about a plot for the grave.” “No, no, my friend.
uz: Men bilgan odamlarning birortasining u yerda ko'milganini kutaman, shuning uchun qabr uchun tuzatish haqida ko'rish uchun borgansiz.Yo'q, yo'q, do'stim.

en: Still, DO you know what I went there for?” “No, of course I cannot tell, barin,” he repeated.
uz: Ammo nima uchun borganimni bilasizmi?Yo'q, albatta men buni aytolmayman, ketaman, - dedi u takrorlab.

en: His voice seemed to me so kind that I decided to edify him by relating the cause of my expedition, and even telling him of the feeling which I had experienced.
uz: Uning ovozi menga shunchalik mehribon ko'rinardiki, men uni safarim sababini aytib, hatto o'zim boshdan kechirgan his-tuyg'ularni aytib, unga dalda berishga qaror qildim.

en: “Shall I tell you?” I said.
uz: Sizga aytishim kerakmi? - dedim men.

en: “Well, you see,”—and I told him all, as well as inflicted upon him a description of my fine sentiments.
uz: Bilasizmi, men unga hamma narsani aytib berdim va unga o'zimning yaxshi his-tuyg'ularimni tushuntirib berdim.

en: To this day I blush at the recollection.
uz: Bu kungacha men eslatma bilan qizg'inaman.

en: “Well, well!” said the cabman non-committally, and for a long while afterwards he remained silent and motionless, except that at intervals he adjusted the skirt of his coat each time that it was jerked from beneath his leg by the joltings of his huge boot on the drozhki’s step.
uz: Ha, ha! deb so'radi haydovchi, va undan keyin uzoq vaqt davomida u jim va harakatsiz qoldi, faqat, u drozhki daraxtidagi ulkan botining shovqinlari tomonidan oyoq ostidan shovqin qilinganida, vaqti-vaqti bilan kiyimining pishrasini o'zgartirdi.

en: I felt sure that he must be thinking of me even as the priest had done.
uz: O'zimni o'ylagandimki, u o'zim haqida ruhoniy kabi o'ylayotgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: That is to say, that he must be thinking that no such fine- spirited young man existed in the world as I.
uz: Ya'ni, u o'zi o'ylayotgan bo'lishi kerakki, dunyoda men kabi aqlli yosh odam yo'q edi.

en: Suddenly he shot at me: “I tell you what, barin.
uz: Toʻsatdan menga oʻq urdi: Men sizga nima deyman, keting.

en: You ought to keep God’s affairs to yourself.” “What?” I said.
uz: Xudoning ishini o'zingiz uchun o'zingiz saqlang.  Nima? dedim men.

en: “Those affairs of yours—they are God’s business,” he repeated, mumbling the words with his toothless lips.
uz: "Sizning ishlaringiz Xudoning ishi", - deb ta'kidladi u, bu so'zlarni o'zlarining tishsiz og'izlari bilan g'ayratli qilib.

en: “No, he has not understood me,” I thought to myself, and said no more to him till we reached home.
uz: - Yo'q, u meni tushunmadi, - deb o'yladim men o'zimga, uyga kelguncha unga boshqa gapirmadim.

en: Although it was not my original sense of reconciliation and reverence, but only a sort of complacency at having experienced such a sense, that lasted in me during the drive home (and that, too, despite the distraction of the crowds of people who now thronged the sunlit streets in every direction), I had no sooner reached home than even my spurious complacency was shattered, for I found that I had not the forty copecks wherewith to pay the cabman!
uz: Garchi bu mening asl tuyg'ularim bo'lmagan bo'lsa-da, balki bunday tuyg'ularni boshdan kechirganimdan mamnun bo'lganim uchun o'zimni o'ylagandim (va shu bilan birga, quyoshli ko'chalarni har tomondan to'playdigan ko'pchilikning chalg'itishiga qaramay), uyga yetib kelganimda, hatto soxta tuyg'ularim ham vayron bo'ldi, chunki men kabinachiga to'lov to'lash uchun yetarlicha qirq to'lov pulim yo'qligini tushundim!

en: To the butler, Gabriel, I already owed a small debt, and he refused to lend me any more.
uz: Butler Gabrielga men allaqachon kichik qarzdor edim va u menga boshqa qarz berishni rad etdi.

en: Seeing me twice run across the courtyard in quest of the money, the cabman must have divined the reason, for, leaping from his drozhki, he—notwithstanding that he had seemed so kind— began to bawl aloud (with an evident desire to punch my head) that people who do not pay for their cab-rides are swindlers.
uz: Meni ikki marta hovlida pul izlab yurganimni ko'rib, taksi haydovchisi sababni aniqlab qo'ygan bo'lishi kerak, chunki o'zining drodzhkisidan sakrab o'tib, u juda mehribon ko'rinishiga qaramay, baland ovoz bilan (boshimni urish istagi bilan) qichqirib boshladi, shuning uchun taksilar uchun pul to'lamaydigan odamlar o'zlarining qichqiriqlari uchun talonchilardir.

en: None of my family were yet out of bed, so that, except for the servants, there was no one from whom to borrow the forty copecks.
uz: Oilamning hech bir a'zosi hali uxlamagan edi, shuning uchun xizmatkorlardan tashqari, qirq kopekni qarz olish uchun hech kim yo'q edi.

en: At length, on my most sacred, sacred word of honour to repay (a word to which, as I could see from his face, he did not altogether trust), Basil so far yielded to his fondness for me and his remembrance of the many services I had done him as to pay the cabman.
uz: Oxir oqibat, men o'zimning eng muqaddas, eng muqaddas so'zimni qaytarishim kerak edi (bu so'z uning yuzidan ko'rinib turganidek, u bunga umuman ishonmagan), Basil hozirgacha menga bo'lgan mehr-shafqatini va men unga xizmat qilgan ko'plab xizmatlarni eslab, taksi haydovchisini to'lash uchun qilgan xizmatimni tan oldi.

en: Thus all my beautiful feelings ended in smoke.
uz: Shunday qilib, barcha go'zal his-tuyg'ularim tutun bilan yakunlandi.

en: When I went upstairs to dress for church and go to Communion with the rest I found that my new clothes had not yet come home, and so I could not wear them.
uz: Men cherkovga kiyinib, qolganlar bilan birga Xushxabarga borganimda, yangi kiyimlarim hali uyga kelmaganini tushundim, shuning uchun ularni kiyish mumkin emas edi.

en: Then I sinned headlong.
uz: So'ngra boshimdan gunoh qildim.

en: Donning my other suit, I went to Communion in a sad state of mental perturbation, and filled with complete distrust of all my finer impulses.
uz: Boshqa kiyimimni kiyganimda, men ruhiy tashvishlar tufayli qayg'uli holatda va barcha yaxshi impulslarimga to'liq ishonchsizlik bilan to'lib-toshgan holda Xudojo'ylikka bordim.

en: HOW I PREPARED MYSELF FOR THE EXAMINATIONS
uz: Qanday qilib o'zimni imtihonlar uchun tayyorladim?

en: On the Thursday in Easter week Papa, my sister, Katenka, and Mimi went away into the country, and no one remained in my grandmother’s great house but Woloda, St.
uz: O'smirlar haftasidagi payshanba kuni dadam, singlim Katenka va Mimi qishloqga ketishdi va bu yerda Voloda shahridagi St. Petersburg shahridan tashqari, buvimning katta uyida hech kim qolmadi.
