en: The frame of mind which I had experienced on the day of my confession and during my subsequent expedition to the monastery had now completely passed away, and left behind it only a dim, though pleasing, memory which daily became more and more submerged by the impressions of this emancipated existence.
uz: Imondoshligim kuni va keyingi monastirga sayohatim davomida ko'rgan ruhim o'tib ketdi va o'z orqasidan faqat kam, garchi yoqimli, xotira qoldirdi, u har kuni bu ozod bo'lgan mavjudot taassurotlari bilan tobora ko'proq o'z ichiga oldi.

en: The folio endorsed “Rules of My Life” lay concealed beneath a pile of school-books.
uz: Folioda qo'llab-quvvatlangan "Mening hayotimning qoidalari" ko'pgina maktab kitoblari ostida yashiringan edi.

en: Although the idea of the possibility of framing rules, for every occasion in my life and always letting myself be guided by them still pleased me (since it appeared an idea at once simple and magnificent, and I was determined to make practical application of it), I seemed somehow to have forgotten to put it into practice at once, and kept deferring doing so until such and such a moment.
uz: Garchi hayotimdagi har bir fursat uchun qoidalar tuzish mumkinligi va har doim ularga yo'naltirilishimning g'oyasi meni hali ham yoqtirgan bo'lsa-da (chunki bu bir vaqtning o'zida oddiy va buyuk bir g'oya bo'lib ko'rinardi va men uni amaliy tarzda qo'llashga qat'iy qaror qildim), men uni bir vaqtning o'zida amalda qo'llashni unutib qo'ygan bo'lsam-da, bunday va shunday bir daqiqaga qadar buni kechiktirishni davom ettirgan bo'lardim.

en: At the same time, I took pleasure in the thought that every idea which now entered my head could be allotted precisely to one or other of my three sections of tasks and duties—those for or to God, those for or to my neighbour, and those for or to myself.
uz: Shu bilan birga, endi boshimga kirgan har bir g'oyani uchta vazifamning bir yoki bir qismiga - Xudoga yoki o'zimga, o'zgaga yoki o'zimga, o'zimga yoki o'zimga tegishli bo'lganlarga ajratish mumkinligi fikridan zavq oldim.

en: “I can always refer everything to them,” I said to myself, “as well as the many, many other ideas which occur to me on one subject or another.” Yet at this period I often asked myself, “Was I better and more truthful when I only believed in the power of the human intellect, or am I more so now, when I am losing the faculty of developing that power, and am in doubt both as to its potency and as to its importance?” To this I could return no positive answer.
uz: Men har doim hamma narsani ularga murojaat qilishim mumkin,  O'zimga aytdim,  shuningdek, menga bir yoki boshqa mavzuda kelib tushgan ko'plab, ko'plab boshqa g'oyalar. Ammo shu davrda men o'zimdan tez-tez: Men faqatgina inson aqli kuchiga ishonganimda yaxshiroq va rostgo'y bo'lganmanmi yoki hozirda, bu kuchni rivojlantirish qobiliyatini yo'qotayotganimda va uning kuch-quvvatidan ham, ahamiyatidan ham shubhalanayotganimda, ko'proq shundaymanmi? Bunga ijobiy javob qaytarolmayman.

en: The sense of freedom, combined with the spring-like feeling of vague expectation to which I have referred already, so unsettled me that I could not keep myself in hand—could make none but the sorriest of preparations for my University ordeal.
uz: Erkinlik hissi, men allaqachon eslatib o'tgan noaniq umidning bahor kabi hissi bilan birlashtirilganida, o'zimni nazorat qila olmasligim uchun meni shunchalik tashvishga soladiki, universitet sinovim uchun tayyorgarliklarning eng ayanchlilaridan biri bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: Thus I was busy in the schoolroom one morning, and fully aware that I must work hard, seeing that to-morrow was the day of my examination in a subject of which I had the two whole questions still to read up; yet no sooner had a breath of spring come wafted through the window than I felt as though there were something quite different that I wished to recall to my memory.
uz: Shunday qilib, men bir kuni ertalab maktabda mashg'ul edim va juda ko'p mehnat qilishim kerakligini yaxshi bilardim, chunki ertaga imtihonim bo'lgan edi va men hali ikkita savolni o'qib chiqishim kerak edi; ammo darhol dam olishdan oldin, darvoza orqali bahorning nafasini o'tkazganimdan so'ng, men o'zimni juda o'zgacha bir narsa borligini his qildim va xotiramga eslatishni xohladim.

en: My hands laid down my book, my feet began to move of themselves, and to set me walking up and down the room, and my
uz: Qo'llarim kitobimni ko'tarib qo'ydi, oyoqlarim o'z-o'zidan harakatlanishni boshladi va meni xonaga ko'tarib-ko'tarib yurishga majbur qildi.

en: head felt as though some one had suddenly touched in it a little spring and set some machine in motion—so easily and swiftly and naturally did all sorts of pleasing fancies of which I could catch no more than the radiancy begin coursing through it.
uz: O'zimni shunday his qildimki, kimdir to'satdan unga kichkina ko'chat qo'yib, mashinani juda oson va tez harakatga qo'ydi va tabiiy ravishda har qanday yoqimli xayollarni o'tkazdi.

en: Thus one hour, two hours, elapsed unperceived.
uz: Shunday qilib, bir soat, ikki soat ko'rinmay o'tdi.

en: Even if I sat down determinedly to my book, and managed to concentrate my whole attention upon what I was reading, suddenly there would sound in the corridor the footsteps of a woman and the rustle of her dress.
uz: Hatto men kitobimga qat'iy o'tirib, butun e'tiborimni o'qiganimga qaratishga muvaffaq bo'lsam ham, darhol koridorda bir ayolning qadamlari va uning kiyimining shov-shuvini eshitish mumkin edi.

en: Instantly everything would escape my mind, and I would find it impossible to remain still any longer, however much I knew that the woman could only be either Gasha or my grandmother’s old sewing-maid moving about in the corridor.
uz: O'shanda hamma narsa mening ongimdan chiqib ketardi va men hech qachon o'zimni to'xtatmaslikni o'ylamasdim, lekin bu ayol faqat Gasha yoki buvimning koridorda harakatlanayotgan keksa tikuvchisi bo'lishi mumkinligini bilardim.

en: “Yet suppose it should be SHE all at once?” I would say to myself.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, bir vaqtning o'zida U bo'lishi kerakmi? O'zimdan so'rayman.

en: “Suppose IT is beginning now, and I were to lose it?” and, darting out into the corridor, I would find, each time, that it was only Gasha.
uz: Aytingki, hozir u boshlanmoqda va men uni yo'qotishim kerak? Va koridorda o'tirib, har safar faqat Gashani topaman.

en: Yet for long enough afterwards I could not recall my attention to my studies.
uz: Biroq, keyinchalik o'qishga bo'lgan e'tiborimni uzoq vaqt eslay olmaganman.

en: A little spring had been touched in my head, and a strange mental ferment started afresh.
uz: Boshimda kichkina bir bahor qo'yilgan edi va g'alati ongli ferment yangi boshlandi.

en: Again, that evening I was sitting alone beside a tallow candle in my room.
uz: O'sha kechqurun men o'z xonamda yonilg'i chiroq yonida yolg'iz o'tirgan edim.

en: Suddenly I looked up for a moment—to snuff the candle, or to straighten myself in my chair—and at once became aware of nothing but the darkness in the corners and the blank of the open doorway.
uz: Toʻsatdan bir zumga koʻzimni koʻtarib, shamolni oʻchirish yoki oʻzimni oʻzimning oʻrinchimda toʻgʻrilash uchun koʻzimni koʻtardim va darhol burchaklardagi qorongʻulik va ochiq eshikning boʻshligidan boshqa hech narsa bilmadim.

en: Then, I also became conscious how still the house was, and felt as though I could do nothing else than go on listening to that stillness, and gazing into the black square of that open doorway, and gradually sinking into a brown study as I sat there without moving.
uz: Keyin men ham uyning qanchalik susayganligini anglab yetdim va o'zimni shu xotirjamlikni tinglab, ochiq eshikning qora kvadratini ko'rib, o'zimni harakatsiz o'tirganimda, asta-sekin ko'k rangli o'rindiqga tushib ketayotganimni his qildim.

en: At intervals, however, I would get up, and go downstairs, and begin wandering through the empty rooms.
uz: Biroq, vaqti-vaqti bilan turardim va pastga tushib, bo'sh xonadonlarni ko'zdan kechirardim.

en: Once I sat a long while in the small drawing-room as I listened to Gasha playing “The Nightingale” (with two fingers) on the piano in the large drawing-room, where a solitary candle burned.
uz: Bir marta men kichkinagina o'yin xonasida katta o'yin xonasidagi klaviaturda Gashani qo'shib o'ynashga quloq solganimda, katta o'yin xonasida yolg'iz shamol yonayotgan edi.

en: Later, when the moon was bright, I felt obliged to get out of bed and to lean out of the window, so that I might gaze into the garden, and at the lighted roof of the Shaposnikoff mansion, the straight tower of our parish church, and the dark shadows of the fence and the lilac-bush where they lay black upon the path.
uz: Keyinchalik, oy yorug' bo'lganida, bog'ga va Shaposnikoff saroyining yoritilgan tomini ko'rib chiqish uchun yotoqdan chiqishga va deraza orqali yonib turishga majbur bo'ldim, jamoat cherkovimizning to'g'ri minorasini ko'rdim va to'siqning qorong'i soyasini ko'rdim.

en: So long did I remain there that, when I at length returned to bed, it was ten o’clock in the morning before I could open my eyes again.
uz: U yerda shunchalik uzoq qoldimki, oxir-oqibat uxlashga qaytganimda, yana ko'zlarimni ochishga muvaffaq bo'lishimdan oldin ertalab soat o'n edi.

en: In short, had it not been for the tutors who came to give me lessons, as well as for St.
uz: Qisqasi, menga dars berishga kelgan o'qituvchilar, shuningdek, St.

en: Jerome (who at intervals, and very grudgingly, applied a spur to my self-conceit) and, most of all, for the desire to figure as “clever” in the eyes of my friend Nechludoff (who looked upon distinctions in University examinations as a matter of first-rate importance)—had it not been for all these things, I say, the spring and my new freedom would have combined to make me forget everything I had ever learnt, and so to go through the examinations to no purpose whatsoever.
uz: Jerom (va vaqti-vaqti bilan va juda xohlamagan holda o'zimni o'ylashga rag'batlantirgan) va eng asosiysi, do'stim Nechludoffning ko'z o'ngida "aqlli" bo'lish istagi tufayli (u oliy o'quv yurti imtihonlarida ajralib o'tishni birinchi darajali ahamiyatga ega deb hisoblagan) agar bularning barchasi bo'lmaganida, men aytamanki, bahor va yangi erkinligim meni hech qachon o'rgangan hamma narsani unutib qo'yish uchun birlashtirgan bo'lardi va shuning uchun imtihonlarni hech qanday maqsadga qo'ymagan bo'lardim.

en: THE EXAMINATION IN HISTORY ON the ൢ൧th of April I entered, for the first time, and under the wing of St.
uz: Aprel oyining th kuni tarixda o'qishga kirdim, birinchi marta, va St.ning qanotlari ostida.

en: Jerome, the great hall of the University.
uz: Jerome, universitetning buyuk zali.

en: I had driven there with St.
uz: Men St. bilan u yerga sayohat qildim.

en: Jerome in our smart phaeton and wearing the first frockcoat of my life, while the whole of my other clothes—even down to my socks and linen—were new and of a grander sort.
uz: Jeronim o'z aqlli faetonimizda va hayotimning birinchi kiyimini kiyganimda, boshqa kiyimlarimning hammasi, hatto shortslarim va choriqlarim ham yangi va buyukroq edi.

en: When a Swiss waiter relieved me of my greatcoat, and I stood before him in all the beauty of my attire, I felt almost sorry to dazzle him so.
uz: Shveytsariyalangan xizmatkor meni ko'ylagimdan olib tashlaganida va men uning oldida kiyimimning go'zalligi bilan turganimda, uni shunchalik ko'nglimdan ko'targanim uchun o'zimni qayg'uli his qilardim.

en: Yet I had no sooner entered the bright, carpeted, crowded hall, and caught sight of hundreds of other young men in gymnasium [The Russian gymnasium = the English grammar or secondary school.] uniforms or frockcoats (of whom but a few threw me an indifferent glance), as well as, at the far end, of some solemn-looking professors who were seated on chairs or walking carelessly about among some tables, than I at once became disabused of the notion that I should attract the general attention, while the expression of my face, which at home, and even in the vestibule of the University buildings, had denoted only a kind of vague regret that I should have to present so important and distinguished an appearance, became exchanged for
uz: Ammo men chiroyli, ko'pchilik bilan to'plangan zaliga kirib, sport zalida yuzlab boshqa yigitlarni ko'rdim (ulardan faqat bir nechtasi menga befarq ko'rindi), shuningdek, oxirida o'rindiqlarda o'tirgan yoki ba'zi stollar o'rtasida beparvolik bilan yurgan ba'zi obro'li professorlarni ko'rdim, lekin men darhol umumiy e'tiborni jalb qilishim kerak degan fikrdan mahrum bo'ldim.

en: an expression of the most acute nervousness and dejection.
uz: Bu eng og'ir g'alati va tushkunlikning ifodasidir.

en: However, I soon picked up again when I perceived sitting at one of the desks a very badly, untidily dressed gentleman who, though not really old, was almost entirely grey.
uz: Biroq, tez orada men bir stolda o'tirgan juda yomon kiyim kiygan va ko'p o'tmagan bir erkakni ko'rdim, u garchi juda katta bo'lmasa-da, deyarli butunlay oq bo'lgan.

en: He was occupying a seat quite at the back of the hall and a little apart from the rest, so I hastened to sit down beside him, and then fell to looking at the candidates for examination, and to forming conclusions about them.
uz: U zalning orqasida o'tirgan va boshqalardan biroz ajralib turgan edi, shuning uchun men uning yonida o'tirishga shoshildim va imtihon uchun nomzodlarga qarab, ular haqida xulosa chiqarishga tushdim.

en: Many different figures and faces were there to be seen there; yet, in my opinion, they all seemed to divide themselves into three classes.
uz: U yerda ko'plab turli shakllar va yuzlar ko'rish mumkin edi; ammo mening fikrimcha, ularning barchasi o'zlarini uchta toifaga bo'lishgan.

en: First of all, there were youths like myself, attending for examination in the company of their parents or tutors.
uz: Birinchidan, o'zim kabi yoshlar ota-onasi yoki o'qituvchilari bilan imtihonga borishgan.

en: Among such I could see the youngest Iwin (accompanied by Frost) and Ilinka Grap (accompanied by his old father).
uz: Ulardan eng kichkinagini - Iwin (Frost bilan birga) va Ilinka Grapni (o'zining keksa otasi bilan birga) ko'rdim.

en: All youths of this class wore the early beginnings of beards, sported prominent linen, sat quietly in their places, and never opened the books and notebooks which they had brought with them, but gazed at the professors and examination tables with ill- concealed nervousness.
uz: Ushbu sinfdagi barcha yoshlar barvalarning erta boshlarini kiyib, ko'pchilikni e'tiborga oluvchi liboslar kiyishgan, o'z o'rinlarida xotirjamlik bilan o'tirishgan va hech qachon o'zlari bilan olib kelgan kitoblar va notebooklarni ochmagan, balki professorlar va imtihon stollariga g'ayrat bilan qaragan.

en: The second class of candidates were young men in gymnasium uniforms.
uz: Ikkinchi sinf nomzodlar sport zavodida kiyinadigan yosh yigitlar edi.

en: Several of them had attained to the dignity of shaving, and most of them knew one another.
uz: Ulardan bir nechtasi sochlarini qirqish sharafiga ega bo'lgan va aksariyati bir-birlarini tanishgan.

en: They talked loudly, called the professors by their names and surnames, occupied themselves in getting their subjects ready, exchanged notebooks, climbed over desks, fetched themselves pies and sandwiches from the vestibule, and ate them then and there merely lowering their heads to the level of a desk for propriety’s sake.
uz: Ular baland ovozda gapirishardi, professorlarni o'z ismlari va familiyasi bilan chaqirardi, o'zlarining mavzularini tayyorlashga band edilar, notabuklar almashdilar, stollar ustiga chiqib, hovlidan tort va sendvichlar olib kelishardi va ularni o'zlari yeb ketishdi.

en: Lastly, the third class of candidates (which seemed a small one) consisted of oldish men—some of them in frock coats, but the majority in jackets, and with no linen to be seen.
uz: Va nihoyat, uchinchi sinf nomzodlar (ko'rinishi kichkina bo'lgan) keksa erkaklardan iborat edi, ularning ba'zilari paltarosh kiyimda edilar, aksariyati esa jaketalarda edilar va ko'rinadigan matolar bo'lmagan edilar.

en: These preserved a serious demeanour, sat by themselves, and had a very dingy look.
uz: Bular jiddiy xulq-atvorni saqlab, o'zlaricha o'tirib, juda yomon ko'rinishga ega edilar.

en: The man who had afforded me consolation by being worse dressed than myself belonged to this class.
uz: O'zimdan ham yomon kiyim kiygan odam meni tasalli bergan kishi shu sinfga kirgan.

en: Leaning forward upon his elbows, and running his fingers through his grey, dishevelled hair as he read some book or another, he had thrown me only a momentary glance —and that not a very friendly one—from a pair of glittering eyes.
uz: U qo'lqoshlari ustida oldinga tiklanib, o'z sariq sochlarini o'qib, bir kitob yoki boshqa kitobni o'qib o'tirganida o'z barmoqlarini o'tkazgan edi.

en: Then, as I sat down, he had frowned grimly, and stuck a shiny elbow out to prevent me from coming any nearer.
uz: Keyin, o'tirganimda, u ko'ngli ko'tarilmay, meni yaqinlashtirmaslik uchun shinam ko'krakni qo'yib qo'ydi.

en: On the other hand, the gymnasium men were over-sociable, and I felt rather afraid of their proximity.
uz: Boshqa tomondan, sport zavodidagi erkaklar juda ijtimoiy edilar va men ularning yaqinligidan qo'rqardim.

en: One of them did not hesitate to thrust a book into my
uz: Ulardan biri mening ko'nglimga kitobni qo'yib yuborishga ikkilanmadi.

en: hands, saying, “Give that to that fellow over there, will you?” while another of them exclaimed as he pushed past me, “By your leave, young fellow!” and a third made use of my shoulder as a prop when he wanted to scramble over a desk.
uz: O'sha odamga qo'l bering, shundaymi? - deb so'rabdi, yana bir kishi meni o'tib ketayotganda: "Yo'q, yigit! - deb hayqirib yubordi.

en: All this seemed to me a little rough and unpleasant, for I looked upon myself as immensely superior to such fellows, and considered that they ought not to treat me with such familiarity.
uz: Bularning barchasi menga biroz shafqatsiz va noqulay tuyuldi, chunki men o'zimni bunday odamlardan juda ustun deb bilardim va ular menga bunday tanishlik bilan munosabatda bo'lmasliklari kerak deb o'ylardim.

en: At length, the names began to be called out.
uz: Vaqt o'tib, ismlar tilga olinishni boshladi.

en: The gymnasium men walked out boldly, answered their questions (apparently) well, and came back looking cheerful.
uz: Gimnaziya erkaklari jasorat bilan chiqib, savollariga (shog'inicha) yaxshi javob berishdi va xursand ko'rinib qaytib kelishdi.

en: My own class of candidates were much more diffident, as well as appeared to answer worse.
uz: Mening o'z sinfdagi nomzodlar ko'proq ishonchsizlik ko'rsatib, yomonroq javob berishgan.

en: Of the oldish men, some answered well, and some very poorly.
uz: Keksalarning ba'zilari yaxshi javob bergan, ba'zilari esa juda yomon javob bergan.

en: When the name “Semenoff” was called out my neighbour with the grey hair and glittering eyes jostled me roughly, stepped over my legs, and went up to one of the examiners’ tables.
uz: Semenoff nomi bilan chaqirilganda, o'g'il sochlari va shiddatli ko'zlari bilan yashirin bo'lgan qo'shnim meni qo'rqitdi, oyoqlarimni bosdi va imtihonchilar dasturxonlaridan biriga bordi.

en: It was plain from the aspect of the professors that he answered well and with assurance, yet, on returning to his place, he did not wait to see where he was placed on the list, but quietly collected his notebooks and departed.
uz: O'qituvchilarning nuqtai nazaridan u yaxshi va ishonch bilan javob berganligi aniq edi, ammo o'z o'rinlariga qaytganida u ro'yxatga qayerda qo'yilganini ko'rishni kutmadi, balki xotirjamlik bilan kitoblarini yig'ib, jo'nab ketdi.

en: Several times I shuddered at the sound of the voice calling out the names, but my turn did not come in exact alphabetical order, though already names had begun to be called beginning with “I.” “Ikonin and Tenieff!” suddenly shouted some one from the professors’ end of the hall.
uz: Men bir necha marta ismlarni chaqiradigan ovoz ovozini eshitib titrardim, lekin mening navbatim aniq alifbo tartibida kelmadi, garchi ismlar allaqachon I.Ikonin va Tenieff bilan boshlanadi deb chaqirilishni boshlagan bo'lsa-da! Birdan professorlarning biri zalning oxiridan baqirib yubordi.

en: You are being called,” said a tall, red-faced gymnasium student near me.
uz: Seni chaqirishyapti, - dedi yonimda yotgan baland, qizil yuzli gimnaziya o'quvchisi.

en: “But who is this BARtenieff or MORtenieff or somebody?
uz: Ammo bu BARtenieff yoki MORtenieff yoki boshqa kim?

en: I don’t know him.” “It must be you,” whispered St.
uz: Men uni tanimayman. Bu siz bo'lishi kerak, shovqin so'zladi St..

en: Jerome loudly in my ear.
uz: Jerom quloqlarimga baland ovoz bilan gapirdi.

en: “MY name is IRtenieff,” I said to the red-faced student.
uz: MING ismim IRtenieff, deb qizil yuzli talabaga aytdim.

en: “Do you think that was the name they were calling out?” “Yes.
uz: Sizning fikringizcha, ular shunday nom qo'yishganmi?Ha.

en: Why on earth don’t you go up?” he replied.
uz: Nima uchun u yerga bormaysan? - deb javob berdi u.

en: “Lord, what a dandy!” he added under his breath, yet not so quietly but that I failed to hear the words as they came wafted to me from below the desk.
uz: "Rabbim, qanday chiroyli!" - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u nafasini olg'a surib, lekin shunga o'xshab emas, balki so'zlar stolning pastligidan menga to'kib kelganini eshitmasdim.

en: In front of me walked Ikonin—a tall young man of about twenty-five, who was one of those whom I had classed as oldish men.
uz: Oldimda Ikonin ismli baland yosh, taxminan yigirma besh yoshli yigit bor edi, u men qariyalar deb hisoblagan odamlardan biri edi.

en: He wore a tight brown frockcoat and a blue satin tie, and had wisps of flaxen hair carefully brushed over his collar in the peasant style.
uz: U qattiq qora rangli ko'ylak kiyimini va ko'k satin kravatni kiygan edi va qo'ylak usti ustida qishloqcha uslubda puxta sochlar o'rnatilgan edi.

en: His appearance had already caught my attention when we were sitting
uz: Uning tashqi ko'rinishi biz o'tirgan paytimda menga e'tibor qaratgan edi.

en: among the desks, and had given me an impression that he was not bad-looking.
uz: Ish stoli o'rtasida o'tirganida, u yomon ko'rinishga ega bo'lmagan degan taassurot qoldirgan edi.

en: Also I had noticed that he was very talkative.
uz: Shuningdek, u juda gapiradigan odam ekanini payqadim.

en: Yet what struck me most about his physiognomy was a tuft, of queer red hairs which he had under his chin, as well as, still more, a strange habit of continually unbuttoning his waistcoat and scratching his chest under his shirt.
uz: Ammo uning jismonasi haqida meni eng hayratda qoldirgan narsa, bu uning burun ostida bo'lgan o'ziga xos qizil sochlar, shuningdek, yanada ko'proq o'ziga xos odati edi, u doimiy ravishda kiyimini ochib, ko'krakini ko'ylagini ko'ylagini pastga qirib tashlaydi.

en: Behind the table to which we were summoned sat three Professors, none of whom acknowledged our salutations.
uz: Biz chaqirilgan dasturxon ortida uchta professor o'tirgan, ularning hech biri bizning salomlarimizni qabul qilmagan.

en: A youngish professor was shuffling a bundle of tickets like a pack of cards; another one, with a star on his frockcoat, was gazing hard at a gymnasium student, who was repeating something at great speed about Charles the Great, and adding to each of his sentences the word nakonetz [= the English colloquialism “you know.”] while a third one—an old man in spectacles—proceeded to bend his head down as we approached, and, peering at us through his glasses, pointed silently to the tickets.
uz: Yosh professor kartalar to'plami kabi chiptalar to'plamini o'rab-o'rab o'tirgan edi; yana biri, kiyimida yulduz bilan, gimnaziya o'quvchisini diqqat bilan kuzatib turardi, u Buyuk Karol haqida bir narsani tezda takrorlab, har bir gapga nakonetz so'zini qo'shardi, uchinchi kishi esa, ko'zguvlarda bo'lgan keksa kishi, biz yaqinlashayotganda boshini egib, ko'zguvlari orqali bizga qarab, jimlik bilan chiptalarni ko'rsatdi.

en: I felt his glance go over both myself and Ikonin, and also felt sure that something about us had displeased him (perhaps it was Ikonin’s red hairs), for, after taking another look at the pair of us, he motioned impatiently to us to be quick in taking our tickets.
uz: Uning ko'z o'zimizga ham, Ikoninga ham o'tib ketayotganini his qildim, shuningdek, biz haqimizda biron bir narsa unga yoqmaganini his qildim (ehtimol, bu Ikoninning qizil sochlari bo'lgan), chunki yana bir bor bizni ko'rib chiqqandan so'ng, u bizni chiptalarimizni tezroq olishimiz uchun sabrsizlik bilan ishora qildi.

en: I felt vexed and offended—firstly, because none of the professors had responded to our bows, and, secondly, because they evidently coupled me with Ikonin under the one denomination of “candidates,” and so were condemning me in advance on account of Ikonin’s red hairs.
uz: Birinchidan, o'qituvchilarning hech biri bizning o'qlarimizga javob bermagani uchun o'zimni xafa va xafa his qildim, ikkinchidan esa, ular meni Ikonin bilan "kandidatlar" nomidan bog'lashgan va meni Ikoninning qizil sochlari tufayli oldindan hukm qilishgan.

en: I took my ticket boldly and made ready to answer, but the professor’s eye passed over my head and alighted upon Ikonin.
uz: Men jasorat bilan chiptaimni olib, javob berishga tayyor bo'ldim, lekin professorning ko'zi boshimdan o'tib, Ikoninni ko'rdim.

en: Accordingly, I occupied myself in reading my ticket.
uz: Shuning uchun men o'zimni chipta o'qishga bag'ishladim.

en: The questions printed on it were all familiar to me, so, as I silently awaited my turn, I gazed at what was passing near me, Ikonin seemed in no way diffident—rather the reverse, for, in reaching for his ticket, he threw his body half-way across the table.
uz: Unda chop etilgan savollar menga tanish edi, shuning uchun men o'z navbatimni hushyorlik bilan kutganimda, yonimda o'tgan narsalarga tikilib qaraganimda, Ikonin hech qanday shak-shubhasiz emas, aksincha, o'ziga tiklangan chiptaga qo'shilib, o'z tanasini jadvalning yarmiga tashladi.

en: Then he gave his long hair a shake, and rapidly conned over what was written on his ticket.
uz: Keyin u o'zining uzun sochlarini shishirdi va tezda chiptaga yozib qo'yilgan narsalarni aldadi.

en: I think he had just opened his mouth to answer when the professor with the star dismissed the gymnasium student with a word of commendation, and then turned and looked at Ikonin.
uz: O'ylaymanki, u o'z og'zini ochib javob bergan edi, ammo yulduzli professor o'quv yurtining o'quvchilarini maqtov so'zi bilan quvib, Ikoninga qarab qo'ydi.

en: At once the latter seemed taken back, and stopped short.
uz: O'sha zahoti bu o'zgarishlar orqaga surildi va qisqacha to'xtadi.

en: For about two minutes there was a dead silence.
uz: Taxminan ikki daqiqa davomida o'lik xotirjamlik hukm surdi.

en: “Well?” said the professor in the spectacles.
uz: Navoiy? dedi professor ko'zguvchida.

en: Once more Ikonin opened his mouth, and once more remained silent.
uz: Ikonin yana og'zini ochdi va yana bir bor sukut saqladi.

en: You are not the only one to be examined.
uz: Siz faqat siz tekshiruvdan o'tmaysiz.

en: Do you mean to answer or do you not?” said the youngish professor, but Ikonin did not even look at him.
uz: Javob berishni xohlaysizmi yoki yo'qmi? - dedi yosh professor, ammo Ikonin unga hatto nazar ham solmadi.

en: He was gazing fixedly at his ticket and uttered not a single word.
uz: O'zining chiptaga qaragan va bir so'z ham aytmagan.

en: The professor in the spectacles scanned him through his glasses, then over them, then without them (for, indeed, he had time to take them off, to wipe their lenses carefully, and to replace them).
uz: O'sha ko'zoynadagi professor uni ko'zoynaklar orqali, keyin ularning ustida, keyin ularsiz skanerladi (chunki, albatta, u ularni olib tashlashga, shishalarini ehtiyotkorlik bilan yuvishga va almashtirish uchun vaqt topgan).

en: Still not a word from Ikonin.
uz: Hndi Ikoninning so'zi ham yo'q.

en: All at once, however, a smile spread itself over his face, and he gave his long hair another shake.
uz: Biroq, birdan uning yuzida tabassum paydo bo'ldi va u o'zining uzun sochlariga yana bir shake berdi.

en: Next he reached across the table, laid down his ticket, looked at each of the professors in turn and then at myself, and finally, wheeling round on his heels, made a gesture with his hand and returned to the desks.
uz: So'ngra stolning orqasidan o'tdi, chiptalarini qo'ydi, professorlarning har biriga o'z navbatida, so'ngra o'zimga qarab, nihoyat, to'qnashuvchi bo'lib, qo'li bilan harakat qilib, stollarga qaytib keldi.

en: The professors stared blankly at one another.
uz: Professorlar bir-birlariga ko'z tikib qarab turishdi.

en: “Bless the fellow!” said the youngish professor.
uz: Bu yigitga barakalar bo'lsin! dedi yosh professor.

en: “What an original!” It was now my turn to move towards the table, but the professors went on talking in undertones among themselves, as though they were unaware of my presence.
uz: Qanday original! Endi mening navbatim bordi, men stolga qarab o'tdim, lekin professorlar o'z-o'zlariga o'xshash so'zlar bilan gapira boshladilar, xuddi mening borligimni bilmayotgandek.

en: At the moment, I felt firmly persuaded that the three of them were engrossed solely with the question of whether I should merely PASS the examination or whether I should pass it WELL, and that it was only swagger which made them pretend that they did not care either way, and behave as though they had not seen me.
uz: O'shanda men o'zimni uchalasi faqatgina imtihonni o'tishim yoki yaxshi o'tishim kerakmi degan savolga chalingan va bu ularni hech qanday qiziqish ko'rsatmayotganini ko'rsatishga va meni ko'rmaganlardek yo'l tutishga undaydigan narsa faqat o'z-o'zidan o'ylash edi.

en: When at length the professor in the spectacles turned to me with an air of indifference, and invited me to answer, I felt hurt, as I looked at him, to think that he should have so undeceived me: wherefore I answered brokenly at first.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, ko'zguda o'tirgan professor menga befarqlik bilan murojaat qilib, javob berishni taklif qilganda, unga qarab, u meni shu qadar begona qilib qo'yishi kerak edi, deb o'ylaganimda, o'zimni xafa his qildim: shuning uchun men dastlab buzib javob berdim.

en: In time, however, things came easier to my tongue, and, inasmuch as all the questions bore upon Russian history (which I knew thoroughly), I ended with eclat, and even went so far, in my desire to convince the professors that I was not Ikonin and that they must not in anyway confound me with him, as to offer to draw a second ticket.
uz: Ammo vaqt o'tib, bu menga osonroq bo'ldi va barcha savollar rus tarixini (men buni yaxshi bilardim) o'z ichiga olganligi sababli, men professorlarni men Ikonin emasligimni va ular meni u bilan hech qanday chalg'itmasligi kerakligiga ishontirish niyatim bilan eklat bilan yakunlandim va hatto bu qadar ketdim.

en: The professor in the spectacles, however, merely nodded his head, said “That will do,” and marked something in his register.
uz: Biroq, ko'zguda bo'lgan professor boshini tikib: "Bu yaxshi bo'ladi", - dedi va ro'yxatida biror narsa belgilab qo'ydi.

en: On returning to the desks, I at once learnt from the gymnasium men (who somehow seemed to know everything) that I had been placed fifth.
uz: Ish stoliga qaytganimda, men darhol sport zavodidagi erkaklardan (ular hamma narsani bilgan bo'lib ko'rinardi) beshinchi o'rinni egallaganimni bilib oldim.

en: MY EXAMINATION IN MATHEMATICS AT the subsequent examinations, I made several new acquaintances in addition to the Graps (whom I considered unworthy of my notice) and Iwin (who for some reason or other avoided me).
uz: Matematika bo'yicha o'zimning imtihonim Keyingi imtihonlarda men Graps (men ularni e'tiborga loyiq deb hisoblaganman) va Iwin (bir sababga ko'ra mendan qochgan) bilan birga bir nechta yangi tanishlar orttirdim.

en: With some of these new friends I grew quite intimate, and even Ikonin plucked up sufficient courage to inform me, when we next met, that he would have to undergo re-examination in history—the reason for his failure this time being that the professor of that faculty had never forgiven him for last year’s examination, and had, indeed, “almost killed” him for it.
uz: Bu yangi do'stlar bilan yaqindan tanishdim va hatto Ikonin o'z navbatida tarixda qayta ko'rib chiqilishi kerakligini aytishga qodir bo'ldi.Bu safar uning muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrashishining sababi shundaki, o'tgan yilgi imtihon uchun uni fakultet professori hech qachon kechirmagan va, aslida, uni o'ldirmoqchi bo'lgan.

en: Semenoff (who was destined for the same faculty as myself— the faculty of mathematics) avoided every one up to the very close of the examinations.
uz: Semenoff (men bilan bir xil matematik fakultetga tayinlangan) imtihonlarning oxirigacha har biridan qochdi.

en: Always leaning forward upon his elbows and running his fingers through his grey hair, he sat silent and alone.
uz: Doimo qo'lqoshlari ustida oldinga tiklanib, o'zining sariq sochlari orqali barmoqlarini o'tkazgan u, bechora va yolg'iz o'tirgan.

en: Nevertheless, when called up for examination in mathematics (he had no companion to accompany him), he came out second.
uz: Shunga qaramay, matematikada imtihon o'tkazish uchun chaqirilganda (ular bilan birga o'tirishga hech kim yo'q edi), u ikkinchi o'rinni egalladi.

en: The first place was taken by a student from the first gymnasium—a tall, dark, lanky, pale-faced fellow who wore a black folded cravat and had his cheeks and forehead dotted all over with pimples.
uz: Birinchi o'rinni birinchi o'quv yurtining o'quvchilari o'tkazdiki, baland, qorong'u, chiroyli, ko'k yuzli yigit qora bo'lib o'ralgan kravat kiygan va chegaralari va forefasida ko'piklar bo'lgan.

en: His hands were shapely and slender, but their nails were so bitten to the quick that the finger-ends looked as though they had been tied round with strips of thread.
uz: Uning qo'llari o'ziga xos va chiroyli edi, ammo uncha ko'tarilmagan bo'lib, barmoqlari to'ng'ichlari iplar bilan bog'langan bo'lgani kabi ko'rinardi.

en: All this seemed to me splendid, and wholly becoming to a student of the first gymnasium.
uz: Bularning barchasi menga chiroyli ko'rindi va birinchi o'quv yurti o'quvchisiga o'xshaydi.

en: He spoke to every one, and we all made friends with him.
uz: U har bir kishi bilan suhbatlashdi va biz hammamiz u bilan do'stlashdik.

en: To me in particular his walk, his every movement, his lips, his dark eyes, all seemed to have in them something extraordinary and magnetic.
uz: Menga, ayniqsa, uning yurishi, har bir harakatlari, og'izlari, qorong'i ko'zlari, barchasi o'zlarida g'ayritabiiy va maqnitli bir narsa bor deb tuyuldi.

en: On the day of the mathematical examination I arrived earlier than usual at the hall.
uz: Matematika imtihoni kunida men odatdagidan oldin zalga keldim.

en: I knew the syllabus well, yet there were two questions in the algebra which my tutor had managed to pass over, and which were therefore quite unknown to me.
uz: Men dasturiy ta'minotni yaxshi bilardim, ammo algebraga oid ikkita savol bor edi, ularni o'qituvchim o'qitishga muvaffaq bo'ldi va shuning uchun men uchun umuman noma'lum edi.

en: If I remember rightly, they were the Theory of Combinations and Newton’s Binomial.
uz: Agar men to'g'ri eslayman bo'lsa, ular kombinatsiyalar nazariyasi va Nyutonning binomiallari edi.

en: seated myself on one of the back benches and pored over the two questions, but, inasmuch as I was not accustomed to working in a noisy room, and had even less time for preparation than I had anticipated, I soon found it difficult to take in all that I was reading.
uz: O'zimni orqa banklarning birida o'tirib, ikkita savolni o'ylab ko'rdim, lekin shovqinli xonada ishlashga o'rganmaganim va tayyorgarlik uchun o'ylagandan ham kamroq vaqtim bo'lgani uchun o'qiganlarimning barchasini qabul qilish qiyin kechdi.

en: This way, Nechludoff,” said Woloda’s familiar voice behind me.
uz: Shu tarzda Nechludoff,  dedi Wolodaning orqamdagi tanish ovozi.

en: I turned and saw my brother and Dimitri—their gowns unbuttoned, and their hands waving a greeting to me—threading their way through the desks.
uz: O'girilib, akam va Dimitriyning kiyimlari tugmachi bo'lmaganini va qo'llari menga salom solib, stollar orqali yo'llarini o'tkazayotganini ko'rdim.

en: A moment’s glance would have sufficed to show any one that they were second-course students—persons to whom the University was as a second home.
uz: Bir daqiqalik ko'z o'tib, ular ikkinchi darajali talabalar ekanliklarini ko'rsatishga yetarli bo'lardi.

en: The mere look of their open gowns expressed at once disdain for the “mere candidate” and a knowledge that the “mere candidate’s” soul was filled with envy and admiration of them.
uz: Ularning ochiq kiyimlarining ko'rinishi bir vaqtning o'zida nomzodga hurmatsizlikni va nomzodning ruhi ularga hasad va hayronlik bilan to'lib-toshganligini bildiradi.

en: I was charmed to think that every one near me could now see that I knew two real second-course students: wherefore I hastened to meet them half-way.
uz: Men atrofimda bo'lganlarning hammasi men ikkita haqiqiy ikkinchi kurs o'quvchilarini taniganimni ko'rishdi, deb o'ylashim meni hayratda qoldirdi: shuning uchun men ularni yarim yo'lda uchratishga shoshildim.

en: Woloda, of course, could not help vaunting his superiority a little.
uz: Albatta, Woloda o'zining ustunligini biroz ko'tarishga yordam bera olmadi.

en: “Hullo, you smug!” he said.
uz: Hullo, sen o'zingni o'zing bilmaysan! dedi.

en: “Haven’t you been examined yet?” “No.” “Well, what are you reading?
uz: Siz hali tekshirilmaganmisiz?Yo'q. Xo'sh, nima o'qiyotgansiz?

en: Aren’t you sufficiently primed?” “Yes, except in two questions.
uz: Siz yetarlicha tayyor emasmisiz?Ha, faqat ikki savoldan tashqari.

en: I don’t understand them at all.” “Eh, what?”—and Woloda straightway began to expound to me Newton’s Binomial, but so rapidly and unintelligibly that, suddenly reading in my eyes certain misgivings as to the soundness of his knowledge, he glanced also at Dimitri’s face.
uz: Men ularni umuman tushunmayman.

en: Clearly, he saw the same misgivings there, for he blushed hotly, though still continuing his involved explanations.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, u o'sha yerda ham shu kabi shubhalarni ko'rgan, chunki u qizg'in qizg'inlagan, ammo u o'z tushuntirishlarini davom ettirgan.

en: “No; hold on, Woloda, and let me try and do it,” put in Dimitri at length, with a glance at the professors’ corner as he seated himself beside me.
uz: Yo'q, Voloda, to'xtang, men uni sinab ko'rsam, Dimitriyni uzluksiz qo'yib, professorning burchagida o'tirganini ko'rib ko'ring.

en: I could see that my friend was in the best of humours.
uz: Men do'stimning humorning eng yaxshi tomonida ekanligini ko'rardim.

en: This was always the case with him when he was satisfied with himself, and was one of the things in him which I liked best.
uz: U o'zidan mamnun bo'lganida hamisha shunday bo'lardi va bu uning eng yaxshi ko'rgan narsalaridan biri edi.

en: Inasmuch as he knew mathematics well and could speak clearly, he hammered the question so thoroughly into my head that I can remember it to this day.
uz: U matematikani yaxshi bilgan va aniq gapirganligi sababli, savolni o'zimning boshimga shunchalik chuqur tushirdiki, uni bugungi kungacha eslay olaman.

en: Hardly had he finished when St.
uz: U St.Qudsda o'qishni to'xtatib bo'lganida, o'qishni to'xtatmagan edi.

en: Jerome said to me in a loud whisper, “A vous, Nicolas,” and I followed Ikonin out from among the
uz: Jerom baland ovoz bilan menga: "A siz, Nikolas", - dedi va men Ikoninni o'rtalaridan ergashib chiqdim.

en: desks without having had an opportunity of going through the OTHER question of which I was ignorant.
uz: Boshqa savolni ko'rib chiqish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lmaganimda, men bu savolni bilmasdim.

en: At the table which we now approached were seated two professors, while before the blackboard stood a gymnasium student, who was working some formula aloud, and knocking bits off the end of the chalk with his too vigorous strokes.
uz: Biz yaqinlashgan stolda ikkita professor o'tirgan edi, ammo jadvalning oldida bir gimnaziya o'quvchisi baland ovoz bilan formulani o'rganayotgan va o'zining juda kuchli urishi bilan maydonning so'ngida maydonlarni urib qo'ygan edi.

en: He even continued writing after one of the Professors had said to him “Enough!” and bidden us draw our tickets.
uz: U hatto professorlardan biri unga "To'g'ri!" deb aytganidan va bizga chiptalarimizni chizishni buyurganidan keyin ham yozishni davom ettirdi.

en: “Suppose I get the Theory of Combinations?” I thought to myself as my tremulous fingers took a ticket from among a bundle wrapped in torn paper.
uz: Agar men kombinatsiyalar nazariyasini o'rgansam? Men o'zimga o'yladimki, qo'rqinchli barmoqlarim parchalangan qog'ozga o'rab olingan to'plamdan chipta oldi.

en: Ikonin, for his part, reached across the table with the same assurance, and the same sidelong movement of his whole body, as he had done at the previous examination.
uz: Ikonin esa o'z navbatida, o'tgan tekshiruvda qilganidek, o'zining butun tanasi bilan o'sha ishonch va yonboshiga o'xshash harakatni ko'rsatdi.

en: Taking the topmost ticket without troubling to make further selection, he just glanced at it, and then frowned angrily.
uz: U eng yuqori chiptaga ega bo'lib, keyinchalik tanlovni davom ettirish uchun tashvishlanmasdan, unga bir nazar tashlab, g'azab bilan yuz o'girdi.

en: “I always draw this kind of thing,” he muttered.
uz: "Men har doim bunday narsalarni chizaman", - deb gapirdi u.

en: It was the Theory of Combinations!
uz: Bu kombinatsiyalar nazariyasi edi!

en: “What have you got?” whispered Ikonin at this point.
uz: Sizda nima bor? Bu vaqtda Ikonin shovqin qildi.

en: “Oh, I know that,” he said.
uz: Oh, men buni bilaman, dedi u.

en: “Will you make an exchange, then?” “No.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa, siz almashinuvni o'tkazasizmi? Yo'q.

en: Besides, it would be all the same for me if I did,” he contrived to whisper just as the professor called us up to the blackboard.
uz: Bundan tashqari, agar shunday qilsam, men uchun hammasi bir xil bo'lardi, professor bizni taxtga chaqirganida, u shov-shuv qila boshladi.

en: “I don’t feel up to anything to-day.” “Then everything is lost!” I thought to myself.
uz: Bugun hech narsaga ega bo'lmayapman.Undan keyin hamma narsa yo'qoladi! - deb o'yladim men o'zimga.

en: Instead of the brilliant result which I had anticipated I should be for ever covered with shame—more so even than Ikonin!
uz: O'zim kutib o'tgan ajoyib natija o'rniga, men abadiylik uchun Ikonindan ham ko'proq sharmanda bo'lishim kerak edi!

en: Suddenly, under the very eyes of the professor, Ikonin turned to me, snatched my ticket out of my hands, and handed me his own.
uz: Toʻsatdan, professorning koʻz oʻngida, Ikonin menga qarab, chiptaimni qoʻlimdan olib, oʻzining chiptalarini berdi.

en: I looked at his ticket.
uz: Men uning chiptasiga qaradim.

en: It was Newton’s Binomial!
uz: Bu Nyutonning binomiyasi edi!

en: The professor was a youngish man, with a pleasant, clever expression of face—an effect chiefly due to the prominence of the lower part of his forehead.
uz: Professor yosh bo'lgan, yuz ta'sirini yoqimli va aqlli ifoda etgan, asosan, uning peshanasining pastki qismi ko'rinishi tufayli.

en: Are you exchanging tickets, gentlemen?” he said.
uz: Sizlar chipta almashyapsizmi, xonimlar? - dedi u.

en: He only gave me his to look at, professor,” answered Ikonin— and, sure enough, the word “professor” was the last word that he uttered there.
uz: U menga faqat o'zini ko'rib chiqishim uchun berdi, professor, - deb javob berdi Ikonin va, albatta, professor so'zi u yerda aytgan so'zining oxirgi so'zi edi.

en: Once again, he stepped backwards towards me from the table, once again he looked at each of the professors in turn and
uz: U yana bir bor stoldan orqaga qarab menga qarab, yana bir bor professorlarning har biriga o'z navbatida qarab turdi va

en: then at myself, once again he smiled faintly, and once again he shrugged his shoulders as much as to say, “It is no use, my good sirs.” Then he returned to the desks.
uz: Keyin o'zimga yana bir bor o'zimni ko'tarib qo'ydi va yana bir bor yelkalarini ko'tarib: "Bu hech qanday foydasi yo'q, xonimlar", - deb aytdi. So'ng u stollarga qaytib keldi.

en: Subsequently, I learnt that this was the third year he had vainly attempted to matriculate.
uz: Keyinchalik men bu uning matrikulyatsiyaga uchinchi yili ekanligini bilib oldim.

en: I answered my question well, for I had just read it up; and the professor, kindly informing me that I had done even better than was required, placed me fifth.
uz: Men savolimga yaxshi javob berdim, chunki men uni o'qib chiqdim; professor esa menga kerak bo'lganidan ham yaxshiroq ish qilganimni mehribonlik bilan aytib, meni beshinchi o'ringa qo'ydi.

en: MY EXAMINATION IN LATIN All went well until my examination in Latin.
uz: Mening lotin tilidagi imtihonimgacha hamma narsa yaxshi o'tdi.

en: So far, a gymnasium student stood first on the list, Semenoff second, and myself third.
uz: Shu paytgacha o'quv yurti o'quvchisi ro'yxatda birinchi o'rinni egallagan, Semenoff ikkinchi o'rinni egallagan va o'zim uchinchi o'rinni egallagan.

en: On the strength of it I had begun to swagger a little, and to think that, for all my youth, I was not to be despised.
uz: Uning kuchiga ko'ra, men biroz o'z-o'zimni o'ylay boshladim va yoshligim uchun meni kamsitish kerak emas deb o'ylay boshladim.

en: From the first day of the examinations, I had heard every one speak with awe of the Professor of Latin, who appeared to be some sort of a wild beast who battened on the financial ruin of young men (of those, that is to say, who paid their own fees) and spoke only in the Greek and Latin tongues.
uz: Sinovlarning birinchi kunidan boshlab har bir kishi latin tili professori haqida qo'rquv bilan gapirganini eshitgan edim, u yoshlarning (ya'ni o'z haqlarini to'laydiganlarning) moliyaviy vayron bo'lishiga uringan yovvoyi hayvon kabi ko'rinardi va faqat yunon va lotin tillarida gapirgan.

en: Jerome, who had coached me in Latin, spoke encouragingly, and I myself thought that, since I could translate Cicero and certain parts of Horace without the aid of a lexicon, I should do no worse than the rest.
uz: Latin tilida menga o'rgatgan Jeronim dalda beruvchi so'zlarni aytdi va men o'zim Ciceron va Horasiyning ba'zi qismlarini leksikon yordamisiz tarjima qila olsam, boshqalarga qaraganda yomonroq ish qilmasligimni o'yladim.

en: Yet things proved otherwise.
uz: Ammo bularning aksini ko'rsatdi.

en: All the morning the air had been full of rumours concerning the tribulations of candidates who had gone up before me: rumours of how one young fellow had been accorded a nought, another one a single mark only, a third one greeted with abuse and threatened with expulsion, and so forth.
uz: Hamma kuni ertalab meni o'zimdan oldin chiqqan nomzodlarning azob-uqubatlariga oid mish-mishlar bilan to'lib-toshgan edi: bir yosh yigitga hech narsa berilmaganligi, boshqasiga faqat bitta belgi berilganligi, uchinchi kishiga zo'ravonlik bilan salomlashganligi va chetlatilish bilan tahdid qilganligi va shu kabilar haqida mish-mishlar.

en: Only Semenoff and the first gymnasium student had, as usual, gone up quietly, and returned to their seats with five marks credited to their names.
uz: Faqat Semenoff va birinchi gimnaziya o'quvchilari odatdagidek, hushyor turib, o'z o'rinlariga o'tirib, o'z nomlariga beshta markalani qo'shdilar.

en: Already I felt a prescience of disaster when Ikonin and myself found ourselves
uz: Ikonin va men o'zimizni topganimizda, o'zim ham halokatga duchor bo'lganimni his qildim.

en: summoned to the little table at which the terrible professor sat in solitary grandeur.
uz: Yovuz professor yolg'iz ulkanlikda o'tirgan kichkina dasturxonga chaqirildi.

en: The terrible professor turned out to be a little thin, bilious-looking man with hair long and greasy and a face expressive of extraordinary sullenness.
uz: Bu dahshatli professor ozgina chiroyli, chiroyli ko'rinadigan, sochlari uzun va yog'li, yuzida esa noyob zaiflik ko'rinadi.

en: Handing Ikonin a copy of Cicero’s Orations, he bid him translate.
uz: Ikoninga Cicero's Orations nusxasini berib, uni tarjima qilishga taklif qildi.

en: To my great astonishment Ikonin not only read off some of the Latin, but even managed to construe a few lines to the professor’s prompting.
uz: Men juda hayratda qoldimki, Ikonin nafaqat latin tilini o'qib berdi, balki professorning iltimosiga ko'ra bir necha satrlarni ham tushuntirib berdi.

en: At the same time, conscious of my superiority over such a feeble companion, I could not help smiling a little, and even looking rather contemptuous, when it came to a question of analysis, and Ikonin, as on previous occasions, plunged into a silence which promised never to end.
uz: Shu bilan birga, o'zimning bunday zaif hamkorimdan ustunligimni anglab, tahlil masalasi bo'lganda biroz tabassum qilishdan va hatto kamsitib ko'rinishdan bosh tortolmadim, Ikonin ham, avvalgidek, hech qachon tugamaydigan ovozga tushib ketdi.

en: I had hoped to please the professor by that knowing, slightly sarcastic smile of mine, but, as a matter of fact, I contrived to do quite the contrary.
uz: Men o'zimning o'ta bilimdon, biroz sarkastikan tabassumim bilan professorni mamnun qilishni umid qilardim, lekin aslida men buning aksi bo'ldi.

en: “Evidently you know better than he, since you are laughing,” he said to me in bad Russian.
uz: Agar siz undan ko'ra yaxshiroq bilasiz, chunki siz kulyapsiz, - dedi u menga yomon rus tilida.

en: “Well, we shall see.
uz: Xo'sh, ko'ramiz.

en: Tell me the answer, then.” Later I learnt that the professor was Ikonin’s guardian, and that Ikonin actually lived with him.
uz: Keyinchalik professor Ikoninning vasiy bo'lganini va Ikonin u bilan birga yashayotganini bilib oldim.

en: I lost no time in answering the question in syntax which had been put to Ikonin, but the professor only pulled a long face and turned away from me.
uz: Men Ikoninga berilgan sintaxadagi savolga javob berishda vaqt o'tkazmadim, lekin professor shunchaki yuz o'girib, mendan yuz o'girdi.

en: “Well, your turn will come presently, and then we shall see how much you know,” he remarked, without looking at me, but proceeding to explain to Ikonin the point on which he had questioned him.
uz: "Sizning navbatingiz yaqin orada keladi va keyin qancha bilimingiz borligini ko'ramiz", - dedi u menga qaramasdan, balki Ikoninga so'rov bergan mavzuni tushuntirib berishga harakat qildi.

en: “That will do,” he added, and I saw him put down four marks to Ikonin in his register.
uz: U qo'shimcha qildi: "U shunday qiladi va men uni Ikoninga ro'yxatida to'rtta belgi qo'yganini ko'rdim.

en: “Come!” I thought to myself.
uz: Kelib kel! O'zim o'zimga o'yladim.

en: “He cannot be so strict after all.” When Ikonin had taken his departure the professor spent fully five minutes—five minutes which seemed to me five hours—in setting his books and tickets in order, in blowing his nose, in adjusting and sprawling about on his chair, in gazing down the hall, and in looking here, there, and everywhere—in doing everything, in fact, except once letting his eye rest upon me.
uz: Ikonin ketgach, professor o'z kitoblari va chiptalarini to'g'rilashda, burni puflashda, o'z o'rinbosari ustida o'tirib yurishda, zalni ko'rib turishda va bu yerga, u erda va har joyga qarab, hamma narsani qilayotib, aslida, bir marta ko'zini menga qaratganidan tashqari, besh soat vaqt sarfladi.

en: Yet even that amount of dissimulation did not seem to satisfy him, for he next opened a book, and pretended to read it, for all the world as though I were not there at all.
uz: Biroq, hatto o'sha ko'plikdagi yashirinlik ham uni qoniqtirmaganidek tuyuldi, chunki u keyingi safar kitobni ochib, uni o'qiyotganini ko'rsatdi va butun dunyo uchun xuddi men u erda bo'lmaganimdek bo'ldi.

en: I moved a little nearer him, and gave a cough.
uz: Men unga biroz yaqinlashdim va qo'shni tutdim.

en: Well, translate me something,” he remarked, handing me a book of some kind.
uz: - Menga biror narsani tarjima qiling, - dedi u, menga biron bir kitobni uzatdi.

en: “But no; you had better take this,” and, turning over the leaves of a Horace, he indicated to me a passage which I should never have imagined possible of translation.
uz: Lekin yo'q, buni olib, Horazning varaqlarini o'girib, men hech qachon tarjima qilish mumkin deb o'ylamagan bir qismni menga ko'rsatdi.

en: “I have not prepared this,” I said.
uz: Men buni tayyorlab qo'ymaganman, dedim.

en: Then you only wish to answer things which you have got by heart, do you?
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, siz faqat yodingizdan chiqarilgan savollarga javob berishni xohlaysiz, shunday emasmi?

en: No, no; translate me that.” I started to grope for the meaning of the passage, but each questioning look which I threw at the professor was met by a shake of the head, a profound sigh, and an exclamation of “No, no!” Finally he banged the book to with such a snap that he caught his finger between the covers.
uz: Yo'q, yo'q; menga buni tarjima qiling. Men o'sha oyatlar ma'nosini o'ylab topishga kirdim, lekin professorga tashlagan har bir savol berayotgan ko'zimni bosh shovqin, chuqur nafas va Yo'q, yo'q! degan ovoz bilan kutib oldim. Oxir-oqibat u kitobni o'ziga o'xshatdi va o'z barmog'ini qopqoqlar orasidan tutdi.

en: Angrily releasing it, he handed me a ticket containing questions in grammar, and, flinging himself back in his chair, maintained a menacing silence.
uz: U g'azablangan holda uni chiqarganidan so'ng, menga grammatika savollarini o'z ichiga olgan chipta berdi va o'zini o'rinboshiga qaytarib, qo'rqinchli so'zsizlikni saqlab qoldi.

en: I should have tried to answer the questions had not the expression of his face so clogged my tongue that nothing seemed to come from it right.
uz: Agar uning yuzidagi ifodasi tilimni shunchalik to'xtatmagan bo'lsa edi, savollarga javob berishga harakat qilgan bo'lar edimki, hech narsa to'g'ri kelmayotgandek tuyulardi.

en: That’s not it at all!” he suddenly exclaimed in his horrible accent as he altered his posture to one of leaning forward upon the table and playing with the gold signet-ring which was nearly slipping from the little finger of his left hand.
uz: O'zining qo'rqinchli aksenti bilan o'z ko'rinishini o'zgartirib, stol ustida oldinga tiklanib, chap qo'lidagi kichkina barmog'idan deyarli chiqayotgan oltin tamg'alar bilan o'ynashga o'xshatdi.

en: “That is not the way to prepare for serious study, my good sir.
uz: Bu jiddiy o'rganishga tayyorgarlik ko'rishning yo'li emas, xudojo'y sir.

en: Fellows like yourself think that, once they have a gown and a blue collar to their backs, they have reached the summit of all things and become students.
uz: Siz kabi yigitlar, bir marta kiyim va orqaga ko'k qo'lqop qo'yib, barcha narsalarning yuqori darajasiga yetib, talaba bo'lishganini o'ylashadi.

en: No, no, my dear sir.
uz: Yo'q, yo'q, aziz sir.

en: A subject needs to be studied FUNDAMENTALLY,” and so on, and so on.
uz: Ma'lumot o'rganish uchun asosiy talablar bor. va shunga o'xshab.

en: During this speech (which was uttered with a clipped sort of intonation) I went on staring dully at his lowered eyelids.
uz: Ushbu nutq paytida (bu nutq o'zgartirilgan intonatsiya bilan so'zlangan edi) men uning pastga tushirilgan ko'z qo'lqoplariga beparvo qarab turdim.

en: Beginning with a fear lest I should lose my place as third on the list, I went on to fear lest I should pass at all.
uz: Ro'yxatdagi uchinchi o'rinni yo'qotish qo'rquvchidan boshlanayotgan bo'lsam-da, umuman o'tish qo'rquvchiman.

en: Next, these feelings became reinforced by a sense of injustice, injured self-respect, and unmerited humiliation, while the contempt which I felt for the professor as some one not quite (according to my ideas) “comme il faut”—a fact which I deduced from the shortness, strength, and roundness of his nails— flared up in me more and more and turned all my other feelings to sheer animosity.
uz: Keyinchalik, bu his-tuyg'ular adolatsizlik, o'z-o'zimizga bo'lgan hurmat va noloyiq kamsitish hissi bilan mustahkamlandi, professorga nisbatan o'zimga kelgan kamsitish esa (o'ylashimga ko'ra) o'zim uchun o'zgacha emas (o'ylashimcha) comme il fauta fakt deb o'ylagandim.

en: Happening, presently, to glance at me, and to note my quivering lips and tear-filled eyes, he seemed to interpret my
uz: Hozircha menga ko'z tikib, qo'rqinchli og'izlarim va ko'zlarim ko'z yosh bilan to'lib-toshganiga e'tibor qaratganida, u mening so'zimni tushuntirib berayotganday tuyuldi.

en: agitation as a desire to be accorded my marks and dismissed: wherefore, with an air of relenting, he said (in the presence of another professor who had just approached): “Very well; I will accord you a ‘pass’” (which signified two marks), “although you do not deserve it.
uz: O'yinlarimdan voz kechish va uni rad etish istagi bilan o'zini g'ayratli his etib, u (ya'ni, yaqinda yaqinlashgan boshqa professorning huzurida) shunday dedi: Chindan ham yaxshi, men sizga pass (ikki ballni anglatadi) beraman, ammo siz bunga loyiq emassiz.

en: I do so simply out of consideration for your youth, and in the hope that, when you begin your University career, you will learn to be less light-minded.” The concluding phrase, uttered in the hearing of the other professor (who at once turned his eyes upon me, as though remarking, “There!
uz: Men buni shunchaki yoshligingizni ko'rib, universitetda ish boshlaganingizda kamroq yengil bo'lishni o'rganishingizga umid qilaman. Boshqa professorning eshitishida so'nggi so'zlarni aytdim (u birdan menga ko'z ochdi, xuddi shunday aytgandek: "U erda!!")

en: You see, young man!”) completed my discomfiture.
uz: Ko'ryapsizmi, yigit!) mening noqulayligimni yakunladi.

en: For a moment, a mist swam before my eyes—a mist in which the terrible professor seemed to be far away, as he sat at his table while for an instant a wild idea danced through my brain.
uz: Bir lahzacha ko'zlarim oldida bulut ko'tarib turdi, bu bulutda dahshatli professor o'z dasturxonida o'tirganida uzoqdan ko'rinardi, bir lahzacha esa bepul fikr mening miyamda raqsga tushdi.

en: “What if I DID do such a thing?” I thought to myself.
uz: Agar men shunday ishni qilsam nima bo'ladi? Men o'zim bilan o'yladim.

en: “What would come of it?” However, I did not do the thing in question, but, on the contrary, made a bow of peculiar reverence to each of the professors, and with a slight smile on my face—presumably the same smile as that with which I had derided Ikonin—turned away from the table.
uz: Nima natijasi bo'ladi? Biroq, men bu ishni qilmadim, aksincha, professorlarning har biriga o'zgacha hurmat bilan sajda qildim va yuzimda bir oz tabassum bilan gumonki, aynan men masxara qilgan tabassum bilan Ikonin stoldan yuz o'girdi.

en: This piece of unfairness affected me so powerfully at the time that, had I been a free agent, I should have attended for no more examinations.
uz: Ushbu adolatsizlik menga o'sha paytda shunchalik ta'sir ko'rsatdiki, agar men erkin agent bo'lganimda, boshqa imtihonlarga bormasdim.

en: My ambition was gone (since now I could not possibly be third), and I therefore let the other examinations pass without any exertion, or even agitation, on my part.
uz: Mening orzu-ixtiyorim yo'q edi (shundan buyon men uchinchi o'rinni qo'lga kiritolmayman), shuning uchun boshqa imtihonlarni hech qanday harakat va hatto g'ayratsiz o'tkazishga ruxsat berdim.

en: In the general list I still stood fourth, but that failed to interest me, since I had reasoned things out to myself, and come to the conclusion that to try for first place was stupid—even “bad form:” that, in fact, it was better to pass neither very well nor very badly, as Woloda had done.
uz: Umumiy ro'yxatda men hali ham to'rtinchi bo'ldim, lekin bu menga qiziqmadi, chunki men o'zim uchun narsalarni o'ylab ko'rdim va birinchi o'rinni olishga harakat qilish ahmoqlik deb xulosa chiqardim, hatto yomon shaklda ham: aslida, Woloda kabi yaxshi yoki yomon o'tish yaxshiroq emas edi.

en: This attitude I decided to maintain throughout the whole of my University career, notwithstanding that it was the first point on which my opinion had differed from that of my friend Dimitri.
uz: Bu munosabatni men butun universitet hayotim davomida saqlab qolishga qaror qildim, garchi mening fikrlarim do'stim Dimitrining fikridan farq qilgan birinchi nuqta bo'lsa ham.

en: Yet, to tell the truth, my thoughts were already turning towards a uniform, a “mortar-board,” and the possession of a drozhki of my own, a room of my own, and, above all, freedom of my own.
uz: Biroq, rostini aytsam, fikrlarim allaqachon bir kiyimga, mortar-bordga va o'z drozhkimga, o'z xonamga, eng asosiysi esa, o'z erkinligimga qaratilgan edi.

en: And certainly the prospect had its charm.
uz: Va shubhasiz, istiqbol o'zining go'zalligi bor edi.

en: I BECOME GROWN-UP When, on May ൩th, I returned home from the final, the divinity, examination, I found my acquaintance, the foreman from Rozonoff’s, awaiting me.
uz: Men o'sganimda, may oyida final, ilohiylik, imtihondan uyga qaytganimda, tanishimni, Rozonoffsdan bo'lgan cho'ri meni kutib turganini ko'rdim.

en: He had called once before to fit me for my gown, as well as for a tunic of glossy black cloth (the lapels of which were, on that occasion, only sketched in chalk), but to-day he had come to bring me the clothes in their finished state, with their gilt buttons wrapped in tissue paper.
uz: U menga bir marta qo'ng'iroq qilib, kiyimim uchun, shuningdek, shishaq qora kiyimdan yasalgan tunika uchun (u paytga kelib, uning qo'llari faqat chalk bilan chizilgan edi), lekin bugun u kiyimlarni tayyor holatda olib keldi, ularning oltin tugmalari to'qima qog'ozga o'rab olingan.

en: Donning the garments, and finding them splendid (notwithstanding that St.
uz: Kiyimlarni kiyib, ularni chiroyli ko'rish (shunga qaramay, St.

en: Jerome assured me that the back of the tunic wrinkled badly), I went downstairs with a complacent smile which I was powerless to banish from my face, and sought Woloda, trying the while to affect unconsciousness of the admiring looks of the servants, who came darting out of the hall and corridor to gaze upon me with ravished eyes.
uz: Jeronim meni kiyimning orqa qismi yomon burchaklanganini ta'kidladi), men o'zimni o'zimning ko'zimdan quvib chiqarolmayotgan o'zimning tabassumim bilan pastga tushib, Wolodaga murojaat qildim va o'shanda xizmatkorlarning hayratlanarli ko'rinishlariga befarq bo'lishga harakat qildim. Ular zal va koridordan dars bilan chiqib, menga ko'zlari quvib qarab turishdi.

en: Gabriel, the butler, overtook me in the salle, and, after congratulating me with much empressement, handed me, according to instructions from my father, four bank-notes, as well as informed me that Papa had also given orders that, from that day forth, the groom Kuzma, the phaeton, and the bay horse Krassavchik were to be entirely at my disposal.
uz: Butler Gabriel meni zalda kutib oldi va otamning ko'rsatmalariga ko'ra menga to'rtta bank notasini berdi va o'sha kundan boshlab kuyov Kuzma, faeton va bay otasi Krassavchik to'liq mening ixtiyorimda bo'lishi haqida otamning buyrug'ini berganini aytdi.

en: I was so overjoyed at this not altogether expected good-fortune that I could no longer feign indifference in Gabriel’s presence, but, flustered and panting, said the first thing which came into my head (“Krassavchik is a splendid trotter,” I think it was).
uz: Bu kutilmagan omaddan shunchalik xursand edimki, endi Gabrielning oldida befarqlikni ko'rsata olmasdim, lekin g'alati va ko'nglimdan nafas olib, boshimga kelgan birinchi narsani aytdim (Krassavchik ajoyib trotter, deb o'ylayman).

en: Then, catching sight of the various heads protruding from the doors of the hall and corridor, I felt that I could bear no more, and set off running at full speed across the salle, dressed as I was in the new tunic, with its shining gilt buttons.
uz: Keyin, zal va koridor eshiklaridan ko'rinadigan turli boshlarni ko'rib, ko'proq ko'ra olmasligimni his qildim va yangi tunika kiygan kiyimda, uning shiddatli oltin tugmalar bilan salonda to'liq tezlikda yugurishga tushdim.

en: Just as I burst into Woloda’s room, I heard behind me the voices of Dubkoff and Nechludoff, who had come to congratulate me, as well as to propose a dinner somewhere and the drinking of much champagne in honour of my matriculation.
uz: Woloda xonasiga kirganimda, orqamdan Dubkoff va Nechludoffning ovozlarini eshitdim, ular meni tabriklash uchun, bir joyda ovqatlanish va matrikulyatsiyamni sharaflash uchun ko'p shampan ichishni taklif qilishdi.

en: Dimitri informed me that, though he did not care for champagne, he would nevertheless join
uz: Dimitri menga shampaniyaga g'amxo'rlik qilmasa-da, unga qo'shilishini aytdi.

en: us that evening and drink my health, while Dubkoff remarked that I looked almost like a colonel, and Woloda omitted to congratulate me at all, merely saying in an acid way that he supposed we should now —i.e.
uz: O'sha kuni kechqurun bizni sog'lig'imni sug'orishga undadi, Dubkoff esa men polkovnik kabi ko'rinishimni aytadi va Woloda menga salom aytishni omon qoldiradi, faqat o'zi o'ylaganidek, biz endi i.e. deb aytishimiz kerakligini aytadi.

en: in two days time—be off into the country.
uz: Ikki kun ichida mamlakatga kirish vaqti.

en: The truth was that Woloda, though pleased at my matriculation, did not altogether like my becoming as grown-up as himself.
uz: Haqiqat shundaki, Voloda matrikulyatsiyadan mamnun bo'lsa-da, o'zi kabi katta bo'lishimni umuman yoqtirmagan.

en: Jerome, who also joined us at this moment, said in a very pompous manner that his duties were now ended, and that, although he did not know whether they had been well done or ill, at least he had done his best, and must depart to-morrow to his Count’s.
uz: O'sha paytda biz bilan birga bo'lgan Jerom ham o'z vazifasini tugatganini va yaxshi yoki yomon bajarilganini bilmasa-da, hech bo'lmaganda o'z kuchini yo'qotganini va ertaga o'z Countlariga jo'nab ketishi kerakligini juda o'zboshimchalik bilan aytdi.

en: In replying to their various remarks I could feel, in spite of myself, a pleased, agreeable, faintly self- sufficient smile playing over my countenance, as well as could remark that that smile, communicated itself to those to whom I was speaking.
uz: Ularning turli so'zlariga javob berganda, o'zimga qaramay, yuzimni quvonchli, yoqimli va kamdan-kam o'z-o'zidan yetarlicha ko'rinadigan tabassum sezishim mumkin edi va bu tabassum men gapirayotgan odamlarga o'zini o'zi yetkazishini aytishim mumkin edi.

en: So here was I without a tutor, yet with my own private drozhki, my name printed on the list of students, a sword and belt of my own, and a chance of an occasional salute from officials!
uz: Shunday qilib, men o'qituvchimsiz, ammo o'z shaxsiy drozhkim bilan, o'quvchilar ro'yxatida ismim yozilgan, o'zimning qilichim va qo'rqinchim va mansabdorlardan vaqti-vaqti bilan salom olish imkoniyatiga ega edim!

en: In short, I was grownup and, I suppose, happy.
uz: Qisqa qilib aytganda, men katta va baxtli bo'lganman.

en: Finally, we arranged to go out and dine at five o’clock, but since Woloda presently went off to Dubkoff’s, and Dimitri disappeared in his usual fashion (saying that there was something he MUST do before dinner), I was left with two whole hours still at my disposal.
uz: Nihoyat, biz beshlarda kechki ovqatga chiqishga qaror qildik, lekin Woloda Dubkoffsga ketgani sababli va Dimitri odatdagidek yo'qolgani sababli (o'sha kuni kechki ovqatdan oldin biror narsa qilish kerakligini aytadi), men hali ham ikki soatdan ortiq vaqtga ega bo'ldim.

en: For a time I walked through the rooms of the house, and looked at myself in all the mirrors—firstly with the tunic buttoned, then with it unbuttoned, and lastly with only the top button fastened.
uz: Bir muncha vaqt men uy xonadonlarini o'ylab, o'zimni barcha ko'rinmalarda ko'rdim, avval kiyimni tugmalar bilan, keyin uni tugmalar bilan, so'ng esa faqat yuqori tugma bilan bog'langan holda.

en: Each time it looked splendid.
uz: Har safar ajoyib ko'rinardi.

en: Eventually, though anxious not to show any excess of delight, I found myself unable to refrain from crossing over to the coach-house and stables to gaze at Krassovchik, Kuzma, and the drozhki.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, hech qanday ortiqcha zavq-shavqatni ko'rsatmaslikka harakat qilganimda, Krassovchik, Kuzma va drozhkilarga qarash uchun avtobusga va cho'nqalarga o'tishdan bosh tortolmadim.

en: Then I returned and once more began my tour of the rooms, where I looked at myself in all the mirrors as before, and counted my money over in my pocket—my face smiling happily the while.
uz: Keyin qaytib kelib, xonadonlarni bir bor ko'rib chiqdim va o'zimni avvalgidek ko'rinmalarda ko'rdim va pulimni poksamda hisoblab chiqdim.

en: Yet not an hour had elapsed before I began to feel slightly ennuye—to feel a shade of regret that no one was present to see me in my splendid position.
uz: Ammo bir soat ham o'tmay, o'zimni biroz bezovta his qila boshladim va o'zimni ajoyib holatda ko'rish uchun hech kim hozir bo'lmaganidan afsuslanaman.

en: I began to long for life and movement, and so sent out orders for the drozhki to be got ready, since I had made up my mind to drive to the Kuznetski Bridge and make some purchases.
uz: Hayot va harakatni orzu qila boshladim, shuning uchun drozhkilar tayyor bo'lishi uchun buyruqlar yubordim, chunki men Kuznetski ko'prisiga sayohat qilib, ba'zi xaridlarni qilishga qaror qildim.

en: In this connection I recalled how, after matriculating, Woloda had gone and bought himself a lithograph of horses by Victor Adam and some pipes and tobacco: wherefore I felt that I too must do the same.
uz: Shu munosabat bilan men Woloda matrikulasiyadan so'ng o'zi uchun Victor Adamning otli litografiyasi va bir nechta quvur va tamaki sotib olganini esladim: shuning uchun men ham xuddi shunday qilishim kerakligini his qildim.

en: Amid glances showered upon me from every side, and with the sunlight reflected from my buttons, cap-badge, and sword, I drove to the Kuznetski Bridge, where, halting at a Picture shop, I entered it with my eyes looking to every side.
uz: Har tarafdan menga ko'rinishlar yuzaga keldi va tugmalarim, to'plam va qilichlarimdan ko'rinadigan quyosh nuri bilan men Kuznetski ko'prisiga yetib keldim, u yerda rasmlar do'konida to'xtab, ko'zlarim har tarafga qaragan holda unga kirdim.

en: It was not precisely horses by Adam which I meant to buy, since I did not wish to be accused of too closely imitating Woloda; wherefore, out of shame for causing the obsequious shopmen such agitation as I appeared to do, I made a hasty selection, and pitched upon a water-colour of a woman’s head which I saw displayed in the window—price twenty roubles.
uz: Men to'g'ri ravishda Odamning otlarini sotib olishni xohlamagan edim, chunki men Wolodaga juda yaqin taqlid qilganlikda ayblanib qolishni istamasdim; shuning uchun men ko'rganidek, buzuq do'konchilar uchun shu qadar g'alati bo'lganimdan orzu qilib, shoshilinch tanlov qildim va o'n ikki rubl narxida oynada ko'rsatilgan bir ayolning boshining akvarolori ustida ko'rdim.

en: Yet no sooner had I paid the twenty roubles over the counter than my heart smote me for having put two such beautifully dressed shop-assistants to so much trouble for such a trifle.
uz: Ammo men 20 rubl pulni kassa orqali to'laganimdan so'ng, ikki chiroyli kiyim kiygan do'kon yordamchisini bunday kichiklik uchun haddan tashqari ko'p qiyinchiliklarga duchor qilganim uchun yuragim tushdi.

en: Moreover, I fancied that they were regarding me with some disdain.
uz: Bundan tashqari, ular menga nisbatan kamsitish ko'rsatayotganini his qildim.

en: Accordingly, in my desire to show them what manner of man I was, I turned my attention to a silver trifle which I saw displayed in a show- case, and, recognising that it was a porte-crayon (price eighteen roubles), requested that it should forthwith be wrapped in paper for me.
uz: Shunday qilib, men qanday inson ekanligimni ularga ko'rsatmoqchi bo'lganimda, bir ko'rgazmada ko'rsatilgan kumush maydonchaga e'tiborimni qaratdim va bu qalamni ko'tarib olishni tan olib, uni darhol qog'ozga o'rab olishni so'radim.

en: Next, the money paid, and the information acquired that splendid pipes and tobacco were to be obtained in an adjacent emporium, I bowed to the two shopmen politely, and issued into the street with the picture under my arm.
uz: Keyin pul to'langanidan so'ng, yaqin atrofdagi emporiumda ajoyib quvurlar va tamaki olish haqida ma'lumot topib, men ikki do'kon egasiga xushmuomalalik bilan sajda qilib, ko'chaga ko'chaga ko'tardim va qo'lim ostida rasm bor edi.

en: At the shop next door (which had painted on its sign-board a negro smoking a cigar) I bought (likewise out of a desire to imitate no one) some Turkish tobacco, a Stamboul hookah, and two pipes.
uz: Qo'shni do'konda (o'zining nishoncha-tavlasida sigaroni chekayotgan qora tanli bo'lgan) men (qaysidir odamga taqlid qilmaslik istagi bilan) turk tamaki, Stamboul hookah va ikkita quvur sotib oldim.

en: On coming out of the shop, I had just entered the drozhki when I caught sight of Semenoff, who was walking hurriedly along the pavement with his head bent down.
uz: Do'kondan chiqqanimda, men droshkiga kirganimda, Semenoffni ko'rdim, u boshini egib, piyoda bo'ylab shoshilinch yuribdi.

en: Vexed that he should not have recognised me, I called out to him pretty loudly, “Hold on a minute!” and, whipping up the drozhki, soon overtook him.
uz: U meni tanib-bilmasligi kerakligini anglab, men unga juda baland ovoz bilan: "Bir daqiqa turinglar!" - deb so'radim va drozhkiga cho'kib, tez orada uni ushlab qoldim.

en: “How do you do?” I said.
uz: Siz qanday yashayapsiz? dedim men.

en: “My respects to you,” he replied, but without stopping.
uz: "Senga hurmatim bor", deb javob berdi u, lekin to'xtamasdan.

en: “Why are you not in your University uniform?” I next inquired.
uz: Nima uchun siz o'zingizning universitet uniformangizda emassiz? Men keyingi savolni berdim.

en: At this he stopped short with a frown, and parted his white teeth as though the sun were hurting his eyes.
uz: Shu payt u ko'z o'g'li bilan to'xtadi va qora quyosh uning ko'zlarini og'ritayotganga o'xshab, oq tishlarini ajratib qo'ydi.

en: The next moment, however,
uz: Biroq, keyingi daqiqa

en: he threw a glance of studied indifference at my drozhki and uniform, and continued on his way.
uz: U o'rganilgan befarqlik ko'rinishida droshkim va uniformimga qarab, yo'lidan davom etdi.

en: From the Kuznetski Bridge, I drove to a confectioner’s in Tverskaia Street, and, much as I should have liked it to be supposed that it was the newspapers which most interested me, I had no choice but to begin falling upon tartlet after tartlet.
uz: Kuznetski ko'prasidan Tverskaia ko'chasidagi konditerxonaga bordim va, gazetani eng ko'p qiziqtirgan deb hisoblashni xohlagan bo'lsam-da, o'zimni tortletdan keyin tortletga tushishdan boshqa ilojim yo'q edi.

en: In fact, for all my bashfulness before a gentleman who kept regarding me with some curiosity from behind a newspaper, I ate with great swiftness a tartlet of each of the eight different sorts which the confectioner kept.
uz: Darhaqiqat, gazeta orqasidan menga qiziqarli munosabatda bo'lgan bir kishi oldida o'zimning o'ylamasligimga qaramay, men kekemchi saqlagan sakkiz turdagi har bir turdagi tortletni tezlik bilan yeb yubordim.

en: On reaching home, I experienced a slight touch of stomach-ache, but paid no attention to it, and set to work to inspect my purchases.
uz: Uyga qaytib kelganimda, men kichkina oshqozon og'rig'ini his qildim, lekin bunga e'tibor bermadim va xaridlarimni tekshirish uchun ishga tushdim.

en: Of these, the picture so much displeased me that, instead of having it framed and hung in my room, as Woloda had done with his, I took pains to hide it behind a chest of drawers, where no one could see it.
uz: Bu rasmlar menga shunchalik yoqmadiki, Woloda o'zidan qilganidek, uni o'zimning xonamda o'rnatish va asrashning o'rniga, uni hech kim ko'rmaydigan joyda qutidoqning orqasida yashirish uchun harakat qildim.

en: Likewise, though I also found the porte-crayon distasteful, I was able, as I laid it on my table, to comfort myself with the thought that it was at least a SILVER article—so much capital, as it were—and likely to be very useful to a student.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, agar men ham qalamni yoqimsiz deb bilsam ham, uni o'z stolimga qo'yganimda, hech bo'lmaganda SILVER maqolasi deb o'ylash bilan o'zimni tasalli berishga muvaffaq bo'ldim, chunki u katta kapitalga ega edi va talaba uchun juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: As for the smoking things, I decided to put them into use at once, and try their capabilities.
uz: Sigaret chekadigan narsalarga kelsak, men ularni darhol ishga tushirib, qobiliyatlarini sinab ko'rishga qaror qildim.

en: Unsealing the four packages, and carefully filling the Stamboul pipe with some fine-cut, reddish-yellow Turkish tobacco, I applied a hot cinder to it, and, taking the mouthpiece between my first and second fingers (a position of the hand which greatly caught my fancy), started to inhale the smoke.
uz: To'rtta paketni ochib, Stamboul quvurini yaxshi kesilgan, qizil sariq turk tamaki bilan to'ldirib, unga issiq cho'g' qo'ydim va og'zimni birinchi va ikkinchi barmoqlarim o'rtasida olib (qolning o'rnagi men uchun juda yoqimli bo'lgan) tutunni nafas oldim.

en: The smell of the tobacco seemed delightful, yet something burnt my mouth and caught me by the breath.
uz: Tütünning shiori yoqimli tuyulgan, ammo bir narsa og'zimni yondirib, nafasimni ushlab oldi.

en: Nevertheless, I hardened my heart, and continued to draw abundant fumes into my interior.
uz: Shunga qaramay, yuragimni qattiq qilib, ichki dunyomga ko'pgina tutunlarni jalb qilishni davom ettirdim.

en: Then I tried blowing rings and retaining the smoke.
uz: So'ngra men to'qnashuvlarni puflab, tutunni saqlab qolishga harakat qildim.

en: Soon the room became filled with blue vapours, while the pipe started to crackle and the tobacco to fly out in sparks.
uz: Tez orada xonada ko'k bug'lar paydo bo'ldi, qo'l tubiga o'q bo'lib, tamaki parcha-parcha bo'lib chiqib ketdi.

en: Presently, also, I began to feel a smarting in my mouth and a giddiness in my head.
uz: Shu paytdan boshlab og'zimda o'z-o'zimni o'zgartirgan va boshimda o'zgaruvchanlik paydo bo'ldi.

en: Accordingly, I was on the point of stopping and going to look at myself and my pipe in the mirror, when, to my surprise, I found myself staggering about.
uz: Shu sababli, o'zimni va o'z qo'lchog'imni aynada ko'rish uchun to'xtatmoqchi edim, ammo o'zimni hayratda qoldirganimda, o'zimni hayratda qoldirdim.

en: The room was whirling round and round, and as I peered into the mirror (which I reached only with some difficulty) I perceived that my face was as white as a sheet.
uz: Xona aylanib borar edi va o'ziga qarab ko'rinishda (men faqat biroz qiyinchilik bilan erishganman) yuzim varaq kabi oqligini payqadim.

en: Hardly had I thrown myself down upon a sofa when such nausea and faintness swept over me that, making
