uz: Men o'zimni sofada o'tirib o'tirganimdan so'ng, o'zimni o'sha-o'sha og'ir og'irlik va o'zimni o'ldirib yuborganimda, o'zimni o'zimga tashlab qo'ydim.

en: up my mind that the pipe had proved my death, I expected every moment to expire.
uz: O'limimni isbotlagan quvurni o'ylayman, har bir daqiqa o'tishini kutardim.

en: Terribly frightened, I tried to call out for some one to come and help me, and to send for the doctor.
uz: Men juda qo'rqib, kimdir menga yordam berishini va shifokorni chaqirib yuborishini so'rashga harakat qildim.

en: However, this panic of mine did not last long, for I soon understood what the matter with me was, and remained lying on the sofa with a racking headache and my limbs relaxed as I stared dully at the stamp on the package of tobacco, the Pipe-tube coiled on the floor, and the odds and ends of tobacco and confectioner’s tartlets which were littered about.
uz: Biroq, bu qo'rquv uzoq davom etmadi, chunki men tezda nima bo'lganini anglab, sofada o'tirib qoldim, bosh og'rig'i va qo'limlar tinchlanib, tamaki paketidagi po'pisaga, tuproqdagi quvurga va to'qimalar bilan to'qilgan tamaki va kek keklar tortillariga ko'z tikdim.

en: “Truly,” I thought to myself in my dejection and disillusionment, “I cannot be quite grown-up if I cannot smoke as other fellows do, and should be fated never to hold a chibouk between my first and second fingers, or to inhale and puff smoke through a flaxen moustache!” When Dimitri called for me at five o’clock, he found me in this unpleasant predicament.
uz: Haqiqatan ham,  Men tushkunlikka tushdim va umidsizlikka tushdim va o'zimga shunday o'yladim: "Agar men boshqa odamlarga o'xshab chekolmasam, katta bo'la olmayman va hech qachon birinchi va ikkinchi barmoqlarim o'rtasida chiboukni ushlab turmasam, yoki laxtli bo'lak orqali tutni nafas olib, puflasam kerak!" Dimitriy meni soat beshda chaqirganida, meni bu noqulay ahvolda topdi.

en: After drinking a glass of water, however, I felt nearly recovered, and ready to go with him.
uz: Biroq, bir stakan suv ichganimdan so'ng, o'zimni deyarli sog'ayib, u bilan birga ketishga tayyor his qildim.

en: “So much for your trying to smoke!” said he as he gazed at the remnants of my debauch.
uz: "Siz chekishga urinayotganingiz uchun shunchalik!" - dedi u, mening buzuqligimning qoldiqlariga qarab.

en: “It is a silly thing to do, and waste of money as well.
uz: Bu ahmoqona ish va pul sarflashdir.

en: I long ago promised myself never to smoke.
uz: Men o'zimga hech qachon chekmaslikka va'da berdim.

en: But come along; we have to call for Dubkoff.”
uz: Lekin kelinglar, Dubkoffni chaqirishimiz kerak.

en: HOW WOLODA AND DUBKOFF AMUSED THEMSELVES THE moment that Dimitri entered my room I perceived from his face, manner of walking, and the signs which, in him, denoted ill-humour— a blinking of the eyes and a grim holding of his head to one side, as though to straighten his collar—that he was in the coldly-correct frame of mind which was his when he felt dissatisfied with himself.
uz: Dimitri xonamga kirgan paytdan boshlab uning yuzidan, yurish usulidan va o'ziga xos qo'rqinchli belgilardan ko'rardim: ko'z burishish va boshini bir tomonga tiklash, xuddi o'z bo'ynini to'g'rilashdek, u o'zidan mamnun bo'lmaganida o'ziga tegishli bo'lgan sovuq-to'g'ri fikrlash tarzida edi.

en: It was a frame of mind, too, which always produced a chilling effect upon my feelings towards him.
uz: Bu esa o'z-o'zimga bo'lgan his-tuyg'ularimga doimo qo'rqinchli ta'sir ko'rsatadigan fikrlash tarzi edi.

en: Of late I had begun to observe and appraise my friend’s character a little more, but our friendship had in no way suffered from that, since it was still too young and strong for me to be able to look upon Dimitri as anything but perfect, no matter in what light I regarded him.
uz: So'nggi paytlarda men do'stimning xarakterini biroz ko'proq kuzatishni va baholashni boshlagan edim, ammo do'stligimiz bundan hech qanday zarar ko'rmagan edi, chunki Dimitriyni qanday ko'rinishda bo'lmasin, mukammal deb ko'rish uchun hali ham yosh va kuchli edim.

en: In him there were two personalities, both of which I thought beautiful.
uz: Uning ichida ikkita shaxs bor edi, ularning ikkalasi ham men uchun chiroyli edi.

en: One, which I loved devotedly, was kind, mild, forgiving, gay, and conscious of being those various things.
uz: Birini chin yurakdan sevardim, u mehribon, muloyim, kechirimli, gey va o'sha turli narsalarga ega bo'lgan.

en: When he was in this frame of mind his whole exterior, the very tone of his voice, his every movement, appeared to say: “I am kind and good-natured, and rejoice in being so, and every one can see that I so rejoice.” The other of his two personalities—one which I had only just begun to apprehend, and before the majesty of which I bowed in spirit—was that of a man who was cold, stern to himself and to others, proud, religious to the point of fanaticism, and pedantically moral.
uz: Bu holatda bo'lganida, uning butun tashqi ko'rinishi, ovozi va har bir harakatlari shunday bo'lib ko'rinardi: "Men mehribon va mehribonman va bunday bo'lishdan xursandman va hamma ham xursand ekanimni ko'rishadi.

en: At the present moment he was, as I say, this second personality.
uz: Hozirgi paytda u, aytganimdek, ikkinchi shaxs edi.

en: With that frankness which constituted a necessary condition of our relations I told him, as soon as we entered the drozhki, how much it
uz: O'z munosabatlarimizning zarur sharti bo'lgan bu ochiqlik bilan men unga drozhkiga kirganimizdan so'ng, qancha pul sarflanishini aytdim.

en: depressed and hurt me to see him, on this my fete-day in a frame of mind so irksome and disagreeable to me.
uz: Uni ko'rish meni tushkunlikka tushirdi va xafa qildi, chunki bu mening bayram kunim edi va bu men uchun juda noqulay va noqulay bo'lgan ruhda edi.

en: “What has upset you so?” I asked him.
uz: Sizni bu qadar xafa qilgan nima? Men undan so'radim.

en: “Will you not tell me?” “My dear Nicolas,” was his slow reply as he gave his head a nervous twitch to one side and blinked his eyes, “since I have given you my word never to conceal anything from you, you have no reason to suspect me of secretiveness.
uz: Menga aytmaysanmi?Soxim Nikolas, boshini bir tomonga urib, ko'zlarini cho'kib qo'yganida, uning sekin javobini berdi,Men sizga hech qachon mendan hech narsani yashirmaslikka va'damni berganim sababli, meni sirlilikda gumon qilishingiz uchun hech qanday sababingiz yo'q.

en: One cannot always be in exactly the same mood, and if I seem at all put out, that is all there is to say about it.” “What a marvellously open, honourable character his is!” I thought to myself, and dropped the subject.
uz: Hech kim har doim ham xuddi shunday ruhda bo'lishi mumkin emas va agar men umuman g'alati tuyulsam, bu haqda aytish kerak bo'lgan hamma narsa.U qanchalik ajoyib ochiq, hurmatli shaxs! Men o'zimga o'yladim va mavzuni qoldirdim.

en: We drove the rest of the way to Dubkoff’s in silence.
uz: Biz Dubkofflargacha qolgan yo'lni sukut saqlashda o'tkazdik.

en: Dubkoff’s flat was an unusually fine one—or, at all events, so it seemed to me.
uz: Dubkoffning xonadoni o'zgacha chiroyli edi, shuning uchun menga o'xshaydi.

en: Everywhere were rugs, pictures, gardenias, striped hangings, photographs, and curved settees, while on the walls hung guns, pistols, pouches, and the mounted heads of wild beasts.
uz: Har yerda xalchalar, rasmlar, gardeniyalar, bo'lakli asarlar, fotosuratlar va egri setlar bor edi, devorlarda esa qurollar, pilastonlar, sumkalar va yovvoyi hayvonlarning boshi o'rnatilgan edi.

en: It was the appearance of this apartment which made me aware whom, it was that Woloda had imitated in the scheme of his own sitting-room.
uz: Bu xonaning tashqi ko'rinishi meni kim, Woloda o'zining yashash xonasi dizaynida kimni taqlid qilganini tushunishga undagan.

en: We found Dubkoff and Woloda engaged in cards, while seated also at the table, and watching the game with close attention, was a gentleman whom I did not know, but who appeared to be of no great importance, judging by the modesty of his attitude.
uz: Dubkoff va Woloda kartalar bilan shug'ullanayotganini, shuningdek, stolda o'tirganini va o'yinni diqqat bilan kuzatayotganini ko'rdik.Men tanimagan, lekin o'z munosabatining kamtarligiga qarab, ahamiyatsiz ko'rinadigan bir gentleman edi.

en: Dubkoff himself was in a silk dressing-gown and soft slippers, while Woloda—seated opposite him on a divan—was in his shirtsleeves, as well as (to judge by his flushed face and the impatient, cursory glance which he gave us for a second as he looked up from the cards) much taken up with the game.
uz: Dubkoffning o'zi ipak kiyimida va yumshoq cho'tkalarda edi, Woloda esa uning o'ng tomonida o'tirgan divanida kiyim-kechaklarida edi va (o'zining qizargan yuziga qarab va kartalardan ko'tarib turgan bir soniya davomida bizga sabr-toqatli va ko'z-ko'z ko'rinishiga qarab) o'yin bilan juda band edi.

en: On seeing me, he reddened still more.
uz: Meni ko'rganida, u yanada qizardi.

en: “Well, it is for you to deal,” he remarked to Dubkoff.
uz: Eh, bu sizning ishingizdir, dedi u Dubkoffga.

en: In an instant I divined that he did not altogether relish my becoming acquainted with the fact that he gambled.
uz: Bir lahzada men uning qimor o'ynashidan zavqlanmayotganini tushundim.

en: Yet his expression had nothing in it of confusion—only a look which seemed to me to say: “Yes, I play cards, and if you are surprised at that, it is only because you are so young.
uz: Ammo uning ifodasida g'alati ko'rinish yo'q edi, faqat bir qarash menga shunday degan edi: "Ha, men karta o'ynayman va agar siz bunga hayron bo'lsangiz, bu sizning yoshligingiz tufayli.

en: There is nothing wrong about it—it is a necessity at our age.” Yes, I at once divined and understood that.
uz: Bunda hech qanday yomonlik yo'q, chunki bu bizning yoshimizdagi zaruriy narsa. Ha, men buni darhol tushundim va tushundim.

en: Instead of dealing, however, Dubkoff rose and shook hands with us; after which he bade us both be seated, and then offered us pipes, which we declined.
uz: Biroq, Dubkoff o'z ishi bilan shug'ullanishning o'rniga turib, qo'limizdan qo'l solib, ikkovimizga ham o'tirishni buyurdi va keyin bizga quvurlar taklif qildi, biz esa rad etdik.

en: “Here is our DIPLOMAT, then—the hero of the day!” he said to me, “Good Lord!
uz: Mana bizning Diplomatimiz, keyin kunning qahramoni! - dedi u menga. - Yaxshi Rabbim!

en: how you look like a colonel!” “H-m!” I muttered in reply, though once more feeling a complacent smile overspread my countenance.
uz: Siz polkovnikga o'xshaysiz!H-m! Men javobda qichqirdim, garchi yana bir bor o'zimni o'zim bilgan tabassum yuzimni qoplagan bo'lsa-da.

en: I stood in that awe of Dubkoff which a sixteen-year-old boy naturally feels for a twenty-seven-year-old man of whom his elders say that he is a very clever young man who can dance well and speak French, and who, though secretly despising one’s youth, endeavours to conceal the fact.
uz: O'n olti yoshli o'g'il o'n yettita yoshli yigitga nisbatan tabiiy ravishda his qiladigan Dubkoffga bo'lgan ehtiromimni ko'rdim, chunki uning kattalari uning juda aqlli yigit ekanligini, yaxshi raqs yuritishi va frantsuz tilida gapirishi mumkinligini va yashirincha o'z yoshligidan nafratlangan bo'lsa-da, buni yashirishga harakat qilayotganini aytishadi.

en: Yet, despite my respect for him, I somehow found it difficult and uncomfortable, throughout my acquaintanceship with him, to look him in the eyes, I have since remarked that there are three kinds of men whom I cannot face easily, namely those who are much better than myself, those who are much worse, and those between whom and myself there is a mutual determination not to mention some particular thing of which we are both aware.
uz: Biroq, unga bo'lgan hurmatimga qaramay, u bilan tanishib, uning ko'zlariga qarash men uchun qiyin va noqulay bo'ldi, keyinchalik men uch turdagi odamlarga osonlikcha duch kelolmasligimni aytdim: o'zimdan ancha yaxshiroq bo'lganlar, o'zimdan ancha yomonroq bo'lganlar va o'zim bilan o'zaro bir xil qarorga kelganlar, ikkovimiz ham o'zimiz bilgan biron bir narsani aytmaslikka qaror qildik.

en: Dubkoff may have been a much better fellow than myself, or he may have been a much worse; but the point was that he lied very frequently without recognising the fact that I was aware of his doing so, yet had determined not to mention it.
uz: Dubkoff mendan ancha yaxshiroq odam bo'lishi mumkin, yoki undan ham yomonroq bo'lishi mumkin; lekin u juda tez-tez yolg'on gapirgan, lekin men uning gapirishini bilardim, lekin buni aytmaslikka qaror qilgan edim.

en: “Let us play another round,” said Woloda, hunching one shoulder after the manner of Papa, and reshuffling the cards.
uz: Biz yana bir raund o'ynaylik, dedi Woloda, ota kabi bir shohni egib, kartalarni o'zgartiradi.

en: “How persistent you are!” said Dubkoff.
uz: "Qanday qattiqqo'lsan!" - dedi Dubkoff.

en: “We can play all we want to afterwards.
uz: Keyinchalik biz xohlagancha o'ynashimiz mumkin.

en: Well, one more round, then.” During the play, I looked at their hands.
uz: Xo'sh, yana bir raund. O'yin davomida ularning qo'llariga qaradim.

en: Woloda’s hands were large and red, whilst in the crook of the thumb and the way in which the other fingers curved themselves round the cards as he held them they so exactly resembled Papa’s that now and then I could not help thinking that Woloda purposely held the cards thus so as to look the more like a grownup.
uz: Woloda qo'llari katta va qizil edi, bosh barmog'ining burchakida va boshqa barmoqlar ularni ushlab turganida kartalarni o'rab olganida, ular Papalarga o'xshash edilar, shuning uchun vaqti-vaqti bilan men Woloda kattalarga o'xshashi uchun kartalarni qasddan ushlab turgani haqida o'ylashdan bosh tortmasdim.

en: Yet the next moment, looking at his face, I could see that he had not a thought in his mind beyond the game.
uz: Ammo keyingi daqiqada uning yuziga qaraganimda, o'yindan tashqaridagi fikrlari uning ongida yo'qligini ko'rdim.

en: Dubkoff’s hands, on the contrary, were small, puffy, and inclined to clench themselves, as well as extremely neat and small-fingered.
uz: Aksincha Dubkoffning qo'llari kichkina, puflangan va o'zlarini yopishishga moyil bo'lgan, shuningdek, nihoyatda bezakli va kichik barmoqli edi.

en: They were just the kind of hands which generally display rings, and which are most to be seen on persons who are both inclined to use them and fond of objets de vertu.
uz: Bular odatda do'konga ega bo'lgan qo'llar va ularni ishlatishga moyil bo'lgan va xayrli narsalarni yaxshi ko'radigan odamlarda ko'proq ko'rinadi.

en: Woloda must have lost, for the gentleman who was watching the play remarked that Vladimir Petrovitch had terribly bad luck, while
uz: Woloda g'olib bo'lishi kerak, chunki o'yinni tomosha qilayotgan xonim Vladimir Petrovitchning juda yomon omadga uchraganini aytdi.

en: Dubkoff reached for a note book, wrote something in it, and then, showing Woloda what he had written, said: “Is that right?” “Yes.” said Woloda, glancing with feigned carelessness at the note book.
uz: Dubkoff notlar daftarini oldiga olgach, u yerda biror narsa yozdi va keyin u nima yozganini Wolodaga ko'rsatib, shunday dedi: Ha, shundaymi? Ha, shundaymi? dedi Woloda. U notlar daftarini soxta ehtiyotsizlik bilan ko'ribdi.

en: “Now let us go.” Woloda took Dubkoff, and I gave Dimitri a lift in my drozhki.
uz: Endi ketaylik. Woloda Dubkoffni olib ketdi, men esa Dimitriyga droshkimda lift berdim.

en: “What were they playing at?” I inquired of Dimitri.
uz: Ular nima bilan o'ynashgan? - deb Dimitriydan so'radim.

en: It is a stupid game.
uz: Bu ahmoqona o'yin.

en: In fact, all such games are stupid.” “And were they playing for much?” “No, not very much, but more than they ought to.” “Do you ever play yourself?” “No; I swore never to do so; but Dubkoff will play with any one he can get hold of.” “He ought not to do that,” I remarked.
uz: Darhaqiqat, bunday o'yinlarning barchasi ahmoqlikdir. Va ular ko'p o'ynashganmi? Yo'q, ko'p emas, balki ular o'ynashlari kerak bo'lganidan ko'proq. O'zingiz o'zingiz o'ynashganmisiz? Yo'q; men hech qachon bunday qilmayman deb qasam ichgan edim; lekin Dubkoff qo'lga kiritadigan har bir kishi bilan o'ynashadi. U bunday qilmasligi kerak, Men shuni ta'kidladim.

en: “So Woloda does not play so well as he does?” “Perhaps Dubkoff ought not to, as you say, yet there is nothing especially bad about it all.
uz: Demak, Voloda o'zi kabi yaxshi o'ynamaydimi?Ehtimol Dubkoff o'zi aytgandek o'ynamasligi kerak, ammo bunda hech qanday yomonlik yo'q.

en: He likes playing, and plays well, but he is a good fellow all the same.” “I had no idea of this,” I said.
uz: U o'ynashni yaxshi ko'radi va yaxshi o'ynaydi, ammo u hali ham yaxshi odam.  Men buni bilmasdim, dedim.

en: “We must not think ill of him,” concluded Dimitri, “since he is a simply splendid fellow.
uz: "Biz unga yomon munosabatda bo'lmasligimiz kerak", - deb xulosa qildi Dimitriy, "chunki u shunchaki ajoyib odam.

en: I like him very much, and always shall like him, in spite of his weakness.” For some reason or another the idea occurred to me that, just BECAUSE Dimitri stuck up so stoutly for Dubkoff, he neither liked nor respected him in reality, but was determined, out of stubbornness and a desire not to be accused of inconstancy, never to own to the fact.
uz: Men uni juda yaxshi ko'raman va uning zaifligiga qaramasdan, har doim ham yaxshi ko'raman. Bir sababdan yoki boshqacha sababga ko'ra, Dimitriy Dubkoff uchun shunchalik qat'iy qo'llab-quvvatlaganligi sababli, u haqiqatda uni yoqtirmadi va hurmat ham qilmadi, balki o'z bo'shashligi va o'ziga qarshi noto'g'ri ish qilmaslik, hech qachon haqiqatga ega bo'lmaslikka qat'iy qaror qildi.

en: He was one of those people who love their friends their life long, not so much because those friends remain always dear to them, as because, having once—possibly mistakenly—liked a person, they look upon it as dishonourable to cease ever to do so.
uz: U do'stlarini umrbod sevgan odamlardan biri bo'lgan, nafaqat bu do'stlar ularga doimo yoqimli bo'lgani uchun, balki bir marta birovga noto'g'ri yoqib qolganidan keyin bunday qilishni to'xtatishni sharafsizlik deb bilgani uchun.

en: I AM FETED AT DINNER
uz: Men kechki ovqatda o'zimni qizdirganman.

en: Dubkoff and Woloda knew every one at the restaurant by name, and every one, from the waiters to the proprietor, paid them great respect.
uz: Dubkoff va Woloda restorandagi har bir kishini ismlari bilan tanishgan va har bir kishi, xizmatkorlardan boshlab, egasiga qadar ularga katta hurmat ko'rsatgan.

en: No time was lost in allotting us a private room, where a bottle of iced champagne-upon which I tried to look with as much indifference as I could—stood ready waiting for us, and where we were served with a most wonderful repast selected by Dubkoff from the French menu.
uz: Bizni alohida xonaga ajratishda vaqt o'tkazilmadi, u erda muzli shampanjon shishalari bo'lib, men uni ko'z o'ngimda ko'rishga harakat qildim va uni tayyorlab, bizni kutib turdim va Dubkoff tomonidan frantsuz menyusidan tanlangan ajoyib taom bilan xizmat qildik.

en: The meal went off most gaily and agreeably, notwithstanding that Dubkoff, as usual, told us blood-curdling tales of doubtful veracity (among others, a tale of how his grandmother once shot dead three robbers who were attacking her—a recital at which I blushed, closed my eyes, and turned away from the narrator), and that Woloda reddened visibly whenever I opened my mouth to speak —which was the more uncalled for on his part, seeing that never once, so far as I can remember, did I say anything shameful.
uz: Ovqat juda quvonchli va yoqimli o'tdi, ammo Dubkoff, odatdagidek, bizga shubhali haqiqatni o'z ichiga olgan qanoqli hikoyalarni aytib berdi (ba'zilar orasida, uning buvisi bir marta qizargan, ko'zimni yopgan va hikoyachiga yuz o'girgan uchta qaroqchini o'ldirganligi haqidagi hikoya) va Voloda men og'zimni ochganimda ko'rinadigan darajada qizarganini aytdi.

en: After we had been given champagne, every one congratulated me, and I drank “hands across” with Dimitri and Dubkoff, and wished them joy.
uz: Bizga shampan berishdan so'ng, hamma meni tabrikladi va men Dimitri va Dubkoff bilan qo'l o'girib ichdim va ularga quvonch tiladim.

en: Since, however, I did not know to whom the bottle of champagne belonged (it was explained to me later that it was common property), I considered that, in return, I ought to treat my friends out of the money which I had never ceased to finger in my pocket.
uz: Biroq, shampanj shisha kimga tegishliligini bilmaganim sababli (o'shanda bu umumiy mulk ekanligini tushuntirdim), men buning o'rniga do'stlarimga o'zim pokligimda qo'yib qo'ygan pullarimni berishim kerak deb o'yladim.

en: Accordingly, I stealthily extracted a ten-rouble note, and, beckoning the waiter to my side, handed him the money, and told him in a whisper (yet not so softly but that every one could hear me, seeing that every one was staring at me in dead silence) to “bring, if you please, a half- bottle of champagne.” At this Woloda reddened again, and began to fidget so violently, and to gaze upon myself and every one else with such a distracted air, that I felt sure I had somehow put my foot in it.
uz: Shuning uchun men yashirincha o'n rubllik notani olib qo'ydim va xizmatkorni yonimga chaqirtirib, pulni unga berdi va shoshib (hozir ham kam emas, lekin hamma meni eshitishi mumkin edi, chunki hamma o'limdan oldin menga ko'z tikib qarayotgan edi) iltimos, yarim shampan shisha olib kelishini aytdim. Shu payt Voloda yana qizarildi va o'zim va boshqalarning har biriga shunday qattiq qaray boshladi. O'zimni va boshqalarning har birini shu qadar chalg'itgan havo bilan ko'rib, shu qadar ishonch hosil qildimki, qaysidir yo'sin unga oyoqlarimni qo'ydim.

en: However, the half-bottle came, and we drank it with great gusto.
uz: Biroq, yarim shisha keldi va biz uni katta zavq bilan ichdik.

en: After that, things went on merrily.
uz: Shundan so'ng hamma narsa xursandchilik bilan davom etdi.

en: Dubkoff continued his unending fairy tales, while Woloda also told funny stories—and told them well, too—in a way I should never have credited him: so that our laughter rang long and loud.
uz: Dubkoff o'zining oxirigacha bo'lmagan hikoyalarini davom ettirgan, Woloda esa qiziqarli hikoyalarni aytib, yaxshi aytib bergan, men unga hech qachon e'tibor bermas edim: shunday qilib, bizning kulishimiz uzoq va baland ovoz bilan eshitildi.

en: Their best efforts lay in imitation, and in variants of a certain well-known saw.
uz: Ularning eng yaxshi sa'y-harakatlari namunaviy va mashhur bir pichoqning variantlarida bo'lgan.

en: “Have you ever been abroad?” one would say to the other, for instance.
uz: Siz chet elda bo'lganmisiz? Masalan, biri o'zgaga aytadi.

en: “No,” the one interrogated would reply, “but my brother plays the fiddle.” Such perfection had the pair attained in this species of comic absurdity that they could answer any question by its means, while they would also endeavour to unite
uz: Yo'q,  so'roq qilinayotgan kishi javob beradi,  lekin akam piyola o'ynaydi. Bu juftlik bu turdagi absurd komediyalarda shunday mukammallikka erishgan bo'lsa ediki, ular har qanday savolga uning yordamida javob bera olishardi, biroq ular ham birlashtirishga harakat qilishardi

en: two absolutely unconnected matters without a previous question having been asked at all, yet say everything with a perfectly serious face and produce a most comic effect.
uz: Oldingi savolni hech qachon so'ramagan holda, ikkita mutlaqo bog'liq bo'lmagan masala, lekin hamma narsani mukammal jiddiy yuz bilan aytish va juda kumik ta'sir ko'rsatish.

en: I too began to try to be funny, but as soon as ever I spoke they either looked at me askance or did not look at me until I had finished: so that my anecdotes fell flat.
uz: Men ham kulgili bo'lishga harakat qila boshladim, lekin gapirganimdan so'ng, ular menga kamtarlik ila qaraydilar yoki men bitguniga qadar menga qaramaydilar: shuning uchun anekdotlarim to'xtab ketadi.

en: Yet, though Dubkoff always remarked, “Our DIPLOMAT is lying, brother,” I felt so exhilarated with the champagne and the company of my elders that the remark scarcely touched me.
uz: Biroq Dubkoff har doim: "DIPLOMATimiz yolg'on gapiryapti, birodar", - deb aytgan bo'lsa-da, men shampan va oqsoqollarimning hamkorligi bilan shunchalik hayajonlangan edimki, bu fikr menga hech qanday ta'sir qilmadi.

en: Only Dimitri, though he drank level with the rest of us, continued in the same severe, serious frame of mind—a fact which put a certain check upon the general hilarity.
uz: Faqat Dimitri, biz bilan bir xil ichgan bo'lsa-da, o'sha jiddiy va jiddiy fikrlash tarzini davom ettirgan, bu esa umuman kulgili bo'lishiga muayyan chek qo'ydi.

en: “Now, look here, gentlemen,” said Dubkoff at last.
uz: Hndi, xo'jayinimlar, bu yerga qaranglar, - dedi Dubkoff nihoyat.

en: “After dinner we ought to take the DIPLOMAT in hand.
uz: Tushlikdan keyin biz diplomatni qo'limizda olishimiz kerak.

en: How would it be for him to go with us to see Auntie?
uz: U biz bilan qizimning oldiga borsa qanday bo'ladi?

en: There we could put him through his paces.” “Ah, but Nechludoff will not go there,” objected Woloda.
uz: U yerda uni o'z qadamlari orqali o'tkazishimiz mumkin.Ah, lekin Nechludoff u yerga bormaydi, deb rad etdi Woloda.

en: “O unbearable, insupportable man of quiet habits that you are!” cried Dubkoff, turning to Dimitri.
uz: Ey chidamsiz, chidamsiz, xotirjamlik odatlari bilan shug'ullanuvchi odam! Dubkoff o'zini Dimitriyga qaratdi.

en: “Yet come with us, and you shall see what an excellent lady my dear Auntie is.” “I will neither go myself nor let him go,” replied Dimitri.
uz: Ammo biz bilan birga keling va azizimning qanday ajoyib xotini ekanligini ko'rasiz. Men o'zim ham ketmayman, uni ham ketishiga yo'l qo'ymayman, - dedi Dimitriy.

en: Why, you yourself saw how he brightened up at the very mention of Auntie.” “It is not so much that I WILL NOT LET HIM go,” continued Dimitri, rising and beginning to pace the room without looking at me, “as that I neither wish him nor advise him to go.
uz: Oʻzingiz koʻrdingizmi, u oʻzi ham onasi haqida aytib oʻtganida qanchalik koʻngillari koʻtarildi. Men uni ketishiga yoʻl qoʻymayman, deb oʻylamayman, Dimitri davom etdi, oʻrnidan turib, menga qaramasdan xonadan yurishni boshladi, chunki men unga borishni xohlamayman va maslahat ham bermayman.

en: He is not a child now, and if he must go he can go alone—without you.
uz: U endi bola emas va agar borishi kerak bo'lsa, sizsiz yolg'iz borishi mumkin.

en: Surely you are ashamed of this, Dubkoff?—ashamed of always wanting others to do all the wrong things that you yourself do?” “But what is there so very wrong in my inviting you all to come and take a cup of tea with my Aunt?” said Dubkoff, with a wink at Woloda.
uz: Shubhasizki, siz bundan uyat chekasiz, Dubkoff?O'zingiz qilayotgan barcha noto'g'ri ishlarni boshqalar hamisha qilishlarini istashdan uyat chekasizmi?Ammo sizlarni hammamizni onam bilan birga choy ichishga taklif qilishimda nima yomonlik bor? deb Dubkoff Wolodaga yuz o'girib dedi.

en: “If you don’t like us going, it is your affair; yet we are going all the same.
uz: Agar biz ketishni yoqtirmasangiz, bu sizning ishingizdir; ammo biz hammamiz bir xil ketamiz.

en: Are you coming, Woloda?” “Yes, yes,” assented Woloda.
uz: Kelarmisiz, Voloda?Ha, ha, Voloda rozi bo'ldi.

en: “We can go there, and then return to my rooms and continue our piquet.” “Do you want to go with them or not?” said Dimitri, approaching me.
uz: Biz u yerga borishimiz mumkin, so'ngra xonamga qaytib, piketimizni davom ettirishimiz mumkin.  Siz ular bilan borishni xohlaysizmi yoki yo'qmi? - dedi Dimitriy menga yaqinlashib.

en: “No,” I replied, at the same time making room for him to sit down beside me on the divan.
uz: - Yo'q, - deb javob berdim men, bir vaqtning o'zida uning yonimda sofanada o'tirishi uchun joy yaratdim.

en: “I did not wish to go in any case, and since
uz: Men hech qanday holatda borishni istamaganman va o'sha paytdan boshlab

en: you advise me not to, nothing on earth will make me go now.
uz: Siz menga bunday qilmaslikni maslahat berasiz, chunki yer yuzidagi hech narsa meni endi ketishga majbur qila olmaydi.

en: Yet,” I added a moment later, “I cannot honestly say that I have NO desire to go.
uz: Biroq, bir muncha vaqt o'tgach, men ketishni istamayman, deb aytolmayman.

en: All I say is that I am glad I am not going.” “That is right,” he said.
uz: Men shunchaki ketmaganimdan xursandman, deb aytaman.Bu to'g'ri, dedi u.

en: “Live your own life, and do not dance to any one’s piping.
uz: O'zingizning hayotingizni o'tkazing va hech kimning qo'shiqlariga raqs qilmang.

en: That is the better way.” This little tiff not only failed to mar our hilarity, but even increased it.
uz: Bu eng yaxshi yo'l. Bu kichkina gap nafaqat o'z hiyla-nayrangimizni buzib qo'ymadi, balki uni ko'paytiradi.

en: Dimitri suddenly reverted to the kindly mood which I loved best— so great (as I afterwards remarked on more than one occasion) was the influence which the consciousness of having done a good deed exercised upon him.
uz: Dimitri to'satdan menga yoqqan mehribon ruhga qaytib keldi shunchalik katta (men keyinchalik bir necha marta aytganimdek) yaxshilik qilganligidan xabardor bo'lish uning ustiga ta'sir ko'rsatgan.

en: At the present moment the source of his satisfaction was the fact that he had stopped my expedition to “Auntie’s.” He grew extraordinarily gay, called for another bottle of champagne (which was against his rules), invited some one who was a perfect stranger into our room, plied him with wine, sang “Gaudeamus igitur,” requested every one to join him in the chorus, and proposed that we should and rink at the Sokolniki.
uz: Hozirgi paytda uning mamnunligi shundaki, u mening Auntiesga sayohatimni to'xtatdi. U juda gey bo'ldi, yana bir shampanj shishalarini chaqirdi (bu uning qoidalariga zid edi), mukammal begona odamni xonamizga taklif qildi, uni sharob bilan to'ldirdi, Gaudeamus igiturni kuyladi, hammani chorusga qo'shilishni iltimos qildi va biz ham Sokolnikida o'tirib turishni taklif qildi.

en: [Mews.] “Let us enjoy ourselves to-night,” he said with a laugh.
uz: [Mews.] Tuncha zavqlanaylik, dedi u kulish bilan.

en: “It is in honour of his matriculation that you now see me getting drunk for the first time in my life.” Yet somehow this merriment sat ill upon him.
uz: Bu uning matrikulasi munosabati bilan, siz mening hayotimda birinchi marta mast bo'lganimni ko'ryapsiz. Ammo qandaydir tarzda bu shodlik unga yomon ta'sir qildi.

en: He was like some good-natured father or tutor who is pleased with his young charges, and lets himself go for their amusement, yet at the same time tries to show them that one can enjoy oneself decently and in an honourable manner.
uz: U o'zining yoshlikdagi ishlaridan mamnun bo'lgan, o'zini ularning zavq-e'tiborida qoldirgan, ammo bir vaqtning o'zida ularga o'zini munosib va hurmatli tarzda zavqlantirishi mumkinligini ko'rsatishga harakat qilgan mehribon ota yoki o'qituvchisiga o'xshardi.

en: However, his unexpected gaiety had an infectious influence upon myself and my companions, and the more so because each of us had now drunk about half a bottle of champagne.
uz: Biroq, uning kutilmagan shodligi menga va do'stlarimga yuqumli ta'sir ko'rsatdi, ayniqsa, endi har birimiz yarim shampaniya shisha ichgan edik.

en: It was in this pleasing frame of mind that I went out into the main salon to smoke a cigarette which Dubkoff had given me.
uz: Men Dubkoff menga bergan sigaretni chekish uchun asosiy salonga mana shu yoqimli ruhda chiqdim.

en: In rising I noticed that my head seemed to swim a little, and that my legs and arms retained their natural positions only when I bent my thoughts determinedly upon them.
uz: O'shanda boshim biroz ko'tarilganini va oyoqlarim va qo'llarim faqat o'z fikrlarimni ularga qat'iy tiklaganimda tabiiy joylarini saqlab qolishini payqadim.

en: At other moments my legs would deviate from the straight line, and my arms describe strange gestures.
uz: Boshqa paytlarda oyoqlarim to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yo'nalishdan chetlatilgan va qo'llarim g'ayrioddiy harakatlarni tasvirlagan.

en: I concentrated my whole attention upon the members in question, forced my hands first to raise themselves and button my tunic, and then to smooth my hair (though they ruffled my locks in doing so), and lastly commanded my legs to march me to the door—a function which they duly performed, though at one time with too much
uz: Men butun e'tiborimni tegishli a'zolarga qaratdim, qo'llarimni avval o'zlarini ko'tarib, kiyimimni tugmalashga majbur qildim, so'ngra sochlarimni tekislashimga majbur qildim (agar ular bu bilan qulflarimni to'ldirib qo'yishsa ham), nihoyat, oyoqlarimga eshik tomon yurishni buyurdim, bu ular to'g'ri bajargan vazifadir, ammo bir vaqtning o'zida juda ko'p.

en: reluctance, and at another with too much ABANDON (the left leg, in particular, coming to a halt every moment on tiptoe).
uz: O'z xohishi bilan, yana bir safar esa juda ko'p ABANDON bilan (ayniqsa, chap oyoq to'g'ridan-to'g'ri to'xtab turadi).

en: Some one called out to me, “Where are you going to?
uz: Kimdir menga: "Qayerga ketyapsan?" - deb so'radi.

en: They will bring you a cigar-light directly,” but I guessed the voice to be Woloda’s, and, feeling satisfied, somehow, that I had succeeded in divining the fact, merely smiled airily in reply, and continued on my way.
uz: Ular sizga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri sigar chiroqini olib kelishadi, lekin men ovozimni Wolodas deb o'yladim va, qandaydir tarzda haqiqatni bilishga muvaffaq bo'lganimdan mamnun bo'lib, shunchaki javobda havo bilan tabassum qilib, yo'limni davom ettirdim.

en: THE QUARREL In the main salon I perceived sitting at a small table a short, squat gentleman of the professional type.
uz: THE QUARREL Bosh salonda men kichik bir stolda professional turdagi qisqa, squat gentleman o'tirganini ko'rdim.

en: He had a red moustache, and was engaged in eating something or another, while by his side sat a tall, clean-shaven individual with whom he was carrying on a conversation in French.
uz: Uning qizil mustasi bor edi va u biron-bir narsani yeyish bilan band edi, uning yonida esa baland, toza shavshan bo'lgan bir kishi o'tirgan edi va u bilan frantsuz tilida suhbatlashayotgan edi.

en: Somehow the aspect of these two persons displeased me; yet I decided, for all that, to light my cigarette at the candelabrum which was standing before them.
uz: Bir yo'l bilan bu ikki kishining tashqi ko'rinishi menga yoqmadi; lekin men, shunga qaramay, ularning oldida turgan chandelabrga sigaretimni yoqishga qaror qildim.

en: Looking from side to side, to avoid meeting their gaze, I approached the table, and applied my cigarette to the flame.
uz: Ularning ko'zlarini ko'rmaslik uchun, yonma-yon ko'rib, stolga yaqinlashib, sigaretimni olovga qo'ydim.

en: When it was fairly alight, I involuntarily threw a glance at the gentleman who was eating, and found his grey eyes fixed upon me with an expression of intense displeasure.
uz: O'zimni xohlamagan holda ovqatlanayotgan kishiga qaradim va uning och ko'zlari menga qattiq ranjitilgan holda ko'z tikib turardi.

en: Just as I was turning away his red moustache moved a little, and he said in French: “I do not like people to smoke when I am dining, my good sir.” I murmured something inaudible.
uz: Men o'zimni o'zgartirganimda, uning qizil mustasi biroz ko'tarildi va u frantsuz tilida shunday dedi: "Men ovqatlanayotganimda odamlarning chekishini yoqtirmayman, xudojo'y sir. Men eshitilmaydigan bir narsani g'iybat qildim.

en: “No, I do not like it at all,” he went on sternly, and with a glance at his clean-shaven companion, as though inviting him to admire the way in which he was about to deal with me.
uz: - Yo'q, bu menga umuman yoqmaydi, - dedi u qattiqqo'llik bilan, sochlarini toza tupurgan hamkoriga qarab, xuddi u menga qanday munosabatda bo'lishini hayratda qoldirmoqchi bo'lganidek.

en: “I do not like it, my good sir, nor do I like people who have the impudence to puff their smoke up one’s very nose.”
uz: Menga yoqmaydi, yaxshi sirim, shuningdek, o'z nuzini tutash uchun o'z tutunini puflashga haqoratli bo'lgan odamlarni yoqtirmayman.

en: By this time I had gathered that it was myself he was scolding, and at first felt as though I had been altogether in the wrong.
uz: O'shanda men uning o'zimni tanqid qilayotganini anglab yetdim va boshida men o'zimni mutlaqo noto'g'ri his qilganman.

en: “I did not mean to inconvenience you,” I said.
uz: Men sizga noqulaylik qilmoqchi emasdim, dedim.

en: “Well, if you did not suppose you were being impertinent, at least I did!
uz: Ha, agar siz o'zingizning o'ylamasligingizni tasavvur qilmasangiz, hech bo'lmaganda men shunday qildim!

en: You are a cad, young sir!” he shouted in reply.
uz: Siz o'g'ilsiz, yigit! deb javob berdi u.

en: “But what right have you to shout at me like that?” I exclaimed, feeling that it was now HE that was insulting ME, and growing angry accordingly.
uz: Ammo menga shunday qichqirish uchun sizda qanday huquq bor? Men endi U meni haqorat qilayotganini his etib, o'zimni g'azabga solib o'tdim.

en: “This much right,” he replied, “that I never allow myself to be overlooked by any one, and that I always teach young fellows like yourself their manners.
uz: U shunday javob berdi: "Men hech qachon o'zimni hech kimning nazaridan chetda qoldirishiga yo'l qo'ymayman va o'zingiz kabi yoshlarga odatlarini o'rgataman.

en: What is your name, young sir, and where do you live?” At this I felt so hurt that my teeth chattered, and I felt as though I were choking.
uz: Sizning ismingiz qanday, yosh sir, va qayerda yashayapsiz? Bu gap menga shunchalik og'riqli bo'ldiki, tishlarim qichqirib ketdi va o'zimni toshbo'ron qilgandek his qildim.

en: Yet all the while I was conscious of being in the wrong, and so, instead of offering any further rudeness to the offended one, humbly told him my name and address.
uz: Ammo shu vaqt davomida men noto'g'ri yo'l tutganimni bilardim, shuning uchun jabrlangan kishiga yanada shafqatsiz bo'lishning o'rniga, kamtarlik ila ism va manzilimni aytdim.

en: “And MY name, young sir,” he returned, “is Kolpikoff, and I will trouble you to be more polite to me in future.—However, You will hear from me again” (“vous aurez de mes nouvelles”—the conversation had been carried on wholly in French), was his concluding remark.
uz: Va mening ismim, yosh sir, u qaytib keldi, is Kolpikoff, va men kelajakda menga nisbatan ko'proq xushmuomala bo'lishingizni bezovta qilaman. Biroq, Siz mendan yana eshitasiz (vous aurez de mes nouvelles suhbat butunlay frantsuz tilida o'tkazilgan edi), uning yakuniy so'zlari edi.

en: To this I replied, “I shall be delighted,” with an infusion of as much hauteur as I could muster into my tone.
uz: Men bunga javob berdim: "Men zavqlanaman, o'z ovozimga imkon qadar balandlik bilan to'ldirib beraman".

en: Then, turning on my heel, I returned with my cigarette—which had meanwhile gone out—to our own room.
uz: So'ngra, to'plamni o'zgartirgan holda, sigaretimni olib qaytib keldim, u o'sha paytgacha o'z xonamizga ketib ketgan edi.

en: I said nothing, either to my brother or my friends, about what had happened (and the more so because they were at that moment engaged in a dispute of their own), but sat down in a corner to think over the strange affair.
uz: Men o'g'limga yoki do'stlarimga nima bo'lganini aytmadim (va ular o'zlarining o'zlarida bahslashayotganlari sababli) lekin burchada o'tirib, o'sha g'alati hodisani o'ylab ko'rdim.

en: The words, “You are a cad, young sir,” vexed me more and more the longer that they sounded in my ears.
uz: "Siz o'g'ilsiz, yigit", degan so'zlar quloqlarimda eshitilganidan ko'ra, meni ko'proq xafa qildi.

en: My tipsiness was gone now, and, in considering my conduct during the dispute, the uncomfortable thought came over me that I had behaved like a coward.
uz: Endi mening g'alatiligim yo'q edi va nizo paytida o'z xulq-atvorimni ko'rib chiqib, qo'rqinchli bo'lganim haqida noqulay fikr paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Yet what right had he to attack me?” I reflected.
uz: Ammo u menga hujum qilish uchun qanday huquqga ega edi? - deb o'yladim.

en: “Why did he not simply intimate to me that I was annoying him?
uz: Nega u menga shunchaki men uni bezovta qilayotganimni aytmadi?

en: After all, it may have been he that was in the wrong.
uz: Axir, u o'zi xato qilgan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Why, too, when he called me a young cad, did I not say to him, ‘A cad, my good sir, is one who takes
uz: Nima uchun, u meni yosh yigit deb ataganida, men unga: "Yaxshi xonim, yigit - o'zi o'zi o'ldiradi", - deb aytmadimmi?

en: Or why did I not simply tell him to hold his tongue?
uz: Yoki nega men unga shunchaki tilini tiyishni aytmadim?

en: That would have been the better course.
uz: Bu yaxshiroq yo'l bo'lar edi.

en: Or why did I not challenge him to a duel?
uz: Yoki nega men uni duellashishga taklif qilmadim?

en: No, I did none of those things, but swallowed his insults like a wretched coward.” Still the words, “You are a cad, young sir,” kept sounding in my ears with maddening iteration.
uz: Yo'q, men o'sha narsalarning hech birini qilmadim, lekin uning haqoratlarini qo'rqinchli qo'rqinch kabi yutib yubordim. Biroq, "Sen bir qotilsan, yosh sir", degan so'zlar quloqlarimda g'azablantiruvchi takrorlashlar bilan tovushlanardi.

en: “I cannot leave things as they are,” I at length decided as I rose to my feet with the fixed intention of returning to the gentleman and saying something outrageous to him —perhaps, also, of breaking the candelabrum over his head if occasion offered.
uz: Ikki borligimni shunday qoldira olmayman, oxir-oqibat men bu yigitga qaytish va unga g'azablantiruvchi gaplarni aytish niyatim bilan to'xtashga qaror qildim,agar imkoniyat bo'lsa, boshidagi chandelabrni sindirib tashlashim mumkin.

en: Yet, though I considered the advisability of this last measure with some pleasure, it was not without a good deal of trepidation that I re-entered the main salon.
uz: Biroq, men bu oxirgi choralarning tavsiya etilishini biroz zavq bilan ko'rib chiqsam ham, asosiy salonga qaytib kirganimda juda ham xavotirlanganman.

en: As luck would have it, M.
uz: Yaxshiyam, M..

en: Kolpikoff was no longer there, but only a waiter engaged in clearing the table.
uz: Kolpikoff endi u yerda yo'q edi, faqatgina stolni tozalashda band bo'lgan xizmatkor bor edi.

en: For a moment I felt like telling the waiter the whole story, and explaining to him my innocence in the matter, but for some reason or another I thought better of it, and once more returned, in the same hazy condition of mind, to our own room.
uz: Bir zum davomida men xizmatkorga butun hikoyani aytib, uning oldida aybsizligimni tushuntirishni istardim, lekin bir sababdan yoki boshqasi tufayli bu haqda yaxshiroq o'yladim va yana bir bor o'zimizning xonadamizga, xuddi shu g'alati holatda qaytib keldim.

en: “What has become of our DIPLOMAT?” Dubkoff was just saying.
uz: DIPLOMATimizga nima bo'ldi? Dubkoff shunchaki gapirgan edi.

en: “Upon him now hang the fortunes of Europe.” “Oh, leave me alone,” I said, turning moodily away.
uz: Avropaning taqdirlari endi uning ustiga bog'liq.Oh, meni tinch qo'ying, dedim men, ruhoniylik bilan yuz o'girib.

en: Then, as I paced the room, something made me begin to think that Dubkoff was not altogether a good fellow.
uz: Keyin, xonada o'tirganimda, Dubkoff umuman yaxshi odam emas deb o'ylashni boshladim.

en: “There is nothing very much to admire in his eternal jokes and his nickname of ‘DIPLOMAT,’” I reflected.
uz: Uning abadiy hazillarida va diplomat deb ataladigan laqabida hech narsa hayratlanarli emas, deb o'yladim.

en: “All he thinks about is to win money from Woloda and to go and see his ‘Auntie.’ There is nothing very nice in all that.
uz: U faqat Wolodan pul topib, oʻz onasini koʻrish haqida oʻylaydi.Bularning barchasida hech qanday yoqimli narsa yoʻq.

en: Besides, everything he says has a touch of blackguardism in it, and he is forever trying to make people laugh.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u aytgan har bir so'zning bir qismi qora qo'riqchilikka aylangan va u har doim odamlarni kulg'atishga harakat qilmoqda.

en: In my opinion he is simply stupid when he is not absolutely a brute.” I spent about five minutes in these reflections, and felt my enmity towards Dubkoff continually increasing.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, u mutlaqo qo'pol bo'lmaganida, u shunchaki ahmoqdir. Men bu fikrlarda besh daqiqa o'tkazdim va Dubkoffga bo'lgan dushmanligimni doimiy ravishda kuchaytirganini his qildim.

en: For his part, he took no notice of me, and that angered me the more.
uz: Uning o'rniga, u menga e'tibor bermadi va bu meni yanada ko'proq g'azabga soladi.

en: I actually felt vexed with Woloda and Dimitri because they went on talking to him.
uz: Aslida, men Woloda va Dimitri bilan gaplashmay qo'yganimdan xafa bo'ldim.

en: “I tell you what, gentlemen: the DIPLOMAT ought to be christened,” said Dubkoff suddenly, with a glance and a smile which seemed to me derisive, and even treacherous.
uz: Men sizga nima deyman, xonimlar: diplomat suvga cho'mish kerak, dedi Dubkoff birdan, menga masxara va hatto xiyonat qiluvchi ko'rinadigan ko'z va tabassum bilan.

en: “Yet, O Lord, what a poor specimen he is!”
uz: Ammo, Rabbim, u qanday ham kambag'al namuna!

en: “You yourself ought to be christened, and you yourself are a sorry specimen!” I retorted with an evil smile, and actually forgetting to address him as “thou.” [In Russian as in French, the second person singular is the form of speech used between intimate friends.] This reply evidently surprised Dubkoff, but he turned away good- humouredly, and went on talking to Woloda and Dimitri.
uz: Siz o'zingiz suvga cho'mishingiz kerak, va siz o'zingiz ham o'zingizdan afsus namuna bo'lasiz! Men yomon tabassum bilan javob berdim va aslida unga thou deb murojaat qilishni unutib qo'ydim. [Rus tilida ham, frantsuz tilida ham, ikkinchi shaxs singular - yaqin do'stlar o'rtasida ishlatiladigan nutq shakli.] Ushbu javob Dubkoffni ajablantirib qo'ydi, ammo u xushmuomalalik bilan yuz o'girdi va Voloda va Dimitriy bilan suhbatni davom ettirdi.

en: I tried to edge myself into the conversation, but, since I felt that I could not keep it up, I soon returned to my corner, and remained there until we left.
uz: Men suhbatga o'zimni jalb qilishga harakat qildim, lekin davom eta olmasligimni his qilganim uchun tez orada burchimga qaytdim va ketmagunimizcha o'sha yerda qoldim.

en: When the bill had been paid and wraps were being put on, Dubkoff turned to Dimitri and said: “Whither are Orestes and Pedalion going now?
uz: Hisobvaraq to'langanidan so'ng Dubkoff Dimitriyga qarab: "Orestes va Pedalion endi qayerga ketmoqdalar?" - deb so'radi.

en: Home, I suppose, to talk about love.
uz: Uyda, men o'ylaymanki, sevgi haqida gapirish uchun.

en: Well, let US go and see my dear Auntie.
uz: Xo'sh, bizlar borib, azizimni ko'ramiz.

en: That will be far more entertaining than your sour company.” “How dare you speak like that, and laugh at us?” I burst out as I approached him with clenched fists.
uz: Bu sizning qaynoq kompaniyangizdan ko'ra ko'proq qiziqarli bo'ladi.  Qanday qilib siz shunday gapirib, bizga kulishishga jur'at qilasiz? Men unga yaqinlashayotganimda o'zimni qo'lga oldim.

en: “How dare you laugh at feelings which you do not understand?
uz: Qanday qilib siz tushunmagan his-tuyg'ularga kulishga jur'at qilasiz?

en: I will not have you do it!
uz: Men buni sizga qilmaslikka ruxsat bermayman!

en: Hold your tongue!” At this point I had to hold my own, for I did not know what to say next, and was, moreover, out of breath with excitement.
uz: Tilingizni tutib turing! Shu payt men o'zimni tutib turishim kerak edi, chunki keyingi so'zlarimni bilmasdim va, bundan tashqari, hayajondan nafasim ketardi.

en: At first Dubkoff was taken aback, but presently he tried to laugh it off, and to take it as a joke.
uz: Dubkoff dastlab hayratga tushdi, lekin hozirda u o'zini o'yin-kulgidan o'tkazishga harakat qildi va uni o'yin sifatida qabul qildi.

en: Finally I was surprised to see him look crestfallen, and lower his eyes.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, uni ko'rib hayron qoldim, ko'zlarini pastga tushirdi.

en: “I NEVER laugh at you or your feelings.
uz: Men SENGA ham, sizning his-tuyg'ularingizga ham hech qachon kulmayman.

en: It is merely my way of speaking,” he said evasively.
uz: Bu shunchaki mening so'zlash uslubim, - dedi u o'zidan qochib.

en: “Indeed?” I cried; yet the next moment I felt ashamed of myself and sorry for him, since his flushed, downcast face had in it no other expression than one of genuine pain.
uz: Haqiqatan ham? Men yig'ladim; lekin keyingi daqiqada o'zimdan uyaldim va u uchun achinardim, chunki uning qizil va tushkun yuzida haqiqiy og'riqdan boshqa ifodasi yo'q edi.

en: “What is the matter with you?” said Woloda and Dimitri simultaneously.
uz: Senga nima bo'ldi? - dedi Woloda va Dimitriy bir vaqtning o'zida.

en: “No one was trying to insult you.” “Yes, he DID try to insult me!” I replied.
uz: Senga hech kim haqorat qilmoqchi emasdi.Ha, U meni haqorat qilishga uringan! Men javob berdim.

en: “What an extraordinary fellow your brother is!” said Dubkoff to Woloda.
uz: O'g'ling qanday ajoyib odam! Dubkoff Wolodaga dedi.

en: At that moment he was passing out of the door, and could not have heard what I said.
uz: O'sha paytda u eshikdan o'tib ketayotgan edi va men nima deyayotganimni eshitmagan edi.

en: Possibly I should have flung myself after him and offered him further insult, had it not been that just at that moment the waiter who had witnessed my encounter with Kolpikoff handed me my greatcoat, and I at once quietened down—merely making such a pretence of having had a difference with Dimitri as
uz: Ehtimol, men o'zimni uning orqasidan tashlab, unga yana haqorat qilishim kerak edi, agar o'sha paytda Kolpikoff bilan uchrashishimga guvoh bo'lgan xizmatkor menga ko'ylagimni berdi, men esa darhol tinchlanib, Dimitri bilan farq qilganimni ko'rsatdim.

en: was necessary to make my sudden appeasement appear nothing extraordinary.
uz: O'shanda, mening to'satdan o'zimni xotirjam tutishim hech qanday g'alati narsa emasdek ko'rinishi uchun bu kerak edi.

en: Next day, when I met Dubkoff at Woloda’s, the quarrel was not raked up, yet he and I still addressed each other as “you,” and found it harder than ever to look one another in the face.
uz: Ertasi kuni Dubkoff bilan Wolodasda uchrashganimda, bahs ko'payib ketmadi, ammo u va men hali ham bir-birimizga "siz" deb murojaat qilardik va bir-birimizga oldinga qaray olish har qachongidan ham qiyin kechdi.

en: The remembrance of my scene with Kolpikoff—who, by the way, never sent me “de ses nouvelles,” either the following day or any day afterwards—remained for years a keen and unpleasant memory.
uz: Kolpikoff bilan yuz bergan voqeani eslab qolish, albatta, keyingi kun yoki undan keyingi kunlarda menga hech qachon yangiliklar yuborgan emas, yillar davomida o'ta qizg'in va yoqimsiz xotira bo'lib qoldi.

en: Even so much as five years after it had happened I would begin fidgeting and muttering to myself whenever I remembered the unavenged insult, and was fain to comfort myself with the satisfaction of recollecting the sort of young fellow I had shown myself to be in my subsequent affair with Dubkoff.
uz: Hatto besh yil o'tgach ham, o'zimga qasd qilmagan haqoratni eslab qolsam, o'zimni tashvishlantirib, o'zimga g'amginlik bilan gapira boshladim va Dubkoff bilan bo'lgan keyingi ishimda o'zimni qanday yosh odam deb ko'rsatganimni eslab, o'zimni mamnuniyat bilan tasalli berardim.

en: In fact, it was only later still that I began to regard the matter in another light, and both to recall with comic appreciation my passage of arms with Kolpikoff, and to regret the undeserved affront which I had offered my good friend Dubkoff.
uz: Darhaqiqat, keyinroq bu mavzuga boshqacha qarashni boshladim va Kolpikoff bilan qo'l urishimni qo'rqinchli tarzda eslab qolish va yaxshi do'stim Dubkoffga taqdim etgan o'ziga yarasha haqoratdan afsuslanish uchun ham.

en: When, at a later hour on the evening of the dinner, I told Dimitri of my affair with Kolpikoff, whose exterior I described in detail, he was astounded.
uz: Kechki kechki ovqat kechasi bir soatdan so'ng Kolpikoff bilan bo'lgan munosabatimni Dimitriyga aytib bersam, uning tashqi ko'rinishini batafsil tasvirlaganimda, u hayron qoldi.

en: “That is the very man!” he cried.
uz: "Bu aynan o'sha odam!" - deb baqirdi u.

en: “Don’t you know that this precious Kolpikoff is a known scamp and sharper, as well as, above all things, a coward, and that he was expelled from his regiment by his brother officers because, having had his face slapped, he would not fight?
uz: Siz bilmaysizmi, ushbu aziz Kolpikoff mashhur bir qo'pol va o'ta o'g'ri, eng asosiysi esa qo'rqinchli, u o'z birodar ofitserlari tomonidan o'z regimentidan quvib chiqarilgan, chunki u yuzidan urilganidan so'ng jang qilmagan?

en: But how came you to let him get away?” he added, with a kindly smile and glance.
uz: Ammo qanday qilib unga qochib ketishga ruxsat berdingiz? - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u mehribon tabassum va ko'z o'ngida.

en: “Surely he could not have said more to you than he did when he called you a cad?” “No,” I admitted with a blush.
uz: Shuni aytish kerakki, u sizga o'g'il deb aytganidan ko'ra ko'proq gapirishi mumkin emas edi.Yo'q,Men bu gapni o'z ko'zim bilan tan oldim.

en: “Well, it was not right, but there is no great harm done,” said Dimitri consolingly.
uz: "To'g'ri yo'q edi, lekin katta zarar yetkazilmagan", - dedi Dimitriy tasalli beruvchi tarzda.

en: Long afterwards, when thinking the matter over at leisure, I suddenly came to the conclusion that it was quite possible that Kolpikoff took the opportunity of vicariously wiping off upon me the slap in the face which he had once received, just as I myself took the opportunity of vicariously wiping off upon the innocent Dubkoff the epithet “cad” which Kolpikoff had just applied to me.
uz: Ko'p vaqt o'tgach, bu haqda o'ylash paytida to'satdan xulosaga keldimki, Kolpikoff bir paytlar yuzidagi tovushni menga o'chirib tashlash imkoniyatiga ega bo'lishi mumkin edi, xuddi men o'zim ham aybsiz Dubkoffga Kolpikoff menga qo'llagan epitetni o'chirib tashlash imkoniga ega bo'lganimdek.

en: I GET READY TO PAY SOME CALLS On awaking next morning my first thoughts were of the affair with Kolpikoff.
uz: Keyingi kuni ertalab uyg'onganimda, birinchi o'ylarim Kolpikoff bilan bo'lgan muomala haqida edi.

en: Once again I muttered to myself and stamped about the room, but there was no help for it.
uz: Men yana o'zimga g'iybat qilib, xonadon atrofini bosib o'tdim, ammo bu menga hech qanday yordam bermadi.

en: To-day was the last day that I was to spend in Moscow, and it was to be spent, by Papa’s orders, in my paying a round of calls which he had written out for me on a piece of paper—his first solicitude on our account being not so much for our morals or our education as for our due observance of the convenances.
uz: Bugun Moskvada o'tkazishim kerak bo'lgan oxirgi kun bo'ldi va bu kunni bobamning buyrug'iga binoan, u menga qog'oz ustiga yozgan qo'ng'iroqlarni to'lashim uchun sarflashim kerak edi.Buning birinchi qiziqishi bizning axloqanimiz yoki ta'limimiz uchun emas, balki majlislarga amal qilishimiz uchun edi.

en: On the piece of paper was written in his swift, broken hand-writing: “(ൢ) Prince Ivan Ivanovitch WITHOUT FAIL; (ൣ) the Iwins WITHOUT FAIL; (൤) Prince Michael; (൥) the Princess Nechludoff and Madame Valakhina if you wish.” Of course I was also to call upon my guardian, upon the rector, and upon the professors.
uz: Qog'ozda uning tezkor, buzilgan qo'li yozuvi bilan quyidagilar yozilgan edi: () Kuniga Ivan Ivanovitch FAILsiz; () Iwins FAILsiz; () Kuniga Michael; () Prince Nechludoff va Madam Valakhina, agar xohlasangiz. Albatta, men ham o'z vasiyimni, rektorni va professorlarni chaqirishim kerak edi.

en: These last-mentioned calls, however, Dimitri advised me not to pay: saying that it was not only unnecessary to do so, but not the thing.
uz: Biroq, Dimitri so'nggi marta aytib o'tilgan qo'ng'iroqlarimni to'lamaslikni maslahat berdi: nafaqat kerak emas, balki kerak emasligini aytdi.

en: However, there were the other visits to be got through.
uz: Biroq, boshqa tashriflar o'tkazilishi kerak edi.

en: It was the first two on the list—those marked as to be paid “WITHOUT FAIL”—that most alarmed me.
uz: Ro'yxatdagi birinchi ikki kishi, ular uchun to'lov to'lash kerak deb belgilanganda, meni eng ko'p xavotirga solgan edi.

en: Prince Ivan Ivanovitch was a commander-in-chief, as well as old, wealthy, and a bachelor.
uz: Prince Ivanoviç bosh qo'mondon, shuningdek, keksa, boy va bachelor edi.

en: Consequently, I foresaw that vis-a-vis conversation between him and myself—myself a sixteen-year-old student!—was not likely to be interesting.
uz: Natijada, o'n olti yoshli talaba sifatida o'zim bilan uning o'rtasidagi suhbat qiziqarli bo'lmasligini ko'rdim.

en: As for the Iwins, they too were rich—the father being a departmental official of high rank who had only on one occasion called at our house during my grandmother’s time.
uz: Iwinlar haqida gap ketganda, ular ham boy edilar, otasi yuqori darajadagi idoraviy mansabdor shaxs bo'lgan va buvimning davrida faqat bir marta uyimizga tashrif buyurgan.

en: Since her death, I had remarked that the younger Iwin had fought shy of us, and seemed to give himself airs.
uz: Uning o'limidan buyon kichik Iwin bizdan qo'rqqanini va o'ziga havo berayotganini aytdim.

en: The elder of the pair, I had heard, had now finished his course in jurisprudence, and gone to hold a post in St.
uz: Men eshitganimcha, bu juftlikning oqsoqollari yurisprudensiya kursini tugatgan va St. Petersburgda lavozimga tayinlangan.

en: Petersburg, while his brother Sergius (the former object of my worship) was also in St.
uz: Uning ukasi Sergiy (ilgari men topinadigan ob'ekt) ham Sankt-Peterburgda bo'lganida.

en: Petersburg, as a great fat cadet in the Corps of Pages.
uz: Sankt-Peterburgda "Sifkalar qo'shinida" katta semiz kadet sifatida.

en: When I was a young man, not only did I dislike intercourse with people who thought themselves above me, but such intercourse was, for me, an unbearable torture, owing partly to my constant dread of being snubbed, and partly to my straining every faculty of my intellect to prove to such people my independence.
uz: Yosh bo'lganimda, o'zimni mendan ustun deb hisoblagan odamlar bilan jinsiy aloqada bo'lishdan nafratlanardim, balki bunday aloqada bo'lish men uchun chiday olmaydigan azob edi, qisman o'zimni rad etishdan qo'rqqanimdan va qisman o'zimning mustaqilligimni isbotlash uchun aql-idrokimning har bir kuchi bilan harakat qilganimdan.

en: Yet, even if I failed to fulfil the latter part of my father’s instructions, I felt that I must carry out the former.
uz: Biroq, agar men otamning buyrug'ining ikkinchi qismini bajarmasam ham, avvalgilarini bajarishim kerakligini his qildim.

en: I paced my room and eyed my clothes ready disposed on chairs—the tunic, the sword, and the cap.
uz: O'zimning xonadamni o'zgartirdim va kiyim-kechakimni o'rindiqlarga tayyorlab qo'yganimni ko'rdim - tunika, qilich va to'pka.

en: Just as I was about to set forth, old Grap called to congratulate me, bringing with him Ilinka.
uz: Men ketmoqchi bo'lganimda, keksa Grap meni tabriklash uchun chaqirib, Ilinkani o'zi bilan birga olib keldi.

en: Grap pere was a Russianised German and an intolerably effusive, sycophantic old man who was more often than not tipsy.
uz: Grap pere ruslashtirilgan nemis va ko'pincha ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan, ko'p o'tirgan va ko'p o'tirgan keksa kishi edi.

en: As a rule, he visited us only when he wanted to ask for something, and although Papa sometimes entertained him in his study, old Grap never came to dinner with us.
uz: Odatda, u bizdan faqat bir narsa so'rashni istaganida tashrif buyurardi va otam ba'zan uni o'z studiyasida o'tkazgan bo'lsa-da, keksa Grap hech qachon biz bilan kechki ovqatga kelmadi.

en: With his subserviency and begging propensities went such a faculty of good-humour and a power of making himself at home that every one looked upon his attachment to us as a great honour.
uz: Uning xizmatkorligi va yolvorishga bo'lgan moyilligi bilan birga o'zini o'zini uyda his qilish qobiliyati va humor qobiliyati shunchalik kuchli bo'lganki, har bir kishi biz bilan bog'liqligini katta sharaf deb bilgan.

en: For my part, however, I never liked him, and felt ashamed when he was speaking.
uz: Ammo men hech qachon uni yoqtirmadim va u gapirganda o'zimni sharmanda his qilardim.

en: I was much put out by the arrival of these visitors, and made no effort to conceal the fact.
uz: Bu tashrif buyuruvchilar kelganidan juda xafa bo'ldim va buni yashirish uchun hech qanday harakat qilmadim.

en: Upon Ilinka I had been so used to look down, and he so used to recognise my right to do so, that it displeased me to think that he was now as much a matriculated student as myself.
uz: Ilinkaga ko'ra, men juda pastga qarab ko'rishga odatlangan edim va u mening bunday qilish huquqimni tan olgani uchun, hozir u ham men kabi matrikulyatsiya olgan talaba bo'lganini o'ylashdan norozi bo'ldim.

en: In some way he appeared to me to have made a POINT of attaining that equality.
uz: Bir yo'l bilan u menga tenglikka erishish yo'lida POINTni yaratgani ko'rinardi.

en: I greeted the pair coldly, and, without offering them any refreshment (since it went against the grain to do so, and I thought they could ask for anything, if they wanted it, without my first inviting them to state their requirements), gave orders for the drozhki to be got ready.
uz: Men bu juftlikni sovuqlik bilan kutib oldim va ularga biron-bir ichimlik taklif qilmasdan (shuning uchun buni qilish qonunga zid bo'lgan va ular istasalar, istalgan narsadan so'rashlari mumkin deb o'yladim, lekin ularni talablarini aytishga taklif qilmasdan), drozhki tayyorlanishini buyurdim.

en: Ilinka was a good- natured, extremely moral, and far from stupid young fellow; yet, for all that, what people call a person of moods.
uz: Ilinka yaxshi tabiatli, nihoyatda axloqiy va ahmoq yosh yigitdan uzoq edi; ammo, bularning barchasi uchun odamlar ruhning odam deb atagan.

en: That is to say, for no apparent reason he was for ever in some PRONOUNCED frame of mind—now lachrymose, now frivolous, now touchy on the very smallest point.
uz: Ya'ni, hech qanday sababsiz, u abadiy ravishda biron bir PRONOUNCED fikrlash tarzida bo'lgan, endi lacrymose, endi yengil, endi eng kichik nuqtada ham sezgir edi.

en: At the present moment he appeared to be in the last- named mood.
uz: Hozirgi paytda u oxirgi nufuzda bo'lgan ko'rinardi.

en: He kept looking from his father to myself without speaking, except when directly addressed, at which times he smiled the self-deprecatory, forced smile under which he was accustomed
uz: U otasidan o'zimga qarab gapirmas edi, faqat to'g'ridan-to'g'ri murojaat qilganda, o'zini kamsitadigan, o'zini majburlaydigan tabassum bilan tabassum qilardi.

en: to conceal his feelings, and more especially that feeling of shame for his father which he must have experienced in our house.
uz: O'z his-tuyg'ularini yashirish uchun, ayniqsa, otasi uchun o'z uyimizda o'tkazgan o'sha sharmandalik his-tuyg'usini yashirish uchun.

en: “So, Nicolas Petrovitch,” the old man said to me, following me everywhere about the room as I went through the operation of dressing, while all the while his fat fingers kept turning over and over a silver snuff-box with which my grandmother had once presented me, “as soon as ever I heard from my son that you had passed your examinations so well (though of course your abilities are well-known to everyone), I at once came to congratulate you, my dear boy.
uz: Nikolas Petroviç menga shunday dedi: "Nikolas Petroviç, men o'zimni kiyish operatsiyasidan o'tayotganimda, keksa odam menga orqamdan ergashib, yonma-yon qaytarib turardi, bu bilan buvim menga bir marta ko'p kumush sovg'alarni taqdim etgan edi, - o'g'limdan siz imtihonlaringizni juda yaxshi o'tkazdingiz, deb eshitganimdan so'ng (agar sizning qobiliyatingiz, albatta, hamma uchun ma'lum bo'lsa-da), men darhol sizni tabriklashga keldim, aziz o'g'lim.

en: Why, I have carried you on my shoulders before now, and God knows that I love you as though you were my own son.
uz: Chunki men seni allaqachon omonimda ko'tarib kelganman va Xudo biladiki, seni o'zimning o'g'limdek sevaman.

en: My Ilinka too has always been fond of you, and feels quite at home with you.” Meanwhile the said Ilinka remained sitting silently by the window, apparently absorbed in contemplation of my three-cornered cap, and every now and then angrily muttering something in an undertone.
uz: Mening Ilinka ham doimo sen bilan do'st bo'lib kelgan va o'zini sen bilan o'zini yaxshi his qilgan. O'sha paytda Ilinka o'sha paytgacha o'rinsiz o'tirgan, ehtimol uch burchakli to'plamni ko'rib o'tirgan va vaqti-vaqti bilan g'azab bilan bir narsani o'z so'zlarida g'ayrat bilan gapirgan.

en: “Now, I also wanted to ask you, Nicolas Petrovitch.” His father went on, “whether my son did well in the examinations?
uz: Hndi men ham sizdan, Nikolas Petrovitchdan so'rashni xohladim. Uning otasi davom etdi, o'g'lim imtihonlarda yaxshi o'tdimi?

en: He tells me that he is going to be in the same faculty as yourself, and that therefore you will be able to keep an eye on him, and advise him, and so on.” “Oh, yes, I suppose he passed well,” I replied, with a glance at Ilinka, who, conscious of my gaze, reddened violently and ceased to move his lips about.
uz: U menga o'zingiz kabi fakultetda bo'lishini va shuning uchun siz uni kuzatib turishingiz, maslahat berishingiz va shunga o'xshash narsalar haqida aytadi.Oh, ha, men o'ylaymanki, u yaxshi o'tdi, Men Ilinkaga qarab javob berdim, uning ko'z o'ngimda bo'lganida, u qattiq qizargan va o'z og'zini ko'tarishni to'xtatgan.

en: “And might he spend the day with you?” was the father’s next request, which he made with a deprecatory smile, as though he stood in actual awe of me, yet always keeping so close to me, wherever I moved, that the fumes of the drink and tobacco in which he had been indulging were constantly perceptible to my nostrils.
uz: Va u siz bilan birga kun o'tkazishi mumkinmi? deb so'ragan otasining keyingi iltijo edi, u meni qo'rqib turganidek, kamtarlik bilan tabassum bilan so'radi, lekin har doim men har qanday joyda harakatlanayotganimda, menga shunchalik yaqin bo'lib turardiki, u o'z ichiga olgan ichimlik va tamaki tutunlari mening burnimda doimiy sezilarli edi.

en: I felt greatly vexed at his placing me in such a false position towards his son, as well as at his distracting my attention from what was, to me, a highly important operation—namely, the operation of dressing; while, over and above all, I was annoyed by the smell of liquor with which he followed me about.
uz: O'g'liga nisbatan meni bunday noto'g'ri nuqtai nazarga qo'yganidan va diqqatimni menga juda muhim operatsiyadan, ya'ni kiyim kiyish operatsiyasidan chalg'itganidan juda xafa bo'ldim.

en: Accordingly, I said very coldly that I could not have the pleasure of Ilinka’s company that day, since I should be out.
uz: Shuning uchun men o'sha kuni Ilinka bilan birga bo'lishdan zavqlanmasligimni juda sovuqlik bilan aytdim, chunki men tashqarida bo'lishim kerak edi.

en: I suppose you are going to see your sister?” put in Ilinka with a smile, but without looking at me.
uz: O'zingizning singlingiz bilan uchrashishingiz kerak, deb o'ylayman? Ilinkaga tabassum bilan, lekin menga nazar solmasdan qo'ydi.

en: “Well, I too have business to attend to.” At this I felt even more put out, as well as pricked with
uz: Ha, men ham ishlashim kerak. Bu bilan men o'zimni yanada ko'proq tashlab ketilgan va o'zimni ko'proq azob chekayotganimni his qildim.

en: compunction; so, to soften my refusal a little, I hastened to say that the reason why I should not be at home that day was that I had to call upon the PRINCE Ivan Ivanovitch, the PRINCESS Kornakoff, and the Monsieur Iwin who held such an influential post, as well as, probably, to dine with the PRINCESS Nechludoff (for I thought that, on learning what important folk I was in the habit of mixing with, the Graps would no longer think it worth while to pretend to me).
uz: Shunday qilib, rad etishimni biroz yumshatish uchun, o'sha kuni uyda bo'lmasligimning sababi shundaki, men PRINCE Ivan Ivanovitch, PRINCESA Kornakoff va shu qadar ta'sirli lavozimda bo'lgan monsieur Iwinni chaqirishim kerak edi, shuningdek, ehtimol, PRINCESA Nechludoff bilan kechki ovqatlanishim kerak edi (chunki men o'yladimki, men qanday muhim odamlar bilan aralashishni odat qilib olganimni bilib olgach, Graplar menga o'ylashning o'rniga o'tirmaydi deb o'ylayman).

en: However, just as they were leaving, I invited Ilinka to come and see me another day; but he only murmured something unintelligible, and it was plain that he meant never to set foot in the house again.
uz: Biroq, ular ketayotganda, Ilinkani yana bir kun menga tashrif buyurishga taklif qildim; lekin u faqat tushunarli bo'lmagan bir narsani g'ayrat bilan aytdi va u yana uyga qadam qo'ymaslikni nazarda tutganini aniq ko'rdim.

en: When they had departed, I set off on my round of calls.
uz: Ular ketgach, men o'z navbatimda qo'ng'iroqlarimni boshladim.

en: Woloda, whom I had asked that morning to come with me, in order that I might not feel quite so shy as when altogether alone, had declined on the ground that for two brothers to be seen driving in one drozhki would appear so horribly “proper.” XVIII.
uz: O'sha kuni ertalab o'zim bilan kelishini so'ragan Woloda, men o'zimni yolg'iz qolganimda bo'lgani kabi o'zimni juda uyalmasligim uchun, ikki birodarning bir drozhki bilan haydashini ko'rish juda dahshatli bo'lishi uchun o'zidan voz kechgan edi. XVIII.

en: THE VALAKHIN FAMILY Accordingly I set off alone.
uz: VALAKIN OILISHI Shunga ko'ra, men yolg'iz yo'lga chiqdim.

en: My first call on the route lay at the Valakhin mansion.
uz: Yo'lda birinchi bor Valakhin uyida o'tirganman.

en: It was now three years since I had seen Sonetchka, and my love for her had long become a thing of the past, yet there still lingered in my heart a sort of clear, touching recollection of our bygone childish affection.
uz: Sonetchkani ko'rmaganimga uch yil bo'ldi va unga bo'lgan muhabbatim o'tmishga aylandi, ammo yuragimda hali ham o'tmishdagi bolalik sevgimiz haqida aniq va hayajonli eslatma bor edi.

en: At intervals, also, during those three years, I had found myself recalling her memory with such force and vividness that I had actually shed tears, and imagined myself to be in love with her again, but those occasions had not lasted more than a few minutes at a time, and had been long in recurring.
uz: Shuningdek, o'sha uch yil davomida vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zimni uning xotirasini shunchalik kuchli va jonli eslab turgan edimki, hatto ko'z yoshlarimni to'kib yubordim va o'zimni yana unga muhabbatli bo'lishimni tasavvur qildim, lekin bu voqealar bir vaqtning o'zida bir necha daqiqadan ko'proq davom etmagan va tez-tez takrorlanayotgan edi.

en: I knew that Sonetchka and her mother had been abroad—that, in fact, they had been so for the last two years.
uz: Sonetchka va uning onasi chet elda bo'lganini bilardim, aslida, ular o'tgan ikki yildan beri shunday bo'lishgan.

en: Also, I had heard that
uz: Bundan tashqari, men buni eshitgan edim

en: they had been in a carriage accident, and that Sonetchka’s face had been so badly cut with the broken glass that her beauty was marred.
uz: Ular avtohalokatga uchragan edilar va Sonetchkaning yuzi buzilgan shisha bilan shunchalik yomon kesilgan ediki, uning go'zalligi buzildi.

en: As I drove to their house, I kept recalling the old Sonetchka to my mind, and wondering what she would look like when I met her.
uz: Ularning uyiga ketayotganimda, eski Sonetchka haqida o'ylayman va u bilan uchrashganimda qanday ko'rinishi mumkinligini o'ylayman.

en: Somehow I imagined that, after her two years’ sojourn abroad, she would look very tall, with a beautiful waist, and, though sedate and imposing, extremely attractive.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, men chet elda ikki yillik sayohatidan so'ng, u juda baland, chiroyli belga ega va juda yoqimli, ammo juda yoqimli ko'rinishini tasavvur qildim.

en: Somehow, also, my imagination refused to picture her with her face disfigured with scars, but, on the contrary, since I had read somewhere of a lover who remained true to his adored one in spite of her disfigurement with smallpox, strove to imagine that I was in love with Sonetchka, for the purpose of priding myself on holding to my troth in spite of her scars—Yet, as a matter of fact, I was not really in love with her during that drive, but having once stirred up in myself old MEMORIES of love, felt PREPARED to fall into that condition, and the more so because, of late, my conscience had often been pricking me for having discarded so many of my old flames.
uz: Shuningdek, bir yo'l bilan tasavvurim uni yuzidagi yaralar bilan o'zgartirilgan surat bilan tasvirlashni rad etdi, aksincha, men qayerda bo'lsa o'zimni sevgan kishiga sadoqatli qolgan sevgini o'qib, o'z ko'z o'ngida kasal kasalligiga duchor bo'lishiga qaramay, men Sonetchka bilan muhabbatda ekanimni tasavvur qilishga harakat qildim, chunki men o'zimni uning yaralariga qaramay, sadoqatimni saqlab qolganimdan faxrlanaman.

en: The Valakhins lived in a neat little wooden mansion approached by a courtyard.
uz: Valakhins oilasi hovli bilan yaqinlashgan yaxshi o'rnatilgan kichik yog'och uyda yashardi.

en: I gained admittance by ringing a bell (then a rarity in Moscow), and was received by a mincing, smartly-attired page.
uz: Men qo'ng'iroq qo'yib (o'shanda Moskvada kamchilik bo'lgan) qabulga kirdim va bir qisqa, smart-attired sahifa tomonidan qabul qilindi.

en: He either could not or made no attempt to inform me whether there was any one at home, but, leaving me alone in the dark hall, ran off down a still darker corridor.
uz: U uyda biror kishi bor-yo'qligini aytolmadi yoki aytishga urinmadi, lekin meni qorong'i zalda yolg'iz qoldirib, yanada qorong'i koridorda yugurib ketdi.

en: For a long time I waited in solitude in this gloomy place, out of which, in addition to the front door and the corridor, there only opened a door which at the moment was closed.
uz: Ko'p vaqt davomida men bu qorong'i joyda yolg'izlik bilan kutdim, u yerdan, old eshik va koridordan tashqari, faqat bir eshik ochildi va u o'sha paytda yopiq edi.

en: Rather surprised at the dismal appearance of the house, I came to the conclusion that the reason was that its inmates were still abroad.
uz: Uyning qorong'i ko'rinishi meni hayratda qoldirdi, shuning uchun uning mahbuslari hali ham chet elda bo'lgani uchun shunday xulosaga keldim.

en: After five minutes, however, the door leading into the salon was opened by the page boy, who then conducted me into a neat, but not richly furnished, drawing-room, where presently I was joined by Sonetchka.
uz: Biroq besh daqiqadan so'ng salonga kiruvchi eshikni sahifachi ochdi va u meni yaxshi jihozlangan, ammo yaxshi jihozlanmagan, turar joyga olib keldi, u yerda Sonetchka meni qo'shdi.

en: She was now seventeen years old, and very small and thin, as well as of an unhealthy pallor of face.
uz: Hozir u o'n yetti yoshda edi va juda kichik va chiroyli edi, shuningdek, yuzi salomat emas.

en: No scars at all were visible, however, and the beautiful, prominent eyes and bright, cheerful smile were the same as I had known and loved in my childhood.
uz: Biroq, hech qanday yaralar ko'rinmas edi va go'zal, ko'rinmas ko'zlar va yorqin, quvonchli tabassum men bolaligimda tanigan va sevgan odamlarning o'zi edi.

en: I had not expected her to look at all like this, and therefore could not at once lavish upon her the sentiment which I had been preparing on the
uz: Men uning bunday ko'rinishini kutmagan edim va shuning uchun men unga birdan o'zim tayyorlagan his-tuyg'ularni o'z ichiga ololmasdim.

en: She gave me her hand in the English fashion (which was then as much a novelty as a door-bell), and, bestowing upon mine a frank squeeze, sat down on the sofa by my side.
uz: U menga ingliz uslubida qo'lini berdi (o'shanda bu eshik qo'ng'iroqlari kabi yangilik edi) va mening qo'ng'iroqimni ochiqchasiga siqib, yonimda joylashgan sofaga o'tirdi.

en: how glad I am to see you, my dear Nicolas!” she said as she looked me in the face with an expression of pleasure so sincere that in the words “my dear Nicolas” I caught the purely friendly rather than the patronising note.
uz: Sizni ko'rishimdan juda xursandman, aziz Nikolas! deb aytdi u, menga yuzma-yuz qarab, shunchalik samimiy quvonch bilan gapirdiki, so'zlar bilan o'z aziz Nikolasimni o'zimga mehribonlik bildirgan nota emas, balki mehribonlik bildirgan nota tushdi.

en: To my surprise she seemed to me simpler, kinder, and more sisterly after her foreign tour than she had been before it.
uz: O'shanda u o'z tashqaridagi sayohatidan so'ng menga oddiy, mehribon va opa-singil bo'lib ko'rindi.

en: True, I could now see that she had two small scars between her nose and temples, but her wonderful eyes and smile fitted in exactly with my recollections, and shone as of old.
uz: To'g'ri, men endi uning burun va templari o'rtasida ikkita kichik yara borligini ko'rardim, ammo uning ajoyib ko'zlari va tabassumlari mening xotiralarimga to'g'ri o'xshaydi va qadimgi kabi porlaydi.

en: “But how greatly you have changed!” she went on.
uz: Ammo siz qanchalik o'zgargansiz! U davom etdi.

en: “You are quite grown-up now.
uz: Siz endi katta bo'ldingiz.

en: And I-I-well, what do you think of me?” “I should never have known you,” I replied, despite the fact that at the moment I was thinking that I should have known her anywhere and always.
uz: Va men-men-men, siz men haqimda nima deb o'ylaysiz? Men sizni hech qachon tanimagan bo'lmas edim, deb javob berdim, shunga qaramay, o'sha paytda men uni har doim va har joyda tanigan bo'lar edim, deb o'yladim.

en: Am I grown so ugly?” she inquired with a movement of her head.
uz: Men shunchalik yomon o'sib bormadimmi? - deb so'radi u boshini ko'targan holda.

en: “Oh, no, decidedly not!” I hastened to reply.
uz: Oh, yo'q, albatta yo'q! Men javob berishga shoshildim.

en: “But you have grown taller and older.
uz: Ammo siz baland va katta bo'lgansiz.

en: As for being uglier, why, you are even— “Yes, yes; never mind.
uz: Qizig'i shundaki, siz o'zingizdan ko'ra ko'proq yoqimli bo'lasiz.

en: Do you remember our dances and games, and St.
uz: Bizning raqs va o'yinlarimizni va St.

en: Jerome, and Madame Dorat?” (As a matter of fact, I could not recollect any Madame Dorat, but saw that Sonetchka was being led away by the joy of her childish recollections, and mixing them up a little).
uz: Jerome va Madame Dorat? (Aslida, men hech qanday Madame Doratni eslay olmadim, lekin Sonetchkaning bolalik xotiralarining quvonchidan hayratda qolganini ko'rdim va ularni biroz aralashtirdim).

en: what a lovely time it was!” she went on—and once more there shone before me the same eyes and smile as I had always carried in my memory.
uz: U davom etdi va yana bir bor mening xotiramda doim borgan ko'zlarim va tabassumim menga yorqin ko'rindi.

en: While she had been speaking, I had been thinking over my position at the present moment, and had come to the conclusion that I was in love with her.
