uz: U gapirganida, men hozirgi mavqeyim haqida o'ylab, unga muhabbat ko'rsatayotganimga amin bo'ldim.

en: The instant, however, that I arrived at that result my careless, happy mood vanished, a mist seemed to arise before me which concealed even her eyes and smile, and, blushing hotly, I became tongue-tied and ill-at-ease.
uz: Biroq, shu natijaga yetib borganimdan so'ng, befarq ruhim yo'q bo'lib ketdi, hatto uning ko'zlari va tabassumini ham yashirgan bulut paydo bo'ldi va men qizg'in qizg'inlashib, tilni bog'lab, o'zimni noqulay his qildim.

en: “But times are different now,” she went on with a sigh and a little lifting of her eyebrows.
uz: Ammo hozir vaqtlar boshqacha, o'zi nafas olib, biroz ko'z burchaklarini ko'tarib davom etdi.

en: “Everything seems worse than it used to be, and ourselves too.
uz: Har narsa avvalgidek yomon ko'rinadi, o'zimizni ham.

en: Is it not so, Nicolas?” I could return her no answer, but sat silently looking at her.
uz: Nikolas, shunday emasmi? Men unga hech qanday javob qaytarolmadim, lekin sukut saqlash bilan unga qarab o'tirdim.

en: “Where are those Iwins and Kornakoffs now?
uz: Bu Iwinlar va Kornakofflar endi qayerda?

en: Do you remember them?” she continued, looking, I think, with some curiosity at my blushing, downcast countenance.
uz: U davom etdi va o'ylaymanki, o'zimning qizg'in va tushkun yuzimni qiziquvchanlik bilan ko'rib chiqdi.

en: “What splendid times we used to have!” Still I could not answer her.
uz: Bizda qanday ajoyib vaqtlar bo'lgan! Ammo men unga javob bera olmadim.

en: The next moment, I was relieved from this awkward position by the entry of old Madame Valakhin into the room.
uz: Keyingi daqiqada, qariya Madame Valakhin xonadonga kirganda, men bu noqulay holatdan xalos bo'ldim.

en: Rising, I bowed, and straightway recovered my faculty of speech.
uz: O'shanda o'zimni ko'tarib, yonma-yon bo'yin egdim va gapirish qobiliyatimni tikladim.

en: On the other hand, an extraordinary change now took place in Sonetchka.
uz: Boshqa tomondan, Sonetchkada katta o'zgarish yuz berdi.

en: All her gaiety and bonhomie disappeared, her smile became quite a different one, and, except for the point of her shortness of stature, she became just the lady from abroad whom I had expected to find in her.
uz: Uning barcha shodligi va mehribonligi yo'qoldi, tabassumlari butunlay boshqacha bo'ldi va, o'zining qisqa bo'lganligi bilan bog'liq bo'lmagan holatdan tashqari, u faqat chet eldan kelgan ayol bo'ldi, men uning ichida topishni kutgan edim.

en: Yet for this change there was no apparent reason, since her mother smiled every whit as pleasantly, and expressed in her every movement just the same benignity, as of old.
uz: Ammo bu o'zgarish uchun aniq sabab yo'q edi, chunki uning onasi har bir o'zidan o'zgacha tabassum bilan tabassum qilib, har bir harakatida qadimgi kabi mehribonlikni namoyon etgan.

en: Seating herself in her arm-chair, the old lady signed to me to come and sit beside her; after which she said something to her daughter in English, and Sonetchka left the room—a fact which still further helped to relieve me.
uz: O'zini o'zining koltukida o'tirgan keksa ayol menga o'z yonida o'tirishga ruxsat berdi; so'ng u o'z qizi bilan ingliz tilida biron narsa aytdi va Sonetchka xonani tark etdi.

en: Madame then inquired after my father and brother, and passed on to speak of her great bereavement—the loss of her husband.
uz: Keyin madam otam va akam haqida so'radi va o'zidan keyin erini yo'qotganidan ko'p qayg'urganini aytib berdi.

en: Presently, however, she seemed to become sensible of the fact that I was not helping much in the conversation, for she gave me a look as much as to say: “If, now, my dear boy, you were to get up, to take your leave, and to depart, it would be well.” But a curious circumstance had overtaken me.
uz: Biroq, hozirda u suhbatda menga ko'p yordam bermayotganimni tushunib yetdi, chunki u menga shunday ko'z tikdi: Agar endi, aziz o'g'lim, turib ketib ketsang, yaxshi bo'lardi. Ammo men o'zimni qiziq bir holatga duchor qildim.

en: While she had been speaking of her bereavement, I had recalled to myself, not only the fact that I was in love, but the probability that the mother knew of it: whereupon such a fit of bashfulness had come upon me that I felt powerless to put any member of my body to its legitimate use.
uz: U o'z qayg'usi haqida gapirganida, men nafaqat o'zimni sevganimni, balki onam buni bilishi ehtimoli borligini o'zimga eslatdim: shundan so'ng men o'zimni o'zimni o'zimning tanamning har qanday a'zosiga qonuniy foydalanishga qo'l qo'yishga qodir emasman deb o'yladim.

en: I knew that if I were to rise and walk I should have to think where to plant each foot, what to do with my head, what with my hands, and so on.
uz: O'zim turib yurishim kerak bo'lsa, har bir oyoqni qayerga qo'yishim, boshim bilan nima qilishim kerakligini, qo'llarim bilan nima qilishim kerakligini o'ylashim kerakligini bilardim.

en: In a word, I foresaw that I should be very much as I had been on the night when I partook too freely of champagne, and therefore, since I felt uncertain of being able to manage myself if I DID rise, I ended by feeling UNABLE to rise.
uz: Bir so'z bilan aytganda, men shampanj ichgan kechaga o'xshash bo'lishimni oldindan ko'rdim va shuning uchun o'zimni o'zim boshqarishga qodir bo'lmasligimdan shubhalanayotganim sababli, o'zimni o'tqazishga qobiliyatsiz his qilganim sababli, oxir-oqibat o'zimni o'tqazishga qodir emasman deb o'yladim.

en: Meanwhile, I should say, Sonetchka had returned to the room with her work, and seated herself in a far corner—a corner whence, as I was nevertheless sensible, she could observe me.
uz: Shu bilan birga, aytishim kerakki, Sonetchka o'z ishi bilan xonaniga qaytib keldi va o'zini uzoq burchada o'tirdi, undan men o'zimni oqilona ko'rib, meni kuzatib turardi.

en: must have felt some surprise as she gazed at my crimson face and noted my complete immobility, but I decided that it was better to continue sitting in that absurd position than to risk something unpleasant by getting up and walking.
uz: O'sha qizil yuzimga qaraganida va to'liq harakatsizligimni payqaganida, u o'zini ajablantirgan his qilgan bo'lishi kerak, lekin men o'sha g'alati holatda o'tirishni davom ettirish yaxshiroq deb o'yladim, o'rnidan turib, yurish orqali yoqimsiz narsani xavf ostiga qo'yishdan ko'ra.

en: Thus I sat on and on, in the hope that some unforeseen chance would deliver me from my predicament.
uz: Shunday qilib, bir necha marta o'tirib, kutilmagan hodisalar meni qiyin vaziyatdan qutqarishiga umid qildim.

en: That unforeseen chance at length presented itself in the person of an unforeseen young man, who entered the room with an air of being one of the household, and bowed to me politely as he did so: whereupon Madame rose, excused herself to me for having to speak with her “homme d’affaires,” and finally gave me a glance which said: “Well, if you DO mean to go on sitting there for ever, at least I can’t drive you away.” Accordingly, with a great effort I also rose, but, finding it impossible to do any leave-taking, moved away towards the door, followed by the pitying glances of mother and daughter.
uz: O'sha kutilmagan hodisa nihoyat o'zini kutilmagan yigitning shaxsiyatida ko'rsatdi, u xonada uydagi odam kabi ko'rindi va menga xushmuomalalik bilan sajda qildi: u holda xonim o'rnidan turib, men bilan homme d'affaires bilan gaplashish uchun uzr so'radi va nihoyat menga bir nazar soladi: Agar siz o'sha yerda abadiy o'tirishni xohlasangiz, hech bo'lmaganda men sizni yurib yuborolmayman. Shuning uchun men ham katta harakat bilan o'rnidan turib qoldim, lekin hech qanday ruxsat olish imkonsiz bo'lganini ko'rib, eshik tomon o'tib ketdim va ona va qizning achinarli ko'zlariga ergashdim.

en: All at once I stumbled over a chair, although it was lying quite out of my route: the reason for my stumbling being that my whole attention was centred upon not tripping over the carpet.
uz: Birdan men o'rindiqdan to'xtab qoldim, ammo u mening yo'limdan chiqib ketdi: to'xtab qolishimning sababi, butun e'tiborim g'alaba qozonishga qaratilgan edi.

en: Driving through the fresh air, however—where at first I muttered and fidgeted about so much that Kuzma, my coachman, asked me what was the matter—I soon found this feeling pass away, and began to meditate quietly concerning my love for Sonetchka and her relations with her mother, which had appeared to me rather strange.
uz: Biroq, toza havo bo'ylab haydashda birinchi marta men shunchalik g'alati va g'alati bo'ldimki, haydovchim Kuzma menga nima bo'lganini so'radi.Qizim tez orada bu his-tuyg'u o'tib ketayotganini ko'rdim va Sonetchkaga bo'lgan sevgim va uning onasi bilan bo'lgan munosabatlarim haqida xotirjamlik bilan mulohaza yuritishni boshladim, bu menga o'zgacha tuyulgan edi.

en: When, afterwards, I told my father that mother and daughter had not seemed on the best of terms with one another, he said: “Yes, Madame leads the poor girl an awful life with her meanness.
uz: Keyinchalik otamga onam va qiz o'zaro yaxshi munosabatda bo'lmaganini aytganimda, u shunday dedi: "Ha, xonim kambag'al qizga o'z kamtarligi bilan dahshatli hayot kechiradi.

en: Yet,” added my father with a greater display of feeling than a man might naturally conceive for a mere relative, “she used to be such an original, dear, charming woman!
uz: Biroq, otam, erkak kishi oddiy qarindoshlari uchun tabiiy ravishda tasavvur qila olmaydigan ko'proq his-tuyg'ularni ko'rsatdi, u o'sha xil asl, sevimli va chiroyli ayol edi!

en: I cannot think what has made her change so much.
uz: Uning shunchalik o'zgarishiga nima sabab bo'lganini tasavvur ham qila olmayman.

en: By the way, you didn’t notice a secretary fellow about, did you?
uz: Aytgancha, siz bir marta ham ko'rmagansiz, shundaymi?

en: Fancy a Russian lady having an affaire with a secretary!” “Yes, I saw him,” I replied.
uz: Rossiyalik ayolning kotibi bilan ishqiy munosabatda bo'lishidan zavqlaning!Ha, men uni ko'rdim, dedim.

en: “And was he at least good-looking?” “No, not at all.” “It is extraordinary!” concluded Papa, with a cough and an irritable hoist of his shoulder.
uz: Va u hech bo'lmaganda chiroyli bo'lganmi?Yo'q, umuman emas.Bu g'alati narsa! Papa kashsalanish va yelkasini g'azabga solib ko'tarish bilan yakunlandi.

en: “Well, I am in love!” was my secret thought to myself as I drove along in my drozhki.
uz: Eh, men o'zimni sevganman! deb o'yladim. Drozhkimda yurganimda, sirim o'zimda edi.

en: THE KORNAKOFFS MY second call on the route lay at the Kornakoffs’, who lived on the first floor of a large mansion facing the Arbat.
uz: KORNAKOFFLAR Yo'nalishdagi ikkinchi qo'ng'iroqim Kornakofflar oilasi tomonidan o'tkazilgan, ular Arbatga qaraydigan katta uyning birinchi qavatida yashardilar.

en: The staircase of the building looked extremely neat and orderly, yet in no way luxurious— being lined only with drugget pinned down with highly-polished brass rods.
uz: Binoning merosimi nihoyatda tartibli va tartibli ko'rinardi, ammo hech qanday darajada hashamatli emas edi, chunki uni faqat yuqori polizlangan mis tayoqlari bilan to'ldirilgan dorixonalar bilan qoplab qo'yilgan edi.

en: Nowhere were there any flowers or mirrors to be seen.
uz: Hech joyda gullar yoki ko'rinmalar ko'rinmagan.

en: The salon, too, with its polished floor, which I traversed on my way to the drawing-room, was decorated in the same cold, severe, unostentatious style.
uz: Salon ham, men salonga borayotganda o'sha yo'lda o'tib o'tgan polizlangan qavatli xonadon bilan, xuddi shunday sovuq, qattiq va ko'ngilsiz uslubda bezatilgan edi.

en: Everything in it looked bright and solid, but not new, and pictures, flower-stands, and articles of bric-a-brac were wholly absent.
uz: Udagi hamma narsa yorqin va mustahkam ko'rinardi, ammo yangi emas edi, rasmlar, gullar stoli va briq-a-braqdan yasalgan buyumlar butunlay yo'q edi.

en: In the drawing-room I found some of the young princesses seated, but seated with the sort of correct, “company” air about them which gave one the impression that they sat like that only when guests were expected.
uz: O'tirish xonasida men ba'zi yosh princesslarni o'tirgan holda topdim, lekin ular atrofida to'g'ri, company havo o'tirganligi sababli ular faqat mehmonlar kutilgan paytda o'tirgan deb taassurot qoldirdi.

en: “Mamma will be here presently,” the eldest of them said to me as she seated herself by my side.
uz: Mamma tez orada bu yerda bo'ladi, - dedi katta o'g'lim o'zini yonimga o'tirib.

en: For the next quarter of an hour, this young lady entertained me with such an easy flow of small-talk that the conversation never flagged a moment.
uz: Keyingi chorak soat davomida bu qiz meni o'yin-kulgi bilan o'tkazdi, suhbat hech qachon bir daqiqa ham o'z ichiga olmagan.

en: Yet somehow she made so patent the fact that she was just entertaining me that I felt not altogether pleased.
uz: Ammo u meni shunchaki o'yin-kulgi qilib qo'yganidan shunchalik mamnun bo'ldiki, men o'zimni uncha mamnun his qilmadim.

en: Amongst other things, she told me that their brother Stephen (whom they called Etienne, and who had been two years at the College of Cadets) had now received his commission.
uz: U menga birodarlari Stiven (Etienne deb nomlangan va ikki yil kadetlar kollejida bo'lgan) endi uning topshirig'ini olganini aytdi.

en: Whenever she spoke of him, and more particularly when she told me that he had flouted his mother’s wishes by entering the Hussars, she assumed a nervous air, and immediately her sisters, sitting there in silence, also assumed a nervous air.
uz: Har qachon u u haqida gapirganida, ayniqsa, u xusarlarga kirib, onasining xohishini buzganini aytganda, u g'alati hissaga ega bo'lgan va shu zahoti uning singillari ham o'tirgan holda g'alati hissaga ega bo'lgan.

en: When, again, she spoke of my
uz: Yana bir bor u, mening o'g'lim haqida gapirganida,

en: grandmother’s death, she assumed a MOURNFUL air, and immediately the others all did the same.
uz: Buvimning o'limi tufayli u G'AMOL ruhni his qildi va shu zahoti qolganlar ham xuddi shunday qildilar.

en: Finally, when she recalled how I had once struck St.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, men bir marta St.

en: Jerome and been expelled from the room, she laughed and showed her bad teeth, and immediately all the other princesses laughed and showed their bad teeth too.
uz: Jerom va xonadan chiqarilganidan so'ng, u kuldi va o'zlarining yomon tishlarini ko'rsatdi, shu zahoti boshqa barcha printsesalar kuldi va o'zlarining yomon tishlarini ko'rsatdi.

en: Next, the Princess-Mother herself entered—a little dried-up woman, with a wandering glance and a habit of always looking at somebody else when she was addressing one.
uz: Keyinchalik, printsesa-ona o'zi bir oz qurigan ayolga kirdi, uning ko'zlari ko'z o'ngida bo'lib, u boshqa odamga murojaat qilganda, doimo boshqa odamga qarab turadigan odat bor edi.

en: Taking my hand, she raised her own to my lips for me to kiss it—which otherwise, not supposing it to be necessary, I should not have done.
uz: Mening qo'limni olib, uni o'pishim uchun o'z og'zimga ko'tardi, agar kerak bo'lmagan bo'lsa, men buni qilmasdim.

en: “How pleased I am to see you!” she said with her usual clearness of articulation as she gazed at her daughters.
uz: "Sizni ko'rishimdan juda xursandman! - deb aytdi u, qizlariga qarab, odatdagidek aniq so'zlarni aytadi.

en: “And how like your mother you look!
uz: Va siz onangizga qanchalik o'xshaysiz!

en: Does he not, Lise?” Lise assented, though I knew for a fact that I did not resemble my mother in the least.
uz: Xo'sh, Lise? Lise rozi bo'ldi, ammo men onamga hech qanday o'xshashim yo'qligini aniq bilardim.

en: “And what a grown-up you have become!
uz: Va qanday katta bo'lgansiz!

en: My Etienne, you will remember, is your second cousin.
uz: Esingizda bo'lsa, mening Etienne sizning ikkinchi qarindoshingiz.

en: No, not second cousin—what is it, Lise?
uz: Yo'q, ikkinchi kuzasi emas, nima, Lise?

en: My mother was Barbara Dimitrievna, daughter of Dimitri Nicolaevitch, and your grandmother was Natalia Nicolaevna.” “Then he is our THIRD cousin, Mamma,” said the eldest girl.
uz: Onam Dimitri Nikolaevchning qizi Barbara Dimitrievna edi, buvim Nataliya Nikolaevna edi.  "U bizning uchinchi qarindoshimiz bo'lsa-da, onam katta qiz deb aytdi.

en: “Oh, how you always confuse me!” was her mother’s angry reply.
uz: Oh, siz meni har doim qanday chalg'itasiz! - dedi onasi g'azablangan javobida.

en: “Not third cousin, but COUSIN GERMAN—that is your relationship to Etienne.
uz: Uchinchi qarindoshim emas, balki QISIM Germaniya, bu sizning Etienne bilan munosabatingizdir.

en: He is an officer now.
uz: U endi ofitser bo'ldi.

en: It is not well that he should have his own way too much.
uz: O'z xohishiga ko'ra ko'p vaqt o'tkazishi yaxshi emas.

en: You young men need keeping in hand, or—!
uz: Siz yoshlar qo'lingizda saqlanishga muhtoj bo'lasiz, yoki!

en: Well, you are not vexed because your old aunt tells you the plain truth?
uz: Xo'sh, siz keksa xotiningiz aniq haqiqatni aytgani uchun xafa emasmisiz?

en: I always kept Etienne strictly in hand, for I found it necessary to do so.” “Yes, that is how our relationship stands,” she went on.
uz: Men Etienneni har doim qo'limdan tutib turardim, chunki buni zarur deb topdim. Ha, bizning munosabatlarimiz shunday, u davom etdi.

en: “Prince Ivan Ivanovitch is my uncle, and your late mother’s uncle also.
uz: Prints Ivan Ivanovitch mening o'g'limdir, o'g'lim onangizning o'g'li ham.

en: Consequently I must have been your mother’s first cousin—no, second cousin.
uz: Demak, men onangizning birinchi qarindoshi, ikkinchi qarindoshi bo'lganim kerak.

en: Tell me, have you been to call on Prince Ivan yet?” I said no, but that I was just going to.
uz: Ayting-chi, siz hozircha Prens Ivonni ko'rishga borganmisiz? Men yo'q dedim, lekin hozircha boryapman.

en: “Ah, is it possible?” she cried.
uz: Ah, bu mumkinmi? U yig'lab yubordi.

en: “Why, you ought to have paid him the first call of all!
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, siz unga birinchi qo'ng'iroqda pul to'lashingiz kerak edi!

en: Surely you know that he stands to you in the position of a father?
uz: U ota sifatida sizga qo'shilganini albatta bilasanmi?

en: He has no children of his own, and his only heirs are yourself and my children.
uz: Uning o'z farzandlari yo'q va uning yagona merosxo'ri siz va mening farzandlarimsiz.

en: You ought to pay him all possible
uz: Siz unga imkon boricha to'lov to'lashingiz kerak.

en: deference, both because of his age, and because of his position in the world, and because of everything else.
uz: Uning yoshligi, dunyodagi mavqei va boshqa hamma narsa tufayli hurmatga sazovor bo'lgan.

en: I know that you young fellows of the present day think nothing of relationships and are not fond of old men, yet do you listen to me, your old aunt, for I am fond of you, and was fond of your mother, and had a great—a very great- liking and respect for your grandmother.
uz: Bilamanki, bugungi yoshlar munosabatlar haqida hech narsa o'ylamaydilar va keksa odamlarni yoqtirmaydilar, ammo siz meni, keksa qizangizni tinglaysiz, chunki men sizlarni yaxshi ko'raman, onangizni yaxshi ko'rdim va buvimni juda yaxshi ko'rdim va hurmat qilardim.

en: You must not fail to call upon him on any account.” I said that I would certainly go, and since my present call seemed to me to have lasted long enough, I rose, and was about to depart, but she restrained me.
uz: Siz hech qanday sababga ko'ra uni chaqirishdan bosh tortmasligingiz kerak. Men albatta ketishimni aytdim va hozirgi qo'ng'iroqim menga etarlicha uzoq davom etgan bo'lgani uchun, men turdim va ketmoqchi edim, lekin u meni to'xtatdi.

en: “No, wait a minute,” she cried.
uz: Yo'q, bir daqiqa turing, u yig'ladi.

en: “Where is your father, Lise?
uz: Yo otang qayerda, Lise?

en: Go and tell him to come here.
uz: Borib, unga bu yerga kelishini ayt.

en: He will be so glad to see you,” she added, turning to me.
uz: U sizni ko'rib juda xursand bo'ladi, - dedi u, menga qarab.

en: Two minutes later Prince Michael entered.
uz: Ikki daqiqa o'tgach, Prince Maykl kirdi.

en: He was a short, thick- set gentleman, very slovenly dressed and ill-shaven, yet wearing such an air of indifference that he looked almost a fool.
uz: U qisqa va qalin bo'lgan yigit edi, juda kam kiyim kiygan va yomon shavshan bo'lgan, ammo u shunchalik befarq ediki, deyarli ahmoq kabi ko'rinardi.

en: He was not in the least glad to see me—at all events he did not intimate that he was; but the Princess (who appeared to stand in considerable awe of him) hastened to say: “Is not Woldemar here” (she seemed to have forgotten my name) “exactly like his mother?” and she gave her husband a glance which forced him to guess what she wanted.
uz: U meni ko'rishdan hech qanday xursand emas edi, lekin u buni aniq aytmagan edi; lekin princess (ular unga juda hurmat ko'rsatgan) shoshilmay: "Bu yerda Voldemar (o'zimning ismimni unutib qo'ygan bo'lib ko'rinadi) o'z onasiga o'xshamaydimi?" - deb aytdi va u eriga ko'z tikib, u nima istayotganini tasavvur qilishga majbur qildi.

en: Accordingly he approached me with his usual passionless, half-discontented expression, and held out to me an unshaven cheek to kiss.
uz: Shuning uchun u menga odatdagidek ishtiyoqsiz, yarim rozi bo'lmagan ko'z o'ngimga keldi va o'zimga o'g'illarini o'g'irlamagan bo'yni uzatdi.

en: “Why, you are not dressed yet, though you have to go out soon!” was the Princess’s next remark to him in the angry tone which she habitually employed in conversation with her domestics.
uz: Hali kiyinmagan bo'lsangiz ham, tezda tashqariga chiqishingiz kerak!- deb aytdi printsesa.- Bu uning uyidagilar bilan suhbatlashishda odatda ishlatadigan g'azablangan so'z edi.

en: “It will only mean your offending some one again, and trying to set people against you.” “In a moment, in a moment, mother,” said Prince Michael, and departed.
uz: Bu faqatgina sizni yana kimnidir ranjitishingizni va odamlarni sizga qarshi qo'yishingizni anglatadi.Bir daqiqadan keyin, bir daqiqadan keyin, ona, - dedi Prince Michael va jo'nab ketdi.

en: I also made my bows and departed.
uz: Men ham o'zimning bo'yinturug'imni tayyorlab, ketdim.

en: This was the first time I had heard of our being related to Prince Ivan Ivanovitch, and the news struck me unpleasantly.
uz: Bu bizning Prens Ivan Ivanovitch bilan qarindosh ekanligimizni birinchi marta eshitganim edi va bu xabar menga yomon taassurot qoldirdi.

en: THE IWINS As for the prospect of my call upon the Prince, it seemed even more unpleasant.
uz: IWINS O'z navbatida, meni Prinsga chaqirish imkoniyati yanada noqulay tuyuldi.

en: However, the order of my route took me first to the Iwins, who lived in a large and splendid mansion in Tverskaia Street.
uz: Biroq, yo'lim tartibi meni birinchi navbatda Tverskaia ko'chasidagi katta va chiroyli uyda yashovchi Iwinlar oilasiga olib bordi.

en: It was not without some nervousness that I entered the great portico where a Swiss major-domo stood armed with his staff of office.
uz: Biroz g'alati bo'lganimda, Shveytsariya majordomi o'zining ofis shtablari bilan qurollanib turgan katta portikga kirdim.

en: To my inquiry as to whether any one was at home he replied: “Whom do you wish to see, sir?
uz: Uyda kim borligini so'raganimda, u shunday javob berdi: "Kimni ko'rishni xohlaysiz, xo'jayinim?

en: The General’s son is within.” “And the General himself?” I asked with forced assurance.
uz: Generalning o'g'li ichkarida.Va generalning o'zi? Men majburiy ishonch bilan so'radim.

en: “I must report to him your business first.
uz: Ikki borangizni unga xabar qilishim kerak.

en: What may it be, sir?” said the major-domo as he rang a bell.
uz: Bu nima bo'lishi mumkin, xonim? - dedi majordom qo'ng'iroq qo'zg'atayotganda.

en: Immediately the gaitered legs of a footman showed themselves on the staircase above; whereupon I was seized with such a fit of nervousness that I hastily bid the lacquey say nothing about my presence to the General, since I would first see his son.
uz: O'sha zahoti ustozning qo'pol oyoqlari ustidagi mertaga ko'rindi; shundan so'ng men shunchalik g'alati bo'ldimki, lackiy boshliqga o'zim borligim haqida hech narsa aytmaslikka to'xtatdim, chunki men uning o'g'lini birinchi bor ko'rishim kerak edi.

en: By the time I had reached the top of the long staircase, I seemed to have grown extremely small (metaphorically, I mean, not actually), and had very much the same feeling within me as had possessed my soul when my drozhki drew up to the great portico, namely, a feeling as though drozhki, horse, and coachman had all of them grown extremely small too.
uz: Uzoq mertabaning yuqori tomoniga yetib borganimda, men juda kichik bo'lib o'sdim (metaforik ma'noda, aslida emas) va ruhimdagi his-tuyg'u, drozhkim katta portikga yetib borganida o'ziga xos edi, ya'ni drozhkim, ot va vagonim ham juda kichik bo'lib o'sganidek edi.

en: I found the General’s son lying asleep on a sofa, with an open book before him.
uz: Generalning o'g'lini sofa ustida uxlab, uning oldida kitob ochilgan holda topdim.

en: His tutor, Monsieur Frost, under whose care he still pursued his studies at home, had entered behind me with a sort of boyish tread, and now awoke his pupil.
uz: Uning o'qituvchisi, M. Frost, u hali ham o'qishni uyda davom ettirgan, uning g'amxo'rligi ostida edi, u mening ortimdan o'g'illik ko'rinishi bilan kirgan edi va endi o'zining o'quvchilarini uyg'otgan edi.

en: Iwin evinced no particular pleasure at seeing me, while I also seemed to notice that, while talking to me, he kept looking at my eyebrows.
uz: Iwin meni ko'rishdan hech qanday zavqlanmayotganini ko'rgach, men ham menga gapirganida, u ko'z burchaklarimga qarab turishini payqadim.

en: Although he was perfectly polite, I conceived that he was “entertaining” me much as the Princess Valakhin had done, and that he not only felt no particular liking for
uz: Garchi u juda xushmuomala bo'lsa-da, men u meni "prinsesa Valakhin kabi o'yin-kulg'ini o'tkazayotganini" tushunib yetdim va u nafaqat o'ziga xos qiziqish ko'rsatgan, balki o'ziga xos qiziqish ko'rsatmaganini ham angladim.

en: me, but even that he considered my acquaintance in no way necessary to one who possessed his own circle of friends.
uz: Ammo hatto o'z do'stlari bor kishi uchun mening tanishim hech qanday zarur emasligini tushunib yetdi.

en: All this arose out of the idea that he was regarding my eyebrows.
uz: Bularning barchasi u mening ko'z burchaklarim haqida gapirayotganidan kelib chiqqan.

en: In short, his bearing towards me appeared to be (as I recognised with an awkward sensation) very much the same as my own towards Ilinka Grap.
uz: Qisqa qilib aytganda, uning menga bo'lgan munosabati Ilinka Grapga bo'lgan munosabatimga o'xshash edi (men bu haqda o'yladim).

en: I began to feel irritated, and to interpret every fleeting glance which he cast at Monsieur Frost as a mute inquiry: “Why has this fellow come to see me?” After some conversation he remarked that his father and mother were at home.
uz: Men g'azablanishni boshladim va monsieur Frostga qo'ygan har bir ko'rinishni soqov so'rov sifatida tushunib yetardim: "Bu odam nega mendan ko'rish uchun keldi? Ba'zi suhbatlardan so'ng, u otasi va onasi uyda ekanliklarini aytdi.

en: Would I not like to visit them too?
uz: Men ham ularga tashrif buyurishni xohlamaymanmi?

en: “First I will go and dress myself,” he added as he departed to another room, notwithstanding that he had seemed to be perfectly well dressed (in a new frockcoat and white waistcoat) in the present one.
uz: Birinch men borib kiyim kiyaman, deb qo'shimcha qildi u boshqa xonani tark etganida, hozirgi xonada (yangi qo'ylak va oq kiyimda) mukammal kiyim kiygan bo'lishiga qaramay.

en: A few minutes later he reappeared in his University uniform, buttoned up to the chin, and we went downstairs together.
uz: Bir necha daqiqa o'tgach, u universitet uniformida yana paydo bo'ldi, qanigacha tugma bilan bog'lanib, biz birgalikda pastga tushdik.

en: The reception rooms through which we passed were lofty and of great size, and seemed to be richly furnished with marble and gilt ornaments, chintz-covered settees, and a number of mirrors.
uz: Biz o'tgan qabulxonalar baland va katta bo'lib, marmor va oltin bezaklar, chintz bilan qoplangan septes va ko'zgular bilan boy jihozlangan bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: Presently Madame Iwin met us, and we went into a little room behind the drawing-room, where, welcoming me in very friendly fashion, she seated herself by my side, and began to inquire after my relations.
uz: O'sha paytdan boshlab, Xonim Iwin bizni uchratdi va biz o'sha turar joyning orqasidagi kichik xonaga kirdik, u yerda u meni juda do'stona kutib oldi va yonimga o'tirib, mening munosabatlarim haqida so'rashdi.

en: Closer acquaintance with Madame (whom I had seen only twice before, and that but for a moment on each occasion) impressed me favourably.
uz: Xonim bilan yaqinroq tanishish (men uni avval faqat ikki marta ko'rgan edim va har safar faqat bir daqiqa) menga ijobiy taassurot qoldirdi.

en: She was tall, thin, and very pale, and looked as though she suffered from chronic depression and fatigue.
uz: U baland, chiroyli va ko'rinmas edi va xuddi xronik tushkunlik va charchaganlik azobidan azob chekkan bo'lsa kerak.

en: Yet, though her smile was a sad one, it was very kind, and her large, mournful eyes, with a slight cast in their vision, added to the pathos and attractiveness of her expression.
uz: Biroq, uning tabassumlari qayg'uli bo'lsa-da, u juda mehribon edi va uning katta, qayg'uli ko'zlari, ko'zlarida biroz mayda bo'lgan holda, uning ifodasining patos va jozibadorligini qo'shimcha qildi.

en: Her attitude, while not precisely that of a hunchback, made her whole form droop, while her every movement expressed languor.
uz: Uning nuqtai nazari, ayniqsa, cho'pon kabi emas, balki butun shakli qulab ketishiga sabab bo'lgan, har bir harakatlari esa g'amginlikni ifodalangan.

en: Likewise, though her speech was deliberate, the timbre of her voice, and the manner in which she lisped her r’s and l’s, were very pleasing to the ear.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, uning so'zlari ham qasddan qilingan bo'lsa-da, uning ovozi va o'z so'zlari va so'zlarini so'zlash usuli quloq uchun juda yoqimli edi.

en: Finally, she did not “ENTERTAIN” me.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, u meni qiziqtirmadi.

en: Unfortunately, the answers which I returned to her questions concerning my relations seemed to afford her a painful interest, and to remind her of happier days: with the result that when, presently, her son left the room, she gazed at me in silence for a moment, and then burst into tears.
uz: Afsuski, men uning munosabatlarimga oid savollariga bergan javoblarim unga og'riqli qiziqish uyg'otgandek tuyuldi va baxtli kunlarni eslatdi: natijada, o'g'li xonani tark etganida, u menga bir daqiqalik sukut saqlash bilan qaradi, so'ngra ko'z yoshlariga tushib qoladi.

en: As I sat there in mute
uz: Men o'zimni so'zsiz o'tirganimda

en: bewilderment, I could not conceive what I had said to bring this about.
uz: Ajablanarlisi shundaki, men buni amalga oshirish uchun nima aytganimni tasavvur ham qila olmadim.

en: At first I felt sorry for her as she sat there weeping with downcast eyes.
uz: Boshida men uning ko'zlarini tushirib, yig'lab o'tirganida, unga achinardim.

en: Next I began to think to myself: “Ought I not to try and comfort her, and how ought that to be done?” Finally, I began to feel vexed with her for placing me in such an awkward position.
uz: Keyin o'zimga o'ylay boshladim: "Men uni tasalli berishga urinib ko'rmayapmanmi va buni qanday qilish kerak?

en: “Surely my appearance is not so moving as all that?” I reflected.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, mening tashqi ko'rinishim shunchalik hayajonli emasmi? Men o'yladim.

en: “Or is she merely acting like this to see what I shall do under the circumstances?” “Yet it would not do for me to go,” I continued to myself, “for that would look too much as though I were fleeing to escape her tears.” Accordingly I began fidgeting about on my seat, in order to remind her of my presence.
uz: Yoki u shunchaki vaziyatda nima qilishimni ko'rish uchun shunday harakat qilyaptimi? Ammo men ketishim kerak emas, Men o'zimga davom ettirdim, chunki bu uning ko'z yoshlaridan qochib ketayotganim kabi ko'rinardi. Shu sababli men uning hozirligini eslatish uchun o'z o'rinimdagi o'rindiqimda tashvishlanishni boshladim.

en: “Oh, how foolish of me!” at length she said, as she gazed at me for a moment and tried to smile.
uz: "Oh, men qanchalik ahmoqman!" - deb so'radi u, bir zum menga tikilib, tabassum qilishga harakat qildi.

en: “There are days when one weeps for no reason whatever.” She felt about for her handkerchief, and then burst out weeping more violently than before.
uz: Ba'zi kunlarda hech qanday sababsiz yig'laymiz. U o'z to'plamini ko'rib, o'zidan ko'ra qattiqroq yig'lab chiqdi.

en: How silly of me to be for ever crying like this!
uz: Men bunday yig'lab yurganim naqadar ahmoqlikdir!

en: Yet I was so fond of your mother!
uz: Ammo men onangizni juda yaxshi ko'rardim!

en: We were such friends!
uz: Biz juda yaxshi do'st edik!

en: We-we—” At this point she found her handkerchief, and, burying her face in it, went on crying.
uz: Shu payt u o'z to'qimachasini topdi va yuzini unga ko'mib, yig'lab yubordi.

en: Once more I found myself in the same protracted dilemma.
uz: Men o'zimni yana bir bor o'sha uzoq davom etgan dilemaga tushirdim.

en: Though vexed, I felt sorry for her, since her tears appeared to be genuine—even though I also had an idea that it was not so much for my mother that she was weeping as for the fact that she was unhappy, and had known happier days.
uz: Garchi u xafa bo'lsa-da, uning ko'z yoshlari rostdek tuyulsa-da, men uning yig'lagani onam uchun emas, balki baxtsizligi va baxtli kunlarini ko'rganligi uchun bo'lganini bilardim.

en: How it would all have ended I do not know, had not her son reappeared and said that his father desired to see her.
uz: Bularning barchasi qanday tug'ilishi mumkin edi, bilmayman, agar uning o'g'li qaytadan paydo bo'lib, otasi uni ko'rishni istayotganini aytmaganida edi.

en: Thereupon she rose, and was just about to leave the room, when the General himself entered.
uz: Shunda u o'rnidan turib, xonadan chiqib ketmoqchi bo'lganida, generalning o'zi kirdi.

en: He was a small, grizzled, thick-set man, with bushy black eyebrows, a grey, close- cropped head, and a very stern, haughty expression of countenance.
uz: U kichkina, grizzled, qalin ko'rinadigan odam edi, qorishqoq qora ko'z burchaklari, oq, yaqin kesilgan bosh, va juda qattiq, mag'rur yuz ko'rinishi bilan.

en: I rose and bowed to him, but the General (who was wearing three stars on his green frockcoat) not only made no response to my salutation, but scarcely even looked at me; so that all at once I felt as though I were not a human being at all, but only some negligible object such as a settee or window; or, if I were a human being, as though I were quite indistinguishable from such a negligible object.
uz: Men turib unga sajda qildim, lekin general (ko'ylak kiyimida uch yulduz kiygan) mening salomlashimga javob bermaygina qolmadi, hatto menga hatto nazar ham solmadi; shu sababli birdan o'zimni umuman inson emas, balki bir set yoki deraza kabi ahamiyatsiz bir narsadan boshqa narsa emasdek his qildim; yoki, agar men inson bo'lsam, bunday ahamiyatsiz narsadan ajratib bo'lmaydigan bo'lib qoldim.

en: “Then you have not yet written to the Countess, my dear?” he said to his wife in French, and with an imperturbable, yet determined,
uz: - Shunday bo'lsa-da, siz hidoyatchiga hali yozmaganmisiz, azizim? - dedi u xotiniga frantsuz tilida va qat'iy, ammo qat'iy fikrda:

en: expression on his countenance.
uz: Uning yuzidagi ifodasini ko'rish.

en: “Good-bye, Monsieur Irtenieff,” Madame said to me, in her turn, as she made a proud gesture with her head and looked at my eyebrows just as her son had done.
uz: Xudojo'y, monsieur Irtenieff, Xonim menga o'z navbatida boshini ko'tarib, o'g'li qilganidek, ko'z burchaklarimga qarab, faxrli harakat qildi.

en: I bowed to her, and again to her husband, but my second salutation made no more impression upon him than if a window had just been opened or closed.
uz: Men unga va yana uning eriga sajda qildim, lekin ikkinchi salomim unga xuddi darcha ochilgan yoki yopilganidan ko'ra ko'proq taassurot qoldirmagan.

en: Nevertheless the younger Iwin accompanied me to the door, and on the way told me that he was to go to St.
uz: Shunga qaramay, kichik Iwin men bilan eshikga hamroh bo'ldi va yo'lda esa St.

en: Petersburg University, since his father had been appointed to a post in that city (and young Iwin named a very high office in the service).
uz: Petersburg universiteti, chunki otasi o'sha shaharda lavozimga tayinlangan edi (va yosh Iwin xizmatda juda yuqori lavozimni o'rnatgan).

en: “Well, his Papa may do whatsoever he likes,” I muttered to myself as I climbed into the drozhki, “but at all events I will never set foot in that house again.
uz: Hmm, uning otasi xohlaganini qila oladi, Drozhkiga chiqib ketayotganimda o'zimga g'iybat qildim,  lekin hech bo'lmaganda bu uyga yana hech qachon qadam qo'ymayman.

en: His wife weeps and looks at me as though I were the embodiment of woe, while that old pig of a General does not even give me a bow.
uz: Uning xotini yig'lab, menga qayg'uning o'zi bo'lganim kabi qaraydi, ammo o'sha generalning keksa cho'zi menga hatto sajda ham qilmaydi.

en: However, I will get even with him some day.” How I meant to do that I do not know, but my words nevertheless came true.
uz: Biroq, bir kun kelib unga qasos olishim kerak. Qanday qilib buni amalga oshirishni xohlaganimni bilmayman, lekin so'zlarim amalga oshdi.

en: Afterwards, I frequently found it necessary to remember the advice of my father when he said that I must cultivate the acquaintanceship of the Iwins, and not expect a man in the position of General Iwin to pay any attention to a boy like myself.
uz: Keyinchalik, otamning maslahatini eslab turish kerakligini ko'pincha ko'rdim, u shunday degan edi: "Men Iwinlar bilan tanishishni rivojlantirishim kerak va general Iwinning o'rniga o'tgan odamdan men kabi o'g'illarga e'tibor berishini kutmasligim kerak".

en: But I had figured in that position long enough.
uz: Ammo men o'sha holatda yetarlicha vaqt o'tkazgan edim.

en: PRINCE IVAN IVANOVITCH “Now for the last call—the visit to Nikitskaia Street,” I said to Kuzma, and we started for Prince Ivan Ivanovitch’s mansion.
uz: PRINCE IVAN IVANOVITCH  Endi so'nggi safar Nikitskaia ko'chasiga tashrif buyurish uchun Men Kuzmaga aytdim va biz Prins Ivan Ivanovitchning saroyiga ketdik.

en: Towards the end, a round of calls usually brings one a certain amount of self-assurance: consequently I was approaching the Prince’s abode in quite a tranquil frame of mind, when suddenly I
uz: Oxiriga kelib, qo'ng'iroqlar davri odatda o'ziga ishonch hosil qiladi: natijada, men o'zimni tinch his etib, printzning uyidan yaqinlashayotgan edim.

en: remembered the Princess Kornakoff’s words that I was his heir, and at the same moment caught sight of two carriages waiting at the portico.
uz: Qizim Kornakoffning men uning merosxo'ri ekanligim haqidagi so'zlarini eslab qoldi va shu paytning o'zida portikada ikkita vagon kutib turganini ko'rdi.

en: Instantly, my former nervousness returned.
uz: O'sha zahoti oldingi tashvishlarim qaytib keldi.

en: Both the old major-domo who opened the door to me, and the footman who took my coat, and the two male and three female visitors whom I found in the drawing-room, and, most of all, Prince Ivan Ivanovitch himself (whom I found clad in a “company” frockcoat and seated on a sofa) seemed to look at me as at an HEIR, and so to eye me with ill-will.
uz: Menga eshikni ochgan eski major-domo, kiyimimni olib ketgan xizmatkor, salonda uchta erkak va uchta ayol mehmon va, eng muhimi, o'zi Prens Ivan Ivanovitch (kuzatuv kiygan va kanepda o'tirgan) menga HEIR kabi qarayotgandek ko'rinardi va menga yomon niyat bilan qarayotgandek ko'rinardi.

en: Yet the Prince was very gracious and, after kissing me (that is to say, after pressing his cold, dry, flabby lips to my cheek for a second), asked me about my plans and pursuits, jested with me, inquired whether I still wrote verses of the kind which I used to indite in honour of my grandmother’s birthdays, and invited me to dine with him that day.
uz: Biroq, Prince juda mehribon bo'ldi va meni o'pgandan so'ng (ya'ni sovuq, quruq, bo'g'ib qolgan og'izlarini yonimga bir soniya bosganidan so'ng), rejalarim va maqsadlarim haqida so'radi, men bilan mashg'ul bo'ldi, men hali ham onamning tug'ilgan kunlari munosabati bilan o'qiganim kabi she'rlarni yozishimni so'radi va o'sha kuni u bilan birga ovqatlanishga taklif qildi.

en: Nevertheless, in proportion as he grew the kinder, the more did I feel persuaded that his civility was only intended to conceal from me the fact that he disliked the idea of my being his heir.
uz: Biroq, u o'sib borgan sari, uning xushmuomalaligi faqat uning merosxo'ri bo'lishimdan nafratlanishini mendan yashirish uchun mo'ljallanganligiga ishonch hosil qildim.

en: He had a custom (due to his false teeth, of which his mouth possessed a complete set) of raising his upper lip a little as he spoke, and producing a slight whistling sound from it; and whenever, on the present occasion, he did so it seemed to me that he was saying to himself: “A boy, a boy—I know it!
uz: Uning odati bor edi (o'zining yolg'on tishlari tufayli, og'zidan to'liq to'plamga ega edi) u gapirganida yuqori og'zini biroz ko'tarib, undan bir oz pishirish tovushini chiqarishi; va har safar u shunday qilganida, o'zimga o'zi shunday tuyuldi: "Qiz, o'g'lim, men buni bilaman!

en: And my heir, too —my heir!” When we were children, we had been used to calling the Prince “dear Uncle;” but now, in my capacity of heir, I could not bring my tongue to the phrase, while to say “Your Highness,” as did one of the other visitors, seemed derogatory to my self-esteem.
uz: Mening merosxo'rim ham - mening merosxo'rim! Biz bolalar bo'lganimizda, biz shohni "xayrli o'g'lim" deb atashgan edik; lekin endi merosxo'r sifatida tilimni so'zlarga to'ldirolmadim, ammo boshqa mehmonlardan biri kabi "Sening Oliyliging", deb aytish o'zimning hurmatimni kamsitadigan bo'ldi.

en: Consequently, never once during that visit did I call him anything at all.
uz: Natijada, bu tashrif paytida hech qachon unga hech qanday nom qo'ymaganman.

en: The personage, however, who most disturbed me was the old Princess who shared with me the position of prospective inheritor, and who lived in the Prince’s house.
uz: Biroq, meni eng ko'p xavotirga solgan shaxs, men bilan bo'lajak merosxo'r bo'lish vazifasini baham ko'radigan va Prinsning uyida yashayotgan qariya printsesa edi.

en: While seated beside her at dinner, I felt firmly persuaded that the reason why she would not speak to me was that she disliked me for being her co-heir, and that the Prince, for his part, paid no attention to our side of the table for the reason that the Princess and myself hoped to succeed him, and so were alike distasteful in his sight.
uz: Ovqatda uning yonida o'tirganimda, u men bilan gaplashmasligining sababi, uning sherik merosxo'ri bo'lganim uchun meni yoqtirmasligidan va princning o'z navbatida bizdan boshqa bir tomonga e'tibor bermasligidan, chunki princess va men uning o'rniga o'tishni umid qilganmiz va shuning uchun uning ko'zida bir xil achinarli ekanmiz, deb o'yladim.

en: “You cannot think how I hated it all!” I said to Dimitrieff the same evening, in a desire to make a parade of disliking the notion of being
uz: Siz o'ylay olmaysiz, men bularning barchasidan qanchalik nafratlanardim! Men Dimitriyevga o'sha kuni kechqurun, o'zimning mavjud bo'lish tushunchasidan nafratlanish paradini o'tkazish istagim bilan aytdim.

en: an heir (somehow I thought it the thing to do).
uz: merosxo'r (bir yo'l bilan men buni qilish kerak deb o'yladim).

en: “You cannot think how I loathed the whole two hours that I spent there!—Yet he is a fine- looking old fellow, and was very kind to me,” I added—wishing, among other things, to disabuse my friend of any possible idea that my loathing had arisen out of the fact that I had felt so small.
uz: Siz o'ylay olmaysiz, men o'sha yerda o'tkazgan ikki soatdan qanchalik nafratlanardim!Shunga qaramay, u juda yaxshi ko'rinadigan keksa odam va menga juda mehribon edi, Men o'zimni o'zimni juda kichik his qilganim tufayli nafratlanishim paydo bo'lganini do'stimga aytmoqchi bo'ldim.

en: “It is only the idea that people may be classing me with the Princess who lives with him, and who licks the dust off his boots.
uz: Men faqatgina o'zim bilan birga yashaydigan va oyoq kiyimlarining tuproqini yulib ketadigan princess bilan tanishib olishimni o'ylayman.

en: He is a wonderful old man, and good and considerate to everybody, but it is awful to see how he treats the Princess.
uz: U ajoyib keksa odam va hammaga mehribon va mehribon, ammo u princesaning munosabatini ko'rish dahshatli.

en: Money is a detestable thing, and ruins all human relations.
uz: Pul - bu jirkanch narsa va barcha inson munosabatlarini buzadi.

en: “Do you know, I think it would be far the best thing for me to have an open explanation with the Prince,” I went on; “to tell him that I respect him as a man, but think nothing of being his heir, and that I desire him to leave me nothing, since that is the only condition on which I can, in future, visit his house.” Instead of bursting out laughing when I said this, Dimitri pondered awhile in silence, and then answered: “You are wrong.
uz: Bilasizmi, mening fikrimcha, shoh bilan ochiq-oydin tushuntirish bo'lishi eng yaxshi narsa bo'lardi, - dedim men; unga uni erkak sifatida hurmat qilayotganimni, lekin uning vorisi bo'lish haqida hech narsa o'ylamaganimni va u menga hech narsa qoldirmasligini xohlayotganimni aytishim kerak, chunki bu kelajakda uning uyiga tashrif buyurishim mumkin bo'lgan yagona shart. Dimitriy bu so'zlarimni aytganda kulishning o'rniga, bir muncha vaqt sukutda mulohaza yuritdi va so'ng javob berdi: Siz noto'g'ri yo'l tutasiz.

en: Either you ought to refrain from supposing that people may be classing you with this Princess of whom you speak, or, if you DO suppose such a thing, you ought to suppose further that people are thinking what you yourself know quite well—namely, that such thoughts are so utterly foreign to your nature that you despise them and would never make them a basis for action.
uz: Yoki siz odamlar sizni siz gapirayotgan bu princess bilan birlashtirib o'tirishini tasavvur qilishdan bosh tortishingiz kerak, yoki agar siz shunday tasavvur qilsangiz, siz ham odamlar o'zingiz yaxshi bilgan narsani o'ylayotganini tasavvur qilishingiz kerak, ya'ni bunday fikrlar sizning tabiatingizga shunchalik chetda, siz ularni hurmat qilmaysiz va ularni hech qachon harakat qilish uchun asos qilmaysiz.

en: Suppose, however, that people DO suppose you to suppose such a thing— Well, to sum up,” he added, feeling that he was getting a little mixed in his pronouncements, “you had much better not suppose anything of the kind.” My friend was perfectly right, though it was not until long, long afterwards that experience of life taught me the evil that comes of thinking—still worse, of saying—much that seems very fine; taught me that there are certain thoughts which should always be kept to oneself, since brave words seldom go with brave deeds.
uz: Biroq, odamlar siz bunday narsani tasavvur qilishingizni tasavvur qilishadi deb tasavvur qiling Xo'sh, qisqacha aytganda, u qo'shimcha qildi, o'z so'zlarida biroz aralashib ketayotganini his etib,Siz bunday fikrlarni tasavvur qilmasligingiz yaxshiroqdir. Do'stim juda to'g'ri fikrda edi, garchi bu uzoq vaqt o'tgunga qadar bo'lmagan bo'lsa-da, hayot tajribasi menga yomonlikni o'rgatgan, xolos, yana yomonroq o'ylash, juda yaxshi ko'rinadigan ko'p narsalarni aytish; ba'zi fikrlar borligini o'rgatdi, ular har doim o'zimizda saqlanishi kerak, chunki jasoratli so'zlar kamdan-kam jasoratli harakatlar bilan birga keladi.

en: I learnt then that the mere fact of giving utterance to a good intention often makes it difficult, nay, impossible, to carry that good intention into effect.
uz: O'shanda o'rgandimki, yaxshi niyatni e'lon qilishning o'zi ko'pincha yaxshi niyatni amalga oshirishni qiyinlashtiradi, hatto imkonsiz qiladi.

en: Yet how is one to refrain from giving utterance to the brave, self- sufficient impulses of youth?
uz: Ammo yoshlikning jasoratli, o'z-o'zini ta'minlaydigan impulslariga qanday qilib javob bermaslik kerak?

en: Only long afterwards does one remember and regret them, even as one incontinently plucks a
uz: Faqat uzoq vaqt o'tgandan so'ng, odam ularni eslab, afsuslanadi, xuddi o'sha paytlarda u o'z-o'zidan ko'ngil uzish bilan o'zini o'ldiradi.

en: flower before its blooming, and subsequently finds it lying crushed and withered on the ground.
uz: gullashdan oldin gullaydi va keyinchalik uni yerga cho'mgan va qurigan holda topadi.

en: The very next morning I, who had just been telling my friend Dimitri that money corrupts all human relations, and had (as we have seen) squandered the whole of my cash on pictures and Turkish pipes, accepted a loan of twenty roubles which he suggested should pay for my travelling expenses into the country, and remained a long while thereafter in his debt!
uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab do'stim Dimitriga pul barcha inson munosabatlarini buzib qo'yganini aytib, butun pulimni rasmlar va turkiy quvurlarga sarflaganimda, men yigirma rubllik qarzni qabul qildim, uning so'zlariga ko'ra, men mamlakatga sayohat xarajatlarini to'lashim kerak edi va keyinchalik uzoq vaqt qarzdor bo'ldim!

en: INTIMATE CONVERSATION WITH MY FRIEND THIS conversation of ours took place in a phaeton on the way to Kuntsevo.
uz: Do'stim bilan yaqin muloqot Kuntsevoga borayotganimizda bu suhbatimiz faetonda bo'lib o'tdi.

en: Dimitri had invited me in the morning to go with him to his mother’s, and had called for me after luncheon; the idea being that I should spend the evening, and perhaps also pass the night, at the country-house where his family lived.
uz: Dimitri meni ertalab o'zi bilan onalariga borishga taklif qilgan edi va kechki ovqatdan so'ng meni chaqirgan edi; mening fikrim shundaki, kechki payt uning oilasi yashaydigan qishloq uyida o'tkazishim kerak edi, ehtimol kechki payt ham o'tirishim kerak edi.

en: Only when we had left the city and exchanged its grimy streets and the unbearably deafening clatter of its pavements for the open vista of fields and the subdued grinding of carriage-wheels on a dusty high road (while the sweet spring air and prospect enveloped us on every side) did I awake from the new impressions and sensations of freedom into which the past two days had plunged me.
uz: Shaharni tark etib, uning qorong'i ko'chalari va yo'llaridagi ko'chalarning ko'rinishi va ko'chalarning ko'rinishi bilan o'zgarib ketgandan so'ng, to'stli yo'ldagi ko'chalar ko'rinishi va ko'chma-ko'chma aravalarning siljishi bilan o'zgarib ketdik (ko'rinish va ko'rinish bizni har tomondan o'rab olgan) so'nggi ikki kun meni o'ziga jalb qilgan yangi his-tuyg'ular va erkinlik his-tuyg'ularidan uyg'onib qoldim.

en: Dimitri was in his kind and sociable mood.
uz: Dimitri o'zining mehribon va mehribon ruhida edi.

en: That is to say, he was neither frowning nor blinking nervously nor straightening his neck in his collar.
uz: Ya'ni, u na burunni burib, na g'azab bilan ko'z yumib, na bo'yni bo'ynini to'g'ridan-to'g'ri to'g'rilab qo'ymagan.

en: For my own part, I was congratulating myself on those noble sentiments which I have expressed above, in the belief that they had led him to overlook my shameful encounter with Kolpikoff, and to refrain from despising me for it.
uz: Men o'zimni yuqorida aytib o'tgan noyob his-tuyg'ularim uchun tabriklab, ular uni Kolpikoff bilan yuz bergan o'yinimni e'tiborsiz qoldirishiga va bu uchun meni kamsitishdan to'xtatishiga sabab bo'lganini bilardim.

en: Thus we talked together on many an intimate subject which
uz: Shunday qilib, biz ko'pchilik bilan yaqin mavzuda suhbatlashdik.

en: even a friend seldom mentions to a friend.
uz: Hatto do'st ham do'st haqida kamdan-kam gapiradi.

en: He told me about his family whose acquaintance I had not yet made—about his mother, his aunt, and his sister, as also about her whom Woloda and Dubkoff believed to be his “flame,” and always spoke of as “the lady with the chestnut locks.” Of his mother he spoke with a certain cold and formal commendation, as though to forestall any further mention of her; his aunt he extolled enthusiastically, though with a touch of condescension in his tone; his sister he scarcely mentioned at all, as though averse to doing so in my presence; but on the subject of “the lady with the chestnut locks” (whose real name was Lubov Sergievna, and who was a grown-up young lady living on a family footing with the Nechludoffs) he discoursed with animation.
uz: U menga onasi, onasi va singlisi haqida, shuningdek, Voloda va Dubkoffning o'ylashicha, u uning lamasi, deb hisoblagan oilasi haqida gapirdi. Onasi haqida u o'zini boshqa hech qanday eslatib o'tmaslik uchun biroz sovuq va rasmiy maqtov bilan gapirdi; onasi haqida u hayajon bilan maqtagan, garchi uning oyog'ida kamtarlik hissasi bo'lsa-da; singlisi haqida u kamdan-kam aytib o'tgan, chunki u mening huzurimda bunday qilishni xohlamagan; lekin 

en: “Yes, she is a wonderful woman,” he said with a conscious reddening of the face, yet looking me in the eyes with dogged temerity.
uz: "Ha, u ajoyib ayol", - dedi u, yuzidagi qizargan ko'rinish bilan, ammo ko'zlarimga qat'iy ehtiyotkorlik bilan qaradi.

en: “True, she is no longer young, and even rather elderly, as well as by no means good-looking; but as for loving a mere featherhead, a mere beauty—well, I never could understand that, for it is such a silly thing to do.” (Dimitri said this as though he had just discovered a most novel and extraordinary truth.) “I am certain, too, that such a soul, such a heart and principles, as are hers are not to be found elsewhere in the world of the present day.” (I do not know whence he had derived the habit of saying that few good things were discoverable in the world of the present day, but at all events he loved to repeat the expression, and it somehow suited him.) “Only, I am afraid,” he went on quietly, after thus annihilating all such men as were foolish enough to admire mere beauty, “I am afraid that you will not understand or realise her quickly.
uz: To'g'ri, u endi yosh emas va hatto yoshi ulug' emas, balki hech qachon chiroyli emas; lekin oddiy tovuqni sevish, oddiy go'zallikni sevish haqida gap ketganda, men buni hech qachon tushunolmayman, chunki bu juda ahmoqona ish. (Dimitri buni xuddi yangilik va g'alati haqiqatni kashf etganidek aytdi.) Men ham shubhalanamanki, uning ruhi, yuragi va me'yorlari singari uning ruhi hozirgi dunyoda boshqa joyda topilmaydi. (Men bilmayman, u hozirgi dunyoda yaxshi narsalarni topish mumkin emas, degan odatni qayerdan olgan, lekin u bu so'zni takrorlashni yaxshi ko'radi va bu unga qandaydir mos keladi.)  Faqat, qo'rqaman, u, shu tariqa, go'zallikka hayron bo'lgan barcha odamlarni o'ldirganidan so'ng, o'zini sekin yo'q qildi. (Men uning go'zalligidan qo'rqmayman, lekin u hozirgi dunyoda juda oz yaxshi narsalarni kashf etish mumkin, deb aytish odati bor edi, deb aytaman.)  Faqat, qo'rqaman,  Men uni tushunaman, shu tarzda tezda davom etdi, shu tarzda barcha odamlarni o'ldirganidan keyin uning go'zalligini hayron qoldirdim.

en: She is modest, even secretive, and by no means fond of exhibiting her beautiful and surprising qualities.
uz: U kamtarin, hatto yashirin va o'zining go'zal va hayratlanarli fazilatlarini ko'rsatishni yoqtirmaydi.

en: Now, my mother—who, as you will see, is a noble, sensible woman—has known Lubov Sergievna, for many years; yet even to this day she does not properly understand her.
uz: Endi, ko'rasiz, onam - buyuk, aqlli ayol - Lubov Sergiyevnani ko'p yillardan beri biladi, ammo hozirgacha uni to'g'ri tushunmayapti.

en: Shall I tell you why I was out of temper last evening when you were questioning me?
uz: Kecha meni so'roq qilayotganingizda nega g'azablanganimni aytsam bo'ladimi?

en: Well, you must know that the day before yesterday Lubov asked me to accompany her to Ivan Yakovlevitch’s (you have heard of him, I suppose?
uz: Balki bilishingiz kerakki, bir kun oldin Lubov meni Ivan Yakovlevitchlarga hamroh bo'lishimni so'rabdi (u haqda eshitganmisiz, deb o'ylayman?

en: the fellow who seems to be mad, but who, in reality, is a very remarkable man).
uz: O'zi g'alati ko'rinadigan, lekin aslida esa ajoyib odam bo'lgan odam).

en: Well, Lubov is extremely religious, and understands Ivan Yakovlevitch to the full.
uz: Lubov juda diniy va Ivan Yakovlevitchni to'liq tushunadi.

en: She often goes to see him, and converses with him, and gives him money for the poor—money which she has earned herself.
uz: Ko'pincha u bilan uchrashishga boradi va u bilan suhbatlashadi va o'zi kasb etgan kambag'al pul uchun unga pul beradi.

en: She is a marvellous woman, as you will see.
uz: Ko'rasiz, u ajoyib ayol.

en: Well, I went with her to Ivan’s, and felt very grateful to her for having afforded me the opportunity of exchanging a word with so remarkable a man; but my mother could not understand our action at all, and discerned in it only superstition.
uz: Men u bilan birga Ivonlarga bordim va menga bunday ajoyib odam bilan suhbatlashish imkoniyatini bergani uchun juda minnatdor edim; lekin onam bizning harakatimizni umuman tushunmadi va u yerda faqat sehr-jodularni ko'rdi.

en: Consequently, last night she and I quarrelled for the first time in our lives.
uz: Natijada, o'tgan kecha u va men hayotimizda birinchi marta bahslashdik.

en: A very bitter one it was, too,” he concluded, with a convulsive shrug of his shoulders, as though the mention of it recalled the feelings which he had then experienced.
uz: Bu ham juda achchiq edi, deb xulosa qildi u, omon qolishi bilan, xuddi bu haqda gap ketganda u o'sha paytda boshdan kechirgan his-tuyg'ularni eslatgandek.

en: “And what are your intentions about it all?” I inquired, to divert him from such a disagreeable recollection.
uz: Va bularning barchasi bilan bog'liq niyatlaringiz nima? Men uni bunday noqulay xotiralardan chalg'itish uchun so'radim.

en: “That is to say, how do you imagine it is going to turn out?
uz: Ya'ni, bu qanday bo'lishini tasavvur qilasiz?

en: Do you ever speak to her about the future, or about how your love or friendship are going to end?” “Do you mean, do I intend to marry her eventually?” he inquired, in his turn, with a renewed blush, but turning himself round and looking me boldly in the face.
uz: Siz u bilan kelajak haqida yoki sizning sevgingiz yoki do'stligingiz qanday tugayotgani haqida gapiryapsizmi?Mening aytgandek, men u bilan keyinchalik turmush qurishni rejalashtiryapmanmi? U o'z navbatida o'z navbatida o'zini o'zgartirgan, ammo o'zini o'zgartirgan va jasorat ila yuzimga qaragan kishi so'radi.

en: “Yes, certainly,” I replied as I settled myself down.
uz: Ha, albatta, O'zimni o'zimga joylashtirganimda javob berdim.

en: “We are both of us grown-up, as well as friends, so we may as well discuss our future life as we drive along.
uz: Biz ikkalasi ham kattalarmiz, do'stlarmiz, shuning uchun sayohatda kelajagimizni muhokama qilishimiz mumkin.

en: No one could very well overlook or overhear us now.” “Why should I NOT marry her?” he went on in response to my reassuring reply.
uz: Hozir hech kim bizni e'tiborsiz qoldirolmaydi yoki eshitolmaydi.  Nima uchun men u bilan turmush qurmasam kerak? U mening tasalli beruvchi javobimga javoban davom etdi.

en: “It is my aim—as it should be the aim of every honourable man—to be as good and as happy as possible; and with her, if she should still be willing when I have become more independent, I should be happier and better than with the greatest beauty in the world.” Absorbed in such conversation, we hardly noticed that we were approaching Kuntsevo, or that the sky was becoming overcast and beginning to threaten rain.
uz: Bu mening maqsadimdir, har bir hurmatli odamning maqsadi iloji boricha yaxshiroq va baxtli bo'lishdir; va agar men mustaqil bo'lganimda ham u bilan birga bo'lish istagini bildirsa, men dunyodagi eng buyuk go'zallikdan ko'ra baxtliroq va yaxshiroq bo'laman. Bunday suhbatda o'zimizni tutgan holda, biz Kuntsevoga yaqinlashayotganimizni yoki osmon bulutga aylanib, yomg'irga tahdid solishni boshlaganimizni anglab yetmagan edik.

en: On the right, the sun was slowly sinking behind the ancient trees of the Kuntsevo park—one half of its brilliant disc obscured with grey, subluminous cloud, and the other half sending forth spokes of flaming light which threw the old trees into striking relief as they stood there with their dense crowns of green showing against a blue patch of sky.
uz: O'ng tomonda quyosh Kuntsevo parkining qadimgi daraxtlari orqasida sekin-sekin botib ketayotgan edi, yarmi o'zining chiroyli diskini griz, yorug'lik bulutlari bilan qoplagan edi, boshqa yarmi esa o'tli nur so'zlarini yuborib, eski daraxtlarni o'zlarining ko'k rangli koronalari bilan ko'k ko'k parchaga qarshi ko'rinayotgan holda turganlarida sezilarli darajada yengillashtirgan edi.

en: The light and shimmer of that patch contrasted sharply with the heavy pink cloud which lay massed above a young birch-tree visible on the horizon before us, while, a
uz: Bu joyning yorug'ligi va chiroqlari biz ko'rgan ko'rinishda ko'rinadigan yosh bir qoramolning ustida joylashgan rosa bulut bilan keskin farq qilardi.

en: little further to the right, the parti-coloured roofs of the Kuntsevo mansion could be seen projecting above a belt of trees and undergrowth—one side of them reflecting the glittering rays of the sun, and the other side harmonising with the more louring portion of the heavens.
uz: O'ng tomondan qisman rangli xonadonning toshlari daraxtlar bo'g'inining ustida ko'rinadi, ularning bir tomoni quyoshning shishaq nurlarini aks ettirgan, boshqa tomoni esa osmonning ko'proq bo'sh qismi bilan uyg'unlashgan.

en: Below us, and to the left, showed the still blue of a pond where it lay surrounded with pale-green laburnums—its dull, concave-looking depths repeating the trees in more sombre shades of colour over the surface of a hillock.
uz: Bizdan pastda va chap tomonda, o'sha hovuzning ko'k ko'k ko'rinishi ko'rinadi, u o'tkir-yashil laburnumlar bilan o'rab olingan.Bu o'tkir, konkav bo'lgan chuqurliklarni ko'rsatadi, daraxtlar ko'proq qorong'u ranglarda tog'ning yuzasida takrorlanadi.

en: Beyond the water spread the black expanse of a ploughed field, with the straight line of a dark- green ridge by which it was bisected running far into the distance, and there joining the leaden, threatening horizon.
uz: Suvning tashqarisida cho'zilgan maydonning qora maydoni bo'lib, qorong'i yashil toshli bo'lakning to'g'ri chizig'i uzoqroq bo'lib ketadi va u erda qo'shilgan qo'llanma, xavf ostiga qo'shilgan gorizontga qo'shiladi.

en: On either side of the soft road along which the phaeton was pursuing the even tenour of its way, bright-green, tangled, juicy belts of rye were sprouting here and there into stalk.
uz: Faeton o'z yo'lining qat'iy bo'linishini izlayotgan yumshatli yo'lning har ikki tomoniga, yorqin-yashil, to'p-to'p, shomish rangli, shomish rangli maydonlar birma-bir o'simlik bo'lib o'sib borar edi.

en: Not a motion was perceptible in the air, only a sweet freshness, and everything looked extraordinarily clear and bright.
uz: Havoda hech qanday harakat ko'rinmas edi, faqat shirin ta'sir ko'rinardi va hamma narsa nihoyatda aniq va yorqin ko'rinardi.

en: Near the road I could see a little brown path winding its way among the dark-green, quarter-grown stems of rye, and somehow that path reminded me vividly of our village, and somehow (through some connection of thought) the idea of that village reminded me vividly of Sonetchka, and so of the fact that I was in love with her.
uz: Yo'l yaqinida qorong'i yashil, chorak o'sgan bo'laklar orasida o'z yo'lini o'rab olgan kichik bir qalin yo'l ko'rardim va bu yo'l meni o'z qishlog'imizni o'z ichiga olgan edi va bir yo'l bilan (o'ylash bilan bog'liq bo'lgan) o'sha qishlog'ning g'oyasi meni Sonetchka va men unga muhabbatli ekanligimni o'z ichiga olgan edi.

en: Notwithstanding my fondness for Dimitri and the pleasure which his frankness had afforded me, I now felt as though I desired to hear no more about his feelings and intentions with regard to Lubov Sergievna, but to talk unstintedly about my own love for Sonetchka, who seemed to me an object of affection of a far higher order.
uz: Dimitriyga bo'lgan sevgim va uning ochiqligi menga bergan zavq-shafqatga qaramay, endi Lubov Sergiyevnaga nisbatan uning his-tuyg'ulari va niyatlari haqida eshitishni istamay, o'zimni ancha yuqori darajadagi sevgi ob'ektiga o'xshatgan Sonetchkaga bo'lgan sevgim haqida to'xtamasdan gapirishni istardim.

en: Yet for some reason or another I could not make up my mind to tell him straight out how splendid it would seem when I had married Sonetchka and we were living in the country—of how we should have little children who would crawl about the floor and call me Papa, and of how delighted I should be when he, Dimitri, brought his wife, Lubov Sergievna, to see us, wearing an expensive gown.
uz: Ammo shu yoki shu sabablarga ko'ra, Men unga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aytishga qaror qila olmadim, Men Sonetchka bilan turmush qurganimda va biz qishloq joyda yashayotganimizda qanday ajoyib ko'rinishi mumkinligini aytish mumkin edi, qanday qilib bizda katta yoshli bolalar bor bo'lishi kerak edi, ular yer yuziga kirishib, meni ota deb atashadi, va Dimitri o'z xotini Lubov Sergievnani bizni ko'rish uchun qimmat kiyim kiygan holda olib kelganida men qanchalik xursand bo'lishim kerak edi.

en: Accordingly, instead of saying all that, I pointed to the setting sun, and merely remarked: “Look, Dimitri!
uz: Shunday qilib, men hammasini aytishning o'rniga, quyosh botayotganini ko'rsatdim va shunchaki: "Qarang, Dimitriy!

en: How splendid!” To this, however, Dimitri made no reply, since he was evidently dissatisfied at my answering his confession (which it had cost him much to make) by directing his attention to natural objects (to which
uz: Qanday ajoyib! Bunga Dimitri javob bermadi, chunki men uning tanloviga javob berishimdan mamnun emas edi (bu uni juda ko'p pul sarflagan edi) va uning e'tiborini tabiiy ob'ektlarga qaratganimda (bularga) mamnun emas edi.

en: he was, in general, indifferent).
uz: u, umuman olganda, befarq edi).

en: Upon him Nature had an effect altogether different to what she had upon myself, for she affected him rather by her industry than by her beauty—he loved her rather with his intellect than with his senses.
uz: U uchun tabiatning o'zimga nisbatan ta'siri umuman boshqacha edi, chunki u uni go'zalligidan ko'ra ko'proq ishbilarmonligi bilan ta'sir qilardi.U uni hissiyotlari bilan emas, aqli bilan yaxshi ko'rgan.

en: “I am absolutely happy,” I went on, without noticing that he was altogether taken up with his own thoughts and oblivious of anything that I might be saying.
uz: Men mutlaqo baxtliman, Men davom ettirdim, u o'z fikrlari bilan to'liq band ekanini va men aytayotgan narsalardan bexabar ekanini sezmay.

en: “You will remember how told you about a girl with whom I used to be in love when was a little boy?
uz: Siz kichikligingizda men sevgan bir qiz haqida sizga nimalar aytilganini eslaysizmi?

en: Well, I saw her again only this morning, and am now infatuated with her.” Then I told him—despite his continued expression of indifference—about my love, and about all my plans for my future connubial happiness.
uz: Xo'sh, men uni yana faqat bugun ertalab ko'rdim va hozir unga juda yoqdim. Keyin men unga sevgim va kelajakdagi baxt uchun barcha rejalarim haqida g'amxo'rlik qilmaganidan qat'iy nazar aytdim.

en: Strangely enough, no sooner had I related in detail the whole strength of my feelings than I instantly became conscious of its diminution.
uz: Ajablanarlisi shundaki, his-tuyg'ularimning butun kuchini batafsil bayon etganimdan so'ng, o'zim tezda ularning kamayishi haqida o'yladim.

en: The rain overtook us just as we were turning into the avenue of birch-trees which led to the house, but it did not really wet us.
uz: Yomg'ir bizni uyga olib boradigan birch daraxtlari yo'liga aylanayotganimizda ushlab qoldi, lekin bizni chindan ham bosmasdi.

en: I only knew that it was raining by the fact that I felt a drop fall, first on my nose, and then on my hand, and heard something begin to patter upon the young, viscous leaves of the birch-trees as, drooping their curly branches overhead, they seemed to imbibe the pure, shining drops with an avidity which filled the whole avenue with scent.
uz: Men faqatgina bu yomg'ir yog'ayotganini bilardim, chunki birinchi navbatda burnimda, so'ngra qo'limda bir tomchi tomchi yog'ayotganini his qildim va bir narsa birqachak daraxtlarining yosh, chiroyli barglariga to'p-to'p bo'lganini eshitdim, chunki ular boshi ustida o'zlarining tikilgan shoxlarini quvib, toza, shinam tomchilarni xushbo'ylik bilan sug'orib, butun ko'chani xushbo'y tutatga to'ldirgan edilar.

en: We descended from the carriage, so as to reach the house the quicker through the garden, but found ourselves confronted at the entrance- door by four ladies, two of whom were knitting, one reading a book, and the fourth walking to and fro with a little dog.
uz: Biz bog'dan tezroq uyga yetib kelish uchun vagonadan tushdik, lekin kirish eshigida to'rtta ayol o'zimizni ko'rdik, ulardan ikkitasi tikishardi, bittasi kitob o'qiyotgan edi, to'rtinchisi esa kichkina it bilan bir-biriga yurib borardi.

en: Thereupon, Dimitri began to present me to his mother, sister, and aunt, as well as to Lubov Sergievna.
uz: Keyin Dimitri meni onasi, singlisi va xotini, shuningdek, Lubov Sergiyevna bilan tanishtirishni boshladi.

en: For a moment they remained where they were, but almost instantly the rain became heavier.
uz: Ular bir muncha vaqt o'zlari turgan joyda qolishdi, lekin deyarli darhol yomg'ir og'irlashdi.

en: “Let us go into the verandah; you can present him to us there,” said the lady whom I took to be Dimitri’s mother, and we all of us ascended the entrance-steps.
uz: Kelinglar, verandaga kiraylik; uni o'sha yerda bizga taqdim etasiz, - dedi Dimitriyning onasi deb bilgan xonim. - Biz hammamiz kirish qadamlariga ko'tardik.

en: From the first, the member of this company who struck me the most was Lubov Sergievna, who, holding a lapdog in her arms and wearing stout laced boots, was the last of the four ladies to ascend the staircase, and twice stopped to gaze at me intently and then kiss her little dog.
uz: Birinchidan, meni eng ko'p hayratda qoldirgan ushbu kompaniyaning a'zosi Lubov Sergiyevna edi, u qo'llarida itni ushlab, kuchli ipli poyabzallar kiygan to'rt ayoldan so'nggi biri bo'lib, daraxtga chiqdi va ikki marta menga diqqat bilan qarash uchun to'xtadi va so'ngra o'zining kichkina itini o'padi.

en: She was anything but good-looking, since she was red- haired, thin, short, and slightly crooked.
uz: U qizil sochli, chiroyli, qisqa va biroz burak bo'lgani sababli, chiroyli emas edi.

en: What made her plain face all the plainer was the queer way in which her hair was parted to one side (it looked like the wigs which bald women contrive for themselves).
uz: Uning yuzini soddalashtirgan narsa - sochlarining bir tomonga bo'linishining g'ayritabiiy usuli edi (u sochli ayollar o'zlari uchun yaratadigan peruklarga o'xshardi).

en: However much I should have liked to applaud my friend, I could not find a single comely feature in her.
uz: Do'stimni qanchalik quvonch bilan qo'llab-quvvatlasam ham, uning hech qanday chiroyli xususiyatini topolmadim.

en: Even her brown eyes, though expressive of good-humour, were small and dull— were, in fact, anything but pretty; while her hands (those most characteristic of features), were though neither large nor ill-shaped, coarse and red.
uz: Hatto uning qaroq ko'zlari ham, garchi yaxshi humorni ko'rsatadigan bo'lsa-da, kichik va chiroyli edi Aslida, go'zaldan tashqari hamma narsa edi; qo'llari esa (bu xususiyatlarning eng xususiyatlari) katta ham emas edi, yomon shakli ham emas edi, qo'pol va qizil.

en: As soon as we reached the verandah, each of the ladies, except Dimitri’s sister Varenika—who also had been regarding me attentively out of her large, dark-grey eyes—said a few words to me before resuming her occupation, while Varenika herself began to read aloud from a book which she held on her lap and steadied with her finger.
uz: Verandaga yetib borganimiz sayin, Dimitrining singlisi Varenika'dan tashqari, har bir ayol menga katta, qorong'i sariq ko'zlari bilan diqqat bilan qarab turardi va o'z ishini davom ettirishdan oldin menga bir necha so'z aytdi, Varenika esa o'zi qo'lida qo'yib, barmog'i bilan o'qib o'qishni boshladi.

en: The Princess Maria Ivanovna was a tall, well-built woman of forty.
uz: Princess Maria Ivanovna qirq yoshli baland, yaxshi qurilgan ayol edi.

en: To judge by the curls of half-grey hair which descended below her cap one might have taken her for more, but as soon as ever one observed the fresh, extraordinarily tender, and almost wrinkleless face, as well as, most of all, the lively, cheerful sparkle of the large eyes, one involuntarily took her for less.
uz: Uning qo'rqinchidan pastga tushayotgan yarim sariq sochli bo'laklardan xulosa qilsak, uni ko'proq deb bilgan bo'lar edi, lekin yangi, nihoyatda tender va deyarli burchaksiz yuzini va eng asosiysi, katta ko'zlarning hayajonli, quvonchli chiroqlarini ko'rganimizda, uni kamroq deb bilgan bo'lamiz.

en: Her eyes were black and very frank, her lips thin and slightly severe, her nose regular and slightly inclined to the left, and her hands ringless, large, and almost like those of a man, but with finely tapering fingers.
uz: Uning ko'zlari qora va juda ochiq, og'zaki chiroyli va biroz og'ir, burni muntazam va biroz chap tomonga moyil, qo'llari ham bog'siz, katta va deyarli erkaklarga o'xshaydi, ammo barmoqlari juda chiroyli.

en: She wore a dark- blue dress fastened to the throat and sitting closely to her firm, still youthful waist—a waist which she evidently pinched.
uz: U qorong'i ko'k rangli kiyim kiygan va qo'liga bog'langan va o'zining mustahkam, hali ham yoshlik belini o'rab olgan.

en: Lastly, she held herself very upright, and was knitting a garment of some kind.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, u o'zini juda to'g'ri tutdi va bir xil kiyim tikardi.

en: As soon as I stepped on to the verandah she took me by the hand, drew me to her as though wishing to scrutinise me more closely, and said, as she gazed at me with the same cold, candid glance as her son’s, that she had long known me by report from Dimitri, and that
uz: Men verandaga qadam bosganimdan so'ng, u qo'limdan ushlab, meni o'ziga jalb qildi, xuddi menga ko'proq e'tibor berishni xohlagandek, va menga o'g'illari kabi sovuq va ochiq ko'z bilan qaraganida, meni uzoq vaqtdan beri Dimitrining xabaridan tanib-bilganini va bu haqda aytdi.

en: therefore, in order to make my acquaintance thoroughly, she had invited me to stay these twenty-four hours in her house.
uz: Shuning uchun, menga yaxshi tanish bo'lish uchun u menga uyida 24 soat turishga taklif qildi.

en: “Do just as you please here,” she said, “and stand on no ceremony whatever with us, even as we shall stand on none with you.
uz: Bu yerda o'zingiz xohlaganingizni qiling, - dedi u, - va biz bilan hech qanday marosimga qo'shilmang, biz ham siz bilan hech qanday marosimga qo'shilmaymiz.

en: Pray walk, read, listen, or sleep as the mood may take you.” Sophia Ivanovna was an old maid and the Princess’s younger sister, though she looked the elder of the two.
uz: Yuz yurish, o'qish, tinglash yoki uxlash uchun ibodat qiling. Sofiya Ivanovna keksa xizmatkor va princesaning singlisi edi, ammo u ikkovidan katta ko'rinardi.

en: She had that exceedingly overstuffed appearance which old maids always present who are short of stature but wear corsets.
uz: Uning ko'rinishi juda ko'p bo'lgan, bu ko'rinish ko'rinishida katta bo'lmagan, lekin korset kiygan keksa xizmatkorlar doim bor edi.

en: It seemed as though her healthiness had shifted upwards to the point of choking her, her short, fat hands would not meet below her projecting bust, and the line of her waist was scarcely visible at all.
uz: Uning sog'lig'i yuqoriga ko'tarilgan, hatto cho'kkancha bo'lib qolgan, qisqa va katta qo'llari o'z boshi ostida uchrashmaydi va belining chizig'i kamdan-kam ko'rinadi.

en: Notwithstanding that the Princess Maria Ivanovna had black hair and eyes, while Sophia Ivanovna had white hair and large, vivacious, tranquilly blue eyes (a rare combination), there was a great likeness between the two sisters, for they had the same expression, nose, and lips.
uz: Princess Maria Ivanovna qora soch va ko'zlarga ega bo'lishiga qaramay, Sofiya Ivanovna oq soch va katta, jonli, xotirjam ko'k ko'zlarga ega bo'lsa-da, ikkita singil o'rtasida katta o'xshashlik bor edi, chunki ularning ifodasi, yuzi va dudasi bir xil edi.

en: The only difference was that Sophia’s nose and lips were a trifle coarser than Maria’s, and that, when she smiled, those features inclined towards the right, whereas Maria’s inclined towards the left.
uz: Faqatgina farqi shundaki, Sofiya ning yuzi va tili Mariyaning yuziga qaraganda biroz qalinroq edi va u tabassum qilganida, bu belgilar o'ng tomonga, Mariyaning esa chap tomonga moyil edi.

en: Sophia, to judge by her dress and coiffure, was still youthful at heart, and would never have displayed grey curls, even if she had possessed them.
uz: Sofiya, kiyim-kechak va sochlarini ko'rib chiqayotganda, hali ham yosh bo'lgan va hatto o'ziga tegishli bo'lsa ham, hech qachon griq bo'ylaklarni ko'rsatmagan.

en: Yet at first her glance and bearing towards me seemed very proud, and made me nervous, whereas I at once felt at home with the Princess.
uz: Biroq, birinchi qarashda uning ko'z o'ngida va menga ko'rinishi juda g'ururli ko'rinardi va meni xavotirga solgan edi, men esa o'zimni darhol o'zimni printsess bilan uyda his qildim.

en: Perhaps it was only Sophia’s stoutness and a certain resemblance to portraits of Catherine the Great that gave her, in my eyes, a haughty aspect, but at all events I felt quite intimidated when she looked at me intently and said, “Friends of our friends are our friends also.” I became reassured and changed my opinion about her only when, after saying those words, she opened her mouth and sighed deeply.
uz: Ehtimol, faqat Sofiyaning jasoratliligi va Katrin buyukning portretiga o'xshashligi uni mening ko'zimda mag'rur ko'rinishga ega qildi, lekin u menga diqqat bilan qarab: "Dostlarimizning do'stlari ham bizning do'stlarimiz", - deb aytganda, men juda qo'rqib ketdim. Men faqat o'sha so'zlarni aytgandan so'ng og'zini ochib, chuqur nafas olgach, u haqida fikrimni o'zgartirib, tasalli topdim.

en: It may be that she owed her habit of sighing after every few words—with a great distention of the mouth and a slight drooping of her large blue eyes—to her stoutness, yet it was none the less one which expressed so much good-humour that I at once lost all fear of her, and found her actually attractive.
uz: Ehtimol, u har bir so'zdan so'ng nafas olish odatini, og'zini ko'p uzatib, katta ko'k ko'zlarini biroz quvib qo'yganini o'zining kuchliligiga bog'lagan bo'lishi mumkin, ammo bu juda ko'p xushmuomalalikni bildirgan narsa edi, shuning uchun men darhol undan qo'rqishni yo'qotib, uni chindan ham jozibali deb topdim.
