en: Her eyes were charming, her voice pleasant and musical, and even the flowing lines of her fullness seemed to my youthful vision not wholly lacking in beauty.
uz: Uning ko'zlari chiroyli edi, ovozi yoqimli va musiqiy edi va hatto to'liqligini ko'rsatadigan so'zlar yoshlik ko'zimga go'zallikdan kam bo'lmaganidek ko'rinardi.

en: I had imagined that Lubov Sergievna, as my friend’s friend, would at once say something friendly and familiar to me; yet, after gazing at me fixedly for a while, as though in doubt whether the remark she was about to make to me would not be too friendly, she at length asked me what faculty I was in.
uz: Men o'zimni do'stimning do'sti sifatida Lubov Sergiyevna menga do'stlik va tanishlik bilan bir narsa aytishini tasavvur qilgan edim; ammo bir muncha vaqt menga qattiq qaraganidan so'ng, u menga aytmoqchi bo'lgan so'z juda mehribon bo'lmasligiga shubha ostiga qolib, oxir-oqibat mendan qaysi fakultetda o'qiganimni so'radi.

en: After that she stared at me as before, in evident hesitation as to whether or not to say something civil and familiar, until, remarking her perplexity, I besought her with a look to speak freely.
uz: Shundan so'ng u menga avvalgidek qaradi va biror xushmuomala va tanish so'zlarni aytish yoki aytmaslik haqida ko'rinmas shubha ostiga qo'ydi, o'sha paytgacha uning g'alatiligini e'tiborga olib, erkin gapirishni iltijo qildim.

en: Yet all she then said was, “They tell me the Universities pay very little attention to science now,” and turned away to call her little dog.
uz: Ammo u faqat shunday dedi: "Menga aytadilarki, hozir universitetlar ilm-fanga juda kam e'tibor qaratmoqdalar" va o'zidan yuz o'girib, o'zining itini chaqirishdi.

en: All that evening she spoke only in disjointed fragments of this kind —fragments which had no connection either with the point or with one another; yet I had such faith in Dimitri, and he so often kept looking from her to me with an expression which mutely asked me, “Now, what do you think of that?” that, though I entirely failed to persuade myself that in Lubov Sergievna there was anything to speak of, I could not bear to express the thought, even to myself.
uz: O'sha kecha davomida u faqatgina bu mavzu bilan ham, bir-biri bilan ham bog'liq bo'lmagan buyumlar bilan gapirdi; lekin men Dimitriga qattiq ishonardim va u ko'p marotaba menga o'z ko'zidan qarab, so'zsiz so'ragan ifodasi bilan: "Hndi bu haqda nima deb o'ylaysiz? Men o'zimni Lubov Sergiyevna haqida gapirish uchun biron narsa borligiga ishontira olmasdim, lekin o'zimni o'zim ham o'zimni o'ylab ko'rishim mumkin emas edi.

en: As for the last member of the family, Varenika, she was a well- developed girl of sixteen.
uz: Oilaning so'nggi a'zosi Varenika o'n olti yoshli yaxshi rivojlangan qiz edi.

en: The only good features in her were a pair of dark-grey eyes,—which, in their expression of gaiety mingled with quiet attention, greatly resembled those of her aunt—a long coil of flaxen hair, and extremely delicate, beautiful hands.
uz: Uning yagona yaxshi xususiyatlari - bu qorong'i sariq ko'zlar,bular shodlik va xotirjamlik bilan aralashgan holda onasi bilan juda o'xshaydi,bularning uzun sochlari va nihoyatda nozik, chiroyli qo'llari bor.

en: “I expect, Monsieur Nicolas, you find it wearisome to hear a story begun from the middle?” said Sophia Ivanovna with her good- natured sigh as she turned over some pieces of clothing which she was sewing.
uz: "Mening fikrimcha, monsieur Nikolay, o'rtalardan boshlangan hikoyani eshitish sizni charchatadi", - dedi Sofiya Ivanovna, o'zi tikuvchi bo'lgan kiyim-kechakni o'g'irlab ketayotganda, o'ziga xos hissiyot bilan.

en: The reading aloud had ceased for the moment because Dimitri had left the room on some errand or another.
uz: Dimitriy biron-bir ish uchun xonani tark etganligi sababli, ovoz chiqarib o'qish hozircha to'xtadi.

en: “Or perhaps you have read Rob Roy before?” she added.
uz: Yoki ehtimol siz Rob Royni ilgari o'qigan bo'lsangiz kerak? deb qo'shimcha qildi.

en: At that period I thought it incumbent upon me, in virtue of my student’s uniform, to reply in a very “clever and original” manner to every question put to me by people whom I did not know very well, and regarded such short, clear answers as “Yes,” “No,” “I like it,” or “I do not care for it,” as things to be ashamed of.
uz: O'sha davrda o'quvchi uniformim tufayli men o'zimni yaxshi bilmagan odamlar tomonidan so'ralgan har bir savolga juda aqlli va original tarzda javob berish vazifasini ko'rdim va "Ha", "Yo'q", "Menga yoqadi" yoki "Menga ahamiyat bermaydi" kabi qisqa, aniq javoblarni sharmanda qilish kerak bo'lgan narsalar deb hisoblardim.

en: Accordingly, looking down at my new and fashionably-cut trousers and the glittering buttons of my tunic, I replied that I had never read Rob Roy, but that it interested me greatly to hear it, since I preferred to read books from the middle rather than from the beginning.
uz: Shu bois, yangi va zamonaviy bo'lib o'tgan paltarlarimga va tunikning shinam tugmalariga qarab, Rob Royni hech qachon o'qimaganimni aytdim, lekin uni eshitish menga katta qiziqish uyg'otganini aytdim, chunki men kitoblarni boshdan o'qishni afzal ko'rdim.

en: “It is twice as interesting,” I added with a self-satisfied smirk; “for then one can guess what has gone before as well as what is to come after.” The Princess smiled what I thought was a forced smile, but one which I discovered later to be her only one.
uz: Bu ikki baravar ko'proq qiziqarli, o'zimdan mamnun bo'lgan tabassum bilan qo'shdim; chunki, o'shanda avval nima bo'lganini va bundan keyin nima bo'lishini tasavvur qilish mumkin. Qizimning tabassumini men majburiy tabassum deb o'ylagandim, ammo keyinchalik uning yagona tabassumini aniqladim.

en: “Well, perhaps that is true,” she said.
uz: Ehtimol, bu haqiqatdir, - dedi u.

en: “But tell me, Nicolas (you will not be offended if I drop the Monsieur)—tell me, are you going to be in town long?
uz: Lekin ayting, Nikolas (Monsieurni tushirsam, xafa bo'lmaysiz) Menga ayting, siz uzoq vaqt shaharda bo'lasizmi?

en: When do you go away?” “I do not know quite.
uz: Qachon ketasiz?Men to'liq bilmayman.

en: Perhaps to-morrow, or perhaps not for some while yet,” I replied for some reason or another, though I knew perfectly well that in reality we were to go to-morrow.
uz: Ehtimol ertaga, yoki ehtimol bir muncha vaqt davomida emas, deb javob berdim, ammo men haqiqatan ham ertaga borishimiz kerakligini yaxshi bilardim.

en: “I wish you could stop longer, both for your own sake and for Dimitri’s,” she said in a meditative manner.
uz: "O'zingiz uchun ham, Dimitriy uchun ham uzoqroq to'xtab turishingizni istardim", - dedi u mulohaza yuritib.

en: “At your age friendship is a weak thing.” I felt that every one was looking at me, and waiting to see what I should say—though certainly Varenika made a pretence of looking at her aunt’s work.
uz: Sizning yoshingizda do'stlik zaif narsa. Hamma menga qarayotgandek his qildim va nima deyishimni kutardim,haqiqatan ham Varenika onasi ishiga qarayotgandek o'zini ko'rsatdi.

en: I felt, in fact, as though I were being put through an examination, and that it behoved me to figure in it as well as possible.
uz: Aslida, o'zimni tekshiruvdan o'tkazuvchi bo'lganim kabi his qildim va bu jarayonda iloji boricha yaxshiroq ishtirok etishim kerakligini his qildim.

en: “Yes, to ME Dimitri’s friendship is most useful,” I replied, “but to HIM mine cannot be of any use at all, since he is a thousand times better than I.” (Dimitri could not hear what I said, or I should have feared his detecting the insincerity of my words.) Again the Princess smiled her unnatural, yet characteristically natural, smile.
uz: Ha, Men uchun Dimitrining do'stligi juda foydali, Men javob berdim, lekin U uchun mening do'stligim hech qanday foyda keltirolmaydi, chunki u mendan ming baravar yaxshiroq. (Dimitri aytganimni eshitolmadi, yoki men uning so'zlarimning samimiyligini aniqlashidan qo'rqishim kerak edi.)

en: “Just listen to him!” she said.
uz: Buni tinglang! dedi u.

en: “But it is YOU who are the little monster of perfection.” “‘Monster of perfection,’” I thought to myself.
uz: Ammo mukammallikning kichkina g'ayrati Senga o'xshaydi.  mukammallikning g'ayrati men o'zimga o'yladim.

en: I must make a note of it.” “Yet, to dismiss yourself, he has been extraordinarily clever in that quarter,” she went on in a lower tone (which pleased me somehow) as she indicated Lubov Sergievna with her eyes, “since he has discovered in our poor little Auntie” (such was the pet name which they gave Lubov) “all sorts of perfections which I, who have known her and her little dog for twenty years, had never yet suspected.
uz: Men buni yozib qo'yishim kerak.Agar o'zingizni chetga solsangiz ham, u o'sha chorakda juda aqlli bo'lgan, u Lubov Sergiyevnani ko'zlari bilan ko'rsatganida kamroq ovoz bilan davom etdi (bu menga qandaydir yoqdi),chunki u kamtarimizdan (Lubovga berilgan uy hayvonining ismi shunga o'xshab edi) men uni va uning kichik itini yigirma yildan beri tanib-bilganimda hech qachon shubha qilmagan barcha mukammalliklarni kashf etgan.

en: Varenika, go and tell them to bring me a glass of water,” she added, letting her eyes wander again.
uz: Varenika, borib, menga bir stakan suv olib kelishlarini ayt, - dedi u yana ko'zlarini ko'targan holda.

en: Probably she had bethought her that
uz: Ehtimol, u bu haqda o'ylagan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: it was too soon, or not entirely necessary, to let me into all the family secrets.
uz: Oilaning barcha sirlarini o'rganish uchun juda erta yoki mutlaqo zarur emas edi.

en: “Yet no—let HIM go, for he has nothing to do, while you are reading.
uz: Ammo, siz o'qiyotganingizda, uni ketishiga yo'l qo'ymang, chunki u hech qanday ish bilan band emas.

en: Pray go to the door, my friend,” she said to me, “and walk about fifteen steps down the passage.
uz: Do'stim, eshikga bor, - dedi u menga, - va o'n besh qadam pastga yur.

en: Then halt and call out pretty loudly, ‘Peter, bring Maria Ivanovna a glass of iced water’”—and she smiled her curious smile once more.
uz: Keyin to'xtab, juda baland ovoz bilan: "Peter, Mariya Ivanovnaga muzli suv bir stakanini olib kel", - deb xitob qildi.

en: “I expect she wants to say something about me in my absence,” I thought to myself as I left the room.
uz: Mening yo'qligimda u men haqimda biror narsa aytmoqchi bo'ladi deb o'ylayman,  xonani tark etganimda o'zim o'zimga o'yladim.

en: “I expect she wants to remark that she can see very clearly that I am a very, very clever young man.” Hardly had I taken a dozen steps when I was overtaken by Sophia Ivanovna, who, though fat and short of breath, trod with surprising lightness and agility.
uz: Mening juda aqlli yosh odam ekanligimni juda aniq ko'ra olishini aytmoqchi bo'ladi, deb o'ylayman. Men Sophia Ivanovna meni orqaga surib, o'nlab qadam ham qo'ymagan edim.

en: “Merci, mon cher,” she said.
uz: Mening rahmatim, qizim, dedi u.

en: “I will go and tell them myself.” XXIV.
uz: Men o'zim borib ularga aytaman. XXIV.

en: LOVE SOPHIA IVANOVNA, as I afterwards came to know her, was one of those rare, young-old women who are born for family life, but to whom that happiness has been denied by fate.
uz: SOPHIA IVANOVNA, men uni keyinchalik taniganimcha, oilaviy hayot uchun tug'ilgan, ammo taqdir bu baxtdan mahrum bo'lgan noyob yosh ayollardan biri edi.

en: Consequently all that store of their love which should have been poured out upon a husband and children becomes pent up in their hearts, until they suddenly decide to let it overflow upon a few chosen individuals.
uz: Natijada, er va bolalarga to'kiladigan sevgining to'plami ularning yuragida to'sib qoladi va ular birdan uni bir necha tanlangan kishilarga to'kib yuborishga qaror qiladilar.

en: Yet so inexhaustible is that store of old maids’ love that, despite the number of individuals so selected, there still remains an abundant surplus of affection which they lavish upon all by whom they are surrounded—upon all, good or bad, whom they may chance to meet in their daily life.
uz: Biroq, qadimgi qizlarning sevgisi shunchalik tugamaydiki, bunday tanlangan kishilar soniga qaramay, ular atrofidagi barchaga, yaxshi yoki yomon bo'lganlarga, kundalik hayotlarida uchrashadiganlarga ko'pgina mehr-muhabbat qo'shishadi.

en: Of love there are three kinds—love of beauty, the love which denies itself, and practical love.
uz: Sevgining uch turidir: go'zallikni sevish, o'zini rad etish va amaliy sevish.

en: Of the desire of a young man for a young woman, as well as of the reverse instance, I am not now speaking, for of such tendresses I am wary, seeing that I have been too unhappy in my life to have been able ever to see in such affection a single spark of truth, but rather a lying pretence in which sensuality, connubial relations, money, and the wish to bind hands or to unloose them have rendered feeling such a complex affair as to defy analysis.
uz: Yosh yigitning yosh ayolga bo'lgan istaklari haqida ham, aksincha, men hozir gapirmayman, chunki men bunday muomalalardan ehtiyotman, chunki men hayotimda shunchalik baxtsiz bo'lganmanki, bunday muhabbatda haqiqatning bir tikasini ko'rishga muvaffaq bo'lmadim, aksincha, shubhasiz, shubhasiz, jinsiy aloqa, nikoh rishtalari, pul va qo'l bog'lash yoki ularni bo'shatish istagi his-tuyg'ularni juda murakkab ish qilib qo'ygan yolg'on so'z.

en: Rather am I speaking of that love for a human being which, according to the spiritual strength of its possessor, concentrates itself either upon a single individual, upon a few, or upon many—of love for a mother, a father, a brother, little children, a friend, a compatriot—of love, in short, for one’s neighbour.
uz: Aksincha, men insonga bo'lgan sevgi haqida gapiryapman, u o'z egasining ma'naviy kuch-quvvatidan kelib chiqqan holda, faqat bitta shaxsga, bir necha kishiga yoki ko'p kishilarga bo'lgan sevgi haqida gapiryapman: onaga, otasiga, aka-ukaga, kichik bolalarga, do'stga, qo'shni-qishloqga bo'lgan sevgi, qisqacha qilib aytganda, o'z yaqinlariga bo'lgan sevgi.

en: Love of beauty consists in a love of the sense of beauty and of its expression.
uz: Go'zallikka bo'lgan sevgi go'zallik hissi va uning ifodasini sevishdan iborat.

en: People who thus love conceive the object of their affection to be desirable only in so far as it arouses in them that pleasurable sensation of which the consciousness and the expression soothes the senses.
uz: Shunday qilib, sevgan insonlar o'zlarining mehr-muhabbat ob'ektini faqatgina u o'zlarida o'sha yoqimli his-tuyg'ularni uyg'otadi, uning his-tuyg'usi va ifodasi his-tuyg'ularni tinchlantiradi.

en: They change the object of their love frequently, since their principal aim consists in ensuring that the voluptuous feeling of their adoration shall be constantly titillated.
uz: Ular ko'pincha o'z sevgisi ob'ektini o'zgartiradilar, chunki ularning asosiy maqsadi o'zlarining e'zozlanishlarining shahvatli his-tuyg'ularini doimiy ravishda kuchaytirishdir.

en: To preserve in themselves this sensuous condition, they talk unceasingly, and in the most elegant terms, on the subject of the love which they feel, not only for its immediate object, but also for objects upon which it does not touch at all.
uz: Bu hissiy holatni o'zlarida saqlab qolish uchun ular nafaqat uning yaqin ob'ekti uchun, balki u hech qachon tegmaydigan narsalar uchun his qiladigan sevgisi haqida to'xtamasdan, eng chiroyli so'zlar bilan gapirishadi.

en: This country of ours contains many such individuals—individuals of that well-known class who, cultivating “the beautiful,” not only discourse of their cult to all and sundry, but speak of it pre-eminently in FRENCH.
uz: Bizning mamlakatimizda bunday odamlar ko'p, shu mashhur sinfdagi odamlar borki, ular go'zallikni rivojlantirib, faqatgina o'z kultlarini hammalarga e'lon qilmay, balki bu haqda fransuz tilida gapirishadi.

en: It may seem a strange and ridiculous thing to say, but I am convinced that among us we have had in the past, and still have, a large section of society —notably women—whose love for their friends, husbands, or children would expire to-morrow if they were debarred from dilating upon it in the tongue of France!
uz: Aytish g'alati va g'alati tuyulishi mumkin, lekin men o'tgan davrda va hozir ham jamiyatning katta qismi bo'lgan, deb o'ylayman - ayniqsa, xotin-qizlar, agar ular fransuz tilida o'zlarining do'stlari, erlari yoki farzandlariga bo'lgan sevgisi ertaga o'tib ketadi, deb aytishmas ekan!

en: Love of the second kind—renunciatory love—consists in a yearning to undergo self-sacrifice for the object beloved, regardless of any consideration whether such self-sacrifice will benefit or injure the object in question.
uz: Ikkinchi turdagi sevgi - o'z-o'zidan voz kechadigan sevgan narsangiz uchun fidoyilik ko'rsatishga intilayotgan bo'lishdir, bunday fidoyilik bu narsangizga foyda yoki zarar keltiradimi yoki yo'qmi degan savolga qaramasdan.

en: “There is no evil which I would not endure to show both the world and him or her whom I adore my devotion.” There we have the formula of this kind of love.
uz: Men dunyoga va men o'z sadoqatimni izzat qilgan odamga ko'rsatadigan hech qanday yomonlikni ko'rmayapman. Bizda bunday sevgi formulasi bor.

en: People who thus love
uz: Shunday qilib, sevgan odamlar

en: never look for reciprocity of affection, since it is a finer thing to sacrifice yourself for one who does not comprehend you.
uz: Hech qachon mehr-shafqatning o'zaro tomonini izlamang, chunki sizni tushunmaydigan kishi uchun o'zingizni qurbon qilish yaxshiroqdir.

en: Also, they are always painfully eager to exaggerate the merits of their sacrifice; usually constant in their love, for the reason that they would find it hard to forego the kudos of the deprivations which they endure for the object beloved; always ready to die, to prove to him or to her the entirety of their devotion; but sparing of such small daily proofs of their love as call for no special effort of self-immolation.
uz: Bundan tashqari, ular har doim o'z qurbonliklarining qadriga yetarli darajada o'tishga harakat qilishadi; odatda o'z sevgida doimiy bo'lishadi, chunki ular sevikli narsasi uchun ko'tarilgan kamchiliklardan voz kechish qiyin bo'ladi; har doim o'lishga tayyor bo'lishadi, unga butun sadoqatini isbotlash uchun; lekin o'z sevgisini ko'rsatadigan kichik kundalik isbotlarni saqlab qolish uchun hech qanday o'z-o'zini qurbon qilish uchun alohida harakat talab qilinmaydi.

en: They do not much care whether you eat well, sleep well, keep your spirits up, or enjoy good health, nor do they ever do anything to obtain for you those blessings if they have it in their power; but, should you be confronting a bullet, or have fallen into the water, or stand in danger of being burnt, or have had your heart broken in a love affair—well, for all these things they are prepared if the occasion should arise.
uz: Ular siz yaxshi ovqatlanyapsizmi, yaxshi uxlaysizmi, ruhingizni saqlaysizmi yoki sog'lig'ingizni yaxshi his qilyapsizmi, ular bu barakalarga ega bo'lish uchun hech qachon biror narsa qilmaydilar; balki, agar siz o'zingizning qo'lingizda bo'lsa, o'zingizni qorong'i bilan duchor qilsangiz, suvga tushib qolsangiz, yonish xavfi ostida bo'lsangiz yoki muhabbat rishtalarida yuragingiz sindirilgan bo'lsa, ular bularning barchasi uchun tayyorgarlik ko'rishadi.

en: Moreover, people addicted to love of such a self-sacrificing order are invariably proud of their love, exacting, jealous, distrustful, and— strange to tell—anxious that the object of their adoration should incur perils (so that they may save it from calamity, and console it thereafter) and even be vicious (so that they may purge it of its vice).
uz: Bundan tashqari, bunday fidoyilikni sevishga bog'liq odamlar o'z sevgisi, talabchanligi, rashki, ishonchsizliklari va o'zlarining e'tirof qilish maqsadi xavfli bo'lishi kerakligini aytish uchun g'ayritabiiy (ular uni baxtsizlikdan qutqarishi va keyin tasalli berishi uchun) va hatto yovuz (ular uni yomonlikdan tozalashi uchun) bilan faxrlanishadi.

en: Suppose, now, that you are living in the country with a wife who loves you in this self-sacrificing manner.
uz: Aytaylik, siz qishloq joyida turmush o'rtog'ingiz bilan yashayapsiz va u sizni shu fidoyilik bilan sevadi.

en: You may be healthy and contented, and have occupations which interest you, while, on the other hand, your wife may be too weak to superintend the household work (which, in consequence, will be left to the servants), or to look after the children (who, in consequence, will be left to the nurses), or to put her heart into any work whatsoever: and all because she loves nobody and nothing but yourself.
uz: Siz sog'lom va qoniqarli bo'lishingiz mumkin va sizga qiziqadigan kasblarga ega bo'lishingiz mumkin, ammo xotiningiz uy ishlarini nazorat qila olmaydigan darajada zaif bo'lishi mumkin (bu esa xizmatkorlarga beriladi), bolalarga g'amxo'rlik qila olmaydigan darajada bo'lishi mumkin (bu esa hamshiralarga beriladi), yoki o'z yuragini har qanday ishda qo'shishi mumkin: chunki u hech kimni va hech narsani o'zingizdan boshqa sevmaydi.

en: She may be patently ill, yet she will say not a word to you about it, for fear of distressing you.
uz: U kasal bo'lishi mumkin, ammo sizni xafa qilishdan qo'rqib, bu haqda sizga hech narsa aytmaydi.

en: She may be patently ennuyee, yet for your sake she will be prepared to be so for the rest of her life.
uz: Ehtimol, u ko'rinadigan darajada charchagan bo'lishi mumkin, ammo siz uchun u butun hayoti davomida shunday bo'lishiga tayyor bo'ladi.

en: She may be patently depressed because you stick so persistently to your occupations (whether sport, books, farming, state service, or anything else) and see clearly that they are doing you harm; yet, for all that, she will keep silence, and suffer it to be so.
uz: U tushkunlikka tushib qolishi mumkin, chunki siz o'zingizning ishingizga (sport, kitoblar, dehqonchilik, davlat xizmati yoki boshqa narsalarga) qattiq bog'lanib, ular sizga zarar etkazayotganini aniq ko'rasiz; ammo, bularning barchasi uchun u sukut saqlaydi va bunga yo'l qo'yadi.

en: Yet, should you but fall sick—and, despite her own ailments and your prayers that she will not distress herself in vain, your loving wife will remain sitting inseparably by your bedside.
uz: Biroq, agar siz kasal bo'lib qolsangiz, va uning o'z kasalligiga va o'zini behuda qiynamasligi uchun ibodat qilsangiz, sevikli xotiningiz sizning yotoq yoningizda bo'lmaslik bilan o'tirib qoladi.

en: Every moment you will feel her sympathetic gaze resting upon you and, as it were,
uz: Har bir daqiqada uning samimiy ko'zlari ustingizga tiklanayotganini his qilasiz.

en: I told you so, but it is all one to me, and I shall not leave you.” In the morning you maybe a little better, and move into another room.
uz: Men sizga aytgan edim, lekin bu men uchun bir narsa, men sizni tashlab ketmayman. Ertalab siz biroz yaxshiroq bo'lib, boshqa xonani tark etasiz.

en: The room, however, will be insufficiently warmed or set in order; the soup which alone you feel you could eat will not have been cooked; nor will any medicine have been sent for.
uz: Biroq, xona yetarlicha isitilmagan yoki tartibga solinmagan bo'ladi; faqat o'zingiz yeyishingiz mumkin bo'lgan shov-shuv pishirilmagan bo'ladi; hech qanday dori yuborilmagan bo'ladi.

en: Yet, though worn out with night watching, your loving wife will continue to regard you with an expression of sympathy, to walk about on tiptoe, and to whisper unaccustomed and obscure orders to the servants.
uz: Biroq, kechasi kuzatib turish bilan charchagan bo'lsa-da, sevuvchi xotiningiz sizga hamdardlik ko'rsatib, to'ng'iroqda yurishni va xizmatkorlarga o'zgacha va noma'lum buyruqlarni shoshib berishni davom ettiradi.

en: You may wish to be read to—and your loving wife will tell you with a sigh that she feels sure you will be unable to hear her reading, and only grow angry at her awkwardness in doing it; wherefore you had better not be read to at all.
uz: Siz o'qishni istaysiz va sevikli xotiningiz o'qishni eshitolmayotganingizga aminligini, faqatgina uning o'qishda noqulayligi uchun g'azablanishini aytadi.

en: You may wish to walk about the room— and she will tell you that it would be far better for you not to do so.
uz: Siz xona atrofida yurishni xohlaysiz va u sizga bunday qilmasangiz yaxshiroq bo'lishini aytadi.

en: You may wish to talk with some friends who have called—and she will tell you that talking is not good for you.
uz: Ehtimol, qo'ng'iroq qilgan do'stlaringiz bilan gaplashmoqchi bo'lasiz va ular sizga gapirish sizga foyda bermasligini aytishadi.

en: At nightfall the fever may come upon you again, and you may wish to be left alone whereupon your loving wife, though wasted, pale, and full of yawns, will go on sitting in a chair opposite you, as dusk falls, until her very slightest movement, her very slightest sound, rouses you to feelings of anger and impatience.
uz: Kechqurun ham sizda yana issiqlik paydo bo'lishi mumkin va siz yolg'iz qolishni xohlashingiz mumkin, shundan so'ng esa sevikli xotiningiz, garchi u yo'q bo'lsa-da, o'g'irlab, ko'ngli cho'kkan bo'lsa-da, kechqurun sizning oldingizda o'tiradi, hatto uning eng kam harakatlari, eng kam ovozi sizni g'azab va sabrsizlik hissi bilan uyg'otadi.

en: You may have a servant who has lived with you for twenty years, and to whom you are attached, and who would tend you well and to your satisfaction during the night, for the reason that he has been asleep all day and is, moreover, paid a salary for his services; yet your wife will not suffer him to wait upon you.
uz: Sizda yigirma yildan beri siz bilan birga yashayotgan, sizga yaqin bo'lgan va kechasi sizni yaxshi va sizning qoniqaringizcha boqadigan xizmatkoringiz bo'lishi mumkin, chunki u kun bo'yi uxlab turadi va xizmatlari uchun ish haqi to'lanadi; ammo xotiningiz unga sizni kutib turishga yo'l qo'ymaydi.

en: No; everything she must do herself with her weak, unaccustomed fingers (of which you follow the movements with suppressed irritation as those pale members do their best to uncork a medicine bottle, to snuff a candle, to pour out physic, or to touch you in a squeamish sort of way).
uz: Yo'q; u o'zi o'zi qilish kerak bo'lgan hamma narsani o'zining zaif, odatsiz barmoqlari bilan qilishi kerak (shularning harakatiga siz o'zingizning g'azabingizni kamaytirgan holda kuzatib borasiz, chunki o'sha so'nggi a'zolar dori-darmon shishalarini ochishga, shamolni o'chirib yuborishga, jismonan to'kib yuborishga yoki sizni bir xil qo'rqinchli tarzda qo'llashga harakat qilishadi).

en: If you are an impatient, hasty sort of man, and beg of her to leave the room, you will hear by the vexed, distressed sounds which come from her that she is humbly sobbing and weeping behind the door, and whispering foolishness of some kind to the servant.
uz: Agar siz sabrsiz, shoshilinch odam bo'lsangiz va undan xonadan chiqib ketishni iltijo qilsangiz, uning tashvishlangan va qayg'urgan tovushlari tufayli u kamtarlik ila yig'lab, eshik orqasida yig'lab, xizmatkorga bir xil ahmoqlik so'zlarini shovqinlik bilan aytishini eshitasiz.

en: Finally if you do not die, your loving wife—who has not slept during the whole three weeks of your illness (a fact of which she will constantly remind you)—will fall ill in her turn, waste away, suffer much, and become even more incapable of any useful pursuit than she was before; while by the time that you have regained your
uz: Va nihoyat, agar siz o'lmasangiz, kasalligingizning uch haftasi davomida uxlamagan sevikli xotiningiz (u sizni doimo eslatib turadi) o'z navbatida kasal bo'lib qoladi, ko'p azob chekadi va u avvalgidek foydali ishlarga qobiliyatsiz bo'ladi.

en: normal state of health she will express to you her self-sacrificing affection only by shedding around you a kind of benignant dullness which involuntarily communicates itself both to yourself and to every one else in your vicinity.
uz: Oddiy sog'lom holatda bo'lgan u, o'zining fidoyi muhabbatini faqat siz atrofingizda o'zingizni va atrofingizdagi har bir odamni o'ziga va o'z xohishiga ko'ra o'zini bevafo ravishda oshkor etadigan yaxshilikchan bir turdagi befarqlikni tashlab yuborish orqali bildiradi.

en: The third kind of love—practical love—consists of a yearning to satisfy every need, every desire, every caprice, nay, every vice, of the being beloved.
uz: Uchinchi sevgi - amaliy sevgi - sevikli kishining har bir ehtiyojini, har bir istakini, har bir caprice-ni, hatto har bir yomonlikni qondirishni orzu qilishdan iborat.

en: People who love thus always love their life long, since, the more they love, the more they get to know the object beloved, and the easier they find the task of loving it—that is to say, of satisfying its desires.
uz: Shunday qilib, sevgan insonlar o'z hayotini doimo uzoqroq sevishadi, chunki qancha ko'proq sevsalar, shunchalik ko'proq sevikli ob'ektni tanib-bilishadi va uni sevish vazifasini shunchalik osonroq ko'rishadi, ya'ni uning istaklarini qondirish.

en: Their love seldom finds expression in words, but if it does so, it expresses itself neither with assurance nor beauty, but rather in a shamefaced, awkward manner, since people of this kind invariably have misgivings that they are loving unworthily.
uz: Ularning sevgisi kamdan-kam so'zlar bilan ifodalanadi, lekin agar shunday bo'lsa, u ishonch va go'zallik bilan emas, balki o'ziga yarasha, o'yin-kulgi va noqulay tarzda ifodalanadi, chunki bunday odamlar doimo o'zlarining munosib emasligini shubha ostiga qo'yishadi.

en: People of this kind love even the faults of their adored one, for the reason that those faults afford them the power of constantly satisfying new desires.
uz: Bunday insonlar hatto o'z azizlarining kamchiliklarini ham yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki bu kamchiliklar ularga doimiy ravishda yangi istaklarni qondirish qobiliyatini beradi.

en: They look for their affection to be returned, and even deceive themselves into believing that it is returned, and are happy accordingly: yet in the reverse case they will still continue to desire happiness for their beloved one, and try by every means in their power—whether moral or material, great or small—to provide it.
uz: Ular o'z mehr-muhabbatlarini qaytarib olishni kutishadi va hatto o'zlarini qaytarib berilishiga ishonib aldashadi va shunga ko'ra baxtli bo'lishadi: agar shunday bo'lmasa, ular hali ham o'z azizlari uchun baxtni orzu qilishni davom ettirishadi va uni taqdim etish uchun o'z kuchlari bilan harakat qilishadi - axloqiy yoki moddiy, katta yoki kichik.

en: Such practical love it was—love for her nephew, for her niece, for her sister, for Lubov Sergievna, and even for myself, because I loved Dimitri—that shone in the eyes, as well as in the every word and movement, of Sophia Ivanovna.
uz: Bunday amaliy muhabbat o'g'li, singlisi, singlisi, Lubov Sergiyevna va hatto o'zim uchun edi, chunki men Sofiya Ivanovnaning ko'zlarida va har bir so'z va harakatida nur sochadigan Dimitriyni yaxshi ko'rdim.

en: Only long afterwards did I learn to value her at her true worth.
uz: Faqat ancha vaqt o'tgach, uni haqiqiy qadriga yetkazish uchun o'rgandim.

en: Yet even now the question occurred to me: “What has made Dimitri— who throughout has tried to understand love differently to other young fellows, and has always had before his eyes the gentle, loving Sophia Ivanovna—suddenly fall so deeply in love with the incomprehensible Lubov Sergievna, and declare that in his aunt he can only find good QUALITIES?
uz: Biroq, hozir ham menga savol tug'ildi: Dimitriyga nima sabab bo'ldi, u o'zga yosh yigitlardan farqli ravishda sevgini tushunishga harakat qildi va doimo mehribon, mehribon Sofiya Ivanovna uning ko'z o'ngida edi, birdan Lubov Sergiyevnaga shunchalik qattiq muhabbatga tushdi va u o'z onasida faqat yaxshi fazilatlarni topishi mumkinligini aytdi?

en: Verily it is a true saying that ‘a prophet hath no honour in his own country.’ One of two things: either every man has in him more of bad than of good, or every man is more receptive to bad than to good.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, payg'ambar o'z yurtida hurmatga sazovor emas, degan so'z haqdir. Ikki narsadan biri: yoki har bir odamda yaxshilikdan ko'ra ko'proq yomonlik bor, yoki har bir odam yaxshilikdan ko'ra yomonlikka ko'proq mos keladi.

en: Lubov Sergievna he has not known for long, whereas his aunt’s love he has known since the day of his birth.”
uz: Lubov Sergiyevnani ko'p vaqtdan beri bilmaydi, ammo onasining sevgisini tug'ilgan kundan boshlab biladi.

en: I BECOME BETTER ACQUAINTED WITH THE NECHLUDOFFS WHEN I returned to the verandah, I found that they were not talking of me at all, as I had anticipated.
uz: Men NECHLUDOFFS bilan yaxshiroq tanishdim Men verandaga qaytib kelganimda, ular mendan umuman gapirmasligini ko'rdim, chunki men buni kutib o'tgan edim.

en: On the contrary, Varenika had laid aside the book, and was engaged in a heated dispute with Dimitri, who, for his part, was walking up and down the verandah, and frowningly adjusting his neck in his collar as he did so.
uz: Aksincha, Varenika kitobni bir chetga qo'yib, Dimitri bilan qizg'in bahslashdi, Dimitri esa shunda verandaga chiqib, o'z bo'yni bilan bo'ynini qo'lga kiritdi.

en: The subject of the quarrel seemed to be Ivan Yakovlevitch and superstition, but it was too animated a difference for its underlying cause not to be something which concerned the family much more nearly.
uz: Urush mavzusi Ivan Yakovlevitch va sehr-jodu bo'lib ko'rinardi, ammo uning asosiy sababi oilani ko'proq qiziqtirmaydigan narsa bo'lish uchun bu farq juda hayajonli edi.

en: Although the Princess and Lubov Sergievna were sitting by in silence, they were following every word, and evidently tempted at times to take part in the dispute; yet always, just when they were about to speak, they checked themselves, and left the field clear for the two principles, Dimitri and Varenika.
uz: Garchi printsesa va Lubov Sergiyevna hushyor o'tirgan bo'lsa-da, ular har bir so'zni kuzatib borishgan va ba'zida bahsda ishtirok etishga moyil bo'lishgan; ammo har doim, gapirishni boshlaganlarida, o'zlarini tekshirib ko'rishgan va Dimitri va Varenika ismli ikkita prinsip uchun maydonni toza qoldirishgan.

en: On my entry, the latter glanced at me with such an indifferent air that I could see she was wholly absorbed in the quarrel and did not care whether she spoke in my presence or not.
uz: Men kirganimda, u menga shunchalik befarq ko'rdiki, u to'liq to'qnashuvda o'tirib qolganini va mening huzurimda gapirgan yoki gapirmaganini ko'rishim mumkin edi.

en: The Princess too looked the same, and was clearly on Varenika’s side, while Dimitri began, if anything, to raise his voice still more when I appeared, and Lubov Sergievna, for her part, observed to no one in particular: “Old people are quite right when they say, ‘Si jeunesse savait, si vieillesse pouvait.’” Nevertheless this quotation did not check the dispute, though it somehow gave me the impression that the side represented by the speaker and her friend was in the wrong.
uz: Qizim ham xuddi shunday ko'rinardi va aniqlik bilan Varenika tomonida edi, Dimitri esa men paydo bo'lganimda ovozini yanada ko'paytirishni boshladi va Lubov Sergievna o'z navbatida hech kimga e'tibor bermadi: "Keksalar, yoshlar bilsa, yoshlar bilsa, yoshlar bilsa", deb aytganda to'g'ri gapirishadi. Biroq bu so'z bahsni tekshirmadi, ammo bu gap gap gapiruvchi va uning do'sti tomonidan namoyish etilayotgan taraf noto'g'ri fikrda bo'lgan degan taassurot qoldirdi.

en: Although it was a little awkward for me to be present at a petty family difference, the fact that the true relations of the family revealed themselves during its progress, and that my presence did nothing to hinder that revelation, afforded me considerable gratification.
uz: Oiladagi kichik farqlarda ishtirok etish men uchun biroz noqulay bo'lsa-da, oiladagi haqiqiy munosabatlar o'z-o'zidan oshkor bo'lganligi va hozirligim bu oshkor bo'lishga to'sqinlik qilmaganligi menga katta mamnuniyat ato etdi.

en: How often it happens that for years one sees a family cover themselves over with a conventional cloak of decorum, and preserve the real relations of its members a secret from every eye!
uz: Ko'p yillar davomida bir oila o'zini odatdagi odatli kiyim bilan qoplaganini va a'zolarining haqiqiy munosabatlarini har bir ko'zdan sir saqlaganini ko'rish qanchalik tez-tez sodir bo'ladi!

en: How often, too, have I remarked that, the more impenetrable (and therefore the more decorous) is the cloak, the harsher are the relations which it conceals!
uz: Men ham qanchalar tez-tez shuni ta'kidlaganmanki, qotib qo'yilgan kiyim qancha ko'proq o'tkir bo'lsa (va shuning uchun ham shunchalik bezakli bo'lsa), u qancha ko'proq yashirsa, munosabatlar shunchalik qattiq bo'ladi!

en: Yet, once let some unexpected question—often a most trivial one (the colour of a woman’s hair, a visit, a man’s horses, and so forth)—arise in that family circle, and without any visible cause there will also arise an ever-growing difference, until in time the cloak of decorum becomes unequal to confining the quarrel within due bounds, and, to the dismay of the disputants and the astonishment of the auditors, the real and ill-adjusted relations of the family are laid bare, and the cloak, now useless for concealment, is bandied from hand to hand among the contending factions until it serves only to remind one of the years during which it successfully deceived one’s perceptions.
uz: Biroq, bir marta oilada kutilmagan savol paydo bo'lishi mumkin (ayolning soch rangi, tashrif, erkakning otlari va hokazolar) va ko'rinadigan sabab bo'lmaganda, o'zgarishlar ham paydo bo'ladi, vaqt o'tgach, munosiblik kiyimini to'g'ri yo'lga qo'ymaydi va bahsda ishtirok etuvchilarning hayajonini va auditorlarning hayronligini keltirib chiqaradi, oiladagi haqiqiy va yomon munosabatlar oshkor qilinadi va endi yashirish uchun foydasiz bo'lgan kiyim, bahslashayotgan fraksiyalar o'rtasida qo'lidan-qo'lga o'tkaziladi, chunki bu faqat bir yil davomida uning taassurotlarini muvaffaqiyatli aldashini eslatadi.

en: Sometimes to strike one’s head violently against a ceiling hurts one less than just to graze some spot which has been hurt and bruised before: and in almost every family there exists some such raw and tender spot.
uz: Ba'zan boshini ustunga qattiq urish avval jarohatlangan va shikastlangan biron bir nuqtaga cho'kishdan kamroq og'riqli bo'ladi: deyarli har bir oilada bunday xom va tender nuqta mavjud.

en: In the Nechludoff family that spot was Dimitri’s extraordinary affection for Lubov Sergievna, which aroused in the mother and sister, if not a jealous feeling, at all events a sense of hurt family pride.
uz: Nechludofflar oilasining o'sha joyida Dimitriyning Lubov Sergievnaga bo'lgan o'zgacha mehr-muhabbati bo'lgan, bu esa ona va singillarda hasad hissi uyg'otgan, aksincha, oilaviy mag'rurlik tuyg'usini o'zgartirgan.

en: This was the grave significance which underlay, for all those present, the seeming dispute about Ivan Yakovlevitch and superstition.
uz: Bu hammamiz uchun Ivan Yakovlevitch va sehr-jodu haqida paydo bo'lgan g'alati nizoga asos bo'lgan jiddiy ahamiyat edi.

en: “In anything that other people deride and despise you invariably profess to see something extraordinarily good!” Varenika was saying in her clear voice, as she articulated each syllable with careful precision.
uz: O'zgalar masxara qiladigan va sizdan nafratlanadigan har qanday narsada har doim ajoyib yaxshilikni ko'rganingizni aytasiz! Varenika har bir silfani diqqat bilan aniqlab o'tkazganida, o'zining aniq ovozi bilan gapirgan edi.

en: “Indeed?” retorted Dimitri with an impatient toss of his head.
uz: Haqiqatan ham? Dimitriy boshini sabrsizlik bilan tashlab, javob berdi.

en: “Now, in the first place, only a most unthinking person could ever speak of DESPISING such a remarkable man as Ivan Yakovlevitch, while, in the second place, it is YOU who invariably profess to see nothing good in what confronts you.” Meanwhile Sophia Ivanovna kept looking anxiously at us as she turned first to her nephew, and then to her niece, and then to myself.
uz: Birinchidan, faqatgina o'ta g'ayritabiiy inson Ivan Yakovlevitch kabi ajoyib odamni tanqid qilish haqida gapira oladi, ikkinchidan esa, sizni duch kelayotgan narsalarda hech qanday yaxshilikni ko'rmasligingizni tanqid qilayotgan Sizsiz. Shu paytgacha Sofiya Ivanovna avvalo o'g'li, so'ngra o'g'li, so'ngra o'zimga murojaat qilib, bizni tashvish bilan ko'rib turardi.

en: Twice she opened her mouth as though to say what was in her mind and drew a deep sigh.
uz: U ikki marta og'zini ochib, o'z fikrini aytgandek, chuqur nafas oldi.

en: “Varia, PLEASE go on reading,” she said at length, at the same time handing her niece the book, and patting her hand kindly.
uz: Varia, iltimos, o'qishni davom ettiring, dedi u uzoq davom etib, bir vaqtning o'zida bu kitobni singlisiga berib, qo'lini mehribonlik bilan tatib qo'ydi.

en: “I wish to know whether he ever found HER again” (as a matter of fact, the novel in question contained not a word about any one finding any one else).
uz: Men uni yana topganini bilishni istayman (aslida, bu romanda hech kim boshqalarni topganligi haqida so'z yo'q edi).

en: “And, Mitia dear,” she added to her nephew, despite the glum looks which he was throwing at her for having interrupted the logical thread of his deductions, “you had better let me poultice your cheek, or your teeth will begin to ache again.” After that the reading was resumed.
uz: Va, aziz Mitia,  o'g'li qarindoshiga qo'shib qo'ydi: "O'z xulosalarining mantiqiy bo'g'ini kesib qo'yganligi uchun uning o'ziga qo'ygan g'amgin ko'rinishlariga qaramay,  sen menga shavqashga ruxsat bersang yaxshi bo'lardi, yoki sizning tishlaringiz yana og'riydi. Shundan so'ng o'qishni davom ettirishdi.

en: Yet the quarrel had in no way dispelled the calm atmosphere of family and intellectual harmony which enveloped this circle of ladies.
uz: Ammo bahs oilaviy va intellektual xotirjamlikdagi tinch muhitni yo'qotib qo'ymagan edi.

en: Clearly deriving its inspiration and character from the Princess Maria Ivanovna, it was a circle which, for me, had a wholly novel and attractive character of logicalness mingled with simplicity and refinement.
uz: O'zining ilhomlantiruvchisi va xarakterini Princess Maria Ivanovnadan aniq olib borgan, bu men uchun soddalik va soflik bilan aralashtirilgan mantiqiylikning butunlay yangi va jozibali xarakterga ega bo'lgan doira edi.

en: That character I could discern in the daintiness, good taste, and solidity of everything about me, whether the handbell, the binding of the book, the settee, or the table.
uz: Bu xarakterni men atrofimda bo'lgan hamma narsa, xoh qo'l qo'ng'iroqlari, kitobning bog'lanishi, settee, yoki stolning chiroyliligi, go'zalligi va mustahkamligidan payqadim.

en: Likewise, I divined it in the upright, well-corseted pose of the Princess, in her pendant curls of grey hair, in the manner in which she had, at our first introduction, called me plain “Nicolas” and “he,” in the occupations of the ladies (the reading and the sewing of garments), and in the unusual whiteness of their hands.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, men buni Princessning to'g'ri, yaxshi ko'rsatilgan pozitsiyasida, uning oq sochlar bilan o'rnatilgan bo'ylaklarida, birinchi tanishish paytida menga oddiy "Nikolas" va "u" deb nomlaganida (qizlarning kasblarida (kiyim o'qish va tikuv) va qo'llarining odatiy emas oqligi bilan ko'rdim.

en: Those hands, en passant, showed a family feature common to all—namely, the feature that the flesh of the palm on the outer side was rosy in colour, and divided by a sharp, straight line from the pure whiteness of the upper portion of the hand.
uz: Bu qo'llar, shu yo'sin, barchaga umumiy bo'lgan oilaviy xususiyatni ko'rsatdi, ya'ni qo'lning tashqaridagi palma go'shti rosa rangda bo'lgani va qo'lning yuqori qismining sof oqligidan keskin, to'g'ri chiziq bilan ajratiladigan xususiyat.

en: Still more was the character of this feminine circle expressed in the manner in which the three ladies spoke Russian and French—spoke them, that is to say, with perfect articulation of syllables and pedantic accuracy of substantives and prepositions.
uz: Ayniqsa, bu ayollarning xarakterini uchta ayol rus va frantsuz tillarida gapirgan, ya'ni silfalarning mukammal so'zlashuvi va substantivlar va prepozitsiyalarning pedant aniqligi namoyon etgan.

en: All this, and more especially the fact that the ladies treated me as simply and as seriously as a real grown-up—telling me their opinions, and listening to my own (a thing to which I was so little accustomed that, for all my glittering buttons and blue facings, I was in constant fear of being told: “Surely you do not think that we are talking SERIOUSLY to you?
uz: Bularning barchasini, ayniqsa, ayollar menga oddiy va jiddiy munosabatda bo'lishlarini, katta odam sifatida o'z fikrlarini aytishlarini va mening o'zimning fikrimni tinglashlarini (men o'zimga shunchalik oz o'rganib qolgan edimki, barcha shovqinli tugmalarim va ko'k yuzlarimga qaramay, menga: "Siz biz sizga jiddiy gapiryapmiz, deb o'ylamayapsizmi?

en: Go away and learn something”)—all this, I say, caused me to feel an entire absence of restraint in this society.
uz: Borib biror narsa o'rganing)Bularning barchasi, deyman, bu jamiyatda o'zimni to'liq yo'qotgan his qilishimga sabab bo'ldi.

en: I ventured at times to rise, to move about, and to talk boldly to each of the ladies except
uz: Ba'zan turishga, harakatlanishga va har bir ayol bilan faqatdan tashqari jasorat bilan gapirishga jur'at qilardim.

en: Varenika (whom I always felt it was unbecoming, or even forbidden, for me to address unless she first spoke to me).
uz: Varenika (men har doim unga murojaat qilish men uchun munosib emas yoki hatto men uchun taqiqlangan deb o'yladim, agar u birinchi bo'lib men bilan gaplashmasa).

en: As I listened to her clear, pleasant voice reading aloud, I kept glancing from her to the path of the flower-garden, where the rain- spots were making small dark circles in the sand, and thence to the lime-trees, upon the leaves of which the rain was pattering down in large detached drops shed from the pale, shimmering edge of the livid blue cloud which hung suspended over us.
uz: Uning ochiq va yoqimli ovozini baland ovoz bilan o'qiyotganini tinglaganimda, men uning yonidan gul bog'ining yo'liga, yomg'ir maydonlari qumda kichik qora doiralar tuzgan joyga, keyin esa namzorlar tomon qarab turardim, ularning barglariga yomg'ir katta bo'sh tomchilariga tushib, bizdan oshib turgan rang-barang ko'k bulutning chiroqli, chiroqli chegarasidan tushdi.

en: Then I would glance at her again, and then at the last purple rays of the setting sun where they were throwing the dense clusters of old, rain-washed birches into brilliant relief.
uz: So'ngra men unga yana bir bor nazar tashlab, quyosh botgan kunning oxirgi bo'yoq nurlariga qarardim, ular eski, yomg'ir bilan yuvib o'tilgan birkalar to'plamini ajoyib ta'sirga aylantirib qo'yishgan edi.

en: Yet again my eyes would return to Varenika, and, each time that they did so, it struck me afresh that she was not nearly so plain as at first I had thought her.
uz: Yana bir bor ko'zlarim Varenikaga qaytib borardi va har safar uni ko'rganimda, u o'zim o'ylaganimdek sodda emasligini ko'rdim.

en: “How I wish that I wasn’t in love already!” I reflected, “or that Sonetchka was Varenika!
uz: Qani endi sevmagan bo'lardim! - deb o'yladim, - yoki Sonetchka Varenika edi!

en: How nice it would be if suddenly I could become a member of this family, and have the three ladies for my mother, aunt, and wife respectively!” All the time that these thoughts kept passing through my head I kept attentively regarding Varenika as she read, until somehow I felt as though I were magnetising her, and that presently she must look at me.
uz: Birdan bu oila a'zosi bo'lib, uchta xonimni onam, xonim va xotinimga aylantirishim mumkin bo'lsa, naqadar yaxshi bo'lardi! Bu fikrlar boshimdan o'tib ketayotgan vaqt davomida men Varenikaga diqqat bilan qaradim, u o'qigan paytda, bir yo'l bilan uni maqnitda qoldirayotgandek his qildim va hozir u menga qarashi kerakligini his qildim.

en: Sure enough, at length she raised her head, threw me a glance, and, meeting my eyes, turned away.
uz: To'g'ri, oxir-oqibat u boshini ko'tarib, menga ko'z tikdi va ko'zlarimni ko'rib, yuz o'girdi.

en: “The rain does not seem to stop,” she remarked.
uz: Yog'i to'xtamaydi, deb aytdi u.

en: Suddenly a new feeling came over me.
uz: Toʻsatdan menga yangi his-tuygʻu keldi.

en: I began to feel as though everything now happening to me was a repetition of some similar occurrence before—as though on some previous occasion a shower of rain had begun to fall, and the sun had set behind birch-trees, and I had been looking at her, and she had been reading aloud, and I had magnetised her, and she had looked up at me.
uz: O'zimga sodir bo'layotgan barcha voqealar avvalgidek sodir bo'lgan voqealarning takrorlanishini his qila boshladim, xuddi avvalgi paytlarda yomg'ir yog'ishni boshlagan va quyosh birch daraxtlari orqasida o'tib ketgan bo'lgandek, men unga qarab turardim, u baland ovoz bilan o'qiyotgan edi, men uni magnetizatsiya qilgan edim va u menga qarab turardi.

en: Yes, all this I seemed to recall as though it had happened once before.
uz: Ha, bularning barchasini bir marta sodir bo'lganidek eslab qolganman.

en: “Surely she is not—SHE?” was my thought.
uz: O'zim o'yladimki, albatta u o'zi emas.

en: “Surely IT is not beginning?” However, I soon decided that Varenika was not the “SHE” referred to, and that “it” was not “beginning.” “In the first place,” I said to myself, “Varenika is not at all BEAUTIFUL.
uz: Shuni aytish joizki, bu boshlanmayapti?Shunga qaramay, men tez orada Varenika haqida gap ketmaganini va u boshlanmayotganini tushundim.Birinchida o'zimga: Varenika hech qachon chiroyli emas, deb o'yladim.

en: She is just an ordinary girl whose acquaintance I have made in the ordinary way, whereas the she whom I shall meet somewhere and some day and in some not ordinary way will be anything but ordinary.
uz: U shunchaki oddiy qiz, men uni oddiy tarzda tanishtirdim, ammo men bir joyda va bir kunda va oddiy emas tarzda uchrashadigan qiz esa oddiy emas.

en: family pleases me so much only because hitherto I have never seen anybody.
uz: Oila menga juda yoqadi, chunki men hech qachon hech kimni ko'rmaganman.

en: Such things will always be happening in the future, and I shall see many more such families during my life.”
uz: Kelajakda ham shunday voqealar sodir bo'ladi va hayotim davomida bunday oilalarni ko'proq ko'raman.

en: I SHOW OFF AT tea time the reading came to an end, and the ladies began to talk among themselves of persons and things unknown to me.
uz: O'qish yakunlandi va xonimlar men uchun noma'lum bo'lgan odamlar va narsalar to'g'risida o'zaro gapira boshlashdi.

en: This I conceived them to be doing on purpose to make me conscious (for all their kind demeanour) of the difference which years and position in the world had set between them and myself.
uz: Men buni ular o'zlari va men o'rtasida yillar va dunyoda o'rnatilgan mavqeyning farqi haqida (barcha mehribon xulq-atvorlari uchun) o'zimni xabardor qilish uchun qasddan qilayotganlarini tasavvur qildim.

en: In general discussions, however, in which I could take part I sought to atone for my late silence by exhibiting that extraordinary cleverness and originality to which I felt compelled by my University uniform.
uz: Biroq, men ishtirok etadigan umumiy muhokamalarda, universitet kiyimim meni majburlagan o'zgacha aql-idrok va o'ziga xoslikni namoyon etib, kechki shubhamni to'xtatishga harakat qildim.

en: For instance, when the conversation turned upon country houses, I said that Prince Ivan Ivanovitch had a villa near Moscow which people came to see even from London and Paris, and that it contained balustrading which had cost ൤൩ൡ,ൡൡൡ roubles.
uz: Masalan, suhbat qishloq uylariga aylanganida, men Prens Ivan Ivanovitchning Moskva yaqinidagi villasi borligini va hatto London va Parijdan kelgan odamlar uni ko'rish uchun kelganini va u yerda balustradalar borligini aytdim.

en: Likewise, I remarked that the Prince was a very near relation of mine, and that, when lunching with him the same day, he had invited me to go and spend the entire summer with him at that villa, but that I had declined, since I knew the villa well, and had stayed in it more than once, and that all those balustradings and bridges did not interest me, since I could not bear ornamental work, especially in the country, where I liked everything to be wholly countrified.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, men shohning mening yaqin qarindoshim ekanligini va o'sha kuni u bilan birga tushlikka chiqqanimda, u meni o'sha villada butun yozni o'tkazishga taklif qilganini aytdim, lekin men uni yaxshi bilganim uchun rad etganimni va u yerda bir necha marta qolganimni va barcha balustradalar va ko'priklar menga qiziqmaganini aytdim, chunki men bezakchilik ishlarini ko'tarolmasdim, ayniqsa, qishloq joylarda, men hamma narsa to'liq mamlakatga aylanishi kerak bo'lgan joyda.

en: After delivering myself of this extraordinary and complicated romance, I grew confused, and blushed so much that every one must have seen that I was lying.
uz: O'zimni bu g'alati va murakkab ishdan ozod qilgandan so'ng, men juda chalg'ib qoldim va shunchalik qizg'in bo'ldimki, hamma men yolg'on gapirayotganimni ko'rgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: Both Varenika, who was handing me a cup of tea, and Sophia Ivanovna, who had been gazing at me throughout, turned their heads away, and began to talk of something else with an expression which I afterwards learnt that good-natured people assume when a very young man has told them a manifest string of lies—an
uz: Menga choy berayotgan Varenika ham, menga ko'z tikib turgan Sofiya Ivanovna ham boshlarini o'zgartirgan va keyinchalik yaxshi odamlar juda yosh yigit ularga ochiq-oydin yolg'onlarni aytib berganida, buni qabul qilishlarini bilib olganimcha, boshqa bir narsa haqida gapira boshlashdi.

en: expression which says, “Yes, we know he is lying, and why he is doing it, the poor young fellow!” What I had said about Prince Ivan Ivanovitch having a country villa, I had related simply because I could find no other pretext for mentioning both my relationship to the Prince and the fact that I had been to luncheon with him that day; yet why I had said all I had about the balustrading costing ൤൩ൡ,ൡൡൡ roubles, and about my having several times visited the Prince at that villa (I had never once been there—more especially since the Prince possessed no residences save in Moscow and Naples, as the Nechludoffs very well knew), I could not possibly tell you.
uz: "Ha, biz uning yolg'on gapirayotganini bilamiz va nega u shunday qilyapti, kambag'al yigit! Men Prens Ivan Ivanovitchning qishloq villasida bo'lishi haqida aytgan gapimni shunchaki Prens bilan munosabatimni va o'sha kuni u bilan birga tushlikka borganimni aytib berish uchun boshqa bahona topa olmasligim uchun aytib berdim; lekin nima uchun men balustradalar narxining , rubllari to'g'risida va o'sha villada bir necha marta Prensga tashrif buyurganligim haqida aytgan edim (Men u erda hech qachon bo'lmaganman) (ayniqsa, Prensning Moskva va Neapolda hech qanday yashash joyi bo'lmaganligi sababli, Nechludofflar bundan mustasno), men sizga aytolmayman.

en: Neither in childhood nor in adolescence nor in riper years did I ever remark in myself the vice of falsehood—on the contrary, I was, if anything, too outspoken and truthful.
uz: Bolaligimda ham, o'smirligimda ham, katta yoshda ham yolg'on gapirishning yomonligini hech qachon o'zimda sezmaganman, aksincha, men juda ochiq va rostgo'y edim.

en: Yet, during this first stage of my manhood, I often found myself seized with a strange and unreasonable tendency to lie in the most desperate fashion.
uz: Biroq, o'smirligimning ushbu dastlabki bosqichi davomida men ko'pincha yolg'on gapirishning g'ayrioddiy va asossiz moyilligiga duch kelganman.

en: I say advisedly “in the most desperate fashion,” for the reason that I lied in matters in which it was the easiest thing in the world to detect me.
uz: Men o'zimni dunyodagi eng oson ish deb topgan masalalarda yolg'on gapirganim sababli, eng ko'ngilsiz tarzda aytaman.

en: On the whole I think that a vain-glorious desire to appear different from what I was, combined with an impossible hope that the lie would never be found out, was the chief cause of this extraordinary impulse.
uz: Umuman olganda, men o'zimdan boshqacha ko'rinishni xohlagan va yolg'on hech qachon aniqlanmaydi degan umid bilan birlashtirilgan behuda shiddatli istak, bu g'alati impulsning asosiy sababi bo'lgan deb o'ylayman.

en: After tea, since the rain had stopped and the after-glow of sunset was calm and clear, the Princess proposed that we should go and stroll in the lower garden, and admire her favourite spots there.
uz: Choydan so'ng, yomg'ir to'xtadi va quyosh botishining yorqinligi tinch va aniq bo'lgani sababli, princess pastki bog'da o'tishga va o'sha yerda sevimli joylarini tomosha qilishga taklif qildi.

en: Following my rule to be always original, and conceiving that clever people like myself and the Princess must surely be above the banalities of politeness, I replied that I could not bear a walk with no object in view, and that, if I DID walk, I liked to walk alone.
uz: Mening har doim original bo'lish qoidamni qo'llab, o'zim va princess kabi aqlli odamlar xushmuomalalikning oddiy hollaridan ustun bo'lishlari kerakligini tushunib, men hech qanday maqsadga ega bo'lmagan holda yurishga chiday olmayotganimni va agar yurishim mumkin bo'lsa, yolg'iz yurishni yaxshi ko'rganimni aytdim.

en: I had no idea that this speech was simply rude; all I thought was that, even as nothing could be more futile than empty compliments, so nothing could be more pleasing and original than a little frank brusquerie.
uz: Bu nutq shunchaki qo'pollik deb o'ylamagan edim; faqatgina o'yladimki, hech narsa bo'sh maqtovlardan ko'ra befoyda bo'lmasligi mumkin bo'lsa-da, hech narsa ozgina frank brusquerie dan ko'ra yoqimli va original bo'lmasligi mumkin.

en: However, though much pleased with my answer, I set out with the rest of the company.
uz: Biroq, javobimdan juda mamnun bo'lsam-da, kompaniya a'zolari bilan birga yo'lga chiqdim.

en: The Princess’s favourite spot of all was at the very bottom of the lower garden, where a little bridge spanned a narrow piece of swamp.
uz: Princessning eng sevimli joyi pastki bog'ning tubida bo'lgan, u yerda kichik ko'prik bo'lakni kesib o'tadi.

en: The view there was very restricted, yet very intimate and pleasing.
uz: U erda ko'rinish juda cheklangan, ammo juda yaqin va yoqimli edi.

en: We are so accustomed to confound art with nature that,
uz: Biz san'atni tabiat bilan qarama-qarshi ko'rishga shunchalik odatlanib qolganmizki,

en: often enough, phenomena of nature which are never to be met with in pictures seem to us unreal, and give us the impression that nature is unnatural, or vice versa; whereas phenomena of nature which occur with too much frequency in pictures seem to us hackneyed, and views which are to be met with in real life, but which appear to us too penetrated with a single idea or a single sentiment, seem to us arabesques.
uz: Ko'pincha rasmlarda hech qachon uchrashmaydigan tabiat hodisalari bizga haqiqiy emas deb tuyuladi va bizga tabiatning tabiiy emasligi yoki aksincha bo'lishi kabi taassurot qoldiradi; ammo rasmlarda tez-tez sodir bo'ladigan tabiat hodisalari bizga o'zgartirilgan deb tuyuladi va haqiqiy hayotda uchrashadigan, ammo bizga bitta fikr yoki bitta his-tuyg'u bilan juda charchagan ko'rinishlar bizga arabesk deb tuyuladi.

en: The view from the Princess’s favourite spot was as follows.
uz: Princessning sevimli joyidan ko'rinish quyidagicha edi.

en: On the further side of a small lake, over-grown with weeds round its edges, rose a steep ascent covered with bushes and with huge old trees of many shades of green, while, overhanging the lake at the foot of the ascent, stood an ancient birch tree which, though partly supported by stout roots implanted in the marshy bank of the lake, rested its crown upon a tall, straight poplar, and dangled its curved branches over the smooth surface of the pond—both branches and the surrounding greenery being reflected therein as in a mirror.
uz: O'zining chegaralari atrofida begona o'tlar bilan to'lib-toshgan kichkina ko'lning boshqa tomoniga ko'plab butalar bilan qoplangan va ko'pcha yashil rangli katta eski daraxtlar bilan qoplangan baland ko'tarilgan, ko'lning past tomonida esa qadimgi bir chiroyli daraxt ko'tarilib turardi, u ko'lning cho'lakli qirg'og'ida o'rnatilgan kuchli ildizlar bilan qisman qo'llab-quvvatlangan bo'lsa-da, uning tojini baland, to'g'ri poplar ustiga o'rnatdi va egri bo'laklarini hovuzning tekis yuzi ustida bog'lab qo'ydi.

en: “How lovely!” said the Princess with a nod of her head, and addressing no one in particular.
uz: "Qo'p yoqimli!" - dedi princess boshini g'iybat qilib, hech kimga murojaat qilmay.

en: “Yes, marvellous!” I replied in my desire to show that had an opinion of my own on every subject.
uz: Ha, ajoyib! Men har bir mavzuda o'zimning fikrim borligini ko'rsatish istagim bilan javob berdim.

en: “Yet somehow it all looks to me so terribly like a scheme of decoration.” The Princess went on gazing at the scene as though she had not heard me, and turning to her sister and Lubov Sergievna at intervals, in order to point out to them its details—especially a curved, pendent bough, with its reflection in the water, which particularly pleased her.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, bu menga juda dahshatli tarzda bezaklash usuliga o'xshaydi. Qizimcha meni eshitmagan bo'lsa-da, o'z singlisi va Lubov Sergiyevnaga vaqti-vaqti bilan murojaat qilib, uning tafsilotlarini, ayniqsa, suvda aks ettirilgan egri, bo'g'ilgan shoxani ko'rsatadi. Bu unga ayniqsa yoqdi.

en: Sophia Ivanovna observed to me that it was all very beautiful, and that she and her sister would sometimes spend hours together at this spot; yet it was clear that her remarks were meant merely to please the Princess.
uz: Sofiya Ivanovna menga hamma narsa juda chiroyli ekanligini va u va singlisi ba'zan bu joyda soatlab birga bo'lishganligini aytdi; ammo uning gaplari faqatgina printsessani mamnun qilish uchun qilinganligi aniq edi.

en: I have noticed that people who are gifted with the faculty of loving are seldom receptive to the beauties of nature.
uz: O'yladimki, sevgi qobiliyatiga ega bo'lgan odamlar tabiatning go'zalliklariga kamdan-kam e'tiborli.

en: Lubov Sergievna also seemed enraptured, and asked (among other things), “How does that birch tree manage to support itself?
uz: Lubov Sergiyevna ham g'ayratga tushdi va so'radi (ba'zi narsalardan tashqari), Bu birch daraxti o'zini qanday ta'minlaydi?

en: Has it stood there long?” Yet the next moment she became absorbed in contemplation of her little dog Susetka, which, with its stumpy paws pattering to and fro upon the bridge in a mincing fashion, seemed to say by the expression of its face that this was the first time it had ever found itself out of doors.
uz: U yerda uzoq vaqt turibdimi? Ammo keyingi daqiqa o'zining kichkina itsi Susetka haqida mulohaza yuritib o'tirdi, u o'z qo'llari ko'prikdan o'z-o'zidan ko'tarib o'tirgan holda ko'prikdan o'z-o'zidan ko'tarib o'tirdi va yuzidagi ifodasi orqali o'zini birinchi marta eshikdan tashqariga chiqarganini aytgandek tuyuldi.

en: As for Dimitri, he fell to discoursing
uz: Dimitriyga kelsak, u nutq so'zlashga tushdi.

en: very logically to his mother on the subject of how no view can be beautiful of which the horizon is limited.
uz: Onasiga hech qanday ko'rinish chiroyli bo'lishi mumkin emasligi to'g'risida juda mantiqiy fikrda bo'lgan.

en: Varenika alone said nothing.
uz: Varenika yolg'iz hech narsa aytmadi.

en: Glancing at her, I saw that she was leaning over the parapet of the bridge, her profile turned towards me, and gazing straight in front of her.
uz: Unga tikilib qaraganimda, ko'prikning pareti ustida yonboshlaganini ko'rdim, uning profili menga qarab, to'g'ri uning oldiga qarab turardi.

en: Something seemed to be interesting her deeply, or even affecting her, since it was clear that she was oblivious to her surroundings, and thinking neither of herself nor of the fact that any one might be regarding her.
uz: O'ziga chuqur qiziqadigan yoki hatto unga ta'sir qiladigan narsa paydo bo'ldi, chunki u atrofidagi narsalarni bilmay, o'zi haqida ham, hech kim uni qiziqtirmasligi haqida ham o'ylamagan.

en: In the expression of her large eyes there was nothing but wrapt attention and quiet, concentrated thought, while her whole attitude seemed so unconstrained and, for all her shortness, so dignified that once more some recollection or another touched me and once more I asked myself, “Is IT, then, beginning?” Yet again I assured myself that I was already in love with Sonetchka, and that Varenika was only an ordinary girl, the sister of my friend.
uz: Uning katta ko'zlarining ifodasida faqat diqqat va xotirjamlik bilan o'ylab ko'rish mumkin edi, ammo uning butun munosabatlari juda cheksiz va qisqa bo'lishiga qaramay, shunchalik qadrli bo'lganki, yana bir bor bir xotira meni qo'zg'atdi va o'zimdan so'radim: Shunday bo'lsa-da, bu boshlanadimi? Yana bir bor o'zimga ishonch hosil qildimki, men allaqachon Sonetchka bilan muhabbatda edim va Varenika oddiy qiz, do'stimning singlisi edi.

en: Though she pleased me at that moment, I somehow felt a vague desire to show her, by word or deed, some small unfriendliness.
uz: Garchi u o'sha paytda menga yoqqan bo'lsa-da, men unga so'z yoki ish orqali kamroq noqulaylikni ko'rsatishni istardim.

en: “I tell you what, Dimitri,” I said to my friend as I moved nearer to Varenika, so that she might overhear what I was going to say, “it seems to me that, even if there had been no mosquitos here, there would have been nothing to commend this spot; whereas “—and here I slapped my cheek, and in very truth annihilated one of those insects—“it is simply awful.” “Then you do not care for nature?” said Varenika without turning her head.
uz: Men sizga nima deyman, Dimitri,  Men Varenikaga yaqinlashayotganimda do'stimga aytdim, shunda u mening aytmoqchi bo'lganimni eshitishi mumkin edi,  Menga o'xshaydi, agar bu yerda iltijolar bo'lmagan bo'lsa ham, bu joyni maqtagan hech narsa bo'lmasdi; lekin  va bu erda men tungiga urdim va haqiqatdan ham bu hasharotlardan birini yo'q qildim, bu shunchaki dahshatli.  "Shunda siz tabiat haqida qayg'urmayapsizmi? dedi Varenika boshini o'zgartirmasdan.

en: “I think it a foolish, futile pursuit,” I replied, well satisfied that I had said something to annoy her, as well as something original.
uz: "Men buni ahmoqlik va behuda ish deb o'ylayman", - deb javob berdim men, uni bezovta qiladigan biron bir gap aytganimdan mamnun bo'lib, biroz original gap aytdim.

en: Varenika only raised her eyebrows a little, with an expression of pity, and went on gazing in front of her as calmly as before.
uz: Varenika o'z ko'z o'nglarini biroz ko'tardi va rahm-shafqat bilan uning oldidagi ko'zlarini xuddi avvalgidek tinchlik bilan ko'rib turdi.

en: I felt vexed with her.
uz: O'zimni u bilan xafa his qilardim.

en: Yet, for all that, the rusty, paint-blistered parapet on which she was leaning, the way in which the dark waters of the pond reflected the drooping branch of the overhanging birch tree (it almost seemed to me as though branch and its reflection met), the rising odour of the swamp, the feeling of crushed mosquito on my cheek, and her absorbed look and statuesque pose—many times afterwards did these things recur with unexpected vividness to my recollection.
uz: Ammo shunga qaramay, u tiklanayotgan rangli, rang-bo'lakli shkaf, hovuzning qorong'i suvlari osilgan bo'lakni aks ettirgan yo'l (o'sha bo'lak va uning aks ettirilishi uchrashganiga o'xshardi), o'rmonning ko'tarilgan xushbo'yligi, yig'ilgan tog'ning his-tuyg'usi va uning chiroyli ko'rinishi va haykalli posesi ko'p marotaba o'tgach, bu voqealar o'zimga kutilmagan tarzda takrorlandi.

en: DIMITRI WHEN we returned to the house from our stroll, Varenika declined to sing as she usually did in the evenings, and I was conceited enough to attribute this to my doing, in the belief that its reason lay in what I had said on the bridge.
uz: DIMITRI, yurganimizdan uyga qaytib kelganimizda, Varenika kechqurun odatdagidek qo'shiq kuylashni rad etdi va men buni o'z ishim bilan bog'lashim uchun o'zimni o'yladim, chunki uning sababi mening ko'prikda aytganlarimga bog'liq edi.

en: The Nechludoffs never had supper, and went to bed early, while to-night, since Dimitri had the toothache (as Sophia Ivanovna had foretold), he departed with me to his room even earlier than usual.
uz: Nechludofflar hech qachon kechki ovqat yemadilar va erta yotgan edilar, Dimitriyning tish og'rig'i bo'lgani sababli (Sofya Ivanovna bashorat qilganidek) bugun kechasi esa u men bilan o'z xonasiga odatdagidan ham erta jo'nab ketdi.

en: Feeling that I had done all that was required of me by my blue collar and gilt buttons, and that every one was very pleased with me, I was in a gratified, complacent mood, while Dimitri, on the other hand, was rendered by his quarrel with his sister and the toothache both taciturn and gloomy.
uz: O'zimni ko'k bo'yinturug' va oltin tugmalar bilan talab qilingan hamma narsani bajarganimni va hamma menga juda rozi bo'lganini his qilganimda, men mamnun va o'z-o'zimga rozi bo'lgan ruhda edim, Dimitri esa singlisi bilan bahslashgani va tish og'rig'i tufayli so'nggi va so'nggi holatda bo'lgan.

en: He sat down at the table, got out a couple of notebooks—a diary and the copy-book in which it was his custom every evening to inscribe the tasks performed by or awaiting him—and, continually frowning and touching his cheek with his hand, continued writing for a while.
uz: U dasturxonga o'tirib, bir necha yorliqlar, bir kunlik kundalik va nusxalar kitobini olib chiqdi, unda har kuni kechqurun uning bajargan yoki uni kutib turgan vazifalarni yozib olish odati bor edi.Ustiga-sekin burunlarini burib, o'z qo'li bilan chehralariga tegib, biroz vaqt yozishni davom ettirdi.

en: “Oh, DO leave me alone!” he cried to the maid whom Sophia Ivanovna sent to ask him whether his teeth were still hurting him, and whether he would not like to have a poultice made.
uz: Oh, meni tinch qo'ymang! Sofiya Ivanovna unga tishlari hali ham og'riqlimi va u poultice qilishni xohlamaydimi deb so'rash uchun yuborgan xizmatkor ayolga baqirdi.

en: Then, saying that my bed would soon be ready for me and that he would be back presently, he departed to Lubov Sergievna’s room.
uz: So'ngra, mening yotoqim tezda tayyor bo'lishini va u tezda qaytib kelishini aytib, u Lubov Sergiyevna xonasiga jo'nab ketdi.

en: “What a pity that Varenika is not good-looking and, in general, Sonetchka!” I reflected when I found myself alone.
uz: Varenika va, umuman aytganda, Sonetchka chiroyli emasligi juda achinarli! O'zimni yolg'iz topganimda o'yladim.

en: “How nice it would be if, after I have left the University, I could go to her and offer her my hand!
uz: Universitetni tark etganimdan keyin uning oldiga borib, qo'limni taklif qilsam, naqadar yaxshi bo'lardi!

en: I would say to her, ‘Princess, though no longer young, and therefore unable to love passionately, I will cherish you as a dear sister.
uz: Men unga shunday deyardim: "Qizim, hali yosh emasman, shuning uchun ishtiyoq bilan sevishga qodir emasman, lekin seni aziz singlim sifatida qadrlayman.

en: And you,’ I would continue to her mother, ‘I greatly respect; and you, Sophia Ivanovna, I value highly.
uz: Sizni esa, onasiga hurmatim katta, sizni esa, Sofiya Ivanovna, juda qadrlayman.

en: Therefore say to me, Varenika (since I ask you to be my wife), just the simple and direct word YES.’ And she would give me her hand, and I should press it, and say, ‘Mine is a love which depends not upon words, but upon deeds.’ And suppose,” next came into my head, “that Dimitri
uz: Shunday qilib, menga "Varenika" deb ayting (chunki men sizdan xotinim bo'lishingizni so'rayman), shunchaki oddiy va to'g'ridan-to'g'ri "Ha" degan so'z. U menga qo'lini uzatadi va men uni bossam, "Mening sevgim so'zlarga emas, balki amallarga bog'liq. Va deying, keyinchalik men o'ylaymanki,Dimitriy

en: should suddenly fall in love with Lubotshka (as Lubotshka has already done with him), and should desire to marry her?
uz: Lubotshka bilan to'satdan muhabbatga tushishi kerakmi (Lubotshka unga o'xshab) va u bilan turmush qurish istagini bildirishi kerakmi?

en: Then either one or the other of us would have to resign all thought of marriage.
uz: Keyin bir yoki ikkovimiz turmush qurishni rad etishimiz kerak bo'ladi.

en: Well, it would be splendid, for in that case I should act thus.
uz: To'g'ri, bu ajoyib bo'lardi, chunki u holda men shunday yo'l tutishim kerak edi.

en: As soon as I had noticed how things were, I should make no remark, but go to Dimitri and say, ‘It is no use, my friend, for you and I to conceal our feelings from one another.
uz: Vaziyat qanday bo'lganini payqaganimdan so'ng, men hech qanday fikr bildirmasdim, balki Dimitriyning oldiga borib: "Xudoyim, sen va men o'z his-tuyg'ularimizni bir-birimizdan yashirishimizning foydasi yo'q.

en: You know that my love for your sister will terminate only with my life.
uz: Siz o'zingiz bilasizki, singilingizga bo'lgan sevgim faqat mening hayotim bilan tugaydi.

en: Yet I know all; and though you have deprived me of all hope, and have rendered me an unhappy man, so that Nicolas Irtenieff will have to bewail his misery for the rest of his existence, yet do you take my sister,’ and I should lay his hand in Lubotshka’s.
uz: Ammo men hamma narsani bilaman; va siz meni har qanday umiddan mahrum qilib, baxtsiz odam qilib qo'ygan bo'lsangiz ham, Nikolas Irtenieff o'z hayoti davomida azob-uqubatidan qayg'urishi kerak bo'lsa-da, siz mening singlimni olib ketasiz va men Lubotshkasga qo'limni qo'yib beraman.

en: Then he would say to me, ‘No, not for all the world!’ and I should reply, ‘Prince Nechludoff, it is in vain for you to attempt to outdo me in nobility.
uz: Keyin u menga: "Yo'q, butun dunyo uchun emas!" - deb aytadi va men javob beraman: "Prints Nechludoff, siz meni asillikdan ustun qo'yishga urinayotganingiz befoyda.

en: Not in the whole world does there exist a more magnanimous being than Nicolas Irtenieff.’ Then I should salute him and depart.
uz: Butun dunyoda Nikolas Irtenieffdan ko'ra ko'proq rahmdil bo'lgan shaxs yo'q. Keyin men unga salom berib ketishim kerak.

en: In tears Dimitri and Lubotshka would pursue me, and entreat me to accept their sacrifice, and I should consent to do so, and, perhaps, be happy ever afterwards—if only I were in love with Varenika.” These fancies tickled my imagination so pleasantly that I felt as though I should like to communicate them to my friend; yet, despite our mutual vow of frankness, I also felt as though I had not the physical energy to do so.
uz: Dimitri va Lubotshka menga ko'z yoshlari bilan ergashib, ularning qurbonligini qabul qilishni iltimos qilishardi va men bunga rozi bo'lishim kerak edi va, ehtimol, bundan keyin ham baxtli bo'lishim kerak edi, agar men faqat Varenikaga muhabbat qilardim. Ushbu xayollar tasavvurimni shunchalik yoqimli qo'zg'atardiki, ularni do'stim bilan baham ko'rishni istardim; ammo, o'zaro rostgo'ylik va'dasidan qat'i nazar, men ham shunday qilish uchun jismoniy kuchim yo'qdek his qildim.

en: Dimitri returned from Lubov Sergievna’s room with some toothache capsules which she had given him, yet in even greater pain, and therefore in even greater depression, than before.
uz: Dimitri Lubov Sergievna xonasidan unga bergan bir nechta tish og'rig'i kapsulalari bilan qaytib keldi, ammo u bundan ham og'riqli va shuning uchun ham avvalgidan ham og'irroq tushkunlikda edi.

en: Evidently no bedroom had yet been prepared for me, for presently the boy who acted as Dimitri’s valet arrived to ask him where I was to sleep.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, men uchun hali hech qanday yotoq xonasi tayyorlanmagan edi, chunki Dimitrining xizmatkori bo'lgan o'g'il endi undan qaerda uxlayotganimni so'rash uchun keldi.

en: “Oh, go to the devil!” cried Dimitri, stamping his foot.
uz: Oh, shaytonning oldiga bor! Dimitriy oyoqlarini cho'kib, baqirib yubordi.

en: “Vasika, Vasika, Vasika!” he went on, the instant that the boy had left the room, with a gradual raising of his voice at each repetition.
uz: "Vasika, Vasika, Vasika!" - deb davom etdi u, o'g'il xonani tark etgan paytdan boshlab, har bir takrorlashda ovozini asta-sekin ko'tardi.

en: “Vasika, lay me out a bed on the floor.” “No, let ME sleep on the floor,” I objected.
uz: Vasika, menga yotoqni yerga qo'ying.Yo'q, menga yotoqda uxlashga ruxsat bering, Men qarshilik ko'rdim.

en: “Well, it is all one.
uz: Ha, bularning hammasi bitta.

en: Lie anywhere you like,” continued Dimitri in the same angry tone.
uz: Qayerda xohlasangiz, yolg'on gapiring, - dedi Dimitri, xuddi shunday g'azabga to'lib.

en: “Vasika, why don’t you go and do what I tell you?” Evidently Vasika did not understand what was demanded of him, for he remained where he was.
uz: Vasika, nima uchun bormaysan va men aytganimni qilmaysan? Vasika, ehtimol, undan nima talab qilinishini tushunmagan, chunki u o'z joyida qoldi.

en: “What is the matter with you?
uz: Siz bilan nima yuz berdi?

en: Go and lay the bed, Vasika, I tell you!” shouted Dimitri, suddenly bursting into a sort of frenzy; yet Vasika still did not understand, but, blushing hotly, stood motionless.
uz: Borib, to'shagingni uzing, Vasika, senga aytaman! - deb baqirib yubordi Dimitri, to'satdan g'azabga to'lib-toshdi; lekin Vasika hali ham tushunmadi, lekin qizg'in qizg'inlab, harakatsiz turdi.

en: “So you are determined to drive me mad, are you?”—and leaping from his chair and rushing upon the boy, Dimitri struck him on the head with the whole weight of his fist, until the boy rushed headlong from the room.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz meni g'azabga tushirishga qat'iy qaror qildingiz, shundaymi?Va o'rindiqidan tushib, o'g'ilning boshiga Dimitriy qo'l og'irligi bilan urib, o'g'ilning boshiga urib qo'ydi.

en: Halting in the doorway, Dimitri glanced at me, and the expression of fury and pain which had sat for a moment on his countenance suddenly gave place to such a boyish, kindly, affectionate, yet ashamed, expression that I felt sorry for him, and reconsidered my intention of leaving him to himself.
uz: Dimitri eshikda toʻxtab menga qaradi va uning yuzida bir zum davomida oʻtirgan gʻazab va ogʻriq ifodasini koʻrib, toʻsatdan oʻgʻillik, mehribonlik, mehribonlik, ammo uyatda boʻlgan ifodasini koʻrsatdi, shuning uchun men unga achinardim va uni oʻzi qoldirish niyatimni qayta koʻrib chiqdim.

en: He said nothing, but for a long time paced the room in silence, occasionally glancing at me with the same deprecatory expression as before.
uz: U hech narsa aytmadi, lekin uzoq vaqt davomida xonadonni xotirjamlik bilan bosib o'tdi va vaqti-vaqti bilan menga avvalgidek tanqislik bilan qarab turardi.

en: Then he took his notebook from the table, wrote something in it, took off his jacket and folded it carefully, and, stepping into the corner where the ikon hung, knelt down and began to say his prayers, with his large white hands folded upon his breast.
uz: So'ngra stoldan yozuv daftarini olib, unga biron narsa yozdi, kiyimini olib, diqqat bilan qatladi va ikoni osilgan burchakga kirib, tiz cho'kib, katta oq qo'llarini ko'krak ustiga qo'yib ibodat qila boshladi.

en: So long did he pray that Vasika had time to bring a mattress and spread it, under my whispered directions, on the floor.
