uz: U shunchalik uzoq ibodat qildiki, Vasika o'ziga matras olib kelib, uni men shoshib aytgan yo'nalishlarim ostida yerga tarqatishga vaqt topdi.

en: Indeed, I had undressed and laid myself down upon the mattress before Dimitri had finished.
uz: Darhaqiqat, Dimitriy o'z ishini tugatishdan oldin men kiyimimni yechib, matrasga o'tirib qoldim.

en: As I contemplated his slightly rounded back and the soles of his feet (which somehow seemed to stick out in my direction in a sort of repentant fashion whenever he made his obeisances), I felt that I liked him more than ever, and debated within myself whether or not I should tell him all I had been fancying concerning our respective sisters.
uz: Uning biroz yuziga aylangan orqasini va oyoq piyodalarini ko'rib chiqqachim (ular har safar sajda qilganida biroz tavba qilgan holda menga qarab turardi), men uni har qachongidan ham ko'proq yoqtirganimni his qildim va o'zimda bu haqda bahslashib o'tdim.

en: When he had finished his prayers, he lay down upon the bed near me, and, propping himself upon his elbow, looked at me in silence, with a kindly, yet abashed, expression.
uz: Ibodatlarini tugatganida, yonimda yotgan o'rinni egalladi va qo'lqovog'iga tiklanib, meni jismonan, ammo sharmanda ko'rinishda tomosha qildi.

en: Evidently he found it difficult to do this, yet meant thus to punish himself.
uz: Ko'rinib turganidek, bu ishni bajarish qiyin edi, ammo u o'zini jazolanish maqsadida shunday qildi.

en: Then I smiled and returned his gaze, and he smiled back at me.
uz: Keyin men tabassum qilib, uning ko'zlarini qaytarib berdim, u esa menga tabassum qildi.

en: “Why do you not tell me that my conduct has been abominable?” he said.
uz: Nima uchun menga mening xatti-harakatim jirkanch ekanini aytmaysiz? - dedi u.

en: “You have been thinking so, have you not?” “Yes,” I replied; and although it was something quite different which had been in my mind, it now seemed to me that that was what I had been thinking.
uz: Siz shunday o'ylayotgandirsiz, shunday emasmi?Ha, Men javob berdim; va bu mening ongimda o'zgacha narsa bo'lsa-da, endi men o'ylaganday tuyuldi.

en: “Yes, it was not right of you, nor should I have expected it of you.” It pleased me particularly at that moment to call
uz: Ha, bu sizdan noto'g'ri bo'ldi va men buni sizdan kutmasdim. O'sha paytda qo'ng'iroq qilish menga ayniqsa yoqdi

en: him by the familiar second person singular.
uz: Unga tanish ikkinchi shaxs singular.

en: “But how are your teeth now?” I added.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, endi tishlaringiz qanday? Men qo'shdim.

en: Nicolinka, my friend,” he went on, and so feelingly that it sounded as though tears were standing in his eyes, “I know and feel that I am bad, but God sees how I try to be better, and how I entreat Him to make me so.
uz: Nikolinka, do'stim, davom etdi va ko'zlarida ko'z yoshlari turganidek tuyuladi, "Men yomonligimni bilaman va his qilaman, lekin Xudo men yaxshiroq bo'lishga harakat qilayotganimni va Uni shunday qilishini iltijo qilayotganimni ko'radi.

en: Yet what am I to do with such an unfortunate, horrible nature as mine?
uz: Ammo men o'zim kabi baxtsiz va dahshatli tabiat bilan nima qilishim kerak?

en: What am I to do with it?
uz: Men bu bilan nima qilishim kerak?

en: I try to keep myself in hand and to rule myself, but suddenly it becomes impossible for me to do so—at all events, impossible for me to do so unaided.
uz: O'zimni nazorat qilishga va o'zimni boshqarishga harakat qilaman, lekin to'satdan barcha vaziyatlarda buni qilish men uchun imkonsiz bo'ladi.

en: I need the help and support of some one.
uz: Menga kimnidir yordam va qo'llab-quvvatlash kerak.

en: Now, there is Lubov Sergievna; SHE understands me, and could help me in this, and I know by my notebook that I have greatly improved in this respect during the past year.
uz: Endi, Lubov Sergiyevna bor; U meni tushunadi va bu borada menga yordam berishi mumkin, va men o'tgan yil davomida bu borada sezilarli darajada yaxshilanishimni eslatmoqdaman.

en: Ah, my dear Nicolinka”—he spoke with the most unusual and unwonted tenderness, and in a tone which had grown calmer now that he had made his confession—“how much the influence of a woman like Lubov could do for me!
uz: Oh, aziz Nikolinka, u eng odatiy va o'zgacha sezgirlik bilan gapirdi va hozirda tanbehini aytganidan keyin tinchroq bo'lgan tovush bilan Lubov kabi ayolning ta'siri menga qanchalar yordam berishi mumkinligini aytdi!

en: Think how good it would be for me if I could have a friend like her to live with when I have become independent!
uz: O'zim mustaqil bo'lganimda, u kabi do'stim bor bo'lsa, men uchun qanchalik yaxshi bo'lishini o'ylab ko'ring!

en: With her I should be another man.” And upon that Dimitri began to unfold to me his plans for marriage, for a life in the country, and for continual self-discipline.
uz: U bilan men boshqa erkak bo'lishim kerak. Va shundan so'ng Dimitriy menga nikoh, qishloq hayoti va doimiy o'zini tarbiyalash rejalarini aytishni boshladi.

en: “Yes, I will live in the country,” he said, “and you shall come to see me when you have married Sonetchka.
uz: - Ha, men qishloqda yashayman, - dedi u, - Sen esa Sonetchka bilan turmush qurganingda menga tashrif buyurasan.

en: Our children shall play together.
uz: Bolalarimiz birgalikda o'ynashadi.

en: All this may seem to you stupid and ridiculous, yet it may very well come to pass.” “Yes, it very well may” I replied with a smile, yet thinking how much nicer it would be if I married his sister.
uz: Bularning barchasi sizga ahmoqlik va g'alati tuyulishi mumkin, ammo u sodir bo'lishi mumkin. Ha, juda yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin. Men tabassum bilan javob berdim, ammo uning singlisi bilan turmush qurganimda qanchalik yaxshi bo'lishini o'yladim.

en: “I tell you what,” he went on presently; “you only imagine yourself to be in love with Sonetchka, whereas I can see that it is all rubbish, and that you do not really know what love means.” I did not protest, for, in truth, I almost agreed with him, and for a while we lay without speaking.
uz: Men sizga nima deyman, u hozir davom etdi; siz faqat o'zingizni Sonetchka bilan muhabbatda bo'lganingizni tasavvur qilasiz, ammo men bularning barchasi axlat ekanligini va siz muhabbat nimani anglatishini bilmasligingizni ko'rib turibman. Men protest qilmadim, chunki, haqiqatdan ham, men deyarli u bilan rozi bo'ldim va bir muncha vaqt biz gapirmasdan uxladik.

en: “Probably you have noticed that I have been in my old bad humour today, and have had a nasty quarrel with Varia?” he resumed.
uz: Ehtimol, bugun men o'zimning eski yomon humorim bilan shug'ullanayotganimni va Varia bilan yomon bahslashganimni sezgansiz? - deb davom etdi u.

en: “I felt bad about it afterwards—more particularly since it occurred in your presence.
uz: Keyinchalik o'zimni yomon his qildim, ayniqsa, bu sizning oldingizda sodir bo'lgani uchun.

en: Although she thinks wrongly on some subjects, she is a splendid girl and very good, as you will soon recognise.”
uz: Ba'zi mavzularda noto'g'ri fikr yuritishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, u ajoyib va juda yaxshi qiz, siz tezda tanishingiz mumkin.

en: His quick transition from mention of my love affairs to praise of his sister pleased me extremely, and made me blush, but I nevertheless said nothing more about his sister, and we went on talking of other things.
uz: Uning tezkor o'zgarishi, mening ishqiy munosabatlarim haqida gapirib, singlisi haqida maqtashdan juda mamnun bo'ldim va meni qizg'inlashtirdi, ammo men uning singlisi haqida boshqa hech narsa aytmadim va boshqa narsalar haqida gapiraverdik.

en: Thus we chattered until the cocks had crowed twice.
uz: Shunday qilib, toʻngʻizlar ikki marta qichqirguniga qadar suhbatlashdik.

en: In fact, the pale dawn was already looking in at the window when at last Dimitri lay down upon his bed and put out the candle.
uz: Darhaqiqat, yorqin tong darchaga qarab turgan edi, nihoyat Dimitriy o'z yotoqida o'tirib, shamolni o'chirib yubordi.

en: “Well, now for sleep,” he said.
uz: Endi uxlash uchun, dedi u.

en: “Yes,” I replied, “but—” “But what?” “Now nice it is to be alive in the daylight!” “Yes, it IS a splendid thing!” he replied in a voice which, even in the darkness, enabled me to see the expression of his cheerful, kindly eyes and boyish smile.
uz: Ha, Men javob berdim,  lekin Lekin nima?  Endi kun yorug'ida yashash yoqimli!  Ha, bu ajoyib narsa! U hatto qorong'ilikda ham uning quvonchli, mehribon ko'zlari va o'g'illik tabassumining ifodasini ko'rishga imkon beradigan ovoz bilan javob berdi.

en: IN THE COUNTRY Next day Woloda and myself departed in a post-chaise for the country.
uz: Ertasi kuni Voloda va men mamlakatga post-chaise bilan ketdik.

en: Turning over various Moscow recollections in my head as we drove along, I suddenly recalled Sonetchka Valakhin—though not until evening, and when we had already covered five stages of the road.
uz: Biz sayohatni davom ettirganimizda, boshimda turli Moskva xotiralarini o'zgartirganimda, to'satdan Sonetchka Valakhinni eslab qoldim, ammo kechgacha emas va yo'lning beshta bosqichini o'tkazdik.

en: “It is a strange thing,” I thought, “that I should be in love, and yet have forgotten all about it.
uz: Men o'yladimki, o'zimni sevgan bo'lsam ham, hamma narsani unutib qo'yishim g'alati.

en: I must start and think about her,” and straightway I proceeded to do so, but only in the way that one thinks when travelling—that is to say, disconnectedly, though vividly.
uz: Men uning haqida o'ylashni boshlashim kerak, va darhol shunday qilishni boshladim, lekin faqat sayohat paytida o'ylaydigan yo'l bilan, ya'ni, aloqasi bo'lmagan holda, ammo jonli ravishda.

en: Thus I brought myself to such a condition that, for the first two days after our arrival home, I somehow considered it incumbent upon me always to appear sad and moody in the presence of the household, and especially before Katenka, whom I looked upon as a great connoisseur in matters of this kind, and to whom I threw out a hint of
uz: Shunday qilib, men o'zimni shunday holatga yetkazdimki, uyga kelganimizdan keyin birinchi ikki kun davomida uydagilar oldida va ayniqsa Katenka oldida, men uni shu kabi masalalar bo'yicha buyuk bilimdon deb bilardim va unga o'zimning g'amginligimni ko'rsatishim kerak deb o'ylardim.

en: the condition in which my heart was situated.
uz: yuragimning holati.

en: Yet, for all my attempts at dissimulation and assiduous adoption of such signs of love sickness as I had occasionally observed in other people, I only succeeded for two days (and that at intervals, and mostly towards evening) in reminding myself of the fact that I was in love, and finally, when I had settled down into the new rut of country life and pursuits, I forgot about my affection for Sonetchka altogether.
uz: Biroq, boshqa odamlarda ba'zan kuzatilgan sevgi kasalligining belgilarini yashirish va g'ayratli qabul qilish uchun qilgan barcha urinishlarimga qaramay, men faqat ikki kun davomida (va bu oraliqlarda, asosan kechqurun) o'zimni o'zim sevganligimni eslatishga muvaffaq bo'ldim va nihoyat, qishloq hayoti va hayotning yangi yo'nalishlariga o'rnashganimda, Sonetchkaga bo'lgan sevgimni butunlay unutdim.

en: We arrived at Petrovskoe in the night time, and I was then so soundly asleep that I saw nothing of the house as we approached it, nor yet of the avenue of birch trees, nor yet of the household—all of whom had long ago betaken themselves to bed and to slumber.
uz: Petrovskoye shahriga kechasi yetib keldik va men o'sha payt shunchalik uxlab ketgandimki, unga yaqinlashayotganimizda uyni ham, birqachak daraxtlari yo'lini ham ko'rmadim, uzoq vaqt oldin o'zlarini uxlashga va uxlashga bag'ishlagan oila a'zolarini ham ko'rmadim.

en: Only old hunchbacked Foka—bare-footed, clad in some sort of a woman’s wadded nightdress, and carrying a candlestick—opened the door to us.
uz: Faqatgina qariya qo'ng'iroqli Fokabare-qiz, ayollarning yotoq kiyimlariga kiyingan va chiroqni ko'tarib, eshikni bizga ochgan.

en: As soon as he saw who we were, he trembled all over with joy, kissed us on the shoulders, hurriedly put on his felt slippers, and started to dress himself properly.
uz: Biz kim ekanimizni ko'rganidan so'ng, u quvonchdan titrab, yelkamizni o'pdi, shoshilinchlik bilan o'zining shisha cho'tkalarini kiydirdi va o'zini munosib kiyishni boshladi.

en: I passed in a semi-waking condition through the porch and up the steps, but in the hall the lock of the door, the bars and bolts, the crooked boards of the flooring, the chest, the ancient candelabrum (splashed all over with grease as of old), the shadows thrown by the crooked, chill, recently-lighted stump of candle, the perennially dusty, unopened window behind which I remembered sorrel to have grown—all was so familiar, so full of memories, so intimate of aspect, so, as it were, knit together by a single idea, that I suddenly became conscious of a tenderness for this quiet old house.
uz: Men yarim uyg'oqlik holatida verandadan va qadamlar ustida o'tdim, lekin zalda eshikning qulflari, barlar va boltlar, polning burakli pillalari, ko'krak, qadimgi chandelabrum (eski kabi yog' bilan qoplangan), burakli, sovuq, yaqinda yoritilgan shamolning soyasidan tashlangan soyalar, ko'p yillik changli, ochilmagan deraza, uning orqasida o'sganimni esladim. Hamma narsa shunchalik tanish edi, xotiralar bilan to'ldirilgan edi, shunchalik yaqin edi, bir xil fikr bilan bog'langan edi, degani kabi, men to'satdan bu xotirjam eski uy uchun mehribonlik hissi paydo bo'ldi.

en: Involuntarily I asked myself, “How have we, the house and I, managed to remain apart so long?” and, hurrying from spot to spot, ran to see if all the other rooms were still the same.
uz: O'zimdan: "Qanday qilib biz, uy va men, shuncha vaqt ajralib turdik?" - deb o'zimdan o'zimni o'yladim va joydan-uyga tez-tez yugurib, boshqa xonalarning hammasi bir xilligini ko'rishga yugurdim.

en: Yes, everything was unchanged, except that everything had become smaller and lower, and I myself taller, heavier, and more filled out.
uz: Ha, hamma narsa o'zgarmagan edi, faqatgina hamma narsa kichikroq va pastga tushdi va men o'zim baland, og'ir va to'la bo'ldim.

en: Yet, even as I was, the old house received me back into its arms, and aroused in me with every board, every window, every step of the stairs, and every sound the shadows of forms, feelings, and events of the happy but irrevocable past.
uz: Ammo, hali ham men shunday edim, eski uy meni qo'liga qaytarib oldi va har bir taxt, har bir deraza, har bir qadam va har bir tovush bilan mening ichimda baxtli, ammo qaytarib olinmaydigan o'tmishning shakllari, his-tuyg'ulari va hodisalarining soyasini uyg'otdi.

en: When we entered our old night nursery, all my childish fears lurked once more in the darkness of the corners and doorway.
uz: Eski kechki bolalar xonaga kirganimizda, bolalik qo'rquvlarim yana bir bor burchaklar va eshiklar qorong'iligida yashiringan.

en: When we passed into the drawing-room, I could feel the old calm motherly love diffusing itself from every object in the apartment.
uz: Jamoaxonadan o'tganimizda, o'sha eski, tinchlikparvar onalik sevgisini kvartiratning har bir ob'ektidan o'zini tarqatayotganini his qilardim.

en: In the breakfast-room, the noisy, careless
uz: Ovqatxonada shovqinli, beparvo odamlar bor.

en: merriment of childhood seemed merely to be waiting to wake to life again.
uz: Bolalik quvonchlari faqat yana tirilish uchun kutishdek tuyuldi.

en: In the divannaia (whither Foka first conducted us, and where he had prepared our beds) everything—mirror, screen, old wooden ikon, the lumps on the walls covered with white paper—seemed to speak of suffering and of death and of what would never come back to us again.
uz: Divannaida (Foka bizni birinchi marta olib borgan va u bizning to'shagimizni tayyorlagan joyda) hamma narsa - ko'rinchoq, ekran, eski yog'och ikoni, oq qog'oz bilan qoplangan devorlardagi bo'laklar - azob-uqubat va o'lim va bizga hech qachon qaytmaydigan narsalar haqida gapiradigan bo'ldi.

en: We got into bed, and Foka, bidding us good-night, retired.
uz: Yotoqga ketdik va Foka bizga yaxshi kecha taklif qilib, pensiyaga chiqdi.

en: “It was in this room that Mamma died, was it not?” said Woloda.
uz: Bu xonada onam vafot etgan, shunday emasmi? dedi Woloda.

en: I made no reply, but pretended to be asleep.
uz: Men hech qanday javob bermadim, balki uxlab yotganimni ko'rsatdim.

en: If I had said anything I should have burst into tears.
uz: Agar men biror narsa aytgan bo'lsam, ko'z yoshlarimga tushib qolishim kerak edi.

en: On awaking next morning, I beheld Papa sitting on Woloda’s bed in his dressing gown and slippers and smoking a cigar.
uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab uyg'onganimda, men otamni Woloda yotoqida o'tirganini ko'rdim, u kiyim-boshida, cho'tkalarida va sigaret chekayotganini ko'rdim.

en: Leaping up with a merry hoist of the shoulders, he came over to me, slapped me on the back with his great hand, and presented me his cheek to press my lips to.
uz: U yelkalarini quvonch bilan ko'tarib, yonimga keldi, katta qo'li bilan mening orqaga urdi va og'zimni bosib turish uchun yig'ini menga taqdim etdi.

en: “Well done, DIPLOMAT!” he said in his most kindly jesting tone as he looked at me with his small bright eyes.
uz: "Yaxshi ishlar qildingiz, diplomat!" - dedi u o'zining juda mehribon hazil tomoni bilan, o'zining kichkina, yorqin ko'zlari bilan menga qaraganida.

en: “Woloda tells me you have passed the examinations well for a youngster, and that is a splendid thing.
uz: Woloda menga o'g'il uchun imtihonlarni yaxshi o'tkazdingiz, deb aytdi va bu ajoyib narsa.

en: Unless you start and play the fool, I shall have another fine little fellow in you.
uz: Agar siz o'zingizni axmoqona ko'rsata olmasangiz, sizda yana bir go'zal yigit bor.

en: Thanks, my dear boy.
uz: Rahmat, aziz o'g'lim.

en: Well, we will have a grand time of it here now, and in the winter, perhaps, we shall move to St.
uz: Biz hozir bu yerda juda yaxshi vaqt o'tkazamiz va qishda esa, ehtimol, Sankt-Sant-Sant-Santga ko'chib o'tamiz.

en: I only wish the hunting was not over yet, or I could have given you some amusement in THAT way.
uz: Faqatgina ov hali tugagan bo'lmaganini xohlardim, yoki sizga o'yin-kulg'ini shunday qilib berardim.

en: Can you shoot, Woldemar?
uz: Siz o'q qila olasizmi, Voldemar?

en: However, whether there is any game or not, I will take you out some day.
uz: Biroq, o'yin bo'ladimi yoki yo'qmi, bir kun sizni olib ketaman.

en: Next winter, if God pleases, we will move to St.
uz: Kelasi qish, Xudo xohlasa, St. Petersburgga ko'chib o'tamiz.

en: Petersburg, and you shall meet people, and make friends, for you are now my two young grown-ups.
uz: Sankt-Peterburgda odamlar bilan uchrashasiz va do'stlashasiz, chunki siz endi mening ikkita yosh kattalarimsiz.

en: I have been telling Woldemar that you are just starting on your careers, whereas my day is ended.
uz: Men Woldemarga, siz karyerangizni boshlayotganingizni aytyapman, mening kunim esa tugadi.

en: You are old enough now to walk by yourselves, but, whenever you wish to confide in me, pray do so, for I am no longer your nurse, but your friend.
uz: Hozir siz o'zingiz yurishga yetarlicha katta bo'ldingiz, lekin menga ishonishni istasangiz, ibodat qiling, chunki men endi sizning hamshiralaringiz emas, balki do'stingizman.

en: At least, I will be your friend and comrade and adviser as much as I can and more than that I cannot do.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda, men sizning do'stingiz, tengdoshingiz va maslahatchingiz bo'lib, qo'limdan kelganicha va undan ko'ra ko'proq narsani qila olmayman.

en: How does that fall in with your philosophy, eh, Koko?
uz: Bu sizning falsafangiz bilan qanday bog'liq, Kok?

en: Well or ill, eh?” Of course I said that it fell in with it entirely, and, indeed, I really thought so.
uz: To'g'ri yoki yomon, shundaymi? Albatta, men u bilan to'liq bog'liqligini aytdim va, albatta, men ham shunday deb o'yladim.

en: That morning Papa had a particularly winning, bright, and happy expression on his face, and these new relations between us, as of equals and comrades, made me love him all the more.
uz: O'sha kuni ertalab dadamning yuzida g'alaba qozonadigan, yorqin va quvonchli taassurot bor edi va o'z tengdoshlari va hamkasblarimiz o'rtasidagi ushbu yangi munosabatlar meni uni yanada ko'proq sevishga undadi.

en: “Now, tell me,” he went on, “did you call upon all our kinsfolk and the Iwins?
uz: Endi, ayting, u davom etdi: "Siz barcha qarindoshlarimizni va Iwinlarni chaqirdingizmi?

en: Did you see the old man, and what did he say to you?
uz: Siz keksa odamni ko'rdingizmi va u sizga nima dedi?

en: And did you go to Prince Ivan’s?” We continued talking so long that, before we were fully dressed, the sun had left the window of the divannaia, and Jakoff (the same old man who of yore had twirled his fingers behind his back and always repeated his words) had entered the room and reported to Papa that the carriage was ready.
uz: Va siz Prens Ivonning oldiga borganmisiz? Biz suhbatni shunchalik davom ettirdikki, to'liq kiyim-kechak bo'lishimizdan oldin, quyosh divannaia oynasidan chiqib ketgan edi va Jakoff (o'tmishda barmoqlarini orqaga tikib, har doim so'zlarini takrorlagan kishi) xonaniga kirib, otamga vagon tayyorligini xabar bergan edi.

en: “Where are you going to?” I asked Papa.
uz: Qayerga ketyapsan? - deb so'radim otamdan.

en: “Oh, I had forgotten all about it!” he replied, with a cough and the usual hoisting of his shoulder.
uz: "Oh, men bu haqda unutib qo'ydim!" - deb javob berdi u, qo'shishi va odatdagidek yelkasini ko'tarishi bilan.

en: “I promised to go and call upon Epifanova to-day.
uz: Men bugun Epifanovaga tashrif buyurishga va'da berdim.

en: You remember Epifanova—‘la belle Flamande’— don’t you, who used to come and see your Mamma?
uz: Epifanovala belle Flamande, onangizni ko'rishga kelganini eslaysizmi?

en: They are nice people.” And with a self-conscious shrug of his shoulders (so it appeared to me) Papa left the room.
uz: Ular yaxshi odamlar. Otam omon qolmay (men uchun shunday ko'rindi) xonani tark etdi.

en: During our conversation, Lubotshka had more than once come to the door and asked “Can I come in?” but Papa had always shouted to her that she could not do so, since we were not dressed yet.
uz: Suhbat paytida Lubotshka bir necha marta eshikga kelib: "Men kirishim mumkinmi?" - deb so'ragan edi, lekin otam biz hali kiyim-kechak bo'lmaganimiz sababli, u buni qila olmaydi, deb unga har doim qichqirgan edi.

en: “What rubbish!” she replied.
uz: "Qanday axlat!" deb javob berdi u.

en: “Why, I have seen you in your dressing-gown.” “Never mind; you cannot see your brothers without their inexpressibles,” rejoined Papa.
uz: Bilasizmi, men sizni kiyim kiyganingizda ko'rdim.Boshimchalik qilmang; siz birodarlaringizni so'zsiz ko'ra olmaysiz, - dedi ota.

en: “If they each of them just go to the door, let that be enough for you.
uz: Agar ularning har biri eshikga borsa, bu sizga yetarli bo'lsin.

en: Even for them to SPEAK to you in such a neglige costume is unbecoming.” “How unbearable you are!” was Lubotshka’s parting retort.
uz: Hatto ular sizga bunday beparvo kostyumda gapirishlari uchun ham munosib emas.  Siz qanchalik chidamsiz! deb javob qaytardi Lubotshka.

en: “Well, at least hurry up and come down to the drawing-room, for Mimi wants to see them.” As soon as Papa had left the room, I hastened to array myself in my student’s uniform, and to repair to the drawing-room.
uz: Ha, hech bo'lmaganda tezroq turing-da, salonga tushing, chunki Mimi ularni ko'rishni xohlaydi. Ota xonadan chiqqanidan so'ng, o'zimni o'quvchi uniformimga kiyib, salonga tiklash uchun shoshildim.

en: Woloda, on the other hand, was in no hurry, but remained sitting on his bed and talking to Jakoff about the best places to find plover and snipe.
uz: Woloda esa shoshilmadi, balki o'z yotoqida o'tirib, Jakoff bilan plover va snipe topish uchun eng yaxshi joylar haqida suhbatlashdi.

en: As I have said, there was nothing in the world he so much feared as to be suspected of any affection for his father, brother, and sister; so that, to escape any expression of that feeling, he often fell into the other extreme, and affected a coldness which shocked people who did not comprehend its cause.
uz: Aytganimdek, dunyodagi hech narsa uning otasi, aka-uka va singlisiga bo'lgan muhabbatidan shubhalanishdan qo'rqmas edi; shuning uchun bu tuyg'ularning har qanday ifodasidan qochish uchun u tez-tez boshqa chetga tushib, sovuqlikni boshdan kechirgan va uning sababini tushunmagan odamlarni hayratda qoldirgan.

en: In the hall, I collided with Papa, who was hurrying towards the carriage with short, rapid steps.
uz: Zalda otam bilan to'qnashdim, u tez va qisqa qadamlar bilan aravachaga yaqinlashib borar edi.

en: He had a new and fashionable Moscow greatcoat on, and smelt of scent.
uz: U yangi va moddiy Moskvadagi ko'ylak kiyib, xushbo'y tutardi.

en: On seeing me, he gave a cheerful nod, as much as to say, “Do you remark my splendour?” and once again I was struck with the happy expression of face which I had noted earlier in the morning.
uz: Meni ko'rganida u quvonchli bir bosh ko'tardi va hatto: "Siz mening ulug'vorligimga e'tibor berdingizmi?" deb aytdi va yana bir bor ertalab ko'rganimdek, yuzning baxtli ifosi meni hayratda qoldirdi.

en: The drawing-room looked the same lofty, bright room as of Yore, with its brown English piano, and its large open windows looking on to the green trees and yellowish-red paths of the garden.
uz: O'tirish xonasi Yore bilan bir xil baland, yorug' xonaga o'xshaydi, uning rangli rangli ingliz klaviatori va katta ochiq oynalari bog'ning yashil daraxtlari va sariq-qizil yo'llariga qaraydi.

en: After kissing Mimi and Lubotshka, I was approaching Katenka for the same purpose when it suddenly struck me that it might be improper for me to salute her in that fashion.
uz: Mimi va Lubotshka bilan o'g'illarini o'g'ib olganimdan so'ng, Katenkaga xuddi shu maqsad bilan yaqinlashayotgan edim, lekin birdan unga shunday salom berish men uchun noto'g'ri bo'lishi mumkinligini tushundim.

en: Accordingly I halted, silent and blushing.
uz: Shuning uchun men to'xtatdim, sukut saqladim va qizg'inlashdim.

en: Katenka, for her part, was quite at her ease as she held out a white hand to me and congratulated me on my passing into the University.
uz: Katenka esa menga oq qo'l uzatganida va universitetga kirishimga tabriklaganida o'zidan juda xotirjam edi.

en: The same thing took place when Woloda entered the drawing-room and met Katenka.
uz: Woloda salonga kirib, Katenka bilan uchrashganda ham xuddi shunday bo'ldi.

en: Indeed, it was something of a problem how, after being brought up together and seeing one another daily, we ought now, after this first separation, to meet again.
uz: Darhaqiqat, birga o'sganimiz va har kuni bir-birimizni ko'rganimizdan keyin, birinchi bo'lib ajralganimizdan so'ng, qanday qilib yana uchrashishimiz kerakligi biroz muammo edi.

en: Katenka had grown better-looking than any of us, yet Woloda seemed not at all confused as, with a slight bow to her, he crossed over to Lubotshka, made a jesting remark to her, and then departed somewhere on some solitary expedition.
uz: Katenka har birimizdan ko'ra ko'proq chiroyli bo'lgan, ammo Woloda unga biroz yonboshlagan holda Lubotshka tomon o'tib, u bilan o'yin-kulgi so'zlashdi va keyin u yolg'iz sayohatga chiqdi.

en: RELATIONS BETWEEN THE GIRLS AND OURSELVES OF the girls Woloda took the strange view that, although he wished that they should have enough to eat, should sleep well, be well dressed, and avoid making such mistakes in French as would shame him before strangers, he would never admit that they could think or feel like human beings, still less that they could converse with him
uz: Qizlar va o'z jinslarimiz o'rtasidagi munosabatlar Woloda qizlarning o'ziga xos nuqtai nazarga ega edi: ular yetarlicha ovqatlanishini, yaxshi uxlashlarini, yaxshi kiyinishlarini va tanqislar oldida uni sharmanda qiladigan fransuz tilidagi xatolardan qochishlarini istasa-da, ular insonlar kabi o'ylashlari yoki his qilishlari mumkinligini hech qachon tan olmaydi.

en: sensibly about anything.
uz: har qanday narsa haqida aqlli fikrda bo'lish.

en: Whenever they addressed to him a serious question (a thing, by the way, which he always tried to avoid), such as asking his opinion on a novel or inquiring about his doings at the University, he invariably pulled a grimace, and either turned away without speaking or answered with some nonsensical French phrase —“Comme c’est tres jolie!” or the like.
uz: Har safar unga jiddiy savol berishganda (o'z navbatida, u har doim undan qochishga harakat qilardi), masalan, romanga nisbatan fikrini so'rash yoki universitetda qilgan ishlari haqida so'rashsa, u har doim makkalarini ko'tarib, so'zsiz yuz o'girib ketardi yoki "Comme cest tres jolie!" yoki shunga o'xshash biron bir behuda frantsuz so'zlari bilan javob berdi.

en: Or again, feigning to look serious and stolidly wise, he would say something absolutely meaningless and bearing no relation whatever to the question asked him, or else suddenly exclaim, with a look of pretended unconsciousness, the word bulku or poyechali or kapustu, [Respectively, “roll of butter,” “away,” and “cabbage.”] or something of the kind; and when, afterwards, I happened to repeat these words to him as having been told me by Lubotshka or Katenka, he would always remark: “Hm!
uz: Yoki yana jiddiy va qat'iy dono ko'rinishga ega bo'lib, u so'ragan savolga hech qanday aloqasi bo'lmagan, mutlaqo ahamiyatsiz gaplarni aytadi, yoki birdan o'ylamaslik ko'rinishi bilan bulku yoki poyechali yoki kapustu so'zlarini aytadi, [vay,vay va cabbage.] yoki shunga o'xshash so'zlarni aytadi va keyin bu so'zlarni Lubotshka yoki Katenka menga aytganidek takrorlaganimda, u har doim: Hm! deb ta'kidlaydi.

en: So you actually care about talking to them?
uz: Demak, siz ular bilan gaplashishni aslida xohlaysizmi?

en: I can see you are a duffer still”—and one needed to see and near him to appreciate the profound, immutable contempt which echoed in this remark.
uz: Ko'rib turibmanki, siz hali ham o'zingizni qo'pol ko'rasiz va bu so'zlarda o'zgacha bo'lgan chuqur, o'zgarmas kamsitishni qadrlash uchun uni ko'rishingiz va yaqinlashishingiz kerak edi.

en: He had been grown-up now two years, and was in love with every good- looking woman that he met; yet, despite the fact that he came in daily contact with Katenka (who during those two years had been wearing long dresses, and was growing prettier every day), the possibility of his falling in love with her never seemed to enter his head.
uz: U endi ikki yil katta bo'lib, uchratgan har bir go'zal ayolga muhabbatkor edi; lekin Katenka bilan har kuni muloqotda bo'lishiga qaramay (u ikki yil davomida uzun kiyim kiygan va har kuni go'zallashib borayotgan edi), uning unga muhabbat qilish imkoniyati uning ongiga hech qachon kirmagan.

en: Whether this proceeded from the fact that the prosaic recollections of childhood were still too fresh in his memory, or whether from the aversion which very young people feel for everything domestic, or whether from the common human weakness which, at a first encounter with anything fair and pretty, leads a man to say to himself, “Ah!
uz: Bu uning xotirasida bolalik haqidagi prozaik xotiralar hali ham juda yangi bo'lganidan yoki juda yoshlar uydagi har bir narsaga nisbatan hissiy nafratlanishidan yoki odatdagi inson zaifligidan kelib chiqqan bo'lsa-da, bu odat tusiga kirgan har qanday adolatli va chiroyli narsa bilan birinchi marta uchrashganda odamni o'ziga: Ah! deb aytishga undaydi.

en: I shall meet much more of the same kind during my life,” but at all events Woloda had never yet looked upon Katenka with a man’s eyes.
uz: Hayotim davomida xuddi shunday odamlarning ko'pini uchrataman, lekin hech bo'lmaganda Woloda Katenkani erkak ko'zlari bilan ko'rmagan.

en: All that summer Woloda appeared to find things very wearisome— a fact which arose out of that contempt for us all which, as I have said, he made no effort to conceal.
uz: O'sha yozda Voloda juda charchatadigan narsalarni topgan edi, bu esa, aytganimdek, u yashirmaslikka harakat qilmagan, barchamizga bo'lgan hurmatsizlikdan kelib chiqqan.

en: His expression of face seemed to be constantly saying, “Phew!
uz: Uning yuzidagi o'z ifodasini doimiy ravishda: "Phew!

en: how it bores me to have no one to speak to!” The first thing in the morning he would go out shooting, or sit reading a book in his room, and not dress until luncheon time.
uz: Kim bilan gaplashmasligim meni qanchalik charchatib qo'yadi! Ertalab ertalab u o'qishga chiqardi, yoki xonasida kitob o'qishga o'tirardi va kechki ovqat paytigacha kiyim kiymaydi.

en: Indeed, if Papa was not at home, he would take his book into that
uz: Darhaqiqat, agar otam uyda bo'lmaganida, u o'z kitobini o'sha kitobga olib kirardi.

en: meal, and go on reading it without addressing so much as a single word to any one of us, who felt, somehow, guilty in his presence.
uz: Ovqatni yeb, uni o'qishni davom ettiring, uning oldida o'zini aybdor his qilgan har birimizga bir so'z ham aytmaysiz.

en: In the evening, too, he would stretch himself on a settee in the drawing- room, and either go to sleep, propped on his elbow, or tell us farcical stories—sometimes stories so improper as to make Mimi grow angry and blush, and ourselves die with laughter.
uz: Kechqurun ham, u o'zini turar joyda o'tirgan joyga uzatib, yonboshiga tayanib uxlaydi yoki bizga farsiyalor hikoyalarni aytib beradi.Ba'zan Mimi g'azabga tushadi, qizg'inlashadi va biz o'zimizni kulgi bilan o'ldiramiz.

en: At other times he would not condescend to address a single serious word to any member of the family except Papa or (occasionally) myself.
uz: Boshqa paytlarda u oila a'zolaridan hech kimga jiddiy so'z aytishga rozi bo'lmas edi, faqat ota yoki (ba'zan) o'zimdan boshqa.

en: Involuntarily I offended against his view of girls, seeing that I was not so afraid of seeming affectionate as he, and, moreover, had not such a profound and confirmed contempt for young women.
uz: Men uning qizlarga bo'lgan nuqtai nazariga bevafolik bilan qarshi chiqdim, chunki men u kabi mehribon ko'rinishdan qo'rqmasligimni va, bundan tashqari, yosh ayollarga nisbatan bunday chuqur va tasdiqlangan hurmatsizlik ko'rsatmasligimni ko'rdim.

en: Yet several times that summer, when driven by lack of amusement to try and engage Lubotshka and Katenka in conversation, I always encountered in them such an absence of any capacity for logical thinking, and such an ignorance of the simplest, most ordinary matters (as, for instance, the nature of money, the subjects studied at universities, the effect of war, and so forth), as well as such indifference to my explanations of such matters, that these attempts of mine only ended in confirming my unfavourable opinion of feminine ability.
uz: Ammo o'sha yozda bir necha marta, Lubotshka va Katenka bilan suhbatlashish uchun o'yin-kulgi yo'qligi sababli, men ular orasida har doim mantiqiy fikrlash qobiliyatining yo'qligi va eng sodda, odatiy masalalarni (masalan, pulning tabiati, universitetlarda o'qiladigan fanlar, urushning ta'siri va hokazolar) bilmasligimni va bunday tushuntirishlarimga befarqligimni ko'rdim, shuning uchun bu harakatlarim faqat ayollik qobiliyatiga nisbatan noqulay fikrimni tasdiqlashga to'sqinlik qildi.

en: I remember one evening when Lubotshka kept repeating some unbearably tedious passage on the piano about a hundred times in succession, while Woloda, who was dozing on a settee in the drawing-room, kept addressing no one in particular as he muttered, “Lord!
uz: Bir kechki payt Lubotshka piano ustida bir necha yuz marotaba bir-biriga o'xshamaydigan, juda charchatiladigan o'qishni takrorlaganini eslayman, Woloda esa o'tirish xonasidagi o'rindiq ustida uxlab, hech kimga murojaat qilmaydi va u: "Lord!" deb qichqirib yurardi.

en: WHAT a Beethoven!” (he always pronounced the composer’s name with especial irony).
uz: BETHOVEN! (U har doim qo'shiqchining ismini o'zgacha ironika bilan aytgan).

en: That’s it!” and so on.
uz: Mana shu! va hokazo.

en: Meanwhile Katenka and I were sitting by the tea-table, and somehow she began to talk about her favourite subject—love.
uz: Bu vaqt ichida Katenka va men choy stolining yonida o'tirgan edik va u qandaydir tarzda sevimli mavzusi haqida gapira boshladi.

en: I was in the right frame of mind to philosophise, and began by loftily defining love as the wish to acquire in another what one does not possess in oneself.
uz: Men falsafa o'rganish uchun to'g'ri nuqtai nazarda edim va sevgini o'zimda bo'lmagan narsani boshqa odamda orttirish istagi sifatida yuqori darajada belgilab, boshladim.

en: To this Katenka retorted that, on the contrary, love is not love at all if a girl desires to marry a man for his money alone, but that, in her opinion, riches were a vain thing, and true love only the affection which can stand the test of separation (this I took to be a hint concerning her love for Dubkoff).
uz: Katenka bunga javob berib, agar qiz faqat pul evaziga erkak bilan turmush qurmoqchi bo'lsa, sevgi umuman sevgi emas, balki uning fikriga ko'ra, boylik behuda narsa, haqiqiy sevgi esa faqat ajralish sinovidan o'tishi mumkin bo'lgan muhabbat ekanligini aytdi (Men buni Dubkoffga bo'lgan sevgisi haqida ma'lumot sifatida qabul qildim).

en: At this point Woloda, who must have been listening all the time, raised himself on his elbow, and cried out some rubbish or another; and I felt that he was right.
uz: Shu payt Woloda, u doim tinglagan bo'lishi mumkin, o'zini qo'lqoshida ko'tarib, bir yoki boshqa axlatni baqirib yubordi va men uning to'g'ri gapirganini his qildim.

en: Apart from the general faculties (more or less developed in different persons) of intellect, sensibility, and artistic feeling, there also exists (more or less developed in different circles of society, and especially in families) a private or individual faculty which I may call APPREHENSION.
uz: Intellekti, hissiyot va san'at hissiyotlarining umumiy (farqli shaxslarda ko'proq yoki kamroq rivojlangan) qobiliyatlaridan tashqari, xususiy yoki yakka tartibdagi qobiliyat mavjud (farqli ijtimoiy doiralarda, ayniqsa oilalarda rivojlangan) va men uni APPREHENSION deb atayman.

en: The essence of this faculty lies in sympathetic appreciation of proportion, and in identical understanding of things.
uz: Ushbu qobiliyatning mohiyati nisbatni hamdardlik bilan qadrlashda va narsalarni bir xil tushunishda joylashgan.

en: Two individuals who possess this faculty and belong to the same social circle or the same family apprehend an expression of feeling precisely to the same point, namely, the point beyond which such expression becomes mere phrasing.
uz: Ushbu qobiliyatga ega bo'lgan va bir xil ijtimoiy doiraga yoki bir xil oilaga tegishli bo'lgan ikki kishi his-tuyg'ularni ifoda etishni aynan bir nuqtaga yetkazishadi, ya'ni bunday ifoda shunchaki so'zlash bo'lgan nuqtaga o'tadi.

en: Thus they apprehend precisely where commendation ends and irony begins, where attraction ends and pretence begins, in a manner which would be impossible for persons possessed of a different order of apprehension.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular maqtovning tugash va ironiklikning boshlanishi, jozibadorlik tugash va o'yin-kulgi boshlanishining to'g'ri joyini aniq tushunishadi, bu esa boshqa rangdagi maqtovga ega bo'lganlar uchun imkonsiz bo'ladi.

en: Persons possessed of identical apprehension view objects in an identically ludicrous, beautiful, or repellent light; and in order to facilitate such identical apprehension between members of the same social circle or family, they usually establish a language, turns of speech, or terms to define such shades of apprehension as exist for them alone.
uz: Xuddi shunday qo'rquvga ega bo'lgan odamlar narsalarni xuddi shu darajada g'alati, chiroyli yoki nojo'ya yorug'likda ko'rishadi; shuningdek, bir xil ijtimoiy doira yoki oila a'zolari o'rtasida xuddi shunday qo'rquvni osonlashtirish uchun ular odatda o'zlari uchun mavjud bo'lgan qo'rquv nuqtalarini belgilash uchun til, nutqning o'zgarishi yoki atamalarini o'rnatadilar.

en: In our particular family such apprehension was common to Papa, Woloda, and myself, and was developed to the highest pitch, Dubkoff also approximated to our coterie in apprehension, but Dimitri, though infinitely more intellectual than Dubkoff, was grosser in this respect.
uz: Bizning oilaimizda bunday qo'rquv Papa, Woloda va men uchun odatiy hol edi va eng yuqori darajaga yetib borardi, Dubkoff ham qo'rquvda bizning qo'rquvimizga yaqinlashdi, ammo Dimitri Dubkoffdan ko'ra aqlli bo'lsa-da, bu borada o'ta zo'r edi.

en: With no one, however, did I bring this faculty to such a point as with Woloda, who had grown up with me under identical conditions.
uz: Biroq, hech kim bilan bu fakultetni men bilan bir xil sharoitlarda o'sgan Woloda bilan o'sib-ulg'aygan darajada yetkazmaganman.

en: Papa stood a long way from us, and much that was to us as clear as “two and two make four” was to him incomprehensible.
uz: Otam bizdan uzoqda turardi va biz uchun ikki va ikki to'rtta kabi aniq bo'lgan ko'p narsalar unga tushunarli emas edi.

en: For instance, I and Woloda managed to establish between ourselves the following terms, with meanings to correspond.
uz: Misol uchun, men va Voloda o'zimiz o'rtasida quyidagi ma'nolarni belgilashga muvaffaq bo'ldik.

en: Izium [Raisins.] meant a desire to boast of one’s money; shishka [Bump or swelling.] (on pronouncing which one had to join one’s fingers together, and to put a particular emphasis upon the two sh’s in the word) meant anything fresh, healthy, and comely, but not elegant; a substantive used in the plural meant an undue partiality for the object which it denoted; and so forth, and so forth.
uz: Izium [Raisins.] - o'z pulidan maqtanish istagini anglatadi; shishka [Bump yoki puflash] (birining barmoqlarini bir-biriga qo'shish kerakligini aytish va so'zdagi ikkita shsga alohida e'tibor qaratish) - yangi, sog'lom va go'zal, ammo chiroyli bo'lmagan narsani anglatadi; ko'plikda ishlatiladigan ma'noli ma'no o'z ko'rsatgan narsasiga nisbatan ortiqcha yuzxotirchilikni anglatadi; va shu kabilar.

en: At the same time, the meaning depended considerably upon the expression of the face and the context of the conversation; so that, no matter what new expression one of us might invent to define a shade of feeling the other could
uz: Shu bilan birga, ma'no yuzning ifodasidan va suhbatning kontekstidan ancha bog'liq edi; shuning uchun, birimizning his-tuyg'u soyasini belgilash uchun qaysi yangi ifodani ixtiro qilsak ham, boshqa birimizning o'zi ham uni topishi mumkin.

en: immediately understand it by a hint alone.
uz: Uni birgina nuqta orqali darhol tushuning.

en: The girls did not share this faculty of apprehension, and herein lay the chief cause of our moral estrangement, and of the contempt which we felt for them.
uz: Qizlar bu qo'rquv qobiliyatini baham ko'rmagan va bu bizning axloqiy ajralishimizning asosiy sababi va ularga nisbatan hissiy kamsitishimizning asosiy sababi edi.

en: It may be that they too had their “apprehension,” but it so little ran with ours that, where we already perceived the “phrasing,” they still saw only the feeling—our irony was for them truth, and so on.
uz: Ehtimol, ular ham o'zlarining tushunchalariga ega edilar, lekin bu bizning tushunchamizga shunchalik oz qo'shildiki, biz o'zimiz o'zimiz o'zimizning tushunchamizni tushunayotganimizda, ular hali ham faqat bizning ironikamiz ularga haqiqat ekanini his qilishganini ko'rishgan.

en: At that time I had not yet learnt to understand that they were in no way to blame for this, and that absence of such apprehension in no way prevented them from being good and clever girls.
uz: O'shanda men hali ular uchun hech qanday ayb yo'qligini va bunday qo'rquvning yo'qligi ularni yaxshi va aqlli qizlar bo'lishga hech qanday xalaqit bermasligini tushunishga o'rganmagan edim.

en: Accordingly I looked down upon them.
uz: Shuning uchun men ularni pastga ko'rdim.

en: Moreover, having once lit upon my precious idea of “frankness,” and being bent upon applying it to the full in myself, I thought the quiet, confiding nature of Lubotshka guilty of secretiveness and dissimulation simply because she saw no necessity for digging up and examining all her thoughts and instincts.
uz: Bundan tashqari, bir paytlar frankness haqidagi qimmatbaho g'oyamga e'tibor qaratganimdan va uni o'zimda to'liq qo'llashga qat'iy qaror qilganimdan so'ng, Lubotshkaning xotirjam, ishonchli tabiati sirli va yashirin bo'lganini tan oldim, chunki u o'z fikrlari va istisnolarini o'rganish uchun hech qanday zarurat ko'rmadi.

en: For instance, the fact that she always signed the sign of the cross over Papa before going to bed, that she and Katenka invariably wept in church when attending requiem masses for Mamma, and that Katenka sighed and rolled her eyes about when playing the piano— all these things seemed to me sheer make-believe, and I asked myself: “At what period did they learn to pretend like grown-up people, and how can they bring themselves to do it?” XXX.
uz: Misol uchun, u doim dadamning ustiga xoch belgisini yotishdan oldin imzolaganligi, u va Katenka onasi uchun requiem massasida ishtirok etishganda cherkovda doim yig'laganligi va Katenka piyano o'ynash paytida nafas olib, ko'zlarini o'girganligi bularning barchasi menga shunchaki tasavvurga o'xshaydi va men o'zimdan so'radim: Qanday davrda ular kattalar kabi o'zlarini ko'rsatishni o'rganishdi va buni qanday qilishlari mumkin? XXX.

en: HOW I EMPLOYED MY TIME Nevertheless, the fact that that summer I developed a passion for music caused me to become better friends with the ladies of our household than I had been for years.
uz: Shunga qaramay, o'sha yozda musiqaga bo'lgan ishtiyoqimni rivojlantirganim tufayli uydagi xonimlar bilan yillar davomida bo'lganimdan ko'ra yaxshiroq do'st bo'ldim.

en: In the spring, a young fellow came to see us, armed with a letter of introduction, who, as soon as ever he entered the drawing-room, fixed his eyes upon the piano, and kept gradually edging his chair closer to it as he talked to Mimi
uz: Bahorda bizga tanishish maktubi bilan qurollangan bir yigit tashrif buyurdi, u esa o'tirishga kirgandan so'ng o'z ko'zlarini klaviaturaga qaratdi va Mimi bilan suhbatlashayotib, o'rinni unga yaqinlashtirdi.

en: After discoursing awhile of the weather and the amenities of country life, he skilfully directed the conversation to piano-tuners, music, and pianos generally, and ended by saying that he himself played—and in truth he did sit down and perform three waltzes, with Mimi, Lubotshka, and Katenka grouped about the instrument, and watching him as he did so.
uz: Bir muncha vaqt ob-havo va qishloq hayoti qulayliklari haqida gapirganidan so'ng, u suhbatni mahoratli ravishda klaviatur-tunerlar, musiqa va umumiy ravishda klaviaturlarga yo'naltirdi va o'zi o'zi o'ynashini aytib yakunladi va haqiqatdan ham o'tirib, uchta valsni ijro etdi, Mimi, Lubotshka va Katenka asbob haqida guruhlarga to'plandilar va uni o'ynashda kuzatib turdilar.

en: He never came to see us again, but his playing, and his attitude when at the piano, and the way in which he kept shaking his long hair, and, most of all, the manner in which he was able to execute octaves with his left hand as he first of all played them rapidly with his thumb and little finger, and then slowly closed those members, and then played the octaves afresh, made a great impression upon me.
uz: U bizni hech qachon ko'rishga kelmadi, lekin o'z o'yin-kulgi, klaviaturada o'ynash va o'zining uzun sochlarini silkitish usuli, eng asosiysi esa, o'z chap qo'li bilan oktavlarni ijro etish usuli, chunki u avval bosh barmog'i va kichkina barmog'i bilan tezda o'ynash, so'ngra bu a'zolarni asta-sekin yopish, so'ngra oktavlarni yangidan o'ynash bilan menga katta taassurot qoldirdi.

en: This graceful gesture of his, together with his easy pose and his shaking of hair and successful winning of the ladies’ applause by his talent, ended by firing me to take up the piano.
uz: Uning bu mehribon harakatlari, uning oson o'rnagi, sochlarini silkitishi va iste'dodini qo'llab-quvvatlagan ayollarning qo'llab-quvvatlanishini muvaffaqiyatli qo'lga kiritishi bilan birga meni pianoga qo'l urishga majbur qildi.

en: Convinced that I possessed both talent and a passion for music, I set myself to learn, and, in doing so, acted just as millions of the male—still more, of the female—sex have done who try to teach themselves without a skilled instructor, without any real turn for the art, or without the smallest understanding either of what the art can give or of what ought to be done to obtain that gift.
uz: O'zimda ham iqtidor, ham musiqaga bo'lgan ishtiyoq borligiga ishonganim uchun o'zimni o'rganishga bag'ishladim va shu yo'sin millionlab erkaklar, ayollarning o'zlarini malakali o'qituvchisiz, san'at uchun hech qanday haqiqiy o'zgarishsiz o'rgatishga harakat qilayotganlarini ko'rdim va san'at nima berishi mumkinligi yoki bu sovg'ani olish uchun nima qilish kerakligini anglamasdan o'zimni o'rganishga harakat qildim.

en: For me music (or rather, piano-playing) was simply a means of winning the ladies’ good graces through their sensibility.
uz: Men uchun musiqa (yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri, piano o'ynash) ayollarning hissiyligi orqali yaxshiliklarini qozonishning bir usuli edi.

en: With the help of Katenka I first learnt the notes (incidentally breaking several of them with my clumsy fingers), and then—that is to say, after two months of hard work, supplemented by ceaseless twiddling of my rebellious fingers on my knees after luncheon, and on the pillow when in bed—went on to “pieces,” which I played (so Katenka assured me) with “soul” (“avec ame”), but altogether regardless of time.
uz: Katenka yordamida men birinchi navbatda notalarni o'rgandim (o'zimning o'ylamagan barmoqlarim bilan bir nechta notalarni buzganman), so'ngra, ya'ni ikki oylik mehnatdan so'ng, kechki ovqatdan so'ng tiz cho'kgan bo'lsam ham, o'zimning isyonkor barmoqlarimning to'xtamas aylanishi bilan to'ldim va yotoqdagi yastog'imda piecesga o'tdim, men uni soul (avec ame) bilan o'ynardim, ammo vaqtdan qat'i nazar.

en: My range of pieces was the usual one—waltzes, galops, “romances,” “arrangements,” etcetera; all of them of the class of delightful compositions of which any one with a little healthy taste could point out a selection among the better class works contained in any volume of music and say, “These are what you ought NOT to play, seeing that anything worse, less tasteful, and more silly has never yet been included in any collection of music,”—but which (probably for that very reason) are to be found on the piano of every
uz: Mening asarlarim odatdagi onewaltzes, galops, romanslar,   arrangements va boshqalar edi; ularning barchasi ajoyib kompozitsiyalar sinfidan iborat edi, ularning har birida sog'lom ta'mga ega bo'lgan har bir kishi har qanday musiqa hajmi bo'lgan eng yaxshi klass asarlaridan birini ko'rsatishi va aytishi mumkin edi: Bu siz o'ynashingiz kerak bo'lmagan narsalar, chunki har qanday musiqa to'plamasiga hech qachon yomonroq, kamroq ta'sirli va ahmoqona narsa kiritilmagan, lekin (muhimki, shu sababdan) har bir musiqa to'plamasida mavjud bo'lganlar.

en: True, we also possessed an unfortunate volume which contained Beethoven’s “Sonate Pathetique” and the C minor Sonata (a volume lamed for life by the ladies—more especially by Lubotshka, who used to discourse music from it in memory of Mamma), as well as certain other good pieces which her teacher in Moscow had given her; but among that collection there were likewise compositions of the teacher’s own, in the shape of clumsy marches and galops—and these too Lubotshka used to play!
uz: To'g'ri, bizda Beethoven'ning "Sonate Pathetique" va "C minor Sonata" (xotin-qizlar tomonidan, ayniqsa, onani xotirlash uchun musiqa bilan ta'lim beradigan Lubotshka) hamda Moskvadagi o'qituvchisi unga bergan boshqa yaxshi asarlar mavjud bo'lgan baxtsiz tomoni ham bor edi; ammo ushbu to'plam orasida o'qituvchining o'z qo'shiqlari ham bor edi, bu ham Lubotshka o'ynashga moyil marsh va galoplar shaklida!

en: Katenka and I cared nothing for serious works, but preferred, above all things, “Le Fou” and “The Nightingale”—the latter of which Katenka would play until her fingers almost became invisible, and which I too was beginning to execute with much vigour and some continuity.
uz: Katenka va men jiddiy ishlarga ahamiyat bermasdik, lekin eng afzalligi - Le Fou va The Nightingale bo'lgan o'yinlarni ko'rdik.

en: I had adopted the gestures of the young man of whom I have spoken, and frequently regretted that there were no strangers present to see me play.
uz: Men o'sha yigitning harakatlarini qabul qildim va ko'pincha o'ynashimni ko'rgan begonalar yo'qligidan afsuslanardim.

en: Soon, however, I began to realise that Liszt and Kalkbrenner were beyond me, and that I should never overtake Katenka.
uz: Biroq, tez orada men Liszt va Kalkbrenner mendan ustun ekanini va Katenkani hech qachon orqaga surib ketmasligimni anglay boshladim.

en: Accordingly, imagining that classical music was easier (as well as, partly, for the sake of originality), I suddenly came to the conclusion that I loved abstruse German music.
uz: Shu bois, klassik musiqa osonroq deb tasavvur qilganimda (va ba'zilari esa asl izlanishlar uchun), to'satdan g'alati nemis musiqasini yaxshi ko'raman degan xulosaga keldim.

en: I began to go into raptures whenever Lubotshka played the “Sonate Pathetique,” and although (if the truth be told) that work had for years driven me to the verge of distraction, I set myself to play Beethoven, and to talk of him as “Beethoven.” Yet through all this chopping and changing and pretence (as I now conceive) there may have run in me a certain vein of talent, since music sometimes affected me even to tears, and things which particularly pleased me I could strum on the piano afterwards (in a certain fashion) without the score; so that, had any one taught me at that period to look upon music as an end, a grace, in itself, and not merely as a means for pleasing womenfolk with the velocity and pseudo-sentiment of one’s playing, I might possibly have become a passable musician.
uz: Lubotshka "Sonate Pathetique"ni o'ynaganida, men o'zimni quvontirishga tushardim. Garchi (chindan ham) bu ish meni yillar davomida chalg'itish chegarasiga yetkazgan bo'lsa-da, men Beethovenni o'ynashga va uni "Beethoven" deb aytishga qaror qildim.Shunga qaramay, bu o'zgarishlar va o'zgarishlar va o'yinlar (haqiqatan ham, men hozir tasavvur qilganimdek) ichida bir xil iste'dod bor edi, chunki musiqa ba'zan menga hatto ko'z yoshlarcha ta'sir qilardi va menga ayniqsa yoqqan narsalar keyinchalik (ba'zicha tarzda) notalarsiz piyano ustida o'ynashim mumkin edi; shuning uchun, agar kimdir o'sha davrda menga musiqani o'z-o'zidan maqsad, ne'mat va nafaqat ayollarni tezlik va o'ziga xos hissiyotlar bilan quvontirish vositasi sifatida ko'rsatgan bo'lsa, ehtimol men o'zimni o'ynash uchun o'yinchi bo'lgan musiqadam bo'laman.

en: The reading of French novels (of which Woloda had brought a large store with him from Moscow) was another of my amusements that summer.
uz: O'sha yozda fransuz romanlarini o'qish (Woloda Moskvadan katta do'konni o'ziga olib kelgan) mening o'yinlarimdan biri edi.

en: At that period Monte Cristo and Taine’s works had just appeared, while I also revelled in stories by Sue, Dumas, and Paul de Kock.
uz: O'sha davrda Monte Cristo va Tainening asarlari hozircha paydo bo'lgan edi, men esa Sue, Dumas va Paul de Kockning hikoyalarida zavqlanardim.

en: Even their most unnatural personages and events were for me as real as actuality, and not only was I incapable of suspecting
uz: Hatto ularning eng noyob shaxslari va hodisalari ham men uchun haqiqatdek haqiqiy edi va nafaqat shubhalanishga qodir edim, balki shubhalanishga qodir edim.

en: an author of lying, but, in my eyes, there existed no author at all.
uz: Yolg'onlarning muallifidir, lekin mening fikrimcha, hech qanday muallif yo'q edi.

en: That is to say, the various personages and events of a book paraded themselves before me on the printed page as personages and events that were alive and real; and although I had never in my life met such characters as I there read about, I never for a second doubted that I should one day do so.
uz: Ya'ni, kitobning turli xarakterlari va hodisalari chop etilgan sahifada menga jonli va haqiqiy bo'lgan xarakterlar va hodisalar sifatida ko'rindi; hayotimda u erda o'qiganim kabi xarakterlar bilan hech qachon uchrashmagan bo'lsam-da, bir soniya ham shubhalanmaganmanki, bir kun buni qilishim kerak.

en: I discovered in myself all the passions described in every novel, as well as a likeness to all the characters—heroes and villains impartially—who figured therein, just as a suspicious man finds in himself the signs of every possible disease when reading a book on medicine.
uz: Men o'zimda har bir romanda tasvirlangan barcha ishtiyoqlarni, shuningdek, ularda o'rin olgan barcha belgilarga o'xshashlikni, shubhalanuvchi odam tibbiyot bo'yicha kitobni o'qiganida o'z ichidan har qanday kasallikning belgilarini topganidek, o'zimda ham shubhalanadigan odamni topdim.

en: I took pleasure both in the cunning designs, the glowing sentiments, the tumultuous events, and the character-drawing of these works.
uz: Bu asarlarning hiyla-nayrangli dizaynlari, yorqin his-tuyg'ular, g'alati hodisalar va xarakterli chizishlaridan zavq oldim.

en: A good man was of the goodness, a bad man of the badness, possible only to the imagination of early youth.
uz: Yaxshi odam yaxshilikdan, yomon odam yomonlikdan iborat edi, bu faqat yoshlik tasavvurining o'zi uchun mumkin edi.

en: Likewise I found great pleasure in the fact that it was all written in French, and that I could lay to heart the fine words which the fine heroes spoke, and recall them for use some day when engaged in some noble deed.
uz: Shuningdek, bularning barchasi frantsuz tilida yozilganligi va go'zal qahramonlarning gapirgan go'zal so'zlarini yodga olib, bir kun buyuk ishda ishtirok etish uchun ularni eslab qolish menga katta mamnuniyat ato etdi.

en: What quantities of French phrases I culled from those books for Kolpikoff’s benefit if I should ever meet him again, as well as for HERS, when at length I should find her and reveal to her my love!
uz: Men o'sha kitoblardan qandaydir fransuzcha iboralarni o'qib olsam, u bilan yana uchrashsam, Kolpikoff uchun foyda keltiradi va oxir-oqibat uni topib, sevgimni unga bildiraman!

en: For them both I prepared speeches which should overcome them as soon as spoken!
uz: Ikkalasi uchun ham nutqlarni tayyorladim, ular nutq so'zlanganda ularni yengish kerak!

en: Upon novels, too, I founded new ideals of the moral qualities which I wished to attain.
uz: Shuningdek, romanlar asosida ham o'zim erishmoqchi bo'lgan axloqiy fazilatlarning yangi ideallariga asos soldim.

en: First of all, I wished to be NOBLE in all my deeds and conduct (I use the French word noble instead of the Russian word blagorodni for the reason that the former has a different meaning to the latter—as the Germans well understood when they adopted noble as nobel and differentiated it from ehrlich); next, to be strenuous; and lastly, to be what I was already inclined to be, namely, comme il faut.
uz: Avvalo, men barcha harakatlarim va xulq-atvorim bilan Aʼlo boʻlishni xohladim (Rusiyaning blagorodni soʻzi oʻrniga frantsuzcha "aʼlo" soʻzini qoʻllayman, chunki avvalo aʼlo "aʼlo" soʻzini qabul qilib, uni ehrlichdan ajratib qoʻyganida nemislar yaxshi tushunishganidek, aʼlo "aʼlo" degan maʼnoga ega boʻlgan; keyin esa zoʻr boʻlish; va nihoyat, men allaqachon boʻlishga moyil boʻlgan boʻlish, yaʼni, comme il faut.

en: I even tried to approximate my appearance and bearing to that of the heroes who possessed these qualities.
uz: Hatto o'z tashqi ko'rinishim va munosabatimni shu fazilatlarga ega bo'lgan qahramonlarningkiga yaqinlashtirishga harakat qildim.

en: In particular I remember how in one of the hundred or so novels which I read that summer there was a very strenuous hero with heavy eyebrows, and that I so greatly wished to resemble him (I felt that I did so already from a moral point of view) that one day, when looking at my eyebrows in the glass, I conceived the idea of clipping them, in order to make them grow bushier.
uz: Ayniqsa, o'sha yozda o'qigan yuzlab romanlardan birida juda og'ir ko'z burchakli juda mehnatsevar qahramon borligini eslayman va men unga o'xshashni shunchalik istaganimni eslayman (men o'zimni axloqiy nuqtai nazardan shunday his qilganimni his qildim)ki, bir kuni o'z burchaklarimga shishaga qaraganimda, ularni kesib tashlash g'oyasi paydo bo'ldi.

en: Unfortunately, after I had started to do so, I happened to clip one spot rather shorter than the rest, and
uz: Afsuski, buni qila boshlaganimdan so'ng, men bir nuqtani qolgan nuqtalarga qaraganda qisqartirgan bo'ldim.

en: so had to level down the rest to it-with the result that, to my horror, I beheld myself eyebrow-less, and anything but presentable.
uz: Shunday qilib, qolgan qismini o'zimga o'xshatishim kerak edi - natijada men o'zimni qo'rqinchli his etib, ko'z burchaksiz va hech narsa ko'rinmas holda ko'rdim.

en: However, I comforted myself with the reflection that my eyebrows would soon sprout again as bushy as my hero’s, and was only perplexed to think how I could explain the circumstance to the household when they next perceived my eyebrow-less condition.
uz: Biroq, o'zimni ko'z o'ngimda ko'kraklarim qahramonlarim kabi o'simlik bo'lib, tez orada yana o'sib chiqishi haqidagi fikr bilan tasalli berardim va keyingi safar ular mening ko'kraksiz holatimni ko'rganida, uydagilarga vaziyatni qanday tushuntirishim mumkinligini o'ylashda g'alati bo'ldim.

en: Accordingly I borrowed some gunpowder from Woloda, rubbed it on my temples, and set it alight.
uz: Shuning uchun men Wolodan biroz qorong'ulikni qarz oldim, uni o'zimning ma'badlarimga surdim va uni yonib qo'ydim.

en: The powder did not fire properly, but I succeeded in singeing myself sufficiently to avert all suspicion of my pranks.
uz: Toʻqima toʻgʻri ishlamagan, lekin oʻzimni oʻzimning oʻyinlarimdan hech qanday shubha yoʻqotib qoʻyishim uchun yetarlicha oʻzimni qoʻlga kiritdim.

en: And, indeed, afterwards, when I had forgotten all about my hero, my eyebrows grew again, and much thicker than they had been before.
uz: Va, albatta, keyinchalik, men o'z qahramonimni unutib qo'yganimda, ko'z burchaklarim yana o'sdi va avvalgidek katta bo'ldi.

en: “COMME IL FAUT” SEVERAL times in the course of this narrative I have hinted at an idea corresponding to the above French heading, and now feel it incumbent upon me to devote a whole chapter to that idea, which was one of the most ruinous, lying notions which ever became engrafted upon my life by my upbringing and social milieu.
uz: COMME IL FAUT Ushbu hikoya davomida bir necha marta yuqorida keltirilgan frantsuz sarlavhasiga mos keladigan g'oyaga ishora qildim va endi o'zimni butun bobni ushbu g'oyaga bag'ishlash vazifasini his qilaman, bu mening tarbiyam va ijtimoiy muhitim tomonidan hayotimga o'rnatilgan eng zararli va yolg'on gaplardan biri edi.

en: The human race may be divided into several categories—rich and poor, good and bad, military and civilian, clever and stupid, and so forth, and so forth.
uz: Insoniyat bir necha toifalarga bo'linishi mumkin: boy va kambag'al, yaxshi va yomon, harbiy va fuqaro, aqlli va ahmoq, va shunga o'xshab.

en: Yet each man has his own favourite, fundamental system of division which he unconsciously uses to class each new person with whom he meets.
uz: Ammo har bir insonning o'zining sevimli, asosiy bo'linish tizimi bor, u bilmasdan uchratgan har bir yangi odamni sinflash uchun foydalanadi.

en: At the time of which I am speaking, my own favourite, fundamental system of division in this respect was into people “comme il faut” and people “comme il ne faut pas”—the latter subdivided, again, into people merely not “comme il faut” and the lower orders.
uz: Men gapirgan paytda, bu borada mening sevimli, asosiy bo'linish tizimim odamlarga va odamlarga bo'lindi, ular yana faqatgina odamlarga bo'linmadilar va past darajalarga bo'lindi.

en: People “comme il faut” I respected, and looked upon as worthy to consort with me as my equals; the second of the above categories I pretended merely to despise, but in reality hated,
uz: Odamlarni hurmat qilardim va ular men bilan tengdosh bo'lishga loyiq deb bilardim; yuqorida keltirilgan toifalardan ikkinchisini men shunchaki hurmat qilmasdim, lekin aslida nafratlanardim, deb o'yladim.

en: and nourished towards them a kind of feeling of offended personality; while the third category had no existence at all, so far as I was concerned, since my contempt for them was too complete.
uz: Men esa ularga nisbatan o'ziga xos tanqid tuyg'usini uyg'otdim; uchinchi toifa esa men uchun umuman mavjud emas edi, chunki men ularni kamsitgan edim.

en: This “comme il faut”-ness of mine lay, first and foremost, in proficiency in French, especially conversational French.
uz: Bu mening birinchi navbatda frantsuz tilini, ayniqsa suhbatdagi frantsuz tilini yaxshi bilishimga bog'liq.

en: A person who spoke that language badly at once aroused in me a feeling of dislike.
uz: O'sha tilni yomon gapirgan kishi darhol menda nafrat tuyg'usini uyg'otdi.

en: “Why do you try to talk as we do when you haven’t a notion how to do it?” I would seem to ask him with my most venomous and quizzing smile.
uz: Nima uchun biz kabi gapirishga harakat qilyapsiz, ammo buni qanday qilish kerakligi haqida hech qanday fikringiz yo'q? Men unga o'zimning eng zaharli va savol berishchan tabassumim bilan so'rab o'tirardim.

en: The second condition of “comme il faut”-ness was long nails that were well kept and clean; the third, ability to bow, dance, and converse; the fourth—and a very important one— indifference to everything, and a constant air of refined, supercilious ennui.
uz: comme il faut-nessning ikkinchi sharti - yaxshi saqlangan va toza bo'lgan uzun to'g'rilar; uchinchi, egilish, raqs qilish va suhbatlashish qobiliyati; to'rtinchi va juda muhim sharti - hamma narsaga befarqlik va doimiy ravishda sof, ulkan g'alati havas.

en: Moreover, there were certain general signs which, I considered, enabled me to tell, without actually speaking to a man, the class to which he belonged.
uz: Bundan tashqari, ba'zi umumiy belgilar bor edi, ular men odam bilan gaplashmasdan, uning qaysi sinfga tegishliligini aniqlashga imkon beradi deb o'yladim.

en: Chief among these signs (the others being the fittings of his rooms, his gloves, his handwriting, his turn- out, and so forth) were his feet.
uz: Ushbu belgilarning asosiy qismi (boshqalari uning xonalari, qo'lqoplari, qo'li yozuvi, o'zgaruvchisi va hokazolar) uning oyoqlari edi.

en: The relation of boots to trousers was sufficient to determine, in my eyes, the social status of a man.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, erkakning ijtimoiy maqomini aniqlash uchun poyabzal va paltaroshkalarning munosabati etarli edi.

en: Heelless boots with angular toes, wedded to narrow, unstrapped trouser-ends—these denoted the vulgarian.
uz: Bular chiroyli bo'lgan, chiroyli bo'g'imlar bilan chiroyli bo'g'imsiz, chiroyli, chiroyli, chiroyli, chiroyli bo'g'imlar bilan bog'liq edi.

en: Boots with narrow, round toes and heels, accompanied either by tight trousers strapped under the instep and fitting close to the leg or by wide trousers similarly strapped, but projecting in a peak over the toe—these meant the man of mauvais genre; and so on, and so on.
uz: Eng chiroyli, to'g'ri barmoq va to'g'ri cho'qqisi bo'lgan poyabzallar, ularning yonida oyoqqa yaqin bo'lgan, orqaga yaqin bo'lgan, orqaga yaqin bo'lgan, orqaga yaqin bo'lgan, orqaga o'xshaydigan, ammo to'g'ri bo'lgan, keng bo'laklar bor edi, lekin to'g'ri bo'lakdan yuqori bo'lgan, bu yomon jinsdagi odamni anglatadi; va shu kabi.

en: It was a curious thing that I who lacked all ability to become “comme il faut,” should have assimilated the idea so completely as I did.
uz: O'zimga kerakli bo'lish qobiliyati yo'q bo'lgan men, bu g'oyani o'zim kabi to'liq qabul qilishim kerak edi.

en: Possibly it was the fact that it had cost me such enormous labour to acquire that brought about its strenuous development in my mind.
uz: Ehtimol, uni olish uchun menga shuncha mehnat kerak bo'lganligi uning ongimda g'ayratli rivojlanishiga sabab bo'lgan.

en: I hardly like to think how much of the best and most valuable time of my first sixteen years of existence I wasted upon its acquisition.
uz: Birinchi o'n olti yillik hayotimning eng yaxshi va eng qimmatli vaqtining qanchaini uni o'zlashtirishga sarflaganimni o'ylashim qiyin.

en: Yet every one whom I imitated—Woloda, Dubkoff, and the majority of my acquaintances—seemed to acquire it easily.
uz: Ammo men o'qib olgan har bir kishi - Woloda, Dubkoff va ko'pchilik tanishlarim uni osonlikcha o'rganishardi.

en: I watched them with envy, and silently toiled to become proficient in French, to bow gracefully and without looking at the person whom I was saluting, to gain dexterity in small-talk and dancing, to cultivate indifference and ennui, and to keep my fingernails well trimmed (though I frequently cut my finger-ends with the scissors in so doing).
uz: Men ularni hasad bilan kuzatib turardim va fransuz tilida mahoratli bo'lish uchun, salom berayotgan odamga nazar solmay, xushmuomalalik bilan egib turish uchun, kichik suhbatlar va raqslarda mahoratni o'rganish uchun, befarqlik va g'alatilikni o'stirish uchun va barmoqlarimni yaxshi o'rnatish uchun (agarda men tez-tez o'zimning barmoq-barmoqlarimni shoshiq bilan kesib qo'ygan bo'lsam-da) sukut ishladim.

en: And all the time I felt that so much remained to be done if I was ever to attain my end!
uz: Va men o'zimning oxiriga erishish uchun hali juda ko'p ish bo'lishi kerakligini his qilganman!

en: A room, a writing-table, an equipage I still found it impossible to arrange “comme il faut,” however much I fought down my aversion to practical matters in my desire to become proficient.
uz: Xona, yozish stoli, jihozlar hali ham kerakli tarzda tashkil etishni men uchun imkonsiz deb topdim, ammo amaliy masalalarga bo'lgan nafratimni ustun qo'yib, mahoratga ega bo'lish istagim bilan kurashdim.

en: Yet everything seemed to arrange itself properly with other people, just as though things could never have been otherwise!
uz: Ammo hamma narsa boshqa odamlar bilan to'g'ri tartibga solingan bo'lib ko'rinardi, xuddi narsa hech qachon boshqacha bo'lishi mumkin bo'lmaganidek!

en: Once I remember asking Dubkoff, after much zealous and careful labouring at my finger-nails (his own were extraordinarily good), whether his nails had always been as now, or whether he had done anything to make them so: to which he replied that never within his recollection had he done anything to them, and that he could not imagine a gentleman’s nails possibly being different.
uz: Bir marta Dubkoffdan, mening barmoqlarimda g'ayratli va ehtiyotkorlik bilan mehnat qilganimdan keyin (uning o'zlarining barmoqlari juda yaxshi edi), uning barmoqlari har doim ham hozirgidek bo'lganmi yoki ularni shunday qilish uchun biror narsa qilganmi, deb so'raganimni eslayman: unga u hech qachon ularga hech narsa qilmaganligini va bir gentlemanning barmoqlari boshqa bo'lishini tasavvur qila olmasligini aytdi.

en: This answer incensed me greatly, for I had not yet learnt that one of the chief conditions of “comme il faut”-ness was to hold one’s tongue about the labour by which it had been acquired.
uz: Bu javob meni juda xafa qildi, chunki men hali ham comme il faut-nessning asosiy shartlaridan biri o'z mehnatini o'z ichiga olgan mehnat haqida gapirishni o'rganmagan edim.

en: “Comme il faut”-ness I looked upon as not only a great merit, a splendid accomplishment, an embodiment of all the perfection which must strive to attain, but as the one indispensable condition without which there could never be happiness, nor glory, nor any good whatsoever in this world.
uz: Men uni nafaqat katta sharaf, ajoyib yutuq, erishish uchun harakat qilish kerak bo'lgan mukammallikning aks ettirilgan qismi deb bilardim, balki bu dunyoda baxt, shon-shuhrat yoki boshqa yaxshilik bo'lmasligi kerak bo'lgan yagona shart sifatida ko'rdim.

en: Even the greatest artist or savant or benefactor of the human race would at that time have won from me no respect if he had not also been “comme il faut.” A man possessed of “comme il faut”-ness stood higher than, and beyond all possible equality with, such people, and might well leave it to them to paint pictures, to compose music, to write books, or to do good.
uz: Hatto insoniyatning eng buyuk san'atkor, olim yoki xayriyachi ham o'sha paytda men tomonidan hurmatga sazovor bo'lmas edi, agar u ham comme il faut bo'lmaganida. comme il faut-nessga ega bo'lgan kishi bunday odamlar bilan tenglikdan yuqori va undan ham yuqori bo'lgan va ularni rasm chizishga, musiqa tuzishga, kitob yozishga yoki yaxshilik qilishga qo'yib yuborishi mumkin edi.

en: Possibly he might commend them for so doing (since why should not merit be commended where-ever it be found?), but he could never stand ON A LEVEL with them, seeing that he was “comme il faut” and they were not—a quite final and sufficient reason.
uz: Ehtimol, u bunday qilishlari uchun ularni maqtagan bo'lishi mumkin (chunki qayerda bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, nima uchun maqtovga loyiq emas?), lekin u hech qachon ular bilan bir qatorda bo'lib, o'zi kerakli bo'lgan va ular to'liq oxirgi va yetarlicha sabab bo'lmaganini ko'rib, hech qachon ular bilan bir qatorda turolmaydi.

en: In fact, I actually believe that, had we possessed a brother or a father or a mother who had not been “comme il faut,” I should have declared it to be a great misfortune for us, and announced that between myself and them there could never be anything in common.
uz: Darhaqiqat, agar birodarimiz, otasi yoki onasi bo'lmagan bo'lsa, men buni biz uchun katta baxtsizlik deb e'lon qilib, o'zim va ular o'rtasida hech qachon umumiy narsa bo'lmasligini e'lon qilgan bo'lar edim.

en: Yet neither waste of the golden hours which I consumed in constantly endeavouring to observe the many arduous, unattainable conditions of “comme il faut”-ness (to the exclusion of any more serious pursuit), nor dislike of and contempt for nine-tenths of the human race, nor disregard of all the beauty that lay outside the
uz: Ammo men o'zimni ko'pgina og'ir, erishish mumkin bo'lmagan comme il faut-ness sharoitlarini kuzatishga harakat qilib sarflagan oltin soatlarimni ziyoda qilmasdim, inson avlodining to'qqizdan to'qqiz qismini yoqtirmasdim va hurmat qilmasdim, shuningdek, o'zimizdan tashqarida joylashgan barcha go'zalliklarni e'tiborsiz qoldirmasdim.

en: narrow circle of “comme il faut”-ness comprised the whole of the evil which the idea wrought in me.
uz: comme il faut-nessning tor doirasi mening fikrimdagi butun yomonlikni o'z ichiga olgan.

en: The chief evil of all lay in the notion acquired that a man need not strive to become a tchinovnik, [Official.] a coachbuilder, a soldier, a savant, or anything useful, so long only as he was “comme il faut “—that by attaining the latter quality he had done all that was demanded of him, and was even superior to most people.
uz: Eng yomon narsa shundaki, odam tchinovnik, ko'chak quruvchi, askar, olim yoki boshqa foydali narsa bo'lishga intilmasligi kerak degan fikrga ega bo'lgan, faqatgina o'zi kerakli bo'lganidek, bu fazilatga ega bo'lib, undan talab qilingan hamma narsani bajargan va hatto ko'pchilikdan ham ustun bo'lgan.

en: Usually, at a given period in youth, and after many errors and excesses, every man recognises the necessity of his taking an active part in social life, and chooses some branch of labour to which to devote himself.
uz: Odatda, yoshlik davrida va ko'plab xato va haddan tashqariliklardan keyin har bir kishi ijtimoiy hayotda faol ishtirok etish zarurligini tan oladi va o'zini bag'ishlaydigan ish tarzini tanlaydi.

en: Only with the “comme il faut” man does this rarely happen.
uz: Faqatgina comme il faut odam bilan bu kamdan-kam sodir bo'ladi.

en: I have known, and know, very, very many people—old, proud, self-satisfied, and opinionated—who to the question (if it should ever present itself to them in their world) “Who have you been, and what have you ever done?” would be unable to reply otherwise than by saying, “Je fus un homme tres comme il faut,” Such a fate was awaiting myself.
uz: Men juda ko'p qariya, mag'rur, o'z-o'zini qoniqtirgan va o'z fikrini bilgan odamlarni bilaman va bilamanki, kim bo'lgansiz va nima qilgansiz? degan savolga javob berishdan boshqa hech narsa bera olmasdi.

en: YOUTH Despite the confusion of ideas raging in my head, I was at least young, innocent, and free that summer—consequently almost happy.
uz: Yoshlik, fikrlarning chalg'ishiga qaramay, men o'sha yozda hech bo'lmaganda yosh, aybsiz va erkin edim va natijada deyarli baxtli edim.

en: Sometimes I would rise quite early in the morning, for I slept on the open verandah, and the bright, horizontal beams of the morning sun would wake me up.
uz: Ba'zan ertalab juda erta turardim, chunki men ochiq verandada uxlardim va ertalab quyoshning yorqin, gorizontal nurlari meni uyg'otardi.

en: Dressing myself quickly, I would tuck a towel and a French novel under my arm, and go off to bathe in the river in the shade of a birch tree which stood half a verst from the house.
uz: O'zimni tez kiyganimda, tuval va fransuz romanini qo'lim ostida qo'yib, uydan yarim kilometr uzoqlikda joylashgan bir chiroyli daraxtning soyasida daryoga suzishga ketardim.

en: Next, I would stretch myself on the grass and read—raising my eyes from time to time to look at the surface of the river where it showed blue in the shade of the trees, at the ripples caused by the first morning breeze, at the yellowing field of rye on the further bank, and at the bright-red sheen of the sunlight as it struck lower and lower down the white trunks of the birch-trees which, ranged in ranks one behind the other, gradually receded into the remote distance of the home park.
uz: Keyin o'zimni o'tga uzatib, o'z ko'zimni vaqti-vaqti bilan ko'tarib, daraxtlar soyasida ko'k ko'rinadigan daryo yuziga qarardim, ertalabki birinchi shamol tufayli yuzaga keladigan to'lqinlarga, keyingi qirg'oqdagi sariq bo'lib o'tgan bo'g'imzorga va quyosh nurining yorqin qizil chiroqlariga qarardim.

en: At such moments I would feel joyously conscious of having within me the same young, fresh force of life as nature was everywhere exuding around me.
uz: Bunday paytlarda men o'zimda o'sha yosh, yangi hayot kuchi borligidan xursand bo'lib, atrofimda tabiatning har qanday joyida to'sib turganidan xabardor edim.

en: When, however, the sky was overcast with grey clouds of morning and I felt chilly after bathing, I would often start to walk at random through the fields and woods, and joyously trail my wet boots in the fresh dew.
uz: Biroq, ertalab osmon bo'lak-bo'lak bilan qoplangan bo'lganida va suvga cho'mganimdan so'ng sovuq bo'lganimda, men ko'pincha dalalar va o'rmonlar orqali tasodifiy yurishni boshlaardim va yangi sho'rda issiq bo'lgan poyabzallarimni quvonch bilan kuzatib borardim.

en: All the while my head would be filled with vivid dreams concerning the heroes of my last-read novel, and I would keep picturing to myself some leader of an army or some statesman or marvellously strong man or devoted lover or another, and looking round me in, a nervous expectation that I should suddenly descry HER somewhere near me, in a meadow or behind a tree.
