uz: O'shanda boshim oxirgi marta o'qigan romanim qahramonlari haqida hayajonli tushlar bilan to'lib turardi va men o'zimga biron bir armiya rahbari yoki davlat arbobini yoki ajoyib darajada kuchli odamni yoki sodiq sevgini yoki boshqa birini tasavvur qilib, atrofimni ko'rib turardim va birdan uni yonimda, cho'lda yoki daraxt ortida bir joyda tasvirlashim kerak degan g'ayratli kutish bilan.

en: Yet, whenever these rambles led me near peasants engaged at their work, all my ignoring of the existence of the
uz: Biroq, bu sayohatlar meni o'z ishlarida band bo'lgan qishloq xo'jaligiga olib borganida, bularning barchasidan bexabar bo'lganman.

en: “common people” did not prevent me from experiencing an involuntary, overpowering sensation of awkwardness; so that I always tried to avoid their seeing me.
uz: Umumiy odamlar menga o'zimni o'ylamasdan, o'zimni qo'ldan boy bermaydigan noqulaylik hissiyotini his qilishdan to'smadilar; shuning uchun men har doim ularni ko'rishdan qochishga harakat qilardim.

en: When the heat of the day had increased, it was not infrequently my habit—if the ladies did not come out of doors for their morning tea—to go rambling through the orchard and kitchen-garden, and to pluck ripe fruit there.
uz: Kunning issiqligi ko'payganida, ayollar ertalab choy ichish uchun eshikdan chiqib, bog' va oshxona bog'lari bo'ylab yurib, o'sha yerda yetgan mevalarni yig'ib olishni odat qilib ko'rardim.

en: Indeed, this was an occupation which furnished me with one of my greatest pleasures.
uz: Darhaqiqat, bu menga eng katta zavqlardan biriga ega bo'lgan kasb edi.

en: Let any one go into an orchard, and dive into the midst of a tall, thick, sprouting raspberry-bed.
uz: Har kim meva bog'iga kirib, baland, qalloqli va ko'payib borayotgan sabzavotli daraxtning o'rtasida bo'lib o'tsin.

en: Above will be seen the clear, glowing sky, and, all around, the pale-green, prickly stems of raspberry-trees where they grow mingled together in a tangle of profusion.
uz: Yuqorida aniq, yorqin osmon va atrofida rang-yashil, tikilgan sabzavot daraxtlari ko'rinadi, ular bir-biriga aralashib, ko'pchilikning to'plamida o'sib o'sadi.

en: At one’s feet springs the dark-green nettle, with its slender crown of flowers, while the broad-leaved burdock, with its bright-pink, prickly blossoms, overtops the raspberries (and even one’s head) with its luxuriant masses, until, with the nettle, it almost meets the pendent, pale-green branches of the old apple-trees where apples, round and lustrous as bone, but as yet unripe, are mellowing in the heat of the sun.
uz: O'zining chiroyli gullari bilan chiroyli ko'k-yashil shoxlari paydo bo'ladi, keng bargli burdoq esa o'zining chiroyli shoxli, chiroyli gullari bilan chiroyli sabzavotlarni (va hatto boshini) o'zining chiroyli massasi bilan qoplaydi, hatto shox bilan deyarli eski olma daraxtlarining ko'tarib turgan, ko'k-ko'k yashil shoxlari bilan uchrashadi.

en: Below, again, are seen young raspberry-shoots, twining themselves around the partially withered, leafless parent plant, and stretching their tendrils towards the sunlight, with green, needle-shaped blades of grass and young, dew-coated pods peering through last year’s leaves, and growing juicily green in the perennial shade, as though they care nothing for the bright sunshine which is playing on the leaves of the apple-trees above them.
uz: Quyida yana yosh sabzavot sho'rlari ko'rinadi, o'zlarini qisman qurigan, bargsiz ota-ona o'simlikning atrofida bog'lashadi va o'z soyalarini quyosh nuri tomon uzaydilar, yashil, igna shakli o'simliklar va o'tgan yilning barglarini ko'rib turgan yosh, yog' bilan qoplangan kishanlar o'sib, ko'p yillik soyasida o'z-o'zidan yashil holda o'sib boradi, xuddi ular o'zlarining ustida bo'lgan olma daraxtlarining barglarida o'ynayotgan yorqin quyosh nuridan umuman g'amxo'rlik qilmayotgandek.

en: In this density there is always moisture—always a smell of confined, perpetual shade, of cobwebs, fallen apples (turning black where they roll on the mouldy sod), raspberries, and earwigs of the kind which impel one to reach hastily for more fruit when one has inadvertently swallowed a member of that insect tribe with the last berry.
uz: Ushbu zichlikda har doim namlik, doimo o'z ichiga cheklangan, doimiy soya, o'simliklar, tushib ketgan olmalar (o'simlik so'ri bilan qoralashadigan joyda qoralashadi), sabzavotlar va quloq cho'g'lari, bularning o'zi odamni oxirgi meva bilan bug'doylar qabilasidan bir a'zosiga qasddan yutib qo'yganida, ko'proq mevalar uchun shoshilinch harakat qilishga undaydi.

en: At every step one’s movements keep flushing the sparrows which always make their home in these depths, and one hears their fussy chirping and the beating of their tiny, fluttering wings against the stalks, and catches the low buzzing of a bumble bee somewhere, and the sound of the gardener’s footsteps (it is half-daft Akim) on the path as he hums his eternal sing-song to himself.
uz: Har qadamda har doim bu chuqurliklarda o'z uyini quradigan cho'g'irlarni ko'tarib turadi va ularning g'ayratli qichqiriqlarini va o'zlarining kichkina, qichqiriq qanotlarining bo'g'inga qarshi urishlarini eshitadi va qayerda bo'lganda bir joyda bo'g'irning past qichqirishini va bog'bonning qadamlari (bu yarim qo'pol Akimdir) ovozini yo'lda o'zi uchun abadiy qo'shiq qo'shiqlarini qo'shib qo'yadi.

en: Then one mutters under one’s breath, “No!
uz: So'ngra bir kishi nafas olganda, "Yo'q!" deb qichqiradi.

en: Neither he nor any one else shall find me here!” yet still one goes on stripping juicy berries from their conical white pilasters,
uz: U ham, boshqa hech kim ham meni bu yerda topolmaydi! lekin hali ham bir kishi ularning konik oq pilastrlaridan shomli mevalarni olib tashlamoqda.

en: and cramming them into one’s mouth.
uz: va ularni birovning og'ziga to'kib qo'yish.

en: At length, one’s legs soaked to the knees as one repeats, over and over again, some rubbish which keeps running in one’s head, and one’s hands and nether limbs (despite the protection of one’s wet trousers) thoroughly stung with the nettles, one comes to the conclusion that the sun’s rays are beating too straight upon one’s head for eating to be any longer desirable, and, sinking down into the tangle of greenery, one remains there—looking and listening, and continuing in mechanical fashion to strip off one or two of the finer berries and swallow them.
uz: Oxir oqibat, birovning oyoqlari to'ng'ichgacha bo'lib, qayta-qayta, boshida biroz cho'g'lar bo'lib turadi, qo'llari va pastki a'zolari (suyuq paltarlar himoyasiga qaramasdan) yirtqichlar bilan yaxshi tikilganida, quyosh nurlari endi iste'mol qilish uchun boshida juda to'g'ri urib ketayotganiga amin bo'lish mumkin, va o'simliklarning to'pasiga tushib, u erda ko'rinish va tinglash bilan shug'ullanadi va mexanik tarzda bir yoki ikkita yaxshi mevalarni yo'q qilib, ularni yutib yuborish uchun davom etadi.

en: At eleven o’clock—that is to say, when the ladies had taken their morning tea and settled down to their occupations—I would repair to the drawing-room.
uz: To'qqizlarda, ya'ni, ayollar ertalab choy ichib, o'z ishlariga joylashganida, men o'zimni xonaga olib borardim.

en: Near the first window, with its unbleached linen blind lowered to exclude the sunshine, but through the chink of which the sun kept throwing brilliant circles of light which hurt the eye to look at them, there would be standing a screen, with flies quietly parading the whiteness of its covering.
uz: Birinchi deraza yaqinida, quyosh nurini istisno qilish uchun oq bo'lmagan to'qima tushirilgan edi, lekin quyosh ularni ko'rish uchun ko'zni og'ritadigan chiroyli yorug'lik to'plamlarini tashlamoqchi bo'lgan chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiro chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiroyli chiro chiro chiro chiroyli chiro chiro chiroyli chiro chiro chiro chiro ch

en: Behind it would be seated Mimi, shaking her head in an irritable manner, and constantly shifting from spot to spot to avoid the sunshine as at intervals it darted her from somewhere and laid a streak of flame upon her hand or face.
uz: Uning orqasida Mimi o'tirardi, boshini g'azablanarli tarzda silkitib, kun o'tib quyosh nuridan qochish uchun doimiy ravishda joydan joyga o'zgarib turardi.

en: Through the other three windows the sun would be throwing three squares of light, crossed with the shadows of the window-frames, and where one of these patches marked the unstained floor of the room there would be lying, in accordance with invariable custom, Milka, with her ears pricked as she watched the flies promenading the lighted space.
uz: Qolgan uchta deraza orqali quyosh uchta kvadrat yorug'lik ko'rinishini ko'rsatadi, u derazalar soyasi bilan o'zaro o'zaro bog'liq bo'ladi va bu parchalardan biri xonaning bo'sh qolmagan qavatini belgilagan joyda, o'zgarmas urf-odatga ko'ra, Milka o'z quloqlari cho'zilgan holda, yorug'lik bilan o'tiradi.

en: Seated on a settee, Katenka would be knitting or reading aloud as from time to time she gave her white sleeves (looking almost transparent in the sunshine) an impatient shake, or tossed her head with a frown to drive away some fly which had settled upon her thick auburn hair and was now buzzing in its tangles.
uz: Katenka setda o'tirganida, o'zining oq qo'lqovusini (kunduzgi quyosh nurida deyarli shaffof ko'rinardi) sabrsizlik bilan shovqin qilib, vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zining to'siq sochlari ustiga o'rnagan va endi o'z to'qimalarida o'tirgan bir mushakni haydab ketish uchun boshini ko'z ko'z bilan tashlab ketardi.

en: Lubotshka would either be walking up and down the room (her hands clasped behind her) until the moment should arrive when a movement would be made towards the garden, or playing some piece of which every note had long been familiar to me.
uz: Lubotshka bog'ga qarab harakatlanadigan vaqt kelguncha xonada ko'tarib-ko'tarib yurardi (qo'llari uning orqasidan to'plandi) yoki har bir nota menga uzoq vaqtdan beri tanish bo'lgan biron bir musiqani o'ynaydi.

en: For my own part, I would sit down somewhere, and listen to the music or the reading until such time as I myself should have an opportunity of performing on the piano.
uz: O'zim ham bir joyda o'tirib, musiqa yoki o'qishni tinglardim, hatto o'zim piano ustida ijro etish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lgan paytgacha.

en: After luncheon I would condescend to take the girls out riding (since to go for a mere walk at that hour seemed
uz: Ovqatdan so'ng qizlarni haydashga olib ketishga rozi bo'ldim (chunki o'sha soatda shunchaki piyoda bo'lish o'rinli edi).

en: to me unsuitable to my years and position in the world), and these excursions of ours—in which I often took my companions through unaccustomed spots and dells—were very pleasant.
uz: Men uchun o'sha yillar va dunyoda o'zimning mavqeyimga mos kelmaydigan edi) va bizning ushbu sayohatlarimiz, men tez-tez hamrohlariimni o'zgacha joylar va joylar orqali olib borganimda, juda yoqimli edi.

en: Indeed, on some of these occasions I grew quite boyish, and the girls would praise my riding and daring, and pretend that I was their protector.
uz: Darhaqiqat, ba'zi hollarda men o'zimni o'g'illikka aylantirganman va qizlar mening otashim va jasoratimni maqtab, men ularning himoyachisi bo'lganimni ko'rsatishgan.

en: In the evening, if we had no guests with us, tea (served in the dim verandah), would be followed by a walk round the homestead with Papa, and then I would stretch myself on my usual settee, and read and ponder as of old, as I listened to Katenka or Lubotshka playing.
uz: Kechqurun, agar bizda mehmonlar bo'lmaganida, choy (quruq verandada xizmat qilinadi), keyin otam bilan uyni aylanib o'tadigan bo'ldim, keyin esa odatdagi settimda o'zimni uzatib, Katenka yoki Lubotshka o'ynashini tinglaganimda, qadimgi kabi o'qib, mulohaza yuritardim.

en: At other times, if I was alone in the drawing-room and Lubotshka was performing some old-time air, I would find myself laying my book down, and gazing through the open doorway on to the balcony at the pendent, sinuous branches of the tall birch-trees where they stood overshadowed by the coming night, and at the clear sky where, if one looked at it intently enough, misty, yellowish spots would appear suddenly, and then disappear again.
uz: Boshqa paytlarda, agar men o'zimgina o'tirgan xonada Lubotshka eski zamon ahvolini o'tkazganida, kitobimni qo'yib, ochiq eshikdan balkonga qarab, baland birkovlarning ko'p bo'lib turgan shoxlarini ko'tarib turardim, ular kecha soyasida turgan edilar va aniq osmonda, agar uni diqqat bilan ko'rsa, bulutli, sariq rangli nuqtalar birdan paydo bo'lib, keyin yana yo'q bo'lib ketardi.

en: Next, as I listened to the sounds of the music wafted from the salon, and to the creaking of gates and the voices of the peasant women when the cattle returned to the village, I would suddenly bethink me of Natalia Savishna and of Mamma and of Karl Ivanitch, and become momentarily sad.
uz: Keyingi safar, salondan to'qnashgan musiqaning tovushlarini, chorvalar qishloqga qaytganda eshiklar qichqirishini va qishloq ayollarining ovozlarini tinglaganimda, to'satdan Nataliya Savishna, Mamma va Karl Ivanitch haqida o'yladim va bir zumda xafa bo'ldim.

en: But in those days my spirit was so full of life and hope that such reminiscences only touched me in passing, and soon fled away again.
uz: Ammo o'sha kunlarda ruhim hayot va umid bilan to'lib-toshgan bo'lib, bunday xotiralar o'tmishda menga ta'sir qildi va tez orada yana qochib ketdi.

en: After supper and (sometimes) a night stroll with some one in the garden (for I was afraid to walk down the dark avenues by myself), I would repair to my solitary sleeping-place on the verandah—a proceeding which, despite the countless mosquitos which always devoured me, afforded me the greatest pleasure.
uz: Kechki ovqatdan va (ba'zan) bog'da birov bilan kechki sayohatdan so'ng (chunki qorong'i yo'llarda yolg'iz yurishdan qo'rqardim), men verandadagi yolg'iz uyquga qaytardim, bu esa, meni har doim yutqazadigan son-sanoqsiz chigirtkalarga qaramay, menga eng katta zavq keltirardi.

en: If the moon was full, I frequently spent whole nights sitting up on my mattress, looking at the light and shade, listening to the sounds or stillness, dreaming of one matter and another (but more particularly of the poetic, voluptuous happiness which, in those days, I believed was to prove the acme of my felicity) and lamenting that until now it had only been given to me to IMAGINE things.
uz: To'liq oy bo'lganda, ko'pincha to'liq kechalarni matrasimda o'tirib, nur va soyalarga qarayman, tovushlar yoki tinchlikni tinglayman, bir narsadan boshqa narsa haqida orzu qilaman (agar ayniqsa, o'sha kunlarda men o'zimning baxtiyorligimning yuksakligini isbotlash deb hisoblagan she'riy, shahvatli baxt haqida) va hozirga qadar menga faqat O'ZGA tasavvur qilish uchun berilgan bo'lganidan qayg'uraman.

en: No sooner had every one dispersed, and I had seen lights pass from the drawing-room to the upper chambers (whence female voices would presently be heard, and the noise of windows opening and shutting), than I would depart to the
uz: Hamma tarqalib ketganidan so'ng, turar joydan yuqori xonalarga chiroqlar o'tib ketayotganini ko'rganimdan so'ng (bu yerda ayollarning ovozi va darvozalarning ochilish va yopilish shovqinlari eshitilishi mumkin edi), men o'sha paytdan boshlab ga jo'nab ketardim.

en: verandah, and walk up and down there as I listened attentively to the sounds from the slumbering mansion.
uz: Verandaga borib, uyqushtirgan uyning tovushlarini diqqat bilan tinglaganimda, u yerga boraman va tushaman.

en: To this day, whenever I feel any expectation (no matter how small and baseless) of realising a fraction of some happiness of which I may be dreaming, I somehow invariably fail to picture to myself what the imagined happiness is going to be like.
uz: Bugungi kunga qadar, men orzu qilgan baxtning bir qismiga erishish uchun har qanday umidni (hazirgi kunlarda qanchalik kichik va asossiz bo'lishidan qat'i nazar) his qilganimda, men o'zim uchun tasavvur qila olmayman.

en: At the least sound of bare footsteps, or of a cough, or of a snore, or of the rattling of a window, or of the rustling of a dress, I would leap from my mattress, and stand furtively gazing and listening, thrown, without any visible cause, into extreme agitation.
uz: O'ylamaydigan qadamlar, kashsish, qichqiriq, derazalarning qichqiriqlari yoki kiyimning qichqiriqlari so'ng, men matrasimdan sakrashdim va hech qanday sababsiz, o'ta g'ayratga tushgan holda, g'ayratli ravishda qarab va tinglab turardim.

en: But the lights would disappear from the upper rooms, the sounds of footsteps and talking give place to snores, the watchman begin his nightly tapping with his stick, the garden grow brighter and more mysterious as the streaks of light vanished from the windows, the last candle pass from the pantry to the hall (throwing a glimmer into the dewy garden as it did so), and the stooping figure of Foka (decked in a nightcap, and carrying the candle) become visible to my eyes as he went to his bed.
uz: Ammo yuqori xonalardan chiroqlar yo'q bo'lib ketardi, qadamlar va gap-so'zlarning ovozi qichqiriqlarga yo'l ochardi, soqchilar o'z tayoqlari bilan kechasi toshishni boshlashardi, bog' darvozalaridan yorug'lik yo'q bo'lganida bog' yanada yorqinroq va sirli bo'lib borardi, omborxonadan zalga oxirgi chiroq o'tadi (o'sha paytdagi chiroyli bog'ga bir nazar soldi) va Foka (tosh qo'rqinchida qoplangan va chiroqni ko'tarib yurgan) ko'zlarimga ko'rinadi.

en: Often I would find a great and fearful pleasure in stealing over the grass, in the black shadow of the house, until I had reached the hall window, where I would stand listening with bated breath to the snoring of the boy, to Foka’s gruntings (in the belief that no one heard him), and to the sound of his senile voice as he drawled out the evening prayers.
uz: Ko'pincha uyning qora soyasida o'g'irlanishni katta va dahshatli zavq bilan o'rganardim, hatto zal darvozasiga yetgunimcha, o'g'ilning qichqirishini, Fokaning qichqirishini (birov uni eshitmagan deb o'ylayman) va kechki ibodatlarni o'qib berayotganida uning qalin ovozini tinglab turardim.

en: At length even his candle would be extinguished, and the window slammed down, so that I would find myself utterly alone; whereupon, glancing nervously from side to side, lest haply I should see the white woman standing near a flower-bed or by my couch, I would run at full speed back to the verandah.
uz: Oxir oqibat, hatto uning chiroqlari ham o'chirib, darcha o'z-o'zimni yolg'iz topishimga sabab bo'ldi; shu paytdan boshlab, bir tomondan boshqa tomonga g'ayrat bilan qarab, ehtimol oq ayolni gulxonada yoki sofa yonida turganini ko'rmasam, to'liq tezlikda verandaga qaytib borardim.

en: Then, and only then, I would lie down with my face to the garden, and, covering myself over, so far as possible, from the mosquitos and bats, fall to gazing in front of me as I listened to the sounds of the night and dreamed of love and happiness.
uz: O'shanda, va faqat o'shanda, men bog'ga yuzma-yuzlab yotardim va o'zimni, iloji boricha ko'pincha, sigirlar va tuproqlardan qoplab, kecha tovushlarini tinglab, sevgi va baxt haqida orzu qilganimda, oldimga qarab qolardim.

en: At such times everything would take on for me a different meaning.
uz: Bunday paytlarda men uchun hamma narsa o'zgacha ma'noga ega bo'lardi.

en: The look of the old birch trees, with the one side of their curling branches showing bright against the moonlit sky, and the other darkening the bushes and carriage-drive with their black shadows; the calm, rich glitter of the pond, ever swelling like a sound; the moonlit sparkle of the dewdrops on the flowers in front of
uz: Qadimgi birkovlarning ko'rinishi, ularning bir tomoni o'z bo'g'illari bilan oyning ko'rinishida yorqin ko'rinadi, boshqasi esa qora soyalar bilan butalarni qorong'ochlashtiradi; hovuzning tinch, boy shov-shuvlari, har doim tovush kabi puflab turadi; o'z oldidagi gullarda yog' tomirlarining oy yorug'ligi;

en: the verandah; the graceful shadows of those flowers where they lay thrown upon the grey stonework; the cry of a quail on the far side of the pond; the voice of some one walking on the high road; the quiet, scarcely audible scrunching of two old birch trees against one another; the humming of a mosquito at my car under the coverlet; the fall of an apple as it caught against a branch and rustled among the dry leaves; the leapings of frogs as they approached almost to the verandah-steps and sat with the moon shining mysteriously on their green backs—all these things took on for me a strange significance—a significance of exceeding beauty and of infinite love.
uz: veranda; ular yotgan kulli toshlar ko'rinishidagi go'zal soyalar; hovuzning o't tomonidagi qichqiriq; yuqori yo'lda yurgan kishining ovozi; ikki eski birkovning bir-biriga qarshi tinch, kamdan-kam eshitilgan qichqirishlari; mashinamda ildizni ko'rmoq; shox bo'lib, quruq barglar o'rtasida o'tirgan olma tushib tushib tushib ketishi; chiroqlarning qichqiriqlari, deyarli veranda qadamlariga yaqinlashib, yashil orqalarida oy sirli tarzda nur sochgan holda o'tirganlari; bularning barchasi men uchun g'ayri ma'noga ega bo'ldi - ajoyib go'zallik va cheksiz sevishning ahamiyati.

en: Before me would rise SHE, with long black tresses and a high bust, but always mournful in her fairness, with bare hands and voluptuous arms.
uz: Mening oldimga U, uzun qora bo'ylaklari va baland burst bilan turardi, lekin har doim o'zining adolatli, yalang'och qo'llari va gullab-yashgan qo'llari bilan qayg'urardi.

en: She loved me, and for one moment of her love I would sacrifice my whole life!—But the moon would go on rising higher and higher, and shining brighter and brighter, in the heavens; the rich sparkle of the pond would swell like a sound, and become ever more and more brilliant, while the shadows would grow blacker and blacker, and the sheen of the moon more and more transparent: until, as I looked at and listened to all this, something would say to me that SHE with the bare hands and voluptuous arms did not represent ALL happiness, that love for her did not represent ALL good; so that, the more I gazed at the full, high-riding moon, the higher would true beauty and goodness appear to me to lie, and the purer and purer they would seem—the nearer and nearer to Him who is the source of all beauty and all goodness.
uz: U meni yaxshi ko'rgan va uning sevgisi uchun men butun hayotimni qurbon qilgan bo'lardim!Ammo oy osmonlarda ko'proq va ko'proq parvarish qilib, ko'proq parvarish qilardi; hovuzning boy chiroqlari tovush kabi yuzaga chiqardi va har doim ko'proq parvarish bo'lardi, soyalar qora va qora bo'lib borardi va oyning shishi har doim shaffofroq bo'lardi: men bularning barchasini ko'rib va tinglaganimda, bir narsa menga aytadiki, u yalang'och qo'llar bilan va shov-shuv bilan BUT baxtni ifoda etmaydi, uning sevgisi yaxshilikni ifoda etmaydi; shuning uchun men to'liq, yuqoriga o'tirgan oyga qaraganim sayin, haqiqiy go'zallik va go'zallik menga yolg'on ko'rinadi, ular esa har qanday go'zallik va go'zallik manbaiga yaqinroq va yaqinroq ko'rinadi.

en: And tears of a sort of unsatisfied, yet tumultuous, joy would fill my eyes.
uz: Ko'zlarim quvonchga to'lib-toshgan, ammo norozi bo'lgan ko'z yoshlari bilan to'lib-toshgan.

en: Always, too, I was alone; yet always, too, it seemed to me that, although great, mysterious Nature could draw the shining disc of the moon to herself, and somehow hold in some high, indefinite place the pale-blue sky, and be everywhere around me, and fill of herself the infinity of space, while I was but a lowly worm, already defiled with the poor, petty passions of humanity—always it seemed to me that, nevertheless, both Nature and the moon and I were one.
uz: Men ham har doim yolg'iz edim; lekin men ham har doim shunday deb o'ylardimki, buyuk va sirli tabiat o'ziga oyning shishqoq diskini jalb qilishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, u qandaydir yuksak, cheksiz joyda o'tkir-oq ko'k osmonni ushlab, atrofimda hamma joyda bo'lib, o'zidan cheksiz makonni to'ldiradi, men esa insonning kambag'al, kichkinagina ishtiyoqlari bilan ifloslangan kamtar qurtadan boshqa hech narsa emas edim.Men har doim shunday deb o'ylardimki, shunga qaramay, tabiat, oy va men birmiz.

en: OUR NEIGHBOURS ON the first day after our arrival, I had been greatly astonished that Papa should speak of our neighbours, the Epifanovs, as “nice people,” and still more so that he should go to call upon them.
uz: O'Z G'IRIMLARIMIZGAN birinchi kun, dadamning qo'shnilarimiz Epifanovlar to'g'risida gapirishini va yana ko'proq gapirishini eshitib, ularni chaqirishini juda hayratda qoldim.

en: The fact was that we had long been at law over some land with this family.
uz: Darhaqiqat, biz bu oila bilan uzoq vaqtdan buyon bir nechta yerlar uchun qonuniy munosabatda bo'lganmiz.

en: When a child, I had more than once heard Papa raging over the litigation, abusing the Epifanovs, and warning people (so I understood him) against them.
uz: Bolaligimda dadamning sud jarayonida g'azablanganini, Epifanovlar oilasining yomon ta'sirini va odamlarni ularga qarshi ogohlantirganini bir necha marta eshitgan edim.

en: Likewise, I had heard Jakoff speak of them as “our enemies” and “black people” and could remember Mamma requesting that their names should never be mentioned in her presence, nor, indeed, in the house at all.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, Jakoff ularni dushmanlarimiz va qora tanli odamlar deb ataganini eshitgan edim va onam ularning ismlarini hech qachon uning huzurida, hatto uyda ham aytmasliklarini so'raganini eslayman.

en: From these data I, as a child, had arrived at the clear and assured conviction that the Epifanovs were foemen of ours who would at any time stab or strangle both Papa and his sons if they should ever come across them, as well as that they were “black people”, in the literal sense of the term.
uz: Bolaligimda men ushbu ma'lumotlardan Epifanovlar bizning dushmanlarimiz ekanligiga aniq va qat'iy ishonch hosil qildim, ular qachonlardir Papa va uning o'g'illari bilan uchrashsa, ularni o'g'irlab qo'yishadi yoki o'g'irlab qo'yishadi.

en: Consequently, when, in the year that Mamma died, I chanced to catch sight of Avdotia (“La Belle Flamande”) on the occasion of a visit which she paid to my mother, I found it hard to believe that she did not come of a family of negroes.
uz: Shuning uchun, onam vafot etgan yili Avdotiyani (La Belle Flamande) onamga tashrif buyurganida ko'rdim, u qora tanli oiladan emasligiga ishonish qiyin edi.

en: All the same, I had the lowest possible opinion of the family, and, for all that we saw much of them that summer, continued to be strongly prejudiced against them.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, men oila haqida kamdan-kam fikrda edim va o'sha yozda ularning ko'pchiligini ko'rganimizda ham, ularga nisbatan qattiq ta'sir ko'rsatishni davom ettirardim.

en: As a matter of fact, their household only consisted of the mother (a widow of fifty, but a very well-preserved, cheery old woman), a beautiful daughter named Avdotia, and a son, Peter, who was a stammerer, unmarried, and of very serious disposition.
uz: Darhaqiqat, ularning uyida faqat ona (bu ellik yoshli beva, ammo juda yaxshi saqlangan, quvonchli keksa ayol), Avdotiya ismli go'zal qiz va Peter ismli bir o'g'il bor edi.

en: For the last twenty years before her husband’s death, Madame Epifanov had lived apart from him—sometimes in St.
uz: Erining o'limidan oldin o'ttiz yil davomida xonim Epifanov undan ajralib yashardi, ba'zan St. Petersburgda.

en: Petersburg, where she had relatives, but more frequently at her village of Mitishtchi, which stood some three versts from ours.
uz: Sankt-Peterburgda qarindoshlari bor edi, lekin ko'proq o'z qishlog'i Mitishtchida, bizning qishlog'imizdan taxminan uch distl uzoqlikda edi.

en: Yet the neighbourhood had taken to circulating such horrible tales concerning her mode of life that Messalina was, by comparison, a
uz: Biroq, mehmonxona uning turmush tarzi to'g'risida shunday dahshatli hikoyalar tarqatishga kirgan ediki, Messalina o'z o'rnida o'yinchi edi.

en: blameless child: which was why my mother had requested her name never to be mentioned.
uz: Ayolsiz bola: shuning uchun onam ismining hech qachon aytib bo'lmasligini so'ragan edi.

en: As a matter of fact, not one-tenth part of the most cruel of all gossip—the gossip of country-houses—is worthy of credence; and although, when I first made Madame’s acquaintance, she had living with her in the house a clerk named Mitusha, who had been promoted from a serf, and who, curled, pomaded, and dressed in a frockcoat of Circassian pattern, always stood behind his mistress’s chair at luncheon, while from time to time she invited her guests to admire his handsome eyes and mouth, there was nothing for gossip to take hold of.
uz: Darhaqiqat, eng shafqatsiz mish-mishlarning o'ndan bir qismi ham e'tirofga sazovor emas; va men birinchi marta Madam bilan tanishganda, u uyda o'zi bilan o'tirgan Mitusha ismli xizmatkor bo'lgan, u qullikdan ko'tarilgan va o'ziga kirishib, mo'l-ko'ylak kiygan va sirkassiyalik kiyim kiygan edi va doimo kechki ovqatda xotini kursi orqasida turardi, ammo vaqti-vaqti bilan mehmonlarini uning go'zal ko'zlari va og'ziga ta'sir qilish uchun taklif qilardi, ammo mish-mish uchun hech narsa yo'q edi.

en: I believe, too, that since the time—ten years earlier—when she had recalled her dutiful son Peter from the service, she had wholly changed her mode of living.
uz: Shuningdek, o'n yil oldin o'g'li Butrusni xizmatdan chaqirib olganidan beri o'z turmush tarzini butunlay o'zgartirganligiga ishonaman.

en: It seems her property had never been a large one—merely a hundred souls or so —[This refers, of course, to the days of serfdom.]and that during her previous life of gaiety she had spent a great deal.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, uning mol-mulki hech qachon katta bo'lmagan, faqat yuz nafasi yoki shunday edi va o'tmishdagi quvonchli hayotida u ko'p vaqt sarflagan.

en: Consequently, when, some ten years ago, those portions of the property which had been mortgaged and re-mortgaged had been foreclosed upon and compulsorily sold by auction, she had come to the conclusion that all these unpleasant details of distress upon and valuation of her property had been due not so much to failure to pay the interest as to the fact that she was a woman: wherefore she had written to her son (then serving with his regiment) to come and save his mother from her embarrassments, and he, like a dutiful son—conceiving that his first duty was to comfort his mother in her old age—had straightway resigned his commission (for all that he had been doing well in his profession, and was hoping soon to become independent), and had come to join her in the country.
uz: Natijada, o'n yil oldin ipoteka va qayta ipoteka qilingan mulklarning qismlari vayron qilingan va majburiy ravishda savdo orqali sotilganida, u o'zining mol-mulkini qadrlash va qadrlashning barcha noqulay tafsilotlari nafaqat uning ayolligi uchun foiz to'lamasligi sababli, balki uning ayolligi uchun ham bo'lganligi haqida xulosa chiqargan edi: shuning uchun u o'g'liga (o'shanda uning to'pkasi bilan xizmat qilgan) xat yozgan edi va onasini uning noqulayliklaridan qutqarish uchun kelishini va u, katta yoshda onasini tasalli berish uchun birinchi vazifasini bajarishi kerakligini anglagan itoatkor o'g'il kabi, o'z vazifasidan darhol voz kechgan edi (o'zining kasbida yaxshi ishlar qilib yurgan va tez orada mustaqil bo'lishga umidvor edi) va u bilan mamlakatga qo'shilgan.

en: Despite his plain face, uncouth demeanour, and fault of stuttering, Peter was a man of unswerving principles and of the most extraordinary good sense.
uz: O'zining sodda yuziga, o'ziga xos xulq-atvorga va gapirishda aybdor bo'lishiga qaramay, Butrus qat'iy me'yorlarga ega bo'lgan va ajoyib aqlga ega bo'lgan odam edi.

en: Somehow—by small borrowings, sundry strokes of business, petitions for grace, and promises to repay—he contrived to carry on the property, and, making himself overseer, donned his father’s greatcoat (still preserved in a drawer), dispensed with horses and carriages, discouraged guests from calling at Mitishtchi, fashioned his own sleighs, increased his arable land and curtailed that of the serfs, felled his own timber, sold his produce in person, and saw to matters generally.
uz: Qaysi ma'noda kichik qarzlar, turli ishlarning o'zi, iltijolar va pul to'lash va'dalari orqali u mulkni saqlab qolish uchun o'zini o'zi yaratdi va nazoratchi qilib, otasining katta kiyimini kiydirdi (hozir ham sovg'axonida saqlanib qolgan), ot va vagonlardan voz kechdi, mehmonlarni Mitishtchiga tashrif buyurishdan qaytardi, o'z san'atlarini yaratdi, ekinzorlarini ko'paytirdi va qullar o'zidan qisqartirdi, o'z daraxtini kesib tashladi, mahsulotlarini shaxsan sotdi va umuman ko'z-qusurdi.

en: Indeed, he swore, and kept his
uz: Haqiqatan ham, u qasam ichib, o'z qasamini bajardi.

en: oath, that, until all outstanding debts were paid, he would never wear any clothes than his father’s greatcoat and a corduroy jacket which he had made for himself, nor yet ride in aught but a country waggon, drawn by peasants’ horses.
uz: Barcha qarzlar to'languncha, u hech qachon otasining katta kiyimidan boshqa kiyim kiymaydi va o'zi o'zi uchun tayyorlagan bo'ylak kiyimidan boshqa kiyim kiymaydi, shuningdek, qishloq vagonidan boshqa hech narsa bilan yurmaydi.

en: This stoical mode of life he sought to apply also to his family, so far as the sympathetic respect which he conceived to be his mother’s due would allow of; so that, although, in the drawing-room, he would show her only stuttering servility, and fulfil all her wishes, and blame any one who did not do precisely as she bid them, in his study or his office he would overhaul the cook if she had served up so much as a duck without his orders, or any one responsible for sending a serf (even though at Madame’s own bidding) to inquire after a neighbour’s health or for despatching the peasant girls into the wood to gather wild raspberries instead of setting them to weed the kitchen-garden.
uz: Bu stoik turmush tarzini u oilasiga ham qo'llashga harakat qildi, uning onasi bo'lishi kerak deb o'ylagan mehribon hurmat imkonini berdi; shuning uchun, agar u o'tirgan xonada uning faqatgina qichqiriq qullig'ini ko'rsatsa ham, uning barcha istaklarini bajarsa ham, u buyurganini bajarmagan har bir kishini ayblashi uchun, u o'z ishxonasida yoki ishxonasida oshxonani qayta ko'rib chiqardi, agar u uning buyruqlariisiz qush kabi xizmat qilgan bo'lsa, yoki bir xizmatkorni (hazirda xonimning o'zi taklif qilgan bo'lsa-da) qo'shni sog'lig'ini so'rash uchun yuborish uchun yoki qishloq qizlarini o'ronga yuborish uchun cho'lda yovvoyi sabzavotlarni yig'ish uchun o't o'rniga, ularni oshxona bog'ida begona o'g'irlarni o'g'irlash uchun o'rnatish uchun.

en: Within four years every debt had been repaid, and Peter had gone to Moscow and returned thence in a new jacket and tarantass.
uz: To'rt yil ichida barcha qarzlar to'langan edi va Peter Moskvaga borib, u yerdan yangi kiyim va tarantassa kiygan holda qaytib kelgan edi.

en: [A two-wheeled carriage.] Yet, despite this flourishing position of affairs, he still preserved the stoical tendencies in which, to tell the truth, he took a certain vague pride before his family and strangers, since he would frequently say with a stutter: “Any one who REALLY wishes to see me will be glad to see me even in my dressing-gown, and to eat nothing but shtchi [Cabbage-soup.] and kasha [Buckwheat gruel.] at my table.” “That is what I eat myself,” he would add.
uz: [Ikkala g'ildirakli vagon] Shunday bo'lsa-da, bu gullab-yashgan holatga qaramay, u hali ham shu stoik tendentsiyalarni saqlab qolgan edi, haqiqatni aytganda, u o'z oilasi va begonalar oldida g'ururli bo'lgan, chunki u tez-tez gapiradigan edi: AQShI meni ko'rmoqchi bo'lgan har bir kishi meni hatto kiyimda ko'rishidan xursand bo'ladi va stolimda shtchi [ko'krak-suppa] va [buckwheat kasha gruel] dan boshqa hech narsa yemaydi.  Bu men o'zim yeyapman, o'zi qo'shadi.

en: In his every word and movement spoke pride based upon a consciousness of having sacrificed himself for his mother and redeemed the property, as well as contempt for any one who had not done something of the same kind.
uz: Uning har bir so'zi va harakatida o'zini onasi uchun qurbon qilganligi va mol-mulkini sotib olganligi haqidagi tafakkurga asoslangan mag'rurlik, shuningdek, xuddi shunday ish qilmagan har bir kishiga nisbatan kamsitish so'zladi.

en: The mother and daughter were altogether different characters from Peter, as well as altogether different from one another.
uz: Onasi va qizi Butrusdan umuman farq qilgan, bir-biridan umuman farq qilgan.

en: The former was one of the most agreeable, uniformly good-tempered, and cheerful women whom one could possibly meet.
uz: Ilk ayol eng yoqimli, yaxshi ruhiy va quvonchli ayollardan biri edi.

en: Anything attractive and genuinely happy delighted her.
uz: Chiroyli va chinakam baxtli bo'lgan har qanday narsa uni quvontirardi.

en: Even the faculty of being pleased with the sight of young people enjoying themselves (it is only in the best-natured of elderly folk that one meets with that TRAIT) she possessed to the full.
uz: Hatto yoshlarning zavqlanayotganini ko'rishdan mamnun bo'lish qobiliyati ham (va faqat keksalarning eng yaxshi tuyg'ulari bilan uchrashish mumkin) unga to'liq ega bo'lgan.

en: On the other hand, her daughter was of a grave turn of mind.
uz: Boshqa tomondan, uning qizi jiddiy fikrlash tarzini o'zgartirdi.

en: Rather, she was of that peculiarly careless, absent-minded, gratuitously distant bearing which
uz: Aksincha, u o'zgacha beparvo, befarq, befarq va uzoq bo'lgan, ammo o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'z-o'zidan uzoqroq bo'lgan.

en: commonly distinguishes unmarried beauties.
uz: odatda turmush qurmagan go'zalliklarni ajratib turadi.

en: Whenever she tried to be gay, her gaiety somehow seemed to be unnatural to her, so that she always appeared to be laughing either at herself or at the persons to whom she was speaking or at the world in general—a thing which, possibly, she had no real intention of doing.
uz: U gey bo'lishga harakat qilganda, uning shodligi unga tabiiy emasdek tuyulardi, shuning uchun u har doim o'ziga yoki gapirgan odamlarga yoki umuman dunyoga kulishi mumkin edi.

en: Often I asked myself in astonishment what she could mean when she said something like, “Yes, I know how terribly good-looking I am,” or, “Of course every one is in love with me,” and so forth.
uz: Ko'pincha o'zimni hayratda qoldirib, u shunday so'zlarni aytganda nima demoqchiligini so'radim: "Ha, men qanchalik chiroyli ekanimni bilaman, yoki, albatta, hamma menga muhabbat qiladi va shu kabilar".

en: Her mother was a person always busy, since she had a passion for housekeeping, gardening, flowers, canaries, and pretty trinkets.
uz: Uning onasi har doim mashg'ul bo'lgan, chunki u uy-joyni tozalash, bog'bonlik, gullar, kanarlar va go'zal ziyofatlar bilan shug'ullanish uchun ishtiyoqga ega edi.

en: Her rooms and garden, it is true, were small and poorly fitted-up, yet everything in them was so neat and methodical, and bore such a general air of that gentle gaiety which one hears expressed in a waltz or polka, that the word “toy” by which guests often expressed their praise of it all exactly suited her surroundings.
uz: To'g'ri, uning xonasi va bog'i kichik va yomon jihozlangan edi, ammo ulardagi hamma narsa juda yaxshi va usulli edi va ularda valts yoki polka bilan ifodalangan go'zallik va quvonch kabi umumiy havo bor edi, mehmonlar ko'pincha maqtab, maqtab turgan toy so'zi uning atrofida to'g'ri o'rin olgan.

en: She herself was a “toy”—being petite, slender, fresh-coloured, small, and pretty-handed, and invariably gay and well-dressed.
uz: U o'zi o'yinchi bo'lib, kichkina, chiroyli, rang-barang, kichkina va chiroyli bo'lgan va har doim g'ay va yaxshi kiyimli bo'lgan.

en: The only fault in her was that a slight over-prominence of the dark-blue veins on her little hands rather marred the general effect of her appearance.
uz: Uning yagona kamchiligi shundaki, uning kichik qo'llarida yashil-kungachli idishlarning biroz ko'p ko'rinishi uning tashqi ko'rinishining umumiy ta'sirini buzdi.

en: On the other hand, her daughter scarcely ever did anything at all.
uz: Boshqa tomondan, uning qizi hech qachon hech narsa qilmagan.

en: Not only had she no love for trifling with flowers and trinkets, but she neglected her personal exterior, and only troubled to dress herself well when guests happened to call.
uz: U nafaqat gullar va arzonliklar bilan o'ynashni yoqtirmagan, balki o'z tashqi ko'rinishini e'tiborsiz qoldirgan va mehmonlar qo'ng'iroq qilganda o'zini yaxshi kiyish bilan shug'ullanardi.

en: Yet, on returning to the room in society costume, she always looked extremely handsome—save for that cold, uniform expression of eyes and smile which is common to all beauties.
uz: Biroq, jamiyat kostyumida xonada qaytib kelganida, u har doim juda chiroyli ko'rinardi, faqatgina barcha go'zalliklarga xos bo'lgan sovuq, bir xil ko'z va tabassum ifodasini qo'yib, juda chiroyli ko'rinardi.

en: In fact, her strictly regular, beautiful face and symmetrical figure always seemed to be saying to you, “Yes, you may look at me.” At the same time, for all the mother’s liveliness of disposition and the daughter’s air of indifference and abstraction, something told one that the former was incapable of feeling affection for anything that was not pretty and gay, but that Avdotia, on the contrary, was one of those natures which, once they love, are willing to sacrifice their whole life for the man they adore.
uz: Darhaqiqat, uning qat'iy muntazam, chiroyli yuzi va simmetrik shakli sizga har doim: "Ha, menga qarab ko'rishingiz mumkin. Shu bilan bir vaqtda, onalarning haroratli munosabati va qizlarning befarqlik va o'ziga xoslik havaslariga qaramasdan, kimgadir bir narsa birovga o'zining go'zal va gey bo'lmagan har bir narsaga mehr-muhabbat his qila olmasligini aytadi, lekin Avdotia, aksincha, bir marta sevgan kishi uchun butun hayotini qurbon qilishga tayyor bo'lgan tabiatlardan biri.

en: MY FATHER’S SECOND MARRIAGE MY father was forty-eight when he took as his second wife Avdotia Vassilievna Epifanov.
uz: Otam o'zining ikkinchi xotini Avdotiya Vassilievna Epifanovni o'g'ir cho'qqiz sakkiz yoshda olgan edi.

en: I suspect that when, that spring, he had departed for the country with the girls, he had been in that communicatively happy, sociable mood in which gamblers usually find themselves who have retired from play after winning large stakes.
uz: O'sha bahorda u qizlar bilan qishloqqa ketganda, u o'zini o'yinchilar ko'pincha katta o'yinlarni qo'lga kiritganidan so'ng o'zlaridan haydashgan, muloqotda baxtli va ijtimoiy muhitda bo'lgan deb o'ylayman.

en: He had felt that he still had a fortune left to him which, so long as he did not squander it on gaming, might be used for our advancement in life.
uz: U hali ham o'zidan qolgan boylik borligini his qilgan edi va bu boylik o'yinlarga sarflanmasa, hayotimizda rivojlanish uchun ishlatilishi mumkin edi.

en: Moreover, it was springtime, he was unexpectedly well supplied with ready money, he was alone, and he had nothing to do.
uz: Bundan tashqari, bahor bo'ldi, u kutilmagan darajada tayyor pul bilan ta'minlangan, yolg'iz edi va hech narsa qilmas edi.

en: As he conversed with Jakoff on various matters, and remembered both the interminable suit with the Epifanovs and Avdotia’s beauty (it was a long while since he had seen her), I can imagine him saying: “How do you think we ought to act in this suit, Jakoff?
uz: U Jakoff bilan turli masalalar bo'yicha suhbatlashar ekan va Epifanovlar va Avdotianing go'zalligi bilan bog'liq bo'lgan uzluksiz kostyumni va go'zalligini eslab turar ekan (ularni ko'rmaganidan ko'p vaqt o'tgan edi), uning: "Bu kostyumda qanday yo'l tutishimiz kerak, deb o'ylaysiz, Jakoff?" - deb so'raganini tasavvur qila olaman.

en: My idea is simply to let the cursed land go.
uz: Mening fikrim shunchaki la'natlangan yurtni tark etishdir.

en: What do you think about it?” I can imagine, too, how, thus interrogated, Jakoff twirled his fingers behind his back in a deprecatory sort of way, and proceeded to argue that it all the same, “Peter Alexandritch, we are in the right.” Nevertheless, I further conjecture, Papa ordered the dogcart to be got ready, put on his fashionable olive-coloured driving-coat, brushed up the remnants of his hair, sprinkled his clothes with scent, and, greatly pleased to think that he was acting a la seignior (as well as, even more, revelling in the prospect of soon seeing a pretty woman), drove off to visit his neighbours.
uz: Siz nima deb o'ylaysiz? Men ham tasavvur qila olamanki, shunday so'roq qilinib, Jakoff barmoqlarini orqaga o'girib qo'ydi va hamma narsa bir xil, Peter Alexandritch, biz to'g'ri ekanimizni aytdi. Shunga qaramay, men yana taxmin qilamanki, otam otani tayyorlab qo'yishni buyurdi, o'zining zamonaviy zaytun rangli haydov kiyimini kiydirdi, sochlarining qolgan qismlarini yuvdi, kiyimlarini xushbo'y tutdi va u la seignior sifatida o'ynayotganini ko'rib juda mamnun bo'ldi (va bundan ham ko'proq, yaqinda go'zal ayol bilan ko'rish istiqbolida hayajonlanib) qo'shnilariga tashrif buyurdi.

en: I can imagine, too, that when the flustered housemaid ran to inform Peter Vassilievitch that Monsieur Irtenieff himself had called, Peter answered angrily, “Well, what has he come for?” and, stepping softly about the house, first went into his study to put on his old soiled jacket, and then sent down word to the cook that on no
uz: Men ham tasavvur qila olamanki, xavotirga toʻlgan uy xonadoni Piter Vassilievitchga monsieur Irtenieffning oʻzi qoʻngʻiroq qilganini xabarlash uchun yugurib borganda, Piter gʻazab bilan javob berdi: "U nima uchun kelgan?" Ha, u uyni sekin oʻylab, avval ishxonasiga kirib, eski kirli kiyimini kiyib, soʻngra oshpazga hech qanday gap yoʻqligini aytadi.

en: account whatever—no, not even if she were ordered to do so by the mistress herself—was she to add anything to luncheon.
uz: Nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, hatto xotining o'zi bu ishni buyurgan bo'lsa ham, u tushlikka biron narsa qo'shishi kerak edi.

en: Since, later, I often saw Papa with Peter, I can form a very good idea of this first interview between them.
uz: Keyinchalik men otamni Peter bilan ko'pincha ko'rganim sababli, ular o'rtasidagi birinchi suhbat haqida juda yaxshi tasavvurga ega bo'ldim.

en: I can imagine that, despite Papa’s proposal to end the suit in a peaceful manner, Peter was morose and resentful at the thought of having sacrificed his career to his mother, and at Papa having done nothing of the kind—a by no means surprising circumstance, Peter probably said to himself.
uz: Dadamning kelgusini tinch yo'l bilan tugatish haqidagi taklifidan qat'i nazar, Butrus o'z karerasini onasiga qurbon qilganidan xafa va g'azabga to'lganini tasavvur qila olaman. Dadamning hech narsa qilmagani ajablanarli holatda bo'lmaganida, Butrus, ehtimol, o'ziga shunday dedi.

en: Next, I can see Papa taking no notice of this ill-humour, but cracking quips and jests, while Peter gradually found himself forced to treat him as a humorist with whom he felt offended one moment and inclined to be reconciled the next.
uz: Keyinchalik, dadamni bu yomon humorga e'tibor bermay, faqat g'alati-g'alati gaplarni gapirayotganini ko'rishim mumkin, Butrus esa asta-sekin uni bir vaqtlar xafa bo'lgan, keyingi paytlarda esa yarashishga moyil bo'lgan humorist sifatida qabul qilishga majbur bo'ldi.

en: Indeed, with his instinct for making fun of everything, Papa often used to address Peter as “Colonel;” and though I can remember Peter once replying, with an unusually violent stutter and his face scarlet with indignation, that he had never been a c-c-colonel, but only a l-l-lieutenant, Papa called him “Colonel” again before another five minutes were out.
uz: Darhaqiqat, o'zining hamma narsani masxara qilish instinktlari bilan otam tez-tez Butrusni "Polonel" deb atagan va bir marta Butrus o'zgacha zo'ravon gapirgan va yuzini g'azablangan holda qizargan holda, u hech qachon polkovnik emas, balki faqat l-l-leytenant bo'lganini aytganini eslay olsam ham, otam uni yana "Polonel" deb atagan, yana besh daqiqa o'tmay.

en: Lubotshka told me that, up to the time of Woloda’s and my arrival from Moscow, there had been daily meetings with the Epifanovs, and that things had been very lively, since Papa, who had a genius for arranging, everything with a touch of originality and wit, as well as in a simple and refined manner, had devised shooting and fishing parties and fireworks for the Epifanovs’ benefit.
uz: Lubotshka menga Wolodalar va Moskvadan kelganimga qadar Epifanovlar bilan har kuni uchrashuvlar o'tkazilganligini va bular juda hayajonli bo'lganini aytdi, chunki o'zining g'ayrioddiy rejasi bo'lgan ota, har bir narsani o'ziga xos xususiyat va aqllilik bilan, shuningdek, sodda va sof tarzda Epifanovlar uchun o'yin-kulgi, baliq ovlash ziyofatlari va o't qo'zg'atishlarini rejalashtirgan edi.

en: All these festivities— so said Lubotshka—would have gone off splendidly but for the intolerable Peter, who had spoilt everything by his puffing and stuttering.
uz: Lubotshka aytganidek, bu bayramlarning hammasi ajoyib bo'lib ketar edi, lekin bu borada o'zining puflashi va gapirishlari bilan hamma narsani buzib qo'ygan ko'rqoq Butrus uchun edi.

en: After our coming, however, the Epifanovs only visited us twice, and we went once to their house, while after St.
uz: Biroq, biz kelganimizdan keyin Epifanovlar bizga faqat ikki marta tashrif buyurishdi va biz bir marta ularning uyiga bordik, ammo St.

en: Peter’s Day (on which, it being Papa’s nameday, the Epifanovs called upon us in common with a crowd of other guests) our relations with that family came entirely to an end, and, in future, only Papa went to see them.
uz: Butrus kunida (Butalar kunida Epifanovlar boshqa mehmonlar bilan birga bizni chaqirdilar) o'sha oila bilan munosabatlarimiz to'liq tugadi va kelajakda ularni faqat ota ko'rish uchun boradi.

en: During the brief period when I had opportunities of seeing Papa and Dunetchka (as her mother called Avdotia) together, this is what I remarked about them.
uz: Dadam va Dunetchka (uning onasi Avdotia deb atagan) bilan birga ko'rish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lgan qisqa davrda men ular haqida shularni aytdim.

en: Papa remained unceasingly in the same buoyant mood as had so greatly struck me on the day after our arrival.
uz: Otam biz kelgan kundan keyingi kuni meni juda hayratda qoldirgan o'sha quvonchli ruhda to'xtamaydi.

en: So gay and youthful and full of life and happy did he seem that the beams of his felicity extended themselves to all around him, and involuntarily communicated to them a similar frame of mind.
uz: U shunchalik gey, yosh, hayotga to'la va baxtli ko'rinardiki, uning baxtiyorligi nurlari atrofidagilarga tarqalib, ularga ixtiyoriy ravishda o'xshash fikr-mulohazalarni bildiradi.

en: never stirred from Avdotia’s side so long as she was in the room, but either kept on plying her with sugary-sweet compliments which made me feel ashamed for him or, with his gaze fixed upon her with an air at once passionate and complacent, sat hitching his shoulder and coughing as from time to time he smiled and whispered something in her ear.
uz: Avdotia xonadonida bo'lganida, u Avdotiyaning yonidan harakatlanardi, lekin u menga u uchun o'zimni o'zimdan o'zimni o'ylaydigan shakarli-zo'rli tabriklar bilan o'zini to'ldirib turardi yoki, uning ko'z o'ziga bir vaqtning o'zida ishtiyoqli va o'z-o'zidan mamnun bo'lgan havo bilan unga qaragan holda, o'zini ko'tarib o'tirardi va qo'shardi, chunki vaqti-vaqti bilan u hech qachon tabassum qilmasdi va uning quloqlariga biror narsa shoshar qilmasdi.

en: Yet throughout he wore the same expression of raillery as was peculiar to him even in the most serious matters.
uz: Ammo u har safar, hatto eng jiddiy masalalarda ham o'ziga xos bo'lgan haqoratni ko'rsatgan.

en: As a rule, Avdotia herself seemed to catch the infection of the happiness which sparkled at this period in Papa’s large blue eyes; yet there were moments also when she would be seized with such a fit of shyness that I, who knew the feeling well, was full of sympathy and compassion as I regarded her embarrassment.
uz: Odatda, Avdotiya o'zi bu davrda otasining katta ko'k ko'zlarida parcha-parcha bo'lgan baxtning yuqumli kasalligiga duchor bo'lib tuyuladi; ammo u o'zini shunday uyatli his qilgan paytlar ham bo'lganki, o'zim o'zimni yaxshi bilgan holda uning noqulayligini ko'rib, samimiylik va rahm-shafqatga to'ldim.

en: At moments of this kind she seemed to be afraid of every glance and every movement—to be supposing that every one was looking at her, every one thinking of no one but her, and that unfavourably.
uz: Bunday paytlarda u har bir ko'z va har bir harakatdan qo'rqadi, chunki hamma uning ko'z o'ngida, har bir kishi o'zidan boshqa hech kim haqida o'ylamaydi, deb o'ylaydi.

en: She would glance timidly from one person to another, the colour coming and going in her cheeks, and then begin to talk loudly and defiantly, but, for the most part, nonsense; until presently, realising this, and supposing that Papa and every one else had heard her, she would blush more painfully than ever.
uz: U qo'rqinchli tarzda bir odamdan boshqasiga qarab turardi, uning yiqlarida rang kelib-ketardi, so'ngra baland ovozda va qarshilik ko'rsatgan holda gapira boshladi, ammo ko'p hollarda bu g'alati so'zlar edi; hozirgacha buni anglab, va otasi va boshqalarning hammasi uni eshitganini tasavvur qilib, u har qachongidan ham og'irroq qizar edi.

en: Yet Papa never noticed her nonsense, for he was too much taken up with coughing and with gazing at her with his look of happy, triumphant devotion.
uz: Ammo otam uning bejizligiga hech qachon e'tibor bermadi, chunki u juda ko'p qo'shnichilik va baxtli, g'alaba qozonadigan sadoqat ko'rinishi bilan unga qaraydi.

en: I noticed, too, that, although these fits of shyness attacked Avdotia, without any visible cause, they not infrequently ensued upon Papa’s mention of one or another young and beautiful woman.
uz: Shuningdek, men shuni ham payqadimki, agar bu o'rinsizlik Avdotiyaga hech qanday sababsiz hujum qilgan bo'lsa-da, ular ko'pincha o'sha yosh va chiroyli ayol haqida Papa aytganida davom etardi.

en: Frequent transitions from depression to that strange, awkward gaiety of hers to which I have referred before the repetition of favourite words and turns of speech of Papa’s; the continuation of discussions with others which Papa had already begun—all these things, if my father had not been the principal actor in the matter and I had been a little older, would have explained to me the relations subsisting between him and Avdotia.
uz: Dadamning sevimli so'zlari va nutqlarining takrorlanishiga qadar aytganimdek, tez-tez depressiyadan uning o'zgacha, noqulay quvonchlariga o'tadigan o'zgarishlar; boshqa odamlar bilan suhbatlarning davom etishi, chunki Dadam allaqachon bu ishlarni boshlagan edi, agar dadam bu masalada asosiy ishtirokchi bo'lmagan va men biroz katta bo'lganimda, u bilan Avdotiya o'rtasidagi munosabatlarni menga tushuntirib bergan bo'lar edi.

en: At the time, however, I never surmised them—no, not even when Papa received from her brother Peter a letter which so upset him that not again until the end of August did he go to call upon the Epifanovs’.
uz: Biroq, o'sha paytda men ularni hech qachon gumon qilmaganman, hatto otam ukasi Piterdan uni shunchalik xafa qilgan xat olganda ham, avgust oyining oxirigacha Epifanovlarni chaqirishga bormagan.

en: Then, however, he began his visits once more, and ended by informing us, on the day before Woloda and I were to
uz: Biroq, u yana bir bor tashrif buyurishni boshladi va Woloda va men ketishdan bir kun oldin bizni xabardor qildi.

en: return to Moscow, that he was about to take Avdotia Vassilievna Epifanov to be his wife.
uz: Moskvaga qaytish uchun Avdotiya Vasilievna Epifanovni xotinlikka olishni rejalashtirganini aytdi.

en: HOW WE RECEIVED THE NEWS Yet, even on the eve of the official announcement, every one had learnt of the matter, and was discussing it.
uz: Qanday qilib biz yangilikni qabul qildik Ammo, hatto rasmiy e'lon qilish arafasida ham hamma bu haqda bilib, muhokama qilishgan.

en: Mimi never left her room that day, and wept copiously.
uz: Mimi o'sha kuni o'z xonasidan chiqmadi va ko'p yig'ladi.

en: Katenka kept her company, and only came out for luncheon, with a grieved expression on her face which was manifestly borrowed from her mother.
uz: Katenka do'stligini saqlab, faqat kechki ovqatga chiqdi, uning yuziga o'z onasidan qarz olgandan ko'rinib turibdi.

en: Lubotshka, on the contrary, was very cheerful, and told us after luncheon that she knew of a splendid secret which she was going to tell no one.
uz: Aksincha, Lubotshka juda quvonchli bo'lib, kechki ovqatdan so'ng hech kimga aytmaydigan ajoyib sirni bilishini aytdi.

en: “There is nothing so splendid about your secret,” said Woloda, who did not in the least share her satisfaction.
uz: Sizning siringizda hech qanday ajoyib narsa yo'q, dedi Woloda, u hech qachon uning mamnuniyatini baham ko'rmadi.

en: “If you were capable of any serious thought at all, you would understand that it is a very bad lookout for us.” Lubotshka stared at him in amazement, and said no more.
uz: Agar siz jiddiy o'ylashga qodir bo'lsangiz, bu biz uchun juda yomon qarash ekanligini tushunasiz. Lubotshka uni hayron ko'rib, o'zini to'xtatdi.

en: After the meal was over, Woloda made a feint of taking me by the arm, and then, fearing that this would seem too much like “affection,” nudged me gently by the elbow, and beckoned me towards the salon.
uz: Ovqat tugaganidan so'ng, Voloda meni qo'limdan ushlab olishni so'zlab berdi va keyin, bu juda mehribonlikka o'xshaydi deb qo'rqqan holda, meni yonboshiga yumshatdi va salonga yo'naltirdi.

en: “You know, I suppose, what the secret is of which Lubotshka was speaking?” he said when he was sure that we were alone.
uz: Lubotshka gapirgan sir nima ekanligini bilasizmi? U biz yolg'iz ekanligimizga amin bo'lganida shunday dedi.

en: It was seldom that he and I spoke together in confidence: with the result that, whenever it came about, we felt a kind of awkwardness in one another’s presence, and “boys began to jump about” in our eyes, as Woloda expressed it.
uz: U va men kamdan-kam bir vaqtlar o'zaro ishonch bilan gaplashardik: natijada, har safar bir-birimizning oldimizda bir xil noqulaylikni his qilardik va Voloda aytganidek, yigitlar ko'zlarimizga o'tib o'tishni boshlashdi.

en: On the present occasion, however, he answered the excitement in my eyes with a grave, fixed look which
uz: Biroq, hozirgi paytda u mening ko'zimdagi hayajonga jiddiy, qat'iy ko'z bilan javob berdi.

en: said: “You need not be surprised, for we are brothers, and we have to consider an important family matter.” I understood him, and he went on: “You know, I suppose, that Papa is going to marry Avdotia Epifanov?” I nodded, for I had already heard so.
uz: U shunday dedi: Siz hayron bo'lmasligingiz kerak, chunki biz aka-ukalarmiz va muhim oilaviy masalalarni ko'rib chiqishimiz kerak. Men uni tushunib oldim va u davom etdi: Siz bilasanmi, dadam Avdotiya Epifanov bilan turmushga chiqishini? Men boshimni yumdim, chunki men buni allaqachon eshitgan edim.

en: “Well, it is not a good thing,” continued Woloda.
uz: Ha, bu yaxshi narsa emas, davom etdi Woloda.

en: “Why so?” “Why?” he repeated irritably.
uz: Nima uchun shunday? nima uchun? u g'azablanarli tarzda takrorladi.

en: “Because it will be so pleasant, won’t it, to have this stuttering ‘colonel’ and all his family for relations!
uz: Buning o'zi juda yoqimli bo'ladi, shunday emasmi?Bu gapiradigan kolonel va uning butun oilasi bilan munosabatlar o'rnatish uchun!

en: Certainly she seems nice enough, as yet; but who knows what she will turn out to be later?
uz: Shubhasiz, hozircha u juda yaxshi ko'rinadi; lekin keyinchalik u nima bo'lishi mumkinligini kim biladi?

en: It won’t matter much to you or myself, but Lubotshka will soon be making her debut, and it will hardly be nice for her to have such a ‘belle mere’ as this—a woman who speaks French badly, and has no manners to teach her.” Although it seemed odd to hear Woloda criticising Papa’s choice so coolly, I felt that he was right.
uz: Siz yoki men uchun bu juda muhim emas, lekin Lubotshka yaqinda debuteringni boshlaydi va u uchun bu kabi chiroyli ayolga ega bo'lish yaxshi emas.Bu ayol fransuz tilida yomon gapiradi va unga o'rgatish uchun odob-axloqga ega emas.Woloda o'z tanlovi haqida so'nggi paytlarda so'nggi marta tanqid qilganini eshitish g'alati tuyulsa-da, men uning to'g'ri fikrda bo'lganini his qildim.

en: “Why is he marrying her?” I asked.
uz: Nima uchun u qiz bilan turmushga chiqyapti? - deb so'radim.

en: “Oh, it is a hole-and-corner business, and God only knows why,” he answered.
uz: "Oh, bu do'zax va burchak ishi va faqat Xudo biladi nima uchun", - deb javob berdi u.

en: “All I know is that her brother, Peter, tried to make conditions about the marriage, and that, although at first Papa would not hear of them, he afterwards took some fancy or knight-errantry or another into his head.
uz: Men bilganim shundaki, uning ukasi Piter nikoh uchun shart-sharoitlar yaratishga harakat qildi va boshida Papa bu haqda eshitmagan bo'lsa-da, keyinchalik u o'ziga biroz hayajonli yoki qahatchilik yoki boshqa narsalarni o'z ichiga oldi.

en: But, as I say, it is a hole-and-corner business.
uz: Ammo, aytganimdek, bu hol va burchak biznesidir.

en: I am only just beginning to understand my father “—the fact that Woloda called Papa “my father” instead of “Papa” somehow hurt me —“and though I can see that he is kind and clever, he is irresponsible and frivolous to a degree that—Well, the whole thing is astonishing.
uz: Men otamning o'g'lini tushunishni boshlayapman Woloda meni Papa ning o'rniga Papa o'g'lim deb ataganligi o'g'lim meni qandaydir tarzda ranjitganligini tushunib yetyapman va men uning mehribon va aqlli ekanligini ko'rishim mumkin bo'lsa-da, u mas'uliyatsiz va g'alati darajada o'zidan-o'zini mahrum qiladi.Hamma narsa hayratlanarli.

en: He cannot so much as look upon a woman calmly.
uz: U hatto ayolga tinchlik bilan qaray olmaydi.

en: You yourself know how he falls in love with every one that he meets.
uz: O'zingiz bilasiz, u uchratgan har bir kishiga qanday qilib muhabbatga tushadi.

en: You know it, and so does Mimi.” “What do you mean?” I said.
uz: Siz buni bilasiz va Mimi ham biladi.  Nima deyapsiz? dedim men.

en: Not long ago I learnt that he used to be in love with Mimi herself when he was a young man, and that he used to send her poetry, and that there really was something between them.
uz: Yaqinda o'zim bildimki, u yosh bo'lganida Mimiga muhabbat qilardi va unga she'rlar yuborardi va ular o'rtasida bir narsa borligini bilib oldim.

en: Mimi is heart-sore about it to this day”—and Woloda burst out laughing.
uz: Mimi shu kungacha bu haqda qayg'uradi va Woloda kulish bilan o'zicha ko'tarildi.

en: “Impossible!” I cried in astonishment.
uz: Impossible! Men hayratda yig'ladim.

en: “But the principal thing at this moment,” went on Woloda, becoming serious again, and relapsing into French, “is to think how delighted all our relations will be with this marriage!
uz: Ammo hozirgi paytda eng muhim narsa - Voloda yana jiddiylashib, fransuz tiliga qaytish - bu nikoh bilan barcha munosabatlarimiz qanchalik quvonchli bo'lishini o'ylashdir!

en: Why, she will probably have children!” Woloda’s prudence and forethought struck me so forcibly that I had no answer to make.
uz: Ehtimol, u farzand ko'radi! Woloda'ning aql-idrok va oldindan o'ylab ko'rish menga shunchalik qattiq ta'sir qildiki, javob berishim mumkin emas edi.

en: Just at this moment Lubotshka approached us.
uz: Shu payt Lubotshka bizga yaqinlashdi.

en: “So you know?” she said with a joyful face.
uz: Shuning o'zi bilasizmi? - dedi u quvonchli yuz bilan.

en: “Still, I am surprised at you, Lubotshka.
uz: Hamma shu bilan birga, men sizdan hayratda qoldim, Lubotshka.

en: You are no longer a baby in long clothes.
uz: Siz endi uzoq kiyimda chaqaloq emassiz.

en: Why should you be so pleased because Papa is going to marry a piece of trash?” At this Lubotshka’s face fell, and she became serious.
uz: Nima uchun ota axlatga uylanayotganidan xursand bo'lishingiz kerak? Shu payt Lubotshkaning yuzi tushib qoldi va u jiddiy bo'ldi.

en: “Oh, Woloda!” she exclaimed.
uz: Oh, Voloda! deb hayqirdi u.

en: “Why ‘a piece of trash’ indeed?
uz: Nima uchun chindan ham chiqindi bo'lib qolmoqda?

en: How can you dare to speak of Avdotia like that?
uz: Avdotiya haqida bunday gapirishga qanday jasorat qila olasiz?

en: If Papa is going to marry her she cannot be ‘trash.’” “No, not trash, so to speak, but—” “No ‘buts’ at all!” interrupted Lubotshka, flaring up.
uz: Agar otam unga turmushga chiqsa, u qaroqsiz bo'lishi mumkin emas.Yo'q, qaroqsiz emas, demak, lekinYog'i yo'q! Lubotshka o'zini to'xtatdi va yonib ketdi.

en: “You have never heard me call the girl whom you are in love with ‘trash!’ How, then, can you speak so of Papa and a respectable woman?
uz: Siz sevgan qizingizni hech qachon "quroq" deb ataganimni eshitmagansiz! Unda qanday qilib siz otangiz va hurmatli ayol haqida shunday gapirishingiz mumkin?

en: Although you are my elder brother, I won’t allow you to speak like that!
uz: Garchi siz mening katta akam bo'lsangiz ham, men sizga shunday gapirishga ruxsat bermayman!

en: You ought not to!” “Mayn’t I even express an opinion about—” “No, you mayn’t!” repeated Lubotshka.
uz: Siz bunday qilmasligingiz kerak! Maynt Men hatto mening fikrimni bildiraman Yo'q, siz maynt! Lubotshka takrorladi.

en: “No one ought to criticise such a father as ours.
uz: Hech kim o'z otamiz kabi o'g'lini tanqid qilmasligi kerak.

en: Mimi has the right to, but not you, however much you may be the eldest brother.” “Oh you don’t understand anything,” said Woloda contemptuously.
uz: Mimi bunga haqli, lekin siz bunga haqli emassiz.Siz hech narsani tushunmayapsiz, - dedi Voloda hurmatsizlik bilan.

en: How can it be a good thing that a ‘Dunetchka’ of an Epifanov should take the place of our dead Mamma?” For a moment Lubotshka was silent.
uz: Qanday qilib Epifanovning Dunetchka o'rinbosari o'lgan onamizning o'rnini egallashi yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin? Lubotshka bir daqiqa davomida sukut saqladi.

en: Then the tears suddenly came into her eyes.
uz: Keyin uning ko'zlariga ko'z yoshlari to'kildi.

en: “I knew that you were conceited, but I never thought that you could be cruel,” she said, and left us.
uz: "Sening mag'rur ekaningni bilar edim, lekin hech qachon shafqatsiz bo'lishingni o'ylamagan edim", - dedi u va bizni tashlab ketdi.

en: “Pshaw!” said Woloda, pulling a serio-comic face and make- believe, stupid eyes.
uz: Pshaw! dedi Woloda, jiddiy-komik yuz va o'ylaydigan, ahmoqona ko'zlar bilan.

en: “That’s what comes of arguing with them.” Evidently he felt that he was at fault in having so far forgot himself as to descend to discuss matters at all with Lubotshka.
uz: Bu ular bilan bahslashishdan kelib chiqadi. U o'zini Lubotshka bilan suhbatlashishga tushish uchun o'zini unutib qo'yganida o'zini aybdor his qilgan.

en: Next day the weather was bad, and neither Papa nor the ladies had come down to morning tea when I entered the drawing-room.
uz: Ertasi kuni havo yomon edi va men o'sha zalga kirganimda, dadam ham, qizlar ham ertalab choy ichishga tushmagan edilar.

en: There had been cold rain in the night, and remnants of the clouds from which it had descended were still scudding across the sky, with the sun’s luminous disc (not yet risen to any great height) showing faintly through them.
uz: Kechasi sovuq yomg'ir yog'gan edi va u tushgan bulutlarning qoldiqlari hali ham osmon bo'ylab ko'tarilgan edi, quyoshning yorug' disklari (hozirgacha hech qanday balandlikka ko'tarilmagan) ular orqali samarasiz ko'rinardi.

en: It was a windy, damp, grey morning.
uz: Bu shamolli, nam, oq ertalab edi.

en: The door into the garden was standing open, and pools left by the night’s rain were drying on the damp-blackened flags of the terrace.
uz: Bog'ning eshiklari ochiq turgan edi va kechasi yomg'ir yog'ib qolgan hovuzlar terasaning boshoq qoralashgan bayroqlari ustida qurib ketar edi.

en: The open door was swinging on its iron hinges in the wind, and all the paths looked wet and muddy.
uz: Ochiq eshik shamolda temir pishirgichlarida aylanib borar edi va barcha yo'llar issiq va loydan ko'rinardi.

en: The old birch trees with their naked white branches, the bushes, the turf, the nettles, the currant-trees, the elders with the pale side of their leaves turned upwards—all were dashing themselves about, and looking as though they were trying to wrench themselves free from their roots.
uz: Oʻzlarining yalangʻoch oq shoxlari boʻlgan eski birka daraxtlari, butalar, oʻtlar, yirtqichlar, oʻsimlik daraxtlari, barglari yuqoriga oʻgirilgan rang-barang boʻlgan keksalar oʻz-oʻzlarini koʻtarib, xuddi oʻzlarining ildizlaridan ozod boʻlishga harakat qilayotganlardek koʻrinardi.

en: From the avenue of lime- trees showers of round, yellow leaves were flying through the air in tossing, eddying circles, and strewing the wet road and soaked aftermath of the hayfield with a clammy carpet.
uz: O'z yo'lidan o'tgach, o'tlar yog'di, sariq barglar havo bo'ylab o'tadi, o'tlar aylanardi va suyuq yo'lni va cho'g'li cho'g'idan sotilgan ko'chma maydonni bo'lak-bo'lak bilan qoplab qo'ydi.

en: At the moment, my thoughts were wholly taken up with my father’s approaching marriage and with the point of view from which Woloda regarded it.
uz: O'sha paytda mening fikrlarim otamning yaqinlashib kelayotgan nikohi va Woloda uni qanday ko'rib turganidan iborat edi.

en: The future seemed to me to bode no good for any of us.
uz: Kelajak hech birimiz uchun hech qanday yaxshilik keltirib chiqarmasdek tuyuldi.

en: I felt distressed to think that a woman who was not only a stranger but young should be going to associate with us in so many relations of life, without having any right to do so—nay, that this young woman was going to usurp the place of our dead mother.
uz: Oʻshanda men nafaqat begona, balki yosh bir ayol biz bilan shunchacha hayot munosabatlarida aloqada boʻlishi kerakligini, buning uchun hech qanday huquqga ega boʻlmasligini, bu yosh ayol oʻlgan onamizning oʻrnini egallashi kerakligini oʻylashdan xafa boʻldim.

en: I felt depressed, and kept thinking more and more that my father was to blame in the matter.
uz: Men tushkunlikka tushdim va o'zimning dadamning aybdor ekanligimni ko'proq o'yladim.

en: Presently I heard his voice and Woloda’s speaking together in the pantry, and, not wishing to meet Papa just then, had just left the room when I was pursued by Lubotshka, who said that Papa wanted to see me.
uz: O'sha paytda men uning ovozini va Wolodalarni oshxonada birgalikda gapirayotganini eshitdim va o'sha paytda otamni uchratishni istamagan bo'lsam ham, Lubotshka meni quvg'in qilib, otam meni ko'rishni xohlaganini aytdi.

en: He was standing in the drawing-room, with his hand resting on the piano, and was gazing in my direction with an air at once grave and impatient.
uz: U o'tirish xonasida qo'li klaviatura ustida turib, yonimga bir vaqtning o'zida og'ir va sabrsizlik bilan qaragan edi.

en: His face no longer wore the youthful, gay expression which had struck me for so long, but, on the contrary, looked sad.
uz: Uning yuzi meni shuncha vaqtdan beri hayratda qoldirgan yoshlik va geyimlik ifodasini ko'rmadi, aksincha, u qayg'uli ko'rinishga ega edi.

en: Woloda was walking about the room with a pipe in his hand.
uz: Woloda o'z qo'lida quvur bilan xona atrofida yuribdi.

en: I approached my father, and bade him good morning.
uz: Men otamga yaqinlashib, unga salom so'radim.

en: “Well, my children,” he said firmly, with a lift of his head and in the peculiarly hurried manner of one who wishes to announce something
uz: Eh, farzandlarim, dedi u qat'iylik bilan, boshini ko'targan holda va biror narsa e'lon qilishni istagan kishi kabi g'ayratli tarzda.

en: obviously unwelcome, but no longer admitting of reconsideration, “you know, I suppose, that I am going to marry Avdotia Epifanov.” He paused a moment.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, bu xush kelmagan, ammo endi qayta ko'rib chiqishni tan olmagan, siz bilaman, men Avdotiya Epifanov bilan turmushga chiqaman. U biroz to'xtadi.

en: “Hitherto I had had no desire for any one to succeed your mother, but”—and again he paused—“it-it is evidently my fate.
uz: Hozirgacha onangizning o'rnini hech kim egallashiga umidim yo'q edi, lekin u yana to'xtatdi - bu mening taqdirim.

en: Dunetchka is an excellent, kind girl, and no longer in her first youth.
uz: Dunetchka ajoyib, mehribon qiz va endi yoshligida emas.

en: I hope, therefore, my children, that you will like her, and she, I know, will be sincerely fond of you, for she is a good woman.
uz: Shunday qilib, farzandlarim, uni yoqtirishni umid qilaman va u sizlarni chin dildan sevishini bilaman, chunki u yaxshi ayol.

en: And now,” he went on, addressing himself more particularly to Woloda and myself, and having the appearance of speaking hurriedly in order to prevent us from interrupting him, “it is time for you to depart, while I myself am going to stay here until the New Year, and then to follow you to Moscow with”—again he hesitated a moment—“my wife and Lubotshka.” It hurt me to see my father standing as though abashed and at fault before us, so I moved a little nearer him, but Woloda only went on walking about the room with his head down, and smoking.
uz: Va endi, u davom etdi, o'zini Woloda va menga ko'proq murojaat qilib, bizni unga aralashtirmaslik uchun shoshilinch gapiradigan ko'rinishga ega bo'ldi, sen ketish vaqti keldi, men esa yangi yilga qadar bu yerda qolishim kerak, so'ngra sizni Moskvaga kuzatib borish uchun yana bir marta o'z xotini va Lubotshka bilan bir zumda shubha qildi. Otamni o'zimiz oldida o'tirib ko'rganimda, uyalgan va aybdor bo'lib qolganimni ko'rish menga og'ri keldi, shuning uchun men unga biroz yaqinlashdim, lekin Woloda faqat boshini past olib, xonada yurishni davom ettirdi va chekardi.

en: “So, my children, that is what your old father has planned to do,” concluded Papa—reddening, coughing, and offering Woloda and myself his hands.
uz: Shunday qilib, farzandlarim, bu sizning otangizning rejalashtirgan ishidir, so'ng Papa reddening, toshqining va Woloda va men uchun qo'llarini taklif qildi.

en: Tears were in his eyes as he said this, and I noticed, too, that the hand which he was holding out to Woloda (who at that moment chanced to be at the other end of the room) was shaking slightly.
uz: U buni aytganida ko'zlarida yoshlar bor edi va men ham uning Wolodaga (o'sha paytda xonaning boshqa tomoniga o'tirgan) uzatgan qo'li biroz titrab turganini payqadim.

en: The sight of that shaking hand gave me an unpleasant shock, for I remembered that Papa had served in ൢ൩ൢൣ, and had been, as every one knew, a brave officer.
uz: O'sha qo'l shovqinini ko'rib, men yoqimsiz hayratga tushdim, chunki otamning da xizmat qilganini va hamma bilganidek, jasoratli ofitser bo'lganini esladim.

en: Seizing the great veiny hand, I covered it with kisses, and he squeezed mine hard in return.
uz: Men ulkan jonli qo'lni ushlab, uni o'pish bilan qopladim va u o'zimning qo'limni qattiq siqdi.

en: Then, with a sob amid his tears, he suddenly threw his arms around Lubotshka’s dark head, and kissed her again and again on the eyes.
uz: Keyin, ko'z yoshlari orasida yig'lab, u to'satdan Lubotshkaning qorong'i boshiga qo'llarini tashlab, uning ko'zlariga qayta-qayta o'pdi.

en: Woloda pretended that he had dropped his pipe, and, bending down, wiped his eyes furtively with the back of his hand.
uz: Woloda o'zining quvurini pastga tushirganini ko'rsatdi va egri bo'lib, o'z ko'zlarini o'z qo'li bilan o'chirib yubordi.

en: Then, endeavouring to escape notice, he left the room.
uz: Keyin, e'tibordan qochishga harakat qilib, xonani tark etdi.

en: THE wedding was to take place in two weeks’ time, but, as our lectures had begun already, Woloda and myself were forced to return to Moscow at the beginning of September.
uz: TUYN ikki haftadan keyin o'tkaziladigan edi, ammo darslar boshlanayotgan bo'lgani uchun, Voloda va men sentyabr oyining boshida Moskvaga qaytishga majbur bo'ldik.

en: The Nechludoffs had also returned from the country, and Dimitri (with whom, on parting, I had made an agreement that we should correspond frequently with the result, of course, that we had never once written to one another) came to see us immediately after our arrival, and arranged to escort me to my first lecture on the morrow.
uz: Nechludofflar ham mamlakatdan qaytib kelgan edilar va Dimitri (men u bilan ajrashganimda tez-tez xat yozish kerakligini va natijada, albatta, biz bir-birimizga hech qachon yozmaganimizni) kelgach bizni ko'rish uchun keldi va ertasiga meni birinchi nutqimga eskirishga tayyorladi.

en: It was a beautiful sunny day.
uz: Bu chiroyli quyoshli kun edi.

en: No sooner had I entered the auditorium than I felt my personality entirely disappear amid the swarm of light-hearted youths who were seething tumultuously through every doorway and corridor under the influence of the sunlight pouring through the great windows.
uz: Auditoriyaga kirganimdan so'ng, har bir eshik va koridorda quyosh nurining ta'siri ostida katta darchalardan oqib ketayotgan bir to'plam yumshoq yoshlar orasida o'zimning shaxsiyatim butunlay yo'qolganini his qildim.

en: I found the sense of being a member of this huge community very pleasing, yet there were few among the throng whom I knew, and that only on terms of a nod and a “How do you do, Irtenieff?” All around me men were shaking hands and chatting together— from every side came expressions of friendship, laughter, jests, and badinage.
uz: Ushbu ulkan jamoaning a'zosi bo'lish hissi menga juda yoqdi, ammo men bilgan ko'pchilik orasida faqatgina bir necha kishi bor edi va bu faqat bir bosh ko'tarish va bir Siz qanday, Irtenieff? Men atrofimda erkaklar qo'l urib suhbatlashayotgan edi Har tomondan do'stlik, kulgi, maza va badinage ifodalari paydo bo'lgan.
