en: We had much better stay HERE and talk.” I scarcely relished the prospect of spending a couple of hours in Bezobiedoff’s company, yet could not make up my mind to go down alone; wherefore, cursing my friend’s vagaries, I seated myself in a rocking-chair, and began rocking myself silently to and fro.
uz: Bu yerda qolsak yaxshi bo'lardi. Men bir necha soat Bezobiedoff kompaniyasida o'tkazishni yoqtirmasdim, ammo yolg'iz tushishga qaror qilolmasdim; shuning uchun do'stimning g'alati-g'alatilarini la'natlab, o'zimni ko'chma-ko'chma o'tirishga o'tirdim va o'zimni bir-biridan siljashga boshladim.

en: I felt vexed with them both for depriving me of the pleasures of the drawing-room, and my only hope as I listened irritably to their conversation was that Bezobiedoff would soon take his departure.
uz: Ikkalasi ham meni o'tirish xonasining zavq-shafqatidan mahrum qilganlari uchun o'zimni xafa his qilardim va ularning suhbatini g'azabga to'la tinglaganimda, faqatgina Bezobiedoff tez orada ketishi mumkinligini umid qilardim.

en: “A nice guest indeed to be sitting with!” I thought to myself when a footman brought in tea and Dimitri had five times to beg Bezobiedoff to have a cup, for the reason that the bashful guest thought it incumbent upon him always to refuse it at first and to say, “No, help yourself.” I could see that Dimitri had to put some restraint upon himself as he resumed the conversation.
uz: Haqiqatan ham o'tirishga yoqimli mehmon! Men o'zimga o'yladim, bir xizmatkor choy olib kelganida va Dimitri besh marta Bezobiedoffga bir qadah berishini iltijo qilganida, uyatchan mehmon uni boshida doim rad etish va o'z-o'zidan yordam berish vazifasini o'z zimmasiga olgan deb o'yladi.Yo'q, o'zingizga yordam bering. Dimitri suhbatni davom ettirganida o'z-o'ziga kamroq bosim o'tkazishi kerakligini ko'rdim.

en: He tried to inveigle me also into it, but I remained glum and silent.
uz: U meni ham unga jalb qilishga urindi, lekin men tushkun va sukut saqlashdim.

en: “I do not mean to let my face give any one the suspicion that I am bored” was my mental remark to Dimitri as I sat quietly rocking myself to and fro with measured beat.
uz: Men hech kimga o'zimni charchatib qo'yishni xohlamayman Dimitriga o'tirganimda, o'zimni o'zimning o'zimga o'xshatib, o'zimni o'lchovli ritm bilan sakrab-sakrab o'tirganimda, men o'zimni charchatib qo'yishim kerak edi.

en: Yet, as the moments passed, I found myself—not without a certain satisfaction—growing more and
uz: Ammo vaqt o'tgach, o'zimni mamnuniyatsiz his qilib, ko'proq va ko'proq o'sib borayotganini ko'rdim.

en: more inwardly hostile to my friend.
uz: Do'stimga nisbatan ichkilik bilan ko'proq dushman.

en: “What a fool he is!” I reflected.
uz: U qanday ahmoq! - deb o'yladim men o'zim.

en: “He might be spending the evening agreeably with his charming family, yet he goes on sitting with this brute!—will go on doing so, too, until it is too late to go down to the drawing-room!” Here I glanced at him over the back of my chair, and thought the general look of his attitude and appearance so offensive and repellant that at the moment I could gladly have offered him some insult, even a most serious one.
uz: U o'zining chiroyli oilasi bilan kechani yoqimli o'tkazishi mumkin, ammo u bu vahshiy bilan o'tirishni davom ettiradi!Jannatga tushish juda kech bo'lmaguncha, u ham shunday qilishni davom ettiradi! Mana, men uning ko'z o'ng tomonini o'zimning o'rinchimdan ko'rdim va uning umumiy nuqtai nazari va ko'rinishi shunchalik tajovuzkorlik va qo'rqinchli deb o'yladimki, hozirda men unga hatto eng jiddiy haqoratni taklif qilishim mumkin edi.

en: At last Bezobiedoff rose, but Dimitri could not easily let such a delightful friend depart, and asked him to stay the night.
uz: Oxir-oqibat Bezobiedoff o'rnidan turibdi, lekin Dimitri shunchalik yoqimli do'stiga osonlikcha qo'yib berolmadi va undan kechasi qolishini so'radi.

en: Fortunately, Bezobiedoff declined the invitation, and departed.
uz: Yaxshiyamki, Bezobiedoff taklifni rad etib, jo'nab ketdi.

en: Having seen him off, Dimitri returned, and, smiling a faintly complacent smile as he did so, and rubbing his hands together (in all probability partly because he had sustained his character for eccentricity, and partly because he had got rid of a bore), started to pace the room, with an occasional glance at myself.
uz: Uni ko'rgach, Dimitri qaytib keldi va o'zini o'zi bilmagan tabassum bilan tabassum qilib, qo'llarini bir-biriga burib qo'ydi (aslida o'zining xarakterini o'ziga xosligi uchun saqlab qolganligi va ba'zi bir qismida charchaganligi sababli), xonani o'zgartira boshladi va vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zimga qarab turardi.

en: I felt more offended with him than ever.
uz: Men u bilan o'zimni har qachongidan ham ko'proq xafa his qildim.

en: “How can he go on walking about the room and grinning like that?” was my inward reflection.
uz: Qanday qilib u xonadon atrofida yurib, shunday tabassum qila oladi? - bu mening ichki o'yishim edi.

en: “What are you so angry about?” he asked me suddenly as he halted in front of my chair.
uz: Nima uchun shunchalik g'azablanasiz? deb so'radi mendan birdan, o'rinchimning oldida to'xtab turganda.

en: “I am not in the least angry,” I replied (as people always do answer under such circumstances).
uz: Men hech qachon g'azablanmayman, deb javob berdim (chunki odamlar bunday holatlarda har doim javob berishadi).

en: “I am merely vexed that you should play- act to me, and to Bezobiedoff, and to yourself.” “What rubbish!” he retorted.
uz: Men faqat menga, Bezobiedoffga va o'zingizga o'yin qilishingizdan xafa bo'laman.Qanday axloqsizlik! deb javob berdi u.

en: “I never play-act to any one.” “I have in mind our rule of frankness,” I replied, “when I tell you that I am certain you cannot bear this Bezobiedoff any more than I can.
uz: Men hech qachon hech kim bilan o'yin-kulgi qilmayman.Men bizning ochiqlik qoidamizni nazarda tutaman, deb javob berdim, men sizga bu Bezobiedoffni men ko'ra ko'proq ko'ra ko'ra olmasligingizga amin ekanligimni aytganimda.

en: He is an absolute cad, yet for some inexplicable reason or another it pleases you to masquerade before him.” “Not at all!
uz: U mutlaqo behuda, ammo biror sababga ko'ra, uning oldida o'zingizni ko'rsatishni yoqtirasiz.  Hech qachon!

en: To begin with, he is a splendid fellow, and—” “But I tell you it IS so.
uz: Avvaliga, u ajoyib odam, va  Ammo men sizga aytamanki, bu shunday.

en: I also tell you that your friendship for Lubov Sergievna is founded on the same basis, namely, that she thinks you a god.” “And I tell you once more that it is not so.” “Oh, I know it for myself,” I retorted with the heat of suppressed anger, and designing to disarm him with my frankness.
uz: Shuningdek, sizga aytamanki, Lubov Sergiyevna bilan do'stligingiz xuddi shu asosda asoslangan, ya'ni u sizni xudo deb biladi. Va men sizga yana bir bor aytamanki, bunday emas.Oh, men buni o'zim bilaman, Men o'zimning g'azabim bilan javob berdim va uni o'z ochiqligim bilan quroldan chiqarish niyatida edim.

en: “I have told you before, and I repeat it now, that you always seem to like people who say pleasant things to you, but that, as soon as ever I come to
uz: Men sizga ilgari aytdim va endi yana aytamanki, siz har doim sizga yoqimli so'zlarni aytadigan odamlarni yaxshi ko'rasiz, lekin men buni tezda tushunaman

en: examine your friendship, I invariably find that there exists no real attachment between you.” “Oh, but you are wrong,” said Dimitri with an angry straightening of the neck in his collar.
uz: Do'stligingizni tekshirib ko'rsam, men o'zingiz o'rtasida haqiqiy bog'liqlik yo'qligini aniqlayman.Oh, lekin siz xato qilyapsiz, dedi Dimitriy bo'yniga g'azablangan holda.

en: “When I like people, neither their praise nor their blame can make any difference to my opinion of them.” “Well, dreadful though it may seem to you, I confess that I myself often used to hate my father when he abused me, and to wish that he was dead.
uz: Men odamlarni yoqtirganimda, ularning maqtovlari ham, ayblovlari ham ular haqida mening fikrimni o'zgartira olmaydi. Bu sizga qanchalik dahshatli tuyulsa ham, men tan olsam, otam meni yomon ko'rganida, men ham odatda undan nafratlanardim va uning o'lganini istayman.

en: In the same way, you—” “Speak for yourself.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, siz ham o'zingiz uchun gapiring.

en: I am very sorry that you could ever have been so—” “No, no!” I cried as I leapt from my chair and faced him with the courage of exasperation.
uz: Siz bunday bo'lishingiz mumkin bo'lganidan juda afsusdaman!Yo'q, yo'q! Men o'rnimdan tushib, g'azabga to'lib-tushgan jasorat bilan unga qaraganimda, yig'ladim.

en: “It is for YOURSELF that you ought to feel sorry—sorry because you never told me a word about this fellow.
uz: Siz o'zingiz uchun kechirimli bo'lishingiz kerak, chunki bu odam haqida menga hech qachon bir so'z aytmagansiz.

en: You know that was not honourable of you.
uz: Bilasizmi, bu sizdan sharafga sazovor bo'lmagan.

en: Nevertheless, I will tell YOU what I think of you,” and, burning to wound him even more than he had wounded me, I set out to prove to him that he was incapable of feeling any real affection for anybody, and that I had the best of grounds (as in very truth I believed I had) for reproaching him.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, men siz haqingizda o'ylayotganimni sizlarga aytaman, va men uni o'zimdan ko'ra ko'proq jarohatlash uchun harakat qilib, unga u hech kimga nisbatan haqiqiy mehr-muhabbat his qila olmaydiganligini va uni ayblash uchun eng yaxshi sabablarim borligini isbotlashga harakat qildim.

en: I took great pleasure in telling him all this, but at the same time forgot that the only conceivable purpose of my doing so—to force him to confess to the faults of which I had accused him—could not possibly be attained at the present moment, when he was in a rage.
uz: Men bularning barchasini aytishdan zavq oldim, ammo shu bilan birga, uni ayblagan xatolarimni tan olishga majburlash uchun uni bunday qilishimning yagona maqsadi hozirgi paytda, u g'azabda bo'lgan paytda amalga oshirilmasligi mumkinligini unutdim.

en: Had he, on the other hand, been in a condition to argue calmly, I should probably never have said what I did.
uz: Agar u esa xotirjamlik bilan bahslasha olmaganida edi, men hech qachon qilgan ishimni aytmas edim.

en: The dispute was verging upon an open quarrel when Dimitri suddenly became silent, and left the room.
uz: Dimitriy to'satdan so'zsiz qoldi va xonadan chiqib ketdi.

en: I pursued him, and continued what I was saying, but he did not answer.
uz: Men uning orqasidan ergashdim va so'zlarni davom ettirdim, lekin u javob bermadi.

en: I knew that his failings included a hasty temper, and that he was now fighting it down; wherefore I cursed his good resolutions the more in my heart.
uz: Men uning xatolari shoshilinch g'azabni o'z ichiga olganini va hozir u o'zini tuta olishini bilardim; shuning uchun uning yaxshi qarorlarini ko'proq yuragimda la'natladim.

en: This, then, was what our rule of frankness had brought us to—the rule that we should “tell one another everything in our minds, and never discuss one another with a third person!” Many a time we had exaggerated frankness to the pitch of making mutual confession of the most shameless thoughts, and of shaming ourselves by voicing to one another proposals or schemes for attaining our desires; yet those confessions had not only failed to draw closer the tie which united us, but had dissipated sympathy and thrust us further apart,
uz: Shunday qilib, rostgo'ylik qoidamiz bizni bir-birimizga o'zimizda bor narsani aytishga va hech qachon uchinchi shaxs bilan bir-birimizni muhokama qilmaslik qoidasiga olib keldi!Ko'p marotaba biz rostgo'ylikni o'zaro o'ylamaslik va o'zimizdan o'zimizdan o'zimizdan o'zimizni orzu qilib, bir-birimizga xohishlarimizga erishish uchun taklif yoki rejalarni bildirish bilan o'zimizni sharmanda qilishning o'rniga haddan tashqari ko'p marta o'zimizdan o'tkazdik.

en: until now pride would not allow him to expose his feelings even in the smallest detail, and we employed in our quarrel the very weapons which we had formerly surrendered to one another—the weapons which could strike the shrewdest blows!
uz: Hozirgacha mag'rurlik unga o'z his-tuyg'ularini hatto eng kichik tafsilotlarga ham ko'rsatishga imkon bermasdi va biz o'z bahsimizda avval bir-birimizga topshirgan qurollarimizni ishlatardik, ular eng aqlli urishlarni o'tkazishi mumkin bo'lgan qurollar!

en: OUR STEPMOTHER Notwithstanding that Papa had not meant to return to Moscow before the New Year, he arrived in October, when there was still good riding to hounds to be had in the country.
uz: Ota-ona yangi yilga qadar Moskvaga qaytishni xohlamagan bo'lsa-da, u oktyabr oyida keldi, o'sha paytda mamlakatda itlarga yaxshi sayohat qilish imkoniyati bor edi.

en: He alleged as his reason for changing his mind that his suit was shortly to come on before the Senate, but Mimi averred that Avdotia had found herself so ennuyee in the country, and had so often talked about Moscow and pretended to be unwell, that Papa had decided to accede to her wishes.
uz: U fikrini o'zgartirganining sababi shundaki, uning da'vosi tez orada Senatga ko'tarilishi kerak edi, ammo Mimi Avdotiya o'zini mamlakatda shunchalik g'alati his etganini va Moskva haqida shunchalik ko'p gapirib, kasal bo'lganini ko'rsatganini aytdi, Dadam uning istaklariga rozi bo'lishga qaror qildi.

en: “You see, she never really loved him—she and her love only kept buzzing about his ears because she wanted to marry a rich man,” added Mimi with a pensive sigh which said: “To think what a certain other person could have done for him if only he had valued her!” Yet that “certain other person” was unjust to Avdotia, seeing that the latter’s affection for Papa—the passionate, devoted love of self- abandonment—revealed itself in her every look and word and movement.
uz: Qaranglar, u hech qachon uni yaxshi ko'rmagan va uning sevgisi uning quloqlariga faqat boy kishiga turmush qurmoqchi bo'lganligi sababli g'oyib bo'lgan, Mimi o'ylab ko'rishni davom ettirdi va o'zi shunday dedi: Agar u uni qadrlaganida, boshqa bir kishi uning uchun nima qilishi mumkin edi, deb o'ylash! Biroq, bu boshqa kishi Avdotiyaga nisbatan adolatsiz edi, chunki u o'zining har bir ko'rinishi, so'zi va harakatida o'zini oshkor etgan.Otasining otaga bo'lgan mehr-muhabbati, o'zini tashlab ketishning g'ayratli, sadoqatli sevgisi.

en: At the same time, that love in no way hindered her, not only from being averse to parting with her adored husband, but also from desiring to visit Madame Annette’s and order there a lovely cap, a hat trimmed with a magnificent blue ostrich feather, and a blue Venetian velvet bodice which was to expose to the public gaze the snowy, well shaped breast and arms which no one had yet gazed upon except her husband and maids.
uz: Shu bilan birga, bu sevgi uni nafaqat sevimli eridan ajralishga qoʻrqmaslikdan, balki Madame Annettega tashrif buyurish va u erda chiroyli toʻpka, ajoyib koʻk ostir feyri bilan moʻljallangan toʻpka va koʻk Venesiya velvet boʻyni bilan qoplangan toʻpka buyurtma qilishdan ham toʻsdi. Bu esa uning qorli, yaxshi shaklidagi koʻkrak va qoʻllarini koʻrgazishga imkon yaratdi, faqat uning eri va xizmatkorlaridan boshqa hech kim koʻrmagan edi.

en: Of course Katenka sided with her mother and, in general, there became established between Avdotia and ourselves, from the day of her arrival, the most
uz: Albatta, Katenka onasining tarafini oldi va umuman aytganda, Avdotiya va biz o'rtasida, uning kelishi kundan boshlab, eng ko'p odamlar o'rnatildi.

en: extraordinary and burlesque order of relations.
uz: munosabatlarning noyob va burlesk tartibi.

en: As soon as she stepped from the carriage, Woloda assumed an air of great seriousness and ceremony, and, advancing towards her with much bowing and scraping, said in the tone of one who is presenting something for acceptance: “I have the honour to greet the arrival of our dear Mamma, and to kiss her hand.” “Ah, my dear son!” she replied with her beautiful, unvarying smile.
uz: Voloda aravachadan tushgandan so'ng, katta jiddiylik va marosimni ko'rsatdi va ko'p quvonch va qo'rqinch bilan unga yaqinlashib, qabul qilish uchun biror narsa taqdim etayotgan kishiga o'xshab shunday dedi: Men sevimli onamizning kelishini kutib olish va uning qo'lidan o'pish sharafiga egaman.Ah, aziz o'g'lim! o'zining go'zal, o'zgarmas tabassum bilan javob berdi.

en: “And do not forget the younger son,” I said as I also approached her hand, with an involuntary imitation of Woloda’s voice and expression.
uz: Va kichik o'g'lini unutmang, - dedim men ham uning qo'liga yaqinlashib, Volodaning ovozi va ifodasini o'z ixtiyori bilan takrorlaganimda.

en: Had our stepmother and ourselves been certain of any mutual affection, that expression might have signified contempt for any outward manifestation of our love.
uz: Agar o'g'il onamiz va biz o'zaro mehr-muhabbatga ega bo'lganimizdan shubhalanmaganimizda edi, bu ifodalgan so'zlar sevgimizning har qanday tashqi ifodasini kamsitishni anglatardi.

en: Had we been ill-disposed towards one another, it might have denoted irony, or contempt for pretence, or a desire to conceal from Papa (standing by the while) our real relations, as well as many other thoughts and sentiments.
uz: Agar biz bir-birimizga yomon munosabatda bo'lganimizda, bu ironiya yoki o'zini ko'rsatishni kamsitish yoki haqiqiy munosabatlarimizni va boshqa ko'plab fikr va his-tuyg'ularimizni otadan yashirish istagi bilan taqqoslangan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: But, as a matter of fact, that expression (which well consorted with Avdotia’s own spirit) simply signified nothing at all—simply concealed the absence of any definite relations between us.
uz: Biroq, aslida, bu ifodasi (Avdotiyaning o'z ruhi bilan uyg'un bo'lgan) shunchaki hech narsa emas edi, shunchaki o'zimiz o'rtasidagi aniq munosabatlarning yo'qligini yashirgan edi.

en: In later life I often had occasion to remark, in the case of other families whose members anticipated among themselves relations not altogether harmonious, the sort of provisional, burlesque relations which they formed for daily use; and it was just such relations as those which now became established between ourselves and our stepmother.
uz: Keyinchalik, boshqa oilalarda o'z a'zolari o'rtasida mutlaqo uyg'un bo'lmagan munosabatlarni oldindan ko'rishganida, ular kundalik foydalanish uchun o'rnatgan vaqtinchalik, burlesk munosabatlarni ko'pincha aytib o'tishim mumkin edi; va bu bizning o'zimiz va qaynonamiz o'rtasida hozirgi munosabatlar kabi munosabatlar edi.

en: We scarcely ever strayed beyond them, but were polite to her, conversed with her in French, bowed and scraped before her, and called her “chere Maman”—a term to which she always responded in a tone of similar lightness and with her beautiful, unchanging smile.
uz: Biz hech qachon ulardan chetda bo'lmaymiz, lekin u bilan xushmuomala bo'lib, frantsuz tilida suhbatlashardik, uning oldiga egib qo'ymadik va uni chere Mamana deb atashganmiz, unga u har doim o'xshash yengillik bilan va o'z go'zal, o'zgarmas tabassum bilan javob berardi.

en: Only the lachrymose Lubotshka, with her goose feet and artless prattle, really liked our stepmother, or tried, in her naive and frequently awkward way, to bring her and ourselves together: wherefore the only person in the world for whom, besides Papa, Avdotia had a spark of affection was Lubotshka.
uz: Faqatgina qo'zi oyoqlari va qo'pol gaplari bilan yashirin Lubotshka o'g'il onamizni juda yoqtirardi yoki o'z naif va ko'pincha noqulay yo'lida uni va o'zimizni birlashtirishga harakat qildi: shuning uchun dunyodagi yagona odam, Avdotiyaga bobomadan tashqari, Lubotshka ham yoqqan edi.

en: Indeed, Avdotia always treated her with a kind of grave admiration and timid deference which greatly surprised me.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, Avdotiya har doim unga chuqur hurmat va qo'rqinchli hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'lgan va bu meni hayratda qoldirdi.

en: From the first Avdotia was very fond of calling herself our stepmother and hinting that, since children and servants usually adopt an unjust and hostile attitude towards a woman thus situated, her own position was likely to prove a difficult one.
uz: Avdotiyaning o'zi o'zini qaynonamiz deb atashini birinchi avloddan boshlab juda yaxshi ko'rardi va bolalar va xizmatkorlar odatda bunday vaziyatga tushib qolgan ayolga nisbatan adolatsiz va dushmanlik munosabatda bo'lgani uchun uning o'z pozitsiyasi qiyin bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatardi.

en: Yet, though she foresaw all the unpleasantness of her predicament, she did nothing to escape from it by (for instance) conciliating this one, giving presents to that other one, and forbearing to grumble—the last a precaution which it would have been easy for her to take, seeing that by nature she was in no way exacting, as well as very good- tempered.
uz: Biroq, u o'z vazifasining barcha noqulayliklarini ko'rib turibdi, lekin (masalan) bu vazifani hal qilish, boshqaga sovg'a berish va oxirgi choralarni ko'rish uchun oson bo'lgan ehtiyotkorlik choralarini ko'rishga to'xtamaslik orqali undan qochish uchun hech narsa qilmadi.

en: Yet, not only did she do none of these things, but her expectation of difficulties led her to adopt the defensive before she had been attacked.
uz: Biroq, u nafaqat bularning hech birini bajargan, balki qiyinchiliklarni kutganligi uni hujumga duch kelishdan oldin himoya qilishni boshlagan.

en: That is to say, supposing that the entire household was designing to show her every kind of insult and annoyance, she would see plots where no plots were, and consider that her most dignified course was to suffer in silence—an attitude of passivity as regards winning AFfection which of course led to DISaffection.
uz: Ya'ni, agar butun uy xonadoni unga har qanday haqorat va g'azabni ko'rsatishni rejalashtirgan bo'lsa, u hech qanday reja yo'q bo'lgan joylarda hiyla-nayranglarni ko'radi va eng munosib yo'l - yo'l - yo'l - yo'lini, albatta, DISaffectionga olib kelgan AFfectionni qo'lga kiritishga nisbatan passivlik nuqtai nazaridan xalos bo'lish deb o'ylaydi.

en: Moreover, she was so totally lacking in that faculty of “apprehension” to which I have already referred as being highly developed in our household, and all her customs were so utterly opposed to those which had long been rooted in our establishment, that those two facts alone were bound to go against her.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u bizning uyimizda juda rivojlangan deb aytgan tushuncha qobiliyatiga juda kam edi va uning barcha urf-odatlari uzoq vaqtdan beri o'z asosini o'rnatgan urf-odatlarga juda zid edi, shuning uchun ushbu ikkita faktning o'zi unga qarshi chiqishi kerak edi.

en: From the first, her mode of life in our tidy, methodical household was that of a person only just arrived there.
uz: Birinchidan, uning tartibli, metodik uyida turmush tarzi yangi kelgan odamning turmush tarzi edi.

en: Sometimes she went to bed late, sometimes early; sometimes she appeared at luncheon, sometimes she did not; sometimes she took supper, sometimes she dispensed with it.
uz: Ba'zan kech, ba'zan erta uxlab ketardi; ba'zan kechki ovqatda paydo bo'lgan, ba'zan yo'q edi; ba'zan kechki ovqatda bo'lgan, ba'zan uni tashlab ketardi.

en: When we had no guests with us she more often than not walked about the house in a semi-nude condition, and was not ashamed to appear before us—even before the servants—in a white chemise, with only a shawl thrown over her bare shoulders.
uz: Bizda mehmonlar bo'lmaganida, u ko'pincha yarim yalang'och holda uy atrofida yurardi va hatto oq ko'ylak kiyimda xizmatkorlar oldida ham ko'rinishdan uyalmadi.

en: At first this Bohemianism pleased me, but before very long it led to my losing the last shred of respect which I felt for her.
uz: Boshida bu bohemizm menga yoqdi, lekin ko'p o'tmay bu menga ayolga nisbatan his qilgan hurmatimning so'nggi qismining yo'qolishiga olib keldi.

en: What struck me as even more strange was the fact that, according as we had or had not guests, she was two different women.
uz: Menga yanada g'alatiroq tuyulgan narsa shundaki, bizda mehmonlar bo'lgan yoki bo'lmaganidan kelib chiqqan holda, u ikki xil ayol edi.

en: The one (the woman figuring in society) was a young and healthy, but rather cold, beauty, a person richly dressed, neither stupid nor clever, and unfailingly cheerful.
uz: Bu (ijtimoiy xonim) yosh va sog'lom, lekin juda sovuq, go'zal, boy kiyim kiygan, na ahmoq, na aqlli, na chiroyli, na chiroyli odam edi.

en: The other woman (the one in evidence when no guests were present) was considerably past her first youth, languid,
uz: Boshqa ayol (qonaqlar yo'qligida ko'rinadigan ayol) o'zining yoshlik davridan ancha o'tgandir.

en: depressed, slovenly, and ennuyee, though affectionate.
uz: tushkunlikka tushgan, g'ayritabiiy va ennuyee bo'lsa-da, mehribon.

en: Frequently, as I looked at her when, smiling, rosy with the winter air, and happy in the consciousness of her beauty, she came in from a round of calls and, taking off her hat, went to look at herself in a mirror; or when, rustling in her rich, decollete ball dress, and at once shy and proud before the servants, she was passing to her carriage; or when, at one of our small receptions at home, she was sitting dressed in a high silken dress finished with some sort of fine lace about her soft neck, and flashing her unvarying, but lovely, smile around her—as I looked at her at such times I could not help wondering what would have been said by persons who had been ravished to behold her thus if they could have seen her as I often saw her, namely, when, waiting in the lonely midnight hours for her husband to return from his club, she would walk like a shadow from room to room, with her hair
uz: Ko'pincha, men unga qarab turardim, qachonki, tabassumli, qish havo bilan gullab-yashgan va go'zalligini bilganidan xursand bo'lib, u bir qator qo'ng'iroqlardan kelib, boshini olib, o'zini o'ziga ko'rinishda ko'rinishga borardi; yoki qachonki, u o'zining boy, ko'ylak kiyimini kiygan va xizmatkorlar oldida bir vaqtning o'zida uyalgan va mag'rur bo'lib, o'z vagonasiga o'tar edi; yoki bizning uydagi kichik qabullarimizdan birida u yuqori iplik kiyimda o'tirgan va o'zining yumshatli bo'yni atrofida qandaydir yaxshi bo'lak bilan to'g'rilangan, o'ziga xos, ammo chiroyli tabassumini ko'targan va men unga qaraganimda, agar men ko'pincha uni ko'rganimcha ko'rishni yoqtirgan kishilar nima deyishlarini tushunib o'tirolmasdim.

en: dishevelled and her form clad in a sort of dressing-jacket.
uz: O'z ko'rinishini ko'tarib, o'ziga xos kiyim kiygan edi.

en: Presently, she would sit down to the piano and, her brows all puckered with the effort, play over the only waltz that she knew; after which she would pick up a novel, read a few pages somewhere in the middle of it, and throw it aside.
uz: Hozirda u pianoga o'tirib, qo'lidan kelgan yagona valsni o'ynaydi va o'sha vaqtdan so'ng romanni olib, uning o'rtasida bir necha sahifa o'qib, uni bir chetga tashlaydi.

en: Next, repairing in person to the dining-room, so as not to disturb the servants, she would get herself a cucumber and some cold veal, and eat it standing by the window- sill—then once more resume her weary, aimless, gloomy wandering from room to room.
uz: Keyin, xizmatkorlarni bezovta qilmaslik uchun ovqatxonani o'zi ta'mirlab, o'zi uchun bir qurt va sovuq buzoq go'shti olib, darcha yonida turib ovqatlanardi.

en: But what, above all other things, caused estrangement between us was that lack of understanding which expressed itself chiefly in the peculiar air of indulgent attention with which she would listen when any one was speaking to her concerning matters of which she had no knowledge.
uz: Ammo, eng asosiysi, o'zimizdan ajralib qolishimizga sababchi bo'lgan tushunmovchilik, asosan, u hech qanday ma'lumotga ega bo'lmagan narsalar haqida gapirganida, uni tinglagan o'ziga xos muloyimlik va muloyimlik ruhida namoyon bo'lgan.

en: It was not her fault that she acquired the unconscious habit of bending her head down and smiling slightly with her lips only when she found it necessary to converse on topics which did not interest her (which meant any topic except herself and her husband); yet that smile and that inclination of the head, when incessantly repeated, could become unbearably wearisome.
uz: O'zining boshini egib, og'izlari bilan biroz tabassum qilish odatini faqat o'zini qiziqtirmaydigan mavzularda suhbatlashish kerakligini bilganida (bu o'zi va eridan boshqa hech qanday mavzuni anglatmaydi) o'z aybidir; ammo o'sha tabassum va boshning buzg'unishi, to'xtamas ravishda takrorlanganida, juda charchatadigan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Also, her peculiar gaiety—which always sounded as though she were laughing at herself, at you, and at the world in general—was gauche and anything but infectious, while her sympathy was too evidently forced.
uz: Bundan tashqari, uning o'ziga, sizga va butun dunyoga kulganday tuyuladigan o'ziga xos quvonchlari kasallik va yuqumli bo'lmagan hamma narsa bo'lgan, ammo uning mehr-shafqatlari juda majburiy edi.

en: Lastly, she knew no reticence with regard to her ceaseless rapturising to all and sundry
uz: Va nihoyat, u har bir kishiga o'zining to'xtamaydigan quvonchini ko'rsatishda hech qanday shubha qilmagan.

en: concerning her love for Papa.
uz: Otamga bo'lgan sevgisi haqida.

en: Although she only spoke the truth when she said that her whole life was bound up with him, and although she proved it her life long, we considered such unrestrained, continual insistence upon her affection for him bad form, and felt more ashamed for her when she was descanting thus before strangers even than we did when she was perpetrating bad blunders in French.
uz: Garchi u butun hayoti bilan u bilan bog'liqligini va hayoti davomida buni isbotlagan bo'lsa-da, uning unga bo'lgan mehr-muhabbati haqida o'ylashni yomon ko'rib chiqardik va u o'zini chet elliklar oldida shunday kamsitganida, bizdan ham ko'proq uyat chekardik.

en: Yet, although, as I have said, she loved her husband more than anything else in the world, and he too had a great affection for her (or at all events he had at first, and when he saw that others besides himself admired her beauty), it seemed almost as though she purposely did everything most likely to displease him—simply to prove to him the strength of her love, her readiness to sacrifice herself for his sake, and the fact that her one aim in life was to win his affection!
uz: Biroq, men aytganimdek, u eriga dunyodagi hamma narsadan ko'ra ko'proq muhabbat ko'rsatgan bo'lsa-da, u ham unga katta muhabbat ko'rsatgan edi (yoki, hech bo'lmaganda, boshida u shunday muhabbat ko'rsatgan edi va o'zidan tashqari boshqalar uning go'zalligiga hayron bo'lganini ko'rganida), deyarli u uni ranjitish uchun hamma narsani qasddan qilgan bo'lsa-da, unga sevgining kuchliligini, uning uchun o'zini qurbon qilishga tayyorligini va hayotdagi yagona maqsadi uning muhabbatini qozonish ekanligini isbotlash uchun!

en: She was fond of display, and my father too liked to see her as a beauty who excited wonder and admiration; yet she sacrificed her weakness for fine clothes to her love for him, and grew more and more accustomed to remain at home in a plain grey blouse.
uz: U ko'rinishni yaxshi ko'rgan, otam ham uni hayrat va hayratga soluvchi go'zallik sifatida ko'rishni yaxshi ko'rgan; ammo u yaxshi kiyimlar uchun o'z zaifligini o'z sevgisiga bag'ishlagan va oddiy griz bluza kiygan holda uyda qolishga odatlanib borgan.

en: Again, Papa considered freedom and equality to be indispensable conditions of family life, and hoped that his favourite Lubotshka and his kind-hearted young wife would become sincere friends; yet once again Avdotia sacrificed herself by considering it incumbent upon her to pay the “real mistress of the house,” as she called Lubotshka, an amount of deference which only shocked and annoyed my father.
uz: Ota yana ozodlik va tenglikni oilaviy hayotning zarur shartlari deb hisoblaydi va sevimli Lubotshka va uning mehribon xotini samimiy do'st bo'lishlarini umid qiladi; lekin Avdotia yana o'zini qurbonlikka keltirdi, chunki u uyning haqiqiy xo'jayiniga, Lubotshka deb ataganidek, pul to'lash vazifasini o'z zimmasiga oladi deb hisoblaydi.

en: Likewise, he played cards a great deal that winter, and lost considerable sums towards the end of it, wherefore, unwilling, as usual, to let his gambling affairs intrude upon his family life, he began to preserve complete secrecy concerning his play; yet Avdotia, though often ailing, as well as, towards the end of the winter, enceinte, considered herself bound always to sit up (in a grey blouse, and with her hair dishevelled) for my father when, at, say, four or five o’clock in the morning, he returned home from the club ashamed, depleted in pocket, and weary.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, u o'sha qishning oxiriga qadar katta miqdorda karta o'ynashgan va ko'p miqdorda pul yo'qotgan edi, shuning uchun o'z qimor o'yinlari oilaviy hayotiga ta'sir qilishiga yo'l qo'ymaslik uchun odatdagidek oilaviy hayotiga to'sqinlik qilishni xohlamagan holda, o'z o'yinini to'liq sir saqlay boshladi; ammo Avdotia, ko'pincha kasal bo'lsa-da, qishning oxiriga kelib, o'zini har doim otam uchun o'tirib turishga majbur deb hisoblagan (oq kiyimda, sochlari bo'shgan holda) agar, deylik, ertalab soat to'rt yoki beshlarda u klubdan uyalganida, uyalgan, keskin va charchagan bo'lsa-da.

en: She would ask him absent-mindedly whether he had been fortunate in play, and listen with indulgent attention, little nods of her head, and a faint smile upon her face as he told her of his doings at the club and begged her, for about the hundredth time, never to sit up for him again.
uz: U undan o'ynashda omadli bo'lgan-bo'lmaganini so'rab, kamtarlik bilan tinglaydi, boshini tikib, yuziga yorqin tabassum qo'shib, klubda qilgan ishlarini aytib beradi va unga, taxminan yuzinchi marta, boshqa hech qachon o'zi uchun o'tirmasligini iltijo qiladi.

en: Yet, though Papa’s winnings or losings (upon which
uz: Biroq, "Papa"ning yutuqlari yoki yo'qotishlari (barcha holatlarda)

en: his substance practically depended) in no way interested her, she was always the first to meet him when he returned home in the small hours of the morning.
uz: Uning tarkibi (ya'ni, uning tarkibi) unga hech qanday qiziqish ko'rsatmadi, u ertalabning kichik soatlarida uyga qaytganda uni doim birinchi uchratgan.

en: This she was incited to do, not only by the strength of her devotion, but by a certain secret jealousy from which she suffered.
uz: Buni unga nafaqat sadoqatining kuchi, balki o'zidan azob chekayotgan sirli hasad ham undadi.

en: No one in the world could persuade her that it was REALLY from his club, and not from a mistress’s, that Papa came home so late.
uz: Dunyoda hech kim uni otasining shuncha kech uyga qaytgani uchun o'zining klubidan emas, balki sevimli ayolidan kelganini aytishga majbur qila olmagan.

en: She would try to read love secrets in his face, and, discerning none there, would sigh with a sort of enjoyment of her grief, and give herself up once more to the contemplation of her unhappiness.
uz: U uning yuziga sevgi sirlarini o'qib berishga harakat qilardi va hech qanday sirni ko'rmay, qayg'udan zavqlanib, o'zini yana bir bor baxtsizligini ko'rishga topshirardi.

en: As the result of these and many other constant sacrifices which occurred in Papa’s relations with his wife during the latter months of that winter (a time when he lost much, and was therefore out of spirits), there gradually grew up between the two an intermittent feeling of tacit hostility—of restrained aversion to the object of devotion of the kind which expresses itself in an unconscious eagerness to show the object in question every possible species of petty annoyance.
uz: O'sha qishning so'nggi oylarida (o'sha paytda u ko'p narsani yo'qotdi va shuning uchun ruhidan mahrum bo'ldi) bu va boshqa ko'plab doimiy qurbonliklarning natijasida ota-ona o'z xotini bilan bo'lgan munosabatlarida paydo bo'lgan, ular o'rtasida asta-sekin so'zsiz dushmanlik hissi paydo bo'ldi.

en: NEW COMRADES The winter had passed imperceptibly and the thaw begun when the list of examinations was posted at the University, and I suddenly remembered that I had to return answers to questions in eighteen subjects on which I had heard lectures delivered, but with regard to some of which I had taken no notes and made no preparation whatever.
uz: Yangi hamkorlar Qish ko'rinmas tarzda o'tib ketdi va imtihonlar ro'yxati universitetda joylashtirilganida, muzqaymoq boshlandi va men darhol o'n sakkiz mavzuda so'rovlarga javob qaytarishim kerakligini esladim, men ularda o'qigan, ammo ba'zi mavzularda yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q yo'q tayyorgarlik ko'rmagan edim.

en: It seems strange that the question “How am I going to pass?” should never have entered my head, but the truth is that all that winter I had been in such a state of haze through the delights of being both grown-up and “comme il faut” that, whenever the question of the examinations had occurred to me, I had mentally compared myself with my comrades, and thought to myself, “They are certain to pass, and as most of them are not ‘comme il faut,’ and I am therefore their personal superior, I too am bound to come out all right.” In fact, the only reason why I attended lectures at all was that I might become an habitue of the University, and obtain Papa’s leave to go in and out of the house.
uz: O'shanda o'zimni o'z tengdoshlarim bilan aqliy jihatdan solishtirib, o'zimga o'yladim: "Ular albatta o'tishadi va ularning aksariyati o'tmaydi, shuning uchun men ularning shaxsiy ustasi bo'laman, shuning uchun men ham yaxshi bo'laman. Aslida, men ham o'quvchi bo'lganim uchun bitta sabab - universitetga odatlanib ketishim, ota-onamni uyga kirishga va chiqishga majbur qilishim edi.

en: Moreover, I had many acquaintances now, and often enjoyed myself vastly at the University.
uz: Bundan tashqari, hozirda ko'plab tanishlarim bor edi va ko'pincha universitetda juda zavqlanardim.

en: I loved the racket, talking, and laughter in the auditorium, the opportunities for sitting on a back bench, and letting the measured voice of the professor lure one into dreams as one contemplated one’s comrades, the occasional runnings across the way for a snack and a glass of vodka (sweetened by the fearful joy of knowing that one might be hauled before the professor for so doing), the stealthy closing of the door as one returned to the auditorium, and the participation in “course versus course” scuffles in the corridors.
uz: Auditoriyadagi racket, suhbat va kulgi, orqa stolida o'tirish imkoniyati va professorning o'lchovli ovozini tushlarga tushirish, tengdoshlarni ko'rib chiqish, o'tish va bir stakan vodka olish uchun vaqti-vaqti bilan o'tish (bu tufayli professor oldidan olib ketilishi mumkinligini bilishning qo'rqinchli quvonchi bilan ta'minlangan), auditoriyaga qaytib kelganingizda eshikning yashirin yopilishi va koridorda o'tishdagi course vs course janglarida ishtirok etishni yaxshi ko'rardim.

en: All this was very enjoyable.
uz: Bularning barchasi juda yoqimli edi.

en: By the time, however, that every one had begun to put in a better attendance at lectures, and the professor of physics had completed his course and taken his leave of us until the examinations came on, and the students were busy collecting their notebooks and arranging to do their preparation in parties, it struck me that I also had better prepare for the ordeal.
uz: Biroq, har bir kishi o'qishga ko'proq qatnashishni boshlaganida, fizika professori o'z kursini tugatganida va imtihonlar bo'lguncha bizdan ketganiga qadar, talabalar o'z notebooklarini yig'ib, tayyorgarlik ko'rishni partiyalarda o'tkazish bilan band bo'lganida, men ham sinovga yaxshiroq tayyorgarlik ko'rishim kerakligini tushundim.

en: Operoff, with whom I still continued on bowing, but otherwise most frigid, terms, suddenly offered not only to lend me his notebooks, but to let me do my preparation with himself and some other students.
uz: Operoff, men u bilan hali ham quvonchga to'lib-toshganman, lekin boshqa hollarda esa juda sovuq bo'lgan, birdan menga shunchaki yozuv daftarlarini berishni emas, balki o'zi va boshqa bir nechta talabalar bilan tayyorgarlik ko'rishimni taklif qildi.

en: I thanked him, and accepted the invitation —hoping by that conferment of honour completely to dissipate our old misunderstanding; but at the same time I requested that the gatherings should always be held at my home, since my quarters were so splendid!
uz: Men unga minnatdorchilik bildirdim va taklifni qabul qildim. O'sha sharafli topshiriq tufayli eski noto'g'ri tushunchamizni to'liq yo'q qilish uchun umid qilaman; lekin shu bilan birga, men uchrashuvlar doimo uyimda o'tkazilishini so'radim, chunki mening xonalar juda ajoyib edi!

en: To this the students replied that they meant to take turn and turn about—sometimes to meet at one fellow’s place, sometimes at another’s, as might be most convenient.
uz: O'quvchilar bunga javob berib, ular o'z navbatlarini o'tkazishga va ba'zan bir joyda, ba'zan boshqa joylarda uchrashish uchun o'z navbatlarini o'tkazishga qaror qilishdi.

en: The first of our reunions was held at Zuchin’s, who had a small partition-room in a large building on the Trubni Boulevard.
uz: Birinchi uchrashuvimiz Trubni bulvaridagi katta binodan kichik bo'lim xonasiga ega bo'lgan Zuchinsda bo'lib o'tdi.

en: The opening night I arrived late, and entered when the reading aloud had already begun.
uz: Avvalgi kecha kech kelib, ovoz chiqarib o'qishni boshlaganimda kirdim.

en: The little apartment was thick with tobacco-smoke, while on the table stood a bottle of vodka, a decanter, some bread, some salt, and a shin-bone of mutton.
uz: Kichik xonadon tamaki tutuni bilan to'lib-toshgan edi, stol ustida esa vodka, dekanter, non, tuz va qo'y go'shti bo'lgan.

en: Without rising, Zuchin asked me to have some vodka and to doff my tunic.
uz: Zuchin ko'tarilmasdan, mendan vodka ichishni va kiyimimni to'ldirishimni so'radi.

en: “I expect you are not accustomed to such entertainment,” he added.
uz: Men shuni kutamanki, siz bunday o'yin-kulgilarga odatlanmagansiz, dedi u.

en: Every one was wearing a dirty cotton shirt and a dickey.
uz: Har bir kishi kirli paxta ko'ylaklari va cho'tka kiygan edi.

en: Endeavouring not to show my contempt for the company, I took off my tunic, and lay down in a sociable manner on the sofa.
uz: Kompaniyaga hurmatsizlik ko'rsatmaslikka harakat qilib, kiyimimni olib tashlab, sofa ustida mehribonlik bilan o'tirdim.

en: Zuchin went on reading aloud and correcting himself with the help of notebooks, while the others occasionally stopped him to ask a question, which he always answered with ability, correctness, and precision.
uz: Zuchin ovoz chiqarib o'qishni davom ettirgan va notabuklar yordamida o'zini tuzatgan, boshqalar esa vaqti-vaqti bilan uni savol berish uchun to'xtatishgan va u har doim qobiliyat, to'g'rilik va aniqlik bilan javob bergan.

en: I listened for a time with the rest, but, not understanding much of it, since I had not been present at what had been read before, soon interpolated a question.
uz: Qolganlari bilan bir muncha vaqt tingladim, lekin ko'p narsani tushunmay, bundan oldin o'qigan narsalarga hozir bo'lmaganim uchun tez orada savol berdim.

en: It will be no good for you to listen if you do not know the subject,” said Zuchin.
uz: Agar mavzuni bilmasangiz, tinglash sizga foyda keltirmaydi, dedi Zuchin.

en: “I will lend you my notebooks, and then you can read it up by to-morrow, and I will explain it to you.”
uz: Men sizga yozuvlarimni qarz beraman, so'ngra siz ularni ertaga o'qib chiqasiz va men sizga tushuntirib beraman.

en: I felt rather ashamed of my ignorance.
uz: Men o'zimning jaholatligimdan o'zimni kamsitdim.

en: Also, I felt the truth of what he said; so I gave up listening, and amused myself by observing my new comrades.
uz: Bundan tashqari, uning gaplarining haqiqatini his qildim, shuning uchun men tinglashni to'xtatdim va yangi hamkorlarimga qarab o'zimni zavqlantirdim.

en: According to my classification of humanity, into persons “comme il faut” and persons not “comme il faut,” they evidently belonged to the latter category, and so aroused in me not only a feeling of contempt, but also a certain sensation of personal hostility, for the reason that, though not “comme il faut,” they accounted me their equal, and actually patronised me in a sort of good-humoured fashion.
uz: Insonlikni o'zimning taqsimotimga ko'ra, comme il faut va comme il faut bo'lmagan shaxslarga aylantirib o'tganman, chunki ular bu ikkinchi toifaga tegishli edilar va men uchun nafrat tuyg'usi emas, balki shaxsiy dushmanlik tuyg'usi paydo bo'ldi.

en: What in particular excited in me this feeling was their feet, their dirty nails and fingers, a particularly long talon on Operoff’s obtrusive little finger, their red shirts, their dickeys, the chaff which they good-naturedly threw at one another, the dirty room, a habit which Zuchin had of continually snuffling and pressing a finger to his nose, and, above all, their manner of speaking—that is to say, their use and intonation of words.
uz: Bu his-tuyg'ularimni ayniqsa ularning oyoqlari, kirli to'g'rilari va barmoqlari, Operoffning g'ayratli kichik barmog'ida o'ta uzun bo'g'i, qizil kiyimlari, cho'g'lari, bir-biriga yaxshilik bilan tashlagan cho'g'lari, kirli xonasi, Zuchinning doimo burchasiga barmog'ini bosish odati va eng asosiysi, ularning gapirish usuli, ya'ni so'zlarning qo'llanilishi va intonatsiyasi bilan ta'sir qildi.

en: For instance, they said “flat” for fool, “just the ticket” for exactly, “grandly” for splendidly, and so on— all of which seemed to me either bookish or disagreeably vulgar.
uz: Misol uchun, ular: "Flat" - buzoqqa, "to'g'ri" - to'g'ri, "ketuvchan" - ajoyib va hokazolar, bularning barchasi menga kitobchan yoki noqulay vulgarlik kabi ko'rinardi.

en: Still more was my “comme il faut” refinement disturbed by the accents which they put upon certain Russian—and, still more, upon foreign— words.
uz: O'sha paytdagi o'zimning "komme il faut" soflashuvimni ba'zi rus tili va chet el so'zlariga qo'yilgan ta'sirchanlik tashvishga solgan edi.

en: Thus they said dieYATelnost for DIEyatelnost, NARochno for naROChno, v’KAMinie for v’kaMINie, SHAKespeare for ShakesPEARe, and so forth.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular dieYATelnost deb aytishdi DIEyatelnost uchun, NARochno uchun naROChno uchun, vKAMinie uchun vkaMINie uchun, SHAKespeare uchun ShakesPEARe uchun va hokazo.

en: Yet, for all their insuperably repellent exterior, I could detect something good in these fellows, and envied them the cheerful good- fellowship which united them in one.
uz: Biroq, ularning g'alaba qozonmaydigan darajada qo'rqinchli tashqi ko'rinishlariga qaramasdan, men bu odamlarda yaxshi narsalarni payqadim va ularni birlashtirgan quvonchli yaxshilik rishtalariga hasad qildim.

en: Consequently, I began to feel attracted towards them, and made up my mind that, come what might, I would become of their number.
uz: Natijada, men ularga nisbatan o'zimni jalb qila boshladim va nima bo'lmasin, ularning bir qismi bo'lishga qaror qildim.

en: The kind and honourable Operoff I knew already, and now the brusque, but exceptionally clever, Zuchin (who evidently took the lead in this circle) began to please me greatly.
uz: Men allaqachon tanigan mehribon va hurmatli Operoff va endi o'ziga xos, ammo juda aqlli Zuchin (bu davrda rahbarlikni o'z zimmasiga olgan) meni juda mamnun qila boshladi.

en: He was a dark, thick-set little fellow, with a perennially glistening, polished face, but one that was extremely lively, intellectual, and independent in its expression.
uz: U qorong'u, qalin ko'rinadigan kichkina yigit edi, ko'p yillar davomida shishqoq, poliz yuzli edi, ammo o'z ifodasini juda jonli, intellektual va mustaqil ko'rsatgan.

en: That expression it derived from a low, but prominent, forehead, deep black eyes, short, bristly hair, and a thick, dark beard which looked as though it stood in constant need of trimming.
uz: Bu ifodasi past, ammo ko'p ko'rinadigan bo'lib, peshanasi, chuqur qora ko'zlari, qisqa, chiroyli sochlari va qalin, qorong'i sakkizdan paydo bo'lgan.

en: Although, too, he seemed to think nothing of himself (a trail which always pleased me in people), it was clear that he never let his brain rest.
uz: Garchi u ham o'zi haqida hech narsa o'ylamagan bo'lsa-da (men har doim odamlarda yoqtirgan iz), lekin u hech qachon o'z miyasiga dam olishiga yo'l qo'ymaganligi aniq edi.

en: those expressive faces which, a few hours after you have seen them for the first time, change suddenly and entirely to your view.
uz: Bir necha soat o'tgach, ularni birinchi marta ko'rganingizdan so'ng, ko'zingizga to'satdan va butunlay o'zgaradigan o'sha ifodalangan yuzlar.

en: Such a change took place, in my eyes, with regard to Zuchin’s face towards the end of that evening.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, Zuchinning yuzi o'sha kechaning oxirida o'zgardi.

en: Suddenly, I seemed to see new wrinkles appear upon its surface, its eyes grow deeper, its smile become a different one, and the whole face assume such an altered aspect that I scarcely recognised it.
uz: Toʻsatdan uning yuzida yangi burchaklar paydo boʻlishini, koʻzlari chuqurroq boʻlishini, tabassumlari boshqacha boʻlishini va butun yuzi shunchalik oʻzgarib qolganini koʻrdimki, men uni yaqindan tan olmasdim.

en: When the reading was ended, Zuchin, the other students, and myself manifested our desire to be “comrades all” by drinking vodka until little remained in the bottle.
uz: O'qish tugaganida, Zuchin, boshqa talabalar va men shishaga oz qolmaguncha vodka ichib, hammamizning hamroh bo'lish istagimizni bildirdik.

en: Thereupon Zuchin asked if any one had a quarter-rouble to spare, so that he could send the old woman who looked after him to buy some more; yet, on my offering to provide the money, he made as though he had not heard me, and turned to Operoff, who pulled out a purse sewn with bugles, and handed him the sum required.
uz: Shu payt Zuchin, kimningdir bir chorak rubli qolishini so'radi, shunda uni boqib turgan keksa ayolga yana birini sotib olish uchun yuborishi mumkin edi; ammo pulni taqdim etishni taklif qilganimda, u meni tinglamagan bo'lib, Operoffga murojaat qildi, u qo'ng'iroqlar bilan tikilgan sumkani olib, kerakli miqdorda pul berdi.

en: “And mind you don’t get drunk,” added the giver, who himself had not partaken of the vodka.
uz: Va mast bo'lmasligingizga e'tibor bering, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi o'zi vodka ichmagan kishi.

en: “By heavens!” answered Zuchin as he sucked the marrow out of a mutton bone (I remember thinking that it must be because he ate marrow that he was so clever).
uz: Osmon haqi! Zuchin qo'y suyaklaridan yurakni sug'urib, javob berdi. (Mening o'ylaymanki, bu uning shunchalik aqlli bo'lgani uchun yurak suyakini yedi deb o'ylardim).

en: “By heavens!” he went on with a slight smile (and his smile was of the kind that one involuntarily noticed, and somehow felt grateful for), “even if I did get drunk, there would be no great harm done.
uz: Alloh haqi! u kichkina tabassum bilan davom etdi (va uning tabassumini o'zi xohlamasdan payqadi va shu sababli minnatdor bo'ladi), Agar men mast bo'lsam ham, katta zarar yetkaza olmasdim.

en: I wonder which of us two could look after himself the better—you or I?
uz: O'ylaymanki, ikkovimizning qaysi birimiz o'ziga yaxshiroq g'amxo'rlik qila olamiz, senmi yoki menmi?

en: Anyway I am willing to make the experiment,” and he slapped his forehead with mock boastfulness.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, men tajribani o'tkazishga tayyorman, va u o'z oldiga o'yin-kulgi bilan urdi.

en: “But what a pity it is that Semenoff has disappeared!
uz: Ammo Semenoffning yo'qolgani juda achinarli!

en: He has gone and completely hidden himself somewhere.” Sure enough, the grey-haired Semenoff who had comforted me so much at my first examination by being worse dressed than myself, and who, after passing the second examination, had attended his lectures regularly during the first month, had disappeared thereafter from view, and never been seen at the University throughout the latter part of the course.
uz: U o'zini bir joyga to'liq yashirib qo'ydi. Albatta, birinchi imtihonimda o'zimdan yomon kiyim kiygan bo'lib meni juda tasalli bergan, ikkinchi imtihonni o'tkazgandan so'ng birinchi oy davomida o'z darslariga muntazam qatnashgan, so'ngra ko'zdan ko'rinmay qolgan va kursning oxirgi qismi davomida universitetda hech qachon ko'rilmagan oqsoqol Semenoff.

en: “Where is he?” asked some one.
uz: U qayerda? - deb so'radi kimdir.

en: “I do not know” replied Zuchin.
uz: - Bilmayman, - deb javob berdi Zuchin.

en: “He has escaped my eye altogether.
uz: U mening ko'zimdan butunlay o'tib ketdi.

en: Yet what fun I used to have with him!
uz: Ammo men u bilan qanchalar zavqlanardim!

en: What fire there was in the man!
uz: U odamda naqadar olov bor edi!

en: and what an intellect!
uz: Va naqadar aqlli!

en: I should be indeed sorry if he has
uz: Agar u shunday qilgan bo'lsa, albatta afsuslanaman.

en: come to grief—and come to grief he probably has, for he was no mere boy to take his University course in instalments.” After a little further conversation, and agreeing to meet again the next night at Zuchin’s, since his abode was the most central point for us all, we began to disperse.
uz: Ehtimol, u ham o'zi uchun qayg'uga kelib qayg'uga tushadi, chunki u universitet kursini qisman o'tkazib o'tadigan oddiy yigit emas edi. Bir oz suhbatdan so'ng va keyingi kecha Zuchin'sda yana uchrashishga rozi bo'lganimizdan so'ng, uning uylari hammamiz uchun eng asosiy nuqta bo'lgani sababli, biz tarqala boshladik.

en: As, one by one, we left the room, my conscience started pricking me because every one seemed to be going home on foot, whereas I had my drozhki.
uz: Xonani birma-bir tashlab ketayotib, vijdonim meni qiynashni boshladi, chunki har bir kishi piyoda uyga qaytayotgandek tuyuldi, men esa droshkimni olib yurgan edim.

en: Accordingly, with some hesitation I offered Operoff a lift.
uz: Shuning uchun men biroz tortinmay Operoffga lift taklif qildim.

en: Zuchin came to the door with us, and, after borrowing a rouble of Operoff, went off to make a night of it with some friends.
uz: Zuchin biz bilan birga eshikga keldi va Operoffdan bir rubl qarz olganidan so'ng, do'stlari bilan kechki ovqatlanishga ketdi.

en: As we drove along, Operoff told me a good deal about Zuchin’s character and mode of life, and on reaching home it was long before I could get to sleep for thinking of the new acquaintances I had made.
uz: Yo'lda yurganimizda, Operoff menga Zuchinning shaxsiyati va turmush tarzi haqida ko'p narsalarni aytib berdi va uyga qaytib kelganimda, yangi tanishlarim haqida o'ylagani uchun uxlay olmayman.

en: For many an hour, as I lay awake, I kept wavering between the respect which their knowledge, simplicity, and sense of honour, as well as the poetry of their youth and courage, excited in my regard, and the distaste which I felt for their outward man.
uz: Ko'p soat davomida uyg'onayotganimda, ularning bilimlari, soddaligi va o'rin-hayotlari, shuningdek, yoshlik va jasoratli bo'lgan she'riyatlari menga nisbatan hayajon qo'ygan hurmat va ularning tashqi odamlariga nisbatan his qilgan nafratim o'rtasida tortinmay yurardim.

en: In spite of my desire to do so, it was at that time literally impossible for me to associate with them, since our ideas were too wholly at variance.
uz: Shunga qaramay, o'sha paytda ular bilan muloqot qilish men uchun chindan ham imkonsiz edi, chunki bizning g'oyalarimiz juda ham to'liq farq qilardi.

en: For me, life’s meaning and charm contained an infinitude of shades of which they had not an inkling, and vice versa.
uz: Men uchun hayotning ma'nosi va jozibaliligi ular bilmagan cheksiz nuqtalarni o'z ichiga oladi va aksincha.

en: The greatest obstacles of all, however, to our better acquaintance I felt to be the twenty roubles’ worth of cloth in my tunic, my drozhki, and my white linen shirt; and they appeared to me most important obstacles, since they made me feel as though I had unwittingly insulted these comrades by displaying such tokens of my wealth.
uz: Biroq, biz bilan tanishish uchun eng katta to'siq bo'lgan narsa - bu kiyimim, drozhkim va oq chiroq kiyimimdagi yigirma rubllik to'qimalar edi; ular menga eng muhim to'siqlar kabi ko'rinardi, chunki ular menga o'zimning boyligimning bunday belgilarini ko'rsatganim bilan o'zimni bilmasdan ushbu tengdoshlarni haqorat qilganimdek his qilardim.

en: I felt guilty in their eyes, and as though, whether I accepted or rejected their acquittal and took a line of my own, I could never enter into equal and unaffected relations with them.
uz: Ularning ko'z o'ngida o'zimni aybdor his qilardim va xuddi o'zimning yo'limni egallab, ularning oqlanishini qabul qilsam ham, rad qilsam ham, ular bilan tenglik va o'zaro munosabatlarga ega bo'lmay qolaman deb o'ylardim.

en: Yet to such an extent did the stirring poetry of the courage which I could detect in Zuchin (in particular) overshadow the coarse, vicious side of his nature that the latter made no unpleasant impression upon me.
uz: Biroq, Zuchinda (ayniqsa, uning jasoratini ko'rishim mumkin bo'lgan) jasoratli she'riyat uning tabiatining qalin va yovuz tomonini shunchalik ko'p ko'paytirganki, Zuchin menga hech qanday yoqimsiz taassurot qoldirmagan.

en: For a couple of weeks I visited Zuchin’s almost every night for purposes of work.
uz: Bir necha hafta davomida men ish uchun deyarli har kecha Zuchinsga borardim.

en: Yet I did very little there, since, as I have said, I had lost ground at the start, and, not having sufficient grit in me to catch up my companions by solitary study, was forced merely to PRETEND that I was listening to and taking in all they were reading.
uz: Ammo men u yerda juda oz ish qildim, chunki, aytganimdek, boshida yerni yo'qotgan edim va o'zimda hamrohlarimga yolg'iz o'rganish orqali yetarlicha kuch-qudratim yo'qligi sababli, ular o'qigan hamma narsani tinglayotganimni va qabul qilayotganimni aytishga majbur bo'ldim.

en: I have an idea, too, that they divined my pretence, since I often
uz: Men ham o'ylaymanki, ular o'zimni ko'p marta o'ylab ko'rganim uchun, o'zimni o'ylashim kerakligini aytishdi.

en: noticed that they passed over points which they themselves knew without first inquiring of me whether I did the same.
uz: Ular o'zlari biladigan narsalarni o'zlari ham o'zlari bilmagan narsalarni o'tkazib yuborishganini, men ham shunday qilyapmanmi, deb so'ramaganini payqadilar.

en: Yet, day by day, I was coming to regard the vulgarity of this circle with more indulgence, to feel increasingly drawn towards its way of life, and to find in it much that was poetical.
uz: Biroq, kun o'tib, men bu to'plamning nopokligiga ko'proq e'tibor qaratishga, uning turmush tarziga tobora ko'proq jalb bo'lishga va unda she'riy narsalar ko'pligini topishga harakat qilardim.

en: Only my word of honour to Dimitri that I would never indulge in dissipation with these new comrades kept me from deciding also to share their diversions.
uz: Faqatgina Dimitriyga bergan ehtirom so'zim, men hech qachon ushbu yangi hamkorlar bilan o'z-o'zimni yo'qotmayman, degan so'zim meni ularning o'yin-kulgilarini ham o'zaro o'tkazishga qaror qilishdan to'xtatdi.

en: Once, I thought I would make a display of my knowledge of literature, particularly French literature, and so led the conversation to that theme.
uz: Bir marta men adabiyotlar, ayniqsa frantsuz adabiyotlari haqidagi bilimimni namoyish etishni o'yladim va suhbatni shu mavzuga olib bordim.

en: Judge, then, of my surprise when I discovered that not only had my companions been reading the foreign passages in Russian, but that they had studied far more foreign works than I had, and knew and could appraise English, and even Spanish, writers of whom I had never so much as heard!
uz: O'shanda, mening hamrohlarim chet ellik oyatlarni rus tilida o'qiganlari bilan birga, mendan ko'ra ko'proq chet ellik asarlarni o'qiganlari va ingliz va hatto ispan tilini bilganlari va baholay olishganlari haqida bilganlari va bilganlari haqida bilib olsam, hayron qoldim!

en: Likewise, Pushkin and Zhukovski represented to them LITERATURE, and not, as to myself, certain books in yellow covers which I had once read and studied when a child.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, Puşkin va Zhukovski ularga adabiyotni taqdim etishgan, o'zim uchun esa bolaligimda o'qib o'qigan va o'qigan sariq qoplamalarda yozilgan ba'zi kitoblarni emas.

en: For Dumas and Sue they had an almost equal contempt, and, in general, were competent to form much better and clearer judgments on literary matters than I was, for all that I refused to recognise the fact.
uz: Dumas va Sue uchun ular deyarli teng hurmatsizlik ko'rsatishgan va, umuman olganda, adabiyot masalasida mendan ko'ra yaxshiroq va aniqroq hukmlar chiqarishga qodir edilar, chunki men buni tan olmaganman.

en: In knowledge of music, too, I could not beat them, and was astonished to find that Operoff played the violin, and another student the cello and piano, while both of them were members of the University orchestra, and possessed a wide knowledge of and appreciation of good music.
uz: Musiqa bo'yicha bilimim ham ularni yengib bo'lmadi va Operoff piyola, yana bir talaba violonchella va piano o'ynashini bilib hayron qoldim, ularning ikkalasi ham universitet orkestrining a'zolari bo'lgan va yaxshi musiqa haqida keng bilimga ega va uni qadrlashgan.

en: In short, with the exception of the French and German languages, my companions were better posted at every point than I was, yet not the least proud of the fact.
uz: Qisqa qilib aytganda, fransuz va nemis tillaridan tashqari, mening hamkorlarim har bir joyda mendan ko'ra ko'proq ma'lumotga ega edilar, ammo bu haqiqatdan kam emas edilar.

en: True, I might have plumed myself on my position as a man of the world, but Woloda excelled me even in that.
uz: To'g'ri, men o'zimni dunyo odamining o'rniga qo'yib qo'ygan bo'lardim, lekin Voloda bu borada ham mendan ustun bo'ldi.

en: Wherein, then, lay the height from which I presumed to look down upon these comrades?
uz: Xo'sh, men bu yo'lboshchilarga salbiy qarashga jur'at qilgan balandlik nimada?

en: In my acquaintanceship with Prince Ivan Ivanovitch?
uz: Prince Ivan Ivanovitch bilan tanishishimda?

en: In my ability to speak French?
uz: Fransiya tilida gapirish qobiliyatimda?

en: “Surely these things are all rubbish,” was the thought which would come flitting through my head under the influence of the envy which the good-fellowship and kindly, youthful gaiety displayed around me excited in my breast.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bularning barchasi axlatdir,  deb o'yladim, bu mening boshimda yaxshi do'stlik va mehribon, yoshlik shodligi atrofimda ko'rsatilgan hasad ta'sirida o'tib ketadi.

en: Every one addressed his interlocutor in the second person singular.
uz: Har bir kishi o'z suhbatdoshini ikkinchi shaxsda alohida tilda murojaat qilgan.

en: True, the familiarity of this address almost approximated to rudeness, yet even the boorish
uz: To'g'ri, ushbu manzilning tanishligi deyarli qo'pollik bilan taqqoslanardi, ammo hatto buyrish ham.

en: exterior of the speaker could not conceal a constant endeavour never to hurt another one’s feelings.
uz: Nutqchining tashqi qismi boshqalarning his-tuyg'ularini hech qachon jarohatlamaslik uchun doimiy harakatni yashira olmaydi.

en: The terms “brute” or “swine,” when used in this good-natured fashion, only convulsed me, and gave me cause for inward merriment.
uz: brute yoki swine, so'zlari bunday xushmuomala tarzda qo'llanilganida, faqat meni silkitdi va ichki shodlikka sabab bo'ldi.

en: In no way did they offend the person addressed, or prevent the company at large from remaining on the most sincere and friendly footing.
uz: Ular hech qanday tarzda murojaat qilgan shaxsni ranjitmagan yoki kompaniyaning eng samimiy va do'stona asosda qolishiga to'sqinlik qilmagan.

en: In all their intercourse these youths were delicate and forbearing in a way that only very poor and very young men can be.
uz: Ushbu yoshlar o'zlarining barcha jinsiy aloqalari davomida faqat juda kambag'al va juda yosh erkaklar bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan nozik va sabr-toqatli bo'lgan.

en: However much I might detect in Zuchin’s character and amusements an element of coarseness and profligacy, I could also detect the fact that his drinking-bouts were of a very different order to the puerility with burnt rum and champagne in which I had participated at Baron Z.‘s.
uz: Zuchinning shaxsiyati va o'yin-kulgilarida qo'pollik va nopoklik elementini ko'rishim mumkin bo'lsa-da, uning ichish-ichish mashg'ulotlari Baron Z.s-da ishtirok etgan yondirilgan rum va shampan bilan o'g'illikka nisbatan juda boshqacha bo'lganligini ham ko'rishim mumkin edi.

en: ZUCHIN AND SEMENOFF Although I do not know what class of society Zuchin belonged to, I know that, without the help either of means or social position, he had matriculated from the Seventh Gymnasium.
uz: ZUCHIN VA SEMENOFF Garchi Zuchin qaysi jamiyat sinfidan ekanligini bilmasam-da, lekin u hech qanday yordamsiz yoki ijtimoiy mavqega ega bo'lmagan holda, yettinchi gimnaziyadan matrikul qilganini bilaman.

en: At that time he was eighteen—though he looked much older—and very clever, especially in his powers of assimilation.
uz: O'sha paytda u o'n sakkiz yoshda edi, ammo u ko'proq yoshda va juda aqlli ko'rinardi, ayniqsa assimilasiya qilish qobiliyatida.

en: To him it was easier to survey the whole of some complicated subject, to foresee its various parts and deductions, than to use that knowledge, when gained, for reasoning out the exact laws to which those deductions were due.
uz: U uchun murakkab mavzularning barchasini o'rganish, uning turli qismlarini va xulosalarini ko'rish, o'sha bilimlarni qo'lga kiritganida, ushbu xulosalar asoslangan aniq qonunlarni asoslash uchun ishlatishdan ko'ra osonroq edi.

en: He knew that he was clever, and of the fact he was proud; yet from that very pride arose the circumstance that he treated every one with unvarying simplicity and good-nature.
uz: U o'zining aqlliligini va bunga g'ururlanishini bilardi; ammo shu g'ururdan kelib chiqqanidek, u har bir kishiga o'zgarmas soddalik va xushmuomalalik bilan munosabatda bo'lgan.

en: Moreover, his experience of life must have been considerable, for already he had squandered much love, friendship, activity, and money.
uz: Bundan tashqari, uning hayotiy tajribasi katta bo'lishi kerak edi, chunki u allaqachon ko'pgina sevgi, do'stlik, faoliyat va pulni ziyoda qilgan edi.

en: Though poor and moving only in the lower ranks of society, there was nothing which he had ever attempted for which he did not thenceforth feel the contempt,
uz: Garchi u kambag'al bo'lsa-da va faqat jamiyatning pastki sinflarida harakatlansa-da, u hech qachon harakat qilgan hech narsa uchun u bundan buyon hurmatsizlik his qilmaydi edi,

en: the indifference, or the utter disregard which were bound to result from his attaining his goal too easily.
uz: Uning maqsadlariga osonlikcha erishishidan kelib chiqqan befarqlik yoki mutlaqo beparvolik.

en: In fact, the very ardour with which he applied himself to a new pursuit seemed to be due to his contempt for what he had already attained, since his abilities always led him to success, and therefore to a certain right to despise it.
uz: Darhaqiqat, u o'zini yangi maqsadga bag'ishlagan g'ayrat, uning allaqachon erishgan yutuqlarini kamsitishidan kelib chiqqan bo'lib tuyuladi, chunki uning qobiliyatlari uni har doim muvaffaqiyatga olib boradi va shuning uchun uni kamsitish huquqiga ega edi.

en: With the sciences it was the same.
uz: Ilmlar bilan ham xuddi shunday edi.

en: Though little interested in them, and taking no notes, he knew mathematics thoroughly, and was uttering no vain boast when he said that he could beat the professor himself.
uz: Garchi ularda qiziqishi kam bo'lsa-da va yozuvlarni o'qamasda bo'lsa-da, u matematikani yaxshi bilgan va professorni o'zi mag'lub qilishi mumkinligini aytganda, behuda mag'rurlik qilmayotgan edi.

en: Much of what he heard said in lectures he thought rubbish, yet with his peculiar habit of unconsciously practical roguishness he feigned to subscribe to all that the professors thought important, and every professor adored him.
uz: O'qiganlarining ko'pchiligi uni axloqsiz deb hisoblagan, ammo o'zidan-o'zini bilmasdan amalda qo'pol bo'lishning o'ziga xos odati bilan u professorlar muhim deb hisoblagan barcha narsalarga rozi bo'lganini ko'rsatgan va har bir professor uni juda yaxshi ko'rgan.

en: True, he was outspoken to the authorities, but they none the less respected him.
uz: To'g'ri, u hokimiyatga ochiqchasiga murojaat qilgan, ammo ular unga hurmat ko'rsatishgan.

en: Besides disliking and despising the sciences, he despised all who laboured to attain what he himself had mastered so easily, since the sciences, as he understood them, did not occupy one-tenth part of his powers.
uz: U fanlardan nafratlanishdan tashqari, u o'zi o'zi o'rgangan narsaga erishish uchun mehnat qilgan barcha odamlarni ham hurmat qilmasdi, chunki fanlar, uning tushunchasi bilan, uning kuchlarining o'ndan birini egallamagan.

en: In fact, life, as he saw it from the student’s standpoint, contained nothing to which he could devote himself wholly, and his impetuous, active nature (as he himself often said) demanded life complete: wherefore he frequented the drinking-bout in so far as he could afford it, and surrendered himself to dissipation chiefly out of a desire to get as far away from himself as possible.
uz: Darhaqiqat, o'quvchi nuqtai nazaridan ko'rgan hayotida u o'zini butunlay bag'ishlashi mumkin bo'lgan hech narsa yo'q edi va uning g'ayratli, faol tabiati (o'zi tez-tez aytgandek) butun hayotni talab qilardi: shuning uchun u imkon qadar ichimlik bilan shug'ullanardi va o'zini yo'qotib yuborishga bag'ishladi, asosan o'zidan imkon qadar uzoqroq bo'lish istagi tufayli.

en: Consequently, just as the examinations were approaching, Operoff’s prophecy to me came true, for Zuchin wasted two whole weeks in this fashion, and we had to do the latter part of our preparation at another student’s.
uz: Natijada, imtihonlar yaqinlashganda, Operoffning men uchun aytgan bashorati amalga oshdi, chunki Zuchin ikki haftani shu tarzda yo'qotdi va biz tayyorgarlikning oxirgi qismini boshqa talabalarda o'tkazishga majbur bo'ldik.

en: Yet at the first examination he reappeared with pale, haggard face and tremulous hands, and passed brilliantly into the second course!
uz: Ammo birinchi imtihonda u o'z ko'zidan ko'rinmas, ko'rinmas yuz va qo'rqinchli qo'llari bilan qaytdi va ikkinchi kursga mukammal o'tdi!

en: The company of roisterers of which Zuchin had been the leader since its formation at the beginning of the term consisted of eight students, among whom, at first, had been numbered Ikonin and Semenoff; but the former had left under the strain of the continuous revelry in which the band had indulged in the early part of the term, and the latter seceded later for reasons which were never wholly explained.
uz: Zuchin sinf boshida tashkil etilganidan buyon rahbarlik qilgan roistererlar kompaniyasi sakkiz nafar talabadan iborat edi, ularning orasida Ikonin va Semenoff ham bor edi; lekin birinchilar sinfning boshida to'xtatish bilan shug'ullanayotgan bandning og'irligi ostida ketishdi, keyinchalik esa ular to'liq tushuntirilmagan sabablarga ko'ra ajralib ketishdi.

en: In its early days this band had been looked upon with awe by all the fellows of our course, and had had its exploits much discussed.
uz: Ushbu guruh o'zining dastlabki kunlarida kursdagi barcha yigitlar tomonidan e'tiborga olinardi va uning yutuqlari haqida ko'p gapirildi.

en: Of these exploits the leading heroes had been Zuchin and, towards the end of the term, Semenoff, but the latter had come
uz: Ushbu yutuqlarning asosiy qahramonlari Zuchin va muddatning oxirida Semenoff bo'lgan, ammo oxirgilar kelib qolgan edi

en: to be generally shunned, and to cause disturbances on the rare occasions when he attended a lecture.
uz: Umuman olganda, undan chetlanish va u nutqqa borgan kamdan-kam hollarda tartibsizlikka sabab bo'lish.

en: Just before the examinations began, he rounded off his drinking exploits in a most energetic and original fashion, as I myself had occasion to witness (through my acquaintanceship with Zuchin).
uz: Sinovlar boshlanishidan oldin u o'z ichimlik ishlarini eng kuchli va original tarzda yakunladi, chunki men o'zim guvoh bo'lish imkoniyatiga ega bo'ldim (Zuchin bilan tanishish orqali).

en: One evening we had just assembled at Zuchin’s, and Operoff, reinforcing a candlestick with a candle stuck in a bottle, had just plunged his nose into his notebooks and begun to read aloud in his thin voice from his neatly-written notes on physics, when the landlady entered the room, and informed Zuchin that some one had brought a note for him...
uz: Bir kuni kechqurun biz Zuchinsda yigʻilgan edik va Operoff, shishaga chiroq qoʻyib, chiroqni qoʻllab-quvvatlab, oʻz nuzini notabuklariga tashlab, fizika haqida oʻz vaqtida yozgan yozuvlaridan qattiq ovoz bilan oʻqishni boshlagan edi.

en: [The remainder of this chapter is omitted in the original.] XLV.
uz: [Originalda ushbu bobning qolgan qismi qoldirilgan.] XLV.

en: I COME TO GRIEF At length the first examination—on differentials and integrals—drew near, but I continued in a vague state which precluded me from forming any clear idea of what was awaiting me.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, differensial va integrallarni o'rganishning birinchi davomiyligi yaqinlashdi, lekin men o'zimni aniq tasavvur qila olmaydigan bir holatda davom ettirdim.

en: Every evening, after consorting with Zuchin and the rest, the thought would occur to me that there was something in my convictions which I must change— something wrong and mistaken; yet every morning the daylight would find me again satisfied to be “comme il faut,” and desirous of no change whatsoever.
uz: Har kuni kechqurun, Zuchin va boshqalar bilan suhbatlashgandan so'ng, o'ylaymanki, mening e'tiqodimda biror narsa bor, uni o'zgartirishim kerak - noto'g'ri va noto'g'ri narsa; lekin har kuni ertalab kun yorug'ligi meni yana shod qilib, kerak bo'lganidek bo'lishdan mamnuniyat topadi va hech qanday o'zgarishning o'zi kelmaydi.

en: Such was the frame of mind in which I attended for the first examination.
uz: Birinchi imtihonda ishtirok etganimda shunday fikrlash tarzi bor edi.

en: I seated myself on the bench where the princes, counts, and barons always sat, and began talking to them in French, with the not unnatural result that I never gave another thought to the answers which I was shortly to return to questions in a subject of which I knew nothing.
uz: Men o'zimni shohlar, homiylar va baronlar doim o'tirgan bankda o'tirib, ularga frantsuz tilida gapira boshladim, natijada hech qachon javoblar haqida o'ylamaganman, bu savollarga tez orada javob berishga majbur bo'lganman, men hech narsa bilmagan mavzuda savollarga qaytaman.

en: I gazed supinely at other students as they went up to be examined, and even allowed myself to chaff some of them.
uz: Boshqa talabalar tekshiruvdan o'tishayotganida, men ularga ko'z tikib qaradim va hatto ba'zilarini o'g'irlashimga ruxsat berdim.

en: “Well, Grap,” I said to Ilinka (who, from our first entry into the University, had shaken off my influence, had ceased to smile when I spoke to him, and always remained ill-disposed towards me), “have you survived the ordeal?” “Yes,” retorted Ilinka.
uz: Albatta, Grap, Ilinkaga (Biz universitetga birinchi marta kirganimizdan boshlab mening ta'sirimni o'chirib yuborgan, men unga gapirganimda tabassum qilishni to'xtatgan va doimo menga yomon munosabatda bo'lgan) dedim:¿Siz sinovdan omon qoldingizmi?Ha, Ilinka javob berdi.

en: “Let us see if YOU can do so.” I smiled contemptuously at the answer, notwithstanding that the doubt which he had expressed had given me a momentary shock.
uz: Sening buni qila olasanmi, deb ko'ramiz. Men javobni hurmatsizlik bilan ko'rdim, ammo uning shak-shubhasi meni biroz tashvishga soladi.

en: Once again, however, indifference overlaid that feeling, and I remained so entirely absent-minded and supine that, the very moment after I had been examined (a mere formality for me, as it turned out) I was making a dinner appointment with Baron Z.
uz: Biroq, yana bir bor befarqlik bu his-tuyg'ularni o'z ichiga oldi va men o'zimni shunday o'zgartirganmanki, meni tekshirib ko'rgandan so'ng (men uchun bu shunchaki rasmiylik bo'ldi) men baron Z bilan kechki ovqatga uchrashishimni rejalashtirgan edim.

en: When called out with Ikonin, I smoothed the creases in my uniform, and walked up to the examiner’s table with perfect sang froid.
uz: Ikonin bilan chaqirilganimda, unifomdagi toʻqimalarni tekisladim va mukammal soʻng sovuq holda imtihonchining dasturxonasiga yaqinlashdim.

en: True, a slight shiver of apprehension ran down my back when the young professor—the same one as had examined me for my matriculation—looked me straight in the face as I reached across to the envelope containing the tickets.
uz: To'g'ri, yosh o'qituvchi - matriklar uchun meni tekshirgan o'qituvchi - chiptalarni o'z ichiga olgan qadoqqa yetib borayotganimda, biroz qo'rqinchli bo'lganim uchun orqaga tushdim.

en: Ikonin, though taking a ticket with the same plunge of his whole body as he had done at the previous examinations, did at least return some sort of an answer this time, though a poor one.
uz: Ikonin avvalgi imtihonlarda qilganidek butun tanasi bilan chiptaga tushishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, bu safar hech bo'lmaganda kamchilik bilan javob qaytardi.

en: I, on the contrary, did just as he had done on the two previous occasions, or even worse, since I took a second ticket, yet for a second time returned no answer.
uz: Aksincha, men o'tgan ikki marta u qilganidek, yoki undan ham yomonroq, ikkinchi marta chipta olganimdan keyin, ikkinchi marta javob qaytarmaganman.

en: The professor looked me compassionately in the face, and said in a quiet, but determined, voice: “You will not pass into the second course, Monsieur Irtenieff.
uz: Professor menga rahm-shafqat bilan qaradi va tinch, ammo qat'iy ovoz bilan shunday deydi: "Siz ikkinchi kursga o'tmaysiz, monsieur Irtenieff.

en: You had better not complete the examinations.
uz: Imtihonlarni o'tkazib bo'lmasangiz yaxshi bo'lardi.

en: The faculty must be weeded out.
uz: Fakultetani o'chirib tashlash kerak.

en: The same with you, Monsieur Ikonin.” Ikonin implored leave to finish the examinations, as a great favour, but the professor replied that he (Ikonin) was not likely to do in two days what he had not succeeded in doing in a year, and that he had not the smallest chance of passing.
uz: Siz bilan ham shunday, M. Ikonin. Ikonin imtihonlarni tugatish uchun ruxsat so'radi, bu katta yordam bo'ldi, lekin professor u (Ikonin) ikki kun ichida bir yil ichida qila olmagan ishni amalga oshirish ehtimoli yo'qligini va o'tish imkoniyati ham yo'qligini aytdi.

en: Ikonin renewed his humble, piteous appeals, but the professor was inexorable.
uz: Ikonin kamtarin va achinarli da'volarini yangiladi, ammo professor o'z ishini davom ettirdi.

en: “You can go, gentlemen,” he remarked in the same quiet, resolute voice.
uz: Sizlar ketishingiz mumkin, xonimlar, - dedi u o'sha xotirjam, qat'iy ovoz bilan.

en: I was only too glad to do so, for I felt ashamed of seeming, by my silent presence, to be joining in Ikonin’s humiliating prayers for grace.
