uz: Men buni qilishdan juda xursand edim, chunki men o'zimning xotirjam bo'lganim tufayli Ikoninning noloyiq iltijolariga qo'shilishimdan o'zimni sharmanda his qilardim.

en: I have no recollection of how I threaded my way through the
uz: Men o'zimni qanday yo'ldan ozdirganimni eslay olmayman.

en: students in the hall, nor of what I replied to their questions, nor of how I passed into the vestibule and departed home.
uz: O'quvchilarning salondagi o'quvchilari, ularning savollariga qanday javob berganim, qanday qilib chodirga kirib, uyga qaytganim haqida ham o'ylamayman.

en: I was offended, humiliated, and genuinely unhappy.
uz: Men xafa bo'ldim, kamsitildim va chinakam baxtsiz edim.

en: For three days I never left my room, and saw no one, but found relief in copious tears.
uz: Uch kun davomida xonamdan hech kimni ko'rmadim, lekin ko'pgina ko'z yoshlarimdan xalos bo'ldim.

en: I should have sought a pistol to shoot myself if I had had the necessary determination for the deed.
uz: Agar o'zimni o'ldiradigan qurol qidirib topgan bo'lsam kerak edi, agar bu harakat uchun kerakli qat'iy qarorim bo'lgan bo'lsa.

en: I thought that Ilinka Grap would spit in my face when he next met me, and that he would have the right to do so; that Operoff would rejoice at my misfortune, and tell every one of it; that Kolpikoff had justly shamed me that night at the restaurant; that my stupid speeches to Princess Kornikoff had had their fitting result; and so on, and so on.
uz: Men Ilinka Grap men bilan uchrashganda yuzimga tishlaydi va bunga haqli bo'ladi deb o'yladim; Operoff mening baxtsizligimdan xursand bo'lib, hamma narsaga gapiradi; Kolpikoff o'sha kecha restoranda meni haqli ravishda sharmanda qilgan; princeska Kornikoffga aytgan ahmoqona nutqlarim o'z natijalariga erishgan; va shu kabilar.

en: All the moments in my life which had been for me most difficult and painful recurred to my mind.
uz: Hayotimdagi eng qiyin va og'ir damlarni eslayman.

en: I tried to blame some one for my calamity, and thought that some one must have done it on purpose—must have conspired a whole intrigue against me.
uz: Men o'zimning baxtsizliklarim uchun kimnidir ayblashga harakat qildim va kimdir buni qasddan qilgan bo'lishi kerak deb o'yladim.

en: Next, I murmured against the professors, against my comrades, Woloda, Dimitri, and Papa (the last for having sent me to the University at all).
uz: Keyin professorlarga, tengdoshlarim Woloda, Dimitri va Papaga (menni universitetga yuborgan oxirgi) qarshi g'iybat qildim.

en: Finally, I railed at Providence for ever having let me see such ignominy.
uz: Nihoyat, men bunday masxaralarni ko'rishimga ruxsat berganim uchun Providencega qarshi chiqdim.

en: Believing myself ruined for ever in the eyes of all who knew me, I besought Papa to let me go into the hussars or to the Caucasus.
uz: O'zimni tanib-bilganlarning ko'z o'ngida abadiy yo'q bo'lib qolganimni his etib, otamdan meni husarlarga yoki Kavkazga joylashtirishga ruxsat berishini iltijo qildim.

en: Naturally, Papa was anything but pleased at what had happened; yet, on seeing my passionate grief, he comforted me by saying that, though it was a bad business, it might yet be mended by my transferring to another faculty.
uz: Tabiiyki, otam sodir bo'lgan hodisalardan mamnun emas edi; ammo o'zimning ruhiy qayg'uimni ko'rib, bu yomon ish bo'lsa-da, boshqa fakultetga o'tishim bilan bu holat tuzatilishi mumkinligini aytib tasalli berdi.

en: Woloda, who also saw nothing very terrible in my misfortune, added that at least I should not be put out of countenance in a new faculty, since I should have new comrades there.
uz: Woloda, mening baxtsizliklarimda hech qanday dahshatli narsani ko'rmagan, hech bo'lmaganda menga yangi fakultetda ko'nglimdan tushmasligi kerakligini qo'shdi, chunki u erda yangi tengdoshlarim bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: As for the ladies of the household, they neither knew nor cared what either an examination or a plucking meant, and condoled with me only because they saw me in such distress.
uz: Uydagi ayollarga kelsak, ular tekshiruv yoki o'tqazish nimani anglatishini bilmas edilar va menga hamdardlik bildirishardi, chunki ular meni shu qadar azob chekayotganini ko'rishardi.

en: Dimitri came to see me every day, and was very kind and consolatory throughout; but for that very reason he seemed to me to have grown colder than before.
uz: Dimitri har kuni menga tashrif buyuradi va juda mehribon va tasalli beruvchi bo'ldi; lekin aynan shu sababdan u menga avvalgidan ham sovuqroq bo'lib qolgan ko'rinadi.

en: It always hurt me and made me feel uncomfortable when he came up to my room and seated himself in silence beside me, much as a doctor might scat himself by the bedside of an awkward patient.
uz: Bu meni har doim og'ritardi va u xonamga kelib, yonimda xotirjamlik bilan o'tirganida noqulay bo'ldim, xuddi shifokor o'zini noqulay bemorning yotoq yonida tarqatishi mumkin bo'lganidek.

en: Sophia Ivanovna and Varenika sent me books for which I had expressed a wish, as also an invitation to go and see them, but in that very thoughtfulness of theirs I saw only proud, humiliating
uz: Sofiya Ivanovna va Varenika menga o'zim xohlagan kitoblar va ularni ko'rish uchun taklifni yubordilar, ammo ularning o'ylashuvida men faqat faxrli va kamsitadigan narsalarni ko'rdim.

en: condescension to one who had fallen beyond forgiveness.
uz: Kechirib bo'lmaydigan odamga nisbatan kamtarlik.

en: Although, in three days’ time, I grew calmer, it was not until we departed for the country that I left the house, but spent the time in nursing my grief and wandering, fearful of all the household, through the various rooms.
uz: Garchi uch kun ichida xotirjam bo'lsam-da, biz mamlakatga ketmaguncha uydan chiqib ketdim, lekin vaqtni qayg'u-alamimni ko'tarib, butun uydagilardan qo'rqqan holda turli xonalar bo'ylab yurishga sarfladim.

en: One evening, as I was sitting deep in thought and listening to Avdotia playing her waltz, I suddenly leapt to my feet, ran upstairs, got out the copy-book whereon I had once inscribed “Rules of My Life,” opened it, and experienced my first moment of repentance and moral resolution.
uz: Bir kuni kechqurun, Avdotiyaning valsini o'ynashini tinglab, chuqur fikrda o'tirganimda, to'satdan oyoqlarimga tushib, ustiga yugurdim, bir marta "O'z hayotimning qoidalari" deb yozilgan nusxa kitobimni olib chiqdim, uni ochdim va tavba va axloqiy qarorning birinchi daqiqalarini his qildim.

en: True, I burst into tears once more, but they were no longer tears of despair.
uz: To'g'ri, men yana bir bor ko'z yoshlarimga tushib yubordim, lekin ular endi umidsizlik ko'z yoshlari emas edi.

en: Pulling myself together, I set about writing out a fresh set of rules, in the assured conviction that never again would I do a wrong action, waste a single moment on frivolity, or alter the rules which I now decided to frame.
uz: O'zimni yig'ib oldim va yana hech qachon noto'g'ri ish qilmayman, hech qachon behudalik qilmayman yoki o'zim qaror qilgan qoidalarni o'zgartirmayman degan ishonch bilan yangi qoidalar to'plamini yozishga kirdim.

en: How long that moral impulse lasted, what it consisted of, and what new principles I devised for my moral growth I will relate when speaking of the ensuing and happier portion of my early manhood.
uz: Bu axloqiy impuls qancha davom etdi, u nimalardan iborat edi va axloqiy o'sishim uchun qanday yangi prinsiplar yaratdim?

en: Dostoevsky was the son of a doctor.
uz: Dostoyevskiy shifokorning o'g'li edi.

en: His parents were very hardworking and deeply religious people, but so poor that they lived with their five children in only two rooms.
uz: Uning ota-onasi juda mehnatsevar va chuqur diniy odamlar edilar, lekin ular shunchalik kambag'al bo'lishganki, beshta farzandlari bilan faqat ikkita xonada yashardilar.

en: The father and mother spent their evenings in reading aloud to their children, generally from books of a serious character.
uz: Ota-onalar kechki paytlarini farzandlariga, odatda jiddiy kitoblardan ovoz chiqarib o'qib berishardi.

en: Though always sickly and delicate Dostoevsky came out third in the final examination of the Petersburg school of Engineering.
uz: Dostoyevskiy har doim kasal va nozik bo'lsa-da, Sankt-Peterburg muhandislik maktabining yakuniy imtihonida uchinchi o'rinni egalladi.

en: There he had already begun his first work, Poor Folk.
uz: U erda u o'zining birinchi asarini, "Kafir xalq" nomli asarini boshlagan edi.

en: This story was published by the poet Nekrassov in his review and was received with acclamations.
uz: Bu hikoya shoir Nekrasov tomonidan o'zining sharhida chop etilgan va maqtovlar bilan qabul qilingan.

en: The shy, unknown youth found himself instantly something of a celebrity.
uz: Uyatchan, noma'lum yosh o'zini shu zahoti o'zi mashhurlikka aylantirgan.

en: A brilliant and successful career seemed to open before him, but those hopes were soon dashed.
uz: Uning oldida ajoyib va muvaffaqiyatli karyera ochilganidek tuyuldi, ammo bu umidlar tez orada yo'q bo'ldi.

en: Though neither by temperament nor conviction a revolutionist, Dostoevsky was one of a little group of young men who met together to read Fourier and Proudhon.
uz: Dostoyevskiy o'z temperamenti yoki e'tiqodi bilan inqilobchi bo'lmagan bo'lsa-da, Fourier va Proudhonni o'qish uchun yig'ilgan yoshlar guruhidan biri edi.

en: He was accused of “taking part in conversations against the censorship, of reading a letter from Byelinsky to Gogol, and of knowing of the intention to set up a printing press.” Under Nicholas I (that “stern and just man,” as Maurice Baring calls him) this was enough, and he was condemned to death.
uz: U tsenzuraga qarshi suhbatlarda ishtirok etgan, Byelinskining Gogolga yozgan maktubini o'qigan va bosmaxona o'rnatish niyatidan xabardor bo'lganlikda ayblangan edi. Nikolay I davrida (Moris Baring aytganidek, u "qattiq va adolatli odam") bu yetarli edi va uni o'limga mahkum qilishdi.

en: After eight months’ imprisonment he was with twenty-one others taken out to the Semyonovsky Square to be shot.
uz: Sakkiz oy qamoqdan o'tgach, u yigirma bir kishi bilan birga o'q qilinish uchun Semyonovskiy maydoniga olib ketilgan edi.

en: Writing to his brother Mihail, Dostoevsky says: “They snapped words over our heads, and they made us put on the white shirts worn by persons condemned to death.
uz: Dostoyevskiy o'z ukasi Mixailga yozgan maktubida shunday deydi: "Ular bizning boshimizdan so'zlarni o'chirib, o'limga mahkum qilingan kishilar kiygan oq ko'ylaklarni kiyishga majbur qilishdi.

en: Thereupon we were bound in threes to stakes,
uz: O'shanda biz uchdan-uchga bog'langan edik.

en: to suffer execution.
uz: o'limga duchor bo'lish uchun.

en: Being the third in the row, I concluded I had only a few minutes of life before me.
uz: Uchinchi bo'lib ketayotgan bo'lsam ham, hayotimning bir necha daqiqasi qolganini tushundim.

en: I thought of you and your dear ones and I contrived to kiss Plestcheiev and Dourov, who were next to me, and to bid them farewell.
uz: Sizlar va yaqinlaringiz haqida o'yladim va yonimda turgan Plestchev va Do'rovni o'pib, ularga xayrlashishga harakat qildim.

en: Suddenly the troops beat a tattoo, we were unbound, brought back upon the scaffold, and informed that his Majesty had spared us our lives.” The sentence was commuted to hard labour.
uz: Toʻsatdan qoʻshinlar oʻgʻlimizga tatuvrat qoʻyishdi, bizni toʻxtatishdi, eskifoldga qaytarib olib kelishdi va majlisi bizga hayotimizni qutqarganini xabar berishdi. Hukm qattiq mehnatga oʻzgartirildi.

en: One of the prisoners, Grigoryev, went mad as soon as he was untied, and never regained his sanity.
uz: Mahbuslardan biri Grigoryev bo'shashtirilganidan so'ng g'alati bo'ldi va hech qachon aqlini tiklamadi.

en: The intense suffering of this experience left a lasting stamp on Dostoevsky’s mind.
uz: Ushbu tajriba tufayli ko'p azob chekish Dostoyevskining ongida doimiy iz qoldirdi.

en: Though his religious temper led him in the end to accept every suffering with resignation and to regard it as a blessing in his own case, he constantly recurs to the subject in his writings.
uz: Garchi uning diniy munosabati uni oxir-oqibat har qanday azob-uqubatni rad etish bilan qabul qilishga va uni o'zi uchun baraka deb hisoblashga undasa-da, u o'z yozishlarida bu mavzuga doimo murojaat qiladi.

en: He describes the awful agony of the condemned man and insists on the cruelty of inflicting such torture.
uz: U mahkumning dahshatli azob-uqubatini tasvirlaydi va bunday azob-uqubatlarga duchor bo'lishning shafqatsizligiga e'tibor qaratadi.

en: Then followed four years of penal servitude, spent in the company of common criminals in Siberia, where he began the Dead House, and some years of service in a disciplinary battalion.
uz: So'ngra to'rt yillik jazoni o'tkazdi, u Sibirdagi oddiy jinoyatchilarning kompaniyasida o'tdi, u erda u o'lik uyni boshladi va bir necha yil intizomiy batalyonda xizmat qildi.

en: He had shown signs of some obscure nervous disease before his arrest and this now developed into violent attacks of epilepsy, from which he suffered for the rest of his life.
uz: U hibsga olishidan oldin noto'g'ri asabiy kasallikning belgilarini ko'rsatgan edi va bu endi epilepsiyaning zo'ravon hujumlariga aylandi va u hayoti davomida azob chekdi.

en: The fits occurred three or four times a year and were more frequent in periods of great strain.
uz: Joriy yilda uch yoki to'rt marta urishlar sodir bo'lgan va ular juda og'ir vaqtlarda tez-tez sodir bo'lgan.

en: In ൢ൩൦൪ he was allowed to return to Russia.
uz: yilda unga Rossiyaga qaytishga ruxsat berildi.

en: He started a journal — Vremya, which was forbidden by the Censorship through a misunderstanding.
uz: U "Vremya" jurnalini yozib qo'ydi, ammo bu jurnal noto'g'ri tushuncha tufayli Senzura tomonidan taqiqlandi.

en: In ൢ൩൧൥ he lost his first wife and his brother Mihail.
uz: yilda birinchi xotini va ukasi Mihailni yo'qotib qo'ydi.

en: He was in terrible poverty, yet he took upon himself the payment of his brother’s debts.
uz: U juda kambag'al edi, ammo akasi qarzlarini to'lashni o'z zimmasiga oldi.

en: He started another journal —The Epoch, which within a few months was also prohibited.
uz: U yana bir jurnal "The Epoch"ni boshladi, bir necha oy ichida u ham taqiqlandi.

en: He was weighed down by debt, his brother’s family was dependent on him, he was forced to write at heartbreaking speed, and is said never to have corrected his work.
uz: U qarzlar bilan og'irlanardi, ukasi oilasi unga bog'liq edi, u qahr-qahr bilan yozishga majbur bo'ldi va hech qachon o'z ishini tuzatmagan deb aytiladi.

en: The later years of his life were much softened by the tenderness and devotion of his second wife.
uz: Uning hayotining oxirgi yillari ikkinchi xotini ko'rsatgan mehribonlik va sadoqat tufayli ancha yumshatildi.

en: A few months later Dostoevsky died.
uz: Bir necha oy o'tgach, Dostoyevskiy vafot etdi.

en: He was followed to the grave by a vast multitude of mourners, who “gave the hapless man the
uz: Uning orqasidan ko'pgina qayg'uchilar qabrga ketishdi va ular baxtsiz odamga o'limni bag'ishladilar.

en: funeral of a king.” He is still probably the most widely read writer in Russia.
uz: Podshohning dafn marosimi. U hali ham Rossiyadagi eng keng o'qilgan yozuvchi hisoblanadi.

en: In the words of a Russian critic, who seeks to explain the feeling inspired by Dostoevsky: “He was one of ourselves, a man of our blood and our bone, but one who has suffered and has seen so much more deeply than we have his insight impresses us as wisdom  … that wisdom of the heart which we seek that we may learn from it how to live.
uz: Dostoyevskiy tomonidan ilhomlantirilgan his-tuyg'ularni tushuntirishga intilayotgan rus tanqidiy so'zlariga ko'ra: "U o'zimizdan biri edi, bizning qonimiz va suyaklarimizdan bo'lgan odam edi, lekin azob chekgan va bizdan ko'ra ko'proq narsani ko'rgan kishi, uning tushunchasi bizga donolik sifatida ta'sir qiladi ... biz undan qanday yashashni o'rganishimiz uchun izlayotgan yurak donoligi.

en: All his other gifts came to him from nature, this he won for himself and through it he became great.”
uz: Boshqa barcha sovg'alari unga tabiatdan kelgan, uni o'zi uchun qo'lga kiritgan va shu orqali ulkan bo'lgan.

en: I On an exceptionally hot evening early in July a young man came out of the garret in which he lodged in S — — Place and walked slowly, as though in hesitation, towards K — — bridge.
uz: I Iyul oyida juda issiq bir kechada bir yigit S   joyida yashaydigan garretdan chiqib, sekin-sekin, xuddi shubha ostiga tushib, K   ko'prining yo'liga bordi.

en: He had successfully avoided meeting his landlady on the staircase.
uz: U o'z uy egasi bilan uchrashishdan muvaffaqiyatli qochgan edi.

en: His garret was under the roof of a high, five-storied house and was more like a cupboard than a room.
uz: Uning garretsi baland besh qavatli uyning tomoni ostida edi va xona emas, balki omborga o'xshardi.

en: The landlady who provided him with garret, dinners, and attendance, lived on the floor below, and every time he went out he was obliged to pass her kitchen, the door of which invariably stood open.
uz: Uy egasi, unga garret, kechki ovqat va xizmatni ta'minlagan ayol, pastdagi qavatda yashardi va har safar u tashqariga chiqsa, uning oshxonasiga o'tishi kerak edi, uning eshiklari doim ochiq edi.

en: And each time he passed, the young man had a sick, frightened feeling, which made him scowl and feel ashamed.
uz: Va har safar o'tib ketganda, yigit kasal, qo'rqqan hissiyotlarga ega bo'lgan, bu uni qo'rqitib, o'zini sharmanda his qilardi.

en: He was hopelessly in debt to his landlady, and was afraid of meeting her.
uz: U uy egasiga umidsizlikka qarzdor edi va u bilan uchrashishdan qo'rqardi.

en: This was not because he was cowardly and abject, quite the contrary; but for some time past he had been in an overstrained irritable condition, verging on hypochondria.
uz: Buning sababi u qo'rqoq va o'ziga yarasha emas, aksincha, balki bir muncha vaqtdan beri juda qattiq xafa bo'lib, hypokondriyaga yaqinlashib qolgan edi.

en: He had become so completely absorbed in himself, and isolated from his fellows that he dreaded meeting, not only his landlady, but anyone at all.
uz: U o'ziga shunchalik ko'p e'tibor qaratgan va o'z odamlaridan ajralib qolganki, u faqat uy egasi bilan emas, balki hamma bilan uchrashishdan qo'rqardi.

en: He was crushed by poverty, but the anxieties of his position had of late ceased to weigh upon him.
uz: U qashshoqlik dastidan azob chekardi, ammo uning o'rniga tashvishlanishlari undan so'ng uni tashvishlantirmay qo'ydi.

en: He had given up attending to matters of practical importance; he had lost all desire to do so.
uz: U amaliy ahamiyatga ega bo'lgan ishlarga ko'proq vaqt ajratishni tashlab qo'ygan edi; bunday qilish istagi yo'q edi.

en: Nothing that any landlady could do had a real terror for him.
uz: Uy egasi qila olishi mumkin bo'lgan hech narsa uning uchun haqiqiy dahshatga tushmagan.

en: But to be stopped on the stairs, to be forced to listen to her trivial, irrelevant gossip, to pestering demands for payment, threats and complaints, and to rack his brains for excuses, to prevaricate, to lie —no, rather than that, he would creep down the stairs like a cat and slip out unseen.
uz: Lekin, uning behuda, ahamiyatsiz g'iybatlarini tinglashga majbur bo'lish, to'lov talablari, tahdid va shikoyatlarni qo'zg'atish va uzr izlash uchun o'z miyalarini to'ldirish, kamtarlik, yolg'on gapirish, aksincha, u mushuk kabi to'xtovga tushib, ko'rinmas tarzda chiqib ketishi kerak edi.

en: This evening, however, on coming out into the street, he became acutely aware of his fears.
uz: Biroq, bu kechqurun ko'chaga chiqgach, u o'z qo'rquvlaridan xabardor bo'ldi.

en: “I want to attempt a thing like that and am frightened by these trifles,” he thought, with an odd smile.
uz: "Men bunday ishni sinab ko'rmoqchiman va bu kichik ishlardan qo'rqaman", - deb o'yladi u o'ziga xos tabassum bilan.

en: “Hm … yes, all is in a man’s hands and he lets it all slip from cowardice, that’s an axiom.
uz: Ha... ha, hamma narsa odamning qo'lida va u hamma narsani qo'rqinchlikdan saqlab qolishga yo'l qo'yadi, bu axiom.

en: It would be interesting to know what it is men are most afraid of.
uz: Erkaklar eng ko'p nimalardan qo'rqishini bilish qiziqarli bo'ladi.

en: Taking a new step, uttering a new word is what they fear most.
uz: Yangi qadam qo'yish, yangi so'zni aytish - ular eng ko'p qo'rqadigan narsa.

en: … But I am talking too much.
uz: Lekin men juda ko'p gapiryapman.

en: It’s because I chatter that I do nothing.
uz: Men hech narsa qilmayman, chunki men gapiryapman.

en: Or perhaps it is that I chatter because I do nothing.
uz: Yoki men hech narsa qilmagani uchun gapiryapman.

en: I’ve learned to chatter this last month, lying for days together in my den thinking … of Jack the Giant-killer.
uz: Men o'tgan oyda gapirishni o'rgandim, kunlar davomida o'zimning g'orimda birga yolg'on gapirib, ulkan qotil Jack haqida o'yladim.

en: Why am I going there now?
uz: Nima uchun men endi u yerga boryapman?

en: Am I capable of that?
uz: Men bunga qodirmanmi?

en: It is not serious at all.
uz: Bu umuman jiddiy emas.

en: It’s simply a fantasy to amuse myself; a plaything!
uz: Bu shunchaki o'zimni o'yin-kulgi qilish uchun o'yin-kulgidir, o'yin-kulgidir!

en: Yes, maybe it is a plaything.” The heat in the street was terrible: and the airlessness, the bustle and the plaster, scaffolding, bricks, and dust all about him, and that special Petersburg stench, so familiar to all who are unable to get out of town in summer —all worked painfully upon the young man’s already overwrought nerves.
uz: Ha, ehtimol u o'yinchoq. Ko'chadagi issiqlik dahshatli edi: uning atrofidagi havosizlik, shov-shuv va gips, asfaltlar, toshlar va changlar, shuningdek, yozda shahardan chiqib ketishga qodir bo'lmaganlarning hammasi uchun tanish bo'lgan o'zgacha Sankt-Peterburg issiqligi yosh yigitning allaqachon bo'lgan g'azablarini og'irlab o'tkazdi.

en: The insufferable stench from the pothouses, which are particularly numerous in that part of the town, and the drunken men whom he met continually, although it was a working day, completed the revolting misery of the picture.
uz: Shaharning o'sha qismida ayniqsa ko'p bo'lgan maydonxonalar va u doimiy ravishda uchrab turadigan ichkilikbozlarning ko'tarilishidan ko'rinmaydigan kirligi, garchi ish kuni bo'lsa ham, rasmning dahshatli qashshoqligini to'ldirgan.

en: An expression of the profoundest disgust gleamed for a moment in the young man’s refined face.
uz: O'sha yigitning sof yuzida chuqur jirkanchlik ifodasi bir zum uchun nurlandi.

en: He was, by the way, exceptionally handsome, above the average in height, slim, well-built, with beautiful dark eyes and dark brown hair.
uz: U juda chiroyli edi, o'rtacha o'rtacha bo'lmagan balandlikda, chiroyli, yaxshi qurilgan, chiroyli qorong'i ko'zlar va qorong'i qora sochli edi.

en: Soon he sank into deep thought, or more accurately speaking into a complete blankness of mind; he walked along not observing what was about him and not caring to observe it.
uz: Ko'p o'tmay u chuqur o'ylashga tushdi, yoki aniqroq aytganda, butunlay bo'sh fikrga tushdi; u atrofida nima bo'lganini kuzatmay va uni kuzatishga qiziqish ko'rsatmay yurdi.

en: From time to time, he would mutter something, from the habit of talking to himself, to which he had just confessed.
uz: Vaqti-vaqti bilan u o'zi bilan gapirish odatidan kelib chiqqan holda biror narsa gapirib turardi.

en: At these moments he would become conscious that his ideas were sometimes in a tangle and that he was very weak; for two days he had scarcely tasted food.
uz: O'sha paytlarda u fikrlarining ba'zan chalg'ib ketayotganini va o'zi juda zaif ekanligini anglab yetardi; ikki kun davomida u ovqatni oz tatib ko'rgan edi.

en: He was so badly dressed that even a man accustomed to shabbiness would have been ashamed to be seen in the street in such rags.
uz: Uning kiyim-kechaklari shunchalik yomon ediki, bu kabi kiyimda ko'chalarda ko'rishdan hatto o'ziga xos axloqsizlikka odatlangan odam ham o'zini sharmanda his qilgan bo'lardi.

en: In that quarter of the town, however, scarcely any shortcoming in dress would have created surprise.
uz: Biroq, shaharning o'sha qismida kiyim-kechakning kamligi hech qanday ajablantirishni keltirib chiqarmagan.

en: Owing to the proximity of the Hay Market, the number of establishments of bad character, the preponderance of the trading and working class population crowded in these streets and alleys in the heart of
uz: Hay bozori yaqinligi, yomon xarakterli korxonalar soni, savdo-sotiq va ishchilarning ko'pligi tufayli ushbu ko'chalar va ko'chalar bilan to'plandi

en: Petersburg, types so various were to be seen in the streets that no figure, however queer, would have caused surprise.
uz: Sankt-Peterburgda ko'chalarda shunchalik turli xil turdagi odamlar ko'rinadiki, hech bir shaxs, qanchalik g'ayritabiiy bo'lmasin, o'zini hayratda qoldirmagan bo'ladi.

en: But there was such accumulated bitterness and contempt in the young man’s heart, that, in spite of all the fastidiousness of youth, he minded his rags least of all in the street.
uz: Ammo yosh yigitning yuragida shunchalik achchiqlik va kamsitish toʻplanib, yoshlikning barcha gʻayratliligiga qaramay, koʻchalarda oʻz kiyimlariga kamroq eʼtibor qaratdi.

en: It was a different matter when he met with acquaintances or with former fellow students, whom, indeed, he disliked meeting at any time.
uz: U taniganlari yoki sobiq sinfdoshlari bilan uchrashganda esa, bu boshqa narsa edi, chunki u hech qachon uchrashishni yoqtirmasdi.

en: And yet when a drunken man who, for some unknown reason, was being taken somewhere in a huge wagon dragged by a heavy dray horse, suddenly shouted at him as he drove past: “Hey there, German hatter” bawling at the top of his voice and pointing at him —the young man stopped suddenly and clutched tremulously at his hat.
uz: Biroq, biron bir sababga ko'ra, og'ir tosh tomonidan tortilgan katta vagon bilan qayerga olib ketilayotgan mast kishi o'sha yo'lda ketayotganda unga to'satdan shunday deb baqirdi: Hey, u erda, nemis g'alaba qozonchisi  o'z ovozini ko'tarib, unga ko'rsatdi sha yigit to'satdan to'xtadi va qo'rqinch bilan g'alaba qozondi.

en: It was a tall round hat from Zimmerman’s, but completely worn out, rusty with age, all torn and bespattered, brimless and bent on one side in a most unseemly fashion.
uz: Bu Zimmermanlarning baland to'g'riroq to'pkasi edi, ammo u butunlay eskirgan, yoshga to'lgan, butunlay yirtilgan va o'g'irlangan, o'tsiz va bir tomondan eng munosib tarzda burilgan edi.

en: Not shame, however, but quite another feeling akin to terror had overtaken him.
uz: Biroq, uyat emas, balki qo'rquvga o'xshash boshqa his-tuyg'ular uni qamrab olgan edi.

en: “I knew it,” he muttered in confusion, “I thought so!
uz: Men buni bilardim, u g'alati so'zlarni aytdi, men shunday deb o'yladim!

en: That’s the worst of all!
uz: Bu eng yomon narsa!

en: Why, a stupid thing like this, the most trivial detail might spoil the whole plan.
uz: Bunday ahmoqona ish, hatto eng kichik tafsilot ham butun rejani buzishi mumkin.

en: Yes, my hat is too noticeable.
uz: Ha, mening to'plam juda ko'rinadi.

en: … It looks absurd and that makes it noticeable.
uz: ... Bu absurd ko'rinadi va bu uni sezilarli qiladi.

en: … With my rags I ought to wear a cap, any sort of old pancake, but not this grotesque thing.
uz: O'zimning to'qimalarim bilan to'pka kiyishim kerak edi, har qanday eski pancake, lekin bu g'alati narsa emas.

en: Nobody wears such a hat, it would be noticed a mile off, it would be remembered.
uz: Hech kim bunday to'pka kiymaydi, uni bir mil uzoqlikda ko'rishadi, eslab qolishadi.

en: … What matters is that people would remember it, and that would give them a clue.
uz: ... Muhimi shundaki, odamlar buni eslab qolishadi va bu ularga izoh beradi.

en: For this business one should be as little conspicuous as possible.
uz: Bu ish uchun eng kam ko'rinadigan narsa bo'lishi kerak.

en: … Trifles, trifles are what matter!
uz: ... Trifllar, trifllar muhim ahamiyatga ega!

en: Why, it’s just such trifles that always ruin everything.
uz: Axir, hamma narsani har doim vayron qiladigan oddiy narsalar.

en: …” He had not far to go; he knew indeed how many steps it was from the gate of his lodging house: exactly seven hundred and thirty.
uz: ... U uzoq yo'l olmagan edi; u o'z uyidagi eshikdan qancha qadamlar borligini bilgan edi: to'g'ri yetti yuz o'ttiz.

en: He had counted them once when he had been lost in dreams.
uz: U tushlarida yo'qolganida ularni bir marta sanab o'tgan edi.

en: At the time he had put no faith in those dreams and was only tantalising himself by their hideous but daring recklessness.
uz: O'sha paytda u bu orzularga ishonmagan edi va faqat ularning dahshatli, ammo jasoratli befarqligi bilan o'zini vasvasaga solgan edi.

en: Now, a month later, he had begun to look upon them differently, and, in spite of the monologues in which he jeered at his own impotence and indecision, he had involuntarily come to regard this “hideous” dream as an exploit to be attempted, although he still did not realise this himself.
uz: Bir oy o'tgach, u ularga boshqacha qarashni boshladi va o'z kuchsizligi va qat'iy qarorsizligiga mazax qilgan monologlariga qaramay, o'z xohishi bilan bu dahshatli orzuga harakat qilish uchun harakat deb qaragan, garchi u hali ham buni anglamagan bo'lsa-da.

en: He was positively going now for a “rehearsal” of his project, and at every step his excitement grew more and more violent.
uz: O'z loyihasining mashg'ulotini o'tkazishga tayyor edi va har qadamda uning hayajonlari kuchayib borardi.

en: With a sinking heart and a nervous tremor, he went up to a huge house which on one side looked on to the canal, and on the other into the street.
uz: Qalb og'irlab, g'azabga to'lib-toshgan holda u katta uyga bordi, u bir tomondan kanalni, boshqa tomondan esa ko'chaga qarab turardi.

en: This house was let out in tiny tenements and was inhabited by working people of all kinds —tailors, locksmiths, cooks, Germans of sorts, girls picking up a living as best they could, petty clerks, etc.
uz: Ushbu uy kichik kvartiralarda ijaraga olingan va unda turli xil ishchilar yashaydigan edi: taylorlar, qulfchilar, oshpazlar, nemislar, qizlar o'zlarining eng yaxshi ishini o'zlashtirishlari mumkin bo'lgan darajada, kichik ishchilar va boshqalar.

en: There was a continual coming and going through the two gates and in the two courtyards of the house.
uz: Uyning ikki darvozasidan va ikki hovlisidan muntazam ravishda kirib-kirib borardi.

en: Three or four doorkeepers were employed on the building.
uz: Binodan uch yoki to'rtta eshikbosh ishlatilgan.

en: The young man was very glad to meet none of them, and at once slipped unnoticed through the door on the right, and up the staircase.
uz: Yosh yigit hech kim bilan uchrashishdan juda xursand bo'ldi va darhol o'ng tomonidagi eshikdan ko'rinmay pastga tushib, sinchkovchadan oshib ketdi.

en: It was a back staircase, dark and narrow, but he was familiar with it already, and knew his way, and he liked all these surroundings: in such darkness even the most inquisitive eyes were not to be dreaded.
uz: Bu qorong'i va tor tikilgan orqa bosqichi edi, ammo u allaqachon unga tanish edi va o'z yo'lini bilgan edi va u atrofdagi barcha joylarni yaxshi ko'rgan: bunday qorong'ilikda hatto eng qiziqarli ko'zlar ham qo'rqmas edi.

en: “If I am so scared now, what would it be if it somehow came to pass that I were really going to do it?” he could not help asking himself as he reached the fourth storey.
uz: Agar men hozir shunchalik qo'rqsam, agar men buni amalga oshirmoqchi bo'lsam, nima bo'ladi? U to'rtinchi qavatga yetib borganida o'zidan so'rashdan bosh tortolmadi.

en: There his progress was barred by some porters who were engaged in moving furniture out of a flat.
uz: U yerda uning taraqqiyoti bir xonadon mebellarini ko'chirish bilan shug'ullanuvchi ba'zi ko'chmachilar tomonidan to'siqlarga duchor bo'ldi.

en: He knew that the flat had been occupied by a German clerk in the civil service, and his family.
uz: U o'sha xonadonni nemis davlat xizmati xodimi va uning oilasi egallab olganini bilardi.

en: This German was moving out then, and so the fourth floor on this staircase would be untenanted except by the old woman.
uz: Bu nemis o'sha paytda ko'chib ketayotgan edi, shuning uchun bu mertabaning to'rtinchi qavatida keksa ayoldan boshqa hech kim bo'lmagan.

en: “That’s a good thing anyway,” he thought to himself, as he rang the bell of the old woman’s flat.
uz: Xo'sh, bu yaxshi narsa, deb o'yladi u, keksa ayolning xonadonidagi qo'ng'iroqni chaqirganida.

en: The bell gave a faint tinkle as though it were made of tin and not of copper.
uz: G'alati qo'ng'iroq xuddi mis emas, qalinlikdan bo'lgani kabi, zaiflik bilan qichqirdi.

en: The little flats in such houses always have bells that ring like that.
uz: Bunday uylardagi kichik kvartiralarda har doim shunga o'xshash qo'ng'iroqlar bor.

en: He had forgotten the note of that bell, and now its peculiar tinkle seemed to remind him of something and to bring it clearly before him.
uz: U o'sha qo'ng'iroqning notasini unutib qo'ygan edi va endi uning o'ziga xos qichqiriqligi unga biror narsani eslatadi va uni aniq ko'rsatadi.

en: … He started, his nerves were terribly overstrained by now.
uz: U boshladi, endi uning hissiyotlari juda ko'p bo'lgan edi.

en: In a little while, the door was opened a tiny crack: the old woman eyed her visitor with evident distrust through the crack, and nothing could be seen but her little eyes, glittering in the darkness.
uz: Qisqa vaqt o'tgach, eshik kichkina bo'lakdan ochildi: keksa ayol o'z tashrif buyuruvchisini bo'lakdan ko'rinmas ishonchsizlik bilan ko'rib chiqdi va qorong'ilikda parcha-parcha bo'lgan kichkina ko'zlaridan boshqa hech narsa ko'rinmadi.

en: But, seeing a number of people on the landing, she grew bolder, and opened the door wide.
uz: Ammo u, ko'plab odamlarni ko'rib, jasoratli bo'lib, eshikni keng ochdi.

en: The young man stepped into the dark entry, which was partitioned off from the tiny kitchen.
uz: Yosh yigit kichkina oshxonadan ajralgan qorong'i kirish tomoniga kirdi.

en: The old woman stood facing him in silence and looking inquiringly at him.
uz: Keksa ayol uncha sukut saqlash bilan unga qaray turibdi va unga savol-javob bilan qaradi.

en: She was a diminutive, withered up old woman of sixty, with sharp malignant eyes and a sharp little nose.
uz: U o'ttiz yoshdagi kamroq, o'tkir qariya ayol edi, o'ta yomon ko'zlar va o'ta kichkina burun bilan.

en: Her colourless, somewhat grizzled hair was thickly smeared with oil, and she wore no kerchief over it.
uz: Uning rangsiz, biroz grizzled sochlari yog' bilan qoplangan edi, va u hech bir choriq kiygan emas edi.

en: Round her thin long neck, which
uz: Uning cho'qqizil uzun bo'yni aylanib boradi.

en: looked like a hen’s leg, was knotted some sort of flannel rag, and, in spite of the heat, there hung flapping on her shoulders, a mangy fur cape, yellow with age.
uz: Bu ayolning oyoqlari tikancha bo'lgan, u bir xil flanel to'qima bilan bog'langan edi va issiqlikka qaramay, uning shoxlarida qovurib turadigan, yoshi bilan sariq bo'lgan mayda to'qima bor edi.

en: The old woman coughed and groaned at every instant.
uz: Qariya ayol har bir daqiqada qo'shnichilik va qayg'urardi.

en: The young man must have looked at her with a rather peculiar expression, for a gleam of mistrust came into her eyes again.
uz: O'sha yigit unga o'zgacha ko'rinish bilan qaragan bo'lishi kerak, chunki uning ko'zlariga yana ishonchsizlik nurlari paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Raskolnikov, a student, I came here a month ago,” the young man made haste to mutter, with a half bow, remembering that he ought to be more polite.
uz: Raskolnikov, talaba, men bu yerga bir oy oldin kelgan edim, yigit o'zidan ko'proq xushmuomala bo'lishi kerakligini eslab, yarim qo'zg'olon bilan shov-shuv qilishga shoshildi.

en: “I remember, my good sir, I remember quite well your coming here,” the old woman said distinctly, still keeping her inquiring eyes on his face.
uz: Men eslayman, yaxshi xonim, sizning bu yerga kelganingizni juda yaxshi eslayman,  qariya ayol aniqlik bilan aytdi, hali ham uning yuzida so'rovchan ko'zlarini saqlab.

en: “And here … I am again on the same errand,” Raskolnikov continued, a little disconcerted and surprised at the old woman’s mistrust.
uz: Raskolnikov davom etdi: "Men yana o'sha vazifani bajaryapman, biroz g'alati va keksa ayolning ishonchsizlikidan hayronman.

en: “Perhaps she is always like that though, only I did not notice it the other time,” he thought with an uneasy feeling.
uz: Ehtimol, u har doim shunday bo'lishi mumkin, lekin men buni boshqa safar sezmaganman, deb o'yladi u noqulay his-tuyg'u bilan.

en: The old woman paused, as though hesitating; then stepped on one side, and pointing to the door of the room, she said, letting her visitor pass in front of her: “Step in, my good sir.” The little room into which the young man walked, with yellow paper on the walls, geraniums and muslin curtains in the windows, was brightly lighted up at that moment by the setting sun.
uz: Keksa ayol to'xtadi, xuddi shubha ostiga qo'ygan bo'lsa-da; so'ngra bir tomonga qadam bosdi va xonaning eshigini ko'rsatib, o'zidan oldinga tashrif buyurgan kishiga: Kishib kiring, yaxshi xonim. Yosh yigit kirgan kichkina xonani, devorlarda sariq qog'oz, derazalarda geranium va muslin pardalari bo'lgan, quyosh botgan paytda yorug'lik bilan yoritdi.

en: “So the sun will shine like this then too!” flashed as it were by chance through Raskolnikov’s mind, and with a rapid glance he scanned everything in the room, trying as far as possible to notice and remember its arrangement.
uz: Shuning uchun quyosh ham shu tarzda porlaydi! Raskolnikovning ongidan tasodifan o'tdi va tez bir ko'z o'rab, u xonadagi hamma narsani skanerlab, uning tartibini sezishga va eslashga harakat qildi.

en: But there was nothing special in the room.
uz: Ammo xonada hech qanday o'zgacha narsa yo'q edi.

en: The furniture, all very old and of yellow wood, consisted of a sofa with a huge bent wooden back, an oval table in front of the sofa, a dressing-table with a looking-glass fixed on it between the windows, chairs along the walls and two or three halfpenny prints in yellow frames, representing German damsels with birds in their hands —that was all.
uz: Barcha juda eski va sariq yog'ochdan yasalgan mebellar katta egri yog'och orqaga ega bo'lgan sofa, sofaning oldidagi ovozli stol, derazalar o'rtasida o'rnatilgan oyna bilan kiyish stolidan, devorlar bo'ylab o'rindiqlardan va ikki yoki uchta yarim penni rasmlaridan iborat edi.

en: In the corner a light was burning before a small icon.
uz: Burchada kichik bir ikona oldida chiroq yonayotgan edi.

en: Everything was very clean; the floor and the furniture were brightly polished; everything shone.
uz: Hamma narsa juda toza edi; pol va mebel chiroyli sozlangan edi; hamma narsa shinam edi.

en: “Lizaveta’s work,” thought the young man.
uz: Lizavetas ish, deb o'yladi yigit.

en: There was not a speck of dust to be seen in the whole flat.
uz: Butun xonadonda bir tosh tosh ham ko'rinmadi.

en: “It’s in the houses of spiteful old widows that one finds such cleanliness,” Raskolnikov thought again, and he stole a curious glance at the cotton curtain over the door leading into another tiny room, in which stood the old woman’s bed and chest of drawers and into which he had never looked before.
uz: Raskolnikov yana o'ylaganidek, bunday tozalikni o'z ko'zlari bilan ko'rish mumkin bo'lgan qariya bevalarning uylarida, u boshqa kichkina xonadonga olib boradigan eshikning ustidagi paxta pardalariga qiziqarli bir qarashni o'g'irladi, u yerda keksa ayolning yotoq va sovg'alari turgan va u hech qachon ko'z olmagan edi.

en: These two rooms made up the whole flat.
uz: Ushbu ikki xona butun kvartirani tashkil etdi.

en: “What do you want?” the old woman said severely, coming into the room and, as before, standing in front of him so as to look him straight in the face.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? - dedi keksa ayol qattiqqo'rlik bilan, xonada kirib, avvalgidek uning oldidan turib, uning yuziga to'g'ri qaradi.

en: “I’ve brought something to pawn here,” and he drew out of his pocket an old-fashioned flat silver watch, on the back of which was engraved a globe; the chain was of steel.
uz: Men bu yerga qarz olish uchun bir narsa olib keldim, va u o'zining qopidan qadimgi shtash kumush soatini olib chiqdi, uning orqasida globul o'ralib o'ralgan edi; zanjir po'latdan edi.

en: “But the time is up for your last pledge.
uz: Ammo oxirgi va'dasining vaqti keldi.

en: The month was up the day before yesterday.” “I will bring you the interest for another month; wait a little.” “But that’s for me to do as I please, my good sir, to wait or to sell your pledge at once.” “How much will you give me for the watch, Alyona Ivanovna?” “You come with such trifles, my good sir, it’s scarcely worth anything.
uz: Oʻtgan kunning ertasi kuni oʻtgan edi.Men sizga yana bir oylik foizni keltiraman; bir oz kuting. Lekin bu mening xohishimcha qilishim kerak, yaxshi sir, sizning garovingizni birdan kutish yoki sotish.Siz menga soat uchun qancha berasiz, Alyona Ivanovna?Siz bunday kichik narsalar bilan kelasiz, yaxshi sir, bu hech narsaga arzimaydi.

en: I gave you two roubles last time for your ring and one could buy it quite new at a jeweler’s for a rouble and a half.” “Give me four roubles for it, I shall redeem it, it was my father’s.
uz: O'tgan safar sizda o'zingizning bag'ringiz uchun ikki rubl berdim va biri uni bir yarim rubl evaziga zargarlikxonada yangi sotib olish mumkin edi. Menga buning uchun to'rt rubl bering, men uni to'lov qilaman, bu mening otamningdir.

en: I shall be getting some money soon.” “A rouble and a half, and interest in advance, if you like!” “A rouble and a half!” cried the young man.
uz: Tez orada pul topaman. Bir yarim rubl va oldindan foizlar, agar xohlasangiz! Bir yarim rubl! deb baqirdi yigit.

en: “Please yourself” —and the old woman handed him back the watch.
uz: O'zingizni iltimos qiling  va keksa ayol unga soatni qaytarib berdi.

en: The young man took it, and was so angry that he was on the point of going away; but checked himself at once, remembering that there was nowhere else he could go, and that he had had another object also in coming.
uz: Yosh yigit uni olib, shunchalik g'azablandiki, ketmoqchi bo'ldi; lekin u o'zini darhol tekshirib ko'rdi va boshqa hech bir joyga borolmasligini va yana bir maqsadi borligini esladi.

en: “Hand it over,” he said roughly.
uz: O'z qo'lingizdan uzating, dedi u taxminan.

en: The old woman fumbled in her pocket for her keys, and disappeared behind the curtain into the other room.
uz: Keksa ayol o'z kalitlarini to'plamga olib kirgan va parda orqasidan boshqa xonaga ko'chib ketgan.

en: The young man, left standing alone in the middle of the room, listened inquisitively, thinking.
uz: Xonaning o'rtasida yolg'iz turgan yigit qiziquvchanlik bilan tinglab, o'ylaydi.

en: He could hear her unlocking the chest of drawers.
uz: U uning sovutxonalar qutisini ochayotganini eshitardi.

en: “It must be the top drawer,” he reflected.
uz: Bu yuqori sovrin bo'lishi kerak, deb o'yladi u.

en: “So she carries the keys in a pocket on the right.
uz: Shunday qilib, u o'ng tomondagi sumkada kalitlarni ushlab turadi.

en: All in one bunch on a steel ring.
uz: Hammasi bir guruhda po'latli bog'da.

en: there’s one key there, three times as big as all the others, with deep notches; that can’t be the key of the chest of drawers … then there must be some other chest or strongbox … that’s worth knowing.
uz: U yerda bitta kalit bor, u boshqalarning barchalaridan uch baravar kattaroq, chuqur o'tlar bilan; bu do'konning kaliti bo'lishi mumkin emas ... u holda boshqa do'kon yoki quti bor bo'lishi kerak ... buni bilish arziydi.

en: Strongboxes always have keys like that … but how degrading it all is.” The old woman came back.
uz: Strongboxlarda har doim shunga o'xshash kalitlar bor... lekin bularning barchasi qanchalik dahshatli. Keksa ayol qaytib keldi.

en: “Here, sir: as we say ten kopecks the rouble a month, so I must take fifteen kopecks from a rouble and a half for the month in advance.
uz: Mana, xo'jayinim: oylik rubl uchun o'n kopek deyilganidek, men o'n yarim rubldan o'n besh kopekni oldindan olishim kerak.

en: But for the two roubles I lent you before, you owe me now twenty kopecks on the same reckoning in advance.
uz: Ammo men sizga ilgari qarz bergan ikkita rubl uchun siz menga hozir oldindan bir xil hisob-kitob qilishda yigirma kopek qarzdorsiz.

en: That makes thirty-five kopecks altogether.
uz: Bu jami 35 kopekni tashkil etadi.

en: So I must give you a rouble and fifteen kopecks for the watch.
uz: Shunday qilib, men sizga soat uchun bir rubl va o'n besh kopek beraman.

en: only a rouble and fifteen kopecks now!” “Just so.” The young man did not dispute it and took the money.
uz: Hozirda faqat bir rubl va o'n besh kopek! Sanoq shunday. Yosh yigit buni tanqid qilmadi va pulni oldi.

en: He looked at the old woman, and was in no hurry to get away, as though there was still something he wanted to say or to do, but he did not himself quite know what.
uz: U keksa ayolga qaradi va hali ham aytmoqchi yoki qilmoqchi bo'lgan biron narsa bo'lgani kabi qochib ketishga shoshilmayapti, lekin u nima ekanligini bilmaydi.

en: “I may be bringing you something else in a day or two, Alyona Ivanovna —a valuable thing —silver —a cigarette-box, as soon as I get it back from a friend …” he broke off in confusion.
uz: Men sizga bir yoki ikki kun ichida boshqa bir narsa olib kelishim mumkin, Alyona Ivanovna bu qimmatbaho narsa pir sigaret qutisi, men uni do'stimdan qaytarib olsam ... u chalg'ib qolib ketdi.

en: “Well, we will talk about it then, sir.” “Goodbye —are you always at home alone, your sister is not here with you?” He asked her as casually as possible as he went out into the passage.
uz: Ha, keyin bu haqda gaplashamiz, xo'jayinim.Xudojo'y Siz har doim uyda yolg'izmisiz, singilingiz siz bilan birga yo'qmi? U undan imkon qadar bevosita so'radi va yo'lga chiqdi.

en: “What business is she of yours, my good sir?” “Oh, nothing particular, I simply asked.
uz: U sizga qanday tegishli, yaxshi sir?  Oh, hech narsa aniq emas, men shunchaki so'radim.

en: … Good day, Alyona Ivanovna.” Raskolnikov went out in complete confusion.
uz: ...Xayrli kunlar, Alyona Ivanovna. Raskolnikov butunlay g'alati bo'lib chiqib ketdi.

en: This confusion became more and more intense.
uz: Bu g'alatilik kundan-kunga kuchayib borardi.

en: As he went down the stairs, he even stopped short, two or three times, as though suddenly struck by some thought.
uz: Turg'izayotganda u hatto ikki-uch marta to'xtab qo'ydi, xuddi to'satdan biron bir fikrga tushib qolgan bo'lsa.

en: When he was in the street he cried out, “Oh, God, how loathsome it all is!
uz: U ko'chada bo'lganida: "O, Xudoyim, bu qanday jirkanch narsa!

en: and can I, can I possibly.
uz: va men mumkinmi, mumkinmi.

en: … No, it’s nonsense, it’s rubbish!” he added resolutely.
uz: Yo'q, bu g'alati gap, bu kulfat! - dedi u qat'iy qo'shimcha qilib.

en: “And how could such an atrocious thing come into my head?
uz: Qanday qilib men o'zimga bunday dahshatli narsani o'ylab topib olsam bo'ladi?

en: What filthy things my heart is capable of.
uz: Qalbim qanday iflos ishlarga qodir!

en: Yes, filthy above all, disgusting, loathsome, loathsome!
uz: Ha, barcha narsadan ustun, iflos, jirkanch, jirkanch!

en: — and for a whole month I’ve been.
uz: va to'liq bir oy davomida bo'lganman.

en: …” But no words, no exclamations,
uz: Ammo so'zlar yo'q, ovozlar yo'q,

en: could express his agitation.
uz: o'z xavotirini ifodalashi mumkin edi.

en: The feeling of intense repulsion, which had begun to oppress and torture his heart while he was on his way to the old woman, had by now reached such a pitch and had taken such a definite form that he did not know what to do with himself to escape from his wretchedness.
uz: Qariya ayolga borayotganida uning qalbini qiynalgan va qiynalgan kuchli jirkanch hissiyot hozircha shunchalik kuchli bo'lib, o'ziga o'xshaydigan bo'ldiki, u o'z qashshoqligidan qochib ketish uchun o'zi bilan nima qilishni bilmasdi.

en: He walked along the pavement like a drunken man, regardless of the passersby, and jostling against them, and only came to his senses when he was in the next street.
uz: U yo'lovchilarga qaramasdan piyoz odam kabi yo'ldan o'tib, ularga qarshi shovqin qilib yurardi va faqat yonidagi ko'chada bo'lganida aqlga kirdi.

en: Looking round, he noticed that he was standing close to a tavern which was entered by steps leading from the pavement to the basement.
uz: U atrofini ko'rib, yonboshiga yo'l qo'yib, yo'ldan pastga olib boradigan qadamlar orqali kiradigan mehmonxona yaqinida turganini payqadi.

en: At that instant two drunken men came out at the door, and abusing and supporting one another, they mounted the steps.
uz: O'sha zahoti eshikdan ikki mast kishi chiqib, bir-birlarini zo'ravonlik qilib, qo'llab-quvvatlab, qadamlar ustiga chiqishdi.

en: Without stopping to think, Raskolnikov went down the steps at once.
uz: Raskolnikov o'ylab ko'rmay, darhol qadamlar ustiga tushdi.

en: Till that moment he had never been into a tavern, but now he felt giddy and was tormented by a burning thirst.
uz: O'sha paytgacha u hech qachon mehmonxonaga kirmagan edi, lekin endi u o'zini ko'ngli to'lib, yonayotgan chanqaganlik bilan azob chekkan edi.

en: He longed for a drink of cold beer, and attributed his sudden weakness to the want of food.
uz: U sovuq pivo ichishni orzu qilib, o'zining to'satdan zaifligini oziq-ovqat yetishmovchiligiga bog'ladi.

en: He sat down at a sticky little table in a dark and dirty corner; ordered some beer, and eagerly drank off the first glassful.
uz: U qorong'i va kirli burchada bo'lgan kichkina qo'pol stolga o'tirdi; biror pivo buyurtma qildi va birinchi shishaga charchagancha ichdi.

en: At once he felt easier; and his thoughts became clear.
uz: O'zini o'sha zahoti yengilroq his qildi va o'z fikrlari aniq bo'ldi.

en: “All that’s nonsense,” he said hopefully, “and there is nothing in it all to worry about!
uz: Bularning barchasi behuda, - dedi u umid bilan, - va bularning barchasida tashvishlanish uchun hech narsa yo'q!

en: It’s simply physical derangement.
uz: Bu shunchaki jismoniy xafagarchilik.

en: Just a glass of beer, a piece of dry bread —and in one moment the brain is stronger, the mind is clearer and the will is firm!
uz: Faqat bir stakan pivo, bir stakan quruq non va bir lahzada miyaning kuchi, ong va irodasi mustahkamlanadi!

en: Phew, how utterly petty it all is!” But in spite of this scornful reflection, he was by now looking cheerful as though he were suddenly set free from a terrible burden: and he gazed round in a friendly way at the people in the room.
uz: Bularning barchasi naqadar kichik! Ammo bu masxara qiluvchi fikrga qaramay, u birdan dahshatli og'irlikdan ozod bo'lgan kabi xursand ko'rinishga ega edi: u xonada bo'lgan odamlarga do'stona qarab turdi.

en: But even at that moment he had a dim foreboding that this happier frame of mind was also not normal.
uz: Ammo hatto o'sha paytda ham u bu baxtli fikrlash tarzi ham normal emasligini bilgan.

en: There were few people at the time in the tavern.
uz: O'sha paytda mehmonxonada kamdan-kam odam bo'lgan.

en: Besides the two drunken men he had met on the steps, a group consisting of about five men and a girl with a concertina had gone out at the same time.
uz: U mertalarda uchratgan ikki mast odamdan tashqari, bir vaqtning o'zida besh nafar erkak va konsertinaga ega bo'lgan bir qizdan iborat guruh tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Their departure left the room quiet and rather empty.
uz: Ularning ketishi xonani tinch va umuman bo'sh qoldirdi.

en: The persons still in the tavern were a man who appeared to be an artisan, drunk, but not extremely so, sitting before a pot of beer, and his companion, a huge, stout man with a grey beard, in a short full-skirted coat.
uz: Mehmonxonada hali ham bo'lganlar - hunarmand, mast, lekin juda ham yomon bo'lmagan, bir qadoq piva oldida o'tirgan bir kishi va uning hamkori, katta, bo'lakli, chiroyli, qisqa, to'liq kiyimli ko'ylakda bo'lgan katta, kuchli kishi edi.

en: He was very drunk: and had dropped asleep on the bench; every now and then, he began as though in his sleep, cracking his fingers, with
uz: U juda mast edi va bankda uxlab ketardi; vaqti-vaqti bilan u o'z uyqusida bo'lgani kabi, barmoqlarini teshiklab, o'z qo'llarini teshiklab yurardi.

en: his arms wide apart and the upper part of his body bounding about on the bench, while he hummed some meaningless refrain, trying to recall some such lines as these: “His wife a year he fondly loved  His wife a —a year he —fondly loved.” Or suddenly waking up again: “Walking along the crowded row  He met the one he used to know.” But no one shared his enjoyment: his silent companion looked with positive hostility and mistrust at all these manifestations.
uz: Qo'llari keng bo'lib, tanasining yuqori qismlari bankda o'tirganida, u ma'nosiz o'rinni o'tkazdi va quyidagi so'zlarni eslab qolishga harakat qildi: Xotiniga bir yil o'zi yaxshi ko'rgan. Xotiniga bir yil o'zi yaxshi ko'rgan. Yoki to'satdan yana uyg'onadi: Xolib qatorda yurib, u ilgari bilgan kishi bilan uchrashdi. Ammo hech kim uning zavqini bo'lishmadi: uning sessiz hamkasbi bu ko'rinishlarga nisbatan ijobiy dushmanlik va ishonchsizlik bilan qaradi.

en: There was another man in the room who looked somewhat like a retired government clerk.
uz: Xonada boshqa bir odam bor edi, u pensiyalangan hukumat ishchisiga o'xshaydigan edi.

en: He was sitting apart, now and then sipping from his pot and looking round at the company.
uz: U bir-biridan ajralib o'tirardi, vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zining idishidan ichib, atrofini ko'rib turardi.

en: He, too, appeared to be in some agitation.
uz: U ham biroz g'ayratli bo'lib ko'rindi.

en: II Raskolnikov was not used to crowds, and, as we said before, he avoided society of every sort, more especially of late.
uz: II Raskolnikov ko'pchilik bilan tanish bo'lmagan va biz ilgari aytib o'tganimizdek, u har qanday jamiyatdan qochgan, ayniqsa oxirgi paytlarda.

en: But now all at once he felt a desire to be with other people.
uz: Ammo hozir u boshqa odamlar bilan bo'lishga istak ko'rsatdi.

en: Something new seemed to be taking place within him, and with it he felt a sort of thirst for company.
uz: Uning ichida yangi narsa sodir bo'layotganini sezdi va u o'zi bilan bir xil kompaniyaga chanqoqlikni his qildi.

en: He was so weary after a whole month of concentrated wretchedness and gloomy excitement that he longed to rest, if only for a moment, in some other world, whatever it might be; and, in spite of the filthiness of the surroundings, he was glad now to stay in the tavern.
uz: U bir oy davomida g'amginlik va g'alati hayajon bilan shug'ullanishdan keyin juda charchagan edi, hatto bir daqiqa uchun ham boshqa bir dunyoda dam olishni orzu qilardi va atrofdagi buzuqlikka qaramay, endi o'z mehmonxonasida qolishdan mamnun edi.

en: The master of the establishment was in another room, but he frequently came down some steps into the main room, his jaunty, tarred boots with red turnover tops coming into view each time before the rest of his person.
uz: Ma'muriyat xo'jayini boshqa xonada edi, lekin u tez-tez asosiy xonada bir nechta qadamlar pastga tushardi, uning jaunty, qizil aylanma to'plari bo'lgan qovurilgan poyabzallari har safar uning qolgan qismi oldida ko'rinardi.

en: He wore a full coat and a horribly greasy black satin waistcoat, with no cravat, and his whole face seemed smeared with oil like an iron lock.
uz: U to'liq kiyim va qo'rqinchli yog'li qora satin kiyim kiygan edi, kravatsiz edi va butun yuzida temir qulf kabi yog' bilan to'ldirilgan ko'rinardi.

en: At the counter stood a boy of about fourteen, and there was another boy somewhat younger who handed whatever was wanted.
uz: Soxtaxonada taxminan o'n to'rt yoshli o'g'il turgan edi va undan biroz kichikroq bo'lgan boshqa o'g'il bor edi.

en: On the counter lay some sliced cucumber, some pieces of dried black bread, and some fish, chopped up small, all smelling very bad.
uz: Soxtaxonada bir necha bo'lak cho'g'i, bir necha bo'lak quruq qora non va kichik bo'lak bo'lak bo'lak bo'lgan baliq bor edi va ularning hammasi juda yomon xushbo'y edi.

en: It was insufferably close, and so heavy with the fumes of spirits that five minutes in such an atmosphere might well make a man drunk.
uz: U juda yaqin edi va ichimliklar tutunlari shunchalik og'ir ediki, bunday muhitda besh daqiqa odamni mast qilishi mumkin edi.

en: There are chance meetings with strangers that interest us from the first moment, before a word is spoken.
uz: O'zgalar bilan yuzaki uchrashuvlar bor, ular bizni birinchi daqiqadan, so'z aytishdan oldin qiziqtiradi.

en: Such was the impression made on Raskolnikov by the person sitting a little distance from him, who looked like a retired clerk.
uz: Raskolnikovga undan biroz uzoqlikda o'tirgan va pensiyalangan ishbilarmon kabi ko'rinadigan kishi shunday taassurot qoldirdi.

en: The young man often recalled this impression afterwards, and even ascribed it to presentiment.
uz: Yosh yigit ko'pincha keyinchalik bu taassurotni eslab turardi va hatto uni hissiyotga asoslab qo'ygan.

en: He looked repeatedly at the clerk, partly no doubt because the latter was
uz: U ko'p marotaba xizmatkorga qarab turardi, ehtimol, buning sababi, u o'z ishini o'zi bajarganidan iborat edi.

en: staring persistently at him, obviously anxious to enter into conversation.
uz: U o'ziga qaraydigan, suhbatga kirishmoqchi bo'lgan kishi.

en: At the other persons in the room, including the tavern- keeper, the clerk looked as though he were used to their company, and weary of it, showing a shade of condescending contempt for them as persons of station and culture inferior to his own, with whom it would be useless for him to converse.
uz: Xonadagi boshqa odamlarga, shu jumladan, mehmonxona nazoratchisiga qaraganda, xizmatkor ularning kompaniyasiga odatlangan va charchagan bo'lib ko'rinardi, ular uchun o'zidan past bo'lgan mavqe va madaniyatga ega bo'lgan, ular bilan suhbatlashish foydasiz bo'lgan odamlarga nisbatan kamtarlik bilan hurmatsizlik ko'rsatardi.

en: He was a man over fifty, bald and grizzled, of medium height, and stoutly built.
uz: U ellik yoshdan oshgan, soqov va grizzled, o'rta balandlik va kuchli qurilgan bir odam edi.

en: His face, bloated from continual drinking, was of a yellow, even greenish, tinge, with swollen eyelids out of which keen reddish eyes gleamed like little chinks.
uz: Uning yuzi doimiy ichishdan puflangan, sariq, hatto yashil rangli, ko'z qo'lqoplari puchgan va ko'zlari qizil rangli bo'lib, kichkinagina cho'g'lar kabi parvarishlagan.

en: But there was something very strange in him; there was a light in his eyes as though of intense feeling —perhaps there were even thought and intelligence, but at the same time there was a gleam of something like madness.
uz: Ammo uning ichida juda g'alati bir narsa bor edi; uning ko'zlarida kuchli his-tuyg'u kabi nur bor edi. ~ Ehtimol, hatto fikr va aql-idrok ham bor edi, lekin bir vaqtning o'zida aqlsizlik kabi bir narsa nurlari paydo bo'lgan.

en: He was wearing an old and hopelessly ragged black dress coat, with all its buttons missing except one, and that one he had buttoned, evidently clinging to this last trace of respectability.
uz: U eski va umidsizlikka cho'zilgan qora libos kiyinayotgan edi, bitta tugmani qo'yib, uning barcha tugmalari yo'q edi va u tugmalar ustiga tugmalar ushlagan edi.

en: A crumpled shirt front, covered with spots and stains, protruded from his canvas waistcoat.
uz: Uning maydon kiyimidan ko'rinadigan, mayda-mayda bo'laklar bilan qoplangan bo'g'irlangan ko'ylakning old qismi ko'rindi.

en: Like a clerk, he wore no beard, nor moustache, but had been so long unshaven that his chin looked like a stiff greyish brush.
uz: Klerk kabi u soqol ham, mustax ham ko'tarmagan, lekin shunchalik uzoq vaqtga qadar sochlari kesilmagan ediki, uning qani qattiq bo'lak kabi ko'rinardi.

en: And there was something respectable and like an official about his manner too.
uz: Uning xulq-atvorida ham hurmatga sazovor va mansabdor shaxs kabi bir narsa bor edi.

en: But he was restless; he ruffled up his hair and from time to time let his head drop into his hands dejectedly resting his ragged elbows on the stained and sticky table.
uz: Ammo u bezovta edi; sochlarini o'rab olib, vaqti-vaqti bilan boshini qo'llariga tushirib qo'ydi va o'z qo'lquruq qo'lquruqlarini bo'g'in va yopishqoq stolga qo'ydi.

en: At last he looked straight at Raskolnikov, and said loudly and resolutely: “May I venture, honoured sir, to engage you in polite conversation?
uz: Nihoyat, u Raskolnikovga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qarab, baland ovozda va qat'iylik bilan shunday dedi: "Mening jasoratim bormi, aziz sir, siz bilan xushmuomala suhbatni boshlashga?

en: Forasmuch as, though your exterior would not command respect, my experience admonishes me that you are a man of education and not accustomed to drinking.
uz: Garchi tashqi ko'rinishingiz hurmatga sazovor bo'lmasa-da, tajribam menga siz o'qigan va ichishga moyil bo'lmagan odam ekanligingizni eslatmoqda.

en: I have always respected education when in conjunction with genuine sentiments, and I am besides a titular counsellor in rank.
uz: Haqiqiy his-tuyg'ular bilan bog'liq bo'lganda, men har doim ta'limga hurmat ko'rsatib kelganman va men, shuningdek, mavzuga ega bo'lgan maslahatchiman.

en: Marmeladov —such is my name; titular counsellor.
uz: Marmeladov such is my name; titular maslahatchi.

en: I make bold to inquire —have you been in the service?” “No, I am studying,” answered the young man, somewhat surprised at the grandiloquent style of the speaker and also at being so directly addressed.
uz: Siz xizmatda bo'lganmisiz? - deb so'rashga jur'at qilaman. - Yo'q, men o'rganyapman, - deb javob berdi yigit, gapiruvchining buyuk ruhli uslubidan va shu qadar bevosita murojaat qilinayotganidan biroz hayron qolgan.

en: In spite of the momentary desire he had just been feeling for company of any sort, on being actually spoken to he
uz: O'sha paytdagi istaklariga qaramay, u shunchaki biron bir kompaniyani his qilgan edi, lekin u bilan gaplashishga haqli edi.

en: felt immediately his habitual irritable and uneasy aversion for any stranger who approached or attempted to approach him.
uz: O'zining odatdagidek g'azabga to'lgan va unga yaqinlashadigan yoki yaqinlashishga urinadigan har qanday begona kishiga nisbatan g'azablanishini darhol sezdi.

en: “A student then, or formerly a student,” cried the clerk.
uz: O'shanda o'quvchi yoki sobiq o'quvchi o'qituvchiga baqirdi.

en: “Just what I thought!
uz: Men o'ylaganday bo'ldi!

en: I’m a man of experience, immense experience, sir,” and he tapped his forehead with his fingers in self-approval.
uz: Men tajribaga ega bo'lgan, ulkan tajribaga ega bo'lgan odamman, xonim, va u o'zini tan olish uchun barmoqlari bilan oyoq boshiga urdi.

en: “You’ve been a student or have attended some learned institution!
uz: Siz o'quvchi bo'lgansiz yoki biror bilimli muassasaga o'qigansiz!

en: …” He got up, staggered, took up his jug and glass, and sat down beside the young man, facing him a little sideways.
uz: U o'rnidan turdi, cho'kdi, qozonini va shishalarini olib, yigitning yonida o'tirdi va unga biroz yonboshi bo'lib qaradi.

en: He was drunk, but spoke fluently and boldly, only occasionally losing the thread of his sentences and drawling his words.
uz: U mast edi, ammo oqilona va jasoratli gapirgan, lekin vaqti-vaqti bilan gaplarning ipini yo'qotgan va so'zlarini o'zgartirgan.

en: He pounced upon Raskolnikov as greedily as though he too had not spoken to a soul for a month.
uz: U Raskolnikovga xuddi o'zi ham bir oy davomida hech kim bilan gaplashmagan kabi ochko'zlik bilan qarshilik ko'rsatdi.

en: “Honoured sir,” he began almost with solemnity, “poverty is not a vice, that’s a true saying.
uz: Honourable sir, u deyarli tantanali ravishda boshladi, xumlik yomonlik emas, bu haq gap.

en: Yet I know too that drunkenness is not a virtue, and that that’s even truer.
uz: Ammo men ham spirtli ichimlik fazilat emasligini bilaman va bu hali ham haq.

en: But beggary, honoured sir, beggary is a vice.
uz: Ammo so'rab-so'rab yurish, xonim, so'rab-so'rab yurish - bu yomonlikdir.

en: In poverty you may still retain your innate nobility of soul, but in beggary —never —no one.
uz: Kambag'allikda siz hali ham o'zingizning tug'ma ruhingiz borligini saqlab qolishingiz mumkin, lekin so'rab-so'rab yurishda hech kim yo'q.

en: For beggary a man is not chased out of human society with a stick, he is swept out with a broom, so as to make it as humiliating as possible; and quite right, too, forasmuch as in beggary I am ready to be the first to humiliate myself.
uz: So'roqchilik uchun odam odam odamzod jamiyatidan tayoq bilan quvib chiqarilmaydi, balki uni o'zini imkon qadar kamsitadigan qilib ko'rsatish uchun idish bilan olib tashlaydilar; va bu ham to'g'ri, chunki so'roqchilikda men o'zimni kamsitadigan birinchi bo'lishga tayyorman.

en: Honoured sir, a month ago Mr.
uz: Oliy ruhoniy, bir oy oldin Mr.

en: Lebeziatnikov gave my wife a beating, and my wife is a very different matter from me!
uz: Lebeziatnikov xotinimni urdi va xotinim men bilan juda farq qiladi!

en: Allow me to ask you another question out of simple curiosity: have you ever spent a night on a hay barge, on the Neva?” “No, I have not happened to,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Sizlarga oddiy qiziqish bilan yana bir savol berishga ruxsat bering: siz hech qachon nevadagi hay kemasida kechani o'tkazganmisiz?Yo'q, men bunday qilmaganman, Raskolnikov javob berdi.

en: “What do you mean?” “Well, I’ve just come from one and it’s the fifth night I’ve slept so.
uz: Nima demoqchi ekansiz?

en: …” He filled his glass, emptied it and paused.
uz: ... O'zining shishalarini to'ldirdi, uni bo'shatdi va to'xtadi.

en: Bits of hay were in fact clinging to his clothes and sticking to his hair.
uz: Aslida, o'g'ilning kiyim-kechaklariga va sochlariga yopishib qolgan cho'g'lar bor edi.

en: It seemed quite probable that he had not undressed or washed for the last five days.
uz: Oxirgi besh kun davomida u kiyimlarini yo'qotgan yoki yuvmaganligi ehtimoldan yiroq emas edi.

en: His hands, particularly, were filthy.
uz: Ayniqsa, uning qo'llari iflos edi.

en: They were fat and red, with black nails.
uz: Ular yog'i va qizil, qora to'g'rilar bilan.

en: His conversation seemed to excite a general though languid interest.
uz: Uning suhbatlari umumiy, garchi kam bo'lsa-da, qiziqish uyg'otganga o'xshaydi.

en: The boys at the counter fell to sniggering.
uz: Soxtaxonadagi yigitlar o'zlarining ko'ngillarini yig'ib qo'yishdi.

en: The innkeeper came down from the upper room, apparently on purpose to listen to the “funny fellow” and sat down at a little distance, yawning lazily, but
uz: Mehmonxona egasi yuqoridagi xonadan tushdi, ko'rinib turibdiki, u o'yinchoqlarni tinglash uchun o'tirdi va biroz uzoqlikda o'tirdi.

en: Evidently Marmeladov was a familiar figure here, and he had most likely acquired his weakness for high-flown speeches from the habit of frequently entering into conversation with strangers of all sorts in the tavern.
uz: Ko'rinib turganidek, Marmeladov bu yerda tanish shaxs edi va u, ehtimol, sovrinda turli xil begona odamlar bilan tez-tez suhbatlashish odatidan yuqori martabali nutqlarga bo'lgan zaifligini o'zlashtirgan.

en: This habit develops into a necessity in some drunkards, and especially in those who are looked after sharply and kept in order at home.
uz: Bu odat ba'zi ichkilikbozlarda, ayniqsa, uyda qattiq g'amxo'rlik ko'rsatib, tartibni saqlashda zarur bo'lib qolmoqda.

en: Hence in the company of other drinkers they try to justify themselves and even if possible obtain consideration.
uz: Shuning uchun ular boshqa ichuvchilar bilan birga o'zlarini oqlashga harakat qilishadi va hatto iloji bo'lsa ham, e'tiborga olishadi.

en: “Funny fellow!” pronounced the innkeeper.
uz: Funny fellow! so'zlab o'tgan mehmonxona xodimi.

en: “And why don’t you work, why aren’t you at your duty, if you are in the service?” “Why am I not at my duty, honoured sir,” Marmeladov went on, addressing himself exclusively to Raskolnikov, as though it had been he who put that question to him.
uz: Va nega siz ishlamasiz, xizmatda bo'lsangiz, nega sizning vazifangizda emassiz? Nega men o'z vazifamda emasman, aziz sir, Marmeladov davom etdi va Raskolnikovga faqat o'zini murojaat qildi, xuddi u o'zi unga bu savolni bergan bo'lsa.

en: “Why am I not at my duty?
uz: Nima uchun men o'z vazifamni bajarmayapman?

en: Does not my heart ache to think what a useless worm I am?
uz: Men qanday yaramas qurt ekanligim haqida o'ylash yuragimni og'ritmaydimi?

en: A month ago when Mr.
uz: Bir oy oldin Mr.

en: Lebeziatnikov beat my wife with his own hands, and I lay drunk, didn’t I suffer?
uz: Lebeziatnikov xotinimni o'z qo'li bilan uribdi va men mast bo'lib yotdim, men azob chekmadimmi?

en: Excuse me, young man, has it ever happened to you … hm … well, to petition hopelessly for a loan?” “Yes, it has.
uz: Kechirasiz, yigit, sizga hech qachon ... hm ... yaxshi, umidsiz ravishda qarz olish uchun ariza berish sodir bo'lganmi?Ha, shunday.

en: But what do you mean by hopelessly?” “Hopelessly in the fullest sense, when you know beforehand that you will get nothing by it.
uz: Ammo umidsizlik deb nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?Tamom ma'noda umidsizlik, agar siz oldindan bilsangiz, bu sizga hech narsa keltirmaydi.

en: You know, for instance, beforehand with positive certainty that this man, this most reputable and exemplary citizen, will on no consideration give you money; and indeed I ask you why should he?
uz: Misol uchun, siz ushbu odam, bu eng yaxshi va namunali fuqaro, sizga pul bermasligini oldindan aniq bilgansiz; va men sizga nima uchun berishini so'rayman?

en: For he knows of course that I shan’t pay it back.
uz: Albatta, u o'zi biladiki, men uni qaytarib bermayman.

en: Lebeziatnikov who keeps up with modern ideas explained the other day that compassion is forbidden nowadays by science itself, and that that’s what is done now in England, where there is political economy.
uz: Zamonaviy g'oyalarni qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan Lebeziatnikov bir kun oldin shuni tushuntirib berdiki, hozirgi paytda hamdardlik fanning o'zi tomonidan taqiqlangan va hozirgi kunda siyosiy iqtisodiyot mavjud bo'lgan Angliyada shunaqa ishlar amalga oshirilmoqda.

en: Why, I ask you, should he give it to me?
uz: Nima uchun, deb so'rayman, u menga berish kerakmi?

en: And yet though I know beforehand that he won’t, I set off to him and …” “Why do you go?” put in Raskolnikov.
uz: Ammo, uning yo'qligini oldindan bilsam-da, men uning yoniga bordim va Raskolnikovni o'rnatdim.

en: “Well, when one has no one, nowhere else one can go!
uz: Ha, agar hech kim bo'lmasa, boshqa hech bir joyga borolmaydi!

en: For every man must have somewhere to go.
uz: Chunki har bir odamning boradigan joyi bo'lishi kerak.

en: Since there are times when one absolutely must go somewhere!
uz: Chunki ba'zi paytlarda biror joyga borish kerak!

en: When my own daughter first went out with a yellow ticket, then I had to go … (for my daughter has a yellow passport),” he added in parenthesis, looking with a certain uneasiness at the young man.
uz: O'z qizim birinchi marta sariq chipta bilan chiqqanida, men ketishim kerak edi... (qizim sariq pasportga ega bo'lgani uchun), u o'z ko'zlari bilan yosh yigitga qarab qo'ydi.

en: “No matter, sir, no matter!” he went on hurriedly and with apparent composure when both the boys at the counter guffawed and even the innkeeper smiled —“No matter, I am
uz: Boshimchalik emas, xo'jayinim, hech narsa emas! U shoshilinch va ko'rinadigan xotirjamlik bilan davom etdi, chunki jangxonadagi yigitlar ham g'ofillashib, hatto mehmonxona egasi ham tabassum qildi.Boshimchalik emas, men shundayman

en: not confounded by the wagging of their heads; for everyone knows everything about it already, and all that is secret is made open.
uz: Boshlarini larzaga solishdan xafa bo'lmaslik kerak, chunki hamma bu haqda allaqachon hamma narsani biladi va yashirin narsa oshkor bo'ladi.

en: And I accept it all, not with contempt, but with humility.
uz: Men hammasini kamsitish bilan emas, kamtarlik bilan qabul qilaman.

en: ‘Behold the man!’ Excuse me, young man, can you.
uz: Mana bu odam! Kechirasiz, yosh yigit, qila olasizmi?

en: … No, to put it more strongly and more distinctly; not can you but dare you, looking upon me, assert that I am not a pig?” The young man did not answer a word.
uz: Yo'q, aniqroq va qat'iyroq aytganda, menga qarab, men cho'chqa emasligimni aytishga jur'at qila olasizmi? Yosh yigit bir so'z ham javob bermadi.

en: “Well,” the orator began again stolidly and with even increased dignity, after waiting for the laughter in the room to subside.
uz: Navoiy xonada kulgi susayishini kutgandan so'ng, yana bir bor qat'iy va hatto qadr-qimmatga ega bo'lib, gapni boshladi.

en: “Well, so be it, I am a pig, but she is a lady!
uz: Ha, shunday bo'lsin, men do'stman, lekin u xonim!

en: I have the semblance of a beast, but Katerina Ivanovna, my spouse, is a person of education and an officer’s daughter.
uz: Men hayvonga o'xshayman, lekin turmush o'rtog'im Katerina Ivanovna ta'lim olgan odam va ofitserning qizi.

en: Granted, granted, I am a scoundrel, but she is a woman of a noble heart, full of sentiments, refined by education.
uz: To'g'ri, albatta, men qo'pol odamman, lekin u xushmuomala, his-tuyg'ularga to'la, ta'lim bilan soflashtirilgan ayol.

en: And yet … oh, if only she felt for me!
uz: Lekin... ah, agar u men uchun hamdard bo'lganida edi!

en: Honoured sir, honoured sir, you know every man ought to have at least one place where people feel for him!
uz: Hurmatli xonim, siz bilamanki, har bir odamda hech bo'lmaganda bir joy bo'lishi kerak, unda odamlar unga nisbatan his-tuyg'u ko'rsatishlari kerak!

en: But Katerina Ivanovna, though she is magnanimous, she is unjust.
uz: Ammo Katerina Ivanovna, agar u mehribon bo'lsa-da, adolatsiz.

en: … And yet, although I realise that when she pulls my hair she only does it out of pity —for I repeat without being ashamed, she pulls my hair, young man,” he declared with redoubled dignity, hearing the sniggering again —“but, my God, if she would but once.
uz: Shunga qaramay, u sochlarimni tortib olganda, uni faqat rahm-shafqatdan qilishini tushunaman, chunki men qayta aytaman, u o'zimdan uyalmay, sochlarimni tortib oldim, yosh yigit, - dedi u ikki marta ko'proq qadr-qimmat bilan, yana bir marta qichqirishni eshitib. - Lekin, ey Xudoyim, agar u bir marta qilsa.

en: It’s all in vain and it’s no use talking!
uz: Bularning barchasi behuda va gapirishning foydasi yo'q!

en: For more than once, my wish did come true and more than once she has felt for me but … such is my fate and I am a beast by nature!” “Rather!” assented the innkeeper yawning.
uz: Bir martadan ko'proq vaqt davomida orzuim ro'yobga chiqdi va bir martadan ko'proq vaqt davomida u men uchun hissa qo'shdi, lekin... bu mening taqdirim va men tabiatimdan hayvonman! Aksincha! - deb qo'shib qo'ydi mehmonxona egasi.

en: Marmeladov struck his fist resolutely on the table.
uz: Marmeladov o'z yumushini jadvalga qat'iy urdi.

en: Do you know, sir, do you know, I have sold her very stockings for drink?
uz: Bilasizmi, xo'jayinim, bilasizmi, men uning juda ko'p cho'tkalarini ichimlik uchun sotdim?

en: Not her shoes —that would be more or less in the order of things, but her stockings, her stockings I have sold for drink!
uz: Uning poyabzallari emas, balki men ichimlik uchun sotgan choriqlari, choriqlari!

en: Her mohair shawl I sold for drink, a present to her long ago, her own property, not mine; and we live in a cold room and she caught cold this winter and has begun coughing and spitting blood too.
uz: Uning mohair shali men ichimlik uchun sotdim, uning uchun uzoq vaqt oldin sovg'a, mening emas, balki uning mulkidir; biz sovuq xonada yashayapmiz va u shu qishda sovuqga tushdi va o'zi ham qo'shishni va qon tupurishni boshladi.

en: We have three little children and Katerina Ivanovna is at work from morning till night; she is scrubbing and cleaning and washing the children, for she’s been used to cleanliness from a child.
uz: Uch nafar kichkina farzandimiz bor va Katerina Ivanovna ertalabdan kechagacha ishda bo'lib, bolalarni tozalab, tozalab, yuvish bilan shug'ullanadi, chunki u bolaligidanoq tozalikka odatlanib kelgan.

en: But her chest is weak and she has a tendency to consumption and I feel it!
uz: Ammo uning ko'kraklari zaif va u iste'mol qilishga moyil va men buni his qilaman!

en: Do you suppose I don’t feel it?
uz: Men buni his qilmayapman deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: And the more I drink the more I feel it.
uz: Va qancha ko'proq ichsam, shuncha ko'proq his qilaman.

en: That’s why I drink too.
uz: Shuning uchun men ham ichaman.

en: I try to find sympathy and feeling in drink.
uz: Men ichganimda hamdardlik va his-tuyg'u izlashga harakat qilaman.

en: drink so that I may suffer twice as much!” And as though in despair he laid his head down on the table.
uz: Men ikki baravar ko'proq azob chekishim uchun ichaman! Va xuddi umidsizlikka tushib, boshini stol ustiga qo'ygan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “Young man,” he went on, raising his head again, “in your face I seem to read some trouble of mind.
uz: Yosh yigit yana boshini ko'tarib, o'z ko'zidan ko'nglingni ko'tarib, ko'nglingni ko'tarib ko'rdim.

en: When you came in I read it, and that was why I addressed you at once.
uz: Sen kirganingda men uni o'qib chiqdim va shuning uchun darhol senga murojaat qildim.

en: For in unfolding to you the story of my life, I do not wish to make myself a laughingstock before these idle listeners, who indeed know all about it already, but I am looking for a man of feeling and education.
uz: Sizlarga hayotimning hikoyasini aytib berganda, men o'zimni bu behuda tinglovchilarning oldida kulgili qilmoqchi emasman, chunki ular bu haqda allaqachon hamma narsani bilishadi, lekin men his-tuyg'u va ta'limga ega bo'lgan kishini izlayapman.

en: Know then that my wife was educated in a high-class school for the daughters of noblemen, and on leaving she danced the shawl dance before the governor and other personages for which she was presented with a gold medal and a certificate of merit.
uz: O'zingiz bilingki, xotinim azizlarning qizlari uchun yuqori darajadagi maktabda o'qigan va ketgach, gubernator va boshqa shaxslarga shawl raqsini o'tkazgan va buning uchun unga oltin medal va mukofot berilgan.

en: The medal … well, the medal of course was sold —long ago, hm … but the certificate of merit is in her trunk still and not long ago she showed it to our landlady.
uz: Medaliyani ... albatta, medali uzoq vaqt oldin sotilgan edi, lekin mukofotnomasi hali ham uning bagajida va yaqinda u uni uy egasiga ko'rsatdi.

en: And although she is most continually on bad terms with the landlady, yet she wanted to tell someone or other of her past honours and of the happy days that are gone.
uz: Garchi u uy egasi bilan doimo yomon munosabatda bo'lsa-da, o'tmishdagi sharaflari va o'tgan baxtli kunlari haqida kimgadir aytmoqchi edi.

en: I don’t condemn her for it, I don’t blame her, for the one thing left her is recollection of the past, and all the rest is dust and ashes.
uz: Men uni ayblamayman, uni ayblamayman, chunki unga qolgan yagona narsa o'tmish xotirasidir, qolganlari esa tuproq va kul bo'lib qoladi.
