en: Would it not be better to go somewhere far off, to the Islands again, and there hide the things in some solitary place, in a wood or under a bush, and mark the spot perhaps?” And though he felt incapable of clear judgment, the idea seemed to him a sound one.
uz: Uzoq bir joyga, yana orollarga borib, o't o'rmon yoki buta ostida biron bir yolg'iz joyda narsalarni yashirib, ehtimol bu joyni belgilab qo'yish yaxshiroq emasmi? Va u o'zini aniq hukm qilishga qodir emas deb his qilgan bo'lsa-da, bu g'oya unga to'g'ri tuyulgan.

en: But he was not destined to go there.
uz: Ammo u o'sha yerga borishga moyil emas edi.

en: For coming out of V — — Prospect towards the square, he saw on the left a passage leading between two blank walls to a courtyard.
uz: V   Prospect-dan tashqariga chiqib, maydonga qarab chiqishi uchun u chap tomonda ikki bo'sh devor o'rtasida hovli tomon olib boradigan o'tish joyini ko'rdi.

en: On the right hand, the blank unwhitewashed wall of a four-storied house stretched far into the court; on the left, a wooden hoarding ran parallel with it for twenty paces into the court, and then turned sharply to the left.
uz: O'ng tomonda to'rt qavatli uyning oq bo'lmagan devorlari cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan hovligacha tarqalib ketgan edi; chap tomonda esa o'g'ir cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'qqisidan cho'g'isidan cho'zib ketgan edi.

en: Here was a deserted fenced-off place where rubbish of different sorts was lying.
uz: Bu yerda turli xil axlatlar yotgan cho'loq, to'siqli joy edi.

en: At the end of the court, the corner of a low, smutty, stone shed, apparently part of some workshop, peeped from behind the hoarding.
uz: hovlisining oxirida past, nopok, tosh shedning burchagida, ko'rinib turganidek, biror ishxonadan bir qismi bo'lgan, xonadonning orqasidan ko'rinardi.

en: It was probably a carriage builder’s or carpenter’s shed; the whole place from the entrance was black with coal dust.
uz: Ehtimol, u vagon quruvchilari yoki o'g'irchoqlar shahriga aylangan bo'lishi mumkin edi; kirishdan butun joy qora va ko'mir changidan qoplangan edi.

en: Here would be the place to throw
uz: Bu erda tashlash uchun joy bo'ladi

en: Not seeing anyone in the yard, he slipped in, and at once saw near the gate a sink, such as is often put in yards where there are many workmen or cabdrivers; and on the hoarding above had been scribbled in chalk the time-honoured witticism, “Standing here strictly forbidden.” This was all the better, for there would be nothing suspicious about his going in.
uz: Yigʻilish zavodida hech kimni koʻrmay, u kirib kirdi va darhol darvoza yaqinida ishchilar yoki taksi haydovchilari koʻp boʻlgan hovlilarda koʻp joylashtiriladigan choʻkuvni koʻrdi; yuqoridagi yigʻilish zavodida esa vaqtdan beri hurmatga sazovor boʻlgan sehrgarlik, "Bu yerda toʻliq taqiqlangan" deb yozilgan edi.Bu shunchalik yaxshi edi, chunki uning kirishi hech qanday shubhali boʻlmasdi.

en: “Here I could throw it all in a heap and get away!” Looking round once more, with his hand already in his pocket, he noticed against the outer wall, between the entrance and the sink, a big unhewn stone, weighing perhaps sixty pounds.
uz: Bu yerda men hamma narsani to'plamga tashlab, qochib ketishim mumkin edi! O'z atrofini yana bir bor ko'rib, qo'li allaqachon kiyimida bo'lganida, u kirish va issiqxona o'rtasida tashqi devorga qarshi, ehtimol oltmish funt og'irligi bo'lgan katta o'qmagan toshni ko'rdi.

en: The other side of the wall was a street.
uz: Devorning boshqa tomonida ko'cha bor edi.

en: He could hear passersby, always numerous in that part, but he could not be seen from the entrance, unless someone came in from the street, which might well happen indeed, so there was need of haste.
uz: U o'tib ketayotganlarning ovozini eshitardi, bu yerda ular doim ko'p edi, lekin ko'chadan kimdir kirmasa, uni ko'rish mumkin emas edi, chunki bu sodir bo'lishi mumkin edi, shuning uchun shoshilinchlik kerak edi.

en: He bent down over the stone, seized the top of it firmly in both hands, and using all his strength turned it over.
uz: U tosh ustiga yiqilib, uning yuqori qismini ikkala qo'lida qattiq ushlab, butun kuchini ishga solib, uni burib yubordi.

en: Under the stone was a small hollow in the ground, and he immediately emptied his pocket into it.
uz: Tosh ostida yerdagi kichkina tuxum bor edi va u darhol o'z joniga kiyimni bo'shatdi.

en: The purse lay at the top, and yet the hollow was not filled up.
uz: Jurnalning yuqori qismida sumka bor edi, ammo bu joy to'liq bo'lmagan.

en: Then he seized the stone again and with one twist turned it back, so that it was in the same position again, though it stood a very little higher.
uz: So'ngra u toshni yana ushlab, bir burchak bilan qaytarib qo'ydi va tosh yana o'sha joyda bo'ldi, ammo u biroz yuqoriga ko'tarildi.

en: But he scraped the earth about it and pressed it at the edges with his foot.
uz: Ammo u atrofida yerni qirib, oyoqlari bilan uning chegaralariga bosdi.

en: Nothing could be noticed.
uz: Hech narsa ko'rinmas edi.

en: Then he went out, and turned into the square.
uz: Keyin tashqariga chiqib, maydonga aylandi.

en: Again an intense, almost unbearable joy overwhelmed him for an instant, as it had in the police-office.
uz: Politsiya xonadonida sodir bo'lganidek, uni yana bir bor qattiq, deyarli chiday olmaydigan quvonch ovora qildi.

en: “I have buried my tracks!
uz: Men o'z izlarimni ko'mdim!

en: And who, who can think of looking under that stone?
uz: Va kim, kim bu tosh ostida ko'rishni o'ylashi mumkin?

en: It has been lying there most likely ever since the house was built, and will lie as many years more.
uz: Ehtimol, u uy qurilganidan beri u erda yotgan va yana ko'p yillar davomida yotgan bo'ladi.

en: And if it were found, who would think of me?
uz: Agar topilsa, meni kim eslaydi?

en: No clue!” And he laughed.
uz: Hech qanday izoh yo'q! Va u kuldi.

en: Yes, he remembered that he began laughing a thin, nervous noiseless laugh, and went on laughing all the time he was crossing the square.
uz: To'g'ri, u o'zidan kechirishni boshlaganini esladi, u yumushsiz, g'ayratli kulishni boshladi va maydonni kesib o'tganda kulishni davom ettirdi.

en: But when he reached the K — — Boulevard where two days before he had come upon that girl, his laughter suddenly ceased.
uz: Ammo u K  Boulevardga yetib kelganida, ikki kun oldin u qizni uchratganida, uning kulishi to'xtadi.

en: Other ideas crept into his mind.
uz: Boshqa g'oyalar uning ongiga kirib keldi.

en: He felt all at once that it would be loathsome to pass that seat on which after the girl was gone, he had sat and pondered, and that it would be hateful, too, to meet that whiskered policeman to whom he had given the twenty kopecks: “Damn him!”
uz: U qiz ketgandan so'ng o'tirgan va o'ylab ko'rgan o'rinni o'tib ketish jirkanch bo'lishini va u yigirma kopekni bergan bo'lsa-da, o'sha burchakli politsiyachini uchratish ham jirkanch bo'lishini birdan his qildi.

en: He walked, looking about him angrily and distractedly.
uz: U yurib, g'azablangan va chalg'itgan holda atrofini ko'rdi.

en: All his ideas now seemed to be circling round some single point, and he felt that there really was such a point, and that now, now, he was left facing that point —and for the first time, indeed, during the last two months.
uz: Endi uning barcha g'oyalari bitta nuqta atrofida aylanib borayotgandek tuyuldi va u bunday nuqta borligini va endi, endi u ushbu nuqta bilan birinchi marta, aslida, so'nggi ikki oy davomida yuz o'girganini his qildi.

en: “Damn it all!” he thought suddenly, in a fit of ungovernable fury.
uz: Damn it all! deb o'yladi u to'satdan, hukm qilinmaydigan g'azabda.

en: “If it has begun, then it has begun.
uz: Agar u boshlangan bo'lsa, unda u boshlangan.

en: Good Lord, how stupid it is!
uz: Xudoyim, bu naqadar ahmoqlikdir!

en: … And what lies I told today!
uz: Va men bugun nima yolg'on aytdim!

en: How despicably I fawned upon that wretched Ilya Petrovitch!
uz: Men o'sha qashshoq Ilya Petrovitchni naqadar noxushlik bilan tanqid qildim!

en: But that is all folly!
uz: Ammo bularning barchasi aqlsizlikdir!

en: What do I care for them all, and my fawning upon them!
uz: Ularning barchasini qayg'uraman va ularga g'amxo'rlik qilaman!

en: It is not that at all!
uz: Aslo bunday emas!

en: It is not that at all!” Suddenly he stopped; a new utterly unexpected and exceedingly simple question perplexed and bitterly confounded him.
uz: Aslo shunday emas! Birdan u to'xtadi; butunlay kutilmagan va juda sodda yangi savol uni hayron qoldirdi va keskin chalg'itdi.

en: “If it all has really been done deliberately and not idiotically, if I really had a certain and definite object, how is it I did not even glance into the purse and don’t know what I had there, for which I have undergone these agonies, and have deliberately undertaken this base, filthy degrading business?
uz: Agar bularning barchasi aslida axmoqona emas, balki qasddan qilingan bo'lsa, agar men aslida aniq va aniq bir narsam bo'lgan bo'lsa, nima uchun men hatto qopqoqqa nazar tashlamaganman va u yerda nima borligini bilmayman, shuning uchun men bu azob-uqubatlarga duchor bo'ldim va qasddan bu oddiy, nopok va axloqsiz ish bilan shug'ullanardim?

en: And here I wanted at once to throw into the water the purse together with all the things which I had not seen either … how’s that?” Yes, that was so, that was all so.
uz: Va men ham ko'rmagan barcha narsalar bilan bir qatorda sumkani darhol suvga tashlamoqchi bo'ldim... qanday qilib? Ha, shunday edi, shunday edi.

en: Yet he had known it all before, and it was not a new question for him, even when it was decided in the night without hesitation and consideration, as though so it must be, as though it could not possibly be otherwise.
uz: Ammo u buni ilgari ham bilgan edi va bu uning uchun yangi savol emas edi, hatto kechasi hech qanday shubha va mulohaza qilmasdan qaror qabul qilinganida ham, xuddi shunday bo'lishi kerak bo'lganidek, hech qanday boshqacha narsa bo'lmasligi mumkin bo'lganidek.

en: … Yes, he had known it all, and understood it all; it surely had all been settled even yesterday at the moment when he was bending over the box and pulling the jewel-cases out of it.
uz: Ha, u hamma narsani bilar edi va hamma narsani tushunar edi; albatta, bularning barchasi o'sha paytgacha to'g'rilashgan edi, o'sha payt o'sha qutuq ustiga egib, uning ichida oltin-o'tinlarni olib chiqar edi.

en: “It is because I am very ill,” he decided grimly at last, “I have been worrying and fretting myself, and I don’t know what I am doing.
uz: Bu men juda kasal bo'lganim uchun,  oxir-oqibat o'zimni qayg'urganman va o'zimni tashvishlantirib yurganman va nima qilayotganimni bilmayman.

en: … Yesterday and the day before yesterday and all this time I have been worrying myself.
uz: ... Kecha va bir kun oldin va butun bu vaqt davomida o'zimni tashvishlantirganman.

en: … I shall get well and I shall not worry.
uz: ... Men sog'ayib ketaman va tashvishlanmayman.

en: … But what if I don’t get well at all?
uz: Ammo agar umuman sog'aymasam nima bo'ladi?

en: Good God, how sick I am of it all!” He walked on without resting.
uz: Xudoyim, bularning barchasidan men qanchalik kasalman! U dam olmasdan davom etdi.

en: He had a terrible longing for some distraction, but he did not know what to do, what to attempt.
uz: U biroz chalg'itishni orzu qilardi, lekin nima qilishni, nima qilishga harakat qilishni bilmasdi.

en: A new overwhelming sensation was gaining more and more mastery over him every moment; this was an immeasurable, almost physical, repulsion for everything surrounding him, an obstinate, malignant feeling of hatred.
uz: U har bir daqiqaga yangi, g'alati his-tuyg'u bilan ustun bo'lib borar edi; bu atrofidagi har bir narsaga nisbatan o'lchovsiz, deyarli jismoniy, jirkanchlik, nafratning qattiqqo'l, yovuz his-tuyg'usi edi.

en: All who met him were loathsome to him —he
uz: U bilan uchrashganlarning hammasi unga nafratli edi.

en: loathed their faces, their movements, their gestures.
uz: Ularning yuzlari, harakatlari va harakatlaridan nafratlangan.

en: If anyone had addressed him, he felt that he might have spat at him or bitten him.
uz: Agar kimdir unga murojaat qilgan bo'lsa, u unga tishlab yoki iltijo qilgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb o'ylagan.

en: … He stopped suddenly, on coming out on the bank of the Little Neva, near the bridge to Vassilyevsky Ostrov.
uz: U to'satdan to'xtadi va Vassilyevskiy Ostrov ko'prisi yaqinidagi Kichik Neva qirg'og'ida chiqdi.

en: “Why, he lives here, in that house,” he thought, “why, I have not come to Razumihin of my own accord!
uz: U bu yerda, shu uyda yashaydi, - deb o'yladi u, - nega men o'zim roziligim bilan Razumihinga kelmadim?

en: Here it’s the same thing over again.
uz: Bu erda yana bir bor xuddi shunday.

en: … Very interesting to know, though; have I come on purpose or have I simply walked here by chance?
uz: Biroq, buni bilish juda qiziqarli; men qasddan keldimmi yoki shunchaki tasodifan bu yerga yurdimmi?

en: Never mind, I said the day before yesterday that I would go and see him the day after; well, and so I will!
uz: Aslida, bir kun oldin, ertasi kuni uni ko'rishga boraman, deb aytgan edim, ammo men ham boraman!

en: Besides I really cannot go further now.” He went up to Razumihin’s room on the fifth floor.
uz: Bundan tashqari, men hozir bundan ortig'ini ko'ra olmayman. U beshinchi qavatdagi Razumihin xonasining oldiga bordi.

en: The latter was at home in his garret, busily writing at the moment, and he opened the door himself.
uz: Bu kishi uyda, o'z garretida, shu paytdagi mashg'ul yozishda edi va u o'zi eshikni ochdi.

en: It was four months since they had seen each other.
uz: Ular bir-birlarini ko'rmaganidan to'rt oy o'tdi.

en: Razumihin was sitting in a ragged dressing-gown, with slippers on his bare feet, unkempt, unshaven and unwashed.
uz: Razumihin boʻlak-boʻlak boʻlib, toʻngʻiz oyoqlarida paltaryuyalar bilan oʻtirgan edi, u toʻgʻri yoʻq edi, sochlari kesilmagan va yuvilmagan edi.

en: His face showed surprise.
uz: Uning yuzi hayratda qolganini ko'rsatdi.

en: “Is it you?” he cried.
uz: Sizmi? - deb yig'ladi u.

en: He looked his comrade up and down; then after a brief pause, he whistled.
uz: U o'z tengdoshiga ko'z tikib qarab, biroz to'xtab o'tirgach, pishirdi.

en: “As hard up as all that!
uz: Bularning barchasi o'ta qattiq!

en: Why, brother, you’ve cut me out!” he added, looking at Raskolnikov’s rags.
uz: Eh, birodarim, sen meni o'chirib yubording! - dedi u Raskolnikovning kiyimlariga qarab.

en: “Come sit down, you are tired, I’ll be bound.” And when he had sunk down on the American leather sofa, which was in even worse condition than his own, Razumihin saw at once that his visitor was ill.
uz: Keling, o'tiring, sen charchagansan, men bog'lanib ketaman. Va u o'zidan ham yomonroq holatda bo'lgan amerikalik charm sofasida bo'lganida, Razumihin mehmonining kasalligini darhol ko'rdi.

en: “Why, you are seriously ill, do you know that?” He began feeling his pulse.
uz: Nima uchun siz jiddiy kasalsiz, buni bilasizmi? U pulsini his qila boshladi.

en: Raskolnikov pulled away his hand.
uz: Raskolnikov qo'lini olib qo'ydi.

en: “Never mind,” he said, “I have come for this: I have no lessons.
uz: Bosh qilma, dedi u,Men shu maqsadda keldim: darslarim yo'q.

en: … I wanted, … but I don’t really want lessons.
uz: Men xohlagan edim, lekin darslarni aslida xohlamayman.

en: You are delirious, you know!” Razumihin observed, watching him carefully.
uz: Siz deliriyalsiz, bilasiz! Razumihin uni diqqat bilan kuzatib, kuzatdi.

en: “No, I am not.” Raskolnikov got up from the sofa.
uz: Yo'q, men yo'q. Raskolnikov sofasidan turdi.

en: As he had mounted the stairs to Razumihin’s, he had not realised that he would be meeting his friend face to face.
uz: Razumihinlargacha turar joyni ko'targanida, u do'sti bilan yuzma-yuz uchrashishini tushunmagan edi.

en: Now, in a flash, he knew, that what he was least of all disposed for at that moment was to be face to face with anyone in the wide world.
uz: O'sha paytda u eng kamdan-kam tayyor bo'lgan narsa - dunyodagi har bir kishi bilan yuzma-yuz bo'lish edi.

en: His spleen rose within him.
uz: Uyning ichidan ko'tarildi.

en: He almost choked with rage at himself as soon as he crossed Razumihin’s threshold.
uz: Razumihin chegarasini o'tib ketgandan so'ng, u o'ziga nisbatan g'azabga to'lib-toshdi.

en: “Goodbye,” he said abruptly, and walked to the door.
uz: "Xudojo'y", - dedi u birdan va eshikga yaqinlashdi.

en: You queer fish.” “I don’t want to,” said the other, again pulling away his hand.
uz: Siz g'ayritabiiy baliqsiz. Men xohlamayman, dedi boshqa, yana qo'lini uzatib.

en: “Then why the devil have you come?
uz: Shunday bo'lsa, nima uchun shayton kelibsiz?

en: Are you mad, or what?
uz: Sen g'azablanmadingmi yoki nima?

en: Why, this is … almost insulting!
uz: Bu... deyarli haqoratli!

en: I won’t let you go like that.” “Well, then, I came to you because I know no one but you who could help … to begin … because you are kinder than anyone — cleverer, I mean, and can judge … and now I see that I want nothing.
uz: Men sizni shunday yo'ldan ozdirmayman.  Xo'sh, men sizning oldingizga keldim, chunki sizdan boshqa hech kimga yordam bera olmaydigan odamni bilmayman ... boshlaning ... chunki siz boshqalardan ko'ra mehribonroqsiz  aqlliroq, ya'ni, hukm qila oladigan ... va endi men hech narsa istamasligimni tushunaman.

en: Nothing at all … no one’s services … no one’s sympathy.
uz: Hech narsa... hech kimning xizmati... hech kimning hamdardligi yo'q.

en: I am by myself … alone.
uz: Men o'zimdan... yolg'izman.

en: Come, that’s enough.
uz: Kelinglar, bu yetarli.

en: Leave me alone.” “Stay a minute, you sweep!
uz: Meni yolg'iz qo'yib yuboring. Bir daqiqa turing, sen ko'z o'g'ri!

en: You are a perfect madman.
uz: Siz mukammal aqldan ozgan odamsiz.

en: As you like for all I care.
uz: Siz xohlaganingizcha, men g'amxo'rlik qilaman.

en: I have no lessons, do you see, and I don’t care about that, but there’s a bookseller, Heruvimov —and he takes the place of a lesson.
uz: Mening darslarim yo'q va bu menga qiziqmaydi, lekin Heruvimov ismli kitob sotuvchi bor va u darsning o'rnini egallaydi.

en: I would not exchange him for five lessons.
uz: Men uni besh dars bilan almashtirmayman.

en: He’s doing publishing of a kind, and issuing natural science manuals and what a circulation they have!
uz: U bir xil nashr etish va tabiiy fanlar qo'llanmalarini nashr etish bilan shug'ullanmoqda va ularning naqadar ko'p tarqalishi bor!

en: The very titles are worth the money!
uz: O'sha unvonlar pulga arziydi!

en: You always maintained that I was a fool, but by Jove, my boy, there are greater fools than I am!
uz: Siz doim meni ahmoq deb hisoblar edingiz, lekin Jove bilan qasamki, o'g'lim, mendan ham ko'proq ahmoqlar bor!

en: Now he is setting up for being advanced, not that he has an inkling of anything, but, of course, I encourage him.
uz: Endi u rivojlanishga tayyorlanmoqda, bu uning biron bir narsadan xabardor bo'lishidan iborat emas, lekin men uni, albatta, rag'batlantiraman.

en: Here are two signatures of the German text —in my opinion, the crudest charlatanism; it discusses the question, ‘Is woman a human being?’ And, of course, triumphantly proves that she is.
uz: Mana nemis matnining ikki imzosi, mening fikrimcha, eng qo'pol charlatanizmdir; u "Xotin - insonmi?" degan savolni muhokama qiladi va, albatta, u shunday ekanligini g'alaba bilan isbotlaydi.

en: Heruvimov is going to bring out this work as a contribution to the woman question; I am translating it; he will expand these two and a half signatures into six, we shall make up a gorgeous title half a page long and bring it out at half a rouble.
uz: Heruvimov bu asarni xotin-qizlar masalasiga qo'shish sifatida taqdim etadi; men uni tarjima qilaman; u ushbu ikki yarim imzolarni oltiga kengaytiradi, biz yarim sahifalik chiroyli sarlavhani tuzamiz va uni yarim rubl evaziga taqdim etamiz.

en: He pays me six roubles the signature, it works out to about fifteen roubles for the job, and I’ve had six already in advance.
uz: U menga imzo uchun olti rubl to'laydi, ish uchun taxminan o'n besh rublga teng bo'ladi va men allaqachon olti rubl oldindan olganman.

en: When we have finished this, we are going to begin a translation about whales, and then some of the dullest scandals out of the second part of Les Confessions we have marked for translation; somebody has told Heruvimov, that Rousseau was a kind of Radishchev.
uz: Buni tugatganimizda, baliqlar haqida tarjima qilishni boshlaymiz va keyin Les Confessions kitobining ikkinchi qismidagi eng og'ir isyonlardan ba'zilarini tarjima qilish uchun belgilab qo'ydik; kimdir Heruvimovga Rousseau bir xil Radishchev deb aytdi.

en: You may be sure I don’t contradict him, hang him!
uz: Men unga zid kelmasligimga amin bo'ling, uni o'g'irlab qo'ying!

en: Well, would you like to do the second signature of ‘Is woman a human being?’ If you would, take the German and pens and paper — all those are provided, and take three roubles; for as I have had six roubles in advance on the whole thing, three roubles come to you for
uz: Xo'sh, "Xotin-qiz insonmi?" deb ikkinchi imzolashni xohlaysizmi? Agar xohlasangiz, nemis va qalam va qog'ozni olib, uch rublni olib qo'yinglar; chunki men butun ishda olti rubl oldindan olgan bo'lsam ham, uch rubl siz uchun keladi

en: And when you have finished the signature there will be another three roubles for you.
uz: Imzolashni tugatganingizda, sizga yana uch rubl beriladi.

en: And please don’t think I am doing you a service; quite the contrary, as soon as you came in, I saw how you could help me; to begin with, I am weak in spelling, and secondly, I am sometimes utterly adrift in German, so that I make it up as I go along for the most part.
uz: Va iltimos, men sizga xizmat qilyapman deb o'ylamang; aksincha, siz kirganingizdan so'ng, menga qanday yordam berishingiz mumkinligini ko'rdim; birinchidan, men yozuvda zaifman, ikkinchidan, men ba'zan nemis tilida butunlay o'zimni o'tkazaman, shuning uchun ko'p vaqt davomida buni o'ylab topaman.

en: The only comfort is, that it’s bound to be a change for the better.
uz: Faqatgina tasalli shundaki, bu yaxshi tomonga o'zgarish bo'lishi kerak.

en: Though who can tell, maybe it’s sometimes for the worse.
uz: Kim bilsa ham, ba'zan bu yomon bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Will you take it?” Raskolnikov took the German sheets in silence, took the three roubles and without a word went out.
uz: Uni qabul qilasizmi? Raskolnikov nemis varaqalarini jimlik bilan oldi, uchta rublni oldi va so'zsiz tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Razumihin gazed after him in astonishment.
uz: Razumihin uni hayron ko'rib qo'ydi.

en: But when Raskolnikov was in the next street, he turned back, mounted the stairs to Razumihin’s again and laying on the table the German article and the three roubles, went out again, still without uttering a word.
uz: Ammo Raskolnikov yonidagi ko'chada bo'lganida, orqaga burildi, Razumihinlarga qadam bosdi va stol ustiga nemis maqolasini va uchta rublni qo'yib, yana tashqariga chiqdi, hali ham so'z aytmadi.

en: “Are you raving, or what?” Razumihin shouted, roused to fury at last.
uz: Siz g'azablanyapsizmi yoki nima? Razumihin qichqirib, nihoyat g'azabga to'lgan.

en: “What farce is this?
uz: Bu qanaqa mashg'ulotlar?

en: You’ll drive me crazy too … what did you come to see me for, damn you?” “I don’t want … translation,” muttered Raskolnikov from the stairs.
uz: Siz meni ham aqldan ozdirishingiz mumkin ... nima uchun meni ko'rishga keldingiz, ahd bo'lsin?

en: “Then what the devil do you want?” shouted Razumihin from above.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa, siz nima istaysiz? deb baland ovoz bilan aytdi Razumihin yuqoridan.

en: Raskolnikov continued descending the staircase in silence.
uz: Raskolnikov xotirjamlik bilan mertaga tushishni davom ettirdi.

en: Where are you living?” No answer.
uz: Qayerda yashayapsiz? Hech qanday javob yo'q.

en: “Well, confound you then!” But Raskolnikov was already stepping into the street.
uz: Xo'sh, o'shanda sizni chalg'itdim! Ammo Raskolnikov allaqachon ko'chaga qadam qo'ygan edi.

en: On the Nikolaevsky Bridge he was roused to full consciousness again by an unpleasant incident.
uz: Nikolayovskiy ko'prasida u bir yoqimsiz hodisa tufayli yana to'liq ongga keldi.

en: A coachman, after shouting at him two or three times, gave him a violent lash on the back with his whip, for having almost fallen under his horses’ hoofs.
uz: Bir ko'chmachi unga ikki-uch marta qichqirib, qo'l urganidan so'ng, deyarli otlarining cho'g'iga tushib qolganligi uchun uni qamchilab orqaga qattiq urdi.

en: The lash so infuriated him that he dashed away to the railing (for some unknown reason he had been walking in the very middle of the bridge in the traffic).
uz: U shunday g'azabga to'ldiki, u railingga yugurib ketdi (bir noma'lum sabab tufayli u ko'prikning o'rtasida harakatlanayotgan edi).

en: He angrily clenched and ground his teeth.
uz: U g'azablanib, o'z tishlarini silkitdi.

en: He heard laughter, of course.
uz: Albatta, u kulishni eshitgan.

en: “Serves him right!” “A pickpocket I dare say.” “Pretending to be drunk, for sure, and getting under the wheels on purpose; and you have to answer for him.” “It’s a regular profession, that’s what it is.”
uz: O'ziga to'g'ri xizmat qiladi! Men aytishga jur'at etamanki, bu pulparast.  O'zini mastdek ko'rsatib, o'ylagandek ko'rsatadi va bilgan holda to'g'ri yo'lga tushadi; va siz uning o'rniga javob berasiz.  Bu odatdagi kasb, bu uning o'zi.

en: But while he stood at the railing, still looking angry and bewildered after the retreating carriage, and rubbing his back, he suddenly felt someone thrust money into his hand.
uz: Ammo u orqaga qarab turar ekan, orqaga qarab, orqaga cho'zib ketayotgan aravachadan keyin hali ham g'azablanib va g'alati ko'rinishda edi, u to'satdan kimdir qo'liga pul tashlayotganini his qildi.

en: It was an elderly woman in a kerchief and goatskin shoes, with a girl, probably her daughter, wearing a hat, and carrying a green parasol.
uz: Bu bir keksa ayol bo'lgan, u choriq va echki teridan bo'lgan poyabzallar kiygan va bir qiz, ehtimol uning qizi bilan birga, to'pka kiygan va yashil chiroq ko'tarib turgan edi.

en: “Take it, my good man, in Christ’s name.” He took it and they passed on.
uz: O'zingni, yaxshi odam, Masih nomidan qabul qil. U uni olib, ular o'tib ketishdi.

en: It was a piece of twenty kopecks.
uz: Bu yigirma kopekning bir qismi edi.

en: From his dress and appearance they might well have taken him for a beggar asking alms in the streets, and the gift of the twenty kopecks he doubtless owed to the blow, which made them feel sorry for him.
uz: Uning kiyim-kechak va tashqi ko'rinishiga ko'ra, uni ko'chalarda sadaqa so'rab yurgan so'roqchi deb hisoblashgan bo'lishlari mumkin, shuningdek, u o'qishga qarzdor bo'lgan yigirma kopekning sovg'asi, shubhasiz, ular uchun achinardi.

en: He closed his hand on the twenty kopecks, walked on for ten paces, and turned facing the Neva, looking towards the palace.
uz: U o'ttiz kopekni qo'lidan yopib, o'n qadam davom etdi va Nevaga qaragan holda saroyga qarab o'girilib ketdi.

en: The sky was without a cloud and the water was almost bright blue, which is so rare in the Neva.
uz: Osmon bulutsiz edi va suv deyarli yorqin ko'k rangda edi, bu Nevada juda kam uchraydigan narsa.

en: The cupola of the cathedral, which is seen at its best from the bridge about twenty paces from the chapel, glittered in the sunlight, and in the pure air every ornament on it could be clearly distinguished.
uz: Katedralning kupolasi, ko'prikdan taxminan yigirma qadam uzoqlikda ko'rinadi, quyosh nuri bilan parlashdi va toza havoda uning har bir bezakligi aniq ko'rinardi.

en: The pain from the lash went off, and Raskolnikov forgot about it; one uneasy and not quite definite idea occupied him now completely.
uz: Raskolnikovni qamchilab o'ldirgan og'riq yo'q bo'lib ketdi va u bu haqda unutib qo'ydi; bir noaniq va aniq bo'lmagan g'oya uni endi butunlay egallab oldi.

en: He stood still, and gazed long and intently into the distance; this spot was especially familiar to him.
uz: U to'xtamay uzoq va diqqat bilan uzoqroq qarab turardi; bu joy unga ayniqsa tanish edi.

en: When he was attending the university, he had hundreds of times — generally on his way home —stood still on this spot, gazed at this truly magnificent spectacle and almost always marvelled at a vague and mysterious emotion it roused in him.
uz: Universitetda bo'lganida, u yuzlab marta uyga qaytayotganda shu yerda to'xtatib, bu chindan ham ajoyib ko'rgazmaga qarab turardi va deyarli har doim u ichidagi noaniq va sirli tuyg'ularga hayron bo'lib turardi.

en: It left him strangely cold; this gorgeous picture was for him blank and lifeless.
uz: Bu uni g'alati darajada sovuq qoldirdi; bu chiroyli rasm unga bo'sh va jonsiz edi.

en: He wondered every time at his sombre and enigmatic impression and, mistrusting himself, put off finding the explanation of it.
uz: U har safar o'zining qorong'i va g'ayritabiiy taassurotidan hayron bo'lib, o'ziga ishonchsizlik qilib, uning tushuntirilishini topishni kechiktirardi.

en: He vividly recalled those old doubts and perplexities, and it seemed to him that it was no mere chance that he recalled them now.
uz: U o'sha eski shubhalar va g'alayonlarni o'z ichiga olgan va hozir ularni eslab qolish shunchaki tasodif emasdek tuyuladi.

en: It struck him as strange and grotesque, that he should have stopped at the same spot as before, as though he actually imagined he could think the same thoughts, be interested in the same theories and pictures that had interested him  … so short a time ago.
uz: U o'ziga g'alati va g'alati tuyuldi, chunki u avvalgidek to'xtatishi kerak edi, xuddi xuddi o'sha fikrlarni o'ylashi mumkinligini tasavvur qilgan bo'lsa kerak, xuddi o'zi qiziqtirgan nazariyalar va rasmlarga qiziqishi mumkinligini tasavvur qilgan bo'lsa kerak ... juda qisqa vaqt oldin.

en: He felt it almost amusing, and yet it wrung his heart.
uz: U buni deyarli qiziqarli his qildi, ammo bu uning qalbini qovurdi.

en: Deep down, hidden far away out of sight all that seemed to him now —all his old past, his old thoughts, his old problems and theories, his old impressions and that picture and himself and all, all.
uz: O'z qalbida, uning oldingi o'tmishlari, eski fikrlari, eski muammolari va nazariyalari, eski taassurotlari va rasmlari, o'zi va hamma narsa.

en: … He felt as though he were flying upwards, and everything were
uz: U o'zini yuqoriga uchib borayotgandek his qilgan va hamma narsa yaxshi edi.

en: vanishing from his sight.
uz: Uning ko'zidan yo'q bo'lib ketmoqda.

en: Making an unconscious movement with his hand, he suddenly became aware of the piece of money in his fist.
uz: Qo'li bilan bexabar harakat qilib, u birdan o'z qo'lida pul to'plamini ko'rdi.

en: He opened his hand, stared at the coin, and with a sweep of his arm flung it into the water; then he turned and went home.
uz: U qo'lini ochib, tangaga tikilib, qo'lini cho'kib suvga tashladi, so'ngra o'girilib uyga qaytib ketdi.

en: It seemed to him, he had cut himself off from everyone and from everything at that moment.
uz: O'sha paytda u o'zini hamma va hamma narsadan ajratib qo'ygan ko'rinardi.

en: Evening was coming on when he reached home, so that he must have been walking about six hours.
uz: U uyga kelganida, kechqurun yaqinlashib qolgan edi, shuning uchun u taxminan olti soat yurgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: How and where he came back he did not remember.
uz: Qaytib qaytib kelganini va qayerga qaytganini eslay olmagan.

en: Undressing, and quivering like an overdriven horse, he lay down on the sofa, drew his greatcoat over him, and at once sank into oblivion.
uz: Kiyimlarini yechib, o'zidan tashqari haydashgan ot kabi titrab, sofa ustiga yotdi, ko'ylagini o'ziga ko'tardi va darhol unutilib ketdi.

en: … It was dusk when he was waked up by a fearful scream.
uz: U qo'rqinchli qichqiriq bilan uyg'onilganida, tun bosgan edi.

en: Good God, what a scream!
uz: Xudoyim, bu qanday qichqiriq!

en: Such unnatural sounds, such howling, wailing, grinding, tears, blows and curses he had never heard.
uz: Bunday tabiiy tovushlar, shunday qichqiriq, yig'lash, qichqirish, ko'z yoshlari, urish va la'natlar u hech qachon eshitmagan edi.

en: He could never have imagined such brutality, such frenzy.
uz: U hech qachon bunday shafqatsizlik, bunday g'alatilikni tasavvur ham qila olmagan.

en: In terror he sat up in bed, almost swooning with agony.
uz: U dahshatga to'lib, o'z yotoqxonasiga o'tirdi va azob-uqubatdan o'z-o'zini o'ldirmoqchi bo'ldi.

en: But the fighting, wailing and cursing grew louder and louder.
uz: Ammo jang, qayg'u va la'natlar ko'proq va ko'proq ovoz chiqardi.

en: And then to his intense amazement he caught the voice of his landlady.
uz: Keyin u o'zining qattiq hayratlanishiga ko'ra, uy egasining ovozini ushlab qoldi.

en: She was howling, shrieking and wailing, rapidly, hurriedly, incoherently, so that he could not make out what she was talking about; she was beseeching, no doubt, not to be beaten, for she was being mercilessly beaten on the stairs.
uz: U qichqirib, qichqirib va yig'lab yurardi, tez, shoshilinch, befarq, shuning uchun u nima haqida gapirayotganini tushunolmasdi; u, shubhasiz, urilmasligini iltijo qilardi, chunki u mertabanlarda shafqatsiz urildi.

en: The voice of her assailant was so horrible from spite and rage that it was almost a croak; but he, too, was saying something, and just as quickly and indistinctly, hurrying and spluttering.
uz: Uning hujumchisi g'azab va g'azabdan shunchalik dahshatli ovoz chiqardiki, u deyarli qichqiriq kabi bo'ldi; lekin u ham biror narsa aytayotgan edi va xuddi shu darajada tez va aniq emas, shoshilmoqda va qichqiriq qiladi.

en: All at once Raskolnikov trembled; he recognised the voice —it was the voice of Ilya Petrovitch.
uz: Raskolnikov birdan titrab ketdi; u ovozini tan oldi - bu Ilya Petrovitchning ovozi edi.

en: Ilya Petrovitch here and beating the landlady!
uz: Ilya Petrovitch bu erda va uy egasini urib!

en: He is kicking her, banging her head against the steps —that’s clear, that can be told from the sounds, from the cries and the thuds.
uz: U qizni urib, boshini pasaytirmoqda, bu aniq, tovushlardan, qichqiriqlardan va qichqiriqlardan ko'rinib turibdi.

en: How is it, is the world topsy-turvy?
uz: Dunyo qanday, dunyo topsy-turvymi?

en: He could hear people running in crowds from all the storeys and all the staircases; he heard voices, exclamations, knocking, doors banging.
uz: U har bir qavatdan va har bir burchakdan to'p-to'p odamlarni yugurib ketayotganini eshitardi; u ovozlarni, baqiriqlarni, taqillatishni, eshiklarning taqillatishini eshitardi.

en: “But why, why, and how could it be?” he repeated, thinking seriously that he had gone mad.
uz: Ammo nima uchun, nima uchun va qanday qilib bo'lishi mumkin? - deb takrorladi u, jiddiy o'ylab, o'zini aqldan ozdirdi.

en: But no, he heard too distinctly!
uz: Ammo yo'q, u juda aniq eshitgan!

en: And they would come to him then next, “for no doubt … it’s all about that … about yesterday.
uz: Keyin esa ular uning oldiga kelib, shubhasizki, hamma narsa shu... kecha haqida.

en: … Good God!” He would have fastened his door with the latch, but he could not lift his hand … besides, it would be useless.
uz: ... Yaxshi Xudo! U eshikni qulflab qo'ygan bo'lar edi, lekin qo'lini ko'tarolmas edi... bundan tashqari, bu foydasiz bo'lar edi.

en: Terror gripped his heart like ice, tortured him and numbed him.
uz: Qo'rquv uning yuragini muz kabi qamrab oldi, uni qiynatib, o'zicha bo'shashtirdi.

en: … But at last all this
uz: Ammo nihoyat bularning barchasi ...

en: uproar, after continuing about ten minutes, began gradually to subside.
uz: O'n daqiqa davom etgan g'alayon, asta-sekin kamayib borishni boshladi.

en: The landlady was moaning and groaning; Ilya Petrovitch was still uttering threats and curses.
uz: Uy egasi g'azablanib, g'azablanardi; Ilya Petrovitch hali ham tahdid va la'natlar aytardi.

en: … But at last he, too, seemed to be silent, and now he could not be heard.
uz: Ammo nihoyat, u ham sukut saqlashdi va endi uni tinglash mumkin emas edi.

en: “Can he have gone away?
uz: U ketib ketgan bo'lishi mumkinmi?

en: Good Lord!” Yes, and now the landlady is going too, still weeping and moaning … and then her door slammed.
uz: Yaxshi Rabbim! Ha, va endi uy egasi ham ketadi, hali ham yig'lab, g'azablanmoqda... keyin esa uning eshigini taqillatdi.

en: … Now the crowd was going from the stairs to their rooms, exclaiming, disputing, calling to one another, raising their voices to a shout, dropping them to a whisper.
uz: ... Endi xaloyiq daraxtdan o'z xonalariga borar edi, baqirib, bahslashib, bir-birlarini chaqirishardi, ovozlarini baland ko'tarib, ularni shoshib qo'yishardi.

en: There must have been numbers of them —almost all the inmates of the block.
uz: Ularning soni ko'p bo'lishi kerak edi - blokning deyarli barcha mahbuslari.

en: “But, good God, how could it be!
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, qanday qilib bo'lishi mumkin?

en: And why, why had he come here!” Raskolnikov sank worn out on the sofa, but could not close his eyes.
uz: Va nima uchun u bu yerga keldi! Raskolnikov sofa ustida charchagan holda botdi, lekin ko'zlarini yopolmadi.

en: He lay for half an hour in such anguish, such an intolerable sensation of infinite terror as he had never experienced before.
uz: U yarim soat davomida bunday qayg'uda, cheksiz dahshat hissi bilan to'xtab qoldi, bu uning ilgari hech qachon boshdan kechirmagan edi.

en: Suddenly a bright light flashed into his room.
uz: Toʻsatdan uning xonasiga yorugʻ yorugʻlik kirdi.

en: Nastasya came in with a candle and a plate of soup.
uz: Nastasya shamol va shov-sov bilan kirdi.

en: Looking at him carefully and ascertaining that he was not asleep, she set the candle on the table and began to lay out what she had brought —bread, salt, a plate, a spoon.
uz: Uni diqqat bilan ko'rib, uyqusida emasligini aniqlab, u chiroqni stol ustiga qo'yib, olib kelgan non, tuz, pishirma, qoshiqlarni ko'tarib berishni boshladi.

en: “You’ve eaten nothing since yesterday, I warrant.
uz: Siz o'tgan kunlardan beri hech narsa yemagansiz, shuni kafolatlayman.

en: You’ve been trudging about all day, and you’re shaking with fever.” “Nastasya … what were they beating the landlady for?” She looked intently at him.
uz: Siz kun bo'yi ko'p harakat qilib yuribsiz va issiqdan titrab yuribsiz.Nastasya... uy egasini nima uchun urishardi? U unga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: “Who beat the landlady?” “Just now … half an hour ago, Ilya Petrovitch, the assistant superintendent, on the stairs.
uz: Xonadon egasini kim urdi?  Haqiqatan... yarim soat oldin, yordamchi nazoratchi Ilya Petrovitch mertabaning ustida edi.

en: … Why was he ill-treating her like that, and … why was he here?” Nastasya scrutinised him, silent and frowning, and her scrutiny lasted a long time.
uz: ... Nima uchun u unga shunday yomon munosabatda edi va ... nima uchun u bu yerda edi? Nastasya uni o'z ko'zidan kechirdi, gapini aytmay va ko'z o'ngida turibdi va uning ko'z o'ngida ko'p vaqt davom etdi.

en: He felt uneasy, even frightened at her searching eyes.
uz: U o'zini noqulay va hatto uning ko'zlarini ko'rib qo'rqqan edi.

en: “Nastasya, why don’t you speak?” he said timidly at last in a weak voice.
uz: "Nastasya, nega gapirmayapsan?" - dedi u qo'rqmasdan, oxir-oqibat zaif ovoz bilan.

en: “It’s the blood,” she answered at last softly, as though speaking to herself.
uz: - Bu qon, - dedi u so'ng o'zi bilan gaplashgandek, so'nggi paytlarda xotirjamlik bilan javob berdi.

en: What blood?” he muttered, growing white and turning towards the wall.
uz: Qaysi qon? deb gapirgan u, oqlanib, devor tomon burildi.

en: Nastasya still looked at him without speaking.
uz: Nastasya hali ham gapirmasdan unga qaradi.

en: “Nobody has been beating the landlady,” she declared at last in a firm, resolute voice.
uz: Hech kim uy egasini urmagan, u nihoyat qat'iy va qat'iy ovoz bilan e'lon qildi.

en: He gazed at her, hardly able to breathe.
uz: U ayolga qaradi va nafas olishni qiyinlashtiradi.

en: … I was not asleep … I was sitting up,” he said still more timidly.
uz: Men uxlamagan edim, o'tirgan edim, - dedi u yana ham qo'rqmasdan.

en: “I listened a long while.
uz: Men uzoq vaqt tingladim.

en: The assistant superintendent came.
uz: Yordamchi nazoratchi keldi.

en: … Everyone ran out on to the stairs from all the flats.” “No one has been here.
uz: ... Har bir kishi barcha xonadonlardan burchaklarga yugurib bordi. Hech kim bu yerda bo'lmagan.

en: That’s the blood crying in your ears.
uz: Bu sizning quloqlaringizda yig'layotgan qon.

en: When there’s no outlet for it and it gets clotted, you begin fancying things.
uz: U uchun hech qanday eshik yo'q bo'lganda va u to'qnashganida, siz o'zingiz uchun o'yin-kulgilar yaratishni boshlaysiz.

en: … Will you eat something?” He made no answer.
uz: ... Siz biron narsa yeysizmi? U hech qanday javob bermadi.

en: Nastasya still stood over him, watching him.
uz: Nastasya hali ham uning ustida turib, uni kuzatib turardi.

en: “Give me something to drink … Nastasya.” She went downstairs and returned with a white earthenware jug of water.
uz: Menga ichimlik ber... Nastasya. U pastga tushib, oq loy suv qadoqasi bilan qaytib keldi.

en: He remembered only swallowing one sip of the cold water and spilling some on his neck.
uz: U sovuq suvning faqat bir qoshiqini yutib, birozini bo'yniga to'kib qo'yganini esladi.

en: Then followed forgetfulness.
uz: So'ngra unutib ketish davom etdi.

en: III He was not completely unconscious, however, all the time he was ill; he was in a feverish state, sometimes delirious, sometimes half conscious.
uz: III. U kasal bo'lgan vaqt davomida to'liq befarq emas edi; u issiq holatda edi, ba'zan deliriumli, ba'zan yarim befarq edi.

en: He remembered a great deal afterwards.
uz: Keyinchalik u ko'p narsalarni esladi.

en: Sometimes it seemed as though there were a number of people round him; they wanted to take him away somewhere, there was a great deal of squabbling and discussing about him.
uz: Ba'zan uning atrofida ko'plab odamlar bo'lganiga o'xshaydi edi; ular uni bir joyga olib ketmoqchi edilar, u haqda ko'p bahs-munozaralar va bahs-munozaralar bo'lgan.

en: Then he would be alone in the room; they had all gone away afraid of him, and only now and then opened the door a crack to look at him; they threatened him, plotted something together, laughed, and mocked at him.
uz: Keyin esa u xonada yolg'iz bo'lardi; hamma undan qo'rqqan holda ketib ketishgan edi va vaqti-vaqti bilan eshikni ochib, unga qarab qo'yishgan edi; uni qo'rqitishardi, biror narsa qilmoqchi bo'lishardi, unga kulishardi va masxara qilishardi.

en: He remembered Nastasya often at his bedside; he distinguished another person, too, whom he seemed to know very well, though he could not remember who he was, and this fretted him, even made him cry.
uz: Nastasya ko'pincha uning yotoq yonida eslab turardi; u boshqa bir kishini ham tanib turardi, uni juda yaxshi bilgan edi, ammo u kimligini eslay olmagan edi va bu uni xavotirga solgan, hatto yig'latgan.

en: Sometimes he fancied he had been lying there a month; at other times it all seemed part of the same day.
uz: Ba'zan u o'zi bir oy o'tirgan deb o'ylagan, ba'zan esa hamma narsa bir kunning bir qismi kabi tuyulgan.

en: But of that —of that he had no recollection, and yet every minute he felt that he had forgotten something he ought to remember.
uz: Ammo u hech qanday xotiraga ega bo'lmagan, ammo har bir daqiqada eslab qolishi kerak bo'lgan narsani unutib qo'yganini his qilardi.

en: He worried and tormented himself trying to remember, moaned, flew into a rage, or sank into awful, intolerable terror.
uz: U eslab qolishga harakat qilib, tashvishlanib, azob chekardi, qayg'urardi, g'azabga tushdi yoki dahshatli, chidamsiz dahshatga tushdi.

en: Then he struggled to get up, would have run away, but someone always prevented him by force, and he sank back into impotence and forgetfulness.
uz: Keyin u turish uchun kurashardi, qochib ketardi, lekin har doim kimdir uni kuch bilan to'xtatib turardi va u yana kuchsizlik va unutishchanlikka tushdi.

en: At last he returned to complete consciousness.
uz: Nihoyat u to'liq ongga qaytdi.

en: It happened at ten o’clock in the morning.
uz: Bu voqea ertalab soat o'nlarda sodir bo'ldi.

en: On fine days the sun shone into the room at that hour, throwing a streak of light on the right wall and the corner near the door.
uz: Go'zal kunlarda quyosh o'sha soatda xonada porlab, o'ng devorga va eshik yaqinidagi burchakga nur sochib o'tadi.

en: Nastasya was standing beside him with another person, a complete stranger, who was looking at him very inquisitively.
uz: Nastasya uning yonida boshqa bir kishi bilan, butunlay begona bir kishi bilan turgan edi va u unga juda qiziqish bilan qarayotgan edi.

en: He was a young man with a beard, wearing a full, short-waisted coat, and looked like a messenger.
uz: U soqovli, to'liq, qisqa belli kiyim kiygan va elchiga o'xshaydigan yosh yigit edi.

en: The landlady was peeping in at the half-opened door.
uz: Uy egasi yarim ochilgan eshikni ko'rib turgan edi.

en: “Who is this, Nastasya?” he asked, pointing to the young man.
uz: "Bu kim, Nastasya?" - deb so'radi u, yosh yigitga ishora qilib.

en: “I say, he’s himself again!” she said.
uz: Men aytamanki, u yana o'zi! - dedi u.

en: “He is himself,” echoed the man.
uz: "U o'zi", - dedi u kishi.

en: Concluding that he had returned to his senses, the landlady closed the door and disappeared.
uz: Uy egasi uning aql-idrok topganini bilib, eshikni yopib, yo'qoldi.

en: She was always shy and dreaded conversations or discussions.
uz: U har doim uyalgan va suhbat yoki muzokaralardan qo'rqqan.

en: She was a woman of forty, not at all bad-looking, fat and buxom, with black eyes and eyebrows, good- natured from fatness and laziness, and absurdly bashful.
uz: U qirq yoshli ayol edi, umuman yomon ko'rinmas edi, semiz va ko'p bo'lgan, qora ko'zlar va ko'z burchaklari bor edi, semizlik va dangasalikdan kelib chiqardi va absurd darajada uyalgan edi.

en: “Who … are you?” he went on, addressing the man.
uz: Siz kimsiz? u odamga murojaat qilib, davom etdi.

en: But at that moment the door was flung open, and, stooping a little, as he was so tall, Razumihin came in.
uz: Ammo o'sha paytda eshik ochildi va u juda baland bo'lgani uchun Razumihin biroz egrilib kirdi.

en: “What a cabin it is!” he cried.
uz: Bu naqadar kulfat! deb baqirdi.

en: “I am always knocking my head.
uz: Men har doim boshimni uryapman.

en: You call this a lodging!
uz: Siz buni uy-joy deb ataysiz!

en: So you are conscious, brother?
uz: Demak, sen o'zingni o'ylagansan, aka?

en: I’ve just heard the news from Pashenka.” “He has just come to,” said Nastasya.
uz: Men Pashenkadan yangiliklarni eshitdim. U hozirda o'zini tikladi, dedi Nastasya.

en: “Just come to,” echoed the man again, with a smile.
uz: Just come to, kishi yana bir bor tabassum bilan javob berdi.

en: “And who are you?” Razumihin asked, suddenly addressing him.
uz: Siz kimsiz? - deb so'radi Razumihin, to'satdan unga murojaat qilib.

en: “My name is Vrazumihin, at your service; not Razumihin, as I am always called, but Vrazumihin, a student and gentleman; and he is my friend.
uz: Mening ismim Vrazumihin, sizning xizmatingiz uchun; men har doim so'raladigan Razumihin emas, balki Vrazumihin, o'quvchi va gentleman; va u mening do'stimdir.

en: And who are you?” “I am the messenger from our office, from the merchant Shelopaev, and I’ve come on business.” “Please sit down.” Razumihin seated himself on the other side of the table.
uz: Va siz kimsiz? Men bizning ofisimizdagi, savdogar Shelopaevning elchisi bo'laman va biznes uchun keldim. Iltimos, o'tiring. Razumihin o'zini stolning boshqa tomoniga o'tirdi.

en: “It’s a good thing you’ve come to, brother,” he went on to Raskolnikov.
uz: Yaxshiyamki, o'zingni o'ylab ko'rding, aka, u Raskolnikovga murojaat qildi.

en: “For the last four days you have scarcely eaten or drunk anything.
uz: So'nggi to'rt kun davomida siz hech narsa yemagansiz yoki ichmagansiz.

en: We had to give you tea in spoonfuls.
uz: Biz sizga qoshiqcha choy berishga majbur bo'ldik.

en: I brought Zossimov to see you twice.
uz: Zossimovni siz bilan ikki marta uchrashish uchun olib keldim.

en: You remember Zossimov?
uz: Zossimovni eslaysizmi?

en: He examined you carefully and said at once it was nothing serious —something seemed to have gone to your head.
uz: U sizni diqqat bilan ko'rib chiqib, darhol jiddiy narsa emasligini aytdi.

en: Some nervous nonsense, the result of bad feeding, he says you have not had enough beer and radish, but it’s nothing much, it will pass and you will be all right.
uz: Biroz g'alati gaplar, yomon ovqatlanish natijasi, u siz uchun ertalab piva va radish yetarli emasligini aytadi, lekin bu juda ko'p narsa emas, u o'tib ketadi va siz yaxshi bo'lasiz.

en: Zossimov is a first-rate fellow!
uz: Zossimov birinchi darajali hamkasbdir!

en: He is making quite a name.
uz: U juda yaxshi nom yaratmoqda.

en: Come, I won’t keep you,” he said, addressing the man again.
uz: Keling, sizni to'xtatmayman, - dedi u, yana bir bor bu odamga murojaat qilib.

en: “Will you explain what you want?
uz: Siz nima istayotganingizni tushuntirib bera olasizmi?

en: You must know, Rodya, this is the second time they have sent from the office; but it was another man last time, and I talked to him.
uz: Bilasiz, Rodya, bu ishxonadan ikkinchi marta jo'natilgan; lekin oxirgi marta boshqa odam edi va men u bilan gaplashdim.

en: Who was it came before?”
uz: Undan oldin kim kelgan?

en: “That was the day before yesterday, I venture to say, if you please, sir.
uz: Bu kechqurun edi, deyishga jur'at qilaman, iltimos, sir.

en: That was Alexey Semyonovitch; he is in our office, too.” “He was more intelligent than you, don’t you think so?” “Yes, indeed, sir, he is of more weight than I am.” “Quite so; go on.” “At your mamma’s request, through Afanasy Ivanovitch Vahrushin, of whom I presume you have heard more than once, a remittance is sent to you from our office,” the man began, addressing Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu Aleksey Semyonovich edi; u ham bizning ofisimizda. U sizdan ko'ra aqlliroq edi, shunday emasmi? Ha, haqiqatan ham, xo'jayinim, u mendan ko'proq og'ir. Ha, shunday, davom eting. Onangizning iltimosiga ko'ra, Afanasy Ivanovitch Vahrushin orqali, uning haqida bir necha marta eshitgan bo'lsangiz kerak, sizga ofisimizdan pul yuboriladi, kishi Raskolnikovga murojaat qilib boshladi.

en: “If you are in an intelligible condition, I’ve thirty-five roubles to remit to you, as Semyon Semyonovitch has received from Afanasy Ivanovitch at your mamma’s request instructions to that effect, as on previous occasions.
uz: Agar siz tushunarli holatda bo'lsangiz, Semyon Semyonovitch o'tgan paytlarda bo'lgani kabi, onangiz Afanasy Ivanovitchdan bu borada ko'rsatmalar olgan bo'lsa, sizga o'ttiz besh rubl yo'l qo'ydim.

en: Do you know him, sir?” “Yes, I remember … Vahrushin,” Raskolnikov said dreamily.
uz: Siz uni taniysizmi, xo'jayinim? Ha, eslayman... Vahrushin, Raskolnikov orzu bilan dedi.

en: “You hear, he knows Vahrushin,” cried Razumihin.
uz: "Siz eshitasiz, u Vahrushinni biladi", - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: “He is in ‘an intelligible condition’!
uz: U tushunarli holatda!

en: And I see you are an intelligent man too.
uz: Ko'rib turganimcha, siz ham aqlli odamsiz.

en: Well, it’s always pleasant to hear words of wisdom.” “That’s the gentleman, Vahrushin, Afanasy Ivanovitch.
uz: Ha, donolik so'zlarini eshitish har doim yoqimli.Bu xonim, Vahrushin, Afanasy Ivanovitch.

en: And at the request of your mamma, who has sent you a remittance once before in the same manner through him, he did not refuse this time also, and sent instructions to Semyon Semyonovitch some days since to hand you thirty-five roubles in the hope of better to come.” “That ‘hoping for better to come’ is the best thing you’ve said, though ‘your mamma’ is not bad either.
uz: Va onangizning iltimosiga ko'ra, u sizga bir marta ham o'zi orqali pul yuborgan edi, lekin u bu safar ham rad etmadi va bir necha kun oldin Semyon Semyonovitchga o'ttiz besh rublni sizga berish haqida yo'l-yo'riq yubordi.

en: Come then, what do you say?
uz: Kelinglar, nima deysiz?

en: Is he fully conscious, eh?” “That’s all right.
uz: U to'liq onglimi, shundaymi?  Bu yaxshi.

en: If only he can sign this little paper.” “He can scrawl his name.
uz: Agar u faqat shu kichik qog'ozni imzolashi mumkin bo'lsa.U o'z ismini ko'tarishi mumkin.

en: Have you got the book?” “Yes, here’s the book.” “Give it to me.
uz: Kitobingiz bormi? Ha, bu kitob.  Menga bering.

en: Here, Rodya, sit up.
uz: Mana, Rodya, o'tirib ko'ring.

en: Take the pen and scribble ‘Raskolnikov’ for him.
uz: Qani, qalamni olib, Raskolnikovni uning o'rniga ko'chirib qo'ying.

en: For just now, brother, money is sweeter to us than treacle.” “I don’t want it,” said Raskolnikov, pushing away the pen.
uz: Hozircha, birodarim, pul biz uchun treakldan ko'ra shirinroq. Men uni xohlamayman, dedi Raskolnikov, qalamni orqaga surib.

en: “Not want it?” “I won’t sign it.” “How the devil can you do without signing it?” “I don’t want … the money.” “Don’t want the money!
uz: I don't want it?   I don't want it.  Qanday qilib siz buni imzolamasdan qila olasiz?   I don't want... the money.  I don't want the money!

en: Come, brother, that’s nonsense, I bear witness.
uz: Keling, aka, bu behudalik, men guvohman.

en: Don’t trouble, please, it’s only that he is on his travels again.
uz: Iltimos, bezovta qilmanglar, lekin u yana sayohatda.

en: But that’s pretty common with him at all times though.
uz: Ammo u bilan bu har doim ham odatiy hol.

en: … You are a man of judgment and we will take him in hand, that is, more simply, take his hand and he will sign it.
uz: ... Siz hukmdor insonsiz va biz uni qo'limizdan oldik, ya'ni qo'limizdan oldik va u imzolaydi.

en: Here.” “But I can come another time.” “No, no.
uz: Bu erda. Lekin men boshqa safar kelishim mumkin.Yo'q, yo'q.

en: Why should we trouble you?
uz: Nima uchun sizni bezovta qilishimiz kerak?

en: You are a man of judgment.
uz: Siz hukm qiluvchi odamsiz.

en: … Now, Rodya, don’t keep your visitor, you see he is waiting,” and he made ready to hold Raskolnikov’s hand in earnest.
uz: Endi, Rodya, tashrif buyuruvchingizni ushlab turmang, ko'rib turibsizki, u kutmoqda va Raskolnikovning qo'lini qattiq ushlab turishga tayyor bo'ldi.

en: “Stop, I’ll do it alone,” said the latter, taking the pen and signing his name.
uz: Stop, men buni yolg'iz qilaman, dedi oxirgi, qalamni olib, o'z nomi bilan imzolaydi.

en: The messenger took out the money and went away.
uz: Xizmatchi pulni olib chiqib ketdi.

en: And now, brother, are you hungry?” “Yes,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Endi esa, birodarim, siz ochmisiz?  Ha, Raskolnikov javob berdi.

en: “Is there any soup?” “Some of yesterday’s,” answered Nastasya, who was still standing there.
uz: Sup bormi?Boshqa kunlar,- deb javob berdi Nastasya, u hali ham o'sha yerda turgan edi.

en: “With potatoes and rice in it?” “Yes.” “I know it by heart.
uz: Shuning ichida kartoshka va riz bor?Ha.Men uni yoddan bilaman.

en: Bring soup and give us some tea.” “Very well.” Raskolnikov looked at all this with profound astonishment and a dull, unreasoning terror.
uz: Choy olib keling va bizga choy bering. Chindan ham yaxshi. Raskolnikov bularning barchasini chuqur hayronlik va g'alati, aqlsiz dahshat bilan ko'rdi.

en: He made up his mind to keep quiet and see what would happen.
uz: U gapni tinglab, nima bo'lishini ko'rishga qaror qildi.

en: “I believe I am not wandering.
uz: Iman qilamanki, men buzuq emasman.

en: I believe it’s reality,” he thought.
uz: Men buni haqiqat deb o'ylayman, deb o'yladi u.

en: In a couple of minutes Nastasya returned with the soup, and announced that the tea would be ready directly.
uz: Bir necha daqiqadan so'ng Nastasya shoppani olib qaytib keldi va choyning to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tayyor bo'lishini e'lon qildi.

en: With the soup she brought two spoons, two plates, salt, pepper, mustard for the beef, and so on.
uz: Cho'p bilan u ikki qoshiq, ikki talad, tuz, paprika, go'sht uchun xantal va hokazolarni olib keldi.

en: The table was set as it had not been for a long time.
uz: O'sha vaqtdan beri o'tmaganidek, stol tayyorlangan edi.

en: The cloth was clean.
uz: To'qima toza edi.

en: “It would not be amiss, Nastasya, if Praskovya Pavlovna were to send us up a couple of bottles of beer.
uz: Nastasya, Praskovya Pavlovna bizga bir necha shisha pivo yuborsa, yomon bo'lmaydi.

en: We could empty them.” “Well, you are a cool hand,” muttered Nastasya, and she departed to carry out his orders.
uz: Biz ularni tozalashimiz mumkin.  Xo'sh, siz chiroyli qo'lingiz, - dedi Nastasya, u esa uning buyruqlarini bajarish uchun jo'nab ketdi.

en: Raskolnikov still gazed wildly with strained attention.
uz: Raskolnikov hali ham g'ayritabiiy tarzda e'tiborini tortgan holda qarab turardi.

en: Meanwhile Razumihin sat down on the sofa beside him, as clumsily as a bear put his left arm round Raskolnikov’s head, although he was able to sit up, and with his right hand gave him a spoonful of soup, blowing on it that it might not burn him.
uz: O'sha paytda Razumihin o'zining yonidagi sofaga o'tirdi va o'ng qo'li bilan bir qoshiq shovqin berib, uni yonmasligi uchun o'ng qo'li bilan shovqin berdi, chunki g'alati g'alati o'zining chap qo'lini Raskolnikovning boshini o'rab oldi.

en: But the soup was only just warm.
uz: Ammo shovqin faqat issiq edi.

en: Raskolnikov swallowed one spoonful greedily, then a second, then a third.
uz: Raskolnikov ochko'zlik bilan bir qoshiqni, keyin ikkinchi, keyin uchinchi qoshiqni yutib yubordi.

en: But after giving him a few more spoonfuls of soup, Razumihin suddenly stopped, and said that he must ask Zossimov whether he ought to have more.
uz: Ammo Razumihin unga yana bir necha qoshiq shovqin bergach, toʻxtadi va Zossimovdan koʻproq isteʼmol qilish kerakligini soʻrash kerakligini aytdi.

en: Nastasya came in with two bottles of beer.
uz: Nastasya ikki shisha pivo bilan keldi.

en: “And will you have tea?” “Yes.” “Cut along, Nastasya, and bring some tea, for tea we may venture on without the faculty.
uz: Va siz choy ichasizmi?   Ha.    O'tkazib yuboring, Nastasya, va choy olib keling, chunki biz choy uchun fakultetsiz sayohat qilishimiz mumkin.

en: But here is the beer!” He moved back to his chair, pulled the soup and meat in front of him, and began eating as though he had not touched food for three days.
uz: Lekin bu pivo! U o'z o'rinbosariga qaytib keldi, shovqin va go'shtni o'zining oldidan tortib oldi va uch kun davomida ovqatga tegmaganidek ovqatlanishni boshladi.

en: “I must tell you, Rodya, I dine like this here every day now,” he mumbled with his mouth full of beef, “and it’s all Pashenka, your dear little landlady, who sees to that; she loves to do anything for me.
uz: Men sizga aytishim kerak, Rodya, men har kuni bu yerda shunday ovqatlanaman,  u og'zini go'sht bilan to'ldirgan holda gapirdi,  va bu Pashenka, sizning sevimli kichik uy egasi, bu haqda g'amxo'rlik qiladi; u men uchun hamma narsani qilishni yaxshi ko'radi.

en: I don’t ask for it, but, of course, I don’t object.
uz: Men buni so'ramayman, lekin, albatta, bunga qarshilik bildirmayman.

en: And here’s Nastasya with the tea.
uz: Mana, Nastasya choy bilan birga.

en: She is a quick girl.
uz: U tezkor qiz.

en: Nastasya, my dear, won’t you have some beer?” “Get along with your nonsense!” “A cup of tea, then?” “A cup of tea, maybe.” “Pour it out.
uz: Nastasya, azizim, biroz pivo ichmaysanmi?  Bu g'alati gaplar bilan birga bo'ling!  O'zingni o'zing o'ylab ko'ring! O'zingni o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'zing o'ga o'g'ang.

en: Stay, I’ll pour it out myself.
uz: Turing, men o'zim to'kib yuboraman.

en: Sit down.” He poured out two cups, left his dinner, and sat on the sofa again.
uz: O'tiring. U ikki kosani to'kib, kechki ovqatni qoldirib, yana sofaga o'tirdi.

en: As before, he put his left arm round the sick man’s head, raised him up and gave him tea in spoonfuls, again blowing each spoonful steadily and earnestly, as though this process was the principal and most effective means towards his friend’s recovery.
uz: Ilgarigidek, chap qo'lini bemorning boshiga o'rnatdi, uni ko'tarib qo'ydi va qoshiqlab choy berdi, yana har bir qoshiqni qat'iy va qat'iy sochib o'tdi, xuddi shu jarayon uning do'stining sog'ayishiga yo'l qo'yishning asosiy va eng samarali vositasi bo'lgani kabi.

en: Raskolnikov said nothing and made no resistance, though he felt quite strong enough to sit up on the sofa without support and could not merely have held a cup or a spoon, but even perhaps could have walked about.
uz: Raskolnikov hech narsa aytmadi va hech qanday qarshilik ko'rsatmadi, garchi u o'zini sofada qo'llab-quvvatlanmasdan o'tirishga qodir deb hisoblagan bo'lsa-da va shunchaki kosani yoki qoshiqni ushlab qolmagan bo'lsa-da, balki hatto yurishi mumkin bo'lgan bo'lsa-da.

en: But from some queer, almost animal, cunning he conceived the idea of hiding his strength and lying low for a time, pretending if necessary not to be yet in full possession of his faculties, and meanwhile listening to find out what was going on.
uz: Ammo u o'z kuchini yashirib, biroz o'rinsiz qolishni, agar kerak bo'lsa, o'z qobiliyatlarini hali to'liq egallamaganini ko'rsatishni va shu vaqt ichida nima bo'layotganini bilib olish uchun tinglashni o'ylagan.

en: Yet he could not overcome his sense of repugnance.
uz: Ammo u o'z nafratini yengib bo'lmadi.

en: After sipping a dozen spoonfuls of tea, he suddenly released his head, pushed the spoon away capriciously, and sank back on the pillow.
uz: O'nlab qoshiq choy ichganidan so'ng, u to'satdan boshini bo'shatdi, qoshiqni capriciously orqaga shoshdi va yostiqqa qaytdi.

en: There were actually real pillows under
uz: Aslida, ostida haqiqiy yostiqlar bor edi.

en: his head now, down pillows in clean cases, he observed that, too, and took note of it.
uz: Endi boshini toza holatda bo'lgan yostiqlarga tushirib, u ham buni kuzatdi va buni e'tiborga oldi.

en: “Pashenka must give us some raspberry jam today to make him some raspberry tea,” said Razumihin, going back to his chair and attacking his soup and beer again.
uz: Pashenka bizga bugun raspberry jamini berishi kerak, shunda unga raspberry choyi tayyorlanadi, dedi Razumihin, o'z kursiga qaytib, yana uning shov-shuv va pivolariga hujum qiladi.

en: “And where is she to get raspberries for you?” asked Nastasya, balancing a saucer on her five outspread fingers and sipping tea through a lump of sugar.
uz: U siz uchun sabzavotlarni qayerdan oladi? deb so'radi Nastasya, besh barmog'ida pishirgan pishirmani o'rab olib, bir qovur sug'or orqali choy ichib.

en: “She’ll get it at the shop, my dear.
uz: Uni do'konda sotib oladi, azizim.

en: You see, Rodya, all sorts of things have been happening while you have been laid up.
uz: Ko'ryapsanmi, Rodya, sen o'tirganingda har xil narsalar sodir bo'ldi.

en: When you decamped in that rascally way without leaving your address, I felt so angry that I resolved to find you out and punish you.
uz: O'zingizning manzilingizni tashlab ketmay, o'zingizning qo'pol yo'llaringiz bilan o'sha joyga ketayotganingizda, men shunchalik g'azablandimki, sizni topib, jazolanishga qaror qildim.

en: I set to work that very day.
uz: Men o'sha kuni ishga kirdim.

en: How I ran about making inquiries for you!
uz: Men siz uchun so'rovlar berishga harakat qildim!

en: This lodging of yours I had forgotten, though I never remembered it, indeed, because I did not know it; and as for your old lodgings, I could only remember it was at the Five Corners, Harlamov’s house.
uz: Bu uyingiz haqida unutib qoldim, lekin hech qachon esga tushmaganman, chunki men buni bilmagan edim; eski uylaringiz haqida gap ketganda, men faqat Harlamovning uyida, beshta burchada, bo'lganini eslayman.

en: I kept trying to find that Harlamov’s house, and afterwards it turned out that it was not Harlamov’s, but Buch’s.
uz: Harlamovning uyini izlashga harakat qilib turardim va keyinchalik bu Harlamovlar emas, balki Buchlar ekanini bilib oldim.

en: How one muddles up sound sometimes!
uz: Ba'zan inson tovushni qanday chalg'itadi!

en: So I lost my temper, and I went on the chance to the address bureau next day, and only fancy, in two minutes they looked you up!
uz: Shunday qilib, men g'azabimni yo'qotdim va ertasi kuni manzil idorasida bo'lish imkoniyatiga ega bo'ldim va ikki daqiqadan so'ng sizni qidirib topishdi!

en: Your name is down there.” “My name!” “I should think so; and yet a General Kobelev they could not find while I was there.
uz: O'sha yerda sizning ismingiz bor.  Mening ismim!  Men shunday o'ylayman; lekin men u yerda bo'lganimda, ular General Kobelevni topa olishmadilar.

en: Well, it’s a long story.
uz: To'g'ri, bu uzoq hikoya.

en: But as soon as I did land on this place, I soon got to know all your affairs —all, all, brother, I know everything; Nastasya here will tell you.
uz: Ammo men bu joyga yetib kelganimdan so'ng, tez orada barcha ishlaringizni bilib oldim, hamma narsani bilaman, birodarim; bu erda Nastasya sizga aytadi.

en: I made the acquaintance of Nikodim Fomitch and Ilya Petrovitch, and the house-porter and Mr.
uz: Nikodim Fomitch va Ilya Petrovitch, uy egasi va Mr. bilan tanishdim.

en: Zametov, Alexandr Grigorievitch, the head clerk in the police office, and, last, but not least, of Pashenka; Nastasya here knows.
uz: Zametov, Aleksandr Grigorievitch, politsiya idorasining bosh kotibi va so'nggi, lekin eng muhimi emas, Pashenka; Nastasya bu haqda biladi.

en: …” “He’s got round her,” Nastasya murmured, smiling slyly.
uz: ... U qizni o'rab oldi, Nastasya g'ayratli tabassum qilib, g'ayrat bilan g'ayratli bo'ldi.

en: “Why don’t you put the sugar in your tea, Nastasya Nikiforovna?” “You are a one!” Nastasya cried suddenly, going off into a giggle.
uz: Nima uchun siz o'zingizning choyingizga shakar qo'ymaysiz, Nastasya Nikiforovna?  Siz birsiz! Nastasya to'satdan yig'lab yubordi va kulishga tushdi.

en: “I am not Nikiforovna, but Petrovna,” she added suddenly, recovering from her mirth.
uz: Men Nikiforovna emasman, balki Petrovna, deb qo'shib qo'ydi u birdan, quvonchdan tiklanayotganda.

en: “I’ll make a note of it.
uz: I bu haqda yozib qo'yaman.

en: Well, brother, to make a long story short, I was going in for a regular explosion here to uproot all malignant
uz: Xo'sh, birodarim, qisqacha aytganda, men bu yerda har qanday zararli kasallikni yo'q qilish uchun muntazam ravishda portlashim kerak edi.

en: influences in the locality, but Pashenka won the day.
uz: Mahalliy ta'sirga ega bo'lganlar, lekin Pashenka g'alaba qozondi.

en: I had not expected, brother, to find her so … prepossessing.
uz: Men uni shunday ... o'ziga xos deb topishni kutmaganman, aka.

en: Eh, what do you think?” Raskolnikov did not speak, but he still kept his eyes fixed upon him, full of alarm.
uz: Eh, nima deb o'ylaysiz? Raskolnikov gapirmadi, lekin u hali ham qo'rqinchga to'lib, ko'zlarini unga qaratdi.

en: “And all that could be wished, indeed, in every respect,” Razumihin went on, not at all embarrassed by his silence.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, har jihatdan xohlab bo'ladigan barcha narsa,  Razumihin o'z so'zidan hech qachon o'zini noqulay his qilmay, davom etdi.

en: “Ah, the sly dog!” Nastasya shrieked again.
uz: Ah, o'g'il it! Nastasya yana qichqirdi.

en: This conversation afforded her unspeakable delight.
uz: Bu suhbat uning so'zlab bo'lmaydigan quvonchini keltirdi.

en: “It’s a pity, brother, that you did not set to work in the right way at first.
uz: Bu juda achinarli, aka, siz dastlab to'g'ri yo'l bilan ishlamaganingiz uchun.

en: You ought to have approached her differently.
uz: Siz unga boshqacha yo'l tutishingiz kerak edi.

en: She is, so to speak, a most unaccountable character.
uz: U, shunday deyish uchun, juda mas'uliyatsiz shaxs.

en: But we will talk about her character later.
uz: Ammo uning shaxsiyati haqida keyinroq gapiramiz.

en: … How could you let things come to such a pass that she gave up sending you your dinner?
uz: ... Qanday qilib siz o'zingizning kechki ovqatingizni yuborishni tashlab qo'yishingiz mumkin?

en: You must have been mad to sign an I.O.U.
uz: Siz I.O.U.ni imzolash uchun g'alati bo'lgansiz.

en: And that promise of marriage when her daughter, Natalya Yegorovna, was alive?
uz: Qizasi Natalya Yegorovna tirik bo'lganida, u qanday nikoh va'dasi bergan?

en: … I know all about it!
uz: Men bu haqda hamma narsani bilaman!

en: But I see that’s a delicate matter and I am an ass; forgive me.
uz: Lekin men bu juda murakkab masala ekanligini va men bir o'g'limman; meni kechiring.

en: But, talking of foolishness, do you know Praskovya Pavlovna is not nearly so foolish as you would think at first sight?” “No,” mumbled Raskolnikov, looking away, but feeling that it was better to keep up the conversation.
uz: Ammo ahmoqlikdan gapirganimizda, Praskovya Pavlovna birinchi qarashda o'ylagandek ahmoq emasligini bilasizmi?Yo'q, Raskolnikov g'amginlik bilan qarab ketdi, lekin suhbatni davom ettirish yaxshiroq bo'lganini his qildi.

en: “She isn’t, is she?” cried Razumihin, delighted to get an answer out of him.
uz: "O'sha emas, shunday emasmi?" - deb qayg'urdi Razumihin, undan javob olishdan xursand bo'ldi.

en: “But she is not very clever either, eh?
uz: Ammo u ham juda aqlli emas, shundaymi?

en: She is essentially, essentially an unaccountable character!
uz: U aslida, aslida, mas'ul bo'lmagan shaxs!

en: I am sometimes quite at a loss, I assure you.
uz: Ba'zan men o'zimni yo'qotib qolaman, sizga ishontiraman.

en: … She must be forty; she says she is thirty-six, and of course she has every right to say so.
uz: ... U qirq yoshda bo'lishi kerak; u o'ttiz olti yoshini aytadi va, albatta, buni aytishga haqli.

en: But I swear I judge her intellectually, simply from the metaphysical point of view; there is a sort of symbolism sprung up between us, a sort of algebra or whatnot!
uz: Lekin qasamki, men uni aqliy jihatdan, shunchaki metafizik nuqtai nazardan hukm qilaman; o'rtamizda bir xil ramziylik paydo bo'ldi, bir xil algebra yoki boshqa narsa!

en: I don’t understand it!
uz: Men buni tushunmayapman!

en: Well, that’s all nonsense.
uz: Toʻgʻri, bularning hammasi behuda.

en: Only, seeing that you are not a student now and have lost your lessons and your clothes, and that through the young lady’s death she has no need to treat you as a relation, she suddenly took fright; and as you hid in your den and dropped all your old relations with her, she planned to get rid of you.
uz: Faqat siz endi talaba emasligingizni, darslaringizni va kiyim-kechaklaringizni yo'qotganingizni va yosh xonimning o'limi tufayli sizni qarindosh sifatida ko'rishning hojati yo'qligini ko'rib, u to'satdan qo'rqib qolib ketdi; siz o'z g'ordaga yashirib, u bilan oldingi barcha munosabatlaringizni qoldirganingizda, u sizdan qutulishni rejalashtirgan.

en: And she’s been cherishing that design a long time, but was sorry to lose the I.O.U., for you assured her yourself that your mother would pay.”
uz: Va u bu dizaynni uzoq vaqtdan beri qadrlab kelmoqda, lekin I.O.U-ni yo'qotish uchun xafa bo'ldi, chunki siz o'zingiz unga onangiz pul to'layotganiga ishontirdingiz.

en: “It was base of me to say that.
uz: Men bu so'zlarni aytish uchun o'zimni aybladim.

en: … My mother herself is almost a beggar … and I told a lie to keep my lodging … and be fed,” Raskolnikov said loudly and distinctly.
uz: ... Onamning o'zi deyarli so'roqchi bo'lib qoldi ... va men uyimni saqlab qolish va ovqatlanish uchun yolg'on gapirdim, - dedi Raskolnikov baland ovozda va aniq.

en: “Yes, you did very sensibly.
uz: Ha, siz juda oqilona yo'l tutgansiz.

en: But the worst of it is that at that point Mr.
uz: Ammo eng yomon joyi shundaki, o'sha paytda Mr.

en: Tchebarov turns up, a business man.
uz: Chebarov paydo bo'ldi, u biznesmen.

en: Pashenka would never have thought of doing anything on her own account, she is too retiring; but the business man is by no means retiring, and first thing he puts the question, ‘Is there any hope of realising the I.O.U.?’ Answer: there is, because he has a mother who would save her Rodya with her hundred and twenty-five roubles pension, if she has to starve herself; and a sister, too, who would go into bondage for his sake.
uz: Pashenka hech qachon o'z hisobidan biror narsa qilishni o'ylamagan, u o'z ishini tugatadi; lekin ishbilarmon hech qachon o'z ishini tugatmaydi va birinchi navbatda u savol beradi: I.O.U.ni amalga oshirishga umid bormi? Javob: bor, chunki uning onasi bor, agar u o'zini ochlikdan o'ldirish kerak bo'lsa, Rodyani uning yuz yigirma besh rubllik pensiyasi bilan qutqaradi.

en: That’s what he was building upon.
uz: Bu uning o'zi uchun qurilgan edi.

en: I know all the ins and outs of your affairs now, my dear boy —it’s not for nothing that you were so open with Pashenka when you were her prospective son-in-law, and I say all this as a friend.
uz: Endi sizning ishlaringizning barcha tafsilotlarini bilaman, aziz o'g'lim.Pashenka bilan bo'lajak qaynonasi bo'lganingizda ochiq bo'lganingiz behuda emas va men bularni do'st sifatida aytaman.

en: … But I tell you what it is; an honest and sensitive man is open; and a business man ‘listens and goes on eating’ you up.
uz: Ammo men sizga nima ekanligini aytaman; halol va hissiy odam ochiq; va ishbilarmon odam tinglaydi va sizni yeb ketadi.

en: Well, then she gave the I.O.U.
uz: Keyin u I.O.U.ni berdi.

en: by way of payment to this Tchebarov, and without hesitation he made a formal demand for payment.
uz: Bu Tchebarovga to'lov sifatida, va u hech qanday shubha qilmasdan rasmiy ravishda to'lov talabini qo'ydi.

en: When I heard of all this I wanted to blow him up, too, to clear my conscience, but by that time harmony reigned between me and Pashenka, and I insisted on stopping the whole affair, engaging that you would pay.
uz: Bularning barchasini eshitganimda, vijdonimni tozalash uchun uni ham portlatmoqchi edim, ammo o'sha paytgacha men va Paşinqa o'rtasida hamjihatlik hukmronlik qildi va men butun ishni to'xtatishga va siz to'lashingizni va'da berishga harakat qildim.

en: I went security for you, brother.
uz: Men siz uchun xavfsizlik xizmatiga bordim, aka.

en: We called Tchebarov, flung him ten roubles and got the I.O.U.
uz: Chebarovga qo'ng'iroq qildik, unga o'n rubl berdik va I.O.U.-ni oldik.

en: back from him, and here I have the honour of presenting it to you.
uz: Undan qaytib keldi va men uni sizga taqdim etish sharafiga egaman.

en: She trusts your word now.
uz: Endi u sizning so'zingizga ishonadi.

en: Here, take it, you see I have torn it.” Razumihin put the note on the table.
uz: Mana, uni oling, ko'rasiz, men uni yirtib yubordim. Razumihin notani stol ustiga qo'ydi.

en: Raskolnikov looked at him and turned to the wall without uttering a word.
uz: Raskolnikov unga qaradi va bir so'z aytmasdan devorga qarabdi.

en: Even Razumihin felt a twinge.
uz: Hatto Razumihin o'ziga ham o'z hissini uyg'otdi.

en: “I see, brother,” he said a moment later, “that I have been playing the fool again.
uz: Ko'rib turibman, aka, bir muncha vaqt o'tgach, u yana o'yinni o'tkazganimni aytdi.

en: I thought I should amuse you with my chatter, and I believe I have only made you cross.” “Was it you I did not recognise when I was delirious?” Raskolnikov asked, after a moment’s pause without turning his head.
uz: Men o'zimning gaplarim bilan sizni o'yin-kulg' qilishim kerak deb o'yladim va men sizni faqat xafa qildim deb o'ylayman. Men deliriumda bo'lganimda sizni tanmaganmanmi? Raskolnikov so'radi, bir daqiqa vaqt o'tgach boshini o'zgartirmasdan to'xtatib turdi.

en: “Yes, and you flew into a rage about it, especially when I brought Zametov one day.”
uz: Ha, va siz bu haqda g'azabga tushdingiz, ayniqsa men bir kuni Zametovni olib kelganimda.

en: What for?” Raskolnikov turned round quickly and fixed his eyes on Razumihin.
uz: Nima uchun? Raskolnikov tez o'girilib, ko'zlarini Razumihinga qaratdi.

en: “What’s the matter with you?
uz: Sizga nima bo'ldi?

en: … What are you upset about?
uz: Nima uchun xafa bo'ldingiz?

en: He wanted to make your acquaintance because I talked to him a lot about you.
uz: U siz bilan tanishishni xohlagan, chunki men u bilan siz haqingizda ko'p gapirardim.

en: … How could I have found out so much except from him?
uz: Undan boshqa men qanday qilib shuncha narsani bilib olsam bo'ladi?

en: He is a capital fellow, brother, first-rate … in his own way, of course.
uz: U kapital a'zo, birodar, birinchi darajali ... albatta, o'z yo'lida.

en: Now we are friends —see each other almost every day.
uz: Endi biz do'stmiz, deyarli har kuni bir-birimizni ko'ramiz.

en: I have moved into this part, you know.
uz: Men bu qismga o'tdim, bilasiz.

en: I have only just moved.
uz: Men faqat o'sha paytda ko'chib o'tdim.

en: I’ve been with him to Luise Ivanovna once or twice.
uz: Luiz Ivonovna bilan bir-ikki marta uchrashganman.

en: … Do you remember Luise, Luise Ivanovna?” “Did I say anything in delirium?” “I should think so!
uz: Luisa, Luisa Ivanovna haqida eslaysizmi?Men deliriumda biron narsa aytdimmi?Men shunday o'ylayman!

en: You were beside yourself.” “What did I rave about?” “What next?
uz: Siz o'zingizdan ajralib qoldingiz.Men nima haqida gapirgan edim?Nimadan keyin?

en: What did you rave about?
uz: Nima haqida g'alaba qozongandirsiz?

en: What people do rave about.
uz: Odamlar nima haqida g'ayrat ko'rsatishadi.

en: … Well, brother, now I must not lose time.
uz: ... Xo'sh, birodar, endi vaqtimni yo'qotmasligim kerak.

en: To work.” He got up from the table and took up his cap.
uz: Ishga borishga. U stoldan turib, to'pkasi bilan qo'lga tushdi.

en: “What did I rave about?” “How he keeps on!
uz: Men nima haqida g'ururlanardim?  Qanday qilib u davom etadi!

en: Are you afraid of having let out some secret?
uz: Sirni oshkor qilishdan qo'rqyapsizmi?

en: Don’t worry yourself; you said nothing about a countess.
uz: O'zingizni xavotirga solmang; siz hidoyatchi haqida hech narsa aytmadingiz.

en: But you said a lot about a bulldog, and about earrings and chains, and about Krestovsky Island, and some porter, and Nikodim Fomitch and Ilya Petrovitch, the assistant superintendent.
uz: Ammo siz bulldog, quloq va zanjirlar, Krestovskiy orol, ba'zi bir portiyer, Nikodim Fomitch va Ilya Petrovitch, yordamchi nazoratchi haqida ko'p gapirgansiz.

en: And another thing that was of special interest to you was your own sock.
uz: Siz uchun alohida qiziqish uyg'otadigan yana bir narsa - o'zingizning shortsingiz edi.

en: You whined, ‘Give me my sock.’ Zametov hunted all about your room for your socks, and with his own scented, ring-bedecked fingers he gave you the rag.
uz: Siz: "Qozog'imni bering", - deb qayg'urgansiz. Zametov sizning xonangizning har bir tomonida sizning choriqlaringizni qidirib topgan va o'zining xushbo'y, o'ziga xos bog'langan barmoqlari bilan sizga tovushni berdi.

en: And only then were you comforted, and for the next twenty-four hours you held the wretched thing in your hand; we could not get it from you.
