uz: Va faqat o'shanda sen tasalli topding va kelgusi yigirma to'rt soat davomida qo'lingda bu qashshoq narsani ushlab turding; biz buni sendan olishimiz mumkin emas edi.

en: It is most likely somewhere under your quilt at this moment.
uz: Ehtimol, u hozirgi paytda sizning quti ostida bir joyda bo'lishi mumkin.

en: And then you asked so piteously for fringe for your trousers.
uz: Keyin esa siz o'zingizning choriqlaringiz uchun shunchalik shafqatsizlik bilan chegara so'radingiz.

en: We tried to find out what sort of fringe, but we could not make it out.
uz: Biz qanday marjinani aniqlashni istardik, lekin uni aniqlay olmadik.

en: Here are thirty-five roubles; I take ten of them, and shall give you an account of them in an hour or two.
uz: Mana, o'ttiz besh rubl; men ulardan o'nini olib, bir yoki ikki soat ichida sizga hisobot beraman.

en: I will let Zossimov know at the same time, though he ought to have been here long ago, for it is nearly twelve.
uz: Zossimovga bir vaqtning o'zida xabar beraman, ammo u bu yerda ancha vaqt oldin bo'lishi kerak edi, chunki soat o'n ikkiga yaqin.

en: And you, Nastasya, look in pretty often while I am away, to see whether he wants a drink or anything else.
uz: Va sen, Nastasya, men yo'q ekanman, uning ichimlik yoki boshqa biron narsa istashini ko'rish uchun tez-tez ko'ring.

en: And I will tell Pashenka what is wanted myself.
uz: Va men o'zim Pashenkaga nima kerakligini aytaman.

en: “He calls her Pashenka!
uz: U uni Pashenka deb ataydi!

en: Ah, he’s a deep one!” said Nastasya as he went out; then she opened the door and stood listening, but could not resist running downstairs after him.
uz: U juda chuqur! - dedi Nastasya u chiqib ketayotganda; keyin u eshikni ochib, tinglab turdi, lekin uning orqasidan pastga yugurib borishga to'sqinlik qila olmadi.

en: She was very eager to hear what he would say to the landlady.
uz: U uning uy egasiga nima deyishini eshitishni juda istaydi.

en: She was evidently quite fascinated by Razumihin.
uz: U Razumihin bilan juda qiziqarli edi.

en: No sooner had she left the room than the sick man flung off the bedclothes and leapt out of bed like a madman.
uz: U xonadan chiqib ketgandan so'ng, kasal odam to'shaklarini tashlab, aqldan ozgan odam kabi to'shagidan chiqdi.

en: With burning, twitching impatience he had waited for them to be gone so that he might set to work.
uz: U o'z ishini boshlash uchun ularning ketishlarini qizg'in, shov-shuvli sabrsizlik bilan kutgan edi.

en: Now, as though to spite him, it eluded him.
uz: Endi, xuddi unga qarshilik ko'rsatmoqchi bo'lganidek, u undan qochib ketdi.

en: “Good God, only tell me one thing: do they know of it yet or not?
uz: Yaxshi Xudo, menga faqat bir narsani ayting: ular bu haqda hali bilishadimi yoki yo'qmi?

en: What if they know it and are only pretending, mocking me while I am laid up, and then they will come in and tell me that it’s been discovered long ago and that they have only … What am I to do now?
uz: Agar ular buni bilsalar va faqat o'ylashsa, o'tirganimda masxara qilib, masxara qilib, keyin kelib, bu uzoq vaqt oldin aniqlanganligini va ular faqatgina... Endi nima qilishim kerakligini aytsalar-chi?

en: That’s what I’ve forgotten, as though on purpose; forgotten it all at once, I remembered a minute ago.” He stood in the middle of the room and gazed in miserable bewilderment about him; he walked to the door, opened it, listened; but that was not what he wanted.
uz: Men buni qasddan unutib qo'yganman; bir lahzada hammasini unutganman, bir daqiqa oldin esladim. U xonaning o'rtasida turib, o'ziga qaraganida g'alati g'alati edi; u eshikga yaqinlashib, uni ochdi va tingladi; lekin u xohlagan narsa emas edi.

en: Suddenly, as though recalling something, he rushed to the corner where there was a hole under the paper, began examining it, put his hand into the hole, fumbled — but that was not it.
uz: Toʻsatdan, xuddi biror narsani eslab qolganidek, u qogʻoz ostida tosh boʻlgan burchada yugurib, uni tekshirib koʻrishni boshladi, qoʻlini toshga qoʻydi, gʻalatiladi, lekin u oʻsha emas edi.

en: He went to the stove, opened it and began rummaging in the ashes; the frayed edges of his trousers and the rags cut off his pocket were lying there just as he had thrown them.
uz: U pechga bordi, uni ochdi va kulga o'tirishni boshladi; uning shortslarining parchalangan chekkasi va kiyimidan kesilgan to'qimalar o'sha yerda yotgan edi, xuddi ularni tashlab yuborganida.

en: No one had looked, then!
uz: O'shanda hech kim ko'rmagan edi!

en: Then he remembered the sock about which Razumihin had just been telling him.
uz: Keyin Razumihin unga aytib o'tgan sokani esladi.

en: Yes, there it lay on the sofa under the quilt, but it was so covered with dust and grime that Zametov could not have seen anything on it.
uz: Ha, u erda u sofaning pastida, qopqoq ostida yotgan edi, ammo u shunchalik tuproq va kir bilan qoplangan ediki, Zametov uni ko'rmagan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: And why am I sent for to the police office?
uz: Va nima uchun meni politsiyaga yuborishadi?

en: I am mixing it up; that was then.
uz: Men uni aralashtiryapman; bu o'sha paytda edi.

en: I looked at my sock then, too, but now … now I have been ill.
uz: O'shanda men ham cho'ntimga qarab ko'rdim, lekin endi... endi men kasalman.

en: But what did Zametov come for?
uz: Ammo Zametov nima uchun kelgan?

en: Why did Razumihin bring him?” he muttered, helplessly sitting on the sofa again.
uz: Nima uchun Razumihin uni olib keldi? - deb gapirdi u, yana yordamsiz sofa ustida o'tirib.

en: Am I still in delirium, or is it real?
uz: Men hali ham deliriumdamanmi yoki u haqiqiymi?

en: I believe it is real.
uz: Menimcha, bu haqiqiy.

en: … Ah, I remember; I must escape!
uz: Ah, eslayman; qochishim kerak!

en: Make haste to escape.
uz: Qochishga shoshiling.

en: Yes, I must, I must escape!
uz: Ha, men qochib ketishim kerak!

en: And where are my clothes?
uz: Mening kiyim-kechaklarim qayerda?

en: They’ve taken them away!
uz: Ular ularni olib ketishdi!

en: They’ve hidden them!
uz: Ular ularni yashirgan!

en: here is my coat —they passed that over!
uz: Mana mening kiyimim. ~Ular buni o'tkazib yubordilar! ~~~

en: And here is money on the table, thank God!
uz: Mana, stol ustida pul bor, Xudoga shukr!

en: And here’s the I.O.U.
uz: Va bu erda I.O.U. bor.

en: … I’ll take the money and go and take another lodging.
uz: ... Men pulni olib, boshqa joyga boraman.

en: … Yes, but the address bureau?
uz: - Ha, lekin manzil idorasi?

en: They’ll find me, Razumihin will find me.
uz: Ular meni topadilar, Razumihin meni topadi.

en: Better escape altogether … far away … to America, and let them do their worst!
uz: Yaxshi bo'lsa, butunlay... uzoq... Amerikaga qochib ketib, o'zlarining eng yomon ishlarini qilishiga yo'l qo'yib yuboring!

en: … it would be of use there.
uz: ... bu erda foydali bo'ladi.

en: … What else shall I take?
uz: Yana nima olishim kerak?

en: They think I am ill!
uz: Ular meni kasal deb o'ylashadi!

en: They don’t know that I can walk, ha- ha-ha!
uz: Ular men yurishni bilishimni bilmaydilar, ha-ha-ha!

en: I could see by their eyes that they know all about it!
uz: Ularning ko'zlari bilan ular bu haqda hamma narsani bilishini ko'rardim!

en: If only I could get downstairs!
uz: Agar men pastga tushsam edi!

en: And what if they have set a watch there — policemen!
uz: Va agar ular u erda soat o'rnatgan bo'lsa-chi?  Politsiyachilar!

en: Ah, and here is beer left, half a bottle, cold!” He snatched up the bottle, which still contained a glassful of beer, and gulped it down with relish, as though quenching a flame in his breast.
uz: Ah, ana shu yerda pivo qoldi, yarim shisha sovuq! U shishaga to'liq bir stakan pivo bo'lgan shishaga qo'l urib, ko'krakidagi olovni o'chirgandek, uni o'z taomida yutib yubordi.

en: But in another minute the beer had gone to his head, and a faint and even pleasant shiver ran down his spine.
uz: Ammo bir daqiqadan so'ng piva uning boshiga yetib bordi va uning cho'qqisida salqin va hatto yoqimli titrishlar bor edi.

en: He lay down and pulled the quilt over him.
uz: U yerga yotdi va qopqoqni o'z ustiga quvib qo'ydi.

en: His sick and incoherent thoughts grew more and more disconnected, and soon a light, pleasant drowsiness came upon him.
uz: Uning kasal va ko'rinmas fikrlari tobora ko'proq bo'shalgan va tez orada unga yengil, yoqimli uyqu paydo bo'ldi.

en: With a sense of comfort he nestled his head into the pillow, wrapped more closely about him the soft, wadded quilt which had replaced the old, ragged greatcoat, sighed softly and sank into a deep, sound, refreshing sleep.
uz: U taskin hissi bilan boshini yostiqqa o'rnatib, eski, charchagan paltog'ini o'rniga olgan yumshatli, yostiq paltog'ini o'ziga yaqinroq o'rab oldi, salomatlik bilan nafas oldi va chuqur, baland, ta'sirchan uyquga tushdi.

en: He woke up, hearing someone come in.
uz: U uyg'onib, kimdir kirib kelishini eshitdi.

en: He opened his eyes and saw Razumihin standing in the doorway, uncertain whether to come in or not.
uz: U ko'zlarini ochib, Razumihinni eshik oldida turganini ko'rdi va u kiradimi yoki yo'qmi bilmagan edi.

en: Raskolnikov sat up quickly on the sofa and gazed at him, as though trying to recall something.
uz: Raskolnikov tezda sofaga o'tirib, unga bir narsani eslashga harakat qilgandek qaradi.

en: “Ah, you are not asleep!
uz: Ah, siz uxlamaysiz!

en: Nastasya, bring in the parcel!” Razumihin shouted down the stairs.
uz: Nastasya, paketni olib keling! Razumihin pasayib chiqayotgandi.

en: “You shall have the account directly.” “What time is it?” asked Raskolnikov, looking round uneasily.
uz: Siz hisobingizni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri olishingiz kerak.Saat necha? - deb so'radi Raskolnikov, atrofini noqulay ko'rib.

en: “Yes, you had a fine sleep, brother, it’s almost evening, it will be six o’clock directly.
uz: Ha, yaxshi uxlading, aka, kechqurun deyarli soat olti bo'ladi, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri soat olti bo'ladi.

en: You have slept more than six hours.” “Good heavens!
uz: Siz olti soatdan ko'proq uxladingiz. Yomon osmon!

en: Have I?” “And why not?
uz: Men ham shunday qildimmi?  Va nima uchun yo'q?

en: It will do you good.
uz: Bu sizga yaxshilik qiladi.

en: We’ve all time before us.
uz: Biz o'zimizdan oldingi vaqtni oldindan o'tkazganmiz.

en: I’ve been waiting for the last three hours for you; I’ve been up twice and found you asleep.
uz: So'nggi uch soatdan beri seni kutyapman; ikki marta uyg'onib, seni uxlab qolgan holda topdim.

en: I’ve called on Zossimov twice; not at home, only fancy!
uz: Men Zossimovni ikki marta chaqirtirganman; uyda emas, faqat o'yin-kulgi!

en: But no matter, he will turn up.
uz: Ammo muhim emas, u paydo bo'ladi.

en: And I’ve been out on my own business, too.
uz: Va men ham o'z ishim bilan shug'ullanardim.

en: moving today, moving with my uncle.
uz: Bugun ko'chib o'tdim, o'g'lim bilan birga ko'chib o'tdim.

en: I have an uncle living with me now.
uz: Hozir men bilan bir o'g'lim yashaydi.

en: But that’s no matter, to business.
uz: Ammo bu muhim emas, biznes uchun.

en: Give me the parcel, Nastasya.
uz: Menga paketni bering, Nastasya.

en: We will open it directly.
uz: Biz uni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ochamiz.

en: And how do you feel now, brother?” “I am quite well, I am not ill.
uz: Endi qanday o'zingizni his qilyapsiz, aka?Men juda yaxshiman, kasal emasman.

en: Razumihin, have you been here long?” “I tell you I’ve been waiting for the last three hours.” “No, before.” “How do you mean?” “How long have you been coming here?” “Why I told you all about it this morning.
uz: Razumihin, bu yerda qancha vaqt bo'lgansiz?Men sizga aytamanki, men so'nggi uch soatdan beri kutyapman.Yo'q, ilgari. Qanday qilib aytmoqchisiz?Qanday vaqtdan beri bu yerga kelyapsiz? Nima uchun men sizga bu ertalab bu haqda hamma narsani aytib berdim.

en: Don’t you remember?” Raskolnikov pondered.
uz: Hatto eslaysizmi? - Raskolnikov mulohaza yuritdi.

en: The morning seemed like a dream to him.
uz: U uchun ertalab bir orzu kabi tuyuldi.

en: He could not remember alone, and looked inquiringly at Razumihin.
uz: U yolg'iz o'zi eslay olmagan va razumihinni o'ylab ko'rgan.

en: “Hm!” said the latter, “he has forgotten.
uz: Hm! so'zlariga ko'ra, u unutib ketgan.

en: I fancied then that you were not quite yourself.
uz: O'shanda o'zimni o'zim deb bilmasligimni tushundim.

en: Now you are better for your sleep.
uz: Endi siz uxlashingiz uchun yaxshiroq.

en: … You really look much better.
uz: ...Siz chindan ham ancha yaxshiroq ko'rinasiz.

en: Look here, my dear boy.” He began untying the bundle, which evidently interested him.
uz: Mana, aziz o'g'lim. U bog'ni ochishni boshladi, bu esa uni qiziqtirganini ko'rsatdi.

en: “Believe me, brother, this is something specially near my heart.
uz: Menga ishoning, aka, bu ayniqsa yuragimga yaqin narsa.

en: For we must make a man of you.
uz: Chunki biz sizdan odam qilishimiz kerak.

en: Let’s begin from the top.
uz: Keling, yuqoridan boshlanaylik.

en: Do you see this cap?” he said, taking out of the bundle a fairly good though cheap and ordinary cap.
uz: Bu to'pchani ko'ryapsizmi? dedi u, to'plamdan juda yaxshi, ammo arzon va oddiy to'pchani olib chiqib.

en: “Let me try it on.” “Presently, afterwards,” said Raskolnikov, waving it off pettishly.
uz: Let me try it on. Presently, afterwards, dedi Raskolnikov, qo'pollik bilan ovutadi.

en: “Come, Rodya, my boy, don’t oppose it, afterwards will be too late; and I shan’t sleep all night, for I bought it by guess, without measure.
uz: Kosh, Rodya, o'g'lim, bunga qarshilik ko'rsatma, keyinchalik juda kech bo'ladi; va men butun kecha uxlamayman, chunki men uni taxmin qilish orqali, o'lchovsiz sotib oldim.

en: Just right!” he cried triumphantly, fitting it on, “just your size!
uz: To'g'ri! u g'alaba bilan baqirib, uni kiygan holda,  faqat sizning o'lchamingiz!

en: A proper head-covering is the first thing in dress and a recommendation in its own way.
uz: To'g'ri boshni qoplash - bu kiyimda birinchi narsa va o'z usuli bilan tavsiya.

en: Tolstyakov, a friend of mine, is always obliged to take off his pudding basin when he goes into any public place where other people wear their hats or caps.
uz: Do'stim Tolstyakov har doim boshqa odamlar o'z to'pkalarini yoki to'pkalarini kiygan ommaviy joyga kirganda pudding maydonini olib tashlashga majbur.

en: People think he does it from slavish politeness, but it’s simply because he is ashamed of his bird’s nest; he is such a boastful fellow!
uz: Odamlar buni qullikdagi xushmuomalalikdan deb o'ylashadi, lekin bu shunchaki u o'z qushlar yuvidan uyalganidan; u juda maqtanchli odam!

en: Look, Nastasya, here are two specimens of headgear: this Palmerston” —he took from the corner Raskolnikov’s old, battered hat, which for some unknown reason, he called a Palmerston —“or this jewel!
uz: Qarang, Nastasya, bu yerda ikkita bosh kiyimlari bor: bu Palmerston u burchadan Raskolnikovning eski, urib ketgan to'pqini olibdi, u nima sababdan, noma'lum sabablarga ko'ra, Palmerston yoki bu marvarid deb ataladi!

en: Guess the price, Rodya, what do you suppose I paid for it, Nastasya!” he said, turning to her, seeing that Raskolnikov did not speak.
uz: Qiymatni tasavvur qiling, Rodya, men buning uchun qancha pul to'laganimni tasavvur qiling, Nastasya! dedi u, Raskolnikov gapirmaganini ko'rib, unga qarab.

en: “Twenty kopecks, no more, I dare say,” answered Nastasya.
uz: 20 kopek, ko'proq emas, deyishga jur'at qilaman, dedi Nastasya.

en: “Twenty kopecks, silly!” he cried, offended.
uz: 20 kopek, ahmoq! u yig'lab yubordi, xafa bo'ldi.

en: “Why, nowadays you would cost more than that —eighty kopecks!
uz: Bugun siz o'ttiz kopekdan ham ko'proq pul to'lashingiz mumkin!

en: And that only because it has been worn.
uz: Va bu faqatgina uni kiyganligi uchun.

en: And it’s bought on condition that when’s it’s worn out, they will give you another next year.
uz: Va uni sotib olish sharti bilan amalga oshiriladi, agar u ishlatib ketsa, kelgusi yilda sizga yana bir taom beradilar.

en: Well, now let us pass to the United States of America, as they called them at school.
uz: Keling, endi Amerika Qo'shma Shtatlariga o'tamiz, chunki ular maktabda ularni shunday deb atashardi.

en: I assure you I am proud of these breeches,” and he exhibited to Raskolnikov a pair of light, summer trousers of grey woollen material.
uz: Sizlarga shuni aytamanki, men bu cho'tkalardan faxrlanaman, va u Raskolnikovga rangli, yozgi shkaflarni griy jun materialidan ko'rsatdi.

en: “No holes, no spots, and quite respectable, although a little worn; and a waistcoat to match, quite in the fashion.
uz: Tushlar yo'q, lentilar yo'q va juda hurmatga sazovor, garchi biroz kiyingan bo'lsa-da; va mos keladigan kiyim, juda modada.

en: And its being worn really is an improvement, it’s softer, smoother.
uz: Va uning kiyinganligi, haqiqatan ham, yaxshilanishdir, u yumshakroq va moslashtiriladi.

en: … You see, Rodya, to my thinking, the great thing for getting on in the world is always to keep to the seasons; if you don’t insist on having asparagus in January, you keep your money in your purse; and it’s the same with this purchase.
uz: Koʻrib turganingizdek, Rodya, mening fikrimcha, dunyoda muvaffaqiyatga erishish uchun eng yaxshi narsa - har doim mavsumlarga rioya qilishdir; agar siz yanvar oyida asparagus olishni istayotgan boʻlsangiz, pulingizni qopqozingizda saqlang; va bu xarid bilan ham xuddi shunday.

en: It’s summer now, so I’ve been buying summer things —warmer materials will be wanted for autumn, so you will have to throw these away in any case … especially as they will be done for by then from their own lack of coherence if not your higher standard of luxury.
uz: Endi yozgi kun, shuning uchun yozgi narsalarni sotib olyapman kuz uchun issiqroq materiallar kerak bo'ladi, shuning uchun siz ularni har holda tashlashingiz kerak bo'ladi ... ayniqsa, ular o'sha paytgacha o'zlarining ko'payishsizligi sababli, agar sizning yuqori darajadagi hashamatingiz bo'lmasa, o'zlari uchun tayyor bo'ladi.

en: Two roubles twenty-five kopecks!
uz: Ikki rubl yigirma besh kopek!

en: And remember the condition: if you wear these out, you will have another suit for nothing!
uz: Va sharti shuni esda tuting: agar siz ularni kiyib yuborsangiz, boshqa kiyimingiz bepul bo'ladi!

en: They only do business on that system at Fedyaev’s; if you’ve bought a thing once, you are satisfied for life, for you will never go there again of your own free will.
uz: Ular faqat Fedyaevlarda ushbu tizim asosida ish olib boradilar; agar siz bir marta narsa sotib olsangiz, siz umrbod mamnun bo'lasiz, chunki siz boshqa hech qachon o'z xohishingiz bilan u yerga bormaysiz.

en: You see that they are a bit worn, but they’ll last a couple of months, for it’s foreign work and foreign leather; the secretary of the English Embassy sold them last week —he had only worn them six days, but he was very short of cash.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizcha, ular biroz ishlangan, lekin ular bir necha oy davom etadi, chunki bu chet el ish va chet el terisi; ingliz elchixonasi kotibi ularni o'tgan hafta sotdi.

en: Price —a rouble and a half.
uz: Qiymati bir yarim rubl.

en: A bargain?” “But perhaps they won’t fit,” observed Nastasya.
uz: Bir kelishuvmi? Ammo ehtimol ular mos kelmasligi mumkin, - dedi Nastasya.

en: Just look!” and he pulled out of his pocket Raskolnikov’s old, broken boot, stiffly coated with dry mud.
uz: Qarang! va u o'zining qariya, buzilgan, quruq loydan qoplangan Raskolnikov botasini qopqoqidan chiqardi.

en: “I did not go empty- handed —they took the size from this monster.
uz: Men bo'sh qo'llar bilan bormadim, ular bu jondorning o'lchamini olishdi.

en: We all did our best.
uz: Hammamiz qo'limizdan kelganini qildik.

en: And as to your linen, your landlady has seen to that.
uz: Sizning chiroyli kiyimingiz haqida gap ketganda, uy egasi bu haqda g'amxo'rlik qildi.

en: Here, to begin with are three shirts, hempen but with a fashionable front.
uz: Bu yerda, boshlanishda, uchta ko'ylak bor, ular qanoqdan, ammo zamonaviy old tomonga ega.

en: … Well now then, eighty kopecks the cap, two roubles twenty-five kopecks the suit —together three roubles five kopecks —a rouble and a half for the boots —for, you see, they are very good —and that makes four roubles fifty-five kopecks; five roubles for the underclothes —they
uz: ... Xo'sh, endi sakson kopek to'pka, ikki rubl yigirma besh kopek kostyumni birlashtiradi, uch rubl besh kopek bir rubl va yarim botlar uchun, chunki ular juda yaxshi, va bu to'rt rubl besh kopek; besh rubl ichki kiyimlar uchun u

en: were bought in the lot —which makes exactly nine roubles fifty-five kopecks.
uz: Lotda sotib olindilar, bu to'qqiz rubl va ellik besh kopekga teng.

en: Forty-five kopecks change in coppers.
uz: To'rt besh kopek pulni ko'plarga aylantiradi.

en: And so, Rodya, you are set up with a complete new rig-out, for your overcoat will serve, and even has a style of its own.
uz: Shunday qilib, Rodya, siz to'liq yangi qurilmalarga ega bo'lasiz, chunki sizning kiyimingiz xizmat qiladi va hatto o'z uslubini o'z ichiga oladi.

en: That comes from getting one’s clothes from Sharmer’s!
uz: Bu esa Sharmerlardan kiyim olishdan kelib chiqadi!

en: As for your socks and other things, I leave them to you; we’ve twenty-five roubles left.
uz: Cho'nqalaringiz va boshqa narsalaringizga kelsak, ularni sizga qoldiraman; bizda yigirma besh rubl qolgan.

en: And as for Pashenka and paying for your lodging, don’t you worry.
uz: Va Pashenka va uy-joyingiz uchun to'lovlar haqida gap ketganda, tashvishlanmang.

en: I tell you she’ll trust you for anything.
uz: Sizga aytamanki, u sizga har qanday narsada ishonadi.

en: And now, brother, let me change your linen, for I daresay you will throw off your illness with your shirt.” “Let me be!
uz: Endi esa, birodarim, senga kiyimni o'zgartirishim kerak, chunki men aytamanki, sen kasalligingni ko'ylaking bilan tashlab yuborasan.  Meni qo'yib yubor!

en: I don’t want to!” Raskolnikov waved him off.
uz: Men xohlamayman! Raskolnikov uni qo'ldan urdi.

en: He had listened with disgust to Razumihin’s efforts to be playful about his purchases.
uz: U Razumihinning xaridlari haqida o'yinli bo'lishga harakat qilishini nafrat bilan tinglagan edi.

en: “Come, brother, don’t tell me I’ve been trudging around for nothing,” Razumihin insisted.
uz: Yay, aka, menga men befoyda harakat qilib kelayotganimni aytma,  Razumihin istaydi.

en: “Nastasya, don’t be bashful, but help me —that’s it,” and in spite of Raskolnikov’s resistance he changed his linen.
uz: Nastasya, uyatchilik qilma, lekin menga yordam ber, Raskolnikovning qarshiligiga qaramay, u kiyimini o'zgartirdi.

en: The latter sank back on the pillows and for a minute or two said nothing.
uz: U o'z yastog'iga qaytdi va bir-ikki daqiqa davomida hech narsa aytmadi.

en: “It will be long before I get rid of them,” he thought.
uz: "Ulardan xalos bo'lishimga ancha vaqt ketadi", deb o'yladi u.

en: “What money was all that bought with?” he asked at last, gazing at the wall.
uz: Buning hammasi qanday pul bilan sotib olingan? deb so'radi u, nihoyat, devorga qarab.

en: Why, your own, what the messenger brought from Vahrushin, your mother sent it.
uz: Ehtimol, o'zingizning, Vahrushindan elchi olib kelgan narsani onangiz yubordi.

en: Have you forgotten that, too?” “I remember now,” said Raskolnikov after a long, sullen silence.
uz: Siz ham buni unutdingizmi?Men endi eslayman, dedi Raskolnikov uzoq, g'alati so'zsizlikdan keyin.

en: Razumihin looked at him, frowning and uneasy.
uz: Razumihin unga ko'z tikib, xavotirlanib qaradi.

en: The door opened and a tall, stout man whose appearance seemed familiar to Raskolnikov came in.
uz: Eshik ochildi va Raskolnikovga tanish ko'rinadigan baland, kuchli odam kirdi.

en: IV Zossimov was a tall, fat man with a puffy, colourless, clean-shaven face and straight flaxen hair.
uz: IV. Zossimov baland, semiz odam bo'lib, yuzi puflangan, rangsiz, toza shavgan va sochlari to'g'ridan-to'g'ri bo'lgan.

en: He wore spectacles, and a big gold ring on his fat finger.
uz: U ko'zoynak kiygan edi va katta oltin bog'chaga o'zining yumshoq barmog'ida bog'langan edi.

en: He was twenty-seven.
uz: U yigirma yetti yoshda edi.

en: He had on a light grey fashionable loose coat, light summer trousers, and everything about him loose, fashionable and spick and span; his linen was irreproachable, his watch-chain was massive.
uz: U yengil bo'lak kiyimda, yorug' yozgi shortsda va uning atrofidagi hamma narsa yengil, moddiy va chiroyli edi; uning kiyim-kechaklari aybsiz edi, uning soat zanjirlari katta edi.

en: In manner he was slow and, as it were, nonchalant, and at the same time studiously free and easy; he made efforts to conceal his self-importance, but it was apparent at every instant.
uz: U asta-sekin va befarq bo'lib, bir vaqtning o'zida o'zboshimchalik bilan erkin va oson edi; o'z qadr-qimmatini yashirish uchun harakat qilardi, ammo bu har bir daqiqada ko'rinib turardi.

en: All his acquaintances found him tedious, but said he was clever at his work.
uz: Uning barcha tanishlari uni charchatgan deb hisoblashgan, ammo uning ishi juda aqlli ekanligini aytishgan.

en: “I’ve been to you twice today, brother.
uz: Bugun siz bilan ikki marta uchrashdim, aka.

en: You see, he’s come to himself,” cried Razumihin.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, u o'z-o'ziga keldi, - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: “I see, I see; and how do we feel now, eh?” said Zossimov to Raskolnikov, watching him carefully and, sitting down at the foot of the sofa, he settled himself as comfortably as he could.
uz: Men ko'ryapman, ko'ryapman; va biz endi qanday his qilyapmiz, eh? dedi Zossimov Raskolnikovga, unga diqqat bilan qaradi va sofaning oyoqida o'tirib, imkon qadar qulay o'zini o'rnatib oladi.

en: “He is still depressed,” Razumihin went on.
uz: U hali ham tushkunlikka tushibdi,  Razumihin davom etdi.

en: “We’ve just changed his linen and he almost cried.” “That’s very natural; you might have put it off if he did not wish it.
uz: Biz uning chiroqlarini o'zgartirdik va u deyarli yig'lab yubordi.Bu juda tabiiy; agar u xohlamasa, siz uni kechiktirgan bo'lar edingiz.

en: … His pulse is first-rate.
uz: Uning pulsi birinchi darajali.

en: Is your head still aching, eh?” “I am well, I am perfectly well!” Raskolnikov declared positively and irritably.
uz: Boshingiz hali ham og'riqlimi, eh?  Men yaxshiman, men mukammal darajada yaxshiman! Raskolnikov ijobiy va g'azabga to'lgan holda e'lon qildi.

en: He raised himself on the sofa and looked at them with glittering eyes, but sank back on to the pillow at once and turned to the wall.
uz: U o'zini sofa ustiga ko'tarib, shinam ko'zlar bilan ularga qaradi, lekin darhol yostiqqa qaytadi va devorga qarab o'tiradi.

en: Zossimov watched him intently.
uz: Zossimov uni diqqat bilan kuzatib turardi.

en: … Going on all right,” he said lazily.
uz: ... To'g'ri davom etib, u lazzat bilan dedi.

en: “Has he eaten anything?” They told him, and asked what he might have.
uz: U biron narsa yemaganmi? Ular unga xabar berishdi va undan nima bo'lishi mumkinligini so'rashdi.

en: “He may have anything … soup, tea … mushrooms and cucumbers, of course, you must not give him; he’d better not have meat either, and … but no need to tell you that!” Razumihin and he looked at each other.
uz: U biron bir narsaga ega bo'lishi mumkin ... shovba, choy ... qo'zg'oq va tegirmonlar, albatta, siz unga bermasligingiz kerak; u ham go'shtga ega bo'lmasligi yaxshiroqdir va ... lekin sizga buni aytishning hojati yo'q! Razumihin va u bir-biriga qarab turishdi.

en: “No more medicine or anything.
uz: O'shanda hech qanday dori-darmon yoki boshqa narsa yo'q.

en: I’ll look at him again tomorrow.
uz: Ertaga uni yana ko'rib chiqaman.

en: Perhaps, today even … but never mind …” “Tomorrow evening I shall take him for a walk,” said Razumihin.
uz: Ehtimol, bugun ham ... lekin hech narsa ahamiyat bermaydi ... Ertaga kechqurun uni ko'chishga olib ketaman, dedi Razumihin.

en: “We are going to the Yusupov garden and then to the Palais de Cristal.” “I would not disturb him tomorrow at all, but I don’t know … a little, maybe … but we’ll see.” “Ach, what a nuisance!
uz: Yusupov bog'iga, so'ngra Kristal saroyiga ketamiz. Men uni ertaga hech qachon bezovta qilmayman, lekin bilmayman... bir oz, ehtimol... lekin ko'ramiz.A, bu qanday noqulaylik!

en: I’ve got a housewarming party tonight; it’s only a step from here.
uz: Bugun uyni quritish partiyasi bo'lib o'tdi; bu yerdan bir qadam uzoq.

en: He could lie on the sofa.
uz: Sofa ustida yotgan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: You are coming?” Razumihin said to Zossimov.
uz: Siz kelyapsizmi? Razumihin Zossimovga dedi.

en: “Don’t forget, you promised.” “All right, only rather later.
uz: Esingizda bo'lsin, siz va'da bergan edingiz.To'g'ri, keyinroq.

en: What are you going to do?” “Oh, nothing —tea, vodka, herrings.
uz: Nima qilmoqchisiz?Oh, hech narsa tea, vodka, hering.

en: There will be a pie … just our friends.” “And who?” “All neighbours here, almost all new friends, except my old uncle, and he is new too —he only arrived in Petersburg yesterday to see to some business of his.
uz: O'sha yerda kek bo'ladi... faqat do'stlarimiz. Va kim? Bu erda barcha qo'shnilar, deyarli barcha yangi do'stlar, balki mening keksa o'g'lim va u ham yangi.U faqat o'z ishini ko'rish uchun kecha Sankt-Peterburgga keldi.

en: We meet once in five years.” “What is he?” “He’s been stagnating all his life as a district postmaster; gets a little pension.
uz: Biz besh yilda bir marta uchrashamiz. U nima? U butun hayoti davomida tuman pochta boshlig'i sifatida to'xtamaydi; u kichik pensiya oladi.

en: He is sixty-five —not worth talking about.
uz: U oltmish besh yoshda, bu haqda gapirishga arziydigan emas.

en: … But I am fond of him.
uz: Lekin men uni yaxshi ko'raman.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch, the head of the Investigation Department here … But you know him.” “Is he a relation of yours, too?” “A very distant one.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch, bu yerda tergov bo'limi boshlig'i... Ammo siz uni bilasiz.¿U sizning ham qarindoshingizmi?U juda uzoq qarindosh.

en: But why are you scowling?
uz: Ammo nega siz g'ayratli bo'lasiz?

en: Because you quarrelled once, won’t you come then?” “I don’t care a damn for him.” “So much the better.
uz: Siz bir marta bahslashganingiz uchun, kelmaysizmi?Menga u haqida hech qanday g'amxo'rlik yo'q.Bu shunchalik yaxshi.

en: Well, there will be some students, a teacher, a government clerk, a musician, an officer and Zametov.” “Do tell me, please, what you or he” —Zossimov nodded at Raskolnikov —“can have in common with this Zametov?” “Oh, you particular gentleman!
uz: O'quvchilar, o'qituvchi, davlat xizmatchisi, musiqachi, ofitser va Zametov bo'ladi.  Menga ayting, iltimos, siz yoki u  Zossimov Raskolnikovga bosh qo'yib qo'ydigan nimalar Raskolnikov bilan umumiy bo'lishi mumkin?   Oh, siz xayrli janob!

en: You are worked by principles, as it were by springs; you won’t venture to turn round on
uz: Sizda prinsiplar, xuddi chiziqlar yordamida ishlaydigan bo'lsangiz ham, siz o'zingizni o'zgartirishga jur'at etmaysiz.

en: If a man is a nice fellow, that’s the only principle I go upon.
uz: Agar erkak yaxshi odam bo'lsa, men faqat shu prinsipga amal qilaman.

en: Zametov is a delightful person.” “Though he does take bribes.” “Well, he does!
uz: Zametov chiroyli odam.  Garchi u rentib olishsa ham.  Xo'sh, u shunday qiladi!

en: I don’t care if he does take bribes,” Razumihin cried with unnatural irritability.
uz: U rentib olsa ham, menga ahamiyat bermayapti, - dedi Razumihin tabiiy bo'lmagan xafalik bilan yig'lab.

en: “I don’t praise him for taking bribes.
uz: Men uni rentiq olish uchun maqtamayman.

en: I only say he is a nice man in his own way!
uz: Men faqat uning o'z uslubida yaxshi odam ekanligini aytaman!

en: But if one looks at men in all ways —are there many good ones left?
uz: Ammo agar insonlarga turlicha qarashsa, yaxshi kishilar ko'p bo'ladimi?

en: Why, I am sure I shouldn’t be worth a baked onion myself … perhaps with you thrown in.” “That’s too little; I’d give two for you.” “And I wouldn’t give more than one for you.
uz: Ehtimol, men o'zim ham pishirilgan soyaga loyiq bo'lmasam kerak... ehtimol, siz o'zingiz tashlaganingizda.Bu juda kam; men siz uchun ikkita beraman. Va men siz uchun bittadan ko'proq bermayman.

en: No more of your jokes!
uz: Sizlarning hazillaringiz tugadi!

en: Zametov is no more than a boy.
uz: Zametov o'g'ildan boshqa narsa emas.

en: I can pull his hair and one must draw him not repel him.
uz: Men uning sochlarini tortib olsam bo'ladi, lekin uni tiriltirmaslik uchun uni tortib olish kerak.

en: You’ll never improve a man by repelling him, especially a boy.
uz: Siz hech qachon odamni, ayniqsa, o'g'ilni rad etib, uni yaxshilay olmaysiz.

en: One has to be twice as careful with a boy.
uz: O'g'il bilan ikki baravar ehtiyot bo'lish kerak.

en: Oh, you progressive dullards!
uz: Oh, siz ilg'or dullardslar!

en: You don’t understand.
uz: Siz tushunmayapsiz.

en: You harm yourselves running another man down.
uz: Boshqa odamni o'ldirganingizda o'zingizni yomon his qilasiz.

en: … But if you want to know, we really have something in common.” “I should like to know what.” “Why, it’s all about a house-painter.
uz: Ammo bilmoqchi bo'lsangiz, bizda juda ham umumiy bir narsa bor.  Men nima haqida bilishni xohlayman.  Nima uchun, bu barcha uy-joy rassomi haqida.

en: … We are getting him out of a mess!
uz: ... Biz uni buzuqlikdan xalos qilmoqdamiz!

en: Though indeed there’s nothing to fear now.
uz: Garchi hozirda qo'rqish uchun hech narsa yo'q bo'lsa-da.

en: The matter is absolutely self-evident.
uz: Bu mutlaqo o'z-o'zidan ko'rinadi.

en: We only put on steam.” “A painter?” “Why, haven’t I told you about it?
uz: Biz faqat bug'ni qo'yamiz. Ressamchi?  Nima uchun, men sizga bu haqda aytmagan edimmi?

en: I only told you the beginning then about the murder of the old pawnbroker-woman.
uz: O'sha paytda men sizga faqatgina qadimgi qarzdor ayolning o'ldirilishi haqida boshlanishni aytib berdim.

en: Well, the painter is mixed up in it …” “Oh, I heard about that murder before and was rather interested in it … partly … for one reason.
uz: Bu yerda rassom o'z o'rnida ...Oh, men o'sha qotillik to'g'risida ilgari eshitgan edim va bu menga qiziqqan edi ... qisman ... bir sababdan.

en: … I read about it in the papers, too.
uz: Men ham bu haqda gazetalarda o'qiganman.

en: …” “Lizaveta was murdered, too,” Nastasya blurted out, suddenly addressing Raskolnikov.
uz: ... Lizaveta ham o'ldirildi, Nastasya o'zini ko'tardi va to'satdan Raskolnikovga murojaat qildi.

en: She remained in the room all the time, standing by the door listening.
uz: U doimo xonada, eshik oldida turib, tinglab turardi.

en: “Lizaveta,” murmured Raskolnikov hardly audibly.
uz: Lizaveta, Raskolnikov kamdan-kam eshitib turibdi.

en: “Lizaveta, who sold old clothes.
uz: Lizaveta, eski kiyim-kechaklarni sotgan.

en: Didn’t you know her?
uz: Siz uni tanib-bilmadingizmi?

en: She used to come here.
uz: U bu yerga kelardi.

en: She mended a shirt for you, too.” Raskolnikov turned to the wall where in the dirty, yellow paper he picked out one clumsy, white flower with brown lines on it and began examining how many petals there were in it, how many scallops in the petals and how many lines on them.
uz: U siz uchun ham ko'ylakni tuzatdi. Raskolnikov devorga qarab, kirli, sariq qog'ozda bir qaroqsiz, oq gul, uning ustida qalin chiziqlar borligini ko'rib chiqdi va u ichida qancha ko'kraklar, ko'kraklar va ularning ustida qancha chiziqlar borligini o'rganishni boshladi.

en: He felt his arms and legs as
uz: U qo'l-oyoqlarini va oyoqlarini xuddi shunday his qilardi.

en: lifeless as though they had been cut off.
uz: O'zlarining hayotlari yo'q bo'lib, xuddi o'zlari kesib ketgandek.

en: He did not attempt to move, but stared obstinately at the flower.
uz: U harakatlanishga harakat qilmadi, balki o'z ko'zlari bilan gulga qaradi.

en: “But what about the painter?” Zossimov interrupted Nastasya’s chatter with marked displeasure.
uz: Agar bo'lsa, rassom haqida nima deyish mumkin? Zossimov Nastasyaxning suhbatini ko'p norozilik bilan uzdi.

en: She sighed and was silent.
uz: U nafas oldi va soʻzsiz qoldi.

en: “Why, he was accused of the murder,” Razumihin went on hotly.
uz: Nima uchun, uni o'ldirishda ayblashdi,  Razumihin qizg'in davom etdi.

en: “Was there evidence against him then?” “Evidence, indeed!
uz: O'shanda unga qarshi dalillar bormidi? Dasturiyat, albatta!

en: Evidence that was no evidence, and that’s what we have to prove.
uz: Bu hech qanday dalil emas edi va biz buni isbotlashimiz kerak.

en: It was just as they pitched on those fellows, Koch and Pestryakov, at first.
uz: Boshida ular Koch va Pestryakovni o'sha yigitlarga qarshi o'ynashgan edi.

en: how stupidly it’s all done, it makes one sick, though it’s not one’s business!
uz: Bularning barchasi qanchalik ahmoqona amalga oshirilsa, bu odamni kasal qiladi, garchi bu uning ishi emas!

en: Pestryakov may be coming tonight.
uz: Pestryakov bugun kechqurun kelishi mumkin.

en: … By the way, Rodya, you’ve heard about the business already; it happened before you were ill, the day before you fainted at the police office while they were talking about it.” Zossimov looked curiously at Raskolnikov.
uz: Aytgancha, Rodya, siz bu ish haqida eshitgansiz; bu kasal bo'lishingizdan oldin, ular bu haqda gapirayotganida siz politsiya xonasida baytilanib qolishdan bir kun oldin sodir bo'ldi. Zossimov Raskolnikovga qiziqarli qarashdi.

en: “But I say, Razumihin, I wonder at you.
uz: Lekin men aytaman, Razumihin, men sizdan hayronman.

en: What a busybody you are!” Zossimov observed.
uz: Siz juda mashg'ulsiz! Zossimov kuzatdi.

en: “Maybe I am, but we will get him off anyway,” shouted Razumihin, bringing his fist down on the table.
uz: Ehtimol, shunday bo'lardim, lekin biz uni har holda olib tashlaymiz, deb baqirib yubordi Razumihin, o'z yumushini stol ustiga tushirdi.

en: “What’s the most offensive is not their lying —one can always forgive lying —lying is a delightful thing, for it leads to truth —what is offensive is that they lie and worship their own lying.
uz: Agar ularning yolg'on gapirishlari eng zo'ravon bo'lmasa, Boshqalarning yolg'on gapirishlarini har doim kechirishi mumkin  yolg'on gapirish yoqimli narsa, chunki u haqiqatga yetaklaydi Agar ular yolg'on gapirib, o'z yolg'onlariga sajda qilishlari zo'ravon bo'ladi.

en: … I respect Porfiry, but … What threw them out at first?
uz: Men Porfirni hurmat qilaman, lekin ularni dastlab nima tashlab yubordi?

en: The door was locked, and when they came back with the porter it was open.
uz: Eshik qulflab qo'yilgan edi va ular portiyer bilan qaytib kelganlarida eshik ochiq edi.

en: So it followed that Koch and Pestryakov were the murderers —that was their logic!” “But don’t excite yourself; they simply detained them, they could not help that.
uz: Shunday qilib, Koch va Pestryakov qotillar ekanligi aniqlandi, bu ularning mantiqiy nuqtai nazari edi! Ammo o'zingizni qo'zg'atmang; ular shunchaki ularni ushlab qo'ydilar, bu ularga yordam bermadi.

en: … And, by the way, I’ve met that man Koch.
uz: Aytgancha, men Koch bilan uchrashdim.

en: He used to buy unredeemed pledges from the old woman?
uz: U keksa ayoldan to'lov qilinmagan qarzdorlikni sotib olganmi?

en: Eh?” “Yes, he is a swindler.
uz: - Ha, u o'g'li o'g'il.

en: He buys up bad debts, too.
uz: U ham yomon qarzlarni sotib oladi.

en: He makes a profession of it.
uz: U bu ishni kasbga aylantiradi.

en: Do you know what makes me angry?
uz: Meni nima g'azablantirishini bilasizmi?

en: It’s their sickening rotten, petrified routine.
uz: Bu ularning jirkanch, o'g'irlangan va toshbo'ronli urf-odatlari.

en: … And this case might be the means of introducing a new method.
uz: ... Va bu holat yangi usulni joriy etish vositasi bo'lishi mumkin.

en: One can show from the psychological data alone how to get on the track of the real man.
uz: Faqatgina psixologik ma'lumotlardan foydalanib, haqiqiy odamning yo'lidan qanday o'tishni ko'rsatsa bo'ladi.

en: ‘We have facts,’ they say.
uz: "Bizda faktlar bor" deyishadi.

en: But facts are not everything —at least half the business lies in how you interpret them!” “Can you interpret them, then?” “Anyway, one can’t hold one’s tongue when one has a feeling, a tangible feeling, that one might be a help if only.
uz: Ammo faktlar hamma narsa emas!Agar yo'q bo'lsa, ularning yarmi siz ularni qanday talqin qilishingizga bog'liq!Shunday bo'lsa, siz ularni qanday talqin qila olasiz? Qanday bo'lmasin, biror kishi hissiyotga, aniq hissiyotga ega bo'lganda tilini ushlab tura olmaydi, chunki u yordam berishi mumkin.

en: the details of the case?” “I am waiting to hear about the painter.” “Oh, yes!
uz: Ishning tafsilotlari? Men rassom haqida eshitishni kutyapman. Oh, ha!

en: Well, here’s the story.
uz: Xo'sh, hikoya shunday.

en: Early on the third day after the murder, when they were still dandling Koch and Pestryakov —though they accounted for every step they took and it was as plain as a pikestaff —an unexpected fact turned up.
uz: O'ldirilgandan keyin uchinchi kunning ertalarida, ular hali ham Koch va Pestryakovni qichqirganlarida, ular qo'ygan har bir qadamlari haqida gapirib berishgan edi va bu pikestaff kabi aniq edi, ammo kutilmagan fakt paydo bo'ldi.

en: A peasant called Dushkin, who keeps a dram-shop facing the house, brought to the police office a jeweller’s case containing some gold earrings, and told a long rigamarole.
uz: Uyga qarata dram-do'konini o'tkazadigan Dushkin ismli qishloq xo'jaligi politsiya xodimiga oltin bo'yindan iborat zargarlik quti olib kelib, uzoq bir rigamaroli so'zladi.

en: ‘The day before yesterday, just after eight o’clock’ — mark the day and the hour!
uz: Kecha, soat sakkizdan so'ng, kun va soatni belgilab oling!

en: —‘a journeyman house-painter, Nikolay, who had been in to see me already that day, brought me this box of gold earrings and stones, and asked me to give him two roubles for them.
uz: O'sha kuni meni ko'rish uchun kelgan Nikolay ismli sayohatchi uy bo'yishi, menga oltin qulog'lar va toshlar bilan to'plam olib keldi va ular uchun ikki rubl berishimni so'radi.

en: When I asked him where he got them, he said that he picked them up in the street.
uz: Men undan ularni qayerdan olganini so'raganimda, u ularni ko'chada olib kelganini aytdi.

en: I did not ask him anything more.’ I am telling you Dushkin’s story.
uz: Men undan boshqa hech narsa so'ramadim. Sizga Dushkinning hikoyasini aytib beryapman.

en: ‘I gave him a note’ —a rouble that is —‘for I thought if he did not pawn it with me he would with another.
uz: Men unga notani berdim Rubl, chunki men uni men bilan bermasa, boshqa bilan berishini o'yladim.

en: It would all come to the same thing —he’d spend it on drink, so the thing had better be with me.
uz: Hamma narsa bir xil narsaga kelib chiqadi, uni ichishga sarflaydi, shuning uchun bu narsa men bilan bo'lishi yaxshiroqdir.

en: The further you hide it the quicker you will find it, and if anything turns up, if I hear any rumours, I’ll take it to the police.’ Of course, that’s all taradiddle; he lies like a horse, for I know this Dushkin, he is a pawnbroker and a receiver of stolen goods, and he did not cheat Nikolay out of a thirty-rouble trinket in order to give it to the police.
uz: Uni qancha ko'proq yashirsangiz, shuncha tezroq topasiz va agar biror narsa paydo bo'lsa, agar biron bir mish-mishni eshitsam, uni politsiyaga olib ketaman. Albatta, bularning hammasi o'ziga yarasha; u ot kabi yolg'on gapiradi, chunki men bu Dushkinni bilaman, u pawnbroker va o'g'irlangan tovarlarni qabul qiluvchi, va u Nikolayni politsiyaga berish uchun o'ttiz rubllik shkafdan o'g'irlamagan.

en: He was simply afraid.
uz: U shunchaki qo'rqqan.

en: But no matter, to return to Dushkin’s story.
uz: Ammo Dushkinning hikoyasiga qaytish uchun hech narsa ahamiyat bermaydi.

en: ‘I’ve known this peasant, Nikolay Dementyev, from a child; he comes from the same province and district of Zaraïsk, we are both Ryazan men.
uz: Men bu qishloq xo'jaligi Nikolay Dementyevni bolaligimdan taniganman; u bir xil viloyat va Zaraisk tumanidan kelgan, biz ikkovimiz ham Ryazan erkaklarimiz.

en: And though Nikolay is not a drunkard, he drinks, and I knew he had a job in that house, painting work with Dmitri, who comes from the same village, too.
uz: Nikolay ichkilikboz bo'lmagan bo'lsa-da, ichadi va men uning o'sha uyda ish topganini bilardim, u ham o'sha qishloqda yashovchi Dmitriy bilan rasm chizish bilan shug'ullanardi.

en: As soon as he got the rouble he changed it, had a couple of glasses, took his change and went out.
uz: Rublni olgandan so'ng o'zgartirdi, bir nechta shisha olib, o'zining o'zgaruvchini olib, tashqariga chiqdi.

en: But I did not see Dmitri with him then.
uz: Ammo o'shanda Dmitriyni u bilan ko'rmaganman.

en: And the next day I heard that someone had murdered Alyona Ivanovna and her sister, Lizaveta Ivanovna, with an axe.
uz: Ertasi kuni kimdir Alyona Ivanovna va uning singlisi Lizaveta Ivanovnani o'g'ir bilan o'ldirganini eshitdim.

en: I knew them, and I felt suspicious about the earrings at once, for I knew the murdered woman lent money on pledges.
uz: Men ularni bilardim va o'sha zahoti bu qulqog'lar haqida shubhalanardim, chunki o'ldirilgan ayolning g'ayb pulini qarz olganini bilardim.

en: I went to the house, and began to make careful inquiries without saying a word to anyone.
uz: Men uyga bordim va hech kimga so'z aytmasdan ehtiyotkorlik bilan tekshirib ko'rishni boshladim.

en: First of all I asked, “Is Nikolay here?” Dmitri told me that Nikolay had gone off on the spree; he had come home at daybreak drunk, stayed in the house about ten
uz: Avvalo, "Nikolay bu yerdami?" deb so'radim.Dmitriy menga Nikolay o'z mashg'ulotini boshlaganini, erta tongda ichkilikboz uyga kelganini, o'nlab soatcha uyda qolganini aytdi.

en: minutes, and went out again.
uz: Bir necha daqiqa o'tgach, yana tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Dmitri didn’t see him again and is finishing the job alone.
uz: Dmitriy uni yana ko'rmadi va uni yolg'iz tugatmoqda.

en: And their job is on the same staircase as the murder, on the second floor.
uz: Ularning ishi esa o'ldirilgan odamning ikkinchi qavatidagi turar joyida.

en: When I heard all that I did not say a word to anyone’ —that’s Dushkin’s tale —‘but I found out what I could about the murder, and went home feeling as suspicious as ever.
uz: Bularning barchasini eshitganimda hech kimga bir so'z aytmadim, bu Dushkinning hikoyasi, lekin qotillik to'g'risida bilganimni bilib, o'zimni har doimgidek shubhali his etib uyga qaytdim.

en: And at eight o’clock this morning’ —that was the third day, you understand —‘I saw Nikolay coming in, not sober, though not to say very drunk —he could understand what was said to him.
uz: Va bugun ertalab soat sakkizlarda - uchinchi kun edi, tushunasiz - Nikolayni ichkariga kirayotganini ko'rdim, u sobit emas, garchi juda mast bo'lmasin - unga nima aytilganini tushunardi.

en: He sat down on the bench and did not speak.
uz: U o'rindiqga o'tirdi va gapirmadi.

en: There was only one stranger in the bar and a man I knew asleep on a bench and our two boys.
uz: Barda faqat bitta begona odam, men bilgan bir kishi va ikkita o'g'limiz bankda uxlab yotgan edi.

en: “Have you seen Dmitri?” said I.
uz: Dmitriyni ko'rganmisiz? dedi men.

en: “No, I haven’t,” said he.
uz: Yo'q, men buni qilmaganman, dedi u.

en: “And you’ve not been here either?” “Not since the day before yesterday,” said he.
uz: Siz ham bu yerga kelmadingizmi? - dedi u. - Kechadan beri yo'q.

en: “And where did you sleep last night?” “In Peski, with the Kolomensky men.” “And where did you get those earrings?” I asked.
uz: Kecha qayerda uxladingiz?Peski shahrida Kolomenskiylar bilan birga.Shuning uchun bu qulqog'larni qayerdan olgansiz? deb so'radim.

en: “I found them in the street,” and the way he said it was a bit queer; he did not look at me.
uz: Men ularni ko'chada topdim va uning so'zlash usuli biroz g'ayritabiiy edi; u menga qaramasdi.

en: “Did you hear what happened that very evening, at that very hour, on that same staircase?” said I.
uz: O'sha kechqurun, o'sha soatda, o'sha daraxtning o'zida nima sodir bo'lganini eshitganmisiz? - deb so'radi men.

en: “No,” said he, “I had not heard,” and all the while he was listening, his eyes were staring out of his head and he turned as white as chalk.
uz: - Yo'q, - dedi u. - Men buni eshitmaganman. - U tinglayotganda ko'zlari boshidan chiqib ko'rindi va u chalk kabi oq bo'ldi.

en: I told him all about it and he took his hat and began getting up.
uz: Men unga hamma narsani aytib berdim va u to'pini olib, turishga kirdi.

en: I wanted to keep him.
uz: Men uni saqlab qolmoqchi edim.

en: “Wait a bit, Nikolay,” said I, “won’t you have a drink?” And I signed to the boy to hold the door, and I came out from behind the bar; but he darted out and down the street to the turning at a run.
uz: Biroz vaqt turing, Nikolay, dedim men, sen ichmaysanmi? Men o'g'ilga eshikni ushlab turishga imzo qo'ydim va men bar orqasidan chiqib keldim; lekin u ko'chadan chiqib, yugurish uchun yugurib ketdi.

en: I have not seen him since.
uz: O'shandan beri uni ko'rmadim.

en: Then my doubts were at an end —it was his doing, as clear as could be.
uz: O'shanda shubhalarim tugadi - bu uning ishi edi, bu aniqroq bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: …’ ” “I should think so,” said Zossimov.
uz: ...   Men shunday o'ylashim kerak, dedi Zossimov.

en: Of course they sought high and low for Nikolay; they detained Dushkin and searched his house; Dmitri, too, was arrested; the Kolomensky men also were turned inside out.
uz: Albatta, ular Nikolay uchun yuqori va past qidirdilar; Dushkinni hibsga olib, uning uyini qidirdilar; Dmitriy ham hibsga olingan; Kolomenskiy odamlari ham orqaga burildi.

en: And the day before yesterday they arrested Nikolay in a tavern at the end of the town.
uz: Bir kun oldin Nikolayni shahar chetidagi mehmonxonada hibsga olishdi.

en: He had gone there, taken the silver cross off his neck and asked for a dram for it.
uz: U o'sha yerga bordi, g'alati ko'ksidan kumush xochni olib, uning uchun bir dram so'radi.

en: They gave it to him.
uz: Uni unga berishdi.

en: A few minutes afterwards the woman went to the cowshed, and through a crack in the wall she saw in the stable adjoining he had made a noose of his sash from the beam, stood on a block of wood, and was trying to put his neck in the noose.
uz: Bir necha daqiqa o'tgach, ayol chorvaxonada bo'ldi va u qo'shni stallda ko'rgan devordagi bo'g'riqni ko'rib, u o'z bo'g'iniga o'g'irni yaratib, yog'och blokida turdi va bo'yniga o'g'irni qo'yishga harakat qildi.

en: The woman screeched her hardest; people ran in.
uz: Ayol eng og'ir ovoz bilan qichqirdi; odamlar yugurib kirishdi.

en: ‘So that’s what you are up to!’ ‘Take me,’ he says, ‘to such-
uz: Shunday qilib, siz ham shu ishni qilyapsiz! Meni olib keting, deydi u, shunday-

en: and-such a police officer; I’ll confess everything.’ Well, they took him to that police station —that is here —with a suitable escort.
uz: va shunday politsiya xodimi; men hamma narsani tan olaman. Xo'sh, ular uni shu politsiya bo'linmasiga olib ketishdi bu yerda o'rinli eskorta bilan.

en: So they asked him this and that, how old he is, ‘twenty-two,’ and so on.
uz: Shunday qilib, undan shu va shu savollar berishdi: unga necha yosh, yigirma ikki yosh va shunga o'xshash savollar berishdi.

en: At the question, ‘When you were working with Dmitri, didn’t you see anyone on the staircase at such-and-such a time?’ —answer: ‘To be sure folks may have gone up and down, but I did not notice them.’ ‘And didn’t you hear anything, any noise, and so on?’ ‘We heard nothing special.’ ‘And did you hear, Nikolay, that on the same day Widow So- and-so and her sister were murdered and robbed?’ ‘I never knew a thing about it.
uz: "Dmitriy bilan ishlayotganingizda, bunday va shunday vaqtlarda merosida hech kimni ko'rmadingizmi?  Javob: To'g'ri, odamlar ko'tarilgan va tushgan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin men ularni sezmaganman. Va siz hech narsa eshitmadingizmi, biron-bir shovqin va shunga o'xshash narsalar?  Biz hech narsa eshitmadik.  Va siz eshitganmisiz, Nikolay, bir kunning o'zida beva So-so va uning singlisi o'ldirilgan va talon qilingan?  Men bu haqda hech qachon hech narsa bilmaganman.

en: The first I heard of it was from Afanasy Pavlovitch the day before yesterday.’ ‘And where did you find the earrings?’ ‘I found them on the pavement.’ ‘Why didn’t you go to work with Dmitri the other day?’ ‘Because I was drinking.’ ‘And where were you drinking?’ ‘Oh, in such-and-such a place.’ ‘Why did you run away from Dushkin’s?’ ‘Because I was awfully frightened.’ ‘What were you frightened of?’ ‘That I should be accused.’ ‘How could you be frightened, if you felt free from guilt?’ Now, Zossimov, you may not believe me, that question was put literally in those words.
uz: Birinchi bor bu haqda eshitganim bir kun oldin Afanasiy Pavlovitchdan edi. Va qayoqdan quloqlarni topdingiz? Men ularni yo'ldan topdim. Nega siz Dmitri bilan ishlashga bormadingiz?  Chunki men ichar edim.  Va qaerda ichar edingiz?  Oh, shunday-ya'ni joyda.  Nima uchun Dushkinlardan qochib ketdingiz?  Chunki men juda qo'rqardim.  Siz nimadan qo'rqardingiz?  Men ayblanishim kerak.  Qanday qilib qo'rqardingiz, agar siz o'zingizni aybdan ozod his qilsangiz? Endi, Zossimov, siz menga ishonmayapsiz, bu savol shu so'zlar bilan so'ragan edi.

en: I know it for a fact, it was repeated to me exactly!
uz: Men buni aniq bilaman, bu menga to'g'ri takrorlandi!

en: What do you say to that?” “Well, anyway, there’s the evidence.” “I am not talking of the evidence now, I am talking about that question, of their own idea of themselves.
uz: Bunga qanday javob berasiz? Xo'sh, har holda, dalillar bor.Men hozir dalillar haqida emas, balki o'sha savol haqida, o'zlarining o'zlari haqida tasavvur qilishlari haqida gapiryapman.

en: Well, so they squeezed and squeezed him and he confessed: ‘I did not find it in the street, but in the flat where I was painting with Dmitri.’ ‘And how was that?’ ‘Why, Dmitri and I were painting there all day, and we were just getting ready to go, and Dmitri took a brush and painted my face, and he ran off and I after him.
uz: Xo'sh, ular uni siqib, siqib olishdi va u tan oldi: Men uni ko'chada emas, balki Dmitri bilan rasm chizgan xonadonda topdim.  Va bu qanday edi?  Nima uchun, Dmitri va men butun kun davomida u yerda rasm chizardik va biz ketishga tayyorgarlik ko'rardik, va Dmitri burchak olib, yuzimni bo'yashdi, u qochib ketdi va men uning orqasidan ergashdim.

en: I ran after him, shouting my hardest, and at the bottom of the stairs I ran right against the porter and some gentlemen —and how many gentlemen were there I don’t remember.
uz: Uning orqasidan yugurib, og'ir ovozim bilan qichqirdim va mertabaning pastida eshikchi va ba'zi rafiqani ushlab yugurdim va u yerda qancha rafiqani ko'rganimni eslay olmayman.

en: And the porter swore at me, and the other porter swore, too, and the porter’s wife came out, and swore at us, too; and a gentleman came into the entry with a lady, and he swore at us, too, for Dmitri and I lay right across the way.
uz: U menga va boshqa porterga qasam ichdi va porterning xotini tashqariga chiqib, bizga ham qasam ichdi va bir janob bir ayol bilan kirib, bizga ham qasam ichdi, chunki Dmitri va men o'sha yo'l o'rtasida yotgan edik.

en: I got hold of Dmitri’s hair and knocked him down and began beating him.
uz: Dmitriyning sochlarini ushlab, uni yerga urdim va urishni boshladim.

en: And Dmitri, too, caught me by the hair and began beating me.
uz: Dmitri ham sochlarimdan ushlab, urishni boshladi.

en: But we did it all not for temper but in a friendly way, for sport.
uz: Ammo biz bularning barchasini g'azablanganlik uchun emas, balki do'stona, sport uchun qildik.

en: And then Dmitri escaped and ran into the street, and I ran after him; but I did not catch him, and went back to
uz: Keyin Dmitri qochib ketib, ko'chaga yugurdi va men uning orqasidan yugurdim, lekin uni ushlab qolmadim, so'ngra yana ko'chaga qaytdim.

en: the flat alone; I had to clear up my things.
uz: Yolg'iz xonadon; men o'z narsalarimni tozalashim kerak edi.

en: I began putting them together, expecting Dmitri to come, and there in the passage, in the corner by the door, I stepped on the box.
uz: Dmitriy kelishini kutib, ularni yig'ishni boshladim va o'sha joyda, eshikning burchagida, qutisiga qadam bosdim.

en: I saw it lying there wrapped up in paper.
uz: Men uni qog'ozga o'rab, u yerda yotganini ko'rdim.

en: I took off the paper, saw some little hooks, undid them, and in the box were the earrings.
uz: Men qog'ozni olib tashladim, ba'zi kichkina qo'rg'oqlarni ko'rdim, ularni o'chirdim va quti ichida quloq o'nglamlari bor edi.

en: …’ ” “Behind the door?
uz: ...   Eshik ortida?

en: Lying behind the door?
uz: Eshik ortida yotganmisiz?

en: Behind the door?” Raskolnikov cried suddenly, staring with a blank look of terror at Razumihin, and he slowly sat up on the sofa, leaning on his hand.
uz: Eshik orqasida? Raskolnikov to'satdan yig'ladi va razumihinga qo'rqinchli ko'z bilan qaradi va o'z qo'li bilan o'tirgan sofaga sekin o'tirdi.

en: What’s wrong?” Razumihin, too, got up from his seat.
uz: Nima bo'ldi? Razumihin ham o'tirgan joyidan turdi.

en: “Nothing,” Raskolnikov answered faintly, turning to the wall.
uz: Raskolnikov hech narsa aytmadi va devorga qarab javob berdi.

en: All were silent for a while.
uz: Hammasi bir muncha vaqt sukut saqlashdi.

en: “He must have waked from a dream,” Razumihin said at last, looking inquiringly at Zossimov.
uz: U tushdan uyg'ongan bo'lishi kerak,  dedi Razumihin nihoyat, Zossimovga savol-javob bilan qarab.

en: The latter slightly shook his head.
uz: Keyinchalik u boshini biroz shovqirdi.

en: “Well, go on,” said Zossimov.
uz: Albatta, davom eting, dedi Zossimov.

en: “What next?” “What next?
uz: Next nima bo'ladi?Next nima bo'ladi?

en: As soon as he saw the earrings, forgetting Dmitri and everything, he took up his cap and ran to Dushkin and, as we know, got a rouble from him.
uz: Qulaqlarni ko'rib, Dmitriy va boshqa narsalarni unutib qo'yganida, u qo'lboshini ko'tarib, Dushkinning oldiga yugurdi va biz bilganidek, undan bir rubl oldi.

en: He told a lie saying he found them in the street, and went off drinking.
uz: U ularni ko'chada topganini aytib yolg'on gapirdi va ichib ketdi.

en: He keeps repeating his old story about the murder: ‘I know nothing of it, never heard of it till the day before yesterday.’ ‘And why didn’t you come to the police till now?’ ‘I was frightened.’ ‘And why did you try to hang yourself?’ ‘From anxiety.’ ‘What anxiety?’ ‘That I should be accused of it.’ Well, that’s the whole story.
uz: U o'zining o'sha o'ldirilganlik haqidagi eski hikoyasini takrorlab turadi: "Men bu haqda hech narsa bilmayman, o'tgan kungacha eshitmaganman. Va nima uchun siz hozirgacha politsiyaga kelmadingiz?  Men qo'rqdim.  Va nega o'zingizni asrashga urinib ko'rdingiz?  Tashvishdan.  Qaysi tashvishdan?  Menga aybdor bo'lishim kerak. Xo'sh, bu butun hikoyadir.

en: And now what do you suppose they deduced from that?” “Why, there’s no supposing.
uz: Va endi ular bundan nima xulosaga kelishgan deb o'ylaysiz? Nima uchun, hech qanday taxmin yo'q.

en: There’s a clue, such as it is, a fact.
uz: Bir dalil bor, masalan, fakt.

en: You wouldn’t have your painter set free?” “Now they’ve simply taken him for the murderer.
uz: Siz o'zingizning rassomingizni ozod qilishingizni istamasmidingiz? Endi ular uni qotil deb o'ylashdi.

en: They haven’t a shadow of doubt.” “That’s nonsense.
uz: Ularning hech qanday shubhalari yo'q.Bu g'alati gap.

en: But what about the earrings?
uz: Ammo quloqlar haqida nima deyish mumkin?

en: You must admit that, if on the very same day and hour earrings from the old woman’s box have come into Nikolay’s hands, they must have come there somehow.
uz: Siz shuni tan olishingiz kerakki, agar Nikolayning qo'liga qariya ayolning qutidagi quloqchalar o'sha kun va soatda tushgan bo'lsa, ular u yerga qandaydir tarzda kelgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: That’s a good deal in such a case.” “How did they get there?
uz: Bunday holatda bu juda yaxshi shartnoma. Qanday qilib ular u yerga kelishdi?

en: How did they get there?” cried Razumihin.
uz: Ular u yerga qanday etib kelishdi? - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: “How can you, a doctor, whose duty it is to study man and who has more opportunity than anyone else for studying human nature —how can you fail to see the character of the man in the whole story?
uz: Qanday qilib siz, insonni o'rganish vazifasi bo'lgan va inson tabiatini o'rganish uchun har kimdan ko'ra ko'proq imkoniyatga ega bo'lgan shifokor, butun hikoyada insonning xarakterini ko'rmay qolishingiz mumkin?

en: Don’t you see at once that the answers he has given in
uz: Uning bergan javoblari birdan ko'rinmaydimi?

en: the examination are the holy truth?
uz: Muqaddas haqiqatni tekshirib ko'rish kerakmi?

en: They came into his hand precisely as he has told us —he stepped on the box and picked it up.” “The holy truth!
uz: Ular uning qo'liga to'g'ri tushdi, xuddi u bizga aytganidek.U qutisiga qadam bosdi va uni olib ketdi. Muqaddas haqiqat!

en: But didn’t he own himself that he told a lie at first?” “Listen to me, listen attentively.
uz: Ammo u avval yolg'on gapirganini o'zi tushunmaganmi? Menga quloq soling, diqqat bilan tinglang.

en: The porter and Koch and Pestryakov and the other porter and the wife of the first porter and the woman who was sitting in the porter’s lodge and the man Kryukov, who had just got out of a cab at that minute and went in at the entry with a lady on his arm, that is eight or ten witnesses, agree that Nikolay had Dmitri on the ground, was lying on him beating him, while Dmitri hung on to his hair, beating him, too.
uz: Porter, Koch, Pestryakov va boshqa porter, birinchi porterning xotini va porterning uyida o'tirgan ayol va o'sha daqiqada taksiga tushgan va qo'lida bir xonim bo'lgan, ya'ni sakkiz yoki o'n shohid bo'lgan Kryukov erkaklar Nikolayning Dmitriyni yerga tashlab, uning ustiga yotganini, Dmitri esa sochlariga bog'lanib, uni ham urganini tan olishadi.

en: They lay right across the way, blocking the thoroughfare.
uz: Ular yo'lning to'g'risida yotgan, yo'lni to'sib qo'yishgan.

en: They were sworn at on all sides while they ‘like children’ (the very words of the witnesses) were falling over one another, squealing, fighting and laughing with the funniest faces, and, chasing one another like children, they ran into the street.
uz: Ular har tarafdan qasam ichib, bir-birlarini bolalar kabi quvg'in qilib, ko'chaga yugurib ketishdi.

en: Now take careful note.
uz: Endi ehtiyotkorlik bilan kuzatib boring.

en: The bodies upstairs were warm, you understand, warm when they found them!
uz: Yuqoridagi jasadlar issiq edi, siz tushunasiz, ular ularni topganida issiq edi!

en: If they, or Nikolay alone, had murdered them and broken open the boxes, or simply taken part in the robbery, allow me to ask you one question: do their state of mind, their squeals and giggles and childish scuffling at the gate fit in with axes, bloodshed, fiendish cunning, robbery?
uz: Agar ular yoki faqat Nikolay ularni o'ldirib, qutilarni ochib yuborgan bo'lsa yoki shunchaki talon-torojda ishtirok etgan bo'lsa, menga bir savol berishim kerak: ularning ruh holati, qichqiriq va kulgi va darvoza oldida bolalarcha to'qnashuvlar o'g'irlar, qon to'kish, yovuz hiyla-nayranglar, talon-toroj bilan mos keladimi?

en: They’d just killed them, not five or ten minutes before, for the bodies were still warm, and at once, leaving the flat open, knowing that people would go there at once, flinging away their booty, they rolled about like children, laughing and attracting general attention.
uz: Ular shunchaki ularni o'ldirgan edilar, besh yoki o'n daqiqa oldin emas, chunki jasadlar hali ham iliq edi va birdan, odamlar birdan u yerga borishini bilib, ochiq xonani qoldirib, o'z olomonlarini tashlab ketishdi, ular bolalar kabi o'z-o'zlarini aylanib yurishdi, kulishdi va umumiy e'tiborni jalb qilishdi.

en: And there are a dozen witnesses to swear to that!” “Of course it is strange!
uz: Bu haqda o'nlab guvohlar qasam ichadi! Albatta, bu g'alati!

en: It’s impossible, indeed, but …” “No, brother, no buts.
uz: To'g'ri, bu imkonsiz, lekin ...Yo'q, birodarim, lekin yo'q.

en: And if the earrings being found in Nikolay’s hands at the very day and hour of the murder constitutes an important piece of circumstantial evidence against him —although the explanation given by him accounts for it, and therefore it does not tell seriously against him —one must take into consideration the facts which prove him innocent, especially as they are facts that cannot be denied.
uz: Va agar Nikolayning qo'lida o'ldirilgan kuni va soatda topilgan bo'lsa, bu unga qarshi muhim dalil bo'lsa, ayniqsa, uning tushuntirishlari bu haqda gapirib bermasa va shuning uchun unga qarshi jiddiy gapirmasa, uni aybsiz deb isbotlaydigan faktlarni hisobga olish kerak, ayniqsa, bu faktlarni inkor etish mumkin emas.

en: And do you suppose, from the character of our legal system, that they will accept, or that they are in a position to accept, this fact —resting simply on a psychological impossibility —as irrefutable and conclusively breaking down the circumstantial evidence for the prosecution?
uz: Sizningcha, bizning huquqiy tizimimizning xususiyatidan kelib chiqqan holda, ular shunchaki psixologik imkonsizlikka asoslangan va ayblov uchun asosli dalillarni buzish bilan bu faktni qabul qilishadi yoki qabul qilishlari mumkinmi?

en: No, they won’t accept it, they certainly won’t, because
uz: Yo'q, ular buni qabul qilmaydilar, albatta qabul qilmaydilar, chunki ular buni qabul qilmaydilar.

en: they found the jewel-case and the man tried to hang himself, ‘which he could not have done if he hadn’t felt guilty.’ That’s the point, that’s what excites me, you must understand!” “Oh, I see you are excited!
uz: Ular marvaridni topdilar va u o'zini asrashga urindi, lekin u o'zini aybdor his qilmaganida buni qila olmasdi. Bu mening g'amginim, siz buni tushunishingiz kerak!Oh, ko'rib turibmanki, siz g'amginsiz!

en: I forgot to ask you; what proof is there that the box came from the old woman?” “That’s been proved,” said Razumihin with apparent reluctance, frowning.
uz: Sizdan so'rashni unutib qo'ydim; qutuq keksa ayoldan kelganligiga qanday dalillar bor?Bu isbotlangan, - dedi Razumihin ko'rinmaslik bilan, ko'z o'ngida.

en: “Koch recognised the jewel-case and gave the name of the owner, who proved conclusively that it was his.” “That’s bad.
uz: Koch marvaridni tan olib, uning egasining ismini aytdi, u esa uni o'zi deb aniq tasdiqladi.

en: Did anyone see Nikolay at the time that Koch and Pestryakov were going upstairs at first, and is there no evidence about that?” “Nobody did see him,” Razumihin answered with vexation.
uz: Koch va Pestryakov birinchi marta yuqoriga chiqqanida Nikolayni ko'rgan bo'lganmi va buning hech qanday isboti yo'qmi?  Hech kim uni ko'rmagan, Razumihin xafa bo'lib javob berdi.

en: “That’s the worst of it.
uz: Bu eng yomon narsa.

en: Even Koch and Pestryakov did not notice them on their way upstairs, though, indeed, their evidence could not have been worth much.
uz: Hatto Koch va Pestryakov ham ular ustiga borayotganda ularni ko'rmadilar, ammo, albatta, ularning dalillari juda qimmatga tushmagan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: They said they saw the flat was open, and that there must be work going on in it, but they took no special notice and could not remember whether there actually were men at work in it.” “Hm!
uz: Ular o'sha xonadonning ochilganligini va u yerda ish olib borilayotganini ko'rishganini aytishdi, lekin ular hech qanday e'tibor bermadilar va u yerda erkaklar ishlayotganini eslay olishmadilar.  Hm!

en: … So the only evidence for the defence is that they were beating one another and laughing.
uz: Shunday qilib, himoya uchun yagona dalil ular bir-birlarini urib, kulishayotganini ko'rsatadi.

en: That constitutes a strong presumption, but … How do you explain the facts yourself?” “How do I explain them?
uz: Bu kuchli taxminni anglatadi, ammo... Siz o'zingiz qanday qilib faktlarni tushuntirasiz?Men ularni qanday tushuntirishim kerak?

en: What is there to explain?
uz: Nima tushuntirish kerak?

en: At any rate, the direction in which explanation is to be sought is clear, and the jewel-case points to it.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, tushuntirishni izlash yo'li aniq va marvarid bu yo'lga ishora qiladi.

en: The real murderer dropped those earrings.
uz: Haqiqiy qotil o'sha quloqlarni quvib yubordi.

en: The murderer was upstairs, locked in, when Koch and Pestryakov knocked at the door.
uz: Qotil yuqori qavatda bo'lganida, Koch va Pestryakov eshikni taqillatishdi.

en: Koch, like an ass, did not stay at the door; so the murderer popped out and ran down, too; for he had no other way of escape.
uz: Koch esa eshik oldida o'tirmadi, shuning uchun qotil ham chiqib, pastga yugurdi, chunki qochib ketishning boshqa yo'li yo'q edi.

en: He hid from Koch, Pestryakov and the porter in the flat when Nikolay and Dmitri had just run out of it.
uz: Nikolay va Dmitriy o'sha xonadan tugagach, u ko'ch, Pestryakov va xonadan yashiringan edi.

en: He stopped there while the porter and others were going upstairs, waited till they were out of hearing, and then went calmly downstairs at the very minute when Dmitri and Nikolay ran out into the street and there was no one in the entry; possibly he was seen, but not noticed.
uz: U darvozabon va boshqa kishilar yuqoriga chiqib ketayotganida to'xtadi, eshitishning oldini olishni kutdi va keyin Dmitri va Nikolay ko'chaga chiqib ketish paytida tinchlik bilan pastga tushdi va u yerda hech kim yo'q edi; ehtimol uni ko'rishgan, lekin hech kim ko'rmagan.

en: There are lots of people going in and out.
uz: Ko'p odamlar kirib-chiqayotgan.

en: He must have dropped the earrings out of his pocket when he stood behind the door, and did not notice he dropped them, because he had other things to think of.
uz: U eshik ortida turganida, quloq o'nglamlarini o'z joniga tashlab qo'ygan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin uni tashlab ketayotganini sezmagan, chunki boshqa narsalar haqida o'ylashi kerak edi.

en: The jewel- case is a conclusive proof that he did stand there.
uz: Bu zargarlik xodimi u yerda turganining aniq isbotidir.

en: … That’s how I explain it.”
uz: Men buni shunday tushuntiraman.

en: No, my boy, you’re too clever.
uz: Yo'q, o'g'lim, sen juda aqllisan.

en: That beats everything.” “But, why, why?” “Why, because everything fits too well … it’s too melodramatic.” “A-ach!” Razumihin was exclaiming, but at that moment the door opened and a personage came in who was a stranger to all present.
uz: Bu hamma narsani mag'lub qiladi.  Ammo, nima uchun, nima uchun?  Nima uchun, chunki hamma narsa juda yaxshi o'xshaydi ... bu juda melodramatik.  A-ach! Razumihin baland ovoz bilan baqirib yurgan edi, lekin o'sha paytda eshik ochildi va barcha ishtirokchilarga noma'lum bo'lgan bir shaxs kirdi.

en: V This was a gentleman no longer young, of a stiff and portly appearance, and a cautious and sour countenance.
uz: Bu yigit endi yosh emas, qattiq va qo'pol ko'rinishga ega bo'lgan, ehtiyotkor va qayg'urgan yuziga ega bo'lgan.

en: He began by stopping short in the doorway, staring about him with offensive and undisguised astonishment, as though asking himself what sort of place he had come to.
uz: Boshida u eshikda to'xtadi va atrofida qo'pol va g'ayritabiiy hayronlik bilan qaradi, xuddi o'ziga qanday joyga kelganini o'ylab ko'radi.

en: Mistrustfully and with an affectation of being alarmed and almost affronted, he scanned Raskolnikov’s low and narrow “cabin.” With the same amazement he stared at Raskolnikov, who lay undressed, dishevelled, unwashed, on his miserable dirty sofa, looking fixedly at him.
uz: U Raskolnikovning past va tor kabinasini o'ziga ishonmasdan va qo'rqinchli va deyarli haqoratli bo'lish hissi bilan skanerladi. O'sha hayronlik bilan u Raskolnikovga qaradi, u kiyim-kechaksiz, chiroyli, yuvmagan holda uning qashshoq kirli sofasida yotgan edi va unga qattiq qaragan edi.

en: Then with the same deliberation he scrutinised the uncouth, unkempt figure and unshaven face of Razumihin, who looked him boldly and inquiringly in the face without rising from his seat.
uz: Keyin u xuddi shu mulohaza bilan Razumihinning o'rinsiz, o'rinsiz va o'tkir yuzini o'rganib chiqdi, u o'tirgan joyidan turmasdan, jasoratli va savol-javob bilan uning yuziga qaradi.

en: A constrained silence lasted for a couple of minutes, and then, as might be expected, some scene-shifting took place.
uz: Bir necha daqiqa davomida kamdan-kam sessizlik davom etdi va keyin, kutilganidek, ko'rinish o'zgarishi yuz berdi.

en: Reflecting, probably from certain fairly unmistakable signs, that he would get nothing in this “cabin” by attempting to overawe them, the gentleman softened somewhat, and civilly, though with some severity, emphasising every syllable of his question, addressed Zossimov: “Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov, a student, or formerly a student?” Zossimov made a slight movement, and would have answered, had not Razumihin anticipated him.
uz: Ehtimol, shubhasiz, aniq belgilardan ko'rinib turibdiki, bu kabinda ularni o'tkazishga harakat qilib, hech narsa topolmaydi, deb o'ylagani sababli, xonim biroz yumshatildi va, xolisona, ammo ba'zi darajada qat'iylik bilan, savolining har bir harfini ta'kidlab, Zossimovga murojaat qildi: Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov, o'quvchi yoki sobiq o'quvchi? Zossimov biroz harakat qildi va javob bergan bo'lar edi, agar Razumihin uni kutib olmagan bo'lsa.

en: “Here he is lying on the sofa!
uz: Mana, u kanepada yotgan!

en: What do you want?” This familiar “what do you want” seemed to cut the ground from the feet of the pompous gentleman.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? Bu tanish what do you want o'z poydevoriy yigitning oyoqlaridan yerni kesib tashlagan bo'ldi.

en: He was turning to Razumihin, but checked himself in time and turned to Zossimov again.
uz: U Razumihinga murojaat qilardi, lekin o'zini vaqt bilan tekshirib ko'rdi va yana Zossimovga murojaat qildi.

en: “This is Raskolnikov,” mumbled Zossimov, nodding towards him.
uz: Bu Raskolnikov, Zossimov g'oyib bo'lib, unga bosh ko'tardi.

en: Then he gave a prolonged yawn, opening his mouth as wide as possible.
uz: So'ngra u uzoq vaqt yig'ib, og'zini iloji boricha kengroq ochdi.

en: Then he lazily put his hand into his waistcoat-pocket, pulled out a huge gold watch in a round hunter’s case, opened it, looked at it and as slowly and lazily proceeded to put it back.
uz: So'ngra u o'z qo'lini kemasi qoshiqlariga qo'yib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ovchi qopqoqidagi ulkan oltin soatni olib chiqdi, uni ochdi, uni ko'rib qoldi va sekin-sakin uni qaytarib qo'ydi.

en: Raskolnikov himself lay without speaking, on his back, gazing persistently, though without understanding, at the stranger.
uz: Raskolnikovning o'zi gapirmasdan, orqasida yotgan edi va begona odamga o'ylamasdan, lekin tushunmasdan qaragan edi.

en: Now that his face was turned away from the strange flower on the paper, it was extremely pale and wore a look of anguish, as though he had just undergone an agonising operation or just been taken from the rack.
uz: Endi uning yuzi qog'ozdagi g'ayrioddiy guldan yuz o'girganida, u nihoyatda oqib, qayg'uli ko'rinishni ko'rsatdi, xuddi u azobli operatsiyadan o'tkazilgan bo'lsa yoki shunchaki rakadan olib tashlangan bo'lsa kerak.

en: But the newcomer gradually began to arouse his attention, then his wonder, then suspicion and even alarm.
uz: Ammo yangi kelgan odam asta-sekin uning e'tiborini, so'ngra hayronligini, so'ngra shubha va hatto xavotirni jalb qila boshladi.

en: When Zossimov said “This is Raskolnikov” he jumped up quickly, sat on the sofa and with an almost defiant, but weak and breaking, voice articulated: “Yes, I am Raskolnikov!
uz: Zossimov: "Bu Raskolnikov", - deganida, u tez turib, sofaga o'tirdi va deyarli qarshilik ko'rsatgan, ammo zaif va bo'g'ib ketgan ovoz bilan: "Ha, men Raskolnikovman!" - deb so'zladi.

en: What do you want?” The visitor scrutinised him and pronounced impressively: “Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? Tashrifchi uni sinchiklab ko'rib chiqib, ta'sirchan tarzda: Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin deb aytdi.

en: I believe I have reason to hope that my name is not wholly unknown to you?” But Raskolnikov, who had expected something quite different, gazed blankly and dreamily at him, making no reply, as though he heard the name of Pyotr Petrovitch for the first time.
uz: Mening ismim sizga noma'lum emasligiga umid qilishim uchun asosim bor, deb o'ylayman? Ammo Raskolnikov, u umuman boshqacha narsani kutgan edi, lekin unga hech qanday javob bermay, ko'ngli va tushlari bilan qaradi, xuddi Pyotr Petrovitch ismini birinchi marta eshitgan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “Is it possible that you can up to the present have received no information?” asked Pyotr Petrovitch, somewhat disconcerted.
uz: Siz hozirgacha hech qanday ma'lumot olmagan bo'lishingiz mumkinmi? deb so'radi Pyotr Petrovitch, biroz xafa bo'lib.

en: In reply Raskolnikov sank languidly back on the pillow, put his hands behind his head and gazed at the ceiling.
uz: Raskolnikov javob qilib, yostiqqa qo'shilib, qo'llarini boshiga qo'ydi va ustunga qarab qo'ydi.

en: A look of dismay came into Luzhin’s face.
uz: Luzhinning yuzida dahshatli ko'rinish paydo bo'ldi.

en: Zossimov and Razumihin stared at him more inquisitively than ever, and at last he showed unmistakable signs of embarrassment.
uz: Zossimov va Razumihin unga har qachongidan ham qiziqarli qarashdi va nihoyat u o'zini noqulay his qilganini ko'rsatdi.

en: “I had presumed and calculated,” he faltered, “that a letter posted more than ten days, if not a fortnight ago …” “I say, why are you standing in the doorway?” Razumihin interrupted suddenly.
uz: Men bir xat o'n kundan ko'proq, agar ikki hafta oldin bo'lmasa, jo'natilganini taxmin qilib, hisob-kitob qildim.  U shubha ostiga tushdi.  Men: "Nima uchun siz eshik oldida turibsiz?" - deb aytdim.  Razumihin to'satdan to'xtadi.

en: “If you’ve something to say, sit down.
uz: Agar sizda aytadigan biror narsa bor bo'lsa, o'tiring.

en: Nastasya and you are so crowded.
uz: Nastasya va siz juda ko'p odamlarga ega bo'lasiz.

en: Nastasya, make room.
uz: Nastasya, joy toping.

en: Here’s a chair, thread your way in!” He moved his chair back from the table, made a little space between the table and his knees, and waited in a rather cramped position for the visitor to “thread his way in.” The minute was so
uz: Mana bir o'rindiq, o'z yo'lingni uzing! U o'rindiqini stoldan orqaga ko'tardi, o'rindiqni stol va dizlariga o'tkazdi va mehmonni o'z yo'lini uzish uchun juda siqilgan joyda kutdi. Minut shunchalik o'zgardi

en: chosen that it was impossible to refuse, and the visitor squeezed his way through, hurrying and stumbling.
uz: To'g'ri, rad etishning iloji yo'qligini tanladi va tashrif buyuruvchi darrov harakat qilib, o'z yo'lini bosib o'tdi.

en: Reaching the chair, he sat down, looking suspiciously at Razumihin.
uz: Ustozga yetib, o'tirdi va Razumihinga shubhali ko'z bilan qaradi.

en: “No need to be nervous,” the latter blurted out.
uz: Xavflanishga hojat yo'q, oxirgi gaplar so'zlandi.

en: “Rodya has been ill for the last five days and delirious for three, but now he is recovering and has got an appetite.
uz: Rodya so'nggi besh kundan beri bemor va uch kundan beri deliriumda edi, ammo hozir u sog'ayib ketmoqda va ochko'zlik qo'lga kiritdi.

en: This is his doctor, who has just had a look at him.
uz: Bu uning shifokori, u hozirgina uni ko'rib chiqdi.
