en: I am a comrade of Rodya’s, like him, formerly a student, and now I am nursing him; so don’t you take any notice of us, but go on with your business.” “Thank you.
uz: Men Rodyalarning hamkasbi, uning o'zi kabi, ilgari talaba, endi esa uni parvarish qilaman; shuning uchun bizdan hech qanday g'amxo'rlik qilmang, o'z ishingizni davom ettiring.Rahmat.

en: But shall I not disturb the invalid by my presence and conversation?” Pyotr Petrovitch asked of Zossimov.
uz: Ammo men o'zimning hozirligim va suhbatim bilan nogironlarni bezovta qilmaymanmi? - deb so'radi Pyotr Petroviç Zossimovdan.

en: “N-no,” mumbled Zossimov; “you may amuse him.” He yawned again.
uz: N-yo'q,  Zossimov g'iybat qildi; siz uni o'yin qilishingiz mumkin. U yana g'iybat qildi.

en: “He has been conscious a long time, since the morning,” went on Razumihin, whose familiarity seemed so much like unaffected good- nature that Pyotr Petrovitch began to be more cheerful, partly, perhaps, because this shabby and impudent person had introduced himself as a student.
uz: U ertalabdan beri ko'p vaqtdan beri ongda edi, deb davom etdi Razumihin, uning tanishligi ta'sirlanmagan yaxshi tabiatga o'xshaydi, shuning uchun Pyotr Petrovitch ko'proq xursand bo'la boshladi, ehtimol qisman, chunki bu xor va g'ayratsiz odam o'zini talaba sifatida taqdim etgan.

en: “Your mamma,” began Luzhin.
uz: Omang, Luzhinni boshladi.

en: “Hm!” Razumihin cleared his throat loudly.
uz: Hm! Razumihin og'zini baland ovoz bilan tozaladi.

en: Luzhin looked at him inquiringly.
uz: Luzhin unga savol-javob bilan qaradi.

en: “That’s all right, go on.” Luzhin shrugged his shoulders.
uz: Thats all right, go on. Luzhin omonlarini yumdi.

en: “Your mamma had commenced a letter to you while I was sojourning in her neighbourhood.
uz: Yo'ng onangiz men uning mahallada bo'lganimda sizga xat yozishni boshlagan edi.

en: On my arrival here I purposely allowed a few days to elapse before coming to see you, in order that I might be fully assured that you were in full possession of the tidings; but now, to my astonishment …” “I know, I know!” Raskolnikov cried suddenly with impatient vexation.
uz: Bu yerga kelganimda, sizlarni ko'rish uchun kelishdan oldin bir necha kun o'tishiga qasddan ruxsat berdim, shunda sizlarning xabaringiz to'liq ekanligiga to'liq amin bo'ldim; lekin endi, hayron bo'lishim uchun ...Men bilaman, bilaman! Raskolnikov kutilmagan xafalik bilan to'satdan yig'ladi.

en: “So you are the fiancé?
uz: Demak, siz g'ayratli yigitmisiz?

en: I know, and that’s enough!” There was no doubt about Pyotr Petrovitch’s being offended this time, but he said nothing.
uz: Bilaman va bu yetarli! Pyotr Petrovitchning bu safar jabrlanishiga hech qanday shubha yo'q edi, lekin u hech narsa aytmadi.

en: He made a violent effort to understand what it all meant.
uz: Bularning barchasining ma'nosini tushunish uchun u zo'ravon harakat qildi.

en: There was a moment’s silence.
uz: O'shanda bir daqiqalik xotirjamlik bo'ldi.

en: Meanwhile Raskolnikov, who had turned a little towards him when he answered, began suddenly staring at him again with marked curiosity, as though he had not had a good look at him yet, or as though something new had struck him; he rose from his pillow on
uz: Raskolnikov javob berganda unga biroz o'girilib qaragan bo'lsa-da, birdan Raskolnikov unga yana ko'z tikib, o'ziga qiziqish bilan qaray boshladi, xuddi unga hali yaxshi ko'rmagan bo'lsa, yoki unga yangi narsa tushib qolgan bo'lsa; u yostiqidan turibdi

en: purpose to stare at him.
uz: Uni ko'rib turish uchun maqsad.

en: There certainly was something peculiar in Pyotr Petrovitch’s whole appearance, something which seemed to justify the title of “fiancé” so unceremoniously applied to him.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitchning butun tashqi ko'rinishida, albatta, o'ziga xos bir narsa bor edi, bu esa unga tanqidsiz ravishda qo'llaniladigan "qiz" unvonini oqlaydi.

en: In the first place, it was evident, far too much so indeed, that Pyotr Petrovitch had made eager use of his few days in the capital to get himself up and rig himself out in expectation of his betrothed —a perfectly innocent and permissible proceeding, indeed.
uz: Birinchidan, Pyotr Petrovitch poytaxtimizdagi bir necha kunidan o'zini o'zini o'zi tiklab, o'zini o'zi tayyorlab qo'yganini, nikohkorining to'liq aybsiz va qonuniy bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan ishini kutganini juda ko'p ko'rish mumkin edi.

en: Even his own, perhaps too complacent, consciousness of the agreeable improvement in his appearance might have been forgiven in such circumstances, seeing that Pyotr Petrovitch had taken up the role of fiancé.
uz: Hatto uning tashqi ko'rinishida yaxshi o'zgarish bo'lganidan o'zi ham, ehtimol o'zidan ko'p mamnun bo'lgan edi, chunki Pyotr Petrovitch turmush o'rtog'ining rolini o'ynagan edi.

en: All his clothes were fresh from the tailor’s and were all right, except for being too new and too distinctly appropriate.
uz: Uning barcha kiyimlari tikuvchilarning yangi kiyimlari edi va ular juda yangi va juda mos bo'lganidan tashqari yaxshi edi.

en: Even the stylish new round hat had the same significance.
uz: Hatto zamonaviy yangi to'g'ri to'pka ham xuddi shunday ahamiyatga ega edi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch treated it too respectfully and held it too carefully in his hands.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch unga juda hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'ldi va uni qo'llarida juda ehtiyotkorlik bilan ushlab turdi.

en: The exquisite pair of lavender gloves, real Louvain, told the same tale, if only from the fact of his not wearing them, but carrying them in his hand for show.
uz: Go'zal lavand qo'lqoplari juftligi, haqiqiy Louvain, xuddi shunday hikoyani aytib berdi, agar faqat ularni kiymaganidan, balki ularni ko'rsatish uchun qo'lida ko'targanidan.

en: Light and youthful colours predominated in Pyotr Petrovitch’s attire.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch kiyimida yorug' va yosh ranglar ustunlik qilgan.

en: He wore a charming summer jacket of a fawn shade, light thin trousers, a waistcoat of the same, new and fine linen, a cravat of the lightest cambric with pink stripes on it, and the best of it was, this all suited Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: U charmli yozgi shashqashta, yorug' kam kiyim, xuddi shunday, yangi va chiroyli kiyimdan tayyorlangan kiyim, eng yengil kambrik kravatni rosa rangli chiziqlar bilan kiydirdi va eng yaxshisi Pyotr Petrovitchga mos kelardi.

en: His very fresh and even handsome face looked younger than his forty-five years at all times.
uz: Uning juda yangi va hatto chiroyli yuzi har doim qirq besh yoshidan yoshroq ko'rinardi.

en: His dark, mutton-chop whiskers made an agreeable setting on both sides, growing thickly upon his shining, clean-shaven chin.
uz: Uning qorong'i, qo'zi cho'p bo'lgan pichoqlari ikkala tomonida ham yoqimli muhit yaratdi va shinam, toza shaven bo'lgan bo'yni ustida zich o'sdi.

en: Even his hair, touched here and there with grey, though it had been combed and curled at a hairdresser’s, did not give him a stupid appearance, as curled hair usually does, by inevitably suggesting a German on his wedding-day.
uz: Hatto uning sochlari ham, bu yerda-bu yerda griq rang bilan to'qilgan bo'lsa-da, lekin soch pishiruvchida pishirilgan va qamalgan bo'lsa-da, to'y kunida nemisni tavsiya etish orqali unga odatda qamalgan sochlar kabi ahmoqona ko'rinish bermadi.

en: If there really was something unpleasing and repulsive in his rather good-looking and imposing countenance, it was due to quite other causes.
uz: Agar uning chiroyli va qo'rqinchli ko'rinishida chindan ham yoqimsiz va jirkanch narsa bo'lsa, bu boshqa sabablarga bog'liq edi.

en: Luzhin unceremoniously, Raskolnikov smiled malignantly, sank back on the pillow and stared at the ceiling as before.
uz: Raskolnikov o'rinsiz tabassum qilib, yostiqqa qaytdi va avvalgidek ustunga qaradi.

en: Luzhin hardened his heart and seemed to determine to take no notice of their oddities.
uz: Luzhin yuragini qattiq qilib, ularning g'ayritabiiyliklariga e'tibor bermaslikka qat'iy qaror qilgan edi.

en: “I feel the greatest regret at finding you in this situation,” he began, again breaking the silence with an effort.
uz: "Men sizni shu vaziyatda topganimdan juda afsuslanaman", - deb boshladi u, yana bir bor harakat bilan xotirjamlikni buzdi.

en: “If I had been aware of your illness I should have come earlier.
uz: Agar men sizning kasalligingiz haqida bilganimda, oldin kelishim kerak edi.

en: But you know what business is.
uz: Ammo siz biznes nima ekanligini bilasiz.

en: have, too, a very important legal affair in the Senate, not to mention other preoccupations which you may well conjecture.
uz: Senatda ham juda muhim huquqiy masala bor, boshqa tashvishlardan tashqari, siz taxmin qilishingiz mumkin bo'lgan boshqa muammolar ham bor.

en: I am expecting your mamma and sister any minute.” Raskolnikov made a movement and seemed about to speak; his face showed some excitement.
uz: Onang va singlingizni har bir daqiqada kutaman. Raskolnikov harakat qilib, gapirishni boshladi; yuzida biroz hayajon bor edi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch paused, waited, but as nothing followed, he went on: “… Any minute.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch to'xtadi, kutdi, lekin hech narsa ketmaganidan so'ng davom etdi: "... Har bir daqiqa.

en: I have found a lodging for them on their arrival.” “Where?” asked Raskolnikov weakly.
uz: Ular kelganda men ularga joy topdim.Qayerda? Raskolnikovni zaiflik bilan so'radi.

en: “Very near here, in Bakaleyev’s house.” “That’s in Voskresensky,” put in Razumihin.
uz: Bu yerga juda yaqin, Bakaleyevning uyida.Bu Voskresenskyda, Razumihinda joylashtirilgan.

en: “There are two storeys of rooms, let by a merchant called Yushin; I’ve been there.” “Yes, rooms …” “A disgusting place —filthy, stinking and, what’s more, of doubtful character.
uz: Yushin ismli savdogar tomonidan ikki qavatli xonalar mavjud; men u erda bo'lganman.  Ha, xonalar ...  A jirkanch joy  kirli, kirli va, eng muhimi, shubhali xarakterli.

en: Things have happened there, and there are all sorts of queer people living there.
uz: U yerda ko'p voqealar sodir bo'ldi va u yerda turli xil g'ayritabiiy odamlar yashaydi.

en: And I went there about a scandalous business.
uz: Men u yerga shov-shuv bilan shug'ullanishga bordim.

en: It’s cheap, though …” “I could not, of course, find out so much about it, for I am a stranger in Petersburg myself,” Pyotr Petrovitch replied huffily.
uz: Bu arzon, ammo ...Men, albatta, bu haqda ko'p narsani bilolmasdim, chunki men o'zim Petersburgda begona odamman, - dedi Pyotr Petrovitch haffily javob berdi.

en: “However, the two rooms are exceedingly clean, and as it is for so short a time … I have already taken a permanent, that is, our future flat,” he said, addressing Raskolnikov, “and I am having it done up.
uz: Shunga qaramay, ikkita xonadon juda toza, va bu juda qisqa vaqt uchun ... Men allaqachon doimiy, ya'ni bizning kelajakdagi kvartiramizni oldim, - dedi u Raskolnikovga murojaat qilib, - va men uni tuzataman.

en: And meanwhile I am myself cramped for room in a lodging with my friend Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov, in the flat of Madame Lippevechsel; it was he who told me of Bakaleyev’s house, too …” “Lebeziatnikov?” said Raskolnikov slowly, as if recalling something.
uz: Shu bilan birga, men ham do'stim Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov bilan birga bo'lgan uyda, Madam Lippevechselning xonadoniga joylashishga ehtiyoj bor edi; u menga Bakaleyevning uyidan ham gapirgan edi ...Lebeziatnikov? dedi Raskolnikov asta-sekin, xuddi biror narsani eslab qolgan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “Yes, Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov, a clerk in the Ministry.
uz: Ha, Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov, vazirlik ishchisi.

en: Do you know him?” “Yes … no,” Raskolnikov answered.
uz: Siz uni taniysizmi? Ha... yo'q, Raskolnikov javob berdi.

en: “Excuse me, I fancied so from your inquiry.
uz: Kechirasiz, men sizning so'rovingizdan o'zimni shunday his qildim.

en: I was once his guardian.
uz: Men bir vaqtlar uning vasiy bo'lganman.

en: … A very nice young man and advanced.
uz: U juda yaxshi yosh va ilg'or kishi edi.

en: I like to meet young people: one learns new things from them.” Luzhin looked round hopefully at them all.
uz: Men yoshlar bilan tanishishni yaxshi ko'raman: ulardan yangi narsalarni o'rganish mumkin. Luzhin ularning barchasini kutib o'tirdi.

en: “How do you mean?” asked Razumihin.
uz: Qanday qilib? - deb so'radi Razumihin.

en: “In the most serious and essential matters,” Pyotr Petrovitch replied, as though delighted at the question.
uz: Arabistonlik Pyotr Petroviç eng jiddiy va muhim masalalarga javob berib, savolga quvonch bilan javob berdi.

en: “You see, it’s ten years since I visited Petersburg.
uz: Qaranglar, men Sankt-Peterburg shahriga borganimdan o'n yil o'tdi.

en: All the novelties, reforms, ideas have
uz: Barcha yangiliklar, islohotlar, g'oyalar mavjud.

en: reached us in the provinces, but to see it all more clearly one must be in Petersburg.
uz: Bizga viloyatlarda yetib keldi, ammo hamma narsani aniqroq ko'rish uchun Peterburgda bo'lish kerak.

en: And it’s my notion that you observe and learn most by watching the younger generation.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, siz yosh avlodni kuzatish orqali ko'proq kuzatasiz va o'rganasiz.

en: And I confess I am delighted …” “At what?” “Your question is a wide one.
uz: Va men xursand ekanligimni tan oldim ...  Qanaqasiga?  Sizning savolingiz keng.

en: I may be mistaken, but I fancy I find clearer views, more, so to say, criticism, more practicality …” “That’s true,” Zossimov let drop.
uz: Xato qilsam bo'ladi, lekin men aniqroq nuqtai nazarni, ko'proq tanqid, amaliyotni topaman deb o'ylayman ...Bu haqiqat, Zossimov qo'yib yuboradi.

en: There’s no practicality.” Razumihin flew at him.
uz: Hech qanday amaliyot yo'q. Razumihin unga uchdi.

en: “Practicality is a difficult thing to find; it does not drop down from heaven.
uz: Praktiklik topish qiyin; u osmondan tushmaydi.

en: And for the last two hundred years we have been divorced from all practical life.
uz: So'nggi ikki yuz yil davomida biz har qanday amaliy hayotdan ajralib turdik.

en: Ideas, if you like, are fermenting,” he said to Pyotr Petrovitch, “and desire for good exists, though it’s in a childish form, and honesty you may find, although there are crowds of brigands.
uz: Agar xohlasangiz, g'oyalar fermentlashmoqda, - dedi u Pyotr Petrovitchga, - yaxshilik istagi mavjud, garchi bu bolalik shaklida bo'lsa-da, va halollik siz topishingiz mumkin, garchi talonchilarning to'plami bo'lsa-da.

en: Anyway, there’s no practicality.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, bu hech qanday amaliyotga ega emas.

en: Practicality goes well shod.” “I don’t agree with you,” Pyotr Petrovitch replied, with evident enjoyment.
uz: Amaliylik yaxshi ishlashi mumkin.Men siz bilan rozi emasman,Pyotr Petrovitch javob berdi, ko'rinadigan zavq bilan.

en: “Of course, people do get carried away and make mistakes, but one must have indulgence; those mistakes are merely evidence of enthusiasm for the cause and of abnormal external environment.
uz: Albatta, odamlar aldanib, xatolar qiladilar, lekin odam o'zlariga rozi bo'lishi kerak; bu xatolar shunchaki sababga bo'lgan g'ayrat va tashqi muhitning odatiy bo'lmaganligini ko'rsatadi.

en: If little has been done, the time has been but short; of means I will not speak.
uz: Agar kamroq ish qilingan bo'lsa, vaqt oz bo'ladi; mablag'lar haqida gapirmayman.

en: It’s my personal view, if you care to know, that something has been accomplished already.
uz: Bu mening shaxsiy nuqtai nazarimdir, agar siz bilmoqchi bo'lsangiz, bir narsa allaqachon amalga oshirilgan.

en: New valuable ideas, new valuable works are circulating in the place of our old dreamy and romantic authors.
uz: Eski orzu va romantik mualliflarimizning o'rniga yangi qimmatli g'oyalar, yangi qimmatli asarlar aylanmoqda.

en: Literature is taking a maturer form, many injurious prejudices have been rooted up and turned into ridicule.
uz: Adabiyotlar o'sib bormoqda, ko'plab zararli oldindan ko'ringan fikrlar o'rnidan tushib, masxaraga aylandi.

en: … In a word, we have cut ourselves off irrevocably from the past, and that, to my thinking, is a great thing …” “He’s learnt it by heart to show off!” Raskolnikov pronounced suddenly.
uz: Bir so'z bilan aytganda, biz o'tmishda o'zimizni o'zimizdan ajratib qo'ydik va bu mening fikrimcha juda yaxshi narsa ...U o'zini ko'rsatishni o'rgandi! Raskolnikov to'satdan aytdi. ...

en: “What?” asked Pyotr Petrovitch, not catching his words; but he received no reply.
uz: What? so'radi Pyotr Petrovitch, so'zlarini ushlab bo'lmaydi; lekin u hech qanday javob olmaydi.

en: “That’s all true,” Zossimov hastened to interpose.
uz: Bularning barchasi to'g'ri, Zossimov tezroq harakat qildi.

en: “Isn’t it so?” Pyotr Petrovitch went on, glancing affably at Zossimov.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch Zossimovga ko'z tikib, davom etdi.

en: “You must admit,” he went on, addressing Razumihin with a shade of triumph and superciliousness —he almost added “young man” —“that there is an advance, or, as they say now, progress in the name of science and economic truth …” “A commonplace.”
uz: Siz tan olishingiz kerak, u davom etdi, Razumihinga g'alaba va takabburlik soyasida murojaat qildi u deyarli qo'shimcha qildi yosh odam ki, ilm-fan va iqtisodiy haqiqat nomidan avgust yoki, endi aytilganidek, taraqqiyot bor ...A commonplace.

en: “No, not a commonplace!
uz: Yo'q, oddiy joy emas!

en: Hitherto, for instance, if I were told, ‘love thy neighbour,’ what came of it?” Pyotr Petrovitch went on, perhaps with excessive haste.
uz: Misol uchun, agar menga, "O'zgani seving", deb aytilsa, bundan nima foyda? - dedi Pyotr Petrovitch, ehtimol juda tezda.

en: “It came to my tearing my coat in half to share with my neighbour and we both were left half naked.
uz: Men qo'shnim bilan bo'lishish uchun kiyimimni yarimga yirtib yubordim va ikkovimizni yarim yalang'och qoldirdik.

en: As a Russian proverb has it, ‘Catch several hares and you won’t catch one.’ Science now tells us, love yourself before all men, for everything in the world rests on self-interest.
uz: Rossiyalik bir maqolani eslatib o'tamiz: "Bir nechta qushni tuting, birorta ham tutmaysan".Siyfaning aytishicha, o'zingizni barcha odamlardan ko'ra ko'proq seving, chunki dunyoda hamma narsa xudbinlikka asoslangan.

en: You love yourself and manage your own affairs properly and your coat remains whole.
uz: Siz o'zingizni sevasiz va o'zingizning ishingizni to'g'ri boshqarasiz va kiyimingiz butun bo'lib qoladi.

en: Economic truth adds that the better private affairs are organised in society —the more whole coats, so to say —the firmer are its foundations and the better is the common welfare organised too.
uz: Iqtisodiy haqiqat shuni qo'shib qo'ydiki, jamiyatda xususiy ishlar qanchalik yaxshi tashkil etilgan bo'lsa, shunchalik butun ko'ylaklar ko'proq bo'ladi, shunda uning poydevorlari qanchalik mustahkam bo'lsa, umumiy farovonlik ham shunchalik yaxshi tashkil etiladi.

en: Therefore, in acquiring wealth solely and exclusively for myself, I am acquiring, so to speak, for all, and helping to bring to pass my neighbour’s getting a little more than a torn coat; and that not from private, personal liberality, but as a consequence of the general advance.
uz: Shuning uchun, faqat o'zim uchun boylik orttirish orqali, men hamma uchun ham boylik orttirib, qo'shnilarimning ko'tarilgan kiyimdan biroz ko'proq narsa topishiga yordam beryapman; va bu xususiy, shaxsiy erkinlikdan emas, balki umumiy taraqqiyot natijasida sodir bo'ladi.

en: The idea is simple, but unhappily it has been a long time reaching us, being hindered by idealism and sentimentality.
uz: G'oya sodda, ammo, afsuski, idealizm va sentimentallik bizni uzoq vaqtdan beri to'xtatmoqda.

en: And yet it would seem to want very little wit to perceive it …” “Excuse me, I’ve very little wit myself,” Razumihin cut in sharply, “and so let us drop it.
uz: Ammo uni ko'rish uchun juda kam aql-idrok kerak bo'lib tuyuladi ... Xullas, o'zim ham juda kam aql-idrokga ega bo'ldim, Razumihin keskin kesib qo'ydi, va shuning uchun uni tashlaymiz.

en: I began this discussion with an object, but I’ve grown so sick during the last three years of this chattering to amuse oneself, of this incessant flow of commonplaces, always the same, that, by Jove, I blush even when other people talk like that.
uz: Men ushbu suhbatni bir narsa bilan boshladim, lekin o'tgan uch yil davomida o'zimni o'yin-kulgi qilib gapirishdan, odatdagi joylarning doimiy oqimidan shunchalik kasal bo'ldimki, hatto boshqa odamlar shunday gapirganda ham, men, Jove tomonidan, qizg'inlashaman.

en: You are in a hurry, no doubt, to exhibit your acquirements; and I don’t blame you, that’s quite pardonable.
uz: Shubhasizki, siz o'zingizning sotib olgan narsalaringiz bilan shug'ullanishga shoshilyapsiz va men sizni ayblamayman, bu juda afzal.

en: I only wanted to find out what sort of man you are, for so many unscrupulous people have got hold of the progressive cause of late and have so distorted in their own interests everything they touched, that the whole cause has been dragged in the mire.
uz: Men faqat siz qanday inson ekanligingizni bilmoqchiman, chunki oxirgi paytlarda juda ko'p nozik odamlar progressiv sababni o'zlariga olishdi va o'z manfaatlari uchun hamma narsani o'zgartirib yubordilar, shuning uchun butun sabab to'p-to'pga quvib ketdi.

en: That’s enough!” “Excuse me, sir,” said Luzhin, affronted, and speaking with excessive dignity.
uz: Mana shu yetarli!  Meni kechiring, xo'jayinim, dedi Luzhin, qo'rqinch bilan gapirib, ortiqcha qadr-qimmat bilan gapirdi.

en: “Do you mean to suggest so unceremoniously that I too …” “Oh, my dear sir … how could I?
uz: Siz o'zingizning fikringizcha, men ham ...Oh, aziz sirim ... qanday qilib men buni qila olaman?

en: … Come, that’s enough,” Razumihin concluded, and he turned abruptly to Zossimov to continue their previous conversation.
uz: ... Keling, bu yetarli, - dedi Razumihin so'nggi suhbatini davom ettirish uchun to'satdan Zossimovga murojaat qildi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch had the good sense to accept the disavowal.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch tanqidni qabul qilish uchun oqilona fikrga ega edi.

en: He made up his mind to take leave in another minute or two.
uz: U yana bir-ikki daqiqada dam olishga qaror qildi.

en: “I trust our acquaintance,” he said, addressing Raskolnikov, “may, upon your recovery and in view of the circumstances of which you are aware, become closer … Above all, I hope for your return to health …” Raskolnikov did not even turn his head.
uz: Men tanishimizga ishonaman, dedi u, Raskolnikovga murojaat qilib, may, sog'ayganingizdan so'ng va o'zingiz bilgan holatlarni ko'rib, yaqinlashing ... Eng asosiysi, sog'ligingizga qaytishingizni umid qilaman ... Raskolnikov hatto boshini o'zgartirmagan.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch began getting up from his chair.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch o'z kursidan turishga tushdi.

en: “One of her customers must have killed her,” Zossimov declared positively.
uz: Zossimovning bir mijozi uni o'ldirgan bo'lishi kerak, deb ijobiy baho berdi.

en: “Not a doubt of it,” replied Razumihin.
uz: Shubhasiz, javob berdi Razumihin.

en: “Porfiry doesn’t give his opinion, but is examining all who have left pledges with her there.” “Examining them?” Raskolnikov asked aloud.
uz: Porfiry o'z fikrini aytmaydi, lekin u u erda u bilan qasam ichganlarning barchasini tekshirmoqda.  Ularni tekshirmoqda? Raskolnikov baland ovoz bilan so'radi.

en: What then?” “Nothing.” “How does he get hold of them?” asked Zossimov.
uz: Xo'sh, nima bo'ladi? Hech narsa. Qanday qilib u ularga ega bo'ladi? - deb so'radi Zossimov.

en: “Koch has given the names of some of them, other names are on the wrappers of the pledges and some have come forward of themselves.” “It must have been a cunning and practised ruffian!
uz: Koch ularning ba'zilarining ismlarini aytib berdi, ba'zilarining ismlari va'dalarning muqovusida, ba'zilari esa o'z-o'zidan kelib chiqqan. Bu hiylasiz va mashg'ul bo'lgan qotil bo'lishi kerak!

en: The coolness!” “That’s just what it wasn’t!” interposed Razumihin.
uz: Chiroylilik! Bu shunchaki o'sha narsa emas edi!- deb qo'shib qo'ydi Razumihin.

en: “That’s what throws you all off the scent.
uz: Bu sizni hamma narsadan chetda qoldiradi.

en: But I maintain that he is not cunning, not practised, and probably this was his first crime!
uz: Lekin men uning hiyla-nayrang va mashqsiz emasligini, ehtimol bu uning birinchi jinoyatchiligi bo'lganini aytaman!

en: The supposition that it was a calculated crime and a cunning criminal doesn’t work.
uz: Bu hisob-kitob qilingan jinoyat va hiylasiz jinoyatchi bo'lgan degan taxmin ishlamaydi.

en: Suppose him to have been inexperienced, and it’s clear that it was only a chance that saved him —and chance may do anything.
uz: Aytaylik, u tajribasiz bo'lgan va bu uni qutqargan faqatgina imkoniyat ekanligi aniq.

en: Why, he did not foresee obstacles, perhaps!
uz: Ehtimol, u to'siqlarni ko'rmagan bo'lsa kerak!

en: And how did he set to work?
uz: Va u qanday ish boshladi?

en: He took jewels worth ten or twenty roubles, stuffing his pockets with them, ransacked the old woman’s trunks, her rags —and they found fifteen hundred roubles, besides notes, in a box in the top drawer of the chest!
uz: U o'n yoki yigirma rubl qiymatidagi zargarliklarni olib, o'z qoplarini to'ldirib, keksa ayolning bagajlarini, kiyimlarini talon-toroj qildi va ko'krakning yuqori sovrinidagi quti ichida notalar bilan birga besh yuz rubllik zargarlik topdi!

en: He did not know how to rob; he could only murder.
uz: U talon-toroj qilishni bilmasdi; u faqatgina qotillik qila olardi.

en: It was his first crime, I assure you, his first crime; he lost his head.
uz: Bu uning birinchi jinoyati edi, sizga ishontiraman, uning birinchi jinoyati edi; u boshini yo'qotib qo'ydi.

en: And he got off more by luck than good counsel!” “You are talking of the murder of the old pawnbroker, I believe?” Pyotr Petrovitch put in, addressing Zossimov.
uz: Va u yaxshi maslahatdan ko'ra ko'proq omad bilan qutqarildi!Siz eski qarzdorning o'ldirilishi haqida gapiryapsiz, deb o'ylaymanmi?Pyotr Petrovitch Zossimovga murojaat qilib, unga murojaat qildi.

en: He was standing, hat and gloves in hand, but before departing he felt disposed to throw off a few more intellectual phrases.
uz: U qo'lida qo'lqop va qo'lqoplar bilan turardi, lekin ketishdan oldin bir nechta intellektual iboralarni aytishga tayyor edi.

en: He was evidently anxious to make a favourable impression and his vanity overcame his prudence.
uz: U yaxshi taassurot qoldirishni xohlagan va o'zining behudaligi o'z aql-idrokini yenggan.

en: You’ve heard of it?” “Oh, yes, being in the neighbourhood.” “Do you know the details?” “I can’t say that; but another circumstance interests me in the case —the whole question, so to say.
uz: Siz buni eshitganmisiz?Oh, ha, bu erda bo'lish.Siz tafsilotlarni bilasizmi?Men buni aytolmayman; lekin menga boshqa bir holat qiziqtiradi.Butun savol, demak.

en: Not to speak of the fact that crime has been greatly on the increase among the lower classes during the last five years, not to speak of the cases of robbery and arson everywhere, what strikes me as the strangest thing is that in the higher classes, too, crime is increasing proportionately.
uz: So'nggi besh yil ichida past sinflar orasida jinoyatchilik juda ko'payganini aytmaylik, har yerda talon-toroj va yong'in o'tkazib yuborish holatlarini aytmaylik, menga eng g'alati narsa shundaki, yuqori sinflarda ham jinoyatchilik o'rtacha ortib bormoqda.

en: In one place one hears of a student’s robbing the mail on the high road; in another place people of good social position forge false banknotes; in Moscow of late a whole gang has been captured who used to forge lottery tickets, and one of the ringleaders was a lecturer in universal history; then our secretary abroad was murdered from some obscure motive of gain.
uz: Bir joyda oliy yo'ldagi pochta xabarini o'g'irlayotgan talaba haqida eshitish mumkin; boshqa joyda ijtimoiy jihatdan yuqori darajadagi odamlar soxta qog'ozlarni soxtalaydilar; Moskvada so'nggi paytlarda lotereya chiptalarini soxtalashtirgan butun to'pka tutildi va uning rahbarlaridan biri universal tarixdan o'qituvchi bo'lgan; keyin chet eldagi kotibimiz noto'g'ri maqsadlar bilan o'ldirilgan.

en: … And if this old woman, the pawnbroker, has been murdered by someone of a higher class in society —for peasants don’t pawn gold trinkets —how are we to explain this demoralisation of the civilised part of our society?” “There are many economic changes,” put in Zossimov.
uz: Va agar bu keksa ayol, qo'ng'iroqchi, jamiyatning yuqori darajasidagi biri tomonidan o'ldirilgan bo'lsa, qishloq xo'jaligi uchun oltin go'zalliklarni qo'ng'iroq qilmaslik kerak, jamiyatimizning madaniy qismi bu axloqsizlikni qanday tushuntirishimiz mumkin?

en: “How are we to explain it?” Razumihin caught him up.
uz: Qanday qilib tushuntirishimiz kerak? Razumihin uni ushlab qoldi.

en: “It might be explained by our inveterate impracticality.” “How do you mean?” “What answer had your lecturer in Moscow to make to the question why he was forging notes?
uz: Bu bizning o'zboshimchalik bilan amalga oshmaydiganligimiz bilan tushuntirilishi mumkin.Siz nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?Moskvadagi o'qituvchingiz nega yozuvlarni soxtalashtirganligi haqidagi savolga qanday javob bergan?

en: ‘Everybody is getting rich one way or another, so I want to make haste to get rich too.’ I don’t remember the exact words, but the upshot was that he wants money for nothing, without waiting or working!
uz: Har bir kishi shu yoki shu tarzda boy bo'lib bormoqda, shuning uchun men ham boy bo'lish uchun shoshilmoqchiman. Aniq so'zlarni eslay olmayman, lekin natijada u pulni hech narsa uchun, kutmasdan yoki ishlashsiz xohlaydi!

en: We’ve grown used to having everything ready-made, to walking on crutches, to having our food chewed for us.
uz: Biz hamma narsa tayyor bo'lishiga, g'iybatda yurishga, ovqatni biz uchun masxara qilishga odatlanib borganmiz.

en: Then the great hour struck,ൢ and every man showed himself in his true colours.” “But morality?
uz: So'ngra buyuk soat keldi, va har bir kishi o'zini o'z haqiqiy ranglarida namoyish etdi. Ammo axloqiy fazilatlar?

en: And so to speak, principles …” “But why do you worry about it?” Raskolnikov interposed suddenly.
uz: Shunday qilib, prinsiplar ...  Ammo nima uchun siz bu haqda tashvishlanasiz? Raskolnikov to'satdan o'zini tutdi.

en: “It’s in accordance with your theory!” “In accordance with my theory?” “Why, carry out logically the theory you were advocating just now, and it follows that people may be killed …” “Upon my word!” cried Luzhin.
uz: Bu sizning nazariyangizga muvofiq! Mening nazariyangizga muvofiq? Nega deganda, siz hozirda targ'ib qilayotgan nazariyani mantiqiy ravishda amalga oshiring va shundan keyin odamlar o'ldirilishi mumkin ... Mening so'zimga ko'ra! - deb baqirdi Luzhin.

en: “No, that’s not so,” put in Zossimov.
uz: Yo'q, bunday emas, Zossimovni qo'ying.

en: Raskolnikov lay with a white face and twitching upper lip, breathing painfully.
uz: Raskolnikov oq yuzli, yuqori cho'zilib, og'riqli nafas olgan holda yotgan edi.

en: “There’s a measure in all things,” Luzhin went on superciliously.
uz: Har bir narsada o'lchov bor, Luzhin mag'rurlik bilan davom etdi.

en: “Economic ideas are not an incitement to murder, and one has but to suppose …” “And is it true,” Raskolnikov interposed once more suddenly, again in a voice quivering with fury and delight in insulting him, “is it true that you told your fiancée … within an hour of her acceptance, that what pleased you most … was that she was a beggar … because it was better to raise a wife from poverty, so that you may have complete control over her, and reproach her with your being her benefactor?” “Upon my word,” Luzhin cried wrathfully and irritably, crimson with confusion, “to distort my words in this way!
uz: Iqtisodiy g'oyalar odam o'ldirish uchun rag'batlantiruvchi emas va odam faqat shunday tasavvur qilishi kerak ...  Va bu haqiqatmi, Raskolnikov yana bir bor to'satdan, yana bir bor g'azabdan titraydigan va uni haqoratlashdan zavqlanayotgan ovoz bilan gapirdi, Siz kelinchingizga ... uni qabul qilishdan bir soat o'tgach, eng ko'p sizga yoqqan narsa ... u yolvorgan ayol ekanligi edi ... chunki siz uning ustidan to'liq nazorat qilishingiz uchun, xotiningizni kambag'allikdan tarbiyalash yaxshiroq edi va uni yaxshilik qiluvchi sifatida ayblashingiz kerakmi?  Mening so'zimga binoan,  Luzhin g'azab va g'azabga to'lib, g'azabga to'lib, g'azabga to'lib, g'azabga to'lib, so'zlarimni bu tarzda buzish uchun o'zingizdan ko'proq xursand bo'ldingiz!

en: Excuse me, allow me to assure you that the report which has reached you, or rather, let me say, has been conveyed to you, has no foundation in truth, and I … suspect who … in a word … this arrow … in a word, your mamma … She seemed to me in other things, with all her excellent qualities, of a somewhat high-flown and romantic way of thinking.
uz: Kechirasizlar, sizga yetib kelgan yoki, aniqrog'i, sizga yetkazilgan xabar haqiqatga asoslanmaganligini sizga ta'kidlayman va men ... kim ... bir so'z bilan ... bu o'q ... bir so'z bilan, sizning onangiz ... menga boshqa narsalarda, barcha ajoyib fazilatlari bilan, biroz yuksak va romantik fikrlash tarzini ko'rsatgan deb o'ylayman.

en: … But I was a thousand miles from supposing that she would misunderstand and misrepresent things in so fanciful a way.
uz: Ammo men uning bu kabi g'alati tarzda noto'g'ri tushunishi va noto'g'ri tasavvur qilishi haqida o'ylamaganman.

en: … And indeed … indeed …” “I tell you what,” cried Raskolnikov, raising himself on his pillow and fixing his piercing, glittering eyes upon him, “I tell you what.” “What?” Luzhin stood still, waiting with a defiant and offended face.
uz: Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham... Haqiqatan ham...

en: Silence lasted for some seconds.
uz: Bir necha soniya davomida xotirjamlik davom etdi.

en: “Why, if ever again … you dare to mention a single word … about my mother … I shall send you flying downstairs!” “What’s the matter with you?” cried Razumihin.
uz: Nega, agar siz yana bir bor ... onam haqida bitta so'z aytishga jur'at qilsangiz ... men sizni pastga o'tkazaman!   Sizga nima bo'ldi? deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: “So that’s how it is?” Luzhin turned pale and bit his lip.
uz: Shunday bo'ladi-ku?Lujin o'z ko'zidan o'zgarib, og'zini o'g'irlab qo'ydi.

en: “Let me tell you, sir,” he began deliberately, doing his utmost to restrain himself but breathing hard, “at the first moment I saw you you were ill- disposed to me, but I remained here on purpose to find out more.
uz: Sizga aytaman, xo'jayinim,  u bila turib boshlandi, o'zini tuta bilish uchun qo'lidan kelganini qildi, lekin qattiq nafas oldi,  sizni birinchi marta ko'rganimda menga yomon munosabatda bo'ldingiz, lekin men ko'proq narsani bilish uchun bu yerda qolishimni xohladim.

en: I could forgive a great deal in a sick man and a connection, but you … never after this …” “I am not ill,” cried Raskolnikov.
uz: Kasal odam va aloqa uchun men ko'p narsani kechirardim, lekin siz ... bundan keyin hech qachon ...  Men kasal emasman, Raskolnikov xitob qildi.

en: “So much the worse …”
uz: Shunday qilib yomonroq bo'ladi ...

en: “Go to hell!” But Luzhin was already leaving without finishing his speech, squeezing between the table and the chair; Razumihin got up this time to let him pass.
uz: Janahatga ketinglar! Lekin Luzhin nutqini tugatmasdan, stol va o'rinni o'rtasiga surib ketayotgan edi; bu safar Razumihin uni o'tkazib yuborish uchun o'rnidan turibdi.

en: Without glancing at anyone, and not even nodding to Zossimov, who had for some time been making signs to him to let the sick man alone, he went out, lifting his hat to the level of his shoulders to avoid crushing it as he stooped to go out of the door.
uz: Hech kimga ko'z tikmay, hatto Zossimovga boshini og'ritmay, u kasal odamni qo'yib yuborish uchun bir muncha vaqt belgilar qilib yurgan edi, lekin u xotiniga qo'shilib, eshikdan chiqib ketayotganda uni ezib tashlamaslik uchun, to'pini yelkasigacha ko'tarib tashqariga chiqdi.

en: And even the curve of his spine was expressive of the horrible insult he had received.
uz: Hatto uning cho'ng'i bo'g'riligi ham unga yetkazilgan dahshatli haqoratning ifodasini ko'rsatdi.

en: “How could you —how could you!” Razumihin said, shaking his head in perplexity.
uz: Qanday qilib qila olasiz! - dedi Razumihin, g'ayratda boshini silkitib.

en: “Let me alone —let me alone all of you!” Raskolnikov cried in a frenzy.
uz: Meni tinch qo'yinglar!Meni tinch qo'yinglar! Raskolnikov g'azabdan yig'ladi.

en: “Will you ever leave off tormenting me?
uz: Siz meni azoblashni to'xtatasizmi?

en: I am not afraid of you!
uz: Men sizlardan qo'rqmayman!

en: I am not afraid of anyone, anyone now!
uz: Men endi hech kimdan qo'rqmayman, hech kimdan qo'rqmayman!

en: I want to be alone, alone, alone!” “Come along,” said Zossimov, nodding to Razumihin.
uz: Men yolg'iz, yolg'iz, yolg'iz bo'lishni istayman!Kelib kelinglar, dedi Zossimov, razumihinga bosh ko'tardi.

en: “But we can’t leave him like this!” “Come along,” Zossimov repeated insistently, and he went out.
uz: Ammo biz uni shunday qoldira olmaymiz!Yolingizga kelinglar,Zossimov qat'iylik bilan takrorladi va u tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Razumihin thought a minute and ran to overtake him.
uz: Razumihin bir daqiqa o'ylab, uni kutib olish uchun yugurdi.

en: “It might be worse not to obey him,” said Zossimov on the stairs.
uz: "Undan bo'ysunmaslik yanada yomon bo'lishi mumkin", - dedi Zossimov mertabanlarda.

en: “He mustn’t be irritated.” “What’s the matter with him?” “If only he could get some favourable shock, that’s what would do it!
uz: U g'azablanib qolmasligi kerak.  Unga nima bo'ldi?  Agar u ijobiy shokga duch kelsa edi, bu uni to'g'rilaydi!

en: At first he was better.
uz: Boshida u yaxshiroq edi.

en: … You know he has got something on his mind!
uz: - Uning biror o'y-fikri borligini bilasiz!

en: Some fixed idea weighing on him.
uz: Uning zimmasida biron bir fikr yuklanmoqda.

en: … I am very much afraid so; he must have!” “Perhaps it’s that gentleman, Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: ... Men juda qo'rqaman; u buni qilgan bo'lishi kerak!Ehtimol, bu Pyotr Petrovitch ismli xonimdir.

en: From his conversation I gather he is going to marry his sister, and that he had received a letter about it just before his illness.
uz: Suhbatidan bilib olsam, u singlisi bilan turmushga chiqmoqchi va kasalligidan sal oldin bu haqda xat olgan.

en: …” “Yes, confound the man!
uz: ... Ha, odamni chalg'itib qo'ying!

en: he may have upset the case altogether.
uz: Ehtimol, u ishni butunlay buzgan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: But have you noticed, he takes no interest in anything, he does not respond to anything except one point on which he seems excited — that’s the murder?” “Yes, yes,” Razumihin agreed, “I noticed that, too.
uz: Ammo siz ham e'tibor berganmisiz, u hech narsa bilan qiziqmaydi, faqat bir nuqtadan tashqari hech narsa bilan javob bermaydi, u erda u hayajonlangan ko'rinadi, ya'ni qotillik? Ha, ha, Razumihin rozi bo'ldi, men ham buni e'tiborga oldim.

en: He is interested, frightened.
uz: U qiziqadi, qo'rqadi.

en: It gave him a shock on the day he was ill in the police office; he fainted.”
uz: Politsiya xonadonida kasal bo'lgan kuni u qattiq hayron bo'ldi; u o'zini yo'qotib qo'ydi.

en: “Tell me more about that this evening and I’ll tell you something afterwards.
uz: Bu kecha menga bu haqda ko'proq aytib bering va keyinroq sizga bir narsa aytib beraman.

en: He interests me very much!
uz: U meni juda qiziqtiradi!

en: In half an hour I’ll go and see him again.
uz: Yarim soatdan keyin uni yana ko'rishga ketaman.

en: … There’ll be no inflammation though.” “Thanks!
uz: ... Garchi bu yerda ildiz otishi yo'q bo'lsa-da. Thanks!

en: And I’ll wait with Pashenka meantime and will keep watch on him through Nastasya.
uz: Va men o'sha paytgacha Pashenka bilan birga kutaman va Nastasya orqali uning ustidan nazoratni o'tkazaman.

en: …” Raskolnikov, left alone, looked with impatience and misery at Nastasya, but she still lingered.
uz: ... Raskolnikov yolg'iz qolgach, sabrsizlik va qayg'u bilan Nastasyaga qaradi, lekin u hali ham ko'p o'tiradi.

en: “Won’t you have some tea now?” she asked.
uz: - Endi choy ichmaysanmi? - deb so'radi u.

en: Leave me.” He turned abruptly to the wall; Nastasya went out.
uz: Meni tark eting. U to'satdan devor tomon burildi; Nastasya tashqariga chiqdi.

en: VI But as soon as she went out, he got up, latched the door, undid the parcel which Razumihin had brought in that evening and had tied up again and began dressing.
uz: Ammo VI ayol chiqib ketgandan so'ng, u o'rnidan turib, eshikni qulflab, o'sha kechqurun Razumihin olib kelgan paketni yechib, yana bog'lab qo'ydi va kiyishni boshladi.

en: Strange to say, he seemed immediately to have become perfectly calm; not a trace of his recent delirium nor of the panic fear that had haunted him of late.
uz: Ajablanarlisi shundaki, u darhol to'liq xotirjam bo'lib qoldi; so'nggi delirining ham, uni oxir-oqibat qiynagan qo'rquvning ham izlari yo'q edi.

en: It was the first moment of a strange sudden calm.
uz: Bu g'alati shodlikning birinchi daqiqa edi.

en: His movements were precise and definite; a firm purpose was evident in them.
uz: Uning harakatlari aniq va aniq edi; ularning aniq maqsadi aniq edi.

en: “Today, today,” he muttered to himself.
uz: Bugun, bugun, o'zi o'zi o'zi uchun g'iybat qildi.

en: He understood that he was still weak, but his intense spiritual concentration gave him strength and self-confidence.
uz: U hali ham zaif ekanligini tushunardi, ammo uning kuchli ma'naviy konsentratsiyasi unga kuch va ishonch ato etdi.

en: He hoped, moreover, that he would not fall down in the street.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u ko'chaga tushib ketmaslikka umidvor edi.

en: When he had dressed in entirely new clothes, he looked at the money lying on the table, and after a moment’s thought put it in his pocket.
uz: To'liq yangi kiyim kiyganidan so'ng, u stol ustida yotgan pulga qarab, bir zum o'ylab, uni kiyiga qo'ydi.

en: It was twenty-five roubles.
uz: Bu yigirma besh rubldan iborat edi.

en: He took also all the copper change from the ten roubles spent by Razumihin on the clothes.
uz: Shuningdek, Razumihin kiyim-kechak uchun sarflagan o'n rubldan barcha mis o'rnini oldi.

en: Then he softly unlatched the door, went out, slipped downstairs and glanced in at the open kitchen door.
uz: Keyin u eshikni sekin-sakin ochib, tashqariga chiqdi, pastga tushib, oshxona eshigini ochib qo'ydi.

en: Nastasya was standing with her back to him, blowing up the landlady’s samovar.
uz: Nastasya uning orqasidan turib, uy egasining samovarini portlatardi.

en: Who would have dreamed of his going out, indeed?
uz: Uning tashqariga chiqishi haqida kim o'ylagan bo'lishi mumkin edi?

en: A minute later he was in the street.
uz: Bir daqiqa o'tgach, u ko'chada edi.

en: It was nearly eight o’clock, the sun was setting.
uz: Deyarli sakkiz soat edi, quyosh botayotgan edi.

en: It was as stifling as before, but he eagerly drank in the stinking, dusty town air.
uz: Oldingi kabi og'ir edi, lekin u shaharning buzuq, changli havoidan juda ham ichdi.

en: His head felt rather dizzy; a sort of savage energy gleamed suddenly in his feverish eyes and his wasted, pale and yellow face.
uz: Uning boshi o'ziga o'xshaydi, bir xil yovvoyi energiya birdan uning issiq ko'zlarida va uning yo'q bo'lib ketgan, soya va sariq yuzida parvarish qildi.

en: He did not know and did not think where he was going, he had one thought only: “that all this must be ended today, once for all, immediately; that he would not return home without it, because he would not go on living like that.” How, with what to make an end?
uz: U qayerga borayotganini bilmas va o'ylamas edi, faqat bitta fikr bor edi: Bularning barchasi bugun, bir marta, darhol tugashi kerak; u o'z uyiga bu yo'lsiz qaytib kelmasligini, chunki u bunday yashashni davom ettira olmasligini. Qanday qilib, nima bilan tugashi kerak?

en: He had not an idea about it,
uz: U bu haqda hech qanday tasavvurga ega emas edi,

en: he did not even want to think of it.
uz: U hatto bu haqda o'ylashni ham istamagan.

en: He drove away thought; thought tortured him.
uz: U fikrni haydab yubordi; fikr uni qiynagan.

en: All he knew, all he felt was that everything must be changed “one way or another,” he repeated with desperate and immovable self-confidence and determination.
uz: U faqatgina hamma narsani o'zgartirishi kerakligini bilardi, faqat o'ziga ishonch va qat'iy qaror bilan aytdi.

en: From old habit he took his usual walk in the direction of the Hay Market.
uz: O'zining eski odatidan kelib, u odatdagidek Hay bozori yo'liga yurdi.

en: A dark-haired young man with a barrel organ was standing in the road in front of a little general shop and was grinding out a very sentimental song.
uz: Bir qora sochli yigit, barrel organini qo'yib, yo'lda kichkina general do'kon oldida turib, juda hissiy qo'shiq kuylab yurgan edi.

en: He was accompanying a girl of fifteen, who stood on the pavement in front of him.
uz: U o'zining oldida piyoda turgan o'n besh yoshli qizchani hamroh qilib borardi.

en: She was dressed up in a crinoline, a mantle and a straw hat with a flame-coloured feather in it, all very old and shabby.
uz: U krinolin kiyimida, choriq va cho'g'li to'pka kiygan edi va u ichida olov rangli piyoda bor edi, bularning hammasi juda eski va yomon edi.

en: In a strong and rather agreeable voice, cracked and coarsened by street singing, she sang in hope of getting a copper from the shop.
uz: Ko'cha qo'shiqlari bilan bo'lgan kuchli va yoqimli ovoz bilan, u do'kondan mis olish umidi bilan kuylagan.

en: Raskolnikov joined two or three listeners, took out a five kopeck piece and put it in the girl’s hand.
uz: Raskolnikov ikki yoki uchta tinglovchiga qo'shildi, besh kopeklik bo'lakni olib, qizning qo'liga qo'ydi.

en: She broke off abruptly on a sentimental high note, shouted sharply to the organ grinder “Come on,” and both moved on to the next shop.
uz: O'shanda u shovqinlik bilan o'z o'rnidan chiqdi, organni o'zgartiruvchi mashinaga o'z ovozini baland ovoz bilan aytdi: "Qo'y, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel, kel!

en: “Do you like street music?” said Raskolnikov, addressing a middle- aged man standing idly by him.
uz: Siz ko'cha musiqasini yoqtirasizmi? dedi Raskolnikov, uning yonida o'rta yoshdagi bir kishiga murojaat qilib.

en: The man looked at him, startled and wondering.
uz: Bu kishi unga qarab, hayron va hayron qoldi.

en: “I love to hear singing to a street organ,” said Raskolnikov, and his manner seemed strangely out of keeping with the subject —“I like it on cold, dark, damp autumn evenings —they must be damp —when all the passersby have pale green, sickly faces, or better still when wet snow is falling straight down, when there’s no wind —you know what I mean?
uz: Men ko'cha organida qo'shiq kuylashni eshitishni yaxshi ko'raman,  dedi Raskolnikov, va uning xulq-atvori mavzuga zid bo'lib tuyuldi Men sovuq, qorong'u, nam kuz kechalari yoqadi ular nam bo'lishi kerak barcha yo'lovchilarning ko'k yashil, kasal yuzlari bo'lganida, yoki yana yaxshi tomondan, shamol yo'q bo'lganida, shamol yo'q bo'lganida.

en: —and the street lamps shine through it …” “I don’t know.
uz: va ko'cha chiroqlari u orqali porlaydi ...   Men bilmayman.

en: … Excuse me …” muttered the stranger, frightened by the question and Raskolnikov’s strange manner, and he crossed over to the other side of the street.
uz: Kechirasiz, bu savol va Raskolnikovning g'alati xatti-harakatidan qo'rqqan begona odam g'ayrat bilan gapirdi va ko'chaga o'tib ketdi.

en: Raskolnikov walked straight on and came out at the corner of the Hay Market, where the huckster and his wife had talked with Lizaveta; but they were not there now.
uz: Raskolnikov to'g'ri yurib, Hay bozori burchagida chiqdi, u erda huckster va uning xotini Lizaveta bilan suhbatlashishgan edilar; lekin hozir ular u yerda yo'q edilar.

en: Recognising the place, he stopped, looked round and addressed a young fellow in a red shirt who stood gaping before a corn chandler’s shop.
uz: Bu joyni tan olib, to'xtab, atrofini ko'rib, bir momaqaldor do'konining oldida o'tirib turgan qizil ko'ylak kiygan yigitga murojaat qildi.

en: “Isn’t there a man who keeps a booth with his wife at this corner?” “All sorts of people keep booths here,” answered the young man, glancing superciliously at Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu burchada xotini bilan bo'yxonaga ega bo'lgan kishi yo'qmi? - deb javob berdi yigit. - Bu yerda har xil odamlar bo'yxonaga ega bo'lishadi.

en: “What he was christened.” “Aren’t you a Zaraïsky man, too?
uz: U suvga cho'mgan edi.Siz ham Zorayskiy odam deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: Which province?” The young man looked at Raskolnikov again.
uz: Qaysi viloyat? Yosh yigit Raskolnikovga yana nazar soladi.

en: “It’s not a province, your excellency, but a district.
uz: Bu viloyat emas, Oliy ruhoniy, balki tuman.

en: Graciously forgive me, your excellency!” “Is that a tavern at the top there?” “Yes, it’s an eating-house and there’s a billiard-room and you’ll find princesses there too.
uz: Rahm-shafqat bilan meni kechiring, Oliy ruhoniy!U erda yuqorida taverna bormi?Ha, bu ovqatlanishxonasi va bir bilyard xonasi bor va u erda siz ham princesslarni topasiz.

en: … La-la!” Raskolnikov crossed the square.
uz: ...La-la! Raskolnikov maydonni kesib o'tdi.

en: In that corner there was a dense crowd of peasants.
uz: O'sha burchada dehqonlar ko'pligi bor edi.

en: He pushed his way into the thickest part of it, looking at the faces.
uz: U yuzlarga qarab, eng qalin qismga kirib keldi.

en: He felt an unaccountable inclination to enter into conversation with people.
uz: U odamlar bilan suhbatga kirishishga o'ziga xos moyillikni his qilardi.

en: But the peasants took no notice of him; they were all shouting in groups together.
uz: Lekin fermerlar unga e'tibor bermadilar, hamma guruh-guruhlar bilan baqirib ketishdi.

en: He stood and thought a little and took a turning to the right in the direction of V — —.
uz: U biroz o'ylab, o'ng tomonga V   yo'nalishida burildi.

en: He had often crossed that little street which turns at an angle, leading from the marketplace to Sadovy Street.
uz: U ko'pincha bozordan Sadoviy ko'chasigacha olib boradigan burchakga aylangan kichik ko'chani kesib o'tgan edi.

en: Of late he had often felt drawn to wander about this district, when he felt depressed, that he might feel more so.
uz: So'nggi paytlarda u ko'pincha o'zini ko'proq his qilish uchun bu tuman atrofida yurishga undaydigan va tushkunlikka tushgan paytlarda o'zini ko'pincha his qilardi.

en: Now he walked along, thinking of nothing.
uz: Endi u hech narsa haqida o'ylamagan holda yurardi.

en: At that point there is a great block of buildings, entirely let out in dram shops and eating- houses; women were continually running in and out, bareheaded and in their indoor clothes.
uz: O'sha paytda binolarning katta qismi bor edi, ular butunlay drama do'konlari va oshxonalarda bo'lgan edi; ayollar bechora boshli va ichki kiyimlarini kiygan holda muntazam ravishda kirib-kirib ketishardi.

en: Here and there they gathered in groups, on the pavement, especially about the entrances to various festive establishments in the lower storeys.
uz: Bu erda va u erda ular guruhlar bo'lib, yo'l ustida yig'ilishardilar, ayniqsa pastki qavatlardagi turli bayram ta'minotlariga kirish yo'nalishlarida.

en: From one of these a loud din, sounds of singing, the tinkling of a guitar and shouts of merriment, floated into the street.
uz: Ulardan biriga baland ovoz, qo'shiq tovushlari, gitaraning qichqiriqlari va quvonchli qichqiriqlar ko'chaga ko'tarildi.

en: A crowd of women were thronging round the door; some were sitting on the steps, others on the pavement, others were standing talking.
uz: Eshik atrofida bir to'plam ayollar to'planib turardi; ba'zilari qadamda, ba'zilari piyoda, ba'zilari esa to'xtab gapirib o'tirardi.

en: A drunken soldier, smoking a cigarette, was walking near them in the road, swearing; he seemed to be trying to find his way somewhere, but had forgotten where.
uz: Ularga yaqin yo'lda ichkilikboz, sigaret chekayotgan askar yuribdi va qasam ichardi; u qayerda bo'lsa-da o'z yo'lini topishga harakat qilganday tuyuldi, ammo qayerdaligini unutib qo'ydi.

en: One beggar was quarrelling with another, and a man dead drunk was lying right across the road.
uz: Bir so'roqchi boshqa so'roqchi bilan bahslashayotgan edi, bir kishi esa yo'l o'rtasida o'lik mast bo'lib yotgan edi.

en: Raskolnikov joined the throng of women, who were talking in husky voices.
uz: Raskolnikov ayollarning to'plamiga qo'shildi va ular o'z ovozlari bilan gapirishdi.

en: They were bareheaded and wore cotton dresses and goatskin shoes.
uz: Ular yalang'och boshli edilar va paxta kiyimlari va echki teridan poyabzallar kiygan edilar.

en: There were women of forty and some not more than seventeen; almost all had blackened eyes.
uz: Ularning orasida qirq yoshli va ba'zilari o'n yettidan ortiq bo'lmagan ayollar bor edi; deyarli ularning barchasi qora ko'zlar bilan ko'rinardi.

en: He felt strangely attracted by the singing and all the noise and uproar in the saloon below … someone could be heard within
uz: U o'zini qo'shiq va pastki saloondagi barcha shov-shuv va shov-shuvdan g'alati jalb qilib ko'rdi ... ichkarida kimnidir eshitish mumkin edi

en: dancing frantically, marking time with his heels to the sounds of the guitar and of a thin falsetto voice singing a jaunty air.
uz: U zo'rlik bilan raqsga tushadi va gitara va yumshatli falsetto ovozini qo'shiq bilan qo'shiq bilan o'tkazadi.

en: He listened intently, gloomily and dreamily, bending down at the entrance and peeping inquisitively in from the pavement.
uz: U diqqat bilan, tush va tush bilan tinglab, eshikda egib, yo'ldan o'zini o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: “Oh, my handsome soldier  Don’t beat me for nothing,” trilled the thin voice of the singer.
uz: Oh, go'zal askarim, meni behuda urma,  qo'shiqchining chiroyli ovozini silkitdi.

en: Raskolnikov felt a great desire to make out what he was singing, as though everything depended on that.
uz: Raskolnikov o'zining qo'shiqlarini aniqlashga katta istak ko'rsatdi, xuddi hamma narsa shu narsadan bog'liq bo'lgani kabi.

en: “Shall I go in?” he thought.
uz: Men kirsam bo'ladimi? - deb o'yladi u.

en: Shall I get drunk?” “Won’t you come in?” one of the women asked him.
uz: Men mast bo'lishim kerakmi?  Siz kirmaysizmi? - deb so'radi ayollardan biri unga.

en: Her voice was still musical and less thick than the others, she was young and not repulsive —the only one of the group.
uz: Uning ovozi hali ham musiqiy va boshqalarga qaraganda kamroq bo'lgan, u yosh va jirkanch emas edi.

en: “Why, she’s pretty,” he said, drawing himself up and looking at her.
uz: "U juda chiroyli", - dedi u, o'zini ko'tarib, unga qarab.

en: She smiled, much pleased at the compliment.
uz: U tabassum qildi va bu maqomdan juda xursand bo'ldi.

en: “You’re very nice looking yourself,” she said.
uz: "Siz juda yaxshi ko'rinasiz", dedi u.

en: “Isn’t he thin though!” observed another woman in a deep bass.
uz: Ammo u chiroyli emasmi? - deb o'yladi boshqa bir ayol chuqur bassda.

en: “Have you just come out of a hospital?” “They’re all generals’ daughters, it seems, but they have all snub noses,” interposed a tipsy peasant with a sly smile on his face, wearing a loose coat.
uz: Shuningcha kasalxonadan chiqqanmisiz?Bularning barchasi generallar qizlar, deb o'ylayman, lekin ularning barchasi burunlari ko'tarilgan, o'z yuziga qo'pol tabassumli, bo'sh kiyim kiygan, o'ziga tikilgan qishloq xo'jaligi o'rtasida o'zaro bog'liq.

en: “See how jolly they are.” “Go along with you!” “I’ll go, sweetie!” And he darted down into the saloon below.
uz: Qarang, ular qanchalik quvonchli.   Siz bilan birga boring!   Men ketaman, qizim!  Va u pastdagi saloonga tushdi.

en: Raskolnikov moved on.
uz: Raskolnikov davom etdi.

en: “I say, sir,” the girl shouted after him.
uz: Men aytaman, xo'jayinim, qiz uning orqasidan qichqirdi.

en: “What is it?” She hesitated.
uz: Nima bu? U shubha ostiga qo'ydi.

en: “I’ll always be pleased to spend an hour with you, kind gentleman, but now I feel shy.
uz: Siz bilan bir soat vaqt o'tkazishga doim rozi bo'laman, aziz rafiqam, lekin endi men o'zimni uyalgan his qilaman.

en: Give me six kopecks for a drink, there’s a nice young man!” Raskolnikov gave her what came first —fifteen kopecks.
uz: Menga bir ichimlik uchun olti kopek bering, yaxshi yigit bor! Raskolnikov unga birinchi bo'lib kelganini berdio'n besh kopek.

en: “Ah, what a good-natured gentleman!” “What’s your name?” “Ask for Duclida.”
uz: Ah, naqadar xushmuomala janob!Qanday ismingiz bor?Duklida so'rang.

en: “Well, that’s too much,” one of the women observed, shaking her head at Duclida.
uz: Eh, bu juda ko'p,  deb kuzatgan ayollardan biri Duclidaga boshini silkitibdi.

en: “I don’t know how you can ask like that.
uz: Qanday qilib bunday savol berish mumkinligini bilmayman.

en: I believe I should drop with shame.
uz: Men o'zimni sharmanda his qilib tushishim kerak deb o'ylayman.

en: …” Raskolnikov looked curiously at the speaker.
uz: ... Raskolnikov nutq so'zlovchiga qiziqarli qarashdi.

en: She was a pockmarked wench of thirty, covered with bruises, with her upper lip swollen.
uz: U o'ttiz yoshli bo'lgan, o'qlari ko'p bo'lgan, yuqori tili puchgan ayol edi.

en: She made her criticism quietly and earnestly.

uz: U qayerda, Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: “Where is it I’ve read that someone condemned to death says or thinks, an hour before his death, that if he had to live on some high rock, on such a narrow ledge that he’d only room to stand, and the ocean, everlasting darkness, everlasting solitude, everlasting tempest around him, if he had to remain standing on a square yard of space all his life, a thousand years, eternity, it were better to live so than to die at once!
uz: Men o'limidan bir soat oldin o'limga mahkum bo'lgan kishi, agar u o'limidan bir soat oldin biron bir baland toshda, shunchalik tor bo'lakda yashashi kerak bo'lsa va okean, abadiy qorong'ilik, abadiy yolg'izlik, atrofida abadiy bo'ron bo'lsa, agar u butun hayoti, ming yil, abadiylik davomida kvadrat maydonda turishi kerak bo'lsa, uni bir marta o'ldirishdan ko'ra o'sha tarzda yashash yaxshiroqdir, deb aytadi yoki o'ylaydi, deb o'qidim.

en: Only to live, to live and live!
uz: Faqatgina yashash, yashash va yashash uchun!

en: Life, whatever it may be!
uz: Hayot, nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar!

en: Man is a vile creature!
uz: Inson - bu yovuz mavjudot!

en: … And vile is he who calls him vile for that,” he added a moment later.
uz: ...U uchun uni yomon deb atagan kishi yovuz, u bir muncha vaqt o'tgach qo'shimcha qildi.

en: He went into another street.
uz: U boshqa ko'chaga chiqib ketdi.

en: “Bah, the Palais de Cristal!
uz: Bah, Kristal saroyi!

en: Razumihin was just talking of the Palais de Cristal.
uz: Razumihin Kristal saroy haqida gapirgan edi.

en: But what on earth was it I wanted?
uz: Lekin men nima istayman?

en: Yes, the newspapers.
uz: Ha, gazetalar.

en: … Zossimov said he’d read it in the papers.
uz: ...Zossimov uni gazetalarda o'qiganini aytdi.

en: Have you the papers?” he asked, going into a very spacious and positively clean restaurant, consisting of several rooms, which were, however, rather empty.
uz: Hujjatlar bormi? deb so'radi u, juda keng va juda toza restoranga kirib, bir nechta xonadan iborat edi, ammo u juda bo'sh edi.

en: Two or three people were drinking tea, and in a room further away were sitting four men drinking champagne.
uz: Ikki-uch kishi choy ichayotgan edi, uzoqroq bir xonada esa to'rt kishi shampan ichib o'tirgan edi.

en: Raskolnikov fancied that Zametov was one of them, but he could not be sure at that distance.
uz: Raskolnikov Zametov ularning biri deb o'ylagan, ammo u o'sha masofada aniq emas edi.

en: “What if it is?” he thought.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa-chi? deb o'yladi.

en: “Will you have vodka?” asked the waiter.
uz: Vodka ichasizmi? deb so'radi xizmatkor.

en: “Give me some tea and bring me the papers, the old ones for the last five days, and I’ll give you something.” “Yes, sir, here’s today’s.
uz: Menga biroz choy berib, so'nggi besh kunlik qog'ozlarni olib keling, men sizga bir narsa beraman.

en: No vodka?” The old newspapers and the tea were brought.
uz: Vodka yo'qmi? Eski gazetalar va choy olib kelingan.

en: Raskolnikov sat down and began to look through them.
uz: Raskolnikov o'tirib, ularni ko'rib chiqdi.

en: “Oh, damn … these are the items of intelligence.
uz: Oh, ha... bu aql-idrokning buyumlari.

en: An accident on a staircase, spontaneous combustion of a shopkeeper from alcohol, a fire in Peski … a fire in the Petersburg quarter … another fire in the Petersburg quarter … and another fire in the Petersburg quarter.
uz: Sinchkovchilar ustida yuz bergan baxtsiz hodisa, do'kon egasining spontenzial ravishda spirtli ichimliklardan yondirilishi, Peski shahrida yong'in yuz bergani, Peterburg kvartalidagi yong'in yuz bergani, Peterburg kvartalidagi yana bir yong'in yuz bergani va Peterburg kvartalidagi yana bir yong'in yuz bergani.

en: … Ah, here it is!” He found at last what he was seeking and began to read it.
uz: Ah, shu yerdadir! Oxir-oqibat o'zi qidirayotgan narsani topdi va uni o'qishni boshladi.

en: The lines danced before his eyes, but he read it all and
uz: Yozuvlar uning ko'z o'ngida raqsga tushdi, lekin u hamma narsani o'qib, uni o'qidi.

en: began eagerly seeking later additions in the following numbers.
uz: Keyinchalik quyidagi raqamlarda qo'shimchalar izlashni boshladi.

en: His hands shook with nervous impatience as he turned the sheets.
uz: Uning qo'llari teshiklarni burib o'tkazganida g'azabga to'lib-toshgan.

en: Suddenly someone sat down beside him at his table.
uz: Toʻsatdan kimdir uning yonida uning dasturxonida oʻtirdi.

en: He looked up, it was the head clerk Zametov, looking just the same, with the rings on his fingers and the watch-chain, with the curly, black hair, parted and pomaded, with the smart waistcoat, rather shabby coat and doubtful linen.
uz: U ko'z ko'tardi, bu bosh xodim Zametov edi, u xuddi shunday ko'rinardi, barmoqlarida bog'liq bo'lgan do'stlar va soat zanjirlari bilan, qalin, qora sochli, bo'linadigan va mo'mlangan, aqlli kiyimli, kam bo'sh kiyimli va shubhali mato bilan.

en: He was in a good humour, at least he was smiling very gaily and good-humouredly.
uz: U yaxshi humorda edi, hech bo'lmaganda u juda quvonchli va xushmuomala tabassum bilan tabassum qilardi.

en: His dark face was rather flushed from the champagne he had drunk.
uz: Uning qorong'i yuzi ichgan shampanjdan ko'ra ko'proq qizg'in edi.

en: “What, you here?” he began in surprise, speaking as though he’d known him all his life.
uz: U hayron bo'lib, uni butun umr tanigan kabi gapira boshladi.

en: “Why, Razumihin told me only yesterday you were unconscious.
uz: Nima uchun, Razumihin menga faqat kecha siz ongsiz ekanligingizni aytdi.

en: And do you know I’ve been to see you?” Raskolnikov knew he would come up to him.
uz: Sizni ko'rish uchun borganimni bilasanmi? Raskolnikov uning o'ziga yaqinlashishini bilardi.

en: He laid aside the papers and turned to Zametov.
uz: U qog'ozlarni bir chetga qo'yib, Zametovga murojaat qildi.

en: There was a smile on his lips, and a new shade of irritable impatience was apparent in that smile.
uz: Uning og'izlarida tabassum bor edi va bu tabassumda g'azablanarli sabrsizlikning yangi soyasi ko'rinardi.

en: “I know you have,” he answered.
uz: Men bilaman, shunday ekansiz, dedi u.

en: You looked for my sock.
uz: Siz mening shortsimni qidirib topdingiz.

en: … And you know Razumihin has lost his heart to you?
uz: Va siz Razumihinning siz uchun yuragini yo'qotganini bilasizmi?

en: He says you’ve been with him to Luise Ivanovna’s —you know, the woman you tried to befriend, for whom you winked to the Explosive Lieutenant and he would not understand.
uz: Uning aytishicha, siz Luiz Ivonovna bilan birga bo'lgansiz, bilasizmi, siz do'st bo'lishga harakat qilgan ayol, u uchun siz Explosive Lt.ga ko'z yumgansiz va u buni tushunmaydi.

en: How could he fail to understand —it was quite clear, wasn’t it?” “What a hot head he is!” “The explosive one?” “No, your friend Razumihin.” “You must have a jolly life, Mr.
uz: Qanday qilib u tushunib yetmadi?  Bu juda aniq edi, shunday emasmi?  U qanday qizg'in bosh!  Portlovchi?  Yo'q, do'stingiz Razumihin.  Siz xursand hayot kechirishingiz kerak, Mr.

en: Zametov; entrance free to the most agreeable places.
uz: Zametov; eng yoqimli joylarga kirish bepul.

en: Who’s been pouring champagne into you just now?” “We’ve just been … having a drink together.
uz: Sizga kim shampan to'kib yubordi?Biz shunchaki... birga ichib o'tganmiz.

en: … You talk about pouring it into me!” “By way of a fee!
uz: ... Menga quyish haqida gapiryapsan!Agar pul bo'lsa!

en: You profit by everything!” Raskolnikov laughed, “it’s all right, my dear boy,” he added, slapping Zametov on the shoulder.
uz: Siz hamma narsadan foyda ko'rasiz! Raskolnikov kuldi, its all right, my dear boy, u qo'shimcha qilib, Zametovning shoxini urib qo'ydi.

en: “I am not speaking from temper, but in a friendly way, for sport, as that workman of yours said when he was scuffling with Dmitri, in the case of the old woman.
uz: Men g'azabdan emas, balki do'stona, sport uchun gapiryapman, chunki sizning ishchiingiz Dmitriy bilan bahslashganda, keksa ayolning misolida aytganidek, sport uchun gapiryapman.

en: …” “How do you know about it?” “Perhaps I know more about it than you do.”
uz: ... Siz bu haqda qayerdan bilasiz?  Balki men sizdan ko'proq bilimga ega bo'laman.

en: “How strange you are.
uz: Siz qanchalik g'alati ekansiz.

en: … I am sure you are still very unwell.
uz: ...Agar hali ham sog'lig'ingiz yomon bo'lsa, shubhasiz.

en: You oughtn’t to have come out.” “Oh, do I seem strange to you?” “Yes.
uz: Siz chiqmasligingiz kerak edi.  Oh, men sizga g'alati tuyulyapmanmi?  Ha.

en: What are you doing, reading the papers?” “Yes.” “There’s a lot about the fires.” “No, I am not reading about the fires.” Here he looked mysteriously at Zametov; his lips were twisted again in a mocking smile.
uz: Nima qilyapsan, gazetalarni o'qiysan? Ha.  Yong'inlar haqida ko'p narsa bor.  Yo'q, men yong'inlar haqida o'qimayapman. Bu yerda u Zametovga sirli ko'z bilan qaradi; uning og'izlari yana masxara qiluvchi tabassum bilan burildi.

en: “No, I am not reading about the fires,” he went on, winking at Zametov.
uz: "Yo'q, men yong'inlar haqida o'qimaganman", - dedi u, Zametovga ko'z yumib.

en: “But confess now, my dear fellow, you’re awfully anxious to know what I am reading about?” “I am not in the least.
uz: Agar hozir tan olsam, azizim, men nima haqda o'qiyotganimni bilish uchun juda xavotirlanasanmi?Men hech qachon bunday emasman.

en: Mayn’t I ask a question?
uz: Bir savol bersam bo'ladimi?

en: Why do you keep on … ?” “Listen, you are a man of culture and education?” “I was in the sixth class at the gymnasium,” said Zametov with some dignity.
uz: Nima uchun davom etyapsiz ... ?  Quloq soling, siz madaniyat va ta'limga ega odamsiz?  Men gimnaziyada oltinchi sinfda o'qigan edim, dedi Zametov ba'zi martabaga ega bo'lib.

en: Ah, my cock-sparrow!
uz: Ah, mening pichoq-sparrowim!

en: With your parting and your rings —you are a gentleman of fortune.
uz: O'zingizning bo'lishingiz va o'zingizning xaloyiqlaringiz bilan siz omadli bir gentlemansiz.

en: what a charming boy!” Here Raskolnikov broke into a nervous laugh right in Zametov’s face.
uz: Qanday go'zal yigit! Raskolnikov bu yerda Zametovning yuzida g'ayratli tabassumga tushdi.

en: The latter drew back, more amazed than offended.
uz: Keyinchalik ular qochib ketishdi, ko'proq ta'sirlanganidan ko'ra hayratda.

en: how strange you are!” Zametov repeated very seriously.
uz: Siz qanchalik g'alati ekansiz! Zametov juda jiddiy ravishda takrorladi.

en: “I can’t help thinking you are still delirious.” “I am delirious?
uz: Siz hali ham deliriumli ekanligingizni o'ylashdan bosh tortmayman.

en: You are fibbing, my cock-sparrow!
uz: Sen g'iybat qilyapsan, o'g'lim!

en: You find me curious, do you?” “Yes, curious.” “Shall I tell you what I was reading about, what I was looking for?
uz: Meni qiziqarli deb o'ylaysizmi?Ha, qiziqarli. Men sizga nima haqida o'qiganimni, nima qidirayotganimni aytsam bo'ladimi?

en: See what a lot of papers I’ve made them bring me.
uz: Ko'ring, men uchun qancha qog'ozlar olib kelganman.

en: Suspicious, eh?” “Well, what is it?” “You prick up your ears?” “How do you mean —‘prick up my ears’?” “I’ll explain that afterwards, but now, my boy, I declare to you … no, better ‘I confess’ … No, that’s not right either; ‘I make a deposition and you take it.’ I depose that I was reading, that I was looking and searching.
uz: Shubhasizmi, eh?  Xo'sh, nima?  Siz quloqlaringizni tikasizmi?   Qanday qilib  Quloqlarimni tikasizmi?  Keyinroq tushuntirib beraman, lekin endi, o'g'lim, sizga e'lon qilaman ... yo'q, yaxshiroq  Men tanqid qilaman ... Yo'q, bu ham to'g'ri emas;  Men guvohlik beraman va siz uni qabul qilasiz. Men o'qiganimni, qidirganimni va qidirganimni bildiraman.

en: …” he screwed up his eyes and paused.
uz: ... ko'zlarini to'xtatdi va to'xtadi.

en: “I was searching —and came here on purpose to do it —for news of the murder of the old pawnbroker woman,” he articulated at last, almost in a whisper, bringing his face exceedingly close to the face of
uz: Men qidirayotgan edim  va bu yerga niyat bilan keldim qizgi qarzdor ayolning o'ldirilishi haqidagi yangilik uchun, u nihoyat, deyarli shov-shuv bilan so'zlab berdi, yuzini o'zining yuziga juda yaqinlashtirdi

en: Zametov looked at him steadily, without moving or drawing his face away.
uz: Zametov unga qat'iy nazar ko'rsatdi, hech qanday harakatlanmasdan yoki yuz o'girmasdan.

en: What struck Zametov afterwards as the strangest part of it all was that silence followed for exactly a minute, and that they gazed at one another all the while.
uz: Keyinchalik Zametovga eng g'alati narsa shundaki, ular bir daqiqa davomida bir-birlariga qarab turishgan edi.

en: “What if you have been reading about it?” he cried at last, perplexed and impatient.
uz: Agar siz bu haqda o'qigan bo'lsangiz-chi? U nihoyat g'alati va sabr-toqatsiz yig'ladi.

en: “That’s no business of mine!
uz: Bu mening ishim emas!

en: What of it?” “The same old woman,” Raskolnikov went on in the same whisper, not heeding Zametov’s explanation, “about whom you were talking in the police-office, you remember, when I fainted.
uz: Xo'sh, nima bo'ldi? Xuddi shu keksa ayol, Raskolnikov xuddi shu shov-shuv bilan davom etdi, Zametovning tushuntirishiga e'tibor bermadi, siz politsiya ofisida kim haqida gapirganingizni eslaysiz, esingizda bo'lsa, men bayonday qoldim.

en: Well, do you understand now?” “What do you mean?
uz: Xo'sh, endi tushunyapsizmi?Siz nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?

en: Understand … what?” Zametov brought out, almost alarmed.
uz: Shuni tushuning... nima? Zametov ko'tarildi, deyarli xavotirga tushdi.

en: Raskolnikov’s set and earnest face was suddenly transformed, and he suddenly went off into the same nervous laugh as before, as though utterly unable to restrain himself.
uz: Raskolnikovning qatʼiy va gʻayratli yuzi toʻsatdan oʻzgarib ketdi va u xuddi avvalgidek gʻalati kulishga tushdi, xuddi oʻzini toʻxtata olmasdek.

en: And in one flash he recalled with extraordinary vividness of sensation a moment in the recent past, that moment when he stood with the axe behind the door, while the latch trembled and the men outside swore and shook it, and he had a sudden desire to shout at them, to swear at them, to put out his tongue at them, to mock them, to laugh, and laugh, and laugh!
uz: Va bir marta u yaqindagi bir paytni, eshik ortida o'sha o'g'ir bilan turganini, qulflar titrab, tashqarida turgan odamlar qasam ichib, shiddat bilan shiddat bilan esladi va u ularga qichqirish, qasam ichish, tilini uzatish, masxara qilish, kulish, kulish va kulish istagi paydo bo'ldi!

en: “You are either mad, or …” began Zametov, and he broke off, as though stunned by the idea that had suddenly flashed into his mind.
uz: Yoki siz g'alati bo'lib ketasiz, yoki ... Zametov boshlandi va u o'z fikridan g'alati o'tib, o'zini to'xtatib qo'ydi.

en: Come, tell me!” “Nothing,” said Zametov, getting angry, “it’s all nonsense!” Both were silent.
uz: Keling, menga ayting! Hech narsa, dedi Zametov, g'azablanib, bularning barchasi g'alati gaplar! Ikkalasi ham sukut saqlashdi.

en: After his sudden fit of laughter Raskolnikov became suddenly thoughtful and melancholy.
uz: Raskolnikov o'zining to'satdan kulganidan so'ng, to'satdan o'ylab ko'rib, melanxol bo'ldi.

en: He put his elbow on the table and leaned his head on his hand.
uz: U qo'lqoshini stol ustiga qo'ydi va boshini qo'liga tikdi.

en: He seemed to have completely forgotten Zametov.
uz: Zametovni butunlay unutib qo'yganiga o'xshaydi.

en: The silence lasted for some time.
uz: Shoshilish bir muncha vaqt davom etdi.

en: “Why don’t you drink your tea?
uz: Nima uchun siz o'zingizning choyingizni ichmaysiz?

en: It’s getting cold,” said Zametov.
uz: Soyuq bo'lib bormoqda, - dedi Zametov.

en: …” Raskolnikov sipped the glass, put a morsel of bread in his mouth and, suddenly looking at Zametov, seemed to remember everything and pulled himself together.
uz: ... Raskolnikov shishaga ichdi, og'ziga nonni qo'ydi va to'satdan Zametovga qarab, hamma narsani eslab, o'zini yig'ib oldi.

en: At the same moment his face resumed its original mocking expression.
uz: Shu paytning o'zida uning yuzi o'zining asl masxara qilish ifodasini tikladi.

en: He went on drinking tea.
uz: U choy ichishni davom ettirdi.

en: “There have been a great many of these crimes lately,” said Zametov.
uz: "So'nggi paytlarda bunday jinoyatlarning ko'pligi sodir bo'ldi", - dedi Zametov.

en: “Only the other day I read in the Moscow News that a
uz: Mana bir kun oldin Moskva Xabarlarida o'qiganimda, a

en: whole gang of false coiners had been caught in Moscow.
uz: Moskvada soxta pul to'lovchilari to'liq to'plangan.

en: It was a regular society.
uz: Bu odatdagi jamiyat edi.

en: They used to forge tickets!” “Oh, but it was a long time ago!
uz: Ular avval chiptalarni soxtalashtirishardi!Oh, lekin bu ancha vaqt oldin edi!

en: I read about it a month ago,” Raskolnikov answered calmly.
uz: Bir oy oldin bu haqda o'qiganimda, Raskolnikov tinch javob berdi.

en: “So you consider them criminals?” he added, smiling.
uz: - Shunday qilib, siz ularni jinoyatchi deb hisoblayapsizmi? - dedi u tabassum bilan qo'shimcha qilib.

en: “Of course they are criminals.” “They?
uz: Albatta ular jinoyatchilardir. Ular?

en: They are children, simpletons, not criminals!
uz: Ular bolalar, begonalar, jinoyatchilar emas!

en: Why, half a hundred people meeting for such an object —what an idea!
uz: Nima uchun, bunday ob'ekt uchun yarim yuz odam yig'ilgan?Qanday g'oya!

en: Three would be too many, and then they want to have more faith in one another than in themselves!
uz: Uch kishi juda ko'p bo'ladi va ular o'zlariga emas, bir-biriga ko'proq ishonishni xohlashadi!

en: One has only to blab in his cups and it all collapses.
uz: Faqatgina ko'chalari bilan to'qnashish kerak bo'lsa, hamma narsa buzib ketadi.

en: They engaged untrustworthy people to change the notes —what a thing to trust to a casual stranger!
uz: Ular noto'g'ri odamlarni noto'g'ri yozuvlarni o'zgartirishga jalb qilishdi Qaysi bir narsaga befarq odamga ishonish kerak!

en: Well, let us suppose that these simpletons succeed and each makes a million, and what follows for the rest of their lives?
uz: Keling, bu oddiy odamlar muvaffaqiyatga erishganini va har biri million pul topganini tasavvur qilaylik va ularning hayoti davomida nima bo'ladi?

en: Each is dependent on the others for the rest of his life!
uz: Har bir kishi o'z hayoti davomida bir-biriga bog'liq bo'ladi!

en: Better hang oneself at once!
uz: O'zingizni birdan asrash yaxshiroqdir!

en: And they did not know how to change the notes either; the man who changed the notes took five thousand roubles, and his hands trembled.
uz: Ular ham notalarni o'zgartirishni bilmas edilar; notalarni o'zgartirgan kishi besh ming rubl pul oldi va qo'llari titrab qoldi.

en: He counted the first four thousand, but did not count the fifth thousand —he was in such a hurry to get the money into his pocket and run away.
uz: U dastlabki to'rt mingni hisoblab chiqdi, lekin beshinchi mingni hisoblamadi.U pulni qopqoqlariga qo'yib, qochib ketish uchun juda shoshgan edi.

en: Of course he roused suspicion.
uz: Albatta, u shubha uyg'otdi.

en: And the whole thing came to a crash through one fool!
uz: Va butun ish bir ahmoqdan kelib tushdi!

en: Is it possible?” “That his hands trembled?” observed Zametov, “yes, that’s quite possible.
uz: Bu mumkinmi?   Uning qo'llari titragan? Zametov ta'kidladi,   ha, bu mumkin.

en: That, I feel quite sure, is possible.
uz: O'zimni shubhasiz his qilamanki, bu mumkin.

en: Sometimes one can’t stand things.” “Can’t stand that?” “Why, could you stand it then?
uz: Ba'zan inson biror narsaga chiday olmaydi.Buni chiday olmaydi.Nega, o'sha paytda siz chiday olasizmi?

en: For the sake of a hundred roubles to face such a terrible experience?
uz: Bunday dahshatli tajribadan bahramand bo'lish uchun yuz rubl uchunmi?

en: To go with false notes into a bank where it’s their business to spot that sort of thing!
uz: Soxta qog'ozlar bilan bankka borishni, bunday narsalarni aniqlash ularning ishi bo'lgan joyda!

en: No, I should not have the face to do it.
uz: Yo'q, men buni qilishga jur'at qilmasam kerak.

en: Would you?” Raskolnikov had an intense desire again “to put his tongue out.” Shivers kept running down his spine.
uz: Raskolnikov yana tilini chiqarib o'tirishni juda istaydi. Shivers o'zining cho'qqisidan yurib borardi.

en: “I should do it quite differently,” Raskolnikov began.
uz: Men buni boshqacha tarzda qilishim kerak edi, Raskolnikov boshladi.

en: “This is how I would change the notes: I’d count the first thousand three or four times backwards and forwards, looking at every note and then I’d set to the second thousand; I’d count that halfway through and then hold some fifty-rouble note to the light, then turn it, then hold it to the light again —to see whether it was a good one.
uz: Notalarni shunday o'zgartirardim: birinchi mingni uch yoki to'rt marta oldinga va orqaga qarab, har bir nuqtaga qarab, keyin ikkinchi mingga o'taman; o'rta yo'lda o'sha nuqtalarni sanab, keyin bir necha ellik rubllik nuqtalarni yorug'likka qo'yib qo'yaman, so'ngra aylantirib, keyin yana yorug'likka qo'yib ko'raman, yaxshi bo'ladimi yoki yo'qmi.

en: ‘I am afraid,’ I would say, ‘a
uz: I'm afraid, I'd say, a

en: relation of mine lost twenty-five roubles the other day through a false note,’ and then I’d tell them the whole story.
