uz: Mening qarindoshim o'tgan kun noto'g'ri yozuv orqali yigirma besh rubl yo'qotdi va keyin men ularga butun hikoyani aytib berardim.

en: And after I began counting the third, ‘No, excuse me,’ I would say, ‘I fancy I made a mistake in the seventh hundred in that second thousand, I am not sure.’ And so I would give up the third thousand and go back to the second and so on to the end.
uz: Uchinchisini sanay boshlaganimdan so'ng, Yo'q, kechiring, Men shunday deyardim, Men o'zimni o'zim bilmayman, chunki ikkinchi mingda yettinchi yuzda xato qildim. Shunday qilib, uchinchi mingdan voz kechib, ikkinchi mingga qaytardim va shu bilan birga oxirigacha davom etardim.

en: And when I had finished, I’d pick out one from the fifth and one from the second thousand and take them again to the light and ask again, ‘Change them, please,’ and put the clerk into such a stew that he would not know how to get rid of me.
uz: Ishni tugatganimda, beshinchi va ikkinchi mingdan birini tanlab, ularni yana yorug'likka olib borardim va yana so'radim: "Ularni o'zgartiring, iltimos", - deb, xizmatkorni meni qanday yo'q qilishni bilmaydigan darajada qo'yib qo'ydim.

en: When I’d finished and had gone out, I’d come back, ‘No, excuse me,’ and ask for some explanation.
uz: Ishni tugatganimda va ketganimda, qaytib kelib: "Yo'q, uzr so'rayman", deb tushuntirish so'rayman.

en: That’s how I’d do it.” “Foo!
uz: Men buni shunday qilishim mumkin.  Foo!

en: what terrible things you say!” said Zametov, laughing.
uz: Qani, qanday dahshatli so'zlar aytasiz! - dedi Zametov, kulish bilan.

en: “But all that is only talk.
uz: Ammo bularning hammasi faqatgina gap-so'z.

en: I dare say when it came to deeds you’d make a slip.
uz: Ishlarga kelganda, siz xato qilsangiz, deb aytishga jur'at qilaman.

en: I believe that even a practised, desperate man cannot always reckon on himself, much less you and I.
uz: O'zimga ishonamanki, hatto tajribali, umidsiz odam ham o'z-o'zidan to'liq umid bog'lay olmaydi, biz ham, siz ham hech qachon umidga ega bo'lmaymiz.

en: To take an example near home —that old woman murdered in our district.
uz: Masalan, uyimiz yaqinida o'sha keksa ayol bizning tumanimizda o'ldirilgan.

en: The murderer seems to have been a desperate fellow, he risked everything in open daylight, was saved by a miracle —but his hands shook, too.
uz: Qotil umidsiz odam bo'lgan ko'rinadi, u kun yorug'ligida hamma narsasini xavf ostiga qo'ydi, mo'jiza bilan qutqardi, lekin qo'llari ham titradi.

en: He did not succeed in robbing the place, he couldn’t stand it.
uz: U o'sha joyni talon-toroj qilishga muvaffaq bo'lmadi, uni to'xtatolmadi.

en: That was clear from the …” Raskolnikov seemed offended.
uz: Raskolnikovning bu so'zlaridan aniq ko'rinib turganidek, u xafa bo'ldi.

en: Why don’t you catch him then?” he cried, maliciously gibing at Zametov.
uz: Nima uchun uni to'qnashtirmaysiz? - deb yig'ladi u, Zametovga yomonlik bilan qarab.

en: “Well, they will catch him.” “Who?
uz: Ehtimol, uni tutishadi.  Kim?

en: Do you suppose you could catch him?
uz: Uni ushlab qolish mumkin deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: A great point for you is whether a man is spending money or not.
uz: Siz uchun katta masala shundaki, erkak kishi pul sarflaydi yoki yo'q.

en: If he had no money and suddenly begins spending, he must be the man.
uz: Agar u pulsiz bo'lib, to'satdan sarflashni boshlasa, u odam bo'lishi kerak.

en: So that any child can mislead you.” “The fact is they always do that, though,” answered Zametov.
uz: Shunday qilib, har qanday bola sizni yo'ldan ozdirishi mumkin.  Aslida ular har doim shunday qilishadi, ammo, Zametov javob berdi.

en: “A man will commit a clever murder at the risk of his life and then at once he goes drinking in a tavern.
uz: Bir kishi o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'z hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'zining hayotini xavf ostiga qo'yib, o'zining hayotini xavf ostiga qo'ydi.

en: They are caught spending money, they are not all as cunning as you are.
uz: Ular pul sarflashda tutilishadi, ularning hammasi siz kabi hiylachan emas.

en: You wouldn’t go to a tavern, of course?” Raskolnikov frowned and looked steadily at Zametov.
uz: Siz, albatta, tavernga bormaysizmi? Raskolnikov yuz o'girib, Zametovga qat'iy nazar solgan.

en: “You seem to enjoy the subject and would like to know how I should behave in that case, too?” he asked with displeasure.
uz: Siz mavzudan zavqlanyapsiz va men ham shunday holatda qanday yo'l tutishim kerakligini bilishni xohlaysiz? deb so'radi u norozilik bilan.

en: “I should like to,” Zametov answered firmly and seriously.
uz: Men xohlayman, Zametov qat'iy va jiddiy javob berdi.

en: Somewhat too much earnestness began to appear in his words and looks.
uz: Uning so'zlari va ko'rinishlarida juda ko'p g'ayrat paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Very much?” “Very much!” “All right then.
uz: Chindan ham ko'p? Chindan ham ko'p!  O'sha paytda hamma narsa yaxshi.

en: This is how I should behave,” Raskolnikov began, again bringing his face close to Zametov’s, again staring at him and speaking in a whisper, so that the latter positively shuddered.
uz: Raskolnikov yana Zametovga yaqinlashdi, yana unga tikilib qarab, shoshib gapirdi, shunda Zametov shubhalandi.

en: “This is what I should have done.
uz: Men aynan shu ishni qilishim kerak edi.

en: I should have taken the money and jewels, I should have walked out of there and have gone straight to some deserted place with fences round it and scarcely anyone to be seen, some kitchen garden or place of that sort.
uz: Pul va zargarliklarni olib, u yerdan chiqib, to'g'ri yo'lga chiqishim kerak edi, atrofida to'siqlar bo'lgan va hech kim ko'rinmaydigan, biron bir oshxona bog'i yoki shunga o'xshash joyga.

en: I should have looked out beforehand some stone weighing a hundredweight or more which had been lying in the corner from the time the house was built.
uz: Uy qurilganidan beri burchada yotgan yuz va undan ko'proq og'irligi bo'lgan toshni oldindan ko'rib chiqishim kerak edi.

en: I would lift that stone —there would sure to be a hollow under it, and I would put the jewels and money in that hole.
uz: O'sha toshni ko'tarib olsam, uning ostiga chuqurlik paydo bo'ladi va o'sha toshga marvaridlar va pulni qo'ydim.

en: Then I’d roll the stone back so that it would look as before, would press it down with my foot and walk away.
uz: So'ngra toshni avvalgidek ko'rinishi uchun qaytarib qo'ydim, oyoqlarim bilan bosaman va ketaman.

en: And for a year or two, three maybe, I would not touch it.
uz: Va bir yoki ikki yil, uch yil, ehtimol, men unga qo'l tegizmayman.

en: And, well, they could search!
uz: Va, allaqachon, ular qidirib topishlari mumkin!

en: There’d be no trace.” “You are a madman,” said Zametov, and for some reason he too spoke in a whisper, and moved away from Raskolnikov, whose eyes were glittering.
uz: Hech qanday iz yo'q.Siz aqldan ozgansiz, dedi Zametov, va nima sababdan u ham shoshib gapirdi va Raskolnikovdan uzoqlashdi, uning ko'zlari shinam edi.

en: He had turned fearfully pale and his upper lip was twitching and quivering.
uz: U qo'rqinchli bo'lib o'tdi va uning yuqori og'zasi titraydi va titraydi.

en: He bent down as close as possible to Zametov, and his lips began to move without uttering a word.
uz: U Zametovga iloji boricha yaqinroq yiqilib, og'izlari bir so'z ham aytmasdan harakatlanishni boshladi.

en: This lasted for half a minute; he knew what he was doing, but could not restrain himself.
uz: Bu yarim daqiqa davom etdi; u nima qilayotganini bilardi, lekin o'zini tuta ololmadi.

en: The terrible word trembled on his lips, like the latch on that door; in another moment it will break out, in another moment he will let it go, he will speak out.
uz: Uning og'zidan qo'rqinchli so'z titrab turardi, xuddi eshikdagi qulf kabi; boshqa bir daqiqada u tushib ketadi, boshqa bir daqiqada u qo'yib yuboradi, u ovoz chiqarib gapiradi.

en: “And what if it was I who murdered the old woman and Lizaveta?” he said suddenly and —realised what he had done.
uz: Va agar bu keksa ayol va Lizavetani men o'ldirgan bo'lsam nima bo'ladi? dedi u to'satdan va nima qilganini tushundi.

en: Zametov looked wildly at him and turned white as the tablecloth.
uz: Zametov unga vahima bilan qaradi va o'zidan o'ta oq bo'lib qoladi.

en: His face wore a contorted smile.
uz: Uning yuzi buzilgan tabassumni ko'rsatardi.

en: “But is it possible?” he brought out faintly.
uz: Ammo bu mumkinmi? - deb so'radi u zaiflik bilan.

en: Raskolnikov looked wrathfully at him.
uz: Raskolnikov g'azabga to'lib unga qaradi.

en: “Own up that you believed it, yes, you did?” “Not a bit of it, I believe it less than ever now,” Zametov cried hastily.
uz: Siz bunga ishonganingizdan so'ng, shundaymi?  Hech narsa emas, men hozir har qachongidan kamroq ishonaman, Zametov shoshilinch yig'ladi.

en: “I’ve caught my cock-sparrow!
uz: Ive caught my cock-sparrow!

en: So you did believe it before, if now you believe less than ever?” “Not at all,” cried Zametov, obviously embarrassed.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz ilgari bunga ishonardingizmi, agar hozir hech qachon bo'lmaganidan kamroq ishonasizmi? Hech qachon emas, - dedi Zametov, ko'rinib turibdiki, u o'zini noqulay his qildi.

en: “Have you been frightening me so as to lead up to this?” “You don’t believe it then?
uz: Siz meni qo'rqitib, shu yo'lni qo'zg'atganmisiz? Siz bunga ishonmayapsizmi?

en: What were you talking about behind my back when I went out of the police-office?
uz: Politsiya xonadonidan chiqib ketayotganimda, mening orqamda nima haqida gapirgan edingiz?

en: And why did the explosive lieutenant question me after I fainted?
uz: Va nega o'zim bayondashganimdan so'ng, portlovchi hujumchi meni so'roq qildi?

en: Hey, there,” he shouted to the waiter, getting up and taking his cap, “how much?” “Thirty kopecks,” the latter replied, running up.
uz: Qani, u kelerga qichqirdi, turib, to'pini olibdi, qancha?O'ttiz kopek, so'nggilari javob berdi, yugurib bordi.

en: “And there is twenty kopecks for vodka.
uz: Va vodka uchun yigirma kopek pul bor.

en: See what a lot of money!” he held out his shaking hand to Zametov with notes in it.
uz: Ko'ring, qancha pul! u Zametovga qo'lini uzatganida, uning ichida yozuvlar bor edi.

en: “Red notes and blue, twenty-five roubles.
uz: Qizil notalar va ko'k, yigirma besh rubl.

en: Where did I get them?
uz: Men ularni qayerdan olganman?

en: And where did my new clothes come from?
uz: Va yangi kiyimim qayerdan paydo bo'ldi?

en: You know I had not a kopeck.
uz: Bilasizmi, mening kopekim yo'q edi.

en: You’ve cross-examined my landlady, I’ll be bound.
uz: Siz uy egasini ko'rib chiqdingiz, meni bog'lab qo'yishadi.

en: … Well, that’s enough!
uz: Xo'sh, bu yetarli!

en: Till we meet again!” He went out, trembling all over from a sort of wild hysterical sensation, in which there was an element of insufferable rapture.
uz: Qayta uchrashmagunimizcha! U bir xil yovvoyi histerik hissiyadan titrab, tashqaridan chiqdi, unda chidamsiz quvonch elementlari bor edi.

en: Yet he was gloomy and terribly tired.
uz: Ammo u juda tushkun va juda charchagan edi.

en: His face was twisted as after a fit.
uz: Uning yuzi fitdan keyin bo'lgani kabi burildi.

en: His fatigue increased rapidly.
uz: Uning charchaganligi tezda oshdi.

en: Any shock, any irritating sensation stimulated and revived his energies at once, but his strength failed as quickly when the stimulus was removed.
uz: Har qanday hayratlanish, har qanday g'azablantiruvchi his-tuyg'u uning energiyasini birdan uyg'otadi va tiriltiradi, ammo uning kuchi stimulus olib tashlanganida ham tezda yo'qoladi.

en: Zametov, left alone, sat for a long time in the same place, plunged in thought.
uz: Zametov yolg'iz qoldirilib, o'sha joyda uzoq vaqt o'tirdi va o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: Raskolnikov had unwittingly worked a revolution in his brain on a certain point and had made up his mind for him conclusively.
uz: Raskolnikov bilmasdan o'z miyasida bir vaqtda inqilobi bo'lib o'tdi va o'zi uchun qat'iy qaror qabul qildi.

en: “Ilya Petrovitch is a blockhead,” he decided.
uz: Ilya Petrovitch - bu blok bosh, - deb qaror qildi u.

en: Raskolnikov had hardly opened the door of the restaurant when he stumbled against Razumihin on the steps.
uz: Raskolnikov mehmonxonaning eshigini ochmaganida, Razumihinni poygachalar ustida uchratdi.

en: They did not see each other till they almost knocked against each other.
uz: Ular bir-birlarini ko'rmaguncha, deyarli bir-birlariga taqillatishdi.

en: For a moment they stood looking each other up and down.
uz: Bir zum ular bir-birlariga qarab turishdi.

en: Razumihin was greatly astounded, then anger, real anger gleamed fiercely in his eyes.
uz: Razumihin juda hayratda qoldi, keyin g'azab, haqiqiy g'azab uning ko'zlariga qizg'in nur sochdi.

en: “So here you are!” he shouted at the top of his voice —“you ran away from your bed!
uz: Mana sen! - dedi u baland ovoz bilan. - Sen o'z yotoqdan qochib ketding!

en: And here I’ve been looking for you under the sofa!
uz: Mana, men seni kanepa ostida qidirib yuribman!

en: We went up to the garret.
uz: Biz garretga bordik.

en: I almost beat Nastasya on your account.
uz: Men deyarli Nastasya-ni sizning hisobingizda mag'lub qildim.

en: And here he is after all.
uz: Va nihoyat, bu erda u bor.

en: What is the meaning of it?
uz: Buning ma'nosi nima?

en: Tell me the whole truth!
uz: Menga butun haqiqatni ayting!

en: “It means that I’m sick to death of you all and I want to be alone,” Raskolnikov answered calmly.
uz: Bu mening hammangizdan o'limgacha bemor ekanligimni va yolg'iz qolishni xohlayotganimni anglatadi,  Raskolnikov xotirjamlik bilan javob berdi.

en: When you are not able to walk, when your face is as white as a sheet and you are gasping for breath!
uz: Yolg'iz yurishga qodir bo'lmaganda, yuzingiz varaqcha kabi oq bo'lganida va nafas olishni xohlayotganingizda!

en: … What have you been doing in the Palais de Cristal?
uz: ... Siz Palais de Cristalda nima qilib yurgansiz?

en: Own up at once!” “Let me go!” said Raskolnikov and tried to pass him.
uz: O'zingni darhol o'zing!  Meni qo'yib yubor! dedi Raskolnikov va uni o'tkazib yuborishga harakat qildi.

en: This was too much for Razumihin; he gripped him firmly by the shoulder.
uz: Bu Razumihin uchun juda ko'p edi; u uni yelkasiga qattiq ushlab qoldi.

en: You dare tell me to let you go?
uz: Siz menga sizni qo'yib yuborishni aytishga jur'at qilasizmi?

en: Do you know what I’ll do with you directly?
uz: Siz bilan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri nima qilishimni bilasizmi?

en: I’ll pick you up, tie you up in a bundle, carry you home under my arm and lock you up!” “Listen, Razumihin,” Raskolnikov began quietly, apparently calm —“can’t you see that I don’t want your benevolence?
uz: Men seni ko'tarib, to'plamga bog'lab, qo'lim ostida uyga olib ketaman va qamab qo'yaman!️ Tinglang, Razumihin, Raskolnikov sekinlik bilan, ko'rinib turganidek, xotirjamlik bilan boshladiœQanday qilib ko'rmaysanki, men sizning mehribonligingizni xohlamayman?

en: A strange desire you have to shower benefits on a man who … curses them, who feels them a burden in fact!
uz: O'zgacha bir istak bo'lib, ularni la'natlaydigan, aslida ularni og'ir his qiladigan odamga foyda keltiradi!

en: Why did you seek me out at the beginning of my illness?
uz: Nima uchun kasalligim boshlanishida menga murojaat qildingiz?

en: Maybe I was very glad to die.
uz: Ehtimol, o'limdan juda xursand edim.

en: Didn’t I tell you plainly enough today that you were torturing me, that I was … sick of you!
uz: Bugun siz meni qiynayotganingizni, men sizdan ... xafa bo'lganimni sizga yetarlicha aniq aytmagan edimmi?

en: You seem to want to torture people!
uz: Siz odamlarni qiynashni xohlayotgandek ko'rinadi!

en: I assure you that all that is seriously hindering my recovery, because it’s continually irritating me.
uz: Sizga shuni ta'kidlaymanki, bularning barchasi mening sog'ayishimga jiddiy xalaqit bermoqda, chunki bu meni doimiy ravishda xafa qilmoqda.

en: You saw Zossimov went away just now to avoid irritating me.
uz: Zossimov meni xafa qilmaslik uchun ketayotganini ko'rdingiz.

en: You leave me alone too, for goodness’ sake!
uz: Meni ham yolg'iz qo'yib keting, Xudoyim!

en: What right have you, indeed, to keep me by force?
uz: Sizda meni kuch bilan ushlab turishga qanday huquq bor?

en: Don’t you see that I am in possession of all my faculties now?
uz: Ko'rmayapsanmi, endi mening barcha qobiliyatlarim bor?

en: How, how can I persuade you not to persecute me with your kindness?
uz: Qanday qilib, qanday qilib sizni mehribonligingiz bilan meni quvg'in qilmasligingizga ishontira olaman?

en: I may be ungrateful, I may be mean, only let me be, for God’s sake, let me be!
uz: Men minnatdorchilik bildirmasligim mumkin, yomon bo'lishim mumkin, faqat menga yo'l qo'y, Xudo uchun, menga yo'l qo'y!

en: Let me be, let me be!” He began calmly, gloating beforehand over the venomous phrases he was about to utter, but finished, panting for breath, in a frenzy, as he had been with Luzhin.
uz: Men bo'lsam, bo'lsam! U tinchlik bilan boshladi, o'zi aytmoqchi bo'lgan zaharli so'zlarga oldindan xursand bo'lib, lekin Luzhin bilan bo'lgani kabi, nafas olishni orzu qilib, tugatdi.

en: Razumihin stood a moment, thought and let his hand drop.
uz: Razumihin bir zum turdi, o'ylab qo'lini tushirdi.

en: “Well, go to hell then,” he said gently and thoughtfully.
uz: Eh, o'shanda jahannamga keting, dedi u muloyimlik va mulohazakorlik bilan.

en: “Stay,” he roared, as Raskolnikov was about to move.
uz: Raskolnikov harakatlanmoqchi bo'lganida, u qichqirib dedi: "To'xtang.

en: Let me tell you, that you are all a set of babbling, posing idiots!
uz: Sizga aytamanki, sizlarning hammangiz gap-so'z qilib, o'yin-kulgi qilib yurgan ahmoqlar to'plami ekansiz!

en: If you’ve any little trouble you brood over it like a hen over an egg.
uz: Agar sizda kichik muammolar bo'lsa, u haqida g'amxo'rlik qilasiz, xuddi tuxumning tuxumini g'amxo'rlik qilgan tuxum kabi.

en: And you are plagiarists even in that!
uz: Sizlar bu borada ham plagiatchilarsiz!

en: There isn’t a sign of independent life in you!
uz: Sizda mustaqil hayotning belgisi yo'q!

en: You are made of spermaceti ointment and you’ve lymph in your veins instead of blood.
uz: Siz spermaceti moyidan yasalgansiz va qonning o'rniga damarlaringizda limfa bor.

en: I don’t believe in anyone of you!
uz: Men sizlardan hech kimga ishonmayman!

en: In any circumstances the first thing for all of you is to be unlike a human
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, sizlarning hammangiz uchun birinchi navbatda insonlardan farq qilish kerak

en: Stop!” he cried with redoubled fury, noticing that Raskolnikov was again making a movement —“hear me out!
uz: To'xtating! u Raskolnikovning yana harakat qilayotganini ko'rib, g'azabini ko'paytirib yubordi! Meni eshittiring!

en: You know I’m having a housewarming this evening, I dare say they’ve arrived by now, but I left my uncle there —I just ran in —to receive the guests.
uz: Bilaman, bugun kechqurun uyimdagilar yig'iladi, ular hozirgacha kelganini aytishga jur'at qilaman, lekin o'g'limni qoldirdim, mehmonlarni qabul qilish uchun o'sha yerga yugurdim.

en: And if you weren’t a fool, a common fool, a perfect fool, if you were an original instead of a translation … you see, Rodya, I recognise you’re a clever fellow, but you’re a fool!
uz: Agar siz ahmoq, oddiy ahmoq, mukammal ahmoq bo'lmasangiz, tarjima o'rniga asl nusxangiz bo'lmasangiz... Rodya, men sizni aqlli odam deb bilaman, lekin siz ahmoqsiz!

en: —and if you weren’t a fool you’d come round to me this evening instead of wearing out your boots in the street!
uz: Agar siz ahmoq bo'lmaganingizda, ko'chalarda poyabzallaringizni kiyishning o'rniga, bugun kechqurun mendan so'rashgan bo'lardingiz!

en: Since you have gone out, there’s no help for it!
uz: Siz chiqib ketgandan beri, buning uchun hech qanday yordam yo'q!

en: I’d give you a snug easy chair, my landlady has one … a cup of tea, company.
uz: Men sizga yoqimli oson o'rindiq berardim, uy egamda bir ... choy finchasi, kompaniya bor.

en: … Or you could lie on the sofa —anyway you would be with us.
uz: Yoki biz bilan birga bo'lganingizda, sofa ustida yotgan bo'lishingiz mumkin.

en: … Zossimov will be there too.
uz: ...Zossimov ham u yerda bo'ladi.

en: Will you come?” “No.” “R-rubbish!” Razumihin shouted, out of patience.
uz: Kelarmisiz? No.  R-rubbish! Razumihin sabr-toqatidan tashqari baqirib yubordi.

en: You can’t answer for yourself!
uz: O'zingiz uchun javob bera olmaysiz!

en: You don’t know anything about it.
uz: Siz bu haqda hech narsa bilmaysiz.

en: … Thousands of times I’ve fought tooth and nail with people and run back to them afterwards.
uz: Men minglab marotaba odamlar bilan to'qnashganman va keyinchalik ularga qaytib borganman.

en: … One feels ashamed and goes back to a man!
uz: ... Bir kishi o'zini sharmanda his qilib, erkak kishiga qaytadi!

en: So remember, Potchinkov’s house on the third storey.
uz: Shunday qilib, esingizda bo'lsin, Potchinkovning uchinchi qavatdagi uyi.

en: Razumihin, I do believe you’d let anybody beat you from sheer benevolence.” “Beat?
uz: Razumihin, men ishonamanki, siz o'zingizning yaxshiliklaringiz tufayli hech kimga sizni urishga yo'l qo'yib berasiz.Beat?

en: I’d twist his nose off at the mere idea!
uz: O'sha g'oya bilan o'z burchini burib yuboraman!

en: Potchinkov’s house, ൥൨, Babushkin’s flat.
uz: Potchinkovning uyi, Babushkinning xonasi.

en: …” “I shall not come, Razumihin.” Raskolnikov turned and walked away.
uz: ... Men kelmayman, Razumihin. Raskolnikov yuz o'girib ketdi va ketib ketdi.

en: “I bet you will,” Razumihin shouted after him.
uz: Shuni bilamanki, siz ham shunday qilasiz, - deb qichqirdi Razumihin uning orqasidan.

en: “I refuse to know you if you don’t!
uz: Agar siz bilmasangiz, men sizni tanishdan bosh tortaman!

en: Stay, hey, is Zametov in there?” “Yes.” “Did you see him?” “Yes.” “Talked to him?” “Yes.” “What about?
uz: Hey, qoling, Zametov u yerda bormi? Siz uni ko'rdingizmi? U bilan gaplashdingizmi??

en: Confound you, don’t tell me then.
uz: Sizni chalg'itdim, o'shanda menga aytma.

en: Potchinkov’s house, ൥൨, Babushkin’s flat, remember!” Raskolnikov walked on and turned the corner into Sadovy Street.
uz: Potchinkovning uyi, Babushkinning xonasi, eslang!Raskolnikov davom etib, burchadan Sadoviy ko'chasiga aylandi.

en: Razumihin looked after him thoughtfully.
uz: Razumihin unga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: Then with a wave of his hand he went into the house but stopped short of the stairs.
uz: Keyin u qo'lini ko'targan holda uyga kirdi, lekin qadam qo'ymagan.

en: “Confound it,” he went on almost aloud.
uz: Buni chalg'itib, u deyarli baland ovoz bilan davom etdi.

en: “He talked sensibly but yet  … I am a fool!
uz: U aqlli gapirgan, ammo hali ham... Men ahmoqman!

en: As if madmen didn’t talk sensibly!
uz: O'sha g'ayritabiiy odamlar aql bilan gapirmasdek!

en: And this was just what Zossimov seemed afraid of.” He struck his finger on his forehead.
uz: Zossimovning qo'rqqan joyi shu edi. U barmog'ini oldiga urdi.

en: “What if … how could I let him go off alone?
uz: Agar... uni yolg'iz qo'yib ketishiga qanday yo'l qo'ysam bo'ladimi?

en: He may drown himself.
uz: U o'zini cho'ktirishi mumkin.

en: … Ach, what a blunder!
uz: Ach, bu qanday xato!

en: I can’t.” And he ran back to overtake Raskolnikov, but there was no trace of him.
uz: I can't. Va u Raskolnikovni orqaga surish uchun qaytib yugurdi, lekin uning izlari yo'q edi.

en: With a curse he returned with rapid steps to the Palais de Cristal to question Zametov.
uz: U la'nat bilan tez qadamlar bilan Palais de Cristalga qaytib keldi va Zametovdan so'roq qildi.

en: Raskolnikov walked straight to X — — Bridge, stood in the middle, and leaning both elbows on the rail stared into the distance.
uz: Raskolnikov to'g'ridan-to'g'ri X   ko'prik tomon yurdi, o'rtaga turdi va ikkala qo'lqusini ham poyezdga tikib, uzoqlikka qaradi.

en: On parting with Razumihin, he felt so much weaker that he could scarcely reach this place.
uz: Razumihin bilan ajralganida u o'zini shunchalik zaif his qildiki, bu yerga barvaqt yetib borolmadi.

en: He longed to sit or lie down somewhere in the street.
uz: U ko'chada bir joyda o'tirishni yoki uxlashni orzu qilardi.

en: Bending over the water, he gazed mechanically at the last pink flush of the sunset, at the row of houses growing dark in the gathering twilight, at one distant attic window on the left bank, flashing as though on fire in the last rays of the setting sun, at the darkening water of the canal, and the water seemed to catch his attention.
uz: Suv ustida egib, u quyosh botishining so'nggi ro'za surishiga, to'planib borayotgan qorong'ilikda qorong'i bo'layotgan uylar qatorlariga, chap qirg'oqdagi uzoqdagi chekkadagi derazalarga mexanik tarzda qarab turardi, qorong'i quyoshning so'nggi nurlarida, kanalning qorong'i bo'lib borayotgan suvlarida xuddi yonib turganidek, suv uning e'tiborini jalb qilgan bo'ldi.

en: At last red circles flashed before his eyes, the houses seemed moving, the passersby, the canal banks, the carriages, all danced before his eyes.
uz: Oxir-oqibat uning ko'z o'ngida qizil to'pkalar paydo bo'ldi, uylar harakatlanayotgandek ko'rindi, o'tishchilar, kanallar, vagonlar uning ko'z o'ngida raqsga tushdi.

en: Suddenly he started, saved again perhaps from swooning by an uncanny and hideous sight.
uz: Toʻsatdan u boshladi, ehtimol yana bir marta gʻayritabiiy va dahshatli koʻrinish tufayli oʻzini oʻldirishdan qutqardi.

en: He became aware of someone standing on the right side of him; he looked and saw a tall woman with a kerchief on her head, with a long, yellow, wasted face and red sunken eyes.
uz: Uning o'ng tomonida kimdir turganini ko'rib qoldi; ko'z o'ngida ko'z o'ngida bo'lgan, uzun, sariq, yorqin yuzli va qizil ko'zlar bilan boshida cho'g'i bor baland bir ayolni ko'rdi.

en: She was looking straight at him, but obviously she saw nothing and recognised no one.
uz: U unga to'g'ri qarab turardi, ammo u hech narsa ko'rmadi va hech kimni tanimadi.

en: Suddenly she leaned her right hand on the parapet, lifted her right leg over the railing, then her left and threw herself into the canal.
uz: Toʻsatdan oʻng qoʻlini parapetga tikladi, oʻng oyoqini paretaga koʻtardi, soʻngra chap qoʻlini qoʻyib, kanalga oʻzini tashladi.

en: The filthy water parted and swallowed up its victim for a moment, but an instant later the drowning woman floated to the surface, moving slowly with the current, her head and legs in the water, her skirt inflated like a balloon over her back.
uz: Bu yovvoyi suv bir zumga bo'lindi va qurbonini yutib yubordi, lekin bir zum o'tib, cho'kkan ayol suv yuziga ko'tarildi, bosh va oyoqlari suvda, cho'nishi orqaga balon kabi ko'tarildi.

en: A woman drowning!” shouted dozens of voices; people ran up, both banks were thronged with spectators, on the bridge people crowded about Raskolnikov, pressing up behind him.
uz: Bir ayol cho'kib ketayotgan! o'nlab ovozlar ovoz chiqardi; odamlar yugurib borishdi, ikkala banki ham tomoshabinlarga to'lib-toshdi, ko'prikda Raskolnikov atrofida to'plangan odamlar uning orqasidan shovqin qildilar.

en: it’s our Afrosinya!” a woman cried tearfully close by.
uz: bu bizning Afrosinya! bir ayol yaqin atrofda yig'lab yig'ladi.

en: kind people, pull her out!”
uz: Yaxshi odamlar, uni olib chiqinglar!

en: “A boat, a boat!” was shouted in the crowd.
uz: Qayiq, qayiq! xaloyiq orasida baqirildi.

en: But there was no need of a boat; a policeman ran down the steps to the canal, threw off his great coat and his boots and rushed into the water.
uz: Ammo qayiqqa ehtiyoj yo'q edi; bir politsiyachi kanalga qadam tashlab, katta kiyimini va poyabzallarini tashlab, suvga cho'kdi.

en: It was easy to reach her: she floated within a couple of yards from the steps, he caught hold of her clothes with his right hand and with his left seized a pole which a comrade held out to him; the drowning woman was pulled out at once.
uz: Unga yetib borish oson edi: u daraxtdan bir necha metr narida suzib borardi, u o'ng qo'li bilan uning kiyimlarini ushlab oldi va chap qo'li bilan qo'shni unga uzatgan ustunni ushlab oldi; cho'kib ketgan ayol darhol olib chiqildi.

en: They laid her on the granite pavement of the embankment.
uz: Ular uni qirg'oqning granit piyodalari ustiga qo'yishdi.

en: She soon recovered consciousness, raised her head, sat up and began sneezing and coughing, stupidly wiping her wet dress with her hands.
uz: Tez orada u ongga qaytdi, boshini ko'tardi, o'tirdi va o'z qo'llari bilan suyuq kiyimini o'chirib qo'ydi.

en: “She’s drunk herself out of her senses,” the same woman’s voice wailed at her side.
uz: U o'zini aqldan ozdirdi, shu ayolning ovozi uning yonida yig'lab yubordi.

en: The other day she tried to hang herself, we cut her down.
uz: Bir kuni u o'zini o'g'irlashga uringanida, biz uni kesib yubordik.

en: I ran out to the shop just now, left my little girl to look after her —and here she’s in trouble again!
uz: Men do'konga yugurib borib, qizog'imni unga g'amxo'rlik qilishga qoldirdim va u yana qayg'uga tushdi!

en: A neighbour, gentleman, a neighbour, we live close by, the second house from the end, see yonder.
uz: Qo'shni, xo'jayini, qo'shni, biz yaqin atrofda yashaymiz, oxirdagi ikkinchi uy, yuqorida ko'ring.

en: …” The crowd broke up.
uz: ... Jamoat bo'linib ketdi.

en: The police still remained round the woman, someone mentioned the police station.
uz: Politsiya ayol atrofida qoldi, kimdir politsiya bo'linmasini eslatib o'tdi.

en: … Raskolnikov looked on with a strange sensation of indifference and apathy.
uz: Raskolnikov g'alati hissiyotga ega bo'lib, befarqlik va befarqlik bilan qarab turdi.

en: “No, that’s loathsome … water … it’s not good enough,” he muttered to himself.
uz: "Yo'q, bu jirkanch ... suv ... bu etarlicha yaxshi emas", - deb o'ziga o'zi o'ylab gapirdi u.

en: “Nothing will come of it,” he added, “no use to wait.
uz: U qo'shimcha qilib aytdi: "Undan hech narsa kelmaydi, kutishning foydasi yo'q.

en: What about the police office … ?
uz: Xo'sh, politsiya idorasi haqida nima deyish mumkin ... ?

en: And why isn’t Zametov at the police office?
uz: Va nima uchun Zametov politsiya idorasida emas?

en: The police office is open till ten o’clock.
uz: Politsiya idorasi soat o'n gacha ochiq.

en: …” He turned his back to the railing and looked about him.
uz: ... U orqaga burildi va atrofini ko'rdi.

en: “Very well then!” he said resolutely; he moved from the bridge and walked in the direction of the police office.
uz: O'sha paytda juda yaxshi! dedi u qat'iy qaror qilib; ko'prikdan chiqib, politsiyaga qarab yurdi.

en: His heart felt hollow and empty.
uz: Uning yuragi o'zidan-o'zidan bo'sh va bo'sh his qilgan.

en: He did not want to think.
uz: U o'ylashni istamadi.

en: Even his depression had passed, there was not a trace now of the energy with which he had set out “to make an end of it all.” Complete apathy had succeeded to it.
uz: Hatto uning tushkunligi ham o'tib ketgan edi, endi u bularning barchasini tugatishga harakat qilgan energiyasining hech qanday izlari yo'q edi. Butun befarqlik unga erishdi.

en: “Well, it’s a way out of it,” he thought, walking slowly and listlessly along the canal bank.
uz: Ehtimol, bu o'zidan chiqib ketish yo'lidir, deb o'yladi u, kanal qirg'og'i bo'ylab asta-sekin yurib.

en: “Anyway I’ll make an end, for I want to.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, men uni tugataman, chunki men xohlayman.

en: … But is it a way out?
uz: Ammo bu bir yo'lmi?

en: What does it matter!
uz: Bu qanday ahamiyatga ega!

en: There’ll be the square yard of space —ha!
uz: Yerning kvadrat yardi bo'ladi!

en: Is it really the end?
uz: Bu haqiqatan ham oxiratmi?

en: Shall I tell them or not?
uz: Men ularga aytishim kerakmi yoki yo'qmi?

en: If I could find somewhere to sit or lie down soon!
uz: Agar tez orada o'tiradigan yoki uxlash uchun joy topsam edi!

en: What I am most ashamed of is its being so stupid.
uz: Eng ko'p uyalganim uning o'ta ahmoqona bo'lgani.

en: But I don’t care about that either!
uz: Ammo bu menga ham ahamiyat bermaydi!

en: What idiotic ideas come into one’s head.”
uz: Birovning boshida qanday ahmoqona g'oyalar paydo bo'ladi.

en: To reach the police office he had to go straight forward and take the second turning to the left.
uz: Politsiyaga yetib borish uchun u to'g'ri oldinga borishi va chapga ikkinchi burishni ko'tarishi kerak edi.

en: It was only a few paces away.
uz: U faqat bir necha qadam uzoqlikda edi.

en: But at the first turning he stopped and, after a minute’s thought, turned into a side street and went two streets out of his way, possibly without any object, or possibly to delay a minute and gain time.
uz: Ammo birinchi burilishda u to'xtadi va bir daqiqa o'ylab, yon ko'chaga aylandi va ikki ko'chadan chiqib ketdi, ehtimol biron bir narsa yo'q, yoki ehtimol bir daqiqa kechiktirib, vaqt topishga harakat qildi.

en: He walked, looking at the ground; suddenly someone seemed to whisper in his ear; he lifted his head and saw that he was standing at the very gate of the house.
uz: U yerga qarab yurganida, to'satdan kimdir uning quloqlariga shovqin aytgandek tuyuldi; boshini ko'tarib, uyning eshigida turganini ko'rdi.

en: He had not passed it, he had not been near it since that evening.
uz: U undan o'tmagan edi, o'sha kechadan beri uning yaqinida ham bo'lmagan edi.

en: An overwhelming, unaccountable prompting drew him on.
uz: Bir katta, mas'ul bo'lmagan harakat uni o'ziga jalb qildi.

en: He went into the house, passed through the gateway, then into the first entrance on the right, and began mounting the familiar staircase to the fourth storey.
uz: U uyga kirdi, darvoza orqali o'tdi, so'ngra o'ng tomondagi birinchi kirish joyidan o'tib, tanish bo'lgan poygachalarni to'rtinchi qavatga ko'tarishni boshladi.

en: The narrow, steep staircase was very dark.
uz: Kichik, tepa qadamlar juda qorong'i edi.

en: He stopped at each landing and looked round him with curiosity; on the first landing the framework of the window had been taken out.
uz: U har bir qirg'oqqa to'xtab, atrofini qiziqish bilan ko'rib turardi; birinchi qirg'oqqa tushib qolganda, deraza ramkalari olib tashlangan edi.

en: “That wasn’t so then,” he thought.
uz: O'shanda bunday bo'lmagan, deb o'yladi u.

en: Here was the flat on the second storey where Nikolay and Dmitri had been working.
uz: Nikolay va Dmitri ishlagan ikkinchi qavatdagi kvartira.

en: “It’s shut up and the door newly painted.
uz: It yopildi va eshik yangi bo'yilgan.

en: So it’s to let.” Then the third storey and the fourth.
uz: Keyin uchinchi va to'rtinchi qavat.

en: “Here!” He was perplexed to find the door of the flat wide open.
uz: Mana! U xonadonning eshigini keng ochilgan holda topib, xafa bo'ldi.

en: There were men there, he could hear voices; he had not expected that.
uz: U yerda erkaklar bor edi, u ovozlarni eshitardi; u buni kutmagan edi.

en: After brief hesitation he mounted the last stairs and went into the flat.
uz: Qisqa shubha ostiga olgach, u so'nggi qadamlarni ko'tarib, xonasiga kirdi.

en: It, too, was being done up; there were workmen in it.
uz: U ham qurilmoqda edi; u yerda ishchilar bor edi.

en: This seemed to amaze him; he somehow fancied that he would find everything as he left it, even perhaps the corpses in the same places on the floor.
uz: Bu uni hayratda qoldirganidek tuyuldi; u hamma narsani qoldirganidek topishini o'ylagan edi, ehtimol hatto to'xtadagi o'sha o'sha joylarda o'lgan jasadlarni ham.

en: And now, bare walls, no furniture; it seemed strange.
uz: Va endi, yalang'och devorlar, mebellar yo'q; bu g'alati ko'rinardi.

en: He walked to the window and sat down on the windowsill.
uz: U darchaga yaqinlashib, darcha ustunida o'tirdi.

en: There were two workmen, both young fellows, but one much younger than the other.
uz: Ikkita ishchi bor edi, ikkalasi ham yosh yigitlar, lekin bittasi ikkinchisidan ancha yosh edi.

en: They were papering the walls with a new white paper covered with lilac flowers, instead of the old, dirty, yellow one.
uz: Ular eski, kirli, sariq rangli qog'ozning o'rniga, lilak gullari bilan qoplangan yangi oq qog'oz bilan devorlarni qog'ozlashtirishdi.

en: Raskolnikov for some reason felt horribly annoyed by this.
uz: Raskolnikov nima sababdan ham bu haqda juda xafa bo'ldi.

en: He looked at the new paper with dislike, as though he felt sorry to have it all so changed.
uz: U yangi gazetaga yoqimsiz qarab, hamma narsa o'zgarganidan xafa bo'lgani uchun xafa bo'lganidek ko'rindi.

en: The workmen had obviously stayed beyond their time and now they were hurriedly rolling up their paper and getting ready to go home.
uz: Ishchilar o'z vaqtlaridan o'tgan bo'lsa kerak va endi ular qog'ozlarini shoshiltirib, uyga qaytishga tayyorlanishardi.

en: They took no notice of Raskolnikov’s coming in; they were talking.
uz: Ular Raskolnikovlarning kirib kelishiga e'tibor bermadilar; ular suhbatlashayotgan edilar.

en: Raskolnikov folded his arms and listened.
uz: Raskolnikov qo'llarini qo'shib, tingladi.

en: “She comes to me in the morning,” said the elder to the younger, “very early, all dressed up.
uz: "U ertalab menga keladi", - dedi katta yoshga, "ko'p erta, hamma kiyim-kechak kiygan.

en: ‘Why are you preening and prinking?’
uz: Nima uchun siz to'ldirib, to'ldirib yurasiz?

en: ‘I am ready to do anything to please you, Tit Vassilitch!’ That’s a way of going on!
uz: Men sizga yoqadigan har qanday ishni qilishga tayyorman, Tit Vassilitch!

en: And she dressed up like a regular fashion book!” “And what is a fashion book?” the younger one asked.
uz: Va u odatdagi moda kitobi kabi kiyinadi!Va moda kitobi nima? - deb so'radi kichikroq.

en: He obviously regarded the other as an authority.
uz: Shubhasizki, u o'zgalarni hokimiyat sifatida ko'rdi.

en: “A fashion book is a lot of pictures, coloured, and they come to the tailors here every Saturday, by post from abroad, to show folks how to dress, the male sex as well as the female.
uz: Moda kitobi ko'plab rasmlar, rang-barang rasmlardir va ular har shanba bu yerdagi tikuvchilarga chet eldan pochta orqali kelib, odamlarga qanday kiyinishni, erkak va ayol jinsini ko'rsatishadi.

en: The gentlemen are generally wearing fur coats and for the ladies’ fluffles, they’re beyond anything you can fancy.” “There’s nothing you can’t find in Petersburg,” the younger cried enthusiastically, “except father and mother, there’s everything!” “Except them, there’s everything to be found, my boy,” the elder declared sententiously.
uz: Odatda, erkaklar pel kiyimlarini kiyishadi va ayollar uchun bular siz o'ylaydigan har qanday narsadan ustun keladi.Peterburgda siz topolmaydigan hech narsa yo'q, yoshroq kishi g'ayrat bilan yig'ladi, ota-onalargina, hamma narsa bor!

en: Raskolnikov got up and walked into the other room where the strong box, the bed, and the chest of drawers had been; the room seemed to him very tiny without furniture in it.
uz: Raskolnikov o'rnidan turib, kuchli quti, yotoq va sovutxona bo'lgan boshqa xonaga kirdi; xonasi unga juda kichkina ko'rinardi, u erda mebellar yo'q edi.

en: The paper was the same; the paper in the corner showed where the case of icons had stood.
uz: Qog'idagi qog'oz xuddi shunday edi; burchakdagi qog'oz ikonalar qutisi qaerda turganini ko'rsatardi.

en: He looked at it and went to the window.
uz: U unga qarab, darcha tomon bordi.

en: The elder workman looked at him askance.
uz: Keksa ishchi unga kamtarlik bilan qaradi.

en: “What do you want?” he asked suddenly.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? deb so'radi u to'satdan.

en: Instead of answering Raskolnikov went into the passage and pulled the bell.
uz: Raskolnikov javob berishning o'rniga yo'lga kirdi va qo'ng'iroqni chaqirdi.

en: The same bell, the same cracked note.
uz: Xuddi shu qo'ng'iroq, xuddi shu buzilgan nota.

en: He rang it a second and a third time; he listened and remembered.
uz: U buni ikkinchi va uchinchi marta o'qib, tinglagan va eslagan.

en: The hideous and agonisingly fearful sensation he had felt then began to come back more and more vividly.
uz: O'shanda u his etgan dahshatli va og'ir darajada qo'rqinchli his-tuyg'ular yanada ko'proq ko'rinishni boshladi.

en: He shuddered at every ring and it gave him more and more satisfaction.
uz: U har bir tuproqdan titragan va bu unga ko'proq mamnuniyat ato etgan.

en: “Well, what do you want?
uz: Xo'sh, siz nima istaysiz?

en: Who are you?” the workman shouted, going out to him.
uz: Siz kimsiz? ishchi qichqirdi va uning oldiga chiqdi.

en: Raskolnikov went inside again.
uz: Raskolnikov yana ichkariga kirdi.

en: “I want to take a flat,” he said.
uz: "Men o'zimga kvartira sotib olishni istayman", - dedi u.

en: “I am looking round.” “It’s not the time to look at rooms at night!
uz: Men atrofimni ko'rib turibman.Bu kechasi xonalarga qarashning vaqti emas!

en: and you ought to come up with the porter.” “The floors have been washed, will they be painted?” Raskolnikov went on.
uz: va siz portiyerni keltirishingiz kerak.  Yerlar yuvilib, bo'yilganmi? Raskolnikov davom etdi.

en: “Is there no blood?” “What blood?” “Why, the old woman and her sister were murdered here.
uz: Qandaq qon bor? Qanaq qon? Nega bu yerda qariya va uning singlisi o'ldirilgan.

en: There was a perfect pool there.” “But who are you?” the workman cried, uneasy.
uz: U yerda mukammal hovuz bor edi. Ammo siz kimsiz? Ishchi qayg'urib, xavotirda qoldi.

en: “Who am I?” “Yes.” “You want to know?
uz: Men kimman?  Ha.  Bilasizmi?

en: Come to the police station, I’ll tell you.” The workmen looked at him in amazement.
uz: Politsiyaga kelinglar, sizga aytaman.Xodimlar unga hayron qarab turishdi.

en: “It’s time for us to go, we are late.
uz: Bu biz uchun ketish vaqti, biz kech.

en: Come along, Alyoshka.
uz: Keling, Alyoshka.

en: We must lock up,” said the elder workman.
uz: Biz qulflashimiz kerak, dedi katta ishchi.

en: “Very well, come along,” said Raskolnikov indifferently, and going out first, he went slowly downstairs.
uz: Chindan ham yaxshi, keling, dedi Raskolnikov befarq holda va birinchi bo'lib chiqib, sekin-sakin pastga tushdi.

en: “Hey, porter,” he cried in the gateway.
uz: Hey, porter, u darvoza oldida yig'ladi.

en: At the entrance several people were standing, staring at the passersby; the two porters, a peasant woman, a man in a long coat and a few others.
uz: Eshikda bir necha kishilar o'tib ketayotganlarni ko'rib turgan edilar; ikkita portiyer, bir fermer ayol, uzun kiyimli kishi va bir necha kishi.

en: Raskolnikov went straight up to them.
uz: Raskolnikov to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ularga yaqinlashdi.

en: “What do you want?” asked one of the porters.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? deb so'ragan kishilardan biri.

en: “Have you been to the police office?” “I’ve just been there.
uz: Siz politsiyaga borganmisiz?Men o'sha yerda edim.

en: What do you want?” “Is it open?” “Of course.” “Is the assistant there?” “He was there for a time.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz?  Bu ochiqmi?  Albatta.  Xizmatchi u erdami?  U bir muncha vaqt u erda bo'lgan.

en: What do you want?” Raskolnikov made no reply, but stood beside them lost in thought.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? Raskolnikov hech qanday javob bermadi, balki ularning yonida o'y-fikr bilan yo'qolgan edi.

en: “He’s been to look at the flat,” said the elder workman, coming forward.
uz: "U xonadonni ko'rib chiqishga borgan", - dedi katta ishchi, o'zini ko'rsatdi.

en: “Which flat?” “Where we are at work.
uz: Qanday kvartira? Biz qayerda ishlaymiz.

en: ‘Why have you washed away the blood?’ says he.
uz: "Nima uchun qonni yuvgansiz?" - deydi u.

en: ‘There has been a murder here,’ says he, ‘and I’ve come to take it.’ And he began ringing at the bell, all but broke it.
uz: U shunday deydi: "Bu yerda bir odam o'ldirilgan va men uni olib ketishga keldim".U qo'ng'iroqni chaqirishni boshladi, ammo uni butunlay buzdi.

en: ‘Come to the police station,’ says he.
uz: U politsiya bo'linmasiga keling, deydi.

en: ‘I’ll tell you everything there.’ He wouldn’t leave us.” The porter looked at Raskolnikov, frowning and perplexed.
uz: Men sizga hamma narsani u erda aytib beraman.U bizni tashlab ketmasdi.Portayer Raskolnikovga ko'z tikib, g'alati ko'rindi.

en: “Who are you?” he shouted as impressively as he could.
uz: - Siz kimsiz? - deb u iloji boricha baland ovoz bilan baqirdi.

en: “I am Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov, formerly a student, I live in Shil’s house, not far from here, flat Number ൢ൥, ask the porter, he knows me.” Raskolnikov said all this in a lazy, dreamy voice, not turning round, but looking intently into the darkening street.
uz: Men Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikovman, ilgari talaba edim, men Shilsning uyida yashayman, bu yerdan uzoq emas, xonadon raqami , chavandozdan so'rang, u meni taniydi. Raskolnikov bularning barchasini kemchi, orzu qiluvchi ovoz bilan aytdi, u o'ziga qarab emas, balki qorong'i ko'chaga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: “Why have you been to the flat?” “To look at it.” “What is there to look at?”
uz: Nima uchun siz xonadonga borgansiz?  Uni ko'rish uchun.  Nimaga ko'rish kerak?

en: “Take him straight to the police station,” the man in the long coat jerked in abruptly.
uz: Uni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri politsiya bo'limiga olib boring, uzoq kiyimli kishi to'satdan kirdi.

en: Raskolnikov looked intently at him over his shoulder and said in the same slow, lazy tones: “Come along.” “Yes, take him,” the man went on more confidently.
uz: Raskolnikov uni yelkasiga ko'tarib, xuddi shunday sekin va shoshib so'zlarni aytdi: Kelib keling.  Ha, uni olib keting, kishi yanada ishonch bilan davom etdi.

en: “Why was he going into that, what’s in his mind, eh?” “He’s not drunk, but God knows what’s the matter with him,” muttered the workman.
uz: Nima uchun u bunga kirgan edi, uning ongida nima bor edi? U mast emas, lekin Xudo biladi, u bilan nima sodir bo'lganini.

en: “But what do you want?” the porter shouted again, beginning to get angry in earnest —“Why are you hanging about?” “You funk the police station then?” said Raskolnikov jeeringly.
uz: Lekin nima istaysiz? portier yana qichqirdi va g'azablanishni boshladi  Nima uchun bu yerda turyapsiz? Siz politsiya bo'limini o'chirib yuborasiz? - dedi Raskolnikov mazax qilib.

en: Why are you hanging about?” “He’s a rogue!” shouted the peasant woman.
uz: Nima uchun bu yerda aylanib yuribsiz? U bir qotil! deb baqirdi qishloq xonadoni.

en: “Why waste time talking to him?” cried the other porter, a huge peasant in a full open coat and with keys on his belt.
uz: Nima uchun u bilan suhbatlashishga vaqt sarflash kerak? - deb qayg'urdi boshqa chavandoz, to'liq ochiq kiyimda va qo'llarida kalitlar bo'lgan ulkan qishloq xo'jaligi.

en: He is a rogue and no mistake.
uz: U o'ziga yarasha odam va hech qanday xato qilmaydi.

en: Get along!” And seizing Raskolnikov by the shoulder he flung him into the street.
uz: Va Raskolnikovni shoxidan ushlab, ko'chaga tashladi.

en: He lurched forward, but recovered his footing, looked at the spectators in silence and walked away.
uz: U o'zini oldinga ko'tardi, lekin o'z qadamlarini tikladi, tomoshabinlarga sukutdan qarab ketdi va ketib ketdi.

en: “Strange man!” observed the workman.
uz: Qizig'i odam! ishchiga e'tibor qaratdi.

en: “There are strange folks about nowadays,” said the woman.
uz: Bugun odamlar orasida g'alati odamlar bor,  dedi ayol.

en: “You should have taken him to the police station all the same,” said the man in the long coat.
uz: Siz uni politsiyaga olib ketishingiz kerak edi, - dedi uzun kiyimli kishi.

en: “Better have nothing to do with him,” decided the big porter.
uz: U bilan hech qanday aloqasi bo'lmasligi yaxshiroq,  deb qaror qildi katta porter.

en: Just what he wants, you may be sure, but once take him up, you won’t get rid of him.
uz: U nimani xohlasa, shubhasiz, lekin bir marta uni ko'tarib olsangiz, undan qutulmaysiz.

en: … We know the sort!” “Shall I go there or not?” thought Raskolnikov, standing in the middle of the thoroughfare at the crossroads, and he looked about him, as though expecting from someone a decisive word.
uz: ... Biz o'sha turni bilamiz! Men u yerga borishim kerakmi yoki yo'qmi? Raskolnikov yo'l chekkasida yo'lning o'rtasida turib, atrofini ko'rdi va kimgadir aniq so'zni kutgandek atrofini ko'rdi.

en: But no sound came, all was dead and silent like the stones on which he walked, dead to him, to him alone.
uz: Ammo hech qanday tovush eshitilmadi, hamma narsa o'lik va o'zi o'zi uchun o'lgan, o'zi uchun yolg'iz o'tirgan toshlar kabi bevafo edi.

en: … All at once at the end of the street, two hundred yards away, in the gathering dusk he saw a crowd and heard talk and shouts.
uz: ... Birdan yo'lning oxirida, ikki yuz metr masofada, yig'ilgan tongda u bir to'plamni ko'rdi va gap-so'zlarni eshitdi va qichqiriqlarni eshitdi.

en: In the middle of the crowd stood a carriage.
uz: Jamoatning o'rtasida aravacha turdi.

en: … A light gleamed in the middle of the street.
uz: ...Ushbu yo'lning o'rtasiga yorug'lik parlashdi.

en: “What is it?” Raskolnikov turned to the right and went up to the crowd.
uz: Nima? Raskolnikov o'ng tomonga burildi va xaloyiqqa chiqib ketdi.

en: He seemed to clutch at everything and smiled coldly when he
uz: U hamma narsaga bog'lanib qolgan va sovuq tabassum bilan tabassum qilgan edi.

en: recognised it, for he had fully made up his mind to go to the police station and knew that it would all soon be over.
uz: U buni tan oldi, chunki u politsiya bo'linmasiga borishga to'liq qaror qildi va bularning hammasi tez orada tugagani ma'lum edi.

en: VII An elegant carriage stood in the middle of the road with a pair of spirited grey horses; there was no one in it, and the coachman had got off his box and stood by; the horses were being held by the bridle.
uz: VII. Yo'lning o'rtasida bir nechta chiroyli oq otlar bilan birga arzon arava turdi; u yerda hech kim yo'q edi va vagonchi qutidan chiqib, yonida turdi; atlar chiroqqa qo'yilgan edi.

en: … A mass of people had gathered round, the police standing in front.
uz: ... Odamlarning ko'pchiligi to'planib, politsiya oldinda turibdi.

en: One of them held a lighted lantern which he was turning on something lying close to the wheels.
uz: Ulardan biri yonayotgan chiroqni ushlab, velosipedlar yonida turgan bir narsaga yonib qo'ygan edi.

en: Everyone was talking, shouting, exclaiming; the coachman seemed at a loss and kept repeating: “What a misfortune!
uz: Hammasi gaplashib, qichqirishdi, qichqirishardi; haydovchi o'zini yo'qotib qolganidek his qilib, takrorlashdi: "Qanday baxtsizlik!

en: Good Lord, what a misfortune!” Raskolnikov pushed his way in as far as he could, and succeeded at last in seeing the object of the commotion and interest.
uz: Rabbim, naqadar baxtsizlik! Raskolnikov iloji boricha ko'proq harakat qilib, nihoyat g'azab va qiziqishning ob'ektini ko'rishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: On the ground a man who had been run over lay apparently unconscious, and covered with blood; he was very badly dressed, but not like a workman.
uz: Yer yuzida o'g'irlab ketilgan bir kishi, ko'rinib turib, befarq va qon bilan qoplangan edi; u juda yomon kiyimda edi, lekin ishchi kabi emas edi.

en: Blood was flowing from his head and face; his face was crushed, mutilated and disfigured.
uz: Uning boshi va yuzidan qon oqib turardi; uning yuzi cho'kgan, jarohatlangan va ko'rinmas edi.

en: He was evidently badly injured.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, u og'ir jarohatlangan.

en: “Merciful heaven!” wailed the coachman, “what more could I do?
uz: Mercyful heaven! ko'chmachi yig'ladi, what more could I do?

en: If I’d been driving fast or had not shouted to him, but I was going quietly, not in a hurry.
uz: Agar tez haydashgan bo'lsam yoki unga qichqirmagan bo'lsam, lekin shoshilmay, xotirjamlik bilan ketardim.

en: Everyone could see I was going along just like everybody else.
uz: Hamma mening ham boshqalarning o'rnagiga ergashayotganimni ko'rdi.

en: A drunken man can’t walk straight, we all know.
uz: Sarxo'r kishi to'g'ri yurishi mumkin emas, buni hammamiz bilamiz.

en: … I saw him crossing the street, staggering and almost falling.
uz: U ko'chadan kesib o'tganini ko'rdim, qoqinib, deyarli qulab tushdi.

en: I shouted again and a second and a third time, then I held the horses in, but he fell straight under their feet!
uz: Men yana qichqirib, ikkinchi va uchinchi marta, keyin otlarni ushlab turdim, lekin u to'g'ri ularning oyoqlari ostiga tushib qoldi!

en: Either he did it on purpose or he was very tipsy.
uz: Yoki u buni qasddan qilgan bo'lsa, yoki u juda ko'p o'tkir edi.

en: … The horses are young and ready to take fright … they started, he screamed … that made them worse.
uz: ... Atlar yosh va qo'rquvga to'la bo'lgan edilar... ular boshlangan edilar, u qichqirdi... bu ularni yanada yomonlashtirdi.

en: That’s how it happened!” “That’s just how it was,” a voice in the crowd confirmed.
uz: Bu shunday bo'ldi!Bu shunday bo'ldi, deb kafolatlagan xaloyiq orasida bir ovoz.

en: “He shouted, that’s true, he shouted three times,” another voice declared.
uz: U qichqirdi, haqiqatan ham, u uch marta qichqirdi, yana bir ovoz gapirdi.

en: “Three times it was, we all heard it,” shouted a third.
uz: Uch marta bo'ldi, hammamiz eshitdik, uchinchi biri qichqirdi.

en: But the coachman was not very much distressed and frightened.
uz: Ammo haydovchi juda ham xavotirlanmagan va qo'rqmagan.

en: It was evident that the carriage belonged to a rich and important person who was awaiting it somewhere; the police, of course, were in no little anxiety to avoid upsetting his arrangements.
uz: Ko'rinib turganidek, u bir joyda uni kutayotgan boy va muhim odamning vagonasiga tegishli edi; albatta, politsiya uning tartibini buzishdan qochish uchun juda ham xavotirda edi.

en: All they had to do was to take the injured man to the police station and the hospital.
uz: Ular faqat yaralangan kishini politsiya bo'limiga va kasalxonaga olib ketishlari kerak edi.

en: No one knew his name.
uz: Hech kim uning ismini bilmagan.

en: Meanwhile Raskolnikov had squeezed in and stooped closer over him.
uz: Shu bilan birga Raskolnikov o'ziga yaqinlashib, uning ustiga o'tiribdi.

en: The lantern suddenly lighted up the unfortunate man’s face.
uz: Birdan lantern baxtsiz odamning yuzini yoritdi.

en: I know him!” he shouted, pushing to the front.
uz: Men uni taniyman! U qichqirdi va oldinga shovqin qildi.

en: “It’s a government clerk retired from the service, Marmeladov.
uz: Bu xizmatdan pensiyaga chiqqan davlat kotibi Marmeladov.

en: He lives close by in Kozel’s house.
uz: U yaqin atrofda, Kozelning uyida yashaydi.

en: … Make haste for a doctor!
uz: ... Shifokorga shoshiling!

en: I will pay, see?” He pulled money out of his pocket and showed it to the policeman.
uz: Men to'layman, ko'ryapsizmi? U sumkasidan pul chiqarib, uni politsiyachiga ko'rsatdi.

en: He was in violent agitation.
uz: U zo'ravon g'alayonlarda edi.

en: The police were glad that they had found out who the man was.
uz: Politsiya bu odamning kimligini bilib, xursand bo'ldi.

en: Raskolnikov gave his own name and address, and, as earnestly as if it had been his father, he besought the police to carry the unconscious Marmeladov to his lodging at once.
uz: Raskolnikov o'z ismi va manzilini bergan va otasi bo'lgani kabi, u politsiyaga befarq Marmeladovni darhol uning uylariga olib borishni iltimos qilgan.

en: “Just here, three houses away,” he said eagerly, “the house belongs to Kozel, a rich German.
uz: Mana, uchta uydan uzoqlikda, - dedi u hayajon bilan, - bu uy boy nemislik Kozelga tegishli.

en: He was going home, no doubt drunk.
uz: U uyga qaytib borayotgan edi, ehtimol u mast edi.

en: I know him, he is a drunkard.
uz: Men uni bilaman, u ichkilikboz.

en: He has a family there, a wife, children, he has one daughter.
uz: U erda oilasi bor, xotini, bolalari bor, bitta qizi bor.

en: … It will take time to take him to the hospital, and there is sure to be a doctor in the house.
uz: ... Uni kasalxonaga olib ketish uchun vaqt kerak bo'ladi va uyda shifokor bo'lishi shubhasizdir.

en: At least he will be looked after at home … they will help him at once.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda u uyda g'amxo'rlik qilinadi ... ular unga darhol yordam berishadi.

en: But he’ll die before you get him to the hospital.” He managed to slip something unseen into the policeman’s hand.
uz: Ammo siz uni kasalxonaga olib borishdan oldin u o'lib ketadi.U ko'rinmas narsani politsiyachining qo'liga o'tkazishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: But the thing was straightforward and legitimate, and in any case help was closer here.
uz: Ammo bu narsa sodda va qonuniy edi va har holda yordam bu erda yaqinroq edi.

en: They raised the injured man; people volunteered to help.
uz: Ular jarohatlangan kishini tarbiyalashdi; odamlar yordamga ko'maklashish uchun ko'ngilli bo'lishdi.

en: Kozel’s house was thirty yards away.
uz: Kozelning uyi o'ttiz metr masofada edi.

en: Raskolnikov walked behind, carefully holding Marmeladov’s head and showing the way.
uz: Raskolnikov Marmeladovning boshini ehtiyotkorlik bilan ushlab, orqaga qarab yurdi va yo'lni ko'rsatdi.

en: “This way, this way!
uz: Bu yo'ldan, bu yo'ldan!

en: We must take him upstairs head foremost.
uz: Biz uni birinchi navbatda yuqoriga boshimiz bilan olib borishimiz kerak.

en: I’ll pay, I’ll make it worth your while,” he muttered.
uz: Men pul to'layman, men buni sizning vaqtingizga arziydigan qilib qo'yaman", - dedi u.

en: Katerina Ivanovna had just begun, as she always did at every free moment, walking to and fro in her little room from window to stove and back again, with her arms folded across her chest, talking to herself and coughing.
uz: Katerina Ivonovna, har doim ham har bir bo'sh daqiqada qilganidek, o'z xonasi bo'ylab o'z xonasi bo'ylab o'tishni boshlagan edi, darhol o'z qo'llarini ko'krak ustiga qo'yib, o'zi bilan gaplashib, qo'shni tashlab ketar edi.

en: Of late she had begun to talk more than ever
uz: So'nggi paytlarda u har qachongidan ko'proq gapira boshladi.

en: to her eldest girl, Polenka, a child of ten, who, though there was much she did not understand, understood very well that her mother needed her, and so always watched her with her big clever eyes and strove her utmost to appear to understand.
uz: Uning katta qizi Polenkaga, o'n yoshli bolaga, o'zi tushunmagan ko'p narsalar bor bo'lsa-da, onasi unga muhtojligini yaxshi tushunardi va shuning uchun u har doim katta, aqlli ko'zlari bilan uni kuzatib turardi va uni tushunishga harakat qilardi.

en: This time Polenka was undressing her little brother, who had been unwell all day and was going to bed.
uz: Bu safar Polenka butun kun bemor bo'lib, uxlashga ketayotgan kichkina ukasini kiyimidan chiqarib qo'ydi.

en: The boy was waiting for her to take off his shirt, which had to be washed at night.
uz: O'g'il uni kechasi yuviladigan ko'ylagini olib tashlashni kutardi.

en: He was sitting straight and motionless on a chair, with a silent, serious face, with his legs stretched out straight before him —heels together and toes turned out.
uz: U o'tirgan kursi ustida to'g'ri va harakatsiz o'tirgan edi, uning yuzi xotirjam va jiddiy edi, oyoqlari to'g'ri uzilgan edi.

en: He was listening to what his mother was saying to his sister, sitting perfectly still with pouting lips and wide-open eyes, just as all good little boys have to sit when they are undressed to go to bed.
uz: U onasi singlisiga nima deyayotganini tinglab, to'liq o'tirgan edi, og'izlari va ko'zlari ochiq edi, xuddi barcha yaxshi bolalar uxlash uchun kiyimsiz o'tirishi kerak bo'lganidek.

en: A little girl, still younger, dressed literally in rags, stood at the screen, waiting for her turn.
uz: Hatto yoshroq bo'lgan kichkina qizcha, chiroyli kiyim kiygan, ekran oldida o'z navbatini kutgan edi.

en: The door on to the stairs was open to relieve them a little from the clouds of tobacco smoke which floated in from the other rooms and brought on long terrible fits of coughing in the poor, consumptive woman.
uz: Turli xonalardan kirib kelayotgan tamaki tutunining bulutlaridan biroz xalos bo'lish uchun eshik ochilgan edi va kambag'al, iste'molchi ayolda uzoq va dahshatli koshlik urishlariga sabab bo'lgan.

en: Katerina Ivanovna seemed to have grown even thinner during that week and the hectic flush on her face was brighter than ever.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna o'sha hafta davomida yanada kamroq bo'lib, yuzidagi qizg'in ko'rinish har qachongidan ham yorqinroq edi.

en: “You wouldn’t believe, you can’t imagine, Polenka,” she said, walking about the room, “what a happy luxurious life we had in my papa’s house and how this drunkard has brought me, and will bring you all, to ruin!
uz: "Siz ishonmaysiz, tasavvur ham qila olmaysiz, Polenka", - dedi u, xonada yurib, "otamning uyida qanday baxtli, farovon hayot kechirganimizni va bu mast odam meni va sizni ham barchangizni halokatga olib kelganini" aytdi.

en: Papa was a civil colonel and only a step from being a governor; so that everyone who came to see him said, ‘We look upon you, Ivan Mihailovitch, as our governor!’ When I … when …” she coughed violently, “oh, cursed life,” she cried, clearing her throat and pressing her hands to her breast, “when I … when at the last ball … at the marshal’s … Princess Bezzemelny saw me —who gave me the blessing when your father and I were married, Polenka —she asked at once ‘Isn’t that the pretty girl who danced the shawl dance at the breaking-up?’ (You must mend that tear, you must take your needle and darn it as I showed you, or tomorrow —cough, cough, cough —he will make the hole bigger,” she articulated with effort.) “Prince Schegolskoy, a kammerjunker, had just come from Petersburg then … he danced the mazurka with me and wanted to make me an offer next day; but I thanked him in flattering
uz: U fuqarolik polkovniki va gubernator bo'lishdan bir qadam uzoqroq edi; shuning uchun uni ko'rishga kelganlarning barchasi: "Biz sizni, Ivan Mihailovitchni, bizning gubernatorimiz sifatida ko'rib turibmiz! Men ... qachon ... u zo'ravon tushib, oh, hayotni la'natladi,  u yig'lab, qo'lini ko'krakga bosdi,  men ... oxirgi baloda ... marshallarda ... Prinsesa Bezzemelny meni ko'rganimda  kim menga duo qildi, ota va men turmush qurganimizda, Polenka  u bir vaqtning o'zida  U bo'shatish paytida shawl raqsini raqs qilgan go'zal qiz emasmi? (Siz bu sochni tuzatishingiz kerak, siz ignalaringizni olib, uni ko'rsatganimcha, yoki ertaga raqsingiz kerak bo'lsa, raqsingiz kerak, raqsingiz kerak, u toshdi,  Prinsesa  u menga shukr qildi, lekin keyingi kuni men uni katta qilib qo'yganman, lekin keyinchalik men u bilan birga bo'lib kelishimni so'radi, lekin keyingi kunida men uni ko'rmoqni taklif qildim, lekin keyin men unga shukr qildim)

en: expressions and told him that my heart had long been another’s.
uz: O'zimning yuragim uzoq vaqtdan beri boshqacha ekanligini aytdim.

en: That other was your father, Polya; papa was fearfully angry.
uz: Bu kishi sizning otangiz edi, Polya; otangiz qo'rqqancha g'azablangan edi.

en: … Is the water ready?
uz: Suv tayyormi?

en: Give me the shirt, and the stockings!
uz: Menga ko'ylak va choriqlarni bering!

en: Lida,” said she to the youngest one, “you must manage without your chemise tonight  … and lay your stockings out with it … I’ll wash them together.
uz: Lida, u eng kichikga aytdi, sen bu kechasi ko'ylaksiz o'ting va shu bilan choriqlaringni qo'yib qo'ying... Men ularni birga yuvaman.

en: … How is it that drunken vagabond doesn’t come in?
uz: Qanday qilib mast bo'lgan bu ko'chaga kirmaydigan odam kirmaydi?

en: He has worn his shirt till it looks like a dish-clout, he has torn it to rags!
uz: U o'z ko'ylagini kiyib, uni to'qimalarga aylantirib yubordi!

en: I’d do it all together, so as not to have to work two nights running!
uz: Men hammasini birgalikda bajaraman, shunda ikki kecha ketma-ket ishlashim shart emas!

en: (Cough, cough, cough, cough!) Again!
uz: (Qo'shish, qo'shish, qo'shish, qo'shish!) Yana!

en: What’s this?” she cried, noticing a crowd in the passage and the men, who were pushing into her room, carrying a burden.
uz: Bu nima? U yo'ldan o'tishda bir to'p odam va uning xonasiga bir og'irlikni ko'tarib kirib kelayotgan odamlarni ko'rib, yig'ladi.

en: What are they bringing?
uz: Ular nima olib kelishmoqda?

en: Mercy on us!” “Where are we to put him?” asked the policeman, looking round when Marmeladov, unconscious and covered with blood, had been carried in.
uz: Bizlarga rahm qiling! Uni qayerga qo'yamiz? - deb so'radi politsiya boshlig'i, atrofini ko'rib, Marmeladov qon bilan to'lib-toshgan va ongidan o'tib ketayotganini ko'rdi.

en: Put him straight on the sofa, with his head this way,” Raskolnikov showed him.
uz: Uni sofada to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qo'yib, boshini shu yo'l bilan ko'rsatdi, Raskolnikov unga ko'rsatdi.

en: “Run over in the road!
uz: Yo'lda yugurib keting!

en: Drunk!” someone shouted in the passage.
uz: Sarxo'r! kimdir yo'lda qichqirdi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna stood, turning white and gasping for breath.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna to'xtadi, oqlanib, nafas olishni istardi.

en: The children were terrified.
uz: Bolalar qo'rqib ketdi.

en: Little Lida screamed, rushed to Polenka and clutched at her, trembling all over.
uz: Kichik Lida qichqirib, Polenkaga yugurib kelib, qo'lini cho'zdi va qo'rqib ketdi.

en: Having laid Marmeladov down, Raskolnikov flew to Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Marmeladovni yerga tashlagan Raskolnikov Katerina Ivanovnaga uchdi.

en: “For God’s sake be calm, don’t be frightened!” he said, speaking quickly, “he was crossing the road and was run over by a carriage, don’t be frightened, he will come to, I told them bring him here … I’ve been here already, you remember?
uz: Alloh haqi, tinch bo'ling, qo'rqmang! dedi u, tez gapirib, yo'lni kesib o'tganida, arava tomonidan to'qnashgan,  qo'rqmang, u kelib qoladi, men ularga uni bu yerga keltirishlarini aytdim... Men allaqachon bu yerda bo'lganman, eslaysizmi?

en: He will come to; I’ll pay!” “He’s done it this time!” Katerina Ivanovna cried despairingly and she rushed to her husband.
uz: U qaytib keladi, men to'layman! U bu safar buni qildi! Katerina Ivanovna umidsizlikka tushib yig'ladi va erining huzuriga shoshdi.

en: Raskolnikov noticed at once that she was not one of those women who swoon easily.
uz: Raskolnikov tezda uning o'zidan o'zini past olib ketadigan ayollardan emasligini payqadi.

en: She instantly placed under the luckless man’s head a pillow, which no one had thought of and began undressing and examining him.
uz: U darhol omadsiz odamning boshi ostida hech kim o'ylamagan yostiq qo'ydi va uni kiyimidan chiqarib, tekshirib ko'rishni boshladi.

en: She kept her head, forgetting herself, biting her trembling lips and stifling the screams which were ready to break from her.
uz: O'zini unutib, boshini saqlab, titrab turgan dudaklarini urib, o'zidan kesilishga tayyor turgan qichqiriqlarni o'chirib qo'ydi.

en: Raskolnikov meanwhile induced someone to run for a doctor.
uz: Raskolnikov shu vaqt ichida kimdir shifokorga murojaat qilishga undadi.

en: There was a doctor, it appeared, next door but one.
uz: O'shanda yonida bir shifokor bo'lgan, lekin bir kishi bor edi.

en: “I’ve sent for a doctor,” he kept assuring Katerina Ivanovna, “don’t be uneasy, I’ll pay.
uz: Men shifokorni chaqirib yubordim, u Katerina Ivanovnaga: "Xavflanmang, men to'layman", - deb ishontirdi.

en: … and give me a napkin or a towel, anything, as quick as you can.
uz: ... va menga servet yoki charchoq yoki har qanday narsani imkon qadar tezroq bering.

en: … He is injured, but not killed, believe me.
uz: ... U jarohatlangan, ammo o'lgan emas, ishoning.

en: … We shall see what the doctor says!” Katerina Ivanovna ran to the window; there, on a broken chair in the corner, a large earthenware basin full of water had been stood, in readiness for washing her children’s and husband’s linen that night.
uz: ... Shifokor nima deyishini ko'ramiz! Katerina Ivonovna darchaga yugurib bordi; u yerda burchakdagi buzilgan o'rinbosarda, o'sha kecha bolalari va erlarining kiyimlarini yuvishga tayyor bo'lgan, suv bilan to'lgan katta tuproq idish turgan edi.

en: This washing was done by Katerina Ivanovna at night at least twice a week, if not oftener.
uz: Ushbu yuvishni Katerina Ivanovna haftada kamida ikki marta, agar tez-tez emas bo'lsa, kechasi amalga oshirdi.

en: For the family had come to such a pass that they were practically without change of linen, and Katerina Ivanovna could not endure uncleanliness and, rather than see dirt in the house, she preferred to wear herself out at night, working beyond her strength when the rest were asleep, so as to get the wet linen hung on a line and dry by the morning.
uz: Chunki oila o'sha qadar ko'p bo'lganki, ular chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan ham chindan en: She took up the basin of water at Raskolnikov’s request, but almost fell down with her burden.
uz: Raskolnikovning iltimosiga ko'ra, u suv havzasini ko'tardi, ammo deyarli yukini ko'targanida qulab tushdi.

en: But the latter had already succeeded in finding a towel, wetted it and began washing the blood off Marmeladov’s face.
uz: Ammo Marmeladovning o'zi ham to'lqin topib, uni nam qilib, Marmeladovning yuzini qon bilan yuvishni boshlagan edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna stood by, breathing painfully and pressing her hands to her breast.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna yonida turib, og'riqli nafas olib, qo'llarini ko'krakga surib qo'ydi.

en: She was in need of attention herself.
uz: O'zi ham e'tiborga muhtoj edi.

en: Raskolnikov began to realise that he might have made a mistake in having the injured man brought here.
uz: Raskolnikov jarohatlangan kishini bu yerga keltirishda xato qilgan bo'lishi mumkinligini anglay boshladi.

en: The policeman, too, stood in hesitation.
uz: Politsiya xodimi ham shubha ostiga qo'ydi.

en: “Polenka,” cried Katerina Ivanovna, “run to Sonia, make haste.
uz: Poloniya, Katerina Ivanovna so'zladi, Soniyaga yugurib, shoshil.

en: If you don’t find her at home, leave word that her father has been run over and that she is to come here at once … when she comes in.
uz: Agar uni uyda topmasangiz, otasining o'g'lini o'g'irlab ketishganini va u kirganida darhol bu yerga kelishi kerakligini xabar bering.

en: there, put on the shawl.” “Run your fastest!” cried the little boy on the chair suddenly, after which he relapsed into the same dumb rigidity, with round eyes, his heels thrust forward and his toes spread out.
uz: O'sha joyda shawlni kiying.O'zingizning eng tezligi bilan yuguring! O'tirgan kichkina o'g'il to'shagida to'satdan baqirib yubordi, so'ngra u o'sha o'zgacha soqovli qatʼiylikka qaytdi, yuzma ko'zlar bilan, toʻlqinlari oldinga ko'tarilgan va barmoqlari tarqalib ketgan edi.

en: Meanwhile the room had become so full of people that you couldn’t have dropped a pin.
uz: Shu bilan birga, xona shunchalik to'lib-toshganki, bir pinni ham tushirmagan bo'lardingiz.

en: The policemen left, all except one, who remained for a time, trying to drive out the people who came in from the stairs.
uz: Politsiya xodimlari ketishdi, bitta kishidan tashqari, hammasi bir muncha vaqt qoldilar va mertalardan kirib kelgan odamlarni quvib chiqarishga harakat qilishdi.

en: Almost all Madame Lippevechsel’s lodgers had streamed in from the inner rooms of the flat; at first they were squeezed together in the doorway, but afterwards they overflowed into the room.
uz: Deyarli barcha Madam Lippevechselning uy egalari xonaning ichki xonalaridan kirib kelgan edilar; dastlab ular eshikda bir-biriga siqilgan edilar, lekin keyinchalik xonani ko'tarib o'tishdi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna flew into a fury.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna g'azabga tushdi.

en: “You might let him die in peace, at least,” she shouted at the crowd, “is it a spectacle for you to gape at?
uz: Siz uni hech bo'lmaganda tinchlik bilan o'lib ketishiga yo'l qo'yishingiz mumkin, u xaloyiqqa baqirdi,¿Bu siz uchun ko'rinishmi?

en: (Cough, cough, cough!) You might as well keep your hats on.
uz: (Qo'shish, qo'shish, qo'shish!) Siz ham to'plaringizni kiyib qo'yishingiz mumkin.

en: … And there is one in his hat!
uz: Va uning to'pkachasida bir kishi bor!

en: You should respect the dead, at least!” Her cough choked her —but her reproaches were not without result.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda o'liklarga hurmat ko'rsatishingiz kerak! Uning toshi uni cho'ktirgan, lekin uning haqoratlari befoyda bo'lmagan.

en: They evidently stood in some awe of Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Ular Katerina Ivonovnaga bo'lgan ehtiromdan qo'rqishgan.

en: The lodgers, one after another, squeezed back into the doorway with that strange inner feeling of satisfaction which may be observed in the presence of a sudden accident, even in those nearest and dearest to the victim, from which no living man is exempt, even in spite of the sincerest sympathy and compassion.
uz: Uy egalari bir-biridan keyin eshikga qaytib kirishdi va o'sha g'alati ichki mamnunlik hissi bilan, hatto qurbonning eng yaqin va eng yaqin kishilarida ham, hatto eng samimiy hamdardlik va rahm-shafqatga qaramay, hech bir tirik odam bundan ozod emas.

en: Voices outside were heard, however, speaking of the hospital and saying that they’d no business to make a disturbance here.
uz: Biroq, tashqaridagi ovozlar kasalxona haqida gapirib, ular bu yerda tartibsizlikni qo'zg'atishning hech qanday ishi yo'qligini aytishdi.

en: “No business to die!” cried Katerina Ivanovna, and she was rushing to the door to vent her wrath upon them, but in the doorway came face to face with Madame Lippevechsel who had only just heard of the accident and ran in to restore order.
uz: "O'lishga hech qanday ish yo'q!" - deb baqirdi Katerina Ivanovna, ularga g'azabini bildirish uchun eshikga shoshdi, lekin eshikda u halokat to'g'risida eshitgan va tartibni tiklash uchun yugurib kelgan Xonim Lippevechsel bilan yuzma-yuz uchrashdi.

en: She was a particularly quarrelsome and irresponsible German.
uz: Ayniqsa, u bahsli va mas'uliyatsiz nemis edi.

en: “Ah, my God!” she cried, clasping her hands, “your husband drunken horses have trampled!
uz: Ay, Xudoyim! - deb yig'ladi u, qo'llarini bir-biriga bog'lab, - eringiz mast atlar boshiga tushdi!

en: To the hospital with him!
uz: U bilan birga shifoxonaga boramiz!

en: I am the landlady!” “Amalia Ludwigovna, I beg you to recollect what you are saying,” Katerina Ivanovna began haughtily (she always took a haughty tone with the landlady that she might “remember her place” and even now could not deny herself this satisfaction).
uz: Men uy egasiman!  Amaliya Ludwigovna, o'zingizning so'zlaringizni eslab qolishingizni iltimos qilaman, Katerina Ivanovna mag'rurlik bilan boshlandi (o'zi uy egasi bilan har doim mag'rurlik ila gapirgan, ehtimol u o'z joyini eslaydi va hatto hozir ham o'zidan bu mamnuniyatni rad qila olmaydi).

en: “Amalia Ludwigovna …” “I have you once before told that you to call me Amalia Ludwigovna may not dare; I am Amalia Ivanovna.” “You are not Amalia Ivanovna, but Amalia Ludwigovna, and as I am not one of your despicable flatterers like Mr.
uz: Amaliya Ludwigovna ...  Sizga bir marta aytdimki, meni Amaliya Ludwigovna deb atashingizga jur'at etmasligingiz mumkin; men Amaliya Ivanovna.  Siz Amaliya Ivanovna emassiz, balki Amaliya Ludwigovnasiz va men sizning Mr.

en: Lebeziatnikov, who’s laughing behind the door at this moment” (a laugh and a cry of “they are at it again” was in fact audible at the door) “so I shall always call you Amalia Ludwigovna, though I fail to understand why you dislike that name.
uz: Lebeziatnikov, u hozir eshik ortida kulmoqda (koʻplar yana kulishadi) Seni doimo Amaliya Ludwigovna deb atayman, ammo nega bu ismni yoqtirmasligingni tushunmayapman.

en: You can see for yourself what has happened to Semyon Zaharovitch; he is dying.
uz: Semyon Zaharovitch bilan nima sodir bo'lganini o'zingiz ko'rasiz; u o'lib ketyapti.

en: I beg you to close that door at once and to admit no one.
uz: Sizdan iltimos qilaman, darhol eshikni yoping va hech kimni qabul qilmang.

en: Let him at least die in peace!
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda tinchlikda o'lishiga yo'l qo'ying!

en: Or I warn you the Governor-General, himself, shall be informed of your conduct tomorrow.
uz: Yoki sizlarni ogohlantiramanki, bosh gubernatorning o'zi ertaga sizning xulq-atvoringiz haqida xabardor bo'ladi.

en: The prince knew me as a girl; he remembers Semyon
uz: Prince meni bolaligimda tanirdi; u Semyonni eslaydi

en: Zaharovitch well and has often been a benefactor to him.
uz: Zaharovitch yaxshi va ko'pincha unga yaxshilik qilgan.

en: Everyone knows that Semyon Zaharovitch had many friends and protectors, whom he abandoned himself from an honourable pride, knowing his unhappy weakness, but now (she pointed to Raskolnikov) a generous young man has come to our assistance, who has wealth and connections and whom Semyon Zaharovitch has known from a child.
uz: Semyon Zaharovitchning ko'plab do'stlari va himoyachilari borligi hamma uchun ma'lumdir, lekin u o'z zaifligini bilgan holda o'zidan voz kechgan, ammo hozir (Raskolnikovga ishora qilgan) bizga yordamga mehribon yigit keldi, u boylik va aloqalarga ega va Semyon Zaharovitch uni bolaligidan tanigan.

en: You may rest assured, Amalia Ludwigovna …” All this was uttered with extreme rapidity, getting quicker and quicker, but a cough suddenly cut short Katerina Ivanovna’s eloquence.
uz: Siz ishonch hosil qilishingiz mumkin, Amaliya Ludwigovna ... Bularning barchasi juda tez, tezroq va tezroq so'zlandi, lekin kashs ketishi Katerina Ivanovnaning so'zlashuvchanligini to'satdan kesib tashladi.

en: At that instant the dying man recovered consciousness and uttered a groan; she ran to him.
uz: O'tib ketayotgan kishi o'sha zahoti ongga qaytdi va o'ziga qarab yugurdi.

en: The injured man opened his eyes and without recognition or understanding gazed at Raskolnikov who was bending over him.
uz: Yovuz odam ko'zlarini ochib, Raskolnikovni tan olish va tushunishning iloji yo'qligini ko'rib, uning ustiga eglanib turganini ko'rdi.

en: He drew deep, slow, painful breaths; blood oozed at the corners of his mouth and drops of perspiration came out on his forehead.
uz: U chuqur, sekin, og'riqli nafas oldi; og'izning burchaklaridan qon oqib, peshanasiga ter tomchiladi.

en: Not recognising Raskolnikov, he began looking round uneasily.
uz: Raskolnikovni tanimay, u o'z atrofini noqulaylik bilan ko'rishni boshladi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna looked at him with a sad but stern face, and tears trickled from her eyes.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna unga qayg'uli, ammo qattiq yuz bilan qaradi va ko'zlaridan yosh oqib ketadi.

en: His whole chest is crushed!
uz: Uning butun ko'kraklari cho'kgan!

en: How he is bleeding,” she said in despair.
uz: Uning qan ketayotganini ko'rib, u umidsizlikka tushdi.

en: “We must take off his clothes.
uz: Biz uning kiyimlarini olib tashlashimiz kerak.

en: Turn a little, Semyon Zaharovitch, if you can,” she cried to him.
uz: Ozgina buring, Semyon Zaharovitch, iloji bo'lsa, u unga baqirdi.

en: Marmeladov recognised her.
uz: Marmeladov uni tan oldi.

en: “A priest,” he articulated huskily.
uz: A priest, he articulated huskly.

en: Katerina Ivanovna walked to the window, laid her head against the window frame and exclaimed in despair: “Oh, cursed life!” “A priest,” the dying man said again after a moment’s silence.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna derazaga yaqinlashdi, boshini derazaga qo'yib, umidsizlikka tushib: "Oh, la'natlangan hayot! Bir ruhoniy, o'lib ketayotgan kishi bir daqiqadan so'ng yana dedi.

en: “They’ve gone for him,” Katerina Ivanovna shouted to him, he obeyed her shout and was silent.
