en: “Leave off, I entreat you, what are you doing?” Pulcheria Alexandrovna cried, greatly distressed.
uz: Chetib keting, iltimos, nima qilyapsan? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna juda xafa bo'lib yig'ladi.

en: “Get up, get up!” said Dounia laughing, though she, too, was upset.
uz: O'rnidan turing, turing! - dedi Dounia, u ham xafa bo'lsa-da, tabassum bilan.

en: “Not for anything till you let me kiss your hands!
uz: Siz menga qo'lingizni o'pishimga ruxsat bermaguningizcha hech narsa uchun emas!

en: I get up and we’ll go on!
uz: Men turaman va biz davom etamiz!

en: I am a luckless fool, I am unworthy of you and drunk … and I am ashamed.
uz: Men omadsiz ahmoqman, men sizdan kam emasman va mastman ... va men uyatdaman.

en: … I am not worthy to love you, but to do homage to you is the duty of every man who is not a perfect beast!
uz: ... Men sizni sevishga loyiq emasman, lekin mukammal hayvon bo'lmagan har bir odamning sizga hurmat ko'rsatish burchidir!

en: And I’ve done homage.
uz: Va men e'tirof qildim.

en: … Here are your lodgings, and for that alone Rodya was right in driving your Pyotr Petrovitch away.
uz: Mana sizning joylaringiz va faqat shu sababli Rodya sizning Pyotr Petrovitchingizni haydashda to'g'ri yo'l tutgan.

en: how dare he put you in such lodgings!
uz: Qanday qilib u sizni bunday uylarga joylashtirishga jur'at qiladi!

en: Do you know the sort of people they take in here?
uz: Bu yerda qanday odamlarni qabul qilishlarini bilasizmi?

en: And you his betrothed!
uz: Va siz uning niqobchisi!

en: You are his betrothed?
uz: Siz uning kelin-qizisiz?

en: Well, then, I’ll tell you, your fiancé is a scoundrel.” “Excuse me, Mr.
uz: Xo'sh, sizga aytamanki, sizning nişanlovchingiz buzoqqa aylangan. Xullasangiz, Mr.

en: Razumihin, you are forgetting …” Pulcheria Alexandrovna was beginning.
uz: Razumihin, siz unutib qo'yyapsiz... Pulcheria Aleksandrovna boshlanayotgan edi.

en: “Yes, yes, you are right, I did forget myself, I am ashamed of it,” Razumihin made haste to apologise.
uz: Ha, ha, to'g'ri aytasiz, o'zimni unutib qo'ydim, bundan o'zimni o'ylayman,  Razumihin kechirim so'rashga shoshdi.

en: “But … but you can’t be angry with me for speaking so!
uz: Lekin... lekin men bunday gapirganim uchun menga g'azablanmaysiz!

en: For I speak sincerely and not because … hm, hm!
uz: Chunki men samimiylik bilan gapiryapman, chunki... hm, hm!

en: That would be disgraceful; in fact not because I’m in … hm!
uz: Bu sharmandalik bo'ladi; aslida, men... um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um.

en: Well, anyway, I won’t say why, I daren’t.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, nima uchun deymayman, men jasoratim yo'q.

en: … But we all saw today when he came in that that man is not of our sort.
uz: Ammo bugun u kelganida hammamiz ko'rdikki, bu odam biz kabi emas.

en: Not because he had his hair curled at the barber’s, not because he was in such a hurry to show his wit, but because he is a spy, a speculator, because he is a skinflint and a buffoon.
uz: U sochlarini cho'g'irga qo'yib qo'yganligi uchun emas, balki o'z aql-idrokini ko'rsatishga shoshganligi uchun emas, balki u g'ayritabiiy, spekulyator, skinflint va bufoon bo'lgani uchun.

en: Do you think him clever?
uz: Siz uni aqlli deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: No, he is a fool, a fool.
uz: Yo'q, u ahmoq, ahmoq.

en: And is he a match for you?
uz: Va u sizga mos keladimi?

en: Do you see, ladies?” he stopped suddenly on the way upstairs to their rooms, “though all my friends there are drunk, yet they are all honest, and though we do talk a lot of trash, and I do, too, yet we shall talk our way to the truth at last, for we are on the right path, while Pyotr Petrovitch … is not on the right path.
uz: Ko'ryapsizmi, xonimlar? u o'z xonalariga borayotganda to'satdan to'xtadi, haddi u erda barcha do'stlarim ichgan bo'lsa-da, ular hammasi rostgo'y va biz juda ko'p gapirsak ham, men ham shunday qilaman, lekin nihoyat haqiqat yo'liga boramiz, chunki biz to'g'ri yo'ldamiz, Pyotr Petrovitch esa ... to'g'ri yo'lda emas.

en: Though I’ve been calling them all sorts of names just now, I do respect them all … though I don’t respect Zametov, I like him, for he is a puppy, and that bullock Zossimov, because he is an honest man and knows his work.
uz: Hozircha ularga har xil ismlar bilan murojaat qilsam-da, ularning barchasini hurmat qilaman... Zametovni hurmat qilmasam-da, uni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki u itdir, va bu buzoq Zossimov, chunki u halol va o'z ishini biladigan odam.

en: But enough, it’s all said and forgiven.
uz: Lekin yetarli, bu hammasi aytilgan va kechirilgan.

en: Well, then, let’s go on.
uz: Xo'sh, keling, davom etaylik.

en: I know this corridor, I’ve been here, there was a scandal here at Number ൤.
uz: Men bu yo'lni bilaman, men bu yerda bo'lganman, bu yerda Numara da shubha bo'lgan.

en: … Where are you here?
uz: ...Qayerda bo'lishingiz mumkin?

en: Well, lock yourselves in for the night, then.
uz: O'zingizni kechasi qamab qo'yinglar.

en: Don’t let anybody in.
uz: Hech kimni kirishiga yo'l qo'ymang.

en: In a quarter of an hour I’ll come back with news, and half an hour later I’ll bring Zossimov, you’ll see!
uz: 25 daqiqadan so'ng men yangiliklar bilan qaytib kelaman, yarim soatdan so'ng esa Zossimovni olib kelaman, ko'rasiz!

en: Goodbye, I’ll run.” “Good heavens, Dounia, what is going to happen?” said Pulcheria Alexandrovna, addressing her daughter with anxiety and dismay.
uz: Xudojo'y, yuguraman.Xudojo'y, Dounia, nima bo'ladi? dedi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, qizini tashvish va xavotir bilan murojaat qilib.

en: “Don’t worry yourself, mother,” said Dounia, taking off her hat and cape.
uz: "O'zingni xavotirga solma, ona", - dedi Dounia, shovqinini va to'pini olib tashlab.

en: “God has sent this gentleman to our aid, though he has come from a drinking party.
uz: Xudo bu xonimni bizga yordam berish uchun yubordi, ammo u ichimlik partiyasidan kelgan.

en: We can depend on him, I assure you.
uz: Biz unga tayangan bo'lishimiz mumkin, sizga ishontiraman.

en: And all that he has done for Rodya.
uz: Va u Rodya uchun qilgan barcha ishlarni.

en: Dounia, goodness knows whether he will come!
uz: Dounia, Xudo biladi, u kelarmi yoki yo'qmi!

en: How could I bring myself to leave Rodya?
uz: Qanday qilib Rodyani tashlab ketishga majbur bo'ldim?

en: … And how different, how different I had fancied our meeting!
uz: Va men o'z tasavvurim bilan uchrashuvimiz qanchalik farq qilganini ko'rdim.

en: How sullen he was, as though not pleased to see us.
uz: U bizni ko'rishdan xursand bo'lmagandek, qanchalik xafa bo'lgan edi.

en: …” Tears came into her eyes.
uz: ... Uning ko'zlariga yoshlar tushdi.

en: “No, it’s not that, mother.
uz: Yo'q, bu o'sha emas, onam.

en: You didn’t see, you were crying all the time.
uz: Siz ko'rmadingiz, doim yig'lar edingiz.

en: He is quite unhinged by serious illness —that’s the reason.” “Ah, that illness!
uz: U jiddiy kasallik tufayli juda xavotirda.Bu sabab.Ah, bu kasallik!

en: What will happen, what will happen?
uz: Nima bo'ladi, nima bo'ladi?

en: And how he talked to you, Dounia!” said the mother, looking timidly at her daughter, trying to read her thoughts and, already half consoled by Dounia’s standing up for her brother, which meant that she had already forgiven him.
uz: U sizga qanday gapirgan, Dounia! - dedi ona, qizini qo'rqinch ila ko'rib, uning fikrlarini o'qishga harakat qildi va Dounia o'z ukasi uchun qo'llab-quvvatlagani bilan yarim tasalli topdi, ya'ni u endi uni kechirdi.

en: “I am sure he will think better of it tomorrow,” she added, probing her further.
uz: Men shubhasiz, u ertaga bu haqda yaxshiroq o'ylaydi, deb qo'shimcha qildi u, uni yanada tekshirib ko'rdi.

en: “And I am sure that he will say the same tomorrow … about that,” Avdotya Romanovna said finally.
uz: Va men shubhasiz, u ertaga ham xuddi shunday so'zlarni aytadi ... bu haqda, Avdotya Romanovna nihoyat aytdi.

en: And, of course, there was no going beyond that, for this was a point which Pulcheria Alexandrovna was afraid to discuss.
uz: Va, albatta, bundan tashqari ketish mumkin emas edi, chunki Pulcheria Aleksandrovna bu masala haqida gapirishdan qo'rqqan edi.

en: Dounia went up and kissed her mother.
uz: Dounia ko'tarilib, onasini o'pdi.

en: warmly embraced her without speaking.
uz: O'zini gapirmasdan qizni iliq o'rab oldi.

en: Then she sat down to wait anxiously for Razumihin’s return, timidly watching her daughter who walked up and down the room with her arms folded, lost in thought.
uz: So'ngra Razumihinning qaytib kelishini kutish uchun o'tirdi va qo'llarini to'kib, o'z xonasiga o'tib borayotgan qizini qo'llari bilan ko'tarib, o'y-xayolidan mahrum bo'lgan qizini qo'rqmasdan kuzatdi.

en: This walking up and down when she was thinking was a habit of Avdotya Romanovna’s and the mother was always afraid to break in on her daughter’s mood at such moments.
uz: O'ylab yurgan paytda Avdotya Romanovnasning bu yurish-turish odati edi va ona har doim o'z qizining ruhini bunday paytlarda buzishdan qo'rqardi.

en: Razumihin, of course, was ridiculous in his sudden drunken infatuation for Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Razumihin, albatta, Avdotya Romanovnaga bo'lgan to'satdan mast bo'lgan muhabbatida g'alati edi.

en: Yet apart from his eccentric condition, many people would have thought it justified if they had seen Avdotya Romanovna, especially at that moment when she was walking to and fro with folded arms, pensive and melancholy.
uz: Biroq, uning g'alati holatidan tashqari, Avdotya Romanovnayni ko'rish ko'pchilik uchun oqilona bo'lgan, ayniqsa u qo'llarini qo'yib, fikr-mulohaza va melanxoniya bilan yurgan paytda.

en: Avdotya Romanovna was remarkably good-looking; she was tall, strikingly well-proportioned, strong and self-reliant —the latter quality was apparent in every gesture, though it did not in the least detract from the grace and softness of her movements.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna juda chiroyli edi; u baland, ko'p o'lchovli, kuchli va o'ziga ishonadigan edi.Bu fazilat har bir harakatida namoyon bo'lgan, ammo harakatlarining xushmuomalaligi va yumshatishidan hech qanday zarar ko'rmagan.

en: In face she resembled her brother, but she might be described as really beautiful.
uz: U yuzida ukasiga o'xshardi, lekin uni chindan ham chiroyli deb aytsa bo'ladi.

en: Her hair was dark brown, a little lighter than her brother’s; there was a proud light in her almost black eyes and yet at times a look of extraordinary kindness.
uz: Uning sochlari qorong'i qora rangli, aka-ukalaridan biroz yorug'roq edi; uning deyarli qora ko'zlarida mag'rur nur bor edi, ammo ba'zida ajoyib mehribonlik ko'rinishi bor edi.

en: She was pale, but it was a healthy pallor; her face was radiant with freshness and vigour.
uz: U o'z ko'rinishida soya edi, ammo bu sog'lom soya edi; uning yuzi yangilik va kuch-qudrat bilan nurlanardi.

en: Her mouth was rather small; the full red lower lip projected a little as did her chin; it was the only irregularity in her beautiful face, but it gave it a peculiarly individual and almost haughty expression.
uz: Uning og'zi juda kichkina edi; to'liq qizil pastki og'zasi uning burunidagi kabi biroz ko'rinardi; bu uning go'zal yuzidagi yagona noaniqlik edi, ammo unga o'zgacha individual va deyarli mag'rurlik bilan ko'rinadi.

en: Her face was always more serious and thoughtful than gay; but how well smiles, how well youthful, lighthearted, irresponsible, laughter suited her face!
uz: Uning yuzi har doim geylardan ko'ra jiddiyroq va mulohaza yuritadigan bo'lgan, ammo qanchalik yaxshi tabassum, yoshlik, yengillik, mas'uliyatsizlik, kulgi uning yuziga mos kelardi!

en: It was natural enough that a warm, open, simple-hearted, honest giant like Razumihin, who had never seen anyone like her and was not quite sober at the time, should lose his head immediately.
uz: O'sha paytlarda u kabi hech kimni ko'rmagan va o'sha paytda o'ziga xos bo'lmagan Razumihin kabi iliq, ochiq, oddiy va halol bo'lgan devon darhol aqldan ozdirishi tabiiy edi.

en: Besides, as chance would have it, he saw Dounia for the first time transfigured by her love for her brother and her joy at meeting him.
uz: Bundan tashqari, Dovud Dovudni birinchi marta birodarini sevgani va uni uchratganidan quvonchga ega bo'lgani uchun o'zgartirganini ko'rdi.

en: Afterwards he saw her lower lip quiver with indignation at her brother’s insolent, cruel and ungrateful words —and his fate was sealed.
uz: Keyinchalik u ukasining g'azablangan, shafqatsiz va minnatdorchiliksizlik so'zlariga ko'ra, uning pastki og'izlari g'azabga to'lib-toshganini ko'rdi va uning taqdirini belgilab qo'ydi.

en: He had spoken the truth, moreover, when he blurted out in his drunken talk on the stairs that Praskovya Pavlovna, Raskolnikov’s eccentric landlady, would be jealous of Pulcheria Alexandrovna as well as of Avdotya Romanovna on his account.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u o'zining mast bo'lgan nutqida, Raskolnikovning g'ayritabiiy uy egasi Praskovya Pavlovna Pulcheria Aleksandrovna va Avdotya Romanovnaga uning nomidan hasad qilishini aytganda, haqiqatni aytdi.

en: Alexandrovna was forty-three, her face still retained traces of her former beauty; she looked much younger than her age, indeed, which is almost always the case with women who retain serenity of spirit, sensitiveness and pure sincere warmth of heart to old age.
uz: Aleksandrovna qirq uch yoshda edi, uning yuzi hali ham o'zining sobiq go'zalligi izlarini saqlab qolgan edi; u o'z yoshidan ancha yoshroq ko'rinardi, aslida, bu deyarli har doim ham keksalikkacha tinchlik ruhini, hissiyligini va pok samimiy yurak iliqligini saqlagan ayollar bilan sodir bo'ladi.

en: We may add in parenthesis that to preserve all this is the only means of retaining beauty to old age.
uz: Bularning barchasini saqlab qolish - keksalikkacha go'zallikni saqlab qolishning yagona yo'li, deb qo'shishimiz mumkin.

en: Her hair had begun to grow grey and thin, there had long been little crow’s foot wrinkles round her eyes, her cheeks were hollow and sunken from anxiety and grief, and yet it was a handsome face.
uz: Uning sochlari oq va chiroyli bo'la boshlagan edi, ko'zlari atrofida uzoq vaqtdan beri kichik qo'rg'onlar oyoq burchaklari bor edi, yig'inlari tuxumli va tashvish va qayg'udan cho'kgan edi, ammo u juda chiroyli yuz edi.

en: She was Dounia over again, twenty years older, but without the projecting underlip.
uz: U yana Dounia edi, u yigirma yoshga katta edi, lekin o'z ichiga o'tkir bo'laksiz edi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna was emotional, but not sentimental, timid and yielding, but only to a certain point.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna hissiy, lekin hissiy emas, uyatchan va bo'shash edi, lekin faqat muayyan darajada.

en: She could give way and accept a great deal even of what was contrary to her convictions, but there was a certain barrier fixed by honesty, principle and the deepest convictions which nothing would induce her to cross.
uz: U hatto o'z e'tiqodlariga zid bo'lgan narsalarga ham ko'p narsani tan olib, qabul qilishi mumkin edi, ammo rostgo'ylik, prinsip va hech narsa uni kesib o'tishga undaydigan eng chuqur e'tiqodlar bilan belgilangan bir to'siq bor edi.

en: Exactly twenty minutes after Razumihin’s departure, there came two subdued but hurried knocks at the door: he had come back.
uz: Razumihin ketgandan to'g'ri yigirma daqiqa o'tgach, eshikga ikki marta kamtarlik bilan, lekin shoshilinch taqillatlar keldi: u qaytib keldi.

en: “I won’t come in, I haven’t time,” he hastened to say when the door was opened.
uz: Men kirmayman, vaqtim yo'q, - deb darrov eshik ochilganini aytdi u.

en: “He sleeps like a top, soundly, quietly, and God grant he may sleep ten hours.
uz: U o'n soat uxlaydi va Xudo unga o'n soat uyqu berishiga ruxsat beradi.

en: Nastasya’s with him; I told her not to leave till I came.
uz: Nastasyas u bilan birga; men unga men kelmagunimcha ketmasligini aytdim.

en: Now I am fetching Zossimov, he will report to you and then you’d better turn in; I can see you are too tired to do anything.
uz: Endi men Zossimovni olib kelyapman, u sizga hisobot beradi va keyin siz o'zingizni o'zingizdan so'rashingiz kerak; ko'rib turibmanki, siz hech narsa qila olmaydigan darajada charchagansiz.

en: …” And he ran off down the corridor.
uz: ... Va u koridorda yugurib ketdi.

en: “What a very competent and … devoted young man!” cried Pulcheria Alexandrovna exceedingly delighted.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna nihoyatda xursand bo'lib: "Bu juda mahoratli va ... sadoqatli yigit!" - dedi.

en: “He seems a splendid person!” Avdotya Romanovna replied with some warmth, resuming her walk up and down the room.
uz: U ajoyib odamga o'xshaydi! Avdotya Romanovna salomli javob berdi va o'sha xonada yurishni davom ettirdi.

en: It was nearly an hour later when they heard footsteps in the corridor and another knock at the door.
uz: Deyarli bir soat o'tgach, ular yo'lda qadamlar eshitishdi va eshikda yana bir taqillat eshitildi.

en: Both women waited this time completely relying on Razumihin’s promise; he actually had succeeded in bringing Zossimov.
uz: Ikkala ayol ham bu safar Razumihinning va'dasiga to'liq tayanib kutishdi; u aslida Zossimovni olib kelishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: Zossimov had agreed at once to desert the drinking party to go to Raskolnikov’s, but he came reluctantly and with the greatest suspicion to see the ladies, mistrusting Razumihin in his exhilarated condition.
uz: Zossimov darhol Raskolnikovlarga borish uchun ichimlik partiyasidan chiqib ketishga rozi bo'ldi, lekin u qizlarni ko'rish uchun istamay va katta shubha bilan keldi, chunki Razumihinning hayajonli holatiga ishonmadi.

en: But his vanity was at once reassured and flattered; he saw that they were really expecting him as an oracle.
uz: Ammo uning behudaligi birdan taskin topdi va maqtovga sazovor bo'ldi; u, aslida, uni oraqol sifatida kutishayotganini ko'rdi.

en: He stayed just ten minutes and
uz: U atigi o'n daqiqa qoldi va o'shanda u o'z ishini boshladi.

en: succeeded in completely convincing and comforting Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna-ni butunlay qondirgan va tasalli bergan.

en: He spoke with marked sympathy, but with the reserve and extreme seriousness of a young doctor at an important consultation.
uz: U ko'p hamdardlik bilan gapirgan, ammo muhim maslahatga kelgan yosh shifokor kabi ehtiyotkorlik va jiddiylik bilan gapirgan.

en: He did not utter a word on any other subject and did not display the slightest desire to enter into more personal relations with the two ladies.
uz: U boshqa hech qanday mavzuda so'z aytmadi va ikki xonim bilan shaxsiy munosabatlarga kirishni xohlamagan.

en: Remarking at his first entrance the dazzling beauty of Avdotya Romanovna, he endeavoured not to notice her at all during his visit and addressed himself solely to Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaning chiroyli go'zalligini birinchi kirishi bilan ta'kidlab, u tashrif paytida uni hech qachon ko'rmaslikka harakat qildi va faqat Pulcheria Aleksandrovnaga murojaat qildi.

en: All this gave him extraordinary inward satisfaction.
uz: Bularning barchasi unga o'zgacha ichki mamnuniyat ato etdi.

en: He declared that he thought the invalid at this moment going on very satisfactorily.
uz: U nogiron odamning hozirgi paytda juda qoniqarli o'tishini o'ylayotganini aytdi.

en: According to his observations the patient’s illness was due partly to his unfortunate material surroundings during the last few months, but it had partly also a moral origin, “was, so to speak, the product of several material and moral influences, anxieties, apprehensions, troubles, certain ideas … and so on.” Noticing stealthily that Avdotya Romanovna was following his words with close attention, Zossimov allowed himself to enlarge on this theme.
uz: Uning e'tiborlariga ko'ra, bemorning kasalligi qisman oxirgi bir necha oy davomida uning noxush moddiy muhitidan kelib chiqqan, ammo qisman axloqiy kelib chiqishi bor edi, bu bir nechta moddiy va axloqiy ta'sirlarning, tashvishlar, qo'rquvlar, muammolar, ba'zi g'oyalar va shu kabilarning natijasi edi. Avdotya Romanovna uning so'zlarini diqqat bilan kuzatayotganini yashirincha payqagan Zossimov o'ziga bu mavzuda ko'proq ma'lumot berishga ruxsat berdi.

en: On Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s anxiously and timidly inquiring as to “some suspicion of insanity,” he replied with a composed and candid smile that his words had been exaggerated; that certainly the patient had some fixed idea, something approaching a monomania —he, Zossimov, was now particularly studying this interesting branch of medicine — but that it must be recollected that until today the patient had been in delirium and … and that no doubt the presence of his family would have a favourable effect on his recovery and distract his mind, “if only all fresh shocks can be avoided,” he added significantly.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovnas tashvish va qo'rqinch bilan aqldan ozganligiga shubha ostiga qo'yganida, u so'zlari haddan ortiq so'zlanganini aniq va samimiy tabassum bilan javob berdi; albatta, bemorning biron bir fikri bor edi, monomansiyaga yaqinlashayotgan narsa.Zossimov hozir ayniqsa tibbiyotning ushbu qiziqarli bo'limiga e'tibor qaratmoqda, lekin shuni yodda tutish kerakki, bugungi kunga qadar bemor deliriumda va ... va, shubhasiz, uning oila a'zoligi uning tiklanishida ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatadi va uning ongini chalg'itadi, agar barcha yangi shoklardan qochish mumkin bo'lsa, o'zi ham sezilarli darajada qo'shimcha qildi.

en: Then he got up, took leave with an impressive and affable bow, while blessings, warm gratitude, and entreaties were showered upon him, and Avdotya Romanovna spontaneously offered her hand to him.
uz: Keyin u o'rnidan turib, quvonchli va mehribon qo'zg'olon bilan jo'nab ketdi, uning ustiga duolar, samimiy minnatdorchilik va iltijolar yog'di va Avdotya Romanovna unga qo'lini o'ziga berdi.

en: He went out exceedingly pleased with his visit and still more so with himself.
uz: U tashrifidan juda mamnun bo'lib, o'zi bilan yana ko'proq xursand bo'ldi.

en: “We’ll talk tomorrow; go to bed at once!” Razumihin said in conclusion, following Zossimov out.
uz: Biz ertaga gaplashamiz; darhol yotoqga boring! Razumihin Zossimovga ergashib, so'nggi so'zlarni aytdi.

en: “I’ll be with you tomorrow morning as early as possible with my report.” “That’s a fetching little girl, Avdotya Romanovna,” remarked Zossimov, almost licking his lips as they both came out into the street.
uz: Men ertalab ertalab sizning oldingizda bo'laman va hisobotimni taqdim etaman.Bu juda yoqimli qizcha Avdotya Romanovna, - dedi Zossimov, ikkalasi ham ko'chaga chiqqanida, deyarli dudaklarini yulib.

en: You said fetching?” roared Razumihin and he flew at Zossimov and seized him by the throat.
uz: Siz olib kelishni aytdingizmi? Razumihin qichqirdi va u Zossimovga uchib kelib, uni qo'ldan tutdi.

en: … Do you understand?
uz: ... Siz buni tushunyapsizmi?

en: Do you understand?” he shouted, shaking him by the collar and squeezing him against the wall.
uz: Siz buni tushunyapsizmi? u qichqirib, uni bo'ynidan silkitib, devorga bosdi.

en: “Do you hear?” “Let me go, you drunken devil,” said Zossimov, struggling and when he had let him go, he stared at him and went off into a sudden guffaw.
uz: Quloq solyapsanmi? Meni ketishimga ruxsat bering, ey mast shayton, - dedi Zossimov, kurash olib borib, uni qo'yib yuborganida unga qaradi va to'satdan g'ofga tushadi.

en: Razumihin stood facing him in gloomy and earnest reflection.
uz: Razumihin uning oldidan qayg'uli va samimiy mulohazalarda turdi.

en: “Of course, I am an ass,” he observed, sombre as a storm cloud, “but still … you are another.” “No, brother, not at all such another.
uz: Albatta, men bir o'g'limman, - dedi u, - buzg'unchilik bulutlari kabi qorong'i, - lekin hali ham... sen boshqa odamsan. - Yo'q, aka, umuman boshqa emas.

en: I am not dreaming of any folly.” They walked along in silence and only when they were close to Raskolnikov’s lodgings, Razumihin broke the silence in considerable anxiety.
uz: Men hech qanday aqlsizlik haqida orzu qilmayapman. Ular xotirjamlik bilan yurishdi va faqat Raskolnikov uylariga yaqinlashganda, Razumihin sezilarli tashvish bilan xotirjamlikni buzdi.

en: “Listen,” he said, “you’re a first-rate fellow, but among your other failings, you’re a loose fish, that I know, and a dirty one, too.
uz: U shunday dedi: "Sen birinchi darajali odamsan, lekin boshqa kamchiliklaring orasida, men bilganimcha, sen - bo'sh baliq va buzuq baliqsan.

en: You are a feeble, nervous wretch, and a mass of whims, you’re getting fat and lazy and can’t deny yourself anything —and I call that dirty because it leads one straight into the dirt.
uz: Siz zaif, g'ayratli va ko'pgina g'ayratli odamsiz, siz o'zingizdan hech narsa rad qila olmaysiz va o'zingizdan hech narsa rad qila olmaysiz va men buni kirli deb atayman, chunki u sizni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yerga olib boradi.

en: You’ve let yourself get so slack that I don’t know how it is you are still a good, even a devoted doctor.
uz: Siz o'zingizni shunchalik beparvo qilib qo'ydingizki, qanday qilib hali ham yaxshi, hatto sodiq shifokor ekanligingizni bilmayman.

en: You —a doctor —sleep on a feather bed and get up at night to your patients!
uz: Siz - shifokor - to'qima yotoqida uxlaysiz va kechasi bemorlaringizga qarab turasiz!

en: In another three or four years you won’t get up for your patients … But hang it all, that’s not the point!
uz: Uch yoki to'rt yildan keyin siz bemorlaringiz uchun turolmaysiz... Ammo hamma narsani to'xtatish, bu mening fikrim emas!

en: … You are going to spend tonight in the landlady’s flat here.
uz: Siz bu kecha uy egasining xonadonida o'tkazasiz.

en: (Hard work I’ve had to persuade her!) And I’ll be in the kitchen.
uz: (Men uni ishontirish uchun juda ko'p mehnat qildim!) Va men oshxonada bo'laman.

en: So here’s a chance for you to get to know her better.
uz: Shunday qilib, bu siz uchun u bilan yaxshiroq tanishish imkoniyati.

en: … It’s not as you think!
uz: Bu siz o'ylaganidek bo'lmaydi!

en: There’s not a trace of anything of the sort, brother … !” “But I don’t think!” “Here you have modesty, brother, silence, bashfulness, a savage virtue … and yet she’s sighing and melting like wax, simply melting!
uz: Bularning hech qanday izlari yo'q, aka... !  Lekin men o'ylamayman!  Mana sizda kamtarlik, aka, sukut, o'yin-kulgi, yovvoyi fazilat bor... va shunga qaramay, u yig'ib-ichib, balchiqday erib-ichib ketmoqda, shunchaki erib ketmoqda!

en: Save me from her, by all that’s unholy!
uz: Meni undan qutqar, bularning barchasi muqaddas emas!

en: She’s most prepossessing … I’ll repay you, I’ll do anything.
uz: U juda ustunlik qilmoqda... Men sizga pul to'layman, men hamma narsani qilaman.

en: …” Zossimov laughed more violently than ever.
uz: ... Zossimov har qachongidan ham zo'ravonroq kuldi.

en: “Well, you are smitten!
uz: Ha, siz allaqachon o'ldirilgansiz!

en: But what am I to do with her?” “It won’t be much trouble, I assure you.
uz: Ammo men u bilan nima qilishim kerak?Bu katta muammo bo'lmaydi, sizga ishontiraman.

en: Talk any rot you like to her, as long as you sit by her and talk.
uz: U bilan o'zing xohlagan har qanday gapni ayt, faqat uning yonida o'tirib gapirasan.

en: You’re a doctor, too; try curing her of something.
uz: Siz ham shifokorsiz; uni biror narsadan davolashga harakat qiling.

en: I swear you won’t regret it.
uz: Qasamki, bundan afsuslanmaysiz.

en: She has a piano, and you
uz: Uning klaviaturasi bor, siz esa.

en: know, I strum a little.
uz: Bilaman, men biroz ko'tarilganman.

en: I have a song there, a genuine Russian one: ‘I shed hot tears.’ She likes the genuine article —and well, it all began with that song; Now you’re a regular performer, a maître, a Rubinstein.
uz: Mening o'sha yerda rus tilidagi qo'shiqim bor: I shed hot tears. U asl maqolani yaxshi ko'radi va yaxshi, bu hammasi shu qo'shiq bilan boshlandi; Endi siz doimiy ijrochi, master, Rubinstein.

en: … I assure you, you won’t regret it!” “But have you made her some promise?
uz: Sizni ishontiramanki, siz bundan afsuslanmaysiz! Ammo siz unga biron bir va'da berganmisiz?

en: A promise of marriage, perhaps?” “Nothing, nothing, absolutely nothing of the kind!
uz: Balki nikoh va'dasi? Hech narsa, hech narsa, hech narsa!

en: Besides she is not that sort at all.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u umuman bunday emas.

en: … Tchebarov tried that.
uz: ...Chebarov buni sinab ko'rdi.

en: …” “Well then, drop her!” “But I can’t drop her like that!” “Why can’t you?” “Well, I can’t, that’s all about it!
uz: Xo'sh, uni tashlab qo'yinglar! lekin men uni shunday tashlab qo'yishim mumkin emas!

en: There’s an element of attraction here, brother.” “Then why have you fascinated her?” “I haven’t fascinated her; perhaps I was fascinated myself in my folly.
uz: Bu yerda jozibadorlik elementlari bor, aka.  Unda nega uni hayratda qoldirdingiz?   Men uni hayratda qoldirmadim; ehtimol men o'zimni o'z aqlsizligim bilan hayratda qoldirganman.

en: But she won’t care a straw whether it’s you or I, so long as somebody sits beside her, sighing.
uz: Ammo u siz yoki men bo'lishimizdan qat'iy nazar, uning yonida kimdir o'tirib, g'iybat qilib yurganidan qat'iy nazar, hech qanday g'amxo'rlik qilmaydi.

en: … I can’t explain the position, brother … look here, you are good at mathematics, and working at it now … begin teaching her the integral calculus; upon my soul, I’m not joking, I’m in earnest, it’ll be just the same to her.
uz: Men bu mavzuni tushuntira olmayman, aka... mana, siz matematikada yaxshi ishlaysiz va hozirda o'z ishingiz bilan shug'ullanasiz... unga integral kalkulusni o'rgatishni boshlang; ruhim uchun, men mayda emasman, jiddiyman, unga ham xuddi shunday bo'ladi.

en: She will gaze at you and sigh for a whole year together.
uz: U sizni ko'rib, bir yil davomida bir-biriga quloq soladi.

en: I talked to her once for two days at a time about the Prussian House of Lords (for one must talk of something) —she just sighed and perspired!
uz: Men bir marta ikki kun davomida bir vaqtning o'zida u bilan prussiya lordlar palatasi haqida gapirganman (chunki biror narsa haqida gapirish kerak) u shunchaki nafas oldi va terlandi!

en: And you mustn’t talk of love —she’s bashful to hysterics —but just let her see you can’t tear yourself away —that’s enough.
uz: Va siz sevgi haqida gapirishingiz mumkin emas, u histeriklarga uyalgan, lekin uni ko'rishiga imkon beringki, siz o'zingizni yirtira olmaysiz, bu etarli.

en: It’s fearfully comfortable; you’re quite at home, you can read, sit, lie about, write.
uz: Bu dahshatli qulay; siz o'zingizning uyingizda o'qiy olasiz, o'tirib o'qiy olasiz, yolg'on gapirib o'qiy olasiz, yozasiz.

en: You may even venture on a kiss, if you’re careful.” “But what do I want with her?” “Ach, I can’t make you understand!
uz: Agar ehtiyotkor bo'lsangiz, hatto o'zingizni o'pishingizga ham jur'at qila olasiz. Lekin men undan nima istayman?A, men sizni tushunishga majburlay olmayman!

en: You see, you are made for each other!
uz: Koʻrib turganingizdek, siz bir-biringiz uchun yaratilgansiz!

en: I have often been reminded of you!
uz: Sizni ko'pincha eslatdim!

en: … You’ll come to it in the end!
uz: Oxir-oqibat siz bunga erishasiz!

en: So does it matter whether it’s sooner or later?
uz: Shunday qilib, erta yoki kech bo'lish muhimmi?

en: There’s the featherbed element here, brother —ach!
uz: Bu erda tovuq element bor, aka ach!

en: There’s an attraction here —here you have the end of the world, an anchorage, a quiet haven, the navel of the earth, the three fishes that are the foundation of the world, the essence of pancakes, of savoury fish- pies, of the evening samovar, of soft sighs and warm shawls, and hot stoves to sleep on —as snug as though you were dead, and yet
uz: Bu erda bir jozibadorlik bor, bu erda sizda dunyoning oxiri, anchoragi, xotirjam o'rin, yer yuzi, dunyoning poydevori bo'lgan uchta baliq, pancakelarning mohiyati, mazali baliq tortlari, kechki samovar, iliq nafaslar va iliq shawllar va o'lganingiz kabi yaqin uxlash uchun issiq pechlar bor.

en: you’re alive —the advantages of both at once!
uz: Siz tiriksiz, bir vaqtning o'zida ikkalasi ham foydalidir!

en: Well, hang it, brother, what stuff I’m talking, it’s bedtime!
uz: Xo'sh, to'xtab qo'ying, aka, men nima haqida gapirayotgan bo'lsam, uxlash vaqti keldi!

en: I sometimes wake up at night; so I’ll go in and look at him.
uz: Ba'zan kechasi uyg'onaman, shuning uchun ichkariga kirib, unga qarab turaman.

en: But there’s no need, it’s all right.
uz: Ammo bu kerak emas, bu yaxshi.

en: Don’t you worry yourself, yet if you like, you might just look in once, too.
uz: O'zingizni tashvishlantirmang, ammo agar xohlasangiz, bir marta ham ko'rib chiqishingiz mumkin.

en: But if you notice anything —delirium or fever —wake me at once.
uz: Ammo agar siz biron bir delirium yoki issiqlikni sezsangiz, meni darhol uyg'oting.

en: II Razumihin waked up next morning at eight o’clock, troubled and serious.
uz: II Razumihin ertasi kuni ertalab soat sakkizlarda uyg'onib, xavotirda va jiddiy edi.

en: He found himself confronted with many new and unlooked- for perplexities.
uz: U o'zini ko'plab yangi va kutilmagan g'alatiliklarga duch kelgan.

en: He had never expected that he would ever wake up feeling like that.
uz: U hech qachon o'zini shunday his etib uyg'onishini kutmagan.

en: He remembered every detail of the previous day and he knew that a perfectly novel experience had befallen him, that he had received an impression unlike anything he had known before.
uz: U o'tgan kunning har bir tafsilotini eslab qolgan va u o'ziga yangilik tushirganini, avval hech qachon ko'rmagan taassurot qoldirganini bilardi.

en: At the same time he recognised clearly that the dream which had fired his imagination was hopelessly unattainable —so unattainable that he felt positively ashamed of it, and he hastened to pass to the other more practical cares and difficulties bequeathed him by that “thrice accursed yesterday.” The most awful recollection of the previous day was the way he had shown himself “base and mean,” not only because he had been drunk, but because he had taken advantage of the young girl’s position to abuse her fiancé in his stupid jealousy, knowing nothing of their mutual relations and obligations and next to nothing of the man himself.
uz: Shu bilan birga, u tasavvurini uyg'otgan orzu umidsizlik bilan erishilmasligini, shu qadar erishilmasligini anglab yetdiki, u bundan o'zini o'ylashdan o'zini o'ylaydi va o'sha kecha uch marta la'natlangan muammosi tufayli unga meros bo'lgan boshqa amaliy g'amxo'rlik va qiyinchiliklarga o'tishga shoshildi. O'tgan kunning eng dahshatli xotirasi u o'zini kamsitgan va yovuz ko'rsatgan yo'lidir, nafaqat mast bo'lgani uchun, balki o'zining ahmoqona hasadida qizning niyatini qo'ldan boy bergani uchun, u o'zining nişanchisini suiiste'mol qilganligi uchun, ularning o'zaro munosabatlari va majburiyatlari haqida hech narsa bilmay, o'zidan hech narsa bilmay, erkakning o'zi haqida hech narsa bilmagan.

en: And what right had he to criticise him in that hasty and unguarded manner?
uz: Va uni bunday tezkor va g'ayritabiiy tarzda tanqid qilishga unga qanday huquq bor edi?

en: Who had asked for his opinion?
uz: Uning fikrini kim so'ragan?

en: Was it thinkable that such a creature as Avdotya Romanovna would be marrying an unworthy man for money?
uz: Avdotya Romanovna kabi yaratilish pul uchun noloyiq odam bilan turmushga chiqishi mumkinmi?

en: So there must be something in him.
uz: Demak, uning ichida biror narsa bo'lishi kerak.

en: But after all how could he know the character of the lodgings?
uz: Ammo u uylarning xarakterini qayerdan bilishi mumkin?

en: He was furnishing a flat … Foo!
uz: U bir kvartirani jihozlab yurgan edi... Foo!

en: how despicable it all was!
uz: Bularning barchasi naqadar nohaq edi!

en: And what justification was it that he was drunk?
uz: Va u mast bo'lganini qanday oqlash mumkin edi?

en: Such a stupid excuse was even more degrading!
uz: Bunday ahmoqona bahona yanada kamsitadigan bo'ldi!

en: In wine is truth, and the truth had all come out, “that is, all the uncleanness of his coarse and envious heart”!
uz: O'sha sharobda haqiqat bor va haqiqatning hammasi chiqdi, ya'ni uning qo'pol va hasadgo'y yuragidagi barcha nopoklik!

en: And would such a dream ever be permissible to him, Razumihin?
uz: Va bunday orzu unga hech qachon mumkinmi, Razumihin?

en: What was he beside such a girl —he, the drunken noisy
uz: U bunday qizning yonida nima edi, u, ichkilikboz shov-shuvli kishi?

en: braggart of last night?
uz: O'tgan kechaning mag'rurligi?

en: Was it possible to imagine so absurd and cynical a juxtaposition?
uz: Bunday absurd va sinik juxtapozitsiyani tasavvur qilish mumkinmi?

en: Razumihin blushed desperately at the very idea and suddenly the recollection forced itself vividly upon him of how he had said last night on the stairs that the landlady would be jealous of Avdotya Romanovna … that was simply intolerable.
uz: Razumihin o'sha g'oyaga juda qizg'inlab ketdi va to'satdan u kechasi uy egasi Avdotya Romanovnaga hasad qilishini aytganini eslatish unga qattiq ta'sir qildi ... bu shunchaki qabul qilinmas edi.

en: He brought his fist down heavily on the kitchen stove, hurt his hand and sent one of the bricks flying.
uz: U o'z yumushini oshxonadagi pechga og'ir tushirdi, qo'lini jarohatlab, tikanlardan birini uchirib yubordi.

en: “Of course,” he muttered to himself a minute later with a feeling of self-abasement, “of course, all these infamies can never be wiped out or smoothed over … and so it’s useless even to think of it, and I must go to them in silence and do my duty … in silence, too … and not ask forgiveness, and say nothing … for all is lost now!” And yet as he dressed he examined his attire more carefully than usual.
uz: Albatta,  o'ziga bir daqiqa o'tgach o'zini kamsitgan holda g'azablandi,  albatta, bu barcha iflosliklar hech qachon o'chirib tashlanmaydi yoki yo'q qilinmaydi ... va shuning uchun bu haqda o'ylash ham foydasiz, va men ular oldiga xotirjamlik bilan borib, o'z vazifamni bajarishim kerak ... xotirjamlik bilan ham ... va kechirim so'ramay, hech narsa aytmay ... chunki hamma narsa endi yo'qolgan! Va ammo u kiyinayotganda o'z kiyimini odatidan ko'ra ko'proq diqqat bilan tekshirgan.

en: He hadn’t another suit —if he had had, perhaps he wouldn’t have put it on.
uz: Uning boshqa kiyimi yo'q edi, agar shunday bo'lganida, ehtimol uni kiymagan bo'lar edi.

en: “I would have made a point of not putting it on.” But in any case he could not remain a cynic and a dirty sloven; he had no right to offend the feelings of others, especially when they were in need of his assistance and asking him to see them.
uz: Men uni kiymagan bo'lardim. Ammo u har holda sinik va nopok bo'lib qololmasdi; u boshqalarning his-tuyg'ularini ranjitishga haqli emas edi, ayniqsa, ular uning yordamiga muhtoj bo'lganda va ularni ko'rishlarini so'rashganda.

en: He brushed his clothes carefully.
uz: U kiyimlarini ehtiyotkorlik bilan yuvgan.

en: His linen was always decent; in that respect he was especially clean.
uz: Uning kiyim-kechaklari har doim munosib edi; shu munosabat bilan u ayniqsa toza edi.

en: He washed that morning scrupulously —he got some soap from Nastasya —he washed his hair, his neck and especially his hands.
uz: U o'sha kuni ertalab sinchkovlik bilan yuvdi, Nastasya tomonidan sabun olib keldi, sochlarini, bo'yni va ayniqsa qo'llarini yuvdi.

en: When it came to the question whether to shave his stubbly chin or not (Praskovya Pavlovna had capital razors that had been left by her late husband), the question was angrily answered in the negative.
uz: O'zining o'g'ir bo'g'ini o'rab olishmi yoki yo'qmi degan savolga kelganda (Praskovya Pavlovna o'z eri tomonidan qoldirilgan kapital bo'g'ishtirmalarga ega edi), savolga g'azab bilan salbiy javob berildi.

en: “Let it stay as it is!
uz: Buni shunday qoldiring!

en: What if they think that I shaved on purpose to … ?
uz: Agar ular mening qasddan sochimni o'rab olganimni o'ylasak nima bo'ladi ... ?

en: They certainly would think so!
uz: Albatta, ular shunday o'ylashadi!

en: Not on any account!” “And … the worst of it was he was so coarse, so dirty, he had the manners of a pothouse; and … and even admitting that he knew he had some of the essentials of a gentleman … what was there in that to be proud of?
uz: Hech qanday sabab bilan emas!  Va ... eng og'ir narsa shundaki, u juda qo'pol, juda iflos edi, u o'zidan-o'zidan pastkixona kabi odobli edi; va ... va hatto u bir gentlemanning ba'zi zarur narsalariga ega ekanini bilishini tan olganda ham ... bunga faxrlanish uchun nima bor edi?

en: Everyone ought to be a gentleman and more than that … and all the same (he remembered) he, too, had done little things … not exactly dishonest, and yet.
uz: Har bir kishi xudojo'y bo'lishi kerak va undan ham ko'proq ... va hali ham (u eslaydi) u ham kichik ishlarni qilgan edi ... to'g'ri yolg'on emas, lekin hali ham.

en: … And what thoughts he sometimes had; hm … and to set all that beside Avdotya Romanovna!
uz: Va u ba'zan qanday fikrlarga ega bo'lgan edi, Avdotya Romanovnaning o'zidan tashqariga qo'yish uchun!

en: Well, he’d make a point then of being dirty, greasy, pothouse in his manners and he wouldn’t care!
uz: U o'z xulq-atvorida kirli, yog'li, qo'pol bo'lib qolishi kerak bo'lgan va u bunga ahamiyat bermas edi!

en: He was engaged in such monologues when Zossimov, who had spent the night in Praskovya Pavlovna’s parlour, came in.
uz: U bunday monologlar bilan shug'ullanar ekan, Praskovya Pavlovna salonida tunni o'tkazgan Zossimov kelib qoldi.

en: He was going home and was in a hurry to look at the invalid first.
uz: U uyga qaytib borayotgan edi va birinchi navbatda nogironni ko'rishga shoshgan edi.

en: Razumihin informed him that Raskolnikov was sleeping like a dormouse.
uz: Razumihin unga Raskolnikov uyqusday uxlayotganini ma'lum qildi.

en: Zossimov gave orders that they shouldn’t wake him and promised to see him again about eleven.
uz: Zossimov uni uyg'otmaslik haqida buyruq berdi va uni yana soat o'n bir atrofida ko'rishlarini va'da qildi.

en: “If he is still at home,” he added.
uz: Agar u hali ham uyda bo'lsa, qo'shimcha qildi.

en: If one can’t control one’s patients, how is one to cure them?
uz: Agar bemorlarni nazorat qila olmasak, qanday qilib ularni davolash mumkin?

en: Do you know whether he will go to them, or whether they are coming here?” “They are coming, I think,” said Razumihin, understanding the object of the question, “and they will discuss their family affairs, no doubt.
uz: U ularning oldiga boradimi yoki ular bu yerga kelyaptimi, bilasizmi?Men o'ylaymanki, ular keladilar, dedi Razumihin, savolning mazmunini tushunib, va ular oilaviy masalalarini muhokama qilishadi, shubhasiz.

en: You, as the doctor, have more right to be here than I.” “But I am not a father confessor; I shall come and go away; I’ve plenty to do besides looking after them.” “One thing worries me,” interposed Razumihin, frowning.
uz: Siz, shifokor sifatida, bu yerda bo'lishga mendan ko'ra ko'proq haqingiz bor. Lekin men gunohkor ota emasman; men kelib-ketaman; ularga g'amxo'rlik qilishdan tashqari, ko'p ishlarim bor.Bir narsa meni xavotirga soladi, - deb so'radi Razumihin.

en: “On the way home I talked a lot of drunken nonsense to him … all sorts of things … and amongst them that you were afraid that he … might become insane.” “You told the ladies so, too.” “I know it was stupid!
uz: Ushbu yo'lda men u bilan ko'pgina mast bo'lgan axloqsiz gaplarni aytdim ... har xil narsalar ... va ularning orasida siz uning ... aqldan ozdirishi mumkinligidan qo'rqqaningizni aytdim.  Siz ham xonimlarga shunday aytdingiz.  Men bu ahmoqlik ekanligini bilaman!

en: You may beat me if you like!
uz: Agar xohlasangiz, meni urishingiz mumkin!

en: Did you think so seriously?” “That’s nonsense, I tell you, how could I think it seriously?
uz: Siz ham shunday jiddiy o'yladingizmi? Bu g'alati gap, sizga aytaman, qanday qilib men buni jiddiy o'ylay olaman?

en: You, yourself, described him as a monomaniac when you fetched me to him … and we added fuel to the fire yesterday, you did, that is, with your story about the painter; it was a nice conversation, when he was, perhaps, mad on that very point!
uz: Siz o'zingiz uni meni unga olib kelganingizda uni monomanik deb tasvirlagansiz ... va biz o'tga kecha yoqilg'i qo'shdik, siz ham shunday qildingiz, ya'ni rassom haqidagi hikoyangiz bilan; bu yaxshi suhbat edi, chunki u, ehtimol, aynan shu mavzuda g'azablanardi!

en: If only I’d known what happened then at the police station and that some wretch … had insulted him with this suspicion!
uz: Agar men o'sha paytda politsiya bo'limida nima sodir bo'lganini bilganimda edi va qaysidir kambag'al ... uni shu shubha bilan haqoratlaganida edi!

en: Hm … I would not have allowed that conversation yesterday.
uz: Men o'sha suhbatga kecha ruxsat bermasdim.

en: These monomaniacs will make a mountain out of a molehill … and see their fancies as solid realities.
uz: Ushbu monomaniklar molehilldan tog'ni yaratadilar va o'z xayollarini mustahkam haqiqat deb ko'rishadi.

en: … As far as I remember, it was Zametov’s story that cleared up half the mystery, to my mind.
uz: ...Mening eslatishimcha, Zametovning hikoyasi mening fikrimcha sirning yarmini hal qildi.

en: Why, I know one case in which a hypochondriac, a man of forty, cut the throat of a little boy of eight, because he couldn’t endure the jokes he made every day at table!
uz: Men bir holatni bilaman, u erda qirq yoshli hypochondriyalik kishi sakkiz yoshli o'g'ilning bo'yni kesib tashladi, chunki u har kuni dasturxonda o'qigan hazillariga chiday olmagan!

en: And in this case his rags, the insolent police officer, the fever and this suspicion!
uz: Va bu holatda uning ko'ylaklari, beparvo politsiya xodimi, issiqlik va shubhasizlik!

en: All that working upon a man half frantic with
uz: Bularning barchasi yarim g'ayritabiiy odam bilan ishlaydi.

en: hypochondria, and with his morbid exceptional vanity!
uz: Hypoxondriya va o'zining ayanchli, o'zgacha behudaligi bilan!

en: That may well have been the starting-point of illness.
uz: Bu kasallikning boshlang'ich nuqtasi bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Well, bother it all!
uz: Toʻgʻri, bularning barchasini tashlab qoʻying!

en: … And, by the way, that Zametov certainly is a nice fellow, but hm … he shouldn’t have told all that last night.
uz: Aytgancha, Zametov chiroyli odam, lekin u o'tgan kecha bu haqda gapirib bermasligi kerak edi.

en: He is an awful chatterbox!” “But whom did he tell it to?
uz: U dahshatli suhbatdosh!  Ammo u buni kimga aytdi?

en: You and me?” “And Porfiry.” “What does that matter?” “And, by the way, have you any influence on them, his mother and sister?
uz: Siz va men? Va Porfiry.  Bu nimaga bog'liq? Va, albatta, siz ularning, uning onasi va singlisi ustidan biron bir ta'sirga egamisiz?

en: Tell them to be more careful with him today.
uz: Bugun unga ko'proq ehtiyot bo'lishlarini ayting.

en: …” “They’ll get on all right!” Razumihin answered reluctantly.
uz: ...  Ular yaxshi munosabatda bo'lishadi! Razumihin o'ylamasdan javob berdi.

en: “Why is he so set against this Luzhin?
uz: Nima uchun u bu Luzhinga qarshi ko'rinadi?

en: A man with money and she doesn’t seem to dislike him … and they haven’t a farthing, I suppose?
uz: Pulli erkak va u undan nafratlanmayotganga o'xshaydi ... va ularning farthinglari yo'q, deb o'ylayman?

en: eh?” “But what business is it of yours?” Razumihin cried with annoyance.
uz: Eh?  Ammo bu sizning qanday ishingiz? Razumihin xafa bo'lib yig'ladi.

en: “How can I tell whether they’ve a farthing?
uz: Ular farthingga ega bo'lishlarini qanday bilsam bo'ladi?

en: Ask them yourself and perhaps you’ll find out.
uz: O'zingizdan so'rang va ehtimol bilib olasiz.

en: what an ass you are sometimes!
uz: Ba'zan siz qanday qahramon bo'lasiz!

en: Last night’s wine has not gone off yet.
uz: O'tgan kechaning sharoblari hali o'tib ketmagan.

en: … Goodbye; thank your Praskovya Pavlovna from me for my night’s lodging.
uz: ... Xo'sh, kechalarim uchun menga Praskovya Pavlovnaga rahmat.

en: She locked herself in, made no reply to my bonjour through the door; she was up at seven o’clock, the samovar was taken into her from the kitchen.
uz: U o'zini o'ziga qulflab qo'ydi, eshikdan kelib salomlarimga javob bermadi; u soat yettida turardi, samovar oshxonadan unga olib ketildi.

en: I was not vouchsafed a personal interview.
uz: Menga shaxsiy intervyu berilmagan.

en: …” At nine o’clock precisely Razumihin reached the lodgings at Bakaleyev’s house.
uz: ... Soat to'qqizda aniq Razumihin Bakaleyevning uyiga yetib keldi.

en: Both ladies were waiting for him with nervous impatience.
uz: Ikkala xonim ham uni tashvish bilan kutishardi.

en: They had risen at seven o’clock or earlier.
uz: Ular soat yettida yoki undan oldin turishgan.

en: He entered looking as black as night, bowed awkwardly and was at once furious with himself for it.
uz: U kirib kirganida, qorong'i kechaga o'xshaydigan ko'rinardi, o'zini noqulay quvib, darhol o'zidan g'azablandi.

en: He had reckoned without his host: Pulcheria Alexandrovna fairly rushed at him, seized him by both hands and was almost kissing them.
uz: U o'z uy egasi bo'lmagan holda hisoblagan edi: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna unga juda tez kelib, uni ikki qo'lidan ham ushlab, deyarli o'pmoqchi edi.

en: He glanced timidly at Avdotya Romanovna, but her proud countenance wore at that moment an expression of such gratitude and friendliness, such complete and unlooked-for respect (in place of the sneering looks and ill-disguised contempt he had expected), that it threw him into greater confusion than if he had been met with abuse.
uz: U Avdotya Romanovnaga qo'rqinchli qarab ko'rdi, ammo uning mag'rur yuzi o'sha paytda minnatdorlik va do'stonalik, shu qadar to'liq va kutilmagan hurmatni ko'rsatdi (u o'ylaganicha masxara qiluvchi ko'rinish va yomon ko'rinishning o'rniga), bu uni haqoratga duchor bo'lganidan ko'ra ko'proq chalg'itishiga olib keldi.

en: Fortunately there was a subject for conversation, and he made haste to snatch at it.
uz: Yaxshiyamki, suhbat uchun bir mavzu bor edi va u tezda uni o'ziga jalb qildi.

en: Hearing that everything was going well and that Rodya had not yet waked, Pulcheria Alexandrovna declared that she was glad to hear
uz: Rodya hali uyg'onmaganligi va hamma narsa yaxshi ketayotganini eshitgach, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna eshitganidan xursand ekanini aytdi.

en: it, because “she had something which it was very, very necessary to talk over beforehand.” Then followed an inquiry about breakfast and an invitation to have it with them; they had waited to have it with him.
uz: Chunki o'zida bir narsa bor edi, bu haqda oldindan gapirish juda muhim edi. So'ngra undan kechki ovqat haqida so'rov va ular bilan birga ovqatlanishga taklif keldi; ular uni o'zlari bilan birga ovqatlanishni kutishgan edi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna rang the bell: it was answered by a ragged dirty waiter, and they asked him to bring tea which was served at last, but in such a dirty and disorderly way that the ladies were ashamed.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna qo'ng'iroqni qo'ng'iroq qildi: unga bir qaroqsiz xizmatkor javob berdi va undan choy olib kelishini so'radilar, ammo oxir-oqibat u shunday qaroq va tartibsiz tarzda xizmat qilindiki, xonimlar uyat chekishdi.

en: Razumihin vigorously attacked the lodgings, but, remembering Luzhin, stopped in embarrassment and was greatly relieved by Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s questions, which showered in a continual stream upon him.
uz: Razumihin uylarga kuchli hujum qildi, lekin Luzhinni eslab, uyatga tushib to'xtadi va Pulcheria Aleksandrovnaning savollari unga to'liq oqib o'tganidan juda xotirjam bo'ldi.

en: He talked for three quarters of an hour, being constantly interrupted by their questions, and succeeded in describing to them all the most important facts he knew of the last year of Raskolnikov’s life, concluding with a circumstantial account of his illness.
uz: U uch chorak soat davomida suhbatlashdi, ularning savollari doimiy ravishda o'z vaqtida kesib turardi va Raskolnikovning hayotining oxirgi yili haqida bilgan eng muhim faktlarni ularga aytib berishga muvaffaq bo'ldi, so'ng kasalligi haqida qisqacha ma'lumot bilan yakunlandi.

en: He omitted, however, many things, which were better omitted, including the scene at the police station with all its consequences.
uz: Biroq, u ko'p narsalarni qoldirdi, ammo bular yaxshiroq qoldirilgan, shu jumladan politsiya bo'linmasidagi voqeani va uning oqibatlarini ham qoldirdi.

en: They listened eagerly to his story, and, when he thought he had finished and satisfied his listeners, he found that they considered he had hardly begun.
uz: Ular uning hikoyasini diqqat bilan tinglashdi va u o'z gapini tugatganini va tinglovchilarini qoniqtirganini o'ylaganda, ular uning boshlanishi haqida o'ylashganini ko'rdi.

en: What do you think … ?
uz: Siz nima deb o'ylaysiz ... ?

en: Excuse me, I still don’t know your name!” Pulcheria Alexandrovna put in hastily.
uz: Kechirasiz, men hali ham sizning ismingizni bilmayman! Pulcheria Aleksandrovna shoshilinchlik bilan qo'ydi.

en: “Dmitri Prokofitch.” “I should like very, very much to know, Dmitri Prokofitch … how he looks … on things in general now, that is, how can I explain, what are his likes and dislikes?
uz: Dmitri Prokofitch. Dmitri Prokofitch ... hozirgi kunda umumiy holatda qanday ko'rinishini bilishni juda, juda xohlayman, ya'ni qanday qilib tushuntirishim mumkin, uning yoqtirgan va yoqtirmagan narsalari nima?

en: Is he always so irritable?
uz: U har doim ham shunday g'azablanadimi?

en: Tell me, if you can, what are his hopes and, so to say, his dreams?
uz: Ayting-chi, mumkin bo'lsa, uning umidlari va, demak, orzulari nima?

en: Under what influences is he now?
uz: Hozir u qanday ta'sir ostida?

en: In a word, I should like …” “Ah, mother, how can he answer all that at once?” observed Dounia.
uz: Bir so'z bilan aytganda, men ...  Ah, ona, u qanday qilib bir vaqtning o'zida bu savollarga javob bera oladi? deb e'tirof etdi Dounia.

en: “Good heavens, I had not expected to find him in the least like this, Dmitri Prokofitch!” “Naturally,” answered Razumihin.
uz: Albatta, men uni hech qachon bunday holda topishni kutmagan edim, Dmitri Prokofitch!Ta'kidlab o'tamiz,-da javob berdi Razumihin.

en: “I have no mother, but my uncle comes every year and almost every time he can scarcely recognise me, even in appearance, though he is a clever man; and your three years’ separation means a great deal.
uz: Mening onam yo'q, lekin o'g'lim har yili kelib turadi va deyarli har safar meni hatto ko'rinishda ham tanira olmaydi, garchi u aqlli odam bo'lsa-da; uch yillik ajralishingiz juda katta ahamiyatga ega.

en: What am I to tell you?
uz: Sizga nima deyishim kerak?

en: I have known Rodion for a year and a half; he is morose, gloomy, proud and haughty, and of late —and perhaps for a long time before —he
uz: Rodionni bir yarim yildan beri bilaman; u g'alati, nozik, mag'rur va mag'rur va oxirgi paytlarda ham, ehtimol uzoq vaqt oldin ham.

en: has been suspicious and fanciful.
uz: shubhasiz va g'ayritabiiy bo'lgan.

en: He has a noble nature and a kind heart.
uz: U buyuk tabiat va mehribon yurakga ega.

en: He does not like showing his feelings and would rather do a cruel thing than open his heart freely.
uz: U o'z his-tuyg'ularini ko'rsatishni yoqtirmaydi va yuragini erkin ochishdan ko'ra shafqatsiz ish qilishni afzal ko'radi.

en: Sometimes, though, he is not at all morbid, but simply cold and inhumanly callous; it’s as though he were alternating between two characters.
uz: Ammo ba'zan u umuman kasal emas, balki shunchaki sovuq va insonparvarlik bilan shafqatsiz bo'ladi; xuddi ikkita belgi o'rtasida o'zgarib turgandek.

en: Sometimes he is fearfully reserved!
uz: Ba'zan u qo'rqinchli ravishda cheklangan bo'ladi!

en: He says he is so busy that everything is a hindrance, and yet he lies in bed doing nothing.
uz: U o'zining shunchalik bandligini aytadiki, hamma narsa to'sqinlik qiladi, ammo u hech narsa qilmay, to'shagida yotadi.

en: He doesn’t jeer at things, not because he hasn’t the wit, but as though he hadn’t time to waste on such trifles.
uz: U biron narsaga kulmaydi, chunki u aqlsiz emas, balki bunday mayda-mayda ishlarga vaqt sarflashga vaqt yo'qdek.

en: He never listens to what is said to him.
uz: U hech qachon unga aytilganlarni tinglamaydi.

en: He is never interested in what interests other people at any given moment.
uz: U hech qachon boshqa odamlarning qiziqishi bilan qiziqmaydi.

en: He thinks very highly of himself and perhaps he is right.
uz: U o'zi haqida juda yuqori fikrda va ehtimol haqli.

en: I think your arrival will have a most beneficial influence upon him.” “God grant it may,” cried Pulcheria Alexandrovna, distressed by Razumihin’s account of her Rodya.
uz: Menimcha, sizning kelishingiz unga juda yaxshi ta'sir qiladi. Xudo xohlasa, shunday deb hayqirdi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, Razumihinning Rodya haqidagi hikoyasidan xafa bo'lgan.

en: And Razumihin ventured to look more boldly at Avdotya Romanovna at last.
uz: Va Razumihin nihoyat Avdotya Romanovnaga yanada jasoratli qarashga jur'at qildi.

en: He glanced at her often while he was talking, but only for a moment and looked away again at once.
uz: U suhbatlashayotganda ko'pincha qizga ko'z tikdi, lekin bir zumdan so'ng yana bir bor yuz o'girib ko'rdi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna sat at the table, listening attentively, then got up again and began walking to and fro with her arms folded and her lips compressed, occasionally putting in a question, without stopping her walk.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna o'tirib, diqqat bilan tinglab turardi, so'ngra yana turib, qo'llarini yopib, og'izlarini siqib yurishni boshladi, vaqti-vaqti bilan savol berishni davom ettirdi, yurishni to'xtatmay.

en: She had the same habit of not listening to what was said.
uz: U gaplarni tinglamaslik odati bor edi.

en: She was wearing a dress of thin dark stuff and she had a white transparent scarf round her neck.
uz: U cho'g'ir qorong'u moddalardan yasalgan kiyim kiygan edi va bo'yniga oq, shaffof shal kiygan edi.

en: Razumihin soon detected signs of extreme poverty in their belongings.
uz: Razumihinlar tez orada o'z mol-mulklarida nihoyatda kambag'allik belgilarini ko'rishdi.

en: Had Avdotya Romanovna been dressed like a queen, he felt that he would not be afraid of her, but perhaps just because she was poorly dressed and that he noticed all the misery of her surroundings, his heart was filled with dread and he began to be afraid of every word he uttered, every gesture he made, which was very trying for a man who already felt diffident.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna shohona kiyingan bo'lsa, u undan qo'rqmasligini his qilgan, balki ehtimol u yomon kiyim kiyganligi va atrofidagi barcha azob-uqubatlarga e'tibor berganligi sababli uning yuragi qo'rquvga to'lib, u aytgan har bir so'zdan, qilgan har bir harakatidan qo'rqishga tushdi.

en: “You’ve told us a great deal that is interesting about my brother’s character … and have told it impartially.
uz: Siz bizga akamning shaxsiyati to'g'risida qiziqarli ma'lumotlar aytdingiz va bu haqda yuzxotirchiliksiz gapirdingiz.

en: I thought that you were too uncritically devoted to him,” observed Avdotya Romanovna with a smile.
uz: Men siz unga juda tanqid qilmagan deb o'yladim, - dedi Avdotya Romanovna tabassum bilan.

en: “I think you are right that he needs a woman’s care,” she added thoughtfully.
uz: Men o'ylaymanki, u ayolning g'amxo'rligiga muhtoj ekanligi to'g'risida to'g'ri fikrda ekansiz, deb o'ylayman,  deb o'ylab qo'shimcha qildi.

en: “I didn’t say so; but I daresay you are right, only …” “What?”
uz: Men shunday aytmaganman; lekin men siz haqli ekanligingizni aytaman, faqatgina ... nima?

en: “He loves no one and perhaps he never will,” Razumihin declared decisively.
uz: U hech kimni sevmaydi va ehtimol hech qachon sevmaydi,  Razumihin qat'iy qaror qildi.

en: “You mean he is not capable of love?” “Do you know, Avdotya Romanovna, you are awfully like your brother, in everything, indeed!” he blurted out suddenly to his own surprise, but remembering at once what he had just before said of her brother, he turned as red as a crab and was overcome with confusion.
uz: Sening aytgansanki, u sevishga qodir emas? Avdotya Romanovna, siz o'z ukangizga juda o'xshaysiz, albatta, hamma narsada! U o'zidan ajablanib, to'satdan o'zini o'zgartirdi, lekin o'sha paytdan boshlab uning ukasi haqida aytganlarini eslab, u karvacha qizillashib, chalg'ib ketdi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna couldn’t help laughing when she looked at him.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna unga qaraganida kulishidan qo'rqmadi.

en: “You may both be mistaken about Rodya,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna remarked, slightly piqued.
uz: "Rodya haqida ikkalaingiz ham noto'g'ri fikrda bo'lishingiz mumkin", - dedi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, biroz g'alati.

en: “I am not talking of our present difficulty, Dounia.
uz: Men hozirgi qiyinchiliklarimiz haqida gapirmayapman, Dounia.

en: What Pyotr Petrovitch writes in this letter and what you and I have supposed may be mistaken, but you can’t imagine, Dmitri Prokofitch, how moody and, so to say, capricious he is.
uz: Pyotr Petroviçning ushbu maktubda yozganlari va biz siz va biz o'ylaganimiz noto'g'ri bo'lishi mumkin, lekin siz Dmitriy Prokofitch, uning qanchalik ruhoniy va, demak, capricious ekanligini tasavvur qila olmaysiz.

en: I never could depend on what he would do when he was only fifteen.
uz: U atigi o'n besh yoshda bo'lganida nima qilishni hech qachon kutolmasdim.

en: And I am sure that he might do something now that nobody else would think of doing … Well, for instance, do you know how a year and a half ago he astounded me and gave me a shock that nearly killed me, when he had the idea of marrying that girl —what was her name —his landlady’s daughter?” “Did you hear about that affair?” asked Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Endi esa u boshqa hech kim o'ylamagan narsani qilishi mumkinligiga aminman ... Masalan, bir yarim yil oldin u meni hayratda qoldirib, o'limga yetarlicha qo'rqinch keltirdi, chunki u o'sha qiz bilan turmush qurish g'oyasi paydo bo'lgan edi.

en: “Do you suppose —” Pulcheria Alexandrovna continued warmly.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna issiqlik bilan davom etdi, deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: “Do you suppose that my tears, my entreaties, my illness, my possible death from grief, our poverty would have made him pause?
uz: Sizningcha, ko'z yoshlarim, iltijolarim, kasalligim, qayg'u tufayli bo'lgan o'limim, kambag'alligimiz uni to'xtatishga undardi?

en: No, he would calmly have disregarded all obstacles.
uz: Yo'q, u har qanday to'siqlarni xotirjamlik bilan e'tiborsiz qoldirgan bo'lardi.

en: And yet it isn’t that he doesn’t love us!” “He has never spoken a word of that affair to me,” Razumihin answered cautiously.
uz: Lekin U bizni sevmaydi degan gap emas! U menga bu haqda hech qachon bir so'z aytmagan, Razumihin ehtiyotkorlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “But I did hear something from Praskovya Pavlovna herself, though she is by no means a gossip.
uz: Lekin Praskovya Pavlovnaning o'zidan biror narsa eshitdim, ammo u hech qachon g'iybat emas.

en: And what I heard certainly was rather strange.” “And what did you hear?” both the ladies asked at once.
uz: Va men eshitgan narsa, albatta, o'ta g'alati edi. Va siz nima eshitgansiz? Ikkala ayol ham birdan so'radilar.

en: “Well, nothing very special.
uz: Xo'sh, hech qanday maxsus narsa yo'q.

en: I only learned that the marriage, which only failed to take place through the girl’s death, was not at all to Praskovya Pavlovna’s liking.
uz: Faqatgina qizning o'limi tufayli amalga oshmagan nikohning Praskovya Pavlovnaga yoqmaganini bilib oldim.

en: They say, too, the girl was not at all pretty, in fact I am told positively ugly … and such an invalid … and queer.
uz: Shuningdek, ular qizning hech qanday chiroyli emasligini aytishadi, aslida menga juda achinarli va bevafo va g'ayritabiiy deb aytishadi.

en: But she seems to have had some good qualities.
uz: Ammo u yaxshi fazilatlarga ega bo'lgan ko'rinadi.

en: She must have had some good qualities or it’s quite inexplicable.
uz: U yaxshi fazilatlarga ega bo'lgan bo'lishi kerak, yoki buni tushuntirib bo'lmaydi.

en: no money either and he wouldn’t have considered her money.
uz: Pul ham yo'q va u ham uning pulini ko'rib chiqmagan bo'lardi.

en: … But it’s always difficult to judge in such matters.” “I am sure she was a good girl,” Avdotya Romanovna observed briefly.
uz: Ammo bunday masalalarda hukm qilish har doim qiyin.Men uning yaxshi qiz ekanligiga aminman, Avdotya Romanovna qisqacha aytdi.

en: “God forgive me, I simply rejoiced at her death.
uz: Xudo meni kechirsin, men shunchaki uning o'limidan xursand bo'ldim.

en: Though I don’t know which of them would have caused most misery to the other — he to her or she to him,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna concluded.
uz: Garchi ulardan qaysi biri boshqa birovga ko'proq azob keltirishi mumkinligini bilmasam-da, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna so'zlariga yakun yasadi.

en: Then she began tentatively questioning him about the scene on the previous day with Luzhin, hesitating and continually glancing at Dounia, obviously to the latter’s annoyance.
uz: So'ngra u Luzhin bilan o'tgan kuni yuz bergan voqeadan so'roq qila boshladi, ikkilanadi va Douniaga uzluksiz qarab turardi, bu esa uning xafa bo'lishiga sabab bo'ldi.

en: This incident more than all the rest evidently caused her uneasiness, even consternation.
uz: Bu hodisa, boshqa barcha hodisalardan ko'ra, uning xavotirini, hatto qo'rqinchini keltirib chiqardi.

en: Razumihin described it in detail again, but this time he added his own conclusions: he openly blamed Raskolnikov for intentionally insulting Pyotr Petrovitch, not seeking to excuse him on the score of his illness.
uz: Razumihin buni yana batafsil tushuntirdi, ammo bu safar o'z xulosalarini qo'shdi: u Raskolnikovni kasalligi tufayli uzr izlamasdan, Pyotr Petrovitchni qasddan haqoratlaganligi uchun ochiqchasiga aybladi.

en: “He had planned it before his illness,” he added.
uz: U kasalligidan oldin buni rejalashtirgan edi, deb qo'shimcha qildi.

en: “I think so, too,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna agreed with a dejected air.
uz: Men ham shunday o'ylayman, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna bu fikrga rozi bo'ldi.

en: But she was very much surprised at hearing Razumihin express himself so carefully and even with a certain respect about Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Ammo u Razumihinning Pyotr Petrovitchga nisbatan o'zini shunchalik ehtiyotkorlik bilan va hatto hurmat bilan izhor etishini eshitib juda hayron qoldi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna, too, was struck by it.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna ham bu bilan hayratda qoldi.

en: “So this is your opinion of Pyotr Petrovitch?” Pulcheria Alexandrovna could not resist asking.
uz: Demak, Pyotr Petrovitch haqida sizning fikringiz shundaymi? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna so'rashdan bosh tortolmadi.

en: “I can have no other opinion of your daughter’s future husband,” Razumihin answered firmly and with warmth, “and I don’t say it simply from vulgar politeness, but because … simply because Avdotya Romanovna has of her own free will deigned to accept this man.
uz: Qizingizning bo'lajak eri haqida boshqa fikrga ega bo'lmayman, deb javob berdi Razumihin qat'iy va iliqlik bilan, va men buni shunchaki vulgar xushmuomalalik bilan aytmayman, balki Avdotya Romanovnaning bu odamni qabul qilishga munosib bo'lgani uchun.

en: If I spoke so rudely of him last night, it was because I was disgustingly drunk and … mad besides; yes, mad, crazy, I lost my head completely … and this morning I am ashamed of it.” He crimsoned and ceased speaking.
uz: Kecha uning haqida shunday qo'pol gapirganimda, bu men jirkanch ichganim va... g'alati bo'lganim uchun edi; ha, g'alati, g'alati bo'lganim uchun, butunlay boshimni yo'qotib yubordim... va bu kuni ertalab men bundan uyalganman. U qizil ko'rindi va gapirishni to'xtatdi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna flushed, but did not break the silence.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna o'zini ko'tardi, ammo ovozini buzmadi.

en: She had not uttered a word from the moment they began to speak of Luzhin.
uz: Ular Luzhin haqida gapira boshlagan paytdan boshlab u bir so'z ham aytmagan edi.

en: Without her support Pulcheria Alexandrovna obviously did not know what to do.
uz: Uning qo'llab-quvvatlanmaganda Pulcheria Aleksandrovna nima qilishni bilmasdi.

en: At last, faltering and continually glancing at her daughter, she confessed that she was exceedingly worried by one circumstance.
uz: Nihoyat, qizini ko'rib turib, o'zidan-o'zidan xavotirlanayotganini aytdi.

en: “You see, Dmitri Prokofitch,” she began.
uz: Qarang, Dmitri Prokofitch, u boshladi.

en: “I’ll be perfectly open with Dmitri Prokofitch, Dounia?” “Of course, mother,” said Avdotya Romanovna emphatically.
uz: Dmitriy Prokofitch bilan to'liq ochiq bo'lamanmi, Dounia? Albatta, ona, Avdotya Romanovna ta'kidlab o'tdi.

en: “This is what it is,” she began in haste, as though the permission to speak of her trouble lifted a weight off her mind.
uz: Bu nima, u shoshilmay boshladi, xuddi muammo haqida gapirishga ruxsat berish uning ongidan og'irlikni olib tashlagandek.

en: “Very early this morning we got a note from Pyotr Petrovitch in reply to our letter announcing our arrival.
uz: Bugun ertalab Pyotr Petroviçdan kelganimizni e'lon qilgan maktubimizga javob sifatida xat oldik.

en: He promised to meet us at the station, you know; instead of that he sent a servant to bring us the address of these lodgings and to show us the way; and he sent a message that he would be here himself this morning.
uz: U biz bilan stantsiyada uchrashishni va'da qildi, ammo o'rniga xizmatkorini yuborib, bu uylarning manzilini keltirib, yo'lni ko'rsatdi va bu ertalab u o'zi bu yerda bo'lishi haqida xabar yubordi.

en: But this morning this note came from him.
uz: Ammo bugun ertalab u tomonidan bu xat keldi.

en: You’d better read it yourself; there is one point in it which worries me very much … you will soon see what that is, and … tell me your candid opinion, Dmitri Prokofitch!
uz: O'zingiz o'qib ko'ring; bu kitobda meni juda xavotirlantiradigan bir narsa bor ... bu nima ekanligini tezda bilib olasiz va ... menga o'zingizning aniq fikringizni ayting, Dmitriy Prokofitch!

en: You know Rodya’s character better than anyone and no one can advise us better than you can.
uz: Siz Rodyaning xarakterini har kimdan yaxshiroq bilasiz va hech kim bizga sizdan yaxshiroq maslahat bera olmaydi.

en: Dounia, I must tell you, made her decision at once, but I still don’t feel sure how to act and I … I’ve been waiting for your opinion.” Razumihin opened the note which was dated the previous evening and read as follows: “Dear Madam, Pulcheria Alexandrovna, I have the honour to inform you that owing to unforeseen obstacles I was rendered unable to meet you at the railway station; I sent a very competent person with the same object in view.
uz: Sizga aytishim kerakki, Dounia o'z qarorini darhol qabul qildi, lekin men hali ham qanday harakat qilishim kerakligini bilmayman va men ... sizning fikringizni kutdim. Razumihin o'tgan kecha sanab o'tilgan notani ochdi va quyidagicha o'qib berdi: Soniyning aziz xonim Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, men sizga xabar berish sharafiga egamanki, kutilmagan to'siqlar tufayli men siz bilan temir yo'l stansiyasida uchrasholmadim; men xuddi shu maqsadga ega bo'lgan juda malakali kishini yubordim.

en: I likewise shall be deprived of the honour of an interview with you tomorrow morning by business in the Senate that does not admit of delay, and also that I may not intrude on your family circle while you are meeting your son, and Avdotya Romanovna her brother.
uz: Shuningdek, sening o'g'ling va uning ukasi Avdotya Romanovna bilan uchrashayotganingda oilangiz bilan suhbatlashish sharafini men ham ertalab Senatda kechiktirishni e'tirof etmaydigan ish bilan o'tkazaman.

en: I shall have the honour of visiting you and paying you my respects at your lodgings not later than tomorrow evening at eight o’clock precisely, and herewith I venture to present my earnest and, I may add, imperative request that Rodion Romanovitch may not be present at our interview —as he offered me a gross and unprecedented affront on the occasion of my visit to him in his illness yesterday, and, moreover, since I desire from you personally an indispensable and circumstantial explanation upon a certain point, in regard to which I wish to learn your own interpretation.
uz: Sizlarni tashrif buyurib, ertaga soat sakkizdan kechikmay uyingizda hurmatimni izhor etish sharafiga ega bo'laman va shu bilan Rodion Romanovitchning suhbatimizga bormasligi uchun chin dildan va, qo'shimcha qilib aytaman, talabimni bildirishga jur'at qilaman, chunki u o'tgan kuni kasalligida unga tashrif buyurganimda menga katta va misli ko'rilmagan haqorat ko'rsatdi va, bundan tashqari, men shaxsan sizdan muayyan bir masalaga bo'lgan mutlaqo va shartsiz tushuntirishni so'rayman, bu haqda o'zingizning ta'rifingizni o'rganishni xohlayman.

en: I have the honour to inform you, in
uz: Sizlarni xabardor qilish sharafiga ega bo'laman.

en: anticipation, that if, in spite of my request, I meet Rodion Romanovitch, I shall be compelled to withdraw immediately and then you have only yourself to blame.
uz: Agar men, so'rovimga qaramay, Rodion Romanovitch bilan uchrasam, darhol voz kechishga majbur bo'laman va o'zingiz aybdor bo'lasiz.

en: I write on the assumption that Rodion Romanovitch who appeared so ill at my visit, suddenly recovered two hours later and so, being able to leave the house, may visit you also.
uz: Men tashrifimda shunchalik kasal ko'rinadigan Rodion Romanovitch ikki soat o'tgach to'satdan sog'ayib ketgani va uydan chiqib ketishi mumkin bo'lganligi sababli sizni ham tashrif buyurishi mumkinligi haqida yozaman.

en: I was confirmed in that belief by the testimony of my own eyes in the lodging of a drunken man who was run over and has since died, to whose daughter, a young woman of notorious behaviour, he gave twenty-five roubles on the pretext of the funeral, which gravely surprised me knowing what pains you were at to raise that sum.
uz: O'zimning ko'zim bilan ko'rgan guvohligim tufayli men o'zimni o'ldirgan bir ichkilikbozning uyida o'ldirganman, uning qiziga, notoriyalangan xulq-atvorli yosh ayolga, u o'z o'limi uchun yigirma besh rubl pulini ko'rsatdi, bu esa meni juda hayratda qoldirdi, chunki siz bu miqdorni to'plash uchun qanday qiyinchiliklarga duch kelganingizni bildim.

en: Herewith expressing my special respect to your estimable daughter, Avdotya Romanovna, I beg you to accept the respectful homage of “Your humble servant, “P.
uz: Shu bilan birga, aziz qizingiz Avdotya Romanovnaga alohida e'tiborimni bildirgan holda, sizlardan sizning kamtarin xizmatkoringiz, P.ning hurmatli e'tirozini qabul qilishingizni so'rayman.

en: Luzhin.” “What am I to do now, Dmitri Prokofitch?” began Pulcheria Alexandrovna, almost weeping.
uz: Luzhin.  Endi nima qilishim kerak, Dmitri Prokofitch? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna boshladi, deyarli yig'lab qoldi.

en: “How can I ask Rodya not to come?
uz: Rodyaga kelmasligini qanday so'rasam bo'ladi?

en: Yesterday he insisted so earnestly on our refusing Pyotr Petrovitch and now we are ordered not to receive Rodya!
uz: Kecha u Pyotr Petroviçni rad etishimizni qattiq istaydi va endi Rodyani qabul qilmaslikka buyurildi!

en: He will come on purpose if he knows, and … what will happen then?” “Act on Avdotya Romanovna’s decision,” Razumihin answered calmly at once.
uz: Agar bilsa, u qasddan keladi va... keyin nima bo'ladi?Avdotya Romanovnaning qaroriga amal qilish, Razumihin darhol xotirjamlik bilan javob berdi.

en: She says … goodness knows what she says, she doesn’t explain her object!
uz: U shunday deydi... Xudo biladi, nima deyishini, o'z ob'ektini tushuntirmaydi!

en: She says that it would be best, at least, not that it would be best, but that it’s absolutely necessary that Rodya should make a point of being here at eight o’clock and that they must meet.
uz: U eng yaxshisi bo'lishi kerakligini aytadi, hech bo'lmaganda, bu eng yaxshi bo'lishi kerakligini aytmaydi, balki Rodya soat sakkizlarda bu yerda bo'lishga qat'iy qaror qilishi va ular uchrashishi kerakligini aytadi.

en: … I didn’t want even to show him the letter, but to prevent him from coming by some stratagem with your help … because he is so irritable.
uz: Men unga xatni ko'rsatmoqchi emasdim, balki sizning yordamingiz bilan biron bir hiyla-nayrang bilan kelishiga yo'l qo'ymayman, chunki u juda g'azablanadi.

en: … Besides I don’t understand about that drunkard who died and that daughter, and how he could have given the daughter all the money … which …” “Which cost you such sacrifice, mother,” put in Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Bundan tashqari, men o'lgan ichkilikboz va o'sha qiz haqida tushunmayapman va qanday qilib u qizga barcha pulni bergan bo'lishi mumkinligini tushunmayapman ... Bu ...Bu sizga shunday qurbonlik qildi, ona, Avdotya Romanovnaga qo'ydi.

en: “He was not himself yesterday,” Razumihin said thoughtfully, “if you only knew what he was up to in a restaurant yesterday, though there
uz: U o'zi o'zi emas edi kecha,  Razumihin o'ylab so'radi, Agar siz o'sha yerda kechqurun restoranda nima qilayotganini bilsangiz edi.

en: was sense in it too.
uz: Bu ham ma'noli edi.

en: He did say something, as we were going home yesterday evening, about a dead man and a girl, but I didn’t understand a word.
uz: Kecha kechasi uyga qaytayotganimizda, u bir o'lik va bir qiz haqida gapirgan edi, lekin men bir so'zni ham tushunmadim.

en: … But last night, I myself …” “The best thing, mother, will be for us to go to him ourselves and there I assure you we shall see at once what’s to be done.
uz: Ammo o'tgan kechasi men o'zim ... Eng yaxshisi, ona, biz o'zimiz Uning oldiga boramiz va u erda sizga ishontiramanki, nima qilish kerakligini darhol ko'ramiz.

en: Besides, it’s getting late —good heavens, it’s past ten,” she cried looking at a splendid gold enamelled watch which hung round her neck on a thin Venetian chain, and looked entirely out of keeping with the rest of her dress.
uz: Bundan tashqari, kech bo'lib qoldi, o'n soat o'tibdi, u o'zining bo'sh bo'sh bo'lib qolgan kiyimidan butunlay farq qilgan holda, bo'sh bo'sh bo'lib qolgan sovg'a bilan bo'lgan bo'sh oltin esmalashtirilgan soatni ko'rib yig'ladi.

en: “A present from her fiancé,” thought Razumihin.
uz: O'zining nişanchisidan sovg'a, deb o'yladi Razumihin.

en: “We must start, Dounia, we must start,” her mother cried in a flutter.
uz: Biz boshlashimiz kerak, Dounia, biz boshlashimiz kerak, onasi qichqiriq bilan yig'ladi.

en: “He will be thinking we are still angry after yesterday, from our coming so late.
uz: U kech kelganimizdan keyin ham biz hali ham g'azablanamiz deb o'ylaydi.

en: Merciful heavens!” While she said this she was hurriedly putting on her hat and mantle; Dounia, too, put on her things.
uz: Rahmatli osmonlar! Buni aytayotganida, u tezda o'z to'pkasi va choriqini kiyib oldi; Dounia ham o'z narsalarini kiyib oldi.

en: Her gloves, as Razumihin noticed, were not merely shabby but had holes in them, and yet this evident poverty gave the two ladies an air of special dignity, which is always found in people who know how to wear poor clothes.
uz: Razumihin ko'rganidek, uning qo'lqoplari shunchaki yomon emas edi, balki ichlarida toshlar bor edi va shunga qaramay, bu aniq kambag'allik ikki xonimga alohida qadr-qimmatga ega bo'lgan tuyg'u berdi, bu esa har doim kambag'al kiyim kiyishni bilgan odamlarda ko'rish mumkin.

en: Razumihin looked reverently at Dounia and felt proud of escorting her.
uz: Razumihin Douniaga hurmat ila qaradi va u bilan birga bo'lganidan g'ururlanadi.
