en: “The queen who mended her stockings in prison,” he thought, “must have looked then every inch a queen and even more a queen than at sumptuous banquets and levées.” “My God!” exclaimed Pulcheria Alexandrovna, “little did I think that I should ever fear seeing my son, my darling, darling Rodya!
uz: Zindonlikda choynaklarini tuzatgan qirolicha, o'zi o'ylaganidek, o'shanda har bir santimetrdan bir xil qirolicha va hatto hashamatli tantanalar va levilarda bo'lganidan ko'ra ko'proq qirolicha ko'rinadi.

en: I am afraid, Dmitri Prokofitch,” she added, glancing at him timidly.
uz: Qo'rqaman, Dmitri Prokofitch, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u, u o'z ko'zidan ko'z yumgan holda unga qarab.

en: “Don’t be afraid, mother,” said Dounia, kissing her, “better have faith in him.” “Oh, dear, I have faith in him, but I haven’t slept all night,” exclaimed the poor woman.
uz: Qo'rqma, ona, - dedi Dounia, uni o'pib, - unga ishonish yaxshiroqdir. - Oh, azizim, men unga ishonaman, lekin men butun kecha uxlamaganman, - dedi kambag'al ayol.

en: They came out into the street.
uz: Ular ko'chaga chiqishdi.

en: “Do you know, Dounia, when I dozed a little this morning I dreamed of Marfa Petrovna … she was all in white … she came up to me, took my hand, and shook her head at me, but so sternly as though she were blaming me.
uz: Bilasizmi, Dounia, bu kuni ertalab biroz uxlaganimda, Marfa Petrovna haqida orzu qildim ... u butunlay oq kiyimda edi ... menga yaqinlashdi, qo'limdan ushlab, boshini menga shovqirdi, lekin xuddi meni ayblayotgan bo'lsa kerak.

en: … Is that a good omen?
uz: Bu yaxshi belgimi?

en: You don’t know, Dmitri Prokofitch, that Marfa Petrovna’s dead!” “No, I didn’t know; who is Marfa Petrovna?” “She died suddenly; and only fancy …”
uz: Siz bilmaysiz, Dmitri Prokofitch, Marfa Petrovna o'lganini!Yo'q, men bilmasdim; Marfa Petrovna kim?U to'satdan vafot etdi; va faqat o'ylash ...

en: “Afterwards, mamma,” put in Dounia.
uz: Afterwards, mama, qo'ying Dounia.

en: “He doesn’t know who Marfa Petrovna is.” “Ah, you don’t know?
uz: U Marfa Petrovna kimligini bilmaydi.Ah, siz bilmayapsizmi?

en: And I was thinking that you knew all about us.
uz: Men esa siz biz haqimizda hamma narsani bilasiz deb o'yladim.

en: Forgive me, Dmitri Prokofitch, I don’t know what I am thinking about these last few days.
uz: Kechirasiz, Dmitri Prokofitch, men so'nggi kunlarda nima haqida o'ylayotganimni bilmayman.

en: I look upon you really as a providence for us, and so I took it for granted that you knew all about us.
uz: Sizni biz uchun Xudovand O'zi ko'rib turibdi, shuning uchun siz biz haqimizda hamma narsani bilarsiz, deb o'yladim.

en: I look on you as a relation.
uz: Men sizlarni munosabat sifatida ko'raman.

en: … Don’t be angry with me for saying so.
uz: Men shunday gapirganimdan g'azablanma.

en: Dear me, what’s the matter with your right hand?
uz: Qizim, o'ng qo'lingda nima bor?

en: Have you knocked it?” “Yes, I bruised it,” muttered Razumihin overjoyed.
uz: Uni taqillatdingizmi? Ha, men uni yaraladim, shodlik bilan Razumihin g'iybat qildi.

en: “I sometimes speak too much from the heart, so that Dounia finds fault with me.
uz: Ba'zan men ko'p so'zlarni yuragimdan gapiraman, shuning uchun Dounia men bilan yomon munosabatda bo'ladi.

en: … But, dear me, what a cupboard he lives in!
uz: Ammo, azizim, u qanday do'konda yashaydi!

en: I wonder whether he is awake?
uz: O'ylaymanki, u uyg'onadimi?

en: Does this woman, his landlady, consider it a room?
uz: Bu ayol, uning uy egasi, uni xona deb biladimi?

en: Listen, you say he does not like to show his feelings, so perhaps I shall annoy him with my … weaknesses?
uz: Quloq soling, siz uning his-tuyg'ularini bildirishni yoqtirmasligini aytasiz, shuning uchun men uni mening ... zaifliklarim bilan bezovta qilsam bo'ladimi?

en: Do advise me, Dmitri Prokofitch, how am I to treat him?
uz: Menga maslahat ber, Dmitri Prokofitch, unga qanday munosabatda bo'lishim kerak?

en: I feel quite distracted, you know.” “Don’t question him too much about anything if you see him frown; don’t ask him too much about his health; he doesn’t like that.” “Ah, Dmitri Prokofitch, how hard it is to be a mother!
uz: O'zimni juda chalg'itdim, bilasiz. Agar uni ko'rsangiz, yuz o'girganini ko'rsangiz, hech narsa haqida undan ortiq so'ramang; sog'lig'i haqida undan ortiq so'ramang; bu unga yoqmaydi.Ah, Dmitriy Prokofitch, ona bo'lish qanchalik qiyin!

en: But here are the stairs.
uz: Ammo mana bu mertarlar.

en: … What an awful staircase!” “Mother, you are quite pale, don’t distress yourself, darling,” said Dounia caressing her, then with flashing eyes she added: “He ought to be happy at seeing you, and you are tormenting yourself so.” “Wait, I’ll peep in and see whether he has waked up.” The ladies slowly followed Razumihin, who went on before, and when they reached the landlady’s door on the fourth storey, they noticed that her door was a tiny crack open and that two keen black eyes were watching them from the darkness within.
uz: Qanday dahshatli qadam!  Onam, sen juda achchiqsan, o'zingni bezovta qilma, azizim, - dedi Dounia, uni yonboshladi, so'ngra chaqmoqli ko'zlar bilan qo'shimcha qildi:  U seni ko'rib xursand bo'lishi kerak, va sen o'zingni shunday qiynayapsan.  Beklab tur, men o'zimni ko'rib turibman. Xotinlar oldin ketayotgan Razumihinni sekin-sekin kuzatib borishdi va to'rtinchi qavatdagi uy egasining eshiga yetib kelganlarida, uning eshigining kichkina bo'g'i ochiq ekanini va ichkaridan ikkita qora ko'z ularni qorong'ilikdan kuzatib borayotganini payqadilar.

en: When their eyes met, the door was suddenly shut with such a slam that Pulcheria Alexandrovna almost cried out.
uz: Ularning ko'zlari to'qnashganida, eshik to'satdan shunchalik qattiq yopildiki, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna deyarli baqirib yubordi.

en: III “He is well, quite well!” Zossimov cried cheerfully as they entered.
uz: III U sog'lom, juda sog'lom! Zossimov ular kirganida quvonch ila yig'ladi.

en: He had come in ten minutes earlier and was sitting in the same place as before, on the sofa.
uz: U o'n daqiqa oldin kelib, avvalgi joyda, kanepada o'tirgan edi.

en: Raskolnikov was sitting in the opposite corner, fully dressed and carefully washed and combed, as he had not been for some time past.
uz: Raskolnikov qarama-qarshi burchada o'tirgan edi, u to'liq kiyim-kechak kiygan va bir muncha vaqtdan beri o'tib ketmagan bo'lgani uchun juda ehtiyotkorlik bilan yuvilib, pishirib o'tirgan edi.

en: The room was immediately crowded, yet Nastasya managed to follow the visitors in and stayed to listen.
uz: Xona darhol to'la bo'lib ketdi, lekin Nastasya tashrif buyuruvchilarni kuzatib kirib, tinglab qoldi.

en: Raskolnikov really was almost well, as compared with his condition the day before, but he was still pale, listless, and sombre.
uz: Raskolnikov o'tgan kun holatiga nisbatan deyarli sog'lom edi, ammo u hali ham soya, istaksiz va qorong'i edi.

en: He looked like a wounded man or one who has undergone some terrible physical suffering.
uz: U jarohatlangan odamga yoki dahshatli jismoniy azoblarga duchor bo'lgan odamga o'xshardi.

en: His brows were knitted, his lips compressed, his eyes feverish.
uz: Uning burunlari tikilgan, og'izlari siqilgan, ko'zlari issiq.

en: He spoke little and reluctantly, as though performing a duty, and there was a restlessness in his movements.
uz: U o'z vazifasini bajarayotgandek, kam va istaksiz gapirgan va harakatlarida xotirjamlik bo'lgan.

en: He only wanted a sling on his arm or a bandage on his finger to complete the impression of a man with a painful abscess or a broken arm.
uz: U faqat og'riqli absces yoki buzilgan qo'li bo'lgan odamning taassurotini to'ldirish uchun qo'lida chastak yoki barmog'ida bandaj bo'lishini xohlagan.

en: The pale, sombre face lighted up for a moment when his mother and sister entered, but this only gave it a look of more intense suffering, in place of its listless dejection.
uz: Onasi va singlisi kirganida, sochiq va qorong'i yuzi bir zum yorug' bo'ldi, ammo bu uning g'amgin tushkunligi o'rniga, yanada og'irroq azob ko'rinishiga sabab bo'ldi.

en: The light soon died away, but the look of suffering remained, and Zossimov, watching and studying his patient with all the zest of a young doctor beginning to practise, noticed in him no joy at the arrival of his mother and sister, but a sort of bitter, hidden determination to bear another hour or two of inevitable torture.
uz: Shoshilinch o'tib ketdi, lekin azob ko'rinishi saqlanib qoldi va Zossimov bemorini yosh shifokorning mashg'ul bo'lish paytida ko'rib, o'rganayotgan bo'lsa, onasi va singlisi kelganidan xursand emas, balki yana bir soat yoki ikki soat azob chekish uchun bir xil achchiq va yashirin qarorni ko'rdi.

en: He saw later that almost every word of the following conversation seemed to touch on some sore place and irritate it.
uz: Keyinchalik u, keyingi suhbatning deyarli har bir so'zi qayg'uli joyga tegib, uni g'azablantirganini ko'rdi.

en: But at the same time he marvelled at the power of controlling himself and hiding his feelings in a patient who the
uz: Ammo u o'zini nazorat qilish va his-tuyg'ularini o'zi biladigan bemorga yashirish qobiliyatiga hayron edi.

en: previous day had, like a monomaniac, fallen into a frenzy at the slightest word.
uz: O'tgan kun monomanik kabi eng kichik bir so'zdan g'alati bo'lgan edi.

en: “Yes, I see myself now that I am almost well,” said Raskolnikov, giving his mother and sister a kiss of welcome which made Pulcheria Alexandrovna radiant at once.
uz: Ha, hozir o'zimni ko'ryapman, deyarli sog'lomman, dedi Raskolnikov, onasi va singlisiga pulcheria Aleksandrovnani birdan yorug' qilib qo'ygan salom o'pishini berdi.

en: “And I don’t say this as I did yesterday,” he said, addressing Razumihin, with a friendly pressure of his hand.
uz: Men buni kecha aytganimdek aytmayapman, - dedi u, Razumihinga murojaat qilib, qo'lini do'stlik bilan bosadi.

en: “Yes, indeed, I am quite surprised at him today,” began Zossimov, much delighted at the ladies’ entrance, for he had not succeeded in keeping up a conversation with his patient for ten minutes.
uz: "Ha, haqiqatan ham, men bugun unga juda hayronman", - deb boshladi Zossimov, xotinning kirish joyidan juda xursand bo'lib, chunki u o'n daqiqa davomida bemor bilan suhbat qurishga muvaffaq bo'lmagan.

en: “In another three or four days, if he goes on like this, he will be just as before, that is, as he was a month ago, or two … or perhaps even three.
uz: Ba'zi uch yoki to'rt kun ichida, agar u shunday davom etsa, u avvalgidek, ya'ni bir oy oldingidek, yoki ikki ... yoki, ehtimol, hatto uch kun oldingidek bo'ladi.

en: This has been coming on for a long while … eh?
uz: Bu uzoq vaqtdan beri davom etmoqda ... eh?

en: Confess, now, that it has been perhaps your own fault?” he added, with a tentative smile, as though still afraid of irritating him.
uz: Endi tan ol, ehtimol bu sizning aybingiz bo'lgan? deb qo'shib qo'ydi, u hali ham uni xafa qilishdan qo'rqqanidek, o'z tabassumini qo'shib qo'ydi.

en: “It is very possible,” answered Raskolnikov coldly.
uz: Bu juda mumkin, Raskolnikov sovuq javob berdi.

en: “I should say, too,” continued Zossimov with zest, “that your complete recovery depends solely on yourself.
uz: Men ham aytishim kerak, Zossimov shodlik bilan davom etdi, ki, sizning to'liq tiklanishingiz faqat o'zingizdan bog'liq.

en: Now that one can talk to you, I should like to impress upon you that it is essential to avoid the elementary, so to speak, fundamental causes tending to produce your morbid condition: in that case you will be cured, if not, it will go from bad to worse.
uz: Endi siz bilan suhbatlashsa bo'ladi, men sizga shuni ta'kidlashni xohlaymanki, sizning kasal holatingizni keltirib chiqaradigan elementar, deganda, asosiy sabablardan qochish muhim: shunday bo'lsa, siz sog'ayasiz, agar yo'q bo'lsa, bu yomonlikdan yomonroq bo'ladi.

en: These fundamental causes I don’t know, but they must be known to you.
uz: Ushbu asosiy sabablarni bilmayman, lekin ular sizga ma'lum bo'lishi kerak.

en: You are an intelligent man, and must have observed yourself, of course.
uz: Siz aqlli odamsiz va, albatta, o'zingizni kuzatib turgandirsiz.

en: I fancy the first stage of your derangement coincides with your leaving the university.
uz: O'ylaymanki, sizning aqldan ozishingizning birinchi bosqichi universitetdan ketishingiz bilan bir vaqtning o'zida yuz beradi.

en: You must not be left without occupation, and so, work and a definite aim set before you might, I fancy, be very beneficial.” “Yes, yes; you are perfectly right.
uz: Siz ishsiz qolmasligingiz kerak, shuning uchun siz oldingizga qo'yilgan ish va aniq maqsad juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin.Ha, ha; siz mutlaqo to'g'ri.

en: … I will make haste and return to the university: and then everything will go smoothly.
uz: ...Ikkiligim bilan universitetga qaytib boraman va keyin hamma narsa yaxshi bo'ladi.

en: …” Zossimov, who had begun his sage advice partly to make an effect before the ladies, was certainly somewhat mystified, when, glancing at his patient, he observed unmistakable mockery on his face.
uz: ... Xotin-qizlarning ko'z o'ngida ta'sir ko'rsatish uchun o'zining dono maslahatini boshlagan Zossimov, albatta, bemorining ko'z o'ngida turib, yuzida aniq masxara ko'rganida biroz g'alati bo'ldi.

en: This lasted an instant, however.
uz: Biroq, bu bir daqiqa davom etdi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna began at once thanking Zossimov, especially for his visit to their lodging the previous night.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna shu zahoti Zossimovga, ayniqsa, o'tgan kecha ularning uyida bo'lganidan minnatdorchilik bildirishni boshladi.

en: he saw you last night?” Raskolnikov asked, as though startled.
uz: U sizni o'tgan kecha ko'rganmi? - deb so'radi Raskolnikov, xuddi qo'rqib ketgandek.

en: “Then you have not slept either after your journey.”
uz: Shunday bo'lsa, sayohatingizdan keyin ham uxlamagan bo'lasiz.

en: “Ach, Rodya, that was only till two o’clock.
uz: Ach, Rodya, bu soat ikkigacha bo'ldi.

en: Dounia and I never go to bed before two at home.” “I don’t know how to thank him either,” Raskolnikov went on, suddenly frowning and looking down.
uz: Dounia va men uyda soat ikkiga qadar hech qachon uxlamaganmiz.Men ham unga qanday minnatdorchilik bildirishni bilmayman, Raskolnikov davom etdi, to'satdan burun ko'rib, pastga qaradi.

en: “Setting aside the question of payment —forgive me for referring to it (he turned to Zossimov) —I really don’t know what I have done to deserve such special attention from you!
uz: To'lov masalasini chetga qo'yib qo'yinglar o'zimga murojaat qilganim uchun kechirim so'raysiz (Zossimovga murojaat qildi) Haqiqatan ham men sizdan bunday alohida e'tiborni olish uchun nima qilganimni bilmayman!

en: I simply don’t understand it … and … and … it weighs upon me, indeed, because I don’t understand it.
uz: Men uni tushunmayapman va bu menga og'ir keladi, chunki men uni tushunmayapman.

en: I tell you so candidly.” “Don’t be irritated.” Zossimov forced himself to laugh.
uz: Men sizga shunday ochiqchasiga aytaman.   G'azablanmang. Zossimov o'zini kulishga majbur qildi.

en: “Assume that you are my first patient —well —we fellows just beginning to practise love our first patients as if they were our children, and some almost fall in love with them.
uz: Siz mening birinchi bemorim ekanligingizni tasavvur qiling well Biz yigitlar ilk bemorlarimizni farzandlarimiz kabi sevishni mashq qila boshlaymiz va ba'zilari deyarli ularga muhabbat qozonadi.

en: And, of course, I am not rich in patients.” “I say nothing about him,” added Raskolnikov, pointing to Razumihin, “though he has had nothing from me either but insult and trouble.” “What nonsense he is talking!
uz: Va, albatta, men bemorlarga boy emasman. Men u haqida hech narsa aytmayman, Raskolnikov shuni qo'shimcha qildi, u Razumihinni ko'rsatdi,chi men ham undan haqorat va muammolardan boshqa hech narsa olmagan bo'lsa ham. U qanday behuda gapiryapti!

en: Why, you are in a sentimental mood today, are you?” shouted Razumihin.
uz: Nima uchun, bugun siz sentimental ruhdamisiz? - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: If he had had more penetration he would have seen that there was no trace of sentimentality in him, but something indeed quite the opposite.
uz: Agar u ko'proq penetratsiyaga ega bo'lganida, u o'zida hissiyotchilikning hech qanday izlari yo'qligini, aksincha, buning aksi ekanligini ko'rgan bo'lardi.

en: But Avdotya Romanovna noticed it.
uz: Ammo Avdotya Romanovna buni payqadi.

en: She was intently and uneasily watching her brother.
uz: U birodarini diqqat bilan kuzatib turardi.

en: “As for you, mother, I don’t dare to speak,” he went on, as though repeating a lesson learned by heart.
uz: "Senga kelsak, ona, men gapirishga jur'at qilmayman", - dedi u, xuddi yoddan o'qilgan saboqni takrorlagan kabi.

en: “It is only today that I have been able to realise a little how distressed you must have been here yesterday, waiting for me to come back.” When he had said this, he suddenly held out his hand to his sister, smiling without a word.
uz: Bugungacha, siz kecha bu yerda qaytib kelishimni kutganingizda qanchalik xafa bo'lganingizni biroz anglab yetdim. Buni aytgach, u birdan singlisiga qo'lini uzatdi va so'zsiz tabassum qildi.

en: But in this smile there was a flash of real unfeigned feeling.
uz: Ammo bu tabassumda haqiqiy soxtalik qilmagan his-tuyg'u paydo bo'ldi.

en: Dounia caught it at once, and warmly pressed his hand, overjoyed and thankful.
uz: Dounia uni darhol ushlab, quvonch va minnatdorchilik bilan qo'lini cho'zdi.

en: It was the first time he had addressed her since their dispute the previous day.
uz: O'tgan kun bahslashganidan beri u ayolga birinchi marta murojaat qilgan edi.

en: The mother’s face lighted up with ecstatic happiness at the sight of this conclusive unspoken reconciliation.
uz: Onaning yuzi shu yakuniy, so'zsiz yarashishning guvohi bo'lganidan xursand bo'ldi.

en: “Yes, that is what I love him for,” Razumihin, exaggerating it all, muttered to himself, with a vigorous turn in his chair.
uz: Ha, men uni shu sababli sevaman,  Razumihin, hamma narsani haddan tashqari o'ylab, o'zi o'zi bilan gaplashib, o'rindiqida kuchli burilish bilan.

en: “He has these movements.” “And how well he does it all,” the mother was thinking to herself.
uz: Bu harakatlari bor.  Va u hamma narsani qanchalik yaxshi bajarishini, ona o'ziga o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: “What generous impulses he has, and how simply, how delicately he put an end to all the misunderstanding with his sister —simply by
uz: U qanchalik saxiy bo'lgan va opasi bilan yuz bergan noto'g'ri tushunchalarga qanday qilib soddalik bilan to'xtatganini ko'rib chiqing.

en: holding out his hand at the right minute and looking at her like that.
uz: O'z qo'lini to'g'ri vaqtda uzatgan va unga shunday qaragan.

en: … And what fine eyes he has, and how fine his whole face is!
uz: Uning ko'zlari naqadar chiroyli va butun yuzi naqadar chiroyli!

en: … He is even better looking than Dounia.
uz: U hatto Douniaga qaraganda yaxshiroq ko'rinadi.

en: … But, good heavens, what a suit —how terribly he’s dressed!
uz: Ammo, Xudoyimiz, u qanday kiyim kiygan!

en: … Vasya, the messenger boy in Afanasy Ivanitch’s shop, is better dressed!
uz: Vasya, Afanasy Ivanitch do'konidagi elchi o'g'li, yaxshiroq kiyinadi!

en: I could rush at him and hug him … weep over him —but I am afraid.
uz: Men unga shoshib, uni quchoqlab, yig'lab yubora olaman, lekin qo'rqaman.

en: … Oh, dear, he’s so strange!
uz: Oh, aziz, u juda g'alati!

en: He’s talking kindly, but I’m afraid!
uz: U mehribon gapiradi, lekin qo'rqaman!

en: Why, what am I afraid of?
uz: Nima uchun, nimaga qo'rqaman?

en: …” “Oh, Rodya, you wouldn’t believe,” she began suddenly, in haste to answer his words to her, “how unhappy Dounia and I were yesterday!
uz: ...Oh, Rodya, siz ishonmaysiz, u to'satdan, uning so'zlariga javob berishga shoshildi,Dunia va men kecha qanchalik baxtsiz edik!

en: Now that it’s all over and done with and we are quite happy again —I can tell you.
uz: Endi bularning barchasi tugagach va biz yana juda baxtli ekanmiz, sizga aytaman.

en: Fancy, we ran here almost straight from the train to embrace you and that woman —ah, here she is!
uz: Fancy, biz sizni va o'sha ayolni quchoqlash uchun deyarli to'g'ridan-to'g'ri poyezddan yugurib keldik!

en: Good morning, Nastasya!
uz: Salom, Nastasya!

en: … She told us at once that you were lying in a high fever and had just run away from the doctor in delirium, and they were looking for you in the streets.
uz: ... U bizga darhol sen og'ir issiqda yotganingni, shifokordan deliriumda qochib ketganingni va ko'chada seni qidirayotganlarini aytdi.

en: You can’t imagine how we felt!
uz: Bizni qanday his qilganimizni tasavvur ham qila olmaysiz!

en: I couldn’t help thinking of the tragic end of Lieutenant Potanchikov, a friend of your father’s —you can’t remember him, Rodya —who ran out in the same way in a high fever and fell into the well in the courtyard and they couldn’t pull him out till next day.
uz: Men otangizning do'sti, Rodya, yuqori issiqlik dastidan xuddi shunday yo'l bilan yugurib chiqib, hovlidagi quduqqa tushib qolgan potanchikovning halokatli o'limini tasavvur qila olmadim.

en: Of course, we exaggerated things.
uz: Albatta, biz o'zimizni haddan tashqari ko'p ko'rsatdik.

en: We were on the point of rushing to find Pyotr Petrovitch to ask him to help.
uz: Biz Pyotr Petrovitchni topishga shoshilishgach, undan yordam so'rash uchun harakat qilardik.

en: … Because we were alone, utterly alone,” she said plaintively and stopped short, suddenly, recollecting it was still somewhat dangerous to speak of Pyotr Petrovitch, although “we are quite happy again.” “Yes, yes.
uz: Biz yolg'iz, butunlay yolg'iz bo'lganimiz uchun, u o'z-o'zidan aytdi va to'xtatdi, to'satdan, Pyotr Petrovitch haqida gapirish hali ham xavfli ekanligini eslab, biroz o'z-o'zidan aytdi, garchi biz yana juda baxtli bo'lsak ham. ... Ha, ha, ha.

en: … Of course it’s very annoying.
uz: Albatta, bu juda g'alati.

en: …” Raskolnikov muttered in reply, but with such a preoccupied and inattentive air that Dounia gazed at him in perplexity.
uz: ... Raskolnikov javob qilib, ammo shunchalik tashvishlangan va beparvo havo bilan, Duniyo unga g'alati qarab turdi.

en: “What else was it I wanted to say?” He went on trying to recollect.
uz: Men yana nima aytmoqchi edim? U o'z fikrini o'z ichiga olishga harakat qildi.

en: “Oh, yes; mother, and you too, Dounia, please don’t think that I didn’t mean to come and see you today and was waiting for you to come first.” “What are you saying, Rodya?” cried Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Oh, ha; ona, va siz ham, Dounia, iltimos, bugun sizni ko'rish uchun kelishni xohlamaganimni va siz birinchi bo'lib kelishni kutganimni o'ylamang. Rodya, nima deyyapsan? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna qayg'urdi.

en: She, too, was surprised.
uz: U ham hayron qoldi.

en: “Is he answering us as a duty?” Dounia wondered.
uz: U bizga majburiyat sifatida javob beryaptimi? Dounia o'zini o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: “Is he being reconciled and asking forgiveness as though he were performing a rite or repeating a lesson?”
uz: O'zi yarashgan va kechirim so'ragan kishi bir marosimni o'tkazgan yoki darsni takrorlagan kabi bo'ladimi?

en: “I’ve only just waked up, and wanted to go to you, but was delayed owing to my clothes; I forgot yesterday to ask her … Nastasya … to wash out the blood … I’ve only just dressed.” “Blood!
uz: Men faqatgina uyg'onib, sizning oldingizga bormoqchi edim, lekin kiyimim tufayli kechikdim; kecha undan ... Nastasya ... qon yuvishini so'rashni unutdim ... Men faqatgina kiyim kiyganman.Qan!

en: What blood?” Pulcheria Alexandrovna asked in alarm.
uz: Qaysi qon? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna xavotirda so'radi.

en: “Oh, nothing —don’t be uneasy.
uz: Oh, hech narsa noqulay bo'lmaydi.

en: It was when I was wandering about yesterday, rather delirious, I chanced upon a man who had been run over … a clerk …” “Delirious?
uz: Kecha biroz halok boʻlib yurganimda, bir odamga toʻxtab qoldim ... bir ishbilarmon ...Delirious?

en: But you remember everything!” Razumihin interrupted.
uz: Ammo siz hamma narsani eslaysiz! Razumihin to'xtatdi.

en: “That’s true,” Raskolnikov answered with special carefulness.
uz: Raskolnikov alohida ehtiyotkorlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “I remember everything even to the slightest detail, and yet —why I did that and went there and said that, I can’t clearly explain now.” “A familiar phenomenon,” interposed Zossimov, “actions are sometimes performed in a masterly and most cunning way, while the direction of the actions is deranged and dependent on various morbid impressions —it’s like a dream.” “Perhaps it’s a good thing really that he should think me almost a madman,” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: Men hamma narsani hatto eng kichik tafsilotlargacha eslayman, lekin nima uchun men shunday qildim va u yerga borib, shunday aytdim, men hozir aniq tushuntira olmayman.Xususan tanish hodisa, Zossimov o'zi bilan gaplashibdi, harakatlar ba'zan ustunlik va hiyla-nayrang bilan amalga oshiriladi, harakatlarning yo'nalishi esa befarq va turli kasalliklarga bog'liq.Bu tush kabi.Ehtimol, meni deyarli aqldan ozgan deb o'ylashi yaxshi narsa. Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: “Why, people in perfect health act in the same way too,” observed Dounia, looking uneasily at Zossimov.
uz: Nima uchun, mukammal sog'lom insonlar ham xuddi shunday harakat qiladilar, deb kuzatdi Dounia, Zossimovga noqulay qarab.

en: “There is some truth in your observation,” the latter replied.
uz: Sizning e'tiboringizda haqiqat bor, - deb javob berdi.

en: “In that sense we are certainly all not infrequently like madmen, but with the slight difference that the deranged are somewhat madder, for we must draw a line.
uz: Bu ma'noda biz hammamiz tez-tez aqldan ozganlarga o'xshamaymiz, ammo aqldan ozganlarning biroz aqldan ozganlari farq qiladi, chunki biz chegara chizishimiz kerak.

en: A normal man, it is true, hardly exists.
uz: To'g'ri, oddiy odam kamdan-kam mavjud.

en: Among dozens —perhaps hundreds of thousands —hardly one is to be met with.” At the word “madman,” carelessly dropped by Zossimov in his chatter on his favourite subject, everyone frowned.
uz: O'nlablar orasida, ehtimol yuz minglablar orasida, hech kim bilan uchrashish qiyin. Zossimov tomonidan sevimli mavzusida gapirishda beparvolik bilan qo'yilgan "madman" degan so'zga hamma ko'z o'ngida.

en: Raskolnikov sat seeming not to pay attention, plunged in thought with a strange smile on his pale lips.
uz: Raskolnikov e'tibor bermay o'tirdi va o'ziga xos tabassum bilan o'ziga e'tibor bermay o'tirdi.

en: He was still meditating on something.
uz: U hali ham biror narsa ustida mulohaza yuritayotgan edi.

en: “Well, what about the man who was run over?
uz: Xo'sh, toshbo'ron qilingan kishi haqida nima deyish mumkin?

en: I interrupted you!” Razumihin cried hastily.
uz: Men sizni to'xtatdim! Razumihin shovqin bilan yig'ladi.

en: “What?” Raskolnikov seemed to wake up.
uz: Nima? Raskolnikov uyg'onayotganga o'xshaydi.

en: “Oh … I got spattered with blood helping to carry him to his lodging.
uz: Oh... uni uyga ko'tarishda yordam berayotganimda, menga qon to'kildi.

en: By the way, mamma, I did an unpardonable thing yesterday.
uz: Aytgancha, onam, kecha men kechirimsiz ish qildim.

en: I was literally out of my mind.
uz: Darhaqiqat, men aqldan ozgan edim.

en: I gave away all the money you sent me … to his wife for the funeral.
uz: Siz menga yuborgan barcha pulni uning xotiniga uning dafn marosimi uchun berdim.

en: She’s a widow now, in consumption, a poor creature … three little
uz: U endi beva, iste'molda, kambag'al mavjudot ... uchta kichkina mavjudot.

en: children, starving … nothing in the house … there’s a daughter, too … perhaps you’d have given it yourself if you’d seen them.
uz: Bolalar ochar, uyda hech narsa yo'q... qiz ham bor... ehtimol siz ularni ko'rganingizda o'zingiz berardingiz.

en: But I had no right to do it I admit, especially as I knew how you needed the money yourself.
uz: Ammo men buni qilishga haqim yo'qligini tan oldim, ayniqsa, pulga qanday muhtoj ekanligingizni bilardim.

en: To help others one must have the right to do it, or else Crevez, chiens, si vous n’êtes pas contents.” He laughed, “That’s right, isn’t it, Dounia?” “No, it’s not,” answered Dounia firmly.
uz: Boshqalarga yordam berish uchun buni qilish huquqiga ega bo'lish kerak, aks holda, Crevez, itlar, agar siz rozi bo'lmasangiz. U kulishdi, That's right, isn't it, Dounia?Yo'q, it's not, Dounia qat'iy javob berdi.

en: you, too, have ideals,” he muttered, looking at her almost with hatred, and smiling sarcastically.
uz: Sizda ham ideallar bor, - deb gapirdi u, unga deyarli nafrat bilan qarab, sarkastika bilan tabassum qildi.

en: “I ought to have considered that.
uz: Men buni o'ylashim kerak edi.

en: … Well, that’s praiseworthy, and it’s better for you … and if you reach a line you won’t overstep, you will be unhappy … and if you overstep it, maybe you will be still unhappier.
uz: Bu maqtovga sazovor va o'zingiz uchun yaxshiroqdir.Agar siz o'tmasligingiz kerak bo'lgan chegaraga yetib kelsangiz, baxtsiz bo'lasiz.Agar siz o'tmasangiz, ehtimol bundan ham baxtsiz bo'lasiz.

en: … But all that’s nonsense,” he added irritably, vexed at being carried away.
uz: Ammo bularning hammasi behuda, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u g'azabga to'lib, uni olib ketishdan xafa bo'lib.

en: “I only meant to say that I beg your forgiveness, mother,” he concluded, shortly and abruptly.
uz: "Men shunchaki kechirim so'rayotganimni aytmoqchiman, ona", - dedi u, qisqa va shoshilinch ravishda.

en: “That’s enough, Rodya, I am sure that everything you do is very good,” said his mother, delighted.
uz: Bu yetarli, Rodya, shuni bilamanki, siz qilayotgan barcha ishlar juda yaxshi, - dedi uning onasi, xursand bo'lib.

en: “Don’t be too sure,” he answered, twisting his mouth into a smile.
uz: "O'zingni shubhalanma", - deb javob berdi u, og'zini tabassumga aylantirib.

en: There was a certain constraint in all this conversation, and in the silence, and in the reconciliation, and in the forgiveness, and all were feeling it.
uz: Bu suhbatda, xotirjamlikda, yarashish va kechirimlilikda muayyan cheklovlar bor edi va hamma buni his qilardi.

en: “It is as though they were afraid of me,” Raskolnikov was thinking to himself, looking askance at his mother and sister.
uz: Raskolnikov o'zicha o'ylab, onasi va singlisiga ko'z tikib qarab turardi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna was indeed growing more timid the longer she kept silent.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, albatta, u qancha vaqt gapirmasa, shuncha ko'proq qo'rqinchli bo'lib qoldi.

en: “Yet in their absence I seemed to love them so much,” flashed through his mind.
uz: Ammo ularning yo'qligida men ularni shunchalik yaxshi ko'raman, deb o'yladi.

en: “Do you know, Rodya, Marfa Petrovna is dead,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna suddenly blurted out.
uz: Bilasizmi, Rodya, Marfa Petrovna o'ldi, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna to'satdan o'zicha bo'ldi.

en: “What Marfa Petrovna?” “Oh, mercy on us —Marfa Petrovna Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Marfa Petrovna nima?Oh, bizga rahm qilMarfa Petrovna Svidrigailov.

en: I wrote you so much about her.” “A-a-h!
uz: Men sizga u haqida juda ko'p yozganman. A-a-h!

en: Oh, really?” he roused himself suddenly, as if waking up.
uz: Ha, haqiqatan ham? u o'zini to'satdan uyg'otdi, xuddi uyg'onayotgandek.

en: “What did she die of?” “Only imagine, quite suddenly,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna answered hurriedly, encouraged by his curiosity.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna uning qiziquvchanligidan dalda olib, shoshilinch javob berdi.

en: “On the very day I was sending you that letter!
uz: Men sizga maktubni yuborgan kunning o'zida!

en: Would you believe it, that awful man seems
uz: Ishonasizmi, bu dahshatli odam ko'rinadi

en: to have been the cause of her death.
uz: Uning o'lim sababi bo'lgan.

en: They say he beat her dreadfully.” “Why, were they on such bad terms?” he asked, addressing his sister.
uz: U qizni dahshatli urgani aytilmoqda. Nega, ular bunday yomon munosabatda edilar? deb so'radi u, opasiga murojaat qilib.

en: Quite the contrary indeed.
uz: To'g'ri, buning aksi bor.

en: With her, he was always very patient, considerate even.
uz: U bilan u har doim juda sabrli, hatto mulohazakor bo'lgan.

en: In fact, all those seven years of their married life he gave way to her, too much so indeed, in many cases.
uz: Darhaqiqat, ularning turmush qurgan yetti yillik hayoti davomida u ayolga o'rin berdi, ko'p hollarda juda ko'p.

en: All of a sudden he seems to have lost patience.” “Then he could not have been so awful if he controlled himself for seven years?
uz: Toʻsatdan sabr-toqatini yoʻqotib qoʻyganiga oʻxshaydi.Shuning oʻrniga, yetti yil davomida oʻzini nazorat qilganida, u shunchalik dahshatli boʻlishi mumkin emasmi?

en: You seem to be defending him, Dounia?” “No, no, he’s an awful man!
uz: Siz uni himoya qilyapsizmi, Dounia? Yo'q, yo'q, u juda yomon odam!

en: I can imagine nothing more awful!” Dounia answered, almost with a shudder, knitting her brows, and sinking into thought.
uz: Men bundan dahshatli hech narsani tasavvur qila olmayman! Dounia deyarli titrab, burunlarini tikib, fikrga tushib qoldi.

en: “That had happened in the morning,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna went on hurriedly.
uz: Bu ertalab sodir bo'lgan edi, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna shoshilinch ravishda davom etdi.

en: “And directly afterwards she ordered the horses to be harnessed to drive to the town immediately after dinner.
uz: Va darhol kechki ovqatdan so'ng otlarni shaharga olib borishga buyurdi.

en: She always used to drive to the town in such cases.
uz: U har doim bunday holatlarda shaharga mashinada ketardi.

en: She ate a very good dinner, I am told.
uz: Menga aytilishicha, u juda yaxshi kechki ovqat yeydi.

en: …” “After the beating?” “That was always her … habit; and immediately after dinner, so as not to be late in starting, she went to the bathhouse.
uz: ... O'qilganidan so'ng?  Bu har doim uning ... odati edi; va kechki ovqatdan so'ng, boshlashda kech qolmaslik uchun, u hammomga bordi.

en: … You see, she was undergoing some treatment with baths.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, u hammomlar bilan davolashdan o'tkazilgan edi.

en: They have a cold spring there, and she used to bathe in it regularly every day, and no sooner had she got into the water when she suddenly had a stroke!” “I should think so,” said Zossimov.
uz: U erda sovuq buloq bor va u har kuni u yerda muntazam ravishda yuvgan va birdan insultga uchraganida suvga tushganidan so'ng!Men buni o'ylayman, dedi Zossimov.

en: “And did he beat her badly?” “What does that matter!” put in Dounia.
uz: Va u qizni qattiq urganmi?Bu nimaga bog'liq! Douniaga qo'yilgan.

en: But I don’t know why you want to tell us such gossip, mother,” said Raskolnikov irritably, as it were in spite of himself.
uz: Ammo men bilmayman, nima uchun siz bizga bunday mish-mishlarni aytmoqchi bo'ldingiz, ona, - dedi Raskolnikov g'azabga to'lib, xuddi o'ziga qarama-qarshi bo'lib.

en: “Ah, my dear, I don’t know what to talk about,” broke from Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Ah, azizim, men nima haqida gapirishim kerakligini bilmayman, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna-dan bo'shatdim.

en: “Why, are you all afraid of me?” he asked, with a constrained smile.
uz: Nima uchun hammangiz mendan qo'rqasizlar? - deb so'radi u, cheklangan tabassum bilan.

en: “That’s certainly true,” said Dounia, looking directly and sternly at her brother.
uz: "Bu albatta haqiqat", - dedi Dounia, aka-ukaga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri va qat'iy nazar ko'rib.

en: “Mother was crossing herself with terror as she came up the stairs.” His face worked, as though in convulsion.
uz: O'g'lim qo'rqinchga to'lib-toshganida, onasi o'zini qo'rqinch bilan ko'tarib turardi. Uning yuzi shovqinli bo'lib, xuddi shovqinli bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: “Ach, what are you saying, Dounia!
uz: Ach, nima deyapsan, Dounia!

en: Don’t be angry, please, Rodya.
uz: Iltimos, g'azablanma, Rodya.

en: … Why did you say that, Dounia?” Pulcheria Alexandrovna began, overwhelmed —“You see, coming here, I was dreaming all the way, in the train, how we should meet, how we should talk over everything together.
uz: Nima uchun shunday aytdingiz, Dounia? Pulcheria Aleksandrovna boshlandi, ko'pdan-ko'p bo'ldi. Mana, bu yerga kelish, men butun yo'lda, poyezdda, qanday uchrashishimiz kerakligini va hamma narsa haqida birgalikda qanday gaplashishimiz kerakligini orzu qilardim.

en: … And I was so happy, I did not notice the journey!
uz: Men shunchalik baxtli edimki, sayohatni payqamasdim!

en: But what am I saying?
uz: Lekin men nima deyapman?

en: … You should not, Dounia.
uz: - Yo'q, Dounia.

en: … I am happy now —simply in seeing you, Rodya.
uz: ... Endi sizni ko'rishimdan xursandman, Rodya.

en: …” “Hush, mother,” he muttered in confusion, not looking at her, but pressing her hand.
uz: ... Hush, ona, u g'alati gapirib, unga qaramasdan, qo'lini bosibdi.

en: “We shall have time to speak freely of everything!” As he said this, he was suddenly overwhelmed with confusion and turned pale.
uz: Bizda hamma narsa haqida erkin gapirish uchun vaqt bo'ladi! U buni aytganda, u to'satdan chalg'ib qoldi va o'z-o'zidan oqib ketdi.

en: Again that awful sensation he had known of late passed with deadly chill over his soul.
uz: Yana o'sha dahshatli his-tuyg'ular uning ruhi ustidan o'ldiruvchi sovuqlik bilan o'tdi.

en: Again it became suddenly plain and perceptible to him that he had just told a fearful lie —that he would never now be able to speak freely of everything —that he would never again be able to speak of anything to anyone.
uz: O'shanda u yana bir bor o'zi uchun dahshatli yolg'on gapirganini va endi hech qachon hamma narsa haqida erkin gapira olmasligini va hech kimga hech qachon hech narsa haqida gapira olmasligini aniq va aniq ko'rdi.

en: The anguish of this thought was such that for a moment he almost forgot himself.
uz: Bu fikrning qayg'usi shunchalik kuchli bo'lganki, u bir zumda o'zini deyarli unutib qo'ydi.

en: He got up from his seat, and not looking at anyone walked towards the door.
uz: U o'tirgan joyidan turib, hech kimga nazar solmay, eshik tomon bordi.

en: “What are you about?” cried Razumihin, clutching him by the arm.
uz: Nima qilyapsan? - deb baqirdi Razumihin, uni qo'lidan ushlab.

en: He sat down again, and began looking about him, in silence.
uz: U yana o'tirdi va o'zini o'rab, sukut saqlashni boshladi.

en: They were all looking at him in perplexity.
uz: Hammasi uni hayronlik bilan ko'rib turardi.

en: “But what are you all so dull for?” he shouted, suddenly and quite unexpectedly.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa ham, nima uchun hammangiz o'sha qadar charchagansiz? deb baqirdi u, to'satdan va kutilmagan holda.

en: What’s the use of sitting like this?
uz: Bunday o'tirishning foydasi nimada?

en: … We meet together and sit in silence.
uz: ... Biz birgalikda yig'ilib, xotirjamlik bilan o'tiramiz.

en: … Come, anything!” “Thank God; I was afraid the same thing as yesterday was beginning again,” said Pulcheria Alexandrovna, crossing herself.
uz: ... Kel, hamma narsa!Allohga shukr, men o'zimni o'ldirgan Pulcheria Aleksandrovna aytdi:Dunyoda kecha boshlanayotgan voqealardan qo'rqardim.

en: “What is the matter, Rodya?” asked Avdotya Romanovna, distrustfully.
uz: Nima bo'ldi, Rodya? deb so'radi Avdotya Romanovna ishonchsizlik bilan.

en: I remembered something,” he answered, and suddenly laughed.
uz: Men bir narsani esladim, - deb javob berdi u, - va to'satdan kuldi.

en: “Well, if you remembered something; that’s all right!
uz: Agar biror narsani eslay olsangiz, yaxshi bo'ladi!

en: … I was beginning to think …” muttered Zossimov, getting up from the sofa.
uz: ... Men o'ylay boshladim ... Zossimov sofasidan turib, qichqirdi.

en: “It is time for me to be off.
uz: Men uchun o'tish vaqti keldi.

en: I will look in again perhaps … if I can …” He made his bows, and went out.
uz: Ehtimol, yana ko'rib chiqaman ... agar bo'lsa ... U o'z bo'yintirishlarini qildi va tashqariga chiqdi.

en: “What an excellent man!” observed Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna: "Bu qanday ajoyib odam!

en: “Yes, excellent, splendid, well-educated, intelligent,” Raskolnikov began, suddenly speaking with surprising rapidity, and a liveliness he had not shown till then.
uz: Ha, ajoyib, chiroyli, ta'lim olgan, aqlli, Raskolnikov boshlandi, to'satdan o'ziga xos tezlik va o'sha paytgacha ko'rsatmagan jonlilik bilan gapirgan.

en: “I can’t remember where I met him before my illness.
uz: Men kasalligimdan oldin uni qaerda uchratganimni eslay olmayman.

en: … I believe I have met him somewhere — … And this is a good man, too,” he nodded at Razumihin.
uz: ...Men uni bir joyda uchratganimni bilaman  ... Bu ham yaxshi odam, u Razumihinga boshini tiydi.

en: “Do you like him, Dounia?” he asked her; and suddenly, for some unknown reason, laughed.
uz: "U sizga yoqadimi, Dounia?" - deb so'radi u ayoldan va to'satdan, noma'lum sabablarga ko'ra, u kuldi.

en: “Very much,” answered Dounia.
uz: Very much, deb javob berdi Dounia.

en: —what a pig you are!” Razumihin protested, blushing in terrible confusion, and he got up from his chair.
uz: Razumihin dahshatli g'alati bilan qizg'inlab, o'z kursidan turdi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna smiled faintly, but Raskolnikov laughed aloud.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna kamroq tabassum qildi, Raskolnikov esa baland ovoz bilan kuldi.

en: “Where are you off to?” “I must go.” “You need not at all.
uz: Qayerga ketyapsan?Men borishim kerak.Sizga hech narsa kerak emas.

en: Zossimov has gone, so you must.
uz: Zossimov ketib ketdi, shuning uchun siz ham ketishingiz kerak.

en: Is it twelve o’clock?
uz: O'n ikki soatmi?

en: What a pretty watch you have got, Dounia.
uz: Qizigʻi shundaki, sizning soatingiz juda chiroyli, Dounia.

en: But why are you all silent again?
uz: Ammo nega sizlar yana sukut saqlashdasizlar?

en: I do all the talking.” “It was a present from Marfa Petrovna,” answered Dounia.
uz: Men hammasini gapiraman. Bu Marfa Petrovna tomonidan sovg'a edi, deb javob berdi Dounia.

en: “And a very expensive one!” added Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Va juda qimmat! Pulcheria Aleksandrovna qo'shdi.

en: Hardly like a lady’s.” “I like that sort,” said Dounia.
uz: Ayollarga o'xshamaydi.Men o'sha turni yaxshi ko'raman, - dedi Dounia.

en: “So it is not a present from her fiancé,” thought Razumihin, and was unreasonably delighted.
uz: Shuning uchun bu uning nişanchisidan sovg'a emas,  deb o'yladi Razumihin va u asossiz darajada xursand bo'ldi.

en: “I thought it was Luzhin’s present,” observed Raskolnikov.
uz: Men bu Luzhinning hozirligi deb o'yladim, Raskolnikov kuzatdi.

en: “No, he has not made Dounia any presents yet.” “A-ah!
uz: Yo'q, u hali Duniyaga sovg'alar bermagan.A-ah!

en: And do you remember, mother, I was in love and wanted to get married?” he said suddenly, looking at his mother, who was disconcerted by the sudden change of subject and the way he spoke of it.
uz: Va eslaysizmi, onam, men o'zimni sevgan edim va turmush qurmoqchi edim? dedi u to'satdan, boshida mavzu o'zgargani va uning gapirish tarzini ko'rib xafa bo'lgan onasiga qarab.

en: “Oh, yes, my dear.” Pulcheria Alexandrovna exchanged glances with Dounia and Razumihin.
uz: Oh, ha, ey azizim. Pulcheria Aleksandrovna Dounia va Razumihin bilan ko'z o'rniga ko'z oldi.

en: What shall I tell you?
uz: Sizga nima deyishim kerak?

en: I don’t remember much indeed.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, ko'p narsani eslay olmayman.

en: She was such a sickly girl,” he went on, growing dreamy and looking down again.
uz: U shunday kasal qiz edi, u davom etdi, orzu qilib, yana pastga qaradi.

en: She was fond of giving alms to the poor, and was always dreaming of a nunnery, and once she burst into tears when she began talking to me about it.
uz: U kambag'allarga sadaqa berishni yaxshi ko'rardi va har doim bir monastir haqida orzu qilar edi va bir marta u menga bu haqda gapira boshlaganida ko'z yoshlariga tushardi.

en: Yes, yes, I remember.
uz: Ha, ha, eslayman.

en: I remember very well.
uz: Men yaxshi eslayman.

en: She was an ugly little thing.
uz: U juda achinarli kichkina narsa edi.

en: don’t know what drew me to her then —I think it was because she was always ill.
uz: O'shanda meni u ayolga nima jalb qilganini bilmayman, deb o'ylayman, chunki u har doim kasal edi.

en: If she had been lame or hunchback, I believe I should have liked her better still,” he smiled dreamily.
uz: Agar u pichoq yoki qo'pol bo'lgan bo'lsa, men uni yanada ko'proq yoqtirardim, deb o'ylayman.

en: “Yes, it was a sort of spring delirium.” “No, it was not only spring delirium,” said Dounia, with warm feeling.
uz: Ha, bu bir xil bahor deliriysi edi.Yo'q, bu faqat bahor deliriysi emas edi, - dedi Dounia, iliq hissiyot bilan.

en: He fixed a strained intent look on his sister, but did not hear or did not understand her words.
uz: U singlisiga g'amgin ko'z tikdi, ammo uning so'zlarini eshitmadi yoki tushunmadi.

en: Then, completely lost in thought, he got up, went up to his mother, kissed her, went back to his place and sat down.
uz: So'ngra butunlay g'alati bo'lib, o'rnidan turib, onasining oldiga bordi, uni o'pdi, o'z joyiga qaytib, o'tirdi.

en: “You love her even now?” said Pulcheria Alexandrovna, touched.
uz: Siz uni hozir ham sevasizmi? - dedi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, qo'ng'iroq qilib.

en: … You ask about her?
uz: Siz u haqida so'raganmisiz?

en: No … that’s all now, as it were, in another world … and so long ago.
uz: Yo'q ... bu hozir boshqa dunyoda bo'lgani kabi ... va uzoq vaqt oldin.

en: And indeed everything happening here seems somehow far away.” He looked attentively at them.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bu yerda sodir bo'layotgan hamma narsa biroz uzoqda ko'rinadi. U ularga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: “You, now … I seem to be looking at you from a thousand miles away … but, goodness knows why we are talking of that!
uz: Sizni, endi... Men sizga ming kilometr uzoqdan qarayotgandek tuyulaman... lekin, Xudo biladi, nega biz bu haqda gaplashyapmiz!

en: And what’s the use of asking about it?” he added with annoyance, and biting his nails, fell into dreamy silence again.
uz: Va bu haqda so'rashning foydasi nimada? - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u xafa bo'lib, to'g'rlarini o'qib, yana bir bor tushlik xotirjamligiga tushdi.

en: “What a wretched lodging you have, Rodya!
uz: Sizning uyingiz naqadar noxush, Rodya!

en: It’s like a tomb,” said Pulcheria Alexandrovna, suddenly breaking the oppressive silence.
uz: Bu xuddi qabrga o'xshaydi, - dedi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, birdan zulm qiluvchi xotirjamlikni buzadi.

en: “I am sure it’s quite half through your lodging you have become so melancholy.” “My lodging,” he answered, listlessly.
uz: Men shubhalanamanki, o'zingizning uy-joyingizning yarmidan keyin siz shunchalik tushkunlikka tushdingiz.Mening uy-joyim, u befarq javob berdi.

en: “Yes, the lodging had a great deal to do with it.
uz: Ha, uy-joy bilan katta aloqasi bor edi.

en: … I thought that, too.
uz: Men ham shunday o'yladim.

en: … If only you knew, though, what a strange thing you said just now, mother,” he said, laughing strangely.
uz: ...Agar siz o'zingiz aytgan g'alati so'zni bilgan bo'lsangiz edi, onam, - dedi u, g'alaticha kulish bilan.

en: A little more, and their companionship, this mother and this sister, with him after three years’ absence, this intimate tone of conversation, in face of the utter impossibility of really speaking about anything, would have been beyond his power of endurance.
uz: Bir oz ko'proq va ularning do'stligi, bu ona va bu singlimiz, uch yil o'tgandan keyin u bilan birga, bu yaqin suhbat, hech narsa haqida gapirishning mutlaqo imkoni bo'lmaganida, uning chidamliligini o'zgartirgan bo'lardi.

en: But there was one urgent matter which must be settled one way or the other that day —so he had decided when he woke.
uz: Ammo o'sha kuni shu yoki shu tarzda hal etilishi kerak bo'lgan bir muhim masala bor edi, shuning uchun u uyg'ongach qaror qabul qildi.

en: Now he was glad to remember it, as a means of escape.
uz: Endi u buni eslab, qochish yo'li sifatida xursand edi.

en: “Listen, Dounia,” he began, gravely and drily, “of course I beg your pardon for yesterday, but I consider it my duty to tell you again that I do not withdraw from my chief point.
uz: "Quloq soling, Dounia", - deb boshladi u, jiddiy va quruqlik bilan. - Albatta, kecha uchun kechirim so'rayman, lekin yana bir bor sizga aytishim kerakki, men asosiy fikrimdan voz kechmayman.

en: scoundrel, you must not be.
uz: Yovuz, siz bo'lmasligingiz kerak.

en: If you marry Luzhin, I cease at once to look on you as a sister.” “Rodya, Rodya!
uz: Agar siz Lujin bilan turmush qursangiz, men sizni bir singlimdek ko'rishni darhol to'xtataman. Rodya, Rodya!

en: It is the same as yesterday again,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna cried, mournfully.
uz: Bugun yana kechaga o'xshaydi, - deb yig'ladi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, qayg'u bilan.

en: “And why do you call yourself a scoundrel?
uz: Nega o'zingizni qo'pol deb atayapsiz?

en: You said the same yesterday.” “Brother,” Dounia answered firmly and with the same dryness.
uz: Siz ham o'sha so'zlarni kecha ham aytdingiz. Kardach, Dounia qat'iy va xuddi shunday quruqlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “In all this there is a mistake on your part.
uz: Bularning barchasida siz xatoga yo'l qo'ygansiz.

en: I thought it over at night, and found out the mistake.
uz: Kechasi bu haqda o'yladim va xatoga yo'l qo'yganimni bilib oldim.

en: It is all because you seem to fancy I am sacrificing myself to someone and for someone.
uz: Buning sababi shundaki, siz mening kimgadir va kimgadir qurbon bo'lishimni o'ylayotgandek tuyulasiz.

en: That is not the case at all.
uz: Bu umuman shunday emas.

en: I am simply marrying for my own sake, because things are hard for me.
uz: Men shunchaki o'zim uchun turmush quryapman, chunki bu men uchun qiyin.

en: Though, of course, I shall be glad if I succeed in being useful to my family.
uz: Garchi, albatta, agar oilamga foydali bo'lishga muvaffaq bo'lsam, xursand bo'laman.

en: But that is not the chief motive for my decision.
uz: Ammo bu mening qarorim uchun asosiy sabab emas.

en: …” “She is lying,” he thought to himself, biting his nails vindictively.
uz: U yolg'on gapiryapti, deb o'ylaganida, o'z qulog'ini o'g'ib qo'ydi.

en: She won’t admit she wants to do it out of charity!
uz: U buni xayriya ishlaridan qilishni xohlayotganini tan olmaydi!

en: Oh, base characters!
uz: Oh, asosiy belgilar!

en: They even love as though they hate.
uz: Ular hatto nafratlanish kabi sevishadi.

en: … Oh, how I … hate them all!” “In fact,” continued Dounia, “I am marrying Pyotr Petrovitch because of two evils I choose the less.
uz: Oh, men ... ulardan hammasini nafratlanaman! Aslida, Dounia davom etdi,Pyotr Petrovitch bilan turmush quraman, chunki men kamroq tanlagan ikkita yomonlik tufayli.

en: I intend to do honestly all he expects of me, so I am not deceiving him.
uz: Men uning mendan kutgan hamma narsani halollik bilan bajarishni rejalashtiryapman, shuning uchun uni aldamayapman.

en: … Why did you smile just now?” She, too, flushed, and there was a gleam of anger in her eyes.
uz: ... Nega hozirgina tabassum qildingiz? U ham qizargan va uning ko'zlarida g'azab nurlari yoritilgan edi.

en: “All?” he asked, with a malignant grin.
uz: "Barchasi?" - deb so'radi u yomon ko'rinish bilan.

en: “Within certain limits.
uz: Ba'zi cheklovlar ichida.

en: Both the manner and form of Pyotr Petrovitch’s courtship showed me at once what he wanted.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitchning tanqid qilish usuli va shakli menga u nima istayotganini birdan ko'rsatdi.

en: He may, of course, think too well of himself, but I hope he esteems me, too.
uz: Albatta, u o'zi haqida juda yaxshi o'ylashi mumkin, lekin umid qilamanki, u meni ham hurmat qiladi.

en: … Why are you laughing again?” “And why are you blushing again?
uz: Nima uchun yana kulyapsan? Va nima uchun yana qizg'inlayapsan?

en: You are lying, sister.
uz: Siz yolg'on gapiryapsiz, singlim.

en: You are intentionally lying, simply from feminine obstinacy, simply to hold your own against me.
uz: Siz faqatgina ayollarning qatʼiyligiga koʻra, faqat menga qarshi oʻz fikrlaringizni qoʻyish uchun qasddan yolgʻon gapiryapsiz.

en: … You cannot respect Luzhin.
uz: Siz Luzhinni hurmat qila olmaysiz.

en: I have seen him and talked with him.
uz: Men uni ko'rdim va u bilan gaplashdim.

en: So you are selling yourself for money, and so in any case you are acting basely, and I am glad at least that you can blush for it.” “It is not true.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz o'zingizni pul uchun sotmoqdasiz va har holda siz o'zingizni oddiy qilib ko'rsata olasiz va hech bo'lmaganda buning uchun qizg'in bo'lishingizga quvonaman. Bu haqiqat emas.

en: I am not lying,” cried Dounia, losing her composure.
uz: Men yolg'on gapirmayapman, - deb qayg'urdi Dounia, o'z xotirjamligini yo'qotdi.

en: “I would not marry him if I were not convinced that he esteems me and thinks highly of me.
uz: U meni hurmat qilishiga va meni yaxshi ko'rishiga amin bo'lmasam, men u bilan turmush qurmasdim.

en: I would not marry him if I were not firmly convinced that I can respect him.
uz: Agar unga hurmat ko'rsatishimga qat'iy amin bo'lmasam, unga turmushga chiqmasdim.

en: Fortunately, I can have convincing
uz: Yaxshiyamki, men ishonch hosil qilishim mumkin

en: proof of it this very day … and such a marriage is not a vileness, as you say!
uz: Bu kunning o'zida buning isboti bo'ldi... va bunday nikoh siz aytganingizdek yomonlik emas!

en: And even if you were right, if I really had determined on a vile action, is it not merciless on your part to speak to me like that?
uz: Va agar siz haqli bo'lsangiz ham, agar men yomon ish qilishga qat'iy qaror qilgan bo'lsam ham, menga shunday gapirishingiz shafqatsiz emasmi?

en: Why do you demand of me a heroism that perhaps you have not either?
uz: Nega mendan sizda ham bo'lmagan g'ayratni talab qilyapsiz?

en: It is despotism; it is tyranny.
uz: Bu despotizm; bu tiraniyadir.

en: If I ruin anyone, it is only myself.
uz: Agar men kimnidir vayron qilsam, o'zimni o'zim vayron qilaman.

en: … I am not committing a murder.
uz: Men qotillik qilmayapman.

en: Why do you look at me like that?
uz: Nega menga shunday qaraysiz?

en: Why are you so pale?
uz: Nima uchun shunchalik yorqinsan?

en: Rodya, darling, what’s the matter?” “Good heavens!
uz: Rodya, sevgilim, nima bo'ldi?

en: You have made him faint,” cried Pulcheria Alexandrovna.
uz: Siz uni o'limdan mahrum qildingiz, - deb baqirdi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna.

en: A little giddiness —not fainting.
uz: Biroz ko'ngilsizlik not baytilish.

en: You have fainting on the brain.
uz: Sizning miyangiz o'zimni yo'qotib qo'ydi.

en: H’m, yes, what was I saying?
uz: Ha, ha, men nima deb yurgan edim?

en: In what way will you get convincing proof today that you can respect him, and that he … esteems you, as you said.
uz: Bugun siz unga hurmat ko'rsata olasiz va u sizni o'zingiz aytgandek qadrlayotganini qanday tasdiqlaysiz?

en: I think you said today?” “Mother, show Rodya Pyotr Petrovitch’s letter,” said Dounia.
uz: O'ylaymanki, siz bugun aytdingiz?Otam, Rodya Pyotr Petrovitchning xatini ko'rsating, dedi Dounia.

en: With trembling hands, Pulcheria Alexandrovna gave him the letter.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna unga maktubni titrayotgan qo'llari bilan berdi.

en: He took it with great interest, but, before opening it, he suddenly looked with a sort of wonder at Dounia.
uz: U uni katta qiziqish bilan qabul qildi, lekin uni ochishdan oldin, to'satdan Douniaga bir xil hayronlik bilan qaradi.

en: “It is strange,” he said, slowly, as though struck by a new idea.
uz: Bu g'alati, dedi u, sekin-sekin, xuddi yangi g'oyaga chalingan bo'lib.

en: “What am I making such a fuss for?
uz: Men nima uchun bunday g'alayon qilyapman?

en: What is it all about?
uz: Bu nima haqida?

en: Marry whom you like!” He said this as though to himself, but said it aloud, and looked for some time at his sister, as though puzzled.
uz: O'zingiz xohlagan kishi bilan turmush quring! U buni o'zi o'zicha aytdi, lekin u buni baland ovoz bilan aytdi va bir muncha vaqt o'z singlisiga qaradi.

en: He opened the letter at last, still with the same look of strange wonder on his face.
uz: U nihoyat maktubni ochdi, hali ham yuzida o'sha g'ayrioddiy taajjub ko'rinishi bor edi.

en: Then, slowly and attentively, he began reading, and read it through twice.
uz: Keyin, asta-sekin va diqqat bilan o'qishni boshladi va uni ikki marta o'qib chiqdi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna showed marked anxiety, and all indeed expected something particular.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna o'ta xavotirga tushdi va hammalari muayyan narsani kutishardi.

en: “What surprises me,” he began, after a short pause, handing the letter to his mother, but not addressing anyone in particular, “is that he is a business man, a lawyer, and his conversation is pretentious indeed, and yet he writes such an uneducated letter.” They all started.
uz: Meni hayratda qoldirgan narsa shundaki, u biroz to'xtab, maktubni onasiga uzatishni boshladi, ammo hech kimga murojaat qilmadi, bu u biznesmen, advokat va suhbatlari haqiqatan ham o'ziga xos bo'lib, ammo u bunday o'qimagan maktubni yozadi. Hammasi boshlandi.

en: They had expected something quite different.
uz: Ular umuman boshqacha narsani kutishgan.

en: “But they all write like that, you know,” Razumihin observed, abruptly.
uz: Ammo ularning barchasi shunday yozadi, siz bilasiz, Razumihin kuzatganidek, to'satdan.

en: “Have you read it?” “Yes.”
uz: Siz uni o'qiganmisiz? Ha.

en: “We showed him, Rodya.
uz: Biz unga ko'rsatdik, Rodya.

en: We … consulted him just now,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna began, embarrassed.
uz: Biz ... u bilan maslahatlashdik, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna boshlandi, uyalgan edi.

en: “That’s just the jargon of the courts,” Razumihin put in.
uz: Bu faqat sudlarning jargonidir,  Razumihin qo'ydi.

en: “Legal documents are written like that to this day.” “Legal?
uz: Hukumat hujjatlari bugungi kungacha shunday yozilmoqda. Hukumat?

en: Yes, it’s just legal —business language —not so very uneducated, and not quite educated —business language!” “Pyotr Petrovitch makes no secret of the fact that he had a cheap education, he is proud indeed of having made his own way,” Avdotya Romanovna observed, somewhat offended by her brother’s tone.
uz: Ha, bu faqat qonuniy biznes tili o'ta o'qimagan va o'ta o'qimagan biznes tili emas!Pyotr Petrovitch arzon ta'lim olganligini yashirmaydi, u o'z yo'lini topganidan g'ururlanadi, Avdotya Romanovna aytdi, akasi o'z tovushidan biroz xafa bo'ldi.

en: “Well, if he’s proud of it, he has reason, I don’t deny it.
uz: Agar u bunga g'ururlansa, buning sababi bor, men buni inkor etmayman.

en: You seem to be offended, sister, at my making only such a frivolous criticism on the letter, and to think that I speak of such trifling matters on purpose to annoy you.
uz: Qizim, maktubni tanqid qilishim va sizni ranjitish uchun bunday kichik narsalar haqida gapirayotganimni o'ylashim sizni xafa qilyapti.

en: It is quite the contrary, an observation apropos of the style occurred to me that is by no means irrelevant as things stand.
uz: Aksincha, men o'zimga kelib chiqqan holda, bu holatda hech qanday ahamiyatga ega bo'lmagan uslubni ko'rib chiqdim.

en: There is one expression, ‘blame yourselves,’ put in very significantly and plainly, and there is besides a threat that he will go away at once if I am present.
uz: O'zingizni ayblang, degan bir ibora juda aniq va aniq qo'llanilgan va agar men hozir bo'lsam, u darhol yo'qolishi xavfi ham bor.

en: That threat to go away is equivalent to a threat to abandon you both if you are disobedient, and to abandon you now after summoning you to Petersburg.
uz: Bu qo'rqinch, agar itoatsiz bo'lsangiz, sizlarni tashlab ketish va sizni Sankt-Peterburgga chaqirtirganimdan keyin sizni hozir tashlab ketish bilan tengdir.

en: Well, what do you think?
uz: Xo'sh, siz nima deb o'ylaysiz?

en: Can one resent such an expression from Luzhin, as we should if he” (he pointed to Razumihin) “had written it, or Zossimov, or one of us?” “N-no,” answered Dounia, with more animation.
uz: Luzhinning bunday so'zlaridan biz ham xafa bo'lishimiz mumkinmi, agar u (u Razumihinni ko'rsatdi) uni yozgan bo'lsa yoki Zossimov yoki bizlardan biri?

en: “I saw clearly that it was too naively expressed, and that perhaps he simply has no skill in writing … that is a true criticism, brother.
uz: Men bu so'zlarning juda naif so'zlanganini va ehtimol u shunchaki yozish mahoratini yo'qligini aniq ko'rdim ... bu haqiqiy tanqid, aka.

en: I did not expect, indeed  …” “It is expressed in legal style, and sounds coarser than perhaps he intended.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, men buni kutmagan edim ... Bu huquqiy uslubda ifodalangan va ehtimol u xohlaganidan ko'ra qattiqroq tuyuladi.

en: But I must disillusion you a little.
uz: Ammo men sizni biroz tushkunlikka tushirgan bo'laman.

en: There is one expression in the letter, one slander about me, and rather a contemptible one.
uz: Maktubda bitta ifodasi, men haqimda bitta tuhmat, balki kamsitilgan ifodasi bor.

en: I gave the money last night to the widow, a woman in consumption, crushed with trouble, and not ‘on the pretext of the funeral,’ but simply to pay for the funeral, and not to the daughter —a young woman, as he writes, of notorious behaviour (whom I saw last night for the first time in my life) —but to the widow.
uz: Kecha pulni beva ayolga berdim, bu ayol xavotirda edi, u xavotirda edi va uni o'z o'limi uchun emas, balki o'lim uchun to'lash uchun bergan edim, qizimga emas, balki notoriyalangan xulq-atvorga ega bo'lgan yosh ayolga bergan edim (u o'tgan kecha hayotimda birinchi marta ko'rdim), lekin beva ayolga.

en: In all this I see a too hasty desire to slander me and to raise dissension between us.
uz: Bularning barchasida meni yomon ko'rish va o'z-o'zimiz bilan kelishmovchilikni uyg'otish uchun juda tezkor istak borligini ko'ryapman.

en: It is expressed again in legal jargon, that is to say, with a too obvious display of the aim, and with a very naive eagerness.
uz: Bu yana huquqiy jargonda, ya'ni maqsadning juda aniq ko'rinishi va juda naif g'ayrat bilan ifodalanadi.

en: He is a man of intelligence, but to act sensibly, intelligence is not enough.
uz: U aqlli odam, lekin aqlli bo'lish uchun aqllilik yetarli emas.

en: shows the man and … I don’t think he has a great esteem for you.
uz: odamni ko'rsatadi va... men o'ylaymanki, u siz uchun katta hurmat ko'rsatmaydi.

en: I tell you this simply to warn you, because I sincerely wish for your good …” Dounia did not reply.
uz: Men buni shunchaki ogohlantirish uchun aytyapman, chunki sizning yaxshiligingizni chin dildan tilayman ... Dounia javob bermadi.

en: Her resolution had been taken.
uz: Uning qarori qabul qilingan edi.

en: She was only awaiting the evening.
uz: U faqat kechani kutardi.

en: “Then what is your decision, Rodya?” asked Pulcheria Alexandrovna, who was more uneasy than ever at the sudden, new businesslike tone of his talk.
uz: - Xo'sh, qaroringiz qanday, Rodya? - deb so'radi Pulcheria Aleksandrovna, uning nutqining to'satdan yangi, ishbilarmon tomoniga ko'ra, u har qachongidan ham ko'proq xavotirda edi.

en: “What decision?” “You see Pyotr Petrovitch writes that you are not to be with us this evening, and that he will go away if you come.
uz: Qanday qaror?Pyotr Petrovitchning bu kechqurun biz bilan bo'lmasligingizni va agar kelsangiz, ketishingizni yozganini ko'rasiz.

en: So will you … come?” “That, of course, is not for me to decide, but for you first, if you are not offended by such a request; and secondly, by Dounia, if she, too, is not offended.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz ... kelasizmi?  Albatta, bu mening qarorim emas, balki birinchi navbatda, agar siz bunday so'rov bilan xafa bo'lmasangiz, siz uchun; va ikkinchidan, Dounia tomonidan, agar u ham xafa bo'lmasa.

en: I will do what you think best,” he added, drily.
uz: Men sizning eng yaxshi deb o'ylayotganingizni qilaman, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u, quruqlik bilan.

en: “Dounia has already decided, and I fully agree with her,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna hastened to declare.
uz: Dunyo allaqachon qaror qabul qildi va men u bilan to'liq rozi bo'laman, deb Pulcheria Aleksandrovna shoshilinch ravishda e'lon qildi.

en: “I decided to ask you, Rodya, to urge you not to fail to be with us at this interview,” said Dounia.
uz: "Sendan, Rodya, ushbu intervyuda biz bilan birga bo'lishingizni iltimos qilishga qaror qildim", - dedi Dounia.

en: “Will you come?” “Yes.” “I will ask you, too, to be with us at eight o’clock,” she said, addressing Razumihin.
uz: Siz kelasizmi?   Ha.  Men sizdan ham soat sakkizlarda biz bilan bo'lishingizni so'rayman, dedi u Razumihinga murojaat qilib.

en: “Mother, I am inviting him, too.” “Quite right, Dounia.
uz: Otam, men ham uni taklif qilyapman. Toʻgʻri, Dounia.

en: Well, since you have decided,” added Pulcheria Alexandrovna, “so be it.
uz: Xo'sh, siz qaror qabul qilganingizdan so'ng Pulcheria Aleksandrovna qo'shdi, shunday bo'lsin.

en: I shall feel easier myself.
uz: O'zim ham o'zimni osonroq his qilaman.

en: I do not like concealment and deception.
uz: Men yashirish va aldashni yoqtirmayman.

en: Better let us have the whole truth.
uz: Biz butun haqiqatni bilib olsak yaxshi bo'lardi.

en: … Pyotr Petrovitch may be angry or not, now!”
uz: ...Pyotr Petrovitch hozir g'azablanadimi yoki yo'qmi!

en: IV At that moment the door was softly opened, and a young girl walked into the room, looking timidly about her.
uz: O'sha paytda eshik sekin ochildi va bir qiz xonadonga kirib, uning atrofida qo'rqqancha ko'rindi.

en: Everyone turned towards her with surprise and curiosity.
uz: Hamma uni hayron va qiziqarli ko'rib qoldi.

en: At first sight, Raskolnikov did not recognise her.
uz: Bir qarashda Raskolnikov uni tanimadi.

en: It was Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladov.
uz: Bu Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladov edi.

en: He had seen her yesterday for the first time, but at such a moment, in such surroundings and in such a dress, that his memory retained a very different image of her.
uz: U ayolni kecha birinchi marta ko'rgan edi, lekin shunday bir paytda, shunday muhitda va shunday kiyimda uning xotirasida u haqida boshqacha tasavvur saqlanib qolgan.

en: Now she was a modestly and poorly-dressed young girl, very young, indeed, almost like a child, with a modest and refined manner, with a candid but somewhat frightened-looking face.
uz: Endi u kamtarlik va yomon kiyim kiygan yosh qiz edi, juda yosh, haqiqatan ham, deyarli bolaga o'xshaydi, kamtarlik va soflik bilan, ochiq, ammo biroz qo'rqqan ko'rinadigan yuziga ega edi.

en: She was wearing a very plain indoor dress, and had on a shabby old-fashioned hat, but she still carried a parasol.
uz: U juda sodda ichki kiyim kiygan edi va eski moddan keskin bo'lgan to'pka kiygan edi, ammo hali ham payvandda edi.

en: Unexpectedly finding the room full of people, she was not so much embarrassed as completely overwhelmed with shyness, like a little child.
uz: O'ylamagan holda xonani odamlar bilan to'lgan holda, u shunchalik o'zlarini noqulay his qilmadi, balki kichkina bola kabi o'zlarini o'zlaricha o'zlaricha o'zlarini noqulay his qilgan.

en: She was even about to retreat.
uz: U hatto orqaga chiqmoqchi edi.

en: “Oh … it’s you!” said Raskolnikov, extremely astonished, and he, too, was confused.
uz: Oh ... bu sizsiz! dedi Raskolnikov, juda hayron va u ham chalg'ib qoldi.

en: He at once recollected that his mother and sister knew through Luzhin’s letter of “some young woman of notorious behaviour.” He had only just been protesting against Luzhin’s calumny and declaring that he had seen the girl last night for the first time, and suddenly she had walked in.
uz: U darhol onasi va singlisi Luzhinning maktubi orqali notoriyalangan xulq-atvorli bir yosh ayol haqida bilganini esladi. U faqat Luzhinning tuhmatiga qarshi norozilik ko'rsatib, o'tgan kecha qizni birinchi marta ko'rganini va to'satdan u kirib kelganini e'lon qildi.

en: He remembered, too, that he had not protested against the expression “of notorious behaviour.” All this passed vaguely and fleetingly through his brain, but looking at her more intently, he saw that the humiliated creature was so humiliated that he felt suddenly sorry for her.
uz: Shuningdek, u noto'g'ri xulq-atvorning ifodasini rad etmaganini ham esladi. Bularning barchasi uning miyasi orqali noaniq va o'tkinchi o'tdi, ammo unga diqqat bilan qarasa, u kamsitilgan yaratilganning shunchalik kamsitilganini ko'rdiki, u uchun to'satdan rahm-shafqat ko'rdi.

en: When she made a movement to retreat in terror, it sent a pang to his heart.
uz: U dahshatga toʻlib, orqaga qaytish harakatini qilganida, uning yuragi qattiq ogʻib ketdi.

en: “I did not expect you,” he said, hurriedly, with a look that made her stop.
uz: Men sizni kutmagan edim, - dedi u, shoshilinchlik bilan, uni to'xtatadigan ko'z bilan.

en: You come, no doubt, from Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Siz, shubhasiz, Katerina Ivanovna tomonidan kelgansiz.

en: Allow me —not there.
uz: Menga ruxsat bering, u erda bo'lmasin.

en: …” At Sonia’s entrance, Razumihin, who had been sitting on one of Raskolnikov’s three chairs, close to the door, got up to allow her to enter.
uz: ... Sonia kirib kelganida, Raskolnikovning uchta o'rinbosari bo'lgan Razumihin eshikdan yaqin o'tirganida, unga kirishga ruxsat berish uchun o'rnidan turibdi.

en: Raskolnikov had at first shown her the place on the sofa where Zossimov had been sitting, but feeling that the sofa which served him as a bed, was too familiar a place, he hurriedly motioned her to Razumihin’s chair.
uz: Raskolnikov dastlab Zossimov o'tirgan sofadagi joyni unga ko'rsatgan edi, lekin unga yotoq sifatida xizmat qiladigan sofa juda tanish joy ekanligini his etib, uni tezda Razumihinning kursiga ishora qildi.

en: “You sit here,” he said to Razumihin, putting him on the sofa.
uz: Siz bu yerda o'tirasiz, - dedi u Razumihinga va uni kanapga qo'ydi.

en: Sonia sat down, almost shaking with terror, and looked timidly at the two ladies.
uz: Sonia qo'rquvdan deyarli titrab, o'tirib, ikki xonimga qo'rqqancha qarab turdi.

en: It was evidently almost inconceivable to herself that she could sit down beside them.
uz: O'zi uchun ularning yonida o'tirishi deyarli tasavvurga ham kelmas edi.

en: At the thought of it, she was so frightened that she hurriedly got up again, and in utter confusion addressed Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu haqda o'ylaganida u shunchalik qo'rqqanki, tez turib, butunlay g'alati Raskolnikovga murojaat qildi.

en: “I … I … have come for one minute.
uz: Men bir daqiqaga keldim.

en: Forgive me for disturbing you,” she began falteringly.
uz: Sizni xafa qilganim uchun kechiringlar, - deb o'ylashni boshladi.

en: “I come from Katerina Ivanovna, and she had no one to send.
uz: Men Katerina Ivanovnadanman va unga jo'natish uchun hech kim yo'q edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna told me to beg you … to be at the service … in the morning … at Mitrofanievsky … and then … to us … to her … to do her the honour … she told me to beg you …” Sonia stammered and ceased speaking.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna menga senga iltijo qilishimni aytdi ... ertalab ... Mitrofanievskida ... xizmatda bo'lishimni va keyin ... bizga ... unga ... onaga ... hurmat ko'rsatishni aytdi ... u menga senga iltijo qilishimni aytdi ... Sonia gapirishni to'xtatdi va gapirishni to'xtatdi.

en: “I will try, certainly, most certainly,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Men harakat qilaman, albatta, albatta,  Raskolnikov javob berdi.

en: He, too, stood up, and he, too, faltered and could not finish his sentence.
uz: U ham o'rnidan turdi va o'zi ham o'z jumlasini bitira olmagan.

en: “Please sit down,” he said, suddenly.
uz: Iltimos, o'tiring, dedi u, birdan.

en: “I want to talk to you.
uz: Men siz bilan gaplashmoqchiman.

en: You are perhaps in a hurry, but please, be so kind, spare me two minutes,” and he drew up a chair for her.
uz: Ehtimol, siz shoshilyapsiz, lekin iltimos, menga ikki daqiqa vaqt ajrating, va u ayol uchun o'rinni tayyorladi.

en: Sonia sat down again, and again timidly she took a hurried, frightened look at the two ladies, and dropped her eyes.
uz: Sonia yana o'tirdi va yana qo'rqqancha ikkita ayolga shoshilinch, qo'rqqan ko'z bilan qarab, ko'zlarini tushirdi.

en: Raskolnikov’s pale face flushed, a shudder passed over him, his eyes glowed.
uz: Raskolnikovning o'tkir yuzlari qizg'inladi, uning ustiga titrishlar o'tdi, ko'zlari yorqin bo'ldi.

en: “Mother,” he said, firmly and insistently, “this is Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladov, the daughter of that unfortunate Mr.
uz: Otam, dedi u qat'iy va qat'iylik bilan,bu Sofiya Semyonovna Marmeladov, o'sha baxtsiz Mr.ning qizi.

en: Marmeladov, who was run over yesterday before my eyes, and of whom I was just telling you.” Pulcheria Alexandrovna glanced at Sonia, and slightly screwed up her eyes.
uz: Kecha ko'zlarim oldida Marmeladovni o'g'irlab o'tkazilgan va men sizga aytib berayotgan edim. Pulcheria Aleksandrovna Soniaga qarab, ko'zlarini biroz o'zgartirgan.

en: In spite of her embarrassment before Rodya’s urgent and challenging look, she could not deny herself that satisfaction.
uz: Rodyaning shoshilinch va qiyin ko'rinishi oldida o'zidan xafa bo'lishiga qaramay, u o'zidan shu qoniqishdan voz kecholmadi.

en: Dounia gazed gravely and intently into the poor girl’s face, and scrutinised
uz: Dounia kambag'al qizning yuziga jiddiy va diqqat bilan qaradi va uni sinchkovlik bilan tekshiradi.

en: her with perplexity.
uz: U g'alati bo'lib qoldi.

en: Sonia, hearing herself introduced, tried to raise her eyes again, but was more embarrassed than ever.
uz: Sonia o'zini tanishtirganini eshitib, yana ko'zlarini ko'tarib ko'rishga harakat qildi, ammo u har qachongidan ham orqaga qarab qolibdi.

en: “I wanted to ask you,” said Raskolnikov, hastily, “how things were arranged yesterday.
uz: Men sizdan so'rashni istardim, dedi Raskolnikov, shoshilinch, chalar kecha qanday tuzilganini.

en: You were not worried by the police, for instance?” “No, that was all right … it was too evident, the cause of death … they did not worry us … only the lodgers are angry.” “Why?” “At the body’s remaining so long.
uz: Misol uchun, siz politsiya haqida tashvishlanmaganmisiz?  Yo'q, bu yaxshi edi ... bu juda aniq edi, o'lim sababi ... ular bizni tashvishlantirmagan edi ... faqat uy egalari g'azablanishmoqda.  Nima uchun?   O'sha paytgacha qolgan jasadlar haqida.

en: You see it is hot now.
uz: Endi issiq bo'lganini ko'rasiz.

en: So that, today, they will carry it to the cemetery, into the chapel, until tomorrow.
uz: Shunday qilib, bugun uni qabrga, chaplaga olib ketishadi, ertagacha.

en: At first Katerina Ivanovna was unwilling, but now she sees herself that it’s necessary …” “Today, then?” “She begs you to do us the honour to be in the church tomorrow for the service, and then to be present at the funeral lunch.” “She is giving a funeral lunch?” “Yes … just a little.
uz: Avvaliga Katerina Ivanovna xohlamagan edi, lekin hozir o'ziga kerakligini ko'radi ...Bugun, shundaymi?U sizlardan ertaga cherkovda xizmat qilish sharafini so'rab, keyin dafn marosimida ishtirok etishingizni so'raydi.U dafn marosimini o'tkazmoqda?Ha... faqat biroz.

en: … She told me to thank you very much for helping us yesterday.
uz: U menga kecha bizga yordam berganingiz uchun katta rahmat aytdi.

en: But for you, we should have had nothing for the funeral.” All at once her lips and chin began trembling, but, with an effort, she controlled herself, looking down again.
uz: Ammo siz uchun, bizda dafn marosimi uchun hech narsa bo'lmasdi. Birdan uning og'izlari va burunlari titra boshladi, ammo u bir bor harakat qilib, o'zini nazorat qilib, yana pastga qarab qoldi.

en: During the conversation, Raskolnikov watched her carefully.
uz: Suhbat paytida Raskolnikov uni diqqat bilan kuzatib turdi.

en: She had a thin, very thin, pale little face, rather irregular and angular, with a sharp little nose and chin.
uz: U juda chiroyli, juda chiroyli, ko'rinmas va burchakli, o'ta chiroyli yuziga ega edi.

en: She could not have been called pretty, but her blue eyes were so clear, and when they lighted up, there was such a kindliness and simplicity in her expression that one could not help being attracted.
uz: Uni go'zal deb atash mumkin emas edi, lekin uning ko'k ko'zlari juda aniq edi va ular yoritilganda uning ifodasida shunchalik mehribonlik va soddalik bor ediki, odam o'ziga jalb bo'lishdan bosh tortmasdi.

en: Her face, and her whole figure indeed, had another peculiar characteristic.
uz: Uning yuzi va butun shaxsiyatida yana bir o'ziga xos xususiyat bor edi.

en: In spite of her eighteen years, she looked almost a little girl —almost a child.
uz: O'n sakkiz yoshga kirishiga qaramay, u deyarli kichkina qizchaga o'xshaydi.

en: And in some of her gestures, this childishness seemed almost absurd.
uz: Va ba'zi harakatlarida bu bolalik deyarli g'alati tuyulgan.

en: “But has Katerina Ivanovna been able to manage with such small means?
uz: Agar Katerina Ivanovna bunday kichik mablag'lar bilan ishlashga muvaffaq bo'lsa-da?

en: Does she even mean to have a funeral lunch?” Raskolnikov asked, persistently keeping up the conversation.
uz: U hatto o'z o'zidan kechki ovqatini o'tkazishni xohlaydimi? - deb so'radi Raskolnikov, suhbatni davom ettirib.

en: “The coffin will be plain, of course … and everything will be plain, so it won’t cost much.
uz: Taxt oddiy bo'ladi, albatta ... va hamma narsa oddiy bo'ladi, shuning uchun u juda qimmatga tushmaydi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna and I have reckoned it all out, so that there will be enough left … and Katerina Ivanovna was
uz: Katerina Ivanovna va men hamma narsani hisoblab chiqdik, shuning uchun yetarlicha qolish kerak ... va Katerina Ivanovna o'z ishini bajargan edi.

en: very anxious it should be so.
uz: Bu shunday bo'lishi kerak, deb juda xavotirlanaman.

en: You know one can’t … it’s a comfort to her … she is like that, you know.
uz: Bilasizmi, odam qila olmaydi ... bu unga tasalli beradi ... u shunday, bilasiz.

en: …” “I understand, I understand … of course … why do you look at my room like that?
uz: ... Men tushunaman, tushunaman ... albatta ... nega siz mening xonamga shunday qaraysiz?

en: My mother has just said it is like a tomb.” “You gave us everything yesterday,” Sonia said suddenly, in reply, in a loud rapid whisper; and again she looked down in confusion.
uz: Onam bu xuddi qabr kabi ekanligini aytdi. Siz bizga hamma narsani kecha berdingiz, Sonia to'satdan javob berib, baland ovoz bilan tezda shovqin so'zladi va yana g'alati ko'z bilan pastga qaradi.

en: Her lips and chin were trembling once more.
uz: Uning og'izlari va burunlari yana titrab turardi.

en: She had been struck at once by Raskolnikov’s poor surroundings, and now these words broke out spontaneously.
uz: U Raskolnikovning kambag'al atrofida o'tirganidan darhol ajablanib qoldi va endi bu so'zlar o'z-o'zidan chiqdi.

en: There was a light in Dounia’s eyes, and even Pulcheria Alexandrovna looked kindly at Sonia.
uz: Dounia ko'zlarida nur bor edi va hatto Pulcheria Aleksandrovna ham Soniaga mehribonlik ila qarab turardi.

en: “Rodya,” she said, getting up, “we shall have dinner together, of course.
uz: "Rodya", - dedi u, o'rnidan turib, "biz, albatta, birga ovqatlanamiz.

en: … And you, Rodya, had better go for a little walk, and then rest and lie down before you come to see us.
uz: Siz ham, Rodya, bir oz yurib, keyin bizga tashrif buyurishdan oldin dam olib, uxlashingiz kerak.

en: … I am afraid we have exhausted you.
uz: O'ylaymanki, biz sizni bezovta qildik.

en: …” “Yes, yes, I’ll come,” he answered, getting up fussily.
uz: "Ha, ha, men kelaman", deb javob berdi u, o'zidan turib, g'azabga to'ldi.
