en: “But I have something to see to.” “But surely you will have dinner together?” cried Razumihin, looking in surprise at Raskolnikov.
uz: Ammo men ko'rib chiqishim kerak bo'lgan bir narsa bor.Ammo sizlar albatta birga ovqatlanasizmi? - deb qayg'urdi Razumihin, Raskolnikovga hayronlik bilan qarab.

en: “What do you mean?” “Yes, yes, I am coming … of course, of course!
uz: Siz nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?Ha, ha, men kelaman... albatta, albatta!

en: And you stay a minute.
uz: Va siz bir daqiqa qoling.

en: You do not want him just now, do you, mother?
uz: Siz uni hozir xohlamaysiz, shundaymi, onam?

en: Or perhaps I am taking him from you?” “Oh, no, no.
uz: Yoki ehtimol men uni sening oldingdan olib ketyapmanmi?Oh, yo'q, yo'q.

en: And will you, Dmitri Prokofitch, do us the favour of dining with us?” “Please do,” added Dounia.
uz: Va siz, Dmitri Prokofitch, biz bilan birga ovqatlanish uchun bizga yordam berasizmi?  Iltimos, qil, Dounia qo'shdi.

en: Razumihin bowed, positively radiant.
uz: Razumihin bo'yin egib, ijobiy ravishda yorqin bo'ldi.

en: For one moment, they were all strangely embarrassed.
uz: Bir zum davomida hamma g'alati darajada o'zlarini noqulay his qildilar.

en: “Goodbye, Rodya, that is till we meet.
uz: Xudojo'y, Rodya, bu biz uchrashuvga qadar.

en: I do not like saying goodbye.
uz: Men salom aytishni yoqtirmayman.

en: Ah, I have said goodbye again.” Pulcheria Alexandrovna meant to greet Sonia, too; but it somehow failed to come off, and she went in a flutter out of the room.
uz: Ah, men yana salom berdim. Pulcheria Aleksandrovna Soniaga ham salom bermoqchi edi; lekin u qandaydir tarzda tushmadi va u xonadan shovqincha chiqib ketdi.

en: But Avdotya Romanovna seemed to await her turn, and following her mother out, gave Sonia an attentive, courteous bow.
uz: Ammo Avdotya Romanovna o'z navbatini kutganday tuyuladi va onasini izlab chiqib, Soniaga diqqatli, xushmuomalalik bilan quloq soldi.

en: Sonia, in confusion, gave a hurried, frightened curtsy.
uz: Sonia g'alati bo'lib, shoshilinch, qo'rqinchli kursiy so'zlarni aytdi.

en: There was a look of poignant discomfort in her face, as though Avdotya Romanovna’s courtesy and attention were oppressive and painful to her.
uz: Uning yuziga o'ta g'alati ko'rinish ko'rindi, xuddi Avdotya Romanovnaning xushmuomalaligi va e'tiborlari unga zulm qiluvchi va og'riqli bo'lgani kabi.

en: “Dounia, goodbye,” called Raskolnikov, in the passage.
uz: Dunia, salom, Raskolnikov deb nomlangan, o'tishida.

en: “Give me your hand.” “Why, I did give it to you.
uz: Menga qo'lingni bering.  Nima uchun, men uni sizga berdim.

en: Have you forgotten?” said Dounia, turning warmly and awkwardly to him.
uz: O'zingizni unutib qo'ydingizmi? - dedi Dounia, unga iliq va noqulay qarab.

en: “Never mind, give it to me again.” And he squeezed her fingers warmly.
uz: Menga xalaqit bermang, yana menga ber. Va u uning barmoqlarini iliq surdi.

en: Dounia smiled, flushed, pulled her hand away, and went off quite happy.
uz: Dounia tabassum qildi, ko'tarildi, qo'lini olib ketdi va juda xursand bo'ldi.

en: “Come, that’s capital,” he said to Sonia, going back and looking brightly at her.
uz: - Kel, bu - poytaxt, - dedi u Soniaga, qaytib kelib, unga chiroyli qarab turdi.

en: “God give peace to the dead, the living have still to live.
uz: Xudo o'liklarga tinchlik bersin, tiriklar hali ham yashashi kerak.

en: That is right, isn’t it?” Sonia looked surprised at the sudden brightness of his face.
uz: Soʻng Sonia yuzidagi toʻsatdan yorqinlikka hayron boʻlib koʻrindi.

en: He looked at her for some moments in silence.
uz: U bir necha daqiqalar sukut saqlash bilan unga qaradi.

en: The whole history of the dead father floated before his memory in those moments.
uz: O'lgan otasining butun tarixi o'sha paytlarda uning xotirasida uchib turardi.

en: … “Heavens, Dounia,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna began, as soon as they were in the street, “I really feel relieved myself at coming away — more at ease.
uz: Osmonlar, Dounia, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna boshlandi, ular ko'chada bo'lganidan so'ng, Men o'zimni yanada xotirjam bo'lib ketayotganimdan chindan ham xotirjam his qildim.

en: How little did I think yesterday in the train that I could ever be glad of that.” “I tell you again, mother, he is still very ill.
uz: Kecha poyezdda men bundan xursand bo'lishim mumkinligini juda kam o'yladim.Sizga yana aytaman, onam, u hali ham juda kasal.

en: Perhaps worrying about us upset him.
uz: Ehtimol, biz uchun tashvishlanib, uni xafa qilgan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: We must be patient, and much, much can be forgiven.” “Well, you were not very patient!” Pulcheria Alexandrovna caught her up, hotly and jealously.
uz: Biz sabrli bo'lishimiz kerak va ko'p, ko'p gunohlar kechirilishi mumkin.Ha, siz juda sabrli emas edingiz! Pulcheria Aleksandrovna uni qizg'in va hasad bilan ushlab oldi.

en: “Do you know, Dounia, I was looking at you two.
uz: Bilasizmi, Dounia, men siz ikkovingizga qarayotgan edim.

en: You are the very portrait of him, and not so much in face as in soul.
uz: Siz uning suratidirsiz, yuzida emas, balki ruhida.

en: You are both melancholy, both morose and hot-tempered, both haughty and both generous.
uz: Sizlar ikkalasi ham melanxoly, ikkalasi ham murakkab va issiq, ikkalasi ham mag'rur va ikkalasi ham saxiysiz.

en: … Surely he can’t be an egoist, Dounia.
uz: Albatta, u xudbin bo'lishi mumkin emas, Dounia.

en: When I think of what is in store for us this evening, my heart sinks!” “Don’t be uneasy, mother.
uz: Bugun kechqurun biz uchun nima bo'lishi haqida o'ylayotganimda, yuragim cho'kadi!Xavotirjam bo'lma, ona.

en: What must be, will be.” “Dounia, only think what a position we are in!
uz: Nima bo'lishi kerak, nima bo'ladi. Dunyo, biz qanday holatda ekanligimizni o'ylab ko'ring!

en: What if Pyotr Petrovitch breaks it off?” poor Pulcheria Alexandrovna blurted out, incautiously.
uz: Bordiyu Pyotr Petrovitch uni buzsa nima bo'ladi? kambag'al Pulcheria Aleksandrovna ehtiyotsizlik bilan gapirib yubordi.

en: “He won’t be worth much if he does,” answered Dounia, sharply and contemptuously.
uz: Agar shunday qilsa, u hech narsaga arzimaydi, deb javob berdi Dounia keskin va nohaqlik bilan.

en: “We did well to come away,” Pulcheria Alexandrovna hurriedly broke in.
uz: Biz ketish uchun yaxshi ish qildik, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna shoshilinch ravishda kirdi.

en: “He was in a hurry about some business or other.
uz: U biron-bir ish bilan shug'ullanish uchun shoshilinch edi.

en: If he gets out and has a breath of air … it is fearfully close in his room.
uz: Agar u tashqariga chiqsa va nafas olsa, uning xonasi qo'rqinchli darajada yaqin bo'ladi.

en: … But where is one to get a breath of air here?
uz: Ammo bu yerda nafas olish uchun qayerdan foydalanish mumkin?

en: The very streets here feel like shut-up rooms.
uz: Bu yerdagi ko'chalar yopilgan xonalarga o'xshaydi.

en: … stay … this side  … they will crush you —carrying something.
uz: ... qoling ... bu tarafda ... ular sizni bir narsani olib yurgan holda ezib tashlaydilar.

en: Why, it is a piano they have got, I declare … how they push!
uz: Axir, ularning bor pianoni bor, deb aytaman... qanday ta'qib qilayotganini!

en: … I am very much afraid of that young woman, too.” “What young woman, mother?” “Why, that Sofya Semyonovna, who was there just now.” “Why?” “I have a presentiment, Dounia.
uz: Men ham o'sha yosh ayoldan juda qo'rqaman.Qanday yosh ayol, ona? Nega, hozir u yerda bo'lgan Sofiya Semyonovna. Nima uchun? Menga bir his-tuyg'u bor, Dounia.

en: Well, you may believe it or not, but as soon as she came in, that very minute, I felt that she was the chief cause of the trouble.
uz: Xo'sh, ishonasizmi yoki yo'qmi, lekin u kelganidan so'ng, aynan o'sha daqiqada, muammolarning asosiy sababchisi u ekanligini his qildim.

en: …” “Nothing of the sort!” cried Dounia, in vexation.
uz: Hech narsa bunday emas! Dounia xafa bo'lib, baqirib yubordi.

en: “What nonsense, with your presentiments, mother!
uz: Sizning his-tuyg'ularingiz bilan nima to'g'rilik, onam!

en: He only made her acquaintance the evening before, and he did not know her when she came in.” “Well, you will see.
uz: O'sha kuni kechqurun u bilan tanishib olgan va u kelganida uni tanimagan.Hmm, ko'rasiz.

en: … She worries me; but you will see, you will see!
uz: U meni xavotirga solmoqda, lekin siz ko'rasiz, ko'rasiz!

en: I was so frightened.
uz: Men juda qo'rqardim.

en: She was gazing at me with those eyes.
uz: U menga o'sha ko'zlar bilan qarab turardi.

en: I could scarcely sit still in my chair when he began introducing her, do you remember?
uz: U uni tanishtirishni boshlaganida, men o'zimning o'rinchimda o'tirib o'tirolmasdim, eslaysizmi?

en: It seems so strange, but Pyotr Petrovitch writes like that about her, and he introduces her to us —to you!
uz: Bu juda g'alati tuyuladi, lekin Pyotr Petrovitch u haqida shunday yozadi va u uni bizga Sizga taqdim etadi!

en: So he must think a great deal of her.” “People will write anything.
uz: Shunday qilib, u bu ayol haqida ko'p o'ylashi kerak.  Odamlar hamma narsani yozishadi.

en: We were talked about and written about, too.
uz: Biz haqimizda ham so'zlab, ham yozib qo'yilganmiz.

en: I am sure that she is a good girl, and that it is all nonsense.” “God grant it may be!” “And Pyotr Petrovitch is a contemptible slanderer,” Dounia snapped out, suddenly.
uz: U yaxshi qiz ekanligiga aminman va bularning hammasi behuda. Xudo xohlasa bo'lsin!Pyotr Petrovitch esa begunoh shubha ostiga qo'ydi, Dounia birdan o'zini tashlab ketdi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna was crushed; the conversation was not resumed.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna vayron bo'ldi; suhbatni tiklashmadi.

en: “I will tell you what I want with you,” said Raskolnikov, drawing Razumihin to the window.
uz: Men senga sen bilan nima qilishni xohlayotganimni aytaman, - dedi Raskolnikov, Razumixinni derazaga chizib.

en: “Then I will tell Katerina Ivanovna that you are coming,” Sonia said hurriedly, preparing to depart.
uz: Keyin Katerina Ivanovnaga kelyapsan, deb aytaman, - dedi Sonia tez-tez, ketishga tayyorlanib.

en: “One minute, Sofya Semyonovna.
uz: Bir daqiqa, Sofya Semyonovna.

en: You are not in our way.
uz: Siz bizning yo'limizda emassiz.

en: I want to have another word or two with you.
uz: Siz bilan yana bir-ikki so'z gaplashmoqchiman.

en: Listen!” he turned suddenly to Razumihin again.
uz: Quloq solinglar! u birdan Razumihinga yana murojaat qildi.

en: “You know that … what’s his name … Porfiry Petrovitch?” “I should think so!
uz: Sening bilganingcha ... uning ismi nima ... Porfiry Petrovitch? Men shunday o'ylayman!

en: Why?” added the latter, with interest.
uz: Nima uchun? so'nggi qo'shib, qiziqish bilan qo'shib qo'ydi.

en: “Is not he managing that case … you know, about that murder?
uz: U o'sha o'ldirilgan kishini o'zi boshqarmaydimi?

en: … You were speaking about it yesterday.” “Yes … well?” Razumihin’s eyes opened wide.
uz: Kecha siz bu haqda gapirgan edingiz.Ha... yaxshi? Razumihining ko'zlari keng ochildi.

en: “He was inquiring for people who had pawned things, and I have some pledges there, too —trifles —a ring my sister gave me as a keepsake when I left home, and my father’s silver watch —they are only worth five or six roubles altogether … but I value them.
uz: U odamlarni g'amxo'rlik qilib olgan kishilar haqida so'ragan edi va men u yerda ba'zi va'dalar, shuningdek, trifles qizog'im uydan ketayotganimda eslatma sifatida bergan bir qurtamning g'alabasi va otamning kumush soatlari u jami besh yoki olti rublga arziydi ... lekin men ularni qadrlayman.

en: So what am I to do now?
uz: Xo'sh, endi nima qilishim kerak?

en: I do not want to lose the things, especially the watch.
uz: Men bu narsalarni, ayniqsa, soatni yo'qotishni istamayman.

en: I was quaking just now, for fear mother would ask to look at it, when we spoke of Dounia’s watch.
uz: Dounia soatlari haqida gapirganimizda, onam uni ko'rishni so'raydi, deb qo'rqqanim uchun hozir titragan edim.

en: It is the only thing of father’s left us.
uz: Otam bizga qoldirgan yagona narsa bu.

en: She would be ill if it were lost.
uz: Agar uni yo'qotsak, u kasal bo'ladi.

en: You know what women are.
uz: Ayollar nima ekanligini bilasiz.

en: So tell me what to do.
uz: Shunday qilib, nima qilishim kerakligini ayting.

en: I know I ought to have given notice at the police station, but would it not be better to go straight to Porfiry?
uz: Men politsiya bo'limida xabar berishim kerakligini bilaman, lekin to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Porfirga borish yaxshiroq emasmi?

en: The matter might be settled more quickly.
uz: Bu masala tezroq hal qilinishi mumkin.

en: You see, mother may ask for it before dinner.” “Certainly not to the police station.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, ona kechki ovqatdan oldin uni so'raydi.Agar politsiya bo'limida bo'lmasin.

en: Certainly to Porfiry,” Razumihin shouted in extraordinary excitement.
uz: Chindan ham Porfirga, Razumihin nihoyatda hayajon bilan baqirib yubordi.

en: “Well, how glad I am.
uz: Ha, men qanchalik xursandman.

en: It is a couple of steps.
uz: Bu bir necha qadamdan iborat.

en: We shall be sure to find him.” “Very well, let us go.” “And he will be very, very glad to make your acquaintance.
uz: Biz uni topishga ishonch hosil qilamiz. Chindan ham yaxshi, ketaylik.  Va u siz bilan tanishishga juda, juda xursand bo'ladi.

en: I have often talked to him of you at different times.
uz: Men siz haqingizda unga ko'p marta turli vaqtda gapirganman.

en: I was speaking of you yesterday.
uz: Kecha men siz haqingizda gapirgan edim.

en: So you knew the old woman?
uz: Demak, siz keksa ayolni tanardingiz?

en: It is all turning out splendidly.
uz: Bularning barchasi chiroyli o'tmoqda.

en: … Oh, yes, Sofya Ivanovna …” “Sofya Semyonovna,” corrected Raskolnikov.
uz: Oh, ha, Sofiya Ivanovna Raskolnikovni tuzatdi.

en: “Sofya Semyonovna, this is my friend Razumihin, and he is a good man.” “If you have to go now,” Sonia was beginning, not looking at Razumihin at all, and still more embarrassed.
uz: Sofya Semyonovna, bu mening do'stim Razumihin va u yaxshi odam.Agar siz endi ketishingiz kerak bo'lsa,Sonya Razumihinni ko'rmay boshlagan edi va bundan ham og'irroq o'zini noqulay his qilardi.

en: “Let us go,” decided Raskolnikov.
uz: Let us go, Raskolnikov qaror qildi.

en: “I will come to you today, Sofya Semyonovna.
uz: Men bugun sizning oldingizga kelaman, Sofiya Semyonovna.

en: Only tell me where you live.”
uz: Faqat qaerda yashayotganingizni ayting.

en: He was not exactly ill at ease, but seemed hurried, and avoided her eyes.
uz: U o'zini yaxshi his qilmagan, lekin shoshilinch ko'rinardi va uning ko'zlaridan qochdi.

en: Sonia gave her address, and flushed as she did so.
uz: Sonia uning manzilini berdi va shu bilan birga o'z ko'zlarini ko'tardi.

en: They all went out together.
uz: Ular hammasi birga chiqib ketishdi.

en: “Don’t you lock up?” asked Razumihin, following him on to the stairs.
uz: siz qulfga kirmayapsizmi? deb so'radi Razumihin, uning orqasidan mertaga bordi.

en: “Never,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Raskolnikov hech qachon javob bermadi.

en: “I have been meaning to buy a lock for these two years.
uz: Men ushbu ikki yildan beri qulf sotib olishni rejalashtiryapman.

en: People are happy who have no need of locks,” he said, laughing, to Sonia.
uz: O'sha odamlar qulfga muhtoj bo'lmaganlar baxtlidir, - dedi u, kulgiga so'ng Soniaga.

en: They stood still in the gateway.
uz: Ular darvoza oldida to'xtashdi.

en: “Do you go to the right, Sofya Semyonovna?
uz: Sofiya Semyonovna, siz o'ng tomonga o'tasizmi?

en: How did you find me, by the way?” he added, as though he wanted to say something quite different.
uz: Meni qanday topdingiz? dedi u, xuddi boshqacha narsani aytmoqchi bo'lganidek.

en: He wanted to look at her soft clear eyes, but this was not easy.
uz: U uning yumshak va shaffof ko'zlarini ko'rishni xohlagan, ammo bu oson emas edi.

en: “Why, you gave your address to Polenka yesterday.” “Polenka?
uz: Nima uchun, siz o'zingizning manzilingizni Polenkaga kecha bergansiz.  Polenka?

en: Oh, yes; Polenka, that is the little girl.
uz: Oh, ha, Polenka, bu kichkina qiz.

en: Did I give her the address?” “Why, had you forgotten?” “No, I remember.” “I had heard my father speak of you … only I did not know your name, and he did not know it.
uz: Men unga manzilni berdimmi?  Nega, siz unutib qo'ydingizmi?  Yo'q, eslayman.  Otam siz haqingizda gapirganini eshitgan edim ... faqat men sizning ismingizni bilmasdim va u ham buni bilmasdi.

en: And now I came … and as I had learnt your name, I asked today, ‘Where does Mr.
uz: Va endi men keldim ... va sizning ismingizni bilib, bugun so'radim,  Mr.

en: Raskolnikov live?’ I did not know you had only a room too.
uz: Raskolnikov jonli? Men sizning ham faqatgina bir xonangiz borligini bilmasdim.

en: … Goodbye, I will tell Katerina Ivanovna.” She was extremely glad to escape at last; she went away looking down, hurrying to get out of sight as soon as possible, to walk the twenty steps to the turning on the right and to be at last alone, and then moving rapidly along, looking at no one, noticing nothing, to think, to remember, to meditate on every word, every detail.
uz: Katerina Ivanovnaga salom aytayman. U nihoyat qochib ketishidan nihoyat xursand edi; u pastga qarab ketdi, ko'zdan tezroq chiqib ketish uchun shoshildi, o'ngga burish uchun yigirma qadam yurdi va nihoyat yolg'iz bo'ldi, so'ngra hech kimga nazar solmay, hech narsa sezmay, har bir so'zni, har bir tafsilotni o'ylab, eslab, mulohaza yuritishga harakat qildi.

en: Never, never had she felt anything like this.
uz: Hech qachon, hech qachon u bunday his-tuyg'ularni his qilmagan.

en: Dimly and unconsciously a whole new world was opening before her.
uz: O'zidan-o'zidan butunlay yangi dunyo uning oldida ochilmoqda edi.

en: She remembered suddenly that Raskolnikov meant to come to her that day, perhaps at once!
uz: U Raskolnikovning o'sha kuni, ehtimol darhol, uning oldiga kelishni rejalashtirganini birdan esladi!

en: “Only not today, please, not today!” she kept muttering with a sinking heart, as though entreating someone, like a frightened child.
uz: Bugun emas, bugun emas, iltimos! u qo'rqib ketgan yurak bilan birovga iltijo qilgandek, qo'rqib ketgan bola kabi g'ayrat bilan gapirgan.

en: to me … to that room … he will see … oh, dear!” She was not capable at that instant of noticing an unknown gentleman who was watching her and following at her heels.
uz: menga ... o'sha xonada ... u ko'radi ... oh, aziz! U o'sha daqiqada uni kuzatib turgan va uning izidan ergashayotgan noma'lum bir xonimni ko'rishga qodir emas edi.

en: He had accompanied her from the gateway.
uz: U qizni darvoza tomondan kuzatib borgan edi.

en: Razumihin, Raskolnikov, and she stood still at parting on the pavement, this gentleman, who was just passing, started on hearing Sonia’s words: “and I asked where Mr.
uz: Razumihin, Raskolnikov va u piyoda bo'lishda to'xtab turishganida, o'tib ketayotgan bu xonim Sonia so'zlarini eshitishni boshladi:

en: Raskolnikov lived?” He turned a rapid but attentive look upon all three, especially upon Raskolnikov, to whom Sonia was speaking; then looked back and noted the house.
uz: Raskolnikov tirikmi? U uchta kishiga, ayniqsa, Sonia bilan gaplashayotgan Raskolnikovga tezda, lekin diqqat bilan qaradi; so'ngra orqaga qarab, uyni ko'rdi.

en: All this was done in an instant as he passed, and trying not to betray his interest, he walked on more slowly as though waiting for something.
uz: Bularning barchasi o'tib ketayotgan bir daqiqada sodir bo'ldi va o'z manfaatini ko'zlamaslikka harakat qilib, u bir narsani kutgandek asta-sekin davom etdi.

en: He was waiting for Sonia; he saw that they were parting, and that Sonia was going home.
uz: U Soniyani kutib turardi; ular ajralib ketayotganini va Soniyaning uyga qaytayotganini ko'rdi.

en: I’ve seen that face somewhere,” he thought.
uz: O'zi o'ylaganidek, men bu yuzini qayerda ko'rganman.

en: “I must find out.” At the turning he crossed over, looked round, and saw Sonia coming the same way, noticing nothing.
uz: Men buni bilishim kerak. Buzib o'tganda u kesib o'tib, atrofga qarab, Sonia ham xuddi shu yo'ldan kelayotganini ko'rdi, lekin hech narsa payqamasdi.

en: She turned the corner.
uz: U burchadan burib ketdi.

en: He followed her on the other side.
uz: U ayolning orqasidan boshqa tomondan ergashib bordi.

en: After about fifty paces he crossed over again, overtook her and kept two or three yards behind her.
uz: Taxminan ellik qadamdan so'ng, u yana o'tib, uni yutib qo'ydi va ikki yoki uch metr orqada qoldi.

en: He was a man about fifty, rather tall and thickly set, with broad high shoulders which made him look as though he stooped a little.
uz: U taxminan ellik yoshda bo'lgan, o'ta baland va katta bo'lgan, keng va baland shohlari bor edi, bu esa uni biroz egri bo'lib ko'rinishga undardi.

en: He wore good and fashionable clothes, and looked like a gentleman of position.
uz: U yaxshi va zamonaviy kiyim kiygan va mansabdor kishiga o'xshaydigan edi.

en: He carried a handsome cane, which he tapped on the pavement at each step; his gloves were spotless.
uz: Uning qo'lida chiroyli tayoq bor edi, uni har qadamda piyoda ushlab turardi; uning qo'lqoplari leksiz edi.

en: He had a broad, rather pleasant face with high cheekbones and a fresh colour, not often seen in Petersburg.
uz: Uning keng, juda yoqimli yuzi, baland cheqmoqlari va yangi rangli yuzi bor edi, bu Petersburgda tez-tez ko'rinmas edi.

en: His flaxen hair was still abundant, and only touched here and there with grey, and his thick square beard was even lighter than his hair.
uz: Uning layneng sochlari hali ham ko'p edi va faqat bu erda-bu erda griy bilan uchragan edi va uning qalin kvadratli sakkizi sochlaridan ham yengilroq edi.

en: His eyes were blue and had a cold and thoughtful look; his lips were crimson.
uz: Uning ko'zlari ko'k va sovuq va mulohaza bilan ko'rinadi; og'izlari qizil.

en: He was a remarkedly well- preserved man and looked much younger than his years.
uz: U juda yaxshi saqlangan odam edi va o'z yoshidan ancha yoshroq ko'rinardi.

en: When Sonia came out on the canal bank, they were the only two persons on the pavement.
uz: Sonia kanal qirg'og'iga chiqqanida, yo'lda faqat ular ikkitasi edi.

en: He observed her dreaminess and preoccupation.
uz: U uning orzu va tashvishlanishini kuzatdi.

en: On reaching the house where she lodged, Sonia turned in at the gate; he followed her, seeming rather surprised.
uz: U yashaydigan uyga yetib kelganida, Sonia eshikdan o'zini o'zgartirdi; u ayolning orqasidan ergashib, juda hayron ko'rindi.

en: In the courtyard she turned to the right corner.
uz: hovlida o'ng burchakga burildi.

en: “Bah!” muttered the unknown gentleman, and mounted the stairs behind her.
uz: Bah! noma'lum xonim g'azablandi va uning orqasidan mertaga chiqib ketdi.

en: Only then Sonia noticed him.
uz: Faqat o'shanda Sonia uni payqadi.

en: She reached the third storey, turned down the passage, and rang at No.
uz: U uchinchi qavatga yetib, yo'lni pastga burdi va No.-ga qo'ng'iroq qildi.

en: On the door was inscribed in chalk, “Kapernaumov, Tailor.” “Bah!” the stranger repeated again, wondering at the strange coincidence, and he rang next door, at No.
uz: Eshikda chalka bilan yozilgan edi, Kapernaumov, Tailor. Bah! Begona odam o'ziga xos hodisaga hayron bo'lib, yana bir bor takrorladi va qo'shni eshikni chaqirdi. No.

en: The doors were two or three yards apart.
uz: Eshiklar ikki yoki uch metr masofada edi.

en: “You lodge at Kapernaumov’s,” he said, looking at Sonia and laughing.
uz: "Sizlar Kafarnahumda yashayapsizlar", - dedi u, Soniaga qarab kulgʻayib.

en: “He altered a waistcoat for me yesterday.
uz: Kecha u men uchun kamon o'zgartirgan.

en: I am staying close here at Madame Resslich’s.
uz: Men bu yerda yaqinda Madame Resslichsda yashayman.

en: How odd!” Sonia looked at him attentively.
uz: Qanday g'alati! Sonia unga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: “We are neighbours,” he went on gaily.
uz: Biz qo'shnilarmiz, u shodlik bilan davom etdi.

en: “I only came to town the day before yesterday.
uz: Men shaharga faqat bir kun oldin keldim.

en: Goodbye for the present.” Sonia made no reply; the door opened and she slipped in.
uz: Hozircha. Sonia hech qanday javob bermadi; eshik ochildi va u salom solib kirdi.

en: She felt for some reason ashamed and uneasy.
uz: U nima sababdan o'zini noloyiq va noqulay his qilgan.

en: On the way to Porfiry’s, Razumihin was obviously excited.
uz: Porfirysga borayotganda Razumihin, albatta, hayajonlangan edi.

en: “That’s capital, brother,” he repeated several times, “and I am glad!
uz: Bu poytaxt, aka, u bir necha bor takrorladi, va men xursandman!

en: I am glad!” “What are you glad about?” Raskolnikov thought to himself.
uz: Men xursandman!  Nima uchun siz xursandsiz? Raskolnikov o'zicha o'yladi.

en: “I didn’t know that you pledged things at the old woman’s, too.
uz: Siz ham keksa ayollarga va'da berganingizni bilmasdim.

en: And  … was it long ago?
uz: Va bu uzoq vaqt oldinmi?

en: I mean, was it long since you were there?” “What a simple-hearted fool he is!” “When was it?” Raskolnikov stopped still to recollect.
uz: Demak, siz u yerda qancha vaqt bo'lgansiz?U naqadar sodda yurakli o'g'il!Bu qachon bo'lgan? Raskolnikov eslab qolish uchun to'xtadi.

en: “Two or three days before her death it must have been.
uz: O'limidan ikki yoki uch kun oldin bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: But I am not going to redeem the things now,” he put in with a sort of hurried and conspicuous solicitude about the things.
uz: Ammo men hozir bu narsalarni sotib olishga bormayman, - dedi u, bir xil shoshilinch va ko'rinadigan qiziqish bilan.

en: “I’ve not more than a silver rouble left … after last night’s accursed delirium!” He laid special emphasis on the delirium.
uz: O'tgan kechalari la'natlangan deliriumdan so'ng... bir kumush rubldan ko'proq qolmadi! U deliriumga alohida e'tibor qaratdi.

en: “Yes, yes,” Razumihin hastened to agree —with what was not clear.
uz: Ha, ha,  Razumihin aniq bo'lmagan narsa bilan rozi bo'lishga shoshildi.

en: “Then that’s why you … were stuck … partly … you know in your delirium you were continually mentioning some rings or chains!
uz: Shundan keyin siz ... to'xtab qoldingiz ... qisman ... bilasizmi, deliriumingizda siz doimo ba'zi bir do'zax yoki zanjirlarni eslatib turgansiz!

en: Yes, yes … that’s clear, it’s all clear now.” “Hullo!
uz: Ha, ha... bu aniq, hozir hamma narsa aniq.Hullo!

en: How that idea must have got about among them.
uz: Qanday qilib bu g'oya ular orasida tarqalgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: Here this man will go to the stake for me, and I find him delighted at having it cleared up why I spoke of rings in my delirium!
uz: Mana, bu kishi men uchun cho'g'ga chiqadi va men uni nega delirimdagi do'zaxlar haqida gapirganimni tushuntirganimdan xursandman!

en: What a hold the idea must have on all of them!” “Shall we find him?” he asked suddenly.
uz: Bu g'oya ularning barchasini qanday ta'sirga tushirgan bo'lishi kerak!Biz Uni topamizmi? deb so'radi u to'satdan.

en: “Oh, yes,” Razumihin answered quickly.
uz: Oh, ha, Razumihin tez javob berdi.

en: “He is a nice fellow, you will see, brother.
uz: U yaxshi odam, ko'rasiz, aka.

en: Rather clumsy, that is to say, he is a man of polished manners, but I mean clumsy in a different sense.
uz: Koʻp oʻtkir, yaʼni u yaxshi xulq-atvorli kishi, lekin men boshqa maʼnoda oʻtkir deb oʻylayman.

en: He is an intelligent fellow, very much so indeed, but he has his own range of
uz: U aqlli odam, haqiqatan ham, juda aqlli, lekin uning o'zlarining o'zlarining o'ziga xos xususiyatlari bor.

en: … He is incredulous, sceptical, cynical … he likes to impose on people, or rather to make fun of them.
uz: ... U ko'rinmas, shubhali, sinik odamdir ... u odamlarga bosim o'tkazishni yaxshi ko'radi, yoki aslida ularni masxara qilishni yaxshi ko'radi.

en: His is the old, circumstantial method.
uz: Uning qadimgi, holatli usuli bor.

en: … But he understands his work … thoroughly.
uz: Ammo u o'z ishini chuqur tushunadi.

en: … Last year he cleared up a case of murder in which the police had hardly a clue.
uz: ...O'tgan yili u o'ldirilganlik to'g'risidagi ishni hal qildi, ammo politsiyaga bu haqda hech qanday ma'lumot yo'q edi.

en: He is very, very anxious to make your acquaintance!” “On what grounds is he so anxious?” “Oh, it’s not exactly … you see, since you’ve been ill I happen to have mentioned you several times.
uz: U siz bilan tanishishni juda istaydi! Nima sababdan u shunchalik tashvishlanmoqda?Oh, bu to'g'ri emas... bilasiz, kasal bo'lganingizdan beri men siz haqingizda bir necha marta aytib o'tganman.

en: … So, when he heard about you  … about your being a law student and not able to finish your studies, he said, ‘What a pity!’ And so I concluded … from everything together, not only that; yesterday Zametov … you know, Rodya, I talked some nonsense on the way home to you yesterday, when I was drunk … I am afraid, brother, of your exaggerating it, you see.” “What?
uz: Shunday qilib, u siz haqingizda eshitganida... siz huquqni o'qigan va o'qishni tugatolmaganingiz haqida gapirganida, u: "Bu juda achinarli! Shunday qilib, men ... hamma narsani birlashtirib, nafaqat o'sha, balki o'tgan kun Zametov... bilasizmi, Rodya, kecha uyga qaytib kelayotganimda, men mast bo'lganimda, sizga biroz g'alati gapirgan edim... Qorchimdaman, aka, siz buni haddan tashqari ko'paytirgan bo'lasiz.  Nima?

en: That they think I am a madman?
uz: Ular meni aqldan ozgan deb o'ylashlarini?

en: Maybe they are right,” he said with a constrained smile.
uz: Ehtimol, ular to'g'ri, - dedi u cheklangan tabassum bilan.

en: … That is, pooh, no!
uz: Demak, pooh, yo'q!

en: … But all that I said (and there was something else too) it was all nonsense, drunken nonsense.” “But why are you apologising?
uz: Ammo men aytgan hamma narsa (va yana bir narsa bor edi) bularning hammasi behuda, mast behuda edi. Ammo nega kechirim so'raysiz?

en: I am so sick of it all!” Raskolnikov cried with exaggerated irritability.
uz: Men bularning barchasidan charchadim! Raskolnikov haddan tashqari xafa bo'lib yig'ladi.

en: It was partly assumed, however.
uz: Biroq, bu qisman qabul qilingan.

en: “I know, I know, I understand.
uz: Men bilaman, bilaman, tushunaman.

en: Believe me, I understand.
uz: Menga ishoning, men tushunaman.

en: One’s ashamed to speak of it.” “If you are ashamed, then don’t speak of it.” Both were silent.
uz: Birov bu haqda gapirishdan uyalishi mumkin. Agar uyalsangiz, gapirmang. Ikkalasi ham sukut saqlashdi.

en: Razumihin was more than ecstatic and Raskolnikov perceived it with repulsion.
uz: Razumihin charchaganidan ko'ra ko'proq edi va Raskolnikov uni nafrat bilan ko'rdi.

en: He was alarmed, too, by what Razumihin had just said about Porfiry.
uz: U ham Razumihinning Porfiry haqida aytgan so'zlaridan xavotirga tushdi.

en: “I shall have to pull a long face with him too,” he thought, with a beating heart, and he turned white, “and do it naturally, too.
uz: Men ham u bilan uzoq masofa tutishim kerak, deb o'yladi u, yurak urib, oq bo'ldi va buni tabiiy ravishda ham qiladi.

en: But the most natural thing would be to do nothing at all.
uz: Ammo eng tabiiy narsa - umuman hech narsa qilmaslik.

en: Carefully do nothing at all!
uz: Ehtiyot bilan hech narsa qilmang!

en: No, carefully would not be natural again.
uz: Yo'q, ehtiyotkorlik bilan yana tabiiy bo'lmaydi.

en: … Oh, well, we shall see how it turns out.
uz: Oh, yaxshi, qanday bo'lishini ko'ramiz.

en: … We shall see … directly.
uz: ... Biz to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ko'ramiz.

en: Is it a good thing to go or not?
uz: Borish yaxshimi yoki yo'qmi?

en: The butterfly flies to the light.
uz: Ko'pik nurga uchadi.

en: My heart is beating, that’s what’s bad!” “In this grey house,” said Razumihin.
uz: Yuragim urmoqda, bu yomon narsa! Bu griq uyda, dedi Razumihin.

en: “The most important thing, does Porfiry know that I was at the old hag’s flat yesterday … and asked about the blood?
uz: Eng muhimi, Porfiry kecha men eski haykallar shahriga borganimni va qon haqida so'raganimni biladimi?

en: I must find that out instantly, as soon as I go in, find out from his face; otherwise … I’ll find out, if it’s my ruin.”
uz: Buni men darhol, kirganimdan so'ng, uning yuzidan bilib olishim kerak; aks holda... agar bu mening halokatim bo'lsa, bilib o'laman.

en: “I say, brother,” he said suddenly, addressing Razumihin, with a sly smile, “I have been noticing all day that you seem to be curiously excited.
uz: "Men aytaman, aka", - dedi u birdan Razumihinga murojaat qilib, o'ziga xos tabassum bilan. - Men kun bo'yi ko'rib kelamanki, siz g'alati hayajonlanayotgansiz.

en: Isn’t it so?” “Excited?
uz: Xo'sh, shunday emasmi?Xursand bo'ldingizmi?

en: Not a bit of it,” said Razumihin, stung to the quick.
uz: Hech bir narsa emas, - dedi Razumihin, tezda qovurib.

en: “Yes, brother, I assure you it’s noticeable.
uz: Ha, birodar, sizga ishontiramanki, bu sezilarli.

en: Why, you sat on your chair in a way you never do sit, on the edge somehow, and you seemed to be writhing all the time.
uz: Siz hech qachon o'tirmaydigan tarzda o'zingizning o'rindiqingizda o'tirgansiz, qandaydir tarzda chekkada o'tirgansiz va siz doimo burib turgandek ko'rinardingiz.

en: You kept jumping up for nothing.
uz: Siz hech narsa uchun qochib o'tmay qoldingiz.

en: One moment you were angry, and the next your face looked like a sweetmeat.
uz: Bir lahzada g'azablanardingiz, keyingi lahzada yuzingiz go'zal go'sht kabi ko'rinardi.

en: You even blushed; especially when you were invited to dinner, you blushed awfully.” “Nothing of the sort, nonsense!
uz: Hatto qizg'inib qo'ydingiz; ayniqsa, kechki ovqatga taklif etilganingizda, juda qizg'inib qo'ydingiz. Bunday narsa yo'q, axloqsiz gaplar!

en: What do you mean?” “But why are you wriggling out of it, like a schoolboy?
uz: Nima deyapsiz?  Ammo nega siz maktab o'quvchisi kabi o'zingizni bu ishdan mahrum qilyapsiz?

en: By Jove, there he’s blushing again.” “What a pig you are!” “But why are you so shamefaced about it?
uz: Yovuz, u yana qizg'inadi.Siz qanday do'st ekansiz! Ammo nega bu haqda o'zingizni o'ylamaysiz?

en: Stay, I’ll tell of you today.
uz: Qoling, men bugun siz haqingizda gapirib beraman.

en: I’ll make mother laugh, and someone else, too  …” “Listen, listen, listen, this is serious.
uz: Men onamni va boshqalarni kulg'ataman... Tinglang, tinglang, tinglang, bu jiddiy.

en: … What next, you fiend!” Razumihin was utterly overwhelmed, turning cold with horror.
uz: Keyin nima bo'ldi, ey iblis! Razumihin qo'rqinchga to'lib, qo'rqinchga to'lib-toshdi.

en: “What will you tell them?
uz: Siz ularga nima deysiz?

en: Come, brother … foo!
uz: Keling, aka... foo!

en: what a pig you are!” “You are like a summer rose.
uz: Qani, siz qanday do'stsiz!Siz yozgi gulga o'xshaysiz.

en: And if only you knew how it suits you; a Romeo over six foot high!
uz: Va agar siz bunga qanday mos kelishini bilganingizda edi; olti fut balandlikda Romeo!

en: And how you’ve washed today — you cleaned your nails, I declare.
uz: Va bugun qanday yuvganingni aytaman, tumshoqlaringni tozalaganingni aytaman.

en: That’s something unheard of!
uz: Bu hali eshitmagan narsa!

en: Why, I do believe you’ve got pomatum on your hair!
uz: Nima uchun, mening fikrimcha, sochlaringizda pomatum bor!

en: Bend down.” “Pig!” Raskolnikov laughed as though he could not restrain himself.
uz: G'iybat qiling. Pig! Raskolnikov o'zini tuta olmaydigan bo'lib kulganday kuldi.

en: So laughing, they entered Porfiry Petrovitch’s flat.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular kulishadi va Porfiry Petrovitchning xonasiga kirishadi.

en: This is what Raskolnikov wanted: from within they could be heard laughing as they came in, still guffawing in the passage.
uz: Raskolnikovning xohishi shuni edi: ichkaridan ular kirib kelganlarida, hali ham yo'ldan o'tish bilan kulishayotganini eshitish mumkin edi.

en: “Not a word here or I’ll … brain you!” Razumihin whispered furiously, seizing Raskolnikov by the shoulder.
uz: Bu yerda hech bir so'z yo'q, yoki men seni ... miyamga beraman! Razumihin g'azablanib, Raskolnikovning yelkasidan ushlab turdi.

en: V Raskolnikov was already entering the room.
uz: V. Raskolnikov allaqachon xonaga kirib kelgan edi.

en: He came in looking as though he had the utmost difficulty not to burst out laughing again.
uz: O'sha paytga kelib, xuddi yana kulishmay qolish uchun juda qiyin bo'lgandek ko'rindi.

en: Behind him Razumihin strode in gawky and awkward, shamefaced and red as a peony, with an utterly crestfallen and ferocious expression.
uz: Uning orqasidan Razumihin cho'g'ri va noqulay, sharmanda va qo'rqinchli bo'lib, o'ziga o'xshaydigan va g'azabga to'lib-toshadi.

en: His face and whole figure really were ridiculous at that moment and amply justified Raskolnikov’s laughter.
uz: Uning yuzi va butun shaxsiyati o'sha paytda juda g'alati edi va Raskolnikovning tabassumini oqlaydi.

en: Raskolnikov, not waiting for an introduction, bowed to Porfiry Petrovitch, who stood in the middle of the room looking inquiringly at them.
uz: Raskolnikov, tanishishni kutmay, Porfiry Petrovitchga sajda qildi, u xonaning o'rtasida turib, ularga savol-javob bilan qaradi.

en: He held out his hand and shook hands, still apparently making desperate efforts to subdue his mirth and utter a few words to introduce himself.
uz: U qo'lini ko'tarib qo'shdi va hali ham xursandchilikni yumshatish va o'zini tanishtirish uchun bir necha so'zlarni aytish uchun juda ko'p harakat qildi.

en: But he had no sooner succeeded in assuming a serious air and muttering something when he suddenly glanced again as though accidentally at Razumihin, and could no longer control himself: his stifled laughter broke out the more irresistibly the more he tried to restrain it.
uz: Ammo u jiddiy tuyg'ularni qabul qilib, bir narsani g'azabga solib o'tirmaganida, to'satdan Razumihinga to'satdan ko'z tikib, o'zini nazorat qila olmadi: uning o'zidan-o'zini tiygan kulishi, uni to'xtatishga harakat qilgan sari, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri chiqdi.

en: The extraordinary ferocity with which Razumihin received this “spontaneous” mirth gave the whole scene the appearance of most genuine fun and naturalness.
uz: Razumihinning o'zboshimchalik bilan xursand bo'lganini ko'rsatgan g'ayratli jahl butun sahnaga haqiqiy kulgi va tabiiylik ko'rinishini berdi.

en: Razumihin strengthened this impression as though on purpose.
uz: Razumihin bu taassurotni qasddan o'tkazgani kabi kuchaytirdi.

en: You fiend,” he roared, waving his arm which at once struck a little round table with an empty tea-glass on it.
uz: U qo'lini o'chirib, qichqirdi, bir lahzada u tomosha bo'lmagan choy shisha bilan kichik davra suhbatiga urildi.

en: Everything was sent flying and crashing.
uz: Hamma narsa uchib ketadi va parchalanib ketadi.

en: “But why break chairs, gentlemen?
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, nega o'rindiqlarni buzish kerak, xonimlar?

en: You know it’s a loss to the Crown,” Porfiry Petrovitch quoted gaily.
uz: Bu Korona uchun ziyon ekanligini bilasiz, - dedi Porfiry Petrovitch xursandchilik bilan.

en: Raskolnikov was still laughing, with his hand in Porfiry Petrovitch’s, but anxious not to overdo it, awaited the right moment to put a natural end to it.
uz: Raskolnikov hali ham o'z qo'li bilan Porfiry Petrovitchlarni ko'tarib kulg'irayotgan edi, lekin o'zini haddan ortiq o'tkazmaslikka intilib, bu ishni tabiiy ravishda tugatish uchun to'g'ri vaqtni kutgan.

en: Razumihin, completely put to confusion by upsetting the table and smashing the glass, gazed gloomily at the
uz: Razumihin, stolni buzgan va shishalarni buzgan holda butunlay g'alati bo'lgan holda, qorong'ilik bilan o'z ko'zlariga qaradi.

en: fragments, cursed and turned sharply to the window where he stood looking out with his back to the company with a fiercely scowling countenance, seeing nothing.
uz: U la'natlangan va keskin o'girilib, o'z orqasidan to'xtatib, hech narsa ko'rmay, qizg'in ko'rinish bilan kompaniyaga qarab turardi.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch laughed and was ready to go on laughing, but obviously looked for explanations.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch kuldi va kulishni davom ettirishga tayyor edi, ammo, albatta, tushuntirish izladi.

en: Zametov had been sitting in the corner, but he rose at the visitors’ entrance and was standing in expectation with a smile on his lips, though he looked with surprise and even it seemed incredulity at the whole scene and at Raskolnikov with a certain embarrassment.
uz: Zametov burchada o'tirgan edi, lekin u tashrif buyuruvchilarning kirish joyida turib, tabassum bilan kutib turgan edi, garchi u hayron va hatto butun voqeada va Raskolnikovga o'ziga yarasha noloyiqlik bilan ishonchsizlik ko'rinar edi.

en: Zametov’s unexpected presence struck Raskolnikov unpleasantly.
uz: Zametovning kutilmagan hozirligi Raskolnikovga yoqimsiz ta'sir ko'rsatdi.

en: “I’ve got to think of that,” he thought.
uz: Men bu haqda o'ylashim kerak, deb o'yladi u.

en: “Excuse me, please,” he began, affecting extreme embarrassment.
uz: Xullas, iltimos, u o'zini juda noqulay his etib boshladi.

en: “Raskolnikov.” “Not at all, very pleasant to see you … and how pleasantly you’ve come in.
uz: Raskolnikov.  Hech bo'lmaganda, sizni ko'rish juda yoqimli ... va qanchalik yoqimli tarzda kirganingizni ko'rdim.

en: … Why, won’t he even say good morning?” Porfiry Petrovitch nodded at Razumihin.
uz: Nima uchun, u hatto salom ham aytmaydi? Porfiry Petrovitch Razumihinga boshini tiydi.

en: “Upon my honour I don’t know why he is in such a rage with me.
uz: Mening hurmatim uchun, nima uchun u menga shunchalik g'azablanayotganini bilmayman.

en: I only told him as we came along that he was like Romeo … and proved it.
uz: O'shanda men unga u Romeoga o'xshaydi deb aytdim va buni isbotladim.

en: And that was all, I think!” “Pig!” ejaculated Razumihin, without turning round.
uz: O'ylaymanki, bu hammasi bo'ldi! Pig! Razumihinni aylanib chiqmasdan chiqardi.

en: “There must have been very grave grounds for it, if he is so furious at the word,” Porfiry laughed.
uz: Bu so'zga juda g'azablanayotgan bo'lsa, bu uchun juda jiddiy sabablar bo'lishi kerak edi, Porfiry kuldi.

en: “Oh, you sharp lawyer!
uz: Oh, sen o'ta oqli advokat!

en: … Damn you all!” snapped Razumihin, and suddenly bursting out laughing himself, he went up to Porfiry with a more cheerful face as though nothing had happened.
uz: Sizlarning barchangizga voy! Razumihin o'zidan-o'zidan ko'tarildi va to'satdan o'zini o'zi ko'tardi va hech narsa sodir bo'lmaganidek, ko'proq quvonchli yuz bilan Porfirga bordi.

en: To come to business.
uz: Biznesga kelish uchun.

en: This is my friend Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov; in the first place he has heard of you and wants to make your acquaintance, and secondly, he has a little matter of business with you.
uz: Bu mening do'stim Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov; birinchidan, u siz haqingizda eshitgan va siz bilan tanishishni xohlaydi, ikkinchidan, u siz bilan kichik biznes ishlari bilan shug'ullanadi.

en: Zametov, what brought you here?
uz: Zametov, sizni bu yerga nima keltirdi?

en: Have you met before?
uz: Sizlar ilgari uchrashganmisiz?

en: Have you known each other long?” “What does this mean?” thought Raskolnikov uneasily.
uz: Sizlar bir-biringizni uzoq vaqtdan beri bilasizmi?  Bu nimani anglatadi? Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: Zametov seemed taken aback, but not very much so.
uz: Zametov ajablanib ketdi, lekin o'ta ko'p emas edi.

en: “Why, it was at your rooms we met yesterday,” he said easily.
uz: - Kecha biz sizning xonangizda uchrashgan edik, - dedi u osonlikcha.

en: “Then I have been spared the trouble.
uz: Shunday qilib, men muammolardan xalos bo'ldim.

en: All last week he was begging me to introduce him to you.
uz: O'tgan hafta davomida u o'zini sizga tanishtirishimni iltijo qilib turardi.

en: Porfiry and you have sniffed each other out without me.
uz: Siz va Porfiry mensiz bir-biringizni ko'rdingiz.

en: Where is your tobacco?” Porfiry Petrovitch was wearing a dressing-gown, very clean linen, and trodden-down slippers.
uz: Sizning tamakilaringiz qayerda? Porfiry Petrovitch kiygan kiyim, juda toza kiyim va cho'tkalar ostida edi.

en: He was a man of about five and thirty, short, stout even to corpulence, and clean shaven.
uz: U taxminan besh va o'ttiz yoshli, qisqa, jasoratli va toza sochli kishi edi.

en: cut short and had a large round head, particularly prominent at the back.
uz: Qisqa bo'lib, katta yuzli boshli edi, ayniqsa orqa qismida ko'rinadi.

en: His soft, round, rather snub-nosed face was of a sickly yellowish colour, but had a vigorous and rather ironical expression.
uz: Uning yumshoq, yuziq, biroz o'tkir burun yuzi kasallik bilan sariq rangda edi, ammo kuchli va biroz ironik ifodasi bor edi.

en: It would have been good-natured except for a look in the eyes, which shone with a watery, mawkish light under almost white, blinking eyelashes.
uz: Ko'zlarning ko'zlarida ko'rinadigan, deyarli oq va ko'rinadigan ko'z burchaklari ostida suvli, ko'ngilchan nur bilan nurlangan ko'z ko'rinishidan tashqari, bu yaxshi xulq-atvorli bo'lardi.

en: The expression of those eyes was strangely out of keeping with his somewhat womanish figure, and gave it something far more serious than could be guessed at first sight.
uz: O'sha ko'zlarning ko'rinishi o'ziga xos tarzda uning biroz ayollik bilan bog'liq bo'lmagan va unga birinchi qarashda tasavvur qilinadiganidan ancha jiddiyroq narsani ato etgan.

en: As soon as Porfiry Petrovitch heard that his visitor had a little matter of business with him, he begged him to sit down on the sofa and sat down himself on the other end, waiting for him to explain his business, with that careful and over-serious attention which is at once oppressive and embarrassing, especially to a stranger, and especially if what you are discussing is in your opinion of far too little importance for such exceptional solemnity.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch mehmonining u bilan ishda bo'lganini eshitgan zahoti, uni kanepada o'tirishga undadi va o'zini boshqa tomonda o'tirishga undadi, uning o'z ishini tushuntirishini kutadi, bu esa bir vaqtning o'zida zo'ravon va noqulay bo'ladi, ayniqsa begona kishi uchun, ayniqsa, agar siz muhokama qilayotgan narsa sizning fikringizda bunday noyob tantana uchun juda kam ahamiyatga ega bo'lsa.

en: But in brief and coherent phrases Raskolnikov explained his business clearly and exactly, and was so well satisfied with himself that he even succeeded in taking a good look at Porfiry.
uz: Ammo qisqacha va qat'iy iboralarda Raskolnikov o'z biznesini aniq va aniq tushuntirdi va o'zidan shunchalik mamnun ediki, hatto Porfiryga diqqat bilan qarashga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch did not once take his eyes off him.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch bir marta ham unga ko'z tikmagan.

en: Razumihin, sitting opposite at the same table, listened warmly and impatiently, looking from one to the other every moment with rather excessive interest.
uz: Razumihin o'sha dasturxonning o'rtasida o'tirib, iliq va sabrsizlik bilan tinglab, har bir daqiqa bir-biridan ortiqcha qiziqish bilan qarab turardi.

en: “Fool,” Raskolnikov swore to himself.
uz: Raskolnikov o'ziga qasam ichdi.

en: “You have to give information to the police,” Porfiry replied, with a most businesslike air, “that having learnt of this incident, that is of the murder, you beg to inform the lawyer in charge of the case that such and such things belong to you, and that you desire to redeem them  … or … but they will write to you.” “That’s just the point, that at the present moment,” Raskolnikov tried his utmost to feign embarrassment, “I am not quite in funds … and even this trifling sum is beyond me … I only wanted, you see, for the present to declare that the things are mine, and that when I have money.
uz: Siz politsiyaga ma'lumot berishingiz kerak,  Porfiry eng ishbilarmonlik bilan javob berdi, ki, bu hodisa, ya'ni qotillik haqida bilib olganingizdan so'ng, siz bu va bu narsalar sizga tegishliligini va ularni sotib olishni xohlayotganingizni ishontirasiz va ... yoki ... lekin ular sizga xat yozadilar.Bu borada Raskolnikov o'zini noqulay deb topishga harakat qildi, Men pulga to'liq ega emasman ... va hatto bu kichkina miqdor ham mendan ustun ... Men hozircha bu narsalarni o'zimga tegishli deb e'lon qilishni xohladim va pulga ega bo'lganimda.

en: …” “That’s no matter,” answered Porfiry Petrovitch, receiving his explanation of his pecuniary position coldly, “but you can, if you prefer, write straight to me, to say, that having been informed of the matter, and claiming such and such as your property, you beg …”
uz: ...  Bu hech qanday ahamiyatga ega emas, Porfiry Petrovitch javob berdi, uning pul masalasining tushuntirilishini sovuqlik bilan qabul qildi,  lekin agar xohlasangiz, menga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yozishingiz mumkin, agar siz bu haqda xabardor bo'lganingizdan va mol-mulkingizni talab qilganingizdan so'ng iltimos qilasiz ...

en: “On an ordinary sheet of paper?” Raskolnikov interrupted eagerly, again interested in the financial side of the question.
uz: Raskolnikov savolning moliyaviy tomonini ko'rib, bu so'zlarni davom ettirgan.

en: “Oh, the most ordinary,” and suddenly Porfiry Petrovitch looked with obvious irony at him, screwing up his eyes and, as it were, winking at him.
uz: Oh, eng odatiy, va to'satdan Porfiry Petrovitch unga ochiq-oydin ironik ko'z bilan qaradi, ko'zlarini buzadi va, bir so'z bilan aytganda, unga yuz o'giradi.

en: But perhaps it was Raskolnikov’s fancy, for it all lasted but a moment.
uz: Ammo, ehtimol, bu Raskolnikovning xayrixohligi edi, chunki bularning barchasi bir daqiqa davom etdi.

en: There was certainly something of the sort, Raskolnikov could have sworn he winked at him, goodness knows why.
uz: Raskolnikov shubhasiz, unga yuz o'girganini qasam ichishi mumkin edi, Xudo biladi nega.

en: “He knows,” flashed through his mind like lightning.
uz: U biladi, o'z ongidan chaqmoq kabi o'tib ketdi.

en: “Forgive my troubling you about such trifles,” he went on, a little disconcerted, “the things are only worth five roubles, but I prize them particularly for the sake of those from whom they came to me, and I must confess that I was alarmed when I heard …” “That’s why you were so much struck when I mentioned to Zossimov that Porfiry was inquiring for everyone who had pledges!” Razumihin put in with obvious intention.
uz: Sizni bunday mayda-mayda narsalar bilan bezovta qilganimdan afsuslaning, u biroz xavotirlanib, davom etdi,bu narsalar atigi besh rublga arziydi, lekin men ularni ayniqsa menga kelganlar uchun qadrlayman va men eshitganimda xavotirlanganimni aytishim kerak ...Xullas, men Zossimovga Porfiry har bir kishi uchun savol berayotganini aytganimda, siz juda hayratda qoldingiz! Razumihin aniq niyat bilan ishga tushdi.

en: This was really unbearable.
uz: Bu aslida yengil emas edi.

en: Raskolnikov could not help glancing at him with a flash of vindictive anger in his black eyes, but immediately recollected himself.
uz: Raskolnikov uning qora ko'zidagi qasosli g'azabni ko'rib, o'ziga qarab turardi, lekin darhol o'zini esladi.

en: “You seem to be jeering at me, brother?” he said to him, with a well-feigned irritability.
uz: "Siz menga xijolat qilyapsiz, aka?" - dedi u unga, o'ziga xos xafalik bilan.

en: “I dare say I do seem to you absurdly anxious about such trash; but you mustn’t think me selfish or grasping for that, and these two things may be anything but trash in my eyes.
uz: Men aytishga jur'at qilamanki, men sizga bunday axloqsizlikka nisbatan absurd darajada tashvishlanaman; lekin siz meni xudbin yoki shu maqsadda qo'l urgan deb o'ylamasligingiz kerak, va bu ikki narsa ko'zimda axloqsizlikdan boshqa hech narsa bo'lmasligi mumkin.

en: I told you just now that the silver watch, though it’s not worth a cent, is the only thing left us of my father’s.
uz: Men sizga endi kumush soat, hatto bir sentga ham arzon bo'lmasa-da, otamning bizga qoldirgan yagona narsasi ekanligini aytdim.

en: You may laugh at me, but my mother is here,” he turned suddenly to Porfiry, “and if she knew,” he turned again hurriedly to Razumihin, carefully making his voice tremble, “that the watch was lost, she would be in despair!
uz: Sizlar menga kulishingiz mumkin, lekin onam shu yerda, u to'satdan Porfirga qarab ketdi, agar u bilsa, tezda Razumihinga qarab ketdi va o'z ovozini qo'rqitdi, chunki soat yo'qolgan edi, u umidsiz bo'lardi!

en: You know what women are!” “Not a bit of it!
uz: Ayollar nima ekanligini bilasiz!  Hech narsa emas!

en: I didn’t mean that at all!
uz: Men buni umuman nazarda tutmaganman!

en: Quite the contrary!” shouted Razumihin distressed.
uz: To'g'ri, to'g'ri! - deb qichqirdi Razumihin xafa bo'lib.

en: Did I overdo it?” Raskolnikov asked himself in a tremor.
uz: Men o'zimni haddan tashqari haddan tashqari ko'p ko'rdimmi? Raskolnikov o'z-o'zidan titrab so'radi.

en: “Why did I say that about women?” “Oh, your mother is with you?” Porfiry Petrovitch inquired.
uz: Nima uchun men ayollar haqida shunday aytdim?Oh, onangiz siz bilan birga? Porfiry Petrovitch so'radi.

en: “Yes.” “When did she come?” “Last night.”
uz: Ha.  U qachon keldi?  O'tgan kecha.

en: Porfiry paused as though reflecting.
uz: Porfiry o'ylab ko'rgandek to'xtadi.

en: “Your things would not in any case be lost,” he went on calmly and coldly.
uz: Sizning mol-mulkingiz hech qanday holatda yo'qolmaydi, u xotirjam va sovuq davom etdi.

en: “I have been expecting you here for some time.” And as though that was a matter of no importance, he carefully offered the ashtray to Razumihin, who was ruthlessly scattering cigarette ash over the carpet.
uz: Men sizni bir muncha vaqtdan beri bu yerda kutyapman. Va bu hech qanday ahamiyatga ega bo'lmagandek, u razumihinga kulolni ehtiyotkorlik bilan taklif qildi, u esa shafqatsizlik bilan karpet ustiga sigaret kulini tarqatayotgan edi.

en: Raskolnikov shuddered, but Porfiry did not seem to be looking at him, and was still concerned with Razumihin’s cigarette.
uz: Raskolnikov dahshatga tushdi, lekin Porfiry unga qaramasdi va hali ham Razumihinning sigareti bilan tashvishlanardi.

en: Why, did you know that he had pledges there?” cried Razumihin.
uz: Nima uchun, uning u yerda vasiyatnomalar borligini bilar edingizmi? - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch addressed himself to Raskolnikov.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch Raskolnikovga murojaat qildi.

en: “Your things, the ring and the watch, were wrapped up together, and on the paper your name was legibly written in pencil, together with the date on which you left them with her …” “How observant you are!” Raskolnikov smiled awkwardly, doing his very utmost to look him straight in the face, but he failed, and suddenly added: “I say that because I suppose there were a great many pledges … that it must be difficult to remember them all.
uz: Sizning narsalaringiz, do'stingiz va soatingiz bir-biri bilan to'plandi va qog'ozda sizning ismingiz qalam bilan yozilgan edi, shuningdek, ularni u bilan qoldirgan sanangiz ham ... Qanday diqqatli ekansiz! Raskolnikov o'ziga xos ko'rinish bilan tabassum qildi va unga to'g'ri qarab ko'rish uchun hamma narsani qildi, lekin u muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchradi va to'satdan qo'shimcha qildi: Men buni aytaman, chunki men ko'pgina va'dalar bor deb o'ylayman ... ularning barchasini eslash qiyin bo'lishi kerak.

en: … But you remember them all so clearly, and … and …” “Stupid!
uz: Ammo siz ularning barchasini juda aniq eslaysiz va ... va ... Stupid!

en: Feeble!” he thought.
uz: Bu juda zaif! - deb o'yladi u.

en: “Why did I add that?” “But we know all who had pledges, and you are the only one who hasn’t come forward,” Porfiry answered with hardly perceptible irony.
uz: Nima uchun men buni qo'shdim?  Ammo biz barcha va'da olganlarni bilamiz va siz faqatgina o'zingiz kelmagansiz, Porfiry kamdan-kam ko'rinadigan ironik javob berdi.

en: “I haven’t been quite well.” “I heard that too.
uz: Men yaxshi holatda emasman.Men ham buni eshitganman.

en: I heard, indeed, that you were in great distress about something.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, siz biron bir narsa tufayli juda qayg'urayotganingizni eshitdim.

en: You look pale still.” “I am not pale at all.
uz: Siz hali ham bo'lak ko'rinasiz.Men umuman bo'lak emasman.

en: … No, I am quite well,” Raskolnikov snapped out rudely and angrily, completely changing his tone.
uz: Yo'q, men yaxshiman, Raskolnikov qo'pol va g'azabga to'lib, o'z so'zini butunlay o'zgartirdi.

en: His anger was mounting, he could not repress it.
uz: Uning g'azabini ko'paytirib borardi, uni kamsitolmadi.

en: “And in my anger I shall betray myself,” flashed through his mind again.
uz: Qahr-g'azabda o'zimga xiyonat qilaman, - deb yana o'ylab ko'rdi u.

en: “Why are they torturing me?” “Not quite well!” Razumihin caught him up.
uz: Nima uchun ular meni qiynaydilar?  Yaxshi emas!  Razumihin uni ushlab qoldi.

en: He was unconscious and delirious all yesterday.
uz: U butun kecha befarq va deliriumli edi.

en: Would you believe, Porfiry, as soon as our backs were turned, he dressed, though he could hardly stand, and gave us the slip and went off on a spree somewhere till midnight, delirious all the time!
uz: Ishonasizmi, Porfiry, biz orqaga burilganimizdan so'ng, u o'zini kiygan, lekin o'rnida turolmagan, bizga qo'l urib, yarim kechagacha bir joyda to'sqinlik qilib yurgan!

en: Would you believe it!
uz: Ishonasizmi!

en: You don’t say so!” Porfiry shook his head in a womanish way.
uz: Siz buni aytmaysiz! Porfiry ayolcha tarzda boshini silkitdi.

en: Don’t you believe it!
uz: Siz bunga ishonmaysiz!

en: But you don’t believe it anyway,” Raskolnikov let slip in his anger.
uz: Ammo siz bunga ishonmaysiz, Raskolnikov g'azabga tushib ketishiga yo'l qo'ydi.

en: But Porfiry Petrovitch did not seem to catch those strange words.
uz: Ammo Porfiry Petrovitch o'sha g'alati so'zlarni tushunmay qolgan.

en: “But how could you have gone out if you hadn’t been delirious?” Razumihin got hot suddenly.
uz: Agar delirium bo'lmaganida qanday qilib chiqib ketardingiz? Razumihin to'satdan issiq bo'ldi.

en: “What did you go out for?
uz: Siz nima uchun tashqariga chiqdingiz?

en: What was the object of it?
uz: Buning maqsadi nima edi?

en: Were you in your senses when you did it?
uz: Buni amalga oshirganingizda aql-idrokingiz bormidi?

en: Now that all danger is over I can speak plainly.” “I was awfully sick of them yesterday.” Raskolnikov addressed Porfiry suddenly with a smile of insolent defiance, “I ran away from them to take lodgings where they wouldn’t find me, and took a lot of money with me.
uz: Endi barcha xavf-xatarlar o'tib ketganidan keyin, men aniq gapira olaman.Men ularni kecha juda yomon ko'rdim. Raskolnikov birdan Porfiryga g'azablangan qarshilik ko'rsatgan tabassum bilan murojaat qildi,Men ulardan qochib ketdim va ular meni topmaydigan joylarga joylashtirdim va ko'p pulni o'zim bilan olib ketdim.

en: Zametov there saw it.
uz: Zametov uni ko'rdi.

en: Zametov, was I sensible or delirious yesterday; settle our dispute.” He could have strangled Zametov at that moment, so hateful were his expression and his silence to him.
uz: Zametov, kecha men aqldan ozganmanmi yoki aqldan ozganmanmi; bahsimizni hal qiling. Zametovni o'sha paytda o'ldirishi mumkin edi, chunki uning ifodasi va sessizligi unga juda nafratli edi.

en: “In my opinion you talked sensibly and even artfully, but you were extremely irritable,” Zametov pronounced dryly.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, siz aqlli va hatto mahoratli gapirgansiz, lekin juda g'azablanasiz, Zametov quruq so'zlab berdi.

en: “And Nikodim Fomitch was telling me today,” put in Porfiry Petrovitch, “that he met you very late last night in the lodging of a man who had been run over.” “And there,” said Razumihin, “weren’t you mad then?
uz: Nikodim Fomitch bugun Porfiry Petrovitchda o'tirganida, o'sha kuni kechqurun sizni haydab o'tgan odamning uyida uchratganini aytib berayotgan edi.

en: You gave your last penny to the widow for the funeral.
uz: Siz oxirgi pulingizni beva ayolga o'z dafn marosimi uchun bergansiz.

en: If you wanted to help, give fifteen or twenty even, but keep three roubles for yourself at least, but he flung away all the twenty-five at once!” “Maybe I found a treasure somewhere and you know nothing of it?
uz: Agar siz yordam bermoqchi bo'lsangiz, o'n besh yoki yigirma kishini qo'shing, lekin hech bo'lmaganda o'zingiz uchun uch rubl qoldiring, lekin u o'n beshni bir vaqtning o'zida tashlab yubordi! Ehtimol, men qaysidir joyda xazina topdim va siz bu haqda hech narsa bilmaysiz?

en: So that’s why I was liberal yesterday.
uz: Demak, aynan shu sababli men kecha liberal bo'lgan edim.

en: Zametov knows I’ve found a treasure!
uz: Zametov bilishicha, men xazina topdim!

en: Excuse us, please, for disturbing you for half an hour with such trivialities,” he said, turning to Porfiry Petrovitch, with trembling lips.
uz: Sizni yarim soat davomida bunday ahamiyatsiz narsalar bilan bezovta qilganimiz uchun uzr so'raylik, - dedi u, Porfiry Petrovitchga yuz o'girib, dudaklari titraydi.

en: “We are boring you, aren’t we?” “Oh no, quite the contrary, quite the contrary!
uz: Biz sizni bezovta qilyapmiz, shunday emasmi?Oh, yo'q, aksincha, aksincha!

en: If only you knew how you interest me!
uz: Agar siz meni qanchalik qiziqtirganingizni bilsangiz edi!

en: It’s interesting to look on and listen … and I am really glad you have come forward at last.” “But you might give us some tea!
uz: Qarang va tinglang, bu qiziqarli bo'ladi... va nihoyat o'zingizni namoyish etganingizdan juda xursandman. Ammo bizga biroz choy berishingiz mumkin!

en: My throat’s dry,” cried Razumihin.
uz: Qo'lim quruq qoldi, - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: Perhaps we will all keep you company.
uz: Ehtimol, hammamiz siz bilan birga bo'lamiz.

en: Wouldn’t you like … something more essential before tea?” “Get along with you!”
uz: Choydan oldin siz ... muhimroq narsani xohlamaydingizmi?  O'zingiz bilan yaxshi munosabatda bo'ling!

en: Porfiry Petrovitch went out to order tea.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch choy buyurtma qilish uchun tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Raskolnikov’s thoughts were in a whirl.
uz: Raskolnikovning fikrlari g'alati holatda edi.

en: He was in terrible exasperation.
uz: U dahshatli g'azabda edi.

en: “The worst of it is they don’t disguise it; they don’t care to stand on ceremony!
uz: Eng yomon joyi shundaki, ular buni yashirmaydilar; ular marosimda turishni xohlamaydilar!

en: And how if you didn’t know me at all, did you come to talk to Nikodim Fomitch about me?
uz: Va agar siz meni hech qachon tanimagan bo'lsangiz, qanday qilib Nikodim Fomitch bilan men to'g'risida gaplashishga keldingiz?

en: So they don’t care to hide that they are tracking me like a pack of dogs.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular meni itlar to'plami kabi kuzatib borayotganini yashirishni xohlamaydilar.

en: They simply spit in my face.” He was shaking with rage.
uz: Ular shunchaki yuzimga tishladilar. U g'azabdan titragan edi.

en: “Come, strike me openly, don’t play with me like a cat with a mouse.
uz: Kosh, menga ochiq ur, mushuk bilan mushuk kabi men bilan o'ynamayin.

en: It’s hardly civil, Porfiry Petrovitch, but perhaps I won’t allow it!
uz: Bu aslida madaniy emas, Porfiry Petrovitch, lekin ehtimol men bunga yo'l qo'ymayman!

en: I shall get up and throw the whole truth in your ugly faces, and you’ll see how I despise you.” He could hardly breathe.
uz: Men turib, butun haqiqatni sizlarning o'tkir yuzingizga tashlayman va siz mening sizni qanchalik kamsitganimni ko'rasiz. U nafas olishni qiyinlashtirgan.

en: “And what if it’s only my fancy?
uz: Va agar bu faqat mening zavq-e'tiborim bo'lsa-chi?

en: What if I am mistaken, and through inexperience I get angry and don’t keep up my nasty part?
uz: Agar men xato qilsam va tajribam yo'qligi tufayli g'azablansam va o'z yomon rolimni bajarmasam nima bo'ladi?

en: Perhaps it’s all unintentional.
uz: Ehtimol, bularning barchasi qasddan bo'lmagan.

en: All their phrases are the usual ones, but there is something about them.
uz: Ularning barcha iboralari odatdagidek bo'ladi, ammo ular haqida bir narsa bor.

en: … It all might be said, but there is something.
uz: ... Bularning barchasi aytilishi mumkin, lekin bir narsa bor.

en: Why did he say bluntly, ‘With her’?
uz: Nima uchun u ochiqchasiga: "U bilan" deb aytdi?

en: Why did Zametov add that I spoke artfully?
uz: Nima uchun Zametov men savodkorlik bilan gapirganimni qo'shdi?

en: Why do they speak in that tone?
uz: Nima uchun ular shunday tovush bilan gapirishadi?

en: … Razumihin is sitting here, why does he see nothing?
uz: Razumihin bu yerda o'tirgan, nega u hech narsa ko'rmaydi?

en: That innocent blockhead never does see anything!
uz: O'sha begunoh burchak hech qachon hech narsa ko'rmaydi!

en: Did Porfiry wink at me just now?
uz: Porfiry menga ko'z ochdimi?

en: Of course it’s nonsense!
uz: Albatta, bu behudalikdir!

en: What could he wink for?
uz: Nima uchun u ko'z yumishi mumkin?

en: Are they trying to upset my nerves or are they teasing me?
uz: Ular mening g'azabimni o'tkazishga harakat qilyaptimi yoki meni haqorat qilyaptimi?

en: Either it’s ill fancy or they know!
uz: Yoki bu yomon fantaziya, yoki ular biladi!

en: Even Zametov is rude.
uz: Hatto Zametov ham qo'pol.

en: Zametov has changed his mind.
uz: Zametov fikrini o'zgartirgan.

en: I foresaw he would change his mind!
uz: Men uning fikrini o'zgartirishini oldindan bilardim!

en: He is at home here, while it’s my first visit.
uz: Bu mening birinchi tashrifim bo'lsa-da, u bu yerda o'z uyida.

en: Porfiry does not consider him a visitor; sits with his back to him.
uz: Porfir uni mehmon deb hisoblamaydi; unga orqaga qarab o'tiradi.

en: They’re as thick as thieves, no doubt, over me!
uz: Ular, shubhasiz, men uchun o'g'ri kabi qalin!

en: Not a doubt they were talking about me before we came.
uz: Shubhasiz, biz kelishdan oldin ular men haqimda gapirishgan.

en: Do they know about the flat?
uz: Ular xonadondan xabardormi?

en: If only they’d make haste!
uz: Agar ular shoshilsalar edi!

en: When I said that I ran away to take a flat he let it pass.
uz: Men uyni olib ketish uchun qochib ketishimni aytganimda, u o'tib ketishiga yo'l qo'ydi.

en: … I put that in cleverly about a flat, it may be of use afterwards.
uz: ...Men buni xonadon haqida aqlli so'zladim, keyinchalik foydali bo'lishi mumkin.

en: … Delirious, indeed … ha-ha-ha!
uz: ... Haqiqatan ham delirioz ... ha-ha-ha!

en: He knows all about last night!
uz: U o'tgan kecha haqida hamma narsani biladi!

en: He didn’t know of my mother’s arrival!
uz: U onamning kelishini bilmagan!

en: The hag had written the date on in pencil!
uz: Qaroqchi kunni qalam bilan yozgan edi!

en: You are wrong, you won’t catch me!
uz: Siz noto'g'ri yo'l tutasiz, meni tutolmaysiz!

en: There are no facts … it’s all supposition!
uz: Hech qanday faktlar yo'q ... bularning barchasi taxminlardir!

en: The flat even isn’t a fact but delirium.
uz: Flat ham fakt emas, balki delirium.

en: I know what to say to them.
uz: Men ularga nima aytishni bilaman.

en: … Do they know about the flat?
uz: Ular xonadon haqida biladimi?

en: I won’t go without finding out.
uz: Men buni bilmasdan ketmayman.

en: What did I come for?
uz: Men nima uchun keldim?

en: But my being angry now, maybe is a fact!
uz: Ammo hozir g'azablanishim, ehtimol, haqiqatdir!

en: Fool, how irritable I am!
uz: Ahmoq, men qanchalik g'azablanaman!

en: Perhaps that’s right; to play
uz: Ehtimol, bu to'g'ri; o'ynash uchun.

en: He will try to catch me.
uz: U meni ushlab turishga harakat qiladi.

en: Why did I come?” All this flashed like lightning through his mind.
uz: Nima uchun keldim? Bularning barchasi uning ongini chaqmoq kabi o'rab oldi.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch returned quickly.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch tez qaytdi.

en: He became suddenly more jovial.
uz: Birdan u ko'proq jonli bo'ldi.

en: “Your party yesterday, brother, has left my head rather.
uz: Kecha o'tkazgan partiyangiz, birodarim, boshimni ko'tardi.

en: … And I am out of sorts altogether,” he began in quite a different tone, laughing to Razumihin.
uz: Men esa umuman o'zimni chalg'itdim, u butunlay boshqacha tomda boshladi va Razumihinga kulishdi.

en: “Was it interesting?
uz: Bu qiziqarli bo'lganmi?

en: I left you yesterday at the most interesting point.
uz: Kecha men sizni eng qiziqarli joyda qoldirdim.

en: Who got the best of it?” “Oh, no one, of course.
uz: Kimdan eng yaxshi foydalandi?Oh, hech kim, albatta.

en: They got on to everlasting questions, floated off into space.” “Only fancy, Rodya, what we got on to yesterday.
uz: Ular abadiy savollarga duch kelishdi, kosmga uchib ketishdi.Rodya, biz kecha nimaga erishganimizni faqat o'ylayman.

en: Whether there is such a thing as crime.
uz: Qiziq, jinoyatchilik mavjudmi?

en: I told you that we talked our heads off.” “What is there strange?
uz: Men sizga biz o'zimiz bilan gaplashdik, deb aytdim. Nima g'alati?

en: It’s an everyday social question,” Raskolnikov answered casually.
uz: Bu kundalik ijtimoiy savol, Raskolnikov bevosita javob berdi.

en: “The question wasn’t put quite like that,” observed Porfiry.
uz: Sovuliyat o'sha tarzda qo'yilmagan, deb ta'kidlagan Porfiry.

en: “Not quite, that’s true,” Razumihin agreed at once, getting warm and hurried as usual.
uz: To'g'ri emas, lekin Razumihin darhol rozi bo'ldi va odatdagidek issiq va shoshilinch bo'ldi.

en: “Listen, Rodion, and tell us your opinion, I want to hear it.
uz: Quloq sol, Rodion, o'z fikringni aytib ber, men uni eshitishni xohlayman.

en: I was fighting tooth and nail with them and wanted you to help me.
uz: Men ular bilan to'qnashuvda edim va menga yordam berishni xohlardim.

en: I told them you were coming.
uz: Men ularga kelayotganingizni aytdim.

en: … It began with the socialist doctrine.
uz: ... Bu sotsialist doktrinasidan boshlandi.

en: You know their doctrine; crime is a protest against the abnormality of the social organisation and nothing more, and nothing more; no other causes admitted!
uz: Siz ularning ta'limotlarini bilasiz; jinoyatchilik - bu ijtimoiy tashkilotning anormalligiga qarshi ko'rsatilgan norozilik va boshqa hech narsa emas; boshqa sabablar yo'q!

en: …” “You are wrong there,” cried Porfiry Petrovitch; he was noticeably animated and kept laughing as he looked at Razumihin, which made him more excited than ever.
uz: ... Siz noto'g'ri yo'ldan ozdirasiz,  Porfiry Petrovitch xitob qildi; u sezilarli darajada hayajonli edi va Razumihinni ko'rib kulishardi, bu uni har qachongidan ham hayajonlantirardi.

en: “Nothing is admitted,” Razumihin interrupted with heat.
uz: Hech narsa qabul qilinmaydi,  Razumihin issiqlik bilan kesilgan.

en: I’ll show you their pamphlets.
uz: Sizga ularning buklamalarini ko'rsataman.

en: Everything with them is ‘the influence of environment,’ and nothing else.
uz: Ular bilan bo'lgan hamma narsa - atrof-muhit ta'siri va boshqa hech narsa emas.

en: Their favourite phrase!
uz: Ularning sevimli so'zlari!

en: From which it follows that, if society is normally organised, all crime will cease at once, since there will be nothing to protest against and all men will become righteous in one instant.
uz: Demak, agar jamiyat odatdagidek tashkil etilgan bo'lsa, barcha jinoyatchilik birdan to'xtadi, chunki protest qilish uchun hech narsa yo'q va barcha odamlar bir daqiqada solih bo'ladi.

en: Human nature is not taken into account, it is excluded, it’s not supposed to exist!
uz: Inson tabiati e'tiborga olinmaydi, chetlatilmoqda, mavjud bo'lmasligi kerak!

en: They don’t recognise that humanity, developing by a historical living process, will become at last a normal society, but they believe that a social system that has come out of some
uz: Ular insoniyat tarixiy hayot jarayoni orqali rivojlanib borayotganini tan olmaydilar va oxir-oqibat normal jamiyatga aylanadilar, ammo ular ijtimoiy tizimning ba'zi bir jarayonlardan kelib chiqqanligiga ishonishadi.

en: mathematical brain is going to organise all humanity at once and make it just and sinless in an instant, quicker than any living process!
uz: Matematika miyasi butun insoniyatni bir vaqtning o'zida tashkil etadi va uni bir lahzada adolatli va gunohsiz qiladi, bu esa har qanday tirik jarayondan tezroq bo'ladi!

en: That’s why they instinctively dislike history, ‘nothing but ugliness and stupidity in it,’ and they explain it all as stupidity!
uz: Shuning uchun ular instinkt bilan tarixdan nafratlanishadi, unda faqat o'tkirlik va ahmoqlik bor va bularning barchasini ahmoqlik deb tushuntirishadi!

en: That’s why they so dislike the living process of life; they don’t want a living soul!
uz: Shuning uchun ular hayotning tirik jarayonidan nafratlanishadi; ular tirik ruhni xohlamaydilar!

en: The living soul demands life, the soul won’t obey the rules of mechanics, the soul is an object of suspicion, the soul is retrograde!
uz: Hayotdagi jon hayotni talab qiladi, jon mexanika qoidalariga rioya qilmaydi, jon shubha ostiga qo'yilgan, jon orqaga qaytgan!

en: But what they want though it smells of death and can be made of India-rubber, at least is not alive, has no will, is servile and won’t revolt!
uz: Ammo ular o'limga xos bo'lsa-da va Hindiston g'ildirakidan tayyorlanishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, hech bo'lmaganda u tirik emas, xohish-irodasi yo'q, qul bo'lib, isyon ko'tarmaydi!

en: And it comes in the end to their reducing everything to the building of walls and the planning of rooms and passages in a phalanstery!
uz: Va oxir-oqibat, ular hamma narsani devorlar qurishga va xonalar va o'tish joylarini falansteryada rejalashtirishga kamaytirishadi!

en: The phalanstery is ready, indeed, but your human nature is not ready for the phalanstery —it wants life, it hasn’t completed its vital process, it’s too soon for the graveyard!
uz: Haqiqatan ham, falansteriya tayyor, ammo inson tabiatingiz falansteriya uchun tayyor emas, u hayotni xohlaydi, o'z hayotiy jarayonini tugatib bo'lmadi, qabriston uchun juda erta!

en: You can’t skip over nature by logic.
uz: Mantiq bilan tabiatdan o'tish mumkin emas.

en: Logic presupposes three possibilities, but there are millions!
uz: Mantiq uchta imkoniyatni nazarda tutadi, ammo bu millionlab imkoniyatlar bor!

en: Cut away a million, and reduce it all to the question of comfort!
uz: Bir millionni kesib tashlang va barchasini qulaylik masalasiga aylantiring!

en: That’s the easiest solution of the problem!
uz: Bu muammoning eng oson yechimidir!

en: It’s seductively clear and you musn’t think about it.
uz: Bu jozibador darajada aniq va siz bu haqda o'ylashingiz shart emas.

en: That’s the great thing, you mustn’t think!
uz: Bu eng zo'r narsa, siz o'ylamasligingiz kerak!

en: The whole secret of life in two pages of print!” “Now he is off, beating the drum!
uz: Hayotning butun siri ikki sahifa bosib chiqarilgan! Endi u qo'ng'iroq qilib, to'ng'ichni urmoqda!

en: Catch hold of him, do!” laughed Porfiry.
uz: Uni qo'lga oling, qil! Porfiry kuldi.

en: “Can you imagine,” he turned to Raskolnikov, “six people holding forth like that last night, in one room, with punch as a preliminary!
uz: O'ylab ko'ring-a, u Raskolnikovga qarab, o'tgan kecha bir xonada shunday o'tirgan oltita odamni o'qidi.

en: No, brother, you are wrong, environment accounts for a great deal in crime; I can assure you of that.” “Oh, I know it does, but just tell me: a man of forty violates a child of ten; was it environment drove him to it?” “Well, strictly speaking, it did,” Porfiry observed with noteworthy gravity; “a crime of that nature may be very well ascribed to the influence of environment.” Razumihin was almost in a frenzy.
uz: Yo'q, aka, siz noto'g'ri gapiryapsiz, atrof-muhit jinoyatchilikning katta qismini o'z ichiga oladi; men sizga shuni ta'kidlay olaman.Oh, bilaman, lekin ayting: qirq yoshli kishi o'n yoshli bolani zo'ravonlik qiladi; atrof-muhit uni bunga majbur qilganmi? Xo'sh, to'g'ri aytganda, shunday bo'lganmi? Porfiry diqqatga sazovor darajada kuzatilgan;bu tabiatdagi jinoyat atrof-muhit ta'siriga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin. Razumihin deyarli g'ayratga tushdi.

en: “Oh, if you like,” he roared.
uz: Oh, agar xohlasangiz,  u qichqirdi.

en: “I’ll prove to you that your white eyelashes may very well be ascribed to the Church of Ivan the Great’s being two hundred and fifty feet high, and I will prove it clearly, exactly, progressively, and even with a Liberal tendency!
uz: Sizga sizning oq ko'z burchaklaringiz katta Ivonning cherkovining ikki yuz ellik fut balandligiga bog'liq ekanligini isbotlayman va buni aniq, aniq, bosqichma-bosqich va hatto liberal tendentsiya bilan isbotlayman!

en: Will you bet on it?” “Done!
uz: Siz bunga pul tikasizmi? Done!

en: Let’s hear, please, how he will prove it!” “He is always humbugging, confound him,” cried Razumihin, jumping up and gesticulating.
uz: Keling, u buni qanday isbotlashi haqida eshitamiz! U har doim qichqirib, uni chalg'itadi, - deb baqirdi Razumihin, ko'tarilib, qo'l urib.

en: “What’s the use of talking to you?
uz: Siz bilan gaplashishning qanday foydasi bor?

en: does all that on purpose; you don’t know him, Rodion!
uz: Bularning barchasini bila turib qiladi; siz uni bilmaysiz, Rodion!

en: He took their side yesterday, simply to make fools of them.
uz: Kecha u ularning tarafini oldi, shunchaki ularni axmoq qilish uchun.

en: And the things he said yesterday!
uz: Va u kecha aytgan narsalar!

en: And they were delighted!
uz: Ular juda xursand bo'lishdi!

en: He can keep it up for a fortnight together.
uz: U o'n ikki hafta birga bo'lib qolishi mumkin.

en: Last year he persuaded us that he was going into a monastery: he stuck to it for two months.
uz: O'tgan yili u bizni o'zi monastirga borayotganini aytishga ishontirdi: u ikki oy davomida unga sodiq qoldi.

en: Not long ago he took it into his head to declare he was going to get married, that he had everything ready for the wedding.
uz: Ko'p yillar oldin u turmushga chiqishini, to'y uchun hamma narsasi tayyor ekanini aytishga qaror qildi.

en: He ordered new clothes indeed.
uz: Haqiqatan ham u yangi kiyimlarni buyurtma qildi.

en: We all began to congratulate him.
uz: Hammamiz uni tabriklashni boshladik.

en: There was no bride, nothing, all pure fantasy!” “Ah, you are wrong!
uz: To'y bo'lmagan, hech narsa bo'lmagan, faqatgina chiroyli xayol bor edi!A, siz xato qilyapsiz!

en: I got the clothes before.
uz: Kiyim-kechaklar men ilgari ham olganman.

en: It was the new clothes in fact that made me think of taking you in.” “Are you such a good dissembler?” Raskolnikov asked carelessly.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, yangi kiyimlar meni sizni qabul qilish haqida o'ylashga undagan. Siz shunday yaxshi dissemblermisiz? Raskolnikov beparvolik bilan so'radi.

en: “You wouldn’t have supposed it, eh?
uz: Siz buni tasavvur qilmas edingiz, shundaymi?

en: Wait a bit, I shall take you in, too.
uz: Bir oz vaqt turing, men ham sizni qabul qilaman.

en: No, I’ll tell you the truth.
uz: Yo'q, men sizga haqiqatni aytaman.

en: All these questions about crime, environment, children, recall to my mind an article of yours which interested me at the time.
uz: Jinoyatchilik, atrof-muhit, bolalar to'g'risidagi barcha savollar o'zimni o'sha paytda qiziqtirgan maqolangizni eslatadi.

en: ‘On Crime’ … or something of the sort, I forget the title, I read it with pleasure two months ago in the Periodical Review.” “My article?
uz: Crime haqida ... yoki shunga o'xshash narsa, men mavzuni unutib qo'ydim, uni ikki oy oldin Periodical Review da o'qib o'tganimdan xursandman. Mening maqolamni?

en: In the Periodical Review?” Raskolnikov asked in astonishment.
uz: Periodical Review-da? Raskolnikov hayronlik bilan so'radi.
