en: “I certainly did write an article upon a book six months ago when I left the university, but I sent it to the Weekly Review.” “But it came out in the Periodical.” “And the Weekly Review ceased to exist, so that’s why it wasn’t printed at the time.” “That’s true; but when it ceased to exist, the Weekly Review was amalgamated with the Periodical, and so your article appeared two months ago in the latter.
uz: Men, albatta, olti oy oldin universitetni tark etganimda, kitob haqida maqola yozgan edim, lekin uni "Havoriy sharh"ga yubordim.  Ammo u "Havoriy sharh"da paydo bo'ldi.  Va "Havoriy sharh" mavjud bo'lmay qoldi, shuning uchun u o'sha paytda nashr etilmagan.  Bu to'g'ri; lekin u mavjud bo'lmay qolganda, "Havoriy sharh" "Havoriy sharh" bilan "Havoriy sharh" birlashtirildi va shuning uchun sizning maqolangiz ikki oy oldin "Havoriy sharh"da paydo bo'ldi.

en: Didn’t you know?” Raskolnikov had not known.
uz: Bilmadingizmi? Raskolnikov buni bilmagan edi.

en: “Why, you might get some money out of them for the article!
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, maqola uchun ulardan pul olishingiz mumkin!

en: What a strange person you are!
uz: Siz qanday g'alati odamsiz!

en: You lead such a solitary life that you know nothing of matters that concern you directly.
uz: Siz shunchalik yolg'iz hayot kechirasizki, sizni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qiziqtiradigan masalalardan hech narsa bilmaysiz.

en: It’s a fact, I assure you.” “Bravo, Rodya!
uz: Bu haqiqat, sizga ishontiraman.Bravo, Rodya!

en: I knew nothing about it either!” cried Razumihin.
uz: Men ham bu haqda hech narsa bilmasdim! - deb baqirdi Razumihin.

en: “I’ll run today to the reading-room and ask for the number.
uz: Bugun o'qishxonasiga chopib, raqamni so'rayman.

en: It doesn’t matter though, I will find it.
uz: Biroq, bu muhim emas, men uni topaman.

en: Think of not telling us!” “How did you find out that the article was mine?
uz: Bizga aytmaslik haqida o'ylab ko'ring! Qanday qilib maqola mening ekanligimni bilib oldingiz?

en: It’s only signed with an initial.”
uz: Bu faqat dastlabki imzo bilan imzolangan.

en: “I only learnt it by chance, the other day.
uz: Men buni bir kun oldin tasodifan o'rganganman.

en: Through the editor; I know him.
uz: Muharriri orqali; men uni bilaman.

en: … I was very much interested.” “I analysed, if I remember, the psychology of a criminal before and after the crime.” “Yes, and you maintained that the perpetration of a crime is always accompanied by illness.
uz: ... Men juda qiziqdim. Men, agar eslayman, jinoyatchilarning jinoyatdan oldin va keyin psixologiyasini tahlil qildim.  Ha, siz jinoyat sodir etish har doim kasallik bilan birga bo'lishini ta'kidladingiz.

en: Very, very original, but … it was not that part of your article that interested me so much, but an idea at the end of the article which I regret to say you merely suggested without working it out clearly.
uz: Juda, juda original, lekin ... meni maqolangizning o'sha qismi emas, balki maqolaning oxiridagi g'oya qiziqtirgan, lekin siz buni aniq o'ylab ko'rmasdan taklif qilganingizni aytish uchun afsuslanaman.

en: There is, if you recollect, a suggestion that there are certain persons who can … that is, not precisely are able to, but have a perfect right to commit breaches of morality and crimes, and that the law is not for them.” Raskolnikov smiled at the exaggerated and intentional distortion of his idea.
uz: Agar esingizda bo'lsa, shunday fikr borki, muayyan shaxslar bo'lishi mumkin ... ya'ni, ular aniq emas, balki axloqiy qonun buzilishlarini va jinoyatlarni sodir etish huquqiga egalar va qonun ular uchun emas. Raskolnikov o'z fikrini haddan tashqari va qasddan buzganida tabassum qildi.

en: But not because of the influence of environment?” Razumihin inquired with some alarm even.
uz: Ammo atrof-muhit ta'siri tufayli emasmi? Razumihin hatto ba'zi xavotir bilan so'radi.

en: “No, not exactly because of it,” answered Porfiry.
uz: "Yo'q, aynan shu sababli emas", - deb javob berdi Porfiry.

en: “In his article all men are divided into ‘ordinary’ and ‘extraordinary.’ Ordinary men have to live in submission, have no right to transgress the law, because, don’t you see, they are ordinary.
uz: O'zining maqolaida barcha odamlar ordinary va extraordinary deb bo'linadi. Oddiy odamlar itoatkorlik bilan yashashlari kerak, ular qonunni buzish huquqiga ega emaslar, chunki ular oddiy odamlar.

en: But extraordinary men have a right to commit any crime and to transgress the law in any way, just because they are extraordinary.
uz: Ammo noyob insonlar noyob bo'lgani uchun har qanday jinoyatni sodir etish va har qanday tarzda qonunni buzish huquqiga ega.

en: That was your idea, if I am not mistaken?” “What do you mean?
uz: Bu sizning g'oyangiz edi, agar men xato qilmasam?  Nima demoqchisiz?

en: That can’t be right?” Razumihin muttered in bewilderment.
uz: Bu to'g'ri bo'lmasligi mumkinmi? Razumihin g'ayratda gapirdi.

en: Raskolnikov smiled again.
uz: Raskolnikov yana tabassum qildi.

en: He saw the point at once, and knew where they wanted to drive him.
uz: U darhol gapni ko'rdi va uni qayerga olib ketmoqchi ekanini bilardi.

en: He decided to take up the challenge.
uz: U o'z vazifasini bajarishga qaror qildi.

en: “That wasn’t quite my contention,” he began simply and modestly.
uz: Bu mening bahsim emas edi, u sodda va kamtarinlik bilan boshladi.

en: “Yet I admit that you have stated it almost correctly; perhaps, if you like, perfectly so.” (It almost gave him pleasure to admit this.) “The only difference is that I don’t contend that extraordinary people are always bound to commit breaches of morals, as you call it.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa-da, men buni deyarli to'g'ri aytganingizni tan oldim; ehtimol, agar xohlasangiz, to'g'ri aytasiz. (Bu uni tan olishdan deyarli zavqlantirgan edi.) Agargina farq shundaki, men noyob odamlar siz aytganidek, har doim axloqiy qoidalarni buzishga majbur bo'lishlarini aytmayman.

en: In fact, I doubt whether such an argument could be published.
uz: Aslida, bunday dalil chop etilishi mumkinligiga shubha qilaman.

en: I simply hinted that an ‘extraordinary’ man has the right … that is not an official right, but an inner right to decide in his own conscience to overstep …
uz: Men shunchaki o'zgacha odamning rasmiy huquq emas, balki vijdonida o'z huquqidan o'tishga qaror qilish huquqi borligini ko'rsatdim.

en: certain obstacles, and only in case it is essential for the practical fulfilment of his idea (sometimes, perhaps, of benefit to the whole of humanity).
uz: Ba'zi to'siqlar mavjud va faqat uning g'oyasi (ba'zan, ehtimol, butun insoniyat uchun foyda keltiradigan) amalda amalga oshirilishi uchun zarur bo'lgan taqdirda.

en: You say that my article isn’t definite; I am ready to make it as clear as I can.
uz: Siz mening maqolamni aniq deb aytmaysiz; men buni imkon qadar aniq aytishga tayyorman.

en: Perhaps I am right in thinking you want me to; very well.
uz: Ehtimol, siz xohlayotganingizni o'ylashda to'g'ri bo'laman; juda yaxshi.

en: I maintain that if the discoveries of Kepler and Newton could not have been made known except by sacrificing the lives of one, a dozen, a hundred, or more men, Newton would have had the right, would indeed have been in duty-bound … to eliminate the dozen or the hundred men for the sake of making his discoveries known to the whole of humanity.
uz: Agar Kepler va Nyutonning kashfiyotlari faqat bitta, o'nlab, yuz yoki undan ortiq odamlarning hayotiga qurbonlik keltirish orqali e'lon qilinishi mumkin bo'lganida, Nyuton o'nlab yoki yuz kishini o'z kashfiyotlarini butun insoniyatga e'lon qilish uchun yo'q qilish huquqiga ega bo'lgan bo'lar edi, deb aytaman.

en: But it does not follow from that that Newton had a right to murder people right and left and to steal every day in the market.
uz: Ammo bu Newtonning har kuni bozorda odamlarni o'ldirish va o'g'irlash huquqiga ega bo'lganini anglatmaydi.

en: Then, I remember, I maintain in my article that all … well, legislators and leaders of men, such as Lycurgus, Solon, Mahomet, Napoleon, and so on, were all without exception criminals, from the very fact that, making a new law, they transgressed the ancient one, handed down from their ancestors and held sacred by the people, and they did not stop short at bloodshed either, if that bloodshed — often of innocent persons fighting bravely in defence of ancient law — were of use to their cause.
uz: Keyin eslaymanki, men maqolaimda barcha... Lycurgus, Solon, Mahomet, Napoleon va boshqalar kabi qonun chiqaruvchilar va insoniy rahbarlarning hammasi, hech bir istisno qilmasdan, jinoyatchilar bo'lganini aytaman, chunki ular yangi qonunni qabul qilish orqali qadimgi qonunni buzishgan, bu qonunni ota-bobolaridan meros qilib olgan va xalq tomonidan muqaddas deb hisoblangan edilar va ular qon to'kishlarda ham to'xtamas edilar, agar qadimgi qonunni himoya qilishda jasorat bilan kurashayotgan aybsiz odamlarning qon to'kishlari ko'pincha o'z ishlarida foydali bo'lgan bo'lsa.

en: It’s remarkable, in fact, that the majority, indeed, of these benefactors and leaders of humanity were guilty of terrible carnage.
uz: Darhaqiqat, bu mehribonlar va insoniyat rahbarlarining aksariyati dahshatli qirg'inchilikda aybdor bo'lganligi diqqatga sazovor.

en: In short, I maintain that all great men or even men a little out of the common, that is to say capable of giving some new word, must from their very nature be criminals —more or less, of course.
uz: Qisqacha aytganda, men barcha buyuk insonlar yoki hatto odatdan biroz chetda qolgan, ya'ni yangi so'zni aytishga qodir odamlar, tabiatda jinoyatchilar bo'lishlari kerakligini aytaman.

en: Otherwise it’s hard for them to get out of the common rut; and to remain in the common rut is what they can’t submit to, from their very nature again, and to my mind they ought not, indeed, to submit to it.
uz: Aks holda, ular uchun umumiy odatdan chiqish qiyin bo'ladi; va odatdagi odatda qolish - bu ular o'z tabiati bilan yana bo'ysuna olmaydigan narsa, mening fikrimcha, ular bunga bo'ysunishlari kerak emas.

en: You see that there is nothing particularly new in all that.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, bularning barchasida yangilik yo'q.

en: The same thing has been printed and read a thousand times before.
uz: Bu haqda o'sha paytgacha ming marta chop etilgan va o'qilgan.

en: As for my division of people into ordinary and extraordinary, I acknowledge that it’s somewhat arbitrary, but I don’t insist upon exact numbers.
uz: Odamlarni oddiy va noyob bo'lishimga kelsak, bu biroz ixtiyoriy ekanligini tan olaman, lekin aniq raqamlarga e'tibor bermayman.

en: I only believe in my leading idea that men are in general divided by a law of nature into two categories, inferior (ordinary), that is, so to say, material that serves only to reproduce its kind, and men who have the gift or the talent to utter a new word.
uz: Men faqat o'zimning asosiy fikrimga ishonamanki, insonlar tabiat qonuni asosida ikki toifaga bo'linadi: past (oddiy), ya'ni faqat o'z turini ko'paytirish uchun ishlatiladigan material va yangi so'zni aytish uchun hadya yoki iste'dodga ega bo'lgan odamlar.

en: There are, of course, innumerable subdivisions, but the distinguishing features of both categories are fairly well marked.
uz: Albatta, ko'pgina bo'linmalar mavjud, ammo ikkala toifaning ham ajralib turadigan xususiyatlari juda yaxshi ko'rsatilgan.

en: The first category, generally speaking, are men conservative in
uz: Birinchi toifa, umuman olganda, konservativ erkaklardir.

en: temperament and law-abiding; they live under control and love to be controlled.
uz: Temperament va qonunbuzarlik; ular nazorat ostida yashaydilar va nazorat qilinishni yaxshi ko'radilar.

en: To my thinking it is their duty to be controlled, because that’s their vocation, and there is nothing humiliating in it for them.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, ular nazorat qilinishlari kerak, chunki bu ularning vazifasi va ular uchun bu kamsitadigan narsa emas.

en: The second category all transgress the law; they are destroyers or disposed to destruction according to their capacities.
uz: Ikkinchi toifa hammasi qonunni buzadi; ular o'z qobiliyatlariga qarab yo'qotib yuboruvchi yoki yo'q qilishga moyil bo'lgan yo'qotib yuboruvchilardir.

en: The crimes of these men are of course relative and varied; for the most part they seek in very varied ways the destruction of the present for the sake of the better.
uz: Albatta, bu odamlarning jinoyatlari nisbiy va turli xil; aksariyat hollarda ular hozirgi zamonni yaxshilik uchun yo'q qilishni turli yo'llar bilan izlaydilar.

en: But if such a one is forced for the sake of his idea to step over a corpse or wade through blood, he can, I maintain, find within himself, in his conscience, a sanction for wading through blood —that depends on the idea and its dimensions, note that.
uz: Ammo agar bunday kishi o'z g'oyasi tufayli jasad ustiga qadam bosishga majbur bo'lsa yoki qon orqali o'tishga majbur bo'lsa, u o'z ichida, vijdonida qon orqali o'tishga ruxsat topishi mumkin, bu g'oya va uning o'lchamlariga bog'liq, e'tibor bering.

en: It’s only in that sense I speak of their right to crime in my article (you remember it began with the legal question).
uz: Faqatgina shu ma'noda men maqolaimda ularning jinoyatchilikka bo'lgan huquqi haqida gapiraman (u qonuniy savol bilan boshlandi, deb eslaysiz).

en: There’s no need for such anxiety, however; the masses will scarcely ever admit this right, they punish them or hang them (more or less), and in doing so fulfil quite justly their conservative vocation.
uz: Biroq bunday tashvishlanishning hojati yo'q; ommaviylar bu huquqni hech qachon tan olmaydilar, ularni jazolaydilar yoki asrashadi (ko'proq-ko'proq), va shu yo'sin o'zlarining konservativ da'vatlarini to'liq haqli ravishda bajaradilar.

en: But the same masses set these criminals on a pedestal in the next generation and worship them (more or less).
uz: Ammo o'sha o'sha ko'pchiliklar ushbu jinoyatchilarni keyingi avlodda ustun qo'yib, ularga (ko'proq-ko'proq) sajda qilishadi.

en: The first category is always the man of the present, the second the man of the future.
uz: Birinchi toifa har doim hozirgi odam, ikkinchisi esa kelajakdagi odamdir.

en: The first preserve the world and people it, the second move the world and lead it to its goal.
uz: Birinchisi dunyoni saqlab qolish va uni inobatga olish, ikkinchisi dunyoni harakatga keltirish va uni maqsadga yetaklashdir.

en: Each class has an equal right to exist.
uz: Har bir sinf barobar yashash huquqiga ega.

en: In fact, all have equal rights with me —and vive la guerre éternelle —till the New Jerusalem, of course!” “Then you believe in the New Jerusalem, do you?” “I do,” Raskolnikov answered firmly; as he said these words and during the whole preceding tirade he kept his eyes on one spot on the carpet.
uz: Darhaqiqat, barchamiz men bilan teng huquqlarga egamiz va abadiy urushda yashaymiz Yangi Quddusga qadar, albatta!Shunda siz Yangi Quddusga ishonasizmi?Men ishonaman, Raskolnikov qat'iy javob berdi; u bu so'zlarni aytganida va butun o'tgan tirada davomida u ko'zlarini ko'ylakning bir nuqtasiga qaratdi.

en: “And … and do you believe in God?
uz: Va... va siz Xudoga ishonasizmi?

en: Excuse my curiosity.” “I do,” repeated Raskolnikov, raising his eyes to Porfiry.
uz: O'zimni qiziqtirganimdan uzr so'raysiz.  Men qilyapman, Raskolnikov takrorladi va ko'zlarini Porfiryga ko'tardi.

en: “And … do you believe in Lazarus’ rising from the dead?” “I … I do.
uz: ... Siz Lazarning o'limdan tirilishiga ishonasizmi?  Men... ishonaman.

en: Why do you ask all this?” “You believe it literally?” “Literally.” “You don’t say so.
uz: Nima uchun bularning barchasini so'rasan?Siz bu so'zlarga chiroyli ishonasizmi?Literally.Siz buni aytmaysiz.

en: … I asked from curiosity.
uz: ...Men qiziquvchanlik bilan so'radim.

en: But let us go back to the question; they are not always executed.
uz: Ammo savolga qaytaylik; ular har doim ham o'ldirilmaydi.

en: Some, on the contrary …” “Triumph in their lifetime?
uz: Ba'zilar, aksincha ...O'z hayotida g'alaba qozonish?

en: Oh, yes, some attain their ends in this life, and then …”
uz: Ha, ba'zilar bu hayotda o'z maqsadlariga erishadilar, keyin esa ...

en: “They begin executing other people?” “If it’s necessary; indeed, for the most part they do.
uz: Ular boshqa odamlarni o'ldirishni boshlaydilarmi? Agar kerak bo'lsa, aksariyat hollarda o'ldiradilar.

en: Your remark is very witty.” “Thank you.
uz: Sizning sharhingiz juda aqlli. Rahmat.

en: But tell me this: how do you distinguish those extraordinary people from the ordinary ones?
uz: Ammo menga bir narsani ayting: qanday qilib siz ushbu noyob odamlarni oddiy odamlardan ajratib olasiz?

en: Are there signs at their birth?
uz: Ularning tug'ilishida belgilar bormi?

en: I feel there ought to be more exactitude, more external definition.
uz: O'ylaymanki, aniqroq, tashqi ma'lumotlar ko'proq bo'lishi kerak.

en: Excuse the natural anxiety of a practical law-abiding citizen, but couldn’t they adopt a special uniform, for instance, couldn’t they wear something, be branded in some way?
uz: Qonunga bo'ysunadigan fuqarolarning tabiiy tashvishlari uchun uzr so'raylik, lekin ular maxsus uniformni qabul qila olishmasmidi, masalan, biron bir narsani kiyib olishmasmidi, biron-bir markaga ega bo'lishmasmidi?

en: For you know if confusion arises and a member of one category imagines that he belongs to the other, begins to ‘eliminate obstacles’ as you so happily expressed it, then …” “Oh, that very often happens!
uz: Chunki bilasizki, agar chalkashlik paydo bo'lib, bir toifa a'zosi o'zini boshqa toifaga tegishli deb o'ylasa, siz xursandchilik bilan aytganingizdek, to'siqlarni yo'q qilishni boshlasa, unda ...Oh, bu juda tez-tez sodir bo'ladi!

en: That remark is wittier than the other.” “Thank you.” “No reason to; but take note that the mistake can only arise in the first category, that is among the ordinary people (as I perhaps unfortunately called them).
uz: Bu fikr boshqalardan ko'ra aqlliroq. Rahmat.  Hech qanday sabab yo'q; lekin e'tibor beringki, xato faqat birinchi toifada, ya'ni oddiy odamlar orasida sodir bo'lishi mumkin (men ularni, ehtimol, afsuski, shunday deb ataganman).

en: In spite of their predisposition to obedience very many of them, through a playfulness of nature, sometimes vouchsafed even to the cow, like to imagine themselves advanced people, ‘destroyers,’ and to push themselves into the ‘new movement,’ and this quite sincerely.
uz: Ularning ko'pchiligi itoatkorlikka moyil bo'lishlariga qaramay, ba'zan tabiatning o'yin-kulgiligi tufayli, hatto sigirga ham sovg'a berishardi, ular o'zlarini ilg'or odamlar, vayronchilar deb tasavvur qilishardi va o'zlarini yangi harakatga qo'shishardi.

en: Meanwhile the really new people are very often unobserved by them, or even despised as reactionaries of grovelling tendencies.
uz: Shu bilan birga, haqiqiy yangi odamlar ko'pincha ular tomonidan kuzatilmaydi yoki hatto g'alati tendentsiyalarning reaktsionerlari sifatida tanqid qilinadi.

en: But I don’t think there is any considerable danger here, and you really need not be uneasy for they never go very far.
uz: Ammo bu yerda jiddiy xavf yo'q, deb o'ylayman va siz xavotirlanishga hojat yo'q, chunki ular hech qachon juda uzoq ketmaydi.

en: Of course, they might have a thrashing sometimes for letting their fancy run away with them and to teach them their place, but no more; in fact, even this isn’t necessary as they castigate themselves, for they are very conscientious: some perform this service for one another and others chastise themselves with their own hands.
uz: To'g'ri, ular ba'zan o'zlarining tasavvurlariga qo'yib ketishlariga va o'z o'rnini o'rgatishlariga to'sqinlik qilishadi, lekin bundan ko'proq; aslida, hatto bu ham o'zlarini tanqid qilish uchun zarur emas, chunki ular juda vijdonli: ba'zilar bir-biri uchun bu xizmatni bajarib, boshqalari esa o'z qo'llari bilan o'zlarini tanqid qilishadi.

en: … They will impose various public acts of penitence upon themselves with a beautiful and edifying effect; in fact you’ve nothing to be uneasy about.
uz: ... Ular o'zlariga turlicha tavba qilish harakatlarini o'zlariga go'zal va o'zlashtiruvchi ta'sir bilan o'tkazadilar; aslida sizda xavotirlanishga hech narsa yo'q.

en: … It’s a law of nature.” “Well, you have certainly set my mind more at rest on that score; but there’s another thing worries me.
uz: Bu tabiat qonuni. Ha, albatta, siz bu borada mening ongimni ko'proq tinchlantirgansiz; lekin meni boshqa bir narsa tashvishlantiradi.

en: Tell me, please, are there many people who have the right to kill others, these extraordinary people?
uz: Menga ayting, iltimos, boshqalarni o'ldirish huquqiga ega bo'lgan ko'plab odamlar bormi, bu noyob odamlar?

en: I am ready to bow down to them, of course, but you must admit it’s alarming if there are a great many of them, eh?”
uz: Albatta, men ularga sajda qilishga tayyorman, lekin ular juda ko'p bo'lsa, bu dahshatli ekanligini tan olishingiz kerak, shunday emasmi?

en: “Oh, you needn’t worry about that either,” Raskolnikov went on in the same tone.
uz: Oh, bu haqda ham tashvishlanishingiz shart emas,  Raskolnikov xuddi shunday so'z bilan davom etdi.

en: “People with new ideas, people with the faintest capacity for saying something new, are extremely few in number, extraordinarily so in fact.
uz: Yangi g'oyalarga ega bo'lgan, yangi narsalarni aytish uchun eng zaif qobiliyatiga ega bo'lgan odamlar son-sanoatda juda kam, aslida esa juda kam.

en: One thing only is clear, that the appearance of all these grades and subdivisions of men must follow with unfailing regularity some law of nature.
uz: Faqat bitta narsa aniq: insonlarning barcha darajalari va bo'linmalari paydo bo'lishi uchun tabiat qonunlariga qat'iy amal qilish kerak.

en: That law, of course, is unknown at present, but I am convinced that it exists, and one day may become known.
uz: Albatta, bu qonun hozirga qadar noma'lum, lekin u borligiga ishonaman va bir kun ma'lum bo'lishi mumkin.

en: The vast mass of mankind is mere material, and only exists in order by some great effort, by some mysterious process, by means of some crossing of races and stocks, to bring into the world at last perhaps one man out of a thousand with a spark of independence.
uz: Insoniyatning ulkan qismi oddiy material bo'lib, faqatgina ba'zi katta sa'y-harakatlar, sirli jarayonlar, irqlar va to'plarning bir-biriga o'tishi orqali, oxir-oqibat mustaqillik parchalari bo'lgan ming kishidan bir kishini dunyoga keltirish uchun mavjud.

en: One in ten thousand perhaps —I speak roughly, approximately —is born with some independence, and with still greater independence one in a hundred thousand.
uz: Ehtimol, o'n mingdan biri taxminan, taxminan, bir yuz mingdan biri mustaqillik bilan tug'ilgan.

en: The man of genius is one of millions, and the great geniuses, the crown of humanity, appear on earth perhaps one in many thousand millions.
uz: G'ayriya odam millionlardan biri, insoniyatning tojidir bo'lgan buyuk g'ayriyalar esa yer yuzida minglab millionlardan biri bo'lishi mumkin.

en: In fact I have not peeped into the retort in which all this takes place.
uz: Aslida, men bularning barchasi sodir bo'lgan javobni ko'rmaganman.

en: But there certainly is and must be a definite law, it cannot be a matter of chance.” “Why, are you both joking?” Razumihin cried at last.
uz: Ammo aniq qonun bor va bo'lishi kerak, u tasodifan bo'lishi mumkin emas. Nega, ikkalasi ham o'yin qilyapsizlar? Razumihin nihoyat yig'ladi.

en: “There you sit, making fun of one another.
uz: Sizlar o'tirib, bir-biringiz bilan kulishasizlar.

en: Are you serious, Rodya?” Raskolnikov raised his pale and almost mournful face and made no reply.
uz: Rodya, siz jiddiymisiz? Raskolnikov o'z ko'rinmas va deyarli qayg'uli yuzini ko'tarib, hech qanday javob bermadi.

en: And the unconcealed, persistent, nervous, and discourteous sarcasm of Porfiry seemed strange to Razumihin beside that quiet and mournful face.
uz: Porfirining yashirin, chidamli, g'ayratli va beparvo sarkasmi bu tinch va qayg'uli yuzdan tashqari Razumihin uchun g'alati tuyuldi.

en: “Well, brother, if you are really serious … You are right, of course, in saying that it’s not new, that it’s like what we’ve read and heard a thousand times already; but what is really original in all this, and is exclusively your own, to my horror, is that you sanction bloodshed in the name of conscience, and, excuse my saying so, with such fanaticism.
uz: Xo'sh, birodarim, agar siz chindan ham jiddiy bo'lsangiz... Albatta, bu yangilik emas, biz ming marta o'qigan va eshitgan narsalarga o'xshaydi, deganingizda to'g'ri bo'lasiz; lekin bularning barchasida aslida asl narsa, va mening qo'rquvim uchun faqat sizning o'zingizniki, vijdon nomidan qon to'kishingizni va, uzr aytsam, bunday fanatizmni qo'llab-quvvatlayotganingizni anglatadi.

en: … That, I take it, is the point of your article.
uz: O'ylaymanki, sizning maqolangizning asosiy maqsadi shundoq.

en: But that sanction of bloodshed by conscience is to my mind … more terrible than the official, legal sanction of bloodshed.
uz: Ammo vijdon bilan qon to'kish uchun qo'llash mening fikrimda qon to'kish uchun rasmiy, qonuniy qo'llashdan ham dahshatlidir.

en: …” “You are quite right, it is more terrible,” Porfiry agreed.
uz: Siz haqsiz, bu yanada dahshatli, Porfiry rozi bo'ldi.

en: “Yes, you must have exaggerated!
uz: Ha, shubhasiz, siz haddan oshgansiz!

en: There is some mistake, I shall read it.
uz: Biror xato bor, uni o'qib chiqaman.

en: You can’t think that!
uz: Siz buni o'ylay olmaysiz!

en: “All that is not in the article, there’s only a hint of it,” said Raskolnikov.
uz: Maqolada yo'q bo'lgan barcha narsalar, faqatgina bir nuqta bor, dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “Yes, yes.” Porfiry couldn’t sit still.
uz: Ha, ha. Porfiry to'xtamay o'tirolmadi.

en: “Your attitude to crime is pretty clear to me now, but … excuse me for my impertinence (I am really ashamed to be worrying you like this), you see, you’ve removed my anxiety as to the two grades getting mixed, but … there are various practical possibilities that make me uneasy!
uz: Sizning jinoyatchilikka bo'lgan munosabatingiz hozir menga juda aniq, lekin ... menga o'zimning befarqligim uchun kechirim so'rang (sizni bunday tashvishlantirganimdan juda uyatdaman), ko'rib turganingizdek, siz ikki daraja o'zaro aralashib ketishi haqida tashvishimni yo'q qildingiz, lekin ... meni noqulay qiladigan turli amaliy imkoniyatlar bor!

en: What if some man or youth imagines that he is a Lycurgus or Mahomet —a future one of course —and suppose he begins to remove all obstacles.
uz: Agar biror kishi yoki yosh kishi o'zini Lycurgus yoki Muhammad deb o'ylasa va barcha to'siqlarni olib tashlashni boshlasa nima bo'ladi?

en: … He has some great enterprise before him and needs money for it … and tries to get it … do you see?” Zametov gave a sudden guffaw in his corner.
uz: ... Uning oldida katta ish bor va unga pul kerak ... va uni olishga harakat qiladi ... ko'ryapsizmi? Zametov uning burchagida to'satdan g'offa qildi.

en: Raskolnikov did not even raise his eyes to him.
uz: Raskolnikov hatto unga ko'zlarini ko'tarmadi.

en: “I must admit,” he went on calmly, “that such cases certainly must arise.
uz: Men shuni tan olsam kerak, u xotirjamlik bilan davom etdi, bunday holatlar albatta paydo bo'lishi kerak.

en: The vain and foolish are particularly apt to fall into that snare; young people especially.” “Yes, you see.
uz: Bu tuzoqqa behuda va nodonlar, ayniqsa yoshlar tushishi mumkin.Ha, ko'rasiz.

en: Well then?” “What then?” Raskolnikov smiled in reply; “that’s not my fault.
uz: Xo'sh, nima bo'ldi? Raskolnikov javobda tabassum qildi; bu mening aybim emas.

en: So it is and so it always will be.
uz: Shunday bo'ldi va shunday bo'ladi hamisha.

en: He said just now (he nodded at Razumihin) that I sanction bloodshed.
uz: U yaqinda (Razumihinga boshini tiydi) qon to'kish uchun ruxsat berayotganimni aytdi.

en: Society is too well protected by prisons, banishment, criminal investigators, penal servitude.
uz: Jamiyat qamoqxonalar, qamoqdan chiqarilish, jinoyat tergovchilari, jinoiy qullik bilan juda yaxshi himoyalangan.

en: There’s no need to be uneasy.
uz: Xavflanishga hojat yo'q.

en: You have but to catch the thief.” “And what if we do catch him?” “Then he gets what he deserves.” “You are certainly logical.
uz: Siz faqat o'g'ri tutib olishingiz kerak. Va agar biz uni tutib olsak nima bo'ladi?Undan keyin u o'ziga loyiq bo'lgan narsani oladi.Siz, albatta, mantiqiysiz.

en: But what of his conscience?” “Why do you care about that?” “Simply from humanity.” “If he has a conscience he will suffer for his mistake.
uz: Ammo uning vijdoni haqida nima deyish mumkin? Nega bu sizga qiziqish uyg'otadi?Soddiy insonlikdan.Agar vijdoni bo'lsa, o'zining xatolari uchun azob chekadi.

en: That will be his punishment —as well as the prison.” “But the real geniuses,” asked Razumihin frowning, “those who have the right to murder?
uz: Bu uning jazosi bo'ladi va qamoq ham. Lekin haqiqiy g'ayriyalar, deb so'radi Razumihin,quloqlarini burib,quloq so'rab,quloq solib,quloq so'rash huquqiga ega bo'lganlar?

en: Oughtn’t they to suffer at all even for the blood they’ve shed?” “Why the word ought?
uz: Ular to'kkan qonlari uchun ham azob chekishlari kerak emasmi? Nima uchun bu so'z kerak?

en: It’s not a matter of permission or prohibition.
uz: Bu ruxsat berish yoki taqiqlash masalasi emas.

en: He will suffer if he is sorry for his victim.
uz: Agar o'z qurboniga rahm qilinsa, azob chekadi.

en: Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart.
uz: Og'riq va azob-uqubat katta aqlli va chuqur yurak uchun har doim muqarrar.

en: The really great men must, I think, have great sadness on earth,” he added dreamily, not in the tone of the conversation.
uz: O'ylaymanki, haqiqiy buyuk insonlar yer yuzida katta qayg'ularga ega bo'lishlari kerak, deb aytdi u, so'z o'qiydigan paytda emas, balki orzu qilib qo'ydi.

en: He raised his eyes, looked earnestly at them all, smiled, and took his cap.
uz: U ko'zlarini ko'tarib, ularning barchasini diqqat bilan ko'rib, tabassum qildi va qo'lboshini olib ketdi.

en: He was too quiet by comparison with his manner at his entrance, and he felt this.
uz: U o'zining kirish joyida o'z xatti-harakatlari bilan taqqoslaganda juda xotirjam edi va buni his qilgan.

en: “Well, you may abuse me, be angry with me if you like,” Porfiry Petrovitch began again, “but I can’t resist.
uz: Ha, siz meni yomon ko'rishingiz mumkin, xohlasangiz, menga g'azablaning,  Porfiry Petrovitch yana boshlandi,  lekin men qarshi tura olmayman.

en: Allow me one little question (I know I am troubling you).
uz: Menga bitta kichik savol berishga ruxsat bering (man sizni bezovta qilayotganimni bilaman).

en: There is just one little notion I want to express, simply that I may not forget it.” “Very good, tell me your little notion,” Raskolnikov stood waiting, pale and grave before him.
uz: Faqat bitta kichik tushuncha bor, uni esdan chiqarmasligim uchun aytmoqchiman. Chindan ham yaxshi, menga o'zingizning kichik tushunchangizni ayting, Raskolnikov uning oldidan bekatlab turgan edi.

en: “Well, you see … I really don’t know how to express it properly.
uz: Ha, ko'ryapsizmi... Men buni qanday qilib to'g'ri ifodalashni bilmayman.

en: … It’s a playful, psychological idea.
uz: Bu o'yinli, psixologik fikr.

en: … When you were writing your article, surely you couldn’t have helped, he-he!
uz: ... Maqolangizni yozganingizda, albatta, yordam bera olmas edingiz!

en: fancying yourself … just a little, an ‘extraordinary’ man, uttering a new word in your sense.
uz: O'zingizni o'zingiz o'ylab ko'ring ... faqat bir oz, o'zgacha odam, o'zingizning ma'noingizda yangi so'zni aytasiz.

en: … That’s so, isn’t it?” “Quite possibly,” Raskolnikov answered contemptuously.
uz: Shunday ekan, shunday emasmi? - Raskolnikov haqorat bilan javob berdi.

en: Razumihin made a movement.
uz: Razumihin harakat qildi.

en: “And, if so, could you bring yourself in case of worldly difficulties and hardship or for some service to humanity —to overstep obstacles?
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, dunyoning qiyinchiliklari va qiyinchiliklari yoki insoniyatga xizmat qilish uchun to'siqlarni bartaraf etish uchun o'zingizni tayyorlay olasizmi?

en: … For instance, to rob and murder?” And again he winked with his left eye, and laughed noiselessly just as before.
uz: Misol uchun, talon-toroj qilish va o'ldirish? Va yana chap ko'zi bilan ko'z yumib, avvalgidek ovozsiz kulishdi.

en: “If I did I certainly should not tell you,” Raskolnikov answered with defiant and haughty contempt.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, albatta sizga aytmasdim,  Raskolnikov g'ayrat va mag'rurlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “No, I was only interested on account of your article, from a literary point of view …” “Foo!
uz: Yo'q, men faqatgina sizning maqolangiz bilan qiziqdim, adabiy nuqtai nazardan ...  Foo!

en: how obvious and insolent that is!” Raskolnikov thought with repulsion.
uz: Bu qanchalik aniq va behuda! Raskolnikov nafrat bilan o'yladi.

en: “Allow me to observe,” he answered dryly, “that I don’t consider myself a Mahomet or a Napoleon, nor any personage of that kind, and not being one of them I cannot tell you how I should act.” “Oh, come, don’t we all think ourselves Napoleons now in Russia?” Porfiry Petrovitch said with alarming familiarity.
uz: Mening e'tiborimni qaratishga ruxsat bering, - dedi u quruq javob berib, - o'zimni Muhammad yoki Napoleon yoki boshqa hech qanday shaxs deb hisoblamayman va ulardan biri bo'lmaganim uchun qanday yo'l tutishim kerakligini aytolmayman.Oh, keling, hozir Rossiyada hammamiz o'zimizni Napoleon deb o'ylamayapmizmi? Porfiry Petrovitch dahshatli tanishlik bilan dedi.

en: Something peculiar betrayed itself in the very intonation of his voice.
uz: O'zining ovozi o'zining intonatsiyasida o'ziga xos narsa paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Perhaps it was one of these future Napoleons who did for Alyona Ivanovna last week?” Zametov blurted out from the corner.
uz: Ehtimol, o'tgan hafta Alyona Ivanovna uchun o'tgan bu kelajakdagi Napoleonlardan biri bo'lgan? Zametov burchadan chiqib ketdi.

en: Raskolnikov did not speak, but looked firmly and intently at Porfiry.
uz: Raskolnikov gapirmadi, lekin Porfiryga qat'iy va diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: Razumihin was scowling gloomily.
uz: Razumihin qo'rqinchli tarzda qichqirgan edi.

en: He seemed before this to be noticing something.
uz: Bundan oldin u biror narsa payqagan ko'rinardi.

en: He looked angrily around.
uz: U g'azablangancha atrofga qaradi.

en: There was a minute of gloomy silence.
uz: Bir daqiqalik soʻzsizlik boʻldi.

en: Raskolnikov turned to go.
uz: Raskolnikov ketishga moyil bo'ldi.

en: “Are you going already?” Porfiry said amiably, holding out his hand with excessive politeness.
uz: Siz allaqachon ketyapsizmi? - dedi Porfiry mehribonlik bilan, qo'lini ko'p xushmuomalalik bilan uzatdi.

en: “Very, very glad of your acquaintance.
uz: Chindan ham, siz bilan tanishishdan juda xursandman.

en: As for your request, have no uneasiness, write just as I told you, or, better still, come to me there yourself in a day or two … tomorrow, indeed.
uz: So'rovingizga kelsak, xavotirga tushmang, aytganimdek yozib qo'ying yoki, eng yaxshisi, bir yoki ikki kun ichida o'zingiz menga tashrif buyuring... ertaga, albatta.

en: I shall be there at eleven o’clock for certain.
uz: Albatta, o'n birda u yerda bo'laman.

en: We’ll arrange it all; we’ll have a talk.
uz: Biz hamma narsani tartibga solamiz; biz gaplashamiz.

en: As one of the last to be there, you might perhaps be able to tell us something,” he added with a most good- natured expression.
uz: So'nggilardan biri sifatida, ehtimol, siz bizga biror narsa aytib bera olasiz, - dedi u juda mehribon so'zlar bilan.

en: “You want to cross-examine me officially in due form?” Raskolnikov asked sharply.
uz: Siz meni rasmiy ravishda to'g'ri shaklda so'roq qilishni xohlaysizmi? Raskolnikov keskin so'radi.

en: That’s not necessary for the present.
uz: Bu hozir uchun zarur emas.

en: You misunderstand me.
uz: Siz meni noto'g'ri tushunasiz.

en: I lose no opportunity, you see, and … I’ve talked with all who had pledges.
uz: Men hech qanday imkoniyatni yo'qotmayman va... Men har bir kishi bilan suhbatlashdim.

en: … I obtained evidence from some of them, and you are the last.
uz: Men ulardan ba'zilaridan dalillar oldim, siz esa oxirchisiz.

en: … Yes, by the way,” he cried, seemingly suddenly delighted, “I just remember, what was I thinking of?” he turned to Razumihin, “you were talking my ears off about that Nikolay … of course, I know, I know very well,” he turned to Raskolnikov, “that the fellow is innocent, but what is one to do?
uz: Ha, bu borada u yig'lab yubordi, ko'rinishicha, birdan quvonchga to'ldi, faqat eslaymanki, men nima haqida o'yladim? - U Razumihinga murojaat qildi, - sen o'sha Nikolay to'g'risida quloqlarimga gapirgan edi. - Albatta, bilaman, juda yaxshi bilaman, - Raskolnikovga murojaat qildi, - bu odam begunoh, lekin nima qilish kerak?

en: We had to trouble Dmitri too.
uz: Biz Dmitriyni ham bezovta qilishimiz kerak edi.

en: … This is the point, this is all: when you went up the stairs it was past seven, wasn’t it?” “Yes,” answered Raskolnikov, with an unpleasant sensation at the very moment he spoke that he need not have said it.
uz: ... Mana shu gap, bu hammasi: sinchkovlarga chiqqaningizda yetti soatdan o'tibdi, shunday emasmi? Ha, Raskolnikov javob berdi, u gapirgan paytning o'zida yoqimsiz his-tuyg'u bilan gapirganida, buni aytishga hojat yo'qligini aytdi.

en: “Then when you went upstairs between seven and eight, didn’t you see in a flat that stood open on a second storey, do you remember?
uz: Keyin yetti va sakkizinchi qavatlar o'rtasida yuqoriga chiqqaningizda, ikkinchi qavatda ochiq turgan bir kvartirani ko'rmadingizmi, eslaysizmi?

en: two workmen or at least one of them?
uz: Ikki ishchi yoki ulardan hech bo'lmaganda bittasi?

en: They were painting there, didn’t you notice them?
uz: Ular bu yerda rasm chizishardi, siz ularni sezmadingizmi?

en: It’s very, very important for them.” “Painters?
uz: Bu ular uchun juda, juda muhim. Ressamlar?

en: No, I didn’t see them,” Raskolnikov answered slowly, as though ransacking his memory, while at the same instant he was racking every nerve, almost swooning with anxiety to conjecture as quickly as possible where the trap lay and not to overlook anything.
uz: Yo'q, men ularni ko'rmadim, - deb javob berdi Raskolnikov sekin-sakin, xuddi xotirasini o'g'irlab ketayotgandek, bir vaqtning o'zida u har qanday g'azabni buzgan, deyarli o'z tashvishidan o'zimni tiygan, tuzoqning qayerda joylashganini tezroq taxmin qilish va hech narsani e'tiborsiz qoldirmaslik uchun.

en: “No, I didn’t see them, and I don’t think I noticed a flat like that open.
uz: Yo'q, men ularni ko'rmadim va bunday ochiq xonadonni ko'rmadim.

en: … But on the fourth storey” (he had mastered the trap now and was
uz: Ammo to'rtinchi qavatda u endi tuzoqni o'zlashtirgan va o'sha paytda u o'ziga xos bo'lgan.

en: triumphant) “I remember now that someone was moving out of the flat opposite Alyona Ivanovna’s.
uz: ) Shuning o'zida kimdir Alyona Ivanovnasning qarshisidagi kvartardan chiqib ketayotganini eslayman.

en: … I remember … I remember it clearly.
uz: ... eslayman... aniq eslayman.

en: Some porters were carrying out a sofa and they squeezed me against the wall.
uz: Ba'zi ko'tarib oluvchilar sofani olib borayotgan edilar va meni devorga shovqatib qo'yishdi.

en: But painters … no, I don’t remember that there were any painters, and I don’t think that there was a flat open anywhere, no, there wasn’t.” “What do you mean?” Razumihin shouted suddenly, as though he had reflected and realised.
uz: Lekin rassomlar... yo'q, men hech qanday rassomlar borligini eslay olmayman va hech joyda ochiq yonma-yon bo'lgan deb o'ylamayman, yo'q, yo'q edi.  Nima demoqchisiz? Razumihin birdan o'ylab ko'rgan va tushunganidek qichqirdi.

en: “Why, it was on the day of the murder the painters were at work, and he was there three days before?
uz: Nima uchun, bu o'ldirilgan kun bo'lganida rassomlar ishda edilar va u uch kun oldin u erda edi?

en: What are you asking?” “Foo!
uz: Nima so'rasan? Foo!

en: I have muddled it!” Porfiry slapped himself on the forehead.
uz: Men uni to'xtatdim! Porfiry o'z oldiga o'zini urdi.

en: This business is turning my brain!” he addressed Raskolnikov somewhat apologetically.
uz: Bu ish mening miyamni aylantirmoqda! u Raskolnikovga uzr so'radi.

en: “It would be such a great thing for us to find out whether anyone had seen them between seven and eight at the flat, so I fancied you could perhaps have told us something.
uz: Ushbu yerda ularni yetti va sakkiz soat o'rtasida ko'rganlar yoki ko'rmaganlarni bilish juda yaxshi bo'lardi, shuning uchun siz bizga biror narsa aytib berishingiz mumkinligini o'yladim.

en: … I quite muddled it.” “Then you should be more careful,” Razumihin observed grimly.
uz: ...Men buni juda chalg'itdim. Shuning uchun siz yanada ehtiyotkor bo'lishingiz kerak, Razumihin sharmandalik bilan kuzatdi.

en: The last words were uttered in the passage.
uz: So'nggi so'zlar o'qishda so'zlangan.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch saw them to the door with excessive politeness.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch ularni eshikdan tashqari xushmuomalalik bilan ko'rdi.

en: They went out into the street gloomy and sullen, and for some steps they did not say a word.
uz: Ular ko'chaga tushishdi, ko'ngillari ko'p bo'lmay, bir necha qadam ham so'z aytmadilar.

en: Raskolnikov drew a deep breath.
uz: Raskolnikov chuqur nafas oldi.

en: VI “I don’t believe it, I can’t believe it!” repeated Razumihin, trying in perplexity to refute Raskolnikov’s arguments.
uz: Men ishonmayman, ishonolmayman! - deb takrorladi Razumihin, ravshanlik bilan Raskolnikovning dalillarini rad etishga harakat qildi.

en: They were by now approaching Bakaleyev’s lodgings, where Pulcheria Alexandrovna and Dounia had been expecting them a long while.
uz: Ular hozirda Bakaleyevlarning uylariga yaqinlashayotgan edilar, Pulcheria Aleksandrovna va Dounia ularni uzoq vaqt kutishgan edi.

en: Razumihin kept stopping on the way in the heat of discussion, confused and excited by the very fact that they were for the first time speaking openly about it.
uz: Razumihin birinchi marta bu haqda ochiqchasiga gapirishganidan g'alati va hayajonlanib, bahs-munozaralar o'rtasida yo'lda to'xtab turdi.

en: “Don’t believe it, then!” answered Raskolnikov, with a cold, careless smile.
uz: Don't believe it, then! javob Raskolnikov, sovuq, beparvo tabassum bilan.

en: “You were noticing nothing as usual, but I was weighing every word.” “You are suspicious.
uz: Siz odatdagidek hech narsaga e'tibor bermayapsiz, lekin men har bir so'zni o'ylab ko'rdim. Siz shubha ostiga qo'ygansiz.

en: That is why you weighed their words … h’m … certainly, I agree, Porfiry’s tone was rather strange, and still more that wretch Zametov!
uz: Shuning uchun siz ularning so'zlarini o'lchab ko'rdingiz ... albatta, men bunga roziman, Porfirining ovozi o'ta g'alati edi va bundan ham ko'proq o'sha qashshoq Zametov!

en: … You are right, there was something about him —but why?
uz: ... Siz haqsiz, u haqida bir narsa bor edi, lekin nima uchun?

en: Why?” “He has changed his mind since last night.” “Quite the contrary!
uz: Nima uchun? U o'z fikrini o'zgartirgan. To'g'ri, aksincha!

en: If they had that brainless idea, they would do their utmost to hide it, and conceal their cards, so as to catch you afterwards.
uz: Agar ular bu aqlsiz g'oyaga ega bo'lishsa, uni yashirish va kartalarini yashirish uchun hamma narsani qilishadi, toki keyinchalik sizni ushlab qolishsin.

en: … But it was all impudent and careless.” “If they had had facts —I mean, real facts —or at least grounds for suspicion, then they would certainly have tried to hide their game, in the hope of getting more (they would have made a search long ago besides).
uz: Ammo bularning hammasi beparvo va beparvo edi. Agar ular haqiqatlarga ega bo'lishganida, Dast haqiqatlarga ega bo'lishganida yoki hech bo'lmaganda shubha ostiga qo'yish uchun sabablar bo'lganida, ular o'z o'yinlarini yashirishga harakat qilishgan bo'lishadi, chunki ular ko'proq narsani topishga umid qilishgan (ular uzoq vaqt oldin qidirib topgan bo'lishadi).

en: But they have no facts, not one.
uz: Ammo ular hech qanday dalillarga ega emaslar.

en: It is all mirage —all ambiguous.
uz: Bularning barchasi o'ziga xos emas.

en: Simply a floating idea.
uz: Bu shunchaki ko'tarilayotgan g'oya.

en: So they try to throw me out by impudence.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular meni shubhasizlik bilan quvib chiqarishga harakat qilishdi.

en: And perhaps, he was irritated at having no facts, and blurted it out in his vexation —or perhaps he has some plan … he seems an intelligent man.
uz: Ehtimol, u hech qanday dalillarga ega bo'lmaganidan xafa bo'lgan va o'z xafaligi bilan gapni so'zlab yuborgan bo'lishi mumkin yoki ehtimol uning biron bir rejasi bor ... u aqlli odamga o'xshaydi.

en: Perhaps he wanted to frighten me by
uz: Ehtimol, u meni qo'rqitmoqchi edi.

en: They have a psychology of their own, brother.
uz: Ularning o'zlarining psixologiyasi bor, aka.

en: But it is loathsome explaining it all.
uz: Ammo bularning barchasini tushuntirish yoqimsiz.

en: Stop!” “And it’s insulting, insulting!
uz: To'xtating! Va bu haqorat, haqorat!

en: But … since we have spoken openly now (and it is an excellent thing that we have at last —I am glad) I will own now frankly that I noticed it in them long ago, this idea.
uz: Ammo ... endi biz ochiqchasiga gapirganimiz sababli (va nihoyat bu juda yaxshi narsa) hozir ochiqchasiga aytamanki, men bu g'oyani uzoq vaqt oldin ular ichida payqadim.

en: Of course the merest hint only —an insinuation —but why an insinuation even?
uz: Albatta, eng oddiy ma'lumot faqatgina an sug'orishdir  lekin nega hatto sug'orish?

en: What foundation have they?
uz: Ular qanday asosga ega?

en: If only you knew how furious I have been.
uz: Agar men qanchalik g'azablanayotganimni bilganingizda edi.

en: Simply because a poor student, unhinged by poverty and hypochondria, on the eve of a severe delirious illness (note that), suspicious, vain, proud, who has not seen a soul to speak to for six months, in rags and in boots without soles, has to face some wretched policemen and put up with their insolence; and the unexpected debt thrust under his nose, the I.O.U.
uz: Shunchaki, kambag'al talaba, qashshoqlik va hipokondriya tufayli bezovta bo'lgan, og'ir kasallik (o'ylab ko'ring), shubhali, behuda, mag'rur bo'lgan, olti oydan beri hech kim bilan gaplashish uchun ruhni ko'rmagan, to'qimalarsiz kiyimda va solamsiz poyabzalda bo'lgan kambag'al talaba, kambag'al politsiyachilarga duch kelib, ularning g'azabini ko'tarishi kerak.

en: presented by Tchebarov, the new paint, thirty degrees Reaumur and a stifling atmosphere, a crowd of people, the talk about the murder of a person where he had been just before, and all that on an empty stomach —he might well have a fainting fit!
uz: Chebarov tomonidan taqdim etilgan yangi bo'yoq, o'ttiz daraja Reaumur va qo'rqinchli muhit, ko'pchilik, u o'tmishda bo'lgan odamning o'ldirilishi haqidagi gaplar va bularning barchasi bo'sh oshqozonida u baytilga tushib qolishi mumkin!

en: And that, that is what they found it all on!
uz: Va bu, ular hamma narsani shu bilan topishdi!

en: I understand how annoying it is, but in your place, Rodya, I would laugh at them, or better still, spit in their ugly faces, and spit a dozen times in all directions.
uz: Bu qanchalik g'alati ekanligini tushunaman, lekin sizning joyingizda bo'lganimda, Rodya, men ularga kulgan bo'lardim, yoki undan ham yaxshiroq bo'lsa, ularning o'tkir yuzlariga tishlab, har tomonga o'nlab marta tishlagan bo'lardim.

en: I’d hit out in all directions, neatly too, and so I’d put an end to it.
uz: Men ham hamma yo'nalishlarda, yaxshi o'ynagan edim va shuning uchun bu ishga chek qo'ydim.

en: Don’t be downhearted.
uz: Yolg'izil bo'lmanglar.

en: It’s a shame!” “He really has put it well, though,” Raskolnikov thought.
uz: Bu juda afsus! U buni juda yaxshi aytdi, deb o'yladi Raskolnikov.

en: But the cross-examination again, tomorrow?” he said with bitterness.
uz: Ammo yana bir bor keskin so'rov, ertaga? dedi u achchiqlanib.

en: “Must I really enter into explanations with them?
uz: Haqiqatan ham men ular bilan tushuntirishlarga kirishim kerakmi?

en: I feel vexed as it is, that I condescended to speak to Zametov yesterday in the restaurant.
uz: Men kechasi restoranda Zametov bilan gaplashishga tushishimdan xafa bo'laman.

en: I will go myself to Porfiry.
uz: Men o'zim Porfirga boraman.

en: I will squeeze it out of him, as one of the family: he must let me know the ins and outs of it all!
uz: Oilaning a'zosi sifatida uni undan chiqarib tashlayman: u menga bularning barchasini bilib berishi kerak!

en: And as for Zametov …” “At last he sees through him!” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: Va Zametovga kelsak... Oxir-oqibat u o'zi orqali ko'radi! - deb o'yladi Raskolnikov.

en: “Stay!” cried Razumihin, seizing him by the shoulder again.
uz: Razumihin uni yana yelkasiga qo'yib, qichqirdi.

en: I have thought it out.
uz: Men buni o'ylab ko'rdim.

en: How was that a trap?
uz: Qanday qilib bu tuzoq edi?

en: You say that the question about the workmen was a trap.
uz: Siz ishchilar haqidagi savol tuzoq edi deysiz.

en: But if you had done that, could you have said you had seen them painting the flat … and the workmen?
uz: Ammo agar siz shunday qilgan bo'lsangiz, ularni kvartirani va ishchilarni bo'yashganini ko'rganingizni aytishingiz mumkinmi?

en: On the contrary, you would
uz: Aksincha, siz ham shunday qilasiz.

en: have seen nothing, even if you had seen it.
uz: Siz ko'rgan bo'lsangiz ham, hech narsa ko'rmagansiz.

en: Who would own it against himself?” “If I had done that thing, I should certainly have said that I had seen the workmen and the flat,” Raskolnikov answered, with reluctance and obvious disgust.
uz: Kim o'ziga qarshi bunga ega bo'ladi? Agar men shunday qilgan bo'lsam, albatta ishchilarni va xonadonni ko'rganimni aytardim, Raskolnikov javob berdi, xohlamaslik va aniq jirkanchlik bilan.

en: “But why speak against yourself?” “Because only peasants, or the most inexperienced novices deny everything flatly at examinations.
uz: Ammo nega o'zingizga qarshi gapirish kerak? Chunki faqat qishloq xo'jaligi yoki eng tajribasiz yangilar imtihonlarda hamma narsani qat'iy rad etadilar.

en: If a man is ever so little developed and experienced, he will certainly try to admit all the external facts that can’t be avoided, but will seek other explanations of them, will introduce some special, unexpected turn, that will give them another significance and put them in another light.
uz: Agar inson o'ta kam rivojlangan va tajribali bo'lsa, albatta, u qochilmaydigan barcha tashqi faktlarni tan olishga harakat qiladi, lekin boshqa tushuntirishlarni izlaydi, ularga alohida, kutilmagan o'zgarish kiritadi, bu ularga boshqa ma'no beradi va ularni boshqacha nurda ko'rsatadi.

en: Porfiry might well reckon that I should be sure to answer so, and say I had seen them to give an air of truth, and then make some explanation.” “But he would have told you at once that the workmen could not have been there two days before, and that therefore you must have been there on the day of the murder at eight o’clock.
uz: Porfiry, albatta, shunday javob berishim kerak, deb o'ylashi mumkin va men ularni biroz haqiqatni aytishlarini ko'rdim, so'ngra ba'zi tushuntirishlar berdim.  Ammo u sizga ikki kun oldin ishchilar u erda bo'lmasligini, shuning uchun siz o'ldirilgan kuni soat sakkizlarda u erda bo'lishingiz kerakligini darhol aytgan bo'lardi.

en: And so he would have caught you over a detail.” “Yes, that is what he was reckoning on, that I should not have time to reflect, and should be in a hurry to make the most likely answer, and so would forget that the workmen could not have been there two days before.” “But how could you forget it?” “Nothing easier.
uz: Shunday qilib, u sizlarni bir tafsilotdan o'rab olgan bo'lardi.Ha, u shu haqda o'ylagan edi, men mulohaza yuritishga vaqt topmay, eng ehtimoldan yiroq javob berishga shoshilinch bo'lishim kerak edi va ishchilar ikki kun oldin u yerda bo'lmasligini unutgan bo'lar edi. Ammo siz buni qanday unutib qo'yishingiz mumkin edi? Hech narsa oson emas.

en: It is in just such stupid things clever people are most easily caught.
uz: Bunday ahmoqona narsalarda aqlli odamlarni eng oson tutishadi.

en: The more cunning a man is, the less he suspects that he will be caught in a simple thing.
uz: Inson qanchalik hiyla-nayrang bo'lsa, sodda ishda tushib qolishidan shubhalanmas.

en: The more cunning a man is, the simpler the trap he must be caught in.
uz: Inson qanchalik hiyla-nayrang bo'lsa, o'sha qadar tuzoqqa tushishi kerak.

en: Porfiry is not such a fool as you think.
uz: Porfiry siz o'ylagandek ahmoq emas.

en: …” “He is a knave then, if that is so!” Raskolnikov could not help laughing.
uz: ... U o'sha paytda o'g'ir bo'lsa! Raskolnikov kulishdan bosh tortolmadi.

en: But at the very moment, he was struck by the strangeness of his own frankness, and the eagerness with which he had made this explanation, though he had kept up all the preceding conversation with gloomy repulsion, obviously with a motive, from necessity.
uz: Ammo o'sha zahoti u o'zining aniqligi va bu tushuntirishni o'tkazishga tayyor bo'lgan g'ayratidan hayratda qoldi, garchi u o'tgan suhbatni kerakli sababdan nohaqlik bilan davom ettirgan bo'lsa-da.

en: “I am getting a relish for certain aspects!” he thought to himself.
uz: Menga ba'zi jihatlar yoqadi! deb o'yladi u o'ziga.

en: But almost at the same instant he became suddenly uneasy, as though an unexpected and alarming idea had occurred to him.
uz: Ammo deyarli shu zahoti u to'satdan xavotirga tushdi, xuddi kutilmagan va dahshatli bir g'oya kelib qolgan bo'lsa.

en: uneasiness kept on increasing.
uz: Xavfsizlik ko'payib bordi.

en: They had just reached the entrance to Bakaleyev’s.
uz: Ular Bakaleyevlar daryosining kirishi joyida qolishgan edi.

en: “Go in alone!” said Raskolnikov suddenly.
uz: Yeganingda o'zing kir! dedi Raskolnikov to'satdan.

en: “I will be back directly.” “Where are you going?
uz: Men to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qaytaman.  Siz qayerga ketyapsiz?

en: Why, we are just here.” “I can’t help it.
uz: Nega deganda, biz hozirgina keldik.   Men buni qila olmayman.

en: … I will come in half an hour.
uz: Men yarim soat ichida kelaman.

en: Tell them.” “Say what you like, I will come with you.” “You, too, want to torture me!” he screamed, with such bitter irritation, such despair in his eyes that Razumihin’s hands dropped.
uz: Ularga ayt.  Nima xohlasangiz, aytinglar, men siz bilan birga boraman.  Siz ham meni qiynashni xohlaysiz! u shunday achchiq g'azab bilan, ko'zlarida shunday umidsizlik bilan qichqirdiki, Razumihinning qo'llari tushdi.

en: He stood for some time on the steps, looking gloomily at Raskolnikov striding rapidly away in the direction of his lodging.
uz: U bir muncha vaqt qadamlar ustida turdi va Raskolnikovni o'z uyidan tez o'tib ketayotganini qorong'ilik bilan ko'rib turdi.

en: At last, gritting his teeth and clenching his fist, he swore he would squeeze Porfiry like a lemon that very day, and went up the stairs to reassure Pulcheria Alexandrovna, who was by now alarmed at their long absence.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, o'z tishlarini teshib, o'z qo'lini tutib, o'sha kuni Porfirini limon kabi siqishga qasam ichdi va Pulcheria Aleksandrovna uzoq vaqt yo'qligidan xavotirda bo'lgan Pulcheria Aleksandrovnaga tasalli berish uchun daraxtga ko'tarildi.

en: When Raskolnikov got home, his hair was soaked with sweat and he was breathing heavily.
uz: Raskolnikov uyga kelganida, sochlari ter bilan to'lib, og'ir nafas olgan edi.

en: He went rapidly up the stairs, walked into his unlocked room and at once fastened the latch.
uz: U tezda daraxtga ko'tarildi, o'z xonasiga kirdi va darhol qulfni o'rnatdi.

en: Then in senseless terror he rushed to the corner, to that hole under the paper where he had put the things; put his hand in, and for some minutes felt carefully in the hole, in every crack and fold of the paper.
uz: So'ngra u aqlsiz dahshatga to'lib, qo'lini qo'ydigan qog'oz ostida bo'lgan bo'g'iga, burchakga shoshdi va bir necha daqiqa davomida qog'ozning har bir bo'g'riligi va qo'yilishiga diqqat bilan e'tibor qaratdi.

en: Finding nothing, he got up and drew a deep breath.
uz: Hech narsa topmay turib, u turib, chuqur nafas oldi.

en: As he was reaching the steps of Bakaleyev’s, he suddenly fancied that something, a chain, a stud or even a bit of paper in which they had been wrapped with the old woman’s handwriting on it, might somehow have slipped out and been lost in some crack, and then might suddenly turn up as unexpected, conclusive evidence against him.
uz: Bakaleyevlarning qadamlariga yetib borganida, u biroz o'ylab ko'rdiki, biroz narsa, zanjir, bir stut yoki hatto qariya ayolning qo'li yozgan qog'ozlari o'rab olingan qog'oz, qandaydir tarzda chiqib ketib, biron bir oraqqa tushib ketishi mumkin va keyin biroz kutilmagan, aniq dalil sifatida unga qarshi paydo bo'lishi mumkin.

en: He stood as though lost in thought, and a strange, humiliated, half senseless smile strayed on his lips.
uz: U fikrlarida adashib qolganidek turdi va uning og'izlarida g'alati, kamsitilgan, yarim behuda tabassum paydo bo'ldi.

en: He took his cap at last and went quietly out of the room.
uz: Oxir-oqibat u to'pini olib, xonadan xotirjamlik bilan chiqib ketdi.

en: His ideas were all tangled.
uz: Uning barcha g'oyalari o'zaro bog'liq edi.

en: He went dreamily through the gateway.
uz: U orzu bilan darvoza orqali o'tdi.

en: “Here he is himself,” shouted a loud voice.
uz: Mana, u o'zi, baland ovoz bilan baqirib yubordi.

en: The porter was standing at the door of his little room and was pointing him out to a short man who looked like an artisan, wearing a long coat and a waistcoat, and looking at a distance remarkably like a woman.
uz: Cho'pon o'zining kichkina xonasi eshigida turib, uni qisqa bo'lgan, hunarmandga o'xshaydigan, uzun kiyim va kiyim kiygan va ayolga o'xshaydigan qisqa bo'lgan odamga ko'rsatardi.

en: He stooped, and his head in a greasy cap hung forward.
uz: O'zini egib qo'ydi, boshini yog'li to'pka bilan oldinga bog'lab qo'ydi.

en: From his wrinkled flabby face he looked over fifty; his little eyes were lost in fat and they looked out grimly, sternly and discontentedly.
uz: O'zining burqlangan va chiroyli yuzidan u ellikdan oshgan ko'rinardi; uning kichik ko'zlari yog' bilan to'lib-toshgan edi va ular qorong'u, qat'iy va norozilik bilan ko'rinardi.

en: “What is it?” Raskolnikov asked, going up to the porter.
uz: Bu nima? Raskolnikov so'radi, portiyerning oldiga chiqib.

en: The man stole a look at him from under his brows and he looked at him attentively, deliberately; then he turned slowly and went out of the gate into the street without saying a word.
uz: O'sha kishi uning ko'z ostidagi ko'rinishni o'g'irladi va u unga diqqat bilan, qasddan qaradi; so'ngra u sekin o'girilib, darvozaxdan tashqariga chiqib, ko'chaga chiqdi va hech narsa aytmadi.

en: “What is it?” cried Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu nima? Raskolnikov baqirib yubordi.

en: “Why, he there was asking whether a student lived here, mentioned your name and whom you lodged with.
uz: U bu yerda o'quvchi yashaydi-yo'qmi deb so'ragan, sizning ismingizni va kim bilan yashayotganingizni aytib berdi.

en: I saw you coming and pointed you out and he went away.
uz: Men sizni kelayotganini ko'rib, ko'rsatdim va u ketib ketdi.

en: It’s funny.” The porter too seemed rather puzzled, but not much so, and after wondering for a moment he turned and went back to his room.
uz: Bu juda qiziqarli. Porter ham juda g'alati ko'rinardi, lekin shunchalik g'alati ko'rinmadi va bir zum o'ylab ko'rgach, o'girilib o'z xonasiga qaytdi.

en: Raskolnikov ran after the stranger, and at once caught sight of him walking along the other side of the street with the same even, deliberate step with his eyes fixed on the ground, as though in meditation.
uz: Raskolnikov begona kishining orqasidan yugurib ketdi va u darhol uni ko'chadan boshqa tomonga o'tib borayotganini ko'rdi, xuddi o'sha o'sha o'rtacha, qasddan ko'zlarini yerga tikib, xuddi o'ylab yurganidek.

en: He soon overtook him, but for some time walked behind him.
uz: U tezda uni yutib oldi, lekin bir muncha vaqt uning orqasidan yurdi.

en: At last, moving on to a level with him, he looked at his face.
uz: Nihoyat, u o'zi bilan tenglikka o'tgach, o'z yuziga qaradi.

en: The man noticed him at once, looked at him quickly, but dropped his eyes again; and so they walked for a minute side by side without uttering a word.
uz: U odam uni darhol ko'rib, tezda unga qaradi, lekin yana ko'zlarini tushiradi; va ular bir daqiqa davomida bir-biriga yonma-yon yurib, so'z aytmasdan yurishadi.

en: “You were inquiring for me … of the porter?” Raskolnikov said at last, but in a curiously quiet voice.
uz: Siz men uchun ... porterni so'raganmisiz? Raskolnikov oxir-oqibat dedi, ammo g'alati xotirjam ovoz bilan.

en: The man made no answer; he didn’t even look at him.
uz: Odam javob bermadi, hatto unga nazar ham solmadi.

en: Again they were both silent.
uz: Yana ikkalasi ham sukut saqlashdi.

en: “Why do you … come and ask for me … and say nothing.
uz: Nima uchun siz ... kelib mendan so'rab ... hech narsa aytmaysiz?

en: … What’s the meaning of it?” Raskolnikov’s voice broke and he seemed unable to articulate the words clearly.
uz: Raskolnikovning ovozi bo'linib, so'zlarni aniq ifodalay olmaydigan bo'lib ko'rindi.

en: The man raised his eyes this time and turned a gloomy sinister look at Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu safar yigit ko'zlarini ko'tarib, Raskolnikovga qorong'i va yovuz ko'rinishni ko'rsatdi.

en: “Murderer!” he said suddenly in a quiet but clear and distinct voice.
uz: "Qotil!" - dedi u to'satdan sukunatli, ammo aniq va aniq ovoz bilan.

en: Raskolnikov went on walking beside him.
uz: Raskolnikov uning yonida yurib ketdi.

en: His legs felt suddenly weak, a cold shiver ran down his spine, and his heart seemed to stand still for a moment, then suddenly began throbbing as though it were set free.
uz: Uning oyoqlari to'satdan zaif bo'lib qoldi, cho'qqisida sovuq titroq bor edi, yuragi bir muncha vaqt to'xtab turardi, keyin to'satdan u erkin bo'lganidek urishni boshladi.

en: So they walked for about a hundred paces, side by side in silence.
uz: Shunday qilib, ular yuz qadam yurib, bir-biriga qo'shilib, xotirjamlik bilan yurishdi.

en: The man did not look at him.
uz: Bu kishi unga qaramasdi.

en: “What do you mean … what is.
uz: Siz nimani nazarda tutyapsiz ... nima.

en: … Who is a murderer?” muttered Raskolnikov hardly audibly.
uz: ... Kim qotil? Raskolnikov o'z so'zidan eshitib bo'lmaydi.

en: “You are a murderer,” the man answered still more articulately and emphatically, with a smile of triumphant hatred, and again he looked straight into Raskolnikov’s pale face and stricken eyes.
uz: "Sen qotilsan", - deb javob berdi u kishi yanada aniq va qat'iy tarzda, g'azabga to'lib-toshgan tabassum bilan, yana Raskolnikovning rang-barang yuziga va ko'zlariga to'g'ri qaradi.

en: They had just reached the crossroads.
uz: Ular yo'l chekkasigacha yetib kelishgan edi.

en: The man turned to the left without looking behind him.
uz: U o'z orqasidan qaramasdan chap tomon o'girilibdi.

en: Raskolnikov remained standing, gazing after him.
uz: Raskolnikov turib, uning orqasidan qarab turdi.

en: He saw him turn round fifty paces away and look back at him still standing there.
uz: U uni 50 qadam uzoqroq o'girib, o'sha yerda turganini ko'rdi.

en: Raskolnikov could not see clearly, but he fancied that he was again smiling the same smile of cold hatred and triumph.
uz: Raskolnikov aniq ko'ra olmagan, lekin u yana bir bor sovuq nafrat va g'alaba tabassumini ko'rib, tabassum qilayotganini his qilgan.

en: With slow faltering steps, with shaking knees, Raskolnikov made his way back to his little garret, feeling chilled all over.
uz: Raskolnikov sekin-sekin harakatlanib, tiz cho'kkancha qadamlar qo'yib, o'zining kichkinagina qovurg'iga qaytib keldi. O'zini hamma joyda sovuq his qildi.

en: He took off his cap and put it on the table, and for ten minutes he stood without moving.
uz: O'z qo'pini olib, stol ustiga qo'ydi va o'n daqiqa davomida harakatlanmasdan turdi.

en: Then he sank exhausted on the sofa and with a weak moan of pain he stretched himself on it.
uz: Keyin u sofa ustida charchagan holda bo'lib, og'riqdan zaif qayg'urib, o'zini unga uzatib qo'ydi.

en: So he lay for half an hour.
uz: Shunday qilib, u yarim soat uxladi.

en: He thought of nothing.
uz: U hech narsa haqida o'ylamagan.

en: Some thoughts or fragments of thoughts, some images without order or coherence floated before his mind — faces of people he had seen in his childhood or met somewhere once, whom he would never have recalled, the belfry of the church at V — —, the billiard table in a restaurant and some officers playing billiards, the smell of cigars in some underground tobacco shop, a tavern room, a back staircase quite dark, all sloppy with dirty water and strewn with eggshells, and the Sunday bells floating in from somewhere.
uz: Ba'zi fikrlar yoki fikrlar parchalari, tartibsiz yoki bir-biriga mos kelmaydigan tasvirlar uning ongida ko'tarib turardi  bolaligida ko'rgan yoki bir marta bir joyda uchrashgan odamlarning yuzlari, ular hech qachon esga olinmagan, V  dagi cherkovning qo'ng'iroq to'pori, restorandagi bilyarda stol va ba'zi ofitserlar bilyarda o'ynashgan, yer ostidagi tamaki do'konidagi sigarlarning shiori, taverna xonasi, juda qorong'i orqa turar joy, bularning barchasi nopok suv va tuxum qo'llari bilan to'ldirilgan, yakshanba qo'ng'iroqlari bir joydan ko'tarib kelayotgan.

en: … The images followed one another, whirling like a hurricane.
uz: ... Rasmlar bir-birini orqaga surib, to'qnashgan bo'lib turadi.

en: Some of them he liked and tried to clutch at, but they faded and all the while there was an oppression within him, but it was not overwhelming, sometimes it was even pleasant.
uz: Ba'zilarini yaxshi ko'rgan va o'zlariga bog'lanib turishga harakat qilgan, lekin ular o'z-o'zidan o'tib ketdi va u ichidagi zulm o'sib borardi, ammo bu juda ko'p bo'lmagan, ba'zan hatto yoqimli bo'lgan.

en: … The slight shivering still persisted, but that too was an almost pleasant sensation.
uz: Ozgina titrash hali ham davom etdi, ammo bu ham deyarli yoqimli his edi.

en: He heard the hurried footsteps of Razumihin; he closed his eyes and pretended to be asleep.
uz: U Razumihinning shoshilinch qadamlarini eshitdi; ko'zlarini yopdi va uxlayotganini ko'rsatdi.

en: Razumihin opened the door and stood for some time in the doorway as though hesitating, then he stepped softly into the room and went cautiously to the sofa.
uz: Razumihin eshikni ochib, bir muncha vaqt eshikda turibdi, xuddi shubha qilgandek, so'ngra xonadonga sekin kirib, ehtiyotkorlik bilan sofaga bordi.

en: Raskolnikov heard Nastasya’s whisper: “Don’t disturb him!
uz: Raskolnikov Nastasyasning: "Uni bezovta qilmanglar!" - deb g'ayratini eshitdi.

en: He can have his dinner later.” “Quite so,” answered Razumihin.
uz: U kechki ovqatni keyinroq o'tkazishi mumkin.  Quyida, Razumihin javob berdi.

en: Both withdrew carefully and closed the door.
uz: Ikkalasi ham ehtiyotkorlik bilan orqaga chiqib, eshikni yopishdi.

en: Another half-hour passed.
uz: Yana bir yarim soat o'tdi.

en: Raskolnikov opened his eyes, turned on his back again, clasping his hands behind his head.
uz: Raskolnikov ko'zlarini ochib, yana orqaga burildi va qo'llarini bosh orqasidan tutib oldi.

en: Who is that man who sprang out of the earth?
uz: Yerdan chiqqani kim?

en: Where was he, what did he see?
uz: Qayerda edi, nima ko'rgan?

en: He has seen it all, that’s clear.
uz: U hamma narsani ko'rgan, bu aniq.

en: And from where did he see?
uz: Va qayerdan ko'rdi?

en: Why has he only now sprung out of the earth?
uz: Nima uchun u yerdan hozirgina paydo bo'ldi?

en: And how could he see?
uz: Va qanday qilib u ko'ra oladi?

en: Hm …” continued Raskolnikov, turning cold and shivering, “and the jewel case Nikolay found behind the door —was that possible?
uz: Raskolnikov sovuq va titraydigan holda davom etdi va Nikolay eshik ortida topgan marvaridlar qutisi mumkinmi?

en: You miss an infinitesimal line and you can build it into a pyramid of evidence!
uz: Siz cheksiz kichik chiziqni o'tkazib yuborasiz va uni dalillar piramidasiga aylantirasiz!

en: A fly flew by and saw it!
uz: Bir uchuv uchib o'tibdi va uni ko'rdi!

en: Is it possible?” He felt with sudden loathing how weak, how physically weak he had become.
uz: Bu mumkinmi? O'zi qanchalik zaif, qanchalik jismoniy zaif bo'lganini birdan nafratlanib his qildi.

en: “I ought to have known it,” he thought with a bitter smile.
uz: "Men buni bilishim kerak edi", - deb o'yladi u achchiq tabassum bilan.

en: “And how dared I, knowing myself, knowing how I should be, take up an axe and shed blood!
uz: O'zimni bilgan, qanday bo'lishim kerakligini bilgan holda, o'zimning o'zimni bilgan holda, o'g'limni o'g'irlab, qon to'kishga qanday jasorat qilganman!

en: I ought to have known beforehand.
uz: Men buni oldindan bilishim kerak edi.

en: … Ah, but I did know!” he whispered in despair.
uz: Ah, lekin men bilardim! u umidsizlikka tushib shovqin qildi.

en: At times he came to a standstill at some thought.
uz: Ba'zan u o'zi haqida o'ylab to'xtadi.

en: “No, those men are not made so.
uz: Yo'q, bu odamlar bunday emaslar.

en: The real Master to whom all is permitted storms Toulon, makes a massacre in Paris, forgets an army in Egypt, wastes half a million men in the Moscow expedition and gets off with a jest at Vilna.
uz: Toulonni to'qnashtirgan, Parijda qirg'inchilik sodir etgan, Misrda armiyani unutgan, Moskva ekspeditsiyasida yarim million kishini yo'qotgan va Vilnada mayda-mayda o'tirgan haqiqiy usta.

en: And altars are set up to him after his death, and so all is permitted.
uz: Va uning o'limidan keyin unga qurbongohlar qurilgan, shuning uchun hamma narsa ruxsat etiladi.

en: No, such people, it seems, are not of flesh but of bronze!” One sudden irrelevant idea almost made him laugh.
uz: Yo'q, bunday odamlar go'sht emas, balki bronza! Birdan bir ahamiyatsiz g'oya uni deyarli kulishga undagan.

en: Napoleon, the pyramids, Waterloo, and a wretched skinny old woman, a pawnbroker with a red trunk under her bed —it’s a nice hash for Porfiry Petrovitch to digest!
uz: Napoleon, piramidalar, Waterloo, va ahvolga tushmagan salqin keksa ayol, yotoq ostidagi qizil trunk bilan sovg'a beruvchi pul beruvchi ayol Porfiry Petrovitch uchun yoqimli hashdir!

en: How can they digest it!
uz: Qanday qilib ular uni sindirishlari mumkin!

en: It’s too inartistic.
uz: Bu juda san'atkor emas.

en: “A Napoleon creep under an old woman’s bed!
uz: Napoleon keksa ayolning yotoq ostiga kiradi!

en: Ugh, how loathsome!” At moments he felt he was raving.
uz: Uff, naqadar jirkanch! Ba'zida u o'zini g'azablanayotgan his qilgan.

en: He sank into a state of feverish excitement.
uz: U o'zini qizg'in hayajon hissi bilan ko'tardi.

en: “The old woman is of no consequence,” he thought, hotly and incoherently.
uz: Qariya ayol hech qanday ahamiyatga ega emas, deb o'yladi u, qizg'in va bir-biriga zid.

en: “The old woman was a mistake perhaps, but she is not what matters!
uz: Keksa ayol xatoga yo'l qo'ygan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin u muhim emas!

en: The old woman was only an illness.
uz: Qariya ayol faqat kasallik edi.

en: … I was in a hurry to overstep.
uz: ... Men o'tish uchun shoshildim.

en: … I didn’t kill a human being, but a principle!
uz: Men insonni emas, balki prinsipni o'ldirganman!

en: I killed the principle, but I didn’t overstep, I stopped on this side.
uz: Men prinsipni o'ldirganman, lekin o'tmay, bu tomondan to'xtab qoldim.

en: … I was only capable of killing.
uz: Men faqatgina o'ldirishga qodir edim.

en: And it seems I wasn’t even capable of that … Principle?
uz: Va shunga o'xshab, men hatto bu prinsipga qodir emasdim.

en: Why was that fool Razumihin abusing the socialists?
uz: Nima uchun bu aqlsiz Razumihin sotsialistlarni suiiste'mol qilmoqda edi?

en: They are industrious, commercial people; ‘the happiness of all’ is their case.
uz: Ular mehnatsevar, tijoratkor odamlardir; ularning misoli - hamma baxtlidir.

en: No, life is only given to me once and I shall never have it again; I don’t want to wait for ‘the happiness of all.’ I want to
uz: Yo'q, hayot menga bir marta beriladi va men uni boshqa hech qachon olmayman; men hamma baxtli bo'lishini kutishni istamayman.

en: live myself, or else better not live at all.
uz: O'zim yashayman yoki umuman yashamayman.

en: I simply couldn’t pass by my mother starving, keeping my rouble in my pocket while I waited for the ‘happiness of all.’ I am putting my little brick into the happiness of all and so my heart is at peace.
uz: Men shunchaki onamning och qolganidan o'tib o'tolmasdim, hamma baxtini kutganimda, rublimni kiyimimda saqlab turardim. Men o'zimning kichkina tikanimni hammaning baxtiga qo'yyapman va shuning uchun yuragim xotirjam bo'ldi.

en: Why have you let me slip?
uz: Nima uchun meni qo'yib yubordingiz?

en: I only live once, I too want.
uz: Men faqat bir marta yashayman, men ham xohlayman.

en: … Ech, I am an aesthetic louse and nothing more,” he added suddenly, laughing like a madman.
uz: ... Men estetik qo'rqinchman va boshqa hech narsa emasman, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u to'satdan, aqldan ozgan kishi kabi kulish bilan.

en: “Yes, I am certainly a louse,” he went on, clutching at the idea, gloating over it and playing with it with vindictive pleasure.
uz: "Ha, men chindan ham bo'g'izman", - deb davom etdi u, g'oyaga qo'l urib, undan xursand bo'lib, qasos olish zavq bilan o'ynaydi.

en: “In the first place, because I can reason that I am one, and secondly, because for a month past I have been troubling benevolent Providence, calling it to witness that not for my own fleshly lusts did I undertake it, but with a grand and noble object —ha-ha!
uz: Birinchidan, men o'zimni o'zim deb hisoblayman va ikkinchidan, o'tgan bir oy davomida mehribon Parvardigorlikni xafa qilib, uni o'z tana istaklarim uchun emas, balki buyuk va buyuk maqsad bilan amalga oshirganimga guvohlik berishga chaqiraman. ha-ha!

en: Thirdly, because I aimed at carrying it out as justly as possible, weighing, measuring and calculating.
uz: Uchinchidan, men uni iloji boricha adolatli ravishda o'lchashga harakat qilardim, uning o'lchami, o'lchami va hisob-kitobini o'lchashga harakat qilardim.

en: Of all the lice I picked out the most useless one and proposed to take from her only as much as I needed for the first step, no more nor less (so the rest would have gone to a monastery, according to her will, ha-ha!).
uz: Barcha qushlardan men eng foydasizni tanlab, undan birinchi qadam uchun kerak bo'lgan miqdorni olishni taklif qildim, ko'proq ham, kam ham emas (shuning uchun qolganlari uning vasiyatiga ko'ra, monastirga borgan bo'lishadi, ha-ha!).

en: And what shows that I am utterly a louse,” he added, grinding his teeth, “is that I am perhaps viler and more loathsome than the louse I killed, and I felt beforehand that I should tell myself so after killing her.
uz: Va men mutlaqo bo'g'iz ekanligimni ko'rsatadigan narsa, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u, tishlarini tishlab, - bu men o'ldirgan bo'g'izdan ham ko'ra ko'proq yomon va jirkanch ekanligimdir va uni o'ldirganimdan keyin o'zimga shunday aytishim kerakligini oldindan his qildim.

en: Can anything be compared with the horror of that?
uz: Bu dahshatga hech narsa teng kela oladimi?

en: I understand the ‘prophet’ with his sabre, on his steed: Allah commands and ‘trembling’ creation must obey!
uz: Men o'z qilichidan, o'z qo'llari bilan payg'ambarni tushunib yetaman: Alloh buyuradi va dahshatli mavjudot itoat qilishi kerak!

en: The ‘prophet’ is right, he is right when he sets a battery across the street and blows up the innocent and the guilty without deigning to explain!
uz: Paygʻambar haqli, u koʻchaga batareya qoʻyib, aybdor va aybdorlarni tushuntirib berishga harakat qilmasdan, oʻsha yerda koʻchadan burib tashlaganida haqli!

en: It’s for you to obey, trembling creation, and not to have desires, for that’s not for you!
uz: Bu siz uchun emas, balki titrab turgan ijodga bo'ysunish va istaklarga ega bo'lmaslik uchun!

en: … I shall never, never forgive the old woman!” His hair was soaked with sweat, his quivering lips were parched, his eyes were fixed on the ceiling.
uz: Men hech qachon, hech qachon keksa ayolga kechirim bermayman! Uning sochlari ter bilan to'lib-toshgan edi, titraydigan dudasi quruq edi, ko'zlari tomonga tiklangan edi.

en: “Mother, sister —how I loved them!
uz: Onam, singlim Men ularni qanchalik yaxshi ko'rdim!

en: Why do I hate them now?
uz: Nima uchun men ulardan hozir nafratlanaman?

en: Yes, I hate them, I feel a physical hatred for them, I can’t bear them near me.
uz: Ha, men ulardan nafratlanaman, ularga nisbatan jismoniy nafratim bor, ularni yonimda ko'tarib o'tirolmayman.

en: … I went up to my mother and kissed her, I remember.
uz: ... Onamning oldiga borib, uni o'pdim, eslayman.

en: … To embrace her and think if she only knew … shall I tell her then?
uz: Uni quchoqlab, o'ylab ko'rishim kerakki, agar u bilsa, men unga aytamanmi?

en: That’s just what I might do.
uz: Men aynan shunday qilishim mumkin.

en: … She must be the same as I am,” he added, straining himself to think, as it were struggling with delirium.
uz: ... U men singari bo'lishi kerak, - deb qo'shimcha qildi u, o'zini o'ylab ko'rishga harakat qilib, xuddi delirium bilan kurashayotgan bo'lgani kabi.

en: “Ah, how I hate the old woman now!
uz: Ah, men endi keksa ayoldan qanchalik nafratlanaman!

en: I feel I should kill her again if she came to life!
uz: Agar u tirilsa, uni yana o'ldirishim kerakligini his qilaman!

en: Why did she come in?
uz: Nega u kirdi?

en: … It’s strange though, why
uz: Ammo bu g'alati, nima uchun?

en: is it I scarcely ever think of her, as though I hadn’t killed her?
uz: Uni o'ldirmaganim kabi, men deyarli hech qachon unga e'tibor bermayapmanmi?

en: Poor gentle things, with gentle eyes.
uz: Yomon muloyim narsalar, muloyim ko'zlar bilan.

en: Why don’t they weep?
uz: Nega ular yig'lamaydilar?

en: Why don’t they moan?
uz: Nima uchun ular nolmaydilar?

en: They give up everything … their eyes are soft and gentle.
uz: Ular hamma narsadan voz kechadilar ... ko'zlari yumshak va mehribon.

en: Gentle Sonia!” He lost consciousness; it seemed strange to him that he didn’t remember how he got into the street.
uz: Janob Sonia! U ongini yo'qotib qo'ydi; ko'chaga qanday tushib qolganini eslay olmasligi unga g'alati tuyuldi.

en: It was late evening.
uz: Kechqurun kech edi.

en: The twilight had fallen and the full moon was shining more and more brightly; but there was a peculiar breathlessness in the air.
uz: Quyosh tushdi va to'liq oy ko'proq yorug'lik bilan parlashdi; lekin havoda o'zgacha nafassizlik bor edi.

en: There were crowds of people in the street; workmen and business people were making their way home; other people had come out for a walk; there was a smell of mortar, dust and stagnant water.
uz: Ko'chada ko'p odamlar bor edi; ishchilar va ishbilarmonlar uylariga qaytib ketayotgan edilar; boshqa odamlar piyoda bo'lish uchun chiqqan edilar; mortar, chang va to'xtab turgan suvning hidini his qilar edilar.

en: Raskolnikov walked along, mournful and anxious; he was distinctly aware of having come out with a purpose, of having to do something in a hurry, but what it was he had forgotten.
