uz: Raskolnikov qayg'u va tashvish bilan yurib ketdi; u maqsadga ko'ra chiqqanini, shoshilinch bir ishni bajarishga majbur bo'lganini aniq bilgan edi, ammo nima ekanligini unutib qo'ygan edi.

en: Suddenly he stood still and saw a man standing on the other side of the street, beckoning to him.
uz: Toʻsatdan u toʻxtab turdi va koʻchadan boshqa tomonda turgan bir odamni koʻrdi.

en: He crossed over to him, but at once the man turned and walked away with his head hanging, as though he had made no sign to him.
uz: U uning yonidan o'tib ketdi, lekin u darhol o'girilib, boshini asrab, xuddi unga hech qanday ish ko'rsatmaganidek ketdi.

en: “Stay, did he really beckon?” Raskolnikov wondered, but he tried to overtake him.
uz: Stay, u haqiqatan ham chaqirdi? Raskolnikov o'zini o'ylab ko'rdi, lekin u uni orqaga surishga harakat qildi.

en: When he was within ten paces he recognised him and was frightened; it was the same man with stooping shoulders in the long coat.
uz: U o'n qadam yaqinida bo'lganida uni tanib, qo'rqib ketdi; bu o'sha uzun kiyimda bo'lgan, ko'tarib turgan yelkalarini egib yurgan kishi edi.

en: Raskolnikov followed him at a distance; his heart was beating; they went down a turning; the man still did not look round.
uz: Raskolnikov uzoqdan uning orqasidan ergashib borardi; uning yuragi urib borardi; ular bir burchakga tushdilar; u kishi hali ham atrofini ko'rmadi.

en: “Does he know I am following him?” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: ¿U uning orqasidan ergashayotganimni biladimi? Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: The man went into the gateway of a big house.
uz: U odam katta uyning darvozalariga kirdi.

en: Raskolnikov hastened to the gate and looked in to see whether he would look round and sign to him.
uz: Raskolnikov darvoza tomon yugurib kirib, atrofga qarab, unga imzo qo'yadi-yo'qligini ko'rdi.

en: In the courtyard the man did turn round and again seemed to beckon him.
uz: Xonadonda u odam o'zini o'zgartirdi va yana uni chaqirtirib yubordi.

en: Raskolnikov at once followed him into the yard, but the man was gone.
uz: Raskolnikov darhol uning orqasidan hovliga kirdi, lekin u odam yo'q edi.

en: He must have gone up the first staircase.
uz: U birinchi darajadagi mertaga chiqqan bo'lishi kerak.

en: Raskolnikov rushed after him.
uz: Raskolnikov uning orqasidan shoshdi.

en: He heard slow measured steps two flights above.
uz: U ikki qavatdan yuqori bo'lgan sekin o'lchanadigan qadamlarni eshitdi.

en: The staircase seemed strangely familiar.
uz: Turg'alar o'zgacha tanish tuyulgan.

en: He reached the window on the first floor; the moon shone through the panes with a melancholy and mysterious light; then he reached the second floor.
uz: U birinchi qavatdagi derazaga yetib keldi; oy o'rindiqlar orqali melanxolis va sirli nur bilan porladi; so'ngra ikkinchi qavatga yetib keldi.

en: this is the flat where the painters were at work … but how was it he did not recognise it at once?
uz: Bu rasmchilarning ishlagan xonasi... lekin qanday qilib u uni birdan tan olmagan?

en: The steps of the man above had died away.
uz: Yuqoridagi odamning qadamlari o'lib ketgan edi.

en: “So he must have stopped or hidden somewhere.” He reached the third storey, should he go on?
uz: Shunday qilib, u to'xtab qolgan yoki qaerda o'zini yashirgan bo'lishi kerak. U uchinchi qavatga yetib, davom etishi kerakmi?

en: There was a stillness that was
uz: Bu yerda tinchlik hukm surgan.

en: The sound of his own footsteps scared and frightened him.
uz: O'z qadamlarining ovozi uni qo'rqitdi va qo'rqitdi.

en: The man must be hiding in some corner here.
uz: Bu odam shu burchada yashiringan bo'lishi kerak.

en: the flat was standing wide open, he hesitated and went in.
uz: Xonadon keng ochilgan edi, u shubha ostiga olib, ichkariga kirdi.

en: It was very dark and empty in the passage, as though everything had been removed; he crept on tiptoe into the parlour which was flooded with moonlight.
uz: Yo'lda juda qorong'i va bo'sh edi, xuddi hamma narsa olib tashlangan bo'lgandek; u oy yorug'ligi bilan to'lib-toshgan salonga oyoq boshiga kirdi.

en: Everything there was as before, the chairs, the looking-glass, the yellow sofa and the pictures in the frames.
uz: Hamma narsa avvalgidek edi: o'rindiqlar, ko'rinma, sariq sofa va ramkalardagi rasmlar.

en: A huge, round, copper-red moon looked in at the windows.
uz: Ulkan, davraliy, mis qizil oy darchalarga qaradi.

en: “It’s the moon that makes it so still, weaving some mystery,” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: Ayni shu qadar susaytiradi, bu sirni o'zgartiradi, deb o'yladi Raskolnikov.

en: He stood and waited, waited a long while, and the more silent the moonlight, the more violently his heart beat, till it was painful.
uz: U to'xtadi va kutdi, uzoq vaqt kutdi va oy nurlari qanchalik sust bo'lsa, yuragi shunchalik qattiq urib, og'ir bo'ldi.

en: And still the same hush.
uz: Va hali ham xuddi shu hushyorlik.

en: Suddenly he heard a momentary sharp crack like the snapping of a splinter and all was still again.
uz: Toʻsatdan u biroz oʻtkir boʻlakni eshitdi va hamma narsa yana toʻxtadi.

en: A fly flew up suddenly and struck the window pane with a plaintive buzz.
uz: Birdan bir uchuv uchib, darcha panjaralariga shovqin tovush bilan urdi.

en: At that moment he noticed in the corner between the window and the little cupboard something like a cloak hanging on the wall.
uz: O'sha paytda u darcha va kichik ombor o'rtasidagi burchada devorga osilgan qopqoqqa o'xshaydigan bir narsani ko'rdi.

en: “Why is that cloak here?” he thought, “it wasn’t there before.
uz: Nima uchun bu qopqog'i bu yerda? - deb o'yladi u, - avval u yerda yo'q edi.

en: …” He went up to it quietly and felt that there was someone hiding behind it.
uz: ... U xotirjamlik bilan uning orqasidan bordi va uning orqasida kimdir yashirinayotganini his qildi.

en: He cautiously moved the cloak and saw, sitting on a chair in the corner, the old woman bent double so that he couldn’t see her face; but it was she.
uz: U ehtiyotkorlik bilan ko'ylakni ko'tardi va burchakdagi o'rindiqda o'tirgan keksa ayolning yuzini ko'rmasligi uchun ikki marta egrilib ketayotganini ko'rdi; lekin u o'sha ayol edi.

en: “She is afraid,” he thought.
uz: U qo'rqadi, deb o'yladi.

en: He stealthily took the axe from the noose and struck her one blow, then another on the skull.
uz: Oʻz-oʻzidan pichoqni tortib olib, qizga bir marta urib, yana boshpanaga uribdi.

en: But strange to say she did not stir, as though she were made of wood.
uz: Ammo u harakatlanmaganini aytish ajablanarli, xuddi yog'ochdan yasalgan bo'lgani kabi.

en: He was frightened, bent down nearer and tried to look at her; but she, too, bent her head lower.
uz: U qo'rqib, yaqinroq yerga yiqilib, unga qarashga harakat qildi, lekin u ham boshini pastga tikdi.

en: He bent right down to the ground and peeped up into her face from below, he peeped and turned cold with horror: the old woman was sitting and laughing, shaking with noiseless laughter, doing her utmost that he should not hear it.
uz: U yerga yiqilib, uning yuziga pastdan qarab, qo'rqinchli ko'rinishda qarib ketdi: keksa ayol o'tirib, kulishardi, ovozsiz kulish bilan titrab, uni eshitmaslik uchun hamma narsani qildi.

en: Suddenly he fancied that the door from the bedroom was opened a little and that there was laughter and whispering within.
uz: Toʻsatdan u yotoq xonasi eshigining biroz ochilganini va ichkarida kulgi va shoshib ketayotganini his qildi.

en: He was overcome with frenzy and he began hitting the old woman on the head with all his force, but at every blow of the axe the laughter and whispering from the bedroom grew louder and the old woman was simply shaking with mirth.
uz: U g'azabga to'lib, keksa ayolning boshini butun kuch bilan urishni boshladi, lekin har bir o'qilganda yotoqxonadan tabassum va shovqinlar kuchayib borardi va keksa ayol shunchaki quvonchdan titrab turardi.

en: He was rushing away, but the passage was full of people, the doors of the flats stood open and on the landing, on the stairs and everywhere below there were people, rows of heads, all looking, but huddled
uz: U darrov ketayotgan edi, lekin yo'l odamlarga to'lib-toshgan edi, xonadonlar eshiklari ochiq edi va jo'natishda, mertabanlarda va pastdagi hamma joyda odamlar, boshlar qatorida, hamma ko'z o'ngida, lekin to'p-to'p bo'lgan edi

en: together in silence and expectation.
uz: Shoshilish va kutib turishda birgalikda.

en: Something gripped his heart, his legs were rooted to the spot, they would not move.
uz: Bir narsa uning yuragini ushlab qoldi, oyoqlari o'z-o'zidan o'rnidan o'rnidan o'rnidan o'tmadi.

en: … He tried to scream and woke up.
uz: U qichqirib turishga harakat qildi va uyg'ondi.

en: He drew a deep breath —but his dream seemed strangely to persist: his door was flung open and a man whom he had never seen stood in the doorway watching him intently.
uz: U chuqur nafas oldi, lekin uning orzuining davom etishi g'alati tuyuldi: eshik ochiq edi va u hech qachon ko'rmagan kishi eshikda turib uni diqqat bilan kuzatib turardi.

en: Raskolnikov had hardly opened his eyes and he instantly closed them again.
uz: Raskolnikov deyarli ko'zlarini ochib, darhol ularni yana yopdi.

en: He lay on his back without stirring.
uz: U o'z orqasida yonboshlagan, hech qanday harakat qilmagan.

en: “Is it still a dream?” he wondered and again raised his eyelids hardly perceptibly; the stranger was standing in the same place, still watching him.
uz: Bu hali ham tushmi? u o'zini o'ylab ko'rdi va yana ko'z qo'lqoplarini ko'rinmas darajada ko'tardi; begona kishi xuddi shu joyda turib, uni kuzatib turardi.

en: He stepped cautiously into the room, carefully closing the door after him, went up to the table, paused a moment, still keeping his eyes on Raskolnikov, and noiselessly seated himself on the chair by the sofa; he put his hat on the floor beside him and leaned his hands on his cane and his chin on his hands.
uz: U ehtiyotkorlik bilan xonaga kirdi, eshikni diqqat bilan yopdi, o'zidan keyin stolga chiqdi, Raskolnikovni ko'rib turib, biroz to'xtadi va sofani qo'yib o'tirdi; chappasini yonidagi qavatga qo'ydi va qo'llarini cho'g'iga, cho'qqisini qo'llariga tikdi.

en: It was evident that he was prepared to wait indefinitely.
uz: U cheksiz vaqtni kutishga tayyor ekanligi aniq edi.

en: As far as Raskolnikov could make out from his stolen glances, he was a man no longer young, stout, with a full, fair, almost whitish beard.
uz: Raskolnikov o'g'irlangan ko'rinishlaridan ko'rinib turganidek, u endi yosh emas, kuchli, to'liq, adolatli, deyarli oq rangli sakkizi bo'lgan odam edi.

en: It was still light, but beginning to get dusk.
uz: Hali yorug' edi, lekin tun boshlangandi.

en: There was complete stillness in the room.
uz: Xonada to'liq tinchlik hukm surdi.

en: Not a sound came from the stairs.
uz: Sotuvlardan hech qanday tovush kelmadi.

en: Only a big fly buzzed and fluttered against the window pane.
uz: Faqatgina katta bir cho'g'ir darcha tomoniga qarshi shov-shuv qildi.

en: It was unbearable at last.
uz: Oxir-oqibat bu ko'ngilsizlik edi.

en: Raskolnikov suddenly got up and sat on the sofa.
uz: Raskolnikov to'satdan turib, sofaga o'tirdi.

en: “Come, tell me what you want.” “I knew you were not asleep, but only pretending,” the stranger answered oddly, laughing calmly.
uz: Kel, nima xohlayotganingni ayt.  Men bilgan edimki, sen uxlamaysan, faqatgina o'zingizni ko'rsatyapsan, yadigan kishi g'alati javob berib, tinchlik bilan kuldi.

en: “Arkady Ivanovitch Svidrigaïlov, allow me to introduce myself.
uz: Arkady Ivanovitch Svidrigailov, menga o'zimni tanishtirishga ruxsat bering.

en: I “Can this be still a dream?” Raskolnikov thought once more.
uz: Bu hali ham orzu bo'lishi mumkinmi? - deb o'yladi Raskolnikov yana bir bor.

en: He looked carefully and suspiciously at the unexpected visitor.
uz: U kutilmagan mehmonni ehtiyotkorlik va shubha bilan ko'rdi.

en: It can’t be!” he said at last aloud in bewilderment.
uz: Bu mumkin emas! - dedi u nihoyat g'alati ovozda.

en: His visitor did not seem at all surprised at this exclamation.
uz: Uning tashrif buyuruvchisi bu hayqiriqdan umuman ajablanib ko'rinmagan.

en: “I’ve come to you for two reasons.
uz: Men sizlarning oldingizga ikki sabab bilan keldim.

en: In the first place, I wanted to make your personal acquaintance, as I have already heard a great deal about you that is interesting and flattering; secondly, I cherish the hope that you may not refuse to assist me in a matter directly concerning the welfare of your sister, Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Birinchidan, men siz bilan shaxsan tanishishni xohladim, chunki men siz haqingizda qiziqarli va xushmuomala bo'lgan ko'plab narsalarni eshitganman; ikkinchidan, siz singlingiz Avdotya Romanovnaning farovonligiga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri taalluqli masalalarda menga yordam berishni rad etmasligingizni umid qilaman.

en: For without your support she might not let me come near her now, for she is prejudiced against me, but with your assistance I reckon on  …” “You reckon wrongly,” interrupted Raskolnikov.
uz: Chunki sizning qo'llab-quvvatlashingiz bo'lmaganda, u menga hozir unga yaqinlashishga ruxsat bermasligi mumkin, chunki u menga nisbatan yuzxotirchilik qilmoqda, lekin sizning yordamingiz bilan men ...Siz noto'g'ri fikrda ekansiz, Raskolnikov meni uzdi.

en: “They only arrived yesterday, may I ask you?” Raskolnikov made no reply.
uz: Ular faqat kecha keldi, sizga so'rasam bo'ladimi? Raskolnikov hech qanday javob bermadi.

en: “It was yesterday, I know.
uz: Bu kecha edi, bilaman.

en: I only arrived myself the day before.
uz: O'zim bir kun oldin kelganman.

en: Well, let me tell you this, Rodion Romanovitch, I don’t consider it necessary to justify myself, but kindly tell me what was there particularly criminal on my part in all this business, speaking without prejudice, with common sense?” Raskolnikov continued to look at him in silence.
uz: Xo'sh, sizga shuni aytaman, Rodion Romanovitch, men o'zimni oqlash kerak deb o'ylamayman, lekin bu ishda men nima uchun juda jinoiy bo'lganimni, yuzxotirchilik qilmasdan, oqilona gapirganimni ayting. Raskolnikov unga sekin qarab turdi.

en: “That in my own house I persecuted a defenceless girl and ‘insulted her with my infamous proposals’ —is that it?
uz: O'z uyimda o'zim himoyasiz qizni quvg'in qilib, o'z mashhur takliflarim bilan uni haqoratlaganimni ¿U shundaymi?

en: (I am anticipating you.) But you’ve only to assume that I, too, am a man et nihil humanum … in a word, that I am capable of being attracted and falling in love (which does not depend on our will), then everything
uz: Ammo siz faqat men ham inson va nihil humanum ekanligimni tasavvur qilishingiz kerak ... bir so'z bilan aytganda, men o'zimni jalb qilishga va o'zimni sevishga qodir ekanligimni (bu bizning xohishimizga bog'liq emas) tasavvur qilishingiz kerak.

en: can be explained in the most natural manner.
uz: Bu holatni eng tabiiy tarzda tushuntirish mumkin.

en: The question is, am I a monster, or am I myself a victim?
uz: Savol shundaki, men hayvondammi yoki o'zim qurbon bo'ldimmi?

en: And what if I am a victim?
uz: Agar men qurbon bo'lsam nima bo'ladi?

en: In proposing to the object of my passion to elope with me to America or Switzerland, I may have cherished the deepest respect for her and may have thought that I was promoting our mutual happiness!
uz: O'zimning ishtiyoqimning maqsadiga Amerika yoki Shveytsariyaga men bilan qochib ketishni taklif qilishda men unga chuqur hurmat ko'rsatgan bo'lsam kerak va o'zimning o'zaro baxtimizni oshirishni nazarda tutgan bo'lsam kerak!

en: Reason is the slave of passion, you know; why, probably, I was doing more harm to myself than anyone!” “But that’s not the point,” Raskolnikov interrupted with disgust.
uz: Aql - aql - ehtirosning qulidir, bilasiz; nima uchun, ehtimol, men o'zimga har kimdan ko'ra ko'proq zarar yetkazganman! Ammo bu o'sha narsa emas, Raskolnikov jirkanchlik bilan to'xtatdi.

en: “It’s simply that whether you are right or wrong, we dislike you.
uz: Bu shunchaki siz haq yoki noto'g'ri bo'lishingizdan qat'iy nazar, biz sizni yoqtirmaymiz.

en: We don’t want to have anything to do with you.
uz: Biz siz bilan hech qanday aloqasi bo'lishni istamaymiz.

en: We show you the door.
uz: Biz sizga eshikni ko'rsatamiz.

en: Go out!” Svidrigaïlov broke into a sudden laugh.
uz: Chiqaring! Svidrigailov to'satdan kulishga tushdi.

en: “But you’re … but there’s no getting round you,” he said, laughing in the frankest way.
uz: Ammo siz... lekin siz bilan hech qanday aloqa yo'q, dedi u, so'nggicha kulish bilan.

en: “I hoped to get round you, but you took up the right line at once!” “But you are trying to get round me still!” “What of it?
uz: Men sizdan oldinga borishni umid qilardim, lekin siz darhol to'g'ri yo'lni tanladingiz!  Ammo siz hali ham meni o'rab olishga harakat qilyapsiz!   Nima bo'ldi?

en: What of it?” cried Svidrigaïlov, laughing openly.
uz: Xo'sh, nima? Svidrigailov ochiqchasiga kulish bilan yig'ladi.

en: “But this is what the French call bonne guerre, and the most innocent form of deception!
uz: Ammo fransuzlar buni "bonne guerre" deb atashadi va bu aldashning eng aybsiz shaklidir!

en: … But still you have interrupted me; one way or another, I repeat again: there would never have been any unpleasantness except for what happened in the garden.
uz: Ammo hali ham siz meni to'xtatgansiz; bir yo'l yoki boshqa yo'l bilan, yana takrorlayman: bog'da sodir bo'lganlardan tashqari hech qachon biron bir noqulaylik bo'lmagan bo'lardi.

en: Marfa Petrovna …” “You have got rid of Marfa Petrovna, too, so they say?” Raskolnikov interrupted rudely.
uz: Marfa Petrovna ... Siz ham Marfa Petrovna-dan qutuldingiz, deyishadi? Raskolnikov qo'pol tarzda to'xtatdi.

en: “Oh, you’ve heard that, too, then?
uz: O'sha payt siz ham buni eshitganmisiz?

en: You’d be sure to, though.
uz: Ammo shubhasizki, shunday bo'ladi.

en: … But as for your question, I really don’t know what to say, though my own conscience is quite at rest on that score.
uz: Ammo sizning savolingizga kelsak, bu borada vijdonim o'z vaqtida bo'lsa-da, nima deb javob berishni bilmayman.

en: Don’t suppose that I am in any apprehension about it.
uz: Men bu haqda hech qanday tashvishlanaman deb o'ylamang.

en: All was regular and in order; the medical inquiry diagnosed apoplexy due to bathing immediately after a heavy dinner and a bottle of wine, and indeed it could have proved nothing else.
uz: Hamma narsa odatiy va tartibli edi; tibbiy tekshiruvda og'ir kechki ovqatdan va bir shisha sharobdan keyin darhol suvga cho'mganlik tufayli apopleksiya aniqlandi va bu boshqa hech narsa isbotlanmagan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: But I’ll tell you what I have been thinking to myself of late, on my way here in the train, especially: didn’t I contribute to all that … calamity, morally, in a way, by irritation or something of the sort.
uz: Ammo men sizga o'zimga o'zimni oxirgi paytlarda, poezdda, ayniqsa, bu yerga borayotganimda o'ylayotganimni aytib beraman: men bularning hammasiga ... ahlak jihatdan, ma'noda, xafa bo'lib yoki shunga o'xshash narsa bilan hissa qo'shmadimmi?

en: But I came to the conclusion that that, too, was quite out of the question.” Raskolnikov laughed.
uz: Ammo men shunga erishdimki, bu ham umuman mumkin emas. Raskolnikov kuldi.

en: “I wonder you trouble yourself about it!”
uz: Men bu haqda o'zingizni xavotirga solganingizga hayronman!

en: “But what are you laughing at?
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, nimaga kulyapsan?

en: Only consider, I struck her just twice with a switch —there were no marks even … don’t regard me as a cynic, please; I am perfectly aware how atrocious it was of me and all that; but I know for certain, too, that Marfa Petrovna was very likely pleased at my, so to say, warmth.
uz: Faqat bir o'ylab ko'ring, men uni faqat ikki marta o'chirgich bilan urganman  hech qanday belgilar yo'q edi ... meni sinik deb hisoblamang, iltimos; men bu men uchun qanchalik dahshatli bo'lganini yaxshi bilaman; lekin Marfa Petrovna mening, deganda, samimiyligimdan juda mamnun bo'lganini ham bilaman.

en: The story of your sister had been wrung out to the last drop; for the last three days Marfa Petrovna had been forced to sit at home; she had nothing to show herself with in the town.
uz: Singlingiz haqidagi hikoya so'nggi uch kun davomida o'z uyida o'tirishga majbur bo'lgan Marfa Petrovna shaharda ko'rinishi uchun hech narsa yo'q edi.

en: Besides, she had bored them so with that letter (you heard about her reading the letter).
uz: Bundan tashqari, u o'sha xat bilan ularni juda charchatib qo'ygan edi (o'sha xatni o'qiganini eshitgan edingiz).

en: And all of a sudden those two switches fell from heaven!
uz: Toʻsatdan bu ikkita oʻgʻri osmondan tushib tushdi!

en: Her first act was to order the carriage to be got out.
uz: Uning birinchi ishi - vagonni olib chiqishni buyurish edi.

en: … Not to speak of the fact that there are cases when women are very, very glad to be insulted in spite of all their show of indignation.
uz: Ayollarning g'azablangan ko'rinishlariga qaramay, haqoratga duch kelganiga juda xursand bo'lgan holatlar ham borligini aytmaylik.

en: There are instances of it with everyone; human beings in general, indeed, greatly love to be insulted, have you noticed that?
uz: Har kimda shunday holatlar bor; umuman olganda, odamlar haqoratga duch kelishlarini juda yaxshi ko'rishadi, buni payqaganmisiz?

en: But it’s particularly so with women.
uz: Ayniqsa, ayollar uchun.

en: One might even say it’s their only amusement.” At one time Raskolnikov thought of getting up and walking out and so finishing the interview.
uz: Hatto bu ularning yagona o'yin-kulgi deb aytsa bo'ladi. Bir paytlar Raskolnikov o'rnidan turib ketishni va suhbatni yakunlashni o'yladi.

en: But some curiosity and even a sort of prudence made him linger for a moment.
uz: Ammo ba'zi qiziquvchanlik va hatto o'z aql-idrokidan foydalanib, u bir muncha vaqt o'tirdi.

en: “You are fond of fighting?” he asked carelessly.
uz: Siz jang qilishni yoqtirasizmi? deb so'radi u ehtiyotsizlik bilan.

en: “No, not very,” Svidrigaïlov answered, calmly.
uz: Yo'q, juda ham emas, Svidrigailov tinchlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “And Marfa Petrovna and I scarcely ever fought.
uz: Marfa Petrovna va men deyarli hech qachon bahslashmadik.

en: We lived very harmoniously, and she was always pleased with me.
uz: Biz juda uyg'un hayot kechirardik va u har doim men bilan rozi bo'lgan.

en: I only used the whip twice in all our seven years (not counting a third occasion of a very ambiguous character).
uz: Yetti yil davomida faqat ikki marta qamchiladim (o'ta ko'p noaniq bo'lgan uchinchi marta ham bo'lmagan).

en: The first time, two months after our marriage, immediately after we arrived in the country, and the last time was that of which we are speaking.
uz: Birinchi marta, turmush qurganimizdan ikki oy o'tgach, mamlakatga kelganimizdan so'ng, so'nggi marta biz gapirgan payt edi.

en: Did you suppose I was such a monster, such a reactionary, such a slave driver?
uz: Siz mening bunday qo'rqinchli, reaktsion, qul haydovchisi bo'lganimni o'ylaganmisiz?

en: By the way, do you remember, Rodion Romanovitch, how a few years ago, in those days of beneficent publicity, a nobleman, I’ve forgotten his name, was put to shame everywhere, in all the papers, for having thrashed a German woman in the railway train.
uz: Aytgancha, Rodion Romanovitch, bir necha yil oldin, yaxshilik bilan mashhur bo'lgan o'sha kunlarda, In ismini unutgan bir nobel kishi, poyezdda nemis ayolni urgani uchun hamma joyda, barcha gazetalarda sharmanda bo'lganini eslaysizmi?

en: It was in those days, that very year I believe, the ‘disgraceful action of the Age’ took place (you know, ‘The Egyptian Nights,’ that public reading, you remember?
uz: O'sha kunlarda, o'sha yilda, men o'ylaymanki, davrning sharafli harakatlari sodir bo'ldi (ya'ni, Misr kechalari,shunday ommaviy o'qish, eslaysizmi?)

en: The dark eyes, you know!
uz: Quruq ko'zlar, bilasiz!

en: Ah, the golden days of our youth, where are they?).
uz: Ah, yoshligimizning oltin kunlari, qayerda?!

en: Well, as for the gentleman who thrashed the German, I feel no sympathy with him, because after all what
uz: Germaniyalikni o'g'irlab yuborgan kishiga kelsak, men unga hech qanday rahm-shafqat ko'rmayapman, chunki nima bo'lganidan so'ng nima bo'ldi?

en: need is there for sympathy?
uz: Rahmdillik kerakmi?

en: But I must say that there are sometimes such provoking ‘Germans’ that I don’t believe there is a progressive who could quite answer for himself.
uz: Ammo aytishim kerakki, ba'zan shunday provokatsiyalar borki, o'zi uchun javob bera oladigan progressiv odam yo'q deb o'ylayman.

en: No one looked at the subject from that point of view then, but that’s the truly humane point of view, I assure you.” After saying this, Svidrigaïlov broke into a sudden laugh again.
uz: O'shanda hech kim mavzuga o'sha nuqtai nazardan qaramasdi, lekin bu haqiqatan ham insoniy nuqtai nazardan, sizga ishontiraman. Buni aytgandan so'ng Svidrigailov yana bir bor tabassumga tushdi.

en: Raskolnikov saw clearly that this was a man with a firm purpose in his mind and able to keep it to himself.
uz: Raskolnikov aniq ko'rdiki, bu odam o'z aqlidagi aniq maqsadga ega bo'lib, uni o'zi uchun saqlab qolishga qodir.

en: “I expect you’ve not talked to anyone for some days?” he asked.
uz: - Bir necha kun davomida hech kim bilan gaplashmaganingizni kutaman? - deb so'radi u.

en: I suppose you are wondering at my being such an adaptable man?” “No, I am only wondering at your being too adaptable a man.” “Because I am not offended at the rudeness of your questions?
uz: O'ylaymanki, siz mening o'zgarishchan odam bo'lishimga o'ylayotgandirsiz? Yo'q, men faqat sizning o'zgarishchan odam bo'lishingizga o'ylayotgandirman. Chunki men sizning savollaringizning qo'polligidan xafa emasman?

en: But why take offence?
uz: Ammo nega haddan tashqari jahldor bo'lish kerak?

en: As you asked, so I answered,” he replied, with a surprising expression of simplicity.
uz: Siz so'raganingizdek, men ham javob berdim, - dedi u, o'ziga xos soddalik bilan.

en: “You know, there’s hardly anything I take interest in,” he went on, as it were dreamily, “especially now, I’ve nothing to do.
uz: Bilaman, men qiziqadigan hech narsa yo'q, - dedi u, bir tasavvur qilib aytganda, - ayniqsa hozir, men uchun hech qanday ish yo'q.

en: … You are quite at liberty to imagine though that I am making up to you with a motive, particularly as I told you I want to see your sister about something.
uz: ... Siz mening sizga biron bir sabab bilan to'g'rilashayotganimni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin, ayniqsa, sizga singilingizni bir narsa bilan ko'rishimni aytganimda.

en: But I’ll confess frankly, I am very much bored.
uz: Lekin rostini aytsam, men juda charchadim.

en: The last three days especially, so I am delighted to see you.
uz: Ayniqsa, so'nggi uch kun, shuning uchun sizlarni ko'rishimdan mamnunman.

en: … Don’t be angry, Rodion Romanovitch, but you seem to be somehow awfully strange yourself.
uz: - G'azablanma, Rodion Romanovitch, lekin o'zing ham juda g'alati bo'lib ko'rinasan.

en: Say what you like, there’s something wrong with you, and now, too … not this very minute, I mean, but now, generally.
uz: O'zingiz xohlaganingizni ayting, sizda ham, hozir ham biron bir muammo bor... bu daqiqa emas, balki hozir, umuman.

en: … Well, well, I won’t, I won’t, don’t scowl!
uz: Xo'sh, men qo'rqmayman, qo'rqmayman, qo'rqmayman!

en: I am not such a bear, you know, as you think.” Raskolnikov looked gloomily at him.
uz: O'zingiz o'ylagandek, men g'alati aylan emasman. Raskolnikov unga qorong'ilik bilan qaradi.

en: “You are not a bear, perhaps, at all,” he said.
uz: "Siz bir qush emassiz, ehtimol, umuman", - dedi u.

en: “I fancy indeed that you are a man of very good breeding, or at least know how on occasion to behave like one.” “I am not particularly interested in anyone’s opinion,” Svidrigaïlov answered, dryly and even with a shade of haughtiness, “and therefore why not be vulgar at times when vulgarity is such a convenient cloak for our climate … and especially if one has a natural propensity that way,” he added, laughing again.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, siz juda yaxshi urug'chilik qiladigan odam ekanligingizni yoki hech bo'lmaganda, ba'zida qanday qilib shunday yo'l tutishni bilishingiz mumkinligini o'ylayman.Men hech kimning fikri bilan qiziqmayman, Svidrigailov quruqlik va hatto mag'rurlik soyasida javob berdi,shunday qilib, nima uchun o'zimizni vulgarlik bizning iqlimimiz uchun qulay qopqog'i bo'lgan paytlarda vulgar bo'lmasligimiz kerak ... va ayniqsa, agar odamda bunday qilishga tabiiy moyillik bo'lsa,-da, u yana o'z so'zini qo'shib qo'ydi.

en: “But I’ve heard you have many friends here.
uz: Ammo sizning bu yerda ko'plab do'stlaringiz borligini eshitdim.

en: You are, as they say, ‘not without connections.’ What can you want with me, then, unless you’ve some special object?”
uz: Aytishlaricha, siz bog'siz emassiz. Agar sizda biron bir maxsus ob'ekt bo'lmasa, unda mendan nima xohlay olasiz?

en: “That’s true that I have friends here,” Svidrigaïlov admitted, not replying to the chief point.
uz: Bu yerda do'stlarim borligi to'g'ri, deb tan oldi Svidrigailov, ammo asosiy mavzuga javob bermadi.

en: “I’ve met some already.
uz: Ive ba'zilari allaqachon uchrashdi.

en: I’ve been lounging about for the last three days, and I’ve seen them, or they’ve seen me.
uz: So'nggi uch kundan beri atrofda yuribman va ularni ko'rdim yoki ular meni ko'rishdi.

en: That’s a matter of course.
uz: Bu tabiiy hol.

en: I am well dressed and reckoned not a poor man; the emancipation of the serfs hasn’t affected me; my property consists chiefly of forests and water meadows.
uz: Men yaxshi kiyim kiyganman va kambag'al odam deb hisoblanmayman; qullarning ozodligi menga hech qanday ta'sir qilmadi; mol-mulkim asosan o'rmonlar va suv o'tlari bilan to'lib-toshgan.

en: The revenue has not fallen off; but … I am not going to see them, I was sick of them long ago.
uz: Umumiy daromadlar kamaygani yo'q, lekin... Men ularni ko'rmayman, men ulardan ancha vaqt oldin xafa bo'ldim.

en: I’ve been here three days and have called on no one.
uz: Uch kun bu yerda bo'lib, hech kimga murojaat qilmadim.

en: … What a town it is!
uz: Bu qanday shahar!

en: How has it come into existence among us, tell me that?
uz: Biz o'rtasida u qanday paydo bo'ldi, ayting?

en: A town of officials and students of all sorts.
uz: Har xil mansabdorlar va talabalar shahri.

en: Yes, there’s a great deal I didn’t notice when I was here eight years ago, kicking up my heels.
uz: Ha, sakkiz yil oldin bu yerda bo'lganimda ko'p narsalarni payqamay qo'ydim.

en: … My only hope now is in anatomy, by Jove, it is!” “Anatomy?” “But as for these clubs, Dussauts, parades, or progress, indeed, maybe —well, all that can go on without me,” he went on, again without noticing the question.
uz: Endi mening yagona umidim anatomiyada, Jove tomonidan, shunday!Anatomiya? Ammo bu klublar, Dussauts, parades yoki taraqqiyot haqida gap ketganda, ehtimol, mensiz davom etishi mumkin bo'lgan barcha narsalar, u yana savolga e'tibor bermasdan davom etdi.

en: “Besides, who wants to be a cardsharper?” “Why, have you been a cardsharper then?” “How could I help being?
uz: Bundan tashqari, kim karta sharperi bo'lishni xohlaydi?  Nima uchun, siz o'sha paytda karta sharperi bo'lganmisiz?  Qanday qilib o'zimga yordam bera olaman?

en: There was a regular set of us, men of the best society, eight years ago; we had a fine time.
uz: Sakkiz yil oldin biz, eng yaxshi jamiyatdan bo'lgan odamlar, bir guruh bo'lib, yaxshi vaqt o'tkazdik.

en: And all men of breeding, you know, poets, men of property.
uz: Va barcha farovon kishilar, siz bilasiz, shoirlar, mulk egalari.

en: And indeed as a rule in our Russian society the best manners are found among those who’ve been thrashed, have you noticed that?
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bizning rus jamiyatimizda eng yaxshi xulq-atvorlar ustun qo'yilganlar orasida ko'p bo'ladi, buni payqaganmisiz?

en: I’ve deteriorated in the country.
uz: Mamlakatda bu holat yomonlashdi.

en: But I did get into prison for debt, through a low Greek who came from Nezhin.
uz: Ammo men Nezhindan kelgan pastki yunon orqali qarz olish uchun zindonga tushdim.

en: Then Marfa Petrovna turned up; she bargained with him and bought me off for thirty thousand silver pieces (I owed seventy thousand).
uz: Keyin Marfa Petrovna paydo bo'ldi; u u bilan muzokara qilib, meni o'ttiz ming kumush tangaga sotib oldi.

en: We were united in lawful wedlock and she bore me off into the country like a treasure.
uz: Biz qonuniy nikohda birlashgan edik va u meni xazina kabi qishloqqa olib kirdi.

en: You know she was five years older than I.
uz: U mendan besh yosh katta edi.

en: She was very fond of me.
uz: U menga juda yoqardi.

en: For seven years I never left the country.
uz: Yetti yil davomida men hech qachon mamlakatni tark etmaganman.

en: And, take note, that all my life she held a document over me, the I.O.U.
uz: Shuni ta'kidlangki, butun hayotim davomida u men, I.O.U. haqida hujjat ushlab turardi.

en: for thirty thousand roubles, so if I were to elect to be restive about anything I should be trapped at once!
uz: O'ttiz ming rubl evaziga, agar men biror narsa haqida g'alati bo'lishni tanlasam, darhol tuzoqqa tushaman!

en: And she would have done it!
uz: Va u buni qilgan bo'lar edi!

en: Women find nothing incompatible in that.” “If it hadn’t been for that, would you have given her the slip?” “I don’t know what to say.
uz: Ayollar bunda hech qanday ziddiyatni ko'rmaydilar.  Agar bu bo'lmaganida, siz unga ishdan bo'shatgan bo'lardingizmi?   Men nima deb aytishni bilmayman.

en: It was scarcely the document restrained me.
uz: Aslida hujjat meni to'xtatib qo'ydi.

en: I didn’t want to go anywhere else.
uz: Men boshqa hech joyga borishni istamaganman.

en: Marfa Petrovna herself invited
uz: Marfa Petrovna o'zi taklif qildi

en: me to go abroad, seeing I was bored, but I’ve been abroad before, and always felt sick there.
uz: Men chet elga ketishimga rozi bo'ldim, chunki men charchagan edim, lekin men ilgari chet elga borganman va u erda doimo kasal bo'lganman.

en: For no reason, but the sunrise, the bay of Naples, the sea —you look at them and it makes you sad.
uz: Hech qanday sabab yo'q, balki quyosh chiqish, Neapol ko'chasi, dengiz - siz ularga qarasangiz, bu sizni xafa qiladi.

en: What’s most revolting is that one is really sad!
uz: Eng dahshatli narsa shundaki, u juda xafa!

en: No, it’s better at home.
uz: Yo'q, uyda yaxshiroq.

en: Here at least one blames others for everything and excuses oneself.
uz: Bu yerda hech bo'lmaganda hamma narsa uchun boshqalarni ayblab, o'zini oqlaydi.

en: I should have gone perhaps on an expedition to the North Pole, because j’ai le vin mauvais and hate drinking, and there’s nothing left but wine.
uz: Ehtimol, men Shimoliy qutbga sayohatga borishim kerak edi, chunki men yomon sharobni yeb, ichishdan nafratlanaman va sharobdan boshqa hech narsa qolmaydi.

en: But, I say, I’ve been told Berg is going up in a great balloon next Sunday from the Yusupov Garden and will take up passengers at a fee.
uz: Lekin men aytamanki, Berg kelgusi yakshanba kuni Yusupov bog'idan katta ballonda chiqib, yo'lovchilar uchun haq to'laydi.

en: Is it true?” “Why, would you go up?” “I … No, oh, no,” muttered Svidrigaïlov really seeming to be deep in thought.
uz: Haqiqat bormi?  Nima uchun, ko'tarib borasiz?  Men ... Yo'q, oh, yo'q, Svidrigailov g'iybat qildi va haqiqatan ham chuqur fikrda bo'lib ko'rinadi.

en: Is he in earnest?” Raskolnikov wondered.
uz: U jiddiymi? Raskolnikov o'zini o'ylab ko'rdi.

en: “No, the document didn’t restrain me,” Svidrigaïlov went on, meditatively.
uz: Yo'q, hujjat meni to'xtatmadi,  Svidrigailov davom etdi, mulohaza bilan.

en: “It was my own doing, not leaving the country, and nearly a year ago Marfa Petrovna gave me back the document on my name-day and made me a present of a considerable sum of money, too.
uz: Bu mening o'zim qilgan ishim edi, mamlakatni tark etmaganman va deyarli bir yil oldin Marfa Petrovna ism kunimdagi hujjatni menga qaytarib berdi va menga katta miqdordagi pul sovg'asini ham berdi.

en: She had a fortune, you know.
uz: Uning mol-mulki bor edi.

en: ‘You see how I trust you, Arkady Ivanovitch’ —that was actually her expression.
uz: Siz ko'ryapsiz, men sizga qanchalik ishonaman, Arkady Ivanovitch  bu aslida uning ifodasidir.

en: You don’t believe she used it?
uz: Siz unga ishonmayapsizmi?

en: But do you know I managed the estate quite decently, they know me in the neighbourhood.
uz: Ammo bilingmi, men mol-mulkni juda yaxshi boshqarganman, ular meni qo'shnilikda tanishadi.

en: I ordered books, too.
uz: Men ham kitoblarni buyurtma qildim.

en: Marfa Petrovna at first approved, but afterwards she was afraid of my over-studying.” “You seem to be missing Marfa Petrovna very much?” “Missing her?
uz: Marfa Petrovna dastlab rozi bo'ldi, lekin keyinchalik mening o'qishimdan qo'rqdi.Marfa Petrovna sizni juda sog'inadi deb o'ylaysiz?Uni sog'inasizmi?

en: Really, perhaps I am.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, ehtimol men shundayman.

en: And, by the way, do you believe in ghosts?” “What ghosts?” “Why, ordinary ghosts.” “Do you believe in them?” “Perhaps not, pour vous plaire.
uz: Aytgancha, siz hayajonlarga ishonasizmi?  Qanday hayajonlar?  Nima uchun, oddiy hayajonlar.  Siz ularga ishonasizmi?  Ehtimol, o'zingizni yoqtirmaslik uchun.

en: … I wouldn’t say no exactly.” “Do you see them, then?” Svidrigaïlov looked at him rather oddly.
uz: Men to'g'ri yo'q demayman. Siz ularni ko'ryapsizmi? Svidrigailov unga o'ta g'alati qarabdi.

en: “Marfa Petrovna is pleased to visit me,” he said, twisting his mouth into a strange smile.
uz: "Marfa Petrovna menga tashrif buyurishdan mamnun", - dedi u, og'zini g'ayrioddiy tabassumga aylantirib.

en: “How do you mean ‘she is pleased to visit you’?”
uz: Qanday qilib u sizni ko'rishdan mamnun bo'ladi?

en: “She has been three times.
uz: U uch marta borgan.

en: I saw her first on the very day of the funeral, an hour after she was buried.
uz: Men uni birinchi marta o'z dafn kuni, ya'ni dafn qilinganidan bir soat o'tib ko'rdim.

en: It was the day before I left to come here.
uz: Bu yerga kelish uchun ketishdan bir kun oldin edi.

en: The second time was the day before yesterday, at daybreak, on the journey at the station of Malaya Vishera, and the third time was two hours ago in the room where I am staying.
uz: Ikkinchi marta kechqurun, tongda, Malaya Vishera stantsiyasida sayohat paytida, uchinchi marta esa ikki soat oldin men turgan xonada bo'ldi.

en: I was alone.” “Were you awake?” “Quite awake.
uz: Men yolg'iz edim.  Siz uyg'onasizmi?  Quyida uyg'onasiz.

en: I was wide awake every time.
uz: Men har safar keng uyg'onib turardim.

en: She comes, speaks to me for a minute and goes out at the door —always at the door.
uz: U kelib, men bilan bir daqiqa gaplashib, eshikdan chiqib ketadi.

en: I can almost hear her.” “What made me think that something of the sort must be happening to you?” Raskolnikov said suddenly.
uz: Men uni deyarli tinglay olaman.  Nima uchun men sizga shunday narsa sodir bo'lishi kerak deb o'yladim? Raskolnikov to'satdan dedi.

en: At the same moment he was surprised at having said it.
uz: Shu vaqtning o'zida u buni aytganidan hayron qoldi.

en: He was much excited.
uz: U juda hayajonlangan edi.

en: Did you think so?” Svidrigaïlov asked in astonishment.
uz: Siz ham shunday deb o'yladingizmi? Svidrigailov hayronlik bilan so'radi.

en: Didn’t I say that there was something in common between us, eh?” “You never said so!” Raskolnikov cried sharply and with heat.
uz: Biz o'rtasida umumiy narsa borligini aytmadimmi? Siz hech qachon shunday aytmadingiz! Raskolnikov og'ir va issiqlik bilan yig'ladi.

en: “Didn’t I?” “No!” “I thought I did.
uz: Men qilmadimmi? - Yo'q! - deb o'yladim.

en: When I came in and saw you lying with your eyes shut, pretending, I said to myself at once, ‘Here’s the man.’ ” “What do you mean by ‘the man?’ What are you talking about?” cried Raskolnikov.
uz: Men kirganimda, seni ko'zlaringni yopib, o'zingizni ko'rsatgandek ko'rdim va darhol o'zimga dedim: "Mana bu odam bor". "Bu odam" deganda nimani nazarda tutyapsan? "Bu nima?" - deb o'ylardim Raskolnikov.

en: I really don’t know.
uz: Haqiqatan ham bilmayman.

en: …” Svidrigaïlov muttered ingenuously, as though he, too, were puzzled.
uz: ... Svidrigailov o'zi ham g'alati bo'lib qolganidek, aql-idrok bilan gapirdi.

en: For a minute they were silent.
uz: Ular bir daqiqa davomida sukut saqlashdi.

en: They stared in each other’s faces.
uz: Ular bir-birlarining yuzlariga qaradi.

en: “That’s all nonsense!” Raskolnikov shouted with vexation.
uz: Bularning barchasi behuda! Raskolnikov xafalik bilan baqirib yubordi.

en: “What does she say when she comes to you?” “She!
uz: Senga kelganida u nima deydi? U!

en: Would you believe it, she talks of the silliest trifles and —man is a strange creature —it makes me angry.
uz: Ishonasizmi, u o'ta g'alati gaplarni aytadi va inson g'alati mavjudotdir. Bu meni g'azabga soladi.

en: The first time she came in (I was tired you know: the funeral service, the funeral ceremony, the lunch afterwards.
uz: U birinchi marta kelganida (men charchagan edim) bilasizmi: dafn marosimi, dafn marosimi, kechki ovqatdan keyin.

en: At last I was left alone in my study.
uz: Nihoyat, men o'zimni ishxonamda yolg'iz qoldirdim.

en: I lighted a cigar and began to think), she came in at the door.
uz: Men sigaret yoqdim va o'ylashga tushdim), u eshikdan kirdi.

en: ‘You’ve been so busy today, Arkady Ivanovitch, you have forgotten to wind the dining-room clock,’ she said.
uz: "Bugun shunchalik mashg'ul bo'ldingki, Arkady Ivanovitch, ovqatxonadagi soatni o'chirib yuborishni unutib qo'yding", - dedi u.

en: All those seven years I’ve wound that clock every week, and if I forgot it she would always remind me.
uz: O'sha yetti yil davomida men har hafta o'sha soatni aylantirganman va uni unutganimda, u meni har doim eslatardi.

en: set off on my way here.
uz: Men bu yerga borayotganimda yo'lga chiqdim.

en: I got out at the station at daybreak; I’d been asleep, tired out, with my eyes half open, I was drinking some coffee.
uz: Men tongda stantsiyadan chiqdim; men uxlab, charchagan edim, ko'zlarim yarim ochilgan edi, men kofe ichar edim.

en: I looked up and there was suddenly Marfa Petrovna sitting beside me with a pack of cards in her hands.
uz: Men ko'zimni ko'tardim va birdan Marfa Petrovna qo'limda kartalar to'plamini olib yonimda o'tirib qoldi.

en: ‘Shall I tell your fortune for the journey, Arkady Ivanovitch?’ She was a great hand at telling fortunes.
uz: Menga sayohat uchun taqdiringizni aytishim kerakmi, Arkady Ivanovitch? U taqdirni aytishda ajoyib qo'l edi.

en: I shall never forgive myself for not asking her to.
uz: O'zimni hech qachon kechira olmayman, chunki men unga buni so'ramaganman.

en: I ran away in a fright, and, besides, the bell rang.
uz: Men qo'rqib qochib ketdim va qo'ng'iroq qo'ng'iroq qildi.

en: I was sitting today, feeling very heavy after a miserable dinner from a cookshop; I was sitting smoking, all of a sudden Marfa Petrovna again.
uz: Bugun men oshxonadan tushkunlikka tushgan kechki ovqatdan keyin juda og'ir his etib, o'tirgan edim; men sigaret chekayotgan edim, to'satdan Marfa Petrovna yana.

en: She came in very smart in a new green silk dress with a long train.
uz: U yangi yashil ipak kiyimda va uzoq poezdda juda aqlli bo'lib keldi.

en: ‘Good day, Arkady Ivanovitch!
uz: Xayrli kunlar, Arkady Ivanovitch!

en: How do you like my dress?
uz: Mening kiyimim sizga yoqadimi?

en: Aniska can’t make like this.’ (Aniska was a dressmaker in the country, one of our former serf girls who had been trained in Moscow, a pretty wench.) She stood turning round before me.
uz: Aniska bunday qilish mumkin emas. (Aniska qishloqdagi kiyim-kechak usuli, Moskvada o'qitilgan sobiq qul qizlarimizdan biri, chiroyli ayol edi.)

en: I looked at the dress, and then I looked carefully, very carefully, at her face.
uz: Men kiyimga qaradim va keyin uning yuziga diqqat bilan, juda diqqat bilan qaradim.

en: ‘I wonder you trouble to come to me about such trifles, Marfa Petrovna.’ ‘Good gracious, you won’t let one disturb you about anything!’ To tease her I said, ‘I want to get married, Marfa Petrovna.’ ‘That’s just like you, Arkady Ivanovitch; it does you very little credit to come looking for a bride when you’ve hardly buried your wife.
uz: Menga bunday mayda-mayda narsalar haqida gapirib berishga qiynalayotganingdan ajablanaman, Marfa Petrovna.Xayrli xayrli, hech kim sizni hech narsa bilan bezovta qilishiga yo'l qo'ymaysiz! Uni mazax qilish uchun men: Men turmush qurmoqchiman, Marfa Petrovna, dedim.Bu sizga o'xshaydi, Arkady Ivanovitch; siz eringizni deyarli ko'mganingizda, kelinni qidirishga kelganingiz sizga juda kam kredit beradi.

en: And if you could make a good choice, at least, but I know it won’t be for your happiness or hers, you will only be a laughingstock to all good people.’ Then she went out and her train seemed to rustle.
uz: Va agar siz hech bo'lmaganda yaxshi tanlov qila olsangiz, lekin bu sizning yoki uning baxtingiz uchun bo'lmasligini bilaman, siz faqat barcha yaxshi odamlar uchun kulgi bo'lasiz. Keyin u tashqariga chiqdi va uning poezdini qichqirishdi.

en: Isn’t it nonsense, eh?” “But perhaps you are telling lies?” Raskolnikov put in.
uz: Ammo ehtimol siz yolg'on gapiryapsizmi? Raskolnikov qo'ydi.

en: “I rarely lie,” answered Svidrigaïlov thoughtfully, apparently not noticing the rudeness of the question.
uz: "Men kamdan-kam yolg'on gapiraman", - deb javob berdi Svidrigailov, ehtimol, savolning qo'polligiga e'tibor bermay.

en: “And in the past, have you ever seen ghosts before?” “Y-yes, I have seen them, but only once in my life, six years ago.
uz: Va o'tmishda siz allaqachon hayajonlarni ko'rganmisiz?Y-ha, men ularni ko'rdim, lekin hayotimda faqat bir marta, olti yil oldin.

en: I had a serf, Filka; just after his burial I called out forgetting ‘Filka, my pipe!’ He came in and went to the cupboard where my pipes were.
uz: Mening Filka ismli serfim bor edi; uning dafnidan so'ng, men uni unutganman, Filka, mening quvurim! U kirib, quvurlarim joylashgan omborga bordi.

en: I sat still and thought ‘he is doing it out of revenge,’ because we had a violent quarrel just before his death.
uz: Men o'zimni to'xtatmay o'tirib, o'yladimki, u buni qasos olish uchun qilyapti, chunki o'limidan oldin biz zo'ravon bahslashgan edik.

en: ‘How dare you come in with a hole in your elbow?’ I said.
uz: Qani, qo'lqovog'ingizda cho'g' bo'lib kirishga jur'at qilasan? - dedim men.

en: ‘Go away, you scamp!’ He turned and went out, and never came again.
uz: Yo'q bo'lib ket, ey qotil! U o'girilib chiqib ketdi va yana qaytib kelmadi.

en: I didn’t tell Marfa Petrovna at the time.
uz: O'shanda men Marfa Petrovnaga aytmagan edim.

en: I wanted to have a service sung for him, but I was ashamed.” “You should go to a doctor.”
uz: Men uning uchun xizmatni kuylashni xohlardim, lekin uyatga tushardim. Siz shifokorga borishingiz kerak.

en: “I know I am not well, without your telling me, though I don’t know what’s wrong; I believe I am five times as strong as you are.
uz: Men yaxshi emasligimni bilaman, lekin sen aytmaganingdan so'ng, nima bo'lganini bilmayman; men o'zimdan besh baravar kuchliroq ekanligimga ishonaman.

en: I didn’t ask you whether you believe that ghosts are seen, but whether you believe that they exist.” “No, I won’t believe it!” Raskolnikov cried, with positive anger.
uz: Men sizdan ruhlarning ko'rinishiga ishonasizmi yoki yo'qmi deb so'ramagan edim. Yo'q, ishonmayman! Raskolnikov og'ir jahl bilan yig'ladi.

en: “What do people generally say?” muttered Svidrigaïlov, as though speaking to himself, looking aside and bowing his head.
uz: Odamlar odatda nima deyishadi? Svidrigailov o'ziga gapirayotganday, o'ziga qarab, boshini egib gapirdi.

en: “They say, ‘You are ill, so what appears to you is only unreal fantasy.’ But that’s not strictly logical.
uz: Ular: "Sen kasalsan, shuning uchun senga ko'rinadigan narsalar faqat haqiqiy bo'lmagan xayol.

en: I agree that ghosts only appear to the sick, but that only proves that they are unable to appear except to the sick, not that they don’t exist.” “Nothing of the sort,” Raskolnikov insisted irritably.
uz: Men shuni tan olamanki, jinlar faqat kasallarga ko'rinadi, lekin bu faqat kasallardan boshqa hech kim ularga ko'rinmaydi, bu ularning mavjud emasligini tasdiqlaydi. Raskolnikov g'azabga to'lib-toshgan holda, bunday narsa yo'qligini ta'kidladi.

en: You don’t think so?” Svidrigaïlov went on, looking at him deliberately.
uz: Siz ham shunday o'ylamasangizmi? Svidrigailov unga qasddan qarab davom etdi.

en: “But what do you say to this argument (help me with it): ghosts are, as it were, shreds and fragments of other worlds, the beginning of them.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, bu dalilga qanday javob berasiz (men bilan yordam bering): ruhiylar boshqa olamlarning parchalari va parchalari, ularning boshlanishi, deb aytish mumkin.

en: A man in health has, of course, no reason to see them, because he is above all a man of this earth and is bound for the sake of completeness and order to live only in this life.
uz: To'g'ri, sog'lom odamda ularni ko'rish uchun hech qanday sabab yo'q, chunki u avvalo bu yerdagi odam va to'liqlik va tartib uchun faqat bu hayotda yashashga majbur.

en: But as soon as one is ill, as soon as the normal earthly order of the organism is broken, one begins to realise the possibility of another world; and the more seriously ill one is, the closer becomes one’s contact with that other world, so that as soon as the man dies he steps straight into that world.
uz: Ammo odam kasal bo'lganidan so'ng, organizmning normal yerdagi tartibini buzganidan so'ng, boshqa dunyo paydo bo'lishi mumkinligini anglay boshlaydi; va odam qanchalik jiddiy kasal bo'lsa, o'sha boshqa dunyo bilan munosabatlari shunchalik yaqinlashadiki, inson o'lganidan so'ng u to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'sha dunyoga kiradi.

en: I thought of that long ago.
uz: Men buni ancha vaqt oldin o'ylab ko'rdim.

en: If you believe in a future life, you could believe in that, too.” “I don’t believe in a future life,” said Raskolnikov.
uz: Agar siz kelajakdagi hayotga ishonsangiz, unga ham ishonishingiz mumkin.Men kelajakdagi hayotga ishonmayman, dedi Raskolnikov.

en: Svidrigaïlov sat lost in thought.
uz: Svidrigailov o'y-fikrida o'tirib qolgan edi.

en: “And what if there are only spiders there, or something of that sort,” he said suddenly.
uz: Va agar u yerda faqat o'tkirlar yoki shunga o'xshash narsa bo'lsa-chi? dedi u to'satdan.

en: “He is a madman,” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: U aqldan ozgan inson, Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: “We always imagine eternity as something beyond our conception, something vast, vast!
uz: Biz abadiylikni har doim tasavvurimizdan o'zga narsa, keng, keng narsa deb tasavvur qilamiz!

en: But why must it be vast?
uz: Ammo nega u keng bo'lishi kerak?

en: Instead of all that, what if it’s one little room, like a bath house in the country, black and grimy and spiders in every corner, and that’s all eternity is?
uz: Buning o'rniga, agar u qishloqdagi hammom kabi bitta kichik xonadir, har bir burchada qora va kirli va o'tlar bor bo'lsa-chi?

en: I sometimes fancy it like that.” “Can it be you can imagine nothing juster and more comforting than that?” Raskolnikov cried, with a feeling of anguish.
uz: Ba'zan men buni shunday tasavvur qilaman.  Siz bundan ham adolatli va tasalli beruvchi hech narsani tasavvur qila olasizmi? Raskolnikov qayg'u hissi bilan yig'ladi.

en: And how can we tell, perhaps that is just, and do you know it’s what I would certainly have made it,” answered Svidrigaïlov, with a vague smile.
uz: Va qanday qilib aytsa bo'ladi, ehtimol bu adolatli, va bilasizmi, men buni albatta qilgan bo'lardim, - dedi Svidrigailov, ko'p o'rinsiz tabassum bilan.

en: This horrible answer sent a cold chill through Raskolnikov.
uz: Ushbu dahshatli javob Raskolnikovni qattiq xafa qildi.

en: Svidrigaïlov raised his head, looked at him, and suddenly began laughing.
uz: Svidrigailov boshini ko'tarib, unga qaradi va to'satdan kulishga tushadi.

en: “Only think,” he cried, “half an hour ago we had never seen each other, we regarded each other as enemies; there is a matter unsettled between us; we’ve thrown it aside, and away we’ve gone into the abstract!
uz: "Yaxshi o'ylab ko'ringlar", - dedi u, "yarim soat oldin biz hech qachon bir-birimizni ko'rmagan edik, biz bir-birimizni dushman deb bilgan edik; o' aramizda bir muammo bor; biz uni bir chetga tashladik va yo'q, biz abstraktlikka kirib keldik!

en: Wasn’t I right in saying that we were birds of a feather?” “Kindly allow me,” Raskolnikov went on irritably, “to ask you to explain why you have honoured me with your visit … and … and I am in a hurry, I have no time to waste.
uz: Biz qushlar ekanligimizni aytishda to'g'ri bo'lmaganmidim?Raskolnikov g'azabga to'lib, nima uchun menga tashrif buyurganingizni tushuntirishingizni so'rash uchun menga ruxsat bering.Va... va men shoshilinchman, vaqtimni yo'qotishga vaqtim yo'q.

en: I want to go out.” “By all means, by all means.
uz: Men tashqariga chiqishni istayman. Haqiqatan ham, haqiqatan ham.

en: Your sister, Avdotya Romanovna, is going to be married to Mr.
uz: Sizning singilingiz Avdotya Romanovna o'z turmush o'rtog'i bilan turmushga chiqadi.

en: Luzhin, Pyotr Petrovitch?” “Can you refrain from any question about my sister and from mentioning her name?
uz: Luzhin, Pyotr Petrovitch? Siz singlim haqida so'rashdan va uning ismini aytishdan voz kechishingiz mumkinmi?

en: I can’t understand how you dare utter her name in my presence, if you really are Svidrigaïlov.” “Why, but I’ve come here to speak about her; how can I avoid mentioning her?” “Very good, speak, but make haste.” “I am sure that you must have formed your own opinion of this Mr.
uz: Agar siz haqiqatan ham Svidrigailov bo'lsangiz, mening huzurimda uning ismini qanday aytishga jur'at qilayotganingizni tushunmayman. Nega, lekin men bu yerga u haqida gapirish uchun keldim; uni qanday eslatishdan qochishim mumkin? juda yaxshi, gapiring, lekin shoshilinch bo'ling.Men shubhalanamanki, siz bu Mr. haqida o'zingizning fikringizni shakllantirgan bo'lishingiz kerak.

en: Luzhin, who is a connection of mine through my wife, if you have only seen him for half an hour, or heard any facts about him.
uz: Luzhin, agar siz uni yarim soatdan beri ko'rmagan bo'lsangiz yoki u haqida biron bir faktni eshitgan bo'lsangiz, u xotinim orqali mening aloqamdir.

en: He is no match for Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: U Avdotya Romanovna bilan hech qanday tenglamaydi.

en: I believe Avdotya Romanovna is sacrificing herself generously and imprudently for the sake of … for the sake of her family.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna o'zini saxiy va g'ayritabiiy ravishda o'zi uchun qurbon qilyapti deb o'ylayman ... oilasi uchun.

en: I fancied from all I had heard of you that you would be very glad if the match could be broken off without the sacrifice of worldly advantages.
uz: Siz haqingizda eshitgan hamma narsadan shuni o'yladimki, agar bu o'yin dunyoviy afzalliklarni qurbon qilmasdan tugatilgan bo'lsa, siz juda xursand bo'lasiz.

en: Now I know you personally, I am convinced of it.” “All this is very naive … excuse me, I should have said impudent on your part,” said Raskolnikov.
uz: Endi men sizni shaxsan bilaman, men bunga aminman. Bularning barchasi juda naifdir ... kechirim so'raysiz, men sizdan qo'pollik deb aytishim kerak edi, dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “You mean to say that I am seeking my own ends.
uz: Siz mening o'z maqsadlarimni izlayotganimni aytmoqchisiz.

en: Don’t be uneasy, Rodion Romanovitch, if I were working for my own advantage, I would not have spoken out so directly.
uz: Xavotirjam bo'lmang, Rodion Romanovitch, agar men o'z manfaatimni ko'zlab ishlagan bo'lsam, o'zimni shunday ochiq ko'rsatmagan bo'lardim.

en: I am not quite a fool.
uz: Men aqlsiz emasman.

en: I will confess something psychologically curious about that: just
uz: Men bunga nisbatan psixologik jihatdan qiziqarli bir narsani tan oldim: shunchaki

en: now, defending my love for Avdotya Romanovna, I said I was myself the victim.
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaga bo'lgan sevgimni himoya qilib, men o'zim qurbon bo'lganimni aytdim.

en: Well, let me tell you that I’ve no feeling of love now, not the slightest, so that I wonder myself indeed, for I really did feel something …” “Through idleness and depravity,” Raskolnikov put in.
uz: Hozirda hech qanday sevgi hissi yo'qligini aytaman, shuning uchun o'zimni o'zimdan o'zim ham o'ylayman, chunki men o'zimni o'zim ham o'yladim ... O'ysizlik va axloqsizlik orqali Raskolnikov qo'ydi.

en: “I certainly am idle and depraved, but your sister has such qualities that even I could not help being impressed by them.
uz: Men, albatta, bepul va nopokman, lekin singlingizning o'ta yaxshi fazilatlari borki, hatto men ham ular bilan taassurot qoldira olmayman.

en: But that’s all nonsense, as I see myself now.” “Have you seen that long?” “I began to be aware of it before, but was only perfectly sure of it the day before yesterday, almost at the moment I arrived in Petersburg.
uz: Ammo hozir o'zimni ko'rganimcha, bularning barchasi behuda.Siz shuncha vaqt ko'rganmisiz?Men bundan oldin ham bu haqda o'ylay boshlagan edim, lekin faqat bir kun oldin, deyarli Sankt-Peterburgga yetib kelganimda, bu haqda to'liq ishonch hosil qildim.

en: I still fancied in Moscow, though, that I was coming to try to get Avdotya Romanovna’s hand and to cut out Mr.
uz: Biroq, Moskvada Avdotya Romanovnaning qo'lini olish va Mr. Romanovnani o'chirib tashlash uchun kelayotganimni hali ham tasavvur qilardim.

en: Luzhin.” “Excuse me for interrupting you; kindly be brief, and come to the object of your visit.
uz: Luzhin.  Sizni aralashtirganim uchun uzr so'rayman; iltimos, qisqacha bo'ling va tashrifingiz mavzusiga keling.

en: I am in a hurry, I want to go out …” “With the greatest pleasure.
uz: Shoshilinchman, men tashqariga chiqmoqchiman ...Qattiq zavq bilan.

en: On arriving here and determining on a certain … journey, I should like to make some necessary preliminary arrangements.
uz: Bu yerga kelganimda va muayyan ... sayohatni rejalashtirganimda, kerakli dastlabki choralarni ko'rishni xohlayman.

en: I left my children with an aunt; they are well provided for; and they have no need of me personally.
uz: Farzandlarimni onam bilan qoldirdim; ular yaxshi ta'minlangan va ular shaxsan menga muhtoj emaslar.

en: And a nice father I should make, too!
uz: Va men ham yaxshi ota bo'lishim kerak!

en: I have taken nothing but what Marfa Petrovna gave me a year ago.
uz: Men Marfa Petrovna menga bir yil oldin bergan narsadan boshqa hech narsa olmaganman.

en: That’s enough for me.
uz: Bu men uchun yetarli.

en: Excuse me, I am just coming to the point.
uz: Kechirasizlar, men faqat gapni aytmoqchiman.

en: Before the journey which may come off, I want to settle Mr.
uz: Bu sayohatdan oldin men Mr. bilan kelishuvni o'rnatishni istayman.

en: It’s not that I detest him so much, but it was through him I quarrelled with Marfa Petrovna when I learned that she had dished up this marriage.
uz: Men uni shunchalik nafratlanmayman, lekin u orqali Marfa Petrovna bilan u bu nikohni buzganini bilib olgach, u bilan bahslashdim.

en: I want now to see Avdotya Romanovna through your mediation, and if you like in your presence, to explain to her that in the first place she will never gain anything but harm from Mr.
uz: Endi Avdotya Romanovna bilan sizning vositachiligingiz orqali uchrashishni va agar sizning oldingizda bo'lishni xohlasangiz, unga birinchi navbatda u hech qachon Mr. Romanovnan zararlanishdan boshqa hech narsa olmaydiligini tushuntirishni xohlayman.

en: Then, begging her pardon for all past unpleasantness, to make her a present of ten thousand roubles and so assist the rupture with Mr.
uz: Keyin, o'tmishdagi barcha noqulayliklar uchun kechirim so'rab, unga o'n ming rubl miqdorida sovg'a berish va shu yo'sin Mr. bilan bo'lishga yordam berish uchun uni kechirim so'rayman.

en: Luzhin, a rupture to which I believe she is herself not disinclined, if she could see the way to it.” “You are certainly mad,” cried Raskolnikov not so much angered as astonished.
uz: Luzhin, bu bo'linish uning o'zidan ham ko'rinib turibdi, deb o'ylayman, agar u yo'lni ko'rsa. "Siz albatta aqldan ozgansiz", - deb baqirdi Raskolnikov, g'azablanib emas, balki hayron bo'lib.

en: “How dare you talk like that!” “I knew you would scream at me; but in the first place, though I am not rich, this ten thousand roubles is perfectly free; I have absolutely no need for it.
uz: Qanday qilib siz shunday gapirishga jur'at qilasiz!Men sizga qichqirishingizni bilardim; lekin birinchi navbatda, men boy bo'lmasam ham, bu o'n ming rubl to'liq bepul; men bunga mutlaqo muhtoj emasman.

en: If Avdotya Romanovna does not accept it, I shall waste it in some more foolish way.
uz: Agar Avdotya Romanovna uni qabul qilmasa, men uni yanada ahmoqona tarzda sarflayman.

en: That’s the first thing.
uz: Bu birinchi narsa.

en: my conscience is perfectly easy; I make the offer with no ulterior motive.
uz: vijdonim juda oson; men taklifni hech qanday sababsiz qilaman.

en: You may not believe it, but in the end Avdotya Romanovna and you will know.
uz: Siz bunga ishonmasangiz ham bo'ladi, lekin oxir-oqibat Avdotya Romanovna va siz bilib olasiz.

en: The point is, that I did actually cause your sister, whom I greatly respect, some trouble and unpleasantness, and so, sincerely regretting it, I want —not to compensate, not to repay her for the unpleasantness, but simply to do something to her advantage, to show that I am not, after all, privileged to do nothing but harm.
uz: Aslida, men sizning aziz singilingizga, men uni juda hurmat qilaman, ba'zi muammo va noqulayliklarga sabab bo'ldim va shuning uchun, chin dildan afsuslanaman, men uni to'lovlash uchun emas, noqulaylik uchun javob qaytarish uchun emas, balki shunchaki uning foydasiga biror narsa qilish uchun, men faqat zarar qilishdan boshqa hech narsa qilmasligimni ko'rsatish uchun afzallik topganman.

en: If there were a millionth fraction of self-interest in my offer, I should not have made it so openly; and I should not have offered her ten thousand only, when five weeks ago I offered her more, Besides, I may, perhaps, very soon marry a young lady, and that alone ought to prevent suspicion of any design on Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Agar taklifimda millionda bir qismi o'z manfaatini ko'zlagan bo'lsa, men buni ochiqchasiga aytmasdim; besh hafta oldin unga ko'proq taklif qilganimda, unga o'nta mingni ham taklif qilmasdim. Bundan tashqari, ehtimol, men juda tezda yosh ayolga uylanishim mumkin, va bu Avdotya Romanovnaning har qanday rejasi haqida gumon qilishdan qochishi kerak.

en: In conclusion, let me say that in marrying Mr.
uz: Xulosa qilib aytamanki, Mr. bilan turmush qurganimda

en: Luzhin, she is taking money just the same, only from another man.
uz: Luzhin, u xuddi shunday pulni oladi, faqat boshqa erkakdan.

en: Don’t be angry, Rodion Romanovitch, think it over coolly and quietly.” Svidrigaïlov himself was exceedingly cool and quiet as he was saying this.
uz: G'azablanma, Rodion Romanovitch, bu haqda sovuq va xotirjam o'ylab ko'ring. Svidrigailovning o'zi bu so'zlarni aytganida juda sovuq va xotirjam edi.

en: “I beg you to say no more,” said Raskolnikov.
uz: Sizdan iltimos qilaman, boshqa aytmang, dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “In any case this is unpardonable impertinence.” “Not in the least.
uz: Hamma holda bu kechirilmaydigan bezovtalikdir. Hech bo'lmaganda.

en: Then a man may do nothing but harm to his neighbour in this world, and is prevented from doing the tiniest bit of good by trivial conventional formalities.
uz: Shunda inson bu dunyoda o'z yaqinlariga zarar yetkazishdan boshqa hech narsa qilmaydi va oddiy odatdagi rasmiyliklar tufayli hech qanday yaxshilik qilolmaydi.

en: If I died, for instance, and left that sum to your sister in my will, surely she wouldn’t refuse it?” “Very likely she would.” “Oh, no, indeed.
uz: Misol uchun, agar men o'lib, o'sha miqdorni singilingizga vasiyatnomada qoldirganimda, albatta, u uni rad etmasmidi?Agar bo'lmasa, rad etishi mumkin.Oh, yo'q, albatta.

en: However, if you refuse it, so be it, though ten thousand roubles is a capital thing to have on occasion.
uz: Biroq, agar siz rad qilsangiz, o'n ming rubl pulga ega bo'lsangiz ham, bunday bo'lsin.

en: In any case I beg you to repeat what I have said to Avdotya Romanovna.” “No, I won’t.” “In that case, Rodion Romanovitch, I shall be obliged to try and see her myself and worry her by doing so.” “And if I do tell her, will you not try to see her?” “I don’t know really what to say.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, Avdotya Romanovnaga aytganimni takrorlashingizni iltimos qilaman. Yo'q, men qilmayman. O'sha holda, Rodion Romanovitch, men uni o'zim ko'rishga va uni tashvishlantirishga majbur bo'laman. Va agar men unga aytsam, siz uni ko'rishga urinmaysizmi?Haqiqatan ham nima deb aytishni bilmayman.

en: I should like very much to see her once more.” “Don’t hope for it.” “I’m sorry.
uz: Men uni yana bir bor ko'rishni juda xohlayman.    Umid qilmang.   Kechirasiz.

en: But you don’t know me.
uz: Ammo siz meni tanimaysiz.

en: Perhaps we may become better friends.”
uz: Ehtimol, biz yaxshiroq do'st bo'lishimiz mumkin.

en: “You think we may become friends?” “And why not?” Svidrigaïlov said, smiling.
uz: Sizning fikringizcha, biz do'st bo'lishimiz mumkinmi?Va nima uchun yo'q? Svidrigailov tabassum bilan dedi.

en: He stood up and took his hat.
uz: U o'rnidan turib, to'pqini olib ketdi.

en: “I didn’t quite intend to disturb you and I came here without reckoning on it … though I was very much struck by your face this morning.” “Where did you see me this morning?” Raskolnikov asked uneasily.
uz: Men sizni bezovta qilish niyatim yo'q edi va men bu yerga o'ylamasdan keldim ... garchi bugun ertalab yuzingiz meni juda hayratda qoldirgan bo'lsa-da.Siz meni bu kuni qayerda ko'rdingiz? Raskolnikov xavotir bilan so'radi.

en: “I saw you by chance.
uz: Men sizni tasodifan ko'rdim.

en: … I kept fancying there is something about you like me.
uz: ... Men o'zim kabi sizda biror narsa borligini o'yladim.

en: … But don’t be uneasy.
uz: Ammo bezovta bo'lmang.

en: I am not intrusive; I used to get on all right with cardsharpers, and I never bored Prince Svirbey, a great personage who is a distant relation of mine, and I could write about Raphael’s Madonna in Madam Prilukov’s album, and I never left Marfa Petrovna’s side for seven years, and I used to stay the night at Viazemsky’s house in the Hay Market in the old days, and I may go up in a balloon with Berg, perhaps.” “Oh, all right.
uz: Men g'alati odam emasman; men kartoshkalar bilan yaxshi munosabatda bo'lganman va mendan uzoq qarindosh bo'lgan Prins Svirbeydan hech qachon charchamaganman va Raphael Madonna haqida Madam Prilukovning albomida yozishim mumkin edi, va men Marfa Petrovnoni yetti yil davomida hech qachon tashlab ketmaganman va eski kunlarda Hay bozoridagi Viazemsky uyida kechalarimni o'tkazardim va men Berg bilan ballonda, ehtimol, o'tishim mumkin.Oh, yaxshi.

en: Are you starting soon on your travels, may I ask?” “What travels?” “Why, on that ‘journey’; you spoke of it yourself.” “A journey?
uz: Safarlaringizga tez orada kirishyapsizmi, so'rasam bo'ladi? nima sayohat qiladi? Nima uchun, o'sha sayohatda; siz o'zingiz bu haqda gapirgansiz.Sayohat?

en: I did speak of a journey.
uz: Men sayohat haqida gapirganman.

en: Well, that’s a wide subject … if only you knew what you are asking,” he added, and gave a sudden, loud, short laugh.
uz: Bu juda keng mavzu... agar siz nima so'raganingizni bilsangiz edi, - dedi u va to'satdan, baland ovoz bilan qichqiriq qildi.

en: “Perhaps I’ll get married instead of the journey.
uz: Ehtimol sayohatning o'rniga uylanaman.

en: They’re making a match for me.” “Here?” “Yes.” “How have you had time for that?” “But I am very anxious to see Avdotya Romanovna once.
uz: Ular men uchun o'yin tayyorlaydilar.  Bu erda?  Ha. Qanday qilib siz uchun vaqt bo'ldi?  Ammo men Avdotya Romanovna bilan bir marta ko'rishni juda xohlayman.

en: Well, goodbye for the present.
uz: Xo'sh, hozirga kelib, xayrlashamiz.

en: I have forgotten something.
uz: Bir narsani unutib qoldim.

en: Tell your sister, Rodion Romanovitch, that Marfa Petrovna remembered her in her will and left her three thousand roubles.
uz: Oʻz singilingizga Rodion Romanovitchga aytingki, Marfa Petrovna uni vasiyatnomasida eslab, unga uch ming rubl qoldirdi.

en: That’s absolutely certain.
uz: Bu mutlaqo aniq.

en: Marfa Petrovna arranged it a week before her death, and it was done in my presence.
uz: Marfa Petrovna o'limidan bir hafta oldin uni tashkil etdi va men hozir bo'lganimda amalga oshirildi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna will be able to receive the money in two or three weeks.” “Are you telling the truth?” “Yes, tell her.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna ikki-uch hafta ichida pulni olish imkoniga ega bo'ladi. Siz haqiqatni aytyapsizmi?Ha, ayting.

en: I am staying very near you.” As he went out, Svidrigaïlov ran up against Razumihin in the doorway.
uz: Men sizlarning yoningizda yashayman. U tashqariga chiqib ketayotganda, Svidrigailov Razumixinga eshikda duch keldi.

en: II It was nearly eight o’clock.
uz: Deyarli sakkiz soat edi.

en: The two young men hurried to Bakaleyev’s, to arrive before Luzhin.
uz: Ikkala yigit Lushinning oldidan kelib qolish uchun Bakaleyevlarga borishga shoshishdi.

en: “Why, who was that?” asked Razumihin, as soon as they were in the street.
uz: Nima uchun, bu kim edi? - deb so'radi Razumihin, ular ko'chada bo'lganida.

en: “It was Svidrigaïlov, that landowner in whose house my sister was insulted when she was their governess.
uz: Svidrigailov, opam o'z gvobanesi bo'lganida uning uyida haqoratga duchor bo'lgan yer egasi edi.

en: Through his persecuting her with his attentions, she was turned out by his wife, Marfa Petrovna.
uz: U ayolga o'z e'tiborini qaratish orqali uni quvg'in qilib, xotini Marfa Petrovna tomonidan o'zini tashlab ketibdi.

en: This Marfa Petrovna begged Dounia’s forgiveness afterwards, and she’s just died suddenly.
uz: Bu Marfa Petrovna keyinchalik Dounia uchun kechirim so'radi va u to'satdan vafot etdi.

en: It was of her we were talking this morning.
uz: Bugun ertalab gapirganimiz o'sha ayol haqida edi.

en: I don’t know why I’m afraid of that man.
uz: Nega men bu odamdan qo'rqqanimni bilmayman.

en: He came here at once after his wife’s funeral.
uz: U xotini dafnidan so'ng darhol bu yerga keldi.

en: He is very strange, and is determined on doing something.
uz: U juda g'ayritabiiy va biror narsa qilishga qat'iy qaror qiladi.

en: … We must guard Dounia from him … that’s what I wanted to tell you, do you hear?” “Guard her!
uz: ... Douniyani undan himoya qilishimiz kerak... shuni sizga aytmoqchi edim, eshityapsizmi?  Uni himoya qiling!

en: What can he do to harm Avdotya Romanovna?
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaga zarar yetkazish uchun u nima qilishi mumkin?

en: Thank you, Rodya, for speaking to me like that.
uz: Menga shunday gapirganingiz uchun rahmat, Rodya.

en: … We will, we will guard her.
uz: Biz uni himoya qilamiz.

en: Where does he live?” “I don’t know.” “Why didn’t you ask?
uz: U qayerda yashaydi?  Men bilmayman.  Nega siz so'ramagansiz?

en: I’ll find out, though.” “Did you see him?” asked Raskolnikov after a pause.
uz: Biroq, bilib olaman. Siz uni ko'rdingizmi? Raskolnikov biroz to'xtab bo'lgandan so'ng so'radi.

en: “Yes, I noticed him, I noticed him well.” “You did really see him?
uz: Ha, men unga e'tibor berdim, yaxshi e'tibor berdim.  Siz chindan ham uni ko'rdingizmi?

en: You saw him clearly?” Raskolnikov insisted.
uz: Siz uni aniq ko'rdingizmi? Raskolnikov istaydi.

en: “Yes, I remember him perfectly, I should know him in a thousand; I have a good memory for faces.” They were silent again.
uz: Ha, men uni mukammal eslayman, uni mingdan taniyman; yuzlarni yaxshi eslayman. Ular yana jim bo'lishdi.

en: … that’s all right,” muttered Raskolnikov.
uz: ... bu yaxshi, - dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “Do you know, I fancied … I keep thinking that it may have been an hallucination.”
uz: Bilasizmi, men o'zimni o'yladim ... bu hallucinatsiya bo'lishi mumkinligini o'ylayman.

en: I don’t understand you.” “Well, you all say,” Raskolnikov went on, twisting his mouth into a smile, “that I am mad.
uz: Men sizlarni tushunmayman. Ha, hammangiz aytasiz, Raskolnikov davom etdi, og'zini tabassumga aylantirib,men g'alati ekanimni aytdi.

en: I thought just now that perhaps I really am mad, and have only seen a phantom.” “What do you mean?” “Why, who can tell?
uz: Men o'zimni haqiqatan ham g'alati deb o'yladim va faqat hayajon ko'rganman.  Nima demoqchisiz?  Nima uchun, kim aytishi mumkin?

en: Perhaps I am really mad, and perhaps everything that happened all these days may be only imagination.” “Ach, Rodya, you have been upset again!
uz: Ehtimol, men haqiqatan ham g'alati bo'lganman va ehtimol bu kunlar davomida sodir bo'lgan hamma narsa shunchaki tasavvur bo'lishi mumkin.Ach, Rodya, siz yana xafa bo'ldingiz!

en: … But what did he say, what did he come for?” Raskolnikov did not answer.
uz: Ammo u nima dedi, nima uchun keldi? Raskolnikov javob bermadi.

en: Razumihin thought a minute.
uz: Razumihin bir daqiqa o'yladi.

en: “Now let me tell you my story,” he began, “I came to you, you were asleep.
uz: Endi o'z hikoyamni aytib beray, - deb boshladi u, - Men sening oldiga keldim, sen uxlab yotgan eding.

en: Then we had dinner and then I went to Porfiry’s, Zametov was still with him.
uz: So'ngra kechki ovqatga bordik va keyin Porfirylarga bordim, Zametov hali ham u bilan edi.

en: I tried to begin, but it was no use.
uz: Men boshlashga harakat qildim, lekin foydasi yo'q edi.

en: I couldn’t speak in the right way.
uz: Men to'g'ri tarzda gapira olmasdim.

en: They don’t seem to understand and can’t understand, but are not a bit ashamed.
uz: Ular tushunmayotganga o'xshaydilar va tushunolmaydilar, ammo biroz ham uyalmaydilar.

en: I drew Porfiry to the window, and began talking to him, but it was still no use.
uz: Men Porfirni derazaga olib bordim va u bilan gaplashishni boshladim, ammo bu hali ham foydasiz edi.

en: He looked away and I looked away.
uz: U o'zgaga qaradi va men o'zgaga qaradim.

en: At last I shook my fist in his ugly face, and told him as a cousin I’d brain him.
uz: Nihoyat, men o'zimning qo'limni uning qo'rqinchli yuziga urdim va unga o'g'lim sifatida aytdimki, men uni o'ylayman.

en: He merely looked at me, I cursed and came away.
uz: U menga shunchaki ko'z tikdi, men la'natlab ketdim va ketdim.

en: To Zametov I didn’t say a word.
uz: Zametovga bir so'z ham aytmadim.

en: But, you see, I thought I’d made a mess of it, but as I went downstairs a brilliant idea struck me: why should we trouble?
uz: Ammo, ko'ryapsizmi, men bu ishni buzganimni o'ylardim, lekin pastga tushayotganimda menga ajoyib bir fikr keldi: nega bezovta qilishimiz kerak?

en: Of course if you were in any danger or anything, but why need you care?
uz: Albatta, agar siz xavf ostida bo'lsangiz yoki boshqa narsada bo'lsangiz, lekin nima uchun bu sizga g'amxo'rlik qilishi kerak?

en: You needn’t care a hang for them.
uz: Siz ular haqida g'amxo'rlik qilishingiz kerak emas.

en: We shall have a laugh at them afterwards, and if I were in your place I’d mystify them more than ever.
uz: Keyinchalik ularga kulishadi va men sizning o'rningda bo'lsam, ularni har qachongidan ham ko'proq g'alatilashtiraman.

en: How ashamed they’ll be afterwards!
uz: Keyinchalik ular qanchalik sharmanda bo'lishadi!

en: We can thrash them afterwards, but let’s laugh at them now!” “To be sure,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Keyingi safar ularni urib tashlashimiz mumkin, lekin hozir ularga kulishamiz! - deb javob berdi Raskolnikov.

en: “But what will you say tomorrow?” he thought to himself.
uz: Ammo ertaga nima deysiz? - deb o'yladi u o'ziga.

en: Strange to say, till that moment it had never occurred to him to wonder what Razumihin would think when he knew.
uz: Ajablanarlisi shundaki, o'sha paytgacha Razumihin bilganda nima deb o'ylashi unga hech qachon kelmagan.

en: As he thought it, Raskolnikov looked at him.
uz: Raskolnikov o'ylab ko'rganida unga qarab qo'ydi.

en: Razumihin’s account of his visit to Porfiry had very little interest for him, so much had come and gone since then.
uz: Razumihinning Porfirga tashrif buyurish haqidagi hikoyasi unga juda kam qiziqish ko'rsatdi, chunki o'sha paytdan beri ko'p narsalar kelib-ketdi.

en: In the corridor they came upon Luzhin; he had arrived punctually at eight, and was looking for the number, so that all three went in together without greeting or looking at one another.
uz: Koridorda ular Luzhinni uchratishdi; u sakkizda o'z vaqtida kelgan edi va raqamni qidirib topgan edi, shuning uchun uchtasi ham salomlashmasdan yoki bir-birlariga qaramasdan birga kirishdi.

en: The young men walked in first, while Pyotr Petrovitch, for good manners, lingered a little in the passage, taking off his coat.
uz: Yoshlar birinchi bo'lib kirishdi, Pyotr Petrovitch esa yaxshi xulq-atvorlar uchun yo'ldan o'tib, ko'ylagini olib, biroz qoldi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna

en: came forward at once to greet him in the doorway, Dounia was welcoming her brother.
uz: Dounia o'z ukasini kutib olish uchun darhol uyiga kelibdi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch walked in and quite amiably, though with redoubled dignity, bowed to the ladies.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch kirib keldi va juda mehribonlik bilan, garchi munosabati ikki baravar ko'paygan bo'lsa-da, xonimlarga sajda qildi.

en: He looked, however, as though he were a little put out and could not yet recover himself.
uz: Biroq, u biroz charchagan va hali o'zini tiklay olmagan bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna, who seemed also a little embarrassed, hastened to make them all sit down at the round table where a samovar was boiling.
uz: Pulcheria Aleksandrovna ham biroz uyalgan ko'rinardi, shunda hammasini samovar qaynatadigan davra suhbatiga o'tirtirtirishga majbur qildi.

en: Dounia and Luzhin were facing one another on opposite sides of the table.
uz: Dounia va Luzhin bir-biriga qaragan holda stolning qarama-qarshi tomonlarida o'tirgan.

en: Razumihin and Raskolnikov were facing Pulcheria Alexandrovna, Razumihin was next to Luzhin and Raskolnikov was beside his sister.
uz: Razumihin va Raskolnikov Pulcheria Alexandrovna bilan qaray boshlashdi, Razumihin Luzhin va Raskolnikov singlisi yonida edi.

en: A moment’s silence followed.
uz: Oʻshanda sekinlik davom etdi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch deliberately drew out a cambric handkerchief reeking of scent and blew his nose with an air of a benevolent man who felt himself slighted, and was firmly resolved to insist on an explanation.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch o'zi bila turib, xushbo'y tutatqi bilan kambrik to'qima chiqqani va o'zini kamsitilgan his qilgan mehribon odamning havo bilan o'z nuzini o'tkazgani sababli, tushuntirishni talab qilishga qat'iy qaror qildi.

en: In the passage the idea had occurred to him to keep on his overcoat and walk away, and so give the two ladies a sharp and emphatic lesson and make them feel the gravity of the position.
uz: O'qiganimizda, uning g'oyalari paydo bo'lgan edi: kiyimini kiyib ketib ketib, ikki xonimga o'ta qattiq va qat'iy saboq berib, o'zlarining vazifasining og'irligini his etishlari kerak.

en: But he could not bring himself to do this.
uz: Ammo u o'zini bunday qilishga majburlay olmagan.
