uz: "Qayta borib, ularning oldiga bor", - dedi u to'satdan va tez o'girilib, uydan chiqib ketdi.

en: I will not attempt to describe how Razumihin went back to the ladies, how he soothed them, how he protested that Rodya needed rest in his illness, protested that Rodya was sure to come, that he would come every day, that he was very, very much upset, that he must not be irritated, that he, Razumihin, would watch over him, would get him a doctor, the best doctor, a consultation.
uz: Razumihin ayollarga qaytib kelganini, ularni qanday tinchlantirganini, Rodya kasalligida dam olishga muhtojligini, Rodya albatta kelishini, har kuni kelishini, juda, juda xafa bo'lganini, g'azablanmasligi kerakligini, u, Razumihin, uning ustidan g'amxo'rlik qilishini, shifokor, eng yaxshi shifokor, maslahat olishini tanqid qilganini tasvirlashga harakat qilmayman.

en: … In fact from that evening Razumihin took his place with them as a son and a brother.
uz: Aslida, o'sha kechadan boshlab Razumihin o'z o'rinini ular bilan o'g'il va aka-uka sifatida egallab oldi.

en: IV Raskolnikov went straight to the house on the canal bank where Sonia lived.
uz: Raskolnikov to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Sonia IV yashaydigan kanal qirg'og'idagi uyga bordi.

en: It was an old green house of three storeys.
uz: Bu eski uch qavatli yashil uy edi.

en: He found the porter and obtained from him vague directions as to the whereabouts of Kapernaumov, the tailor.
uz: U portiyerni topib, undan ko'rinmas yo'nalishlarni olgan va ko'rinmas ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rinishdagi ko'rsatmalarni olgan.

en: Having found in the corner of the courtyard the entrance to the dark and narrow staircase, he mounted to the second floor and came out into a gallery that ran round the whole second storey over the yard.
uz: hovuzning burchagida qorong'i va chekkani eshikni topib, u ikkinchi qavatga chiqib, hovuz ustidan ikkinchi qavatni aylanib o'tadigan galereyaga kirdi.

en: While he was wandering in the darkness, uncertain where to turn for Kapernaumov’s door, a door opened three paces from him; he mechanically took hold of it.
uz: U qorong'ilikda aylanib yurganida, qayerga borishni bilmay, Kafarnahumning eshigidan uch qadam uzoqlikda bir eshik ochildi; u mashinada uni ushlab qoldi.

en: “Who is there?” a woman’s voice asked uneasily.
uz: Kim bor? - deb so'radi ayolning ovozi.

en: “It’s I … come to see you,” answered Raskolnikov, and he walked into the tiny entry.
uz: Men ... sizni ko'rish uchun keldim, - deb javob berdi Raskolnikov va u kichkina eshikga kirdi.

en: On a broken chair stood a candle in a battered copper candlestick.
uz: Buzilgan o'rinbosar ustida toshbo'ronlangan mis chiroqchada chiroq turgan edi.

en: Good heavens!” cried Sonia weakly, and she stood rooted to the spot.
uz: Yaxshi osmonlar! - deb Sonia zaiflik bilan baqirdi va u o'z o'rnida turib oldi.

en: “Which is your room?
uz: Sizning xonangiz qayerda?

en: This way?” and Raskolnikov, trying not to look at her, hastened in.
uz: Shu yo'ldan? va Raskolnikov unga qaramaslikka harakat qilib, orqaga kirdi.

en: A minute later Sonia, too, came in with the candle, set down the candlestick and, completely disconcerted, stood before him inexpressibly agitated and apparently frightened by his unexpected visit.
uz: Bir daqiqa o'tgach, Sonia ham shisha bilan kirib keldi, chiroqni qo'ydi va butunlay g'alati bo'lib, so'zsiz g'ayratli va uning kutilmagan tashrifi tufayli qo'rqqan holda uning oldida turdi.

en: The colour rushed suddenly to her pale face and tears came into her eyes … She felt sick and ashamed and happy, too.
uz: Birdan uning ko'z o'g'rilari ko'z yoshlariga tushib ketdi va u kasal, uyat va baxtli bo'ldi.

en: … Raskolnikov turned away quickly and sat on a chair by the table.
uz: ... Raskolnikov tezda yuz o'girib, stol yonidagi o'rindiqga o'tirdi.

en: He scanned the room in a rapid glance.
uz: U xonani tezda ko'rib chiqdi.

en: It was a large but exceedingly low-pitched room, the only one let by the Kapernaumovs, to whose rooms a closed door led in the wall on the left.
uz: Bu katta, ammo juda past bo'lgan xona edi, faqatgina Kapernaumovlar tomonidan qo'yilgan xonadir, ularning xonalariga chap tomonidagi devor orqali yopilgan eshik olib borardi.

en: In the opposite side on the right hand wall was another
uz: O'ng qo'lning o'ng tomonidagi devorning qarama-qarshi tomonida yana bir devor bor edi

en: door, always kept locked.
uz: Eshikni doimo qulflab qo'ying.

en: That led to the next flat, which formed a separate lodging.
uz: Bu esa keyingi kvartiraga olib keldi, u alohida uyni tashkil etdi.

en: Sonia’s room looked like a barn; it was a very irregular quadrangle and this gave it a grotesque appearance.
uz: Sonia xonasi cho'nqaga o'xshaydi; u juda noaniq to'rtburchak edi va bu unga g'alati ko'rinishni beradi.

en: A wall with three windows looking out on to the canal ran aslant so that one corner formed a very acute angle, and it was difficult to see in it without very strong light.
uz: Kanalga qarashli uchta oynali devor o'z-o'zidan oshib borardi, shuning uchun bir burchak juda keskin burchani tashkil etdi va juda kuchli yorug'lik bo'lmasa, u erda ko'rish qiyin edi.

en: The other corner was disproportionately obtuse.
uz: Boshqa burchak o'z-o'zidan ko'p bo'lmagan darajada bo'sh edi.

en: There was scarcely any furniture in the big room: in the corner on the right was a bedstead, beside it, nearest the door, a chair.
uz: Katta xonada deyarli hech qanday mebel yo'q edi: o'ng burchakda yotoq, uning yonida, eshikdan eng yaqin, o'rindiq bor edi.

en: A plain, deal table covered by a blue cloth stood against the same wall, close to the door into the other flat.
uz: O'sha devorga o'xshaydigan, ko'k kiyim bilan qoplangan oddiy ish stoli boshqa xonadonga kiradigan eshikning yaqinida turardi.

en: Two rush-bottom chairs stood by the table.
uz: Ishxonada ikki taxt o'rinbosari o'tirgan.

en: On the opposite wall near the acute angle stood a small plain wooden chest of drawers looking, as it were, lost in a desert.
uz: O'tkir burchak yaqinidagi qarama-qarshi devorda kichik oddiy yog'och sovg'alar qutisi turgan edi, xuddi sahroda yo'qolganidek ko'rinardi.

en: That was all there was in the room.
uz: Xonada faqat shu narsa bor edi.

en: The yellow, scratched and shabby wallpaper was black in the corners.
uz: Sariq, qirg'oq va bo'g'in wallpaper burchaklarda qora edi.

en: It must have been damp and full of fumes in the winter.
uz: Qishda u nam va tutun bilan to'lib-toshgan bo'lishi kerak.

en: There was every sign of poverty; even the bedstead had no curtain.
uz: Kambag'allikning barcha belgilari bor edi; hatto yotoqxonada parda yo'q edi.

en: Sonia looked in silence at her visitor, who was so attentively and unceremoniously scrutinising her room, and even began at last to tremble with terror, as though she was standing before her judge and the arbiter of her destinies.
uz: Sonia o'z xonasini shu qadar diqqat bilan va marosimsiz tekshirgan mehmonni sukut saqlash bilan ko'rib turdi va hatto nihoyat qo'rquvdan titra boshladi, xuddi o'z hakamining va taqdirining hakamining oldida turgandek.

en: … It’s eleven, isn’t it?” he asked, still not lifting his eyes.
uz: - O'n bir soat, shunday emasmi? - deb so'radi u, hali ham ko'zlarini ko'tarmay.

en: “Yes,” muttered Sonia, “oh yes, it is,” she added, hastily, as though in that lay her means of escape.
uz: Ha,  shubhalandi Sonia, oh, ha, shunday,  u shoshilinch qo'shimcha qildi, xuddi u yerda uning qochish usuli bo'lgani kabi.

en: “My landlady’s clock has just struck  … I heard it myself.
uz: Mening uy egasining soati to'g'ri urdi... O'zim eshitdim.

en: …” “I’ve come to you for the last time,” Raskolnikov went on gloomily, although this was the first time.
uz: ...Men sizlarning oldingizga so'nggi marta keldim, Raskolnikov bu birinchi marta bo'lsa-da, tushkunlikka tushdi.

en: “I may perhaps not see you again …” “Are you … going away?” “I don’t know … tomorrow.
uz: Ehtimol, men sizni yana ko'rmasam bo'ladi... Siz... ketyapsizmi? Bilmayman... ertaga.

en: …” “Then you are not coming to Katerina Ivanovna tomorrow?” Sonia’s voice shook.
uz: ... Shunday bo'lsa, ertaga Katerina Ivanovnaga kelmaysanmi? Sonia ovozidan shovqin keldi.

en: I shall know tomorrow morning.
uz: Ertaga ertalab bilaman.

en: … Never mind that: I’ve come to say one word.
uz: ... Buni e'tiborsiz qoldiring: men bir so'z aytishga keldim.

en: …” He raised his brooding eyes to her and suddenly noticed that he was sitting down while she was all the while standing before him.
uz: ... U qizga ko'zlarini ko'tarib, birdan uning o'tirganini payqadi, u esa uning oldida to'xtadi.

en: “Why are you standing?
uz: Nima uchun to'xtab turibsiz?

en: Sit down,” he said in a changed voice, gentle and friendly.
uz: O'tiring, - dedi u o'zgartirilgan ovoz bilan, muloyim va do'stona.

en: He looked kindly and almost compassionately at her.
uz: U ayolga mehribonlik va mehribonlik ila qaradi.

en: Quite transparent, like a dead hand.” He took her hand.
uz: Toʻgʻri shaffof, oʻlik qoʻl kabi. U uning qoʻlini oldi.

en: Sonia smiled faintly.
uz: Soniya kamchilik bilan tabassum qildi.

en: “I have always been like that,” she said.
uz: "Men har doim ham shunday edim", - dedi u.

en: “Even when you lived at home?” “Yes.” “Of course, you were,” he added abruptly and the expression of his face and the sound of his voice changed again suddenly.
uz: Hatto uyda yashaganingizda ham?Ha. Albatta, shunday edingiz, u to'satdan qo'shimcha qildi va yuzning ifodasini va ovozini eshitish so'zi birdan yana o'zgarib ketdi.

en: He looked round him once more.
uz: U yana atrofini ko'rdi.

en: “You rent this room from the Kapernaumovs?” “Yes.
uz: Siz bu xonani Kapernaumovlardan ijaraga olganmisiz? Ha.

en: …” “They live there, through that door?” “Yes.
uz: ... Ular shu eshikdan o'sha yerda yashaydilarmi?   Ha.

en: … They have another room like this.” “All in one room?” “Yes.” “I should be afraid in your room at night,” he observed gloomily.
uz: Ularda yana bir xonasi ham bor. Hamma bir xonada?Ha. Kechasi sizning xonangizda qo'rqishim kerak, - dedi u tushkunlik bilan.

en: “They are very good people, very kind,” answered Sonia, who still seemed bewildered, “and all the furniture, everything … everything is theirs.
uz: Ular juda yaxshi odamlar, juda mehribon, - deb javob berdi Sonia, u hali ham g'alati ko'rinardi, - va barcha mebellar, hamma narsa ... hamma narsa ularning.

en: And they are very kind and the children, too, often come to see me.” “They all stammer, don’t they?” “Yes.
uz: Ular juda mehribon va bolalar ham meni ko'pincha ko'rishga kelishadi. Ular hammasi qichqirishadi, shunday emasmi?Ha.

en: … He stammers and he’s lame.
uz: ... U stammers va u s cho'loq.

en: … It’s not exactly that she stammers, but she can’t speak plainly.
uz: ... U to'g'ridan-to'g'ri gapirmaydi, lekin aniq gapira olmaydi.

en: She is a very kind woman.
uz: U juda mehribon ayol.

en: And he used to be a house serf.
uz: Va u bir vaqtlar uy qul bo'lgan.

en: And there are seven children … and it’s only the eldest one that stammers and the others are simply ill … but they don’t stammer.
uz: Yetti nafar bola bor va faqat keksa bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bemor bo'ladi... lekin bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lmasa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lsa, bo'lmasa bo'lsa, bo'lmasa bo'ladi.

en: … But where did you hear about them?” she added with some surprise.
uz: Ammo siz ular haqida qayerdan eshitgansiz? u ba'zi bir ajablanib qo'shimcha qildi.

en: “Your father told me, then.
uz: Otam menga aytdi, o'shanda.

en: He told me all about you.
uz: U menga siz haqingizda hamma narsani aytib berdi.

en: … And how you went out at six o’clock and came back at nine and how Katerina Ivanovna knelt down by your bed.” Sonia was confused.
uz: ...Va soat oltida chiqib, to'qqizda qaytib kelganingiz va Katerina Ivanovna sizning yotoq yoningizda tiz cho'kkaningiz haqida. Sonia g'alati edi.

en: “I fancied I saw him today,” she whispered hesitatingly.
uz: Bugun uni ko'rdim deb o'yladim, deb o'yladim.

en: I was walking in the street, out there at the corner, about ten o’clock and he seemed to be walking in front.
uz: Men ko'chada, burchada, soat o'n atrofida yurgan edim va u oldinda yurayotganini ko'rardim.

en: I wanted to go to Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Men Katerina Ivanovna bilan uchrashishni xohladim.

en: …” “You were walking in the streets?” “Yes,” Sonia whispered abruptly, again overcome with confusion and looking down.
uz: ... Siz ko'chalarda yurganmisiz?  Ha, Sonia birdan shovqin qildi, yana g'alati va pastga qarab qoldi.

en: “Katerina Ivanovna used to beat you, I dare say?” “Oh no, what are you saying?
uz: Katerina Ivanovna sizni urardi, deyishga jur'at qilamanmi?Oh yo'q, nima deyyapsan?

en: No!” Sonia looked at him almost with dismay.
uz: Yo'q! Sonia unga deyarli tushkunlikka tushib qaradi.

en: “You love her, then?” “Love her?
uz: Shunday qilib, siz uni sevasizmi?

en: Of course!” said Sonia with plaintive emphasis, and she clasped her hands in distress.
uz: Shubhasiz! - dedi Sonia shikoyatkorlik bilan va u xavotirda qo'llarini qo'shdi.

en: You see, she is quite like a child.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, u bola kabi.

en: … Her mind is quite unhinged, you see … from sorrow.
uz: Uning ongini juda ko'p o'zgartirib qo'ydi, siz ko'rib turibsiz... qayg'udan.

en: And how clever she used to be … how generous … how kind!
uz: Va u qanchalik aqlli edi ... qanchalik saxiy ... qanchalik mehribon!

en: Ah, you don’t understand, you don’t understand!” Sonia said this as though in despair, wringing her hands in excitement and distress.
uz: Ah, siz tushunmayapsiz, tushunmayapsiz! Sonia bu so'zlarni umidsizlikka tushib, qo'llarini g'ayrat va qayg'uga to'kib-tushirib aytgan.

en: Her pale cheeks flushed, there was a look of anguish in her eyes.
uz: Uning ko'p bo'laklari qizg'inlab, ko'zlarida qayg'u ko'rinishi paydo bo'ldi.

en: It was clear that she was stirred to the very depths, that she was longing to speak, to champion, to express something.
uz: U chuqur o'ziga jalb bo'lganini, gapirishni, chempionlik qilishni, biror narsani ifoda etishni orzu qilganini aniq ko'rish mumkin edi.

en: A sort of insatiable compassion, if one may so express it, was reflected in every feature of her face.
uz: Uning yuzidagi har bir nuqtada, agar shunday qilib ifodalash mumkin bo'lsa, charchamaydigan rahm-shafqat ko'rindi.

en: Good heavens, beat me!
uz: Yaxshi osmonlar, meni mag'lub qiling!

en: And if she did beat me, what then?
uz: Va agar u meni ursa, keyin nima bo'ladi?

en: You know nothing, nothing about it.
uz: Siz hech narsa bilmaysiz, hech narsa bilmaysiz.

en: … She is so unhappy … ah, how unhappy!
uz: U juda baxtsiz... ah, naqadar baxtsiz!

en: … She is seeking righteousness, she is pure.
uz: U adolatni izlaydi, pokdir.

en: She has such faith that there must be righteousness everywhere and she expects it.
uz: U har yerda adolat bo'lishi kerakligiga ishonadi va buni kutadi.

en: … And if you were to torture her, she wouldn’t do wrong.
uz: Va agar siz uni qiynashingiz kerak bo'lsa, u hech qanday yomon ish qilmaydi.

en: She doesn’t see that it’s impossible for people to be righteous and she is angry at it.
uz: U odamlarning solih bo'lishlari mumkin emasligini ko'rmaydi va bunga g'azablangan.

en: Like a child, like a child.
uz: Bola kabi, bola kabi.

en: She is good!” “And what will happen to you?” Sonia looked at him inquiringly.
uz: U yaxshi odam! Va senga nima bo'ladi? Sonia unga savol-javob bilan qaradi.

en: “They are left on your hands, you see.
uz: Ular sizning qo'lingizda qoldirilgan.

en: They were all on your hands before, though.
uz: Biroq, ularning barchasi ilgari sizning qo'lingizda edi.

en: … And your father came to you to beg for drink.
uz: Otamiz ichimlik so'rab senga kelibdi.

en: Well, how will it be now?” “I don’t know,” Sonia articulated mournfully.
uz: Xo'sh, endi qanday bo'ladi?Bilmayman,Sonia qayg'uli so'zlarni aytdi.

en: “Will they stay there?” “I don’t know.
uz: Ular o'sha yerda qoladilarmi? Bilmayman.

en: … They are in debt for the lodging, but the landlady, I hear, said today that she wanted to get rid of them, and Katerina
uz: Ular uy-joy uchun qarzdor, lekin uy egasi bugun ularni yo'q qilishni xohlaganini aytdi va Katerina ham.

en: Ivanovna says that she won’t stay another minute.” “How is it she is so bold?
uz: Ivanovna yana bir daqiqa qolmayotganini aytadi.Qanday qilib u bunday jasoratli?

en: She relies upon you?” “Oh, no, don’t talk like that.
uz: U sizga tayanadi?

en: … We are one, we live like one.” Sonia was agitated again and even angry, as though a canary or some other little bird were to be angry.
uz: ... Biz birmiz, biz birdek yashaymiz. Sonia yana g'azabga to'ldi va hatto g'azabga to'ldi, xuddi kanari yoki boshqa bir qush g'azabga to'lganidek.

en: “And what could she do?
uz: Va u nima qila oladi?

en: What, what could she do?” she persisted, getting hot and excited.
uz: Nima, nima qila oladi? U issiq va hayajonli bo'lib, o'zini tutdi.

en: “And how she cried today!
uz: Va u bugun qanchalik yig'ladi!

en: Her mind is unhinged, haven’t you noticed it?
uz: Uning ongi o'zgarib qolgan, buni sezmayapsizmi?

en: At one minute she is worrying like a child that everything should be right tomorrow, the lunch and all that.
uz: Bir daqiqada u bola kabi ertaga hamma narsa yaxshi bo'lishi kerakligi haqida tashvishlanmoqda, kechki ovqat va shunga o'xshash narsalar.

en: … Then she is wringing her hands, spitting blood, weeping, and all at once she will begin knocking her head against the wall, in despair.
uz: Keyin u qo'llarini burib, qon oqib, yig'lay boshlaydi va birdan boshini devorga urib, umidsizlikka tushadi.

en: Then she will be comforted again.
uz: Keyin u yana tasalli topadi.

en: She builds all her hopes on you; she says that you will help her now and that she will borrow a little money somewhere and go to her native town with me and set up a boarding school for the daughters of gentlemen and take me to superintend it, and we will begin a new splendid life.
uz: U barcha umidlarini sizga bog'laydi; siz unga hozir yordam berasiz va u bir joyda biroz pul qarz oladi, men bilan o'z shaharchasida yashaydi, xonimlarning qizlari uchun internat o'rnatadi va meni uni nazorat qilishga olib ketadi, biz esa yangi ajoyib hayotga boshlanamiz.

en: And she kisses and hugs me, comforts me, and you know she has such faith, such faith in her fancies!
uz: Va u meni o'padi va quchoqlaydi, meni tasalli beradi va siz uning o'z xayollariga ishonishi mumkinligini bilasiz!

en: One can’t contradict her.
uz: Unga zid bo'lish mumkin emas.

en: And all the day long she has been washing, cleaning, mending.
uz: Va kun bo'yi u yuvishni, tozalashni, tuzatishni davom ettirmoqda.

en: She dragged the wash tub into the room with her feeble hands and sank on the bed, gasping for breath.
uz: U o'z qo'llari zaif bo'lib, suvni xonaga tortib olib kirdi va nafas olish uchun nafas olib, yotoq ustiga cho'kdi.

en: We went this morning to the shops to buy shoes for Polenka and Lida for theirs are quite worn out.
uz: Bugun ertalab biz Polenka va Lida uchun poyabzal sotib olish uchun do'konlarga bordik, chunki ularning poyabzallari juda eskirgan.

en: Only the money we’d reckoned wasn’t enough, not nearly enough.
uz: Faqat biz hisoblagan pul yetarli emas, deyarli yetarli emas edi.

en: And she picked out such dear little boots, for she has taste, you don’t know.
uz: Va u shuncha qimmatli kichik botlarni tanladi, chunki uning ta'mi bor, siz bilmaysiz.

en: And there in the shop she burst out crying before the shopmen because she hadn’t enough.
uz: Keyin do'konda u do'konchilar oldida yig'lab yubordi, chunki u yetarlicha yo'q edi.

en: … Ah, it was sad to see her.
uz: Ah, uni ko'rish juda achinarli edi.

en: …” “Well, after that I can understand your living like this,” Raskolnikov said with a bitter smile.
uz: ...Ehtimol, bundan keyin men sizning hayotingizni shunday tushunaman, - dedi Raskolnikov achchiq tabassum bilan.

en: “And aren’t you sorry for them?
uz: Va siz ular uchun achinmayapsizmi?

en: Aren’t you sorry?” Sonia flew at him again.
uz: Xo'sh, afsuslanmayapsanmi? Sonia yana unga uchdi.

en: “Why, I know, you gave your last penny yourself, though you’d seen nothing of it, and if you’d seen everything, oh dear!
uz: Nima uchun, bilaman, siz hech narsa ko'rmagan bo'lsangiz ham, o'zingiz ham so'nggi tangalaringizni bergansiz va agar hamma narsani ko'rgan bo'lsangiz ham, oh, aziz!

en: And how often, how often I’ve brought her to tears!
uz: Va men uni qanchalik tez-tez, qanchalik tez-tez ko'z yoshlariga to'ldirganman!

en: Only a week before his death.
uz: O'limidan atigi bir hafta oldin.

en: And how often I’ve done it!
uz: Va men buni qanchalik tez-tez qildim!

en: Ah, I’ve been wretched at the thought of it all day!” Sonia wrung her hands as she spoke at the pain of remembering it.
uz: Ah, bu haqda butun kun o'ylagani menga og'ir keldi! Sonia buni eslab qolish og'rig'ida gapirganida qo'llarini qovurib qo'ydi.

en: I went to see them,” she went on, weeping, “and father said, ‘read me something, Sonia, my head aches, read to me, here’s a book.’ He had a book he had got from Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov, he lives there, he always used to get hold of such funny books.
uz: Men ularni ko'rishga bordim, u yig'lab ketdi, otam esa: "Meni bir narsa o'qib ber, Sonia, boshim og'riydi, o'qib ber, bu yerda bir kitob bor.

en: And I said, ‘I can’t stay,’ as I didn’t want to read, and I’d gone in chiefly to show Katerina Ivanovna some collars.
uz: Men: "Men qololmayman, chunki o'qishni istamayman", - dedim va asosan Katerina Ivanovnaga ko'rinish to'plamini ko'rsatishga bordim.

en: Lizaveta, the pedlar, sold me some collars and cuffs cheap, pretty, new, embroidered ones.
uz: Lizaveta, o'g'irlatgich, menga arzon, chiroyli, yangi, tikilgan bo'yinchoqlar va qo'ychoqlar sotdi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna liked them very much; she put them on and looked at herself in the glass and was delighted with them.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna ularni juda yaxshi ko'rdi; u ularni kiydirib, o'ziga ko'rinadi va ulardan mamnun bo'ldi.

en: ‘Make me a present of them, Sonia,’ she said, ‘please do.’ ‘Please do,’ she said, she wanted them so much.
uz: Ular uchun menga sovg'a bering, Sonia, - dedi u. - Iltimos, qilinglar. - Iltimos, qilinglar, - dedi u. - U ularni juda xohlagan.

en: And when could she wear them?
uz: Va qachon u ularni kiyishi mumkin?

en: They just reminded her of her old happy days.
uz: Ular faqatgina qadimgi baxtli kunlarini eslatishdi.

en: She looked at herself in the glass, admired herself, and she has no clothes at all, no things of her own, hasn’t had all these years!
uz: O'ziga o'zi ko'rinardi, o'ziga e'tibor qaratdi va bu yillar davomida hech qanday kiyim-kechak, o'z narsalari yo'q edi!

en: And she never asks anyone for anything; she is proud, she’d sooner give away everything.
uz: U hech kimdan hech narsa so'ramaydi; u mag'rur, hamma narsasini berishdan ko'ra tezroq o'zini tashlaydi.

en: And these she asked for, she liked them so much.
uz: Va bularni u so'ragan, u juda yaxshi ko'rgan.

en: And I was sorry to give them.
uz: Va men ularni berishim uchun afsuslanaman.

en: ‘What use are they to you, Katerina Ivanovna?’ I said.
uz: Ular sizga qanday foyda keltiradi, Katerina Ivanovna? - dedim men.

en: I spoke like that to her, I ought not to have said that!
uz: Men unga shunday gapirganman, men bunday aytmasam kerak edi!

en: She gave me such a look.
uz: U menga shunday ko'z tikdi.

en: And she was so grieved, so grieved at my refusing her.
uz: Men uni rad etganimdan u juda xafa edi.

en: And it was so sad to see.
uz: Va uni ko'rish juda ayanchli edi.

en: … And she was not grieved for the collars, but for my refusing, I saw that.
uz: U bo'yniklar uchun emas, balki men rad etganim uchun xafa bo'lganini ko'rdim.

en: Ah, if only I could bring it all back, change it, take back those words!
uz: Ah, agar men hammasini qaytarib, o'zgartirgan bo'lsam, o'sha so'zlarni qaytarib olsam edi!

en: Ah, if I … but it’s nothing to you!” “Did you know Lizaveta, the pedlar?” “Yes.
uz: Ah, agar men... lekin bu sen uchun hech qanday ahamiyatga ega emas!Lizzaveta, o'yinchi, siz uni tanardingizmi?Ha.

en: … Did you know her?” Sonia asked with some surprise.
uz: - Siz uni taniydingizmi? - so'radi Sonia biroz hayratda.

en: “Katerina Ivanovna is in consumption, rapid consumption; she will soon die,” said Raskolnikov after a pause, without answering her question.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna iste'molda, tez iste'molda; u yaqinda o'ladi, dedi Raskolnikov biroz to'xtab, savollariga javob bermasdan.

en: “Oh, no, no, no!” And Sonia unconsciously clutched both his hands, as though imploring that she should not.
uz: Oh, yo'q, yo'q, yo'q! So'niya o'z-o'zidan qo'llarini o'rab oldi, xuddi buni qilmasligini iltijo qilgan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “But it will be better if she does die.” “No, not better, not at all better!” Sonia unconsciously repeated in dismay.
uz: Ammo u o'lsa yaxshiroq bo'ladi.Yo'q, yaxshi emas, umuman yaxshi emas! Sonia ongsiz ravishda dahshatga tushdi.

en: What can you do except take them to live with you?”
uz: Ular bilan birga yashashdan boshqa nima qilishingiz mumkin?

en: “Oh, I don’t know,” cried Sonia, almost in despair, and she put her hands to her head.
uz: - Bilmayman, - deya qayg'urdi Sonia, deyarli umidsizlikka tushib, qo'llarini boshga qo'ydi.

en: It was evident that that idea had very often occurred to her before and he had only roused it again.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, bu g'oya unga ko'pincha o'tgan va u uni faqat yana uyg'otgan.

en: “And, what, if even now, while Katerina Ivanovna is alive, you get ill and are taken to the hospital, what will happen then?” he persisted pitilessly.
uz: Agar Katerina Ivanovna tirik bo'lganida, hozir ham kasal bo'lib, kasalxonaga yotqizilsangiz, nima bo'ladi? - dedi u shafqatsizlik bilan.

en: That cannot be!” And Sonia’s face worked with awful terror.
uz: Bu bo'lmasligi mumkin! Sonia yuzida dahshatli dahshat paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Cannot be?” Raskolnikov went on with a harsh smile.
uz: Raskolnikov qattiq tabassum bilan davom etdi.

en: “You are not insured against it, are you?
uz: Siz bunga qarshi sug'urta qilinmayapsiz, shundaymi?

en: What will happen to them then?
uz: Keyin ularga nima bo'ladi?

en: They will be in the street, all of them, she will cough and beg and knock her head against some wall, as she did today, and the children will cry.
uz: Ular ko'chada bo'ladilar, hammalari, u bugun qilganidek, qo'shiq, yolvorib, boshini devorga uradi va bolalar yig'laydi.

en: … Then she will fall down, be taken to the police station and to the hospital, she will die, and the children …” “Oh, no.
uz: Keyin u yerga yiqilib, politsiya bo'limiga va kasalxonaga olib ketiladi, u o'lib ketadi va bolalar ...Oh, yo'q.

en: … God will not let it be!” broke at last from Sonia’s overburdened bosom.
uz: ... Xudo bunga yo'l qo'ymaydi! Sofiyaning ortiqcha og'irligi boshiga tushdi.

en: She listened, looking imploringly at him, clasping her hands in dumb entreaty, as though it all depended upon him.
uz: U tinglab, unga iltijo bilan qaradi va hamma narsa unga bog'liq bo'lgani kabi, o'z qo'llarini o'zi bilan bog'lab, so'zsiz iltijo qiladi.

en: Raskolnikov got up and began to walk about the room.
uz: Raskolnikov o'rnidan turib, xonadon atrofida yurishni boshladi.

en: Sonia was standing with her hands and her head hanging in terrible dejection.
uz: Sonia qo'llari va boshini ko'tarib, dahshatli tushkunlikka tushib turardi.

en: “And can’t you save?
uz: Va siz qutqara olmaysizmi?

en: Put by for a rainy day?” he asked, stopping suddenly before her.
uz: Yomg'ir yog'adigan kun uchun qo'yib qo'yganmanmi? - deb so'radi u, birdan uning oldida to'xtab qoldi.

en: “No,” whispered Sonia.
uz: Yo'q,  Sonia shovqin qildi.

en: Have you tried?” he added almost ironically.
uz: Siz harakat qildingizmi? u deyarli ironik tarzda qo'shdi.

en: “Yes.” “And it didn’t come off!
uz: Yes.  Va u tushmadi!

en: No need to ask.” And again he paced the room.
uz: So'rashning hojati yo'q. Va yana u xonani o'zgartirdi.

en: Another minute passed.
uz: Yana bir daqiqa o'tdi.

en: “You don’t get money every day?” Sonia was more confused than ever and colour rushed into her face again.
uz: Siz har kuni pul olmayapsizmi?Sonya har qachongidan ham g'alati bo'lib qoldi va yana uning yuziga rang tushdi.

en: “No,” she whispered with a painful effort.
uz: Yo'q, u og'ir urinish bilan shoshib yubordi.

en: “It will be the same with Polenka, no doubt,” he said suddenly.
uz: "Polenka bilan ham xuddi shunday bo'ladi, shubhasiz", - dedi u to'satdan.

en: It can’t be, no!” Sonia cried aloud in desperation, as though she had been stabbed.
uz: Yo'q bo'lishi mumkin emas! Sonia tushkunlikka tushib, xuddi o'zi bo'g'ib ketgandek baland ovoz bilan yig'ladi.

en: “God would not allow anything so awful!”
uz: Xudo bunday dahshatli ishlarga yo'l qo'ymaydi!

en: “He lets others come to it.” “No, no!
uz: U boshqalarga o'z yo'lidan yurishga ruxsat beradi.Yo'q, yo'q!

en: God will protect her, God!” she repeated beside herself.
uz: Xudo uni himoya qiladi, Xudo! U o'zi yonida takrorladi.

en: “But, perhaps, there is no God at all,” Raskolnikov answered with a sort of malignance, laughed and looked at her.
uz: Ammo, ehtimol, hech qanday Xudo yo'q, Raskolnikov bir xil yomonlik bilan javob berdi, kuldi va unga qarab qo'ydi.

en: Sonia’s face suddenly changed; a tremor passed over it.
uz: Sonisaning yuzi to'satdan o'zgarib ketdi; u titrashdan o'tdi.

en: She looked at him with unutterable reproach, tried to say something, but could not speak and broke into bitter, bitter sobs, hiding her face in her hands.
uz: U unga so'zsiz tanqid bilan qaradi, biror narsa aytishga harakat qiladi, lekin gapira olmaydi va o'z qo'llarida yuzini yashirib, achchiq, achchiq yig'lab yuboraveradi.

en: “You say Katerina Ivanovna’s mind is unhinged; your own mind is unhinged,” he said after a brief silence.
uz: "Sen Katerina Ivonovna fikrini o'zgartirib qo'yganingni aytasan, o'z fikring ham o'zgartirib qo'ygan", - dedi u biroz sukutdan so'ng.

en: Five minutes passed.
uz: Besh daqiqa o'tdi.

en: He still paced up and down the room in silence, not looking at her.
uz: U hali ham xonadonning o'rnidan-o'rnidan pastga va pastga sukut saqlashdi, ayolga qaramasdi.

en: At last he went up to her; his eyes glittered.
uz: Nihoyat, u ayolning oldiga bordi; uning ko'zlari yorqinlik bilan yoritib turardi.

en: He put his two hands on her shoulders and looked straight into her tearful face.
uz: U qo'llarini ayolning shoxlariga qo'ydi va uning ko'z yoshli yuziga to'g'ri qaradi.

en: His eyes were hard, feverish and piercing, his lips were twitching.
uz: Uning ko'zlari qattiq, issiq va cho'kkan edi, og'izlari titraydigan edi.

en: All at once he bent down quickly and dropping to the ground, kissed her foot.
uz: Birdan u tezda tiz cho'kib, yerga yiqilib, uning oyoqlarini o'pdi.

en: Sonia drew back from him as from a madman.
uz: Sonia undan aqldan ozgan odam kabi voz kechdi.

en: And certainly he looked like a madman.
uz: Va albatta, u aqldan ozgan odamga o'xshardi.

en: “What are you doing to me?” she muttered, turning pale, and a sudden anguish clutched at her heart.
uz: - Menga nima qilyapsan? - deb o'yladi u, o'z ko'zidan oqib, ko'nglida qayg'u paydo bo'ldi.

en: He stood up at once.
uz: U darhol turdi.

en: “I did not bow down to you, I bowed down to all the suffering of humanity,” he said wildly and walked away to the window.
uz: "Senga sajda qilmadim, insoniyatning barcha azob-uqubatlariga sajda qildim", - dedi u vahshiy va darchaga qarab ketdi.

en: “Listen,” he added, turning to her a minute later.
uz: U bir daqiqadan so'ng unga qarab qo'shimcha qildi.

en: “I said just now to an insolent man that he was not worth your little finger … and that I did my sister honour making her sit beside you.” “Ach, you said that to them!
uz: Haqiqatan ham men o'zimning kichkina barmog'ingizga loyiq emasligimni va singlimni sizning yoningizda o'tirtirishga majbur qilganimni aytdim.Aha, siz ularga shunday aytdingiz!

en: And in her presence?” cried Sonia, frightened.
uz: Va uning huzurida? - deya qo'rqqan Soniya qichqirdi.

en: Why, I’m … dishonourable.
uz: Nima uchun, men ... sharafsizman.

en: … Ah, why did you say that?” “It was not because of your dishonour and your sin I said that of you, but because of your great suffering.
uz: ... Ah, nima uchun shunday aytdingiz?  Men siz haqingizda aytgan gapim sizning nopoklik va gunohlaringiz tufayli emas, balki sizning ko'p azob chekayotganingiz uchun edi.

en: But you are a great sinner, that’s true,” he added almost solemnly, “and your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing.
uz: Ammo siz katta gunohkorsiz, haqiqatan ham shunday, - dedi u, deyarli tantanali ravishda qo'shimcha qilib, - va eng katta gunohingiz - o'zingizni behuda yo'q qilishingiz va aldashingizdir.

en: Isn’t it fearful that you are living in this filth which you loathe so, and at the same time you know yourself (you’ve only to open your eyes) that you are not helping anyone by it, not saving anyone from anything?
uz: Sizni yomon ko'radigan bu yovuz dunyoda yashayotganingiz va o'zingizni (ko'zlaringizni ochish uchun) bilganingiz uchun hech kimga yordam bermayotganingiz, hech narsadan hech kimni qutqarmayotganingiz qo'rqinchli emasmi?

en: Tell me,” he went on almost in a frenzy, “how this shame and degradation can exist in you side by side with other, opposite,
uz: Ayting-chi, u deyarli g'alati ravishda davom etdi,bu orzu va kamsitish sizda qanday qilib boshqa, qarama-qarshi,

en: It would be better, a thousand times better and wiser to leap into the water and end it all!” “But what would become of them?” Sonia asked faintly, gazing at him with eyes of anguish, but not seeming surprised at his suggestion.
uz: Bu yaxshiroq, ming barobar yaxshiroq va aqlliroq bo'lib, suvga tushib, hamma narsani tugatish mumkin! Ammo ular bilan nima bo'ladi? Sonia so'radi, so'zlab qo'ydi: "Soniyaning taklifidan hayron bo'lmay, qayg'uli ko'zlar bilan unga qarayotgandim".

en: Raskolnikov looked strangely at her.
uz: Raskolnikov unga g'alati ko'z bilan qaradi.

en: He read it all in her face; so she must have had that thought already, perhaps many times, and earnestly she had thought out in her despair how to end it and so earnestly, that now she scarcely wondered at his suggestion.
uz: U hamma narsani uning yuziga o'qib berdi; shuning uchun u bu fikrni allaqachon, ehtimol ko'p marotaba o'ylab ko'rgan bo'lishi mumkin va u tushkunlikka tushib, uni qanday tugatishni o'ylab ko'rgan bo'lishi mumkin edi va shu qadar qattiq ediki, endi u uning taklifini o'ylab ko'rmadi.

en: She had not even noticed the cruelty of his words.
uz: U hatto uning so'zlarining shafqatsizligini ham sezmagan edi.

en: (The significance of his reproaches and his peculiar attitude to her shame she had, of course, not noticed either, and that, too, was clear to him.) But he saw how monstrously the thought of her disgraceful, shameful position was torturing her and had long tortured her.
uz: (Uning tanqidlarining ahamiyati va uning o'ziga xos munosabati uning sharmandaligiga ham e'tibor bermagan edi va bu ham unga aniq edi.) Ammo u uning sharmanda, sharmandalik bilan tug'ilgan mavqeyi haqida o'ylash uni qanchalik dahshatli azob chekayotganini va uzoq vaqt davomida uni azob chekayotganini ko'rdi.

en: “What, what,” he thought, “could hitherto have hindered her from putting an end to it?” Only then he realised what those poor little orphan children and that pitiful half-crazy Katerina Ivanovna, knocking her head against the wall in her consumption, meant for Sonia.
uz: nima, nima, o'zi o'ylaganidek, bu vaqtgacha uni bu ishga chek qo'ymaslikka to'sqinlik qilgan bo'lishi mumkin? Faqat o'sha paytdan keyin u o'sha kambag'al yetim bolalar va o'sha shafqatsiz yarim aqldan ozgan Katerina Ivanovna Sonia uchun nima ekanligini angladi.

en: But, nevertheless, it was clear to him again that with her character and the amount of education she had after all received, she could not in any case remain so.
uz: Biroq, unga yana aniq ediki, o'zining xarakter va ta'lim-tarbiyasi bilan u hech qanday holatda shunday bo'lib qololmaydi.

en: He was still confronted by the question, how could she have remained so long in that position without going out of her mind, since she could not bring herself to jump into the water?
uz: U hali ham bu savolga duch kelgan edi: qanday qilib u suvga cho'kishga o'zini majburlay olmagan bo'lsa-da, shuncha vaqt davomida o'sha holatda bo'lib, aqldan ozdirmagan?

en: Of course he knew that Sonia’s position was an exceptional case, though unhappily not unique and not infrequent, indeed; but that very exceptionalness, her tinge of education, her previous life might, one would have thought, have killed her at the first step on that revolting path.
uz: Albatta, u Sonaning mavqeining noyob holat ekanligini bilardi, ammo afsuski, bu noyob va kam emas edi; lekin o'sha noyoblik, uning ta'lim-tarbiyasi, o'tmishdagi hayoti uni o'ldirgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb o'ylash mumkin edi.

en: What held her up —surely not depravity?
uz: Uni nima to'xtatgan, albatta, buzuqlik emasmi?

en: All that infamy had obviously only touched her mechanically, not one drop of real depravity had penetrated to her heart; he saw that.
uz: O'sha barcha ifloslik uni faqat mexanik jihatdan ta'sir qilgan edi, uning yuragida hech bir tomchi haqiqiy fohishalik tushib qolmagan edi; u buni ko'rgan edi.

en: He saw through her as she stood before him.
uz: Uning oldida turgan ayolning ko'z o'ngidan ko'rdi.

en: … “There are three ways before her,” he thought, “the canal, the madhouse, or … at last to sink into depravity which obscures the mind and turns the heart to stone.” The last idea was the most revolting, but he was a sceptic, he was young, abstract, and therefore cruel, and so he could not help believing that the last end was the most likely.
uz: U o'ylaganidek, uning oldida uchta yo'l bor: kanal, aqldan ozgan uy yoki nihoyat ongni qorong'i qilib, qalbni toshga aylantiradigan buzuqlikka tushish.O'tgan g'oya eng dahshatli edi, ammo u sceptik, yosh, ma'noli va shuning uchun shafqatsiz edi.

en: “But can that be true?” he cried to himself.
uz: Ammo bu haqiqat bo'lishi mumkinmi? - dedi u o'z-o'zidan.

en: “Can that creature who has still preserved the purity of her spirit be consciously drawn at last into that sink of filth and iniquity?
uz: O'z ruhining pokligini saqlab qolgan bu yaratilish oxir-oqibat o'zini bu yovuzlik va nopoklik bilan to'kib solishi mumkinmi?

en: Can the process already have begun?
uz: Bu jarayon allaqachon boshlangan bo'lishi mumkinmi?

en: Can it be that she has only been able to bear it till now, because vice has begun to be less loathsome to her?
uz: U faqatgina bu vaqtgacha uni ko'tarishga muvaffaq bo'lgan, chunki buzuqlik unga yoqimsiz bo'la boshlaganmi?

en: No, no, that cannot be!” he cried, as Sonia had just before.
uz: Yo'q, yo'q, bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas! u Sonia singari yig'ladi.

en: “No, what has kept her from the canal till now is the idea of sin and they, the children.
uz: Yo'q, uni hozirgacha kanaldan saqlab qolgan narsa gunoh va ular, bolalar haqidagi g'oya.

en: … And if she has not gone out of her mind … but who says she has not gone out of her mind?
uz: Va agar u aqldan ozdirmagan bo'lsa-yu, kim aytishi mumkinki, u aqldan ozdirmagan?

en: Is she in her senses?
uz: U aqli bilanmi?

en: Can one talk, can one reason as she does?
uz: Bir kishi gapirishi mumkinmi, u gapirishi mumkinmi?

en: How can she sit on the edge of the abyss of loathsomeness into which she is slipping and refuse to listen when she is told of danger?
uz: Qanday qilib u o'zidan-o'zi quvib o'tirgan jirkanchlik chuqurligining chegarasida o'tirib, xavf haqida gap ketganda tinglashni rad etadi?

en: Does she expect a miracle?
uz: U moʻʼjiza kutadimi?

en: Doesn’t that all mean madness?” He stayed obstinately at that thought.
uz: Bularning barchasi aqlsizlik emasmi? U o'sha fikrga qat'iy ishonib qoldi.

en: He liked that explanation indeed better than any other.
uz: U bu tushuntirishni boshqa hech qanday tushuntirishdan ko'ra ko'proq yoqtirgan.

en: He began looking more intently at her.
uz: U ayolga ko'proq diqqat bilan qaray boshladi.

en: “So you pray to God a great deal, Sonia?” he asked her.
uz: - Shunday qilib, sen Xudoga ko'p ibodat qilyapsanmi, Sonia? - deb so'radi u.

en: Sonia did not speak; he stood beside her waiting for an answer.
uz: Sonia gapirmadi; u uning yonida turib, javob kutdi.

en: “What should I be without God?” she whispered rapidly, forcibly, glancing at him with suddenly flashing eyes, and squeezing his hand.
uz: Xudo yo'qligida men nima bo'lar edim? - deb tez-tez, kuch-qudrat bilan shovqin qildi u, ko'zlarini to'satdan chaqmoq bilan ko'tarib, qo'lini siqib.

en: “Ah, so that is it!” he thought.
uz: Ah, shunday qilib, bu o'zi! deb o'yladi.

en: “And what does God do for you?” he asked, probing her further.
uz: Xudo siz uchun nimalar qiladi? - deb so'radi u, ayolni yanada tekshirib ko'rdi.

en: Sonia was silent a long while, as though she could not answer.
uz: Sonia ancha vaqt sukut saqladi, xuddi javob bera olmasdek.

en: Her weak chest kept heaving with emotion.
uz: Uning zaif ko'kraklari hissiyotlar bilan ko'tarilgan edi.

en: You don’t deserve!” she cried suddenly, looking sternly and wrathfully at him.
uz: Siz bunga loyiq emassiz! - deb, u to'satdan yig'lab yubordi, unga qattiq va g'azablangan ko'z bilan qaradi.

en: “That’s it, that’s it,” he repeated to himself.
uz: Mana shu, mana shu, - deb o'ziga takrorladi u.

en: “He does everything,” she whispered quickly, looking down again.
uz: U hamma narsani qiladi, u tezda shovqin qildi va yana pastga qarab ketdi.

en: “That’s the way out!
uz: Uchdan chiqish yo'li!

en: That’s the explanation,” he decided, scrutinising her with eager curiosity, with a new, strange, almost morbid feeling.
uz: Bu uning tushuntirilishi, - deb qaror qildi u, qizni qiziqarli qiziqish bilan, yangi, g'alati, deyarli kasallik hissi bilan tekshirib ko'rdi.

en: He gazed at that pale, thin, irregular, angular little face, those soft blue eyes, which could flash with such fire, such stern energy, that little body still shaking with indignation and anger —and it all seemed to him more and more strange, almost impossible.
uz: U o'sha bo'lak-bo'lak, chiroyli, noaniq, burchakli kichik yuzga, o'sha yumshoq ko'k ko'zlarga qaradi, ular o'sha olov, o'sha qattiq energiya bilan chaqnaydi, o'sha kichik tana hali ham g'azab va g'azabdan titraydi va hamma narsa unga yanada g'alati, deyarli imkonsiz ko'rindi.

en: “She is a religious maniac!” he repeated to himself.
uz: U diniy manikadir! o'zi o'ziga takrorladi.

en: There was a book lying on the chest of drawers.
uz: Kamonlarda bir kitob yotgan edi.

en: He had noticed it every time he paced up and down the room.
uz: U xonadan oshib-oshib borgan har safar buni payqadi.

en: Now he took it up and
uz: Endi u uni ko'tarib oldi va

en: It was the New Testament in the Russian translation.
uz: Bu rus tilidagi Yangi Ahd edi.

en: It was bound in leather, old and worn.
uz: U charm bilan bog'langan, eski va kiyingan edi.

en: “Where did you get that?” he called to her across the room.
uz: Qayerdan olgansiz? u xonadonning o'rtasida unga chaqirgan.

en: She was still standing in the same place, three steps from the table.
uz: U hali ham o'sha joyda, stoldan uch qadam uzoqlikda turibdi.

en: “It was brought me,” she answered, as it were unwillingly, not looking at him.
uz: U menga olib kelingan, deb javob berdi, xuddi xohlamasdan, unga qaramasdan.

en: “Who brought it?” “Lizaveta, I asked her for it.” “Lizaveta!
uz: Kim olib keldi?  Lizaveta, men undan uni so'radim.  Lizaveta!

en: strange!” he thought.
uz: O'zi o'ylaganidek, bu g'alati!

en: Everything about Sonia seemed to him stranger and more wonderful every moment.
uz: Sonia haqidagi hamma narsa unga har bir daqiqaga yanada g'alati va ajoyib ko'rinardi.

en: He carried the book to the candle and began to turn over the pages.
uz: U kitobni chiroqga olib borib, sahifalarni aylantirishni boshladi.

en: “Where is the story of Lazarus?” he asked suddenly.
uz: Lazaro haqidagi hikoya qayerda? deb so'radi u to'satdan.

en: Sonia looked obstinately at the ground and would not answer.
uz: Soniya qattiqqo'l holda yerga qarab, javob bermadi.

en: She was standing sideways to the table.
uz: U stolning yon tomonida turibdi.

en: “Where is the raising of Lazarus?
uz: Lazaronning tirilishi qayerda?

en: Find it for me, Sonia.” She stole a glance at him.
uz: Uni menga top, Sonia. U unga bir nazar tashladi.

en: “You are not looking in the right place.
uz: Siz to'g'ri joyda qidirmayapsiz.

en: … It’s in the fourth gospel,” she whispered sternly, without looking at him.
uz: To'rtinchi Injilda u unga qaramasdan, qattiq va g'azablangan so'zlarni aytdi.

en: “Find it and read it to me,” he said.
uz: Uni topib menga o'qib bering, dedi.

en: He sat down with his elbow on the table, leaned his head on his hand and looked away sullenly, prepared to listen.
uz: U qo'l qo'shigi bilan dasturxonga o'tirib, boshini qo'liga tikib, tinglashga tayyor bo'lib, qayg'urgancha qarab ketdi.

en: “In three weeks’ time they’ll welcome me in the madhouse!
uz: Uch hafta ichida ular meni aqldan ozgan uyga qabul qilishadi!

en: I shall be there if I am not in a worse place,” he muttered to himself.
uz: Agar men yomon joyda bo'lmasam, u erda bo'laman, - deb o'ziga o'zi g'iybat qildi u.

en: Sonia heard Raskolnikov’s request distrustfully and moved hesitatingly to the table.
uz: Sonia Raskolnikovning iltimosini ishonchsizlik bilan eshitdi va shubha ostiga olib, dasturxon tomon o'tdi.

en: She took the book however.
uz: Ammo u kitobni olib ketdi.

en: “Haven’t you read it?” she asked, looking up at him across the table.
uz: Siz uni o'qimaganmisiz? - deb so'radi u, uni stolning boshqa tomonida ko'rib.

en: Her voice became sterner and sterner.
uz: Uning ovozi yanada kuchli bo'ldi.

en: … When I was at school.
uz: Men maktabda o'qiganimda.

en: Read!” “And haven’t you heard it in church?” “I … haven’t been.
uz: O'qing! Va siz buni cherkovda eshitmaganmisiz? Men ... bo'lmaganman.

en: Do you often go?” “N-no,” whispered Sonia.
uz: Siz tez-tez borasizmi? N-yo'q, Sonia shovqin qildi.

en: … And you won’t go to your father’s funeral tomorrow?”
uz: Ertaga otangizning dafn marosimiga bormaysanmi?

en: I was at church last week, too … I had a requiem service.” “For whom?” “For Lizaveta.
uz: O'tgan hafta men ham cherkovga bordim ... Men bir requiem xizmatiga bordim.Kim uchun?Lizaveta uchun.

en: She was killed with an axe.” His nerves were more and more strained.
uz: U o'g'li bilan o'ldirildi. Uning g'azablari kundan-kunga kuchliroq edi.

en: His head began to go round.
uz: Uning boshi aylanib ketishni boshladi.

en: “Were you friends with Lizaveta?” “Yes.
uz: Siz Lizaveta bilan do'st bo'lganmisiz?

en: … She was good … she used to come … not often … she couldn’t.
uz: U yaxshi odam edi, tez-tez kelmasdi, ko'pincha kelolmasdi.

en: … We used to read together and … talk.
uz: ... Biz birga o'qib, suhbatlashardik.

en: She will see God.” The last phrase sounded strange in his ears.
uz: U Xudoni ko'radi. So'nggi gap uning quloqlarida g'alati tuyuldi.

en: And here was something new again: the mysterious meetings with Lizaveta and both of them —religious maniacs.
uz: Yana bir yangilik bor edi: Lizaveta va ularning ikkalasi ham diniy maniklar bilan bo'lgan sirli uchrashuvlar.

en: “I shall be a religious maniac myself soon!
uz: Men tez orada o'zim ham diniy maniac bo'laman!

en: It’s infectious!” “Read!” he cried irritably and insistently.
uz: Bu yuqumli!Qo'qing! u g'azab va qat'iylik bilan yig'ladi.

en: Sonia still hesitated.
uz: Sonia hali ham shubha ostiga qo'ydi.

en: Her heart was throbbing.
uz: Uning yuragi urib ketdi.

en: She hardly dared to read to him.
uz: U unga o'qib berishga charchagan.

en: He looked almost with exasperation at the “unhappy lunatic.” “What for?
uz: U o'sha baxtsiz aqldan ozgan odamga deyarli g'azablanib qaradi. Nima uchun?

en: …” she whispered softly and as it were breathlessly.
uz: ... u sekin va xuddi nafassiz shovqin qildi.

en: I want you to,” he persisted.
uz: Men buni xohlayman, - dedi u, - lekin u istig'for aytmadi.

en: “You used to read to Lizaveta.” Sonia opened the book and found the place.
uz: Siz Lizavetaga o'qigan edingiz. Sonia kitobni ochib, joyni topdi.

en: Her hands were shaking, her voice failed her.
uz: Uning qo'llari titrab, ovozi puchga chiqardi.

en: Twice she tried to begin and could not bring out the first syllable.
uz: U ikki marta boshlashga harakat qildi va birinchi silfani chiqarolmadi.

en: “Now a certain man was sick named Lazarus of Bethany …” she forced herself at last to read, but at the third word her voice broke like an overstrained string.
uz: Betanialik Lazar ismli bir odam kasal edi ... u oxiri o'qishga majbur bo'ldi, lekin uchinchi so'z bilan uning ovozi ortiqcha to'qnashuvga o'xshaydi.

en: There was a catch in her breath.
uz: Uning nafasida o'tkirlik paydo bo'ldi.

en: Raskolnikov saw in part why Sonia could not bring herself to read to him and the more he saw this, the more roughly and irritably he insisted on her doing so.
uz: Raskolnikov, nega Sonia unga o'qib berolmayotganini qisman ko'rdi va uni ko'rgan sari, u uni o'qib berishga qattiq va g'azabga to'ldirdi.

en: He understood only too well how painful it was for her to betray and unveil all that was her own.
uz: U ayolning o'ziga tegishli bo'lgan hamma narsani xiyonat qilib, oshkor qilish qanchalik og'irligini juda yaxshi tushunardi.

en: He understood that these feelings really were her secret treasure, which she had kept perhaps for years, perhaps from childhood, while she lived with an unhappy father and a distracted stepmother crazed by grief, in the midst of starving children and unseemly abuse and reproaches.
uz: U bu his-tuyg'ular uning sirli xazinasi ekanligini tushunardi, ehtimol u yillar davomida, ehtimol bolaligidan buyon, baxtsiz otasi va qayg'u-qarshiligidan bezovta bo'lgan qayg'uli o'g'il bilan yashayotganida, och qolgan bolalar va yomon ta'qiblar va haqoratlar orasida yashardi.

en: But at the same time he knew now and knew for certain that, although it filled her with dread and suffering, yet she had a tormenting desire to read and to read to him that he might hear it,
uz: Ammo u hozir bilgan va shubhasiz bilgan ediki, bu ayolni qo'rquv va azob-uqubat bilan to'ldirgan bo'lsa-da, u uni eshitishi uchun o'qishga va unga o'qishga qattiq ishtiyoqga ega edi.

en: and to read now whatever might come of it!
uz: Va endi nima bo'lishidan qat'iy nazar, uni o'qish uchun!

en: … He read this in her eyes, he could see it in her intense emotion.
uz: U buni uning ko'zlaridan o'qib, uni uning kuchli his-tuyg'ularida ko'rishgan.

en: She mastered herself, controlled the spasm in her throat and went on reading the eleventh chapter of St.
uz: U o'zini o'zi boshqargan, qo'ldagi spasmni nazorat qilgan va o'n birinchi bobni o'qishni davom ettirgan.

en: She went on to the nineteenth verse: “And many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother.
uz: Keyin u o'n to'qqizinchi oyatga o'tdi: Ko'pgina yahudiylar Marta va Maryamning ukasi haqida tasalli berish uchun ularning oldiga kelishdi.

en: “Then Martha as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming went and met Him: but Mary sat still in the house.
uz: Marta Isoning kelayotganini eshitgan chogʻida Uni kutib olishga chiqdi, ammo Maryam hali ham uyda o'tirgan edi.

en: “Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if Thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
uz: Shunda Marta Isoga: "Rabbim, agar Sen bu yerda bo'lganingda, akam o'lmasdi", - dedi.

en: “But I know that even now whatsoever Thou wilt ask of God, God will give it Thee.
uz: Lekin hozir ham Allohdan nimaiki so'rasang, U senga beradi, deb bilaman.

en: …” Then she stopped again with a shamefaced feeling that her voice would quiver and break again.
uz: Keyin u o'z ovozini titraydi va yana buzadi deb o'ylagan o'ylash bilan yana to'xtadi.

en: “Jesus said unto her, thy brother shall rise again.
uz: Iso unga dedi: "Qardaching tiriladi".

en: “Martha saith unto Him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection, at the last day.
uz: Marta Unga: "O'tgan kun qiyomatda tirilishini bilaman", - dedi.

en: “Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in Me though he were dead, yet shall he live.
uz: Iso unga dedi: "Qiyomat va hayot Menman. Menga ishongan kishi o'lsa ham, tirik qoladi.

en: “And whosoever liveth and believeth in Me shall never die.
uz: Kimki yashasa va Menga ishonsa, hech qachon o'lmaydi.

en: Believest thou this?
uz: Siz bunga ishonasizmi?

en: “She saith unto Him,” (And drawing a painful breath, Sonia read distinctly and forcibly as though she were making a public confession of faith.) “Yea, Lord: I believe that Thou art the Christ, the Son of God Which should come into the world.” She stopped and looked up quickly at him, but controlling herself went on reading.
uz: U Unga shunday dedi: (Soniya og'ir nafas olib, xuddi imonini ochiqchasiga e'tirof etgandek aniq va qat'iy o'qib chiqdi.) Ha, Rabbim: Sen dunyoga keladigan Xudoning O'g'li Masihsan, deb ishonaman. U to'xtadi va tezda unga ko'z tikdi, lekin o'zini nazorat qilib, o'qishni davom ettirdi.

en: Raskolnikov sat without moving, his elbows on the table and his eyes turned away.
uz: Raskolnikov o'tirgancha, qo'lqoplari stol ustida, ko'zlari esa orqaga burildi.

en: She read to the thirty-second verse.
uz: U o'ttiz ikkinchi oyatni o'qib chiqdi.

en: “Then when Mary was come where Jesus was and saw Him, she fell down at His feet, saying unto Him, Lord if Thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
uz: Maryam Isoning oldiga kelib, Uni ko'rganida, Uning oyoqlariga yiqilib: "Rabbim, agar Sen bu yerda bo'lganingda, akam o'lmagan bo'lar edi", - dedi.

en: “When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, He groaned in the spirit and was troubled, “And said, Where have ye laid him?
uz: Shu sababli, Iso Maryamni va u bilan birga kelgan yahudiylarni yig'layotganini ko'rganida, ruhidan g'amgin bo'lib, qayg'urib: "Uni qayerda qo'ydingizlar?" - dedi.

en: They said unto Him, Lord, come and see.
uz: Ular Unga: "Rabbim, kel, ko'rgin", - deyishdi.

en: “Then said the Jews, behold how He loved him!
uz: Keyin yahudiylar: "Qaranglar, U uni qanchalik yaxshi ko'rgan!" - deyishdi.

en: “And some of them said, could not this Man which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?” Raskolnikov turned and looked at her with emotion.
uz: Ulardan ba'zilari: "Ko'rlarning ko'zlarini ochgan bu Odam, hatto bu odam ham o'lmasligiga sabab bo'lishi mumkin emasmi?" - deyishdi. Raskolnikov o'girilib, ayolga hissiy ko'z bilan qaradi.

en: Yes, he had known it!
uz: Ha, u buni bilar edi!

en: She was trembling in a real physical fever.
uz: U haqiqiy jismoniy issiqdan titragan edi.

en: She was getting near the story of the greatest miracle and a feeling of immense triumph came over her.
uz: U eng buyuk moʻʼjiza haqidagi hikoyaga yaqinlashayotgan edi va katta gʻalaba hissi unga tushib qoldi.

en: Her voice rang out like a bell; triumph and joy gave it power.
uz: Uning ovozi qo'ng'iroq kabi ovoz chiqardi; g'alaba va quvonch unga kuch ato etdi.

en: The lines danced before her eyes, but she knew what she was reading by heart.
uz: Uning ko'z o'ngida so'zlar raqsga tushdi, ammo u o'qiganini yodda tutgan.

en: At the last verse, “Could not this Man which opened the eyes of the blind …” dropping her voice she passionately reproduced the doubt, the reproach and censure of the blind disbelieving Jews, who in another moment would fall at His feet as though struck by thunder, sobbing and believing.
uz: So'nggi oyatda: "Ko'rlarning ko'zlarini ochgan bu Odam ..." deb aytsa bo'lmasmidi?... O'z ovozini pastga solganida, u ko'r imonsiz yahudiylarning shubhalarini, haqoratlarini va tanqidlarini ishtiyoq bilan takrorladi, ular boshqa bir daqiqada g'azabga cho'kib, imon keltirib, Isoning oyoqlariga yiqilib ketishardi.

en: … “And he, he —too, is blinded and unbelieving, he, too, will hear, he, too, will believe, yes, yes!
uz: ... U ham ko'r va imonsiz, u ham eshitadi, u ham ishonadi, ha, ha!

en: At once, now,” was what she was dreaming, and she was quivering with happy anticipation.
uz: O'sha zahoti u orzu qilgan narsa edi va u quvonchli kutib olish bilan titrab turardi.

en: “Jesus therefore again groaning in Himself cometh to the grave.
uz: Shu sababli, Iso yana o'z yuragida qayg'urib, qabrga keldi.

en: It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
uz: Bu gʻor edi va ustida tosh oʻrnagan edi.

en: “Jesus said, Take ye away the stone.
uz: Iso: "Toshni olib tashlanglar", - dedi.

en: Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto Him, Lord by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.” She laid emphasis on the word four.
uz: O'lgan kishining singlisi Marta Unga: "Rabbim, hozircha bu erga kiradi, chunki u to'rt kundir o'lgan", - dedi. U to'rtta so'zga e'tiborini qaratdi.

en: “Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee that if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?
uz: Iso unga dedi: - Agar imon keltirsang, Xudoning ulug'vorligini ko'rasan, demaganmidim?

en: “Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid.
uz: So'ngra ular o'lik qo'yilgan joydan toshni olib tashladilar.

en: And Jesus lifted up His eyes and said, Father, I thank Thee that Thou hast heard Me.
uz: Iso ko'zlarini ko'tarib, dedi: "Otam, Meni eshitganing uchun Senga shukr aytaman.

en: “And I knew that Thou hearest Me always; but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that Thou hast sent Me.
uz: Sen Meni har doim tinglayotganingni bilar edim, lekin bu so'zlarni atrofimda turgan odamlar uchun aytdim, toki ular Sen Meni yuborganingga ishonsinlar".

en: “And when He thus had spoken, He cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
uz: Bu so'zlarni aytib bo'lgach, Iso baland ovoz bilan: "Lazaro, chiq!" - deb baqirib yubordi.

en: “And he that was dead came forth.” (She read loudly, cold and trembling with ecstasy, as though she were seeing it before her eyes.)
uz: O'lgan kishi tashqariga chiqdi. (O'sha ayol baland ovoz bilan, sovuq va ekstazdan titrab o'qigan edi, xuddi ko'z o'ngida ko'rgan bo'lsa kerak.)

en: “Bound hand and foot with graveclothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin.
uz: Qo'l-qo'lni qabr matolari bilan bog'lagan, yuzini esa sovut bilan bog'lagan.

en: Jesus saith unto them, Loose him and let him go.
uz: Iso ularga: "Uni yechib tashlanglar va ketishiga yo'l qo'yinglar", - dedi.

en: “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary and had seen the things which Jesus did believed on Him.” She could read no more, closed the book and got up from her chair quickly.
uz: Maryamning oldiga kelgan va Iso qilgan ishlarni ko'rgan yahudiylarning ko'pchiligi Unga ishonishdi.

en: “That is all about the raising of Lazarus,” she whispered severely and abruptly, and turning away she stood motionless, not daring to raise her eyes to him.
uz: Lazardan o'sish haqida gap ketyapti, u qattiq va shoshilinch so'zladi va yuz o'girib, ko'zlarini unga ko'tarishga jur'at qilmay, harakatsiz turibdi.

en: She still trembled feverishly.
uz: U hali ham qizg'in titrar edi.

en: The candle-end was flickering out in the battered candlestick, dimly lighting up in the poverty-stricken room the murderer and the harlot who had so strangely been reading together the eternal book.
uz: Shamolning o'tishi chiroqning cho'kkan chiroqchasiga o'xshaydi va kamchilikka to'lgan xonada qotil va fohisha o'qib turgan abadiy kitobni birgalikda o'qiyotgan kishilar ko'rinadi.

en: Five minutes or more passed.
uz: Besh daqiqa yoki undan ko'proq vaqt o'tdi.

en: “I came to speak of something,” Raskolnikov said aloud, frowning.
uz: "Men biror narsa haqida gapirish uchun keldim", - dedi Raskolnikov baland ovoz bilan.

en: He got up and went to Sonia.
uz: U o'rnidan turib, Soniyaning oldiga bordi.

en: She lifted her eyes to him in silence.
uz: Oʻsha paytda u oʻziga koʻzlarini baland koʻtarib, sukut saqlashdi.

en: His face was particularly stern and there was a sort of savage determination in it.
uz: Uning yuzi ayniqsa qattiq edi va unda bir xil yovvoyi qat'iylik bor edi.

en: “I have abandoned my family today,” he said, “my mother and sister.
uz: Bugun oilamni tashlab ketdim, dedi u, onam va singlim.

en: I am not going to see them.
uz: Men ularni ko'rmayman.

en: I’ve broken with them completely.” “What for?” asked Sonia amazed.
uz: Men ular bilan to'liq uzildi.   Nima uchun? so'radi Sonia hayratda.

en: Her recent meeting with his mother and sister had left a great impression which she could not analyse.
uz: Uning onasi va singlisi bilan yaqinda yuz bergan uchrashuvi katta taassurot qoldirdi, uni tahlil qila olmagan.

en: She heard his news almost with horror.
uz: Uning xabarini eshitib, u dahshatga tushdi.

en: “I have only you now,” he added.
uz: Hozirda faqat sen bor, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u.

en: “Let us go together.
uz: Keling, birga boraylik.

en: … I’ve come to you, we are both accursed, let us go our way together!” His eyes glittered “as though he were mad,” Sonia thought, in her turn.
uz: ... Men sening oldiga keldim, ikkalasi ham la'natlanganmiz, keling, birgalikda yo'limizni bosib o'tamiz! Uning ko'zlari xuddi g'alati bo'lganidek shinamlashib ketdi, - deb o'yladi Sonia.

en: “Go where?” she asked in alarm and she involuntarily stepped back.
uz: Qayerga ketish kerak? - deb so'radi u qo'rqinchli so'zlarni eshitib, o'z xohishiga ko'ra orqaga qaytdi.

en: I only know it’s the same road, I know that and nothing more.
uz: Faqatgina shuni bilamanki, bu bir xil yo'l, buni bilaman va bundan boshqa hech narsa yo'q.

en: It’s the same goal!” She looked at him and understood nothing.
uz: Bu bir xil maqsad! U unga qarab, hech narsani tushunmadi.

en: She knew only that he was terribly, infinitely unhappy.
uz: U faqat uning juda, juda baxtsiz ekanligini bilardi.

en: “No one of them will understand, if you tell them, but I have understood.
uz: Agar siz ularga aytsangiz, ularning hech biri tushunmaydi, lekin men tushundim.

en: I need you, that is why I have come to you.” “I don’t understand,” whispered Sonia.
uz: Men sizga muhtojman, shuning uchun sizga keldim.     Men tushunmayman, Sonia shoshladi.

en: “You’ll understand later.
uz: Siz keyinroq tushunasiz.

en: Haven’t you done the same?
uz: Siz ham shunday qilmadingizmi?

en: You, too, have transgressed … have had the strength to transgress.
uz: Siz ham gunoh qilgansiz... gunoh qilish uchun kuchga ega bo'ldingiz.

en: You have laid hands on yourself, you have destroyed a life … your own (it’s all the same!).
uz: Siz o'zingizga qo'l qo'ydingiz, hayotingizni yo'q qildingiz ... o'zingizning hayotingizni (hammasi bir xil!).

en: You might have lived in spirit and understanding, but you’ll end in the Hay Market.
uz: Ehtimol siz ruh va tushuncha bilan yashagan bo'lasiz, lekin siz Hay bozoriga borasiz.

en: … But you won’t be able to stand it, and if you remain alone you’ll go out of your mind like me.
uz: Ammo siz bunga chiday olmaysiz va agar yolg'iz qolsangiz, men kabi aqldan ozasiz.

en: You are like a mad creature already.
uz: Siz allaqachon aqldan ozgan mavjudot kabi bo'lasiz.

en: So we must go together on the same road!
uz: Shunday qilib, biz bir xil yo'lda birgalikda borishimiz kerak!

en: Let us go!” “What for?
uz: Keling, ketaylik! Nima uchun?

en: What’s all this for?” said Sonia, strangely and violently agitated by his words.
uz: Bularning barchasi nima uchun? - dedi Sonia, uning so'zlaridan g'alati va zo'ravonlik bilan xavotirlanib.

en: Because you can’t remain like this, that’s why!
uz: Chunki siz shunday qololmaysiz, shuning uchun!

en: You must look things straight in the face at last, and not weep like a child and cry that God won’t allow it.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, o'zingizni to'g'ri his etib, Xudo bunga yo'l qo'ymaydi, deb bola kabi yig'lamay, yig'lab turmang.

en: What will happen, if you should really be taken to the hospital tomorrow?
uz: Bordi-yu, ertaga kasalxonaga olib ketish kerak bo'lsa, nima bo'ladi?

en: She is mad and in consumption, she’ll soon die and the children?
uz: U g'alati va iste'molda, u tez orada o'lib ketadi va bolalar?

en: Do you mean to tell me Polenka won’t come to grief?
uz: Polenka qayg'uga kelmaydi, deb aytmoqchimisan?

en: Haven’t you seen children here at the street corners sent out by their mothers to beg?
uz: Bu yerda, ko'cha burchaklarida bo'lgan bolalarni ko'rganmisiz, ularning onalari ularni yolvorib yuboribdi?

en: I’ve found out where those mothers live and in what surroundings.
uz: Bu onalar qayerda va qanday muhitda yashayotganini bilib oldim.

en: Children can’t remain children there!
uz: Bolalar o'sha yerda bola bo'lib qololmaydi!

en: At seven the child is vicious and a thief.
uz: Yetti yoshda bolaning o'zi shafqatsiz va o'g'ri.

en: Yet children, you know, are the image of Christ: ‘theirs is the kingdom of Heaven.’ He bade us honour and love them, they are the humanity of the future.
uz: Ammo bolalar, siz bilasiz, Masihning tasviri: Ularning osmon Shohligi. U bizga ularni hurmat qilish va sevishni buyurdi, chunki ular kelajakda insoniyatdir.

en: …” “What’s to be done, what’s to be done?” repeated Sonia, weeping hysterically and wringing her hands.
uz: ...  nima qilish kerak, nima qilish kerak? so'ng Sonia histerik ravishda yig'lab, qo'llarini burib qo'ydi.

en: Break what must be broken, once for all, that’s all, and take the suffering on oneself.
uz: Bir martalik qilib, butunlayin bo'shatilishi kerak bo'lgan narsalarni buzish va azob-uqubatlarni o'z zimmangizga olish.

en: What, you don’t understand?
uz: Nima, tushunmayapsanmi?

en: You’ll understand later.
uz: Keyinroq tushunasiz.

en: … Freedom and power, and above all, power!
uz: ... Erkinlik va kuch, eng asosiysi esa, kuch!

en: Over all trembling creation and all the ant-heap!
uz: Barcha dahshatli yaratilish va barcha qurtlar to'plami ustidan!

en: … That’s the goal, remember that!
uz: Bu maqsad, esingizda bo'lsin!

en: That’s my farewell message.
uz: Bu mening xayrli xabarim.

en: Perhaps it’s the last time I shall speak to you.
uz: Ehtimol, bu men siz bilan so'nggi marta gaplashishimdir.

en: If I don’t come tomorrow, you’ll hear of it all, and then remember these words.
uz: Agar ertaga kelmasam, hamma narsani eshitasiz va keyin ushbu so'zlarni eslang.

en: And some day later on, in years to come, you’ll understand perhaps what they meant.
uz: Va bir kun o'tgach, kelgusi yillarda, ehtimol ular nimani nazarda tutganini tushunasiz.

en: If I come tomorrow, I’ll tell you who killed Lizaveta.
uz: Agar ertaga kelsam, sizga Lizavetani kim o'ldirganini aytaman.

en: … Goodbye.” Sonia started with terror.
uz: Salom. Sonia terror bilan boshladi.

en: “Why, do you know who killed her?” she asked, chilled with horror, looking wildly at him.
uz: - Nima uchun, kim uni o'ldirganini bilasizmi? - deb so'radi u qo'rqinchga to'lib, unga vahshiy qarab.

en: “I know and will tell … you, only you.
uz: Men bilaman va sizga aytaman... faqat siz.

en: I have chosen you out.
uz: Men seni tanladim.

en: I’m not coming to you to ask forgiveness, but simply to tell you.
uz: Men sizdan kechirim so'rash uchun emas, balki shunchaki aytish uchun keldim.

en: I chose you out long ago to hear this, when your father talked of you and when Lizaveta was alive, I thought of it.
uz: Otam siz haqingizda gapirganida va Lizaveta tirik bo'lganida, men bu haqda o'yladim.

en: Goodbye, don’t shake hands.
uz: Xo'sh, qo'lingiz bilan qo'l urmang.

en: Tomorrow!” He went out.
uz: Ertaga! U tashqariga chiqdi.

en: Sonia gazed at him as at a madman.
uz: Sonia unga aqldan ozgan kishi kabi qaradi.

en: But she herself was like one insane and felt it.
uz: Ammo u o'zi aqldan ozgan kishi kabi edi va uni his qilgan.

en: Her head was going round.
uz: Uning boshi aylanib borardi.

en: “Good heavens, how does he know who killed Lizaveta?
uz: Albatta, u Lizavetani kim o'ldirganini qayerdan biladi?

en: What did those words mean?
uz: O'sha so'zlar nimani anglatadi?

en: It’s awful!” But at the same time the idea did not enter her head, not for a moment!
uz: Bu juda dahshatli! Ammo shu bilan birga, bu g'oya uning g'oyasiga bir zum ham kirmadi!

en: “Oh, he must be terribly unhappy!
uz: Oh, u juda baxtsiz bo'lishi kerak!

en: … He has abandoned his mother and sister.
uz: U onasi va singlisi bilan tashlab ketgan.

en: And what had he in his mind?
uz: Va uning fikri nima edi?

en: What did he say to her?
uz: U unga nima dedi?

en: He had kissed her foot and said … said (yes, he had said it clearly) that he could not live without her.
uz: U uning oyoqlarini o'pdi va dedi ... dedi (ha, u buni aniq aytdi) u o'zidan tashqari yashay olmasligini aytdi.

en: … Oh, merciful heavens!” Sonia spent the whole night feverish and delirious.
uz: Oh, rahmli osmonlar! Sonia butun kecha issiq va delirium bilan o'tkazdi.

en: She jumped up from time to time, wept and wrung her hands, then sank again into feverish sleep and dreamt of Polenka, Katerina Ivanovna and Lizaveta, of reading the gospel and him … him with pale face, with burning eyes … kissing her feet, weeping.
uz: U vaqti-vaqti bilan turib, yig'lab qo'llarini qovurardi, so'ngra yana issiq uyquga tushdi va Polenka, Katerina Ivanovna va Lizaveta Injilni o'qiganlarini va u bilan ... uning yorqin yuzli, yonayotgan ko'zlari bilan ... oyoqlarini o'pib, yig'layotganini orzu qildi.

en: On the other side of the door on the right, which divided Sonia’s room from Madame Resslich’s flat, was a room which had long stood empty.
uz: O'ng tomonidagi eshikning o'ng tomonida, Sonia xonasini Madame Resslichning xonasidan ajratib turadigan xona uzoq vaqtdan beri bo'sh turgan edi.

en: A card was fixed on the gate and a notice stuck in the windows over the canal advertising it to let.
uz: Eshikda karta o'rnatilgan edi va kanalning o'tkiridagi derazalarda e'lon qilib, uni ijaraga berishga e'lon qilgan xabarni o'rnatishgan.

en: Sonia had long been accustomed to the room’s being uninhabited.
uz: Sonia uzoq vaqtdan beri xonadonlarda yashamaydigan odamlarga o'rganib qolgan edi.

en: But all that time Mr.
uz: Ammo shu vaqt davomida Mr.

en: Svidrigaïlov had been standing, listening at the door of the empty room.
uz: Svidrigailov bo'sh xonaning eshigida turib, tinglagan edi.

en: When Raskolnikov went out he stood still, thought a moment, went on tiptoe to his own room which adjoined the empty one, brought a chair and noiselessly carried it to the door that led to Sonia’s room.
uz: Raskolnikov tashqariga chiqqanida, u to'xtadi, biroz o'ylab ko'rdi, bo'sh xonasiga qo'shilgan o'z xonasiga qadam qo'ydi, o'rinni olib keldi va uni Sonia xonasiga yetaklaydigan eshikga ovozli olib keldi.

en: The conversation had struck him as interesting and remarkable, and he had greatly enjoyed it —so much so that he brought a chair that he might not in the future, tomorrow, for instance, have to endure the inconvenience of standing a whole hour, but might listen in comfort.
uz: Suhbat unga qiziqarli va diqqatga sazovor bo'lib tuyuldi va u juda zavqlandi, shuning uchun u o'rindiqni olib keldi, ehtimol kelajakda, masalan, ertaga butun soat turishning noqulayligini ko'ra olmaydi, lekin u qulaylik bilan tinglashi mumkin.

en: V When next morning at eleven o’clock punctually Raskolnikov went into the department of the investigation of criminal causes and sent his name in to Porfiry Petrovitch, he was surprised at being kept waiting so long: it was at least ten minutes before he was summoned.
uz: V. Ertasi kuni ertalab soat o'n birlarda Raskolnikov jinoiy ishlarni tekshirish bo'limiga kirib, nomini Porfiry Petrovitchga jo'natganda, u shuncha vaqt kutishlariga hayron qoldi: uni chaqirishdan kamida o'n daqiqa oldin.

en: He had expected that they would pounce upon him.
uz: U ular o'z ustiga qo'shilishlarini kutgan edi.

en: But he stood in the waiting-room, and people, who apparently had nothing to do with him, were continually passing to and fro before him.
uz: Lekin u kutish xonasida turibdi va uning oldida hech qanday aloqasi bo'lmagan odamlar o'tib-o'tib ketayotgan edi.

en: In the next room which looked like an office, several clerks were sitting writing and obviously they had no notion who or what Raskolnikov might be.
uz: Qo'shni xonada, ofisga o'xshaydigan xonada, bir nechta ishchilar o'tirib yozishardi va Raskolnikov kim yoki nima bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida hech qanday tasavvurga ega emas edilar.

en: He looked uneasily and suspiciously about him to see whether there was not some guard, some mysterious watch being kept on him to prevent his escape.
uz: U qayg'urgan va shubha ostiga olib, uning qochib ketishiga yo'l qo'ymaslik uchun uning atrofida biron bir qo'riqchi yoki sirli qo'riqchi bo'lmaganini ko'rish uchun o'ziga qarab turdi.

en: But there was nothing of the sort: he saw only the faces of clerks absorbed in petty details, then other people, no one seemed to have any concern with him.
uz: Ammo bunday narsa yo'q edi: u faqatgina kichik xossalarga chalingan ishchilar va boshqa odamlarning yuzlarini ko'rdi, hech kim unga hech qanday qiziqish ko'rsatmagan.

en: He might go where he liked for them.
uz: U ular uchun xohlagan joyga borishi mumkin.

en: The conviction grew stronger in him that if that enigmatic man of yesterday, that phantom sprung out of the earth, had seen everything, they would not have let him stand and wait like that.
uz: Agar o'sha o'tmishdagi g'ayritabiiy odam, yerdan chiqqan hayajon hamma narsani ko'rgan bo'lsa edi, uni shunday turib kutishga qo'ymagan bo'lishganligiga ishonch kuchayib borardi.

en: And would they have waited till he elected to appear at eleven?
uz: Va ular u o'n birida paydo bo'lishni tanlaganini kutishardi?

en: Either the man had not yet given information, or … or simply he knew nothing, had seen nothing (and how could he have seen anything?) and so all that had happened to him the day before was again a phantom exaggerated by his sick and overstrained imagination.
uz: Yoki odam hali ma'lumot bermagan edi, yoki ... yoki shunchaki hech narsa bilmagan, hech narsa ko'rmagan edi (va qanday qilib u hech narsa ko'rgan bo'lishi mumkin edi?) va shuning uchun bir kun oldin unga sodir bo'lgan barcha narsa yana kasal va haddan tashqari ovora bo'lgan tasavvurlari tomonidan o'tkazilgan hayajon edi.

en: This conjecture had begun to grow strong the day before, in the midst of all his alarm and despair.
uz: Bu taxminlar uning tashvishlari va umidsizlikka toʻlib-toshgan kunlari kuchayib borgan edi.

en: Thinking it all over now and preparing for a fresh conflict, he was suddenly aware that he was trembling —and he felt a rush of indignation at the thought that he was trembling with fear at facing
uz: Hozir bu haqda o'ylab, yangi jangga tayyorgarlik ko'rgach, u birdan o'zini titrab turganini sezdi va qo'rquvdan titrab turganini ko'rib, g'azabga to'ldi.

en: that hateful Porfiry Petrovitch.
uz: O'sha nafratli Porfiry Petrovitch.

en: What he dreaded above all was meeting that man again; he hated him with an intense, unmitigated hatred and was afraid his hatred might betray him.
uz: Eng asosiysi, u bu odam bilan yana uchrashishdan qo'rqardi; u undan qattiq, qattiq nafrat bilan nafratlangan va nafratidan xafa bo'lishidan qo'rqqan.

en: His indignation was such that he ceased trembling at once; he made ready to go in with a cold and arrogant bearing and vowed to himself to keep as silent as possible, to watch and listen and for once at least to control his overstrained nerves.
uz: Uning g'azabi shunchalik kuchli bo'lganki, u darhol titrashni to'xtatdi; u sovuq va takabburlik bilan kirishga tayyor bo'ldi va iloji boricha ko'proq sukut saqlash, kuzatib turish va tinglash va hech bo'lmaganda bir bor haddan ortiq bosim o'tkazishga va'da berdi.

en: At that moment he was summoned to Porfiry Petrovitch.
uz: O'sha paytda uni Porfiry Petrovitchga chaqirishdi.

en: He found Porfiry Petrovitch alone in his study.
uz: U Porfiry Petrovitchni o'z studiyasida yolg'iz topdi.

en: His study was a room neither large nor small, furnished with a large writing-table, that stood before a sofa, upholstered in checked material, a bureau, a bookcase in the corner and several chairs —all government furniture, of polished yellow wood.
uz: Uning xonasi katta ham, kichik ham bo'lmagan, katta yozish stoli bilan jihozlangan, sofa oldida turgan, cheklangan materiallar bilan qoplangan xona edi, biro, burchadagi kitob xazinasi va bir nechta o'rindiqlar.

en: In the further wall there was a closed door, beyond it there were no doubt other rooms.
uz: Keyinroq devorda yopiq eshik bor edi, undan tashqarida boshqa xonalar bor edi.

en: On Raskolnikov’s entrance Porfiry Petrovitch had at once closed the door by which he had come in and they remained alone.
uz: Raskolnikovning kirishi bilan Porfiry Petrovitch darhol u kirib kelgan eshikni yopib qo'ydi va ular yolg'iz qolishdi.

en: He met his visitor with an apparently genial and good-tempered air, and it was only after a few minutes that Raskolnikov saw signs of a certain awkwardness in him, as though he had been thrown out of his reckoning or caught in something very secret.
uz: U mehmonini ko'rinib turganiday genial va xushmuomalalik bilan uchratdi va Raskolnikov bir necha daqiqadan so'ng uning o'ziga xos noqulaylik belgilarini ko'rdi, xuddi u o'z hisobidan tashlab ketilgan yoki juda sirli narsada tutilgandek edi.

en: “Ah, my dear fellow!
uz: Ah, aziz do'stim!

en: Here you are … in our domain” … began Porfiry, holding out both hands to him.
uz: Mana sizlar... bizning yurtimizda... Porfirni boshlagansiz, unga qo'llaringizni uzatgansiz.

en: “Come, sit down, old man … or perhaps you don’t like to be called ‘my dear fellow’ and ‘old man!’ —tout court?
uz: Kosh, o'tir, keksa odam ... yoki ehtimol siz mening aziz hamkasbim va keksa odam deb atashni yoqtirmaysiz!tout court?

en: Please don’t think it too familiar.
uz: Iltimos, uni juda tanish deb o'ylamang.

en: … Here, on the sofa.” Raskolnikov sat down, keeping his eyes fixed on him.
uz: Raskolnikov o'tirdi va ko'zlarini unga qaratdi.

en: “In our domain,” the apologies for familiarity, the French phrase tout court, were all characteristic signs.
uz: Bizning hududimizda tanishlik uchun uzr so'rab, frantsuzcha "tout court" so'zi hammasi o'ziga xos belgilar edi.

en: “He held out both hands to me, but he did not give me one —he drew it back in time,” struck him suspiciously.
uz: U menga qo'llarini uzatdi, lekin menga qo'l bermadi, uni vaqt o'tishi bilan orqaga surdi va unga shubha bilan urdi.

en: Both were watching each other, but when their eyes met, quick as lightning they looked away.
uz: Ikkalasi ham bir-birlariga qarab turardi, lekin ko'zlari bir-biriga to'g'ri kelganida, ular chaqmoq kabi tez bir yo'ldan o'zlarini chetga qaradilar.

en: “I brought you this paper … about the watch.
uz: Men sizga soat haqida ushbu qog'ozni olib keldim.

en: Is it all right or shall I copy it again?” “What?
uz: Bu yaxshimi yoki uni yana nusxa olishim kerakmi? Nima?
