en: For ten seconds there was silence as though all had been struck dumb; even the warder stepped back, mechanically retreated to the door, and stood immovable.
uz: O'n soniya davomida hamma so'zsiz qolganidek, xotirjamlik bo'ldi; hatto soqchi ham orqaga qarab, mexanik ravishda eshik tomon orqaga qaytdi va o'rnida turdi.

en: “What is it?” cried Porfiry Petrovitch, recovering from his momentary stupefaction.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch o'zining vaqtinchalik qo'rqinchligidan tiklanayotganda: "Bu nima?" - deb qayg'urdi.

en: “I … am the murderer,” repeated Nikolay, after a brief pause.
uz: "Men ... qotilman", - deb takrorladi Nikolay, biroz to'xtab o'tirganidan so'ng.

en: “What … you … what … whom did you kill?” Porfiry Petrovitch was obviously bewildered.
uz: Nima ... siz ... nima ... kimni o'ldirdingiz? Porfiry Petrovitch, albatta, g'alati edi.

en: Nikolay again was silent for a moment.
uz: Nikolay yana bir muncha sukut saqladi.

en: “Alyona Ivanovna and her sister Lizaveta Ivanovna, I … killed … with an axe.
uz: Alyona Ivanovna va uning singlisi Lizaveta Ivanovna, men ... o'ldirib yubordim ... balt bilan.

en: Darkness came over me,” he added suddenly, and was again silent.
uz: Qorong'ilik meni o'rab oldi, - dedi u birdan qo'shimcha qilib, yana bir bor so'zsiz qoldi.

en: He still remained on his knees.
uz: U hali ham tiz cho'kkan edi.

en: Porfiry Petrovitch stood for some moments as though meditating, but suddenly roused himself and waved back the uninvited spectators.
uz: Porfiry Petrovitch bir necha daqiqa o'ylab turgan, lekin to'satdan o'zini uyg'otdi va taklif qilinmagan tomoshabinlarni o'ziga jalb qildi.

en: They instantly vanished and closed the door.
uz: Ular darhol yo'qolishdi va eshikni yopishdi.

en: Then he looked towards Raskolnikov, who was standing in the corner, staring wildly at Nikolay and moved towards him, but stopped short, looked from Nikolay to Raskolnikov and then again at Nikolay, and seeming unable to restrain himself darted at the latter.
uz: Keyin u burchada turgan Raskolnikovga qaradi va Nikolayga vahima bilan qaradi va uning yoniga harakatlanadi, lekin ozgina to'xtadi, Nikolaydan Raskolnikovga va keyin yana Nikolayga qaradi va o'zini to'xtata olmaydigan bo'lib ko'rinadi.

en: “You’re in too great a hurry,” he shouted at him, almost angrily.
uz: "Siz juda tez yuribsiz", - deb qichqirdi u, deyarli g'azabga to'lib.

en: “I didn’t ask you what came over you.
uz: Men senga nima yuz berganini so'ramagan edim.

en: … Speak, did you kill them?” “I am the murderer.
uz: ... gapir, siz ularni o'ldirganmisiz?Men qotilman.

en: … I want to give evidence,” Nikolay pronounced.
uz: ... Men guvohlik bermoqchiman, - dedi Nikolay.

en: What did you kill them with?” “An axe.
uz: Ularni nima bilan o'ldirgansiz?Bir o'g'ir.

en: I had it ready.” “Ach, he is in a hurry!
uz: Men uni tayyorlab qo'ygan edim.A, u shoshilmoqda!

en: Alone?” Nikolay did not understand the question.
uz: yolg'iz? Nikolay savolni tushunmadi.

en: “Did you do it alone?” “Yes, alone.
uz: Siz buni yolg'iz qildingizmi?  Ha, yolg'iz.

en: And Mitka is not guilty and had no share in it.” “Don’t be in a hurry about Mitka!
uz: Va Mitka aybdor emas va bunga hech qanday ulushi yo'q.Mitka haqida shoshilmang!

en: How was it you ran downstairs like that at the time?
uz: O'sha paytda qanday qilib pastga shunday yugurib borgansiz?

en: The porters met you both!” “It was to put them off the scent … I ran after Mitka,” Nikolay replied hurriedly, as though he had prepared the answer.
uz: "Kofirlar ikkovingizni uchratdi! Bu ularni g'amdan chiqarish uchun edi... Men Mitka orqasidan yugurdim", - deb javob berdi Nikolay shoshilinch, xuddi javobni tayyorlagan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “I knew it!” cried Porfiry, with vexation.
uz: Men buni bilardim! Porfiry g'azabdan baqirib yubordi.

en: “It’s not his own tale he is telling,” he muttered as though to himself, and suddenly his eyes rested on Raskolnikov again.
uz: U o'z hikoyasini aytmayapti, o'zi o'zi o'zi haqida gapirayotgandek gapirdi va birdan ko'zlari Raskolnikovga qaytdi.

en: He was apparently so taken up with Nikolay that for a moment he had forgotten Raskolnikov.
uz: Nikolay bilan shunchalik band bo'lganki, bir zum Raskolnikovni unutib qo'ydi.

en: He was a little taken aback.
uz: U biroz ajablanib qoldi.

en: “My dear Rodion Romanovitch, excuse me!” he flew up to him, “this won’t do; I’m afraid you must go … it’s no good your staying … I will … you see, what a surprise!
uz: My dear Rodion Romanovitch, meni kechiring! u unga uchib keldi, this do'st bo'lmaydi; Men qo'rqaman, siz ketishingiz kerak ... bu sizning qolishingizning hech qanday foydasi yo'q ... Men ... ko'rasiz, nima ajablanarli!

en: … Goodbye!” And taking him by the arm, he showed him to the door.
uz: Xo'sh, salom! Uni qo'lidan ushlab, eshikga olib bordi.

en: “I suppose you didn’t expect it?” said Raskolnikov who, though he had not yet fully grasped the situation, had regained his courage.
uz: Raskolnikov hali vaziyatni to'liq tushunmagan bo'lsa-da, jasoratini tiklagan.

en: “You did not expect it either, my friend.
uz: Siz ham buni kutmagan edingiz, do'stim.

en: See how your hand is trembling!
uz: Ko'ring, qo'ling qanday titraydi!

en: He-he!” “You’re trembling, too, Porfiry Petrovitch!” “Yes, I am; I didn’t expect it.” They were already at the door; Porfiry was impatient for Raskolnikov to be gone.
uz: Ha! Siz ham titrab yuribsiz, Porfiry Petrovitch!  Ha, shundayman; men buni kutilmaganman. Ular allaqachon eshik oldida edilar; Porfiry Raskolnikovning ketishini intizorlik bilan kutardi.

en: “And your little surprise, aren’t you going to show it to me?” Raskolnikov said, sarcastically.
uz: Va sizning kichkina ajablanishingiz, menga ko'rsatmaysizmi? Raskolnikov sarkastika bilan dedi.

en: “Why, his teeth are chattering as he asks, he-he!
uz: Nima uchun, u so'rab turganida, uning tishlari qichqirib ketyapti, he-he!

en: You are an ironical person!
uz: Siz ironik insonsiz!

en: Come, till we meet!” “I believe we can say goodbye!” “That’s in God’s hands,” muttered Porfiry, with an unnatural smile.
uz: Kelinglar, uchrashuvga qadar!Men o'ylaymanki, biz xayrlashishimiz mumkin!Bu Xudo qo'lida, murmurli Porfiry, tabiiy bo'lmagan tabassum bilan.

en: As he walked through the office, Raskolnikov noticed that many people were looking at him.
uz: Raskolnikov ofis orqali o'tib ketayotganda, ko'p odamlar unga qarab turganini payqadi.

en: Among them he saw the two porters from the house, whom he had invited that night to the police station.
uz: Ular orasida u o'sha kecha politsiya bo'linmasiga taklif qilgan uydagi ikkita portiyerni ko'rdi.

en: They stood there waiting.
uz: Ular o'sha yerda kutib turishdi.

en: But he was no sooner on the stairs than he heard the voice of Porfiry Petrovitch behind him.
uz: Ammo u qadam bosganidan so'ng orqasidan Porfiry Petrovitchning ovozini eshitdi.

en: Turning round, he saw the latter running after him, out of breath.
uz: O'girilib ko'rganida, o'sha yigitning orqasidan ergashib, nafasini ketkazganini ko'rdi.

en: “One word, Rodion Romanovitch; as to all the rest, it’s in God’s hands, but as a matter of form there are some questions I shall have
uz: Bir so'z, Rodion Romanovitch; qolgan hamma narsa Xudoning qo'lida, lekin shakl masalasi bo'yicha ba'zi savollarim bor.

en: to ask you … so we shall meet again, shan’t we?” And Porfiry stood still, facing him with a smile.
uz: Sizdan so'rashim kerak... yana uchrashamiz, shunday emasmi? Porfiry esa o'rnidan turib, unga tabassum bilan qaradi.

en: “Shan’t we?” he added again.
uz: Shant we? u yana qo'shdi.

en: He seemed to want to say something more, but could not speak out.
uz: U yana ko'proq gapirishni xohlagan, ammo ko'proq gapirishni istamagan.

en: “You must forgive me, Porfiry Petrovitch, for what has just passed  … I lost my temper,” began Raskolnikov, who had so far regained his courage that he felt irresistibly inclined to display his coolness.
uz: Siz meni kechirishingiz kerak, Porfiry Petrovitch, o'tgan voqealar uchun ... Men o'zimni yo'qotdim, dedi Raskolnikov, u hozirgacha jasoratini tiklagan va o'z sovuqligini ko'rsatish uchun o'zini qarshiliksiz moyil his qilgan.

en: “Don’t mention it, don’t mention it,” Porfiry replied, almost gleefully.
uz: Don't mention it, don't mention it, Porfiry javob berdi, deyarli xursandchilik bilan.

en: “I myself, too … I have a wicked temper, I admit it!
uz: O'zim ham... men yomon ruhiy hissiyotga egaman, buni tan olaman!

en: But we shall meet again.
uz: Ammo biz yana uchrashamiz.

en: If it’s God’s will, we may see a great deal of one another.” “And will get to know each other through and through?” added Raskolnikov.
uz: Agar Xudoning irodasi bo'lsa, biz bir-birimizni ko'p ko'rishimiz mumkin. Va bir-birimizni to'liq va to'liq bilib olamizmi? Raskolnikov qo'shimcha qildi.

en: “Yes; know each other through and through,” assented Porfiry Petrovitch, and he screwed up his eyes, looking earnestly at Raskolnikov.
uz: "Ha, bir-birimizni to'liq tanishimiz kerak", - dedi Porfiry Petrovitch va Raskolnikovga e'tiborli bo'lib, ko'zlarini o'zgartirgan.

en: “Now you’re going to a birthday party?” “To a funeral.” “Of course, the funeral!
uz: Endi tug'ilgan kun to'g'risidagi partiyaga boryapsizmi?

en: Take care of yourself, and get well.” “I don’t know what to wish you,” said Raskolnikov, who had begun to descend the stairs, but looked back again.
uz: O'zingga g'amxo'rlik qilib, sog'ayib ket. Sizga nima tilayman, bilmayman, - dedi Raskolnikov, u qadam bosgan edi, lekin yana orqaga qarab qoldi.

en: “I should like to wish you success, but your office is such a comical one.” “Why comical?” Porfiry Petrovitch had turned to go, but he seemed to prick up his ears at this.
uz: Men sizga muvaffaqiyat tilayman, lekin sizning ishxonangiz juda kulgili.  Nima uchun kulgili? Porfiry Petrovitch ketish uchun o'zini o'zgartirgan edi, ammo u bu haqda o'z quloqlarini tikkan bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: “Why, how you must have been torturing and harassing that poor Nikolay psychologically, after your fashion, till he confessed!
uz: Qani, siz bechora Nikolayni tan olmaguncha, o'zingizning uslubingizcha, qandaydir azob-uqubatlarga duchor bo'lib, ruhiy jihatdan qayg'urgan bo'lsangiz kerak!

en: You must have been at him day and night, proving to him that he was the murderer, and now that he has confessed, you’ll begin vivisecting him again.
uz: Siz unga kechayu kunduz bo'lib, u qotil ekanini isbotlagan bo'lishingiz kerak va hozir u tan olganidan so'ng, uni qayta tiriklashtirishni boshlashingiz kerak.

en: ‘You are lying,’ you’ll say.
uz: Siz yolg'on gapiryapsiz, deysiz.

en: ‘You are not the murderer!
uz: Siz qotil emassiz!

en: It’s not your own tale you are telling!’ You must admit it’s a comical business!” “He-he-he!
uz: Siz o'zingizning hikoyangizni aytmaysiz! Siz tan olishingiz kerakki, bu komediya ishidir!He-he-he!

en: You noticed then that I said to Nikolay just now that it was not his own tale he was telling?” “How could I help noticing it!” “He-he!
uz: O'sha paytda siz Nikolayga u o'z hikoyasi emasligini aytganimni payqagan edingizmi?Men buni payqashdan qanday qochishim mumkin?He-he!

en: You are quick-witted.
uz: Siz tezkor bo'lasiz.

en: You notice everything!
uz: Siz hamma narsaga e'tibor berasiz!

en: You’ve really a playful mind!
uz: Siz haqiqatan ham o'yinchi ongingiz bor!

en: And you always fasten on the comic side … he-he!
uz: Va siz har doim komiks tarafida bog'lanasiz ... u-u!

en: They say that was the marked characteristic of Gogol, among the writers.”
uz: Ular aytishicha, bu yozuvchilar orasida Gogolning aniq xususiyati edi.

en: “Yes, of Gogol.” “Yes, of Gogol.
uz: Yes, Gogol. Yes, Gogol.

en: … I shall look forward to meeting you.” “So shall I.” Raskolnikov walked straight home.
uz: ... Siz bilan uchrashishni orziqib kutaman.  Shunday qilib, I. Raskolnikov to'g'ridan-to'g'ri uyga yurdi.

en: He was so muddled and bewildered that on getting home he sat for a quarter of an hour on the sofa, trying to collect his thoughts.
uz: U shunchalik g'alati va g'alati bo'lganki, uyga qaytgach, sofa ustida qirq soat o'tirdi va o'z fikrlarini to'plashga harakat qildi.

en: He did not attempt to think about Nikolay; he was stupefied; he felt that his confession was something inexplicable, amazing —something beyond his understanding.
uz: U Nikolay haqida o'ylashga harakat qilmadi; u hayron edi; uning tanbehini tushuntirib bo'lmaydigan, hayratlanarli bir narsa deb o'ylardi.

en: But Nikolay’s confession was an actual fact.
uz: Ammo Nikolayning tanbehlari haqiqiy fakt edi.

en: The consequences of this fact were clear to him at once, its falsehood could not fail to be discovered, and then they would be after him again.
uz: Bu faktning oqibatlari unga darhol ayon bo'ldi, uning yolg'onligi aniqlanishiga to'sqinlik qila olmaydi va keyin ular yana uning orqasidan quvg'in qilishadi.

en: Till then, at least, he was free and must do something for himself, for the danger was imminent.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda o'sha paytgacha u erkin edi va o'zi uchun biror narsa qilishi kerak edi, chunki xavf-xatar yaqin edi.

en: His position gradually became clear to him.
uz: Keyinchalik uning mavqeyi unga asta-sekin ayon bo'ldi.

en: Remembering, sketchily, the main outlines of his recent scene with Porfiry, he could not help shuddering again with horror.
uz: Porfir bilan o'zining so'nggi sahnasining asosiy ko'rinishlarini eslatib, u yana dahshatga tushdi.

en: Of course, he did not yet know all Porfiry’s aims, he could not see into all his calculations.
uz: Albatta, u hali Porfirining barcha maqsadlarini bilmagan, barcha hisob-kitoblarini aniqlay olmagan.

en: But he had already partly shown his hand, and no one knew better than Raskolnikov how terrible Porfiry’s “lead” had been for him.
uz: Ammo u allaqachon qisman qo'lini ko'rsatgan edi va hech kim Raskolnikovdan ko'ra Porfirys uchun qanchalik dahshatli bo'lganini yaxshi bilmagan.

en: A little more and he might have given himself away completely, circumstantially.
uz: Bir oz ko'proq va u o'zini to'liq, shunga yarasha berishi mumkin edi.

en: Knowing his nervous temperament and from the first glance seeing through him, Porfiry, though playing a bold game, was bound to win.
uz: Uning g'ayratli tuyg'usini bilgan va birinchi qarashda uni ko'rgan Porfiry jasoratli o'yin o'ynagan bo'lsa-da, albatta g'alaba qozonadi.

en: There’s no denying that Raskolnikov had compromised himself seriously, but no facts had come to light as yet; there was nothing positive.
uz: Raskolnikovning o'zini jiddiy halokatga solganini inkor qilish mumkin emas, ammo hali hech qanday fakt oshkor etilmagan; hech qanday ijobiy narsa yo'q edi.

en: But was he taking a true view of the position?
uz: Ammo u o'z vazifasini to'g'ri ko'rib turibdimi?

en: What had Porfiry been trying to get at?
uz: Porfiry nimaga erishmoqchi edi?

en: Had he really some surprise prepared for him?
uz: Haqiqatan ham, u o'zi uchun biron bir kutilmagani tayyorlaganmi?

en: Had he really been expecting something or not?
uz: Haqiqatan ham u biror narsani kutganmi yoki yo'qmi?

en: How would they have parted if it had not been for the unexpected appearance of Nikolay?
uz: Nikolayning kutilmagan ko'rinishi bo'lmaganida, ular qanday ajrashgan bo'lishardi?

en: Porfiry had shown almost all his cards —of course, he had risked something in showing them —and if he had really had anything up his sleeve (Raskolnikov reflected), he would have shown that, too.
uz: Porfiry deyarli barcha kartalarini ko'rsatgan edi, albatta, ularni ko'rsatishda u biror narsa xavf ostiga qo'ygan edi va agar u chindan ham biror narsa ko'rsatgan bo'lsa (Raskolnikov o'ylagan), u ham buni ko'rsatgan bo'lardi.

en: What was that “surprise”?
uz: Bu qanday "o'yin-kulg'i" edi?

en: Had it meant anything?
uz: Bu biron bir narsani anglatadimi?

en: Could it have concealed anything like a fact, a piece of positive evidence?
uz: Bu haqiqatni, ijobiy dalillarni yashirishi mumkinmi?

en: His yesterday’s visitor?
uz: Uning kechagi tashrif buyuruvchisi?

en: What had become of him?
uz: Uning hayoti nimaga aylandi?

en: If Porfiry really had any evidence, it must be connected with him.
uz: Agar Porfirning biron bir dalillari bor bo'lsa, bu uning o'zi bilan bog'liq bo'lishi kerak.

en: … He sat on the sofa with his elbows on his knees and his face hidden in his hands.
uz: U sofa ustida o'tirdi, qo'lqoplari tiz cho'kib, yuzini qo'llarida yashirib qo'ydi.

en: He was still shivering nervously.
uz: U hali ham g'azabdan titrab yurgan edi.

en: At last he got up, took his cap, thought a minute, and went to the door.
uz: Nihoyat, u o'rnidan turib, to'pini olib, bir daqiqa o'ylab, eshikga bordi.

en: He had a sort of presentiment that for today, at least, he might consider himself out of danger.
uz: U hozircha hech bo'lmaganda o'zini xavfdan xalos deb hisoblashi mumkinligini his qilgan.

en: He had a sudden sense almost of joy; he wanted to make haste to Katerina Ivanovna’s.
uz: U to'satdan quvonch hissi paydo bo'ldi; u Katerina Ivanovnaga shoshilmoqchi bo'ldi.

en: He would be too late for the funeral, of course, but he would be in time for the memorial dinner, and there at once he would see Sonia.
uz: Albatta, u dafn marosimiga kech ketadi, lekin marosimga o'z vaqtida keladi va shu zahoti u Soniyani ko'radi.

en: He stood still, thought a moment, and a suffering smile came for a moment on to his lips.
uz: U to'xtadi, bir daqiqa o'ylab ko'rdi va bir daqiqa davomida uning og'zidan og'ir tabassum paydo bo'ldi.

en: Today,” he repeated to himself.
uz: Bugun u o'ziga takrorladi.

en: …” But as he was about to open the door, it began opening of itself.
uz: Ammo u eshikni ochmoqchi bo'lganida, u o'z-o'zidan ochilishni boshladi.

en: He started and moved back.
uz: U boshladi va orqaga qaytdi.

en: The door opened gently and slowly, and there suddenly appeared a figure —yesterday’s visitor from underground.
uz: Eshikni sekin-sekin ochib, to'satdan yer ostidagi bir kishi paydo bo'ldi.

en: The man stood in the doorway, looked at Raskolnikov without speaking, and took a step forward into the room.
uz: Oʻsha kishi eshikda turib, Raskolnikovga gapirmasdan qaradi va bir qadam oldinga kirib xonaga kiradi.

en: He was exactly the same as yesterday; the same figure, the same dress, but there was a great change in his face; he looked dejected and sighed deeply.
uz: U to'g'ri kechagidek edi; xuddi shu shakl, xuddi shu kiyim, lekin yuzida katta o'zgarish bo'ldi; u tushkun ko'rinishga ega edi va chuqur nafas oldi.

en: If he had only put his hand up to his cheek and leaned his head on one side he would have looked exactly like a peasant woman.
uz: Agar u qo'lini jilovga qo'yib, boshini bir tomonga tiklaganida edi, xuddi qishloq ayolga o'xshar edi.

en: “What do you want?” asked Raskolnikov, numb with terror.
uz: Siz nima istaysiz? deb so'radi Raskolnikov, qo'rquvdan befarq bo'lib.

en: The man was still silent, but suddenly he bowed down almost to the ground, touching it with his finger.
uz: U hali ham sukut saqlab qoldi, lekin to'satdan deyarli yerga yiqilib, uni barmog'i bilan tutibdi.

en: “I have sinned,” the man articulated softly.
uz: Men gunoh qildim,  kishi sekin so'zladi.

en: “How?” “By evil thoughts.” They looked at one another.
uz: Qanday?  Yomon fikrlar bilan. Ular bir-birlariga qarab turishdi.

en: When you came, perhaps in drink, and bade the porters go to the police station and asked about the blood, I was vexed that they let you go and took you for drunken.
uz: Siz, ehtimol, ichgan holda kelganingizda va portiyerlarga politsiya bo'linmasiga borib, qon haqida so'rashni buyurganingizda, men sizni ketishga ruxsat berishganidan xafa bo'ldim va sizni mast deb o'ylagani uchun xafa bo'ldim.

en: I was so vexed that I lost my sleep.
uz: Men shunchalik xafa bo'ldimki, uxlamaganman.

en: And remembering the address we came here yesterday and asked for you.
uz: Kecha bu yerga kelganimiz va sizdan so'raganimiz manzilni eslatib turamiz.

en: “Who came?” Raskolnikov interrupted, instantly beginning to recollect.
uz: Kim keldi? Raskolnikov to'xtatdi va darhol eslay boshladi.

en: “I did, I’ve wronged you.” “Then you come from that house?” “I was standing at the gate with them … don’t you remember?
uz: Men sizga yomonlik qildim, sizga yomonlik qildim.  Keyin siz o'sha uydan keldingizmi?  Men ular bilan darvoza oldida turgan edim ... eslaysizmi?

en: We have carried on our trade in that house for years past.
uz: Biz o'tgan yillar davomida o'sha uyda savdo-sotiqni davom ettirdik.

en: We cure and prepare hides, we take work home … most of all I was vexed.
uz: Biz terini davolash va tayyorlash, ishni uyga olib borish ... eng asosiysi men xafa bo'ldim.

en: …” And the whole scene of the day before yesterday in the gateway came clearly before Raskolnikov’s mind; he recollected that there had been several people there besides the porters, women among them.
uz: ... O'tgan kunning darvozachasidagi butun sahna Raskolnikovning ongida aniq paydo bo'ldi; u u erda portiyerlardan tashqari bir nechta odam borligini esladi, ular orasida ayollar ham bor edi.

en: He remembered one voice had suggested taking him straight to the police-station.
uz: U bir ovoz uni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri politsiya bo'linmasiga olib ketishni taklif qilganini esladi.

en: He could not recall the face of the speaker, and even now he did not recognise it, but he remembered that he had turned round and made him some answer.
uz: U nutq so'zlovchining yuzini eslay olmagan va hozir ham uni tanib olmagan, lekin u o'girilib, unga javob berganini esladi.

en: … So this was the solution of yesterday’s horror.
uz: Shunday qilib, bu kechalik dahshatning yechimi edi.

en: The most awful thought was that he had been actually almost lost, had almost done for himself on account of such a trivial circumstance.
uz: Eng dahshatli fikr shundaki, u o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi uchun o'zi yo'zi yo'zi yo'ldirib qo'g'g'g'g'g'ladi.

en: So this man could tell nothing except his asking about the flat and the blood stains.
uz: Shunday qilib, bu odam o'sha xonadon va qon leklari haqida so'rashdan boshqa hech narsa aytolmadi.

en: So Porfiry, too, had nothing but that delirium, no facts but this psychology which cuts both ways, nothing positive.
uz: Shunday qilib, Porfirida ham bu deliriyadan boshqa hech narsa yo'q edi, faktlar yo'q edi, balki ikki yo'lni kesadigan psixologiya bor edi, ijobiy narsa yo'q edi.

en: So if no more facts come to light (and they must not, they must not!) then … then what can they do to him?
uz: Shunday qilib, agar boshqa hech qanday fakt oshkor bo'lmasa (va ular oshkor bo'lmasligi kerak, ular ham oshkor bo'lmasligi kerak!) u holda ... ular unga nima qilishlari mumkin?

en: How can they convict him, even if they arrest him?
uz: Qanday qilib uni hibsga olishsa ham, uni hukm qilishlari mumkin?

en: And Porfiry then had only just heard about the flat and had not known about it before.
uz: O'shanda Porfiry bu xonadon haqida faqatgina eshitgan edi va bu haqda ilgari bilmagan edi.

en: “Was it you who told Porfiry … that I’d been there?” he cried, struck by a sudden idea.
uz: Porfirga o'sha yerda bo'lganimni aytgan sizmisiz? U to'satdan g'oyaga tushib yig'ladi.

en: “What Porfiry?” “The head of the detective department?” “Yes.
uz: What Porfiry?Detektivlar bo'limi boshlig'i?Ha.

en: The porters did not go there, but I went.” “Today?” “I got there two minutes before you.
uz: Tashkivchilar u yerga bormagan, lekin men borganman.Bugun?Men sizdan ikki daqiqa oldin u yerga keldim.

en: And I heard, I heard it all, how he worried you.” “Where?
uz: Va men uning sizni qanchalik xavotirga solganini eshitdim, hamma narsani eshitdim.  Qayerda?

en: When?” “Why, in the next room.
uz: Qachon?  Nima uchun, qo'shni xonada.

en: I was sitting there all the time.” “What?
uz: Men doim o'sha yerda o'tirardim.  Nima?

en: Why, then you were the surprise?
uz: Nima uchun, unda siz hayratlanarli bo'ldingiz?

en: But how could it happen?
uz: Ammo bu qanday bo'lishi mumkin?

en: “I saw that the porters did not want to do what I said,” began the man; “for it’s too late, said they, and maybe he’ll be angry that we did not come at the time.
uz: Men ko'rdimki, portiyerlar mening so'zlarimni bajarishni istamadilar,  odamni boshladi; bu juda kech ekan, deb aytishdi, va ehtimol biz o'z vaqtida kelmaganimiz uchun u g'azablanadi.

en: I was vexed and I lost my sleep, and I began making inquiries.
uz: Men xafa bo'lib, uxlamaganman va savollar berishni boshladim.

en: And finding out yesterday where to go, I went today.
uz: Kecha qaerga borishni bilganimda, bugun bordim.

en: The first time I went he wasn’t there, when I came an hour later he couldn’t see me.
uz: Birinchi bor u yerda bo'lmagan, bir soat o'tib kelganimda meni ko'rmadi.

en: I went the third time, and they showed me in.
uz: Uchinchi marta borganimda, meni ichkariga olib kirishdi.

en: I informed him of everything, just as it happened, and he began skipping about the room and punching himself on the chest.
uz: Men unga hamma narsani xuddi sodir bo'lganidek aytib berdim va u xonadan tashqariga chiqib, ko'krakga urishni boshladi.

en: ‘What do you scoundrels mean by it?
uz: Sizlar bu so'z bilan nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?

en: If I’d known about it I should have arrested him!’ Then he ran out, called somebody and began talking to him in the corner, then he turned to me, scolding and questioning me.
uz: Agar bilganimda uni hibsga olishim kerak edi! Keyin u yugurib chiqib, kimnidir chaqirib, burchada u bilan gaplashishni boshladi, so'ngra menga qarab, meni tanqid qildi va so'rov berdi.

en: He scolded me a great deal; and I told him everything, and I told him that you didn’t dare to say a word in answer to me yesterday and that you didn’t recognise me.
uz: U meni qattiq tanqid qildi; men unga hamma narsani aytib berdim va siz kecha menga javob berishga jur'at etmaganingizni va meni tanimaganingizni aytdim.

en: And he fell to running about again and kept hitting himself on the chest, and getting angry and running about, and when you were announced he told me to go into the next room.
uz: U yana qochib o'zini ko'krakga urib, g'azablanib, qochib o'tadi va sizni e'lon qilishganida menga qo'shni xonaniga kirishimni aytdi.

en: ‘Sit there a bit,’ he said.
uz: "Biroz o'tiring", dedi u.

en: ‘Don’t move, whatever you may hear.’ And he set a chair there for me and locked me in.
uz: Sizlar nima eshitsangiz ham, harakatlanmanglar. U menga o'rinni o'rnatdi va meni o'sha yerga qulflab qo'ydi.

en: ‘Perhaps,’ he said, ‘I may call you.’ And when Nikolay’d been brought he let me out as soon as you were gone.
uz: Balki, - dedi u, - seni chaqirsam bo'ladi. - Nikolay olib kelingach, sen ketgandan so'ng meni qo'yib yubordi.

en: ‘I shall send for you again and question you,’ he said.” “And did he question Nikolay while you were there?” “He got rid of me as he did of you, before he spoke to Nikolay.” The man stood still, and again suddenly bowed down, touching the ground with his finger.
uz: Men sizni yana chaqirtirib, so'rab yuboraman, - dedi u. - Siz u yerda bo'lganingizda u Nikolayni so'raganmi? - Nikolay bilan gaplashishdan oldin, siz bilan bo'lganidek, meni ham so'rab oldi. - U kishi to'xtadi va birdan yana tiz cho'kib, barmog'i bilan yerga tegdi.

en: “Forgive me for my evil thoughts, and my slander.” “May God forgive you,” answered Raskolnikov.
uz: Mening yomon fikrlarim va tuhmatlarim uchun meni kechiring. Xudo sizni kechirsin, - deb javob berdi Raskolnikov.

en: And as he said this, the man bowed down again, but not to the ground, turned slowly and went out of the room.
uz: Bu so'zlarni aytgandan so'ng, u odam yana tiz cho'kdi, lekin yerga tashlanmay, sekin-sakin o'girilib, xonadan chiqib ketdi.

en: “It all cuts both ways, now it all cuts both ways,” repeated Raskolnikov, and he went out more confident than ever.
uz: Bu har ikki yo'lni kesadi, endi hammasi har ikki yo'lni kesadi, Raskolnikov takrorladi va u har qachongidan ko'ra ko'proq ishonch bilan chiqdi.

en: “Now we’ll make a fight for it,” he said, with a malicious smile, as he went down the stairs.
uz: Endi biz buning uchun kurashamiz, - dedi u, o'rinsiz tabassum bilan, poyezddan tushayotganda.

en: His malice was aimed at himself; with shame and contempt he recollected his “cowardice.”
uz: Uning yovuzligi o'ziga qaratilgan edi; uyat va kamsitish bilan u o'z qo'rqinchligini esladi.

en: I The morning that followed the fateful interview with Dounia and her mother brought sobering influences to bear on Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Dounia va uning onasi bilan o'tkazilgan halokatli intervyudan keyingi ertalab Pyotr Petrovitchga o'ziga xos ta'sir ko'rsatdi.

en: Intensely unpleasant as it was, he was forced little by little to accept as a fact beyond recall what had seemed to him only the day before fantastic and incredible.
uz: Bu juda yoqimsiz bo'lsa-da, u bir kun oldin ajoyib va ajoyib tuyulgan narsalarni esdan chiqarmay qabul qilishga majbur bo'ldi.

en: The black snake of wounded vanity had been gnawing at his heart all night.
uz: Yog'irlikning qora ilonasi butun kecha uning yuragida o'tirgan edi.

en: When he got out of bed, Pyotr Petrovitch immediately looked in the looking-glass.
uz: Yotoqdan turib, Pyotr Petrovitch darhol o'ziga qaradi.

en: He was afraid that he had jaundice.
uz: U sarg'ayib qolganidan qo'rqardi.

en: However his health seemed unimpaired so far, and looking at his noble, clear-skinned countenance which had grown fattish of late, Pyotr Petrovitch for an instant was positively comforted in the conviction that he would find another bride and, perhaps, even a better one.
uz: Biroq, sog'lig'i hozirgacha salomat ko'rinardi va oxirgi paytlarda o'zining shalgan, ko'rinmas, ko'rinmas ko'rinishiga qarab, Pyotr Petrovitch bir zum uchun boshqa, ehtimol, hatto yaxshiroq kelinni topishi haqidagi ishonch bilan tasalli topdi.

en: But coming back to the sense of his present position, he turned aside and spat vigorously, which excited a sarcastic smile in Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov, the young friend with whom he was staying.
uz: Ammo hozirgi vazifasini tushunib, u o'ziga qarab qolib, kuchli tupurdi, bu esa u yashayotgan yosh do'sti Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikovning sarkastika tabassumini uyg'otdi.

en: That smile Pyotr Petrovitch noticed, and at once set it down against his young friend’s account.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch bu tabassumni payqadi va uni o'z yosh do'sti hisobidan o'rnatdi.

en: He had set down a good many points against him of late.
uz: So'nggi paytlarda u o'ziga qarshi ko'plab o'yinlar o'tkazdi.

en: His anger was redoubled when he reflected that he ought not to have told Andrey Semyonovitch about the result of yesterday’s interview.
uz: O'zining g'azabini o'z ichiga olgan ko'pchilik Andrey Semyonovitchga o'tgan kungi intervyu natijalarini aytmasligi kerakligini o'ylab ko'rganidan keyin ko'proq ko'paydi.

en: That was the second mistake he had made in temper, through impulsiveness and irritability.
uz: Bu uning g'azablantirish va g'azablanish orqali qilgan ikkinchi xato edi.

en: … Moreover, all that morning one unpleasantness followed another.
uz: ... Bundan tashqari, butun ertalab bir yomonlik yana bir yomonlikdan keyin davom etdi.

en: He even found a hitch awaiting him in his legal case in the senate.
uz: U hatto senatda o'zining qonuniy da'volarida uni kutib turgan bir muammoni topdi.

en: He was particularly irritated by the owner of the flat which had been taken in view of his approaching marriage and was being redecorated at his own expense; the owner, a rich German tradesman, would not entertain the idea of breaking the contract which had just been signed and
uz: Ayniqsa, u o'zining yaqinlashib kelayotgan nikohi sababli olib ketilgan va o'z xarajatlari bilan qayta bezatilgan kvartira egasi tomonidan g'azablanardi; boy nemis savdogari bo'lgan egasi shartnoma tuzilgan va imzolangan kontraktni buzish g'oyasini yoqtirmadi.

en: insisted on the full forfeit money, though Pyotr Petrovitch would be giving him back the flat practically redecorated.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch unga deyarli yangidan bezatilgan kvartirani qaytarib berishiga qaramay, to'liq to'lov pulini talab qildi.

en: In the same way the upholsterers refused to return a single rouble of the instalment paid for the furniture purchased but not yet removed to the flat.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, polyerlar sotib olingan, ammo hali kvartiraga olib ketilmagan mebel uchun to'langan haqning bir bor rublini qaytarishni rad etishdi.

en: “Am I to get married simply for the sake of the furniture?” Pyotr Petrovitch ground his teeth and at the same time once more he had a gleam of desperate hope.
uz: Menga faqat mebellar uchun turmushga chiqishim kerakmi? Pyotr Petrovitch o'z tishlarini yirtdi va shu bilan birga yana bir bor umidsizlikka to'lgan.

en: “Can all that be really so irrevocably over?
uz: Bularning barchasi haqiqatan ham o'z nihoyasiga yetishi mumkinmi?

en: Is it no use to make another effort?” The thought of Dounia sent a voluptuous pang through his heart.
uz: Yana bir urinishning foydasi yo'qmi? Dounia haqida o'ylash uning qalbiga o'tkir qichqiriq yubordi.

en: He endured anguish at that moment, and if it had been possible to slay Raskolnikov instantly by wishing it, Pyotr Petrovitch would promptly have uttered the wish.
uz: U o'sha paytda g'amginlikni boshdan kechirgan va agar Raskolnikovni o'ldirmoqchi bo'lganida, Pyotr Petrovitch ham o'sha istakni tezda aytgan bo'lardi.

en: “It was my mistake, too, not to have given them money,” he thought, as he returned dejectedly to Lebeziatnikov’s room, “and why on earth was I such a Jew?
uz: "Ularga pul bermaganim ham mening xatoim edi", - deb o'yladi u, tushkunlikka tushib, Lebeziatnikovning xonasiga qaytib kelganida, "va nega men bunday yahudiy bo'ldim?

en: It was false economy!
uz: Bu soxta iqtisodiyot edi!

en: I meant to keep them without a penny so that they should turn to me as their providence, and look at them!
uz: Men ularni hech qanday pulsiz qoldirishni xohladim, shuning uchun ular menga qarab, ularga qarab turishlari kerak edi!

en: If I’d spent some fifteen hundred roubles on them for the trousseau and presents, on knickknacks, dressing-cases, jewellery, materials, and all that sort of trash from Knopp’s and the English shop, my position would have been better and … stronger!
uz: Agar men ular uchun trousseau va sovg'alar uchun taxminan besh yuz rubl sarflaganimda edi, ular uchun knickknacks, kiyim-kechaklar, zargarlik, materiallar va Knopp's va ingliz do'konining barcha buyumlari uchun, mening mavqeyim yaxshiroq va ... kuchli bo'lardi!

en: They could not have refused me so easily!
uz: Ular meni shunchalik oson rad etishlari mumkin emas edi!

en: They are the sort of people that would feel bound to return money and presents if they broke it off; and they would find it hard to do it!
uz: Ular pul va sovg'alarni uzishsa qaytarib berishga majbur bo'lgan odamlarning turidirlar va buni qilish qiyin bo'ladi!

en: And their conscience would prick them: how can we dismiss a man who has hitherto been so generous and delicate?
uz: Ularning vijdoni ularga: "Hazrgacha shunchalik saxiy va mehribon bo'lgan kishini qanday rad etishimiz mumkin?" - degan savolni berardi.

en: I’ve made a blunder.” And grinding his teeth again, Pyotr Petrovitch called himself a fool —but not aloud, of course.
uz: Men xatoga yo'l qo'ydim. Va yana o'z tishlarini silkitib, Pyotr Petrovitch o'zini ahmoq deb atadi, lekin, albatta, baland ovoz bilan emas.

en: He returned home, twice as irritated and angry as before.
uz: U avvalgidek ikki baravar g'azab va g'azabga to'lgan holda uyga qaytib keldi.

en: The preparations for the funeral dinner at Katerina Ivanovna’s excited his curiosity as he passed.
uz: Katerina Ivanovnaxda o'tkaziladigan o'lim marosimiga tayyorgarlik ko'rish uning qiziqishini uyg'otdi.

en: He had heard about it the day before; he fancied, indeed, that he had been invited, but absorbed in his own cares he had paid no attention.
uz: O'sha kuni u bu haqda eshitgan edi; albatta, u taklif qilinganini o'ylagan edi, lekin o'z tashvishlari bilan band bo'lib, e'tibor bermagan.

en: Inquiring of Madame Lippevechsel who was busy laying the table while Katerina Ivanovna was away at the cemetery, he heard that the entertainment was to be a great affair, that all the lodgers had been invited, among them some who had not known the dead man, that even Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov was invited in spite of his previous quarrel with
uz: Katerina Ivanovna qabristonada bo'lganida, stolni o'rnatishda band bo'lgan Lippevechsel xonimdan so'rab, u o'yin-kulgi katta mashg'ulotlar bo'lishini, barcha mehmonlarni, shu jumladan, o'lgan kishini tanimaganlarni taklif etgani, hatto Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikovni ham taklif etgani haqida eshitdi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna, that he, Pyotr Petrovitch, was not only invited, but was eagerly expected as he was the most important of the lodgers.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna, u, Pyotr Petrovitch, nafaqat taklif etilgan, balki u mehmonlarning eng muhimsi bo'lgani uchun juda kutilgan.

en: Amalia Ivanovna herself had been invited with great ceremony in spite of the recent unpleasantness, and so she was very busy with preparations and was taking a positive pleasure in them; she was moreover dressed up to the nines, all in new black silk, and she was proud of it.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna o'zi yaqinda yuz bergan noqulayliklarga qaramay, katta marosim bilan taklif etilgan edi va shuning uchun u tayyorgarlik ishlari bilan juda band edi va ulardan ijobiy zavq olib borardi; bundan tashqari, u yangi qora ipak kiyimlari bilan to'qqizta rangga ega edi va bunga g'ururlanardi.

en: All this suggested an idea to Pyotr Petrovitch and he went into his room, or rather Lebeziatnikov’s, somewhat thoughtful.
uz: Bularning barchasi Pyotr Petrovitchga g'oya tug'dirdi va u o'z xonasiga, yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Lebeziatnikovlarga, biroz mulohaza yuritib ketdi.

en: He had learnt that Raskolnikov was to be one of the guests.
uz: U Raskolnikov mehmonlardan biri bo'lishini bilib olgan edi.

en: Andrey Semyonovitch had been at home all the morning.
uz: Andrey Semyonovitch butun ertalab uyda bo'lgan.

en: The attitude of Pyotr Petrovitch to this gentleman was strange, though perhaps natural.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitchning bu xonimga bo'lgan munosabati g'ayrioddiy, ammo tabiiy bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch had despised and hated him from the day he came to stay with him and at the same time he seemed somewhat afraid of him.
uz: Pyotr Petroviç u bilan birga yashash uchun kelgan kundan boshlab uni kamsitgan va nafratlangan edi va shu bilan birga, u undan biroz qo'rqqan ko'rinardi.

en: He had not come to stay with him on his arrival in Petersburg simply from parsimony, though that had been perhaps his chief object.
uz: U Sankt-Peterburgga kelganida u bilan shunchaki parsimoniyadan kelib qolmagan edi, garchi bu uning asosiy maqsadi bo'lgan bo'lsa-da.

en: He had heard of Andrey Semyonovitch, who had once been his ward, as a leading young progressive who was taking an important part in certain interesting circles, the doings of which were a legend in the provinces.
uz: U bir vaqtlar uning bo'linmasi bo'lgan Andrey Semyonovitch haqida eshitgan edi, u muayyan qiziqarli doiralarda muhim o'rinni egallagan, o'z faoliyatini viloyatlarda afsona deb bilgan yetakchi yosh progressiv yigit edi.

en: It had impressed Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Bu Pyotr Petrovitchga ta'sir qildi.

en: These powerful omniscient circles who despised everyone and showed everyone up had long inspired in him a peculiar but quite vague alarm.
uz: Hammaga begunohlik ko'rsatib, hamma ko'rinishini ko'rsatadigan bu qudratli hamma narsani biluvchi doiralar uzoq vaqtdan beri uning o'ziga xos, ammo juda nodon ogohlantirishini uyg'otishgan edi.

en: He had not, of course, been able to form even an approximate notion of what they meant.
uz: Albatta, u ularning ma'nosini hatto taxminan tushunib yetmagan edi.

en: He, like everyone, had heard that there were, especially in Petersburg, progressives of some sort, nihilists and so on, and, like many people, he exaggerated and distorted the significance of those words to an absurd degree.
uz: U ham hamma kabi, ayniqsa Sankt-Peterburgda progressivlar, nihilistlar va shu kabilar borligini eshitgan edi va ko'plab odamlar kabi u ham bu so'zlarning ma'nosini absurd darajada o'zgartirib, buzib qo'ygan.

en: What for many years past he had feared more than anything was being shown up and this was the chief ground for his continual uneasiness at the thought of transferring his business to Petersburg.
uz: O'tgan yillar davomida u eng ko'p qo'rqqan narsa ko'rinadi va bu uning biznesini Sankt-Peterburgga o'tkazish fikridan doimiy xavotirlanishiga sabab bo'ldi.

en: He was afraid of this as little children are sometimes panic-stricken.
uz: U bundan qo'rqardi, chunki kichik bolalar ba'zan qo'rquvga tushib qolishadi.

en: Some years before, when he was just entering on his own career, he had come upon two cases in which rather important personages in the province, patrons of his, had been cruelly shown up.
uz: Bir necha yil oldin, u o'z faoliyatini boshlaganida, o'sha viloyatning muhim shaxslari, uning do'stlari, shafqatsiz ravishda ko'rsatilgan ikki holatga duch kelgan edi.

en: One instance had ended in great scandal for the person attacked and the other had very nearly ended in serious trouble.
uz: Bir holatda hujumga uchragan shaxs uchun katta shubha tug'ildi va ikkinchisi esa jiddiy muammolarga duch kelishga to'xtab qoldi.

en: For this reason Pyotr Petrovitch intended to go into the subject as soon as he reached Petersburg and, if necessary, to anticipate contingencies by
uz: Shuning uchun Pyotr Petrovitch Sankt-Peterburg shahriga yetib borganidan so'ng mavzuga kirib, zarur bo'lganda, bu mavzuda o'zgarishlar yuz berishini oldindan ko'rishni rejalashtirgan.

en: seeking the favour of “our younger generation.” He relied on Andrey Semyonovitch for this and before his visit to Raskolnikov he had succeeded in picking up some current phrases.
uz: Yosh avlodimizning roziligini izlash. U bu uchun Andrey Semyonovitchga tayanardi va Raskolnikovga tashrifidan oldin u ba'zi zamonaviy iboralarni o'rganishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

en: He soon discovered that Andrey Semyonovitch was a commonplace simpleton, but that by no means reassured Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: U tezda Andrey Semyonovitch oddiy odam ekanini, ammo bu Pyotr Petrovitchni hech qanday jihatdan xotirjamlashtirmaganini aniqladi.

en: Even if he had been certain that all the progressives were fools like him, it would not have allayed his uneasiness.
uz: Garchi u barcha progressivlar ham o'zi kabi axmoqlar ekanligiga amin bo'lsa ham, bu uning xavotirini kamaytirmagan bo'lardi.

en: All the doctrines, the ideas, the systems, with which Andrey Semyonovitch pestered him had no interest for him.
uz: Andrey Semyonovitch uni haqorat qilgan barcha ta'limotlar, g'oyalar va tizimlar u uchun qiziqish ko'rsatmadi.

en: He had his own object —he simply wanted to find out at once what was happening here.
uz: Uning o'z ob'ekti bor edi, u shunchaki bu yerda nima sodir bo'layotganini darhol bilmoqchi edi.

en: Had these people any power or not?
uz: Ushbu odamlar biron bir kuchga ega bo'lishadimi yoki yo'qmi?

en: Had he anything to fear from them?
uz: Ulardan qo'rqishi kerak bo'lgan biron narsa bormi?

en: Would they expose any enterprise of his?
uz: Ular uning biron bir ishini fosh etadimi?

en: And what precisely was now the object of their attacks?
uz: Va ularning hujumlari nimaga qaratilgan edi?

en: Could he somehow make up to them and get round them if they really were powerful?
uz: Agar ular chindan ham kuchli bo'lganida, u ularni qandaydir tarzda qo'llab-quvvatlay olishi mumkinmi?

en: Was this the thing to do or not?
uz: Bu ishni qilish kerakmi yoki yo'qmi?

en: Couldn’t he gain something through them?
uz: Ular orqali u biror narsa topolmaydimi?

en: In fact hundreds of questions presented themselves.
uz: Aslida yuzlab savollar paydo bo'ldi.

en: Andrey Semyonovitch was an anæmic, scrofulous little man, with strangely flaxen mutton-chop whiskers of which he was very proud.
uz: Andrey Semyonovitch anemiy, ko'ngilsiz va g'alati bo'lgan kichkinagina odam edi, u juda faxrlanadigan g'alati, chiroyli qo'zi cho'g'i bo'laklari bilan.

en: He was a clerk and had almost always something wrong with his eyes.
uz: U ishchi bo'lgan va deyarli har doim ko'zlarida biron bir muammo bor edi.

en: He was rather softhearted, but self-confident and sometimes extremely conceited in speech, which had an absurd effect, incongruous with his little figure.
uz: U o'z yuragini yumshatgan, ammo o'ziga ishonadigan va ba'zan o'ta mag'rur bo'lgan so'zlarni gapirgan edi, bu esa absurd ta'sir ko'rsatgan va uning kichkina figurasidan farq qilardi.

en: He was one of the lodgers most respected by Amalia Ivanovna, for he did not get drunk and paid regularly for his lodgings.
uz: U Amaliya Ivanovna tomonidan eng hurmatli ijaraga oluvchilardan biri edi, chunki u mast bo'lmagan va o'z uylari uchun muntazam ravishda pul to'lagan.

en: Andrey Semyonovitch really was rather stupid; he attached himself to the cause of progress and “our younger generation” from enthusiasm.
uz: Andrey Semyonovitch haqiqatan ham ahmoqona edi; u o'zini taraqqiyot va yosh avlodimizning ishiga g'ayrat bilan bog'ladi.

en: He was one of the numerous and varied legion of dullards, of half-animate abortions, conceited, half-educated coxcombs, who attach themselves to the idea most in fashion only to vulgarise it and who caricature every cause they serve, however sincerely.
uz: U ko'plab va turli xil bo'lgan, yarim jonli abortlar, mag'rur, yarim o'qilgan ko'kraklar qo'shinidan biri edi, ular faqatgina uni vulgarlashtirish uchun fikrga juda mo'ljallangan va ular xizmat qiladigan har bir sababni karikatura qiladilar, ammo chin dildan.

en: Though Lebeziatnikov was so good-natured, he, too, was beginning to dislike Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Lebeziatnikov juda mehribon bo'lsa-da, u ham Pyotr Petrovitchdan nafratlanishni boshlagan.

en: This happened on both sides unconsciously.
uz: Bu ikkala tomon ham bexabar sodir bo'ldi.

en: However simple Andrey Semyonovitch might be, he began to see that Pyotr Petrovitch was duping him and secretly despising him, and that “he was not the right sort of man.” He had tried expounding to him the system of Fourier and the Darwinian theory, but of late Pyotr Petrovitch began to listen too sarcastically
uz: Andrey Semyonovitch qanchalik oddiy bo'lmasin, u Pyotr Petrovitch uni aldashini va yashirincha undan nafratlanishini va u to'g'ri odam emasligini anglay boshladi. U Fourier tizimi va Darvin nazariyasini unga tushuntirishga harakat qilgan edi, ammo oxirgi paytlarda Pyotr Petrovitch juda sarkastika bilan tinglay boshladi

en: and even to be rude.
uz: va hatto nojo'ya bo'lish uchun ham.

en: The fact was he had begun instinctively to guess that Lebeziatnikov was not merely a commonplace simpleton, but, perhaps, a liar, too, and that he had no connections of any consequence even in his own circle, but had simply picked things up third-hand; and that very likely he did not even know much about his own work of propaganda, for he was in too great a muddle.
uz: Darhaqiqat, u instinktli ravishda Lebeziatnikov oddiy oddiy odam emas, balki yolg'onchi ham bo'lganini va hatto o'z atrofida ham hech qanday ahamiyatga ega bo'lmagan aloqalarga ega bo'lmaganini, balki o'z ishlarini uchinchi qo'ldan o'tkazganini taxmin qilishni boshlaganini va ehtimol u o'z targ'ibot ishi haqida ham ko'p bilmaganini, chunki u juda katta chalkashlikda edi.

en: A fine person he would be to show anyone up!
uz: Kimni-kimga ko'rsatadigan yaxshi odam bo'ladi!

en: It must be noted, by the way, that Pyotr Petrovitch had during those ten days eagerly accepted the strangest praise from Andrey Semyonovitch; he had not protested, for instance, when Andrey Semyonovitch belauded him for being ready to contribute to the establishment of the new “commune,” or to abstain from christening his future children, or to acquiesce if Dounia were to take a lover a month after marriage, and so on.
uz: Aytish joizki, Pyotr Petrovitch o'n kun davomida Andrey Semyonovitchning eng g'alati maqtovlarini xohish bilan qabul qilgan; masalan, Andrey Semyonovitch uni yangi commune tashkil etishga hissa qo'shishga tayyorligi, kelajakdagi farzandlarini suvga cho'mdirishdan voz kechish, Dounia nikohdan bir oy o'tgach sevgini olib ketishi mumkin bo'lganda rozi bo'lish uchun tanqid qilmagan.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch so enjoyed hearing his own praises that he did not disdain even such virtues when they were attributed to him.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch o'z maqomlarini eshitishdan shunchalik zavqlanardiki, hatto bunday fazilatlar unga mansub bo'lganida ham, ularni kamsitmadi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch had had occasion that morning to realise some five-percent bonds and now he sat down to the table and counted over bundles of notes.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch o'sha kuni ertalab besh foizlik obligatsiyalarni sotishga imkoniyat yaratgan edi va endi stolga o'tirib, notlar to'plamini sanab o'tdi.

en: Andrey Semyonovitch who hardly ever had any money walked about the room pretending to himself to look at all those bank notes with indifference and even contempt.
uz: Kamdan-kam pulga ega bo'lgan Andrey Semyonovitch o'ziga ko'z tikib, bu banknotlarga beparvolik va hatto kamsitish bilan qarayotgandek o'zini ko'rsatdi.

en: Nothing would have convinced Pyotr Petrovitch that Andrey Semyonovitch could really look on the money unmoved, and the latter, on his side, kept thinking bitterly that Pyotr Petrovitch was capable of entertaining such an idea about him and was, perhaps, glad of the opportunity of teasing his young friend by reminding him of his inferiority and the great difference between them.
uz: Hech narsa Pyotr Petrovitchni Andrey Semyonovich pulga o'zgarmas qarab turishi mumkinligiga ishontirmagan bo'lardi va Pyotr Petrovitch o'zi haqida bunday fikr yuritishi mumkinligini va ehtimol uning kamchiligi va ularning orasidagi katta farq haqida eslatish orqali yosh do'stini haqoratlash imkoniyatiga ega bo'lganidan xursand edi.

en: He found him incredibly inattentive and irritable, though he, Andrey Semyonovitch, began enlarging on his favourite subject, the foundation of a new special “commune.” The brief remarks that dropped from Pyotr Petrovitch between the clicking of the beads on the reckoning frame betrayed unmistakable and discourteous irony.
uz: U uni juda befarq va g'azablanarli deb topdi, ammo Andrey Semyonovich o'zining sevimli mavzusini, yangi maxsus commune asosini kengaytirishni boshladi. Pyotr Petrovitchning hisob-kitob ramkasidagi marvaridlarning bosilishi orasidagi qisqa izohlari aniq va beparvo ironiyani namoyish etdi.

en: But the “humane” Andrey Semyonovitch ascribed Pyotr Petrovitch’s ill-humour to his recent breach with Dounia and he was burning with impatience to discourse on that theme.
uz: Ammo insonparvar Andrey Semyonovich Pyotr Petrovitchning yomon humorini Dounia bilan yaqinda bo'lgan bo'shlig'iga bog'ladi va u bu mavzuda nutq so'zlash uchun sabrsizlik bilan yonayotgan edi.

en: He had something progressive to say on the subject which might console his worthy friend and “could not fail” to promote his development.
uz: U bu mavzuda o'zining munosib do'stiga tasalli beradigan va rivojlanishiga ko'maklashadigan ilg'orlik bilan gapiradigan bir narsa bor edi.

en: “There is some sort of festivity being prepared at that … at the widow’s, isn’t there?” Pyotr Petrovitch asked suddenly, interrupting Andrey Semyonovitch at the most interesting passage.
uz: O'sha bevalar uyida qandaydir bayram tayyorlanmoqda, shunday emasmi? Pyotr Petrovitch to'satdan so'radi va Andrey Semyonovitchni eng qiziqarli o'tish joyida to'xtatdi.

en: “Why, don’t you know?
uz: Nima uchun, bilmayapsanmi?

en: Why, I was telling you last night what I think about all such ceremonies.
uz: Kecha men sizga bunday marosimlar haqida o'ylayotganimni aytib berardim.

en: And she invited you too, I heard.
uz: Men eshitganimcha, u sizni ham taklif qildi.

en: You were talking to her yesterday …” “I should never have expected that beggarly fool would have spent on this feast all the money she got from that other fool, Raskolnikov.
uz: Kecha siz u bilan gaplashgandirsiz ... Men hech qachon o'ylamagan edimki, o'sha begona o'g'lim o'sha o'g'lim Raskolnikovdan olgan pulni bu ziyofatga sarflaydi.

en: I was surprised just now as I came through at the preparations there, the wines!
uz: Men o'sha yerda tayyorgarlik ko'rishni boshlaganimda, sharoblarni ko'rib hayron qoldim!

en: Several people are invited.
uz: Bir nechta odam taklif etiladi.

en: It’s beyond everything!” continued Pyotr Petrovitch, who seemed to have some object in pursuing the conversation.
uz: Bu hamma narsadan ustundir! - deb davom etdi Pyotr Petrovitch, suhbatni davom ettirishda biron bir muammoga ega bo'lgan ko'rinardi.

en: You say I am asked too?
uz: Menga ham so'raganini aytasizmi?

en: I only said a word to her in passing yesterday of the possibility of her obtaining a year’s salary as a destitute widow of a government clerk.
uz: Kecha o'tib ketayotganimda, men unga faqatgina bir so'z aytdim, chunki u davlat ishchisi beva ayol sifatida bir yillik ish haqiga ega bo'lishi mumkin.

en: I suppose she has invited me on that account, hasn’t she?
uz: O'ylaymanki, u meni shu maqsadda taklif qildi, shunday emasmi?

en: He-he- he!” “I don’t intend to go either,” said Lebeziatnikov.
uz: "Men ham bormoqchi emasman", dedi Lebeziatnikov.

en: “I should think not, after giving her a thrashing!
uz: Men unga to'qnashgandan keyin, bunday deb o'ylamasligim kerak!

en: You might well hesitate, he-he!” “Who thrashed?
uz: Siz shubha ostiga qo'yishingiz mumkin, xolos!  Kim urib yubordi?

en: Whom?” cried Lebeziatnikov, flustered and blushing.
uz: Lebeziatnikovni ko'targan va qizg'inlab ketgan.

en: “Why, you thrashed Katerina Ivanovna a month ago.
uz: Nima uchun, siz bir oy oldin Katerina Ivanovnani o'ldirgansiz.

en: I heard so yesterday … so that’s what your convictions amount to … and the woman question, too, wasn’t quite sound, he-he-he!” and Pyotr Petrovitch, as though comforted, went back to clicking his beads.
uz: Kecha men buni eshitgan edim ... shuning uchun sizning e'tiqodlaringiz shunga teng ... va ayolning so'rovi ham juda sog'lom emas edi, u-u-u! va Pyotr Petrovitch, tasalli topganidek, o'z ko'kraklarini bosishga qaytdi.

en: “It’s all slander and nonsense!” cried Lebeziatnikov, who was always afraid of allusions to the subject.
uz: Bularning barchasi tuhmat va axloqsizlikdir! - deb baqirdi Lebeziatnikov, u har doim mavzuga ishora qilishdan qo'rqardi.

en: “It was not like that at all, it was quite different.
uz: Bu umuman shunday emas edi, u umuman boshqacha edi.

en: You’ve heard it wrong; it’s a libel.
uz: Siz buni noto'g'ri eshitgansiz; bu tuhmat.

en: I was simply defending myself.
uz: Men shunchaki o'zimni himoya qilardim.

en: She rushed at me first with her nails, she pulled out all my whiskers.
uz: U birinchi bo'lib o'z to'g'rilari bilan menga shovqin qildi, barcha mustaklarimni chiqarib oldi.

en: … It’s permissable for anyone, I should hope, to defend himself and I never allow anyone to use violence to me on principle, for it’s an act of despotism.
uz: Umid qilamanki, har kim o'zini himoya qilishi mumkin va men hech qachon hech kimga menga nisbatan zo'ravonlik qilishga yo'l qo'ymayman, chunki bu despotizm amalidir.

en: I simply pushed her back.” “He-he-he!” Luzhin went on laughing maliciously.
uz: Men shunchaki uni orqaga surdim. He-he-he! Luzhin yomon ko'rinishda kulgan.

en: “You keep on like that because you are out of humour yourself.
uz: Siz o'zingizni shunday saqlaysiz, chunki siz o'zingiz ham humordan mahrum bo'lgansiz.

en: … But that’s nonsense and it has nothing, nothing whatever to do with
uz: Ammo bu g'alati gap va u bilan hech qanday aloqasi yo'q.

en: You don’t understand; I used to think, indeed, that if women are equal to men in all respects, even in strength (as is maintained now) there ought to be equality in that, too.
uz: Siz buni tushunmaysiz; men, albatta, agar xotin-qizlar har jihatdan erkaklar bilan teng bo'lsa, hatto kuch-quvvatda ham (hozirgicha) tenglik bo'lishi kerak, deb o'yladim.

en: Of course, I reflected afterwards that such a question ought not really to arise, for there ought not to be fighting and in the future society fighting is unthinkable … and that it would be a queer thing to seek for equality in fighting.
uz: Albatta, keyinchalik shunday savol tug'ilmasligi kerak, chunki urush bo'lmasligi kerak va kelajakda jamiyatda urush o'ylanarli emas ... va urushda tenglikni izlash g'alati ish bo'lishini o'yladim.

en: I am not so stupid … though, of course, there is fighting … there won’t be later, but at present there is … confound it!
uz: Men shunchalik ahmoq emasman... ammo, albatta, urushlar bor... keyinroq bo'lmaydi, lekin hozirda... uni chalg'itish bor!

en: How muddled one gets with you!
uz: Siz bilan odam qanchalik chalg'ib ketganini ko'ring!

en: It’s not on that account that I am not going.
uz: Men bormasligimning sababi shu emas.

en: I am not going on principle, not to take part in the revolting convention of memorial dinners, that’s why!
uz: Men prinsip bo'yicha, memorial kechki ovqatlarining g'alati konvensiyasida ishtirok etmaslikka harakat qilmayman, shuning uchun ham!

en: Though, of course, one might go to laugh at it.
uz: Garchi, albatta, bu haqda kulish mumkin bo'lsa-da.

en: … I am sorry there won’t be any priests at it.
uz: Men afsuski, bu yerda ruhoniylar bo'lmaydi.

en: I should certainly go if there were.” “Then you would sit down at another man’s table and insult it and those who invited you.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, albatta men borardim. Keyin siz boshqa odamning dasturxonida o'tirib, uni va sizni taklif qilganlarni haqorat qilasiz.

en: Eh?” “Certainly not insult, but protest.
uz: Eh?  Albatta haqorat emas, balki protest.

en: I should do it with a good object.
uz: Men buni yaxshi ob'ekt bilan qilishim kerak.

en: I might indirectly assist the cause of enlightenment and propaganda.
uz: Ehtimol, men bevosita ma'rifat va targ'ibot ishiga yordam beraman.

en: It’s a duty of every man to work for enlightenment and propaganda and the more harshly, perhaps, the better.
uz: Har bir odamning vazifasi - ma'rifat va targ'ibot uchun ishlash va qanchalik qattiqroq, ehtimol, shunchalik yaxshi bo'lishi kerak.

en: I might drop a seed, an idea.
uz: Men urug'ni, g'oyani tashlab ketishim mumkin.

en: … And something might grow up from that seed.
uz: Va bu urug'dan biror narsa o'sib chiqishi mumkin.

en: How should I be insulting them?
uz: Qanday qilib ularni haqoratlashim kerak?

en: They might be offended at first, but afterwards they’d see I’d done them a service.
uz: Ular boshida xafa bo'lishlari mumkin, lekin keyinchalik men ularga yaxshilik qilganimni ko'rishadi.

en: You know, Terebyeva (who is in the community now) was blamed because when she left her family and … devoted … herself, she wrote to her father and mother that she wouldn’t go on living conventionally and was entering on a free marriage and it was said that that was too harsh, that she might have spared them and have written more kindly.
uz: Bilasizmi, Terebyeva (hozir jamiyatda) ayblandi, chunki u oilasini tashlab ketgach va o'zini ... bag'ishlaganida, ota-onasiga o'zining an'asiga yozgan ediki, u an'anaviy hayot kechirmay, erkin nikohga kiradi va bu juda og'ir bo'lgan, ehtimol ularni qutqargan bo'lishi mumkin edi va ko'proq mehribonlik bilan yozgan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: I think that’s all nonsense and there’s no need of softness; on the contrary, what’s wanted is protest.
uz: Men o'ylaymanki, bularning hammasi behuda va yumshatishning hojati yo'q; aksincha, ular protest qilishni xohlashadi.

en: Varents had been married seven years, she abandoned her two children, she told her husband straight out in a letter: ‘I have realised that I cannot be happy with you.
uz: Varents yetti yildan beri turmush qurgan, ikkita farzandini tashlab ketgan va eriga xat orqali aniq gapirib: "Men siz bilan baxtli bo'lishim mumkin emasligini angladim.

en: I can never forgive you that you have deceived me by concealing from me that there is another organisation of society by means of the communities.
uz: Siz meni aldashingiz va jamiyatning boshqa tashkilotining jamiyatlar orqali mavjudligini mendan yashirishingiz uchun hech qachon kechira olmayman.

en: I have only lately learned it from a greathearted man to whom I have given myself and with whom I am establishing a community.
uz: O'zimni unga bag'ishlagan va jamoa qurayotgan katta yurakli odamdan buni yaqinda o'rgandim.

en: I speak plainly because I consider it dishonest to deceive you.
uz: Men aniq gapiryapman, chunki sizlarni aldashni halokatli deb bilaman.

en: Do as you think best.
uz: Yaxshi deb o'ylaganicha qiling.

en: Do not hope to get me back, you are too late.
uz: Meni qaytarib olishni umid qilmang, siz juda kech qoldingiz.

en: I hope you will be happy.’ That’s how letters like that ought to be written!” “Is that Terebyeva the one you said had made a third free marriage?” “No, it’s only the second, really!
uz: Umid qilamanki, siz baxtli bo'lasiz. Bunday xatlar shunday yozilishi kerak!Siz aytganidek, Terebyeva uchinchi marta turmush qurganmi?Yo'q, bu faqat ikkinchisi!

en: But what if it were the fourth, what if it were the fifteenth, that’s all nonsense!
uz: Ammo to'rtinchi, o'n beshinchi bo'lsa-chi, bularning barchasi behudalikdir!

en: And if ever I regretted the death of my father and mother, it is now, and I sometimes think if my parents were living what a protest I would have aimed at them!
uz: Ota-onam va onamning o'limidan afsuslansam, hozir bo'ladi va ba'zan ota-onam hayotda bo'lganida, men ularga qarshi qanday norozilik ko'rsatgan bo'lardim, deb o'ylayman!

en: I would have done something on purpose … I would have shown them!
uz: Men bilgan holda biror narsa qilgan bo'lardim... ularga ko'rsatgan bo'lardim!

en: I would have astonished them!
uz: Men ularni hayratda qoldirgan bo'lardim!

en: I am really sorry there is no one!” “To surprise!
uz: Haqiqatan ham, hech kim bo'lmaganidan afsusdaman!Sorpresa uchun!

en: Well, be that as you will,” Pyotr Petrovitch interrupted, “but tell me this; do you know the dead man’s daughter, the delicate-looking little thing?
uz: Xo'sh, siz xohlaganidek bo'lsin, - dedi Pyotr Petrovitch, - lekin menga bir narsani ayting; siz o'lgan odamning qizi, nozik ko'rinadigan kichkina narsani bilasizmi?

en: It’s true what they say about her, isn’t it?” “What of it?
uz: U haqida nima deyilganligi to'g'ri, shunday emasmi?

en: I think, that is, it is my own personal conviction that this is the normal condition of women.
uz: O'ylaymanki, bu mening shaxsiy e'tiqodimdirki, bu ayollarning normal holatidir.

en: I mean, distinguons.
uz: Ya'ni, dististons.

en: In our present society it is not altogether normal, because it is compulsory, but in the future society it will be perfectly normal, because it will be voluntary.
uz: Hozirgi jamiyatimizda bu mutlaqo normal emas, chunki bu majburiy, ammo kelajakda bu mutlaqo normal bo'ladi, chunki bu ixtiyoriy bo'ladi.

en: Even as it is, she was quite right: she was suffering and that was her asset, so to speak, her capital which she had a perfect right to dispose of.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, u to'g'ri yo'l tutgan: u azob chekayotgan edi va bu uning boyligi edi, shunday qilib aytish kerak, uning kapitali edi, undan foydalanish huquqiga ega edi.

en: Of course, in the future society there will be no need of assets, but her part will have another significance, rational and in harmony with her environment.
uz: Albatta, kelajakda jamiyatda boyliklarga ehtiyoj yo'q bo'ladi, ammo uning o'rni boshqa ahamiyatga ega bo'ladi, bu oqilona va atrof-muhitga uyg'un bo'ladi.

en: As to Sofya Semyonovna personally, I regard her action as a vigorous protest against the organisation of society, and I respect her deeply for it; I rejoice indeed when I look at her!” “I was told that you got her turned out of these lodgings.” Lebeziatnikov was enraged.
uz: Shaxsan Sofiya Semyonovnaga kelsak, uning harakatini jamiyat tashkilotlariga qarshi kuchli protest deb bilaman va bu uchun uni chuqur hurmat qilaman; men unga qaraganimda juda xursandman!Menga bu uylardan chiqarganingiz haqida aytildi. Lebeziatnikov g'azabga to'ldi.

en: “That’s another slander,” he yelled.
uz: Bu yana bir tuhmat, - deb baqirdi u.

en: “It was not so at all!
uz: Bu umuman shunday bo'lmagan!

en: That was all Katerina Ivanovna’s invention, for she did not understand!
uz: Bu Katerina Ivanovna tomonidan yaratilgan narsa edi, chunki u buni tushunmagan edi!

en: And I never made love to Sofya Semyonovna!
uz: Va men Sofiya Semyonovna bilan hech qachon sevib ko'rmadim!

en: I was simply developing her, entirely disinterestedly, trying to rouse her to protest.
uz: Men shunchaki uni o'z manfaatini ko'zlamasdan rivojlantirib, uni protest qilishga undashga harakat qilardim.

en: … All I wanted was her protest and Sofya Semyonovna could not have remained here anyway!” “Have you asked her to join your community?”
uz: ... Men faqat uning noroziligini xohladim va Sofiya Semyonovna ham bu yerda qolishi mumkin emas edi!Sizdan uning jamoangizga qo'shilishini so'raganmisiz?

en: “You keep on laughing and very inappropriately, allow me to tell you.
uz: Siz ko'proq kulishni davom ettirasiz va juda munosib emas, sizga aytaman.

en: You don’t understand!
uz: Siz tushunmayapsiz!

en: There is no such role in a community.
uz: Jamiyatda bunday o'rin yo'q.

en: The community is established that there should be no such roles.
uz: Jamoat bunday rollar bo'lmasligi kerak deb o'rnatilgan.

en: In a community, such a role is essentially transformed and what is stupid here is sensible there, what, under present conditions, is unnatural becomes perfectly natural in the community.
uz: Jamiyatda bunday rol aslida o'zgarib, bu erda ahmoqlik bo'lgan narsa o'sha yerda sezgilidir, hozirgi sharoitlarda tabiiy emas bo'lgan narsa jamiyatda mutlaqo tabiiy bo'ladi.

en: It all depends on the environment.
uz: Hammasi atrof-muhitga bog'liq.

en: It’s all the environment and man himself is nothing.
uz: Bu hamma atrof-muhit va insonning o'zi hech narsa emas.

en: And I am on good terms with Sofya Semyonovna to this day, which is a proof that she never regarded me as having wronged her.
uz: Sofiya Semyonovna bilan hali ham yaxshi munosabatda bo'ldim, bu esa uni hech qachon o'ziga zulm qilganim haqida o'ylamaganligini isbotlaydi.

en: I am trying now to attract her to the community, but on quite, quite a different footing.
uz: Hozir uni jamiyatga jalb qilishga harakat qilyapman, lekin bu o'zgacha asosda.

en: What are you laughing at?
uz: Nega kulyapsan?

en: We are trying to establish a community of our own, a special one, on a broader basis.
uz: Biz o'z jamoamizni, o'zgacha jamoani, kengroq asosda barpo etishga harakat qilyapmiz.

en: We have gone further in our convictions.
uz: Biz o'z e'tiqodlarimizda yanada uzoqroq bordik.

en: And meanwhile I’m still developing Sofya Semyonovna.
uz: Va shu bilan birga men Sofiya Semyonovna-ni hali ham ishlab chiqyapman.

en: She has a beautiful, beautiful character!” “And you take advantage of her fine character, eh?
uz: Uning chiroyli, chiroyli xarakterlari bor! Va siz uning chiroyli xarakteridan foydalanasiz, ha?

en: On the contrary.” “Oh, on the contrary!
uz: Aksincha.Oh, aksincha!

en: A queer thing to say!” “Believe me!
uz: Aytish uchun o'ta g'alati narsa!   Menga ishoning!

en: Why should I disguise it?
uz: Nima uchun uni yashirsam bo'ladi?

en: In fact, I feel it strange myself how timid, chaste and modern she is with me!” “And you, of course, are developing her … he-he!
uz: Darhaqiqat, men o'zim ham uning men bilan qanchalik qo'rqinchli, sof va zamonaviy bo'lishiga g'alati his qilaman! Va siz, albatta, uni rivojlantiryapsiz... u-u!

en: trying to prove to her that all that modesty is nonsense?” “Not at all, not at all!
uz: O'sha kamtarinlik behuda ekanligini unga isbotlashga harakat qilyapsizmi? Hech qachon, hech qachon!

en: How coarsely, how stupidly —excuse me saying so —you misunderstand the word development!
uz: Qanday qo'pol, qanday ahmoqlik bilan so'zlashimga uzr bering, siz rivojlanish so'zini noto'g'ri tushunasiz!

en: Good heavens, how … crude you still are!
uz: Yaxshi osmonlar, siz hali ham qanday hamilsiz!

en: We are striving for the freedom of women and you have only one idea in your head.
uz: Biz xotin-qizlarning erkinligi uchun kurashmoqdamiz va sizda faqat bitta g'oya bor.

en: … Setting aside the general question of chastity and feminine modesty as useless in themselves and indeed prejudices, I fully accept her chastity with me, because that’s for her to decide.
uz: O'z-o'zidan foydasiz va o'ziga xos tanqidlar kabi xudojo'ylik va ayollarning kamtarligi haqidagi umumiy savolni chetga qoldirgan holda, men uning xudojo'ligini men bilan birga to'liq qabul qilaman, chunki bu o'zi qaror qabul qilishi kerak.

en: Of course if she were to tell me herself that she wanted me, I should think myself very lucky, because I like the girl very much; but as it is, no one has ever treated her more courteously than I, with more respect for her dignity … I wait in hopes, that’s all!” “You had much better make her a present of something.
uz: Albatta, agar u menga o'zi xohlayotganini aytsa, men o'zimni juda baxtli deb hisoblayman, chunki men qizni juda yaxshi ko'raman; lekin hozirgi paytda hech kim unga mendan ko'ra xushmuomalaroq munosabatda bo'lmagan, uning qadr-qimmatiga hurmat ko'rsatgan... Umid bilan kutyapman, shu qadar! Siz unga biron narsa sovg'asini berishingiz kerak edi.

en: I bet you never thought of that.” “You don’t understand, as I’ve told you already!
uz: Ishonchim komilki, siz bu haqda hech qachon o'ylamagansiz.Siz buni tushunmayapsiz, chunki men sizga allaqachon aytgan edim!

en: Of course, she is in such a position, but it’s another question.
uz: Albatta, u bunday holatda, lekin bu boshqa savol.

en: Quite another question!
uz: Bu boshqa savol!

en: You simply despise her.
uz: Siz shunchaki uni kamsitasiz.

en: Seeing a fact which you mistakenly consider deserving of contempt, you refuse to take a humane view of a fellow creature.
uz: Siz noto'g'ri tanqid qilishga loyiq deb hisoblaydigan faktni ko'rib, bir jonzangizga insoniy nuqtai nazar bilan qarashdan bosh tortasiz.

en: You don’t know what a character she is!
uz: U qanday xarakterli ekanligini bilmaysiz!

en: I am only sorry that of late she has quite given up reading and borrowing books.
uz: Faqatgina kechki paytlarda u kitob o'qish va qarz olishdan voz kechgani uchun afsuslanaman.

en: I used to lend them to her.
uz: Men ularni unga qarz berardim.

en: I am sorry, too, that with all the energy and resolution in protesting —which she has already shown once —she has little self-reliance, little, so to say, independence, so as to break free from certain prejudices and certain foolish ideas.
uz: Men ham afsuslanamanki, u bir marta ko'rsatgan protest qilishda ko'p kuch va qat'iy qarorga ega bo'lsa-da, ba'zi bir oldindan ko'ringan fikrlardan va ahmoqona fikrlardan xalos bo'lish uchun o'z-o'zidan kamroq mustaqillikka ega.

en: Yet she thoroughly understands some questions, for instance about kissing of hands, that is, that it’s an insult to a woman for a man to kiss her hand, because it’s a sign of inequality.
uz: Ammo u ba'zi savollarni yaxshi tushunadi, masalan, qo'llarni o'pish haqida, ya'ni erkak kishi qo'lini o'psa, ayolga haqorat bo'lishi mumkin, chunki bu tengsizlik belgisi.

en: We had a debate about it and I described it to her.
uz: Biz bu haqda bahslashib oldik va men uni unga tushuntirdim.

en: She listened attentively to an account of the workmen’s associations in France, too.
uz: U Fransiyadagi ishchilar uyushmalarining hisobotlarini ham diqqat bilan tingladi.

en: Now I am explaining the question of coming into the room in the future society.” “And what’s that, pray?” “We had a debate lately on the question: Has a member of the community the right to enter another member’s room, whether man or woman, at any time … and we decided that he has!” “It might be at an inconvenient moment, he-he!” Lebeziatnikov was really angry.
uz: Endi men kelajakdagi jamiyatda xonada bo'lish masalasini tushuntirib beryapman. Va bu nima, ibodat qiling? Biz so'nggi paytlarda bu savol haqida munozara o'tkazdik: jamoa a'zosi boshqa a'zolarning xonasiga, erkakmi yoki ayolmi, istalgan vaqtda kirishga haqlimi... va biz bunga qaror qildik! Bu noqulay paytda bo'lishi mumkin, u-u! Lebeziatnikov juda g'azab edi.

en: “You are always thinking of something unpleasant,” he cried with aversion.
uz: "Siz har doim yoqimsiz narsani o'ylaysiz", - dedi u nafratdan yig'lab.

en: How vexed I am that when I was expounding our system, I referred prematurely to the question of personal privacy!
uz: Bizning tizimimizni tushuntirayotib, shaxsiy hayotimiz masalasiga ertalab murojaat qilganimdan juda xafa bo'ldim!

en: It’s always a stumbling-block to people like you, they turn it into ridicule before they understand it.
uz: Siz kabi odamlar uchun bu har doim to'siq bo'lib qoladi, ular buni tushunishdan oldin masxara qilishadi.

en: And how proud they are of it, too!
uz: Va ular bundan ham g'ururlanmoqdalar!

en: I’ve often maintained that that question should not be approached by a novice till he has a firm faith in the system.
uz: Men ko'pincha ushbu savolga yangi boshlanuvchi tizimga qattiq ishonmaguncha murojaat qilmasligi kerakligini ta'kidlaganman.

en: And tell me, please, what do you find so shameful even in cesspools?
uz: Va menga ayting-chi, nima sizda bu qadar sharmanda, hatto o'simlik quduqlarida ham?

en: I should be the first to be ready to clean out any cesspool you like.
uz: Men siz xohlagan har qanday o'simlikni tozalashga tayyor bo'lgan birinchi bo'lishim kerak.

en: And it’s not a question of self-sacrifice, it’s simply work, honourable, useful work which is as good as any other and much better than the work of a Raphael and a Pushkin, because it is more useful.” “And more honourable, more honourable, he-he-he!” “What do you mean by ‘more honourable’?
uz: Va bu o'z-o'zidan voz kechish emas, balki shunchaki mehnat, sharafli, foydali ish, u har qanday boshqa ish kabi yaxshi va Rafail va Pushkinning ishidan ancha yaxshiroqdir, chunki u ko'proq foydali.Va ko'proq hurmatli, ko'proq hurmatli, u-u-u!Siz "ko'proq hurmatli" deb nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?

en: I don’t understand such expressions to describe human activity.
uz: Inson faoliyatini tasvirlash uchun bunday iboralarni tushunmayman.

en: ‘More honourable,’ ‘nobler’ —all those are old-fashioned prejudices which I reject.
uz: Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar, Arabistlar,

en: Everything which is of use to mankind is honourable.
uz: Insoniyat uchun foydali bo'lgan hamma narsa hurmatga sazovor.

en: understand one word: useful!
uz: bitta so'zni tushuning: foydali!

en: You can snigger as much as you like, but that’s so!” Pyotr Petrovitch laughed heartily.
uz: O'zingiz xohlagancha qichqirishingiz mumkin, lekin bu shunday! Pyotr Petrovitch ko'ngli bilan kuldi.

en: He had finished counting the money and was putting it away.
uz: U pulni sanashni tugatdi va uni qo'yib qo'ydi.

en: But some of the notes he left on the table.
uz: Ammo u bir nechta yozuvlarni stol ustida qoldirdi.

en: The “cesspool question” had already been a subject of dispute between them.
uz: cesspool masalasi ular o'rtasida allaqachon bahs-munozara bo'lgan.

en: What was absurd was that it made Lebeziatnikov really angry, while it amused Luzhin and at that moment he particularly wanted to anger his young friend.
uz: Ajablanarlisi shundaki, bu Lebeziatnikovni chindan ham g'azabga solib, Lushinni zavqlantirgan va ayniqsa o'sha paytda u o'zining yosh do'stiga g'azablantirmoqchi edi.

en: “It’s your ill-luck yesterday that makes you so ill-humoured and annoying,” blurted out Lebeziatnikov, who in spite of his “independence” and his “protests” did not venture to oppose Pyotr Petrovitch and still behaved to him with some of the respect habitual in earlier years.
uz: Kecha sizning yomon omadingiz sizni shunchalik g'azablantirgan va g'azablantirgan, deb aytdi Lebeziatnikov, o'z mustaqilligi va noroziliklariga qaramay, Pyotr Petrovitchga qarshi chiqishga jur'at etmagan va hali ham unga avvalgi yillarda odatdagi hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'lgan.

en: “You’d better tell me this,” Pyotr Petrovitch interrupted with haughty displeasure, “can you … or rather are you really friendly enough with that young person to ask her to step in here for a minute?
uz: Siz menga buni aytishingiz kerak, - dedi Pyotr Petroviç mag'rurlik bilan to'xtatib, - siz qila olasizmi ... yoki, aslida, siz o'sha yosh odam bilan shunchalik do'stsizki, undan bir daqiqaga kirib kelishini so'rashingiz mumkinmi?

en: I think they’ve all come back from the cemetery … I heard the sound of steps … I want to see her, that young person.” “What for?” Lebeziatnikov asked with surprise.
uz: O'ylaymanki, ular hammasi qabristondan qaytib kelishdi... Men qadamlarning ovozini eshitdim... Men uni ko'rmoqchiman, o'sha yosh kishini. Nima uchun? Lebeziatnikov hayronlik bilan so'radi.

en: I am leaving here today or tomorrow and therefore I wanted to speak to her about … However, you may be present during the interview.
uz: Men bugun yoki ertaga bu yerdan ketyapman va shuning uchun men u bilan suhbatlashishni xohladim ... Biroq, siz intervyu davomida hozir bo'lishingiz mumkin.

en: It’s better you should be, indeed.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bo'lishingiz kerak.

en: For there’s no knowing what you might imagine.” “I shan’t imagine anything.
uz: Chunki siz tasavvur qila oladigan narsani bilishning iloji yo'q.

en: I only asked and, if you’ve anything to say to her, nothing is easier than to call her in.
uz: Men faqat so'radim va agar unga aytadigan biron narsaingiz bo'lsa, uni chaqirishdan osonroq narsa yo'q.

en: I’ll go directly and you may be sure I won’t be in your way.” Five minutes later Lebeziatnikov came in with Sonia.
uz: Men to'g'ridan-to'g'ri boraman va siz mening sizning yo'lingizda bo'lmasligimga amin bo'lishingiz mumkin.Besh daqiqa o'tgach, Lebeziatnikov Sonia bilan kirib keldi.

en: She came in very much surprised and overcome with shyness as usual.
uz: U o'zining odatdagidek juda hayratda va o'z xudojo'yligini yengib keldi.
