en: She was always shy in such circumstances and was always afraid of new people, she had been as a child and was even more so now.
uz: Bunday sharoitlarda u doim uyalgan va yangi odamlardan qo'rqqan, u bolaligidanoq shunday edi va hozir bundan ham ko'proq.

en: … Pyotr Petrovitch met her “politely and affably,” but with a certain shade of bantering familiarity which in his opinion was suitable for a man of his respectability and weight in dealing with a creature so young and so interesting as she.
uz: ...Pyotr Petrovitch uni o'zini yaxshi va mehribon ko'rishdi, lekin uning fikriga ko'ra, u kabi yosh va qiziqarli mavjudot bilan muomala qilishda o'zining hurmat va ahamiyatiga ega bo'lgan odam uchun mos keladigan bir soya bilan tanishdi.

en: He hastened to “reassure” her and made her sit down facing him at the table.
uz: U qizni tasalli berishga shoshildi va uni o'ziga qarata stolga o'tirtirishga majbur qildi.

en: Sonia sat down, looked about her — at Lebeziatnikov, at the notes lying on the table and then again at Pyotr Petrovitch and her eyes remained riveted on him.
uz: Sonia o'tirib, atrofini ko'rib turibdi: Lebeziatnikov, stol ustida yotgan yozuvlar va keyin yana Pyotr Petrovitch.

en: Lebeziatnikov was moving to the door.
uz: Lebeziatnikov eshikga yaqinlashayotgan edi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch signed to Sonia to remain seated and stopped Lebeziatnikov.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch Soniaga o'tirishga va Lebeziatnikovni to'xtatishga rozi bo'ldi.

en: “Is Raskolnikov in there?
uz: Raskolnikov u yerda bormi?

en: Has he come?” he asked him in a whisper.
uz: U kelganmi? - deb so'radi u shoshib.

en: I saw him just come in.
uz: Men uni shunchaki kirganini ko'rdim.

en: … Why?” “Well, I particularly beg you to remain here with us and not to leave me alone with this … young woman.
uz: Nima uchun? Xususan, biz bilan birga qolishingizni va meni bu yosh ayol bilan yolg'iz qoldirmasligingizni iltimos qilaman.

en: I only want a few words with her, but God knows what they may make of it.
uz: Men u bilan faqat bir necha so'z gaplashmoqchiman, lekin Xudo biladi, ular bu haqda qanday fikrda bo'lishlari mumkin.

en: I shouldn’t like Raskolnikov to repeat anything.
uz: Raskolnikovning biror narsani takrorlashini yoqtirmasdim.

en: … You understand what I mean?” “I understand!” Lebeziatnikov saw the point.
uz: ... Nima demoqchi ekanimni tushunasizmi?

en: “Yes, you are right.
uz: Ha, siz haqsiz.

en: … Of course, I am convinced personally that you have no reason to be uneasy, but … still, you are right.
uz: Albatta, shaxsan men sizning xavotirlanishingiz uchun hech qanday sababingiz yo'qligiga aminman, ammo... shunga qaramay, siz haqsiz.

en: Certainly I’ll stay.
uz: Shubhasiz, men qolishim kerak.

en: I’ll stand here at the window and not be in your way … I think you are right …” Pyotr Petrovitch returned to the sofa, sat down opposite Sonia, looked attentively at her and assumed an extremely dignified, even severe expression, as much as to say, “don’t you make any mistake, madam.” Sonia was overwhelmed with embarrassment.
uz: Men sizlarning yo'lingizda bo'lmasin, darcha oldida turibman... Siz haqsiz deb o'ylayman... Pyotr Petrovitch sofaga qaytib kelib, Soniaga qaraganda o'tirdi, unga diqqat bilan qaradi va nihoyatda qadrli, hatto qat'iy ifodani qabul qildi, hatto: "Siz hech qanday xato qilmaysiz, xonim", deb aytish uchun ham.

en: “In the first place, Sofya Semyonovna, will you make my excuses to your respected mamma.
uz: Birinchidan, Sofiya Semyonovna, hurmatli onangizga uzr so'rab murojaat qilasizmi?

en: … That’s right, isn’t it?
uz: Bu to'g'ri, shunday emasmi?

en: Katerina Ivanovna stands in the place of a mother to you?” Pyotr Petrovitch began with great dignity, though affably.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna sizning onangizning o'rniga turibdimi? Pyotr Petrovitch katta qadr-qimmat bilan, ammo mehribonlik bilan boshlandi.

en: It was evident that his intentions were friendly.
uz: Uning niyatlari do'stona ekanligi aniq edi.

en: “Quite so, yes; the place of a mother,” Sonia answered, timidly and hurriedly.
uz: "Ha, shunday; onalik o'rni", - deya javob berdi Sonia, uyatchan va shoshilinchlik bilan.

en: “Then will you make my apologies to her?
uz: O'shanda unga uzr so'raysizmi?

en: Through inevitable circumstances I am forced to be absent and shall not be at the dinner in spite of your mamma’s kind invitation.” “Yes … I’ll tell her … at once.” And Sonia hastily jumped up from her seat.
uz: Muqarrar holatlar tufayli men kechki ovqatda bo'lmaslikka majburman va sizning onangizning mehribon taklifiga qaramay, kechki ovqatga bormayman.  Ha... Men unga aytaman... birdan. Soʻngra Sonia tezda oʻtirgan joyidan oʻtib ketdi.

en: “Wait, that’s not all,” Pyotr Petrovitch detained her, smiling at her simplicity and ignorance of good manners, “and you know me little, my dear Sofya Semyonovna, if you suppose I would have ventured to trouble a person like you for a matter of so little consequence affecting myself only.
uz: Sot, bu hammasi emas, Pyotr Petrovitch uni ushlab qo'ydi, uning soddaligi va yaxshi xulq-atvorni bilmasligiga tabassum qilib, va siz meni juda kam tanasiz, aziz Sofiya Semyonovna, agar siz o'ylasangiz, men faqat o'zimga tegishli bo'lgan juda kam ahamiyatga ega bo'lgan masala uchun siz kabi odamni bezovta qilishga jur'at qilgan bo'lardim.

en: I have another object.” Sonia sat down hurriedly.
uz: Mening yana bir ob'ektim bor. Sonia shoshilinch o'tirdi.

en: Her eyes rested again for an instant on the grey-and-rainbow-coloured notes that remained on the table, but
uz: Uning ko'zlari bir zumga yana stol ustida qoladigan sariq va yomg'ir rangli notalarga tiklandi, ammo

en: she quickly looked away and fixed her eyes on Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: U tezda yuz o'girib, Pyotr Petrovitchga ko'zlarini tikdi.

en: She felt it horribly indecorous, especially for her, to look at another person’s money.
uz: U o'zi uchun, ayniqsa, boshqa odamning pulini ko'rish juda behuda tuyulgan.

en: She stared at the gold eyeglass which Pyotr Petrovitch held in his left hand and at the massive and extremely handsome ring with a yellow stone on his middle finger.
uz: U Pyotr Petrovitchning chap qo'lida tutgan oltin ko'zguga va o'rta barmog'ida sariq tosh bo'lgan ulkan va nihoyatda chiroyli bag'riga qaradi.

en: But suddenly she looked away and, not knowing where to turn, ended by staring Pyotr Petrovitch again straight in the face.
uz: Ammo u to'satdan boshqa tomonga qaradi va qayerga borishni bilmay, yana Pyotr Petroviçning yuziga qaradi.

en: After a pause of still greater dignity he continued.
uz: Bundan tashqari, o'zining qadr-qimmatini ko'rsatgan biroz to'xtalishdan so'ng, u davom etdi.

en: “I chanced yesterday in passing to exchange a couple of words with Katerina Ivanovna, poor woman.
uz: Kecha o'tib ketayotganimda, kambag'al ayol Katerina Ivanovna bilan bir necha so'z almashishga to'g'ri keldi.

en: That was sufficient to enable me to ascertain that she is in a position —preternatural, if one may so express it.” “Yes … preternatural …” Sonia hurriedly assented.
uz: Bu esa uni preternatural holatda ekanligiga ishonch hosil qilishim uchun etarli edi.Ha, ...preternatural ... Sonia shoshilinch rozi bo'ldi.

en: “Or it would be simpler and more comprehensible to say, ill.” “Yes, simpler and more comprehen … yes, ill.” “Quite so.
uz: Yoki kasallik deb aytish osonroq va tushunarliroq bo'ladi.Ha, oddiyroq va tushunarliroq ... ha, kasallik.Ha, shunday.

en: So then from a feeling of humanity and so to speak compassion, I should be glad to be of service to her in any way, foreseeing her unfortunate position.
uz: Shunday qilib, insonparvarlik va rahm-shafqat hissi bilan unga qandaydir yordam ko'rsatganimdan xursand bo'lishim kerak, chunki uning ayanchli ahvolini ko'rib turibman.

en: I believe the whole of this poverty-stricken family depends now entirely on you?” “Allow me to ask,” Sonia rose to her feet, “did you say something to her yesterday of the possibility of a pension?
uz: O'ylaymanki, bu qashshoqlik ostida yashovchi butun oila endi butunlay sizdan bog'liq?Mening so'rashimga ruxsat bering,Sonya o'z oyoqlaridan turdi,Siz o'tgan kun unga pensiya olish imkoniyati to'g'risida biron narsa aytdingizmi?

en: Because she told me you had undertaken to get her one.
uz: Chunki u menga siz uning uchun birorta qurbonlik olishni va'da qilganingizni aytdi.

en: Was that true?” “Not in the slightest, and indeed it’s an absurdity!
uz: Bu haqiqatmi edi? Hech kam emas va bu absurdlikdir!

en: I merely hinted at her obtaining temporary assistance as the widow of an official who had died in the service —if only she has patronage … but apparently your late parent had not served his full term and had not indeed been in the service at all of late.
uz: Men faqat xizmatda vafot etgan mansabdor kishining bechori sifatida uning vaqtincha yordam olishini ko'rsatdim ... agar u faqat o'z me'yorida bo'lsa ... ammo ko'rinib turganidek, sizning ketib ketgan ota-onangiz to'liq muddatini o'tkazmagan edi va aslida hech qachon xizmatda kech qolmagan edi.

en: In fact, if there could be any hope, it would be very ephemeral, because there would be no claim for assistance in that case, far from it.
uz: Darhaqiqat, agar umid bo'lsa, bu juda vaqtinchalik bo'ladi, chunki bu holatda yordam talab qilinmaydi.

en: … And she is dreaming of a pension already, he-he-he!
uz: Va u allaqachon pensiya haqida orzu qilmoqda, u-u-u!

en: … A go-ahead lady!” “Yes, she is.
uz: ... Go-ahead xonim! Ha, u shunday.

en: For she is credulous and good-hearted, and she believes everything from the goodness of her heart and … and … and she is like that … yes … You must excuse her,” said Sonia, and again she got up to go.
uz: Chunki u e'tiqodkor va yaxshi yurakli, u hamma narsaga qalbida yaxshilik bilan ishonadi va ... va ... va u shunday ... ha ... Siz uni kechirishingiz kerak, - dedi Sonia, - va yana u ketish uchun turdi.

en: “But you haven’t heard what I have to say.” “No, I haven’t heard,” muttered Sonia.
uz: Ammo siz mening aytadigan so'zlarimni eshitmadingiz.Yo'q, men eshitmadim, - dedi Sonia.

en: “Then sit down.” She was terribly confused; she sat down again a third time.
uz: Keyin o'tirdi. U juda chalg'ib qoldi; u yana uchinchi marta o'tirdi.

en: “Seeing her position with her unfortunate little ones, I should be glad, as I have said before, so far as lies in my power, to be of service, that is, so far as is in my power, not more.
uz: O'zining baxtsiz bolalari bilan bo'lgan munosabatini ko'rib, men bundan oldin aytganimdek, xizmat qilish uchun qo'limdan kelganicha, ya'ni qo'limdan kelganicha, bundan ko'ra ko'proq bo'lmasligimdan xursand bo'laman.

en: One might for instance get up a subscription for her, or a lottery, something of the sort, such as is always arranged in such cases by friends or even outsiders desirous of assisting people.
uz: Misol uchun, unga obuna bo'lish yoki lotereya olish mumkin, masalan, bunday holatlarda do'stlar yoki hatto odamlarga yordam berishni istagan chet elliklar tomonidan do'stlashtiriladi.

en: It was of that I intended to speak to you; it might be done.” “Yes, yes … God will repay you for it,” faltered Sonia, gazing intently at Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Siz bilan gaplashmoqchi bo'lganim shundan iborat edi; bu amalga oshishi mumkin.Ha, ha... Xudo sizga buning evaziga mukofot beradi, so'zladi Sonia, Pyotr Petrovitchga diqqat bilan qarab.

en: “It might be, but we will talk of it later.
uz: Bu bo'lishi mumkin, lekin keyinroq gaplashamiz.

en: We might begin it today, we will talk it over this evening and lay the foundation so to speak.
uz: Biz uni bugun boshlashimiz mumkin, biz bu kechqurun muhokama qilamiz va asosni qo'yamiz.

en: Come to me at seven o’clock.
uz: Yettida mendan so'ng kelinglar.

en: Lebeziatnikov, I hope, will assist us.
uz: Lebeziatnikov, umid qilamanki, bizga yordam beradi.

en: But there is one circumstance of which I ought to warn you beforehand and for which I venture to trouble you, Sofya Semyonovna, to come here.
uz: Ammo men sizni oldindan ogohlantirishim kerak bo'lgan bir holat bor va shu sababli sizni, Sofiya Semyonovna, bu yerga kelish uchun bezovta qilishga jur'at qilaman.

en: In my opinion money cannot be, indeed it’s unsafe to put it into Katerina Ivanovna’s own hands.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, pulni Katerina Ivanovna o'z qo'llariga qo'yish mumkin emas, balki xavfli.

en: The dinner today is a proof of that.
uz: Bugungi kechki ovqat buning isbotidir.

en: Though she has not, so to speak, a crust of bread for tomorrow and … well, boots or shoes, or anything; she has bought today Jamaica rum, and even, I believe, Madeira and … and coffee.
uz: Garchi u ertaga non qo'shishi va ... yaxshi, poyabzal yoki poyabzal yoki boshqa narsa bo'lmasa-da, bugungi kunda u Jamaika rumini, hatto, menimcha, Madeiraning va ... va kofe sotib oldi.

en: I saw it as I passed through.
uz: Men o'sha yerdan o'tganimda uni ko'rdim.

en: Tomorrow it will all fall upon you again, they won’t have a crust of bread.
uz: Ertaga hammasi sizga qaytadi, ularga bir qadoq ham non yo'q.

en: It’s absurd, really, and so, to my thinking, a subscription ought to be raised so that the unhappy widow should not know of the money, but only you, for instance.
uz: Haqiqatan ham absurd, shuning uchun, mening fikrimcha, beva ayol pul haqida bilmasligi uchun obuna to'planishi kerak, masalan, faqat siz bilishingiz kerak.

en: Am I right?” “I don’t know … this is only today, once in her life.
uz: Men to'g'rimi?    Bilmayman ... bu faqat bugun, uning hayotida bir marta.

en: … She was so anxious to do honour, to celebrate the memory.
uz: ... U hurmatni namoyon etish, xotiralarni nishonlash uchun shu qadar intizor edi.

en: … And she is very sensible … but just as you think and I shall be very, very … they will all be … and God will reward … and the orphans …” Sonia burst into tears.
uz: Va u juda aqlli ... lekin siz va men o'ylagandek, ular ham juda, juda ... bo'lishadi ... va Xudo mukofotlaydi ... va yetimlarni ... Sonia ko'z yoshlariga tushib ketdi.

en: “Very well, then, keep it in mind; and now will you accept for the benefit of your relation the small sum that I am able to spare, from me personally.
uz: Shunday qilib, buni yodda tuting va endi men o'zimdan qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan kichik miqdorni o'z munosabatlaringiz uchun qabul qila olasizmi?

en: I am very anxious that my name should not be mentioned in connection with it.
uz: O'zimning ismim bu bilan bog'liq bo'lmasligi uchun juda tashvishlanaman.

en: Here … having so to speak anxieties of my own, I cannot do more …”
uz: Bu yerda... o'zimning tashvishlarim borligi sababli, men bundan ko'ra ko'proq qila olmayman ...

en: And Pyotr Petrovitch held out to Sonia a ten-rouble note carefully unfolded.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch esa Soniaga o'n rubllik ehtiyotkorlik bilan ochilgan qog'ozni uzatdi.

en: Sonia took it, flushed crimson, jumped up, muttered something and began taking leave.
uz: Sonia uni olib, qizil qizil ko'ylakni ko'tardi, ko'tarilib ketdi, biror narsa gapirib berdi va dam olishni boshladi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch accompanied her ceremoniously to the door.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch uni marosimli ravishda eshikgacha kuzatib bordi.

en: She got out of the room at last, agitated and distressed, and returned to Katerina Ivanovna, overwhelmed with confusion.
uz: Oxir-oqibat u tashvishli va qayg'urgan holda xonadan chiqib, Katerina Ivanovna oldiga qaytib keldi.

en: All this time Lebeziatnikov had stood at the window or walked about the room, anxious not to interrupt the conversation; when Sonia had gone he walked up to Pyotr Petrovitch and solemnly held out his hand.
uz: Bu vaqt davomida Lebeziatnikov do'zax oldida turardi yoki xonadon atrofida yurardi, suhbatni uzmaslik uchun xavotirda edi; Sonia ketgach, u Pyotr Petrovitchning oldiga borib, tantanali ravishda qo'lini uzatdi.

en: “I heard and saw everything,” he said, laying stress on the last verb.
uz: "Men hamma narsani eshitdim va ko'rdim", - dedi u, so'nggi amalni ta'kidlab.

en: “That is honourable, I mean to say, it’s humane!
uz: Bu hurmatga sazovor, demak, bu insoniylikdir!

en: You wanted to avoid gratitude, I saw!
uz: Ko'rib turganimcha, siz minnatdorchilikdan qochmoqchi bo'lgansiz!

en: And although I cannot, I confess, in principle sympathise with private charity, for it not only fails to eradicate the evil but even promotes it, yet I must admit that I saw your action with pleasure —yes, yes, I like it.” “That’s all nonsense,” muttered Pyotr Petrovitch, somewhat disconcerted, looking carefully at Lebeziatnikov.
uz: Garchi men xususiy xayrixohlikka asosda hamdard bo'lmasam-da, uni nafaqat yomonlikni yo'q qilishga, balki uni ham rivojlantirishga qodir emasman, lekin sizning harakatingizni zavq bilan ko'rganimni tan olishim kerak. Ha, men buni yaxshi ko'raman. Bularning barchasi behudalik, Pyotr Petrovitch biroz g'alati bo'lib, Lebeziatnikovga diqqat bilan qaragan.

en: “No, it’s not nonsense!
uz: Yo'q, bu behudalik emas!

en: A man who has suffered distress and annoyance as you did yesterday and who yet can sympathise with the misery of others, such a man … even though he is making a social mistake —is still deserving of respect!
uz: Kecha siz kabi qayg'u va g'azabga uchragan, ammo boshqalarning azob-uqubatlariga rahm-shafqat ko'rsatadigan kishi, bunday kishi ... ijtimoiy xato qilishiga qaramay, hurmatga sazovor!

en: I did not expect it indeed of you, Pyotr Petrovitch, especially as according to your ideas … oh, what a drawback your ideas are to you!
uz: Sizdan buni aslida kutmagan edim, Pyotr Petrovitch, ayniqsa, sizning g'oyalaringizga ko'ra ... oh, sizning g'oyalaringiz sizga qanday kamchilik keltiradi!

en: How distressed you are for instance by your ill-luck yesterday,” cried the simple-hearted Lebeziatnikov, who felt a return of affection for Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Misol uchun, siz o'tgan kuningizdagi omadsizlikdan qanchalik xafa bo'lganingizni ko'rdingiz, - deb qayg'urgan oddiy yurakli Lebeziatnikov, Pyotr Petrovitchga nisbatan mehr-muhabbatni his qildi.

en: “And, what do you want with marriage, with legal marriage, my dear, noble Pyotr Petrovitch?
uz: Va siz nikohdan, qonuniy nikohdan nima istaysiz, aziz, aziz Pyotr Petrovitch?

en: Why do you cling to this legality of marriage?
uz: Nima uchun siz nikohning qonuniyligiga qattiq qo'shilyapsiz?

en: Well, you may beat me if you like, but I am glad, positively glad it hasn’t come off, that you are free, that you are not quite lost for humanity … you see, I’ve spoken my mind!” “Because I don’t want in your free marriage to be made a fool of and to bring up another man’s children, that’s why I want legal marriage,” Luzhin replied in order to make some answer.
uz: Agar xohlasangiz, meni urishingiz mumkin, lekin men xursandman, albatta xursandmanki, bu o'zgarmagan, siz erkinsiz, insoniyat uchun o'zingizni yo'qotgansiz... ko'ribsizlarmi, men o'z fikrimni aytdim! Chunki men sizning erkin nikohingizda boshqa odamning bolalarini tarbiyalash va o'yin-kulgi qilishni xohlamayman, shuning uchun men qonuniy nikohni xohlayman, - deb javob berdi Luzhin.

en: He seemed preoccupied by something.
uz: U biror narsa bilan mashg'ul bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: You referred to children,” Lebeziatnikov started off like a warhorse at the trumpet call.
uz: Siz bolalar haqida gapirgansiz, Lebeziatnikov qo'ng'iroqda jang otasi kabi boshlandi.

en: “Children are a social question and a
uz: Bolalar ijtimoiy savol va muammo hisoblanadi.

en: question of first importance, I agree; but the question of children has another solution.
uz: Birinchidan, bu muhim masala, men bunga rozi bo'laman; lekin bolalar masalasiga boshqa yechim bor.

en: Some refuse to have children altogether, because they suggest the institution of the family.
uz: Ba'zilar farzand ko'rishni butunlay rad etishadi, chunki ular oila institutini taklif qilishadi.

en: We’ll speak of children later, but now as to the question of honour, I confess that’s my weak point.
uz: Keyinroq bolalar haqida gap boradi, lekin endi sharaflilik masalasiga kelsak, bu mening zaif tomonim ekanligini tan olaman.

en: That horrid, military, Pushkin expression is unthinkable in the dictionary of the future.
uz: Bu dahshatli, harbiy, Puşkinning ifodasini kelajakning lug'atida tasavvur qilish mumkin emas.

en: What does it mean indeed?
uz: Haqiqatan ham bu nimani anglatadi?

en: It’s nonsense, there will be no deception in a free marriage!
uz: To'g'ri gap, bepul nikohda aldash yo'q!

en: That is only the natural consequence of a legal marriage, so to say, its corrective, a protest.
uz: Bu faqat qonuniy nikohning tabiiy oqibatidir, demak, uning tuzatishi, protestdir.

en: So that indeed it’s not humiliating … and if I ever, to suppose an absurdity, were to be legally married, I should be positively glad of it.
uz: Shunday qilib, bu, albatta, sharmandalik emas ... va agar men biron bir vaqtda qonuniy ravishda turmush qurgan bo'lsam, men bundan xursand bo'lishim kerak.

en: I should say to my wife: ‘My dear, hitherto I have loved you, now I respect you, for you’ve shown you can protest!’ You laugh!
uz: Xotinimga shunday deyishim kerak: "Xotinim, men seni allaqachon yaxshi ko'rdim, endi hurmat qilaman, chunki sen protest qila olishingni ko'rsatding! Sen kulyapsan!

en: That’s because you are incapable of getting away from prejudices.
uz: Buning sababi siz oldindan tanqid qilishdan qochishga qodir emasligingizdir.

en: I understand now where the unpleasantness is of being deceived in a legal marriage, but it’s simply a despicable consequence of a despicable position in which both are humiliated.
uz: Endi men qonuniy nikohda aldanib qolishning yoqimsizligini tushunib yetaman, lekin bu shunchaki ikkalasi ham kamsitilgan kamsitilgan holatning yomon oqibatidir.

en: When the deception is open, as in a free marriage, then it does not exist, it’s unthinkable.
uz: Yolg'on ochiq bo'lganda, erkin nikohda bo'lgani kabi, u yo'q, tasavvur ham bo'lmaydi.

en: Your wife will only prove how she respects you by considering you incapable of opposing her happiness and avenging yourself on her for her new husband.
uz: Xotiningiz sizni hurmat qilayotganini faqatgina sizning baxtga qarshilik ko'rsatib, yangi eringiz uchun undan o'ch olishingiz mumkin emasligingizni ko'rib, ko'rsatadi.

en: I sometimes dream if I were to be married, pfoo!
uz: Ba'zan uylanishni orzu qilaman, pfoo!

en: I mean if I were to marry, legally or not, it’s just the same, I should present my wife with a lover if she had not found one for herself.
uz: Demak, agar men qonuniy ravishda yoki yo'q holda turmush qursam ham, o'sha-o'sha bo'ladi, agar xotin o'zi uchun sevgini topmagan bo'lsa, xotinimga sevgini taqdim etaman.

en: ‘My dear,’ I should say, ‘I love you, but even more than that I desire you to respect me.
uz: Soni sevaman, lekin bundan ham ko'proq meni hurmat qilishingni istayman.

en: See!’ Am I not right?” Pyotr Petrovitch sniggered as he listened, but without much merriment.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch tinglayotganda qichqirib ketdi, lekin ko'p quvonchsiz.

en: He hardly heard it indeed.
uz: Aslida, u buni eshitmagan.

en: He was preoccupied with something else and even Lebeziatnikov at last noticed it.
uz: U boshqa bir narsa bilan band edi va hatto Lebeziatnikov ham oxir-oqibat buni payqadi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch seemed excited and rubbed his hands.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitch hayajonlanib, qo'llarini silkitdi.

en: Lebeziatnikov remembered all this and reflected upon it afterwards.
uz: Lebeziatnikov bularning barchasini eslab, keyinchalik bu haqda mulohaza yuritdi.

en: II It would be difficult to explain exactly what could have originated the idea of that senseless dinner in Katerina Ivanovna’s disordered brain.
uz: II. Katerina Ivanovnaning buzilgan miyasida o'sha behuda kechki ovqat fikrining kelib chiqishi nima bo'lishi mumkinligini aniq tushuntirish qiyin bo'ladi.

en: Nearly ten of the twenty roubles, given by Raskolnikov for Marmeladov’s funeral, were wasted upon it.
uz: Raskolnikov tomonidan Marmeladovning dafn marosimi uchun berilgan yigirma rubldan deyarli o'n nafari unga sarflandi.

en: Possibly Katerina Ivanovna felt obliged to honour the memory of the deceased “suitably,” that all the lodgers, and still more Amalia Ivanovna, might know “that he was in no way their inferior, and perhaps very much their superior,” and that no one had the right “to turn up his nose at him.” Perhaps the chief element was that peculiar “poor man’s pride,” which compels many poor people to spend their last savings on some traditional social ceremony, simply in order to do “like other people,” and not to “be looked down upon.” It is very probable, too, that Katerina Ivanovna longed on this occasion, at the moment when she seemed to be abandoned by everyone, to show those “wretched contemptible lodgers” that she knew “how to do things, how to entertain” and that she had been brought up “in a genteel, she might almost say aristocratic colonel’s family” and had not been meant for sweeping
uz: Katerina Ivanovna o'zini marhumning xotirasiga munosib hurmat ko'rsatishga majbur deb hisobladi, shunda barcha ijaraga oluvchilar va, ehtimol, bundan ham ko'proq Amaliya Ivanovna ham uning hech qanday kamroq emasligini, ehtimol, juda ham yuqori ekanligini va hech kim unga yuz o'girish huquqiga ega emasligini bilishlari mumkin.Agarki asosiy omil o'sha o'ziga xos "faqir odam" g'ururidir, chunki bu ko'plab kambag'allarni o'zlarining oxirgi jamg'armalarini boshqa odamlarga o'xshatish uchun, boshqa odamlarga o'xshatish uchun, ijtimoiy marosimlarga sarflashga majburlaydi.Agar bo'lmasa, Katerina Ivanovna ham bu fursatda, deyarli hamma tomonidan tashlab ketilgan bo'lgan paytda, o'sha "faqir" ijaraga oluvchilarga o'zini qanday qilib ko'rsatishni bilishini, o'zini qanday qilib ko'ngillashtirishni bilishini, o'zini ko'rsatishni va o'zini ko'targanini, shuningdek, kolonel oilasiga o'zi qanday qilib ko'rsatishni xohlaganini ko'rsatishi mumkin.

en: floors and washing the children’s rags at night.
uz: Yotoqlarni yuvish va kechasi bolalar kiyimlarini yuvish.

en: Even the poorest and most broken-spirited people are sometimes liable to these paroxysms of pride and vanity which take the form of an irresistible nervous craving.
uz: Hatto eng kambag'al va ruhiy tushkun odamlar ham ba'zida mag'rurlik va begʻuborlikning bu paroxizmlariga duchor bo'lishadi, bular esa beqaror g'azabga aylanadi.

en: And Katerina Ivanovna was not broken- spirited; she might have been killed by circumstance, but her spirit could not have been broken, that is, she could not have been intimidated, her will could not be crushed.
uz: Katerina Ivonovna esa ruhiy tushkunlikka tushmagan edi; u vaziyat tufayli o'ldirilgan bo'lishi mumkin edi, ammo uning ruhi tushkunlikka tushmagan, ya'ni qo'rqitilmagan, irodasi ezilgan bo'lmasdi.

en: Moreover Sonia had said with good reason that her mind was unhinged.
uz: Bundan tashqari, Sonia o'z ongini o'zgartirmaganini yaxshi sabab bilan aytdi.

en: She could not be said to be insane, but for a year past she had been so harassed that her
uz: Uning aqldan ozganligi haqida aytish mumkin emas edi, lekin o'tgan bir yil davomida u shunchalik ta'qib qilingan ediki, uning

en: mind might well be overstrained.
uz: O'z aql-idrokingiz ortiqcha bo'lishi mumkin.

en: The later stages of consumption are apt, doctors tell us, to affect the intellect.
uz: Shifokorlarning aytishicha, iste'molning keyingi bosqichlari aqlga ta'sir ko'rsatadi.

en: There was no great variety of wines, nor was there Madeira; but wine there was.
uz: Turli xil sharoblar yo'q edi, Madeira ham yo'q edi, lekin sharob bor edi.

en: There was vodka, rum and Lisbon wine, all of the poorest quality but in sufficient quantity.
uz: Vodka, rum va Lissabon sharoblari mavjud edi, barchasi eng yomon sifatli, ammo yetarli miqdorda.

en: Besides the traditional rice and honey, there were three or four dishes, one of which consisted of pancakes, all prepared in Amalia Ivanovna’s kitchen.
uz: An'anaviy riz va asaldan tashqari, uch yoki to'rtta taom mavjud edi, ulardan biri pancakelardan iborat edi, hammasi Amaliya Ivanovna oshxonasida tayyorlangan edi.

en: Two samovars were boiling, that tea and punch might be offered after dinner.
uz: Ikki samovar qaynab ketayotgan edi, kechki ovqatdan keyin choy va cho'p taklif qilinishi mumkin edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna had herself seen to purchasing the provisions, with the help of one of the lodgers, an unfortunate little Pole who had somehow been stranded at Madame Lippevechsel’s.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna o'zi oziq-ovqat mahsulotlarini xarid qilishga g'amxo'rlik qilgan edi, u yerda yashovchilarning biri, qandaydir tarzda Madame Lippevechsel'sda to'xtab qolgan baxtsiz kichik polyak edi.

en: He promptly put himself at Katerina Ivanovna’s disposal and had been all that morning and all the day before running about as fast as his legs could carry him, and very anxious that everyone should be aware of it.
uz: U darhol Katerina Ivanovnaga o'zini taqdim etdi va butun ertalab va kun davomida oyoqlari uni ko'tarib olishi mumkin bo'lgan darajada tezda yugurib bordi va hamma buni bilishi uchun juda xavotirda edi.

en: For every trifle he ran to Katerina Ivanovna, even hunting her out at the bazaar, at every instant called her “Pani.” She was heartily sick of him before the end, though she had declared at first that she could not have got on without this “serviceable and magnanimous man.” It was one of Katerina Ivanovna’s characteristics to paint everyone she met in the most glowing colours.
uz: Har bir kichik ish uchun u Katerina Ivanovna oldinga yugurib, hatto bazarda uni ovlab, har bir daqiqada uni "Pani" deb chaqirardi. Oxirigacha u undan juda kasal edi, garchi dastlab u bu xizmatkor va mehribon odamsiz o'zini tuta olmasligini e'lon qilgan bo'lsa-da. Katerina Ivanovna uchratgan har bir kishini eng yorqin ranglarda bo'yintirishni o'z xususiyatlaridan biri deb bilgan.

en: Her praises were so exaggerated as sometimes to be embarrassing; she would invent various circumstances to the credit of her new acquaintance and quite genuinely believe in their reality.
uz: Uning maqtovlari o'ta haddan tashqari bo'lib, ba'zan uyatchan bo'lishi mumkin edi; u yangi tanisidan kelib chiqqan turli holatlarni o'ylab topadi va ularning haqiqiyligiga chin dildan ishonadi.

en: Then all of a sudden she would be disillusioned and would rudely and contemptuously repulse the person she had only a few hours before been literally adoring.
uz: Keyin u to'satdan tushkunlikka tushib, bir necha soat oldin aslida tabriklagan odamni qo'pollik va kamsitish bilan rad etadi.

en: She was naturally of a gay, lively and peace-loving disposition, but from continual failures and misfortunes she had come to desire so keenly that all should live in peace and joy and should not dare to break the peace, that the slightest jar, the smallest disaster reduced her almost to frenzy, and she would pass in an instant from the brightest hopes and fancies to cursing her fate and raving, and knocking her head against the wall.
uz: U tabiiy ravishda gey, jonli va tinchlikparvar bo'lgan, ammo doimiy muvaffaqiyatsizliklar va baxtsizliklar tufayli hamma tinchlik va quvonchda yashashiga va tinchlikni buzishga jur'at qilmasligi uchun shunchalik kuchli istakga ega bo'lganki, eng kichkina qadoq, eng kichik fojia uni deyarli g'azabga aylantirdi va u bir daqiqa ichida eng ajoyib umid va xayollardan o'tib, o'z taqdirini la'natlashga va g'azablanishga va boshini devorga urishga o'tadi.

en: Amalia Ivanovna, too, suddenly acquired extraordinary importance in Katerina Ivanovna’s eyes and was treated by her with extraordinary respect, probably only because Amalia Ivanovna had thrown herself heart and soul into the preparations.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna ham Katerina Ivanovna nazarida noyob ahamiyatga ega bo'ldi va u tomonidan noyob hurmat bilan muomala qilindi, ehtimol, faqatgina Amaliya Ivanovna tayyorgarlikka jon-jahdini bag'ishlaganligi uchun.

en: She had undertaken to lay the table, to provide the linen, crockery, etc., and
uz: U dasturxon o'rnatishni, lenon, sovg'a va hokazolarni taqdim etishni va boshqalarni ta'minlashni boshlagan edi.

en: to cook the dishes in her kitchen, and Katerina Ivanovna had left it all in her hands and gone herself to the cemetery.
uz: oshxonada ovqat pishirish uchun, Katerina Ivanovna hamma narsani o'z qo'lida qoldirib, o'zi qabrga ketdi.

en: Everything had been well done.
uz: Hamma narsa yaxshi bajarilgan edi.

en: Even the tablecloth was nearly clean; the crockery, knives, forks and glasses were, of course, of all shapes and patterns, lent by different lodgers, but the table was properly laid at the time fixed, and Amalia Ivanovna, feeling she had done her work well, had put on a black silk dress and a cap with new mourning ribbons and met the returning party with some pride.
uz: Hatto oshxonasi ham deyarli toza edi; asbob-uskunalar, pichoqlar, furqonlar va oynalar, albatta, turli xil shakllar va namunalar bo'lgan, turli uy egalari tomonidan qarz olindi, lekin stol belgilangan vaqtda to'g'ri joylashtirilgan edi va Amaliya Ivanovna o'z ishini yaxshi bajarganini his etib, qora ipak kiyim va yangi yig'ilish lentlari bilan qopqoq kiygan va qaytib kelayotgan partiyani ba'zi bir faxr bilan kutib olgan.

en: This pride, though justifiable, displeased Katerina Ivanovna for some reason: “as though the table could not have been laid except by Amalia Ivanovna!” She disliked the cap with new ribbons, too.
uz: Garchi bu maqtanish oqlanishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, Katerina Ivanovna bir sababga ko'ra norozi bo'ldi: Amoliya Ivanovnadan boshqa stol qo'yilmagan bo'lsa kerak! U ham yangi qo'shiqlar bilan to'plamni yoqtirmadi.

en: “Could she be stuck up, the stupid German, because she was mistress of the house, and had consented as a favour to help her poor lodgers!
uz: Agar u, ahmoq nemis ayol, uy egasi bo'lgani va kambag'al ijaraga oluvchilarga yordam berishga rozi bo'lganligi uchun o'zini tutgan bo'lsa kerak!

en: Katerina Ivanovna’s father who had been a colonel and almost a governor had sometimes had the table set for forty persons, and then anyone like Amalia Ivanovna, or rather Ludwigovna, would not have been allowed into the kitchen.” Katerina Ivanovna, however, put off expressing her feelings for the time and contented herself with treating her coldly, though she decided inwardly that she would certainly have to put Amalia Ivanovna down and set her in her proper place, for goodness only knew what she was fancying herself.
uz: Katerina Ivanovnaning otasi kolonel va deyarli gubernator bo'lgan bo'lsa-da, ba'zan qirq kishiga ovqat tayyorlab qo'yishardi, so'ngra kimdir Amaliya Ivanovna yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Ludwigovna kabi kishi oshxonaga kirishiga yo'l qo'yilmasdi. Katerina Ivanovna, ammo o'sha vaqt uchun o'z his-tuyg'ularini ifoda etishni kechiktirdi va unga sovuq munosabatda bo'lish bilan kifoyalandi, garchi u o'zicha Amaliya Ivanovna-ni pastga surib, o'z o'rinlariga joylashtirishi kerakligini o'zi o'ylagan bo'lsa ham.

en: Katerina Ivanovna was irritated too by the fact that hardly any of the lodgers invited had come to the funeral, except the Pole who had just managed to run into the cemetery, while to the memorial dinner the poorest and most insignificant of them had turned up, the wretched creatures, many of them not quite sober.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna ham taklif etilgan mehmonlarning deyarli hech biri marosimga kelmagani uchun g'azabga tushdi, faqatgina chindan ham qabrga yugurib kelgan polyakdan tashqari, ammo marosimga eng kambag'al va eng ahamiyatsiz kishilar, ko'plari o'zlarini yaxshi ko'rmagan qashshoq mavjudotlar paydo bo'ldi.

en: The older and more respectable of them all, as if by common consent, stayed away.
uz: Ularning kattaroq va hurmatga sazovor bo'lganlari, xuddi umumiy rozilik bilan bo'lgani kabi, chetda qolishdi.

en: Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin, for instance, who might be said to be the most respectable of all the lodgers, did not appear, though Katerina Ivanovna had the evening before told all the world, that is Amalia Ivanovna, Polenka, Sonia and the Pole, that he was the most generous, noble-hearted man with a large property and vast connections, who had been a friend of her first husband’s, and a guest in her father’s house, and that he had promised to use all his influence to secure her a considerable pension.
uz: Misol uchun, barcha ijaraga oluvchilarning eng hurmatli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin paydo bo'lmadi, garchi Katerina Ivanovna o'tgan kechqurun butun dunyoga, ya'ni Amaliya Ivanovna, Polenka, Sonia va Polga, u katta mol-mulk va ulkan aloqalarga ega bo'lgan eng saxiy, buyuk yurakli odam ekanligini, birinchi erlarining do'sti va otasining uyiga mehmon bo'lganini va u katta pensiya olish uchun butun ta'siridan foydalanishni va'da qilganini aytdi.

en: It must be noted that when Katerina Ivanovna exalted anyone’s connections and fortune, it was without any ulterior motive,
uz: Shuni ta'kidlash kerakki, Katerina Ivanovna kimningdir bog'liqligi va omadini ulug'laganida, bu hech qanday boshqa sababsiz edi.

en: quite disinterestedly, for the mere pleasure of adding to the consequence of the person praised.
uz: To'g'ri, o'z manfaatini ko'zlamasdan, faqat maqtovga sazovor bo'lgan kishining natijalariga qo'shish uchun.

en: Probably “taking his cue” from Luzhin, “that contemptible wretch Lebeziatnikov had not turned up either.
uz: Ehtimol, Luzhindan o'z ko'rsatkichini olib, u begunoh va begunoh Lebeziatnikov ham ko'rinmagan.

en: What did he fancy himself?
uz: U o'ziga nima yoqardi?

en: He was only asked out of kindness and because he was sharing the same room with Pyotr Petrovitch and was a friend of his, so that it would have been awkward not to invite him.” Among those who failed to appear were “the genteel lady and her old-maidish daughter,” who had only been lodgers in the house for the last fortnight, but had several times complained of the noise and uproar in Katerina Ivanovna’s room, especially when Marmeladov had come back drunk.
uz: Uni faqat mehribonlik va Pyotr Petrovitch bilan bir xonada bo'lishgani va uning do'sti bo'lgani uchun, uni taklif qilmaslik noqulay bo'lgan. Ko'rinishda bo'lmaganlar orasida bu yaxshi xonim va uning keksa qizchasi, so'nggi ikki haftadan beri uyda faqatgina yashovchi edilar, lekin Katerina Ivanovna xonasidagi shov-shuv va g'alati haqida bir necha marta shikoyat qilgan edilar, ayniqsa Marmeladov mast bo'lganida.

en: Katerina Ivanovna heard this from Amalia Ivanovna who, quarrelling with Katerina Ivanovna, and threatening to turn the whole family out of doors, had shouted at her that they “were not worth the foot” of the honourable lodgers whom they were disturbing.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna buni Amaliya Ivanovna tomonidan eshitgan edi, u Katerina Ivanovna bilan bahslashib, butun oilani darvozalardan tashqariga chiqarish bilan tahdid qilgan edi va ularga ular bezovta qilayotgan hurmatli ijaraga oluvchilarning qiyofasiga loyiq emasligini baqirgan edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna determined now to invite this lady and her daughter, “whose foot she was not worth,” and who had turned away haughtily when she casually met them, so that they might know that “she was more noble in her thoughts and feelings and did not harbour malice,” and might see that she was not accustomed to her way of living.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna endi bu xonimni va uning qizini taklif qilishga qaror qildi, chunki ularning oyoqlari unga arzon edi va ular bilan to'xtab bo'lganida mag'rurlik bilan yuz o'girgan edilar, shunda ular uning fikr va his-tuyg'ularida ko'proq noyob ekanligini va yomonlik ko'rsatmaganligini bilib olishlari va o'z turmush tarzini o'rganmaganligini ko'rishlari mumkin edi.

en: She had proposed to make this clear to them at dinner with allusions to her late father’s governorship, and also at the same time to hint that it was exceedingly stupid of them to turn away on meeting her.
uz: U kechki ovqat paytida o'z otasining gubernatorligiga ishora qilib, bu haqda ularga aniq aytishni taklif qilgan edi va shu bilan birga, ular o'zlarining u bilan uchrashishdan yuz o'girishlarining juda ahmoqlik ekanligini isbotlagan edi.

en: The fat colonel-major (he was really a discharged officer of low rank) was also absent, but it appeared that he had been “not himself” for the last two days.
uz: Shunga o'xshab, yumshoq polkovnik-major (haqiqatan ham u past darajadagi bo'shashtirilgan ofitser edi) ham yo'q edi, ammo u o'zi emas edi o'zi so'nggi ikki kun davomida.

en: The party consisted of the Pole, a wretched looking clerk with a spotty face and a greasy coat, who had not a word to say for himself, and smelt abominably, a deaf and almost blind old man who had once been in the post office and who had been from immemorial ages maintained by someone at Amalia Ivanovna’s.
uz: Tashkilotda Polyak, ko'rinmas yuzli va yog'li kiyimli, o'zi uchun aytadigan so'zlari yo'q bo'lgan, o'ziga yomon hid ko'rsatadigan, bir vaqtlar pochtaxonasiga kirgan va qadimgi zamonlardan beri Amaliya Ivanovna bilan bog'liq bo'lgan soqov va deyarli ko'r keksa kishi bo'lgan.

en: A retired clerk of the commissariat department came, too; he was drunk, had a loud and most unseemly laugh and only fancy —was without a waistcoat!
uz: Komissariat idorasining pensiyalangan xodimi ham keldi; u mast edi, baland ovoz bilan kulishardi va faqat o'yin-kulgi edi!

en: One of the visitors sat straight down to the table without even greeting Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Mehmonlardan biri Katerina Ivanovnaga salom ham bermasdan, to'g'ri dasturxonga o'tirdi.

en: Finally one person having no suit appeared in his dressing-gown, but this was too much, and the efforts of Amalia Ivanovna and the Pole succeeded in removing
uz: Nihoyat, kiyimsiz bo'lgan bir kishi kiyimida paydo bo'ldi, ammo bu juda ko'p edi va Amaliya Ivanovna va Polyakning sa'y-harakatlari uni olib tashlashga muvaffaq bo'ldi

en: The Pole brought with him, however, two other Poles who did not live at Amalia Ivanovna’s and whom no one had seen here before.
uz: Biroq, polyak o'zi bilan Amaliya Ivanovnasda yashamagan va bu yerda hech kim ko'rmagan boshqa ikki polyakni ham olib keldi.

en: All this irritated Katerina Ivanovna intensely.
uz: Bularning barchasi Katerina Ivanovnani qattiq xafa qildi.

en: “For whom had they made all these preparations then?” To make room for the visitors the children had not even been laid for at the table; but the two little ones were sitting on a bench in the furthest corner with their dinner laid on a box, while Polenka as a big girl had to look after them, feed them, and keep their noses wiped like well-bred children’s.
uz: O'shanda ular kim uchun bunday tayyorgarlik ko'rishgan edi?Moshbalar uchun joy yaratish uchun bolalar hatto stolga qo'yilmagan edi; lekin ikkita kichkina bola o'tirgan bo'lib, kechki ovqatlari qutisiga qo'yilgan edi, Polenka esa katta bo'lganida ularga g'amxo'rlik qilish, ovqat berish va yaxshi tarbiyalangan bolalar kabi burunlarini silkish kerak edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna, in fact, could hardly help meeting her guests with increased dignity, and even haughtiness.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna, aslida, mehmonlarini yanada qadrli va hatto mag'rurlik bilan kutib olishdan bosh tortishi mumkin emas edi.

en: She stared at some of them with special severity, and loftily invited them to take their seats.
uz: U ulardan ba'zilariga alohida qat'iylik bilan qaradi va ularni o'z o'rinlariga o'tirishga taklif qiladi.

en: Rushing to the conclusion that Amalia Ivanovna must be responsible for those who were absent, she began treating her with extreme nonchalance, which the latter promptly observed and resented.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna o'tirmaganlar uchun javobgar bo'lishi kerak degan xulosaga kelib, u ayolga nisbatan juda salbiy munosabatda bo'ldi, bu ayol buni tezda ko'rib, xafa bo'ldi.

en: Such a beginning was no good omen for the end.
uz: Bunday boshlanish oxirat uchun yaxshi belgi emas edi.

en: All were seated at last.
uz: Oxir-oqibat hamma o'tirdi.

en: Raskolnikov came in almost at the moment of their return from the cemetery.
uz: Raskolnikovlar qabristondan qaytish paytida deyarli o'zlariga keldilar.

en: Katerina Ivanovna was greatly delighted to see him, in the first place, because he was the one “educated visitor, and, as everyone knew, was in two years to take a professorship in the university,” and secondly because he immediately and respectfully apologised for having been unable to be at the funeral.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna uni ko'rishdan juda xursand bo'ldi, birinchidan, chunki u o'ta bilimli tashrif buyuruvchi bo'lgan va, hamma bilganidek, ikki yildan keyin universitetda professor bo'lishga majbur bo'lgan va ikkinchidan, u o'z navbatida, o'lim marosimiga kelolmaganligi uchun darhol va hurmat ila uzr so'radi.

en: She positively pounced upon him, and made him sit on her left hand (Amalia Ivanovna was on her right).
uz: O'zi unga qarshi chiqdi va uni o'z chap qo'lida o'tirtirtirishga majbur qildi (Amaliya Ivanovna o'ng tarafida edi).

en: In spite of her continual anxiety that the dishes should be passed round correctly and that everyone should taste them, in spite of the agonising cough which interrupted her every minute and seemed to have grown worse during the last few days, she hastened to pour out in a half whisper to Raskolnikov all her suppressed feelings and her just indignation at the failure of the dinner, interspersing her remarks with lively and uncontrollable laughter at the expense of her visitors and especially of her landlady.
uz: U ovqatlarni to'g'ri o'tkazish va hamma ularni tanovul qilishi haqida doimiy tashvishlanishiga qaramay, har daqiqada uni kesib tashlaydigan va so'nggi bir necha kun ichida yomonlashganiga o'xshaydigan og'ir toshqinlikka qaramay, Raskolnikovga o'rtacha shvoshda o'zining barcha tushkun his-tuyg'ularini va kechki ovqatning muvaffaqiyatsiz ketishiga nisbatan adolatsiz g'azabini to'kib solishga harakat qildi, o'z fikrlarini mehmonlari, ayniqsa, uy egasining zararidan jonli va nazoratsiz kulgi bilan aralashtirdi.

en: “It’s all that cuckoo’s fault!
uz: Bularning hammasi bu qushning aybi bilan sodir bo'ldi!

en: You know whom I mean?
uz: Kimni nazarda tutganimni bilasizmi?

en: Her, her!” Katerina Ivanovna nodded towards the landlady.
uz: Her, her! Katerina Ivanovna uy egasiga bosh ko'tardi.

en: “Look at her, she’s making round eyes, she feels that we are talking about her and can’t understand.
uz: Unga qarang, u to'g'ri ko'zlar bilan ko'rinadi, biz u haqida gapirayotganimizni his qiladi va buni tushunmaydi.

en: (Cough-cough-cough.) And what does she put on that cap for?
uz: Va nima uchun u o'sha qo'pkazni kiyadi?

en: (Cough-cough-cough.) Have you noticed that she wants everyone to consider that she is patronising
uz: (Qo'sh-qush-qush) U hamma uning patronlik qilayotganini ko'rib chiqishini xohlaganini payqaganmisiz?

en: me and doing me an honour by being here?
uz: Meni bu yerda bo'lib, menga hurmat ko'rsatyapsizmi?

en: I asked her like a sensible woman to invite people, especially those who knew my late husband, and look at the set of fools she has brought!
uz: Men unga aql-idrokli ayol kabi odamlarni, ayniqsa, o'tgan erimni bilganlarni taklif qilishni so'radim va u bilan birga qancha axmoqlarni olib kelganini ko'ring!

en: Look at that one with the spotty face.
uz: O'sha burchakli yuziga qarang.

en: And those wretched Poles, ha- ha-ha!
uz: Va o'sha qashshoq polyaklar, ha-ha-ha!

en: (Cough-cough-cough.) Not one of them has ever poked his nose in here, I’ve never set eyes on them.
uz: Ularning hech biri bu yerga burunini kiritmagan, men hech qachon ularni ko'rmaganman.

en: What have they come here for, I ask you?
uz: Sizdan nima uchun ular bu yerga kelishganini so'rasam bo'ladi?

en: There they sit in a row.
uz: U yerda ular qatorda o'tirishadi.

en: Hey, pan!” she cried suddenly to one of them, “have you tasted the pancakes?
uz: Hey, pan! u ulardan biriga to'satdan qichqirdi,¿Pankeklarni tatib ko'rdingizmi?

en: Won’t you have some vodka?
uz: Vodka ichishni istamaysizmi?

en: Look, he’s jumped up and is making his bows, they must be quite starved, poor things.
uz: Qarang, u o'z qo'llarini qo'zg'atadi, ular juda och bo'lishlari kerak, kambag'al narsalar.

en: Never mind, let them eat!
uz: Aslo ahamiyat yo'q, ularga ovqatlanishga ruxsat bering!

en: They don’t make a noise, anyway, though I’m really afraid for our landlady’s silver spoons … Amalia Ivanovna!” she addressed her suddenly, almost aloud, “if your spoons should happen to be stolen, I won’t be responsible, I warn you!
uz: Ular hech qanday ovozni chiqarmaydilar, garchi uy egasining kumush qoshiqlari uchun qo'rqsam-da... Amaliya Ivanovna! u to'satdan, deyarli baland ovoz bilan unga murojaat qildi, agar sizning qoshiqlaringiz o'g'irlansa, men javobgar bo'lmayman, sizga ogohlantiraman!

en: Ha-ha-ha!” She laughed turning to Raskolnikov, and again nodding towards the landlady, in high glee at her sally.
uz: Ha-ha-ha! U Raskolnikovga qarab kulishdi va uy egasiga yana bosh ko'tardi.

en: “She didn’t understand, she didn’t understand again!
uz: U tushunmadi, yana tushunmadi!

en: Look how she sits with her mouth open!
uz: Qaranglar, u og'zini ochgan holda o'tiradi!

en: An owl in new ribbons, ha-ha-ha!” Here her laugh turned again to an insufferable fit of coughing that lasted five minutes.
uz: Yangi qo'shiqlarda bo'lgan g'uvuvon, ha-ha-ha! Bu yerda uning kulgi yana besh daqiqa davom etgan ko'tarishsiz qo'shqinchga aylandi.

en: Drops of perspiration stood out on her forehead and her handkerchief was stained with blood.
uz: Uning peshanasida ter tomlari paydo bo'ldi va uning to'pkasi qon bilan to'ldirilgan edi.

en: She showed Raskolnikov the blood in silence, and as soon as she could get her breath began whispering to him again with extreme animation and a hectic flush on her cheeks.
uz: U Raskolnikovga xotirjamlik bilan qon ko'rsatdi va nafas olishni boshlaganida, unga yana shov-shuv qila boshladi.

en: “Do you know, I gave her the most delicate instructions, so to speak, for inviting that lady and her daughter, you understand of whom I am speaking?
uz: Bilasizmi, men unga xonim va uning qizini taklif qilish uchun eng murakkab yo'l-yo'riqlarni berdim, shunday deyish mumkin, kim haqida gapirayotganimni tushunasizmi?

en: It needed the utmost delicacy, the greatest nicety, but she has managed things so that that fool, that conceited baggage, that provincial nonentity, simply because she is the widow of a major, and has come to try and get a pension and to fray out her skirts in the government offices, because at fifty she paints her face (everybody knows it) … a creature like that did not think fit to come, and has not even answered the invitation, which the most ordinary good manners required!
uz: Bu eng yaxshi mehribonlik va mehribonlik kerak edi, lekin u o'z vazifasini shunday bajardiki, o'sha ahmoq, o'zboshimcha bagaj, o'sha provinsiyalik noaniqlik, shunchaki o'zi majordorning bechori bo'lgani uchun va pensiyani olishga va hukumat ofislarida pishiradigan bo'ladi, chunki 50 yoshida u o'z yuzini bo'yashadi (barchasi buni biladi) ... bunday yaratilish kelishga munosib deb o'ylamadi va hatto taklifga javob ham bermadi, bu odatdagi eng yaxshi odoblar talab qiladi!

en: I can’t understand why Pyotr Petrovitch has not come?
uz: Nima uchun Pyotr Petrovitch kelmaganini tushunmayapman.

en: Ah, there she is at last!
uz: Ah, nihoyat u erda!

en: what is it, Sonia, where have you been?
uz: Nima bo'ldi, Sonia, qayerda bo'lding?

en: It’s odd that even at your father’s funeral you should be so unpunctual.
uz: O'zingizning otangizning dafnida ham o'zingizning vaqtingizni to'g'rilashingiz ajablanarli emas.

en: Romanovitch, make room for her beside you.
uz: Romanovitch, uning yonida joy toping.

en: That’s your place, Sonia … take what you like.
uz: Bu sizning joyingiz, Sonia... xohlaganingizni oling.

en: Have some of the cold entrée with jelly, that’s the best.
uz: Soyuqdan jelly bilan kiring, bu eng yaxshisi.

en: They’ll bring the pancakes directly.
uz: Ular pancakelarni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri olib kelishadi.

en: Have they given the children some?
uz: Ular bolalarga biroz berishganmi?

en: Polenka, have you got everything?
uz: Polenka, hamma narsangiz bormikin?

en: (Cough- cough-cough.) That’s all right.
uz: (Qo'shish-qushish-qushish) Bu yaxshi.

en: Be a good girl, Lida, and, Kolya, don’t fidget with your feet; sit like a little gentleman.
uz: Yaxshi qiz bo'ling, Lida, Kolya, oyoqlaringiz bilan o'tirmang, kichik bir gentleman kabi o'tiring.

en: What are you saying, Sonia?” Sonia hastened to give her Pyotr Petrovitch’s apologies, trying to speak loud enough for everyone to hear and carefully choosing the most respectful phrases which she attributed to Pyotr Petrovitch.
uz: Nima demoqchisiz, Sonia? Sonia Pyotr Petrovitchdan uzr so'rab, hamma eshitishi mumkin bo'lgan darajada baland ovoz bilan gapirishga harakat qildi va Pyotr Petrovitchga asoslangan eng hurmatli iboralarni diqqat bilan tanladi.

en: She added that Pyotr Petrovitch had particularly told her to say that, as soon as he possibly could, he would come immediately to discuss business alone with her and to consider what could be done for her, etc., etc.
uz: U qo'shimcha qilib aytdiki, Pyotr Petrovitch unga imkon boricha tezroq kelishini va u bilan yakka o'zi biznesni muhokama qilishini va u uchun nima qilish mumkinligini o'ylab ko'rishini aytishni aytdi.

en: Sonia knew that this would comfort Katerina Ivanovna, would flatter her and gratify her pride.
uz: Sonia bu Katerina Ivanovnaga tasalli berishini, uni maqtanishini va g'ururini qondirishini bilardi.

en: She sat down beside Raskolnikov; she made him a hurried bow, glancing curiously at him.
uz: U Raskolnikovning yonida o'tirib, unga shoshilinch bir qo'zg'olon berdi va qiziqarli tarzda unga qarab qo'ydi.

en: But for the rest of the time she seemed to avoid looking at him or speaking to him.
uz: Ammo qolgan vaqt davomida u unga qaramasdan yoki u bilan gaplashmasdan qochgan.

en: She seemed absentminded, though she kept looking at Katerina Ivanovna, trying to please her.
uz: Garchi u Katerina Ivanovnaga ko'z tikib, uni mamnun qilishga harakat qilgan bo'lsa-da, u aqldan ozgan ko'rinardi.

en: Neither she nor Katerina Ivanovna had been able to get mourning; Sonia was wearing dark brown, and Katerina Ivanovna had on her only dress, a dark striped cotton one.
uz: U ham, Katerina Ivanovna ham qayg'urishga muvaffaq bo'lmadilar; Sonia qorong'u qora rangli kiyim kiygan edi, Katerina Ivanovna esa yagona kiyim kiygan edi, bu qorong'u bo'lakli koton kiyim edi.

en: The message from Pyotr Petrovitch was very successful.
uz: Pyotr Petrovitchning xabarlari juda muvaffaqiyatli edi.

en: Listening to Sonia with dignity, Katerina Ivanovna inquired with equal dignity how Pyotr Petrovitch was, then at once whispered almost aloud to Raskolnikov that it certainly would have been strange for a man of Pyotr Petrovitch’s position and standing to find himself in such “extraordinary company,” in spite of his devotion to her family and his old friendship with her father.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna Soniaga hurmat bilan quloq solib, Pyotr Petrovitchning holati haqida ham o'z munosabati bilan so'radi, so'ngra Raskolnikovga deyarli ovoz chiqarib, Pyotr Petrovitchning o'rnagi va o'rnagiga ega bo'lgan kishi uchun o'zini bunday "ajralgan" jamiyatda topish, uning oilasiga bo'lgan sadoqati va otasi bilan eski do'stligiga qaramay, o'ziga g'alati tuyulishi mumkinligini aytdi.

en: “That’s why I am so grateful to you, Rodion Romanovitch, that you have not disdained my hospitality, even in such surroundings,” she added almost aloud.
uz: Shuning uchun men sizga juda minnatdorman, Rodion Romanovitch, chunki siz bunday muhitda ham, mehmondo'stligimga beparvo bo'lmagansiz, - deb qo'shimcha qildi u deyarli baland ovoz bilan.

en: “But I am sure that it was only your special affection for my poor husband that has made you keep your promise.” Then once more with pride and dignity she scanned her visitors, and suddenly inquired aloud across the table of the deaf man:
uz: Shundan so'ng u yana bir bor faxr va qadr-qimmat bilan tashrif buyuruvchilarini tekshirib ko'rdi va to'satdan kar odamning dasturxonida baland ovoz bilan so'radi:

en: “Wouldn’t he have some more meat, and had he been given some wine?” The old man made no answer and for a long while could not understand what he was asked, though his neighbours amused themselves by poking and shaking him.
uz: Qariya javob bermadi va uzoq vaqt davomida nima haqida so'raganini tushunmadi, garchi uning qo'shnilari uni tishlab qo'yib, qo'zg'atish bilan o'zlarini zavqlantirgan bo'lsa-da.

en: He simply gazed about him with his mouth open, which only increased the general mirth.
uz: U shunchaki og'zini ochgan holda atrofga qarab turardi, bu esa umuman quvonchni oshirdi.

en: But as to Pyotr Petrovitch, I always had confidence in him,” Katerina Ivanovna continued, “and, of course, he is not like …” with an extremely stern face she addressed Amalia Ivanovna so sharply and loudly that the latter was quite disconcerted, “not like your dressed up draggletails whom my father would not have taken as cooks into his kitchen, and my late husband would have done them honour if he had invited them in the goodness of his heart.” “Yes, he was fond of drink, he was fond of it, he did drink!” cried the commissariat clerk, gulping down his twelfth glass of vodka.
uz: Ammo Pyotr Petrovitchga kelsak, men unga doimo ishonardim, - dedi Katerina Ivanovna davom etib, - va, albatta, u ... juda qattiq yuz bilan Amaliya Ivanovnaga shunday keskin va baland ovoz bilan murojaat qildiki, u juda xafa bo'ldi, o'g'lim o'z oshxonasiga oshpaz sifatida otam qabul qilmagan kiyimli bo'g'imlaringiz kabi emas, va marhum erim ularni yaxshi ko'rganida hurmat qilgan bo'lardi.Ha, u ichishni yoqtirgan, yoqtirgan, ichgan! Komisariat vakili o'zining o'n ikkinchi shisha vodkasini yutib yubordi.

en: “My late husband certainly had that weakness, and everyone knows it,” Katerina Ivanovna attacked him at once, “but he was a kind and honourable man, who loved and respected his family.
uz: Erimning o'sha zaifligi bor edi va bu hammaga ma'lum, Katerina Ivanovna unga darhol hujum qildi, lekin u mehribon va hurmatli odam edi, u oilasini yaxshi ko'rgan va hurmat qilgan.

en: The worst of it was his good nature made him trust all sorts of disreputable people, and he drank with fellows who were not worth the sole of his shoe.
uz: Eng yomoni, uning yaxshi tabiati unga barcha nojo'ya odamlarga ishonishga sabab bo'lgan va u o'z poyabzaliga ham yaramas bo'lgan odamlar bilan ichardi.

en: Would you believe it, Rodion Romanovitch, they found a gingerbread cock in his pocket; he was dead drunk, but he did not forget the children!” “A cock?
uz: Ishonasizmi, Rodion Romanovitch, uning kiyimida gingerbread sherigi topildi; u o'lib mast edi, lekin bolalarni unutmadi!Sherigi?

en: Did you say a cock?” shouted the commissariat clerk.
uz: Siz pichoq deganmisiz? - deb baqirdi komisariat xodimi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna did not vouchsafe a reply.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna javob bermadi.

en: She sighed, lost in thought.
uz: O'y-xayolida g'oyib bo'lib, o'zi g'oyib bo'ldi.

en: “No doubt you think, like everyone, that I was too severe with him,” she went on, addressing Raskolnikov.
uz: Shubhasizki, siz ham hamma singari, men ham unga nisbatan juda qat'iy bo'lganimni o'ylaysiz, deb aytdi u Raskolnikovga murojaat qilib.

en: He respected me, he respected me very much!
uz: U meni hurmat qilardi, juda ham hurmat qilardi!

en: He was a kindhearted man!
uz: U mehribon odam edi!

en: And how sorry I was for him sometimes!
uz: Ba'zan men uning uchun juda achinar edim!

en: He would sit in a corner and look at me, I used to feel so sorry for him, I used to want to be kind to him and then would think to myself: ‘Be kind to him and he will drink again,’ it was only by severity that you could keep him within bounds.” “Yes, he used to get his hair pulled pretty often,” roared the commissariat clerk again, swallowing another glass of vodka.
uz: U burchada o'tirib menga qarab turardi, men uning uchun juda achinar edim, men unga mehribon bo'lishni xohlardim va keyin o'zimga shunday deb o'ylardim: Uga mehribon bo'ling va u yana ichadi, uni faqat qat'iylik tufayli cheklovlar ichida ushlab turish mumkin edi. Ha, u sochlarini tez-tez tortib olishardi, komisariat xodimi yana qichqirdi va yana bir stakan vodka yutib oldi.

en: “Some fools would be the better for a good drubbing, as well as having their hair pulled.
uz: Ba'zi ahmoqlar yaxshi sochlarni to'kib tashlash uchun, shuningdek, sochlarini tortib olish uchun yaxshiroq bo'lishadi.

en: I am not talking of my late husband now!” Katerina Ivanovna snapped at him.
uz: Men endi marhum erim haqida gapirmayapman! Katerina Ivanovna unga qattiq urildi.

en: The flush on her cheeks grew more and more marked, her chest heaved.
uz: Uning yig'inlarida ko'tarilgan ko'kraklar ko'proq va ko'proq ko'rindi, ko'kraklari ko'tarildi.

en: In another minute she would have been ready to make a scene.
uz: Yana bir daqiqadan so'ng, u o'z o'rnini ishga tushirishga tayyor bo'lardi.

en: Many of the visitors were sniggering, evidently delighted.
uz: Ko'pgina tashrif buyuruvchilar shov-shuv qilib, ko'rinib turibdiki, xursand edilar.

en: They began poking the commissariat clerk and whispering something to him.
uz: Ular komissariat xodimiga urib, unga biror narsa shoshlashni boshlashdi.

en: They were evidently trying to egg him on.
uz: Ular, ehtimol, uni o'g'irlab yubormoqchi edilar.

en: “Allow me to ask what are you alluding to,” began the clerk, “that is to say, whose … about whom … did you say just now … But I don’t care!
uz: Siz nimaga ishora qilyapsiz deb so'rasam bo'ladi, - deb boshladi ma'ruzachi, ya'ni, kimning ... kim haqida ... siz hali-ya'ni aytdingiz ... lekin men o'zimni qiziqtirmayman!

en: … Pass!” And he took another drink of vodka.
uz: ... O'tish! Va u yana bir vodka ichdi.

en: Raskolnikov sat in silence, listening with disgust.
uz: Raskolnikov sukut saqlashda o'tirib, jirkanchlik bilan tinglagan.

en: He only ate from politeness, just tasting the food that Katerina Ivanovna was continually putting on his plate, to avoid hurting her feelings.
uz: U faqat xushmuomalalik bilan ovqatlanardi, faqat Katerina Ivanovna o'z taomlariga doimiy ravishda qo'ygan ovqatni tanovul qildi, uning his-tuyg'ularini jarohatlamaslik uchun.

en: He watched Sonia intently.
uz: U Soniaga diqqat bilan qarab turardi.

en: But Sonia became more and more anxious and distressed; she, too, foresaw that the dinner would not end peaceably, and saw with terror Katerina Ivanovna’s growing irritation.
uz: Lekin Sonia tashvish va xavotirga to'lib-toshdi; u ham kechki ovqatning tinch yakunlanmasligini ko'rib, Katerina Ivanovna ning g'azabini ko'targanida qo'rquvga tushdi.

en: She knew that she, Sonia, was the chief reason for the “genteel” ladies’ contemptuous treatment of Katerina Ivanovna’s invitation.
uz: U, Sonia, Katerina Ivanovna taklifini hurmatsizlik bilan qabul qilishining asosiy sababi ekanligini bilardi.

en: She had heard from Amalia Ivanovna that the mother was positively offended at the invitation and had asked the question: “How could she let her daughter sit down beside that young person?” Sonia had a feeling that Katerina Ivanovna had already heard this and an insult to Sonia meant more to Katerina Ivanovna than an insult to herself, her children, or her father, Sonia knew that Katerina Ivanovna would not be satisfied now, “till she had shown those draggletails that they were both …” To make matters worse someone passed Sonia, from the other end of the table, a plate with two hearts pierced with an arrow, cut out of black bread.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna onasi taklifdan rosa xafa bo'lganini eshitib, savol berdi: Qizini bu yosh odamning yonida qanday o'tirtirishga ruxsat berishi mumkin? Sonia Katerina Ivanovna buni eshitganini his qilgan va Soniaga qilingan haqorat o'ziga, bolalariga yoki otasiga qilingan haqoratdan ko'ra Katerina Ivanovna uchun ko'proq ahamiyatga ega edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna flushed crimson and at once said aloud across the table that the man who sent it was “a drunken ass!” Amalia Ivanovna was foreseeing something amiss, and at the same time deeply wounded by Katerina Ivanovna’s haughtiness, and to restore the good-humour of the company and raise herself in their esteem she began, apropos of nothing, telling a story about an acquaintance of hers “Karl from the chemist’s,” who was driving one
uz: Katerina Ivanovna qizil rangni ko'tarib, uni yuborgan kishi mast o'g'il ekanligini oshkora qilib aytdi! Amaliya Ivanovna noto'g'ri narsani ko'rib, Katerina Ivanovna mag'rurligidan chuqur jarohatlangan edi va kompaniyaning xushmuomalaligini tiklash va o'zini ularning hurmatida ko'tarish uchun u hech narsa haqida gapirmay, kimyoviy mashinada o'tirgan uning tanishlari Karl haqida hikoya qilishni boshladi.

en: night in a cab, and that “the cabman wanted him to kill, and Karl very much begged him not to kill, and wept and clasped hands, and frightened and from fear pierced his heart.” Though Katerina Ivanovna smiled, she observed at once that Amalia Ivanovna ought not to tell anecdotes in Russian; the latter was still more offended, and she retorted that her “Vater aus Berlin was a very important man, and always went with his hands in pockets.” Katerina Ivanovna could not restrain herself and laughed so much that Amalia Ivanovna lost patience and could scarcely control herself.
uz: O'zini taksiga olib bormoqchi edi, Karl esa uni o'ldirmaslikka iltijo qilib, yig'lab qo'lini to'pladi va qo'rqib yuragini o'rab oldi. Katerina Ivanovna tabassum qilgan bo'lsa-da, Amaliya Ivanovna rus tilida anekdotlarni aytib bermasligi kerakligini darhol ko'rdi; bu ayol bundan ham ko'proq xafa bo'ldi va uning "Vater aus Berlin" juda muhim odam ekanligini va har doim o'z qo'llarini to'plamaganini aytdi. Katerina Ivanovna o'zini tuta olmagan va juda ko'p kulgan, hatto Amaliya Ivanovna sabr-toqatni yo'qotdi va o'zini nazorat qila olmadi.

en: “Listen to the owl!” Katerina Ivanovna whispered at once, her good-humour almost restored, “she meant to say he kept his hands in his pockets, but she said he put his hands in people’s pockets.
uz: Katerina Ivonovna shu zahoti shovqin qildi, uning xushmuomalaligi deyarli tiklandi, u o'z qo'llarini odamlarning qoshiqlariga qo'yib qo'yganini aytmoqchi edi, lekin u qo'llarini odamlarning qoshiqlariga qo'yganini aytdi.

en: (Cough-cough.) And have you noticed, Rodion Romanovitch, that all these Petersburg foreigners, the Germans especially, are all stupider than we!
uz: (Qo'sh-ko'sh) Va siz, Rodion Romanovitch, ko'rib chiqdingizmi, bu barcha Sankt-Peterburg chet elliklari, ayniqsa nemislar bizdan ham ahmoqroq!

en: Can you fancy anyone of us telling how ‘Karl from the chemist’s’ ‘pierced his heart from fear’ and that the idiot, instead of punishing the cabman, ‘clasped his hands and wept, and much begged.’ Ah, the fool!
uz: Bizlardan kim o'ylab ko'rsa bo'ladi, kimyoviy kimyoviy Karlning qo'rquvdan yuragini teshganini va bu g'alati odam taksi haydovchisini jazolashning o'rniga qo'llarini qo'yib yig'laganini va ko'p so'raganini aytib beryapti.

en: And you know she fancies it’s very touching and does not suspect how stupid she is!
uz: Va siz bilamanki, u bu juda hayajonli va u qanchalik ahmoq ekanligiga shubha qilmaydi!

en: To my thinking that drunken commissariat clerk is a great deal cleverer, anyway one can see that he has addled his brains with drink, but you know, these foreigners are always so well behaved and serious.
uz: O'ylaymanki, mast bo'lgan komisariat xodimi ko'proq aqlli bo'ladi, shunga qaramay, u o'z miyalarini ichimlik bilan o'zgartirganini ko'rish mumkin, ammo bilasizmi, bu chet elliklar har doim yaxshi xulq-atvorli va jiddiy.

en: … Look how she sits glaring!
uz: Qaranglar, u qanday o'tirganini ko'ringlar!

en: She is angry, ha-ha!
uz: U g'azablangan, ha-ha!

en: (Cough-cough-cough.)” Regaining her good-humour, Katerina Ivanovna began at once telling Raskolnikov that when she had obtained her pension, she intended to open a school for the daughters of gentlemen in her native town T — —.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna o'z humorini tiklab, Raskolnikovga pensiyani olganidan so'ng o'z shaharchasida xudojo'ylarning qizlari uchun maktab ochishni rejalashtirganini aytishni boshladi.

en: This was the first time she had spoken to him of the project, and she launched out into the most alluring details.
uz: Bu u bilan loyiha haqida birinchi marta gapirganida edi va u eng jozibali tafsilotlarga kirib keldi.

en: It suddenly appeared that Katerina Ivanovna had in her hands the very certificate of honour of which Marmeladov had spoken to Raskolnikov in the tavern, when he told him that Katerina Ivanovna, his wife, had danced the shawl dance before the governor and other great personages on leaving school.
uz: Toʻsatdan, Katerina Ivanovna qoʻlida Marmeladov oʻz tavernasida Raskolnikov bilan suhbatlashgan faxriy guvohnomani olib, uning rafiqasi Katerina Ivanovna maktabdan chiqqanida gubernator va boshqa buyuk kishilar oldida shawl raqsini raqsga tushirganini aytdi.

en: This certificate of honour was obviously intended now to prove Katerina Ivanovna’s right to open a boarding-school; but she had armed herself with it chiefly with the object of overwhelming “those two stuck-up draggletails” if they came to the dinner, and proving incontestably that Katerina Ivanovna
uz: Ushbu faxriy sertifikat, albatta, Katerina Ivanovna internat maktabini ochish huquqini isbotlash maqsadida berilgan edi; lekin u o'zi bilan o'zini asosiy maqsad bilan qurollangan edi, agar ular kechki ovqatga kelishsa, o'sha ikki to'xtatilgan tirnoqlarni g'alaba qozonish va Katerina Ivanovna o'zini shubhasiz qo'lga kiritganini isbotlash.

en: was of the most noble, “she might even say aristocratic family, a colonel’s daughter and was far superior to certain adventuresses who have been so much to the fore of late.” The certificate of honour immediately passed into the hands of the drunken guests, and Katerina Ivanovna did not try to retain it, for it actually contained the statement en toutes lettres, that her father was of the rank of a major, and also a companion of an order, so that she really was almost the daughter of a colonel.
uz: U hatto aristokrat oilasining eng buyuk, deb aytish mumkin, polkovnikning qizi edi va oxirgi kunlarda juda ko'p birinchi o'rinni egallagan ba'zi sayohatchi ayollardan ancha ustun bo'lgan. Sharaf guvohnomasi darhol mast mehmonlarning qo'liga o'tdi va Katerina Ivanovna uni saqlab qolishga harakat qilmadi, chunki u aslida otasining majordor darajasidagi, shuningdek, ordenning hamkori bo'lganligi haqidagi barcha xatlardagi bayonotni o'z ichiga olgan edi, shuning uchun u haqiqatan ham polkovnikning qizi deyarli edi.

en: Warming up, Katerina Ivanovna proceeded to enlarge on the peaceful and happy life they would lead in T — —, on the gymnasium teachers whom she would engage to give lessons in her boarding- school, one a most respectable old Frenchman, one Mangot, who had taught Katerina Ivanovna herself in old days and was still living in T — —, and would no doubt teach in her school on moderate terms.
uz: Issiq bo'lib, Katerina Ivanovna T   da o'tkazadigan tinch va baxtli hayot, internatida dars berishga yollaydigan gimnaziya o'qituvchilari, eng hurmatli keksa frantsuz, eski kunlarda Katerina Ivanovna o'ziga o'rgatgan va hali ham T   da yashaydigan Mangot o'qituvchilari, shubhasiz, o'z maktabida o'rta darajada o'rgatadigan o'qituvchilari haqida ko'proq ma'lumot berdi.

en: Next she spoke of Sonia who would go with her to T — — and help her in all her plans.
uz: Keyingi marta u Sonia haqida gapirdi, u u bilan birga Tga boradi va barcha rejalarida unga yordam beradi.

en: At this someone at the further end of the table gave a sudden guffaw.
uz: Shu bilan birga, stolning o'ng tomoniga o'tirgan kimdir to'satdan g'ofil qildi.

en: Though Katerina Ivanovna tried to appear to be disdainfully unaware of it, she raised her voice and began at once speaking with conviction of Sonia’s undoubted ability to assist her, of “her gentleness, patience, devotion, generosity and good education,” tapping Sonia on the cheek and kissing her warmly twice.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna bu haqda g'azablantirib o'ylamagan ko'rinishga harakat qilgan bo'lsa-da, ovozini ko'tardi va Sonia unga yordam berish qobiliyatiga ishonib gapira boshladi, uning muloyimligi, sabr-toqat, sadoqati, saxiyligi va yaxshi ta'lim-tarbiyaga ega bo'lganligi haqida, Soniaga tungiga tegib, ikki marta iliq o'pdi.

en: Sonia flushed crimson, and Katerina Ivanovna suddenly burst into tears, immediately observing that she was “nervous and silly, that she was too much upset, that it was time to finish, and as the dinner was over, it was time to hand round the tea.” At that moment, Amalia Ivanovna, deeply aggrieved at taking no part in the conversation, and not being listened to, made one last effort, and with secret misgivings ventured on an exceedingly deep and weighty observation, that “in the future boarding-school she would have to pay particular attention to die Wäsche, and that there certainly must be a good dame to look after the linen, and secondly that the young ladies must not novels at night read.” Katerina Ivanovna, who certainly was upset and very tired, as well as heartily sick of the dinner, at once cut short Amalia Ivanovna, saying “she knew nothing about it and was talking nonsense, that
uz: Sonia qizil rangga tushdi va Katerina Ivanovna darhol ko'z yoshlariga tushib ketdi, u darhol o'zining g'alati va g'alati ekanligini, juda xafa bo'lganini, o'z vaqtida to'xtatish vaqti kelganini va kechki ovqat tugaganida, choyni o'tkazishga vaqt keldi. O'sha paytda suhbatda ishtirok etmaganidan va tinglanmaganidan juda xafa bo'lgan Amaliya Ivanovna so'nggi bir sa'y-harakat qildi va yashirin shubhalar bilan juda chuqur va og'ir e'tiborga tushdi, kelajakdagi internatda u Väsche o'lishiga alohida e'tibor qaratishi kerakligini va chiroyli kiyimni boqadigan yaxshi bir xonim bo'lishi kerakligini va ikkinchi navbatda, qizlar kechqurun roman o'qimaganligini bilishi kerakligini ko'rdi. Katerina Ivanovna xafa bo'ldi va hech narsa juda chiroyli va chiroyli emas edi, chunki u ham kasal bo'lishi kerak edi, chunki u bir marta kechki ovqatni kesib tashlagan va bu gaplarni aytgan Amaliya Ivanovna bir marta gapirgan edi.

en: it was the business of the laundry maid, and not of the directress of a
uz: Bu ish kiyim-kechak xizmatkori bilan bog'liq edi, balki bir uy direktori bilan bog'liq emas edi.

en: high-class boarding-school to look after die Wäsche, and as for novel-reading, that was simply rudeness, and she begged her to be silent.” Amalia Ivanovna fired up and getting angry observed that she only “meant her good,” and that “she had meant her very good,” and that “it was long since she had paid her gold for the lodgings.” Katerina Ivanovna at once “set her down,” saying that it was a lie to say she wished her good, because only yesterday when her dead husband was lying on the table, she had worried her about the lodgings.
uz: Väschega g'amxo'rlik qilish va romanlarni o'qish uchun o'rinli internat maktabi, bu shunchaki qo'pollik edi va u undan so'z aytmaslikni iltimos qildi. Amaliya Ivanovna o'zini ko'tardi va g'azabga tushdi, chunki u faqat o'z yaxshiligini xohlaganini, va o'zining juda yaxshiligini xohlaganini, va uzoq vaqtdan beri uy uchun oltin to'laganini ko'rdi. Katerina Ivanovna uni darhol o'tirib qo'ydi, uning yaxshiligini xohlaganini aytish yolg'on ekanligini aytdi, chunki faqat kecha o'lim eri stol ustida yotganda, u uy haqida tashvishlanardi.

en: To this Amalia Ivanovna very appropriately observed that she had invited those ladies, but “those ladies had not come, because those ladies are ladies and cannot come to a lady who is not a lady.” Katerina Ivanovna at once pointed out to her, that as she was a slut she could not judge what made one really a lady.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna bu ayollarni taklif qilganini, lekin ular kelmaganini aniq ko'rdi, chunki bu ayollar ayollar va ayol emas ayolga kelishi mumkin emas.Katerina Ivanovna unga darhol shuni ta'kidladiki, u bir kaltak bo'lgani uchun odamni ayolni nima qilganini o'ylay olmaydi.

en: Amalia Ivanovna at once declared that her “Vater aus Berlin was a very, very important man, and both hands in pockets went, and always used to say: ‘Poof!
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna darhol uning Berlinlik Vater juda muhim odam ekanligini va har ikki qo'lini ham to'plamga olganini va har doim: Poof! deb aytganini e'lon qildi.

en: poof!’ ” and she leapt up from the table to represent her father, sticking her hands in her pockets, puffing her cheeks, and uttering vague sounds resembling “poof!
uz: va u o'z otasini ifoda etish uchun stoldan ko'tarildi, qo'llarini kiyimlariga qo'yib, yig'ini puflab, pufga o'xshaydigan noaniq tovushlarni chiqardi!

en: poof!” amid loud laughter from all the lodgers, who purposely encouraged Amalia Ivanovna, hoping for a fight.
uz: Barcha uy egalarining katta kulgi o'rtasida, Amaliya Ivanovnaga qasddan kurashga umidvorlik bilan dalda berganlar.

en: But this was too much for Katerina Ivanovna, and she at once declared, so that all could hear, that Amalia Ivanovna probably never had a father, but was simply a drunken Petersburg Finn, and had certainly once been a cook and probably something worse.
uz: Ammo bu Katerina Ivanovna uchun juda ko'p edi va u hammaning eshitishi uchun, Amaliya Ivanovna, ehtimol, hech qachon otasi bo'lmagan, balki shunchaki mast bo'lgan Peterburg Finlandiyasi bo'lganini va bir vaqtlar oshpaz bo'lganini va ehtimol bundan ham og'irroq bo'lganini darhol e'lon qildi.

en: Amalia Ivanovna turned as red as a lobster and squealed that perhaps Katerina Ivanovna never had a father, “but she had a Vater aus Berlin and that he wore a long coat and always said poof-poof-poof!” Katerina Ivanovna observed contemptuously that all knew what her family was and that on that very certificate of honour it was stated in print that her father was a colonel, while Amalia Ivanovna’s father —if she really had one —was probably some Finnish milkman, but that probably she never had a father at all, since it was still uncertain whether her name was Amalia Ivanovna or Amalia Ludwigovna.
uz: Amaliya Ivanovna qo'rqinch kabi qizildi va, ehtimol, Katerina Ivanovna hech qachon otasi bo'lmagan, lekin u bor edi, bir Vater aus Berlin va u uzun kiyim kiygan va har doim poof-poof-poof deb aytgan! Katerina Ivanovna har kim uning oilasi nima ekanligini biladi va shu faxriy guvohnomada uning otasi polkovnik, Amaliya Ivanovna otasining otasi bo'lsa, ehtimol, bir finlik sutxo'r bo'lgan, lekin u hech qachon otasiga ega bo'lmagan, chunki uning ismi Amaliya Ivanovna yoki Amaliya Ludovna ekanligi hali ham noma'lum edi.

en: At this Amalia Ivanovna, lashed to fury, struck the table with her fist, and shrieked that she was Amalia Ivanovna, and not Ludwigovna, “that her Vater was named Johann and that he was a
uz: Shunda Amaliya Ivanovna g'azabga to'lib, o'z qo'lidan dasturxonni urdi va u o'zi Ludwigovna emas, balki Amaliya Ivanovna ekanligini, otasining ismi Johann ekanligini va uning o'g'li o'g'il ekanligini aytdi.

en: burgomeister, and that Katerina Ivanovna’s Vater was quite never a burgomeister.” Katerina Ivanovna rose from her chair, and with a stern and apparently calm voice (though she was pale and her chest was heaving) observed that “if she dared for one moment to set her contemptible wretch of a father on a level with her papa, she, Katerina Ivanovna, would tear her cap off her head and trample it under foot.” Amalia Ivanovna ran about the room, shouting at the top of her voice, that she was mistress of the house and that Katerina Ivanovna should leave the lodgings that minute; then she rushed for some reason to collect the silver spoons from the table.
