uz: Ular hech qachon bunday qilmaydilar. Va u Sonia haqida o'yladi.

en: There was a breath of fresh air from the window.
uz: Dushmanning tovuqlari chiroqdan chiqdi.

en: The daylight was fading.
uz: Kundagi yorug'lik yo'q bo'lib ketayotgan edi.

en: He took up his cap and went out.
uz: O'zining to'pqini ko'tarib, tashqariga chiqdi.

en: He could not, of course, and would not consider how ill he was.
uz: Albatta, u o'zining kasalligini ko'rib chiqolmadi va o'ylamaydi.

en: But all this continual anxiety and agony of mind could not but affect him.
uz: Ammo bu doimiy tashvishlar va ong og'rig'i unga ta'sir qilib turardi.

en: And if he were not lying in high fever it was perhaps just because this continual inner strain helped to keep him on his legs
uz: Va agar u yuqori issiqlikda yotgan bo'lmagan bo'lsa, ehtimol, bu doimiy ichki bosim uni oyoqlari ustida ushlab turishga yordam berganligi uchun edi.

en: and in possession of his faculties.
uz: va o'z qobiliyatlariga ega bo'lgan.

en: But this artificial excitement could not last long.
uz: Ammo bu sun'iy hayajon uzoq davom etmadi.

en: He wandered aimlessly.
uz: U maqsadsiz yo'ldan ozdi.

en: The sun was setting.
uz: Quyosh botayotgan edi.

en: A special form of misery had begun to oppress him of late.
uz: Oxirgi paytlarda uni kamsitishning o'ziga xos turi boshlangan edi.

en: There was nothing poignant, nothing acute about it; but there was a feeling of permanence, of eternity about it; it brought a foretaste of hopeless years of this cold leaden misery, a foretaste of an eternity “on a square yard of space.” Towards evening this sensation usually began to weigh on him more heavily.
uz: Bu yerda hech narsa o'ziga xos emas, hech narsa o'ziga xos emas edi; lekin bu erda doimiylik, abadiylik hissi paydo bo'lgan; bu bu sovuq la'nat azob-uqubatining umidsiz yillarining dastlabki tadmini keltirib chiqardi, bir kvadrat metr maydonda abadiylik tadmini keltirib chiqardi. Kechaga kelib, bu hissiyot odatda u uchun og'irroq bo'ldi.

en: “With this idiotic, purely physical weakness, depending on the sunset or something, one can’t help doing something stupid!
uz: Bu ahmoqona, sof jismoniy zaiflik bilan, quyosh botishi yoki boshqa narsalarga bog'liq bo'lgan holda, biror ahmoqona ish qilishdan qochish mumkin emas!

en: You’ll go to Dounia, as well as to Sonia,” he muttered bitterly.
uz: Siz Douniaga, shuningdek, Soniaga borasiz, - dedi u og'irlik bilan.

en: He heard his name called.
uz: O'z ismini eshitdi.

en: Lebeziatnikov rushed up to him.
uz: Lebeziatnikov unga yaqinlashdi.

en: “Only fancy, I’ve been to your room looking for you.
uz: Just fancy, Men sizning xonangizda sizni qidirib kelganman.

en: Only fancy, she’s carried out her plan, and taken away the children.
uz: U faqat o'ziga xos fikrda bo'lib, o'z rejasiga amal qildi va bolalarni olib ketdi.

en: Sofya Semyonovna and I have had a job to find them.
uz: Sofiya Semyonovna va men ularni topish uchun ish topdik.

en: She is rapping on a frying-pan and making the children dance.
uz: U pishirish panida rap qilmoqda va bolalarni raqsga chorlamoqda.

en: The children are crying.
uz: Bolalar yig'lab yuribdi.

en: They keep stopping at the crossroads and in front of shops; there’s a crowd of fools running after them.
uz: Ular yo'l chekkasida va do'konlar oldida to'xtab turishadi; ularning orqasidan ahmoqlar to'plami yugurib bormoqda.

en: Come along!” “And Sonia?” Raskolnikov asked anxiously, hurrying after Lebeziatnikov.
uz: Kelinglar!  And Sonia? Raskolnikov tashvish bilan so'radi va Lebeziatnikovga shoshilmoqda.

en: That is, it’s not Sofya Semyonovna’s frantic, but Katerina Ivanovna, though Sofya Semyonova’s frantic too.
uz: Demak, Sofiya Semyonovna g'ayritabiiy emas, balki Katerina Ivanovna g'ayritabiiy, ammo Sofiya Semyonova ham g'ayritabiiy.

en: But Katerina Ivanovna is absolutely frantic.
uz: Ammo Katerina Ivanovna mutlaqo g'ayritabiiy.

en: I tell you she is quite mad.
uz: Sizga aytamanki, u juda g'alati.

en: They’ll be taken to the police.
uz: Ular politsiyaga olib ketiladi.

en: You can fancy what an effect that will have.
uz: Bu qanday ta'sir qilishi mumkinligini tasavvur qila olasiz.

en: … They are on the canal bank, near the bridge now, not far from Sofya Semyonovna’s, quite close.” On the canal bank near the bridge and not two houses away from the one where Sonia lodged, there was a crowd of people, consisting principally of gutter children.
uz: Ular kanal qirg'og'ida, ko'prik yaqinida, Sofya Semyonovnasdan uzoq emas, juda yaqin. Ko'prik yaqinidagi kanal qirg'og'ida va Sonia yashagan uydan ikki uy uzoqlikda, odamlar ko'p bo'lib, asosan qirg'oqchi bolalardan iborat edi.

en: The hoarse broken voice of Katerina Ivanovna could be heard from the bridge, and it certainly was a strange spectacle likely to attract a street crowd.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna ning qichqiriq ovozini ko'prikdan eshitish mumkin edi va bu, albatta, ko'chaga ko'pchilikni jalb qiladigan g'ayritabiiy spektakl edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna in her old dress with the green shawl, wearing a torn straw hat, crushed in a hideous way on one side, was really frantic.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna o'zining eski kiyimida, yashil shali bilan, yirtilgan palka to'pkasi bilan, bir tomondan dahshatli tarzda ezib tashlangan, haqiqatan ham g'alati edi.

en: She was exhausted and breathless.
uz: U charchagan va nafassiz edi.

en: Her wasted consumptive face looked more suffering than ever, and indeed out of doors in the sunshine a
uz: Uning yo'q qilingan iste'molchilik yuzida har qachongidan ko'ra ko'proq azob chekayotgan edi va hatto quyosh nurida eshikdan tashqariga chiqardi.

en: consumptive always looks worse than at home.
uz: Iste'molchilar uyda bo'lganidan ham yomon ko'rinadi.

en: But her excitement did not flag, and every moment her irritation grew more intense.
uz: Ammo uning hayajonlari ko'tarilmadi va har bir daqiqada g'azablari kuchayib borardi.

en: She rushed at the children, shouted at them, coaxed them, told them before the crowd how to dance and what to sing, began explaining to them why it was necessary, and driven to desperation by their not understanding, beat them.
uz: U bolalarga yugurib, qichqirdi, ularni ishontirdi, ko'pchilik oldida qanday raqs o'ynash va nimani kuylash kerakligini ularga aytib berdi, nima uchun bu kerakligini tushuntirib berdi va ularning tushunmovchiligi tufayli umidsizlikka uchratib, ularni urdi.

en: … Then she would make a rush at the crowd; if she noticed any decently dressed person stopping to look, she immediately appealed to him to see what these children “from a genteel, one may say aristocratic, house” had been brought to.
uz: Keyin u xaloyiqqa shovqinlik qilardi; agar munosib kiyim kiygan odamni to'xtatib ko'rishni ko'rsa, darhol unga murojaat qilib, bu bolalarni o'zgacha aristokratik uydan nimaga olib kelishganini ko'rishni so'radi.

en: If she heard laughter or jeering in the crowd, she would rush at once at the scoffers and begin squabbling with them.
uz: Agar u xaloyiqda kulish yoki masxara qilishni eshitsa, u darhol masxarachilarga shovqin qilib, ular bilan bahslashishni boshlaydi.

en: Some people laughed, others shook their heads, but everyone felt curious at the sight of the madwoman with the frightened children.
uz: Ba'zilar kulishdi, ba'zilar boshlarini silkitdilar, lekin hamma qo'rqqan bolalari bilan aqldan ozgan ayolni ko'rib hayron bo'ldi.

en: The frying-pan of which Lebeziatnikov had spoken was not there, at least Raskolnikov did not see it.
uz: Lebeziatnikov gapirgan pishirish pishi u yerda yo'q edi, hech bo'lmaganda Raskolnikov uni ko'rmagan.

en: But instead of rapping on the pan, Katerina Ivanovna began clapping her wasted hands, when she made Lida and Kolya dance and Polenka sing.
uz: Ammo Katerina Ivanovna panada raplashning o'rniga, Lida va Kolyani raqsga tushirib, Polenka qo'shiq kuylagani uchun o'z qo'llarini tatib qo'yishni boshladi.

en: She too joined in the singing, but broke down at the second note with a fearful cough, which made her curse in despair and even shed tears.
uz: U ham qo'shiq kuylashga qo'shildi, lekin ikkinchi nota bilan qo'rqqan ko'tarildi, bu esa uni tushkunlikka tushirdi va hatto ko'z yoshlarini to'kdi.

en: What made her most furious was the weeping and terror of Kolya and Lida.
uz: Uni eng g'azablantirgan narsa Kolya va Lidaning yig'lashlari va dahshatlari edi.

en: Some effort had been made to dress the children up as street singers are dressed.
uz: Bolalarni ko'cha qo'shiqchilari kiygan kiyimga kiyish uchun ba'zi sa'y-harakatlar amalga oshirildi.

en: The boy had on a turban made of something red and white to look like a Turk.
uz: O'g'il Turkga o'xshaydigan qizil-oq narsalardan yasalgan turband kiyib olgan edi.

en: There had been no costume for Lida; she simply had a red knitted cap, or rather a night cap that had belonged to Marmeladov, decorated with a broken piece of white ostrich feather, which had been Katerina Ivanovna’s grandmother’s and had been preserved as a family possession.
uz: Lida uchun kostyum yo'q edi; u shunchaki qizil tikilgan to'pka yoki, ko'proq aytganda, Marmeladovga tegishli bo'lgan kechki to'pka bilan bezatilgan, bu Katerina Ivanovna bobosi bo'lgan oq ostrich fe'ridan bo'lgan va oilaviy mulk sifatida saqlangan.

en: Polenka was in her everyday dress; she looked in timid perplexity at her mother, and kept at her side, hiding her tears.
uz: Polenka kundalik kiyimida edi; u o'z onasiga qo'rqqancha qaradi va ko'z yoshlarini yashirib, uning yonida turadi.

en: She dimly realised her mother’s condition, and looked uneasily about her.
uz: U o'z onasining holatini kamdan-kam tushunib, uni tashvishlanib ko'rdi.

en: She was terribly frightened of the street and the crowd.
uz: U ko'cha va xaloyiqdan juda qo'rqardi.

en: Sonia followed Katerina Ivanovna, weeping and beseeching her to return home, but Katerina Ivanovna was not to be persuaded.
uz: Sonia Katerina Ivanovna orqasidan yurib, yig'lab, uyiga qaytib kelishini iltijo qildi, lekin Katerina Ivanovna bunga rozi bo'lmadi.

en: “Leave off, Sonia, leave off,” she shouted, speaking fast, panting and coughing.
uz: Chet, Sonia, ket, ket, u qichqirib, tez gapirib, nafas olib, qo'shiq chiqardi.

en: “You don’t know what you ask; you are like a child!
uz: Siz nima so'rayotganingizni bilmaysiz; siz bola kabisiz!

en: I’ve told you before that I am not coming back to that drunken German.
uz: Men sizga avval ham aytgan edimki, men o'sha mast nemis odamga qaytib kelmayman.

en: Let everyone, let all Petersburg see the children begging in the streets, though their father was an honourable man who served
uz: Har kim, butun Sankt-Peterburgda bolalar ko'chalarda yolvorib ko'rsin, garchi ularning otasi xizmat qilgan sharafli kishi bo'lsa ham.

en: all his life in truth and fidelity, and one may say died in the service.” (Katerina Ivanovna had by now invented this fantastic story and thoroughly believed it.) “Let that wretch of a general see it!
uz: Uning butun hayoti haqiqat va sadoqatda bo'lib, xizmatda o'lgan deb aytsa bo'ladi. (Katerina Ivanovna bu ajoyib hikoyani o'ylab topib, unga to'liq ishonib qolgan edi.) O'sha qashshoq general uni ko'rsin!

en: And you are silly, Sonia: what have we to eat?
uz: Siz esa ahmoqsiz, Sonia: biz nima yeymiz?

en: We have worried you enough, I won’t go on so!
uz: Biz sizni etarlicha tashvishlantirganmiz, men bundan buyon ham bunday qilmayman!

en: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch, is that you?” she cried, seeing Raskolnikov and rushing up to him.
uz: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch, bu senmi? Raskolnikovni ko'rib, yig'ladi va unga yugurib bordi.

en: “Explain to this silly girl, please, that nothing better could be done!
uz: Bu ahmoq qizga, iltimos, bundan yaxshiroq narsa yo'qligini tushuntiring!

en: Even organ- grinders earn their living, and everyone will see at once that we are different, that we are an honourable and bereaved family reduced to beggary.
uz: Hatto organ-milliyerlar ham rizq-ro'z olishadi va hamma bizdan farq qilayotganimizni, o'zimizni begonalikka aylantirilgan hurmatli va qayg'u chekkan oila ekanimizni birdan ko'rishadi.

en: And that general will lose his post, you’ll see!
uz: Va bu general o'z lavozimini yo'qotadi, siz ko'rasiz!

en: We shall perform under his windows every day, and if the Tsar drives by, I’ll fall on my knees, put the children before me, show them to him, and say ‘Defend us father.’ He is the father of the fatherless, he is merciful, he’ll protect us, you’ll see, and that wretch of a general.
uz: Biz har kuni uning oynalari ostida ijro qilamiz va agar tsar o'tib ketsa, men tiz cho'kib, bolalarni oldimga qo'yib, unga ko'rsataman va: "Bizni himoya qil, otam!" - deb aytaman.

en: … Lida, tenez vous droite!
uz: Lida, to'g'ri turing!

en: Kolya, you’ll dance again.
uz: Kolya, sen yana raqs qilasan.

en: Why are you whimpering?
uz: Nima uchun qichqiryapsan?

en: What are you afraid of, stupid?
uz: Nimaga qo'rqasan, ahmoq?

en: Goodness, what am I to do with them, Rodion Romanovitch?
uz: Yaxshilik, men ular bilan nima qilishim kerak, Rodion Romanovitch?

en: If you only knew how stupid they are!
uz: Agar ular qanchalik ahmoq ekanligini bilganingizda edi!

en: What’s one to do with such children?” And she, almost crying herself —which did not stop her uninterrupted, rapid flow of talk —pointed to the crying children.
uz: Bunday bolalar bilan nima qilish kerak? Va u o'zini deyarli yig'lab yubordi, lekin bu uning to'xtamas, tez-tez gapirishini to'xtatmadi, u yig'layotgan bolalarga ishora qildi.

en: Raskolnikov tried to persuade her to go home, and even said, hoping to work on her vanity, that it was unseemly for her to be wandering about the streets like an organ-grinder, as she was intending to become the principal of a boarding-school.
uz: Raskolnikov uni uyga borishga ishontirmoqchi bo'ldi va hatto o'z behudaligidan xalos bo'lishga umidvor bo'lib, u maktabda maktab direktorini o'z xohishi bilan o'tkazgani uchun, u organ o'g'irlagichi kabi ko'chalarda yurish unchalik munosib emasligini aytdi.

en: “A boarding-school, ha-ha-ha!
uz: Bir internat maktabi, ha-ha-ha!

en: A castle in the air,” cried Katerina Ivanovna, her laugh ending in a cough.
uz: Havodagi qalʼa, - dedi Katerina Ivanovna, uning kulgi qoʻshish bilan tugadi.

en: “No, Rodion Romanovitch, that dream is over!
uz: Yo'q, Rodion Romanovitch, bu orzu tugadi!

en: All have forsaken us!
uz: Hammasi bizni tashlab ketishdi!

en: … You know, Rodion Romanovitch, I threw an inkpot at him —it happened to be standing in the waiting-room by the paper where you sign your name.
uz: ... Bilasizmi, Rodion Romanovitch, men unga qora qavat tashladim, u o'z nomini imzolagan qog'ozning yonida kutib turish xonasida turgan edi.

en: I wrote my name, threw it at him and ran away.
uz: Men o'z nomimni yozib, unga tashladim va qochib ketdim.

en: Oh, the scoundrels, the scoundrels!
uz: Oh, qozoqlar, qozoqlar!

en: But enough of them, now I’ll provide for the children myself, I won’t bow down to anybody!
uz: Ammo ular yetarli, endi bolalarni o'zim ta'minlayman, hech kimga sajda qilmayman!

en: She has had to bear enough for us!” she pointed to Sonia.
uz: U biz uchun yetarlicha azob chekdi! U Soniaga ishora qildi.

en: “Polenka, how much have you got?
uz: Polenka, qancha pulingiz bor?

en: What, only two farthings!
uz: Nima, faqat ikki farthing!

en: Oh, the mean wretches!
uz: Oh, yovuz kambag'allar!

en: They give us nothing, only run after us, putting their tongues out.
uz: Ular bizga hech narsa bermaydilar, faqat orqamizdan yurib, tillarini chiqarib yuborishadi.

en: There, what is that blockhead laughing at?” (She
uz: Mana, bu qo'rqinchli odam nimaga kulmoqda?

en: pointed to a man in the crowd.) “It’s all because Kolya here is so stupid; I have such a bother with him.
uz: ko'pchilik orasida bo'lgan bir kishiga ishora qildi.) Buning hammasi Kolya juda ahmoqona bo'lgani uchun; men u bilan shunchalik muammon bo'ldim.

en: What do you want, Polenka?
uz: Siz nima istaysiz, Polenka?

en: Tell me in French, parlez-moi français.
uz: Menga frantsuz tilida ayting, menga frantsuz tilida gapiring.

en: Why, I’ve taught you, you know some phrases.
uz: Men sizga o'rgatganman, siz ba'zi iboralarni bilasiz.

en: Else how are you to show that you are of good family, well brought-up children, and not at all like other organ- grinders?
uz: Aks holda, qanday qilib yaxshi oiladan, yaxshi tarbiyalangan bolalardan, boshqa organ o'chiruvchilardan umuman farq qilayotganingizni ko'rsata olasiz?

en: We aren’t going to have a Punch and Judy show in the street, but to sing a genteel song.
uz: Biz ko'chalarda Punch va Judy sho'yini o'tkazmaymiz, balki bir go'zal qo'shiqni kuylaymiz.

en: … Ah, yes, … What are we to sing?
uz: Ha, ha, nima kuylashimiz kerak?

en: You keep putting me out, but we … you see, we are standing here, Rodion Romanovitch, to find something to sing and get money, something Kolya can dance to.
uz: Siz meni tashlab ketishni davom ettirasiz, lekin biz... ko'rasiz, biz bu yerda turibmiz, Rodion Romanovitch, qo'shiq kuylash va pul topish uchun biror narsa topmoqdamiz, Kolya raqs qila oladigan narsa.

en: … For, as you can fancy, our performance is all impromptu.
uz: Chunki, siz tasavvur qilganingizdek, bizning namoyishlarimiz hammasi o'z-o'zidan bo'lgan.

en: … We must talk it over and rehearse it all thoroughly, and then we shall go to Nevsky, where there are far more people of good society, and we shall be noticed at once.
uz: ... Biz bu haqda gaplashib, hamma narsani puxta o'rganishimiz kerak, so'ngra Nevsky shahriga boramiz, u yerda yaxshi jamiyatda ko'proq odamlar bor va bizni darhol ko'rishadi.

en: Lida knows ‘My Village’ only, nothing but ‘My Village,’ and everyone sings that.
uz: Lida faqat "My Village" ni, faqat "My Village" ni biladi va hamma buni kuylaydi.

en: We must sing something far more genteel.
uz: Biz ancha ko'proq yaxshilik bilan kuylashimiz kerak.

en: … Well, have you thought of anything, Polenka?
uz: - Xo'sh, Polenka, biror narsa haqida o'ylab ko'rganmisiz?

en: If only you’d help your mother!
uz: Agar siz onangizga yordam berganingizda edi!

en: My memory’s quite gone, or I should have thought of something.
uz: Xotiralarim butunlay yo'qoldi, yo'q bo'lsa biror narsa o'ylab ko'rishim kerak edi.

en: We really can’t sing ‘An Hussar.’ Ah, let us sing in French, ‘Cinq sous,’ I have taught it you, I have taught it you.
uz: Biz haqiqatan ham kuylay olmaymiz An Hussar. Ah, fransuz tilida kuylaylik, Cinq sous, Men sizga o'rgatdim, men sizga o'rgatdim.

en: And as it is in French, people will see at once that you are children of good family, and that will be much more touching.
uz: Fransiya tilida gapirganimizdek, odamlar siz yaxshi oila farzandlari ekanligingizni birdan ko'rishadi va bu yanada hayajonli bo'ladi.

en: … You might sing ‘Marlborough s’en va-t-en guerre,’ for that’s quite a child’s song and is sung as a lullaby in all the aristocratic houses.
uz: Siz "Marlborough sen va-t-en guerre"ni kuylashingiz mumkin, chunki bu bolalar uchun juda yaxshi qo'shiq va barcha aristokratik uylarda to'shak qo'shigi sifatida kuylanadi.

en: “Marlborough s’en va-t-en guerre  Ne sait quand reviendra …” she began singing.
uz: Marlborough jangga ketadi qachon qaytishini bilmaydi ... u qo'shiq kuylashni boshladi.

en: “But no, better sing ‘Cinq sous.’ Now, Kolya, your hands on your hips, make haste, and you, Lida, keep turning the other way, and Polenka and I will sing and clap our hands!
uz: Ammo yo'q, o'zingizning qo'lingiz bilan qo'lingizni qo'lga oling. Endi Kolya, qo'lingizni qo'lingizga qo'yinglar, shoshilinglar, siz esa, Lida, boshqa tomonga burilishni davom ettiringlar, Polenka va men qo'lingiz bilan to'playlik!

en: “Cinq sous, cinq sous  Pour monter notre ménage.” (Cough-cough-cough!) “Set your dress straight, Polenka, it’s slipped down on your shoulders,” she observed, panting from coughing.
uz: Besh so'z, besh so'z Bizni uyga joylashtirish uchun. (Qo'sh-ko'sh-ko'sh!) Koshingizni to'g'ri yozib qo'ying, Polenka, bu sizning yelkangizga chiqqandi, u qo'shishdan nafas olib, kuzatib o'tdi.

en: “Now it’s particularly necessary to behave nicely and genteelly, that all may see that you are wellborn children.
uz: Hozirgi kunda siz yaxshi tug'ilgan bolalar ekanligingizni hamma ko'rish uchun yaxshi va mehribon bo'lish juda muhimdir.

en: the time that the bodice should be cut longer, and made of two widths.
uz: O'z vaqtida bo'lakni uzoqroq kesib, ikki kenglikdan tayyorlash kerak.

en: It was your fault, Sonia, with your advice to make it shorter, and now you see the child is quite deformed by it.
uz: Bu sizning xatoingiz edi, Sonia, bu ishni qisqartirishga maslahat berganingiz uchun, endi ko'rib turibsizki, bola bu tufayli juda buzib ketgan.

en: … Why, you’re all crying again!
uz: Sizlar yana yig'layotgandirsiz!

en: What’s the matter, stupids?
uz: Nima bo'ldi, ahmoqlar?

en: Make haste, make haste!
uz: Shoshil, shoshil!

en: Oh, what an unbearable child!
uz: Oh, naqadar yengil bola!

en: “Cinq sous, cinq sous.
uz: Besh sous, besh sous.

en: What do you want?” A policeman was indeed forcing his way through the crowd.
uz: Nima istaysiz? Bir politsiyachi, haqiqatan ham, xaloyiq orasida o'zini majburlab o'tkazgan.

en: But at that moment a gentleman in civilian uniform and an overcoat —a solid-looking official of about fifty with a decoration on his neck (which delighted Katerina Ivanovna and had its effect on the policeman) —approached and without a word handed her a green three-rouble note.
uz: Ammo o'sha paytda fuqarolik uniformasi va kiyim kiygan bir kishi yaqinlashib, unga bir so'z aytmasdan, bo'yniga o'lchamli ornitma qo'yilgan taxminan ellik yoshdagi kuchli ko'rinadigan mansabdor shaxs (katerina Ivanovna xursand bo'lgan va politsiyachiga ta'sir qilgan) unga yashil uch rubllik notani berdi.

en: His face wore a look of genuine sympathy.
uz: Uning yuzida samimiy hamdardlik ko'rinishi bor edi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna took it and gave him a polite, even ceremonious, bow.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna uni olib, unga xushmuomala, hatto marosimli bo'lib sajda qildi.

en: “I thank you, honoured sir,” she began loftily.
uz: Men sizga rahmat aytaman, aziz sir, u yuksaklik bilan boshladi.

en: “The causes that have induced us (take the money, Polenka: you see there are generous and honourable people who are ready to help a poor gentlewoman in distress).
uz: Bizni rag'batlantirgan sabablar (pulni oling, Polenka: siz ko'rasiz, kambag'al ayolga yordam berishga tayyor bo'lgan saxiy va hurmatli odamlar bor).

en: You see, honoured sir, these orphans of good family —I might even say of aristocratic connections —and that wretch of a general sat eating grouse … and stamped at my disturbing him.
uz: Siz ko'rasiz, aziz sir, yaxshi oiladagi bu yetimlar Men hatto aristokratik aloqalar haqida aytishim mumkin  va o'sha qashshoq general o'tirganida, men uni bezovta qilayotganimdan ko'p xursand bo'ldi.

en: ‘Your excellency,’ I said, ‘protect the orphans, for you knew my late husband, Semyon Zaharovitch, and on the very day of his death the basest of scoundrels slandered his only daughter.’ … That policeman again!
uz: Mening oliy ruhoniyligim,  dedim,  yetimlarni himoya qiling, chunki siz mening marhum erim Semyon Zaharovitchni tanardingiz va uning o'limi kunida eng kam o'g'il uning yagona qizini haqoratladi.... Yana bu politsiyachi!

en: Protect me,” she cried to the official.
uz: Meni himoya qiling, - deb rasmiylarga baqirdi u.

en: “Why is that policeman edging up to me?
uz: Nega bu politsiyachi menga yaqinlashmoqda?

en: We have only just run away from one of them.
uz: Biz ulardan faqat bittadan qochib ketdik.

en: What do you want, fool?” “It’s forbidden in the streets.
uz: Nima istaysan, ahmoq?U ko'chalarda taqiqlangan.

en: You mustn’t make a disturbance.” “It’s you’re making a disturbance.
uz: Siz buzilib ketmasligingiz kerak.    Bu siz buzilib ketayotganingiz.

en: It’s just the same as if I were grinding an organ.
uz: Bu xuddi organni o'qib yurganimdek.

en: What business is it of yours?” “You have to get a licence for an organ, and you haven’t got one, and in that way you collect a crowd.
uz: Bu sizning ishingizmi? Organ uchun litsenziyani olishingiz kerak, ammo sizda yo'q, shuning uchun siz ko'pchilikni to'playsiz.

en: Where do you lodge?” “What, a license?” wailed Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Qayerda yashaysiz? nima, litsenziya? Katerina Ivanovna qayg'urdi.

en: “I buried my husband today.
uz: Men bugun erimni ko'mdim.

en: What need of a license?”
uz: Nima uchun litsenziyaga ehtiyoj bor?

en: “Calm yourself, madam, calm yourself,” began the official.
uz: O'zingizni tinchlang, xonim, o'zingizni tinchlang, rasmiy boshlandi.

en: “Come along; I will escort you.
uz: Kelib keling, men sizni kuzatib boraman.

en: … This is no place for you in the crowd.
uz: ... Bu ko'pchilik orasida siz uchun joy emas.

en: You are ill.” “Honoured sir, honoured sir, you don’t know,” screamed Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Siz kasalsiz. "Marangiz sir, ma'rangiz sir, siz bilmaysiz", - deb qichqirdi Katerina Ivanovna.

en: “We are going to the Nevsky.
uz: Biz Nevskyga boramiz.

en: What’s the matter with you all?
uz: Sizlarning hammangiz bilan nima yuz berdi?

en: Kolya, Lida, where are you going?” she cried suddenly in alarm.
uz: Kolya, Lida, qayerga ketyapsizlar? U qo'rquvdan birdan yig'ladi.

en: “Oh, silly children!
uz: Oh, ahmoq bolalar!

en: Kolya, Lida, where are they off to?
uz: Kolya, Lida, ular qayerga ketmoqdalar?

en: …” Kolya and Lida, scared out of their wits by the crowd, and their mother’s mad pranks, suddenly seized each other by the hand, and ran off at the sight of the policeman who wanted to take them away somewhere.
uz: Kolya va Lida xaloyiq va onasining g'alati mashg'ulotlaridan qo'rqqan holda bir-birlarining qo'llarini qo'lga olishdi va ularni qayerga olib ketmoqchi bo'lgan politsiyachini ko'rib qochib ketishdi.

en: Weeping and wailing, poor Katerina Ivanovna ran after them.
uz: Qizig'i Katerina Ivanovna yig'lab, ularning orqasidan yugurib ketdi.

en: She was a piteous and unseemly spectacle, as she ran, weeping and panting for breath.
uz: U yig'lab-ichib, nafas olishni orzu qilib, yugurib ketayotganda, o'ziga yarasha va yomon ko'rinish ko'rsatgan edi.

en: Sonia and Polenka rushed after them.
uz: Sonia va Polenka ularning orqasidan ergashishdi.

en: “Bring them back, bring them back, Sonia!
uz: Ularni qaytarib keling, qaytarib keling, Sonia!

en: Oh stupid, ungrateful children!
uz: Oh ahmoq, shukrsiz bolalar!

en: … It’s for your sakes I …” She stumbled as she ran and fell down.
uz: ... Bu siz uchun, men ... U yugurib yiqilib, yiqilib ketdi.

en: “She’s cut herself, she’s bleeding!
uz: O'zini kesib olgan, qon ketayotgan!

en: Oh, dear!” cried Sonia, bending over her.
uz: Oh, aziz! Sonia yig'ladi va uning ustiga yiqildi.

en: All ran up and crowded around.
uz: Hamma yig'ilib, to'planib ketdi.

en: Raskolnikov and Lebeziatnikov were the first at her side, the official too hastened up, and behind him the policeman who muttered, “Bother!” with a gesture of impatience, feeling that the job was going to be a troublesome one.
uz: Raskolnikov va Lebeziatnikov uning yonida birinchi bo'lib o'tirdilar, rasmiy ham shoshildi va uning orqasida "Bother!" deb qichqirgan politsiya xodimi, ish og'ir bo'lishini his etib, sabrsizlikni ko'rsatdi.

en: Pass on!” he said to the crowd that pressed forward.
uz: O'tkazib yubor! dedi u oldinga bosgan xaloyiqqa.

en: “She’s dying,” someone shouted.
uz: U o'lib ketyapti, kimdir qichqirdi.

en: “She’s gone out of her mind,” said another.
uz: "U aqldan ozdi", - dedi yana bir kishi.

en: “Lord have mercy upon us,” said a woman, crossing herself.
uz: "Rabbim, bizga marhamat qilgin", - dedi bir ayol o'zini o'zi ko'targan holda.

en: “Have they caught the little girl and the boy?
uz: Qiz va o'g'ilni ushlab qolishganmi?

en: They’re being brought back, the elder one’s got them.
uz: Ular qaytarib kelinmoqda, kattalar ularni oldi.

en: … Ah, the naughty imps!” When they examined Katerina Ivanovna carefully, they saw that she had not cut herself against a stone, as Sonia thought, but that the blood that stained the pavement red was from her chest.
uz: Ah, xudojo'y o'g'illar! Katerina Ivonovnaga diqqat bilan qarab, ular Sonia o'ylagandek, u o'zini toshga o'g'irlamaganini, aksincha, yo'lni qizillab qo'ygan qon uning ko'krakidan chiqqanini ko'rishdi.

en: “I’ve seen that before,” muttered the official to Raskolnikov and Lebeziatnikov; “that’s consumption; the blood flows and chokes the patient.
uz: Men buni ilgari ko'rganman,  rasmiy Raskolnikov va Lebeziatnikovga gapirdi;  bu iste'mol; qon oqib, bemorni cho'ktiradi.

en: I saw the same thing with a relative of my own not long ago
uz: Yaqinda o'zimning qarindoshim bilan ham xuddi shunday sodir bo'lganini ko'rdim.

en: … nearly a pint of blood, all in a minute.
uz: ... deyarli bir litr qon, barchasi bir daqiqada.

en: … What’s to be done though?
uz: Ammo nima qilish kerak?

en: She is dying.” “This way, this way, to my room!” Sonia implored.
uz: U o'lib ketyapti. Bu yo'ldan, bu yo'ldan, xonamga! Sonia iltijo qildi.

en: … See, that house, the second from here.
uz: Mana, o'sha uy, bu yerdan keyingi ikkinchi uy.

en: … Come to me, make haste,” she turned from one to the other.
uz: ... Mening oldimga kel, shoshiling, u bir tomondan boshqa tomonga o'tdi.

en: “Send for the doctor!
uz: Doktorni chaqiring!

en: Oh, dear!” Thanks to the official’s efforts, this plan was adopted, the policeman even helping to carry Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Oh, aziz! Xodimlarning saʼy-harakatlari tufayli ushbu reja qabul qilindi, hatto politsiyachi Katerina Ivanovnani koʻtarib olishga yordam berdi.

en: She was carried to Sonia’s room, almost unconscious, and laid on the bed.
uz: U deyarli beva bo'lib, Sonia xonasiga olib ketilgan va o'z yotoqida yotgan edi.

en: The blood was still flowing, but she seemed to be coming to herself.
uz: Qon hali ham oqib turgan edi, lekin u o'z-o'zidan o'zini o'zgartirayotgandek ko'rinardi.

en: Raskolnikov, Lebeziatnikov, and the official accompanied Sonia into the room and were followed by the policeman, who first drove back the crowd which followed to the very door.
uz: Raskolnikov, Lebeziatnikov va mansabdor shaxs Sonia bilan birga xonaga kirishdi va ular politsiyachi tomonidan kuzatib borildi, u birinchi navbatda xaloyiqni orqaga qaytardi, ular esa eshikgacha ergashib borishdi.

en: Polenka came in holding Kolya and Lida, who were trembling and weeping.
uz: Polenka Kolya va Lidani qo'lga olib keldi, ular titrab yig'lab yurishgan edi.

en: Several persons came in too from the Kapernaumovs’ room; the landlord, a lame one- eyed man of strange appearance with whiskers and hair that stood up like a brush, his wife, a woman with an everlastingly scared expression, and several open-mouthed children with wonder-struck faces.
uz: Shuningdek, Kafarnahumlar xonasidan bir necha kishilar kirishdi; uy egasi, o'zgacha ko'rinishdagi bir ko'zli cho'k odam, burchak kabi ko'tariladigan mo'l va sochlar, uning xotini, doimo qo'rqqan ayol va bir necha og'izli bolalar va hayratda qolgan yuzlar.

en: Among these, Svidrigaïlov suddenly made his appearance.
uz: Shular orasida Svidrigailov to'satdan paydo bo'ldi.

en: Raskolnikov looked at him with surprise, not understanding where he had come from and not having noticed him in the crowd.
uz: Raskolnikov unga hayronlik bilan qaradi, u qayerdan kelganini tushunmaydi va xaloyiqda uni ko'rmaydi.

en: A doctor and priest wore spoken of.
uz: Bir shifokor va ruhoniy haqida gap ketar edi.

en: The official whispered to Raskolnikov that he thought it was too late now for the doctor, but he ordered him to be sent for.
uz: Xizmatkor Raskolnikovga shifokor uchun endi kech bo'lgan deb o'ylaganini shoshladi, ammo u uni chaqirtirishni buyurdi.

en: Kapernaumov ran himself.
uz: Kafarnahumov o'z-o'zini yo'lga qo'ydi.

en: Meanwhile Katerina Ivanovna had regained her breath.
uz: Shu bilan birga, Katerina Ivanovna nafasini qaytarib oldi.

en: The bleeding ceased for a time.
uz: Bir muncha vaqt davomida qon ketish to'xtadi.

en: She looked with sick but intent and penetrating eyes at Sonia, who stood pale and trembling, wiping the sweat from her brow with a handkerchief.
uz: U Soniaga kasal, ammo niyatli va o'ziga xos ko'zlar bilan qaradi, u soch-qo'shiq va titralib turardi va qo'lqop bilan yuzidagi terni silkadi.

en: At last she asked to be raised.
uz: Nihoyat, u o'sishni so'radi.

en: They sat her up on the bed, supporting her on both sides.
uz: Ular uni yotoq ustiga qo'yib, ikki tomondan qo'llab-quvvatladilar.

en: “Where are the children?” she said in a faint voice.
uz: "Bolalar qayerda?" - deb so'radi u o'z so'zlarida.

en: “You’ve brought them, Polenka?
uz: Siz ularni olib keldingizmi, Polenka?

en: Why did you run away.
uz: Nima uchun qochgansiz?

en: … Och!” Once more her parched lips were covered with blood.
uz: Oʻsha paytning oʻzida yana uning quruq ogʻizlari qon bilan qoplangan edi.

en: She moved her eyes, looking about her.
uz: U ko'zlarini ko'tardi va atrofini ko'rdi.

en: “So that’s how you live, Sonia!
uz: Shunday qilib, siz shunday yashayapsiz, Sonia!

en: Never once have I been in your room.” She looked at her with a face of suffering.
uz: Men hech qachon sizning xonangizda bo'lmaganman. U unga azob chekayotgan ko'z bilan qaradi.

en: “We have been your ruin, Sonia.
uz: Biz sening vayroning bo'ldik, Sonia.

en: Polenka, Lida, Kolya, come here!
uz: Polenka, Lida, Kolya, bu yerga kelinglar!

en: Well, here they are, Sonia, take them all!
uz: Mana ular bor, Sonia, ularning barchasini olib ket!

en: I hand them over to you,
uz: Men ularni sizga topshiraman,

en: The ball is over.” (Cough!) “Lay me down, let me die in peace.” They laid her back on the pillow.
uz: Top tugagan. (Qo'shish!) Meni yerga tashlang, tinchlikda o'laman. Ular uni yostiqqa qo'ydilar.

en: You haven’t got a rouble to spare.
uz: Sizda qolish uchun bir rubl ham yo'q.

en: God must forgive me without that.
uz: Xudo meni shu yo'l bilan kechirishi kerak.

en: He knows how I have suffered.
uz: U men qanchalik azob chekganimni biladi.

en: … And if He won’t forgive me, I don’t care!” She sank more and more into uneasy delirium.
uz: Va agar U meni kechirmasa, men o'zimni qiziqtirmayman! U ko'proq va ko'proq noqulay deliriumga tushdi.

en: At times she shuddered, turned her eyes from side to side, recognised everyone for a minute, but at once sank into delirium again.
uz: Ba'zan u titrab, ko'zlarini yonma-yon burib, hammalarni bir daqiqa tan oldi, lekin darhol yana deliriumga tushdi.

en: Her breathing was hoarse and difficult, there was a sort of rattle in her throat.
uz: Uning nafas olishi qattiq va qiyin edi, bo'yniga bir xil qichqiriq tushdi.

en: “I said to him, your excellency,” she ejaculated, gasping after each word.
uz: Men unga, Oliy ruhoniy, dedim: "U har bir so'zdan so'ng nafas olib, o'z ko'zidan chiqdi.

en: “That Amalia Ludwigovna, ah!
uz: Bu Amaliya Ludwigovna, ah!

en: Lida, Kolya, hands on your hips, make haste!
uz: Lida, Kolya, qo'llaringizni ustingizga qo'yinglar, shoshilinch bo'linglar!

en: Tap with your heels, be a graceful child!
uz: Tovushlaringizga taqillatinglar, xushmuomala bola bo'linglar!

en: “Du hast Diamanten und Perlen “What next?
uz: Sizda olmos va marvaridlar bor Bundan keyin nima bo'ladi?

en: That’s the thing to sing.
uz: Mana shu qo'shiqning maqsadi.

en: “Du hast die schönsten Augen,  Mädchen, was willst du mehr?
uz: Sizda eng chiroyli ko'zlar bor, qizim, yana nima istaysiz?

en: What things the fool invents!
uz: Aqlsiz inson qanday narsalarni yaratadi!

en: “In the heat of midday in the vale of Dagestan.
uz: Dagestan vodiysida kun yorug'ida issiqlikda.

en: “Ah, how I loved it!
uz: Ah, men uni qanchalik yaxshi ko'rdim!

en: I loved that song to distraction, Polenka!
uz: O'sha qo'shiqni diqqatimni chalg'itadigan darajada yaxshi ko'rdim, Polenka!

en: Your father, you know, used to sing it when we were engaged.
uz: Bilasizmi, sizning otangiz biz nişanlanayotgan paytimizda buni kuylagan.

en: Oh that’s the thing for us to sing!
uz: Oh, bu biz kuylashimiz kerak bo'lgan narsa!

en: How was it?” She was violently excited and tried to sit up.
uz: Qanday bo'ldi? U juda hayajonlanib, o'tirishga harakat qildi.

en: At last, in a horribly hoarse, broken voice, she began, shrieking and gasping at every word, with a look of growing terror.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, qo'rqinchli, buzilgan ovoz bilan, u har bir so'zga qichqiriq va nafas olib, qo'rqinchli ko'rinish bilan boshladi.

en: “In the heat of midday!
uz: Tush kunning issiqligida!

en: …  With lead in my breast!
uz: ... Mening ko'kraklarimda oltin bor!

en: “Your excellency!” she wailed suddenly with a heartrending scream and a flood of tears, “protect the orphans!
uz: Yo'q! U birdan qichqiriq va ko'z yoshlari bilan yig'ladi, Yitmishilarni himoya qiling!

en: You have been their father’s guest … one may say aristocratic.
uz: Siz ularning otasining mehmoningiz bo'lgansiz ... bir kishi aristokrat deb aytishi mumkin.

en: …” She started, regaining consciousness, and gazed at all with a sort of terror, but at once recognised Sonia.
uz: ... U hushini tiklab, qo'rqinch bilan qarab boshladi, lekin shu zahoti Soniaga e'tiborini qaratdi.

en: “Sonia, Sonia!” she articulated softly and caressingly, as though surprised to find her there.
uz: "Sonia, Sonia!" - deb so'zlasha boshladi u, xuddi uni u yerda topib hayratda qolganidek.

en: “Sonia darling, are you here, too?” They lifted her up again.
uz: Sonia darling, sen ham shu yerdamisiz? Uni yana ko'tarib olishdi.

en: Farewell, poor thing!
uz: Xo'sh, kambag'al!

en: I am broken!” she cried with vindictive despair, and her head fell heavily back on the pillow.
uz: Men buzilganman! U qasos chekkan umidsizlikdan yig'ladi va boshini yostiqqa og'irlab qo'ydi.

en: She sank into unconsciousness again, but this time it did not last long.
uz: U yana bexabarlikka tushdi, ammo bu safar bu uzoq davom etmadi.

en: Her pale, yellow, wasted face dropped back, her mouth fell open, her leg moved convulsively, she gave a deep, deep sigh and died.
uz: Uning bo'lak, sariq, bo'lak bo'lgan yuzi orqaga tushdi, og'zi ochildi, oyoqlari shovqinli harakatlandi, u chuqur, chuqur nafas oldi va vafot etdi.

en: Sonia fell upon her, flung her arms about her, and remained motionless with her head pressed to the dead woman’s wasted bosom.
uz: Sonia uning ustiga yiqildi, qo'llarini o'ziga tashladi va boshini o'lik ayolning bo'g'iga bosgan holda harakatsiz qoldi.

en: Polenka threw herself at her mother’s feet, kissing them and weeping violently.
uz: Polenka o'zini onasining oyoqlariga tashlab, ularni o'pdi va qattiq yig'ladi.

en: Though Kolya and Lida did not understand what had happened, they had a feeling that it was something terrible; they put their hands on each other’s little shoulders, stared straight at one another and both at once opened their mouths and began screaming.
uz: Kolya va Lida nima sodir bo'lganini tushunmagan bo'lsa-da, bu juda dahshatli bo'lganini his qilishdi; ular qo'llarini bir-birlarining kichkina shoxlariga qo'yib, bir-birlariga to'g'ri qarab turishdi va ikkalasi ham bir zumda og'izlarini ochdilar va qichqirishni boshlashdi.

en: They were both still in their fancy dress; one in a turban, the other in the cap with the ostrich feather.
uz: Ikkalasi ham hali ham o'z go'zal kiyimlarida edilar; biri turbandda, ikkinchisi ostrich fe'rli to'pka kiygan edi.

en: And how did “the certificate of merit” come to be on the bed beside Katerina Ivanovna?
uz: Qiziq, qanday qilib Katerina Ivonovna yonida o'tirgan sariyoqda o'zining qadr-qimmatliligi sertifikatlari bo'ldi?

en: It lay there by the pillow; Raskolnikov saw it.
uz: U yostiq yonida yotgan edi; Raskolnikov uni ko'rgan edi.

en: He walked away to the window.
uz: U darcha tomon yurdi.

en: Lebeziatnikov skipped up to him.
uz: Lebeziatnikov uning yonidan o'tib ketdi.

en: “She is dead,” he said.
uz: "U o'lgan", dedi u.

en: “Rodion Romanovitch, I must have two words with you,” said Svidrigaïlov, coming up to them.
uz: "Rodion Romanovitch, men siz bilan ikki so'z gaplashishim kerak", - dedi Svidrigailov ularga yaqinlashib.

en: Lebeziatnikov at once made room for him and delicately withdrew.
uz: Lebeziatnikov darhol uning uchun joy yaratdi va o'zidan xolislik bilan voz kechdi.

en: Svidrigaïlov drew Raskolnikov further away.
uz: Svidrigailov Raskolnikovni yanada uzoqlashtirdi.

en: “I will undertake all the arrangements, the funeral and that.
uz: Men barcha tadbirlarni, marosim va shu kabi ishlarni o'z zimmamga oldim.

en: You know it’s a question of money and, as I told you, I have plenty to spare.
uz: Bu pul masalasi ekanligini bilasiz va sizga aytganimdek, men uchun ko'p narsalar bor.

en: I will put those two little ones and Polenka into some good orphan asylum, and I will settle fifteen hundred roubles to be paid to each on coming of age, so that Sofya Semyonovna need have no
uz: Men o'sha ikkita bola va Polenkani yaxshi yetimlar uyida joylashtiraman va Sofiya Semyonovnaga hech qanday ehtiyoj qolmasligi uchun, ularning har biri katta bo'lganda to'lanadigan o'n besh yuz rubl to'lovini tuzaman.

en: And I will pull her out of the mud too, for she is a good girl, isn’t she?
uz: Men uni ham gʻamdan chiqarib tashlayman, chunki u yaxshi qiz, shunday emasmi?

en: So tell Avdotya Romanovna that that is how I am spending her ten thousand.” “What is your motive for such benevolence?” asked Raskolnikov.
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaga o'nta mingni shu tarzda sarflayotganimni ayting. Sizning bunday mehribonlik qilishingizning sabablari nima? - deb so'radi Raskolnikov.

en: you sceptical person!” laughed Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Sen sceptik odam! Svidrigailov kuldi.

en: “I told you I had no need of that money.
uz: Men sizga o'sha pulga muhtoj emasligimni aytdim.

en: Won’t you admit that it’s simply done from humanity?
uz: Bu shunchaki insoniyat tomonidan amalga oshirilganini tan olmaysizmi?

en: She wasn’t ‘a louse,’ you know” (he pointed to the corner where the dead woman lay), “was she, like some old pawnbroker woman?
uz: U tovuq emas edi (u o'lik ayol yotgan burchada ko'rsatdi), lekin u bir qariya qarzdor ayolga o'xsharmidi?

en: Come, you’ll agree, is Luzhin to go on living, and doing wicked things or is she to die?
uz: Keling, siz rozi bo'lasiz, Luzhin yashashi va yovuz ishlar qilishi kerakmi yoki o'lishi kerakmi?

en: And if I didn’t help them, Polenka would go the same way.” He said this with an air of a sort of gay winking slyness, keeping his eyes fixed on Raskolnikov, who turned white and cold, hearing his own phrases, spoken to Sonia.
uz: Agar men ularga yordam bermasdim, Polenka ham xuddi shunday yo'l tutardi. U buni bir xil gey g'alati ko'rinish bilan aytdi, ko'zlarini oq va sovuq bo'lgan Raskolnikovga qaratdi, u Sonia bilan gapirgan o'z iboralarini eshitib, oq va sovuq bo'ldi.

en: He quickly stepped back and looked wildly at Svidrigaïlov.
uz: U tezda orqaga qadam bosdi va Svidrigailovga vahima bilan qaradi.

en: “How do you know?” he whispered, hardly able to breathe.
uz: Qanday qilib bilasiz? - deb shovqin qildi u, nafas olishni qiyinlashtirdi.

en: “Why, I lodge here at Madame Resslich’s, the other side of the wall.
uz: Men bu yerda, devorning boshqa tomonidagi Resslichs xonadonida yashayman.

en: Here is Kapernaumov, and there lives Madame Resslich, an old and devoted friend of mine.
uz: Bu yerda Kapernaumov va u erda mening eski va sadoqatli do'stim, madam Resslich yashaydi.

en: I am a neighbour.” “You?” “Yes,” continued Svidrigaïlov, shaking with laughter.
uz: Men qo'shniman. Siz? Ha, Svidrigailov davom etdi va kulishdan shovqin qildi.

en: “I assure you on my honour, dear Rodion Romanovitch, that you have interested me enormously.
uz: Men sizlarni hurmatim bilan ta'kidlayman, aziz Rodion Romanovitch, siz meni juda qiziqtirgansiz.

en: I told you we should become friends, I foretold it.
uz: Men sizga do'st bo'lishimiz kerakligini aytdim, buni oldindan aytdim.

en: And you will see what an accommodating person I am.
uz: Va men qanchalik mehribon odam ekanligimni ko'rasiz.

en: You’ll see that you can get on with me!”
uz: Siz men bilan birga bo'lishingizga ishonch hosil qilasiz!

en: I A strange period began for Raskolnikov: it was as though a fog had fallen upon him and wrapped him in a dreary solitude from which there was no escape.
uz: Raskolnikov uchun g'alati davr boshlandi: xuddi unga tuman tushib, uni hech qanday qochish imkoni bo'lmaydigan bir yolg'izlikka o'rab olganidek bo'ldi.

en: Recalling that period long after, he believed that his mind had been clouded at times, and that it had continued so, with intervals, till the final catastrophe.
uz: O'sha davrni ko'p vaqt o'tgach eslab, u o'z ongining ba'zida bulutli bo'lganiga va oxirgi fojiaga qadar vaqti-vaqti bilan shunday davom etganligiga ishondi.

en: He was convinced that he had been mistaken about many things at that time, for instance as to the date of certain events.
uz: U o'sha paytda ko'p narsalarda, masalan, ba'zi voqealarning sanasi borasida noto'g'ri fikrda bo'lganiga amin edi.

en: Anyway, when he tried later on to piece his recollections together, he learnt a great deal about himself from what other people told him.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, keyinchalik u o'z xotiralarini birlashtirishga harakat qilganida, boshqa odamlar unga nima deyishganidan o'zi haqida ko'p narsalarni bilib oldi.

en: He had mixed up incidents and had explained events as due to circumstances which existed only in his imagination.
uz: U hodisalarni aralashtirib, hodisalarni faqat tasavvurida mavjud bo'lgan holatlar tufayli sodir bo'lgan deb tushuntirdi.

en: At times he was a prey to agonies of morbid uneasiness, amounting sometimes to panic.
uz: Ba'zan u kasallik bilan bezovta bo'lgan azob-uqubatlarga qurbon bo'lib, ba'zan qo'rqinchga tushadi.

en: But he remembered, too, moments, hours, perhaps whole days, of complete apathy, which came upon him as a reaction from his previous terror and might be compared with the abnormal insensibility, sometimes seen in the dying.
uz: Ammo u, shuningdek, o'tgan dahshatidan kelib chiqqan va ba'zan o'tib ketayotgan kishilarda ko'rinadigan anormal hissiyotsizlik bilan taqqoslanishi mumkin bo'lgan to'liq befarqlik davrlarini, soatlarni, ehtimol kunlarni ham esladi.

en: He seemed to be trying in that latter stage to escape from a full and clear understanding of his position.
uz: O'sha oxirgi bosqichda u o'z pozitsiyasini to'liq va aniq tushunishdan qochishga harakat qilyapti.

en: Certain essential facts which required immediate consideration were particularly irksome to him.
uz: Darhol ko'rib chiqilishi kerak bo'lgan ba'zi muhim faktlar uni ayniqsa xafa qildi.

en: How glad he would have been to be free from some cares, the neglect of which would have threatened him with complete, inevitable ruin.
uz: U ba'zi tashvishlardan xalos bo'lganidan naqadar xursand bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak edi, ularning beparvoligi uni mutlaqo yo'q bo'lib ketish bilan tahdid qilgan bo'lardi.

en: He was particularly worried about Svidrigaïlov, he might be said to be permanently thinking of Svidrigaïlov.
uz: U Svidrigaylov haqida ayniqsa tashvishlangan, Svidrigaylov haqida doimiy ravishda o'ylayotganini aytsa bo'ladi.

en: From the time of Svidrigaïlov’s too menacing and unmistakable words in Sonia’s room at the moment of Katerina Ivanovna’s death, the normal working of his mind seemed to break down.
uz: Svidrigailovning Sonia xonasidagi qo'rqinchli va aniq so'zlaridan boshlab Katerina Ivanovna o'lgan paytgacha uning ongining odatiy faoliyati buzilib ketgan.

en: But although this new fact caused him extreme uneasiness, Raskolnikov was in no hurry for an
uz: Biroq, ushbu yangi fakt uni juda xavotirga solgan bo'lsa-da, Raskolnikov bir necha kunga shoshilmadi.

en: At times, finding himself in a solitary and remote part of the town, in some wretched eating-house, sitting alone lost in thought, hardly knowing how he had come there, he suddenly thought of Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Ba'zan o'zini shaharning yolg'iz va chekka qismida, ba'zi qashshoq ovqatxonada, yolg'iz o'tirib, fikr-mulohazalarda adashib, qayerdan kelganini bilmay, birdan Svidrigailov haqida o'yladi.

en: He recognised suddenly, clearly, and with dismay that he ought at once to come to an understanding with that man and to make what terms he could.
uz: U to'satdan, aniq va dahshatga to'lib, o'sha odam bilan darhol kelishuvga erishish va imkon qadar shart-sharoitlar tuzish kerakligini angladi.

en: Walking outside the city gates one day, he positively fancied that they had fixed a meeting there, that he was waiting for Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Bir kuni shahar darvozalari tashqarisida yurganida, u o'zi Svidrigaylovni kutib turganini, ular u yerda uchrashuv o'tkazganini aniq tasavvur qildi.

en: Another time he woke up before daybreak lying on the ground under some bushes and could not at first understand how he had come there.
uz: Boshqa safar esa u kunduz yorug'ligidan oldin er yuzida bir nechta butalar ostida yotgan holda uyg'onib qoldi va dastlab u yerga qanday yetib kelganini tushunmadi.

en: But during the two or three days after Katerina Ivanovna’s death, he had two or three times met Svidrigaïlov at Sonia’s lodging, where he had gone aimlessly for a moment.
uz: Ammo Katerina Ivanovna vafot etganidan ikki-uch kun o'tgach, u ikki-uch marta Svidrigailov bilan Sonia uyida uchrashdi, u yerda u biroz maqsadsiz ketdi.

en: They exchanged a few words and made no reference to the vital subject, as though they were tacitly agreed not to speak of it for a time.
uz: Ular bir necha so'z almashdilar va muhim mavzuga hech qanday izoh bermadilar, xuddi biroz vaqt davomida bu mavzu haqida gaplashmaslik to'g'risida so'zsiz kelishib olganlar kabi.

en: Katerina Ivanovna’s body was still lying in the coffin, Svidrigaïlov was busy making arrangements for the funeral.
uz: Katerina Ivanovna jasadi hali ham ko'krakda yotgan edi, Svidrigailov esa o'z vaqtida o'lim marosimiga tayyorgarlik ko'rish bilan band edi.

en: Sonia too was very busy.
uz: Sonia ham juda band edi.

en: At their last meeting Svidrigaïlov informed Raskolnikov that he had made an arrangement, and a very satisfactory one, for Katerina Ivanovna’s children; that he had, through certain connections, succeeded in getting hold of certain personages by whose help the three orphans could be at once placed in very suitable institutions; that the money he had settled on them had been of great assistance, as it is much easier to place orphans with some property than destitute ones.
uz: Ularning so'nggi uchrashuvida Svidrigailov Raskolnikovga Katerina Ivanovna farzandlari uchun juda mamnuniyatli kelishuvni amalga oshirganini, ba'zi aloqalar orqali uchta yetimning yordamida birdan juda mos muassasalarga joylashtirilishi mumkin bo'lgan ba'zi shaxslarga ega bo'lganini va yetimlarni moddiy tomondan joylashtirish ancha osonroq bo'lgani sababli, ular uchun ajratilgan pul juda yordamchi ekanligini aytdi.

en: He said something too about Sonia and promised to come himself in a day or two to see Raskolnikov, mentioning that “he would like to consult with him, that there were things they must talk over.
uz: U Sonia haqida ham gapirgan va Raskolnikovni ko'rish uchun bir-ikki kun ichida o'zi kelishni va'da qilgan.

en: …” This conversation took place in the passage on the stairs.
uz: ... Ushbu suhbat mertabaning o'tishida bo'lib o'tdi.

en: Svidrigaïlov looked intently at Raskolnikov and suddenly, after a brief pause, dropping his voice, asked: “But how is it, Rodion Romanovitch; you don’t seem yourself?
uz: Svidrigailov Raskolnikovga diqqat bilan qaradi va to'satdan, biroz to'xtab, ovozini pastga solgach, so'radi: "Agar shunday bo'lsa-da, Rodion Romanovitch; o'zingizni ko'rmayapsizlarmi?

en: You look and you listen, but you don’t seem to understand.
uz: Siz ko'rib, tinglaysiz, lekin tushunmayapsiz.

en: We’ll talk things over; I am only sorry, I’ve so much to do of my own business and other people’s.
uz: Biz bu haqda gaplashamiz; faqat uzr so'rayman, men o'z ishim va boshqa odamlarning ishida juda ko'p ishlarim bor.

en: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch,” he added suddenly, “what all men need is fresh air, fresh air … more than anything!”
uz: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch, u to'satdan qo'shimcha qildi,barcha odamlar toza havoga, toza havoga muhtojlar... hamma narsadan ko'ra ko'proq!

en: He moved to one side to make way for the priest and server, who were coming up the stairs.
uz: U bir tomonga o'tib, pastga ko'tarilgan ruhoniy va xizmatkorga yo'l ochdi.

en: They had come for the requiem service.
uz: Ular requiem xizmati uchun kelgan edilar.

en: By Svidrigaïlov’s orders it was sung twice a day punctually.
uz: Svidrigailovning buyrug'i bo'yicha kuniga ikki marta to'g'ri o'tkazilardi.

en: Svidrigaïlov went his way.
uz: Svidrigailov o'z yo'lidan ketdi.

en: Raskolnikov stood still a moment, thought, and followed the priest into Sonia’s room.
uz: Raskolnikov bir muncha vaqt to'xtadi, o'yladi va ruhoniyni Sonia xonasiga ergashib kirdi.

en: He stood at the door.
uz: U eshik oldida turgan edi.

en: They began quietly, slowly and mournfully singing the service.
uz: Ular xotirjamlik bilan, sekin-sekin va qayg'u bilan xizmatni kuylashdi.

en: From his childhood the thought of death and the presence of death had something oppressive and mysteriously awful; and it was long since he had heard the requiem service.
uz: Bolaligidan boshlab o'lim va uning mavjudligi haqidagi fikrlar g'amgin va sirli darajada dahshatli edi; va u uzoq vaqtdan beri requiem xizmatini eshitmagan edi.

en: And there was something else here as well, too awful and disturbing.
uz: Bu yerda ham boshqa bir narsa bor edi, juda dahshatli va xavotirga soluvchi.

en: He looked at the children: they were all kneeling by the coffin; Polenka was weeping.
uz: U bolalarga qaradi: ularning hammasi ko'krak yonida tiz cho'kgan edilar; Polenka yig'lab yurgan edi.

en: Behind them Sonia prayed, softly and, as it were, timidly weeping.
uz: Sonia ularning orqasidan so'ng, so'nggicha va qo'rqmasdan yig'lab ibodat qilardi.

en: “These last two days she hasn’t said a word to me, she hasn’t glanced at me,” Raskolnikov thought suddenly.
uz: O'tgan ikki kun ichida u menga bir so'z aytmadi, menga nazar solmadi, Raskolnikov to'satdan o'yladi.

en: The sunlight was bright in the room; the incense rose in clouds; the priest read, “Give rest, oh Lord.
uz: Xonada quyosh nuri porlab turardi; xushbo'y tutatqi bulutlar ichida ko'tarildi; ruhoniy o'qib o'tdi: "Ey Rabbim, dam olgin.

en: …” Raskolnikov stayed all through the service.
uz: ... Raskolnikov butun xizmat davomida qoldi.

en: As he blessed them and took his leave, the priest looked round strangely.
uz: U ularni duo qilib ketayotganda, ruhoniy atrofini g'ayrioddiy ko'rib qoldi.

en: After the service, Raskolnikov went up to Sonia.
uz: Xizmatdan so'ng Raskolnikov Soniaga bordi.

en: She took both his hands and let her head sink on his shoulder.
uz: U ikkala qo'lini ham olib, boshini uning yelkasiga qo'yib qo'ydi.

en: This slight friendly gesture bewildered Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu yengil do'stona harakat Raskolnikovni hayratda qoldirdi.

en: It seemed strange to him that there was no trace of repugnance, no trace of disgust, no tremor in her hand.
uz: Uning qo'lida jirkanchlik, jirkanchlik, titrashning hech qanday izlari yo'qligi unga g'alati tuyuldi.

en: It was the furthest limit of self-abnegation, at least so he interpreted it.
uz: Bu o'z-o'zidan voz kechishning eng uzoq chegarasi edi, hech bo'lmaganda u buni shunday ta'riflagan.

en: Raskolnikov pressed her hand and went out.
uz: Raskolnikov uning qo'lini bosib, tashqariga chiqdi.

en: He felt very miserable.
uz: U o'zini juda baxtsiz his qilgan.

en: If it had been possible to escape to some solitude, he would have thought himself lucky, even if he had to spend his whole life there.
uz: Agar u yolg'izlikka qochib ketish mumkin bo'lgan bo'lsa, u o'zini baxtli deb hisoblagan bo'lardi, hatto butun umrini u yerda o'tkazishi kerak bo'lgan bo'lsa ham.

en: But although he had almost always been by himself of late, he had never been able to feel alone.
uz: Ammo u deyarli har doim o'zicha bo'lgan bo'lsa-da, hech qachon o'zini yolg'iz his qila olmagan.

en: Sometimes he walked out of the town on to the high road, once he had even reached a little wood, but the lonelier the place was, the more he seemed to be aware of an uneasy presence near him.
uz: Ba'zan u shahardan tashqariga chiqib, yo'lga chiqardi, hatto o'rmishga yetib borganida, lekin u joy qanchalik yolg'iz bo'lsa, yaqin atrofidagi noqulay holatni shunchalik yaxshi tushunardi.

en: It did not frighten him, but greatly annoyed him, so that he made haste to return to the town, to mingle with the crowd, to enter restaurants and taverns, to walk in busy thoroughfares.
uz: Bu uni qo'rqitmadi, balki juda xafa qildi, shuning uchun u shaharga qaytib, xaloyiq bilan aralashib, restoranlar va tavernalarga kirishga, mashhur yo'llarda yurishga shoshildi.

en: There he felt easier and even more solitary.
uz: U yerda u o'zini osonroq va hatto yolg'izroq his qilgan.

en: One day at dusk he sat for an hour listening to songs in a tavern and he remembered that he positively enjoyed it.
uz: Bir kuni tong tushganda u bir soat davomida bir mehmonxonada qo'shiqlarni tinglab o'tirdi va unga yoqqanini esladi.

en: But at last he had suddenly felt the same uneasiness again, as though his
uz: Ammo nihoyat, to'satdan u o'sha noqulaylikni yana his qilgan edi, xuddi o'zidan kelib chiqqanidek.

en: conscience smote him.
uz: Uni vijdon urgan.

en: “Here I sit listening to singing, is that what I ought to be doing?” he thought.
uz: Men shu yerda o'tirib qo'shiq tinglayman, men shunday qilishim kerakmi? - deb o'yladi u.

en: Yet he felt at once that that was not the only cause of his uneasiness; there was something requiring immediate decision, but it was something he could not clearly understand or put into words.
uz: Ammo u darhol o'z xavotirining yagona sababi emasligini his qildi; biror qaror qabul qilish kerak bo'lgan narsa bor edi, ammo u buni aniq tushunish yoki so'zlar bilan ifodalash mumkin emas edi.

en: It was a hopeless tangle.
uz: Bu umidsizlikka uchraydi.

en: “No, better the struggle again!
uz: Yo'q, yana kurash yaxshidir!

en: Better Porfiry again … or Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Yaxshi Porfiry yana ... yoki Svidrigailov.

en: … Better some challenge again … some attack.
uz: ... Yana bir bor qiyinchilikka duch kelsa yaxshi bo'lardi.

en: Yes, yes!” he thought.
uz: Ha, ha! deb o'yladi u.

en: He went out of the tavern and rushed away almost at a run.
uz: U mehmonxonadan chiqib, deyarli yugurib ketdi.

en: The thought of Dounia and his mother suddenly reduced him almost to a panic.
uz: Dounia va uning onasi haqida o'ylash uni to'satdan deyarli qo'rquvga tushirdi.

en: That night he woke up before morning among some bushes in Krestovsky Island, trembling all over with fever; he walked home, and it was early morning when he arrived.
uz: O'sha kecha u Krestovskiy orolidagi bir nechta butalar orasidan ertalab uyg'onib, butun joyida issiqdan titrab, uyga yurdi va ertalab kelganida ertalab edi.

en: After some hours’ sleep the fever left him, but he woke up late, two o’clock in the afternoon.
uz: Bir necha soat uxlaganidan so'ng, issiqlik uni tark etdi, lekin u kech uyg'ondi, kechki payt soat ikkilarda.

en: He remembered that Katerina Ivanovna’s funeral had been fixed for that day, and was glad that he was not present at it.
uz: U Katerina Ivanovna o'z dafn marosimi o'sha kun uchun rejalashtirilganligini eslab, u yerda bo'lmaganidan xursand bo'ldi.

en: Nastasya brought him some food; he ate and drank with appetite, almost with greediness.
uz: Nastasya unga ovqat olib keldi; u ochko'zlik bilan, deyarli ochko'zlik bilan yeb-ichdi.

en: His head was fresher and he was calmer than he had been for the last three days.
uz: Uning boshi yangi va so'nggi uch kundan beri bo'lganiga qaraganda xotirjamroq edi.

en: He even felt a passing wonder at his previous attacks of panic.
uz: U hatto o'zining avvalgi qo'rquv hujumlariga o'tib ketayotgan hayratlanishini his qildi.

en: The door opened and Razumihin came in.
uz: Eshik ochildi va Razumihin kirdi.

en: “Ah, he’s eating, then he’s not ill,” said Razumihin.
uz: Ah, u ovqatlanmoqda, shuning uchun u kasal emas, - dedi Razumihin.

en: He took a chair and sat down at the table opposite Raskolnikov.
uz: U o'rinni olib, Raskolnikovning qarshisidagi stolga o'tirdi.

en: He was troubled and did not attempt to conceal it.
uz: U xavotirga tushdi va buni yashirishga urinmadi.

en: He spoke with evident annoyance, but without hurry or raising his voice.
uz: U ochiq-oydin xafalik bilan gapirgan, lekin shoshilmasdan yoki ovozini ko'tarmasdan.

en: He looked as though he had some special fixed determination.
uz: U o'ziga xos qat'iy qarorga ega bo'lgani kabi ko'rinardi.

en: “Listen,” he began resolutely.
uz: Quloq solinglar, u qat'iylik bilan boshladi.

en: “As far as I am concerned, you may all go to hell, but from what I see, it’s clear to me that I can’t make head or tail of it; please don’t think I’ve come to ask you questions.
uz: Menga kelsak, hammangiz jahannamga ketishingiz mumkin, lekin ko'rganimdan ko'rinib turibdiki, men bu haqda o'ylamasligimni aniq bilaman; iltimos, savol berish uchun kelganimni o'ylamang.

en: I don’t want to know, hang it!
uz: Bilishni istamayman, asring!

en: If you begin telling me your secrets, I dare say I shouldn’t stay to listen, I should go away cursing.
uz: Agar siz menga sirlaringizni aytishni boshlayotgan bo'lsangiz, men tinglash uchun qolishim kerak emas, deb aytishga jur'at qilaman.

en: I have only come to find out once for all whether it’s a fact that you are mad?
uz: Men faqatgina bir marta va butunlayin bilishim uchun keldim, agar siz g'alati ekanligingiz to'g'ri yoki yo'qmi?

en: There is a conviction in the air that you are mad or very nearly so.
uz: Havoda siz aqldan ozganingiz yoki deyarli aqldan ozganingiz haqidagi fikr bor.

en: I admit I’ve been disposed to that opinion myself, judging from your stupid, repulsive and quite inexplicable actions, and from your recent behavior to your mother and sister.
uz: Men o'zim ham o'sha fikrga moyil bo'lganimni tan olaman, sizning ahmoqona, jirkanch va to'liq tushuntirilmaydigan harakatlaringiz va o'zingizning onangiz va singil-singilingizga nisbatan so'nggi davringizda qanday munosabatda bo'lganingizdan so'ng.

en: Only a monster or a madman could treat them as you have; so you must be mad.” “When did you see them last?”
uz: Faqatgina g'ayritabiiy hayvon yoki aqldan ozgan odam ularga siz kabi munosabatda bo'lishi mumkin; shuning uchun siz g'alati bo'lishingiz kerak.  Siz ularni oxirgi marta qachon ko'rdingiz?

en: Haven’t you seen them since then?
uz: O'shandan beri ularni ko'rmadingizmi?

en: What have you been doing with yourself?
uz: O'zingiz bilan nima qilyapsiz?

en: I’ve been to you three times already.
uz: Men sizlarning oldingizga uch marta borganman.

en: Your mother has been seriously ill since yesterday.
uz: Onangiz kechadan boshlab jiddiy kasal bo'lgan.

en: She had made up her mind to come to you; Avdotya Romanovna tried to prevent her; she wouldn’t hear a word.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna unga to'sqinlik qilishga harakat qildi, lekin u bir so'z ham eshitmadi.

en: ‘If he is ill, if his mind is giving way, who can look after him like his mother?’ she said.
uz: Agar u bemor bo'lsa, agar uning ongi ketayotgan bo'lsa, unga onasi kabi kim g'amxo'rlik qila oladi? - dedi u.

en: We all came here together, we couldn’t let her come alone all the way.
uz: Biz hammamiz birga keldik, biz uni butun yo'lni yolg'iz ketishiga yo'l qo'ymaymiz.

en: We kept begging her to be calm.
uz: Biz unga tinchlikni saqlab qolish uchun iltijo qilardik.

en: We came in, you weren’t here; she sat down, and stayed ten minutes, while we stood waiting in silence.
uz: Biz kirdik, siz kelmadingiz; u o'tirib, o'n daqiqa o'tirdi, biz esa xotirjamlik bilan kutib turdik.

en: She got up and said: ‘If he’s gone out, that is, if he is well, and has forgotten his mother, it’s humiliating and unseemly for his mother to stand at his door begging for kindness.’ She returned home and took to her bed; now she is in a fever.
uz: U o'rnidan turib shunday dedi: "Agar u chiqib ketgan bo'lsa, ya'ni u sog'lom bo'lsa va onasini unutib qo'ygan bo'lsa, onasi uning eshigida uning inoyatini so'rab turishi noloyiq va noloyiqdir. U uyga qaytib, o'z yotoqxonasiga o'tirdi; hozir u issiqdan azob chekadi.

en: ‘I see,’ she said, ‘that he has time for his girl.’ She means by your girl Sofya Semyonovna, your betrothed or your mistress, I don’t know.
uz: U: "Qizim uchun vaqt borligini bilaman", - dedi.U qizingiz Sofiya Semyonovna, sening kelin-qizing yoki sevgiling haqida gapiryapti, men bilmayman.

en: I went at once to Sofya Semyonovna’s, for I wanted to know what was going on.
uz: Men darhol Sofiya Semyonovnasga bordim, chunki nima bo'layotganini bilmoqchi edim.

en: I looked round, I saw the coffin, the children crying, and Sofya Semyonovna trying them on mourning dresses.
uz: Men atrofimni ko'rdim, ko'krakni, yig'layotgan bolalarni va Sofya Semyonovna ularni qayg'u liboslari bilan sinab ko'rdim.

en: I apologised, came away, and reported to Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Men kechirim so'radim, ketdim va Avdotya Romanovnaga xabar berdim.

en: So that’s all nonsense and you haven’t got a girl; the most likely thing is that you are mad.
uz: Demak, bularning hammasi behuda va sizda qiz yo'q; ehtimol siz g'alati ekansiz.

en: But here you sit, guzzling boiled beef as though you’d not had a bite for three days.
uz: Ammo mana, uch kun davomida biron narsa yemaganingiz kabi, qaynatilgan go'sht go'shti bilan o'tiribsiz.

en: Though as far as that goes, madmen eat too, but though you have not said a word to me yet … you are not mad!
uz: Garchi shunga qaramasdan, aqldan ozganlar ham ovqat yeyishsa-da, lekin siz menga hali bir so'z aytmagan bo'lsangiz ham... siz aqldan ozgan emassiz!

en: Above all, you are not mad!
uz: Eng muhimi, siz g'alati emassiz!

en: So you may go to hell, all of you, for there’s some mystery, some secret about it, and I don’t intend to worry my brains over your secrets.
uz: Shunday qilib, barchangiz jahannamga ketishingiz mumkin, chunki bu erda bir nechta sir, sir bor va men sizning sirlaringiz haqida o'z miyamni tashvishlantirmoqchi emasman.

en: So I’ve simply come to swear at you,” he finished, getting up, “to relieve my mind.
uz: Shunday qilib, men shunchaki senga qasam ichishga keldim, - dedi u, so'ng o'rnidan turib, fikrimni yengillashtirdi.

en: And I know what to do now.” “What do you mean to do now?” “What business is it of yours what I mean to do?” “You are going in for a drinking bout.” “How … how did you know?” “Why, it’s pretty plain.” Razumihin paused for a minute.
uz: Endi nima qilishimni bilaman.  Hozir nima qilishni xohlaysiz?  Men nima qilishni xohlayotganimni sizga nima bog'liq?  Siz ichimlik to'g'risida bahslashyapsiz.  Qanday qilib bilding?  Nima uchun, bu juda aniq. Razumihin bir daqiqa to'xtadi.

en: “You always have been a very rational person and you’ve never been mad, never,” he observed suddenly with warmth.
uz: Siz har doim juda oqilona inson bo'lgansiz va hech qachon g'alati bo'lmagansiz, hech qachon, - deb o'yladi u kutilmaganda iliqlik bilan.

en: “You’re right: I shall drink.
uz: Siz haqsiz: men ichaman.

en: And he moved to go out.
uz: U tashqariga chiqishga harakat qildi.

en: “I was talking with my sister —the day before yesterday, I think it was —about you, Razumihin.” “About me!
uz: Kecha opam bilan gaplashayotgan edim, o'ylaymanki, bu sen haqingda, Razumihin.

en: But … where can you have seen her the day before yesterday?” Razumihin stopped short and even turned a little pale.
uz: Ammo ... siz uni bir kun oldin qaerda ko'rgan bo'lasiz? Razumihin qisqa vaqt ichida to'xtadi va hatto biroz o'tkirlandi.

en: One could see that his heart was throbbing slowly and violently.
uz: Uning yuragi asta-sekin va qattiq urib ketayotganini ko'rish mumkin edi.

en: “She came here by herself, sat there and talked to me.” “She did!” “Yes.” “What did you say to her … I mean, about me?” “I told her you were a very good, honest, and industrious man.
uz: U bu yerga o'zi kelib, o'tirdi va men bilan gaplashdi.  U shunday qildi!  Ha.  Unga nima deyish kerak edi... o'zim haqida?  Men unga juda yaxshi, halol va mehnatsevar odam ekanligingizni aytdim.

en: I didn’t tell her you love her, because she knows that herself.” “She knows that herself?” “Well, it’s pretty plain.
uz: Men unga sevganingizni aytmadim, chunki u buni o'zi biladi. O'zi buni biladi? Ha, bu juda aniq.

en: Wherever I might go, whatever happened to me, you would remain to look after them.
uz: Men qayerga borsam ham, menga nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, siz ularga g'amxo'rlik qilish uchun qolishingiz kerak edi.

en: I, so to speak, give them into your keeping, Razumihin.
uz: Men, demak, ularni sizning saqlashingizga beraman, Razumihin.

en: I say this because I know quite well how you love her, and am convinced of the purity of your heart.
uz: Men buni aytaman, chunki men uni qanchalik yaxshi ko'rganingizni yaxshi bilaman va yuragingiz pokligiga ishonaman.

en: I know that she too may love you and perhaps does love you already.
uz: Men uning ham seni sevishini bilaman va ehtimol allaqachon seni yaxshi ko'radi.

en: Now decide for yourself, as you know best, whether you need go in for a drinking bout or not.” “Rodya!
uz: Endi siz yaxshi bilganingizdek, o'zingiz hal qiling, ichimlik bilan shug'ullanishingiz kerakmi yoki yo'qmi. Rodya!

en: But where do you mean to go?
uz: Ammo qayerga borishni xohlaysiz?

en: Of course, if it’s all a secret, never mind.
uz: Albatta, agar bu hamma narsa sir bo'lsa, bu muhim emas.

en: … But I … I shall find out the secret … and I am sure that it must be some ridiculous nonsense and that you’ve made it all up.
uz: Lekin men sirni bilib olaman va shubhasizki, bu biroz g'alati gap bo'lishi kerak va siz hammasini o'zingiz uydirib qo'ydingiz.

en: Anyway you are a capital fellow, a capital fellow!
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, siz kapitallik a'zosiz, kapitallik a'zosiz!

en: …” “That was just what I wanted to add, only you interrupted, that that was a very good decision of yours not to find out these secrets.
uz: ... Mana shularni qo'shmoqchi edim, faqat siz aralashtirdingiz, bu sizning bu sirlarni bilmaslik to'g'risidagi juda yaxshi qaroringiz edi.

en: Leave it to time, don’t worry about it.
uz: O'z vaqtida qoldiring, bu haqda tashvishlanmang.

en: You’ll know it all in time when it must be.
uz: Vaqt o'tib, hamma narsani bilib olasiz.

en: Yesterday a man said to me that what a man needs is fresh air, fresh air, fresh air.
uz: Kecha bir kishi menga erkak kishiga toza havo, toza havo, toza havo kerakligini aytdi.

en: I mean to go to him directly to find out what he meant by that.” Razumihin stood lost in thought and excitement, making a silent conclusion.
uz: Men to'g'ridan-to'g'ri uning oldiga borib, u bu so'zlar bilan nima demoqchiligini bilib olmoqchiman. Razumihin o'ylashda va hayajonda adashib, so'zsiz xulosa chiqardi.

en: “He’s a political conspirator!
uz: U siyosiy tuzumchilardir!

en: And he’s on the eve of some desperate step, that’s certain.
uz: Va u, shubhasiz, biron bir umidsiz qadam qo'yish arafasida.

en: It can only be that!
uz: Bu faqat shu bo'lishi mumkin!

en: And … and Dounia knows,” he thought suddenly.
uz: Va ... va Dounia biladi, u to'satdan o'yladi.

en: “So Avdotya Romanovna comes to see you,” he said, weighing each syllable, “and you’re going to see a man who says we need more air, and so of course that letter … that too must have something to do with it,” he concluded to himself.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna sizni ko'rishga keladi, - dedi u, har bir harfni o'lchab, - va siz ko'rasiz, u bizga ko'proq havo kerak, deb aytadigan odam, va shu sababli, albatta, bu xat ... bu ham bunga aloqasi bor, - deb o'zicha xulosa qildi u.

en: “What letter?” “She got a letter today.
uz: Qanday xat?U bugun xat oldi.

en: It upset her very much —very much indeed.
uz: Bu uni juda ko'p xafa qildi.

en: I began speaking of you, she begged me not to.
uz: Men siz haqingizda gapirishni boshladim, lekin u buni qilmaslikka iltijo qildi.

en: Then  … then she said that perhaps we should very soon have to part … then she began warmly thanking me for something; then she went to her room and locked herself in.” “She got a letter?” Raskolnikov asked thoughtfully.
uz: Keyin ... keyin u, ehtimol biz tez orada ajrashishimiz kerakligini aytdi ... keyin u menga biron narsa uchun samimiy minnatdorchilik bildirishni boshladi; keyin o'z xonasidan chiqib, o'zini o'ziga qulflab qo'ydi.  U xat oldi? Raskolnikov mulohaza bilan so'radi.

en: “Yes, and you didn’t know?
uz: Ha, lekin siz bilmas edingizmi?

en: hm …” They were both silent.
uz: Ular ikkalasi ham sukut saqlashdi.

en: There was a time, brother, when I.
uz: Bir vaqtlar, birodarim, men.

en: … Never mind, goodbye.
uz: ...Mening o'ylaymanki, xayrlashamiz.

en: You see, there was a time.
uz: Ko'rib turganingizdek, bir vaqtlar ham shunday bo'lgan.

en: I am not going to drink.
uz: Men ichmayman.

en: There’s no need now.
uz: Hozir bu kerak emas.

en: … That’s all stuff!” He hurried out; but when he had almost closed the door behind him, he suddenly opened it again, and said, looking away: “Oh, by the way, do you remember that murder, you know Porfiry’s, that old woman?
uz: U shoshilib chiqdi, lekin deyarli eshikni yopib qo'yganida, uni birdan qayta ochdi va chetga qarab: "Oh, shu yo'l bilan, o'sha qotillikni eslaysizmi, bu Porfirylarni, bu keksa ayolni?

en: Do you know the murderer has been found, he has confessed and given the proofs.
uz: Qotil topilgan, tan olgan va dalillar berganini bilasizmi?

en: It’s one of those very workmen, the painter, only fancy!
uz: Bu o'sha ishchilardan biri, rassom, faqat o'yinchi!

en: Do you remember I defended them here?
uz: Men ularni bu yerda himoya qilganimni eslaysizmi?

en: Would you believe it, all that scene of fighting and laughing with his companions on the stairs while the porter and the two witnesses were going up, he got up on purpose to disarm suspicion.
uz: Ishonchim komilki, eshikni ko'tarib turgan portiyer va ikkita shohidlar bilan uchrashib, uning do'stlari bilan to'qnashgan va kulgan ko'rinishi, u o'zi bilgan holda shubhalarni bartaraf etish uchun o'rnidan turdi.

en: The cunning, the presence of mind of the young dog!
uz: Yigitning hiyla-nayrangligi, aql-idrokining mavjudligi!

en: One can hardly credit it; but it’s his own explanation, he has confessed it all.
uz: Buni hech kim e'tirof qila olmaydi; lekin bu uning o'z tushuntirishi, u hamma narsani tan oldi.

en: And what a fool I was about it!
uz: Va men bu borada qanday ahmoq bo'lganman!

en: Well, he’s simply a genius of hypocrisy and resourcefulness in disarming the suspicions of the lawyers —so there’s nothing much to wonder at, I suppose!
uz: Ha, u shunchaki advokatlarning shubhalarini bartaraf etishda ikkiyuzlamachilik va aql-idrokning geniysi, shuning uchun, taxmin qilamanki, hayron bo'lish uchun hech narsa yo'q!

en: Of course people like that are always possible.
uz: Albatta, bunday odamlar har doim ham mumkin.

en: And the fact that he couldn’t keep up the character, but confessed, makes him easier to believe in.
uz: Va u o'z xarakterini saqlay olmaganligi, ammo tan olganligi unga ishonishni osonlashtiradi.

en: But what a fool I was!
uz: Ammo men qanday ahmoq bo'lganman!

en: I was frantic on their side!” “Tell me, please, from whom did you hear that, and why does it interest you so?” Raskolnikov asked with unmistakable agitation.
uz: Men ularning tarafida g'azablanardim!  Iltimos, menga ayt, buni kimdan eshitgansiz va nega bu sizga shunchalik qiziqish uyg'otadi? Raskolnikov aniq g'ayrat bilan so'radi.

en: You ask me why it interests me!
uz: Siz mendan nega bu menga qiziqish ko'rsatishini so'raysiz!

en: … Well, I heard it from Porfiry, among others … It was from him I heard almost all about it.” “From Porfiry?” “From Porfiry.” “What … what did he say?” Raskolnikov asked in dismay.
uz: Men buni Porfiridan, shu jumladan, boshqalardan eshitdim... Undan deyarli hamma narsani eshitganman.Porfiridan?Porfiridan. nima... nima dedi? Raskolnikov dahshatga tushib so'radi.

en: “He gave me a capital explanation of it.
uz: U menga bu haqda katta tushuntirish berdi.

en: Psychologically, after his fashion.” “He explained it?
uz: Psixologik jihatdan esa, o'z modasiga qarab.U buni tushuntirdi?

en: Explained it himself?” “Yes, yes; goodbye.
uz: Buni o'zi tushuntirganmi?Ha, ha; salom.

en: I’ll tell you all about it another time, but now I’m busy.
uz: Bu haqda boshqa safar aytib beraman, lekin hozir juda bandman.

en: There was a time when I fancied … But no matter, another time!
uz: Bir vaqtlar men o'zimni o'ylagandim, lekin boshqa bir vaqtda!

en: … What need is there for me to drink now?
uz: Endi men nima ichishim kerak?

en: You have made me drunk without wine.
uz: Siz meni sharobsiz mast qildingiz.

en: I’ll come again very soon.” He went out.
uz: Men tezda qaytaman.U tashqariga chiqdi.

en: “He’s a political conspirator, there’s not a doubt about it,” Razumihin decided, as he slowly descended the stairs.
uz: U siyosiy sherik, shubhasiz,  Razumihin qaror qildi, u sekin-sakin mertabanlardan tushdi.

en: “And he’s drawn his sister in; that’s quite, quite in keeping with Avdotya Romanovna’s character.
uz: Va u o'z singlisini o'ziga jalb qildi; bu Avdotya Romanovna xarakteriga to'g'ri, to'g'ri mos keladi.

en: There are interviews between them!
uz: Ular o'rtasida intervyular bor!

en: … She hinted at it too … So many of her words … and hints … bear that meaning!
uz: Uning so'zlari va izohlarining ko'pchiligi bu ma'noga ega!

en: And how else can all this tangle be explained?
uz: Va boshqa qanday qilib bu to'siqni tushuntirish mumkin?

en: And I was almost thinking … Good heavens, what I thought!
uz: Va men deyarli o'ylay boshlagan edim... Xudoyim, men o'ylaganday bo'ldim!

en: Yes, I took leave of my senses and I wronged him!
uz: Ha, men aqldan ozdim va unga zulm qildim!

en: It was his doing, under the lamp in the corridor that day.
uz: O'sha kuni koridordagi chiroq ostida o'z ishi edi.

en: What a crude, nasty, vile idea on my part!
uz: Mening o'zimdan bu qanday qo'pol, jirkanch va yomon fikr!

en: Nikolay is a brick, for confessing.
uz: Nikolay tanbeh berish uchun tosh bo'lgan.

en: … And how clear it all is now!
uz: Va hozir hamma narsa qanchalik aniq!

en: His illness then, all his strange actions … before this, in the university, how morose he used to be, how gloomy.
uz: O'sha paytdagi kasalligi, uning barcha g'alati harakatlari... bundan oldin universitetda, u qanchalik chiroyli, qanchalik tushkun edi.

en: … But what’s the meaning now of that letter?
uz: Ammo bu harfning hozirgi ma'nosi nima?

en: There’s something in that, too, perhaps.
uz: Ehtimol, bunda ham biror narsa bor.

en: No, I must find out!” He thought of Dounia, realising all he had heard and his heart throbbed, and he suddenly broke into a run.
uz: Yo'q, bilishim kerak! U Duniyani o'ylab ko'rdi, eshitganlarining barchasini anglab, yuragi urib ketdi va to'satdan u yugurib ketdi.

en: As soon as Razumihin went out, Raskolnikov got up, turned to the window, walked into one corner and then into another, as though forgetting the smallness of his room, and sat down again on the sofa.
uz: Razumihin chiqib ketgandan so'ng, Raskolnikov o'rnidan turib, darchaga qarab, bir burchakga, keyin esa boshqa burchakga kirdi va o'z xonasining kichikligini unutib qo'ygani kabi sofaga yana o'tirdi.

en: He felt, so to speak, renewed; again the struggle, so a means of escape had come.
uz: U o'zini xuddi yangilab ko'rgan bo'lsa kerak; yana kurash, shuning uchun qochish usuli paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Yes, a means of escape had come!
uz: Ha, qochish usuli paydo bo'ldi!
