uz: Agar uning sirini bilib, uning ustidan hokimiyatni egallagan bo'lsa-chi, uni Douniaga qarshi qurol sifatida ishlatsa-chi?

en: This idea sometimes even tormented his dreams, but it had never presented itself so vividly to him as on his way to Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Ba'zan bu g'oya hatto uning orzularini qiynagan, ammo u hech qachon Svidrigailovga borayotganida unga o'zini shunday yorqin ko'rsatmagan.

en: The very thought moved him to gloomy rage.
uz: O'sha fikr uni qayg'uli g'azabga tushirdi.

en: To begin with, this would transform everything, even his own position; he would have at once to confess his secret to Dounia.
uz: Avval, bu hamma narsani, hatto o'z pozitsiyasini ham o'zgartiradi; u darhol Douniaga sirini aytishi kerak bo'ladi.

en: Would he have to give himself up perhaps to prevent Dounia from taking some rash step?
uz: Ehtimol, Dounia o'zini o'zi tashlab ketishiga yo'l qo'ymaslik uchun u o'zini berishga majbur bo'larmidi?

en: This morning Dounia had received a letter.
uz: Bugun ertalab Dounia xat oldi.

en: From whom could she get letters in Petersburg?
uz: Sankt-Peterburgda kimdan xatlar olish mumkin?

en: It’s true Razumihin was there to protect her, but Razumihin knew nothing of the position.
uz: To'g'ri, Razumihin uni himoya qilish uchun u erda edi, lekin Razumihin o'z vazifasini bilmagan.

en: Perhaps it was his duty to tell Razumihin?
uz: Ehtimol, Razumihinga aytish uning vazifasi edi?

en: He thought of it with repugnance.
uz: U bu haqda jirkanch fikrda edi.

en: In any case he must see Svidrigaïlov as soon as possible, he decided finally.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, u Svidrigailov bilan tezroq uchrashishi kerak, degan qarorga keldi.

en: Thank God, the details of the interview were of little
uz: Xudoga shukr, intervyu tafsilotlari kamroq edi.

en: consequence, if only he could get at the root of the matter; but if Svidrigaïlov were capable … if he were intriguing against Dounia — then … Raskolnikov was so exhausted by what he had passed through that month that he could only decide such questions in one way; “then I shall kill him,” he thought in cold despair.
uz: Agar Svidrigailov qobiliyatli bo'lganida, agar u Duniyaga qarshi g'alaba qozonishga qodir bo'lganida, Raskolnikov o'sha oy o'tgan voqealardan shunchalik charchagan ediki, bunday masalalarni faqat bir yo'l bilan hal qila olishi mumkin edi; "Shuning uchun uni o'ldiraman", - deb o'yladi u sovuq umidsizlikda.

en: A sudden anguish oppressed his heart, he stood still in the middle of the street and began looking about to see where he was and which way he was going.
uz: To'satdan dard yuragini bosib oldi, u ko'cha o'rtasida to'xtadi va qayerda va qay yo'ldan borayotganini ko'rish uchun atrofga qarab turdi.

en: He found himself in X — — Prospect, thirty or forty paces from the Hay Market, through which he had come.
uz: U o'zini X   Prospect-da topdi, u o'tgan Hay bozoriga o'ttiz yoki qirq qadam uzoqlikda edi.

en: The whole second storey of the house on the left was used as a tavern.
uz: Chapdagi uyning ikkinchi qavatidagi butun xonadon mehmonxona sifatida ishlatilgan.

en: All the windows were wide open; judging from the figures moving at the windows, the rooms were full to overflowing.
uz: Barcha derazalar keng ochilgan edi; derazalarda harakatlanayotgan raqamlardan ko'ra, xonalar to'liq bo'lib, to'lib-toshgan edi.

en: There were sounds of singing, of clarionet and violin, and the boom of a Turkish drum.
uz: Qo'shiq, klarineta va piyola tovushlari va turk davri shovqinlari eshitildi.

en: He could hear women shrieking.
uz: U ayollarning qichqiriqlarini eshitishi mumkin edi.

en: He was about to turn back wondering why he had come to the X — — Prospect, when suddenly at one of the end windows he saw Svidrigaïlov, sitting at a tea-table right in the open window with a pipe in his mouth.
uz: U nima uchun X   prospektiga kelganini o'ylab qaytib bormoqchi edi, lekin to'satdan o'tkir darchalardan birida Svidrigailovni ochilgan darcha oldida choy stolida o'tirganini ko'rdi.

en: Raskolnikov was dreadfully taken aback, almost terrified.
uz: Raskolnikov qo'rqinchli tarzda hayratda qoldi, deyarli qo'rqib ketdi.

en: Svidrigaïlov was silently watching and scrutinising him and, what struck Raskolnikov at once, seemed to be meaning to get up and slip away unobserved.
uz: Svidrigailov uni hushyorlik bilan kuzatib, sinchiklab o'tirardi va Raskolnikovni birdan urgan narsa ko'rinishicha, o'rnidan turib, ko'rinmay qochib ketmoqchi bo'ldi.

en: Raskolnikov at once pretended not to have seen him, but to be looking absentmindedly away, while he watched him out of the corner of his eye.
uz: Raskolnikov darhol uni ko'rmaganicha ko'z o'ngida ko'rib turardi va uni ko'z burchagidan ko'rib turardi.

en: His heart was beating violently.
uz: Uning yuragi qattiq urib turardi.

en: Yet, it was evident that Svidrigaïlov did not want to be seen.
uz: Shunga qaramay, Svidrigaylovning ko'rinishni istamasligi aniq edi.

en: He took the pipe out of his mouth and was on the point of concealing himself, but as he got up and moved back his chair, he seemed to have become suddenly aware that Raskolnikov had seen him, and was watching him.
uz: O'z og'zidan quvurni olib, o'zini yashirmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin o'rnidan turib, o'rindiqini o'zgartirganida, Raskolnikov uni ko'rganini va uni kuzatib turganini birdan sezdi.

en: What had passed between them was much the same as what happened at their first meeting in Raskolnikov’s room.
uz: Ularning o'rtasidagi voqealar Raskolnikov xonasidagi birinchi uchrashuvlarida sodir bo'lgan voqealarga o'xshaydi.

en: A sly smile came into Svidrigaïlov’s face and grew broader and broader.
uz: Svidrigailovning yuziga o'g'rilik ko'tarilib, ko'proq va ko'proq ko'paydi.

en: Each knew that he was seen and watched by the other.
uz: Har bir kishi o'zini boshqa birov ko'rib, kuzatib turganini bilardi.

en: At last Svidrigaïlov broke into a loud laugh.
uz: Oxir-oqibat Svidrigailov baland ovoz bilan kulishga tushdi.

en: “Well, well, come in if you want me; I am here!” he shouted from the window.
uz: - Agar meni xohlasangiz, kiringlar, men bu yerdaman! - deb o'qidi u o'rindiqdan.

en: Raskolnikov went up into the tavern.
uz: Raskolnikov mehmonxonaga bordi.

en: He found Svidrigaïlov in a tiny back room, adjoining the saloon in which merchants, clerks and
uz: U Svidrigaylovni saloonga yaqin joylashgan kichik orqa xonada topdi, unda savdogarlar, xizmatchilar va ishchilar yashardi.

en: numbers of people of all sorts were drinking tea at twenty little tables to the desperate bawling of a chorus of singers.
uz: Turli xil odamlar yigirma kichik stolda choy ichib, qo'shiqchilar chorusining g'amgin qichqiriqlariga to'g'ri keldi.

en: The click of billiard balls could be heard in the distance.
uz: Bilyarda g'iybatlari toshqini uzoqdan eshitildi.

en: On the table before Svidrigaïlov stood an open bottle and a glass half full of champagne.
uz: Svidrigailovning oldiga o'tirgan dasturxonda ochiq shisha va yarim shampanjga to'lgan shisha turgan edi.

en: In the room he found also a boy with a little hand organ, a healthy-looking red- cheeked girl of eighteen, wearing a tucked-up striped skirt, and a Tyrolese hat with ribbons.
uz: Xonada u kichik qo'l organli o'g'il, sog'lom ko'rinadigan o'n sakkiz yoshli qizil yigirmonni ham topdi.

en: In spite of the chorus in the other room, she was singing some servants’ hall song in a rather husky contralto, to the accompaniment of the organ.
uz: Boshqa xonada qo'shiq qo'shiqlariga qaramay, u orqan qo'shiqlarini qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarini qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlarida qo'shiq qo'shiq qo'shiqlari bilan kuylagan.

en: “Come, that’s enough,” Svidrigaïlov stopped her at Raskolnikov’s entrance.
uz: Yay, shu yetarli, Svidrigailov uni Raskolnikovning kirish joyida to'xtatdi.

en: The girl at once broke off and stood waiting respectfully.
uz: Qiz darhol bo'shashdi va hurmat bilan kutdi.

en: She had sung her guttural rhymes, too, with a serious and respectful expression in her face.
uz: O'zining guttural rimlarini ham, yuzidagi jiddiy va hurmat bilan kuylagan edi.

en: “Hey, Philip, a glass!” shouted Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Hey, Filip, bir stakan! Svidrigailov baqirib yubordi.

en: “I won’t drink anything,” said Raskolnikov.
uz: "Men hech narsa ichmayman", - dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “As you like, I didn’t mean it for you.
uz: Siz xohlagandek, men siz uchun buni nazarda tutmagan edim.

en: I don’t want anything more today, you can go.” He poured her out a full glass, and laid down a yellow note.
uz: Bugun men boshqa hech narsa istamayman, siz ketishingiz mumkin. U qizga to'liq shisha to'kib, sariq nota qo'ydi.

en: Katia drank off her glass of wine, as women do, without putting it down, in twenty gulps, took the note and kissed Svidrigaïlov’s hand, which he allowed quite seriously.
uz: Katia, ayollarga o'xshab, sharob shishalarini yigirma qoshiq ichida tushirmasdan ichdi, yozuvni oldi va Svidrigailovning qo'lini o'pdi.

en: She went out of the room and the boy trailed after her with the organ.
uz: U xonadan chiqib ketdi va o'g'il uning orqasidan organ bilan ergashib keldi.

en: Both had been brought in from the street.
uz: Ikkalasi ham ko'chadan olib kelingan edi.

en: Svidrigaïlov had not been a week in Petersburg, but everything about him was already, so to speak, on a patriarchal footing; the waiter, Philip, was by now an old friend and very obsequious.
uz: Svidrigailov Sankt-Peterburgda bir hafta ham bo'lmagan edi, ammo uning atrofidagi hamma narsa patriarkal asosda edi; xizmatkor Filip allaqachon eski do'st va juda itoatkor edi.

en: The door leading to the saloon had a lock on it.
uz: Salonga olib boradigan eshik qulflab qo'yilgan edi.

en: Svidrigaïlov was at home in this room and perhaps spent whole days in it.
uz: Svidrigailov uyda shu xonada bo'lgan va ehtimol u yerda kunlar o'tkazgan.

en: The tavern was dirty and wretched, not even second-rate.
uz: Mehmonxona kirli va qashshoq edi, hatto ikkinchi darajali ham emas edi.

en: “I was going to see you and looking for you,” Raskolnikov began, “but I don’t know what made me turn from the Hay Market into the X — — Prospect just now.
uz: Men sizni ko'rish va qidirish uchun ketardim,  Raskolnikov boshladi,  lekin men bilmayman, nima tufayli men Hay bozoriga o'tdim va hozir X   istiqbolga aylandim.

en: I never take this turning.
uz: Men hech qachon bu burilishni qabul qilmayman.

en: I turn to the right from the Hay Market.
uz: Men Hay bozori shahriga o'ng tomonga burindim.

en: And this isn’t the way to you.
uz: Va bu sizning yo'lingiz emas.

en: I simply turned and here you are.
uz: Men shunchaki o'girdim va mana sen borasan.

en: It is strange!” “Why don’t you say at once ‘it’s a miracle’?” “Because it may be only chance.”
uz: Bu g'alati narsa! Nega siz darhol mo'jiza deb aytmaysiz? Chunki bu shunchaki tasodif bo'lishi mumkin.

en: “Oh, that’s the way with all you folk,” laughed Svidrigaïlov.
uz: - Ey, sizlar bilan shunday yo'l bor, - dedi Svidrigailov kulish bilan.

en: “You won’t admit it, even if you do inwardly believe it a miracle!
uz: Hatto ichingizda mo'ʼjiza deb bilsangiz ham, buni tan olmaysiz!

en: Here you say that it may be only chance.
uz: Bu erda siz bu shunchaki tasodif bo'lishi mumkinligini aytasiz.

en: And what cowards they all are here, about having an opinion of their own, you can’t fancy, Rodion Romanovitch.
uz: Va ularning barchasi qanday qo'rqoqlar ekanligi, o'z fikrlari borligi haqida o'ylamaslik mumkin, Rodion Romanovitch.

en: I don’t mean you, you have an opinion of your own and are not afraid to have it.
uz: Men siz haqingizda gapirmayapman, sizda o'zingizning fikringiz bor va uni aytishdan qo'rqmaysiz.

en: That’s how it was you attracted my curiosity.” “Nothing else?” “Well, that’s enough, you know,” Svidrigaïlov was obviously exhilarated, but only slightly so, he had not had more than half a glass of wine.
uz: Mana shunday qilib siz mening qiziqishimni jalb qildingiz. Boshqa hech narsa emas? Xo'sh, shu qadar yetdi, bilasiz, Svidrigailov, albatta, hayajonlangan edi, lekin faqat bir oz, u yarim stakan sharobdan ortiq ichmagan edi.

en: “I fancy you came to see me before you knew that I was capable of having what you call an opinion of my own,” observed Raskolnikov.
uz: "Siz mening fikrim deb atayotgan narsamga ega bo'lishga qodir ekanimni bilishdan oldin meni ko'rishga keldingiz, deb o'ylayman", - dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “Oh, well, it was a different matter.
uz: Oh, yaxshi, bu boshqa narsa edi.

en: Everyone has his own plans.
uz: Har kimning o'z rejalari bor.

en: And apropos of the miracle let me tell you that I think you have been asleep for the last two or three days.
uz: Moʻʼjiza haqida gap ketganda, sizga aytamanki, oxirgi ikki-uch kundan beri uxlab yurgansiz.

en: I told you of this tavern myself, there is no miracle in your coming straight here.
uz: Bu mehmonxona haqida o'zim sizga aytdim, bu yerga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri kelishingizda hech qanday mo'jiza yo'q.

en: I explained the way myself, told you where it was, and the hours you could find me here.
uz: Men o'zim yo'lni tushuntirdim, qayerdaligini va meni bu yerda topish uchun vaqtni aytib berdim.

en: Do you remember?” “I don’t remember,” answered Raskolnikov with surprise.
uz: Eslaysizmi?  Men eslay olmayman, Raskolnikov hayratda turib javob berdi.

en: The address has been stamped mechanically on your memory.
uz: Manzil sizning xotirangizda mexanik ravishda muhrlangan.

en: You turned this way mechanically and yet precisely according to the direction, though you are not aware of it.
uz: Bu yo'lni mexanik ravishda va aniq yo'nalishda aylantirgansiz, ammo buni bilmaysiz.

en: When I told you then, I hardly hoped you understood me.
uz: O'shanda sizga aytganimda, siz meni tushunasiz deb umid qilmasdim.

en: You give yourself away too much, Rodion Romanovitch.
uz: Siz o'zingizni juda ko'p berasiz, Rodion Romanovitch.

en: And another thing, I’m convinced there are lots of people in Petersburg who talk to themselves as they walk.
uz: Yana bir narsa, men o'zimni ishontirganimcha, Sankt-Peterburgda o'zlari bilan yurib gaplashadigan ko'plab odamlar bor.

en: This is a town of crazy people.
uz: Bu aqldan ozgan odamlar yashaydigan shahar.

en: If only we had scientific men, doctors, lawyers and philosophers might make most valuable investigations in Petersburg each in his own line.
uz: Agar bizda olimlar, shifokorlar, advokatlar va falsafachilar bo'lganida, ular Sankt-Peterburgda eng qimmatli tadqiqotlarni o'z yo'lida amalga oshirishi mumkin edi.

en: There are few places where there are so many gloomy, strong and queer influences on the soul of man as in Petersburg.
uz: Odamning ruhiga shunchalik ko'p qaynoq, kuchli va g'ayritabiiy ta'sir ko'rsatadigan joylar kam emas, balki Sankt-Peterburgda.

en: The mere influences of climate mean so much.
uz: Faqat iqlimning ta'siri juda ko'p narsani anglatadi.

en: And it’s the administrative centre of all Russia and its character must be reflected on the whole country.
uz: Bu butun Rossiyaning ma'muriy markazi va uning xarakteri butun mamlakatda aks ettirilishi kerak.

en: But that is neither here nor there now.
uz: Ammo bu yerda ham, hozir ham yo'q.

en: The point is that I have several times watched you.
uz: Darhaqiqat, men sizni bir necha bor kuzatib kelganman.

en: You walk out of your house — holding your head high —twenty paces from home you let it sink, and
uz: Siz uyingizdan chiqib ketasiz  boshingizni baland ushlab turib Uydan yigirma qadam uzoqlikda bo'lganingizda uni quvib ketishiga yo'l qo'yasiz va

en: fold your hands behind your back.
uz: Qo'lingizni orqaga qo'ying.

en: You look and evidently see nothing before nor beside you.
uz: Siz o'zingizning oldingizda yoki yoningizda hech narsa ko'rmayapsiz.

en: At last you begin moving your lips and talking to yourself, and sometimes you wave one hand and declaim, and at last stand still in the middle of the road.
uz: Nihoyat siz og'zingizni ko'chirib, o'zingiz bilan gaplashishni boshlaysiz va ba'zida siz bir qo'lingizni o'girib, e'lon qilasiz va nihoyat yo'lning o'rtasida to'xtamaysiz.

en: That’s not at all the thing.
uz: Bu umuman shu emas.

en: Someone may be watching you besides me, and it won’t do you any good.
uz: Ehtimol, mendan tashqari kimdir sizni kuzatib boradi va bu sizga hech qanday foyda keltirmaydi.

en: It’s nothing really to do with me and I can’t cure you, but, of course, you understand me.” “Do you know that I am being followed?” asked Raskolnikov, looking inquisitively at him.
uz: Bu men bilan hech qanday aloqasi yo'q va men sizni davolay olmayman, lekin, albatta, siz meni tushunasiz.

en: “No, I know nothing about it,” said Svidrigaïlov, seeming surprised.
uz: "Yo'q, men bu haqda hech narsa bilmayman", - dedi Svidrigailov, hayron ko'rinib.

en: “Well, then, let us leave me alone,” Raskolnikov muttered, frowning.
uz: Eh, o'shanda meni yolg'iz qo'yib ketamiz, Raskolnikov shov-shuv qilib, burunlarini ko'tardi.

en: “Very good, let us leave you alone.” “You had better tell me, if you come here to drink, and directed me twice to come here to you, why did you hide, and try to get away just now when I looked at the window from the street?
uz: Chindan ham yaxshi, sizni tinch qoldiramiz.  Agar siz bu yerga ichishga kelgan bo'lsangiz va menga ikki marta bu yerga kelishimni buyurgan bo'lsangiz, nega siz yashirinib, darhol ko'chadan oynasiga qarab qochishga harakat qildingiz?

en: And why was it you lay on your sofa with closed eyes and pretended to be asleep, though you were wide awake while I stood in your doorway?
uz: Nima uchun siz o'zingizning sofasingizda yopilgan ko'zlar bilan uxlab yurganingizni ko'rdingiz va men sizning eshikingizda turganimda, o'zingizni uyg'onasiz deb o'ylar edingiz?

en: I saw it.” “I may have had … reasons.
uz: Men uni ko'rdim.Mening ... sabablarim bo'lishi mumkin.

en: You know that yourself.” “And I may have had my reasons, though you don’t know them.” Raskolnikov dropped his right elbow on the table, leaned his chin in the fingers of his right hand, and stared intently at Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Siz buni o'zingiz ham bilasiz.  Va mening sabablarim bo'lishi mumkin, ammo siz ularni bilmaysiz. Raskolnikov o'ng qo'lqovusini stol ustiga tashladi, o'ng qo'li barmoqlariga burchakni tikladi va Svidrigaylovga diqqat bilan qaradi.

en: For a full minute he scrutinised his face, which had impressed him before.
uz: U butun bir daqiqa davomida o'z yuzini ko'rib chiqdi, bu esa ilgari uni taassurot qoldirgan edi.

en: It was a strange face, like a mask; white and red, with bright red lips, with a flaxen beard, and still thick flaxen hair.
uz: Bu yuzning o'zi maskaga o'xshaydi, oq va qizil, yorqin qizil og'izlari, rangli sakkizi va hali ham qalin rangli sochlari bor edi.

en: His eyes were somehow too blue and their expression somehow too heavy and fixed.
uz: Uning ko'zlari juda ko'k edi va ko'z ko'rinishi juda og'ir va qat'iy edi.

en: There was something awfully unpleasant in that handsome face, which looked so wonderfully young for his age.
uz: O'sha chiroyli yuzida juda yoqimsiz bir narsa bor edi, u yoshligi uchun juda yosh ko'rinardi.

en: Svidrigaïlov was smartly dressed in light summer clothes and was particularly dainty in his linen.
uz: Svidrigailov yorqin yozgi kiyimlar bilan kiyingan va o'zining chiroyli kiyimlarida juda chiroyli edi.

en: He wore a huge ring with a precious stone in it.
uz: U o'zida qimmatbaho tosh bo'lgan ulkan xoch kiygan edi.

en: “Have I got to bother myself about you, too, now?” said Raskolnikov suddenly, coming with nervous impatience straight to the point.
uz: Men ham siz uchun tashvishlanishim kerakmi? dedi Raskolnikov to'satdan, g'ayritabiiy sabrsizlik bilan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri mavzuga kelib.

en: “Even though perhaps you are the most dangerous man if you care to injure me, I don’t want to put myself out any more.
uz: Agar meni yomon ko'rmoqchi bo'lsangiz, ehtimol siz eng xavfli odam bo'lishingiz mumkin, lekin men o'zimni boshqa tashlab ketishni istamayman.

en: I will show you at once that I don’t prize myself as you probably think I do.
uz: Men o'zimni siz o'ylagandek qadrlamayotganimni tezda ko'rsataman.

en: I’ve come to tell you at once that if you keep to your former intentions
uz: Men sizga bir marta aytishga keldimki, agar siz o'tmishdagi niyatlaringizga sodiq qolsangiz,

en: with regard to my sister and if you think to derive any benefit in that direction from what has been discovered of late, I will kill you before you get me locked up.
uz: opamga nisbatan va agar siz yaqinda topilgan narsalardan bu yo'nalishda biron bir foyda olishni o'ylasangiz, meni hibsga olishingizdan oldin sizni o'ldiraman.

en: You can reckon on my word.
uz: Siz mening so'zimga ishonishingiz mumkin.

en: You know that I can keep it.
uz: Uni saqlab qolishim mumkinligini bilasiz.

en: And in the second place if you want to tell me anything — for I keep fancying all this time that you have something to tell me — make haste and tell it, for time is precious and very likely it will soon be too late.” “Why in such haste?” asked Svidrigaïlov, looking at him curiously.
uz: Ikkinchidan, agar siz menga biror narsa aytmoqchi bo'lsangiz, menga aytishingiz kerak bo'lgan biror narsa borligini ko'p vaqt o'ylab yuribman, chunki vaqt qimmatbaho va ehtimol juda tez kech bo'ladi.Svidrigailov savol berdi: "Nima uchun bunday shoshilinch?

en: “Everyone has his plans,” Raskolnikov answered gloomily and impatiently.
uz: Har kimning o'z rejalari bor, Raskolnikov dahshatli va sabrsizlik bilan javob berdi.

en: “You urged me yourself to frankness just now, and at the first question you refuse to answer,” Svidrigaïlov observed with a smile.
uz: Siz o'zingiz meni hozirgina ochiqchasiga aytishga rag'batlantirgansiz va birinchi savolga javob berishni rad etasiz, Svidrigailov tabassum bilan kuzatdi.

en: “You keep fancying that I have aims of my own and so you look at me with suspicion.
uz: Siz mening o'z maqsadlarim bor deb o'ylayotgandirsiz va shu sababli menga shubha bilan qarayotgandirsiz.

en: Of course it’s perfectly natural in your position.
uz: Albatta, sizning vaziyatingizda bu tabiiy hol.

en: But though I should like to be friends with you, I shan’t trouble myself to convince you of the contrary.
uz: Ammo men siz bilan do'st bo'lishni xohlasam-da, sizlarni buning aksiga ishontirish uchun o'zimni tashvishlantirmayman.

en: The game isn’t worth the candle and I wasn’t intending to talk to you about anything special.” “What did you want me, for, then?
uz: O'yin shishaga arzimaydi va men siz bilan hech qanday maxsus narsa haqida gaplashmoqchi emasdim. Nima uchun meni xohladingiz?

en: It was you who came hanging about me.” “Why, simply as an interesting subject for observation.
uz: Siz mening atrofimda o'tirishga kelgansiz.  Nima uchun, shunchaki kuzatuv uchun qiziqarli mavzu sifatida.

en: I liked the fantastic nature of your position —that’s what it was!
uz: Sizning pozitsiyangizning ajoyib xususiyati menga yoqdi!

en: Besides you are the brother of a person who greatly interested me, and from that person I had in the past heard a very great deal about you, from which I gathered that you had a great influence over her; isn’t that enough?
uz: Bundan tashqari, siz menga katta qiziqish ko'rsatgan odamning ukasisiz va men o'tmishda siz haqingizda juda ko'p narsalarni eshitgan odamdan uning ustida katta ta'sir ko'rsatganingizni bilib oldim; bu yetarli emasmi?

en: Still I must admit that your question is rather complex, and is difficult for me to answer.
uz: Shunga qaramay, sizning savolingiz juda murakkab va javob berish men uchun qiyin ekanligini tan oldim.

en: Here, you, for instance, have come to me not only for a definite object, but for the sake of hearing something new.
uz: Misol uchun, siz menga faqat aniq bir narsa uchun emas, balki yangi narsalarni eshitish uchun keldingiz.

en: Isn’t that so?” persisted Svidrigaïlov with a sly smile.
uz: Bu haqiqat emasmi? - dedi Svidrigailov o'ziga xos tabassum bilan.

en: “Well, can’t you fancy then that I, too, on my way here in the train was reckoning on you, on your telling me something new, and on my making some profit out of you!
uz: Xo'sh, siz o'ylab ko'rmayapsizmi, men ham poyezdda sizdan umidvor bo'lib, menga yangi narsalarni aytib, sizdan foyda ko'rishimga umidvor bo'ldim!

en: You see what rich men we are!” “What profit could you make?” “How can I tell you?
uz: Biz qanchalik boy odam ekanimizni ko'ryapsizmi?Siz qanday foyda ko'rishingiz mumkin?Qanday qilib aytishim mumkin?

en: You see in what a tavern I spend all my time and it’s my enjoyment, that’s to say it’s no great enjoyment, but one must sit somewhere; that poor Katia now —you
uz: Ko'rib turibsiz, men qancha vaqt o'tkazaman va bu mening zavqimdir, ya'ni katta zavq emas, lekin biror joyda o'tirib turish kerak; bu kambag'al Katia endi you

en: … If only I had been a glutton now, a club gourmand, but you see I can eat this.” He pointed to a little table in the corner where the remnants of a terrible-looking beefsteak and potatoes lay on a tin dish.
uz: ... Kechki, men endi g'amgin, klub go'rmand bo'lganimda edi, lekin ko'rasiz, men buni yeyishim mumkin. U burchakdagi kichkina stolga ishora qildi, u yerda qorong'i ko'rinishdagi go'sht va kartoshkalarning qoldiqlari qadoqlab qo'yilgan idish ustida o'tirgan.

en: “Have you dined, by the way?
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, kechki ovqat yemaganmisiz?

en: I’ve had something and want nothing more.
uz: Biror narsa bor edi va boshqa hech narsa istamayman.

en: I don’t drink, for instance, at all.
uz: Masalan, men umuman ichmayman.

en: Except for champagne I never touch anything, and not more than a glass of that all the evening, and even that is enough to make my head ache.
uz: Shampanjdan tashqari men hech qachon hech narsaga qo'l tegizmayman va kechasi bir stakanidan ko'proq bo'lmaydi va hatto bu bosh og'rig'imga sabab bo'ladi.

en: I ordered it just now to wind myself up, for I am just going off somewhere and you see me in a peculiar state of mind.
uz: Men o'zimni to'ldirish uchun hozir buyurdim, chunki men bir joyga ketyapman va siz meni o'zgacha ruhda ko'rasiz.

en: That was why I hid myself just now like a schoolboy, for I was afraid you would hinder me.
uz: Shuning uchun men o'zimni maktab o'quvchisi kabi yashirgan edim, chunki siz meni to'xtatishingizdan qo'rqardim.

en: But I believe,” he pulled out his watch, “I can spend an hour with you.
uz: Lekin men ishonaman, u o'z soatini olib chiqib, bir soat o'tirsa bo'ladi.

en: It’s half-past four now.
uz: Hozir soat to'rt yarim o'tibdi.

en: If only I’d been something, a landowner, a father, a cavalry officer, a photographer, a journalist … I am nothing, no specialty, and sometimes I am positively bored.
uz: Agar men biror narsa bo'lgan bo'lsam, yer egasi, ota, kavaleriya boshlig'i, fotograf, jurnalist bo'lgan bo'lardim... Men hech narsa emasman, hech qanday mutaxassislik emasman va ba'zan charchamayman.

en: I really thought you would tell me something new.” “But what are you, and why have you come here?” “What am I?
uz: Siz menga yangi narsalarni aytasiz deb o'yladim. Lekin siz kimsiz va nega bu yerga keldingiz?Men nima edim?

en: You know, a gentleman, I served for two years in the cavalry, then I knocked about here in Petersburg, then I married Marfa Petrovna and lived in the country.
uz: Bilasizmi, bir gentleman, men ikki yil qo'shinida xizmat qildim, so'ngra Petersburgda bu yerga taqillatdim, keyin Marfa Petrovna bilan turmush qurdim va qishloq joyda yashadim.

en: There you have my biography!” “You are a gambler, I believe?” “No, a poor sort of gambler.
uz: Mana mening tarjimai holim!Siz qimor o'yinchisiz, deb o'ylayman?Yo'q, kambag'al qimor o'yinchisi.

en: A cardsharper —not a gambler.” “You have been a cardsharper then?” “Yes, I’ve been a cardsharper too.” “Didn’t you get thrashed sometimes?” “It did happen.
uz: Kartsharper qimor o'yinchisi emas. Siz o'shanda kartsharper bo'lganmisiz?  Ha, men ham kartsharper bo'lganman. Ba'zan sizni o'g'rilashmaganmi?  Bu sodir bo'ldi.

en: Why?” “Why, you might have challenged them … altogether it must have been lively.” “I won’t contradict you, and besides I am no hand at philosophy.
uz: Nima uchun? Nima uchun, siz ularni tanqid qilgan bo'lishingiz mumkin edi ... umuman bu jonli bo'lishi kerak edi. Men sizga zid kelmayman va bundan tashqari men falsafaning hech bir qo'li emasman.

en: I confess that I hastened here for the sake of the women.” “As soon as you buried Marfa Petrovna?” “Quite so,” Svidrigaïlov smiled with engaging candour.
uz: Men ayollar uchun bu yerga tezlik bilan kelganimni tan olaman.Marfa Petrovnoni ko'mganingizdan so'ng?Haqiqatan ham,Svidrigailov o'ziga xos samimiylik bilan tabassum qildi.

en: You seem to find something wrong in my speaking like that about women?” “You ask whether I find anything wrong in vice?”
uz: Ayollar haqida shunday gapirganimda siz biron bir xato topyapsizmi?Sizdan bu yomonlikdan biron bir xato topyapmanmi deb so'raysiz?

en: Oh, that’s what you are after!
uz: Oh, siz shundan orzu qilyapsiz!

en: But I’ll answer you in order, first about women in general; you know I am fond of talking.
uz: Ammo men sizlarga tartib bilan javob beraman, avvalo, umuman ayollar haqida; men gapirishni yaxshi ko'raman.

en: Tell me, what should I restrain myself for?
uz: Menga ayting, nimaga o'zimni to'xtatishim kerak?

en: Why should I give up women, since I have a passion for them?
uz: Ayollarga bo'lgan ishtiyoqim bo'lsa, nega xotin-qizlardan voz kechishim kerak?

en: It’s an occupation, anyway.” “So you hope for nothing here but vice?” “Oh, very well, for vice then.
uz: Shunday qilib, siz bu yerda faqatgina vijdondan boshqa narsani umid qilmayapsizmi?

en: You insist on its being vice.
uz: Siz uning yomonlik ekanligini istaysiz.

en: But anyway I like a direct question.
uz: Ammo men aniq savolni yoqtiraman.

en: In this vice at least there is something permanent, founded indeed upon nature and not dependent on fantasy, something present in the blood like an ever- burning ember, forever setting one on fire and, maybe, not to be quickly extinguished, even with years.
uz: Bu yomonlikda hech bo'lmaganda tabiatga asoslangan va xayolga bog'liq bo'lmagan, doimo mavjud bo'lgan bir narsa bor, qonda yonib turgan olov kabi mavjud bo'lgan bir narsa bor, uni doimo yonib qo'yadi va ehtimol yillar o'tgach ham tezda o'chirib ketmaydi.

en: You’ll agree it’s an occupation of a sort.” “That’s nothing to rejoice at, it’s a disease and a dangerous one.” “Oh, that’s what you think, is it!
uz: Siz bunga rozi bo'lasizki, bu bir xil kasbdir.Bu xursand bo'lish uchun hech narsa emas, bu kasallik va xavfli.Bu sizning fikringiz!

en: I agree, that it is a disease like everything that exceeds moderation.
uz: Men bunga rozi bo'laman, bu o'rtacha o'lchovdan ortiq bo'lgan har qanday narsa kabi kasallik.

en: And, of course, in this one must exceed moderation.
uz: Va, albatta, bu borada o'rtacha o'lchovdan oshish kerak.

en: But in the first place, everybody does so in one way or another, and in the second place, of course, one ought to be moderate and prudent, however mean it may be, but what am I to do?
uz: Ammo birinchi navbatda, hamma bu yo'ldan yoki undan boshqa yo'ldan yuradi va ikkinchi navbatda, albatta, odam o'rtacha va ehtiyotkor bo'lishi kerak, bu qanday bo'lishidan qat'iy nazar, lekin men nima qilishim kerak?

en: If I hadn’t this, I might have to shoot myself.
uz: Agar men buni qilmasam, o'zimni o'ldirishim kerak bo'lishi mumkin.

en: I am ready to admit that a decent man ought to put up with being bored, but yet …” “And could you shoot yourself?” “Oh, come!” Svidrigaïlov parried with disgust.
uz: Men yaxshi odam charchashga chidamli bo'lishi kerakligini tan olishga tayyorman, ammo shunga qaramay ...  Va o'zingizni o'zingiz o'ldirasizmi?  Oh, keling! Svidrigailov jirkanchlik bilan parlay boshladi.

en: “Please don’t speak of it,” he added hurriedly and with none of the bragging tone he had shown in all the previous conversation.
uz: Iltimos, bu haqda gapirmang, - dedi u shoshilinch ravishda va avvalgi suhbatda ko'rsatgan maqtanish tonidan hech qanday narsa bilan qo'shimcha qildi.

en: His face quite changed.
uz: Uning yuzi ancha o'zgarib ketdi.

en: “I admit it’s an unpardonable weakness, but I can’t help it.
uz: Men buni kechirilmaydigan zaiflik deb tan olsam ham, ammo men bunga yordam bera olmayman.

en: I am afraid of death and I dislike its being talked of.
uz: O'limdan qo'rqaman va uning haqida gapirishni yoqtirmayman.

en: Do you know that I am to a certain extent a mystic?” “Ah, the apparitions of Marfa Petrovna!
uz: Bilganmisiz, men bir darajada mistikman?Ah, Marfa Petrovnoning ko'rinishlari!

en: Do they still go on visiting you?” “Oh, don’t talk of them; there have been no more in Petersburg, confound them!” he cried with an air of irritation.
uz: Ular hali ham sizni ko'rib turadimi?Oh, ular haqida gapirmang; ular Sankt-Peterburgda yo'q edi, ularni chalg'iting! u g'azabga to'lib-toshgan holda yig'ladi.

en: “Let’s rather talk of that … though … H’m!
uz: Keling, bu haqda gapiramiz... lekin... Hm!

en: I have not much time, and can’t stay long with you, it’s a pity!
uz: Men ko'p vaqtga ega emasman va siz bilan uzoq vaqt qololmayman, bu juda achinarli!

en: I should have found plenty to tell you.” “What’s your engagement, a woman?” “Yes, a woman, a casual incident.
uz: Sizga aytish uchun ko'p narsani topishim kerak edi.Sizning niyatingiz nima, ayol?Ha, ayol, tasodifiy hodisa.

en: … No, that’s not what I want to talk of.”
uz: Yo'q, men bu haqda gapirishni istamayman.

en: “And the hideousness, the filthiness of all your surroundings, doesn’t that affect you?
uz: Va atrofingizdagi barcha jirkanchlik va nopoklik sizga ta'sir qilmaydimi?

en: Have you lost the strength to stop yourself?” “And do you pretend to strength, too?
uz: O'zingizni to'xtatish uchun kuchingizni yo'qotdingizmi?Va siz ham kuchga aylanasizmi?

en: You surprised me just now, Rodion Romanovitch, though I knew beforehand it would be so.
uz: Siz meni hozirgina hayratda qoldirdingiz, Rodion Romanovitch, garchi men buni oldindan bilardim.

en: You preach to me about vice and aesthetics!
uz: Siz menga yomonlik va estetika haqida va'z qilasiz!

en: You —a Schiller, you —an idealist!
uz: Siz - Shiller, siz - idealist!

en: Of course that’s all as it should be and it would be surprising if it were not so, yet it is strange in reality.
uz: To'g'ri, bunday bo'lishi kerak va agar shunday bo'lmasa ajablanarli bo'lardi, ammo haqiqatda bu g'alati.

en: … Ah, what a pity I have no time, for you’re a most interesting type!
uz: Oh, men uchun vaqt yo'qligim juda achinarli, chunki siz juda qiziqarli odamsiz!

en: And, by the way, are you fond of Schiller?
uz: Aytgancha, siz Shillerni yoqtirasizmi?

en: I am awfully fond of him.” “But what a braggart you are,” Raskolnikov said with some disgust.
uz: Men uni juda yaxshi ko'raman.  Ammo siz qanday maqtanchsiz, Raskolnikov biroz jirkanchlik bilan dedi.

en: “Upon my word, I am not,” answered Svidrigaïlov laughing.
uz: "Men emasman" degan so'zimga binoan Svidrigailov kulish bilan javob berdi.

en: “However, I won’t dispute it, let me be a braggart, why not brag, if it hurts no one?
uz: Biroq, men bu haqda bahslashmayman, men mag'rur bo'laman, nima uchun hech kimni xafa qilmayapman, agar bu hech kimni xafa qilmasa?

en: I spent seven years in the country with Marfa Petrovna, so now when I come across an intelligent person like you —intelligent and highly interesting —I am simply glad to talk and, besides, I’ve drunk that half-glass of champagne and it’s gone to my head a little.
uz: Men Marfa Petrovna bilan yetti yil qishloqda bo'ldim, shuning uchun endi siz kabi aqlli odam bilan uchrashganimda - aqlli va juda qiziqarli - men shunchaki suhbatdan mamnunman va, bundan tashqari, men o'sha yarim stakan shampan ichganman va bu biroz boshimga o'tdi.

en: And besides, there’s a certain fact that has wound me up tremendously, but about that I … will keep quiet.
uz: Bundan tashqari, meni juda xafa qilgan bir fakt bor, lekin men bu haqda... sukut saqlayman.

en: Where are you off to?” he asked in alarm.
uz: Qayerga ketyapsiz? - deb so'radi u qo'rqinchli so'zlar bilan.

en: Raskolnikov had begun getting up.
uz: Raskolnikov o'rnidan turishni boshlagan edi.

en: He felt oppressed and stifled and, as it were, ill at ease at having come here.
uz: U o'zini ezilgan va cho'ktirilgan va shubhasiz, bu yerga kelgani uchun o'zini noqulay his qilardi.

en: He felt convinced that Svidrigaïlov was the most worthless scoundrel on the face of the earth.
uz: U Svidrigailovning yer yuzidagi eng behuda haykal ekaniga o'zini ishontirdi.

en: Sit down, stay a little!” Svidrigaïlov begged.
uz: O'tiring, biroz qoling! Svidrigailov iltijo qildi.

en: “Let them bring you some tea, anyway.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa-da, ular sizga choy olib kelishsin.

en: Stay a little, I won’t talk nonsense, about myself, I mean.
uz: Bir oz qoling, men o'zim haqida axloqsiz gaplarni aytmayman.

en: I’ll tell you something.
uz: Sizga bir narsa aytaman.

en: If you like I’ll tell you how a woman tried ‘to save’ me, as you would call it?
uz: Agar xohlasangiz, sizga qanday qilib bir ayol meni qutqarishga harakat qilganini aytib beraman?

en: It will be an answer to your first question indeed, for the woman was your sister.
uz: Bu sizning birinchi savolingizga javob bo'ladi, chunki bu ayol sizning singilingiz edi.

en: It will help to spend the time.” “Tell me, but I trust that you …” “Oh, don’t be uneasy.
uz: Vaqtni o'tkazishga yordam beradi.  Menga ayting, lekin men sizga ishonaman ...   Oh, bezovta bo'lmang.

en: Besides, even in a worthless low fellow like me, Avdotya Romanovna can only excite the deepest respect.”
uz: Bundan tashqari, hatto men kabi behuda kam odamda ham Avdotya Romanovna faqat chuqur hurmatni uyg'otishi mumkin.

en: IV “You know perhaps —yes, I told you myself,” began Svidrigaïlov, “that I was in the debtors’ prison here, for an immense sum, and had not any expectation of being able to pay it.
uz: Ehtimol, IV. Siz bilasiz, men sizga o'zim aytdim, Svidrigailov men bu yerda qarzdorlar qamoqxonasida katta miqdorda bo'lganimni va uni to'lashga qodir bo'lishimni kutmaganimni aytdi.

en: There’s no need to go into particulars how Marfa Petrovna bought me out; do you know to what a point of insanity a woman can sometimes love?
uz: Marfa Petrovna meni qanday sotib olganini batafsil tushuntirishning hojati yo'q; bir ayol ba'zan qanday aqldan ozgan darajada sevishi mumkinligini bilasizmi?

en: She was an honest woman, and very sensible, although completely uneducated.
uz: U halol va aqlli ayol edi, garchi o'qimagan bo'lsa ham.

en: Would you believe that this honest and jealous woman, after many scenes of hysterics and reproaches, condescended to enter into a kind of contract with me which she kept throughout our married life?
uz: Bu halol va hasadli ayol, ko'pgina histeriya va tanqid sahnalaridan so'ng, men bilan turmush qurganimiz davomida o'z ixtiyori bilan shartnoma tuzishga rozi bo'ldi, deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: She was considerably older than I, and besides, she always kept a clove or something in her mouth.
uz: U mendan ancha kattaroq edi va, bundan tashqari, u har doim og'zida cho'g'i yoki boshqa narsani saqlab turardi.

en: There was so much swinishness in my soul and honesty too, of a sort, as to tell her straight out that I couldn’t be absolutely faithful to her.
uz: O'zimning ruhimda shunchalik g'ayritabiiylik va rostgo'ylik bor ediki, men unga to'g'ri va to'g'ri gapirib, unga mutlaqo sodiq bo'lmayman, deb aytardim.

en: This confession drove her to frenzy, but yet she seems in a way to have liked my brutal frankness.
uz: Ushbu tanbeh uni g'alatilikka olib keldi, ammo u bir yo'l bilan mening shafqatsiz ochiqligimni yoqtirganiga o'xshaydi.

en: She thought it showed I was unwilling to deceive her if I warned her like this beforehand and for a jealous woman, you know, that’s the first consideration.
uz: Agar men uni oldindan shunday ogohlantirsam, men uni aldashga tayyor emasligimni ko'rsataman deb o'ylagan va hasadgo'y ayol uchun bu birinchi o'rinni egallaydi.

en: After many tears an unwritten contract was drawn up between us: first, that I would never leave Marfa Petrovna and would always be her husband; secondly, that I would never absent myself without her permission; thirdly, that I would never set up a permanent mistress; fourthly, in return for this, Marfa Petrovna gave me a free hand with the maidservants, but only with her secret knowledge; fifthly, God forbid my falling in love with a woman of our class; sixthly, in case I —which God forbid —should be visited by a great serious passion I was bound to reveal it to Marfa Petrovna.
uz: Ko'p yig'ishdan keyin o'zimiz o'rtasida yozma shartnoma tuzdik: birinchidan, men Marfa Petrovnani hech qachon tashlab ketmayman va uning eri bo'laman; ikkinchidan, uning iznisiz hech qachon yo'q bo'laman; uchinchidan, men hech qachon doimiy sevimli ayolga ega bo'lmayman; to'rtinchidan, Marfa Petrovna menga xizmatkor qizlar bilan, lekin faqat uning sirli bilimlari bilan erkin qo'l berdi; beshinchidan, Xudo menga sinfdagi ayolga muhabbat qilishdan saqlasin; oltinchidan, agar men  Xudo buyurmagan g'iroblik bilan tashrif buyursam, uni Marfa Petrovnga oshkor qilishim kerak edi.

en: On this last score, however, Marfa Petrovna was fairly at ease.
uz: Biroq, bu oxirgi natija bo'yicha Marfa Petrovna o'zini juda xotirjam his qildi.

en: She was a sensible woman and so she could not help looking upon me as a
uz: U aqlli ayol edi, shuning uchun menga o'z o'rnida ko'rinmas edi.

en: dissolute profligate incapable of real love.
uz: Haqiqiy sevgiga qodir bo'lmagan bo'g'izbozlik qiluvchi botil.

en: But a sensible woman and a jealous woman are two very different things, and that’s where the trouble came in.
uz: Ammo aqlli ayol va hasadgo'y ayol juda farq qiladi va shu yerda muammo paydo bo'ldi.

en: But to judge some people impartially we must renounce certain preconceived opinions and our habitual attitude to the ordinary people about us.
uz: Ammo ba'zi odamlarni yuzxotirchilik bilan hukm qilish uchun biz o'zimizdan oldingi fikrlardan va atrofdagi oddiy odamlarga nisbatan odatdagi munosabatimizdan voz kechishimiz kerak.

en: I have reason to have faith in your judgment rather than in anyone’s.
uz: Men hech kimga emas, balki sizning hukmingizga ishonishga asosim bor.

en: Perhaps you have already heard a great deal that was ridiculous and absurd about Marfa Petrovna.
uz: Ehtimol, siz Marfa Petrovna haqida juda ko'p g'alati va absurd narsalarni eshitgansiz.

en: She certainly had some very ridiculous ways, but I tell you frankly that I feel really sorry for the innumerable woes of which I was the cause.
uz: Albatta, u juda g'alati xulq-atvorlarga ega edi, lekin rostini aytsam, men o'zim sabab bo'lgan ko'pgina azob-uqubatlar uchun juda afsuslanaman.

en: Well, and that’s enough, I think, by way of a decorous oraison funèbre for the most tender wife of a most tender husband.
uz: Menimcha, bu eng mehribon erning eng mehribon xotiniga munosib marosim orqali yetarli.

en: When we quarrelled, I usually held my tongue and did not irritate her and that gentlemanly conduct rarely failed to attain its object, it influenced her, it pleased her, indeed.
uz: To'qnashganimizda, men odatda tilimni tutib, uni ranjitmasdim va bu gentlemanlik odatda maqsadga erishmaydi, uni ta'sir qiladi, yoqtiradi.

en: These were times when she was positively proud of me.
uz: O'sha paytlarda u men bilan juda faxrlanardi.

en: But your sister she couldn’t put up with, anyway.
uz: Ammo singlingiz unga chidab bo'lmadi.

en: And however she came to risk taking such a beautiful creature into her house as a governess.
uz: Ammo u bunday go'zal yaratilganni o'z uyiga o'qituvchi sifatida olib kirishni xavf ostiga qo'ydi.

en: My explanation is that Marfa Petrovna was an ardent and impressionable woman and simply fell in love herself —literally fell in love —with your sister.
uz: Mening tushuntirishim shundaki, Marfa Petrovna qizg'in va ta'sirchan ayol bo'lgan va u shunchaki o'ziga muhabbat ko'rsatgan, aslida singlisiga muhabbat ko'rsatgan.

en: Well, little wonder — look at Avdotya Romanovna!
uz: Xo'sh, Avdotya Romanovnaga qarang!

en: I saw the danger at the first glance and what do you think, I resolved not to look at her even.
uz: Men xavf-xatarni birinchi qarashda ko'rdim va siz nima deb o'ylaysiz, men unga hatto nazar ham solmaslikka qaror qildim.

en: But Avdotya Romanovna herself made the first step, would you believe it?
uz: Ammo Avdotya Romanovna o'zi birinchi qadam qo'ydi, ishonasizmi?

en: Would you believe it too that Marfa Petrovna was positively angry with me at first for my persistent silence about your sister, for my careless reception of her continual adoring praises of Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Siz ham o'ylaysizmi, Marfa Petrovna avvaliga mening singilingiz haqida o'zimning o'ylamaslik va Avdotya Romanovnaga bo'lgan sadoqatli maqtovlarini beparvolik bilan qabul qilganim uchun menga qattiq g'azablangan edi.

en: I don’t know what it was she wanted!
uz: U nima xohlaganini bilmayman!

en: Well, of course, Marfa Petrovna told Avdotya Romanovna every detail about me.
uz: Albatta, Marfa Petrovna Avdotya Romanovnaga men to'g'risidagi har bir tafsilotni aytib berdi.

en: She had the unfortunate habit of telling literally everyone all our family secrets and continually complaining of me; how could she fail to confide in such a delightful new friend?
uz: U butun oilaviy sirlarimizni har bir kishiga gapirib, menga shikoyat qilish odati bor edi; qanday qilib u bunday yoqimli yangi do'stga ishonmay qolishi mumkin edi?

en: I expect they talked of nothing else but me and no doubt Avdotya Romanovna heard all those dark mysterious rumours that were current about me.
uz: O'ylaymanki, ular mendan boshqa hech narsa haqida gapirmagan va hech shubhasiz Avdotya Romanovna men to'g'risida keng tarqalgan barcha qorong'i sirli mish-mishlarni eshitgan.

en: … I don’t mind betting that you too have heard something of the sort already?” “I have.
uz: ... Siz ham shu kabi gaplarni eshitganmisiz deb o'ylayman?Men eshitganman.

en: Luzhin charged you with having caused the death of a child.
uz: Luzhin sizni bola o'limiga sababchi bo'lganingiz uchun aybladi.

en: Is that true?” “Don’t refer to those vulgar tales, I beg,” said Svidrigaïlov with disgust and annoyance.
uz: Bu haqiqatmi?Ushbu vulgar hikoyalarga ishora qilmang, iltimos, dedi Svidrigailov jirkanch va g'azabga to'lib.

en: “If you insist on wanting to know about all
uz: Agar siz hamma narsani bilishni istayotgan bo'lsangiz

en: that idiocy, I will tell you one day, but now …” “I was told too about some footman of yours in the country whom you treated badly.” “I beg you to drop the subject,” Svidrigaïlov interrupted again with obvious impatience.
uz: O'sha axloqsizlikni bir kun sizga aytib beraman, lekin endi ...  Menga ham o'sha mamlakatda siz yomon munosabatda bo'lgan bir xizmatkoringiz haqida aytildi.  Bu mavzudan voz kechishingizni iltimos qilaman, Svidrigailov yana ko'rinadigan sabrsizlik bilan to'xtatdi.

en: “Was that the footman who came to you after death to fill your pipe?
uz: Bu o'limdan so'ng sizning quvuringizni to'ldirish uchun oldingizga kelgan xizmatkormi?

en: … you told me about it yourself.” Raskolnikov felt more and more irritated.
uz: ... siz menga bu haqda o'zingiz aytib berdingiz. Raskolnikov o'zini ko'proq g'azablanayotgan his qildi.

en: Svidrigaïlov looked at him attentively and Raskolnikov fancied he caught a flash of spiteful mockery in that look.
uz: Svidrigailov unga diqqat bilan qaradi va Raskolnikov o'zicha o'sha ko'rinishda o'ziga yomon taassurot qoldirganini his qiladi.

en: But Svidrigaïlov restrained himself and answered very civilly: “Yes, it was.
uz: Ammo Svidrigailov o'zini tuta olgan va juda madaniy javob berdi: "Ha, shunday edi.

en: I see that you, too, are extremely interested and shall feel it my duty to satisfy your curiosity at the first opportunity.
uz: Ko'rib turibmanki, siz ham juda qiziqasiz va birinchi imkoniyatdan foydalanib, sizning qiziqishingizni qondirishni o'z burchim deb hisoblayman.

en: I see that I really might pass for a romantic figure with some people.
uz: Ko'rib turibmanki, men ba'zi odamlar bilan romantik shaxs deb o'ylashim mumkin.

en: Judge how grateful I must be to Marfa Petrovna for having repeated to Avdotya Romanovna such mysterious and interesting gossip about me.
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaga men haqimda bunday sirli va qiziqarli mish-mishlarni takrorlagan Marfa Petrovnaga qanchalik minnatdor bo'lishim kerakligini o'ylab ko'ring.

en: I dare not guess what impression it made on her, but in any case it worked in my interests.
uz: Bu ayolga qanday taassurot qoldirganini bilmayman, lekin bu mening manfaatimni ko'zlaydi.

en: With all Avdotya Romanovna’s natural aversion and in spite of my invariably gloomy and repellent aspect —she did at least feel pity for me, pity for a lost soul.
uz: Avdotya Romanovnaning tabiiy nafratlari bilan va mening doimo noxush va noxush ko'rinishimga qaramay, u hech bo'lmaganda menga rahm qildi, yo'qolgan ruhimga rahm qildi.

en: And if once a girl’s heart is moved to pity, it’s more dangerous than anything.
uz: Va agar qizning yuragi bir marta rahm-shafqatga tushsa, bu hamma narsadan ham xavfliroqdir.

en: She is bound to want to ‘save him,’ to bring him to his senses, and lift him up and draw him to nobler aims, and restore him to new life and usefulness —well, we all know how far such dreams can go.
uz: Shubhasiz, u uni xalos etishni, aqlini tiklashni, uni ko'tarishni va yanada buyuk maqsadlarga olib borishni va uni yangi hayotga va foydalilikka qaytarishni xohlaydi.Ha, biz hammamiz bunday orzularning qanchalik uzoq davom etishini bilamiz.

en: I saw at once that the bird was flying into the cage of herself.
uz: O'sha zahoti qushning o'z qovoshiga uchayotganini ko'rdim.

en: And I too made ready.
uz: Men ham tayyorgarlik ko'rdim.

en: I think you are frowning, Rodion Romanovitch?
uz: O'ylaymanki, siz qovurib ketyapsiz, Rodion Romanovitch?

en: As you know, it all ended in smoke.
uz: Bilasizmi, bularning barchasi tutun bilan yakunlandi.

en: (Hang it all, what a lot I am drinking!) Do you know, I always, from the very beginning, regretted that it wasn’t your sister’s fate to be born in the second or third century AD, as the daughter of a reigning prince or some governor or proconsul in Asia Minor.
uz: Bilasizmi, men har doim, boshidan boshlab, opangizning ikkinchi yoki uchinchi asrda, kichik Osiyoda hukmronlik qilayotgan shohning yoki gubernator yoki prokonsulning qizi sifatida tug'ilishining nasibasi bo'lmaganidan afsuslanardim.

en: She would undoubtedly have been one of those who would endure martyrdom and would have smiled when they branded her bosom with hot pincers.
uz: Shubhasizki, u o'z martirligini ko'targan kishilardan bo'lib, ko'nglini issiq shkaflar bilan to'ldirganida tabassum qilgan bo'lardi.

en: And she would have gone to it of herself.
uz: Va u o'z ixtiyori bilan bunga borgan bo'lardi.

en: And in the fourth or fifth century she would have walked away into the Egyptian desert and would have stayed there thirty years living on roots and ecstasies and visions.
uz: Va to'rt yoki beshinchi asrda u Misr sahroga borib, o'ttiz yil davomida ildiz va ekstaziyalar va vahiylar bilan yashashi mumkin edi.

en: She is simply thirsting to face some torture for
uz: U shunchaki azob-uqubatlarga duch kelishga chanqoq.

en: someone, and if she can’t get her torture, she’ll throw herself out of a window.
uz: Kimdir, va agar u azob chekolmasa, o'zini oynadan tashqariga tashlaydi.

en: I’ve heard something of a Mr.
uz: Men bir Mr. haqida eshitganman.

en: Razumihin —he’s said to be a sensible fellow; his surname suggests it, indeed.
uz: Razumihin hes aqlli odam deb aytiladi; uning familiyasi buni ta'kidlaydi.

en: He’s probably a divinity student.
uz: Ehtimol u xudojo'ylikni o'rganayotgan kishi.

en: Well, he’d better look after your sister!
uz: Xo'sh, u opangizga g'amxo'rlik qilishi kerak!

en: I believe I understand her, and I am proud of it.
uz: Men uni tushunishimga ishonaman va bunga faxrlanaman.

en: But at the beginning of an acquaintance, as you know, one is apt to be more heedless and stupid.
uz: Ammo tanishlikning boshida, siz bilganingizdek, odam ko'proq befarq va ahmoq bo'lishga moyil.

en: One doesn’t see clearly.
uz: Odam aniq ko'rmaydi.

en: Hang it all, why is she so handsome?
uz: Hamma narsani to'xtat, nega u shunchalik chiroyli?

en: In fact, it began on my side with a most irresistible physical desire.
uz: Aslida, bu mening tomonimda juda chidamsiz jismoniy istak bilan boshlandi.

en: Avdotya Romanovna is awfully chaste, incredibly and phenomenally so.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna juda sof, ajoyib va ajoyib.

en: Take note, I tell you this about your sister as a fact.
uz: Eslatib o'tish kerak, men sizga singilingiz haqida fakt sifatida aytaman.

en: She is almost morbidly chaste, in spite of her broad intelligence, and it will stand in her way.
uz: Uning keng aqli borligiga qaramay, u deyarli kasallik bilan pokdir va bu uning yo'liga to'sqinlik qiladi.

en: There happened to be a girl in the house then, Parasha, a black-eyed wench, whom I had never seen before —she had just come from another village —very pretty, but incredibly stupid: she burst into tears, wailed so that she could be heard all over the place and caused scandal.
uz: O'shanda uyda bir qiz bo'lgan, Parasha, qora ko'zlarli qiz, men uni hech qachon ko'rmagan edim.U boshqa qishloqdan kelgan edi.U juda chiroyli, ammo juda ahmoq: u yig'lab yubordi, hamma joyda eshitilishi uchun yig'ladi va bu esa shubha tug'dirdi.

en: One day after dinner Avdotya Romanovna followed me into an avenue in the garden and with flashing eyes insisted on my leaving poor Parasha alone.
uz: Bir kuni kechki ovqatdan so'ng Avdotya Romanovna meni bog'dagi chodirga ergashdi va ko'z o'chirib, kambag'al Parashani yolg'iz qoldirishimni istaydi.

en: It was almost our first conversation by ourselves.
uz: Bu deyarli birinchi marta o'zimiz bilan suhbatlashdik.

en: I, of course, was only too pleased to obey her wishes, tried to appear disconcerted, embarrassed, in fact played my part not badly.
uz: Albatta, men uning istaklariga quloq solishdan juda mamnun edim, xavotirda bo'lib ko'rinishga harakat qilardim, uyalgan edim, aslida o'z rolimni yomon o'ynamasdim.

en: Then came interviews, mysterious conversations, exhortations, entreaties, supplications, even tears —would you believe it, even tears?
uz: Keyin intervyular, sirli suhbatlar, nasihatlar, iltijolar, iltijolar, hatto ko'z yoshlari keldi.

en: Think what the passion for propaganda will bring some girls to!
uz: Bir o'ylab ko'ring, propagandaga bo'lgan ishtiyoq ba'zi qizlarni nimaga olib keladi!

en: I, of course, threw it all on my destiny, posed as hungering and thirsting for light, and finally resorted to the most powerful weapon in the subjection of the female heart, a weapon which never fails one.
uz: Albatta, men hamma narsani o'z taqdirimga tashladim, yorug'lik uchun och va chanqoq bo'lib o'zimni ko'rsatdim va nihoyat, ayol yuragiga bo'ysunishning eng kuchli qurolini ishlatdim, bu qurol hech qachon puchga chiqmaydi.

en: It’s the well-known resource —flattery.
uz: Bu mashhur manba - "Flattery".

en: Nothing in the world is harder than speaking the truth and nothing easier than flattery.
uz: Dunyoda haqiqatni aytishdan qiyinroq hech narsa yo'q va maqtanishdan osonroq hech narsa yo'q.

en: If there’s the hundredth part of a false note in speaking the truth, it leads to a discord, and that leads to trouble.
uz: Agar haqiqatni gapirishda yolg'on notaning yuzdan bir qismi bo'lsa, bu kelishmovchiliklarga olib keladi va bu muammolarga olib keladi.

en: But if all, to the last note, is false in flattery, it is just as agreeable, and is heard not without satisfaction.
uz: Ammo agar hamma narsa, so'nggi notasigacha, lazzat bilan yolg'on bo'lsa, u ham yoqimli va mamnunliksiz eshitilmaydi.

en: It may be a coarse satisfaction, but still a satisfaction.
uz: Bu katta mamnuniyat bo'lishi mumkin, ammo u hali ham mamnuniyatdir.

en: And however coarse the flattery, at least half will be sure to seem true.
uz: Qolaversa, maqtanish qanchalik jiddiy bo'lmasin, kamida uning yarmi haqiqatdek tuyuladi.

en: That’s so for all stages of development and classes of society.
uz: Bu rivojlanishning barcha bosqichlari va jamiyatning barcha sinflari uchun ham shunday.

en: A vestal virgin might be seduced by flattery.
uz: Vestal virjining g'ayratli bo'lishi mumkin.

en: I can never remember without laughter how I once seduced a lady who was devoted to her husband, her children,
uz: Men bir marta eriga, bolalariga, bolalariga sodiq qolgan bir ayolga qanday qilib qo'l urganimni hech qachon kulgisiz eslay olmayman.

en: What fun it was and how little trouble!
uz: Bu juda qiziqarli edi va juda kam muammo bor edi!

en: And the lady really had principles —of her own, anyway.
uz: Xonimning o'z me'yorlari bor edi.

en: All my tactics lay in simply being utterly annihilated and prostrate before her purity.
uz: Mening barcha taktikam shunchaki butunlayin yo'q qilinish va uning pokligiga sajda qilish edi.

en: I flattered her shamelessly, and as soon as I succeeded in getting a pressure of the hand, even a glance from her, I would reproach myself for having snatched it by force, and would declare that she had resisted, so that I could never have gained anything but for my being so unprincipled.
uz: Men uni uyatsiz maqtanardim va qo'limdan bosim o'tkazishga muvaffaq bo'lganimdan so'ng, hatto ko'z o'ngimda ko'rgach, uni kuch bilan o'g'irlab olganim uchun o'zimni ayblayman va u qarshilik ko'rsatganini aytaman, shuning uchun men hech qachon o'zim uchun hech narsa topolmasdim, lekin juda beg'ubor bo'lganim uchun.

en: I maintained that she was so innocent that she could not foresee my treachery, and yielded to me unconsciously, unawares, and so on.
uz: Men uning shunchalik aybsiz ekanligini, mening xiyonatimni ko'ra olmaydigan darajada aybsizligini ta'kidlab, o'zim bilmasdan, bilmasdan va hokazolar bilan menga bo'ysunib ketdim.

en: In fact, I triumphed, while my lady remained firmly convinced that she was innocent, chaste, and faithful to all her duties and obligations and had succumbed quite by accident.
uz: Darhaqiqat, men g'alaba qozondim, xonim esa o'zining aybsiz, xudojo'y va barcha vazifa va majburiyatlariga sodiq ekanligiga qat'iy ishonib, tasodifan vafot etgan.

en: And how angry she was with me when I explained to her at last that it was my sincere conviction that she was just as eager as I.
uz: Va nihoyat, men unga o'zimning samimiy e'tiqodim bo'lganini tushuntirganimda, u ham men kabi g'ayratli ekanligiga qanchalik g'azablanayotganini aytdim.

en: Poor Marfa Petrovna was awfully weak on the side of flattery, and if I had only cared to, I might have had all her property settled on me during her lifetime.
uz: kambag'al Marfa Petrovna maqtanchlik yo'lida juda zaif edi va agar men bunga e'tibor bersam, uning butun mol-mulki uning hayoti davomida menga tegishli bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: (I am drinking an awful lot of wine now and talking too much.) I hope you won’t be angry if I mention now that I was beginning to produce the same effect on Avdotya Romanovna.
uz: Umid qilamanki, Avdotya Romanovnaga ham xuddi shunday ta'sir ko'rsatishni boshlaganimni aytsam, g'azablanmaysiz.

en: But I was stupid and impatient and spoiled it all.
uz: Ammo men ahmoq va sabrsizlik bilan hamma narsani buzganman.

en: Avdotya Romanovna had several times —and one time in particular —been greatly displeased by the expression of my eyes, would you believe it?
uz: Avdotya Romanovna ko'p marta va ayniqsa bir marta ko'zlarim ko'rinishidan juda xafa bo'lgan, ishonasizmi?

en: There was sometimes a light in them which frightened her and grew stronger and stronger and more unguarded till it was hateful to her.
uz: Ba'zan ular ichida nur bor edi, bu uni qo'rqitadi va kuchli va kuchli bo'lib, uni nafratlanarli qilib ko'radi.

en: No need to go into detail, but we parted.
uz: Xulosaga kirishning hojati yo'q, lekin biz ajralib ketdik.

en: There I acted stupidly again.
uz: O'sha yerda men yana ahmoqona yo'l tutdim.

en: I fell to jeering in the coarsest way at all such propaganda and efforts to convert me; Parasha came on to the scene again, and not she alone; in fact there was a tremendous to-do.
uz: O'sha kabi targ'ibot va meni tavba qilish uchun qilingan harakatlar haqida men o'zimni qo'pol tarzda masxara qila boshladim; Parasha yana o'zi emas, balki o'zi ham o'rinni egallab oldi; aslida, juda ko'p ish bor edi.

en: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch, if you could only see how your sister’s eyes can flash sometimes!
uz: Ah, Rodion Romanovitch, agar siz ba'zan singillaringizning ko'zlari qanday chaqmoq chiqayotganini ko'rsangiz!

en: Never mind my being drunk at this moment and having had a whole glass of wine.
uz: Men hozir mast bo'lib, to'liq stakan sharob ichgan bo'lsam ham, bu menga ahamiyat bermaydi.

en: I am speaking the truth.
uz: Men haqiqatni aytyapman.

en: I assure you that this glance has haunted my dreams; the very rustle of her dress was more than I could stand at last.
uz: Sizga shuni ta'kidlaymanki, bu ko'rinish mening orzularimni qiynagan; uning kiyimining shovqinligi nihoyatda ko'proq edi.

en: I really began to think that I might become epileptic.
uz: Men epilepsiyaga chalingan bo'lishim mumkinligini o'ylay boshladim.

en: I could never have believed that I could be moved to such a frenzy.
uz: O'zimni bunday g'ayritabiiy holatga yetkazishimga hech qachon ishonolmasdim.

en: It was essential, indeed, to be reconciled, but by then it was impossible.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, yarashish muhim edi, ammo o'sha paytga kelib bu imkonsiz edi.

en: And imagine what I did then!
uz: Va o'shanda nima qilganimni tasavvur qiling!

en: To what a pitch of stupidity a man can be brought by frenzy!
uz: Insonni g'alati ahmoqlikka yetkazishi mumkin!

en: anything in a frenzy, Rodion Romanovitch.
uz: Har qanday narsa g'alati, Rodion Romanovitch.

en: I reflected that Avdotya Romanovna was after all a beggar (ach, excuse me, that’s not the word … but does it matter if it expresses the meaning?), that she lived by her work, that she had her mother and you to keep (ach, hang it, you are frowning again), and I resolved to offer her all my money —thirty thousand roubles I could have realised then —if she would run away with me here, to Petersburg.
uz: Avdotya Romanovna so'zsiz bo'lganini (ach, kechiring, bu so'z emas... lekin ma'nosini ifoda etishi muhimmi?), o'z ishi bilan yashayotganini, onasi va sizni saqlab qolish kerakligini (ach, o'tkazib yuboring, yana ko'nglingni teshib qo'yyapsan) o'ylab, unga butun pulimni taklif qilishga qaror qildim.

en: Of course I should have vowed eternal love, rapture, and so on.
uz: Albatta, men abadiy sevgi, quvonch va hokazolarga qasam ichardim.

en: Do you know, I was so wild about her at that time that if she had told me to poison Marfa Petrovna or to cut her throat and to marry herself, it would have been done at once!
uz: O'sha paytda men uni shunchalik yoqtirgan edimki, agar u menga Marfa Petrovnoni zaharlashimni yoki o'z qo'llarini kesib o'z o'zini turmushga chiqarishni aytganida edi, bu darhol sodir bo'lardi!

en: But it ended in the catastrophe of which you know already.
uz: Ammo bu siz allaqachon bilgan fojia bilan yakunlandi.

en: You can fancy how frantic I was when I heard that Marfa Petrovna had got hold of that scoundrelly attorney, Luzhin, and had almost made a match between them —which would really have been just the same thing as I was proposing.
uz: Marfa Petrovna o'sha g'alati advokat Luzhinni qo'lga olgani va ular o'rtasida deyarli to'g'rilashuvni o'rnatgani haqida eshitganimda men qanchalik g'alati bo'lganimni tasavvur qiling.

en: I notice that you’ve begun to be very attentive … you interesting young man.
uz: Ko'rib turibmanki, siz juda diqqatli bo'la boshladingiz, ey qiziqarli yigit.

en: …” Svidrigaïlov struck the table with his fist impatiently.
uz: ... Svidrigailov o'z qo'l bilan o'tirgan dasturxonni sabrsizlik bilan urdi.

en: Raskolnikov saw clearly that the glass or glass and a half of champagne that he had sipped almost unconsciously was affecting him —and he resolved to take advantage of the opportunity.
uz: Raskolnikov o'zi deyarli bexabar ichib olgan shampanjning bir stakan yoki yarim stakanining uni ta'sir qilayotganini aniq ko'rdi va imkoniyatdan foydalanishga qaror qildi.

en: He felt very suspicious of Svidrigaïlov.
uz: U Svidrigaylovga nisbatan juda shubhali bo'lgan.

en: “Well, after what you have said, I am fully convinced that you have come to Petersburg with designs on my sister,” he said directly to Svidrigaïlov, in order to irritate him further.
uz: Ha, aytganlaringizdan so'ng, siz Svidrigailovga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob berib, uni yanada g'azablantirish maqsadida opamning dizaynlari bilan Sankt-Peterburgga kelganingizga aminman.

en: “Oh, nonsense,” said Svidrigaïlov, seeming to rouse himself.
uz: Oh, aqlsizlik, dedi Svidrigailov, o'zini uyg'otishga o'xshaydi.

en: “Why, I told you … besides your sister can’t endure me.” “Yes, I am certain that she can’t, but that’s not the point.” “Are you so sure that she can’t?” Svidrigaïlov screwed up his eyes and smiled mockingly.
uz: Nima uchun, men sizga aytdim ... shundan tashqari singilingiz menga chiday olmaydi.  Ha, men uning chiday olmasligiga aminman, lekin bu gap emas.  Siz uning chiday olmasligiga shu qadar aminmisiz? Svidrigailov ko'zlarini to'kib, masxara qilib tabassum qildi.

en: “You are right, she doesn’t love me, but you can never be sure of what has passed between husband and wife or lover and mistress.
uz: Siz haqsiz, u meni yaxshi ko'rmaydi, lekin er-xotin yoki sevgilisi va sevimlisi o'rtasida nima sodir bo'lganidan hech qachon amin bo'la olmaysiz.

en: There’s always a little corner which remains a secret to the world and is only known to those two.
uz: Dunyo uchun sir bo'lib qolgan va faqat o'sha ikki kishiga ma'lum bo'lgan kichkina burchak har doim bor.

en: Will you answer for it that Avdotya Romanovna regarded me with aversion?” “From some words you’ve dropped, I notice that you still have designs —and of course evil ones —on Dounia and mean to carry them out promptly.”
uz: Avdotya Romanovna menga nafrat bilan qaraganidan javob berasizmi?Birinchi so'zlaringizdan ko'rinib turibdiki, sizda hali ham Douniaga qarshi rejalar bor va albatta yovuz rejalar bor va ularni tezda amalga oshirishni xohlaysiz.

en: “What, have I dropped words like that?” Svidrigaïlov asked in naive dismay, taking not the slightest notice of the epithet bestowed on his designs.
uz: Nima, men shunday so'zlarni qo'yib yubordimmi? Svidrigailov o'z dizaynlariga berilgan epitetni hech qachon e'tiborsiz qoldirib, naiflik bilan so'radi.

en: “Why, you are dropping them even now.
uz: Nima uchun, siz ularni hozir ham tashlayapsiz.

en: Why are you so frightened?
uz: Nima uchun shuncha qo'rqasiz?

en: What are you so afraid of now?” “Me —afraid?
uz: Endi nima uchun shuncha qo'rqasiz? Mening qo'rqqanimdan?

en: You have rather to be afraid of me, cher ami.
uz: Siz undan ko'ra mendan qo'rqishingiz kerak, aziz do'stim.

en: … I’ve drunk too much though, I see that.
uz: Ammo men juda ko'p ichganman, buni ko'rib turibman.

en: I was almost saying too much again.
uz: Men yana juda ko'p gapirardim.

en: there, water!” He snatched up the champagne bottle and flung it without ceremony out of the window.
uz: U yerda suv bor! U shampaning shishalarini olib, uni ceremoniyasiz darchaga tashladi.

en: Philip brought the water.
uz: Filip suvni olib keldi.

en: “That’s all nonsense!” said Svidrigaïlov, wetting a towel and putting it to his head.
uz: Bularning hammasi behuda! - dedi Svidrigailov, bir to'varchani bosqin qilib, boshini qo'yib.

en: “But I can answer you in one word and annihilate all your suspicions.
uz: Ammo men sizga bitta so'z bilan javob berib, barcha shubhalaringizni yo'q qila olaman.

en: Do you know that I am going to get married?” “You told me so before.” “Did I?
uz: Men turmushga chiqishimni bilasanmi?Siz menga buni oldin ham aytgandirsiz.Men shunday qildimmi?

en: But I couldn’t have told you so for certain for I had not even seen my betrothed; I only meant to.
uz: Ammo men sizga shubhasiz aytolmasdim, chunki men hatto qizimni ko'rmagan edim; faqat xohlagan edim.

en: But now I really have a betrothed and it’s a settled thing, and if it weren’t that I have business that can’t be put off, I would have taken you to see them at once, for I should like to ask your advice.
uz: Ammo hozirda men haqiqatan ham g'ayratli bo'lib qoldim va bu hal bo'ldi va agar mening kechiktirolmaydigan ishim bo'lmaganida, men sizni darhol ularga borishga olib ketardim, chunki men sizning maslahatingizni so'rashni xohlayman.

en: Ach, hang it, only ten minutes left!
uz: O'n daqiqadan so'ng, to'xtab qo'yinglar!

en: See, look at the watch.
uz: Qarang, soatga qarang.

en: But I must tell you, for it’s an interesting story, my marriage, in its own way.
uz: Ammo men sizga aytishim kerak, chunki bu qiziqarli hikoya, mening nikohim o'z uslubida.

en: Where are you off to?
uz: Qayerga ketyapsiz?

en: Going again?” “No, I’m not going away now.” “Not at all?
uz: Yana ketyapmanmi?  Yo'q, men endi ketmayman.  Hech qachon emas?

en: I’ll take you there, I’ll show you my betrothed, only not now.
uz: Men sizni o'sha yerga olib boraman, men sizga qizimni ko'rsataman, lekin hozir emas.

en: For you’ll soon have to be off.
uz: Chunki siz tez orada ketishingiz kerak bo'ladi.

en: You have to go to the right and I to the left.
uz: Siz o'ng tomonga, men esa chap tomonga borishim kerak.

en: Do you know that Madame Resslich, the woman I am lodging with now, eh?
uz: Siz ma'lummi, hozir men bilan birga yashayotgan ayol Resslich xonim?

en: I know what you’re thinking, that she’s the woman whose girl they say drowned herself in the winter.
uz: O'zingiz nima haqida o'ylayotganingizni bilaman, bu qiz qishda o'zini g'arq qilgan deb aytilgan ayol.

en: Come, are you listening?
uz: Kel, tinglayapsizmi?

en: She arranged it all for me.
uz: U hamma narsani men uchun tartibga soldi.

en: You’re bored, she said, you want something to fill up your time.
uz: U: "Siz charchagansiz, vaqtingizni to'ldirish uchun biror narsa xohlaysiz.

en: For, you know, I am a gloomy, depressed person.
uz: Chunki, bilasizmi, men tushkunlikka tushgan va tushkun odamman.

en: Do you think I’m lighthearted?
uz: Sizningcha, men yengilmanmi?

en: I do no harm, but sit in a corner without speaking a word for three days at a time.
uz: Men hech qanday zarar yetkazmayman, lekin uch kun bir burchada bir so'z aytmasdan o'tirib turaman.

en: And that Resslich is a sly hussy, I tell you.
uz: Va Resslich - o'zboshimchalik bilan g'ayritabiiy odam, demayman.

en: I know what she has got in her mind; she thinks I shall get sick of it, abandon my wife and depart, and she’ll get hold of her and make a profit out of her —in our class, of course, or higher.
uz: Men uning fikrini bilaman; u mening bundan bezovta bo'lishimni, xotinimni tashlab ketishimni va uni qo'lga olib, undan foyda olishimni o'ylaydi, albatta, bizning sinfimizda yoki undan yuqori sinfda.

en: She told me the father was a broken-down retired official, who has been sitting in a chair for the last three years with his legs paralysed.
uz: O'sha ayolning otasi nafaqaga chiqqan va so'nggi uch yil davomida oyoqlari to'sqin bo'lib, o'tirgan mansabdor shaxs ekanini aytdi.

en: The mamma, she said, was a sensible woman.
uz: Uning aytishicha, onasi aqlli ayol edi.

en: There is a son serving in the provinces, but he doesn’t help; there is a daughter, who is married, but she doesn’t visit them.
uz: Bir o'g'il viloyatlarda xizmat qiladi, lekin u yordam bermaydi; bir qizi turmush qurgan, lekin u ularga tashrif buyurmaydi.

en: And they’ve two little nephews on their hands, as though their own children were not enough, and they’ve taken from school their youngest daughter, a girl who’ll be sixteen in another month, so that then she can be married.
uz: Ularning qo'lida ikkita kichkina nevara bor, xuddi o'z farzandlari yetarli bo'lmaganidek, ular o'zlarining eng kichkina qizlarini maktabdan olib ketishdi, o'n olti yoshga to'lagan qiz boshqa oyda turmushga chiqishi mumkin.

en: I present myself —a landowner, a widower, of a well-known name, with connections, with a fortune.
uz: Men o'zimni o'z yer egasi, beva, mashhur ismli, bog'liq va boy odam sifatida tanitaman.

en: What if I am fifty and she is not sixteen?
uz: Agar men ellik yoshda bo'lsam va u o'n olti yoshda bo'lmasa nima bo'ladi?

en: But it’s fascinating, isn’t it?
uz: Ammo bu qiziqarli, shunday emasmi?

en: It is fascinating, ha- ha!
uz: Bu ajoyib, ha-ha!

en: You should have seen how I talked to the papa and mamma.
uz: Otam va onam bilan qanday suhbatlashayotganimni ko'rishingiz kerak edi.

en: It was worth paying to have seen me at that moment.
uz: O'sha paytda meni ko'rish uchun pul to'lashga arziydi.

en: She comes in, curtseys, you can fancy, still in a short frock —an unopened bud!
uz: U kiradi, curtseys, siz o'ylashingiz mumkin, hali ham qisqa kiyimda an ochilmagan bud!

en: Flushing like a sunset —she had been told, no doubt.
uz: Quyosh botish kabi oqib ketayotganini aytishgan edi, shubhasiz.

en: I don’t know how you feel about female faces, but to my mind these sixteen years, these childish eyes, shyness and tears of bashfulness are better than beauty; and she is a perfect little picture, too.
uz: Ayollar yuzlari haqida siz nima deb o'ylayotganingizni bilmayman, lekin mening fikrimcha, o'n olti yil davomida bu bolalik ko'zlari, uyat va o'ylamaslik ko'z yoshlari go'zallikdan yaxshiroqdir; va u ham mukammal kichik rasmdir.

en: Fair hair in little curls, like a lamb’s, full little rosy lips, tiny feet, a charmer!
uz: Kichik bo'laklarda chiroyli sochlar, qo'zi kabi, to'liq gullab-yashirilgan kichik dudlar, kichkina oyoqlar, charmer!

en: … Well, we made friends.
uz: Biz do'st bo'ldik.

en: I told them I was in a hurry owing to domestic circumstances, and the next day, that is the day before yesterday, we were betrothed.
uz: Men ularga oilaviy sharoitlar tufayli shoshilinch ekanligimni aytdim va ertasi kuni, ya'ni o'tgan kun oldin, biz kelin-qiz bo'ldik.

en: When I go now I take her on my knee at once and keep her there.
uz: Endi ketayotganimda, uni darhol tiz cho'kib, o'sha yerda qoldiraman.

en: … Well, she flushes like a sunset and I kiss her every minute.
uz: U quyosh botish kabi o'tadi va men har daqiqada uni o'paman.

en: Her mamma of course impresses on her that this is her husband and that this must be so.
uz: Uning onasi, albatta, bu uning eri ekanligini va bu shunday bo'lishi kerakligini unga ta'kidlaydi.

en: It’s simply delicious!
uz: Bu shunchaki mazali!

en: The present betrothed condition is perhaps better than marriage.
uz: Ehtimol, hozirgi kelinlik holati nikohdan yaxshiroqdir.

en: Here you have what is called la nature et la vérité, ha-ha!
uz: Bu erda sizda tabiat va haqiqat deb ataladigan narsa bor, ha-ha!

en: I’ve talked to her twice, she is far from a fool.
uz: Men u bilan ikki marta gapirganman, u ahmoqlikdan uzoq.

en: Sometimes she steals a look at me that positively scorches me.
uz: Ba'zan u menga o'g'irlab ko'rinadi va bu meni qattiq qo'zg'atadi.

en: Her face is like Raphael’s Madonna.
uz: Uning yuzi Rafaelning Madonnaga o'xshaydi.

en: You know, the Sistine Madonna’s face has something fantastic in it, the face of mournful religious ecstasy.
uz: Bilasizmi, Sixtina Madonna yuzida ajoyib narsa bor, bu qayg'uli diniy ekstaz yuzidir.

en: Haven’t you noticed it?
uz: Buni payqaganmisiz?

en: Well, she’s something in that line.
uz: Xo'sh, u o'sha satrda biror narsa bor.

en: The day after we’d been betrothed, I bought her presents to the value of fifteen hundred roubles —a set of diamonds and another of pearls and a silver dressing-case as large as this, with all sorts of things in it, so that even my Madonna’s face glowed.
uz: Turmush qurganimizdan bir kun o'tgach, men unga besh yuz rubl qiymatidagi sovg'alarni sotib oldim. ~~~ Bir qator olmoslar va yana bir marvaridlar va shu qadar katta kumush sovg'a, unda har xil narsalar bor edi, hatto mening Madonna yuzim ham yoritib turardi.

en: I sat her on my knee, yesterday, and I suppose rather too
uz: Kecha men uni tiz cho'kib o'tirdim va ehtimol men ham shunday qildim.

en: unceremoniously —she flushed crimson and the tears started, but she didn’t want to show it.
uz: U marosimsiz qizil qizil ko'rinishni o'chirib yubordi va ko'z yoshlari boshlandi, ammo buni ko'rsatishni istamadi.

en: We were left alone, she suddenly flung herself on my neck (for the first time of her own accord), put her little arms round me, kissed me, and vowed that she would be an obedient, faithful, and good wife, would make me happy, would devote all her life, every minute of her life, would sacrifice everything, everything, and that all she asks in return is my respect, and that she wants ‘nothing, nothing more from me, no presents.’ You’ll admit that to hear such a confession, alone, from an angel of sixteen in a muslin frock, with little curls, with a flush of maiden shyness in her cheeks and tears of enthusiasm in her eyes is rather fascinating!
uz: Biz yolg'iz qoldik, u to'satdan mening bo'yniga o'zini tashladi (o'z xohishi bilan birinchi marta), o'z qo'llarini o'rab oldi, meni o'pdi va meni itoatkor, sadoqatli va yaxshi xotin bo'lishga va meni baxtli qilishga va butun hayoti, har bir daqiqa hayotini qurbon qilishga va hamma narsani qurbon qilishga va faqat mening hurmatimni so'rashga va mendan boshqa hech narsa, hech narsa, hech qanday sovg'alarni istamaydi. Siz tan olishingiz kerakki, o'n olti yoshli farishtaning o'zidan o'z-o'zidan muslin kiyimda, kichik bo'g'imlar bilan, qizlik qorong'ilik shovqinligi chehralarida va ko'zlarida g'ayratning ko'z yoshlari bilan bunday tanbehni eshitish juda hayajonli!

en: Isn’t it fascinating?
uz: Bu qiziqarli emasmi?

en: It’s worth paying for, isn’t it?
uz: Buning uchun pul to'lash arziydi, shunday emasmi?

en: Well … listen, we’ll go to see my betrothed, only not just now!” “The fact is this monstrous difference in age and development excites your sensuality!
uz: Mana... tinglang, biz kelinimni ko'rishga ketamiz, lekin hozir emas!  Haqiqat shundaki, yosh va rivojlanishning bu ulkan farqi sizning hissiyligingizni hayajonlantiradi!

en: Will you really make such a marriage?” “Why, of course.
uz: Siz haqiqatan ham bunday nikoh qurasizmi?  Nima uchun, albatta.

en: Everyone thinks of himself, and he lives most gaily who knows best how to deceive himself.
uz: Har kim o'zini o'zi haqida o'ylaydi va o'zini qanday aldashni eng yaxshi biladigan kishi eng quvonchli hayot kechiradi.

en: But why are you so keen about virtue?
uz: Ammo nima uchun siz solihlikka shunchalik qiziqasiz?

en: Have mercy on me, my good friend.
uz: Menga rahm qil, yaxshi do'stim.

en: Ha-ha-ha!” “But you have provided for the children of Katerina Ivanovna.
uz: Ha-ha-ha!  Ammo siz Katerina Ivanovna bolalariga g'amxo'rlik qildingiz.

en: Though … though you had your own reasons.
uz: Garchi sizda o'zingizning sabablaringiz bo'lsa-da.

en: … I understand it all now.” “I am always fond of children, very fond of them,” laughed Svidrigaïlov.
uz: Hozir hamma narsani tushunib yetdim. Men har doim bolalarni yaxshi ko'raman, juda yaxshi ko'raman, - dedi Svidrigailov kulish bilan.

en: “I can tell you one curious instance of it.
