uz: Men o'zimni zaif his qilaman, Dounia, men juda charchadim; va men o'zimni nazorat qila olaman deb o'ylagandim. U unga ishonchsizlik bilan qarashdi.

en: “Where were you all night?” “I don’t remember clearly.
uz: Siz butun kecha qayerda bo'lgansiz? Men aniq eslay olmayman.

en: You see, sister, I wanted to make up my mind once for all, and several times I walked by the Neva, I remember that I wanted to end it all there, but … I couldn’t make up my mind,” he whispered, looking at her mistrustfully again.
uz: Mana, singlim, men bir marta va bir necha marta Neva yonidan o'tib ketishni istardim, men bu ishni o'sha yerda tugatishni xohlaganimni eslayman, lekin... Men qarorimni qabul qila olmadim, - deb peshvo qildi u, yana unga ishonchsizlik bilan qaradi.

en: That was just what we were afraid of, Sofya Semyonovna and I.
uz: Biz Sofiya Semyonovna va men qo'rqqanimiz shu edi.

en: Then you still have faith in life?
uz: Shunday qilib, siz hali ham hayotga ishonasizmi?

en: Thank God, thank God!” Raskolnikov smiled bitterly.
uz: Xudoga shukr, Xudoga shukr! Raskolnikov achchiq tabassum bilan tabassum qildi.

en: “I haven’t faith, but I have just been weeping in mother’s arms; I haven’t faith, but I have just asked her to pray for me.
uz: Imonim yo'q, lekin onamning qo'llarida yig'lab yurganman; imonim yo'q, lekin u men uchun ibodat qilishni so'raganman.

en: I don’t know how it is, Dounia, I don’t understand it.” “Have you been at mother’s?
uz: Men buni tushunmayapman, Dounia, men buni tushunmayapman.  Siz onalar uyida bo'lganmisiz?

en: Have you told her?” cried Dounia, horror-stricken.
uz: Siz unga aytdingizmi? Dounia qo'rqinchga to'lib, yig'ladi.

en: “Surely you haven’t done that?” “No, I didn’t tell her … in words; but she understood a great deal.
uz: Shubhasizki, siz buni qilmaganmisiz?Xo'r, men unga... so'zlar bilan aytmaganman; lekin u juda ko'p narsani tushunardi.

en: She heard you talking in your sleep.
uz: U sizni uxlab gapirganingizni eshitdi.

en: I am sure she half understands it already.
uz: Ishonchim komilki, u allaqachon buni yarmini tushunadi.

en: Perhaps I did wrong in going to see her.
uz: Ehtimol, men uni ko'rishga borganimda xato qilgan bo'lardim.

en: I don’t know why I did go.
uz: Nima uchun borganimni bilmayman.

en: I am a contemptible person, Dounia.” “A contemptible person, but ready to face suffering!
uz: Men nafratlanarli odamman, Dounia. Fatratlanarli odam, lekin azob-uqubatlarga duch kelishga tayyorman!

en: You are, aren’t you?” “Yes, I am going.
uz: Siz boryapsiz, shunday emasmi?Ha, men boryapman.

en: Yes, to escape the disgrace I thought of drowning myself, Dounia, but as I looked into the water, I thought that if I had considered myself strong till now I’d better not be afraid of disgrace,” he said, hurrying on.
uz: Ha, sharmandalikdan qochish uchun men o'zimni cho'kib tashlashni o'yladim, Dounia, lekin suvga qarab, agar hozirgacha o'zimni kuchli deb hisoblagan bo'lsam, sharmandalikdan qo'rqmasligim kerak, deb o'yladim.

en: “It’s pride, Dounia.” “Pride, Rodya.” There was a gleam of fire in his lustreless eyes; he seemed to be glad to think that he was still proud.
uz: Bu g'urur, Dounia.Rodya, g'urur.O'z ko'zlarida o't yoritib turardi; u hali ham g'ururlanayotganini ko'rib xursand bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: “You don’t think, sister, that I was simply afraid of the water?” he asked, looking into her face with a sinister smile.
uz: - Siz mening suvdan qo'rqqanimni o'ylamayapsizmi, singlim? - deb so'radi u, uning yuziga noxush tabassum bilan qarab.

en: “Oh, Rodya, hush!” cried Dounia bitterly.
uz: Oh, Rodya, hush! Dounia og'irlik bilan yig'ladi.

en: Silence lasted for two minutes.
uz: Ikki daqiqa davomida xotirjamlik davom etdi.

en: He sat with his eyes fixed on the floor; Dounia stood at the other end of the table and looked at him with anguish.
uz: U yerga ko'z tikib o'tirgan edi, Dounia esa stolning boshqa tomoniga turib, unga qayg'u bilan qaragan edi.

en: “It’s late, it’s time to go!
uz: kech, ketish vaqti keldi!

en: I am going at once to give myself up.
uz: Men o'zimni o'zimdan berishga harakat qilaman.

en: But I don’t know why I am going to give myself up.” Big tears fell down her cheeks.
uz: Ammo nega o'zimni topshirishim kerakligini bilmayman. Uning yig'i-yig'ini ko'p ko'tardi.

en: “You are crying, sister, but can you hold out your hand to me?” “You doubted it?” She threw her arms round him.
uz: Siz yig'layapsiz, singlim, lekin menga qo'lingizni uzatishingiz mumkinmi?

en: “Aren’t you half expiating your crime by facing the suffering?” she cried, holding him close and kissing him.
uz: Siz o'z jinoyatingizni azob chekayotgan kishiga duch kelib, yarim to'lov qilmayapsizmi? - deb yig'lab yubordi u, uni yaqinlab, o'pdi.

en: What crime?” he cried in sudden fury.
uz: Qaysi jinoyat? u to'satdan g'azabda yig'ladi.

en: “That I killed a vile noxious insect, an old pawnbroker woman, of use to no one!
uz: Men yomon zararli hasharotni, qadimgi qarzdor ayolni o'ldirganimni, hech kimga foydasi yo'qligini!

en: … Killing her was atonement for forty sins.
uz: ... Uni o'ldirish qirq gunohning kechirilishi edi.

en: She was sucking the life out of poor people.
uz: U kambag'al odamlarning hayotini sug'urib yurgan.

en: I am not thinking of it and I am not thinking of expiating it, and why are you all rubbing it in on all sides?
uz: Men bu haqda o'ylamayman va uni oqlash haqida ham o'ylamayman, nima uchun hammangiz uni har tomondan o'rab-o'rab yurasizlar?

en: a crime!’ Only now I see clearly the imbecility of my cowardice, now that I have decided to face this superfluous disgrace.
uz: Jinoyat! Faqatgina endi men qo'rqoqligimning ahmoqligini aniq ko'ryapman, endi men bu ortiqcha sharmandalikka duch kelishga qaror qildim.

en: It’s simply because I am contemptible and have nothing in me that I have decided to, perhaps too for my advantage, as that … Porfiry … suggested!” “Brother, brother, what are you saying?
uz: Faqatgina men nafratlanaman va ichimda hech narsa yo'qligim sababli, ehtimol o'z foydam uchun ham bunga qaror qildim, chunki bu ... Porfiry ... taklif qildi!Xotin, birodar, nima deyyapsan?

en: Why, you have shed blood?” cried Dounia in despair.
uz: Nima uchun, sen qon to'kding? Dounia umidsizlikka tushib yig'ladi.

en: “Which all men shed,” he put in almost frantically, “which flows and has always flowed in streams, which is spilt like champagne, and for which men are crowned in the Capitol and are called afterwards benefactors of mankind.
uz: Barcha odamlar to'kib solgan, deyarli g'alati ravishda qo'ygan, oqib o'tgan va doimo oqib kelgan, shampan kabi oqib o'tgan, va bu uchun odamlar Kapitolida tojlanadilar va keyinchalik insoniyatning xayrixohlari deb ataladilar.

en: Look into it more carefully and understand it!
uz: Buni diqqat bilan ko'rib chiqing va tushuning!

en: I too wanted to do good to men and would have done hundreds, thousands of good deeds to make up for that one piece of stupidity, not stupidity even, simply clumsiness, for the idea was by no means so stupid as it seems now that it has failed.
uz: Men ham odamlarga yaxshilik qilishni istardim va bu ahmoqlikni, hatto ahmoqlikni emas, shunchaki behudalikni qoplash uchun yuzlab, minglab yaxshiliklarni qilgan bo'lar edim, chunki g'oya hozirda muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchraganidek ahmoqlik emas edi.

en: … (Everything seems stupid when it fails.) By that stupidity I only wanted to put myself into an independent position, to take the first step, to obtain means, and then everything would have been smoothed over by benefits immeasurable in comparison.
uz: (Barcha narsa muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchraganda ahmoqlik kabi ko'rinadi) O'sha ahmoqlik bilan o'zimni mustaqil holatga qo'yish, birinchi qadam qo'yish, mablag'lar olishni istardim va keyin hamma narsa o'lchovsiz foyda bilan yengillashtirilgan bo'lardi.

en: … But I … I couldn’t carry out even the first step, because I am contemptible, that’s what’s the matter!
uz: Ammo men... hatto birinchi qadamni ham bajarolmadim, chunki men nafratlanarli emasman, shu muammo bor!

en: yet I won’t look at it as you do.
uz: Ammo men bunga siz kabi qaramasdim.

en: If I had succeeded I should have been crowned with glory, but now I’m trapped.” “But that’s not so, not so!
uz: Agar men muvaffaqiyatga erishgan bo'lsam, ulug'vorlik tojini olgan bo'lar edim, lekin endi men tuzoqqa tushdim.

en: Brother, what are you saying?” “Ah, it’s not picturesque, not aesthetically attractive!
uz: Birodar, nima deyyapsan?Ah, bu naqshli emas, estetik jihatdan ham jozibali emas!

en: I fail to understand why bombarding people by regular siege is more honourable.
uz: Nega odamlarni muntazam ravishda qo'rqib bombardimon qilish sharafliroq ekanini tushunmayapman.

en: The fear of appearances is the first symptom of impotence.
uz: Ko'rinishlardan qo'rqish - bu impotentlikning birinchi alomatidir.

en: I’ve never, never recognised this more clearly than now, and I am further than ever from seeing that what I did was a crime.
uz: Men buni hech qachon, hech qachon hozirdan ko'ra aniqroq tan olmaganman va qilgan ishim jinoyat ekanligini ko'rishdan hech qachon uzoqroqman.

en: I’ve never, never been stronger and more convinced than now.” The colour had rushed into his pale exhausted face, but as he uttered his last explanation, he happened to meet Dounia’s eyes and he saw such anguish in them that he could not help being checked.
uz: Men hech qachon, hech qachon hozirgidan ko'ra kuchliroq va ishonchliroq bo'lmaganman. Rang uning charchagan yuziga tushib ketgan edi, lekin u so'nggi tushuntirishini berayotganda, u Dounia ko'zlariga tushib qoldi va ularda shunchalik qayg'u ko'rdiki, uni tekshirib ko'rishdan to'xtamaydi.

en: He felt that he had, anyway, made these two poor women miserable, that he was, anyway, the cause … “Dounia darling, if I am guilty forgive me (though I cannot be forgiven if I am guilty).
uz: U o'zi bu ikki kambag'al ayolni qayg'uli qilib qo'yganini va o'zi sababchi bo'lganini his qilgan edi... Dounia azizim, agar men aybdor bo'lsam, meni kechirgin (agar aybdor bo'lsam, meni kechirolmaydi).

en: It’s time, high time to go.
uz: Vaqti keldi, ketish vaqti keldi.

en: Don’t follow me, I beseech you, I have somewhere else to go.
uz: Menga ergashmanglar, iltimos, boshqa joyga borishim kerak.

en: … But you go at once and sit with mother.
uz: Ammo siz darhol borib, onangiz bilan o'tirasiz.

en: It’s my last request of you.
uz: Bu sizdan so'nggi so'rovim.

en: Don’t leave her at all; I left her in a state of anxiety, that she is not fit to bear; she will die or go out of her mind.
uz: Hech qachon uni tashlab ketmang; men uni tashvishlanish holatida qoldirdim, uni ko'tarishga yaroqsiz; u o'ladi yoki aqldan ozadi.

en: Razumihin will be with you.
uz: Razumihin siz bilan birga bo'ladi.

en: I’ve been talking to him.
uz: Men u bilan suhbatlashyapman.

en: … Don’t cry about me: I’ll try to be honest and manly all my life, even if I am a murderer.
uz: ... Men uchun yig'lama: hatto qotil bo'lsam ham, butun hayotim davomida rostgo'y va erkak bo'lishga harakat qilaman.

en: Perhaps I shall some day make a name.
uz: Ehtimol, bir kun o'zimga o'zimni mashhur qila olaman.

en: I won’t disgrace you, you will see; I’ll still show.
uz: Men sizni sharmanda qilmayman, siz ko'rasiz; Men hali ham ko'rsataman.

en: … Now goodbye for the present,” he concluded hurriedly, noticing again a strange expression in Dounia’s eyes at his last words and promises.
uz: ... Endi hozirga salom, u shoshilinch yakunladi, yana Dounianing so'nggi so'zlari va va'dalarida g'ayrioddiy ifodani ko'rdi.

en: “Why are you crying?
uz: Nima uchun yig'layapsiz?

en: Don’t cry, don’t cry: we are not parting forever!
uz: Yig'lama, yig'lama: biz abadiy ajralmaymiz!

en: Wait a minute, I’d forgotten!” He went to the table, took up a thick dusty book, opened it and took from between the pages a little watercolour portrait on ivory.
uz: Bir daqiqa turing, men unutib qo'ydim! U stolga borib, toʻg'ri bo'lgan katta kitobni olib, ochdi va sahifalar orasidan fil xodaga o'xshash kichik akvarel portretini oldi.

en: It was the portrait of his landlady’s daughter, who had died of fever, that strange girl who had wanted to be a nun.
uz: Bu uning uy egasi qizining, issiqdan vafot etgan, qaynon bo'lishni istagan o'zgacha qizning portretidir.

en: For a minute he gazed at the delicate expressive face of his betrothed, kissed the portrait and gave it to Dounia.
uz: Bir daqiqa davomida u qizning nozik va ifodalangan yuziga qaradi, portretni o'qib, uni Douniaga beradi.

en: “I used to talk a great deal about it to her, only to her,” he said thoughtfully.
uz: "Men bu haqda u bilan ko'p gapirardim, faqat u bilan", - dedi u o'ylab.

en: “To her heart I confided much of what has since been so hideously realised.
uz: Men o'sha paytdan beri juda dahshatli tarzda amalga oshirilgan ko'p narsalarni uning qalbiga ishonib topshirdim.

en: Don’t be uneasy,” he returned to Dounia, “she
uz: O'zingizni noqulay his qilmang, u Douniaga qaytib keldi.

en: was as much opposed to it as you, and I am glad that she is gone.
uz: Siz kabi bunga qarshi bo'lgan edim va u yo'qolganidan xursandman.

en: The great point is that everything now is going to be different, is going to be broken in two,” he cried, suddenly returning to his dejection.
uz: Eng muhimi shundaki, hozir hamma narsa o'zgacha bo'lib, ikkiga bo'linadi, - deb yig'ladi u, birdan tushkunlikka qaytadi.

en: “Everything, everything, and am I prepared for it?
uz: Hamma narsa, hamma narsa va men bunga tayyormanmi?

en: Do I want it myself?
uz: O'zim xohlaymanmi?

en: They say it is necessary for me to suffer!
uz: Ular mening azob chekishim kerakligini aytishadi!

en: What’s the object of these senseless sufferings?
uz: Ushbu behuda azoblarning maqsadi nimada?

en: shall I know any better what they are for, when I am crushed by hardships and idiocy, and weak as an old man after twenty years’ penal servitude?
uz: Men og'irlik va axmoqlik tufayli vayron bo'lganimda va yigirma yillik qamoq qulligidan keyin keksa odam sifatida zaif bo'lganimda, ular nima uchun ishlayotganini yaxshiroq bilishim kerakmi?

en: And what shall I have to live for then?
uz: O'shanda nima uchun yashashim kerak?

en: Why am I consenting to that life now?
uz: Nima uchun men hozir bu hayotga rozi bo'lyapman?

en: Oh, I knew I was contemptible when I stood looking at the Neva at daybreak today!” At last they both went out.
uz: Bugun tongda Nevaga qarab turganimda, men nafratlanayotganimni bilardim! Oxir-oqibat ikkalasi ham chiqib ketishdi.

en: It was hard for Dounia, but she loved him.
uz: Dounia uchun bu qiyin edi, lekin u uni yaxshi ko'rgan.

en: She walked away, but after going fifty paces she turned round to look at him again.
uz: U ketib ketdi, ammo ellik qadam yurgandan so'ng yana unga qarashi uchun orqaga burildi.

en: He was still in sight.
uz: U hali ham ko'rinishda edi.

en: At the corner he too turned and for the last time their eyes met; but noticing that she was looking at him, he motioned her away with impatience and even vexation, and turned the corner abruptly.
uz: U ham burchada o'girilib, ularning ko'zlari oxirgi marta uchrashdi; lekin u ayolning unga qarayotganini ko'rib, uni sabrsizlik va hatto xafalik bilan olib ketishga ishora qildi va burchani keskin o'zgartirdi.

en: “I am wicked, I see that,” he thought to himself, feeling ashamed a moment later of his angry gesture to Dounia.
uz: Men yovuzman, buni ko'ryapman, deb o'yladi u o'ziga, bir zum o'tib Douniaga qo'ygan g'azabli harakatidan uyalgan.

en: “But why are they so fond of me if I don’t deserve it?
uz: Ammo nega men bunga loyiq bo'lmaganimda, ular meni shunchalik yaxshi ko'rishadi?

en: Oh, if only I were alone and no one loved me and I too had never loved anyone!
uz: Oh, agar men yolg'iz bo'lganimda va hech kim meni sevmagan bo'lsam va men ham hech kimni sevmagan bo'lsam!

en: Nothing of all this would have happened.
uz: Bularning hech biri sodir bo'lmagan bo'lardi.

en: But I wonder shall I in those fifteen or twenty years grow so meek that I shall humble myself before people and whimper at every word that I am a criminal?
uz: Ammo o'zimni o'sha o'n besh yoki yigirma yil ichida odamlarning oldida o'zimni kamtarin his etib, jinoyatchi ekanligim haqidagi har bir so'zdan ko'nglimni og'diraman, deb o'ylayman.

en: Yes, that’s it, that’s it, that’s what they are sending me there for, that’s what they want.
uz: Ha, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday, shunday!

en: Look at them running to and fro about the streets, every one of them a scoundrel and a criminal at heart and, worse still, an idiot.
uz: Ularni ko'chalarda yugurib-yugurib ko'ring, ularning har biri yuragida jinoyatchi, yuragida esa jinoyatchi va eng og'irini esa, ahmoq.

en: But try to get me off and they’d be wild with righteous indignation.
uz: Ammo meni tushirmoqchi bo'lsangiz, ular adolatli g'azabga tushishadi.

en: Oh, how I hate them all!” He fell to musing by what process it could come to pass, that he could be humbled before all of them, indiscriminately —humbled by conviction.
uz: Oʻshalarning hammasini qanday nafratlayman! U qanday jarayon yuz berishi mumkinligini oʻylab, ularning barchasi oldida kamtarin boʻlishi mumkinligini, tanqid bilan kamtarin boʻlishi mumkinligini oʻylashga tushdi.

en: Would not twenty years of continual bondage crush him utterly?
uz: Ikki yuz yillik doimiy qullik uni butunlayin ezib tashlamasmidi?

en: Water wears out a stone.
uz: Suv toshni yo'q qiladi.

en: And why, why should he live after that?
uz: Va nima uchun, nima uchun u bundan keyin yashashi kerak?

en: Why should he go now when he knew that it would be so?
uz: Nima uchun u endi ketishi kerak edi, chunki u buni bilgan edi?

en: It was the hundredth time perhaps that he had asked himself that question since the previous evening, but still he went.
uz: Ehtimol, o'tgan kechadan buyon o'ziga bu savolni bergani yuzinchi marta bo'lgan, lekin u hali ham bordi.

en: VIII When he went into Sonia’s room, it was already getting dark.
uz: Sonia VIII xonasiga kirganida, qorong'ilik boshlangan edi.

en: All day Sonia had been waiting for him in terrible anxiety.
uz: Sonia uni kun bo'yi dahshatli xavotirda kutgan edi.

en: Dounia had been waiting with her.
uz: Dounia u bilan birga kutgan edi.

en: She had come to her that morning, remembering Svidrigaïlov’s words that Sonia knew.
uz: O'sha kuni ertalab Svidrigailovning Sonia bilgan so'zlarini eslab, uning oldiga keldi.

en: We will not describe the conversation and tears of the two girls, and how friendly they became.
uz: Ikkala qizning suhbatini, ko'z yoshlarini va ular qanchalik do'stona munosabatda bo'lganlarini tasvirlab bermaymiz.

en: Dounia gained one comfort at least from that interview, that her brother would not be alone.
uz: Dounia o'sha suhbatdan hech bo'lmaganda bitta tasalli topdi: ukasi yolg'iz qolmaydi.

en: He had gone to her, Sonia, first with his confession; he had gone to her for human fellowship when he needed it; she would go with him wherever fate might send him.
uz: U birinchi bo'lib Soniaga tanbehini aytdi, kerak bo'lganda unga insonlik rishtalari uchun murojaat qildi, u uni taqdir qayerga yuborgan bo'lsa ham, u bilan birga borardi.

en: Dounia did not ask, but she knew it was so.
uz: Dounia so'ramadi, lekin u buni bilardi.

en: She looked at Sonia almost with reverence and at first almost embarrassed her by it.
uz: U Soniaga taxminan hurmat bilan qaradi va boshida bu uni deyarli urib qo'yadi.

en: Sonia was almost on the point of tears.
uz: Sonia deyarli ko'z yoshlariga tushib qoldi.

en: She felt herself, on the contrary, hardly worthy to look at Dounia.
uz: Aksincha, u o'zini Douniaga qarashga loyiq emas deb hisoblagan.

en: Dounia’s gracious image when she had bowed to her so attentively and respectfully at their first meeting in Raskolnikov’s room had remained in her mind as one of the fairest visions of her life.
uz: Dounia Raskolnikov xonasidagi birinchi uchrashuvida unga shunchalik diqqat va hurmat bilan sajda qilganida, uning mehribonligi uning ongida hayotining eng go'zal tasavvurlaridan biri sifatida saqlanib qolgan edi.

en: Dounia at last became impatient and, leaving Sonia, went to her brother’s room to await him there; she kept thinking that he would come there first.
uz: Dounia nihoyat sabrsizlikka toʻlib, Soniyani qoldirib, ukasining xonasiga borib, uni kutib turdi; u oʻzi birinchi boʻlib u yerga kelishini oʻylagan.

en: When she had gone, Sonia began to be tortured by the dread of his committing suicide, and Dounia too feared it.
uz: U ketgach, Sonia uning o'z joniga qasd qilishidan qo'rqqanidan azob chekishni boshladi va Dounia ham undan qo'rqardi.

en: But they had spent the day trying to persuade each other that that could not be, and both were less anxious while they were together.
uz: Ammo ular kun bo'yi bir-birlarini bunday bo'lmasligiga ishontirishga harakat qilishdi va ular birga bo'lganlarida, ikkovi ham kamroq tashvishlanishardi.

en: As soon as they parted, each thought of nothing else.
uz: Ular ajrashganidan so'ng, har biri boshqa hech narsa haqida o'ylamagan.

en: Sonia remembered how Svidrigaïlov had said to her the day before that Raskolnikov had two alternatives —Siberia or … Besides she knew his vanity, his pride and his lack of faith.
uz: Sonia Svidrigailov bir kun oldin Raskolnikovning ikkita variant borligini aytganini esladi.Siberiya yoki... Bundan tashqari, u uning beg'uborligini, mag'rurligini va imonsizligini bilardi.

en: “Is it possible that he has nothing but cowardice and fear of death to make him live?” she thought at last in despair.
uz: Uni tirik qoldirish uchun qo'rquv va o'limdan qo'rqishdan boshqa hech narsa yo'qligi mumkinmi? U nihoyat umidsizlikda o'yladi.

en: Meanwhile the sun was setting.
uz: Shu vaqt ichida quyosh botib borayotgan edi.

en: Sonia was standing in dejection, looking intently out of the window, but from it she could see nothing but the unwhitewashed blank wall of the next house.
uz: Sonia tushkunlikka tushib, darchaga diqqat bilan qarayotgan edi, lekin undan olis uyning oq bo'lmagan quruq devoridan boshqa hech narsa ko'rmagan.

en: At last when she began to feel sure of his death —he walked into the room.
uz: Nihoyat, uning o'limiga ishonch hosil qila boshlaganida, u xonasiga kirdi.

en: She gave a cry of joy, but looking carefully into his face she turned pale.
uz: U quvonchdan qichqirib yubordi, lekin uning yuziga diqqat bilan qaraganida, o'sha ayol o'z-o'zidan oqib ketdi.

en: “Yes,” said Raskolnikov, smiling.
uz: Ha, dedi Raskolnikov, tabassum bilan.

en: “I have come for your cross, Sonia.
uz: Men sizning xochingiz uchun keldim, Sonia.

en: It was you told me to go to the crossroads; why is it you are frightened now it’s come to that?” Sonia gazed at him astonished.
uz: Menga yo'l chekkasiga borishimni aytishgan edilar, endi nima uchun qo'rqasiz? - Sonia uni hayron ko'rib qoldi.

en: His tone seemed strange to her; a cold shiver ran over her, but in a moment she guessed that the tone and the words were a mask.
uz: Uning tovoni unga g'alati ko'rinardi; uning ustiga sovuq titroq tushdi, lekin bir daqiqada u tovon va so'zlarning niqobga o'xshashligini tushundi.

en: He spoke to her looking away, as though to avoid meeting her eyes.
uz: U ayolga qarab gapirdi, xuddi uning ko'zlarini ko'rmaslik uchun.

en: “You see, Sonia, I’ve decided that it will be better so.
uz: Qarang, Sonia, men shunga o'xshab yaxshiroq bo'lishini qaror qildim.

en: … But it’s a long story and there’s no need to discuss it.
uz: Ammo bu uzoq hikoya va uni muhokama qilishning hojati yo'q.

en: But do you know what angers me?
uz: Ammo nima meni g'azablantirishini bilasizmi?

en: It annoys me that all those stupid brutish faces will be gaping at me directly, pestering me with their stupid questions, which I shall have to answer —they’ll point their fingers at me.
uz: O'sha ahmoqona vahshiy yuzlarning menga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri nazar solib, o'zlarining ahmoqona savollari bilan meni qiynashgani menga g'alati keladi, ularga javob berishim kerak bo'ladi.

en: You know I am not going to Porfiry, I am sick of him.
uz: Men Porfirga bormayman, uni tashlab ketishimdan bezovta ekanimni bilasiz.

en: I’d rather go to my friend, the Explosive Lieutenant; how I shall surprise him, what a sensation I shall make!
uz: Men do'stimning oldiga borishni afzal ko'raman, u "Explosive Lieutenant" bo'lib, uni qanday hayratda qoldirishim kerak, qanday taassurot qoldirishim kerak!

en: But I must be cooler; I’ve become too irritable of late.
uz: Ammo men salqinroq bo'lishim kerak; men so'nggi paytlarda juda g'azablanarli bo'ldim.

en: You know I was nearly shaking my fist at my sister just now, because she turned to take a last look at me.
uz: O'zingiz bilasiz, men hozir singlimga qo'limni qo'zg'atmoqchi edim, chunki u menga so'nggi marta ko'z tikdi.

en: It’s a brutal state to be in!
uz: Bu yovuz holatda bo'lish naqadar dahshatli!

en: what am I coming to!
uz: Men nimaga boryapman!

en: Well, where are the crosses?” He seemed hardly to know what he was doing.
uz: Xo'sh, xochlar qayerda? U nima qilayotganini bilmagan bo'lib tuyuladi.

en: He could not stay still or concentrate his attention on anything; his ideas seemed to gallop after one another, he talked incoherently, his hands trembled slightly.
uz: U to'xtamay, hech narsaga e'tiborini qaratolmasdi; fikrlari bir-biriga galop bo'lib ketayotgandek tuyuldi, u bir-biriga to'g'ri kelmay gapirardi, qo'llari biroz titrayotgandek bo'ldi.

en: Without a word Sonia took out of the drawer two crosses, one of cypress wood and one of copper.
uz: Sonia bir so'z aytmay, qutidan ikkita xochni olib chiqdi, biri sapres yog'ochidan, biri esa misdan.

en: She made the sign of the cross over herself and over him, and put the wooden cross on his neck.
uz: U o'zi va uning ustiga xoch belgisini yasab, uning bo'yniga yog'och xochni qo'ydi.

en: “It’s the symbol of my taking up the cross,” he laughed.
uz: "Bu mening xochni ko'tarishimning ramzi", - dedi u kulish bilan.

en: “As though I had not suffered much till now!
uz: Agar men hozirgacha ko'p azob chekmagan bo'lsam!

en: The wooden cross, that is the peasant one; the copper one, that is Lizaveta’s —you will wear
uz: Daraxt xoch - bu qishloq xo'jaligi, mis xoch - bu Lizavetas, siz uni kiyasiz.

en: So she had it on … at that moment?
uz: Demak, u o'sha paytda uni kiyib olganmi?

en: I remember two things like these too, a silver one and a little icon.
uz: Men ham shu kabi ikkita narsani eslayman: kumush va kichkina ikoni.

en: I threw them back on the old woman’s neck.
uz: Men ularni keksa ayolning bo'yniga qaytarib yubordim.

en: Those would be appropriate now, really, those are what I ought to put on now.
uz: Bular hozir o'rinli bo'ladi, haqiqatan ham, men hozir kiyishi kerak bo'lgan narsalar.

en: … But I am talking nonsense and forgetting what matters; I’m somehow forgetful.
uz: Ammo men behuda gapirib, muhim bo'lgan narsani unutib qo'yyapman; men qaysidir jihatdan unutib qo'yaman.

en: … You see I have come to warn you, Sonia, so that you might know … that’s all —that’s all I came for.
uz: Ko'ryapsanmi, men seni ogohlantirish uchun keldim, Sonia, shuni bilishing uchun, men faqat shu maqsadda keldim.

en: But I thought I had more to say.
uz: Ammo men aytadigan so'zlarim bor deb o'yladim.

en: You wanted me to go yourself.
uz: O'zing borishimni xohlading.

en: Well, now I am going to prison and you’ll have your wish.
uz: Endi men qamoqqa ketyapman va siz o'zingizning xohishingiz amalga oshadi.

en: Well, what are you crying for?
uz: Xo'sh, nima uchun yig'layapsan?

en: Oh, how I hate it all!” But his feeling was stirred; his heart ached, as he looked at her.
uz: Oh, men bularning barchasidan nafratlanaman! Ammo uning his-tuyg'ulari g'ayratga tushdi; unga qarab yuragi og'riqli bo'ldi.

en: “Why is she grieving too?” he thought to himself.
uz: U ham nega qayg'urmoqda? - deb o'yladi u o'ziga.

en: Why is she looking after me, like my mother or Dounia?
uz: Nima uchun u mening onam yoki Dounia kabi menga g'amxo'rlik qiladi?

en: She’ll be my nurse.” “Cross yourself, say at least one prayer,” Sonia begged in a timid broken voice.
uz: U mening hamshiralarim bo'ladi.Soniya o'zini o'ziga o'tkazadi, hech bo'lmaganda bitta ibodatni aytadi.Soniya uyatchan va buzilgan ovoz bilan iltijo qildi.

en: “Oh certainly, as much as you like!
uz: Oh, albatta, xohlaganingizcha!

en: And sincerely, Sonia, sincerely.
uz: Va chin dildan, Sonia, chin dildan.

en: …” But he wanted to say something quite different.
uz: Ammo u ancha boshqacha narsani aytmoqchi edi.

en: He crossed himself several times.
uz: U o'zini bir necha marta o'zi o'ldirgan.

en: Sonia took up her shawl and put it over her head.
uz: Sonia shallini olib, boshining ustiga qo'ydi.

en: It was the green drap de dames shawl of which Marmeladov had spoken, “the family shawl.” Raskolnikov thought of that looking at it, but he did not ask.
uz: Bu Marmeladov aytib o'tgan yashil shal, "Oila shal" edi. Raskolnikov uni ko'rib turganini o'yladi, lekin so'ramadi.

en: He began to feel himself that he was certainly forgetting things and was disgustingly agitated.
uz: U o'zini, albatta, narsalarni unutayotganini his qila boshladi va jirkanch darajada g'ayratga tushdi.

en: He was frightened at this.
uz: U bundan qo'rqqan edi.

en: He was suddenly struck too by the thought that Sonia meant to go with him.
uz: U ham Sonia bilan birga ketmoqchi bo'lganini birdan ko'rib qoldi.

en: “What are you doing?
uz: Siz nima qilyapsiz?

en: Where are you going?
uz: Qayerga ketyapsan?

en: I’ll go alone,” he cried in cowardly vexation, and almost resentful, he moved towards the door.
uz: Men yolg'iz ketaman, - deb qo'rqinchli xafalik bilan yig'ladi u, deyarli g'azabga to'lib, eshik tomon harakatlandi.

en: “What’s the use of going in procession?” he muttered going out.
uz: Porsessiyada yurishning foydasi nimada? u tashqariga chiqishni g'iybat qildi.

en: Sonia remained standing in the middle of the room.
uz: Sonia xonaning o'rtasida turib qoldi.

en: He had not even said goodbye to her; he had forgotten her.
uz: U hatto xotiniga salom ham aytmagan edi, uni unutib qo'ygan edi.

en: A poignant and rebellious doubt surged in his heart.
uz: Uning qalbida qattiq va isyonkor shubha paydo bo'ldi.

en: “Was it right, was it right, all this?” he thought again as he went down the stairs.
uz: Bularning barchasi to'g'ri bo'lganmi yoki yo'qmi? deb o'yladi u, daraxtdan tushayotganda.

en: “Couldn’t he stop and retract it all … and not go?” But still he went.
uz: U to'xtatib, hamma narsani orqaga surib, ketmay qololmaydimi?

en: He felt suddenly once for all that he mustn’t ask himself questions.
uz: Toʻsatdan bir marta oʻziga savol berish kerak emasligini his qildi.

en: As he turned into the street he remembered that
uz: U ko'chaga o'tar ekan, o'sha narsani esladi.

en: he had not said goodbye to Sonia, that he had left her in the middle of the room in her green shawl, not daring to stir after he had shouted at her, and he stopped short for a moment.
uz: U Sonia bilan xayrlashmagan, uni o'rtada yashil shaliga qo'yib qo'ygan, unga qichqirganidan keyin qo'zg'atishga jur'at etmagan va bir zumga to'xtatgan.

en: At the same instant, another thought dawned upon him, as though it had been lying in wait to strike him then.
uz: Shu paytning o'zida unga boshqa bir fikr keldi, xuddi o'sha paytda uni urish uchun o'tirgan bo'lsa kerak.

en: “Why, with what object did I go to her just now?
uz: Nima uchun, men u ayolga qanday maqsad bilan borgan edim?

en: I told her —on business; on what business?
uz: Men unga biznes haqida aytdim; qanday biznes haqida?

en: I had no sort of business!
uz: Mening hech qanday ishim yo'q edi!

en: To tell her I was going; but where was the need?
uz: Men unga borayotganimni aytmoqchiman, lekin nima kerak edi?

en: No, no, I drove her away just now like a dog.
uz: Yo'q, yo'q, men uni it kabi haydab yubordim.

en: Did I want her crosses?
uz: Men uning xochlarini xohlarmidim?

en: Oh, how low I’ve sunk!
uz: Oh, men qanchalik pastga qulab ketganman!

en: No, I wanted her tears, I wanted to see her terror, to see how her heart ached!
uz: Yo'q, men uning ko'z yoshlarini, qo'rquvni ko'rishni, yuragidagi og'riqlarni ko'rishni xohladim!

en: I had to have something to cling to, something to delay me, some friendly face to see!
uz: Menga qo'shilib turadigan narsa, meni kechiktiradigan narsa, ko'rish uchun do'stlik yuzi kerak edi!

en: And I dared to believe in myself, to dream of what I would do!
uz: O'zimga ishonishga va nima qilishni orzu qilishga jur'at qildim!

en: I am a beggarly contemptible wretch, contemptible!” He walked along the canal bank, and he had not much further to go.
uz: Men begona begona, begona odamman! U kanal qirg'og'i bo'ylab yurgan va ko'proq ketishi kerak bo'lmagan.

en: But on reaching the bridge he stopped and turning out of his way along it went to the Hay Market.
uz: Ammo ko'prikga yetganida to'xtadi va yo'lidan o'tib, Hay bozoriga bordi.

en: He looked eagerly to right and left, gazed intently at every object and could not fix his attention on anything; everything slipped away.
uz: U o'ng va chap tomonga ko'z tikib, har bir narsaga diqqat bilan qaradi va hech narsaga e'tiborini qaratolmaydi; hamma narsa o'tib ketadi.

en: “In another week, another month I shall be driven in a prison van over this bridge, how shall I look at the canal then?
uz: Boshqa bir hafta, yana bir oy ichida men qamoq mashinasida bu ko'prikdan o'tib ketaman, o'shanda kanalga qanday qarashim kerak?

en: I should like to remember this!” slipped into his mind.
uz: Men buni eslab qolishni xohlayman! Uning ongiga o'tdi.

en: How shall I read those letters then?
uz: Xo'sh, bu xatlarni qanday o'qishim kerak?

en: It’s written here ‘Campany,’ that’s a thing to remember, that letter a, and to look at it again in a month —how shall I look at it then?
uz: Bu yerda Kampanani yozgan, bu  bir narsani eslab qolish kerak, bu harf a, va bir oy ichida yana bir bor uni ko'rib chiqish shunday bo'lsa, qanday qilib uni ko'rib chiqaman?

en: What shall I be feeling and thinking then?
uz: O'shanda nima his-tuyg'u va o'ylayman?

en: … How trivial it all must be, what I am fretting about now!
uz: Men hozir g'amgin bo'lgan narsalarning barchasi qanchalik ahamiyatsiz bo'lishi kerak!

en: Of course it must all be interesting … in its way … (Ha-ha-ha!
uz: Albatta, bularning barchasi o'z uslubida qiziqarli bo'lishi kerak... (Ha-ha-ha!)

en: What am I thinking about?) I am becoming a baby, I am showing off to myself; why am I ashamed?
uz: Nima haqida o'ylayapman?) Men chaqaloq bo'lib, o'zimni ko'rsatyapman; nima uchun uyalyapman?

en: that fat man —a German he must be —who pushed against me, does he know whom he pushed?
uz: O'sha semiz nemis o'zi bo'lishi kerak, menga qarshi shovqin qilgan, kimni shovqin qilganini biladimi?

en: There’s a peasant woman with a baby, begging.
uz: U yerda bir qishloq xonadoni chaqaloq bilan yolvorib yuribdi.

en: It’s curious that she thinks me happier than she is.
uz: O'ziga qaraganda meni ko'proq baxtli deb o'ylashi g'alati.

en: I might give her something, for the incongruity of it.
uz: Ehtimol, men unga bir narsa beraman, chunki bu ziddiyat bor.

en: Here’s a five kopeck piece left in my pocket, where did I get it?
uz: Bu mening qutimda qolgan besh kopek daraxt, men uni qayerdan oldim?

en: Here, here … take it, my good woman!” “God bless you,” the beggar chanted in a lachrymose voice.
uz: Mana, mana... oling, yaxshi xotinim! Xudo seni duo qilsin, so'roqchi qichqiriq ovoz bilan qo'shiq aytdi.

en: He went into the Hay Market.
uz: U Hay bozoriga bordi.

en: It was distasteful, very distasteful to be in a crowd, but he walked just where he saw most people.
uz: Jamoatda bo'lish yoqimsiz edi, juda yoqimsiz edi, lekin u ko'pchilikni ko'rgan joyda yurardi.

en: would have given anything in the world to be alone; but he knew himself that he would not have remained alone for a moment.
uz: U yolg'iz qolish uchun dunyodagi hamma narsani berardi; lekin u o'zi bilganidek, bir zum ham yolg'iz qolmaydi.

en: There was a man drunk and disorderly in the crowd; he kept trying to dance and falling down.
uz: Xaloyiq orasida mast va tartibsiz bir kishi bor edi; u raqsga urinib, yerga yiqilib qolibdi.

en: There was a ring round him.
uz: Uning atrofida bir do'zax bor edi.

en: Raskolnikov squeezed his way through the crowd, stared for some minutes at the drunken man and suddenly gave a short jerky laugh.
uz: Raskolnikov xaloyiq orasidan o'zini siqib, bir necha daqiqa davomida mast odamga tikilib, to'satdan qisqacha qichqiriq qildi.

en: A minute later he had forgotten him and did not see him, though he still stared.
uz: Bir daqiqa o'tgach, u uni unutib qo'ydi va uni ko'rmadi, ammo u hali ham ko'z o'ngida turibdi.

en: He moved away at last, not remembering where he was; but when he got into the middle of the square an emotion suddenly came over him, overwhelming him body and mind.
uz: Oxir-oqibat u qayerdaligini eslay olmay, ketib ketdi; ammo maydonga kirib kelganida, u birdan his-tuyg'ularni boshidan kechirib, tanasini va ongini o'rab oldi.

en: He suddenly recalled Sonia’s words, “Go to the crossroads, bow down to the people, kiss the earth, for you have sinned against it too, and say aloud to the whole world, ‘I am a murderer.’ ” He trembled, remembering that.
uz: Birdan u Sonaning so'zlarini esladi: "Yo'l chekkasiga boring, xalqqa sajda qiling, yerni o'pish, chunki siz ham unga qarshi gunoh qildingiz va butun dunyoga baland ovoz bilan ayting: "Men qotilman".

en: And the hopeless misery and anxiety of all that time, especially of the last hours, had weighed so heavily upon him that he positively clutched at the chance of this new unmixed, complete sensation.
uz: Va o'sha vaqtning, ayniqsa so'nggi soatlarning umidsiz qayg'usi va tashvishlari unga shunchalik og'ir bo'lganki, u ushbu yangi, to'liq va to'liq hissiyotga ega bo'lish imkoniyatini qo'lga kiritdi.

en: It came over him like a fit; it was like a single spark kindled in his soul and spreading fire through him.
uz: Bu uning ustiga o't kabi tushdi; u uning ruhida yonib, o'z ichiga olovni tarqatgan bitta shvashqanday edi.

en: Everything in him softened at once and the tears started into his eyes.
uz: Uning ichidagi hamma narsa birdan yumshatildi va ko'zlariga yoshlar tushdi.

en: He fell to the earth on the spot.
uz: U darhol yerga yiqildi.

en: … He knelt down in the middle of the square, bowed down to the earth, and kissed that filthy earth with bliss and rapture.
uz: U maydonga tiz cho'kib, yerga sajda qildi va o'sha nopok yerni quvonch va quvonch bilan o'pdi.

en: He got up and bowed down a second time.
uz: U o'rnidan turib, ikkinchi marta sajda qildi.

en: “He’s boozed,” a youth near him observed.
uz: U boozlangan, u atrofidagi bir yigit uni kuzatgan.

en: There was a roar of laughter.
uz: Qichqiriqlarning qichqiriqlari eshitildi.

en: “He’s going to Jerusalem, brothers, and saying goodbye to his children and his country.
uz: U Quddusga ketadi, birodarlar, o'z farzandlari va o'z yurtiga salom aytadi.

en: He’s bowing down to all the world and kissing the great city of St.
uz: U butun dunyoga sajda qilib, buyuk St. Petersburg shahrini o'pishmoqda.

en: Petersburg and its pavement,” added a workman who was a little drunk.
uz: Sankt-Peterburg va uning pavimentolari, biroz mast bo'lgan ishchi qo'shildi.

en: “Quite a young man, too!” observed a third.
uz: Toʻgʻri yosh yigit ham! uchinchi kishi kuzatdi.

en: “And a gentleman,” someone observed soberly.
uz: Va bir gentleman, kimdir soberlik bilan kuzatdi.

en: “There’s no knowing who’s a gentleman and who isn’t nowadays.” These exclamations and remarks checked Raskolnikov, and the words, “I am a murderer,” which were perhaps on the point of dropping from his lips, died away.
uz: Bugun kim xonim, kim xonim emasligini bilish mumkin emas. Ushbu ovozlar va izohlar Raskolnikovni tekshirib ko'rdi va, ehtimol, uning og'zidan tushib ketmoqchi bo'lgan "Men qotilman" degan so'zlar o'lib ketdi.

en: He bore these remarks quietly, however, and, without looking round, he turned down a street leading to the police office.
uz: Biroq u bu so'zlarni xotirjamlik bilan qabul qildi va atrofga nazar solmasdan, politsiyaga olib boradigan ko'chaga qarab ketdi.

en: He had a glimpse of something on the way which
uz: U yo'lda bir narsa ko'rinishini ko'rdi.

en: did not surprise him; he had felt that it must be so.
uz: Bu uni hayratda qoldirmagan, chunki u o'zini shunday his qilgan.

en: The second time he bowed down in the Hay Market he saw, standing fifty paces from him on the left, Sonia.
uz: Ikkinchi marta u Hay bozoriga yiqilganida, sol tomonidagi Sonia undan ellik qadam uzoqlikda turganini ko'rdi.

en: She was hiding from him behind one of the wooden shanties in the marketplace.
uz: U undan bozordagi yogʻochli shantsiyalarning birida yashiringan.

en: She had followed him then on his painful way!
uz: Keyinchalik u uning og'ir yo'lidan ergashib ketgan edi!

en: Raskolnikov at that moment felt and knew once for all that Sonia was with him forever and would follow him to the ends of the earth, wherever fate might take him.
uz: Raskolnikov o'sha paytda Sonia uning yonida bo'lganini va uning yerning chetlarigacha, taqdir uni qayerga olib ketayotganini bir marta his qildi va bildi.

en: It wrung his heart … but he was just reaching the fatal place.
uz: Bu uning qalbini g'amgin qildi ... lekin u o'z o'limini kutadigan joyga yetib borayotgan edi.

en: He went into the yard fairly resolutely.
uz: U juda qat'iylik bilan hovliga kirdi.

en: He had to mount to the third storey.
uz: U uchinchi qavatga ko'tarilishi kerak edi.

en: “I shall be some time going up,” he thought.
uz: O'zi o'ylaganidek, bir muncha vaqt o'tgach o'sha yerga boraman.

en: He felt as though the fateful moment was still far off, as though he had plenty of time left for consideration.
uz: O'zini o'ziga yaqin vaqt qolganidek his qildi, o'ziga ko'p vaqt qolganidek.

en: Again the same rubbish, the same eggshells lying about on the spiral stairs, again the open doors of the flats, again the same kitchens and the same fumes and stench coming from them.
uz: Yana bir bor xuddi shunday chiqindilar, spiral qadamlar ustida yotgan xuddi shunday tuxumlar, yana bir bor xonadonlarning ochiq eshiklari, yana bir bor xuddi shunday oshxonalar va ulardan xuddi shunday tutun va issiq tutun kelib chiqadi.

en: Raskolnikov had not been here since that day.
uz: Raskolnikov o'sha kundan beri bu yerda bo'lmagan edi.

en: His legs were numb and gave way under him, but still they moved forward.
uz: Uning oyoqlari o'zboshimchalik bilan bo'lib, uning ostida qolib ketadi, ammo ular hali ham oldinga harakatlanmoqda.

en: He stopped for a moment to take breath, to collect himself, so as to enter like a man.
uz: U nafas olish uchun bir zum to'xtadi, o'zini yig'di va odam kabi kirdi.

en: what for?” he wondered, reflecting.
uz: Nima uchun? deb o'yladi u, fikr yuritib.

en: “If I must drink the cup what difference does it make?
uz: Agar men kosa ichishim kerak bo'lsa, bu qanday ahamiyatga ega?

en: The more revolting the better.” He imagined for an instant the figure of the “explosive lieutenant,” Ilya Petrovitch.
uz: Qanchalik ko'p bo'lsa, shunchalik yaxshi. U bir daqiqa uchun portlovchi leytenant Ilya Petrovitchning shaxsiyatini tasavvur qildi.

en: Was he actually going to him?
uz: U haqiqatan ham uning oldiga borganmi?

en: Couldn’t he go to someone else?
uz: U boshqa odamga borishi mumkin emasmi?

en: Couldn’t he turn back and go straight to Nikodim Fomitch’s lodgings?
uz: U o'zini o'zgartirib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Nikodim Fomitchning uylariga borishi mumkin emasmi?

en: At least then it would be done privately.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda, bu xususiy ravishda amalga oshiriladi.

en: To the “explosive lieutenant”!
uz: Ploshlantiruvchi leytenentga!!

en: If he must drink it, drink it off at once.
uz: Agar ichishi kerak bo'lsa, uni darhol iching.

en: Turning cold and hardly conscious, he opened the door of the office.
uz: Soyuqlanib, o'zini o'ylamagan holda, u ofis eshikini ochdi.

en: There were very few people in it this time —only a house porter and a peasant.
uz: Bu safar u yerda juda oz odam bor edi, faqat uy egasi va dehqonlar bor edi.

en: The doorkeeper did not even peep out from behind his screen.
uz: Eshikboshi hatto ekrani orqasidan ko'z ochmadi.

en: Raskolnikov walked into the next room.
uz: Raskolnikov yonma-yon xonaga kirdi.

en: “Perhaps I still need not speak,” passed through his mind.
uz: Ehtimol, men hali ham gapirishim kerak emas, bu uning ongidan o'tdi.

en: Some sort of clerk not wearing a uniform was settling himself at a bureau to write.
uz: Unifomi bo'lmagan bir xil ishchi yozish uchun ofisga joylashib olgan edi.

en: In a corner another clerk was seating himself.
uz: Bir burchada boshqa bir xizmatkor o'zini o'tirgan edi.

en: Zametov was not there, nor, of course, Nikodim Fomitch.
uz: Zametov va, albatta, Nikodim Fomitch u yerda bo'lmagan.

en: “No one in?” Raskolnikov asked, addressing the person at the bureau.
uz: Hech kim kirmagan? Raskolnikov ofisdagi kishiga murojaat qilib so'radi.

en: Not a sound was heard, not a sight was seen, but I scent the Russian … how does it go on in the fairy tale … I’ve forgotten!
uz: Hech qanday tovush eshitilmadi, ko'rinish ham ko'rilmadi, lekin men rusning hidini his qildim ... hikoyada nima sodir bo'ladi ... Men unutib qo'ydim!

en: ‘At your service!’ ” a familiar voice cried suddenly.
uz: Sizning xizmatingizda! O'zingiz bilgan bir ovoz to'satdan qichqirdi.

en: Raskolnikov shuddered.
uz: Raskolnikov dahshatga tushdi.

en: The Explosive Lieutenant stood before him.
uz: Uning oldida Explosiv leytenant turgan edi.

en: He had just come in from the third room.
uz: U uchinchi xonadan kelgan edi.

en: “It is the hand of fate,” thought Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu taqdir qo'li, Raskolnikov o'yladi.

en: “Why is he here?” “You’ve come to see us?
uz: Nima uchun u bu yerda? Siz bizni ko'rish uchun keldingizmi?

en: What about?” cried Ilya Petrovitch.
uz: Nima haqida? Ilya Petrovitch yig'ladi.

en: He was obviously in an exceedingly good humour and perhaps a trifle exhilarated.
uz: U juda yaxshi humorda va ehtimol biroz hayajonlangan edi.

en: “If it’s on business you are rather early.൤ It’s only a chance that I am here … however I’ll do what I can.
uz: Agar bu ish bo'lsa, siz juda erta. Agar men bu yerda bo'lishim mumkin bo'lsa... lekin men qo'limdan kelganicha harakat qilaman.

en: I must admit, I … what is it, what is it?
uz: Shuni tan olishim kerakki, men ... nima, nima?

en: …” “Raskolnikov.” “Of course, Raskolnikov.
uz: ... Raskolnikov.  Albatta, Raskolnikov.

en: You didn’t imagine I’d forgotten?
uz: Men unutilganimni tasavvur qilmadingmi?

en: Don’t think I am like that … Rodion Ro —Ro —Rodionovitch, that’s it, isn’t it?” “Rodion Romanovitch.” “Yes, yes, of course, Rodion Romanovitch!
uz: O'zimni shunday deb o'ylamang ... Rodion Ro Ro Ro Rodionovitch, shunday emasmi?

en: I was just getting at it.
uz: Men o'zimni o'zimga bag'ishladim.

en: I made many inquiries about you.
uz: Men siz haqingizda ko'p so'rovlar qildim.

en: I assure you I’ve been genuinely grieved since that … since I behaved like that … it was explained to me afterwards that you were a literary man … and a learned one too  … and so to say the first steps … Mercy on us!
uz: Sizga shuni ta'kidlaymanki, o'sha paytdan beri ... men shunday harakat qilganimdan ... keyinchalik menga siz adabiy odam ekanligingiz va o'qigan odam ekanligingiz tushuntirilgan edi ... va birinchi qadamlar deb aytish uchun ... bizga rahm qilgin!

en: What literary or scientific man does not begin by some originality of conduct!
uz: Qaysi adabiy yoki ilmiy odam xulq-atvorining biroz originalligi bilan boshlanmaydi!

en: My wife and I have the greatest respect for literature, in my wife it’s a genuine passion!
uz: Xotinim va men adabiyotga katta hurmat ko'rsatamiz, xotinimda bu haqiqiy ishtiyoqdir!

en: If only a man is a gentleman, all the rest can be gained by talents, learning, good sense, genius.
uz: Agar erkak kishi faqatgina xudojo'y bo'lsa, qolgan hamma narsa iqtidor, o'rganish, aql-idrok, aql-idrok bilan erishilishi mumkin.

en: As for a hat —well, what does a hat matter?
uz: G'azabga kelsak, g'azab nimaga bog'liq?

en: I can buy a hat as easily as I can a bun; but what’s under the hat, what the hat covers, I can’t buy that!
uz: Men to'pka kabi osonlikcha sovut sotib olsam bo'ladi; lekin to'pka ostida nima bor, to'pka nimani qamrab oladi, men buni sotib ololmayman!

en: I was even meaning to come and apologise to you, but thought maybe you’d … But I am forgetting to ask you, is there anything you want really?
uz: Hatto kechirim so'rashni ham xohlardim, lekin siz ham shunday qilishingiz mumkin deb o'yladim... Ammo sizdan so'rashni unutib qo'yyapman, siz haqiqatan ham biror narsani xohlaysizmi?

en: I hear your family have come?” “Yes, my mother and sister.” “I’ve even had the honour and happiness of meeting your sister —a highly cultivated and charming person.
uz: Oilangiz kelganini eshitganmanmi?Ha, onam va singlim.Xotin-singilingiz bilan uchrashish sharafi va quvonchidan bahramand bo'ldim.Yengilab, chiroyli inson.

en: I confess I was sorry I got so hot with you.
uz: Siz bilan shunchalik qizg'in bo'lganimdan afsuslanganimni tan oldim.

en: But as for my looking suspiciously at your fainting fit —that affair has been cleared up splendidly!
uz: Ammo sizning baytilishingizga shubha bilan qaraganimda, bu holat ajoyib tarzda hal qilindi!

en: Bigotry and fanaticism!
uz: Bigotriya va fanatizm!

en: I understand your indignation.
uz: Men sizning g'azabingizni tushunaman.

en: Perhaps you are changing your lodging on account of your family’s arriving?”
uz: Ehtimol, oila a'zolaringiz kelishi sababli uyingizni o'zgartirasiz?

en: “No, I only looked in … I came to ask … I thought that I should find Zametov here.” “Oh, yes!
uz: Yo'q, men faqat o'zimni ko'rdim... so'rash uchun keldim... Zametovni bu yerda topishim kerak, deb o'yladim. Oh, ha!

en: Of course, you’ve made friends, I heard.
uz: Albatta, siz do'stlar orttirdingiz, deb eshitdim.

en: Well, no, Zametov is not here.
uz: Yo'q, Zametov bu yerda yo'q.

en: Yes, we’ve lost Zametov.
uz: Ha, biz Zametovni yo'qotdik.

en: He’s not been here since yesterday … he quarrelled with everyone on leaving … in the rudest way.
uz: U kechadan buyon bu yerda emas edi ... u hamma bilan ketish haqida bahslashdi ... eng shafqatsiz tarzda.

en: He is a feather-headed youngster, that’s all; one might have expected something from him, but there, you know what they are, our brilliant young men.
uz: U to'qima boshli yigit, shu qadar; undan biror narsa kutish mumkin edi, lekin u erda, bilasiz, ular nima, bizning ajoyib yigitlarimiz.

en: He wanted to go in for some examination, but it’s only to talk and boast about it, it will go no further than that.
uz: U muayyan imtihon o'tkazish uchun kirmoqchi edi, lekin bu faqat gapirish va maqtanish uchun, bu bundan tashqari ketmaydi.

en: Of course it’s a very different matter with you or Mr.
uz: Albatta, siz yoki Mr.

en: Razumihin there, your friend.
uz: Razumihin u erda, sizning do'stingiz.

en: Your career is an intellectual one and you won’t be deterred by failure.
uz: Sizning karyerangiz intellektual va muvaffaqiyatsizlik sizni chalg'itmaydi.

en: For you, one may say, all the attractions of life nihil est —you are an ascetic, a monk, a hermit!
uz: Siz uchun, deyish mumkin, hayotning barcha diqqatga sazovor joyi yo'q, chunki siz asket, rafiq, erimsiz!

en: … A book, a pen behind your ear, a learned research —that’s where your spirit soars!
uz: Kitob, qanoq quloq orqasida, o'rganilgan tadqiqotlar, ruhingiz o'sib boradigan joy!

en: I am the same way myself.
uz: O'zim ham xuddi shunday.

en: … Have you read Livingstone’s Travels?” “No.” “Oh, I have.
uz: ...Livingstonning sayohatlarini o'qiganmisiz?Yo'q.Oh, men o'qiganman.

en: There are a great many Nihilists about nowadays, you know, and indeed it is not to be wondered at.
uz: Bugungi kunda juda ko'p nihilistlar bor va bu juda ajablanarli emas.

en: What sort of days are they?
uz: Bu qanday kunlar?

en: But we thought … you are not a Nihilist of course?
uz: Ammo biz o'yladikki... siz, albatta, nihilist emassiz?

en: Answer me openly, openly!” “N-no …” “Believe me, you can speak openly to me as you would to yourself!
uz: Menga ochiqchasiga javob bering! N-yo'q ...  Menga ishoning, o'zingiz bilan gapirganingizdek menga ochiqchasiga gapirishingiz mumkin!

en: Official duty is one thing but … you are thinking I meant to say friendship is quite another?
uz: Rasmiy vazifa bir narsa, lekin... siz mening do'stlik to'g'ri boshqa narsa deb aytmoqchi ekanligimni o'ylaysizmi?

en: It’s not friendship, but the feeling of a man and a citizen, the feeling of humanity and of love for the Almighty.
uz: Bu do'stlik emas, balki inson va fuqarolik hissi, insoniylik va Qodir Tangriga bo'lgan sevgi hissi.

en: I may be an official, but I am always bound to feel myself a man and a citizen.
uz: Men rasmiy bo'lishim mumkin, lekin men o'zimni har doim erkak va fuqaro sifatida his qilishim kerak.

en: … You were asking about Zametov.
uz: Siz Zametov haqida so'ragan edingiz.

en: Zametov will make a scandal in the French style in a house of bad reputation, over a glass of champagne … that’s all your Zametov is good for!
uz: Zametov frantsuz uslubida, yomon nomga ega uyda, shampanj ko'rinishi uchun shovqin qiladi ... bu sizning Zametovingiz uchun yaxshi narsa!

en: While I’m perhaps, so to speak, burning with devotion and lofty feelings, and besides I have rank, consequence, a post!
uz: Ehtimol, men, shunday deyish uchun, sadoqat va yuksak his-tuyg'ular bilan yonayotgan bo'lsam-da, shuningdek, daraja, ahamiyat va lavozimga ega bo'laman!

en: I am married and have children, I fulfil the duties of a man and a citizen, but who is he, may I ask?
uz: Men turmush qurganman va bolalarim bor, erkak va fuqarolik vazifasini bajaraman, lekin u kim, deb so'rasam bo'ladi?

en: I appeal to you as a man ennobled by education … Then these midwives, too, have become extraordinarily numerous.”
uz: Men sizga ta'lim bilan ulug'langan odam sifatida murojaat qilaman ... Keyin bu hamrahmonlar juda ko'p bo'ldi.

en: Raskolnikov raised his eyebrows inquiringly.
uz: Raskolnikov ko'z burchaklarini savol-javob bilan ko'tardi.

en: The words of Ilya Petrovitch, who had obviously been dining, were for the most part a stream of empty sounds for him.
uz: Ilya Petrovitchning ovqatlanayotgan so'zlari uning uchun ko'pincha bo'sh tovushlar oqimi edi.

en: But some of them he understood.
uz: Ammo ba'zilarini u tushunardi.

en: He looked at him inquiringly, not knowing how it would end.
uz: U unga savol-javob bilan qaradi va uning qanday yakun topishini bilmaydi.

en: “I mean those crop-headed wenches,” the talkative Ilya Petrovitch continued.
uz: Men o'sha o'simlik boshli qizlarni nazarda tutyapman, deb davom ettirdi gapiruvchi Ilya Petrovitch.

en: “Midwives is my name for them.
uz: Midwives - bu mening ularga ismim.

en: I think it a very satisfactory one, ha-ha!
uz: Men buni juda qoniqarli deb o'ylayman, ha-ha!

en: They go to the Academy, study anatomy.
uz: Ular akademiyaga borishadi, anatomiyani o'rganishadi.

en: If I fall ill, am I to send for a young lady to treat me?
uz: Agar kasal bo'lsam, meni davolash uchun yosh xonimni chaqirishim kerakmi?

en: Ha-ha!” Ilya Petrovitch laughed, quite pleased with his own wit.
uz: Ha-ha! Ilya Petrovitch o'z aql-idrokidan juda mamnun bo'lib, kuldi.

en: “It’s an immoderate zeal for education, but once you’re educated, that’s enough.
uz: Bu ta'limga bo'lgan o'rtacha g'ayratdir, lekin bir bor ta'lim olganingizdan so'ng, bu yetarli.

en: Why insult honourable people, as that scoundrel Zametov does?
uz: Nima uchun Zametov kabi hurmatli odamlarni haqoratlash kerak?

en: Why did he insult me, I ask you?
uz: Nima uchun u meni haqorat qildi, deb so'rasam bo'ladi?

en: Look at these suicides, too, how common they are, you can’t fancy!
uz: Bu o'z joniga qasd qilganlarning ham o'zlariga nazar soling, ular qanchalik keng tarqalganini tasavvur qiling!

en: People spend their last halfpenny and kill themselves, boys and girls and old people.
uz: Odamlar o'zlarining so'nggi yarim tangalarini sarflab, o'zlarini o'ldiradilar, o'g'il-qizlar va keksalar.

en: Only this morning we heard about a gentleman who had just come to town.
uz: Faqat bugun ertalab shaharga yangi kelgan bir gentleman haqida eshitdik.

en: Nil Pavlitch, I say, what was the name of that gentleman who shot himself?” “Svidrigaïlov,” someone answered from the other room with drowsy listlessness.
uz: Nil Pavlitch, o'zini o'zi o'qigan odamning ismi qanday edi?Svidrigaïlov, kimdir boshqa xonada uxlab, ochko'zlik bilan javob berdi.

en: Raskolnikov started.
uz: Raskolnikov boshladi.

en: Svidrigaïlov has shot himself!” he cried.
uz: Svidrigailov o'zini o'zi o'ldirgan! deb baqirdi.

en: “What, do you know Svidrigaïlov?” “Yes … I knew him.
uz: Siz Svidrigailovni bilasizmi?Ha, men uni bilardim.

en: … He hadn’t been here long.” “Yes, that’s so.
uz: ...U uzoq vaqt bu yerda bo'lmagan.Ha, shunday.

en: He had lost his wife, was a man of reckless habits and all of a sudden shot himself, and in such a shocking way.
uz: U xotini yo'qotib, beparvolik odatlari bilan shug'ullanayotgan kishi edi va to'satdan o'z-o'zini o'ldirgan edi.

en: … He left in his notebook a few words: that he dies in full possession of his faculties and that no one is to blame for his death.
uz: ... U o'z yozuvchisiga bir necha so'z qoldirdi: u o'z qobiliyatiga ega bo'lgan holda o'lib ketishi va o'limida hech kim aybdor emasligi haqida.

en: He had money, they say.
uz: Uning pullari bor, deyishadi.

en: How did you come to know him?” “I … was acquainted … my sister was governess in his family.” “Bah-bah-bah!
uz: U bilan qanday tanishib oldingiz?  Men ... tanish edim ... singlim uning oilasi bo'ylab o'qituvchi bo'lgan.  Bah-bah-bah!

en: Then no doubt you can tell us something about him.
uz: Shuni aytish joizki, u holda siz bizga u haqida biror narsa aytib bera olasiz.

en: You had no suspicion?” “I saw him yesterday … he … was drinking wine; I knew nothing.” Raskolnikov felt as though something had fallen on him and was stifling him.
uz: Sizda hech qanday shubha yo'qmidi? Men uni kecha ko'rdim ... u ... sharob ichayotgan edi; men hech narsa bilmasdim. Raskolnikov o'ziga biror narsa tushib, uni o'ldirganini his qildi.

en: “You’ve turned pale again.
uz: Youve yana o'g'irlashdi.

en: It’s so stuffy here …” “Yes, I must go,” muttered Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu erda juda to'liq ...Ha, men borishim kerak, - dedi Raskolnikov.

en: “Excuse my troubling you.
uz: Sizni xafa qilganimdan uzr so'raysiz.

en: “Oh, not at all, as often as you like.
uz: Oh, umuman emas, xohlaganingizcha tez-tez.

en: It’s a pleasure to see you and I am glad to say so.” Ilya Petrovitch held out his hand.
uz: Sizni ko'rish juda xursand va men buni aytishdan xursandman. Ilya Petrovitch qo'lini uzatdi.

en: “I only wanted … I came to see Zametov.” “I understand, I understand, and it’s a pleasure to see you.” “I … am very glad … goodbye,” Raskolnikov smiled.
uz: I only wanted ... I came to see Zametov. I understand, I understand, and it's a pleasure to see you.  I ... I am very glad ... bye, Raskolnikov smiled.

en: He went out; he reeled, he was overtaken with giddiness and did not know what he was doing.
uz: U tashqariga chiqdi; u o'z-o'zidan g'alati bo'lib, o'zini ko'rmay qolgan va nima qilayotganini bilmagan.

en: He began going down the stairs, supporting himself with his right hand against the wall.
uz: U o'ng qo'li bilan devorga qo'yib, o'zini qo'llab-quvvatlab, daraxtdan tushishni boshladi.

en: He fancied that a porter pushed past him on his way upstairs to the police office, that a dog in the lower storey kept up a shrill barking and that a woman flung a rolling-pin at it and shouted.
uz: U politsiyaga borayotganda portiyer o'tkazib yuborilganini, pastki qavatdagi it qo'rqqanini va ayol o'ziga o'g'irlab o'tirganini va qichqirishini tasavvur qildi.

en: He went down and out into the yard.
uz: U pastga tushib, hovliga chiqdi.

en: There, not far from the entrance, stood Sonia, pale and horror-stricken.
uz: U yerda, kirishdan uzoq emas, Sonia soyalib, dahshatga tushdi.

en: She looked wildly at him.
uz: U unga vahima bilan qaradi.

en: He stood still before her.
uz: U ayolning oldida toʻxtamay turibdi.

en: There was a look of poignant agony, of despair, in her face.
uz: Uning yuziga og'ir azob, umidsizlik ko'rindi.

en: She clasped her hands.
uz: U qo'llarini qo'shdi.

en: His lips worked in an ugly, meaningless smile.
uz: Uning og'izlari achchiq, ma'nosiz tabassum bilan ishlaydi.

en: He stood still a minute, grinned and went back to the police office.
uz: U bir daqiqa turdi, tabassum qildi va politsiyaga qaytib ketdi.

en: Ilya Petrovitch had sat down and was rummaging among some papers.
uz: Ilya Petrovitch o'tirib, ba'zi qog'ozlar o'rtasida o'tirgan edi.

en: Before him stood the same peasant who had pushed by on the stairs.
uz: Uning oldiga o'sha qishloq xo'jaligi o'tgan edi.

en: have you left something behind?
uz: Orqada biron narsa qoldirdingizmi?

en: What’s the matter?” Raskolnikov, with white lips and staring eyes, came slowly nearer.
uz: Raskolnikov oq og'izlar va ko'zlar bilan sekin-sakin yaqinlashdi.

en: He walked right to the table, leaned his hand on it, tried to say something, but could not; only incoherent sounds were audible.
uz: U to'g'ridan-to'g'ri stolga yaqinlashdi, qo'lini ushlab, biror narsa aytishga harakat qildi, lekin qila olmadi; faqat noto'g'ri tovushlar eshitildi.

en: “You are feeling ill, a chair!
uz: Siz o'zingizni kasal his qilyapsiz, o'rindiq!

en: Some water!” Raskolnikov dropped on to a chair, but he kept his eyes fixed on the face of Ilya Petrovitch, which expressed unpleasant surprise.
uz: Raskolnikov o'rindiqga tushdi, lekin ko'zlarini Ilya Petrovitchning yuziga qaratdi.

en: Both looked at one another for a minute and waited.
uz: Ikkalasi ham bir daqiqa bir-birlariga qarab, kutishdi.

en: “It was I …” began Raskolnikov.
uz: Bu men ... Raskolnikovni boshladi.

en: “Drink some water.” Raskolnikov refused the water with his hand, and softly and brokenly, but distinctly said: “It was I killed the old pawnbroker woman and her sister Lizaveta with an axe and robbed them.” Ilya Petrovitch opened his mouth.
uz: Ba'zi suv iching. Raskolnikov qo'li bilan suvdan voz kechdi va yumshatgancha, lekin aniqlik bilan shunday dedi: Bu men keksa qarzdor ayolni va uning singlisi Lizavetani balt bilan o'ldirganman va o'g'irlaganman. Ilya Petrovitch og'zini ochdi.

en: People ran up on all sides.
uz: Har tarafdan odamlar yig'ilib borishdi.

en: Raskolnikov repeated his statement.
uz: Raskolnikov o'z so'zlarini takrorladi.

en: On the banks of a broad solitary river stands a town, one of the administrative centres of Russia; in the town there is a fortress, in the fortress there is a prison.
uz: O'ziga xos keng daryo qirg'og'ida Rossiyaning ma'muriy markazlaridan biri bo'lgan shahar turibdi; shaharda qal'a, qal'ada qamoqxona bor.

en: In the prison the second-class convict Rodion Raskolnikov has been confined for nine months.
uz: Zindonlikda ikkinchi darajali mahkum Rodion Raskolnikov to'qqiz oy davomida qamoqda o'tirgan.

en: Almost a year and a half has passed since his crime.
uz: Uning jinoyatidan deyarli bir yarim yil o'tdi.

en: There had been little difficulty about his trial.
uz: Uning sudlanishi bilan bog'liq muammolar kam edi.

en: The criminal adhered exactly, firmly, and clearly to his statement.
uz: Jinoyatchi aniq, qat'iy va aniq ravishda o'z so'zlariga amal qildi.

en: He did not confuse nor misrepresent the facts, nor soften them in his own interest, nor omit the smallest detail.
uz: U faktlarni chalg'itmagan, noto'g'ri tasvirlamagan, o'z manfaatini ko'zlab ularni yumshatmagan, hatto kichik tafsilotlarni ham qoldirmagan.

en: He explained every incident of the murder, the secret of the pledge (the piece of wood with a strip of metal) which was found in the murdered woman’s hand.
uz: U o'ldirilgan ayolning qo'lida topilgan garovning (metall tarmog'i bo'lgan yog'ochning) sirini tushuntirdi.

en: He described minutely how he had taken her keys, what they were like, as well as the chest and its contents; he explained the mystery of Lizaveta’s murder; described how Koch and, after him, the student knocked, and repeated all they had said to one another; how he afterwards had run downstairs and heard Nikolay and Dmitri shouting; how he had hidden in the empty flat and afterwards gone home.
uz: U uning kalitlarini qanday olganini, ular qanday bo'lganini, shuningdek, ko'krak va uning tarkibini batafsil tasvirlagan; Lizaveta o'ldirilishi sirini tushuntirib bergan; Koch va uning ortidan o'quvchi qanday taqillatib, bir-biriga aytganlarini takrorlaganini batafsil tasvirlagan; keyinchalik qanday qilib pastga yugurganini va Nikolay va Dmitrining qichqiriqlarini eshitganini; qanday qilib u bo'sh xonadonda yashirinib, keyin uyga ketganini tushuntirib bergan.

en: He ended by indicating the stone in the yard off the Voznesensky Prospect under which the purse and the trinkets were found.
uz: U Voznesenskiy prospekti yonidagi hovlidagi toshni ko'rsatdi va uning ostida sumka va arzonlik topildi.

en: The whole thing, in fact, was perfectly clear.
uz: Darhaqiqat, hamma narsa to'liq aniq edi.

en: The lawyers and the judges were very much struck, among other things, by the fact that he had hidden the trinkets and the purse under a stone, without making use of them,
uz: Advokatlar va hakamlar, shu jumladan, u buyumlar va qopchani tosh ostida yashirib qo'yganidan juda hayratda qolishdi, lekin ulardan foydalangan emas.

en: and that, what was more, he did not now remember what the trinkets were like, or even how many there were.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u endi bu asboblarning qanday bo'lishini yoki hatto qanchaligini eslay olmagan.

en: The fact that he had never opened the purse and did not even know how much was in it seemed incredible.
uz: Uning hech qachon qopchani ochmaganligi va uning ichida qancha pul borligini bilmaganligi ajoyib tuyulgan.

en: There turned out to be in the purse three hundred and seventeen roubles and sixty kopecks.
uz: O'shanda sumkada uch yuz o'n yettita rubl va oltmish kopek bor edi.

en: From being so long under the stone, some of the most valuable notes lying uppermost had suffered from the damp.
uz: Tosh ostida shuncha vaqt bo'lganidan, eng qimmatbaho notalarning ba'zilari yuqoriga tushib, namlikdan azob chekishdi.

en: They were a long while trying to discover why the accused man should tell a lie about this, when about everything else he had made a truthful and straightforward confession.
uz: Ular nega ayblovchining bu haqda yolg'on gapirishini aniqlashga harakat qilishdi, chunki u boshqa hamma narsa haqida rostgo'y va bevosita tan olgan edi.

en: Finally some of the lawyers more versed in psychology admitted that it was possible he had really not looked into the purse, and so didn’t know what was in it when he hid it under the stone.
uz: Nihoyat, psixologiyadan ko'proq bilimga ega bo'lgan ba'zi advokatlar u sumkani ko'rmagan bo'lishi mumkinligini tan olishdi, shuning uchun uni tosh ostida yashirganida uning ichida nima borligini bilmasdi.

en: But they immediately drew the deduction that the crime could only have been committed through temporary mental derangement, through homicidal mania, without object or the pursuit of gain.
uz: Ammo ular darhol jinoyatni faqat vaqtincha aqliy xafagarchilik, qotillik mansiyasi orqali, maqsadsiz yoki foyda orzu qilmasdan sodir etish mumkinligi haqida xulosa chiqarishdi.

en: This fell in with the most recent fashionable theory of temporary insanity, so often applied in our days in criminal cases.
uz: Bu, bizning kunlarimizda jinoiy ishlarda tez-tez qo'llaniladigan vaqtinchalik aqlsizlikning eng so'nggi zamonaviy nazariyasiga uyg'un bo'ldi.

en: Moreover Raskolnikov’s hypochondriacal condition was proved by many witnesses, by Dr.
uz: Bundan tashqari, Raskolnikovning ipokondriyalik holati ko'plab guvohlar tomonidan isbotlandi.

en: Zossimov, his former fellow students, his landlady and her servant.
uz: Zossimov, uning sobiq o'quvchi hamkasblari, uy egasi va uning xizmatkori.

en: All this pointed strongly to the conclusion that Raskolnikov was not quite like an ordinary murderer and robber, but that there was another element in the case.
uz: Bularning barchasi Raskolnikovning oddiy qotil va talonchiga o'xshamasligini, balki bu ishda boshqa bir element borligini ta'kidlagan.

en: To the intense annoyance of those who maintained this opinion, the criminal scarcely attempted to defend himself.
uz: Bunday fikrda bo'lganlarning qattiq xafa bo'lishiga ko'ra, jinoyatchi o'zini himoya qilishga oz harakat qildi.

en: To the decisive question as to what motive impelled him to the murder and the robbery, he answered very clearly with the coarsest frankness that the cause was his miserable position, his poverty and helplessness, and his desire to provide for his first steps in life by the help of the three thousand roubles he had reckoned on finding.
uz: O'lim va talon-torojga nima sabab bo'lganligi to'g'risidagi hal qiluvchi savolga u aniq javob berdi va aniqlik bilan aytdiki, buning sababi uning ayanchli holati, qashshoqligi va yordamsizlik va hayotining birinchi qadamlarini o'z uch ming rubl yordamida ta'minlash istagi edi.

en: He had been led to the murder through his shallow and cowardly nature, exasperated moreover by privation and failure.
uz: U o'zining past va qo'rqinchli tabiati tufayli o'ldirilgan, bundan tashqari, kamchilik va muvaffaqiyatsizliklar uni g'azablantirgan edi.

en: To the question what led him to confess, he answered that it was his heartfelt repentance.
uz: Uni tan olish uchun nima sabab bo'lganini so'raganida, u o'zining chin dildan tavba qilganligi haqida javob berdi.

en: All this was almost coarse.
uz: Bularning barchasi deyarli qo'pol edi.

en: … The sentence however was more merciful than could have been expected, perhaps partly because the criminal had not tried to justify himself, but had rather shown a desire to exaggerate his guilt.
uz: ... Biroq, jazosi kutilganidan ko'ra rahmdilroq bo'ldi, ehtimol qisman jinoyatchi o'zini oqlashga urinmaganligi, aksincha, o'zining aybdorligini haddan tashqari ko'rsatmoqchi bo'lganligi sababli.

en: All the strange and peculiar circumstances of the crime were taken into
uz: Jinoyatning barcha g'alati va o'ziga xos holatlari hisobga olingan.

en: There could be no doubt of the abnormal and poverty- stricken condition of the criminal at the time.
uz: O'sha paytda jinoyatchining g'alati va kambag'al holatida hech qanday shubha yo'q edi.

en: The fact that he had made no use of what he had stolen was put down partly to the effect of remorse, partly to his abnormal mental condition at the time of the crime.
uz: O'g'irlagan narsadan foydalanmaganligi qisman afsuslanish va jinoyat sodir etilgan paytda uning anormal psixiy ahvolidan kelib chiqqan.

en: Incidentally the murder of Lizaveta served indeed to confirm the last hypothesis: a man commits two murders and forgets that the door is open!
uz: Lizavetaning o'ldirilishi, albatta, so'nggi g'oyalarni tasdiqlaydi: bir kishi ikkita o'ldirishni sodir etadi va eshik ochiq ekanligini unutib qo'yadi!

en: Finally, the confession, at the very moment when the case was hopelessly muddled by the false evidence given by Nikolay through melancholy and fanaticism, and when, moreover, there were no proofs against the real criminal, no suspicions even (Porfiry Petrovitch fully kept his word) —all this did much to soften the sentence.
uz: Va nihoyat, Nikolay tomonidan melanxollik va fanatizm orqali berilgan soxta dalillar bilan ishni umidsizlikka aylantirib qo'yilgan va, bundan tashqari, haqiqiy jinoyatchiga qarshi hech qanday dalillar, hatto shubhalar yo'q (Porfiry Petrovitch so'zini to'liq bajargan) da, tanbehning o'zi ham o'z jazosini yumshatishga katta hissa qo'shdi.

en: Other circumstances, too, in the prisoner’s favour came out quite unexpectedly.
uz: Boshqa holatlar ham mahbusning foydasiga kutilmagan tarzda paydo bo'ldi.

en: Razumihin somehow discovered and proved that while Raskolnikov was at the university he had helped a poor consumptive fellow student and had spent his last penny on supporting him for six months, and when this student died, leaving a decrepit old father whom he had maintained almost from his thirteenth year, Raskolnikov had got the old man into a hospital and paid for his funeral when he died.
uz: Razumihin bir yo'l bilan Raskolnikov universitetda bo'lganida kambag'al iste'molchi o'quvchiga yordam berganini va uni olti oy davomida qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun so'nggi pulini sarflaganini aniqladi va isbotladi va bu o'quvchi vafot etganida, u o'n uchinchi yoshidan beri ta'minlab yurgan eski otasini qoldirib ketganda, Raskolnikov o'sha keksa odamni kasalxonaga joylashtirdi va o'lganida uning dafn xarajatlarini to'ladi.

en: Raskolnikov’s landlady bore witness, too, that when they had lived in another house at Five Corners, Raskolnikov had rescued two little children from a house on fire and was burnt in doing so.
uz: Raskolnikovning uy egasi ham guvohlik berdiki, ular beshta burchakdagi boshqa uyda yashaganida, Raskolnikov olovga to'lgan uydan ikkita kichkina bolani qutqardi va o'sha paytda yondirib yuborildi.

en: This was investigated and fairly well confirmed by many witnesses.
uz: Bu holat ko'plab guvohlar tomonidan aniq ko'rib chiqilgan va tasdiqlangan.

en: These facts made an impression in his favour.
uz: Ushbu faktlar uning foydasiga taassurot qoldirdi.

en: And in the end the criminal was, in consideration of extenuating circumstances, condemned to penal servitude in the second class for a term of eight years only.
uz: Va nihoyat jinoyatchi yengillashtiruvchi holatlarni hisobga olgan holda, faqat sakkiz yil muddatga ikkinchi darajali qullikka hukm qilindi.

en: At the very beginning of the trial Raskolnikov’s mother fell ill.
uz: Raskolnikovning onasi sud jarayonining boshida kasal bo'ldi.

en: Dounia and Razumihin found it possible to get her out of Petersburg during the trial.
uz: Dounia va Razumihin uni sud jarayonida Sankt-Peterburgdan olib chiqishga muvaffaq bo'lishdi.

en: Razumihin chose a town on the railway not far from Petersburg, so as to be able to follow every step of the trial and at the same time to see Avdotya Romanovna as often as possible.
uz: Razumihin Sankt-Peterburgdan uzoq bo'lmagan temir yo'l bo'ylab joylashgan shaharni tanladi, shunda u sud jarayonining har bir bosqichini kuzatib boradi va Avdotya Romanovna bilan imkon qadar tez-tez uchrashadi.

en: Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s illness was a strange nervous one and was accompanied by a partial derangement of her intellect.
uz: Pulcheria Alexandrovnaning kasalligi g'ayrioddiy g'alati kasallik edi va uning intellektining qisman buzilishi bilan birga edi.

en: When Dounia returned from her last interview with her brother, she had found her mother already ill, in feverish delirium.
uz: Dounia ukasi bilan so'nggi intervyudan qaytib kelganida, onasi allaqachon kasal va issiq delirida bo'lganini ko'rdi.

en: That evening Razumihin and she agreed what answers they must make to her
uz: O'sha kechqurun Razumihin bilan ular unga qanday javob berishlari kerakligini kelishdi.

en: mother’s questions about Raskolnikov and made up a complete story for her mother’s benefit of his having to go away to a distant part of Russia on a business commission, which would bring him in the end money and reputation.
uz: Onasi Raskolnikov haqida savollar bergan va onasi uchun butun hikoyani o'ylab topgan, chunki u biznes-komissiya uchun uzoq Rossiyaga ketishi kerak edi, bu esa uni oxirgi pul va obro'ga yetkazadi.

en: But they were struck by the fact that Pulcheria Alexandrovna never asked them anything on the subject, neither then nor thereafter.
uz: Ammo ular Pulcheria Aleksandrovna tomonidan bu mavzuda hech qachon so'ralmaganidan hayratda qolishdi, keyin ham, keyin ham.

en: On the contrary, she had her own version of her son’s sudden departure; she told them with tears how he had come to say goodbye to her, hinting that she alone knew many mysterious and important facts, and that Rodya had many very powerful enemies, so that it was necessary for him to be in hiding.
uz: Aksincha, o'g'lining to'satdan ketishi haqida o'z versiyasi bor edi; u o'g'li qanday qilib unga salom aytgani haqida ko'z yoshlari bilan aytib berdi va Rodyaning ko'pgina sirli va muhim faktlarni bilishini va uning ko'pgina kuchli dushmanlari borligini, shuning uchun u yashirib qolishi kerakligini ko'rsatdi.

en: As for his future career, she had no doubt that it would be brilliant when certain sinister influences could be removed.
uz: Kelajakdagi karyerasiga kelsak, u ba'zi yovuz ta'sirlarni yo'q qilish juda ajoyib bo'lishiga shubha qilmagan.

en: She assured Razumihin that her son would be one day a great statesman, that his article and brilliant literary talent proved it.
uz: U Razumihinning o'g'li bir kun buyuk davlat egasi bo'lishini, uning maqolasi va ajoyib adabiy talanti buni isbotlashini ta'kidladi.

en: This article she was continually reading, she even read it aloud, almost took it to bed with her, but scarcely asked where Rodya was, though the subject was obviously avoided by the others, which might have been enough to awaken her suspicions.
uz: Bu maqolani u doimiy ravishda o'qiyotgan edi, hatto baland ovoz bilan o'qiyotgan edi, deyarli u o'zi bilan yotishga ketadi, lekin Rodya qayerdaligini deyarli so'ramadi, garchi bu mavzu boshqalar tomonidan qochilgan bo'lsa-da, bu uning shubhalarini uyg'otish uchun etarli bo'lishi mumkin.

en: They began to be frightened at last at Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s strange silence on certain subjects.
uz: Ular Pulcheria Aleksandrovnaning muayyan mavzularda g'alati sukutligidan qo'rqishni boshlashdi.

en: She did not, for instance, complain of getting no letters from him, though in previous years she had only lived on the hope of letters from her beloved Rodya.
uz: Misol uchun, u undan hech qanday xat olmaganidan shikoyat qilmagan, garchi o'tgan yillarda u faqat sevimli Rodya xatlaridan umidvor bo'lgan bo'lsa-da.

en: This was the cause of great uneasiness to Dounia; the idea occurred to her that her mother suspected that there was something terrible in her son’s fate and was afraid to ask, for fear of hearing something still more awful.
uz: Bu Duniyaning juda xavotirlanishiga sabab bo'ldi; uning onasi o'g'lining taqdirida dahshatli narsa borligini shubha ostiga qo'ydi va undan ham dahshatliroq narsani eshitish qo'rquvidan so'rashdan qo'rqardi.

en: In any case, Dounia saw clearly that her mother was not in full possession of her faculties.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, Dounia onasi o'z qobiliyatlarini to'liq egallamayotganini aniq ko'rgan.
