en: The suggestion of a melodramatic reversal of that scene, in the same Hall of Mirrors, was overpowering.
uz: O'sha sahnani xuddi Oynalar zalida melodramatik teskari o'zgartirish taklifi juda kuchli edi.

en: Whatever generosities had appeared in the opening phases of the Great War had long been exhausted.
uz: Buyuk urushning dastlabki bosqichlarida paydo bo'lgan saxiyliklar allaqachon tugab ketgan edi.

en: The populations of the victorious countries were acutely aware of their own losses and sufferings, and entirely regard- less of the fact that the defeated had paid in the like manner.
uz: G'alaba qozongan davlatlarning aholisi o'z yo'qotishlari va azoblarini juda yaxshi anglab yetgan edilar, mag'lub bo'lganlarning ham xuddi shunday tarzda to'laganlari haqida umuman e'tibor bermas edilar.

en: The war had arisen as a natural and inevitable consequence of the competitive nation- alisms of Europe and the absence of any Federal adjustment of these com- petitive forces; war is the necessary logical consummation of independent sovereign nationalities living in too small an area with too powerful an ar- mament; and if the great war had not come in the form it did it would have come in some similar form—just as it will certainly return upon a still more disastrous scale in twenty or thirty years’ time if no political uniﬁcation an- ticipates and prevents it.
uz: Urush Yevropaning raqobatbardosh millatlari - alizmalarining tabiiy va muqarrar oqibati sifatida paydo bo'lgan edi va bu raqobatbardosh kuchlarning Federal sozlamalarining yo'qligi; urush juda kichik hududda yashovchi mustaqil suveren millatlarning zarur mantiqiy yakunidir; va agar buyuk urush shunday shaklda kelmaganida, u qandaydir o'xshash shaklda kelardi  xuddi siyosiy birlashuv yo'q bo'lsa, u yigirma yoki o'ttiz yildan keyin yanada halokatli miqyosda qaytishi kabi.

en: States organized for war will make wars as surely as hens will lay eggs, but the feeling of these distressed and war-worn coun- tries disregarded this fact, and the whole of the defeated peoples were treat- ed as morally and materially responsible for all the damage, as they would no doubt have treated the victor peoples had the issue of war been different.
uz: Urush uchun tashkil etilgan davlatlar urushlarni tovuqlar tuxum qo'yganidek aniq qiladilar, lekin bu azob chekkan va urushga botgan mamlakatlarning hissiyotlari bu faktni e'tiborga olmagan va butun mag'lub etilgan xalqlar barcha zarar uchun axloqiy va moddiy jihatdan javobgar deb hisoblangan, chunki ular urush masalasi boshqacha bo'lganda g'olib xalqlarga nisbatan munosabatda bo'lishlari shubhasiz.

en: The French and English thought the Germans were to blame, the Germans thought the Russians, French and English were to blame, and only an intel- ligent minority thought that there was anything to blame in the fragmentary political constitution of Europe.
uz: Fransuzlar va inglizlar nemislarni aybdor deb hisoblashgan, nemislar ruslarni, fransuzlar va inglizlarni aybdor deb hisoblashgan va faqatgina aqlli ozchilik Yevropaning bo'laklangan siyosiy konstitutsiyasida aybdor narsa bor deb o'ylashgan.

en: The treaty of Versailles was intended to be exemplary and vindictive; it provided tremendous penalties for the van- quished; it sought to provide compensations for the wounded and suffering victors by imposing enormous debts upon nations already bankrupt, and its attempts to reconstitute international relations by the establishment of a League of Nations against war were manifestly insincere and inadequate.
uz: Versal shartnomasi namunaviy va qasoskor bo'lishi maqsad qilingan edi; u vayron bo'lganlar uchun ulkan jazolarni ta'minladi; u bankrot bo'lgan davlatlarga ulkan qarzlarni yuklash orqali jarohatlangan va azob chekkan g'oliblarga kompensatsiya berishga intildi va urushga qarshi Millatlar Ligasini tashkil etish orqali xalqaro munosabatlarni tiklashga urinishlari ochiqchasiga samimiy va yetarli emas edi.

en: PASSENGER AEROPLANE FLYING OVER NORTHOLT  (Photo taken by another ’plane by the Central Aerophoto Co.) So far as Europe was concerned it is doubtful if there would have been any attempt whatever to organize international relations for a permanent peace.
uz: YO'LOVCHI AEROPLAN SHIMOL UCHUN UCHARISH (Surat boshqa  Markaziy Aerophoto Co. tomonidan olingan samolyot). Yevropa nuqtai nazaridan, doimiy tinchlik uchun xalqaro munosabatlarni tashkil etishga biron bir urinish bo'lgan bo'lishi dargumon.

en: The proposal of the League of Nations was brought into practical politics by the President of the United States of America, President Wilson.
uz: Millatlar Ligasi taklifi Amerika Qo'shma Shtatlari Prezidenti, Prezident Wilson tomonidan amaliy siyosatga kiritildi.

en: Its chief support was in America.
uz: Uning asosiy tayanchi Amerikada edi.

en: So far the United States, this new modern state, had developed no distinctive ideas of international relationship be- yond the Monroe Doctrine, which protected the new world from European interference.
uz: Hozirgacha Qo'shma Shtatlar, bu yangi zamonaviy davlat, yangi dunyoni Yevropa aralashuvidan himoya qilgan Monro doktrinasi tufayli xalqaro munosabatlarning o'ziga xos g'oyalarini ishlab chiqmagan edi.

en: Now suddenly it was called upon for its mental contribution to the vast problem of the time.
uz: Endi birdaniga u o'sha davrning ulkan muammosiga aqliy hissa qo'shgani uchun chaqirilardi.

en: The natural disposition of the American people was towards a permanent world peace.
uz: Amerika xalqining tabiiy moyilligi doimiy jahon tinchligiga qaratilgan edi.

en: With this however was linked a strong traditional distrust of old-world polities and a habit of isolation from old-world entanglements.
uz: Lekin bu bilan eski dunyo siyosatlariga kuchli an'anaviy ishonchsizlik va eski dunyo chalkashliklaridan ajralish odati bog'langan edi.

en: The Americans had hardly begun to think out an American solution of world problems when the submarine campaign of the Germans dragged them into the war on the side of the anti- German allies.
uz: Amerikaliklar nemislarning suv osti kampaniyasi ularni Germaniyaga qarshi ittifoqchilar tomonida urushga tortganda, jahon muammolariga Amerika yechimini o'ylashni deyarli boshlashmagan edi.

en: President Wilson’s scheme of a League of Nations was an attempt at short notice to create a distinctively American world project.
uz: Prezident Wilsonning Millatlar Ligasi sxemasi qisqa vaqt ichida o'ziga xos Amerikaviy dunyo loyihasini yaratishga urinish edi.

en: was a sketchy, inadequate and dangerous scheme.
uz: bu noaniq, mos kelmaydigan va xavfli sxema edi.

en: In Europe however it was taken as a matured American point of view.
uz: Ammo Yevropada bu yetuk Amerika nuqtai nazari sifatida qabul qilingan.

en: The generality of mankind in 1918-19 was intensely weary of war and anxious at almost any sacriﬁce to erect barriers against its recurrence, but there was not a single government in the old world willing to waive one iota of its sovereign independence to attain any such end.
uz: 1918-19 yillarda insoniyat umuman olganda urushdan juda charchagan va uning takrorlanishiga qarshi to'siqlar o'rnatish uchun deyarli har qanday qurbonlikdan xavotirda edi, ammo eski dunyoda hech qanday hukumat bunday maqsadga erishish uchun o'zining suveren mustaqilligidan birorta ham voz kechishga tayyor emas edi.

en: The public utterances of President Wilson leading up to the project of a World League of Nations seemed for a time to appeal right over the heads of the governments to the peoples of the world; they were taken as expressing the ripe intentions of America, and the response was enormous.
uz: Prezident Wilsonning Jahon Millatlar Ligasi loyihasiga olib borayotgan ommaviy nutqlari bir vaqtlar hukumatlarning boshidan turib dunyo xalqlariga murojaat qilgandek tuyuldi; ular Amerikaning yetuk niyatlarini ifodalash deb qabul qilindi va javob juda katta bo'ldi.

en: Unhappily President Wilson had to deal with governments and not with peoples; he was a man capable of tremendous ﬂashes of vision and yet when put to the test egotistical and limited, and the great wave of enthu- siasm he evoked passed and was wasted.
uz: Afsuski, Prezident Wilson xalqlar bilan emas, balki hukumatlar bilan shug'ullanishga majbur edi; u ulkan ko'rish qobiliyatiga ega odam edi, ammo sinovdan o'tganda xudbin va cheklangan edi va u uyg'otgan katta hayajon to'lqini o'tib ketdi va bekorga ketdi.

en: Dillon in his book, The Peace Conference: “Europe, when the President touched its shores, was as clay ready for the creative potter.
uz: Dillon o'zining Tinchlik Konferensiyasi kitobida shunday dedi: Yevropa, Prezident o'z sohillariga tegganda, ijodiy kulol uchun loy kabi tayyor edi.

en: Never before were the nations so eager to follow a Moses who would take them to the long-promised land where wars are prohibited and blockades unknown.
uz: Hech qachon ilgari xalqlar urushlar taqiqlangan va blokadalar noma'lum bo'lgan uzoq vaqtdan beri va'da qilingan yurtga olib boradigan Musoga shunchalik ishtiyoq bilan ergashmagan edilar.

en: And to their thinking he was just that great leader.
uz: Ularning fikricha, u aynan o'sha buyuk yetakchi edi.

en: In France men bowed down before him with awe and affection.
uz: Fransiyada erkaklar unga hurmat va mehr bilan ta'zim qilishdi.

en: Labour leaders in Paris told me that they shed tears of joy in his presence, and that their comrades would go through ﬁre and water to help him to realize his noble schemes.
uz: Parijdagi ishchilar yetakchilari menga uning huzurida quvonchdan ko'z yoshlari to'kilishini va o'z safdoshlari uning olijanob rejalarini amalga oshirishda yordam berish uchun olov va suvdan o'tishini aytishdi.

en: To the working classes in Italy his name was a heavenly clarion at the sound of which the earth would be renewed.
uz: Italiyadagi ishchi sinflar uchun uning ismi osmoniy chiroq edi, uning ovozi bilan yer yangilanardi.

en: The Germans regarded him and his doc- trine as their sheet-anchor of safety.
uz: Nemislar uni va uning doktor-trine'sini o'zlarining xavfsizlik to'siq-ankori deb hisoblashgan.

en: The fearless Herr Muehlon said: ‘If President Wilson were to address the Germans and pronounce a severe sen- tence upon them, they would accept it with resignation and without a mur- mur and set to work at once.’ In German-Austria his fame was that of a sav- iour, and the mere mention of his name brought balm to the suffering and surcease of sorrow to the afﬂicted ...
uz: Qo'rqmas janob Muehlon aytdi: Agar Prezident Wilson nemislarga murojaat qilib, ularga nisbatan qattiq sanktsiya e'lon qilsa, ular buni iste'foga chiqarib, murmursiz qabul qilishardi va darhol ishga tushishardi. Nemis-Avstriyada uning shuhrati najot haqida edi va uning nomini shunchaki tilga olish azob chekish va azob chekish uchun malham berardi...

en: .” Such were the overpowering expectations that President Wilson raised.
uz: Prezident Wilsonning qo'zg'atgan kuchli umidlari shunday edi.

en: How completely he disappointed them and how weak and futile was the League of Nations he made is too long and too distressful a story to tell here.
uz: U ularni qanchalik butunlay xafa qilganligi va u yaratgan Millatlar Ligasi qanchalik zaif va befoyda ekanligi bu yerda aytib berish uchun juda uzun va qayg'uli hikoya.

en: He exaggerated in his person our common human tragedy, he was so very great in his dreams and so incapable in his performance.
uz: U o'z shaxsiyatida bizning odatiy insoniy fojiamizni mubolag'a qildi, u tushlarida juda buyuk edi va o'z ijrosida juda ojiz edi.

en: America dis- sented from the acts of its President and would not join the League Europe accepted from him.
uz: Amerika o'z Prezidentining harakatlaridan chetlatildi va undan qabul qilingan Yevropa Ligasiga qo'shilmadi.

en: There was a slow realization on the part of the Ameri-
uz: Amerika tomonidan sekin anglash bo'ldi...

en: can people that it had been rushed into something for which it was totally unprepared.
uz: Odamlar shoshilinch ravishda tayyor bo'lmagan narsaga shoshilgani mumkinmi?

en: There was a corresponding realization on the part of Europe that America had nothing ready to give to the old world in its extremity.
uz: Yevropa tomonidan Amerika o'z chegarasida eski dunyoga berishga tayyor emasligi haqida tegishli tushuncha mavjud edi.

en: Born prematurely and crippled at its birth, that League has become indeed, with its elaborate and unpractical constitution and its manifest limitations of power, a serious obstacle in the way of any effective reorganization of in- ternational relationships.
uz: Tug'ilishidan oldin tug'ilgan va nogiron bo'lgan o'sha Liga, o'zining murakkab va amaliy bo'lmagan konstitutsiyasi va hokimiyatning ochiq cheklanganligi bilan xalqaro munosabatlarni samarali qayta tashkil etish yo'lida jiddiy to'siqga aylandi.

en: The problem would be a clearer one if the League did not yet exist.
uz: Agar Liga hali mavjud bo'lmaganida, muammo yanada aniqroq bo'lar edi.

en: Yet that world-wide blaze of enthusiasm that ﬁrst wel- comed the project, that readiness of men everywhere round and about the earth, of men, that is, as distinguished from governments, for a world con- trol of war, is a thing to be recorded with emphasis in any history.
uz: Lekin loyihani birinchi bo'lib qabul qilgan butun dunyo bo'ylab ishtiyoq alangasi, odamlarning har yerda va yer yuzida, odamlarning, ya'ni hukumatlardan farqli o'laroq, jahon urushi trolisiga tayyorligi har qanday tarixda alohida qayd etilishi kerak bo'lgan narsadir.

en: Behind the short-sighted governments that divide and mismanage human affairs, a real force for world unity and world order exists and grows.
uz: Inson ishlarini bo'lib-bo'lib, noto'g'ri boshqaradigan kalta qarashli hukumatlarning ortida jahon birligi va jahon tartibi uchun haqiqiy kuch mavjud va o'sib boradi.

en: From 1918 onward the world entered upon an age of conferences.
uz: 1918 yildan boshlab dunyo konferensiyalar davriga kirdi.

en: Of these the Conference at Washington called by President Harding (1921) has been the most successful and suggestive.
uz: Ulardan Vashingtondagi Prezident Harding tomonidan chaqirilgan Konferensiya (1921) eng muvaffaqiyatli va ijobiy bo'ldi.

en: Notable, too, is the Genoa Confer- ence (1922) for the appearance of German and Russian delegates at its de- liberations.
uz: Shuni ham ta'kidlash joizki, Genua Konferensiyasi (1922) nemis va rus delegatlarining ozodlikdan mahrum qilish jarayonida ishtirok etishi bilan ajralib turadi.

en: We will not discuss this long procession of conferences and ten- tatives in any detail.
uz: Biz bu uzoq konferensiyalar va o'n kishilik jarayonni hech qanday tafsilot bilan muhokama qilmaymiz.

en: It becomes more and more clearly manifest that a huge work of reconstruction has to be done by mankind if a crescendo of such convulsions and world massacres as that of the great war is to be averted.
uz: Agar buyuk urush kabi shovqinlar va jahon qirg'inlarining kuchayishini oldini olish uchun insoniyat tomonidan ulkan rekonstruksiya ishlari amalga oshirilishi kerakligi tobora yaqqolroq namoyon bo'lmoqda.

en: No such hasty improvisation as the League of Nations, no patched-up sys- tem of Conferences between this group of states and that, which change nothing with an air of settling everything, will meet the complex political needs of the new age that lies before us.
uz: Millatlar Ligasi kabi shoshilinch improvizatsiya yo'q, bu davlatlar guruhi bilan hamma narsani hal qilish havosi bilan hech narsani o'zgartirmaydigan, oldimizda turgan yangi davrning murakkab siyosiy ehtiyojlarini qondiradigan tuzatilgan Konferensiyalar tizimi yo'q.

en: A systematic development and a systematic application of the sciences of human relationship, of personal and group psychology, of ﬁnancial and economic science and of education, sciences still only in their infancy, is required.
uz: Inson munosabatlari, shaxsiy va guruh psixologiyasi, moliyaviy va iqtisodiy fanlar hamda ta'lim fanlarining tizimli rivojlanishi va tizimli qo'llanilishi talab etiladi, bu fanlar hali endigina go'dakligida.

en: Narrow and obsolete, dead and dying moral and political ideas have to be replaced by a clearer and a simpler conception of the common origins and destinies of our kind.
uz: Tor va eskirgan, o'lik va o'layotgan axloqiy va siyosiy g'oyalar o'z turimizning umumiy kelib chiqishi va taqdirlari haqida aniqroq va soddaroq tushuncha bilan almashtirilishi kerak.

en: A PEACEFUL GARDEN IN ENGLAND  Given wisdom, all mankind might live in such gardens But if the dangers, confusions and disasters that crowd upon man in these days are enormous beyond any experience of the past, it is because science has brought him such powers as he never had before.
uz: Angliyada tinch bog'. Barcha insoniyat shunday bog'larda yashashi mumkin edi. Ammo hozirgi kunda insonni qamrab oluvchi xavf-xatarlar, chalkashliklar va falokatlar o'tmish tajribasidan ham kattaroq bo'lsa, demak, u ilgari hech qachon bo'lmagan kuchlarni fanga olib kelgan.

en: And the scientiﬁc method of fearless thought, exhaustively lucid statement, and exhaustively criticized planning, which has given him these as yet uncontrollable pow-
uz: Va qo'rqmas fikrlashning ilmiy usuli, charchagancha tiniq bayonot va charchagancha tanqid qilingan rejalashtirish unga hali nazorat qilib bo'lmaydigan kuchlarni berdi.

en: ers, gives him also the hope of controlling these powers.
uz: Ehri, unga bu kuchlarni nazorat qilish umidini ham beradi.

en: Man is still only adolescent.
uz: Inson hali faqat o'spirin.

en: His troubles are not the troubles of senility and exhaustion but of increasing and still undisciplined strength.
uz: Uning muammolari keksalik va charchoq muammolari emas, balki kuchayib borayotgan va hali ham intizomiy kuchdir.

en: When we look at all history as one process, as we have been doing in this book, when we see the steadfast upward struggle of life towards vision and control, then we see in their true proportions the hopes and dangers of the present time.
uz: Qachonki biz butun tarixga shu kitobda qilganimizdek, bir jarayon sifatida qarasak, qachonki hayotning tasavvur va nazoratga qaratilgan barqaror yuqoriga ko'tarilish kurashini ko'rsak, unda biz ularning haqiqiy nisbatlarida hozirgi zamon umidlari va xavflarini ko'ramiz.

en: As yet we are hardly in the earliest dawn of human greatness.
uz: Hozircha biz insoniy buyuklikning eng erta tongida emasmiz.

en: But in the beauty of ﬂower and sunset, in the happy and perfect movement of young animals and in the de- light of ten thousand various landscapes, we have some intimations of what life can do for us, and in some few works of plastic and pictorial art, in some great music, in a few noble buildings and happy gardens, we have an intimation of what the human will can do with material possibilities.
uz: Lekin gullarning go'zalligida va quyosh botishida, yosh hayvonlarning baxtli va mukammal harakatida va o'n ming turli landshaftlarning yorug'ligida hayot biz uchun nima qila olishi mumkinligi haqida ba'zi bir tasavvurlarga egamiz, plastik va tasviriy san'atning ba'zi bir asarlarida, ba'zi buyuk musiqalarda, bir nechta olijanob binolarda va baxtli bog'larda inson irodasi moddiy imkoniyatlar bilan nima qila olishi mumkinligi haqida tasavvurga egamiz.

en: We have dreams; we have at present undisciplined but ever increasing power.
uz: Bizda orzular bor; hozirda intizomiz, lekin doimiy ravishda o'sib borayotgan kuchimiz bor.

en: Can we doubt that presently our race will more than realize our boldest imaginations, that it will achieve unity and peace, that it will live, the chil- dren of our blood and lives will live, in a world made more splendid and lovely than any palace or garden that we know, going on from strength to strength in an ever widening circle of adventure and achievement?
uz: Hozirgi kunda bizning irqimiz bizning eng jasur tasavvurlarimizni amalga oshirishdan ko'ra ko'proq narsaga erishishiga, birlik va tinchlikka erishishiga, u yashashiga, qonimiz va hayotimizning to'kilishiga, biz bilgan har qanday saroy yoki bog'dan ko'ra ajoyibroq va go'zalroq bo'lgan dunyoda, doimiy ravishda kengayib borayotgan sarguzasht va yutuqlar doirasida kuchdan kuchga aylanishiga shubha qila olamizmi?

en: What man has done, the little triumphs of his present state, and all this history we have told, form but the prelude to the things that man has got to do.
uz: Inson nima qilgan bo'lsa, uning hozirgi holatidagi kichik g'alabalar va biz aytib bergan barcha tarix, inson qilishi kerak bo'lgan ishlarning davomi xolos.

en: CHRONOLOGICAL TABLE About the year 1000 B.C.
uz: XRONOLOGIY JADVAL Taxminan miloddan avvalgi 1000 yil.

en: the Aryan peoples were establishing themselves in the peninsulas of Spain, Italy and the Balkans, and they were established in North India; Cnossos was already destroyed and the spacious times of Egypt, of Thothmes III, Amenophis III and Rameses II were three or four centuries away.
uz: Aryan xalqlari Ispaniya, Italiya va Bolqon yarim orollarida o'rnashayotgan edi va ular Shimoliy Hindistonda joylashgan edi; Knossos allaqachon vayron qilingan edi va Misrning keng davri, Tothmes III, Amenophis III va Ramesses II uch-to'rt asr oldinda edi.

en: Weak monarchs of the XXIst Dynasty were ruling in the Nile Valley.
uz: Nil vodiysida XXI suloladagi zaif monarxlar hukmronlik qilmoqda edi.

en: Israel was united under her early kings; Saul or David or possi- bly even Solomon may have been reigning.
uz: Isroil o'zining dastlabki shohlari ostida birlashgan edi; Shoul yoki Dovud yoki ehtimol hatto Sulaymon hukmronlik qilgan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: Sargon I (2750 B.C.) of the Akkadian Sumerian Empire was a remote memory in Babylonian history, more remote than is Constantine the Great from the world of the present
uz: Akkad Shumer imperiyasining Sargon I (miloddan avvalgi 2750-yil) Bobil tarixidagi uzoq xotira bo'lgan, hozirgi dunyodagi Buyuk Konstantinodan ham uzoqroq.

en: Hammurabi had been dead a thousand years.
uz: Hammurabi ming yil o'lgan edi.

en: The Assyrians were al- ready dominating the less military Babylonians.
uz: Ossuriyaliklar kamroq harbiy bo'lgan Bobilliklarga hukmronlik qilishga tayyor edilar.

en: Tiglath Pileser I had taken Babylon.
uz: Tiglath Pileser, men Bobilni egallagan edim.

en: But there was no permanent conquest; Assyria and Babylonia were still separate empires.
uz: Lekin doimiy bosib olish bo'lmadi; Ossuriya va Bobil hali ham alohida imperiya edi.

en: In China the new Chow dynasty was ﬂourishing.
uz: Xitoyda yangi Chow sulolasi gullab-yashnadi.

en: Stonehenge in England was already some hundreds of years old.
uz: Angliyadagi Stonehenge allaqachon yuzlab yillar edi.

en: The next two centuries saw a renascence of Egypt under the XXIInd Dy- nasty, the splitting up of the brief little Hebrew kingdom of Solomon, the spreading of the Greeks in the Balkans, South Italy and Asia Minor, and the days of Etruscan predominance in Central Italy.
uz: Keyingi ikki asr Misrning XXII yovuz davr ostida qayta tug'ilishini, Sulaymonning qisqa kichik ibroniy shohligining bo'linishini, yunonlarning Bolqon, Janubiy Italiya va Kichik Osiyoda tarqalishini va Markaziy Italiyada etruskalarning ustunligini ko'rdi.

en: We begin our list of ascer- tainable dates with B.C.
uz: Ascer-tainable sanalarimiz ro'yxatini miloddan avvalgi davr bilan boshlaymiz.

en: The building of Carthage.
uz: Kartagen binosi.

en: The Ethiopian conquest of Egypt (founding the XXVth Dynasty).
uz: Misrning Efiopiya bosqini (XXV sulolaga asos solgan).

en: Tiglath Pileser III conquered Babylonia and founded the New Assyrian Empire.
uz: Tiglat Pileser III Bobilni zabt etdi va Yangi Ossuriya imperiyasiga asos soldi.

en: Sargon II armed the Assyrians with iron weapons.
uz: Sargon II ossuriyaliklarni temir qurollar bilan qurollantirdi.

en: He deported the Israelites.
uz: U Isroilliklarni deportatsiya qildi.

en: Esarhaddon took Thebes in Egypt (over- throwing the Ethiopian XXVth Dynasty).
uz: Esarhaddon Misrdagi Tebani egalladi ( Efiopiya XXV sulolasini ag'dardi).

en: Psammetichus I restored the freedom of Egypt and founded the XXVIth Dynasty (to 610).
uz: Psammetichus I Misr ozodligini tikladi va XXVI sulolaga asos soldi (610 yilgacha).

en: Necho of Egypt defeated Josiah, king of Ju- dah, at the battle of Megiddo.
uz: Misrlik Nexo Yo'shiyo, Yahudo shohini Megido jangida mag'lub etdi.

en: Capture of Nineveh by the Chaldeans and Medes.
uz: Nineviyani xaldeylar va medlar tomonidan zabt etish.

en: Foundation of the Chaldean Empire.
uz: Xaldeya imperiyasining asosi.

en: Necho pushed to the Euphrates and was overthrown by Nebuchadnezzar II.
uz: Nexo Furot daryosiga surildi va Nabukadnezar II tomonidan ag'darildi.

en: (Nebuchadnezzar carried off the Jews to Babylon.)   550.
uz: (Nebukadnezar yahudiylarni Bobilga olib ketdi.) 550

en: Cyrus the Persian succeeded Cyaxares the Mede.
uz: Forslik Kir Kyakxaros meddaning o'rnini egalladi.

en: Cyrus conquered Crœsus.
uz: Kir Kir Xronni zabt etdi.

en: Buddha lived about this time.
uz: Budda taxminan shu davrda yashagan.

en: So also did Confucius and Lao Tse.
uz: Xuddi shunday Konfutsiy va Lao Tse ham qildi.

en: Cyrus took Babylon and founded the Per- sian Empire.
uz: Kir Bobilni egalladi va Per-sian imperiyasiga asos soldi.

en: Darius I, the son of Hystaspes, ruled from the Hellespont to the Indus.
uz: Dariy I, Hystaspesning o'g'li, Hellespontdan Indusgacha hukmronlik qildi.

en: His expedition to Scythia.
uz: Uning Skifiyaga ekspeditsiyasi.

en: Battles of Thermopylï and Salamis.
uz: Termopil va Salamis janglari.

en: The battles of Platea and Mycale completed the repulse of Persia.
uz: Platya va Mikal janglari Forsning rad etilishini yakunladi.

en: Etruscan ﬂeet destroyed by the Sicilian Greeks.
uz: Etruska floti Sitsiliyalik yunonlar tomonidan vayron qilindi.

en: Peloponnesian War began (to 404)   401.
uz: Peloponnes urushi boshlandi (404 yilgacha) 401 yil.

en: Retreat of the Ten Thousand.
uz: O'n mingliklarning chekinishi.

en: Philip became king of Macedonia.
uz: Filip Makedoniya qiroli bo'ldi.

en: Macedonian troops crossed into Asia.
uz: Makedoniya qo'shinlari Osiyoga o'tdi.

en: Battle of the Granicus.
uz: Granicus jangi.

en: Death of Alexander the Great.
uz: Aleksandr Makedonskiyning o'limi.

en: Rise of Chandragupta in the Punjab.
uz: Chandraguptaning Panjobda ko'tarilishi.

en: The Romans completely beaten by the Sam- nites at the battle of the Caudine Forks.
uz: Rimliklar Caudine Forks jangida Sam-nites tomonidan butunlay mag'lub etildi.

en: Pyrrhus invaded Italy.
uz: Pirr Italiyaga bostirib kirdi.

en: Gauls raided into Asia Minor and settled in Galatia.
uz: Gallar Kichik Osiyoga bostirib kirishdi va Galatiyaga joylashdilar.

en: (Asoka began to reign in Be- har—to 227.)   260.
uz: Asoka Be-harda hukmronlik qila boshladi  227.) 260.

en: Shi-Hwang-ti became King of Ts’in.
uz: Shi-Hwang-ti Tsin qiroliga aylandi.

en: Shi-Hwang-ti became Emperor of China.
uz: Shi-Hwang-ti Xitoy imperatoriga aylandi.

en: Great Wall of China begun.
uz: Buyuk Xitoy devori boshlandi.

en: Death of Shi-Hwang-ti.
uz: Shi-Hwang-ti o'limi.

en: Attalus bequeathed Pergamum to Rome.
uz: Attalus Pergamni Rimga meros qilib qoldirdi.

en: Marius drove back Germans.
uz: Marius nemislarni orqaga haydab chiqardi.

en: (Chinese conquering the Tarim valley.)   89.
uz: (Xitoyliklar Tarim vodiysini zabt etishmoqda.) 89.

en: All Italians became Roman citizens.
uz: Barcha italyanlar Rim fuqaroligiga aylandi.

en: The revolt of the slaves under Spartacus.
uz: Spartakos boshchiligidagi qullarning isyoni.

en: Defeat and end of Spartacus.
uz: Mag'lubiyat va Spartakning oxiri.

en: Pompey led Roman troops to the Caspian and Euphrates.
uz: Pompey Rim qo'shinlarini Kaspiy va Furotga olib bordi.

en: He encountered the Alani.
uz: U Alanilarga duch keldi.

en: Julius Cïsar defeated Pompey at Pharsalos.
uz: Yuliyliyliyliyus Pompeyni Pharsalosda mag'lub etdi.

en: Julius Cïsar assassinated.
uz: Yuliusuris o'ldirildi.

en: Augustus Cïsar princeps (until 14 A.D.).
uz: Avgustliyusliyoslik shahzodalar (milodiy 14 yilgacha).

en: True date of birth of Jesus of Nazareth.
uz: Nosiralik Iso Masihning haqiqiy tug'ilgan sanasi.

en: Christian Era began.
uz: Xristian davri boshlandi.

en: Jesus of Nazareth cruciﬁed.
uz: Nosiralik Iso xochga mixlangan.

en: Claudius (the ﬁrst emperor of the legions) made emperor by pretorian guard after mur-
uz: Klaudiy (legionlarning birinchi imperatori) pretorian qo'riqchilari tomonidan murdan keyin imperator etib tayinlandi.

en: (Galba, Otho, Vitellus, em- perors in succession.)   69.
uz: Galba, Otho, Vitellus, ketma-ket imperatorlar.

en: Pan Chau on the Caspian Sea.
uz: Kaspiy dengizidagi Pan Chau.

en: Hadrian succeeded Trajan.
uz: Hadrian Trayan o'rnini egalladi.

en: Roman Empire at its greatest extent.
uz: Rim imperiyasi eng katta darajada.

en: (The Indo-Scythians at this time were de- stroying the last traces of Hellenic rule in India.)   161.
uz: Hind-skiylar o'sha paytda Hindistonda Gellin hukmronligining so'nggi izlarini yo'q qilishayotgan edi. 161.

en: Marcus Aurelius succeeded Antoninus Pius.
uz: Mark Avreliy Antonin Pyu o'rnini egalladi.

en: Great plague began, and lasted to the death of M.
uz: Buyuk vabo boshlandi va M.ning o'limigacha davom etdi.

en: This also devastated all Asia.
uz: Bu butun Osiyoni ham vayron qildi.

en: (Nearly a century of war and disorder began in the Roman Empire.)   220.
uz: Rim imperiyasida deyarli bir asrlik urush va tartibsizlik boshlandi. 220.

en: End of the Han dynasty.
uz: Xan sulolasining oxiri.

en: Beginning of four hundred years of division in China.
uz: Xitoyda to'rt yuz yillik bo'linishning boshlanishi.

en: Ardashir I (ﬁrst Sassanid shah) put an end to Arsacid line in Persia.
uz: Ardashir I (birinchi Sassanid shohi) Forsda Arsatsid liniyasiga chek qo'ydi.

en: Mani began his teaching.
uz: Mani o'z ta'limini boshladi.

en: Goths crossed Danube in a great raid.
uz: Gotikalar buyuk hujumda Dunayni kesib o'tishdi.

en: Great victory of Goths.
uz: Gotikalarning buyuk g'alabasi.

en: Emperor Decius killed.
uz: Imperator Detsiy o'ldirildi.

en: Sapor I, the second Sassanid shah, took Anti- och, captured the Emperor Valerian, and was cut up on his return from Asia Minor by Ode- nathus of Palmyra.
uz: Sapor I, ikkinchi Sassanid shohi, Anti-ochni egalladi, imperator Valerianni asirga oldi va Kichik Osiyodan qaytganida Ode- nathus Palmyra tomonidan kesib tashlandi.

en: Mani cruciﬁed in Persia.
uz: Mani Forsda xochga mixlangan.

en: Diocletian became emperor.
uz: Diokletian imperator bo'ldi.

en: Diocletian persecuted the Christians.
uz: Diokletian xristianlarni ta'qib qildi.

en: Galerius abandoned the persecution of the Christians.
uz: Galeriy xristianlarning ta'qibidan voz kechdi.

en: Constantine the Great became emperor.
uz: Konstantin Buyuk imperator bo'ldi.

en: Constantine presided over the Council of Nicïa.
uz: Konstantin Nikaya Kengashini boshqardi.

en: Constantine baptized on his deathbed.
uz: Konstantin o'lim to'shagida suvga cho'mdirildi.

en: Julian the Apostate attempted to substitute Mithraism for Christianity.
uz: Yulian Apostat Mitraizmni xristianlik o'rniga almashtirishga harakat qildi.

en: Theodosius the Great emperor of east and west.
uz: Teodosiy Sharq va G'arb buyuk imperatori.

en: Theodosius the Great died.
uz: Teodosiy Buyuk vafot etdi.

en: Honorius and Ar- cadius redivided the empire with Stilicho and Alaric as their masters and protectors.
uz: Honorius va Ar-kadius imperiyani Stilicho va Alaric bilan o'z xo'jayinlari va himoyachilari sifatida qayta bo'lishdi.

en: The Visigoths under Alaric captured Rome.
uz: Alaric boshchiligidagi Visigotlar Rimni egalladi.

en: Vandals settling in south of Spain.
uz: Ispaniya janubida joylashgan vandallar.

en: Huns in Pannonia, Goths in Dalmatia.
uz: Pannoniyadagi gunnlar, Dalmatiyadagi gotlar.

en: Visigoths and Suevi in Portugal and North Spain.
uz: Portugaliya va Shimoliy Ispaniyadagi Vizigotlar va Suvaylar.

en: English invading Britain.
uz: Inglizlar Britaniyaga bostirib kirmoqda.

en: Vandals took Carthage.
uz: Vandallar Kartageni egalladi.

en: Attila raided Gaul and was defeated by Franks, Alemanni and Romans at Troyes.
uz: Attila Gollga hujum qildi va Troyesda Franklar, Alemannilar va Rimliklarga mag'lub bo'ldi.

en: Vandals sacked Rome.
uz: Vandallar Rimni talon-toroj qilishdi.

en: Odoacer, king of a medley of Teutonic tribes, informed Constantinople that there was no emperor in the West.
uz: Teuton qabilalarining bir to'dasi qiroli Oduaxer Konstantinopolga G'arbda imperator yo'qligini xabar qildi.

en: End of the Western Empire.
uz: G'arbiy imperiyaning oxiri.

en: Theodoric, the Ostrogoth, conquered Italy and became King of Italy, but was nominally sub- ject to Constantinople.
uz: Teodorik, Ostrogot, Italiyani zabt etdi va Italiyaning qiroli bo'ldi, lekin nominal ravishda Konstantinopolga bo'ysundirilib ketdi.

en: (Gothic kings in Italy.
uz: Italiyadagi gotika shohlari.

en: Goths settled on special conﬁscated lands as a garrison.)   527.
uz: Gotikalar maxsus musodara qilingan yerlarga garnizon sifatida joylashdilar. 527.

en: Justinian closed the schools at Athens, which had ﬂourished nearly a thousand years.
uz: Yustinian Afina shahridagi maktablarni yopdi, ular deyarli ming yil gullab-yashnagan edi.

en: Belis- arius (Justinian’s general) took Naples.
uz: Belis-arius (Yustinianning generali) Neapolni egalladi.

en: Chosroes I began to reign.
uz: Chosroes I hukmronlik qila boshladi.

en: Great plague in Constantinople.
uz: Konstantinopoldagi buyuk vabo.

en: Goths expelled from Italy by Justinian.
uz: Gotikalar Yustinian tomonidan Italiyadan quvildi.

en: The Lombards conquered most of North Italy (leaving Ravenna and Rome Byzantine).
uz: Lombardlar Shimoliy Italiyaning ko'p qismini zabt etishdi (Ravvenna va Rim Vizantiyani tark etishdi).

en: (The Lombards dominant in Italy.)   590.
uz: Italiyada hukmron bo'lgan Lombardlar. 590-yil.

en: Plague raged in Rome.
uz: Rimda vabo tarqaldi.

en: Chosroes II began to reign.
uz: Xosroes II hukmronlik qila boshladi.

en: Heraclius began to reign.
uz: Gerakliy hukmronlik qila boshladi.

en: Chosroes II held Egypt, Jerusalem, Damas- cus, and armies on Hellespont.
uz: Xosro II Misr, Quddus, Damashq va Hellespontda armiyalarni boshqargan.

en: Tang dynasty began in China.
uz: Tang sulolasi Xitoyda boshlangan.

en: Great Persian defeat at Nineveh by Heraclius.
uz: Buyuk Forsning Nineva shahrida Gerakl tomonidan mag'lubiyati.

en: Tai-tsung became Emperor of China.
uz: Tai-tsung Xitoy imperatoriga aylandi.

en: Kavadh II murdered and succeeded his father, Chosroes II.
uz: Kavadh II o'z otasi Xosroes II ni o'ldirib, uning o'rnini egalladi.

en: Muhammad wrote letters to all the rulers of the earth.
uz: Muhammad yer yuzidagi barcha hukmdorlarga xatlar yozdi.

en: Muhammad returned to Mecca.
uz: Muhammad Makkaga qaytib keldi.

en: Battle of the Yarmuk.
uz: Yarmuk jangi.

en: Tai-tsung received Nestorian missionaries.
uz: Tai-tsung nestorian missionerlarini qabul qildi.

en: Jerusalem surrendered to the Caliph Omar.
uz: Quddus xalifa Umarga taslim bo'ldi.

en: Othman third Caliph.
uz: Othman uchinchi xalifa.

en: Defeat of the Byzantine ﬂeet by the Moslems.
uz: Vizantiya flotining musulmonlar tomonidan mag'lubiyati.

en: The Caliph Moawija attacked Constantinople by sea.
uz: Xalifa Moawija Qustantiniyaga dengiz orqali hujum qildi.

en: Pepin of Hersthal, mayor of the palace, re- united Austrasia and Neustria.
uz: Pepin Herstal saroyi meri Avstraliya va Neustryani qayta birlashtirdi.

en: Moslem army invaded Spain from Africa.
uz: Musulmon armiyasi Afrikadan Ispaniyaga bostirib kirdi.

en: The domains of the Caliph Walid I extended from the Pyrenees to China.
uz: Xalifa Valid Ining hududlari Piriney tog'laridan Xitoygacha cho'zilgan.

en: 717- Suleiman, son and successor of Walid, failed
uz: 717- Sulaymon, Validning o'g'li va vorisi, muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchradi.

en: to take Constantinople.
uz: Konstantinopolni egallash uchun.

en: Charles Martel defeated the Moslems near Poitiers.
uz: Charlz Martel Poitiers yaqinida musulmonlarni mag'lub etdi.

en: Pepin crowned King of the French.

en: A kindly thing it is to have compassion of the afﬂicted and albeit it well be- seemeth everyone, yet of those is it more particularly required who have erst had need of comfort and have found it in any, amongst whom, if ever any had need thereof or held it dear or took pleasure therein aforetimes, certes, I am one of these.
uz: Azob chekkanlarga rahm qilish yaxshi ishdir va garchi bu hammaga yaxshi tuyulsa ham, lekin bu avval tasalliga muhtoj bo'lgan va uni har qanday odamda topganlar uchun ayniqsa talab etiladi. Agar ularning orasida kimdir unga muhtoj bo'lsa yoki uni qadrlasa yoki undan zavq olsa, albatta, men ulardan biriman.

en: For that, having from my ﬁrst youth unto this present been beyond measure inﬂamed with a very high and noble passion (higher and nobler, perchance, than might appear, were I to relate it, to sort with my low estate) albeit by persons of discretion who had intelligence thereof I was commended therefor and accounted so much the more worth, natheless a passing sore travail it was to me to bear it, not, certes, by reason of the cruelty of the beloved lady, but because of the exceeding ardour be- gotten in my breast of an ill-ordered appetite, for which, for that it suffered me not to stand content at any reasonable bounds, caused me ofttimes feel more chagrin than I had occasion for.
uz: Shuning uchun ham, yoshligimdan hozirgi kungacha juda yuqori va olijanob ishtiyoq bilan cheksiz darajada alanga olgan bo'lsam (ko'rinishidan ham yuqori va olijanobroq, ehtimol, agar men uni o'z quyi ahvolim bilan solishtirsam), garchi bu haqda aqlli odamlar tomonidan maqtovga sazovor bo'lsam ham va undan ko'proq qadrlansam ham, lekin bu menga o'tkinchi azob edi, albatta, sevgan xonimning shafqatsizligi tufayli emas, balki mening ko'kragimga noto'g'ri ishtaha tushgani uchun, chunki bu menga hech qanday oqilona chegaralarda to'yib turishga imkon bermadi, ko'pincha menga sabab bo'lganidan ko'ra ko'proq qayg'uga botirdi.

en: In this my afﬂiction the pleasant dis- course of a certain friend of mine and his admirable consolations afforded me such refreshment that I ﬁrmly believe of these it came that I died not.
uz: Bu azobimda, bir do'stimning yoqimli xatti-harakatlari va uning hayratlanarli tasallilari menga shunday taskin berdi, men bularning barchasidan o'lmasligimga qat'iy ishonaman.

en: But, as it pleased Him who, being Himself inﬁnite, hath for immutable law appointed unto all things mundane that they shall have an end, my love — beyond every other fervent and which nor stress of reasoning nor counsel, no, nor yet manifest shame nor peril that might ensue thereof, had availed either to break or to bend —of its own motion, in process of time, on such
uz: Lekin, O'zi cheksiz bo'lgan Zotga ma'qul kelganidek, U barcha dunyoviy narsalarga oxirini belgilab qo'ygan o'zgarmas qonuniyat, mening muhabbatim - har qanday boshqa ishtiyoqsiz va hech qanday fikrlash yoki maslahat, hech qanday tashvishsiz, hech qanday sharmandalik yoki xavf bo'lmagan, vaqt o'tishi bilan o'z harakatini sindirish yoki bukish uchun foydalangan edi.

en: wise abated that of itself at this present it hath left me only that pleasance which it is used to afford unto whoso adventureth himself not too far in the navigation of its profounder oceans; by reason whereof, all chagrin being done away, I feel it grown delightsome, whereas it used to be grievous.
uz: O'z-o'zidan aql-idrokni yo'qotdi, hozir menga faqatgina uning chuqur okeanlarida sayohat qilib, o'zini juda uzoqqa olib bormaydiganlarga taqdim etadigan lazzatni qoldirdi; shu sababli, barcha qayg'u yo'q bo'lib ketganidan so'ng, men uni quvonchli bo'lib qolganini his qilyapman, garchi u ilgari qayg'uli bo'lgan bo'lsa ham.

en: Yet, albeit the pain hath ceased, not, therefore, is the memory ﬂed of the beneﬁts whilom received and the kindnesses bestowed on me by those to whom, of the goodwill they bore me, my troubles were grievous; nor, as I deem, will it ever pass away, save for death.
uz: Lekin, og'riq to'xtasa ham, demak, men olgan foydalar va menga bergan mehribonliklar xotirasi qochib ketdi. Ular meni ko'targan yaxshi niyat tufayli, mening tashvishlarim og'riqli edi; va men o'ylagandek, u hech qachon o'tib ketmaydi, faqat o'lim uchun.

en: And for that gratitude, to my thinking, is, among the other virtues, especially commendable and its contrary blame- worthy, I have, that I may not appear ungrateful, bethought myself, now that I can call myself free, to endeavour, in that little which is possible to me, to afford some relief, in requital of that which I received aforetime —if not to those who succoured me and who, belike, by reason of their good sense or of their fortune, have no occasion therefor —to those, at least, who stand in need thereof.
uz: Va shu minnatdorchilik, o'ylashimcha, boshqa fazilatlar qatorida, ayniqsa maqtovga sazovor va unga teskari aybdor, men o'zimni noshukr ko'rsatmasligimga arziydi, deb o'yladim, endi o'zimni erkin deb atay olaman, o'zim uchun imkoni bo'lgan ozgina narsada, avval olganim evaziga biroz yengillik olishga harakat qilishga harakat qilaman  agar menga yordam berganlarga emas va, masalan, ularning yaxshi aqli yoki omadlari tufayli bunga hech qanday imkoniyati bo'lmasa  hech bo'lmaganda, ularga muhtoj bo'lganlarga.

en: And albeit my support, or rather I should say my comfort, may be and indeed is of little enough avail to the afﬂicted, nathe- less meseemeth it should rather be proffered whereas the need appeareth greater, as well because it will there do more service as for that it will still be there the liefer had.
uz: Va garchi mening qo'llab-quvvatlashim, to'g'rirog'i, tasalli berishim kerak bo'lsa ham, aziyat chekkanlarga kam foyda keltirishi mumkin va haqiqatan ham, kamroq foyda keltirsa ham, ehtiyoj kattaroq ko'rinsa, u ko'proq xizmat qilishi kerak, chunki u hali ham yolg'onchiga kerak bo'lgan joyda bo'ladi.

en: And who will deny that this [comfort], whatsoever [worth] it be, it behoveth much more to give unto lovesick ladies than unto men?
uz: Va kim inkor etadi, bu [qulaylik] nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, sevgiga botgan ayollarga erkaklarga qaraganda ko'proq berish kerak?

en: For that these within their tender bosoms, fearful and shamefast, hold hid the ﬁres of love (which those who have proved know how much more puissance they have than those which are manifest), and constrained by the wishes, the pleasures, the commandments of fathers, mothers, brothers and husbands, abide most time enmewed in the narrow compass of their cham- bers and sitting in a manner idle, willing and willing not in one breath, re- volve in themselves various thoughts which it is not possible should still be merry.
uz: Chunki bular o'zlarining mayin ko'kraklarida, qo'rqoq va uyatchan, sevgi olovini yashiradi (ularda namoyon bo'lganlardan ko'ra qanchalik qudrat borligini bilganlar) va otalar, onalar, aka-ukalar va erlarning istaklari, rohatlari, amrlari bilan cheklanadi, ko'p vaqt davomida o'zlarining xonalarining tor doirasiga singib, beparvo o'tiradi, bir nafasda xohlamaydi va xohlamaydi, o'zida hali ham xursand bo'lishi mumkin bo'lmagan turli xil fikrlarni qayta-qayta o'ylaydi.

en: By reason whereof if there arise in their minds any melancholy, bred of ardent desire, needs must it with grievous annoy abide therein, except it be done away by new discourse; more by token that they are far less strong than men to endure.
uz: Shuning uchun ham, agar ularning ongida har qanday qayg'u paydo bo'lsa, u yerda achchiq-chuyda g'azab bilan yashashi kerak, agar u yangi nutq bilan yo'q qilinmasa; ayniqsa, ular odamlardan ko'ra bardosh berish uchun ancha kuchsiz ekanligi sababli.

en: With men in love it happeneth not on this wise, as we may manifestly see.
uz: Muhabbatdagi odamlar bilan bu yo'l bilan sodir bo'lmaydi, buni ko'rinib turibdiki.

en: They, if any melancholy or heaviness of thought op- press them, have many means of easing it or doing it away, for that to them, an they have a mind thereto, there lacketh not commodity of going about hearing and seeing many things, fowling, hunting, ﬁshing, riding, gaming and trafﬁcking; each of which means hath, altogether or in part, power to draw the mind unto itself and to divert it from troublous thought, at least for
uz: Agar ularni har qanday tushkunlik yoki o'y og'irligi bosib tursa, uni yengillashtirish yoki yo'qotishning ko'p usullari bor, chunki ularga bu haqda aql bor, ko'p narsalarni eshitish va ko'rish, ov qilish, ov qilish, baliq ovlash, otda yurish, o'yin o'ynash va savdo qilish uchun qulaylik yo'q; ularning har biri, umuman yoki qisman, ongni o'ziga tortish va uni bezovta fikrlardan chalg'itish uchun kuchga ega, hech bo'lmaganda

en: some space of time, whereafter, one way or another, either solacement su- perveneth or else the annoy groweth less.
uz: Vaqt oralig'ida, keyin, bir yo'l bilan yoki boshqacha yo'l bilan, yoki tasalli paydo bo'ladi, yoki boshqa yo'l bilan bezovtalik kamroq o'sadi.

en: Wherefore, to the end that the un- right of Fortune may by me in part be amended, which, where there is the less strength to endure, as we see it in delicate ladies, hath there been the more niggard of support, I purpose, for the succour and solace of ladies in love (unto others2 the needle and the spindle and the reel sufﬁce) to recount an hundred stories or fables or parables or histories or whatever you like to style them, in ten days’ time related by an honourable company of seven ladies and three young men made in the days of the late deadly pestilence, together with sundry canzonets sung by the aforesaid ladies for their diver- sion.
uz: Shuning uchun, omadning huquqsizligi meni tomonidan qisman o'zgartirilishi uchun, nozik ayollarda ko'rganimizdek, bardosh berish uchun kuch kam bo'lgan joyda, sevgi ayollarining yordami va tasalli uchun (boshqalarga igna, shpindel va g'altak yetarli) o'n kun ichida yuzta hikoya yoki ertak yoki masal yoki tarix yoki ularni qanday uslubda yozishni xohlasangiz, o'n kun ichida, yetti xonimdan iborat hurmatli jamoa va uch nafar yosh yigit tomonidan oxirgi halokat kunlarida aytilgan turli xil qo'shiqlar bilan birga aytib berishni maqsad qilaman.

en: In these stories will be found love-chances,3 both gladsome and griev- ous, and other accidents of fortune befallen as well in times present as in days of old, whereof the ladies aforesaid, who shall read them, may at once take solace from the delectable things therein shown forth and useful coun- sel, inasmuch as they may learn thereby what is to be eschewed and what is on like wise to be ensued —the which methinketh cannot betide without cease of chagrin.
uz: Bu hikoyalarda sevgi-muhabbat imkoniyatlari uchraydi, 3 ham quvonchli, ham qayg'uli, va qadimgi kunlardagi kabi hozirgi zamonda ham baxtsiz hodisalar sodir bo'ladi. Ularni o'qigan ayollar, darhol u yerda ko'rsatilgan yoqimli va foydali narsalardan tasalli olishlari mumkin, chunki ular shu orqali nimani chetlab o'tish kerakligini va nima oqilona bo'lishini o'rganadilar  bu narsalarga tinimsiz chidab bo'lmaydi.

en: If it happen thus (as God grant it may) let them render thanks therefor to Love, who, by loosing me from his bonds, hath vouch- safed me the power of applying myself to the service of their pleasures.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa (Xudo xohlasa), ular sevgiga shu uchun minnatdorchilik bildirsinlar. U meni o'z bog'laridan ozod qilib, o'z zavqlariga xizmat qilish qobiliyatini berdi.

en: DAY THE FIRST INTRODUCTION Here beginneth the ﬁrst day of the Decameron wherein (after demonstration made by the author of the manner in which it came to pass that the persons who are hereinafter presented foregathered for the purpose of devising together) under the governance of Pampinea is discoursed of that which is most agreeable unto each.
uz: KUN BIRINCHI KIRISH Bu yerda Dekameronning birinchi kuni boshlanadi (muallif tomonidan taqdim etilgan usulni ko'rsatgandan so'ng, keyinchalik birgalikda tuzish maqsadida oldindan taqdim etilgan shaxslar) Pampiyaning boshqaruvi ostida har biriga eng maqbul bo'lgan narsa muhokama qilinadi.

en: As often, most gracious ladies, as, taking thought in myself, I mind me how very pitiful you are all by nature, so often do I recognize that this present work will, to your thinking, have a grievous and a weariful beginning, inas- much as the dolorous remembrance of the late pestiferous mortality, which it beareth on its forefront, is universally irksome to all who saw or other- wise knew it.
uz: Ko'pincha, eng hurmatli xonimlar, o'zimni o'ylab, sizlarning tabiatingiz qanchalik achinarli ekanligingiz haqida o'ylayman, ko'pincha anglaymanki, bu hozirgi ish sizning fikrlashingizga ko'ra, qayg'uli va zerikarli boshlanadi, xuddi uning oldingi qismida bo'lgan kech o'latli o'limning achinarli xotirasi uni ko'rgan yoki boshqa - dono biladiganlarning barchasiga umumjahon masxara qiladi.

en: But I would not therefore have this affright you from reading further, as if in the reading you were still to fare among sighs and tears.
uz: Lekin men sizni bundan keyin ham o'qishdan xavotir olmagan bo'lardim, go'yo o'qishda siz hali ham oh-voh va ko'z yoshlar orasida yashayotgandek.

en: Let this grisly beginning be none other to you than is to wayfarers a rugged and steep mountain, beyond which is situate a most fair and delightful plain, which latter cometh so much the pleasanter to them as the greater was the hardship of the ascent and the descent; for, like as dolour occupieth the ex- treme of gladness, even so are miseries determined by imminent joyance.
uz: Bu kulrang boshlanishi siz uchun yo'lovchilarga qo'pol va tik tog'dan boshqa narsa bo'lmasin, uning orqasida eng go'zal va yoqimli tekislik joylashgan bo'lsin. Bu tekislik ularga ko'tarilish va tushish qiyinchiligi qanchalik katta bo'lsa, shunchalik yoqimli bo'lsin; chunki, xuddi dolour xursandchilikning oldingi titrasini egallagandek, xuddi shunday baxtsizliklar ham yaqinlashib kelayotgan quvonch bilan belgilanadi.

en: This brief annoy (I say brief, inasmuch as it is contained in few pages) is straightway succeeded by the pleasance and delight which I have already promised you and which, belike, were it not aforesaid, might not be looked for from such a beginning.
uz: Bu qisqa bezovta qiluvchi (men qisqa deyman, chunki u bir necha sahifada mavjud) sizga allaqachon va'da qilgan va, ehtimol, yuqorida aytilmaganida, bunday boshidanoq qidirilmagan lazzat va rohat bilan darhol o'z o'rnini egallaydi.

en: And in truth, could I fairly have availed to bring you to my desire otherwise than by so rugged a path as this will be I had gladly done it; but being in a manner constrained thereto, for that, without this reminiscence of our past miseries, it might not be shown what was the occasion of the coming about of the things that will hereafter be read, I have brought myself to write them.4
uz: Haqiqatan ham, men sizni o'z xohishimga yetkazish uchun shunchalik qattiq yo'ldan foydalanmagan bo'lsam ham, buni xursandchilik bilan qilgan bo'lardim; lekin bunga majbur bo'lganim uchun, o'tmishdagi musibatlarimizni eslamasdan, kelajakda o'qiladigan narsalarning paydo bo'lishining sababi nima ekanligini ko'rsatish mumkin emas edi, shuning uchun men ularni yozishga o'zimni majburladim.

en: I say, then, that the years [of the era] of the fruitful Incarnation of the Son of God had attained to the number of one thousand three hundred and forty- eight, when into the notable city of Florence, fair over every other of Italy, there came the death-dealing pestilence, which, through the operation of the heavenly bodies or of our own iniquitous dealings, being sent down upon mankind for our correction by the just wrath of God, had some years before appeared in the parts of the East and after having bereft these latter of an innumerable number of inhabitants, extending without cease from one place to another, had now unhappily spread towards the West.
uz: Shunday qilib, men aytamanki, Xudoning o'g'lining mevali mujassam bo'lish yillari bir ming uch yuz qirq sakkiz kishiga yetgan edi, o'shanda Italiyaning barcha hududlaridan ancha yuqori bo'lgan Florensiya shahriga o'limga olib keluvchi vabo kelgan edi, u samoviy jismlarning ishlashi yoki o'z gunohkor harakatlarimiz orqali insoniyatga Xudoning adolatli g'azabi bilan tuzatish uchun yuborilgan edi, bir necha yil oldin Sharqning bir qismlarida paydo bo'lgan edi va son-sanoqsiz aholini yo'qotganidan so'ng, bir joydan ikkinchi joyiga tarqalgan edi, endi baxtsiz tarzda G'arbga tarqaldi.

en: And thereagainst no wisdom availing nor human foresight (whereby the city was purged of many impurities by ofﬁcers deputed to that end and it was forbidden unto any sick person to enter therein and many were the counsels given5 for the preservation of health) nor yet humble supplications, not once but many times both in ordered processions and on other wise made unto God by de- vout persons —about the coming in of the Spring of the aforesaid year, it began on horrible and miraculous wise to show forth its dolorous effects.
uz: Va bunga na donolik foyda keltirmaydi, na insoniy bashorat (shunga ko'ra shahar shu maqsadda tayinlangan amaldorlar tomonidan ko'plab nopokliklardan tozalandi va u yerga har qanday bemorga kirish taqiqlandi va sog'lig'ini saqlash bo'yicha ko'p maslahatlar berildi) va na kamtarona duolar, na bir necha marta, na tartibli marosimlarda va boshqa yo'llar bilan de-vout shaxslar tomonidan Xudoga qilingan  yuqoridagi yilning bahori kelishi haqida, u dahshatli va mo'jizaviy tarzda uning og'riqli oqibatlarini ko'rsatishni boshladi.

en: Yet not as it had done in the East, where, if any bled at the nose, it was a manifest sign of inevitable death; nay, but in men and women alike there appeared, at the beginning of the malady, certain swellings, either on the groin or under the armpits, whereof some waxed of the bigness of a com- mon apple, others like unto an egg, some more and some less, and these the vulgar named plague-boils.
uz: Lekin Sharqda bo'lgani kabi emas edi, u yerda, agar burundan qon chiqsa, bu muqarrar o'limning yaqqol belgisi edi; yo'q, lekin erkaklar va ayollarda kasallikning boshida ba'zi shishlar paydo bo'ldi, xoh belda, xoh qo'ltiq ostida, ularning ba'zilari bir olma qalinligidan, ba'zilari tuxumga o'xshardi, ba'zilari ko'proq va ba'zilari kamroq, va bularning qo'polligi vabo-bo'ron deb atalgan.

en: From these two parts the aforesaid death-bear- ing plague-boils proceeded, in brief space, to appear and come indifferently in every part of the body; wherefrom, after awhile, the fashion of the conta- gion began to change into black or livid blotches, which showed themselves in many [ﬁrst] on the arms and about the thighs and [after spread to] every other part of the person, in some large and sparse and in others small and thick-sown; and like as the plague-boils had been ﬁrst (and yet were) a very certain token of coming death, even so were these for everyone to whom they came.
uz: Ushbu ikki qismdan yuqorida aytilgan o'limga olib keluvchi vabo-bo'ronlar qisqa vaqt ichida paydo bo'lib, tananing har bir qismida befarq kelib turardi; shundan so'ng, ma'lum vaqt o'tgach, contagionning uslubi qora yoki yashil dog'larga aylana boshladi, ular ko'p hollarda qo'llarda va sonlar atrofida ko'rinardi va odamning har bir boshqa qismiga tarqaldi, ba'zilarida katta va zich, boshqalarida esa kichik va qalin ekilgan; va xuddi vabo'ronlar birinchi bo'lib (va hali ham) o'limning aniq belgisi bo'lgani kabi, ular kelgan har bir kishi uchun ham shunday edi.

en: To the cure of these maladies nor counsel6 of physician nor virtue of any medicine appeared to avail or proﬁt aught; on the contrary —whether it was that the nature of the infection suffered it not or that the ignorance of the physicians (of whom, over and above the men of art, the number, both men and women, who had never had any teaching of medicine, was become ex- ceeding great), availed not to know whence it arose and consequently took not due measures thereagainst —not only did few recover thereof, but well
uz: Ushbu kasalliklarni davolashda na shifokorning maslahati, na hech qanday dori-darmonning kuchi foyda keltirmaydi; aksincha  bu infeksiyaning tabiati unga zarar yetkazmagan bo'lsa ham yoki shifokorlarning bilimsizligi (ularning san'at odamlaridan tashqari, tibbiyot bo'yicha hech qanday ta'limga ega bo'lmagan erkaklar va ayollar soni ham katta bo'lib ketgan), qayerdan kelib chiqqanini bilishga yordam bermadi va shuning uchun unga qarshi tegishli choralar ko'rmadi  nafaqat ozchilik undan tuzalib ketdi, balki

en: nigh all died within the third day from the appearance of the aforesaid signs, this sooner and that later, and for the most part without fever or other accident.7 And this pestilence was the more virulent for that, by communic- ation with those who were sick thereof, it gat hold upon the sound, no oth- erwise than ﬁre upon things dry or greasy, whenas they are brought very near thereunto.
uz: deyarli hamma yuqorida aytilgan belgilar paydo bo'lganidan keyin uch kun ichida vafot etdi, bu erta va keyinroq, va ko'p hollarda isitma yoki boshqa tasodifsiz.7 Va bu vabo shunchalik xavfli ediki, u kasal bo'lganlar bilan muloqot qilish orqali, quruq yoki yog'li narsalarga o't qo'zg'atgandan ko'ra, ular unga juda yaqin kelganda, tovushga chidamli edi.

en: Nay, the mischief was yet greater; for that not only did con- verse and consortion with the sick give to the sound infection of cause of common death, but the mere touching of the clothes or of whatsoever other thing had been touched or used of the sick appeared of itself to communic- ate the malady to the toucher.
uz: Yo'q, buzilish yanada katta edi; chunki nafaqat kasallar bilan aloqa va maslahatlashish umumiy o'lim sabab bo'lgan sog'lom infeksiyaga sabab bo'ldi, balki kasalning kiyimlariga yoki tegilgan yoki ishlatilgan boshqa narsalariga teginish kasallikni teginuvchiga yetkazish uchun o'z-o'zidan paydo bo'ldi.

en: A marvellous thing to hear is that which I have to tell and one which, had it not been seen of many men’s eyes and of mine own, I had scarce dared credit, much less set down in writing, though I had heard it from one worthy of belief.
uz: Ajoyib eshitish kerak bo'lgan narsa shuki, men buni aytishim kerak va agar ko'pchilikning ko'zlari va o'zimning ko'zlarim bilan ko'rmaganida, men uni ishonishga jur'at etmagan bo'lardim, ayniqsa yozma ravishda yozgan bo'lardim, garchi uni ishonishga arziydigan bir kishidan eshitgan bo'lsam ham.

en: I say, then, that of such efﬁcience was the nature of the pestilence in question in communicating itself from one to another, that, not only did it pass from man to man, but this, which is much more, it many times visibly did; —to wit, a thing which had pertained to a man sick or dead of the aforesaid sickness, being touched by an animal foreign to the human species, not only infected this latter with the plague, but in a very brief space of time killed it.
uz: Shunday qilib, men aytamanki, bunday samaradorlikning mohiyati bu o'latning bir-biridan o'zini o'zi yetkazishi edi, nafaqat u odamdan odamga o'tdi, balki bu, bundan tashqari, ko'p marta ko'rinib turardi;  xususan, yuqorida aytilgan kasallikdan kasal yoki o'lgan odamga tegishli bo'lgan narsa, inson zotiga begona hayvon tomonidan teginishi, nafaqat bu odamni vabo bilan yuqtirdi, balki juda qisqa vaqt ichida uni o'ldirdi.

en: Of this mine own eyes (as hath a little before been said) had one day, among others, experience on this wise; to wit, that the rags of a poor man, who had died of the plague, being cast out into the public way, two hogs came up to them and having ﬁrst, after their wont, rooted amain among them with their snouts, took them in their mouths and tossed them about their jaws; then, in a little while, after turning round and round, they both, as if they had taken poison, fell down dead upon the rags with which they had in an ill hour intermeddled.
uz: Bundan o'zimning ko'zlarim (biroz oldin aytilganidek) bir kuni boshqalardan ham shunday tajriba topgan edi: ya'ni, bir kambag'al odamning cho'chqog'i, vabo tufayli vafot etib, jamoat yo'liga uloqtirilganda, ularning oldiga ikkita cho'chqa kelib, avval o'z odatlaridan so'ng, burunlari bilan ularning orasiga ildiz otdi, og'ziga oldi va jag'lariga tashladi; keyin, bir oz vaqtdan so'ng, aylanib-aylanib, go'yo zahar olganlardek, ular bir yomon soat ichida aralashgan cho'chqog'iga o'lik holda yiqilishdi.

en: From these things and many others like unto them or yet stranger divers fears and conceits were begotten in those who abode alive, which well nigh all tended to a very barbarous conclusion, namely, to shun and ﬂee from the sick and all that pertained to them, and thus doing, each thought to secure immunity for himself.
uz: Bu narsalar va ularga o'xshash ko'plab boshqa narsalar yoki shunga o'xshash g'alatiroq turli xil qo'rquvlar va kibrlar tirik qolganlarda paydo bo'ldi, bularning barchasi juda vahshiyona xulosaga yaqinlashdi, ya'ni bemorlardan va ularga tegishli bo'lgan hamma narsadan qochish va qochish, shu bilan har bir o'y o'zi uchun immunitetni ta'minlash uchun.

en: Some there were who conceived that to live moder- ately and keep oneself from all excess was the best defence against such a danger; wherefore, making up their company, they lived removed from every other and shut themselves up in those houses where none had been sick and where living was best; and there, using very temperately of the most delicate viands and the ﬁnest wines and eschewing all incontinence, they abode with music and such other diversions as they might have, never
uz: Ba'zilar o'rtacha yashash va o'zini har qanday haddan tashqari narsalardan himoya qilish bunday xavfdan eng yaxshi himoya deb o'ylashgan; shuning uchun, ular o'zlarining hamrohlarini bir-biridan uzoqroqda yashab, hech kim kasal bo'lmagan va yashash eng yaxshi bo'lgan uylarda yashaydilar; va u yerda, eng nozik go'shtlardan va eng yaxshi vinolardan juda ehtiyotkorlik bilan foydalanib, har qanday tiyilmaslikdan qochib, ular musiqa va boshqa chalg'ituvchi mashg'ulotlar bilan birga yashaydilar.

en: suffering themselves to speak with any nor choosing to hear any news from without of death or sick folk.
uz: O'zlarini hech kim bilan gaplashishga tortishmaydi, shuningdek, o'lim yoki kasal odamlar haqida tashqaridan xabar eshitishni tanlamaydilar.

en: Others, inclining to the contrary opinion, maintained that to carouse and make merry and go about singing and frol- icking and satisfy the appetite in everything possible and laugh and scoff at whatsoever befell was a very certain remedy for such an ill.
uz: Boshqalar esa, aksincha fikrga moyil bo'lgan holda, g'azablanish va xursandchilik qilish, qo'shiq aytib, xursandchilik qilib yurish, istakni hamma narsada qondirish va nima bo'lishidan kulish va masxara qilish bunday kasallik uchun juda aniq yechim ekanligini ta'kidlashdi.

en: That which they said they put in practice as best they might, going about day and night, now to this tavern, now to that, drinking without stint or measure; and on this wise they did yet more freely in other folk’s houses, so but they scented there aught that liked or tempted them, as they might lightly do, for that everyone —as he were to live no longer —had abandoned all care of his pos- sessions, as of himself, wherefore the most part of the houses were become common good and strangers used them, whenas they happened upon them, like as the very owner might have done; and with all this bestial preoccupa- tion, they still shunned the sick to the best of their power.
uz: Ular aytganlaricha, qo'llaridan kelgancha amaliyotga tatbiq etishardi, kunduzi-kechasi bu tavernga, endi u yerga, hech qanday o'lchovsiz ichishardi; va shu tariqa ular boshqa odamlarning uylarida yanada erkinroq qilishardi, lekin u yerda ularga yoqqan yoki ularni vasvasaga soladigan narsa hidini sezishardi, xuddi yengillik bilan qilishlari mumkin bo'lganidek, chunki har bir kishi  endi yashamasligi kerak edi  o'zi kabi  barcha g'amxo'rliklarini tashlab ketgan edi, shuning uchun uylarning aksariyati oddiy yaxshi va begonalarga ishlatilgan edi, ular bilan sodir bo'lganda, xuddi egasi qilgan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lganidek; va bu barcha hayvoniy ish bilan, ular hali ham bemorlarni o'z kuchlarining eng yaxshi tomonga urib qo'yishardi.

en: In this sore afﬂiction and misery of our city, the reverend authority of the laws, both human and divine, was all in a manner dissolved and fallen into decay, for [lack of] the ministers and executors thereof, who, like other men, were all either dead or sick or else left so destitute of followers that they were unable to exercise any ofﬁce, wherefore everyone had license to do whatsoever pleased him.
uz: Shahrimizning bu azob-uqubatlari va musibatlarida, qonunlarning hurmatli hokimiyati, ham insoniy, ham ilohiy, butunlay tarqalib, chirib ketdi, chunki uning vazirlari va ijrochilari, boshqa odamlar kabi, hammasi o'lik yoki kasal yoki shunday izdoshlari yo'q edilarki, hech qanday lavozimni bajara olmas edilar, shuning uchun har kim o'ziga yoqqan narsani qilishga ruxsat olardi.

en: Many others held a middle course between the two aforesaid, not straitening themselves so exactly in the matter of diet as the ﬁrst neither allowing themselves such license in drinking and other de- bauchery as the second, but using things in sufﬁciency, according to their appetites; nor did they seclude themselves, but went about, carrying in their hands, some ﬂowers, some odoriferous herbs and other some divers kinds of spiceries,8 which they set often to their noses, accounting it an excellent thing to fortify the brain with such odours, more by token that the air seemed all heavy and attainted with the stench of the dead bodies and that of the sick and of the remedies used.
uz: Boshqa ko'pchilik yuqorida aytilgan ikki narsa o'rtasida o'rtacha yo'l tutdi, ovqatlanish masalasida o'zlarini aynan shunday qattiqlashtirmadilar, chunki birinchisi ichishga va ikkinchisi kabi boshqa de-bauchery kabi litsenziyaga yo'l qo'ymadi, lekin o'z ishtahalariga ko'ra yetarli darajada ishlatishardi; shuningdek, o'zlarini ajratib olishmadi, balki qo'llarida ba'zi gullar, ba'zi xushbo'y o'tlar va boshqa turli xil ziravorlarni olib yurishdi, 8 ularni ko'pincha burunlariga qo'yishardi, bularni miyani bunday hidlar bilan mustahkamlash uchun ajoyib narsa deb hisoblashardi, ko'proq havo og'ir va ishlatilgan kasallarning badbo'yi bilan qoplangan edi.

en: Some were of a more barbarous, though, peradventure, a surer way of thinking, avouching that there was no remedy against pestilences better than —no, nor any so good as —to ﬂee before them; wherefore, moved by this reasoning and recking of nought but themselves, very many, both men and women, abandoned their own city, their own houses and homes, their kinsfolk and possessions, and sought the country seats of others, or, at the least, their own, as if the wrath of God, being moved to punish the iniquity of mankind, would not proceed to do so wheresoever they might be, but
uz: Ba'zilar yanada vahshiy, ammo, tasodifan, aniqroq fikrlash tarziga ega edilar, chunki ularning oldidan qochishdan yaxshiroq, yo'q, va undan ham yaxshiroq chora yo'q edi; shuning uchun, bu mulohaza va o'zlarini hisobga olishdan ko'ra, juda ko'p erkaklar va ayollar o'z shaharlarini, o'z uylari va uylarini, qarindoshlarini va mol-mulklarini tashlab, boshqalarning qishloq joylarini qidirdilar, yoki hech bo'lmaganda, Xudoning g'azabi odamlarning gunohlarini jazolashga undayotgandek, o'zlarining o'zlarining...

en: would content itself with afﬂicting those only who were found within the walls of their city, or as if they were persuaded that no person was to remain therein and that its last hour was come.
uz: o'zini faqat o'z shaharining devorlari ichida topilganlarni azoblash bilan kifoyalanardi, yoki go'yo u yerda hech kim qolmasligi va uning oxirgi soati kelganiga ishontirardi.

en: And albeit these, who opined thus variously, died not all, yet neither did they all escape; nay, many of each way of thinking and in every place sickened of the plague and languished on all sides, well nigh abandoned, having themselves, what while they were whole, set the example to those who abode in health.
uz: Va garchi bu turli fikrda bo'lganlar hammasi o'lmagan bo'lsa-da, ularning hammasi ham qutulmagan; aksincha, har bir fikrlash tarzi va har bir joyda vabo kasalligi va har tomondan bedor, deyarli tashlab ketilgan, o'zlari sog'lom bo'lgan holda sog'lom bo'lganlar uchun namuna bo'lganlar.

en: Indeed, leaving be that townsman avoided townsman and that well nigh no neighbour took thought unto other and that kinsfolk seldom or never vis- ited one another and held no converse together save from afar, this tribula- tion had stricken such terror to the hearts of all, men and women alike, that brother forsook brother, uncle nephew and sister brother and oftentimes wife husband; nay (what is yet more extraordinary and well nigh incredible) fathers and mothers refused to visit or tend their very children, as they had not been theirs.
uz: Darhaqiqat, shaharlik shaharlikdan qochgan va deyarli qo'shnilar bir-birini o'ylamagan, qarindoshlar kamdan-kam hollarda bir-birini ko'rishmagan va uzoqdan boshqa hech qachon birga suhbatlashmagan holda, bu musibat barcha odamlarning, erkaklar va ayollarning qalbida shunday dahshatni keltirdi, hatto aka-uka aka-uka, amaki, jiyan va opa-singillarni va ko'pincha xotin-xotinni tashlab ketardi; yo'q (bu yanada g'ayrioddiy va aql bovar qilmas darajada) ota-onalar o'z farzandlariga tashrif buyurishdan yoki ularga g'amxo'rlik qilishdan bosh tortdilar, chunki ular ularning o'z farzandlari emas edi.

en: By reason whereof there remained unto those (and the num- ber of them, both males and females, was incalculable) who fell sick, none other succour than that which they owed either to the charity of friends (and of these there were few) or the greed of servants, who tended them, allured by high and extravagant wage; albeit, for all this, these latter were not grown many, and those men and women of mean understanding and for the most part unused to such ofﬁces, who served for well nigh nought but to reach things called for by the sick or to note when they died; and in the do- ing of these services many of them perished with their gain.
uz: Shuning uchun ham (va ularning soni, erkaklar ham, ayollar ham, sanob bo'lmas edi) kasal bo'lganlarga do'stlarining xayriyasidan yoki ularni yuqori va dabdabali ish haqi bilan o'ziga rom etgan xizmatkorlarning ochko'zligidan boshqa hech qanday yordam qolmadi.

en: Of this abandonment of the sick by neighbours, kinsfolk and friends and of the scarcity of servants arose an usage before well nigh unheard, to wit, that no woman, how fair or lovesome or wellborn soever she might be, once fallen sick, recked aught of having a man to tend her, whatever he might be, or young or old, and without any shame discovered to him every part of her body, no otherwise than she would have done to a woman, so but the neces- sity of her sickness required it; the which belike, in those who recovered, was the occasion of lesser modesty in time to come.
uz: Qo'shnilar, qarindoshlar va do'stlar tomonidan bemorlarni tashlab ketish va xizmatkorlarning yetishmasligi haqida ilgari deyarli eshitilmagan bir odat paydo bo'lgan edi, xususan, hech bir ayol, qanchalik go'zal yoki mehribon yoki yaxshi tug'ilgan bo'lmasin, kasal bo'lganida, unga g'amxo'rlik qiladigan erkak borligini hech narsa deb hisoblamagan, u yosh yoki keksa bo'lmasin, va u uchun uning tanasining har bir qismi hech qanday uyatsiz topilmagan, ayolga qilganidan boshqa hech narsa emas edi, lekin uning kasalligi zarurligi buni talab qilardi; bu, sog'ayganlarda, kelajakda kamroq kamtarlik uchun sabab bo'lardi.

en: Moreover, there ensued of this abandonment the death of many who peradventure, had they been succoured, would have escaped alive; wherefore, as well for the lack of the opportune services which the sick availed not to have as for the virulence of the plague, such was the multitude of those who died in the city by day and by night that it was an astonishment to hear tell thereof, much more to see
uz: Qolaversa, bu tashlab ketish natijasida ko'pchilikning o'limi sodir bo'ldi, agar ular yordam berilsa, tirik qutulib qolishardi; shuning uchun, kasallar zararkunandalik xavfi uchun foydalanmaydigan qulay xizmatlarning yo'qligi sababli, shaharda kunduzi va kechasi o'lganlarning soni shunchalik ko'p ediki, buni eshitish hayratlanarli edi, ko'proq...

en: it; and thence, as it were of necessity, there sprang up among those who abode alive things contrary to the pristine manners of the townsfolk.
uz: u; va shundan so'ng, go'yo zarurat bo'lgandek, shahar aholisining asl odatlariga zid bo'lgan tirik narsalar yashovchilar orasida paydo bo'ldi.

en: It was then (even as we yet see it used) a custom that the kinswomen and she-neighbours of the dead should assemble in his house and there condole with those who more nearly pertained unto him, whilst his neighbours and many other citizens foregathered with his next of kin before his house, whither, according to the dead man’s quality, came the clergy, and he with funeral pomp of chants and candles was borne on the shoulders of his peers to the church chosen by himself before his death; which usages, after the virulence of the plague began to increase, were either altogether or for the most part laid aside, and other and strange customs sprang up in their stead.
uz: O'shanda (hali ham ko'rayotganimizdek) marhumning qarindoshlari va qo'shnilari uning uyida yig'ilib, unga yaqinroq bo'lganlar bilan xotirjamlik bildirishlari odati edi, qo'shnilari va boshqa ko'plab fuqarolar esa o'z qarindoshlari bilan uyning oldida oldinga yig'ilishardi. U yerga, marhumning sifatiga ko'ra, ruhoniylar kelardi va u dafn marosimlari va shamlar bilan o'z tengdoshlari yelkasiga o'zi o'limidan oldin tanlagan cherkovga olib borardi; bu odatlar, vabo kuchayganidan keyin, butunlay yoki asosan chetga surildi va boshqa g'alati urf-odatlar paydo bo'ldi.

en: For that, not only did folk die without having a multitude of women about them, but many there were who departed this life without witness and few indeed were they to whom the pious plaints and bitter tears of their kinsfolk were vouchsafed; nay, in lieu of these things there obtained, for the most part, laughter and jests and gibes and feasting and merrymaking in com- pany; which usance women, laying aside womanly pitifulness, had right well learned for their own safety.
uz: Shuning uchun nafaqat odamlar o'z atrofida ko'p ayollar bo'lmasdan o'lishdi, balki ko'pchilik bu hayotdan guvohliksiz ketganlar ham bor edi va juda ozchilik qarindoshlarining taqvodor shikoyatlari va achchiq ko'z yoshlari ularga nasib etgan edi; aksincha, bu narsalar o'rniga ko'p hollarda kulgi, hazil-mutoyiba, ziyofat va xursandchilik olishdi; bu odatlarni ayollar, ayollik achinishlarini chetga surib, o'z xavfsizliklari uchun yaxshi o'rganishgan edi.

en: Few, again, were they whose bodies were accompanied to the church by more than half a score or a dozen of their neighbours, and of these no wor- shipful and illustrious citizens, but a sort of bloodsuckers, sprung from the dregs of the people, who styled themselves pickmen9 and did such ofﬁces for hire, shouldered the bier and bore it with hurried steps, not to that church which the dead man had chosen before his death, but most times to the nearest, behind ﬁve or six10 priests, with little light11 and whiles none at all, which latter, with the aid of the said pickmen, thrust him into what grave soever they ﬁrst found unoccupied, without troubling themselves with too long or too formal a service.
uz: Yana kamdan-kam odamlar bor edi, ularning jasadlari cherkovga o'z qo'shnilarining yarimdan ko'p yoki o'nlab qo'shnilari bilan birga borgan edi, va bularning hech qanday tashvishlanarli va mashhur fuqarolari yo'q edi, balki xalqning dog'laridan chiqqan, o'zlarini pickmen deb ataydigan va shunday lavozimlarni ijaraga bergan, yelkalarini ko'tarib, shoshilinch qadamlar bilan olib boradigan, o'sha cherkovga emas, balki ko'pincha eng yaqin, besh yoki olti ruhoniy orqasida, hech qanday yorug'liksiz11 va hech qanday qahramonlar yordamida, ular uni birinchi bo'lmaganicha tashlab, o'zlarini juda uzoq yoki rasmiy xizmat bilan band qilmasdan.

en: The condition of the common people (and belike, in great part, of the middle class also) was yet more pitiable to behold, for that these, for the most part retained by hope12 or poverty in their houses and abiding in their own quarters, sickened by the thousand daily and being altogether untended and unsuccoured, died well nigh all without recourse.
uz: Oddiy odamlarning ahvoli (va ayniqsa, katta qismi o'rta sinfning ahvoli ham) yanada achinarli edi, chunki ularning ko'pchiligi o'z uylarida umid yoki qashshoqlik tufayli saqlanib qolgan va o'z xonalarida yashayotgan, minglab kundalik kasallikka chalingan va umuman parvarishlanmagan va sug'orilmagan holda, deyarli hech qanday chora ko'rmasdan vafot etgan edi.

en: Many breathed their last in the open street, whilst other many, for all they died in their houses, made it known to the neighbours that they were dead rather by the stench of their rotting bodies than otherwise; and of these and others who died all about the whole city was full.
uz: Ko'pchilik ochiq ko'chada so'nggi nafaslarini olishdi, boshqa ko'pchilik esa, chunki ularning barchasi o'z uylarida vafot etishdi, qo'shnilarga o'zlarining chirigan tanalarining badbo'y hididan ko'ra o'lik ekanliklarini bildirishdi; va bu va boshqa o'lganlarning butun shahri to'la edi.

en: For the most part one same usance was ob-
uz: Ko'p hollarda bir xil usul ob- edi.

en: served by the neighbours, moved more by fear lest the corruption of the dead bodies should imperil themselves than by any charity they had for the departed; to wit, that either with their own hands or with the aid of certain bearers, whenas they might have any, they brought the bodies of those who had died forth of their houses and laid them before their doors, where, espe- cially in the morning, those who went about might see corpses without number; then they fetched biers and some, in default thereof, they laid upon some board or other.
uz: Qo'shnilar tomonidan xizmat ko'rsatilib, o'lik jasadlarning buzilishi ularning o'lganlarga qilgan xayriyalaridan ko'ra xavfli bo'lishidan ko'proq qo'rqishardi; ya'ni, o'z qo'llari bilan yoki ayrim tashuvchilar yordamida, agar ular shunday bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa, uylaridan o'lganlarning jasadlarini olib chiqib, eshiklari oldiga qo'yishardi, ayniqsa ertalab, aylanib yurganlar son-sanoqsiz jasadlarni ko'rishardi; keyin ular piyozlarni olib kelishardi va ba'zilari, bu xato bo'lsa, ularni bir taxtaga yotqizishardi.

en: Nor was it only one bier that carried two or three corpses, nor did this happen but once; nay, many might have been counted which contained husband and wife, two or three brothers, father and son or the like.
uz: Na faqat bitta pichoq ikki yoki uchta jasadni ko'tarib yurgan edi, na bu faqat bir marta sodir bo'lgan edi; aksincha, ko'pchilik er-xotin, ikki yoki uch aka-uka, ota-bola yoki shunga o'xshashlarni o'z ichiga olgan deb hisoblangan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

en: And an inﬁnite number of times it befell that, two priests going with one cross for some one, three or four biers, borne by bearers, ranged themselves behind the latter,13 and whereas the priests thought to have but one dead man to bury, they had six or eight, and whiles more.
