en: It happeneth to every man, how devout soever he be, that, after long fasting, meat seemeth good to him, and after travail, drink.’ ‘Alack, father mine,’ rejoined Ciappelletto, ‘tell me not this to comfort me; you must know I know that things done for the service of God should be done sincerely and with an ungrudging mind; and whoso doth otherwise sinneth.’ Quoth the friar, exceeding well pleased, ‘I am content that thou shouldst thus apprehend it and thy pure and good conscience therein pleaseth me exceedingly.
uz: Har bir inson, qanchalik dindor bo'lmasin, uzoq ro'za tutgandan so'ng unga go'sht yoqadi, mehnatdan keyin esa ichadi." "Alak, otam," dedi yana Ciappelletto, "menga tasalli berish uchun bu gapni aytma; bilishing kerakki, Xudo xizmatida qilingan ishlar chin dildan va xolis aql bilan qilinishi kerak; va kimki boshqacha qilsa, gunoh qiladi".

en: But, tell me, hast thou sinned by way of avarice, desiring more than beﬁtted or withholding that which it behoved thee not to withhold?’ ‘Father mine,’ replied Ciappelletto, ‘I would not have you look to my being in the house of these usurers; I have nought to do here; nay, I came hither to admonish and chasten them and turn them from this their ab- ominable way of gain; and methinketh I should have made shift to do so, had not God thus visited me.
uz: Lekin, ayting-chi, siz ochko'zlik yo'li bilan gunoh qildingizmi, o'zingizga to'g'ri kelmagan narsani xohlab yoki o'zingizga to'g'ri kelmaydigan narsani ushlab turibmi? Otam, javob berdi Ciappelletto, Men sizni bu pul ozuqachilari uyida bo'lishingizga qaramasligingizni xohlardim; men bu yerda hech narsa qilmaganman; yo'q, men ularni tanbeh berish va jazolash uchun keldim va bu kabi imkonsiz daromad yo'lidan qaytarish uchun; va men buni qilish uchun o'zgarish qilgan bo'lardim, agar Xudo meni shunday yo'l bilan jazolamaganida.

en: But you must know that I was left a rich man by my father, of whose good, when he was dead, I bestowed the most part in alms, and after, to sustain my life and that I might be able to succour Christ’s poor, I have done my little trafﬁckings, and in these I have desired to gain; but still with God’s poor have I shared that which I gained, convert- ing my own half to my occasion and giving them the other, and in this so well hath my Creator prospered me that my affairs have still gone from good to better.’
uz: Lekin shuni bilishingiz kerakki, men otamdan boy odam qoldirdim. U o'lganida, uning mol-mulkidan ko'p qismini sadaqaga berardim. Keyin esa, hayotimni ta'minlash va Masihning kambag'allariga yordam bera olishim uchun, ozgina savdolar qildim va shu orqali foyda olishni xohladim; lekin baribir Xudoning kambag'allari bilan olganimni baham ko'rdim, o'z yarmini o'z maqsadimga aylantirib, boshqa bir qismini ularga berdim. Va bu bilan Yaratuvchim meni shunday muvaffaqiyatli qildi, ishlarim hali ham yaxshilanmoqda.

en: ‘Well hast thou done,’ said the friar; ‘but hast thou often been angered?’ ‘Oh,’ cried Master Ciappelletto, ‘that I must tell you I have very often been!
uz: Xo'p qildingiz,  dedi rohib;  lekin tez-tez g'azablandingizmi?  Oh,  deb baqirdi Ustoz Ciappelletto,  sizga aytishim kerakki, men juda tez-tez kelganman!

en: And who could keep himself therefrom, seeing men do unseemly things all day long, keeping not the commandments of God neither fearing His judg- ment?
uz: Va kim o'zini undan saqlay olardi, odamlar kun bo'yi behayo ishlar qilishini ko'rib, Xudoning amrlariga rioya qilmayaptimi va Uning hukmiga qo'rqmayaptimi?

en: Many times a day I had liefer been dead than alive, seeing young men follow after vanities and hearing them curse and forswear themselves, haunting the taverns, visiting not the churches and ensuing rather the ways of the world than that of God.’ ‘My son,’ said the friar, ‘this is a righteous anger, nor for my part might I enjoin thee any penance therefor.
uz: Kunning ko'p hollarda men tirikligimdan ko'ra o'lik bo'lgan edim, yosh yigitlarni butparastlik ortidan ergashib, ularni la'natlab, o'zlarini so'kinishlarini eshitib, mehmonxonalarni ta'qib qilib, cherkovlarga bormay, Xudoning yo'lidan yurishni afzal ko'rardim. O'g'lim,  dedi rohib, bu adolatli g'azab, men senga buning uchun hech qanday tavba buyurmayman.

en: But hath anger at any time availed to move thee to do any manslaughter or to be- speak anyone unseemly or do any other unright?’ ‘Alack, sir,’ answered the sick man, ‘you, who seem to me a man of God, how can you say such words?
uz: Ammo g'azab sizni hech qachon odam o'ldirishga yoki - hech kimga behayo gapirishga yoki boshqa noto'g'ri ish qilishga undadimi?  Alack, janob,  javob berdi bemor odam,  siz, menga Xudoning odami kabi ko'rinadigan, qanday qilib bunday so'zlarni ayta olasiz?

en: Had I ever had the least thought of doing any one of the things whereof you speak, think you I believe that God would so long have for- borne me?
uz: Agar men siz gapirayotgan narsalardan birortasini qilish haqida hech qachon o'ylamaganimda, Xudo meni uzoq vaqt oldin tug'ib yuborishiga ishonaman deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: These be the doings of outlaws and men of nought, whereof I never saw any but I said still, “Go, may God amend thee!” ’ Then said the friar, ‘Now tell me, my son (blessed be thou of God), hast thou never borne false witness against any or missaid of another, or taken others’ good, without leave of him to whom it pertained?’ ‘Ay, indeed, sir,’ replied Master Ciappelletto; ‘I have missaid of others; for that I had a neighbour aforetime, who, with the greatest unright in the world, did nought but beat his wife, insomuch that I once spoke ill of him to her kinsfolk, so great was the compassion that overcame me for the poor woman, whom he used as God alone can tell, whenassoever he had drunken overmuch.’ Quoth the friar, ‘Thou tellest me thou hast been a merchant.
uz: Bular noqonuniylar va hech kimga tegishli bo'lmagan odamlarning ishidir, men hech qachon ularning birortasini ko'rmadim, lekin men baribir aytdim: "Bor, Xudo seni isloh qilsin!"  Shunda rohib dedi: "Endi ayting-chi, o'g'lim, sen boshqa birovga qarshi yolg'on guvohlik bermadingmi yoki boshqa birovga nisbatan yolg'on gapirmadingmi, yoki boshqalarni qabul qilmadingmi, unga tegishli bo'lmagan odamga ruxsat bermadingmi?" Ha, janob,  Master Ciappelletto javob berdi; Men boshqalarni yomon ko'rdim; chunki mening bir qo'shnim bor edi, u dunyodagi eng katta adolatsizlik bilan xotinini urgan, chunki men bir marta u haqida yomon gapirdim, shuning uchun u menga shunday shafqat ko'rsatdi, chunki u Xudo kabi bir ayolga nisbatan yolg'on gapirgan edi, chunki u uni yolg'on...

en: Hast thou never cheated anyone, as merchants do whiles!’ ‘I’ faith, yes, sir,’ answered Mas- ter Ciappelletto; ‘but I know not whom, except it were a certain man, who once brought me monies which he owed me for cloth I had sold him and which I threw into a chest, without counting.
uz: "Sen hech qachon hech kimni aldamaganmisan, xuddi savdogarlar do'pposlaganidek!" Men  ishonaman, ha, janob,  javob berdi Mas- ter Ciappelletto;  lekin men kimni bilmayman, faqatgina bir odam edi, u menga bir vaqtlar to'qima uchun qarzdor bo'lgan pullarni olib kelgan edi, men uni sotgandim va uni sandiqqa sanamasdan tashladim.

en: A good month after, I found that they were four farthings more than they should have been; wherefore, not seeing him again and having kept them by me a full year, that I might restore them to him, I gave them away in alms.’ Quoth the friar, ‘This was a small matter, and thou didst well to deal with it as thou didst.’ Then he questioned him of many other things, of all which he answered after the same fashion, and the holy father offering to proceed to absolution, Master Ciappelletto said, ‘Sir, I have yet sundry sins that I have not told you.’ The friar asked him what they were, and he answered, ‘I mind me that
uz: Yaxshi bir oy o'tgach, ular ular bo'lishi kerak bo'lganidan to'rt farthing ko'proq ekanligini aniqladim; shuning uchun, uni yana ko'rmay, to'liq bir yil davomida men bilan birga saqlab qolganimdan so'ng, ularni unga qaytarishim uchun sadaqa qilib yubordim." Ruhoniy dedi: "Bu kichik masala edi, va sen unga qilganingdek munosabatda bo'lishing yaxshi edi." Keyin u uni boshqa ko'p narsalar haqida so'radi, u xuddi shunday javob berdi va muqaddas ota absolyutga borishni taklif qildi, Ustoz Ciappelletto dedi: "Janob, men hali senga aytmagan turli gunohlarim bor." Ruhoniy undan so'radi: "Men buni eslayman."

en: one Saturday, after none, I caused my servant sweep out the house and had not that reverence for the Lord’s holy day which it behoved me have.’ ‘Oh,’ said the friar, ‘that is a light matter, my son.’ ‘Nay,’ rejoined Master Ciappel- letto, ‘call it not a light matter, for that the Lord’s Day is greatly to be hon- oured, seeing that on such a day our Lord rose from the dead.’ Then said the friar, ‘Well, hast thou done aught else?’ ‘Ay, sir,’ answered Master Ciappel- letto; ‘once, unthinking what I did, I spat in the church of God.’ Thereupon the friar fell a-smiling, and said, ‘My son, that is no thing to be recked of; we who are of the clergy, we spit there all day long.’ ‘And you do very ill,’ rejoined Master Ciappelletto; ‘for that there is nought which it so straitly behoveth to keep clean as the holy temple wherein is rendered sacriﬁce to God.’ Brief, he told him great plenty of
uz: Bir shanba kuni, hech kimdan keyin, men xizmatkorimga uyni supurib tashlashni buyurdim va menga kerak bo'lganidek, Egamizning muqaddas kuniga hurmatim yo'q edi." Oh, dedi rohib, bu yengil narsa, o'g'lim. Yo'q, dedi Master Ciappel- letto, bu yengil narsa demang, chunki Egamizning kuni juda ulug'lanadi, chunki shunday kunda Rabbimiz o'liklardan tirildi. Shunda rohib dedi: Xo'sh, siz boshqa narsa qildingizmi?  Ay, janob,  Ciappel- letto; Men nima qilganimni o'ylab, Xudoning cherkovida tupurdim. Shunda rohib kuldi va qisqa dedi: O'g'lim, bu narsa biz uchun juda zarur emas, chunki u juda ko'p narsani qurbonlik qiladi.

en: suchlike things and presently fell a- sighing and after weeping sore, as he knew full well to do, whenas he would.
uz: shunga o'xshash narsalar va darhol yiqildi - xo'rsindi va yig'lagandan keyin og'riq bilan, qachon qilmoqchi bo'lsa, yaxshi bilardi.

en: Quoth the holy friar, ‘What aileth thee, my son?’ ‘Alas, sir,’ replied Master Ciappelletto, ‘I have one sin left, whereof I never yet confessed me, such shame have I to tell it; and every time I call it to mind, I weep, even as you see, and meseemeth very certain that God will never pardon it me.’ ‘Go to, son,’ rejoined the friar; ‘what is this thou sayest?
uz: Muqaddas rohib aytdi: Senga nima boldi, oglim? Alas, janob, javob berdi Ustoz Ciappelletto, Menda bir gunoh qoldi, uni hali tan olmadi, aytishga uyat bor; va har safar eslasam, yiglayman, hatto korib turibsan, va Xudo meni hech qachon kechirmasligiga juda aminman.Boring, oglim, deb javob berdi rohib; Bu nima deysan?

en: If all the sins that were ever wrought or are yet to be wrought of all mankind, what while the world endureth, were all in one man and he repented him thereof and were con- trite therefor, as I see thee, such is the mercy and loving-kindness of God that, upon confession, He would freely pardon them to him.
uz: Agar butun insoniyat tomonidan qilingan yoki hali qilinadigan barcha gunohlar, dunyo azob chekayotgan bir paytda, hammasi bir insonda bo'lganida edi va u ulardan tavba qilib, uni shu gunohlardan xalos qilgan bo'lsa, men seni ko'rayotganimdek, Xudoning rahm-shafqati va mehr-muhabbati shundayki, tan olganida, U ularni bemalol unga kechiradi.

en: Wherefore do thou tell it in all assurance.’ Quoth Master Ciappelletto, still weeping sore, ‘Alack, father mine, mine is too great a sin, and I can scarce believe that it will ever be forgiven me of God, except your prayers strive for me.’ Then said the friar, ‘Tell it me in all assurance, for I promise thee to pray God for thee.’ Master Ciappelletto, however, still wept and said nought; but, after he had thus held the friar a great while in suspense, he heaved a deep sigh and said, ‘Father mine, since you promise me to pray God for me, I will e’en tell it you.
uz: Shuning uchun ham ishonch bilan ayting. Ustoz Ciappellietto, hali ham achchiq yig'lab,  Alack, otam, mening gunohim juda katta, va men Xudo meni hech qachon kechirishiga ishonmayman, agar sizning duolaringiz men uchun harakat qilmasa. Shunda friar dedi:  Menga ishonch bilan ayting, chunki men sizga Xudo uchun ibodat qilishga va'da beraman. Ustoz Ciappellietto, ammo, hali ham yig'lab, hech narsa demadi; lekin u friarni uzoq vaqt davomida xavotirda ushlab turganidan so'ng, u chuqur xo'rsindi va dedi:  Otam, siz menga Xudo uchun ibodat qilishga va'da berganingiz sababli, men sizga aytaman.

en: Know, then, that, when I was little, I once cursed my mother.’ So saying, he fell again to weeping sore.
uz: Shuni bilingki, men kichkinaligimda onamni bir marta la'natlaganman. Shunday deb, u yana yig'lab yig'ladi.

en: ‘O my son,’ quoth the friar, ‘seemeth this to thee so heinous a sin?
uz: Ey oglim,  deb soradi rohib,  senga bu shunchalik dahshatli gunohdek tuyuladimi?

en: Why, men blaspheme God all day long and He freely pardoneth whoso repenteth him of having blasphemed Him; and deemest thou not He will pardon thee this?
uz: Nega odamlar butun kun davomida Xudoga kufr so'zlaydilar va U O'ziga kufr so'zlaganidan tavba qilganlarni bemalol kechiradi; va sen buni U seni kechirmaydi deb o'ylamaysanmi?

en: Weep not, but comfort thyself; for, certes, wert thou one of those who set Him on the cross, He would par-
uz: Yig'lama, balki o'zingni ovut; chunki, albatta, sen Uni xochga mixlaganlardan eding, U seni...

en: don thee, in favour of such contrition as I see in thee.’ ‘Alack, father mine, what say you?’ replied Ciappelletto.
uz: "Men sendan ko'rgan bunday pushaymonlik tufayli senga iltijo qil." "Alak, otam, sen nima deysan?" - javob berdi Ciappelletto.

en: ‘My kind mother, who bore me nine months in her body, day and night, and carried me on her neck an hundred times and more, I did passing ill to curse her and it was an exceeding great sin; and except you pray God for me, it will not be forgiven me.’ The friar, then, seeing that Master Ciappelletto had no more to say, gave him absolution and bestowed on him his benison, holding him a very holy man and devoutly believing all that he had told him to be true.
uz: "Mening mehribon onam, meni to'qqiz oy davomida, tunu kun o'z tanasida tug'gan va yuz marta ko'proq bo'ynida ko'tarib yurgan, men uni la'natlash uchun bemor bo'ldim va bu juda katta gunoh edi; va agar siz men uchun Xudoga ibodat qilmasangiz, meni kechirmaydi." Shunday qilib, rohib, Ustoz Ciappelletto boshqa hech narsa deyishga hojat yo'qligini ko'rib, unga kechirildi va unga o'z marhamatini berdi, uni juda muqaddas odam deb ushlab turdi va u aytgan hamma narsani rost deb topdi."

en: And who would not have believed it, hearing a man at the point of death speak thus?
uz: Va o'lim arafasida bir odamning bunday gapirganini eshitganda kim ishonmagan bo'lardi?

en: Then, after all this, he said to him, ‘Master Ciappelletto, with God’s help you will speedily be whole; but, should it come to pass that God call your blessed and well-disposed soul to Himself, would it please you that your body be buried in our convent?’ ‘Ay, would it, sir,’ replied Master Ciappel- letto.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u unga dedi: Master Ciappelletto, Xudoning yordami bilan tezda sog'ayib ketasiz; lekin, agar Xudo sizning barakali va yaxshi niyatli joningizni O'ziga chaqirsa, sizning jasadingiz bizning monastirimizga dafn etilishini xohlarmidingiz? Ha, shunday bo'lardi, janob,  javob berdi Master Ciappel- lit.

en: ‘Nay, I would fain no be buried otherwhere, since you have promised to pray God for me; more by token that I have ever had a special regard for your order.
uz: Yo'q, men boshqa joyga dafn etilishni xohlamayman, chunki siz Xudo uchun ibodat qilishga va'da bergan edingiz; ayniqsa, sizning buyrug'ingizga alohida e'tibor berganim uchun.

en: Wherefore I pray you that whenas you return to your lodging, you must cause bring me that most veritable body of Christ, which you con- secrate a-mornings upon the altar, for that, with your leave, I purpose (all unworthy as I am) to take it and after, holy and extreme unction, to the in- tent that, if I have lived as a sinner, I may at the least die like a Christian.’ The good friar replied that it pleased him much and that he said well and promised to see it presently brought him; and so was it done.
uz: Shuning uchun, sizdan iltimos qilaman, turar joyiga qaytib kelganingizda, menga Masihning eng haqiqiy jasadini olib kelishingiz kerak, uni ertalab qurbongohga yashirasiz. Shuning uchun, sizning ruxsatingiz bilan men uni (men qanday bo'lsam, hammasi noqulay) olib, keyin, muqaddas va haddan tashqari muqaddaslash, chodirga olib borishni maqsad qilaman, agar men gunohkor bo'lib yashagan bo'lsam, hech bo'lmaganda xristian kabi o'laman.

en: Meanwhile, the two brothers, misdoubting them sore lest Master Ciappel- letto should play them false, had posted themselves behind a wainscot, that divided the chamber where he lay from another, and listening, easily heard and apprehended that which he said to the friar and had whiles so great a mind to laugh, hearing the things which he confessed to having done, that they were like to burst and said, one to other, ‘What manner of man is this, whom neither old age nor sickness nor fear of death, whereunto he seeth himself near, nor yet of God, before whose judgment-seat he looketh to be ere long, have availed to turn from his wickedness nor hinder him from choosing to die as he hath lived?’ However, seeing that he had so spoken that he should be admitted to burial in a church, they recked nought of the rest.
uz: Ayni paytda, ikki aka-uka, Ustoz Ciappel- letto ularni yolg'onchi deb o'ylamasligi uchun ularni qattiq shubha ostiga qo'yishdi, o'zlarini boshqa odamdan ajratadigan va tinglaydigan o'yinchoq ortiga qo'yishdi va u rohibga aytgan gapini oson eshitib, tushunishardi va u qilgan ishini tan olganini eshitib, shunday katta aqlga ega edilarki, ular bir-birlariga: "Bu qanday odam, u o'zini qarilik ham, kasallik ham, o'limdan qo'rqish ham emas, u o'zini yaqin ko'rmaydi, hali ham Xudoning oldida ko'rmaydi, u uzoq muddatga ko'rmaydi, yomonligidan yuz o'girmadi va uni tirikligida o'lishni tanlamasdan to'xtatmadi?"

en: Master Ciappelletto presently took the sacrament and, growing rapidly worse, received extreme unction, and a little after evensong of the day he had made his ﬁne confession, he died; whereupon the two brothers, having,
uz: Ustoz Ciappellletto darhol sakramentni qabul qildi va tez sur'atlar bilan yomonlashib, haddan tashqari moylashni oldi va u o'zining nozik e'tirofini aytgan kunning bir yarmidan so'ng vafot etdi; shundan so'ng ikki aka-uka,

en: of his proper monies, taken order for his honourable burial, sent to the con- vent to acquaint the friars therewith, bidding them come thither that night to hold vigil, according to usance, and fetch away the body in the morning, and meanwhile made ready all that was needful thereunto.
uz: o'zining tegishli mablag'laridan, uning sharafli dafn marosimiga buyurtma olib, ruhoniylarni u bilan tanishtirish uchun konsentrga jo'natdi, ularni o'sha kecha u yerga odatga ko'ra, uyg'oqlik o'tkazish va ertalab jasadni olib ketish uchun buyurdi va shu bilan birga u yerda zarur bo'lgan hamma narsani tayyorladi.

en: The holy friar, who had shriven him, hearing that he had departed this life, betook himself to the prior of the convent and, letting ring to chapter, gave out to the brethren therein assembled that Master Ciappelletto had been a holy man, according to that which he had gathered from his confes- sion, and persuaded them to receive his body with the utmost reverence and devotion, in the hope that God should show forth many miracles through him.
uz: Uni qisqartirgan aziz rohib, u bu hayotdan ketganini eshitib, monastir ruhoniysiga murojaat qildi va u yerdagi birodarlarga Ustoz Ciappelletto o'z iqroridan to'plagan narsalariga ko'ra muqaddas inson ekanligini aytdi va Xudo u orqali ko'plab mo'jizalar ko'rsatishiga umid qilib, uning jasadini eng katta hurmat va sadoqat bilan qabul qilishga ko'ndirdi.

en: To this the prior and brethren credulously consented and that same evening, coming all whereas Master Ciappelletto lay dead, they held high and solemn vigil over him and on the morrow, clad all in albs and copes, book in hand and crosses before them, they went, chanting the while, for his body and brought it with the utmost pomp and solemnity to their church, followed by well nigh all the people of the city, men and women.
uz: Bunga ruhoniylar va aka-ukalar ishonch bilan rozi bo'lishdi va o'sha oqshomning o'zida, Ustoz Ciappelletto o'lik holda kelganida, ular uning ustida baland va tantanali qo'riqlash marosimini o'tkazishdi va ertasi kuni, hammasini albomlar va mislar bilan kiyib, qo'lida kitoblar va xochlar bilan oldinga olib borishdi, ketib, uning jasadini maqtab, uni o'z cherkovlariga eng katta dabdaba va tantanali ravishda olib kelishdi. Shundan so'ng shaharning barcha odamlari, erkaklar va ayollar uni yaxshi kutib olishdi.

en: As soon as they had set the body down in the church, the holy friar, who had confessed him, mounted the pulpit and fell a-preaching marvellous things of the dead man and of his life, his fasts, his virginity, his simplicity and innocence and sanctity, recounting, amongst other things, that which he had confessed to him as his greatest sin and how he had hardly availed to persuade him that God would forgive it him; thence passing on to reprove the folk who hearkened, ‘And you, accursed that you are,’ quoth he, ‘for every waif of straw that stirreth between your feet, you blaspheme God and the Virgin and all the host of heaven.’ Moreover, he told them many other things of his loyalty and purity of heart; brief, with his speech, whereto en- tire faith was yielded of the people of the city, he so established the dead man in the reverent consideration of all who were present that, no sooner
uz: Ular jasadni cherkovga qo'yishlari bilanoq, uni tan olgan muqaddas rohib minbarga chiqib, o'lik odam va uning hayoti, uning ro'zalari, bokiraligi, soddaligi, beg'uborligi va muqaddasligi haqidagi ajoyib xabarlarni tarqatdi. U unga eng katta gunoh deb tan berganini va Xudo uni kechishiga ishontirishga qanchalik erisha olmaganini, "va siz, siz ekanligingizni qasam ichganingiz uchun", dedi u, "oyog'laringiz o'rtasida harakatlanayotgan har bir soyabon uchun, siz Xudoga va osmonga hamda butun qo'shinga kufr keltirdingiz."

en: was the service at an end, than they all with the utmost eagerness ﬂocked to kiss his hands and feet and the clothes were torn off his back, he holding himself blessed who might avail to have never so little thereof; and needs must they leave him thus all that day, so he might be seen and visited of all.
uz: Xizmat nihoyasiga yetganda, ularning hammasi qo'llari va oyoqlarini o'pishga juda ishtiyoq bilan yig'ilishdi va kiyimlari orqasiga yirtildi. U o'zini shunday kam narsaga ega bo'lishdan foydalanishga arziydigan baxtli deb hisoblardi; va kerak bo'lsa, uni shu kun bo'yi shunday tark etishlari kerak edi, toki u hamma ko'risin va ziyorat qilsin.

en: The following night he was honourably buried in a marble tomb in one of the chapels of the church and on the morrow the folk began incontinent to come and burn candles and offer up prayers and make vows to him and hang images of wax40 at his shrine, according to the promise made.
uz: Ertasi kuni kechasi u cherkov ibodatxonalaridan birida marmar qabrga hurmat bilan dafn etildi va ertasi kuni odamlar tinimsiz kelib sham yoqib, unga duolar aytib, qasam ichishni va uning ziyoratgohiga mumdan yasalgan 40 ta haykalni osib qo'yishni boshlashdi, bu va'da qilingan edi.

en: Nay, on such wise waxed the frame of his sanctity and men’s devotion to him that
uz: Yo'q, shunday qilib Uning muqaddasligi va odamlarning Unga sadoqat ramkasi nurlandi,

en: there was scarce any who, being in adversity, would vow himself to another saint than him; and they styled and yet style him Saint Ciappelletto and avouch that God through him hath wrought many miracles and yet worketh, them every day for whoso devoutly commendeth himself unto him.
uz: Qiyinchilikda bo'lgan hech kim o'zini undan ko'ra boshqa avliyoga qasamyod qiladigan odam kam edi; va ular uni Muqaddas Ciappelletto deb atashdi va u orqali Xudo ko'p mo'jizalar yaratganini va har kuni o'zini Unga sadoqat bilan tavsiya qilayotganlar uchun ishlayotganini aytishdi.

en: Thus, then, lived and died Master Cepperello41 da Prato and became a saint, as you have heard; nor would I deny it to be possible that he is beati- ﬁed in God’s presence, for that, albeit his life was wicked and perverse, he may at his last extremity have shown such contrition that peradventure God had mercy on him and received him into His kingdom; but, for that this is hidden from us, I reason according to that which, is apparent and say that he should rather be in the hands of the devil in perdition than in Paradise.
uz: Shunday qilib, Ustoz Cepperello41 da Prato yashadi va va vafot etdi va avliyo bo'ldi, siz eshitganingizdek; shuningdek, uning Xudoning huzurida barakali bo'lishi mumkinligini inkor etmayman, chunki, garchi uning hayoti yovuz va buzuq bo'lsa ham, u oxirgi oxirida shunday tavba ko'rsatgan bo'lishi mumkin edi, ehtimol Xudo unga rahm qildi va uni O'z Shohligiga qabul qildi; lekin, chunki bu bizdan yashirilgan, men shunga ko'ra aql yuritaman, yaqqol va aytamanki, u jannatdagidan ko'ra shaytonning qo'lida halokatda bo'lishi kerak.

en: And if so it be, we may know from this how great is God’s loving-kindness to- wards us, which, having regard not to our error, but to the purity of our faith, whenas we thus make an enemy (deeming him a friend) of His our intermediary, giveth ear unto us, even as if we had recourse unto one truly holy, as intercessor for His favour.
uz: Agar shunday bo'lsa, shundan Xudoning bizga bo'lgan mehribonligi qanchalik buyuk ekanligini bilishimiz mumkin. U bizning xatolarimizga emas, balki imonimizning pokligiga e'tibor qaratgan holda, biz Uni dushman qilib (o'z vositachimiz deb) qabul qilganimizda, bizga quloq soladi, go'yo biz Uning marhamati uchun shafoatchi sifatida chinakam muqaddas Zotga murojaat qilgan bo'lsak.

en: Wherefore, to the end that by His grace we may be preserved safe and sound in this present adversity and in this so joyous company, let us, magnifying His name, in which we have begun our diversion, and holding Him in reverence, commend ourselves to Him in our necessities, well assured of being heard.” And with this he was silent.
uz: Shunday ekan, Uning marhamati bilan biz hozirgi musibatda va shu qadar quvnoq hamrohlikda omon va sog'lom saqlanishimiz uchun, biz o'z qiziqishlarimizni boshlagan Uning ismini ulug'lab, Unga hurmat bilan murojaat qilaylik va eshitilishiga ishonch hosil qilib, o'z ehtiyojlarimizda Unga taslim bo'laylik.

en: THE SECOND STORY Abraham the Jew, at the instigation of Jehannot de Chevigné, goeth to the court of Rome and seeing the depravity of the clergy, returneth to Paris and there becometh a Christian.
uz: IKKINCHI HIKOYA Ibrohim yahudiy Jehannot de Chevignéning undovi bilan Rim saroyiga boradi va ruhoniylarning buzuqligini ko'rib, Parijga qaytib keladi va u yerda xristian bo'ladi.

en: Pamﬁlo’s story was in part laughed at and altogether commended by the ladies, and it being come to its end, after being diligently hearkened, the queen bade Neiﬁle, who sat next him, ensue the ordinance of the com- menced diversion by telling one42 of her fashion.
uz: Pamfilaning hikoyasi qisman kulgusi chiqdi va ayollar tomonidan butunlay maqtovga sazovor bo'ldi. Uning oxiriga yetgach, diqqat bilan tinglangandan so'ng, uning yonida o'tirgan qirolicha Badie Neifile o'z modasidan42 birini aytib, kom-mened diversion tartibini ta'minladi.

en: Neiﬁle, who was distin- guished no less by courteous manners than by beauty, answered blithely that she would well and began on this wise: “Pamﬁlo hath shown us in his story that God’s benignness regardeth not our errors, when they proceed from that which is beyond our ken; and I, in mine, purpose to show you how this same benignness —patiently suffering the defaults of those who, being especially bounden both with words and deeds to bear true witness thereof43 yet practise the contrary —exhibiteth unto us an infallible proof of itself, to the intent that we may, with the more constancy of mind, ensue that which we believe.
uz: Neifile, go'zallikdan kam bo'lmagan odob-axloq bilan ajralib turadigan ayol, u yaxshi deb javob berdi va shunday boshladi:  Pamfilo o'z hikoyasida Xudoning mehribonligi bizning xatolarimizga e'tibor bermasligini ko'rsatdi, qachonki ular bizning bilimimizdan tashqari bo'lsa; va men o'zimning maqsadim sizga xuddi shu mehribonlikni  ayniqsa, so'z va harakatlar bilan bog'langan bo'lib, haqiqatga guvohlik berish uchun 43 lekin aksincha amalda bo'lganlarning kamchiliklariga sabr bilan bardosh berishni  bizga o'zimizning bexato isbotini ko'rsatadi, shunday niyatda, biz ko'proq aql-idrok bilan, ishonadigan narsani ta'minlaymiz.

en: As I have heard tell, gracious ladies, there was once in Paris a great mer- chant and a very loyal and upright man, whose name was Jehannot de Chevigné and who was of great trafﬁc in silks and stuffs.
uz: Eshitganimdek, hurmatli xonimlar, Parijda bir vaqtlar juda katta "mer-sant" va juda sadoqatli va to'g'ri odam bor edi, uning ismi Jehannot de Chevigné edi va ipak va boshqa narsalar bilan katta savdoda edi.

en: He had particular friendship for a very rich Jew called Abraham, who was also a merchant and a very honest and trusty man, and seeing the latter’s worth and loyalty, it began to irk him sore that the soul of so worthy and discreet and good a man should go to perdition for default of faith; wherefore he fell to beseech- ing him on friendly wise leave the errors of the Jewish faith and turn to the Christian verity, which he might see still wax and prosper, as being holy and good, whereas his own faith, on the contrary, was manifestly on the wane
uz: Uning juda boy yahudiy Ibrohim bilan o'zgacha do'stligi bor edi, u savdogar, shuningdek, juda halol va ishonchli odam edi. Oxirgilarning qadri va sadoqatini ko'rib, unga shunchalik munosib, ehtiyotkor va yaxshi odamning imonsizlik uchun halokatga ketishi achchiqlana boshladi; shuning uchun u Yahudo dinining xatolarini do'stona yo'l bilan tark etish va xristian haqiqatga yuzlanish uchun iltimos qilishga tushdi, uni hali ham muqaddas va yaxshi deb ko'rishi mumkin, o'z dini esa, aksincha, yaqqol ko'rinardi.

en: and dwindling to nought.
uz: va nolga aylanib bormoqda.

en: The Jew made answer that he held no faith holy or good save only the Jewish, that in this latter he was born and therein meant to live and die, nor should aught ever make him remove therefrom.
uz: Yahudiy javob berdi, u faqat yahudiylardan boshqa hech qanday muqaddas yoki yaxshi e'tiqodga ega emas edi, chunki u faqat yahudiylarda tug'ilgan va u yerda yashash va o'lishga mo'ljallangan edi, va hech narsa uni undan uzoqlashtirmasligi kerak edi.

en: Jehannot for all that desisted not from him, but some days after returned to the attack with similar words, showing him, on rude enough wise (for that merchants for the most part can no better), for what reasons our reli- gion is better than the Jewish; and albeit the Jew was a past master in their law, nevertheless, whether it was the great friendship he bore Jehannot that moved him or peradventure words wrought it that the Holy Ghost put into the good simple man’s mouth, the latter’s arguments began greatly to please him; but yet, persisting in his own belief, he would not suffer himself to be converted.
uz: Jehannot undan voz kechmadi, balki bir necha kundan keyin hujumga shunga o'xshash so'zlar bilan qaytdi, unga yetarlicha qo'pol tarzda (chunki savdogarlar ko'p hollarda bundan yaxshiroq qila olmaydilar), nima uchun bizning dinimiz yahudiylardan yaxshiroq ekanligini ko'rsatdi; va garchi yahudiy ularning qonuniyatida o'tmishdagi ustasi bo'lsa ham, shunga qaramay, uni hayratga solgan Jehannotning buyuk do'stligi bo'ladimi yoki tasodifiy so'zlar Muqaddas Ruhning yaxshi oddiy odamning og'ziga solganini ko'rsatib, oxirgilarning dalillari uni juda xursand qila boshladi; ammo, o'z e'tiqodida qat'iy turib, u o'zini qabul qilishga ruxsat bermas edi.

en: Like as he abode obstinate, even so Jehannot never gave over importuning him, till at last the Jew, overcome by such continual insistence, said, ‘Look you, Jehannot, thou wouldst have me become a Christian and I am disposed to do it; insomuch, indeed, that I mean, in the ﬁrst place, to go to Rome and there see him who, thou sayest, is God’s Vicar upon earth and consider his manners and fashions and likewise those of his chief brethren.44 If these appear to me such that I may, by them, as well as by your words, apprehend that your faith is better than mine, even as thou hast studied to show me, I will do as I have said; and if it be not so, I will remain a Jew as I am.’ When Jehannot heard this, he was beyond measure chagrined and said in himself, ‘I have lost my pains, which meseemed I had right well bestowed, thinking to have converted this man; for that, an he go to the court of Rome
uz: Xuddi u qaysarlik bilan yashaganidek, Jehannot ham uni bezovta qilishni to'xtatmadi, toki nihoyat yahudiy, bunday doimiy qat'iyat bilan mag'lub bo'lib, dedi: "Mana, Jehannot, sen meni nasroniy bo'lishimni xohlaysan va men buni qilishga tayyorman; demak, men birinchi navbatda Rimga borib, u yerda sen aytgandek, Xudoning yer yuzidagi vakili bo'lgan va uning odob-axloqlari, modalari va shuningdek, uning bosh birodarlarining odob-axloqlarini hisobga olgan odamni ko'rmoqchiman." 44 Agar bular menga shunday ko'rinsa, men ular orqali ham, sening so'zlaring orqali ham, sen menga o'rgatganingdek, sening imoning mennikidan yaxshiroq ekanligini anglayman, men ham aytganimdek qilaman; va agar shunday bo'lmasa, men o'zim uchun shunday bo'lgan odamni ko'rmoqchiman, agar u yahudiy bo'lsa, u o'zimni yo'qtirgan bo'lsam, men bu...

en: and see the lewd and wicked life of the clergy, not only will he never be- come a Christian, but, were he already a Christian, he would infallibly turn Jew again.’ Then, turning to Abraham, he said to him, ‘Alack, my friend, why wilt thou undertake this travail and so great a charge as it will be to thee to go from here to Rome?
uz: va ruhoniylarning behayo va yovuz hayotini ko'rsa, nafaqat u hech qachon nasroniy bo'lmaydi, balki u allaqachon nasroniy bo'lganida, u yana yahudiy bo'lib ketardi." Keyin, Ibrohimga o'girilib, u unga dedi: "Alak, do'stim, nega bu ishni va bu kabi katta yukni bu yerdan Rimga borish senga bo'ladigan darajada yuklaysan?"

en: More by token that, both by sea and by land, the road is full of perils for a rich man such as thou art.
uz: Ko'proq shuni anglatadiki, dengiz bo'ylab ham, quruqlik bo'ylab ham, sen kabi boy odam uchun yo'l xavflarga to'la.

en: Thinkest thou not to ﬁnd here who shall give thee baptism?
uz: Sizni suvga cho'mdiradigan odamni bu yerda topa olmaysiz deb o'ylayapsizmi?

en: Or, if peradventure thou have any doubts concerning the faith which I have propounded to thee, where are there greater doctors and men more learned in the matter than are here or better able to resolve thee of that which thou wilt know or ask?
uz: Yoki, agar men senga taklif qilgan imon haqida shubhalaring bo'lsa, bu yerda bo'lganlardan ko'ra buyukroq va bilimdonroq shifokorlar yoki bilmoqchi bo'lgan yoki so'ramoqchi bo'lgan narsada seni hal qila oladigan yaxshiroq odamlar qayerda bor?

en: Wherefore, to my thinking, this thy going is superﬂuous.
uz: Shuning uchun, mening fikrimcha, sening borishing ortiqcha.

en: Bethink thee that the prelates there are even such as those thou mayst have seen here, and indeed so much the better as they are nearer unto the Chief Pastor.
uz: O'ylab ko'ring-chi, u yerdagi ruhoniylar, hatto bu yerda ko'rganlaringiz kabi, va ular Bosh Cho'ponga yaqinroq bo'lgani uchun shunchalik yaxshiroqdir.

en: Wherefore, an thou wilt
uz: Shuning uchun, va sen xohlaysan

en: be counselled by me, thou wilt reserve this travail unto another time against some jubilee or other, whereunto it may be I will bear thee company.’ To this the Jew made answer, ‘I doubt not, Jehannot, but it is as thou tellest me; but, to sum up many words in one, I am altogether determined, an thou wouldst have me do that whereof thou hast so instantly besought me, to go thither; else will I never do aught thereof.’ Jehannot, seeing his determina- tion, said, ‘Go and good luck go with thee!’ And inwardly assured that he would never become a Christian, when once he should have seen the court of Rome, but availing45 nothing in the matter, he desisted.
uz: Menga maslahat bering, bu ishni boshqa bir yilga yoki boshqa bir yilga qoldirmoqchisan, shunda men senga hamroh bo'lishim mumkin. Bunga yahudiy javob berdi: "Men shubha qilmayman, Jehannot, lekin sen aytganingdek; lekin, ko'p so'zlarni bir so'z bilan jamlash uchun, men butunlay qat'iyman, va sen meni u yerga borishimni so'raganingni qilmoqchisan; aks holda men hech qachon bunday qilmayman." Jehannot, uning qat'iyligini ko'rib, dedi: "Bor va omad senga!" Va ich-ichidan ishontirdi, u hech qachon xristian bo'lmas edi, agar u Rim sudini ko'rganida, lekin bu masalada hech narsaga erisha olmas edi.

en: The Jew mounted to horse and as quickliest he might betook himself to the court of Rome, he was honourably entertained of his brethren, and there abiding, without telling any the reason of his coming, he began diligently to enquire into the manners and fashions of the Pope and Cardinals and other prelates and of all the members of his court, and what with that which he himself noted, being a mighty quick-witted man, and that which he gathered from others, he found all, from the highest to the lowest, most shamefully given to the sin of lust, and that not only in the way of nature, but after the Sodomitical fashion, without any restraint of remorse or shamefastness, in- somuch that the interest of courtezans and catamites was of no small avail there in obtaining any considerable thing.
uz: Yahudiy otga minib, imkon qadar tezroq Rim saroyiga bordi, u o'z birodarlaridan faxr bilan xursand edi va u yerda o'z kelish sababini hech kimga aytmasdan turib, Rim Papasi, Kardinallar va boshqa prelatlar hamda uning saroyining barcha a'zolarining odob-axloqlari va uslublarini astoydil o'rganishni boshladi. O'zi ham kuchli, tezkor odam bo'lgani va boshqalardan to'plagan narsalarini, eng yuqori va eng pastdan boshlab, shahvoniy gunohga eng uyat bilan berilganini va nafaqat tabiat yo'lida, balki Sodomitar uslubda, hech qanday pushaymonasiz yoki uyatsizliksiz, hatto ularda katta foyda ko'rmaganini aniqladi.

en: Moreover, he manifestly perceived them to be universally gluttons, wine- bibbers, drunkards and slaves to their bellies, brute-beast fashion, more than to aught else after lust.
uz: Qolaversa, u ularni shahvoniy istakdan ko'ra ko'proq, butun dunyo bo'ylab ochko'z, vinoxo'r, mast va qorin qullari, qo'pol hayvonlar modasi sifatida idrok etdi.

en: And looking farther, he saw them all covetous and greedy after money, insomuch that human, nay, Christian blood, no less than things sacred, whatsoever they might be, whether pertaining to the sac- riﬁces of the altar or to the beneﬁces of the church, they sold and bought indifferently for a price, making a greater trafﬁc and having more brokers thereof than folk at Paris of silks and stuffs or whatnot else.
uz: Va uzoqroq qarasa, ularning hammasini pulga ishtiyoqmand va ochko'z ko'rdi, shunchalikki, inson, yo'q, xristian qoni, muqaddas narsalardan kam bo'lmagan narsalar, ular qanday bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, qurbongohning muqaddas narsalariga yoki cherkovning xayriyalariga tegishli bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, ular befarq ravishda narxda sotishardi va sotib olishardi, Parijda ipak va matolardan ko'ra ko'proq savdo qilishardi va ularning brokerlari bor edi.

en: Manifest si- mony they had christened ‘procuration’ and gluttony ‘sustentation,’ as if God apprehended not —let be the meaning of words but —the intention of depraved minds and would suffer Himself, after the fashion of men, to be duped by the names of things.
uz: Ular "procuration" va gluttony substance" deb suvga cho'mdirishganini ko'rsatishdi, go'yo Xudo so'zlarning ma'nosini emas, balki buzuq aqllarning niyatini anglab yetgandek va O'zini odamlarning uslubiga ko'ra narsalarning nomlari bilan aldashga majbur qilardi.

en: All this, together with much else which must be left unsaid, was supremely displeasing to the Jew, who was a sober and modest man, and himseeming he had seen enough, he determined to return to Paris and did so.
uz: Bularning barchasi, aytib o'tilmasligi kerak bo'lgan ko'p narsalar bilan birga, yahudiyga juda yoqmas edi. Yahudiy hushyor va kamtar inson edi va u yetarlicha ko'rgandek bo'lib, Parijga qaytishga qaror qildi va shunday qildi.

en: As soon as Jehannot knew of his return, he betook himself to him, hoping nothing less than that he should become a Christian, and they greeted each
uz: Jehannot o'zining qaytganini bilishi bilanoq, u unga yaqinlashdi va uning xristian bo'lishidan umidi bor edi, va ular har biriga salom berishdi.

en: other with the utmost joy.
uz: Boshqalar eng katta quvonch bilan.

en: Then, after Abraham had rested some days, Je- hannot asked him how himseemed of the Holy Father and of the cardinals and others of his court.
uz: Keyin, Ibrohim bir necha kun dam olganidan so'ng, Je- Hannot undan Muqaddas Ota, kardinallar va uning saroyidagi boshqalardan qanday ko'rinishini so'radi.

en: Whereto the Jew promptly answered, ‘Meseemeth, God give them ill one and all!
uz: Shunda yahudiy tezda javob berdi: Menga ma'lum, Xudo ularga hammaga yomonlik qilsin!

en: And I say this for that, if I was able to ob- serve aright, no piety, no devoutness, no good work or example of life or otherwhat did I see there in any who was a churchman; nay, but lust, covet- ise, gluttony and the like and worse (if worse can be) meseemed to be there in such favour with all that I hold it for a forgingplace of things diabolical rather than divine.
uz: Va men buni shunday deyapmanki, agar men to'g'ri xizmat qila olsam, hech qanday taqvodorlik, taqvodorlik, yaxshi ish yoki hayot namunasi yoki boshqa hech kimda cherkovdoshda ko'rgan narsam bo'lmas edi; yo'q, lekin shahvat, hirs, ochko'zlik va shunga o'xshash narsalar (agar undan ham yomoni bor bo'lsa) men uni ilohiy emas, balki shayton narsalarining zarbgohi deb hisoblaydigan hamma narsa bilan shunday afzallikda bo'lib tuyulmas edi.

en: And as far as I can judge, meseemeth your chief pastor and consequently all the others endeavour with all diligence and all their wit and every art to bring to nought and banish from the world the Christian religion, whereas they should be its foundation and support.
uz: Va men baholay oladiganimcha, sizning bosh ruhoniyingiz va shuning uchun qolganlarning hammasi xristian dinini dunyoga olib chiqish va haydash uchun bor kuch-g'ayratlari, aql-idroklari va san'atlari bilan harakat qilishadi, chunki ular uning asosi va tayanchi bo'lishi kerak.

en: And for that I see that this whereafter they strive cometh not to pass, but that your religion continually increaseth and waxeth still brighter and more glorious, me- seemeth I manifestly discern that the Holy Spirit is verily the foundation and support thereof, as of that which is true and holy over any other.
uz: Shunday qilib, men ularning intilishi amalga oshmayotganini, diningiz doimiy ravishda o'sib borayotganini va yanada yorqin va ulug'vor bo'layotganini ko'ryapman, demak, Muqaddas Ruh uning asosi va tayanchi ekanligi, boshqalardan ko'ra haqiqat va muqaddasroq narsa ekanligi aniq anglayman.

en: Wherefore, whereas, aforetime I abode obdurate and insensible to thine ex- hortations and would not be persuaded to embrace thy faith, I now tell thee frankly that for nothing in the world would I forbear to become a Christian.
uz: Shunday qilib, ilgari men sening oldingi ta'qiblaringga beparvo va sezgir bo'lib yashagan bo'lsam-da, sening e'tiqodingni qabul qilishga ko'ndirilmagan bo'lsam ham, endi senga ochiqchasiga aytamanki, dunyoda hech narsa uchun xristian bo'lishdan bosh tortmayman.

en: Let us, then, to church and there have me baptized, according to the rite and ordinance of your holy faith.’ Jehannot, who looked for a directly contrary conclusion to this, was the joyfullest man that might be, when he heard him speak thus, and repairing with him to our Lady’s Church of Paris, required the clergy there to give Abraham baptism.
uz: Shunday ekan, kelinglar, cherkovga boraylik va meni u yerda sizning muqaddas imoningiz marosimi va tartib-qoidasiga muvofiq suvga cho'mdiraylik.  Jehannot, bunga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qarama-qarshi xulosa izlayotgan edi, uni shunday gapirayotganini eshitib, u bilan birga Parijdagi Bibi Maryam cherkoviga kirganida, u yerdagi ruhoniylardan Ibrohimni suvga cho'mdirishni talab qilgan eng quvonchli odam edi.

en: They, hearing that the Jew himself demanded it, straight- way proceeded to baptize him, whilst Jehannot raised him from the sacred font46 and named him Giovanni.
uz: Yahudiyning o'zi buni talab qilganini eshitib, ular uni suvga cho'mdirish uchun to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yo'lga tushdilar, Jehannot esa uni muqaddas bulutdan tiriltirdi46 va unga Jovanni deb nom berdi.

en: After this, he had him thoroughly lessoned by men of great worth and learning in the tenets of our holy faith, which he speedily apprehended and thenceforward was a good man and a worthy and one of a devout life.”
uz: Shundan so'ng, u ulug'vor insonlar tomonidan bizning muqaddas imonimiz tamoyillarini yaxshilab o'rgatdi va tezda angladi, shundan so'ng u yaxshi inson, munosib va taqvodor hayotga ega bo'ldi.

en: THE THIRD STORY Melchizedek the Jew, with a story of three rings, escapeth a parlous snare set for him by Saladin.
uz: UCHINCHI HIKOYA Yahudiy Melxisedek, uch halqali hikoya bilan, Saladin tomonidan unga o'rnatilgan g'alati tuzoqdan qochadi.

en: Neiﬁle having made an end of her story, which was commended of all, Filomena, by the queen’s good pleasure, proceeded to speak thus: “The story told by Neiﬁle bringeth to my mind a parlous case the once betided a Jew; and for that, it having already been excellent well spoken both of God and of the verity of our faith, it should not henceforth be forbidden us to descend to the doings of mankind and the events that have befallen them, I will now proceed to relate to you the case aforesaid, which having heard, you will peradventure become more wary in answering the questions that may be put to you.
uz: Neifile o'zining barcha maqtovga sazovor bo'lgan hikoyasini tugatgach, Filomena, malika roziligi bilan shunday dedi: Neifile tomonidan hikoya qilingan hikoya menga bir vaqtlar yahudiy haqida gapirgan g'alati voqeani eslatadi; va shuning uchun, u allaqachon Xudo haqida ham, imonimiz haqiqati haqida ham yaxshi gapirgan bo'lsa, bundan buyon bizga insoniyat ishlari va ularga yuz bergan voqealarga kirish taqiqlanmasligi kerak, endi men sizga yuqorida aytilgan voqeani yetkazishga o'taman, uni eshitganingizdan so'ng, ehtimol, sizga qo'yiladigan savollarga javob berishda yanada ehtiyotkor bo'lasiz.

en: You must know, lovesome47 companions48 mine, that, like as folly ofttimes draweth folk forth of happy estate and casteth them into the utmost misery, even so doth good sense extricate the wise man from the greatest perils and place him in assurance and tranquillity.
uz: Siz bilishingiz kerakki, sevimli47 nafar hamrohim48 mening, xuddi ahmoqlik odamlarni baxtli holatdan olib chiqib, ularni eng katta musibatga tashlagandek, aql ham dono odamni eng katta xavflardan qutqaradi va uni ishonch va osoyishtalikka olib keladi.

en: How true it is that folly bringeth many an one from fair estate unto misery is seen by multitude of examples, with the recounting whereof we have no present concern, considering that a thousand instances thereof do every day mani- festly appear to us; but that good sense is a cause of solacement I will, as I promised, brieﬂy show you by a little story.
uz: Naqadar rostki, ahmoqlik ko'p odamni boylikdan qashshoqlikka olib kelishi ko'plab misollar bilan ko'rinadi, ularning rivoyatlari bilan bizda hozircha hech qanday tashvish yo'q, chunki ularning minglab holatlari har kuni bizga ochiq-oydin ko'rinadi; lekin bu yaxshi aql - taskin sababidir. Va'da berganimdek, men sizga qisqacha hikoya bilan ko'rsataman.

en: Saladin —whose valour was such that not only from a man of little ac- count it made him Soldan of Babylon, but gained him many victories over kings Saracen and Christian —having in divers wars and in the exercise of his extraordinary muniﬁcences expended his whole treasure and having an urgent occasion for a good sum of money nor seeing whence he might avail to have it as promptly as it behoved him, called to mind a rich Jew, by name Melchizedek, who lent at usance in Alexandria, and bethought himself that
uz: Salohiddin  uning jasorati shunday ediki, u nafaqat kichkina odamdan uni Bobil askariga aylantirdi, balki unga Saracen va Christian podshohlari ustidan ko'plab g'alabalar qozondi  turli urushlarda va o'zining favqulodda boyliklarini amalga oshirishda butun xazinasini sarflab, yaxshi miqdorda pul topish uchun shoshilinch imkoniyatiga ega bo'lib, uni o'zi xohlagancha tezda qayerdan olishni ko'rmay, Aleksandriyada qarz bergan Melxisedek ismli boy yahudiyni esladi va o'zini o'yladi.

en: this latter had the wherewithal to oblige him, and he would; but he was so miserly that he would never have done it of his freewill and Saladin was loath to use force with him; wherefore, need constraining him, he set his every wit awork to ﬁnd a means how the Jew might be brought to serve him in this and presently concluded to do him a violence coloured by some show of reason.
uz: Bu oxirgisida uni majburlash uchun vositalar bor edi va u shunday qilardi; lekin u shunchalik beparvo ediki, buni hech qachon o'z xohishi bilan qilmagan va Saladin unga kuch ishlatishga haqli emas edi; shuning uchun, uni majburlash zarurati bo'lganda, u yahudiyni unga qanday qilib xizmat qilishga olib kelish mumkinligini topish uchun bor kuchini ishga soldi va tez orada unga qandaydir aql ko'rsatmasi bilan tasvirlangan zo'ravonlik qilish haqida xulosa chiqardi.

en: Accordingly he sent for Melchizedek and receiving him familiarly, seated him by himself, then said to him, ‘Honest man, I have understood from divers persons that thou art a very learned man and deeply versed in matters of divinity; wherefore I would fain know of thee whether of the three Laws thou reputest the true, the Jewish, the Saracen or the Christian.’ The Jew, who was in truth a man of learning and understanding, perceived but too well that Saladin looked to entrap him in words, so he might fasten a quar- rel on him, and bethought himself that he could not praise any of the three more than the others without giving him the occasion he sought.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u Melxisedekni chaqirib yubordi va uni yaxshi kutib oldi, o'zi o'tirdi va unga dedi: "Ey halol inson, men turli odamlardan angladimki, sen juda bilimdon inson va ilohiy masalalarda chuqur xabardorsan; shuning uchun men seni uchta Qonundan to'g'ri deb hisoblaysanmi, yahudiymi, sarasyenmi yoki nasroniymi, bilmoqchiman." Haqiqatan ham, bilimdon va tushunchli odam bo'lgan yahudiy, Saladin uni so'zlarga qamashtirmoqchi ekanligini juda yaxshi angladi, shunda u unga qarshi bahs o'rnatishi mumkin edi va o'zi uchun uchta qonundan ko'ra ko'proq maqtov bera olmasligini o'yladi.

en: Accord- ingly, sharpening his wits, as became one who felt himself in need of an an- swer by which he might not be taken at a vantage, there speedily occurred to him that which it behoved him reply and he said, ‘My lord, the question that you propound to me is a nice one and to acquaint you with that which I think of the matter, it behoveth me tell you a little story, which you shall hear.
uz: Shunday qilib, aql-idrokini o'zgartirib, o'zini ustunlikka olib bo'lmaydigan bir g'alabaga muhtoj deb his qilgan odam kabi, unga javob berish kerak bo'lgan narsa tezda yodiga tushdi va u dedi: "Ey Rabbim, siz menga bergan savol yaxshi va men bu borada o'ylagan fikrim bilan sizni tanishtirish uchun sizga eshitadigan kichik bir hikoya aytib berishim kerak."

en: An I mistake not, I mind me to have many a time heard tell that there was once a great man and a rich, who among other very precious jewels in his treasury, had a very goodly and costly ring, whereunto being minded, for its worth and beauty, to do honour and wishing to leave it in perpetuity to his descendants, he declared that whichsoever of his sons should, at his death, be found in possession thereof, by his bequest unto him, should be recog- nized as his heir and be held of all the others in honour and reverence as chief and head.
uz: Men adashmayman, menimcha, bir vaqtlar bir buyuk va boy odam haqida ko'p eshitganman, u o'z xazinasida juda qimmatbaho javohirlar qatorida juda yaxshi va qimmatbaho uzukga ega edi. U o'z qadri va go'zalligi uchun hurmatga sazovor bo'lib, uni abadiy avlodlariga qoldirmoqchi edi. U o'z o'g'illaridan o'limida uning mulkiga ega bo'lib qolishi kerakligini, o'z vasiyatiga ko'ra o'zining vorisi sifatida tan olinishi va boshqalarning oldida hurmat va ehtiromda boshliq va boshliq bo'lishi kerakligini e'lon qilgan edi.

en: He to whom the ring was left by him held a like course with his own descendants and did even as his father had done.
uz: Undan uzuk qolgan odam o'z avlodlari bilan ham xuddi shunday yo'l tutdi va hatto otasi qilganidek qildi.

en: In brief the ring passed from hand to hand, through many generations, and came at last into the possession of a man who had three goodly and virtuous sons, all very obedient to their father wherefore he loved them all three alike.
uz: Qisqacha qilib aytganda, uzuk ko'p avlodlar davomida qo'ldan-qo'lga o'tdi va nihoyat otasiga juda itoatkor bo'lgan uchta yaxshi va fazilatli o'g'liga ega bo'lgan odamga tegishli bo'ldi, shuning uchun u ularni hammasini bir xilda sevdi.

en: The young men, knowing the usance of the ring, each for himself, desiring to be the most honoured among his folk, as best he might, besought his father, who was now an old man, to leave him the ring, whenas he came to die.
uz: Yigitlar uzukning odatini bilgan holda, har biri o'z xalqi orasida eng hurmatli bo'lishni, iloji boricha yaxshiroq bo'lishni xohlagan holda, endi keksa bo'lgan otasidan o'limga kelganda unga uzukni qoldirishni so'rashdi.

en: The worthy man, who loved them all alike and knew not himself how to choose
uz: Ular hammasini birdek sevgan va o'zi qanday tanlashni bilmagan munosib odam.

en: to which he had liefer leave the ring, bethought himself, having promised it to each, to seek to satisfy all three and privily let make by a good craftsman other two rings, which were so like unto the ﬁrst that he himself scarce knew which was the true.
uz: Unga uzukni tashlab ketishni buyurdi, deb o'yladi, har biriga va'da berib, uchalasini ham qondirishga harakat qiladi va yaxshi hunarmand tomonidan boshqa ikkita uzuk yasashga ruxsat beradi, ular birinchisidek edi, hatto o'zi ham qaysi biri haqiqiy ekanligini deyarli bilmas edi.

en: When he came to die, he secretly gave each one of his sons his ring, wherefore each of them, seeking after their father’s death, to occupy the inheritance and the honour and denying it to the others, produced his ring, in witness of his right, and the three rings being found so like unto one another that the true might not be known, the question which was the father’s very heir abode pending and yet pendeth.
uz: U o'layotganida, o'g'illarining har biriga yashirincha o'z uzugi berdi. Shuning uchun ularning har biri otasining o'limini izlab, meros va sharafni egallashni va boshqalarga inkor etishni istar ekan, o'z uzugi bilan o'z huquqini ko'rsatdi va uchta uzuk bir-biriga shunday o'xshash bo'lib chiqdiki, haqiqiy narsa ma'lum bo'lmas edi, bu savol otasining merosxo'ri bo'lgan va hali ham mavjud.

en: And so say I to you, my lord, of the three Laws to the three peoples given of God the Fath- er, whereof you question me; each people deemeth itself to have his inherit- ance, His true Law and His commandments; but of which in very deed hath them, even as of the rings, the question yet pendeth.’ Saladin perceived that the Jew had excellently well contrived to escape the snare which he had spread before his feet; wherefore he concluded to discover to him his need and see if he were willing to serve him; and so ac- cordingly he did, confessing to him that which he had it in mind to do, had he not answered him on such discreet wise.
uz: Shunday qilib, men sizga, janobim, Xudo Ota bergan uchta xalqqa berilgan uchta Qonun haqida aytaman: meni so'rayapsiz; har bir xalq o'z merosga, Uning haqiqiy Qonuniga va Uning amrlariga ega deb hisoblaydi; lekin amalda, hatto halqalar haqida ham savol hali ko'rinmayapti." Saladin yahudiy oyoqlari oldidan tarqatgan tuzoqdan qutulishni juda yaxshi o'ylab topganini angladi; shuning uchun u unga o'z ehtiyojini topishga qaror qildi va unga xizmat qilmoqchi ekanligini ko'rdi; va shunday qilib, unga o'zi qilmoqchi bo'lgan narsani tan oldi, agar u unga bunday nozik javob bermagan bo'lsa edi.

en: The Jew freely furnished him with all that he required, and the Soldan after satisﬁed him in full; moreover, he gave him very great gifts and still had him to friend and main- tained him about his own person in high and honourable estate.”
uz: Yahudiy unga kerak bo'lgan hamma narsani bemalol ta'minladi va soldan keyin uni to'liq qondirdi; bundan tashqari, u unga juda katta sovg'alar berdi va hali ham uni yuqori va sharafli maqomdagi o'z shaxsiyati haqida do'st tutdi va asosan unga g'amxo'rlik qildi.

en: THE FOURTH STORY A monk, having fallen into a sin deserving of very grievous punishment, adroitly reproaching the same fault to his abbot, quitteth himself of the penalty.
uz: TO'RTINCHI HIKOYA Bir rohib juda og'ir jazoga loyiq gunohga botgan holda, xuddi shu aybni mohirona o'z abtini ayblab, o'zini jazosidan ozod qiladi.

en: Filomena, having despatched her story, was now silent, whereupon Dioneo, who sat next her, knowing already, by the ordinance begun, that it fell to his turn to tell, proceeded, without awaiting farther commandment from the queen, to speak on this wise: “Lovesome ladies, if I have rightly apprehen- ded the intention of you all, we are here to divert ourselves with story- telling; wherefore, so but it be not done contrary to this our purpose, I hold it lawful unto each (even as our queen told us a while agone) to tell such story as he deemeth may afford most entertainment.
uz: Filomena uning hikoyasini yo'llab, endi jim edi, shundan so'ng uning yonida o'tirgan Dioneo, buyruq boshlanganidan so'ng, aytish o'z navbatida ekanligini bilgach, qirolichadan boshqa buyruq kutmasdan, shunday dedi: "Sevimli xonimlar, agar men sizlarning maqsadingizni to'g'ri anglagan bo'lsam, biz bu yerda hikoya bilan o'zimizni chalg'itmoqchimiz; shuning uchun, lekin bu bizning maqsadimizga zid bo'lmasa ham, har bir kishiga (qirolichamiz bizga biroz azob chekkanini aytganidek) o'zi ko'zi ko'proq ko'ngilxushlik qilishga haqli deb hisoblagan hikoyani aytish mumkin deb hisoblayman.

en: Accordingly having heard how, by the good counsels of Jehannot de Chevigné, Abraham had his soul saved and how Melchizedek, by his good sense, defended his riches from Saladin’s ambushes, I purpose, without looking for reprehension from you, brieﬂy to relate with what address a monk delivered his body from a very grievous punishment.
uz: Shunday qilib, Jehannot de Chevignéning yaxshi maslahatlari bilan Ibrohimning joni qanday qutqarilganini va Melxisedek o'zining oq aqli bilan o'z boyliklarini Saladinning tuzoqlaridan qanday himoya qilganini eshitganimdan so'ng, sizdan tanbeh izlamasdan, rohibning o'z tanasini juda og'ir jazolardan qanday qutqarganini qisqacha aytib o'tmoqchiman.

en: There was in Lunigiana, a country not very far hence, a monastery whilere more abounding in sanctity and monks than it is nowadays, and therein, among others, was a young monk, whose vigour and lustiness neither fasts nor vigils availed to mortify.
uz: Lunigyanada, unchalik uzoqda bo'lmagan mamlakatda, hozirgidan ko'ra muqaddaslik va rohiblarga boyroq monastir bor edi va u yerda, boshqa narsalar qatorida, yosh rohib bor edi, uning kuch-quvvat va shahvoniyligi na ro'za tutishga, na uyg'oqlikka yordam berardi.

en: It chanced one day, towards noon- tide, when all the other monks slept, that, as he went all alone round about the convent,49 which stood in a very solitary place, he espied a very well- favoured lass, belike some husbandman’s daughter of the country, who went about the ﬁelds culling certain herbs, and no sooner had he set eyes on her than he was violently assailed by carnal appetite.
uz: Bir kuni, tush payti yaqinida, qolgan rohiblar hammasi uxlab yotganida, u monastir atrofida yolg'iz aylanib yurganida, 49 juda yolg'iz joyda turganida, u juda yaxshi ko'rilgan bir qizni kuzatdi, go'yo qishloqning bir dehqon qizi kabi, u dalalarda ma'lum o'tlarni terib yurgan edi va u unga ko'z tashlaganidan ko'p o'tmay, u shahvoniy ishtaha bilan hujumga uchradi.

en: Wherefore, accosting her, he entered into parley with her and so led on from one thing to another
uz: Shuning uchun, uni quchoqlab, u bilan birga majlisga kirdi va shu tariqa bir narsadan ikkinchisiga olib bordi.

en: that he came to an accord with her and brought her to his cell, unperceived of any; but whilst, carried away by overmuch ardour, he disported himself with her less cautiously than was prudent, it chanced that the abbot arose from sleep and softly passing by the monk’s cell, heard the racket that the twain made together; whereupon he came stealthily up to the door to listen, that he might the better recognize the voices, and manifestly perceiving that there was a woman in the cell, was at ﬁrst minded to cause open to him, but after bethought himself to hold another course in the matter and, returning to his chamber, awaited the monk’s coming forth.
uz: U unga rozi bo'ldi va uni hech kim sezmasdan o'z hujrasiga olib keldi; lekin, haddan tashqari g'ayratga berilib, u ehtiyot bo'lmaganda, u bilan bahslashdi. Shunday bo'ldiki, abbot uyqudan turib, rohibning hujrasi yonidan sekin o'tib, Twain birgalikda qilgan shovqinni eshitdi; shundan so'ng u eshikga jim kelib, ovozlarni yaxshiroq taniydi va xonada ayol borligini aniq sezdi, avvaliga unga ochish niyatida edi, lekin keyin o'zini bu masalada boshqa yo'l tutishga o'yladi va o'z xonasiga qaytib, rohibni kutdi.

en: The latter, all taken up as he was with the wench and his exceeding pleas- ure and delight in her company, was none the less on his guard and him- seeming he heard some scufﬂing of feet in the dormitory, he set his eye to a crevice and plainly saw the abbot stand hearkening unto him; whereby he understood but too well that the latter must have gotten wind of the wench’s presence in his cell and knowing that sore punishment would ensue to him thereof, he was beyond measure chagrined.
uz: Oxirgisi, u kampir bilan birga bo'lgani va uning kompaniyasidagi haddan tashqari iltijo va quvonchi bilan birga, ham xuddi shunday hushyor edi va u - yotoqxonada oyoqlarning biroz urilishini eshitgandek, ko'zini yoriqga qaratdi va yaqqol qilib abbotning unga quloq solayotganini ko'rdi; shu bilan u kampirning xonasida bo'lganidan xabar topganini va azobli jazo unga kelib chiqishini bilganini juda yaxshi tushundi, shuning uchun u haddan tashqari g'azabda edi.

en: However, without discovering aught of his concern to the girl, he hastily revolved many things in himself, seeking to ﬁnd some means of escape, and presently hit upon a rare device, which went straight to the mark he aimed at.
uz: Biroq, u qizga hech qanday tashvish sezmasdan, shoshilinch ravishda o'zida ko'p narsalarni aylantirib, qandaydir qochish yo'lini topishga harakat qildi va shu zahotiyoq noyob qurilmaga duch keldi, u to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'z nishoniga yetdi.

en: Accordingly, making a show of thinking he had abidden long enough with the damsel, he said to her, ‘I must go cast about for a means how thou mayest win forth hence, without being seen; wherefore do thou abide quietly until my return.’ Then, going forth and locking the cell door on her, he betook himself straight to the abbot’s chamber and presenting him with the key, according as each monk did, whenas he went abroad, said to him, with a good coun- tenance, ‘Sir, I was unable to make an end this morning of bringing off all the faggots I had cut; wherefore with your leave I will presently go to the wood and fetch them away.’ The abbot, deeming the monk unaware that he had been seen of him, was glad of such an opportunity to inform himself more fully of the offence committed by him and accordingly took the key and gave him the leave he sought.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u qiz bilan yetarlicha uzoq yashiringanini ko'rsatib, u unga dedi: "Men bu yerdan qanday g'alaba qozonish uchun bir yo'l topib, ko'rinmay yurishim kerak; shuning uchun men qaytgunimcha jim turing." Keyin, chiqib, xonadagi eshikni qulflab, u to'g'ridan-to'g'ri abbotning xonasiga bordi va unga kalitni taqdim etdi. Har bir rohib, chet elga ketayotganda, unga yaxshi niyat bilan dedi: "Janob, men bugun ertalab kesilgan barcha teshiklarni olib kelishga qodir emasman; shuning uchun sizning ruxsatingiz bilan men o'rmonga borib, ularni olib ketaman." Ruhoniy, o'zini ko'rganidan bexabar deb hisoblab, uni to'liq xabardor qilish imkoniyatiga ega bo'ldi va unga...

en: Then, as soon as he saw him gone, he fell to considering which he should rather do, whether open his cell in the pres- ence of all the other monks and cause them to see his default, so they might after have no occasion to murmur against himself, whenas he should punish the offender, or seek ﬁrst to learn from the girl herself how the thing had passed; and bethinking himself that she might perchance be the wife or daughter of such a man that he would be loath to have done her the shame
uz: Keyin, uni ketayotganini ko'rishi bilanoq, u o'zi nima qilishni afzal ko'rishi kerakligini o'ylashga tushdi: barcha boshqa rohiblar oldida o'z xonasini ochib, ularga o'z kamchiliklarini ko'rsatishi kerakmi, shunda ular o'ziga qarshi pichirlash uchun hech qanday sababga ega bo'lmasliklari kerak edi, chunki u jinoyatchini jazolashi kerak edi, yoki avval qizning o'zidan nima sodir bo'lganini o'rganish kerak edi; va o'zini shunday odamning xotini yoki qizi bo'lishi mumkinligini o'ylab, u unga bunday qilmoqchi edi.

en: of showing her to all the monks, he determined ﬁrst to see her and after come to a conclusion; wherefore, betaking himself to the cell, he opened it and, entering, shut the door after him.
uz: Uni barcha rohiblarga ko'rsatgandan so'ng, avval uni ko'rishga qaror qildi, keyin xulosaga keldi; shuning uchun, o'zini xonada ko'rsatib, uni ochdi va kirib, eshikni undan keyin yopdi.

en: The girl, seeing the abbot enter, was all aghast and fell a-weeping for fear of shame; but my lord abbot, casting his eyes upon her and seeing her young and handsome, old as he was, suddenly felt the pricks of the ﬂesh no less importunate than his young monk had done and fell a-saying in him- self, ‘Marry, why should I not take somewhat of pleasure, whenas I may, more by token that displeasance and annoy are still at hand, whenever I have a mind to them?
uz: Qiz abbotning kirganini ko'rib, butunlay hayratga tushdi va uyatdan yig'lab yubordi; lekin mening janob abdomat unga ko'zini tashlab, uning yosh va chiroyli, keksaligini ko'rib, birdan yosh rohibidan kam bo'lmagan go'sht teshiklarini his qildi va o'ziga dedi: "Marry, nega men biroz zavq olmasligim kerak, agar men xohlasam, ko'proq norozilik va g'azab hali ham yaqin, qachonki men ularga bo'lsa?"

en: This is a handsome wench and is here unknown of any in the world.
uz: Bu chiroyli qiz va bu yerda dunyodagi hech kimga ma'lum emas.

en: If I can bring her to do my pleasure, I know not why I should not do it.
uz: Agar uni o'z xohishimga ko'ra o'ziga jalb qila olsam, nega bunday qilmasligim kerakligini bilmayman.

en: No one will ever know it and a sin that’s hidden is half forgiven.
uz: Hech kim buni hech qachon bilmaydi va yashirin gunoh yarim kechiriladi.

en: Maybe this chance will never occur again.
uz: Balki bu imkoniyat boshqa hech qachon takrorlanmasdir.

en: I hold it great sense to avail ourselves of a good, whenas God the Lord sende- th us thereof.’ So saying and having altogether changed purpose from that wherewith he came, he drew near to the girl and began gently to comfort her, praying her not to weep, and passing from one word to another, he ended by discover- ing to her his desire.
uz: "Men yaxshilikdan foyda olish uchun juda katta ma'noga egaman, chunki Xudo Egam bizga uni yuboradi." Shunday qilib, u kelgan narsadan butunlay o'zgarib, qizga yaqinlashdi va uni sekinlik bilan yupata boshladi, yig'lamasligini so'radi va bir so'zdan ikkinchisiga o'tib, oxirida o'z xohishini unga oshkor qildi."

en: The girl, who was neither iron nor adamant, readily enough lent herself to the pleasure of the abbot, who, after he had clipped and kissed her again and again, mounted upon the monk’s pallet and having belike regard to the grave burden of his dignity and the girl’s tender age and fearful of irking her for overmuch heaviness, bestrode not her breast, but set her upon his own and so a great while disported himself with her.
uz: Qiz, na temir edi, na soxta, o'zini bemalol abbotning roziligiga bag'ishladi. Abbot uni qayta-qayta qirqib, o'pgandan so'ng, rohibning palletiga o'tirdi va o'z qadr-qimmatining og'ir yukini, qizning mayin yoshini va uni ortiqcha og'irlik uchun bezovta qilishdan qo'rqib, uni ko'kragini buzmadi, balki o'ziga qo'ydi va shunday qilib, o'zini u bilan juda yaxshi vaqt o'tkazdi.

en: Meanwhile, the monk, who had only made believe to go to the wood and had hidden himself in the dormitory, was altogether reassured, whenas he saw the abbot enter his cell alone, doubting not but his device should have effect, and when he saw him lock the door from within, he held it for cer- tain.
uz: Ayni paytda, o'rmonga borishga ishongan va yotoqxonada yashiringan rohib, abbotning xonasiga yolg'iz kirganini ko'rib, uning qurilmasi ta'sir qilishi kerakligiga shubha qilmay, butunlay xotirjam edi va uni ichkaridan eshikni qulflaganini ko'rgach, uni mahkam ushladi.

en: Accordingly, coming forth of his hiding-place, he stealthily betook himself to a crevice, through which he both heard and saw all that the abbot did and said.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, yashirin joydan chiqib, u o'zini yashirincha yoriqqa botirdi, u orqali u abbotning qilgan va aytgan hamma narsani eshitdi va ko'rdi.

en: When it seemed to the latter that he had tarried long enough with the damsel, he locked her in the cell and returned to his own chamber, whence, after awhile, he heard the monk stirring and deeming him returned from the wood, thought to rebuke him severely and cast him into prison, so himself might alone possess the prey he had gotten; wherefore, sending for him, he very grievously rebuked him and with a stern countenance and commanded that he should be put in prison.
uz: Oxirgisi qiz bilan yetarlicha uzoq qolganiga o'xshab qolgach, u uni xonada qamab, o'z xonasiga qaytdi. Shundan so'ng, bir oz vaqt o'tgach, rohibning harakatlanayotganini eshitdi va uni o'rmondan qaytib kelgan deb hisobladi. Uni qattiq tanbeh berib, qamoqqa tashlashni o'yladi, toki o'zi olgan o'ljasiga ega bo'lsin; shuning uchun uni yuborib, juda qattiq tanbeh berdi va qattiq yuz bilan qamoqqa tashlashni buyurdi.

en: The monk very readily answered, ‘Sir, I have not yet pertained long enough to the order of St.
uz: Rohib juda bemalol javob berdi: Janob, men hali Avliyolik buyrug'iga yetarlicha uzoq vaqt ega bo'lmadim.

en: Benedict to have been able to learn every particu- lar thereof, and you had not yet shown me that monks should make of wo- men a means of mortiﬁcation,50 as of fasts and vigils; but, now that you have shown it me, I promise you, so you will pardon me this default, never again to offend therein, but still to do as I have seen you do.’ The abbot, who was a quick-witted man, readily understood that the monk not only knew more than himself, but had seen what he did; wherefore, his con- science pricking him for his own default, he was ashamed to inﬂict on the monk a punishment which he himself had merited even as he.
uz: Benedikt ularning har bir qismini o'rgangan bo'lishi kerak edi, va siz menga rohiblar odamlarni o'ldirish vositasi qilishlari kerakligini hali ko'rsatmagan edingiz, 50 ro'za va hushyorlik kabi; lekin, endi buni menga ko'rsatib berganingizdan so'ng, sizga va'da beraman, meni bu kamchilikni kechirasiz, hech qachon bu yerda xafa bo'lmaysiz, lekin baribir men ko'rganingizni qilasiz." Tezkor odam bo'lgan abbat, rohib nafaqat o'zidan ko'proq narsani bilardi, balki nima qilganini ham ko'rgan edi, shuning uchun, o'z kamchiligi uchun uni urganidan, u rohibga o'zi ham haqli bo'lgan jazosini qo'llashdan uyaldi.

en: Accordingly, pardoning him and charging him keep silence of that which he had seen, they privily put the girl out of doors and it is believed that they caused her return thither more than once thereafterward.”
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uni kechirib, ko'rgan narsalariga nisbatan sukut saqlashni ayblab, ular qizni yashirincha eshiklardan tashqariga chiqarib yuborishdi va shunga ishonish mumkinki, ular uning orqaga bir necha marta qaytib kelishiga sabab bo'lishdi.

en: THE FIFTH STORY The Marchioness of Monferrato, with a dinner of hens and certain sprightly words, curbeth the extravagant passion of the King of France.
uz: BESHINCHI HIKOYA Monferrato marchisi, tovuqlardan iborat kechki ovqat va ba'zi yorqin so'zlar bilan, Fransiya qirolining dabdabali ehtirosini cheklaydi.

en: The story told by Dioneo at ﬁrst pricked the hearts of the listening ladies with somewhat of shamefastness, whereof a modest redness appearing in their faces gave token; but after, looking one at other and being scarce able to keep their countenance, they listened, laughing in their sleeves.
uz: Dioneo tomonidan aytilgan hikoya dastlab tinglayotgan ayollarning yuragini biroz uyatchilik bilan teshdi, ularning yuzlarida kamtarona qizarish paydo bo'lishiga ishora qildi; lekin keyin bir-biriga qarab, yuzlarini saqlab qolishga qodir bo'lmagani uchun, ular yenglarida kulgan holda tinglashdi.

en: The end thereof being come, after they had gently chidden him, giving him to under- stand that such tales were not ﬁt to be told among ladies, the queen, turning to Fiammetta, who sat next him on the grass, bade her follow on the ordin- ance.
uz: Uning oxiri kelgach, ular uni muloyimlik bilan sabr-toqat qilib, bu kabi hikoyalar xonimlar orasida aytib berishga yaroqsizligini tasdiqlab, malika unga o't ustida yonida o'tirgan Fiammettaga murojaat qilib, unga buyruq bo'yicha ergashishni buyurdi.

en: Accordingly, she began with a good grace and a cheerful countenance, “It hath occurred to my mind, fair my ladies —at once because it pleaseth me that we have entered upon showing by stories how great is the efﬁcacy of prompt and goodly answers and because, like as in men it is great good sense to seek still to love a lady of higher lineage than themselves,51 so in women it is great discretion to know how to keep themselves from being taken with the love of men of greater condition than they —to set forth to you, in the story which it falleth to me to tell, how both with deeds and words a noble lady guarded herself against this and diverted another therefrom.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u yaxshi inoyat va quvnoq yuz bilan boshladi: Mening xayolimga keldi, xonimlar  darhol, chunki biz tezkor va yaxshi javoblarning qanchalik katta samaradorligini hikoyalar orqali ko'rsatib berganimiz meni xursand qiladi va chunki, erkaklarda o'zidan yuqori naslga ega bo'lgan xonimni sevishni istash juda oqilona bo'lgani kabi, 51 ayollarda ham o'zlarini undan ham yuqori darajadagi erkaklarning mehriga tortilishdan qanday saqlashni bilish juda oqilonadir  sizga aytib berish uchun, menga vazifasi kelgan hikoyani, qanday qilib bir olijanob xonim o'zini bu narsadan himoya qildi va undan boshqa bir kishini yo'naltirdi.

en: The Marquis of Monferrato, a man of high worth and gonfalonier52 of the church, had passed beyond seas on the occasion of a general crusade under- taken by the Christians, arms in hand, and it being one day discoursed of his merit at the court of King Phillippe le Borgne,53 who was then making ready to depart France upon the same crusade, it was avouched by a gentle- man present that there was not under the stars a couple to match with the marquis and his lady, for that, even as he was renowned among knights for
uz: Monferrato markizi, yuqori martabali inson va cherkovning g'amxo'r 52-odami, xristianlar tomonidan qo'lda qurol bilan qabul qilingan umumiy xoch yurishi munosabati bilan dengizlardan o'tib ketgan edi va bir kuni u qirol Filipppe le Borgne saroyida o'z merosi haqida gapirgan edi. 53 o'sha paytda u Fransiyani shu xoch yurishida tark etishga tayyor edi.

en: every virtue, so was she the fairest and noblest of all the ladies in the world.
uz: Har bir fazilatga ko'ra, u dunyodagi barcha ayollarning eng go'zali va olijanobisi edi.

en: These words took such hold upon the mind of the King of France that, without having seen the marchioness, he fell of a sudden ardently in love with her and determined to take ship for the crusade, on which he was to go, no otherwhere than at Genoa, in order that, journeying thither by land, he might have an honourable occasion of visiting the marchioness, doubting not but that, the marquis being absent, he might avail to give effect to his desire.
uz: Bu so'zlar Fransiya qirolining ongiga shunday ta'sir ko'rsatdiki, u markizani ko'rmasdan turib, birdaniga uni juda qattiq sevib qoldi va Genuadan boshqa joyga boradigan kruiz safariga kema olib borishga qaror qildi, shunda u yerga quruqlik orqali sayohat qilib, markizani ziyorat qilish sharafiga ega bo'lishi mumkin edi, lekin shubhalanmadi, lekin markiz yo'qligida u o'z xohishlariga erishishga qodir bo'lardi.

en: As he had bethought himself, so he put his thought into execution; for, having sent forward all his power, he set out, attended only by some few gentlemen, and coming within a day’s journey of the marquis’s domains, despatched a vauntcourier to bid the lady expect him the following morning to dinner.
uz: O'zi o'ylaganidek, u o'z fikrini amalga oshirdi; chunki, bor kuchini ishga solib, u yo'lga chiqdi, faqat bir necha janoblar ishtirok etdi va bir kunlik markiz yurti bo'ylab kelgach, ertalab ertalab uni kechki ovqatga kutish uchun xonimga xabar yubordi.

en: The marchioness, who was well advised and discreet, replied blithely that in this he did her the greatest of favours and that he would be welcome and after bethought herself what this might mean that such a king should come to visit her in her husband’s absence, nor was she deceived in the conclusion to which she came, to wit, that the report of her beauty drew him thither.
uz: Maritsa, yaxshi maslahatli va ehtiyotkor bo'lgan, unga shu bilan eng katta marhamat ko'rsatganini va u xush kelibsiz bo'lishini aytdi, so'ngra erining yo'qligida bunday shoh uning oldiga kelishi nimani anglatishi mumkinligini o'ylab ko'rdi, shuningdek, uning go'zalligi haqidagi xabar uni o'sha yerga jalb qilgan degan xulosasiga ham aldanib qolmadi.
