U yerda, bir kichik mehmonxonaga duch kelib, yaxshi bir beva odam tomonidan saqlangan holda, u yerda o'z uyini oldi va bechora ziyoratchining uslubida, xo'jayinidan xabar eshitishga sabrsizlik bilan yashadi.

en: It befell, then, that on the morrow of her arrival she saw Bertrand pass before her lodging, a-horseback with his company, and albeit she knew him full well, natheless she asked the good woman of the inn who he was.
uz: Shunday qilib, u kelgan kundan ertasi kuni Bertrand uning mehmonxonasi oldida, otda o'zi bilan birga o'tayotganini ko'rdi va garchi uni yaxshi bilgan bo'lsa ham, mehmonxonaning yaxshi ayolidan u kimligini so'radi.

en: The hostess answered, ‘That is a stranger gentleman, who calleth himself Count Bertrand, a pleasant man and a courteous and much loved in this city; and he is the most enamoured man in the world of a she-neighbour of ours, who is a gentlewoman, but poor.
uz: Xonim javob berdi: Bu notanish janob, u ozini graf Bertrand deb ataydi, bu shaharda yoqimli, odobli va juda sevilgan odam; va u bizning qoshnimizning dunyodagi eng oshiq odamidir, u muloyim ayol, lekin kambagal.

en: Sooth to say, she is a very virtuous damsel and abideth, being yet unmarried for poverty, with her mother, a very good and discreet lady, but for whom, maybe, she had already done the count’s pleas- ure.’ The countess took good note of what she heard and having more closely enquired into every particular and apprehended all aright, determ- ined in herself how she should do.
uz: Aytish mumkinki, u juda fazilatli qiz va hali kambag'allik uchun turmushga chiqmagan holda, onasi bilan yashaydi, juda yaxshi va ehtiyotkor ayol, lekin u uchun, ehtimol, u allaqachon grafning iltijolarini qilgan edi. Grafin eshitgan narsalariga yaxshi e'tibor qaratdi va har bir detalni yanada yaqindan o'rganib, hamma narsani to'g'ri tushundi, o'zida qanday qilish kerakligini aniqladi.

en: Accordingly, having learned the house and name of the lady whose daughter the count loved, she one day repaired privily thither in her pil- grim’s habit and ﬁnding the mother and daughter in very poor case, saluted them and told the former that, an it pleased her, she would fain speak with her alone.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, graf qizi sevuvchi xonimning uyi va ismini bilgach, u bir kuni o'z odatida o'sha yerga kirib, onasi va qizini juda kambag'al holatda topdi, ularga salom berdi va birinchisiga aytdi: "U unga yoqqanidan, u bilan yolg'iz gaplashishni xohlardi".

en: The gentlewoman, rising, replied that she was ready to hearken to her and accordingly carried her into a chamber of hers, where they seated themselves and the countess began thus, ‘Madam, meseemeth you are of the enemies of Fortune, even as I am; but, an you will, belike you may be able to relieve both yourself and me.’ The lady answered that she desired nothing better than to relieve herself by any honest means; and the countess went on, ‘Needs must you pledge me your faith, whereto an I commit myself and you deceive me, you will mar your own affairs and mine.’ ‘Tell me anything you will in all assurance,’ replied the gentlewoman; ‘for never shall you ﬁnd yourself deceived of me.’
uz: Janob ayol o'rnidan turib, unga quloq solishga tayyorligini aytdi va shunga ko'ra uni o'z xonasiga olib kirdi. Ular o'tirishdi va grafin shunday dedi: "Xonim, menimcha, siz omad dushmanlaridan biriz, xuddi men kabi; lekin, siz ham o'zingizni, ham meni tinchlantira olasiz." Janob ayol javob berdi: "O'zini har qanday halol yo'l bilan tinchlantirishdan yaxshiroq narsa xohlamadi; va grafin davom etdi: "Siz menga o'z imoningizni va'zingizga ishonishingiz kerak, men o'zimni va siz meni aldasangiz, siz o'z ishlaringizni va o'zimnikini yo'q qilasiz." "Menga hech qachon o'zingizni aldamaysiz."

en: Thereupon the countess, beginning with her ﬁrst enamourment, recoun- ted to her who she was and all that had betided her to that day after such a fashion that the gentlewoman, putting faith in her words and having, in- deed, already in part heard her story from others, began to have compassion of her.
uz: Shundan so'ng, grafess birinchi muhabbatidan boshlab, o'zining kimligini va o'sha kungacha unga shunday ta'sir ko'rsatgan barcha narsalarini shunday hikoya qildi, shundayki, janob ayol uning so'zlariga ishonib, amalda uning hikoyasini boshqalardan eshitganidan so'ng, unga rahm qila boshladi.

en: The countess, having related her adventures, went on to say, ‘You have now, amongst my other troubles, heard what are the two things which it behoveth me have, an I would have my husband, and to which I know none who can help me, save only yourself, if that be true which I hear, to wit, that the count my husband is passionately enamoured of your daughter.’ ‘Madam,’ answered the gentlewoman, ‘if the count love my daughter I know not; indeed he maketh a great show thereof.
uz: Grafin o'z sarguzashtlarini aytib berib, davom etdi: Endi siz, boshqa tashvishlarim orasida, menga kerak bo'lgan ikkita narsani eshitdingiz, men erim bo'lishini xohlardim va menga yordam bera oladigan hech kimni bilmayman, faqat o'zingizdan boshqa hech kimni bilmayman, agar eshitganim rost bo'lsa, ya'ni, mening erim sizning qizingizga ishtiyoq bilan oshiq ekan. Xonim,  javob berdi janob ayol,  agar graf qizimni sevsa, bilmayman; haqiqatan ham, u bunga katta ishora qiladi.

en: But, an it be so, what can I do in this that you desire?’ ‘Madam,’ rejoined the countess, ‘I will tell you; but ﬁrst I will e’en show you what I purpose shall ensue thereof to you, an you serve me.
uz: Lekin, agar shunday bo'lsa, siz xohlagan ishda nima qilsam bo'ladi? Xonim,  deb javob berdi grafin, Men sizga aytaman; lekin avval sizga bundan kelib chiqadigan maqsadimni ko'rsataman, chunki siz menga xizmat qilasiz.

en: I see your daughter fair and of age for a husband and accord- ing to what I have heard, meseemeth I understand the lack of good to marry her withal it is that causeth you keep her at home.
uz: Men sizning qizingizni chiroyli va erga mos yoshda ko'ryapman va eshitganlarimga mos kelayotgandek, unga turmushga chiqishning yomonligini tushunaman, chunki bu uni uyda saqlashingizga sabab bo'ladi.

en: Now I purpose, in requit- al of the service you shall do me, to give her forthright of mine own monies such a dowry as you yourself shall deem necessary to marry her honorably.’ The mother, being needy, was pleased with the offer; algates, having the spirit of a gentlewoman, she said, ‘Madam, tell me what I can do for you; if it consist with my honour, I will willingly do it, and you shall after do that which shall please you.’ Then said the countess, ‘It behoveth me that you let tell the count my husband by some one in whom you trust, that your daugh- ter is ready to do his every pleasure, so she may but be certiﬁed that he loveth her as he pretendeth, the which she will never believe, except he send her the ring which he carrieth on his ﬁnger and by which she hath heard he setteth such store.
uz: Endi siz menga qilgan xizmatingiz evaziga, unga o'zingiz munosib tarzda turmushga chiqish uchun zarur deb hisoblagan miqdorda bevosita o'z mablag'imdan berishingizni niyat qilaman. Ona, muhtoj bo'lgani uchun, taklifdan mamnun bo'ldi va aytdi: "Xonim, men siz uchun nima qila olaman; agar bu mening hurmatimga mos kelsa, men buni ixtiyoriy ravishda qilaman va siz sizga yoqqan ishni qilasiz." Shunda graf aytdi: "Siz menga erimga siz ishonadigan odamdan aytishingiz kerak, qizingiz uning xohishidek ish qilishga tayyor, shunda u uni sevadi, lekin u uni hech qachon eshitmaydi, faqat u uni o'zi ushlab turgan barmog'iga yuboradi."

en: An he send you the ring, you must give it to me and after send to him to say that your daughter is ready do his pleasure; then bring him hither in secret and privily put me to bed to him in the stead of your daughter.
uz: Agar u senga uzuk yuborsa, uni menga berishing kerak va keyin unga aytishing kerakki, qizing o'z xohishlarini bajarishga tayyor; so'ngra uni bu yerga yashirincha olib keling va meni qizingiz o'rniga unga yashirincha yotqizing.

en: It may be God will vouchsafe me to conceive and on this wise, having his ring on my ﬁnger and a child in mine arms of him begot- ten, I shall presently regain him and abide with him, as a wife should abide with her husband, and you will have been the cause thereof.’ This seemed a grave matter to the gentlewoman, who feared lest blame should haply ensue thereof to her daughter; nevertheless, bethinking her it were honourably done to help the poor lady recover her husband and that she went about to do this to a worthy end and trusting in the good and hon-
uz: Ehtimol, Xudo menga homilador bo'lish imkonini beradi va shu yo'l bilan, barmog'imda uzugi bor va uning qo'lida farzandim bor - o'n, men uni tezda qaytarib olib, unga qolaman, xuddi xotin erida qolishi kerak bo'lganidek, va siz bunga sabab bo'lgan bo'lardingiz.

en: est intention of the countess, she not only promised her to do it, but, before many days, dealing with prudence and secrecy, in accordance with the lat- ter’s instructions, she both got the ring (albeit this seemed somewhat griev- ous to the count) and adroitly put her to bed with her husband, in the place of her own daughter.
uz: Grafinaning niyati shu edi, u nafaqat buni qilishga va'da berdi, balki ko'p kunlardan oldin, ehtiyotkorlik va maxfiylik bilan shug'ullanib, oxirgi ko'rsatmalarga muvofiq, u ham uzukni oldi (garchi bu graf uchun biroz achinarli tuyulgan bo'lsa ham) va uni o'z qizi o'rniga, mohirona eriga yotqizdi.

en: In these ﬁrst embracements, most ardently sought of the count, the lady, by God’s pleasure, became with child of two sons, as her delivery in due time made manifest.
uz: Ushbu birinchi quchoqlarda, grafdan eng ko'p izlangan holda, xonim Xudoning marhamati bilan ikki o'g'il farzand ko'rdi, uning o'z vaqtida tug'ilishi namoyon bo'ldi.

en: Nor once only, but many times, did the gentlewoman gratify the countess with her husband’s embraces, contriv- ing so secretly that never was a word known of the matter, whilst the count still believed himself to have been, not with his wife, but with her whom he loved; and whenas he came to take leave of a morning, he gave her, at one time and another, divers goodly and precious jewels, which the countess laid up with all diligence.
uz: Na bir marta, balki ko'p marta, janob ayol grafini erining quchoqlari bilan xursand qildi, shu qadar yashirincha, bu haqda hech qachon xabar bo'lmadi, garchi graf hali ham o'zini xotin bilan emas, balki sevuvchi ayol bilan birga deb hisoblardi; va bir ertalab u bilan ketishga kelganda, u unga vaqti-vaqti bilan turli xil yaxshi va qimmatbaho javohirlar berdi, ularni graf butun mehnat bilan tayyorladi.

en: Then, feeling herself with child and unwilling to burden the gentlewoman farther with such an ofﬁce, she said to her, ‘Madam, thanks to God and you, I have gotten that which I desired, wherefore it is time that I do that which shall content you and after get me gone hence.’ The gentlewoman answered that, if she had gotten that which contented her, she was well pleased, but that she had not done this of any hope of reward, nay, for that herseemed it behoved her to do it, an she would do well.
uz: Keyin, o'zini farzandli his qilib va janob ayolga bunday lavozimni yanada yuklashni istamagan holda, u unga dedi: "Xonim, Xudoga va sizga rahmat, men xohlagan narsamni oldim, shuning uchun sizni qoniqtiradigan narsani qilish vaqti keldi va keyin meni bu yerdan olib keting." Janob ayol javob berdi: "Agar u o'zini qoniqtiradigan narsani olgan bo'lsa, u xursand edi, lekin buni mukofotga umid qilmagan edi, yo'q, chunki u buni qilishga majbur edi, u yaxshi qiladi."

en: ‘Madam,’ rejoined the countess, ‘that which you say liketh me well and so on my part I purpose not to give you that which you shall ask of me by way of reward, but to do well, for that meseemeth behoveful so to do.’ The gentlewoman, then, constrained by necessity, with the utmost shamefastness, asked her an hundred pounds to marry her daughter withal; but the countess, seeing her confusion and hear- ing her modest demand, gave her ﬁve hundred and so many rare and pre- cious jewels as were worth maybe as much more.
uz: Xonim,  deb javob berdi grafin,  siz aytadigan narsa menga yoqadi va shuning uchun men siz mendan so'ragan narsani mukofot sifatida berishni emas, balki yaxshilik qilishni maqsad qilganman, chunki buni qilish juda zarur emas. Shunda janob ayol, zaruratga majbur bo'lib, o'ta uyatchanlik bilan, undan o'z qiziga uylanish uchun yuz funt so'radi; lekin grafin uning chalkashligini ko'rib va uning kamtarona talabini eshitib, unga undan ham qimmatroq bo'lgan besh yuzdan ortiq noyob va qimmatbaho toshlar berdi.

en: With this the gentlewo- man was far more than satisﬁed and rendered the countess the best thanks in her power; whereupon the latter, taking leave of her, returned to the inn, whilst the other, to deprive Bertrand of all farther occasion of coming or sending to her house, removed with her daughter into the country to the house of one of her kinsfolk, and he, being a little after recalled by his vas- sals and hearing that the countess had departed the country, returned to his own house.
uz: Shu bilan muloyim odam ancha qoniqdi va grafinaning qudratiga eng yaxshi minnatdorchilik bildirdi; shundan so'ng, u undan xayrlashib, mehmonxonaga qaytdi, boshqalari esa Bertrandni uning uyiga kelish yoki yuborish imkoniyatidan mahrum qilish uchun qizini qishloqqa, qarindoshlaridan birining uyiga olib ketishdi va u ozgina vaqt o'tgach, o'z vasiylari tomonidan esga olinib, grafining mamlakatni tark etganini eshitib, o'z uyiga qaytdi.

en: The countess, hearing that he had departed Florence and returned to his county, was mightily rejoiced and abode at Florence till her time came to be delivered, when she gave birth to two male children, most like their father,
uz: Grafin Florensiyani tark etib, o'z okrugiga qaytganini eshitib, juda xursand bo'ldi va Florensiyada tug'ilish vaqti kelguncha qoldi, shundan so'ng u otasiga o'xshagan ikki o'g'il farzand ko'rdi.

en: and let rear them with all diligence.
uz: va ularni butun mehnat bilan ko'tarsin.

en: Whenas it seemed to her time, she set out and came, without being known of any, to Montpellier, where having rested some days and made enquiry of the count and where he was, she learned that he was to hold a great entertainment of knights and ladies at Roussillon on All Saints’ Day and betook herself thither, still in her pil- grim’s habit that she was wont to wear.
uz: Vaqti o'z vaqti bo'lgandek tuyulgach, u yo'lga chiqdi va hech kim bilmasdan Montpellierga keldi. U yerda bir necha kun dam olib, graf va uning qayerdaligini so'radi. U barcha avliyolar kuni Roussillon shahrida ritsarlar va xonimlarning katta ko'ngilochar tadbirini o'tkazishi kerakligini bilib, u yerga o'zini, hali ham o'zi kiymaydigan xunuk odatida olib bordi.

en: Finding the knights and ladies as- sembled in the count’s palace and about to sit down to table, she went up, with her children in her arms and without changing her dress, into the ban- queting hall and making her way between man and man whereas she saw the count, cast herself at his feet and said, weeping, ‘I am thine unhappy wife, who, to let thee return and abide in thy house, have long gone wander- ing miserably about the world.
uz: Graf saroyida o'tirgan ritsarlar va xonimlarni topib, stolga o'tirmoqchi bo'ldi, u bolalari qo'lida va ko'ylaklarini o'zgartirmasdan, taqiq zalga chiqdi va odam bilan odam o'rtasida yo'l oldi. Grafni ko'rganida, o'zini uning oyoqlariga tashladi va yig'lab dedi: "Men sizning baxtsiz xotiningman, seni qaytib kelishga va uyingda qolishga ruxsat berish uchun, uzoq vaqt davomida dunyo bo'ylab g'am-g'am bo'lib yurganman."

en: I conjure thee, in the name of God, to ac- complish unto me thy promise upon the condition appointed me by the two knights I sent thee; for, behold, here in mine arms is not only one son of thine, but two, and here is thy ring.
uz: Seni Xudoning nomi bilan iltimos qilaman, senga yuborgan ikki ritsar tomonidan tayinlangan shartga ko'ra menga bergan va'dangni bajar. Chunki, mana, mening qo'llarimda faqat bitta o'g'ling emas, balki ikkita o'g'ling bor, mana sening uzaging.

en: It is time, then, that I be received of thee as a wife, according to thy promise.’ The count, hearing this, was all confounded and recognized the ring and the children also, so like were they to him; but yet he said, ‘How can this have come to pass?’ The countess, then, to his exceeding wonderment and that of all others who were present, orderly recounted that which had passed and how it had happened; whereupon the count, feeling that she spoke sooth and seeing her constancy and wit and moreover two such goodly children, as well for the observance of his promise as to pleasure all his liegemen and the ladies, who all besought him thenceforth to receive and honour her as his lawful wife, put off his obstinate despite and raising the countess to her feet, embraced her and kissing her, acknowledged her for his lawful wife and those for his children.
uz: Shunday qilib, meni sening va'dangga ko'ra xotin sifatida qabul qilish vaqti keldi." Buni eshitgan graf hammasi xijolatda qoldi va uzukni va bolalarni ham tanidi, ular ham unga o'xshagan edilar; ammo u dedi: "Bu qanday qilib sodir bo'lishi mumkin edi?" Shunda graf, o'zining nihoyatda hayratiga va hozir bo'lganlarning hammasiga ko'ra, nima bo'lganini va qanday sodir bo'lganini tartibli tarzda hikoya qildi; shundan so'ng graf, u tinch gapirganini va o'zining qat'iyatliligi va donoligini ko'rib, shuningdek, barcha o'z rafiqalarilari va xonimlariga nisbatan va'dasiga rioya qilganini his qilib, keyinchalik uni qonuniy xotin sifatida qabul qilish va hurmat qilish uchun, uning xotinini o'z oyoqlariga qo'yib, uni o'pib, uning farzandlari uchun uni o'z

en: Then, letting clothe her in apparel such as be- seemed her quality, to the exceeding joyance of as many as were there and of all other his vassals who heard the news, he held high festival, not only all that day, but sundry others, and from that day forth still honoured her as his bride and his wife and loved and tendered her over all.”
uz: Keyin, uni shunday kiyimga kiydirdiki, bu uning sifatiga o'xshardi, bu yerda bo'lganlarning va bu xabarni eshitgan boshqa barcha vassallarining haddan tashqari xursandchiligiga sabab bo'ldi, u nafaqat o'sha kuni, balki turli xil bayramlarni ham nishonladi va o'sha kundan boshlab uni kelin va xotin sifatida hurmat qildi, sevdi va hamma narsadan afzal ko'rdi.

en: THE TENTH STORY Alibech, turning hermit, is taught by Rustico, a monk, to put the devil in hell, and being after brought away thence, becometh Neerbale his wife.
uz: O'NCHINCHI HIKOYA Alibek, begona odamga aylanib, rohib Rustiko tomonidan iblisni do'zaxga tashlashni o'rgatadi va u yerdan olib ketilgandan so'ng, Neer bale uning xotiniga aylanadi.

en: Dioneo, who had diligently hearkened to the queen’s story, seeing that it was ended and that it rested with him alone to tell, without awaiting com- mandment, smilingly began to speak as follows: “Charming ladies, maybe you have never heard tell how one putteth the devil in hell; wherefore, without much departing from the tenor of that whereof you have discoursed all this day, I will e’en tell it you.
uz: Dioneo, qirolichaning hikoyasini diqqat bilan tinglagan edi, chunki u tugadi va buyruqni kutmasdan, uni aytish faqat o'zida qoldi, shunday dedi kulib: Joyli xonimlar, ehtimol siz hech qachon iblisni do'zaxga qanday tashlash haqida eshitmagansiz; shuning uchun, shu kun davomida muhokama qilgan narsalaringizdan uncha uzoq ketmasdan, men sizga aytaman.

en: Belike, having learned it, you may catch the spirit204 thereof and come to know that, albeit Love sojourneth liefer in jocund palaces and luxurious chambers than in the hovels of the poor, yet none the less doth he whiles make his power felt midmost thick forests and rugged mountains and in desert caverns; whereby it may be understood that all things are subject to his puissance.
uz: Shunday qilib, uni o'rganganingizdan so'ng, uning ruhini ushlashingiz va bilib olishingiz mumkinki, garchi sevgi kambag'allarning hovlilaridan ko'ra ko'proq hashamatli saroylar va hashamatli xonalarda yashasa ham, u o'z kuchini eng qalin o'rmonlar, qo'pol tog'lar va cho'l g'orlarida his qiladi; shu orqali barcha narsalar uning qudratiga bo'ysunishini tushunish mumkin.

en: To come, then, to the fact, I say that in the city of Capsa in Barbary there was aforetime a very rich man, who, among his other children, had a fair and winsome young daughter, by name Alibech.
uz: Xo'sh, haqiqatga kelsak, aytishim mumkinki, Barbaridagi Kapsa shahrida bir vaqtlar juda boy odam bor edi, uning boshqa farzandlari orasida Alibech ismli go'zal va jozibali yosh qizi bor edi.

en: She, not being a Christian and hearing many Christians who abode in the town mightily extol the Christian faith and the service of God, one day questioned one of them in what manner one might avail to serve God with the least hindrance.
uz: U xristian bo'lmagani va shaharda yashovchi ko'plab xristianlarning xristian e'tiqodini va Xudoning xizmatini kuchli tarzda ulug'laganini eshitib, bir kuni ulardan biriga Xudoga eng kam to'siqlarsiz xizmat qilish uchun qanday foydalanish mumkinligini so'radi.

en: The other answered that they best served God who most strictly eschewed the things of the world, as those did who had betaken them into the solitudes of the deserts of Thebais.
uz: Boshqasi javob berdi: ular dunyoni eng qat'iy chetlab o'tgan Xudoga, xuddi ularni Tebay cho'llarining cho'llariga tashlaganlar kabi, eng yaxshi xizmat qilishadi.

en: The girl, who was maybe fourteen years old and very simple, moved by no ordered desire, but by some childish fancy, set off next morning by stealth and all alone, to go to the desert of Thebais, without letting any know her intent.
uz: Qiz, ehtimol o'n to'rt yoshda va juda oddiy edi, tartibsiz istakdan, balki ba'zi bir bolalarcha xayol bilan ta'sirlanib, ertasi kuni ertalab yashirincha va yolg'iz holda, hech kimga bildirmasdan, Tebay cho'liga yo'l oldi.

en: After some days, her desire persisting, she won, with no little toil, to the deserts in question and seeing a hut afar
uz: Bir necha kundan so'ng, uning istagi tinimsiz qolgach, u hech qanday qiyinchiliksiz, so'ralgan cho'lga va uzoqdagi kulbani ko'rishga g'alaba qozondi.

en: off, went thither and found at the door a holy man, who marvelled to see her there and asked her what she sought.
uz: ketib, u yerga bordi va eshik oldida bir muqaddas odamni topdi. U uni u yerda ko'rib hayratda qoldi va undan nimani qidirayotganini so'radi.

en: She replied that, being inspired of God, she went seeking to enter into His service and was now in quest of one who should teach her how it behoved to serve Him.
uz: U javob berdi: "Xudodan ilhomlanib, Uning xizmatida bo'lishga intildi va endi Unga qanday xizmat qilish kerakligini o'rgatadigan odamni qidirayotgan edi."

en: The worthy man, seeing her young and very fair and fearing lest, an he entertained her, the devil should beguile him, commended her pious intent and giving her somewhat to eat of roots of herbs and wild apples and dates and to drink of water, said to her, ‘Daughter mine, not far hence is a holy man, who is a much better master than I of that which thou goest seeking; do thou betake thyself to him’; and put her in the way.
uz: Haqdor odam, uning yosh va juda chiroyli ekanligini ko'rib, shayton uni aldashidan qo'rqqan edi, uning xolis niyatini maqtadi va unga o't ildizi, yovvoyi olma va xurmolardan yeyishga biroz berdi, unga dedi: "Qizim, yaqin atrofda muqaddas bir odam bor, u mendan ko'ra yaxshiroq xo'jayin, sen unga o'zingni ber" va uni yo'lga qo'ydi.

en: However, when she reached the man in question, she had of him the same answer and faring farther, came to the cell of a young hermit, a very devout and good man, whose name was Rustico and to whom she made the same request as she had done to the others.
uz: Ammo u so'ralgan odamga yetib borgach, u ham xuddi shu javobni oldi va uzoqroqqa borgach, Rustico ismli juda dindor va yaxshi odamning xonasiga keldi va unga boshqalarga qilganidek bir xil so'rovni berdi.

en: He, having a mind to make a trial of his own con- stancy, sent her not away, as the others had done, but received her into his cell, and the night being come, he made her a little bed of palm-fronds and bade her lie down to rest thereon.
uz: U, o'z roziligi bilan sinov o'tkazishni o'ylab, uni boshqalar qilganidek jo'natmadi, balki uni o'z xonasiga qabul qildi va tun bo'lishi bilan unga palma barglaridan kichik bir karavot yasadi va unga dam olish uchun yotishni buyurdi.

en: This done, temptations tarried not to give battle to his powers of resistance and he, ﬁnding himself grossly deceived by these latter, turned tail, without awaiting many assaults, and confessed himself beaten; then, laying aside devout thoughts and orisons and mortiﬁc- ations, he fell to revolving in his memory the youth and beauty of the dam- sel and bethinking himself what course he should take with her, so as to win to that which he desired of her, without her taking him for a debauched fellow.
uz: Shu bilan birga, qarshilik kuchlariga qarshi kurashmaslikka vasvasalar cheklandi va u, o'zini bularning qo'pol aldab ketganini his qilib, ko'p hujumlarni kutmasdan orqaga burildi va o'zini kaltaklangan deb tan oldi; so'ngra, dindorlik fikrlari, g'azab va o'limga olib keluvchi harakatlarni chetga surib, dam-selning yoshligi va go'zalligini xotirasiga aylantirib, u bilan qanday yo'l tutishi kerakligini o'ylab, uni yomon odam deb bilmasdan, undan xohlagan narsaga erishish uchun.

en: Accordingly, having sounded her with sundry questions, he found that she had never known man and was in truth as simple as she seemed; where- fore he bethought him how, under colour of the service of God, he might bring her to his pleasures.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uni turli savollar bilan qiziqtirganidan so'ng, u hech qachon erkakni tanimasligini va haqiqatan ham o'zi ko'ringanidek oddiy ekanligini angladi; chunki u uni Xudoning xizmatining rangi ostida qanday qilib o'z zavqiga olib kelishi mumkinligi haqida o'yladi.

en: In the ﬁrst place, he showeth her with many words how great an enemy the devil was of God the Lord and after gave her to understand that the most acceptable service that could be rendered to God was to put back the devil into hell, whereto he had condemned him.
uz: Avvalo, u unga ko'p so'zlar bilan shayton Xudoning Rabbining qanday buyuk dushmani ekanligini ko'rsatadi va keyin unga Xudoga taqdim etilishi mumkin bo'lgan eng maqbul xizmat shaytonni do'zaxga qaytarish ekanligini tushunishga yordam beradi, u yerda uni hukm qilgan edi.

en: The girl asked him how this might be done; and he, ‘Thou shalt soon know that; do thou but as thou shalt see me do.’ So saying, he proceeded to put off the few garments he had and abode stark naked, as likewise did the girl, whereupon he fell on his knees, as he would pray, and caused her abide over against himself.205
uz: Qiz undan buni qanday amalga oshirish mumkinligini so'radi; va u dedi: "Sen buni tezda bilib olasan; faqat meni ko'rganingdek qil." Shunday qilib, u o'zining oz miqdordagi kiyimlarini yechib, yalang'och holda qoldi, xuddi qiz kabi, shundan so'ng u tizzalari bilan yiqildi, ibodat qilgandek va uni o'ziga qarshi turishga majbur qildi.

en: Whereupon Rustico, seeing her so fair, felt an accession of desire, and therewith came an insurgence of the ﬂesh, which Alibech marking with sur- prise, said: —“Rustico, what is this, which I see thee have, that so protrudes, and which I have not?” “Oh!
uz: Shundan so'ng Rustiko uni shunchalik go'zal ko'rib, istak qo'zg'alishini his qildi va shu bilan birga go'shtning qo'zg'alishi paydo bo'ldi. Alibek uni ustunlik bilan belgilab, dedi: "Rustiko, senga ko'rishim mumkin bo'lgan, bunchalik ko'tariladigan va menda yo'q bo'lgan narsa nima?" "Oh!

en: my daughter,” said Rustico, “ ’tis the Devil of whom I have told thee: and, seest thou?
uz: Qizim,  dedi Rustiko,  senga aytgan iblismi: va, ko'ryapsanmi?

en: he is now tormenting me most grievously, insomuch that I am scarce able to hold out.” Then: —“Praise be to God,” said the girl, “I see that I am in better case than thou, for no such Devil have I.” “Sooth sayst thou,” returned Rustico; “but instead of him thou hast somewhat else that I have not.” “Oh!” said Alibech, “what may that be?” “Hell,” answered Rustico: “and I tell thee, that ’tis my belief that God has sent thee hither for the salvation of my soul; seeing that, if this Devil shall continue to plague me thus, then, so thou wilt have compassion on me and permit me to put him in hell, thou wilt both afford me great and exceed- ing great solace, and render to God an exceeding most acceptable service, if, as thou sayst, thou art come into these parts for such a purpose.” In good faith the girl made answer: —“As I have hell to match your Devil, be it, my father, as and when you will.”
uz: U meni hozir juda qattiq azoblayapti, shunchalikki, men juda ham chiday olmayapman. Keyin: Allohga hamd bo'lsin, dedi qiz, Men sendan yaxshiroq ahvolda ekanligimni ko'ryapman, chunki menda bunday Iblis yo'q. Xush deysan, javob berdi Rustiko; lekin uning o'rniga menda yo'q nimadir bor. Oh! dedi Alibek,  nima bo'lishi mumkin? Do'zax,  javob berdi Rustiko: va men senga aytaman, Men seni Xudo jonimning najoti uchun yuborgan deb ishonaman; chunki, agar bu Iblis meni azoblasa, unda menga rahm qilgin va menga uni do'zaxga qo'yishga ruxsat berasan,  Agar sen menga yordam berishing kerak bo'lsa, men senga shunday buyuk bir

en: Whereupon: —“Bless thee, my daughter,” said Rustico, “go we then, and put him there, that he leave me henceforth in peace.” Which said, he took the girl to one of the beds and taught her the posture in which she must lie in order to incarcerate this spirit accursed of God.
uz: Shundan so'ng:  Seni duo et, qizim,  dedi Rustiko,  unda boraylik, uni u yerga qo'yamiz, toki u meni bundan buyon tinch qo'ysin. Shunda u qizni bir karavotga olib bordi va unga Xudo la'natlagan bu ruhni qamoqqa tashlash uchun qanday holatda yotishi kerakligini o'rgatdi.

en: The girl, having never before put any devil in hell, felt on this ﬁrst oc- casion a twinge of pain: wherefore she said to Rustico: — “Of a surety, my father, he must be a wicked fellow, this devil, and in very truth a foe to God; for there is sorrow even in hell —not to speak of other places —when he is put there.” “Daughter,” said Rustico, “ ’twill not be always so.” And for better assurance thereof they put him there six times before they quitted the bed; whereby they so thoroughly abased his pride that he was fain to be quiet.
uz: Qiz, hech qachon do'zaxga hech qanday shaytonni kiritmagan edi, bu birinchi safar bir chimdim og'riqni his qildi: shuning uchun u Rusticoga dedi: Albatta, otam, u yovuz odam, bu shayton, va haqiqatan ham Xudoga dushman bo'lishi kerak; chunki do'zaxda ham qayg'u bor  boshqa joylar haqida gapirmasa ham bo'ladi  u u yerga qo'yilganda. Qizim,  dedi Rustico,  doim ham shunday bo'lmasin. Va bundan yaxshiroq ishonch hosil qilish uchun, uni to'shakdan chiqishdan oldin olti marta u yerga qo'yishdi; shu bilan ular uning g'ururini shunchalik kamsitishdi, hatto u jim bo'lishiga majbur edi.

en: However, the proud ﬁt returning upon him from time to time, and the girl addressing herself always obediently to its reduc- tion, it so befell that she began to ﬁnd the game agreeable, and would say to Rustico: —“Now see I plainly that ’twas true, what the worthy men said at Capsa, of the service of God being so delightful: indeed I cannot remember that in aught that ever I did I had so much pleasure, so much solace, as in putting the Devil in hell; for which cause I deem it insensate folly on the part of anyone to have a care to aught else than the service of God.” Where- fore many a time she would come to Rustico, and say to him: —“My father, ’twas to serve God that I came hither, and not to pass my days in idleness:
uz: Ammo, vaqti-vaqti bilan unga qaytadigan mag'rurlik, va qiz doimo o'zini qisqartirishga itoatkorona murojaat qilib, shunday bo'ldiki, u o'yinni yoqimli deb topishni boshladi va Rusticoga dedi: Endi aniq ko'rdimki,  Capsada munosib odamlar aytganlari rost edi, Xudoning xizmati shunchalik yoqimli edi: haqiqatan ham, men hech qachon shaytonga do'zaxga tashlash kabi ko'p zavq, shunchalik tasalli berganimni eslay olmayman; shuning uchun men hech kimning Xudoga xizmat qilishdan ko'ra boshqa narsaga e'tibor berishini aqlsizlik deb hisoblayman. Avval ko'p marta u Rusticoga kelib, unga aytdi: Otam, men Xudoga kelganim uchun hech qachon o'tmagan edim, va men o'z kunlarimni...

en: go we then, and put the Devil in hell.” And while they did so, she would now and again say: —“I know not, Rustico, why the Devil should escape from hell; were he but as ready to stay there as hell is to receive and retain him, he would never come out of it.” So, the girl thus frequently inviting and exhorting Rustico to the service of God, there came at length a time when she had so thoroughly lightened his doublet that he shivered when an- other would have sweated; wherefore he began to instruct her that the Devil was not to be corrected and put in hell, save when his head was exalted with pride; adding, “and we by God’s grace have brought him to so sober a mind that he prays God he may be left in peace;” by which means he for a time kept the girl quiet.
uz: Shunday qilib, ketdik, iblisni do'zaxga qo'yamiz." Va ular shunday qilishar ekan, u vaqti-vaqti bilan yana aytardi: "Men bilmayman, Rustiko, Iblis nega do'zaxdan qochishi kerak; agar u do'zax uni qabul qilishga va ushlab turishga tayyor bo'lsa, u hech qachon undan chiqmas edi." Shunday qilib, qiz Rustiko'ni Xudoga xizmat qilishga tez-tez chaqirib va undashi bilan, oxir-oqibatda bir vaqt kelib, u uning shaklini shunday yengillashtirdiki, u birov terlaganida titrardi; u yerda u unga iblisni tuzatish va do'zaxga qo'yish kerak emasligini, faqat uning boshi g'urur bilan ko'tarilganda, deb o'rgatdi; qo'shimcha qilib aytdi: "Va biz Xudoning marhamati bilan uni shunday hushyor qilib, Xudo uni tinch qo'yishi mumkin edi, deb o'ylashdi, chunki u..."

en: But when she saw that Rustico had no more occasion for her to put the Devil in hell, she said to him one day: —“Rustico, if thy Devil is chastened and gives thee no more trouble, my hell, on the other hand, gives me no peace; wherefore, I with my hell have holpen thee to abase the pride of thy Devil, so thou wouldst do well to lend me the aid of thy Devil to allay the fervent heat of my hell.” Rustico, who lived on roots and water, could ill avail to answer her calls and told her that it would need overmany devils to appease hell, but he would do what he might thereof.
uz: Ammo u Rustikoga iblisni do'zaxga tashlash uchun boshqa imkoniyat bo'lmaganiga ko'rgach, bir kuni unga dedi: "Rustiko, agar sening iblising seni jazolasa va senga boshqa tashvish bermasa, mening do'zaxim, aksincha, menga tinchlik bermaydi; shuning uchun, men do'zaxim bilan senga iblisingning g'ururini pasaytirishga yordam berdim, shuning uchun do'zaximning qizg'in issig'ini yengillashtirish uchun menga iblising yordamini berishing yaxshi bo'lardi."

en: Accordingly he satisﬁed her bytimes, but so seldom it was but casting a bean into the lion’s mouth; whereas the girl, herseeming she served not God as diligently as she would fain have done, murmured somewhat.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u uni bir necha marta qoniqtirardi, lekin bu juda kamdan-kam hollarda sherning og'ziga loviya tashlashdan boshqa narsa emas edi; qiz esa, o'zini Xudoga unchalik astoydil xizmat qilmagandek ko'rsatib, biroz pichirladi.

en: But, whilst this debate was toward between Rustico his devil and Alibech her hell, for overmuch desire on the one part and lack of power on the other, it befell that a ﬁre broke out in Capsa and burnt Alibech’s father in his own house, with as many children and other family as he had; by reason whereof she abode heir to all his good.
uz: Lekin, bu bahs Rustiko o'z shaytonining va Alibekning do'zaxi tomonida bo'lgan bo'lsa-da, bir tomondan haddan tashqari istak va boshqa tomondan hokimiyat yetishmasligi sababli, Kapsada yong'in kelib chiqib, Alibekning otasini o'z uyida, uning farzandlari va boshqa oilasi bilan birga yoqib yubordi; shu sababli u uning barcha yaxshiliklariga merosxo'r bo'lib qoldi.

en: Thereupon, a young man called Neerbale, who had spent all his substance in gallantry, hearing that she was alive, set out in search of her and ﬁnding her, before the court206 had laid hands upon her father’s estate, as that of a man dying without heir, to Rustico’s great satisfaction, but against her own will, brought her back to Capsa, where he took her to wife and succeeded, in her right, to the ample inheritance of her father.
uz: Shundan so'ng, Neerbale ismli bir yigit, uning tirikligini eshitib, butun boyligini saxiylikka sarflagan edi, uni qidirib, topishga yo'l oldi. 1936-yilda sud o'z otasining mulkini merosxo'rsiz o'layotgan odamning mulkini qo'lga kiritmasidan oldin, Rustico'ning katta mamnuniyatiga ko'ra, lekin o'z irodasidan kelib chiqib, uni Kapsaga qaytarib olib keldi va u yerda uni xotinlikka oldi va o'z huquqi bilan otasining keng merosga ega bo'ldi.

en: There, being asked by the women at what she served God in the desert, she answered (Neerbale having not yet lain with her) that she served Him at putting the devil in hell and that Neerbale had done a grievous sin in that he had taken her from such service.
uz: U yerda ayollar undan cho'lda Xudoga nima xizmat qilganini so'rashganda, u (Neerbale hali u bilan yotmagan holda) unga shaytonni do'zaxga tashlashda Unga xizmat qilganini va Neerbale uni bunday xizmatdan olib tashlashda og'ir gunoh qilganini aytdi.

en: The ladies asked, ‘How putteth one the devil in hell?’ And the girl, what with words and what with gestures, ex-
uz: Xonimlar so'radilar: Iblisni do'zaxga qanday qo'yish mumkin? Qiz esa, so'zlar bilan nima, imo-ishoralar bilan nima, sobiq...

en: pounded it to them; whereat they set up so great a laughing that they laugh yet and said, ‘Give yourself no concern, my child; nay, for that is done here also and Neerbale will serve our Lord full well with thee at this.’ Thereafter, telling it from one to another throughout the city, they brought it to a com- mon saying there that the most acceptable service one could render to God was to put the devil in hell, which byword, having passed the sea hither, is yet current here.
uz: Ularga shunday ta'sir ko'rsatdiki, ular shunday katta kulgi ko'tardilarki, hali ham kulishdi va dedilar: "O'zingni tashvishga solma, bolam; yo'q, bu yerda ham shunday qilinadi va Neer bale Rabbimizga sen bilan birga to'liq xizmat qiladi." Shundan so'ng, butun shahar bo'ylab bir-birlariga aytib, u yerda Xudoga xizmat qilishning eng maqbul xizmati shaytonni do'zaxga tashlash edi, u so'zma-so'z dengizdan o'tib, hali ham shu yerda mavjud.

en: Wherefore do all you young ladies, who have need of God’s grace, learn to put the devil in hell, for that this is highly acceptable to Him and pleasing to both parties and much good may grow and ensue thereof.” A thousand times or more had Dioneo’s story moved the modest ladies to laughter, so quaint and comical did his words appear to them; then, whenas he had made an end thereof, the queen, knowing the term of her sovranty to be come, lifted the laurel from her head and set it merrily on that of Filostrato, saying: “We shall presently see if the wolf will know how to govern the ewes better than the ewes have governed the wolves.” Filostrato, hearing this, said, laughing, “An I were hearkened to, the wolves had taught the ewes to put the devil in hell, no worse than Rustico taught Alibech; wherefore do ye not style us wolven, since you yourselves have not been ewen.
uz: Shuning uchun, Xudoning marhamatiga muhtoj bo'lgan barcha yosh xonimlar, shaytonni do'zaxga tashlashni o'rganinglar, chunki bu U uchun juda maqbul va ikki tomonga ham yoqadi va undan ko'p yaxshilik o'sishi mumkin." Dioneoning hikoyasi kamtarona ayollarni ming marta yoki undan ko'proq kulishga undadi, shuning uchun uning so'zlari g'alati va kulgili ko'rindi; so'ngra, u buni tugatgach, malika o'z hukmronligi muddatini bilgach, lavrni boshidan olib, filostratoning ustiga joylashtirdi va dedi: "Hozir ko'ramiz, hokim qo'ylarni qo'ylardan yaxshiroq boshqarishni biladimi?" Filostrat, dedi, kulgach, "Men bo'rilarni eshitgan edim, chunki ular bizni do'zaxga tashlash uchun yomonroq bo'ladilar, chunki siz...

en: Algates, I will govern the kingdom committed to me to the best of my power.” “Harkye, Filostrato,” rejoined Neiﬁle, “in seeking to teach us, you might have chanced to learn sense, even as did Masetto of Lamporec- chio of the nuns, and ﬁnd your tongue what time your bones should have learnt to whistle without a master.” Filostrato, ﬁnding that he still got a Roland for his Oliver,207 gave over pleasantry and addressed himself to the governance of the kingdom com- mitted to him.
uz: "Algetlar, men o'zimga sodiq qolgan shohlikni qo'limdan kelgancha boshqaraman." Harkye, Filostrato,  deb javob berdi Neifile,  bizni o'rgatishga intilganingizda, siz ham ma'no o'rganishga muvaffaq bo'lishingiz mumkin edi, xuddi Lamporekning Masetto kabi rohibalar kabi, va suyaklaringiz ustozsiz hushtak chalishni o'rganishi kerak bo'lgan vaqtni topishingiz mumkin edi. Filostrato, o'zining Oliver uchun hali ham Roland olganini anglab, 207-yilda o'zini yoqtirdi va unga topshirilgan shohlik boshqaruviga yo'naltirdi.

en: Wherefore, letting call the seneschal, he was fain to know at what point things stood all and after discreetly ordained that which he judged would be well and would content the company for such time as his seignory should endure.
uz: Shuning uchun, oqsoqolni chaqirib, u hamma narsa qanday holatda ekanligini bilishga intildi va o'zi yaxshi deb hisoblagan narsani yashirincha belgilab, uning oliyjanobligi davom etishi kerak bo'lgan vaqt davomida kompaniyani qoniqtirdi.

en: Then, turning to the ladies, “Lovesome ladies,” quoth he, “since I knew good from evil, I have, for my ill fortune, been still subject unto Love for the charms of one or other of you; nor hath humility neither obedience, no, nor the assiduous ensuing him in all his usances, in so far as it hath been known of me, availed me but that ﬁrst I have been
uz: Keyin ayollarga o'girilib, u dedi: Sevgichli ayollar, chunki men yaxshilik va yomonlikni bilardim, men o'z baxtsizlikim tufayli sizlarning biringizning yoki boshqa biringizning jozibasidan muhabbatga bo'ysundim; na kamtarlik, na itoatkorlik, na uning barcha urf-odatlarida qat'iy ergashish menga foyda keltirmadi, balki avval men...

en: abandoned for another and after have still gone from bad to worse; and so I believe I shall fare unto my death; wherefore it pleaseth me that it be dis- coursed tomorrow of none other matter than that which is most conformable to mine own case, to wit, OF THOSE WHOSE LOVES HAVE HAD UNHAPPY ENDING, for that I in the long run look for a most unhappy [issue to mine own]; nor was the name by which you call me conferred on me for otherwhat by such an one who knew well what it meant.”208 So saying, he rose to his feet and dismissed everyone until suppertime.
uz: Boshqaga tashlab ketilgan va keyin ham yomonlikdan yomonroqqa qarab ketganman; va shuning uchun o'limimga erishaman deb o'ylayman; shuning uchun u ertaga o'z holatimga mos keladigan narsadan boshqa hech qanday narsa bilan hal qilinmasligidan xursandman, ya'ni, SEVISHLARIM UCHUN BAXTIY BO'LGAN, chunki men uzoq muddatda eng baxtsiz [o'zimnikiga bog'liq muammo]ni qidiraman; va siz meni boshqa narsa uchun chaqirayotgan ism menga yaxshi biladigan odam tomonidan topshirilmagan.

en: The garden was so goodly and so delightsome that there was none who elected to go forth thereof, in the hope of ﬁnding more pleasance elsewhere.
uz: Bog' shunchalik go'zal va nafis ediki, undan boshqa joyda ko'proq zavq topish umidida chiqishni tanlagan hech kim yo'q edi.

en: Nay, the sun, now grown mild, making it nowise irksome to give chase to the fawns and kids and rabbits and other beasts which were thereabout and which, as they sat, had come maybe an hundred times to disturb them by skipping through their midst, some addressed themselves to pursue them.
uz: Yo'q, quyosh endi yumshoqlashib, atrofdagi hayvonlar, bolalar, quyonlar va boshqa hayvonlarni quvib o'tishni bezovta qiladi va ular o'tirganlarida, ularni bir necha yuz marta bezovta qilish uchun ularning o'rtasidan sakrab o'tib kelgan edi, ba'zilar ularni ta'qib qilish uchun o'zlariga murojaat qilishdi.

en: Dioneo and Fiammetta fell to singing of Messer Guglielmo and the Lady of Vergiu,209 whilst Filomena and Pamﬁlo sat down to chess; and so, some do- ing one thing and some another, the time passed on such wise that the hour of supper came well nigh unlooked for; whereupon, the tables being set round about the fair fountain, they supped there in the evening with the ut- most delight.
uz: Dioneo va Fiammetta Messer Guglielmo va Vergiuning xonimi qo'shig'iga berilib qolishdi, 209 yil, Filomena va Pamfilo esa shaxmatga o'tirishdi; va shunday qilib, ba'zilar bir narsani, ba'zilar esa boshqa narsani qilishdi, vaqt shunchalik donolik bilan o'tdi, kechki ovqat vaqti deyarli kutilmagan edi; shundan so'ng, chiroyli favvora atrofida o'rnatilayotgan stollar, ular kechqurun u yerda eng ko'p zavq bilan ovqatlanishdi.

en: As soon as the tables were taken away, Filostrato, not to depart from the course holden of those who had been queens before him, commanded Laur- etta to lead up a dance and sing a song.
uz: Stollar olib qo'yilishi bilanoq, Filostrato o'zidan oldingi malika bo'lganlarning yo'lidan ketmaslikni buyurdi va Laur-ettaga raqsga tushishni va qo'shiq kuylashni buyurdi.

en: “My lord,” answered she, “I know none of other folk’s songs, nor have I in mind any of mine own which should best beseem so joyous a company; but, an you choose one of those which I have, I will willingly sing it.” Quote the king, “Nothing of thine can be other than goodly and pleasing; wherefore sing us such as thou hast.” Lauretta, then, with a sweet voice enough, but in a somewhat plaintive style, began thus, the other ladies answering: No maid disconsolate  Hath cause as I, alack!
uz: Hazratim,  javob berdi u, Men boshqa xalq qoshiqlarini bilmayman, na ozimning ozimning ozimniki ham shunday quvnoq bir jamoa bolishi kerakligini oylamayman; lekin, agar siz menda borlaridan birini tanlasangiz, uni ozim xohlab kuylayman. Shohdan iqtibos keltiraman: Sizdan boshqa hech narsa yaxshi va yoqimli bolmaydi; shuning uchun siz kabi bizni kuylang. Lauretta, keyin, yetarli darajada shirin ovoz bilan, lekin biroz gamginona uslubda, boshqa xonimlar shunday javob berishdi: Hech qanday xizmatkor men kabi xafa qilmaydi, alack!

en: Who sigh for love in vain, to mourn her fate.
uz: Sevgini behuda sog'inadigan, taqdirini motam tutadigan.

en: He who moves heaven and all the stars in air  Made me for His delight  Lovesome and sprightly, kind and debonair,  E’en here below to give each lofty spright
uz: Osmonni va havoda barcha yulduzlarni harakatga keltiruvchi Zot meni O'z zavqi uchun yaratdi. Sevimli va yorqin, mehribon va beg'ubor, va bu yerda har bir yuksak yorqinlikni berish uchun.

en: Some inkling of that fair  That still in heaven abideth in His sight;  But erring men’s unright,  Ill knowing me, my worth  Accepted not, nay, with dispraise did bate.
uz: O'sha go'zallikning bir qismi Uning ko'z o'ngida yashiringan; Ammo adashgan odamlarning noto'g'riligi, Meni bilmasligim, qadr-qimmatim qabul qilinmadi, aksincha, haqorat bilan urildi.

en: Erst was there one who held me dear and fain  Took me, a youngling maid,  Into his arms and thought and heart and brain,  Caught ﬁre at my sweet eyes; yea time, unstayed  Of aught, that ﬂits amain  And lightly, all to wooing me he laid.
uz: Avval meni sevuvchi va mehribon ushlagan bir kishi bor edi, meni, yosh qizni, quchoqlariga, fikrlariga, yuragiga va miyasiga olib kirdi, shirin ko'zlarimga olov tutdi; ha, vaqt o'tmadi, hayratlanarli va yengil, meni o'ziga rom etayotgan narsalardan.

en: I, courteous, nought gainsaid  And held210 him worthy me;  But now, woe’s me, of him I’m desolate.
uz: Men, muloyim, hech qanday g'alaba qozonmadim Va uni menga munosib deb hisobladim; Ammo endi, voy menga, undan xaroba bo'ldim.

en: Then unto me there did himself present  A youngling proud and haught,  Renowning him for valorous and gent;  He took and holds me and with erring thought211  To jealousy is bent;  Whence I, alack!
uz: Keyin menga o'zini bir yosh takabbur va takabbur ko'rsatdi, uni jasur va muloyim deb rad etdi; U meni oldi va xato fikr bilan ushladi211 Hasad egildi; Qayerda men, alack!

en: nigh to despair am wrought,  As knowing myself —brought  Into this world for good  Of many an one —engrossed of one sole mate.
uz: Umidsizlikka yaqin bo'ldim, O'zimni bilganimdek  bu dunyoga yaxshilik uchun olib kelingan Ko'pchilikdan bir kishi  bitta turmush o'rtog'iga singib ketgan.

en: The luckless hour I curse, in very deed,  When I, alas!
uz: Omadsiz soatni la'natlayman, aslida, Qachonki men, afsuski!

en: said yea,  Vesture to change —so fair in that dusk wede  I was and glad, whereas in this more gay  A weary life I lead,  Far less than erst held honest, welaway!
uz: Ha, dedi, kiyim o'zgarish uchun  shunchalik chiroyli edim va xursand edim o'sha shabnamda, shu paytda bu ko'proq gey Hayotda men zerikarli yashayman, avvalgidek halol bo'lganimdan ancha kam, yaxshi!

en: Ah, dolorous bridal day,  Would God I had been dead  Or e’er I proved thee in such ill estate!
uz: Oh, achinarli kelin kuni, Xudo xohlasa o'lgan bo'lardim Yo'qsa, seni bunchalik yomon ahvolda sinab ko'rardim!

en: O lover dear, with whom well pleased was I  Whilere past all that be —  Who now before Him sittest in the sky  Who fashioned us —have pity upon me  Who cannot, though I die,
uz: Ey aziz oshiq, men bor bo'lgan narsaning hammasidan o'tib ketganimda, menga rahm qilgan, bizni shakllantirgan, hozir osmonda Uning oldida o'tirgan, o'lsam ham, menga rahm qila olmaydigan.

en: Forget thee for another; cause me see  The ﬂame that kindled thee  For me lives yet unquenched  And my recall up thither212 impetrate.
uz: O'zingni boshqa birov uchun unut; menga ko'rsat seni yoqqan olov. U hali ham o'chmagan va mening xotiram u yerga kirib boradi.

en: Here Lauretta made an end of her song, wherein, albeit attentively fol- lowed of all, she was diversely apprehended of divers persons, and there were those who would e’en understand, Milan-fashion, that a good hog was better than a handsome wench;213 but others were of a loftier and better and truer apprehension, whereof it booteth not to tell at this present.
uz: Bu yerda Lauretta o'z qo'shig'ini yakunladi, unda, garchi diqqat bilan hammadan pastroq bo'lsa-da, u turli xil odamlardan xilma-xil tarzda tushunildi va Milan uslubida yaxshi cho'chqa chiroyli qizdan yaxshiroq ekanligini tushunadiganlar bor edi; 213 lekin boshqalar yanada baland, yaxshiroq va haqiqiy xotirjamlikka ega edilar, buni hozir aytishga imkon yo'q.

en: Thereafter the king let kindle store of ﬂambeaux upon the grass and among the ﬂowers and caused sing divers other songs, until every star began to decline, that was above the horizon, when, deeming it time for sleep, he bade all with a good night betake themselves to their chambers.
uz: Shundan so'ng shoh o't ustida va gullar orasida olov yoqdi va turli xil qo'shiqlarni kuyladi, toki har bir yulduz ufqdan yuqori bo'lganda, uyqu vaqti deb hisoblaganida, hammaga xonasiga yaxshi tun bilan qaytishni buyurdi.

en: Here endeth the Third Day of the Decameron.
uz: Mana Dekameronning Uchinchi Kuni tugaydi.

en: DAY THE FOURTH INTRODUCTION Here beginneth the fourth day of the Decameron wherein under the governance of Filostrato is discoursed of those whose loves have had unhappy endings.
uz: TO'RTINCHI KUN Kirish Mana, Dekameronning to'rtinchi kuni boshlanadi, unda Filostrat hukmronligi ostida sevgilari baxtsiz yakunlarga ega bo'lganlar haqida gapiriladi.

en: Dearest ladies, as well by words of wise men heard as by things many a time both seen and read of myself, I had conceived that the boisterous and burning blast of envy was apt to smite none but lofty towers or the highest summits of the trees; but I ﬁnd myself mistaken in my conceit, for that, ﬂee- ing, as I have still studied to ﬂee, from the cruel onslaught of that raging wind, I have striven to go, not only in the plains, but in the very deepest of the valleys, as many manifestly enough appear to whoso considereth these present stories, the which have been written by me, not only in vulgar Florentine and in prose and without [author’s] name, but eke in as humble and sober a style as might be.
uz: Hurmatli xonimlar, shuningdek, o'zim ko'p marta ko'rgan va o'qigan narsalardan eshitgan dono odamlarning so'zlari bilan, men havasning shovqinli va yonib ketayotgan portlashi faqat baland minoralar yoki daraxtlarning eng baland cho'qqilarini urishga moyil deb o'ylagandim; lekin men o'z tasavvurimda adashganman, chunki, men hali ham o'sha shiddatli shamolning shafqatsiz hujumidan qochishni o'rganganimdek, men nafaqat tekisliklarda, balki eng chuqur vodiylarda, ko'pchilik men tomonidan yozilgan ushbu hozirgi hikoyalarni ko'rib chiqishga yetarli darajada ochiq ko'rinadigan darajada kamtarona va sobit uslubda borishga harakat qildim.

en: Yet for all this have I not availed to escape being cruelly shaken, nay, well nigh uprooted, of the aforesaid wind and all torn of the fangs of envy; wherefore I can very manifestly understand that to be true which the wise use to say, to wit, that misery alone in things present is without envy.214 There are then, discreet ladies, some who, reading these stories, have said that you please me overmuch and that it is not a seemly thing that I should take so much delight in pleasuring and solacing you; and some have said yet worse of commending you as I do.
uz: Shunga qaramay, men shafqatsizlarcha silkitilganimdan, yo'q, yuqorida aytilgan shamoldan va hasad ildizlaridan yirtilganimdan qutulishga ulgurmadim; shuning uchun men juda aniq tushunamanki, aql bilan aytish kerakki, hozirgi narsalarda faqat baxtsizlik hasadsizdir.

en: Others, making a show of wishing to speak more maturely, have said that it sorteth ill with mine age henceforth to follow after things of this kind, to wit, to discourse of women or to study to please them.
uz: Boshqalar, yanada yetukroq gapirishni xohlashlarini ko'rsatib, mening yoshimga bundan buyon bunday narsalarga ergashish, ya'ni ayollarni muhokama qilish yoki ularni xursand qilish uchun o'qish yomon ekanligini aytishdi.

en: And many, feigning themselves mighty tender of my repute, avouch that I should do more wisely to abide with the Muses on Parnassus than to busy myself among you with these toys.
uz: Va ko'pchilik, o'zlarini mening obro'yimga moyil ko'rsatib, Parnassusdagi Muslar bilan birga qolishim, o'zimni sizlar bilan shu o'yinchoqlar bilan band qilishdan ko'ra oqilonaroq bo'lishini o'ylashadi.

en: Again, there be some who,
uz: Yana, shundaylar borki,

en: speaking more despitefully than advisedly, have said that I should do more discreetly to consider whence I might get me bread than to go peddling after these baubles, feeding upon wind; and certain others, in disparagement of my pains, study to prove the things recounted by me to have been otherwise than as I present them to you.
uz: Maslahatli emas, balki norozilik bilan gapiradigan bo'lsam, men nonni qayerdan olishim mumkinligini o'ylab ko'proq ehtiyot bo'lishim kerakligini aytdim, shamoldan oziqlanib, bu go'shtlarni sotishga ketishdan ko'ra; va ba'zi boshqalar, azoblarimni kamsitib, men aytgan narsalarni sizga taqdim etganimdagidan boshqacha bo'lganini isbotlash uchun o'rganishadi.

en: With such, then, and so many blusterings,215 such atrocious backbitings, such needle-pricks, noble ladies, am I, what while I battle in your service, bafﬂed and buffeted and transﬁxed even to the quick.
uz: Shunday qilib, va shuncha ko'p g'iybatlar bilan, 215 ta shunday dahshatli mish-mishlar, shuncha igna tishlari bilan, hurmatli xonimlar, men sizning xizmatingizda jang qilayotganimda, hayratda, buffetda va hatto tezkorlarga ham o'tiribman.

en: The which things, God knoweth, I hear and apprehend with an untroubled mind; and albeit my defence in this pertaineth altogether unto you, natheless, I purpose not to spare mine own pains; nay, without answering so much [at large] as it might behove, I mean to rid mine ears of them with some slight rejoinder, and that without delay; for that if even now, I being not yet come to216 the third part of my travail, they217 are many and presume amain, I opine that, ere I come to the end thereof, they may, having had no rebuff at the ﬁrst, on such wise be multiplied that with whatsoever little pains of theirs they might over- throw me, nor might your powers, great though they be, avail to withstand this.
uz: Xudo biladi, men bu haqda xotirjam aql bilan eshitaman va tushunaman; va garchi mening himoya qilishim bu borada faqat sizga tegishli bo'lsa ham, lekin men o'z azoblarimni ayamaslikni maqsad qilganman; yo'q, imkon qadar ko'p javob bermasdan, quloqlarimni ulardan biroz qayg'urish bilan, va hech qanday kechikishsiz qutqarmoqchiman; chunki agar hozir ham, men ishimning uchdan bir qismiga yetib kelmagan bo'lsam, ular ko'p va ishonamanki, men oxiriga yetib kelganimda, ular avval hech qanday qarshilik ko'rsatmagan holda, o'zlarining kichik azoblari bilan meni tashlab yuborishlari mumkin, va sizning kuchlaringiz, garchi ular juda katta bo'lsalar ham, bunga bardosh berishlari mumkin.

en: But, ere I come to make answer to any of them, it pleaseth me, in mine own defence, to relate, not an entire story —lest it should seem I would fain mingle mine own stories with those of so commendable a company as that which I have presented to you —but a part of one —that so its very default [of completeness] may attest that it is none of those —and accordingly, speaking to my assailants, I say that in our city, a good while agone, there was a townsman, by name Filippo Balducci, a man of mean enough extrac- tion, but rich and well addressed and versed in such matters as his condition comported.
uz: Lekin, ularning har biriga javob berishga kelishimdan oldin, o'z himoyamda butun hikoyani emas, balki hikoyani aytishni yoqtiraman  shunday tuyulmasin, men sizga taqdim etgan kabi maqtanishga arziydigan kompaniya haqidagi hikoyalarimni aralashtirishni xohlardim  lekin ularning bir qismi  shuning uchun uning o'z deformati (ko'pincha) ularning hech biri emasligini tasdiqlashi mumkin  va shunga ko'ra, mening hujumchilarimga gapiradigan bo'lsam, aytamanki, bizning shaharimizda bir vaqtlar Filippo Balducci ismli bir shaharlik odam bor edi, u o'z holatiga ko'ra, juda oddiy, ammo boy va yaxshi yondashuvchan va tajribaga ega edi.

en: He had a wife, whom he loved with an exceeding love, as she him, and they lived a peaceful life together, studying nothing so much as wholly to please one another.
uz: Uning xotini bor edi, uni ham o'zi kabi nihoyatda sevardi va ular birga tinch hayot kechirardilar, bir-birlarini xursand qilish uchun faqat o'rganishardi.

en: In course of time it came to pass, as it cometh to pass of all, that the good lady departed this life and left Filippo nought of herself but one only son, begotten of him and maybe two years old.
uz: Vaqt o'tishi bilan shunday bo'ldi, hammasi shunday bo'lib o'tgandek, yaxshi xonim bu hayotdan ketdi va Filippo'ni faqat o'zining yagona o'g'li, undan tug'ilgan va ehtimol ikki yoshda qoldirdi.

en: Filippo for the death of his lady abode as disconsolate as ever man might, having lost a beloved one, and seeing himself left alone and forlorn of that com- pany which most he loved, he resolved to be no more of the world, but to give himself altogether to the service of God and do the like with his little son.
uz: Filippo o'z xonimining o'limi tufayli inson qanchalik xafa bo'lmasin, sevikli insonini yo'qotgan va o'zini eng ko'p sevgan insondan yolg'iz va befarq holda ko'rganidan so'ng, u endi dunyodan bo'lmaslikka, balki o'zini Xudoga butunlay bag'ishlashga va o'g'li bilan xuddi shunday qilishga qaror qildi.

en: Wherefore, bestowing all his good for the love of God,218 he repaired without delay to the top of Mount Asinajo, where he took up his abode with
uz: Shuning uchun, Xudoning muhabbati uchun bor mol-mulkini sarflab, 218-yilda u kechiktirmasdan Asinajo tog'ining cho'qqisiga tomon yo'l oldi va u yerda o'z maskanini...

en: his son in a little hut and there living with him upon alms, in the practice of fasts and prayers, straitly guarded himself from discoursing whereas the boy was, of any temporal thing, neither suffered him see aught thereof, lest this should divert him from the service aforesaid, but still bespoke him of the glories of life eternal and of God and the saints, teaching him nought but pious orisons; and in this way of life he kept him many years, never suffer- ing him go forth of the hermitage nor showing him aught other than himself.
uz: Uning o'g'li kichik kulbada edi va u yerda u bilan sadaqa qilib, ro'za tutish va ibodat qilishda yashab, o'zini har qanday vaqtinchalik narsadan qat'iy saqlardi, bola esa undan hech narsa ko'rmasdi, aks holda bu uni yuqorida aytilgan xizmatdan chalg'itardi, lekin baribir uni abadiy hayot va Xudoning hamda avliyolarning shon-shuhratlaridan mahrum qilardi, unga faqat taqvodorlik yoki gunohlarni o'rgatardi; va bu hayot tarzida uni ko'p yillar saqlardi, hech qachon uni xarobaxonadan chiqishiga yo'l qo'ymasdi va o'zidan boshqa hech narsani ko'rsatmasdi.

en: Now the good man was used to come whiles into Florence, where being succoured, according to his occasions, of the friends of God, he returned to his hut, and it chanced one day that, his son being now eighteen years old and Filippo an old man, the lad asked him whither he went.
uz: Endi yaxshi odam Florensiyaga velosipedlar bilan kelishga odatlangan edi, u yerda, o'z imkoniyatlariga ko'ra, Xudoning do'stlaridan yordam olgach, u o'z kulbasiga qaytdi va bir kuni, o'g'li endi o'n sakkiz yoshda va Filippo qari odam bo'lgani sababli, yigit undan qayerga borayotganini so'radi.

en: Filippo told him and the boy said, “Father mine, you are now an old man and can ill endure fatigue; why do you not whiles carry me to Florence and bring me to know the friends and devotees of God and yourself, to the end that I, who am young and better able to toil than you, may after, whenas it pleaseth you, go to Florence for our occasions, whilst you abide here?” The worthy man, considering that his son was now grown to man’s estate and thinking him so inured to the service of God that the things of this world might thenceforth uneath allure him to themselves, said in himself, “The lad saith well”; and accordingly, having occasion to go thither, he carried him with him.
uz: Filippo unga aytdi va bola dedi: Otam, sen endi keksa odamsan va charchoqqa chiday olmaysan; nega meni Florensiyaga olib bormaysan va meni dostlari va Xudoning sadoqatlilarini hamda ozingni tanitib olib kelmaysan, toki men, yoshroq va sendan kora koproq mehnat qilishga qodir bolganim, keyin, senga yoqqanida, Florensiyaga bizning tadbirlarimiz uchun borsam, sen shu yerda qolsang? munosib odam ogli endi odamning mulkiga yetganini va uni Xudoga xizmat qilishga shunchalik moyil deb oylaganidan keyin, uni oziga jalb qila olmaydi, deb ozida dedi: Yigit yaxshi deydi; va shunga kora, u bilan birga bordi.

en: There the youth, seeing the palaces, the houses, the churches and all the other things whereof one seeth all the city full, began, as one who had never to his recollection beheld the like, to marvel amain and questioned his father of many things what they were and how they were called.
uz: O'sha yerda yoshlar saroylar, uylar, cherkovlar va butun shahar to'la ko'rinadigan boshqa narsalarni ko'rib, hech qachon bunday narsani ko'rmagan odam kabi, otasiga hayratda qolib, ularning nima ekanligi va qanday atalgani haqida savol bera boshladilar.

en: Filippo told him and he, hearing him, abode content and questioned of somewhat else.
uz: Filippo unga aytdi va u, uni eshitib, mamnuniyat bilan qoldi va boshqa nimadir haqida so'radi.

en: As they went thus, the son asking and the father answering, they en- countered by chance a company of pretty and well-dressed young women, coming from a wedding, whom as soon as the young man saw, he asked his father what manner of things these were.
uz: Ular shu yo'l bilan ketayotganlarida, o'g'il so'rayotganda va ota javob berayotganda, tasodifan to'ydan kelayotgan chiroyli va yaxshi kiyingan yosh ayollar jamoasiga duch kelishdi. Yigit ularni ko'rishi bilanoq, otasidan bularning qanday narsalar ekanligini so'radi.

en: “My son,” answered Filippo, “cast your eyes on the ground and look not at them, for that they are an ill thing.” Quoth the son, “And how are they called?” The father, not to awaken in the lad’s mind a carnal appetite less than useful, would not name them by the proper name, to wit, women, but said, “They are called green geese.” Whereupon, marvellous to relate, he who had never seen a woman and who recked not of palaces nor oxen nor horses nor asses nor monies nor of aught else he had seen, said suddenly, “Father mine, I prithee get me one of these
uz: O'g'lim,  javob berdi Filippo, ko'zlaringni yerga tashla va ularga qarama, chunki ular yomon narsa. O'g'il so'radi: Va ular qanday ataladi? Ota bolaning ongida foydali bo'lmagan shahvoniy ishtaha uyg'otmaslik uchun ularni o'z nomi bilan, ya'ni, ayollar deb atamasdi, balki dedi: Ular yashil g'ozlar deb ataladi. Shunday qilib, aytish jozibali, hech qachon ayol ko'rmagan va saroylar, ho'kizlar, otlar, eshaklar, pullar yoki boshqa hech narsani ko'rmagan odam, to'satdan dedi: Otam, men

en: green geese.” “Alack, my son,” replied the father, “hold thy peace; I tell thee they are an ill thing.” “How!” asked the youth.
uz: "Yashil g'ozlar."  Alack, o'g'lim,  javob berdi ota,  tinchlan; senga aytyapman, ular yomon narsa.  Qanday qilib!  deb so'radi yosh.

en: “Are ill things then made after this fashion?” and Filippo answered, “Ay.” Then said the son, “I know not what you would say nor why these are an ill thing; for my part, me- seemeth I never yet saw aught goodly or pleasing as are these.
uz: Yomon narsalar shunday uslubda qilinadimi? Filippo javob berdi: Ha. Shunda ogil dedi: Nima deyishingizni ham, nega bular yomon narsa ekanligini ham bilmayman; men uchun esa, hech qachon bu kabi yaxshi yoki yoqimli narsani kormaganman.

en: They are fairer than the painted angels you have shown me whiles.
uz: Ular siz menga ko'rsatgan bo'yalgan farishtalardan ham go'zalroq.

en: For God’s sake, an you reck of me, contrive that we may carry one of yonder green geese back with us up yonder, and I will give it to eat.” “Nay,” answered the father, “I will not: thou knowest not whereon they feed.” And he understood incon- tinent that nature was stronger than his wit and repented him of having brought the youth to Florence.
uz: Xudo haqqi, meni hisoblang, o'sha yashil g'ozlardan birini o'zimiz bilan u yerga olib borishni o'ylab toping, men uni yeyishga beraman. Yo'q, javob berdi ota, Yo'q, men qilmayman: sen ularning qayerdan ovqatlanishini bilmaysan. Va u tabiat uning aql-idrokidan kuchliroq ekanligini aniq tushundi va yoshlarni Florensiyaga olib kelganidan afsuslandi.

en: But I will have it sufﬁce me to have told this much of the present story and return to those for whose behoof I have re- lated it.
uz: Lekin men hozirgi hikoyaning ko'p qismini aytib berganim kifoya qiladi va uni qayta-qayta qo'yganlarimga qaytib boraman.

en: Some, then, of my censurers say that I do ill, young ladies, in studying overmuch to please you and that you please me overmuch.
uz: Shunday qilib, ba'zi senzurachilarim sizlarni xursand qilish uchun haddan tashqari ko'p o'qishda yomonlik qilaman, yosh ayollar, va siz meni juda ko'p xursand qilasiz, deyishadi.

en: Which things I do most openly confess, to wit, that you please me and that I study to please you, and I ask them if they marvel thereat —considering (let be the having known the dulcet kisses and amorous embracements and delightsome coup- lings that are of you, most sweet ladies, often gotten) only my having seen and still seeing your dainty manners and lovesome beauty and sprightly grace and above all your womanly courtesy —whenas he who had been reared and bred on a wild and solitary mountain and within the bounds of a little cell, without other company than his father, no sooner set eyes on you than you alone were desired of him, you alone sought, you alone followed with the eagerness of passion.
uz: Eng ko'p nimalarni ochiqchasiga tan olaman, ya'ni, siz meni xursand qilasiz va men sizni xursand qilish uchun o'qiyman, va ulardan hayratlanishni so'rayman  (shuningdek, siz, eng shirin xonimlar, ko'pincha olgan shirin o'pishlar va sevgi bag'rikengliklari va yoqimli muomalalaringizni ko'rganim va hali ham ko'rib turganim uchun) faqat sizning nozik xulq-atvoringizni, yoqimli go'zalligingizni va ochiq nafosatingizni va eng asosiysi, sizning ayollik odobingizni ko'rganim uchun  qachonki u yovvoyi va yolg'iz tog'da va kichik bir xujayrada, otasidan boshqa hech kim bilan birga bo'lmagan holda o'sib-o'sgan, sizga ko'z ko'zi bilan ko'rmagan, siz yolg'iz uni qidirgansiz, yolg'iz o'zingiz ishtiyoq bilan ergashganingiz.

en: Will they, then, blame me, back bite me, rend me with their tongues if I, whose body Heaven created all apt to love you, I, who from my childhood vowed my soul to you, feeling the potency of the light of your eyes and the sweetness of your honeyed words and the ﬂame enkindled by your piteous sighs —if, I say, you please me or if I study to please you, seeing that you over all else pleased a hermitling, a lad without understanding, nay, rather, a wild animal?
uz: Shunda ular meni ayblashadi, orqaga tishlaydilar, tillari bilan yirtib tashlaydilar, agar men, tanasi osmon seni sevishga moyil yaratgan bo'lsam, men, bolaligimdan senga jonimni qasam ichgan, ko'zlaring nurini, shirin so'zlaringni va achinarli ohlaringdan uyg'ongan olovni his qilgan bo'lsam  agar, desam, meni rozi qilsang yoki senga yoqish uchun o'qigan bo'lsam, sen hamma narsadan ko'ra begona, tushunmaydigan bola, yo'q, balki yovvoyi hayvonni yoqtirganingni ko'rsam?

en: Certes, it is only those, who, hav- ing neither sense nor cognizance of the pleasures and potency of natural af- fection, love you not nor desire to be loved of you, that chide me thus; and of these I reck little.
uz: Albatta, meni faqatgina tabiiy muhabbatning lazzatlari va qudratini sezmay, bilmay, sizni sevmaydigan va sizdan sevilishni istamaydiganlargina shunday tanbeh beradi; va men bulardan unchalik voz kechmayman.

en: As for those who go railing anent mine age, it would seem they know ill that, for all the leek hath a white head, the tail thereof is green.
uz: Mening yoshimdagilarni haqorat qiladiganlarga kelsak, go'yo ular bilishadi, chunki barcha ko'zbo'yoqlar oq boshga ega, dumlari yashil.

en: But to these, laying aside pleasantry, I answer that never, no, not to the extreme limit of
uz: Lekin bularga, xushmuomalalikni chetga surib, men hech qachon, yo'q, haddan tashqari cheklanmagan deb javob beraman.

en: my life, shall I repute it to myself for shame to seek to please those whom Guido Cavalcanti and Dante Alighieri, when already stricken in years, and Messer Cino da Pistoja, when a very old man, held in honour and whose approof was dear to them.
uz: Hayotimni o'zimga uyat deb hisoblaymanmi, Guido Cavalcanti va Dante Alighieri, allaqachon yillar davomida azob chekkan, va Messer Cino da Pistoja, juda keksa odam bo'lganida, hurmatga sazovor bo'lgan va yaqinligi ularga qadrli bo'lgan odamlarni xursand qilishga urinish.

en: And were it not to depart from the wonted usance of discourse, I would cite history in support and show it to be all full of stories of ancient and noble men who in their ripest years have still above all studied to please the ladies, the which an they know not, let them go learn.
uz: Agar nutqning odatdagi odatlaridan chetga chiqmasam, men tarixni qo'llab-quvvatlab, uni qadimiy va olijanob odamlarning hikoyalariga to'la ekanligini ko'rsatardim, ular o'zlarining eng yetuk yillarida ayollarni xursand qilish uchun eng muhimi o'qiganlar, lekin ular bilmagan narsalarni o'rganishsin.

en: That I should abide with the Muses on Parnassus, I confess to be good counsel; but, since we can neither abide forever with the Muses, nor they with us, it is nothing blameworthy if, whenas it chanceth a man is par- ted from them, he take delight in seeing that which is like unto them.
uz: Parnassusdagi Muslar bilan birga qolishimni yaxshi maslahat deb tan olaman; lekin, chunki biz Muslar bilan abadiy qololmaymiz, ular ham biz bilan birga bo'la olmaydi, agar odam ulardan ajralgan bo'lsa, ularga o'xshash narsalarni ko'rishdan zavq olishi hech qanday aybga loyiq emas.

en: The muses are women, and albeit women may not avail to match with them, yet at ﬁrst sight they have a semblance of them; insomuch that, an they pleased me not for aught else, for this they should please me; more by token that women have aforetime been to me the occasion of composing a thousand verses, whereas the Muses never were to me the occasion of making any.
uz: Musolar ayollardir, va garchi ayollar ularga mos kelmasa ham, bir qarashda ularga o'xshashlik bor; shuning uchun, ular meni boshqa hech narsa bilan xursand qilmadilar, shuning uchun ular meni xursand qilishlari kerak edi; ayniqsa, ayollar ilgari men uchun mingta she'r yozish imkoniyati bo'lgan, ammo Musolar men uchun hech qachon hech qanday yaratish imkoniyati bo'lmagan.

en: They aided me, indeed, and showed me how to compose the verses in ques- tion; and peradventure, in the writing of these present things, all lowly though they be, they have come whiles to abide with me, in token maybe and honour of the likeness that women bear to them; wherefore, in inditing these toys, I stray not so far from Mount Parnassus nor from the Muses as many belike conceive.
uz: Ular menga yordam berishdi, haqiqatan ham, va savollar bo'yicha she'rlarni qanday yozishni ko'rsatdilar; va, ehtimol, hozirgi narsalarni yozishda, ularning barchasi past bo'lsa ham, ular men bilan birga yashash uchun kelishdi, ehtimol va ayollarning ularga bo'lgan o'xshashligini hurmat qilish uchun; shuning uchun, bu o'yinchoqlarni tasvirlashda, men Parnassus tog'idan ham, Musadan ham ko'pchilik o'ylagandek uzoqlashmayman.

en: But what shall we say to those who have such compassion on my hunger that they counsel me provide myself bread?
uz: Lekin ochligimga shunchalik rahm qilganlarga nima deymizki, ular menga o'zimga non berishni maslahat berishadi?

en: Certes, I know not, save that, whenas I seek to imagine in myself what would be their answer, an I should of necessity beseech them thereof, to wit, of bread, methinketh they would reply, “Go seek it among thy fables.” Indeed, aforetime poets have found more thereof among their fables than many a rich man among his treasures, and many, following after their fables, have caused their age to ﬂourish; whereas, on the contrary, many, in seeking to have more bread than they needed, have perished miserably.
uz: Albatta, men bilmayman, faqat o'zimda ularning javobi qanday bo'lishini tasavvur qilmoqchi bo'lganimda, men ulardan, masalan, non so'rasam, ular javob berishadi deb o'ylayman: "Bor ertaklaring orasida qidir." Haqiqatan ham, ilgari shoirlar o'z ertaklarida ko'proq boy odamni o'z xazinalari orasida topdilar va ko'pchilik o'z ertaklariga ergashib, yoshlarini gullab-yashnadi; aksincha, ko'pchilik, ularga kerak bo'lganidan ko'proq non olishni izlab, bechora halok bo'lishdi.

en: What more [shall I say]?
uz: Yana nima deyish mumkin?

en: Let them drive me forth, whenas I ask it of them, not that, Godamercy, I have yet need thereof; and even should need betide, I know with the Apostle Paul both how to abound and suffer need;219 wherefore let none be more careful of me than I am of myself.
uz: Ular meni quvib chiqarishsin, men ulardan so'rasam, Xudo rahm qilsin, menga hali bu narsa kerak emas; va hatto muhtoj bo'lsam ham, men havoriy Pavlus bilan birga qanday boylik va muhtojlikni ham bilaman;219 shuning uchun hech kim mendan o'zimdan ko'ra ko'proq ehtiyot bo'lmasin.

en: For those who say that these things have not been such as I have here set them down, I would fain have them produce the ori- ginals, and an these latter accord not with that of which I write, I will con-
uz: Bu narsalar men bu yerda yozganimdek bo'lmagan deb aytadiganlar uchun, men ularni asl nusxalarni keltirishlarini xohlardim, va agar bularning oxirgisi men yozayotgan narsalarga mos kelmasa, men...

en: fess their objection for just and will study to amend myself; but till other- what than words appeareth, I will leave them to their opinion and follow mine own, saying of them that which they say of me.
uz: Ularning adolat uchun e'tirozini rad etaman va o'zimni tuzatishni o'rganaman; lekin boshqa so'zlar paydo bo'lguncha, ularni o'z fikriga qoldiraman va o'zimnikiga ergashaman, ular haqida men haqimda nima deyishsa, shuni aytaman.

en: Wherefore, deeming that for the nonce I have answered enough, I say that, armed, as I hope to be, with God’s aid and yours, gentlest ladies, and with fair patience, I will fare on with this that I have begun, turning my back to the wind aforesaid and letting it blow, for that I see not that aught can betide me other than that which betideth thin dust, the which a whirl- wind, whenas it bloweth, either stirreth not from the earth, or, an it stir it, carrieth it aloft and leaveth it oftentimes upon the heads of men and upon the crowns of kings and emperors, nay, bytimes upon high palaces and lofty towers, whence an it fall, it cannot go lower than the place wherefrom it was uplifted.
uz: Shuning uchun, men yetarlicha javob berganim uchun, shunday deyman: qurollangan holda, Xudo va sizning yordamingiz bilan, eng muloyim xonimlar va ancha sabr bilan, men boshlagan ishimni davom ettiraman, oldindan aytilgan shamolga orqa burib, uni esishiga qo'yib beraman, chunki men meni yupqa tuproqqa o'xshaydigan boshqa hech narsa ko'rmayapman, u yerdan esayotganda, yoki uni ko'targanda, balandga ko'tarib, odamlarning boshlariga va shohlar va imperatorlar tojlariga ko'tarib qo'yadi, yo'q, baland saroylar va baland minoralarga, undan pastga tushmaydi, u ko'tarilgan joydan pastga tushmaydi.

en: And if ever with all my might I vowed myself to seek to please you in aught, now more than ever shall I address myself thereto; for that I know none can with reason say otherwhat than that I and others who love you do according to nature, whose laws to seek to gainstand demande- th overgreat strength, and oftentimes not only in vain, but to the exceeding hurt of whoso striveth to that end, is this strength employed.
uz: Agar hech qachon bor kuchim bilan sizni nimadir bilan xursand qilishga qasam ichgan bo'lsam, endi har qachongidan ham ko'proq o'zimga murojaat qilaman; chunki men bilaman, men va sizni tabiatga ko'ra sevgan boshqa odamlar, ularning qonunlari buyuk kuchga erishish uchun talab qiladi, va ko'pincha nafaqat behuda, balki shu maqsadda harakat qilayotganlarning haddan tashqari zarariga ham qarshi ishlatiladi.

en: Such strength I confess I have not nor ever desired in this to have; and an I had it, I had liefer lend it to others than use it for myself.
