U o'z xohishidan ko'ra, boshqalarni aldash va barcha Perugiyaliklardan gumonlanayotgan bosh shubhalarni yumshatish uchun unga xotin olib, va bunda omad uning moyilligiga shunchalik mos kelardi, chunki u olgan xotin qalin, qizil sochli, issiq-yonsimon qiz edi, u yolg'ondan ko'ra ikkita erga ega bo'lgan bo'lardi, u esa undan ko'ra ko'proq boshqalarga moyil bo'lgan odamga duch keldi.

en: Becoming, in process of time, aware of this and seeing herself fair and fresh and feeling herself buxom and lusty, she began by being sore incensed thereat and came once and again to unseemly words thereof with her husband, with whom she was well nigh always at variance.
uz: Vaqt o'tishi bilan, buni anglab yetib, o'zini go'zal va yangi his qilib, o'zini to'q va shahvoniy his qilib, u bundan qattiq g'azablanib boshladi va eriga bu haqda bir necha bor noto'g'ri so'zlarga keldi, u bilan doim kelishmovchilikda edi.

en: Then, seeing that this might result rather in her own exhaustion than in the amendment of her husband’s depravity, she said in herself, ‘Yonder caitiff forsaketh me to go of his ribaldries on pattens through the dry, and I will study to carry oth- ers on shipboard through the wet.
uz: Keyin, bu uning erining buzuqligiga o'zgartirish kiritishdan ko'ra ko'proq o'z charchoqlariga olib kelishi mumkinligini ko'rib, u o'zida dedi: "Yonder kaitiff menga qovurg'alari bilan quruqlikdan o'tishga ruxsat beradi, va men boshqalarni kemada namlikdan olib o'tishga o'rganaman."

en: I took him to husband and brought him a ﬁne great dowry, knowing him to be a man and supposing him desireful of that whereunto men are and should be fain; and had I not believed that he would play the part of a man, I had never taken him.
uz: Men uni turmushga olib ketdim va unga juda katta maroy olib keldim, uni erkak ekanligini bilardim va odamlar nimaga ishtiyoqi bor va nimaga ishtiyoqi bor deb o'ylardim; va agar u erkak rolini o'ynashiga ishonmaganimda, hech qachon uni qabul qilmagan bo'lardim.

en: He knew that I was a woman; why, then, did he take me to wife, if women were not to his mind?
uz: U meni ayol ekanligimni bilardi; unda nega u meni xotinlikka oldi, agar ayollar uning xayoliga kelmagan bo'lsa?

en: This is not to be suffered.
uz: Bu azoblanishga arzimaydi.

en: Were I minded to renounce the world, I should have made myself a nun; but, if, choosing to live in the world, as I do, I look for delight or pleasure from yonder fellow, I may belike grow old, ex- pecting in vain, and whenas I shall be old, I shall in vain repent and bemoan myself of having wasted my youth, which latter he himself is a very good teacher and demonstrator how I should solace, showing me by example how I should delect myself with that wherein he delighteth, more by token that this were commendable in me, whereas in him it is exceeding blame- worthy, seeing that I should offend against the laws alone, whereas he of- fendeth against both law and nature.’ Accordingly, the good lady, having thus bethought herself and belike more than once, to give effect privily to these considerations, clapped up an acquaintance with an old woman who showed like Saint Verdiana, that giv- eth
uz: Agar men dunyodan voz kechishga qaror qilgan bo'lsam, o'zimni rohiba qilishim kerak edi; lekin agar, dunyoda yashashni tanlaganimda, xuddi men kabi, o'sha odamdan lazzat yoki rohat izlasam, men behuda qarigan bo'lishim mumkin, va qariganimda, behuda tavba qilaman va yoshligimni behuda sarflaganimdan afsuslanaman, bu uning o'zi juda yaxshi o'qituvchi va men qanday taskin berishim kerakligini ko'rsatuvchi misol bo'lib, bu menga maqtovga loyiq edi, garchi unda bu juda arziydi, chunki men qonunlarga qarshi yolg'iz o'zim haqorat qilishim kerak edi, garchi u ham qonunga qarshi kurashadi.

en: the serpents to eat, and still went to every pardoning, beads in hand, nor ever talked of aught but the lives of the Holy Fathers or of the wounds of St.
uz: ilonlarni yeyish uchun, va baribir har bir kechirimga borardi, qo'lida munchoqlar bor edi, hech qachon Muqaddas Otalarning hayoti yoki Avliyo Maryamning jarohatlaridan boshqa hech narsa haqida gapirmadi.

en: Francis and was of well nigh all reputed a saint, and whenas it seemed to her time, frankly discovered to her her intent.
uz: Fransisk deyarli barcha avliyo deb hisoblanardi va o'z zamoniga o'xshasa ham, unga o'z niyatini ochiqchasiga ochib berdi.

en: ‘Daughter mine,’ replied the beldam, ‘God who knoweth all knoweth that thou wilt do exceeding well,
uz: Qizim,  javob berdi qo'ng'iroqchi,  Hammasini biladigan Xudo sening haddan tashqari yaxshi ish qilishingni biladi,

en: and if for nought else, yet shouldst thou do it, thou and every other young woman, not to lose the time of your youth, for that to whoso hath under- standing, there is no grief like that of having lost one’s time.
uz: Va agar hech narsasiz bo'lsa ham, buni qil, sen va har bir boshqa yosh ayol, yoshliging vaqtini yo'qotmaslik uchun, chunki kimda bir narsa bo'lsa, uning vaqtini yo'qotgandek qayg'u yo'q.

en: And what a devil are we women good for, once we are old, save to keep the ashes about the ﬁre-pot?
uz: Va biz ayollar qariganimizdan so'ng, olov qozoni atrofidagi kulni saqlashdan boshqa qanday shaytonga arziydiganmiz?

en: If none else knoweth it and can bear witness thereof, that do and can I; for, now that I am old, I recognize without avail, but not without very sore and bitter remorse of mind, the time that I let slip, and albeit I lost it not altogether (for that I would not have thee deem me a ninny), still I did not what I might have done; whereof whenas I remember me, seeing myself fashioned as thou seest me at this present, so that thou wouldst ﬁnd none to give me ﬁre to my tinder,288 God knoweth what chagrin I feel.
uz: Agar buni boshqa hech kim bilmasa va guvohlik bera olmasa, buni men ham qila olaman va qila olaman; chunki, endi men keksa bo'lsam, befoyda, lekin juda achchiq va achchiq pushaymonliksiz tan olmayman, o'sha vaqtni qo'yib yuborganimni, hatto uni butunlay yo'qotmagan bo'lsam ham (chunki seni hech kim deb hisoblamayman), men nima qilishim mumkin edi, lekin men buni eslasam, o'zimni hozirgi kunda sen ko'rganingdek shakllantirilganimni ko'rib, o'zimga o't qo'yadigan hech kimni topmasliging uchun, 288 Xudo nimani his qilayotganimni biladi.

en: With men it is not so; they are born apt for a thousand things, not for this alone, and most part of them are of much more account old than young; but women are born into the world for nothing but to do this and bear children, and it is for this that they are prized; the which, if from nought else, thou mayst appre- hend from this, that we women are still ready for the sport; more by token that one woman would tire out many men at the game, whereas many men cannot tire one woman; and for that we are born unto this, I tell thee again that thou wilt do exceeding well to return thy husband a loaf for his ban- nock, so thy soul may have no cause to reproach thy ﬂesh in thine old age.
uz: Erkaklar bilan bunday emas; ular ming narsaga mohir bo'lib tug'iladilar, faqat shu uchun emas, va ularning aksariyati yoshlardan ko'ra ancha katta hisoblanadi; lekin ayollar dunyoga faqat shu ishni qilish va farzand ko'rish uchun tug'iladilar, va shuning uchun ular qadrlanadilar; agar hech narsadan boshqa narsa bo'lsa, shundan ogoh bo'lishing mumkinki, biz ayollar hali ham sportga tayyormiz; ayniqsa, bir ayol o'yinda ko'p erkaklarni charchatadi, lekin ko'p erkaklar bir ayolni charchata olmaydilar; va biz shu sababli tug'ilganmiz, yana bir bor senga aytamanki, sen eringga uning bo'yinturug'i uchun non qaytarishni haddan tashqari yaxshi ko'rasan, shunda joning keksaligingda go'shtingni ayblamasligi kerak.

en: Each one hath of this world just so much as he taketh to himself thereof, and especially is this the case with women, whom it behoveth, much more than men, make use of their time, whilst they have it; for thou mayst see how, when we grow old, nor husband nor other will look at us; nay, they send us off to the kitchen to tell tales to the cat and count the pots and pans; and what is worse, they tag rhymes on us and say, “Tidbits for wenches young;  Gags289 for the old wife’s tongue.” And many another thing to the like purpose.
uz: Har bir inson bu dunyodan o'ziga ma'qul ko'radigan darajada ega, ayniqsa, erkaklardan ko'ra ko'proq ayollarda shunday bo'ladi, ular vaqtdan foydalanib, o'zlarida bor paytda foydalanadilar; chunki ko'rib turibsanki, qariganimizda na er, na boshqa odam bizga qaramaydi; yo'q, bizni oshxonaga yuborishadi, mushukka ertaklar aytib, idish-tovoqlarni sanash uchun; va undan ham yomoni, bizga qofiyalar yopishtirishadi va "Yosh qizlar uchun maslahatlar; Keksa xotin uchun qo'shimchalar" deyishadi. Va shunga o'xshash ko'p narsalar.

en: And that I may hold thee no longer in parley, I tell thee in ﬁne that thou couldst not have discovered thy mind to anyone in the world who can be more useful to thee than I, for that there is no man so high and mighty but I dare tell him what behoveth, nor any so dour or churlish but I know how to supple him aright and bring him to what I will.
uz: Va seni endi hech kimga o'xshatmasligim uchun, senga aniq aytamanki, sen dunyodagi hech kimga sening fikringni mendan ko'ra foydaliroq bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan odamga kashf eta olmas eding, chunki men unga nima kerakligini aytishga jur'at etadigan, yoki unga qanday yordam berishni va uni o'zim xohlagan narsaga olib kelishni biladigan hech kim yo'q.

en: Wherefore do thou but show me who pleaseth thee and after leave me do; but one thing I commend to thee, daughter mine, and that is,
uz: Shuning uchun menga kim sizga yoqishini ko'rsating, keyin meni tashlab keting; lekin senga bir narsani buyuraman, qizim, va bu...

en: that thou be mindful of me, for that I am a poor body and would have thee henceforth a sharer in all my pardonings and in all the paternosters I shall say, so God may make them light and candles for thy dead.’290 With this she made an end of her discourse, and the young lady came to an understanding with her that, whenas she chanced to spy a certain young spark who passed often through that quarter and whose every feature she set out to her, she should know what she had to do; then, giving her a piece of salt meat, she dismissed her with God’s blessing; nor had many days passed ere the old woman brought her him of whom she had bespoken her privily into her chamber, and a little while after, another and another, according as they chanced to take the lady’s fancy, who stinted not to indulge herself in this as often as occasion offered, though still fearful of her husband.
uz: Menga e'tibor ber, chunki men kambag'al tanaman va bundan buyon seni barcha afvlarimda va barcha paternosterlarimda ulushga ega bo'lishini xohlardim, shunda Xudo sening o'liming uchun ularni yorug'lik va shamlar qilsin.

en: It chanced one evening that, her husband being to sup abroad with a friend of his, Ercolano by name, she charged the old woman bring her a youth, who was one of the goodliest and most agreeable of all Perugia, which she promptly did; but hardly had the lady seated herself at table to sup with her gallant, when, behold, Pietro called out at the door to have it opened to him.
uz: Bir kuni kechqurun erining o'zining do'sti Ercolano bilan chet elda kechki ovqat yeyishi bilan, u kampirga Perugiyaning eng yaxshi va xushmuomalalaridan biri bo'lgan bir yigitni olib kelishni buyurdi, buni u darhol qildi; lekin xonim o'zini mehribonligi bilan kechki ovqat yeyishga o'tirganidan ko'p o'tmay, mana, Pietro unga eshikni ochish uchun eshik oldida chaqirib yubordi.

en: She, hearing this, gave herself up for lost, but yet desiring, an she might, to conceal the youth and not having the presence of mind to send him away or hide him elsewhere, made him take refuge under a hen-coop, that was in a shed adjoining the chamber where they were at supper, and cast over him the sacking of a pallet-bed that she had that day let empty.
uz: U buni eshitib, o'zini yo'qotilgan deb taslim qildi, ammo u yoshni yashirishga va uni jo'natishga yoki boshqa joyga yashirishga aqli yetmagan holda, uni kechki ovqatda bo'lgan xonaga tutash joyda joylashgan tovuq to'rga qo'ydi va o'sha kuni bo'sh qoldirgan pallet-krovatning yirtqichini uning ustiga tashladi.

en: This done, she made haste to open to her husband, to whom quoth she, as soon as he entered the house, ‘You have very soon despatched this supper of yours!’ ‘We have not so much as tasted it,’ replied he; and she said, ‘How was that?’ Quoth he, ‘I will tell thee.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u eriga shoshildi va u uyga kirishi bilanoq unga: Siz bu kechki ovqatingizni juda tezda jo'natdingiz! Biz uni tatib ko'rmadik,  deb javob berdi u; va u: Bu qanday edi?  dedi u: Men sizga aytaman.

en: Scarce were we seated at table, Er- colano and his wife and I, when we heard someone sneeze hard by, whereof we took no note the ﬁrst time nor the second; but, he who sneezed sneezing yet a third time and a fourth and a ﬁfth and many other times, it made us all marvel; whereupon Ercolano, who was somewhat vexed with his wife for that she had kept us a great while standing at the door, without opening to us, said, as if in a rage, “What meaneth this?
uz: Kamdan-kam hollarda biz stolga o'tirgan edik, Er-kolano va uning xotini va men, kimdir qattiq aksirganini eshitganimizda, buni birinchi va ikkinchi marta ham e'tiborga olmasdik; lekin, aksirgan odam uchinchi marta, to'rtinchi va beshinchi marta aksirgan bo'lsa, bu hammamizni hayratga soldi; shundan so'ng Erkolano, xotini bizni eshik oldida uzoq vaqt ushlab turgani uchun biroz g'azablangan, bizga ochilmasdan, g'azab bilan go'yo, "Bu nimani anglatadi?" dedi.

en: Who is it sneezeth thus?” And rising from table, made for a stair that stood near at hand and under which, hard by the stairfoot, was a closure of planks, wherein to bestow all manner things, as we see those do every day who set their houses in order.
uz: Kim shunday aksiradi? Va stoldan ko'tarilib, qo'l ostida turgan va uning ostida, zinapoyadan qattiq pastda, taxtaning yopilishi bor edi, u yerda har xil narsalarni sovg'a qilish kerak edi, xuddi har kuni uylarini tartibga soladiganlarni ko'rayotganimizdek.

en: Him- seeming it was from this that came the noise of sneezing, he opened a little door that was therein and no sooner had he done this than there issued forth
uz: U - xuddi bundan aksirish shovqini kelganidek tuyuldi, u ichkarida joylashgan kichik eshikni ochdi va u buni undan oldin qilmagan edi, shundan keyin tashqariga chiqdi.

en: thereof the frightfullest stench of sulphur that might be.
uz: Undan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan eng dahshatli oltingugurt hidi.

en: Somewhat of this smell had already reached us and we complaining thereof, the lady had said, “It is because I was but now in act to bleach my veils with sulphur and after set the pan, over which I had spread them to catch the fumes, under the stair, so that it yet smoketh thereof.” As soon as the smoke was somewhat spent, Ercolano looked into the cup- board and there espied him who had sneezed and who was yet in act to sneeze, for that the fumes of the sulphur constrained him thereto, and in- deed they had by this time so straitened his breast that, had he abidden a while longer, he had never sneezed nor done aught else again.
uz: Bu hid bizga allaqachon yetib kelgan edi va biz undan shikoyat qilardik, xonim aytdi: "Bu men endi pardalarni oltingugurt bilan oqartirish uchun harakat qilayotganim va ustiga tutunlarni tutatish uchun tarqatgan tovani zinapoya ostiga qo'yganim uchundir, shunda u hali ham tutun chiqaradi." Tutun biroz tugagan zahoti, Ercolano stakan taxtasiga qaradi va u yerda aksirgan va aksirmoqchi bo'lganni kuzatdi, chunki oltingugurt tutunlari uni bunga majburlagan edi va aslida ular shu vaqtga kelib uning ko'kragini shunchalik qattiqlashtirgan ediki, u uzoqroq yashiringanida, u boshqa hech qachon aksirmagan edi."

en: Ercolano, seeing him, cried out, “Now, wife, I see why, whenas we came hither awhile ago, we were kept so long at the door, without its being opened to us; but may I never again have aught that shall please me, an I pay thee not for this!” The lady, hearing this and seeing that her sin was discovered, stayed not to make any excuse, but started up from table and made off I know not whither.
uz: Erkolano uni ko'rib, qichqirdi: Endi, xonim, men tushunaman, nega biz bu yerga bir oz vaqt oldin kelganimizda, eshik bizga ochilmasdan shunchalik uzoq vaqt eshik oldida ushlab turilgan edik; lekin hech qachon menga yoqadigan hech narsa bo'lmasin, men senga buning uchun to'lamayman! Xonim buni eshitdi va gunohining aniqlanganini ko'rib, hech qanday bahona topmadi, lekin stoldan turib, qayerga ketayotganini bilmayman.

en: Ercolano, without remarking his wife’s ﬂight, again and again bade him who sneezed come forth; but the latter, who was now at the last gasp, offered not to stir, for all that he could say; whereupon, taking him by one foot, he haled him forth of his hiding-place and ran for a knife to kill him; but I, fearing the police on mine own account, arose and suffered him not to slay him or do him any hurt; nay, crying out and defending him, I gave the alarm to certain of the neighbours, who ran thither and taking the now half- dead youth, carried him forth the house I know not whither.
uz: Erkolano, xotining qochganiga e'tibor bermasdan, qayta-qayta aksirgan odamni tashqariga chiqishni buyurdi; lekin oxirgi nafratlangan odam, aytishi mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsa uchun, qo'zg'almaslikni taklif qildi; shundan so'ng, uni bir oyog'i bilan olib, yashirin joyining tashqarisiga olib chiqib, uni o'ldirish uchun pichoq qidirdi; lekin men, o'z hisobimdan politsiyadan qo'rqib, uni o'ldirishga yoki unga zarar yetkazmaslikka turdim va unga ruxsat berdim; yo'q, baqirib va uni himoya qilib, men u yerga yugurgan qo'shnilarning ba'zilariga signal berdim va yarim o'lik yoshni, uni qayerga olib ketayotganimni bilmayman.

en: Wherefore, our supper being disturbed by these things, I have not only not despatched it, nay, I have, as I said, not even tasted it.’ The lady, hearing this, knew that there were other women as wise as her- self, albeit illhap bytimes betided some of them thereof, and would fain have defended Ercolano’s wife with words; but herseeming that, by blaming others’ defaults, she might make freer way for her own, she began to say, ‘Here be ﬁne doings!
uz: Shuning uchun, kechki ovqatimiz shu narsalardan bezovta bo'lgani uchun, men uni nafaqat jo'natmadim, balki, aytganimdek, hatto tatib ko'rmadim ham." Xonim buni eshitib, o'zi kabi dono boshqa ayollar borligini bilardi, garchi ba'zi hollarda ularning ba'zilariga yomonlik qilgan bo'lsa ham, Ercolano'ning xotinini so'zlar bilan himoya qilgan bo'lar edi; lekin boshqalarni ayblab, o'zi uchun osonroq yo'l ochishi mumkinligini ko'rib, u: "Mana yaxshi ishlar qilinglar!" - deb boshladi.

en: A holy and virtuous lady indeed she must be!
uz: U haqiqatan ham muqaddas va fazilatli ayol bo'lishi kerak!

en: She, to whom, as I am an honest woman, I would have confessed myself, so spir- itually minded meseemed she was!
uz: U, men halol ayol bo'lganim uchun, o'zimni tan olgan bo'lardim, shunchalik ruhiy jihatdan o'ylagandek edi!

en: And the worst of it is that she, being presently an old woman, setteth a mighty ﬁne example to the young.
uz: Va eng yomoni shundaki, u hozir keksa ayol bo'lib, yoshlarga ajoyib namuna bo'lib turibdi.

en: Ac- cursed by the hour she came into the world and she also, who suffereth her- self to live, perﬁdious and vile woman that she must be, the general re- proach and shame of all the ladies of this city, who, casting to the winds her honour and the faith plighted to her husband and the world’s esteem, is not
uz: U dunyoga kelgan soat la'natlangan va u ham, o'zini yashashga majbur qiladigan, xiyonatkor va jirkanch ayol bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan, bu shaharning barcha ayollarining umumiy haqorat va sharmandaligi, u shamollarga o'z sharafini va eriga va dunyo hurmatini bag'ishlagan imonini tashlab,

en: ashamed to dishonour him, and herself with him, for another man, him who is such a man and so worshipful a citizen and who used her so well!
uz: Uni va o'zini u bilan birga boshqa bir odam uchun sharmanda qilishdan uyalgan, bunday odam va shunchalik ibodat qiluvchi fuqaro bo'lgan va undan shunchalik yaxshi foydalangan odam!

en: So God save me, there should be no mercy had of such women as she; they should be put to death; they should be cast alive into the ﬁre and burned to ashes.’ Then, bethinking her of her gallant, whom she had hard by under the coop, she began to exhort Pietro to betake himself to bed, for that it was time; but he, having more mind to eat than to sleep, enquired if there was aught for supper.
uz: Xudo meni asrasin, bunday ayollarga rahm bo'lmasin, ular o'ldirilsin; ular tiriklayin olovga tashlansin va kulga aylantirilsin. Keyin, uni o'zining zodagonidan xotirlab, u uni qovog'i ostida qattiq ushlab qolganini ko'rib, Petrni vaqt kelgani uchun o'zini yotishga unday boshladi; lekin u uxlashdan ko'ra ko'proq ovqat yeyishga qaror qilib, kechki ovqat uchun biror narsa bor-yo'qligini so'radi.

en: ‘Supper, quotha!’ answered the lady.
uz: "Supper, qacha!" deb javob berdi xonim.

en: ‘Truly, we are much used to get supper, whenas thou art abroad!
uz: Haqiqatan ham, biz kechki ovqatga ko'nikib qolganmiz, sen esa chet elda bo'lsang!

en: Dost thou take me for Ercolano’s wife?
uz: Meni Ercolano'ning xotini deb olasanmi?

en: Alack, why dost thou not go to sleep for tonight?
uz: Afsus, nega bugun kechqurun uxlamaysan?

en: How far better thou wilt do!’ Now it chanced that, certain husbandmen of Pietro’s being come that evening with sundry matters from the farm and having put up their asses, without watering them, in a little stable adjoining the shed, one of the latter, being sore athirst, slipped his head out of the hal- ter and making his way out of the stable, went smelling to everything, so haply he might ﬁnd some water, and going thus, he came presently full on the hen-coop, under which was the young man.
uz: Qanchalik yaxshiroq qilmaysan! Endi shunday bo'ldiki, Pietro'ning ba'zi dehqonlari o'sha kechqurun fermadan turli xil ishlar bilan kelib, eshaklarini sug'ormasdan, shedga yaqin bir kichik o'rmaga qo'yishdi, oxirgilaridan biri chanqoq bo'lib, halterdan boshini sirg'alib, o'rmondan chiqib, hamma narsani hidlab ketardi, shunda u biroz suv topishi mumkin edi, va shu tariqa, u hozir to'la tovuqdan keldi, uning ostida yigit bor edi.

en: The latter having, for that it behoved him abide on all fours, put out the ﬁngers of one hand on the ground beyond the coop, such was his luck, or rather let us say, his ill luck, that the ass set his hoof on them, whereupon the youth, feeling an exceeding great pain, set up a terrible outcry.
uz: Oxirgisi, shuning uchun ham to'rt oyoqda turishi kerak edi, bir qo'lining barmoqlarini tuproqqa qo'ydi, go'yo uning omadliligi, to'g'rirog'i, omadsizligi shunday edi, eshak ularning ustiga oyoq qo'ydi, shundan so'ng yoshlar nihoyatda katta azobni his qilib, dahshatli faryod ko'tardilar.

en: Pietro, hearing this, marvelled and per- ceived that the noise came from within the house; wherefore he went out into the shed and hearing the other still clamouring, for that the ass had not lifted up his hoof from his ﬁngers, but still trod hard upon them, said, ‘Who is there?’ Then, running to the hen-coop, he raised it and espied the young man, who, beside the pain he suffered from his ﬁngers that were crushed by the ass’s hoof, was all a-trembling for fear lest Pietro should do him a mischief.
uz: Pietro buni eshitgach, hayratga tushdi va shovqin uy ichidan kelganini angladi; shuning uchun u omboriga chiqdi va boshqa birovning hali ham baqirayotganini eshitdi, chunki eshak barmoqlaridan tuyoqini ko'tarmagan edi, lekin baribir ularga qattiq qadam tashlagan edi, dedi: "U yerda kim bor?" Keyin, tovuqqa yugurib, uni ko'tardi va eshak tuyoqidan ezilgan barmoqlaridan azob chekkan yigitni kuzatdi.

en: The latter, knowing him for one whom he had long pursued for his lewd ends, asked him what he did there, whereto he answered him nothing, but prayed him for the love of God do him no harm.
uz: Oxirgisi, uni uzoq vaqtdan beri o'zining behayo maqsadlari yo'lida izlagan odam ekanligini bilgan holda, undan u yerda nima qilganini so'radi, unga hech narsa javob bermadi, lekin Xudoga bo'lgan muhabbatidan unga zarar yetkazmasligini so'radi.

en: Quoth Pietro, ‘Arise and fear not that I will do thee any hurt; but tell me how thou comest here and for what purpose.’ The youth told him all, whereupon Pietro, no less re- joiced to have found him than his wife was woeful, taking him by the hand, carried him into the chamber, where the lady awaited him with the greatest affright in the world, and seating himself overagainst her, said, ‘But now thou cursedst Ercolano’s wife and avouchedst that she should be burnt and
uz: Quoth Pietro dedi: Tur va senga hech qanday zarar yetkazmasligimdan qorqma; lekin menga bu yerga qanday va nima maqsadda kelganingni ayt. Yigit unga hamma narsani aytdi. Shunda Pietro xotini uni topganidan xursand bolib, uni qolidan ushladi, uni xonaga olib kirdi, u yerda xonim uni dunyodagi eng katta azob bilan kutib turardi va ozi unga qarshi otirardi, dedi: Endi sen Ercolano xotini lanatlading va u yoqilishi kerakligini xabar berding.

en: that she was the disgrace of all you women; why didst thou not speak of thyself?
uz: U siz ayollarning sharmandaligingiz edi; nega o'zingiz haqingizda gapirmading?

en: Or, an thou choosedst not to speak of thyself, how could thy con- science suffer thee to speak thus of her, knowing thyself to have done even as did she?
uz: Yoki, o'zing haqingda gapirmaslikni tanlaganing uchun, qanday qilib sening biliming senga u haqida shunday gapirishga yo'l qo'yishi mumkin edi, o'zing ham u qilganidek qilganingni bilasanmi?

en: Certes, none other thing moved thee thereunto save that you wo- men are all made thus and look to cover your own doings with others’ de- faults; would ﬁre might come from heaven to burn you all up, perverse gen- eration that you are!’ The lady, seeing that, in the ﬁrst heat of the discovery, he had done her no harm other than in words and herseeming she saw that he was all agog with joy for that he held so goodly a stripling by the hand, took heart and said, ‘Of this much, indeed, I am mighty well assured, that thou wouldst have ﬁre come from heaven to burn us women all up, being, as thou art, as fain to us as a dog to cudgels; but, by Christ His cross, thou shalt not get thy wish.
uz: Albatta, seni bunga boshqa hech narsa undamadi, faqatgina sen - odamlar shunday yaratilgan va o'z ishlaringni boshqalar bilan yashirishni xohlaysan - xatolar; osmondan olov kelib, hammangizni yoqib yuborishi mumkin edi, buzuq avlod ekansiz! Xonim, kashfiyotning birinchi issig'ida, unga faqat so'zlar va o'ziga xos ko'rinish bilan zarar yetkazmaganini ko'rib, u shunchalik yaxshi qo'ldan ushlaganidan xursand edi, yuragini oldirdi va dedi: "Bundan, albatta, men juda aminmanki, siz osmondan olov kelib, bizni ayollar bilan birga yoqib yuborasiz, chunki siz bizga it kabi yoqib yuborasiz; lekin, Masihning xochidan, siz o'z xohishingizga erishingni

en: However, I would fain have a little discourse with thee, so I may know of what thou complainest.
uz: Lekin men siz bilan ozgina gaplashishni xohlardim, shunda nima haqida shikoyat qilayotganingizni bilsam.

en: Certes, it were a ﬁne thing an thou shouldst seek to even me with Ercolano’s wife, who is a beat-breast, a smell-sin,291 and hath of her husband what she will and is of him held dear as a wife should be, the which is not the case with me.
uz: Albatta, bu yaxshi narsa edi va sen Ercolano'ning xotini bilan birga menga ham murojaat qilishing kerak edi. Erkolano ko'krakni uradigan, hidli gunohdir. 291 Uning erida u xohlagan narsa bor va u undan xotin bo'lishi kerak bo'lganidek qadrlanadi, bu men bilan sodir bo'lmaydi.

en: For, grant that I am well clad and shod of thee, thou knowest but too well how I fare for the rest and how long it is since thou hast lain with me; and I had liefer go barefoot and rags to my back and be well used of thee abed than have all these things, being used as I am of thee.
uz: Chunki, agar men senga yaxshi kiyim kiygan bo'lsam va senga beparvo bo'lsam, sen qolganlar uchun qanday ahvolimni va sen men bilan birga yotganingdan beri qancha vaqt o'tganini juda yaxshi bilasan; va men yalang'och oyoqlarda va yelkamga latta olib, senga beparvo bo'lishni va senga beparvo bo'lishni, men senga beparvo bo'lganim kabi senga beparvo bo'lishni afzal ko'rardim.

en: For understand plainly, Pietro; I am a woman like other wo- men and have a mind unto that which other women desire; so that, an I pro- cure me thereof, not having it from thee, thou hast no call to missay of me therefor; at the least, I do thee this much honour that I have not to do with horseboys and scald-heads.’ Pietro perceived that words were not like to fail her for all that night; wherefore, as one who recked little of her, ‘Wife,’ said he, ‘no more for the present; I will content thee aright of this matter; but thou wilt do us a great courtesy to let us have somewhat to sup withal, for that meseemeth this lad, like myself, hath not yet supped.’ ‘Certes, no,’ answered the lady, ‘he hath not yet supped; for we were sitting down to table, when thou camest in thine ill hour.’ ‘Go, then,’ rejoined Pietro, ‘contrive that we may sup, and after I will order this matter on such wise that
uz: Chunki aniq tushunaman, Pietro; men boshqa erkaklar kabi ayolman va boshqa ayollar xohlagan narsaga ko'z yugurtiraman; shuning uchun, men uni davolayman, sendan olmayman, shuning uchun meni sog'inishga hech qanday sabab yo'q; hech bo'lmaganda, men senga shunday hurmat ko'rsatamanki, otbo'yinlar va qo'zg'alish bilan shug'ullanmayman."

en: thou shalt have no cause to complain.’ The lady, ﬁnding that her husband was satisﬁed, arose and caused straightway reset the table; then, letting bring the supper she had prepared, she supped merrily in company with her caitiff of a husband and
uz: Sizda shikoyat qilishga hech qanday sabab bo'lmaydi. Xonim erining rozi ekanligini bilib, o'rnidan turdi va darhol stolni o'rnatdi; so'ngra, tayyorlagan kechki ovqatni olib kelgach, erining xizmatkori bilan birga xursandchilik bilan ovqatlandi va...

en: After supper, what Pietro devised for the satisfaction of all three hath escaped my mind; but this much I know that on the following morning the youth was escorted back to the public place, not altogether cer- tain which he had the more been that night, wife or husband.
uz: Kechki ovqatdan so'ng, Pietro uchalasi ham qoniqish uchun o'ylab topgan narsa esimdan chiqib ketdi; lekin men bilamanki, ertasi kuni ertalab yigit jamoat joyiga qaytarildi, umuman olganda u o'sha kechada ko'proq xotin yoki er bo'lgan edi.

en: Wherefore, dear my ladies, this will I say to you, ‘Whoso doth it to you, do you it to him’; and if you cannot presently, keep it in mind till such time as you can, so he may get as good as he giveth.” Dioneo having made an end of his story, which had been less laughed at by the ladies [than usual], more for shamefastness than for the little delight they took therein, the queen, seeing the end of her sovranty come, rose to her feet and putting off the laurel crown, set it blithely on Elisa’s head, say- ing, “With you, madam, henceforth it resteth to command.” Elisa, accepting the honour, did even as it had been done before her, in that, having ﬁrst, to the satisfaction of the company, taken order with the seneschal for that whereof there was need for the time of her governance, she said, “We have many a time heard how, by dint of smart sayings and ready repartees and prompt advisements,
uz: Shuning uchun, aziz xonimlar, sizga shunday deyman: Kim sizga shunday qilsa, siz ham unga shunday qiling; va agar hozircha iloji bo'lmasa, uni imkon qadar yaxshilash uchun yodda tuting. Dioneo o'z hikoyasini tugatdi, bu hikoya xonimlar tomonidan (odatdagidan ko'ra) kam kuldirilgan edi, ularda olingan kichik lazzatdan ko'ra ko'proq uyatchilik uchun, malika o'z hukmronligining oxiri kelganini ko'rib, oyoqqa turdi va lavr tojini yechdi, uni Elishaning boshiga yopishtirib qo'ydi, Siz bilan, xonim, shuning uchun buyruq berishga majbur, deb aytdi.

en: many have availed with an apt retort292 to take the edge off other folks’ teeth or to fend off imminent perils; and, for that the matter is goodly and may be useful,293 I will that tomorrow, with God’s aid, it be discoursed within these terms, to wit, OF WHOSO, BEING ASSAILED WITH SOME JIBING SPEECH, HATH VINDICATED HIMSELF OR HATH WITH SOME READY REPLY OR ADVISEMENT ESCAPED LOSS, PERIL OR SHAME.” This was much commended of all, whereupon the queen, rising to her feet, dismissed them all until supper time.
uz: Ko'pchilik boshqa odamlarning tishlaridan qochish yoki yaqinlashib kelayotgan xavflardan himoya qilish uchun mohirona javobni qo'llagan; va, shuning uchun bu masala yaxshi va foydali bo'lishi mumkin, 293 Men ertaga, Xudoning yordami bilan, bu shartlar doirasida muhokama qilinishini xohlayman, ya'ni, QAYSI QANDAY JABBATLI nutq bilan ASOD ETILGAN, O'ZIGA O'ZNI YAXSHI YOKI O'ZGA O'ZGA O'RG'RILGAN YOKI O'ZGA O'RG'RILGAN, XAVF YOKI SHAMGA O'TKAZGAN.

en: The honourable company, seeing her risen, stood up all and each, according to the wonted fashion, applied himself to that which was most agreeable to him.
uz: Hurmatli kompaniya, uning tirilganini ko'rib, hamma o'rnidan turdi va har biri odatdagi uslubga ko'ra, o'ziga eng yoqqan narsaga murojaat qildi.

en: But, the crickets having now given over singing, the queen let call everyone and they betook them- selves to supper, which being despatched with merry cheer, they all gave themselves to singing and making music, and Emilia having, at the queen’s commandment, set up a dance, Dioneo was bidden sing a song, whereupon he straightway struck up with “Mistress Aldruda, come lift up your fud-a, for I bring you, I bring you, good tidings.” Whereat all the ladies fell a- laughing and especially the queen, who bade him leave that and sing anoth- er.
uz: Ammo, qichqiriqlar endi qo'shiq aytishni tashlab, malika hammaga qo'ng'iroq qildi va ular ularni kechki ovqatga chaqirdilar, bu xursandchilik bilan jo'natildi, ularning hammasi o'zlarini qo'shiq aytishga va musiqa yaratishga bag'ishladilar, Emilia esa malika buyrug'iga ko'ra raqsga tushdi, Dioneoga qo'shiq aytishga buyurildi, shundan so'ng u darhol "Xonim Aldruda, keling, ko'taring, chunki men sizni olib kelaman, men sizga xushxabar keltiraman" deb qo'ydi.

en: Quoth Dioneo, “Madam, had I a tabret, I would sing ‘Come truss your
uz: Quoth Dioneo, Xonim, agar menda tabret bo'lsa, men kuylagan bo'lardim Keling, sizning...

en: coats, I prithee, Mistress Burdock,’ or ‘Under the olive the grass is’; or will you have me say ‘The waves of the sea do great evil to me’?
uz: "Paltoslar, men go'zalman, Bekasi Burdock," yoki "Zaytun ostida o't bor"; yoki "Dengiz to'lqinlari menga katta zarar yetkazadi" deyishimga majbur qilasizmi?

en: But I have no tabret, so look which you will of these others.
uz: Lekin menda tabret yo'q, shuning uchun bu boshqalardan qaysi birini xohlasangiz, qarang.

en: Will it please you have ‘Come forth unto us, so it may be cut down, like a May in the midst of the meadows’?” “Nay,” answered the queen; “give us another.” “Then,” said Di- oneo, “shall I sing, ‘Mistress Simona, embarrel, embarrel!
uz: Sizdan "Bizga chiqing, o'tloqlar o'rtasida may kabi kesilishi mumkin" deb so'rasam maylimi? "Yo'q," dedi malika; "boshqa bering." "Unda," dedi Di-oneo, "men kuylayman: "Xonim Simona, uyal, uyal!"

en: It is not the month of October’?” Quoth the queen, laughing, “Ill luck to thee, sing us a goodly one, an thou wilt, for we will none of these.” “Nay, madam,” re- joined Dioneo, “fash not yourself; but which then like you better?
uz: "Bu oktyabr oyi emasmi?" Qirolicha kuldi: "Senga omad tilayman, bizga yaxshi bir qo'shiq ayt, sen xohlaysan, chunki biz bularning hech birini xohlamaymiz." "Yo'q, xonim," dedi Dioneo yana qo'shilib, "o'zingni yomon ko'rma; lekin unda senga qaysi biri yaxshiroq yoqadi?"

en: I know more than a thousand.
uz: Men mingdan ortiq narsani bilaman.

en: Will you have ‘This my shell an I prick it not well,’ or ‘Fair and softly, husband mine’ or ‘I’ll buy me a cock, a cock of an hun- dred pounds sterling’?”294 Therewithal the queen, somewhat provoked, though all the other ladies laughed, said, “Dioneo, leave jesting and sing us a goodly one; else shalt thou prove how I can be angry.” Hearing this, he gave over his quips and cranks and forthright fell a-singing after this fashion: O Love, the amorous light  That beameth from yon fair one’s lovely eyes  Hath made me thine and hers in servant-guise.
uz: Sizda "Bu mening qobig'im va men uni yaxshi tishlamayman", yoki "Odil va mayin, erim" yoki "Men menga xo'roz, o'ralgan funt sterlingdan xo'roz sotib olaman" bo'ladimi?294 Shundan so'ng malika biroz g'azablanib, garchi qolgan barcha xonimlar kulishsa ham, dedi: "Dioneo, bizni hazillashib, yaxshilab kuyla; aks holda qanday qilib men g'azablanishim mumkinligini isbotlaysan." Buni eshitgach, u to'g'ri bilaklari va tirnoqlarini tashladi va shu tarzda qo'shiq aytdi: "Ey Sevgi, go'zal ko'zlaringdan keladigan shahvoniy nur meni o'ziga va o'zining xizmatkoriga aylantirdi."

en: The splendour of her lovely eyes, it wrought  That ﬁrst thy ﬂames were kindled in my breast,  Passing thereto through mine;  Yea, and thy virtue ﬁrst unto my thought  Her visage fair it was made manifest,  Which picturing, I twine  And lay before her shrine  All virtues, that to her I sacriﬁce,  Become the new occasion of my sighs.
uz: Uning go'zal ko'zlarining ulug'vorligi shunday bo'ldiki, avval sening olovlaring mening ko'kragimda yondi, mening ko'kragim orqali o'tib bordi; Ha, va sening fazilating birinchi o'ylimga Uning go'zal yuzi namoyon bo'ldi, Uni tasvirlab, Men barcha fazilatlarni uning ziyoratgohi oldida yotqizaman, unga qurbonlik qilaman, Mening ohlarimning yangi vazifasi bo'lsin.

en: Thus, dear my lord, thy vassal am I grown  And of thy might obediently await  Grace for my lowliness;  Yet wot I not if wholly there be known  The high desire that in my breast thou’st set  And my sheer faith, no less,  Of her who doth possess
uz: Shunday qilib, aziz hazratim, men sizning vassalingizman va sizning qudratingizdan itoatkorlik bilan kamtarligim uchun marhamat kutaman; lekin agar butunlay ko'kragimda siz o'rnatgan baland istak va mening sof imonim ma'lum bo'lsa edi, hech qanday kam emas, kimga egalik qilsam.

en: My heart so that from none beneath the skies,  Save her alone, peace would I take or prize.
uz: Qalbim shundayki, osmon ostidagi hech kimdan, Uni yolg'iz qutqar, tinchlik olsam yoki mukofot olsam.

en: Wherefore I pray thee, sweet my lord and sire,  Discover it to her and cause her taste  Some scantling of thy heat  Tome-ward —for thou seest that in the ﬁre,  Loving, I languish and for torment waste  By inches at her feet —  And eke in season meet  Commend me to her favour on such wise  As I would plead for thee, should need arise.295 Dioneo, by his silence, showing that his song was ended, the queen let sing many others, having natheless much commended his.
uz: Shunday ekan, iltimos qilaman, ey xo'jayinim va rafiqam, uni unga ochib ber va uning ta'mini tatib ko'rgin. Sening issig'ingning bir qismi Tom-wardga tushadi. Chunki sen o'tda ko'rasan, Sevgan, men azob chekaman va oyoqlari ostida bir necha dyuym azob chekaman. Va agar mavsumda uchrashsam, senga iltijo qilganimdek, meni uning marhamatiga buyur.

en: Then, somedele of the night being spent and the queen feeling the heat of the day to be now overcome of the coolness of the night, she bade each at his pleasure betake himself to rest against the ensuing day.
uz: Keyin, tunning bir qismi o'tib, malika kunning issig'ini his qilib, endi tunning salqinligidan g'olib bo'ldi, u har bir kishi o'z xohishiga ko'ra keyingi kunga qarshi dam olishni buyurdi.

en: Here endeth the Fifth Day of the Decameron.
uz: Mana Dekameronning beshinchi kuni tugaydi.

en: DAY THE SIXTH INTRODUCTION Here beginneth the sixth day of the Decameron wherein under the governance of Elisa is discoursed of whoso being assailed with some jibing speech hath vindicated himself or hath with some ready reply or advisement escaped loss, peril or shame.
uz: OLTINCHI KUN Kirish Bu yerda Dekameronning oltinchi kuni boshlanadi, unda Elisa hukmronligi ostida kimki qandaydir g'azablantiruvchi nutq bilan hujumga uchragan bo'lsa, o'zini oqlagan yoki qandaydir tayyor javob yoki maslahat bilan yo'qotish, xavf yoki sharmandalikdan qutulgan bo'lsa, muhokama qilinadi.

en: The moon, being now in the middest heaven, had lost its radiance and every part of our world was bright with the new coming light, when, the queen arising and letting call her company, they all with slow step fared forth and rambled over the dewy grass to a little distance from the fair hill, holding various discourse of one thing and another and debating of the more or less goodliness of the stories told, what while they renewed their laughter at the various adventures related therein, till such time as the sun mounting high and beginning to wax hot, it seemed well to them all to turn homeward.
uz: Oy, hozir eng o'rta osmonda bo'lgani uchun, o'z nurini yo'qotdi va dunyoimizning har bir qismi yangi kelayotgan nur bilan yorqin edi. Qirolicha turib, o'z kompaniyasini chaqirganida, ular sekin qadamlar bilan oldinga chiqib, go'zal tepalikdan biroz uzoqroqqacha bo'lgan ilohiy o'tlar ustida sayr qilishdi, bir narsa va boshqa haqida turli xil nutq so'zlashdi va hikoyalarning ko'pmi yoki kammi yaxshiligi haqida bahslashdilar. Ular u bilan bog'liq turli sarguzashtlarga nisbatan kulglarini yangilashardilar, quyosh balandga ko'tarilib, issiq nur sochishni boshlaguncha, ularning barchasiga uyga qaytish yaxshi tuyuldi.

en: Wherefore, reversing their steps, they returned to the palace and there, by the queen’s commandment, the tables being already laid and everything strewn with sweet-scented herbs and fair ﬂowers, they addressed them- selves to eat, ere the heat should grow greater.
uz: Shuning uchun, qadamlarini teskari o'girib, ular saroyga qaytdilar va u yerda, malika buyrug'iga ko'ra, stollar allaqachon yotqizilgan va hamma narsa shirin hidli o'tlar va chiroyli gullar bilan to'ldirilgan holda, ular ularga murojaat qilishdi - issiqlik kuchayib ketishidan oldin o'zlari ovqatlanish uchun.

en: This being joyously accom- plished, ere they did otherwhat, they sang divers goodly and pleasant can- zonets, after which some went to sleep, whilst some sat down to play at chess and other some at tables and Dioneo fell to singing, in concert with Lauretta, of Troilus and Cressida.
uz: Bu quvonch bilan amalga oshirildi, ular boshqa narsa qilishlaridan oldin, diverslar yaxshi va yoqimli kan-zonlarni kuylashdi, shundan so'ng ba'zilar uxlashga ketishdi, ba'zilar esa shaxmat o'ynashga o'tirishdi, boshqalari esa stollarda o'tirishdi va Dioneo Lauretta, Troilus va Cressida bilan birgalikda qo'shiq aytishga tushdi.

en: Then, the hour come for their reas- sembling after the wonted fashion,296 they all, being summoned on the part of the queen, seated themselves, as of their usance, about the fountain; but, as she was about to call for the ﬁrst story, there befell a thing that had not yet befallen there, to wit, that a great clamour was heard by her and by all, made by the wenches and serving-men in the kitchen.
uz: Keyin, odatdagi uslubga ko'ra o'zlarining aql-idroklari uchun soat keldi. 296 Ularning barchasi, malika tomonidan chaqirilgan holda, odatlariga ko'ra, favvora atrofida o'tirishdi; lekin, u birinchi hikoyani chaqirishga tayyor bo'lganida, u yerda hali sodir bo'lmagan narsa sodir bo'ldi, ya'ni, u va hamma tomonidan, oshxonadagi qizlar va xizmatchilar tomonidan qilingan katta shovqin eshitildi.

en: The seneschal, being called and questioned who it was that cried thus and what might be the occasion of the turmoil, answered that the clamour was between Licisca and Tindaro, but that he knew not the cause thereof, being but then come thither to make them bide quiet, whenas he had been summoned on her part.
uz: Senesxal chaqirilib, shunday qichqirayotgan kim ekanligi va tartibsizlikning sababi nima bo'lishi mumkinligi so'ralganda, shovqin Licisca va Tindaro o'rtasida ekanligini, lekin buning sababini bilmasligini, lekin keyin ularni tinchlantirish uchun u yerga kelishini, chunki u uning tomondan chaqirilgan edi, deb javob berdi.

en: The queen bade him incontinent fetch thither the two offenders and they being come, enquired what was the cause of their clamour; whereto Tindaro offering to reply, Licisca, who was well in years and somewhat overmasterful, being heated with the outcry she had made, turned to him with an angry air and said, “Mark this brute of a man who dareth to speak before me, whereas I am!
uz: Qirolicha unga ikki jinoyatchini u yerga olib kelishni buyurdi va ular kelib, ularning shovqinining sababi nima ekanligini so'radilar. Shunda Tindaro javob berishni taklif qildi: "Licisca, yoshida yaxshi va biroz ustasi, u aytgan baqiriqdan jahli chiqib, g'azablangan holda unga o'girilib dedi: "Mening oldimda gapirishga jur'at etayotgan odamning bu shafqatsizligiga e'tibor bering, men esa shundayman!"

en: Let me speak.” Then, turning again to the queen, “Madam,” quoth she, “this fellow would teach me, for- sooth, to know Sicofante’s wife and neither more nor less than as if I had not been familiar with her, would fain give me to believe that, the ﬁrst night her husband lay with her, Squire Maul297 made his entry into Black Hill298 by force and with effusion of blood; and I say that it is not true; nay, he entered there in peace and to the great contentment of those within.
uz: Keling, gapirsam. Keyin, yana qirolichaga murojaat qilib, Xonim, dedi u, bu odam menga, albatta, Sicofantening xotinini bilishni orgatardi va xuddi men uni tanimasagandek, undan ham kam emas, balki ishonishga imkon berardi, erining u bilan yotgan birinchi kechasida, Squire Maul297 Black Hill298 ga kuch va qon tokilishi bilan kirgan edi; va men aytaman, bu rost emas; yoq, u u yerga tinch va ichkaridagilarning katta mamnuniyatidan kirdi.

en: Marry, this fellow is simple enough to believe wenches to be such ninnies that they stand to lose their time, abiding the commodity of their fathers and brothers, who six times out of seven tarry three or four years more than they should to marry them.
uz: Uylang, bu yigit qizlarni shunday to'qqizlik ekanligiga ishonish uchun yetarlicha oddiyki, ular o'z vaqtlarini yo'qotishga tayyor bo'lishadi, otalari va aka-ukalarining mol-mulklariga berilib ketishadi, ular ularga turmushga chiqishlari kerak bo'lganidan ko'ra yetti tadan olti barobar ko'proq, uch yoki to'rt yilga ko'proq vaqt sarflashadi.

en: Well would they fare, forsooth, were they to wait so long!
uz: Qaniydi, agar ular bunchalik uzoq kutishsa, yaxshi bo'lardi!

en: By Christ His faith (and I should know what I say, when I swear thus) I have not a single gossip who went a maid to her husband; and as for the wives, I know full well how many and what tricks they play their husbands; and this blockhead would teach me to know women, as if I had been born yesterday.” What while Licisca spoke, the ladies kept up such a laughing that you might have drawn all their teeth; and the queen imposed silence upon her a good half dozen times, but to no purpose; she stinted not till she had said her say.
uz: Iso Masihning imoniga qasam ichganimda (va men nima deyishimni bilishim kerak edi) eriga xizmatkor bo'lib ketgan birorta ham g'iybatim yo'q; va xotinlarga kelsak, ular erlariga qancha va qanday hiyla o'ynashlarini yaxshi bilaman; va bu kalta odam menga ayollarni bilishni o'rgatardi, xuddi kecha tug'ilgandek.

en: When she had at last made an end of her talk, the queen turned to Dioneo and said, laughing, “Dioneo, this is a matter for thy jurisdiction; wherefore, when we shall have made an end of our stories, thou shalt pro- ceed to give ﬁnal judgment thereon.” Whereto he answered promptly, “Madam, the judgment is already given, without hearing more of the mat- ter; and I say that Licisca is in the right and opine that it is even as she saith and that Tindaro is an ass.” Licisca, hearing this, fell a-laughing and turning to Tindaro, said, “I told thee so; begone and God go with thee; thinkest thou thou knowest better than I, thou whose eyes are not yet dry?299 Gramercy, I
uz: U nihoyat gapini tugatgach, malika Dioneoga o'girilib kuldi va dedi: Dioneo, bu sizning huquqingizga tegishli masala; shuning uchun, hikoyalarimizni tugatganimizdan so'ng, bu haqda yakuniy hukm chiqarishni to'xtating. U zudlik bilan javob berdi: Xonim, hukm allaqachon berilgan, hech narsa eshitmagan holda; va men aytyapmanki, Liceca o'ngda va u xuddi u Tindaro eshak deb aytganidek, deb o'ylayapti. Liceca buni eshitib, kuldi va tindaroga o'girilib dedi: Men aytdim; boring va Xudo bilan birga boring; sen o'zingni mendan yaxshiroq bilasan, sen hali quruq emassan.

en: have not lived here below for nothing, no, not I!” And had not the queen with an angry air imposed silence on her and sent her and Tindaro away, bidding her make no more words or clamour, an she would not be ﬂogged, they had had nought to do all that day but attend to her.
uz: "Men bu yerda bekorga yashamaganman, yo'q, men emasman!" Va qirolicha g'azablangan havoda unga sukut saqlab, uni va Tindaroni jo'natmagan edi, unga boshqa gapirmaslikni yoki shovqin chiqarmaslikni buyurgan edi, aks holda uni qamchilashmagan bo'lardi, ularning o'sha kuni unga g'amxo'rlik qilishdan boshqa hech qanday ishi yo'q edi.

en: When they were gone, the queen called on Filomena to make a beginning with the day’s stories and she blithely began thus:
uz: Ular ketganlaridan so'ng, malika Filomenani kun hikoyalaridan boshlashga chaqirib, shunday dedi:

en: THE FIRST STORY A gentleman engageth to Madam Oretta to carry her a-horseback with a story, but, telling it disorderly, is prayed by her to set her down again.
uz: BIRINCHI HIKOYA Bir janob Madam Orettaga uni bir hikoya bilan otda olib yurish uchun yollashadi, lekin tartibsiz tarzda aytib, uni yana o'rnatish uchun duo qiladi.

en: “Young ladies, like as stars, in the clear nights, are the ornaments of the heavens and the ﬂowers and the leaf-clad shrubs, in the Spring, of the green ﬁelds and the hillsides, even so are praiseworthy manners and goodly dis- course adorned by sprightly sallies, the which, for that they are brief, be- seem women yet better than men, inasmuch as much speaking is more for- bidden to the former than to the latter.
uz: Yosh xonimlar, xuddi yulduzlar kabi, tiniq tunlarda, osmonning bezaklari, gullar va bargli butalar kabi, bahorda, yashil dalalarda va tepaliklarda ham maqtovga sazovor xulq-atvorlar va yorqin salliylar bilan bezatilgan yaxshi xulq-atvorlar bor, ular qisqacha bo'lgani uchun ayollar erkaklardan ham yaxshiroq ko'rinadi, chunki ko'p gapirganda avvalgilarga oxirgilarga qaraganda ko'proq iltijo etiladi.

en: Yet, true it is, whatever the cause, whether it be the meanness of our300 understanding or some particular grudge borne by heaven to our times, that there be nowadays few or no wo- men left who know how to say a witty word in due season or who, an it be said to them, know how to apprehend it as it behoveth; the which is a gener- al reproach to our whole sex.
uz: Lekin, rost bo'lsa-da, sabab nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, bizning 300 tushunchamizning maydaligi yoki osmon tomonidan zamonimizga yetkazilgan qandaydir nafrat bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, hozirgi kunda o'z vaqtida aqlli so'zni qanday aytishni biladigan yoki ularga aytilsa, uni zarur bo'lganidek qabul qilishni biladigan odamlar kam yoki umuman qolmaydi; bu butun jinsimiz uchun umumiy aybdir.

en: However, for that enough hath been said aforetime on the subject by Pampinea,301 I purpose to say no more thereof; but, to give you to understand how much goodliness there is in witty say- ings, when spoken in due season, it pleaseth me to recount to you the cour- teous fashion in which a lady imposed silence upon a gentleman.
uz: Ammo, bu haqda Pampinea tomonidan avval ham aytilgan bo'lsa, 301 bundan ortiq gapirmoqchi emasman; lekin, o'z vaqtida aytilganda, dono so'zlarda qanchalik yaxshilik borligini tushunish uchun, bir xonim bir janobga qanday odob bilan jimlik o'rnatganini sizga aytib berishdan mamnunman.

en: As many of you ladies may either know by sight or have heard tell, there was not long since in our city a noble and well-bred and well-spoken gen- tlewoman, whose worth merited not that her name be left unsaid.
uz: Ko'pchiligingiz ko'rganingiz yoki eshitganingizdek, yaqinda bizning shaharda shunday olijanob, yaxshi tarbiyalangan va yaxshi gapiradigan ayol paydo bo'lgan edi, uning qadri uning ismi aytilmasligiga arzimagan edi.

en: She was called, then, Madam Oretta and was the wife of Messer Geri Spina.
uz: U holda u Madam Oretta deb atalgan va Messer Geri Spinaning rafiqasi edi.

en: She chanced to be, as we are, in the country, going from place to place, by way of diversion, with a company of ladies and gentlemen, whom she had that day entertained to dinner at her house, and the way being belike somewhat long from the place whence they set out to that whither they were all pur- posed to go afoot, one of the gentlemen said to her, ‘Madam Oretta, an you
uz: U tasodifan, xuddi biz kabi, qishloqda bo'lib, joydan joyga, chalg'ish yo'li bilan, bir guruh xonimlar va janoblar bilan birga bo'lib, o'sha kuni u uyida kechki ovqatga taklif qildi. Ular ketayotgan joydan uzoqroq bo'lgan yo'l, ularning hammasi yo'lga qo'yilganiga o'xshardi, janoblardan biri unga dedi: "Xonim Oretta,

en: will, I will carry you a-horseback great part of the way we have to go with one of the ﬁnest stories in the world.’ ‘Nay, sir,’ answered the lady, ‘I pray you instantly thereof; indeed, it will be most agreeable to me.’ Master cava- lier, who maybe fared no better, sword at side than tale on tongue, hearing this, began a story of his, which of itself was in truth very goodly; but he, now thrice or four or even half a dozen times repeating one same word, anon turning back and whiles saying, ‘I said not aright,’ and often erring in the names and putting one for another, marred it cruelly, more by token that he delivered himself exceedingly ill, having regard to the quality of the per- sons and the nature of the incidents of his tale.
uz: "Men senga otda yuraman, dunyodagi eng yaxshi hikoyalardan biri bilan borishimiz kerak bo'lgan yo'lning katta qismini." Yo'q, janob,  javob berdi xonim, Sizdan darhol iltimos qilaman; haqiqatan ham, bu menga eng yoqadi. Master cava-li, balki undan ham yaxshiroq ish ko'rmagan, tilga qilichdan ko'ra, buni eshitib, o'z hikoyasini boshladi, bu o'zi juda yaxshi edi; lekin u, endi uch marta yoki to'rt marta yoki hatto yarim o'n marta bir xil so'zni takrorlab, orqaga o'girilib, "Men noto'g'ri aytdim," dedi va ko'pincha ismlarda xato qilib, bir-biriga qo'yib, uni shafqatsizlarcha yo'qotgan edi, ko'proq o'zini o'g'illarining tabiatiga va voqealariga nisbatan haddan tashqari yomon ko'rsatgan edi."

en: By reason whereof, Madam Oretta, hearkening to him, was many a time taken with a sweat and failing of the heart, as she were sick and near her end, and at last, being unable to brook the thing any more and seeing the gentleman engaged in an imbroglio from which he was not like to extricate himself, she said to him pleasantly, ‘Sir, this horse of yours hath too hard a trot; wherefore I pray you be pleased to set me down.’ The gentleman, who, as it chanced, understood a hint better than he told a story, took the jest in good part and turning it off with a laugh, fell to discoursing of other matters and left unﬁnished the story that he had begun and conducted so ill.”
uz: Shuning uchun ham, Oretta xonim unga quloq solib, ko'p vaqt terlab va yuragi ishlamay yurardi, chunki u kasal edi va oxiriga yaqin edi, va nihoyat, bu narsani endi ko'ra olmasligi va janobning o'zini qo'yib yuborishni xohlamaydigan imbrogliyo bilan shug'ullanganini ko'rib, u unga yoqimli tarzda dedi: "Janob, bu otingiz juda qattiq yuradi; shuning uchun sizdan iltimos qilaman, meni tushirishingizni so'rayman."

en: THE SECOND STORY Cisti the baker with a word of his fashion maketh Messer Geri Spina sensible of an indiscreet request of his.
uz: IKKINCHI HIKOYA Nonvoy Sisti o'z moda so'zi bilan Messer Geri Spina'ni uning beparvo so'roviga ishontirdi.

en: Madam Oretta’s saying was greatly commended of all, ladies and men, and the queen bidding Pampinea follow on, she began thus: “Fair ladies, I know not of mine own motion to resolve me which is the more at fault, whether nature in ﬁtting to a noble soul a mean body or fortune in imposing a mean condition upon a body endowed with a noble soul, as in one our townsman Cisti and in many another we may have seen it happen; which Cisti being gifted with a very lofty spirit, fortune made him a baker.
uz: Madam Oretta'ning so'zi hammaga juda maqtovga sazovor bo'ldi, xonimlar va erkaklar, va malika Pampeniyani davom ettirishni buyurdi, u shunday boshladi: "Adolatli xonimlar, men o'z xohishim bilan meni hal qilishni bilmayman, qaysi biri ko'proq aybdor, tabiat oliyjanob ruhga oddiy tanani moslashda yoki boylik bilan oliyjanob ruhga ega bo'lgan tanani oddiy holatga solishda, xuddi bizning bir shaharchimiz Kistida va boshqa ko'plarida sodir bo'lganini ko'rgan bo'lsak; Kisti juda yuksak ruh bilan sovg'a qilingan, boylik uni novvoyga aylantirdi.

en: And for this, certes, I should curse both nature and fortune like, did I not know the one to be most discreet and the other to have a thousand eyes, albeit fools picture her blind; and I imagine, therefore, that, being exceeding well-advised, they do that which is oftentimes done of human beings, who, uncertain of future events, bury their most precious things, against their occasions, in the meanest places of their houses, as being the least suspect, and thence bring them forth in their greatest needs, the mean place having the while kept them more surely than would the goodly chamber.
uz: Va buning uchun, albatta, men tabiatni ham, taqdirni ham la'natlashim kerak edi, xuddi shunday, men birinchisini eng yashirin va ikkinchisini mingta ko'zga ega ekanligini bilmasmidim, garchi ahmoqlar uni ko'r deb bilsalar ham; va men tasavvur qilaman, shuning uchun ular haddan tashqari oqilona bo'lgan holda, kelajakdagi voqealarni bilmagan holda, o'zlarining eng qimmatbaho narsalarini, o'z uylarining eng arzon joylariga, eng kam gumon qilgandek ko'mib, ularni eng katta ehtiyojlarida olib kelishadi, chunki o'sha joy ularni yaxshi odamlardan ko'ra ko'proq saqlagan bo'ladi.

en: And so, meseemeth, do the governors of the world hide oftentimes their most precious things under the shadow of crafts and conditions reputed most mean, to the end that, bringing them forth therefrom in time of need, their lustre may show the brighter.
uz: Shunday qilib, dunyoning hokimlari ko'pincha o'zlarining eng qimmatbaho narsalarini eng arzimas deb hisoblangan hunarmandchilik va sharoitlar soyasida yashirishadi, toki ularni zarur paytda undan olib chiqib, ularning yaltirog'i yanada yorqinroq ko'rinishi mumkin.

en: Which how Cisti the baker made manifest, though in but a triﬂing matter, restoring to Messer Geri Spina (whom the story but now told of Madam Oretta, who was his wife, hath recalled to my memory) the eyes of the understanding, it pleaseth me to show you in a very short story.
uz: Kisti novvoy Messer Geri Spinaga (hozir uning xotini bo'lgan Madam Oretta haqida hikoya qilingan) tushunish ko'zlarini qanday namoyon etganini, garchi mayda masala bo'lsa ham, juda qisqa hikoyada ko'rsatishdan mamnunman.

en: I must tell you, then, that Pope Boniface, with whom Messer Geri Spina was in very great favour, having despatched to Florence certain of his gen-
uz: Shuni aytishim kerakki, Rim Papasi Bonifik, Messer Geri Spina bilan juda katta hurmatda bo'lgan, Florensiyaga o'z genini aniq jo'natgan edi.

en: tlemen on an embassy concerning sundry important matters of his, they lighted down at the house of Messer Geri and he treating the pope’s affairs in company with them, it chanced, whatever might have been the occasion thereof, that he and they passed well nigh every morning afoot before Santa Maria Ughi, where Cisti the baker had his bakehouse and plied his craft in person.
uz: Elchixonada uning turli muhim masalalari bo'yicha mehmonlar, ular Messer Gerining uyini yoritishdi va u ular bilan birga Rim Papasining ishlarini olib borayotgan edi, ehtimol, buning sababi nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, u va ular har kuni ertalab Santa Maria Ughi oldida, qayerda nonvoy Cisti o'z pishirishxonasi bor edi va o'z hunarini shaxsan o'ynardilar.

en: Now, albeit fortune had appointed Cisti a humble enough condition, she had so far at the least been kind to him therein that he was grown very rich and without ever choosing to abandon it for any other, lived very splen- didly, having, amongst his other good things, the best wines, white and red, that were to be found in Florence or in the neighbouring country.
uz: Endi, garchi omad Cistiga yetarlicha kamtarona holat tayinlagan bo'lsa ham, u unga shu qadar mehribon edi, u juda boy bo'lib ketdi va hech qachon boshqa hech kimga tashlab ketishni tanlamadi, juda to'yimli hayot kechirardi, uning boshqa yaxshi narsalari orasida Florensiyada yoki qo'shni mamlakatda topiladigan eng yaxshi vinolar, oq va qizil vinolar bor edi.

en: Seeing Messer Geri and the pope’s ambassadors pass every morning before his door and the heat being great, he bethought himself that it were a great courtesy to give them to drink of his good white wine; but, having regard to his own condition and that of Messer Geri, he deemed it not a seemly thing to presume to invite them, but determined to bear himself on such wise as should lead Messer Geri to invite himself.
uz: Messer Gerini va Papa elchilarini har kuni ertalab uning eshigi oldida o'tib ketayotganini va issiqlik juda kuchli bo'lganini ko'rib, u o'zini ularga o'zining yaxshi oq vinosini ichirish katta odob deb hisoblardi; lekin o'zining va Messer Gerining ahvolini hisobga olgan holda, ularni taklif qilishga jur'at etish o'rinli narsa emas deb hisobladi, balki o'zini Messer Gerini taklif qilishga undashi kerak bo'lganidek oqilona tutishga qaror qildi.

en: Accordingly, having still on his body a very white doublet and an apron fresh from the wash, which bespoke him rather a miller than a baker, he let set before his door, every morning, towards the time when he looked for Messer Geri and the ambassadors to pass, a new tinned pail of fair water and a small pitcher of new Bolognese ware, full of his good white wine, to- gether with two beakers, which seemed of silver, so bright they were, and seated himself there, against they should pass, when, after clearing his throat once or twice, he fell to drinking of that his wine with such a relish that he had made a dead man’s mouth water for it.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, tanasida juda oq qo'shaloq va yuvilgan yangi pervan bo'lgani uchun, uni nonvoy emas, balki tegirmonchi o'ziga xos qilib ko'rsatgan holda, u har kuni ertalab, Messer Geri va elchilarni kutgan paytga kelib, uning eshigi oldiga yangi idishdagi toza suv va uning yaxshi oq vinolaridan iborat kichik bir banka Bologniya mahsulotlarini qo'ydi. Ular kumushdan ko'rinadigan, juda yorqin edi, va u yerda o'tirardi, ular o'tishi kerak edi, qachonki bir-ikki marta tomoqni ochgandan so'ng, u o'sha sharobidan shunday zavq bilan ichishga tushardi, hatto u o'lik odamning og'ziga suv tayyorlagan edi.

en: Messer Geri, having seen him do thus one and two mornings, said on the third, ‘How now, Cisti?
uz: Messer Geri, uni bir-ikki ertalab shunday qilayotganini ko'rib, uchinchi kuni dedi: Endi nima, Cisti?

en: Is it good?’ Whereupon he started to his feet and said, ‘Ay is it, Sir; but how good I cannot give you to understand, except you taste thereof.’ Messer Geri, in whom either the nature of the weather or belike the relish with which he saw Cisti drink had begotten a thirst, turned to the ambassadors and said, smiling, ‘Gentlemen, we shall do well to taste this honest man’s wine; belike it is such that we shall not repent thereof.’ Accordingly, he made with them towards Cisti, who let bring a goodly settle out of his bake- house and praying them sit, said to their serving-men, who pressed forward to rinse the beakers, ‘Stand back, friends, and leave this ofﬁce to me, for that I know no less well how to skink than to wield the baking-peel; and look you not to taste a drop thereof.’ So saying, he with his own hands
uz: Yaxshimi? Shundan so'ng u oyoqlari bilan turdi va dedi: Ha, shundaymi, janob; lekin men sizga buni tatib ko'rmaguningizcha tushunishga qanday yaxshilik bera olmayman. Messer Geri, unda ob-havo tabiati yoki Cisti ichimligini ko'rgan lazzat bilan chanqoqlikni keltirib chiqargan edi, elchilarga o'girilib, tabassum bilan dedi: Janoblar, biz bu halol odamning vinosini tatib ko'rsak yaxshi bo'ladi; go'yo biz undan tavba qilmaymiz. Shunga ko'ra, u ularga o'z pishirish uyinidan yaxshi joy olib kelishga ruxsat beradi va ularni o'tirishga buyuradi.

en: washed out four new and goodly beakers and letting bring a little pitcher of his good wine, busied himself with giving Messer Geri and his companions to drink, to whom the wine seemed the best they had drunken that great while; wherefore they commended it greatly, and well nigh every morning, whilst the ambassadors abode there, Messer Geri went thither to drink in company with them.
uz: To'rtta yangi va yaxshi piyolalarni yuvib tashladi va o'zining yaxshi vinosidan ozgina idish olib kelishga ruxsat berdi, o'zini Messer Geri va uning hamrohlariga ichish bilan band qildi. Ular uchun bu vino o'sha paytdagi eng yaxshi ichilgandek tuyuldi; shuning uchun ular uni juda maqtashdi va har kuni ertalab, elchilar u yerda qolganda, Messer Geri u yerga ular bilan birga ichish uchun bordi.

en: After awhile, their business being despatched and they about to depart, Messer Geri made them a magniﬁcent banquet, whereto he bade a number of the most worshipful citizens and amongst the rest, Cisti, who would, however, on no condition go thither; whereupon Messer Geri bade one of his serving-men go fetch a ﬂask of the baker’s wine and give each guest a half beaker thereof with the ﬁrst course.
uz: Biroz vaqt o'tgach, ularning ishi jo'natilgan va ular ketmoqchi bo'lganida, Messer Geri ularga ajoyib ziyofat tayyorladi. U yerda u eng sadoqatli fuqarolarning bir qismini va qolganlardan Cistini taklif qildi, ular hech qanday shart bilan u yerga bormas edilar; shundan so'ng Messer Geri o'z xizmatkorlaridan birini nonvoyning vinosini olib kelishga va har bir mehmonga undan yarim stakanni birinchi taom bilan berishga buyurdi.

en: The servant, despiteful most like for that he had never availed to drink of the wine, took a great ﬂagon, which when Cisti saw, ‘My son,’ said he, ‘Messer Geri sent thee not to me.’ The man avouched again and again that he had, but, getting none other answer, returned to Messer Geri and reported it to him.
uz: Xizmatkor, hech qachon sharob ichishga tayyor bo'lmagani uchun eng yaxshi ko'ringan bo'lishiga qaramay, katta qadah oldi. Cisti "O'g'lim," deb ko'rgach, u dedi: "Messer Geri seni menga yubormadi." Erkak yana va yana o'zi borligini aytdi, lekin boshqa javob ololmay, Messer Geriga qaytib, unga xabar berdi.

en: Quoth he, ‘Go back to him and tell him that I do indeed send thee to him; and if he still make thee the same answer, ask him to whom I send thee, [an it be not to him.]’ Accord- ingly, the servant went back to the baker and said to him, ‘Cisti, for certain Messer Geri sendeth me to thee and none other.’ ‘For certain, my son,’ answered the baker, ‘he doth it not.’ ‘Then,’ said the man, ‘to whom doth he send me?’ ‘To the Arno,’ replied Cisti; which answer when the servant re- ported to Messer Geri, the eyes of his understanding were of a sudden opened and he said to the man, ‘Let me see what ﬂask thou carriedst thither.’ When he saw the great ﬂagon aforesaid, he said, ‘Cisti saith sooth,’ and giving the man a sharp reproof, made him take a sortable ﬂask, which when Cisti saw, ‘Now,’ quoth he, ‘I know full well that he sendeth thee to me,’ and cheerfully ﬁlled it unto him.
uz: U aytdi: Uni oldiga qaytib bor va unga ayt, men seni unga yuboraman, agar u senga ham xuddi shunday javob bersa, seni kimga yuborayotganimni so'ra. Shunga rozi bo'ldi, xizmatchi nonvoyga qaytib kelib, unga dedi: Custy, albatta, Messer Geri meni senga yuboradi, boshqa hech kimga emas. Albatta, o'g'lim,  nonvoychi javob berdi:  u buni qilmaydi.  Unda,  u meni kimga yuboryapti? dedi,  Arnoga javob berdi.

en: Then, that same day, he let ﬁll a little cask with the like wine and causing carry it softly to Messer Geri’s house, went presently thither and ﬁnding him there, said to him, ‘Sir.
uz: Shundan so'ng, o'sha kuni u ozgina idishni shunga o'xshash vino bilan to'ldirdi va uni Messer Gerining uyiga sekin olib bordi, u yerga borib, uni u yerda topdi va unga dedi: Janob.

en: I would not have you think that the great ﬂagon of this morning frightened me; nay, but, me- seeming that which I have of these past days shown you with my little pitchers had escaped your mind, to wit, that this is no household wine,302 I wished to recall it to you.
uz: Sizni bugun ertalabki katta qadah meni qo'rqitdi deb o'ylamasligingizni xohlardim; yo'q, lekin, men - xuddi shu o'tgan kunlarda kichik idishlarim bilan sizga ko'rsatgan narsalar xotirangizdan chiqib ketgandek, ya'ni bu uy vino emas, 302 buni sizga eslatib o'tmoqchiman.

en: But, now, for that I purpose no longer to be your steward thereof, I have sent it all to you; henceforward do with it as it pleaseth you.’ Messer Geri set great store by Cisti’s present and rendering
uz: Lekin, endi men bu haqda sizning boshlig'ingiz bo'lishni xohlamayman, shuning uchun hammasini sizga yubordim; bundan buyon u sizga yoqqanidek qilsin." Messer Geri Cisti'ning hozirgi va taqdimotini juda qadrladi.

en: him such thanks as he deemed sortable, ever after held him for a man of great worth and for friend.”
uz: Unga shunday minnatdorchiliklar berganki, u uni do'st sifatida va juda qadrli inson sifatida his qilganidan keyin ham, uni tanlash mumkin deb hisoblardi.

en: THE THIRD STORY Madam Nonna de’ Pulci, with a ready retort to a not altogether seemly pleasantry, imposeth silence on the Bishop of Florence.
uz: UCHINCHI HIKOYA Madam Nonna de Pulci, umuman yoqimtoy ko'rinmayotganga tayyor javob bilan, Florensiya yepiskopiga sukut o'rnatadi.

en: Pampinea having made an end of her story and both Cisti’s reply and his liberality having been much commended of all, it pleased the queen that the next story should be told by Lauretta, who blithely began as follows, “Joc- und ladies, ﬁrst Pampinea and now Filomena have spoken truly enough touching our little worth and the excellence of pithy sayings, whereto that there may be no need now to return, I would fain remind you, over and above that which hath been said on the subject, that the nature of smart say- ings is such that they should bite upon the hearer, not as the dog, but as the sheep biteth; for that, an a trait bit like a dog, it were not a trait, but an af- front.
uz: Pampiyena o'z hikoyasini tugatdi va Kistining javobi ham, uning bag'rikengligi ham ham hammaga maqtovga sazovor bo'ldi. Qirolichaning keyingi hikoyani Lauretta aytib berishi ma'qul keldi. Lauretta shunday dedi: Joc- und ladies, first Pampinea and now Philomena have spoken truly enough touching our little worth and the excellence of pityy sayings, where there may not be a need to return now, I would like to remind you, above and above what has been said on the subject, that the nature of smart sayings is such that they should bite the listener, not like the dog, but like the sheep; for that, a trait like a dog, it was not a trait, but a

en: The right mean in this was excellently well hit both by Madam Or- etta’s speech and Cisti’s reply.
uz: Bu boradagi to'g'ri o'rtacha ma'no Madam Or-ettaning nutqi va Cisti'ning javobi tomonidan juda yaxshi aniqlandi.

en: It is true that, if a smart thing be said by way of retort, and the answerer biteth like a dog, having been bitten on like wise, meseemeth he is not to be blamed as he would have been, had this not been the case; wherefore it behoveth us look how and with whom, no less than when and where, we bandy jests; to which considerations, a prelate of ours, taking too little heed, received at least as sharp a bite as he thought to give, as I shall show you in a little story.
uz: To'g'ri, agar aqlli narsa javob berish yo'li bilan aytilsa va javob beruvchi itdek tishlasa, dono kabi tishlangan bo'lsa, demak, u shunday bo'lmaganida, qanday ayblanmagan bo'lardi; shuning uchun biz qachon va qayerda, qanday va kim bilan, hech bo'lmaganda, yomon hazillashamiz; bunga e'tibor qaratgan holda, bizning bir prelatimiz, juda kam e'tibor qaratgan holda, hech bo'lmaganda o'zi bermoqchi bo'lganidek o'tkir tish oldi, buni sizga kichik hikoyada ko'rsataman.

en: Messer Antonio d’Orso, a learned and worthy prelate, being Bishop of Florence, there came thither a Catalan gentleman, called Messer Dego della Ratta, marshal for King Robert, who, being a man of a very ﬁne person and a great amorist, took a liking to one among other Florentine ladies, a very fair lady and granddaughter to a brother of the said bishop, and hearing that her husband, albeit a man of good family, was very sordid and miserly, agreed with him to give him ﬁve hundred gold ﬂorins, so he would suffer
uz: Messer Antonio dOrso, oqimishli va munosib prelat, Florensiya yepiskopi bolgan, u yerga Kataloniyalik janob keldi. U yerda Messer Dego della Ratta, Robert qirolining marshali bor edi. U juda yaxshi inson va katta amorist bolgani uchun, boshqa Florensiyalik ayollardan biriga yoqdi. U juda gozal xonim va shu yepiskopning akasiga nabirasi edi. Uning eri, garchi yaxshi oila azosi bolsa ham, juda xunuk va bechora ekanligi haqida eshitib, unga besh yuz oltin florin berishga rozi boldi, shunda u...

en: him lie a night with his wife.
uz: U xotini bilan bir kecha yotadi.

en: Accordingly, he let gild so many silver pop- lins,303 a coin which was then current, and having lain with the lady, though against her will, gave them to the husband.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u juda ko'p kumush pop-linlarni 303 tangaga tilla soldi, u o'sha paytda dolzarb edi va xonim bilan yotgach, uning xohishiga qarshi bo'lsa ham, ularni eriga berdi.

en: The thing after coming to be known everywhere, the sordid wretch of a husband reaped both loss and scorn, but the bishop, like a discreet man as he was, affected to know noth- ing of the matter.
uz: Bu narsa hamma joyda ma'lum bo'lgandan so'ng, erining bechora bechori ham yo'qotish, ham haqoratni yig'di, lekin yepiskop, o'zi kabi xotirjam odam kabi, bu masalani bilmaslikka ta'sir qildi.

en: Wherefore, he and the marshal consorting much together, it chanced, as they rode side by side with each other, one St.
uz: Shuning uchun, u va marshal ko'p birga bo'lishganda, bir-birlari bilan yonma-yon ketayotganlarida, bir St. paydo bo'ldi.

en: John’s Day, viewing the ladies on either side of the way where the mantle is run for,304 the prelate espied a young lady —of whom this present pestilence hath bereft us and whom all you ladies must have known, Madam Nonna de’ Pulci by name, cousin to Messer Alessio Rinucci, a fresh and fair young woman, both well-spoken and high-spirited, then not long before married in Porta San Piero —and pointed her out to the marshal; then, being near her, he laid his hand on the latter’s shoulder and said to her, ‘Nonna, how deemest thou of this gallant?
uz: Jon kuni, yo'lning har ikki tomonidagi ayollarga qarab, manti 304 yilga cho'zilgan joyda, ruhoniy hozirgi vabo bizni yo'qotgan yosh xotinni kuzatdi va siz barcha xonimlar bilgan bo'lsangiz kerak, Madam Nonna de' Pulci ismli, Messer Alessio Rinucchining amakivachchasi, yangi va chiroyli yosh ayol, ham yaxshi gapiradigan, ham yuqori ruhli, keyin ko'p o'tmay Porta San Pieroda turmushga chiqqan edi  va uni marshalga ko'rsatdi; keyin, uning yaqinida bo'lganda, u oxirgisining yelkasiga qo'lini qo'ydi va unga dedi: "Nonna, bu gallantni qanday deb hisoblaysan?"

en: Thinkest thou thou couldst make a conquest of him?’ It seemed to the lady that those words somewhat trenched upon her honour and were like to sully it in the eyes of those (and there were many there) who heard them; wherefore, not thinking to purge away the soil, but to return blow for blow, she promptly answered, ‘Maybe, sir, he would not make a conquest of me; but, in any case, I should want good money.’ The marshal and the bishop, hearing this, felt themselves alike touched to the quick by her speech, the one as the author of the cheat put upon the bishop’s brother’s granddaughter and the other as having suffered the affront in the person of his kinswoman, and made off, shamefast and silent, without look- ing at one another or saying aught more to her that day.
uz: Siz unga g'alaba qozona olasiz deb o'ylaysizmi? Xonimga bu so'zlar uning sharafiga biroz chuqur tushgandek tuyuldi va ularni eshitganlarning ko'z o'ngida (va u yerda ko'pchilik bor edi); shuning uchun, tuproqni tozalashni o'ylamay, balki zarba evaziga qaytishni o'ylamay, u tezda javob berdi: Balki, janob, u menga g'alaba qozonmas edi; lekin, har qanday holatda, men yaxshi pul xohlardim. Marshal va yepiskop buni eshitib, o'zlarini uning nutqi bilan tezda ta'sirlangan his qildilar.

en: Thus, then, the young lady having been bitten, it was not forbidden her to bite her biter with a retort.”
uz: Shunday qilib, yosh xonim chaqilganidan so'ng, uning tishlagini javob bilan tishlashi taqiqlanmagan edi.

en: THE FOURTH STORY Chichibio, cook to Currado Gianﬁgliazzi, with a ready word spoken to save himself, turneth his master’s anger into laughter and escapeth the punishment threatened him by the latter.
uz: TO'RTINCHI HIKOYA Chichibio, Kurrado Gianfigliazziga pishiruvchi, o'zini qutqarish uchun tayyor so'z bilan, xo'jayinining g'azabini kulgiga aylantiradi va oxirgi tomonidan tahdid qilingan jazodan qutuladi.

en: Lauretta being silent and Nonna having been mightily commended of all, the queen charged Neiﬁle to follow on, and she said, “Although, lovesome ladies, a ready wit doth often furnish folk with words both prompt and use- ful and goodly, according to the circumstances, yet fortune whiles cometh to the help of the fearful and putteth of a sudden into their mouths such an- swers as might never of malice aforethought be found of the speaker, as I purpose to show you by my story.
uz: Lauretta jim bo'lib, Nonna hammaga juda maqtovga sazovor bo'lgani uchun, malika Neifilega davom etishni buyurdi va u dedi: Agarki, mehribon xonimlar, tayyor hazil ko'pincha odamlarni tezkor, to'liq va yaxshi so'zlar bilan ta'minlaydi, vaziyatga qarab, ammo omad qo'rqoqlarga yordam beradi va to'satdan ularning og'ziga shunday qilichlarni so'zlashuvchi haqida hech qachon o'ylamagan yomonlikdan paydo bo'lishi mumkin, buni sizga o'z hikoyam orqali ko'rsatmoqchiman.

en: Currado Gianﬁgliazzi, as each of you ladies may have both heard and seen, hath still been a noble citizen of our city, liberal and magniﬁcent, and leading a knightly life, hath ever, letting be for the present his weightier do- ings, taken delight in hawks and hounds.
