uz: Kurrado Gianfigliazzi, har biringiz, xonimlar, eshitganingiz va ko'rganingizdek, hali ham shahrimizning olijanob fuqarosi, liberal va ulug'vor, ritsarona hayot kechirgan, hozircha eng og'ir ishlaridan voz kechib, kovaklar va itlardan zavq olgan.

en: Having one day with a falcon of his brought down a crane and ﬁnding it young and fat, he sent it to a good cook he had, a Venetian hight Chichibio, bidding him roast it for supper and dress it well.
uz: Bir kuni o'zining varrak bilan kranni tushirib, uni yosh va semiz deb topgach, u uni yaxshi oshpazga, Venetsiyalik baland Chichibioga yubordi va kechki ovqatga qovurib, yaxshilab kiydirishni buyurdi.

en: Chichibio, who looked the new-caught gull he was, trussed the crane and setting it to the ﬁre, proceeded to cook it diligently.
uz: Chichibio, yangi qo'lga tushirilgan Olmosga o'xshab, kranni qo'ydi va olovga qo'ydi, keyin uni astoydil pishirishga kirishdi.

en: When it was all but done and gave out a very savoury smell, it chanced that a wench of the neighbourhood, Brunetta by name, of whom Chichibio was sore enam- oured, entered the kitchen and smelling the crane and seeing it, instantly be- sought him to give her a thigh thereof.
uz: Hammasi tugagandan so'ng va juda mazali hid tarqatgach, bir voqea sodir bo'ldi: qo'shnilardan bir qiz, nomi Brunetta, Chichibio uni juda yaxshi ko'rgan edi, oshxonaga kirdi va kranni hidlab, uni ko'rib, darhol undan bir sonini berishni so'radi.

en: He answered her, singing, and said, ‘Thou shalt not have it from me, Mistress Brunetta, thou shalt not have it from me.’ Whereat she, being vexed, said to him, ‘By God His faith, an thou give it me not, thou shalt never have of me aught that shall pleasure thee.’ In brief, many were the words between them and at last, Chichibio,
uz: U unga javob berib, kuyladi va dedi: Mendan olmaysan, Brunetta xonim, mendan olmaysan. Ammo u xafa bolib, unga dedi: Xudoga qasamki, menga berma, sendan hech qachon senga yoqadigan hech narsa olmaysan. Qisqacha qilib aytganda, ularning orasida kop sozlar bor edi va nihoyat, Chichibio,

en: not to anger his mistress, cut off one of the thighs of the crane and gave it her.
uz: Xo'jayiniga jahl chiqarmaslik uchun, kranning sonlaridan birini kesib, unga berdi.

en: The bird being after set before Messer Currado and certain stranger guests of his, lacking a thigh, and the former marvelling thereat, he let call Chichibio and asked him what was come of the other thigh; whereto the liar of a Venetian answered without hesitation, ‘Sir, cranes have but one thigh and one leg.’ ‘What a devil?’ cried Currado in a rage.
uz: Qush keyin Ser Kurrado va uning ba'zi notanish mehmonlari oldida o'rnashib, sonini yo'qligi va avvalgi hayratlanarli bo'lgani uchun, u Chichibioni chaqirib, boshqa sonidan nima kelganini so'radi; unga venetsiyalik yolg'onchi hech ikkilanmasdan javob berdi: "Janob, kranlarning faqat bir son va bir oyog'i bor." "Qanday jin?" - deb jahl bilan baqirdi Kurrado.

en: ‘They have but one thigh and one leg?
uz: Ularning faqat bitta sonlari va bitta oyog'i bor-ku?

en: Have I never seen a crane before?’ ‘Sir,’ replied Chichi- bio, ‘it is as I tell you, and whenas it pleaseth you, I will cause you see it in the quick.’ Currado, out of regard for the strangers he had with him, chose not to make more words of the matter, but said, ‘Since thou sayst thou wilt cause me see it in the quick, a thing I never yet saw or heard tell of, I desire to see it tomorrow morning, in which case I shall be content; but I swear to thee, by Christ His body, that, an it be otherwise, I will have thee served on such wise that thou shalt still have cause to remember my name to thy sor- row so long as thou livest.’ There was an end of the talk for that night; but, next morning, as soon as it was day, Currado, whose anger was nothing abated for sleep, arose, still full of wrath, and bade bring the horses; then, mounting Chichibio upon a rouncey, he carried him off towards a
uz: Men hech qachon kranni ko'rmaganmanmi?  Janob,  javob berdi Chichi- bio, Men sizga aytganimdek, va sizga yoqqanida, men uni tezda ko'rsataman. Currado, u bilan birga bo'lgan notanish odamlarni hurmat qilib, bu haqda ko'proq gapirmaslikni tanladi, balki dedi: Sen menga tezda ko'rsatasan, deb aytgandan beri, men hali ko'rmagan yoki eshitmagan narsani, men uni ertaga ertalab ko'rmoqchiman, shunda men rozi bo'laman; lekin men sizga qasam ichaman, Masihning tanasiga qasam ichaman, agar shunday bo'lsa, men sizga mening ismimni tirik qolganingizcha eslashga sabab bo'ladigan darajada xizmat qilaman. O'sha tun uchun gapning oxiri bor edi, chunki u g'azabga to'la edi, lekin keyin, u...

en: water- course, on whose banks cranes were still to be seen at break of day, saying, ‘We shall soon see who lied yestereve, thou or I.’ Chichibio, seeing that his master’s wrath yet endured and that needs must be made good his lie and knowing not how he should avail thereunto, rode after Currado in the greatest fright that might be, and fain would he have ﬂed, so but he might.
uz: Suv yo'li, uning qirg'og'ida kun yorishi bilan kranlar hali ko'rinardi, "Yaqinda kim yolg'on gapirganini ko'ramiz, senmi yoki menmi" deyishardi. Chichibio xo'jayinining g'azabi hali ham chidaganini va uning yolg'onini yaxshilash kerakligini ko'rib, unga qanday foyda olishni bilmay, Currado ortidan eng katta qo'rquvda bordi va u qochib ketgan bo'lardi, lekin u...

en: But, seeing no way of escape, he looked now before him and now behind and now on either side and took all he saw for cranes standing on two feet.
uz: Ammo, qochishning hech qanday yo'lini ko'rmay, u hozir oldinga, hozir orqaga va endi har ikki tomonga qaradi va ikki oyoqda turgan kranlar uchun ko'rgan hamma narsani oldi.

en: Presently, coming near to the river, he chanced to catch sight, before any other, of a round dozen of cranes on the bank, all perched on one leg, as they use to do, when they sleep; whereupon he straightway showed them to Currado, saying, ‘Now, sir, if you look at those that stand yonder, you may very well see that I told you the truth yes- ternight, to wit, that cranes have but one thigh and one leg.’ Currado, seeing them, answered, ‘Wait and I will show thee that they have two,’ and going somewhat nearer to them, he cried out, ‘Ho!
uz: Hozir daryoga yaqinlashganda, u boshqalardan ko'ra ko'proq qirg'oqda o'nlab kranlarni ko'rishga muvaffaq bo'ldi, ularning barchasi uxlayotganda bir oyoqqa qo'yilgan, xuddi odatdagidek. Shundan so'ng u ularni Curradoga ko'rsatdi va dedi: "Endi, janob, agar u yerda turganlarga qarasangiz, men sizga rostini aytganimni juda yaxshi ko'rishingiz mumkin - uch kecha, ya'ni, kranlarning faqat bir son va bir oyog'i bor edi." Currado ularni ko'rib, javob berdi: "Kutib turing, men ularning ikkita borligini ko'rsataman," va ularga biroz yaqinroq borgach, u baqirib dedi: "Ho!

en: Ho!’ At this the cranes, putting down the other leg, all, after some steps, took to ﬂight; whereupon Currado said to him, ‘How sayst thou now, malapert knave that thou art?
uz: Ho! Shundan so'ng kranlar, boshqa oyog'ini qo'yib, bir necha qadamdan so'ng, hammasi uchib ketishdi; shundan so'ng Kurrado unga dedi: Endi qanday deysan, yomon odam, sen o'zing ekanligingni?

en: Deemest thou they have two legs?’ Chichibio, all confounded and knowing not
uz: Ularning ikki oyog'i bor deb o'ylaysanmi? Chichibio, hammasi xijolatda va bilmayapti.

en: whether he stood on his head or his heels,305 answered, ‘Ay, sir; but you did not cry, “Ho!
uz: U boshida turdimi yoki poshnalarida, 305 kishi javob berdi: Ha, janob; lekin siz yig'lamading: Ha!

en: Ho!” to yesternight’s crane; had you cried thus, it would have put out the other thigh and the other leg, even as did those yonder.’ This reply so tickled Currado that all his wrath was changed into mirth and laughter and he said, ‘Chichibio, thou art in the right; indeed, I should have done it.’ Thus, then, with his prompt and comical answer did Chichibio avert ill luck and made his peace with his master.”
uz: "Ho!"  kecha kunidagi kranga; agar sen shunday qichqirsang, u boshqa sonni va boshqa oyog'ini, xuddi u yerdagilar kabi chiqarib tashlagan bo'lardi. Bu javob Kurradoni shunchalik g'azablantiradiki, u xursandchilik va kulgiga aylandi va u dedi: "Chichibio, sen haqsan; haqiqatan ham, men buni qilishim kerak edi." Shunday qilib, o'zining tezkor va kulgili javobi bilan Chichibio omadsizlikni oldini oldi va xo'jayini bilan tinchlik o'rnatdi.

en: THE FIFTH STORY Messer Forese da Rabatta and Master Giotto the painter coming from Mugello, each jestingly rallieth the other on his scurvy favour.
uz: BESHINCHI HIKOYA Messer Forese da Rabatta va Mugello'dan kelayotgan rassom Ustoz Giotto, har biri o'zining sharpalik marhamatiga hazillashib, bir-birini qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

en: Neiﬁle being silent and the ladies having taken much pleasure in Chichi- bio’s reply, Pamﬁlo, by the queen’s desire, spoke thus: “Dearest ladies, it chanceth often that, like as fortune whiles hideth very great treasures of worth and virtue under mean conditions, as hath been a little before shown by Pampinea, even so, under the sorriest of human forms are marvellous wits found to have been lodged by nature; and this very plainly appeared in two townsmen of ours, of whom I purpose brieﬂy to entertain you.
uz: Negafile jim bo'lgani va xonimlar Chichi-bioning javobidan juda zavqlanib, Pamfilo, malika xohishiga ko'ra, shunday dedi: "Azizimli xonimlar, ko'pincha shunday bo'ladiki, xuddi omad Pampiyaning biroz oldin ko'rsatganidek, o'rtacha sharoitlarda juda katta boylik va fazilat xazinalarini yashirgandek, shunday bo'lsa ham, tabiat tomonidan yotqizilgan ajoyib aql-idrok mavjud; va bu juda aniq bizning ikki shaharchimizda paydo bo'ldi, ulardan men sizni qisqacha ko'ngilxush qilish uchun mo'ljallanganman."

en: For that the one, who was called Messer Forese da Rabatta, though little of person and misshapen, with a ﬂat camoys face, that had been an eyesore on the shoulders of the foulest cadger in Florence, was yet of such excellence in the interpretation of the laws, that he was of many men of worth reputed a very treasury of civil right; whilst the other, whose name was Giotto, had so excellent a genius that there was nothing of all which Nature, mother and mover of all things, presenteth unto us by the ceaseless revolution of the heavens, but he with pencil and pen and brush depicted it and that so closely that not like, nay, but rather the thing itself it seemed, insomuch that men’s visual sense is found to have been oftentimes deceived in things of his fashion, taking that for real which was but depictured.
uz: Chunki Messer Forese da Rabatta deb atalgan, garchi kam odam bo'lsa ham va noto'g'ri shakllangan bo'lsa ham, tekis loyqa yuzli, Florensiyadagi eng bema'ni odamning yelkasiga ko'z ochadigan ko'rinish bo'lgan odam, qonunlarni talqin qilishda hali shunchalik a'lo darajada edi, ko'pchilik odamlar uchun u fuqarolik huquqining juda qimmatli xazinasi edi; shu bilan birga, uning ismi Giotto bo'lgan boshqa bir zot, tabiatning, barcha narsalarning onasi va harakatlantiruvchisining bizga osmonning tinimsiz inqilobini taqdim etadigan hech narsa yo'q edi, lekin u uni qalam, ruchka va cho'tka bilan tasvirlagan va shunday yaqinroq, balki o'ziga o'xshardi, chunki odamlarning qadri ko'p hollarda o'z uslubida aldangan deb topilgan edi, lekin u...

en: Wherefore, he having brought back to the light this art, which had for many an age lain buried under the errors of certain folk who painted more to divert the eyes of the ignorant than to please the understanding of the judicious, he may de- servedly be styled one of the chief glories of Florence, the more so that he bore the honours he had gained with the utmost humility and although, while he lived, chief over all else in his art, he still refused to be called mas-
uz: Shuning uchun, u ko'p asrlar davomida nodonlarning ko'zlarini chalg'itish uchun emas, balki donolarning tushunchasiga yoqish uchun ko'proq rassomlik qilgan ba'zi odamlarning xatolari ostida yashiringan bu san'atni yoritib berganidan so'ng, u Florensiyaning eng katta shon-shuhratlaridan biriga aylanishi mumkin edi, ayniqsa u o'zining eng kamtarligi bilan qo'lga kiritgan sharaflarini ko'targan va u o'z san'tida hamma narsadan ustun bo'lib yashagan bo'lsa ham, u hali ham nomlanishni istamadi.

en: ter, which title, though rejected by him, shone so much the more gloriously in him as it was with greater eagerness greedily usurped by those who knew less than he, or by his disciples.
uz: "Ter," degan unvon, garchi u tomonidan rad etilgan bo'lsa-da, unda shunchalik ulug'vor nur sochdi, chunki u undan kam bilganlar yoki uning shogirdlari tomonidan ochko'zlik bilan o'zlashtirilgan edi.

en: Yet, great as was his skill, he was not there- fore anywise goodlier of person or better favoured than Messer Forese.
uz: Lekin, uning mahorati qanchalik buyuk bo'lmasin, u yerda hech qanday tarzda Messer Forese'dan ko'ra yaxshiroq inson yoki afzalroq emas edi.

en: But, to come to my story: I must tell you that Messer Forese and Giotto had each his country house at Mugello and the former, having gone to visit his estates, at that season of the summer when the Courts hold holiday, and returning thence on a sorry carthorse, chanced to fall in with the aforesaid Giotto, who had been on the same errand and was then on his way back to Florence nowise better equipped than himself in horse and accoutrements.
uz: Lekin, hikoyamga kelsak, sizga aytishim kerakki, Messer Forese va Giottolarning har biri Mugelloda o'z qishloq uylari bor edi va avvalgilari ham o'z mulklariga tashrif buyurib, o'sha yoz faslida, Sudlar dam olishni o'tkazganda, u yerdan achinarli otda qaytib, xuddi shu vazifada bo'lgan va keyin Florensiyaga qaytish yo'lida bo'lgan yuqorida aytilgan Giotto bilan uchrashishga muvaffaq bo'lishdi, endi ot va jihozlarda o'zidan yaxshiroq jihozlangan edi.

en: Accordingly, they joined company and fared on softly, like old men as they were.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, ular kompaniyaga qo'shilishdi va xuddi keksa odamlarga o'xshab, muloyimlik bilan davom etishdi.

en: Presently, it chanced, as we often see it happen in summer time, that a sudden shower overtook them, from which, as quickliest they might, they took shelter in the house of a husbandman, a friend and acquaintance of both of them.
uz: Hozirgi kunda, yozda ko'p uchraydiganidek, ularni to'satdan dush quvib tushdi, undan ular imkon qadar tezroq bir dehqonning, ularning do'sti va tanisining uyida panoh topishdi.

en: After awhile, the rain showing no sign of giving over and they wishing to reach Florence by daylight, they borrowed of their host two old homespun cloaks and two hats, rusty with age, for that there were no better to be had, and set out again upon their way.
uz: Biroz vaqt o'tgach, yomg'ir taslim bo'lish alomatini ko'rsatmay, kunduzgi kungacha Florensiyaga yetib borishni istashdi, ular o'z mehmonlaridan ikkita eski uyga mos ko'ylak va keksalik bilan zanglagan ikkita shapka olishdi, chunki bundan yaxshiroq narsa yo'q edi va yana yo'lga chiqishdi.

en: When they had gone awhile and were all drenched and bemired with the splashing that their hackneys kept up with their hoofs —things which use not to add worship to anyone’s looks —the weather began to clear a little and the two wayfarers, who had long fared on in silence, fell to conversing together.
uz: Ular bir oz vaqt ketib, hammasi ho'l bo'lib, tuflilari oyoqlariga mos keladigan, hech kimga sig'inishni qo'shmaydigan narsalardan xafa bo'lganlaridan so'ng, ob-havo biroz tiniqlashni boshladi va uzoq vaqtdan beri jim yurgan ikki yo'lovchi bir-birlari bilan suhbatlashishga tushishdi.

en: Messer Forese, as he rode, hearkening to Giotto, who was a very ﬁne talker, fell to considering his companion from head to foot and seeing him everywise so ill accoutred and in such scurvy case, burst out laughing and without taking any thought to his own plight, said to him, ‘How sayst thou, Giotto?
uz: Messer Forese, minayotganda, Giottoga quloq solib, u juda yaxshi so'zlashuvchi edi. U o'zining hamrohini boshidan oyoqqa qadar o'ylab, uni juda yomon ko'rib, shunday qiyshiq holatda ekanligini ko'rib, o'z ahvoli haqida o'ylamasdan kuldi va unga dedi: "Qanday deysan, Giotto?"

en: An there encountered us here a stranger who had never seen thee, thinkest thou he would believe thee to be, as thou art, the ﬁnest painter in the world?’ ‘Ay, sir,’ answered Giotto forthright, ‘methinketh he might e’en believe it whenas, looking upon you, he should believe that you knew your A.B.C.’ Messer Forese, hearing this, was sensible of his error and saw himself paid with money such as the wares he had sold.”306
uz: U yerda sizni hech qachon ko'rmagan notanish odam bizga duch keldi, sizni dunyodagi eng yaxshi rassom deb o'ylaysizmi? Ha, janob,  dedi Giotto to'g'ridan-to'g'ri,  menimcha, siz A.B.C.ingizni bilganingizga ishonishi mumkin edi, chunki sizga qarab, siz A.B.C.ingizni bilasiz. Messer Forese buni eshitib, o'z xatosiga amin bo'ldi va o'zini sotgan tovarlaridek pul bilan to'langanini ko'rdi.

en: THE SIXTH STORY Michele Scalza proveth to certain young men that the cadgers of Florence are the best gentlemen of the world or the Maremma and winneth a supper.
uz: OLTINCHI HIKOYA Michele Scalza ba'zi yosh yigitlarga Florensiyadagi kadrlar dunyoning eng yaxshi janoblari yoki Maremma ekanligini isbotlaydi va kechki ovqatni yutadi.

en: The ladies yet laughed at Giotto’s prompt retort, when the queen charged Fiammetta follow on and she proceeded to speak thus: “Young ladies, the mention by Pamﬁlo of the cadgers of Florence, whom peradventure you know not as doth he, hath brought to my mind a story, wherein, without de- viating from our appointed theme, it is demonstrated how great is their no- bility; and it pleaseth me, therefore, to relate it.
uz: Xonimlar Giottoning tezkor javobidan kulishdi, qirolicha Fiammettaga davom ettirishni buyurdi va u shunday dedi: Yosh xonimlar, Pamfilo tomonidan Florensiyadagi cadgerlar haqida tilga olingan gap, ehtimol siz ularni bilmasligingiz mumkin, menga shunday bir hikoyani eslatdi, unda bizning belgilangan mavzuimizdan chetga chiqmasdan, ularning qanday buyuk bo'lmasligi ko'rsatiladi; va shuning uchun men buni aytib berishni xohlayman.

en: It is no great while since there was in our city a young man called Michele Scalza, who was the merriest and most agreeable man in the world and he had still the rarest stories in hand, wherefore the young Florentines were exceeding glad to have his company whenas they made a party of pleasure amongst themselves.
uz: Bizning shaharda Michele Scalza ismli yosh yigit bor edi, u dunyodagi eng quvnoq va xushmuomala odam edi va u hali ham eng kam uchraydigan hikoyalarni qo'lida ushlab turardi, shuning uchun yosh florensiyaliklar o'zaro xursandchilik uyushtirganlarida uning kompaniyasiga ega bo'lishdan juda xursand edilar.

en: It chanced one day, he being with certain folk at Monte Ughi, that the question was started among them of who were the best and oldest gentlemen of Florence.
uz: Bir kuni, u Monte Ugidagi ba'zi odamlar bilan birga bo'lganida, ularning orasida Florensiyaning eng yaxshi va eng keksa janoblari kim ekanligi haqida savol paydo bo'ldi.

en: Some said the Uberti, others the Lamberti, and one this family and another that, according as it occurred to his mind; which Scalza hearing, he fell a-laughing and said, ‘Go to, addle- pates that you are!
uz: Ba'zilar Uberti deyishdi, boshqalar Lamberti deyishdi, va biri shu oiladan, yana biri esa o'ziga kelganidek; buni eshitib Scalza kuldi va dedi: "Bor, adle- pat, sen qandaysan!"

en: You know not what you say.
uz: Nima deyayotganingni bilmaysan.

en: The best gentlemen and the oldest, not only of Florence, but of all the world or the Maremma,307 are the Cadgers,308 a matter upon which all the phisopholers and everyone who knoweth them, as I do, are of accord; and lest you should understand it of others, I speak of the Cadgers your neighbors of Santa Maria Maggiore.’ When the young men, who looked for him to say otherwhat, heard this, they all made mock of him and said, ‘Thou gullest us, as if we knew not the Cadgers, even as thou dost.’ ‘By the Evangels,’ replied Scalza, ‘I gull you not; nay, I speak the truth, and if there be any here who will lay a supper
uz: Eng yaxshi janoblar va eng keksalari, nafaqat Florensiyaning, balki butun dunyo yoki Maremmalarning 307 nafari Cadgerlardir. 308 bu masala men kabi barcha fizofollar va ularni bilganlarning hammasi bir fikrda; va siz buni boshqalardan tushunmasligingiz uchun, Santa Maria Maggiorening qo'shnilaringiz Cadgerlar haqida gapiryapman.

en: thereon, to be given to the winner and half a dozen companions of his choosing, I will willingly hold the wager; and I will do yet more for you, for I will abide by the judgment of whomsoever you will.’ Quoth one of them, called Neri Mannini, ‘I am ready to try to win the supper in question’; whereupon, having agreed together to take Piero di Fiorentino, in whose house they were, to judge, they betook themselves to him, followed by all the rest, who looked to see Scalza lose and to make merry over his discom- ﬁture, and recounted to him all that had passed.
uz: Shundan so'ng, g'olibga va uning tanlagan yarim o'n nafar hamrohiga berilishi uchun, garovni ixtiyoriy ravishda ushlab turaman; va siz uchun undan ham ko'proq qilaman, chunki men siz xohlagan odamning hukmiga amal qilaman." Ularning biri, Neri Mannini deb atadi, "Men bu kechki ovqatni yutishga harakat qilishga tayyorman"; shundan so'ng, ular birgalikda Piero di Fiorentino'ni olishni kelishib oldilar, uning uyida hukm qilish uchun, unga o'zlarini tashlashdi, keyin qolganlarning hammasi Scalza'ning mag'lub bo'lishini ko'rishga va uning noqulayligidan xursand bo'lishga harakat qilishdi va unga o'tgan hamma narsani aytib berishdi.

en: Piero, who was a discreet young man, having ﬁrst heard Neri’s argument, turned to Scalza and said to him, ‘And thou, how canst thou prove this that thou afﬁrmest?’ ‘How, say- est thou?’ answered Scalza.
uz: Piero, Neriyning bahsini birinchi marta eshitib, dono yigit bo'lgan edi, Scalzaga o'girilib, unga dedi: Sen esa buni qanday isbotlay olasan, sen buni tasdiqlayapsanmi? Qanday, sen aytyapsanmi?  javob berdi Scalza.

en: ‘Nay, I will prove it by such reasoning that not only thou, but he who denieth it, shall acknowledge that I speak sooth.
uz: Yo'q, men buni shunday dalillar bilan isbotlaymanki, nafaqat sen, balki uni inkor etadigan odam ham mening rost gapirganimni tan olsin.

en: You know that, the ancienter men are, the nobler they are; and so was it said but now among these.
uz: Bilasanki, qadimgi odamlar, ular oliyjanobroqdirlar; va shunday deyilgan edi, lekin hozir bular orasida.

en: Now the Cadgers are more ancient than anyone else, so that they are nobler; and showing you how they are the most ancient, I shall undoubtedly have won the wager.
uz: Endi Cadgerlar boshqalardan ko'ra qadimroq, shuning uchun ular oliyjanobroqdirlar; va sizga ularning eng qadimgi ekanligini ko'rsatib, men shubhasiz garovni yutgan bo'lardim.

en: You must know, then, that the Cadgers were made by God the Lord in the days when He ﬁrst began to learn to draw; but the rest of mankind were made after He knew how to draw.
uz: Shuni bilishingiz kerakki, Cadgerlar Xudo Rabbiy tomonidan chizishni birinchi marta o'rganishni boshlagan kunlarda yaratilgan edi; lekin qolgan insoniyat U chizishni bilganidan keyin yaratilgan edi.

en: And to assure yourselves that in this I say sooth, do but consider the Cadgers in comparison with other folk; whereas you see all the rest of mankind with faces well composed and duly proportioned, you may see the Cadgers, this with a visnomy very long and strait and with a face out of all measure broad; one hath too long and another too short a nose and a third hath a chin jutting out and turned upward and huge jawbones that show as they were those of an ass, whilst some there be who have one eye bigger than the oth- er and other some who have one set lower than the other, like the faces that children used to make, whenas they ﬁrst begin to learn to draw.
uz: Va o'zingizga ishonch hosil qilinglar, men bu gapda xotirjamlik bilan aytaman, faqatgina Kadgerlarni boshqa odamlar bilan solishtiringlar; shu bilan birga, siz butun insoniyatning yaxshi tuzilgan va to'g'ri moslashtirilgan yuzlarini ko'rasiz, siz Kadgerlarni ko'rishingiz mumkin, bu juda uzun va tor va butunlay keng yuz bilan; biri juda uzun va yana biri juda qisqa burunli va uchdan birining tagi chiqib, yuqoriga o'girilgan va katta jag' suyaklari bor, ular eshak suyaklari kabi ko'rinadi, ba'zilari esa bir ko'zi kattaroq va boshqalariga qaraganda pastroq, xuddi bolalar chizishni boshlagan paytdagi yuzlari kabi.

en: Wherefore, as I have already said, it is abundantly apparent that God the Lord made them, what time He was learning to draw; so that they are more ancient and consequently nobler than the rest of mankind.’ At this, both Piero, who was the judge, and Neri, who had wagered the supper, and all the rest, hearing Scalza’s comical argument and remembering themselves,309 fell all a-laugh- ing and afﬁrmed that he was in the right and had won the supper, for that the Cadgers were assuredly the noblest and most ancient gentlemen that were to be found not in Florence alone, but in the world or the Maremma.
uz: Shuning uchun, men allaqachon aytganimdek, Xudo ularni yaratgani, U qanday vaqt chizishni o'rganayotgani juda aniq; shunday qilib, ular insoniyatning qolgan qismidan qadimroq va shuning uchun ham olijanobroqdir. Shu bilan birga, hakam bo'lgan Piero ham, kechki ovqatni garovga qo'ygan Neri ham, qolganlar ham Scalzaning kulgili dalilini eshitib, o'zlarini eslab, 309 ta kulishdi va u haq ekanligini va kechki ovqatda g'alaba qozonganini tasdiqladilar, chunki Cadgerlar, albatta, faqat Florensiyada emas, balki dunyoda yoki Maredda topilishi kerak bo'lgan eng olijanob va qadimgi janoblar edi.

en: Wherefore it was very justly said of Pamﬁlo, seeking to show the foulness
uz: Shuning uchun Pamfilo haqida juda adolatli aytildi, nopoklikni ko'rsatishga harakat qilish uchun.

en: of Messer Forese’s visnomy, that it would have showed notably ugly on one of the Cadgers.”
uz: Messer Foresening shiddatidan, bu Cadgerlardan birida sezilarli darajada xunuk ko'rsatgan bo'lardi.

en: THE SEVENTH STORY Madam Filippa, being found by her husband with a lover of hers and brought to justice, delivereth herself with a prompt and pleasant answer and causeth modify the statute.
uz: YETINCHINCHI HIKOYA Madam Filippa erining sevgilisi bilan topilishi va sudga tortilishi sababli, tezkor va yoqimli javob bilan o'zini qutqaradi va qonunni o'zgartirishga majbur qiladi.

en: Fiammetta was now silent and all laughed yet at the novel argument used by Scalza for the ennoblement over all of the Cadgers, when the queen en- joined Filostrato to tell and he accordingly began to say, “It is everywise a ﬁne thing, noble ladies, to know how to speak well, but I hold it yet goodli- er to know how to do it whereas necessity requireth it, even as a gentlewo- man, of whom I purpose to entertain you, knew well how to do on such wise that not only did she afford her hearers matter for mirth and laughter, but did herself loose from the toils of an ignominious death, as you shall presently hear.
uz: Fiammetta hozir jim edi va hamma Scalza tomonidan Cadgerlarning barchasi ustidan zodagonlik uchun ishlatilgan yangicha argumentga hali kuldi, qachonki qirolicha Filostratga qo'shilib aytib berishga kirdi va u shunga mos ravishda shunday dedi: "To'g'ri gapirishni bilish har qanday yaxshi narsa, hurmatli xonimlar, lekin men buni hali ham yaxshi deb bilaman - buni zarur bo'lganda qanday qilishni bilish, hatto sizni xursand qilishni maqsad qilgan muloyim odam kabi, u nafaqat tinglovchilariga mas'uliyat va kulguga yo'l qo'ydi, balki o'zi ham sharmandali o'lim azoblaridan qutuldi, xuddi siz hozirda bo'lasiz."

en: There was, then, aforetime, in the city of Prato, a statute in truth no less blameworthy than cruel, which, without making any distinction, ordained that any woman found by her husband in adultery with any her lover should be burnt, even as she who should be discovered to have sold her favours for money.
uz: Shunday qilib, bir vaqtlar, Prato shahrida, aslida, shafqatsizlikdan kam aybdor bo'lmagan qonun bor edi, u hech qanday farq qilmasdan, erining har qanday sevgilisi bilan zinoda topgan har qanday ayolni yoqib yuborish kerak edi, xuddi pulga o'z imtiyozlarini sotganligi aniqlangandek.

en: What while this statute was in force, it befell that a noble and beau- tiful lady, by name Madam Filippa, who was of a singularly amorous com- plexion, was one night found by Rinaldo de’ Pugliesi her husband, in her own chamber in the arms of Lazzerino de’ Guazzagliotri, a noble and hand- some youth of that city, whom she loved even as herself.
uz: Ushbu qonun kuchda bo'lgan bir paytda, Madam Filippa ismli olijanob va go'zal xonimning bir kecha Rinaldo de Pugliesi tomonidan uning eri Lazzerino de Guazzagliotrining qo'lida, o'sha shaharning olijanob va qo'lidagi bir yosh yigitining qo'lida topilishi sodir bo'ldi, uni hatto o'zi kabi sevdi.

en: Rinaldo, seeing this, was sore enraged and scarce contained himself from falling upon them and slaying them; and but that he feared for himself, an he should ensue the promptings of his anger, he had certainly done it.
uz: Rinaldo buni ko'rib, juda g'azablangan edi va ularga yiqilib, ularni o'ldirishdan o'zini juda kam ushlab turardi; lekin u o'zi uchun qo'rqqan edi, chunki u g'azabining qo'llanmalarini qo'llab-quvvatlashi kerak edi, u buni albatta qilgan edi.

en: However, he forbore from this, but could not refrain from seeking of the law of Prato that which it was not permitted him to accomplish with his own hand, to wit, the death of his
uz: Biroq, u bundan taqiqladi, lekin Prato qonuniga o'z qo'li bilan amalga oshirishga ruxsat etilmagan narsani, ya'ni o'limini izlashdan bosh tortolmadi.

en: Having, therefore, very sufﬁcient evidence to prove the lady’s default, no sooner was the day come than, without taking other counsel, he lodged an accusation against her and caused summon her before the provost.
uz: Shunday qilib, xonimning bu ishdan bo'shatilganligini isbotlash uchun yetarli dalillarga ega bo'lgani uchun, boshqa maslahatlarsiz, u unga qarshi ayblov qo'ydi va uni provostga chaqirishga majbur qildi.

en: Madam Filippa, being great of heart, as women commonly are who are verily in love, resolved, although counselled to the contrary by many of her friends and kinsfolk, to appear, choosing rather, confessing the truth, to die with an undaunted spirit, than, meanly ﬂeeing, to live an outlaw in exile and confess herself unworthy of such a lover as he in whose arms she had been the foregoing night.
uz: Filippa xonim, odatda chin dildan sevishgan ayollar kabi, yuragi ulug' bo'lgani uchun, ko'plab do'stlari va qarindoshlari tomonidan aksincha maslahat berilgan bo'lsa-da, ko'rinishga qaror qildi, ko'rinishni afzal ko'rdi, haqiqatni tanladi, qo'rqmasdan o'ladi, yo'lboshchi sifatida surgunda yashashdan va o'zini o'tgan kecha uning qo'lida bo'lgan kabi oshiqga loyiq emasligini tan olmadi.

en: Wherefore, presenting herself before the provost, atten- ded by a great company of men and ladies and exhorted of all to deny the charge, she demanded, with a ﬁrm voice and an assured air, what he would with her.
uz: Shuning uchun, o'zini ruhoniy huzuriga ko'tarib, katta bir guruh erkaklar va ayollar tomonidan kutib olinib, barcha ayblovni rad etishga undalgan holda, u qat'iy ovoz va ishonchli ruh bilan u bilan nima qilmoqchiligini talab qildi.

en: The magistrate, looking upon her and seeing her very fair and commendable of carriage and according as her words testiﬁed, of a lofty spirit, began to have compassion of her, fearing lest she should confess somewhat wherefore it should behoove him, for his own honour’s sake, condemn her to die.
uz: Magistrat unga qarab, uning juda chiroyli va maqtovga sazovor bo'lganligi va uning so'zlariga ko'ra, balandparvoz ruhga ega ekanligini ko'rib, unga rahm qila boshladi, u o'z sharafi uchun uni o'limga hukm qilish kerakligini tan olmasligidan qo'rqib.

en: However, having no choice but to question her of that which was laid to her charge, he said to her, ‘Madam, as you see, here is Rinaldo your husband, who complaineth of you, avouching himself to have found you in adultery with another man and demanding that I should punish you therefor by putting you to death, according to the tenor of a statute which here obtaineth; but this I cannot do, except you confess it; wherefore look well what you answer and tell me if that be true whereof your husband impeacheth you.’ The lady, no wise dismayed, replied very cheerfully, ‘Sir, true it is that Rinaldo is my husband and that he found me last night in the arms of Laz- zarino, wherein, for the great and perfect love I bear him, I have many a time been; nor am I anywise minded to deny this.
uz: Ammo, unga ayblangan narsa haqida so'roq qilishdan boshqa iloji bo'lmagani uchun, u unga dedi: "Xonim, ko'rib turganingizdek, mana sizning eringiz Rinaldo sizdan shikoyat qilmoqda, sizni boshqa bir erkak bilan zinoda topganingizni o'ylab, sizni o'limga tortishimni talab qilmoqda; lekin men buni qila olmayman, faqat siz buni tan olasiz; shuning uchun nimaga javob berayotganingizni yaxshilab ko'ring va agar bu sizning eringiz sizni ayblayotganda to'g'ri bo'lsa, menga ayting." Xonim, juda xursand bo'lib, javob berdi: "Janob, Rinaldo mening erim ekanligi rost va u meni kecha kechqurun Lazino qo'lida topganini, unda men katta va mukammal sevgiga ega bo'lganim uchun, men uni hech qanday vaqt ko'rmaganman; men buni inkor etmayman."

en: But, as I am assured you know, laws should be common to all and made with the consent of those whom they concern; and this is not the case with this statute, which is bind- ing only upon us unhappy women, who might far better than men avail to satisfy many; more by token that, when it was made, not only did no wo- man yield consent thereunto, but none of us was even cited to do so; where- fore it may justly be styled naught.
uz: Lekin, ishonchim komilki, bilasizki, qonunlar hammaga umumiy bo'lishi va ularga tegishli bo'lganlarning roziligi bilan qabul qilinishi kerak; va bu holat faqat biz baxtsiz ayollarga bog'liq emas, ular erkaklardan ko'ra ko'pchilikni qoniqtirishga qodir bo'lishi mumkin; bundan tashqari, u yaratilganda, nafaqat hech kim bunga rozilik bermagan, balki hech birimiz bunga taklif qilinmaganmiz; chunki u adolatli tarzda yaratilishi mumkin.

en: However, an you choose, to the preju- dice of my body and of your own soul, to be the executor of this unright- eous law, it resteth with you to do so; but, ere you proceed to adjudge aught, I pray you do me one slight favour, to wit, that you question my husband if
uz: Lekin, agar siz tanlagan bo'lsangiz, mening tanam va o'z joningizning zarblariga ko'ra, bu noto'g'ri qonunning ijrochisi bo'lish, buni qilish sizdan qoladi; lekin, biror narsani hal qilishga kirishishdan oldin, iltimos qilaman, menga bir kichik bir yordam ko'rsating, ya'ni erimni so'roq qilsangiz.

en: at all times and as often as it pleased him, without ever saying him nay, I have or not vouchsafed him entire commodity of myself.’ Rinaldo, without waiting to be questioned of the provost, straightway made answer that undoubtedly the lady had, at his every request, accorded him his every pleasure of herself; whereupon, ‘Then, my lord provost,’ straightway rejoined she, ‘if he have still taken of me that which was need- ful and pleasing to him, what, I ask you, was or am I to do with that which remaineth over and above his requirements?
uz: Har doim va unga yoqqancha, hech qachon "yo'q" demasdan, men unga o'zimning butun mol-mulkimni berdim yoki bermadim. Rinaldo, provostdan so'rashni kutmasdan, darhol javob berdi: shubhasiz, xonim uning har bir so'roviga ko'ra unga o'zining har qanday xohishini berdi; shuning uchun, "Unda, janob provost," deb javob berdi u darhol, "agar u mendan unga kerakli va yoqimli bo'lgan narsani olib qo'ygan bo'lsa, men sizdan so'rayman, nima qilishim kerak edi yoki undan yuqori bo'lgan narsa bilan shug'ullanishim kerakmi?"

en: Should I cast it to the dogs?
uz: Uni itlarga tashlashim kerakmi?

en: Was it not far better to gratify withal a gentleman who loveth me more than himself, than to leave it waste or spoil?’ Now well nigh all the people of Prato had ﬂocked thither to the trial of such a matter and of so fair and fam- ous a lady, and hearing so comical a question, they all, after much laughter, cried out as with one voice that she was in the right of it and that she said well.
uz: "Meni o'zidan ko'ra ko'proq sevuvchi janob bilan xursand bo'lish, uni xarob yoki o'ljaga qoldirishdan ko'ra yaxshiroq emasmi?" Endi deyarli butun Prato xalqi shunday ish va shunchalik go'zal va mashhur bir xonimning sudga yig'ilgan edi, va shunchalik kulgili savolni eshitib, ularning barchasi, ko'p kulgidan so'ng, xuddi bir ovozdan uning haqli ekanligi va u yaxshi deganidek qichqirdilar.

en: Moreover, ere they departed thence, at the instance of the provost, they modiﬁed the cruel statute and left it to apply to those women only who should for money make default to their husbands.
uz: Qolaversa, ular u yerdan ketishlaridan oldin, provostning ko'rsatmasi bilan, shafqatsiz nizomni o'zgartirib, uni faqatgina pul evaziga erlariga qarzdorlik qilishi kerak bo'lgan ayollarga qo'llash uchun qoldirishdi.

en: Thereupon Rinaldo, hav- ing taken nought but shame by so fond an emprise, departed the court, and the lady returned in triumph to her own house, joyful and free and in a man- ner raised up out of the ﬁre.”
uz: Shundan so'ng, Rinaldo, shunchalik mehribonlik bilan hech narsani uyalgan holda, saroydan ketdi va xonim o'z uyiga g'alaba bilan, quvonchli va erkin, olovdan tirilgan holda qaytdi.

en: THE EIGHTH STORY Fresco exhorteth his niece not to mirror herself in the glass, if, as she saith, it irketh her to see disagreeable folk.
uz: Sakkizinchi Hikoya: Fresko jiyanini o'zini oynada ko'rsatmaslikka chaqiradi, agar u aytganidek, yoqimsiz odamlarni ko'rish uni bezovta qilsa.

en: The story told by Filostrato at ﬁrst touched the hearts of the listening ladies with some little shamefastness and they gave token thereof by a modest red- ness that appeared upon their faces; but, after looking one at another, they hearkened thereto, tittering the while and scarce able to abstain from laugh- ing.
uz: Filostrat tomonidan aytilgan hikoya dastlab tinglayotgan ayollarning qalbiga biroz uyat bilan tegdi va ular bunga ularning yuzlarida paydo bo'lgan kamtarona qizarish bilan guvoh bo'lishdi; lekin bir-biriga qaraganlaridan so'ng, ular bir vaqtning o'zida titrab va kulishdan tiyilishga qodir bo'lishdi.

en: As soon as he was come to the end thereof, the queen turned to Emilia and bade her follow on, whereupon, sighing no otherwise than as she had been aroused from a dream, she began, “Lovesome lasses, for that long thought hath held me far from here, I shall, to obey our queen content my- self with [relating] a story belike much slighter than that which I might have bethought myself to tell, had my mind been present here, recounting to you the silly default of a damsel, corrected by an uncle of hers with a jocular re- tort, had she been woman enough to have apprehended it.
uz: Uning oxiriga yetishi bilanoq, malika Emiliyaga o'girilib, unga ergashishni buyurdi. Shundan so'ng, tushdan uyg'onganidan boshqa hech narsa deb oh tortmay, u boshladi: "Sevgilim qizlar, uzoq fikr meni bu yerdan uzoqroq ushlab turgani uchun, men malikaga itoat etaman, o'zim o'ylagandek, o'zim aytganidan ancha yengilroq hikoyani aytib beraman, agar mening fikrim shu yerda bo'lganida, u sizga bir kampirning ahmoqona xatoligini aytib berardi, uning amakisi tomonidan hazil bilan tuzatilgan, u ayol bo'lgan bo'lsa, uni ushlagan bo'lardi."

en: A certain Fresco da Celatico, then, had a niece familiarly called Ciesca,310 who, having a comely face and person (though none of those an- gelical beauties that we have often seen aforetime), set so much store by herself and accounted herself so noble that she had gotten a habit of carping at both men and women and everything she saw, without anywise taking thought to herself, who was so much more fashous, froward and humour- some than any other of her sex that nothing could be done to her liking.
uz: Shunday qilib, bir Fresco da Celaticoda Ciesca, 310 deb nomlanuvchi jiyan bor edi. U chiroyli yuz va shaxsga ega edi (garchi biz ilgari ko'p ko'rgan gelik go'zalliklardan hech biri bo'lmasa ham), o'zini shunchalik hurmat qilgan va o'zini shunchalik olijanob deb hisoblaganki, u erkaklar va ayollar, shuningdek, ko'rgan hamma narsani o'ziga o'ylamasdan, o'ziga o'ylab yurish odatini olgan edi, u o'z jinsidagi har qanday jinsdan ko'ra juda ko'proq jozibali, beparvo va hazilkordir edi.

en: Be- side all this, she was so prideful that, had she been of the blood royal of France, it had been overweening; and when she went abroad, she gave her- self so many airs that she did nought but make wry faces, as if there came to her a stench from whomsoever she saw or met.
uz: Bundan tashqari, u shunchalik mag'rur ediki, u Fransiya qirolichasidan bo'lganida, bu juda achchiq edi; va u chet elga ketganida, o'ziga shunchalik ko'p havo berdi, hatto u hech narsa qilmadi, faqat g'alati yuzlarni yaratdi, go'yo unga ko'rgan yoki uchratgan har bir kishidan badbo'y hid kelardi.

en: But, letting be many other vexatious and tiresome fashions of hers, it chanced one day that she came
uz: Lekin, uning boshqa ko'plab bezovta qiluvchi va zerikarli modalarini hisobga olmaganda, bir kun kelib qolishi mumkin edi.

en: back to the house, where Fresco was, and seating herself near him, all full of airs and grimaces, did nothing but puff and blow; whereupon quoth he, ‘What meaneth this, Ciesca, that, today being a holiday, thou comest home so early?’ To which she answered, all like to die away with affectation, ‘It is true I have come back soon, for that I believe there were never in this city so many disagreeable and tiresome people, both men and women, as there are today; there passeth none about the streets but is hateful to me as ill- chance, and I do not believe there is a woman in the world to whom it is more irksome to see disagreeable folk than it is to me; wherefore I have re- turned thus early, not to see them.’ ‘My lass,’ rejoined Fresco, to whom his niece’s airs and graces were mighty displeasing, ‘if disagreeable folk be so distasteful to thee as thou sayest, never mirror thyself in the
uz: Fresko yotgan uyga qaytib, uning yonida o'tirdi, hammasi havo va grimga to'la, faqat puflab esladi; shundan so'ng u dedi: "Bu nima, Ciesca, bugun bayram bo'lgani uchun, uyga shunchalik erta keldingmi?" Unga javob berdi, hammasi ta'sirlanib o'lishga o'xshaydi, "To'g'ri, men tezda qaytib keldim, chunki men bu shaharda hech qachon shu qadar ko'p yoqimsiz va zerikarli odamlar, erkaklar va ayollar bo'lmagan deb o'ylayman, bugungi kunda boridek; ko'chalarda hech narsa o'tmaydi, lekin menga baxtsizlikdek yoqimsiz, va men dunyoda hech kimga yoqimsiz odamlarni ko'rish men uchun yoqimliroq emas; shuning uchun men ularni erta ko'rishga majbur emasman, chunki men ularni ko'rishga majbur emasman.

en: glass, so thou wouldst live merry.’ But she, emptier than a reed, albeit herseemed she was a match for Solomon in wit, apprehended Fresco’s true speech no better than a block; nay, she said that she chose to mirror herself in the glass like other women; and so she abode in her folly and therein abideth yet.”
uz: Shisha, shunda xursandchilik bilan yashaysan. Ammo u qamishdan ko'ra bo'shroq edi, garchi o'zini Sulaymonga mos ko'rsatsa ham, Freskoning chin so'zini blokdan yaxshiroq tushundi; yo'q, u o'zini boshqa ayollar kabi shishaga oynalashni tanladi, dedi; va shuning uchun u o'z ahmoqligida yashadi va u yerda hali ham yashaydi.

en: THE NINTH STORY Guido Cavalcanti with a pithy speech courteously ﬂouteth certain Florentine gentlemen who had taken him by surprise.
uz: TO'IXINCHI HIKOY Guido Cavalcanti nozik nutq bilan uni hayratga solgan ba'zi Florensiyalik janoblarni xushmuomalalik bilan hayratga soladi.

en: The queen, seeing Emilia delivered of her story and that it rested with none other than herself to tell, saving him who was privileged to speak last, began thus, “Although, sprightly ladies, you have this day taken out of my mouth at the least two stories, whereof I had purposed to relate one, I have yet one left to tell, the end whereof compriseth a saying of such a fashion that none, peradventure, of such pertinence, hath yet been cited to us.
uz: Qirolicha, Emiliya o'z hikoyasini aytib berganini va uni o'zidan boshqa hech kimga aytishga qolmaganini ko'rib, so'nggi so'zlashiga haqli bo'lgan odamni qutqargan holda, shunday dedi: Agarki, hurmatli xonimlar, siz bu kunni og'zimdan kamida ikki hikoya olib tashladingiz, ulardan birini aytib berishni maqsad qilgan edim, men hali aytadigan bitta hikoya qoldim, uning oxiri shunday bir iborani tushunadi, hech biri, hech qanday tasodif, bunday ahamiyatga ega bo'lmagan gap bizga hali keltirilgan emas.

en: You must know, then, that there were in our city, of times past, many goodly and commendable usances, whereof none is left there nowadays, thanks to the avarice that hath waxed therein with wealth and hath banished them all.
uz: Shuni bilishingiz kerakki, bizning shaharimizda, o'tmish zamonlarida, ko'plab yaxshi va maqtovga sazovor odatlar bor edi, ularning hech biri hozirgi kunda u yerda qolmagan, chunki u yerda boylik bilan o'sgan va ularning hammasini surgun qilgan baxillik tufayli.

en: Among these there was a custom to the effect that the gentlemen of the various quarters of Florence assembled together in divers places about the town and formed themselves into companies of a certain number, having a care to admit thereinto such only as might aptly bear the expense, whereof today the one and tomorrow the other, and so all in turn, hold open house, each his day, for the whole company.
uz: Florensiyaning turli hududlaridan kelgan janoblar shahar atrofidagi turli joylarda yig'ilib, ma'lum miqdordagi kompaniyalarga aylanishlari odati bor edi. Ular faqatgina bugungi kunning bir qismi va ertasi kunning ikkinchisi bo'ladigan xarajatlarni o'z zimmasiga oladiganlarga e'tirof etishlari kerak edi, shuning uchun hammasi o'z navbatida, har bir kuni butun kompaniya uchun ochiq uyda bo'lishardi.

en: At these banquets they often entertained both stranger gentlemen, whenas there came any thither, and those of the city; and on like wise, once at the least in the year, they clad themselves alike and rode in procession through the city on the most not- able days and whiles they held passes of arms, especially on the chief holi- days or whenas some glad news of victory or the like came to the city.
uz: Bu ziyofatlarda ular ko'pincha begona janoblarni ham, u yerga kelganlarni ham, shaharliklarni ham xursand qilishardi; va xuddi donolar kabi, yil davomida hech bo'lmaganda bir xil kiyinishardi va eng zaif kunlarda shahar bo'ylab yurishardi, ayniqsa eng muhim bayramlarda yoki shaharga g'alaba yoki shunga o'xshash xushxabarlar kelganda.

en: Amongst these companies was one of Messer Betto Brunelleschi, where- into the latter and his companions had studied amain to draw Guido, son of Messer Cavalcante de’ Cavalcanti, and not without cause; for that, besides being one of the best logicians in the world and an excellent natural philo-
uz: Bu kompaniyalardan biri Messer Betto Brunelleski edi, u yerda - oxirgi va uning hamrohlari Messer Cavalcante de Cavalcanti o'g'li Guido'ni chizish uchun juda ko'p o'qishgan edi, va buning uchun bejizga emas; buning uchun, dunyodagi eng yaxshi logiklardan biri va ajoyib tabiiy fil...

en: sopher (of which things, indeed, they recked little), he was very sprightly and well-bred and a mighty well-spoken man and knew better than any oth- er to do everything that he would and that pertained unto a gentleman, more by token that he was very rich and knew wonder-well how to entertain whomsoever he deemed deserving of honour.
uz: sopher (aslida, ular bu haqda kam gapirishardi), u juda to'g'ri va yaxshi tarbiyalangan va kuchli, yaxshi gapiradigan odam edi va boshqalardan ko'ra yaxshiroq bilardi - o'zi xohlagan va janobga tegishli bo'lgan hamma narsani qilishni, ayniqsa juda boy bo'lgani va kimni sharafga loyiq deb bilsa, qanday qilib xursand qilishni juda yaxshi bilardi.

en: But Messer Betto had never been able to win and to have him, and he and his companions believed that this betided for that Guido, being whiles engaged in abstract speculations, became much distraught from mankind; and for that he inclined somewhat to the opinion of the Epicureans, it was reported among the common folk that these his speculations consisted only in seeking if it might be dis- covered that God was not.
uz: Ammo Messer Betto hech qachon g'alaba qozona olmadi va uni qo'lga kiritishga qodir bo'lmadi, va u va uning hamrohlari bu Gvidoning g'alati taxminlar bilan shug'ullanganligi sababli insoniyatdan ancha chalg'igan deb hisoblashgan edi; va shuning uchun u epikurlarning fikriga biroz moyil bo'lgani uchun, oddiy xalq orasida uning bu taxminlari faqat Xudo yo'qligini yashirish mumkinligini qidirishdan iborat ekanligi xabar qilingan edi.

en: It chanced one day that Guido set out from Orto San Michele and came by way of the Corso degli Ademari, the which was oftentimes his road, to San Giovanni, round about which there were at that present divers great marble tombs (which are nowadays at Santa Reparata) and many others.
uz: Bir kuni Guido Orto San Michele'dan jo'nab, ko'pincha o'zining yo'li bo'lgan Corso degli Ademari orqali San Giovanni'ga yetib bordi. Uning atrofida o'sha paytda katta marmar qabrlar (hozir Santa Reparata'da) va boshqa ko'plab qabrlar bor edi.

en: As he was between the columns of porphyry there and the tombs in question and the door of the church, which was shut, Messer Betto and his company, coming a-horseback along the Piazza di Santa Reparata, espied him among the tombs and said, ‘Let us go plague him.’ Accordingly, spurring their horses, they charged all down upon him in sport and coming upon him ere he was aware of them, said to him, ‘Guido, thou refusest to be of our com- pany; but, harkye, whenas thou shalt have found that God is not, what wilt thou have accomplished?’ Guido, seeing himself hemmed in by them, answered promptly, ‘Gentlemen, you may say what you will to me in your own house’; then, laying his hand on one of the great tombs aforesaid and being very nimble of body, he took a spring and alighting on the other side, made off, having thus rid himself of them.
uz: U yerda porfir ustunlari va bahsli qabrlar o'rtasida va yopiq cherkov eshigi orasida bo'lganida, Messer Betto va uning kompaniyasi Piazza di Santa Reparata bo'ylab otda kelayotganda, uni qabrlar orasida kuzatishdi va dedilar: "Kelinglar, uni qiynaylik." Shunga ko'ra, otlarini itarib, ular unga sportda tushishdi va u ularga yetib kelguncha unga tegishdi. U unga dedi: "Guido, sen bizning qo'limizdan voz kechding; lekin, qachonki Xudo yo'qligini aniqlaganingda, nima qilmoqchisan?" Guido ulardan o'zini ko'rib, tezda javob berdi: "Janoblar, siz menga o'z uyingizda nima deyishingiz mumkin?"

en: The gentlemen abode looking one upon another and fell a-saying that he was a crack-brain and that this that he had answered them amounted to nought seeing that there where they were they had no more to do than all the other citizens, nor Guido himself less than any of themselves.
uz: Janoblar bir-birlariga tikilib qolishdi va u aqli ochiq ekanligini va u ularga bergan javob hech narsaga teng kelmasligini, chunki u yerda boshqa barcha fuqarolardan ko'ra hech narsa qilishlari kerak emasligini va Guido o'zi ham hech kimdan kam emasligini ko'rishardi.

en: But Mess- er Betto turned to them and said, ‘It is you who are the crackbrains, if you have not apprehended him.
uz: Ammo Mess-er Betto ularga qarab dedi: Agar uni ushlab qolmagan bo'lsangiz, aynan siz aqldan ozgan odamlarsiz.

en: He hath courteously and in a few words given us the sharpest rebuke in the world; for that, an you consider aright, these tombs are the houses of the dead, seeing they are laid and abide therein, and these, saith he, are our house, meaning thus to show us that we and other foolish and unlettered men are, compared with him and other men of learn-
uz: U bizga dunyodagi eng keskin tanbehni xushmuomalalik bilan va qisqa so'zlar bilan berdi; chunki, agar siz to'g'ri deb hisoblasangiz, bu qabrlar o'liklarning uylaridir, chunki ular u yerda yotqiziladi va yashaydi, va bular, deydi u, bizning uyimizdir, ya'ni bizga biz va boshqa ahmoq va savodsiz odamlar, unga va boshqa odamlarga nisbatan...

en: ing, worse than dead folk; wherefore, being here, we are in our own house.’ Thereupon each understood what Guido had meant to say and was abashed nor ever plagued him more, but held Messer Betto thenceforward a gentle- man of a subtle wit and an understanding.”
uz: o'lik odamlardan ham yomonroq; shuning uchun, bu yerda bo'lganimiz uchun, biz o'z uyimizdamiz." Shundan so'ng, har bir kishi Guido nima demoqchi ekanligini tushundi va uyatga tushdi va uni hech qachon boshqa bezovta qilmadi, lekin bundan buyon Messer Betni nozik aql va tushunishga ega bo'lgan muloyim odam deb hisobladi.

en: THE TENTH STORY Fra Cipolla promiseth certain country folk to show them one of the angel Gabriel’s feathers and ﬁnding coals in place thereof, avoucheth these latter to be of those which roasted St.
uz: O'NCHINCHI HIKOYA Fra Cipolla ayrim qishloq odamlariga farishta Jabroilning patlaridan birini ko'rsatishga va uning o'rniga ko'mir topishga va'da beradi, bularning oxirgilarini Avvushani qovurganlardan biri deb biladi.

en: Each of the company being now quit of his311 story, Dioneo perceived that it rested with him to tell; whereupon, without awaiting more formal com- mandment, he began on this wise, silence having ﬁrst been imposed on those who commended Guido’s pregnant retort: “Charming ladies, albeit I am privileged to speak of that which most liketh me, I purpose not today to depart from the matter whereof you have all very aptly spoken; but, ensuing in your footsteps, I mean to show you how cunningly a friar of the order of St.
uz: Har bir kompaniya endi o'zining 311 hikoyasidan voz kechganidan so'ng, Dioneo o'ziga aytish qolganini angladi; shundan so'ng, rasmiy buyruqni kutmasdan, u shu yo'l bilan boshladi. Guido'ning homilador javobini maqtovga olganlarga birinchi navbatda sukut yuklandi: "Joyli xonimlar, garchi menga eng yoqqan narsa haqida gapirish sharafiga muyassar bo'lsam ham, bugun sizlarning barchangiz juda yaxshi aytgan masalani tark etishni maqsad qilmayman; lekin, sizning qadamlaringizdan ergashib, men sizga Avliyo Ordenning qanday hiyla-nayrangligini ko'rsatmoqchiman.

en: Anthony, by name Fra Cipolla, contrived with a sudden shift to extricate himself from a snare312 which had been set for him by two young men; nor should it irk you if, for the complete telling of the story, I enlarge somewhat in speaking, an you consider the sun, which is yet amiddleward in the sky.
uz: Entoni, Fra Cipolla nomi bilan tanilgan, ikki yosh yigit tomonidan unga qo'yilgan 312-tuzoqdan to'satdan qutulish uchun o'ylab topdi; hikoyani to'liq aytib berish uchun biroz kattalashsam ham, sizni bezovta qilmasligi kerak, chunki siz hali osmonda o'rtacha bo'lgan quyoshni o'ylaysiz.

en: Certaldo, as you may have heard, is a burgh of Val d’ Elsa situate in our county, which, small though it be, was once inhabited by gentlemen and men of substance; and thither, for that he found good pasture there, one of the friars of the order of St.
uz: Certaldo, eshitganingizdek, bizning okrugimizda joylashgan Val dElsaning bir shahri bo'lib, u kichik bo'lsa ham, bir vaqtlar janoblar va boy odamlar yashar edi; va u yerda u yaxshi yaylov topgani uchun, Avliyo ordeni rohiblaridan biri edi.

en: Anthony was long used to resort once a year, to get in the alms bestowed by simpletons upon him and his brethren.
uz: Entoni uzoq vaqtdan beri yiliga bir marta murojaat qilishga odatlangan edi, o'ziga va birodarlariga soddalar tomonidan berilgan sadaqalarga ega bo'lish uchun.

en: His name was Fra Cipolla and he was gladly seen there, no less belike, for his name’s sake313 than for other reasons, seeing that these parts produce onions that are famous throughout all Tuscany.
uz: Uning ismi Fra Cipolla edi va u yerda boshqa sabablarga qaraganda, o'z nomi uchun 313 dan kam bo'lmagan xursandchilik bilan ko'ringan, chunki bu qismlar butun Toskana bo'ylab mashhur bo'lgan piyozlarni ishlab chiqaradi.

en: This Fra Cipolla was little of person, red-haired and merry of countenance, the jolliest rascal in the world, and to boot, for all he was no scholar, he was so ﬁne a talker and so ready of wit that those who knew him not would not only have esteemed him a great rhetorician, but had avouched him to be Tully himself or may
uz: Bu Fra Cipolla kam odam, qizil sochli va xursand yuzli, dunyodagi eng quvnoq firibgar edi, va aslida u olim emas edi, u shunchalik yaxshi gapiruvchi va aql-zakovatga tayyor ediki, uni bilmaganlar uni nafaqat buyuk notiq deb hisoblashgan, balki uni Tulli bo'lishga majbur qilgan edilar yoki

en: be Quintilian; and he was gossip or friend or well-wisher314 to well nigh everyone in the country.
uz: Kvintil bo'lsin; va u mamlakatdagi hamma odamga yaxshilik tilaydigan, g'iybat qiluvchi yoki do'st edi.

en: One August among others he betook himself thither according to his wont, and on a Sunday morning, all the goodmen and goodwives of the vil- lages around being come to hear mass at the parish church, he came for- ward, whenas it seemed to him time, and said, ‘Gentlemen and ladies, it is, as you know, your usance to send every year to the poor of our lord Baron St.
uz: Bir avgust kuni u odatlariga ko'ra o'zini u yerga olib bordi va yakshanba kuni ertalab atrofdagi qishloqning barcha yaxshi erkaklari va yaxshi xotinlari cherkov cherkovida massaj tinglash uchun kelishdi. U o'ziga vaqtdek tuyulganida, u yerga keldi va dedi: "Janoblar va xonimlar, siz bilasizki, har yili bizning xo'jayinimiz Baron Stning kambag'allariga yuborish odatdir."

en: Anthony of your corn and of your oats, this little and that much, accord- ing to his means and his devoutness, to the intent that the blessed St.
uz: Antoni sizning makkajo'xori va sulidan, bu kichkina va bu ko'p narsa, o'z boyligi va sadoqatidan kelib chiqib, muqaddas avliyo...

en: An- thony may keep watch over your beeves and asses and swine and sheep; and besides this, you use to pay, especially such of you as are inscribed into our company, that small due which is payable once a year.
uz: An- Thony sizning asalaringiz, eshaklaringiz, cho'chqalaringiz va qo'ylaringiz ustidan nazorat o'tkazishi mumkin; bundan tashqari, siz, ayniqsa bizning kompaniyamizga ro'yxatdan o'tganlar, yiliga bir marta to'lanadigan kichik to'lovni to'laysiz.

en: To collect these I have been sent by my superior, to wit, my lord abbot; wherefore, with the blessing of God, you shall, after none, whenas you hear the bells ring, come hither without the church, where I will make preachment to you after the wonted fashion and you shall kiss the cross; moreover, for that I know you all to be great devotees of our lord St.
uz: Bularni yig'ish uchun meni mening boshlig'im, ya'ni, janob abbim yubordi; shuning uchun, Xudoning marhamati bilan, hech kimdan keyin, qo'ng'iroqlarni eshitganingizdan so'ng, cherkovdan tashqari bu yerga kelmaysiz, u yerda men sizga odatdagidek va'z qilaman va siz xochni o'pasiz; bundan tashqari, men sizlarning barchangiz janobimizning buyuk sadoqatli ekanligingizni bilaman.

en: Anthony, I will, as an especial favour show you a very holy and goodly relic, which I myself brought aforetime from the holy lands beyond seas; and that is one of the Angel Gabriel’s feathers, which remained in the Virgin Mary’s chamber, whenas he came to announce to her in Nazareth.’ This said, he broke off and went on with his mass.
uz: Antoni, men sizga alohida marhamat sifatida juda muqaddas va yaxshi yodgorlikni ko'rsataman, uni o'zim ham bir vaqtlar dengiz ortidagi muqaddas yerlardan olib kelganman; va bu farishta Jabroilning patlaridan biri bo'lib, u Maryam Maryam Maryamning xonasida qoldi, u unga Nosirada xabar berish uchun kelganida.

en: Now, when he said this, there were in the church, among many others, two roguish young fellows, hight one Giovanni del Bragioniera and the oth- er Biagio Pizzini, who, after laughing with one another awhile over Fra Cipolla’s relic, took counsel together, for all they were great friends and cronies of his, to play him some trick in the matter of the feather in ques- tion.
uz: Endi u bu gapni aytganida, cherkovda ko'pchilik orasida ikki sho'x yosh yigit bor edi, ulardan biri Giovanni del Bragioniera va ikkinchisi Biagio Pizzini. Ular Fra Cipolla'ning qoldig'i ustidan biroz kulgandan so'ng, uning buyuk do'stlari va do'stlari bo'lgani uchun, unga savolda pat masalasida biror hiyla o'ynashni maslahatlashdilar.

en: Accordingly, having learned that he was to dine that morning with a friend of his in the burgh, they went down into the street as soon as they knew him to be at table, and betook themselves to the inn where he had alighted, purposing that Biagio should hold his servant in parley, whilst Giovanni should search his baggage for the feather aforesaid, whatever it might be, and carry it off, to see what he should say to the people of the matter.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u o'sha kuni ertalab bir do'sti bilan burgda ovqatlanishini bilgach, ular uni stolda o'tirganini bilishlari bilanoq ko'chaga tushishdi va u tushgan mehmonxonaga o'zlarini olib borishdi, Biagio o'z xizmatchisini parleyda ushlab turishini, Giovanni esa uning yukini yuqorida aytilgan patni qidirib, nima bo'lishidan qat'iy nazar, bu masalada odamlarga nima deyishi kerakligini ko'rishni maqsad qilishdi.

en: Fra Cipolla had a servant, whom some called Guccio315 Balena,316 others Guccio Imbratta317 and yet others Guccia Porco318 and who was such a scurvy knave that Lipo Topo319 never wrought his like, inasmuch as his
uz: Fra Cipollaning bir xizmatkori bor edi, uni ba'zilar Guccio315 Balena, boshqalar Guccio Imbratta317 va boshqalar Guccia Porco318 deb atashardi va u shunchalik qaltiragan ediki, Lipo Topo319 hech qachon unga o'xshagani yo'q edi, hatto...

en: master used oftentimes to jest of him with his cronies and say, ‘My servant hath in him nine defaults, such that, were one of them in Solomon or Aris- totle or Seneca, it would sufﬁce to mar all their worth, all their wit and all their sanctity.
uz: Ustoz ko'pincha uni do'stlari bilan masxara qilib, shunday der edi: "Mening xizmatkorimda to'qqizta nuqson bor, agar ulardan biri Sulaymon yoki Aris-totle yoki Senekada bo'lsa, ularning barcha qadriyatlarini, barcha aql-idroklarini va barcha muqaddasliklarini yo'q qilish kifoya edi."

en: Consider, then, what a man he must be, who hath all nine of them and in whom there is neither worth nor wit nor sanctity.’ Being ques- tioned whiles what were these nine defaults and having put them into doggerel rhyme, he would answer, ‘I will tell you.
uz: Shunday ekan, u qanday odam bo'lishi kerakligini o'ylab ko'ring, unda ularning to'qqiztasining hammasi bor va unda na qadriyat, na donolik, na muqaddaslik yo'q." Bu to'qqizta nuqson nima edi va ularni doggerel qofiyaga qo'yganidan so'ragan holda, u javob berardi: "Men sizga aytaman."

en: He’s a liar, a sloven, a slugabed; disobedient, neglectful, ill bred; o’erweening, foul-spoken, a dun- derhead; beside which he hath divers other peccadilloes, whereof it booteth not to speak.
uz: U yolg'onchi, dangasa, qul bo'lgan; itoatsiz, beparvo, yomon tarbiyalangan; g'azablantiruvchi, iflos gapiruvchi, befarosat; undan tashqari uning boshqa gunohlari ham bor, ularni aytishga unchalik qodir emas.

en: But what is most laughable of all his fashions is that, wherever he goeth, he is still for taking a wife and hiring a house; for, having a big black greasy beard, him-seemeth he is so exceeding handsome and agree- able that he conceiteth himself all the women who see him fall in love with him, and if you let him alone, he would run after them all till he lost his girdle.320 Sooth to say, he is of great assistance to me, for that none can ever seek to speak with me so secretly but he must needs hear his share; and if it chance that I be questioned of aught, he is so fearful lest I should not know how to answer, that he straightway answereth for me both Ay and No, as he judgeth sortable.’ Now Fra Cipolla, in leaving him at the inn, had bidden him look well that none touched his gear, and more particularly his saddlebags, for that therein were the sacred things.
uz: Ammo uning barcha modalari eng kulgili tomoni shundaki, u qayerga bormasin, u hali ham xotin olib, uy ijaraga olgani uchun; chunki katta qora, yog'li soqolli bo'lgani uchun, u juda chiroyli va kelishgan ko'rinadi, uni sevib qolgan barcha ayollarni o'ziga ishonadi va agar uni qo'yib yuborsangiz, u hammasini yo'qotib qo'yadi.

en: But Guccio, who was fonder of the kitchen than the nightingale of the green boughs, especially if he scented some serving- wench there, and who had seen in that of the inn a gross fat cookmaid, un- dersized and ill-made, with a pair of paps that showed like two manure-bas- kets and a face like a cadger’s, all sweaty, greasy and smoky, leaving Fra Cipolla’s chamber and all his gear to care for themselves, swooped down upon the kitchen, even as the vulture swoopeth upon carrion, and seating himself by the ﬁre, for all it was August, entered into discourse with the wench in question, whose name was Nuta, telling her that he was by rights a gentleman and had more than nine millions of ﬂorins, beside that which he had to give others, which was rather more than less, and that he could do and say God only knew what.
uz: Ammo Guccio, oshxonaga yashil shoxlarning bulbulidan ko'ra ko'proq muxlis edi, ayniqsa u yerda ba'zi bir xizmatkor qizning hidini sezgan bo'lsa, va mehmonxonada qo'pol semiz oshxonachi, beparvo va yomon ko'rganini ko'rgan edi, ikki go'ng-bas mushukchalar va cadger kabi yuzli, barcha terlangan, yog'li va tutunli, Fra Cipolla'ning xonasini va barcha jihozlarini o'ziga qaratib, oshxonaga tushib ketdi, hatto qush o'limga urilganda, va o'zini olov yonida o'tirganida, chunki bu avgust edi, Nuta ismli qiz bilan bahslashdi, uning o'zi to'qqiz milliondan ortiq huquqga ega edi, u faqatgina erkak va boshqalarga nima berishni bilganidan ko'ra,

en: Moreover, without regard to his bonnet, whereon was grease enough to have seasoned the caldron of Altopascio,321 and his doublet all torn and pieced and enamelled with ﬁlth about the collar and under the armpits, with more spots and patches of divers colours than ever had Turkey or India stuffs, and his shoes all broken and hose unsewn,
uz: Qolaversa, uning dubulg'asiga qaramay, Altopascio kalderonini ziravorlash uchun yetarli yog' bor edi, 321 va uning ikki qismi bo'yin bo'yniga va qo'ltiq ostidagi ifloslik bilan yirtilgan va bo'laklangan, Turkiya yoki Hindiston buyumlaridan ko'ra ko'proq turli xil rangdagi dog'lar va dog'lar bor edi, va uning poyabzallari butunlay singan va shlangi tikilmagan edi.

en: he told her, as he had been the Sieur de Châtillon,322 that he meant to clothe her and trick her out anew and deliver her from the wretchedness of abiding with others,323 and bring her to hope of better fortune, if without any great wealth in possession, and many other things, which, for all he delivered them very earnestly, all turned to wind and came to nought, as did most of his enterprises.
uz: U unga aytdiki, u o'zi Châtillon xonimi bo'lgani kabi, 322-yilda uni yana kiydirish, aldash va boshqa odamlar bilan yashash azobidan qutqarishni, 323-yilda uni katta boylik bo'lmasa ham, yaxshiroq omadga umid qilish va boshqa ko'plab narsalarni, lekin u ularni juda chin dildan yetkazib bergan bo'lsa, hammasi shamolga aylanib, yo'q bo'lib ketdi, xuddi uning ko'pchilik korxonalari kabi.

en: The two young men, accordingly, found Guccio busy about Nuta, where- at they were well pleased, for that it spared them half their pains, and enter- ing Fra Cipolla’s chamber, which they found open, the ﬁrst thing that came under their examination was the saddlebags wherein was the feather.
uz: Ikki yigit, shunga ko'ra, Guccio Nuta haqida band ekanligini topdilar, bu ularga juda mamnun edi, chunki bu ularning og'riqlarining yarmini saqlab qoldi va ular ochiq deb topgan Fra Cipolla'ning xonasiga kirdilar. Ularning tekshiruvlariga birinchi bo'lib pat tushadigan egar sumkalari tushdi.

en: In these they found, enveloped in a great taffetas wrapper, a little casket and opening this latter, discovered therein a parrot’s tail-feather, which they concluded must be that which the friar had promised to show the people of Certaldo.
uz: Ularda ular katta taffeta o'rami bilan o'ralgan, kichik bir sandiqni topdilar va bu oxirgisini ochib, u yerda to'tiqushning dum patini topdilar. Ularning xulosaga kelishicha, bu rohib Certaldo xalqiga ko'rsatishga va'da qilgan narsa bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: And certes he might lightly cause it to be believed in those days, for that the reﬁnements of Egypt had not yet made their way save into a small part of Tuscany, as they have since done in very great abundance, to the undoing of all Italy; and wherever they may have been some little known, in those parts they were well nigh altogether unknown of the inhab- itants; nay the rude honesty of the ancients yet enduring there, not only had they never set eyes on a parrot, but were far from having ever heard tell of such a bird.
uz: Va albatta, u o'sha kunlarda bunga yengil ishonishga yordam berishi mumkin edi, chunki Misrning nafisliklari hali Toskaning kichik bir qismiga yetib bormagan edi, chunki ular butun Italiyani vayron qilish uchun juda ko'p miqdorda qilgan edilar; va ular qayerda unchalik ma'lum bo'lmasin, o'sha qismlarda ular mahalliy aholi uchun deyarli umuman noma'lum edi; yo'q, qadimgilarning hali ham o'sha yerda saqlanib qolgan qo'pol halolligi, ular hech qachon to'tiqushga ko'z qo'ymaganlari, balki bunday qush haqida eshitmaganlari ham edi.

en: The young men, then, rejoiced at ﬁnding the feather, laid hands on it and not to leave the casket empty, ﬁlled it with some coals they saw in a corner of the room and shut it again.
uz: Yigitlar esa patni topganlaridan xursand bo'lishdi, unga qo'llarini qo'yishdi va tobutni bo'sh qoldirmaslik uchun uni xonaning bir burchagida ko'rgan ko'mirlar bilan to'ldirishdi va yana yopishdi.

en: Then, putting all things in order as they had found them, they made off in high glee with the feather, without having been seen, and began to await what Fra Cipolli should say, when he found the coals in place thereof.
uz: Keyin, hamma narsani topganlaricha tartibga solib, ular ko'rinmasdan, pat bilan yuqori quvonchda ketishdi va Fra Cipollining ko'mirlarni o'z joyida topganida nima deyishini kutishga kirishdi.

en: The simple men and women who were in the church, hearing that they were to see the Angel Gabriel’s feather after none, returned home, as soon as mass was over, and neighbor telling it to neighbor and gossip to gossip, no sooner had they all dined than so many men and women ﬂocked to the burgh that it would scarce hold them, all looking eagerly to see the afore- said feather.
uz: Cherkovda bo'lgan oddiy erkaklar va ayollar, farishta Jabroilning patini ko'rishlari kerakligini eshitib, massaj tugagandan so'ng, uyga qaytishdi va qo'shnilarga aytib, g'iybat qilishdi. Ularning hammasi ovqatdan ko'p o'tmay, ko'plab erkaklar va ayollar ularni juda kam ushlab turadigan burga oqib kelishdi, ularning hammasi oldindan aytilgan patni ko'rishga intilar edilar.

en: Fra Cipolla, having well dined and after slept awhile, arose a little after none and hearing of the great multitude of country folk come to see the feather, sent to bid Guccio Imbratta come thither with the bells and bring his saddlebags.
uz: Fra Cipolla yaxshilab ovqatlanib, biroz uxlagandan so'ng, birozdan keyin turdi va patni ko'rishga kelgan qishloq odamlarining katta olomonini eshitib, Guccio Imbrattaga qo'ng'iroqlar bilan u yerga kelishni va egar sumkalarini olib kelishni taklif qildi.

en: Guccio, tearing himself with difﬁculty away from the kitchen and Nuta, betook himself with the things required to the appointed place, whither coming, out of breath, for that the water he had drunken had
uz: Guccio oshxonadan va Nutadan zo'rg'a uzoqlashib, o'zini belgilangan joyga kerakli narsalar bilan bezadi, u yerga kelganda, nafasdan tashqari, chunki u ichgan suv bor edi.

en: made his belly swell amain, he repaired, by his master’s commandment, to the church door and fell to ringing the bells lustily.
uz: Qorinini shishirib yubordi, u xo'jayinining buyrug'i bilan cherkov eshigini tuzatdi va qo'ng'iroqlarni shahvoniy tarzda chalishga tushdi.

en: When all the people were assembled there, Fra Cipolla, without ob- serving that aught of his had been meddled with, began his preachment and said many words anent his affairs; after which, thinking to come to the showing of the Angel Gabriel’s feather, he ﬁrst recited the Conﬁteor with the utmost solemnity and let kindle a pair of ﬂambeaux; then, pulling off his bonnet, he delicately unfolded the taffetas wrapper and brought out the cas- ket.
uz: U yerda barcha odamlar to'planganida, Fra Cipolla hech narsaga aloqasi bo'lmagan holda, o'z va'zini boshladi va o'z ishi haqida ko'p so'z aytdi; shundan so'ng, Farishta Jabroilning patini ko'rsatishga kelishni o'ylab, avval Confiteorni eng katta tantana bilan o'qidi va bir juft olov yoqdi; keyin, bosh kiyimini yechib, tafetani nozik ochdi va kas-ketni olib chiqdi.

en: Having ﬁrst pronounced certain ejaculations in praise and commenda- tion of the Angel Gabriel and of his relic, he opened the casket and seeing it full of coals, suspected not Guccio Balena of having played him this trick, for that he knew him not to be man enough; nor did he curse him for having kept ill watch lest others should do it, but silently cursed himself for having committed to him the care of his gear, knowing him, as he did, to be negli- gent, disobedient, careless and forgetful.
uz: Gabriel farishtasini va uning merosini maqtash va maqtash uchun ba'zi eyakulyatsiyalarni birinchi marta aytganidan so'ng, u sandiqni ochdi va uni ko'mirga to'la ko'rdi. Guccio Balena unga bu hiyla o'ynaganini gumon qilmadi, chunki u uni yetarlicha odam emasligini bilardi; shuningdek, boshqalar buni qilmasligi uchun yomon kuzatgani uchun la'natlamadi, lekin o'ziga o'z jihozlariga g'amxo'rlik qilganligi uchun o'zini sukut bilan la'natladi, uni u qilganidek, muloyim, itoatsiz, beparvo va unutuvchan ekanligini bilgan edi.

en: Nevertheless, without changing colour, he raised his eyes and hands to heaven and said, so as to be heard of all, ‘O God, praised be still thy puis- sance!’ Then, shutting the casket and turning to the people, ‘Gentlemen and ladies,’ quoth he, ‘you must know that, whilst I was yet very young, I was dispatched by my superior to those parts where the sun riseth and it was ex- pressly commanded me that I should seek till I found the Privileges of Por- cellana, which, though they cost nothing to seal, are much more useful to others than to us.
uz: Shunga qaramay, rangini o'zgartirmasdan, u ko'zlarini va qo'llarini osmonga ko'tardi va hammaga eshitiladigan tarzda dedi: "Ey Xudo, hamon Sening qudrating ulug'vor bo'lsin!" Keyin, tobutni yopib, odamlarga murojaat qilib, u dedi: "Janoblar va xonimlar, shuni bilinglarki, hali juda yosh bo'lganimda, meni mening boshlig'im quyosh chiqadigan joylarga jo'natgan edi va menga oldindan aniq buyruq bergan edi, men Por-cellana imtiyozlarini topguncha qidirishim kerak edi, ular muhrlashga arzimaydi, lekin bizga qaraganda boshqalarga ancha foydaliroq.

en: On this errand I set out from Venice and passed through Borgo de’ Greci,324 whence, riding through the kingdom of Algarve and Baldacca,325 I came to Parione,326 and from there, not without thirst, I came after awhile into Sardinia.
uz: Shu ish bilan men Venetsiyadan jo'nab, Borgo de Gresi orqali o'tdim, 324. U yerdan Algarve va Baldakka qirolligi bo'ylab sayohat qilib, 325 Parionega keldim, 326. U yerdan esa chanqamasdan Sardiniyaga birozdan keyin keldim.

en: But what booteth it to set out to you in detail all the lands explored by me?
uz: Lekin men o'rgangan barcha yerlarni sizga batafsil bayon etishga nima majbur qiladi?

en: Passing the straits of San Giorgio,327 I came into Trufﬁa328 and Bufﬁa,329 countries much inhabited and with great popula- tions, and thence into the land of Menzogna,330 where I found great plenty of our brethren and of friars of other religious orders, who all went about those parts, shunning unease for the love of God, recking little of others’ travail, whenas they saw their own advantage to ensue, and spending none other money than such as was uncoined.331 Thence I passed into the land of the Abruzzi, where the men and women go in clogs over the mountains, clothing the swine in their own guts;332 and a little farther I found folk who carried bread on sticks and wine in bags.
uz: San Giorgio bo'g'ozlaridan o'tib, 327 Men Truffia328 va Buffia329 ga keldim, ko'p aholi yashovchi va katta aholi yashovchi davlatlar, va u yerdan Menzogna yurtiga. 330 U yerda men ko'plab birodarlarimizni va boshqa diniy tartibdagi rohiblarni topdim. Ularning barchasi o'sha joylarda yurishardi, Xudoga bo'lgan muhabbatdan qochishardi, o'zgalarning mehnatidan uncha ko'rmasdi, chunki ular o'zlarining afzalliklarini ko'rishardi va hech qanday pul sarflamasdi. 331 U yerdan men Abruzzi yurtiga bordim, u yerda erkaklar va ayollar tog'lar ustida g'o'lalarda yurishardi, o'z ichaklarida cho'chqalarni kiyishardi; 332 va bir oz uzoqroq joyda non va vino olib yuradigan odamlarni topdim.

en: From this I came to the Mountains
uz: Shundan Tog'larga keldim.

en: of the Bachi, where all the waters run down hill; and in brief, I made my way so far inward that I won at last even to India Pastinaca,333 where I swear to you, by the habit I wear on my back, that I saw hedge-bills334 ﬂy, a thing incredible to whoso hath not seen it.
uz: Bachi daryosidan, u yerda barcha suvlar tepalik bo'ylab oqib tushadi; va qisqacha aytganda, men shunchalik ichkariga yo'l oldimki, nihoyat Hindiston Pastinaca, 333 ga ham g'alaba qozondim, u yerda sizga qasam ichaman, orqa tomon kiyadigan odatim bilan, men qirish-bills334 uchayotganini ko'rdim, buni ko'rmaganlar uchun aql bovar qilmas narsa.

en: But of this Maso del Saggio will conﬁrm me, whom I found there a great merchant, cracking walnuts and selling the shells by retail.
uz: Lekin buni Maso del Saggio tasdiqlaydi, men u yerda yong'oqni yorib, qobiqlarni chakana savdoda sotadigan buyuk savdogarni topdim.

en: Being unable to ﬁnd that which I went seeking, for that thence one goeth thither by water, I turned back and arrived in those holy countries, where, in summer-years, cold bread is worth four farthings a loaf and the hot goeth for nothing.
uz: Qidirgan narsamni topa olmaganim uchun, u yerdan suv orqali boriladi, shuning uchun orqaga qaytib, o'sha muqaddas yurtlarga yetib keldim, u yerda yoz yillarida sovuq non to'rt farthingga, issiq non esa hech narsaga arziydi.

en: There I found the venerable father my lord Blamemenot Anit- pleaseyou, the very worshipful Patriarch of Jerusalem, who, for reverence of the habit I have still worn of my lord Baron St.
