en: Not long after, whatever might have been the reason, it came to pass that Rinaldo turned friar and whether or not he found the pasturage to his liking, he persevered in that way of life; and albeit, in the days of his becoming a monk, he had for awhile laid on one side the love he bore his gossip, togeth- er with sundry other vanities of his, yet, in process of time, without quitting the monk’s habit, he resumed them347 and began to delight in making a show and wearing ﬁne stuffs and being dainty and elegant in all his fashions and making canzonets and sonnets and ballads and in singing and all man- ner other things of the like sort.
uz: Ko'p o'tmay, sabab nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, Rinaldo rohib bo'lib qoldi va o'ziga yoqqan yaylovni topadimi yo'qmi, u o'sha hayot tarziga sodiq qoldi; va rohib bo'lgan kunlarida, u bir muddat o'zining g'iybatini ko'tarib yurgan muhabbatini bir chetga surib qo'ygan bo'lsa ham, vaqt o'tishi bilan rohibning odatidan voz kechmasdan, u ularni tiklay boshladi347 va barcha modalarida nafis va nafis bo'lishdan hamda kanzonlar, sonnetlar va balladalar yasashdan hamda qo'shiq va boshqa odamlarning barcha narsalaridan zavqlanishni boshladi.

en: But what say I of our Fra Rinaldo, of whom we speak?
uz: Ammo men gapirayotgan frasi Rinaldo haqida nima deyman?

en: What monks are there that do not thus?
uz: Qanday rohiblar bunday qilmaydi?

en: Alack, shame that they are of the corrupt world, they blush not to appear fat and ruddy in the face, dainty in their garb and in all that pertaineth unto them, and strut along, not like doves, but like very turkey-cocks, with crest erect and breast puffed out; and what is worse (to say nothing of having their cells full of gallipots crammed with electuaries and unguents, of boxes full of various confec- tions, of phials and ﬂagons of distilled waters and oils, of pitchers brimming with Malmsey and Cyprus and other wines of price, insomuch that they seem to the beholder not friars’ cells, but rather apothecaries’ or perfumers’ shops) they think no shame that folk should know them to be gouty, con- ceiving that others see not nor know that strict fasting, coarse viands and spare and sober living make men lean and slender and for the most part sound of body, and that if indeed some sicken
uz: Afsuski, ular buzuq dunyoga mansub bo'lishidan uyat, yuzlarida semiz va qizg'ish ko'rinmasligi uchun qizarishadi, kiyimlarida va ularga tegishli bo'lgan hamma narsada nafislik bor, va xuddi kaptarlar kabi emas, balki juda katta kurka-xo'rozlar kabi yurishadi, cho'qqisi tik va ko'kraklari puflangan; va undan ham yomoni (o'zlarining xujayralarida turli xil konfetlar bilan to'ldirilgan gallipotlar, turli xil idishlar, damlangan suvlar va moylar, Malm va Kipr va boshqa qimmatbaho vinolar bilan to'la idishlar borligi haqida gapirmasa ham bo'ladi.

en: thereof, at least they sicken not of the gout, whereto it is used to give, for medicine, chastity and everything else that pertaineth to the natural way of living of an honest friar.
uz: Hech bo'lmaganda, ular halol rohibning tabiiy turmush tarziga tegishli dori, poklik va boshqa hamma narsa uchun beriladigan yo'taldan kasal bo'lishmaydi.

en: Yet they persuade themselves that others know not that —let alone the scant and sober living —long vigils, praying and discipline should make men pale and mortiﬁed and that neither St.
uz: Lekin ular o'zlarini boshqalarning bilmasligiga ishontirishadi, chunki  nafaqat kambag'al va hushyor hayot kechirish  uzoq vaqt davomida hushyor bo'lish, ibodat qilish va intizom odamlarni oqarib, xor qilishi kerak va na Muqaddas...

en: Francis, far from having four gowns for one, clad themselves in cloth dyed in grain nor in other ﬁne stuffs, but in garments of coarse wool and undyed, to keep out the cold and not to make a show.
uz: Fransisk, bitta uchun to'rtta ko'ylakdan yiroq, don bilan bo'yalgan matoga emas, boshqa nozik narsalarga emas, balki sovuqdan qochish va ko'z-ko'z qilish uchun qo'pol jun va bo'yalmagan kiyimlarga kiyinardi.

en: For which things, as well as for the souls of the sim- pletons who nourish them, there is need that God provide.
uz: Qaysi narsalar uchun, shuningdek, ularni oziqlantiradigan sim-plesionlarning ruhlari uchun ham, Xudo ta'minlaydigan ehtiyoj bor.

en: Fra Rinaldo, then, having returned to his former appetites, began to pay frequent visits to his gossip and waxing in assurance, proceeded to solicit her with more than his former instancy to that which he desired of her.
uz: Fr Rinaldo, o'zining avvalgi ishtahalariga qaytgach, o'zining g'iybatlariga tez-tez tashrif buyurishni boshladi va ishonch bilan ko'tarilib, avvalgi instansiyasidan ko'ra undan xohlagan narsasini so'rashga kirishdi.

en: The good lady, seeing herself hard pressed and Fra Rinaldo seeming to her be- like goodlier than she had thought him aforetime, being one day sore impor- tuned of him, had recourse to that argument which all women use who have
uz: Yaxshi xonim, o'zini qattiq bosim o'tkazilganini va Fra Rinaldo o'ziga avval o'ylaganidan ko'ra yaxshiroq ko'rinayotganini ko'rib, bir kuni unga qattiq e'tibor qaratib, barcha ayollar foydalanadigan o'sha bahsga murojaat qildi.

en: a mind to yield that which is asked of them and said, ‘How now, Fra Rinaldo?
uz: Ulardan so'ralgan narsaga rozi bo'lish va: Xo'sh, Fra Rinaldo, endi nima bo'ldi?  degan fikrga ega bo'lish.

en: Do monks such things?’ ‘Madam,’ answered he, ‘when as I shall have this gown off my back —and I can put it off mighty easily —I shall ap- pear to you a man fashioned like other men and not a monk.’ The lady pulled a demure face and said, ‘Alack, wretched me!
uz: Rohiblar shunday ishlarni qiladimi? Xonim, deb javob berdi u, qachonki bu koylakni yelkamdan yechib olsam  va uni juda oson yechib tashlasam  sizga rohib emas, balki boshqa odamlarga oxshash odamni taqdim etaman. Xonim xotirjam yuzini tortdi va dedi: Lalak, menga achinarli!

en: You are my gossip; how can I do this?
uz: Siz mening g'iybatimsiz; buni qanday qilsam bo'ladi?

en: It were sadly ill, and I have heard many a time that it is a very great sin; but, certes, were it not for this, I would do that which you wish.’ Quoth Fra Rinaldo, ‘You are a simpleton, if you forbear for this; I do not say that it is not a sin, but God pardoneth greater than this to whoso re- penteth.
uz: Afsuski, bu juda yomon edi va men bu juda katta gunoh ekanligini ko'p eshitganman; lekin, albatta, agar bu uchun bo'lmaganida, siz xohlagan narsani qilgan bo'lardim." Fr Rinaldo ta'kidladi: "Agar bunga e'tibor bermasangiz, siz ahmoqsiz; men bu gunoh emas demoqchiman, lekin Xudo kimki afv qilsa, undan ham kattaroq afv qiladi."

en: But tell me, who is more akin to your child, I who held him at bap- tism or your husband who begat him?’ ‘My husband is more akin to him,’ answered the lady; whereupon, ‘You say sooth,’ rejoined the friar.
uz: Lekin ayting-chi, farzandingizga kim yaqinroq, uni suvga cho'mgan menmi yoki uni tug'gan eringizmi? Erim unga yaqinroq,  javob berdi xonim; shundan so'ng, Siz tinchlik aytasiz,  dedi rohib.

en: ‘And doth not your husband lie with you?’ ‘Ay doth he,’ replied she.
uz: Va eringiz siz bilan yotmaydimi?  Voy u yotadi,  javob berdi u.

en: ‘Then,’ said Fra Rinaldo, ‘I, who am less akin to your child than is your husband, may lie with you even as doth he.’ The lady, who knew no logic and needed little persuasion, either believed or made a show of believing that the friar spoke the truth and answered, ‘Who might avail to answer your learned words?’ And after, notwithstanding the gossipship, she resigned herself to do his pleasure; nor did they content themselves with one bout, but foregathered many and many a time, having the more commodity thereof under cover of the gossipship, for that there was less suspicion.
uz: Unda,  dedi Fra Rinaldo, Men, sizning farzandingizga eringizdan kamroq yaqin bo'lganim, u bilan ham xuddi shunday yotishim mumkin. Mantiqni bilmagan va kamroq ishontirishga muhtoj bo'lgan xonim, yoki rohibning rost gapirganiga ishongan yoki ishonganini ko'rsatib, javob berdi: Sizning bilimdon so'zlaringizga kim javob bera oladi? Va keyin, g'iybatga qaramay, u o'zini uning roziligiga rozi qildi; va ular bir bilan kifoyalanmadilar, balki ko'p va ko'p vaqtlar o'tdilar, g'iybatni yashirib, uning qulayligini ko'rsatdilar, chunki bu kamroq gumon edi.

en: But once, amongst other times, it befell that Fra Rinaldo, coming to the lady’s house and ﬁnding none with her but a little maid of hers, who was very pretty and agreeable, despatched his comrade with the latter to the pi- geon-loft, to teach her her Paternoster, and entered with the lady, who had her child in her hand, into her bedchamber, where they locked themselves in and fell to taking their pleasure upon a daybed that was there.
uz: Ammo bir safar, boshqa vaqtlar qatorida, Fra Rinaldo xonimning uyiga kelib, u bilan faqatgina uning kichkina xizmatchisini topib, juda chiroyli va xushmuomala edi, o'zining o'rtoqini pi-geon-loftga, unga o'z Paternosterini o'rgatish uchun jo'natdi va xonim bilan birga uning yotoqxonasiga kirdi, u yerda o'zlarini qulflab, u yerda bo'lgan kunduzgi karavotga quladilar.

en: As they were thus engaged, it chanced that the husband came home and making for the bedchamber-door, unperceived of any, knocked and called to the lady, who, hearing this, said to the friar, ‘I am a dead woman, for here is my husband, and now he will certainly perceive what is the reason of our familiarity.’ Now Rinaldo was stripped to his waistcoat, to wit, he had put off his gown and his scapulary, and hearing this, answered, ‘You say sooth; were I but dressed, there might be some means; but, if you open to him and he ﬁnd me thus, there can be no excuse for us.’ The lady, seized with a sudden idea, said, ‘Harkye, dress yourself and when you are dressed, take your godchild in your arms and hearken well to that which I shall say to him, so your
uz: Ular shunday unashtirilganlarida, er uyga kelib, hech kim sezmasdan yotoqxona eshigini tayyorlab, xonimga qo'ng'iroq qildi. Xonim buni eshitib, rohibga dedi: "Men o'lik ayolman, chunki bu mening erim, endi u bizning tanishligimiz sababini aniq anglaydi". Endi Rinaldo belbog'ini yechdi, xususan, u ko'ylagini va eshaklarini yechgan edi va buni eshitib, javob berdi: "Siz yaxshi deysiz; agar men kiyingan bo'lsam, biror narsa bo'lishi mumkin edi; lekin agar siz unga ochsangiz va u meni topsa, biz uchun hech qanday bahona bo'lmaydi." Xonim birdan bir fikrga kelib, dedi: "Hark, o'zingni kiyganing va qachonki, o'z xotiningni qo'lga olsangiz, men uni yaxshi ko'rayman,

en: words may after accord with mine, and leave me do.’ Then, to the good man, who had not yet left knocking, ‘I come to thee,’ quoth she and rising, opened the chamber-door and said, with a good countenance, ‘Husband mine, I must tell thee that Fra Rinaldo, our gossip, is come hither and it was God sent him to us; for, certes, but for his coming, we should today have lost our child.’ The good simple man, hearing this, was like to swoon and said, ‘How so?’ ‘O husband mine,’ answered Agnesa, ‘there took him but now of a sud- den a fainting-ﬁt, that methought he was dead, and I knew not what to do or say; but just then Fra Rinaldo our gossip came in and taking him in his arms, said, “Gossip, these be worms he hath in his body, the which draw near to his heart and would infallibly kill him; but have no fear, for I will conjure them and make them all die; and ere I go hence, you shall see the
uz: So'zlarim bilan kelishib, meni qo'yib yuboring." Keyin, yaxshi odamga, u hali qo'ng'iroq qilishni tashlab ketmagan edi, dedi: "Men senga kelaman," u turdi va xonaning eshigini ochdi va yaxshi ko'rinish bilan dedi: "Egam, senga aytishim kerakki, Fra Rinaldo, bizning g'iybatimiz, bu yerga keldi va Xudo uni bizga yuborgan edi; chunki, albatta, uning kelishi uchun bugun biz farzandimizni yo'qotishimiz kerak edi." Yaxshi oddiy odam buni eshitib, "Qanday bo'ldi?" dedi." "Ey er," javob berdi Ag nisa, "Endi uni suddan olib ketishdi, u o'lgan deb o'yladi va men uni nima qilish kerakligini bilmadim; lekin, albatta, uning qo'llarida va u bilan birga o'lib ketish kerak edi, lekin men uni o'ldiraman, lekin u...

en: child whole again as ever you saw him.” And for that we had need of thee to repeat certain orisons and that the maid could not ﬁnd thee, he caused his comrade say them in the highest room of our house, whilst he and I came hither and locked ourselves in, so none should hinder us, for that none other than the child’s mother might be present at such an ofﬁce.
uz: Bola yana sog'lom edi, xuddi uni ko'rganingizdek." Va biz sizga ba'zi so'rovlarni takrorlashingiz kerak edi va xizmatkor sizni topa olmasligi uchun, u o'rtoqingizga ularni uyimizning eng yuqori xonasida aytishga buyurdi, u va men esa bu yerga kelib, o'zimizni qamab oldik, shunda hech kim bizga xalaqit bermasligi kerak edi, chunki bolaning onasidan boshqa hech kim bunday ofisda bo'lmas edi.

en: Indeed, he hath the child yet in his arms and methinketh he waiteth but for his comrade to have made an end of saying the orisons and it will be done, for that the boy is already altogether restored to himself.’ The good simple man, believing all this, was so straitened with concern for his child that it never entered his mind to suspect the cheat put upon him by his wife; but, heaving a great sigh, he said, ‘I will go see him.’ ‘Nay,’ answered she, ‘thou wouldst mar that which hath been done.
uz: Darhaqiqat, u hali bolani qo'lida va o'ylaydi, o'rtog'i orzularni aytishni tugatguncha kutadi va bu amalga oshiriladi, chunki bola allaqachon o'ziga qaytdi." Yaxshi oddiy odam bularning barchasiga ishonib, o'z farzandi haqida qayg'urib, hech qachon xotini tomonidan unga nisbatan xiyonat bo'lganini gumon qilish uning xayoliga kirmasdi; lekin, katta xo'rsinish bilan u dedi: "Men uni ko'rishga boraman." "Yo'q," dedi u, "sen nima qilinganini ko'rmoqchisan."

en: Wait; I will go see an thou mayst come in and call thee.’ Meanwhile, Fra Rinaldo, who had heard everything and had dressed him- self at his leisure, took the child in his arms and called out, as soon as he had ordered matters to his mind, saying, ‘Harkye, gossip, hear I not my gos- sip your husband there?’ ‘Ay, sir,’ answered the simpleton; whereupon, ‘Then,’ said the other, ‘come hither.’ The cuckold went to him and Fra Rinaldo said to him, ‘Take your son by the grace of God whole and well, whereas I deemed but now you would not see him alive at vespers; and look you let make a waxen image of his bigness and set it up, to the praise and glory of God, before the statue of our lord St.
uz: Kuting; men boraman, shunda siz kirib, sizni chaqiraman." Ayni paytda, hamma narsani eshitib, o'zini o'zi kiygan Fra Rinaldo, bolani quchoqlab, chaqirib oldi va o'ziga ish buyurishi bilanoq, dedi: "Harkye, g'iybat, men eringizni u yerda eshitmayapmanmi - so'rish?" "Ha, janob," dedi sodda; shundan so'ng, "Unda," dedi ikkinchisi, "bu yerga keling." Pakana unga bordi va Fra Rinaldo unga dedi: "O'g'lingizni Xudoning marhamati bilan sog'lom va yaxshi olib keting, men uni kechqurun tirik ko'rmaysiz deb o'ylagandim; va uni momiga ko'rsatib, Xudoning ulug'vorligi va ulug'vorligi uchun mum yasating.

en: Ambrose, through whose in- tercession He hath vouchsafed to restore him unto you.’ The child, seeing his father, ran to him and caressed him, as little children used to do, whilst
uz: Ambrose, uning orqali U uni sizga qaytarishni va'da qilgan. Bola otasini ko'rib, yugurib uning oldiga keldi va kichkina bolalar odatdagidek uni erkaladi.

en: the latter, taking him, weeping, in his arms, no otherwise than as he had brought him forth of the grave, fell to kissing him and returning thanks to his gossip for that he had made him whole.
uz: Oxirgisi uni yig'lab, quchog'iga olib, xuddi uni qabrdan chiqarib olganidek, uni o'pishga tushdi va uni sog'aytirgani uchun uning g'iybatidan minnatdorchilik bilan qaytdi.

en: Meanwhile, Fra Rinaldo’s comrade, who had by this taught the serving- wench not one, but maybe more than four paternosters, and had given her a little purse of white thread, which he had from a nun, and made her his de- votee, hearing the cuckold call at his wife’s chamber-door, had softly be- taken himself to a place whence he could, himself unseen, both see and hear what should betide and presently, seeing that all had passed off well, came down and entering the chamber, said, ‘Fra Rinaldo, I have despatched all four of the orisons which you bade me say.’ ‘Brother mine,’ answered the friar, ‘thou hast a good wind and hast done well; I, for my part, had said but two thereof, when my gossip came; but God the Lord, what with thy pains and mine, hath shown us such favour that the child is healed.’ Therewithal the cuckold let bring good wines and confections and entertained his gossip and
uz: Ayni paytda, janob Rinaldo'ning o'rtog'i, bu bilan xizmatchi qizga bir emas, balki to'rtta otaxonni o'rgatgan edi, va unga rohiba tomonidan berilgan oq ipdan biroz hamyon bergan edi, va uni o'z ho'jayiniga aylantirdi. Xotining xonasi eshigidagi qo'ng'iroqni eshitib, xotirjamlik bilan o'zi ko'rinmaydigan joyga olib bordi, ham ko'rishi va eshitishi kerak bo'lgan narsani ko'rdi va hozir, hamma narsa yaxshi o'tganini ko'rib, pastga tushdi va xonaga kirdi, dedi: "Janob Rinaldo, men siz menga aytgan to'rtta g'iybatni yo'q qildim." "Birodarim," janob, "sen yaxshi shamol va g'iybat keltirding; men o'z farzandim uchun yaxshi g'iybat qildim, lekin Xudo meni shunday yaxshilik bilan olib kirdi," dedi.

en: the latter’s comrade with that whereof they had more need than of aught else.
uz: Oxirgisi ularning boshqa narsalardan ko'ra ko'proq muhtoj bo'lgan narsalari bilan o'rtoq edi.

en: Then, attending them to the door, he commended them to God and letting make the waxen image without delay, he sent to hang it up with the others348 before the statue of St.
uz: So'ngra, ularni eshikgacha kuzatib borar ekan, u ularni Xudoga topshirdi va mumli haykalni kechiktirmasdan yasashga ruxsat berib, uni boshqa 348 kishi bilan birga Avliyo haykali oldida osib qo'yishga yubordi.

en: Ambrose, but not that of Milan.”349
uz: Ambrose, lekin Milanniki emas.349

en: THE FOURTH STORY Tofano one night shutteth his wife out of doors, who, availing not to re- enter by dint of entreaties, feigneth to cast herself into a well and casteth therein a great stone.
uz: TO'RTINCHI HIKOYA Tofanoning bir kuni kechasi xotini eshikdan tashqariga chiqarib yuboradi. U iltijolar bilan qayta kirishga imkon bermay, o'zini quduqqa tashlamoqchi bo'lib, unga katta tosh tashlaydi.

en: Tofano cometh forth of the house and runneth thither, whereupon she slippeth in and locking him out, bawleth reproaches at him from the window.
uz: Tofano uydan chiqib, u yerga yugurib boradi, shundan so'ng u kirib, uni qulflab, derazadan unga nisbatan malomatlar aytadi.

en: The king no sooner perceived Elisa’s story to be ended than, turning without delay to Lauretta, he signiﬁed to her his pleasure that she should tell; whereupon she, without hesitation, began thus, “O Love, how great and how various is thy might!
uz: Qirol Elisaning hikoyasi tugagandan so'ng, darhol Laurettaga o'girilib, unga aytishi kerak bo'lgan ma'qulligini bildirdi; shundan so'ng u hech ikkilanmasdan shunday boshladi: "Ey Sevgi, qanday buyuk va qanday xilma-xil qudrating bor!"

en: How many thy resources and thy devices!
uz: Naqadar ko'p resurslaring va hiylalaring bor!

en: What philosopher, what craftsman350 could ever have availed or might avail to teach those shifts, those feints, those subterfuges which thou on the spur of the moment suggestest to whoso ensueth in thy traces!
uz: Qanday faylasuf, qanday hunarmand 350 o'sha o'zgarishlarni, o'sha feintlarni, o'sha subterfuglarni o'rgatishga qodir bo'lgan yoki qodir bo'lishi mumkin edi, ularni sening izingda bo'lganlarga shu zahotiyoq taklif qilyapsan!

en: Certes, all others’ teaching is halting compared with thine, as may very well have been appre- hended by the devices which have already been set forth and to which, lovesome ladies, I will add one practised by a woman of a simple wit enough and such as I know none but Love could have taught her.
uz: Albatta, boshqalarning hammasi sizning ta'limingiz bilan solishtirganda to'xtaydi, chunki ular allaqachon taqdim etilgan va men, yoqimli ayollar, oddiy aqlga ega ayol tomonidan mashq qilingan va men bilganidek, Sevgidan boshqa hech kim unga o'rgatolmagan qurilmalar tufayli juda yaxshi tushunilgan bo'lishi mumkin.

en: There was once, then, in Arezzo, a rich man called Tofano and he was given to wife a very fair lady, by name Madam Ghita, of whom, without knowing why, he quickly waxed jealous.
uz: O'shanda, Arezzoda Tofano ismli bir boy odam bor edi va unga Madam Ghita ismli juda chiroyli xonim xotinlik qilib berilgan edi. Uning negaligini bilmasdan, u tezda rashk qildi.

en: The lady, becoming aware of this, was despited thereat and questioned him once and again of the reason of his jealousy; but he was able to assign her none, save such as were general and naught; wherefore it occurred to her mind to cause him die of the disease whereof he stood without reason in fear.
uz: Xonim bundan xabardor bo'lib, undan xafa bo'ldi va rashkining sababini qayta-qayta so'radi; lekin u unga umumiy va hech narsa bo'lmagan narsalardan boshqa hech narsa tayinlay olmadi; shuning uchun uning xayoliga uni bejizga qo'rqib turgan kasallikdan o'ldirishni o'yladi.

en: Accordingly, perceiving that a young man, who was much to her taste, sighed for her, she proceeded dis- creetly to come to an understanding with him and things being so far ad- vanced between them that there lacked but with deeds to give effect to
uz: Shunga ko'ra, unga juda yoqqan bir yigit uni sog'inganini anglab yetgach, u u bilan tushunishga shoshilishga va ular o'rtasida shunchalik o'tib ketgan narsalarga erishishga shoshildilarki, faqatgina ta'sir ko'rsatish uchun amallar yetishmadi.

en: words, she cast about for a means of bringing this also to pass; wherefore, having already remarked, amongst her husband’s other ill usances, that he delighted in drinking, she began not only to commend this to him, but would often artfully incite him thereto.
uz: so'zlarni, u buni ham amalga oshirish vositasi sifatida tashladi; shuning uchun, erining boshqa yomon odatlari orasida, u ichishdan zavqlanishini aytib bo'lgach, u nafaqat buni unga maqtashni boshladi, balki uni ko'pincha mohirona undardi.

en: This became so much his wont that, well nigh whensoever it pleased her, she led him to drink even to intoxica- tion, and putting him to bed whenas she saw him well drunken, she a ﬁrst time foregathered with her lover, with whom many a time thereafter she continued to do so in all security.
uz: Bu uning odatiga shunchalik o'xshab ketdi, unga yoqqan har qanday holatda ham, u uni hatto mast qilishgacha ichishga majbur qildi va uni mast holda ko'rganida yotqizdi, u birinchi marta sevgilisi bilan uchrashdi va undan keyin ko'p vaqt davomida bu ishni butun xavfsizlik bilan davom ettirdi.

en: Indeed, she grew to put such trust in her husband’s drunkenness that not only did she make bold to bring her gallant into the house, but went whiles to pass a great part of the night with him in his own house, which was not very far distant.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, u erining mastligiga shunchalik ishonib qoldi, nafaqat u o'zining zodagonini uyga olib kirishga jur'at etdi, balki tunning katta qismini u bilan o'zining uyida o'tkazishga harakat qildi, bu uy unchalik uzoqda emas edi.

en: The enamoured lady continuing on this wise, it befell that the wretched husband came to perceive that she, whilst encouraging him to drink, nathe- less herself drank never; wherefore suspicion took him that it might be as in truth it was, to wit, that she made him drunken, so she might after do her pleasure what while he slept, and wishing to make proof of this, an it were so, he one evening, not having drunken that day, feigned himself, both in words and fashions, the drunkenest man that was aye.
uz: Oshiq xonim shu yo'l bilan davom etar ekan, bechora er uni ichishga undasa ham, hech qachon ichmasligini anglab yetdi; shuning uchun u uni mast qilgandek bo'lishi mumkin deb gumon qildi, chunki u uxlayotganda o'ziga yoqqan narsani qilmoqchi edi va buning isbotini ko'rsatmoqchi edi, bir kuni kechqurun u o'sha kuni mast bo'lmagani uchun, so'zlarda ham, modalarda ham o'zini eng mast odamga o'xshatdi.

en: The lady, believing this and judging that he needed no more drink, put him to bed in all haste and this done, betook herself, as she was used to do whiles, to the house of her lover, where she abode till midnight.
uz: Xonim bunga ishonib, unga boshqa ichimlik kerak emas deb hisoblab, uni shoshilinch ravishda yotqizdi va bu bilan o'zini, odatdagidek, sevgilisining uyiga olib bordi, u yerda yarim tungacha turardi.

en: As for Tofano, no sooner did he know the lady to have left the house than he straightway arose and going to the doors, locked them from within; after which he posted himself at the window, so he might see her return and show her that he had gotten wind of her fashions; and there he abode till such time as she came back.
uz: Tofanoga kelsak, u xonimning uydan chiqqanini bilmasdanoq, darhol o'rnidan turib eshiklarga bordi, ularni ichkaridan qulfladi; shundan so'ng o'zini derazadan joylashtirdi, toki uning qaytganini ko'rishi va uning modalaridan nafas olganini ko'rsatishi uchun; va u yerda u qaytib kelguncha qoldi.

en: The lady, returning home and ﬁnding herself locked out, was beyond measure woeful and began to essay an she might avail to open the door by force, which, after Tofano had awhile suffered, ‘Wife,’ quoth he, ‘thou weariest thyself in vain, for thou canst nowise come in here again.
uz: Xonim uyga qaytib kelib, o'zini qulfdan chiqarib olganini ko'rib, cheksiz qayg'uga to'ldi va eshikni kuch bilan ochishga harakat qila boshladi. Tofanoning biroz azob chekkanidan so'ng, "Xotin," dedi u, "siz bekorga o'zingizni charchatdingiz, chunki endi bu yerga qayta kirishingiz mumkin."

en: Go, get thee back whereas thou hast been till now and be assured that thou shalt never return thither till such time as I shall have done thee, in respect of this affair, such honour as beseemeth thee in the presence of thy kinsfolk and of the neighbours.’ The lady fell to beseeching him for the love of God that it would please him open to her, for that she came not whence he supposed, but from keep- ing vigil with a she-neighbour of hers, for that the nights were long and she could not sleep them all out nor watch at home alone.
uz: Bor, shu paytgacha bo'lgan joyingga qaytib kel va ishonch hosil qilginki, men senga bu ish bo'yicha, qarindoshlaring va qo'shnilaring oldida senga shunday sharaf keltiradigan paytgacha u yerga hech qachon qaytmaysan." Xonim uni Xudoning muhabbati bilan iltimos qildi, u unga yoqsin, chunki u uning kutgan joydan kelmagan edi, balki uning qo'shnisi bilan birga yurishdan, chunki tunlar uzun edi va u ularni uxlay olmasdi va uyda yolg'iz turardi.

en: However, prayers proﬁted her nought, for that her brute of a husband was minded to have all
uz: Ammo, duolar unga hech qanday foyda bermadi, chunki uning eriga barcha narsa kerak edi.

en: the Aretines351 know their shame, whereas none as yet knew it; wherefore, seeing that prayers availed her not, she had recourse to threats and said, ‘An thou open not to me, I will make thee the woefullest man alive.’ ‘And what canst thou do to me?’ asked Tofano, and Mistress Tessa, whose wits Love had already whetted with his counsels, replied, ‘Rather than brook the shame which thou wouldst wrongfully cause me suffer, I will cast myself into this well that is herenigh, where when I am found dead, there is none will believe otherwise than that thou, for very drunkenness, hast cast me therein; wherefore it will behove thee ﬂee and lose all thou hast and abide in banishment or have thy head cut off for my murderer, as thou wilt in truth have been.’ Tofano was nowise moved by these words from his besotted intent; wherefore quoth she to him, ‘Harkye now, I can no longer brook this thy
uz: Aretinlar 351 o'zlarining sharmandaliklarini bilishadi, ammo hech kim buni hali bilmaydi; shuning uchun, duolar unga foyda bermaganini ko'rib, u tahdidlarga murojaat qildi va dedi: "Menga ochilmasang, seni eng to'la odamga tirik qo'yaman." "Va menga nima qila olasan?" - so'radi Tofano, va Tessa xonim, uning aqli sevgi bilan maslahatlari bilan allaqachon oqarib ketgan edi, javob berdi: "Sen meni nohaq azob bermoqchi bo'lgan sharmandalikni tashlashdan ko'ra, men o'zimni bu yaqin quduqqa tashlayman, men o'lik holda topilganimda, bundan boshqa hech kim ishonmaydi, chunki sen meni juda mast holda tashlading; u yerda seni qochib ketadi va seni butunlay tashlab yuboradi, yoki seni o'zingning so'zlaring uchun yo'q qilmoqchi bo'lding, chunki sen uni endi bu yerda yo'q qilmoqchi bo'lding, chunki sen uni...

en: fashery, God pardon it thee!
uz: Fasheriy, Xudo seni kechirsin!

en: Look thou cause lay up352 this distaff of mine that I leave here.’ So saying, the night being so dark that one might scarce see other by the way, she went up to the well and taking a great stone that lay thereby, cried out, ‘God pardon me!’ and let it drop into the water.
uz: "Mana, nega bu yerdan ketayotganim uchun 352 ta yotib qo'y." Shunday qilib, tun shunchalik qorong'i ediki, yo'lda boshqalarni deyarli ko'rmas edi, u quduqqa chiqib, uning yonida yotgan katta toshni olib, "Xudo meni kechiring!" deb baqirdi va suvga tashladi.

en: The stone, striking the water, made a very great noise, which when Tofano heard, he verily believed that she had cast herself in; wherefore, snatching up the bucket and the rope, he rushed out of the house and ran to the well to succour her.
uz: Tosh suvga urilib, juda katta shovqin chiqardi, Tofano buni eshitgach, u haqiqatan ham o'zini tashlaganligiga ishondirdi; shuning uchun, chelak va arqonni olib, uydan chiqib, uni qutqarish uchun quduqqa yugurdi.

en: The lady, who had hidden herself near the door, no sooner saw him run to the well than she slipped into the house and locked herself in; then, getting her to the window, ‘You should water your wine, whenas you drink it,’ quoth she, ‘and not after and by night.’ Tofano, hearing this, knew himself to have been fooled and returned to the door, but could get no ad- mission and proceeded to bid her open to him; but she left speaking softly, as she had done till then, and began, well nigh at a scream, to say, ‘By Christ His Cross, tiresome sot that thou art, thou shalt not enter here to- night; I cannot brook these thy fashions any longer; needs must I let every- one see what manner of man thou art and at what hour thou comest home anights.’ Tofano, on his side, ﬂying into a rage, began to rail at her and bawl; whereupon the neighbours, hearing the clamour, arose, both men and women, and
uz: Xonim, eshik yonida yashirinib yotgan edi, uni quduqqa yugurganini ko'rmasdanoq, u uyga kirib, o'zini qamab oldi; keyin, uni derazadan olib, dedi: "Vinayingni ichganingda, keyin ham, kechasi ham ichma." Tofano buni eshitgach, o'zini aldanganini va eshikga qaytganini bildi, lekin hech qanday e'lon ololmadi va unga uni ochishni boshladi; lekin u sekinlik bilan o'tib ketdi, o'sha paytgacha qilganidek, va qichqirib dedi: "Masihning Xochidan qasam ich, zerikarli, sen bu yerga kirmaysan; men bu liboslarni ko'ra olmayman; har bir kishiga qanday odamni qanday qilib va nima qilayotganingni ko'rishim kerak edi.

en: coming to the windows, asked what was to do.
uz: Derazalarga kelib, nima qilish kerakligini so'radi.

en: The lady answered, weeping, ‘It is this wretch of a man, who still returneth to me of an evening, drunken, or falleth asleep about the taverns and after cometh home at this hour; the which I have long suffered, but, it availing me not and I being unable to put up with it longer, I have bethought me to shame
uz: Xonim yig'lab javob berdi: Bu bechora odam, u hali ham kechqurun menga qaytadi, mast, yoki tavernalar atrofida uxlab qoladi va keyin shu soatda uyga keladi; men uzoq azob chekkan, lekin u menga foyda bermaydi va men bunga chiday olmayotganim sababli, men o'zimni... deb o'yladim.

en: him therefor by locking him out of doors, to see and he will mend himself thereof.’ Tofano, on the other hand, told them, like an ass as he was, how the case stood and threatened her sore; but she said to the neighbours, ‘Look you now what a man he is!
uz: Shuning uchun uni eshiklardan tashqariga qulflab, ko'rsin, shunda u o'zini tuzatadi." Tofanoning o'zi esa, xuddi eshakdek, ish qanday turgani va uning og'rig'iga tahdid solgani haqida ularga aytdi; lekin u qo'shnilarga dedi: "Endi qaranglar, u qanday odam ekan!"

en: What would you say, were I in the street, as he is, and he in the house, as am I?
uz: Siz nima der edingiz, men ko'chada u kabi edim, u esa uyda men kabi?

en: By God His faith, I doubt me you would be- lieve he said sooth.
uz: Xudoga qasamki, Uning ishonchi bilan, men sizdan xotirjam bo'lishingizga shubham bor edi, dedi u.

en: By this you may judge of his wits; he saith I have done just what methinketh he hath himself done.
uz: Shu bilan uning aqlini baholay olasiz; u o'zi qilgan deb o'ylagan narsani qildim, deydi.

en: He thought to fear me by cast- ing I know not what into the well; but would God he had cast himself there in good sooth and drowned himself, so he might have well watered the wine which he hath drunken to excess.’ The neighbours, both men and women, all fell to blaming Tofano, holding him at fault, and chid him for that which he said against the lady; and in a short time the report was so noised abroad from neighbour to neighbour that it reached the ears of the lady’s kinsfolk, who came thither and hearing the thing from one and another of the neigh- bours, took Tofano and gave him such a drubbing that they broke every bone in his body.
uz: U meni qudug'ga uloqtirish orqali qo'rqish uchun o'yladi, bilmayman nima ekanligini; lekin Xudo o'zini u yerga tinch holda uloqtirib, cho'kib ketgan bo'lardi, shunda u haddan tashqari ichgan vinoni yaxshilab sug'organ bo'lardi. Qo'shnilar, erkaklar ham, ayollar ham Tofanoni ayblab, uni aybdor deb ayblashdi va xonimga qarshi aytgan gaplari uchun uni chidashdi; va qisqa vaqt ichida xabar shunchalik tarqaldi, xonimning qulog'iga yetib bordi, ular u yerga kelib, bir-biridan gap eshitib, Tofanoni olib, unga shunday urishdi, hatto uning tanasidagi har bir suyakni sindirishdi.

en: Then, entering the house, they took the lady’s gear and carried her off home with them, threatening Tofano with worse.
uz: Keyin, uyga kirgach, ular xonimning jihozlarini olib, uni o'zlari bilan uyga olib ketishdi va Tofanoni yomonroq narsa bilan tahdid qilishdi.

en: The latter, ﬁnding himself in ill case and seeing that his jealousy had brought him to a sorry pass, for that he still loved his wife heartily,353 procured certain friends to intercede for him and so wrought that he made his peace with the lady and had her home again with him, promising her that he would never be jealous again.
uz: Oxirgisi, o'zini yomon ahvolda his qilib, uning rashki uni achinarli ahvolga olib kelganini ko'rib, xotiniga hali ham chin dildan muhabbat qo'yganini ko'rib, 353 unga shafoat qilish uchun ba'zi do'stlarni topdi va shunday harakat qildi, hatto xonim bilan tinchlik o'rnatdi va u bilan uning uyi yana bir bor bo'ldi, unga hech qachon rashk qilmasligini va'da qildi.

en: Moreover, he gave her leave to do her every pleasure, provided she wrought so discreetly that he should know nothing thereof; and on this wise, like a crackbrained churl as he was, he made peace after suffering damage.
uz: Qolaversa, u unga har qanday xohish bilan shug'ullanishga ruxsat berdi, agar u shu qadar yashirincha ish qilsa, u bundan hech narsa bilmasligi kerak edi; va shu tariqa, xuddi u singan miyasi kabi, zarar ko'rganidan keyin tinchlik qildi.

en: So long live Love and death to war and all its company!”
uz: Yashasin, urush va uning butun kompaniyasiga muhabbat va o'lim!

en: THE FIFTH STORY A jealous husband, in the guise of a priest, confesseth his wife, who giveth him to believe that she loveth a priest, who cometh to her every night; and whilst the husband secretly keepeth watch at the door for the latter, the lady bringeth in a lover of hers by the roof and lieth with him.
uz: BESHINCHI HIKOYA rashkkor er ruhoniy qiyofasida xotiniga iqror bo'ladi, u har kecha unga keladigan ruhoniyni sevishiga ishontiradi; va er oxirgi uchun eshikda yashirincha qo'riqlaydi, lekin xonim o'z sevgilisini tomga olib keladi va u bilan yotadi.

en: Lauretta having made an end of her story and all having commended the lady for that she had done aright and even as beﬁtted her wretch of a hus- band, the king, to lose no time, turned to Fiammetta and courteously im- posed on her the burden of the story-telling; whereupon she began thus, “Most noble ladies, the foregoing story moveth me to tell you, on like wise, of a jealous husband, accounting, as I do, all that their wives do unto such — particularly whenas they are jealous without cause —to be well done and holding that, if the makers of the laws had considered everything, they should have appointed none other penalty unto women who offend in this than that which they appoint unto whoso offendeth against other in self-de- fence; for that jealous men are plotters against the lives of young women and most diligent procurers of their deaths.
uz: Lauretta o'z hikoyasini tugatdi va xonimni to'g'ri qilganligi uchun maqtadi, hatto unga munosib bo'lganidek, bechora xotini, qirol, hech qanday vaqt yo'qotmaslik uchun, Fiammettaga o'girilib, unga hikoya yukini xushmuomalalik bilan yukladi; shundan so'ng u shunday boshladi: "Eng aziz xonimlar, oldingi hikoya meni sizga xuddi men kabi dono, rashk qiluvchi er haqida aytishga undaydi, ularning xotinlari nima qilishlarini - ayniqsa, ular bejizga rashk qilishsa - yaxshi bo'lishadi va agar qonun chiqaruvchilari hamma narsani ko'rib chiqqan bo'lsalar, ular boshqa ayollarni o'zlariga nisbatan qilmoqchi bo'lgan ishlardan ko'ra jazo tayinlashlari kerak edi; chunki rashk qiluvchi erkaklar o'z hayotini o'z-o'zidan

en: Wives abide all the week mewed up at home, occupying themselves with domestic ofﬁces and the oc- casions of their families and households, and after they would fain, like everyone else, have some solace and some rest on holidays and be at leisure to take some diversion even as do the tillers of the ﬁelds, the artisans of the towns and the administrators of the laws, according to the example of God himself, who rested from all His labours the seventh day, and to the intent of the laws, both human and Divine, which, looking to the honour of God and the common weal of all, have distinguished working days from those of repose.
uz: Xotinlar butun hafta davomida uyda o'tirib, o'z oilalari va xonadonlarining uy ishlari bilan band bo'lishadi, va ular hammaga o'xshab, ta'tillarda biroz tasalli topib, dam olishni xohlashadi va dam olishni xohlashadi, xuddi dala dehqonlari, shahar hunarmandlari va qonunlar ma'murlari kabi, Xudoning o'ziga ko'ra, yettinchi kuni barcha mehnatlaridan dam olgan va qonunlarning maqsadiga ko'ra, Xudoning sharafiga va hammaning umumiy farovonligiga qarab, ish kunlarini dam olishdan ajratib ko'rsatgan.

en: But to this jealous men will on no wise consent; nay, those days which are gladsome for all other women they make wretcheder and more
uz: Ammo rashk qiluvchi erkaklar bunga hech qanday rozilik bildirmaydilar; aksincha, boshqa ayollar uchun quvonchli bo'lgan o'sha kunlar ularni yanada achinarli qiladi.

en: doleful than the others to their wives, keeping them yet closelier straitened and conﬁned; and what a misery and a languishment this is for the poor creatures those only know who have proved it.
uz: Xotinlariga boshqalardan ko'ra ko'proq muhtoj, ularni yanada toraytirgan va cheklangan holda ushlab turadi; va bu faqat buni isbotlagan bechora maxluqlar uchun qanday baxtsizlik va umidsizlikdir.

en: Wherefore, to conclude, I say that what a woman doth to a husband who is jealous without cause should certes not be condemned, but rather commended.
uz: Shuning uchun, xulosa qilib aytishim mumkinki, ayolning hech qanday sababsiz rashk qiladigan eriga qilgan ishi albatta qoralanmasligi kerak, aksincha, maqtovga sazovor bo'lishi kerak.

en: There was, then, in Arimino a merchant, very rich both in lands and mon- ies, who, having to wife a very fair lady, became beyond measure jealous of her; nor had he other cause for this save that, as he loved her exceedingly and held her very fair and saw that she studied with all her might to please him, even so he imagined that every man loved her and that she appeared fair to all and eke that she studied to please others as she did himself, which was the reasoning of a man of nought and one of little sense.
uz: Shunday qilib, Ariminonda bir savdogar bor edi, u yerda ham yerlar, ham dunyo boylari juda boy edi. U juda go'zal xonimga turmushga chiqib, unga haddan tashqari hasad qildi; va buning boshqa sababi ham yo'q edi, chunki u uni juda ham yaxshi ko'rardi va uni juda go'zal ko'rardi va u unga yoqish uchun bor kuchini sarflaganini ko'rardi. Shunday qilib, u har bir odam uni yaxshi ko'rishini va u hammaga adolatli ko'rinishini va o'zi kabi boshqalarni ham yoqtirish uchun o'rganishini tasavvur qilardi. Bu hech narsa emas va bir odamning fikrlashidir.

en: Being grown thus jealous, he kept such strict watch over her and held her in such con- straint that belike many there be of those who are condemned to capital punishment who are less straitly guarded of their gaolers; for, far from be- ing at liberty to go to weddings or entertainments or to church or indeed anywise to set foot without the house, she dared not even stand at the win- dow nor look abroad on any occasion; wherefore her life was most wretched and she brooked this annoy with the more impatience as she felt herself the less to blame.
uz: Shunday rashk bilan ulg'ayganidan so'ng, u uni shunchalik qattiq kuzatib turardi va shunday bosim ostida ushlab turardi, hatto ko'pchilik o'z yaqinlaridan kamroq qo'riqlanadigan o'lim jazosiga mahkum bo'lganlar ham bor edi; chunki, to'ylarga yoki ko'ngilochar tadbirlarga yoki cherkovga borishga yoki umuman uysiz yurishga erkin bo'lishdan yiroq edi, u hech qanday vaziyatda g'alaba qozonishga ham jur'at eta olmadi va chet elga qaramadi; shuning uchun uning hayoti juda achinarli edi va u o'zini kamroq aybdor his qilgani uchun bu g'azabni shunchalik sabrsizlik bilan qabul qilardi.

en: Accordingly, seeing herself unjustly suspected of her husband, she determined, for her own solacement, to ﬁnd a means (an she but might) of doing on such wise that he should have reason for his ill usage of her.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, o'zini eridan adolatsiz gumon qilgani sababli, u o'ziga tasalli topish uchun shunday donolik bilan ish qilishning bir yo'lini topishga qaror qildi, toki u undan yomon foydalanish uchun sababga ega bo'lsin.

en: And for that she might not station herself at the window and so had no opportunity of showing herself favourable to the suit of anyone who might take note of her, as he passed along her street, and pay his court to her —knowing that in the adjoining house there was a certain young man both handsome and agreeable —she bethought herself to look if there were any hole in the wall that parted the two houses and therethrough to spy once and again till such time as she should see the youth aforesaid and ﬁnd an occasion of speaking with him and bestowing on him her love, so he would accept thereof, purposing, if a means could be found, to foregather with him bytimes and on this wise while away her sorry life till such time as the de- mon [of jealousy] should take leave of her husband.
uz: Va shuning uchun u derazada o'zini turmasligi va ko'chasidan o'tib ketayotganda, uni kuzatib boradigan va unga o'z marhamatini to'laydigan har qanday odamga o'zini yoqtirish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lmasligi uchun  qo'shni uyda bir yigit borligini bilgan holda, ham chiroyli, ham xushmuomala  u o'zini ikki uyni ajratib turuvchi devorda teshik bor-yo'qligini ko'rishga va u bilan gaplashishga, unga muhabbat ko'rsatishga imkon topmaguncha, u buni qabul qilardi, agar iloji bo'lsa, u bilan bir zumda uchrashishni va shu bilan birga o'z hayotini tashlab ketishni maqsad qilgan holda, u eriga g'azabni ko'rmaguncha.

en: Accordingly, she went spying about the walls of the house, now in one part and now in another, whenas her husband was abroad, and happened at last upon a very privy place where the wall was somewhat opened by a ﬁs- sure and looking therethrough, albeit she could ill discover what was on the
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u uyning devorlarini, hozir bir qismida, endi boshqa qismida, josuslik qilib yurdi, er chet elda bo'lganida, va nihoyat devor biroz ochiq bo'lgan juda maxfiy joyga duch keldi, garchi u yerda nima borligini aniqlay olmasa ham.

en: other side, algates she perceived that the opening gave upon a bedchamber there and said in herself, ‘Should this be the chamber of Filippo,’ to wit, the youth her neighbour, ‘I were half sped.’ Then, causing secretly enquire of this by a maid of hers, who had pity upon her, she found that the young man did indeed sleep in that chamber all alone; wherefore, by dint of often visit- ing the crevice and dropping pebbles and such small matters, whenas she perceived him to be there, she wrought on such wise that he came to the opening, to see what was to do; whereupon she called to him softly.
uz: Boshqa tomondan, Algates u yerda yotoqxonaga teshik ochilganini sezdi va o'zida dedi: "Bu Filipponing xonasi bo'lishi kerakmi?" - ya'ni, uning qo'shnisi yosh, "Men yarim tez edim". Keyin, unga rahm qilgan xizmatchisi tomonidan bu haqda yashirincha so'rashga majbur bo'lib, u yigit haqiqatan ham o'sha xonada yolg'iz uxlayotganini angladi; shuning uchun, tez-tez yoriqlarga tashrif buyurib, toshlarni va shunga o'xshash mayda narsalarni tashlab, uni u yerda bo'lishi kerak bo'lganda, u shunday donolik bilan harakat qildi, u teshikka kelib, nima qilish kerakligini ko'rdi; shundan so'ng, u uni sekin chaqirdi.

en: He, knowing her voice, answered her, and she, proﬁting by the occasion, dis- covered to him in brief all her mind; whereat the youth was mightily con- tent and made shift to enlarge the hole from his side on such wise that none could perceive it; and therethrough they many a time bespoke one another and touched hands, but could go no farther, for the jealous vigilance of the husband.
uz: U uning ovozini bilgach, unga javob berdi, va u, imkoniyatdan foydalanib, unga butun aqlini qisqacha yopdi; shu bilan birga yosh yigit uning yonidagi teshikni hech kim sezmaydigan darajada kattalashtirishga kuch bilan harakat qildi; va shu orqali ular bir-birlarini ko'p marta so'rashdi va qo'llarini tekkizishdi, lekin erning rashk bilan hushyorligi uchun uzoqqa bora olmadilar.

en: After awhile, the Feast of the Nativity drawing near, the lady told her husband that, an it pleased him, she would fain go to church on Christmas morning and confess and take the sacrament, as other Christians did.
uz: Biroz vaqt o'tgach, Rojdestvo bayrami yaqinlashganda, xonim eriga, unga ma'qul bo'lgani uchun, Rojdestvo kuni ertalab cherkovga borib, boshqa xristianlar kabi iqror bo'lib, sakrament qabul qilishini aytdi.

en: Quoth he, ‘And what sin hast thou committed that thou wouldst confess?’ ‘How?’ answered the lady.
uz: U so'radi: Va sen qanday gunoh qilganingni tan olmoqchisan? Qanday qilib? deb javob berdi xonim.

en: ‘Thinkest thou that I am a saint, because thou keepest me mewed up?
uz: Siz meni xafa qilganingiz uchun men muqaddasman deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: Thou must know well enough that I commit sins like all others that live in this world; but I will not tell them to thee, for that thou art not a priest.’ The jealous wretch took suspicion at these words and determ- ined to seek to know what sins she had committed; wherefore, having be- thought himself of a means whereby he might gain his end, he answered that he was content, but that he would have her go to no other church than their parish chapel and that thither she must go betimes in the morning and confess herself either to their chaplain or to such priest as the latter should appoint her and to none other and presently return home.
uz: Sen yaxshi bilishing kerakki, men ham bu dunyoda yashaydigan barcha odamlar kabi gunohlar qilaman; lekin men bularni senga aytmayman, chunki sen ruhoniy emassan. Hasadgo'y bechora bu so'zlarga shubha bilan qaradi va qanday gunohlar qilganini bilishga qaror qildi; shuning uchun, o'zini oxiriga erishish yo'li deb o'ylagan holda, u rozi ekanligini, lekin uni ularning cherkovidan boshqa cherkovga borishini xohlashini va u yerga ertalab borib, o'zini ruhoniyga yoki ruhoniyga tan olishi kerakligini, chunki u uni tayinlashi kerak edi va boshqa hech kimga qaytib kelmasligini aytdi.

en: Herseemed she half apprehended his meaning; but without saying otherwhat, she answered that she would do as he said.
uz: U uning ma'nosini yarim anglagandek edi; lekin boshqa hech narsa demasdan, u uning aytganini qiladi deb javob berdi.

en: Accordingly, Christmas Day come, the lady arose at daybreak and attir- ing herself, repaired to the church appointed her of her husband, who, on his part, betook himself to the same place and reached it before her.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Rojdestvo kuni kelgach, xonim tong otishida turdi va o'zini tuzatgan holda, cherkovga tayinladi. Er esa, o'z navbatida, o'zini shu yerga olib bordi va undan oldin yetib bordi.

en: Having already taken order with the chaplain of that which he had a mind to do, he hastily donned one of the latter’s gowns, with a great ﬂapped cowl, such as we see priests wear, and drawing the hood a little over his face, seated him- self in the choir.
uz: U o'zi o'ylab topgan ishning ruhoniysidan buyurtma olganidan so'ng, u shoshilinch ravishda oxirgilarning ko'ylaklaridan birini kiydirdi, ruhoniylar kiygan kabi katta yumshoq qopqoq bilan, va boshidagi kaputni biroz ko'tarib, xorda o'tirdi.

en: The lady, entering the chapel, enquired for the chaplain,
uz: Xonim ibodatxonaga kirib, ruhoniy haqida so'radi.

en: who came and hearing from her that she would fain confess, said that he could not hear her, but would send her one of his brethren.
uz: U kelib, undan iqror bo'lishni xohlayotganini eshitib, uni eshitolmasligini, lekin unga birodarlaridan birini yuborishini aytdi.

en: Accordingly, go- ing away, he sent her the jealous man, in an ill hour for the latter, who came up with a very grave air, and albeit the day was not over bright and he had drawn the cowl far over his eyes, knew not so well to disguise himself but he was readily recognized by the lady, who, seeing this, said in herself, ‘Praised be God!
uz: Shunga ko'ra, ketayotib, u unga hasadgo'y odamni yubordi, oxirgisi uchun yomon vaqtda, u juda jiddiy havo bilan keldi va garchi kun yorqin bo'lmasa ham va u ko'zlariga ko'rpani uzoqroq tortgan bo'lsa ham, o'zini niqoblashni unchalik yaxshi bilmas edi, lekin uni xonim osonlik bilan tanib oldi, u buni ko'rib, o'zida dedi: "Allohim!"

en: From a jealous man he is turned priest; but no matter; I will e’en give him what he goeth seeking.’ Accordingly, feigning not to know him, she seated herself at his feet.
uz: Hasadgo'y odamdan ruhoniy bo'ldi; lekin farqi yo'q; men unga izlagan narsasini beraman. Shunday qilib, uni tanimay, o'zini uning oyoqlari ostiga o'tqazdi.

en: My lord Jealousy had put some pebbles in his mouth, to impede his speech somewhat, so his wife might not know him by his voice, himseeming he was in every other particular so thoroughly disguised that he was nowise fearful of being recognized by her.
uz: Rabbim rashk uning nutqiga biroz to'sqinlik qilish uchun og'ziga toshlarni qo'ygan edi, shunda xotini uni ovozi bilan tanimasdi, go'yo u har bir boshqa narsada shunchalik yaxshi niqoblangan ediki, endi u uni tanishdan qo'rqardi.

en: To come to the confession, the lady told him, amongst other things, (having ﬁrst declared herself to be married), that she was enamoured of a priest, who came every night to lie with her.
uz: E'tirofga kelish uchun, xonim unga, boshqa narsalar qatorida (avval o'zini turmushga chiqqanini e'lon qilgan holda), har kecha u bilan yotishga keladigan ruhoniyga oshiq ekanligini aytdi.

en: When the jealous man heard this, himseemed he had gotten a knife-thrust in the heart, and had not desire constrained him to know more, he had abandoned the confession and gone away.
uz: Hasadgo'y bu gapni eshitgach, go'yo yuragiga pichoq sanchildi va uni ko'proq bilishga majbur qilmadi, tan olishdan voz kechib ketdi.

en: Standing fast, then, he asked the lady, ‘How!
uz: To'g'ri turib, u xonimdan so'radi: Qanday!

en: Doth not your husband lie with you?’ ‘Ay doth he, sir,’ replied she.
uz: Eringiz siz bilan yotmaydimi? Yoq, xojayin,  javob berdi u.

en: ‘How, then,’ asked the jealous man, ‘can the priest also lie with you?’ ‘Sir,’ answered she, ‘by what art he doth it I know not, but there is not a door in the house so fast locked but it openeth so soon as he toucheth it; and he tell- eth me that, whenas he cometh to the door of my chamber, before opening it, he pronounceth certain words, by virtue whereof my husband incontinent falleth asleep, and so soon as he perceiveth him to be fast, he openeth the door and cometh in and lieth with me; and this never faileth.’ Quoth the mock priest, ‘Madam, this is ill done, and it behoveth you altogether to re- frain therefrom.’ ‘Sir,’ answered the lady, ‘methinketh I could never do that, for that I love him too well.’ ‘Then,’ said the other, ‘I cannot shrive you.’ Quoth she, ‘I am grieved for that; but I came not hither to tell you lies; an I thought I could do it, I would tell you so.’ ‘In
uz: Xo'sh, qanday qilib,  so'radi hasadgo'y odam,  ruhoniy ham siz bilan yotishi mumkinmi?  Janob,  javob berdi u,  nima bilan ekanligini bilmayman, lekin uyda tez qulflanadigan eshik yo'q, lekin u unga tegishi bilan ochiladi; va u menga aytadi-ki, u mening xonam eshigiga kelganda, uni ochishdan oldin, u ba'zi so'zlarni aytadi, chunki erim tinimsiz uxlab qoladi, va u uni tez uxlashga majbur qilsa, u eshikni ochadi va men bilan birga yotadi; va bu hech qachon zaif bo'lmaydi.

en: truth, madam,’ replied the hus- band, ‘I am concerned for you, for that I see you lose your soul at this game; but, to do you service, I will well to take the pains of putting up my special orisons to God in your name, the which maybe shall proﬁt you, and I will send you bytimes a little clerk of mine, to whom you shall say if they have proﬁted you or not; and if they have proﬁted you, we will proceed farther.’ ‘Sir,’ answered the lady, ‘whatever you do, send none to me at
uz: Haqiqatan ham, xonim,  javob berdi xus-band,  men siz haqingizda xavotirdaman, chunki men sizni bu o'yinda joningizni yo'qotayotganingizni ko'ryapman; lekin, sizga xizmat qilish uchun, men sizning nomingizdan Xudoga bo'lgan maxsus mas'uliyatlarimga bardosh berish azobini o'z zimmamga olishga tayyorman, bu sizga foyda keltirishi mumkin, va men sizga vaqti-vaqti bilan kichik bir kotibni yuboraman, unga sizga foyda keltirganmi yoki yo'qmi, deb ayting; va agar ular sizga foyda keltirgan bo'lsa, biz yanada uzoqroqqa boramiz. Janob,  javob berdi xonim,  nima qilsangiz, menga hech narsa yubormang

en: home, for, should my husband come to know of it, he is so terribly jealous that nothing in the world would get it out of his head that your messenger came hither for nought354 but ill, and I should have no peace with him this year to come.’ Quoth the other, ‘Madam, have no fear of that, for I will cer- tainly contrive it on such wise that you shall never hear a word of the matter from him.’ Then said she, ‘So but you can engage to do that, I am content.’ Then, having made her confession and gotten her penance, she rose to her feet and went off to hear mass; whilst the jealous man (ill luck go with him!) withdrew, bursting with rage, to put off his priest’s habit, and returned home, impatient to ﬁnd a means of surprising the priest with his wife, so he might play the one and the other an ill turn.
uz: Uyga, chunki, agar erim bu haqda bilsa, u dunyodagi hech narsa uning xayolidan chiqmasligi uchun juda rashk qiladi, shuning uchun sizning elchingiz bu yerga hech qanday zarar ko'rmagan holda keldi, va bu yil u bilan tinchlik bo'lmasligi kerak." Boshqa biri aytdi: "Xonim, bundan qo'rqmang, chunki men buni shunday usulda o'ylab topamanki, undan bu haqda hech qachon eshitmaysiz." Keyin u dedi: "Xo'sh, siz buni qilishga rozi bo'lasiz, men rozi bo'laman." Keyin, uni tan olib, tavbasini qabul qilib, u oyoqqa turdi va ommaviy tinglashga ketdi.

en: Presently the lady came back from church and saw plainly enough from her husband’s looks that she had given him an ill Christmas; albeit he stud- ied, as most he might, to conceal that which he had done and what him- seemed he had learned.
uz: Ayni paytda xonim cherkovdan qaytib keldi va erining ko'rinishidan unga yomon Rojdestvo berganini aniq ko'rdi; garchi u har safar, qo'lidan kelgancha, u qilgan ishini va o'rgangan narsani yashirishga harakat qilardi.

en: Then, being inwardly resolved to lie in wait near the street-door that night and watch for the priest’s coming, he said to the lady, ‘Needs must I sup and lie abroad tonight, wherefore look thou lock the street-door fast, as well as that of the midstair and that of thy chamber, and get thee to bed, whenas it seemeth good to thee.’ The lady answered, ‘It is well,’ and betaking herself, as soon as she had leisure, to the hole in the wall, she made the wonted signal, which when Filippo heard, he came to her forthright.
uz: Keyin, o'sha kechasi ko'cha eshigi yonida kutib yotishga va ruhoniyning kelishini kutishga qaror qilib, u xonimga dedi: "Bu tun uxlab yotishim kerak, shuning uchun ko'cha eshigini, shuningdek, o'rta zinapoyani va xonangizni tez qulflab, senga yoqqancha yot." Xonim javob berdi: "Xo'p," va dam olishi bilanoq, devordagi teshikka o'zini qo'yib, u devordagi teshikni ko'rsatdi. Filippo eshitgach, u unga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri keldi.

en: She told him how she had done that morning and what her husband had said to her after dinner and added, ‘I am certain he will not leave the house, but will set himself to watch the door; wherefore do thou ﬁnd means to come hither to me tonight by the roof, so we may lie together.’ The young man was mightily rejoiced at this and answered, ‘Madam, leave me do.’ Accordingly, the night come, the jealous man took his arms and hid him- self by stealth in a room on the ground ﬂoor, whilst the lady, whenas it seemed to her time —having caused lock all the doors and in particular that of the midstair, so he might not avail to come up —summoned the young man, who came to her from his side by a very privy way.
uz: U unga o'sha ertalab nima qilganini va erining kechki ovqatdan keyin unga nima deganini aytib berdi va qo'shib qo'ydi: "Men aniq u uyni tark etmaydi, balki eshikni qo'riqlashga o'tiradi; shuning uchun bugun kechqurun tom bo'ylab bu yerga kelishga qanday yo'l topasan, toki birga yotamiz". Yigit bundan juda xursand bo'ldi va javob berdi: "Xonim, meni qo'ying." Shunga ko'ra, tun bo'lgach, hasadgo'y odam qo'llarini olib, uni yerga yashirdi - o'zini o'zi, xonada yashirgan holda, xonim esa, vaqt o'tgandek tuyulganda  hamma eshiklar va ayniqsa o'rta zinapoyadan qulfga ega bo'lgani uchun, u yuqoriga chiqishga imkon bermas edi  yigit uni uning yonidan juda maxfiy tarzda chaqirdi.

en: Thereupon they went to bed and gave themselves a good time, taking their pleasure one of the other till daybreak, when the young man returned to his own house.
uz: Shundan so'ng ular yotishga ketishdi va bir-birlaridan rohatlanib, yaxshi vaqt o'tkazishdi, yigit o'z uyiga qaytib kelganidan keyin tong otguncha.

en: Meanwhile, the jealous man stood to his arms well nigh all night beside the street-door, sorry and supperless and dying of cold, and waited for the priest to come till near upon day, when, unable to watch any longer, he returned to
uz: Ayni paytda, hasadgo'y odam butun tun ko'cha eshigi yonida uning quchog'iga yaqin turardi, achinib, kechki ovqatsiz va sovuqdan o'layotgan holda, ruhoniyning yaqinlashishini kutardi, keyin esa, uzoqroq kuzatolmay, qaytib keldi.

en: the ground ﬂoor room and there fell asleep.
uz: Birinchi qavat xonasi va u yerda uxlab qoldi.

en: Towards tierce he awoke and the street door being now open, he made a show of returning from other- where and went up into his house and dined.
uz: Birinchi qavatga yaqin u uyg'ondi va ko'cha eshigi endi ochiq bo'lib, u boshqa joydan qaytganini ko'rsatdi - u yerda uyiga chiqib ovqatlandi.

en: A little after, he sent a lad, as he were the priest’s clerkling that had confessed her, to the lady to ask if she wot of were come thither again.
uz: Biroz vaqt o'tgach, u ruhoniyning xizmatkori bo'lib, uni tan olgan bir yigitni xonimga yana u yerga kelganmi yoki yo'qmi deb so'rash uchun yubordi.

en: She knew the messenger well enough and answered that he had not come thither that night and that if he did thus, he might haply pass out of her mind, albeit she wished it not.
uz: U xabarchini yetarlicha yaxshi bilardi va u o'sha kecha u yerga kelmaganini va agar shunday qilsa, u xayolidan o'tib ketishi mumkinligini, garchi u xohlamasa ham, javob berdi.

en: What more should I tell you?
uz: Sizga yana nima deyishim kerak?

en: The jealous man abode on the watch night after night, looking to catch the priest at his entering in, and the lady still had a merry life with her lover the while.
uz: Hasadgo'y odam kechasi-kechasi qo'riqxonada o'tirardi, ruhoniyni kirayotganda ushlashga intilardi, xonim esa shu vaqtgacha sevgilisi bilan xursandchilik bilan yashardi.

en: At length the cuckold, able to contain himself no longer, asked his wife, with an angry air, what she had said to the priest the morning she had con- fessed herself to him.
uz: Oxir-oqibat, o'zini tuta olmagan cuckold xotiniga g'azablangan holda, ertalab unga o'zini tan olgan ruhoniyga nima deganini so'radi.

en: She answered that she would not tell him, for that it was neither a just thing nor a seemly; whereupon, ‘Vile woman that thou art!’ cried he.
uz: U unga aytmasligini aytdi, chunki bu na adolatli ish, na jozibali ish emas edi; shuning uchun u: Naqadar yomon ayolsan! deb baqirdi.

en: ‘In despite of thee I know what thou saidst to him, and needs must I know the priest of whom thou art so mightily enamoured and who, by means of his conjurations, lieth with thee every night; else will I slit thy weasand.’ She replied that it was not true that she was enamoured of any priest.
uz: Senga qaramay, unga nima deganingni bilaman, va senga shunchalik qattiq oshiq bo'lgan ruhoniyni bilishim kerak, u har kecha o'z fitnalari orqali senga yotadi; aks holda sening qumingni kesaman. U hech qanday ruhonga oshiq bo'lgani rost emas, deb javob berdi.

en: ‘How?’ cried the husband, ‘Saidst thou not thus and thus to the priest who confessed thee?’ And she, ‘Thou couldst not have reported it better, not to say if he had told it thee, but if thou hadst been present; ay, I did tell him this.’ ‘Then,’ rejoined the jealous man, ‘tell me who is this priest, and that quickly.’ The lady fell a-smiling and answered, ‘It rejoiceth me mightily to see a wise man led by the nose by a woman, even as one leadeth a ram by the horns to the shambles, albeit thou art no longer wise nor hast been since the hour when, unknowing why, thou sufferedst the malignant spirit of jealousy to enter thy breast; and the sillier and more besotted thou art, so much the less is my glory thereof.
uz: Qanday qilib? deb qichqirdi er, Seni tan olgan ruhoniyga shunday-shunday demadingmi? Va u dedi: Senga aytmaganingdan yaxshiroq xabar bera olmas eding, agar u senga aytgan bolsa edi, lekin agar sen bolganingda edi; ey, men unga shunday aytgan bolardim.  Unda,  rashk odam javob berdi,  menga bu ruhoniy kim ekanligini ayt, va u tezda. Xonim tabassum qilib javob berdi: Men bir ayolning burunidan boshqariladigan dono odamni korganimdan juda xursandman, xuddi bir qozichoqni shoxlari bilan shambullarga yetaklaganidek.

en: Deemest thou, husband mine, I am as blind of the eyes of the body as thou of those of the mind?
uz: Ey erim, men sening aql ko'zlaring kabi tana ko'zlariga ko'rman, deb o'ylaysanmi?

en: Certes, no; I perceived at ﬁrst sight who was the priest that confessed me and know that thou wast he; but I had it at heart to give thee that which thou wentest seeking, and in sooth I have done it.
uz: Albatta, yo'q; meni tan olgan ruhoniy kim ekanligini birinchi ko'rishda angladim va bilardimki, sen o'sha odamsan; lekin qalbimda senga izlagan narsangni berishga qaror qildim va xotirjam holda buni qildim.

en: Wert thou as wise as thou thinkest to be, thou wouldst not have essayed by this means to learn the secrets of thy good wife, but wouldst, without taking vain suspicion, have recognized that which she confessed to thee to be the very truth, without her having sinned in aught.
uz: O'zingni qanchalik dono deb o'ylaganingcha, sen bu vosita bilan yaxshi xotining sirlarini o'rganmas eding, balki behuda gumon qilmasdan, u senga tan bergan narsani hech qanday gunoh qilmagan holda, haqiqat ekanligini tan olarding.

en: I told thee that I loved a priest, and wast not thou, whom I am much to blame
uz: Men senga bir ruhoniyni sevganimni aytdim, lekin sen emassan, men uni ko'p ayblayman.

en: to love as I do, become a priest?
uz: Xuddi men kabi sevish, ruhoniy bo'lishmi?

en: I told thee that no door of my house could abide locked, whenas he had a mind to lie with me; and what door in the house was ever kept against thee, whenas thou wouldst come whereas I might be?
uz: Men senga aytdimki, uyimning hech bir eshigi qulflanib qolmas edi, toki u men bilan yotmoqchi bo'lsa; va uyning qaysi eshigi senga qarshi qo'riqlangan edi, toki men bo'lgan joyga kelishing mumkin bo'lsa?

en: I told thee that the priest lay with me every night, and when was it that thou layest not with me?
uz: Men senga ruhoniy har kecha men bilan yotgani haqida aytdim, va sen qachon men bilan yotmading?

en: And whenassoever thou sentest thy clerk to me, which was thou knowest, as often as thou layest from me, I sent thee word that the priest had not been with me.
uz: Va qachonki menga o'z kotibingni yuborsang, uni bilganingdek, mendan uzoqlashganda, ruhoniy men bilan birga bo'lmaganligini senga xabar yubordim.

en: What other than a crack-brain like thee, who has suffered thyself to be blinded by thy jealousy, had failed to understand these things?
uz: Sen kabi aqldan ozgan, rashkingga ko'r bo'lishingga yo'l qo'ygan odamdan boshqa nima bu narsalarni tushunmagan edi?

en: Thou hast abidden in the house, keeping watch anights, and thoughtest to have given me to believe that thou wast gone abroad to sup and sleep.
uz: Siz uyda yashirindingiz, tunlari bedor bo'ldingiz va menga ovqatlanish va uxlash uchun chet elga ketganingizga ishontirdim deb o'yladingiz.

en: Bethink thee henceforth and become a man again, as thou wast wont to be; and make not thyself a laughing stock to whoso knoweth thy fashions, as do I, and leave this unconscionable watching that thou keepest; for I swear to God that, an the fancy took me to make thee wear the horns, I would engage, haddest thou an hundred eyes, as thou hast but two, to do my pleasure on such wise that thou shouldst not be ware thereof.’ The jealous wretch, who thought to have very adroitly surprised his wife’s secrets, hearing this, avouched himself befooled and without answer- ing otherwhat, held the lady for virtuous and discreet; and whenas it be- hoved him to be jealous, he altogether divested himself of his jealousy, even as he had put it on, what time he had no need thereof.
uz: Endi o'zingni o'ylab, odatdagidek odam bo'lgin; va o'zingni men kabi o'z modalaringni biladiganlarga kulgili qilma, va bu befarosat kuzatuvni saqlab qolma; chunki Xudoga qasam ichamanki, men seni shoxlarni kiyintirish uchun o'ylagandim, agar sening yuz ko'zing bo'lsa edi, faqat ikki ko'zing bo'lsa edi, mening xohishimni shunday qilishing kerak ediki, sen bundan xavotirlanmas eding.

en: Wherefore the dis- creet lady, being in a manner licensed to do her pleasures, thenceforward no longer caused her lover to come to her by the roof, as go the cats, but e’en brought him in at the door, and dealing advisedly, many a day thereafter gave herself a good time and led a merry life with him.”
uz: Shuning uchun, xotinning o'z zavqlarini bajara olish huquqiga ega bo'lgani uchun, u bundan buyon sevgilisiga mushuklar kabi tom bo'ylab uning oldiga kelishiga yo'l qo'ymadi, balki uni eshikdan olib kirdi va maslahatli munosabatda bo'ldi, keyin ko'p kunlar o'ziga yaxshi vaqt berdi va u bilan quvnoq hayot kechirdi.

en: THE SIXTH STORY Madam Isabella, being in company with Leonetto her lover, is visited by one Messer Lambertuccio, of whom she is beloved; her husband returning (unexpected) she sendeth Lambertuccio forth of the house, whinger in hand, and the husband after escorteth Leonetto home.
uz: OLTINCHI HIKOYA Madam Izabella Leonetto bilan birga bo'lib, uni bir janob Lambertuccio ziyorat qiladi, u uni sevadi; eri qaytib kelganda (kutilmaganda) u Lambertucciyni qo'lida ingrash bilan uydan jo'natadi va er uni Leonetto uyiga kuzatib boradi.

en: The company were wonder-well pleased with Fiammetta’s story, all afﬁrm- ing that the lady had done excellently well and as it behoved unto such a brute of a man, and after it was ended, the king bade Pampinea follow on, who proceeded to say, “There are many who, speaking ignorantly, avouch that love bereaveth folk of their senses and causeth whoso loveth to become witless.
uz: Kompaniya Fiammetta'ning hikoyasidan juda xursand edi, ularning barchasi xonim juda yaxshi ish qilganini va bunday shafqatsiz odamga kerak bo'lganini tasdiqladilar. U tugagandan so'ng, shoh Pampineaga ergashishni buyurdi va u shunday dedi: "Bilmasdan gapiradigan ko'pchilik bor, sevgi odamlarni aqldan ozdiradi va sevgan odamni aqlsiz qiladi."

en: Meseemeth this is a foolish opinion, as hath indeed been well enough shown by the things already related, and I purpose yet again to demonstrate it.
uz: Menimcha, bu ahmoqona fikr, buni allaqachon bog'langan narsalar yaxshi ko'rsatgan va men uni yana bir bor namoyish etishni maqsad qilganman.

en: In our city, which aboundeth in all good things, there was once a young lady both gently born and very fair, who was the wife of a very worthy and notable gentleman; and as it happeneth often that folk cannot forever brook one same food, but desire bytimes to vary their diet, this lady, her husband not altogether satisfying her, became enamoured of a young man called Le- onetto and very well bred and agreeable, for all he was of no great extrac- tion.
uz: Bizning shaharimizda, barcha yaxshi narsalarga boy bo'lgan bir paytda, juda ham muloyim tug'ilgan va juda chiroyli yosh bir ayol bor edi, u juda munosib va e'tiborli janobning xotini edi; va ko'pincha odamlar bir xil taomni abadiy qabul qila olmasligi, balki vaqti-vaqti bilan o'z taomlarini o'zgartirishni xohlashi mumkin bo'lgani kabi, bu ayol, uning eri uni umuman qoniqtirmagan holda, Le-onetto ismli yosh yigitga oshiq bo'lib qoldi va juda yaxshi tarbiyalangan va kelishgan edi, chunki u hech qanday ajoyib xususiyatga ega emas edi.

en: He on like wise fell in love with her, and as you know that seldom doth that which both parties desire abide without effect, it was no great while before accomplishment was given to their loves.
uz: U donolik bilan unga oshiq bo'lib qoldi va bilasizki, har ikki tomon xohlagan narsa kamdan-kam hollarda samarasiz qoladi, bu ularning muhabbatlariga erishishdan oldin unchalik katta emas edi.

en: Now it chanced that, she being a fair and engaging lady, a gentleman called Messer Lambertuc- cio became sore enamoured of her, whom, for that he seemed to her a dis- agreeable man and a tiresome, she could not for aught in the world bring herself to love.
uz: Endi shunday bo'ldiki, u go'zal va qiziqarli ayol bo'lgani uchun, Messer Lambertuc-tio deb nomlangan bir janob unga juda oshiq bo'lib qoldi. U unga noqulay va zerikarli odamdek tuyulgani uchun, u dunyoga hech narsa uchun o'zini sevishga olib kelolmasdi.

en: However, after soliciting her amain with messages and it availing him nought, he sent to her threatening her, for that he was a notable
uz: Ammo, uni xabarlar bilan qiziqtirganidan so'ng va bu unga hech qanday foyda bermagandan so'ng, u unga tahdid qilib yubordi, chunki u diqqatga sazovor edi.

en: man, to dishonour her, an she did not his pleasure; wherefore she, fearful and knowing his character, submitted herself to do his will.
uz: Erkak, uni sharmanda qilish uchun, u uning xohishiga yo'l qo'ymadi; shuning uchun u, qo'rqib va uning xarakterini bilgan holda, uning irodasini bajarishga bo'ysundi.

en: It chanced one day that the lady, whose name was Madam Isabella, being gone, as is our custom in summertime, to abide at a very goodly estate she had in the country and her husband having ridden somewhither to pass some days abroad, she sent for Leonetto to come and be with her, whereat he was mightily rejoiced and betook himself thither incontinent.
uz: Bir kuni Madam Izabella ismli xonim yozda odatdagidek, o'zining qishloqda bo'lgan juda yaxshi mulkida qolgani va eri chet elda bir necha kun o'tkazish uchun u yerga borgani uchun ketib, Leonettoni u bilan birga bo'lishga chaqirib yubordi, u yerda juda xursand bo'ldi va u yerga bemalol bordi.

en: Meanwhile Messer Lambertuccio, hearing that her husband was gone abroad, took horse and repairing, all alone, to her house, knocked at the door.
uz: Ayni paytda, Messer Lambertuccio erining chet elga ketganini eshitib, ot olib, butunlay yolg'iz o'zi uning uyiga qaytdi va eshikni taqillatdi.

en: The lady’s waiting-woman, seeing him, came straight to her mistress, who was closeted with Leonetto, and called to her, saying, ‘Madam, Messer Lamber- tuccio is below, all alone.’ The lady, hearing this, was the woefullest woman in the world, but, as she stood in great fear of Messer Lambertuccio, she be- sought Leonetto not to take it ill to hide himself awhile behind the curtains of her bed till such time as the other should be gone.
uz: Xonimning kutib turgan xotini uni ko'rib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Leonetto bilan birga bo'lgan bekasi oldiga keldi va unga qo'ng'iroq qilib dedi: "Xonim, janob Lamber- tuccio pastda, butunlay yolg'iz." Buni eshitgan xonim dunyodagi eng ko'krakdor ayol edi, lekin u janob Lambertucciodan juda qo'rqib turganligi sababli, undan Leonettoga bir oz vaqt uning to'shagining pardalari orqasida yashirinishni istamasligini so'radi, toki boshqasini yo'q qilmaguncha.

en: Accordingly, Leonetto, who feared him no less than did the lady, hid himself there and she bade the maid go open to Messer Lambertuccio, which being done, he lighted down in the courtyard and making his palfrey fast to a staple there, went up into the house.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Leonetto, undan xonimdan kam qo'rqmagan holda, u yerda yashirindi va u xizmatchi qizga Messer Lambertuccioga ochilishni buyurdi. Shundan so'ng, u hovlida yoritib, o'zining palfreyini u yerdagi ustunga aylantirib, uyga chiqdi.

en: The lady put on a cheerful countenance and coming to the head of the stair, received him with as good a grace as she might and asked him what brought him thither; whereupon he caught her in his arms and clipped her and kissed her, saying, ‘My soul, I understood that your husband was abroad and am come accordingly to be with you awhile.’ After these words, they entered a bedchamber, where they locked themselves in, and Messer Lambertuccio fell to taking delight of her.
uz: Xonim quvnoq ko'rinish ko'rsatdi va zinapoyaning boshiga kelib, uni imkon qadar yaxshilik bilan qabul qildi va undan u yerga nima olib kelganini so'radi; shundan so'ng u uni quchoqlariga oldi, qirqdi va o'pdi, dedi: "Jonim, men sizning eringiz chet elda ekanligini tushundim va shunga ko'ra siz bilan bir oz vaqt qolishga keldim." Shundan so'ng, ular bir yotoqxonaga kirishdi, u yerda o'zlarini qulflashdi, va Messer Lambertuccio undan zavq olish uchun yiqildi.

en: As they were thus engaged, it befell, altogether out of the lady’s expecta- tion, that her husband returned, whom when the maid saw near the house, she ran in haste to the lady’s chamber and said, ‘Madam, here is my lord come back; methinketh he is already below in the courtyard.’ When the lady heard this, bethinking her that she had two men in the house and knowing that there was no hiding Messer Lambertuccio, by reason of his palfrey which was in the courtyard, she gave herself up for lost.
uz: Ular shunday unashtirilganlarida, xonimning kutilmaganda, eri qaytib keldi. Xizmatchi uni uy yaqinida ko'rgach, xonimning xonasiga shoshilib bordi va dedi: "Xonim, mana xo'jayinim qaytib keldi; u allaqachon hovlida deb o'ylayapti." Xonim buni eshitgach, u uyda ikki kishi borligini va Messer Lambertuccio yashirin bo'lmaganini bilgan holda, hovlida bo'lgan sariyog'i tufayli o'zini yo'qotdi.

en: Nevertheless, tak- ing a sudden resolution, she sprang hastily down from the bed and said to Messer Lambertuccio, ‘Sir, an you wish me anywise well and would save me from death, do that which I shall bid you.
uz: Shunga qaramay, to'satdan qaror qabul qilib, u shoshilinch ravishda karovatdan pastga sakrab tushdi va Messer Lambertuccioga dedi: "Janob, agar siz menga yaxshilik tilasangiz va meni o'limdan qutqarmoqchi bo'lsangiz, men sizga buyuradigan ishni qiling."

en: Take your hanger naked in your hand and go down the stair with an angry air and all disordered and begone, saying, “I vow to God that I will take him elsewhere.” And should
uz: Qo'lingizda yalang'och ilgakni oling va g'azablangan holda zinadan pastga tushing va butunlay tartibsiz bo'lib, "Men Xudoga qasam ichaman, uni boshqa joyga olib boraman" deb boshladim.

en: my husband offer to detain you or question you of aught, do you say no oth- erwhat than that which I have told you, but take horse and look you abide not with him on any account.’ The gentleman answered that he would well, and accordingly, drawing his hanger, he did as she had enjoined him, with a face all aﬁre what with the swink he had furnished and with anger at the husband’s return.
uz: Erim sizni ushlab turishni yoki biror narsa haqida so'roq qilishni taklif qilyapti, siz men aytganimdan boshqa hech narsa demayapsizmi, lekin ot olib, u bilan hech qanday sababga ko'ra qolmang." Janob javob berdi: "Xo'p bo'lardi, va shunga ko'ra, osmani tortib, u unga buyurganidek qildi, yuzi o'ziga kelgan g'azab bilan va erining qaytib kelishiga g'azab bilan."

en: The latter was by this dismounted in the courtyard and marvelled to see the palfrey there; then, offering to go up into the house, he saw Messer Lambertuccio come down and wondering both at his words and his air, said, ‘What is this, sir?’ Messer Lambertuccio putting his foot in the stirrup and mounting to horse, said nought but, ‘Cock’s body, I shall ﬁnd him again otherwhere,’ and made off.
uz: Oxirgisi shu sababli hovlida tushib ketdi va u yerdagi o'tloqni ko'rib hayratda qoldi; keyin u uyga chiqmoqchi bo'lganida, Messer Lambertuccio pastga tushib, uning so'zlariga ham, havosiga ham hayron bo'lib, dedi: "Bu nima, janob?" Messer Lambertuccio oyoqlarini qo'zg'alishga qo'yib, otga minib, hech narsa demadi, lekin: "Tovuqning jasadini, men uni yana boshqa joydan topaman", - dedi va yo'lga chiqdi.

en: The gentleman, going up, found his wife at the stairhead, all disordered and fearful, and said to her, ‘What is all this?
