uz: Shunday qilib, agar u mening ishonchim uchun uchta so'raydigan narsani qilsa, u keyin menga hech narsa buyurmaydi, lekin men buni qilaman - to'g'ri.

en: And the three things I desire are these: ﬁrst, that in Nicostratus his presence she slay his good hawk; secondly, that she send me a lock of her husband’s beard and lastly, one of his best teeth.’ These conditions seemed hard unto Lusca and to the lady harder yet; however, Love, who is an excel- lent comforter356 and a past master in shifts and devices, made her resolve to do his pleasure and accordingly she sent him word by her chamberwo- man that she would punctually do what he required and that quickly, and that over and above this, for that he deemed Nicostratus so well-advised, she would solace herself with him in her husband’s presence and make the latter believe that it was not true.
uz: Va men xohlagan uch narsa quyidagilar: birinchidan, Nikostratning huzurida u uning yaxshi bolg'asini o'ldirsin; ikkinchidan, u menga erining soqolini va nihoyat, eng yaxshi tishlaridan birini yuborsin. Bu shartlar Luska va xonim uchun qiyinroq tuyuldi; ammo, sevgi, ajoyib tasalli beruvchi va o'tmishdagi usta, uning xohish-istaklarini bajarishga qaror qildi va shunga ko'ra, u unga uning talabini tezda bajaradi, va bundan tashqari, u Nikostratni juda yaxshi maslahat bergan deb hisoblaganligi uchun, u o'zini erining huzurida tasalli berardi va oxirgi odamni bu haqiqat emas deb ishontirdi.

en: Pyrrhus, accordingly, began to await what the lady should do, and Nicostratus having, a few days after, made, as he oftentimes used to do, a great dinner to certain gentlemen, Madam Lydia, whenas the tables were cleared away, came forth of her chamber, clad in green samite and richly bedecked, and entered the saloon where the guests were.
uz: Pirrus, shunga ko'ra, xonim nima qilishi kerakligini kutishni boshladi va bir necha kundan so'ng Nikostratus, odatda odatdagidek, ba'zi janoblarga katta kechki ovqat tayyorlab berdi. Madam Lydia, stollar tozalanib bo'lgandan so'ng, o'z xonasidan yashil samit libosida va boy kiyimda chiqib, mehmonlar turgan zalga kirdi.

en: There, in the sight of Pyrrhus and of all the rest, she went up to the perch, whereon was the hawk that Nicostratus held so dear, and cast it loose, as she would set it on
uz: U yerda, Pirr va qolganlarning ko'z o'ngida, u Nikostratus juda qadrlaydigan akani ushlab turgan joyga ko'tarildi va uni o'zi qo'yadiganidek bo'shatdi.

en: her hand; then, taking it by the jesses, she dashed it against the wall and killed it; whereupon Nicostratus cried out at her, saying, ‘Alack, wife, what hast thou done?’ She answered him nothing, but, turning to the gentlemen who had eaten with him, she said to them, ‘Gentlemen, I should ill know how to avenge myself on a king who did me a despite, an I dared not take my wreak of a hawk.
uz: Uning qo'li; so'ngra uni dumbalardan ushladi va devorga urib o'ldirdi; shundan so'ng Nikostratus unga qichqirib dedi: "Alak, xotinim, nima qilding?" U unga hech narsa javob bermadi, lekin u bilan birga ovqatlangan janoblarga murojaat qilib, ularga dedi: "Janoblar, men menga qarshilik ko'rsatgan shohdan o'zimni qanday qasos olishni bilmas edim, lekin men bir xo'rozni qabul qilishga jur'at eta olmadim."

en: You must know that this bird hath long robbed me of all the time which should of men be accorded to the pleasuring of the ladies; for that no sooner is the day risen than Nicostratus is up and drest and away he goeth a-horseback, with his hawk on his ﬁst, to the open plains, to see him ﬂy, whilst I, such as you see me, abide in bed alone and ill-content; wherefore I have many a time had a mind to do that which I have now done, nor hath aught hindered me therefrom but that I waited to do it in the presence of gentlemen who would be just judges in my quarrel, as methinketh you will be.’ The gentlemen, hearing this and believing her affection for Nicostratus to be no otherwise than as her words denoted, turned all to the latter, who was angered, and said, laughing, ‘Ecod, how well hath the lady done to avenge herself of her wrong by the death of the hawk!’ Then, with divers of pleasantries
uz: Siz bilishingiz kerakki, bu qush meni allaqachon xonimlarning rohatlanishi uchun ajratilishi kerak bo'lgan barcha vaqtdan o'g'irladi; chunki Nicostratus tirilguncha, u o'zining mushtini tutgan holda, ochiq tekisliklarga otda uchib boradi, men esa, siz ko'rib turganingizdek, to'shakda yolg'iz va norozi holda yashayman; shuning uchun men hozir qilgan ishimni qilish uchun ko'p vaqt o'ylab yurganman, menga hech narsa to'sqinlik qilmadi, lekin men buni mening janoblarim huzurida qilish uchun kutdim, ular mening janjaramda adolatli hakam bo'lishadi, deb o'ylashingiz mumkin.

en: upon the subject (the lady being now gone back to her chamber), they turned Nicostratus his annoy into laughter; whilst Pyrrhus, seeing all this, said in himself, ‘The lady hath giv- en a noble beginning to my happy loves; God grant she persevere!’ Lydia having thus slain the hawk, not many days were passed when, be- ing in her chamber with Nicostratus, she fell to toying and frolicking with him, and he, pulling her somedele by the hair, by way of sport, gave her oc- casion to accomplish the second thing required of her by Pyrrhus.
uz: Bu mavzuda (xonim endi o'z xonasiga qaytib borayotgan edi), ular Nikostratni g'azabini kulgiga aylantirishdi; Pirr esa, bularning barchasini ko'rib, o'zida dedi: "Xonim mening baxtli muhabbatlarimga olijanob boshlandi; Xudo unga bardosh bersin!" Shunday qilib, Lidiya akani o'ldirganidan ko'p o'tmay, Nikostrat bilan xonasida bo'lib, u bilan o'ynashga va xursandchilikka tushdi, va u, sport usulida uning sochidan tortib, unga Pirr tomonidan talab qilingan ikkinchi ishni bajarishga imkon berdi.

en: Accord- ingly, taking him of a sudden by a lock of his beard, she tugged so hard at it, laughing the while, that she plucked it clean out of his chin; whereof he complaining, ‘How now?’ quoth she.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uni birdaniga soqolining qulfidan ushladi, u shunday qattiq tortdi, kulgancha, uni tagiga chiqarib tashladi; undan shikoyat qilib: "Endi nima?" - deb so'radi u.

en: ‘What aileth thee to pull such a face?
uz: Sizga bunday yuzni tortishga nima yetadi?

en: Is it because I have plucked out maybe half a dozen hairs of thy beard?
uz: Balki soqolingdan yarim o'n sochni yechib olganim uchunmi?

en: Thou feltest not that which I suffered, whenas thou pulledst me now by the hair.’ On this wise continuing their disport from one word to another, she privily kept the lock of hair that she had plucked from his beard and sent it that same day to her lover.
uz: Sen meni hozir sochimdan tortib olganingda, men azob chekkanimni his qilmading. Shu tariqa, ularning bir so'zdan ikkinchisiga tortishishlarini davom ettirib, u soqolidan yirtib olgan soch qulfini yashirincha saqlab qoldi va o'sha kuni sevgilisiga yubordi.

en: Anent the last of the three things required by Pyrrhus she was harder put to it for a device; nevertheless, being of a surpassing wit and Love making her yet quicker of invention, she soon bethought herself what means she should use to give it accomplishment.
uz: Pirrga kerak bo'lgan uchta narsadan oxirgisi unga qurilma uchun qiyinroq edi; shunga qaramay, aql bovar qilmas darajada aql-idrok va muhabbat uni ixtiroga yanada tezlashtirgani sababli, u tez orada unga muvaffaqiyat berish uchun qanday vositalardan foydalanish kerakligini o'ylab topdi.

en: Nicostratus had two boys given him
uz: Nikostratga ikki o'g'il berdi.

en: of their father, to the intent that, being of gentle birth, they might learn somewhat of manners and good breeding in his house, of whom, whenas he was at meat, one carved before him and the other gave him to drink.
uz: otasidan, muloyim kelib chiqishi sababli, uning uyida odob-axloq va yaxshi tarbiya o'rganishlari uchun, u yerda go'sht yeyayotganida, ulardan biri uning oldida o'yib, ikkinchisi esa unga ichimlik berardi.

en: Lydia called them both and giving them to believe that they stank at the mouth, enjoined them that, whenas they served Nicostratus, they should still hold their heads backward as most they might nor ever tell this to any.
uz: Lidiya ularni ikkalasi ham chaqirib, og'izdan badbo'y hid kelishiga ishontirib, Nikostratga xizmat qilayotganlarida, hech kimga bu haqda hech qachon aytmasalar ham, boshlarini orqaga tortishlari kerakligini buyurdi.

en: The boys, believing that which she said, proceeded to do as she had lessoned them, and she after a while said to her husband one day, ‘Hast thou noted that which yonder boys do, whenas they serve thee?’ ‘Ay have I,’ replied Nicostratus; ‘and indeed I had it in mind to ask them why they did it.’ Quoth the lady, ‘Do it not, for I can tell thee the reason; and I have kept it silent from thee this long while, not to cause thee annoy; but, now I perceive that others begin to be aware thereof, it skilleth not to hide it from thee longer.
uz: Bolalar uning aytganlariga ishonib, unga o'rgatganidek qilishdi. Va u bir kun eriga dedi: "Eshikdagi bolalarning senga xizmat qilayotganini sezyapsanmi?" "Ha, men shunday qildim," dedi Nikostratus; "va haqiqatan ham ulardan nega bunday qilganlarini so'rashni o'yladim." Xonim aytdi: "Yo'q qilma, chunki men senga sababini aytishim mumkin; va men buni sendan uzoq vaqt davomida yashirdim, seni xafa qilmaslik uchun; lekin, endi men boshqalarning bundan xabardor bo'la boshlaganini anglayman, endi uni sendan yashirmaslikka harakat qilaman."

en: This betideth thee for none other what than that thou stinkest terribly at the mouth, and I know not what can be the cause thereof; for that it used not to be thus.
uz: Bu senga faqat og'zingda dahshatli hid taratganingdan boshqa hech narsa bilan bog'liq emas, va buning sababi nima bo'lishi mumkinligini bilmayman; chunki avval bunday bo'lmagan edi.

en: Now this is a very unseemly thing for thee who hast to do with gen- tlemen, and needs must we see for a means of curing it.’ Whereupon said he, ‘What can this be?
uz: Endi bu siz uchun juda noqulay narsa, siz gen-tlemenlar bilan shug'ullanasiz va uni davolash vositasi ko'rishimiz kerak." Shunda u dedi: "Bu nima bo'lishi mumkin?"

en: Can I have some rotten tooth in my head?’ ‘Maybe ay,’ answered Lydia and carried him to a window, where she made him open his mouth, and after she had viewed it in every part, ‘O Nicostratus,’ cried she, ‘how canst thou have put up with it so long?
uz: "Mening boshimda chirigan tish bo'lishi mumkinmi?"  Ehtimol, shundaydir,  javob berdi Lidiya va uni derazadan olib chiqdi, u yerda og'zini ochdi va uni har bir qismida ko'rib chiqqandan so'ng, Ey Nikostratus, deb baqirdi u,  bunchalik uzoq vaqtga qanday bardosh bera olding?

en: Thou hast a tooth on this side which meseemth is not only decayed, but altogether rotten, and as- suredly, and thou keep it much longer in thy mouth, it will mar thee those which be on either side; wherefore I counsel thee have it drawn, ere the thing go farther.’ ‘Since it seemeth good to thee,’ answered he, ‘I will well; let a surgeon be sent for without more delay, who shall draw it for me.’ ‘God forbid,’ rejoined the lady, ‘that a surgeon come hither for that!
uz: Sizning bu tomonda tishingiz bor, u nafaqat chirigan, balki butunlay chirigan va albatta, og'zingda uzoqroq saqlaysan, u ikki tomondagilarni ham o'ldiradi; shuning uchun men senga maslahat beraman, narsa undan uzoqroqqa ketmasidan oldin uni tortib ol." Senga ma'qul bo'lgani uchun,  deb javob berdi u, Men yaxshi bo'laman; menga tezroq jarroh yuborilsin, u uni tortib beradi. Xudo saqlasin,  dedi xonim,  bu yerda jarroh kelmasin!

en: Me- thinketh it lieth on such wise that I myself, without any surgeon, can very well draw it for thee; more by token that these same surgeons are so barbar- ous in doing such ofﬁces that my heart would on no account suffer me to see or know thee in the hands of any one of them; for, an it irk thee over- much, I will at least loose thee incontinent, which a surgeon would not do.’ Accordingly, she let fetch the proper instruments and sent everyone forth of the chamber, except only Lusca; after which, locking herself in, she made Nicostratus lie down on a table and thrusting the pincers into his mouth, what while the maid held him fast, she pulled out one of his teeth by main force, albeit he roared out lustily for the pain.
uz: Menimcha, bu shunday donolikka asoslanganki, men ham hech qanday jarrohsiz uni senga juda yaxshi chizishim mumkin; ayniqsa, bu jarrohlar shunday vahshiylarki, yuragim hech qanday sababga ko'ra seni ularning qo'lida ko'rishga yoki bilishga yo'l qo'ymaydi; chunki, seni juda bezovta qilsam, hech bo'lmaganda seni tashlab yuboraman, bu jarroh qilmagan bo'lardi.

en: Then, keeping to herself that
uz: Keyin, o'zida saqlab qolgan holda,

en: which she had drawn, she brought out a frightfully decayed tooth she had ready in her hand and showed it to her husband, half dead as he was for pain, saying, ‘See what thou hast had in thy mouth all this while.’ Nicostratus believed what she said and now that the tooth was out, for all he had suffered the most grievous pain and made sore complaint thereof, him seemed he was cured; and presently, having comforted himself with one thing and another and the pain being abated, he went forth of the chamber; whereupon his wife took the tooth and straightway despatched it to her gal- lant, who, being now certiﬁed of her love, professed himself ready to do her every pleasure.
uz: Uni tortib olgan, qo'lida tayyorlagan dahshatli chirigan tishini chiqarib oldi va uni eriga, yarim o'lik holda og'riqdan ko'rsatdi va dedi: "Ko'r, shu vaqt davomida og'zingda nima bor edi." Nikostratus uning aytganlariga ishondi va tish chiqqanidan so'ng, chunki u eng og'riqli og'riqni boshidan kechirgan edi va undan qattiq shikoyat qilgan edi, u tuzalib qolgandek edi; va darhol bir narsa va boshqa narsa bilan o'zini ovutgandan so'ng, u xonadan chiqdi; shundan so'ng xotini tishni oldi va uni darhol unga jo'natib yubordi.

en: The lady, albeit every hour seemed to her a thousand till she should be with him, desiring to give him farther assurance and wishful to perform that which she had promised him, made a show one day of being ailing and be- ing visited after dinner by Nicostratus, with no one in his company but Pyrrhus, she prayed them, by way of allaying her unease, to help her go into the garden.
uz: Xonim, garchi har soatda unga mingta ko'rinsa ham, u bilan birga bo'lguncha, unga yanada ishonch berishni va unga va'da bergan narsani bajarishni xohlagan holda, bir kuni kasal ekanligi va kechki ovqatdan keyin Nikostratus tomonidan ziyorat qilinishini ko'rsatdi, uning safida Pirrusdan boshqa hech kim bo'lmasa ham, u o'z tashvishlarini yengillashtirish, unga bog'ga kirishga yordam berish uchun ularga iltijo qildi.

en: Accordingly, Nicostratus taking her on one side and Pyrrhus on the other, they carried her into the garden and set her down on a grassplot, at the foot of a ﬁne pear-tree; where, after they had sat awhile, the lady, who had already given her gallant to know what he had to do, said, ‘Pyrrhus, I have a great desire to eat of yonder pears; do thou climb up and throw us down some of them.’ Pyrrhus straightway climbed up into the tree and fell to throwing down of the pears, which as he did, he began to say, ‘How now, my lord!
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Nikostratus uni bir tomondan, Pirr esa boshqa tomondan olib, bog'ga olib kirishdi va uni nozik nok daraxti etagiga yotqizishdi; u yerda biroz o'tirgach, unga nima qilish kerakligini bilish uchun hadya bergan xonim dedi: "Pirrhus, men u yerdagi noklardan yeyishga juda xohlayman; sen ko'tarilib, ulardan bir nechtasini pastga tashla." Pirrush darhol daraxtga chiqib, noklarni tashlashga tushdi, u shunday qildi va dedi: "Xo'sh, xo'jayinim!"

en: What is this you do?
uz: Bu nima ishing?

en: And you, madam, are you not ashamed to suffer it in my presence?
uz: Siz-chi, xonim, mening huzurimda azob chekishdan uyalmaysizmi?

en: Think you I am blind?
uz: Siz meni ko'r deb o'ylaysizmi?

en: But now you were sore dis- ordered; how cometh it you have so quickly recovered that you do such things?
uz: Lekin endi siz qattiq bezovta edingiz; qanday qilib bunchalik tezda tuzalib, bunday ishlarni qilasiz?

en: An you have a mind unto this, you have store of goodly chambers; why go you not do it in one of these?
uz: Sizda bu haqda fikr bor, yaxshi xonalar omboringiz bor; nega buni shulardan birida qilmaysiz?

en: It were more seemly than in my pres- ence.’ The lady turned to her husband and said, ‘What saith Pyrrhus?
uz: Bu mening homiladorligimdan ko'ra ko'proq ko'rinardi. Xonim eriga o'girilib dedi: Pyrr nima deyapti?

en: Doth he rave?’ ‘No, madam,’ answered the young man, ‘I rave not.
uz: U g'azablanadimi? Yo'q, xonim,  javob berdi yigit, Men g'azablanmayman.

en: Think you I can- not see?’ As for Nicostratus, he marvelled sore and said, ‘Verily, Pyrrhus, methinketh thou dreamest.’ ‘My lord,’ replied Pyrrhus, ‘I dream not a jot, neither do you dream; nay, you bestir yourselves on such wise that were this tree to do likewise, there would not be a pear left on it.’ Quoth the lady, ‘What may this be?
uz: "Men ko'ra olmayman deb o'ylayapsanmi?" Nikostratga kelsak, u xafa bo'lib dedi: "Haqiqatan ham, Pirr, sen tush ko'ryapsan." "Ey xo'jayinim," javob berdi Pirr, "Men tush ko'rmayapman, na sen tush ko'rmayapsan; yo'q, agar bu daraxt ham shunday qilsaydi, unda nok qolmas edi." Xonim dedi: "Bu nima bo'lishi mumkin?"

en: Can it be that this he saith appeareth to him to be true?
uz: Nahotki uning aytganlari unga haqiqatdek tuyulsa?

en: So God save me, and I were whole as I was aforetime, I would climb up into the tree, to see what marvels are those which this fellow saith he seeth.’
uz: Shunday qilib, Xudo meni qutqarsin, va men avvalgidek sog'aydim, men daraxtga ko'tarilib, bu odam ko'rayotgan ajoyibotlar qanday ekanligini ko'rmoqchiman.

en: Meanwhile Pyrrhus from the top of the pear-tree still said the same thing and kept up the pretence; whereupon Nicostratus bade him come down.
uz: Shu bilan birga, Pirr xali ham nok daraxti tepasidan xuddi shunday dedi va o'zini shunday ko'rsatdi; shundan so'ng Nikostratus unga pastga tushishni buyurdi.

en: Ac- cordingly he came down and his master said to him, ‘Now, what sayst thou thou sawest?’ ‘Methinketh,’ answered he, ‘you take me for a lackwit or a loggerhead.
uz: Shunday qilib, u pastga tushdi va xo'jayini unga dedi: Endi nima deysan ko'rdingmi? O'ylayapsan, dedi u, menni aqldan ozgan yoki daraxt kesuvchi deb o'ylayapsan.

en: Since I must needs say it, I saw you atop of your lady, and after, as I came down, I saw you arise and seat yourself where you presently are.’ ‘Assuredly,’ said Nicostratus, ‘thou dotest; for we have not stirred a jot, save as thou seest, since thou climbest up into the pear-tree.’ Whereupon quoth Pyrrhus, ‘What booteth it to make words of the matter?
uz: Shuni aytishim kerak bo'lgani uchun, seni xoniming ustida ko'rdim, keyin esa pastga tushgach, seni o'rningdan turib, hozir turgan joyingda o'tirganingni ko'rdim. Albatta, dedi Nikostratus, sen yetuksan; chunki biz hech qanday qo'zg'atmadik, faqat sen ko'rib turganingdek, sen nok daraxtiga chiqding. Shunda Pirr dedi: Bu masalada gapirishga nima majbur qiladi?

en: I certainly saw you; and if I did see you, it was atop of your own.’ Nicostratus waxed momently more and more astonished, insomuch that he said, ‘Needs must I see if this pear-tree is enchanted and if whoso is thereon seeth marvels.’ Thereupon he climbed up into the tree and no sooner was he come to the top than the lady and Pyrrhus fell to solacing them- selves together; which when Nicostratus saw, he began to cry out, saying, ‘Ah, vile woman that thou art, what is this thou dost?
uz: Men seni ko'rdim, albatta; agar ko'rsam, u o'z ustingda edi." Nikostratus bir zumda tobora hayratga tushdi, shunday dedi: "Men bu nok daraxti sehrlanganmi va u yerda kim bo'lsa, mo'jizalarni ko'rishini ko'rishim kerakmi." Shunda u daraxtga chiqdi va xonimdan ko'p o'tmay tepaga chiqdi va Pirrus ularni birga tasalli berishga tushdi; Nikostratus buni ko'rgach, u baqirib dedi: "Oh, yomon ayol, sen nima qilyapsan?"

en: And thou, Pyrrhus, in whom I most trusted?’ So saying, he proceeded to descend the tree, whilst the lovers said, ‘We are sitting here’; then, seeing him come down, they re- seated themselves whereas he had left them.
uz: "Sen-chi, Pirrus, men senga eng ko'p ishongan odam?" Shunday deb, u daraxtni tushirishga yurdi, oshiqlar esa: "Biz bu yerda o'tiramiz", deyishdi; keyin, uni tushayotganini ko'rib, u ularni tashlab ketgan joyda o'tirdilar.

en: As soon as he was down and saw his wife and Pyrrhus where he had left them, he fell a-railing at them; whereupon quoth Pyrrhus, ‘Now, verily, Nicostratus, I acknowledged that, as you said before, I must have seen falsely what while I was in the pear- tree, nor do I know it otherwise than by this, that I see and know yourself to have seen falsely in the like case.
uz: U pastga tushib, xotini va Pirrusni ularni tashlab ketgan joyida ko'rishi bilanoq, u ularga qarshi g'azablanib yiqildi; shundan so'ng Pirrus dedi: "Endi, haqiqatan ham, Nikostratus, men tan oldimki, siz avval aytganingizdek, men nok daraxtida bo'lganimda nimani yolg'on ko'rgan bo'lsam kerak, buni bundan boshqa bilmayman, men o'zingizni xuddi shunday holatda yolg'on ko'rganingizni ko'ryapman va bilaman."

en: And that I speak the truth nought else should be needful to certify you but that you have regard to the circum- stances of the case and consider if it be possible that your lady, who is the most virtuous of women and discreeter than any other of her sex, could, an she had a mind to outrage you on such wise, bring herself to do it before your very eyes.
uz: Haqiqatni gapirayotganimni tasdiqlash uchun boshqa hech narsa kerak emas, lekin siz ish holatlariga e'tibor bering va ayollarning eng fazilatli va o'z jinsidagi har qanday insondan ko'ra kamtarroq bo'lgan xonimingiz sizni bunday tarzda xafa qilish niyatida bo'lsa, buni ko'z o'ngingizda qilishga majbur bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rib chiqing.

en: I speak not of myself, who would rather suffer myself to be torn limb-meal than so much as think of such a thing, much more come to do it in your presence.
uz: Men o'zim haqimda gapirmayapman, men bunday narsani o'ylagandan ko'ra, o'zimni oyoq-qo'l bilan yirtishga majbur qilishni afzal ko'rardim, balki bu ishni sizning huzuringizda qilishga kelardim.

en: Wherefore the fault of this misseeing must needs proceed from the pear-tree, for that all the world had not made me believe but that you were in act to have carnal knowledge of your lady here, had I not heard you say that it appeared to yourself that I did what I know most certainly I never thought, much less did.’ Thereupon the lady, feigning to be mightily incensed, rose to her feet and said, ‘Ill luck betide thee, dost thou hold me so little of wit that, an I had a
uz: Shuning uchun bu noto'g'ri qarashning aybi nok daraxtidan kelib chiqishi kerak edi, chunki butun dunyo meni ishonishga majbur qilmagan edi, balki sen bu yerda xonim haqida ma'naviy bilimga ega bo'lganingni, agar men seni o'zingga shunday tuyulganini aytganingni eshitmaganimda edi, men hech qachon o'ylamagan narsani qilgan bo'lardim.

en: mind to such ﬁlthy fashions as thou wouldst have us believe thou sawest, I should come to do them before thy very eyes?
uz: Shunday iflos modalarga e'tibor bering, biz ularni ko'z o'ngingizda qilish uchun kelishimni xohlaganingizdek, ko'rdingizmi?

en: Thou mayst be assured of this that, if ever the fancy took me thereof, I should not come hither; marry, methinketh I should have sense enough to contrive it in one of our cham- bers, on such wise and after such a fashion that it would seem to me an ex- traordinary thing if ever thou camest to know of it.’ Nicostratus, himseem- ing that what the lady and Pyrrhus said was true, to wit, that they would never have ventured upon such an act there before himself, gave over words and reproaches and fell to discoursing of the strangeness of the fact and the miracle of the sight, which was thus changed unto whoso climbed up into the pear-tree.
uz: Siz shunga amin bo'lishingiz mumkinki, agar hech qachon xayol meni bu yerga olib kelmasa, men bu yerga kelmas edim; turmush qurish uchun, menimcha, men buni bizning bir tanamizda shunday usulda va shunday uslubda o'ylab topishga yetarlicha aqlga ega bo'lardimki, agar siz bu haqda bilsangiz, menga g'ayrioddiy narsa tuyulsa." Nikostratus, u xonim va Pirrning aytganlari rost edi, ya'ni ular hech qachon o'zidan oldin bunday ishga jur'at etmagan, so'z va malomatlar bermagan va faktning g'alatiligi va manzaraning mo'jizligini, bu esa kimga ko'rinishga o'zgartirilgan edi.

en: But his wife, feigning herself chagrined for the ill thought he had shown of her, said, ‘Verily, this pear-tree shall never again, if I can help it, do me nor any other lady the like of this shame; wherefore do thou run, Pyrrhus, and fetch a hatchet and at one stroke avenge both thyself and me by cutting it down; albeit it were better yet lay it about Nicostratus his cosard, who, without any consideration, suffered the eyes of his understand- ing to be so quickly blinded, whenas, however certain that which thou357 saidst might seem to those358 which thou hast in thy head, thou shouldst for nought in the world in the judgment of thy mind have believed or allowed that such a thing could be.’ Pyrrhus very readily fetched the hatchet and cut down the tree, which when the lady saw fallen, she said to Nicostratus, ‘Since I see the enemy of mine honour overthrown, my anger is past,’ and
uz: Ammo uning xotini, unga nisbatan ko'rsatgan yomon fikridan xafa bo'lib, dedi: "Haqiqatan ham, bu nok daraxti hech qachon, agar men yordam bera olsam, menga ham, boshqa hech bir xonimga ham bu sharmandalik kabi qilmaydi; shuning uchun yugurasan, Pirros, o'zingni ham, meni ham bir zarba bilan qasos ol va uni kesib tashla; garchi undan ham yaxshiroq bo'lsa-da, Nikostratusning bo'yniga qo'y, u hech qanday e'tibor bermasdan, uning tushunish ko'zlarini bunchalik tezda ko'r qilishiga yo'l qo'ydi, garchi, sen aytgan narsa senga ko'rinishi mumkin edi, sen o'z boshingdagi 358 ta narsaga ishonib, dunyoda hech narsa ko'rmasliging kerak edi, yoki bunday narsa sodir bo'lishi mumkin edi."

en: graciously forgave her hus- band, who besought her thereof, charging him that it should never again happen to him to presume such a thing of her, who loved him better than herself.
uz: U undan iltimos qilgan xotiniga rahm-shafqat bilan kechirdi va uni o'zidan ko'ra yaxshiroq sevuvchi ayoldan bunday narsa boshqa hech qachon sodir bo'lmasligini ta'kidladi.

en: Accordingly, the wretched husband, thus befooled, returned with her and her lover to the palace, where many a time thereafterward Pyrrhus took delight and pleasance more at ease of Lydia and she of him.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, bechora er, shu tariqa xor bo'lib, u va uning sevgilisi bilan saroyga qaytdi, u yerda keyinroq Pirrus Lidiya va undan ko'proq zavq va rohat olardi.

en: God grant us as much!”
uz: Xudo bizga shunchalik ko'p bersin!

en: THE TENTH STORY Two Siennese love a lady, who is gossip to one of them; the latter dieth and returning to his companion, according to promise made him, relateth to him how folk fare in the other world.
uz: O'NCHINCHI HIKOYA Ikki Siyenlik bir xonimni yaxshi ko'radilar, u ulardan biriga g'iybat qiladi; oxirgi xonim o'ladi va o'z hamrohiga qaytadi, unga bergan va'dasiga ko'ra, unga boshqa dunyoda odamlar qanday yashashi haqida xabar beradi.

en: It now rested only with the king to tell and he accordingly, as soon as he saw the ladies quieted, who lamented the cutting down of the unoffending pear-tree, began, “It is a very manifest thing that every just king should be the ﬁrst to observe the laws made by him, and an he do otherwise, he must be adjudged a slave deserving of punishment and not a king, into which of- fence and under which reproach I, who am your king, am in a manner con- strained to fall.
uz: Endi faqatgina shohga aytish kerak edi va u, xonimlarning tinch qolganini ko'rishi bilanoq, betakror nok daraxti kesilganidan qayg'urgan holda, shunday dedi: "Har bir adolatli shoh o'zi tomonidan yaratilgan qonunlarga birinchi bo'lib rioya qilishi kerakligi juda aniq, va agar u boshqacha qilmasa, u jazolanishga loyiq qul deb baholanishi kerak, shoh emas, unga o'tirgan va men, sizning shohingiz, qandaydir tarzda yiqilish uchun zo'r bo'lgan."

en: True it is that yesterday I laid down the law for today’s dis- courses, purposing not this day to make use of my privilege, but, submitting myself to the same obligation as you, to discourse of that whereof you have all discoursed.
uz: To'g'ri, kecha men bugungi bahslar uchun qonunni belgiladim, bugungi kunda o'z imtiyozimdan foydalanish maqsadida emas, balki o'zimni ham siz bilan bir xil majburiyatga bo'ysundirib, hammangiz bahslashgan narsani muhokama qilish uchun.

en: However, not only hath that story been told which I had thought to tell, but so many other and far ﬁner things have been said upon the matter that, for my part, ransack my memory as I will, I can call nothing to mind and must avouch myself unable to say aught anent such a subject that may compare with those stories which have already been told.
uz: Lekin nafaqat men aytmoqchi bo'lgan hikoya aytib berildi, balki bu borada shunchalik ko'p va ancha nozik narsalar aytildiki, men o'z xotiramni xohlaganimcha buzaman, hech narsani eslay olmayman va o'zimni allaqachon aytib o'tilgan hikoyalar bilan solishtiradigan hech qanday mavzuni ayta olmaslikka majbur qilaman.

en: Where- fore, it behoving me transgress against the law made by myself, I declare myself in advance ready, as one deserving of punishment, to submit to any forfeit which may be imposed on me, and so have recourse to my wonted privilege.
uz: Qayerda bo'lsa ham, o'zim tomonidan yaratilgan qonunni buzishga majbur bo'lsam, o'zimni oldindan jazoga loyiq deb e'lon qilaman, menga yuklanishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday tovonga bo'ysunishga va shu bilan birga o'zimning odatdagi imtiyozimga murojaat qilishga tayyorman.

en: Accordingly, dearest ladies, I say that Elisa’s story of Fra Rinaldo and his gossip and eke the simplicity of the Siennese have such efﬁcacy that they induce me, letting be the cheats put upon foolish husbands by their wily wives, to tell you a slight story of them,359 which though it have in it no little of that which must not be believed, will natheless in part, at least, be pleasing to hear.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, aziz xonimlar, men Elisaning Fra Rinaldo haqidagi hikoyasi va uning g'iybatlari va siyenliklarning soddaligi shunchalik samara beradiki, ular meni ahmoqona xotinlari tomonidan ahmoq erlarga qo'yiladigan firibgarlarga ularni ozgina hikoya qilishga undaydilar, 359 garchi unda ishonish kerak bo'lmagan hech qanday narsa bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda, eshitishga yoqadi.

en: There were, then, in Siena two young men of the people, whereof one was called Tingoccio Mini and the other Meuccio di Tura; they abode at Porta Salaja and consorted well nigh never save one with the other.
uz: O'shanda Siena shahrida ikki yosh yigit bor edi, ulardan biri Tingoccio Mini deb atalardi, ikkinchisi Meuccio di Tura; ular Porta Salajada yashar va bir-birlari bilan deyarli hech qachon aloqada bo'lmas edilar.

en: To all appearance they loved each exceedingly and resorting, as men do, to churches and preachings, they had many a time heard tell of the happiness and of the misery that are, according to their deserts, allotted in the next world to the souls of those who die; of which things desiring to have certain news and ﬁnding no way thereto, they promised one another that whichever of them died ﬁrst should, an he might, return to him who abode on life and give him tidings of that which he would fain know; and this they conﬁrmed with an oath.
uz: Ular bir-birlarini juda ham yaxshi ko'rishardi va odamlar kabi cherkovlar va va'zlarga murojaat qilishardi. Ular ko'p marta o'z sahrolariga ko'ra, o'ladiganlarning jonlariga keladigan baxt va musibat haqida xabar berishgan edi. Ular bu haqda aniq xabar olishni va bunga yo'l topishni istashgan holda, bir-birlariga va'da berishardi: ulardan qaysi biri birinchi bo'lib o'lsa, u hayotda qolgan odamga qaytib kelishi va unga bilmaydigan narsalar haqida xabar berishi kerak; va buni qasam bilan tasdiqladilar.

en: Having come to this accord and companying still together, as hath been said, it chanced that Tingoccio became godfather to a child which one Ambruogio Anselmini, abiding at Campo Reggi, had had of his wife, Mistress Mita by name, and from time to time visiting, together with Meuc- cio, his gossip who was a very fair and lovesome lady, he became, notwith- standing the gossipship, enamoured of her.
uz: Bu kelishuvga kelib, aytilganidek, hali ham birga bo'lganimizdan so'ng, tingoccio Campo Reggi shahrida yashovchi Ambruogio Anselmining xotini, Mistress Mita ismli rafiqasi bo'lgan va vaqti-vaqti bilan Meuc-tio bilan birga mehmon bo'lgan, uning g'iybatlari juda go'zal va yoqimli ayol edi, u g'iybatchilikni to'xtatmasdan, unga oshiq bo'lib qoldi.

en: Meuccio, on like wise, hearing her mightily commended of his friend and being himself much pleased with her, fell in love with her, and each hid his love from the other, but not for one same reason.
uz: Meuccio, do'sti uni juda maqtashini eshitib, o'zi ham undan juda mamnun bo'lgani uchun, unga oshiq bo'lib qoldi va har biri o'z muhabbatini bir-biridan yashirdi, lekin bir xil sababga ko'ra emas.

en: Tingoccio was careful not to discover it to Meuccio, on account of the naughty deed which himseemed he did to love his gossip and which he had been ashamed that any should know.
uz: Tingoccio buni Meuccioga oshkor qilmaslikka ehtiyot bo'ldi, chunki u o'zining g'iybatini yaxshi ko'rgan va har kim bilishi kerak bo'lgan uyatchidan uyalgan yomon ish qilgan edi.

en: Meuccio, on the other hand, kept himself therefrom,360 for that he had already perceived that the lady pleased Tingoccio; whereupon he said in himself, ‘If I discover this to him, he will wax jealous of me and being able, as her gossip, to bespeak her at his every pleasure, he will, inasmuch as he may, bring me in ill savour with her, and so I shall never have of her aught that may please me.’ Things being at this pass, it befell that Tingoccio, having more leisure of discovering his every desire to the lady, contrived with acts and words so to do that he had his will of her, of which Meuccio soon became aware and albeit it sore misliked him, yet, hoping some time or other to compass his desire, he feigned ignorance thereof, so Tingoccio might not have cause or occasion to do him an ill turn or hinder him in any of his affairs.
uz: Meuccio esa, o'zini bundan tiydi, 360 chunki u xonim Tingotsiyga yoqqanini allaqachon sezgan edi; shuning uchun u o'zida dedi: "Agar men buni unga aniqlasam, u menga hasad qiladi va uning g'iybatidek, uni har qanday xohishiga ko'ra so'zlay oladi, u, imkon qadar, meni u bilan yomon ta'minlaydi va shuning uchun meni hech qachon xursand qilmaydigan narsasiga ega bo'lmayman."

en: The two friends loving thus, the one more happily than the other, it befell that Tin- goccio, ﬁnding the soil of his gossip’s demesne soft and eath to till, so delved and laboured there that there overcame him thereof a malady, which after some days waxed so heavy upon him that, being unable to brook it, he departed this life.
uz: Ikki do'st shunday sevishardi, biri ikkinchisidan ko'ra baxtliroq edi, shunday bo'ldiki, Tin-goccio o'zining g'iybatining tuprog'ini topib, u yerda shunchalik chuqurlashib, mehnat qildilarki, u yerda unga kasallik yengdi, bir necha kundan so'ng unga shunchalik og'ir tushdiki, uni tashlab bo'lmay, bu hayotdan ketdi.

en: The third day after his death (for that belike he had not
uz: Uning o'limidan keyingi uchinchi kuni (chunki u bunday emas edi).

en: before been able) he came by night, according to the promise made, into Meuccio’s chamber and called the latter, who slept fast.
uz: Qodir bo'lishidan oldin) u kechasi, berilgan va'daga ko'ra, Meuccio xonasiga keldi va tez uxlaydigan oxirgisini chaqirib oldi.

en: Meuccio awoke and said, ‘Who art thou?’ Whereto he answered, ‘I am Tingoccio, who, accord- ing to the promise which I made thee, am come back to thee to give thee news of the other world.’ Meuccio was somewhat affrighted at seeing him; nevertheless, taking heart, ‘Thou art welcome, brother mine,’ quoth he, and presently asked him if he were lost.
uz: Meuccio uyg'onib, dedi: Sen kimsan? Shunda u javob berdi: Men Tingoccio bo'laman, senga bergan va'damga muvofiq, senga boshqa dunyo haqida xabar berish uchun qaytdim. Meuccio uni ko'rib biroz qo'rqib ketdi; shunga qaramay, yuragini olgach, Xush kelibsan, akam, dedi u va darhol undan adashganmi, deb so'radi.

en: ‘Things are lost that are not to be found,’ replied Tingoccio; ‘and how should I be here, if I were lost?’ ‘Alack,’ cried Meuccio, ‘I say not so; nay, I ask thee if thou art among the damned souls in the avenging ﬁre of hell.’ Whereto quoth Tingoccio, ‘As for that, no; but I am, notwithstand- ing, in very grievous and anguishful torment for the sins committed by me.’ Meuccio then particularly enquired of him what punishments were awarded in the other world for each of the sins that folk use to commit here below, and he told him them all.
uz: topilmaydigan narsalar yoqolgan,  javob berdi Tingotsio;  va agar yoqolgan bolsam, bu yerda qanday bolishim kerak?  Alack,  deb baqirdi Meuccio,  Men bunday demayman; yoq, men sendan sorayman, sen dozaxning qasos otidagi la'natlangan jonlardanmisan. Tingotsio shunday dedi:  Bunga kelsak, yoq; lekin men, men qilgan gunohlarim uchun juda ogir va azob chekyapman.

en: After this Meuccio asked if there were aught he might do for him in this world, whereto Tingoccio replied that there was, to wit, that he should let say for him masses and orisons and do alms in his name, for that these things were mightily proﬁtable to those who abode yonder.
uz: Shundan so'ng Meuccio u uchun bu dunyoda biror narsa qila oladimi deb so'radi, Tingoccio esa, ya'ni, u uchun ommaviy va orzular qilish va uning nomi bilan sadaqa qilish kerakligini aytdi, chunki bu narsalar u yerda yashovchilar uchun juda foydali edi, deb javob berdi.

en: Meuccio said that he would well and Tingoccio offering to take leave of him, he remembered himself of the latter’s amour with his gossip and raising his head, said, ‘Now that I bethink me, Tingoccio, what punish- ment is given thee over yonder anent thy gossip, with whom thou layest, whenas thou wast here below?’ ‘Brother mine,’ answered Tingoccio, ‘when- as I came yonder, there was one who it seemed knew all my sins by heart and bade me betake myself to a certain place, where I bemoaned my of- fences in exceeding sore punishment and where I found many companions condemned to the same penance as myself.
uz: Meuccio aytdiki, u yaxshi ko'rardi va Tingoccio undan voz kechishni taklif qildi, u o'zining g'iybatlari va boshini ko'targan holda, uning sevgisini esladi va dedi: "Endi meni o'ylab, Tingoccio, sen bilan yotgan g'iybating uchun senga nima jazo beriladi, sen esa shu yerda yotganingda?" "Birodarim," deb javob berdi Tingoccio, "men u yerga kelganimda, u mening barcha gunohlarimni yurakdan bilardi va meni qaysidir joyga taklif qilardi, u yerda men o'zimning og'riqli jazolarimdan xafa bo'lardim va u yerda men ham xuddi o'zim kabi tavba qilishga mahkum bo'lgan ko'plab hamrohlarni topdim.

en: Being among them and remem- bering me of that which I had done whilere with my gossip, I looked for a much sorer punishment on account thereof than that which had presently been given me and went all shivering for fear, albeit I was in a great ﬁre and an exceeding hot; which one who was by my side perceiving, he said to me, “What aileth thee more than all the others who are here that thou shiverest, being in the ﬁre?” “Marry,” said I, “my friend, I am sore in fear of the sen- tence I expect for a grievous sin I wrought aforetime.” The other asked me what sin this was, and I answered, “It was that I lay with a gossip of mine, and that with such a vengeance that it cost me my life”; whereupon quoth he, making merry over my fear, “Go to, fool; have no fear.
uz: Ularning orasida bo'lganimda va g'iybatim bilan birga qilgan ishimni eslatib turing, men shu sababli hozir berilganidan ko'ra ancha achinarli jazo qidirdim va qo'rquvdan titradim, garchi men katta olovda va juda issiq edim; kim yonimda ekanligini anglagan bo'lsa, u menga dedi: "Senga bu yerda qolganlarning hammasidan ko'ra ko'proq nima tegadi, sen olovda bo'lib qolsang?" "Uylan," dedim men, "do'stim, men oldindan qilgan og'ir gunoh uchun sen-tensiydan qo'rqaman." Boshqa biri mendan bu gunoh nima edi, deb so'radi va men javob berdim: "Bu mening g'iybatim bilan yotishim edi, va u mening hayotimni shunday qiynamoq edi, qo'rquv, qo'rquv, qo'rquv,

en: ner of account taken of gossips.” Which when I heard, I was altogether reas- sured.’ This said and the day drawing near, ‘Meuccio,’ quoth he, ‘abide with God, for I may no longer be with thee,’ and was suddenly gone.
uz: "G'iybatlar haqida xabar topdim." Buni eshitganimda, butunlay hayron bo'ldim." Bu gap va kun yaqinlashganda, "Meuccio," dedi u, "Xudo bilan birga qoling, chunki men endi siz bilan bo'lmasligim mumkin", va birdaniga ketdi.

en: Meuccio, hearing that no account was taken of gossips in the world to come, began to make mock of his own simplicity, for that whiles he had spared several of them; wherefore, laying by his ignorance, he became wiser in that respect for the future.
uz: Meuccio, kelajakda dunyoda g'iybatchilarga hech qanday e'tibor berilmaganini eshitib, o'zining soddaligi haqida masxara qila boshladi, chunki u ulardan bir nechtasini ayirgan edi; shuning uchun, o'zining jaholatidan kelib chiqib, kelajakka nisbatan donoroq bo'ldi.

en: Which things if Fra Rinaldo had known, he had not needed to go a-syllogizing,361 whenas he converted his good gossip to his pleasure.” Zephyr was now arisen, for the sun that drew near unto the setting, when the king, having made an end of his story and there being none other left to tell, put off the crown from his own head and set it on that of Lauretta, say- ing, “Madam, with yourself362 I crown you queen of our company; do you then, from this time forth, as sovereign lady, command that which you may deem shall be for the pleasure and solacement of all.” This said, he reseated himself, whereupon Lauretta, become queen, let call the seneschal and bade him look that the tables be set in the pleasant valley somewhat earlier than of wont, so they might return to the palace at their leisure; after which she instructed him what he should do what while her sovranty lasted.
uz: Agar Fra Rinaldo bilganida edi, u o'zining yaxshi g'iybatini o'ziga ma'qul qilganida, 361 ga borishga hojat qolmas edi.  Zefir endi ko'tarildi, chunki quyosh botishga yaqinlashardi. Qachonki shoh o'z hikoyasini tugatgan va aytadigan boshqa narsa qolmaganida, tojni o'z boshidan olib, Laurettaning ustiga qo'ydi va dedi: "Xonim, o'zingiz bilan birga seni bizning kompaniyamizning malikasiga aylantiraman; shundan keyin, hukmdor xonim sifatida, hamma uchun xursandchilik va tasalli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan narsalarni buyurasizmi?"

en: Then, turning to the company, she said, “Dioneo willed yesterday that we should discourse today of the tricks that women play their husbands and but that I am loath to show myself of the tribe of snappish curs, which are fain incon- tinent to avenge themselves of any affront done them, I would say that to- morrow’s discourse should be of the tricks that men play their wives.
uz: Keyin, kompaniyaga murojaat qilib, u aytdi: Dioneo kecha erlariga aytilgan hiylalarni muhokama qilishimiz kerakligini xohladi va men o'zimni har qanday haqoratdan o'zini qasos olishga tayyor bo'lmagan, o'g'ri qabiladan ekanligini ko'rsatishdan nafratlanaman, men ertaga erkaklar o'z xotinlarini o'ynaydigan hiylalar haqida gapirishimiz kerakligini aytardim.

en: But, letting that be, I ordain that each bethink himself to tell OF THE TRICKS THAT ALL DAY LONG WOMEN PLAY MEN OR MEN WOMEN OR MEN ONE ANOTHER; and I doubt not but that in this363 there will be no less of pleasant discourse than there hath been today.” So saying, she rose to her feet and dismissed the company till suppertime.
uz: Lekin, shunga qaramay, har bir kishi o'zini "Hamma kun uzoq ayollar erkaklar yoki ayollar yoki erkaklar boshqa o'yinlarni o'ynaydigan hiylalar haqida o'ylashga majbur qilaman; va men shubhalanmayman, lekin bu 363 da bugungi kundagidan kam yoqimli nutq bo'lmaydi." Shunday qilib, u oyoqqa turdi va kechki ovqatgacha odamlarni jo'natib yubordi.

en: Accordingly, they all, ladies and men alike, arose and some began to go barefoot through the clear water, whilst others went a-pleasuring upon the greensward among the straight and goodly trees.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, ularning hammasi, ayollar ham, erkaklar ham, o'rnidan turdilar va ba'zilari ochiq suvdan yalangoyoq o'ta boshladilar, boshqalari esa to'g'ri va yaxshi daraxtlar orasida yashillikka qarab, rohatlanib yurdilar.

en: Dioneo and Fiammetta sang together a great while of Arcite and Palemon, and on this wise, taking various and divers delights, they passed the time with the utmost satisfac- tion until the hour of supper; which being come, they seated themselves at
uz: Dioneo va Fiammetta birgalikda Arkit va Palemonning ajoyib vaqtlarini kuylashdi va shu tariqa turli xil va xilma-xil lazzatlarni qabul qilib, kechki ovqat soatigacha vaqtni eng yuqori qoniqish bilan o'tkazishdi; shundan so'ng ular o'tirishdi.

en: table beside the lakelet and there, to the song of a thousand birds, still re- freshed by a gentle breeze, that came from the little hills around, and un- troubled of any ﬂy, they supped in peace and cheer.
uz: Ko'lmak yonidagi stol va u yerda, minglab qushlarning qo'shig'iga, hali ham mayin shabada bilan tetiklangan, atrofdagi kichik tepaliklardan kelgan va hech qanday pashshadan bezovta bo'lmagan holda, ular tinch va xursandchilik bilan ovqatlanishdi.

en: Then, the tables being removed and the sun being yet half-vespers364 high, after they had gone awhile round about the pleasant valley, they wended their way again, even as it pleased their queen, with slow steps towards their wonted dwelling- place, and jesting and chattering a thousand things, as well of those whereof it had been that day discoursed as of others, they came near upon nightfall to the fair palace, where having with the coolest of wines and confections done away the fatigues of the little journey, they presently fell to dancing about the fair fountain, carolling365 now to the sound of Tindaro’s bagpipe and anon to that of other instruments.
uz: Keyin, stollar olib tashlanib, quyosh hali yarim chiroyli vodiyni aylanib chiqqandan so'ng, ular yana yo'lga tushdilar, hatto malikaga yoqqanidek, odatdagi yashash joyiga sekin qadamlar bilan, hazillashib va ming narsa gapirib, o'sha kuni boshqalardan ko'ra tilga olingan narsalardan tashqari, ular tun tushishi bilan adolatli saroyga yaqinlashdilar, u yerda eng zo'r vinolar va shirinliklar bilan kichik sayohatning charchoqlarini olib tashlab, ular tezda adolatli favvora atrofida raqsga tushdilar, hozir anonaro'ning nayasi va Tindaning boshqa asboblari ovoziga qo'shilib.

en: But, after awhile, the queen bade Filomena sing a song, whereupon she began thus: Alack, my life forlorn!
uz: Ammo, bir oz vaqt o'tgach, malika Filomenaga bir qo'shiq kuylashni buyurdi, shundan so'ng u shunday boshladi: Alack, mening hayotim behuda!

en: Will’t ever chance I may once more regain  Th’ estate whence sorry fortune hath me torn?
uz: Hech qachon, afsuski, baxt meni yirtgan mulkni yana bir bor qaytarib olishimning imkoni bo'lmaydimi?

en: Certes, I know not, such a wish of ﬁre  I carry in my thought  To ﬁnd me where, alas!
uz: Albatta, bilmayman, o'yimda shunday olov tilagim bor, meni qayerdan topish uchun, afsus!

en: O dear my treasure, thou my sole desire,  That holdst my heart distraught.
uz: Ey aziz xazinam, sen mening yagona orzuimsan, qalbimni tashvishga solgan.

en: Tell it me, thou; for whom I know nor dare  To ask it otherwhere.
uz: Ayt menga, sen; kim uchun bilsam ham, boshqa joyda so'rashga jur'at etmasam ham.

en: Ah, dear my lord, oh, cause me hope again,  So I may comfort me my spright wayworn.
uz: Oh, aziz hazratim, oh, menga yana umid bering, toki men o'zimning yorqin yo'ldan ketgan odamimni ovutishim mumkin bo'lsin.

en: What was the charm I cannot rightly tell  That kindled in me such  A ﬂame of love that rest nor day nor night  I ﬁnd; for, by some strong unwonted spell,  Hearing and touch  And seeing each new ﬁres in me did light,  Wherein I burn outright;  Nor other than thyself can soothe my pain  Nor call my senses back, by love o’erborne.
uz: Qanday joziba ekanligini to'g'ri ayta olmayman, U menga shunday muhabbat alangasini yoqdi, na kunduzi, na kechasi men uni topmayman; chunki, ba'zi kuchli, o'chirilmagan sehr orqali, eshitish va tegish va ichimdagi har bir yangi olovni ko'rish yorug'lik berdi, Unda men butunlay yonaman; Na o'zingdan boshqa mening dardimni tinchlantirolmaydi, Na sezgilarimni qaytarib chaqirolmaydi, sevgi bilan begona.

en: O tell me if and when, then, it shall be  That I shall ﬁnd thee e’er
uz: Agar va qachon bo'lsa, menga ayting, keyin men sizni topaman.

en: Whereas I kissed those eyes that did me slay.
uz: Meni o'ldirgan ko'zlarimni o'pdim.

en: O dear my good, my soul, ah, tell it me,  When thou wilt come back there,  And saying “Quickly,” comfort my dismay  Somedele.
uz: Ey azizim, ey jonim, ayting-chi, qachonki u yerga qaytib kelib, "Tezroq" deb, xavotirimni tinchlantirsang, Somedele.

en: Short be the stay  Until thou come, and long mayst thou remain!
uz: Kelguningcha qisqa qol, uzoq qol!

en: I’m so love-struck, I reck not of men’s scorn.
uz: Men shunchalik muhabbatga berilib ketdimki, erkaklarning haqoratidan voz kechmayman.

en: If once again I chance to hold thee aye,  I will not be so fond  As erst I was to suffer thee to ﬂy;  Nay, fast I’ll hold thee, hap of it what may,  And having thee in bond,  Of thy sweet mouth my lust I’ll satisfy.
uz: Agar seni yana bir bor ushlashga to'g'ri kelsa, seni uchirishga qo'yib yuborishga majbur bo'lganimdek mehrga to'la bo'lmayman; Yo'q, tezda seni ushlayman, nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, Seni bog'lab, shirin og'zingdan shahvatimni qondiraman.

en: Now of nought else will I  Discourse.
uz: Endi boshqa hech narsa haqida gapirmayman.

en: Quick, to thy bosom come me strain;  The sheer thought bids me sing like lark at morn.
uz: Tez, ko'kragingga zo'riqish kelyapti; Ochiq xayol meni ertalabki piyoz kabi kuylashga majbur qilyapti.

en: This song caused all the company conclude that a new and pleasing love held Filomena in bonds, and as by the words it appeared that she had tasted more thereof than sight alone, she was envied of this by certain who were there and who held her therefor so much the happier.
uz: Bu qo'shiq butun kompaniyaga Filomena'ni yangi va yoqimli sevgi bog'lab turgani haqida xulosa chiqarishga sabab bo'ldi va so'zlardan ko'rinib turibdiki, u faqat ko'rishdan ko'ra ko'proq tatib ko'rgan edi, shuning uchun u yerda bo'lgan va uni shu sababli shunchalik baxtli deb hisoblagan ba'zi odamlar tomonidan unga hasad qilindi.

en: But, after her song was ended, the queen, remembering her that the ensuing day was Friday, thus graciously bespoke all, “You know, noble ladies and you also, young men, that tomorrow is the day consecrated to the passion of our Lord, the which, an you remember aright, what time Neiﬁle was queen, we celebrated devoutly and therein gave pause to our delightsome discoursements, and on like wise we did with the following Saturday.
uz: Ammo, uning qo'shig'i tugagandan so'ng, malika, keyingi kun juma ekanligini eslab, hammaga marhamat bilan shunday dedi: "Bilasiz-ku, olijanob xonimlar va siz ham, yoshlar, ertaga Rabbimizning azob-uqubatiga bag'ishlangan kun, uni, to'g'ri eslaysiz, nima zamonlarda Neifile malika edi, biz u yerda xudojo'ylik bilan nishonladik va o'zimizning yoqimli nutqlarimizga to'xtadik, va xuddi donolik bilan keyingi shanba bilan ham shunday qildik."

en: Wherefore, being minded to follow the good example given us by Neiﬁle, I hold it seemly that tomorrow and the next day we abstain, even as we did a week agone, from our pleas- ant story-telling, recalling to memory that which on those days befell whilere for the salvation of our souls.” The queen’s pious speech was pleas- ing unto all and a good part of the night being now past, they all, dismissed by her, betook them to repose.
uz: Shuning uchun, Neifile tomonidan berilgan yaxshi namunaga ergashishga intilib, men ertaga va ertasi kuni, xuddi bir hafta oldin qilganimizdek, o'sha kunlarda jonimizni saqlab qolganlarni eslab, hikoya qilishdan to'xtaydiganga o'xshayman. Qirolichaning taqvodor nutqi hammaga ilhom berdi va tunning yaxshi bir qismi o'tib ketdi, ularning barchasi, u tomonidan rad etilganlar, ularni dam olishga chaqirdi.

en: Here endeth the Seventh Day of the Decameron.
uz: Mana Dekameronning yettinchi kuni tugaydi.

en: DAY THE EIGHTH INTRODUCTION Here beginneth the eighth day of the Decameron wherein under the governance of Lauretta is discoursed of the tricks that all day long women play men or men women or men one another.
uz: Sakkizinchi KUN Kirish Mana, Decameronning sakkizinchi kuni boshlanadi, unda Lauretta boshqaruvi ostida ayollar butun kun davomida erkaklar yoki erkaklar, ayollar yoki erkaklar bir-birini o'ynaydigan hiylalar haqida gapiriladi.

en: Already on the Sunday morning the rays of the rising light appeared on the summits of the higher mountains and every shadow having departed, things might manifestly be discerned, when the queen, arising with her company, went wandering ﬁrst through the dewy grass and after, towards half- tierce,366 visiting a little neighboring church, heard there divine service; then, returning home, they ate with mirth and joyance and after sang and danced awhile till the queen dismissed them, so whoso would might go rest himself.
uz: Yakshanba kuni ertalabdan yuqori tog'larning cho'qqilarida chiqayotgan nurlar paydo bo'ldi va har bir soya ketganidan so'ng, narsalarni aniq anglash mumkin edi, qirolicha o'z kompaniyasi bilan turib, avval ilohiy o'tlar bo'ylab sayr qildi va keyin, yarim darajaga tomon,366 kichik qo'shni cherkovga tashrif buyurdi, u yerda ilohiy xizmat eshitdi; keyin, uyga qaytib, xursandchilik va quvonch bilan ovqatlanishdi va keyin qirolicha ularni haydab yubormaguncha biroz vaqt kuylab raqsga tushishdi, shunda kim o'zi dam olishi mumkin edi.

en: But, whenas the sun had passed the meridian, they all seated them- selves, according as it pleased the queen, near the fair fountain, for the wonted story-telling, and Neiﬁle, by her commandment, began thus:
uz: Ammo quyosh meridian bo'ylab o'tgach, ularning hammasi o'tirishdi  malika xohlaganicha, go'zal favvora yaqinida, chunki odatdagidek hikoya qilish va uning buyrug'iga ko'ra nopoklik shunday boshlandi:

en: THE FIRST STORY Gulfardo borroweth of Guasparruolo certain monies, for which he hath agreed with his wife that he shall lie with her, and accordingly giveth them to her; then, in her presence, he telleth Guasparruolo that he gave them to her, and she confesseth it to be true.
uz: BIRINCHI HIKOYA Gulfardo Guasparruolodan ma'lum miqdordagi pul qarz oladi, buning uchun u xotini bilan birga yotishga kelishib oladi va shunga ko'ra unga beradi; keyin, uning huzurida Guasparruolodan unga berganini aytadi va u buni rost deb tan oladi.

en: “Since God hath so ordered it that I am to give a beginning to the present day’s discourses, with my story, I am content, and therefore, lovesome ladies, seeing that much hath been said of the tricks played by women upon men, it is my pleasure to relate one played by a man upon a woman, not that I mean therein to blame that which the man did or to deny that it served the woman aright, nay, rather to commend the man and blame the woman and to show that men also know how to cozen those who put faith in them, even as themselves are cozened by those in whom they believe.
uz: Xudo shunday buyurganki, men o'z hikoyam bilan hozirgi kundagi nutqlarni boshlashim kerak, shuning uchun men rozi bo'ldim va shuning uchun, mehribon ayollar, ayollar erkaklarga o'ynagan hiylalar haqida ko'p gapirilganini ko'rib, men erkakning ayolga o'ynaganini aytib berishdan mamnunman, bu yerda erkakning qilgan ishini ayblash yoki ayolga to'g'ri kelganini inkor etishni emas, balki erkakni maqtash va ayolni ayblash va erkaklar ham ularga ishonganlarni, hatto o'zlari ishonganlar tomonidan o'ynaganlarni qanday ayblashni bilishini ko'rsatishni nazarda tutyapman.

en: Indeed, to speak more precisely, that whereof I have to tell should not be called cozenage; nay, it should rather be styled a just requital; for that, albeit a woman should still be virtuous and guard her chastity as her life nor on any account suffer herself be persuaded to sully it, yet, seeing that, by reason of our frailty, this is not always possible as fully as should be, I afﬁrm that she who consenteth to her own dishonour for a price is worthy of the ﬁre, whereas she who yiel- deth for Love’s sake, knowing his exceeding great puissance, meriteth for- giveness from a judge not too severe, even as, a few days agone, Filostrato showed it to have been observed towards Madam Filippa at Prato.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, aniqroq aytadigan bo'lsak, men aytishim kerak bo'lgan narsa "kozenage" deb atalmasligi kerak; aksincha, uni adolatli qasos deb atash kerak; chunki, garchi ayol hali ham o'z hayoti kabi fazilatli bo'lishi va o'z beg'uborligini saqlashi kerak bo'lsa-da, hech qanday sababga ko'ra uni haqoratlashga ko'ndirilishiga yo'l qo'ymasligi kerak, ammo, bizning zaifligimiz tufayli bu har doim ham to'liq bo'lishi mumkin emasligini ko'rib, men tasdiqlaymanki, o'z sharmandaligiga narx evaziga rozi bo'lgan ayol olovga loyiqdir, garchi u sevgi uchun qurbonlik qilgan bo'lsa ham, o'zining buyuk qudratini bilgan holda, bir necha kun o'tib, Filostrato buni juda og'ir emas, balki unga nisbatan ko'rsatilganini ko'rsatdi.

en: There was, then, aforetime at Milan a German, by name Gulfardo, in the pay of the state, a stout fellow of his person and very loyal to those in whose service he engaged himself, which is seldom the case with Germans; and for that he was a very punctual repayer of such loans as were made him, he might always ﬁnd many merchants ready to lend him any quantity
uz: Shunday qilib, bir vaqtlar Milanda Gulfardo ismli bir nemis bor edi, u davlatning pullik hisobidan o'zining zodagon do'sti edi va u o'zi xizmat qilayotganlarga juda sodiq edi, bu nemislar bilan kamdan-kam uchraydi; va shuning uchun u unga berilgan bunday kreditlarni juda tezda to'laydigan odam edi, u har doim unga har qanday miqdorda qarz berishga tayyor ko'plab savdogarlarni topishi mumkin edi.

en: of money at little usance.
uz: pulning kamdan-kam foydalanishi.

en: During his sojourn in Milan, he set his heart upon a very fair lady called Madam Ambruogia, the wife of a rich merchant, by name Guasparruolo Cagastraccio, who was much his acquaintance and friend, and loving her very discreetly, so that neither her husband nor any other suspected it, he sent one day to speak with her, praying her that it would please her vouchsafe him her favours and protesting that he, on his part, was ready to do whatsoever she should command him.
uz: Milanda bo'lgan davrida u juda go'zal Madam Ambruogia ismli xotinga, boy savdogarning xotini Guasparruolo Cagastraccioga ko'nglini qaratdi. Guasparruolo Cagastraccio uning tanishi va do'sti edi va uni juda yashirincha yaxshi ko'rardi. Shunday qilib, na eri, na boshqa hech kim buni gumon qilmas edi, u bilan gaplashishga bir kun jo'natdi, unga uning unga o'z marhamatini berishini so'radi va u, o'z navbatida, unga buyurishi kerak bo'lgan har qanday ishni qilishga tayyorligini ta'kidladi.

en: The lady, after many parleys, came to this conclusion, that she was ready to do that which Gulfardo wished, provided two things should ensue thereof; one, that this should never be by him discovered to any and the other, that, as she had need of two hundred gold ﬂorins for some occasion of hers, he, who was a rich man, should give them to her; after which she would still be at his service.
uz: Xonim, ko'p suhbatlardan so'ng, Gulfardo xohlagan narsani qilishga tayyor ekanligiga, agar undan ikki narsa kelib chiqsa, shunday xulosaga keldi: biri, bu hech qachon uning tomonidan hech kimga ma'lum bo'lmasligi kerak, ikkinchisi esa, unga qandaydir bir imkoniyat uchun ikki yuz oltin florin kerak bo'lgani uchun, boy odam unga berishi kerak edi; shundan keyin u hali ham uning xizmatida bo'lardi.

en: Gulfardo, hearing this and indignant at the sordidness of her whom he had accounted a lady of worth, was like to exchange his fervent love for hatred and thinking to cheat her, sent back to her, saying that he would very willingly do this and all else in his power that might please her and that therefore she should e’en send him word when she would have him go to her, for that he would carry her the money, nor should any ever hear aught of the matter, save a comrade of his in whom he trusted greatly and who still bore him company in whatsoever he did.
uz: Gulfardo bu gapni eshitib, uning beodobligidan g'azablanib, uni qimmatbaho xonim deb hisoblagan edi, o'zining achchiq muhabbatini nafratga almashtirmoqchi edi va uni aldashni o'ylagandek, unga qaytib keldi. U bunga va unga yoqadigan barcha narsaga juda xohish bilan murojaat qilardi va shuning uchun u uni unga borishini so'raganida, pulni olib borishini va bu haqda hech kim eshitmasligi kerak edi, faqat o'ziga ishonadigan va u qilgan har qanday ishda ham unga sherik bo'ladigan o'rtoqidan boshqa.

en: The lady, or rather, I should say, the vile woman, hearing this, was well pleased and sent to him, saying that Guasparruolo her husband was to go to Genoa for his occasions a few days hence and that she would presently let him know of this and send for him.
uz: Xonim, to'g'rirog'i, aytishim kerakki, bu narsani eshitib, jirkanch ayol juda xursand bo'lib, unga Guasparruolo uning eri bir necha kundan keyin uning tadbirlari uchun Genuyaga borishini va tez orada unga bu haqda xabar berishini va uni chaqirib yuborishini aytdi.

en: Meanwhile, Gulfardo, taking his opportunity, repaired to Guasparruolo and said to him, ‘I have present occasion for two hundred gold ﬂorins, the which I would have thee lend me at that same usance whereat thou art wont to lend me other monies.’ The other replied that he would well and straight- way counted out to him the money.
uz: Ayni paytda, Gulfardo imkoniyatdan foydalanib, Guasparruoloni ta'mirladi va unga dedi: "Menda hozir ikki yuz oltin florin bor, uni xuddi o'sha tarzda berishingni xohlardim, sen esa menga boshqa pul bermaysan". Boshqa biri esa u pulni yaxshi va to'g'ridan-to'g'ri hisoblab berishini aytdi.

en: A few days thereafterward Guasparruolo went to Genoa, even as the lady had said, whereupon she sent to Gulfardo to come to her and bring the two hundred gold ﬂorins.
uz: Bir necha kundan so'ng Guasparruolo Genuyaga ketdi, xuddi xonim aytganidek, shundan so'ng u Gulfardoga uning oldiga kelib, ikki yuz tilla florinni olib kelishini yubordi.

en: Accordingly, he took his comrade and repaired to the lady’s house, where ﬁnding her expecting him, the ﬁrst thing he did was to put into her hands the two hundred gold ﬂorins, in his friend’s presence, saying to her, ‘Madam, take these monies and give them to your husband, whenas he shall be returned.’ The lady took them, never guessing why he said thus, but supposing that he did it so his comrade should not perceive
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u o'z o'rtoqini olib, xonimning uyiga jo'nadi. U uni kutib turganini topgach, birinchi qilgan ishi do'stining huzurida ikki yuz tilla florinni uning qo'liga qo'yib, unga dedi: "Xonim, bu pullarni olib, eringizga qaytib kelganda bering." Xonim ularni olib, u nega bunday deganini hech qachon tushunmadi, lekin o'rtoqining buni ko'rmasligi uchun shunday qilganini taxmin qildi.

en: that he gave them to her by way of price, and answered, ‘With all my heart; but I would fain see how many they are.’ Accordingly, she turned them out upon the table and ﬁnding them full two hundred, laid them up, mighty con- tent in herself; then, returning to Gulfardo and carrying him into her cham- ber, she satisﬁed him of her person not that night only, but many others be- fore her husband returned from Genoa.
uz: U ularni unga narx bo'yicha berdi va javob berdi: "Butun qalbim bilan; lekin ularning qancha ekanligini ko'rishni xohlardim." Shunga ko'ra, u ularni stol ustiga ag'dardi va to'la ikki yuzni topdi, o'zida qudratli chodir yotqizdi; so'ngra, Gulfardoga qaytib kelib, uni o'z xonasiga olib kirgach, u nafaqat o'sha kechada, balki ko'plab boshqa odamlardan ham mamnun bo'ldi.

en: As soon as the latter came back, Gulfardo, having spied out a time when he was in company with his wife, betook himself to him, together with his comrade aforesaid, and said to him, in the lady’s presence, ‘Guasparruolo, I had no occasion for the monies, to wit, the two hundred gold ﬂorins, thou lentest me the other day, for that I could not compass the business for which I borrowed them.
uz: Oxirgisi qaytib kelishi bilanoq, Gulfardo, xotini bilan birga bo'lgan vaqtni kuzatib, unga, yuqorida aytib o'tilgan o'rtog'i bilan yaqinlashdi va xonimning huzurida unga dedi: "Guasparruolo, men pulga, ya'ni, ikki yuz oltin floringa hech qanday haqim yo'q edi, sen menga o'tgan kuni qarz bergan eding, chunki men ularni qarzga olgan biznesimni o'rgana olmadim."

en: Accordingly, I brought them presently back to thy lady here and gave them to her; wherefore look thou cancel my account.’ Guas- parruolo, turning to his wife, asked her if she had the monies, and she, see- ing the witness present, knew not how to deny, but said, ‘Ay, I had them and had not yet remembered me to tell thee.’ Whereupon quoth Guasparruolo, ‘Gulfardo, I am satisﬁed; get you gone and God go with you: I will settle your account aright.’ Gulfardo gone, the lady, ﬁnding herself cozened, gave her husband the dishonourable price of her baseness; and on this wise the crafty lover enjoyed his sordid mistress without cost.”
uz: Shunga ko'ra, men ularni shu zahotiyoq xonimingizga qaytarib keldim va unga berdim; shuning uchun, mana, hisobimni bekor qil." Guas-parruolo xotiniga o'girilib, undan pul bor-yo'qligini so'radi. U guvohlarni ko'rib, qanday inkor qilishni bilmas edi, lekin dedi: "Ha, men ularni olgan edim va senga aytishni hali eslamagan edim." Shunda Guasparruolo dedi: "Gulfardo, men rozi bo'ldim; seni ket va Xudo sen bilan boradi: men sening hisobingni to'g'ri hal qilaman." Gulfardo ketdi, xonim o'zini pishirib, o'zini xor deb topib, eriga o'zining xorligini xor narxini berdi; va shunga qaramay, ayyor oshiq xotining beaybdan rohatlandi.

en: THE SECOND STORY The parish priest of Varlungo lieth with mistress Belcolore and leaveth her a cloak of his in pledge; then, borrowing a mortar of her, he sendeth it back to her, demanding in return the cloak left by way of token, which the good woman grudgingly giveth him back.
uz: IKKINCHI HIKOYA Varlungo cherkov ruhoniysi bekasi Belcolor bilan yotadi va unga o'zining ko'ylagini garovga qoldiradi; so'ngra, undan bir soyabon qarz olib, uni unga qaytarib yuboradi, buning evaziga yaxshi ayol unga qaytarib berayotgan ko'ylakni belgi sifatida talab qiladi.

en: Men and ladies alike commended that which Gulfardo had done to the sor- did Milanese lady, and the queen, turning to Pamﬁlo, smilingly charged him follow on; whereupon quoth he, “Fair ladies, it occurreth to me to tell you a little story against those who continually offend against us, without being open to retaliation on our part, to wit, the clergy, who have proclaimed a crusade against our wives and who, whenas they avail to get one of the lat- ter under them, conceive themselves to have gained forgiveness of fault and pardon of penalty no otherwise than as they had brought the Soldan bound from Alexandria to Avignon.367 Whereof the wretched laymen cannot re- turn them the like, albeit they wreak their ire upon the priests’ mothers and sisters, doxies and daughters, assailing them with no less ardour than the former do their wives.
uz: Erkaklar ham, ayollar ham Gulfardo milanlik xonimga qilgan ishini maqtashdi, va malika Pamfiloga qarab, unga tabassum bilan ergashishni buyurdi; shundan so'ng u dedi: "Adolatli xonimlar, sizga bizga qarshi doimiy ravishda xafa bo'lganlarga qarshi kichik bir hikoya aytishga to'g'ri keladi, ular biz tomondan qasos olishga ochiq emaslar, ya'ni, ruhoniylar, ular xotinlarimizga qarshi salib yurishini e'lon qilganlar va ular ulardan birortasini olishga muvaffaq bo'lganlarida, o'zlarini Soldanni Iskandariyadan Avignonga olib kelganlaridan ko'ra kamroq jazo va jazo mag'firatiga erishgan deb hisoblashadi."

en: Wherefore I purpose to recount to you a village love- affair, more laughable for its conclusion than long in words, wherefrom you may yet gather, by way of fruit, that priests are not always to be believed in everything.
uz: Shuning uchun men sizga qishloqdagi sevgi voqeasini hikoya qilishni niyat qilaman, uning yakunlanishi so'zlarda uzoqroq bo'lganidan ko'ra kulgiliroq, undan siz hali ham meva sifatida ruhoniylarga har doim ham hamma narsaga ishonish kerak emasligini anglashingiz mumkin.

en: You must know, then, that there was once at Varlungo —a village very near here, as each of you ladies either knoweth or may have heard —a worthy priest and a lusty of his person in the service of the ladies, who, al- beit he knew not overwell how to read, natheless regaled his parishioners with store of good and pious saws at the elmfoot on Sundays and visited their women, whenas they went abroad anywhither, more diligently than any priest who had been there aforetime, carrying them fairings and holy
uz: Shuni bilishingiz kerakki, Varlungo shahrida bir vaqtlar  bu yerga juda yaqin qishloqda, har biringizning bilganingiz yoki eshitganingizdek  munosib ruhoniy va ayollarga xizmat qilayotgan shahvatparast odam bor edi. U, ehtimol, o'qishni yaxshi bilmas edi, ammo yakshanba kunlari cherkov a'zolarini yelka oyog'ida yaxshi va taqvodor arralar bilan ta'minlab, ayollarini ziyorat qilardi, ular chet elga qayerga borganlarida, avvalroq u yerda bo'lgan har qanday ruhoniydan ko'ra astoydilroq.

en: water and a stray candle-end or so, whiles even to their houses.
uz: Suv va adashgan sham uchi yoki shunga o'xshash, hatto uylariga ham oqadi.

en: Now it chanced that, among other his she-parishioners who were most to his liking, one pleased him over all, by name Mistress Belcolore, the wife of a hus- bandman who styled himself Bentivegna del Mazzo, a jolly, buxom country wench, brown-favoured and tight-made, as apt at turning the mill368 as any woman alive.
uz: Endi shunday bo'ldiki, uning eng yoqtirgan ayol-parishionerlari orasida, uni hammadan ko'proq yoqtirgan biri bor edi, uning ismi Mistress Belcolore edi, o'zini Bentivegna del Mazzo deb ataydigan erkakning rafiqasi, quvnoq, to'lishgan qishloq kampirasi, jigarrang yoqimli va tor, har qanday ayol kabi mill368ni haydashga qodir edi.

en: Moreover, it was she who knew how to play the tabret and sing ‘The water runneth to the ravine’ and lead up the haye and the round, when need was, with a ﬁne muckender in her hand and a quaint, better than any woman of her neighbourhood; by reason of which things my lord priest became so sore enamoured of her that he was like to lose his wits therefor and would prowl about all day long to get a sight of her.
uz: Qolaversa, aynan u tabret chalashni va "Suv jarlikka oqadi" deb kuylashni bilardi, kerak bo'lganda esa, qo'lida nozik muckender va qo'shnilaridan yaxshiroq g'aroyib bir ayol bilan haye va roundni olib chiqardi; shu sababli ruhoniy hazratim unga shunchalik oshiq bo'lib ketdiki, u shu sababli aqldan ozdi va uni ko'rish uchun kun bo'yi aylanib yurardi.

en: Whenas he espied her in church of a Sunday morning, he would say a Kyrie and a Sanctus, studying to show himself a past master in descant, that it seemed as it were an ass a-braying; whereas, when he saw her not there, he passed that part of the service over lightly enough.
uz: U uni yakshanba kuni ertalab cherkovda kuzatib borar ekan, o'zini pastdagi ustoz deb ko'rsatish uchun Kyrie va Sanctus deb o'qir edi, go'yo xuddi eshak o'ynagandek tuyulardi; lekin u uni u yerda ko'rmaganda, xizmatning o'sha qismini yengillik bilan o'tkazib yuborgan edi.

en: But yet he made shift to do on such wise that neither Bentivegna nor any of his neighbours suspected aught; and the better to gain Mistress Belcolore’s goodwill, he made her presents from time to time, sending her whiles a clove of garlic, which he had the ﬁnest of all the countryside in a garden he tilled with his own hands, and otherwhiles a punnet of peascods or a bunch of chives or scallions, and whenas he saw his opportunity, he would ogle her askance and cast a friendly gibe at her; but she, putting on the prude, made a show of not observing it and passed on with a demure air; wherefore my lord priest could not come by his will of her.
uz: Lekin u shunday donolik bilan ish tutdiki, na Bentivegna, na uning qo'shnilarining hech biri hech narsadan gumon qilmasdi; va xonim Belcolorning yaxshi niyatini qozonish uchun, u vaqti-vaqti bilan unga sovg'alar tayyorlardi, unga sarimsoq bo'lakni jo'natardi, uni o'z qo'llari bilan bog'da eng yaxshi bo'lardi, boshqa bo'laklarni esa bir dasta bo'lak yoki bir to'da mayda yoki mayda-chuyda, va u o'z imkoniyatini ko'rganda, unga shahvoniylik ko'rsatib, unga do'stona sovg'a tashlardi; lekin u kibr bilan buni kuzatmaslikni ko'rsatdi va xotirjamlik bilan o'tib ketdi; shuning uchun ruhoniy o'z xo'jayini tomonidan kelolmadi.

en: It chanced one day that as he sauntered about the quarter on the stroke of noon, he encountered Bentivegna del Mazzo, driving an ass laden with gear, and accosting him, asked whither he went.
uz: Bir kuni, tush paytida chorak atrofida sayohat qilib yurganida, u Bentivegna del Mazzoga duch keldi. U tishli eshakni haydab, unga yaqinlashib, qayerga ketayotganini so'radi.

en: ‘Faith, sir,’ answered the hus- bandman, ‘to tell you the truth, I am going to town about a business of mine and am carrying these things to Squire Bonaccorri da Ginestreto, so he may help me in I know not what whereof the police-court judge hath summoned me by his proctor for a peremptory attendance.’ The priest was rejoiced to hear this and said, ‘Thou dost well, my son; go now with my benison and return speedily; and shouldst thou chance to see Lapuccio or Naldino, forget not to bid them bring me those straps they wot of for my ﬂails.’ Bentivegna answered that it should be done and went his way towards Florence, whereupon the priest bethought himself that now was his time to go try his luck with Belcolore.
uz: Faith, janob,  javob berdi hus-bandman,  rostini aytsam, men shaharga oz ishim bilan boryapman va bu narsalarni Squire Bonaccorrri da Ginestretoga olib ketyapman, shunda u menga yordam berishi mumkin. Bilmayman, politsiya-sud hakami meni oz prokurori tomonidan tezkor tashrifga chaqirgan. Ruhoniy buni eshitib xursand boldi va dedi: Siz yaxshisiz, oglim; hozir mening benisonim bilan keting va tezda qaytib keling; va Lapuccio yoki Naldino bilan korish imkoniyatiga ega bolsangiz, menga ular mening qovurgularim uchun osha tasmalarni olib kelishni unutmang. Bentivegna javob berdi va u Florensiya tomon yol oldi, u yerda ruhoniy ozining omadini sinab korish vaqti keldi deb oyladi.

en: Accordingly, he let not the grass grow under his feet,
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u oyoqlari ostiga o't o'sishiga yo'l qo'ymadi.

en: but set off forthright and stayed not till he came to her house and entering in, said, ‘God send us all well!
uz: Ammo to'g'ri yo'lga chiqdi va u uning uyiga kelib, ichkariga kirguncha qolmadi va dedi: "Alloh hammamizni sog'aytirsin!"

en: Who is within there?’ Belcolore, who was gone up into the hayloft, hearing him, said, ‘Marry, sir, you are welcome; but what do you gadding it abroad in this heat?’ ‘So God give me good luck,’ answered he, ‘I came to abide with thee awhile, for that I met thy man going to town.’ Belcolore came down and taking a seat, fell to picking over cabbage-seed which her husband had threshed out a while before; whereupon quoth the priest to her, ‘Well, Belcolore, wilt thou still cause me die for thee on this wise?’ She laughed and answered, ‘What is it I do to you?’ Quoth he, ‘Thou dost nought to me, but thou sufferest me not do to thee that which I would fain do and which God commandeth.’ ‘Alack!’ cried Belcolore, ‘Go to, go to.
uz: U yerda kim bor? Belcolor, uni eshitib, hayvonga chiqqan edi, dedi: Uylaning, janob, xush kelibsiz; lekin bu issiqda chet elda nima qilyapsiz? Xudo menga omad bersin, javob berdi u, Men bir oz siz bilan yashashga keldim, chunki men sizning odamingizni shaharga borayotganda uchratdim. Belcolor tushdi va otirdi, erining biroz oldin terib chiqqan karam urugini terishga tushdi; keyin ruhoniy unga dedi: Belcolor, siz meni shu yol bilan oldirasizmi? U kuldi va javob berdi: Siz menga nima qilmoqchisiz? U dedi: Sen menga yoq, lekin menga yoq, men senga buyurgan narsani qilmaslikka ruxsat bermaysan, Belka,  keting,

en: Do priests do such things?’ ‘Ay do we,’ replied he, ‘as well as other men; and why not?
uz: Ruhoniylar bunday ishlarni qilishadimi? Ayo, biz ham,  javob berdi u,  boshqa odamlar kabi; va nega unday emas?

en: And I tell thee more, we do far and away better work and knowest thou why?
uz: Va senga yana aytaman, biz ancha yaxshi ishlar qilamiz va nega ekanligini bilasanmi?

en: Because we grind with a full head of water.
uz: Chunki biz to'la bosh suv bilan maydalaymiz.

en: But in good sooth it shall be shrewdly to thy proﬁt, an thou wilt but abide quiet and let me do.’ ‘And what might this “shrewdly to my proﬁt” be?’ asked she.
uz: Ammo yaxshi holatda bu senga foyda keltiradigan darajada ayyor bo'ladi, sen esa jim turgin va menga qo'yib bergin.Va bu mening foydamga ayyor nima bo'lishi mumkin? deb so'radi u.

en: ‘For all you priests are stingier than the devil.’ Quoth he, ‘I know not; ask thou.
uz: Chunki sizlar ruhoniylar iblisdan ham badbo'yroqsizlar. U javob berdi: Bilmayman; so'ra.

en: Wilt have a pair of shoes or a head-lace or a ﬁne stammel waistband or what thou wilt?’ ‘Pshaw!’ cried Belcolore.
uz: "Bir juft poyabzal, bosh bog'lami yoki mayda po'stlog'i belbog'im bormi yoki nima qilmoqchisan?" Psha! deb baqirdi Belcolore.

en: ‘I have enough and to spare of such things; but an you wish me so well, why do you not render me a service, and I will do what you will?’ Quoth the priest, ‘Say what thou wilt have of me, and I will do it willingly.’ Then said she, ‘Needs must I go to Florence, come Saturday, to carry back the wool I have spun and get my spinning- wheel mended; and an you will lend me ﬁve crowns, which I know you have by you, I can take my watchet gown out of pawn and my Sunday girdle369 that I brought my husband, for you see I cannot go to church nor to any decent place, because I have them not; and after I will still do what you would have me.’ ‘So God give me a good year,’ replied the priest, ‘I have them not about me; but believe me, ere Saturday come, I will contrive that thou shalt have them, and that very willingly.’ ‘Ay,’ said Belcolore, ‘you are all like this, great promisers, and after perform
