uz: Menda bunday narsalardan ehtiyot bo'lish yetarli; lekin siz menga shunchalik yaxshi niyat qilasiz, nega menga xizmat ko'rsatmaysiz, men ham xohlaganingizni qilaman? Ruhoniy aytdi: Mendan xohlaganingizni ayting, men ham xohlaganimcha qilaman. Keyin u aytdi: Men Florensiyaga borishim kerak, shanba kuni keling, o'ragan junimni olib qaytarib, g'ildiragimni tuzataman; va siz menga beshta toj berasiz, men sizning qo'lingizda borligini bilaman, men piyoda kiyimni va yakshanba kamarimni olsam bo'ladi. Ruhoniy aytdi: Men siz uchun cherkovga ham, hech qanday munosib joyga borolmayman, chunki men ularni ko'ra olmayman; va keyin ham siz menga berganingizni qilaman.

en: nothing to any.
uz: Hech kimga hech narsa yo'q.

en: Think you to do with me as you did with Biliuzza, who went off with the ghittern- player?370 Cock’s faith, then, you shall not, for that she is turned a common drab only for that.
uz: Menimcha, meni Biliuzza bilan qilganingizdek, ghittern-player bilan ketgandek qilasizmi?370 Xo'rozning ishonchi, demak, qilmasligingiz kerak, chunki u faqat shu uchun umumiy bezakga aylangan.

en: If you have them not about you, go for them.’ ‘Alack,’ cried the priest, ‘put me not upon going all the way home.
uz: Agar ular yoningizda bo'lmasa, ularni toping." Alack, - deb baqirdi ruhoniy, - meni uyga boradigan yo'lga qo'ymang.

en: Thou seest that I have the luck just now to ﬁnd thee alone, but maybe, when I return, there
uz: Ko'rib turibsan-ku, hozir seni yolg'iz topishga omadim keldi, lekin ehtimol, qaytib kelganimda, u yerda bo'lar.

en: will be some one or other here to hinder us; and I know not when I shall ﬁnd so good an opportunity again.’ Quoth she, ‘It is well; an you choose to go, go; if not, go without.’ The priest, seeing that she was not in the humour to do his pleasure without a salvum me fac, whereas he would fain have done it sine custodiâ, said, ‘Harkye, thou believest not that I will bring thee the money; but, so thou mayst credit me, I will leave thee this my blue-cloth cloak.’ Belcolore raised her eyes and said, ‘Eh what!
uz: Bizga xalaqit beradigan kimdir bo'ladi; va men qachon yana shunday yaxshi imkoniyat topishimni bilmayman." U aytdi: "Yaxshi; agar siz borishni tanlasangiz, keting; agar yo'q bo'lsa, tashqariga chiqing." Ruhoniy, u o'z xohish-istaklarini hech qanday salvimsiz qilish uchun hazilda emasligini ko'rib, u buni hech qanday ehtiyotsizlik bilan qilmagan bo'lardi, dedi: "Harkye, siz pulni sizga olib keladiganimga ishonmaysiz; lekin, agar menga ishonishingiz mumkin bo'lsa, men bu ko'k xalatimni sizga qoldiraman." Belcolore ko'zlarini ko'tardi va dedi: "Ah nima!"

en: What is it worth?’ ‘Worth?’ answered the priest.
uz: Buning nima keragi bor? Arziydimi? deb javob berdi ruhoniy.

en: ‘I would have thee know that it is cloth of Douay, nay, Threeay, and there be some of our folk here who hold it for Fouray.371 It is scarce a fortnight since it cost me seven crowns of hard money to Lotto the broker, and according to what Buglietto telleth me (and thou knowest he is a judge of this kind of cloth), I had it good ﬁve shillings overcheap.’ ‘In- deed!’ quoth Belcolore.
uz: Men senga bilishingni xohlardimki, bu Douayning matosi, yo'q, Uchayning matosi, va bu yerda bizning odamlarimizdan ba'zilari uni Fouray uchun ushlab turishadi. 371 Bu menga Lotto brokerga yetti qattiq pulga tushganidan beri deyarli o'n besh kun bo'ldi, va Buglietto menga aytganidek (va sen bilasan u bu turdagi matoning hakami), men buni besh shillindan arzonroq sotib olgan edim. Haqiqatan ham!  deydi Belcolore.

en: ‘So God be mine aid, I had never thought it.
uz: Xudo menga yordam bersin, men buni hech qachon o'ylamagan edim.

en: But give it me ﬁrst of all.’ My lord priest, who had his arbalest ready cocked, pulled off the cloak and gave it her; and she, after she had laid it up, said, ‘Come, sir, let us go into the barn, for no one ever cometh there.’ And so they did.
uz: Lekin avvalo menga bering. Ruhoniy hazratim, uning ko'ylagi pishirilgan edi, ko'ylagini yechib, unga berdi; va u uni qo'ygandan so'ng, dedi: "Keling, hazrat, omborxonaga kiraylik, chunki u yerga hech kim kelmaydi." Va shunday qilishdi.

en: There the priest gave her the heartiest busses in the world and making her sib to God Almighty,372 solaced himself with her a great while; after which he took leave of her and returned to the parsonage in his cas- sock, as it were he came from ofﬁciating at a wedding.
uz: U yerda ruhoniy unga dunyodagi eng issiq avtobuslarni berdi va uni Qodir Tangriga yaqinlashtirdi. 372 U bilan uzoq vaqt tasalli berdi; shundan so'ng u bilan xayrlashdi va go'yo to'yda xizmatdan kelganidek, paypoq kiygan ruhoniyga qaytdi.

en: There, bethinking himself that all the candle-ends he got by way of offer- tory in all the year were not worth the half of ﬁve crowns, himseemed he had done ill and repenting him of having left the cloak, he fell to consider- ing how he might have it again without cost.
uz: U yerda, butun yil davomida sovg'a sifatida olgan barcha sham uchlari besh kronning yarmiga arzimaydi deb o'ylab, xuddi yomonlik qilgan va palto tashlab ketganidan pushaymon bo'lgandek, u uni qanday qilib bepulga qaytarib olishni o'ylab qoldi.

en: Being shrewd enough in a small way, he soon hit upon a device and it succeeded to his wish; for that on the morrow, it being a holiday, he sent a neighbour’s lad of his to Mis- tress Belcolore’s house, with a message praying her be pleased to lend him her stone mortar, for that Binguccio dal Poggio and Nuto Buglietti were to dine with him that morning and he had a mind to make sauce.
uz: Kichkina darajada aqlli bo'lgani uchun, u tez orada bir qurilmaga duch keldi va bu uning orzusi amalga oshdi; chunki ertaga, bayram bo'lgani uchun, u qo'shnining bir yigitni Mis-tress Belcolorening uyiga yubordi, unga toshdan yasalgan ohak berishni so'rab xabar berdi, chunki Binguccio dal Poggio va Nuto Buglietti o'sha kuni ertalab u bilan ovqatlanishlari kerak edi va u sous tayyorlashni o'ylab edi.

en: She sent it to him and towards dinnertime, the priest, having spied out when Bentivegna and his wife were at meat together, called his clerk and said to him, ‘Carry this mortar back to Belcolore and say to her, “His reverence biddeth you gramercy and prayeth you send him back the cloak that the boy left you by way of token.” ’ The clerk accordingly repaired to her house and there, ﬁnd- ing her at table with Bentivegna, set down the mortar and did the priest’s errand.
uz: U uni unga yubordi va kechki ovqatga yaqin ruhoniy, Bentivegna va uning xotini birga ovqatlanayotganda, uning xizmatchisini chaqirib, unga dedi: Bu gʻaltakni Belcolorga qaytarib olib bor va unga ayt: Uning hurmatli xodimi senga gʻamxoʻrlik qilishni buyuradi va undan oʻgʻil senga belgi sifatida qoldirgan koʻylakni qaytarishni soʻraydi.  Ruhoniy shunga koʻra uning uyiga qaytdi va u yerda uni Bentivegna bilan stol ustida topdi, gʻaltakni qoʻydi va ruhoniy topshirigʻini bajardi.

en: Belcolore, hearing require the cloak again, would have answered;
uz: Belcolore, eshitish yana xalatni talab qiladi, javob bergan bo'lardi;

en: but her husband said, with an angry air, ‘Takest thou a pledge of his rever- ence?
uz: Lekin eri g'azablangan holda dedi: Sen uning hurmatini qasam ichdingmi?

en: I vow to Christ, I have a mind to give thee a good clout over the head!
uz: Masihga qasam ichaman, senga boshingni yaxshilab o'rashni o'ylayman!

en: Go, give it quickly back to him, pox take thee!
uz: Bor, uni tezda unga qaytarib ber, o'zingni olib ket!

en: And in future, let him ask what he will of ours, (ay, though he should seek our ass), look that it be not denied him.’ Belcolore rose, grumbling, and pulling the cloak out of the chest, gave it to the clerk, saying, ‘Tell his reverence from me, Belcolore saith, she voweth to God you shall never again pound sauce in her mortar; you have done her no such ﬁne honour of this bout.’ The clerk made off with the cloak and did her message to the priest, who said, laughing, ‘Tell her, when thou seest her, that, an she will not lend me her mortar, I will not lend her my pestle; and so we shall be quits.’ Bentive- gna concluded that his wife had said this, because he had chidden her, and took no heed thereof; but Belcolore bore the priest a grudge and held him at arm’s length till vintage-time; when, he having threatened to cause her go into the mouth of Lucifer the great devil, for very fear she
uz: Va kelajakda, u bizdan nimani xohlashini so'rasin, (ey, u bizning eshakimizni qidirishi kerak bo'lsa ham), shunda u rad etilmasin." Belcolore ro'za, g'azablanib, ko'kragidan ko'ylakni tortib olib, kotibga berdi va dedi: "Menga hurmatingizni ayting, Belcolor aytadi, u Xudoga qasam ichadi, hech qachon o'z ohakida sous urmaysiz; siz unga bunday yaxshilik qilmadingiz." Kotib ko'ylagini olib, ruhoniyga xabar berdi. Ruhoniy kuldi: "Uni ko'rganingda, u menga o'z ohakini bermaydi, men unga o'z qo'zg'amini bermayman; va shunday qilib, biz ketamiz." Bentive-g'na uning xotiniga bu ishdan hech qanday nafrat ko'rsatmadi, chunki u uni juda uzoq vaqt davomida ushlab turdi, lekin u uni ko'p vaqt davomida qo'l bilan olib,

en: made her peace with him over must and roast chestnuts and they after made merry together time and again.
uz: U bilan must va qovurilgan kashtanlar ustida tinchlik o'rnatdi va ular keyin qayta-qayta birga xursandchilik qilishdi.

en: In lieu of the ﬁve crowns, the priest let put new parchment to her tabret and string thereto a cast of hawk’s bells, and with this she was fain to be content.”
uz: Besh toj o'rniga ruhoniy uning tabrisiga yangi pergament qo'ydi va unga xo'roz qo'ng'iroqlarini bog'ladi, va bu bilan u qoniqdi.

en: THE THIRD STORY Calandrino, Bruno and Buffalmacco go coasting along the Mugnone in search of the heliotrope and Calandrino thinketh to have found it.
uz: UCHINCHI HIKOYA Kalandrino, Bruno va Buffalmacco gelyotropni qidirib Mugnona bo'ylab sayohatga ketishadi va Kalandrino uni topgan deb o'ylaydi.

en: Accordingly he returneth home, laden with stones, and his wife chideth him; whereupon, ﬂying out into a rage, he beateth her and recounteth to his companions that which they know better than he.
uz: Shunday qilib, u uyga qaytadi, toshlar bilan to'ldirilgan, va xotini uni ta'qib qiladi; shundan so'ng, g'azabga to'lib, uni urib, o'z sheriklariga o'zidan yaxshiroq bilganlarini aytadi.

en: Pamﬁlo having made an end of his story, at which the ladies had laughed so much that they laugh yet, the queen bade Elisa follow on, who, still laugh- ing, began, “I know not, charming ladies, if with a little story of mine, no less true than pleasant, I shall succeed in making you laugh as much as Pamﬁlo hath done with his; but I will do my endeavor thereof.
uz: Pamfilo o'z hikoyasini tugatdi, unga qarab xonimlar juda ko'p kulardi, lekin ular hali ham kulishardi. Shunda qirolicha Elisa uning orqasidan borishni buyurdi. U hali ham kuldi va boshladi: "Bilmayman, yoqimli xonimlar, agar mening kichik hikoyamiz, yoqimli bo'lishidan kam bo'lmasa, sizni Pamfilo o'zining bilan qilganidek kuldirishga muvaffaq bo'laman; lekin men bunga harakat qilaman."

en: In our city, then, which hath ever abounded in various fashions and strange folk, there was once, no great while since, a painter called Calandrino, a simple-witted man and of strange usances.
uz: Bizning shaharimizda, u doimo turli xil moda va g'alati xalqlarga boy bo'lgan edi, bir vaqtlar, undan beri buyuk bo'lmagan paytlarda, Calandrino deb nomlangan rassom, oddiy va g'alati odatlarga ega odam bor edi.

en: He companied most of his time with other two painters, called the one Bruno and the other Buffalmacco, both very merry men, but otherwise well-advised and shrewd, who consorted with Calandrino for that they ofttimes had great diversion of his fashions and his simplicity.
uz: U o'z vaqtining ko'p qismini boshqa ikki rassom bilan birga o'tkazgan, biri Bruno, ikkinchisi Buffalmacco deb atalgan, ikkalasi ham juda xursand odamlar, lekin boshqacha qilib aytganda, yaxshi maslahatli va aqlli odamlar edi. Ular Calandrino bilan hamkorlik qilishardi, chunki ular ko'pincha uning modalari va soddaligidan katta chalg'ishardi.

en: There was then also in Florence a young man of a mighty pleasant humor and marvellously adroit in all he had a mind to do, astute and plausible, who was called Maso del Saggio, and who, hearing certain traits of Calandrino’s simplicity, determined to amuse him- self at his expense by putting off some cheat on him or causing him believe some strange thing.
uz: O'shanda Florensiyada qudratli, yoqimli hazilga ega va har bir ishida ajoyib darajada mohir bo'lgan bir yigit ham bor edi. U Maso del Saggio deb atalgan edi va u, Calandrino'ning soddaligining ba'zi xususiyatlarini eshitib, uni o'z hisobidan o'ziga yoqtirishga qaror qildi, unga biror firibgarlik qilib qo'yish yoki uni g'alati narsaga ishontirish orqali.

en: He chanced one day to come upon him in the church of San Giovanni and seeing him intent upon the carved work and paintings of the pyx, which is upon the altar of the said church and which had then not long been placed there, he judged the place and time opportune for carrying his intent into execution.
uz: U bir kuni San-Giannining cherkovida unga duch kelishga va uni o'sha cherkovning qurbongohida o'yilgan pyxning o'yilgan asari va rasmlarini ko'rishga muvaffaq bo'ldi. U o'sha cherkovda uzoq vaqt o'tmay qo'yilgan edi va u o'z niyatini amalga oshirish uchun qulay joy va vaqt deb hisobladi.

en: Accordingly, acquainting a friend of his with that
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uning do'stini shu bilan tanishtirish.

en: which he purposed to do, they both drew near unto the place where Calandrino sat alone and feigning not to see him, fell a-discoursing together of the virtues of divers stones, whereof Maso spoke as authoritatively as if he had been a great and famous lapidary.
uz: U nima qilishni niyat qilgan bo'lsa, ikkalasi ham Kalandrino yolg'iz o'tirgan joyga yaqinlashdilar va uni ko'rmaslikka o'xshatib, turli xil toshlarning fazilatlarini birgalikda muhokama qilib, Maso haqida xuddi buyuk va mashhur toshbo'ron bo'lgandek ishonchli gapirdilar.

en: Calandrino gave ear to their talk and presently, seeing that it was no secret, he rose to his feet and joined himself to them, to the no small satis- faction of Maso, who, pursuing his discourse, was asked by Calandrino where these wonder-working stones were to be found.
uz: Kalandrino ularning gaplariga quloq solib, bu sir emasligini ko'rib, o'rnidan turdi va ularga qo'shildi. Maso'ning ozgina bo'lmagan qoniqish guruhiga, uning nutqini davom ettirib, Kalandrino tomonidan bu mo'jizaviy toshlarni qayerdan topish mumkinligi so'raldi.

en: Maso replied that the most of them were found in Berlinzone, a city of the Basques, in a country called Bengodi,373 where the vines are tied up with sausages and a goose is to be had for a farthing374 and a gosling into the bargain, and that there was a mountain all of grated Parmesan cheese, whereon abode folk who did nothing but make maccaroni and ravioli375 and cook them in capon-broth, after which they threw them down thence and whoso got most thereof had most; and that hard by ran a rivulet of vernage,376 the best ever was drunk, without a drop of water therein.
uz: Maso javob berdi, ularning aksariyati Berlin zonasida, Basklar shahri, Bengodi deb nomlangan mamlakatda topilgan,373 u yerda uzumlar kolbasalar bilan bog'langan va g'oz sotib olish uchun farthing374 va g'o'la savdosiga qo'yiladi, va u yerda butunlay qirg'ichli Parmesan pishlog'i tog'i bor edi, unda makaron va ravioli375 tayyorlashdan boshqa hech narsa qilmaydigan odamlar yashardi va ularni kapon-brunada pishirishardi, keyin ularni u yerdan uloqtirishardi va ulardan ko'pini olganlar ko'proq olardi; va bu yerda qattiq yugurib, Vernage daryosi,376 eng yaxshisi ichilgan, u yerda bir tomchi suvsiz edi.

en: ‘Marry,’ cried Calandrino, ‘that were a ﬁne country; but tell me, what is done with the capons that they boil for broth?’ Quoth Maso, ‘The Basques eat them all.’ Then said Calandrino, ‘Wast thou ever there?’ ‘Was I ever there, quotha!’ replied Maso.
uz: Turmush qur,  deb baqirdi Kalandrino,  bu yaxshi yurt edi; lekin ayting-chi, bulyon qaynatadigan qalpoqlar bilan nima qilinadi? Quoth Maso, Basklar ularni hammasini yeydi. Shunda Kalandrino dedi: Sen u yerga borganmisan? Men u yerga borganmidim, qissa! javob berdi Maso.

en: ‘If I have been there once I have been there a thousand times.’ ‘And how many miles is it distant hence?’ asked Calandrino; and Maso, ‘How many?
uz: Agar men u yerda bir marta bo'lgan bo'lsam, ming marta bo'lganman. Va u yerdan necha mil uzoqlikda? deb so'radi Kalandrino; va Maso: Qancha?

en: a million or more; you might count them all night and not know.’ ‘Then,’ said Calandrino, ‘it must be farther off than the Abruzzi?’ ‘Ay, indeed,’ answered Maso; ‘it is a triﬂe farther.’ Calandrino, like a simpleton as he was, hearing Maso tell all this with an assured air and without laughing, gave such credence thereto as can be giv- en to whatsoever verity is most manifest and so, holding it for truth, said, ‘That is overfar for my money; though, were it nearer, I tell thee aright I would go thither with thee once upon a time, if but to see the maccaroni come tumbling headlong down and take my ﬁll thereof.
uz: million yoki undan ko'proq; ularni butun tun davomida sanashingiz mumkin va bilmasligingiz mumkin.  Unda,  dedi Kalandrino,  u Abruzzilardan ham uzoqroq bo'lishi kerakmi?  Ha, ha,  javob berdi Maso;  bu biroz uzoqroq.  Kalandrino, xuddi ahmoqdek, Maso bularning hammasini ishonch bilan va kulmasdan aytib berganini eshitib, haqiqat eng ko'rinib turgan narsaga shunday ishonch bildirdi va shunday qilib, uni haqiqat deb hisoblab, dedi:  Bu mening pulim uchun juda katta; lekin, agar yaqinroq bo'lsa, senga aytaman, bir marta u yerga sen bilan borardim, lekin agar makaronlar to'lib-to'lib kelganini ko'rsam, boshimni olib tashlardim.

en: But tell me, God keep thee merry, is there none of those wonder-working stones to be found in these parts?’ ‘Ay is there,’ answered Maso; ‘there be two kinds of stones of very great virtue found here; the ﬁrst are the grits of Settignano and Montisci, by virtue whereof, when they are wrought into millstones, ﬂour is made; wherefore it is said in those parts that grace cometh from God and millstones from Montisci; but there is such great plenty of these grits that they are as little prized with us as emeralds with the folk over yonder, where
uz: Lekin menga ayting, Xudo sizni xursand qilsin, bu joylarda o'sha mo'jizaviy toshlar topilmaydimi? Ay, u yerda bor,  javob berdi Maso; bu yerda juda buyuk fazilatga ega ikki xil tosh bor; birinchisi Settignano va Montisci toshlari, ular tegirmon toshlariga aylantirilganda, un hosil bo'ladi; shuning uchun u joylarda Xudo tomonidan va Montisci toshlaridan keladigan inoyat, deb aytiladi; lekin bu toshlarning shunchalik ko'pki, ular biz bilan xuddi u yerdagi odamlar bilan zumrad kabi qadrlanmaydi,

en: they have mountains of them bigger than Mount Morello, which shine in the middle of the night, I warrant thee.
uz: Ularning Morello tog'idan ham kattaroq tog'lari bor, ular tun o'rtasida porlaydi, senga kafolat beraman.

en: And thou must know that whoso should cause set ﬁne and perfect millstones, before they are pierced, in rings and carry them to the Soldan might have for them what he would.
uz: Va shuni bilginki, kim nozik va mukammal tegirmon toshlarini teshishdan oldin halqalarga o'rnatib, Soldanga olib borsa, u uchun nima xohlasa, o'sha bo'ladi.

en: The other is what we lapidaries call Heliotrope, a stone of exceeding great vir- tue, for that whoso hath it about him is not seen of any other person where- as he is not, what while he holdeth it.’ Quoth Calandrino, ‘These be indeed great virtues; but where is this second stone found?’ To which Maso replied that it was commonly found in the Mugnone.
uz: Boshqasi biz toshbo'ronlar Heliotrope deb ataydigan narsa, juda buyuk vir- tua toshi, chunki uning atrofida bo'lgan narsa boshqa hech kimda ko'rinmaydi - u bo'lmaganidek, u uni ushlab turganda nima bo'lardi." Kalandrino ta'kidladi: "Bular haqiqatan ham buyuk fazilatlar; lekin bu ikkinchi tosh qayerda topilgan?" Maso unga javob berdi: "U odatda Mugnonda topiladi."

en: ‘What bigness is this stone,’ asked Calandrino, ‘and what is its colour?’ Quoth Maso, ‘It is of various sizes, some more and some less; but all are well nigh black of colour.’ Calandrino noted all this in himself and feigning to have otherwhat to do, took leave of Maso, inwardly determined to go seek the stone in question, but bethought himself not to do it without the knowledge of Bruno and Buffalmacco, whom he most particularly affected.
uz: Bu tosh qanday kattalik,  deb so'radi Kalandrino,  va uning rangi nima?  Masodan so'radi:  U turli o'lchamlarda, ba'zilari ko'proq va ba'zilari kamroq; lekin hammasi deyarli qora rangda.  Kalandrino bularning barchasini o'zida qayd etdi va boshqa narsa qilishga o'xshatib, Maso'dan ketdi, ich-ichidan so'ralgan toshni qidirishga qaror qildi, lekin o'zini Bruno va Buffalmacco'dan xabardor bo'lmasdan buni qilmaslikka o'yladi, ularni ayniqsa ta'sirladi.

en: Accordingly he ad- dressed himself to seek for them, so they might, without delay and before any else, set about the search, and spent all the rest of the morning seeking them.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u ularni qidirish uchun o'zini kiyintirdi, shunda ular kechikmasdan va boshqa hech kimdan oldin qidiruvga otlanishlari va butun ertalab ularni qidirishardi.

en: At last, when it was past none, he remembered him that they were awork in the Ladies’ Convent at Faenza and leaving all his other business, he betook himself thither well nigh at a run, notwithstanding the great heat.
uz: Nihoyat, hech narsa o'tmaganda, u Faenza shahridagi Ayollar monastirida ishlamayotganlarini esladi va boshqa barcha ishlarini tashlab, katta issiqlikka qaramay, u yerga yaqinroq yugurib bordi.

en: As soon as he saw them, he called them and bespoke them thus: ‘Comrades, an you will hearken to me, we may become the richest men in all Florence, for that I have learned from a man worthy of belief that in the Mugnone is to be found a stone, which whoso carrieth about him is not seen of any; wherefore meseemeth we were best go thither in quest thereof without delay, ere any forestall us.
uz: Ularni ko'rishi bilanoq, ularni chaqirib, shunday dedi: "O'rtoqlar, menga quloq solinglar, biz butun Florensiyadagi eng boy odamlarga aylanishimiz mumkin, chunki men Mugnonda tosh topiladi, uni tashayotgan odam hech kim ko'rmaydi, degan ishonchga loyiq odamdan o'rgandim; shuning uchun hech kim bizni to'xtatmasdan, uni qidirib borganimiz ma'qul edi."

en: We shall certainly ﬁnd it, for that I know it well, and when we have gotten it, what have we to do but put it in our poke and getting us to the moneychangers’ tables, which you know stand still laden with groats and ﬂorins, take as much as we will thereof?
uz: Biz uni albatta topamiz, chunki men buni yaxshi bilaman va uni olganimizdan so'ng, uni cho'ntagimizga solib, pul almashtiruvchilarning stollariga olib borishdan boshqa nima qilishimiz kerak, ular siz bilasiz, go'sht va gullar bilan to'la, undan xohlagancha olamiz?

en: None will see us, and so may we grow rich of a sudden, without having to smear walls all day long, snail-fashion.’ Bruno and Buffalmacco, hearing this, fell a-laughing in their sleeves and eyeing each other askance, made a show of exceeding wonderment and praised Calandrino’s counsel, but Bruno asked how the stone in question was called.
uz: Hech kim bizni ko'rmaydi va shunday qilib, birdan boyib ketishimiz mumkin, butun kun davomida devorlarga surtmasdan, salyangoz-mode. Buni eshitgan Bruno va Buffalmacco yenglariga kulishib, bir-birlariga qichqirib qarashdi, nihoyatda hayratda bo'lishdi va Kalandrino'ning maslahatini maqtashdi, lekin Bruno so'radi: "Bu tosh qanday atalgan?"

en: Calandrino, who was a clod-pated fellow, had already forgotten the name, wherefore quoth he, ‘What have we to do with the name, since we know the virtue of the stone?
uz: Kalandrino, qovurg'ali yigit bo'lgan, ismni allaqachon unutib qo'ygan edi, shuning uchun u dedi: Toshning fazilatini bilganimiz uchun, bu ismga nima aloqamiz bor?

en: Meseemeth we were best go about the
uz: Mayli, biz eng yaxshisi bu haqda gapirishimiz kerak edi.

en: quest without more ado.’ ‘Well, then,’ said Bruno, ‘how is it fashioned?’ ‘It is of all fashions,’ replied Calandrino; ‘but all are well nigh black; where- fore meseemeth that what we have to do is to gather up all the black stones we see, till we happen upon the right.
uz: "Endi hech qanday tashvishlanmasdan."  Xo'sh, unda,  dedi Bruno,  qanday qilib yasalgan?  Bu barcha modalardan,  javob berdi Kalandrino;  lekin hammasi yaxshi, qoraga yaqin; qayerdan  oldindan shuni ko'ryapmizki, biz ko'radigan barcha qora toshlarni to'plashimiz kerak, toki o'ng tomonda bo'lguncha."

en: So let us lose no time, but get us gone.’ Quoth Bruno, ‘Wait awhile,’ and turning to his comrade, said, ‘Me- thinketh Calandrino saith well; but meseemeth this is no season for the search, for that the sun is high and shineth full upon the Mugnone, where it hath dried all the stones, so that certain of those that be there appear presently white, which of a morning, ere the sun have dried them, show black; more by token that, today being a working day, there be many folk, on one occasion or another abroad along the banks, who, seeing us, may guess what we are about and maybe do likewise, whereby the stone may come to their hands and we shall have lost the trot for the amble.
uz: Shunday ekan, vaqtni yo'qotmaylik, lekin ketaylik." Qoth Bruno, "Bir oz kuting," dedi va o'z safdoshiga o'girilib, dedi: "Men- Calandrino yaxshi deydi; lekin bu qidiruv uchun mavsum emas, chunki quyosh baland va to'la Mugnone ustida porlaydi, u yerda barcha toshlarni quritdi, shuning uchun u yerda bo'lgan ba'zilar hozir oq ko'rinadi, quyosh quritmasdan oldin, qora ko'rinadi; yana shuni aytish kerakki, bugun ish kuni bo'lganda, qirg'oq bo'ylab bir necha odamlar bor, bizni ko'rib, nima ekanligimizni taxmin qilishlari mumkin va ehtimol shunday qilishlari mumkin, shu orqali tosh ularning qo'llariga kelishi mumkin va biz uchun yo'qotamiz.

en: Me- seemeth (an you be of the same way of thinking) that this is a business to be undertaken of a morning, whenas the black may be the better known from the white, and of a holiday, when there will be none there to see us.’ Buffalmacco commended Bruno’s counsel and Calandrino fell in there- with; wherefore they agreed to go seek for the stone all three on the follow- ing Sunday morning, and Calandrino besought them over all else not to say a word of the matter to anyone alive, for that it had been imparted to him in conﬁdence, and after told them that which he had heard tell of the land of Bengodi, afﬁrming with an oath that it was as he said.
uz: Menimcha (siz ham xuddi shunday fikrda bo'lsangiz), bu ertalabki ish bo'lib, qora tanli oq tanlilardan ko'ra yaxshiroq tanilishi mumkin, va bizni ko'rish uchun u yerda hech kim bo'lmaydigan bayramdir. Buffalmacco Brunoning maslahatini maqtadi va Kalandrino u yerga tushdi; shuning uchun ular uchalasi ham keyingi yakshanba kuni ertalab toshni qidirishga kelishdi va Kalandrino ulardan hech kimga bu haqda hech narsa demaslikni iltimos qildi, chunki bu narsa unga ishonch bilan yetkazilgan edi va ularga Bengodi yeridan eshitganlarini aytib, u aytganidek edi.

en: As soon as he had taken his leave, the two others agreed with each other what they should do in the matter and Calandrino impatiently awaited the Sunday morning, which being come, he arose at break of day and called his friends, with whom he sallied forth of the city by the San Gallo gate and descending into the bed of the Mugnone, began to go searching down stream for the stone.
uz: U ketishi bilanoq, qolgan ikki kishi bu masalada nima qilish kerakligini bir-birlari bilan kelishib olishdi va Kalandrino yakshanba kuni ertalabni sabrsizlik bilan kutdi. U tong otishida turib, do'stlarini chaqirib oldi. Ular bilan birga u San-Gallo darvozasi bo'ylab shahardan chiqib, Mugnonening to'riga tushdi va daryo bo'ylab tosh qidirishni boshladi.

en: Calandrino, as the eagerest of the three, went on before, skipping nimbly hither and thither, and whenever he espied any black stone, he pounced upon it and picking it up, thrust it into his bosom.
uz: Kalandrino, uchovchisidan eng ishtiyoqiysi bo'lgan holda, oldinga o'tib, bu yoqqa va bu yoqqa chaqqonlik bilan sakrab yurardi va har safar qora toshni ko'rganida, unga sakrab, uni o'z bag'riga tiqardi.

en: His comrades followed after him picking up now one stone and now another; but Calandrino had not gone far before he had his bosom full of stones; wherefore, gathering up the skirts of his grown, which was not cut Flanders fashion,377 he tucked them well into his surcingle all round and made an ample lap thereof.
uz: Uning safdoshlari uning orqasidan bir toshni, keyin boshqa toshni olib yurishdi; lekin Kalandrino ko'kragini toshlarga to'ldirishidan oldin uzoqqa bormagan edi; shuning uchun, Flanders uslubida kesilmagan o'sgan yubkalarini yig'ib, 377 ularni butun atrofida o'zining aylanasiga yaxshilab joylashtirdi va keng aylantirdi.

en: How- ever, it was no great while ere he had ﬁlled it, and making a lap on like wise of his mantle, soon ﬁlled this also with stones.
uz: Qanday bo'lmasin, u uni to'ldirmaguncha unchalik zo'r emas edi, va o'zining donoligiga o'xshab, tez orada buni ham toshlar bilan to'ldirdi.

en: Presently, the two others see- ing that he had gotten his load and that dinnertime drew nigh, quoth Bruno
uz: Hozirda qolgan ikkalasi ham yukni olganini va kechki ovqat vaqti yaqinlashayotganini ko'rishmoqda, dedi Bruno.

en: to Buffalmacco, in accordance with the plan concerted between them, ‘Where is Calandrino?’ Buffalmacco, who saw him hard by, turned about and looking now here and now there, answered, ‘I know not; but he was be- fore us but now.’ ‘But now, quotha!’ cried Bruno.
uz: Buffalmaccoga, ular o'rtasida kelishilgan rejaga muvofiq, Calandrino qayerda? Buffalmacco, uni qattiq ko'rib, o'girilib, hozir u yerga qaragan holda, javob berdi: Men bilmayman; lekin u oldinda edi, lekin hozir. Endi, qacha! deb baqirdi Bruno.

en: ‘I warrant you he is presently at home at dinner and hath left us to play the fool here, seeking black stones down the Mugnone.’ ‘Egad,’ rejoined Buffalmacco ‘he hath done well to make mock of us and leave us here, since we were fools enough to credit him.
uz: Sizga kafolat beraman, u hozir uyda kechki ovqatda va bizni bu yerda ahmoqona o'ynashga, Mugnone bo'ylab qora toshlarni qidirishga tashlab ketdi. Egad,  deb javob berdi Buffalmacco  u bizni masxara qilib, bizni bu yerda qoldirgani yaxshi, chunki biz unga ishonish uchun yetarli ahmoq edik.

en: Marry, who but we had been simple enough to believe that a stone of such virtue was to be found in the Mugnone?’ Calandrino, hearing this, concluded that the heliotrope had fallen into his hands and that by virtue thereof they saw him not, albeit he was present with them, and rejoiced beyond measure at such a piece of good luck, answered them not a word, but determined to return; wherefore, turning back, he set off homeward.
uz: Uylang, bizdan boshqa kim bunday fazilatli tosh Mugnonda topilishiga ishonish uchun shunchalik sodda edi? Buni eshitgan Kalandrino, heliotrop uning qo'liga tushganini va shu sababli uni ko'rmaganini, garchi u ular bilan birga bo'lsa ham, cheksiz xursand bo'lganini, ularga bir so'z ham javob bermaganini, balki qaytishga qaror qilganini xulosa qildi; shuning uchun, orqaga o'girilib, uyiga yo'l oldi.

en: Buffalmacco, seeing this, said to Bruno, ‘What shall we do?
uz: Buffalmacco buni ko'rib, Brunoga dedi: Nima qilaylik?

en: Why do we not get us gone?’ Whereto Bruno answered, ‘Let us begone; but I vow to God that Calandrino shall never again serve me thus, and were I presently near him as I have been all the morning, I would give him such a clout on the shins with this stone that he should have cause to remember this trick for maybe a month to come.’ To say this and to let ﬂy at Calandrino’s shins with the stone were one and the same thing; and the latter, feeling the pain, lifted up his leg and began to puff and blow, but yet held his peace and fared on.
uz: Nima uchun ketmaymiz? Shunda Bruno javob berdi: Keling, boshlaylik; lekin men Xudoga qasam ichamanki, Kalandrino menga hech qachon bunday xizmat qilmaydi. Agar men u bilan ertalab bo'lganimdek yaqin bo'lsam, unga shu tosh bilan shunday ta'sir ko'rsatardimki, u bu hiylani bir oy davomida eslab qolishi kerak edi. Buni aytish va Kalandrino'ning tosh bilan ta'sir ko'rsatishi bir xil edi; va oxirgi, og'riqni his qilib, oyog'ini ko'tardi va puflay boshladi, lekin shunga qaramay, tinch qoldi va davom etdi.

en: Presently Buffalmacco took one of the ﬂints he had picked up and said to Bruno, ‘Look at this ﬁne ﬂint; here should go for Calandrino’s loins!’ So saying, he let ﬂy and dealt him a sore rap in the small of the back with the stone.
uz: Ayni paytda Buffalmacco o'zi olib qo'ygan tikanlardan birini olib, Brunoga dedi: "Mana shu mayda tikanni; mana Calandrino'ning belini oling!" Shunday qilib, u uchib ketdi va unga orqa tomondan tosh bilan og'riqli zarba berdi.

en: Brief, on this wise, now with one word and now with another, they went pelting him up the Mugnone till they came to the San Gallo gate, where they threw down the stones they had gathered and halted awhile at the custom house.
uz: Xullas, shu ma'noda, endi bir so'z bilan, endi boshqa so'z bilan, ular uni Mugnone'ga urib, San Gallo darvozasiga yetib kelishdi, u yerda yig'ilgan toshlarni tashlab, bojxona uyida biroz to'xtashdi.

en: The ofﬁcers, forewarned by them, feigned not to see Calandrino and let him pass, laughing heartily at the jest, whilst he, without stopping, made straight for his house, which was near the Canto alla Macina, and fortune so far favoured the cheat that none accosted him, as he came up the stream and after through the city, as, indeed, he met with few, for that well nigh every- one was at dinner.
uz: Ofitserlar oldindan ogohlantirilgan holda, Calandrino'ni ko'rmaslikka va uni o'tkazib yuborishga harakat qilishdi, hazilga dildan kulishardi, u esa to'xtamasdan to'g'ri o'z uyiga yo'l oldi, u Canto alla Macina yaqinida edi va omad shu paytgacha hech kim uni yaqinlashtirmaydigan hiylaga yo'l qo'yardi, chunki u daryo bo'ylab va keyin shahar bo'ylab kelardi, chunki u deyarli har bir kishi kechki ovqatda edi.

en: Accordingly, he reached his house, thus laden, and as chance would have it, his wife, a fair and virtuous lady, by name Mistress Tessa, was at the stairhead.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u uyiga yetib keldi, shunday yuklangan edi va tasodifan, uning xotini, go'zal va fazilatli xonim, ismi Mistress Tessa edi, zinapoyada edi.

en: Seeing him come and somewhat provoked at his long tarriance, she began to rail at him, saying, ‘Devil take the man!
uz: Uning kelishini ko'rib, uzoq muddatga qotib qolganidan biroz xafa bo'lib, u unga qarshi g'azablana boshladi va dedi: "Iblis odamni ol!"

en: thou never think to come home betimes?
uz: Hech qachon uyga vaqt o'tishi haqida o'ylamaysanmi?

en: All the folk have already dined whenas thou comest back to dinner.’ Calandrino, hearing this and ﬁnding that he was seen, was overwhelmed with chagrin and vexation and cried out, ‘Alack, wicked woman that thou art, wast thou there?
uz: Hamma odamlar kechki ovqatga qaytganingda allaqachon ovqatlanib bo'lishdi." Buni eshitib va ko'rinib qolganiga ko'ra, Kalandrino xafalik va g'azabdan to'lib-toshdi va qichqirdi: "Alak, yomon ayol, sen u yerda edingmi?"

en: Thou hast un- done me; but, by God His faith, I will pay thee therefor!’ Therewithal he ran up to a little saloon he had and there disburdened himself of the mass of stones he had brought home; then, running in a fury at his wife, he laid hold of her by the hair and throwing her down at his feet, cuffed and kicked her in every part as long as he could wag his arms and legs, without leaving a hair on her head or a bone in her body that was not beaten to a mash, nor did it avail her aught to cry him mercy with clasped hands.
uz: Sen meni qilmading; lekin, Xudoga qasam ichaman, senga buning uchun to'layman! Shundan so'ng u o'zining kichkina salooniga yugurdi va u yerga olib kelgan toshlar to'plamidan xalos bo'ldi; so'ngra, xotiniga g'azablanib, uni sochidan ushladi va oyoqlari ostiga tashladi, uni qo'llari va oyoqlari bilan harakatlantira olguncha har bir qismida qo'lga oldi va tepdi, boshida bir tuk ham qoldirmadi, tanasida birorta ham urilmagan suyak ham qoldirmadi, unga qo'llari bilan rahm-shafqat ko'rsatmadi.

en: Meanwhile Bruno and Buffalmacco, after laughing awhile with the keep- ers of the gate, proceeded with slow step to follow Calandrino afar off and presently coming to the door of his house, heard the cruel beating he was in act to give his wife; whereupon, making a show of having but then come back, they called Calandrino, who came to the window, all asweat and red with anger and vexation, and prayed them come up to him.
uz: Shu bilan birga, Bruno va Buffalmacco darvoza qo'riqchilari bilan biroz kulgandan so'ng, Calandrino orqaga sekin qadam tashlab, yaqin orada uyning eshigiga kelishdi. U o'z xotiniga bergan shafqatsiz kaltakni eshitdi; shundan so'ng, o'zini qaytib kelganini ko'rsatib, derazadan kelgan Calandrinoga, g'azab va g'azabdan terlab, qizarib kelgan holda, ularni oldiga chaqirishdi.

en: Accordingly, they went up, making believe to be somewhat vexed, and seeing the room full of stones and the lady, all torn and dishevelled and black and blue in the face for bruises, weeping piteously in one corner of the room, whilst Calandrino sat in another, untrussed and panting like one forspent, eyed them awhile, then said, ‘What is this, Calandrino?
uz: Shunga ko'ra, ular o'zlarini biroz g'azablangan ko'rsatib, yuqoriga ko'tarilishdi va xonani toshlar bilan to'ldirgan va xonimning butunlay yirtilgan va parchalangan, yuziga ko'k-qora ko'rinishlarni ko'rishdi. Xonaning bir burchagida achinarli yig'layotgan edilar, Kalandrino esa boshqa burchagida o'tirardi, biroz g'amgin va g'amgin bo'lib, ularga tikilib turardi, keyin dedi: "Bu nima, Kalandrino?"

en: Art thou for building, that we see all these stones here?
uz: Siz bu yerda shu toshlarni ko'rayotganimiz uchun qurmoqchimisiz?

en: And Mistress Tessa, what aileth her?
uz: Va Tessa xonim, unga nima bo'ldi?

en: It seemeth thou hast beaten her.
uz: Ko'rinishidan, sen uni uribsan.

en: What is all this ado?’ Calandrino, outwearied with the weight of the stones and the fury with which he had beaten his wife, no less than with chagrin for the luck which himseemed he had lost, could not muster breath to give them aught but broken words in reply; wherefore, as he delayed to answer, Buffalmacco went on, ‘Harkye, Calandrino, whatever other cause for anger thou mightest have had, thou shouldst not have fooled us as thou hast done, in that, after thou hadst car- ried us off to seek with thee for the wonder-working stone, thou leftest us in the Mugnone, like a couple of gulls, and madest off home, without saying so much as God be with you or devil; the which we take exceeding ill; but assuredly this shall be the last trick thou shalt ever play us.’ Therewithal, Calandrino enforcing himself,378 answered, ‘Comrades, be not angered; the case standeth otherwise than as you deem.
uz: Bularning hammasi nima? Kalandrino, toshlarning og'irligi va xotinini urgan g'azabidan charchagan holda, o'zi yo'qotgan deb o'ylagan omadidan xafa bo'lganidan kam bo'lmagani uchun, ularga javob berish uchun faqatgina singan so'zlarni aytishga nafas topa olmadi; shuning uchun, javob berishga kechikkanida, Buffalmacco davom etdi: Harkye, Kalandrino, g'azabga boshqa sababingiz bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, siz bizni xuddi siz qilganingizdek aldamas edingiz kerak edi, chunki siz bizni mo'jizaviy toshni qidirishga majbur qilganingizdan so'ng, siz bizni xuddi bir juft oltin kabi, va eng g'azablangan uyda qoldirdingiz, Xudo siz bilan birga bo'lsa ham, yoki shayton bilan birga bo'lsa ham; lekin siz hech qachon o'zingiz bilan o'ynamaysiz, chunki siz hech qachon...

en: I (unlucky wretch that I am!) had found the stone in question, and you shall hear if I
uz: Men (baxtsiz bechora odam ekanman!) so'ralgan toshni topgan edim, va agar men...

en: When ﬁrst you questioned one another of me, I was less than half a score yards distant from you; but, seeing that you made off and saw me not, I went on before you and came back hither, still keeping a little in front of you.’ Then, beginning from the beginning, he recounted to them all that they had said and done, ﬁrst and last, and showed them how the stones had served his back and shins; after which, ‘And I may tell you,’ continued he, ‘that, whenas I entered in at the gate, with all these stones about me which you see here, there was nothing said to me, albeit you know how vexatious and tiresome these gatekeepers use to be in wanting to see everything; more by token that I met by the way several of my friends and gossips, who are still wont to accost me and invite me to drink; but none of them said a word to me, no, nor half a word, as those who saw me not.
uz: Sizlar bir-biringizdan so'raganingizda, men sizlardan yarim yarddan kamroq uzoqlikda edim; lekin, sizlar ketib, meni ko'rmasligingizni ko'rib, men oldingizdan bordim va shu yerga qaytib keldim, hali biroz oldingizda turib. Keyin, boshidan boshlab, u ularga aytgan va qilgan barcha narsalarini aytib berdi, avvalo va oxirida, va ularga toshlar uning orqasiga qanday xizmat qilganini ko'rsatdi; keyin, "Sizlarga aytaman," dedi u, "Men darvozaga kirganimda, siz ko'rayotgan bu atrofimdagi barcha toshlar bilan, menga hech narsa aytilmadi, garchi siz bu darvozabonlar hamma narsani ko'rishni xohlashda qanchalik g'amgin va zerikarli ekanligini bilasiz; shundan so'ng, men bir nechta do'stlarim bilan uchrashdim va ular meni ichishga taklif qilishadi, lekin ular meni hech kimni ko'rmadilar.

en: At last, being come home hither, this accursed devil of a woman presented herself before me, for that, as you know, women cause everything lose its virtue, wherefore I, who might else have called myself the luckiest man in Florence, am become the most unlucky.
uz: Nihoyat, u yerga qaytib kelganimda, bu la'nati ayolning shaytoni menga ko'rindi, chunki, bilasizki, ayollar hamma narsani o'z fazilatidan mahrum qiladi, shuning uchun men, o'zimni Florensiyadagi eng omadli odam deb atagan bo'lsam ham, eng omadsiz odamga aylandim.

en: For this I have beaten her as long as I could wag my ﬁsts and I know not what hindereth me from slitting her weasand, accursed be the hour when ﬁrst I saw her and when she came to me in this house.’ Then, ﬂaming out into fresh anger, he offered to rise and beat her anew.
uz: Shuning uchun men uni qo'limdan kelguncha urdim va uning o'tlarini kesishga nima to'sqinlik qilayotganini bilmayman, uni birinchi marta ko'rgan vaqtim va bu uyga kelgan vaqtim la'nat bo'lsin. Keyin, yangi g'azabga to'lib, u yana turishni va urishni taklif qildi.

en: Bruno and Buffalmacco, hearing all this, made believe to marvel exceed- ingly and often conﬁrmed that which Calandrino said, albeit they had the while so great a mind to laugh that they were like to burst; but, seeing him start up in a rage to beat his wife again, they rose upon him and withheld him, avouching that the lady was nowise at fault, but that he had only him- self to blame for that which had happened, since he knew that women caused things to lose their virtue and had not bidden her beware of appear- ing before him that day, and that God had bereft him of foresight to provide against this, either for that the adventure was not to be his or because he had had it in mind to cozen his comrades, to whom he should have discovered the matter, as soon as he perceived that he had found the stone.
uz: Bruno va Buffalmacco bularning hammasini eshitib, Calandrino aytgan gapni juda hayratga tushishdi va ko'pincha tasdiqladilar, garchi ularning o'sha paytda shunday katta aql-idroklari bo'lsa ham, kulishga shunchalik tayyor ediki, ular yorilib ketganday edilar; lekin, uni xotini yana urish uchun g'azabda boshlaganini ko'rib, unga qarshi turishdi va ushlab turishdi, xonim hozirda aybdor ekanligini, lekin u sodir bo'lgan voqea uchun faqat o'zini aybdor deb hisoblashdi, chunki u ayollarning o'z fazilatlarini yo'qotishiga sabab bo'lganini va u o'sha kuni unga ko'rinishidan ogoh bo'lishini buyurmaganini, va Xudo unga bu haqda oldindan ko'rish imkoniyatini berganini, yoki sarguzasht uning o'zi uchun emasligini yoki u o'z do'stlarini, unga aniqlaganini anglaganidan keyin,

en: Brief, after many words, they made peace, not without much ado, between him and the woebegone lady and went their ways, leaving him disconsolate, with the house full of stones.”
uz: Qisqacha, ko'p so'zlardan so'ng, ular u bilan g'amgin xonim o'rtasida tinchlik o'rnatishdi, ko'p bekorga emas, va yo'llariga ketishdi, uni xafa qilib, uy toshlarga to'la edi.

en: THE FOURTH STORY The rector of Fiesole loveth a widow lady, but is not loved by her and thinking to lie with her, lieth with a serving-wench of hers, whilst the lady’s brothers cause the bishop ﬁnd him in this case.
uz: TO'RTINCHI HIKOYA Fiesole rektori bir beva xotinni yaxshi ko'radi, lekin uni sevmaydi va u bilan yotishni o'ylaydi, uning xizmatkori bilan yotadi, xotinning akalari esa yepiskopni bu holatda topishiga sabab bo'ladi.

en: Elisa being come to the end of her story, which she had related to the no small pleasure of all the company, the queen turned to Emilia, and signiﬁed to her her wish that she should follow after with her story, whereupon she promptly began thus: “I have not forgotten, noble ladies, that it hath already been shown, in sundry of the foregoing stories, how much we women are exposed to the importunities of the priests and friars and clergy of every kind; but, seeing that so much cannot be said thereof but that yet more will remain to say, I purpose, to boot, to tell you a story of a rector, who, maugre all the world, would e’en have a gentlewoman wish him well,379 whether she would or not; whereupon she, like a very discreet woman as she was, used him as he deserved.
uz: Elisa o'z hikoyasining oxiriga yetib borgach, uni butun kompaniyaning ardoqi bilan bog'lagan edi, qirolicha Emiliyaga o'girilib, unga o'z hikoyasini davom ettirish istagini bildirdi. Shunda u tezda shunday boshladi: Men unutmadim, hurmatli xonimlar, yuqoridagi hikoyalarning turli xillarida biz ayollar ruhoniylar, rohiblar va ruhoniylarning har qanday ahamiyatiga qanchalik duchor ekanligimiz ko'rsatilgan; lekin bu haqda ko'p narsa aytib bo'lmasligini ko'rib, yana aytish kerak bo'ladi, men sizga butun dunyo bo'ylab azob chekkan, unga yaxshilik tilaydigan, 379 ayolning hikoyasini aytmoqchiman, u juda ehtiyotkor edi, u unga munosib edi.

en: As all of you know, Fiesole, whose hill we can see hence, was once a very great and ancient city, nor, albeit it is nowadays all undone, hath it ever ceased to be, as it is yet, the seat of a bishop.
uz: Hammangizga ma'lumki, Fiesole, uning tepaligini shu yerdan ko'rishimiz mumkin, bir vaqtlar juda buyuk va qadimiy shahar bo'lgan, va garchi hozirda butunlay buzib tashlangan bo'lsa ham, u hali ham yepiskopning o'rni bo'lishdan to'xtadi.

en: Near the cathedral church there a widow lady of noble birth, by name Madam Piccarda, had an estate, where, for that she was not overwell to do, she abode the most part of the year in a house of hers that was not very big, and with her, two brothers of hers, very courteous and worthy youths.
uz: Katedral cherkovi yaqinida Madam Piccarda ismli olijanob beva ayolning mulklari bor edi. U yerda u ishdan xavotirda qolmaganligi sababli, yilning ko'p qismini uniki unchalik katta bo'lmagan uyda o'tkazardi va u bilan birga ikki akasi, juda odobli va munosib yoshlar ham bor edi.

en: It chanced that, the lady frequent- ing the cathedral church and being yet very young and fair and agreeable, the rector of the church became so sore enamoured of her that he could think of nothing else, and after awhile, making bold to discover his mind to her, he prayed her accept of his love and love him as he loved her.
uz: Shunday bo'ldiki, xonim sobor cherkoviga tez-tez kirib, hali juda yosh, go'zal va xushmuomala edi, cherkov rektori unga shunchalik oshiq bo'lib qoldi, boshqa hech narsa o'ylay olmadi va bir oz vaqt o'tgach, unga o'z fikrini ochishga jur'at etib, uning muhabbatini qabul qilishini va uni sevgani kabi sevishini so'radi.

en: Now he was already old in years, but very young in wit, malapert and arrogant and
uz: Endi u allaqachon yoshi katta edi, lekin aqli juda yosh edi, zaif va takabbur va...

en: presumptuous in the extreme, with manners and fashions full of conceit and ill grace, and withal so froward and ill-conditioned that there was none who wished him well; and if any had scant regard for him, it was the lady in question, who not only wished him no whit of good, but hated him worse than the megrims; wherefore, like a discreet woman as she was, she answered him, ‘Sir, that you love me should be mighty pleasing to me, who am bound to love you and will gladly do so; but between your love and mine nothing unseemly should ever befall.
uz: O'ta takabbur, odob-axloq va nafosatga to'la, shu qadar takabbur va badjahlki, unga yaxshilik tilaydigan hech kim bo'lmas edi; va agar unga kam e'tibor beradigan odam bo'lsa, bu xonim edi, u nafaqat unga yaxshilik tilardi, balki undan ko'ra yomonroq nafratlanardi; shuning uchun, o'zi qanday bo'lsa, o'zini oqlagan ayol kabi, u unga javob berdi: "Janob, meni sevganingiz menga juda yoqishi kerak, men sizni sevishga majburman va buni xursand bo'laman; lekin sizning muhabbatingiz va mening...

en: You are my spiritual father and a priest and are presently well stricken in years, all which things should make you both modest and chaste; whilst I, on the other hand, am no girl, nor do these amorous toys beseem my present condition, for that I am a widow and you well know what discretion is required in widows; wherefore I pray you hold me excused, for that I shall never love you after the fashion whereof you require me; nor do I wish to be thus loved of you.’ The rector could get of her no other answer for that time, but, nowise daunted or disheartened by the ﬁrst rebuff, solicited her again and again with the most overweening importunity, both by letter and message, nay, even by word of mouth, whenas he saw her come into the church.
uz: Siz mening ma'naviy otam va ruhoniymizsiz va hozirda yillar davomida yaxshi ta'qibga uchragansiz, bularning barchasi sizni ham kamtar va xor qiladi; men esa, boshqa tomondan, qiz emasman, bu ishqiy o'yinchoqlar hozirgi holatimga mos kelmaydi, chunki men beva edim va siz bevalarda qanday ehtiyotkorlik talab qilinishini yaxshi bilasiz; shuning uchun meni kechiring, chunki men sizni hech qachon siz talab qilgan tarzda sevmayman; va men sizdan shunday sevib qolishni xohlamayman.

en: Where- for, herseeming that this was too great and too grievous an annoy, she cast about to rid herself of him after such a fashion as he deserved, since she could no otherwise, but would do nought ere she had taken counsel with her brothers.
uz: Qayerda bo'lsa ham, bu juda katta va juda qayg'uli bir bezovtachiga o'xshatib, u o'zi loyiq bo'lgan uslubda undan qutulishga otlandi, chunki boshqa iloji bo'lmadi, akasi bilan maslahatlashmaguncha hech narsa qilmasdi.

en: Accordingly, she acquainted them with the rector’s behaviour to- wards her and that which she purposed to do, and having therein full license from them, went a few days after to the church, as was her wont.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u ularni rektorning o'ziga nisbatan xatti-harakatlari va o'zi qilmoqchi bo'lgan ish bilan tanishtirdi va ulardan to'liq ruxsat olgan holda, bir necha kundan keyin odatdagidek cherkovga bordi.

en: As soon as the rector saw her, he came up to her and with his usual assurance, accosted her familiarly.
uz: Rektor uni ko'rishi bilanoq, uning oldiga keldi va o'zining odatdagi ishontirishi bilan, uni tanish tarzda yaqinlashtirdi.

en: The lady received him with a cheerful countenance and with- drawing apart with him, after he had said many words to her in his wonted style, she heaved a great sigh and said, ‘Sir, I have heard that there is no fortalice so strong but that, being every day assaulted, it cometh at last to be taken, and this I can very well see to have happened to myself; for that you have so closely beset me with soft words and with one complaisance and another, that you have made me break my resolve, and I am now disposed, since I please you thus, to consent to be yours.’ ‘Gramercy, madam,’ answered the rector, overjoyed, ‘to tell you the truth, I have often wondered how you could hold out so long, considering that never did the like betide me with any woman; nay, I have said whiles, “Were women of silver, they would not be worth a farthing, for that not one of them would stand the
uz: Xonim uni quvnoq yuz bilan kutib oldi va undan uzoqlashdi. U unga o'zining odatdagi uslubida ko'p so'zlaganidan so'ng, u katta xo'rsindi va dedi: "Janob, men eshitdimki, bunchalik kuchli qo'rg'on yo'q, lekin har kuni hujumga uchragan holda, nihoyat tortib olinadi, va men buni o'zim bilan sodir bo'lganini juda yaxshi ko'raman; chunki siz meni shunchalik yumshoq so'zlar va bir murosasizlik va boshqa bir narsa bilan o'rab oldingizki, meni buzib qo'ydingiz, va men endi sizdan iltimos qilaman, sizniki bo'lishga rozilik berishga tayyorman." "Gertsiya, xonim," deb javob berdi rektor xursand bo'lib, "Sizga rostini aytaman, men ko'p marta shunday uzoq vaqt davomida men bilan birga turishga majbur bo'lganingizni, hech kimga aytmagan bo'lmas edi, men ularga ayollar uchun...

en: hammer.” But let that pass for the present.
uz: bolg'a. Lekin hozircha o'tadi.

en: When and where can we be to- gether?’ Whereto quoth the lady, ‘Sweet my lord, as for the when, it may be what time soever most pleaseth us, for that I have no husband to whom it behoveth me render an account of my nights; but for the where I know not how to contrive.’ ‘How?’ cried the priest.
uz: Qachon va qayerda birga bo'lishimiz mumkin? Xonim qayerga murojaat qildi: Mening xo'jayinim, qachon, qachon bizga eng yoqadigan vaqt bo'lishi mumkin, chunki tunlarim haqida hisob berishim kerak bo'lgan erim yo'q; lekin qayerga kelishni bilmayman. Qanday qilib? deb baqirdi ruhoniy.

en: ‘Why, in your house to be sure.’ ‘Sir,’ answered the lady, ‘you know I have two young brothers, who come and go about the house with their companions day and night, and my house is not overbig; wherefore it may not be there, except one chose to abide there mute-fashion, without saying a word or making the least sound, and be in the dark, after the manner of the blind.
uz: Nega, albatta uyingizda bo'lsin. Janob,  javob berdi xonim,  bilasizki, mening ikki yosh aka-ukalarim bor, ular uyga o'z hamrohlari bilan kunduzi va kechasi kelib yurishadi, mening uyim juda katta emas; shuning uchun u yerda bo'lmasligi mumkin, agar biri u yerda bir so'z demasdan yoki hech qanday ovoz chiqarmasdan, zulmatda bo'lishni tanlamasa, ko'rlar kabi.

en: An you be content to do this, it might be, for they meddle not with my bedchamber; but their own is so close to mine that one cannot whisper the least word, without its being heard.’ ‘Madam,’ answered the rector, ‘this shall not hinder us for a night or two, against I bethink me where we may foregather more at ease.’ Quoth she, ‘Sir, let that rest with you; but of one thing I pray you, that this abide secret, so no word be ever known thereof.’ ‘Madam,’ replied he, ‘have no fear for that; but, an it may be, make shift that we shall foregather this even- ing.’ ‘With all my heart,’ said the lady; and appointing him how and when he should come, she took leave of him and returned home.
uz: Agar siz buni qilishga rozi bo'lsangiz, ehtimol, ular mening yotoqxonamga aralashmaydilar; lekin ularning o'zlari mening yotoqxonamga shunchalik yaqinki, uni eshitmasdan turib hech qanday so'zni pichirlay olmaysiz." Xonim,  deb javob berdi rektor, bu bizga bir-ikki kecha xalaqit bermaydi, menimcha, qayerga ko'proq dam olishimiz mumkin. U aytdi: Janob, bu siz bilan qolsin; lekin bir narsani iltimos qilaman, bu sir bo'lsin, shunda bu haqda hech narsa ma'lum bo'lmasin. Xonim,  deb javob berdi u, shundan qo'rqmang; lekin, bo'lishi mumkin, biz bu yerga qaytib kelishimiz kerak. Butun qalbim bilan,  dedi xonim; va uni qanday qilib kelishini tayinlab, u uni uydan olib ketishi kerak edi.

en: Now she had a serving-wench, who was not overyoung, but had the foulest and worst-favoured visnomy was ever seen; for she had a nose ﬂattened sore, a mouth all awry, thick lips and great ill-set teeth; moreover, she inclined to squint, nor was ever without sore eyes, and had a green and yellow complexion, which gave her the air of having passed the summer not at Fiesole, but at Sinigaglia.380 Besides all this, she was hipshot and a thought crooked on the right side.
uz: Endi uning xizmatchi kelini bor edi, u yosh emas edi, lekin eng xunuk va eng yomon yoqtirilgan ko'rinishga ega edi; chunki uning burni tekis, og'zi butunlay noto'g'ri, lablari qalin va katta noto'g'ri tishlari bor edi; bundan tashqari, u ko'z yugurtirishga moyil edi, ko'zlari ham hech qachon og'riqsiz emas edi, va uning yashil va sariq rangi bor edi, bu unga yozni Fiesole'da emas, balki Sinigaglia'da o'tkazgandek tuyuldi. 380 Bundan tashqari, u hipshot va o'ng tomonda egri fikr edi.

en: Her name was Ciuta, but, for that she had such a dog’s visnomy of her own, she was called of everyone Ciutazza;381 and for all she was misshapen of her person, she was not without a spice of roguishness.
uz: Uning ismi Xudo edi, lekin, uning o'ziga xos itning sha'niga ega bo'lgani uchun, uni hamma Xudozza deb atardi; 381 va uning shaxsiyatidan xatosiz bo'lgani uchun ham, u badbo'ylikning ta'midan xoli emas edi.

en: The lady called her and said to her, ‘Harkye, Ciutazza, an thou wilt do me a service this night.
uz: Xonim uni chaqirib, dedi: Harkye, Xudozza, bugun kechasi menga bir ish qilmoqchisan.

en: I will give thee a ﬁne new shift.’ Ciutazza, hearing speak of the shift, answered, ‘Madam, so you give me a shift, I will cast myself into the ﬁre, let alone otherwhat.’ ‘Well, then,’ said her mistress, ‘I would have thee lie tonight with a man in my bed and load him with caresses, but take good care not to say a word, lest thou be heard by my brothers, who, as thou knowest, sleep in the next room; and after I will give thee the shift.’ Quoth Ciutazza, ‘With all my heart.
uz: Sizga yaxshi yangi navbatchilik beraman. Xudozza, navbatchilik haqida gapirganini eshitib, javob berdi: Xonim, agar siz menga navbatchilik bersangiz, men o'zimni olovga tashlayman, boshqa hech narsa yo'q. Xo'sh, unda, dedi xonasi, men sizni bugun kechqurun to'shagimda bir odam bilan yotganingizga va uni erkalashingizga buyurmoqchiman, lekin bir so'z aytmaslikka ehtiyot bo'ling, chunki siz bilganingizdek, keyingi xonada uxlayotgan birodarlarim tomonidan eshitilmaysiz; va keyin men sizga navbatchilik beraman. Xudo aytdi:  Butun qalbim bilan.

en: I will lie with half a dozen men, if need be, let alone one.’ Accordingly, at nightfall, my lord the
uz: Agar kerak bo'lsa, yarim o'n kishi bilan yotaman, bir kishi yo'q. Shunga ko'ra, tun tushganda, xo'jayinim...

en: rector made his appearance, according to agreement, whilst the two young men, by the lady’s appointment, were in their bedchamber and took good care to make themselves heard; wherefore he entered the lady’s chamber in silence and darkness and betook himself, as she had bidden him, straight to the bed, whither on her part came Ciutazza, who had been well lessoned by the lady of that which she had to do.
uz: Rektor kelishuviga ko'ra paydo bo'ldi, ikki yigit esa, xonimning tayinlanishi bilan, o'z yotoqxonasida bo'lishar va o'zlarini eshitishga yaxshi e'tibor berishardi; shuning uchun u xonimning xonasiga jim va zulmatda kirdi va o'zini, u buyurganidek, to'g'ri to'shakka qaradi, u yerda xonim tomonidan nima qilish kerakligi haqida yaxshi o'rgatilgan Ciutazza kelardi.

en: My lord rector, thinking he had his mistress beside him, caught Ciutazza in his arms and fell to kissing her, without saying a word, and she him; whereupon he proceeded to solace himself with her, taking, as he thought, possession of the long-desired good.
uz: Rektor hazratim, uning yonida bekasi bor deb o'ylab, Xudozzani quchoqlariga oldi va hech narsa demasdan uni o'pishga tushdi, u ham uni; shundan so'ng u bilan o'zini ovutishga kirishdi, o'zi o'ylaganidek, uzoq vaqtdan beri orzu qilingan yaxshilikka ega bo'ldi.

en: The lady, having done this, charged her brothers carry the rest of the plot into execution, wherefore, stealing softly out of the chamber, they made for the great square and fortune was more favorable to them than they them- selves asked in that which they had a mind to do, inasmuch as, the heat be- ing great, the bishop had enquired for the two young gentlemen, so he might go a-pleasuring to their house and drink with them.
uz: Xonim shunday qilib, o'z birodarlariga uchastkaning qolgan qismini ijro etishni buyurdi. Shuning uchun, xonadan sekin o'g'irlanib, ular katta maydonni o'zlariga qulayroq qilib qo'yishdi va boylik ularga ulardan ko'ra ko'proq foyda keltirdi - o'zlari nima qilish haqida o'ylashdi, chunki issiqlik juda kuchli edi, yepiskop ikki yosh janobni so'ragan edi, shunda u ularning uyiga borib, ular bilan birga ichishi mumkin edi.

en: But, seeing them coming, he acquainted them with his wish and returned with them to their house, where, entering a cool little courtyard of theirs, in which were many ﬂambeaux alight, he drank with great pleasure of an excellent wine of theirs.
uz: Ammo, ularni kelayotganini ko'rib, u o'z xohishi bilan tanishtirdi va ular bilan ularning uyiga qaytib keldi. U yerda ularning salqin kichik hovlisiga kirib, u yerda ko'plab olov chiroqlari yonardi va ularning ajoyib vinosidan katta zavq bilan ichdi.

en: When he had drunken, the young men said to him, ‘My lord, since you have done us so much favour as to deign to visit this our poor house, whereto we came to invite you, we would have you be pleased to view a small matter with which we would fain show you.’ The bishop answered that he would well; whereupon one of the young men, taking a lighted ﬂam- beau in his hand, made for the chamber where my lord rector lay with Ciutazza, followed by the bishop and all the rest.
uz: U mast bo'lgandan so'ng, yigitlar unga dedilar: "Hazratim, siz bizga shunchalik ko'p marhamat ko'rsatdingizki, sizni taklif qilishga kelgan bechora uyimizga tashrif buyurishga majbur bo'ldingiz, biz sizga ko'rsatmoqchi bo'lgan kichik bir masalani ko'rib, xursand bo'lardik." Yepiskop javob berdi: "Yaxshi bo'lardi; shundan so'ng yigitlardan biri qo'lida olov yoqib, hazratimning rektori Xudozza bilan, keyin yepiskop va qolganlarning hammasi yotgan xonaga yo'l ochdi."

en: The rector, to arrive the quicklier at his journey’s end, had hastened to take horse and had already ridden more than three miles before they came thither; wherefore, being somewhat weary, he had, notwithstanding the heat, fallen asleep with Ciutazza in his arms.
uz: Rektor sayohatining oxirida tezroq yetib borishi uchun otga shoshildi va ular u yerga yetib kelishidan oldin uch mildan ortiq yo'l bosib o'tdi; shuning uchun, biroz charchagan holda, issiqlikka qaramay, Xudozzani qo'llarida ushlab uxlab qoldi.

en: Accordingly, when the young man entered the cham- ber, light in hand, and after him the bishop and all the others, he was shown to the prelate in this plight; whereupon he awoke and seeing the light and the folk about him, was sore abashed and hid his head for fear under the bedclothes.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, yosh yigit qo'lida chiroq bilan kameraga kirgach, undan keyin yepiskop va boshqalarning hammasi uni shu ahvolda ruhoniyga ko'rsatishdi; shundan so'ng u uyg'onib, chiroqni va uning atrofidagi odamlarni ko'rib, og'riqli edi va qo'rquvdan boshini karavot ostiga yashirdi.

en: The bishop gave him a sound rating and made him put out his head and see with whom he had lain; whereupon the rector, understanding the trick that had been played him of the lady, what with this and what with the disgrace himseemed he had gotten, became of a sudden the woefullest man that was aye.
uz: Yepiskop unga ovoz baho berdi va boshini qo'yib, kim bilan yotganini ko'rishga majbur qildi; shundan so'ng rektor xonimning unga o'ynalgan hiylasini, bu bilan nima olganini va u qanday sharmandalikka uchraganini tushunib, birdaniga eng qattiqqo'l odamga aylandi.

en: Then, having, by the bishop’s commandment, reclad him-
uz: Keyin, yepiskopning buyrug'iga ko'ra, uni qayta kiydirib...

en: self, he was despatched to his house under good guard, to suffer sore pen- ance for the sin he had committed.
uz: O'zi, u yaxshi qo'riq ostida o'z uyiga jo'natildi, gunohlari uchun azob chekish uchun.

en: The bishop presently enquiring how it came to pass that he had gone thither to lie with Ciutazza, the young men orderly related everything to him, which having heard, he greatly commen- ded both the lady and her brothers for that, without choosing to imbrue their hands in the blood of a priest, they had entreated him as he deserved.
uz: Yepiskop shu zahotiyoq Xudozza bilan qanday qilib u yerga yotgani haqida so'rayotgan edi, yigitlar unga hamma narsani tartibli tarzda aytib berishdi. Eshitgach, u xonimni ham, uning akalarini ham ruhoniyning qoniga qo'l urishni istamagan holda, unga munosib tarzda yolvorishardi.

en: As for the rector, he caused him bewail his offence forty days’ space; but love and despite made him rue it for more than nine-and-forty,382 more by token that, for a great while after, he could never go abroad but the children would point at him and say, ‘See, there is he who lay with Ciutazza’; the which was so sore an annoy to him that he was like to go mad therefor.
uz: Rektorga kelsak, u qirq kun davomida o'z aybini ko'rsatdi; lekin sevgi va garchi uni to'qqiz qirqdan ortiq vaqtga yo'qotgan bo'lsa ham, 382 yilga ko'proq shuni anglatadiki, ancha vaqtdan keyin u hech qachon chet elga chiqa olmas edi, lekin bolalar unga ishora qilib: "Mana, Xudozzani yotgan odam bor", deyishardi; bu unga shunchalik achinarli ediki, u undan telba bo'lib ketgandek edi.

en: On such wise did the worthy lady rid herself of the importunity of the malapert rect- or and Ciutazza gained the shift and a merry night.”
uz: Shunday qilib, munosib xonim o'zini malakpert to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'yin-kulgidan xalos qildi va Ciutazza navbatchilikni va quvnoq tunni qo'lga kiritdi.

en: THE FIFTH STORY Three young men pull the breeches off a Marchegan judge in Florence, what while he is on the bench, administering justice.
uz: BESHINCHI HIKOYA Uch nafar yigit Florensiyadagi Marchegan sudyasining ichki kiyimini yechdi, u o'rindiqda adolatni amalga oshirayotgan paytda.

en: Emilia having made an end of her story and the widow lady having been commended of all, the queen looked to Filostrato and said, “It is now thy turn to tell.” He answered promptly that he was ready and began, “Delight- some ladies, the mention by Elisa a little before of a certain young man, to wit, Maso del Saggio, hath caused me leave a story I purposed to tell you, so I may relate to you one of him and certain companions of his, which, if (albeit it is nowise unseemly) it offer certain expressions which you think shame to use, is natheless so laughable that I will e’en tell it.
uz: Emiliya o'z hikoyasini tugatdi va beva xonim hammaga maqtovga sazovor bo'ldi. Qirolicha Filostratga qaradi va dedi: "Endi aytish sizning navbatingiz keldi." U tezda tayyor ekanligi haqida javob berdi va boshladi: "Xush kelibsiz, ba'zi xonimlar, Elishaning biroz oldin bir yigit haqida aytgan so'zi, masalan, Maso del Saggio, meni sizga aytmoqchi bo'lgan bir hikoyani qoldirishga majbur qildi, shuning uchun men sizga u va uning ba'zi hamrohlari haqida xabar berishim mumkin, agar u (hozir u noqulay bo'lsa ham) ishlatishga uyat qiladigan ba'zi iboralarni taklif qilsa, lekin u juda kulgili, men uni aytib beraman."

en: As you may all have heard, there come oftentimes to our city governors from the Marches of Ancona, who are commonly mean-spirited folk and so paltry and sordid of life that their every fashion seemeth nought other than a lousy cadger’s trick; and of this innate paltriness and avarice, they bring with them judges and notaries, who seem men taken from the plough-tail or the cobbler’s stall rather than from the schools of law.
uz: Hammangiz eshitganingizdek, ko'pincha shahar hokimlarimizga Ankonadagi marshlardan kelib turishadi. Ular odatda yomon ruhli xalq bo'lib, hayotlarining har bir uslubi faqatgina xunuk odamning hiyosidan boshqa narsa emasdek tuyuladi; va shu tug'ma xasislik va ochko'zlikdan o'zlari bilan sudyalar va notariuslarni olib kelishadi, ular qonun maktablaridan emas, balki arra dumidan yoki kulol ustaxonasidan olingan odamlardek ko'rinishadi.

en: Now, one of these being come hither for Provost, among the many judges whom he brought with him was one who styled himself Messer Niccola da San Lepidio and who had more the air of a tinker than of aught else, and he was set with oth- er judges to hear criminal causes.
uz: Endi, bu yerga Provost uchun kelganlardan biri, u o'zi bilan olib kelgan ko'plab sudyalardan biri o'zini Messer Niccola da San Lepidio deb atagan va boshqa hech narsadan ko'ra tuzatgichga o'xshagan edi va u boshqa sudyalar bilan birga jinoiy ishlarni eshitishga tayinlangan edi.

en: As it oft happeneth that, for all the towns- folk have nought in the world to do at the courts of law, yet bytimes they go thither, it befell that Maso del Saggio went thither one morning, in quest of a friend of his, and chancing to cast his eyes whereas this said Messer Nic- cola sat, himseemed that here was a rare outlandish kind of wild fowl.
uz: Ko'pincha shunday bo'ladiki, barcha shaharlarda odamlar sudda hech narsa qilmagan bo'lsalar ham, lekin ba'zan u yerga borsalar ham, Maso del Saggio bir kuni ertalab do'stini qidirib borgan va shu paytga ko'zini tashlab, Messer Nic-Cola o'tirganini aytganida, u yerda noyob g'alati yovvoyi qush bor edi, deb o'yladi.

en: Ac- cordingly, he went on to examine him from head to foot, and albeit he saw him with the miniver bonnet on his head all black with smoke and grease
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u uni boshidan oyoqqacha tekshirib ko'rdi va garchi boshida tutun va yog' bilan qoplangan qora miniver qalpoq bilan ko'rsa ham.

en: and a paltry inkhorn at his girdle, a gown longer than his mantle and store of other things all foreign to a man of good breeding and manners, yet of all these the most notable, to his thinking, was a pair of breeches, the backside whereof, as the judge sat, with his clothes standing open in front for strait- ness, he perceived came halfway down his legs.
uz: va uning kamarida mayin siyoh shoxi, uning ko'ylagidan uzunroq ko'ylak va odob-axloqli odamga begona bo'lgan boshqa narsalar do'koni, ammo bularning barchasidan eng e'tiborlisi, uning fikricha, bir juft ko'ylak edi, uning orqa tomoni, sudya o'tirganida, uning kiyimlari old tomondan ochiq turgan holda, uning oyoqlarining yarmigacha tushayotganini sezdi.

en: Thereupon, without tarry- ing longer to look upon him, he left him with whom he went seeking and beginning a new quest, presently found two comrades of his, called one Ribi and the other Matteuzzo, men much of the same mad humour as him- self, and said to them, ‘As you tender me, come with me to the law courts, for I wish to show you the rarest scarecrow you ever saw.’ Accordingly, carrying them to the court house, he showed them the afore- said judge and his breeches, whereat they fell a-laughing, as soon as they caught sight of him afar off; then, drawing nearer to the platform whereon my lord judge sat, they saw that one might lightly pass thereunder and that, moreover, the boards under his feet were so broken that one might with great ease thrust his hand and arm between them; whereupon quoth Maso to his comrades, ‘Needs must we pull him off those breeches of his altogether, for that
uz: Shundan so'ng, unga ko'proq tikilib turmasdan, u uni tark etdi, u bilan birga yangi izlanishni boshladi, tez orada uning ikki o'rtog'ini topdi, biri Ribi va ikkinchisi Matteuzzo, o'zi kabi bir xil aqldan ozgan odamlar, va ularga dedi: "Siz menga yumshoqlik bilan kelinglar, men bilan sudga kelinglar, chunki men sizga eng kam uchraydigan qo'rqinchli narsani ko'rsatmoqchiman." Shunga ko'ra, ularni sud uyiga olib borar ekan, u oldingi sudyani va uning ko'rpalarini ko'rsatdi, ular undan uzoqroqga tushib ketgandek kulishardi; keyin, mening xo'jayinimga yaqinroq kelganlarida, ular uning qo'li bilan yengil o'tib ketishi mumkin edi va, ko'proq, uning oyoqlari bilan birga bo'lgan edi.

en: it may very well be done.’ Each of the others had already seen how;383 wherefore, having agreed among themselves what they should say and do, they returned thither next morning, when, the court being very full of folk, Matteuzzo, without being seen of any, crept under the bench and posted himself immediately beneath the judge’s feet.
uz: Bu juda yaxshi amalga oshirilishi mumkin. Qolganlarning har biri allaqachon qanday ekanligini ko'rgan edi; 383 shuning uchun, nima deyish va nima qilish kerakligini o'zaro kelishib, ular ertasi kuni ertalab u yerga qaytdilar, shunda, sud juda to'la odamlarga to'la bo'lganida, Matteuzzo hech kim ko'rinmasdan, o'rindiqqa kirib, darhol sudyaning oyoqlari ostiga o'tirdi.

en: Meanwhile, Maso came up to my lord judge on one side and taking him by the skirt of his gown, whilst Ribi did the like on the other side, began to say, ‘My lord, my lord, I pray you for God’s sake, ere yonder scurvy thief on the other side of you go elsewhere, make him restore me a pair of saddlebags whereof he hath saith indeed he did it not; but I saw him, not a month ago, in act to have them resoled.’ Ribi on his side cried out with all his might, ‘Believe him not, my lord; he is an arrant knave, and for that he knoweth I am come to lay a complaint against him for a pair of saddlebags whereof he hath robbed me, he cometh now with his story of the boothose, which I have had in my house this many a day.
uz: Ayni paytda, Maso xo'jayinimning bir tomoniga yaqinlashib, uni ko'ylagining etagidan ushladi, Ribi esa boshqa tomonda xuddi shunday qildi va dedi: "Hazratim, xo'jayinim, men sizni Xudo haqqi bilan iltimos qilaman, narigi tomondagi o'g'ri boshqa joyga bormang, menga bir juft egar sumkasini qaytarib bering, u buni qilmaganini aytdi; lekin men uni bir oy oldin emas, ularni qaytarib olishga harakat qilganini ko'rdim." Ribi uning yonida butun kuchini bilan qichqirib dedi: "Uga ishonmang, xo'jayinim; u g'irchoq, va u meni o'g'irlagan bir juft egar sumkasi uchun unga shikoyat qilish uchun kelganimni bilgani uchun, u meni o'g'irladi."

en: An you believe me not, I can bring you to wit- ness my next-door neighbor Trecca and Grassa the tripewoman and one who goeth gathering the sweepings from Santa Masia at Verjaza, who saw him when he came back from the country.
uz: Agar ishonmasangiz, men sizni qo'shni qo'shnim Trecca va Grassa bilan uchrashtirishim mumkin, u tripewoman va Santa Masia at Verjaza'dan supurishlarni yig'ishga borayotgan, uni qishloqdan qaytib kelganida ko'rgan odam edi.

en: Maso on the other hand suffered not Ribi to speak, but bawled his loudest, whereupon the other but shouted the more.
uz: Maso esa Ribiga gapirishga yo'l qo'ymadi, balki eng baland ovozda baqirardi, shunga qaramay, ikkinchisi yanada baqirardi.

en: The judge stood up and
uz: Sudya o'rnidan turdi va

en: leaned towards them, so he might the better apprehend what they had to say, wherefore Matteuzzo, watching his opportunity, thrust his hand between the crack of the boards and laying hold of Messer Niccola’s galligaskins by the breech, tugged at them amain.
uz: Ularga suyanib, ularning nima deyayotganini yaxshiroq tushunishi uchun, Matteuzzo o'z imkoniyatini kuzatib, doskalarning yoriqlari orasiga qo'lini surib, Messer Niccoloning galligaskinslarini ko'ylakdan ushlab, ularga hayrat bilan tortib keldi.

en: The breeches came down incontinent, for that the judge was lean and lank of the crupper; whereupon, feeling this and knowing not what it might be, he would have sat down again and pulled his skirts forward to cover himself; but Maso on the one side and Ribi on the other still held him fast and cried out, ‘My lord, you do ill not to do me justice and to seek to avoid hearing me and get you gone otherwhere; there be no writs granted in this city for such small matters as this.’ So saying, they held him fast by the clothes on such wise that all who were in the court perceived that his breeches had been pulled down.
uz: Ko'ylaklar tinimsiz tushdi, chunki sudya o'g'irchoqning ozg'in va dangasa edi; shundan so'ng, buni his qilib va nima bo'lishini bilmay, u yana o'tirgan bo'lardi va yubkalarini oldinga tortib, o'zini yopgan bo'lardi; lekin Maso bir tomonda va Ribi boshqa tomonda uni ushlab turardi va baqirdi: "Ey xo'jayin, siz menga adolat qilmaysiz va meni eshitishdan qochishga va sizni boshqa joyga olib ketishga harakat qilmaysiz; bu shaharda bunday mayda ishlar uchun hech qanday yo'l yo'q." Shunday qilib, ular uni kiyimdan shunday ushlab turdilarki, suddagilarning barchasi uning ko'ylaklari tortib olinganini sezdilar.

en: However, Matteuzzo, after he had held them awhile, let them go and coming forth from under the platform, made off out of the court and went his way without being seen; whereupon quoth Ribi, himseeming he had done enough, ‘I vow to God I will appeal to the syndicate!’ Whilst Maso, on his part, let go the mantle and said, ‘Nay, I will e’en come hither again and again until such time as I ﬁnd you not hindered as you seem to be this morning.’ So saying, they both made off as quickliest they might, each on his own side, whilst my lord judge pulled up his breeches in everyone’s presence, as if he were arisen from sleep; then, perceiving how the case stood, he enquired whither they were gone who were at difference anent the boothose and the saddlebags; but they were not to be found, whereupon he began to swear by Cock’s bowels that need must he know and learn if it were the wont at Florence to
uz: Ammo, Matteuzzo ularni biroz ushlab turganidan so'ng, ularni platforma ostidan chiqib kelishga qo'yib yubordi, suddan chiqib ketdi va ko'rinmasdan yo'lga chiqdi; shundan so'ng Ribi, ko'rinishicha yetarli bo'ldi, dedi: "Men Xudoga qasam ichaman, sindikatga murojaat qilaman!" Maso esa, o'z navbatida, mantiyani qo'yib yubordi va dedi: "Yo'q, men sizni bugun ertalab ko'rmaguncha qayta-qayta bu yerga kelaman." Shunday qilib, ular har biri o'z tomoniga, ikkalasi ham o'zlarining ko'rpalarini tortdi, go'yo u uyqudan turgandek edi; keyin, u qayerga borayotganini so'radi, agar ular qayerda bo'lishlari kerak edi va u...

en: pull down the judges’ breeches, whenas they sat on the judicial bench.
uz: Hakamlarning ichki kiyimlarini sud zalida o'tirganlarida pastga torting.

en: The Provost, on his part, hearing of this, made a great stir; but, his friends hav- ing shown him that this had only been done to give him notice that the Florentines right well understood how, whereas he should have brought judges, he had brought them sorry patches, to have them better cheap, he thought it best to hold his peace, and so the thing went no farther for the nonce.”
