en: Neiﬁle’s canzonet was much commended both of the king and of the oth- er ladies; after which, for that a great part of the night was now spent, the king commanded that all should betake themselves to rest until the day.
uz: Neifile'ning qo'shig'i shohdan ham, boshqa ayollardan ham juda maqtovga sazovor edi; shundan so'ng, tunning katta qismi o'tkazilgani sababli, shoh hamma o'zlarini kunduzgacha dam olish uchun dam olishni buyurdi.

en: Here endeth the Ninth Day of the Decameron.
uz: Mana Dekameronning to'qqizinchi kuni tugaydi.

en: DAY THE TENTH INTRODUCTION Here beginneth the tenth and last day of the Decameron wherein under the governance of Pamﬁlo is discoursed of whoso hath anywise wrought generously or magniﬁcently in matters of love or otherwhat.
uz: O'NINCHI KUN Kirish Mana, Dekameronning o'ninchi va oxirgi kuni boshlanadi, unda Pamfiloning boshqaruvi ostida sevgi yoki boshqa masalalarda saxiy yoki ulug'vor ish qilgan har bir kishi haqida gapiriladi.

en: Certain cloudlets in the West were yet vermeil, what time those of the East were already at their marges grown lucent like unto very gold, when Pam- ﬁlo, arising, let call his comrades and the ladies, who being all come, he took counsel with them of whither they should go for their diversion and fared forth with slow step, accompanied by Filomena and Fiammetta, whilst all the others followed after.
uz: G'arbdagi ba'zi bulutchalar hali ko'p edi, Sharqdagilar o'z chetlarida allaqachon juda oltinga o'xshab yaltiroq bo'lgan paytda, Pam- filo o'rnidan turib, o'rtoqlari va xonimlarini chaqirib oldi. Ularning hammasi kelganidan so'ng, ular qayerga ketishlari kerakligi haqida maslahatlashdi va Filomena va Fiammetta hamrohligida sekin qadam tashladi, qolganlarning hammasi esa ergashdi.

en: On this wise, devising and telling and answer- ing many things of their future life together, they went a great while a- pleasuring; then, having made a pretty long circuit and the sun beginning to wax overhot, they returned to the palace.
uz: Shu tariqa, kelajakdagi hayotlarining ko'p narsalarni birgalikda o'ylab, aytib, javob berib, ular ajoyib va rohatlantiruvchi vaqt o'tkazishdi; so'ngra ancha uzoq aylana o'tkazib, quyosh issiq tusha boshlagach, saroyga qaytdilar.

en: There they let rinse the beakers in the clear fountain and whoso would drank somewhat; after which they went frolicking among the pleasant shades of the garden until the eating-hour.
uz: U yerda ular ochiq favvora ichimliklarini yuvishga ruxsat berishardi va kim biroz ichmoqchi bo'lsa, keyin ovqatlanish vaqtigacha bog'ning yoqimli soyalari orasida xursandchilik qilishardi.

en: Then, having eaten and slept, as of their wont, they assembled whereas it pleased the king and there he called upon Neiﬁle for the ﬁrst discourse, who blithely began thus:
uz: Keyin, odatlariga ko'ra ovqatlanib uxlab bo'lgach, ular shohga yoqqanidek yig'ilishdi va u yerda Neifileni birinchi nutq uchun chaqirib oldi, u esa shovqin bilan shunday boshladi:

en: THE FIRST STORY A knight in the king’s service of Spain thinking himself ill guerdoned, the king by very certain proof showeth him that this is not his fault, but that of his own perverse fortune, and after largesseth him magniﬁcently.
uz: BIRINCHI HIKOYA Ispaniya qirolining xizmatidagi ritsar o'zini yomon qo'riqladi deb o'ylagan holda, qirol unga bu uning aybi emas, balki o'zining buzuq boyligining aybi ekanligini aniq dalillar bilan ko'rsatadi va keyin uni ulug'vor tarzda ulug'laydi.

en: “Needs, honourable ladies, must I repute it a singular favour to myself that our king hath preferred me unto such an honour as it is to be the ﬁrst to tell of magniﬁcence, the which, even as the sun is the glory and adornment of all the heaven, is the light and lustre of every other virtue.
uz: Hurmatli xonimlar, shohimiz meni shunday sharafga afzal ko'rganini o'zimga alohida minnatdorchilik deb hisoblasam kerakki, u birinchi bo'lib ulug'vorlik haqida gapiradigan bo'lishim kerak edi, bu ulug'vorlik quyosh butun osmonning shon-shuhrati va bezagi bo'lgani kabi, har bir boshqa fazilatning nuri va yaltirog'idir.

en: I will, therefore, tell you a little story thereof, quaint and pleasant enough to my thinking, which to recall can certes be none other than useful.
uz: Shunday qilib, men sizga uning haqida ozgina hikoya aytib beraman, g'alati va fikrlashimga yetarlicha yoqimli, uni eslash, albatta, foydali bo'lishi mumkin.

en: You must know, then, that, among the other gallant gentlemen who have from time immemorial graced our city, there was one (and maybe the most of worth) by name Messer Ruggieri de’ Figiovanni, who, being both rich and high-spirited and seeing that, in view of the way of living and of the us- ages of Tuscany, he might, if he tarried there, avail to display little or noth- ing of his merit, resolved to seek service awhile with Alfonso, King of Spain, the renown of whose valiance transcended that of every other prince of his time; wherefore he betook himself, very honourably furnished with arms and horses and followers, to Alfonso in Spain and was by him gra- ciously received.
uz: Shuni bilishingiz kerakki, bizning shahrimizni qadim zamonlardan beri bezagan boshqa jasur janoblar orasida, Messer Ruggieri de Figiovanni ismli (va ehtimol eng qimmatli) bir kishi bor edi. U ham boy, ham yuqori ruhli edi va Toskaniyaning turmush tarzi va amerikalik asrlarini hisobga olgan holda, u yerda qolsa, o'z fazilatlarining ozmi-yo'qmi ko'rsatishga qaror qilishi mumkin edi, u Ispaniya qiroli Alfonsoga xizmat qilishga qaror qildi, uning shahzodi o'z davrining har bir shahzodasidan ustun edi; shuning uchun u o'zini juda sharafli tarzda qurol-yarog' va izdoshlar bilan ta'minlagan holda, Ispaniyaga Alfonsoga ko'rsatdi va u tomonidan ulug'vor qabul qilindi.

en: Accordingly, he took up his abode there and living splen- didly and doing marvellous deeds of arms, he very soon made himself known for a man of worth and valour.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u yerda o'z maskanini qurollantirdi va ajoyib qurol-yarog' ishlarini qilib yashadi, tez orada o'zini qadrli va jasur inson sifatida tanidi.

en: When he had sojourned there a pretty while and had taken particular note of the king’s fashions, himseemed he bestowed castles and cities and baron- ies now upon one and now upon another with little enough discretion, as giving them to those who were unworthy thereof, and for that to him, who held himself for that which he was, nothing was given, he conceived that
uz: U yerda bir oz vaqt turgach va podshohning modalarini alohida e'tiborga olganidan so'ng, u qasrlar, shaharlar va baronlarni bir-biriga kamroq ehtiyotkorlik bilan sovg'a qilgan, ularga loyiq bo'lmaganlarga bergan, va shuning uchun o'ziga hech narsa berilmagan narsa uchun o'zini tutgan odamga, u o'yladi:

en: his repute would be much abated by reason thereof; wherefore he determ- ined to depart and craved leave of the king.
uz: Uning obro'si shu sababli juda pasayadi; shuning uchun u ketishga qaror qildi va shohdan ketishni xohladi.

en: The latter granted him the leave he sought and gave him one of the best and ﬁnest mules that ever was rid- den, the which, for the long journey he had to make, was very acceptable to Messer Ruggieri.
uz: Oxirgisi unga o'zi so'ragan ruxsatni berdi va unga hech qachon qutulmagan eng yaxshi va eng yaxshi mullardan birini berdi, bu uzoq sayohat uchun Messer Ruggieriga juda ma'qul edi.

en: Moreover, he charged a discreet servant of his that he should study, by such means as seemed to him best, to ride with Messer Ruggieri on such wise that he should not appear to have been sent by the king, and note everything he should say of him, so as he might avail to re- peat it to him, and that on the ensuing morning he should command him re- turn to the court.
uz: Qolaversa, u o'zining dono xizmatkoriga o'ziga ma'qul tuyulgan yo'llar bilan o'qishni buyurdi, u Messer Ruggieri bilan shunday donolik bilan minsinki, u shoh tomonidan yuborilgandek ko'rinmasin va u haqida aytadigan hamma narsani yozib olsin, toki u unga qayta-qayta xabar berishi mumkin bo'lsin va ertasi kuni ertalab unga sudga qaytishni buyursin.

en: Accordingly, the servant, lying in wait for Messer Rug- gieri’s departure, accosted him, as he came forth the city, and very aptly joined company with him, giving him to understand that he also was bound for Italy.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, xizmatkor, Messer Rug-gierining ketishini kutgan holda, shaharga chiqayotganda unga yaqinlashdi va u bilan juda mohirona hamkorlik qildi, bu unga Italiyaga ham borishi kerakligini tushunishga yordam berdi.

en: Messer Ruggieri, then, fared on, riding the mule given him by the king and devising of one thing and another with the latter’s servant, till hard upon tierce, when he said, ‘Methinketh it were well done to let our beasts stale.’ Accordingly, they put them up in a stable and they all staled, except the mule; then they rode on again, whilst the squire still took note of the gentleman’s words, and came presently to a river, where, as they watered their cattle, the mule staled in the stream; which Messer Ruggieri seeing, ‘Marry,’ quoth he, ‘God confound thee, beast, for that thou art made after the same fashion as the prince who gave thee to me!’ The squire noted these words and albeit he took store of many others, as he journeyed with him all that day, he heard him say nought else but what was to the highest praise of the king.
uz: Messer Ruggieri o'sha paytda podshoh tomonidan berilgan mulyani minib, oxirgi xizmatkor bilan bir-birini o'ylab yurdi, to uchinchi marta qattiq turib, u dedi: "Bizning hayvonlarimizni qo'yib yuborish yaxshi deb o'ylaydi". Shunga ko'ra, ularni o'rmaga qo'yishdi va ular hammasi qo'yib ketdi, faqat muldan tashqari; keyin ular yana yo'lga tushishdi, shunda squire janobning so'zlarini esladi va darhol daryoga keldi. U yerda, chorva mollarini sug'orib yurganlarida, mul daryoda qolib ketdi; uni ko'rib, Messer Ruggieri dedi: "Marry," u aytdi: "Xudo seni aybladi, chunki sen menga bergan shahzoda kabi bo'lding!" Shunga qaramay, squire bu so'zlarni qabul qildi va u uni ko'p marta maqtadi, lekin u bilan birga ko'p...

en: Next morning, they being mounted and Ruggieri offering to ride towards Tuscany, the squire imparted to him the king’s commandment, whereupon he incontinent turned back.
uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab, ular o'tirib, Ruggieri Toskaniyaga qarab minmoqchi bo'lganida, squire unga podshohning buyrug'ini yetkazdi, shundan so'ng u bemalol orqaga qaytdi.

en: When he arrived at court, the king, learning what he had said of the mule, let call him to himself and receiving him with a cheerful favour, asked him why he had likened him to his mule, or rather why he had likened the mule to him.
uz: U saroyga yetib borgach, shoh, uning mul haqida aytganlarini bilib, uni o'ziga chaqirib, quvnoqlik bilan qabul qilib, undan nega uni o'z mulisiga o'xshatganini, aniqrog'i, nega mulini o'ziga o'xshatganini so'radi.

en: ‘My lord,’ replied Ruggieri frankly, ‘I likened her to you for that, like as you give whereas it behoveth not and give not whereas it behoveth, even so she staled not whereas it behoved, but staled whereas it behoved not.’ Then said the king, ‘Messer Ruggieri, if I have not given to you, as I have given unto many who are of no account in comparison with you, it happened not because I knew you not for a most valiant cavalier and worthy of every great gift; nay, but it is your fortune, which hath not suffered me guerdon you according to your deserts, that hath
uz: Janobim,  dedi Ruggeri ochiqchasiga,  men uni sizga oxshatdim, xuddi siz kerak bolmaganda berganingiz va kerak bolmaganda bermaganingiz kabi, xuddi u kerak bolmaganda zanglamagan, lekin kerak bolmaganda zanglamagan. Shunda shoh dedi:  Janob Ruggeri, agar men sizga siz bilan solishtirganda arzimagan kop kishilarga berganimdek, bu siz eng jasur chavandoz va har qanday buyuk sovgaga loyiq emasligingizni bilganim uchun sodir bolmadi, balki bu sizning boyligingizdir, bu sizga meni sizning sahrolaringizga qarab qoriqlashga majbur qilmadi,

en: sinned in this, and not I; and that I may say sooth I will manifestly prove to you.’ ‘My lord,’ replied Ruggieri, ‘I was not chagrined because I have got- ten no largesse of you, for that I desire not to be richer than I am, but be- cause you have on no wise borne witness to my merit.
uz: Men gunoh qildim, bunda men emas; va men tinchlik aytishim uchun sizga aniq isbotlayman. Ey Rabbim,  javob berdi Ruggieri, Men sizdan on marta kop narsa olgani uchun xafa bolmadim, chunki men mendan boyroq bolishni xohlamayman, lekin chunki siz mening fazilatimga hech qanday guvohlik bermagansiz.

en: Natheless, I hold your excuse for good and honourable and am ready to see that which it shall please you show me, albeit I believe you without proof.’ The king then car- ried him into a great hall of his, where, as he had ordered it beforehand, were two great locked coffers, and said to him, in presence of many, ‘Mess- er Ruggieri, in one of these coffers is my crown, the royal sceptre and the orb, together with many goodly girdles and ouches and rings of mine, and in ﬁne every precious jewel I have; and the other is full of earth.
uz: Shunday bo'lsa ham, men sizning bahonangizni yaxshi va sharafli deb bilaman va siz menga ko'rsatadigan narsani ko'rishga tayyorman, garchi men sizga hech qanday dalilsiz ishonsam ham." Shunda shoh uni o'zining katta zaliga olib kirdi, u yerda, avval buyurganidek, ikkita katta qulflangan sandiq bor edi va unga ko'pchilikning oldida dedi: "Messess- er Ruggieri, bu sandiqlarning birida mening tojim, qirollik qamchisi va shar, shuningdek, ko'plab yaxshi kamarlarim, o'ramlarim va uzuklarim, va menda bor har bir qimmatbaho taqinchoq bor edi; va ikkinchisi tuproqqa to'la.

en: Take, then, one and be that which you shall take yours; and you may thus see whether of the twain hath been ungrateful to your worth, myself of your ill fortune.’ Messer Ruggieri, seeing that it was the king’s pleasure, took one of the coffers, which, being opened by Alfonso’s commandment, was found to be that which was full of earth; whereupon quoth the king, laughing, ‘Now can you see, Messer Ruggieri, that this that I tell you of your fortune is true; but certes your worth meriteth that I should oppose myself to her might.
uz: Shunday qilib, birini olib, o'zingizniki bo'ling; va shunday qilib, o'zingizning boyligingizga, o'z baxtsizligingizga befarq bo'lganingizni ko'rishingiz mumkin." Messer Ruggieri, bu shohning xohishi ekanligini ko'rib, sandiqlardan birini oldi. Alfonso buyrug'i bilan ochilganda, u yer bilan to'la deb topildi; shundan so'ng shoh kuldi: "Endi ko'ryapsizmi, Messer Ruggieri, men sizga boyligingiz haqida aytgan gapim rost; lekin albatta, men unga qarshi turishimga arziydi."

en: I know you have no mind to turn Spaniard and therefore I will bestow upon you neither castle nor city in these parts; but this coffer, of which fortune de- prived you, I will in her despite shall be yours, so you may carry it off to your own country and justly glorify yourself of your worth in the sight of your countrymen by the witness of my gifts.’ Messer Ruggieri accordingly took the coffer and having rendered the king those thanks which sorted with such a gift, joyfully returned therewith to Tuscany.”
uz: Men bilaman, siz ispan bo'lish niyatida emassiz va shuning uchun men sizga bu qismlarda na qasr, na shahar sovg'a qilaman; lekin bu sandiq, undan sizni mahrum qilgan bo'lsa ham, unda o'zingizniki bo'ladi, shunda uni o'z mamlakatingizga olib ketishingiz va o'z qadringizni o'z yurtdoshlaringiz oldida mening sovg'amning guvohi bo'lishingiz mumkin." Messer Ruggieri shunday qilib sandiqni oldi va bunday sovg'a bilan saralab olingan rahmatlarni qirolga minnatdorchilik bilan topshirdi va u bilan birga xursandchilik bilan qaytdi.

en: THE SECOND STORY Ghino di Tacco taketh the Abbot of Cluny and having cured him of the stomach-complaint, letteth him go; whereupon the abbot, returning to the court of Rome, reconcileth him with Pope Boniface and maketh him a prior of the hospitallers.
uz: IKKINCHI HIKOYA Ghino di Takko Kluny abbatini oladi va uni qorin shikoyatidan davolanib, qo'yib yuboradi; shundan so'ng abbat Rim saroyiga qaytib, uni Papa Bonifatiy bilan yarashtiradi va kasalxona xodimlaridan biriga aylantiradi.

en: The magniﬁcence shown by King Alfonso to the Florentine cavalier having been duly commended, the king, who had been mightily pleased therewith, enjoined Elisa to follow on, and she straightway began thus: “Dainty dames, it cannot be denied that for a king to be muniﬁcent and to have shown his muniﬁcence to him who had served him is a great and a praise- worthy thing; but what shall we say if a churchman be related to have prac- tised marvellous magnanimity towards one, whom if he had used as an en- emy, he had of none been blamed therefor?
uz: Florensiyalik chavandozga qirol Alfonso tomonidan ko'rsatilgan ulug'vorlik munosib tarzda maqtangandan so'ng, qirol bundan juda mamnun bo'lgan holda, Elisaga davom etishni buyurdi va u darhol shunday boshladi: Go'zal xonimlar, qirolning saxiy bo'lishi va unga xizmat qilgan odamga saxiyligini ko'rsatishi buyuk va maqtovga loyiq narsa ekanligini inkor etib bo'lmaydi; lekin cherkov a'zosiga nisbatan ajoyib saxiylik ko'rsatgani haqida nima deyish mumkin, agar u en-em sifatida ishlagan bo'lsa, u hech qanday ayblanmagan bo'lsa?

en: Certes, we can say none other- wise than that the king’s magniﬁcence was a virtue, whilst that of the churchman was a miracle, inasmuch as the clergy are all exceeding nig- gardly, nay, far more so than women, and sworn enemies of all manner of liberality; and albeit all men naturally hunger after vengeance for affronts received, we see churchmen, for all they preach patience and especially commend the remission of offences, pursue it more eagerly than other folk.
uz: Albatta, biz hech kimdan boshqa aql-idrok topa olmaymiz, faqatgina shohning ulug'vorligi fazilat edi, cherkovchining ulug'vorligi esa mo'jiza edi, chunki ruhoniylar ayollardan ko'ra haddan tashqari qo'rqoq, yo'q, va har qanday erkinlikning qasamyod dushmanlari edi; va garchi barcha erkaklar tabiiy ravishda qabul qilingan haqoratlar uchun qasos olishga chanqoq bo'lsalar ham, biz cherkov a'zolarini ko'ramiz, chunki ular sabr-toqat va ayniqsa ayblarning kechirilishini maqtab, uni boshqa odamlardan ko'ra ko'proq ishtiyoq bilan izlaydilar.

en: This, then, to wit, how a churchman was magnanimous, you may manifestly learn from the following story of mine.
uz: Demak, cherkov xodimi qanday saxovatli bo'lgani haqida quyidagi hikoyamdan aniq bilib olishingiz mumkin.

en: Ghino di Tacco, a man very famous for his cruelty and his robberies, be- ing expelled from Siena and at feud with the Counts of Santa Fiore, raised Radicofani against the Church of Rome and taking up his sojourn there, caused his swashbucklers despoil whosoever passed through the surround- ing country.
uz: Ghino di Tacco, o'zining shafqatsizligi va o'g'irligi bilan juda mashhur bo'lgan odam, Siena shahridan haydalgan va Santa Fiore graflari bilan janjallashgan holda, Radikofani Rim cherkoviga qarshi ko'tardi va u yerda qolishni boshladi, bu uning o'g'rilariga atrof-muhitdan o'tgan har kimni talon-toroj qilishga sabab bo'ldi.

en: Now, Boniface the Eighth being pope in Rome, there came to court the Abbot of Cluny, who is believed to be one of the richest prelates
uz: Endi Rimda Rim papasi bo'lgan Bonifik Sakkizinchi, eng boy prelatlardan biri deb hisoblanadigan Kluny abbasi sudga keldi.

en: in the world, and having there marred his stomach, he was advised by the physicians to repair to the baths of Siena and he would without fail be cured.
uz: dunyoda, va u yerda qorni shikastlanganidan so'ng, shifokorlar unga Siena vannalariga davolanishni maslahat berishdi va u bemalol tuzalib ketadi.

en: Accordingly, having gotten the pope’s leave, he set out on his way thither in great pomp of gear and baggage and horses and servitors, unreck- ing of Ghino’s [ill] report.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Papa ruxsat olgach, u u yerga katta dabdaba va yuklar, otlar va xizmatkorlar bilan yo'lga chiqdi, Ghinoning hisobotlarini hisobga olmaganda.

en: The latter, hearing of his coming, spread his nets and hemmed him and all his household and gear about in a strait place, without letting a single footboy escape.
uz: Oxirgisi uning kelishini eshitib, to'rlarini yoydi va uni, butun xonadonini va barcha jihozlarini tor joyda aylantirib, birorta ham futbolchini qochishga qo'ymadi.

en: This done, he despatched to the ab- bot one, the most sufﬁcient, of his men, well accompanied, who in his name very lovingly prayed him be pleased to light down and sojourn with the aforesaid Ghino in his castle.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u o'z odamlarining eng yetarli bo'lgan, yaxshi hamroh bo'lgan abbotga jo'natdi. Ular uning nomidan yuqorida aytilgan Ghinoning qasrida yoritib, qolishlarini juda mehr bilan duo qilishdi.

en: The abbot, hearing this, answered furiously that he would nowise do it, having nought to do with Ghino, but that he would fare on and would fain see who should forbid his passage.
uz: Buni eshitgan abbat g'azab bilan javob berdi: "Bu ishni Ghinoni hech qanday aloqasi bo'lmagani uchun qilmoqchiman, lekin o'zimga kelmayman va kim uning o'tishiga to'sqinlik qilishi kerakligini ko'rmoqchiman".

en: Whereto quoth the messenger on humble wise, ‘Sir, you are come into parts where, barring God His might, there is nothing to fear for us and where excommu- nications and interdicts are all excommunicated; wherefore, may it please you, you were best comply with Ghino in this.’ During this parley, the whole place had been encompassed about with men-at-arms; wherefore the abbot, seeing himself taken with his men, betook himself, sore against his will, to the castle, in company with the am- bassador, and with him all his household and gear, and alighting there, was, by Ghino’s orders, lodged all alone in a very dark and mean little chamber in one of the pavilions, whilst everyone else was well enough accommod- ated, according to his quality, about the castle and the horses and all the gear put in safety, without aught thereof being touched.
uz: Xullas, elchi kamtarona donolik bilan aytdi: Janob, siz shunday joylarga keldingizki, Xudo O'z qudratidan tashqari, biz uchun qo'rqadigan hech narsa yo'q va barcha excommunications va interdicts chetlatilgan; shuning uchun, sizga yoqsa, siz Ghinoning bu ishiga amal qiling. Ushbu suhbat davomida butun joy qo'l bilan o'ralgan odamlar bilan o'ralgan edi; shuning uchun abbot o'zini o'z odamlari bilan olib ketilganini ko'rib, o'z irodasidan xafagarchilik bilan qasriga, am-bassador bilan birga, u bilan birga butun uy aholisi va jihozlari bilan tushdi va u yerga tushdi. Ghinoning buyrug'i bilan, juda qorong'i va ozgina xonada yotdi.

en: This done, Ghino betook himself to the abbot and said to him, ‘Sir, Ghino, whose guest you are, sendeth to you, praying you acquaint him whither you are bound and on what occasion.’ The abbot, like a wise man, had by this laid by his pride and told him whither he went and why.
uz: Shundan so'ng, Ghino o'zini abbat huzuriga olib bordi va unga dedi: "Janob, siz mehmon bo'lgan Ghino sizga murojaat qilib, uni qayerga bog'langaningizni va qanday holatda tanishtirishni so'rayapti." Abbat, dono odamga o'xshab, shu bilan faxrlanib, qayerga borishini va nima uchun borishini aytdi.

en: Ghino, hearing this, took his leave and bethought himself to go about to cure him without baths.
uz: Buni eshitib, Ghinoning xayrlashiga qaror qildi va uni vannalarsiz davolash uchun o'zini tashlab ketishni o'yladi.

en: Accordingly, he let keep a great ﬁre still burning in the little room and causing guard the place well, returned not to the abbot till the following morning, when he brought him, in a very white napkin, two slices of toasted bread and a great beaker of his own Corniglia vernage443 and bespoke him thus, ‘Sir, when Ghino was young, he studied medicine and saith that he learned there was no better remedy for the stomach-complaint than that which he purposeth to apply to you and of which these things that I bring you are the beginning; wherefore do you take them and refresh yourself.’
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u kichik xonada katta olov yonib turishiga va joyni yaxshi qo'riqlashga ruxsat berdi, ertasi kuni ertalabgacha abbotga qaytmadi. Keyin u unga juda oq salfetkada ikki bo'lak qovurilgan non va o'zining Corniglia Vernage443 dan katta kosa olib keldi va shunday dedi: "Janob, Ghinoning yoshligida u tibbiyotni o'rgangan va u sizga qo'llamoqchi bo'lganidan ko'ra yaxshiroq qorin shikoyatiga qarshi hech qanday davo yo'qligini o'rgangan, shuning uchun men sizga olib kelayotgan bu narsalar boshlanishi; shuning uchun ularni oling va o'zingizni tetiklantiring."

en: The abbot, whose hunger was greater than his desire to bandy words, ate the bread and drank the wine, though he did it with an ill will, and after made many haughty speeches, asking and counselling of many things and demanding in particular to see Ghino.
uz: Abbat, uning bandit so'zlarga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi undan ham kattaroq edi, nonni yedi va vinoni ichdi, garchi buni yomon niyat bilan qilgan bo'lsa ham, keyin ko'p takabbur nutqlar qildi, ko'p narsalarni so'radi va maslahat berdi, ayniqsa Ghinoni ko'rishni talab qildi.

en: The latter, hearing this talk, let part of it pass as idle and answered the rest very courteously, avouching that Ghino would visit him as quickliest he might.
uz: Oxirgisi bu gapni eshitib, uning bir qismini bekorchi deb ko'rsatdi va qolganlariga juda odob bilan javob berdi, Ghinoning unga imkon qadar tezroq tashrif buyurishini kutdi.

en: This said, he took his leave of him and returned not until the ensuing day, when he brought him as much toasted bread and as much malmsey; and so he kept him several days, till such time as he perceived that he had eaten some dried beans, which he had of intent aforethought brought secretly thither and left there; whereupon he asked him, on Ghino’s part, how he found himself about the stomach.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u undan ketdi va ertasi kungacha qaytib kelmadi. Shunda u unga ko'p qovurilgan non va ko'p malmesi olib keldi. Shunday qilib, u uni bir necha kun saqladi, toki u quritilgan loviya yeganini anglab yetguncha, uni oldindan yashirincha u yerga olib kelib, u yerga tashlab ketgan edi. Shundan so'ng, Ghino'dan o'zidan qanday ahvolda ekanligini so'radi.

en: The abbot answered, ‘Meseemeth I should fare well, were I but out of his hands; and after that, I have no greater desire than to eat, so well have his remedies cured me.’ Thereupon Ghino caused the abbot’s own people array him a goodly chamber with his own gear and let make ready a magniﬁcent ban- quet, to which he bade the prelate’s whole household, together with many folk of the burgh.
uz: Abbot javob berdi: Agar men uning qolidan chiqmaganimda, yaxshi bolardim, deb oylayman; va shundan song, ovqat yeyishdan kora koproq ishtiyoqim yoq edi, shuning uchun ham uning dori-darmonlari meni davoladi.Shundan song, Ghinoning oz odamlari abbotga oz jihozlari bilan yaxshi bir xona yigishtirdi va ulkan bir taom tayyorladi, unga u prelatning butun xonadonini, shuningdek, koplab shahar aholisini buyurdi.

en: Next morning, he betook himself to the abbot and said to him, ‘Sir, since you feel yourself well, it is time to leave the inﬁrmary.’ Then, taking him by the hand, he brought him to the chamber prepared for him and leaving him there in company of his own people, occupied himself with caring that the banquet should be a magniﬁcent one.
uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab u abbotning oldiga bordi va unga dedi: Janob, ozingizni yaxshi his qilsangiz, shifoxonani tark etish vaqti keldi. Keyin, uni qolidan ushlab, u uchun tayyorlangan xonaga olib keldi va oz xalqi bilan birga qoldirdi, ziyofat ajoyib bolishi kerakligi haqida qaygurdi.

en: The abbot solaced himself awhile with his men and told them what his life had been since his capture, whilst they, on the other hand, avouched themselves all to have been wonder-well entreated of Ghino.
uz: Abbot bir oz vaqt o'z odamlari bilan tinchlandi va ularga asirga olinganidan beri hayoti qanday bo'lganini aytdi, ular esa, boshqa tomondan, Ghinodan ajoyib tarzda iltijo qilishganidan butunlay xavotirda edilar.

en: The eating- hour come, the abbot and the rest were well and orderly served with goodly viands and ﬁne wines, without Ghino yet letting himself be known of the prelate; but, after the latter had abidden some days on this wise, the outlaw, having let bring all his gear into one saloon and all his horses, down to the sorriest rouncey, into a courtyard that was under the windows thereof, betook himself to him and asked him how he did and if he deemed himself strong enough to take horse.
uz: Ovqatlanish vaqti keldi, abbat va qolganlar yaxshi va tartibli go'shtlar va nozik vinolar bilan ta'minlangan edilar, Ghino esa hali ruhoniyga ko'rinmas edi; lekin, oxirgi bir necha kun shu yo'l bilan yashiringanidan so'ng, noqonuniy, barcha jihozlarini bir saloonga va barcha otlarini, eng achinarli aylanishgacha, uning derazalari ostidagi hovliga olib kirgandan so'ng, unga qaradi va undan qanday qilganini, ot olish uchun o'zini yetarlicha kuchli deb hisoblaganini so'radi.

en: The abbot answered that he was strong enough and quite recovered of his stomach-complaint and that he should fare per- fectly well, once he should be out of Ghino’s hands.
uz: Abbat javob berdi: u yetarlicha kuchli va qorin shikoyatidan butunlay sog'aygan edi va Ghinoning qo'lidan chiqib ketgandan so'ng, amalda yaxshi ahvolda bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: Ghino then brought him into the saloon, wherein was his gear and all his train, and carrying him to a window, whence he might see all his horses, said, ‘My lord abbot, you must know that it was the being a gentleman and expelled from his house and poor and having many and puissant enemies, and not evilness of mind,
uz: Ghinno uni salonga olib kirdi, u yerda uning jihozlari va butun poyezdi bor edi, va uni derazaga olib bordi, u yerda barcha otlarini ko'rishi mumkin edi, dedi: "Ey janob abbat, bilishingiz kerakki, bu uydan haydalgan va kambag'al, ko'plab va qudratli dushmanlarga ega bo'lgan, va ong yomonligi emas edi."

en: that brought Ghino di Tacco (who is none other than myself) to be, for the defence of his life and his nobility, a highway-robber and an enemy of the court of Rome.
uz: Bu Ghino di Takkoning (o'zimdan boshqa hech kim yo'q) o'z hayoti va zodagonligini himoya qilish uchun yo'l o'g'ri va Rim saroyiga dushman bo'lishiga olib keldi.

en: Nevertheless, for that you seem to me a worthy gentleman, I purpose not, now that I have cured you of your stomach-complaint, to use you as I would another, from whom, he being in my hands as you are, I would take for myself such part of his goods as seemed well to me; nay, it is my intent that you, having regard to my need, shall appoint to me such part of your good as you yourself will.
uz: Shunga qaramay, sen menga munosib janobdek tuyulishing uchun, men seni qorningdan shikoyat qilishingdan tuzatganimdan so'ng, seni boshqa birovga o'xshab ishlatishni maqsad qilmayman. U mening qo'limda bo'lsa, uning mol-mulkining menga ma'qul kelgan qismini o'zimga oldim; aksincha, mening maqsadim shuki, sen mening ehtiyojimga qarab, o'zing xohlagan mol-mulkingning bir qismini menga tayinlaysan.

en: It is all here before you in its entirety and your horses you may from this window see in the courtyard; take, therefore, both part and all, as it pleaseth you, and from this time forth be it at your pleasure to go or to stay.’ The abbot marvelled to hear such generous words from a highway-robber and was exceeding well pleased therewith, insomuch that, his anger and despite being of a sudden fallen, nay, changed into goodwill, he became Ghino’s hearty friend and ran to embrace him, saying, ‘I vow to God that, to gain the friendship of a man such as I presently judge thee to be, I would gladly consent to suffer a far greater affront than that which meseemed but now thou hadst done me.
uz: Hammasi sizning oldingizda butunlay va otlaringizni shu derazadan hovlida ko'rishingiz mumkin; shuning uchun, xohlaganingizcha, hammasini oling, va bundan buyon borish yoki qolish sizning xohishingizga ko'ra bo'lsin." Abbot yo'l o'g'risidan bunday saxiy so'zlarni eshitib hayratga tushdi va bundan juda mamnun edi, shuning uchun g'azabi birdan tushgan bo'lsa ham, yo'q, balki yaxshilikka aylandi, u Ghinoning chin dildan do'stiga aylandi va uni quchoqlashga yugurdi, dedi: "Men Xudoga qasam ichamanki, men hozirda sizga qilgan ishingizdan ko'ra ko'proq jabr ko'rishga rozi bo'lgan odamning do'stligini qozonaman."

en: Accursed be fortune that constrained thee to so damnable a trade!’ Then, letting take of his many goods but a very few ne- cessary things, and the like of his horses, he left all the rest to Ghino and returned to Rome.
uz: La'nat bo'lsin senga, seni bunday la'nati kasbga majbur qilgan baxtga! Keyin, o'zining ko'p mol-mulkidan faqat oz-ozdan keraksiz narsalar va otlariga o'xshash narsalarni olib qo'yib, qolgan hamma narsani Ghinoga qoldirib, Rimga qaytib keldi.

en: The pope had had news of the taking of the abbot and albeit it had given him sore concern, he asked him, when he saw him, how the baths had proﬁted him; whereto he replied, smiling, ‘Holy Father, I found a worthy physician nearer than at the baths, who hath excellently well cured me’; and told him how, whereat the pope laughed, and the abbot, fol- lowing on his speech and moved by a magnanimous spirit, craved a boon of him.
uz: Rim Papasi abbotning olinishi haqida xabar topgan edi va garchi bu uni qattiq tashvishga solgan bo'lsa ham, u uni ko'rganida, vannalar unga qanday foyda keltirganini so'radi; unga tabassum bilan javob berdi: "Muqaddas Ota, men vannalardan ko'ra yaqinroq, meni mukammal davolagan munosib shifokorni topdim"; va unga Rim Papasi qanday kulganini va abbot uning so'zlariga quloq solib, bag'rikeng ruhdan ta'sirlanganini aytib berdi.

en: The pope, thinking he would demand otherwhat, freely offered to do that which he should ask; and the abbot said, ‘Holy Father, that which I mean to ask of you is that you restore your favour to Ghino di Tacco, my physician, for that, of all the men of worth and high account whom I ever knew, he is certes one of the most deserving; and for this ill that he doth, I hold it much more fortune’s fault than his; the which444 if you change by bestowing on him somewhat whereby he may live according to his condi- tion, I doubt not anywise but you will, in brief space of time, deem of him even as I do.’ The pope, who was great of soul and a lover of men of worth, hearing this, replied that he would gladly do it, an Ghino were indeed of such account as the abbot avouched, and bade the latter cause him come
uz: Rim Papasi, boshqa narsani talab qilmoqchi deb o'ylagan holda, o'zi so'ragan narsani bemalol qilishni taklif qildi; va abbat dedi: "Muqaddas Ota, sizdan so'ramoqchi bo'lgan narsa shuki, siz Ghinoni di Takkoga, mening shifokorimga o'z marhamatingizni qaytaring, chunki men uni tanigan barcha arzirli va yuqori martabali odamlardan biri, albatta, eng arzirli odamlardan biri; va u qilgan bu yomonlik uchun men uni undan ko'ra boyroq deb hisoblayman; 444 agar siz unga qisqa shartlariga ko'ra yashashi mumkin bo'lgan narsani berish orqali o'zgartirsangiz, men hech qanday shubha qilmayman, lekin vaqt o'tishi bilan siz uni men kabi deb hisoblaysiz."

en: thither in all security.
uz: U yerga barcha xavfsizlikda.

en: Accordingly, Ghino, at the abbot’s instance, came to court, upon that assurance, nor had he been long about the pope’s person ere the latter reputed him a man of worth and taking him into favour, bestowed on him a grand priory of those of the Hospitallers, having ﬁrst let make him a knight of that order; which ofﬁce he held whilst he lived, still approving himself a loyal friend and servant of Holy Church and of the Abbot of Cluny.”
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Ghino, abbatning o'rnida, shu ishonchga ko'ra sudga keldi, va u Papa shaxsi haqida uzoq vaqt bilmagan edi, toki u uni arzirli inson deb hisoblab, unga kasalxonachilarning ulkan ustunligini bergan, avval uni shu ordenning ritsariga aylantirib qo'ygan edi; bu lavozimni u tirikligida egallagan, o'zini Muqaddas Cherkov va Kluny abbatining sodiq do'sti va xizmatkori deb tasdiqlagan.

en: THE THIRD STORY Mithridanes, envying Nathan his hospitality and generosity and going to kill him, falleth in with himself, without knowing him, and is by him instructed of the course he shall take to accomplish his purpose; by means whereof he ﬁndeth him, as he himself had ordered it, in a coppice and recognizing him, is ashamed and becometh his friend.
uz: UCHINCHI HIKOYA Mitridanlar, Natanning mehmondo'stligi va saxiyligiga hasad qilib, uni o'ldirishga ketayotganda, uni bilmasdan o'zi bilan qulaydilar va o'z maqsadiga erishish uchun qanday yo'l tutishi kerakligi haqida unga ko'rsatmalar beradilar; shu orqali u uni o'zi buyurganidek, bir piyozda topadi va tan oladi, uyaladi va do'stini o'ldiradi.

en: Themseemed all they had heard what was like unto a miracle, to wit, that a churchman should have wrought anywhat magniﬁcently; but, as soon as the ladies had left discoursing thereof, the king bade Filostrato proceed, who forthright began, “Noble ladies, great was the magniﬁcence of the King of Spain and that of the Abbot of Cluny a thing belike never yet heard of; but maybe it will seem to you no less marvellous a thing to hear how a man, that he might do generosity to another who thirsted for his blood, nay, for the very breath of his nostrils, privily bethought himself to give them to him, ay, and would have done it, had the other willed to take them, even as I purpose to show you in a little story of mine.
uz: Ularning barchasi moʻjizaga oʻxshagan narsani eshitgandek tuyuldi, yaʼni cherkov aʼzosi qandaydir ajoyib ish qilishi kerak edi; lekin, xonimlar bu haqda gapirishni toʻxtatgandan soʻng, shoh Filostratga oʻtishni buyurdi va u toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri gap boshladi: Aziz xonimlar, Ispaniya qirolining va Kluny abbatining ulugʻvorligi hech qachon eshitilmagan narsa edi; lekin balki sizga odamning qonini tashvishga chanqoq boʻlgan boshqa bir kishiga qanday saxovat koʻrsatishi, hatto burun teshiklarining nafasini ham, oʻzi ularga berishni oʻylab, ey, va buni qilgan boʻlardi, boshqa odam ularni olishni xohlagan boʻlardi, men sizga kichik hikoyamda koʻrsatganimdek.

en: It is a very certain thing (if credit may be given to the report of divers Genoese and others who have been in those countries) that there was afore- time in the parts of Cattajo445 a man of noble lineage and rich beyond com- pare, called Nathan, who, having an estate adjoining a highway whereby as of necessity passed all who sought to go from the Ponant to the Levant or from the Levant to the Ponant, and being a man of great and generous soul and desirous that it should be known by his works, assembled a great multi- tude of artiﬁcers and let build there, in a little space of time, one of the fairest and greatest and richest palaces that had ever been seen, the which he caused excellently well furnished with all that was apt unto the reception and entertainment of gentlemen.
uz: Kattajo445 hududida allaqachon olijanob nasl-nasab va tengi yo'q boy bo'lgan Natan ismli odam borligi juda aniq (agar u yerda bo'lgan turli Genua va boshqalarning hisobotiga e'tibor qaratish mumkin bo'lsa), u Ponantdan Levantga yoki Levantdan Ponantga bormoqchi bo'lganlarning barchasini zarur bo'lganda kesib o'tadigan shosselga ega bo'lib, o'z asarlari bilan tanilishi kerak bo'lgan buyuk va saxiy inson bo'lgani uchun, u yerda ko'p sonli hunarmandchilikni yig'di va qisqa vaqt ichida ko'rilgan eng go'zal va eng boy saroylardan birini qurdi, u uni doimo qabul qilish va ko'ngilxushlik uchun mukammal jihozladi.

en: Then, having a great and goodly house-
uz: Keyin, ajoyib va chiroyli uyga ega bo'lish-

en: hold, he there received and honourably entertained, with joyance and good cheer, whosoever came and went; and in this praiseworthy usance he per- severed insomuch that not only the Levant, but well nigh all the Ponant, knew him by report.
uz: U yerda u xursandchilik va yaxshi xursandchilik bilan qabul qildi va hurmat bilan ko'rildi, kim kelgan va ketgan bo'lsa ham; va bu maqtovga sazovor urfda u nafaqat Levantni, balki butun Ponantni ham xabardor qilib tanishi uchun shunday kesib tashladi.

en: He was already full of years nor was therefore grown weary of the practice of hospitality, when it chanced that his fame reached the ears of a young man of a country not far from his own, by name Mith- ridanes, who, knowing himself no less rich than Nathan and waxing envious of his renown and his virtues, bethought himself to eclipse or shadow them with greater liberality.
uz: U allaqachon yoshga to'lgan edi, shuning uchun ham mehmondo'stlik amaliyotidan charchamagan edi, qachonki uning shuhrati o'zidan uncha uzoq bo'lmagan yurtning o'g'li Mith-ridanesning qulog'iga yetib bordi. U o'zini Natandan kam bo'lmagan boyligini va uning shuhrati va fazilatlariga hasad qilayotganini bilgan holda, o'zini ularni yanada katta erkinlik bilan qamrab olish yoki soyalash deb o'ylagan edi.

en: Accordingly, letting build a palace like unto that of Nathan, he proceeded to do the most unbounded courtesies446 that ever any did whosoever came or went about those parts, and in a short time he be- came without doubt very famous.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Natan saroyiga o'xshash saroy qurishga ruxsat berib, u o'sha joylarga kelgan yoki borgan har qanday odam qilgan eng cheksiz xushmuomalalik 446 ni amalga oshirdi va qisqa vaqt ichida u shubhasiz juda mashhur bo'ldi.

en: It chanced one day that, as he abode all alone in the midcourt of his palace, there came in, by one of the gates, a poor woman, who sought of him an alms and had it; then, coming in again to him by the second, she had of him another alms, and so on for twelve times in succession; but, whenas she returned for the thirteenth time, he said to her, ‘Good woman, thou art very diligent in this thine asking,’ and natheless gave her an alms.
uz: Bir kuni, u o'z saroyining o'rtasida yolg'iz yashaganida, darvozalardan birida bir bechora ayol kirib keldi. U undan sadaqa so'radi va unga berdi. Keyin, ikkinchi ayol uning oldiga qaytib kelib, u undan yana sadaqa qildi, va hokazo, ketma-ket o'n ikki marta; lekin, u o'n uchinchi marta qaytib kelganida, u unga dedi: "Yaxshi ayol, sen bu so'rovingda juda g'ayratli ekansan", va unga sadaqa berdi.

en: The old crone, hearing these words, exclaimed, ‘O liberality of Nathan, how mar- vellous art thou!
uz: Keksa tanishli odam bu so'zlarni eshitib, dedi: Ey Natanning bag'rikengligi, naqadar jozibali ekansan!

en: For that, entering in by each of the two-and-thirty gates which his palace hath, and asking of him an alms, never, for all that he showed, was I recognized of him, and still I had it; whilst here, having as yet come in but at thirteen gates, I have been both recognized and chidden.’ So saying, she went her ways and returned thither no more.
uz: Shuning uchun, uning saroyi bor ikki o'ttiz darvozadan har biriga kirib, undan sadaqa so'raganimda, hech qachon, u ko'rsatgan hamma narsa uchun, men undan tanilmagan edim va hali ham bor edim; bu yerda esa, hali o'n uchta darvozadan kirgan bo'lsam ham, men ham tanilganman va bardoshli bo'lganman." Shunday qilib, u o'z yo'lidan ketdi va u yerga qaytib kelmadi.

en: Mithridanes, hearing the old woman’s words, ﬂamed up into a furious rage, as he who held that which he heard of Nathan’s fame a diminishment of his own, and fell to saying, ‘Alack, woe is me!
uz: Mithridanlar kampirning so'zlarini eshitib, g'azabga to'lib ketdilar, xuddi Natanning shuhrati haqida eshitgan gapini o'ziga kamsitilgan deb hisoblagan va shunday dedi: "Alak, menga voy!"

en: When shall I attain to Nathan’s liberality in great things, let alone overpass it, as I seek to do, seeing that I cannot ap- proach him in the smallest?
uz: Natanning katta narsalarda erkinligiga qachon erisha olaman, undan o'tib ketmaydimi, men uni eng kichik narsalarda ham o'zib ketolmasligimni ko'rib, buni qilishga harakat qilamanmi?

en: Verily, I weary myself in vain, an I remove him not from the earth; wherefore, since eld carrieth him not off, needs must I with mine own hands do it without delay.’ Accordingly, rising upon that motion, he took horse with a small com- pany, without communicating his design to any, and came after three days whereas Nathan abode.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, men behuda charchadim, uni yerdan olib tashlamayman; shuning uchun, eld uni ko'tarib ketmagani uchun, buni o'z qo'llarim bilan kechiktirmasdan qilishim kerak. Shunday qilib, bu taklifga ko'ra, u ozgina qo'l bilan ot oldi, hech kimga o'z loyihasini aytmadi va uch kundan keyin keldi, Nathan esa u yerda turardi.

en: He arrived there at eventide and bidding his follow- ers make a show of not being with him and provide themselves with lodging, against they should hear farther from him, abode alone at no great distance from the fair palace, where he found Nathan all unattended, as he
uz: U u yerga kechqurun yetib keldi va o'z izdoshlariga u bilan bo'lmasligini ko'rsatish va o'zlarini uy bilan ta'minlashni buyurdi, aks holda ular undan uzoqroqqa, go'zal saroydan uncha uzoq bo'lmagan masofada yolg'iz yashashi kerak edi, u yerda Natanni butunlay qarovsiz holda topdi, chunki u...

en: went walking for his diversion, without any pomp of apparel, and knowing him not, asked him if he could inform him where Nathan dwelt.
uz: U o'zining qiziqarli yo'nalishi bo'yicha hech qanday dabdaba kiyimisiz yurdi va uni tanimay, undan Natan qayerda yashayotganini xabar bera olasizmi deb so'radi.

en: ‘My son,’ answered the latter cheerfully, ‘there is none in these parts who is better able than I to show thee that; wherefore, whenas it pleaseth thee, I will carry thee thither.’ Mithridanes rejoined that this would be very acceptable to him, but that, an it might be, he would fain be neither seen nor known of Nathan; and the latter said, ‘That also will I do, since it pleaseth thee.’ Mith- ridanes accordingly dismounted and repaired to the goodly palace, in com- pany with Nathan, who quickly engaged him in most pleasant discourse.
uz: O'g'lim,  javob berdi oxirgi xursand bo'lib, bu yerda senga buni ko'rsatishga mendan yaxshiroq qodir odam yo'q; shuning uchun, qachonki senga yoqsa, seni u yerga olib boraman. Mithridanes bu unga juda ma'qul bo'lishini, lekin, ehtimol, u Natan tomonidan na ko'rinmas va na ma'lum bo'lmasligini aytdi; va ikkinchisi dedi: Men ham shunday qilaman, chunki senga yoqadi. Mith-ridanes shunga ko'ra yaxshi saroyga tushdi va uni ta'mirladi, Natan bilan hamkorlikda, u uni eng yoqimli suhbatga jalb qildi.

en: There he caused one of his servants take the young man’s horse and putting his mouth to his ear, charged him take order with all those of the house, so none should tell the youth that he was Nathan; and so was it done.
uz: U yerda u o'z xizmatkorlaridan birini yigitning otini olib, uning og'zini qulog'iga qo'ydi va unga uydagilarning hammasi bilan kelishishni buyurdi, toki hech kim yigitga uning Natan ekanligini aytmasin; va shunday bo'ldi.

en: Moreover, he lodged him in a very goodly chamber, where none saw him, save those whom he had deputed to this service, and let entertain him with the utmost honour, himself bearing him company.
uz: Qolaversa, uni juda yaxshi xonada yotqizdi, uni faqat shu xizmatga tayinlaganlardan boshqa hech kim ko'rmasdi va uni eng katta sharaf bilan kutib olsin, o'zi hamrohlik qilsin.

en: After Mithridanes had abidden with him awhile on this wise, he asked him (albeit he held him in reverence as a father) who he was; to which Nathan answered, ‘I am an unworthy servant of Nathan, who have grown old with him from my childhood, nor hath he ever advanced me to other- what than that which thou seest me; wherefore, albeit everyone else is mighty well pleased with him, I for my part have little cause to thank him.’ These words afforded Mithridanes some hope of availing with more certi- tude and more safety to give effect to his perverse design, and Nathan very courteously asking him who he was and what occasion brought him into those parts and proffering him his advice and assistance insomuch as lay in his power, he hesitated awhile to reply, but, presently, resolving to trust himself to him, he with a long circuit of words447 required him ﬁrst of secrecy and after of aid and
uz: Mithridanes u bilan shu yoʻl bilan biroz yashiringanidan soʻng, u undan kimligini soʻradi (garchi u otasi sifatida hurmat qilgan boʻlsa ham); Natan javob berdi: "Men Natanning yaroqsiz xizmatkori boʻlaman, bolaligimdan u bilan birga keksalashganman, u meni hech qachon koʻrgan narsamdan boshqa narsaga oldinga siljitmagan; shuning uchun, hamma undan juda xursand boʻlsa ham, men uchun unga minnatdorchilik bildirishga hech qanday sabab yoʻq." Bu soʻzlar Mithridanesga oʻz loyihasiga koʻproq ishonch va xavfsizlik bilan taʼsir koʻrsatish uchun biroz umid berdi va Natan undan kim ekanligini va uni oʻsha joylarga nima olib kelganini soʻradi va unga maslahat va yordam berishni istadi, lekin u oʻzi bilan birga yordam berishga qaror qildi.

en: counsel and entirely discovered to him who he was and wherefore and on what motion he came.
uz: Maslahat berdi va uning kimligi, nega va qanday taklifga ko'ra kelgani to'liq ma'lum bo'ldi.

en: Nathan, hearing his dis- course and his cruel design, was inwardly all disordered; but nevertheless, without much hesitation, he answered him with an undaunted mind and a ﬁrm countenance, saying, ‘Mithridanes, thy father was a noble man and thou showest thyself minded not to degenerate from him, in having entered upon so high an emprise as this thou hast undertaken, to wit, to be liberal unto all; and greatly do I commend the jealousy thou bearest unto Nathan’s virtues, for that, were there many such,448 the world, that is most wretched, would soon become good.
uz: Natan uning buzuqligi va shafqatsiz niyatini eshitib, ichki tomondan tartibsiz edi; ammo shunga qaramay, ko'p ikkilanmasdan, u unga xotirjamlik va qat'iy yuz bilan javob berdi va dedi: "Mithridanlar, otang olijanob inson edi va sen undan voz kechmaslikka o'zingni intilyapsan, chunki sen bunday yuksak hokimiyatga kirding, ya'ni hamma uchun erkin bo'lish uchun; va men Natanning fazilatlariga bo'lgan rashkingga katta baho beraman, chunki, agar shunday ko'p bo'lganda, dunyo, eng nochor, tezda yaxshi bo'lardi."

en: The design that thou hast discovered to me I will
uz: Siz menga kashf etgan dizaynni men...

en: without fail keep secret; but for the accomplishment thereof I can rather give thee useful counsel than great help; the which is this.
uz: Albatta sir saqlang; lekin uning amalga oshirilishi uchun senga katta yordam berishdan ko'ra foydali maslahat bera olaman; bu shu.

en: Thou mayst from here see a coppice, maybe half a mile hence, wherein Nathan well nigh every morning walketh all alone, taking his pleasure there a pretty long while; and there it will be a light matter to thee to ﬁnd him and do thy will of him.
uz: Bu yerdan yarim mil uzoqlikda bir piyola ko'rishingiz mumkin, unda Natan har kuni ertalab yolg'iz yurib, u yerda ancha vaqt zavqlanib yuradi; va u yerda uni topish va undan o'z xohishingizni bajarish sizga oson bo'ladi.

en: If thou slay him, thou must, so thou mayst return home without hindrance, get thee gone, not by that way thou camest, but by that which thou wilt see issue forth of the coppice on the left hand, for that, albeit it is somewhat wilder, it is nearer to thy country and safer for thee.’ Mithridanes, having received this information and Nathan having taken leave of him, privily let his companions, who had, like himself, taken up their sojourn in the palace, know where they should look for him on the morrow; and the new day came, Nathan, whose intent was nowise at vari- ance with the counsel he had given Mithridanes nor was anywise changed, betook himself alone to the coppice, there to die.
uz: Agar uni o'ldirsang, to'xtovsiz uyga qaytishing kerak, ket, sen kelgan yo'l bilan emas, balki chap tomondagi misdan chiqqanini ko'rasan, chunki u biroz yovvoyiroq bo'lsa ham, sening mamlakatingga yaqinroq va senga xavfsizroqdir." Mithridanlar bu xabarni eshitib, Natan uni tark etganidan so'ng, o'zi kabi saroyda qolgan sheriklariga ertaga uni qayerdan qidirish kerakligini bilishlariga ruxsat berishdi. Va yangi kun keldi, Natan, uning maqsadi hozirda Mithridan bergan maslahatlari bilan bir xil edi va hech qanday o'zgarish bo'lmadi, o'zini o'sha yerda misga tashladi.

en: Meanwhile, Mithridanes arose and taking his bow and his sword, for other arms he had not, mounted to horse and made for the coppice, where he saw Nathan from afar go walk- ing all alone.
uz: Ayni paytda Mitridenes o'rnidan turib, kamonini va qilichini oldi, boshqa qurollari yo'q edi, otga o'tirdi va cho'tka yasadi, u yerda uzoqdan Natanni yolg'iz yurganini ko'rdi.

en: Being resolved, ere he attacked him, to seek to see him and hear him speak, he ran towards him and seizing him by the ﬁllet he had about his head, said, ‘Old man, thou art dead.’ Whereto Nathan answered no otherwhat than, ‘Then have I merited it.’ Mithridanes, hearing his voice and looking him in the face, knew him forthright for him who had so lovingly received him and familiarly companied with him and faithfully counselled him; whereupon his fury incontinent subsided and his rage was changed into shame.
uz: Qat'iyatli bo'lib, unga hujum qilmasidan oldin, uni ko'rishga va uning gapirganini eshitishga intilib, u uning yoniga yugurdi va boshidagi filedan ushladi, dedi: "Keksa odam, sen o'lgansan." Shunda Natan faqat: "Unda men bunga loyiq bo'ldim." Mithridanlar uning ovozini eshitib va yuziga qarab, uni shunday sevgi bilan qabul qilgan, unga yaqinlik bilan hamroh bo'lgan va unga sadoqat bilan maslahat bergan odam uchun aniq tanidilar; shundan so'ng uning g'azabi to'xtadi va g'azabi sharmandaga aylandi.

en: Accordingly, casting away the sword, which he had already pulled out to smite him, and lighting down from his horse, he ran, weeping, to throw himself at Nathan’s feet and said to him, ‘Now, dearest father, do I manifestly recognize your liberality, considering with what secrecy you are come hither to give me your life, whereof, without any reason, I showed myself desirous, and that to yourself; but God, more careful of mine honour than I myself, hath, in the extremest hour of need, opened the eyes of my understanding, which vile envy had closed.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uni urish uchun allaqachon tortib olgan qilichini tashlab, otidan tushib, u yig'lab yugurib, Natan oyoqlariga tashlandi va unga dedi: "Endi, aziz ota, men sizning saxiyligingizni aniq taniymanmi, siz menga jon berish uchun bu yerga qanday sir bilan kelganingizni hisobga olsam, men hech qanday sababsiz o'zimni xohlaganman va o'zingizga shunday ko'rsatdim; lekin Xudo, men o'zimdan ko'ra ko'proq hurmatga e'tiborli bo'lgan, eng chekka muhtojlikda, nafratli hasad yopiq edi.

en: Wherefore, the readier you have been to comply with me, so much the more do I confess myself beholden to do penance for my default.
uz: Shuning uchun, siz mendan rozi bo'lishga qanchalik tayyor bo'lsangiz, shunchalik ko'proq men o'zimning xatolarim uchun tavba qilishga majbur ekanligimni tan olaman.

en: Take, then, of me the vengeance which you deem conformable to my sin.’ Nathan raised Mithridanes to his feet and tenderly embraced and kissed him, saying, ‘My son, it needeth not that thou shouldst ask nor that I should
uz: Shunday ekan, mendan mening gunohimga mos keladigan qasos oling." Natan Mitridani oyoqqa turg'azdi va uni mayin quchoqlab, o'pdi va dedi: "O'g'lim, so'rashing ham, so'rashing ham shart emas."

en: grant forgiveness of thine emprise, whatever thou choosest to style it, whether wicked or otherwise; for that thou pursuedst it, not of hatred, but to win to be held better.
uz: O'z hukmronligingni kechiring, uni qanday uslubda o'rnatishni xohlasang ham, yomon bo'ladimi yoki boshqachami; chunki sen uni nafratdan emas, balki yaxshiroq ushlab turish uchun g'alaba qozonish uchun izlading.

en: Live, then, secure from me and be assured that there is no man alive who loveth thee as I do, having regard to the loftiness of thy soul, which hath given itself, not to the amassing of monies, as do the cov- etous, but to the expenditure of those that have been amassed.
uz: Shunday ekan, mendan xotirjam yashang va shunga amin bo'lingki, seni men kabi sevadigan hech kim yashamaydi, joningning baxtiga qarab, u o'zini pul yig'ishga emas, balki yig'ilganlarning xarajatlariga bag'ishladi.

en: Neither be thou ashamed of having sought to slay me, so though mightest become fam- ous, nor think that I marvel thereat.
uz: Meni o'ldirmoqchi bo'lganingdan uyalma, garchi shuhrat qozonishing mumkin bo'lsa ham, va men bundan hayratlanaman deb o'ylama.

en: The greatest emperors and the most il- lustrious kings have, with well nigh none other art than that of slaying, not one man, as thou wouldst have done, but an inﬁnite multitude of men, and burning countries and razing cities, enlarged their realms and consequently their fame; wherefore, an thou wouldst, to make thyself more famous, have slain me only, thou diddest no new nor extraordinary thing, but one much used.’ Mithridanes, without holding himself excused of his perverse design, commended the honourable excuse found by Nathan and came, in course of converse with him, to say that he marvelled beyond measure how he could have brought himself to meet his death and have gone so far as even to give him means and counsel to that end; whereto quoth Nathan, ‘Mithridanes, I would not have thee marvel at my resolution nor at the counsel I gave thee, for that, since I have been mine own master
uz: Eng buyuk imperatorlar va eng shonli podshohlarning o'ldirishdan boshqa hunari yo'q edi, xuddi sen xohlaganingdek, birorta odam emas, balki cheksiz ko'p sonli odamlar, yonayotgan mamlakatlar va vayron qiluvchi shaharlar o'z saltanatlarini va shu sababli ularning shuhratini kattalashtirdi; shuning uchun, o'zingni mashhurroq qilmoqchi bo'lsang, faqat meni o'ldir, sen hech qanday yangi yoki g'ayrioddiy narsa qilmading, lekin juda ko'p ishlatding.

en: and have addressed myself to do that same thing which thou hast undertaken to do, there came never any to my house but I contented him, so far as in me lay, of that which was re- quired of me by him.
uz: va o'zimga shunday qilishga murojaat qildim, xuddi sen ham qilishga qaror qilganingdek, hech kim uyimga kelmadi, lekin men uni, men yotganimgacha, mendan so'ragan narsadan mamnun qildim.

en: Thou camest hither, desirous of my life; wherefore, learning that thou soughtest it, I straightway determined to give it thee, so thou mightest not be the only one to depart hence without his wish; and in order that thou mightest have thy desire, I gave thee such counsel as I thought apt to enable thee to have my life and not lose thine own; and there- fore I tell thee once more and pray thee, an it please thee, take it and satisfy thyself thereof.
uz: Sen bu yerga kelib, hayotimni xohlaysan; shuning uchun, sening uni izlayotganingni bilib, men uni senga berishga darhol qaror qildim, toki sen o'z xohishisiz bu yerdan ketadigan yagona odam bo'lmasang; va sening xohishing bo'lishi uchun, senga hayotimni topishga va o'zingnikini yo'qotmaslikka imkon beradigan maslahat berdim; va shundan keyin yana bir bor senga aytaman va iltimos qilaman, agar senga yoqsa, uni ol va o'zingni qondir.

en: I know not how I may better bestow it.
uz: Uni qanday qilib yaxshiroq sovg'a qilishim mumkinligini bilmayman.

en: These fourscore years have I occupied it and used it about my pleasures and my diversions, and I know that in the course of nature, according as it fareth with other men and with things in general, it can now be left me but a little while longer; wherefore I hold it far better to bestow it by way of gift, like as I have still given and expended my [other] treasures, than to seek to keep it until such times as it shall be taken from me by nature against my will.
uz: Bu to'rt yil uni o'z zavqlarim va qiziqarli mashg'ulotlarim uchun band qildim va ishlatdim. Va bilamanki, tabiat jarayonida, boshqa odamlar va umuman narsalar bilan bo'lgani kabi, u menga biroz ko'proq qoldirilishi mumkin; shuning uchun men uni sovg'a sifatida berishdan ancha yaxshiroqman, xuddi men hali ham bergan va sarflagan boshqa xazinalarim kabi, uni tabiat tomonidan mendan o'z xohishimga zid ravishda olinadigan vaqtlargacha saqlashga urinishdan ko'ra.

en: To give an hundred years is no great boon; how much less, then, is it to give
uz: Yuz yil berish katta marhamat emas; undan ham kamroq, demak, berish kerak.

en: the six or eight I have yet to abide here?
uz: Olti yoki sakkizta hali bu yerda qolishim kerakmi?

en: Take it, then, an it like thee.
uz: Uni ol, unda ham senga o'xshab.

en: Prithee, then, take it, an thou have a mind thereto; for that never yet, what while I have lived here, have I found any who hath desired it, nor know I when I may ﬁnd any such, an thou, who demandest it, take it not.
uz: Xo'sh, uni ol, chunki sening bu haqda fikring bor; chunki men bu yerda yashab yurganimda, uni xohlagan odamni topmadimmi, qachon shunday odamni topishimni ham bilmayman, va uni talab qilgan sen uni olma.

en: And even should I chance to ﬁnd anyone, I know that, the longer I keep it, the less worth will it be; therefore, ere it wax sorrier, take it, I beseech thee.’ Mithridanes was sore abashed and replied, ‘God forbid I should, let alone take and sever from you a thing of such price as your life, but even desire to do so, as but late I did —your life, whose years far from seeking to lessen, I would willingly add thereto of mine own!’ Whereto Nathan straightway re- joined, ‘And art thou indeed willing, it being in thy power to do it, to add of thy years unto mine and in so doing, to cause me do for thee that which I never yet did for any man, to wit, take of thy good, I who never yet took aught of others?’ ‘Ay am I,’ answered Mithridanes in haste.
uz: Va hatto agar biror odamni topsam ham, bilaman, qancha uzoq saqlasam, shuncha qimmat bo'lmaydi; shuning uchun, afsuslanishidan oldin, uni oling, iltimos,  Mithridanes juda xafa bo'lib javob berdi: Xudo saqlasin, men sizdan hayotingiz kabi qimmatbaho narsani olib tashlamasdan, hatto buni xohlamasdan ham, lekin men buni kechroq qilganimdek  hayotingizni, uning yillari kamaytirishga urinishidan uzoqroq bo'lganini, o'zimnikiga qo'shishni xohlardim! Nathan darhol qo'shildi: Va siz haqiqatan ham buni qilishga qodirsiz, o'z yillaringizni qo'shish uchun va shunday qilish uchun, men hech qachon hech kim uchun qilmagan narsani qilish uchun, men sizni hech kimga yaxshilik qilish uchun, men sizni kimdan hech qachon olmaganingizni olish uchun, men sizni hech qachon... deb javob berdi.

en: ‘Then,’ said Nathan, ‘thou must do as I shall bid thee.
uz: Unda,  dedi Natan,  men senga buyurganimdek qilishing kerak.

en: Thou shalt take up thine abode, young as thou art, here in my house and bear the name of Nathan, whilst I will betake myself to thy house and let still call myself Mithridanes.’ Quoth Mithridanes, ‘An I knew how to do as well as you have done and do, I would, without hesitation, take that which you proffer me; but, since me- seemeth very certain that my actions would be a diminishment of Nathan’s fame and as I purpose not to mar in another that which I know not how to order in myself, I will not take it.’ These and many other courteous dis- courses having passed between them, they returned, at Nathan’s instance, to the latter’s palace, where he entertained Mithridanes with the utmost honour sundry days, heartening him in his great and noble purpose with all manner of wit and wisdom.
uz: "Sen o'zingning uyingda, yoshligingda o'zingning maskaningni olgin va Natan ismini ko'targin, shu bilan birga men o'z uyingda o'zimni Mithridan deb atayman." Mithridanes aytdi: "Men sening qilganingdek yaxshi ish qilishni bilardim, men hech ikkilanmay, sen menga aytganingni qabul qilaman; lekin, mening harakatlarim Natanning shuhratini kamaytirishiga juda ishonchim komil bo'lgani uchun va men o'zimda qanday buyurishni bilmagan boshqa bir narsani o'ylamasligim uchun, men uni qabul qilmayman." Bu va boshqa ko'plab odobsiz kurslar o'rtasida o'tib, ular Natanning so'nggi kunlariga qaytdilar, u yerda Mithridanni o'zining ulug'vorlik va donoligi bilan ko'p marta qabul qildi."

en: Then, Mithridanes desiring to return to his own house with his company, he dismissed him, having throughly given him to know that he might never avail to outdo him in liberality.”
uz: Keyin, Mitridenes o'z uyiga o'z kompaniyasi bilan qaytishni xohlagan holda, uni ishdan bo'shatdi va unga hech qachon undan ko'ra erkinroq bo'lish imkoni bo'lmasligini bildirish uchun uni butunlay ishdan bo'shatdi.

en: THE FOURTH STORY Messer Gentile de’ Carisendi, coming from Modona, taketh forth of the sepulchre a lady whom he loveth and who hath been buried for dead.
uz: TO'RTINCHI HIKOYA Messer Gentile de  Carisendi, Modona shahridan kelib, qabrdan o'zi sevgan va o'lik deb dafn etilgan bir xonimni olib chiqadi.

en: The lady, restored to life, beareth a male child and Messer Gentile restoreth her and her son to Niccoluccio Caccianimico, her husband.
uz: Hayotga qaytgan xonim o'g'il tug'adi va Messer Gentile uni va o'g'lini turmush o'rtog'i Nikcoluccio Caccianimicoga qaytaradi.

en: It seemed to all a marvellous thing that a man should be lavish of his own blood and they declared Nathan’s liberality to have verily transcended that of the King of Spain and the Abbot of Cluny.
uz: Odam o'z qonini boy berishi hammaga ajoyib narsadek tuyuldi va ular Natanning erkinligini Ispaniya qiroli va Kluny abbatining erkinligidan haqiqatan ham ustun deb e'lon qilishdi.

en: But, after enough to one and the other effect had been said thereof, the king, looking towards Lauretta, signed to her that he would have her tell, whereupon she straightway began, “Young ladies, magniﬁcent and goodly are the things that have been re- counted, nor meseemeth is there aught left unto us who have yet to tell, wherethrough we may range a story-telling, so throughly have they all449 been occupied with the loftiness of the magniﬁcences related, except we have recourse to the affairs of love, which latter afford a great abundance of matter for discourse on every subject; wherefore, at once on this account and for that the theme is one to which our age must needs especially incline us, it pleaseth me to relate to you an act of magnanimity done by a lover, which, all things considered, will peradventure appear to you nowise inferi- or to any of those already set forth, if it be
uz: Lekin, bu va bu ta'sir haqida gapirilgandan so'ng, podshoh, Laurettaga qarab, unga aytmoqchi bo'lishiga imzo chekdi, shundan so'ng u darhol boshladi: "Yosh xonimlar, qayta sanalgan narsalar ajoyib va yaxshi, demak, bizga hali aytib berish kerak bo'lgan hech narsa qolmadi, shu orqali biz hikoya qilishimiz mumkin, shuning uchun ularning barchasi 449 bilan bog'liq ulug'vorliklarning balandligi bilan band bo'ldi, biz sevgi ishlariga murojaat qildik, bu esa har bir mavzuda muhokamaga juda ko'p narsa beradi; shuning uchun, agar bu mavzu ayniqsa yoshimiz bizni jalb qilishi kerak bo'lsa, men sizga sevgilik harakatlari bilan bog'lanishni xohlayman, agar u allaqachon shunday bo'lsa,

en: true that treasures are lavished, enmities forgotten and life itself, nay, what is far more, honour and renown, exposed to a thousand perils, so we may avail to possess the thing beloved.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, xazinalar boy berilgan, dushmanlik unutilgan va hayotning o'zi, yo'q, undan ham ko'proq, sharaf va shuhrat ming xavf ostida, shunday qilib biz sevimli narsaga ega bo'lishdan foydalanishimiz mumkin.

en: There was, then, in Bologna, a very noble city of Lombardy, a gentleman very notable for virtue and nobility of blood, called Messer Gentile Caris- endi, who, being young, became enamoured of a noble lady called Madam Catalina, the wife of one Niccoluccio Caccianimico; and for that he was ill repaid of his love by the lady, being named provost of Modona, he betook
uz: O'shanda Bolonyada, Lombardiyaning juda olijanob shahrida, fazilatlari va qon olijanobligi bilan juda mashhur bo'lgan janob bor edi, u Messer Gentile Caris edi. Endi u yosh bo'lganida, bir Niccoluccio Caccianimico xotini Madam Catalina ismli olijanob xonimga oshiq bo'lib qoldi; va shuning uchun u xonim tomonidan o'z muhabbatidan yomon javob oldi, u Modona provost deb tayinlandi.

en: himself thither, as in despair of her.
uz: o'zini u yerga, xuddi undan umidsizdek.

en: Meanwhile, Niccoluccio being absent from Bologna and the lady having, for that she was with child, gone to abide at a country house she had maybe three miles distant from the city, she was suddenly seized with a grievous ﬁt of sickness,450 which overcame her with such violence that it extinguished in her all sign of life, so that she was even adjudged dead of divers physicians; and for that her nearest kins- women declared themselves to have had it from herself that she had not been so long pregnant that the child could be fully formed, without giving themselves farther concern, they buried her, such as she was, after much lamentation, in one of the vaults of a neighbouring church.
uz: Ayni paytda, Nikolutsiyo Bolonyadan yo'q edi va xonim homiladorligi sababli, shahardan taxminan uch milya uzoqroq bo'lgan qishloq uyida yashashga borgan edi, u to'satdan og'ir kasallikka chalingan edi. 450 Bu uni shunchalik zo'ravonlik bilan yengib o'tdi, hatto uni turli xil shifokorlar o'limiga hukm qilishdi; va shuning uchun uning eng yaqin qarindoshlari - ayollar o'zlaridan bola to'liq shakllanishi mumkinligini uzoq vaqt o'tmaganini, o'zlarini tashvishtirmasdan, uni xuddi ko'p afsusdan keyin qo'shni cherkovning g'aznasidan birida ko'mib qo'yishdi.

en: The thing was forthright signiﬁed by a friend of his to Messer Gentile, who, poor as he had still been of her favour, grieved sore therefor and ulti- mately said in himself, ‘Harkye, Madam Catalina, thou art dead, thou of whom, what while thou livedst, I could never avail to have so much as a look; wherefore, now thou canst not defend thyself, needs must I take of thee a kiss or two, all dead as thou art.’ This said, he took order so his going should be secret and it being presently night, he mounted to horse with one of his servants and rode, without halting, till he came whereas the lady was buried and opened the sepulchre with all despatch.
uz: Bu narsa uning do'sti Messer Gentilega aniq ma'lum bo'ldi, u, hali ham uning marhamatiga ega bo'lgani uchun, juda qayg'urdi va oxir-oqibat o'zida dedi: "Harkye, Madam Catalina, sen o'liksan, sen tirik ekansan, men hech qachon unga bunchalik ko'z tashlashga qodir emas edim; shuning uchun, endi o'zingni himoya qila olmaysan, men sendan bir-ikki o'pich olishim kerak, hamma o'lik bo'lgani kabi."

en: Then, entering therein, he laid himself beside her and putting his face to hers, kissed her again and again with many tears.
uz: Keyin u yerga kirib, uning yoniga yotdi va yuzini uning yoniga qo'ydi, uni qayta-qayta ko'p yosh bilan o'pdi.

en: But presently —as we see men’s appetites never abide content within any limit, but still desire farther, and especially those of lovers —having bethought himself to tarry there no longer, he said, ‘Marry, now that I am here, why should I not touch her somedele on the breast?
uz: Ammo hozirgi vaqtda  ko'rib turganimizdek, erkaklarning ishtahalari hech qachon hech qanday chegara ichida qoniqmaydi, lekin baribir uzoqroqqa, ayniqsa oshiqlarning ishtahalariga intiladi  u yerda qolishni o'ylamagan edi, u dedi: Marry, endi men shu yerdaman, nega uning ko'kragidagi somedelega tegmasligim kerak?

en: I may never touch her more, nor have I ever yet done so.’ Accord- ingly, overcome with this desire, he put his hand into her bosom and hold- ing it there awhile, himseemed he felt her heart beat somewhat.
uz: Men unga hech qachon boshqa tegmasligim mumkin, hech qachon ham tegmaganman." Shunga ko'ra, bu istakdan g'olib bo'lib, u qo'lini uning bag'riga qo'ydi va uni bir oz ushlab turdi, go'yo uning yuragi biroz urayotganini his qilgandek edi.

en: Thereupon, putting aside all fear, he sought more diligently and found that she was cer- tainly not dead, scant and feeble as he deemed the life [that lingered in her]; wherefore, with the help of his servant, he brought her forth of the tomb, as softliest he might, and setting her before him on his horse, carried her priv- ily to his house in Bologna.
uz: Shundan so'ng, barcha qo'rquvni chetga surib, u yanada astoydil izladi va u hayot deb hisoblaganidek, albatta o'lik emasligini, kam va zaif ekanligini topdi; shuning uchun, xizmatkorining yordami bilan, u uni qabrdan imkon qadar yumshoqroq olib chiqdi va o'z otida uning oldiga qo'ydi, uni Bolonyadagi uyiga olib bordi.

en: There was his mother, a worthy and discreet gentlewoman, and she, after she had heard everything at large from her son, moved to compassion, quietly addressed herself by means of hot baths and great ﬁres to recall the strayed life to the lady, who, coming presently to herself, heaved a great sigh and said, ‘Ah me, where am I?’ To which the good lady replied, ‘Be of
uz: Uning onasi bor edi, munosib va ehtiyotkor muloyim ayol, va u o'g'lidan hamma narsani eshitgach, rahm-shafqatga to'lib, xonimga adashgan hayotni eslash uchun issiq vannalar va katta olovlar orqali sokin murojaat qildi. Xonim yaqinda o'ziga kelib, katta xo'rsindi va dedi: "Ah men, qayerdaman?" Yaxshi xonim javob berdi: "Bo'l.

en: good comfort; thou art in safety.’ Madam Catalina, collecting herself, looked about her and knew not aright where she was; but, seeing Messer Gentile before her, she was ﬁlled with wonderment and besought his mother to tell her how she came thither; whereupon Messer Gentile related to her everything in order.
uz: Yaxshi tasalli; sen xavfsizsan. Madam Katalina o'zini yig'ishtirib, unga qaradi va qayerda ekanligini aniq bilmas edi; lekin, uning oldida Messer Gentile ni ko'rib, hayratga to'ldi va onasidan u yerga qanday yetib kelganini aytishini so'radi; shundan so'ng Messer Gentile unga hamma narsani tartibli tarzda aytdi.

en: At this she was sore afﬂicted, but presently rendered him such thanks as she might and after conjured him, by the love he had erst borne her and of his courtesy, that she might not in his house suffer at his hands aught that should be anywise contrary to her honour and that of her husband and that, as soon as the day should be come, he would suffer her return to her own house.
uz: Shunda u juda azob chekdi, lekin darhol unga imkon qadar minnatdorchilik bildirdi va uni so'raganidan so'ng, unga birinchi bo'lib bergan muhabbati va mehribonligi tufayli, u uning uyida uning va erining sharafiga zid bo'ladigan hech qanday narsadan aziyat chekmasligi va kun kelishi bilanoq, u o'z uyiga qaytishiga ruxsat berishi kerak edi.

en: ‘Madam,’ answered Messer Gentile, ‘whatso- ever may have been my desire of time past, I purpose not, either at this present or ever henceforth, (since God hath vouchsafed me this grace that He hath restored you to me from death to life, and that by means of the love I have hitherto borne you), to use you either here or elsewhere otherwise than as a dear sister; but this my service that I have done you tonight mer- iteth some recompense; wherefore I would have you deny me not a favour that I shall ask you.’ The lady very graciously replied that she was ready to do his desire, so but she might and it were honourable.
uz: Xonim,  javob berdi Messer Gentile,  hech qachon o'tmishdagi orzuim bo'lmagan bo'lishi mumkin edi, men hozir ham, bundan keyin ham, (chunki Xudo menga sizni o'limdan hayotga qaytarganligi va shu kungacha sizga bergan muhabbatim orqali) sizni bu yerda yoki boshqa joyda aziz opa-singlim sifatida ishlatishni maqsad qilmaganman; lekin bu mening sizga bugun kechqurun qilgan xizmatim  bu qandaydir mukofotdir; shuning uchun sizdan so'rashim kerak bo'lgan bir marhamatni rad etishni xohlardim. Xonim juda mehribonlik bilan javob berdi: u o'z xohishini bajarishga tayyor edi, lekin u shunday edi va u sharafli edi.

en: Then said he, ‘Madam, your kinsfolk and all the Bolognese believe and hold you for certain to be dead, where- fore there is no one who looketh for you more at home, and therefore I would have you of your favour be pleased to abide quietly here with my mother till such time as I shall return from Modona, which will be soon.
uz: Shunda u aytdi: Xonim, qarindoshlaringiz va barcha Bolonyaliklar sizni o'limingizga ishonishadi va ishonishadi, chunki uyda sizni ko'proq qidiradigan hech kim yo'q, shuning uchun sizdan onam bilan tinchgina shu yerda qolishingizni so'rayman, Modonadan qaytib kelgan vaqtimgacha, bu tez orada bo'ladi.

en: And the reason for which I require you of this is that I purpose to make a dear and solemn present of you to your husband in the presence of the most notable citizens of this place.’ The lady, confessing herself beholden to the gentleman and that his request was an honourable one, determined to do as he asked, how much soever she desired to gladden her kinsfolk of her life,451 and so she promised it to him upon her faith.
uz: Va men sizdan buni talab qilishimning sababi shundaki, men sizdan eringizga shu joyning eng taniqli fuqarolari huzurida hurmatli va tantanali sovg'a qilishni niyat qilaman." Xonim janobga qarzdorligini tan olib, uning so'rovi sharafli ekanligini tan oldi va u so'raganidek qilishga qaror qildi, qarindoshlarini hayotidan qanchalik xursand qilmoqchi bo'lsa, 451 va shuning uchun u unga o'z diniga asoslanib va'da berdi.

en: Hardly had she made an end of her reply, when she felt the time of her delivery to be come and not long after, being lovingly tended of Messer Gentile’s mother, she gave birth to a goodly male child, which manifold redoubled his gladness and her own.
uz: U javobini deyarli tugata olmaganda, tug'ilish vaqti yaqinlashayotganini his qildi va ko'p o'tmay, Messer Gentile onasining mehr bilan g'amxo'rligi tufayli, u yaxshi bir o'g'il bolani dunyoga keltirdi, bu uning xursandchiligini va o'zining xursandchiligini bir necha barobar oshirdi.

en: Messer Gentile took order that all things needful should be forthcom- ing and that she should be tended as she were his proper wife and presently returned in secret to Modona.
uz: Messer Gentile barcha zaruriy narsalar tayyor bo'lishi va unga o'ziga xos xotin kabi g'amxo'rlik qilinishi kerakligini buyurdi va hozirda Modonaga yashirincha qaytib keldi.

en: There, having served the term of his ofﬁce and being about to return to Bologna, he took order for the holding of a great and goodly banquet at his house on the morning he was to enter the
uz: U yerda, o'z lavozim muddatini o'tab bo'lgach va Bolonyaga qaytmoqchi bo'lgach, u ertalab kirishi kerak bo'lgan kuni o'z uyida katta va yaxshi ziyofat o'tkazish uchun buyurtma oldi.

en: city, and thereto he bade many gentlemen of the place, amongst whom was Niccoluccio Caccianimico.
uz: shahar, va u yerga u joydagi ko'plab janoblarni taklif qildi, ularning orasida Nikolutsiyo Kaksianimiko ham bor edi.

en: Accordingly, when he returned and dismounted, he found them all awaiting him, as likewise the lady, fairer and sounder than ever, and her little son in good case, and with inexpressible joy seating his guests at table, he let serve them magniﬁcently with various meats.
