en: ternight, and now this man cometh and saith that it was not thou, but he that slew him.’ Gisippus looked and seeing that it was Titus, perceived full well that he did this to save him, as grateful for the service aforetime received from him; wherefore, weeping for pity, ‘Varro,’ quoth he, ‘indeed it was I slew him and Titus his solicitude for my safety is now too late.’ Titus on the other hand, said, ‘Praetor, do as thou seest, this man is a stranger and was found without arms beside the murdered man, and thou mayst see that his wretchedness giveth him occasion to wish to die; wherefore do thou release him and punish me, who have deserved it.’ Varro marvelled at the insistence of these two and beginning now to presume that neither of them might be guilty, was casting about for a means of acquitting them, when, behold, up came a youth called Publius Ambustus, a man of notorious ill life
uz: "Uchinchi tunda bu odam kelib, uni o'ldirgan sen emas, balki u edi, deydi." Gisippus ko'rib, bu Tit ekanligini ko'rib, uni qutqarish uchun shunday qilganini yaxshi angladi, chunki u undan oldindan olingan xizmat uchun minnatdor edi; shuning uchun, rahm-shafqatdan yig'lab, "Varro," dedi u, "haqiqatan ham uni o'ldirdim va Tit mening xavfsizligimga intilishi endi juda kech edi." "Praytor, ko'rganingdek qil, bu odam begona va o'ldirilgan odam yonida qurolsiz topilgan, va sen uning shafqati unga o'lishni xohlashini ko'rasan; shuning uchun uni ozod qil va meni jazolagin, chunki bu mening xavfsizligimga arziydi."

en: and known to all the Romans for an arrant rogue, who had actually done the murder and knowing neither of the twain to be guilty of that whereof each accused himself, such was the pity that overcame his heart for the inno- cence of the two friends that, moved by supreme compassion, he came be- fore Varro and said, ‘Praetor, my fates impel me to solve the grievous con- tention of these twain and I know not what God within me spurreth and im- portuneth me to discover to thee my sin.
uz: va barcha rimliklarga taniqli bo'lgan, aslida qotillik qilgan va har birining o'zini ayblaganida hech biri aybdor emasligini bilgan, ikki do'stning beg'uborligi uchun yuragini bosib o'tgan achinish shunday ediki, oliy rahm-shafqatdan ta'sirlanib, u Varro huzuriga kelib dedi: "Praytor, mening taqdirim meni shu Twainlarning qayg'uli xotirjamligini hal qilishga undaydi va men ichimdagi Xudo meni senga gunohimni ochishga undaydigan narsani bilmayman."

en: Know, then, that neither of these men is guilty of that whereof each accuseth himself.
uz: Shuni bilingki, bu odamlarning hech biri o'zini ayblaydigan narsada aybdor emas.

en: I am verily he who slew yonder man this morning towards daybreak and I saw this poor wretch asleep there, what while I was in act to divide the booty gotten with him whom I slew.
uz: Men bugun ertalab tong otishi arafasida o'sha odamni o'ldirgan odamman va u yerda shu bechora bechora uxlayotganini ko'rdim, men o'ldirgan odam bilan qo'lga kiritilgan o'ljani bo'lish uchun harakat qilayotganimda.

en: There is no need for me to excuse Titus; his renown is every- where manifest and everyone knoweth him to be no man of such a condi- tion.
uz: Titni kechirishga hojat yo'q; uning shuhrati hamma joyda namoyon bo'ladi va hamma uni bunday holatdagi odam emasligini biladi.

en: Release him, therefore, and take of me that forfeit which the laws im- pose on me.’ By this Octavianus had notice of the matter and causing all three be brought before him, desired to hear what cause had moved each of them to seek to be the condemned man.
uz: Uni qo'yib yuboringlar, shuning uchun, va qonunlar menga yuklaydigan o'sha tovonni mendan olinglar." Shu bilan Oktavian bu masalani bilib, uchalasi ham uning oldiga kelishini xohladi, ularning har biriga hukm qilingan odam bo'lishga nima sabab bo'lganini eshitishni xohladi.

en: Accordingly, each related his own story, whereupon Octavianus released the two friends, for that they were innocent, and pardoned the other for the love of them.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, har biri o'z hikoyasini aytib berdi, shundan so'ng Oktavian ikki do'stini ozod qildi, chunki ular begunoh edilar va ularni sevgani uchun boshqa do'stini kechirdi.

en: Thereupon Titus took his Gisippus and ﬁrst reproaching him sore for lukewarmness471 and difﬁdence, rejoiced in him with marvellous great joy and carried him to his house, where Sophronia with tears of compassion received him as a brother.
uz: Shundan so'ng, Tit Gisippni olib, avval uni iliqligi va ishonchsizligi uchun qattiq tanqid qildi. U undan ajoyib quvonch bilan quvonib, uni o'z uyiga olib bordi. U yerda Sofron uni achchiq ko'z yoshlari bilan birodar sifatida qabul qildi.

en: Then, having awhile recruited him with rest and refreshment and reclothed him and restored him to such a habit as sorted with his worth and quality, he ﬁrst
uz: Keyin, uni bir oz dam olish va tetiklantirish bilan yollab, qayta kiydirib, qadri va sifatiga mos keladigan odatga qaytargach, u avval...

en: shared all his treasures and estates in common with him and after gave him to wife a young sister of his, called Fulvia, saying, ‘Gisippus, henceforth it resteth with thee whether thou wilt abide here with me or return with everything I have given thee into Achaia.’ Gisippus, constrained on the one hand by his banishment from his native land and on the other by the love which he justly bore to the cherished friendship of Titus, consented to be- come a Roman and accordingly took up his abode in the city, where he with his Fulvia and Titus with his Sophronia lived long and happily, still abiding in one house and waxing more friends (an more they might be) every day.
uz: U bilan birga barcha xazinalari va mulkini bo'lishdi va keyin unga Fulviya ismli yosh singlisini xotinlikka berdi va dedi: "Gisippus, endi sen bilan shu yerda qolishing yoki men senga bergan hamma narsam bilan Axayaga qaytishing senga tegishli." Gisippus, bir tomondan o'z ona yurtidan surgun qilinishi va ikkinchi tomondan Titning aziz do'stligiga bo'lgan muhabbati tufayli cheklangan, Rim fuqarosi bo'lishga rozi bo'ldi va shunga ko'ra o'z uyini shu shaharda egalladi. U Fulviya va Tit bilan birga Sofhroniya bilan uzoq va baxtli yashadi, hali ham bir uyda yashardi va har kuni ko'proq do'st orttirardi.

en: A most sacred thing, then, is friendship and worthy not only of especial reverence, but to be commended with perpetual praise, as the most discreet mother of magnanimity and honour, the sister of gratitude and charity and the enemy of hatred and avarice, still, without waiting to be entreated, ready virtuously to do unto others that which it would have done to itself.
uz: Shunday ekan, eng muqaddas narsa do'stlikdir va nafaqat alohida hurmatga loyiq, balki doimiy maqtov bilan maqtovga sazovor bo'lishdir, mehribonlik va hurmatning eng sokin onasi, minnatdorchilik va xayriya singlisi hamda nafrat va ochko'zlik dushmani sifatida, hali ham iltimos qilinishini kutmasdan, o'ziga qilgan ishini boshqalarga qilishga fazilat bilan tayyor.

en: Nowadays its divine effects are very rarely to be seen in any twain, by the fault and to the shame of the wretched cupidity of mankind, which, regard- ing only its own proﬁt, hath relegated it to perpetual exile, beyond the ex- tremest limits of the earth.
uz: Hozirgi kunda uning ilohiy ta'siri hech bir insonda kamdan-kam hollarda ko'rinadi, insoniyatning bechora baxilligining aybi va sharmandaligi tufayli, u faqat o'z foydasini hisobga olmaguncha, uni yer yuzidagi eng dahshatli chegaralardan tashqari abadiy surgunlikka tushirdi.

en: What love, what riches, what kinship, what, ex- cept friendship, could have made Gisippus feel in his heart the ardour, the tears and the sighs of Titus with such efﬁcacy as to cause him yield up to his friend his betrothed bride, fair and gentle and beloved of him?
uz: Qanday sevgi, qanday boylik, qanday qarindoshlik, qanday eski do'stlik Gisippni o'z qalbida Titning g'ayratini, ko'z yoshlari va ohlarini shunchalik ta'sirli his qildirishi mumkin ediki, bu unga do'stiga unashtirilgan kelini, go'zal, muloyim va sevikli kelini topshirishga undaydi?

en: What laws, what menaces, what fears could have enforced the young arms of Gisippus to abstain, in solitary places and in dark, nay, in his very bed, from the embraces of the fair damsel, she mayhap bytimes inviting him, had friendship not done it?
uz: Qanday qonunlar, qanday tahdidlar, qanday qo'rquvlar Gisippning yosh qo'llarini yolg'iz joylarda va qorong'ida o'zini tiyishga majbur qilgan bo'lishi mumkin edi, yo'q, uning to'shagida, go'zal qizning quchog'idan, u uni vaqti-vaqti bilan chaqirib, do'stlik buni qilmagan bo'lishi mumkin edi?

en: What honours, what rewards, what advancements, what, indeed, but friendship, could have made Gisippus reck not of losing his own kinsfolk and those of Sophronia nor of the unmannerly clamours of the populace nor of scoffs and insults, so that he might pleasure his friend?
uz: Qanday sharaflar, qanday mukofotlar, qanday yutuqlar, aslida, faqatgina do'stlik Gisippni o'z qarindoshlari va Sofroniyaning qarindoshlarini yo'qotishdan, xalqning odobsiz faryodlaridan, masxara va haqoratlardan, do'stini xursand qilish uchun qayg'urmaslikka majbur qilishi mumkin edi?

en: On the other hand, what, but friendship, could have prompted Titus, whenas he might fairly have feigned not to see, unhesitatingly to compass his own death, that he might deliver Gisippus from the cross to which he had of his own motion procured himself to be condemned?
uz: Boshqa tomondan, Titga faqatgina do'stlik nima undashi mumkin edi, garchi u o'zini ko'rmasdek ko'rsatgan bo'lsa ham, o'z o'limini hech ikkilanmasdan o'ylab, Gisippni o'z xohishi bilan o'zini hukm qilinadigan xochdan qutqarishi mumkin edi?

en: What else could have made Titus, without the least demur, so liberal in sharing his most ample patrimony with Gisippus, whom fortune had bereft of his own?
uz: Titni eng kam demur bo'lmagan holda, boyligi o'zidan mahrum bo'lgan Gisipp bilan eng keng merosini bo'lishishda bunchalik erkin qiladigan yana nima bo'lishi mumkin edi?

en: What else could have made him so forward to vouchsafe his sister to his friend, albeit he saw him very poor and reduced to the extreme of misery?
uz: Uni o'z singlisini do'stiga sovg'a qilishga undaydigan yana nima bo'lishi mumkin edi, garchi u uni juda kambag'al va nihoyatda nochor ko'rsa ham?

en: Let men, then, covet a multitude of comrades, troops of brethren and children galore and
uz: Shunday ekan, odamlar o'rtoqlarning ko'pligini, birodarlarning qo'shinlarini va bolalarning ko'pligini istasinlar va...

en: add, by dint of monies, to the number of their servitors, considering not that every one of these, who and whatsoever he may be, is more fearful of every least danger of his own than careful to do away the great472 from father or brother or master, whereas we see a friend do altogether the contrary.”
uz: O'z xizmatkorlarining soniga mol-mulk bilan qo'shing, shuni hisobga olmangki, ularning har biri, kim va nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, otasi, akasi yoki xo'jayinasidan buyuk472 ni yo'q qilishga ehtiyot bo'lishdan ko'ra, o'zining eng kichik xavfidan qo'rqadi, ammo do'stning butunlay aksincha qilayotganini ko'ramiz.

en: THE NINTH STORY Saladin, in the disguise of a merchant, is honourably entertained by Messer Torello d’Istria, who, presently undertaking the (third) crusade, appointeth his wife a term for her marrying again.
uz: TO'IXINCHI HIKOYA Saladin, savdogar qiyofasida, hurmat bilan Messer Torello dIistriya tomonidan o'ynatiladi. U hozirda (uchinchi) salib yurishini boshlagan holda, xotiniga uni qayta turmushga chiqarish muddatini belgilaydi.

en: He is taken (by the Saracens) and cometh, by his skill in training hawks, under the notice of the soldan, who knoweth him again and discovering himself to him, entreateth him with the utmost honour.
uz: U (saratsinlar tomonidan) olinadi va o'z mahorati bilan so'qmoqlarni o'rgatish orqali, uni yana taniydigan va unga o'zini topib, uni eng katta sharaf bilan yolvoradigan soldanning e'tiboriga keladi.

en: Then, Torello falling sick for languishment, he is by magical art transported in one night (from Alexandria) to Pavia, where, being recognized by his wife at the bride-feast held for her marrying again, he returneth with her to his own house.
uz: Keyin, Torello chanqoqlikdan kasal bo'lib, u sehrli san'at yordamida bir kechada (Aleksandariyadan) Paviyaga olib ketiladi. U yerda, uning xotini uni qayta turmushga chiqish uchun o'tkazgan kelin-toyda tanisa, u bilan o'z uyiga qaytadi.

en: Filomena having made an end of her discourse and the magniﬁcent gratit- ude of Titus having been of all alike commended, the king, reserving the last place unto Dioneo, proceeded to speak thus: “Assuredly, lovesome ladies, Filomena speaketh sooth in that which she saith of friendship and with reason complaineth, in concluding her discourse, of its being so little in favour with mankind.
uz: Filomena o'z nutqini tugatgach va Titning ajoyib tabriklari hammaga birdek maqtanib, shoh Dioneoga oxirgi o'rinni qo'yib, shunday dedi: Albatta, go'zal xonimlar, Filomena do'stlik haqida gapirganda xotirjam gapiradi va o'z nutqini yakunlashda insoniyat oldida unchalik yaxshi emasligidan aql bilan shikoyat qiladi.

en: If we were here for the purpose of correcting the defaults of the age or even of reprehending them, I might ensue her words with a discourse at large upon the subject; but, for that we aim at otherwhat, it hath occurred to my mind to set forth to you, in a story belike somewhat overlong, but withal altogether pleasing, one of the magniﬁcences of Salad- in, to the end that, if, by reason of our defaults, the friendship of anyone may not be throughly acquired, we may, at the least, be led, by the things which you shall hear in my story, to take delight in doing service, in the hope that, whenassoever it may be, reward will ensue to us thereof.
uz: Agar biz bu yerda zamon nuqsonlarini tuzatish yoki hatto ularni tanqid qilish maqsadida bo'lganimizda, men uning so'zlarini mavzu bo'yicha umumiy ma'ruza bilan tasdiqlasam bo'ladi; lekin, biz boshqa narsaga qaratilgan bo'lsak, sizlarga biroz uzunroq, ammo umuman olganda yoqimli bo'lmagan, Saladning ulug'vorliklaridan birini taqdim etishni o'ylab topdim. Shu maqsadda, agar bizning nuqsonlarimiz tufayli hech kimning do'stligi to'liq qozonilmasa, hech bo'lmaganda, mening hikoyamda eshitadigan narsalar bilan yo'naltirilishimiz mumkin, xizmat qilishdan zavq olishimiz mumkin, umid qilamizki, qachonki u bizga mukofot beradi.

en: I must tell you, then, that, according to that which divers folk afﬁrm, a general crusade was, in the days of the Emperor Frederick the First, under- taken by the Christians for the recovery of the Holy Land, whereof Saladin,
uz: Shuni aytishim kerakki, turli xalq ta'kidlaganidek, imperator Frederik I davrida Xristianlar tomonidan Muqaddas Zaminni qayta tiklash uchun umumiy salib yurishi amalga oshirilgan edi, unda Saladin...

en: a very noble and valiant prince, who was then Soldan of Babylon, having notice awhile beforehand, he bethought himself to seek in his own person to see the preparations of the Christian princes for the undertaking in question, so he might the better avail to provide himself.
uz: Juda olijanob va jasur shahzoda, o'shanda Bobil askari bo'lgan edi, buni ancha oldindan sezgan holda, u o'z shaxsiyatida xristian shahzodalarning ushbu tadbirga tayyorgarligini ko'rishni o'yladi, shunda u o'zini ta'minlash uchun yaxshiroq foydalanishlari mumkin edi.

en: Accordingly, having ordered all his affairs in Egypt, he made a show of going a pilgrimage and set out in the disguise of a merchant, attended by two only of his chiefest and sagest ofﬁcers and three serving-men.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, Misrdagi barcha ishlarini tartibga solib, u ziyoratga borayotgandek ko'rindi va savdogar qiyofasida jo'nab ketdi, unga faqat ikki nafar eng katta va eng kichkina ofitseri va uch nafar xizmatchisi tashrif buyurdi.

en: After he had visited many Christian coun- tries, it chanced that, as they rode through Lombardy, thinking to pass bey- ond the mountains,473 they encountered, about vespers, on the road from Milan to Pavia, a gentleman of the latter place, by name Messer Torello d’Istria, who was on his way, with his servants and dogs and falcons, to so- journ at a goodly country seat he had upon the Tesino, and no sooner set eyes on Saladin and his company than he knew them for gentlemen and strangers; wherefore, the Soldan enquiring of one of his servants how far they were yet distant from Pavia and if he might win thither in time to enter the city, he suffered not the man to reply, but himself answered, ‘Gentle- men, you cannot reach Pavia in time to enter therein.’ ‘Then,’ said Saladin, ‘may it please you acquaint us (for that we are strangers) where we may best lodge the night.’ Quoth Messer
uz: U ko'plab xristian mamlakatlariga tashrif buyurganidan so'ng, shunday bo'ldiki, ular Lombardiya bo'ylab sayohat qilib, tog'lardan pastga o'tmoqchi bo'lishar ekan, 473 yillarda Milandan Paviyaga yo'lda oxirgi joydan kelgan janobga duch kelishdi. Uning ismi Messer Torello dIstria edi. U o'z xizmatkorlari, itlari va falconlari bilan Tesinoga borayotgan edi, shuning uchun u yaxshi qishloq o'rindig'iga borardi va Saladin va uning kompaniyasiga ularni janoblar va begonalar uchun bilganidan tezroq ko'z tashlardi. Shuning uchun, Soldan o'z xizmatkorlaridan birining Paviyadan qanchalik uzoqda ekanligini so'radi va agar u shaharga kirishga ulgursa, u odamga javob bermadi, lekin o'zi javob berdi: "Gent odamlari, siz ularni kechasi bilan tanisholmaysiz."

en: Torello, ‘That will I willingly do.
uz: Torello, Men buni ixtiyoriy ravishda qilaman.

en: I had it presently in mind to dispatch one of my men here to the neighborhood of Pavia for somewhat: I will send him with you and he shall bring you to a place where you may lodge conveniently enough.’ Then, turning to the dis- creetest of his men he [privily] enjoined him what he should do and sent him with them, whilst he himself, making for his country house, let order, as best he might, a goodly supper and set the tables in the garden; which done, he posted himself at the door to await his guests.
uz: Men o'z odamlarimdan birini shu yerdan Paviya mahallasiga bir oz muddatga jo'natishni o'yladim: men uni siz bilan jo'nataman va u sizni qulay dam olishingiz mumkin bo'lgan joyga olib keladi. Keyin, o'z odamlaridan eng ko'p narsaga murojaat qilib, unga nima qilish kerakligini buyurdi va ularni o'zi bilan jo'natdi. O'zi esa o'z qishloq uyiga borar ekan, imkon qadar yaxshi kechki ovqatni tayyorlab, bog'da stollarni qo'ydi; bu bilan u mehmonlarini kutish uchun eshik oldida o'zini qo'ydi.

en: Meanwhile, the servant, devising with the gentlemen of one thing and an- other, led them about by certain byroads and brought them, without their suspecting it, to his lord’s residence, where, whenas Messer Torello saw them, he came to meet them afoot and said, smiling, ‘Gentlemen, you are very welcome.’ Saladin, who was very quick of apprehension, understood that the gentleman had misdoubted him they would not have accepted his invitation, had he bidden them whenas he fell in with them, and had, there- fore, brought them by practice to his house, so they might not avail to re- fuse to pass the night with him, and accordingly, returning his greeting, he said, ‘Sir, an one could complain of men of courtesy, we might complain of you, for that (letting be that you have somewhat hindered us from our road)
uz: Ayni paytda, xizmatkor, bir narsa va boshqa bir narsa haqida janoblar bilan maslahatlashib, ularni ma'lum bir yo'llardan olib bordi va ular buni bilmasdan, o'z xo'jayinining qarorgohiga olib keldi. U yerda, janob Torello ularni ko'rgach, ularni kutib oldi va tabassum bilan dedi: "Janoblar, siz juda xush kelibsiz." Saladin, juda tez xavotirda bo'lgan, janob uni adashtirganini tushundi, ular uning taklifini qabul qilmagan bo'lishardi, u ularni u bilan birga tushganda taklif qilganida edi, va u yerda ularni amaliyot bilan o'z uyiga olib kelgan edi, shunda ular u bilan tunni o'tkazishga majbur bo'lmasdilar va shunga ko'ra, o'z salomini qaytargan holda, u dedi: "Janob, sizdan bir kishi kelib, bizdan shikoyat qilishimiz mumkin edi, chunki siz...

en: you have, without our having merited your goodwill otherwise than by a mere salutation, constrained us to accept of such noble hospitality as is this of yours.’ ‘Gentlemen,’ answered Messer Torello, who was a discreet and well-spoken man, ‘it is but a sorry hospitality that you will receive from us, regard had to that which should behove unto you, an I may judge by that which I apprehend from your carriage and that of your companions; but in truth you could nowhere out of Pavia have found any decent place of enter- tainment; wherefore, let it not irk you to have gone somedele beside your way, to have a little less unease.’ Meanwhile, his servants came round about the travellers and helping them to dismount, eased474 their horses.
uz: Siz bizni, sizning yaxshi niyatingizni shunchaki salom berishdan boshqa narsaga loyiq bo'lmasdan, bunday olijanob mehmondo'stlikni qabul qilishga majbur qildingiz.  Janoblar,  deb javob berdi sirli va xushmuomala inson bo'lgan Messer Torello, bu siz bizdan oladigan achinarli mehmondo'stlik xolos, sizga tegishli bo'lgan narsaga e'tibor bering, men sizning aravachangiz va hamrohlaringiznikidan ko'rganim bilan baho beraman; lekin rostini aytsam, siz Paviyadan hech qayerda munosib dam olish joyini topa olmaysiz; shuning uchun, yo'lingiz bo'ylab biroz kamroq noqulaylik bo'lishi uchun borganingizni xafa qilmang. Ayni paytda, uning xizmatkorlari sayohatchilar atrofida kelib, ularga yordam berishdi.

en: Messer Torello then brought the three stranger gentlemen to the chambers prepared for them, where he let unboot them and refresh them somewhat with very cool wines and entertained them in agreeable discourse till such time as they might sup.
uz: Messer Torello keyin uchta notanish janobni ular uchun tayyorlangan xonalarga olib keldi, u yerda ularni ishga tushirdi va juda salqin vinolar bilan biroz tetiklantirdi va ular ovqatlanishlari mumkin bo'lgan vaqtgacha yoqimli suhbatda ularni xursand qildi.

en: Saladin and his companions and servants all knew Latin, wherefore they understood very well and were understood, and it seemed to each of them that this gentleman was the most pleasant and well- mannered man they had ever seen, ay, and the best spoken.
uz: Saladin va uning hamrohlari va xizmatkorlarining hammasi lotin tilini bilishgan, shuning uchun ular juda yaxshi tushunishardi va tushunishardi, va ularning har biriga bu janob ularning ko'rgan eng yoqimli va odobli odamiga o'xshardi, ha, va eng yaxshi gapirardi.

en: It appeared to Messer Torello, on the other hand, that they were men of magniﬁcent fash- ions and much more of account than he had at ﬁrst conceived, wherefore he was inwardly chagrined that he could not honour them that evening with companions and with a more considerable entertainment.
uz: Messer Torelloga, aksincha, ular ajoyib moda odamlari va u o'ylaganidan ko'ra ancha ko'p ma'noga ega odamlardek tuyuldi, shuning uchun u o'sha oqshomni hamrohlar bilan va ancha ko'p ko'ngilxushlik bilan ularga hurmat ko'rsata olmasligidan ich-ichidan xafa edi.

en: But for this he be- thought himself to make them amends on the morrow, and accordingly, hav- ing instructed one of his servants of that which he would have done, he des- patched him to Pavia, which was very near at hand and where no gate was ever locked, to his lady, who was exceeding discreet and greathearted.
uz: Lekin buning uchun u ertaga o'zi ularni tuzatadi deb o'yladi va shunga ko'ra, o'z xizmatkorlaridan biriga nima qilish kerakligini ko'rsatib, uni juda yaqin va hech qachon qulflanmagan Paviyaga, o'ta ehtiyotkor va katta yurakli xonimga jo'natdi.

en: Then, carrying the gentlemen into the garden, he courteously asked them who they were, to which Saladin answered, ‘We are merchants from Cyprus and are bound to Paris on our occasions.’ ‘Would to God,’ cried Messer Torello, ‘that this our country produced gentlemen of such a fashion as I see Cyprus doth merchants!’ In these and other discourses they abode till it was time to sup, whereupon he left it to them to honour themselves at table,475 and there, for an improvised supper, they were very well and orderly served; nor had they abidden long after the tables were removed, when Messer Torello, judging them to be weary, put them to sleep in very goodly beds and himself a little after in like manner betook himself to rest.
uz: So'ngra, janoblarni bog'ga olib kirgach, u ulardan kim ekanliklarini xushmuomalalik bilan so'radi, Saladin ularga javob berdi: "Biz Kiprlik savdogarmiz va Parijga tashrif buyurishimiz kerak." "Xudoga qasamki," deb baqirdi Messer Torello, "bu yurtimiz Kiprni ko'rganimdek shunday janoblarni ishlab chiqargan bo'lsa edi!" Bu va boshqa gaplarda ular zichlash vaqti kelguncha qoldilar, shundan so'ng u ularga stol ustida o'zlarini hurmat qilishni qoldirdi. 475 va u yerda, biroz kechki ovqat uchun, ular juda yaxshi va tartibli xizmat ko'rsatishdi; shuningdek, stollar olib tashlanganidan keyin uzoq vaqt yashirmagan bo'lsalar ham, Messer Torello ularni charchagan deb hisoblab, o'zi kabi yaxshi to'shaklarda uxlatdi.

en: Meanwhile the servant sent to Pavia did his errand to the lady, who, with no womanly, but with a royal spirit, let call in haste a great number of the
uz: Ayni paytda xizmatkor Paviyaga ayolga topshirig'ini qildi, u ayol emas, balki qirollik ruhiga ega bo'lib, shoshilinch ravishda ko'plab odamlarni chaqirdi.

en: friends and servants of Messer Torello and made ready all that behoved unto a magniﬁcent banquet.
uz: Messer Torelloning do'stlari va xizmatkorlari ajoyib ziyofatga zarur bo'lgan hamma narsani tayyorladilar.

en: Moreover, she let bid by torchlight many of the noblest of the townfolk to the banquet and bringing out cloths and silks and furs, caused throughly order that which her husband had sent to bid her do.
uz: Qolaversa, u shahar aholisining ko'p zodagonlarini ziyofatga chaqirdi va mato, ipak va mo'ynalar olib chiqdi, shu bilan erining unga buyurganlarini butunlay tartibga soldi.

en: The day come, Saladin and his companions arose, whereupon Messer Torello took horse with them and sending for his falcons, carried them to a neighbouring ford and there showed them how the latter ﬂew; then, Saladin enquiring for someone who should bring him to Pavia and to the best inn, his host said, ‘I will be your guide, for that it behoveth me go thither.’ The others, believing this, were content and set out in company with him for the city, which they reached about tierce and thinking to be on their way to the best inn, were carried by Messer Torello to his own house, where a good half-hundred of the most considerable citizens were already come to receive the stranger gentlemen and were straightway about their bridles and stir- rups.
uz: Kun kelib, Saladin va uning hamrohlari turdilar. Shundan so'ng, Messer Torello otni olib, so'rg'ichlarini olib ketdi, ularni qo'shni daryoga olib bordi va u yerda ularning qanday uchganini ko'rsatdi. Shunda, Saladin uni Paviyaga olib boradigan odamni va eng yaxshi mehmonxonaga olib borishni so'raganida, uning xo'jayin: "Men sizning yo'lboshchingiz bo'laman, chunki menga u yerga borish kerak", dedi. Qolganlar bunga ishonib, u bilan birga shaharga yo'l olishdi. Ular taxminan uchinchi qavatga yetib kelishdi va eng yaxshi mehmonxonaga ketayotganini o'ylab, Messer Torello tomonidan o'z uyiga olib ketildi. U yerda eng yaxshi yarim yuz nafar fuqaro begonalarni qabul qilish uchun allaqachon kelgan edi va darhol kelinlari va xonimlari haqida gapirishdi.

en: Saladin and his companions, seeing this, understood but too well what was forward and said, ‘Messer Torello, this is not what we asked of you; you have done enough for us this past night, ay, and far more than we are worth; wherefore you might now ﬁtly suffer us fare on our way.’ ‘Gentle- men,’ replied Messer Torello, ‘for my yesternight’s dealing with you I am more indebted to fortune than to you, which took you on the road at an hour when it behoved you come to my poor house; but of your this morning’s visit I shall be beholden to yourselves, and with me all these gentlemen who are about you and to whom an it seem to you courteous to refuse to dine with them, you can do so, if you will.’ Saladin and his companions, overcome, dismounted and being joyfully received by the assembled company, were carried to chambers which had been most sumptuously arrayed for them, where having put off
uz: Salohiddin va uning hamrohlari buni ko'rib, oldinda nima borligini juda yaxshi tushundilar va dedilar: "Janob Torello, biz sizdan so'ragan narsa emas; siz o'tgan kecha biz uchun yetarli ish qildingiz, ey, va bizdan ko'ra ancha ko'p; shuning uchun endi siz bizga yo'lda yo'l berishingiz mumkin." "Janoblar," dedi janob Torello, "siz bilan bo'lgan munosabatlarim uchun men sizdan ko'ra boylikka qarzdorman, bu sizni bechora uyimga kelishingiz kerak bo'lgan soatda yo'lga olib ketdi."

en: their travel- ling gear and somewhat refreshed themselves, they repaired to the saloon, where the banquet was splendidly prepared.
uz: Ularning sayohat anjomlari va biroz tetiklanib, ziyofat ajoyib tarzda tayyorlangan salonga qaytishdi.

en: Water having been given to the hands, they were seated at table with the goodliest and most orderly observ- ance and magniﬁcently served with many viands, insomuch that, were the emperor himself come thither, it had been impossible to do him more hon- our, and albeit Saladin and his companions were great lords and used to see very great things, natheless, they were mightily wondered at this and it seemed to them of the greatest, having regard to the quality of the gentle- man, whom they knew to be only a citizen and not a lord.
uz: Qo'llariga suv berilganidan so'ng, ular eng yaxshi va tartibli kuzatuvchilar bilan dasturxonga o'tirdilar - va ko'plab go'shtlar bilan ajoyib tarzda taomlanishdi. Shunday qilib, imperatorning o'zi u yerga kelganda, unga ko'proq hurmat ko'rsatishning iloji bo'lmas edi, va garchi Saladin va uning hamrohlari buyuk xo'jayinlar bo'lishgan va juda katta narsalarni ko'rishgan bo'lsalar ham, ular bunga juda hayratda edilar va bu ularga eng buyuklardan biriga o'xshardi, muloyim odamning sifatini hisobga olgan holda, uni faqat fuqaro deb bilishardi, xo'jayin emas.

en: Dinner ended and the tables removed, they conversed awhile of divers things; then, at Messer
uz: Kechki ovqat tugab, stollar olib tashlandi, ular bir oz vaqt turli xil narsalar haqida suhbatlashdilar; keyin, Messerda

en: Torello’s instance, the heat being great, the gentlemen of Pavia all betook themselves to repose, whilst he himself, abiding alone with his three guests, carried them into a chamber and (that no precious thing of his should re- main unseen of them) let call thither his noble lady.
uz: Torelloning misoli, issiqlik juda kuchli bo'lgani sababli, Paviyaning janoblari dam olish uchun o'zlarini bezovta qilishdi, u esa o'zining uch mehmon bilan yolg'iz o'tirib, ularni xonaga olib kirdi va (ulardan ko'rinmas qimmatbaho narsa bo'lishi kerak edi) u yerga o'zining olijanob xonimni chaqirdi.

en: Accordingly, the latter, who was very fair and tall of her person, came in to them, arrayed in rich apparel and ﬂanked by two little sons of hers, as they were two angels, and saluted them courteously.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, uning juda chiroyli va baland bo'yli bo'yli bo'lgan ikkinchisi ularning oldiga keldi, boy kiyimda edi va uning ikki kichkina o'g'li bilan yonma-yon turardi, go'yo ular ikki farishta edi, va ularni xushmuomalalik bilan salomladi.

en: The strangers, seeing her, rose to their feet and receiving her with worship, caused her sit among them and made much of her two fair children.
uz: Begonalar uni ko'rib, o'rnidan turishdi va uni sig'inish bilan kutib olishdi, ularni o'rtasida o'tirishga majbur qilishdi va ikki go'zal farzandidan ko'p narsa qilishdi.

en: Therewithal she entered into pleasant discourse with them and presently, Messer Torello having gone out awhile, she asked them courteously whence they were and whither they went; to which they made answer even as they had done to her husband; whereupon quoth she, with a blithe air, ‘Then see I that my womanly advisement will be useful; where- fore I pray you, of your especial favour, refuse me not neither disdain a slight present, which I shall cause bring you, but accept it, considering that women, of their little heart, give little things and regarding more the good- will of the giver than the value of the gift.’ Then, letting fetch them each two gowns, one lined with silk and the other with miniver, no wise citizens’ clothes nor merchants, but ﬁt for great lords to wear, and three doublets of sendal and linen breeches to match, she said, ‘Take these; I have clad my lord in gowns of
uz: Shundan so'ng u ular bilan yoqimli suhbatga kirdi va darhol, janob Torello bir oz vaqtga chiqib, ulardan qayerdan va qayerga borayotganliklarini odob bilan so'radi; unga eriga qilganidek javob berishdi; shundan so'ng u xushmuomalalik bilan dedi: "Shuning uchun mening ayolona maslahatim foydali bo'lishini ko'raman; iltimos, sizdan iltimos qilaman, men sizga olib keladigan kichik bir sovg'ani rad etmang, lekin uni qabul qiling, chunki ayollar o'z qalbi bilan sovg'a beruvchining yaxshi xohishidan ko'ra ko'proq narsalarni berishadi." Keyin, ularga har biriga ikkita ko'ylak olib kelishga ruxsat berdi, biri ipak bilan qoplangan va ikkinchisi esa, hech qanday fuqarolarga mos kelmaydigan kiyimlar, ikki kishilik kiyimlar, ikki kishilik kiyimlar va ko'ylaklar, lekin u menga buyuk

en: the like fashion, and the other things, for all they are little worth, may be acceptable to you, considering that you are far from your ladies and the length of the way you have travelled and that which is yet to travel and that merchants are proper men and nice of their persons.’ The Saracens marvelled and manifestly perceived that Messer Torello was minded to leave no particular of hospitality undone them; nay, seeing the magniﬁcence of the unmerchantlike gowns, they misdoubted them they had been recognized of him.
uz: Shunga o'xshash moda va boshqa narsalar, ularning barchasi arzimagan bo'lsa ham, siz uchun maqbul bo'lishi mumkin, chunki siz xonimlaringizdan uzoqda, sayohat qilgan yo'lingiz uzunligi va hali sayohat qilinmagan narsalardan va savdogarlar o'zlarining odobli odamlari va mehribonlari ekanligini hisobga olsak. Saracenlar hayratda qolishdi va aniq angladiki, janob Torello ularni hech qanday mehmondo'stlikdan chetda qoldirmoqchi emas edi; aksincha, savdosiz liboslarning ajoyibligini ko'rib, ular u tomonidan tan olinganliklarini gumon qilishdi.

en: However, one of them made answer to the lady, saying, ‘Madam, these are very great matters and such as should not lightly be accepted, an your prayers, to which it is impossible to say no, constrained us not thereto.’ This done and Messer Torello being now re- turned, the lady, commending them to God, took leave of them and let fur- nish their servants with like things such as sorted with their condition.
uz: Biroq, ulardan biri xonimga javob berib dedi: Xonim, bular juda katta ishlar va ularni yengil qabul qilmaslik kerak, lekin sizning duolaringiz, ularga yoq deyishning iloji yoq, bizni bunga majbur qilmadi. Bu ish tugagandan song, janob Torello endi qaytdi, xonim ularni Xudoga topshirib, ulardan voz kechdi va xizmatkorlarini ularning holatiga mos keladigan narsalar bilan taminladi.

en: Messer Torello with many prayers prevailed upon them to abide with him all that day; wherefore, after they had slept awhile, they donned their gowns and rode with him somedele about the city; then, the supper-hour come, they supped magniﬁcently with many worshipful companions and in due
uz: Messer Torello ularni shu kun bo'yi u bilan qolishga ko'p duolar bilan undadi; shuning uchun, ular biroz uxlagandan so'ng, ko'ylaklarini kiydirib, u bilan birga shahar bo'ylab sayohat qilishdi; keyin, kechki ovqat soati kelgach, ular ko'plab ibodat qiluvchi hamrohlar bilan ajoyib ovqatlanishdi va

en: time betook themselves to rest.
uz: Vaqt o'zlarini dam olishga majbur qildi.

en: On the morrow they arose with day and found, in place of their tired hackneys, three stout and good palfreys, and on likewise fresh and strong horses for their servants, which when Saladin saw, he turned to his companions and said, ‘I vow to God that never was there a more accomplished gentleman nor a more courteous and apprehensive than this one, and if the kings of the Christians are kings of such a fashion as this is a gentleman, the Soldan of Babylon can never hope to stand against a single one of them, not to speak of the many whom we see make ready to fall upon him.’ Then, knowing that it were in vain to seek to refuse this new gift, they very courteously thanked him therefor and mounted to horse.
uz: Ertasi kuni ular ertalab turdilar va charchoq xakneylari o'rniga uchta kuchli va yaxshi palfreysni topdilar, shuningdek, xizmatkorlari uchun yangi va kuchli otlarni ham topdilar. Saladin ularni ko'rganida, o'z hamrohlariga o'girilib dedi: "Men Xudoga qasam ichamanki, bundan ko'ra yetukroq janob ham, undan ko'ra odobli va qo'rqoqroq zot yo'q edi, va agar xristianlar shohlari shunday uslubdagi podshohlar bo'lsalar, Bobil soldani ularning hech biriga qarshi turishga umid qila olmaydi, biz unga yiqishga tayyor ko'rgan ko'pchilik haqida gapirmasa ham bo'lmaydi." Keyin, bu yangi sovg'ani rad etish uchun juda befoyda minnatdorchilik bildirdilar va otga minib ketishdi.

en: Messer Torello, with many companions, brought them a great way without the city, till, grievous as it was to Saladin to part from him, (so much was he by this grown enamoured of him), natheless, need constrain- ing him to press on, he presently besought him to turn back; whereupon, loath as he was to leave them, ‘Gentlemen,’ quoth he, ‘since it pleaseth you, I will do it; but one thing I will e’en say to you; I know not who you are nor do I ask to know more thereof than it pleaseth you to tell me; but, be you who you may, you will never make me believe that you are merchants, and so I commend you to God.’ Saladin, having by this taken leave of all Messer Torello’s companions, replied to him, saying, ‘Sir, we may yet chance to let you see somewhat of our merchandise, whereby we may conﬁrm your be- lief;476 meantime, God be with you.’ Thereupon he departed with his fol- lowers, ﬁrmly
uz: Janob Torello, ko'p hamrohlari bilan ularni shahardan tashqariga olib chiqdi, toki, Saladin undan ajralish uchun qanchalik qayg'urgan bo'lsa ham, (shuningdek, u unga shunchalik oshiq bo'lib qolgan edi), ammo uni bosishga majburlash kerak edi, u darhol orqaga qaytishni so'radi; shundan so'ng, ularni tark etar ekan, u dedi: "Janoblar," chunki sizga yoqadi, men buni qilaman; lekin sizga bir narsani aytaman; men siz kimligingizni bilmayman va sizdan menga aytishdan ko'ra ko'proq narsani so'ramayman; lekin, siz meni hech qachon savdogarlar ekanligingizga ishontirmaysiz, shuning uchun men sizni Xudoga tavsiya qilaman." Jazob Saladin, barcha Jannosning hamrohlari tomonidan olib ketilgan, biz siz bilan biroz...

en: resolved, if life should endure to him and the war he looked for undo him not, to do Messer Torello no less honour than that which he had done him, and much did he discourse with his companions of him and of his lady and all his affairs and fashions and dealings, mightily commend- ing everything.
uz: Agar hayot unga bardosh bersa va u izlagan urush uni bekor qilmasa, Messer Torelloni unga qilgan ishidan kam bo'lmagan sharafga aylantirishga qaror qildi va u o'z hamrohlari bilan uning va uning xonimining, barcha ishlarining, modalarining va ishlarining haqida ko'p muhokama qildi, hamma narsani kuchli maqtadi.

en: Then, after he had, with no little fatigue, visited all the West, he took ship with his companions and returned to Alexandria, where, being now fully informed, he addressed himself to his defence.
uz: Keyin, u hech qanday charchoqsiz butun G'arbga tashrif buyurgach, o'z hamrohlari bilan kemaga chiqib, Iskandariyaga qaytib keldi. U yerda, to'liq xabardor bo'lgan holda, o'zini himoya qilishga murojaat qildi.

en: As for Messer Torello, he returned to Pavia and went long in thought who these might be, but never hit upon the truth, no, nor came near it.
uz: Messer Torelloga kelsak, u Paviyaga qaytib keldi va bular kim bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida uzoq o'yladi, lekin hech qachon haqiqatga duch kelmadi, yo'q, unga yaqinlashmadi ham.

en: The time being now come for the crusade and great preparations made everywhere, Messer Torello, notwithstanding the tears and entreaties of his wife, was altogether resolved to go thereon and having made his every pro- vision and being about to take horse, he said to his lady, whom he loved over all, ‘Wife, as thou seest, I go on this crusade, as well for the honour of my body as for the health of my soul.
uz: Endi xoch yurishi va hamma joyda qilingan ulkan tayyorgarlik vaqti kelgan edi, janob Torello, xotinining ko'z yoshlari va iltijolariga qaramay, u yerga borishga qat'iy qaror qildi va har bir o'zini ko'rsatib, otga ot olish arafasida bo'lganida, u xotiniga dedi: "Xotin, ko'rib turganingizdek, men bu xoch yurish uchun boraman, nafaqat tanamning sharafi uchun, balki ruhimning sog'lig'i uchun ham."

en: I commend to thee our affairs and our
uz: Men senga ishlarimizni va bizning...

en: honour, and for that I am certain of the going, but of the returning, for a thousand chances that may betide, I have no assurance, I will have thee do me a favour, to wit, that whatever befall of me, an thou have not certain news of my life, thou shalt await me a year and a month and a day, ere thou marry again, beginning from this the day of my departure.’ The lady, who wept sore, answered, ‘Messer Torello, I know not how I shall endure the chagrin wherein you leave me by your departure; but, an my life prove stronger than my grief and aught befall you, you may live and die assured that I shall live and die the wife of Messer Torello and of his memory.’ ‘Wife,’ rejoined Messer Torello, ‘I am very certain that, inasmuch as in thee lieth, this that thou promisest me will come to pass; but thou art a young woman and fair and of high family and thy worth is great and everywhere known;
uz: Sharaf, va shuning uchun men ketishga aminman, lekin qaytishga, mingta ehtimolga ko'ra, men hech qanday kafolatga ega emasman, men sizga yordam beraman, ya'ni, menga nima bo'lishidan qat'iy nazar, hayotim haqida aniq xabaringiz yo'q, siz meni bir yil, bir oy va bir kun kutasiz, toki yana turmushga chiqmasligingiz, ketayotgan kunimdan boshlab.

en: wherefore I doubt not but many great and noble gentlemen will, should aught be misdoubted of me,477 demand thee of thy brethren and kinsfolk; from whose importunities, how much soever thou mightest wish, thou wilt not be able to defend thyself and it will behove thee perforce com- ply with their wishes; and this is why I ask of thee this term and not a great- er one.’ Quoth the lady, ‘I will do what I may of that which I have told you, and should it nevertheless behove me to do otherwise, I will assuredly obey you in this that you enjoin me; but I pray God that He bring nor you nor me to such an extremity in these days.’ This said, she embraced him, weeping, and drawing a ring from her ﬁnger, gave it to him, saying, ‘And it chance that I die ere I see you again, remember me when you look upon this ring.’ Torello took the ring and mounted to horse; then, bidding all his people adieu, he
uz: Shuning uchun men shubha qilmayman, lekin ko'plab buyuk va olijanob janoblar, agar mendan biror narsa gumon qilinsa, 477 seni o'z birodarlaring va qarindoshlaringdan so'rashadi; ularning muhimliklaridan, qancha xohlasang ham, o'zingni himoya qila olmaysan va bu seni ularning istaklariga mos ravishda majbur qiladi; va shuning uchun men sendan bu atamani so'rayman, lekin buyuk emas.

en: set out on his journey and came presently with his company to Genoa.
uz: Sayohatga otlandi va tez orada o'z kompaniyasi bilan Genuyaga keldi.

en: There he embarked on board a galleon and coming in a little while to Acre, joined himself to the other army478 of the Christians, wherein, well nigh out of hand, there began a sore sickness and mortality.
uz: U yerda u galleonga chiqdi va birozdan so'ng Akrega kelib, xristianlarning boshqa 478 armiyasiga qo'shildi, u yerda, deyarli hech qanday yordam bo'lmasa, og'ir kasallik va o'lim boshlandi.

en: During this, whether by Saladin’s skill or of his good fortune, well nigh all the remnant of the Christians who had escaped alive were taken by him, without blow stricken, and divided among many cities and imprisoned.
uz: Shu vaqt ichida, xoh Salohidinning mahorati bilan, xoh uning omadidan, tirik qutulgan xristianlarning deyarli barcha qoldiqlari u tomonidan zarbalarsiz olib ketildi va ko'plab shaharlar orasida bo'lindi va qamoqqa tashlandi.

en: Messer Torello was one of those taken and was carried prisoner to Alexandria, where, be- ing unknown and fearing to make himself known, he addressed himself, of necessity constrained, to the training of hawks, of which he was a great master, and by this he came under the notice of Saladin, who took him out of prison and entertained him for his falconer.
uz: Messer Torello asirga olib ketilganlardan biri bo'lgan va Iskandariyaga olib ketilgan. U yerda, noma'lum bo'lib, o'zini tanishtirishdan qo'rqqan holda, majburiy ravishda cheklangan holda, xorklarni o'qitishga murojaat qilgan, ularning buyuk ustasi edi va shu bilan u Saladinning xabariga tushdi, u uni qamoqdan chiqarib, o'zining falconeri uchun qabul qildi.

en: Messer Torello, who was called by the Soldan by none other name than the Christian, recognized him
uz: Messer Torello, Soldanlar tomonidan xristiandan boshqa ism bilan atalmagan, uni tanidi.

en: not nor did Saladin recognize him; nay, all his thoughts were in Pavia and he had more than once essayed to ﬂee, but without avail; wherefore, certain Genoese coming ambassadors to Saladin, to treat for the ransom of sundry of their townsmen, and being about to depart, he bethought himself to write to his lady, giving her to know that he was alive and would return to her as quickliest he might and bidding her await him.
uz: Salohiddin uni tanimasdi ham; yo'q, uning barcha fikrlari Paviyada edi va u bir necha bor qochishga urinib ko'rgan edi, lekin hech qanday natijaga erisha olmadi; shuning uchun, ba'zi genovalik elchilar Salohiddin huzuriga kelib, o'zlarining turli shahar aholisining to'lovini ko'rib chiqish uchun kelishdi va ketmoqchi bo'lganida, u o'z xonimiga yozishni o'yladi, unga o'zi tirik ekanligini va iloji boricha tezroq unga qaytishini aytib, uni kutishni buyurdi.

en: Accordingly, he wrote letters to this effect and instantly besought one of the ambassadors, whom he knew, to cause them come to the hands of the Abbot of San Pietro in Ciel d’Oro, who was his uncle.
uz: Shunga ko'ra, u shu maqsadda xatlar yozdi va darhol o'zi bilgan elchilardan birini ularning San Pietro in Ciel dOro abbatining qo'liga kelishini so'radi, u uning amakisi edi.

en: Things being at this pass with him, it befell one day that, as Saladin was devising with him of his hawks, Messer Torello chanced to smile and made a motion with his mouth, which the former had much noted, what while he was in his house at Pavia.
uz: Shu bilan birga bo'lgan voqealar bir kuni sodir bo'ldi: Saladin o'z so'rg'ichlarini o'zi bilan o'ylab yurganida, janob Torello tasodifan tabassum qilib, og'zi bilan harakat qildi, buni avvalgi odam juda ko'p payqagan edi, u Paviyadagi uyida bo'lganida.

en: This brought the gentleman to his mind and look- ing steadfastly upon him, himseemed it was himself; wherefore, leaving the former discourse, ‘Harkye, Christian,’ said he, ‘What countryman art thou of the West?’ ‘My lord,’ replied Torello, ‘I am a Lombard of a city called Pavia, a poor man and of mean condition.’ Saladin, hearing this, was in a manner certiﬁed of the truth of his suspicion and said joyfully in himself, ‘God hath vouchsafed me an opportunity of showing this man how grateful his courtesy was to me.’ Accordingly, without saying otherwhat, he let lay out all his apparel in a chamber and carrying him thither, said to him, ‘Look, Christian, if there be any among these gowns that thou hast ever seen.’ Torello looked and saw those which his lady had given Saladin; but, natheless, conceiving not that they could possibly be the same, he answered, ‘My lord, I know none of them;
uz: Bu janobni eslatdi va unga tik tikilib qaradi, go'yo bu o'zi edi; shuning uchun, avvalgi nutqni tashlab, u dedi: "Harkye, Christian," u dedi: "Siz G'arbdan bo'lgan qishloq odammisiz?" "Mening xo'jayinim," javob berdi Torello, "Men Paviya shahridan kelgan Lombardman, bir kambag'al odamman va ahvolim yomon." Saladin buni eshitib, o'z gumonining haqiqatligiga amin bo'ldi va xursand bo'lib dedi: "Alloh menga bu odamga uning menga qanchalik minnatdor ekanligini ko'rsatish imkoniyatini berdi." Shunga ko'ra, u o'zining barcha kiyimlarini xonaga tashladi va uni unga dedi: "Mana, hech kimga bunday ko'rmagan bo'lsa ham, men ularni ko'rmaganman."

en: albeit, in good sooth, these twain do favour certain gowns wherewithal I, together with three merchants who came to my house, was invested aforetime.’ Thereupon Saladin, unable to contain himself farther, embraced him tenderly, saying, ‘You are Messer Torello d’Istria and I am one of the three merchants to whom your lady gave these gowns; and now is the time come to certify you what manner merchandise mine is, even as I told you, at my parting from you, might chance to betide.’ Messer Torello, hearing this, was at once rejoiced and ashamed; rejoiced to have had such a guest and ashamed for that him- seemed he had entertained him but scurvily.
uz: Garchi, yaxshi holatda bo'lsa ham, bu ikkalasi ham bir nechta ko'ylaklarni yaxshi ko'rishadi, ular bilan birga mening uyimga kelgan uch nafar savdogar ham ilgari sarmoya kiritgan edi." Shunda Saladin o'zini uzoqroq ushlab tura olmay, uni muloyimlik bilan quchoqlab, dedi: "Sen Istriyalik Torello janobisan va men bu ko'ylaklarni bergan uch nafar savdogardan biriman; va endi mening tovarim nima ekanligini sizga tasdiqlash vaqti keldi, hatto men sizdan ketayotganimda uni o'ziga tortish imkoniyati bor edi deb aytgan edim." Buni eshitib, janob Torello darhol xursand bo'ldi va uyaldi; bunday mehmon bo'lganidan xursand bo'ldi va uyaldi, lekin u...

en: Then said Saladin, ‘Messer Torello, since God hath sent you hither to me, henceforth consider that not I, but you are master here.’ Accordingly, after they had mightily rejoiced in each other, he clad him in royal apparel and carrying him into the presence
uz: Shunda Saladin dedi: "Janob Torello, Xudo sizni bu yerga menga yuborgan ekan, bundan buyon men emas, balki siz bu yerda xo'jayin ekanligingizni hisobga oling." Shunga ko'ra, ular bir-birlaridan juda xursand bo'lgandan so'ng, u uni qirollik kiyimida kiydirdi va olib kirdi.

en: of all his chief barons, commanded, after saying many things in praise of his worth, that he should of all who held his favour dear be honoured as himself, which was thenceforward done of all, but above all of the two gen- tlemen who had been Saladin’s companions in his house.
uz: Uning barcha bosh baronlari, o'z qadrini maqtash uchun ko'p gapirganidan so'ng, o'z marhamatini qadrlaganlarning barchasi oldida o'zi kabi hurmatga sazovor bo'lishini buyurdilar, bu esa bundan buyon hammaga, faqatgina Saladinning uyida hamroh bo'lgan ikki janobdan ustun edi.

en: The sudden height of glory to which Messer Torello thus found himself advanced put his Lombardy affairs somedele out of his mind, more by token that he had good reason to hope that his letters were by this come to his uncle’s hands.
uz: Messer Torello o'zini shunday rivojlangan deb topgan birdanki shon-shuhrat cho'qqisi uning Lombardiya ishlarini unutib qo'ydi, ko'proq uning xatlari shu orqali amakisining qo'liga yetib borishiga umid qilish uchun asosli sababga ega edi.

en: Now there had died and been buried in the camp or rather in the host, of the Christians, the day they were taken by Saladin, a Provençal gentleman of little account, by name Messer Torello de Dignes, by reason whereof, Messer Torello d’Istria being renowned throughout the army for his magniﬁcence, whosoever heard say, ‘Messer Torello is dead,’ believed it of Messer Torello d’Istria, not of him of Dignes.
uz: Xristianlar lagerda yoki aniqrog'i qo'shinda o'lgan va dafn etilgan edi, o'sha kuni ular Saladin tomonidan olib ketilgan edi, provensial janob, kichik hisobda, Messer Torello de Dignes nomi bilan. Shuning uchun, Messer Torello dIstria o'z ulug'vorligi bilan butun armiyada mashhur bo'lgani sababli, "Messer Torello o'ldi", deganini eshitgan har bir kishi buni Messer Torello dIstria deb ishonardi, Dignes haqida emas.

en: The hazard of the capture that ensued thereupon suffered not those who had been thus misled to be undeceived; wherefore many Italians returned with this news, amongst whom were some who scrupled not to avouch that they had seen him dead and had been at the burial.
uz: Natijada qo'lga tushish xavfi shu yo'l bilan chalg'itilganlarni chalg'imaslikka olib kelmadi; shuning uchun ko'plab italyanlar bu xabar bilan qaytishdi, ularning orasida uni o'lik holda ko'rganlarini va dafn marosimida bo'lganlarini aytishdan bosh tortganlar ham bor edi.

en: This, coming to be known of his wife and kinsfolk, was the cause of grievous and inexpressible sorrow, not only to them, but to all who had known him.
uz: Bu uning xotini va qarindoshlari tomonidan ma'lum bo'lib, nafaqat ularga, balki uni bilgan barcha odamlarga ham qayg'u va ifodalab bo'lmaydigan qayg'u keltirdi.

en: It were longsome to set forth what and how great was the grief and sorrow and lamentation of his lady; but, after having bemoaned herself some months in continual afﬂiction, coming to sorrow less and being sought in marriage with the chiefest men in Lom- bardy, she began to be presently importuned by her brothers and other her kinsfolk to marry again.
uz: Uning xonimining qayg'usi, qayg'usi va nolasi qanchalik buyuk ekanligini aytish juda qiyin edi; lekin, bir necha oy davomida doimiy azobda o'ziga achinib, kamroq qayg'uga kelib, Lom-garidagi eng zo'r erkaklar bilan turmushga chiqishga intilgandan so'ng, u yana turmushga chiqishga birodarlari va boshqa qarindoshlari tomonidan qiziqtirilishni boshladi.

en: After having again and again refused with many tears, needs must she at the last consent perforce to do her kinsfolk’s will, on condition that she should abide, without going to a husband, so long as she had promised Messer Torello.
uz: Ko'p ko'z yoshlari bilan qayta-qayta rad etganidan so'ng, u oxirgi rozilik bilan qarindoshlari irodasini bajarishga majbur bo'lishi kerak edi, sharti shuki u eriga bormasdan, Messer Torelloga va'da bergan taqdirdagina yashasin.

en: The lady’s affairs at Pavia being at this pass and there lacking maybe eight days of the term appointed for her going to her new husband, it chanced that Messer Torello espied one day in Alexandria one whom he had seen embark with the Genoese ambassadors on board the galley that was to carry them back to Genoa, and calling him, asked him what manner voyage they had had and when they had reached Genoa; whereto the other replied, ‘Sir, the galleon (as I heard in Crete, where I remained), made an ill voyage; for that, as she drew near unto Sicily, there arose a furious northerly wind, which drove her on to the Barbary quicksands, nor was anyone saved; and amongst the rest two brothers of mine perished there.’ Messer Torello, giv-
uz: Paviyadagi xonimning ishlari shu yo'lda bo'lgani va uning yangi eriga borishi uchun belgilangan muddatga sakkiz kun yetarli bo'lmagani sababli, Messer Torello bir kuni Iskandariyada Genua elchilari bilan birga ularni Genuaga olib ketadigan galleyga chiqqanini ko'rganini kuzatgan va uni chaqirib, qanday sayohat qilganlari va Genuyaga qachon yetib kelganlari haqida so'ragan edi; shunga javoban, "Janob, galley (men Kritda qolganim)da eshitganimdek, yomon sayohat qilgan; chunki u Sitsiliyaga yaqinlashganda, uni Barbary qirg'oqlariga haydab kelgan g'azablantiroq shamol paydo bo'ldi, u qutqarilmadi; va qolgan ikki birodarim orasida hech kim..." dedi Messer Torello.

en: ing credit to his words, which were indeed but too true, and remembering him that the term required by him of his wife ended a few days thence, con- cluded that nothing could be known at Pavia of his condition and held it for certain that the lady must have married again; wherefore he fell into such a chagrin that he lost [sleep and] appetite and taking to his bed, determined to die.
uz: Uning so'zlariga ishonib, bu so'zlari juda ham to'g'ri edi, va uni xotiniga talab qilingan muddat bir necha kundan keyin tugaydi deb eslab, Paviyada uning ahvoli haqida hech narsa bilish mumkin emasligini angladi va xonim qayta turmushga chiqishi kerakligini aniq deb hisobladi; shuning uchun u shunchalik xafa bo'ldiki, ishtahani yo'qotdi va o'z karavoyiga yotdi, o'lishga qaror qildi.

en: When Saladin, who loved him above all, heard of this, he came to him and having, by dint of many and urgent prayers, learned the cause of his grief and his sickness, upbraided him sore for that he had not before told it to him and after besought him to be comforted, assuring him that, if he would but take heart, he would so contrive that he should be in Pavia at the appointed term and told him how.
uz: Salohiddin, uni eng ko'p sevgan inson, bu haqda eshitgach, uning oldiga keldi va ko'p va shoshilinch ibodatlar bilan uning qayg'usi va kasalligining sababini bilib, unga bu haqda oldin aytmaganligi uchun qattiq tanbeh berdi va undan tasalli so'raganidan so'ng, agar u jasorat topmoqchi bo'lsa, belgilangan muddatga Paviyada bo'lishga harakat qilishini va unga qanday qilib aytishini ishontirdi.

en: Messer Torello, putting faith in Saladin’s words and having many a time heard say that this was possible and had in- deed been often enough done, began to take comfort and pressed Saladin to despatch.
uz: Messer Torello, Saladinning so'zlariga ishonib, bu mumkin edi va amalda tez-tez qilingan degan gaplarni ko'p eshitib, tasalli ola boshladi va Saladinni jo'natishga undadi.

en: The Soldan accordingly charged a nigromancer of his, of whose skill he had aforetime made proof, to cast about for a means whereby Mess- er Torello should be in one night transported upon a bed to Pavia, to which the magician replied that it should be done, but that, for the gentleman’s own weal, he must put him to sleep.
uz: Soldan o'zining bir nigromantiga, uning mahorati allaqachon isbotlangan bo'lsa ham, Mess-er Torelloni bir kechada Paviyaga ko'tarib olib ketish uchun bir vosita qidirishni buyurdi. Sehrgar unga shunday qilish kerakligini, lekin janobning o'zi uchun uni uxlatishi kerakligini aytdi.

en: This done, Saladin returned to Messer Torello and ﬁnding him altogether resolved to seek at any hazard to be in Pavia at the term appointed, if it were possible, and in default thereof, to die, bespoke him thus; ‘Messer Torello, God knoweth that I neither will nor can anywise blame you if you tenderly love your lady and are fearful of her becoming another’s, for that, of all the women I ever saw, she it is whose manners, whose fashions and whose demeanour, (leaving be her beauty, which is but a short-lived ﬂower), appear to me most worthy to be commended and held dear.
uz: Shundan so'ng, Saladin Messer Torello huzuriga qaytib keldi va uni Paviyada tayinlangan muddatga, agar iloji bo'lsa, o'lish uchun har qanday xavfni izlashga qat'iy qaror qilgan holda topdi. Shunda, u shunday dedi: "Messer Torello, Xudo biladi, men sizni na samimiy sevgi bilan sevsam, na undan boshqa bo'lishdan qo'rqaman, chunki men ko'rgan barcha ayollardan, u o'z odoblari, modalari va xulq-atvorlari (qisqa umr ko'radigan guli go'zalligidan tashqari), menga eng maqtalishga loyiq va qadrlanadigan ko'rinadi."

en: It had been very grateful to me, since fortune hath sent you hither, that we should have passed together, as equal masters in the governance of this my realm, such time as you and I have to live, and if this was not to be vouchsafed me of God, it being fated that you should take it to heart to seek either to die or to ﬁnd yourself in Pavia at the appointed term, I should above all have de- sired to know it in time, that I might have you transported to your house with such honour, such magniﬁcence and in such company as your worth meriteth.
uz: Men uchun juda minnatdor bo'lgan edim, chunki omad sizni bu yerga yuborgan edi, siz va men yashashimiz kerak bo'lgan davrda mening saltanatim boshqaruvida teng ustozlar sifatida birga o'tgan bo'lishimiz kerak edi. Agar bu Xudo tomonidan menga nasib qilmagan bo'lsa, siz o'lishni yoki belgilangan muddatda Paviyada o'zingizni topishni o'z yuragingizga olishingiz kerak edi, men, avvalo, buni o'z vaqtida bilishga qaror qilgan bo'lardim, sizni uyingizga shunday sharaf bilan, shunday ulug'vorlik bilan va siz haqli bo'lganidek hamrohlikda olib kelishim mumkin edi.

en: However, since this hath not been vouchsafed and you desire to be presently there, I will e’en, as I may, despatch you thither after the fashion whereof I have bespoken you.’ ‘My lord,’ replied Messer Torello, ‘your acts, without your words, have given me sufﬁcient proof of your favour, which I
uz: Ammo, bu taqdirlanmagan va siz u yerda hozir bo'lishni xohlayotgan ekansiz, men sizni o'sha yo'l bilan u yerga jo'nataman. Ey xo'jayin, javob berdi Messer Torello, sening so'zlaringsiz qilgan ishlaring menga o'z marhamatingni yetarli darajada isbotladi,

en: have never merited in such supreme degree, and of that which you say, though you had not said it, I shall live and die most assured; but, since I have taken this resolve, I pray you that that which you tell me you will do may be done speedily, for that tomorrow is the last day I am to be looked for.’ Saladin answered that this should without fail be accomplished and ac- cordingly, on the morrow, meaning to send him away that same night, he let make, in a great hall of his palace, a very goodly and rich bed of mattresses, all, according to their usance, of velvet and cloth of gold and caused lay thereon a counterpoint curiously wrought in various ﬁgures with great pearls and jewels of great price (the which here in Italy was after esteemed an inestimable treasure) and two pillows such as sorted with a bed of that fashion.
uz: Hech qachon bunday oliy darajaga loyiq bo'lmaganman, va siz aytgan gapingizdan, garchi siz aytmagan bo'lsangiz ham, men juda ishonch bilan yashayman va o'laman; lekin, men bu qarorni qabul qilganimdan so'ng, siz menga aytgan ish tezroq amalga oshirilsin, chunki ertaga men qidirilishi kerak bo'lgan oxirgi kun." Saladin javob berdi: "Bu albatta amalga oshirilishi kerak va shu kuni, ya'ni o'sha kecha uni jo'natish kerak, u o'z saroyining katta zalida, o'z qoidalariga ko'ra, baxmal va oltindan yasalgan juda yaxshi va boy matraslar to'shagini yasadi va u yerda katta marvaridlar va qimmatbaho durdonalar bilan bezatilgan (bu yerda Italiyada qimmatbaho xazina bo'lgan) va shunday ikki xil yostiq bilan

en: This done, he bade invest Messer Torello, who was presently well and strong again, in a gown of the Saracen fashion, the richest and goodliest thing that had ever been seen of any, and wind about his head, after their guise, one of his longest turban-cloths.479 Then, it growing late, he betook himself with many of his barons to the chamber where Messer Torello was and seating himself, well nigh weeping, by his side, bespoke him thus; ‘Messer Torello, the hour draweth near that is to sunder me from you, and since I may not bear you company nor cause you to be accompanied, by reason of the nature of the journey you have to make, which suffereth it not, needs must I take leave of you here in this chamber, to which end I am come hither.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u Saratsan uslubidagi ko'ylakka, hozirda sog'lom va kuchli bo'lgan janob Torelloga eng boy va eng yaxshi narsani joylashtirmoqchi edi, va ularning ko'rinishiga ko'ra, boshida eng uzun turban-ko'ylaklaridan biri bo'lardi. 479 Keyin, kech bo'lib, u o'zining ko'plab baronlari bilan janob Torello o'tirgan xonaga bordi va o'zi yig'lab, uning yonida shunday dedi: "Janob Torello, meni sizdan ajratib yuboradigan soat yaqinlashmoqda va men sizni na birga olib yurishga majbur emasman, chunki sayohatning mohiyati tufayli siz bilan birga bo'lishingiz kerak, bu esa...

en: Wherefore, ere I commend you to God, I conjure you, by that love and that friendship that is between us, that you remember you of me and if it be possible, ere our times come to an end, that, whenas you have ordered your affairs in Lombardy, you come at the least once to see me, to the end that, what while I am cheered by your sight, I may then supply the default which needs must I presently commit by reason of your haste; and against that betide, let it not irk you to visit me with letters and require me of such things as shall please you; for that of a surety I will more gladly do them for you than for any man alive.’ As for Messer Torello, he could not contain his tears; wherefore, being hindered thereby, he answered, in a few words, that it was impossible his beneﬁts and his nobility should ever escape his mind and that he would without fail do that which he enjoined him, whenas
uz: Shuning uchun, seni Xudoga taslim etmasimdan oldin, o'sha sevgi va o'rtamizdagi do'stlik orqali seni meni eslashga undayman va agar iloji bo'lsa, zamonimiz tugashidan oldin, Lombardiyada ishlaringga buyurganingdan so'ng, hech bo'lmaganda bir marta meni ko'rishga kelishingni so'rayman. Oxirida, men seni ko'rib xursand bo'lganimda, shoshilinchliging tufayli hozirda amalga oshirishim kerak bo'lgan xatolarni ta'minlay olaman; va o'sha xatoga qarshi, meni xatlar bilan ko'rishga va senga yoqadigan narsalarni so'ramaslikka undama; chunki, albatta, men ularni siz uchun tirik odamdan ko'ra ko'proq xursand bo'laman.

en: occasion should be af- forded him; whereupon Saladin, having tenderly embraced him and kissed him, bade him with many tears God speed and departed the chamber.
uz: Unga imkoniyat yaratib berilsin; shundan so'ng Saladin uni mehr bilan quchoqlab, o'pdi, ko'p yoshlar bilan Xudo tezligini so'radi va xonadan ketdi.

en: other barons then all took leave of him and followed the Soldan into the hall where he had caused make ready the bed.
uz: Boshqa baronlar hammasi undan xayrlashdilar va Soldanning ortidan yotoqni tayyorlashga buyurgan zalga kirishdi.

en: Meanwhile, it waxing late and the nigromant awaiting and pressing for despatch, there came a physician to Messer Torello with a draught and making him believe that he gave it him to fortify him, caused him drink it; nor was it long ere he fell asleep and so, by Saladin’s commandment, was carried into the hall and laid upon the bed aforesaid, whereon the Soldan placed a great and goodly crown of great price and inscribed it on such wise that it was after manifestly understood to be sent by him to Messer Torello’s lady; after which he put on Torello’s ﬁn- ger a ring, wherein was a carbuncle enchased, so resplendent that it seemed a lighted ﬂambeau, the value whereof could scarce be reckoned, and girt him with a sword, whose garniture might not lightly be appraised.
uz: Ayni paytda, kech bo'layotganda va noshudlar jo'natishni kutayotganda, bir shifokor janob Torelloning oldiga bir cho'tka bilan keldi va uni o'zi uni mustahkamlab, ichishga majbur qilganiga ishontirdi; u uxlab qolishi ham ko'p bo'lmadi va shuning uchun, Saladinning buyrug'i bilan, zalga olib kirildi va yuqorida aytilgan karavotga qo'yildi. Soldan katta va yaxshi bir tojni katta narxga qo'ydi va uni shunday yozib qo'ydi, shunda u o'zi tomonidan janob Torelloning xonimiga yuborilishi aniq edi; shundan so'ng u Torelloning qanoq uzug'iga taqdi, unda qilich taqilgan edi, shunday yorqinki, u yengil bo'lishi mumkin edi, va uning bilan birga qotirilgan

en: Moreover, he let hang a fermail on his breast, wherein were pearls whose like were never seen, together with other precious stones galore, and on his either side he caused set two great basins of gold, full of doubloons, and many strings of pearls and rings and girdles and other things, which it were tedious to recount, round about him.
uz: Qolaversa, u ko'kragiga marjon osib qo'ydi, unda hech qachon ko'rmagan marvaridlar, boshqa qimmatbaho toshlar bilan birga, va uning ikki tomonida ikki katta oltin havzasi o'rnatdi, ular ikki xil rangga to'la edi, va atrofida ko'plab marvaridlar, halqalar, kamarlar va boshqa narsalarni ko'rsatdi, ularni aytib berish zerikarli edi.

en: This done, he kissed him once more and bade the nigromant despatch, whereupon, in his presence, the bed was incontinent taken away, Messer Torello and all, and Saladin abode devising of him with his barons.
uz: Shundan so'ng, u uni yana bir bor o'pdi va beparvo odamni jo'natib yubordi, shundan so'ng, uning huzurida karavot butunlay olib qo'yildi, janob Torello va boshqalar, va Saladin uning baronlari bilan birga uni o'ylab yashadi.

en: Meanwhile, Messer Torello had been set down, even as he had requested, in the church of San Pietro in Ciel d’Oro at Pavia, with all the jewels and ornaments aforesaid, and yet slept when, matins having sounded, the sac- ristan of the church entered, with a light in his hand, and chancing suddenly to espy the rich bed, not only marvelled, but, seized with a terrible fright, turned and ﬂed.
uz: Ayni paytda, janob Torello, o'zi so'raganidek, Paviyadagi San Pietro in Ciel dOro cherkovida, barcha zargarlik buyumlari va bezaklari bilan yotardi va shunga qaramay, uxlardi, qachonki, ertalabki kunlar yangraganidan so'ng, cherkovning muqaddas qismiga kirdi, qo'lida chiroq bilan, va to'satdan boy to'shakka qarab, nafaqat hayratga tushdi, balki dahshatli qo'rquv bilan qamrab olindi, o'girilib qochdi.

en: The abbot and the monks, seeing him ﬂee, marvelled and questioned him of the cause, which he told them; whereupon quoth the ab- bot, ‘Marry, thou art no child nor art thou new to the church that thou shouldst thus lightly take fright; let us go see who hath played the bugbear with thee.’ Accordingly, kindling several lights, the abbot and all his monks entered the church and saw that wonder-rich and goodly bed and thereon the gentleman asleep; and what while, misdoubting and fearful, they gazed upon the noble jewels, without drawing anywise near to the bed, it befell that, the virtue of the draught being spent, Messer Torello awoke and heaved a great sigh, which when the monks saw and heard, they took to ﬂight, abbot and all, affrighted and crying, ‘Lord aid us!’ Messer Torello opened his eyes and looking about him, plainly perceived himself to be
uz: Abbot va rohiblar, uni qochganini ko'rib, hayratda qolishdi va sababini so'roq qilishdi, u ularga aytdi; shundan so'ng abbot dedi: "Uylan, sen na bola, na endi cherkovga qo'rqishing kerak; keling, sen bilan qurtni kim o'ynaganini ko'raylik." Shunga ko'ra, bir necha chiroq yoqib, abbot va uning barcha rohiblari cherkovga kirdilar va u ajoyib va yaxshi yotoqni va u yerda uxlayotgan janobni ko'rdilar; va shu bilan birga, ikkilanish va xavotir bilan, ular qimmatbaho toshlarga tikilib, hech qanday yaqinlashmasdan, to'shakka yaqinlashdi, Messerello uyg'onib, katta bir ko'rinishni ko'rdi, shunda ular monksni ko'rishdi va uni ko'rishdi, va uni ko'rishdi, ko'zlarini ochib, yordam berishdi va...

en: whereas he had asked Saladin to have him carried, at which he was mightily content.
uz: Holbuki, u Salohiddan uni ko'tarib yurishni so'ragan edi, shunda u juda mamnun edi.

en: Then, sitting up, he particularly examined that which he had about him, and for all he had before known of the magniﬁcence of Saladin, it seemed to him now greater and he knew it more.
uz: So'ngra o'rnidan turib, u o'zi haqida nima borligini ayniqsa ko'rib chiqdi va avvalroq Saladinning ulug'vorligi haqida bilgan bo'lsa ham, bu unga endi kattaroq ko'rindi va u buni ko'proq bilardi.

en: Nevertheless, without moving farther, seeing the monks ﬂee and divining why, he proceeded to call the abbot by name, praying him be not afraid, for that he was Torello his nephew.
uz: Shunga qaramay, uzoqroqqa harakat qilmasdan, rohiblar qochayotganini ko'rib va nima uchunligini aniqlab, u abbotni ismlari bilan chaqirib, undan qo'rqmaslikni so'radi, chunki u Torello uning jiyani edi.

en: The abbot, hearing this, waxed yet more fearful, as holding him as dead many months before; but, after awhile, taking assurance by true ar- guments and hearing himself called, he made the sign of the cross and went up to him; whereupon quoth Messer Torello, ‘How now, father mine, of what are you adread?
uz: Buni eshitib, abbat yanada qo'rqib ketdi, go'yo uni o'likdek ko'p oylar oldin ushlab turgandek edi; lekin, biroz vaqt o'tgach, haqiqiy ar- gumentlar bilan ishonch hosil qilib, o'zini chaqirilganini eshitib, xoch belgisini qildi va unga ko'tarildi; shundan so'ng Messer Torello dedi: "Hozir qanday, otam, nimadan qaytyapsan?"

en: Godamercy, I am alive and returned hither from bey- ond seas.’ The abbot, for all he had a great beard and was clad after the Saracen fashion, presently recognized him and altogether reassured, took him by the hand, saying, ‘My son, thou art welcome back.’ Then he continued, ‘Thou must not marvel at our affright, for that there is not a man in these parts but ﬁrmly believeth thee to be dead, insomuch that I must tell thee that Madam Adalieta thy wife, overmastered by the prayers and threats of her kinsfolk and against her own will, is married again and is this morning to go to her new husband; ay, and the bride-feast and all that pertaineth unto the nuptial festivities is prepared.’ Therewithal Messer Torello arose from off the rich bed and greeting the abbot and the monks with marvellous joyance, prayed them all to speak with none of that his return, against he should have des- patched
uz: Yaxshiyam, men tirikman va bey-ond dengizlaridan bu yerga qaytdim." Abbat, chunki u katta soqolga ega edi va Saracen uslubida kiyingan edi, darhol uni tanib oldi va butunlay xotirjam bo'lib, uni qo'lidan ushladi va dedi: "O'g'lim, sen qaytib kelding." Keyin u davom etdi: "Bizning ahvolimizga hayron bo'lma, chunki bu hududlarda seni o'lgan deb qat'iy ishonadigan odam yo'q, shuning uchun men senga shuni aytishim kerakki, Madam Adalieta xotining, qarindoshlarining ibodatlari va tahdidlari tufayli va o'z xohishiga qarshi, yana turmushga chiqdi va bugun ertalab uning yangi eriga boradi; ha, kelin va barcha katta bayramlarga tegishli bo'lgan narsa bilan birga qaytdi.

en: an occasion of his; after which, having caused lay up the costly jewels in safety, he recounted to his uncle all that had befallen him up to that moment.
uz: Uning bir munosabati; shundan so'ng, qimmatbaho javohirlarni xavfsizlikka qo'yib, u amakiga o'sha paytgacha bo'lgan hamma narsani aytib berdi.

en: The abbot rejoiced in his happy fortunes and together with him, rendered thanks to God, after which Messer Torello asked him who was his lady’s new husband.
uz: Abbot o'zining baxtli taqdiridan xursand bo'ldi va u bilan birga Xudoga shukr qildi, shundan so'ng Messer Torello undan xonimning yangi eri kimligini so'radi.

en: The abbot told him and Torello said, ‘I have a mind, ere folk know of my return, to see what manner countenance is that of my wife in these nuptials; wherefore, albeit it is not the usance of men of your habit to go to entertainments of this kind, I would have you contrive, for the love of me, that we may go thither, you and I.’ The abbot replied that he would well and accordingly, as soon as it was day, he sent to the new bridegroom, saying that he would fain be at his nuptials with a friend of his, whereto the gentleman answered that it liked him passing well.
uz: Abbot unga aytdi va Torello dedi: Menda bir fikr bor edi, odamlar mening qaytishimni bilmasidan oldin, bu toylarda xotinimning qanday korinishini korish uchun; shuning uchun, garchi sizning odatingiz bolmasa ham, bunday kongilochar tadbirlarga borish odatiy odat emas, lekin men sizni oylab topishni xohlardim, menga muhabbat bilan, siz va men u yerga borishimiz mumkin. Abbot javob berdi: Yaxshi bolardi va shunga kora, kun bolishi bilanoq, u yangi kuyovga xabar yubordi, u dosti bilan toylarida bolishini aytdi, u yerda janob unga yaxshi otishni yoqtirardi.

en: Accordingly, eating-time come, Messer Torello, clad as he was, repaired with his uncle to the bridegroom’s house, beheld with wonderment of all
uz: Shunga ko'ra, ovqatlanish vaqti keldi, Messer Torello, o'zi qanday kiyinayotgan bo'lsa, amakisi bilan kuyovning uyiga qaytdi, hammaga hayrat bilan qaradi.

en: who saw him, but recognized of none; and the abbot told everyone that he was a Saracen sent ambassador from the Soldan to the King of France.
uz: Uni ko'rganlar, lekin hech kimni tanimasdi; va abbat hammaga u Saldondan Fransiya qiroliga elchi yuborilgan saracen ekanligini aytdi.

en: He was, therefore, seated at a table right overagainst his lady, whom he beheld with the utmost pleasure, and himseemed she was troubled in countenance at these new nuptials.
uz: Shunday qilib, u o'zining xonimining yonidagi stolga o'tirardi, uni juda xursandchilik bilan ko'rardi va unga bu yangi to'ylarda uning yuzida tashvish paydo bo'lgandek tuyuldi.

en: She, in her turn, looked whiles upon him, but not of any cognizance that she had of him, for that his great beard and outlandish habit and the ﬁrm assurance she had that he was dead hindered her thereof.
uz: U, o'z navbatida, unga befarq qaradi, lekin u haqida hech qanday xabardor emas edi, chunki uning katta soqollari va g'alati odatlari hamda uning o'lganligiga bo'lgan qat'iy ishonchi unga bunga to'sqinlik qilardi.

en: Presently, whenas it seemed to him time to essay if she remembered her of him, he took the ring she had given him at his parting and calling a lad who served before her, said to him, ‘Say to the bride, on my part, that it is the usance in my country, whenas any stranger, such as I am here, eateth at the bride-feast of any new-married lady, like herself, that she, in token that she holdeth him welcome at her table, send him the cup, wherein she drinketh, full of wine, whereof after the stranger hath drunken what he will, the cup being covered again, the bride drinketh the rest.’ The page did his errand to the lady, who, like a well-bred and discreet woman as she was, believing him to be some great gentleman, commanded, to show him that she had his coming in gree, that a great gilded cup, which stood before her, should be washed and ﬁlled with wine and carried to the gentleman; and so it
uz: Hozirda, u uni eslashiga urinib ko'rishga vaqti kelganda, u xayrlashuvi paytida bergan uzukni oldi va undan oldinda xizmat qilgan yigitni chaqirib, unga dedi: "Kelinga ayting, men bu mening mamlakatimda odatdir, chunki men bu yerda bo'lgan har qanday begona, o'zi kabi yangi turmush qurgan ayolning kelinlik ziyofatida yeydi, shunda u uni stolida kutib olgani uchun unga piyola yuboradi, unda u sharob bilan to'la ichadi, undan keyin u xohlaganidan keyin, piyola qoplanganidan keyin, kelin qolganini ichadi." Sahifa uni ayolga buyurdi.

en: was done.
uz: Ish bitdi.

en: Messer Torello, taking her ring in his mouth, contrived in drinking to drop it, unseen of any, into the cup, wherein having left but a little wine, he covered it again and despatched it to the lady.
