en: To these I am bound to render and do render thanks, for that, moved by a virtuous jealousy, they are so tender of my fame; but to their objection I reply on this wise; I confess to being a man of weight and to have been often weighed in my time, wherefore, speaking to those ladies who have not weighed me, I declare that I am not heavy; nay, I am so light that I abide like a nutgall in water, and considering that the preachments made of friars, to rebuke men of their sins, are nowadays for the most part seen full of quips and cranks and gibes, I conceived that these latter would not sit amiss in my stories written to ease women of melancholy.
uz: Men ularga minnatdorchilik bildirishim va minnatdorchilik bildirishim shart, chunki ular, fazilatli rashkdan ta'sirlanib, mening shuhratimga shunchalik mehribon; lekin ularning e'tiroziga shunday javob beraman: men o'z davrimda og'ir inson bo'lganimni va ko'p o'lchanganimni tan olaman. Shuning uchun, meni o'lchamaydigan ayollarga murojaat qilib, men og'ir emasligimni e'lon qilaman; aksincha, men shunchalik yengilmanki, suvda bir gayka kabi bardosh beraman va rohiblarning gunohlaridan ogohlantirish uchun qilingan va'dalari hozirgi kunda ko'p hollarda mayda-chuyda, teshiklar va g'ijirlarga to'la ko'riladi, deb o'yladimki, bularning oxirg'inlari ayollarni yengillashtirish uchun yozilgan hikoyalarimda o'tirmaydi.

en: Algates, an they should laugh overmuch on that account, the Lamentations of Jeremiah, the Passion of our Saviour and the Complaint of Mary Magdalen will lightly avail to cure them thereof.
uz: Algetlar, ular bu haqda juda ko'p kulishlari kerak edi, Yeremiyoning motamlari, Najotkorimizning azoblari va Magdalalik Maryamning shikoyati ularni davolash uchun yengil yordam beradi.

en: Again, who can doubt but there will to boot be found some to say that I have an ill tongue and a venomous, for that I have in sundry places written the truth anent the friars?
uz: Yana kim shubha qilishi mumkin, lekin mening yomon tilim va zaharli tilim borligini aytadiganlar topiladi, chunki men turli joylarda rohiblar haqida haqiqatni yozganman?

en: To those who shall say thus it must be forgiven, since it is not credible that they are moved by other than just cause, for that the friars are a good sort of folk, who eschew unease for the love of God and who grind with a full head of water and tell no tales, and but that they all savour somewhat of the buck-goat, their commerce would be far more agreeable.
uz: Shunday deydiganlarga kechirim berilishi kerak, chunki ularning adolatdan boshqa sababga ko'ra ta'sirlanishiga ishonish mumkin emas, chunki rohiblar Xudoning muhabbati uchun noqulaylikdan qochadigan, to'la bosh suv bilan mehnat qiladigan va hech qanday hikoya aytmaydigan yaxshi xalqdir, lekin ularning barchasi biroz echkining ta'mini his qilishsa, ularning savdosi ancha maqbul bo'lardi.

en: Natheless, I confess that the things of this world have no stability and are still on the change, and so may it have befallen of my tongue, the which, not to trust to mine own judgment, (which I eschew as most I may in my affairs), a she-neighbour of mine told me, not long since, was the best and sweetest in the world; and in good sooth, were this the case, there had been few of the foregoing stories to write.
uz: Shunga qaramay, tan olamanki, bu dunyoning narsalari barqaror emas va hali ham o'zgarib bormoqda, va shunday bo'lishi mumkinki, u mening tilimga tushdi, mening o'z hukmimga ishonmaslikka, (uni men ishlarimda eng ko'p chetlab o'tishim mumkin), qo'shnim menga yaqinda dunyodagi eng yaxshi va eng shirin deb aytgan edi; va xotirjamlik bilan aytganda, agar shunday bo'lsa, yuqorida aytilgan hikoyalarni yozish uchun kam bo'lardi.

en: But, for that those who say thus speak despitefully, I will have that which hath been said sufﬁce them for a reply; wherefore, leaving each of you henceforth to say and believe as seemeth good to her, it is time for me to make an end of words, humbly thanking Him who hath, after so long a labour, brought us with His help to the desired end.
uz: Lekin, shunday so'zlashuvchilar haqorat bilan gapiradigan bo'lsalar, aytganlarim ularga javob uchun yetarli bo'ladi; shuning uchun, har biringizni bundan buyon o'ziga ma'qul ko'ringanidek aytishga va ishonishga qo'yib, so'zlarni yakunlash va shunchalik uzoq mehnatdan so'ng bizni O'z yordamida kerakli maqsadga olib kelgan Zotga kamtarona minnatdorchilik bildirish vaqti keldi.

en: And you, charming ladies, abide you in peace with His fa- vour, remembering you of me, if perchance it proﬁt any of you aught to have read these stories.
uz: Sizlar ham, go'zal ayollar, Uning fazli bilan tinch yashanglar, meni eslab, agar bu hikoyalarni o'qiganingizdan hech kimga foyda kelmasa.

en: Here endeth the book called Decameron and surnamed Prince Galahalt.
uz: Bu yerda Dekameron deb nomlangan va shahzoda Galaxalt familiyasi bilan atalgan kitob tugaydi.

en: Galahalt or Gallehaut (Ital.
uz: Galahalt yoki Gallehaut (Italiya.

en: Galeotto), a personage of the old chivalric romance of “Lancelot du Lac,” where he is described as a neighbouring king (“roy doultre les marches”), who, after ﬁrst opposing the hero, is vanquished by him and becoming his conﬁdant, brings about the ﬁrst amorous interview between him and Guenevere; hence his name is generically used by Boccacio (following his great and favourite ex- amplar, Dante cf.
uz: Galeotto, Lancelot du Lacning eski ritsarlik romanining personaji, unda u qoshni qirol sifatida tavsiflangan (roy doultre les marches), u qahramonga qarshi chiqqanidan song, u bilan maglub bolib, uning sirdoshiga aylanadi, bu esa u va Guenevere ortasidagi birinchi sevgi suhbatiga olib keladi; shuning uchun uning nomini Boccacio (ozining buyuk va sevimli sobiq amplidan keyin, Dante cf.

en: 137, “Galeotto fu il libro e chi lo scrisse”), for a pander, go-between or one who kindles amorous desire in women and provokes them to satisfy it.
uz: 137, Galeotto fu il libro e che lo scrivere), ayollarda ishqiy istakni uyg'otuvchi va ularni uni qondirishga undaydigan odam uchun.

en: In this case he seems, by giving this surname to his book (or perhaps rather merely recording the fact that it had been so surnamed) to imply that its perusal is likely to have the same effect upon lovers or persons amorously inclined as that of the book unknown the reading of which played the Galahalt between Francesca and Paolo, loco citato.
uz: Bu holatda u o'z kitobiga shu familiyani berish orqali (balki shunchaki uning shunday familiyani yozganini yozish orqali) uning o'qilishi Francesca va Paolo o'rtasidagi "Galahalt" o'qilishi noma'lum bo'lgan kitobning sevgiga moyil bo'lgan ishqibozlari yoki shaxslarga ta'siriga ega bo'lishi mumkinligini nazarda tutgandek tuyuladi.

en: It is, however, not improb- able that the words “and surnamed Prince Galahalt” may have been added by someone other than Boccaccio, although the implied refer- ence to Dante is so much in his style and habit of thought as to make it at least probable that he was himself responsible for the addition.
uz: Ammo, "va familiyasi shahzoda Galahalt" so'zlari Bokachcho'dan boshqa birov tomonidan qo'shilgan bo'lishi mumkinligi mumkin emas, garchi Dantenga nisbatan nazarda tutilgan ishora uning uslubi va fikrlash odatlariga shunchalik bog'liqki, bu qo'shilish uchun uning o'zi mas'ul bo'lganini hech bo'lmaganda ehtimoliy ko'rsatadi.

en: It may be noted, by the way, that Galahalt appears in the Morte d’Arthur, where he is always styled “le haut prince,” but does not ﬁgure as go- between the two lovers.
uz: Aytgancha, Galahalt "Artur o'limi"da paydo bo'lishi mumkin, u yerda u doimo "katta shahzoda" deb ataladi, lekin ikki oshiq o'rtasida "go" sifatida ko'rinmaydi.

en: the few pages of which he speaks above.
uz: yuqorida aytib o'tgan bir necha sahifalari.

en: provisions made or means taken (consigli dati).
uz: Qo'llanilgan yoki qo'llanilgan choralar (maslahatlar).

en: Boccaccio con- stantly uses consiglio in this latter sense.
uz: Boccaccio doimiy ravishda maslahatni shu oxirgi ma'noda ishlatadi.

en: Accidente, what a modern physician would call “complication.” “Symptom” does not express the whole meaning of the Italian word.
uz: Baxtsiz hodisa, zamonaviy shifokor "asorat" deb ataydi. "Symptom" italyancha so'zning butun ma'nosini ifodalamaydi.

en: gravediggers (becchini).
uz: qabr qazuvchilar (becchini).

en: This is the equivalent Italian idiom.
uz: Bu italyancha idiomga teng.

en: expectation of gain from acting as tenders of the sick, gravedig- gers, etc.
uz: Kasal, dafn etilayotganlar va hokazolarning tenderlari vazifasini bajarishdan foyda kutish.

en: The word speranza is, however, constantly used by Dante and his follower Boccaccio in the contrary sense of “fear,” and may be so meant in the present instance.
uz: Umid so'zi, ammo, Dante va uning izdoshisi Bokachcho tomonidan doimiy ravishda "qo'rquv" ma'nosida ishlatiladi va hozirgi holatda shunday ma'noni anglatishi mumkin.

en: Or character (qualità).
uz: Yoki sifat.

en: I know of no explanation of these names by the commentators, who seem, indeed, after the manner of their kind, to have generally con- ﬁned themselves to the elaborate illustration and elucidation (or rather, alas!
uz: Men bu ismlarning sharhlovchilar tomonidan hech qanday tushuntirilishini bilmayman, ular, aslida, o'z turidagi odatlari tufayli, odatda o'zlarini murakkab tasvirlar va tushuntirishlarga (yoki to'g'rirog'i, afsuski!

en: too often, obscuration) of passages already perfectly plain, leav- ing the difﬁcult passages for the most part untouched.
uz: Ko'pincha, allaqachon mukammal oddiy bo'lgan yo'laklarning xiraligi, qiyin yo'laklarni asosan teginmasdan qoldiradi.

en: The following is the best I can make of them.
uz: Quyida ulardan qila oladigan eng yaxshi narsa bor.

en: Pampinea appears to be formed from the Greek πᾶν, all, and πινύω, I advise, admonish or inform, and to mean all-advising or admonishing, which would agree well enough with the
uz: Pampinea yunoncha πν, all va πινύω so'zlaridan shakllangan ko'rinadi, men maslahat beraman, tanbeh beraman yoki xabar beraman, va hamma narsani maslahat beruvchi yoki ogohlantiruvchi degan ma'noni anglatadi, bu esa ... bilan yetarli darajada mos keladi.

en: character of Pampinea, who is represented as the eldest and sagest of the female personages of the Decameron and as taking the lead in everything.
uz: Pampinea xarakteri, u Dekamerondagi ayol qahramonlarning eng katta va eng kichiksi sifatida va hamma narsada yetakchi sifatida namoyon etilgan.

en: Fiammetta is the name by which Boccaccio designates his mistress, the Princess Maria of Naples (the lady for whom he cher- ished “the very high and noble passion” of which he speaks in his Proem), in his earlier opuscule, the Elégia di Madonna Fiammetta, de- scribing, in her name, the torments of separation from the beloved.
uz: Fiammetta Boccaccio o'zining bekasi, Neapollik malika Mariya (u o'zining "Proem"ida "juda yuksak va olijanob ehtiros"ni qadrlaydigan xonim)ni o'zining dastlabki opuskulyasida, "Elegia di Madonna Fiammetta"da sevgilisidan ajralish azoblarini uning nomidan yozib, tasvirlagan nomidir.

en: In this work he speaks of himself under the name of Pamﬁlo (Gr.
uz: Ushbu asarda u o'zi haqida Pamfilo (Gr.

en: πᾶν, all, and φιλέω, I love, i.e.
uz: "Qo'p, hammasi, va men sevaman, ya'ni."

en: the all-loving or the passionate lover), and it is probable, therefore, that under these names he intended to introduce his royal ladylove and himself in the present work.
uz: hammasini sevuvchi yoki ehtirosli oshiq), va shuning uchun ham ehtimolki, u shu nomlar ostida o'zining qirollik oshiqini va o'zini hozirgi ishga tanishtirmoqchi edi.

en: Filomena (Italian form of Philomela, a nightingale, Greek φίλος loving, and μελός, melody, song, i.e.
uz: Filomenalar (Italiyacha Philomela shakli, bulbul, yunoncha sevgilik do'st va μελός, ohang, qo'shiq, ya'ni.

en: song-loving) is perhaps so styled for her love of mu- sic, and Emilia’s character, as it appears in the course of the work, jus- tiﬁes the derivation of her name from the Greek αἱμύλιος, pleasing, engaging in manners and behaviour, cajoling.
uz: Qo'shiqsevar) balki uning mu-sicga bo'lgan muhabbati uchun shunday uslubga ega bo'lgandir, va Emilia'ning xarakteri, asar davomida ko'rinib turganidek, uning ismining yunoncha αμύλιος dan kelib chiqishini, yoqimli, odob va xulq-atvorga jalb qiluvchi, qoyil qoldiradigan.

en: Lauretta Boccaccio probably intends us to look upon as a learned lady, if, as we may sup- pose, her name is a corruption of laureata, laurel-crowned; whilst Nei- ﬁle’s name (Greek νεῖος [νεός] new, and φιλέω, I love, i.e.
uz: Lauretta Boccaccio, ehtimol, bizni o'qimishli ayol sifatida ko'rishni niyat qiladi, agar, biz ko'rsatayotganimizdek, uning ismi laureatning buzilishi, laurel tojli; nega-faylning nomi (yunoncha νεῖος [νεός] yangi, va φιλέω, I love, ya'ni

en: novelty- loving) stamps her as being of a somewhat curious disposition, eager “to tell or to hear some new thing.” The name Elisa is not so easily to be explained as the others; possibly it was intended by the author as a reminiscence of Dido, to whom the name (which is by some authorit- ies explained to mean “Godlike,” from a Hebrew root) is said to have been given “quòd plurima supra animi muliebris fortitudinem gesserit.” It does not, however, appear that there was in Elisa’s charac- ter or life anything to justify the implied comparison.
uz: Yangilikni sevuvchi) uni biroz qiziqarli xarakterga ega ekanligi, bir narsa aytishga yoki eshitishga ishtiyoqi borligi kabi belgilaydi. "Elisa ismini boshqalar kabi oson tushuntirish mumkin emas; ehtimol, muallif tomonidan Didoga esdalik sifatida mo'ljallangan edi, unga bu ism (ba'zi mualliflar tomonidan ibroniy ildizidan Xudojo'y ma'nosida tushuntirilgan) quòd plurima supra animi muliebris fortitudinem gesserit berilgan deb aytiladi."

en: This phrase may also be read “persuading themselves that that (i.e.
uz: Bu iborani o'qish ham mumkin  o'zlarini shunga ishontirib (ya'ni...

en: their breach of the laws of obedience, etc.) beseemeth them and is for- bidden only to others” (faccendosi a credere che quello a lor si con- venga e non si disdica che all’ altre); but the reading in the text ap- pears more in harmony with the general sense and is indeed indicated by the punctuation of the Giunta Edition of 1527, which I generally follow in case of doubt.
uz: Ularning itoat qonunlarini buzishlari ularni hurmat qiladi va faqatgina boshqalarga buyurilgan (shuning uchun, ularning buzilishi hammaga ma'qul emas deb ishonish mumkin); lekin matndagi o'qish umumiy ma'noga ko'proq mos keladi va haqiqatan ham 1527-yilgi Giunta nashrining nuqtalari bilan ko'rsatiladi, bunga men odatda shubha bo'lsa ham amal qilaman.

en: See note 17 earlier in the introduction.
uz: Kirishdagi 17-eslatmaga qarang.

en: Filostrato, Greek φίλος, loving, and στρατὸς, army, metaphorically strife, war, i.e.
uz: Filostrato, yunon do'sti, muhabbatli va qo'rqoq, armiya, metaforik janjal, urush, ya'ni.

en: one who loves strife.
uz: Janjalni sevuvchi odam.

en: This name appears to be a remin- iscence of Boccaccio’s poem (“Il Filostrato,” well known through its translation by Chaucer and the Senechal d’Anjou) upon the subject of the loves of Troilus and Cressida and to be in this instance used by him as a synonym for an unhappy lover, whom no rebuffs, no treachery can divert from his ill-starred passion.
uz: Bu nom Boccaccio'ning she'ri (Il Filostrato, Chaucer va Senechal dAnjou tarjimasi orqali yaxshi tanilgan)ning Troilus va Cressidaning muhabbat mavzusiga bag'ishlangan yodgorligi bo'lib ko'rinadi va bu holatda u tomonidan baxtsiz oshiqning sinonim sifatida ishlatiladi, uni hech qanday rad etish, hech qanday xiyonat o'zining yulduzsiz ishtiyoqidan chalg'ita olmaydi.

en: Such a lover may well be said to be in love with strife, and that the Filostrato of the Decameron sufﬁciently answers to this description we learn later on from his own lips.
uz: Bunday oshiqni janjalga oshiq deb aytish mumkin, va Dekameronning Filostrati bu ta'rifga keyinroq uning o'z lablaridan yetarli javob beradi deb o'ylashimiz mumkin.

en: Dioneo, a name probably coined from the Greek Διωνη, one of the ag- nomina of Venus (properly her mother’s name) and intended to denote the amorous temperament of his personage, to which, indeed, the erot- ic character of most of the stories told by him bears sufﬁcient witness.
uz: Dioneo, ehtimol yunoncha Διωνη dan o'ylab topilgan ism, Venera ismlaridan biri (aslida uning onasining ismi) va uning xarakterining ishqiy temperamentini ifodalashga mo'ljallangan bo'lib, unga, aslida, u aytib bergan ko'p hikoyalarning erotik xarakteri yetarli guvohlik beradi.

en: E prima mandato là dove, etc.
uz: Va birinchi jo'natma dovdir, va hokazo.

en: This passage is obscure and may be read to mean “and having ﬁrst despatched [a messenger] (or sent [word]) whereas,” etc.
uz: Bu parcha noaniq va uni va avval xabarchi yuborib (yoki so'zni yuborib) qo'ygan bo'lsa, va hokazo degan ma'noda o'qish mumkin.

en: I think, however, that mandato is a copyist’s er- ror for mandata, in which case the meaning would be as in the text.
uz: Menimcha, mandat nusxa ko'chirishchining mandat uchun er- roridir, bunda ma'no matndagi kabi bo'ladi.

en: Or balconies (loggie).
uz: Yoki balkonlar (loggilar).

en: Boccaccio’s habit of measuring time by the ca- nonical hours has been a sore stumbling-block to the ordinary English and French translator, who is generally terribly at sea as to his mean- ing, inclining to render tierce three, sexte six o’clock and none noon and making shots of the same wild kind at the other hours.
uz: Boccacconing vaqtni ka-nikal soatlar bilan o'lchash odati oddiy ingliz va fransuz tarjimonlari uchun og'riqli to'siq bo'lib kelgan, u odatda o'z ma'nosiga ko'ra juda dahshatli darajada dengizda bo'lib, uchinchi, oltinchi soat va tushlik emasligini ko'rsatishga moyil bo'lib, boshqa soatlarda xuddi shunday yovvoyi turdagi suratlarni suratga oladi.

en: The monas- terial rule (which before the general introduction of clocks was com- monly followed by the medieval public in the computation of time) di- vided the twenty-four hours of the day and night into seven parts (six of three hours each and one of six), the inception of which was de- noted by the sound of the bells that summoned the clergy to the per- formance of the seven canonical ofﬁces i.e.
uz: Monastir qoidasi (soatlarning umumiy joriy etilishidan oldin o'rta asrlar jamoatchiligi vaqt hisobida umumiy ravishda amal qilgan) kun va tunning yigirma to'rt soatini yetti qismga bo'lgan (har biri uch soatdan olti qismdan iborat), uning boshlanishi ruhoniylarni yetti kanonik idorani bajarishga chaqiradigan qo'ng'iroqlar ovozi bilan qayd etilgan, ya'ni

en: Matins at 3 a.m., Prime at 6 a.m., Tierce at 9 a.m., Sexte or Noonsong at noon, None at 3 p.m.,
uz: Ertalab soat 3:00 da, ertalab soat 6:00 da boshlang'ich, ertalab soat 9:00 da, tush paytida soat 6:00 da yoki tush paytida, kech soat 15:00 da yo'q.

en: Vespers or Evensong at 6 p.m.
uz: Kechki oqshom yoki kechki oqshom soat 18:00 da.

en: and Complines or Nightsong at 9 p.m., and at the same time served the laity as a clock.
uz: va Komplinlar yoki Tungi Qo'shiq soat 21:00 da, va shu bilan birga oddiy odamlarga soat kabi xizmat qildi.

en: The table of Boccaccio’s time was a mere board upon trestles, which when not in actual use, was stowed away, for room’s sake, against the wall.
uz: Boccaccio davri stollari oddiy taxta edi, u haqiqiy foydalanilmayotganda, xona uchun devorga qo'yilardi.

en: to take the siesta or midday nap common in hot countries.
uz: Issiq mamlakatlarda odatiy bo'lgan siesta yoki kunduzi uxlash uchun.

en: A Florentine merchant settled in France; he had great inﬂuence over Philippe le Bel and made use of the royal favour to enrich himself by means of monopolies granted at the expense of his compatriots.
uz: Florensiyalik savdogar Fransiyaga joylashdi; u Filipp Le Belga katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi va qirollik imtiyozidan foydalanib, o'z vatandoshlari hisobiga berilgan monopoliyalar orqali boyidi.

en: Charles, Comte de Valois et d’Alençon.
uz: Charlz, Valois va Alenson graflari.

en: Philippe le Bel, AD 1268 – 1314.
uz: Filipp Le Bel, Milodiy 1268  1314 yillar.

en: Cepparello means a log or stump.
uz: Cepparello - bu yog'och yoki poya degan ma'noni anglatadi.

en: Ciapperello is apparently a dia- lectic variant of the same word.
uz: Ciapperello, ko'rinishidan, xuddi shu so'zning dialektik variantidir.

en: Diminutive of Cappello.
uz: Cappelloning diminutivi.

en: This passage is obscure and most likely cor- rupt.
uz: Bu yo'lak noaniq va ehtimol, yoriqdir.

en: Boccaccio probably meant to write “hat” instead of “chaplet” (ghirlanda), as the meaning of cappello, chaplet (diminutive of Old English chapel, a hat), being the meaning of ciappelletto (properly cappelletto).
uz: Boccaccio, ehtimol, "haplet" (ghirlanda) o'rniga "hat" deb yozgan bo'lsa kerak, bu "cappello" ma'nosidir, "chaplet" (Qadimgi inglizcha ibodatxonaning qisqartmasi, shapka), bu esa ciappelletto (to'g'ri qilib aytganda cappelletto) ma'nosidir.

en: A “twopence-coloured” sketch of an impossible villain, drawn with a crudeness unusual in Boccaccio.
uz: Boccaccchida g'ayrioddiy qo'pollik bilan chizilgan, imkonsiz yovuz shaxsning "ikki rangli" eskizi.

en: if there be such a thing as a holy and worthy friar.
uz: Agar muqaddas va munosib rohib kabi narsa bo'lsa.

en: It will be noted that this is Boccaccio’s third variant of his hero’s name (the others being Ciapperello and Cepparello) and the edition of 1527 furnishes us with a fourth and a ﬁfth form i.e.
uz: Shuni ta'kidlash joizki, bu Bokachcho'ning qahramonining ismining uchinchi varianti (boshqalari Kiapperello va Cepparello) va 1527-yilgi nashri bizga to'rtinchi va beshinchi shakllarni taqdim etadi, ya'ni.

en: Ciepparello and Ciepperello.
uz: Ciepparello va Ciepperello.

en: of God’s benignness.
uz: Xudoning inoyatidan.

en: cardinal brethren (fratelli cardinali).
uz: Kardinal birodarlar.

en: losing (perdendo), but this is probably some copyist’s mistake for podendo, the old form of potendo, availing.
uz: yo'qotish (perdendo), lekin bu, ehtimol, ba'zi nusxachilarning "podendo" uchun xatosi bo'lsa kerak, bu "potendo"ning eski shakli bo'lib, foydalanishdir.

en: stood sponsor for him.
uz: U uchun homiy bo'ldi.

en: amorous (amorose), but Boccaccio frequently uses amoroso, vago, and other adjectives, which are now understood in an active or transit- ive sense only, in their ancient passive or intransitive sense of love- some, desirable, etc.
uz: amoroso (amoroz), lekin Bokkacko ko'pincha amoroso, vago va boshqa sifatlardan foydalanadi, ular endi faqat faol yoki tranzit ma'noda tushuniladi, qadimgi passiv yoki intransitiv sevgi ma'nosida - ba'zilar, istalgan va hokazo.

en: Filomena is addressing the female part of the company.
uz: Filomena kompaniyaning ayol qismiga murojaat qilmoqda.

en: his church (sua chiesa); but the context seems to indicate that the monastery itself is meant.
uz: uning cherkovi (sua chiesa); lekin kontekst monastirning o'zi nazarda tutilganini ko'rsatadiganga o'xshaydi.

en: a pressure or oppression (priemere, hod.
uz: bosim yoki zulm (priemere, hod.

en: premere, to press or op- press, indicative used as a noun).
uz: oldin, bosish yoki op-press, ot sifatida ishlatiladigan ko'rsatkich).

en: The monk of course refers to the pos- ture in which he had seen the abbot have to do with the girl, pretending to believe that he placed her on his own breast (instead of mounting on hers) out of a sentiment of humility and a desire to mortify his ﬂesh ipsâ in voluptate.
uz: Rohib, albatta, abbotning qiz bilan bog'liqligini ko'rgan holatga ishora qiladi, u uni kamtarlik tuyg'usi va o'z tanasini o'ldirish istagi tufayli o'z ko'kragida (uning ko'kragida o'tirgandan ko'ra) qo'yganligiga ishonganini ko'rsatadi.

en: An evident allusion to Boccaccio’s passion for the Princess Maria, i.e.
uz: Boccacconing malika Mariyaga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi, ya'ni...

en: le myope, the shortsighted, the Italian word [Il Bornio] having both meanings), i.e.
uz: "le myope", "qisqa ko'ruvchi", italyancha so'z [Il Bornio] har ikki ma'noga ega), ya'ni.

en: Philip II of France, better known as Philip Augustus.
uz: Fransiyalik Filipp II, ko'proq Filip Avgust nomi bilan tanilgan.

en: with sword and whips, a technical term of ecclesiastical procedure, about equivalent to our “with the strong arm of the law.” ↩  55.
uz: qilich va qamchilar bilan, cherkov tartibining texnik atamasi, bizning "qonunning kuchli qo'li bilan"ga teng.  55.

en: This word has been another grievous stumbling block to the French and English translators of Boccaccio, who render it liter- ally “courtier.” The reader need hardly be reminded that the minstrel of the middle ages was commonly jester, gleeman and storyteller all in one and in these several capacities was allowed the utmost license of speech.
uz: Bu so'z Boccaccio'ning fransuz va ingliz tarjimonlari uchun yana bir og'ir to'siq bo'lib kelgan, ular uni harf-so'z bo'yicha ittifoqchi solih deb tarjima qilishadi. O'quvchiga o'rta asrlarning minstrellari odatda hazilkash, yaltiroq va hikoyachi bo'lganligi va shu bir nechta xususiyatlarda so'zlashuvga maksimal ruxsat berilganligi eslatib o'tilmaydi.

en: He was generally attached to the court of some king or sover- eign prince, but, in default of some such permanent appointment, passed his time in visiting the courts and mansions of princes and men of wealth and liberty, where his talents were likely to be appreciated and rewarded; hence the name uomo di corte, “man of court” (not “courtier,” which is cortigiano).
uz: U odatda qandaydir podshoh yoki sovernik shahzoda saroyiga biriktirilgan edi, lekin, bunday doimiy tayinlanishni buzganda, o'z vaqtini shahzodalar va boylik va erkinlik egalarining saroylariga va saroylariga tashrif buyurish bilan o'tkazardi, u yerda uning iste'dodlari qadrlanishi va mukofotlanishi mumkin edi; shuning uchun u "kurti odami" deb nomlangan.

en: The cardinal struggle between the two factions took place over the succes- sion to the throne of Naples and Sicily, to which the Pope appointed Charles of Anjou, who overcame and killed the reigning sovereign Manfred, but was himself, through the machinations of the Ghibel- lines, expelled from Sicily by the celebrated popular rising known as the Sicilian Vespers.
uz: Ikki fraktsiya o'rtasidagi kardinal kurash Neapol va Sitsiliya taxtini egallash uchun bo'lib o'tdi, bunga Rim Papasi Anjoulik Charlzni tayinladi. U hukmron hukmdor Manfredni yengib o'ldirgan, ammo Ghibel liniyasining fitnalari orqali o'zi Sitsiliyalik Vesperlar deb nomlanuvchi mashhur xalq ko'tarilishi tomonidan Sitsiliyadan haydalgan edi.

en: to which general joy.
uz: Umumiy quvonchga.

en: Pedro of Arragon, son-in-law of Manfred, who, in consequence of the Sicilian Vespers, succeeded Charles d’Anjou as King of Sicily.

uz: Misr, Qohira o'rta asrlarda Misr Bobili nomi bilan tanilgan. Shuni ta'kidlash kerakki, Injildagi Bobil bu nomdagi shahar edi, Furot daryosida, Xaldeyaning qadimgi poytaxti (Iroq Bobili).

en: AD 912, when, upon the death of Louis III, the last prince of the Carlovingian race, Conrad, Duke of Franconia, was elected Emperor and the Empire, which had till then been hereditary in the descendants of Charlemagne, became elective and remained thenceforth in German hands.
uz: Milodiy 912-yilda, Karlvingiy irqining oxirgi shahzodasi Lui III vafotidan so'ng, Frankon gersogi Konrad imperator etib saylandi va Charlz Buyukning avlodlarida merosxo'r bo'lgan imperiya tanlab olindi va bundan keyin nemis qo'lida qoldi.

uz: Men ko'rgan barcha versiyalarda Gautier Graf dAngers yoki Angiers deb ataladi, bu tarjimonlar Antverpen, Flandriyaning bir qismi sifatida, o'shanda Fransiya tojining mulki bo'lganidan xabardor bo'lishgan yoki bexabar bo'lishgan, ko'rinishidan, bu shahar haqida gapirish xato edi va Anjou qadimiy poytaxtining nomini o'z mas'uliyatlari bilan almashtirgan.

en: This confusion of persons constantly occurs in Boccaccio, espe- cially in the conversational parts of the Decameron, in which he makes the freest use of the various forms of enallage and of other rhetorical ﬁgures, such as hyperbaton, synecdoche, etc., to the no small detriment of his style in the matter of clearness.

en: The plural of a surname is, in strictness, always used by the Italians in speaking of a man by his full name, dei being understood between the Christian and surname, as Benedetto (dei) Ferondi, Benedict of the Ferondos or Ferondo family, whilst, when he is denominated by the surname alone, it is used in the singular, il (the) being understood, e.g.
uz: Ismning ko'plik qismi, qat'iy nazar, italyanlar tomonidan erkakni uning to'liq ismi bilan aytishda doimo ishlatiladi, ular xristian va familiya o'rtasida Benedetto (dei) Ferondi, Ferondos oilasining Benedikt yoki Ferondo kabi tushuniladi, ammo u faqat familiya bilan atalganda, u birlikda ishlatiladi, tushuniladigan narsa, masalan.

uz: Ha, Xudo Oliylari meni O'z irodasiga ko'ra yengillashtirishi mumkin edi, Agar Unga ma'qul bo'lsa, Meni shunday adolatsiz va yomon qilgan odamdan; U mening rayhon qozonimni o'g'irlagan odamni do'zax azoblariga tashladi, u hali ham...

en: All dole its savour did from me away;  It was so redolent,  When, with the risen sun, at early day  To water it I went,  The folk would marvel all at it and say,  “Whence comes the sweetest scent?”  And I for love of it shall surely die.
uz: Hamma uning ta'mini mendan olib tashladi; U shunchalik achchiq edi, quyosh chiqishi bilan erta tongda uni sug'orishga borganimda, odamlar unga hayratlanib: "Eng shirin hid qayerdan keladi?" deyishardi. Va men uni sevganimdan albatta o'lardim.

uz: Ha, men uni sevganim uchun albatta o'laman, Sevgi, qayg'u va og'riq uchun.

en: A Pardon is a sort of minor jubilee of the Roman Catholic Church, held in honour of some local saint, at which certain indulgences and remissions of sins (hence the name) are granted to the faithful attending the services of the occasion.
uz: Kechirim Rim-katolik cherkovining kichik yubileyi bo'lib, u mahalliy aziz sharafiga o'tkaziladi, unda muayyan indulgensiyalar va gunohlarning kechirilishi (shundan kelib chiqib, nom) ushbu tadbir xizmatlarida qatnashayotgan sadoqatlilarga beriladi.

en: Gianni (Giovanni) di Procida was a Sicilian noble, to whose efforts in stirring up the island to revolt against Charles of Anjou was mainly due the popular rising known as the Sicilian Vespers (AD 1283) which expelled the French usurper from Sicily and transferred the crown to the house of Arragon.
uz: Gianni (Giovanni) di Procida Sitsiliyalik zodagon edi, uning orolni Charlz Anjouga qarshi isyon ko'tarishga undashga urinishlari asosan Sitsiliyalik Vesperlar deb nomlanuvchi mashhur qo'zg'olon (AD 1283) tufayli bo'lgan, bu esa fransuz usurperini Sitsiliyadan haydab chiqargan va tojni Arragon xonasiga o'tkazgan.

en: CHAPTER 1 JONATHAN HARKER'S JOURNAL 3 May.
uz: 1 bob Jonathan Harkerning 3 may kuni jurnalida.

en: —Left Munich at 8:35 P.
uz: Munixni 8:35 da qoldiring.

en: M, on 1st May, arriving at Vienna early next morning; should have arrived at 6:46, but train was an hour late.
uz: M, 1-may kuni, ertasi kuni ertalab Vyanada yetib boradi; soat 6:46 da etib borishi kerak edi, lekin poezd bir soat kechikdi.

en: Buda-Pesth seems a wonderful place, from the glimpse which I got of it from the train and the little I could walk through the streets.
uz: Buda-Pest ajoyib joyga o'xshaydi, chunki men uni poezdda ko'rdim va ko'chalarda yurganim uchun ko'p bo'lmagan.

en: I feared to go very far from the station, as we had arrived late and would start as near the correct time as possible.
uz: Men stantsiyadan juda uzoqqa ketishdan qo'rqardim, chunki biz kech kelib, iloji boricha to'g'ri vaqtga yaqinroq boshlagan edik.

en: The impression I had was that we were leaving the West and entering the East; the most western of splendid bridges over the Danube, which is here of noble width and depth, took us among the traditions of Turkish rule.
uz: Mening fikrimcha, biz G'arbdan chiqib, Sharqqa qadam qo'yyapmiz; Dunyo bo'ylab ajoyib ko'priklarning eng g'arbiy qismi, bu yerda kenglik va chuqurlik bor, bizni turk hukmronligi an'analari orasida olib bordi.

en: We left in pretty good time, and came after nightfall to Klausenburgh.
uz: Biz juda yaxshi vaqtda jo'nab, kechqurun Klausenburgga keldik.

en: Here I stopped for the night at the Hotel Royale.
uz: Bu yerda men Hotel Royaleda kecha turdim.

en: I had for dinner, or rather supper, a chicken done up some way with red pepper, which was very good but thirsty.
uz: Men kechki ovqatda, yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri, kechki ovqatda qizil chigit bilan tayyorlangan tovuqni yezdim, u juda yaxshi edi, ammo chanqagan edi.

en: get recipe for Mina.) I asked the waiter, and he said it was called paprika hendl, and that, as it was a national dish, I should be able to get it anywhere along the Carpathians.
uz: Men xizmatkordan so'radim va u paprika hendl deb ataladi va bu milliy taom bo'lgani uchun, uni Karpatlar bo'ylab qayerda bo'lmasin olishim kerakligini aytdi.

en: I found my smattering of German very useful here, indeed, I don't know how I should be able to get on without it.
uz: Germaniya tilini o'rganishim bu yerda juda foydali deb o'yladim, aslida, uningsiz qanday yashay olishim mumkinligini bilmayman.

en: Having had some time at my disposal when in London, I had visited the British Museum, and made search among the books and maps in the library regarding Transylvania; it had struck me that some foreknowledge of the country could hardly fail to have some importance in dealing with a noble- man of that country.
uz: Londonda vaqtim bo'lganidan so'ng, Men Britaniya muzeyiga borib, Transilvaniyaga oid kutubxonadagi kitoblar va xaritalarni qidirib topdim; o'sha mamlakatni oldindan bilganlarning bir qismi o'sha mamlakatning aziz kishilari bilan munosabatda bo'lishda muhim ahamiyatga ega bo'lishi mumkinligini tushunib yetdim.

en: I ﬁnd that the district he named is in the extreme east of the country, just on the borders of three states, Transylvania, Moldavia, and Bukovina, in the midst of the Carpathian mountains; one of the wildest and least known por- tions of Europe.
uz: Men uning nomlagan tumanining mamlakatning chekka sharqidagi, uchta davlat - Transilvaniya, Moldaviya va Bukovina chegarasida, Karpat tog'lari o'rtasida joylashganligini bilaman; Evropaning eng yovvoyi va kamdan-kam ma'lum qismlaridan biri.

en: I was not able to light on any map or work giving the exact locality of the Castle Dracula, as there are no maps of this country as yet to compare with our own Ordance Survey Maps; but I found that Bistritz, the post town named by Count Dracula, is a fairly well-known place.
uz: Men hech qanday xarita yoki ishda Dracula qalʼasining aniq joylashuvini aniqlab berishga muvaffaq boʻlmadim, chunki hozircha bu mamlakatning Ordance Survey Maps bilan taqqoslash uchun hech qanday xaritalari yoʻq; lekin Count Dracula tomonidan nomlangan pochta shahri Bistritz juda mashhur joy ekanligini aniqladim.

en: I shall enter here some of my notes, as they may refresh my memory when I talk over my travels with Mina.
uz: Men bu yerda ba'zi yozuvlarimni kiritaman, chunki men Mina bilan sayohatlarim haqida gapirganimda, ular xotiraimni yangilaydi.

en: In the population of Transylvania there are four distinct nationalities: Saxons in the South, and mixed with them the Wallachs, who are the de- scendants of the Dacians; Magyars in the West, and Szekelys in the East and North.
uz: Transilvaniya aholisida to'rtta millat mavjud: Janubiy qismida saksonlar va ular bilan aralashilgan valaklar, ular daqslarning avlodlari; G'arbiy qismida majarlar va Sharq va Shimoliy qismida sekellar.

en: I am going among the latter, who claim to be descended from Attila and the Huns.
uz: Men o'zimni Attila va hunlardan kelib chiqqan deb e'tirof qiladigan oxirgilarning birida qoldim.

en: This may be so, for when the Magyars conquered the country in the eleventh century they found the Huns settled in it.
uz: Bu shunday bo'lishi mumkin, chunki XI asrda majarlar mamlakatni egallab olganda, ular bu yerda hunlar o'rnashganini topdilar.

en: I read that every known superstition in the world is gathered into the horseshoe of the Carpathians, as if it were the centre of some sort of imagi- native whirlpool; if so my stay may be very interesting.
uz: Dunyodagi barcha ma'lum bo'lgan sehr-jodular Karpatlar jangida to'planganini o'qigan edim, xuddi bu yer bir xil tasavvurga asoslangan burilishning markazi bo'lgani kabi; agar shunday bo'lsa, mening turishim juda qiziqarli bo'lishi mumkin.

en: (Mem., I must ask the Count all about them.) I did not sleep well, though my bed was comfortable enough, for I had all sorts of queer dreams.
uz: Men yaxshi uxlamaganman, garchi yotoqim yetarlicha qulay bo'lsa-da, chunki men turli xil g'ayritabiiy orzular ko'rdim.

en: There was a dog howling all night under my window, which may have had something to do with it; or it may have been the papri- ka, for I had to drink up all the water in my carafe, and was still thirsty.
uz: Oynazim ostida butun kecha bo'yi bir it qichqirdi, ehtimol bu bilan bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin; yoki bu papri-ka bo'lishi mumkin edi, chunki men karafdagi suvni ichib, hali ham chanqoq edim.

en: To- wards morning I slept and was wakened by the continuous knocking at my door, so I guess I must have been sleeping soundly then.
uz: Ertalab uyquga ketdim va eshikda to'liq taqillatish bilan uyg'onib qoldim, shuning uchun o'sha paytda yaxshi uxlagan bo'lardim.

en: I had for breakfast more paprika, and a sort of porridge of maize ﬂour which they said was mamaliga, and egg-plant stuffed with forcemeat, a very excellent dish, which they call impletata.
uz: Men kechki ovqatda ko'proq paprika va mamaliga deb atalgan moma unining bir turi va impletata deb atalgan juda yaxshi taom bo'lgan go'sht eti bilan to'ldirilgan tuxumli tuxumni yeb o'tirdim.

en: (Mem.,get recipe for this also.) I had to hurry breakfast, for the train started a little before eight, or rather it ought to have done so, for after rushing to the station at 7:30 I had to sit in the carriage for more than an hour before we began to move.
uz: (Mem.,shuning uchun retseptni ham oling.) Men kechki ovqatni tezlashtirishim kerak edi, chunki poezd soat sakkizdan biroz oldin boshladi, yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri, shunday bo'lishi kerak edi, chunki soat 7:30 da poydevorga borganimdan so'ng biz harakatlanishni boshlashdan oldin bir soatdan ko'proq vaqt aravaxonada o'tirishim kerak edi.

en: It seems to me that the further east you go the more unpunctual are the trains.
uz: Menga ko'rinishicha, qancha sharqqa borsa, shunchalik tezda poezdlar o'tadi.

en: What ought they to be in China?
uz: Ular Xitoyda qanday bo'lishi kerak?

en: All day long we seemed to dawdle through a country which was full of beauty of every kind.
uz: Biz kun bo'yi turli xil go'zalliklarga to'la mamlakatni ko'zdan kechirgan edik.

en: Sometimes we saw little towns or castles on the top of steep hills such as we see in old missals; sometimes we ran by rivers and streams which seemed from the wide stony margin on each side of them to be subject of great ﬂoods.
uz: Ba'zan biz eski misallarda ko'rganimiz kabi tepa tog'lar ustida kichik shaharchalar yoki qal'alarni ko'rdik; ba'zan biz daryolar va oqimlar bo'ylab yugurardik, ularning har bir tomonidagi keng toshli bo'lakdan katta to'lqinlarga duchor bo'lib ko'rinardi.

en: It takes a lot of water, and running strong, to sweep the outside edge of a river clear.
uz: Daryoning tashqi sohigini tozalash uchun ko'p suv va kuchli harakat kerak.

en: At every station there were groups of people, sometimes crowds, and in all sorts of attire.
uz: Har bir stantsiyada odamlar to'plami, ba'zan ko'pchilik va turli kiyim-kechaklar bor edi.

en: Some of them were just like the peasants at home or those I saw coming through France and Germany, with short jackets, and round hats, and home-made trousers; but others were very picturesque.
uz: Ularning ba'zilari uydagi qishloq xo'jaligiga yoki Fransiya va Germaniya orqali kelayotganlarini ko'rganimdek, qisqa kiyim, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri to'pka va uyda tayyorlangan paltarlar bilan; ammo ba'zilari juda chiroyli edi.

en: The women looked pretty, except when you got near them, but they were very clumsy about the waist.
uz: Ayollar juda chiroyli ko'rinardi, faqat ularga yaqinlashganingizda edi, lekin ular belga nisbatan juda qo'pol edi.

en: They had all full white sleeves of some kind or other, and most of them had big belts with a lot of strips of something ﬂut- tering from them like the dresses in a ballet, but of course there were petti- coats under them.
uz: Ularning barchasi o'zlarining to'liq oq qo'lqoplariga ega edilar va aksariyatlarining katta kamarlari bo'lib, ularning ustida baletdagi liboslarga o'xshaydigan ko'rinishlarning ko'pchiligi bo'lgan, lekin ularning ostida, albatta, chiroyli kiyimlar bor edi.

en: The strangest ﬁgures we saw were the Slovaks, who were more barbarian than the rest, with their big cow-boy hats, great baggy dirty-white trousers, white linen shirts, and enormous heavy leather belts, nearly a foot wide, all studded over with brass nails.
uz: Biz ko'rgan eng g'ayrioddiy shaxslar Slovaklar edi, ular boshqalarga qaraganda ko'proq barbarlar edilar, ularning katta kovboy to'pkalari, katta to'qimaq qora-oq kiyimlari, oq lino kiyimlari va deyarli bir fut keng bo'lgan ulkan og'ir charm kamarlari bor edilar, ularning barchasi mis to'g'irlari bilan to'ldirilgan edi.

en: They wore high boots, with their trousers tucked into them, and had long black hair and heavy black moustaches.
uz: Ular yuqori bo'laklar kiyib, choriqlarini o'z ichiga olgan, uzun qora sochlari va og'ir qora mustaklari bor edilar.

en: They are very picturesque, but do not look prepossessing.
uz: Ular juda chiroyli, lekin o'z-o'zidan ko'rinmas.

en: On the stage they would be set down at once as some old Oriental band of brigands.
uz: Sahnada ular birdan biron bir eski sharqiy qo'g'irchoqlar guruhi sifatida ko'tariladi.

en: They are, however, I am told, very harmless and rather wanting in natural self- assertion.
uz: Biroq, menga aytilishicha, ular juda zararsiz va tabiiy ravishda o'zini o'zi tasdiqlashga muhtoj.

en: It was on the dark side of twilight when we got to Bistritz, which is a very interesting old place.
uz: Biz Bistritzga yetib borganimizda, qorong'i kunning qorong'i tomonida edik, bu juda qiziqarli eski joy.

en: Being practically on the frontier—for the Borgo Pass leads from it into Bukovina—it has had a very stormy existence, and it certainly shows marks of it.
uz: Borgo o'tishining chegarasida bo'lish bu yerdan Bukovinaga olib boradi, bu juda bo'ronli mavjudotga ega bo'ldi va bu, albatta, uning izlarini ko'rsatadi.

en: Fifty years ago a series of great ﬁres took place, which made terrible havoc on ﬁve separate occasions.
uz: Ellik yil oldin bir qator katta yong'inlar sodir bo'ldi, ular besh marta dahshatli ziyon keltirdi.

en: At the very begin- ning of the seventeenth century it underwent a siege of three weeks and lost 13,000 people, the casualties of war proper being assisted by famine and disease.
uz: O'n yettinchi asrning boshlarida u uch haftalik qamalga duchor bo'lib, 13 ming kishini yo'qotgan edi, urushning qurbonliklari ochlik va kasalliklar bilan qo'llab-quvvatlangan edi.

en: Count Dracula had directed me to go to the Golden Krone Hotel, which I found, to my great delight, to be thoroughly old-fashioned, for of course I wanted to see all I could of the ways of the country.
uz: Count Dracula meni Golden Krone Hotelga borishga buyurgan edi, men uni katta mamnunlikka to'g'ri oldindan o'rnatgan holda ko'rdim, chunki men, albatta, mamlakatning yo'l-yo'riqlarini ko'rishni xohlardim.

en: I was evidently expected, for when I got near the door I faced a cheery- looking elderly woman in the usual peasant dress—white undergarment with a long double apron, front, and back, of coloured stuff ﬁtting almost too tight for modesty.
uz: Albatta, meni kutishardi, chunki eshikga yaqinlashganda, odatdagi qishloq kiyimiga ega bo'lgan, ko'pchilik ko'rinadigan oq ichki kiyim kiygan, ko'p bo'lgan ikki xil shkaf, old va orqa tomondan rangli narsalarni o'rnatgan, kamtarlik uchun deyarli juda qattiq bo'lgan bir keksa ayolga duch keldim.

en: When I came close she bowed and said, The Herr Englishman? Yes, I said, Jonathan Harker. She smiled, and gave some message to an elderly man in white shirt- sleeves, who had followed her to the door.
uz: Men yaqinlashganimda, u tiz cho'kib: Herr Englishman? - deb so'radi. Ha, - dedim men, Jonathan Harker. - U tabassum qildi va oq ko'ylak kiyimli keksa kishiga xabar berdi.

en: He went, but immediately returned with a letter: My friend.—Welcome to the Carpathians.
uz: U ketib ketdi, lekin darhol xat bilan qaytib keldi: Dostim.Karpatlarga xush kelibsiz.

en: I am anxiously expecting you.
uz: Men sizni tashvish bilan kutyapman.

en: At three tomorrow the diligence will start for Bukovina; a place on it is kept for you.
uz: Ertaga soat uchda Bukovina uchun harakatlanish boshlanadi; u erda siz uchun joy saqlanadi.

en: At the Borgo Pass my carriage will await you and will bring you to me.
uz: Borgo o'tishida mening vagonim sizni kutib, menga olib keladi.

en: I trust that your journey from London has been a happy one, and that you will enjoy your stay in my beautiful land.—Your friend, Dracula. 4 May—I found that my landlord had got a letter from the Count, direct- ing him to secure the best place on the coach for me; but on making in- quiries as to details he seemed somewhat reticent, and pretended that he could not understand my German.
uz: Londondan sayohatingiz baxtli bo'lganiga ishonaman va mening chiroyli yurtimda qolishingizdan zavqlanasiz.Do'stingiz Drakula. 4 MayMen uy egasining Countdan menga avtobusda eng yaxshi o'rinni ta'minlashga yo'l-yo'riq beradigan xat olganini tushundim; lekin tafsilotlarni so'rashda u biroz ehtiyotkor bo'lib, nemis tilimni tushunmayapman deb o'ylagani haqida o'yladim.

en: This could not be true, because up to then he had understood it perfectly; at least, he answered my questions exactly as if he did.
uz: Bu haqiqat bo'lishi mumkin emas, chunki o'sha paytgacha u buni mukammal darajada tushunardi; hech bo'lmaganda, savollarimga xuddi shunday javob bergan bo'lsa kerak.

en: He and his wife, the old lady who had received me, looked at each other in a frightened sort of way.
uz: U va xotini, meni qabul qilgan keksa ayol, qo'rqqancha bir-birlariga qarab turishdi.

en: He mumbled out that the money had been sent in a letter, and that was all he knew.
uz: U pulning xat orqali yuborilganini g'ayrat bilan aytdi va u faqat shularni bilardi.

en: When I asked him if he knew Count Dracula, and could tell me anything of his castle, both he and his wife crossed themselves, and, saying that they knew nothing at all, simply re- fused to speak further.
uz: Men undan Count Draculani tanib-bilishini so'raganimda, u va uning xotini o'z qal'asi haqida biron narsa aytib berishlari mumkinmi, deb so'raganimda, ular o'zlarini o'zlarini o'ylashdi va hech narsa bilmasliklarini aytib, shunchaki gapirishni rad etishdi.

en: It was so near the time of starting that I had no time to ask anyone else, for it was all very mysterious and not by any means comforting.
uz: O'sha payt boshlanish vaqti shunchalik yaqin ediki, boshqalardan so'rash uchun vaqtim bo'lmadi, chunki bu juda sirli va hech qanday tasalli bermaydigan voqea edi.

en: Just before I was leaving, the old lady came up to my room and said in a hysterical way: Must you go?
uz: Men ketishdan oldin, keksa ayol xonamga kelib, histerik tarzda: Siz ketishingiz kerakmi?

en: Young Herr, must you go? She was in such an excited state that she seemed to have lost her grip of what German she knew, and mixed it all up with some other language which I did not know at all.
uz: Yosh xonim, ketishingiz kerakmi? U shunchalik hayajonlangan ediki, nemis tilida bilgan narsalarini o'zidan mahrum qilib, men umuman bilmagan boshqa til bilan aralashtirib yubordi.

en: I was just able to follow her by asking many questions.
uz: Men faqat ko'p savollar berib, uning orqasidan ergashishga muvaffaq bo'ldim.

en: When I told her that I must go at once, and that I was engaged on important busi- ness, she asked again: Do you know what day it is? I answered that it was the fourth of May.
uz: Men unga darhol ketishim kerakligini va muhim ishlar bilan band ekanligimni aytganimda, u yana: Bu kunning qaysi kuni ekanligini bilasizmi? - deb so'radi.

en: She shook her head as she said again: Oh, yes!
uz: U yana boshini silkitib dedi: O, ha!

en: I know that, but do you know what day it is? On my saying that I did not understand, she went on: It is the eve of St.
uz: Men buni bilaman, lekin bugun qanday kun ekanligini bilasizmi? - deb so'raganimda, men tushunmaganimni aytganda, u davom etdi: Bu St. kunining arafasidir.

en: Do you not know that to-night, when the clock strikes midnight, all the evil things in the world will have full sway?
uz: Bugun kechasi soat yarim kecha urganda, dunyoning barcha yovuz narsalari to'liq hukmronlik qilishini bilmayapsizmi?

en: Do you know where you are going, and what you are going to? She was in such evident distress that I tried to comfort her, but without effect.
uz: Qayerga ketayotganingni va nimaga ketayotganingni bilasanmi? - deb so'raganida, u shunchalik og'ir ahvolda ediki, men uni tasalli berishga harakat qildim, lekin hech qanday natija bo'lmadi.

en: Finally, she went down on her knees and implored me not to go; at least to wait a day or two before starting.
uz: Nihoyat, u tiz cho'kib, ketmasligimni iltijo qildi; hech bo'lmaganda boshlashdan oldin bir yoki ikki kun kutishim kerak edi.

en: It was all very ridiculous but I did not feel comfortable.
uz: Hammasi juda g'alati edi, lekin men o'zimni qulay his qilmasdim.

en: However, there was business to be done, and I could allow nothing to interfere with it.
uz: Biroq, ish bo'lishi kerak edi va men hech narsaga xalaqit berishiga yo'l qo'ymayman.

en: I tried to raise her up, and said, as gravely as I could, that I thanked her, but my duty was imperative, and that I must go.
uz: Men uni ko'tarishga harakat qildim va imkon qadar jiddiy bo'lib, unga minnatdorchilik bildirdim, lekin mening vazifam juda muhim va ketishim kerakligini aytdim.

en: She then rose and dried her eyes, and taking a cruciﬁx from her neck of- fered it to me.
uz: So'ngra u o'rnidan turib ko'zlarini quritdi va bo'yniga xoch olib, menga berdi.

en: I did not know what to do, for, as an English Churchman, I have been taught to regard such things as in some measure idolatrous, and yet it seemed so ungracious to refuse an old lady meaning so well and in such a state of mind.
uz: Men nima qilishim kerakligini bilmasdim, chunki ingliz cherkovchisi sifatida men bunday narsalarni bir darajada butparast deb bilishni o'rgandim, ammo shunday yaxshi va aqliy holatda bo'lgan keksa ayoldan voz kechish juda yomon ko'rinardi.

en: She saw, I suppose, the doubt in my face, for she put the rosary round my neck and said, For your mother's sake, and went out of the room.
uz: O'ylaymanki, u ko'zimdagi shubhalarni ko'rdi, chunki ro'zaxni bo'yniga o'tarib, Omang uchun dedi va xonadan chiqib ketdi.

en: I am writing up this part of the diary whilst I am waiting for the coach, which is, of course, late; and the cruciﬁx is still round my neck.
uz: Men bu qismini yozib yuribman, chunki men trenerni kutyapman, bu, albatta, kech bo'ldi; va xoch hali ham bo'yniga o'xshaydi.

en: Whether it is the old lady's fear, or the many ghostly traditions of this place, or the cruciﬁx itself, I do not know, but I am not feeling nearly as easy in my mind as usual.
uz: Bu keksa ayolning qo'rquvi, bu joyning ko'plab hayajonli an'analari yoki xochning o'zi bo'ladimi, bilmayman, lekin o'zimni odatdagidek oson his qilmayapman.

en: If this book should ever reach Mina before I do, let it bring my good-bye.
uz: Agar bu kitob Minaga mendan ilgari yetib borsa, unda men bilan xayrlashsam bo'ladi.

en: Here comes the coach!
uz: Mana, cho'nqin keldi!

en: The Castle.—The gray of the morning has passed, and the sun is high over the distant horizon, which seems jagged, whether with trees or hills I know not, for it is so far off that big things and little are mixed.
uz: Qaroq.Sabahning qalinligi o'tib ketdi va quyosh uzoq ko'rinishda juda baland bo'lib, u daraxtlar yoki tog'lar bilan bog'liq bo'ladimi yoki yo'qmi, bilmayman, chunki u shunchalik uzoq bo'lib, katta va kichik narsalar aralashadi.

en: I am not sleepy, and, as I am not to be called till I awake, naturally I write till sleep comes.
uz: Men uxlamayman va uyg'onmagunimcha menga hech kim chaqirmaydi, shuning uchun uyqu kelmaguncha yozaman.

en: There are many odd things to put down, and, lest who reads them may fancy that I dined too well before I left Bistritz, let me put down my dinner exactly.
uz: O'qish uchun ko'plab g'alati narsalarni yozib qo'yish kerak va ularni o'qigan kishilar Bistritzni tark etishdan oldin men juda yaxshi ovqatlanishim haqida o'ylamasliklari uchun, men ovqatimni aniq yozib qo'yaman.

en: I dined on what they called robber steak—bits of bacon, onion, and beef, seasoned with red pepper, and strung on sticks, and roasted over the ﬁre, in simple style of the London cat's meat!
uz: Men o'g'rilar tomonidan qaroqchi biftek deb nomlangan ovqatni yeydim, bular maydon, soya va go'sht, qizil chigit bilan mo'l-ko'l qilib, o'g'illarga bog'lab, olov ustida qovurib, London mushuklarining go'shti kabi sodda uslubda tayyorlangan edi!

en: The wine was Golden Mediasch, which produces a queer sting on the tongue, which is, however, not disagreeable.
uz: Shahra Golden Mediasch edi, u tilda g'ayritabiiy bo'lib o'tadi, ammo bu yoqimsiz emas.

en: I had only a couple of glasses of this, and nothing else.
uz: Men faqat bir necha stakan shu narsa bor edi, va boshqa hech narsa.

en: When I got on the coach, the driver had not taken his seat, and I saw him talking to the landlady.
uz: Avtobusga kirganimda haydovchi o'rinni egallamagan edi va men uni uy egasi bilan suhbatlashayotganini ko'rdim.

en: They were evidently talking of me, for every now and then they looked at me, and some of the people who were sitting on the bench outside the door —came and listened, and then looked at me, most of them pityingly.
uz: Ular men haqimda gapirishgan, chunki vaqti-vaqti bilan menga qarab turardilar va eshikdan tashqari bankda o'tirgan ba'zi odamlar kelib tinglab, keyin menga qarab turardilar, aksariyati esa rahmdillik bilan.

en: I could hear a lot of words often repeated, queer words, for there were many nation- alities in the crowd, so I quietly got my polyglot dictionary from my bag and looked them out.
uz: Ko'p tillarda takrorlanadigan ko'pgina so'zlarni eshitardim, g'alati so'zlarni, chunki xaloyiqda ko'plab millatlar bor edi, shuning uchun men xotirjamlik bilan ko'p tilli lug'atimni sumkamdan olib, ularni ko'rdim.

en: I must say they were not cheering to me, for amongst them were Ordog—Satan, Pokol—hell, stregoica—witch, vrolok and vlkoslak—both mean the same thing, one being Slovak and the other Ser- vian for something that is either werewolf or vampire.
uz: Men aytishim kerakki, ular menga quvonch qoʻyishmagan, chunki ularning orasida OrdogSatan, Pokolhel, stregoicawitch, vrolok va vlkoslak har ikkalasi ham bir xil maʼnoga ega edilar, biri slovak, ikkinchisi esa serbian boʻlib, biri bo'lib oʻrtoq yoki vampir boʻlgan narsani anglatadi.

en: (Mem.,I must ask the Count about these superstitions.) When we started, the crowd round the inn door, which had by this time swelled to a considerable size, all made the sign of the cross and pointed two ﬁngers towards me.
uz: (Mem.,Men bu sehr-jodular haqida Countdan so'rashim kerak) Biz boshlaganimizda, mehmonxona eshigini o'rab olgan xaloyiq, bu vaqtga kelib sezilarli darajada ko'paygan edi, barchasi xoch belgisini ko'tarib, menga ikkita barmoqni ko'rsatishdi.

en: With some difﬁculty, I got a fellow passenger to tell me what they meant.
uz: Biroz qiyinchilikka duch kelganimda, yo'lovchilar o'rtasidagi munosabatlar menga nimani anglatishini aytishga muvaffaq bo'ldim.

en: He would not answer at ﬁrst, but on learning that I was English, he ex- plained that it was a charm or guard against the evil eye.
uz: Boshida u javob bermadi, lekin men inglizligimni bilib olgach, bu sehr yoki yovuz ko'zdan himoya deb tushuntirdi.

en: This was not very pleasant for me, just starting for an unknown place to meet an unknown man.
uz: Bu men uchun juda yoqimli emas edi, chunki men bir nomukammal odam bilan uchrashish uchun nomukammal joyga borishni boshlagan edim.

en: But everyone seemed so kind-hearted, and so sor- rowful, and so sympathetic that I could not but be touched.
uz: Lekin hamma shunchalik mehribon, g'alati va mehribon bo'lib ko'rinardiki, menga ko'nglim tushdi.

en: I shall never forget the last glimpse which I had of the inn yard and its crowd of picturesque ﬁgures, all crossing themselves, as they stood round the wide archway, with its background of rich foliage of oleander and or- ange trees in green tubs clustered in the centre of the yard.
uz: Oʻzimga kelgan oxirgi koʻrinishimni hech qachon unutmayman, u yerdagi mehmonxona hovli va uning koʻpgina ramziy suratlar bilan oʻzaro oʻzaro bogʻlangan boʻlib, keng archa atrofida oʻtirgan edilar.

en: Then our driver, whose wide linen drawers covered the whole front of the boxseat,—gotza they call them—cracked his big whip over his four small horses, which ran abreast, and we set off on our journey.
uz: Keyin shoferimiz, keng kiyimli qutilar esa quti o'rindiqining butun old tomonini qoplagan edi, ular gotza deb atab, katta qamchini to'rtta kichkina otining ustiga urdi va biz sayohatni boshladik.

en: I soon lost sight and recollection of ghostly fears in the beauty of the scene as we drove along, although had I known the language, or rather lan- guages, which my fellow-passengers were speaking, I might not have been able to throw them off so easily.
uz: Tez orada men ko'zimni yo'qotdim va ko'rinishning go'zalligidan hayajonli qo'rquvlarni eslay olmay qoldim, garchi men samolyotchilar gapirayotgan tilni, yoki to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yo'lovchilarni bilganimda ham, ularni shunchalik osonlikcha tashlab yuborolmasdim.

en: Before us lay a green sloping land full of forests and woods, with here and there steep hills, crowned with clumps of trees or with farmhouses, the blank gable end to the road.
uz: Biz oldimizda o'rmon va o'rmonlarga to'la yashil bo'sh joy, bu erda va u erda tepa tepa tog'lar, daraxtlar to'plamlari yoki fermalar bilan to'nilgan, yo'lning so'ngida bo'sh bo'lgan bo'sh joy bor edi.

en: There was every- where a bewildering mass of fruit blossom—apple, plum, pear, cherry.
uz: Har bir joyda mevalar gullab-yashnashi, plum, pir, cherryning g'alati ko'pligi bor edi.

en: And as we drove by I could see the green grass under the trees spangled with the fallen petals.
uz: O'sha yo'ldan o'tib ketayotganimizda, daraxtlar ostidan yog'ilgan yashil o'tlarni ko'rdim.

en: In and out amongst these green hills of what they call here the Mittel Land ran the road, losing itself as it swept round the grassy curve,
uz: Bu yerda Mittel Land deb ataladigan yashil tog'lar orasida yo'l yurib, o'zini yo'qotib, o'z-o'zini o'zi yo'qotib, o'z yo'llarini o'tkazib, o'z yo'llarini yo'qotib qo'ydi.

en: or was shut out by the straggling ends of pine woods, which here and there ran down the hillsides like tongues of ﬂame.
uz: yoki tog'lar yonayotgan olov tillari kabi tog'lar bo'ylab to'xtab o'tib ketayotgan bor-yo'g'i bo'g'oqlarning to'xtalgan shoxlari tomonidan yopilgan edi.

en: The road was rugged, but still we seemed to ﬂy over it with a feverish haste.
uz: Yo'l toshqin edi, ammo biz unga o'tib o'tib ketayotganimizni ko'rdik.

en: I could not understand then what the haste meant, but the driver was evidently bent on losing no time in reaching Borgo Prund.
uz: O'shanda shoshilinchlikning nima ekanligini tushunolmadim, lekin haydovchi Borgo Prundga yetib borish uchun hech qanday vaqtni yo'qotmaslikka qat'iy qaror qilgan.

en: I was told that this road is in summertime excellent, but that it had not yet been put in order after the winter snows.
uz: Bu yo'l yozda juda yaxshi, lekin qishki qarlar bo'lganidan keyin hali to'g'rilashmaganligi haqida xabar topdim.

en: In this re- spect it is different from the general run of roads in the Carpathians, for it is an old tradition that they are not to be kept in too good order.
uz: Bu nuqtai nazar bilan u Karpatlar yo'llarining umumiy harakatidan farq qiladi, chunki ular juda yaxshi holatda saqlanmasligi qadimgi an'ana.

en: Of old the Hospadars would not repair them, lest the Turk should think that they were preparing to bring in foreign troops, and so hasten the war which was al- ways really at loading point.
uz: Qadimda Hospadarlar ularni tuzatmas edilar, chunki turklar chet el qo'shinlarini olib kelishga tayyorgarlik ko'rishlarini o'ylashi mumkin edi va urushni tezlashtirishi mumkin edi.

en: Beyond the green swelling hills of the Mittel Land rose mighty slopes of forest up to the lofty steeps of the Carpathians themselves.
uz: O'rta mamlakatning yashil, ko'tarilgan tepaliklaridan tashqari, o'rmonlarning qudratli tepaliklari Karpatlarning o'zlarining baland tepaliklarigacha ko'tarildi.

en: Right and left of us they towered, with the afternoon sun falling full upon them and bringing out all the glorious colours of this beautiful range, deep blue and purple in the shadows of the peaks, green and brown where grass and rock mingled, and an endless perspective of jagged rock and pointed crags, till these were themselves lost in the distance, where the snowy peaks rose grandly.
uz: Bizdan o'ng va chap tomonlari baland ko'tarilib, kechqurun quyosh ularning ustiga to'lib-to'lib tushdi va bu go'zal rangning barcha ulug'vor ranglarini ko'rsatdi, cho'qqizlar soyasida chuqur ko'k va bo'yoq, daraxtlar va toshlar aralashadigan yashil va qora rangli joylar va chiroyli toshlar va keskin toshlarning cheksiz ko'rinishi, ular o'zlarini uzoqlikda yo'qotib, qarli cho'qqizlar ulkan darajada ko'tarilgan joylarga olib keldi.

en: Here and there seemed mighty rifts in the mountains, through which, as the sun began to sink, we saw now and again the white gleam of falling water.
uz: Bu yerda tog'larda katta bo'g'riqlar paydo bo'lib, quyosh botishni boshlaganida, biz bir necha marta oq suvning oq shishishini ko'rardik.

en: One of my companions touched my arm as we swept round the base of a hill and opened up the lofty, snow-covered peak of a mountain, which seemed, as we wound on our serpentine way, to be right before us.
uz: Yolg'izlarimdan biri mening qo'limga qo'l tegizdi va biz tog'ning baland, qor bilan qoplangan tepalig'ini ochdik, biz o'z yirik yo'limizda yurganimizda, xuddi oldimizda bo'lganidek ko'rinardi.

en: Isten szek!—God's seat!—and he crossed himself reverently.
uz: Xudo ko'p!Xudo o'rinbosari! va u o'zini hurmat ila ko'tardi.

en: As we wound on our endless way, and the sun sank lower and lower be- hind us, the shadows of the evening began to creep round us.
uz: Biz cheksiz yo'limizda yurganimizda va quyosh ortimizdan ko'proq pastga tushayotganda, kechqurun soyalari atrofimizga kirib keldi.

en: This was em- phasized by the fact that the snowy mountain-top still held the sunset, and seemed to glow out with a delicate cool pink.
uz: Bu esa qarli tog'ning tomida hali ham quyosh botishi turganligi va o'sha paytda o'sha qizil ro'za qizil rang bilan parvarish qilayotganligi tufayli oshkor bo'ldi.

en: Here and there we passed Cszeks and slovaks, all in picturesque attire, but I noticed that goitre was painfully prevalent.
uz: Bu erda va u erda biz tseks va slovaklardan o'tib ketdik, barchasi chiroyli kiyimda edilar, lekin men goitre og'riqli darajada keng tarqalganini payqadim.

en: By the roadside were many crosses, and as we swept by, my companions all crossed themselves.
uz: Yo'l yonida ko'plab xochlar bor edi va biz o'sha yo'ldan o'tib ketayotganimizda, hammamiz o'zimizni o'sha yo'ldan o'tkazgan edik.

en: Here and there was a peasant man or woman kneeling before a shrine, who did not even turn round as we approached, but seemed in the self-surrender of devotion to have neither eyes nor ears for the outer world.
uz: Bu yerda va u erda bir qishloq erkak yoki ayol ma'bad oldida tiz cho'kkan edi, u biz yaqinlashayotganda hatto o'girilib ham o'tirmagan edi, balki o'z-o'zini bag'ishlash bilan tashqi dunyoga ko'zlari ham, quloqlari ham bo'lmaganidek ko'rinardi.

en: There were many things new to me.
uz: Men uchun ko'plab yangiliklar bor edi.

en: For instance, hay-ricks in the trees, and here and there very beautiful masses of weeping birch, their white stems shining like silver through the delicate green of the leaves.
uz: Misol uchun, daraxtlarda cho'qqizlar, shu va shu yerda juda chiroyli yig'lovchi birchlar to'plami bor, ularning oq bo'g'lari varaqlarning nozik yashil rangidan kumush kabi porlaydi.

en: Now and again we passed a leiter-wagon—the ordinary peasants's cart— with its long, snakelike vertebra, calculated to suit the inequalities of the road.
uz: Vaqti-vaqti bilan yo'lning tengsizligiga mos keladigan uzun, ilonga o'xshaydigan cho'g'irlari bo'lgan oddiy qishloq xo'jaligi aravachasidan o'tardik.

en: On this were sure to be seated quite a group of homecoming peasants, the Cszeks with their white, and the Slovaks with their coloured sheepskins, the latter carrying lance-fashion their long staves, with axe at end.
uz: Bu yerda uyga qaytish paytida ko'plab qishloq xo'jalari o'tirgan, shubhasiz, chekslar oq va Slovaklar esa rangli qo'y terisi bilan, oxirgilar esa o'zlarining uzun tayoqlarini o'zlari bilan olib, so'nggilarida to'g'ri bilan o'tirgan.

en: As the evening fell it began to get very cold, and the growing twilight seemed to merge into one dark mistiness the gloom of the trees, oak, beech, and pine, though in the valleys which ran deep between the spurs of the hills, as we ascended through the Pass, the dark ﬁrs stood out here and there against the background of latelying snow.
uz: Kechqurun juda sovuq bo'ldi va o'sib borayotgan tong bir qorong'i bulutga aylanardi: daraxtlar, o'rmonlar, buklar va bo'yoqlarning qorong'iligi, ammo tog'larning cho'qqisi o'rtasida chuqur bo'lgan vodiylar ichida, biz o'tish yo'lidan chiqib ketayotganda, qorong'i cho'g'lar oxirgi paytlarda qorning fonida bir-biridan ko'tarilib turardi.

en: Sometimes, as the road was cut through the pine woods that seemed in the darkness to be closing down upon us, great masses of greyness which here and there bestrewed the trees, produced a peculiarly weird and solemn effect, which carried on the thoughts and grim fancies engendered earlier in the evening, when the falling sunset threw into strange relief the ghost-like clouds which amongst the Carpathians seem to wind ceaselessly through the valleys.
uz: Ba'zan, qorong'ilikda bizga yaqinlashayotgan ko'rinadigan bo'ron o'rmonlari orqali yo'l kesilganida, daraxtlarni o'rab olgan katta o'rmonlar o'ziga xos g'alati va tantanali ta'sir ko'rsatdi, bu esa kechqurun tushayotgan quyosh botishi bilan karpatlar orasidagi g'ayritabiiy bulutlarni g'ayritabiiy ta'sirga solgan va vodiylar orqali to'xtamasdan shamol sochib o'tgan.

en: Sometimes the hills were so steep that, despite our driver's haste, the horses could only go slowly.
uz: Ba'zan tog'lar shunchalik baland bo'lganki, haydovchining shoshilinchligiga qaramay, otlar faqat sekin-sakin yurishardi.

en: I wished to get down and walk up them, as we do at home, but the driver would not hear of it.
uz: Men uyda qilganimizdek, pastga tushib, ularni ko'tarishni xohlardim, lekin haydovchi buni eshitmasdi.

en: You must not walk here.
uz: Bu yerda yurish mumkin emas.

en: The dogs are too ﬁerce. And then he added, with what he evidently meant for grim pleas- antry—for he looked round to catch the approving smile of the rest—And you may have enough of such matters before you go to sleep. The only stop he would make was a moment's pause to light his lamps.
uz: Itlar juda shafqatsiz. Keyin u o'z navbatida, o'z navbatida, o'ziga xos so'zlar bilan qo'shib qo'ydi: Qolganlarning rozilik bilan tabassumini ko'rish uchun atrofini ko'rdim, - dedi. Ushbu kabi narsalar uyquga ketishdan oldin yetarli bo'lishi mumkin. Uning yagona to'xtasi - lampalarini yoqish uchun bir daqiqalik to'xtab turish edi.

en: When it grew dark there seemed to be some excitement amongst the pas- sengers, and they kept speaking to him, one after the other, as though urging him to further speed.
uz: Kechqurun yo'lovchilar orasida biroz hayajon paydo bo'ldi va ular bir-biridan so'ng, xuddi uni tezroq harakatlanishga rag'batlantirish kabi, unga gapirishni davom ettirishdi.

en: He lashed the horses unmercifully with his long whip, and with wild cries of encouragement urged them on to further exertions.
uz: O'zining uzun qamchilagi bilan otlarni shafqatsiz ravishda urib, qo'pol iltijolar bilan ularni yanada ko'proq harakat qilishga rag'batlantirdi.

en: Then through the darkness I could see a sort of patch of grey light ahead of us, as though there were a cleft in the hills.
uz: Keyin qorong'ilik orasidan biz oldimizda bo'lgan o'g'ir yorug'lik parchalarini ko'rdim, xuddi tog'larda bo'g'rilik bo'lganidek.

en: The excitement of the passen- gers grew greater.
uz: O'yinchilarning hayajonlari yanada oshdi.

en: The crazy coach rocked on its great leather springs, and swayed like a boat tossed on a stormy sea.
uz: G'alati cho'pon o'zining ulkan charmli buloqlari ustida sarosimaga tushdi va bo'ronli dengizga tashlangan qayiq kabi o'zidan-o'zidan burib ketdi.

en: The road grew more level, and we appeared to ﬂy along.
uz: Yo'l ko'proq tekislanib, biz o'sha yo'lda uchib ketayotganimizni ko'rdik.

en: Then the mountains seemed to come nearer to us on each side and to frown down upon us.
uz: Keyin tog'lar har ikki tomondan bizga yaqinlashib, bizdan ko'z o'rab, ko'z o'ngimizga ko'rinardi.

en: We were enter- ing on the Borgo Pass.
uz: Biz Borgo yo'lboshchisida kirib ketayotgan edik.

en: One by one several of the passengers offered me gifts, which they pressed upon me with an earnestness which would take no denial.
uz: Yo'lovchilar bir-biridan menga sovg'alar taklif qildilar va ular meni tanqid qilmaydigan g'ayrat bilan tortishdi.

en: These were certainly of an odd and varied kind, but each was given in simple good faith, with a kindly word, and a blessing, and that same
uz: Bular, albatta, o'zgacha va turli xil edi, lekin har biri oddiy yaxshi ishtiyoq bilan, yaxshi so'z bilan, baraka bilan va shunga o'xshab berilgan edi

en: strange mixture of fear-meaning movements which I had seen outside the hotel at Bistritz— the sign of the cross and the guard against the evil eye.
uz: Bistritzdagi mehmonxonadan tashqarida ko'rgan qo'rquv harakatlarining g'ayrioddiy aralashuvi - xoch belgisi va yovuz ko'zga qarshi qo'riqchi.

en: Then, as we ﬂew along, the driver leaned forward, and on each side the pas- sengers, craning over the edge of the coach, peered eagerly into the dark- ness.
uz: Keyin, biz uchib borayotganimizda haydovchi oldinga yopishibdi va har bir tomondan yo'lovchilar avtobusning bo'yiga ko'tarilib, qorong'ilikka e'tiborini qaratishdi.

en: It was evident that something very exciting was either happening or expected, but though I asked each passenger, no one would give me the slightest explanation.
uz: Ko'rinib turibdiki, juda hayajonli narsa sodir bo'layotgan yoki kutilayotgan edi, lekin har bir yo'lovchidan so'rasam ham, hech kim menga hech qanday tushuntirish bermasdi.

en: This state of excitement kept on for some little time.
uz: Bu hayajonli holat biroz vaqt davom etdi.

en: And at last we saw before us the Pass opening out on the eastern side.
uz: Va nihoyat, biz oldimizda sharqiy tomondan ochiladigan o'tishni ko'rdik.

en: There were dark, rolling clouds overhead, and in the air the heavy, oppressive sense of thunder.
uz: Yuz ustida qorong'i, g'ayratli bulutlar bor edi va havoda g'ildirakning og'ir, zulmatli hissi bor edi.

en: It seemed as though the mountain range had separated two atmospheres, and that now we had got into the thunderous one.
uz: Koʻrinardi, togʻlar ikki atmosferaga ajralib ketgan boʻlib, endi biz gʻalati atmosferaga kirganmiz.

en: I was now myself looking out for the conveyance which was to take me to the Count.
uz: Endi men o'zim meni Countning oldiga olib ketadigan transport vositalarini qidirib topardim.

en: Each moment I expected to see the glare of lamps through the blackness, but all was dark.
uz: Har bir daqiqada qorong'ilik orqali chiroqlarning yorqinligini ko'rishni kutardim, lekin hamma narsa qorong'i edi.

en: The only light was the ﬂickering rays of our own lamps, in which the steam from our hard-driven horses rose in a white cloud.
uz: Yagona nur bizning o'z lampalarimizning parcha-parcha nurlari edi, ular bilan bizning qattiq otlarimizning bug'i oq bulutda ko'tarildi.

en: We could see now the sandy road lying white before us, but there was on it no sign of a vehicle.
uz: Endi biz oldimizda oq bo'lgan qumli yo'lni ko'rishimiz mumkin edi, lekin u erda transport vositasining izlari yo'q edi.

en: The passengers drew back with a sigh of gladness, which seemed to mock my own disappointment.
uz: Yo'lovchilar quvonchli his-tuyg'u bilan orqaga qaytishdi, bu esa mening o'zimning tushkunligimni masxara qilganday tuyuldi.

en: I was already thinking what I had best do, when the driver, looking at his watch, said to the others something which I could hardly hear, it was spoken so quietly and in so low a tone, I thought it was An hour less than the time. Then turning to me, he spoke in German worse than my own.
uz: Men allaqachon nima qilishim kerakligini o'ylayotgan edim, haydovchi o'z soatini ko'rib, boshqalarga eshitolmaydigan narsani aytganda, u shunchalik sekin va past tovush bilan gapirildiki, vaqtdan bir soat kamroq deb o'yladim. Keyin menga qarab, u nemis tilida o'zimnikiga qaraganda og'irroq gapirgan.

en: There is no carriage here.
uz: Bu yerda hech qanday vagon yo'q.

en: The Herr is not expected after all.
uz: Xullas, Hrni kutib bo'lmaydi.

en: He will now come on to Bukovina, and return tomorrow or the next day, better the next day. Whilst he was speaking the horses began to neigh and snort and plunge wildly, so that the driver had to hold them up.
uz: Endi u Bukovinaga boradi va erta yoki ertasi kuni qaytib keladi, ertasi kun yaxshiroqdir. U gapirgan paytda otlar qichqirib, qichqirib, vahshiy bo'lib o'tishga boshladilar, shuning uchun haydovchi ularni ushlab turishi kerak edi.

en: Then, amongst a cho- rus of screams from the peasants and a universal crossing of themselves, a caleche, with four horses, drove up behind us, overtook us, and drew up be- side the coach.
uz: Keyin, fermerlarning qichqiriqlari va o'zlarining umumiy o'tishida, to'rtta otli cho'cha orqamizdan kelib, bizni orqaga surib, vagonning yonidan chiqdi.

en: I could see from the ﬂash of our lamps as the rays fell on them, that the horses were coal-black and splendid animals.
uz: Chiziqlar ularning ustiga tushganda, chiroqlarimizning shovqinidan atlarning ko'mir qora va chiroyli hayvonlar ekanligini ko'rardim.

en: They were dri- ven by a tall man, with a long brown beard and a great black hat, which seemed to hide his face from us.
uz: Ular uzun qalin sakkizi va katta qora to'pka bilan baland bir odam tomonidan boshqarilgan edi, bu esa bizdan yuzini yashirgan ko'rinardi.

en: I could only see the gleam of a pair of very bright eyes, which seemed red in the lamplight, as he turned to us.
uz: U bizga qarab turganda, men faqat chiroq yorug'ligida qizil ko'rinadigan juda yorqin ko'zlar parlashini ko'rardim.

en: He said to the driver, You are early tonight, my friend. The man stammered in reply, The English Herr was in a hurry. To which the stranger replied, That is why, I suppose, you wished him to go on to Bukovina.
uz: U haydovchisiga: Bu kechasi erta kelding, do'stim! - dedi. - Ingliz xonadoni tezda bor edi, - deb javob berdi u kishi. - O'sha sababdan siz unga Bukovinaga borishni xohladingiz, deb o'ylayman.

en: You cannot deceive me, my friend.
uz: Siz meni aldashingiz mumkin emas, do'stim.

en: and my horses are swift. As he spoke he smiled, and the lamplight fell on a hardlooking mouth, with very red lips and sharp-looking teeth, as white as ivory.
uz: Atlarim tezkor. U gapirganida tabassum qildi va chiroq chiroqlari ko'rinmas og'ziga, juda qizil og'izlari va o'ta oq ko'rinadigan tishlari bilan, fil-dush kabi oq bo'lgan og'ziga tushdi.

en: One of my companions whispered to another the line from Burger's Lenore.
uz: Bir do'stim Burgerning Lenore kitobidagi so'zlarni bir-biriga shoshib berdi.

en: Denn die Todten reiten Schnell. (For the dead travel fast.) The strange driver evidently heard the words, for he looked up with a gleaming smile.
uz: Denn die Todten reiten Schnell. (O'liklar tez sayohat qilishadi.) O'zgacha haydovchi so'zlarni eshitgan bo'lishi mumkin, chunki u parcha-parcha tabassum bilan ko'taribdi.

en: The passenger turned his face away, at the same time putting out his two ﬁngers and crossing himself.
uz: Yo'lovchi yuz o'girib, bir vaqtning o'zida o'z barmoqlarini ko'tarib, o'zini o'zi kesib o'tdi.

en: Give me the Herr's lug- gage, said the driver, and with exceeding alacrity my bags were handed out and put in the caleche.
uz: Menga Herrning bagajlarini beringlar, - dedi haydovchi va juda ham g'ayratli bo'lib, sumkamni uzatishdi va ko'ylakka qo'yishdi.

en: Then I descended from the side of the coach, as the caleche was close alongside, the driver helping me with a hand which caught my arm in a grip of steel.
uz: So'ngra men cho'nqining yonidan tushdim, chunki cho'pka yonida edi, haydovchi menga qo'limni po'latdan tutgan qo'lim bilan yordam berardi.

en: His strength must have been prodigious.
uz: Uning kuch-qudrati ajoyib bo'lishi kerak edi.

en: Without a word he shook his reins, the horses turned, and we swept into the darkness of the pass.
uz: U bir so'z aytmay, o'z qo'rqinchlarini silkitdi, otlar aylandi va biz o'tish yo'li qorong'iligiga tushib ketdik.

en: As I looked back I saw the steam from the horses of the coach by the light of the lamps, and projected against it the ﬁgures of my late companions crossing themselves.
uz: Orqaga nazar solib, lampaning yoritishi bilan vagonning otlaridan bug'ni ko'rdim va uning ustiga o'zlarini kesib o'tayotgan marhum do'stlarimning suratlarini ko'rdim.

en: Then the driver cracked his whip and called to his horses, and off they swept on their way to Bukovina.
uz: Keyin haydovchi qamchini buzdi va otlarini chaqirdi va ular Bukovinaga borishdi.

en: As they sank into the darkness I felt a strange chill, and a lonely feeling come over me.
uz: Ular qorong'ilikka kirib ketayotganda, men o'zimni g'alati sovuq va yolg'izlik hissi bilan his qildim.

en: But a cloak was thrown over my shoulders, and a rug across my knees, and the driver said in excellent German— The night is chill, mein Herr, and my master the Count bade me take all care of you.
uz: Ammo yelkamdan choriq, dizlarimdan cho'pka tashlandi va haydovchi ajoyib nemis tilida: Tunlar sovuq, xonim, xo'jayinim Count meni sizga g'amxo'rlik qilishni buyurdi.

en: There is a ﬂask of slivovitz (the plum brandy of the country) underneath the seat, if you should require it. I did not take any, but it was a comfort to know it was there all the same.
uz: O'rindiq ostida slivovitz (mamlakatning plum brendi) shisha bor, agar kerak bo'lsa. Men hech birini qabul qilmadim, lekin u yerda hammasi borligini bilish tasalli baxsh etdi.
