uz: Men ham so'zlasha oladigan, maslahat so'ra oladigan hech kimim yo'q.

en: Of course, one does not look for an adviser in the street; but you are an exception.
uz: Albatta, ko'chalarda maslahatchi izlash mumkin emas; lekin siz bundan mustasno.

en: though we had been friends for twenty years.
uz: Garchi biz yigirma yildan beri do'st bo'lgan bo'lsak-da.

en: You won't deceive me, will you?
uz: Siz meni aldamaysiz, shundaymi?

en: the only thing is, I don't know how I am going to sur- vive the next twenty-four hours. Sleep soundly.
uz: Faqatgina birgina narsa shundaki, kelgusi yigirma to'rt soat davomida qanday yashay olaman, deb o'ylamayman.

en: Good-night, and remember that I have trusted you al- ready.
uz: Yaxshi kechalar, va men sizga ishonishimni unutmang.

en: But you exclaimed so nicely just now, 'Surely one can't be held re- sponsible for every feeling, even for brotherly sympathy!' Do you know, that was so nicely said, that the idea struck me at once, that I might conﬁde in you? For God's sake do; but about what?
uz: Ammo siz allaqachon shunday yaxshilik bilan: Hatto bir kishi har bir his-tuyg'u, hatto birodarlik hamdardligi uchun javobgar bo'lishi mumkin emas! - deb aytdingiz.

en: What is it? Wait till tomorrow.
uz: Nima? - Ertagacha kuting.

en: Meanwhile, let that be a secret.
uz: Shu bilan birga, bu sir bo'lsin.

en: So much the better for you; it will give it a faint ﬂavour of romance.
uz: Bu sizga shunchalik yaxshi bo'ladi, chunki bu unga romansning salqin lazzatini beradi.

en: Perhaps I will tell you to-morrow, and perhaps not.
uz: Ehtimol, ertaga sizga aytaman, ehtimol yo'q.

en: I will talk to you a little more beforehand; we will get to know each other better.
uz: Siz bilan oldindan biroz gaplashaman; biz bir-birimizni yaxshiroq bilib olamiz.

en: . Oh yes, I will tell you all about myself tomorrow!
uz: Ha, ertaga o'zim haqida hamma narsani aytib beraman!

en: But what has hap- pened?
uz: Ammo nima sodir bo'ldi?

en: It is as though a miracle had befallen me.
uz: O'zimni mo'ʼjizaviy tarzda o'ldirganimdek tuyuladi.

en: Come, tell me aren't you glad that you were not angry and did not drive me away at the ﬁrst moment, as any other woman would have done?
uz: Keling, menga ayting, boshqa har qanday ayol qilganidek, birinchi daqiqada g'azablanib, meni quvib chiqarmaganingizdan xursand emasmisiz?

en: In two minutes you have made me happy for ever.
uz: Ikki daqiqada siz meni abadiy baxtli qildingiz.

en: Yes, happy; who knows, per- haps, you have reconciled me with myself, solved my doubts!
uz: Ha, baxtli; kim biladi, ehtimol siz meni o'zim bilan yarashtirgansiz, shubhalarimni hal qilgansiz!

en: Perhaps such moments come upon me.
uz: Ehtimol, men o'sha paytlarga duch kelaman.

en: But there I will tell you all about it to- morrow, you shall know everything, everything.
uz: Ammo men sizga ertaga bu haqda hamma narsani aytib beraman, siz hamma narsani, hamma narsani bilasiz.

en: . Very well, I consent; you shall begin.
uz: To'g'ri, men rozi bo'laman; siz boshlashingiz kerak.

en: . Agreed. Good-bye till tomorrow! Till tomorrow! And we parted.
uz: - To'g'ri keldi. - Bugunga qadar, Bugunga qadar! - Bugunga qadar! - deb so'rashdi va biz ayrıldik.

en: I walked about all night; I could not make up my mind to go home.
uz: Men butun kecha aylanib yurdim; uyga qaytishga qaror qilolmadim.

en: SECOND NIGHT Well, so you have survived! she said, pressing both my hands.
uz: Ikkinchi kecha: Ha, shuning uchun siz omon qoldingiz! - dedi u, ikkala qo'limni ham bosdi.

en: I've been here for the last two hours; you don't know what a state I have been in all day. I know, I know.
uz: Men bu yerda ikki soat bo'lib o'tganman; kun bo'yi qanday holatda bo'lganimni bilmaysan.

en: Do you know why I have come?
uz: Nima uchun kelganimni bilasizmi?

en: Not to talk nonsense, as I did yesterday.
uz: Kecha qilganimdek, behuda gapirish uchun emas.

en: I tell you what, we must behave more sen- sibly in future.
uz: Sizga nima deyman, kelajakda biz yanada aqlli bo'lishimiz kerak.

en: I thought a great deal about it last night. In what way—in what must we be more sensible?
uz: Kecha bu haqda ko'p o'yladim. Qanday qilib biz qaysi jihatdan ko'proq aqlli bo'lishimiz kerak?

en: I am ready for my part; but, really, nothing more sensible has happened to me in my life than this, now. Really?
uz: Men o'z hissamni qo'shishga tayyorman; lekin, aslida, hayotimda bundan ko'ra oqilonaroq narsa sodir bo'lmagan.

en: In the ﬁrst place, I beg you not to squeeze my hands so; secondly, I must tell you that I spent a long time thinking about you and feeling doubtful today. And how did it end? How did it end?
uz: Birinchidan, qo'llarimni shunday siqmasligingizni iltijo qilaman; ikkinchidan, sizga aytishim kerakki, men siz haqingizda ko'p vaqt o'yladim va bugun shubha tuyg'ularini his qildim.

en: The upshot of it is that we must begin all over again, because the conclusion I reached today was that I don't know you at all; that I behaved like a baby last night, like a little girl; and, of course, the fact of it is, that it's my soft heart that is to blame—that is, I sang my own praises, as one always does in the end when one analyses one's conduct.
uz: Buning natijasi shundaki, biz hamma narsani yangidan boshlashimiz kerak, chunki bugun sizning fikringizga keldimki, men sizni umuman tanimayman; kecha go'dak kabi, kichkina qizcha kabi harakat qildim; va, albatta, buning asosi shundaki, aybdor bo'lgan o'z yumshak yuragimdirya'ni, men o'z maqtuvimni kuyladim, chunki odam har doim o'z xulq-atvorini tahlil qilganda oxirida shunday qiladi.

en: And therefore to correct my mistake, I've made up my mind to ﬁnd out all about you minutely.
uz: Shuning uchun xatoimni to'g'rilash uchun men siz haqingizda hamma narsani bir daqiqada bilib olishga qaror qildim.

en: But as I have no one from whom I can ﬁnd out anything, you must tell me everything fully yourself.
uz: Ammo men hech kimdan biror narsa bilishim mumkin bo'lmaganligi sababli, siz menga hamma narsani o'zingiz aytib berishingiz kerak.

en: Well, what sort of man are you?
uz: Xo'sh, siz qanday insonsiz?

en: Come, make haste—begin—tell me your whole history. My history! I cried in alarm.
uz: Kel, shoshil, butun tarixingizni menga aytib ber! - deb qo'rqitdim.

en: But who has told you I have a history?
uz: Ammo mening tarixim borligini sizga kim aytdi?

en: . Then how have you lived, if you have no history? she interrupted, laughing.
uz: - Agar tarixingiz yo'q bo'lsa, qanday yashang? - dedi u kulish bilan.

en: Absolutely without any history!
uz: Absolutda hech qanday tarixsiz!

en: I have lived, as they say, keeping my- self to myself, that is, utterly alone—alone, entirely alone.
uz: Ular aytishicha, men o'zimni o'zim uchun saqlab, ya'ni butunlay yolg'iz, butunlay yolg'iz yashadim.

en: Do you know what it means to be alone? But how alone?
uz: Yolg'iz qolish nimani anglatishini bilasizmi? - deb so'radi. - Lekin qanday qilib yolg'iz qolish mumkin?

en: Do you mean you never saw any one? Oh no, I see people, of course; but still I am alone. Why, do you never talk to any one?
uz: Siz hech kimni ko'rmadingizmi? - deb so'rashdi. - Yo'q, albatta, men odamlarni ko'raman, lekin hali ham yolg'izman. - Nima uchun hech kim bilan gaplashmaysan? - deb so'rashdi.

en: Strictly speaking, with no one. Who are you then?
uz: Qattiq gapirganda, hech kim bilan emas.

en: Stay, I guess: most likely, like me you have a grandmother.
uz: O'shanda qoling, deb o'ylayman: ehtimol siz ham men kabi buvim bor.

en: She is blind and will never let me go anywhere, so that I have almost forgotten how to talk; and when I played some pranks two years ago, and she saw there was no holding me in, she called me up and pinned my dress to hers, and ever since we sit like that for days togeth- er; she knits a stocking, though she's blind, and I sit beside her, sew or read aloud to her—it's such a queer habit, here for two years I've been pinned to her.
uz: U ko'r bo'lib, hech qachon meni hech narsaga qo'ymaydi, shuning uchun men gapirishni deyarli unutib qo'ydim; ikki yil oldin bir nechta mashq o'tkazganimda va meni hech qanday ushlab qolmasligini ko'rganida, u menga chaqirib, kiyimi o'zidan o'tkazdi va biz bir necha kun o'tirib o'tirganimizdan beri; u ko'r bo'lsa-da, shoshiq tikadi va men uning yonida o'tirib, o'tkirib o'qizib, o'qiganimni aytaman.

en: But no, I haven't a grandmother like that. Well, if you haven't why do you sit at home?
uz: Ammo yo'q, mening bunday buvim yo'q. Agar yo'q bo'lsa, nega uyda o'tiribsiz?

en: . Listen, do you want to know the sort of man I am? Yes, yes! In the strict sense of the word? In the very strictest sense of the word. Very well, I am a type! Type, type!
uz: Quloq solinglar, men qanday inson ekanimni bilmoqchimisiz? Ha, ha! Shuning qat'iy ma'nosida? Shuning eng qat'iy ma'nosida. Chindan ham yaxshi, men tipman! Tip, tip!

en: What sort of type? cried the girl, laughing, as though she had not had a chance of laughing for a whole year.
uz: Qaysi turdagi? - deb qichqirdi qiz, xuddi bir yil davomida kulish imkoniga ega bo'lmaganidek.

en: Yes, it's very amusing talking to you.
uz: Ha, siz bilan suhbatlashish juda qiziqarli.

en: Look, here's a seat, let us sit down.
uz: Qarang, bu yerda o'tirishga joy boradi, keling, o'tiramiz.

en: No one is passing here, no one will hear us, and—begin your history.
uz: Hech kim bu yerdan o'tmaydi, bizni hech kim eshitmaydi va o'zingizning tarixingizni boshlashingiz mumkin.

en: For it's no good your telling me, I know you have a history; only you are concealing it.
uz: Menga aytishning foydasi yo'q, chunki sizning tarixingiz borligini bilaman; faqat siz buni yashiryapsiz.

en: To begin with, what is a type? A type?
uz: Avvalo, tip nima? Tip nima?

en: A type is an original, it's an absurd person! I said, infected by her childish laughter.
uz: Tip - bu original, bu absurd odam! - dedim men, uning bolalik tabassumidan zarar ko'rgan holda.

en: Listen; do you know what is meant by a dreamer? A dreamer!
uz: Tinglang, siz tush ko'ruvchi nimani anglatishini bilasizmi?

en: Indeed I should think I do know.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bilishim kerak.

en: I am a dreamer myself.
uz: O'zim ham orzu qiluvchi odamman.

en: Sometimes, as I sit by grandmother, all sorts of things come into my head.
uz: Ba'zan, buvimning yonida o'tirganimda, boshimga turli xil narsalar keladi.

en: Why, when one begins dreaming one lets one's fancy run away with one— why, I marry a Chinese Prince!
uz: Axir, inson tushlarga tushib qolsa, o'z xayol-shafqatini bir kishi bilan qochib ketishiga yo'l qo'yadi-ku, men Xitoy shohi bilan turmushga chiqaman!

en: Though sometimes it is a good thing to dream!
uz: Garchi ba'zan orzu qilish yaxshi bo'lsa-da!

en: But, goodness knows!
uz: Ammo, Xudo biladi!

en: Especially when one has something to think of apart from dreams, added the girl, this time rather seriously.
uz: Ayniqsa, inson tushlaridan tashqari o'ylashi kerak bo'lgan narsalarga ega bo'lganda, - dedi qiz, bu safar esa jiddiy.

en: If you have been married to a Chinese Emperor, you will quite understand me.
uz: Agar siz Xitoy imperatori bilan turmush qurgan bo'lsangiz, meni tushunasiz.

en: But one minute, I don't know your name yet. At last!
uz: Ammo bir daqiqa, men sizning ismingizni hali bilmayman.

en: You have been in no hurry to think of it! Oh, my goodness!
uz: Siz bu haqda o'ylashga shoshilmadingiz! - deb aytdi. - Oh, Xudoyim!

en: It never entered my head, I felt quite happy as it was.
uz: O'zimni hech qachon o'ylayman deb o'ylamaganman, lekin o'zimni juda baxtli his qilardim.

en: . My name is Nastenka. Nastenka!
uz: - Mening ismim Nastenka. - Nastenka!

en: And nothing else? Nothing else!
uz: Va boshqa hech narsa? - O'zga hech narsa!

en: Why, is not that enough for you, you insatiable person? Not enough?
uz: Nima uchun, bu sen uchun yetarli emasmi, ey to'qmas odam?

en: On the contrary, it's a great deal, a very great deal, Nastenka; you kind girl, if you are Nastenka for me from the ﬁrst. Quite so!
uz: Aksincha, bu juda ko'p, juda ko'p narsa, Nastenka; siz yaxshi qiz, agar siz men uchun dastlabki Nastenka bo'lsangiz.

en: Well? Well, listen, Nastenka, now for this absurd history. I sat down beside her, assumed a pedantically serious attitude, and began as though reading from a manuscript:— There are, Nastenka, though you may not know it, strange nooks in Pe- tersburg.
uz: - Xo'sh, eshit, Nastenka, endi bu absurd tarixni ko'rib chiqamiz. - Men uning yonida o'tirib, o'ylanarli darajada jiddiy munosabatda bo'ldim va qo'lyozmalardan o'qishni boshladim: Pe- tersburgda g'alati joylar bor, Nastenka, siz buni bilmasangiz ham bo'ladi.

en: It seems as though the same sun as shines for all Petersburg people does not peep into those spots, but some other different new one, bespoken expressly for those nooks, and it throws a different light on everything.
uz: Ko'rinishicha, barcha Sankt-Peterburg aholisi uchun shashayotgan quyosh o'sha nuqtalarga nazar solmaydi, balki o'zgacha yangi bir quyosh, ushbu burchaklar uchun aniq so'zlangan va hamma narsaga boshqacha yorug'lik beradi.

en: In these corners, dear Nastenka, a quite different life is lived, quite unlike the life that is surging round us, but such as perhaps exists in some unknown realm, not among us in our serious, over-serious, time.
uz: Ushbu burchaklarda, aziz Nastenka, atrofimizda paydo bo'layotgan hayotdan umuman farq qiladi, ammo ehtimol, biz o'z vaqtida jiddiy, jiddiy bo'lmagan holda, noma'lum bir olamda mavjud bo'lishi mumkin.

en: Well, that life is a mixture of something purely fantastic, fervently ideal, with something (alas!
uz: Hayot - bu chindan ham ajoyib, g'ayratli, mukammal bir narsa bilan bir aralashma (hayot!)

en: Nastenka) dingily prosaic and ordinary, not to say incredibly vulgar. Foo!
uz: Nastenka) dahshatli prosaik va odat tusiga kirgan, g'ayritabiiy vulgarlikni aytmaslik uchun.

en: What do I hear? Listen, Nastenka.
uz: Men nima eshityapman? - Quloq sol, Nastenka.

en: (It seems to me I shall never be tired of calling you Nastenka.) Let me tell you that in these corners live strange people— dreamers.
uz: (Menga o'xshaydi, men sizni Nastenka deb atashdan hech qachon charchamayman) Sizga aytamanki, bu burchaklarda g'alati odamlar yashaydilar orzuchilar.

en: The dreamer—if you want an exact deﬁnition—is not a human being, but a creature of an intermediate sort.
uz: Agar aniq ta'rifni istasangiz, orzu qiluvchi inson emas, balki o'rtacha turdagi mavjudot.

en: For the most part he settles in some inaccessible corner, as though hiding from the light of day; once he slips into his corner, he grows to it like a snail, or, anyway, he is in that re- spect very much like that remarkable creature, which is an animal and a
uz: Aksariyat hollarda u kun yorug'ligidan yashiringanidek, biron bir tutashmas burchada o'rnashadi; bir marta uning burchasiga kirsa, u bu burchada bo'g'ayra kabi o'sadi, yoki har holda, u bu ko'rinishda o'sha ajoyib mavjudotga juda o'xshaydi, u hayvon va o'simlikdir.

en: house both at once, and is called a tortoise.
uz: Ikkala uyni ham bir vaqtning o'zida uylaydi va u qorin deb ataladi.

en: Why do you suppose he is so fond of his four walls, which are invariably painted green, grimy, dismal and reeking unpardonably of tobacco smoke?
uz: Nima uchun u o'zining to'rtta devorini shunchalik yaxshi ko'radi deb o'ylaysiz, ular har doim yashil, qorong'i, chiroyli bo'lib, tamaki tutunidan kechirilmas ravishda xushbo'y bo'ladi?

en: Why is it that when this ab- surd gentleman is visited by one of his few acquaintances (and he ends by getting rid of all his friends), why does this absurd person meet him with such embarrassment, changing countenance and overcome with confusion, as though he had only just committed some crime within its four walls; as though he had been forging counterfeit notes, or as though he were writing verses to be sent to a journal with an anonymous letter, in which he states that the real poet is dead, and that his friend thinks it his sacred duty to pub- lish his things?
uz: Nima uchun bu bejiz kishi, bu bejiz kishi uning bir necha tanisidan tashrif buyurganida (va u oxiriga qadar barcha do'stlarini yo'qotib qo'yganida), unga shunchalik o'z-o'zidan xafa bo'lib, yuz o'zgartirgan va g'alati holga tushib, xuddi u to'rt devor ichida jinoyat sodir etgan bo'lgandek, xuddi soxta yozuvlarni soxtalashtirgandek, yoki xuddi haqiqiy shoir o'lganini va do'sti o'zlarining narsalarni e'lon qilishini muqaddas deb hisoblagan nomsiz maktub bilan jurnalga yuborish uchun oyatlarni yozayotganini aytadi?

en: Why, tell me, Nastenka, why is it conversation is not easy between the two friends?
uz: Menga ayt, Nastenka, nima uchun bu ikki do'st o'rtasida suhbat oson emas?

en: Why is there no laughter?
uz: Nega kulgi yo'q?

en: Why does no lively word ﬂy from the tongue of the perplexed newcomer, who at other times may be very fond of laughter, lively words, conversation about the fair sex, and other cheerful subjects?
uz: Nima uchun g'alati yangi kelgan odamning tilidan hech qanday jonli so'z uchmaydi, chunki u boshqa paytlarda kulgi, jonli so'zlar, adolatli jinsiy aloqa va boshqa quvonchli mavzular haqida suhbatni juda yaxshi ko'radi?

en: And why does this friend, probably a new friend and on his ﬁrst visit—for there will hardly be a second, and the friend will never come again—why is the friend himself so confused, so tongue- tied, in spite of his wit (if he has any), as he looks at the downcast face of his host, who in his turn becomes utterly helpless and at his wits' end after gigantic but fruitless efforts to smooth things over and enliven the conversa- tion, to show his knowledge of polite society, to talk, too, of the fair sex, and by such humble endeavour, to please the poor man, who like a ﬁsh out of water has mistakenly come to visit him?
uz: Va nima uchun bu do'st, ehtimol yangi do'st va birinchi marta tashrif buyurganida, nima uchun o'sha do'st ikkinchi marta kelmaydi va do'st yana hech qachon kelmaydi? Nega do'st o'zi o'zining aql-idrokidan (agar bor bo'lsa) qat'i nazar, o'zining mehmonining kamtarlik bilan ko'zlangan yuziga qaraydi, u o'z navbatida yordamsiz va aql-idrokidan mahrum bo'lib qoladi, chunki katta, ammo befoyda harakatlar bilan ishlarni to'xtatishga va suhbatni uyg'otishga harakat qiladi, xushmuomala jamiyat haqida bilimini ko'rsatadi, adolatli jinsiy aloqa haqida ham gapiradi va bunday kamtarin harakatlar bilan kambag'al kishiga, suvdan chiqqan baliq kabi, uni to'xtatishga kelganini ayblanib ko'rsatadi?

en: Why does the gentleman, all at once remembering some very necessary business which never existed, sud- denly seize his hat and hurriedly make off, snatching away his hand from the warm grip of his host, who was trying his utmost to show his regret and retrieve the lost position?
uz: Nima uchun birdan bir marta hech qachon mavjud bo'lmagan juda zarur ishlarni eslab, xudojo'y kishi to'pini qo'lga olib, o'z qo'lini uy egasining iliq qo'lidan olib ketadi, u o'z afsusini ko'rsatish va yo'qolgan mavqega ega bo'lish uchun qo'lidan kelganini qildi?

en: Why does the friend chuckle as he goes out of the door, and swear never to come and see this queer creature again, though the queer creature is really a very good fellow, and at the same time he cannot refuse his imagination the little diversion of comparing the queer fellow's countenance during their conversation with the expression of an unhappy kitten treacherously captured, roughly handled, frightened and subjected to all sorts of indignities by children, till, utterly crestfallen, it hides away from them under a chair in the dark, and there must needs at its leisure bris- tle up, spit, and wash its insulted face with both paws, and long afterwards look angrily at life and nature, and even at the bits saved from the master's dinner for it by the sympathetic housekeeper? Listen, interrupted Nasten-
uz: Nima uchun do'st eshikdan chiqib ketayotganda kulishadi va hech qachon bu g'ayritabiiy mavjudotni yana ko'rmaslikka qasam ichadi, garchi g'ayritabiiy mavjudot aslida juda yaxshi odam bo'lsa-da, bir vaqtning o'zida u o'z tasavvurini g'ayritabiiy kishaning suhbat paytida g'ayritabiiy yigitning ko'z ko'rinishini aldashdan bosh tortishi mumkin emas, u xiyonat qilib qo'lga olingan, qo'pol ravishda ushlab olingan, qo'rqitilgan va bolalar tomonidan har xil haqoratlarga duchor bo'lgan, hatto, butunlay o'zini qorong'ida o'tirgan holda, ulardan yashirinib, qorong'ida o'tirgan o'rinni pastga tushadi va uning dam olish, teshiklash va har ikki oyoq bilan haqoratlangan yuzini yuvishning kichik bir mashg'ulotidan voz kechadi va uzoq vaqt o'tgach tabiatga g'azablanib, hayotga va hayotga qarab turadi, hatto uy xo'jayining kechki ovqatidan bo'lgan qismlarga ham nazar soladi?

en: ka, who had listened to me all the time in amazement, opening her eyes and her little mouth.
uz: U meni har doim hayronlik bilan tinglagan, ko'zlarini va kichkina og'zini ochgan.

en: Listen; I don't know in the least why it happened and why you ask me such absurd questions; all I know is, that this adventure must have happened word for word to you. Doubtless, I answered, with the gravest face.
uz: Quloq solinglar, nima uchun bu sodir bo'lganini va nima uchun menga shunday absurd savollar berayotganingizni hech qachon bilmayman; faqatgina bilamanki, bu sayohat siz uchun so'z-so'z bo'lgan bo'lishi kerak. - Shubhasiz, - deb javob berdim men, eng jiddiy yuz bilan.

en: Well, since there is no doubt about it, go on, said Nastenka, because I want very much to know how it will end. You want to know, Nastenka, what our hero, that is I—for the hero of the whole business was my humble self—did in his corner?
uz: Hamma narsa shubhasiz bo'lgani uchun, boring, dedi Nastenka, chunki men bu qanday yakunlanishini juda xohlayman. Sen bilmoqchimisan, Nastenka, bizning qahramonimiz, ya'ni butun ishning qahramoni mening kamtarin o'zim bo'ldim, uning burchagida?

en: You want to know why I lost my head and was upset for the whole day by the unexpect- ed visit of a friend?
uz: Nima uchun do'stimning kutilmagan tashrifidan butun kunim g'azablanib, aqldan ozganimni bilmoqchimisiz?

en: You want to know why I was so startled, why I blushed when the door of my room was opened, why I was not able to entertain my visitor, and why I was crushed under the weight of my own hospitality? Why, yes, yes, answered Nastenka, that's the point.
uz: Nima uchun men shunchalik qo'rqib ketdim, nega xonamning eshigini ochganimda qizardim, nega mehmondo'stligimning og'irligi ostida tushkunlikka tushdim va nega o'z mehmondo'stligim bilan xursand bo'ldim, deb bilmoqchisiz? - dedi Nastenka.

en: You de- scribe it all splendidly, but couldn't you perhaps describe it a little less splendidly?
uz: Siz hamma narsani ajoyib tarzda yozgansiz, lekin ehtimol uni biroz kamroq ajoyib tarzda tasvirlab berolmaysizmi?

en: You talk as though you were reading it out of a book. Nastenka, I answered in a stern and digniﬁed voice, hardly able to keep from laughing, dear Nastenka, I know I describe splendidly, but, excuse me, I don't know how else to do it.
uz: Siz kitobdan o'qiganingiz kabi gapirasiz. - Nastenka, - deb javob berdim men qattiq va munosib ovoz bilan, kulishdan qochishga ojizman, - Sevg'im Nastenka, men buni ajoyib tarzda tasvirlaganimni bilaman, lekin kechirim so'raysiz, buni qanday qilish kerakligini bilmayman.

en: At this moment, dear Nastenka, at this moment I am like the spirit of King Solomon when, after lying a thousand years under seven seals in his urn, those seven seals were at last taken off.
uz: Hozirgi paytda, aziz Nastenka, men shoh Sulaymonning ruhiga o'xshab, ming yil davomida o'z urnasida yetti muhr ostida yotganimda, bu yetti muhr nihoyat tushdi.

en: At this moment, Nastenka, when we have met at last after such a long sepa- ration—for I have known you for ages, Nastenka, because I have been look- ing for some one for ages, and that is a sign that it was you I was looking for, and it was ordained that we should meet now—at this moment a thou- sand valves have opened in my head, and I must let myself ﬂow in a river of words, or I shall choke.
uz: Mana shu paytda, Nastenka, nihoyat, shunday uzoq vaqtdan keyin uchrashganmiz, chunki men seni asrlar davomida bilardim, Nastenka, chunki men asrlar davomida kimnidir qidirib yurganman va bu men qidirayotgan sen ekanligingning belgisi va biz hozir uchrashishimiz kerakligi tayinlangan edi.Bu paytda boshimda minglab qum valvullari ochildi va men o'zimni so'zlar daryosida oqib ketishim kerak, aks holda men cho'kaman.

en: And so I beg you not to interrupt me, Nastenka, but listen humbly and obediently, or I will be silent. No, no, no!
uz: Shunday qilib, men sizga iltijo qilaman, menga aralashmang, Nastenka, lekin kamtarlik va itoatkorlik bilan tinglang, yoki men sukut saqlashim kerak.

en: I won't say a word! I will continue.
uz: Men bir so'z ham aytmayman! - deb davom ettirdim.

en: There is, my friend Nastenka, one hour in my day which I like extremely.
uz: Do'stim Nastenka, kunimga juda yoqadigan bir soat bor.

en: That is the hour when almost all business, work and duties are over, and every one is hurrying home to dinner, to lie down, to rest, and on the way all are cogitating on other more cheerful subjects relating to their evenings, their nights, and all the rest of their free time.
uz: Bu deyarli barcha ish, ish va vazifalar tugagandan so'ng, har bir kishi kechki ovqatga, uxlashga, dam olishga shoshilmoqda va yo'lda boshqa quvonchli mavzularni o'z kechki paytlari, kechki paytlari va bo'sh vaqtlari haqida o'ylaydi.

en: At that hour our hero—for
uz: O'sha soatda bizning qahramonimiz bor.

en: allow me, Nastenka, to tell my story in the third person, for one feels awful- ly ashamed to tell it in the ﬁrst person—and so at that hour our hero, who had his work too, was pacing along after the others.
uz: Nastenka, menga o'z hikoyamni uchinchi shaxsda aytib berishga ruxsat bering, chunki uni birinchi shaxsda aytishdan juda uyalish mumkin, shuning uchun o'sha soatda bizning qahramonimiz, uning ishi ham bor edi, boshqalarning orqasidan ergashib borardi.

en: But a strange feeling of pleasure set his pale, rather crumpled-looking face working.
uz: Ammo o'zgacha quvonch hissi uning o'tkir, chiroyli ko'rinadigan yuzini ishga tushirdi.

en: He looked not with indifference on the evening glow which was slowly fading on the cold Petersburg sky.
uz: Soyuq Petersburg osmonida sekin-sekin o'tib ketayotgan kechki yorug'likka u befarq emas edi.

en: When I say he looked, I am lying: he did not look at it, but saw it as it were without realizing, as though tired or preoccupied with some other more interesting subject, so that he could scarcely spare a glance for anything about him.
uz: Men ko'rdim deganimda, men yolg'on gapiryapman: u ko'rmadi, lekin buni o'ylamagancha ko'rdi, xuddi charchagan yoki boshqa qiziqarli mavzu bilan mashg'ul bo'lganidek, shuning uchun u o'zi haqida hech narsa ko'rmay qo'yadi.

en: He was pleased because till next day he was re- leased from business irksome to him, and happy as a schoolboy let out from the class-room to his games and mischief.
uz: U xursand edi, chunki ertasigacha u o'ziga og'ir bo'lgan ishdan qayta ijaraga olindi va maktab o'quvchisi sinfdan o'yinlari va yomonliklariga chiqarib yuborilganida xursand edi.

en: Take a look at him, Nastenka; you will see at once that joyful emotion has already had an effect on his weak nerves and morbidly excited fancy.
uz: Unga bir nazar soling, Nastenka; birdan ko'rasiz, quvonchli his-tuyg'ular uning zaif g'azablari va kasallik bilan hayajonlangan xayollariga ta'sir ko'rsatdi.

en: You see he is thinking of some- thing.
uz: Ko'rib turibsizki, u biror narsa haqida o'ylayapti.

en: Of dinner, do you imagine?
uz: Ovqatni tasavvur qila olasizmi?

en: What is he looking at like that?
uz: U nimaga shunday qarayapti?

en: Is it at that gentleman of digniﬁed appearance who is bowing so picturesquely to the lady who rolls by in a carriage drawn by prancing hors- es?
uz: Qarang, o'sha munosib ko'rinishda bo'lgan yigit, o'z ko'rinishida o'tirgan otlar aravachasida o'tib o'tgan ayolga shunchalik chiroyli sajda qilib sajda qilmoqda-ku?

en: No, Nastenka; what are all those trivialities to him now?
uz: Yo'q, Nastenka; u uchun endi bu behudaliklar nima?

en: He is rich now with his own individual life; he has suddenly become rich, and it is not for nothing that the fading sunset sheds its farewell gleams so gaily before him, and calls forth a swarm of impressions from his warmed heart.
uz: U endi o'z shaxsiy hayoti bilan boy bo'ldi; u to'satdan boy bo'ldi va bu behuda emaski, o'tib ketayotgan quyosh botish uning oldida o'z salomini shodlik bilan shod qiladi va uning iliq qalbida taassurotlar to'plamini keltirib chiqaradi.

en: Now he hardly notices the road, on which the tiniest details at other times would strike him.
uz: Endi u yo'lni kamdan-kam ko'radi, boshqa paytlarda unga eng kichik tafsilotlar ham yetib boradi.

en: Now 'the Goddess of Fancy' (if you have read Zhukovsky, dear Nastenka) has already with fantastic hand spun her golden warp and begun weaving upon it patterns of marvellous magic life—and who knows, maybe, her fantastic hand has borne him to the seventh crystal heaven far from the excellent granite pavement on which he was walking his way?
uz: Endi Fantasiyaning xudosi (agar siz Zhukovskiyni o'qigan bo'lsangiz, aziz Nastenka) allaqachon o'zining oltin bo'g'ini ajoyib qo'li bilan o'zgartirgan va uning ustiga ajoyib sehrli hayotning namunalarini tikishni boshlagan va kim biladi, ehtimol uning ajoyib qo'li uni yo'lidan yurgan ajoyib granit pavimentodan uzoq bo'lgan yettinchi kristal osmonga olib borgan?

en: Try stopping him now, ask him suddenly where he is standing now, through what streets he is going—he will, probably remember nothing, neither where he is going nor where he is standing now, and ﬂushing with vexation he will certainly tell some lie to save appearances.
uz: Uni hozir to'xtatishga harakat qiling, to'satdan unga hozir qayerda turganini, qaysi ko'chalardan o'tishini so'rang, ehtimol hech narsa esda qolmaydi, qayerga ketayotganini ham, qayerda turganini ham esda tutmaydi, va xafa bo'lib, ko'rinishlarni saqlab qolish uchun albatta yolg'on gapiradi.

en: That is why he starts, al- most cries out, and looks round with horror when a respectable old lady stops him politely in the middle of the pavement and asks her way.
uz: Shuning uchun u boshlanadi, ko'pchilik qichqiradi va qo'rqinch bilan atrofini ko'radi, bir hurmatli keksa ayol uni martabani o'rtasida xushmuomalalik bilan to'xtatib, yo'l so'raydi.

en: Frown- ing with vexation he strides on, scarcely noticing that more than one passer- by smiles and turns round to look after him, and that a little girl, moving out of his way in alarm, laughs aloud, gazing open-eyed at his broad meditative smile and gesticulations.
uz: O'zini bezovta qilib, o'tib ketadi va birdan ortiq kishilar o'tib o'tib o'tib, unga g'amxo'rlik qilish uchun tabassum qilib, aylanib ketayotganini va qo'rqinchli bo'lib, uning yo'lidan chiqib ketayotgan kichkina qizchaning uning keng mulohazaviy tabassumini va jimligini ko'rib, ko'z ochib, baland ovoz bilan kulishayotganini sezmaydi.

en: But fancy catches up in its playful ﬂight the old woman, the curious passers-by, and the laughing child, and the peasants
uz: Ammo Fantasy o'yinchi samolyotida keksa ayol, qiziqarli o'tishchilar, kulgan bola va qishloq xo'jaligi bilan uchib boradi.

en: spending their nights in their barges on Fontanka (our hero, let us suppose, is walking along the canal-side at that moment), and capriciously weaves every one and everything into the canvas like a ﬂy in a spider's web.
uz: Fontankada kechalarini qaynoqlarida o'tkazish (qahramonimiz shu paytdagi kanal bo'ylab yurayotganini tasavvur qilaylik) va o'zlarining har birini va hamma narsalarini o'z ichiga olgan to'qimaga qo'shib qo'yadi.

en: And it is only after the queer fellow has returned to his comfortable den with fresh stores for his mind to work on, has sat down and ﬁnished his dinner, that he comes to himself, when Matrona who waits upon him—always thoughtful and depressed—clears the table and gives him his pipe; he comes to himself then and recalls with surprise that he has dined, though he has absolutely no notion how it has happened.
uz: Va faqatgina o'ziga qulay va yangi do'konlarga ega bo'lgan o'zining qulay do'konga qaytib kelganidan so'ng, o'tirib, ovqatni tugatganidan so'ng, u o'ziga keladi, uni har doim mulohaza yuritib va tushkunlik bilan kutib turgan Matrona dasturxonni tozalab, unga pipohani beradi; u o'ziga keladi va o'zi ovqatlanganini hayratda qoldirib eslaydi, garchi u qanday sodir bo'lganini hech qachon bilmaydi.

en: It has grown dark in the room; his soul is sad and empty; the whole kingdom of fancies drops to pieces about him, drops to pieces without a trace, without a sound, ﬂoats away like a dream, and he cannot himself remember what he was dreaming.
uz: Xonada qorong'ilik paydo bo'ldi; uning ruhi qayg'urgan va bo'sh; butun tasavvurlar shohligi uning atrofida parchalanib, izsiz, tovushsiz parchalanib ketadi, tush kabi ko'tarib ketadi va u o'zi nimani orzu qilganini eslay olmaydi.

en: But a vague sensation faintly stirs his heart and sets it aching, some new desire temptingly tickles and excites his fancy, and imperceptibly evokes a swarm of fresh phantoms.
uz: Ammo bir noaniq his-tuyg'u uning qalbini salqin o'zgartiradi va uni og'riqli qiladi, yangi istak uni vasvasaga solib, o'ziga xos fikr-mulohazalarni uyg'otadi va ko'rinmas darajada yangi sehrgarlar to'pini keltirib chiqaradi.

en: Stillness reigns in the little room; imagination is fostered by solitude and idleness; it is faintly smouldering, faintly simmering, like the water with which old Matrona is making her coffee as she moves quietly about in the kitchen close by.
uz: Kichik xonada tinchlik hukmronlik qiladi; tasavvur yolg'izlik va behudalik tomonidan qo'llab-quvvatlanadi; u kamdan-kam qovuradi, kamdan-kam qaynab ketadi, xuddi keksa Matrona yaqindagi oshxonada kamdan-kam harakatlanayotganda kofe tayyorlaydigan suv kabi.

en: Now it breaks out spasmodically; and the book, picked up aimlessly and at random, drops from my dreamer's hand before he has reached the third page.
uz: Endi u spasmodik ravishda tushib chiqadi; va maqsadsiz va tasodifiy olib qo'yilgan kitob uchinchi sahifaga yetib kelishidan oldin orzuchi qo'limdan tushadi.

en: His imagination is again stirred and at work, and again a new world, a new fascinating life opens vistas before him.
uz: Uning tasavvurlari yana uyg'onadi va ishda davom etadi va yana yangi dunyo, yangi hayajonli hayot unga ko'rinishni ochadi.

en: A fresh dream—fresh happiness!
uz: Yangi orzu, yangi baxt!

en: A fresh rush of delicate, voluptuous poison!
uz: Xavfsiz, g'ayratli zaharning yangi to'plami!

en: What is real life to him!
uz: U uchun haqiqiy hayot nima!

en: To his corrupted eyes we live, you and I, Nastenka, so torpidly, slowly, insipidly; in his eyes we are all so dissatisﬁed with our fate, so exhausted by our life!
uz: Uning buzuq ko'zlariga ko'ra, biz, sen va men, Nastenka, juda yorqin, asta-sekin, bezovta yashayapmiz; uning ko'zlariga ko'ra, biz barchamiz taqdirimizdan juda mamnun emasmiz, hayotimizdan juda charchabmiz!

en: And, truly, see how at ﬁrst sight everything is cold, morose, as though ill-humoured among us.
uz: Haqiqatan ham, bir qarashda hamma narsa sovuq, chiroyli, xuddi o'z-o'zimizga yomon hazil bo'lganini ko'ring.

en: And it is no wonder that he thinks it!
uz: Va u buni o'ylagani ajablanarli emas!

en: Look at these magic phan- tasms, which so enchantingly, so whimsically, so carelessly and freely group before him in such a magic, animated picture, in which the most prominent ﬁgure in the foreground is of course himself, our dreamer, in his precious person.
uz: Ushbu sehrli fan-tasmlarga qaranglar, ular o'zining sehrli, jonli suratida juda mashhur shaxs sifatida o'zini, albatta, bizning orzuchilarimizni, o'zining qimmatbaho shaxsini o'z huzurida mashhur qiladi.

en: See what varied adventures, what an endless swarm of ec- static dreams.
uz: Qarang, qanday turlicha mashg'ulotlar, qanday cheksiz ekstatik orzular to'plami.

en: You ask, perhaps, what he is dreaming of, Why ask that?— why, of everything.
uz: Ehtimol, siz uning orzu qilgan narsasi haqida, nima uchun buni so'rash kerakligini, nima uchun, hamma narsadan so'rashingiz mumkinligini so'rayotgandirsiz.

en: of the lot of the poet, ﬁrst unrecognized, then crowned with laurels; of friendship with Hoffmann, St.
uz: Shoirning nasibasi, avval tan olinmagan, so'ngra laurellari bilan tojlangan; Hoffmann bilan do'stlik, St..

en: Bartholomew's Night, of Diana Vernon, of playing the hero at the taking of Kazan by Ivan Vassilyevitch, of Clara Mowbray, of Efﬁe Deans, of the council of the prelates and Huss before them, of the rising of the dead in 'Robert the Devil'
uz: Diyana Vernonning Bartolomey kechasi, Ivan Vassilyevitch tomonidan Qozonni egallab olishda qahramonlikni o'ynash, Clara Mowbrayning, Effie Deanlarning, prelatlar kengashi va ularning oldiga kelgan Hussning, Robert iblisda o'liklarning tirilishi haqidagi hikoyalarning qahramonligini o'ynash.

en: (do you remember the music, it smells of the churchyard!), of Minna and Brenda, of the battle of Berezina, of the reading of a poem at Countess V.
uz: (muzikni eslaysizmi, u cherkov hovlisining hidini oladi!), Minna va Brendan, Berezina jangidan, Countess Vda she'r o'qishdan.

en: D.'s, of Danton, of Cleopatra ei suoi amanti, of a little house in Kolomna, of a little home of one's own and beside one a dear creature who listens to one on a winter's evening, opening her little mouth and eyes as you are listening to me now, my angel.
uz: D.s, Danton, Kleopatra va uning xudojo'ylari, Kolomnadagi kichkina uy, o'z uy va yonida qish oqshomida sizni tinglaydigan sevimli mavjudot bo'lib, siz meni hozir tinglayotganingizda o'zining kichkina og'zini va ko'zlarini ochib, qish oqshomida tinglaydi.

en: No, Nastenka, what is there, what is there for him, voluptuous sluggard, in this life, for which you and I have such a longing?
uz: Yo'q, Nastenka, bu hayotda u uchun nima bor, bu hayotda u uchun nima bor, bu hayotda u uchun nima bor, bu hayotda biz ham, siz ham juda orzu qilamiz?

en: He thinks that this is a poor pitiful life, not foreseeing that for him too, maybe, sometime the mournful hour may strike, when for one day of that pitiful life he would give all his years of phantasy, and would give them not only for joy and for happiness, but without caring to make distinctions in that hour of sadness, remorse and unchecked grief.
uz: U o'zi uchun ham, ehtimol, bir kun o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'sha o'

en: But so far that threaten- ing time has not arrived—he desires nothing, because he is superior to all desire, because he has everything, because he is satiated, because he isthe artist of his own life, and creates it for himself every hour to suit his latest whim.
uz: Ammo bu xavfli vaqt hali kelmagan ekan, u hech narsa istamaydi, chunki u har qanday istakdan ustundir, chunki u hamma narsaga ega, chunki u to'yangan, chunki u o'z hayotining san'atkoridir va uni har soatda o'zi uchun yaratadi.

en: And you know this fantastic world of fairyland is so easily, so natu- rally created!
uz: Va siz bilsangiz, bu hayajonli go'yolar dunyosi juda oson, shu qadar tabiiy ravishda yaratilgan!

en: As though it were not a delusion!
uz: O'sha aldam bo'lmaganidek!

en: Indeed, he is ready to be- lieve at some moments that all this life is not suggested by feeling, is not mirage, not a delusion of the imagination, but that it is concrete, real, sub- stantial!
uz: Darhaqiqat, u ba'zi bir paytlarda, bu butun hayot his-tuyg'ular bilan tug'ilmagan, o'ziga xos emas, balki aniq, haqiqiy, mazmunli, degan xayol-mulohazaga ishonishga tayyor!

en: Why is it, Nastenka, why is it at such moments one holds one's breath?
uz: Nima uchun, Nastenka, nima uchun bunday paytlarda inson nafasini ushlab turadi?

en: Why, by what sorcery, through what incomprehensible caprice, is the pulse quickened, does a tear start from the dreamer's eye, while his pale moist cheeks glow, while his whole being is suffused with an inexpressible sense of consolation?
uz: Nima uchun, qaysi sehr-jodu, qaysi tushunarsiz caprice orqali puls tezlashtiriladi, orzuchi ko'zidan yosh boshlanadi, uning bo'lak-bo'laklari yorqin bo'lsa, butun mavjudotining so'zlab bo'lmaydigan tasalli hissi bilan to'lib-toshgan bo'lsa?

en: Why is it that whole sleepless nights pass like a ﬂash in inexhaustible gladness and happiness, and when the dawn gleams rosy at the window and daybreak ﬂoods the gloomy room with uncertain, fantastic light, as in Petersburg, our dreamer, worn out and exhausted, ﬂings himself on his bed and drops asleep with thrills of delight in his morbidly over- wrought spirit, and with a weary sweet ache in his heart?
uz: Nima uchun to'liq uxlamaydigan kechalar to'liq quvonch va baxt-saodat bilan o'tib ketadi, ertangi tong o'rindiqida ro'za parvarish qilganda, kunduz yorug'ligi qorong'i xonani noaniq, ajoyib yorug'lik bilan to'ldirganda, xuddi Sankt-Peterburgda bo'lganidek, orzuchi, charchagan va charchagan holda, o'zini to'shagida tashlab ketadi va o'zining kasallik bilan o'zgartirilgan ruhi va yuragidagi charchagan shirin og'rig'i bilan quvonchga to'lib uxlaydi?

en: Yes, Nastenka, one deceives oneself and unconsciously believes that real true passion is stirring one's soul, one unconsciously believes that there is something liv- ing, tangible in one's immaterial dreams!
uz: Ha, Nastenka, odam o'zini aldaydi va bexabarlik bilan haqiqiy haqiqiy ishtiyoqning o'z ruhini qo'zg'atishiga ishonadi, bexabarlik bilan o'z hayoti va ma'lum bo'lgan narsa borligiga ishonadi!

en: Here love, for instance, is bound up with all its fathomless joy, all its torturing agonies in his bosom.
uz: Masalan, bu yerda sevgi o'z quvonchi bilan bog'liq, uning ko'nglida azob chekayotgan azob-uqubatlar bilan bog'liq.

en: Only look at him, and you will be convinced!
uz: Faqat unga qarasangiz, ishonch hosil qilasiz!

en: Would you be- lieve, looking at him, dear Nastenka, that he has never known her whom he loves in his ecstatic dreams?
uz: Unga qaraganingizda, aziz Nastenka, u o'z tushlarida sevgan qizini hech qachon bilmaganini yoqtirasizmi?

en: Can it be that he has only seen her in seductive visions, and that this passion has been nothing but a dream?
uz: U uni faqat hayratga soluvchi vahiylarda ko'rgan bo'lishi mumkinmi va bu ishtiyoq faqat bir orzu bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkinmi?

en: must have spent years hand in hand together—alone the two of them, cast- ing off all the world and each uniting his or her life with the other's?
uz: Ular bir necha yillar birga qo'l-qo'l qilib, butun dunyoni tashlab, har biri o'z hayotini o'z hayoti bilan birlashtirgan bo'lishlari kerakmi?

en: Surely when the hour of parting came she must have lain sobbing and grieving on his bosom, heedless of the tempest raging under the sullen sky, heedless of the wind which snatches and bears away the tear from her black eyelashes?
uz: Chindan ham, ajrashish vaqti kelganda, u o'z ko'krakida yig'lab, qayg'urgan bo'lishi kerak edi, o'zining qorong'i osmon ostida bo'lgan bo'ronni, uning qora ko'z burchaklaridan ko'z yoshini olib ketayotgan shamolni ko'rmagan edi.

en: Can all of that have been a dream—and that garden, dejected, forsaken, run wild, with its little moss-grown paths, solitary, gloomy, where they used to walk so happily together, where they hoped, grieved, loved, loved each oth- er so long, 'so long and so fondly?' And that queer ancestral house where she spent so many years lonely and sad with her morose old husband, al- ways silent and splenetic, who frightened them, while timid as children they hid their love from each others?
uz: Bularning barchasi bir orzu edi va o'sha tushkun, tashlab ketilgan, yovvoyi bog', o'zlarining kichik mo'g'ir yo'llari bilan, yolg'iz, qorong'i, ular bir-biriga shunchalik baxtli yurishgan, umid bog'lagan, qayg'urgan, sevgan, bir-birlarini shunchalik uzoq vaqt, shunchalik uzoq va shunchalik mehr ila sevgan bog' va o'sha g'ayritabiiy ota-ona uyi, u o'zidan ko'p yillar davomida yolg'iz va qayg'urgan keksa eri bilan o'tkazgan, o'zidan-o'zi xafa va g'alati bo'lgan, ularni qo'rqitgan, o'zlaridan qo'rqqan, o'g'il bo'lganlarida o'z sevgisini bir-biridan yashirgan o'sha g'ayritabiiy ota-onalar uyi?

en: What torments they suffered, what agonies of terror, how innocent, how pure was their love, and how (I need hardly say, Nastenka) malicious people were!
uz: Ular qanday azob chekishgan, qanday dahshatli azob chekishgan, qanchalik aybsiz, qanchalik sof sevgisi va (nastenka) qanday yovuz odamlar bo'lganini aytishning hojati yo'q!

en: surely he met her afterwards, far from their native shores, under alien skies, in the hot south in the divinely eternal city, in the dazzling splendour of the ball to the crash of music, in a palazzo (it must be in a palazzo}, drowned in a sea of lights, on the balcony, wreathed in myrtle and roses, where, recognizing him, she hurriedly removes her mask and whispering, 'I am free,' ﬂings her- self trembling into his arms, and with a cry of rapture, clinging to one an- other, in one instant they forget their sorrow and their parting and all their agonies, and the gloomy house and the old man and the dismal garden in that distant land, and the seat on which with a last passionate kiss she tore herself away from his arms numb with anguish and despair.
uz: Keyinchalik u u bilan uchrashdi, u o'z yurtlaridan uzoqda, begona osmon ostida, issiq janubiy joyda, ilohiy abadiy shaharda, musiqa to'plamining charchagan chiroqida, palatada (bu palatada bo'lishi kerak), yorug'lik dengizida cho'kgan, balkonda, mirta va gullar bilan to'ldirilgan, uni tanib-bilganida, u darhol maskani olib tashlaydi va: Men ozodman, deb shov-shuv qilib, o'zini uning qo'liga tashlaydi, bir-birlariga bog'lanib, bir-birlariga qo'shilib, o'zini qo'rqinchli qichqiriq bilan, bir lahzada o'zlarining qayg'usi va ajralishi va barcha azoblarini, o'sha uzoq mamlakatdagi qorong'i uy, keksa odam va qorong'i bog'ni va o'tirgan o'rinni darrov o'chirib oladi.

en: Oh, Nasten- ka, you must admit that one would start, betray confusion, and blush like a schoolboy who has just stuffed in his pocket an apple stolen from a neigh- bour's garden, when your uninvited visitor, some stalwart, lanky fellow, a festive soul fond of a joke, opens your door and shouts out as though noth- ing were happening; 'My dear boy, I have this minute come from Pavlovsk.' My goodness!
uz: Oh, Nasten-ka, siz tan olishingiz kerakki, odam boshlanadi, chalkashlikka va qizg'inlikka duchor bo'ladi, xuddi qo'shnilar bog'idan o'g'irlangan olma to'plamini qopqoqlariga to'ldirgan maktab o'g'li kabi, agar sizning taklif etilmagan mehmoningiz, ba'zi bir qat'iy, shovqinlik qiladigan, bayram ruhini o'rganadigan bir kishi sizning eshikingizni ochib, hech narsa bo'lmagandek qichqiradi: Sevam, men bu daqiqani Pavlovskdan olganman.

en: the old count is dead, unutterable happiness is close at hand —and people arrive from Pavlovsk! Finishing my pathetic appeal, I paused pathetically.
uz: Eski homiy o'ldi, so'zsiz baxt yaqinlashib qoldi va Pavlovskdan odamlar keladi! - deb o'yladim.

en: I remembered that I had an intense desire to force myself to laugh, for I was already feeling that a malignant demon was stirring within me, that there was a lump in my throat, that my chin was beginning to twitch, and that my eyes were grow- ing more and more moist.
uz: O'zimni kulishga majburlashga kuchli istak borligimni esladim, chunki men allaqachon ichimda yovuz shayton harakatlanayotganini his qilardim, qo'limda bir bulut borligini, burnim titrashni boshlaganini va ko'zlarim yanada suyuqlashib borayotganini esladim.

en: I expected Nastenka, who listened to me opening her clever eyes, would break into her childish, irrepressible laugh; and I was already regretting that I had gone so far, that I had unnecessarily described what had long been simmering in my heart, about which I could speak as though from a written account of it, because I had long ago passed judgment on myself and now could not resist reading it, making my confession, without expecting to be understood; but to my surprise she was silent, waiting a little, then she faint- ly pressed my hand and with timid sympathy asked— Surely you haven't lived like that all your life? All my life, Nastenka, I answered; all my life, and it seems to me I shall go on so to the end. No, that won't do, she said uneasily, that must not be; and so, maybe, I shall spend all my life beside grandmother.
uz: O'z aqlli ko'zlarini ochayotganimda, Nastenka o'zining bolalikcha, bosimsiz kulgiga tushib ketishini kutib o'tirgan edim; va men allaqachon shunchagacha ketishimdan, uzoq vaqt davomida qalbimda qaynayotgan narsani ortiqcha tasvirlaganimdan afsuslanardim, bu haqda yozma hikoyadan o'zimni o'zim hukm qilganim kabi gapirishim mumkin edi, chunki men o'zimni o'zimdan uzoq vaqt oldin hukm qilgan edim va endi uni o'qib, tanbehimni aytishga to'sqinlik qila olmadim; lekin u biroz sukut bo'lib, biroz kutganidan so'ng, qo'limni sovirib qo'ydi va qo'rqinchli hamdardlik bilan so'radi: Agar sen butun hayotingda shunday umr ko'rmadingmi? - deb javob berdim men: O'z hayotim davomida, Nastenka, - dedim men: O'z hayotim davomida, o'zimni oxirigacha shunday umr ko'ryapman.

en: Do you know, it is not at all good to live like that? I know, Nastenka, I know! I cried, unable to restrain my feelings longer.
uz: Bilasizmi, bunday yashash umuman yaxshi emas? - Bilaman, Nastenka, bilaman! - deb yig'ladim, his-tuyg'ularimni endi to'xtata olmasdim.

en: And I realize now, more than ever, that I have lost all my best years!
uz: Va men endi, har qachongidan ko'ra, eng yaxshi yillarimni yo'qotganimni anglayman!

en: And now I know it and feel it more painfully from recognising that God has sent me you, my good angel, to tell me that and show it.
uz: Endi esa buni bilaman va Xudo buni menga aytish va ko'rsatish uchun seni, yaxshi farishtamni, menga yuborganini tan olgach, yanada og'irroq his qilaman.

en: Now that I sit beside you and talk to you it is strange for me to think of the future, for in the future—there is loneliness again, again this musty, useless life; and what shall I have to dream of when I have been so happy in reality beside you!
uz: Endi men sizning yoningizda o'tirib, siz bilan suhbatlashayotgan ekanman, kelajak haqida o'ylash menga o'zgacha tuyuladi, chunki kelajakda yana yolg'izlik, yana bu qovurgan, foydasiz hayot bo'ladi; va siz bilan birga hayotda juda baxtli bo'lganimdan keyin nima haqida orzu qilishim kerak!

en: Oh, may you be blessed, dear girl, for not having repulsed me at ﬁrst, for enabling me to say that for two evenings, at least, I have lived. Oh, no, no! cried Nastenka and tears glistened in her eyes.
uz: Oh, sen barakali bo'lsang, aziz qizim, menga boshida yomonlik qilmaganing uchun, hech bo'lmaganda ikki kecha umr ko'rdim, deb aytishimga imkon berganing uchun. - O, yo'q, yo'q! - deb baqirdi Nastenka, ko'zlaridan yoshlar oqib ketdi.

en: No, it mustn't be so any more; we must not part like that!
uz: Yo'q, bu endi shunday bo'lmasligi kerak; biz bunday bo'lishimiz kerak emas!

en: what are two evenings? Oh, Nastenka, Nastenka!
uz: Oh, Nastenka, Nastenka!

en: Do you know how far you have reconciled me to myself?
uz: O'zim bilan qanchalik yarashganingizni bilasizmi?

en: Do you know now that I shall not think so ill of myself, as I have at some moments?
uz: Endi o'zimni yomon ko'rmayapman, deb o'ylaysizmi, ba'zi paytlarda o'zimni yomon ko'rmayapman.

en: Do you know that, maybe, I shall leave off grieving over the crime and sin of my life?
uz: Ehtimol, o'z hayotimdagi jinoyat va gunoh uchun qayg'urishni to'xtatishim kerakligini bilasizmi?

en: for such a life is a crime and a sin.
uz: Chunki bunday hayot jinoyat va gunohdir.

en: And do not imagine that I have been exaggerating anything—for goodness' sake don't think that, Nastenka: for at times such misery comes over me, such misery.
uz: Va men biror narsani o'ylamayotganimni tasavvur qilma, Nastenka, xolos, shunday o'ylamang: ba'zan men o'zimni bunday azob-uqubatlarga duchor qilaman.

en: Because it begins to seem to me at such times that I am incapable of be- ginning a life in real life, because it has seemed to me that I have lost all touch, all instinct for the actual, the real; because at last I have cursed my-
uz: Chunki o'sha paytlarda menga haqiqiy hayotda yashashga qodir emasman, deb o'ylay boshladi, chunki men barcha tuyg'ularimni, haqiqiy, haqiqiy bo'lish instinktini yo'qotgan deb o'ylardim; chunki nihoyat men o'z-o'zimni la'natladim.

en: self; because after my fantastic nights I have moments of returning sobriety, which are awful!
uz: Chunki o'zimning ajoyib kechalarimdan so'ng, men o'zimni o'ylayman va o'zimni o'ylayman, bu esa dahshatli paytlardir!

en: Meanwhile, you hear the whirl and roar of the crowd in the vortex of life around you; you hear, you see, men living in reality; you see that life for them is not forbidden, that their life does not ﬂoat away like a dream, like a vision; that their life is being eternally renewed, eternally youthful, and not one hour of it is the same as another; while fancy is so spiritless, monotonous to vulgarity and easily scared, the slave of shadows, of the idea, the slave of the ﬁrst cloud that shrouds the sun, and overcasts with depression the true Petersburg heart so devoted to the sun—and what is fancy in depression!
uz: Shu bilan birga, siz atrofingizdagi hayot shov-shuvidagi xaloyiqning shov-shuvini eshitasiz; siz haqiqatda yashayotgan odamlarni eshitasiz, ko'rasiz; ular uchun hayot taqiqlanmaganini, ularning hayoti orzu, ko'rgu kabi ko'tarilmayotganini ko'rasiz; ularning hayoti abadiy yangilanmoqda, abadiy yosh, va bir soat ham boshqaga o'xshamaydi; o'ylab ko'rish juda ruhsiz, vulgarlikka monoton va osonlikcha qo'rqinchli bo'lsa-da, soyalar, g'oyalar, quyoshni o'rab olgan birinchi bulutning quli, quyoshga bag'ishlangan va tushkunlikka to'lib-toshkan haqiqiy Sankt-Peterburg yuragi va tushkunlikda nima o'ylab ko'rish mumkin!

en: One feels that this inexhaustible fancy is weary at last and worn out with continual exercise, because one is growing into man- hood, outgrowing one's old ideals: they are being shattered into fragments, into dust; if there is no other life one must build one up from the fragments.
uz: O'shanda inson o'zi o'zining eski ideallaridan ustun qolib, o'sib bormoqda: ular parchalanib, tuproqga aylanadi; agar boshqa hayot yo'q bo'lsa, o'sha parchalablardan o'sha hayotni tiklash kerak.

en: And meanwhile the soul longs and craves for something else!
uz: Va shu bilan birga, ruh boshqa narsani orzu qiladi va orzu qiladi!

en: And in vain the dreamer rakes over his old dreams, as though seeking a spark among the embers, to fan them into ﬂame, to warm his chilled heart by the rekindled ﬁre, and to rouse up in it again all that was so sweet, that touched his heart, that set his blood boiling, drew tears from his eyes, and so luxuriously de- ceived him!
uz: Va bekorga orzu qiluvchi o'zining eski orzularini ko'taradi, xuddi o'simliklar orasida chiroq izlab, ularni olovga aylantirib, o'zining sovuq yuragini o'chirib turgan olov bilan isitib, uning yuragida shunchalik shirin, qalblariga ta'sir qiladigan, qonini qaynatadigan, ko'zlaridan yoshlar chiqarib, uni o'ziga xos tarzda yo'q qilgan barcha narsani uyg'otadi!

en: Do you know, Nastenka, the point I have reached?
uz: Bilasanmi, Nastenka, men yetib kelgan nuqta?

en: Do you know that I am forced now to celebrate the anniversary of my own sensa- tions, the anniversary of that which was once so sweet, which never existed in reality—for this anniversary is kept in memory of those same foolish, shadowy dreams—and to do this because those foolish dreams are no more, because I have nothing to earn them with; you know even dreams do not come for nothing!
uz: O'z his-tuyg'ularimning yubileyini nishonlashga majbur bo'lganimni bilasizmi, bir vaqtlar juda shirin bo'lgan, aslida hech qachon mavjud bo'lmagan narsa yubileyi, chunki bu yubiley o'sha ahmoqona, soya tushlari xotirasida saqlanadi va buni o'sha ahmoqona orzular yo'q bo'lganligi uchun qilaman, chunki men ularga ega bo'lish uchun hech narsa yo'q; hatto orzular befoyda kelmaydi!

en: Do you know that I love now to recall and visit at certain dates the places where I was once happy in my own way?
uz: O'zingiz bilasizmi, endi men o'z yo'limda baxtli bo'lgan joylarimni eslab turishni va muayyan kunlarda tashrif buyurishni yaxshi ko'raman?

en: I love to build up my present in harmony with the irrevocable past, and I often wander like a shadow, aimless, sad and dejected, about the streets and crooked lanes of Petersburg.
uz: O'tmishda o'tgan hodisalar bilan uyg'unlikda hozirni qurishni yaxshi ko'raman va ko'pincha men ko'chalar va bo'g'ir yo'llar bo'ylab ko'chalarda soya kabi, maqsadsiz, qayg'u va tushkunlikka tushib yuraman.

en: What memories they are!
uz: Bu qanday xotiralar!

en: To remember, for instance, that here just a year ago, just at this time, at this hour, on this pavement, I wandered just as lonely, just as dejected as to-day.
uz: Misol uchun, bir yil oldin, mana shu vaqtda, shu soatda, bu yo'l ustida yolg'izlik va tushkunlikka tushib yurganimni eslaylik.

en: And one remembers that then one's dreams were sad, and though the past was no better one feels as though it had somehow been better, and that life was more peaceful, that one was free from the black thoughts that haunt one now; that one was free from the gnawing of conscience—the gloomy, sullen gnawing which now gives me no rest by day or by night.
uz: O'shanda inson o'zining orzulari g'amgin bo'lganini va o'tmish yaxshi bo'lmaganini eslaydi, lekin u o'zini qandaydir tarzda yaxshiroq bo'lganidek his qiladi va hayot tinchroq, hozir uni qiynayotgan qora fikrlardan ozod bo'ladi; vijdonning qichqiriqidan ozod bo'ladi - kun yoki kechasi menga hech qanday dam bermaydigan qorong'i, qichqiriq qichqiriq.

en: And one asks oneself where are one's dreams.
uz: Va odam o'zidan so'radi: O'z orzularingiz qayerda?

en: And one shakes one's head and says how rapidly the years ﬂy by!
uz: Va boshni silkitib, yillar qanchalik tez o'tib o'tishini aytadi!

en: again one asks oneself what has one done with one's years.
uz: Yana bir bor o'zimizga savol beramiz: o'z yillarimiz bilan nima qilganmiz?

en: Where have you buried your best days?
uz: Eng yaxshi kunlaringizni qayerda ko'mgansiz?

en: Have you lived or not?
uz: Siz yashadingizmi yoki yo'qmi?

en: Look, one says to oneself, look how cold the world is growing.
uz: Birov o'ziga: Dunyo qanchalik sovuq bo'layotganini ko'ringlar! - deb aytadi.

en: Some more years will pass, and after them will come gloomy solitude; then will come old age trembling on its crutch, and after it misery and desolation.
uz: Yana bir necha yillar o'tib ketadi va ulardan keyin qorong'i yolg'izlik keladi; keyin keksalik o'z qo'llari bilan titraydi va undan keyin qashshoqlik va halokat keladi.

en: Your fantastic world will grow pale, your dreams will fade and die and will fall like the yellow leaves from the trees.
uz: Sizning ajoyib dunyosingiz o'tkirlashib, orzularingiz so'lib, o'lib, daraxtlarning sariq barglari kabi qulab ketadi.

en: you know it will be sad to be left alone, utterly alone, and to have not even anything to regret—nothing, absolutely nothing.
uz: O'zingiz bilasiz, yolg'iz qolish, butunlay yolg'iz qolish va hatto afsuslanish uchun hech narsa yo'q bo'lish juda achinarli bo'ladi hech narsa, mutlaqo hech narsa.

en: for all that you have lost, all that, all was nothing, stupid, simple nullity, there has been nothing but dreams! Come, don't work on my feelings any more, said Nastenka, wiping away a tear which was trickling down her cheek.
uz: Siz yo'qotgan barcha narsalar uchun, bularning barchasi hech narsa emas edi, ahmoqlik va oddiy befoydalik, faqat orzular bor edi! - dedi Nastenka.

en: Now we shall be two together.
uz: Endi biz ikkitamiz birga bo'lamiz.

en: Now whatever happens to me, we will never part.
uz: Endi menga nima bo'lishidan qat'i nazar, biz hech qachon ajrashmaymiz.

en: Listen; I am a simple girl, I have not had much education, though grand- mother did get a teacher for me, but truly I understand you, for all that you have described I have been through myself, when grandmother pinned me to her dress.
uz: Eshiting, men oddiy qizman, men ko'p ta'lim olmaganman, ammo buvim menga o'qituvchi topgan, lekin men sizni chin dildan tushunaman, siz aytgan barcha narsalarga ko'ra, buvim meni o'z kiyimimga bog'laganida, o'zim o'zimdan o'tganman.

en: Of course, I should not have described it so well as you have; I am not educated, she added timidly, for she was still feeling a sort of re- spect for my pathetic eloquence and lofty style; but I am very glad that you have been quite open with me.
uz: Albatta, men buni siz kabi yaxshi tasvirlamagan bo'lar edim; men o'qimagan emasman, - deb qo'shib qo'ydi u qo'rqqan holda, chunki u hali ham o'zimning achinarli so'zlashuvchanligim va yuksak uslubim uchun o'ziga o'xshaydi.

en: Now I know you thoroughly, all of you.
uz: Endi men sizlarni, barchangizni yaxshi bilaman.

en: And do you know what?
uz: Va nima qilishni bilasizmi?

en: I want to tell you my history too, all without conceal- ment, and after that you must give me advice.
uz: Men sizga o'z tariximni ham so'zlab berishni xohlayman, bularning hammasi yashirincha bo'lmaydi, keyin esa menga maslahat berishingiz kerak.

en: You are a very clever man; will you promise to give me advice? Ah, Nastenka, I cried, though I have never given advice, still less sen- sible advice, yet I see now that if we always go on like this that it will be very sensible, and that each of us will give the other a great deal of sensible advice!
uz: Siz juda aqlli odamsiz; menga maslahat berishga va'da berasizmi? - deb o'ylardim men: A, Nastenka, men hech qachon maslahat bermagan bo'lsam-da, yana kamroq oqilona maslahat bermagan bo'lsam-da, hozir shuni ko'ryapmanki, agar biz har doim shunday yo'l tutsak, bu juda oqilona bo'ladi va har birimiz bir-birimizga ko'p oqilona maslahatlar beramiz!

en: Well, my pretty Nastenka, what sort of advise do you want?
uz: Xo'sh, yoqimli Nastenka, qanday maslahatni xohlaysiz?

en: Tell me frankly; at this moment I am so gay and happy, so bold and sensible, that it won't be difﬁcult for me to ﬁnd words. No, no! Nastenka interrupted, laughing.
uz: Ayting-chi, hozir men shunchalik gey va baxtli, shunchalik jasoratli va aqllimanki, so'zlarni topish men uchun qiyin bo'lmaydi. - Yo'q, yo'q! - dedi Nastenka kulish bilan.

en: I don't only want sensible ad- vice, I want warm brotherly advice, as though you had been fond of me all your life! Agreed, Nastenka, agreed! I cried delighted; and if I had been fond of you for twenty years, I couldn't have been fonder of you than I am now. Your hand, said Nastenka.
uz: Men nafaqat oqilona maslahatni, balki birodarlik maslahatini ham xohlayman, xuddi sen butun umr meni sevgan bo'lgandek! - dedim. Kahramon, Nastenka, rozi bo'lding! - deb xursand bo'lib yig'ladim men. Agar men seni yigirma yil sevgan bo'lsam, hozirgidek ko'proq sevgan bo'lar edim.

en: Here it is, said I, giving her my hand.
uz: Men unga qo'limni berib: Buni ko'ring, - dedim.

en: And so let us begin my history!
uz: Va shuning uchun mening tariximni boshlashimiz kerak!

en: NASTENKA'S HISTORY Half my story you know already—that is, you know that I have an old grandmother.
uz: NASTENKA TARJIMASI Xatrimning yarmini siz allaqachon bilasiz, ya'ni mening keksa buvim borligini bilasiz.

en: . If the other half is as brief as that.
uz: Agar ikkinchi yarmi shu qadar qisqa bo'lsa.

en: . I interrupted, laughing.
uz: . - deb o'yladim va kulganman.

en: Be quiet and listen.
uz: Shuningdan so'ng, hushyor turing va tinglang.

en: First of all you must agree not to interrupt me, or else, perhaps I shall get in a muddle!
uz: Avvalo, meni to'xtatmaslikka rozi bo'lishingiz kerak, aks holda, ehtimol men chalg'ib ketaman!

en: Come, listen quietly.
uz: Kelinglar, tinchlik bilan tinglanglar.

en: I have an old grandmother.
uz: Mening keksa buvim bor.

en: I came into her hands when I was quite a lit- tle girl, for my father and mother are dead.
uz: Men o'zimni o'ta yosh bo'lganimda uning qo'liga tushdim, chunki otam va onam o'lgan.

en: It must be supposed that grand- mother was once richer, for now she recalls better days.
uz: Ehtimol, buvim bir vaqtlar boyroq bo'lgan, lekin hozir u yaxshiroq kunlarni eslaydi.

en: She taught me French, and then got a teacher for me.
uz: U menga frantsuz tilini o'rgatdi, so'ngra menga o'qituvchi topdi.

en: When I was ﬁfteen (and now I am seventeen) we gave up having lessons.
uz: O'n besh yoshimda (va hozir o'n yetti yoshda) dars o'qishni tashladik.

en: It was at that time that I got into mischief; what I did I won't tell you; it's enough to say that it wasn't very important.
uz: O'sha paytda men yomonlikka tushdim; nima qilganimni sizga aytmayman; bu juda muhim emasligini aytish kifoya.

en: But grandmother called me to her one morning and said that as she was blind she could not look after me; she took a pin and pinned my dress to hers, and said that we should sit like that for the rest of our lives if, of course, I did not become a better girl.
uz: Ammo buvim meni bir kuni ertalab chaqirib, ko'r bo'lgani uchun menga g'amxo'rlik qila olmasligini aytdi; u cho'g'imni olib, kiyimi o'zining kiyimlariga bog'ladi va agar men yaxshi qiz bo'lmasam, hayotimizning oxirigacha shunday o'tirib turishimiz kerakligini aytdi.

en: In fact, at ﬁrst it was impossible to get away from her: I had to work, to read and to study all beside grand- mother.
uz: Aslida, dastlab undan qochishim mumkin emas edi: men hammamiz bilan birga ishlash, o'qish va o'qish kerak edi.

en: I tried to deceive her once, and persuaded Fekla to sit in my place.
uz: Men bir marta uni aldashga harakat qildim va Feklani o'zimning o'rnimda o'tirishga ishontirdim.

en: Fekla is our charwoman, she is deaf.
uz: Fekla bizning charwoman, u kar.

en: Fekla sat there instead of me; grand- mother was asleep in her armchair at the time, and I went off to see a friend close by.
uz: Fekla o'zim o'rniga o'tirdi; buvim o'sha paytda o'zining kursi ustida uxlab yotgan edi va men yaqin atrofdagi do'stim bilan uchrashishga bordim.

en: Well, it ended in trouble.
uz: Xo'sh, bu muammolarga tushib qoldi.

en: Grandmother woke up while I was out, and asked some questions; she thought I was still sitting quietly in my place.
uz: Men tashqarida bo'lganimda, buvim uyg'onib, bir necha savollar berdi va men hali ham o'zimning joyimda xotirjam o'tirganimni o'ylagan.

en: Fekla saw that grandmother was asking her something, but could not tell what it was; she wondered what to do, undid the pin and ran away.
uz: Fekla buni ko'rib, buvisi undan bir narsa so'raganini ko'rdi, ammo nima ekanligini aytolmadi; u nima qilish kerakligini o'ylab, pinni olib tashladi va qochib ketdi.

en: . At this point Nastenka stopped and began laughing.
uz: . Natijada Nastenka to'xtadi va kulishni boshladi.

en: She left off at once.
uz: U darhol to'xtadi.

en: I tell you what, don't you laugh at grandmother.
uz: Senga nima deyman, buvisiga kulmang.

en: I laugh because it is fun- ny.
uz: Men kulishim kerak, chunki bu qiziqarli.

en: What can I do, since grandmother is like that; but yet I am fond of her in a way.
uz: Men nima qila olaman, chunki buvim shunday; lekin men uni bir yo'l bilan yaxshi ko'raman.

en: Oh, well, I did catch it that time.
uz: O'sha safar uni ushlab qoldim.

en: I had to sit down in my place at once, and after that I was not allowed to stir.
uz: Men darhol o'z joyimga o'tirishim kerak edi va bundan keyin menga harakatlanishga ruxsat berilmadi.

en: Oh, I forgot to tell you that our house belongs to us, that is to grand- mother; it is a little wooden house with three windows as old as grandmoth- er herself, with a little upper storey; well, there moved into our upper storey a new lodger.
uz: Oh, sizga aytishni unutib qo'ydimki, uyimiz bizga tegishli, ya'ni buvimizga tegishli; bu bobomning o'zi kabi uchta oynali, kichik bir yuqori qavatli yog'och uy; yaxshi, bizning yuqori qavatimizga yangi uy egasi ko'chib o'tdi.

en: Then you had an old lodger, I observed casually.
uz: Shuning uchun eski uy egasi bor edi, - deb o'yladim men.

en: Yes, of course, an- swered Nastenka, and one who knew how to hold his tongue better than you do.
uz: Ha, albatta, dedi Nastenka, va tilini sizdan yaxshiroq ushlab turishni bilgan kishi.

en: In fact, he hardly ever used his tongue at all.
uz: Aslida, u hech qachon tildan foydalanmagan.

en: He was a dumb, blind, lame, dried-up little old man, so that at last he could not go on living, he died; so then we had to ﬁnd a new lodger, for we could not live without a lodger—the rent, together with grandmother's pension, is almost all we have.
uz: U soqov, ko'r, cho'loq, quruq bo'lgan kichik keksa kishi edi, shuning uchun u hayotini davom ettira olmadi, o'ldi; shuning uchun biz yangi ijaraga oluvchi topishimiz kerak edi, chunki biz ijaraga olmasdan yashay olmasdik.

en: But the new lodger, as luck would have it, was a young man, a stranger not of these parts.
uz: Ammo yangi uy egasi, omadli bo'lganidek, yosh yigit edi, bu joylardan chetda bo'lmagan.

en: As he did not haggle over the rent, grandmother accepted him, and only afterwards she asked me: 'Tell me, Nastenka, what is our lodger like—is he young or old?' I did not want to lie, so I told grand- mother that he wasn't exactly young and that he wasn't old.
uz: U ijara haqini so'zlamaganligi sababli, buvim uni qabul qildi va keyinchalik menga: Menga ayting, Nastenka, bizning uy egamiz nima, yoshmi yoki keksami? deb so'radi.

en: 'And is he pleasant looking?' asked grandmother.
uz: 'Va u yoqimli ko'rinishga egami?' - deb so'radi buvim.

en: Again I did not want to tell a lie: 'Yes, he is pleasant looking, grand- mother,' I said.
uz: Men yana yolg'on gapirishni istamagan edim: Ha, u yoqimli, buvim, - dedim men.

en: And grandmother said: 'Oh, what a nuisance, what a nui- sance!
uz: Shunda buvim shunday dedi: Oh, bu naqadar noqulaylik, naqadar noqulaylik!

en: I tell you this, grandchild,that you may not be looking after him.
uz: Men senga buni aytaman, nevam, ehtimol unga g'amxo'rlik qilmaysan.

en: What times these are!
uz: Hozir qanday vaqtlar!

en: Why a paltry lodger like this, and he must be pleasant looking too; it was very different in the old days!' Grandmother was always regretting the old days—she was younger in old days, and the sun was warmer in old days, and cream did not turn so sour in old days—it was always the old days!
uz: Nima uchun bunday kamtarlik bilan yashaydigan kishi bor va u ham chiroyli ko'rinadi; bu qadimgi kunlarda juda farq qilardi! - deb aytdi. - Nenicha onam har doim eski kunlardan afsuslanardi.

en: I would sit still and hold my tongue and think to myself: why did grandmother suggest it to me?
uz: Men o'zimni to'xtatib, tilimni tutib, o'zimga o'ylayman: nega buvim menga buni taklif qildi?

en: Why did she ask whether the lodger was young and good-looking?
uz: Nega u uy egasining yosh va chiroyliligini so'radi?

en: But that was all, I just thought it, began counting my stitches again, went on knitting my stocking, and forgot all about it.
uz: Ammo bu hammasi edi, deb o'yladim, yana tikuvlarimni sanay boshladim, shkaflarimni tikdim va hamma narsani unutib qo'ydim.

en: Well, one morning the lodger came in to see us; he asked about a prom- ise to paper his rooms.
uz: Bir kuni ertalab uy egasi bizni ko'rish uchun keldi va o'z xonadonlarini qog'ozlashtirish uchun promot haqida so'radi.

en: One thing led to another.
uz: Bir narsa boshqa narsaga olib keldi.

en: Grandmother was talkative, and she said: 'Go, Nastenka, into my bedroom and bring me my reckoner.' I jumped up at once; I blushed all over, I don't know why, and forgot I was sitting pinned to grandmother; instead of quietly undoing the pin, so that the lodger should not see—I jumped so that grandmother's chair moved.
uz: Buyuk onam gapiradigan bo'lib, u: Nastenka, uyxonamga kir va hisoblagichimni keltiring, - deb aytdi. Men darhol ko'tarildim; hamma tomondan qizillab ketdim, nima sababini bilmayman, va bu yerda o'tirganimni unutib qo'ydim; uy egasi ko'rmasin deb, pinni xotirjamlik bilan bekor qilishning o'rniga Men o'tib ketdim va bu bilan bu ayolning o'rinbosari harakatlandi.

en: When I saw that the lodger knew all about me now, I blushed, stood still as though I had been shot, and suddenly began to cry—I felt so ashamed and miser- able at that minute, that I didn't know where to look!
uz: Uy egasi endi men haqimda hamma narsani bilganini ko'rgach, qizg'inib, xuddi o'qilgan bo'lsam-da, to'xtab turdim va to'satdan yig'la boshladim.O'sha daqiqada men o'zimni shunchalik uyalgan va noxush his qildimki, qayerga qarashni bilmasdim!

en: Grandmother called out, 'What are you waiting for?' and I went on worse than ever.
uz: Buvim: Nimaga kutyapsan? - deb hayqiribdi va men bundan buyon ham yomonlashib ketdim.

en: lodger saw, saw that I was ashamed on his account, he bowed and went away at once!
uz: Uy egasi ko'rib, men uning uchun uyalganimni ko'rib, tiz cho'kib, darhol ketib ketdi!

en: After that I felt ready to die at the least sound in the passage.
uz: Undan keyin o'zimni o'limga tayyor his qildim, hatto o'sha yo'nalishdagi eng kam ovoz ham.

en: 'It's the lodger,' I kept thinking; I stealthily undid the pin in case.
uz: Men o'yladim: Bu uy egasi, - deb o'yladim, o'zim ham o'zimni o'yladim.

en: But it always turned out not to be, he never came.
uz: Ammo bu har doim ham bo'lmagan, u hech qachon kelmagan.

en: A fortnight passed; the lodger sent word through Fyokla that he had a great number of French books, and that they were all good books that I might read, so would not grandmother like me to read them that I might not be dull?
uz: Ikki hafta o'tgach, uy egasi Fyokla orqali uning ko'plab frantsuz kitoblari borligini va ularning barchasi men o'qigan yaxshi kitoblar ekanligini xabar qildi.

en: Grandmother agreed with grati- tude, but kept asking if they were moral books, for if the books were im- moral it would be out of the question, one would learn evil from them. 'And what should I learn, grandmother?
uz: Buyuk onam bunga rozi bo'ldi, lekin ular axloqiy kitoblar bo'ladimi, deb so'ragan, chunki agar ular axloqiy emas bo'lsa, bu savolga javob bermaydi, odam ulardan yomonlik o'rganadi.

en: What is there written in them?' 'Ah,' she said, 'what's described in them, is how young men seduce vir- tuous girls; how, on the excuse that they want to marry them, they carry them off from their parents' houses; how afterwards they leave these unhap- py girls to their fate, and they perish in the most pitiful way.
uz: Ularda nima yozilgan? - dedi u, - Aha, bularda aytilishicha, yigitlar qanday qilib qizlarni ayyorlaydilar; qanday qilib ular bilan turmush qurmoqchi bo'lish bahosi bilan ularni ota-onasi uylaridan olib ketishadi; qanday qilib keyinchalik bu baxtsiz qizlarni o'z taqdirlariga qoldirib ketishadi va ular eng achinarli tarzda halok bo'lishadi.

en: I read a great many books,' said grandmother, 'and it is all so well described that one sits up all night and reads them on the sly.
uz: Men juda ko'p kitoblarni o'qib chiqdim, - dedi buvim, - va hamma narsa shunchalik yaxshi tasvirlanganki, odam butun kecha uxlab, ularni yashirincha o'qiydi.

en: So mind you don't read them, Nas- tenka,' said she.
uz: Shunday qilib, ularni o'qimaganing uchun ehtiyot bo'l, Nas-tenka, - dedi u.

en: 'What books has he sent?' 'They are all Walter Scott's novels, grandmother.' 'Walter Scott's novels!
uz: U qanday kitoblarni yubordi? Ularning barchasi Uolter Skotning romani, buvim. Uolter Skotning romani!

en: But stay, isn't there some trick about it?
uz: Ammo qoling, bu erda biron bir hiyla yo'qmi?

en: Look, hasn't he stuck a love-letter among them?' 'No, grandmother,' I said, 'there isn't a love-letter.' 'But look under the binding; they sometimes stuff it under the bindings, the rascals!' 'No, grandmother, there is nothing under the binding.' 'Well, that's all right.' 'So we began reading Walter Scott, and in a month or so we had read al- most half.
uz: Yo'q, buvim, - dedim men, buvim yo'q. Ammo bog'lanish ostida ko'ringlar, ba'zan uni bog'lanish ostida to'ldiradilar, o'g'rilar! Yo'q, buvim, bog'lanish ostida hech narsa yo'q. Ha, yaxshi.   So'ngra biz Valter Skotni o'qishni boshladik va bir oy o'tgach, ko'pchilikni o'qib chiqdik.

en: Then he sent us more and more.
uz: So'ngra bizni ko'proq va ko'proq yubordi.

en: He sent us Pushkin, too; so that at last I could not get on without a book, and left off dreaming of how ﬁne it would be to marry a Chinese Prince.
uz: U bizga Puşkinni ham yubordi; nihoyat, men kitobsiz o'tib ketolmasdim va Xitoy prensi bilan turmush qurish qanchalik yaxshi bo'lishini orzu qilishni to'xtatdim.

en: That's how things were when I chanced one day to meet our lodger on the stairs.
uz: Bir kuni men turar joyda yashaydigan kishi bilan uchrashganimda, vaziyat shunday edi.

en: Grandmother had sent me to fetch something.
uz: Buyuk onam meni biror narsa olib kelishimga yubordi.

en: blushed and he blushed; he laughed, though, said good-morning to me, asked after grandmother, and said: 'Well, have you read the books?' I an- swered that I had.
uz: Qizig'i qizg'inadi va o'zi qizg'inadi; lekin u kulishdi, menga salom so'radi, buvimning nomini so'radi va: Siz kitoblarni o'qirdingizmi? - deb so'radi.

en: 'Which did you like best?' he asked.
uz: Senga qaysi biri ko'proq yoqdi? deb so'radi u.

en: I said, 'Ivanhoe, and Pushkin best of all,' and so our talk ended for that time.
uz: Men: Ivanho va Pushkin eng yaxshisi, - dedim va suhbatimiz o'sha payt uchun yakunlandi.

en: A week later I met him again on the stairs.
uz: Bir hafta o'tgach, men u bilan yana turg'unlarda uchrashdim.

en: That time grandmother had not sent me, I wanted to get something for myself.
uz: Oʻsha paytlarda buvim meni yuborgan boʻlmaganda, oʻzim uchun biror narsa olishni xohladim.

en: It was past two, and the lodger used to come home at that time.
uz: Soat ikki o'tgach edi va uy egasi o'sha paytda uyga qaytadi.

en: 'Good-afternoon,' said he.
uz: Xayrli kechki payt, dedi u.

en: I said good-afternoon, too.
uz: Men ham yaxshi kecha so'radim.

en: 'Aren't you dull,' he said, 'sitting all day with your grandmother?' When he asked that, I blushed, I don't know why; I felt ashamed, and again I felt offended—I suppose because other people had begun to ask me about that.
